payload.page_title: Observability Onboarding Playbook for Security-Sensitive Tenants

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the recommended observability onboarding flow for enterprise tenants with elevated security or compliance requirements (e.g., regulated data, VPC/private deployments, customer-managed KMS). It covers required telemetry types, minimal sampling & redact rules, validation steps, and a short escalation matrix for observability-related incidents during and immediately after cutover.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployment modes where tenants require restricted telemetry or local-only logs.
- Intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSE), Solutions Architects (SA), Platform Oncall, and the customer's SRE/Platform teams.
- Not a replacement for full security reviews or legal signoff; follow the enterprise compliance checklist in the related pages for evidence collection.

Goals:
- Ensure observability provides sufficient coverage for SLO verification while maintaining tenant privacy and compliance constraints.
- Deliver a repeatable runbook that reduces onboarding time and clarifies escalation paths.

Prerequisites:
1) Signed contract with telemetry retention and access terms documented.
2) Customer provides target telemetry endpoints (push or collector) and access credentials or ensures TLS mutual auth is configured.
3) Customer and Redwood agree on redaction rules for sensitive fields (PII, PHI, etc.).
4) Tenant has completed network peering/firewall rules and provided sample request traces.

Ownership and Roles:
- Customer Success (CSE): primary owner for onboarding timeline and checklist completion.
- Solutions Architect (SA): verifies architecture, telemetry schema alignment and sample payloads.
- Platform Oncall: validates alerting and synthetic checks in Redwood-managed monitoring (if permitted).
- Customer SRE: provides local log/metric endpoints and participates in validation.

Telemetry Requirements (minimum):
| Category | Required signals | Minimum retention | Redaction notes |
|----------|------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Traces | Ingress request traces with trace-id, latency, error flag | 30 days (or per contract) | Strip user identifiers; hash tenant ids if needed |
| Metrics | Request QPS, p95/p99 latency, error rates, token consumption | 90 days | Aggregated only across user cohorts |
| Logs | Request-level logs for error-level events + request-id | 14 days | Remove raw user content; keep request metadata |
| Telemetry Health | Agent heartbeats, SDK version, buffer backpressure metrics | 90 days | N/A |

Step-by-step Onboarding Procedure:
1. Kickoff and Alignment (Day -14 to -7):
   - Schedule a kickoff with CSE, SA, Customer SRE, and Platform Oncall.
   - Confirm telemetry endpoints, credentials, and allowed IP ranges.
   - Agree on the redaction rules and sign the telemetry access addendum.

2. Minimal Instrumentation Delivery (Day -7 to -3):
   - Customer sends 2 representative request traces and one synthetic workload run.
   - SA runs schema validation and returns a compliance brief noting any missing fields.

3. Telemetry Channel Setup (Day -3 to -1):
   - If customer provides collector: verify TLS, client certs, and authentication.
   - If Redwood pushes telemetry into customer endpoint: set up a short-lived proof-of-concept stream with limited retention.
   - Apply the agreed redaction/transformation rules in the pipeline.

4. Validation and Synthetic Checks (Day 0):
   - Run the synthetic health suite against the tenant for 2 hours covering cold-start, peak burst, and steady traffic.
   - Validate that p95/p99 latencies are within expected bounds and that trace sampling is consistent.
   - Customer and SA sign the Observability Acceptance checklist (see Validation Checklist below).

5. Cutover and Monitoring Window (Day 0 to +7):
   - Monitor telemetry for anomalous error rates, unexpected high cardinality metrics, or missing traces.
   - Execute daily tail-sampling review for the first 72 hours to ensure no sensitive payloads leak into logs.

Validation Checklist (to be signed by SA and Customer SRE):
- [ ] TLS and auth validated for telemetry endpoints.
- [ ] Redaction rules applied and sample payloads confirmed.
- [ ] Trace and log correlation (request-id) present in samples.
- [ ] Synthetic suite p95/p99 within agreed thresholds.
- [ ] Alerting configured for the tenant’s SLOs.
- [ ] Data retention settings match contract.

SLOs and Alert Thresholds (example defaults, adapt per customer):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for inference API (customer-level). Alert: > 3% error rate sustained for 10 minutes.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short requests, p99 < 800ms. Alert: p99 > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Telemetry Pipeline Health: dropped events > 0.5% over 1 hour => Pager.

Escalation Matrix (observability-specific):
| Severity | Trigger | Initial owner | Escalation (15m) | Notes |
|----------|---------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| Sev 1 | Telemetry pipeline outage (no traces) during cutover | Platform Oncall | Engineering SRE lead -> CSE Director | Customer-impacted visibility; page customer SLA contacts |
| Sev 2 | Aggressive data leakage risk (sensitive fields detected) | SA + Customer SRE | Security team and Legal notified | Temporary data flow stop may be required |
| Sev 3 | Missing minor metrics or gaps in synthetic checks | CSE | Platform Observability PO | Operational impact, no immediate customer outage |

Immediate Mitigations for Data Leakage:
1. Pause forwarding to Redwood-managed collectors and retain only locally (customer-managed).
2. Re-run redaction/transformation pipeline on a sampled dataset.
3. Notify Security and Legal; prepare evidence packet if required by contract.

Rollback and Safe-Fail Plans:
- If any critical telemetry validation fails, revert routing to the pre-onboarding telemetry stream for 1 hour while root cause is investigated.
- If rollback is not possible due to networking, disable non-essential telemetry streams (detailed in the Appendix config).

Operational Playbook for Platform Oncall (first 72 hours):
- Verify agent heartbeats every 15 minutes; confirm no buffer-overflow alerts.
- Run manual tail-sampling at 09:00, 15:00, and 21:00 UTC to inspect for accidental PII.
- If telemetry drops below 90% expected events, trigger Sev2 and follow escalation.

Appendix A — Example Transformation Rules (YAML):
```yaml
# Example pipeline fragment used to redact user text and hash tenant ids
transformations:
  - name: redact_user_text
    type: redact_regex
    fields: [request.body, request.prompt]
    pattern: '(?i)(ssn|credit_card|\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b)'
    replacement: '[REDACTED]'
  - name: hash_tenant_id
    type: hash
    fields: [tenant.id]
    algorithm: SHA256
    salt: '{{contract_salt}}'
```

Appendix B — Sample Acceptance Signoff (copy into ticket):
- "We confirm telemetry endpoints are validated, redaction rules applied, synthetic checks passed, and data retention settings comply with contract. Customer SRE: <name>, Redwood SA: <name>. Signed: <date>."

References and Related Pages:
- Enterprise telemetry and compliance checklist (linked in related_pages).
- Observability Operator runbook (internal): /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/observability-operator-runbook

Revision History:
- 2025-03-12: Drafted by Ava Martinez.
- 2025-05-06: Added data-leak mitigations after customer incident (postmortem ref: INC-2025-00412).
- 2025-07-01: Published after reviewer approvals.

payload.page_title: Tenant Onboarding: Acceptance Testing & Telemetry Assertions

sections.body:
A structured acceptance-testing playbook to validate tenant readiness after provisioning and before hand-back. Defines telemetry assertions, synthetic scenarios, and safe rollback/fallback steps tailored to Dedicated and Private tenants.
Purpose

This playbook provides a repeatable acceptance-testing and telemetry-assertion checklist for enterprise tenant cutovers (Dedicated and Private modes). Its goal is to ensure customers meet their SLOs and observability expectations before the CX hand-off.

Scope and audience

- Audience: Customer Success Engineers (CSE), Solutions Engineers, Oncall SREs, and Platform Engineers executing go-live validation.
- Scope: Post-provisioning validation window (first 72 hours), focused on latency, error rates, throughput, billing signals, and data-plane connectivity. Not intended for long-term performance tuning.

Prerequisites

1. Tenant is provisioned and accessible; operator has admin token and tenant ID.
2. Telemetry forwarding (metrics/traces/logs) enabled to central telemetry workspace or customer-managed forwarder.
3. Canary API key created and injected into test harness.

Quick checklist (high level)

- [ ] DNS / network reachability verified (ping, curl).
- [ ] TLS certificate chain validated for private endpoints.
- [ ] Basic API call succeeds and returns expected schema.
- [ ] Ingress egress firewall rules allow control-plane callbacks (if Private).
- [ ] Telemetry streams ingest baseline synthetic traffic.

Acceptance criteria (signal-level)

Provide these pass/fail assertions to the customer and engineering stakeholders. If any assertion fails, execute the rollback/fallback procedure below.

| Signal | Metric | Assertion (pass) |
|---|---:|---|
| Availability | 5m rolling availability | >= 99.5% during acceptance window |
| Latency (generate) | p95 gen latency | <= 600ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) |
| Error rate | 1m error rate (5xx + 429) | < 0.5% |
| Throughput | steady-state rps | Sustains expected commit profile ±10% |
| Cost signal | estimated projected daily token cost | Within agreed finance cap ±15% |
| Telemetry lag | metric ingestion lag | < 60s for critical alerts |

Telemetry assertions (concrete checks)

- Metrics to assert in the first 72 hours:
  - request.count by route and model variant
  - request.latency.p50/p95/p99 by route
  - request.errors.5xx and request.errors.ratelimit
  - kvcache.hit_ratio and kvcache.miss_ratio (if KV cache enabled)
  - pod.resource.cpu_util and pod.resource.gpu_util per node pool
  - billing.estimate.daily_tokens and billing.estimate.24h_projection

- Alert thresholds to temporarily enable for acceptance:
  - latency.p95 > 800ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - errors.5xx >= 1% for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - telemetry.lag > 120s -> Sev3

Synthetic test scenarios (run in order)

1) Smoke: Basic generation and embeddings
   - Command: curl -X POST https://{tenant-host}/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer {canary_key}" -d '{"prompt": "Hello world","max_tokens": 20}'
   - Expected: 200 OK, model output length <= 40 tokens, schema contains request_id and latency_ms

2) Latency profile: Burst of short prompts
   - Run: 100 short prompt requests over 60s (ramp 0->100rps) using our load harness
   - Expected: p95 latency within asserted bound; no tail errors or rate-limit biasing normal routes

3) Throughput profile: Sustained throughput at committed RPS
   - Run: sustained RPS for 15 minutes equal to tenant commit (or 50% of commit if in dry-run)
   - Expected: no autoscaler thrash; no OOMs on pods; stable CPU/GPU util curves

4) KV cache warm/cold cycle (if enabled)
   - Run a prefix-heavy scenario, measure kvcache.hit_ratio rising above 40% within 5 minutes for typical workloads

5) Failure injection: Simulate model fallback
   - Trigger: mark primary variant unhealthy via platform toggle; confirm automatic routing to fallback variant within policy window and acceptable quality degradation metrics tracked

Operational commands and tooling

- Test harness quickstart (example):
  - docker run --rm -e TENANT_HOST={tenant-host} -e API_KEY={canary_key} redwood/load-harness:latest --script short-burst.json

- Curl example for telemetry assertion (prometheus query):
  - curl -s "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=request_latency_p95{tenant=\"{tenant_id}\"}" | jq .data.result

Rollback and fallback (safe steps)

If acceptance fails for any critical assertion, follow the safe rollback below in order. Document each step in the ticket.

1. Pause customer traffic (edge ACL or routing flag). Record timestamp.
2. If degraded due to model variant, revert routing to the last verified variant (platform toggle):
   - UI: Console -> Tenants -> {tenant} -> Traffic routing -> Revert to stable
   - API: POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/routing?action=revert&to=stable
3. If resource saturation (OOMs/GC spikes): scale up GPU pool by +1 node or apply temporary burst capacity policy.
4. If networking (Private) issues: re-run firewall handshake and verify peering configurations; escalate to network infra.
5. If cost projection exceeded: engage FinOps and set soft quota throttle at 90% of projected cap.

Ownership and escalation matrix

| Role | Primary | Secondary | Pager | Escalation criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSE | Aisha Kaur | Ruth Chen | N/A | Any acceptance failure requiring customer comms |
| Platform SRE | Owen Patel | Diego Martinez | oncall-sre@redwood.com | Resource OOMs, autoscaler thrash
| Network | Priya Sharma | Lukas Berg | network-oncall@redwood.com | Private peering / firewall failures
| FinOps | Maya Singh | Jonah Park | finops@redwood.com | Projected spend > cap + 10%

Post-acceptance handback checklist

- Confirm all temporary high-sensitivity alerts are returned to normal thresholds.
- Remove canary API key and rotate if requested.
- Share a short acceptance report with: customer, AE, CSE, and Platform owner. Report should include: acceptance window metrics snapshot, synthetic script outputs, and any remediation performed.
- Schedule QBR readiness meeting within 30 days to review long-term SLOs and cost profile.

Telemetry dashboard templates (recommended panels)

- Tenant Overview: availability, p95/p99 latency, error rate, synthetic test pass/fail
- Model Variants: per-variant request count, fallbacks, average latency
- Resource Utilization: per-node GPU/CPU, pod restarts, OOM counts
- Cost: 24h token estimate, projected 7d and 30d spend

Appendix: Example acceptance report snippet

- Acceptance window: 2026-02-10 02:00 -> 2026-02-10 08:00 UTC
- p95 latency (generate, short prompts): 412ms
- Availability: 99.92%
- kvcache.hit_ratio: 46% after warm-up
- Actions performed: Increased burst capacity by 1 node at 02:45 UTC; reverted routing at 03:10 UTC after model health check.

Related pages and artifacts

- Canary harness repo: git@github.com:redwood/load-harness.git
- Telemetry queries library: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tenant-telemetry-queries-2025

Contact and communication templates

- Short acceptance success email template included in internal snippets: "Subject: Tenant {tenant} — Acceptance Complete. Summary: [key metrics]. Next: schedule QBR"

Notes and version history

- v1.0 (2025-11-12) initial creation by Aisha Kaur
- v1.1 (2025-12-08) added KV-cache warm/cold assertions (reviewer: Diego Martinez)
- v1.2 (2026-02-15) tightened latency assertions for p95 and clarified rollback step 2 (reviewer: Ruth Chen)

payload.page_title: Billing dispute and chargeback resolution playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the operational process, SLAs, communications templates, and ownership for resolving enterprise billing disputes and chargeback requests during onboarding and the first 90 days post-go-live. It is intended for CSMs, BillingOps, Finance, Support Engineering, and Legal.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Purpose: Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for billing disputes, ensure consistent customer communications, protect revenue recognition, and capture audit evidence for chargebacks or credits.
- Scope: Applies to all enterprise tenants (Dedicated and Private) with contract value >= $50k ARR during onboarding and the first 90 days after go-live. Does not replace Finance-led invoicing corrections for legacy invoices; it coordinates with Finance for those cases.
sections.heading: Purpose and scope

sections.body:
- Dispute: A customer-initiated claim that an invoice, usage charge, or billing calculation is incorrect.
- Chargeback: A request to reverse or offset billed amount against a future invoice or issue a formal credit.
- Priority levels:
  1) P0 — Billing outage affecting all invoices or system-side errors that systematically overcharge customers; target acknowledgement < 1 business hour; remediation plan in 4 hours.
  2) P1 — Material dispute where customer-facing usage appears incorrect (>10% deviation or > $5k discrepancy); target acknowledgement < 4 business hours; resolution in 3 business days.
  3) P2 — Minor disagreement or clarification (<10% and < $5k); target acknowledgement within 1 business day; resolution in 10 business days.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- First responder: Customer Success Manager (CSM) — initial intake, triage, and customer comms.
- Technical validation: Support Engineering (SE) — investigates telemetry, request logs, KV/cache behavior, and model fallback records.
- Billing operations: BillingOps — recalculates usage, verifies aggregation + quota logic, prepares credits.
- Finance: Signs off on formal credits and updates AR records.
- Legal: Engaged when contractual dispute or potential revenue recognition impact.
sections.heading: Ownership and contacts

sections.body:
1) CSM escalates to SE (channel: #billing-ops-escalations, tag @oncall-se) after initial intake if P0/P1.
2) SE triages, produces technical findings and a short timeline (within 8 hours for P1).
3) If disagreement remains after technical validation, CSM opens BillingOps ticket (billing-api) and informs Finance.
4) If resolution crosses 5 business days or exceeds $50k, escalate to Director of Customer Success + Head of Billing for approval and external comms.
sections.heading: Escalation matrix

sections.body:
1) Intake (CSM)
   - Capture: customer contact, invoice ID, invoice date, disputed amount, business impact, and preferred remedy (credit, refund, or adjustment).
   - Assign priority (P0/P1/P2) and open the internal incident in the Customer Success ticketing queue (prefix: BILL-). Attach customer-provided artifacts (screenshots, billing CSVs).
2) Triage (CSM, within SLA for priority)
   - Verify customer identity and contract tier. Confirm invoice numbers and timeframe.
   - If P0, immediately declare incident and notify #ops-all and on-call SRE.
3) Technical investigation (SE)
   - Confirm request routing and model selection logs: check `billing-api` request logs, `ingress-gateway` traces, and `telemetry-gatekeeper` aggregation.
   - Query usage records: run query against `usage-aggregation` table (example SQL):
     SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as total_tokens, model_name, date
     FROM usage_aggregation
     WHERE tenant_id = 'TENANT_X' AND date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-10-31'
     GROUP BY tenant_id, model_name, date;
   - Verify any cache-busting events, canary rollouts, or model-fanout that could double-count tokens.
   - Produce a short findings doc (one-page) that lists root-cause candidates and evidence links.
4) BillingOps reconciliation
   - Recompute the invoice using the canonical aggregation export (CSV/JSON) and the rate-card in effect for the invoice period. Maintain a checksumed export and attach to the case.
   - If code/aggregation bug found, create a paging ticket in engineering backlog with severity and request a hotfix/retroactive adjustment.
5) Proposal and customer communication (CSM + BillingOps)
   - Draft proposed remedy (credit/refund/adjustment) and the timeline for application.
   - Use the communication templates below.
6) Finance sign-off and execution
   - Finance validates credit amount, posts credit memo or refund, updates AR, and records reason codes.
   - BillingOps updates invoice metadata and attaches evidence to the ticket.
7) Closure and retrospective
   - Confirm customer acceptance, update ticket with resolution artifacts, and schedule a 1-week postmortem for P0/P1 cases.
   - Capture follow-up actions in the customer QBR if systemic.
sections.heading: Operational procedure (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Customer-submitted dispute form or email (archive).
- Relevant invoice PDF and raw aggregation export (CSV/JSON).
- Query IDs and trace IDs from `ingress-gateway` and `billing-api` (trace links).
- Findings doc from SE and final recalculation spreadsheet with checksum.
- Finance credit memo number or refund transaction ID.

Communication templates (examples)
1) Acknowledgement (send within SLA)
Subject: Acknowledged — Billing enquiry for invoice INV-12345
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
Thank you — we have received your billing enquiry for invoice INV-12345 (amount: $X). We have opened case BILL-6789 and assigned it priority [P1]. Our technical and billing teams will investigate and we will update you inside the SLA timelines. If you have additional artifacts, please attach them to this thread.
2) Interim status (P1/P0)
Subject: Interim update — Billing enquiry INV-12345 (case BILL-6789)
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
We are actively investigating. Current findings: [short summary]. Target resolution: [date/time]. If the issue is high-impact we will provide hourly updates.
3) Resolution and credit confirmation
Subject: Resolved — Billing enquiry INV-12345 (case BILL-6789)
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
We have completed our investigation and applied the following remedy: [credit/refund/adjustment details with reference #]. The credit will appear on your next invoice (or refund dispatched on [date]). Summary of cause: [one-paragraph root cause]. Preventative steps taken: [bullet list].

Customer-facing acceptance criteria (must be documented in ticket):
- The refunded or credited amount equals the agreed remedy.
- Finance has produced a credit memo or refund transaction ID and AR is updated.
- Customer confirms acceptance in writing.
sections.heading: Evidence and artifacts to collect (minimum)

sections.body:
- Automate evidence collection: attach aggregated usage export and trace IDs at intake using the `billing-intake` Lambda hook.
- Add a billing dispute webhook to notify `#billing-ops-escalations` with structured payload: {"case_id":"BILL-XXXXX","tenant_id":"T-123","priority":"P1","invoice_id":"INV-..."} (engineering backlog item: BILLING-2381).
- Maintain a shared Google Sheet (read-only for customers) for long-running reconciliations; link in the ticket.
sections.heading: Automation and tooling recommendations

sections.body:
- SLA compliance: percent of disputes acknowledged within target SLA (goal >= 98%).
- MTTR by priority: target P1 <= 3 business days (rolling 90-day median).
- Error rate: percent of invoices requiring adjustment after go-live (target <= 0.5%).
- Fiscal impact: mean credit amount and top contributing root causes.
sections.heading: Reporting and KPIs

sections.body:
- Duplicate charge due to canary rollback: If SE confirms double-counting tied to canary rollback, proceed with immediate credit and create an engineering incident.
- Customer claims lost feature credits (promo/discount not applied): verify contract-level entitlements and reconcile with rate card; escalate to Finance/Legal for contract amendment if needed.
- Suspected fraud / abuse: pause account billing (billing-api flag: billing_hold = true), notify Legal and follow fraud handling SOP.
sections.heading: Playbook examples and edge cases

sections.body:
- For P0/P1 incidents, schedule a 1-week postmortem with CSM, SE, BillingOps, and Finance. Capture root cause, corrective action, and preventive measures.
- Feed recurring root causes into the onboarding playbook and update rate-card validations in the billing pipeline.

Appendix A — Quick triage checklist (for CSMs)
1) Confirm invoice ID, disputed amount, and date range.
2) Confirm tenant tier and active contract adjustments.
3) Attach customer artifacts and create BILL- ticket.
4) Ping #billing-ops-escalations with case link for P0/P1.
5) Confirm SE assigned and expected update time.

Appendix B — Example internal Slack alert (to #billing-ops-escalations)
Payload (one-line): BILL-6789 | TENANT_T-123 | P1 | INV-12345 | $8,900 | @priya.nambiar — investigation assigned to @oncall-se. Link: <ticket_url>

Appendix C — Minimal JSON export schema for reconciliation artifacts
- ticket_id: string
- tenant_id: string
- invoice_id: string
- period_start: YYYY-MM-DD
- period_end: YYYY-MM-DD
- raw_usage_export_url: https://...
- recalculated_amount: string (decimal)
- evidence_links: [comma-separated links]
sections.heading: Postmortem and continuous improvement

sections.body:
- Service names referenced: billing-api, ingestion-gateway, usage-aggregation, telemetry-gatekeeper, billing-intake lambda.
- See related playbooks: tenant-finops-cutover-governance-playbook (onboarding), enterprise-cost-anomaly-detection-and-action-playbook (health & QBR).
sections.heading: Notes and links

sections.body:
- Document owner: Priya Nambiar (Customer Success).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0/P1 incident.

payload.page_title: Observability Conformance and Failover Certification Playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a standardized certification process for enterprise onboarding focused on observability conformance and failover simulation. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable test-suite that validates a tenant's integration with Redwood's telemetry, alerting, and failover behaviors before and during go‑live.

Why this exists:
- Ensure consistent telemetry quality and signal availability for QBRs and SLO enforcement.
- Reduce post‑go‑live escalations by pre‑validating failure modes and remediation paths.
- Provide a clear sign‑off for both Customer Success and the customer’s engineering team.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Customer Success engineers (CSEs), Onboarding architects, Customer reliability engineers, SRE on-call.
- Applies to: Dedicated and Private tenants (VPC/on‑prem), customers with reserved capacity, and any Hosted customers requesting enterprise SLA/observability contracts.
- Not in scope: low‑volume self‑serve signups unless otherwise requested.

Certification objectives (pass criteria):
1) Observability conformance: required metrics, traces, and logs are present, correctly tagged, and within fidelity bounds.
2) Alert and paging behavior: alerts fire at configured thresholds and route to intended escalation targets.
3) Failover simulation: tenant can gracefully fallback to configured model‑variant and/or region policy without data loss or broken requests within SLOs.
4) Performance parity: tail latency and 95p token throughput are within 10% of the accepted baseline for the tenant profile.

Prerequisites (customer and Redwood):
- Customer provides: representative API keys, ingress IP ranges, and a traffic seed (synthetic workload or production snapshot).
- Contracted observability level agreed (metrics retention window, trace sampling rate).
- Access: cross-account metrics forwarding set up (if Dedicated/Private), service account for telemetry validation, and customer contact list for paging.
- Baseline established: a 24h baseline run capturing normal traffic characteristics and sequence length distribution.

Conformance test suite (run by CSE):
- Metrics coverage checklist (automated assertions):
  - Per-tenant request count (counter)
  - Per-model token count (counter)
  - Per-route 95th and 99th percent latency (histogram)
  - Inference errors by class (5xx, 4xx, model-timeout)
  - KV cache hit ratio (gauge)
  - Batching statistics (avg batch size, dropout count)
  - Memory/GC and GPU memory pressure (hosted or dedicated telemetry exporters)
- Tracing:
  - Root span includes route, model.id, request.id, tenant.id, and sequence_len tags.
  - KV cache warmup and cache-miss traces for long‑running sessions.
  - Downstream service spans (e.g., affinity proxy, telemetry bridge) present and correlated.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, severity, tenant_id, request_id, model_variant, error_code.

Telemetry assertion examples (fail/pass matrix):
- Metric emission: per-tenant request counter emits once per request -> pass if >=99.9% of sampled requests have metrics.
- Tag fidelity: model_variant tag present -> pass if present in >=99% of traces.
- Sampling: trace sampling at configured rate within ±2% of target.

Failover simulation scenarios (minimum required):
1) Model variant degradation: simulate a regression in primary model (increased generation time or error rate). Expected behavior: automatic traffic shift to fallback variant within configured rollout window; client-facing failures <=0.1% during switch.
2) Regional outage: simulate region R failover to R2. Expected behavior: DNS/Anycast routing handoff, warming of KV cache for hot prefixes, and latency impact within contractual SLOs (95p latency < 2x baseline or configured threshold).
3) GPU node eviction (Dedicated): simulate node preemption and validate autoscaler rehydration, batch redistribution, and request retry behavior.
4) Telemetry bridge loss: simulate loss of telemetry export for 5 minutes and validate local buffering, partial metrics backfill correctness, and alert suppression mechanisms.

Detailed runbook (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (T-72 to T-1 days):
  - T-72: Confirm prerequisites, sign OSS (if applicable), and create certification ticket in JIRA (label: obs-cert).
  - T-48: Customer provides traffic seed and auth tokens for test harness.
  - T-24: Baseline run completed and validated; acceptance thresholds documented.
  - T-1: Final smoke test and contact list validated.
2) Execution day (D):
  - 09:00: Kickoff call with stakeholders.
  - 09:30–11:00: Run observability conformance scripts (see commands below).
  - 11:00–12:30: Run failover scenario 1 (model variant). Monitor telemetry and collect traces.
  - 13:30–15:30: Run region failover simulation with staged traffic migration.
  - 15:30–16:30: Run node eviction and telemetry bridge tests.
  - 16:30–17:30: Analyze results, compile pass/fail, and agree next steps.
3) Post-exec (D+1 to D+7):
  - D+1: Deliver certification report and recommended remediations.
  - D+3–D+7: Re-run specific tests on fixes and mark items closed in certification ticket.

Automation commands and snippets (examples):
- Run metric smoke test (CLI):
```
redwoodctl observability assert --tenant $TENANT_ID --duration 15m --checks metrics,logs,traces --out results.yaml
```
- Inject model latency fault (test harness uses canary traffic):
```
redwoodctl inject fault --target model:$MODEL_ID --type delay --p50 200ms --p95 1200ms --duration 10m
```
- Simulate region drain (staged):
```
redwoodctl region failover --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --staged 50,75,100 --monitoring-window 5m
```

Pass/fail reporting and artifact collection:
- Artifacts required for sign-off: results.yaml (assertions), raw trace archive (.zip), sample logs (masked PII), screenshots of dashboards showing baseline vs test windows, and a short executive summary (1 page).
- Pass requires: all high-priority conformance checks passed AND no more than 2 medium severity failover gaps (with tied remediation plan).

Remediation and escalation matrix:
- Severity classification:
  - P0: cert-blocker (missing tenant id tags, missing request counter, or failover causes >1% client errors) -> Engineering oncall + CSE triage within 1 hour.
  - P1: degraded observability signals (missing noncritical tags, sampling misalignment) -> Owner team fix within 72 hours.
  - P2: cosmetic issues (logging format differences) -> backlog item for future patch.
- Escalation flow: CSE -> Platform Oncall -> Runtime Engineering -> Head of SRE. Use the internal pager channel #obs-cert-paging for P0.

Sign-off and handover:
- Sign-off stakeholders: Customer Success Manager, Customer Reliability Lead, Onboarding Architect, and SRE certifier.
- Sign-off artifact: single JSON certificate stored in the ticket with fields: tenant_id, cert_date, results_uri, signer_emails, scope (observability/failover), and expiry (90 days).

Operational notes and cautions:
- For Private deployments with air-gapped telemetry, ensure local artifact encryption and transfer controls are in place.
- Avoid running production traffic seeding during business critical windows; prefer weekend or agreed maintenance windows.
- When simulating paid capacity changes (autoscaler stress), ensure commercial approval for potential billing spikes.

Ownership and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Morgan Reyes (Customer Success – Observability Lead).
- Primary engineering contact: Kai Huang (Runtime Engineering).
- SRE escalation: Oncall rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rotation).

Templates and checklists (appendix):
- Preflight checklist (checkbox list):
  - [ ] Traffic seed uploaded and validated
  - [ ] Cross-account metrics forwarding configured
  - [ ] Pager rotations updated
  - [ ] Baseline run completed
  - [ ] JIRA ticket created and stakeholders invited
- Certification report template (fields to populate):
  - Tenant ID, Customer contact, Certification date, Tests run, Pass/fail summary, Remediation items, Signers.

QBR integration and recurring validation:
- If certified, tenant will be enrolled in a quarterly telemetry health check. The certification expiry triggers a reminder 30 days before expiry to schedule a re-certification window. Failures found during QBR health checks feed back into the remediation board and may require out-of-band recertification.

Related resources and references:
- Observability contract template (product-docs/pricing-and-packaging)
- Telemetry exporters and agent configuration examples (integration-guides/telemetry-onboarding)
- Oncall runbooks and escalation playbooks (oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process)

Revision history:
- 2026-02-14: Draft authored by Morgan Reyes.
- 2026-04-02: Added telemetry bridge simulation details. Reviewer: Kai Huang.
- 2026-06-01: Updated pass criteria and automation commands; added private deployment note. Reviewer: Leah Thompson.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Customer Telemetry Synthesis and Action Runbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook describes the standardized process Customer Success and Support use to synthesize customer telemetry into actionable signals during enterprise onboarding, early go‑live, and post‑cutover QBRs. It is designed to reduce time‑to‑remediation, align SLO interpretations across teams, and automate low‑risk actions where safe.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and hosted customers that have integrated Redwood telemetry (metrics, traces, logs, synthetic tests) via the Telemetry Gatekeeper or native SDK integration. Does NOT replace incident runbooks for platform SRE; it supports customer‑facing stability and cost alerts.

Audience: Customer Success Managers, Support Engineers (L1/L2), Solutions Engineers, Onboarding Engineers, and Customer Reliability Engineers.

Summary of key flows

- Telemetry ingestion mapping and synthesis: map raw metrics -> SLIs -> composite customer stability score.
- Alert triage flow: auto‑enrich alerts with context (tenant profile, recent model rollouts, recent config changes) before paging L2.
- Automated remediation actions: controlled actions that Support can trigger (cache flush, model fallback, transient quota bump).
- QBR inputs: aggregated signals and synthetic results to inform health reviews and contractual SLO discussions.

Definitions and SLO mapping
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- SLI: Service Level Indicator (e.g., p50/p95/latency, token cost per request).
- SLO: Service Level Objective (target on an SLI, e.g., p95 < 600ms).
- Stability Score: 0–100 composite derived from weighted SLIs for a tenant.

Example SLI -> SLO mapping (table):
| SLI name | Collection source | Aggregation | Baseline SLO | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| inference_p95_latency_ms | ingress-gateway.metrics/latency_ms | 5m window p95 | < 600 | Apply per‑route, per‑model when available |
| error_rate_pct | service.errors/total_requests | 1h window rate | < 0.5 | Include 4xx/5xx split |
| kvcache_hit_rate_pct | runtime.kvcache/hits_total | 30m avg | > 75 | Most effective for prompt-heavy workloads |
| token_cost_per_1k | billing.tokens/units | rolling 24h avg | < $0.08 | Important for FinOps/QBR |

SLO thresholds in alerts: the thresholds above are defaults; for enterprise customers we expect to map contract SLAs to these fields and override thresholds in tenant config.

Telemetry synthesis: algorithm (high level)

1. Normalize raw metrics to common time windows (5m/30m/1h/24h).
2. Compute scaled z‑scores relative to tenant historic baseline (30 days).
3. Apply weightings: latency 40%, error_rate 30%, kvcache_hit_rate 20%, cost 10%.
4. Output Stability Score = 100 - weighted_penalty, with discrete buckets: Healthy >= 90, Watch 70-89, Degraded 50-69, Critical < 50.

Actionable alerts and enrichment

When an alert fires, the gatekeeper enrichment pipeline must attach:
- Tenant metadata: tier (self-serve/enterprise), region, dedicated/private, service owner contact.
- Recent deployments: last model version deploy time, quantization profile version, recent rollout policy.
- Recent telemetry anomalies: 30m jump in token_cost_per_1k, 5m p95 spike, kvcache drop.

Example alert rule (Prometheus/Alertmanager style, translated):
- alert: TenantHighLatency
  expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ingress_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=~"$TENANT"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000) > 0.6
  for: 5m
  labels: { severity: warn, category: latency }
  annotations: { runbook_url: "https://confluence/redwood/customer-telemetry-synthesis-and-action-runbook" }

Auto‑enrichment example (pseudocode):
1. Receive alert payload -> extract tenant_id.
2. Query tenant profile API: GET /internal/api/tenant/{tenant_id}/profile -> return tier, owner, models_in_use.
3. Query rollout history: GET /internal/api/deployments?tenant={tenant_id}&since=1h.
4. Attach top 3 correlated anomalies (promql results) to alert.

Triage playbook (step‑by‑step)

1) L1 intake (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm alert details and enrichment metadata.
- Run quick checks: synthetic latency test (see commands below), kvcache delta check, model version consistency.
- If Stability Score >= 90 and alert severity warn, file a ticket and set PENDING_AUTOMATION; if automation exists, trigger (see AutomatedRemediations section).

2) L2 triage (10–45 minutes)
- Validate root cause hypothesis: traffic surge, model rollback, upstream DNS/peering, customer config change.
- Check recent deployments and customer change log (tracked in tenant audit index).
- If infrastructure issue (network/cloud provider), hand off to Platform SRE via #sre-customer-handoff and include enriched evidence.

3) Escalation to Customer Success & Solutions (45–120 minutes)
- If customer-visible impact and partial mitigation not found, notify CSM and schedule a 15‑minute bridge.
- Notify legal/compliance for regulated tenants if data exfil or KMS errors are indicated.

AutomatedRemediations (approved actions L1 can run)

- flush_kvcache (low risk): clears Redis/KV cache for tenant; idempotent.
- fallback_to_small_model: switch tenant routing to a compatible smaller model variant for 1 hour.
- transient_quota_bump: raise rate limit by 20% for 10 minutes for bursty onboarding flows (requires audit logging).
sections.heading: Important definitions (abbreviations used in this runbook)

sections.body:
$ rw-support run-action --tenant t-12345 --action flush_kvcache --reason "p95 spike during onboarding"
Response: { "status": "accepted", "action_id":"act-20270310-0001" }

Safety checks before automation: verify that tenant is not on restricted list and that action is allowed in tenant profile (tenant_profile.automation_allowed==true). All automated actions create an audit event and a support ticket.

Diagnostic commands and queries

- Synthetic latency probe (curl):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_API_KEY" -X POST https://ingress.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b", "prompt":"ping"}' -D /tmp/latency_hdrs -o /tmp/latency_body
- KV cache delta (PromQL):
avg_over_time((increase(runtime_kvcache_hits_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[30m]) / increase(runtime_kvcache_requests_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[30m])) * 100)[30m:5m]
- Recent model deployment (curl):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_API_KEY" https://internal-api.redwood.ai/deployments?tenant=$TENANT&limit=5

Sample webhook payload to create an action ticket in the Support system (JSON):
{
  "tenant_id": "t-12345",
  "alert_id": "alert-9876",
  "stability_score": 62,
  "playbook_step": "L2 triage",
  "recommended_actions": ["flush_kvcache","fallback_to_small_model"],
  "evidence": ["p95 1200ms (5m)", "kvcache hit rate 41% (30m)"]
}

Customer onboarding checklist (telemetry specific)

- Telemetry Gatekeeper configured and validated (ingress metrics, traces, logs forwarded).
- SDK installed for detailed request tagging when Gatekeeper not available.
- Baseline period collected: 72 hours of production‑like traffic for baseline modeling.
- Synthetic test suite created: 10 synthetic journeys covering critical routes (generation, embeddings, streaming).
- Cost guardrails configured: per‑tenant token cost alerting and Quota Protector webhook configured.

QBR and health report inputs

For quarterly business reviews (QBR) produce the following tenant deliverables:
- 1‑page health snapshot: Stability Score trend, p95 latency trend, error rate, top 3 regressions and actions.
- Cost delta analysis: token_cost_per_1k and top heavy prompts/calls.
- Synthetic report: pass/fail for the canonical 10 journeys and median latency for each.
- Action log: all automated remediations and manual interventions since last QBR.

Maintenance and ownership

- Telemetry synthesis service (team: Observability Platform) owns the pipeline and model weights for stability score.
- Support Playbook owner: Customer Success Operations (Maya Chen).
- Scheduled runbook review: once per quarter or after major infra changes; owners must sign off on tuning parameters.

Onboarding ramp guidelines (recommended cadence)

Week 0: Gatekeeper/Synthetic setup and baseline data collection.
Week 1: Monitor Stability Score hourly; run daily health sweep with L1.
Week 2: Tune kvcache config and batching settings with Solutions Eng.
Week 3–4: Move to automated guardrails for cost and token spikes; transition monitoring to standard QBR cadence.

Appendix: common root causes and fast checks

- Root cause: Model rollback/upgrade -> Check deployment history, model perf delta, and revert if regression confirmed.
- Root cause: Ingress gateway misrouting -> Verify route table, certificates, and ingress error logs.
- Root cause: Customer traffic pattern shift (batching/parallelization) -> Review request histogram and kvcache utilization.

Useful links and references

- Telemetry Gatekeeper onboarding guide: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/telemetry-gatekeeper-onboarding-and-qbr-integration-guide-2026
- Support CLI reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/support-cli-reference
- Platform SRE handoff template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/sre-handoff-template

Change log

- 2027-02-15: Initial published version (Maya Chen).
- 2027-03-10: Added automated remediation safeguards and CLI examples (reviewers: Jose Alvarez, Priya Narang).

payload.page_title: Scheduled Model Upgrade: Tenant Notification, Canary Rollout, and Rollback Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the cross-functional process for scheduled model upgrades that affect enterprise tenants (hosted, dedicated, and private). It covers pre-upgrade validation, tenant communications, canary rollout strategy, automated and manual rollback criteria, post-upgrade verification, and escalation paths. The goal is to ensure predictable, low-risk upgrades with clear customer-facing communication and rapid mitigation if quality or reliability regressions are detected.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to any non-trivial model version change (weights or tokenizer changes, quantization/format changes, runtime ABI changes) scheduled during standard maintenance windows.
- Includes Hosted API customers, Redwood Dedicated tenants, and Private deployments where Redwood coordinates or provides upgrade artifacts.
- Excludes entirely internal-only test model swaps performed in isolated staging environments.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Product Release Lead: triage owner for upgrade schedule and customer notices. (Owner: Product Release Manager)
- Customer Success Lead: primary point of contact for affected enterprise customers and for communicating impacts. (Owner: Customer Success Manager)
- Runtime/Serving Owner: executes canary rollout and rollback, validates metrics, and performs emergency rollback when required. (Owner: Serving Runtime SRE)
- Observability Owner: ensures dashboards, alerts, and synthetic tests are active and tuned for the upgrade. (Owner: Observability Engineer)
- Security/Compliance Owner: confirms approval for upgrades that touch sensitive data or private tenants. (Owner: Security PM)
sections.heading: Owners & Roles

sections.body:
1) Release artifacts prepared and smoke-tested in staging: model binaries, container images, migration scripts.
2) Canary config baked: percentage targets, tenant selectors, fallback model mapping, and time-limited canary windows.
3) Automated sanity suite green on staging: tokenization, generation smoke prompts, and embedding regression checks.
4) SLO baseline capture: last 14 days of latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost per request, and model quality evals on canonical prompt set.
5) Observability readiness: dashboards, anomaly detectors, and SLO alert thresholds verified.
6) Communication artifacts ready: customer email template, incident-communication template, and support-runbook snippets.
7) Rollback playbooks validated in a dry-run: scripted rollback and clear state reconciliation steps.
8) Approval gate signoffs: Product, CS, Serving Runtime, and Security as required.
sections.heading: Pre-Upgrade Checklist (minimum gating criteria)

sections.body:
- Maintenance window: prefer low-traffic windows in tenant region (e.g., 0100–0400 local). For multi-region tenants, coordinate a single targeted rollout with time-zone-aware notices.
- Notification cadence (enterprise tenants):
  * 14 days before: high-level notice with expected impact, upgrade window, and opt-out instructions (if available).
  * 3 days before: detailed technical notice including canary percentage, API version pin instructions, and rollback SLAs.
  * 24 hours before: reminder and pre-upgrade checklist for tenant (recommended testing plan).
  * 1 hour before: imminent reminder via Slack/email to named contacts.
- Communication templates: include standard subject lines, summary sections, and a clear “what to do if you see issues” section. See template snippets below.
sections.heading: Scheduling & Tenant Notification

sections.body:
1) Stage 0 — Internal smoke (0% tenant traffic): run all internal synthetic scenarios and trace logs for 60–120 minutes.
2) Stage 1 — Very small external canary (1–2% of traffic or single volunteer tenant): monitor for 30–60 minutes.
3) Stage 2 — Expanded canary (5–10% of traffic or a small cohort of non-critical tenants): monitor for 60–120 minutes.
4) Stage 3 — Progressive ramp (25% then 50%): if metrics stable, increase to these bands with 2× monitoring intervals.
5) Stage 4 — Full rollout (100%): gated final decision after passing Stage 3 checks.

For Dedicated/Private customers where per-tenant pinning is supported: use tenant selector labels to apply the model only to specified tenants; prefer volunteer tenants for initial stages. If tenant declines participation, do not include them in the canary.

Automated Metrics & Acceptance Criteria (must be continuously evaluated during canary):
- Latency: p50 and p95 should not regress by more than +20% (absolute threshold: p95 <= 800ms for text-generation default profile).
- Error rate: total 5xx and request-failures must remain <= existing baseline + 0.1 percentage points and absolute <= 0.5%.
- Token cost: average tokens-per-request should not increase more than +10% without documented cause.
- Quality regression: automated eval on canonical prompt set must show no >3% drop in primary metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity or custom eval).
- Fuzzy anomaly detection: anomaly score on model outputs (semantic drift detector) must remain below configured threshold for the canary cohort.

If any single critical threshold is violated, the system will:
- Immediately pause canary ramping.
- Notify the on-call Serving Runtime engineer and Customer Success Lead.
- Trigger a fast rollback if the issue materially impacts customer SLAs (see Rollback Criteria).
sections.heading: Canary Rollout Strategy (recommended default)

sections.body:
- Severity 1 (service-impacting, persistent): automatic rollback within 15 minutes. Examples: sustained p95 > 1200ms, error rate > 1.5% sustained over 5 minutes, or loss of model responses for a tenant.
- Severity 2 (quality-impacting but non-blocking): pause and evaluate; manual rollback within 60 minutes if no mitigation. Examples: quality metric drop > 6% on canonical eval or customer-reported misbehavior on production prompts.
- Severity 3 (transient anomalies): continue monitoring; remediation via config patch or retry logic. Examples: short-lived spike in latencies or intermittent downstream infra error.
sections.heading: Decision matrix (examples)

sections.body:
1) Re-route affected traffic back to prior pinned model version using the canary control plane API. Example CLI: redwoodctl rollout --tenant <tenant-id> --from-version <new> --to-version <previous> --reason "automatic-rollback: latency regressed"
2) Validate traffic routing and confirm that pre-upgrade model is serving for the affected tenant(s).
3) Re-run smoke generation tests against the restored model and confirm baseline metrics.
4) Notify Customer Success and the customer POC immediately with the rollback summary and next steps.
5) Open a post-incident triage ticket and schedule a cross-team RCA within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Rollback steps (serving runtime owner executes)

sections.body:
- 24-hour and 7-day checks: confirm sustained SLO adherence and no regression in quality metrics.
- Customer validation: deliver a short validation checklist to the customer POC to confirm expected behavior.
- Billing/Cost reconciliation: capture token-cost delta and alert finance if variance > 8% month-to-date.
sections.heading: Post-Upgrade Verification (after full rollout)

sections.body:
- Dashboards to monitor: Model Serving Overview, Canary Cohort Health, Latency Heatmap (by tenant), Error Distribution, Model Quality Snapshot.
- Quick checks (CLI / API):
  * Get canary assignment: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/model-assignment
  * Fetch model metrics: redwood-metrics query "model.latency.p95{model=\"<model-name>\"}" --last 15m
  * Trigger synthetic test: curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.ai/synthetics/run -d '{"test_suite":"upgrade-smoke","model":"<model-name>"}'
sections.heading: Observability Playbook (quick commands and dashboards)

sections.body:
- Subject: "Planned model upgrade for <Tenant Name> — maintenance window <date/time>"
- Body: include short summary, expected impact (likely none), canary approach, opt-out link (if applicable), contact info, and guidance for quick verification.
- Incident messaging (if rollback occurs): short description of customer exposure, actions taken (rollback executed), expected follow-up timeline, and link to RCA.

Support Triage Flow (if customers report issues during or after upgrade):
1) First-line support: run the tenant validation checklist and capture examples (request_id, timestamps, prompt text, returned output).
2) If reproducible, escalate to Serving Runtime on-call with logs, metrics, and customer-observed sample.
3) If issue is quality-related, hand off to Applied ML & Evals team for evaluation against canonical prompt sets.
4) Engage Product & CS to determine whether to pause rollout for additional testing or to rollback.
sections.heading: Customer-Facing Messaging (templates)

sections.body:
- Example canary API payload: {\"canary_percent\":5,\"cohort_selector\":\"label:volunteer\",\"max_duration_min\":120}
- Example rollback CLI snippet: redwoodctl rollback --scope tenant --id <tenant-id> --target-version <sha-or-tag> --reason "fast-rollback: automatic-threshold"
sections.heading: Runbook Attachments (snippets)

sections.body:
- For any automatic rollback or Severity 1 outage: publish a written RCA within 72 hours, with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and responsible owners for fixes.
- For Severity 2 escalations: summary RCA within 7 days and a follow-up plan for model tuning or augmenting synthetic tests.
sections.heading: Postmortem & RCA expectations

sections.body:
- Pre-upgrade: confirm POC has a test plan and knows how to pin model versions if they want a freeze.
- During canary: maintain an open channel with the customer POC and provide live updates at milestone gates.
- After rollback: coordinate follow-up postmortem call and share remediation timelines.

Appendix: Example Email Template (short)
Subject: Planned model upgrade for <TenantName> — <Date/Window>
Hi <POC>,
We will be performing a scheduled model upgrade that may affect inference quality for a small subset of requests. We are using a conservative canary rollout and expect no disruption for most customers. If you prefer to be excluded from the canary, reply to this message before <X>.
Planned window: <Date/Time>
What we will do: staged canary, monitoring, and rapid rollback if thresholds are violated.
How you can test: run the quick verification checklist attached.
Who to contact: <CS POC contact> (phone/slack)
Thanks,
Customer Success (Redwood)

Appendix: Quick Verification Checklist for Tenants
- Run 5 representative prompts and compare responses to baseline.
- Verify latency for 10 requests does not exceed usual p95 by >40%.
- Report any unexpected formatting, hallucination, or API errors with timestamps and request IDs.
sections.heading: Customer Success Playbook Actions (for CSMs)

sections.body:
- 2025-11-03: Initial draft (Ravi Patel).
- 2025-12-10: Added canary percentage guidance and automated metrics (Maya Chen).
- 2026-02-14: Clarified rollback thresholds and added observability CLI snippets (Sofia Alvarez).

sections.body:

- Runtime rollback API reference: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/rollback-api-reference
- Canary cohort selection guide: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/canary-selection-guidelines

payload.page_title: Enterprise Metric Ownership and Alert Routing Cookbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This cookbook defines a pragmatic, repeatable approach for mapping customer-visible telemetry to clear owners, creating routing rules in our alerting stack, and operationalizing those alerts inside Customer Success (CS) and Engineering workflows. It is intended for CS onboarding leads, SREs, and product owners who need consistent, auditable alerts that drive fast, customer-facing outcomes.

Scope: applies to all enterprise tenants (hosted, dedicated, private) and the following telemetry sources: telemetry-gateway, redwood-proxy, model-router, kvcache-service, embeddings-indexer. This doc focuses on customer-impacting metrics (latency, error-rate, cost-anomaly, model-quality regression) rather than internal infra-only metrics.

Owner and Contact

- Primary owner: Customer Success Observability (team-ops-cs-observability)
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE (team-sre-platform)
- Oncall escalation: Eng SRE PagerDuty (PD: team-sre-platform)

Definitions and Goal Metrics

- Customer-visible metric: any metric or log pattern that maps to a customer SLA, feature, or billing impact (examples below).
- Severity tiers and target time-to-ack (TTA):
  - Sev P0 (Critical): customer-facing outage, >5% of tenant traffic impacted or entire tenant unreachable — TTA: 15 minutes
  - Sev P1 (High): degraded experience (latency or increased error rate) for a production route — TTA: 60 minutes
  - Sev P2 (Medium): cost anomaly or single-model quality regression flagged by evaluations — TTA: 8 hours
  - Sev P3 (Low): informational alerts, trend warnings for QBR — TTA: 72 hours

Metric-to-Owner Matrix (examples)

| Metric name | Observable source | Owner team | Default severity | Notes |
|-------------|-------------------|------------|------------------|-------|
| request.p50.latency| telemetry-gateway | team-sre-platform | P1 | If tenant p50 increases > 2x baseline for >10m |
| request.error_rate | redwood-proxy | team-sre-platform | P0 | If error_rate > 5% for a tenant and sustained |
| embed.indexing.lag | embeddings-indexer | team-data-ops | P1 | Backpressure on indexer affecting search freshness |
| kvcache.kv_miss_rate | kvcache-service | team-serving-runtime | P1 | Rapid rise correlates with token spend increase |
| model.quality.regression.alpha | model-router/evals | team-applied-ml | P2 | Triggered by evaluation harness comparing model vN to baseline |
| tenant.cost.per_hour | billing-collector | customer-success | P2 | Sudden cost > 3x expected forecast |

Alert Routing and Naming Conventions

- Alert name format: cs.<tenant>.<service>.<metric>.<severity>. Example: cs.acme-corp.redis-proxy.request-error-rate.P0
- Tags/labels to include: tenant_id, customer_tier (enterprise/dedicated/private), region, route, last_deployed_model, runbook_id
- Recommended Slack channels: #cs-alerts (triage), #sre-ops (escalation), #cust-<tenant_short> (customer-specific comms if enabled)

Routing Rules (examples)

1) Immediate P0 routing
   - Condition: alert severity == P0 AND tenant.tier == enterprise
   - Action: page Eng SRE PD (team-sre-platform) AND notify #cs-alerts Slack channel. Create CS incident in Zendesk with priority urgent.
2) P1 automated triage
   - Condition: severity == P1 AND first_alert_count >= 3 in 30m
   - Action: create short-lived support ticket assigned to CS Observability, attach grafana dashboard and recent traces. If no ack in 60m, escalate to Eng SRE PD.
3) Cost/Quality P2 handling
   - Condition: metric in {tenant.cost.per_hour, model.quality.regression.alpha}
   - Action: assign to CS FinOps or Applied ML respectively; auto-generate customer notification draft for review.

Alert Payload Example (YAML for routing system)

---
alert_name: "cs.{{tenant}}.telemetry-gateway.p50.latency.P1"
tenant: "{{tenant}}"
threshold: "p50 > baseline*2 for >10m"
owner: "team-sre-platform"
pagerduty: "team-sre-platform"
slack_channels: ["#cs-alerts", "#sre-ops"]
runbook_id: "rr-metric-p50-latency-v1"

Runbook: p50 latency spike (rr-metric-p50-latency-v1)

1) Verify the scope
   - Query: Grafana dashboard: Dashboard ID: cs-onboarding/latency-summary. Apply tenant filter = <tenant_id> and route filter = <route>.
   - Confirm whether spike is single region or cross-region and whether multiple tenants are affected.
2) Quick mitigations (first 30 min)
   - If proxy CPU > 85%: scale proxy pool (kubectl scale deploy proxy --replicas=+2 for dedicated pools).
   - If model hot-sharding: switch route to fallback model variant (use model-router override API: POST /v1/admin/overrides).
   - If KV cache miss storm: temporarily enable cache-skim mode (feature flag: kvcache.skim=true) for tenant.
3) Deeper triage (30m–4h)
   - Collect flamegraphs (perf profiler), recent traces (x-trace-id), and last 6 hours of redeploy events.
   - Correlate with release tags: last_deployed_model and infra-deploy-id.
4) Communication
   - Customer comms template (initial):
     Subject: "[Redwood] Brief outage affecting <feature> for <tenant>"
     Body: "We are investigating elevated latency impacting <route>. Initial mitigation steps are in progress. We will update within 60 minutes with next steps. Owner: <owner_name> (CS). Escalation: Eng SRE oncall."

Onboarding Checklist for New Enterprise Tenants (observability handoff)

- Before prod cutover:
  1. Ensure tenant metadata is registered in the telemetry-gateway (tenant_id, billing_code, support_contacts).
  2. Validate tenant-specific dashboards exist (latency, error-rate, cost, model-quality) and are shared with CS and SRE.
  3. Add tenant to alert routing rules with correct owner and Slack channels.
  4. Confirm PagerDuty escalation path is present and tested (test page with PD test key).
  5. Run a synthetic journey (see synthetic-journey-sla-calibration-playbook) and confirm alerts are not noisy.

Operational Playflows

- Normal triage (P1/P2): CS Observability owns first-touch. Use the CS triage checklist inside the Zendesk ticket: attach dashboards, record mitigation actions, propose next steps (mitigate, rollback, model-swap, capacity increase).
- Immediate escalation (P0): Eng SRE paged immediately. CS takes ownership of customer communication cadence and QBR action items.
- Post-incident: create an RCA within 48 hours if incident severity >= P1 and affected revenue or >10 customers. Assign action owners with due dates and track in the QBR.

Noise Reduction and Alert Health

- Weekly review: CS Observability runs an alert hygiene sweep every Monday: remove stale alerts, update thresholds based on tenant baselines, and collapse duplicate alerts across services.
- Signal-to-noise metric: track alerts_per_week_per_tenant and target < 3 actionable alerts/week for enterprise. If exceeded, assign an action to reduce.

Integration snippets and examples

1) Grafana dashboard sharing (CLI snippet)
   - grafana-cli dashboard export 12345 > acme-latency-dash.json
   - grafana-cli dashboard import --folder "Tenants/Acme" acme-latency-dash.json
2) Routing rule (example JSON for alert manager):
   {
     "match": {"tenant":"acme-corp","severity":"P1"},
     "route_to": ["team-sre-platform","channel:#cs-alerts"],
     "suppress_if": {"maintenance_mode":true}
   }

Customer Communication Templates

- 60-minute update (short)
  - Subject: "Update: ongoing issue affecting <feature> — <tenant>"
  - Body: "Summary: elevated latency persisted affecting <route>. Mitigation: scaled proxy and switched to fallback model. Next update in 2 hours or sooner. Contact: <cs_owner>@redwood.ai"

- Post-incident summary (example)
  - Subject: "Incident report: <short-id> — impact summary and remediation"
  - Body: "What happened, Customer impact, Timeline of mitigations, Root cause (investigating/identified), Actions taken, Preventative actions and expected timeline for completion."

SLO and Escalation thresholds (customer-facing)

- Availability: 99.95% per month for hosted Tier 1 routes. Escalate to P0 when availability drops below 99.5% in a rolling 1h window.
- Latency: p95 < 450ms. Escalate to P1 when p95 > 900ms for >10 minutes.
- Error rate: <1% across tenant traffic. Escalate to P0 when error rate >5% for >5 minutes.

Governance, Reporting, and QBR Inputs

- Each month CS Observability exports the following artifacts for QBRs: top 3 incidents for the tenant, alert burn rate, cost anomalies detected, model quality deltas.
- Action ownership: every alert that results in an RCA must have an owner and a completion date recorded in the quarter backlog.

Appendices

A. Common mitigations quick list
- Scale dedicated pools, swap to model-variant, enable cache-skim, temporary rate-limiting per-tenant, rollback last infra deploy.

B. Useful links
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cs-onboarding/latency-summary
- PagerDuty: https://pd.redwood.internal/services/team-sre-platform
- Runbook repo: docs/runbooks/rr-metric-p50-latency-v1

C. Change log
- 2025-09-12: Document created by Maya Chen (CS Observability).
- 2026-02-10: Updated severity TTA targets and added cost anomaly routing (reviewers: Julian Park, Lena Novak).

If you have questions or need a tenant added to routing rules, open a ticket to #cs-ops-requests with payload: tenant_id, owner_email, desired_channels.
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Tenant Stability Predictive Signals Runbook

sections.body:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This runbook defines the predictive signals, automated enrichment, and operational play for preventing tenant instability during the first 90 days after provisioning and at scale. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SREs, Platform Engineers, and on-call Support. The playbook covers detection thresholds, triage steps, automated mitigations, customer communications, and post-incident follow-up templates.

Why this exists
-----------------
- Many early-stage incidents for enterprise tenants are preceded by measurable leading indicators (cache miss spikes, request token variance, route fan-out changes, model mismatch regressions).
- Acting on signals reduces severity, shortens time to mitigation, and reduces churn risk.
- Provides clear ownership and automation recipes to reduce manual toil.

Key definitions and roles
------------------------
- Tenant: A single enterprise customer tenant (dedicated or hosted).
- Predictive signal: A metric or composite metric that historically correlates with a stability degradation within 1–72 hours.
- Owner roles:
  - CSE (Customer Success Engineer): Primary customer-facing technical owner during onboarding and early life.
  - SRE: Operational owner responsible for infra/slo remediation and incident escalation.
  - Platform Eng: Owner for deployment/rollback actions and model routing policies.
  - Escalation Lead: Designated cross-functional lead for Sev2+ events.

SLOs referenced
---------------
- Tenant 99p tail latency (in-region): 500 ms target, 750 ms warning, 1200 ms Sev2 threshold
- 95p success rate (per-tenant, per-hour): 99.5% target, 99.0% warning, 97.0% Sev2 threshold
- KV cache hit rate (per-tenant, rolling 10m): 85% target, 70% warning, 50% Sev2 threshold

Priority predictive signals (ranked)
----------------------------------
1) KV cache miss rate sudden increase (delta > 20 pp within 10 minutes)
   - Why: Causes token re-computation and tail latency spikes.
   - Detection: rolling10m_kv_cache_miss_rate{tenant_id="$TENANT"} - alert if > 0.20 AND increase > 0.20 vs prev10m
   - PromQL example: (increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])) > 0.2
2) Token-per-request (TPR) variance spike (p99 TPR > baseline * 1.6)
   - Why: Unexpected prompt/agent behavior or malformed client input causes cost and latency escalation.
   - Detection: compare p99(TPR, 30m) vs tenant baseline over 7d.
3) Model-variant mismatch errors (client requested variant not available + auto-fallback rate > 5%)
   - Why: Rollouts or capacity limits can trigger silent fallbacks and degrade quality.
4) Request fan-out increase (downstream retries causing multiple backend requests)
   - Why: Retries/backpressure loops amplify load; common during intermittent network issues.
5) 99p latency climb above warning threshold while success rate holds steady
   - Why: Often first sign of degraded hardware or contention (GPU saturation, NVMe throttling).

Alerting taxonomy and severity mapping
------------------------------------
- Predictive Warning: Single-signal threshold crossed (pager suppressed, Slack #cs-early-warning posted, ticket created).
- Predictive Sev3: Two related signals active for > 15m; page CSE and SRE (Slack @oncall and create incident record).
- Predictive Sev2: Any Sev2 SLO breached OR composite signal score > 0.8 for 30m. Pager escalation: SRE, Platform Eng, Escalation Lead.

Automated enrichment and alert payload content
--------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- tenant_id, tenant_name, customer_tier (dedicated/hosted/private), region, active_model, model_variant, recent_deployments (IDs), recent_rollout_percentages, last_2h_kv_cache_rates, last_2h_tpr_p95_p99, last_5m_error_types, related_traces (URLs), recent_autoscale_events, current_capacity_pool_id
- Attach: 1) top 10 slow traces (sampled), 2) snapshot of the last successful and failed request payloads (redact PII), 3) CSV of per-route qps last 60m.

Initial automated remediation recipes (safe by default)
----------------------------------------------------
These automation recipes are executed by the Platform Eng runbook bot (redwood-ops). All actions are reversible.
1) Read-only route throttle (rate-limit non-critical routes)
   - Command: redwood-ops route throttle --tenant $TENANT --route-pattern "/api/v1/agents/*" --qps 10 --reason "auto-kvcache-miss-mitigation"
2) Increase KV cache warming priority for tenant (pin prefixes to warm pool)
   - Command: redwood-ops cache prioritize --tenant $TENANT --prefix-list-file recent-prefixes.csv
3) Temporary model routing to stable variant (no config changes to customer code)
   - Command: redwood-ops reroute --tenant $TENANT --from-variant v2 --to-variant v1 --duration 30m --annot "predictive-signal-failback"
4) Allocate burst capacity from dedicated reserve (if tenant is on Dedicated plan)
   - Command: redwood-ops capacity allocate --pool reserve-dedicated --tenant $TENANT --minutes 60

Triage play (ordered steps)
---------------------------
1) Receive alert and review automated enrichment (within 5m).
   - Who: CSE + oncall SRE (piggyback on Slack alert).
2) Validate signal: check KV cache hit/miss graphs, top traces, and recent deploy IDs.
   - Who: SRE.
3) If KV cache miss delta is confirmed, trigger cache prioritize recipe (automated or manual).
   - Who: Platform Eng or redwood-ops bot.
4) If TPR spike present, open Customer Insights ticket and ask CSM to validate recent prompt changes or agents.
   - Who: CSE + CSM.
5) If model-variant fallback is >5% or quality regression signalled, initiate controlled rollback to last known-good model variant and notify customer (see Customer Communication templates).
   - Who: Platform Eng + CSE.
6) If latency continues to degrade or success rate drops below 97%, escalate to Sev2 and follow incident process (page Execs per escalation matrix).

Customer communications (templates)
--------------------------------
Use these templates to reduce confusion and set expectations. Customize cadence depending on severity.
- Early-warning (Predictive Warning, not service impacting):
  Subject: Redwood – Early Notice: Observed increased request variance for your tenant
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, our monitoring has detected an increase in request complexity for tenant <tenant_name> that may cause degraded latency. We are applying targeted, reversible mitigations (cache warming and route throttles) and will update in 30 minutes. No action is required from your side unless you observed recent agent/prompt changes.
- Action required (Sev3):
  Subject: Redwood – Attention: Elevated errors affecting some requests
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are investigating elevated errors and have initiated mitigations. Please confirm whether you have recently modified prompts, added agents, or changed request fan-out. We will provide a status update within 20 minutes.
- Outage/Sev2:
  Subject: Redwood – Incident: Impacting availability for <tenant_name>
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are actively responding to an incident impacting request success for your tenant. Our teams (SRE, Platform, CSE) are engaged. We will provide ETA for restoration and next steps within 15 minutes. We will also give a post-incident summary after remediation.

Escalation matrix and contact list
----------------------------------
- Sev3: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng (pager)
- Sev2: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng -> Escalation Lead -> Head of Customer Success (page all)
- Pager channels: Ops PagerDuty, #cs-early-warning, #prod-incidents
- Contact list (on-call rota referenced from roster page):
  - CSE: oncall-cse@redwood.ai
  - SRE oncall: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
  - Platform Eng: platform-oncall@redwood.ai

Post-incident follow-up checklist
--------------------------------
- Short-term (within 24h):
  1) Confirm root cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline.
  2) Share initial incident summary with customer and internal stakeholders.
  3) Create postmortem ticket and assign owners.
- Long-term (within 14 days):
  1) Implement durable fixes (hotfix or config change).
  2) Add predictive signal tuning (threshold/weight) to the sentinel rules if noisy or missed.
  3) Schedule QBR discussion if customer impact > 2 days or repeat issues occurred within 90 days.

Runbook maintenance and signal governance
----------------------------------------
- Quarterly signal review: CS + SRE + Platform will review predictive signal performance (precision, recall, false positives).
- Owners must adjust thresholds and enrichment payload fields if root cause patterns change.
- New signals should be documented with: name, owner, detection query, historical precision/recall, and a test harness for simulation.

Telemetry and dashboards (reference)
-----------------------------------
- Dashboards: Tenant Stability Overview (per-tenant filter), KV Cache Heatmap, Model Variant Rollout Monitor, Route Fanout Explorer.
- Key Grafana panels and queries required for triage are linked from the alert (always include dashboard URL in the alert).
- Required metrics: kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_requests_total, request_tokens_per_request, request_latency_p50_p95_p99, request_success_count, model_variant_fallback_count, autoscale_events_total

Playbook automation safety and governance
----------------------------------------
- Auto-mitigations are enabled for enterprise tenants after a 7-day probation window and only if the customer has opted into "proactive mitigations" during onboarding.
- All automated actions are logged and must include: actor, reason, diff of the config change, and rollback command.
- For restricted tenants (high-security), auto actions are dry-run only and require manual approval by the customer contact.

Appendix A — PromQL examples and helper queries
------------------------------------------------
- KV cache miss rate (10m):
  increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])
- p99 tokens per request (30m):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(tokens_per_request_bucket{tenant="$TENANT"}[30m])) by (le))
- Composite predictive score (example heuristic):
  0.5 * normalized_kv_miss_delta + 0.3 * normalized_tpr_p99_delta + 0.2 * model_fallback_rate

Appendix B — Example incident Slack message (copy template)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Channel: #cs-early-warning
- Message: @oncall SRE, predictive-warning for tenant *$TENANT* (KV miss + TPR spike). Enrichment: <link to alert>. Action: running cache-prioritize; if latency 99p > 900ms in 15m escalate to Sev2.

Appendix C — Post-incident report template (fill-in)
---------------------------------------------------
- Incident ID:
- Tenant:
- Timeline: detection -> mitigation -> resolved (timestamps)
- Root cause:
- Mitigation steps taken: automated and manual
- Customer impact: number of failed requests, duration, affected routes
- Action items (owner + due date)

Contacts and escalation URLs
--------------------------
- Redwoods Ops Console (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/ops
- Incident ticketing (internal): https://issues.redwood.ai/browse/OPS
- On-call roster: https://people.redwood.ai/oncall-roster

Notes and versioning
--------------------
- Owner: Customer Success Engineering (Aisha Patel)
- Document version: 1.2
- Next review date: 2026-04-01

End of document

h1. Purpose
This page defines the minimum customer-facing communication requirements for production model version rollouts. Rollout plans MUST include a Customer communications section that follows these rules.

h1. Who must be notified

h2. Always notify
* Any Dedicated customer receiving the new version as default
* Any Private customer (VPC/on-prem) impacted by the change

h2. Notify when material behavior changes
For Hosted API customers, notify when any of the following change materially for a commonly used alias:
* output format or tool-calling behavior
* maximum context/output token limits
* latency or reliability expectations
* safety behaviors (refusals, content filtering)

h1. Timing
* Dedicated: at least 5 business days before the change window, unless the customer agrees otherwise.

h1. Required message content
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
* What is changing (model alias and new version id if customer pins versions)

* When (date/time + timezone + duration)
* Impact assessment (best-case and worst-case)
* How to opt out or pin a version
* How to get help (support channel and escalation path)
* Rollback posture (we can roll back during window if thresholds violated)

h1. Channels
* Dedicated/Private: email to customer technical contacts + a support ticket for tracking
* Hosted: release notes; optionally email to top impacted orgs
* If the change triggers an incident or wide impact, use the status page rules

h1. Approvals

If you need to remain on the previous model version, we can pin your deployment to <old version> for at least 30 days. Reply to this email or comment on the support ticket to request pinning.
