payload.page_title: First-Line LLM Quality Triage & Eval Handoff Playbook

sections.body: Overview
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This playbook describes the first-line process for handling customer-reported LLM quality issues during enterprise onboarding and the formal handoff to Applied ML / eng teams for evaluation and remediation. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Support Tier 1/2, Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Applied ML reviewers.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Quickly triage user-facing quality regressions and determine severity.
- Capture reproducible test cases and metadata needed for deterministic evals.
- Execute lightweight mitigations (prompt guardrails, model switchover, reranking) when safe.
- Perform a clean handoff to Applied ML or Eng with a complete evaluation package.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers during the first 90 days of onboarding and to production incidents that are suspected regressions in model output quality.
- Not intended for purely infrastructure outages (see incident playbooks).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Customer Success (owner): overall coordination, communication with customer.
- Support Tier 1: initial intake, basic repro steps, short-term mitigations.
- Support Tier 2 / CSE: advanced triage, telemetry capture, auth to access customer logs.
- Solutions Eng: assist with integration-level fixes (payload / tokenization).
- Applied ML: run evaluations, propose model/strategy changes, approve rollouts.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: engineering fixes for runtime-related degradation (KV cache, batching issues).
sections.heading: Owner and Roles

sections.body:
- Slack channel: #cs-quality-triage (pager: @cs-oncall)
- Pager (for sev-2+ regressions): CS Ops Escalation Pager (see oncall rota)
- Email: cs-incident@redwood.ai (for formal handoffs)

Severity Matrix (Guidance)
- Sev 1 (Critical): Customer-facing data corruption, hallucinations causing safety/regulatory violations, or blocking revenue-generating flows. Response target: 1 hour.
- Sev 2 (High): Severe quality regression affecting major workflows but with an acceptable workaround. Response target: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized quality issues or intermittent regressions. Response target: 24 hours.
- Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic or non-urgent degradations. Response target: 3 business days.

Immediate Intake Checklist (Support Tier 1)
1. Record incident metadata in ticket system (CS-Ticket-Template): customer ID, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), model name + pinned version, route name, time window, example prompt(s), example outputs, user-visible impact, and severity estimate.
2. Confirm customer can reproduce and capture a minimal reproducible test case (MRT): short prompt, model config (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), and exact API request payload if possible.
3. Capture opaque IDs: request_id, trace_id, tenant_id, and model_instance_id (if present).
4. Check common quick mitigations: revert to previously pinned model variant, lower temperature to 0.2, enable deterministic sampling, or temporarily route to fallback model. Document actions.

Telemetry & Artifacts to Collect (Tier 2 / CSE)
- Request logs: full request/response bodies (redact PII per data-retention policy).
- Token-level latency histogram for the requests in question.
- Trace (X-Trace-ID) and corresponding route logs in the console.
- Model serving metrics: batch size, KV cache hit rate, gpu_util (%), model_load_error_count.
- Prompt/response diffs: before/after changes to prompts or system messages.
- Evaluation harness snapshot: failing test cases saved as a JSONL file with fields: "input","expected","actual","model","seed","config". Example:
sections.heading: Contact Channels

sections.body:
{"input":"Summarize the following policy: ...","expected":"Key points: A, B, C","actual":"Irrelevant personal opinion","model":"gpt-open-64b-v2","seed":1234,"config":"{\"temperature\":0.7,\"max_tokens\":256}"}

Lightweight Repro Steps (run locally / from console)
- Recommended curl example for reproducibility (hosted API):

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{REDACTED}}" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-64b-v2","input":"<INSERT_PROMPT>","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":200}'

- For streaming routes, include stream flag to capture chunk ordering.
- For embeddings regressions use /v1/embeddings and include the index id and vector fingerprint.

Quick Mitigations (to attempt before escalation)
- Prompt-level: tighten system messages, add positive/negative examples, or add explicit instructions to avoid forbidden content.
- Model switch: move to a verified-stable variant (documented in the model catalog) and monitor.
- Config change: reduce temperature, set top_p to 0.0, set max_tokens to stricter limit.
- Rate-limit adjustment: check for token-throttling-induced truncation.

When to Escalate to Applied ML / Eng
sections.heading: Example eval snapshot (JSONL line)

sections.body:
- MRT reproduces a quality regression on the verified-stable model catalog variant.
- Problem appears after a model rollout or quantization change.
- There is evidence of runtime-level anomalies (batching misordering, cache poisoning, sequence length handling).
- Customer impact meets Sev 1/Sev 2 thresholds.

Required Handoff Payload (email and ticket body)
1. Executive summary (1-2 sentences): observed regression, impact, and customer business effect.
2. Severity and SLA target.
3. MRT JSONL file (attached) with at least 3 failing and 3 passing cases.
4. Telemetry links (console traces, request IDs, metric charts) with timestamps.
5. Exact model config used and recommended mitigation attempts and results.
6. Access notes (whether customer has consented to sharing PII and any additional privacy constraints).
7. Point of contact for customer + next check-in ETA.
sections.heading: Escalate if any of the following are true

sections.body:
[Handoff] Customer ACME Corp — Sev2 hallucination regression — model gpt-open-64b-v2 — 2026-02-15

Advanced Investigation Steps (Applied ML)
1. Re-run failing MRT against the model binaries used in production (note quantization/FP config). Record random seeds.
2. Run delta-eval: compare outputs across model variants and quantization profiles, and record semantic similarity metrics (BERTScore >= 0.92 expected for paraphrase-preservation).
3. Run targeted attribution tests if hallucination suspected (prompt perturbation and source retrieval trace).
4. If embedding degradation: compute recall@K and centroids shifts, and run index consistency checks (shard consistency, vector dimensionality).
5. If runtime suspected: validate KV cache lookup for long-context queries (KV cache hit rate should be > 98% for identical prefixes).
6. Produce remediation recommendation: prompt patch, model rollback, re-quantize, or runtime patch, plus monitoring gating criteria.

Rollout & Canary Guidance
- Any model or runtime fix must be rolled out as a canary to 1–5% of traffic for 24–72 hours with automated quality regression checks.
- Key metrics to monitor during canary: failure_rate, latency_p95, token_cost_per_request, semantic_similarity_score, customer-reported TTR.
- Automatic rollback trigger: >3x increase in failure_rate or >5 point drop in semantic_similarity_score over baseline.

Communication and Customer Updates
- For Sev1/Sev2 incidents provide hourly updates until mitigated.
- For Sev3 provide daily updates until resolved.
- Use templated status updates (see CS incident templates) and always include: what we know, what we tried, next steps, ETA.

Post-Incident Activities
- Postmortem owner: Applied ML if model-related; Eng-Serving-Runtime if runtime-related; CS owner for communications.
- Postmortem template fields: timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence, mitigation, follow-ups, and action owner + due date.
- Create evergreen test cases in the eval-harness repo and add to the customer-specific prompt set for regression monitoring.

Operational Metrics & SLOs (for monitoring quality during onboarding)
- Quality baseline: semantic_similarity_score (customer prompt set) >= 0.88 for pass.
- False hallucination rate <= 1% for critical domains (legal, finance, regulated content).
- Regression detection latency: alert < 6 hours from first customer report or automated detection.

Templates and Artifacts (links)
- CS-Ticket-Template (use when creating an intake ticket)
- Eval harness snapshot template (JSONL)
- Onboarding prompt set location: /datasets/onboarding_prompts/{customer_id} (request access via SE)
- Model catalog: /tools/model-catalog (contains verified-stable variants)

Security and Data Privacy Notes
- Always follow the Sensitive Data Handling Policy when collecting request/response bodies. Redact or pseudonymize PII before sharing with applied/engineering teams unless explicit customer consent is recorded.
- For private and on-prem customers, ensure handoff procedures respect the customer's network and data-residency constraints — attachments should be stored in the customer's secure workspace.

Training & Playbook Refresh
- CSEs and Tier 2 are expected to run through the playbook in quarterly game-days.
- This playbook is reviewed every 6 months; file change requests should be submitted to the owner (Customer Success) with supporting examples.

Appendix: Quick check commands and grep helpers
- Find recent requests containing a prompt substring (console CLI):
redwood-cli logs query --tenant acme-corp --from 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --to 2026-02-15T00:00:00Z --query "prompt:\"refund policy\""

- Extract request IDs that match a trace and dump bodies (example jq filter):
redwood-cli logs tail --trace 1234abcd | jq -r '. | select(.route=="/v1/generate") | {request_id: .id, payload: .body}'

- Basic JSONL eval harness format reminder:
input\texpected\tactual\tmodel\tseed\tconfig
Use tab-separated JSONL for import into evaluation tools.

Document History and Contacts
- Maintainer: Aisha Kumar (Customer Success) — aisha@redwood.ai
- Revision log:
  - 2025-11-02: Created initial playbook (A. Kumar)
  - 2026-01-20: Added canary guidance and severity matrix (R. Park)
  - 2026-02-15: Added embedding-specific checks and telemetry commands (Dr. E. Zhao)

End of document.

payload.page_title: Enterprise Avalanche Surge: Preparation and Stabilization Playbook

sections.body: This playbook describes the end-to-end procedures for preparing for, detecting, and stabilizing a sudden high-volume traffic event we call an "avalanche surge" for enterprise tenants (e.g., large customer marketing campaigns, viral product hooks, or third-party spikes). It covers pre-cutover preparation, detection thresholds, immediate actions (first 15–60 minutes), escalation behavior, automated mitigations, safe-failback, customer communications templates, and post-incident QBR artifacts.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Any customer-facing production spike where observed request volume, token throughput, or request concurrency increases by >= 5x baseline within a 5 minute window.
- Alerts triggered by the Avalanche Detector rule (see Telemetry) or when a customer reports widespread latency / 5xxs tied to a single tenant.
sections.heading: When to use this playbook

sections.body:
- Preserve customer-visible availability (success rate >= 99.5%) during surge where possible.
- Maintain 95th percentile token latency <= 2x baseline SLO for dedicated tenants; notify if this cannot be met.
- Ensure cost containment and fairness across multi-tenant pools (automatic throttles engaged when thresholds are hit).
- Provide clear, timely communications to stakeholders and customers within 15 minutes of detection.
sections.heading: Goals and acceptance criteria

sections.body:
- ingress-proxy (tenant routing / ingress rate shaping)
- model-router (routes to model variants: full, quantized, low-cost-fallback)
- kvcache (KV cache for prefix reuse)
- rate-limiter (per-tenant quotas and adaptive throttling)
- telemetry-gatekeeper (synthetic checks, avalanche detector)
- batch-gateway (batched inference for asynchronous workloads)
- billing-telemetry (cost-attribution and anomaly flags)

Pre-runbook: preparation checklist (owner: customer-success + eng-sre)
1) Tenant profiling: ensure each enterprise customer has a current surge profile in the tenant registry. Profile fields: typical QPS, peak QPS observed historically, critical endpoints, consumer-facing SLAs.
2) Canary thresholds: add tenant to synthetic canary with 30s and 10s latency checks; ensure synthetic runner frequency is 1m during high-risk windows.
3) Capacity reservations: for Dedicated customers verify reserved GPU capacity is provisioned and autoscale policy is set (min, target, max).
4) Communication plan: assign primary CSM, escalation engineer (oncall SRE), and product contact. Document these contacts on the tenant row in the Customer Ops spreadsheet.
5) Automated fallback policy: ensure the tenant has an allowed fallback model-variant list and an explicit fallback policy (e.g., prefer quantized-7b then low-cost-llama if full model unavailable).
6) Cost protections: optional quota-protector enabled for tenant with threshold 2x baseline QPS by default.

Telemetry and detection (owner: eng-sre / telemetry):
- Avalanche Detector rule:
  - Trigger when tenant QPS >= 5x baseline over 5 consecutive minutes OR 95th-token-latency >= 3x baseline for 6+ minutes.
  - Secondary triggers: sudden KV cache miss ratio > 50%, rate-limiter saturation, or sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 10 minutes.
- Dashboards to monitor: Tenant Surge Overview, Pool Utilization, Model Router Latency by variant, Rate-limiter saturation heatmap, KVC cache hit/miss.
- Automatic Pager: if Avalanche Detector triggers, send page to SRE oncall with priority P1 and notify CSM and account owner via email/SMS bridge.

Immediate response (first 0–15 minutes):
1) Triage owner acknowledges alert within 2 minutes.
2) Run a quick impact sweep: check error rates, 95th latency, queue depth on ingress-proxy, and which model-variant is receiving traffic.
3) Communication out: send initial customer-facing note (template below) within 15 minutes.
4) If available capacity exists in dedicated pool: issue temporary horizontal scale:
   - CLI: rcap scale --tenant <TENANT_ID> --pool dedicated --delta +2 --reason "avalanche temporary"
5) If autoscale cannot provision fast enough, initiate controlled throttling:
   - Increase per-tenant rate-limiter token cost for non-critical routes by 50% (see routing rule list).
   - Enable adaptive batching for synchronous endpoints where latency impact is acceptable.
6) Activate model-router fallback: shift a percentage of traffic to lower-cost quantized variants. Example policy: 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 10-minute windows if success rate stabilizes.

Stabilization checklist (minutes 15–60):
- Observe error rate and latency trends every 60s.
- If 5xxs remain high after fallback and throttles, escalate to multi-tier mitigations:
  - Enable per-endpoint backpressure headers to clients (Retry-After).
  - Move non-critical tenants on same pool to spillover routing.
  - Offload heavy batch workloads to batch-gateway with relaxed latency SLA.
- If costs are rising quickly, flip on the quota-protector to enforce hard cap; notify customer immediately.
sections.heading: Key services and components referenced

sections.body:
- CSM: primary customer comms, coordinates commercial/cost decisions.
- SRE oncall: technical triage and execution of scaling/route changes.
- Serving runtime lead (if >30 minutes): coordinates kernel/quantization swap or emergency model-reload.
- Product PM (optional): decides on temporary feature gating if surge is caused by a new product hook.
sections.heading: Escalation and ownership matrix

sections.body:
- Adaptive batching toggle (runtime flag): toggles between low-latency and high-throughput batch profiles.
- KV cache aggressive TTL fallback: short-circuit cache rehydration for high churning prefixes.
- Prefill cold KV for high-frequency prefixes using synthetic runner.
- Traffic-splitting policy: automated progressive traffic shifting to fallback variants with health checks.
sections.heading: Automated mitigations (what we rely on)

sections.body:
1) If degradation persists or customer explicitly requests rollback, revert traffic split to primary model and drain fallback nodes gracefully.
   - CLI: model-router set-split --tenant <TENANT_ID> --primary 100 --fallback 0 --drain 300s
2) If scaling caused noisy neighbor effects, revert temporary scale and open a capacity incident to procure additional GPUs.
3) Record all changes with runbook tags and timestamps. Use audit CLI: runbook log --incident <INC_ID> --changes "..."
sections.heading: Safety and rollback (safe-failback)

sections.body:
- Initial (within 15m):
  Subject: [Redwood] We detected elevated traffic for your account — initial update
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,

  We detected a sudden increase in traffic for your account beginning at <time>. Our automated systems flagged an "avalanche" event and our operations team is actively stabilizing traffic. Expected impacts: transient increased latency and limited throttling on non-critical routes. We will follow up in 15 minutes with more detail.

  Owner: <CSM name> | support@redwood.ai | Escalation: +1-555-0123

- Follow-up (30–60m):
  Subject: [Redwood] Update on traffic surge for your account — actions taken
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,

  Summary of actions taken: enabled adaptive batching, progressive model fallback (quantized variants), and temporary rate shaping on non-critical endpoints. Current status: success rate: 99.3% (target 99.5%), 95th-token-latency: 1.8x baseline. Next steps: monitoring and preparing safe-failback.

  If you need to pause traffic from your side we recommend returning HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

Post-incident actions and QBR artifacts (owner: CSM + SRE):
- Incident timeline with all runbook logs and CLI commands.
- Cost delta report: compute minutes used vs baseline and estimated bill impact.
- Root-cause hypothesis and mitigation grooming ticket for product/serving teams.
- Customer-facing RCA draft and final RCA with timeline and preventative actions.
- Add a segment to the next QBR titled "Surge events and capacity readiness" including:
  - What happened, customer impact, timeline of mitigations, residual risk, recommended capacity reservations, and any commercial remedies.
sections.heading: Customer communications (templates)

sections.body:
- Scale dedicated pool: rcap scale --tenant TEN-42 --pool dedicated --delta 3 --tag "avalanche-temp"
- Set progressive fallback: model-router split --tenant TEN-42 --primary 70 --fallback 30 --policy progressive-10m
- Lock quota-protector: quota-protector lock --tenant TEN-42 --limit 2x-baseline --reason "avalanche"

Postmortem checklist (owner: SRE lead):
1) Collect telemetry (raw traces, ingress logs, model router metrics, KV cache traces).
2) Annotate timeline with all automated interventions and human actions.
3) Complete RCA within 7 business days and share with customer and internal stakeholders.
4) Propose concrete changes: autoscale tweak, pre-warming policy, fallback variants list update, cost-guard thresholds.
sections.heading: Operational playbook snippets (CLI examples)

sections.body:
A. Quick triage matrix (one-page):
- Symptom: High 95th latency; Likely cause: KV cache miss spike or model hot path saturation; Immediate action: enable quantized fallback, prefill KV, scale.
- Symptom: Rising 5xx; Likely cause: ingress-proxy queue overflow; Immediate action: enable backpressure headers, spill to batch gateway, scale ingress.

B. Dashboard IDs and links: Tenant Surge Overview: dash-ops-tn-surge-17; Model Router Health: dash-model-router-04; KV Cache Monitor: dash-kvcache-02.

C. Recommended QBR slides (bullets):
- Event summary, mitigation timeline, compute delta, recommended SLA/commit changes, open action items with owners and target dates.
sections.heading: Appendices

sections.body:
- Owner: Customer Success (playbook steward)
- Technical reviewer: Eng SRE (runtime stability)
- Review cadence: annual or after any enterprise-scale surge incident.
sections.heading: Document ownership and review cadence

sections.body:

- 2026-12-18: Added automated mitigation CLI and telemetry thresholds (Aisha Patel).
- 2027-01-15: Formal review and publication; added customer comms templates and QBR artifacts (Sofia Ramirez).

payload.page_title: Enterprise failure injection and resilience runbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This runbook describes a safe, repeatable program for conducting failure-injection and resilience validation exercises for enterprise tenants that use Redwood Inference (hosted, Dedicated, or Private). The goal is to validate customer-facing behaviours (failover, throttling, model fallback, and data isolation) and ensure Customer Success (CS) and Support teams have playbooks for communication, rollback, and remediation.

Scope
-----
- Applies to enterprise onboarding, stability game-days, and periodic resilience testing for dedicated/private tenants.
- Exercises include network partitioning, ingress throttling, model variant fallback, KV cache eviction, GPU preemption simulation, and telemetry loss scenarios.
- Not intended for experiments that modify persistent customer data or escalate to legal/regulatory gates without prior approvals.

Goals and acceptance criteria
----------------------------
- Assert that customer SLOs degrade gracefully with automated fallback policies engaged (latency SLO: p95 < 750ms under nominal; during controlled degradation, p95 may increase to 2s but requests must not return internal server error > 1% for 1h).
- Validate canary rollback path: 100% automated switchback to last-known-good model or region within 5 minutes of abort.
- Telemetry completeness: 99% of experiment events are recorded and grouped under experiment_id tag within Redwood tracing/metrics.
- Customer-facing incidents are handled within the escalation SLA documented in the Customer Incident Communications Matrix.

Owners and roles
----------------
- Experiment owner: Customer Success (CS) Solutions Engineer (primary contact for customer).
- Run executor: Platform Reliability (or customer SRE for Private installs).
- Observability lead: Observability engineer assigned to the tenant.
- Escalation liaison: Support Tier 2 lead.
- Approval authority: Customer Success manager + Security reviewer for Private/Dedicated customers.

When to use this runbook
------------------------
1. During enterprise onboarding (week 2–6) to validate cutover safety nets.
2. Prior to production model changes where rollback risk must be validated.
3. As part of quarterly resilience game-days or after major infra updates.
4. Whenever a customer requests a proof-of-resilience report for compliance.

Prerequisites
-------------
- Experiment plan approved (signed by CS manager and customer SRE if Private).
- Maintenance window scheduled and customer opt-in obtained when required.
- Backup/abort hooks verified (model pinning, routing policy override, traffic split control).
- Observability asserts configured: synthetic journey, per-route p50/p95/p99, error-rate alerts, and experiment_id tagging.
- Safety guardrails enabled: automatic circuit-breaker with threshold and manual abort endpoint.

Experiment catalogue (examples)
-------------------------------
Each experiment below includes intent, expected customer impact, telemetry assertions, and safe abort steps.

1) Ingress throttling (controlled egress saturation)
- Intent: validate adaptive rate limiter and quota-protector webhook under client surge.
- Customer impact: elevated latency, some client 429s expected within quota design.
- Telemetry asserts: 95th-percentile latency and 429-rate should match modelled profile.
- Abort: revert rate limiter to baseline policy, clear client token bucket; traffic should normalize within 60s.

2) Regional failover simulation (control-plane switch)
- Intent: ensure request routing falls back to alternate region or model variant without exposing token leakage.
- Customer impact: ~100–300ms added latency for routed requests, no data exposure.
- Telemetry asserts: requests routed via fallback path include header X-Redwood-Fallback: true and trace link.
- Abort: revert routing policy, trigger warm cache rebuild for primary region.

3) Model variant fallback under degraded GPU throughput
- Intent: validate automatic model switchover to quantized/fast variant when latency SLO is violated.
- Customer impact: small semantic variance in outputs; provide notice to customers during test.
- Telemetry asserts: model_variant metric should flip to fallback model id and tokenization stats logged.
- Abort: force-publish pinned model version for tenant and drain fallback nodes.

4) KV cache eviction and cold-start behavior
- Intent: emulate cache purge and validate KV cold-warm startup times and cost spike characteristics.
- Customer impact: transient cost spike and higher token latency for first requests.
- Telemetry asserts: cache-miss-rate, kv-lookup-latency, and per-token cost tags.
- Abort: warm caches using synthetic seeds and verify hit-rate > 90% within window.

5) Telemetry ingestion throttling / partial metrics loss
- Intent: test how downstream alerting and QBR metrics behave when observability sampling rate is reduced.
- Customer impact: none to user-facing systems, but internal dashboards may report degraded fidelity.
- Telemetry asserts: sampling tags and synthetic route alerts must surface to incident channel; missing spans must be flagged.
- Abort: restore sampling rate and reindex experiment traces.

Safe experiment design pattern
-----------------------------
- Start small: run experiments in a narrow tenant subset or sandboxed tenant.
- Canary stages: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic, with explicit automated hold/pause gates between stages.
- Timebox: every stage should have a maximum duration and an automatic rollback trigger on threshold breach.
- Communication: annotate customer slack channel and incident bridge before starting.

Scheduling, communications and customer consent
---------------------------------------------
- For hosted customers: experiments requiring visible degradation must include email + console notification 72 hours before, and a maintenance window with opt-out link.
- For Dedicated/Private customers: follow the private deployment change control and require SRE signoff; schedule during agreed maintenance windows.
- Template customer notification: (1) summary of intent, (2) expected customer impact, (3) start/end time, (4) roll back criteria, (5) contact matrix.

Execution checklist (pre-flight)
-------------------------------
1. Verify feature-flag toggles and model pins are set.
2. Confirm observability asserts and experiment_id tagging in tracing.
3. Snapshot current routing and scaling policies.
4. Notify stakeholders and create incident bridge.
5. Run low-risk dry-run in sandbox.
6. Have abort playbook open and test abort endpoint.

Numbered procedure: running an ingress throttling experiment
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Create experiment run: POST /internal/experiments with body {\n   "experiment_id": "exp-<tenant>-20260610",\n   "type": "ingress-throttle",\n   "stage": "canary-1"\n}
2. Apply rate limit via adaptive-rate-limiter API:
   redwood-cli rate-limit apply --tenant <ID> --policy ex-throttle-1 --limit 100req/s
3. Verify traces: run query tracer.query("service:ingress AND experiment_id:<id>")
4. Wait 10 minutes monitoring p95 and error rate.
5. If thresholds exceeded (error-rate > 1% or p95 > 2s), call abort.
6. Abort: redwood-cli rate-limit revert --tenant <ID> --policy ex-throttle-1
7. Confirm traffic normalized and post metrics to experiment dashboard.

Telemetry assertions and SLO checks
----------------------------------
- Mandatory dashboards for every experiment: synthetic-journey, per-tenant error-rate, per-model latency, token-cost per-minute, and experiment_event_log.
- SLO guardrails to configure before start: p95 latency thresholds, error-rate ceilings, and model-fidelity signal (eval set pass-rate).
- Example PromQL checks:
  - latency_p95_tenant{tenant="<id>"} > 2.0 (trigger),
  - http_error_rate{tenant="<id>"} > 0.01 (trigger)

Abort/rollback paths and verification
------------------------------------
- Automated abort: circuit-breaker triggers will stop canary progression and run abort-hooks.
- Manual abort: support-runbook command documented below can be executed by Support Tier 2.
- Verification: confirm post-abort metrics return to baseline within the timewindow defined in the run plan.

Customer communications and incident templates
--------------------------------------------
- Short blurb for console banner: "Redwood is running a resilience validation for tenant <org>. Expected transient latency increases; contact <CS> for concerns."
- Incident postmortem summary template for customer: summary, timeline, root cause, impact, corrective actions, and compensation if SLA breached.

Post-experiment analysis and QBR deliverables
--------------------------------------------
- Deliverables: resilience report (one-pager), experiment artifacts (traces, config diffs, logs), customer-facing summary, and action items.
- QBR signals to include: mean-time-to-rollback, percentage of experiments passing acceptance, number of customer-visible degradations, and suggested mitigations (e.g., increase warm-start capacity, adjust model fallback thresholds).

Risk matrix and mitigations
--------------------------
- High risk: experiments that touch customer data pipelines or long-lived storage (require legal review). Mitigation: use synthetic data or isolated sandbox.
- Medium risk: full-tenant failover tests during business hours. Mitigation: timebox and use staged canaries.
- Low risk: observability sampling reductions. Mitigation: test in non-production first.

Appendix: CLI snippets and Kubernetes plays
-----------------------------------------
- Sample abort command (Support Tier 2):
  curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TOKEN" \
    https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/experiments/exp-<tenant>-20260610/abort

- Force model pin via API:
  redwood-cli models pin --tenant <ID> --model-id rwd-fast-quant-1 --reason "abort experiment"

- Simulate GPU preemption (dev-only):
  kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Postmortem and RCA template
---------------------------
1. Executive summary (3 bullets)
2. Timeline of events (with timestamps in UTC)
3. Impact analysis (customers affected, duration, business impact)
4. Root cause hypothesis and evidence (traces, logs, recordings)
5. Remediation steps and owners (who will fix, timeframe)
6. Follow-up experiments and regression checks

Change log
----------
- 2026-02-12: Initial published runbook by Maya Chen.
- 2026-04-21: Added telemetry asserts and PromQL examples (reviewer: Evan Hart).
- 2026-06-10: Expanded experiment catalogue with KV cache eviction case and regional failover scenario.

Related pages
-------------
- See also: enterprise-onboarding/private-deployment-acceptance (link internal), incident-response-security runbooks, and observability-fallback-circuit guide.

Contact and escalation list
--------------------------
- CS Solutions (primary): maya.chen@redwood.ai
- Platform Reliability: platform-sre@redwood.ai
- Support Tier 2: support-t2@redwood.ai
- Observability: obs-team@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Tenant Observability Contract Lifecycle and Versioning Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the lifecycle, versioning rules, testing gates, and rollout procedures for tenant-specific observability contracts used during enterprise onboarding and post-go-live operations. It standardizes how telemetry schemas, labels, and SLO-related metrics are introduced, evolved, and deprecated for dedicated and private tenants. The aim is to reduce integration friction, preserve downstream SLO integrity, and provide clear rollback and remediation steps for customers and internal teams.

Goals
-----
- Provide a predictable, auditable change process for tenant telemetry schemas ("contract").
- Minimize customer-side parsing and dashboard breakage during schema changes.
- Ensure SLO and billing signals remain consistent across contract versions.
- Define operational runbooks for validation, rollout, and rollback.

Scope
-----
Includes: ingress metrics, request/response metadata, model-identifiers, latency/billing tokens, event tracing IDs, and tenant-specific labels emitted by ingress-proxy, model-router, and telemetry-gatekeeper.
Excludes: internal-only debug traces and ephemeral dev-only flags.

Principles
----------
1) Backward compatibility first: additive fields only for patch/minor updates whenever possible.
2) Explicit version header: every telemetry payload must include `telemetry_contract_version` and `schema_version`.
3) Consumer-driven validation: create a consumer schema test harness prior to rollout.
4) SLO continuity: any change that impacts token counting or latency buckets requires SLO owner sign-off.

Contract Versioning Rules
-------------------------
- Versioning scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (SemVer-like, but focused on consumer compatibility):
  - MAJOR: incompatible changes (removal/rename of required fields, semantic changes to metric meaning). Requires coordinated migration and 90-day deprecation notice.
  - MINOR: additive fields and new optional labels. Safe for rolling updates.
  - PATCH: bug fixes in serialization, typos, or clarifications that do not change semantics.
- Filesystem path / registry: contracts are stored in the telemetry registry (internal git repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/). Each version has a manifest and migration notes.

Telemetry Contract Example (minimal JSON payload example)
--------------------------------------------------------
Note: this example is intentionally concise — real payloads will include additional tracing and debug metadata.

{
  "telemetry_contract_version": "1.2.0",
  "tenant_id": "enterprise-42",
  "request_id": "r-8ab3cd",
  "model_id": "redwood-compat-13b-q4",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "tokens_input": 128,
  "tokens_output": 42,
  "latency_ms": 78.2,
  "cost_units": 0.0038,
  "timestamp": "2026-01-29T15:22:03Z",
  "labels": {"region":"eu-west-1", "deployment_tier":"dedicated", "privacy_level":"high"}
}

Migration and Rollout Procedure
-------------------------------
1) Design phase (owner: CS integration engineer)
   - Author the new contract in the registry and add migration notes.
   - Identify all internal consumers (billing, SLO dashboards, QBR reports, cost attribution jobs, alerting rules).
   - Create a migration ticket and assign reviewers (SRE, Billing, Observability, Product).

2) Validation harness (owner: Observability team)
   - Add the new schema to the consumer test harness.
   - Run the following checks:
     a) Parsing test (clickhouse/bq ingestion): ingest 1000 synthetic payloads and confirm no schema rejections.
     b) SLO equivalence: simulate token counts and latency buckets to ensure SLOs do not change >1%.
     c) Dashboard smoke: run dashboard snapshots of top-10 queries for differences.

3) Canary (owner: CS + SRE)
   - Canary window (default 48 hours): enable new contract for 2% of tenant traffic per region.
   - Monitor: error rate, ingestion rejects, billing delta, and SLO drift. Alerts: any of the following triggers immediate rollback:
     - ingestion_reject_rate > 0.1% sustained over 30m
     - billing_signal_delta > 5% compared to baseline
     - SLO metric drift > 2%

4) Gradual rollout
   - 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over successive windows (24–72 hours each), adjust based on risk and test results.

5) Complete and document
   - Mark registry entry as active and update related onboarding docs and QBR templates.
   - Notify customer success contacts and tenant POCs.

Rollback and Emergency Remediation
----------------------------------
- Hot rollback: flip ingestion to last-stable schema at the telemetry-gatekeeper layer. This is expected to be near-instant but requires a follow-up migration postmortem.
- If hot rollback is not possible (e.g., semantic change in token counting), escalate immediately to SRE and Billing and open a severity-1 incident with the standard incident comms template.
- Triage checklist for rollback incident:
  1) Capture affected tenant list and time window.
  2) Freeze billing-related aggregations and mark as provisional.
  3) Notify customer POCs with a templated message (see Appendix A).

Validation Tests and Gating
--------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Schema lint (jsonschema) passes.
- Consumer test harness run with zero parsing failures.
- SLO smoke equivalence within guardrails (default: SLO drift < 1% for latency; token count variance < 0.5%).
- Billing delta within tolerance (default: < 2% over the canary window).

Sample Prometheus Alert Rule (conceptual)
----------------------------------------
sections.heading: Mandatory gating checks before any minor or major update

sections.body:
expr: rate(telemetry_ingestion_rejects_total[5m]) / rate(telemetry_ingest_total[5m]) > 0.001
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "High telemetry ingestion reject rate (>0.1%)"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/telemetry-ingest-failure"

SLO Mapping and QBR Implications
--------------------------------
- Each telemetry contract version must include a metadata file that maps emitted fields to product SLOs and QBR KPIs. Example mapping: `tokens_output` -> billing.units, `latency_ms` -> platform.latency.slo.
- During QBR prep, the CS team must verify that the contract version used in the QBR timeframe matches the contract recorded in the migration registry. Discrepancies must be annotated in the QBR appendix.

Ownership and Notifications
---------------------------
- Contract author: CS integration engineering (primary).
- Observability: owns consumer test harness and alerting.
- Billing: approves any change that affects token counting or cost_units.
- SRE: approves rollout windows and manages canary routing.

Communication and Customer-Facing Steps
--------------------------------------
1) Pre-schedule notification: send a 14-day heads-up for major changes, 7 days for minor changes.
2) Pre-cutover checklist: share a migration plan and sample payloads with tenant POC and solutions engineer.
3) Post-cutover confirmation: within 24 hours confirm telemetry ingestion is stable and provide a simple validation script tenant can run.

Appendix A — Templated Customer Notification (short)
---------------------------------------------------
Subject: Upcoming Telemetry Schema Update (telemetry_contract_version 1.2.0)

Hello <Tenant POC>,

We are planning a telemetry schema update that will be enabled for your tenant on <date>. The change is additive (new optional labels and an additional `cost_units` field) and should not require action. During the canary window, you may see a small variance in billing aggregates; we will monitor closely and share results. If you prefer a scheduled cutover or need a private testing window, reply to this thread and we will coordinate.

Regards,
Redwood Customer Success

Appendix B — Example Validation CLI (tenant-facing)
----------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: name: Telemetry_Ingestion_Rejects

sections.body:
curl -X POST "https://telemetry-test.redwood.com/ingest" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"telemetry_contract_version":"1.2.0","tenant_id":"<your-tenant>","request_id":"r-test","model_id":"m-test","tokens_input":10,"tokens_output":5,"latency_ms":40.0,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
sections.heading: curl example payload to the telemetry gatekeeper (test endpoint)

sections.body:
cat sample-payload.json | jq '.telemetry_contract_version == "1.2.0" and .tokens_output > 0'

Appendix C — Quick Checklist (for rollout ticket)
-------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Registry entry created and reviewed
- [ ] Consumer harness run and green
- [ ] Billing sign-off obtained (if required)
- [ ] Canary window scheduled (2% start)
- [ ] Pager/alert rules adjusted and runbook linked
- [ ] Customer POC notified per pre-schedule
- [ ] Post-cutover validation completed

Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------
- telemetry contracts repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/ (internal git)
- Observability test harness: /confluence/eng-platform/telemetry-test-harness
- Incident runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/telemetry-ingest-failures

Questions or feedback
--------------------
If you are the owner of an internal consumer (dashboards, billing jobs, or QBR reports), please review the contract registry entry during the design phase and add yourself as a reviewer. For urgent issues during a rollout, page #observability on Slack and follow the incident escalation procedure.

payload.page_title: Enterprise LLM Behavior Delta Detection and Customer Triage Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook documents a repeatable, measurable process for detecting and triaging behavioral deltas (quality regressions or shifts) in LLM outputs that materially affect enterprise customers. It focuses on automated detection signals, deterministic first-line triage, evidence packaging for root-cause analysis (RCA), and customer-safe communications. Use this playbook when telemetry or customers indicate unexpected changes in output behavior ( hallucinations, repeated refusal patterns, persona drift, or factual regressions ).

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted and Dedicated tenants (hosted API and dedicated capacity).
- Covers model serving changes, quantization/rewrites, prompt-layer changes, routing/fanout, and inference runtime rollouts.
- Does NOT replace safety escalation for clear safety violations; refer to the LLM Safety Escalation Matrix for safety-first incidents.

Goals and success criteria:
- Detect behavior deltas within 5 business minutes for enterprise customers with active synthetic monitors.
- First-line response (triage started) within 30 minutes of alert.
- Deliver a reproducible evidence bundle to eng/research within 2 business hours.
- Provide customer-facing summary or mitigation within 4 business hours for P1/P2 severity.

Signal sources (ranked):
1) Synthetic customer-specific probes (Customer Synthetic Suite) — highest fidelity.
2) EvalHub regression alerts (score delta > 3 std dev on key prompts).
3) Production telemetry anomalies: embedding drift, decrease in token-efficiency, unexpected inference latency-correlated quality drops.
4) Customer-reported examples via support ticket or CSE Slack.
5) Observability-sourced NLP-based diff alerts (ModelGuard behavioral clustering).

Key monitoring metrics and thresholds (examples):
- DeltaRate.alert: fraction of probe prompts with changed top-1 intent (threshold 0.2 => 20% of probes changed)
- Answer-Confidence-drop: moving average of model log-prob changes (threshold -1.5 nats per token)
- BLEU/ROUGE/PolicyScore degradation on gold prompts (threshold: 15% relative drop)
- Embedding-similarity mean shift (Cosine drop > 0.08)

Alerting and severity mapping:
- P1 (Customer-impacting production degradation): >50% probe failures OR direct revenue loss signal. Pager to oncall, #cust-incident, immediate exec notification.
- P2 (Material degradation): 20–50% probe failures or consistent customer reports; page oncall, slack channel, triage meeting within 30 minutes.
- P3 (Degradation but limited scope): investigate during business hours; ticket and owner assigned.

Runbook: First-line triage (ordered steps)
1) Ingest alert and classify: note source (synthetic/telemetry/customer) and affected tenant(s).
2) Snapshot evidence: run the customer’s last-known-good prompt set through current and rollback model variants (use EvalHub quick-run).
3) Confirm reproducibility: reproduce with customer prompt and with 3 controlled paraphrases. If behavior is inconsistent, mark as "non-deterministic — sample variance."
4) Capture traces: collect request_id(s), model version hash, kernel config, quantization profile, routing path, and telemetry window (+/- 15 mins).
5) Check recent deploys and infra events: query Deployment Audit (last 24 hours) and infra incidents (GPU preemption, autoscaler events).
6) Short mitigation: consider fallbacks per mitigation matrix (see Mitigation guidance).
7) If P1/P2, assemble evidence bundle and notify Eng SRE + Applied ML with severity tags.

Mitigation guidance (quick options):
- Automatic rollback to pinned model version for the tenant (if configured).
- Route customer traffic to higher-fidelity variant (e.g.,.fp16 -> int8? prefer higher-precision model).
- Apply prompt-layer shim: inject customer-specific guard prompt or primer to correct drift while RCA proceeds.
- Temporary rate-limit or sampling policy to reduce exposure window for hallucinations.

Evidence bundle requirements (must be attached to ticket):
- 3x failing customer examples with timestamps + paraphrases
- Model metadata: model_name, model_version, model_hash, quant_profile_id
- Inference runtime snapshot: kernel selection, batch size, GPU_id, node_id, kv-cache-size
- Telemetry traces: request_id, trace_id, relevant logs (stderr/stdout) clipped to 2000 lines total
- EvalHub run summary CSV and diff image (if applicable)

Customer communication templates (short, editable):
- Initial acknowledgement (within 1hr for P1/P2):
  "We’ve received your report and are actively investigating. We have identified a behavioral regression impacting your inference results and are prioritizing a mitigation. Initial mitigation options are under evaluation; next update in 60–120 minutes. — Customer Success Ops"
- Post-mitigation summary (post RCA):
  "Root cause: [brief summary]. Actions taken: [rollback/patch/deployment tweak]. Impacted timeframe: [t0..t1]. Recommended customer action: [if any]. We will follow up with formal RCA within X business days."

Escalation matrix (who to contact and when):
1) Customer Success Ops (owner) — immediate on triage start
2) Applied ML model-owner — if model delta suspected or sample-based regression confirmed
3) Eng SRE — if infrastructure/capacity signals present or rollback required
4) Product/Account Exec — for high-value customers and contractual SLA implications
5) Legal/Security — if customer data or privacy impact is detected

Operational checklist for engineers (fast reference):
- Confirm model hash: curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/models/{tenant}/versions | jq .current_hash
- Run controlled eval: evalhub run --tenant TID --suite customer-probes --variants baseline,current --output tmp/diff.csv
- Apply temporary routing: rctl set-route --tenant TID --route override --model baseline --duration 2h

Table: Suggested mitigations by root cause
| Root cause category | Short mitigation | Owner |
|---------------------|------------------|-------|
| Model rollout regression | Rollback to previous pinned model, enable canary gating | Applied ML
| Quantization artifact | Re-route to non-quantized variant, escalate to runtime team | Eng Serving Runtime
| Inference kernel mismatch | Force kernel compatibility profile, schedule hotfix | Eng Serving Runtime
| Prompt-layer change | Revert primer change, inject customer primer override | Customer Success / DevEx
| Routing/fanout bug | Apply safe fanout limit, route to single region | Eng Platform / SRE

Retention and evidence policy:
- Keep evidence bundles for 90 days on S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/YYYY/MM/tenantID/incidentID
- Attach EvalHub runs to the ticket and tag with incidentID.

Automation and tooling integration (operational notes):
- Telemetry Gatekeeper rules: create rule with type=behavioral_delta, window=24h, sensitivity=customer_high. Example JSON rule used by Telemetry Gatekeeper included below.
- EvalHub periodic rebaseline: schedule weekly rebaselines for enterprise tenants with heavy customization.

Example Telemetry Gatekeeper rule (JSON):
{
  "rule_id": "cust_behavior_delta_v1",
  "scope": "tenant:{{TENANT_ID}}",
  "metric": "probe_top1_changed_fraction",
  "window_minutes": 60,
  "threshold": 0.20,
  "consecutive_windows": 2,
  "actions": ["ticket:create:CS-TRIAGE", "page:oncall:cs_oncall", "run:evalhub_quickrun"]
}

Operational handoff to Eng (RCA expectations):
- Deliver the evidence bundle within 2 hours for P1 incidents.
- Include a short reproduction script and the exact EvalHub command used.
- Provide hypothesis list prioritized by likelihood with data pointers.

Post-incident steps and QBR inputs:
1) Postmortem: publish within 72 hours (summary + timeline + RCA owner).
2) Follow-up action items tracked in the incident board and closed by owner.
3) Add any new customer probes to the Customer Synthetic Suite if gap discovered.
4) Feed regression into the monthly QBR: include severity, uptime impact, and mitigation cost.

Appendix A — Runbook checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Timestamp and ticket created
- [ ] Evidence bundle attached
- [ ] Repro script included
- [ ] Notified Applied ML & Eng SRE
- [ ] Customer informed (template used)
- [ ] RCA draft in board

Appendix B — Links and references:
- Customer Synthetic Suite docs: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/customer-synthetic-suite
- EvalHub quick-run guide: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quick-run-guide
- LLM Safety Escalation Matrix: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/llm-safety-escalation-matrix

Appendix C — Example paraphrase strategy for reproducibility tests:
1) Exact prompt (customer-submitted)
2) P1: collapse numerals to words
3) P2: shorten each sentence to 75% length
4) P3: replace named entities with placeholders

Ownership and contact list:
- Customer Success Ops: cs-ops@redwood.example (owner for triage)
- Applied ML oncall: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.example (escalation for model-owner)
- Eng SRE: sre-oncall@redwood.example

Change log:
- 2026-02-18: Created by Priya Nair
- 2026-07-10: Updated mitigation matrix and Telemetry Gatekeeper example (reviewers: Ethan Park, Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez)

End of document.

payload.page_title: Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)

sections.body: This page documents how Support should handle and count reports of a **token accounting discrepancy** across intake channels. These cases frequently arrive via Slack, email, or Jira, and can be double-counted unless we normalize to a single canonical support record.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body: We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.
sections.heading: Definition (use this phrase)

sections.body:
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)
- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance
sections.heading: Approved intake channels

sections.body:
1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.
2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).
3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.
sections.heading: How to avoid double counting

sections.body:
- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)
- Client counts only final chunk tokens
- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization
- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings
- Tool-call serialization adds tokens
- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)
sections.heading: Common root causes to check

sections.body:
- SUP-2841: streaming retry/reconnect behavior leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-2917: embeddings tokenizer mismatch leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-3009: cache-hit + tool calling bug leading to real token accounting discrepancy
sections.heading: Known examples (for reference)

sections.body: When answering: "Which intake channel has the most reports of token accounting discrepancy?" be sure to include Slack and Gmail-origin cases even if a SUP ticket was created later.

payload.page_title: Model Change Approval & Customer Governance Runbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This runbook defines the governance, approval paths, operational checks, and customer communication templates for any model or model-configuration change that impacts enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments). It is intended for Customer Success, Product, SRE, Serving Runtime, and Security teams. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions, keep customers informed, and make rollbacks predictable.

Scope
-----
- Applies to model version swaps, quantization profile changes, prompt-template migrations, model serving config changes (e.g., max_tokens, sampling defaults), and runtime kernel changes that may alter output semantics or latency by >5%.
- Includes both Redwood-initiated and customer-requested changes for enterprise tenants.
- Excludes purely infra-only upgrades that do not alter model observable behavior (see Appendix A for classification rules).

Why we need this
-----------------
Enterprise customers require predictable output quality and clear change windows. Uncoordinated changes generate escalations, churn risk, and operational burden. This runbook balances speed with customer safety using a two-track approval model (minor vs major) and objective telemetry gates.

Primary stakeholders and ownership
---------------------------------
- Customer Success (CS): final customer communications, risk assessment for accounts, QBR notes.
- Product: change justification, rollout strategy, canary criteria.
- Eng - Serving Runtime: technical rollout, canary execution, rollback hooks.
- Eng - SRE: capacity and latency SLO guardrails, escalation path.
- Security/Compliance: signoff for private deployments or regulated customers.
- Owner: Customer Success (contact: marcos.rivera@redwood.com).

Decision categories (classification)
-----------------------------------
1) Minor change (fast-track):
   - Non-production-facing prompt-template tweaks, minor sampling seed updates, telemetry-only instrumentation.
   - Expected impact: negligible change to model outputs; latency delta <5%.
   - Approval: Product + CS peer review.
2) Major change (full review):
   - Model family change (e.g., v1->v2), quantization profile change altering float->int path, new architecture variant, or changes that affect factuality/behavior.
   - Expected impact: potential behavioral regressions or latency change >=5%.
   - Approval: Product + CS + Serving Runtime + SRE + Security (if Private) + Exec sponsor.

Approval matrix (summary)
-------------------------
- Minor: Product (owner) -> CS notify -> rollout during maintenance window or low-traffic canary.
- Major: Model Change Request (MCR) RFC -> Cross-functional review meeting -> Signed approval via ticket (Jira PRD) -> Scheduled canary -> Customer opt-in for early testing or staged opt-out.

Pre-change checklist (must be completed before any scheduled rollout)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- Define classification (minor/major) and document justification.
- Owner assigns cross-functional reviewers (list in ticket).
- Identify impacted customers (list enterprise tenants) and their SLA tier.
- Create a rollback plan with RTO goals and quick rollback triggers.
- Create automated telemetry assertions (see Telemetry & validations).
- Schedule rollout window and reserve SRE on-call for the change window + 2 hours.
- Draft customer-facing communication (CS drafts, Product approves).

Change execution procedure (canary & rollout)
-------------------------------------------
1) Pre-canary steps (T-48 to T-2 hours):
   - Deploy change to internal staging and run the predefined prompt-suite (see Appendix B).
   - Run synthetic traffic at production-like token distribution for 30m.
   - Verify cost delta and latency distribution vs baseline.
2) Canary (T):
   - Route 0.5-2% steady-state traffic from canary tenants or synthetic tenancy to the new variant for 1 hour.
   - Run automated evals: output-delta metric, hallucination score, top-k token distribution, and latency P95.
   - Monitor errors and backend resource consumption.
3) Scale canary (T+1h):
   - If all assertions pass, increase to 10% for 2 hours.
   - If still green, schedule a rolling increase with checkpoints at 25%, 50%, 100% each with 2-hour observation windows.
4) Abort/rollback:
   - Any assertion failure or customer-reported regression escalates to the Runbook Owner who initiates rollback. See Rollback criteria.

Telemetry & validations (objective gates)
---------------------------------------
Create assertions that are executed automatically during rollout. Example set:
- Functional quality: output-delta rate < 2% across canonical prompt-set (per tenant).
- Hallucination signal: composite hallucination score delta <= 0.5 points (normalized).
- Latency: P95 latency delta <= 15% absolute or <= 200ms (whichever is smaller).
- Error budget: 5xx rate not to exceed 0.1% above baseline.
- Cost: per-token compute cost delta <= 10% for Dedicated customers without prior consent.
- Tokenization/regression checks: no >0.2% increase in truncation/invalid-token counts.

Incident/escalation flow for regressions during rollout
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Tier 1 detection: automated assertion breach -> Alert on Slack #canary-alerts and PagerDuty to Serving Runtime on-call.
2) Triage (10–30 minutes): Owner and runtime on-call validate and reproduce.
3) Customer notification (30–60 minutes): If customer MCR was not pre-signed, CS sends a status update using the "Short Incident Notice" template below.
4) Decision window (60–120 minutes): Either quick rollback or targeted mitigation (e.g., revert sampling param).
5) Postmortem and RCA: If rollback occurred or customer impact exceeded 15 minutes, open a postmortem ticket and schedule a cross-team review in 3 business days.

Rollback criteria (explicit triggers)
-----------------------------------
- Any assertion breach listed above for >15 minutes sustained.
- More than one enterprise tenant reports a reproducible semantic regression within 60 minutes.
- P95 latency increase >250ms causing SLA violation risk.
- Unexpected 5xx spike >0.5% absolute.
- Cost surge alarm for Dedicated customer where budget controls exist.

Customer communication templates (use and adapt per account)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1) Short Incident Notice (for initial outreach):
Subject: Service update: model rollout observation - [CustomerName]
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Hi [CustomerName] team,
We are observing an unexpected behavior during a model update that may impact a subset of requests. We have paused the rollout for your tenant and our engineering team is investigating. We will share an update within 60 minutes and provide mitigation steps if needed.
Best,
[CS Rep]

2) Post-Rollback Summary (within 24 hours):
Subject: Post-rollback summary & next steps - [CustomerName]
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
Hi [CustomerName],
We reverted the recent model change for your tenant at [time]. Summary of what happened, impact window, and next steps (including optional test schedule and QBR notes). Attach the synthetic test-report PDF and link to the RCA when available.

Post-change QA and QBR integration
----------------------------------
- Add the change event to the next customer QBR agenda under "Operational Changes & Risk" with: description, canary metrics, customer impact (if any), and recommended next steps.
- Maintain a change log for each enterprise tenant with: change id, date, owner, pre/post metric snapshots, and artifacts (test reports, canary dashboards).

Edge cases and private deployments
---------------------------------
- For Private deployments, Security must confirm that the new model binary/quantization artifacts meet the customer FIPS/HSM constraints before approval.
- For heavily regulated customers (marked in account metadata as "regulated: true"), require an explicit customer opt-in unless the change is security-critical.

Operational tooling and runbook automation
----------------------------------------
- Use the MCR (Model Change Request) ticket template in Jira and attach: rationale, canary plan, telemetry assertions, rollback plan, impacted tenant list, and customer comms draft.
- Canary dashboards: link to Grafana panels: model_canary_{change_id}_quality and model_canary_{change_id}_latency.
- Automate assertion evaluation via the canary-orchestrator job (CLI example below).

CLI examples and request payloads
--------------------------------
- Start a canary run (internal):
  redwood-canaryctl start --change-id MCR-1234 --duration 60m --traffic 2% --prompt-suite default-sanity

- Example MCR JSON payload (attach to Jira):
  {
    "change_id": "MCR-1234",
    "author": "marcos.rivera@redwood.com",
    "classification": "major",
    "description": "Upgrade from model-x-1.3 to model-x-2.0 (chiefly factuality and perf improvements)",
    "impact_scope": ["tenant-abc", "tenant-xyz"],
    "telemetry_assertions": ["output-delta<2%","p95-latency-delta<15%"],
    "rollback_plan": "automated switch to model-x-1.3 and invalidate kvcache for canary tenants",
    "scheduled_window": "2026-07-29T02:00:00Z/2026-07-29T06:00:00Z"
  }

Note: The JSON above should be pasted into the Jira change artifact.

Postmortem and RCA expectations
-------------------------------
- If the change causes customer-visible regression, open a postmortem within 24 hours. Include: timeline, root causes, detection signals, and action items with owners and due dates.
- If regression is prevented by telemetry, capture the assertion data and mark the MCR as "near-miss". Add to monthly governance review for trending.

Appendix A — classification decision rules (quick)
------------------------------------------------
- If the change modifies model weights or tokenizer, classify as Major.
- If change only tweaks hyperparameters that do not cross a rational threshold (e.g., temperature 0.7->0.72), classify as Minor.
- If ambiguity remains, default to Major and follow full signoff.

Appendix B — recommended canonical prompt-suite (summary)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Customer-canonical: 30 representative prompts derived from top-ten customer intents.
- Safety-canonical: 40 prompts designed to surface hallucinations, instruction following, and refusal behavior.
- Latency-canonical: 20 long-sequence prompts (avg 1024 tokens).

Appendix C — escalation contacts
-------------------------------
- CS Runbook Owner: marcos.rivera@redwood.com (Pager: paged via #cs-runbook)
- Serving Runtime on-call: runtime-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty)
- SRE: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Security: security-escalation@redwood.com

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-03-11: Created by Marcos Rivera.
- 2026-07-20: Added explicit telemetry assertions and Private deployment signoff requirement.

This document should be used as a normative checklist for all enterprise-impacting model changes. Questions or suggested updates should be submitted to the runbook owner or opened as a Confluence comment against this page.

payload.page_title: First 14-Day Entitlement and Remediation Runbook for Enterprise Go-Live

sections.body:
Summary:

This runbook defines the operational checklist, entitlement validation, telemetry assertions, and remediation steps for the first 14 calendar days after an enterprise tenant goes live with Redwood. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and oncall SRE/Platform engineers supporting dedicated and private deployments.

Purpose and scope:
- Ensure contractual entitlements and configuration match production behavior (rate limits, reserved capacity, feature flags).
- Verify baseline performance, cost signals, and functional correctness across the tenant surface (ingress, model routing, responses).
- Provide clear, actionable remediation steps for common failure modes observed during early adoption.
- Standardize communication templates for customer updates and internal escalation.

Quick reference SLOs to validate (tenant-visible):
- Token generation latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 400ms (hosted); for Dedicated SLA values negotiated per contract.
- Request success rate: >= 99.5% (5xx + client-error excluding rate-limit).
- Input-to-output throughput: within +/-25% of capacity reservation in first 14 days.
- Cost anomaly guardrail: daily spend drift <= 30% vs baseline estimate.

Prerequisites (pre-go-live verification):
1) Entitlement manifest uploaded to tenant account and validated (rate limits, model access, quota tiers).
2) Telemetry gatekeeper integration completed and test events flowing to telemetry index (tenant-metrics-collector).
3) Ingress and egress firewalls or peering verified (for Private deployments).
4) Canary traffic and synthetic journeys executed with pass criteria met (see Acceptance criteria).

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success Lead: primary contact for customer communication and business escalation.
- Solutions Engineer: owns configuration validation, post-provision tuning, and acceptance tests.
- SRE oncall: owns production remediation activities, service-level alerts, and rollbacks.
- Model Ops: validates model correctness, quality drift, and rollout adjustments.

Entitlement and configuration validation checklist (first 48 hours):
1) Confirm rate-limiting policy applied to tenant: run endpoint check against /v1/usage/limits and compare to contract.
2) Validate model catalog access: attempt to instantiate the tenant-default model with SDK key and ensure model-router returns expected model hash.
3) Verify reserved capacity is reachable: confirm at least one GPU pool connection is established (service: gpu-allocator).
4) Confirm data plane encryption and KMS key access (for Private): kms: TestEncrypt API returns 200.
5) Check billing tags and cost attribution metadata are attached to tenant requests.

Telemetry assertions (queries and thresholds to run daily):
- Request success rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID",code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) > 0.995

- Request latency (p95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) by (le)) < 0.4

- Token cost per 1k tokens (derived): daily_token_cost = sum(token_cost_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"}) / (sum(tokens_generated_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"})/1000)
  Alert if daily_token_cost > expected_unit_cost * 1.5

- Synthetic journey success (example curl):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b", "input":"The capital of France is"}'
  Expected: 200, contains "Paris" or equivalent.

Acceptance criteria for steady state (end of day 14):
- All telemetry assertions pass for at least 72% of 12-hour windows during day 8–14.
- No more than two major incidents attributable to platform plumbing (networking, quota enforcement, ingress) during first 14 days.
- Customer-specified quality regression tests (prompt-set) maintain >= 90% pass rate versus baseline.

Runbook: top-level remediation flows (ordered by likelihood)

1) High error rate (5xx spikes)
- Observable signals: 5xx spike in redwood_api_requests_total, sudden p95 latency surge, GPU pool utilization near 100%.
- Immediate steps (SRE oncall):
  a) Silence non-actionable alerts and annotate incident channel (#cs-tenant-TENANTID) with initial findings.
  b) Check gpu-allocator and model-router health: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=gpu-allocator; kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-router\  c) If GPU pool OOMs or ejects pods, remove tenant from routing (via control plane: POST /admin/route/remove-tenant) and failover to a compatible fallback model (see control-plane runbook snippet).
  d) If ingress NLB shows connection errors, run tcpdump on ingress gateway and escalate to network team.
- Customer comms template: "We've detected elevated error rates affecting your tenant. We've removed traffic from the impacted pool while we investigate; your traffic is being routed to a fallback model to preserve availability. Expected ETA: 30–90 minutes."

2) Latency regressions with normal error rate
- Signals: p95 latency increased > 2x baseline while success rate remains > 99%.
- Remediation (SE + SRE):
  a) Check continuous batching and KV cache hit rate stats: query tenant_kvcache_hit_ratio{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[10m]
  b) If cache miss spike: warm cache by replaying synthetic prefix requests (see synthetic warmup script below).
  c) If batching latency high: adjust max_batch_size for tenant via tenant config API and schedule a controlled scaling of worker replicas.

Synthetic warmup script (example):
```
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"tenant-default","input":"Warmup prompt '$i'"}' >/dev/null &
done
wait
```

3) Unexpected quality regressions (model output accuracy or hallucinations)
- Signals: customer report, failing prompt-set evals, sudden divergence in evaluation scores in eval-harness.
- Remediation (Model Ops + SE):
  a) Re-run prompt-set locally against model hash reported in runtime logs.
  b) If regression confirmed, initiate model rollback to prior model hash using the rollout API and notify customer.
  c) Open a model-regression ticket with Research with full prompt-set + failure examples.

4) Cost surge (unexpected spend)
- Signals: daily_token_cost spike, unexpected embedding indexing runs, long-running batch jobs attributed to tenant.
- Remediation (CS + FinOps + SE):
  a) Temporarily restrict tenant concurrency or reduce max_tokens and max_concurrent requests via entitlement config.
  b) If chargeback rules apply, create a cost hold and notify billing.
  c) Analyze request traces to identify runaway loops or bots. Provide sample request IDs to customer.

Escalation matrix (when to escalate to engineering and execs):
- Level 1 (CS + SE): service-impacting but contained, ETA < 4 hours.
- Level 2 (SRE + Model Ops): multi-region impact or stuck routing, ETA < 8 hours.
- Level 3 (VP-eng + Legal + Customer Exec): prolonged outage > 8 hours, data exposure, contract breach risk.

Internal communication templates (use in incident channel and customer emails):
- Initial: "We have observed an operational issue affecting your service. We are investigating and have put temporary mitigations in place. We will provide an update within 30 minutes."
- Update: "Root cause update: [summary]. Current impact: [number of affected requests / %]. Next action: [action]. ETA: [time window]."
- Resolution: "The issue is resolved. Root cause: [summary]. Remediation steps taken: [list]. Postmortem ETA: [date/time]."

Checklist: daily run cadence (days 0–14):
- Day 0–2: entitlement checks, basic telemetry smoke tests, synthetic journeys every 2 hours, billing tag verification.
- Day 3–7: add expanded prompt-set runs, monitor for anomalies in quality and cost, weekly SE tuning session.
- Day 8–14: stability acceptance tests, QBR prep package assembled for customer (see QBR signals below).

QBR signals to prepare for week 2 review (deliverable list):
- Telemetry summary: request volume, latency curves (p50/p95), error rate, token cost per 1k tokens.
- Prompt-set evaluation results (pass/fail counts and examples).
- Entitlement verification report (actual vs contracted limits).
- Incidents and remediation log (timeline, impact, and customer-facing notes).
- Recommended changes: capacity, batching, or model variant suggestions.

Related runbooks & links:
- tenant-observability-contract-lifecycle (link internal)
- canary-simulation-and-auto-alert-playbook (link internal)
- model-switchover-fallback-triage-runbook (link internal)

Appendix: common commands and API snippets
- Validate entitlement API:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/TENANT_ID/entitlements

- Remove tenant from pool (control-plane):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","action":"remove_from_pool"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/route

- Rollback model (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","route":"default","model_hash":"<previous_hash>"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/rollout

Concluding notes:
This runbook is iterative. During onboarding of new enterprise tenants, please capture any new failure modes in the ticket stub below and propose additions to this document. Maintain a record of all customer-facing messages in the tenant's go-live folder for audit and QBR preparation.

Audit ticket stub (copy into JIRA/Ticket):
- Tenant: TENANT_ID
- Onboarded by: <CS lead>
- Start date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Key incidents (summary, timestamps, owner)
- Actions taken and follow-ups
- Postmortem link (if applicable)
