payload.page_title: SLO Governance and Customer Ops QBR Playbook

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines a repeatable SLO governance-centered QBR (Quarterly Business Review) and associated operational procedures for enterprise customers. It is intended to align Customer Success, SRE, and Account Engineering on what to measure, how to act on regressions, and the cadence for communication during onboarding and steady-state.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: enterprise accounts using Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments that require SLO-driven operational reviews.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), SREs, Account Engineers, Solutions Architects, and Customer stakeholders (technical leads).

High-level principles
---------------------
1. Make QBRs evidence-driven: every recommendation must reference metric trends or incident artifacts.
2. Tie remediation to economic impact (latency/cost/error-rate).
3. Default to short, repeatable actions: small policy changes + measurement cycles.
4. Use the same SLO definitions and dashboards across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to avoid measurement drift.

SLO catalog (recommended defaults)
--------------------------------
| SLO name | Target | Measurement window | Alert threshold | Owner | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| API p95 latency (generation) | < 350ms | 30d rolling | p95 > 450ms for 12h | eng-sre | User latency impacts product UX and token throughput |
| Request success rate (4xx/5xx) | >= 99.6% | 30d rolling | error rate < 99.0% for 6h | customer-success / eng-sre | Core availability for customer integrations |
| Token e2e cost per 1k tokens | <= baseline + 15% | 30d rolling | cost delta > +25% for 7d | customer-success/finance | Prevent billing shocks and ROI regressions |
| Embeddings recall on canonical dataset | >= 92% | 14d rolling | recall < 88% for 3d | applied-ml | Data quality regressions detected early |

Note: For Private deployments, measurement window may be locally configured — ensure telemetry export to centralized metrics when possible.

QBR cadence, agenda, and templates
----------------------------------
Cadence: Quarterly (standard), with accelerated QBRs triggered by:
- Repeated SLO breaches (three alerts in a 30d window)
- Post-migration or major model swap within 30 days
- Customer request following business-impacting event

Standard QBR agenda (60–90 minutes)
1) Welcome, participants, and outcomes (5 mins)
2) Health snapshot: SLOs and trend lines (10 mins)
3) Incident summary and root cause highlights since last QBR (10 mins)
4) Cost & utilization review (10 mins)
5) Model/feature changes and A/B results (10 mins)
6) Action items and owners (15 mins)
7) Open discussion / roadmap alignment (10–20 mins)

QBR slide checklist (deliverables to attach)
- Single-page SLO dashboard (p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput)
- Top 3 incidents with timelines and mitigations
- Cost-per-1000 token trend with annotation of config changes
- SLA/SLO compliance table for the quarter
- Action item register with owner+ETA

Operational playbook: SLO breach -> action path
------------------------------------------------
1. Detection and Triage (0–30 minutes)
   - Auto-alert on relevant channel (PagerDuty or shared Slack #customer-{id}-alerts).
   - Triage lead (SRE on-call) acknowledges within 15 minutes.
   - Quick snapshot: deployment hash, model name, route, region, recent deploys.

2. Short-term mitigation (30–240 minutes)
   - If latency spike: shift traffic to a lower-latency model variant or region (policy: canary fallback).
   - If error-rate spike: enable degraded-response mode (reduce max_tokens, disable streaming) or rollback last deploy.
   - Document mitigations in incident ticket and notify CSM.

3. Root Cause Analysis and Remediation (24–72 hours)
   - Post-incident RCA meeting within 72 hours.
   - Assign engineering/ML owners for code/runtime/model changes.
   - For cost regressions: run per-route costing job and propose batching/quantization changes.

4. QBR escalation and follow-up (quarterly/triggered)
   - If regression persists across measurement windows, schedule an accelerated QBR and include product leadership.

First-90-days operational checklist (onboarding)
------------------------------------------------
- Day 0–7: Account setup, API keys, basic integration test, confirm telemetry ingestion to customer dashboards.
- Day 7–30: Baseline SLO measurement; identify high-frequency routes and token distributions.
- Day 30–60: Apply initial performance optimizations (batching, KV cache hints, model variant routing).
- Day 60–90: Run a QBR-lite with customer stakeholders: show baseline, changes, and next 90-day plan.

Ownership matrix
----------------
| Activity | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Escalation contact |
| On-call triage | eng-sre | account-engineering | Pager duty SRE lead |
| SLO reporting | eng-platform | customer-success | Head of Analytics |
| Cost review | finance | customer-success | Billing ops |
| Model performance | applied-ml | account-engineering | Model onboarding lead |

Required dashboards and reports
------------------------------
- Live SLO dashboard (Grafana): p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, throughput per route/model/region.
- Cost report (daily): cost per route and per 1k tokens (CSV export).
- Embeddings quality (weekly): recall/precision on canonical prompt set.
- Onboarding audit (one-time): integration checklist with timestamps.

Example queries and snippets
---------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: - query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30d])) by (le, route))
sections.heading: Prometheus example (p95 latency over 30d)

sections.body:
- SELECT route, SUM(cost_usd) / (SUM(tokens) / 1000) AS cost_per_1k_tokens
  FROM billing.events
  WHERE account_id = 'ACCOUNT_ID' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY route;

Slack/PD routing conventions
---------------------------
- Channel naming: #cust-{account_short}-alerts, #cust-{account_short}-ops (for runbook comms).
- PagerDuty: use service per product tier; escalate to on-call SRE for Sev>=2.

Customer comms templates
------------------------
- Immediate notification (post-detection)
  Subject: [Action required] {Account} SLO breach - {metric} - {short summary}
  Body: one-paragraph summary + link to incident ticket + expected ETA for mitigation.

- QBR invite template: include SLO snapshot and pre-read (2 slides). Request 30 minutes pre-brief with CSM + SRE.

Change policy for QBR recommendations
------------------------------------
- All QBR recommendations must include: technical owner, expected impact (metric delta), risk classification (low/medium/high), rollout plan, and rollback plan.
- Low-risk changes (config tweaks) can be executed by Account Engineering after CSM approval.
- Medium/high risk changes require a documented canary and SRE sign-off.

Post-QBR follow-up and tracking
-------------------------------
- Action items auto-created in Jira with labels: qbr/{account}/{quarter}. Owners update status weekly.
- CSM sends a 10-day check-in email summarizing progress on action items.
- Persistent items roll into the next QBR with additional monitoring.

Appendix: Example action register (CSV-friendly)
------------------------------------------------
- columns: action_id, account_id, short_description, owner, due_date, status, notes
- sample row: QBR-2024-07-001, ACCOUNT_123, "Reduce p95 by 40ms with KV cache hinting", account-eng-jane, 2024-08-10, in-progress, "Canary rolling now"

Appendix: Common recovery patterns and estimated times
------------------------------------------------------
- Traffic reroute to fall-back model variant: 5–20 minutes (automation + validation).
- Rollback to previous deployment: 10–30 minutes (depends on stateful caches).
- Apply batching/kv-cache tuning: 1–3 days (measure then iterate).

Contacts and escalation roster
-----------------------------
- Customer Success lead: Asha Mehta (asha@redwood.ai)
- SRE on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (link)
- Account Engineering: ae-oncall@redwood.ai

Change log
----------
- 2024-05-10: Created playbook (Asha Mehta).
- 2024-11-14: Added cost-per-1k token guidance and SQL example (Liam Chen).
- 2025-02-03: Clarified QBR cadence and added accelerated-QBR triggers (Sofia Patel).

payload.page_title: Slack Bridge and Incident Channel Conventions (Support Escalations)

sections.body: This page standardizes **how Support starts and runs a Slack bridge** for customer-impacting escalations, and how/when we transition the conversation into **#incidents**.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Reduce time-to-triage by ensuring every bridge starts with complete context.
- Ensure Engineering/SRE can take action quickly without back-and-forth.
- Keep Jira (SUP tickets) and Slack synchronized so escalations are discoverable after the bridge ends.
- Ensure **one owner** is accountable for customer-facing updates (email / ticket / status page).
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Replace the company incident process. If an issue meets incident criteria, we transition to #incidents and follow the incident playbook.

---
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
- **Support bridge:** A short-lived Slack channel created by Support to coordinate triage/mitigation for a customer escalation.
- **Incident channel:** A channel created/owned under **#incidents** conventions for cross-functional incident response.
- **SUP ticket:** Jira ticket in the Customer Support project (e.g., SUP-1842).

---
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
Start a Support bridge when **any** of the following are true:
1) Potential **P0/P1** (see severity matrix) or escalating customer pressure.
2) Multiple reports suggest broader impact (same endpoint/model/region).
3) You need synchronous collaboration with SRE/Platform/Runtime to unblock mitigation.
4) A workaround requires coordinated comms and verification.

Do **not** start a bridge for routine troubleshooting if async triage in the SUP ticket is sufficient.

---
sections.heading: When to start a Support bridge

sections.body: Use consistent, searchable names.
sections.heading: Channel naming conventions

sections.body: - `#sup-bridge-<sup_id>-<short-topic>-<region>`
sections.heading: Format

sections.body:
- `#sup-bridge-sup-1842-streaming-resets-us-east`
- `#sup-bridge-sup-1850-embeddings-timeouts-eu-west`
sections.heading: Examples

sections.body:
- Use the **primary SUP ticket** as the anchor.
- Keep `<short-topic>` under ~20 characters (abbreviate if needed).
- Include region when relevant (`us-east`, `eu-west`, `ap-sg`).
sections.heading: Guidelines

sections.body:
Transition to an incident channel with the incident naming standard (managed by incident tooling / SRE). The Support bridge can remain open for customer-specific comms, but decision-making and technical coordination should move to the incident channel.

---
sections.heading: If it becomes an incident

sections.body: Immediately after creating the channel, post the **Bridge Kickoff Template** below. This is required for paging/on-call engagement.
sections.heading: Required context (must be posted in the first message)

sections.body:
**Summary (1–2 sentences):**
-

**Customer impact:**
- Tier: (self_serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)
- Deployment: (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Region(s):
- Endpoint(s): (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank, etc.)
- Affected model(s) + version pinning (if any):
- Blast radius: (single customer / multiple customers suspected)

**Severity (Support P0–P4):**
- Proposed priority:
- Why (symptoms + business impact):

**Timing:**
- Start time (approx):
- Still ongoing? (Y/N)

**Symptoms / errors:**
- Error codes/messages:
- % failure / latency impact (if known):

**Artifacts (do not paste sensitive payloads):**
- Request IDs (3–10 examples):
- Correlation IDs / Trace IDs (if available):
- SDK + version (and language):
- Client environment: (cloud/provider, VPC?, proxy?)

**What we’ve tried (and results):**
-

**Links:**
- Jira: SUP-____ (primary) + related SUPs
- Dashboard(s):
- Known issue / workaround link (if applicable):

**Ask:**
- What do you need from Eng/SRE right now? (e.g., confirm degradation, enable mitigation, validate workaround)
sections.heading: Bridge Kickoff Template (copy/paste)

sections.body:
- Do **not** paste customer secrets, tokens, full prompts, or production payloads.
- Prefer request IDs and sanitized error snippets.
- If logs are needed, follow the Support intake checklist for customer-safe collection.

---
sections.heading: Notes on safe sharing

sections.body: Invite only what you need, but ensure the minimum set is present.
sections.heading: Required participants (who to invite)

sections.body:
- **Support owner (Bridge Lead):** the person who created the bridge (default).
- **On-call Eng/SRE (as applicable):** based on product area and symptoms.
- **CSM (for Enterprise/Dedicated/Private):** to manage customer expectations and align comms.
sections.heading: Minimum set

sections.body:
- **SRE**: suspected regional degradation, elevated errors/latency, capacity/routing/fallback behavior, multi-customer impact.
- **Platform**: auth/SSO, quota/rate limit enforcement, audit logs, control plane workflows, console access.
- **Serving Runtime**: streaming disconnects, runtime regressions, model-specific failures.
- **Dedicated/Capacity**: autoscaling oscillation, burst capacity issues, GPU pool saturation.
- **Docs/DevEx**: if we are validating or publishing a workaround/KB article during the incident.
sections.heading: Add based on issue type

sections.body:
When you page or request on-call help, include:
- SUP ticket link
- Channel link
- 3–10 request IDs
- Region + endpoint + model
- “What’s the ask” (confirm issue? mitigation? rollback? routing policy?)

---
sections.heading: Escalation expectation (paging hygiene)

sections.body: Slack bridges must be anchored in Jira to preserve context and support SLA tracking.
sections.heading: Jira linking requirements (SUP tickets)

sections.body:
- Pick the earliest/highest severity ticket that best represents the issue.
- If multiple customers are affected, keep separate SUP tickets per customer, but designate a single “primary” for the bridge.
sections.heading: 1) Choose a primary SUP ticket

sections.body:
- Add the Slack channel URL in the designated field (per Jira field guidelines).
- Add it to the ticket description under **“Links”** if a dedicated field isn’t available.
sections.heading: In the primary SUP ticket

sections.body:
- Pin the primary SUP ticket link.
- Also pin dashboards and any approved workaround/KB link.
sections.heading: In the bridge channel

sections.body:
During the bridge, the Bridge Lead is responsible for:
- Adding a short timestamped summary of major decisions (mitigation enabled, rollback, routing change, customer workaround provided).
- Capturing next update time and owner.
sections.heading: 4) Keep Jira updated with decision-quality notes

sections.body:
Incident tooling and automations are expected to prompt/pin SUP links during bridge creation (see internal automation work: Slack workflow updates and Jira reminders).

---
sections.heading: Tooling note

sections.body: A Support bridge is appropriate for **customer-specific escalations** or early triage. Move to #incidents when the situation is broader or requires formal incident management.
sections.heading: When to move from a Support bridge to #incidents

sections.body:
- Suspected **multi-customer** or multi-region impact.
- Error rate or latency suggests a **service degradation/outage**.
- You need coordinated rollback/mitigation that affects production systems.
- You anticipate needing a status page update.
- You need a structured incident commander (IC) + comms lead roles.
sections.heading: Move to #incidents if any are true

sections.body:
1) Bridge Lead posts: “Escalating to #incidents due to <reason>.”
2) Create/join the incident channel (per incident process).
3) Post a short context handoff message in the incident channel (reuse the kickoff template; keep it tight).
4) Update the primary SUP ticket:
   - Link the incident channel.
   - Note that technical coordination has moved to the incident.
5) Keep the Support bridge open only if needed for customer-specific coordination; otherwise archive after resolution.

---
sections.heading: Transition process (do this fast; don’t debate in the moment)

sections.body: Clarity on “who does what” prevents dropped comms and duplicated work.
sections.heading: Roles and ownership during a bridge

sections.body:
- Post kickoff template and keep pins updated.
- Ensure Jira is linked and updated with key decisions.
- Drive the “next action / next update time” cadence.
- Decide when to escalate to #incidents (in partnership with on-call).
sections.heading: Responsibilities

sections.body:
- Own investigation plan and technical mitigation.
- Confirm whether symptoms match known issues.
- Provide customer-safe explanation of root cause hypothesis and mitigation status.
sections.heading: Responsibilities

sections.body:
- **Support** owns customer updates in the SUP ticket for Hosted/self-serve.
- **CSM** owns customer updates for Dedicated/Private/Enterprise accounts, with Support support.
sections.heading: Default owner

sections.body:
- There must be exactly **one** named comms owner per escalation.
- The comms owner drafts and sends updates; Eng/SRE provides approved technical language.
- Status page updates follow the comms alignment guidance and required approvals.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
If exec escalation triggers are met, follow the executive escalation protocol. Do not ad-hoc loop executives into a bridge without using the defined summary template.

---
sections.heading: Executive escalation

sections.body:
- **P0/P1:** Post an internal bridge update at least every **30 minutes** until stable mitigation is in place (even if the update is “still investigating”).
- **P2+:** At least every **60–120 minutes** during active investigation.
sections.heading: Update cadence inside the bridge

sections.body:
- What changed since last update
- Current hypothesis
- Next action + owner
- Next internal update time
- Customer update plan (if applicable)

---
sections.heading: Each update should include

sections.body:
1) Ensure the primary SUP ticket has:
   - Final resolution summary
   - Mitigation steps taken
   - Customer-facing explanation (approved)
   - Links to incident review (if any)
   - Follow-up engineering tasks (Linear links) and owners
2) If a workaround was used:
   - Link the KB article (or create a doc task if missing)
   - Mark whether workaround is temporary and what “done” looks like
3) Post a final Slack message:
   - “Resolved at <time>”
   - What customers should do (if anything)
   - Where ongoing tracking lives (SUP/incident/Linear)

---
sections.heading: Before archiving the channel

sections.body:
**Q: Can we keep everything in #support instead of creating a bridge channel?**
A: No for P0/P1 or when paging is involved. The dedicated bridge channel + template reduces time-to-triage and keeps escalation artifacts organized.

**Q: Who decides if this becomes a formal incident?**
A: The Support Bridge Lead should propose escalation; on-call SRE/Eng confirms and helps initiate the incident process. When in doubt, escalate.

**Q: Can Support post on the status page?**
A: Follow the customer incident comms alignment guidance. Status updates require the defined approval flow; Support/CS should not unilaterally post.
sections.heading: FAQ

payload.page_title: Support SLA Policy by Customer Tier (Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Enterprise)

sections.body:
This page defines Redwood Inference Support SLAs by customer tier (Self-serve Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Enterprise). It standardizes:
- **First response targets** (time to first human acknowledgement)
- **Update cadence** (how often we provide meaningful progress updates)
- **Escalation thresholds** (when Support must page Engineering/SRE and/or start a bridge)
- **After-hours policy** (what is covered 24/7 vs business-hours only)
- **Credits requests & contract exceptions** (how to handle safely and consistently)

**Important:** These are *internal operating targets* and default policies. If a customer contract includes custom SLAs/terms, the contract governs. When in doubt, follow the “Contract exceptions” section and engage Legal/CS leadership.

---
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- **Tier**: support coverage and targets based on a customer’s commercial plan.
- **Priority (P0–P4)**: Support ticket priority (see severity rubric for examples and mapping to incident severity).
- **First response**: a human response confirming receipt + requesting any missing diagnostics + stating next update time.
- **Update**: a non-empty change (new findings, mitigation, ETA change, or explicit “no change; still investigating; next update at X”).
- **Business hours (BH)**: Mon–Fri, 09:00–17:00 in the customer’s primary region where possible (default: PT for North America customers, GMT for EMEA customers). If a team member is not staffed for that timezone, use PT and note it in the first response.

---
sections.heading: Definitions (quick)

sections.body:
- Typical: PLG / pay-as-you-go Hosted API customers.
- Coverage: **Business hours** (BH) default.
sections.heading: Self-serve (Hosted API)

sections.body:
- Reserved capacity customers (dedicated GPU pools, SLA-backed performance/uptime terms).
- Coverage: **24/7 for P0/P1**, BH for P2–P4.
sections.heading: Dedicated

sections.body:
- VPC and/or on-prem deployments (regulated environments, customer-managed networking).
- Coverage: **24/7 for P0/P1**, BH for P2–P4.
sections.heading: Private

sections.body:
- Enterprise plan customers (may be Hosted, Dedicated, and/or Private) with contract terms and executive visibility.
- Coverage: **24/7 for P0/P1**, BH for P2–P4 (unless contract states otherwise).

---
sections.heading: Enterprise

sections.body: Use this table after setting ticket priority per the severity rubric.
sections.heading: SLA targets by tier and priority

sections.body:
> If a ticket spans multiple systems (e.g., Hosted API + Console + billing), set priority to the *highest-impact* issue and coordinate internally; do not create separate parallel customer threads.

| Priority | Typical impact (summary) | Self-serve (Hosted API) | Dedicated | Private | Enterprise |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **P0** | Service down, major security/compliance risk, or severe degradation with broad impact | **First response:** 1 hour (BH) \| **Updates:** every 2 hours (BH) \| **Bridge:** if multi-customer/widespread | **First response:** 15 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 30 min (24/7) \| **Bridge:** start within 15 min | **First response:** 15 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 30 min (24/7) \| **Bridge:** start within 15 min | **First response:** 15 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 30 min (24/7) \| **Bridge:** start within 15 min |
| **P1** | Material feature outage or high error/latency impacting core workloads; workaround may exist but isn’t acceptable for most users | **First response:** 4 hours (BH) \| **Updates:** daily (BH) or when material change | **First response:** 30 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 60 min while actively mitigating (24/7) | **First response:** 30 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 60 min while actively mitigating (24/7) | **First response:** 30 min (24/7) \| **Updates:** every 60 min while actively mitigating (24/7) |
| **P2** | Degradation with partial workaround; isolated region/model; limited subset of users | **First response:** 1 business day \| **Updates:** every 2 business days | **First response:** 4 hours (BH) \| **Updates:** daily (BH) | **First response:** 4 hours (BH) \| **Updates:** daily (BH) | **First response:** 2 hours (BH) \| **Updates:** daily (BH) |
| **P3** | Minor issue, question, documentation/UX confusion; low business impact | **First response:** 2 business days \| **Updates:** weekly or upon change | **First response:** 1 business day \| **Updates:** weekly or upon change | **First response:** 1 business day \| **Updates:** weekly or upon change | **First response:** 1 business day \| **Updates:** weekly or upon change |
| **P4** | How-to requests, enhancement asks, non-urgent follow-ups | **First response:** 5 business days \| **Updates:** as available | **First response:** 2 business days \| **Updates:** as available | **First response:** 2 business days \| **Updates:** as available | **First response:** 2 business days \| **Updates:** as available |
sections.heading: Table A — First response and update cadence

sections.body:
- For **Dedicated/Private/Enterprise P0/P1**, updates are expected **even if Engineering is still investigating**. Support owns keeping the customer looped in.
- For **Self-serve**, Support does not run 24/7 coverage. If a Self-serve incident is **widespread** (multiple customers, multi-region, status-page-worthy), Support should follow the incident process and escalation triggers below.

---
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body: Escalations must follow the escalation playbook and severity rubric. The goal is to page consistently with Engineering/SRE on-call expectations and avoid ad-hoc bypassing.
sections.heading: Escalation thresholds (paging + bridges)

sections.body:
| Priority | Self-serve (Hosted API) | Dedicated | Private | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Escalate if any of: (1) multi-customer impact, (2) region-wide degradation, (3) auth/outage patterns, (4) safety/compliance concern. Start Support bridge and move to **#incidents** if it qualifies as an incident. | **Page immediately** per routing matrix. Start Support bridge within 15 min. If SRE declares incident, move to **#incidents**. | **Page immediately** to Private Deployments/Platform on-call + SRE as needed. Start bridge within 15 min. | **Page immediately** + notify CS lead. Start bridge within 15 min. Consider executive escalation protocol if revenue/brand risk is high. |
| **P1** | Escalate if: sustained errors/latency beyond 30 minutes affecting multiple customers OR no meaningful next step after 1 BH. | Escalate if no mitigation path within 60 min or if dashboard signals indicate continued customer impact. | Escalate if mitigation requires config change/rollback or installer/deploy actions beyond Support playbooks. | Escalate if customer indicates business-critical impact, legal/compliance risk, or explicit SLA language invoked. |
| **P2–P4** | Escalate only when: reproducible product defect with clear evidence, or repeated tickets indicate a known issue needing publication, or safety/compliance concerns. | Escalate when repeated impact or no progress for >2 BH and customer’s workload is at risk. | Escalate when there is risk of customer environment instability or unsafe change guidance. | Escalate when there is contract/SLA interpretation needed or customer pressure requires leadership alignment. |
sections.heading: Table B — When Support must escalate beyond standard triage

sections.body:
Support should not guess incident state solely from a single ticket. Use available signals:
- **Error rate / gateway errors:** sudden spikes in 5xx, connection resets, or 429 patterns correlated across customers.
- **Latency:** p95/p99 deviation from baseline with confirmed customer impact.
- **Routing / fallback:** any evidence of fallback activation that contradicts customer expectations (e.g., model pinning concerns) should be validated using the routing/fallback metrics.
- **Region scope:** if multiple regions show correlated symptoms, treat as potential incident.

When escalating, include the required context template (request IDs, region, model/version, SDK version, timeframe, and any recent deploys).

---
sections.heading: Signal-based escalation guidance (use with the severity rubric)

sections.body:
- **Dedicated/Private/Enterprise:**
  - **P0/P1:** covered **24/7** for acknowledgement, coordination, and customer updates.
  - **P2–P4:** handled during **business hours** unless explicitly upgraded to P0/P1.
- **Self-serve:**
  - Default is **business hours only**.
  - If a widespread incident is detected after-hours via monitoring/on-call processes, incident response proceeds through Engineering/SRE. Support will provide customer updates when staffed; do not promise 24/7 comms for Self-serve.
sections.heading: What Support covers after-hours

sections.body:
- Use the escalation playbook handoff rules: summarize current state, what changed since last update, customer impact statement, and next actions.
- Pin the customer-impact summary in the bridge channel and keep Jira updated so the next shift can continue without re-triage.

---
sections.heading: Handoffs and continuity

sections.body:
- If **additional customer info is required** (logs, request IDs, reproduction), set status to **Waiting on Customer** in Jira.
- Post a clear ask with:
  - exact fields needed (e.g., request IDs, timestamps, region, model/version)
  - why it’s needed
  - a suggested safe way to share (no secrets; redact tokens)
- **SLA clock policy (internal):** While Waiting on Customer, we do not count the period toward “next update due,” but we still send a reminder per tier:
  - Enterprise/Dedicated/Private: remind after **1 business day** (or sooner for P1)
  - Self-serve: remind after **2 business days**
- If the customer responds with partial info, move back to **In Progress** and re-commit to the next update time.

---
sections.heading: To avoid SLA confusion and missed comms

sections.body:
- Do **not** promise credits in a Support ticket.
- Credits decisions depend on: contract terms, measured impact, prior credits, and Finance/CS approvals.
- Support’s responsibility is to provide an accurate timeline and impact summary and route the request correctly.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
Route to CS lead / account team when any of the following are true:
- Customer explicitly requests credits or references an SLA breach.
- Incident is P0 and there is clear unavailability/degradation beyond SLO targets.
- Enterprise account signals renewal risk due to operational impact.
sections.heading: When to route for credits consideration

sections.body:
- Ticket ID(s) and incident/bridge link
- Affected product surface (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region(s), model(s)
- Impact window (start/end time in UTC) and customer-confirmed symptoms
- Mitigation steps attempted and final resolution state
- Comms timeline (first response time, update cadence adherence)
- Any contractual notes (if known) + link to CRM record
sections.heading: Include in the internal escalation summary

sections.body:
- **Enterprise/Dedicated/Private:** CS lead (Rachel Kim or delegate) + **VP CS (Jasmine Liu)** approval; Finance/legal review if contract language is involved.
- **Self-serve:** typically handled via standard billing/support policy; escalate only for exceptional cases.

---
sections.heading: Approval path (default)

sections.body:
1. Confirm the terms via the account team (CSM/AE) and/or the contract repository.
2. Add a note in CRM and link it in the Jira ticket.
3. Follow the stricter of (a) contract requirement or (b) this policy.
4. If interpretation is unclear, escalate to CS leadership and Legal (Sofia Mendes) before committing to specific numbers in customer-facing communication.

**Operational note:** Customers may describe expectations informally (“we need 15-minute updates”). Only commit to an update cadence if it is (a) aligned with tier policy/contract and (b) realistically supportable with the current incident state.

---
sections.heading: If a customer has a custom SLA or special coverage terms

sections.body:
- Use comms templates and keep language consistent between:
  - Support email responses
  - Slack bridge summaries (internal)
  - Status page updates (if applicable)
- Always include:
  - current impact statement
  - what we’re doing now
  - what customers can do (workaround if validated)
  - next update time

See the incident comms alignment page for when to post a status event vs a docs banner vs a console alert.

---
sections.heading: For P0/P1 incidents

sections.body:
1. Set **Priority (P0–P4)** using the severity rubric.
2. Confirm **tier** (Self-serve / Dedicated / Private / Enterprise) and document it in Jira.
3. Commit to **first response** and **next update time** per Table A.
4. If escalation threshold is met, follow Table B:
   - create bridge channel (per conventions)
   - page correct on-call group
   - link/pin Jira ticket(s)
5. Keep Jira current with: timestamps, mitigation attempts, and customer-visible summary.
6. If credits are requested, route internally with the required timeline summary.

---
sections.heading: Operational checklist for Support (per ticket)

sections.body:
- **2026-02-15:** Clarified P0/P1 update cadence language (30 min vs 60 min) and standardized after-hours coverage notes; added explicit “Waiting on Customer” reminder policy.
- **2026-02-10:** Added contract exception workflow and credits approvals guidance.
- **2026-02-06:** Initial publication as part of escalation playbook refresh.
sections.heading: Changelog

payload.page_title: Rapid SLA Triage Runbook and External Briefing Templates

sections.body: This document defines a compact, operator-focused runbook for rapid triage of SLA-impacting events (availability, latency, throughput regressions) and provides tested external briefing templates for customers and execs. It is optimized for the first 30/60/180 minutes of an incident where the primary goal is to stabilize SLAs and communicate clearly.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Scope: multi-region inference control plane and serving stack (hosted API + Dedicated routing).
- Non-scope: billing pipeline, long-term capacity planning (see related pages).
- Intent: provide a predictable, low-cognitive triage path that on-call responders, bridge operators, and customer success can adopt with minimal prep.
sections.heading: Scope and intent

sections.body:
- SLA-impacting: any event causing a measurable drop below an SLO threshold for availability or 95th/99th latency for a paid customer tier.
- Triage Owner: primary on-call for the service indicated by PagerDuty alert tag (e.g., inference-runtime-prod).
- Bridge Lead: SRE on the active bridge who owns external comms until handed to Customer Success.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
| Metric                     | Target        | Alert threshold (auto-trigger) | PagerDuty severity |
|---------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------|--------------------|
| API availability (global) | 99.95% monthly| < 99.9% (15m window)          | Sev 1              |
| 95th latency (text gen)   | < 300ms       | > 350ms (5m window)           | Sev 2              |
| 99th latency (embeds)     | < 1200ms      | > 1600ms (10m window)         | Sev 1              |
| Error rate (5m)           | < 0.1%        | > 0.5%                        | Sev 1              |
sections.heading: SLO thresholds (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Triage Owner: fix-forward actions, log collection, scope.
- Bridge Lead: status cadence, external messages.
- Model/Serving Owner: kernel/quantization teams for model regressions.
- CS Liaison: customer notices and ticket updates.

Rapid SLA Triage: 0–30 minutes (stabilize & estimate)
1) Acknowledge and create the bridge (Triage Owner / Bridge Lead):
   - Create an incident bridge: #oncall-bridge-<service>-<ts>. Invite CS and PM if > 30 customers impacted.
   - Confirm severity via the SLO dashboard and metric snapshot.
2) Immediate controls (first 5–10 minutes):
   - Apply emergency mitigation(s) prioritized by lowest-customer-impact first:
     a) Route traffic to healthy region: runbook command: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/routing/shift -d '{"region":"us-west-2","service":"inference"}'
     b) Temporarily increase fallback model capacity: ops-cli models set-capacity --model redwood-v1-small --pool dedicated --scale 2
     c) Toggle caching layer to read-only mode to reduce write pressure: redis-cli -h cache-main CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
3) Rapid evidence capture (parallel):
   - Export traces for 15 minutes around alert:
     - tracing-cli export --service inference-runtime --since "-15m" --out /tmp/trace-<incident>.zip
   - Grab top error logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-runtime --tail=500 > /tmp/errors-<incident>.log
   - Snapshot autoscaler and pool metrics: ops-monitor snapshot --pools inference* --out /tmp/pools-<incident>.json
4) Estimate impact & ETA (10–20 minutes):
   - Use dashboard: open /dashboards/slo-latency?window=15m and capture 1m/5m/15m deltas.
   - Bridge Lead gives initial ETA: stabilize estimate (e.g., 30m) and next update cadence (10m).

Triage: 30–60 minutes (diagnose & mitigate)
5) Narrow root cause hypotheses (30–45 minutes):
   - Common buckets: noisy neighbor (GPU saturation), kernel regression (recent runtime release), networking (regional AZ issues), model size/kv-cache eviction.
   - Quick checks: GPU utilization (nvidia-smi via fleet-agent), kernel-level error traces, and latest deploy tags: git rev-parse --short HEAD on runtime node.
6) Apply scoped mitigations (45–60 minutes):
   - If deployment suspect: rollback runtime: ops-deploy rollback inference-runtime --to-tag v2025.04.12 || kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime -n inference
   - If noisy neighbor: isolate offending instance pool and evict pods: kubectl cordon <node>; drain --ignore-daemonsets
   - If model quality regression: route traffic to previous model variant and throttle new variant: ops-cli models route --from new-variant --to old-variant --weight 0.9
7) Confirm SLO recovery and document evidence (60 minutes):
   - Once SLOs back above alert thresholds for 15m window, declare partial mitigation. Capture recovery artifact IDs and evidence bundles.

Escalation ladder and when to involve execs (decision rules):
- Escalate to on-call manager & PM if: 2 hours elapsed with no sustained SLO recovery or > 5% of paid customers impacted.
- Engage Legal/Comms if incident is customer data exposure or regulatory risk.
- For cross-region outages, engage Cloud Ops and network providers immediately.

Customer and executive briefing templates (copyable)
- Initial acknowledgement (within 10 minutes):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting inference API — we’re investigating
  Body: Hello — we are aware of an issue affecting inference API performance for some customers. Our engineers have opened an incident and are investigating root cause. We're prioritizing SLA stability and will provide an update by <ETA in minutes>. Bridge ID: #oncall-bridge-inference-<ts>.

- Status update (10/30/60 minute cadence):
  Subject: [Redwood] Update — inference API incident — progress update
  Body: Current status: Mitigations in progress (routing changes / temporary capacity increases). Impact: X% of requests affected; primary symptom: increased 95th/99th latency. Next update: in 20 minutes. For urgent support, reply to this message or open a support ticket: <link>.

- Resolution notice (post-stabilization):
  Subject: [Redwood] Resolved — inference API incident — summary and next steps
  Body: The incident affecting inference API performance has been resolved as of <timestamp>. Root cause: <brief cause>. Actions taken: list of mitigations/rollbacks and timeline. Customer impact: estimated duration and affected customers. If you saw persistent issues, please contact your CS rep. We will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours.

- Executive brief (if escalated):
  - One-line: Major SLA-impacting incident affecting inference API, partial customer impact, mitigation in place.
  - Metrics snapshot: availability pre/post, peak error rate, affected regions.
  - Next steps: timeline for RCA, compensatory credit assessment, and product/infra remediation plan.
sections.heading: Ownership matrix (quick)

sections.body:
- Objectives: validate bridge process, verify external templates, practice three mitigations (route shift, runtime rollback, pool isolation).
- Participants: SRE, runtime team, CS, PM, legal (optional).
- Pre-reqs: synthetic load harness, shadow customer, snapshot restore point.
- Day-of script: 1) Inject latency to us-west-2 pool. 2) Trigger pager and follow the 0–60 minute runbook. 3) Time each step, capture gaps.
sections.heading: Game day and simulation checklist (pre-run)

sections.body:
- Primary on-call should be reachable for 15 minutes for SEV1 pages and start bridge within 10 minutes.
- Handoff template (two lines): current active mitigations; next steps; outstanding manual actions.
- Shadow to primary progression: shadow for 3 rotations, then co-take for 2, then primary.

Post-incident writeup / evidence checklist (what to attach to the postmortem):
- Incident timeline with wall-clock stamps.
- Evidence bundle IDs (traces, logs, snapshots).
- Root cause hypothesis and confirmation steps.
- Customer impact list and support ticket IDs.
- Action items (owner + due date) and severity remediations (quick/medium/long term).
sections.heading: On-call rotation guidance (practical rules)

sections.body:
- Check SLOs: curl -s "https://ops-monitor.internal/api/v1/slo?service=inference&window=5m" | jq .
- Route traffic to a region (API): curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/routing/shift -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"service":"inference","target_region":"eu-west-1","drain_seconds":30}'
- Runtime rollback (k8s): kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision=3
- Snapshot traces: tracing-cli export --service inference-runtime --since "-30m" --out s3://incidents/trace-<id>.zip
sections.heading: Technical play snippets and commands (copy/paste)

sections.body:
- Every play must have a single owner listed in the runbook header (owner_name@example.com). Owners must review the play annually and after any SEV1 incident.
- After each game day run, update the playbook with any temporary hacks that became standard operating practice or remove them if unsafe.
sections.heading: Runbook maintenance and ownership rules

sections.body:
- 2024-11-05: Adopted 10/30/60 minute cadence as default for SLA incidents.
- 2025-03-18: Added customer-facing templates and mandatory CS liaison for incidents > 30m.
sections.heading: Decision log (quick ADR entries for this playbook)

sections.body:
- SLO library (link): /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Incident evidence standard: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-collection-standard-2025.json

Appendix: Example customer acknowledgement (multi-tenant sample)
---
Hello <CustomerName>,

We detected elevated latency for inference requests affecting some tenants between <start> and <end>. Our engineers mitigated the issue by shifting traffic and performing a controlled rollback. We estimate <percent> of your requests were affected for <duration>. A detailed post-incident report will follow.

Regards,
The Redwood Inference Reliability Team
---
sections.heading: Related artifacts and page links

sections.body:
- Keep this runbook concise — long investigations belong in the postmortem.
- If you're unsure which mitigations to use, prioritize actions that reduce customer-visible impact over full root-cause proof.

Maintenance log: last reviewed by Maya Chen on 2025-06-12.
