payload.page_title: Dedicated Throughput SLO Escalation Playbook

sections.body:
This playbook defines the end-to-end process for handling Dedicated **Throughput SLO** misses or suspected misses. It is designed for Customer Success (CS) and Support to:
- Triage quickly and consistently.
- Engage the correct on-call teams (SRE / Infra / Observability) at the right time.
- Communicate clearly with customers, including status updates and written summaries.
- Route service-credit / compensation requests through the correct approval path.

This page is **restricted** because it includes internal paging triggers and credit approval guidance.

---
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
Dedicated Throughput SLO guarantees a **minimum sustained throughput floor** for an eligible Dedicated deployment under defined conditions.

**High-level definition (internal summary):**
- Metric: throughput measured as **billable output tokens per second**, computed per deployment, aggregated over a rolling window.
- Scope: Dedicated deployments only (not Hosted API, not eval/sandbox deployments).
- Eligibility: model/version and configuration must be within the customer’s contracted Dedicated configuration (e.g., pinned model family/version, supported max context, supported shape).

**Common non-eligibility / exclusions (not exhaustive):**
- Customer-side throttling or client concurrency limits causing underutilization.
- Customer workload violating sizing assumptions (e.g., contexts above configured limit, unsupported parameter combinations).
- Warm-up periods after scale-from-zero or cold start (tier-dependent; see “Warm pool / startup” below).
- Incidents due to customer networking/VPC misconfig in Private connectivity paths (if applicable).

When in doubt, treat as potentially eligible, start the triage, and engage SRE.

---
sections.heading: What is the Dedicated Throughput SLO (customer-facing summary)

sections.body:
**Support/CS (Incident Driver for customer comms)**
- Owns the customer thread, updates, and expectation management.
- Owns the case record: timeline, impact, and customer confirmations.
- Initiates escalation and ensures correct teams are engaged.

**SRE On-Call (Technical Incident Lead)**
- Confirms whether the SLO is breached per the canonical evaluator.
- Drives mitigation and coordinates cross-functional response.
- Provides internal/external technical summary for comms.

**Infra/Fleet On-Call (Capacity / shape / provisioning owner)**
- Addresses capacity constraints, noisy-neighbor isolation issues, node failures, and shape-level performance anomalies.

**Observability (as-needed)**
- Validates metric correctness (e.g., streaming accounting anomalies), dashboard discrepancies, missing tags.

**Product Dedicated (as-needed)**
- Confirms entitlement interpretation (tier rules, burst policy, failover posture).
- Aligns on customer-facing messaging for edge cases.

**Finance/FP&A + Legal (as-needed for credits/comp)**
- Approves service credits above policy thresholds and any non-standard compensation.

---
sections.heading: Roles and ownership during an SLO event

sections.body:
Use these severities to standardize response; SRE may map to their incident severities.

**SEV-1 (Critical, likely customer-impacting breach)**
- Premium tier customer reports sustained throughput below floor OR SRE burn-rate alert is firing.
- Clear production impact (e.g., queue buildup, timeouts, user-visible latency spikes).
- Immediate paging required.

**SEV-2 (High, likely degradation / at-risk of breach)**
- Throughput is below expected but not yet confirmed as an SLO breach.
- Customer impact is moderate OR limited to a subset of traffic/routes.
- Paging may be required depending on tier and duration.

**SEV-3 (Moderate, investigation / metrics discrepancy)**
- Conflicting metrics (customer vs Redwood dashboards), short-lived dips, or suspected measurement artifacts.
- No clear production impact.

---
sections.heading: Severity levels (Support/CS view)

sections.body:
- Premium tier customer: reported throughput below committed floor for **>10 minutes**, AND they confirm they are not client-throttled.
- Any tier: a Dedicated Throughput SLO **burn-rate alert** is firing for the deployment.
- Any tier: repeated or escalating customer timeouts/5xx correlated with throughput drop.
- Any tier: throughput drop correlates with recent Redwood changes (rollout, routing, driver/runtime update).
sections.heading: Page SRE On-Call immediately when any of the following is true

sections.body:
- GPU/node health signals indicate failures, evictions, ECC errors, or repeated container restarts.
- Saturation: GPU utilization pinned while throughput drops (suspected contention, thermal throttling, network bottleneck).
- Capacity: the deployment appears mapped to the wrong pool/shape or lacks the expected headroom.
- Region-wide capacity constraint impacting Dedicated pools.
sections.heading: Page Infra/Fleet On-Call when any of the following is true (often in parallel)

sections.body:
- Throughput dashboards disagree with billing/export numbers.
- Recent metric changes (e.g., streaming token accounting) suspected.
- Missing labels (deployment_id, model, region) prevents accurate attribution.

---
sections.heading: Engage Observability (not a page; async unless SEV-1)

sections.body: Perform steps 1–8 before (or while) paging; do not block paging for SEV-1.
sections.heading: Triage checklist (Support/CS)

sections.body:
- Deployment ID(s)
- Customer name + environment (prod/stage)
- Region
- Tier (Standard / Plus / Premium)
- Model + version (exact identifier)
- Shape (if known)
- Time window of impact (with timezone)
- Symptoms (queueing, latency, timeouts, functional failure)
sections.heading: Collect

sections.body:
- Current request concurrency
- Any client-side rate limiting (explicit QPS cap, worker pool limit)
- Any recent application deploy or traffic change

If the customer is under-driving load, throughput may be low without being an SLO failure.
sections.heading: Ask

sections.body:
- Context lengths: are they within contracted max context / recommended ranges?
- Parameters: extreme max_tokens or non-streaming vs streaming changes?
- Model/version pin: did they change models recently?
sections.heading: 3) Validate “eligibility” red flags quickly

sections.body:
- Rolling-window throughput vs committed floor
- Error rate/timeout correlation
- GPU saturation, queue depth, admission control shedding
- Recent routing pool changes or failovers
sections.heading: Look for

sections.body:
- Ask what they are measuring (wall-clock end-to-end, tokens counted, streaming vs non-streaming).
- Request a single representative request ID and a 10–20 minute sample window.
sections.heading: If customer numbers differ from Redwood

sections.body:
- One deployment vs multiple
- One region vs multiple
- One model family vs multiple
sections.heading: 6) Determine if the issue is isolated or systemic

sections.body:
These are customer-facing actions CS/Support may propose, with SRE confirmation where possible:
- Temporarily reduce max context / max output tokens (if within acceptable product behavior).
- Temporarily shift traffic to the contracted primary route only (avoid experimental routes).
- Enable/disable streaming based on their client constraints (note: streaming affects perceived latency but should not invalidate throughput).
- If the customer has multi-deployment setup: fail over to a secondary deployment (Premium: may be Redwood-assisted).

Do not promise failover across regions unless the tier/contract explicitly includes it.
sections.heading: 7) Mitigation options you can offer immediately (tier-dependent)

sections.body:
- Create/associate the internal incident ticket.
- Add the customer support ticket link.
- Add a running timeline (timestamps for all key events).

---
sections.heading: 8) Open an incident record (internal) if SEV-1/SEV-2

sections.body:
Some tiers include warm pool guarantees (or faster recovery expectations). During triage, identify if the customer is within a warm-up window:
- Did the deployment recently scale from zero?
- Was there a recent model reload, config change, or node replacement?
- Did traffic resume after prolonged inactivity?

If warm-up is suspected, note it explicitly in the customer thread and ask SRE to confirm whether the event is excluded by policy.

---
sections.heading: Warm pool / startup considerations

sections.body:
- Use a single owner for customer updates (CS/Support), even if multiple engineering teams are engaged.
- Acknowledge impact quickly; avoid speculating on root cause.
- Provide time-bound next update (“next update in 30 minutes”).
- For Premium accounts, default to more frequent updates and written summaries.
sections.heading: Communication principles

sections.body:
- SEV-1: initial response within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes until stable.
- SEV-2: initial response within 1 hour; updates every 2–4 hours until stable.
- SEV-3: initial response within 1 business day; updates daily or as material changes occur.

---
sections.heading: Target update cadence (recommended)

sections.body:
Subject: Dedicated deployment throughput investigation (Deployment {{deployment_id}})

Hi {{customer_name}},

Thanks for flagging this. We’re investigating reduced throughput on your Dedicated deployment ({{deployment_id}}) in {{region}}.

To help us confirm impact and correlate logs/metrics, could you share:
- The approximate start time and whether the issue is ongoing
- The model + version you’re using
- A representative request ID (or a small set) from the impacted window
- Any recent traffic/concurrency changes on your side

We’ll provide the next update by {{time}}.

Best,
{{agent_name}}
sections.heading: Template A — Initial acknowledgement (suspected throughput miss)

sections.body:
Subject: Update: Dedicated throughput degradation (Deployment {{deployment_id}})

Hi {{customer_name}},

We’ve confirmed a throughput degradation affecting your Dedicated deployment ({{deployment_id}}). We’ve engaged our Site Reliability Engineering and Infrastructure on-call teams and are actively mitigating.
sections.heading: Template B — Confirmed incident + engaged on-call
Current status

sections.body:
Subject: Quick check: request load/concurrency for Dedicated deployment {{deployment_id}}

Hi {{customer_name}},

To confirm whether the deployment is being fully utilized during the impacted window, can you confirm:
- Current concurrency / worker count hitting the deployment
- Whether you have any client-side QPS limits or retries/backoff changes
- Whether the workload mix changed (context length, max output tokens, streaming on/off)

This helps us differentiate capacity/perf issues from under-driven traffic.

Thanks,
{{agent_name}}
sections.heading: Template C — Request customer confirmation on throttling / load

sections.body:
Subject: Resolved: Dedicated throughput issue (Deployment {{deployment_id}})

Hi {{customer_name}},

The throughput issue affecting your Dedicated deployment ({{deployment_id}}) is now resolved as of {{resolved_time_utc}}.
sections.heading: Template D — Resolution note + next steps
Summary

sections.body:
Subject: Dedicated throughput incident — service credit review

Hi {{customer_name}},

We can review this incident for service credits under your Dedicated terms. To proceed, we will document:
- Deployment ID(s)
- Impact window (UTC)
- Confirmed SLO measurement from Redwood’s evaluator

We’ll share the outcome of the credit review by {{date}}.

Best,
{{agent_name}}

---
sections.heading: Template E — Service credit intake (do not pre-approve)

sections.body: **Important:** Do not commit to a credit amount in writing until approvals are complete.
sections.heading: Service credits / compensation (internal guidance)

sections.body:
- **Premium:** written throughput commitment; credit review is standard for confirmed breaches.
- **Plus:** may be eligible depending on contract addenda; treat as “review required.”
- **Standard:** generally best-effort; credit requests require Product + Finance approval.
sections.heading: Which tiers are typically credit-eligible?

sections.body:
- SRE confirms an SLO breach per canonical evaluator, AND
- The breach is not excluded (e.g., customer throttling), AND
- The customer requests credits OR the account team recommends proactive review.
sections.heading: Initiate when

sections.body:
1) CS/Support compiles incident details and SRE confirmation.
2) SRE provides breach window + summary.
3) Product Dedicated confirms entitlement interpretation (tier/exclusions).
4) Finance (Laura Bennett / delegate) validates policy compliance and amount.
5) Legal (Sofia Mendes / delegate) reviews if there is contract ambiguity or if a non-standard remedy is proposed.
6) CS communicates outcome to customer.
sections.heading: Approval path (default)

sections.body:
- Customer + contract/tier
- Deployment ID(s)
- Breach window (start/end in UTC)
- Evidence links: dashboard screenshots/links, evaluator output
- Customer impact summary (what broke, business impact if shared)
- Exclusion checks performed (throttling, workload constraints, warm-up)
- Proposed remedy type (service credit vs other)

---
sections.heading: What to include in the internal credit request

sections.body:
For any SEV-1/SEV-2 and any credit review, capture:
- Customer ticket link
- Incident link (if created)
- Dashboard links (throughput vs floor, saturation, errors)
- Request IDs / traces used for debugging
- Summary of customer-side traffic confirmation
- Timeline of mitigations and when throughput stabilized

---
sections.heading: Evidence and logging requirements

sections.body:
- **Customer sees lower throughput than Redwood reports:** often a measurement mismatch (streaming token accounting, end-to-end latency vs throughput, counting input tokens). Engage Observability if persistent.
- **Throughput drops with GPU pegged:** suspect contention, node health, thermal throttling, network bottleneck; page Infra.
- **Throughput drops with low utilization:** suspect admission control limiting, customer throttling, or workload shift to longer contexts; page SRE; ask customer for concurrency/workload details.
- **Regional capacity constraint / failover behavior:** check tier failover posture; page Infra and SRE; do not promise cross-region without tier/contract confirmation.

---
sections.heading: Common failure modes and quick routing hints

sections.body:
For confirmed Premium-tier breaches (and significant Plus-tier events), request:
- SRE-written incident summary within 5 business days.
- Follow-up action items tagged to owning teams (SRE/Infra/Observability/Routing).
- If credits were issued: ensure the billing/metering record reflects committed vs burst usage correctly.

---
sections.heading: Post-incident expectations

sections.body:
When paging SRE/Infra, include:
- “Dedicated Throughput SLO: suspected/confirmed”
- Deployment ID
- Tier + region
- Time window and whether ongoing
- Customer-confirmed load/concurrency (if available)
- Dashboard link
- Any correlated symptoms (timeouts, 5xx, queue depth)

This reduces back-and-forth and speeds mitigation.
sections.heading: Appendix: Minimal internal handoff note (for paging)

payload.page_title: Using Incident Taxonomy for Customer Communications (CS/Support Playbook)

sections.body: This playbook explains how Customer Success (CS) and Support should use the **Incident Taxonomy (v1)** in customer communications.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Communicate clearly and consistently without speculating on root cause.
- Set correct expectations for mitigations and next updates.
- Trigger the right escalation path based on incident type, severity, and customer tier (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Ensure comms align with remediation SLA expectations (time-to-mitigate/time-to-fix) and contractual commitments.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Support engineers and CS managers handling active incidents and escalations
- Incident Comms Owners (ICOs) for Dedicated/Private accounts
- Support leadership coordinating status-page updates and executive escalations
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- “This is classified as a **Routing/Fallback** incident”
- “We are seeing **elevated 5xx** due to **capacity constraints in region X**” (only if confirmed by on-call)
- “Mitigation in progress: traffic shifting / scaling / rollback”
sections.heading: Allowed

sections.body:
- Unverified causes (“GPU driver bug”, “kernel issue”, “bad deploy”) unless the incident owner explicitly confirms.
- Internal-only system names that confuse customers (e.g., “router v3”, “cp-write-path”) unless the customer already uses those terms and the owner approves.
- Over-specific ETAs (“fixed in 10 minutes”). Provide update cadence instead.
sections.heading: Avoid

sections.body: Internal incident_type/subtype should be captured in incident tooling and can be used verbatim **only** when the term is customer-safe. When in doubt, translate into plain language (examples below).
sections.heading: Separate customer-facing language from internal classification

sections.body:
If we cannot share a cause, provide:
- Current impact and scope
- What mitigation is being attempted
- Next update time
- Workaround (if any)
sections.heading: Update cadence beats speculative detail

sections.body:
- Dedicated/Private customer emails and Slack channels
- Support ticket updates when the incident is active and customer-impacting
- Post-incident review (PIR) summaries

Do not proactively mention taxonomy to Hosted/self-serve customers unless it improves clarity. For Hosted, prefer plain-language “service degradation” wording plus a status page link.
sections.heading: Use incident taxonomy language in

sections.body:
1) **Is the customer actively impacted (errors/latency/disconnects/config failures)?**
- If yes: send an initial acknowledgement and link to status page (or state “status page update pending” for Dedicated/Private).

2) **Is there an open incident channel and an Incident Commander (IC)?**
- If yes: follow comms cadence set by IC/ICO.
- If no but impact is likely Sev0/Sev1: page/engage on-call via Support escalation immediately.

3) **Is the incident type one that requires proactive outreach?**
- See “Proactive outreach triggers” below.

4) **Does this involve Dedicated or Private?**
- If yes: use the Dedicated/Private templates and ensure the account owner (CSM) is looped.
sections.heading: Quick decision guide: what’s the right comms posture?

sections.body: Proactive outreach means: CS/Support initiates customer messaging even if the customer has not yet opened a ticket, because impact is likely and customer expectations are higher.
sections.heading: Proactive outreach triggers by incident type

sections.body:
| Taxonomy type (customer-safe label) | Examples of customer symptoms | Proactive outreach for Hosted | Proactive outreach for Dedicated | Proactive outreach for Private |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Availability: 5xx / request failures | 5xx spike, failed completions/embeddings | Status page + only if widespread | Yes (within comms SLA) | Yes (within comms SLA) |
| Latency regression | p95/p99 latency elevated, timeouts | If widespread + material | Yes | Yes |
| Streaming disconnects | SSE/WebSocket resets, partial outputs | If widespread | Yes | Yes |
| Routing/fallback misbehavior | Wrong region/model, unexpected fallback, higher cost/quality change | If widespread | Yes (esp. committed capacity) | Yes |
| Capacity/fleet shortage | 429/overload, throughput drop, queueing | If widespread | Yes (capacity commitments) | Yes (if customer-managed fleet impacted) |
| Control plane outage | Cannot change policies, deploy model, update keys/config | Rare | Yes (if blocks ops) | Yes (often critical) |
| Auth/RBAC failures | 401/403, token rejected, permission issues | If widespread | Yes | Yes |
| Telemetry/metrics blind spot | “No data” dashboards, missing audit logs | No (unless blocks customer ops/compliance) | Sometimes (if affects reporting/audits) | Sometimes (esp. audit/compliance) |
| Private connectivity/config issue | DNS/TLS failures, VPC routing, firewall blocks after upgrade | N/A | N/A | Yes (direct outreach) |
sections.heading: Trigger table (v1)

sections.body:
- “Proactive outreach” is triggered by **confirmed impact** OR **high confidence** that impact is imminent (e.g., region capacity incident where customer is pinned to that region).
- For Dedicated/Private, assume higher expectations; err on the side of earlier outreach.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- **Incident Commander (IC)** (SRE or owning engineering team) controls internal timeline, mitigations, and severity.
- **Incident Comms Owner (ICO)** is responsible for customer-facing updates. For Dedicated/Private, this is usually CS (Account CSM) with Support as drafter; for broad outages, SRE may publish status updates and provide approved language.
- **Support** owns ticket hygiene: linking customer tickets to the incident, capturing customer-specific impact, and ensuring follow-ups are scheduled.
sections.heading: Who owns what during an incident

sections.body:
1) Support detects probable incident (multiple customers, clear outage signals)
- Open/confirm incident channel and tag on-call.
- Ask IC (or on-call) to confirm **incident_type/subtype** and **current mitigation plan**.

2) During active incident
- Support/CS publishes updates using approved content from IC/ICO.
- If the incident type changes (e.g., from “Capacity” to “Routing/Fallback”), update the customer summary without rewriting history (“Earlier we observed… We now believe primary driver is…”).

3) Resolution and post-incident
- Provide final update + next steps.
- For Sev0/Sev1, schedule PIR and ensure taxonomy is included.
sections.heading: Standard handoff rules

sections.body:
- Severity is Sev0/Sev1 (customer-impacting) OR the scope is unclear and potentially broad.
- You need approval for customer commitments (credits, contract language, bespoke mitigation plans).
- The incident type is unclear and paging/routing is disputed.
sections.heading: Escalate to SRE immediately when

sections.body:
- Auth failures appear suspicious (credential stuffing, unusual geo/IP patterns).
- There is potential data exposure or integrity concerns.
- You are asked by a customer about “breach” implications.
Reference: Security incident alignment page.
sections.heading: Escalate to Security Ops immediately when

sections.body:
Use these translations by default unless IC approves more specific language.

- Availability: 5xx / overload
  - Customer-safe: “elevated error rates” / “requests failing”
- Latency regression
  - Customer-safe: “elevated response times” / “time-outs for some requests”
- Streaming disconnects
  - Customer-safe: “streaming responses intermittently disconnecting” / “partial responses”
- Routing/fallback misbehavior
  - Customer-safe: “traffic routing behavior not matching expected policy” / “unexpected failover/fallback behavior”
- Capacity/fleet shortage
  - Customer-safe: “insufficient capacity in the affected region/pool” / “throughput constrained; requests may be throttled”
- Control plane outage
  - Customer-safe: “management/API operations degraded (configuration updates failing)”
- Auth/RBAC failures
  - Customer-safe: “authentication/authorization failures affecting access”
- Telemetry/metrics blind spot
  - Customer-safe: “monitoring/visibility degraded; service may be healthy but reporting is delayed”
- Private connectivity/config issue
  - Customer-safe: “connectivity issues between your environment and the private deployment endpoint”
sections.heading: Customer-safe translations of common incident types

sections.body: Templates are intentionally generic. Fill in the bracketed fields with confirmed details.
sections.heading: Communication templates

sections.body:
Subject: [Dedicated] Service degradation — [short symptom] — [region/pool]

Hi [Name/Team],

We’re investigating an active service issue affecting your dedicated deployment.

- **What we’re seeing:** [elevated 5xx / elevated latency / streaming disconnects / throttling]
- **Scope:** [region/pool], starting at approximately [time + timezone]
- **Classification:** [taxonomy type in customer-safe terms]
- **Current mitigation:** [traffic shifting / scaling / rollback / config change in progress]

We will send the next update by **[time]** (or sooner if status changes).

If you can share request IDs, timestamps, and affected routes/models, we can validate impact faster.

Thanks,
[Your name]
sections.heading: Template A — Initial acknowledgement (Dedicated)

sections.body:
Subject: [Private] Connectivity/configuration issue — [customer env] — [symptom]

Hi [Name/Team],

We’re investigating an issue affecting your private deployment connectivity/configuration.

- **What we’re seeing:** [DNS/TLS failures / connection resets / config update failures]
- **Classification:** Private connectivity/config issue (taxonomy)
- **Current mitigation:** [workaround steps if available]
- **What we need from you:** [recent changes, firewall rules, certificate updates, upgrade version]

Next update by **[time]**.

Regards,
[Your name]
sections.heading: Template B — Initial acknowledgement (Private)

sections.body:
Subject: Update — [Dedicated/Private] [symptom] — [region/pool/env]

Hi [Name/Team],
sections.heading: Template C — Update during mitigation (Dedicated/Private)

sections.body:
- **Current impact:** [still elevated / improving / intermittent]
- **What changed since last update:** [mitigation step attempted, rollback started, capacity added]
- **What we’re doing next:** [next mitigation step]
- **Next update:** [time]

We’ll continue to share confirmed information as it becomes available.

Thanks,
[Your name]
sections.heading: Update on the ongoing issue

sections.body:
Subject: Resolved — [Dedicated/Private] [symptom] — [region/pool/env]

Hi [Name/Team],

The issue appears resolved as of **[time]**.

- **Summary:** [one paragraph, customer-safe]
- **Classification:** [taxonomy type]
- **Customer impact window:** [start–end]
- **What we did:** [rollback/scale/traffic shift]
sections.heading: Template D — Resolution notice + next steps

sections.body:
- We will complete a post-incident review and share a summary / schedule a PIR if appropriate.
- If you are still seeing issues, please send [request IDs/timestamps] and we will investigate.

Regards,
[Your name]
sections.heading: Next steps

sections.body:
- For broad Hosted incidents, rely on the public status page as the source of truth.
- For Dedicated/Private, coordinate with IC/ICO on whether to:
  - post a public status note (rare; only for multi-customer impact), or
  - keep comms direct to affected accounts.

If a customer asks “Why doesn’t this show on the status page?” use:
- “The status page covers broad platform impact. This incident is isolated to a specific dedicated/private deployment; we are providing direct updates here.”
sections.heading: Status page guidance

sections.body: During the first ~10–20 minutes, internal classification may still be **Unknown**. Customer comms should still go out.
sections.heading: Handling “Unknown / Unclassified” incident type

sections.body: - “We are investigating elevated [errors/latency] affecting [scope]. We will share additional details as soon as confirmed.”
sections.heading: Use

sections.body:
- Guess at whether it’s capacity vs routing vs runtime.

Once IC confirms the incident type, update the customer summary in the next message.
sections.heading: Do not

sections.body:
CS/Support should not quote internal remediation SLA numbers unless:
- it is part of the customer contract/commitment, AND
- the Account CSM + Support lead agrees, AND
- the IC (or SRE delegate) confirms it’s appropriate for the specific incident.

Instead, communicate:
- Update cadence
- Current mitigation plan
- Any available workaround
sections.heading: SLA and expectation setting (customer-facing)

sections.body: - Acknowledge and route to the CSM + SRE program lead for aligned response.
sections.heading: If a customer explicitly requests SLA adherence

sections.body:
If engineering identifies multiple contributing factors (e.g., “capacity shortage + routing fallback misbehavior”):
- Customer comms should describe the **primary symptom** and the **mitigation path**.
- Avoid listing multiple speculative causes.
- If asked, you can say: “We’re investigating multiple contributing factors; we’ll share confirmed findings in the post-incident summary.”
sections.heading: Multi-cause incidents

sections.body:
If the incident is driven by a cloud provider or regional disruption:
- Use: “an upstream cloud provider issue in [region]” only after IC confirmation.
- Do not blame a provider without confirmation.
sections.heading: Cloud provider/regional events

sections.body:
- Do not discuss details of suspicious activity.
- Use: “We are investigating authentication failures; we’ll provide updates on service restoration.”
- Any mention of compromise, breach, or data exposure must be handled by Security + Legal/Comms.
sections.heading: If Security Ops is engaged

sections.body:
- Incident channel/link (Slack) or incident ID
- Confirmed incident_type/subtype (once available)
- Customer-specific impact (routes/models/regions)
- Customer constraints (pinned region, strict latency, compliance requirements)
- Update timestamps and next update commitment
- Whether proactive outreach occurred and who approved messaging
sections.heading: For every customer escalation linked to an incident

sections.body:
**Q: Can I tell customers the incident_type/subtype verbatim?**
A: Only if it’s customer-safe and confirmed by IC. Prefer plain-language translations.

**Q: The customer is seeing 429s. Is that always capacity?**
A: No. It can be quota enforcement or true overload. Ask IC to confirm whether it’s “Quota/Policy” vs “Capacity/Fleet shortage” before stating cause.

**Q: Customer is Dedicated and wants a PIR. When do we schedule?**
A: For Sev0/Sev1 or high-impact Sev2, schedule within 3–5 business days after resolution, once the postmortem draft is available.
sections.heading: FAQs

sections.body:
- 2026-02-12: Added “Unknown/Unclassified” guidance and security-adjacent language guardrails.
- 2026-01-18: Initial published version aligned to Incident Taxonomy v1 rollout.
sections.heading: Changelog

payload.page_title: Third-Party Vendor Coordination and Escalation Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the customer-success and engineering operational procedures for incidents where a third-party vendor (cloud provider, telemetry backend, datastore, or network provider) materially impacts enterprise customer availability, latency, or data integrity. It focuses on coordination, authoritative communication, and minimizing customer impact while preserving evidence and contractual obligations.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated & Private).
- Trigger conditions (use if ANY apply):
  1) Customer reports degraded responses traceable to external dependency (timeouts, 5xxs with vendor path).
  2) Platform telemetry shows cross-tenant error spikes correlated to external service call failures.
  3) Vendor posts a public incident with potential impact to Redwood-hosted tenants.
- Not for: routine internal service outages fully owned and resolved by Redwood (use standard incident runbooks).
sections.heading: Scope and when to use this playbook

sections.body:
- Customer Success Lead (CSL) — primary point for customer communication and SLA negotiation.
- Incident Commander (IC) — typically eng-sre on-call; owns technical coordination and declaration.
- Vendor Liaison (VL) — support/partner engineering contact who interfaces with vendor support and legal (if needed).
- Product Owner (PO) — evaluates feature or model impact and approves workaround rollouts.
- Legal & Compliance — engaged if data exposure or contractual breaches suspected.
- Solutions Engineer (SE) — assists with customer-specific configuration changes and rollback.
sections.heading: Stakeholders and roles

sections.body:
| Symptom | First responder | Escalate to | External contact window | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Transient API 429/5xx from vendor | On-call SRE | VL within 15m | Contact vendor support (priority P2) | Add correlation IDs to ticket |
| Sustained degraded throughput >20% 30m | IC + CSL | Product & Legal | Vendor account manager within 30m | Consider traffic-shaping fallback |
| Data loss or divergence | IC + Legal | CTO + Vendor Exec | Escalate to vendor SE/Legal immediately (30m) | Preserve logs, avoid write operations |
sections.heading: Escalation matrix (decision table)

sections.body:
1) Triage and classify:
   - Confirm customer-facing scope (single tenant, cohort, global).
   - Collect identifiers: tenant_id, request_ids, sample timestamps (UTC), error codes.
2) Contain impact:
   - If possible, enable safe-fail: route affected customers to compatible model-variant or degraded mode.
   - Apply rate-limits at gateway for noisy tenants.
3) Open authoritative incident:
   - Create incident in PagerDuty with severity: P2 (degraded) or P1 (outage).
   - Populate incident ticket with vendor name, ticket ID (if already opened), sample traces, and correlation query links.
4) Vendor engagement:
   - VL opens ticket with vendor, attaching RBAC-limited logs and correlation IDs. Use the following template (replace bracketed fields):

   Subject: "Redwood Incident [INC-<id>] — [Vendor] API timeouts impacting enterprise tenants"
sections.heading: Immediate steps (first 30 minutes)

sections.body:
- Redwood Incident ID: [INC-<id>]
   - Time window (UTC): [start..end]
   - Affected tenant(s): [tenant-ids]
   - Observable symptoms: [5xx rate, latency, failed writes]
   - Correlation IDs / traces: [links]
   - Priority: P2 (Customer-impacting).

   Attach: sanitized logs, network traceroutes, and sample payloads.
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
- Initial acknowledgement (within 30m): short, factual, owner, next update ETA.
  "Hello <CustomerName>, we are aware of an issue affecting <feature>. Our on-call team has identified this is related to <vendor>. We are investigating and will update within 60 minutes. Owner: <CSL-name> (email/phone)."
- Status update (every 60m while active): include scope, mitigation steps, ETA, and whether workaround is available.
- Post-incident summary (within 48h): include root cause (if known), impact, mitigations, and corrective actions.
sections.heading: Customer communications (templates and cadence)

sections.body:
- Authorization and access:
  - Verify support contract & escalation path (AM, Technical Account Manager (TAM), SE).
  - Confirm least-privilege data exchange: generate temporary log bundles, masked PII.
- Evidence collection:
  - Time-synced traces (UTC), service mesh spans, TCP dumps (pcap), and error-rate time series.
  - Preserve raw artifacts for 14 days in secure bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<INC-id>/ (do not modify).
- Workaround validation:
  - Test traffic shaping / fallback in staging tenant before applying to production.
  - Document rollback steps for each change.
- SLA & credit assessment:
  - VL and Legal to map incident to vendor SLOs and customer contract terms within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Vendor coordination checklist (practical items)

sections.body:
- Prometheus: error-rate by target_vendor
  query: rate(http_requests_total{vendor="X",code=~"5.."}[5m])
- Traces: sample span filter (Jaeger/Zipkin)
  filter: span.tags.vendor == "X" && span.tags.http.status_code >= 500
- SQL: find impacted tenant list (example)
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as failures FROM request_log WHERE vendor = 'X' AND timestamp >= '2026-02-12T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY failures DESC LIMIT 50;
- Network: tcpdump capture guidance
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <vendor-ip> and port <vendor-port> -w /tmp/vendor-<INC-id>.pcap
sections.heading: Telemetry queries and diagnostics (examples)

sections.body:
- Initial customer acknowledgement: CSL (within 30m)
- Technical updates: IC/VL (every 60m)
- Executive escalation & legal notices: VP Customer Success / Legal (as required)
- Final root-cause & QBR summary: CSL + PO (deliver within 48h; include mitigation plan for next 90 days)
sections.heading: Communication ownership matrix

sections.body:
"Hello <VendorSupport>,

We are Redwood Inc (Account: <account-id>). We are experiencing increased 5xx rates when calling <api-endpoint>. Incident ID: <INC-id>. Please escalate internally to engineering and share ETA. We can provide traces and pcap. Contact: <VL-email> + <VL-phone>.

Regards,
Vendor Liaison — Redwood"
sections.heading: Templated escalation email to vendor (short form)

sections.body:
- Every workaround that modifies routing, quotas, or model variants requires:
  - a short risk assessment,
  - approval by IC and PO,
  - automated rollback configured and smoke test passing within 10 minutes.
- Changes must be recorded in change-log and synchronized to customer CSL.
sections.heading: Rollback and change control guidance

sections.body:
1) Evidence bucket review and retention confirmation.
2) RCA draft: root cause, contributing factors, timeline, and customer impact table (tenant-level).
3) Customer remediation plan: fixes, timeline, and compensatory credit if applicable.
4) Vendor follow-up: request for technical write-up and SLA response.
5) Preventative actions: add probes, synthetic checks, or alternate vendor routing where warranted.
6) QBR item: include incident summary, change plan, and KPIs for next quarter.
sections.heading: Post-incident actions and artifacts (within 72h)

sections.body:
- Useful internal links:
  - Incident channel: #inc-redwood-production (Slack)
  - Vendor management wiki: /confluence/sales/vendor-accounts
  - Evidence bucket SOP: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/evidence-retention
- Escalation PD schedule: See PagerDuty schedule for "vendor-liaison" rotation.

Appendix A — Vendor contact index (sensitive):
- Vendor: TelemetryCo — TAM: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@telemetryco.example), Support portal: https://support.telemetryco.example, Escalation SLA: 2 hours (P1)
- Vendor: CloudA — Account Exec: Maria Fernandes (maria.fernandes@clouda.example), Technical Support: https://status.clouda.example, Network NOC: +1-555-0102

(Contacts above are redacted in public exports; see restricted directory for full contact details.)

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: When do we issue an SLA credit to customers?
A: Follow customer contract rules; use the customer-impact table from the RCA and coordinate with Legal and Finance for any credits.

Q: Can we switch vendors for an impacted tenant?
A: Short-term fallbacks (cache-only, degraded model variant) are preferred. Vendor switches require Product approval and at least one-week lead time for provisioning.
sections.heading: Operational runbook appendix

sections.body:
- 2025-09-14 — Created by Ava Martinez (initial version).
- 2026-01-22 — Added telemetry queries and evidence retention SOP references (reviewers: Ethan Chen, Priya Nair).
- 2026-02-12 — Clarified timeline for vendor SLA mapping and added rollback controls (Sanjay Patel review).

Appendix C — Quick triage checklist (printable):
1) Create incident & set severity. 2) Notify CSL & affected customers (30m). 3) Collect traces & preserve pcap. 4) Open vendor ticket with correlation IDs. 5) Test and apply fallback if safe. 6) Schedule RCA and customer summary within 48h.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Executive Escalation Protocol (Support/CS → Leadership)

sections.body:
This protocol defines **when and how Support/CS escalates to executive leadership** and what information must be included to enable fast, consistent decisions. It is designed to:
- Reduce time-to-decision for high-stakes customer-impacting events
- Ensure Support SLAs and Engineering incident processes stay aligned
- Standardize approvals for **credits**, **custom mitigations**, and **status page** actions

**This page is restricted** because executive escalations often contain customer-sensitive details (account context, contract terms, timelines, credit discussions).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Customer-impacting incidents where leadership visibility or approval is required
- Enterprise/Dedicated/Private escalations with contractual/SLA implications
- Any request for credits, special handling, or deviations from standard process
sections.heading: Use this protocol for

sections.body:
- Routine escalations that can be resolved through the standard Support → Eng/SRE path
- General product roadmap requests (route to the normal Product/CS intake)
sections.heading: Not in scope

sections.body:
- **Exec Escalation:** Leadership visibility + decision support. It does **not** replace the incident process.
- **Incident Management:** Engineering/SRE-led process in **#incidents** with Incident Commander (IC) ownership.
- **Account Escalation:** A customer relationship escalation (e.g., renewal risk) that may be concurrent with technical mitigation.
sections.heading: Definitions (quick)

sections.body:
**Support Incident Lead (SIL)** (Support on point; often the SUP ticket assignee)
- Owns customer-safe communications cadence (or delegates)
- Ensures required artifacts are captured (request IDs, regions, timelines)

**Enterprise CS Lead** (account context; escalation sponsor)
- Owns executive relationship management and coordination with Sales
- Owns customer expectation management (within contract/SLA policy)

**SRE/Engineering On-Call**
- Owns technical mitigation, incident updates, and operational truth
- Provides root-cause hypothesis + mitigation status statements suitable for customer email

**Leadership participants (by role)**
- **VP, Customer Success/Support:** approval for customer-facing commitments and escalated comms strategy
- **VP, Engineering:** approval for engineering-level commitments that change priority/rollout/safety posture
- **Sales Leadership / Account Executive (AE):** aligned messaging, renewal/commercial risk, and commitments to the account
- **Legal/Finance (as needed):** credits language, contractual exceptions, or compliance-sensitive commitments
sections.heading: Roles & decision owners

sections.body: Initiate an exec escalation if **any** of the triggers below are met.
sections.heading: When to initiate an executive escalation

sections.body:
1) **P0/P1 for an Enterprise, Dedicated, or Private customer** with material business impact
2) Broad impact across multiple customers/regions that may require **public comms** (status page or banner)
3) Incident duration is likely to exceed customer expectations (see SLA policy) and requires leadership visibility
4) Security/compliance risk is suspected (e.g., audit log integrity concerns, access/auth anomalies)
sections.heading: Escalate when any of the following are true

sections.body:
1) A customer claims an **SLA breach** (or one is likely) and requests remediation
2) A **credit request** is expected or already requested (especially if material)
3) The customer requests a **contractual exception** (custom update cadence, bespoke reporting, bespoke mitigations)
sections.heading: Escalate when

sections.body:
1) Renewal/expansion is at risk due to the incident
2) Customer threatens to churn, go public, or escalate via legal/procurement
3) Sales/CS requests executive involvement to align on account-level messaging
sections.heading: Escalate when

sections.body:
1) There is ambiguity on whether to post to the **status page**
2) There is a request to bypass standard incident processes (e.g., “hotfix in production now” without usual approvals)
3) There is disagreement across teams on severity, ownership, or comms posture
sections.heading: Escalate when

sections.body:
- **Within 15 minutes** of recognizing an exec trigger: start the exec escalation thread and post the initial summary.
- **Within 30 minutes**: leadership has a clear “ask” and recommended decision path (even if mitigation is still in progress).
- **Ongoing**: update the exec thread at the same cadence as customer updates, or at minimum:
  - every **30–60 minutes** during active major impact
  - whenever there is a material change (mitigation started, rollback, confirmed RCA, ETA changes)
sections.heading: Timing expectations

sections.body:
1) Confirm there is a single source-of-truth ticket:
   - Support: Jira **SUP-####**
   - Engineering incident (if applicable): #incidents channel + incident timeline
2) Create (or link) the Slack bridge per **Slack Bridge & Incident Channel Conventions**.
3) Start an exec escalation thread/channel using the approved internal naming convention (keep customer name out of widely visible channels if required).
4) Post the **Executive Escalation Summary** (template below).
5) Pin:
   - SUP ticket link
   - incident channel link (if any)
   - latest customer message (or draft)
   - dashboards/runbook links used to assess mitigation
sections.heading: How to start an exec escalation

sections.body:
**Title:** [Short description] — [Tier] — [Region/model if relevant]

**Customer / Account:**
- Customer: [Name] (Enterprise/Dedicated/Private/Hosted)
- Commercial context (optional, keep minimal): [renewal date / expansion / sensitivity]

**Impact:**
- Customer-reported symptoms:
- Redwood-observed symptoms/metrics:
- Affected endpoints/features: [chat/streaming/embeddings/audit logs/etc.]
- Scope: [single account / multiple accounts / region-wide]

**Timeline (UTC):**
- Start time (observed):
- Start time (customer noticed):
- Key events so far (deploys/rollbacks/mitigations):

**Current status:**
- Status: Investigating / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved
- Leading hypothesis (clearly labeled):
- Mitigation in progress:
- Next technical milestone:

**Customer communications:**
- Last customer update time:
- Next planned update time:
- Current message posture (customer-safe):

**Asks / decisions needed:**
- Decision 1: [e.g., status page post?] — recommended: [yes/no + rationale]
- Decision 2: [e.g., credits posture?] — recommended: [policy-based guidance]
- Decision 3: [e.g., custom mitigation / capacity shift] — recommended: [what + risk]

**Owners:**
- Support Incident Lead:
- CS Lead:
- Eng/SRE on-call:
- Sales/AE:

**Links:**
- SUP ticket:
- Incident channel (if any):
- Dashboards:
- Runbook/known-issue (if relevant):
sections.heading: Executive Escalation Summary (paste template)

sections.body: All exec decisions must be logged in a durable place so Support/CS/SRE can reference them later.
sections.heading: Decision log expectations (required)

sections.body:
- Primary: add a **Decision Log** section in the SUP ticket (internal comments) and link it in the exec thread.
- If there is an incident: record in the incident timeline and link back to the SUP ticket.
- If there are contractual implications: summarize in the CS account notes per CS ops guidance (do not paste contract text into broad channels).
sections.heading: Where to record decisions

sections.body:
- Decision timestamp (UTC)
- Decision owner(s) (role + name)
- Options considered (1–3 bullets)
- Final decision + rationale
- Customer-facing language approved (copy/paste safe)
- Follow-ups and deadlines (who/what/when)
sections.heading: Record

sections.body:
1) **Credits** approval/denial and the rationale
2) Any **status page** publication decision (post / don’t post / delay)
3) Any **custom mitigation** (special routing, capacity reallocation, bespoke operational handling)
4) Any commitment of an **ETA** that is not backed by Engineering/SRE
sections.heading: Decisions that always require explicit logging

sections.body:
Credits are not promised in real-time during mitigation. Use this approach:
- Acknowledge the request and state we will review per policy after stabilization and timeline confirmation.
- Do not reference internal error budgets, internal-only SLOs, or speculative root cause.
sections.heading: Credits & remediation guidance (policy-aligned)

sections.body:
- Standard discretionary credits (low): CS Leadership approval
- Material credits or contractual exception: CS Leadership + Sales leadership + Legal/Finance review

**Required inputs before approval:**
- Confirmed incident timeline and scope (from SRE/IC)
- Customer tier + relevant contract/SLA clause summary (no contract copy/paste into Slack)
- Evidence of impact (metrics and/or customer logs)
sections.heading: Approval thresholds (internal)

sections.body: Status page decisions must align with **Customer Incident Comms Alignment**.
sections.heading: Status page decision guidelines (alignment)

sections.body:
- Impact is likely to affect multiple customers or a full region
- We have high confidence in customer-facing symptoms even if RCA is in progress
- Customer visibility is required to reduce inbound volume and set expectations
sections.heading: Escalate for leadership decision when

sections.body:
- Keep language customer-safe and symptom-based
- Include next update time (do not promise ETAs unless confirmed)
- Ensure Support email updates and status page updates do not conflict
sections.heading: When posting

sections.body:
**Do:**
- Use symptom-based language and measurable current state
- Clearly label hypotheses vs confirmed facts
- Provide the next update time every time you communicate

**Don’t:**
- Promise credits, ETAs, or root cause before verification
- Share customer-sensitive details in broad channels
- Create parallel “shadow incident management” outside #incidents when Engineering has declared an incident
sections.heading: Communication do’s and don’ts

sections.body:
- [ ] SUP ticket has: tier, region, model, request IDs, timestamps (UTC)
- [ ] Severity/Priority is set correctly and matches the severity rubric
- [ ] Slack bridge is created and required participants are present
- [ ] Exec summary posted with a clear ask
- [ ] Decision log started in SUP ticket
- [ ] Customer comms cadence scheduled and consistent
sections.heading: Appendix: fast checklist for the Support Incident Lead

payload.page_title: Status Page Customer Escalation Playbook (Disputed Status Accuracy)

sections.body:
This playbook is used by Support and Customer Success when a customer reports that the public status page does not reflect the impact they are experiencing ("status page says everything is OK, but we are failing"). It provides:
- A standard intake checklist to quickly validate what the customer is seeing.
- A clear escalation path to SRE/on-call and the incident Comms Lead.
- Approved customer-facing responses and guardrails.
- A consistent way to correct status page inaccuracies without increasing on-call burden.

This is a customer trust workflow. Our goals are (1) fast acknowledgement, (2) accurate classification to the right public component(s), and (3) avoiding speculative or customer-sensitive disclosures.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Customer claims status page indicates "Operational" but they have errors/latency.
- Customer claims wrong component/region is marked degraded.
- Customer claims incident is missing (no active incident) while multiple customers are impacted.
- Customer requests proof/evidence of impact or asks for a post-incident summary while the status page remains green.
sections.heading: Use this playbook when any of the following are true

sections.body:
- Single-tenant Dedicated or Private issues isolated to a single customer environment without broader platform impact (see "Dedicated/Private guidance").
- Pure how-to questions about interpreting the status page components (route to Docs/DevEx guidance).
sections.heading: Do NOT use this playbook for

sections.body:
- The status page reflects *platform component health* by product surface and region (e.g., Hosted API – US-East, Streaming – EU-West).
- It is not a guarantee that every request is successful for every customer, and it does not expose customer-specific capacity constraints.
sections.heading: What the public status page represents

sections.body:
- Do not disclose: customer-specific capacity, noisy-neighbor details, account identifiers, or security-sensitive root cause.
- Do not over-promise SLA credits or contractual remedies in Support channels.
- Do not speculate on root cause. Stick to observed symptoms, mitigations underway, and next update timing.
- For Sev0/Sev1: do not publish new public status updates yourself unless explicitly authorized (see escalation section). Support/CS can draft wording, but SRE/IC owns publish unless delegated.
sections.heading: Required guardrails (must follow)

sections.body:
- **Support L1 (Frontline):** intake, collect evidence, acknowledge customer, initiate escalation when criteria are met.
- **Support L2 / Escalations (Support Ops):** ensure complete evidence, coordinate with CS owner, maintain customer thread.
- **CS Owner / CSM:** manage stakeholder expectations, coordinate timelines and post-incident follow-up requests.
- **SRE On-call:** validates signals, confirms impacted public components, initiates or updates incident.
- **Incident Commander (IC):** owns incident handling and severity.
- **Comms Lead:** owns customer-facing updates (status page + internal alignment), ensures consistent wording.
sections.heading: Roles

sections.body:
- **Acknowledgement to customer:** within 15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1 claims during business hours; within 30 minutes otherwise.
- **Time to escalate to SRE (if criteria met):** within 10 minutes of receiving required evidence.
- **Status page correction (if inaccurate):** as soon as SRE validates; prioritize before deep RCA when customer impact is ongoing.
sections.heading: Targets (internal operating targets; not customer-facing commitments)

sections.body:
Collect the following information in the customer ticket/thread before escalating.

**Customer / environment**
- Customer name + contract type: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
- Primary region(s) impacted (customer’s view): US-East / US-West / EU-West / APAC-SG, etc.
- Workspace/org ID (internal only) and support plan tier

**Time window**
- Impact start time (with timezone) and whether ongoing
- Whether impact is intermittent or continuous

**Symptoms (choose all that apply)**
- Elevated 5xx / 429 / timeouts
- Latency regression (p50/p95/p99)
- Streaming disconnects / stalled streams
- Embeddings failures
- Reranking failures
- Console access issues

**Request evidence**
- 3–5 example request IDs (or correlation IDs) with timestamps
- Example error messages and HTTP status codes
- Endpoint/route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings) and SDK/version
- If streaming: transport details (SSE/websocket), and client timeout settings

**Customer impact**
- Severity from customer perspective (prod down vs degraded)
- Approximate failure rate if known (e.g., 10–20% of requests)
- Business impact (optional, customer-provided)
sections.heading: Step 1 — Intake checklist (copy/paste)

sections.body:
Before escalating, do a 3–5 minute check to avoid false alarms:
1) Check https://status.redwoodinference.com for active incidents and impacted components/regions.
2) Check internal dashboards for the relevant component/region (links in "Internal validation links").
3) Verify whether the symptom aligns with a component-specific failure mode (e.g., streaming disconnects may not show in generic API error rate).
4) If there is a mismatch, proceed to escalation.

If dashboards are fully green and evidence is weak (no request IDs, no timestamps), ask the customer for the missing items using the template in "Customer follow-up for missing data".
sections.heading: Step 2 — Quick self-validation (Support/CS)

sections.body:
- Multiple customers report similar symptoms in the same region within 30 minutes.
- Customer provides request IDs showing elevated 5xx/timeouts and internal dashboards show any correlated increase.
- Streaming disconnect spikes are reported (these are historically under-represented in generic error views).
- Enterprise customer indicates material production impact and the status page remains green.
- The customer disputes an active incident’s scope (wrong region/component) with evidence.
sections.heading: Escalate to SRE On-call immediately if ANY are true

sections.body:
- Customer reports mild latency regression with no errors, and internal latency is elevated but below incident thresholds.
- Customer requests a retro/post-incident summary formatting change (route to Comms Lead + PM, not on-call).
sections.heading: Escalate to SRE during business hours (non-page) if

sections.body:
- Primary: **#support-escalations** (start here; keep customer context centralized)
- Add as needed:
  - **#incidents** (if you believe it should be treated as an incident)
  - **#eng-oncall** (for quick on-call attention if criteria met)
  - **#statuspage** (if your org uses a dedicated channel for status updates)
sections.heading: Slack channel routing

sections.body:
- Tag **SRE On-call** (PagerDuty user: "SRE Oncall") when criteria are met.
- If an incident exists, tag the current **IC** and **Comms Lead** (from the incident channel topic / incident-bot output).
sections.heading: Who to tag

sections.body:
Subject: Potential status page mismatch — [Component?] [Region] — customer reports [symptom]

- Customer: [name] ([Hosted/Dedicated/Private], plan tier)
- Reported region(s): [US-East/EU-West/etc]
- Symptoms: [errors/latency/streaming disconnects/embeddings]
- Impact window: [start time] to [now]
- Evidence: request IDs + timestamps: [list]
- Current status page: [Operational / Incident ongoing / Wrong component]
- Our quick validation: [dashboard summary in 1–2 lines]
- Ask: please validate component mapping and advise whether to update status page / open incident
sections.heading: Required escalation message format (copy/paste)

sections.body:
- Ensure the customer ticket includes the intake checklist.
- Add an internal note: "Status page accuracy dispute — escalated to SRE".
- If enterprise: notify the assigned CSM in the ticket and in Slack.
sections.heading: Ticket hygiene

sections.body:
- Acknowledge the customer quickly using an approved template (below).
- Ask for any missing evidence (request IDs, timestamps) if needed.
- Do not state that an incident exists until SRE/IC confirms.
- If the customer is blocked, suggest short-term mitigations that are generally safe (e.g., retry with backoff, enable fallback model if they already use it, reduce concurrency) without implying a platform defect.
sections.heading: Step 4 — What Support/CS should do while SRE validates

sections.body:
If SRE confirms a mismatch (wrong component/region or missing incident), the expected flow is:
1) SRE/IC identifies the correct public components (per taxonomy) and confirms status signal evidence.
2) Comms Lead posts or adjusts the status page update using the incident templates.
3) Support/CS follows up with the customer linking to the incident and summarizing the correction.

If the incident is Sev0/Sev1 and an approval step is required, Comms Lead will obtain the required approval (IC or Support lead, depending on incident workflow). Support should be ready to rapidly review wording for clarity (not for technical accuracy).
sections.heading: Step 5 — If status page is inaccurate (correction workflow)

sections.body: Dedicated and Private deployments may have customer-specific incidents that are not appropriate for the public status page.
sections.heading: Dedicated / Private guidance (important)

sections.body:
- If a Dedicated/Private issue is isolated: acknowledge and treat it as a customer incident via the dedicated/private support path. Do not push for a public incident unless SRE confirms shared control-plane or multi-tenant platform impact.
- If the issue appears tied to shared control plane (auth, console, model registry, routing) affecting multiple dedicated customers: escalate as a potential public component impact ("Dedicated Control Plane") per taxonomy.
sections.heading: Approved guidance

sections.body: - "Your cluster ran out of capacity" or "another customer caused this".
sections.heading: Never say

sections.body: - "We’re investigating your environment’s health signals and will share updates in this ticket. If we confirm broader platform impact, we’ll reflect that on our status page."
sections.heading: Preferred language

sections.body:
Use the following internal assets for quick checks (do not share screenshots externally unless approved by Comms Lead + Legal for an enterprise exception):
- Status page component taxonomy (definitions + ownership): oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/status-page-component-taxonomy
- Status page update runbook (how to verify and post): oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/status-page-update-runbook
- Customer-facing status signals standard (thresholds, anti-flap, what qualifies as degraded): architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/customer-facing-status-signals-standard
- Component health dashboards (per region/capability): eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/status-page-component-health-dashboards
- SLO alignment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private): eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/status-page-transparency-slo-alignment
sections.heading: Internal validation links (reference)

sections.body: "Thanks for flagging this. We’re investigating the errors/latency you’re seeing and comparing them against our regional health signals now. If we confirm broader impact, we’ll reflect it on our public status page. In the meantime, could you share 3–5 example request IDs (with timestamps/timezone) so we can trace the failures end-to-end?"
sections.heading: 1) Acknowledgement (status page currently green)

sections.body: "Thanks — we see the active incident on our status page and we’re validating whether the impacted components/regions match what you’re experiencing. We’ll update the incident if we confirm additional scope. If you can share a few request IDs (with timestamps), we can validate routing/region and align the public component status accurately."
sections.heading: 2) Acknowledgement (active incident exists but scope disputed)

sections.body: "We confirmed broader impact consistent with what you reported and have updated our public status page to reflect the affected components/regions. You can follow updates here: https://status.redwoodinference.com. We’ll continue to post progress there until fully resolved."
sections.heading: 3) We confirmed a mismatch and updated status page

sections.body: "We’ve reviewed our platform health signals for the relevant region/components and we’re not currently seeing widespread impact. That said, we’re continuing to investigate your specific requests. If you can share additional request IDs (and the region/endpoint), we can narrow down whether this is route-specific, configuration-related, or isolated to a subset of traffic."
sections.heading: 4) We did NOT confirm broader impact (yet)

sections.body: "To help us investigate quickly, could you provide: (1) 3–5 request IDs (or correlation IDs), (2) timestamps with timezone, (3) the endpoint you’re calling (chat/embeddings/reranking/streaming), and (4) whether the issue is continuous or intermittent? With those, we can trace the requests and confirm whether a status page update is warranted."
sections.heading: 5) Customer follow-up for missing data

sections.body: "Yes — once the incident is resolved, we publish a customer-facing summary with impact and remediation details when appropriate. If you have specific information requirements (e.g., impact window, regions, mitigations), reply here and we’ll ensure they’re addressed in the published summary or in a direct follow-up if customer-specific."
sections.heading: 6) Post-incident summary request

sections.body: - Component taxonomy split (Embeddings vs Chat) not reflected or misclassified.
sections.heading: Likely causes

sections.body:
- Collect evidence: endpoint must be /v1/embeddings (or SDK embedding call), request IDs.
- Escalate with emphasis: "possible component misclassification".
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body: - Streaming-specific failure mode; generic error rate dashboards may remain green.
sections.heading: Likely causes

sections.body:
- Collect: client type, timeout, disconnect rate estimate, request IDs.
- Escalate: include "streaming disconnect" keyword.
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body: - Capacity pressure, kernel regression, routing shift; may not cross incident thresholds.
sections.heading: Likely causes

sections.body:
- Gather p95/p99 and endpoints; check status signal standard for latency thresholds.
- Escalate non-page unless enterprise-prod-down or corroborated by dashboards.
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body: - Dedicated environment isolated; public status page remains green.
sections.heading: Likely causes

sections.body: - Follow Dedicated/Private guidance; escalate to dedicated on-call; do not push public update unless shared control-plane.
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body:
1) Support L1: intake + acknowledge + quick validation.
2) Support L2 / Escalations: ensure evidence complete; coordinate with CSM.
3) SRE On-call: validate internal signals + mapping; advise on public components.
4) IC/Comms Lead: publish/adjust status page updates; maintain incident timeline for post-incident summary.
5) Post-incident: link customer to published summary; capture feedback as an input to status accuracy audits.
sections.heading: Escalation ladder (summary)

sections.body:
- Tag the ticket: "Status Page Accuracy".
- Add an internal note with:
  - affected component(s) suspected
  - region(s)
  - request IDs
  - whether a status page change occurred
- For enterprise disputes: create a short internal recap in #support-escalations and link the ticket.
- If status page was incorrect, file a follow-up task against the component mapping owner (SRE/Observability) with the evidence and timestamps.
sections.heading: Logging and follow-ups

sections.body:
**Q: Can Support update the status page directly?**
A: Only if explicitly delegated for a specific incident by the IC/Comms Lead. Default is SRE/Comms Lead publishes.

**Q: Customer asks "Why wasn’t this on the status page?"**
A: Use neutral language: "The status page tracks platform component health; we’re validating whether this reflects broader impact. We will update it if we confirm it does." Avoid details about capacity partitioning or other customers.

**Q: Customer asks for dashboards/screenshots as proof.**
A: Do not share internal dashboards by default. If needed for an enterprise security review, request approval from Comms Lead + Legal (Michael Grant) and provide a sanitized written summary instead of screenshots whenever possible.
