payload.page_title: Adaptive Degradation Safety & Verification Manual

sections.body:
Summary:

This manual defines the safety contracts, verification checks, benchmarking protocols, and operational runbooks we use to validate adaptive degradation and fallback behavior in the Redwood serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and release owners who gate runtime and scheduler changes. The document consolidates architecture contracts, test harnesses, profiling playbooks, measurable acceptance criteria, and incident response steps into a single reference.

Scope:
- Covers adaptive degradation (fidelity staircases, model-variant fallback, burst shedding) and scheduler/kernel interactions.
- Includes verification checks executed in CI, pre-release staging, and canary phases.
- Prescribes profiling and benchmark procedures for SLO verification and performance regressions.
- Provides runbooks for on-call and release owners for graceful rollback and mitigation.

Principles and safety goals:
1) Observable and measurable: every degradation path must have a minimal observable signal (metrics, traces, events) and a single source-of-truth trace ID for forensic replay.
2) Fail open vs fail closed rationale: correctness-critical requests (enterprise-configured) should prefer fail-closed; non-critical/latency-sensitive requests can fail open to preserved throughput.
3) Bounded fidelity loss: fidelity steps should degrade quality predictably (quantified by eval sets) and be reversible.
4) Deterministic rollback: any automated fallback must expose a deterministic rollback path and human-confirmable guardrails.

Architecture contracts (high-level):
- Degradation tiers: primary (full model), degraded-1 (quantized), degraded-2 (short-context variant), fallback (smaller model / cached-embeddings). Each tier has an SLO budget and cost profile.
- Kernel scheduling contract: the scheduler must maintain per-request kernel affinity for the first N tokens and preserve KV cache affinity during tier transition windows (default N=16).
- Eviction and warmup contract: when a session is evicted from KV cache, a warmup window of configurable length (default 60s) is reserved to rehydrate frequently-seen prompts without degrading SLOs.

Verification matrix (summary table):
| Check ID | Purpose | Where executed | Acceptance threshold | Action on fail | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VD-01 | End-to-end tail latency under 95th percentile SLO | CI staging + canary | p95 < 1200ms for interactive path | block release, auto-rollback in canary | runtime-sre |
| VD-02 | Kernel latency jitter for hot kernels | perf-lab | 95th/50th ratio < 3.0 | schedule throttling + revert kernel flags | runtime-kernel-team |
| VD-03 | Fidelity regression on golden prompt set | automated evals | task-specific metric delta < 1.5% | fail gating | applied-ml |
| VD-04 | KV cache hitrate during warmup | synthetic replay | hitrate > 70% after 120s | degrade to cached-response fallback | runtime-sre |
| VD-05 | Correctness of fallback routing (no request loss) | chaos lab | 0 dropped requests during routing switch | incident | runtime-oncall |

Verifiable artifacts for each check:
- Synthetic replay corpus snapshot (sha256) used in CI.
- Expected telemetry schemas (metric names, tags) and trace samples.
- Baseline benchmark outputs (binary artifacts) for diff-based gating.

CI and pre-release harnesses:
1) CI unit stage: microbenchmarks for individual kernels (latency, occupancy, memory). Thresholds are enforced as fast-fail rules.
2) Staging perf run: full-stack replay of production traffic sampled (1:1000) with degraded-tier injection. Output artifacts: histogram dumps, kernel traces, KV cache heatmaps.
3) Canary: traffic ramp with A/B model variants and automated rollback on VD-* failures. Canary policy: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 30m windows with automated health checks every 5m.

Benchmarking protocol (detailed):
- Workloads to run:
  - Interactive short-chat (mean tokens=40, 90th=128) — target low-latency SLOs.
  - Streaming long-output (mean tokens=800) — target throughput and memory stability.
  - Embeddings burst (large batch sizes) — target batching efficiency and memory footprint.
- Metrics collected:
  - end_to_end_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99), kernel_exec_time_ms per-kernel, gpu_mem_used_mb, kv_cache_hitrate_pct, tokens_per_second_per_gpu.
- Tooling & commands (examples):
  - Run synthetic replay: 
    ./perf-runner --profile=replay --corpus=sha256:abcd1234 --duration=15m --out=artifacts/replay-$(date +%s).tgz
  - Microbenchmark kernel: 
    python tools/microbench.py --kernel matmul --batch 1 --seq 128 --out json --repeat 50
  - Collect trace samples for a request: 
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<<golden>>"}' -o /tmp/trace.json
- Acceptance criteria pattern:
  - No p95 regression > 8% vs baseline.
  - Kernel jitter (95/50) <= 3.0.
  - KV cache delta < 5% hitrate loss after warmup period.

Profiling playbook snippets (how-to):
1) Latency fingerprint collection (on perf-lab machine):
  - Start full instrumentation: export PERF_SAMPLER=on; ./runtime --enable-tracing --trace-sample-rate=0.01
  - Run workload for 10 minutes and collect traces: tar -czf traces.tgz /var/tmp/traces/*
  - Post-process: python tools/trace-aggregate.py --input traces.tgz --output traces-summary.json
2) Kernel causality mapping:
  - Use kernel-hint exporter to annotate kernels with request-id and token-index. Example PromQL to find kernel hotpaths: sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (kernel_name)
3) Latency attribution checklist:
  - Confirm p95 skew aligns with a specific kernel or queue time via trace waterfall.
  - Check GPU utilization and eviction events within the window.
  - Validate KV cache hit/miss correlation with session affinity changes.

Runbook: Adaptive Degradation incident triage (short):
1) Detection: Alert triggers if p95 or error-rate breaches gating thresholds (see Verification matrix).
2) Initial triage (first 10 min):
  - Owner: oncall-runtime.
  - Query: run the baseline PromQL dashboards (listed below) and capture current vs baseline.
  - Commands:
    - promql: rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (route)
    - runtime CLI: runtimectl list-sessions --filter=evicted=true --since=10m
3) Containment (10–30 min):
  - If caused by kernel regression: flip kernel rollout gate to previous stable tag (runtimectl kernel-set active:stable-<tag>) and pause canaries.
  - If caused by cache warmup regression: enable elevated pre-warm (config: prewarm_multiplier=2) and route new sessions to degraded-1 temporarily.
4) Remediation (30–90 min):
  - Roll back flagged config or kernel. Run perf-runner quick replay to validate.
  - If degradation persists, scale dedicated pool capacity for 15 minutes to reduce pressure and collect artifacts.
5) Post-incident verification: Ensure all VD-* checks pass in staging before re-enabling automated rollouts.

Release gating checklist (for runtime and scheduler changes):
- Code owner review and ADR reference.
- Automated CI checks: unit tests, lint, kernel microbenchmarks.
- Perf artifacts present: replay corpus, baseline histograms, and guard thresholds.
- Canary policy configured and health checks defined (list health checks and thresholds attached).
- Rollback plan and human approvers designated in the release ticket.

Instrumentation and metrics schema (quick reference):
- metric names: runtime.request.latency_ms, runtime.kernel.exec_ms, runtime.kv.hits, runtime.fidelity.tier, runtime.eviction.count
- required tags: service, model_name, model_variant, route, region, canary_id
- recommended tracing fields: request_id, session_id, token_index, kernel_name, warmup_phase

Ownership and escalation:
- Runtime architecture owner: runtime-arch@redwood.ai (primary: Sanjay Rao).
- Kernel scheduling owner: kernel-team@redwood.ai.
- Oncall rota: runtime-sre (see internal roster).
- Escalation path: oncall -> SRE lead -> runtime-arch -> Eng Director (timed escalation at 45m).

Appendices:
A) YAML example: adaptive degradation policy (example config to be applied via runtime fleet config)

  degradation_policy:
    tiers:
      - name: primary
        model_variant: v2-full
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 900
      - name: degraded-1
        model_variant: v2-quantized
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 700
      - name: degraded-2
        model_variant: v2-shortctx
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 350
    warmup:
      kv_cache_warmup_seconds: 120
      prewarm_multiplier: 1.5
    fallback:
      strategy: route-to-smaller-model
      max_inflight_fallback: 250

B) PromQL examples (quick):
- p95 latency for route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- kernel jitter index: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel)))/(histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel)))

C) Minimal reproduction recipe for regressions:
1) Snapshot failing commit and baseline artifacts.
2) Run perf-runner with the failing kernel flag enabled and the baseline corpus.
3) Collect traces (traces.tgz) and microbench outputs.
4) Upload artifacts to /artifacts/regressions/<ticket-id>.

Related reading and references:
- See routing and fallback architecture ADR (link in related_pages).
- Profiling playbooks and telemetry contract (links in related_pages).

Notes and change log:
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft and adoption of verification matrix (S. Rao).
- 2026-03-10: Added canary ramp policy and refined kernel warmup contract; added runbook remediation steps (E. Hart, D. Alvarez).

If you are implementing a new scheduler or kernel change, follow this manual start-to-finish: 1) add microbench checks, 2) register threshold baselines, 3) run staging replay, 4) validate VD-* checks, 5) enable canary with the configured ramp, 6) monitor and be ready to rollback.

payload.page_title: Lighthouse Serving Roundtable: Rollout Readiness Checklist (Canary A / Quantized v2)

sections.body:
This page standardizes what we review in the Lighthouse Serving Roundtable before changing the Canary A rollout percentage for the quantized v2 serving path. It is intended to keep the weekly discussion focused on decision-quality inputs: customer impact risk, capacity readiness, instrumentation coverage, and rollback safety.

This document replaces ad-hoc personal prep notes and should be used as the pre-read template for the roundtable thread.

---
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
**Cadence:** Weekly (Tuesday) 30 minutes

**Expected attendees:**
- Serving runtime core
- Infrastructure (capacity / cluster)
- Console (route configuration / UX)
- SRE on-call (rota)
- Product PM (as needed for release gating)

**Primary goal:** Make (or defer) a clear decision to (a) proceed to the next canary step, (b) hold at current %, or (c) roll back.

---
sections.heading: Meeting format

sections.body:
**In scope**
- Canary A (quantized v2) rollout readiness and gating checks
- High-risk regressions that could change rollout decisions (latency tail, error rates, warm-start behavior)
- Fallback policy configuration for route-level safety

**Out of scope**
- Deep debugging during the 30-minute slot (schedule a dedicated 60-minute deep dive with traces/logs preloaded)

---
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- **Release target:** Serving Runtime **0.9.3** (updated from earlier 0.9.2 plan)
- **Canary stream:** Canary A (quantized v2)
- **Proposed next step:** 10% → 25% (only if all gates below are met)

---
sections.heading: Current rollout target

sections.body:
Proceed only if all are true for the last 24 hours in each primary region (at minimum: us-west-2, us-east-1):
- **p99 latency:** ≤ **900 ms** for small-sequence workloads (median ~128 tokens) OR no more than **+20%** versus float32 control on matched traffic.
- **Error rate (5xx + timeouts):** ≤ **0.30%** and not increasing week-over-week.
- **Retry rate:** no anomalous increases attributable to quantized path.
sections.heading: 1) Customer impact gates

sections.body: - The p99 tail is the primary customer-risk metric. If p99 is above gate but p50/p95 are healthy, treat as a hold condition and require a concrete remediation plan.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- Confirm **≥ 20% spare capacity** in the dedicated canary pool for the full rollout window.
- Confirm an **emergency scale** procedure is on-call owned and tested within the last 30 days.
- Confirm cluster autoscaling safeguards do not conflict with pinned canary nodes.
sections.heading: 2) Capacity gates (Infra/SRE)

sections.body:
- 7-day latency histograms are available and reviewed (p50/p95/p99), segmented by:
  - region
  - workload size (short vs long sequences)
  - model variant (quantized v2 vs float32)
- Canary dashboards include:
  - token cost metrics (avg and distribution)
  - memory pressure signals (RSS, OOM events)
  - queueing time vs compute time breakdown
- Alerts exist and are actionable for:
  - p99 latency regression
  - warm-start throughput degradation
  - error rate spikes
sections.heading: 3) Observability gates (Runtime/SRE)

sections.body:
- Rollback plan has been reviewed and is executable in **< 15 minutes**.
- Route-level fallback behavior is documented and tested:
  - Manual fallback to float32 variant is validated.
  - Auto-fallback is allowed only if telemetry is sufficient to avoid oscillation (see below).

---
sections.heading: 4) Rollback and fallback gates (Console/Runtime)

sections.body:
**Original symptom (observed early March):** p99 for small-seq workloads increased substantially under HTTP/2 traffic.

**Updated status (as of 2026-03-21):**
- Root cause narrowed to an HTTP/2 connection management interaction in the sidecar/proxy path.
- Mitigation implemented via runtime + proxy tuning; fix tracked in **GH PR 497**.
- Current p99 in us-west-2 for the same segment is down from the earlier peak and has been stable over the last 48 hours.

**Roundtable requirement:**
- Mikael (runtime) confirms the fix is in the candidate build for 0.9.3 and shares a short before/after comparison.
sections.heading: RED-2147: HTTP/2 p99 latency spike

sections.body:
**Original symptom:** stalled throughput for multiple minutes after node restart.

**Updated status (as of 2026-03-21):**
- Instrumentation added for warm-start duration and cache rebuild time.
- Throughput drop duration reduced; remaining issue is variance during peak queue depth.

**Roundtable requirement:**
- Priya (runtime) confirms alerting thresholds and links to the dashboard panel used for the gate.

---
sections.heading: RED-2199: KV cache invalidation after quantized warm-start

sections.body:
Provide the following bullet summary (one line each) plus links to dashboards:
- **Latency (quantized v2 vs float32):** p50 / p95 / p99, by region
- **Cost:** avg token cost delta (target: negative) and any variance by workload class
- **Errors:** 5xx, timeouts, retries (absolute + change)
- **Stability:** OOMs, restarts, warm-start duration
sections.heading: Metrics snapshot (what to include in the roundtable pre-read)

sections.body:
- "Canary A: token cost -20%, p50 +6%, p95 +9%, p99 +14% (stable), error rate 0.18% (flat), no new OOMs."

---
sections.heading: Recommended one-liner format

sections.body: Fallback exists to preserve customer experience if the quantized path regresses (tail latency, errors) while limiting churn and avoiding oscillation.
sections.heading: Policy intent

sections.body:
- **Manual fallback:** Supported and required to be tested each rollout step.
- **Auto-fallback toggle:** Not GA by default until we have:
  1) per-route telemetry surfaced in Console (error/latency deltas), and
  2) a cooldown mechanism to prevent flip-flopping.
sections.heading: Current stance (updated)

sections.body:
- Add a route-level quick link to canary metrics (dashboard deep link).
- Display the current model variant and canary status on the route page.

Owner: Zara Thompson (Console)

---
sections.heading: Console requirements

sections.body:
1) **Quick wins since last sync (3m)**
   - Each team: one sentence
2) **Incidents / regressions (8m)**
   - RED-2147 HTTP/2 p99 status
   - RED-2199 warm-start/cache status
3) **Rollout readiness decision (10m)**
   - Review decision gates (customer impact, capacity, observability, rollback)
   - Decision: proceed to next step vs hold vs roll back
4) **Console / UX readiness (4m)**
   - Route metrics link status
   - Fallback UI status
5) **Action items & owners (5m)**

---
sections.heading: Standard agenda (30 minutes)

sections.body:
- **Decision:** Proceed / Hold / Roll back
- **Actions:**
  - Owner — Deliverable — Due date — Link
- **Customer comms (if needed):** Owner — Audience — When

---
sections.heading: Use this structure in the meeting thread

sections.body:
- Omar Ruiz: publish weekly one-pager with p50/p95/p99 graphs + cost delta for Canary A (includes region segmentation). Due: 2026-03-22.
- Mikael Andersson: close out investigation for RED-2147 with fix summary and verification evidence (includes perf traces). Due: 2026-03-24.
- Priya Nair: validate RED-2199 alert thresholds and add runbook link to the alert description. Due: 2026-03-25.
- Zara Thompson: implement route page link to canary metrics and propose copy for fallback controls (manual only for now). Due: 2026-03-26.
- SRE rota: confirm capacity cushion for next canary step and link the emergency scale playbook. Due: 2026-03-22.

---
sections.heading: Current action items (carried forward)

sections.body:
- Latency response guidance: confluence:serving-runtime/latency-playbook
- Tickets: JIRA:RED-2147, JIRA:RED-2199
- Recent PRs: GH PR 482 (historical graphs), GH PR 497 (current mitigation)

---
sections.heading: References

sections.body:
- 2026-03-13: Created checklist from prior roundtable prep notes.
- 2026-03-18: Updated release target to 0.9.3 and formalized decision gates.
- 2026-03-21: Updated known-issue status and clarified auto-fallback stance pending telemetry.

payload.page_title: Deterministic Playback Manifest Format (v1)

sections.body:
This page defines the **Deterministic Playback Manifest** format (v1): a lightweight, self-contained JSON document intended to capture everything needed to deterministically replay an inference session (or an ordered set of requests) across model rollouts, runtime variants, kernel changes, and quantization profiles.

The primary goal is to make postmortems, regression triage, and model A/B comparisons reproducible **without requiring full environment cloning**.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
The manifest is intentionally not a full provenance ledger.

**Out of scope for v1**
- Capturing private customer data inline. Manifests must reference redacted payloads or point to approved secure storage locations.
- General-purpose data lineage, training provenance, or governance/audit trails.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
- **Minimal**: reference large artifacts instead of embedding blobs.
- **Deterministic intent**: include all inputs that can affect output (tokenizer, seeds, runtime config, policies/hooks).
- **Portable**: JSON, human-readable, attachable to support tickets and GitHub issues.
- **Privacy-aware**: PII-bearing content must be referenced via controlled pointers and governed by a privacy policy token.
sections.heading: Design principles

sections.body:
- This page defines **v1** of the format. Breaking changes require a new `manifest_version`.
- Forward-compatible additions must be optional and ignored by older runners.
sections.heading: Applicability and versioning

sections.body:
All top-level fields are JSON keys.

**Identity and metadata**
- `manifest_version` (required): must be `"1"`
- `manifest_id` (required): short stable id (UUID recommended)
- `created_by` (required): name/email of authoring agent (person or system)
- `created_at` (required): RFC3339 timestamp
- `source_context` (required): freeform string describing scenario (UI flow, API route, ticket)

**Artifacts and execution**
- `model_artifact` (required): model id + artifact digest
- `tokenizer` (required): tokenizer id + digest
- `environment` (required): runtime/environment snapshot string (see "Environment fields")
- `requests` (required): ordered list encoded as JSON array in the manifest; each element is a request descriptor (see below)

**Determinism controls**
- `runtime_flags` (required): list of `key=value` strings affecting execution (e.g., `use_kv_cache=true`)
- `deterministic_seeds` (required): list of seed assignments (e.g., `global_seed=42`, `sampler_seed=42`)
- `determinism_mode` (required): one of `strict | best_effort`

**Observability and privacy**
- `telemetry_refs` (optional but recommended): pointers to associated logs/traces/metrics
- `privacy_policy` (required): one of `none | partial | strict`
- `payload_policy` (required): one of `inline_redacted | pointer_required`

**Integrity (updated in v1)**
- `integrity` (optional): a compact string describing integrity mechanism. v1 runners support:
  - `none`
  - `sha256-only` (checksums required; no signature)
  - `sigstore-oidc` (signature envelope stored separately; manifest contains reference)

> Update vs. early draft: `signature` is no longer a direct embedded blob in v1. Use `integrity` plus `integrity_ref` (see below) to avoid copying large envelopes into tickets.
sections.heading: Required top-level fields (v1)

sections.body:
- `telemetry_bundle_ref`: URI to a packaged bundle (trace + token metrics + logs) when available.
- `integrity_ref`: URI to signature/envelope material when `integrity` != `none`.
- `notes`: freeform human notes.
sections.heading: Optional top-level fields (v1)

sections.body:
Each `requests[]` element represents one request in a deterministic sequence.

**Required request fields**
- `request_id`: short id, unique within manifest
- `timestamp`: RFC3339 timestamp of original request
- `api_route`: e.g., `/v1/generate` or `/v1/chat/completions`
- `raw_payload_ref`: pointer to stored payload (GCS/S3/secure-store) OR inline redacted JSON string when permitted by policy
- `input_checksums`: list of checksums for payload-derived inputs
- `sampling_config`: canonical string encoding of sampling knobs

**Recommended request fields**
- `client_sdk`: client library + version
- `pre_hooks`: ordered list of transformations applied pre-runtime (name@version + checksum)
- `post_hooks`: ordered list of transformations applied post-runtime
- `expected_response_fingerprint`: fingerprint of original response for quick divergence checks
- `fallback_policy_trace`: record of any fallbacks (model switch, retry, safety downgrade) with timestamps

> Update vs. early draft: v1 standardizes on `expected_response_fingerprint` rather than "signature" wording to avoid confusion with cryptographic signatures.
sections.heading: Request descriptor (v1)

sections.body:
Environment is represented as a compact semicolon-delimited string of `key=value` pairs to keep manifests small and friendly to ticket systems.

**Required environment keys**
- `runtime_image`: container name + digest (must include digest)
- `host_os`: e.g., `ubuntu-22.04`
- `region`: e.g., `us-west-2`
- `accelerator`: e.g., `a100-80gb` or `cpu`

**Recommended environment keys**
- `runtime_release`: serving runtime release tag
- `kernel_determinism`: `on | off | mixed`
- `concurrency_profile`: `single-req | batched`
- `num_shards`: integer

> Update vs. early draft: `runtime_image` **must include a digest** (e.g., `redwood/runtime-infer@sha256:...`) because tags are not stable enough for deterministic repro.
sections.heading: Environment fields (v1)

sections.body:
- Checksums must be `sha256`.
- `input_checksums` entries are strings with a prefix:
  - `raw:sha256:<hex>` for raw payload bytes (post-redaction if redacted inline)
  - `tok:sha256:<hex>` for tokenized input ids (canonical serialization)
sections.heading: Input checksums

sections.body:
The response fingerprint algorithm is fixed in v1 to avoid ambiguity:
- Normalize model output by:
  1) converting CRLF to LF
  2) trimming trailing whitespace on each line
  3) ensuring final newline is absent
- Compute `sha256` over UTF-8 bytes of the normalized string
- Encode as `resp:sha256:<hex>`

> Update vs. early draft: v1 explicitly uses **sha256 of normalized text** (not embeddings) for `expected_response_fingerprint`. Embedding similarity is permitted in reports but not a manifest primitive.
sections.heading: Response fingerprint (v1)

sections.body:
`telemetry_refs` are URIs (or internal artifact ids) pointing to:
- structured trace (Jaeger/Tempo trace id)
- token-level metrics (latency per token, logprobs if enabled)
- server logs (filtered range)
- resource utilization snapshot

When available, prefer a single `telemetry_bundle_ref` that points to a packaged artifact.
sections.heading: Telemetry references (v1)

sections.body:
- `raw_payload_ref` must comply with `privacy_policy` and `payload_policy`.
- For `privacy_policy=strict`, manifests **must not** include raw text content; use secure pointers only.
- Redacted inline payloads are permitted only with `privacy_policy=partial` and `payload_policy=inline_redacted`.
- If payload pointers are used, the pointer must reference an access-controlled store with audit logs.
sections.heading: Privacy and security

sections.body:
Below is an illustrative example (fields shown as a single JSON document). Values are representative.

{
  "manifest_version": "1",
  "manifest_id": "m-3c9f2d4b",
  "created_by": "aisha@redwood.ai",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10T15:04:12Z",
  "source_context": "support-ticket #12345 - user reported hallucination on invoice extraction",
  "model_artifact": "gptx-4-quant-v3;sha256=7b1c...",
  "tokenizer": "tokenizer-v4;sha256=ef56...",
  "environment": "runtime_image=redwood/runtime-infer@sha256:91aa...;host_os=ubuntu-22.04;accelerator=a100-80gb;region=us-west-2;kernel_determinism=on;concurrency_profile=single-req",
  "determinism_mode": "strict",
  "runtime_flags": ["use_kv_cache=true", "kv_prefetch=on"],
  "deterministic_seeds": ["global_seed=42", "sampler_seed=42"],
  "privacy_policy": "strict",
  "payload_policy": "pointer_required",
  "integrity": "sha256-only",
  "requests": [
    {
      "request_id": "r1",
      "timestamp": "2026-03-09T22:10:03Z",
      "api_route": "/v1/chat/completions",
      "client_sdk": "python:openai-compat@1.8.2",
      "raw_payload_ref": "gcs://redwood-playback/12345/payload-r1.json.redacted",
      "input_checksums": ["raw:sha256:aaa...", "tok:sha256:fff..."],
      "sampling_config": "temp=0.0;top_p=1.0;top_k=0;seed=42",
      "pre_hooks": ["prompt-template@2.1.0;sha256=19c..."],
      "expected_response_fingerprint": "resp:sha256:0d4..."
    }
  ],
  "telemetry_refs": ["jaeger://trace/abc123", "gcs://redwood-playback/12345/token_metrics.json"],
  "notes": "Repro runner should fail fast if kernel_determinism is not on."
}
sections.heading: JSON example (v1)

sections.body:
A compliant playback runner (e.g., `rps` in eng-serving-runtime) should:
1. **Validate manifest**: check required fields, validate checksums are well-formed.
2. **Resolve artifacts**: fetch model and tokenizer by digest; verify sha256.
3. **Materialize inputs**: fetch `raw_payload_ref` under policy; apply `pre_hooks` in order.
4. **Recompute checksums**: assert `raw:` and `tok:` checksums match.
5. **Configure runtime**: apply `runtime_flags`, set determinism mode, seed RNGs.
6. **Execute**: run requests in order. In `strict` mode, disable/avoid nondeterministic kernels; if not possible, fail with a clear reason.
7. **Compare**: compute `expected_response_fingerprint` and compare; produce a delta report.
8. **Report artifacts**: emit a bundle containing outputs, token logs, timings, and a summary (attach via `telemetry_bundle_ref` or external storage).
sections.heading: Runner procedure (Serving Runtime reference)

sections.body:
- `manifest_version` is now mandatory and must be `"1"`.
- `runtime_image` must include an immutable digest.
- `expected_response_fingerprint` algorithm is fixed (normalized-text sha256).
- Cryptographic signing is supported via references (`integrity` + `integrity_ref`) rather than embedding a signature blob in the manifest.
sections.heading: Compatibility notes and updates since the draft

sections.body:
- Primary owner: **Serving Runtime** (eng-serving-runtime)
- For schema changes: file an issue under **ENGSR** and tag **repro/playback**.
- For privacy questions: consult **Security & Compliance** and reference SEC-201.
sections.heading: Ownership and support

payload.page_title: Runtime signal conciliation and latency cohorting

sections.body:
Summary
This page defines a single, operationally actionable taxonomy for runtime signals (conciliation) and a pragmatic approach to grouping traffic by latency cohorts (cohorting). The goal is to standardize how the runtime reconciles competing signals — SLOs, kernel pressure, KV cache warm state, and cost guidance — and how the scheduler harmonizes execution decisions across those cohorts to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput and cost targets.

Intended audience
- Runtime engineers (kernel, scheduler, dispatch)
- SREs and oncall engineers owning latency SLOs
- Performance and profiling owners

Why this exists
We observed repeated flapping between priority policies during mixed workloads: short chat requests bouncing against long generation jobs; KV cache warmup causing transient tail spikes; and adaptive batching oscillations that increase mean latency. Those issues trace back to inconsistent interpretation of telemetry signals across components. This doc prescribes: 1) a shared signal vocabulary, 2) cohorting rules, 3) a scheduler harmonization contract, and 4) an operational playbook for experiments and incidents.

Key concepts
- Signal conciliation: the deterministic process by which the runtime reduces multiple, possibly conflicting telemetry inputs into an ordered set of actions (e.g., throttle, preempt, hedging, fallback).
- Latency cohort: a stable label assigned to a request (or request class) representing its expected latency distribution and tolerance (e.g., interactive-50ms, elastic-200ms, batch-1s). Cohorts are used to drive scheduling, admission, and caching policies.
- Steering signals: canonical telemetry used for conciliation. See table below.

Steering signals (canonical)
- SLO_gap: (SLO_target_ms - observed_p95_ms) normalized by SLO_target_ms. Positive = healthy.
- Queue_depth: per-queue pending requests count and age histogram (0-10ms, 10-100ms, >100ms).
- Kernel_pressure_index (KPI): weighted sum of GPU occupancy, active kernels, enqueue latency, and memory stall rate. Range [0,100].
- KV_warm_fraction: fraction of requests expected to hit prefix/KV cache (0-1).
- Cost_signal: per-token cost estimate and priority cost budget remaining for the route/customer.
- Error_rate: percent of responses that triggered fallback/retry in the last minute.

Latency cohorts (recommended defaults)
1) interactive-50ms: requests with strict p50/p95 targets (e.g., UI autocompletion).
2) interactive-150ms: session chat turns that can tolerate modest tail but expect snappy median.
3) elastic-400ms: longer generations where batching accelerates cost efficiency.
4) background-batch-1s: large offline or low-priority requests eligible for queueing and high batching.

Cohort assignment rules
1. Assign cohort at ingress based on route metadata and model profile (explicit route overrides default).
2. If request includes max_latency_ms or max_tokens, map to cohort using the mapping table in Appendix A.
3. Dynamic reclassification: on warmstart/kvcache-warmup events, mark requests as "warming-elastic" for up to 2s to bias toward nodes with warm cache.

Scheduler harmonization contract (short)
- Purpose: give a deterministic algorithm for turning conciliated signals into actions across the admission-controller, slot allocator, and kernel dispatcher.
- Input: steering signals + cohort label + route SLA tier + model-variant cost guidance.
- Output: admission decision (accept/defer/redirect), slot allocation (slots, preemptible flag), kernel hints (preferred kernel ID, quantization path), and fallback instruction (model-variant or queue route).

Decision precedence (ordered)
1. Safety blocks (OOM, watchdog) — immediate reject/evict.
2. SLO preservation for interactive cohorts when SLO_gap < 0.1 — apply hedging, reduce batch size, reserve non-preemptible slot.
3. KPI escalation — if KPI > 80, favor elastic/background cohorts for eviction or delayed admission.
4. Cost_controls — if cost budget is exhausted for a high-cost route, redirect to quantized variant or lower-fidelity model.
5. KV_warm_fraction optimization — prefer nodes with warm fraction >= 0.7 for cohorts that benefit from cache; otherwise allow warmup cohort routing.

Operational playbook (incident / experiment flow)
1. Detection: Alert triggers if p95_interactive > SLO_target * 1.2 for 3 minutes OR KPI > 85 for 2 minutes.
2. Triage rapid checks (2 min):
   - Check SLO_gap, KPI, Queue_depth, KV_warm_fraction across affected nodes.
   - Identify cohort skew (which cohorts show disproportionate latency).
3. Rapid mitigation (5–15 min):
   - If KPI high and elastic/background load is > 40% of active kernels, temporarily drain new batch routes and redirect to spare pool.
   - If KV_warm_fraction low and interactive cohorts are affected, enable warm-prefetch for interactive routes and nominate warm nodes using routing tag warm-preferred=true.
   - Apply emergency hedging for interactive cohorts: spawn second probe request on separate slot and cancel slower completion.
4. Follow-up (post-mitigation):
   - Run microbenchmark traffic shaped to reproduce cohort mix that triggered incident (see Benchmarking protocol section).
   - Capture full traces for 30 minutes and export to profiling lab.

Benchmarking protocol (cohort-aware replay)
- Purpose: validate scheduler decisions under realistic mixed cohorts.
- Core steps:
  1. Build a traffic shape with 3 lanes: interactive-50ms (40% qps), interactive-150ms (30% qps), elastic-400ms (30% qps).
  2. Run three scenarios: baseline (no harmonization), harmonization-lite (conciliation but no preemptive evict), harmonization-full (all rules enabled).
  3. Measure: p50/p95/p99 per cohort, mean tokens/sec, kernel context-switches, KPI, KV hit delta, cost_per_1k_tokens.
  4. Acceptance criteria: interactive-50ms p95 improvement >= 20% vs baseline and overall cost increase <= 8%.

Profiling playbook (fast experiment loop)
- Sampling: mark 1% of interactive requests and 0.5% of elastic as deep-sampled for full trace collection.
- Instrumentation: include kernel_id, batch_size, slot_id, kv_hit, enqueue_time_ms, kernel_start_ms, kernel_end_ms, total_response_ms.
- Replay: use the captured traces to run stepwise synthetic replays in the profiling lab with and without harmonization – compare kernel dispatch histograms.

Configuration reference (examples)
Table: Scheduler conciliation thresholds (human-readable)
- interactive_reserve_slots: 20% (reserve always-available non-preemptible slots per node for interactive cohorts)
- hedging_probe_delay_ms: 30 (time after which hedging probe is launched for interactive when queue_age > 10ms)
- kpi_preempt_threshold: 80
- warm_preferred_fraction_threshold: 0.7
- cost_redirect_threshold_usd_per_1k: 2.50

Example YAML snippet (route-level override)
- route: /api/chat/fast
  cohort: interactive-50ms
  reserve_slots: 0.25
  max_batch_size: 8
  fallback_variant: model-lite-quantized-v2

Runbook excerpt: latency spike play actions (cheat sheet)
1. Acknowledge alert and post on #runtime-incidents.
2. Run `runtime-cli get-signals --nodes affected` and snapshot KPI/queue/kv.
3. If KPI > 85: scale out spare-pool by +10% and enable batch-drain on background pools.
4. If interactive p95 > target*1.2 and KV_warm_fraction < 0.6: set routing tag warm-preferred=true for interactive routes and re-route 10% traffic to warm nodes.
5. If no improvement in 10 minutes: failover to regional fallback model family (defined in Release Playbook).

Dashboards and alerts (minimum)
- Dashboards: cohort-latency-heatmap, KPI-over-time, kv-warm-fraction-by-node, admission-decision-by-cohort.
- Alerts: High KPI, cohort p95 breach, sustained hedging rate > 5%, sudden KV_warm_fraction drop > 0.2 in 5m.

Ownership and contacts
- Runtime scheduler owner: Marcus Lee (pager: eng-runtime-scheduler)
- Kernel infra owner: Elena García (pager: eng-kernel)
- Profiling & benchmarks: Jordan Kim (profiling@redwood.ai)

Appendix A — cohort mapping guidelines
- max_latency_ms <= 50 -> interactive-50ms
- 50 < max_latency_ms <= 200 -> interactive-150ms
- 200 < max_latency_ms <= 600 -> elastic-400ms
- max_latency_ms > 600 or large token budgets -> background-batch-1s

Appendix B — experiment checklist for safe rollout
1. Feature-flagged rollout (10% traffic) for 48h with continuous monitoring.
2. Canary cluster with identical HW profile and KV warm snapshot.
3. Compare p99 and error delta vs baseline; gate at 2% p99 regression or 0.5% error rate increase.

Change log
- 2025-09-14: Document created (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-11-02: Added hedging parameters and KPI definition (Marcus Lee).
- 2026-02-03: Tuned benchmark acceptance criteria and added warm-preferred routing guidance (Elena García).

Related artifacts
- Synthetic replay harness: repo: infra/perf/replay/cohort-replay
- Profiling lab dashboard: dashboards/runtime/cohort-profiles

Finally
This doc is normative for any scheduling or admission change that touches cohorted traffic. If you propose a change that modifies the conciliation algorithm, update the decision precedence table and run the cohort-aware benchmark suite described above prior to rollout.

payload.page_title: Runtime experiment signal catalog and hypothesis matrix

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This document centralizes the signal definitions, collection guidance, and hypothesis matrix for runtime experiments across Redwood's serving stack. It is intended for engineers running controlled performance experiments, A/B rollouts, profiling campaigns, and benchmark suites. The goal is to reduce ambiguity about which telemetry to use for which kind of experiment and to standardize evaluation heuristics and rollback criteria.

Scope
-----
Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime variants. Focused on: request path telemetry, kernel scheduling metrics, KV cache signals, batching utilization, and cost-attribution signals used by Redwood Optimize and runtime autoscalers. Not a replacement for incident runbooks; where an experiment reveals an incident, follow the incident playbooks in oncall_and_incident_response.

Quick summary (one-line)
----------------------
Use this catalog to: (1) select 3–5 core signals for hypothesis acceptance, (2) set primary/secondary thresholds, (3) follow the step-by-step experiment run, and (4) export the result to the benchmark suite for regression tracking.

Signal catalog and rationale
---------------------------
Each signal below includes: name, cardinality (per-request / per-slot / host-level), sampling guidance, expected distribution shape, primary/secondary use, and recommended alert thresholds for experiments.

1) request.latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99} (per-route, per-model)
- Cardinality: per-request aggregated by route/model/region.
- Sampling: full for release-level A/B; 10% for long-running smoke experiments.
- Distribution: heavy right tail; expect multiple modes if mixed sequence lengths.
- Use: Primary for latency SLO experiments.
- Experiment thresholds: delta(p95) <= +10% relative for canary acceptance; delta(p99) <= +20% triggers manual triage.

2) kernel.queue_depth_avg (per-device, per-kernel-type)
- Cardinality: device,kernel-type (attention, ff, matmul).
- Sampling: continuous at 1s resolution.
- Distribution: near-zero for elastic workloads; spikes indicate contention.
- Use: Secondary signal to explain latency regressions.
- Thresholds: sustained > 50% of peak slot count for >30s => consider reducing concurrency or increasing slots.

3) kvcache.hit_rate (session-id, per-model)
- Cardinality: session-level aggregated to route/model.
- Sampling: computed on write-window (1m).
- Distribution: dependent on prompt reuse; typical baseline for chat products is 0.35–0.85.
- Use: Primary when testing prefix caching or warmup strategies.
- Thresholds: drop > 15 percentage points relative -> expect token cost increase; auto-fallthrough if paired with latency increase.

4) batch_utilization_pct (executor-pod, per-1m)
- Cardinality: executor-pod.
- Sampling: 10s rolling window.
- Distribution: multi-modal depending on client batching.
- Use: Primary for cost-efficiency experiments; correlate with tokens/sec.
- Thresholds: sustained < 20% while throughput stable suggests misconfiguration (e.g., slice size mismatch).

5) kernel.exec_time_ms.{mean,95th} (per-kernel-type, per-device)
- Cardinality: kernel-type, device.
- Use: Diagnosing scheduling vs kernel inefficiency.
- Thresholds: > +25% mean vs baseline => flag for kernel rollout hold.

6) memory.gpu.free_mb and memory.gpu.fragmentation_pct (node-level)
- Use: Safety signals for private/on-prem experiments; fragmentation > 60% + free_mb < reserve -> OOM risk.

7) cost.per_token_usd (route, model_variant)
- Use: Primary for Optimize-driven experiments.
- Calculation: (infra_cost + reserved_amortization) / tokens_generated.

Instrumentation and collection guidance
-------------------------------------
- Services and names: rdx-runtime-dispatcher (ingest), rdx-kernel-agent (device-facing), rdx-kvcache (session store), rdx-metrics-aggregator, rdx-benchmark-runner. Tag metrics with: service, cluster, region, model, model_variant, route, experiment_id, canary_group.
- Metric format: Prometheus-style timeseries with labels above; export to metrics pipeline with 10s scrape where possible and 1s for kernel-level counters.
- Logs: include structured JSON request events with fields: request_id, route, model, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, kernel_hints, start_ts, end_ts. Example:

```json
{
  "request_id": "r-7f3a2c",
  "route": "chat-default",
  "model": "open-vicuna-13b-quant-v2",
  "seq_len_in": 64,
  "seq_len_out": 128,
  "kernel_hints": "sharded-attn",
  "start_ts": "2027-02-10T15:12:03.123Z",
  "end_ts": "2027-02-10T15:12:03.379Z"
}
```

Benchmark config and expected artifacts
--------------------------------------
When converting an experiment to a benchmark, include a config file. Minimal example (YAML):

```yaml
benchmark_name: kvcache-warmup-vs-none
model: rdx-llama-30b-q4
routes: [chat-default]
workload_profile: production-sampled-2027-01
duration: 30m
concurrency: 64
metrics: [request.latency_ms.p95, kvcache.hit_rate, batch_utilization_pct, cost.per_token_usd]
export_to: perf-db://benchmarks/kvcache-warmup-vs-none-2027-02-10
```
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- raw telemetry (prometheus histograms + traces)
- per-request logs (parquet)
- experiment summary (markdown) with stat tests (see below)

Hypothesis matrix and statistical evaluation rules
--------------------------------------------------
Use the following convention for experiment outcomes: Primary signals (1–2) must meet acceptance thresholds; secondary signals should exhibit no regression beyond soft thresholds.

- Hypothesis example: "Enabling async kvcache prefetch will reduce p95 latency by >= 8% without increasing cost per token by > 5%."
- Primary signals: request.latency_ms.p95 (delta <= -8%) and kvcache.hit_rate (delta >= +6 percentage points).
- Secondary signals: cost.per_token_usd (delta <= +5%), kernel.queue_depth_avg (no sustained >75% saturation).
sections.heading: Expected artifacts

sections.body:
1) Use bootstrap resampling over per-request latencies; report 95% confidence intervals for deltas.
2) Accept only if delta and CI both exceed the acceptance threshold in the favorable direction.
3) For cost signals where variance is high, cap sample variance by stratifying on seq_len buckets: [0-64, 65-256, 257+].

Experiment runbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Define experiment_id and register in the experiments board (team-wiki experiments index).
2) Select the core signals (max 5). Mark primaries.
3) Create benchmark config and a dedicated metrics dashboard with experiment_id filter.
4) Run warmup: 10 minutes at 25% target load to populate caches.
5) Execute canary: 5–10% traffic for 30 minutes.
6) Collect telemetry and run stats pipeline:
   - Command: rdx-benchmark-runner analyze --experiment-id EXP123 --save-summary ./summary.md
7) Evaluate acceptance per hypothesis matrix.
8) If accepted, escalate to rollout plan (see rollout checklist). If rejected, capture triage notes and create a follow-up profiling ticket.

Rollout checklist and safety gates
----------------------------------
- Gate 1 (canary acceptance): primary signals meet thresholds; no kernel exec_time regression > 25%.
- Gate 2 (stability hold): run 2h at 50% traffic with continuous monitoring; no alerts fired.
- Gate 3 (full rollout): ramp to 100% over 3 steps (50%, 75%, 100%) with 10–20 minute hold per step.

Rollback criteria (automated and manual)
---------------------------------------
Automated rollback (preferred): any of:
- request.latency_ms.p99 increases > 40% for > 2 minutes.
- kernel.queue_depth_avg sustained > 80% for > 60s and accompanied by increase in request errors.
- memory.gpu.fragmentation_pct leads to OOM events.

Manual rollback: triggered by oncall if triage finds systemic regression in model quality (see eval signals) or client-facing error rates > 0.5% over 10m.

Tracing and attribution guidance
-------------------------------
- Ensure each request carries experiment_id, route, and model_variant. Span composition should include: dispatcher -> scheduler -> kernel-agent -> kvcache.
- For expensive experiments, enable 100% traces for canaries for 5–10 minutes to capture tail behaviors.

Examples: short triage checklist for a regression
------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm metric delta with raw per-request data (avoid dashboard smoothing artifacts).
2) Check kernel.exec_time_ms by kernel-type to see if new kernel hints caused regressions.
3) Inspect kvcache.hit_rate and warmup windows; check prefetch logs.
4) Run microbench: single-request microbench with the failing profile using rdx-runtime-local-runner.
5) If kernel-level, annotate a kernel snapshot and assign to kernel-team for kernel rollout revert.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Document owner: runtime-performance guild (alias: #runtime-performance).
- Primary engineering owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example.com).
- Secondary owners: Marco Chen (kernel), Dana Ortiz (profiling/telemetry).
- Pager: runtime-oncall (see oncall rotation page).

Appendix A — canonical metrics queries
--------------------------------------
sections.heading: Statistical rules

sections.body:
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="chat-default",experiment_id=~"EXP.*"}[1m])) by (le))
- kvcache hit rate: sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total{model=~".*"}[1m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_requests_total{model=~".*"}[1m]))

Appendix B — experiment result template (markdown)
--------------------------------------------------
- experiment_id: EXP123
- hypothesis: text
- primary_signals: list with baselines and deltas
- secondary_signals: list
- raw_artifacts: link to perf-db
- statistical_summary: link
- verdict: accept | reject | inconclusive
- triage_notes: free text

Related pages and references
----------------------------
- Runtime profiling playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025
- Benchmarking suite guide: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite-2026
- Autotune framework: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/runtime-autotune-framework-spec-2026

Change log
----------
- 2026-11-15: created by Aisha Patel (first draft).
- 2026-12-21: added bootstrap rules and cost stratification (reviewer: Marco Chen).
- 2027-02-10: updated thresholds and rollout ramping guidance (reviewer: Dana Ortiz).

End of document

payload.page_title: Runtime Simulator Playbook and Operator Index

sections.body: This playbook defines the canonical simulator suite, operator-facing index, and step-by-step validation checklist used to exercise degradation paths, canary rollouts, and SLA acceptance for runtime changes. It is intended for runtime operators, SREs, and experiment owners running pre-release canaries and postmortem reconstructions.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Provide a repeatable simulation matrix that spans: latency tail, KV-cache warmup, kernel contention, memory pressure, quantization-induced quality drift, and mixed-cohort interference.
- Produce deterministic artifacts (replay traces, golden traces, acceptance matrices) that feed the release gating pipeline.
- Offer an operator index mapping common symptoms to simulator scenarios and corresponding escalation/runbook pages.
sections.heading: Scope and intent

sections.body:
- Author: Lina Ortiz (Runtime Infrastructure)
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime team (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
- Oncall contact (operator rotas): runtime-ops@redwood.ai; Pager: #runtime-oncall in Slack
- Escalation: follow SRE escalation ladder; see related_pages for circuit-breaker runbook.
sections.heading: Ownership and roles

sections.body:
The suite is composed of modular scenarios. Each scenario has: description, input corpus, traffic shape, hardware profile, kernel variants, and acceptance thresholds.
1) Latency-tail sculptor
   - Description: injects realistic bursts (90/95/99/99.9 quantiles) across sequence lengths and concurrency shapes.
   - Traffic shapes: steady, microburst (10s), diurnal ramp, randomized spike trains.
   - Hardware profiles: a2-highmem (single GPU), mixed pool (A100+T4), and dedicated-8x (reserved capacity).
   - Acceptance thresholds: 99.9p must not exceed baseline+120ms for production models; see Acceptance Criteria.

2) KV-cache warmup and prefetch simulation
   - Description: synthetic session mixes that reveal cold-start and warmup delta for prefix caching and prefetch heuristics.
   - Workload: long-session (avg 400 tokens), short-chat (avg 40 tokens), streaming token bursts.
   - Key metric: time-to-90%-hit-rate (T90) on KV cache, target <= 25s for dedicated pools.

3) Kernel contention and slot-saturation
   - Description: schedule overlapping kernel windows to exercise admission controller and preemption.
   - Variants: cooperative preemption on/off, batch-slicing enabled, credit accounting stress.
   - Safety checks: no priority inversion lasting >120s; kernel watchdog alerts must fire at 30s.

4) Memory-pressure and eviction cascade
   - Description: ramp synthetic multi-tenant memory growth to trigger cross-tenant eviction and compaction.
   - Acceptance: successful graceful eviction and resident set compaction without OOMs; failed reconcilers must be captured as incident tickets.

5) Quantization fidelity drift (greybox)
   - Description: compare generation quality across float16, int8, and hybrid-quantized kernels using a fixed prompt set.
   - Metrics: ROUGE/CHR-F/semantic-similarity delta, synthetic hallucination score.
   - Thresholds: any quality regression >4% on primary prompts triggers rollback gate.

6) Mixed-cohort interference
   - Description: run heterogeneous tenant mixes (high throughput + low-latency critical) to detect scheduling artifacts.
   - Observability: token-level trace correlation, kernel credit debits, admission latency heatmaps.
sections.heading: Simulator suite overview (matrix)

sections.body:
- Symptom: sudden 99.9p spike across all models
  - Simulator scenario: Latency-tail sculptor — microburst with high concurrency
  - Immediate checks: scheduler-queue-depth, kernel-queue length, NVLink saturation, GPU thermals
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/tail-latency-investigation-and-mitigation-playbook-2026

- Symptom: sustained increase in cold-start errors after deploy
  - Simulator scenario: KV-cache warmup
  - Immediate checks: KV-epoch sync logs, prefix-cache-miss-rate, prefetch worker backlog
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/dynamic-kvcache-resilience-and-warmup-playbook-2026

- Symptom: per-tenant quality regressions after quantization rollout
  - Simulator scenario: Quantization fidelity drift (greybox)
  - Immediate checks: eval-suite pass rates, sample outputs vs golden, embedding-similarity drift
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026

Pre-release acceptance checklist (use when gating canaries or kernel rollouts):
1) Baseline capture: record golden traces for the target service and model (include token-level timing, kernel map, KV hits).
2) Scenario replay: run all simulator scenarios listed above at three scales: smoke (1x), nominal (1–2x), stress (5–10x nominal).
3) Observability validation: ensure telemetry pipelines capture token_id, kernel_id, slot_id, and admission_decision for every request.
4) SLA validation: compute quantile deltas vs baseline. Acceptance rule: for release to proceed, no critical SLA (99.9p latency, error rate, or KV warmup T90) may exceed baseline by >20% or hard thresholds (see numeric list below).
4a) Numeric thresholds (examples):
   - 50p latency delta <= +15ms
   - 95p latency delta <= +50ms
   - 99.9p latency delta <= +120ms
   - Error rate delta <= +0.1% absolute
   - KV T90 delta <= +40%
   - Quality regression >4% (primary prompt set) => block
5) Regression signals: automatic alerts must be raised to #runtime-ci and an incident template must be populated if any metric crosses gate.
6) Canary roll: progressive traffic ramp (5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with a 30–60 minute hold and continuous SLO check. Abort conditions: any threshold breach or anomalous CPU/GPU error logs.
sections.heading: Runbook index (operator quick reference)

sections.body:
A) Running the simulator locally (developer sandbox)
   1. Checkout infra repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/runtime-sim.git
   2. Start environment: cd runtime-sim && scripts/start-sim --profile=dedicated-8x --corpus=golden-prompts.json
   3. Kick off a latency-tail run: ./bin/run-scenario --name=latency_tail --duration=10m --shape=microburst
   4. Collect artifacts: ./bin/collect-artifacts --out=/tmp/sim-artifacts/$(date +%F)-tail

B) Running a canary with simulator validation (CI pipeline)
   1. Trigger pipeline: ci/release/run_canary.yml with param SIM_RUN=true
   2. Pipeline stages: capture-baseline -> run-simulators -> compare-metrics -> gate/abort -> rollout
   3. On failure: pipeline creates an incident with prefilled fields: commit hash, artifact links, failing metric snapshots.
sections.heading: Operator procedures (step-by-step examples)

sections.body:
- Field: token_timestamp — description: per-token timestamp emitted at kernel handoff — retention: 90d
- Field: kernel_id — description: identifier for kernel variant (eg: attention-sharded-v2) — retention: 90d
- Field: admission_decision — description: admission result (allowed/preempted/hedged) — retention: 30d
- Field: kv_hit — description: boolean and hit_latency_ms — retention: 30d
- Field: sample_flags — description: labels for sampled traces (canary/gold/control) — retention: 365d
sections.heading: Observability and telemetry requirements (table)

sections.body:
- Golden traces stored in s3://redwood-ci/runtime-goldens/YYYY-MM-DD/ with metadata JSON including commit, model, and hardware profile.
- Simulator artifacts must include: metrics.csv, token_traces.jsonl (for 1% sample), kernel_profiles.pb, and an HTML perf-diff report.
sections.heading: Artifact management and storage

sections.body:
- Kernel oscillation (symptom: repeated 500ms spikes correlated to kernel-switch events): inspect kernel-profile timeline and admission_decision traces; enable kernel debug mode and reproduce with microburst shape.
- KV epoch skew (symptom: high cache-miss across coordination window): check KV coordinator logs for epoch drift >5s and run kvcache-epoch-repair utility.
- Admission backpressure (symptom: queue length growth + drop in throughput): identify the admission controller heavy path; consider temporary increase in slot count or enable cooperative preemption.
sections.heading: Troubleshooting heuristics (common failure signatures)

sections.body:
- Tail latency investigation: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/tail-latency-investigation-and-mitigation-playbook-2026
- KV warmup & resilience: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/dynamic-kvcache-resilience-and-warmup-playbook-2026
- Quantization rollout gate: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026
- Canary & rollback circuit: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026
sections.heading: Runbook links (operator navigation index)

sections.body:
- Confirm model binary and kernel image checksums match golden (sha256).
- Validate telemetry ingestion end-to-end with a small smoke trace.
- Ensure SLO dashboards have synthetic baselines pinned for the test window.

Appendix A — example perf-diff command (CI):
- ./tools/perf-diff --baseline s3://redwood-ci/runtime-goldens/2026-06-01 --candidate /tmp/sim-artifacts --metrics latency_95,latency_999,error_rate --output report.html

Appendix B — emergency abort template (to be auto-filled by CI on gate breach):
- Title: CANARY ABORT: <service> <commit>
- Short description: Automatic gate breach detected during simulator validation.
- Failing metrics: list with quantile snapshots and links to artifacts.
- Immediate action: Revert route traffic, disable candidate kernels, and open P1 incident.
sections.heading: Data collection checklist (pre-run)

sections.body:
- Simulation harness is intended to be conservative; always re-run failing scenarios at higher sampling to reduce false positives.
- Future work: add NVSwitch-level contention scenario and an asynchronous kernel-handshake injector.
sections.heading: Notes and follow-ups

sections.body:
- 2026-06-10: Created by Lina Ortiz (initial draft)
- 2026-09-14: Added KV warmup T90 thresholds and artifact schema (reviewers: Aisha Patel)
- 2026-11-30: Updated acceptance numeric thresholds and expanded operator procedures (reviewers: Jared Kim, Marco Silva)

payload.page_title: Execution Inspection Proxy — Experimentation & Rollout Runbook

sections.body:
Overview

This page defines the Execution Inspection Proxy (EIP): a lightweight, in-path inspection layer designed to enable low-overhead sampling, causal tracing, and feature experimentation against live inference traffic. The intent is to provide a safe way to surface execution-level signals (kernel selection, batching decisions, KV-cache warmup, and tail latency contributors) without modifying the core runtime or blocking production flows.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Capture causal telemetry for sampled requests: kernel selection, batch composition, queue wait, dispatch, and kernel execution durations.
  - Support non-invasive shadow sampling and replay capture for downstream profiling.
  - Provide a controlled canary rollout pattern with clear safety gates and rollback criteria.
  - Emit structured events compatible with our observability pipeline (OTLP/jaeger-compatible spans + JSON payloads to kinesis).
- Non-goals:
  - This proxy is not a replacement for full kernel-level instrumentation. It intentionally samples and reconstructs rather than tracing every token event.

Architectural overview
- Deployment: the EIP runs as a co-located process on runtime nodes (container sidecar or host process) and accepts a mirrored subset of requests via the request-router. It has two logical components: the fast-path forwarder and the asynchronous inspector.
- Fast-path forwarder:
  - For mirrored/inspected requests, forward to runtime with TCP passthrough and minimal packetization to preserve latency characteristics.
  - Add only a single hop and a configurable metadata header (x-eip-sampled: id, sample-rate, sample-reason).
- Asynchronous inspector:
  - Receives sampling copies via the forwarder and enriches them by collecting decision traces from scheduler hooks and kernel handshake messages.
  - Persists captures to the profiling bucket and emits telemetry events.

Textual diagram
  Request Router --> [Runtime Node] --> (EIP forwarder) --> Runtime Core
                                     
                                     (copied sample) --> (EIP inspector) --> telemetry / profiling-bucket

Kernel scheduling interactions and safety considerations
- Priority propagation:
  1) The EIP must not change runtime scheduling priorities. To avoid priority inversion, the proxy only annotates metadata; it never adjusts request priority headers unless explicitly enabled in experiment mode.
  2) When experiment mode is enabled, a separate gating service (priority-gate) authorizes transient priority hints stored in a short-lived config (TTL 60s) to the scheduler.
- Backpressure and admission control:
  - EIP respects runtime admission controller signals. If the runtime returns HTTP 429 for a mirrored request, inspector drops additional enrichment traffic for that request to avoid amplification.
- Kernel handshake correlation:
  - The inspector consumes the kernel handshake stream (read-only subscription) to correlate kernel ID -> execution timings. This subscription path is throttled to 1% of live handshakes by default.

Profiling & benchmarking plan
- Success metrics for experiment:
  - End-to-end p50 overhead introduced by EIP on observed requests <= 0.5ms.
  - End-to-end p99 overhead <= 5ms and never larger than 5% relative increase over baseline p99.
  - CPU usage for EIP sidecar <= 3% of node CPU under typical traffic; memory overhead < 200MB.
  - Sampling fidelity: inspector correlates >= 95% of sampled requests to kernel handshake when sampling rate is 1/1000.
- Benchmarks to run:
  1) Baseline synthetic workload: 10k RPS mixed seq-lengths (8/64/512) using shadow-generator v2. Command: 
     ./shadow-generator --rps 10000 --mix "0.6:8,0.3:64,0.1:512" --duration 30m --dest <router>
  2) Canary real-traffic mirror: 0.1% live traffic mirrored for 24 hours with continuous telemetry checks.
  3) Load spike stress test: inject a 5x traffic spike for 10 minutes and observe EIP behavior under kernel negotiation churn.
- Measurement guidance:
  - Use histogram exports for latency (client-observed), EIP forwarder add-on latency, and inspector processing time.
  - Collect kernel handshake correlation rate and amount of additional memory allocated for captured artifacts.
  - Compare generation token throughput and tail latency against baseline snapshots collected immediately prior to EIP enablement.

Runbook: Canary rollout (step-by-step)
1) Pre-checks (owner: runtime-ops)
   - Confirm benchmark baseline snapshots exist (p50/p95/p99 for last 24h).
   - Ensure profiling-bucket has >= 5GB free and write policy enforces retention 30d.
   - Verify OTLP pipeline is green and downstream parsers accept EIP schema.
2) Deploy to 2% of fleet as sidecar in passive mode (sampling disabled, headers present) and run 2-hour smoke watch.
3) Enable sampling at 0.01% (1/10000) for 1 hour; run automated checks:
   - CPU delta per node < 2%
   - Additional p99 latency delta < 3%
   - No increase in kernel failure counts or eviction incidents
4) If automated checks pass, raise sample-rate to 0.1% and observe for 6 hours.
5) If still stable, raise to 1% for 24 hours and run the full profiling capture pipeline to produce sample artifacts for kernel team analysis.
6) If any safety gate fails, follow rollback procedure below.

Rollback procedure (critical)
- Trigger conditions (any):
  - Measured p99 latency increase > 5% absolute compared to baseline or > 10% relative increase.
  - Node-level CPU increase > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Any increase in error-rate or kernel OOM/invocations > threshold.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Toggle sampling to 0% via feature-flag (flag name: eip_sampling_rate) and set traffic routing to bypass EIP forwarder.
  2) If bypass fails, stop the EIP process using: systemctl stop eip-sidecar or kubectl delete pod <eip-pod> --namespace runtime-canary
  3) Open incident with runtime-sre and tag priority P1. Attach profiling artifacts.
  4) Follow post-incident diagnostics checklist (see Diagnostics section).

Diagnostics: investigation checklist
- Correlate any latency spike with:
  - Request-size mix changes in the router logs.
  - Kernel handshake error counts in the last 30 minutes.
  - Memory pressure events (dmesg/kernel logs) and GPU eviction traces.
- Useful queries (PromQL examples):
  - avg_over_time(eip_forwarder_latency_ms[5m]) by (node) > 1.0
  - rate(kernel_handshake_errors_total[5m]) > 0
  - sum(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"eip-sidecar.*"}) by (node)

Known issues and mitigations
- Issue: occasional handshake desynchronization during heavy evictions.
  - Symptom: inspector cannot correlate kernel ID to request and marks sample as orphaned.
  - Mitigation: enable conservative sampling (lower rate) during high eviction windows; implement a short buffer (250ms) in inspector to wait for delayed handshake.
- Issue: small spikes in p99 when inspector writes large captures to disk synchronously.
  - Mitigation: use async write workers with backpressure (queue size 512). Limit per-request artifact size to 128KB.
- Issue: increased observability pipeline cardinality when sampling rate becomes large.
  - Mitigation: normalize dimension tags (drop high-cardinality request-id tag in telemetry; reserve it only for artifact payloads).

Telemetry & dashboarding (owner: observability)
- Minimum signals to emit:
  - eip.forwarder.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
  - eip.inspector.processing_ms (histogram)
  - eip.sample.correlation_rate (ratio of inspector->handshake correlates)
  - eip.disk.write_backpressure_events
  - eip.node.cpu_pct and eip.node.mem_bytes
- Suggested dashboards:
  - EIP Health overview (per-cluster): latency trends, CPU/mem, correlation_rate, artifact write volume.
  - Canary gate panel: real-time pass/fail indicators for sampling checks.

Ownership, contacts and escalation
- Feature owner: Jordan Li (eng-serving-runtime)
- Oncall escalation: runtime-sre pager (primary: smsg to #runtime-sre on PagerDuty)
- Observability contact: Priya Nair
- Kernel handshake analysis: Ethan Morales

Appendix: sample config (YAML)
```yaml
# eip-config.yaml
enabled: true
mode: canary # passive | canary | experiment
sampling_rate: 0.001 # fractional (0.001 = 0.1%)
max_artifact_size_bytes: 131072
artifact_write_workers: 4
handshake_subscribe_rate: 0.01 # throttle handshake subscription to 1% by default
forwarder_override_header: "x-eip-sampled"
backpressure_queue_size: 512
```

Appendix: quick CLI & debug commands
- Check status: kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=eip-sidecar -o wide
- Tail logs (fast-path): kubectl -n runtime logs -f deployment/eip-forwarder
- Force disable sampling: curl -X POST $EIP_ADMIN/flags -d '{"eip_sampling_rate": 0}'

Notes & revision history
- 2026-01-15: initial draft and architecture sketch.
- 2026-02-10: added kernel handshake correlation plan and sample-rate gating.
- 2026-03-02: formalized rollout gates, added CLI commands and PromQL examples.

Related reading
- Runtime decision graph and observed behaviour catalog (for expected kernel handshake semantics)
- Kernel-team checklist: kernel-handshake-contract.md
- Observability adapter design notes

If you are preparing a canary for EIP or need help interpreting profiler artifacts, ping the feature owner in #eng-serving-runtime and schedule a 1:1 with the kernel team.

payload.page_title: Runtime Cohesion and Integration Manual

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This manual describes how the serving runtime components must integrate to preserve predictable inference SLAs while enabling safe experimentation. It consolidates architecture contracts, scheduler integration expectations, a compact profiling playbook, benchmarking guidance, release checklists, and concise runbook actions. The audience is runtime engineers, platform owners, and SREs who operate or extend the inference stack.

Scope
-----
Covers the following subsystems and artifacts: inference-router, kernel-coordinator, kernel-manager, kv-cache, fidelity-orchestrator, batching-service, telemetry-adapter, and the benchmarking harness (op-sim). It intentionally excludes SDK-level API ergonomics and customer Console UI.

Design principles
-----------------
- Observable contracts: every handoff between components must carry an event with correlation_id and causality_trace.
- Fail-fast, degrade-safe: fallbacks must preserve API success (200s) with explicit fidelity headers when possible.
- Testability: each integration point must be exercised via the op-sim harness before rollout.
- Bounded blast radius: experimental scheduler plugins run in sandbox cohorts with quota-limited traffic.

Architecture components and responsibilities
------------------------------------------
- inference-router: performs tenant routing, request classification, and initial priority tagging. Must attach request.metadata.priority and request.metadata.expiry_ts.
- kernel-coordinator: authoritative placement decision-maker; returns allocation tokens and kernel_hint (e.g., "segmented-attn-v2", "quantized-8bit").
- kernel-manager: asserts kernel version compatibility, triggers handoff to the GPU dispatcher, and surfaces kernel telemetry with kernel_signature and kernel_commit.
- kv-cache: manages prefix caches per-session; emits cache_warmup events and provides warmup_score (0..1).
- fidelity-orchestrator: maps workload -> model_variant with policy evaluation (latency vs cost vs quality).
- batching-service: consolidates requests, exposes queue_depth and current_burst_size metrics.
- telemetry-adapter: normalises and annotates traces for downstream SLO dashboards.

Scheduler integration contract (must be implemented on every kernel path)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Table: Required fields on kernel allocation response
| field | type | meaning | example |
| correlation_id | string | mirrors router trace | rtr-01b2.. |
| allocation_token | string | ephemeral token to acquire GPU slot | tok-3ef4.. |
| kernel_hint | string | suggested kernel variant | segmented-attn-v2 |
| estimated_tail_ms | int | estimated tail latency for this request shape | 45 |
| fallback_variants | list | ordered fallbacks when capacity misses | [lrg-8q, lrg-4q] |
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) kernel-manager must validate allocation_token within 200ms of issuance.
2) If kernel-manager cannot satisfy kernel_hint, it must return first compatible fallback_variants and set response.header.x-fidelity-degraded = true.
3) Any allocation that waits > 2s must be annotated with queue_backpressure=true and emit an alert to the SLO monitoring stream.

Profiling playbook (compact)
---------------------------
Purpose: enable fast root cause between request-shape, kernel choice, KV hit-rate, and tail-latency.
sections.heading: Behavioral expectations

sections.body:
1) Reproduce under op-sim with identical request distribution (seeded corpus).
2) Enable full trace on a 1% sampleset (trace_level=full) for 10 minutes.
3) Correlate kernel_signature -> kernel_latency_ms histogram and kv_hit boolean.
4) If tail > SLO (95p > 120ms), run microbench: single-tenant kernel warmstart and memory-pressure sweep.
sections.heading: Quick steps

sections.body:
- ./op-sim run --profile-corpus corpuses/production-seed-2026.json --sampling 1%
- curl -H "X-Debug-Trace: capture" https://inference-router/api/v1/debug/trace?request_id=<id>

Benchmarking suite guidance
--------------------------
- Baselines: maintain L1 baselines for the following canonical shapes: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-completion (>=512 tokens), embedding-batch (batch_size=128).
- Metrics to capture: p50, p90, p95 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, CPU steal, KV hit-rate, and per-token cost_estimate_usd.
- Canary policy: new kernel builds must pass the op-sim synthetic corpus with <=+5% p95 regression and <=+2% cost increase versus baseline.
- Repro steps for suspect builds: 1) pin commit, 2) run three independent op-sim runs at scaled load (0.25x, 0.75x, 1.25x), 3) run kernel microbenchmark with isolated device.

Release and rollout checklist (runtime component)
------------------------------------------------
1) Feature branch: include integration tests that validate allocation_token flow.
2) Pre-merge: create a canary matrix (tenants, shapes, model-variants) and run op-sim.
3) Canary: deploy to 5% traffic in region-us-west1 for 24 hours. Monitor: p95 latency, error-rate, kernel-failure-rate.
4) Gradual roll: 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 1h gates and automated rollback on SLO breach.
5) Post-mortem: collect trace samples and a kernel-perf snapshot.

Known issues and mitigations
--------------------------
- Symptom: sporadic 500s on long-completion shapes when KV cache warmup_score is low.
  Mitigation: enable prefetch for sessions with entropy_score < 0.15 and increase kv-cache prewarm concurrency.
- Symptom: kernel-manager reports transient kernel_commit mismatch after rolling kernel update.
  Mitigation: adopt dual-run intersection checks: kernels serve concurrently for 30 minutes while allocation_token includes kernel_commit_v2.
- Symptom: burst-traffic leads to request prioritisation inversion.
  Mitigation: enforce priority drain windows and apply reserve slots for high-SLA tenants (reserve ratio 0.12).

Runbook (quick actions)
----------------------
1) P95 latency spike (owner: runtime-oncall):
   a) check telemetry-adapter for sudden drop in kv_hit_rate and burst in queue_depth.
   b) if kernel failures > 0.5% in last 10m, flip canary fallback routing (set routing.policy.fallback_rate=0.4).
   c) scale up dedicated burst-pool by +20% for 15 minutes.
2) Kernel deadlock (owner: kernel-team):
   a) identify affected host via kernel-heartbeat missing.
   b) set host to drain and restart kernel-manager process with core-dump enabled.
   c) redirect traffic via inference-router override to alternate pool.

Ownership, escalation and docs
-----------------------------
- Primary owner: Runtime Platform team (runtime-platform@redwood.ai).
- Oncall rotation: runtime-oncall (pager duty) handled by eng-sre and runtime engineers.
- Escalation matrix: runtime-oncall -> kernel-team lead -> eng-sre manager -> CPE.

Appendix: sample config snippets
-------------------------------
1) kernel-allocation response (JSON example):
{
  "correlation_id": "rtr-01b2abcd",
  "allocation_token": "tok-3ef4xyz",
  "kernel_hint": "segmented-attn-v2",
  "estimated_tail_ms": "45",
  "fallback_variants": "[lrg-8q,lrg-4q]"
}

2) op-sim command to run canary corpus:
./op-sim run --corpus corpuses/canary-may-2026.json --concurrency 64 --capture-traces yes --output results/canary-may-2026.json

Document history
----------------
- 2026-02-15 authored by Sofia Martinez
- 2026-03-04 reviewed and updated threshold values (Amit Rao)
- 2026-06-10 added runbook quick actions and profiling command examples (Claire Jensen)

Related reading and links
-------------------------
See also: runtime-decision-graph-and-observed-behaviour-catalog-2026 (architecture), latency-sensitivity-and-graceful-migration-playbook-2026 (scheduling), runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025 (profiling).
