payload.page_title: Third-party accelerator compatibility and dependency matrix (compatibility manifest)

sections.body:
Summary:
This page is the canonical compatibility and dependency matrix for third-party accelerators that the runtime supports or plans to support. It codifies driver/runtime/library versions, expected kernel features, known incompatibilities, required CI smoke tests, ownership, and an automated manifest format (JSON) used by our onboarding toolchain. Use this when: planning support for a new accelerator, triaging inference regressions on a new hardware class, or validating release gates before a runtime rollout.

Goals:
- Capture the minimal set of platform packages (drivers, runtimes, libs) required for the serving runtime to deliver production SLOs.
- Provide reproducible test matrix entries used by CI and the hardware lab.
- Surface common failure modes and triage steps specific to each vendor.
- Define rollback and mitigation procedures when a hardware-specific kernel or driver causes regressions.

Scope and conventions:
- This document covers: NVIDIA (CUDA/NVML/NCCL), AMD (ROCm/MIOpen), AWS accelerators (Inferentia/Trainium), Intel/OneAPI-backed accelerators, Graphcore/Poplar, and other partner ASICs where we have lab access.
- Each matrix row includes: vendor, model family, required host kernel ABI, driver/runtime version range, critical libraries, recommended Docker base images, CI test IDs, owner, and known-risk flags.
- Version ranges are inclusive. Entries marked "experimental" must pass the experimental-canary CI suite, not just the smoke suite.

Compatibility matrix (text table):
Note: use this table as a quick reference. The source-of-truth is the JSON manifest in the repository at infra/accelerator-manifests/compatibility-manifest.json.

| Vendor | Family / Models | Host kernel ABI | Driver / Runtime | Critical libs / plugins | Recommended image tag | CI test(s) | Owner | Risk notes |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|-----------|-------|------------|
| NVIDIA | A100, H100 (Tensor) | linux-5.15+ (glibc ABI stable) | CUDA 12.2 - 12.4, NVIDIA driver 535+ | cuBLAS, cuDNN, NCCL, NVML | redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026 | ci-accel-nvidia-smoke, ci-nvlink-stress | runtime-hw | NVLink firmware mismatch causes memory teleport errors (see known issues) |
| AMD | MI250, MI300 | linux-5.15+ (ROCm-ready ABI) | ROCm 5.8 - 6.0 | MIOpen, ROCm NCCL-compatible libs | redwood/runtime-amd:rocm5.8-rt-2026 | ci-accel-amd-smoke, ci-rocm-memory-fft | runtime-hw | GPU page table fragmentation risk under high concurrency |
| AWS | Inferentia | linux-5.10+ (aws kernel) | Neuron SDK 2.3+ | neuron-libs, neuron-runtime | redwood/runtime-aws:neuron2.3-rt | ci-aws-inferentia-smoke | platform-partner | Binary ABI for Neuron is sensitive to compiler flags; require vendor-signed kernels |
| Intel | Gaudi/ Habana (Partner) | linux-5.15+ | Poplar / OneAPI stacks | poplar-rt, onednn | redwood/runtime-intel:oneapi-2026-rt | ci-intel-accel-smoke | runtime-hw | Driver installer writes kernel modules to non-standard paths; watch mknod/udev permissions |
| Graphcore | IPU-M2000 | linux-5.15+ | Poplar 2.x series | poplar-plugins | redwood/runtime-ipu:poplar2-rt | ci-ipu-smoke | runtime-hw | High cold-start memory usage; require warmup harness |

(For an up-to-date machine-readable matrix, see infra/accelerator-manifests/compatibility-manifest.json in the infra repo.)

Manifest format (example JSON snippet):
This is the canonical object the onboarding automation consumes. Store one file per vendor-family in infra/accelerator-manifests/.

{
  "vendor": "nvidia",
  "family": "h100",
  "models": ["h100-sxm", "h100-pcie"],
  "host_kernel_min": "5.15",
  "driver_version_range": "12.2:12.4",
  "required_packages": ["nvidia-driver>=535", "cuda-toolkit>=12.2", "libnccl>=2.15"],
  "recommended_image": "redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026",
  "ci_gate": "ci-accel-nvidia-smoke",
  "risk_flags": ["nvlink_firmware_sensitivity"]
}
(When editing the manifest, increment the manifest_version field and attach the matching lab test run id.)

CI and lab test design:
- Smoke suite (ci-*-smoke): quick boot, telemetry, single-request inference for canonical models, KV cache sanity, and basic memory pressure. Completes in < 5 minutes per node. Required for all PRs that touch runtime scheduler or kernel selection.
- Stress suite (ci-*-stress): multi-concurrency sustained runs, NVLink/PCIe saturation tests, rendezvous N random seeds to detect numerical drift. Runs in ~2 hours across our lab pool. Used for release gating on major driver bumps.
- Fidelity suite (ci-*-fidelity): compares output distributions against golden corpora, quantization toggles, and mixed-precision paths. Used when enabling quantization profiles.

CI matrix YAML example (used by our GitHub Actions):

name: Accelerator Compatibility Matrix
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  matrix-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        vendor: [nvidia, amd, aws]
        model_family: [h100, a100, mi300, inferentia]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Launch lab node (or mock)
        run: ./infra/labctl/launch_node --vendor ${{ matrix.vendor }} --family ${{ matrix.model_family }}
      - name: Run smoke tests
        run: ./infra/ci/run_compatibility_smoke.sh --manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/${{ matrix.vendor }}-${{ matrix.model_family }}.json

Known failure modes and triage playbook (quick reference):
1) Driver mismatch at startup (symptoms: driver load failures, NVML unavailable, crate reports "missing kernel symbols").
   - Commands: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv; rocminfo; sudo modinfo nvidia
   - If driver ABI mismatch: pin to the last known-good driver (see infra/accelerator-manifests/last-known-good) and trigger a canary rollout.
2) NVLink firmware mismatch (symptoms: inter-GPU copy hang, elevated kernel errors, OOMs during large KV cache warmups).
   - Triage: check nvidia-smi -q -d LINK; check firmware version table in infra/hardware-inventory/firmware.csv. If mismatch detected: set scheduling policy to avoid cross-socket NVLink paths (see mitigation below) and file an infra ticket for firmware alignment.
3) Host kernel OOPS when loading vendor kernel modules (symptoms: kernel oops, machine reboots, module load stacktrace).
   - Triage: capture vmcore if possible; collect /var/log/kern.log; isolate kernel version and report to partner. Revert kernel update and boot previous AMI.
4) Inference numerical drift after driver update (symptoms: fidelity alerts, increased model perplexity).
   - Triage: run ci-*-fidelity suite on the same commit+driver to confirm; if deterministic, mark driver as blocked for quantized paths and force fallback to float kernels; open follow-up with research and vendor.

Mitigations and operational knobs:
- Scheduler-level mitigation: 'evict-across-nvlink' boolean in scheduling profiles. When true, the scheduler will prefer cross-socket placement only for requests that are tagged as high-throughput and tolerant of additional latency.
- Kernel selection fallback: runtime keeps a per-node kernel-hint file produced by the onboarding manifest. If a kernel path is missing at startup, runtime will: 1) degrade to a compatible kernel plugin (if available), 2) reduce concurrency quota for the tenant, and 3) emit an operational alert with a suggested rollback.
- Container image pinning: all production pools use image digests (sha256) instead of tags. The manifest includes recommended image digests under recommended_image_digest.

Rollback and canary process for driver/runtime changes:
1) Staging validation: the proposed driver/runtime version must pass the smoke and stress suites in staging (staging-lab with 3 nodes) and not regress more than 1% on 95th p99 latency for canonical prompts.
2) Canary: roll to 5% of production traffic in a single region with canary telemetry enabled. Observe per-model fidelity metrics for 24 hours.
3) Rollback criteria: any of the following triggers a rollback: p99 latency increase >10% vs baseline, fidelity regression >0.5% for golden prompts, GPU hardware errors >0.1% of requests.
4) Rollback steps (operator):
   - Set scheduling policy to avoid affected pool(s): curl -X POST $RUNTIME_API/pools/scale -d '{"pool":"h100-rt-prod","target":0.9}'
   - Trigger node drain: infra/labctl/drain_node --node h100-rt-12
   - Re-image node with last-known-good driver image: infra/ami-bootstrap/reimage --ami ami-xyz --manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/last-known-good/nvidia-h100.json
   - Monitor: validate smoke-suite; close incident if green.

Ownership and contact matrix (text):
- runtime-hw (owner): Priya Nambiar, Luis Ortega — Responsible for manifests, smoke tests, and lab coordination.
- infra (owner): Jonah Park — Responsible for AMIs, kernel builds, and lab node boots.
- research/applied-ml: Maya Chen — Responsible for fidelity suite, golden corpora, and drift triage.
- platform-partner: Partner PM / Partner Eng — vendor-specific escalation.

Lab checklist before declaring full support:
1) Run full stress and fidelity suites for 48 hours across 3 nodes.
2) Validate billing/chargeback hooks for the pool (cost attribution).
3) Document warmup and eviction behaviors in the runtime pool README.
4) Add entries to hardware-inventory, include firmware and BIOS versions.

Operational examples and debug commands (cheat sheet):
- Check basic GPU health (NVIDIA): nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,LINK
- Check NVLink details: nvidia-smi -q -d LINK | egrep -A4 "Link"
- ROCm diagnostics: /opt/rocm/bin/rocminfo; /opt/rocm/bin/rocm-smi -d 0 --showtemp
- Container runtime test: docker run --rm --gpus all --privileged redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026 nvidia-smi -L
- Kernel module info: sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 40

Appendix A — Example compatibility test case (text):
- Test id: ci-accel-nvidia-smoke-001
- Purpose: Validate A100/H100 basic inference path and KV cache warmup under 8 concurrent workers.
- Steps:
  1) Boot node with manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/nvidia-h100.json
  2) Pull recommended image digest and run containerized test harness: infra/ci/harness/run_infer_test.sh --image sha256:abcd... --concurrency 8 --model gpt-redwood-small
  3) Assert: 95th latency < 200ms, memory growth < 2GB/worker after 30s warmup, no GPU driver errors in dmesg.

Appendix B — How to update this manifest:
1) Edit infra/accelerator-manifests/<vendor>-<family>.json and bump manifest_version.
2) Run ./infra/ci/run_compatibility_smoke.sh --manifest <path> locally against a mock node or in the lab.
3) Create a PR against infra with the manifest and the lab run id attached. Tag runtime-hw and infra teams as reviewers.

Change log (brief):
- 2026-05-12: initial published manifest and CI matrix (Priya Nambiar).
- 2026-08-16: added ROCm 5.8 compatibility entries and stress test IDs (Luis Ortega).
- 2026-10-03: added Graphcore IPU entry and expanded rollback procedure (Priya Nambiar).

Related resources (internal):
- infra/accelerator-manifests/ (repo)
- infra/hardware-inventory/firmware.csv
- infra/ci/ (compatibility test harness)
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/runtime-onboarding-for-third-party-accelerators-2026
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/seamless-model-swap-and-kv-consistency-guide-2025

If you are adding a new accelerator family and do not have lab access, open an infra-lab request with subject: "New accelerator onboarding - <vendor> <family>" and attach expected manifest draft.

End of document.

sections.body:
Overview:
This document defines the canonical approach for enriching runtime telemetry (traces, kernel events, request metadata) with contextual labels and cost tags so downstream consumers (alerting, billing, profiler, experiments) can reliably join signals. The goal is consistent, low-cost enrichment that enables accurate SLO attribution, cost-per-inference accounting, and fidelity-aware debugging across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Why this matters:
- Inconsistent labels are the single largest source of signal fragmentation when debugging tail latency and kernel regressions.
- Cost and energy tags let product and finance teams reconcile per-route economics without pulling raw traces.
- Enriched, compact traces speed triage for oncall by surfacing the minimum causal set of attributes needed to reproduce or route incidents.

Principles:
1) Minimal, stable keyset: restrict primary labels to a small set that is unlikely to change (see Label Taxonomy).
2) Schema-first: all labels follow the canonical key names and types in this doc; any extension requires a review.
3) Cost-aware sampling: enrich higher-value requests at a higher sampling rate; inexpensive warmup traces sampled low.
4) Privacy & minimal PII: do not attach user PII or raw prompt text to traces. Use hashes or prompt-ids where needed.
5) Low-latency enrichment: enrichment must not add more than 1 ms on the request path in p95. Use asynchronous enrichers for non-blocking attributes.

Label taxonomy (canonical keys):
- request.id: stable UUID for the user request (string)
- route.name: product route or API path (string)
- model.variant: model name and variant (e.g., gptx-16q8) (string)
- kernel.path: kernel family / variant invoked (string)
- hw.pool: accelerator pool identifier (e.g., a100-pool-3) (string)
- cost.token_estimate: integer estimated token count (stringified integer)
- fidelity.flag: one of [full, approximate, degraded] (string)
- kvcache.hit_ratio: float (0.0-1.0) represented as string
- customer.tier: free | standard | enterprise (string)
- region: cloud region (string)
- trace.version: schema version (string)

Note: store numeric values as strings for telemetry pluggability and to avoid downstream parsing discrepancies.

Table: retention and storage hints (recommended):
- traces.enriched.retention: 30d (for fully enriched traces used in oncall workflows)
- traces.minimal.retention: 7d (for minimal traces used only for perf sampling)
- aggregated.metrics.retention: 365d
- cold-storage.export: weekly snapshots to S3 for compliance (retention 2y)

Sampling policy (high-level):
1) Baseline sampling: 0.5% of all requests capture minimal trace (spans + request.id + route.name).
2) Enriched sampling tiers:
   - High-value routes (customer.tier=enterprise or routes flagged by product): 20% enriched.
   - Potential-regressions: traffic flagged by the anomaly-detector (see procedure) gets 100% enrichment for 1h.
   - Manual oncall escalations: toggle enrich=true via /api/operator/enrich-toggle for the given route for immediate 15-minute capture.
3) Dynamic cost weighting: If cost.token_estimate > 10k, escalate enriched sampling by +5x for that request bucket.

Enrichment pipeline (component roles):
- Request Ingress (lightweight): attaches request.id, route.name, and region synchronously.
- Async Enricher (nonblocking): fetches model.variant, hw.pool membership, kvcache.hit_ratio from the runtime metadata service; annotates trace with these fields.
- Cost Estimator (streaming): estimates token count using header hints and concise tokenizer lookup; writes cost.token_estimate into trace.
- Privacy Redactor: replaces prompt text with prompt.id before long-term retention.

CLI examples:
- Toggle enrichment for route for 15m (operator):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" 
    https://internal-api.redwood.local/operator/enrich-toggle 
    -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/llm", "enrich": true, "duration_m":15}'

- Query enriched trace sample (example using internal tracer):
  rtr-cli get-trace --id 8a7f3c2b --compact=true

JSON example of a canonical enriched trace (compact):
{
  "trace.id": "8a7f3c2b-9c1d-4f8d-bf3a-abcdef012345",
  "route.name": "/v1/generate/completion",
  "model.variant": "redwood/longformer-32k-16q8",
  "kernel.path": "attention-sharded-v2",
  "hw.pool": "a100-pool-3",
  "cost.token_estimate": "1200",
  "fidelity.flag": "full",
  "kvcache.hit_ratio": "0.82",
  "customer.tier": "standard",
  "trace.version": "v1"
}

Enrichment performance budget:
- Synchronous enrichment: <1 ms p95
- Full async enrichment completion: <50 ms median, <200 ms p99
- Failure modes: if enricher times out, record enricher.timeout=true and proceed without fields to avoid on-path tail inflation.

Debugging and incident workflows (runbook excerpt):
1) If tail latency breach detected for route X:
   a) Check sampled enriched traces for route.name==X in the last 15m.
   b) Filter traces where fidelity.flag != full and compare kernel.path distributions.
   c) If kernel.path change or hw.pool migration is visible, escalate to runtime-kernel-oncall and attach 5 representative traces (use rtr-cli sample-attach).
2) If cost-per-inference anomalies observed:
   a) Aggregate cost.token_estimate by model.variant and route.name for the window.
   b) If sudden token estimate inflation, run tokenizer audit (tokenizer-audit --route X --window 1h).
   c) Notify SRE and product: add label incident.cost_inflation.

Extension and governance process:
- To add a new canonical label or change type, open an ADR and include: motivation, schema change, migration plan, and storage impact estimate.
- Small labels (non-critical) may be trialed as optional.enricher.* keys for 4 weeks before approval.

Table: enforcement thresholds and alerts:
- Missing trace.version on >1% enriched traces for 1h -> P2 alert to observability team.
- enricher.timeout > 0.5% of enriched traces in 5m -> P1 to runtime infra.
- prompt-id absent on any trace stored beyond 7d -> security incident, restrict retention immediately.

Operational rollout checklist (numbered):
1) Deploy async enricher v1 to canary fleet (10% traffic).
2) Run canary for 72h, monitor enricher.timeout and enrichment-completion latency.
3) Validate label presence against schema for 95% of enriched traces.
4) Run tokenizer-audit on canary traffic to confirm cost estimates alpha accuracy within 15%.
5) Gradual ramp to 100% canary-to-prod over 48h if all checks pass.

Ownership and contacts:
- Observability Infrastructure (primary): Marcus Lee (oncall rotation: infra-observe@redwood.com)
- Runtime Telemetry Enricher owner: Elena Rodriguez
- Security & Privacy reviewer: Aisha Patel

Appendix A — Example instrumenter snippet (Python):
# pseudo-code, meant for the runtime's tracer shim
from internal_tracer import start_span, annotate
span = start_span('request')
span.annotate('request.id', request_id)
span.annotate('route.name', route_name)
# schedule async enricher task
async_enricher.schedule(request_id, context_headers)

Appendix B — Migration notes for older schemas:
- Older traces used trace.schema v0 and stored model and kernel under model_info.*; ingestion pipeline must map model_info.name -> model.variant and kernel.variant -> kernel.path at read time. Backfill of trace.version=v1 is optional; if required, create a daily job to migrate high-value route traces first.

Related artifacts and reading:
- runtime-telemetry-sampling-cost-aware-profiling-2027 (sampling rules)
- kernel-telemetry-annotation-guidelines-2025 (kernel-specific annotation practices)
- privacy-redaction-spec-2024

Document change log:
- 2024-11-12 (Elena Rodriguez): created initial draft.
- 2025-02-10 (Marcus Lee): clarified sampling multipliers for token-heavy requests.
- 2025-04-02 (Aisha Patel): added privacy enforcement thresholds and updated retention hints.

payload.page_title: Operational Signal Fabric and Cohorted Scheduler Handbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This handbook describes the Operational Signal Fabric and the Cohorted Scheduler approach used by Redwood's serving runtime to map runtime observability signals to scheduler decisions, incident triage actions, profiling experiments, and benchmarking checks. It is written for runtime engineers, SREs, and subsystem owners responsible for scheduler policies, telemetry alignment, and production rollouts.

Goals
-----
- Define a single signal taxonomy (the Signal Fabric) that is consumed by scheduling heuristics, alerting rules, and profiling experiments.
- Describe how execution cohorts are derived, annotated, and persisted for deterministic investigations.
- Provide concrete runbooks for common scheduler/resilience incidents and profiling experiments.
- Give a rollout checklist for scheduler policy changes that minimizes regressions in latency, cost, and fidelity.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all runtime scheduler components (priority governor, admission controller, kernel mapper), kernel plugins that expose telemetry hooks, and the profiling/benchmarking suites that validate scheduling changes. This document does NOT specify kernel implementation details; it focuses on operational mapping between signals and scheduler behavior.

Core concepts
-------------
1) Signal Fabric: canonical names, units, and retention for runtime signals consumed by scheduling logic. Signals are emitted at three layers: request-surface (API/router), kernel-dispatch (runtime kernels), and infra (node/accelerator).
2) Cohorts: deterministic classification of requests into buckets based on stable attributes (model_id, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, client_tier, route_flags). Cohorts allow targeted profiling and rollback.
3) Decision Bindings: declarative rules that map signal thresholds and cohort identities to scheduler actions (prioritize, throttle, preempt, fallback to variant).
4) Fidelity Guards: safety checks (quality/eval) attached to any scheduler action that can change model variant/quantization.

Signal Fabric (canonical table)
--------------------------------
| Signal name                     | Layer           | Unit           | Cardinality | Producer                 | TTL   | Use cases |
|---------------------------------|-----------------|----------------|-------------|--------------------------|-------|-----------|
| request.p90_latency_ms          | request-surface | milliseconds   | per-route   | router                   | 90d   | SLO monitoring, alerts |
| kvcache.hit_rate                | kernel-dispatch | fraction (0-1) | shard       | kvcache                  | 30d   | batching hints, warmup |
| kernel.queue_depth              | kernel-dispatch | integer        | shard       | dispatcher               | 14d   | admission control, preempt decisions |
| node.gpu_util_pct               | infra           | percent        | node        | node_agent               | 60d   | capacity planning, admission |
| token.emission_rate_per_s       | request-surface | tokens/s       | tenant      | runtime_router           | 30d   | billing/cost throttles |
| request.sequence_bucket         | request-surface | enum (S/M/L/XL) | per-request | router                   | 90d   | cohorting, kernel hints |
| kernel.latency_per_op_ms        | kernel-dispatch | ms/op          | kernel      | kernel_profiler          | 90d   | kernel selection, canary gating |

Note: Cardinality indicates the level at which the signal is indexed. Keep high-cardinality signals off the hot path unless sampled.

Cohort definition and lifecycle
-------------------------------
- Cohort keys: model_id, model_variant_id, sequence_bucket, client_tier, route_tag.
- Generation: router computes the cohort_key at request admission and attaches headers: X-Runtime-Cohort: model=v3.1;var=quant-8bit;len=XL;tier=gold;route=chat_inline
- Storage: cohort annotations are copied into trace/span baggage and a lightweight cohort index (redis-backed) for 72 hours to simplify postmortem replay.
- Decay policy: if a cohort observes < 0.1% of traffic over 24h, mark as transient and expire cohort metadata to reduce index noise.

Decision bindings (examples)
---------------------------
Decision bindings are simple JSON-like rules (stored in policy-service) that map signal predicates to actions. Example binding:

```
{
  "binding_id": "bind-high-queue-preempt-2026-01",
  "predicate": "kernel.queue_depth > 120 AND node.gpu_util_pct > 85",
  "cohort_filter": "*",
  "action": "preempt_background_slots",
  "action_params": {"max_preempt_per_node": 2, "backoff_minutes": 5},
  "safety_check": "fidelity_guard_alpha"
}
```

- Predicates are evaluated by the decision engine at 10s cadence. Keep predicates simple to avoid evaluation amplification.
- Actions include: increase_priority, decrease_priority, admit_burst, preempt_background_slots, route_to_variant, throttle_tenant.

Scheduler resilience runbooks (triage-first)
-------------------------------------------
1) Symptom: sudden p99 latency increase for a high-traffic route.
   - Owner: runtime-oncall
   - Steps:
     1. Query recent cohorts for the route: kubectl run query-cohorts --route=<route> --since=1h
     2. Check request.p90_latency_ms and kernel.queue_depth across cohorts.
     3. If kernel.queue_depth > 100 on > 3 nodes, execute emergency admission: policy-service apply emergency-admit=throttle-background
     4. If queue depth is concentrated in a cohort with sequence_bucket=XL, enable sequence-length-capping variant: policy-service route cohort -> variant=shortened-context
     5. Open incident with SRE and attach cohort index snapshot and the last 3 kernel.profiler traces.

2) Symptom: kernel plugin experiencing increased op failure rate.
   - Owner: kernel-team
   - Steps:
     1. Collect kernel.latency_per_op_ms and kernel.plugin_errors by kernel version.
     2. If error rate > 0.5% for 5m, pin runtime to previous kernel and trigger canary rollback: rollout-service rollback kernel-plugin --to=stable-20260201
     3. Run controlled profiling (see Profiling experiments) for the failing kernel on a replay corpus.

Profiling experiments: structure and templates
--------------------------------------------
Purpose: isolate scheduler and kernel interactions for targeted cohorts.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Select cohort(s) and timeframe (use cohort index).
2. Construct replay corpus (use request-surface traces and synthetic sequences to reproduce distribution).
3. Baseline: run 3x baseline runs with current scheduler policy, collect kernel.latency_per_op_ms, kvcache.hit_rate, and tail latency distribution.
4. Apply one policy change at a time (decision binding tweak), re-run 3x, and compare deltas.
5. Metrics to record: p50/p90/p99 latency, per-token energy (if available), kvcache warmup time, variance across runs.
6. Tag experiment with experiment_id and attach results to policy change PR.

Profiling CLI snippets
---------------------
- Build replay corpus:
  ./tooling/replay-builder --cohort "model=v3.1;len=M" --since 2026-02-14T00:00:00Z --out corpus.tgz
- Run replay with scheduler override (local lab):
  ./tooling/runtime-replay --corpus corpus.tgz --scheduler-overrides ./overrides/policy-test.json --repeat 3 --collect-traces

Benchmark and validation checklist for scheduler change
-----------------------------------------------------
- Unit gates (automated):
  - scheduler-policy-lint: no circular bindings
  - predicate-safety-check: no policy that can reduce admitted capacity below 60% for any tenant without a manual guard
- Staging gates (synthetic):
  - run mixed-load benchmark against production-like mix for 30m; verify p90 delta < 8% and p99 delta < 15% for stable cohorts.
  - run capacity burst test to verify no kernel plugin regressions.
- Canary gates (shadow & live):
  - enable policy for 5% tenant shadow for 24h, compare decisions and ensure no negative action rate > 0.1%
  - live canary on non-critical region for 4h; require rollback if any cohort exceeds fidelity-guard threshold.

Release and rollout checklist (scheduler policy changes)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Author creates policy change PR with decision bindings and rationale.
2. Automated policy lint and unit tests pass.
3. Run profiling experiments and attach results to PR.
4. Execute staging benchmark checklist and attach artifacts.
5. Reviewer sign-off from kernel-team and SRE.
6. Staged canary (shadow + 5% live) for 24h.
7. If canary is green, ramp to 25% for 12h, then 100% with monitoring.
8. Post-rollout 48h observation window; capture cohort-indexed telemetry and store artifacts under /artifacts/scheduler-rollouts/<pr-number>.

Safety and fidelity guards
-------------------------
- Any action that routes to a lower-fidelity variant must require an active fidelity_guard check that validates the last known eval delta < configured threshold (default 0.03 quality drop).
- Quality-eval integration: policy-service must call eval-api with a short prompt set for the affected cohort before allowing auto-variant-routing in production.

Operational telemetry dashboards and alerts (recommended)
------------------------------------------------------
- Dashboard: "Scheduler Decision Surface" (node-level tiles, cohort heatmap, decision-rate chart).
- Essential alerts:
  - A1: kernel.queue_depth > 150 for > 3 nodes (P0)
  - A2: preempt_action_rate > 5% sustained for 10m (P1)
  - A3: fidelity_guard_failures > 0.1% for 30m (P1)
  - A4: cohort.latency_regression_delta_p99 > 20% (P0)

Ownership and contacts
---------------------
- Scheduler policy service: owner "runtime-policy-team" (pager: #runtime-policy)
- Kernel plugins: owner "kernel-team" (pager: #kernel-team)
- Oncall escalation path: runtime-oncall -> runtime-sre -> kernel-lead -> eng-manager

Appendix A: sample decision binding catalog (short)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Background fairness governor (default): throttle tenants consuming > 75% of background credits in 5m window.
2) Sequence-length capper: for cohorts with median_sequence_length > XL and p99 queue_depth > 100, cap to L variant.
3) Opportunistic admission: if node.gpu_util_pct < 35% and queue_depth < 20, allow burst admissions up to 50 concurrent short jobs.

Appendix B: common investigation commands and scripts
-----------------------------------------------------
- cohort index dump for route: ./tools/cohort-dump --route=chat_inline --since=2h --out=cohort-dump.json
- decision binding dry-run: curl -X POST https://policy-service.internal/v1/dry-run -d @overrides/policy-test.json -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- collect trace bundle for a node: ./tools/collect-trace --node node-123 --since 2026-02-17T12:00:00Z --out node-123-traces.tgz

Related reading and links
-------------------------
- Kernel telemetry synthesis (internal): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/kernel-telemetry-annotation-guidelines-2025
- Runtime decision graphs and behavior catalog: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/runtime-decision-graph-and-observed-behaviour-catalog-2026

Change history
--------------
- 2025-11-13: created by Ava Martinez (initial draft)
- 2026-02-18: added profiling templates and updated cohort decay policy (Samir Patel review)

Contact and feedback
--------------------
Send feedback to #runtime-policy or email avam@redwood-inference.example."

payload.page_title: Runtime safety: telemetry contracts and chaos-embargo plan

sections.body:
This document defines a compact, operational telemetry contract for the serving runtime and the engineering policy we call the "chaos embargo"—time windows and gating rules that restrict disruptive experiments (kernel rollouts, hardware rebalancing, large-scale quantization flips, and canary expansion) unless safety conditions are met. The goal is to reduce blast radius during peak business hours and give SRE/Owners deterministic signal windows for fast assessment.

1) Why this exists
- Serving runtime changes interact with low-level GPU kernels and KV caching; small regressions can cause correlated tail-latency spikes and cross-tenant noise.
- We must guarantee experiments only proceed when essential health signals are stable, and we must have a fast path to freeze/rollback if we observe early regressions.

2) Scope and applicability
- Applies to all changes that can affect runtime execution fidelity, scheduling, or memory (examples: kernel binary changes, scheduler policy updates, eviction heuristics, major quantization profile flips, large-scale model swaps).
- Does not apply to pure documentation or client-side SDK changes.

3) Telemetry contract (signals & canonical definitions)
- Source: Prometheus metrics, per-request traces, aggregated token histograms, runtime kernel telemetry, and error logs.
- Canonical signals (names used in alerts/queries):
  - runtime_request_p95_latency_ms (histogram p95; measured at ingress service boundary)
  - runtime_request_p99_latency_ms
  - kernel_execution_tail_ratio (fraction of kernel calls > 2x median kernel latency)
  - kvcache_miss_rate (per-shard)
  - kvcache_warmup_time_seconds (median warmup per session)
  - gpu_memory_pressure_pct (95th percentile across nodes)
  - grpc_connection_error_rate (errors / minute per node)
  - fidelity_degradation_score (synthetic eval online regression score, see section 6)
  - tenant_error_spike_ratio (ratio of tenant error rate to baseline over last 15m)

- Contract guarantees:
  - All experiments must publish a 48h baseline for the signals above before rollout starts. Baseline must include at least one high-traffic weekday peak if available.
  - Signal tags: every metric must be tagged with release_id, kernel_variant, region, and cohort.

4) Safety thresholds (gating rules for experiments)
- Absolute thresholds (fail immediately):
  - runtime_request_p99_latency_ms > 1200ms (global) OR > 2x baseline p99 for the cohort -> immediate abort/rollback.
  - kernel_execution_tail_ratio increases by > 3x relative to baseline -> pause rollout and investigate.
  - gpu_memory_pressure_pct > 93% sustained for 5 minutes -> reject new allocations and drain optional cohorts.
  - tenant_error_spike_ratio > 4 -> trigger page and throttle new canary traffic.

- Degradation windows (require human review if crossed):
  - runtime_request_p95_latency_ms increases by 20-40% for an hour -> require PM + SRE review before further rollout.
  - fidelity_degradation_score drop >= 5 points on production eval set -> require product signoff prior to further expansion.

5) Chaos embargo policy (calendar and exception flow)
- Default embargo windows (no disruptive experiments allowed):
  - Monday–Friday 07:00–20:00 UTC (company peak coverage hours)
  - Any documented customer QBR windows or enterprise go-live days (tagged in the calendar)
- Allowed during embargo: monitoring-only tests, small non-disruptive config changes (no kernel swaps, no canary expansion > 2% traffic).
- Exceptions: emergency fixes or mitigations may be executed inside embargo with the following steps:
  1. Pager duty owner (SRE lead) triages and documents the risk.
  2. Run the preflight signal checklist (section 7) and gain approval from on-call and release owner.
  3. If approval granted, a narrow mitigation can be executed with real-time monitoring and a rollback playbook on standby.

6) Fidelity evaluation (online synthetic checks)
- Short synthetic eval harness runs on canary cohort traffic to compute fidelity_degradation_score. The harness compares a small set of golden prompts and checks:
  - Semantic divergence (embedding cosine distance threshold)
  - Token-level generation anomalies (sudden repetition or cutoffs)
  - Safety classification regressions (NLP safety binary classifier rate)
- Scoring is normalized to a 0–100 scale with historical baselining. A drop of 2–5 points is a yellow flag; >5 points is a hard stop for canary expansion.

7) Preflight checklist (must be completed before non-trivial rollout)
- Automated checks (pass/fail):
  - Baseline metrics uploaded for 48h and validated by the release pipeline.
  - Smoke test suite green on canary (latency p95 within 15% of baseline; error rate <= 2x baseline).
  - KVCache checksum/consistency check for canary shards.
  - Canary synthetic fidelity harness run with result >= 95% of baseline score.
- Manual approvals (must be recorded in rollout ticket):
  - Release owner (engineer) confirms risk and rollback plan.
  - On-call SRE approves time window and monitoring readiness.
  - PM or product owner acknowledges potential user-visible impact for fidelity-sensitive releases.

8) Operational procedures and runbook snippets
- Immediate abort (scripted):
  1. Run the control API to set canary weight to 0 for release_id = <id>. Example curl (replace tokens):
     curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/release/adjust" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
     -d '{"release_id":"RELEASE-1234","canary_weight":0}'
  2. Trigger automatic rollback job: POST /release/rollback with same auth header.
  3. Open a critical incident with tag runtime-regression and notify product and infra channels.

- Emergency GPU memory pressure mitigation:
  1. Set admission controller to "restrict" for affected pool: kubectl -n runtime patch configmap admission --patch '{"data":{"mode":"restrict"}}'
  2. Evict non-critical cohorts via the operator: runtimectl evict --pool=persistent --cohort=best-effort
  3. If pressure persists, initiate cross-region spill policy: runtimectl spill --target-region=us-west-2

9) Example Prometheus rule (text form):
- ALERT RuntimeP99Spike
  IF increase(runtime_request_p99_latency_ms[5m]) > (2 * baseline_p99_ratio)
  FOR 2m
  LABELS {severity="page", team="runtime"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Runtime p99 latency doubled for cohort {{ $labels.cohort }}"}

10) Dashboard and runbook links (actionable views)
- Canary health dashboard: /dashboards/runtime/canary-health (contains p50/p95/p99, kernel tail heatmap, synthetic fidelity, kvcache per-shard heatmap)
- Rollout inspector (time-travel query): /dashboards/runtime/rollout-inspector?release_id={{release_id}}
- Incident runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-incident-orchestration-and-capacity-decision-matrix-2026

11) Ownership, cadence, and review
- Owners:
  - Telemetry contract steward: Priya Natarajan (observability team)
  - Chaos embargo steward: Diego Alvarez (platform SRE)
  - Fidelity harness owner: Samir Patel (applied ML)
- Cadence: Monthly safety review meeting to audit baselines, embargo calendar exceptions, and recent near-misses (chair rotates between owners).

12) Onboarding notes for experimenters
- Minimum artifact checklist for an experiment ticket:
  - Baseline data export (48h) attached as CSV.
  - Short summary of expected impact and rollback steps.
  - Preflight results attached (smoke tests and synthetic harness).
- Slack template for announcing a canary kick-off in #infra-experiments and #sre-oncall (copy into ticket).

13) Postmortem and learning loop
- Every aborted or failed rollout under this policy must produce a short postmortem within 72 hours, using the template: summary, what happened, detection signals, root cause, actions (owner + due date). Attach telemetry snapshots and kernel traces to the postmortem.

Appendix A — Suggested PromQL queries (text):
- p99 over 15m: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_bucket[15m])) by (le, cohort))
- kernel tail ratio: sum(rate(kernel_call_duration_seconds_bucket{le=">0.02"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kernel_call_duration_seconds_count[5m]))

Appendix B — Synthetic harness golden prompt examples (text):
- Prompt 1 (instruction): "Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence: ..."
- Prompt 2 (dialogue): short multi-turn assistant/user interaction used to detect unexpected repetition or cutoff.

If there are questions or suggested edits, ping the telemetry steward or open a PR against this page.

payload.page_title: Runtime Extension and Observability Integration Handbook

sections.body:
Summary

This handbook defines the extension/plugin model and the associated observability and benchmarking contracts for Redwood's serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, plugin authors (internal and partner vendors), SREs, and Performance Engineers who integrate custom kernels, pre/post-processing hooks, or telemetry exporters with the serving runtime. The goal is to provide a stable, low-friction integration surface while preserving runtime SLOs and operational observability.

Audience and scope
- Primary audience: eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, and applied-ml teams.
- Scope: plugin lifecycle, API/telemetry contracts, recommended profiling hooks, benchmark integration, safe rollout checklist, and runbooks for extension-related incidents.

Design goals
- Safety-first: extensions must not violate memory or latency SLOs.
- Observable: every extension must expose standard telemetry and traces.
- Deterministic lifecycle: load/unload, canary, and rollback paths are explicitly defined.
- Low-onramp: standard manifests and a reference SDK accelerate partner integrations.

High-level architecture and key services referenced
- runtime-orchestrator: controls placement and lifecycle of model shards and extensions.
- kernel-scheduler-service: responsible for mapping requests to kernel implementations and enforcing priority/quotas.
- kv-cache-agent: shared KV prefix cache used by model sessions; extensions may read-only access via a guarded API.
- telemetry-pipeline: receives Prometheus metrics, OTLP traces, and logs (forwarded to internal observability stacks).
- perf-harness-runner: benchmark runner that executes synthetic and recorded traces against runtime variants.

Extension surface and lifecycle
1) Extension manifest (required fields)
   - name: unique identifier (namespace-qualified)
   - version: semver
   - type: kernel | preprocessor | postprocessor | telemetry-exporter
   - entrypoint: binary or module path
   - resources: cpu, gpu, memory soft/hard limits
   - capabilities: [kv_read, metrics, traces]
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
name: redwood.ext.fast-attn
   version: 0.3.1
   type: kernel
   entrypoint: /opt/extensions/fast_attn.so
   resources:
     cpu: "2"
     gpu: "1"
     memory: "8Gi"
   capabilities: [kv_read, metrics, traces]

2) Load sequence
   - Orchestration: runtime-orchestrator validates manifest signature and resource claims, then schedules extension.
   - Warmup: extension must run a registration callback that reports supported kernel shapes and an internal readiness check (see API contract).
   - Activation: kernel-scheduler-service adds the extension to the routing table for compatible requests.

3) Unload sequence and safe rollback
   - New requests are drained within a configurable drain_window (default 30s).
   - Active requests are allowed to complete with a max_grace (default 120s).
   - Forced termination only with explicit operator approval and after emitting a decommission trace.

API and observability contract (required)
- Health and readiness endpoints: /healthz, /ready (HTTP 200/503 semantics).
- Registration RPC: RegisterExtension({shapes:[], capabilities:[]}) -> {success, diagnostics}. Called on startup and after hot-reload.
- Metrics: expose Prometheus-style metrics namespace: redwood_ext_<name>_*. All extensions must export the following metrics (names are exact):
  - redwood_ext_<name>_invocations_total (counter)
  - redwood_ext_<name>_invocation_errors_total (counter)
  - redwood_ext_<name>_processing_seconds_bucket (histogram)
  - redwood_ext_<name>_active_workers (gauge)

Standard metric SLOs and thresholds (enforced by SRE checks)
  - p95 processing latency for kernel extensions: < 50ms for small-shape requests (<=512 tokens), <150ms for long-shape requests (>=2048 tokens).
  - invocation error rate: < 0.1% sustained per 5 minute window.
  - active_workers: should not exceed the declared resources*2 without explicit autoscale approval.

Trace & span conventions
- All extension-related spans must use the following span.kind attributes: {span.kind: internal, ext.name: <name>, ext.version: <ver>, runtime.node: <node-id>}
- Must emit pre-kernel and post-kernel spans with attributes: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, token_count, kernel_shape_hint.
- Sampling: default 10% across normal traffic; can be increased to 100% for canaries (configurable via runtime-orchestrator).

Profiling hooks and kernel telemetry
- Extensions must implement lightweight event hooks for the following events: kernel_dispatch (include queue_size and priority), kernel_start (include occupancy_estimate), kernel_complete (include cycles, bytes_read, bytes_written), kernel_preempt (include preempt_reason).
- Recommended profiling context: when running the continuous profiler, the profiler must annotate samples with ext.name and kernel_hint to enable join with kernel-level traces.
- Kernel event JSON example (line-delimited in logs / OTLP):
{
  "ts": "2026-03-01T12:45:12.123Z",
  "event": "kernel_start",
  "ext": "redwood.ext.fast-attn",
  "node": "node-az1-07",
  "occupancy_estimate": 0.78,
  "queue_size": 3
}

Benchmarking integration (perf-harness-runner)
- Integration points: the extension manifests must include a benchmark_profile stanza describing synthetic shapes the perf-harness-runner can use.
- Profiles should map to: payloads (sequence lengths), concurrency shapes, and memory-budgeted allocation.
- Command example to run the reference profile:
  perf-harness-runner --target runtime-orchestrator:443 --extension redwood.ext.fast-attn --profile small-seq-512 --duration 600s --out /tmp/bench-run.json

- Result schema (perf-harness-runner output):
  - throughput_tokens_per_sec, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, memory_young_bytes, memory_total_bytes, kernel_evicts

- Performance gate: a reference kernel extension must meet baseline envelope for green canary: latency_p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 and memory_total_bytes <= baseline_memory * 1.20. Failure blocks automated canary promotion.

Rollout and canary checklist
1) Manifest signed and uploaded to extension-registry (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
2) Run unit and integration tests (CI job: ext-ci/fast-attn)
3) Run perf-harness-runner against a dev cluster; collect metrics and traces
4) Canary to 1% traffic for 30 minutes; sample traces at 100% for canary window
5) Evaluate SLOs: p95 latency, invocation error rate, scheduler queue length, KV cache hit behavior
6) Promote to 10% for 2 hours; run full benchmark profile
7) Full rollout after passing automated gates and manual review by SRE and runtime lead

Runbook: Extension-induced latency regression
- Symptoms:
  - sudden p95 spike for model routes pinned to new kernel variant
  - redwood_ext_<name>_processing_seconds_bucket shows increased tail
  - kernel-scheduler-service queue_length metric increases > 2x baseline

- Immediate actions (pager):
  1) If invocation_errors_total rate > 0.5% over 1 minute: trigger rollback and page oncall (eng-sre).
  2) If latency_p95 breached threshold by >20% for 5 minutes: toggle routing in kernel-scheduler-service to fallback variant: curl -X POST https://kernel-scheduler.internal/_admin/fallback?variant=cpu-fallback
  3) Temporarily isolate the extension by marking it non-preferred: runtime-orchestrator API: POST /extensions/<name>/isolate
  4) Capture a 2-minute profiler run and attach ext.name tag, then escalate to runtime team.

Post-incident triage checklist
- Collect: perf-harness-runner results, OTLP traces for the period, Prometheus metrics (10m before/after), kernel dispatcher logs, kv-cache-agent metrics.
- Hypothesis-driven triage steps: check for memory growth in extension, kernel preemption events, unexpected concurrency spikes, network stalls on telemetry-pipeline.
- RCA artifacts: timeline, root-cause hypothesis, corrective change, and automated gate added to CI (if applicable).

Known integration pitfalls and recommended mitigations
| Issue | Likely cause | Recommended mitigation |
|-------|--------------|------------------------|
| Unbounded worker spawn | Extension ignores resources field on manifest | Reject manifest on validation; implement soft cgroups limits and autoscale advisory |
| Kernel preemption thrash | Long-running kernels without cooperative yield | Add cooperative yield hooks; break kernels into smaller micro-kernels |
| KV cache stampede | Extension performs cold synchronous cache fills | Use async prefetch; set max_prefetch_inflight=4; use per-tenant rate limit |
| OTLP flooding | Excessive debug-level spans from extension | Require sampling controls and log-level thresholds; telemetry-pipeline enforces rate limits |

Ownership and contacts
- Runtime extension registry & policy: eng-serving-runtime (owners: Marcus Liu, Elena Petrova)
- Observability & profiling policy: eng-sre (owner: Ravi Menon)
- Performance gating and perf-harness-runner: applied-ml-and-evals (owner: Priya Das)

Appendix A: Example Prometheus metric exposition (text-format)
sections.heading: Example (YAML manifest)

sections.body: redwood_ext_fast_attn_invocations_total{status="ok",node="node-az1-07"} 12345
sections.heading: TYPE redwood_ext_fast_attn_invocations_total counter

sections.body:
redwood_ext_fast_attn_processing_seconds_bucket{le="0.01"} 1000
redwood_ext_fast_attn_processing_seconds_bucket{le="0.05"} 12000

Appendix B: Minimal extension SDK checklist (for authors)
- Implement /healthz and /ready endpoints
- Emit the required metrics with correct naming
- Register shapes via RegisterExtension before accepting requests
- Honor resources settings and implement graceful shutdown hooks
- Provide a benchmark_profile and test vectors in the manifest

Document change log
- 2026-02-10: Draft created by Aisha Khan
- 2026-03-01: Added runbook actions and benchmark gate thresholds; reviewers: Marcus Liu, Elena Petrova, Ravi Menon

Related artifacts and links
- Extension registry UI: https://internal.redwood/extensions
- Kernel scheduler admin API: https://kernel-scheduler.internal/_admin
- Perf harness job template: //ci/pipelines/perf-harness/extension-profile-run

If you are integrating a third-party extension, file a request in the #runtime-extensions slack channel and follow the vendor-onboarding runbook referenced from the registry UI.

payload.page_title: Runtime resource annotation taxonomy and signal enrichment

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines a canonical taxonomy for resource annotations used across the serving runtime, plus the enrichment pipeline that turns raw telemetry + config into scored signals used by the scheduler, admission controller, and autoscaler. The goal is to standardize names, types, semantics, and operational practices so that components can interoperate without brittle ad-hoc mappings.

Motivation

- Multiple teams (scheduler, kernel mapper, autoscaler, Observability) require consistent, machine-readable metadata about model-serving resources (GPUs, shards, model variants, containers, and requests).
- Inconsistent annotation names caused mismatches in fallback routing and incorrect prefetch decisions during Q3 incidents.
- A small, well-documented set of canonical fields reduces cognitive load for owners and speeds rollouts of policy changes.

Scope

- This taxonomy applies to: GPU nodes, runtime shards, model-variant instances, session tokens (provenance), and request classes.
- Out of scope: long-term billing tags (managed by Finance) and user-level semantic labels (managed by product teams).

Core principles

1) Backwards-compatible: existing annotation keys must continue to be supported; new keys should have clear deprecation paths.
2) Idempotent enrichment: repeated enrichment runs should produce identical signals for the same inputs.
3) Typed and validated: each key has a strict type and acceptable value range.
4) Explainable scores: any composite score must be reproducible and accompanied by its component weights.

Canonical annotation table (summary)

| key | type | description | primary consumers | default/notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| resource_type | string | one of [gpu-node, shard, model-variant, session, request-class] | all | required |
| affinity | string | affinity class: one of [high, medium, low] used for co-location heuristics | scheduler, autoscaler | default: medium |
| eviction_priority | integer | 0 (never) - 100 (highest) eviction ranking, lower = safer to evict | scheduler, runtime | default: 50 |
| kvcache_hotness | float | 0.0-1.0 locality score for KV cache reuse | kernel-mapper, scheduler | computed by enrichment pipeline |
| kernel_hint | string | preferred kernel execution path (e.g. attention-sliced-v2, fused-mlp) | kernel-mapper | optional |
| fidelity_profile | string | fidelity target: [max_quality, balanced, cost_saver] | autoscaler, rollout | impacts quantization and fallback policies |
| estimated_tps | float | estimated tokens-per-second capacity for this resource | admission, autoscaler | derived from microbenchmarks and telemetry |
| thermal_headroom | float | 0.0-1.0 available thermal headroom; <0.2 triggers soft-limits | scheduler, SRE | pulled from node sensors |
| model_variant_compat | list | list of variant ids this resource is compatible with | orchestrator | canonicalized to short ids |
| provenance | string | origin id of last configuration change | all | helps audit and debugging |
| isolation_class | string | [best_effort, strict, dedicated] determines multi-tenancy isolation | scheduler, infra | default: best_effort |
| prefetch_hint | string | [none, small, aggressive] KV prefetch strategy expected | kernel-mapper | influences warmstart behavior |
| billing_bucket | string | internal billing categorization | billing, finance | optional, tie-breaker only |

Full field definitions and validation rules

- resource_type (string, required): must be one of the canonical values. Reject unknown types during ingestion and route to owner for classification.

- affinity (enum): used by the placement policy to express co-location sensitivity. Implementation note: treat affinity high as an additive score +30 in placement ranking.

- eviction_priority (int 0-100): lower values protected; eviction_policy: pick candidate with highest eviction_priority first. For multi-tenant nodes, maintain per-tenant min_protected_threshold.

- kvcache_hotness (float 0.0-1.0): computed by enrichment pipeline using a sliding-window merge of request provenance + access patterns. See Enrichment pipeline section. Values <0.15 are considered cold.

- kernel_hint (string): free-form but validated against KernelHintRegistry (see Operational pointers). Unrecognized hints fall back to kernel auto-selection with telemetry annotation.

- fidelity_profile (enum): toggles quality/cost tradeoffs; must be supported by model_variant. If a requested fidelity_profile is unsupported, admission rejects with a 409 and details recommended alternatives.

Enrichment pipeline (architecture)

The enrichment pipeline converts raw inputs into canonical annotated-resource records. Design choices: streaming-first but compact, idempotent, and vectorizable for fast scoring.

Inputs
- Telemetry: hot-prefix traces, KV access logs, per-request latency and token counts, node sensor readings (temp, power), kernel failure traces.
- Config/state: model manifests, node labels, feature flags, recent rollout history.
- Microbenchmarks: per-variant short-run throughput/latency profiles stored in the Benchmark Catalog.

Stages (high-level)
1) Ingest and canonicalize keys: map vendor-specific labels (e.g., nvidia.gpu.type -> resource_type/gpu_model) using Canonicalizer map.
2) Join time windows: create sliding windows (default 5m, 1h) for hotness and latency measures.
3) Compute primitive signals: mean_ttfb, median_tokens, kv_access_rate, error_rate, thermal_percentile.
4) Normalize & clamp: scale signals into canonical ranges, clamp outliers (z-score guardrails).
5) Composite scoring: calculate kvcache_hotness, estimated_tps, eviction_priority_delta using weighted sums. Weights are stored in the ScoreConfig repo and are versioned.
6) Publish annotated record: write to Annotated Resource Store (a lightweight document store with versioned entries).

Example enrichment rule (pseudocode)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
window = last_15_minutes(requests.filter(model==X))
kv_hits = sum(window.map(r -> r.kv_hit ? 1 : 0))
kv_accesses = sum(window.map(r -> r.kv_accesses))
hotness = (kv_hits + 0.5 * kv_accesses) / max(1, window.request_count)
normalized_hotness = sigmoid_scale(hotness, scale=0.8)  # clamp to 0..1

Operational notes on enrichment weights
- ScoreConfig is a Git-backed JSON with simple schema: {"kv_weight": "0.6", "latency_weight": "0.3", "thermal_penalty": "0.1"}. Changes require a review and a CI gate that replays enrichment on a representative sample.

Storage and API

- Annotated Resource Store: path /annotated-resources/{resource_id}, JSON document with last_enriched_at and version tag. The store supports conditional writes (ETag) to avoid stomping concurrent enrichments.
- Read API: /api/v1/annotated-resources?filter=... supports predicates on canonical fields and returns stable snapshots.

Consumers and contracts

- Scheduler: consumes annotated records and uses affinity + kvcache_hotness + thermal_headroom to rank placement. Contract: annotated record must be <5s old for scheduling decisions.
- Kernel-mapper: consumes kernel_hint + kvcache_hotness to pick kernel and prefetch budget. Contract: if kernel_hint missing, mapper must annotate chosen kernel back into resource record.
- Autoscaler: consumes estimated_tps and error_rate; expects monotonicity of estimated_tps across enrichment runs unless a flagged recalibration event occurred.

Sample annotation (JSON example)

{
  \"resource_id\": \"shard-az2-gpu-47\",
  \"resource_type\": \"shard\",
  \"affinity\": \"high\",
  \"eviction_priority\": \"20\",
  \"kvcache_hotness\": \"0.73\",
  \"kernel_hint\": \"attention-sliced-v2\",
  \"fidelity_profile\": \"balanced\",
  \"estimated_tps\": \"120.5\",
  \"thermal_headroom\": \"0.62\",
  \"model_variant_compat\": [\"rv1-small-int8\", \"rv1-small-fp16\"],
  \"last_enriched_at\": \"2026-11-03T14:22:11Z\"
}

(Consumers should parse the types—this example renders numbers as strings for Transport-level simplicity; the API schema documents native types.)

Producer guidelines (how to add or change annotations)

1) Create a proposal in the ScoreConfig repo for new fields or weights and add a small integration test that exercises enrichment.
2) Add a validator in the Enrichment Validator module with a clear error message and remediation steps.
3) Increment the scoreconfig version and open a changelist referencing this Confluence page.
4) Run enrichment replay on the low-cost sample corpus (CI job) and upload diff report.

Common failure modes and mitigations

- Symptom: kvcache_hotness drops suddenly for a shard after rollout.
  - Check: recent model_variant rollout, kernel_hint change, and cold-start events in warmup logs.
  - Mitigation: increase prefetch_hint for the shard, and re-run warmup job for 1-2 minutes.

- Symptom: scheduler rejects placement citing thermal_headroom < 0.2 unexpectedly.
  - Check: node sensor telemetry, recent firmware updates, and thermal_headroom normalization params.
  - Mitigation: temporarily lower thermal_penalty in ScoreConfig and trigger prioritized drain if needed.

Versioning, deprecation, and migration

- New keys must include a deprecation plan in the PR: alias mapping, 90-day dual-write window, and a one-time migration job for historical entries.
- ScoreConfig versions are semver: enrichment-runner uses the highest-stable tag unless an override is present.

Rollout checklist (for ScoreConfig or field additions)

1) Draft ScoreConfig change and unit tests.
2) Reviewer sign-off (2 reviewers including one SRE).
3) Run enrichment replay against sample corpus.
4) Deploy to enrichment-staging and run a 1h shadow pipeline.
5) Monitor divergence metrics: annotated-record-delta-rate < 1% and scheduler-placement-change-rate < 0.5% for safe rollout.
6) Promote to production with a 10-minute canary window, monitor live SLOs.

Operator runbook snippets

- Quick check: get last enriched record for a shard

curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  https://internal-api.redwood.local/api/v1/annotated-resources/shard-az2-gpu-47 | jq .

- Replay enrichment for a single resource (local dev)
sections.heading: kvcache_hotness calculation - pseudocode

sections.body:
ENRICHMENT_CONFIG=s3://scoreconfig/prod.json enrichment-runner --resource-id shard-az2-gpu-47 --window 15m --dry-run

Operational ownership and contacts

- Owners: Serving Runtime Observability & Enrichment squad (primary)
- Oncall escalation: runtime-oncall -> eng-sre -> platform-eng lead.
- Suggested reviewers for changes: Diego Ramirez (Scheduler), Priya Shah (Kernel-mapper), Ellen Zhou (SRE).

Open action items

- [ ] Add KV access enrichment test to the standard microbenchmark corpus (assigned: Priya, due: 2026-12-01).
- [ ] Publish a lightweight SDK for writing annotations from third-party tools (assigned: Asha, due: 2027-01-15).

References and links

- ScoreConfig repo: git://redwood/scoreconfig (internal)
- Annotated Resource Store API spec: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/annotated-resource-store-api-spec-2026 (draft)
- Benchmark Catalog: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/ (see per-variant microbenchmarks)

Appendix: example ScoreConfig fragment

{
  \"version\": \"1.4.0\",
  \"weights\": {
    \"kv_weight\": \"0.55\",
    \"latency_weight\": \"0.30\",
    \"thermal_penalty\": \"0.15\"
  },
  \"normalization\": {
    \"kv_scale\": \"0.8\",
    \"tps_clamp\": \"500.0\"
  }
}

Glossary

- Annotated Resource Store: the authoritative, versioned store of enriched resource records.
- KernelHintRegistry: authoritative list of supported kernel execution hints.
- ScoreConfig: versioned config that defines weights and normalization for composite scoring.

If you have questions or want a walkthrough, DM the owners or schedule a 30m sync using the runtime-observability calendar.
