payload.page_title: Runtime Shadow Rehearsal and Localized Probe Synthesis Playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook defines the runtime "shadow rehearsal" pattern: an operationalized workflow that (1) synthesizes localized evaluation probes targeted at tenant cohorts, locales, and latency bands; (2) runs those probes in a low-risk shadow mesh against quantized and mixed-precision artifacts; and (3) performs cost-aware rehearsal passes that validate quality, latency, and coherence before a real rollout. The goal is to detect regressions and quant-induced degradations earlier while bounding evaluation cost and preserving tenant privacy.

Scope

- Applies to model promotion and quantized rollouts for text generation and multi-turn chat services (service names: eval-orch, shadow-mesh, rehearsal-runner).
- Covers probe generation, seed selection, rehearsal execution, gating metrics, and rollback triggers.
- Intended for on-prem, private VPC, and hosted Dedicated deployments.

Why this pattern

- Longtail and locale-specific regressions often escape coarse global evals. Localized probes increase sensitivity to per-tenant failure modes.
- Running rehearsals against quantized artifacts in a shadow mesh simulates production mixing without impacting production traffic.
- Cost-aware caps and staged rehearsal passes allow teams to validate risk under budget constraints.

High-level components

1) Probe Fabricator (probe-fabricator)
   - Responsible for localized probe synthesis: locale-aware lexical meshes, few-shot priming templates, and context anchors.
   - Inputs: seed traffic fingerprints, tenant taxonomy, priming registry, localization lexicons.
2) Shadow Mesh (shadow-mesh)
   - Lightweight runtime that replays probes against quantized variants and the nominal FP32 baseline.
   - Provides instrumentation (response_coherence, fidelity_delta, q_loss, latency_p95, token_emissions).
3) Rehearsal Runner (rehearsal-runner)
   - Orchestrates rehearsal passes, enforces cost caps, aggregates metrics, and writes rehearsal artifacts to eval-orch ledger.
4) Gating Engine
   - Applies SLOs and guardrail rules. Produces pass/fail verdicts and recommended rollout decisions.

Localized probe synthesis strategy

- Taxonomy partitioning: split the tenant base into cohorts along three orthogonal axes: locale (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP), intent surface (support, search, compose), and latency band (fast p95 < 150ms, medium 150–500ms, slow > 500ms).
- For each cohort generate probes across these buckets:
  - 40% anchor probes (real user anonymized seeds sampled from last 90 days)
  - 40% synthetic perturbations (paraphrases, tokenization edgecases, punctuation/noise injection)
  - 20% adversarial variants (contrastive prompts designed to stress hallucination and instruction-following)
- Probe counts per rehearsal pass are configurable; default targeted sample: 1k probes per cohort for small services, 10k for high-volume services.

Privacy and provenance

- Anchor probes must be redacted and hashed before leaving telemetry storage (hash-salt per rehearsal job). Raw PII is never exported.
- Provenance metadata attached to each probe includes cohort_id, seed_hash, probe_type, and priming_template_id.

Rehearsal execution modes (staged passes)

1) Dry-run (low-cost smoke)
   - Run: 1–2% of full probe set, quant variants only, no baseline comparison.
   - Purpose: surface obvious failures and infra incompatibilities. Cost cap: $X/day (set by team).
2) Contrast-pass
   - Run: 20% sample, run against FP32 baseline and quant variant(s). Compute fidelity_delta metrics and delta-significance tests.
3) Full-rehearsal
   - Run: 100% probe set, cohort-balanced. Includes heavier metrics (token-level divergence, functioncall stability).

Gating metrics and thresholds

We compute both statistical and decisionable thresholds. Primary signals:

- fidelity_delta (KL-style scoring + templated semantic similarity): fail if cohort mean fidelity_delta > 0.12 and throughput-corrected CI excludes zero.
- response_coherence (annotator-simulated score 0–1): fail if cohort P90 < 0.70 and drop vs baseline > 0.08.
- q_loss (quantization artifact score): fail if absolute q_loss increase > 0.05 and correlated with token_emission anomalies.
- latency_p95: fail if latency_p95 increase > 2x and exceeds target SLO band for that cohort.
- embedding_stability (for retrieval/rerank): fail if cosine shift > 0.06 on average for critical slices.

Decision matrix (simplified)

- If any cohort fails fidelity_delta AND response_coherence -> abort rollout for that cohort and open regression ticket.
- If only latency_p95 regression observed but coherence preserved -> engage ops throttling + capacity reroute and run narrow replay.
- If q_loss is high but coherence preserved for anchor-probes -> schedule quant-tuning pass and run targeted micro-rehearsal.

Runbook: step-by-step rehearsal for a scheduled quant rollout

1) Preflight (owner: ModelOnboard Team)
   - Create rehearsal job in eval-orch: include cohort list, probe budget, quant-variant ids, and expected cost cap.
   - Run quick smoke locally with rehearsal-runner dry-run mode: run command below.
2) Dry-run review (owner: Release Lead)
   - Confirm no infra errors in shadow-mesh logs, check instrumentation counters (request_e2e_errors < 0.5%).
3) Contrast-pass (owner: Evaluation Engineers)
   - Run contrast-pass, collect fidelity_delta, response_coherence, and q_loss.
4) Analysis (owner: Applied ML)
   - Run automated delta-significance test (see CLI step). Produce report, tag failing cohorts.
5) Decision (owner: Release Lead + Product)
   - If no failing cohorts -> proceed to phased production rollout.
   - If some cohorts fail -> open triage (link created) and either rollback quant artifact or schedule micro-tunings.
6) Post-rehearsal monitoring (owner: SRE)
   - Enable rehearsal-derived sentinels for 72 hours post-rollout and maintain elevated sampling of failed cohorts.

CLI examples
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: rehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-01 --cohorts en-US:support:fast,de-DE:compose:medium --mode dry-run --probe-budget 200 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --cost-cap 200
sections.heading: Start a dry-run rehearsal (example)

sections.body:
rehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-02 --mode contrast --probe-budget 2000 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --baseline mv-1.0 --report-bucket s3://eval-orch/reports/rjr-20260712-02

YAML rehearsal job manifest (example)

job_id: rjr-20260712-02
owner: model-onboard
cohorts:
  - id: en-US-support-fast
    locale: en-US
    intent: support
    latency_band: fast
    probe_target: 1000
  - id: de-DE-compose-medium
    locale: de-DE
    intent: compose
    latency_band: medium
    probe_target: 1000
quant_variants:
  - qv-2.1
baseline: mv-1.0
mode: contrast
cost_cap_usd: "1500"
retention_days: "30"

Interpretation and reporting

- Reports include cohort-level summaries, ranked failure slices, example failing probes, and suggested remediation actions. Attachments include raw witness tokens (hashed) and aggregated diff visualizations.
- Use the provided report template (report-template-v2) for consistency.

Cost control and budgeting

- Rehearsal-runner enforces a hard cost cap at job-level. If cost consumption reaches 90% of cap during a mid-pass, execution pauses, and a partial report is emitted for review.
- Default cost guidance: small service full-rehearsal ~ $800–1,200; large service ~ $4k–8k depending on probe complexity and annotator simulation.

Integration with quant profiles and eval-harness

- Rehearsal jobs reference quant profile IDs from the quantization catalog. Rehearsals must include quant metadata (bitwidth, kernel-profile, stash-policy).
- The probe-fabricator consults the eval-harness priming registry to select few-shot templates, ensuring parity between rehearsal prompts and production priming.

Failure triage and escalation playbook

1) Triage run (owner: Applied ML)
   - Label failing probes by failure mode (hallucination, truncation, functioncall-mismatch, tokenization-error).
2) Cross-team incident (owner: Release Lead)
   - If multiple cohorts fail fidelity_delta or coherence -> declare a Rehearsal Incident (severity: S2) and run causal regression investigation.
3) Rollback policy
   - Immediate rollback recommended when anchor-probe P90 coherence drops below 0.6 for >3 cohorts or when similarity drift >= 0.18 with statistical significance.

Postmortem artifacts and follow-ups

- Create a rehearsal incident dossier containing: rehearsal job manifest, cohort failure matrix, top 50 failing probes, annotator sample, and timeline of actions. Attach to the central incident tracker and link to model-promote PR.
- Follow-ups commonly include: micro-quant-tune, priming-template adjustment, or probe-corpus augmentation.

Ownership and contacts

- Probe Fabricator: Applied ML (owner: Priya Natarajan)
- Rehearsal orchestration: Platform Eval (owner: Marcus Holt)
- Gating & artifacts: ModelOnboard (owner: Sofia Alvarez)
- SRE & post-deploy monitoring: Platform SRE (owner: Liam Chen)

Appendices

A) Metrics table (columns: metric, description, alert-threshold, owner)

metric | description | alert-threshold | owner
fidelity_delta | semantic divergence vs baseline | >0.12 cohort mean | Applied ML
response_coherence | simulated annotator coherence 0–1 | cohort P90 < 0.70 | Evaluation
q_loss | quant artifact amplitude | absolute increase > 0.05 | ModelOnboard
latency_p95 | 95th percentile E2E latency | >2x baseline for cohort | SRE
embedding_stability | avg cosine shift per slice | >0.06 | Retrieval Team

B) Delta-significance command (example)
sections.heading: Run contrast-pass and upload report

sections.body:
python tools/delta_test.py --baseline reports/mv-1.0/metrics.json --variant reports/qv-2.1/metrics.json --metric fidelity_delta --alpha 0.05 --output reports/delta-ci.json

C) Quick checklist before scheduling a full rehearsal

- [ ] Manifest created and reviewed, probes budgeted and redaction confirmed.
- [ ] Quant variant artifacts uploaded to artifact store and kernel-profile declared.
- [ ] Shadow mesh capacity validated and can accept N concurrent rehearsal workers.
- [ ] Cost cap set and billing owner notified.
- [ ] Reviewers assigned and report template linked.

Related links and references

- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026 for quant fallback patterns.
- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026 for end-to-end shadow orchestration.

Document revision history

- 2026-02-10: initial draft (S. Alvarez)
- 2026-04-02: added cohort taxonomy and cost guidance (Marcus Holt)
- 2026-07-12: finalized gating thresholds and rollout runbook (S. Alvarez, Priya N.)

payload.page_title: Precision budgeting and observability manifest

sections.body:
Summary
This document defines the Precision Budgeting concept: a compact, auditable manifest that maps workload classes to a quantization "budget" (precision/bitwidth + KV-cache policy + preferred fallback tier) and the observability contract required to safely onboard, operate, and roll back mixed-precision LLM artifacts. The goal is to make quant tradeoffs explicit, measurable, and automatable across the eval harness, onboarding gates, production routing, and regression triage.

Why this exists
- Quantization reduces unit cost but introduces subtle failure modes that are workload-dependent.
- Teams need a single artifact to capture the acceptable quality-budget tradeoffs for a service so the platform can automate routing, monitoring, and rollback decisions.
- This manifest bridges model-onboarding checks, eval harness requirements, quality guardrails, and incident triage signals.

Scope and audience
- Audience: model owners, applied ML engineers, runtime engineers, SREs, and evaluation stewards.
- Scope: inference quantization (dynamic/static/int8/mixed precision), KV-cache interaction policies, probe/eval contracts, and production observability thresholds. Not covered: training-time quant-aware fine-tuning or model architecture changes.

Key concepts
1) Precision budget (single-line): human-readable token that describes the allowable precision for a workload. Example: "pb:service_search_v2=fp16+int8_kv:0.75:fallthrough=dense" meaning: use fp16 base with int8-quantized KV-cache tuned to 0.75 fidelity tolerance, fallback to dense (no quant) if fidelity breaches.
2) Workload class: logical grouping by semantic/latency/stretch (e.g., search-rerank, chat-assistant-short, billing-batch).
3) Fidelity budget: numeric tolerance (0.0–1.0) that maps to acceptable delta on service-level quality metrics (e.g., F1, exact-match, RSI).
4) Observability contract: set of telemetry signals and alert thresholds that must be live before a budget becomes active.

Precision Budget Manifest (recommended schema)
The manifest is a small YAML saved alongside model artifacts and eval reports. The manifest must be generated during the onboarding pipeline and checked into the model service registry. Example YAML (illustrative):

precision_budget:
  service: service_search_v2
  model_family: rwx-2b
  artifact_tag: rwx-2b-int8-kv-2026-02
  workload_class: search-rerank
  base_precision: fp16
  kv_cache_precision: int8
  kv_cache_policy: per-tenant-disabled
  fidelity_budget: "0.06"  # allowed drop in primary metric (fractional)
  primary_metric: MAP@10
  secondary_metrics: ["latency_p95_ms","response_stability_index"]
  fallback_tier: dense
  canary_percent: 5
  observability:
    telemetry_keys: ["probe_delta_v1","rsi","latency_ms_p95","quant_error_rate"]
    required_retention_days: 14
    alert_rules:
      - name: fidelity-violation
        when: probe_delta_v1 > 0.06 and quant_error_rate > 0.01 for 30m
        action: rollback-to-fallback
      - name: latency-degradation
        when: latency_ms_p95 > 300 for 15m
        action: investigate-scheduling
  owner: team-search
  onboarding_status: gated

Operational readiness checklist
1) Eval harness integration (required)
   - Run quantized artifact through the synthetic eval suite at the same or larger sample as the production shadow set.
   - Metrics to collect: primary_metric (drift), probe_delta_v1 (probe family), response_stability_index (RSI), token-efficiency delta.
   - Run functioncall and streaming probes to cover behavior changes introduced by quant kernels.
   - Automated acceptance if primary_metric drop <= fidelity_budget AND RSI delta <= 0.03.

2) Observability gating (required)
   - The following telemetry must be ingesting to the eval mesh and stored for on-call lookback: probe_delta_v1, rsi, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, tail_token_repeat_rate, quant_error_rate, cache_hit_ratio.
   - Alerts created in monitoring stack with the same names as manifest alert_rules.

3) Canary and shadowing (required)
   - Start with canary_percent from the manifest (recommend 1–5%).
   - Maintain continuous shadow traffic for 48 hours with per-slice diff reporting every 15 minutes.
   - If any alert fires during canary, automatic rollback must be triggered.

4) Cost benchmarking (informational)
   - Record tokens-per-dollar before and after quantization using the platform cost harness. Target at least 15% cost improvement for int8 KV-cache cases, otherwise re-evaluate quant knob.

Decision matrix: when to accept a quant profile
- Accept if: primary_metric_drop <= fidelity_budget AND RSI_delta <= 0.03 AND no severity>=P2 alerts during 48h canary.
- Reject if: primary_metric_drop > fidelity_budget OR any data-loss or hallucination class > 0.5% on sensitive slices.
- Manual review if: cost saving > 30% but RSI_delta between 0.03–0.07 (requires engineering + product signoff).

Escalation and regression triage playbook
1) First responder: the model owner must triage incoming fidelity-violation alert.
2) Quick triage steps (15 min):
   - Compare shadow metrics vs baseline using the eval harness snapshot.
   - Check quant_error_rate and top-10 failing probes.
   - If failure concentrated on small slice: create probe patch and temporarily increase fallback percent for affected tenant slice.
3) Rollback criteria (automatic): fidelity-violation alert action=rollback-to-fallback.
4) Post-incident investigation (3 day window): run regression bisect using the quant artifact variants (fp16, fp16+int8-kv@low, int8-only) and produce a hypothesis matrix.

Operator runbook (commands)
- Extract probe diffs from eval mesh:
  curl -sS "https://eval-internal/api/v1/probe-diffs?service=service_search_v2&tag=rwx-2b-int8-kv-2026-02" | jq .

- Trigger a controlled rollback via ops CLI:
  redwood ops service rollback --service service_search_v2 --to-tier dense --reason "precision-budget breach"

- Promote revalidated artifact:
  redwood model promote --artifact rwx-2b-int8-kv-2026-02 --env production --manifest precision-budget.yml

Observability metrics and recommended thresholds
- primary_metric (service-specific): fidelity_budget (manifest)
- probe_delta_v1: alert if > fidelity_budget for 30m
- response_stability_index (RSI): alert if drop > 0.03 or absolute < 0.60 for user-facing services
- quant_error_rate: alert if > 0.01 sustained for 30m
- latency_p95_ms: alert if increased > 1.5x baseline or > 300ms (whichever is lower)
- tail_token_repeat_rate: alert if > 0.5%

Onboarding workflow (step-by-step)
1) Model owner: prepare candidate artifact and generate precision_budget manifest in repo.
2) CI: run unit tests + compatibility smoke (tokenization, functioncall shape tests).
3) Eval harness: run full mixed-slice probe sweep (costed budget) and produce artifact-level report.
4) SRE/Platform: verify observability contract (telemetry ingestion + alerts).
5) Product signoff (if manual review flagged).
6) Canary promotion (monitoring enabled).
7) Full rollout if canary passes for configured window.

Best practices and pitfalls
- Avoid single global fidelity numbers: quant sensitivity is probe-family-dependent. Use localized probe budgets for high-risk slices (payments, legal, privacy).
- Always include a KV-cache policy in the manifest: quantizing KV-cache often has larger behavioral impact than base weight quantization.
- Prefer staged quant knob sweeps (int8-low -> int8-mid -> int8-high) rather than one-step jumps.
- Keep an up-to-date regression probe set that contains adversarial, boundary, and functioncall sequences.

Example quick-check list (for reviewers)
- Is there a precision_budget manifest with owner and contact?
- Are all manifest telemetry_keys ingesting and retained for 14+ days?
- Did the quant artifact pass the eval harness acceptance criteria?
- Were canary and shadow windows configured and monitored?
- Is there an explicit fallback_tier and rollback action defined?

Appendix: sample manifest checklist table
- manifest present: YES
- primary_metric defined: YES (MAP@10)
- fidelity_budget: 0.06
- observability hooks: probe_delta_v1, rsi, latency_ms_p95, quant_error_rate
- canary_percent: 5%
- cost_target_improvement: >= 15%
- owner: team-search

Related documents and references
- Model onboarding: onboarding-fidelity-sla-and-noise-budget-manifest (see model-onboarding)
- Eval harness: quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout spec
- Regression triage: causal-regression-investigation-handbook

Maintainers and ownership
- Primary: team-search (model owners)
- Platform & tooling: serving-runtime team
- Observability: eng-platform

Revision history
- 2026-02-10: initial draft (Ava Martinez)
- 2026-03-12: added automated alert rules and decision matrix; clarified KV-cache policy guidance (reviewers: Marco D'Souza, Priya Nair, Jonah Reed)

Feedback and next steps
If you are onboarding a quantized artifact, include a link to this manifest in your model service PR and ping the serving-runtime channel for a short readiness review.

payload.page_title: evaluation-federation-onboarding-and-tenant-safety-guide

sections.body: This playbook defines the processes, contractual artifacts, telemetry gates, and safety controls for onboarding federated evaluators (internal teams, channel partners, and third-party annotator pools) into Redwood's eval-harness. The goal is to enable distributed evaluation capacity while preserving tenant isolation, model and data confidentiality, and consistent quality guarantees across federated runs.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applied ML engineers running evaluation orchestration
- Eval platform operators and privacy engineers
- Solutions/Customer engineering teams onboarding partner evaluators
- Security/compliance reviewers for third-party evaluators
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body:
- Goals:
  - Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist that ensures privacy-safe federation of evaluators.
  - Standardize eval contracts and runtime gating to protect tenant telemetry and artifacts.
  - Define SLOs, telemetry, and remediation steps for federated evaluation runs.
- Non-goals:
  - This document does not replace formal legal contracts (NDAs/SOWs) but provides the operational artifacts needed for them.
sections.heading: Goals and non-goals

sections.body:
- Applies to: shadow, synthetic, and targeted-slice evaluation runs executed outside the central eval-fleet (including cloud-hosted partner pools and air-gapped contractor environments).
- Out of scope: live production inference serving, customer-facing A/B experiments, and on-device user telemetry.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Federated evaluator: any non-central evaluator (external contractor, partner, or separate internal org) that receives probes and returns annotations or metrics.
- Tenant-safe run: an evaluation run guaranteed not to leak identifiable tenant data, metadata distributions, or telemetry that can be re-linked to production traffic.
- Eval contract: a machine-readable manifest and runtime policy (YAML) that declares allowed inputs/outputs, retention, and privacy parameters.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
- Eval Platform (owner: eval-harness team): provides the federation APIs, contract verification, and telemetry gating.
- Privacy & Security: signs off on contracts, DP parameters, K-anonymity thresholds.
- Onboarding Lead (customer/product engineering): coordinates partner onboarding and verifies artifacts.
- QA/Evals steward: validates annotation quality and sample representativeness.
sections.heading: Roles & ownership

sections.body:
1) Intake & classification:
   - Collect evaluator identity, jurisdiction, and infrastructure class (cloud/shared / dedicated / air-gapped).
   - Classify evaluator into risk tier: low, medium, high based on access, data sensitivity, and past audits.
2) Contract & artifacts:
   - Exchange NDAs and SOWs as required by Legal.
   - Produce an eval contract (see template below) signed by both parties.
3) Technical attestation:
   - Validate the evaluator can run the assigned harness (version compatibility).
   - Confirm cryptographic keys (if using encrypted payloads) and key rotation cadence.
4) Privacy controls setup:
   - Configure differential-privacy (DP) parameters or k-anonymity masking per the contract.
   - Set telemetry redaction rules and retention TTL.
5) Sandbox trial runs:
   - Run a minimum of 3 seed experiments using synthetic probes and noise-injected inputs.
   - Verify outputs against a golden-checker within the central eval-harness.
6) Quality calibration:
   - Run annotator calibration tasks and compute Krippendorff's alpha or Cohen's kappa.
   - Define per-slice pass/fail thresholds.
7) Production gating:
   - Gradually increase sample volume and remove synthetic-only constraints after 48 hours of stable output and telemetry.
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

sections.body:
| Control | Purpose | Default threshold | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| DP epsilon | Limit information leakage from outputs | 1.0 (high-risk slices 0.5) | Privacy |
| K-anonymity masking | Remove identifier granularity | k>=50 | Privacy |
| Telemetry sampling | Reduce exposure of token-level logs | 0.1% by default | Eval Platform |
| Retention TTL | Max stored artifact lifetime | 30 days (reviewed per contract) | Legal/Eval Platform |
| Output watermarking | Tag outputs generated by federated runs | required | Eval Platform |
sections.heading: Safety & privacy controls (table)

sections.body:
```yaml
contract_version: 1.0
evaluator_id: "partner-acme-annotators"
jurisdiction: "EU"
risk_tier: "medium"
allowed_probe_types:
  - synthetic
  - shadow
  - slice_specific
max_sample_rate_per_tenant: 0.002
privacy:
  differential_privacy:
    enabled: true
    epsilon: 0.8
  k_anonymity_min_k: 50
retention:
  artifacts_seconds: 2592000  # 30 days
telemetry:
  sample_rate: 0.001
  redaction: ["user_id", "ip", "session_token"]
signatures:
  eval_platform_sig: "sha256:..."
```
sections.heading: Eval contract (example YAML manifest)

sections.body:
- Pre-flight checks (automated): contract schema validation, signature verification, and DP parameter sanity checks.
- Runtime gates (must pass to proceed):
  - No-probe-leak test: candidate run must not include raw tenant IDs in any return channel.
  - Output-consistency test: sampled outputs compared to central golden-checker; divergence > delta triggers fail.
  - Latency anomaly detection: sudden latency variance indicates environment instability; pause run for investigation.
sections.heading: Telemetry & gating

sections.body:
- Annotator agreement: Krippendorff's alpha >= 0.70 on core slices.
- Coverage: federated pool must cover 95% of assigned slices within agreed TTL.
- Stability: output distribution divergence (JS distance) to central harness < 0.05 for 24h.
sections.heading: Quality metrics and SLOs

sections.body:
1) Privacy gate fail (e.g., epsilon too large / identifiers detected)
   - Immediate: halt run, revoke evaluator tokens, notify privacy owner.
   - Follow-up: run artifact redaction and re-run synthetic-only checks.
2) Low annotator agreement
   - Immediate: reduce sample volume and require calibration tasks.
   - Follow-up: impose retraining and re-certification for the annotator pool.
3) Telemetry spike or exfil suspicion
   - Immediate: isolate network access and snapshot evaluator workspace; escalate to Security.
   - Follow-up: forensic log review, legal notification if required.
sections.heading: Failure modes and triage steps (numbered)

sections.body:
| Step | Artifact required | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| Contract signed | Signed eval contract (YAML + signatures) | Present and verified |
| Sandbox trial | 3 trial runs with synthetic probes | No privacy gate failures |
| Calibration | Annotator calibration report | Agreement >= 0.7 |
| Telemetry | Telemetry gating logs | Sampling and redaction confirmed |
| Production ramp | Gradual sample increase plan | Stable for 48h |
sections.heading: Rollout & certification checklist (table)

sections.body:
- Generate an eval contract skeleton:
  - CLI: redwood-eval contract create --evaluator partner-acme --jurisdiction EU --risk medium > contract.yaml
- Validate contract schema locally:
  - CLI: redwood-eval contract validate contract.yaml
- Run a gated sandbox job:
  - CLI: redwood-eval run create --contract contract.yaml --mode sandbox --probes probes/synthetic-seed-01.json

Appendix A — audit evidence bundle requirements:
- Signed YAML contract with platform and partner signatures.
- Snapshot of trial run outputs (redacted) and golden-checker diffs.
- Annotator calibration artifacts (raw annotations, agreement metrics).
- Telemetry gating logs and sampling snapshots.

Appendix B — recommended DP & privacy presets by slice sensitivity:
- High-sensitivity (PII or proprietary content): epsilon <= 0.5, k>=100, telemetry sample_rate <= 0.0005
- Medium-sensitivity (business intent, non-identifying): epsilon <= 1.0, k>=50, telemetry sample_rate <= 0.001
- Low-sensitivity (public content): epsilon <= 2.0, k>=20, telemetry sample_rate <= 0.01
sections.heading: Operational playbooks (quick commands)

payload.page_title: Evaluation Retrospective & Priority Synthesis Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines a standardized retrospective process and a quantitative priority-synthesis framework for managing evaluation probes, probe budgets, and regression triage across model families and deployment tiers. It is intended for evaluators, model stewards, and platform engineers responsible for maintaining production quality while balancing cost and latency.

Why this exists

- We operate multiple evaluator fleets (shadow, canary, long-tail) with limited probe budget. Without a consistent prioritization algorithm and retrospective cadence, high-impact failures are discovered late and cost is allocated inefficiently.
- This playbook aligns the eval lifecycle with quantization migration, shadowing experiments, and incident triage so that responsibility, telemetry, and rollback paths are clear.

Scope & Terminology

- Probe: a single test instance (prompt + metadata) executed against a model variant as part of an evaluation job.
- Slice: a grouped set of probes targeting a semantic/functional area (e.g., payment-intent, legal-forms, multi-turn-coherence).
- Priority Score: numeric score used by the scheduler to allocate probes under budget constraints.
- Cohort Shadow: a runtime shadowing run that mirrors a subset of live traffic to a candidate model.

Principles

1. Value-first: prioritize probes that reduce customer-facing risk (safety, correctness, regression severity) ahead of exploratory coverage.
2. Cost-aware: embed per-probe expected token cost and latency into prioritization so we can trade coverage against spend.
3. Signal-driven retrospectives: run a short (weekly) quantitative retrospective that re-weights slices based on recent incidents, regressions, and drift.
4. Cross-model comparability: all shadow and eval runs must surface the same minimal telemetry contract (see Telemetry contract table).

Telemetry contract (minimum)

| Key | Type | Description | Owner | Example |
|------|------|-------------|-------|---------|
| probe_id | string | Unique probe identifier | evaluator-service | probe-20261102-0001 |
| slice_id | string | Logical slice name | probe-catalog | payment-intent-highvalue |
| model_variant | string | model id + quantization tag | model-onboarding | redwood-v2.1-8bit |
| latency_ms | integer | end-to-end inference latency | runtime | 84 |
| token_cost_est | float | estimated token cost for this probe | cost-service | 0.0042 |
| fidelity_delta | float | eval metric delta vs baseline (application-specific) | evaluator | -0.07 |
| pass_fail | enum | pass/fail/unknown based on sentinel | evaluator | fail |

Priority synthesis algorithm (high level)

PriorityScore = w_sev * SeverityImpact + w_freq * UsageFrequency + w_drift * DriftScore - w_cost * NormalizedCost - w_latency * NormalizedLatency + w_recency * RecencyBoost

Where weights (w_*) are learned/managed at the squad level and updated during retrospectives. Default weight suggestions (initial):

- w_sev = 6.0
- w_freq = 3.0
- w_drift = 2.5
- w_cost = 1.4
- w_latency = 0.8
- w_recency = 1.0
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- SeverityImpact is in [0,1] and estimated from historical user-impact events (see Incident-map).
- NormalizedCost is token_cost_est scaled to the fleet median cost per probe.
- RecencyBoost = exp(-days_since_last_evaluation / tau) with tau default 21.

Practical scheduler rules

1. Reserve 15% of weekly probe budget for critical-safety and top-10 slices (guaranteed)
2. Reserve 10% for quant-migration shadow cohorts (so we can test quant fallbacks without starving safety probes)
3. Remaining budget is allocated by PriorityScore descending until budget exhausted
4. For mixed-precision candidates, ensure at least N=50 probes per slice are run in both float and quant variants for statistical comparability (N configurable per slice)

Weekly retrospective process (30–60 minutes) — running steps

1. Data prep (Automated): exporter job builds a summary of the past 7 days: top failing slices, probe spend, latency distribution, newly landed PRs touching model/serving/runtime. (owner: evaluator-ops)
2. Incident alignment (5–10m): map any user-facing incidents or reliability alerts to affected slices and hypothesize causes.
3. Weight tuning (10–20m): update w_* weights where justified (evidence: fidelity_delta, incident severity counts, and cost overrides). Document changes with rationale.
4. Allocation commit (5m): commit the adjusted budget allocations and publish to scheduler config in the eval-mesh. Tag the config with weekly-retro-YYYYMMDD.
5. Follow-ups (as needed): create action items (e.g., increase probe coverage, add sentinel, run focused quant sweep). Assign owners and due dates.

Runbook: urgent regression detected in baseline service

1. Pager triggers (if fidelity_delta on production sentinel exceeds threshold): immediately spin a high-priority shadow cohort for the suspected model version (owner: model-oncall).
2. Triage (15m): gather first-pass diagnostics: top failing probes, tokenization diffs, latency spikes, quantization tags. Use the regression-hunt notebook template.
3. Canary rollback (if regression confirmed and severity >= P1): initiate model rollback per deployment playbook and open an incident.
4. Postmortem: run the retrospective process with emphasis on causality: code change, model data shift, quant misalignment, runtime bug.

Quant-aware eval addendum

- When testing quantized candidates, attach probe-level metadata: quant_backend (e.g., q4_0, int8_v2), kernel_variant, and fallback-path.
- Add a "coherence-sentinel" for multi-turn and function-call probes to detect early breakdowns unique to precision reduction.
- If quant candidate shows systematic token-level divergence > tol (default 0.12 BLEU-like delta for structured outputs) on high-value slices, escalate to quant-safety review.

Example scheduler config snippet (YAML)

scheduler_weekly_budget: 100000  # number of probes
reserves:
  safety_slices: 0.15
  quant_shadow: 0.10
  ad_hoc: 0.05
weights:
  severity: 6.0
  frequency: 3.0
  drift: 2.5
  cost: 1.4
  latency: 0.8
  recency: 1.0

Promptset stewardship and retirements

1. Promptsets must declare a retire-after window (default 18 months) and a stable-owner (team/squad).
2. During retrospectives, if a slice shows persistent low-fidelity signal and low usage, mark for scheduled deprecation and reallocation of probes.
3. When retiring, create a migration manifest that lists representative probes to preserve for historical reproducibility.

Ownership & roles

- Evaluator-ops: runs the scheduler, exports retrospectives, maintains probe-catalog.
- Model-steward: signs off on slice re-weighting for their model family and owns follow-up action items.
- Platform-runtime: ensures telemetry contract is honored and provides cost estimates per probe.
- Incident-team: owns serving rollback and postmortem coordination.

Metrics & SLOs for the eval system

- Coverage SLO: Top-25 slices must have weekly probe runs >= 90% of target (target defined per slice)
- Detection latency SLO: median time from regression emergence to detection in shadow runs <= 48 hours
- Probe cost SLO: weekly probe spend variance <= 20% vs planned budget

Template: weekly-retrospective summary (copy/paste)

Title: Weekly Eval Retro — YYYY-MM-DD
Owner: <evaluator-ops-person>
Top failing slices: [sliceA (n fails), sliceB (n fails)]
Top change causes: [quant-rollout, tokenizer-patch, prompt-regression]
Weight changes committed: [severity 6.0 -> 7.0] (rationale)
Budget commit: total X probes (safety: Y, quant: Z, ad_hoc: W)
Action items: - Replace sentinel for sliceA (owner: Alice) due: YYYY-MM-DD

Appendices

A. Regression hunting checklist (short)
- Confirm probe pass/fail criteria and re-run failing probes with seed control
- Compare tokenization and pre/post-processor diffs
- Verify model artifact (git tag), quant backend, and runtime kernels match expectations
- Run replay harness for 1000 nearest-neighbor probes to failing set

B. Quick CLI snippets
sections.heading: Normalization and scaling notes

sections.body: redwood-evalctl configs list --env=prod --tag=weekly-retro
sections.heading: list scheduled configs

sections.body:
redwood-evalctl cohort submit --model redwood-v2.3 --variant=q4_0 --slices payment-intent,legal-forms --budget 2000

C. FAQ (short)
Q: Who can change weights?
A: Squad model-stewards during the weekly retrospective or evaluator-ops for emergency adjustments with notification.

Q: What if the budget is exceeded mid-week?
A: Pause low-priority ad_hoc probes and re-run scheduler with an updated budget. If overruns persist, raise a finance-ops ticket.

Related docs and links

- Eval mesh scheduler spec: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-topology-and-slotting-cookbook-2026
- Quant migration safety contract: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

Contact

For questions, open a ticket in the evaluator-ops channel or ping #eval-retros on Slack.

Document change log

- 2026-05-11: Added quant addendum and CLI examples (Rohit Kapoor)
- 2026-11-02: Weight tuning defaults adjusted and runbook clarified (Elena García)

payload.page_title: Fidelity Anchoring and Shadow Cost Slate Allocator

sections.body: This playbook defines the Fidelity Anchoring protocol and the Shadow Cost Slate Allocation policy. It provides operational steps, configuration recipes, and escalation triggers designed to preserve response quality while bounding evaluation cost during shadow/onboarding and mixed-precision rollouts. The approach ties together: shadow evaluation orchestration, probe prioritization, tenant-aware cost allocation, quant-compat checks, and fast-triage triggers for regressions.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Goals:
  - Ensure production parity for critical quality slices (fidelity anchors) before model promotion.
  - Limit the eval spending of shadow fleets to a predictable monthly budget per service/tenant.
  - Provide deterministic triggers that surface fidelity regressions earlier in the onboarding pipeline.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a general-purpose model selection guide (see model-onboarding).
  - This playbook does not replace tenant billing systems; it provides allocation rules for evaluation spend only.
sections.heading: Goals and non-goals

sections.body:
- Applicable to: shadow fleets, canary evals, quant-shadow cohorts, and prompt-set probes used in onboarding for hosted/dedicated/private tiers.
- Components affected: eval-orchestrator, probe-scheduler, shadow-mesh, evaluator-sidecar, telemetry collector, cost-accounting service (eval-ledger).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Fidelity Anchor: a curated probe slice (usually 50-200 probes) representing production-critical behavior that must meet fidelity thresholds prior to rollout.
- Shadow Slate: a set of probes and traffic segments routed to a shadow service instance for evaluation.
- Slate Allocator: the policy engine that assigns budget and probe quotas to shadow slates.
- Quant Shadow: a shadow cohort running quantized model artifacts for compatibility testing.
sections.heading: Definitions (short)

sections.body:
- Probe Stewards (Applied ML team): curate anchors and maintain prompt templates.
- Onboarding Owner (Service/Product): request slate allocations and define critical slices.
- Eval Platform (engineering/infra): implements allocator, enforces budgets, exposes metrics.
- Runbook Owner (eng-sre): owns escalation and rollback steps when fidelity or cost breaches occur.
sections.heading: Roles & ownership

sections.body:
1) Anchor definition and acceptance criteria:
   - For every onboarding request, the Probe Steward provides 1-3 Fidelity Anchors with: rationale, probe examples, expected behavior, and acceptance thresholds (see example table).
sections.heading: Fidelity Anchoring protocol (practical steps)

sections.body:
| Anchor name | Probes | Metric | Accept threshold | Owner | Notes |
   |-------------|--------|--------|------------------|-------|-------|
   | billing-edge | 120 probes | semantic-accuracy @ top-1 | >= 92% | Payments SME | critical for SLO satisfaction |
   | session-completion | 80 probes | reply-coherence (human-rated) | >= 4.2/5 | Product owner | includes chained function calls |

2) Instrumentation contract:
   - Every shadow response must emit: probe_id, slate_id, seed, quant_profile, latency_ms, token_count, evaluator_version, and fidelity_scores (per-anchor metric).
   - Telemetry keys: eval.anchor_id, eval.slate, eval.quant_tag, eval.cost_units.

3) Anchor-first gating:
   - The promotion gate fails if any anchor for a service drops below its accept threshold for 3 consecutive daily windows or if drift >= 3 percentage points vs baseline.
sections.heading: Example acceptance table

sections.body:
- Objectives: cap monthly eval spend, fairly allocate budget between tenants, prefer targeted anchors over broad slices when budget constrained.
- Inputs:
  - Monthly eval_budget_per_service (USD) from product onboarding form
  - Probe cost estimate (cost_units per probe) derived from median token_count and backend cost model
  - Priority score (from Probe Steward) 0.0-1.0

- Core algorithm (description):
  1. Rank slates by priority_score * urgency_factor (urgency: hotfix/on-demand/test).
  2. For each slate in rank order, allocate probes until either the slate's anchor coverage target is met or remaining budget_exhaustion_threshold (RE_T) would be breached.
  3. If budget exhausted, partition remaining budget across top-K anchors (K configurable, default 2) proportional to priority_score.

- Configurable parameters (defaults):
  - RE_T (remaining budget exhaustion threshold) = 8% of monthly budget
  - K (top anchors to preserve) = 2
  - min_anchor_quota = 25 probes
sections.heading: Shadow Cost Slate Allocator (policy)

sections.body:
- Priority = 0.6 * owner_criticality + 0.3 * slice_prevalence + 0.1 * regression_history_score
- owner_criticality: 0/1/2 mapped to 0.2/0.6/1.0
- slice_prevalence: fraction of production traffic represented (0.0-1.0)
- regression_history_score: normalized 0-1 where 1 = frequent past regressions
sections.heading: Probe prioritization heuristic (short)

sections.body:
- Before a quant-shadow cohort is allowed any slate allocation, run the Quant Preflight (fast, synthetic) pipeline:
  1. Token-preservation check: run 200 synthetic prompts representative of anchors, verify token_count degradation < 1.5%
  2. Latency SLO check: median latency increase < 20% for target sequence lengths
  3. Coherence quick-scan: embed-based semantic similarity against float baseline; mean cosine >= 0.92
- Preflight failure modes and actions:
  - Token-preservation fail -> block quant-shadow from being scheduled and route to quant-tuning team for retraining/safety.
  - Latency fail -> allow with throttled quota and label as 'latency-risk' in slate metadata.
sections.heading: Quant compatibility and preflight checks

sections.body:
- Automated triggers that open a regression incident (triage priority):
  - Any Fidelity Anchor drop > 4 absolute percentage points in a 24h window -> severity P1 regression.
  - Drift in top-10 production slices that correlates with quant_tag or evaluator_version with p-value < 0.01 (stat test) -> P2.
  - Unexpected increase in human-reported failures from canary cohort > 3x baseline -> P2.
- Fast-path actions (immediate):
  1. Isolate failing slate and stop traffic to the shadow cohort.
  2. Snapshot probe examples and attach to incident ticket with anchor_id and quant_tag.
  3. Notify Probe Steward and Onboarding Owner.
  4. If anchor is critical and degradation persists, automatic rollback of rollout job (if any).
sections.heading: Regression triage triggers and fast-path

sections.body:
1) New onboarding request received:
   - Onboarding Owner fills eval_budget_per_service and marks up to 3 anchors with priority and acceptance criteria.
2) Probe Steward creates anchors and registers them in Probe Registry (probe-registry CLI: registry add-anchor --service payments --file anchors/payments-billing-anchor.yaml).
3) Eval Platform schedules a shadow slate via the Slate Allocator API (example below).
4) Run Quant Preflight for quant-shadow cohorts and mark slate metadata accordingly.
5) Continuous monitoring: dashboards for eval.anchor_health, eval.slate_cost, eval.monthly_spend_by_service. Alerts: anchor_drop, budget_exhaust, quant_preflight_fail.
sections.heading: Operational runbook (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Request:
  POST /api/v1/slates/allocate
sections.heading: Slate Allocator API example (pseudo-CLI)

sections.body:
service: payments
  requested_slates:
    - name: billing-edge-anchored
      anchor_id: payments-billing-v1
      target_probes: 120
      priority: high
  monthly_budget_usd: 1200

- Response:
  slate_id: SLATE-20260302-47
  allocated_probes: 95
  estimated_cost_usd: 83.60
  status: allocated
sections.heading: Body (YAML)

sections.body:
- Use the eval-alert CLI to generate a triage ticket and bundle artifacts:
  eval-alert create --slate SLATE-20260302-47 --anchor payments-billing-v1 --reason "anchor_drop" --attach probes.csv
sections.heading: Example notifier snippet (for incident)

sections.body:
- eval.anchor_health_percent (windowed daily)
- eval.slate_cost_usd (real-time)
- eval.monthly_spend_by_service (rolling 30d)
- eval.quant_preflight_pass_rate
- eval.anchor_regression_count (30d)
sections.heading: Metrics to monitor (essential)

sections.body:
| param | description | default | notes |
| RE_T | remaining budget threshold | 0.08 | fraction of monthly budget kept for emergency slates |
| min_anchor_quota | minimum probes per anchor | 25 | prevents starving small but critical anchors |
| K | protected anchors when budget exhausted | 2 | protect top-K anchors proportional to priority |
| preflight_latency_pct | maximum latency increase allowed in preflight | 20 | percent |

Rollout checklist for enabling Fidelity Anchoring for a new service:
1. Product/Service owner provides monthly eval budget and marks anchors.
2. Probe Steward registers anchors and verifies coverage against production logs.
3. Eval Platform configures allocator quota and schedules initial shadow slate with conservative quota (50% of requested).
4. Run quant preflight (if applicable).
5. Monitor anchor health for 7 days; if stable, increase quota to requested level.
6. Promote only after anchors meet acceptance criteria for 3 consecutive daily windows.
sections.heading: Example configuration table (configurable in allocator)

sections.body:
- Probe examples used for anchors must be redacted for PII before being stored in probe-registry.
- The Slate Allocator exposes per-tenant spend; privacy-sensitive slates should be labeled and flagged to the compliance queue.
sections.heading: Privacy and cost controls

sections.body:
- If anchor_health_percent intermittently toggles, check seed variance in probe generation and ensure seed is fixed for anchor probes.
- If monthly_spend_by_service shows unexpected spikes, inspect eval.slate_cost_usd and token_count distributions for recent slates.
sections.heading: Troubleshooting notes

sections.body:
- See eval-cost-slice-prioritization-and-resource-budgeting-2026 for budget baseline methodology.
- See quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026 for quant tuning and fallback procedures.

Appendix: example anchor YAML (registration):
---
anchor_id: payments-billing-v1
service: payments
owner: payments-product@redwood.com
priority: 0.9
probes_count: 120
metrics:
  - name: semantic_accuracy
    comparator: top1
    threshold: 0.92
notes: >
  Anchor derived from top-20 billing error samples and session logs. Redacted.
---
sections.heading: References and related materials

sections.body:
- Probe Stewarding: applied-ml@redwood.com (Maya Chen)
- Eval Platform: eng-eval@redwood.com
- Runbook owner (SRE): oncall-sre@redwood.com
sections.heading: Contact

sections.body:
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft and prototype allocator parameters added.
- 2026-02-01: Added quant preflight checks and CLI examples.
- 2026-03-02: Finalized metric names and escalations; published.

payload.page_title: Multi-seed aggregation and variance budgeting for eval stability

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This document defines the Multi-seed Aggregation and Variance Budgeting protocol (MAVB) used by Redwood's eval harness to quantify output stochasticity, attribute variance to sources (prompting, model nondeterminism, quantization, runtime caching), and set actionable variance budgets for production rollouts and regression triage.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all internal evaluation runs that influence model promotion, quantization decisions, or production rollouts (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Intended for use by applied-ML, model-onboarding, runtime, and SRE teams.
- Covers generation (chat/text), reranking, and embedding stability analyses where multiple random seeds or sampling strategies are relevant.

Definitions
-----------
- Seed run: One execution of an evaluation workload with a single RNG seed and fixed runtime settings.
- Seed ensemble: A set of N seed runs used to measure variance for a given workload slice.
- Variance budget: A pre-defined acceptable range (σ or interquartile range) for metric fluctuation attributable to nondeterminism.
- Attribution buckets: "prompt variance", "model stochasticity", "quantization impact", "runtime cache/batching".

Roles & Ownership
-----------------
- Evaluation Owner (Applied-ML): defines workload slices, target metrics, and baseline model.
- Runtime Owner (Serving Runtime): provides reproducible runtime configs and documents non-deterministic behaviors.
- Onboarding Lead (Model Onboarding): approves variance budgets for model promotion and signs off on triage.
- Regression Lead (Regression Triage): coordinates bisecting and blames assignment when variance exceeds budgets.

High-level protocol summary
---------------------------
1. Define workload slices (by prompt-type / user-slice / sequence length / language / quantization profile).
2. For each slice, run a seed ensemble of N runs (default N=7; N minimum = 5 for preliminary checks).
3. Compute per-metric aggregation (mean, median, stdev, IQR, bootstrap CI) across seeds.
4. Compare against the variance budget table; if exceeded, run attribution steps and trigger triage.
5. Record all raw seed traces, RNG seeds, runtime config, and KV-cache state hash in the eval store.

Determining ensemble size (N)
-----------------------------
- Small slices or quick smoke tests: N = 3–5 (informational only).
- Standard production slices: N = 7 (balance of power and cost).
- High-sensitivity slices (legal, safety): N = 15+ and use stratified sampling across RNG engine settings.
- Guidance: choose N such that 95% bootstrap CI of the primary metric width <= half the variance budget.

Aggregation methods and rationale
---------------------------------
- Use median as the primary central tendency for skewed generation metrics (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU for few-shot outputs).
- Report both stdev and IQR; prefer IQR for heavy-tailed distributions.
- Provide bootstrap percentile CI (1k resamples) for each metric and seed-aggregated score.
- For binary pass/fail checks (safety filters), report the proportion across seeds with Clopper–Pearson 95% CI.

Variance budgeting table (example)
----------------------------------
| Slice category            | Primary metric         | Variance budget (IQR) | Notes |
|--------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|-------|
| Short FAQ prompts (<64)  | answer-accuracy @1     | <= 3% points           | typical low variance |
| Long-context summarization | ROUGE-L               | <= 5 pts IQR           | cache-sensitive |
| Multi-lingual short prompts | BLEU (en→xx)         | <= 4 pts IQR           | cross-tokenization noise |
| Safety filter pass rate   | pass-rate (%)         | <= 1.5% points         | high-sensitivity |
| Embedding cosine (µ)      | mean cosine           | <= 0.005               | quantization-sensitive |

Attribution workflow
--------------------
1. If variance budget exceeded, re-run the seed ensemble with controlled toggles:
   - Fix RNG engine to deterministic mode (if supported).
   - Disable prefix/KV cache.
   - Run on a reference model binary (unquantized) and then on the quantized artifact.
   - Switch sampling strategy to greedy to isolate sampling noise.
2. For each toggle, compute delta in metric stdev/IQR. Attribute percent of variance explained to each bucket.
3. If quantization explains > 60% of excess variance, fail quantization promotion and open a quant-triage ticket.
4. If runtime cache/batching contributes > 30%, create a runtime investigation with traces and GPU scheduling logs.

Regression triage playbook (short)
----------------------------------
1. Tag the failing eval run and mark related traces as P0 for triage.
2. Run an automated bisect across commits and model checkpoints using the eval harness (see CLI below).
3. For suspected infra/runtime causes, reproduce on a minimal dedicated node with identical runtime config.
4. If model change suspected, request an annotated diff of token-level outputs across seeds and an error-slice report.
5. Document conclusion in the regression tracker with blame attribution and corrective action (rollback, quant-tune, prompt-harden).

Practical examples and CLI
-------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
```yaml
name: long-summary-xlang
baseline_model: redwood-open-7b-v2
slices:
  - name: long-docs
    length_range: [1024, 8192]
    prompt_template: templates/long-summary-v2.jinja
seeds: 7
sampling:
  method: top-p
  p: 0.92
  temperature: 0.8
runtime_config:
  kv_cache: enabled
  batch_size: 8
  quant_profile: q4_0
output_metrics:
  - rouge_l
  - readability_score
  - latency_ms
```
sections.heading: Example eval config (YAML) used by the harness

sections.body: $ eval-harness run --config long-summary-xlang.yaml --store /evals/mavb/2026-02-15
sections.heading: Run command (eval harness)

sections.body:
$ eval-harness bisect --config long-summary-xlang.yaml --commit-range abc123..def456 --seeds 5 --report /tmp/bisect.html

Data retention and artifact requirements
---------------------------------------
- Keep raw seed outputs and RNG seeds for 90 days for general audits; 365 days for safety-critical slices.
- Save runtime traces (trace ids) including kernel selection logs, KV-cache hashes, and batching metadata in the eval store.
- Attach quantization artifact id and build metadata when running quantized profiles.

Alerting thresholds and play-trigger rules
-----------------------------------------
- Automated alert when primary metric IQR exceeds budget on three consecutive runs for the same slice.
- PagerRule: if safety-filter pass-rate variance > budget, page Regression Lead and Safety Owner.
- Generate a "variance-drift" ticket automatically when long-term drift exceeds 2x budget over 30 days.

Integration with model onboarding and Optimize
---------------------------------------------
- Model onboarding adds variance budgets to the promotion checklist. The onboarding job fails if high-sensitivity slices exceed budgets.
- Redwood Optimize can suggest alternative quant profiles when quantization-attributed variance is detected; attach suggested profiles to the quant-triage ticket.

Quick reference checklist
-------------------------
- [ ] Define slices and primary metric
- [ ] Choose N seeds (≥5 for production)
- [ ] Run seed ensemble and compute IQR/CI
- [ ] Compare to variance budget table
- [ ] If exceeded: run attribution toggles
- [ ] If still failed: trigger regression triage
- [ ] Record findings and attach raw traces

Appendix A — Example report output (CSV columns)
------------------------------------------------
run_id, seed, slice_name, metric_name, metric_value, runtime_config_id, quant_artifact_id, kv_cache_hash, trace_id

Appendix B — Troubleshooting tips
---------------------------------
- High variance but low mean change: likely sampling noise — increase seeds or fix to greedy for diagnostic runs.
- Variance concentrated in long-context slices: look for KV cache fingerprint mismatches or tokenization boundary issues.
- Quantization large jumps in specific tokens: run token-level log-prob difference across seeds and check for Outlier Token Instances (OTIs).

Related pages
-------------
- See also: Stochastic Eval Replay and Determinism Protocol (link above), Quantization Failure Modes and Recovery Playbook, Regression Bisect Assistant.

payload.page_title: Probe Reshaper and Quant-Routing Manual

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the Probe Reshaper component of the Eval Harness: a runtime subsystem that transforms incoming evaluation probes (prompt + context bundles) to improve stability under mixed-quant deployments while preserving privacy constraints and probe fidelity. The Reshaper sits in the eval ingress path and cooperates with the Quant Routing policy engine to decide target variants (fp16, q4, q8_0, etc.), prompt rewrites, and when to fall back to higher-fidelity evaluation.

Goals

- Reduce false-positive regressions caused purely by quantization-induced prompt sensitivity.
- Maintain probe privacy (avoid leaking tenant metadata) during on-host transformations and routing decisions.
- Provide deterministic, auditable transformations so eval results are reproducible.
- Minimize additional latency and token-cost overhead across the eval fleet.

Scope and Non-Goals

- In scope: runtime probe normalization, token-level rewrite heuristics, routing decisions to quantized artifact variants, per-probe fidelity annotations, audit logging and provenance metadata.
- Out of scope: model training, core quantizer development, human annotation workflows (except where annotations are needed for rollback debugging).

Terminology

- Probe: an evaluation input consisting of prompt text, metadata (tenant_id, slice_id), and optional attachment(s).
- Reshaping: a deterministic transformation applied to a probe (canonicalization, priming normalization, token-preserving rewrites).

Design overview

1) Ingress flow (high level):
- EvalOrchestrator -> ProbeReshaper -> QuantRoutingPolicy -> ShadowDispatcher -> Runner (target variant)

2) Two-layer decision model:
- Static eligibility checks (probe size, tenant opt-outs, confidentiality flags).
- Dynamic sensitivity estimation (fast SIMD tokenizer pass + learned sensitivity model) that assigns a QuantRiskScore.

Probe Reshaper responsibilities

- Canonicalize whitespace, normalize non-semantic Unicode (NFKC), and normalize date/time mentions into token-short forms when appropriate.
- Apply deterministic priming compression for long-context probes using the PrimingCompact pattern (keeps anchors and last N-turns intact).
- Execute token-preserving obfuscation for tenant-identifying strings (email, org names) when tenant requests privacy gating. Obfuscation is reversible only within the audit enclave (KMS-protected key) and replaced with a stable placeholder for the runner.
- Emit a provenance blob: {reshaper_version, seed, deterministic_hash, transformations_applied} appended to probe metadata for downstream reconciliation.

Quant Routing policy

Routing decisions are the joint output of: static rules, quant risk score, and traffic cost budget. The routing policy maps to target variant IDs and optional fidelity gates (e.g., force high-fidelity when a quality probe fails).

Policy matrix (example)

| QuantRiskScore | ProbeLengthTokens | TenantTier | RouteRecommendation |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0-0.15 | <512 | any | q8_0 (fast) |
| 0.15-0.45 | <1024 | standard | q4 + priming-compact |
| 0.45-0.80 | any | standard | shadow-first: run on q8_0 with synchronous high-fidelity replay on fp16 if variance > threshold |
| >0.80 | any | enterprise | fp16 (no quant) |

Note: thresholds are tunable per-service via the RoutingConfig manifest (see examples).

Deterministic Rewrites and Auditing

- All rewrites are deterministic and keyed by probe deterministic_hash and reshaper_version. Repro playbacks should yield identical rewritten prompts.
- The provenance blob is stored alongside probe outputs in the EvalArtifact store. For privacy, reversible obfuscation keys are stored in KMSEnclave and are auditable via the Audit Service.

Prompt rewrite strategies (examples)

1) Anchor-preserving compression
- Keep anchor sentences (first and last 2 sentences) and compress middle paragraphs by extracting salient bullet points using a light-weight extractor (heuristic based on punctuation + named entity density).
- Use when probe length > 2x median and QuantRiskScore > 0.2.

2) Lexical normalization
- Replace numerals/dates with canonical tokens (e.g., 2026-02-12 -> [DATE_2026]) when the probe is judged to be structurally invariant. This reduces tokenization variance across quant builds.

3) Controlled paraphrase (limited)
- Apply a single-pass paraphrase using the on-host micro-transformer only when sensitivity model predicts reduced variance and tenant has opted-in. Paraphrases are constrained to preserve named entities and function-call signatures.

Example config manifests (YAML snippet)

---
reshaper_version: v2.1
max_rewrite_tokens: 120
paraphrase_allowed: false
privacy_gating: true
sensitivity_model: fast-token-mlr-v1
provenance_fields: [reshaper_version,det_hash,transformations]
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
---
default_thresholds:
  low: 0.15
  medium: 0.45
  high: 0.80
tenant_overrides:
  enterprise-tenant: {force_fp16: true}
cost_budget_bucket: standard

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Onboarding a new probe suite:
  a) Register the probe set with the Eval Registry including expected fidelity label (anchor, high-fidelity, smoke).
  b) Run the local Reshaper CLI to preview transformed probes: eval-reshaaper --manifest manifest.yml --preview > previews.tar.gz
  c) Submit preview to the shadow farm with routingConfig=test to generate a delta heatmap.

2) Investigating a regression suspected to be quant-sensitive:
  1. Identify failing probes via Eval Dashboard. Note provenance blob for each probe.
  2. Re-run failing probes with --force-fp16 on the Reshaper CLI to compare diffs.
  3. If diffs disappear on fp16, tag the slice with quant-risk and schedule targeted annotation.
  4. Optionally enable synchronous shadow replay (q8_0 + fp16) for the impacted slice for 24–72 hours.

CLI examples

- Preview transformations:
  eval-reshaper preview --input probes.jsonl --manifest routing-test.yml --out previews.tar.gz

- Run a single probe through the reshaper locally and print provenance:
  echo '{"prompt":"How do I reset password?","metadata":{"tenant":"acme"}}' | eval-reshaper transform --print-provenance

Monitoring and SLOs

- Reshaper CPU P95 per-probe latency: < 25ms (target); alert if > 50ms on median traffic.
- Provenance attach rate: 100% for all reshaped probes.
- Determinism assertion failure rate: < 0.01% (identified by hash mismatch between preview and runtime).
- QuantRouting misclassification (observed variance > 0.05 between selected variant and fp16 baseline): < 2% of traffic per week.

Telemetry and dashboards

- Key dashboards: ProbeReshaper-Latency, QuantRisk-Distribution, ShadowReplay-DeltaHeatmap, Provenance-Integrity.
- Important alerts: sudden shift in QuantRisk distribution, increase in deterministic mismatch, rapid growth of privacy-gated probes.

Privacy and security considerations

- Tenant-identifying obfuscation: only stable placeholders and deterministic hashes are present outside the audit enclave. Restore requires KMS permissions and a documented audit trail.
- Provenance storage: provenance blobs for restricted probes are stored with confidentiality flag and retention policy aligned with legal.

Rollout checklist (canary -> global)

1) Unit tests for all rewrite strategies and determinism checks.
2) Local preview and manual review by Probe Stewards.
3) Shadow run against q8_0 + fp16 for 48 hours on a representative slice.
4) Validate telemetry and SLOs on canary fleet (1% traffic).
5) Gradual rollout with 5/20/50/100% stages, validating misclassification and latency quotas at each stage.

Ownership and contacts

- Component owner: Jordan Patel (Applied ML Platform)
- Oncall rotation: applied-ml-eval-oncall@redwood.internal (week-based)
- Reviewers: Dr. Mei Chen (Evaluator models), Rafael Gomez (Quant infra)

Appendix: troubleshooting quick hits

- If deterministic hashes differ between preview and runtime: check reshaper_version mismatch; ensure feature flags match and pull the latest manifest from ConfigStore.
- If QuantRiskScore is anomalously high for short probes: verify tokenization model alignment (tokenizer revisions are listed in quant-profile manifest).

Changelog

- 2026-02-12: v1.0 initial draft.
- 2026-03-04: v2.1 add privacy gating, provenance schema, and updated routing thresholds.

References

- Eval Mesh topology cookbook (internal): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-topology-and-slotting-cookbook-2026
- Quant shadow fidelity simulator: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quant-shadow-fidelity-simulator-2026

Feedback and next steps

- Submit PRs to the Reshaper repo and attach unit test results to the manifest. For feature requests or disputes about routing thresholds, open an RFC in the Applied ML team board and tag the reviewers.

payload.page_title: Longtail Continuous Scan Playbook for Production Evals

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook describes the Longtail Continuous Scan (LCS) process: an automated, prioritized, and privacy-conscious approach to running small, frequent, and broad-spectrum evaluations of models in production-like conditions. LCS targets tail distributions and low-frequency prompt slices that commonly surface quality regressions after deployments, quantization, or major prompt/handler changes.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood studio-managed models and verified open-model variants used in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers evaluation orchestration, slicing, scheduling, metric thresholds, alerting, and first-response triage for long-tail failures.
- Excludes heavy offline human-labeling efforts (those are handled by the annotation pipeline documented separately).

Objectives and SLOs

- Detect regression signals originating from: model updates, quantization changes, routing fallback, KV-cache invalidation, and prompt-surface changes.
- Time-to-detect: median 6 hours from the first anomalous tail observation.
- Time-to-triage (initial owner assignment): 2 hours after a severity-2 alert.
- False-positive rate target: < 12% for automated alerts after calibration.

Glossary

- Longtail slice: A prompt/user pattern with low request volume but high business risk (e.g., legal disclaimers, financial templates, multi-step instructions).
- Scan job: A configured run of LCS that samples prompts, model variants, and runtime settings.
- Seedset: Curated minimal prompt examples used to bootstrap a slice.

Architecture overview

1) Controller: Scheduler service that farms jobs to the eval harness.
2) Runner pool: Ephemeral workers that execute model calls (can run against hosted endpoints, dedicated pools, or shadow VPC endpoints).
3) Aggregator: Time-series store and comparator that computes stability metrics and drift signals.
4) Alerting layer: Rule engine that applies thresholds and enriches signals with provenance to emit alerts to PagerDuty/Slack.

Scan types and when to run them

- Smoke Scan (hourly): 100 weighted prompts across high-priority slices. Fast checks for immediate regressions after traffic-shaping or small rollouts.
- Focus Scan (every 6 hours): 500 prompts concentrated on business-critical low-volume slices and recent failing seeds. Includes edge-case adversarial prompts.
- Exploration Scan (daily): 3k prompts sampled stratified by locale, token-length buckets, user-agent signals, and model-quantization variant. Used for drift discovery and slice expansion.

Prioritization and budgeting

- Each customer and route is assigned a priority weight (0-10) by product owners. Priority influences sampling probability.
- GPU budget caps: LCS jobs cannot exceed 8 GPU-hours per region per day by default; request increases via capacity requests.

Data handling and privacy

- Do not store raw customer prompt text unless explicitly consented. All LCS jobs use pseudonymized prompt keys and salted hashing.
- Seedsets that contain customer data must be tagged "PII-sensitive" and routed to a private shadow cluster with KMS-protected logs.
- Logs kept for debug: sanitized prompt hash, token counts, model variant, latency, and top-3 token-probability deltas. Retention: 30 days by default.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Response Stability Index (RSI): measures distributional shift over n-gram/embedding space. Threshold: RSI delta > 0.12 triggers a warning; > 0.25 triggers an incident.
- Semantic Recall (SR): fraction of ground-truth keyphrases present in model outputs for structured tasks. Threshold: drop > 6% (relative) triggers a high-priority alert.
- Safety-Trigger Rate (STR): rate of policy-flagging tokens per 1k responses. Threshold: absolute STR > 4 and increase > 2x baseline triggers immediate review.
sections.heading: Primary metrics (automatic)

sections.body:
- Median latency (ms), 95th percentile latency, kv-cache hit ratio, and truncated-output rate.

Regression detection heuristics

- Multi-evidence consensus: an alert requires at least two metric classes to exhibit degradation (e.g., RSI + SR), unless the metric is a safety hit.
- Rolling-window confirmation: short blips are suppressed using a 3-sample exponential smoothing prior to alerting.
- Model-variant correlation: anomalies that correlate only with a single variant (e.g., quantized-int8) tag the alert as "quant-suspect".

Triage playbook (first 6 steps)

1) Alert enrichment: The aggregator appends last-known rollout id, model-commit, quant-profile id, and route config.
2) Owner assignment: PagerDuty integration assigns the alert to the model-owner rotation.
3) Immediate checks (automated):
   a) Verify model-commit changed in the last 24 hours.
   b) Check KV cache flush events or recent cache eviction logs.
   c) Examine autoscaler events and pod restarts for the model cluster.
4) Canary rollback: If the regression aligns to the canary rollout id and the rollback window is open, trigger automated rollback to prior canary snapshot.
5) Shadow replay: Launch focused shadow-run against previous known-good variant for 200 seeds. Compare diffs and attach to the ticket.
6) Human review: If automated checks are inconclusive, assign to applied-ml for semantic review and label impacted slices.
sections.heading: Secondary metrics (profiling)

sections.body:
- Verify reproducibility using the seedset with deterministic RNG.
- Re-run with and without quantization to isolate numeric sensitivity.
- Re-run with cached KV disabled to test cache-sensitivity regressions.
- If safety flags increased, run the safety-deep-eval (1000 synthetic adversarial prompts) before public rollback.

Observability, alert templates, and runbook snippets
sections.heading: Detailed triage checklist (owners should follow)

sections.body:
- Title: LCS Alert: {metric} regression on {route} (severity {1|2|3})
- Body: One-line summary, metric deltas, affected model-variants, last rollout id, link to aggregator graph, and link to reproduction job.
sections.heading: Alert template (Slack / PagerDuty summary)

sections.body:
- RSI time-series with slice decomposition (lines per locale/token-length).
- SR per variant as bar-chart with error bands.
- Top-10 diffs in token-probability mass as a table.

Automation recipes and example configs

Example LCS job config (YAML, abbreviated):

```
job_id: lcs.focus.20260305
priority_weight: 8
slices:
  - id: legal-disclaimer
    seedset: s3://lcs/seeds/legal-v3.csv
    sample_ratio: 0.6
  - id: financial-templates
    seedset: s3://lcs/seeds/finance-v2.csv
    sample_ratio: 0.3
variants:
  - model: rdx-gpt-13b
    quant_profile: quant-int8-a
  - model: rdx-gpt-13b
    quant_profile: fq-16
budget:
  max_gpu_hours: 2
  max_concurrent_workers: 6
output_policy: hash-only
```

CLI example to kick off a Focus Scan against a private endpoint:

$ rdx-eval run --job-config s3://lcs/configs/lcs.focus.20260305.yaml --target private-shadow --concurrency 4 --tags longtail,focus

Onboarding checklist for a new model into LCS

1) Register model variant and quant profiles with the aggregator catalog.
2) Provide initial seedsets for priority slices (min 40 seeds per slice).
3) Configure run-time limits and private-vpc access if seeds contain customer-derived patterns.
4) Run a baseline Exploration Scan and upload baseline metric snapshots to the baseline store.

Ownership and escalation

- LCS Controller: eng-infra (owner: Priya Gupta)
- Aggregator & rules: applied-ml (owner: Arjun Patel)
- On-call triage: model-owner rotation (list maintained in Oncall Playbook)

Related pages and artifacts

- Seedset schema: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/seedset-schema-spec-2025
- Safety deep-eval: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/continuous-safety-eval-pipeline-and-integration-guide-2026
- Quantization safety checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-failure-modes-and-recovery-playbook-2026

Appendix: sample alert payload (JSON)

{
  "alert_id": "lcs-20260305-8fb2",
  "route": "/api/v1/generate",
  "metric": "RSI",
  "delta": "0.31",
  "top_slices": ["legal-disclaimer", "long-form-instructions"],
  "variants": ["rdx-gpt-13b:quant-int8-a"],
  "links": {"repro_job": "https://internal.redwood/eval/12345"}
}

This playbook will be revised as LCS matures; for questions or improvement proposals, contact the owners listed above.
