payload.page_title: Adaptive Eval Mixer: Scheduling, Safety & Cost-aware Mixing

sections.body:
Overview:

This document describes the Adaptive Eval Mixer (AEM) — a scheduling and mixing policy for the eval harness that balances safety coverage, latency-sensitive probes, and cost budgets across hybrid workloads (shadow, synthetic, and live-mirrored traffic). AEM is intended for use by the eval-harness service (eval-mixer-service) and the probe-orchestrator layer when routing probes to private/dedicated/hosted model endpoints.

Goals:
- Maintain a minimum safety probe coverage (SLO) across critical slices while minimizing incremental token cost.
- Prioritize low-latency functional checks for production-impacting routes.
- Adapt probe mix to changing workload fingerprints and telemetry (cold-starts, quantized deployments, new model versions).
- Provide clear roll-forward and rollback criteria when the probe mix detects regressions.

Scope and Audience:
- Applies to eval-harness orchestration and the probe scheduling stage; integrates with eval-mesh and promotion pipelines.
- Intended readers: SREs, Applied ML Engineers, Oncall evaluators, Release engineers.

Motivation and Problem Statement:
Teams running continuous evaluations face three competing constraints: safety (need broad behavioral coverage), fidelity (samples that reflect production slices), and cost (token/compute budgets for evaluators). Existing static schedules either overspend or leave blind spots when workload distributions shift. AEM provides a lightweight, adaptive control loop to rebalance probe types and priorities with explicit safety cordons.

Design Summary:
1) Probe classes:
   - Safety Probes: curated sentinel prompts and adversarial probes (high priority).
   - Functional Probes: workload-derived samples (medium priority).
   - Smoke Probes: short health checks and latency-sensitive triggers (high priority, low cost).
   - Quant Probes: model/quantization-specific stress tests (expense varies).

2) Mixer Policy Layers:
   - Hard Safety Floor: a minimum percentage of probe budget always reserved for Safety Probes per model-route slice (default 15%).
   - Priority Buckets: smoke > safety > functional > quant; each bucket has a configured concurrency cap and token cap.
   - Adaptive Rebalancer: every 10 minutes assesses telemetry and shifts share between functional and quant probes using an exponential moving average (EMA) of failure rate and token burn.

3) Cost Smoothing and Throttles:
   - Daily token budget per model name and environment (e.g., prod-shadow: 1.2M tokens/day).
   - Burst window: allow 2x budget for 30 minutes if safety health is green; otherwise capped to 85% of baseline.

Config (defaults):
| setting | default | description |
|---|---:|---|
| safety_floor_pct | "15" | percent of probe budget reserved for safety probes per slice |
| smoke_concurrency | "50" | max concurrent smoke probes per region |
| functional_share_initial | "60" | initial percent share for functional probes |
| quant_share_initial | "10" | initial percent share for quant probes |
| rebalancer_interval_sec | "600" | seconds between rebalancer runs |
| token_budget_prod_shadow | "1200000" | tokens/day for prod-shadow workload |

Mixer algorithm (high level):
1. Gather slice telemetry (failure_rate, p95_latency, token_burn) for the last monitoring window.
2. If any safety sentinel tripped in last window: raise safety priority and pause quant probes for 30 minutes.
3. Compute desired_share for functional vs quant using:
   desired_share_functional = clamp(functional_share_current * (1 + alpha*(failure_rate - target_failure)), 30%, 90%)
   desired_share_quant = 100% - safety_floor_pct - desired_share_functional - smoke_share_estimate
4. Apply smoothing with EMA (beta=0.3) to avoid oscillations.
5. Enforce token budget caps and per-region concurrency constraints.

Telemetrics and SLOs:
- Safety coverage SLO: ">= 99% of canonical sentinels executed per 24h window".
- Probe latency SLO (smoke probes): p95 < 120ms for synthetic network and p95 < 300ms for private deployments.
- Daily token budget utilization alert: > 85% of daily budget for any model-route triggers a cost review.

Integration points and components:
- eval-mixer-service: central mixer that exposes a scheduling API (/v1/mixer/schedule).
- probe-orchestrator: worker pool that accepts schedules and stimulates endpoints.
- telemetry-collector: ingest probe results and emits metrics (aem.safety.tripped, aem.token.burn).
- rollout-controller: listens for regression events and can pause/reduce functional probe share across slices.

API examples:
1) Request schedule (POST /v1/mixer/schedule):
{
  "model": "redwood-v2-13b-quant",
  "route": "chat-completion-prod",
  "window": "10m"
}
Response:
{
  "schedule_id": "sch-2026022011",
  "buckets": {"smoke": 10, "safety": 60, "functional": 120, "quant": 10},
  "token_budget_alloc": 45000
}

YAML config snippet (eval-mixer.yaml):
rebalancer_interval_sec: 600
safety_floor_pct: 15
smoke_share_estimate: 5
functional_share_initial: 60
quant_share_initial: 10
per_model_daily_token_budget:
  redwood-v2-13b-quant:
    prod-shadow: 1200000
    canary: 300000

Operational procedures (runbook):
1) On safety sentinel failure:
   a) Pager to applied-ml oncall.
   b) eval-mixer automatically pauses quant probes for affected slice for 30 minutes.
   c) Triage steps: reproduce with safety probe locally, capture outputs and tokenization diff, annotate in incident ticket.
2) On budget overrun alert (>85%):
   a) Ownership: cost-ops and model-owner.
   b) Short-term mitigation: set functional_share_initial -= 15%, increase rebalancer_interval_sec to 1200s.
   c) Long-term: re-evaluate probe sampling policy and archive low-value probes.
3) On persistent p95 latency regressions for smoke probes:
   a) Route smoke probes to an alternate region (if available).
   b) If region-level degradation persists, mark route degraded and notify SREs.

Validation and Promotion Criteria for New Mixer Rules:
- Unit tests covering rebalancer math and clamp behaviors.
- Integration test: simulated telemetry scenarios (safety trip, burst, cold-start) with deterministic outcomes.
- Shadow rollout for 48 hours against prod-shadow with feature-flag true; require zero safety sentinel regressions and token spend within 110% of expected.

Rollout plan:
1. Canary: enable AEM on 5% of shadow traffic for 48h.
2. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 7 days with holds at each step and automated validation checks.
3. Post-rollout audit: QA to run cross-workload fidelity suite and report anomalies.

Ownership and Contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (Applied ML Infrastructure)
- Secondary: Diego Alvarez (SRE)
- Oncall: eval-harness rotation (see /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/oncall-contacts)

Related pages:

- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026

Appendix: Example telemetry alert mappings (prometheus rules)
- aem_safety_tripped_total > 0 -> pager to applied-ml (severity P1)
- aem_token_budget_ratio > 0.85 -> email to cost-ops (severity P2)

Notes and Future work:
- Explore reinforcement-learning-based mixing for long-lived models with stable telemetry.
- Add per-customer privacy-aware censors for safety probes when running on private deployments.

payload.page_title: Probe Artifact Versioning and Reproducibility Manifest

sections.body:
Summary
This document defines the artifact model, versioning policy, and reproducibility guarantees for evaluation probes, synthesized test cases, and derived evaluation artifacts used by the Eval Harness. It prescribes manifest formats, CI gating rules, archival tiers, and an operational playbook for diagnosing non-reproducible runs.

Audience
- Applied ML engineers building evaluation probes and test artifacts
- Evaluator maintainers who run scheduled and on-demand evaluation workloads
- SRE and CI owners responsible for eval artifact storage and retrieval

Goals
1. Provide a single canonical manifest format that captures provenance for every eval artifact (probes, annotation sets, priming templates, seed RNG, quant profiles).
2. Make evaluation runs reproducible end-to-end for at least 90% of scheduled regression/eval jobs (exceptions explained below).
3. Reduce time-to-investigation for non-reproducible failures via deterministic manifest-driven replay.
4. Define retention/archival and access controls appropriate for artifact sensitivity.

Key terminology
- Probe: an individual test case or stimulus used to exercise a model (e.g., prompt + metadata + expected slice tag).
- Artifact: any file produced or consumed by eval jobs (probes, annotations, model weights reference, quant profiles, tokenizer snapshots).
- Manifest: a single JSON (see Appendix) that references artifacts, their checksums, seed values, environment hashes, and toolchain versions.
- Reproducible run: an eval execution that, when replayed using the manifest and identical model binary/tag, produces the same scoring outputs within defined stability bounds.

Artifact model and manifest fields
Every artifact must be registered with the registry service and accompanied by a manifest. The manifest fields below are mandatory unless noted as optional. Store manifests alongside artifacts in the eval-asset S3 bucket path prefixed by service/owner/date/manifest.json.

Table: Mandatory manifest fields (ASCII table)
| field | type | description | example |
| manifest_version | string | manifest schema version | v1 |
| artifact_id | string | stable GUID for the probe batch | probe-batch-20241112-7f3a |
| artifacts | list | list of artifact entries (see entry table) | [ ... ] |
| rng_seed | string | PRNG seed used to synthesize stochastic probes (hex) or "none" | 0x9f1a2b |
| tokenizer_snapshot | string | tokenizer version/hash used for tokenization | token-v202405-abc123 |
| toolchain_hash | string | git commit hash of evaluator & adapters used | d4f7c9e |
| environment_os | string | base image identifier | ubuntu-22.04-eval-2024 |
| quant_profile_ref | string (optional) | reference to quantization profile used during shadow/quant runs | quant-profiles/q1-2025 |
| created_by | string | author or pipeline that produced the manifest | eval-factory-v2 |
| checksum | string | SHA256 checksum of the concatenated artifact contents referenced by the manifest | sha256:... |

Table: artifacts entry fields (per artifact)
| name | path | content_type | checksum | role |
| user-intent-probes.json | s3://eval-assets/probes/2024/11/ .. | application/json | sha256:... | probe_batch |
| annotator-csv | s3://... | text/csv | sha256:... | labels |

Versioning policy (short)
1) Use semantic manifest_version (v1, v2) to signal schema changes. 2) Artifact IDs are immutable. If a probe set is modified, produce a new artifact_id and manifest. 3) All artifacts must include a checksum (SHA256) and a human-readable changelog in the manifest metadata. 4) Atomically publish manifests: a manifest is only considered 'promoted' when it is visible in the registry index and the checksum validates against stored objects.

Reproducibility classes and tolerance windows
Not all eval workloads are fully deterministic. We define three reproducibility classes to set expectations:
- Deterministic (class D): Tokenization + model call + deterministic seeds -> bytewise identical outputs expected.
- Stable (class S): Outputs may differ by formatting or whitespace or minor probabilistic variance. We define stability thresholds: e.g., top-1 label agreement >= 98% and scalar metric delta <= 0.5%.
- Non-deterministic (class N): Scenarios that rely on external stochastic components (human-in-the-loop re-rankers, external API augmentations). Acceptable reproduction is manual triage.

Every eval job must declare its reproducibility_class in the job spec. CI will mark runs that do not meet the class target as "repro-check-failed" and attach the manifest and diffs.

Repro checklist (authoring guidance)
- Record and include PRNG seed (or explicit "none" if omitted).
- Snapshot tokenizer and any normalization code. Include pre-tokenization scripts in artifact list.
- Lock evaluator toolchain at a commit hash; include build artifacts or container image digest.
- Avoid external dependency calls during probe synthesis; if unavoidable, capture response corpus as an artifact.
- Annotator assignments: include annotator hash (anonymized), annotation tool version, and sampling policy.

CI/CD integration and gating rules
Gating rules for commit pipelines that change probes, evaluator code, or scheduling:
1. Probe author submits artifact PR that includes: artifact files, manifest draft, unit tests for probes (schema validation), and a smoke script to run the probe batch locally.
2. CI validations: schema validation, checksum verification, tokenization smoke-run, lightweight eval against a canned model snapshot (<= 10 examples) to validate end-to-end path.
3. If CI passes, the artifact is staged into the shadow registry (staging prefix) and a promotion job is scheduled to run against the nightly shadow fleet.
4. Promotion policies: 24h shadow runs with coverage targets (see below) must pass to allow artifact_id to be included in production-scheduled evals.

Coverage targets for promotion
- For standard probe batches: >= 95% execution coverage across probe items in shadow runs.
- For long-tail slices: randomized sampling of 5% of items with priority to unique tokens.
- For quant-sensitivity profiles: all probes targeting quant edgecases must execute at least once in a mixed-precision shadow cohort.

Investigating non-reproducible runs: runbook (operator steps)
1. Collect manifest and the run metadata (job id, fleet view, model tag).
2. Validate artifact checksums: run the manifest checksum verification script.
   - CLI: eval-registry verify --manifest s3://.../manifest.json
3. Re-run locally with the manifest pinned to the same toolchain hash and tokenizer snapshot. Use docker image digest if provided.
   - Example: docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work eval-evaluator:d4f7c9e /work/run_replay --manifest /work/manifest.json --model-tag redwood/gpt-serve:v3
4. If local replay differs, diff output to identify drift: whitespace/tokenization vs semantic. Use the repro-diff tool: repro-diff --left run1.json --right run2.json --thresholds config.yaml
5. If diff indicates tokenizer drift, compare tokenizer snapshots and token counts per prompt. If toolchain mismatch, escalate to evaluator owners. If stochastic variance, check rng_seed and class.
6. Document the triage in the regression tracker with tags: repro:failed, cause:<tokenizer|toolchain|stochastic|external>, mitigation_plan, and attach the manifest.

Archival, retention, and sensitivity tiers
- Tier A (public-safe): non-PII probes and public prompts. Retain 730 days, hot retrieval.
- Tier B (sensitive but internal): contains potential client-specific or sensitive structure. Retain 365 days, warm. Access requires team role binding.
- Tier C (PII/regulated): encrypt-at-rest, HSM-managed keys, retain 90 days unless retention exception approved by privacy team.
Manifests must include "confidentiality_tier" and link to the access control group in the registry.

Operational metrics to track
- Repro success rate per job type (target: 90% deterministic reproducibility for scheduled regression jobs).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for non-reproducible runs (target: < 2 hours from job completion to triage start).
- Ratio of manifest-promoted artifacts to total staged artifacts (target: >= 0.8 after three shadow iterations).

Appendix: minimal manifest example (v1)
{"manifest_version": "v1",
  "artifact_id": "probe-batch-20241112-7f3a",
  "artifacts": [
    {"name": "user-intent-probes.json", "path": "s3://eval-assets/probes/2024/11/user-intent-probes.json", "content_type": "application/json", "checksum": "sha256:abcd...", "role": "probe_batch"},
    {"name": "annotators.csv", "path": "s3://eval-assets/annotations/2024/11/annotators.csv", "content_type": "text/csv", "checksum": "sha256:ef01...", "role": "labels"}
  ],
  "rng_seed": "0x9f1a2b",
  "tokenizer_snapshot": "token-v202405-abc123",
  "toolchain_hash": "d4f7c9e",
  "environment_os": "ubuntu-22.04-eval-2024",
  "created_by": "eval-factory-v2",
  "checksum": "sha256:masterchecksum...",
  "confidentiality_tier": "Tier B"
}

Appendix: helper CLI commands
- Register artifact: eval-registry register --manifest ./manifest.json --bucket eval-assets --owner team-evals
- Verify: eval-registry verify --manifest s3://eval-assets/.../manifest.json
- Replay: eval-replay --manifest /tmp/manifest.json --model-tag redwood/gpt-serve:v3 --output /tmp/replay.json

Ownership and contacts
- Primary: Applied ML Eval Platform (team-evals@redwood.ai)
- Secondary: Model Onboarding (model-onboarding@redwood.ai)
- Pager: eng-oncall (for production shadow failures affecting evaluation SLAs)

Change log
- 2024-11-12: v1 initial draft and publication.
- 2025-06-03: Clarified triage steps and added retention tiers.

Related pages and references
- Evaluation asset registry service contract (internal)
- Shadow-run promotion job details and CI templates
- Tokenizer snapshot format spec

End of document

payload.page_title: Eval metrics heuristics and explainable slice signatures

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This document defines a pragmatic set of metric selection heuristics and a compact, explainable "slice signature" format for describing and tracking behavioral slices used across our eval harness. The goal is to make metric choices auditable, stabilize alerting, and speed regression triage by attaching human-readable signatures and automated fingerprints to each slice used in continuous and shadow evals.

Intended audience
- Applied ML engineers
- Evaluators and data scientists
- SREs and oncall reviewers handling model regressions

Motivation
- Many regressions are surfaced by noisy metrics or improperly scoped slices. We need a lightweight, reproducible contract that encodes what a slice measures, why the metric matters for product quality, and how to interpret alerts.
- Slice signatures make it quicker to determine whether a signal is a data/telemetry problem, a model-level behavioral change, or an infrastructural artifact (e.g., quantization/KV cache interaction).

Scope
- Applies to: shadow and continuous eval pipelines, canary validations, and longtail probe runs.
- Not covered here: complete annotation processes (see probe annotation charters) or privacy-preserving aggregation techniques (see privacy-first-shadow-eval).

Key concepts
- Slice: A targeted subset of traffic or synthetic probes defined by input predicates (e.g., "contains code block", "non-English answer request", "multi-turn > 5 steps").
- Signature: A short, human-readable descriptor + machine-friendly fingerprint that encodes the slice predicate, primary metric, baseline window, and guardrail tolerances.
- Explainability payload: Text describing the rationale and expected failure modes for the slice; used by triage playbooks and alerting.

Slice signature format (compact)
Each slice signature is a single-line descriptor and a 16-character fingerprint (SHA-1 truncated) emitted into telemetry. Example format:

  <short-id> | <primary-metric> | <baseline-window> | <tolerance> | <fingerprint>
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
code-block-clarity | ROUGE-L@avg | 14d | -5%/+8% | 3f1b8c7a2d9e5f1a

The explainability payload stored in eval metadata (long text) includes: human rationale, common false positives, recommended mitigating probes, and ownership.

Metric selection heuristics
1) Start with alignment to user-visible outcomes. Prefer metrics that map to product KPIs (e.g., exact match for code synthesis snippets, ROUGE-L for summarization fidelity, embedding cosine for retrieval relevance).
2) Match metric family to slice behavior. Use n-gram/overlap metrics for surface fidelity, token-level perplexity for fluency-related slices, and embedding distances for semantic drift checks.
3) Prefer robust statistics for noisy slices: median or trimmed-mean over arithmetic mean; report interquartile range (IQR) and 95% bootstrap CI.
4) Use delta-based thresholds anchored to a baseline window (14 days default). Always include both relative and absolute deltas in alerts.
5) Composite metrics: for complex slices combine primary metric + quality guardrail. Example: retrieval-safety = (embedding-sim >= 0.78) AND (toxicity-score <= 0.02).

Guardrail heuristics (when to alert)
- Primary rule: trigger triage when relative drop exceeds tolerance AND the change is statistically significant (95% CI does not cross baseline).
- Secondary rule: if absolute metric value crosses a safety floor/ceiling (e.g., toxicity > 0.05), trigger immediate pager routing.
- Noise filters: ignore changes explained by traffic composition shift >20% for core demographic slices unless accompanied by metric degradation within the subgroup.

Signature examples and table (text representation)
| short-id | predicate (human) | primary metric | baseline | tolerance | sample size min | owner |
| code-block-clarity | input contains fenced code blocks or triple backticks | ROUGE-L@avg | 14d | -5%/+8% | 2k probes | applied-ml-evals |
| short-chat-context | >3-turn multi-turn conversational prompts | CoherenceScore@median | 30d | -7%/+7% | 5k sessions | chat-eval-team |
| retrieval-qa-fact | user asks factoid with linked doc URL | EmbSim@mean | 14d | -4%/+6% | 1k probe-doc pairs | rtr-team |

How to construct a useful slice signature (step-by-step)
1) Define the user-visible failure you're trying to detect (1 sentence).
2) Pick the smallest predicate that isolates the behavior; prefer syntactic predicates (tokens, tags) over semantic heuristics when possible.
3) Select a primary metric per heuristics above and a secondary guardrail metric.
4) Decide on baseline window and minimum sample size for stable CI.
5) Draft the explainability payload (who, why, false positives, known mitigations).
6) Publish signature to eval registry and link to product/SLI docs.

Example explainability payload (text)
Rationale: "Fenced code block answers require higher token exactness; ROUGE-L correlates with executable snippet fidelity for our code-completion customers."
Common false positives: "Code formatting changes only (whitespace/clang-format) — mark as surface-only if UAST parsing indicates identical AST."
Mitigations: "Add AST-normalization probe, include canonicalization step in annotation pipeline."
Owner: "applied-ml-evals / Sofia Patel"

Telemetry instrumentation guide (what the runtime emits)
- tags to attach to probe/result events: slice.short_id, slice.fingerprint, metric.primary, metric.value, metric.lower_ci, metric.upper_ci, baseline_window, sample_count, quant_mode (int8/float16/none), cache_hit_rate.
- recommended sampling cadence: daily aggregates for high-volume slices, hourly for SLO-critical slices.
- retention: full probe traces for 30 days, aggregated slice history for 2 years.

Metric contract YAML example (human-readable)
```yaml
short_id: code-block-clarity
primary_metric: ROUGE-L@avg
baseline_window: 14d
tolerance: {relative_down: 0.05, relative_up: 0.08}
min_sample_size: 2000
alert_rules:
  - name: regression_triage_rule
    trigger: relative_drop_and_significant
    ci: 0.95
owner: applied-ml-evals
```

Automated triage runbook (high level)
1) Receive alert with slice.signature + delta + CI.
2) Check telemetry tags: quant_mode, cache_hit_rate, region, model_variant.
3) Run quick fingerprint diff: compare probe-input fingerprints (hash of normalized prompt) against baseline to detect distributional drift.
4) If distribution shift > 20% or sample_count below min, label as "data/coverage" and route to probe-stewards.
5) If quant_mode changed or quantized fallback active, follow quant-fallback triage (see quant-fallback-quality-sla).
6) If step 4/5 negative, escalate to model-oncall with prepared context bundle (signature, time window, examples, telemetry links).

Prepared context bundle (what the alert should include)
- slice.signature and fingerprint
- primary metric delta and CI
- 10 representative probe inputs and model outputs (with normalized hashes)
- quant_mode and cache_hit_rate snapshot
- link to recent shadow eval runs and relevant changelog entries

Rolling out new signatures and contracts
- Draft signature in eval staging and run 7-day shadow to collect baseline statistics.
- Verify sample sufficiency and stability (IQR < 12% for the primary metric).
- Move to production with "observability-only" for first 2 weeks (no pager).
- After stability, enable alerting with conservative tolerance; review after 30 days for tuning.

Ownership and governance
- authoring: applied-ml-evals team owns signature design and maintenance.
- approvals: signatures that affect customer-facing SLAs must be reviewed by product and SRE (add approvals in metadata).
- periodic review: every signature must have an annotated review every 180 days or when the model family changes.

Debugging examples (concise)
- Case A: ROUGE-L drop while embedding-sim stable -> likely surface wording/formatting regression. Action: run normalization probes.
- Case B: Embedding-sim drop and ROUGE-L drop -> semantic regression or retrieval upstream issue. Action: check index freshness and retrieval logs.
- Case C: Metric drop with high cache miss rate -> warmup/kv-cache regression. Action: reproduce with cold-start shadow runs.

Appendix: fingerprint generation
- Fingerprint is SHA1(normalized-predicate-string + primary_metric + baseline_window) truncated to 16 hex chars. Normalization rules: lowercase, remove extra whitespace, standardize token tags (e.g., [CODE] -> code), sort predicate clauses lexicographically.

Changelog
- 2026-01-10: Added telemetry tags and prepared context bundle section (Sofia).
- 2025-03-02: Initial production rollout guidance and baseline heuristics (Ajay Kumar).

References
- probe-telemetry-compression-scheduling-playbook-2026
- quant-fallback-quality-sla-and-rollout-spec-2026
- eval-cost-slice-prioritization-and-resource-budgeting-2026

Contact
- primary: applied-ml-evals (applied-ml@redwood.com)
- owner: Sofia Patel (sofia.patel@redwood.ai)

payload.page_title: Model launch evaluation gates (Hosted API catalog)

sections.body: This page defines the required evaluation gates for launching a new model into the Hosted API model catalog. The goal is to ensure we can safely serve the model, meet product quality expectations, and detect regressions after launch.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Gate owner (quality): Applied ML (Onboarding + Evals)
- Required signoff: Applied ML + Product (for model positioning)
- Optional signoff: Customer Success (if a launch is for a named account)
sections.heading: Ownership and signoff

sections.body: All Hosted API catalog launches must pass *all* suites below. Each suite must be run on the candidate model build (exact weights + tokenizer + runtime config) and logged in the eval harness.
sections.heading: Required evaluation suites

sections.body:
- Source: `prompt-sets/hosted-api/core-regression`
- Metrics: win-rate vs current default in family; structured output adherence for required schemas
- Pass criteria:
  - Overall win-rate >= 50% vs baseline (no regression)
  - Any critical prompt tagged `p0` must not regress
- Artifact: eval harness run link + summary paragraph
sections.heading: Suite A: Internal prompt set regression

sections.body:
- Source: curated public tasks (e.g., MMLU subset, GSM8K subset, HumanEval-lite)
- Purpose: catch obvious misconfigs, broken tokenizer, prompt formatting issues
- Pass criteria:
  - No single task drops > 5% absolute vs upstream reported numbers *after adjusting for our settings*
  - If upstream numbers are unavailable, compare vs adjacent model sizes in family and explain outliers
- Artifact: table of scores + notes
sections.heading: Suite B: Public benchmark sanity

sections.body:
- Source: policy prompts + refusal behavior checks
- Pass criteria:
  - No increase in disallowed content generation on policy set
  - Refusal templates must be compatible with Redwood policy layer
- Artifact: pass/fail summary + any required policy config notes
sections.heading: Suite C: Safety and policy screening (lightweight)

sections.body:
- Required when the model is marketed for tools/function calling
- Pass criteria:
  - JSON schema conformance >= 99% on tool-calling prompt set
- Artifact: schema validation report link
sections.heading: Suite D: Tool/function calling compatibility (if applicable)

sections.body:
1. Eval harness run URLs for all required suites
2. A one-paragraph risk assessment (what could go wrong in prod)
3. A recommended default inference config (temperature/top_p/max_tokens defaults)

payload.page_title: Latency-aware Probe Federation and Reconciliation

sections.body:
Summary
This document describes the Latency-aware Probe Federation and Reconciliation (LPFR) pattern: a systematic way to coordinate distributed probe generation and evaluation across heterogeneous evaluator fleets (shadow, canary, and production shadow meshes) while preserving latency SLOs and providing deterministic reconciliation and rollback criteria when probes detect regressions. LPFR is intended for multi-tier evaluations that exercise quantized variants, function-call behavior, long-context scenarios, and streaming/functioncall edge cases.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Provide a telemetry contract between probe producers, federated evaluators, and the reconciliation engine so latency-sensitive probes are prioritized without starving quality coverage.
  - Define deterministic reconciliation rules that map probe signal patterns to automated rollback, partial isolation, or investigator escalations.
  - Enable mixed-precision and quant-shadow probing with cost-aware throttling and latency hedges.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a replacement for long-running human annotation pipelines or adjudicated safety reviews.
  - LPFR does not define new annotation schemas; it assumes existing probe labels and slice taxonomy.

Definitions
- Probe: a single synthetic or replayed request generated to exercise a model/service path.
- Federation: the set of evaluator endpoints (shadow, quant-shadow, canary evaluators) which accept probes.
- Reconciliation engine: the service that ingests probe telemetry and decides promotion, rollback, or escalation.
- Latency SLO budget: the aggregate token/response latency threshold allocated to evaluation traffic for a given service or lane.

When to use LPFR
- Rolling out a quantized model variant where tail latency and failure-to-response increase risk.
- Canarying multi-turn functioncall models where downstream tool latency is variable.
- Coordinating cross-region shadowing where network egress and region cost constraints require dynamic probe routing.

Architecture overview
1) Probe Producer Layer
   - Responsible for probe sampling, priming, contextualization, and tagging with priorities.
   - Tags: slice_id, intent, expected_latency_bucket (fast|medium|slow), cost_tier, privacy_budget_flag.
2) Federation Router
   - Routes probes to evaluator backends based on routing policy (latency sensitivity, cost cap, model compatibility).
   - Maintains live budget accounting per lane.
3) Evaluator Backends
   - Shadow evaluators: full-fidelity but slower; used for deep-fidelity checks.
   - Fast evaluators: quant-shadow and trimmed-context evaluators that prioritize latency and approximate quality signals.
   - Canary evaluators: small production-traffic mirrors with strict SLOs.
4) Telemetry Ingest and Reconciliation
   - Collects probe-level telemetry (latency_ms P50/P95/P99, tokens_generated, response_coherence_score, functioncall_success, exception_type).
   - Applies reconciliation heuristics and publishes actions to Rollout Orchestrator.

Telemetry contract (required fields)
- probe_id: string
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601 string
- slice_id: string
- evaluator_id: string
- model_variant: string
- expected_latency_bucket: one of [fast, medium, slow]
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end response time)
- tokens_generated: integer
- coherence_score: float (0.0-1.0)
- functioncall_status: one of [noop, success, partial, failure]
- error_code: optional string (if failure)
- quant_flag: one of [float32, int8, int4, mixed]
- network_region: string
- telemetry_version: string

Contract semantics and sampling guidance
- Every probe must include expected_latency_bucket so the federation router can route to an evaluator that meets the bucket expectation.
- Sampling policy must ensure at least 5% of fast-bucket probes are processed by full-fidelity shadow evaluators weekly to detect silent fidelity regressions in fast-approx eval paths.
- Quant-shadow probes must be tagged with quant_flag. At least one quant-shadow probe per slice per model_variant is required on every promotion candidate.

Federation routing policy (pseudo)
1. If expected_latency_bucket == fast and lane_budget.fast > 0 then route to fast evaluator; else fallback to canary if available.
2. If quant_flag != float32 and quant_shadow_quota_available then route 80% to quant-shadow, 20% to full-fidelity shadow.
3. For privacy_budget_flag==true, only route to privacy-anchored evaluators.
4. Enforce per-model monthly cost cap; when reached, degrade sampling of low-priority slices first.

Reconciliation heuristics (decision matrix)
- Input signals considered: latency P99 increase, coherence_score delta, functioncall failure rate, cross-evaluator divergence.
- Example rule table (applies to a given model_variant and slice_id):
  - If P99 increases > 2x baseline AND coherence_score drops >= 0.08 -> Action: immediate partial rollback (traffic routed to previous variant) + create incident.
  - If functioncall_failure_rate > 5% for three consecutive 10-minute windows -> Action: canary isolate (stop canary traffic), escalate to SRE and ML engineer.
  - If quant-shadow divergence (fast eval vs full shadow) coherence delta > 0.12 for >100 probes -> Action: hold rollout and enqueue detailed triage runbook.
  - If only latency increases but coherence unchanged -> Action: add latency hedging (increase fast-queue capacity) and trigger slow-path performance run.

Automated rollback and staged interventions
- Rollback modes:
  - Full rollback: immediate revert to previous model variant across all lanes.
  - Partial rollback: reduce percentage of traffic to variant (e.g., 20% -> 0%) for affected slices only.
  - Canary isolate: stop canary traffic and preserve data for triage.
- Staged intervention steps (automated pipeline):
  1) Alert creation with reconciliation evidence bundle.
  2) Automated partial rollback to 10% for affected slice and throttle probe ingress.
  3) Trigger synthetic triage job (replay 2k probes in isolated sandbox with full-fidelity shadow).
  4) If triage confirms issue -> escalate (human) and full rollback; otherwise auto-increment canary after 60m observation window.

Runbook: on-probe-regression-detected (short form)
1) Triage owner confirmed by reconciliation engine (auto-assign to model oncall).
2) Snapshot: collect 1-hour probe telemetry, 30 example probes (redacted), evaluator logs, and quant artifact versions.
3) Reproduce: kick off isolated replay with 3 seeds and full-fidelity model.
4) Decide: rollback or continue with mitigation. Decision must include metric deltas and rationale.
5) Postmortem: create incident postmortem within 72 hours if rollback happened.

Operational thresholds and SLO influence
- Evaluation traffic may consume up to 5% of an endpoint's latency SLO budget by default. Teams must request exceptions for higher budgets.
- Recommended thresholds (starting defaults):
  - latency_p99_alert_multiplier: 2.0
  - coherence_delta_alert_threshold: 0.08
  - functioncall_failure_rate_alert: 0.05
  - quant_divergence_alert: 0.12

Metrics to expose in dashboards
- probe_ingest_rate (per-slice)
- evaluator_latency_p50/p95/p99 (by evaluator_id)
- coherence_score_histogram (by model_variant)
- cross_evaluator_divergence_rate (fraction of probes with delta > 0.1)
- automated_action_count (rollbacks, partial rollbacks, isolates)

Example telemetry JSON (single probe)
{
  \"probe_id\": \"probe-20260302-8ac9\",
  \"timestamp_utc\": \"2026-03-02T18:22:40Z\",
  \"slice_id\": \"billing-invoice-format\",
  \"evaluator_id\": \"fast-eval-us-west-2-3\",
  \"model_variant\": \"rwdl-v2-quant-int8\",
  \"expected_latency_bucket\": \"fast\",
  \"latency_ms\": 210,
  \"tokens_generated\": 42,
  \"coherence_score\": 0.74,
  \"functioncall_status\": \"success\",
  \"error_code\": \"\",
  \"quant_flag\": \"int8\",
  \"network_region\": \"us-west-2\",
  \"telemetry_version\": \"1.2\"
}

Safety and privacy considerations
- Redaction: probes that contain PII must be redacted at production ingress and flagged with privacy_budget_flag. Redacted probes should still carry enough context for slice attribution.
- Sampling bias: ensure low-volume slices maintain a minimum weekly sample floor (n>=50) to avoid silent regressions.
- Cost control: reconciliation engine will enforce monthly cost caps and gracefully degrade low-priority probe sampling when thresholds approached.

Testing and rollout plan for LPFR
1) Internal smoke: wire probe producer to a synthetic evaluator and validate telemetry contract for 72 hours.
2) Canary: run LPFR on a single non-critical service (internal docs summarization) for 2 weeks.
3) Mixed-workload stress: run 10k probes across fast/medium/slow buckets with quant-shadow enabled to measure divergence false-positive rate.
4) Gradual adoption: expose LPFR as an opt-in flag in the evaluator mesh config, require model teams to opt-in and certify quant probes before using.

Open questions and future work
- Should we expose an intelligible explanation for reconciliation decisions (human readable reasoning tree)?
- How to standardize cross-team coherence_score computation to avoid calibration drift between services?
- Explore adaptive sampling where fast-bucket probes are occasionally escalated to full-fidelity shadow based on model drift detectors.

Ownership and contacts
- LPFR ownership: Applied ML Evaluation team (applied-ml-and-evals).
- Primary contacts: Maya Chen (author), Diego Morales (evaluation infra), Aisha Patel (SLO and metrics).

Appendix: migration checklist (for model teams)
- Add expected_latency_bucket and quant_flag to probe producer payloads.
- Update probe registry with slice_id and privacy_budget_flag mapping.
- Run the LPFR smoke test and obtain signoff from evaluation infra.
- Schedule a 2-week canary with monitoring on the LPFR dashboards.

Document change log
- 2026-01-11: Draft created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-02-10: Added reconciliation rules and example telemetry. Reviewer feedback from Diego and Aisha incorporated.
- 2026-03-02: Published: clarified sampling guidance and thresholds.

payload.page_title: Token-Economy Evaluation and Benchmarking Playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a company-standard process for evaluating model behavior in the context of token accounting, per-token latency cost, and downstream economic impact (the `token economy`). It explains measurement primitives, benchmark designs, integration points with the EvalRunner harness, and regression triage steps when token-related regressions are detected. The goal is to make token cost and behavior first-class signals in model promotion and runtime configuration decisions.

Why this matters:
- Per-token cost is a major driver of customer unit economics and product UX.
- Small changes in generation behavior (longer prefixes, repeated tokens, verbose completions) compound across large volumes.
- Quantization and runtime batching can change tokenization/decoding performance unpredictably; we need standardized measurement and triage.

Scope:
- Applies to all text-generation and chat-oriented model evaluations for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Includes metrics for: token throughput (tokens/sec), tokens-per-request distribution, token-cost-per-request (USD), token-variance across prompt slices, and token-induced latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99).
- Not in scope: embedding-only workloads (see separate embedding-cost playbook).

Key Concepts and Definitions:
- billable_tokens: tokens counted by our billing pipeline for a single request (string).
- decode_tokens: number of tokens emitted by the model (includes stop tokens).
- prefix_tokens: tokens contributed by prompt+context.
- average_tokens_per_session (ATPS): mean total tokens per user session for a workload slice.
- token_economy_index (TEI): composite score used to rank model variants by cost-quality tradeoff. TEI = (normalized_cost * alpha) + (quality_penalty * beta) where alpha/beta are configurable.

Measurement Primitives (what to collect):
1) Request-level counters (from EvalRunner / ShadowRunner):
   - billable_tokens (integer)
   - prefix_tokens (integer)
   - decode_tokens (integer)
   - request_start_ts, request_end_ts (ISO 8601)
   - model_variant and quant_profile labels

2) Sampling strategy: stratified by workload slice, language, prompt length buckets, and user intent (inferred when available). Minimum sample sizes are in the "Sampling Table" below.

Sampling Table (minimum samples per slice):
| Slice size | Min samples | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|
| High-volume (>=10k/day) | 5,000 | prioritize P95/P99 stability |
| Mid-volume (1k-10k/day) | 2,000 | include overnight/peak |
| Low-volume (<1k/day) | 500 | aggregate across days |

Benchmark Design Patterns:
- Baseline run: run the candidate model and the promoted baseline side-by-side using identical randomized seeds and prompt batches. Collect billable_tokens and latency distributions.
- Prefix-sensitivity bench: artificially extend prefixes with repeated context to test KV-cache performance and token growth.
- Verbosity probe set: a targeted prompt set that elicits low/medium/high verbosity responses to measure decode_token inflation under temperature/top-p variations.
- Failure-mode stressbench: generate adversarial prompts that lead to repetition loops or runaway decoding to ensure guardrails trigger at configured token caps.

TEI Calculation and Thresholds:
- Calculate normalized_cost = (avg_billable_tokens * per_token_price_usd) normalized to [0,1] across candidates.
- quality_penalty: measured as 1 - quality_score (from downstream evals) where quality_score in [0,1].
- Default weights: alpha=0.6, beta=0.4. Adjust for latency-sensitive products (alpha -> 0.7) or quality-sensitive (beta -> 0.6).
- Promotion requirement: TEI(candidate) <= TEI(baseline) - 0.03 OR quality_score(candidate) >= quality_score(baseline) + 0.02.

Integration with EvalRunner (practical steps):
1) New benchmark definition YAML (example snippet):

--
name: token-economy-baseline-2026
workload: product-chat-simulator
samples: 5000
seed: 42
slices:
  - name: short-query
    prompt_length_max: 64
    weight: 0.5
  - name: long-context
    prompt_length_min: 200
    weight: 0.3
  - name: adversarial-repetition
    weight: 0.2
models:
  - candidate: redwood-open-2.1
  - baseline: redwood-stable-1.8
quant_profiles: [fp16, int8-default]
--

2) Hook the run to metric exporters: push per-request counters to the eval-metrics Kafka topic and ensure aggregators compute TEI daily.
3) Dashboarding: standard Grafana panel template: Token throughput, tokens per request histogram, TEI trend, and cost delta vs baseline. Template ID: ER-TOKEN-001.

Quality Guardrails and Automated Alerts:
- Hard token cap: if any request exceeds 2x expected billable_tokens for its slice, flag as token-anomaly.
- Auto-fallback: models in production must have fallback policy to lower verbosity or shorter model variant on >0.1% token-anomaly rate over 1 hour.
- Alert thresholds (first-line):
  - token_anomaly_rate > 0.1% -> paging to oncall (P3)
  - avg_billable_tokens increase > 8% vs 7-day baseline -> notify cost-ops Slack channel
  - decode_tokens P99 increase > 15% -> create auto-ticket for Applied ML team

Quantization and Runtime Considerations:
- When evaluating quant_profiles, record both billable_tokens and observed latency delta. Some quantization paths may change tokenization due to mixed-precision decoding heuristics; include tokenizer-DIFF tests to detect any unintended token boundary shifts.
- Run the quant_profile through the "KV-cache hit-rate probe": measure cache hit-rate across synthetic session sequences. A drop >5 percentage points should block promotion.

Regression Triage Playbook (token regressions):
1) Detect: alert livedetected by metric pipeline (token_anomaly_rate or TEI delta).
2) Reproduce locally: use the failing slice seed and EvalRunner to replay top 200 anomalous requests against baseline and candidate.
3) Binary isolation: switch out one axis at a time (decoder impl, tokenizer version, quant_profile, sampling params) to localize cause.
4) Blame candidate or runtime: run targeted A/B shadow runs to determine if the behavior is model-intrinsic or introduced by runtime (batcher/quant).
5) If model-intrinsic: open a model-regression issue and attach seeds, prompt examples, and per-request token traces (prefix, decode tokens).
6) If runtime-intrinsic: create an infra ticket and include kernel logs, quant config, and GPU distribution topology.
7) Rollback criteria: if TEI delta > 0.05 with adverse quality delta or token_anomaly_rate > 0.3% sustained for >30 minutes, perform rollback to previous promoted variant.

Operator Playbook (oncall steps):
1) Acknowledge alert in Ops channel and run the quick-repro script: evalctl replay --slice <name> --top 200 --variant candidate
2) Check Grafana panels (ER-TOKEN-001) for correlated CPU/GPU spikes and queue latency.
3) If auto-fallback did not trigger, manually toggle fallback route to lower-verbosity variant and monitor TEI.
4) Notify Applied ML and Runtime teams and create incident page with initial findings.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Applied ML: primary owner for benchmark definitions, TEI weights, and quality scoring (sla: 2 business days for Triage ack).
- Runtime / Serving: primary owner for quant_profile validation and KV-cache behavior (sla: 8 business hours for critical infra tickets).
- Cost-Ops: owner for cost-related dashboards and billing integration (sla: 3 business days for cost anomalies).

Appendix A — Example artifact (JSON metric sample):
{
  "request_id": "req_20260215_0001",
  "model_variant": "redwood-open-2.1",
  "prefix_tokens": 42,
  "decode_tokens": 128,
  "billable_tokens": 170,
  "start_ts": "2026-02-15T14:01:02Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-02-15T14:01:02.200Z"
}

Appendix B — Common troubleshooting checklist:
- Verify tokenizer versions match between baseline and candidate.
- Replay seeds deterministically (seed + RNG path).
- Check sampling param drift (temperature/top-p) in request logs.
- Inspect KV-cache hit counters for session workloads.
- Run tiny-batch vs large-batch runs to observe batching amplification effects.

How to use this playbook:
- When creating a new model promotion PR, include a Token-Economy section with TEI numbers, sampling slices, and any discovered token anomalies.
- For runtime changes (quant or batching), run the token-economy baseline and verify no TEI regressions before deployment to canary.

Contacts:
- Applied ML oncall: #applied-ml-oncall (Slack)
- Runtime SRE: #runtime-sre (Slack)
- Cost Ops owner: cost-ops@redwood.ai

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12: Created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2026-02-20: Reviewed and published; clarified TEI thresholds and rollback criteria.

payload.page_title: Anchor + Primer Compact Benchmark and Production Probe Suite

sections.body:
Overview

This page describes the Anchor + Primer Compact Benchmark (APCB): a small, production-focused probe suite designed to measure and track priming/anchoring robustness across model variants, quantization profiles, and KV-cache behaviors. APCB is intended as a low-cost continuous probe that can run in shadow and canary lanes of the eval harness to catch early regressions in few-shot priming fidelity and primer decay across contexts.

Purpose and goals

- Provide a repeatable, small-footprint benchmark (50–200 probes) suitable for continuous runs.
- Measure anchor retention (how long a primer continues to influence outputs) and primer-channel isolation (whether the primer leaks into unrelated generations).
- Surface interactions between priming, quantization, and KV-cache reuse that could cause semantic drift or hallucination.
- Produce actionable signals with clear triage steps and remediation recommendations.

Scope

- Applied to text-only and single-turn few-shot prompts (1–5 examples). Not a multimodal benchmark.
- Runs against: hosted model variants, dedicated instances (representative instance types), and quantized shadow artifacts.
- Intended for both offline eval harness scheduling and lightweight in-production shadow sampling.

Design principles

1. Compact: keep the probe set small (~100 probes) while covering key failure modes.
2. Anchored: each probe explicitly includes an anchor section (highly directive text) and a neutral test segment to check anchor spill.
3. Diversity: include multiple prompt styles (instruction, QA, roleplay, function-call templates).
4. Deterministic scoring when possible: use token-level and semantic similarity metrics plus human-calibrated thresholds.

Probe taxonomy

- Anchor-retention probes: measure how many tokens/turns the primer continues to influence when context length increases.
- Anchor-leak probes: detect primer words or intent appearing in unrelated outputs.
- Function-call anchoring probes: check parameter name/value adherence after priming.
- Stochasticity probes: measure variance across seeds and streaming starts.

Probe synthesis and dataset

1. Seed corpus: 250 canonical seeds derived from real workloads (support, search snippets, chat intents). Seeds are anonymized and stripped of PII.
2. Primer types: directive ("Always answer in bullet points"), persona ("You are a helpful historian"), safety ("Do not provide legal advice"), and structural (function call scaffolding).
3. For each seed, generate 3–4 probe variants combining primer type and prompt style.

Sampling rules

- Shuffle probes per run and cap to N=100 per continuous run.
- Include deterministic random seed for reproducibility in the eval harness.
- Run both cold-start (no KV cache) and warm-start (KV cache primed with a short history) variants.

Metrics and scoring
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Anchor Retention Index (ARI): fraction of probes where the primary anchored instruction persists at specified context offsets (0, +50, +200 tokens). Values 0.0–1.0.
- Anchor Leakage Rate (ALR): percent of probes where anchor tokens or anchor intent appear in a mismatched output segment.
- Function-call Fidelity (FCF): percent of function-call probes that return the correct parameter structure and canonical values.
- Seed Variance (SV): standard deviation of ARI across 5 seeds (captures stochastic instability).
sections.heading: Primary metrics (numeric)

sections.body:
- Token overlap counts between anchor and output.
- Edit distance to expected canonical answer.
- Embedding cosine similarity to anchored answer (for semantic retention).

Acceptance thresholds (example table)

| Metric | Acceptable | Warning | Fail |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ARI (0 token offset) | >= 0.92 | 0.80–0.91 | < 0.80 |
| ARI (+200 tokens) | >= 0.78 | 0.65–0.77 | < 0.65 |
| ALR | <= 0.04 | 0.05–0.10 | > 0.10 |
| FCF | >= 0.95 | 0.85–0.94 | < 0.85 |
| SV | <= 0.03 | 0.03–0.08 | > 0.08 |

Note: thresholds should be tuned per-model family and per-quantization profile. Use this table as a starting guardrail rather than absolutes.

Integration with eval harness and CI

- Harness job: a lightweight job runner named apcb-compact-runner. It supports parallelism=8 and artifacts exported as JSON L2 summaries.
- Schedule: run every 4 hours in shadow for high-traffic models; nightly for low-traffic.
- CI gate: failing the Fail thresholds for two consecutive runs triggers a blocking ticket and auto-notification to model-onboarding and serving-runtime on-call.

CLI example (eval harness adapter)
sections.heading: Auxiliary signals (diagnostic)

sections.body: apcb-runner --model redwood-gptx-1b-qa --profiles cold,warm --seed 42 --limit 100 --output s3://apcb/artifacts/${RUN_ID}.json
sections.heading: Run APCB against a model variant

sections.body:
job_name: apcb-compact-nightly
schedule: nightly
parallelism: 8
profile: [cold, warm]
seeds: 42,43,44
limit: 100
notify_on: [warning, fail]
sections.heading: Sample eval job YAML (for harness scheduler)

sections.body:
- run_id
- model_variant
- profile
- probe_id
- metrics: {ari, alr, fcf, sv}
- raw_output_text
- tokens_for_anchor

(Artifacts must remain JSON lines compliant for downstream triage tools.)

Triage flow and remediation playbook

1. Automated triage: the harness computes delta against baseline (previous stable variant).
2. If Fail thresholds hit: open regression ticket with tags [apcb, regression, model:<variant>]. Attach full run artifact and delta summary.
3. Quick manual checks (Owner: model-onboarding):
   - Re-run failing probes with 5 different seeds and both cold/warm profiles.
   - Compare against unquantized reference to isolate quantization impact.
   - Inspect tokenization differences (special tokens, subword splits).
4. Escalation matrix:
   - If isolated to quant profile -> engage quant team and apply rollback to previous quant profile.
   - If isolated to KV cache behavior -> route to serving-runtime with run_id and capture trace.
   - If model variant-regression across all profiles -> open rollback and coordinate release blocking.

Remediation suggestions (common fixes)

- Primer rewrite / anchoring strengthening: add explicit delimiting tokens or anchor markers to primers.
- Quant fallback: temporarily route production traffic to unquantized or higher-precision variant for affected route.
- KV-cache priming hygiene: truncate reused context and inject anchor sentinel tokens at start of primed sections.
- Function-call schema tightening: enforce strict schema validators and add replayed function-call unit tests to the evaluator.

Ownership and runbook contact list

- Maintainer (apcb steward): Sofia Martinez (applied-ml) — apcb-maintain@redwood.ai
- Model-onboarding lead: Arjun Patel — model-onboarding@redwood.ai
- Quant team pager: #quant-ops (Slack) and quant-oncall@redwood.ai
- Serving-runtime oncall: via SRE rota (see /eng-serving-runtime/runbooks)

Versioning and baseline management

- Baselines: keep a baseline per major model family (e.g., gptx-1, gptx-2) and per quantization profile. Baselines are immutable and stored in the artifact registry with tags baseline/YYYYMMDD.
- Baseline promotion: after a canary passes APCB for 72 hours with no Fail alerts, promotion is recorded with a baseline tag and release notes.

Privacy and dataset handling

- All probe seeds are scrubbed for PII and customer-sensitive terms before inclusion.
- Long-term retention: raw outputs retained for 90 days, aggregated metrics retained for 3 years.

Appendix: sample primer and probe examples

1) Directive anchor (anchor-retention probe)
sections.heading: Artifact schema (short)

sections.body:
"You MUST answer in numbered steps, and do not include any examples."
Seed test: "Explain how to rotate an API key."
Expected: numbered-step answer and no example blocks.

2) Function-call anchor
sections.heading: Primer

sections.body:
"When answering, return a JSON object matching the schema: {\"action\":string, \"params\":{}}"
Seed test: "Create a function call to schedule an email to user@example.com next Tuesday."
Expected: JSON with action=\"schedule_email\" and params.email present.

3) Anchor-leak probe
sections.heading: Primer

sections.body:
"You are a customer service agent for Acme Roofing. Avoid mentioning Acme if unrelated."
Seed test: "Summarize the difference between asphalt and metal shingles."
Pass condition: no mention of Acme in unrelated context.

Appendix: recommended dashboard widgets

- ARI time-series (0/50/200 token offsets) with model/quantization profile breakdown.
- ALR heatmap by probe type and model family.
- Daily FCF pass rate with quick links to failing probes.

Notes and next steps

- We recommend running APCB as part of any quantization rollout and as a steady-state shadow job for high-volume models.
- Roadmap items: expand to multimodal primers, integrate differential privacy noise-aware variants, and add automated primer-rewrite suggestions into the remediation pipeline.

Document change log

- 2026-11-15: Initial draft (S. Martinez).
- 2026-12-20: Added CI gating and artifact schema (Arjun Patel review).
- 2027-02-03: Tuned thresholds and added KV-cache warm-start profile (Maya Chen review).

payload.page_title: Shadow Sequencer and Fallback Orchestration Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-----
This playbook documents the Shadow Sequencer pattern and fallback orchestration used by the eval harness to safely validate new model variants (including quantized and trimmed kernels) across live workloads. It prescribes sequencing rules, sampling policies, telemetry contracts, and incident-runbook steps to keep production SLOs intact while maximizing signal for model onboarding and regression triage.

Audience
--------
- Applied ML engineers running model onboarding and continuous evals
- Serving runtime engineers integrating shadow pipelines
- SRE and platform teams responsible for routing and fallbacks

Goals
-----
1. Collect high-fidelity shadowed request/response pairs for evaluation without impacting user-perceived latency or correctness.
2. Provide deterministic sequencing and prioritization so limited eval capacity focuses on the most informative traffic slices.
3. Automate safe fallback to production variants on degradation (quality or latency).
4. Integrate with quantization and KV-cache-aware on-device evaluation flows.

Terminology
-----------
- Shadow request: a copy of a production request routed to an eval model for offline scoring and telemetry.
- Sequencer: the service that decides which production requests to shadow and at what priority. (service: eval-sequencer)
- Shadow bus: asynchronous pipeline that delivers shadow traffic to eval environments with metadata. (service: shadow-bus)
- Fallback policy: policy that triggers automatic rollback or traffic diversion when a health gate fails.

Architecture overview
---------------------
1. Production ingress -> routing layer (redwood-router).
2. redwood-router emits a sampling key and forwards the request to production model variant.
3. eval-sequencer subscribes to routing metadata and decides shadow eligibility using the Sequencing Policy DB (see configs).
4. Eligible requests are serialized and posted to shadow-bus (Kafka topic: shadows.v1) with encryption and a metadata envelope.
5. Shadow consumers (dedicated eval-pools, private shadow runners) pull and run model variants; results written to eval-store and linked back to the originating request id for later comparison.

Sequencing policy (high level)
-----------------------------
- Priority classes (in descending order):
  - P0: production slow-paths and SLA-critical endpoints (sample rate: 0.1% default)
  - P1: high-business-value cohorts (paid customers, sample rate: 1%)
  - P2: high-entropy prompts (identified by probe classifier, sample rate: 5%)
  - P3: heavy compute or long-context examples (sample rate: 0.5%)
- Global budget: max 3% of total QPS can be shadowed into any single eval-cluster to avoid resource interference.
- Adaptive throttle: sample rates are dynamically lowered if the eval-cluster CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for 5m window.

Sequencing config table (editable YAML snippet)
------------------------------------------------
| key | meaning | recommended value |
|-----|---------|-------------------|
| sequencer.default_rate | baseline sampling | 0.01 |
| sequencer.priority_p1_rate | paid customers | 0.01 |
| sequencer.max_cluster_shadow_pct | cap per cluster | 0.03 |
| sequencer.cpu_util_throttle_pct | throttling threshold | 0.75 |

(Example YAML for a sequence rule)
```yaml
- id: p1_paid_customers
  match: request.customer_tier == \"paid\"
  sample_rate: 0.01
  priority: P1
  destinations: [\"eval-dedicated-a\", \"eval-private-vpc\"]
```

Security and privacy controls
-----------------------------
- All shadow payloads are hashed at ingress and PII fields redacted according to the redaction ruleset (service: pii-filter).
- Shadow bus messages are encrypted with customer-scoped keys; private deployment shadows can be configured to never persist in central eval-store.
- For regulated customers, use DP-mode: add Laplace noise to numeric telemetry and strip verbatim user content before storage.

Telemetry and SLOs
------------------
- Critical SLOs that must not be violated by shadowing:
  - P99 production latency change: <= +1.5ms attributable to shadowing hooks.
  - Error budget: shadow subsystem must not cause >0.1% increase in 5xx rate.
- Observability outputs:
  - metric: eval.shadowed_requests_count (tags: priority, destination, model_variant)
  - metric: eval.shadow_processing_lag_seconds (95th)
  - log: shadow-envelope-{request_id} includes: request_id, sampling_key, model_variant, seq_rule, cluster_id

Quality gates and automated fallback triggers
-------------------------------------------
We evaluate shadow-run results weekly and in near real-time for the following gates. Any failure above thresholds triggers one of the fallback actions below.

Quality gates (examples)
- Token-level degradation: LM_delta_bleu > 0.12 vs baseline for customer-critical prompts
- Latency regressions: 95th percentile increase > 15% for the model variant under test
- Regression alerts per 10k shadowed requests > 3

Fallback actions (ranked)
1. Circuit-breaker: stop all new shadowing for the failing variant for 30 minutes.
2. Auto-rollforward: if degradation persists and a compatible fallback exists (quantized->float or small->large), route canary traffic to fallback variant with gradual ramping.
3. Live rollback: for Dedicated or Private deployments with observed customer impact, automatically switch traffic away from the failing variant at the routing layer and create incident.

Operational runbook (incident scenario: spike in token degradation)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Triage: PagerDuty -> oncall-eng (eval). Confirm spike via grafana: eval.quality.regression_rate (5m).
2. Identify sequencer keys correlated with regressions via:
   - CLI: rcli seq-query --from 2026-03-02T09:00Z --to 2026-03-02T09:30Z --filter=regression=1
3. Stop shadowing for the implicated variant:
   - curl -XPOST https://eval-sequencer/api/v1/rules/disable -d '{"rule_id":"<id>"}'
4. If spike persists > 30m, enable fallback route to previous stable variant:
   - rcli routes update --route-id prod-chat --fallback-variant redwood-gpt-3b-stable --weight 100
5. Postmortem: capture root-cause, model diff, and submit to regression-triage workspace.

Integration checklist for model onboarding
----------------------------------------
- Ensure the model is registered in model-catalog with the following metadata: variant_id, quant_profile, kv_cache_compatibility, expected_latency_ms.
- Attach an eval-suite that includes: production prompt slices, adversarial probes, and a small human-labeled gold set for P1 customers.
- Verify shadow-run: run 1k synthetic shadow requests using the shadow-runner utility:
  - shadow-runner --variant <id> --sample-size 1000 --emulate-headers
- Confirm telemetry: eval.shadowed_requests_count > 1000 and eval.quality.sentinal_pass == true

Operational tips (best practices)
--------------------------------
- Prefer deterministic hashing for stable slice selection to enable reproducible comparisons.
- Use higher sampling for rare high-value slices (e.g., B2B integrations) and lower sampling for generic low-value traffic.
- For quantized variants, annotate messages with quant_profile to enable downstream analysts to compare like-for-like.

Example CLI snippets
--------------------
- Create a new sequencing rule:
  rcli sequencer create --name p2_high_entropy --match-file p2_match.json --sample-rate 0.05 --destinations eval-dedicated-a
- Disable shadowing for a variant immediately:
  rcli shadow disable --variant-id ql-6b-quant-v2

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Owner: Maya Patel (Applied ML)
- Runtime integration: Jin Park (serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Aisha Khan
- Oncall escalation: eval-oncall@redwood.com

Related pages
-------------
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/shadow-bus-maintenance

Appendix: example shadow-envelope format
--------------------------------------
{
  \"request_id\": \"uuid-v4\",
  \"sampling_key\": \"seq-2026-0001\",
  \"seq_rule\": \"p1_paid_customers\",
  \"metadata\": {
    \"model_variant\": \"redwood-gpt-3b-quant-v2\",
    \"customer_tier\": \"paid\"
  },
  \"payload\": \"<redacted-or-encrypted-bytes>\"
}

Change log
----------
- 2026-01-12: created initial playbook (M. Patel)
- 2026-03-02: added adaptive throttle rules and DP-mode guidance (M. Patel)

payload.page_title: Zero-Trust Networking and Observability Playbook for Private Deploys

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook describes a hardened, repeatable pattern for private Redwood Inference deployments that combines zero-trust network controls, telemetry-first observability, and an explicit canary-based upgrade & rollback procedure. It is intended for VPC-based and on-premises private deployments (customer-managed control plane or hybrid), and covers preflight checks, network policy templates, metrics/tracing requirements, alert thresholds, canary rollout choreography, and post-rollback remediation steps.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: Private deployments (VPC, connected colos, and on-prem clusters) running Redwood control plane + serving runtime.
- Not covered: hosted API multi-tenant deployments, experimental developer sandboxes.
- Audience: SRE/Platform, Private Deployments engineering, Customer Success (handoff), and Security reviewers.

Goals:
- Enforce least-privilege communication between services (zero-trust) while preserving performance for inference workloads.
- Provide deterministic observability (metrics, traces, logs) for rollout decisions and postmortem analysis.
- Standardize canary upgrade / rollback steps to limit blast radius and enable fast recovery.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Network controls and policy templates: eng-private-deployments team (Primary: Anna Kim).
- Observability and alerts: eng-platform (Primary: Thomas Keller).
- Canary orchestration & runbook authoring: eng-serving-runtime (Primary: Sanjeev Patel).
- SLO target during rollouts: 99.9% availability for control-plane RPCs, p50 token latency degradation < 20% versus baseline.

Prerequisites (pre-flight checklist):
1) Inventory and baseline:
   - List of cluster endpoints, subnets, and NAT gateways.
   - Baseline latency and token-per-second (TPS) metrics for each model route captured for 72 hours.
   - KMS/HSM access validated, customer KMS key ARN present for encryption-at-rest.
2) IAM & identities:
   - Service identities created and mapped to least-privilege roles.
   - TLS certificates issued and rotated frequently (<= 90 days) for internal mTLS.
3) Observability hooks installed:
   - Prometheus scraping targets, OTLP traces ingestion, and centralized log forwarder (ELK/EFK or Splunk) confirmed.
4) Canary capacity reserved:
   - At least 10% of capacity reserved for canary traffic or isolated node pool with identical instance types.

Zero-Trust Network Pattern (high level):
- Enforce mTLS between all Redwood services and sidecars (control-plane, router, runtime executor).
- Explicit allowlists (not blacklists): only defined service-to-service flows are permitted.
- Short-lived credentials: use ephemeral tokens via Vault or cloud-native STS where supported.

Network policy template (Kubernetes NetworkPolicy example):
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-controlplane-to-runtime
  namespace: redwood-runtime
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: runtime-executor
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          redwood-role: control-plane
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 7070

Notes:
- Apply equivalent rules for egress restrictions where host-level packet filters are required on-prem. Avoid overly broad CIDR ranges (prefer security-group-per-service pattern).

Service Mesh and Proxy considerations:
- Use sidecar proxies (Envoy) only if the latency budget allows; for extremely latency-sensitive model inference, prefer lightweight mTLS without full mesh features.
- If deploying service mesh, enable observability filters (access logs, upstream clusters) and limit retries on inference paths to 0 or 1 to avoid duplicate token costs.

Observability requirements (must-have signals):
- Metrics (Prometheus):
  - request_count{route,model,variant,status_code}
  - token_generation_rate{route,model}
  - p50/p95/p99 latency per route (generation and total end-to-end)
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio and batch_size_distribution
  - GPU_utilization, GPU_memory_free, host_cpu_usage
- Traces (OTel):
  - End-to-end trace spanning API gateway -> control plane -> runtime executor with span attributes: model_id, request_id, token_count, hardware_type
  - Sampling: 100% for errors, 1-5% for success requests (adjust for cost)
- Logs:
  - Structured logs with request_id correlation and log-level mapping (info/warn/error). Include deterministic fields for repro (model_checksum, config_hash).

Dashboard & alerting baseline:
- Canary dashboard tiles:
  - Canary_p50_latency_vs_baseline, Canary_error_rate, Canary_token_cost_delta, Canary_throughput
- Critical alerts (examples):
  - Alert: control_plane_rpc_error_rate > 1% for 5m -> Severity: P1 -> Notify oncall + escalation to eng-serving-runtime.
  - Alert: canary_p95_latency > baseline_p95 * 1.5 for 10m -> Severity: P1 -> Pause rollout and trigger rollback.
  - Alert: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m -> Severity: P2 -> Investigate cache warmup or slot misconfiguration.

Prometheus alert rule example (YAML snippet):
- alert: CanaryHighLatency
  expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime", env="canary"}[5m])) by (le))) > (scalar(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime", env="baseline"}[5m])) by (le))) * 1.5)
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Canary p95 latency > 1.5x baseline"

Canary upgrade choreography (recommended pattern):
1) Prepare canary image/config in isolated node pool.
2) Run smoke tests against canary control-plane endpoints (liveness, model list, key retrieval) — pass must be 100%.
3) Inject synthetic traffic at low TPS (1-2% of normal) with real prompt shapes and measure: latency, error rate, token cost delta, model output quality (if available).
4) If metrics within thresholds for 30 minutes proceed to 10% production traffic for 60 minutes.
5) Run evaluation harness on a reserved prompt set (sliced by top routes) to detect quality regressions.
6) If still green, ramp to 50% for 30 minutes, then full rollout with automated tapering of the canary node pool.

Rollout thresholds (fail-fast):
- Error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute over baseline for 10m.
- p95 latency regression > 30% for 10m.
- Token cost increase > 10% sustained for 15m without quality improvement evidence.
- Eval harness quality drop (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) beyond threshold defined in product route policy.

Rollback procedure (step-by-step):
1) Pause traffic routing system (gateway/mesh) to stop further canary traffic shifts.
2) Re-target affected routes to the previous stable revision. If rollout used node pools, cordon/drain canary pool and uncordon stable pool.
3) Confirm traffic has migrated back and monitor the primary SLOs for 15 minutes.
4) Capture forensic artifacts: call traces, last 100 error logs, sample prompts (sanitized), and config diffs.
5) Open a post-rollback incident with required owners and begin RCA within 24 hours.

Day-2 operational playbook snippets:
- Scaling up for load spikes:
  - Step 1: Observe GPU_utilization > 80% sustained for 10m and backlog growing -> trigger scale policy to add N nodes (N based on model mix).
  - Step 2: Monitor per-node queue latency; if latency improves, increase autoscaler cooldown to 3m.
- Key rotation for private KMS:
  - Precondition: rotation window approved by customer.
  - Steps: rotate KMS key in test environment -> validate decrypt/encrypt operations for runtime -> schedule rotation in maintenance window (low traffic) -> rotate in prod with canary decryption test.
- Telemetry disruption mitigation:
  - If OTLP ingestion fails, fall back to local disk buffer (configurable) and alert SRE. Ensure retention window for buffered telemetry is at least 24 hours.

Hardware and minimal network requirements (table):
- CPU per runtime node: 32 vCPU
- RAM per runtime node: 256 GiB
- GPU: A100 or H100 family recommended (customer can supply equivalent), GPU interconnect: NVLink recommended for multi-GPU models
- Network: 25 Gbps NIC minimum per node for inference clusters
- Storage: 2 TB NVMe local for model shards and KV cache (redundant replication recommended)

(As flat JSON this table is represented as lines)

Acceptance and handoff checklist for Customer Success:
- Signed operational contract specifying SLAs and support windows.
- Customer-run preflight report attached showing baseline TPS, latency, and model usage matrix.
- Mutually agreed escalation path and oncall rotation with contact information.

Examples and troubleshooting tips:
- Symptom: rising token cost with no latency change -> check batch size distribution and batching configuration; a sudden drop in batch size often increases per-token overhead.
- Symptom: intermittent RPC timeouts during rollout -> verify network-policy egress rules and sidecar connection timeouts; consider increasing TCP keepalive and reducing proxy connection pooling limits.

Post-incident RCA requirements (if rollback triggered):
- Timeline of events with 1-minute granularity for the window +/- 30 minutes around rollback.
- Top 10 error traces and a sample of 50 requests (sanitized) demonstrating regression.
- Config diff between baseline and canary, and clear action items to remediate.

References and related artifacts:
- Deployment templates: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026
- Canary traffic generator (internal tool): repo: infra/canary-generator (see README for usage and synthetic prompt sets)

FAQ (short):
Q: "Can I run full service mesh and still meet <50ms p50 latency for small models?"
A: You may, but validate with a synthetic baseline; full mesh introduces CPU/latency overhead — for sub-50ms SLAs prefer lightweight mTLS.

Q: "What level of telemetry sampling do we recommend for cost-sensitive customers?"
A: Sample 100% of errors, 3% of successes, increase to 10% on canaries.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets
- Check canary status (kubectl):
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l env=canary -o wide
- Force rollback to revision v1.2.3 (example):
  redwoodctl rollout set image --service=runtime --image=registry.redwood/v1.2.3 --namespace=redwood-runtime

Document maintenance:
- This playbook should be reviewed quarterly or after any production rollback. Major changes to the serving runtime or the underlying networking model must trigger a review and re-validation of the canary thresholds.

Owners and escalation contacts:
- eng-private-deployments: Anna Kim (primary), sanjeev.patel@redwood.ai (oncall contact)
- eng-serving-runtime: Sanjeev Patel
- eng-platform (observability): Thomas Keller
