payload.page_title: Probe Scheduling for Mixed-Precision Evaluation Orchestration

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a probe-scheduling strategy and orchestration pattern for running mixed-precision (MPX) evaluation workloads across the eval-harness. It centralizes how probes (synthetic requests, prompt slices, and adversarial cases) should be scheduled, prioritized, and routed to candidate model/quantization variants so we can detect quality regressions and quant-degradation early without overspending GPU cycles.

Goals
-----
- Detect regressions introduced by mixed-precision and quantization changes within 24 hours of a rollout candidate being staged.
- Prioritize probes that historically surface degradations while preserving sampling diversity to catch new failure modes.
- Keep incremental compute overhead <= 12% of production-like dedicated shadow capacity.
- Provide deterministic scheduling outputs for reproducible triage and automated alerts.

Scope
-----
Applies to: eval-harness orchestration, model-onboarding shadow deployments (hosted, dedicated, private), quantization profiles used by production-serving. Excludes: offline batch-only research experiments and one-off ad hoc label collections.

Definitions
-----------
- Probe: a single test case derived from the prompt catalog (single- or multi-turn) with metadata (slice, expected behavior, anchor model output).
- MPX candidate: a model variant that uses mixed-precision kernels (e.g., int8+f16 hybrid) or a quantized artifact targeted for private/dedicated deployment.
- Probe Farm: the eval-harness pool service that schedules probes to worker lanes.
- Priority Score: numeric score used by scheduler to order probes; see algorithm below.

High-level Architecture
-----------------------
1. Probe Catalog (Prompt Sets): persisted in S3 + metadata in the eval database. Each probe has tags: slice, risk_score, cost_estimate, anchor_hash, last_seen_failure.
2. Scheduler Service (probe-scheduler): computes a daily schedule manifest for each MPX candidate.
3. Orchestrator (eval-orch): reads manifests and executes probes on the shadow fleet, collecting telemetry to ingestion topic eval-telemetry-prod.
4. Analyzer (probe-analyzer): computes signal (response stability index, semantic-embedding divergence, length-normalized token-delta) and writes alerts to PagerDuty and regression-triage queue.

Probe Types and Weighting
------------------------
We categorize probes into 4 types with default target proportions for a daily run:
- High-risk regressors (15%): known slices that have produced past regressions (high precision recall).
- Random coverage (30%): uniformly sampled to detect unknowns.
- Adversarial perturbations (20%): syntactic and semantic noise variants.
- Long-context & KV-cache sensitive (35%): multi-turn sequences emphasizing cache stability.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
priority = clamp(0.0, 1.0, 0.5 * normalized_risk + 0.3 * age_factor + 0.2 * impact_estimate)
Where: normalized_risk in [0,1] from probe metadata; age_factor = min(days_since_last_run/30,1); impact_estimate derived from upstream product usage weight.

Scheduling Algorithm
--------------------
1. For each MPX candidate, fetch last-run outcomes and compute a reweight table for probes.
2. Reserve N high-priority slots (N = ceil(0.12 * daily_budget_slots)) for probes with last_seen_failure = true.
3. Fill remaining slots by sampling per target proportions with stratified sampling across languages, device types, and traffic cohorts.
4. Annotate schedule with preferred lane (gpu-v2, cpu-sim, or quant-sim) and estimated token-cost.
5. Persist manifest and start execution window.

Operational Runbook: daily execution
-----------------------------------
1. probe-scheduler triggers at 02:00 UTC and emits manifests per candidate.
2. eval-orch pulls manifests and runs probes over a 2-hour window. Long-context probes are rate-limited to spread memory pressure.
3. probe-analyzer runs streaming checks and posts signals:
   - Response Stability Index (RSI) drop > 0.07 -> create regression triage ticket (severity P2).
   - Embedding Cosine Drift > 0.12 on median of slice -> add to regression queue.
   - Token Delta > 20% on top-k token distribution -> flag for quantization failure-mode.
4. If more than 5 distinct probes fail automatic gates for the same candidate, automatically set deployment status to HOLD and notify Model Onboarding channel (@model-onboard).

SLOs and Alert Thresholds
-------------------------
- Coverage: At least 80% of manifest probes must complete successfully within the 2-hour window.
- Latency: median probe execution latency <= 800ms per probe on gpu-v2 lane.
- Detection window: regressions must be detected and a ticket created within 6 hours of detection.

Gates and Automated Actions
--------------------------
- Soft Gate: RSI drop between 0.03–0.07 -> create a low-priority regression ticket; schedule follow-up re-run with expanded adversarial cases.
- Hard Gate: RSI drop > 0.07 or Embedding Drift > 0.12 -> set candidate to HOLD and notify oncall and onboarding owners.
- Emergency Fallback: If an MPX candidate is promoted to dedicated and field telemetry indicates correlated errors, the Routing Service will fallback to the anchor model for 1 hour while triage proceeds.

Promotion Checklist (for MPX candidate)
--------------------------------------
- [ ] All scheduled probes pass soft gates in two consecutive daily runs.
- [ ] No hard gate triggers in the last 7 days.
- [ ] Token-cost delta within expected budget +/- 8%.
- [ ] Shadow-to-field calibration run completed (see 'shadow-rollforward' playbook).
- [ ] Owners and validators listed in onboarding ticket have signed off.

Sample manifest excerpt (YAML)
----------------------------
---
candidate: mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid
date: 2025-02-10
slots: 1200
reserved_high_risk: 150
probes:
  - id: probe-15033
    slice: billing-invoice-extraction
    type: long-context
    lane: gpu-v2
    expected_anchor_hash: 7f2a9d
  - id: probe-1122
    slice: frontend-dialogue-clarity
    type: adversarial
    lane: quant-sim
    expected_anchor_hash: 9c4b1a

Config table: scheduler tunables
--------------------------------
| key                         | description                                    | default  | notes |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------|----------|-------|
| daily_budget_slots          | total probe executions per candidate per day  | 1200     | scales with candidate priority |
| reserved_failure_slots_pct  | percent reserved for recent failures          | 12       | set to 0 for experimental runs |
| long_context_rate_limit_ms  | per-probe cooldown for long-context probes    | 1500     | avoid GPU memory thrash |
| sample_seed                 | deterministic seed for sampling               | 42       | increment per run for variance |

Telemetry and Metrics (collected per-probe)
--------------------------------------------
- run_id, probe_id, candidate, lane, start_ts, end_ts
- tokens_in, tokens_out, wall_ms, gpu_mem_peak_mb
- response_hash, embedding_vector_id, rsi_score, token_delta_percent
- annotations: human_label (if escalated), triage_ticket_id

Triage Flow and Responsibilities
--------------------------------
- Initial Triage: Model Onboarding -> verify whether difference is expected for quant profile.
- Deep Triage: Applied ML (Regression Squad) -> reproduce with debug flags, compare kernel traces, KV cache traces.
- Ops Action: If a resource bottleneck is suspected (gpu_mem_peak_mb > threshold 90%), engage eng-infra to reprofile.

Owner and Escalation Contacts
----------------------------
- Probe Scheduler (owner): Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.ai)
- Probe Analyzer (owner): Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Regression Squad Lead: Priya Menon (pri@redwood.ai)
- Oncall: see eng-oncall rota (link internal)

Example CLI commands
--------------------
sections.heading: Priority score formula (used to sort queue)

sections.body: make run-probe-scheduler CANDIDANT=mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid RUN_DATE=2025-02-10
sections.heading: Generate schedule for candidate

sections.body:
aws s3 cp s3://eval-manifests/mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid/2025-02-10/manifest.yaml -

Appendix: common failure modes and remediation
-----------------------------------------------
1) Token distribution collapse (spike in token_delta_percent)
   - Likely cause: quant kernel top-k instability.
   - Remediation: tighten quantization calibration, run quant-sim with higher precision for top-k.
2) Embedding semantic shift
   - Likely cause: fused kernel numerical drift or tokenizer mismatch for rare unicode.
   - Remediation: run tokenizer normalization pass, add targeted probes for affected Unicode ranges.
3) Intermittent OOM on long-context probes
   - Likely cause: batch packing + long context combinatorics.
   - Remediation: reduce pack size for long-context lane and increase long_context_rate_limit_ms.

Related artifacts and references
-------------------------------
- Scheduler service repo: git@internal:redwood/eval-scheduler.git
- Probe catalog schema: s3://eval-catalog/schema/v2/probe-schema.yaml
- Regression triage template: confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/triage-ticket-template

Revision history
----------------
2025-01-15 — Dana Kim — initial draft
2025-02-12 — Dana Kim — added automated gate thresholds and sample manifest

payload.page_title: adaptive-probe-retargeting-telemetry-feedback-playbook-2026

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines an operational pattern and a concrete implementation template for adaptive probe retargeting: the automated process by which our eval harness reassigns probe traffic (synthetic and seeded probes) across workload slices in response to telemetry. The goal is to concentrate evaluation budget on emerging hotspots, reduce wasted probes on stable slices, and recover coverage for rare long-tail slices without human manual scheduling.

Scope
-----
Applies to: eval-harness orchestration (probe scheduler), probe-farms, offline-to-online continuity, and the telemetry ingestion pipeline.
Not covered: manual annotation workflows, external customer experiments (those follow customer-specific guardrails).

Motivation
----------
- Telemetry shows that a small subset of slices (10% of slices) account for >60% of quality alerts; static probe schedules under-sample these hotspots.
- Manually adjusting probe targets is slow and reactive.
- We need a closed-loop that uses signals (error-rate, response-stability-index, embedding-drift, latency anomalies) to retarget probes autonomously and transparently.

Principles
----------
- Safety-first: never divert >40% of total probe budget without human signoff for the first 24h of a retargeting policy change.
- Explainability: all retarget decisions must be logged with rationale and signal deltas for auditing and triage.
- Reversibility: every retarget event must include an automatic rollforward and rollback TTL with checkpoints.
- Budget-awareness: respect slice-level and global token/credit budgets.

Signals and thresholds used for retargeting
-----------------------------------------
- Quality alerts (QA): aggregated score where QA >= 0.7 triggers high-priority candidate.
- Response Stability Index (RSI): RSI drop of >0.12 over 6h for a slice marks it for review.
- Embedding Drift (cosine): mean embedding shift > 0.08 vs baseline for a week.
- Latency tail (p95/p99): p99 increase > 2x baseline AND p95 > 1.5s.
- Error budget burn rate: slice-level SLO burn > 3x expected.

Priority tiers (example)
----------------------
1. Tier A — immediate retarget: QA >= 0.7 OR RSI drop + error-burn.
2. Tier B — increased sampling: embedding drift sustained 48h OR p99 latency bump.
3. Tier C — exploratory probe seeding: low-traffic slices with sporadic failures or new data patterns.

Retargeting procedure (operational steps)
---------------------------------------
1. Signal aggregation (automated): telemetry ingestion groups signals by slice and computes delta vs baseline windows (1h, 6h, 7d).
2. Candidate generation (automated): rule engine emits a ranked list of slices with suggested delta in probe allocation (e.g., +5%, +20%).
3. Safety checks (automated): budget guardrails and cross-slice collision detector run. If budget overcommit, scale via soft-throttling rules.
4. Dry-run & audit snapshot (automated): scheduler simulates retarget for 30 minutes with shadow metrics and writes a decision record.
5. Soft-retarget deployment (canary) (automated): apply change to 10% of probe-farm capacity with TTL=6h.
6. Monitoring window (automated + human): monitor quality and cost metrics. If metrics improve continue ramp; if regress beyond rollback thresholds, automatic rollback occurs.
7. Full rollout (automated with human signoff after first 24h if large changes): ramp to desired allocation.
8. Documentation & annotation (human): owner annotates the change in the decision log and links root-cause or contextual notes.

Rollback and failure modes
-------------------------
- Immediate auto-rollback triggers:
  - Quality delta worsens by >10% relative to pre-retarget within 1h.
  - Token spend increases by >30% without measurable improvement in QA.
  - Unauthorized budget exceedance.
- Manual rollback: Oncall or Eval-Owners can initiate rollback via the eval CLI: `redwood-evalctl rollback --event-id <id>`

Retention and audit trail requirements
------------------------------------
- Decision records for retarget events must be persisted for 365 days with the following fields: event_id, timestamp, slices_affected, allocation_delta, signals_snapshot, initiating_rule, operator (system or user), dry_run_metrics, rollout_status, rollback_trigger_reason.
- Logs must be correlated with trace IDs from the scheduling service for triage.

Example scheduler config (YAML)
-----------------------------
| field | meaning | example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| policy_name | Friendly name for the retarget policy | "adaptive-hotspot-retarget-v1" |
| max_budget_pct | Maximum percent of total probe budget allowed for retarget ops | 30 |
| initial_canary_pct | Percent of capacity used for the first soft-retarget | 10 |
| rollback_thresholds | JSON-encoded thresholds for automatic rollback | '{"quality_pct_drop":10, "cost_pct_increase":30}' |
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
```
policy_name: adaptive-hotspot-retarget-v1
max_budget_pct: 30
initial_canary_pct: 10
rollout_steps:
  - canary: 10
  - ramp: 30
  - full: 100
enabled_signals: ["qa_score","rsi","embedding_drift","p99_latency","slo_burn_rate"]
```

SQL telemetry examples
----------------------
- Top candidate slices by QA delta (example):
```
SELECT slice_id, avg(qa_score) as qa_1h, avg(qa_score) OVER (PARTITION BY slice_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as qa_7d
FROM eval_telemetry
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY slice_id
ORDER BY qa_1h - qa_7d DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

CLI examples
------------
- Dry-run a retarget plan and produce a decision record:
```
redwood-evalctl propose-retarget --policy adaptive-hotspot-retarget-v1 --dry-run --output decision-12345.json
```
- Apply a small retarget change (controlled):
```
redwood-evalctl apply-retarget --event decision-12345.json --canary 10
```

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Signal owners: Observability team (alerts & collection) — ensures signal quality and baseline windows.
- Scheduler owner: Eval orchestration team — implements the rule engine and rollout logic.
- Cost guardrail owner: Finance-ML partnership — enforces budget limits and approval flows.
- Oncall: Eval-oncall — authorized to manual rollback.

Operational metrics to track (dashboards)
--------------------------------------
- Probe efficiency: fraction of probes that detect actionable regressions per 1,000 probes.
- Retarget impact: delta in QA and RSI within 6h, 24h, 7d.
- Cost delta: token spend attributable to retarget actions.
- False-positive rate: proportion of retarget events that caused no meaningful triage within 7d.

Safety review checklist (pre-deployment)
-------------------------------------
1. Policy has a max_budget_pct <= 30%.
2. Decision engine includes at least two orthogonal signals (example: QA + embedding drift).
3. Dry-run produces a decision record with no rollbacks flagged.
4. Observability dashboards and alerts are linked in the decision record.
5. Finance approved if expected cost delta > $500/day.

Example retrospective template (fill after each retarget event)
--------------------------------------------------------------
- Event ID:
- Initiating signal(s):
- Rationale summary:
- Was the retarget successful? (yes/no/mixed)
- Key metrics improved/worsened (6h/24h/7d):
- Cost impact:
- Root cause discovered:
- Follow-ups and owners:

References and related playbooks
-------------------------------
- Eval lifecycle & private/dedicated integration playbook (link in related_pages).
- Probe-farm orchestration for rare regressions (see regression-triage folder).
- Prompt coverage matrix and drift repair guide.

Appendix: small implementation notes
-----------------------------------
- Use decoupled components: signal-collector -> rule-engine -> scheduler -> probe-farm. Each component must emit the event_id to the event-log.
- Keep the rule-engine deterministic and versioned: store rule-versions with semantic versioning.
- Provide a readonly UI for decision review: columns must include signal deltas, suggested allocation delta, canary plan, and cost estimate.

Contact
-------
For questions or to propose a policy change, ping the eval-orchestration channel or email eval-platform@redwood.com.

payload.page_title: Quantization Shadow Fidelity Simulator and Regression Hypothesis Bundle

sections.body:
Overview

This document describes the Quantization Shadow Fidelity Simulator (QSFS) — a lightweight, modular evaluator used by the eval-harness to predict behavioral deltas introduced by quantized model artifacts before production rollout — and the accompanying Regression Hypothesis Bundle (RHB) for structured triage if the simulator surfaces risk. QSFS is intended for use during model-onboarding, quantization-profile generation, and pre-rollout canary design.

Why we built QSFS

- Reduce time and cost: simulate large-scale quantized behavior deterministically on small reference workloads rather than running full shadow fleets.
- Improve triage velocity: provide prioritized hypotheses and signal extraction to accelerate root cause identification for regressions tied to quant artifacts.
- Standardize handoffs: produce an artifact (RHB) consumed by regression teams, SRE, and model owners with uniform fields and triage runbooks.

Scope and non-goals

- In-scope: sequence-level fidelity simulation for text generation and reranking models (causal and encoder-decoder), token-level divergence metrics, prompt-conditioning sensitivity, and KV-cache interaction emulation.
- Out-of-scope: full GPU kernel performance estimation, detailed latency/throughput microbenchmarks, or end-to-end production traffic replay (use shadow-fleet or production mirror for that).

High-level architecture
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Probe Fabricator: selects and prepares workload slices (priming context, few-shot examples, edge-case seeds).
2) Quantized Emulator: runs a quantized-inference deterministic emulator that applies quant noise models and cache-decay approximations to a floating-point baseline.
3) Analyzer & Hypothesis Composer: produces fidelity metrics, diffs, and structured hypotheses (RHB).

Each module can be executed independently in the eval-harness pipeline or as a single command. Ownership: eval-harness team owns the code; applied-ml stewards the probe catalog.

Probe Fabrication and Selection

- Inputs: workload fingerprint, slice definitions, probe budget, and tenant constraints.
- Strategy: stratified sampling across context lengths (short/medium/long), priming density (0/1/5 shots), and token-entropy buckets.
sections.heading: QSFS consists of three coordinated modules

sections.body:
- Baseline-stability probes: produce deterministic seeds used for consistency checks.
- Quant-stress probes: perturbations (token swap, suffix truncation, numeric precision stressors).
- Edge semantic probes: adversarially generated prompts targeting critical functionality (e.g., code generation, instruction-following).

Simulator configuration (table)

| parameter | description | default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| quant_profile | identifier for quant recipe (e.g., q4f, q8a) | q4f-default | maps to quantization-profiles catalog |
| seed_set | probe catalog id | small-core-100 | use larger for release candidate |
| kv_cache_modeling | none | "approximate" | options: none, approximate, exact-sim |
| temperature | sampling temp for stochastic probes | 0.0 | 0.0 forces deterministic sampling |
| rerun_count | number of emulator passes per probe | 3 | aggregate variance budget |
| divergence_threshold | alert-level for token-level divergence | 0.06 | used to generate RHB alerts |

Execution procedure (step-by-step)

1. Prepare context: map service-level workload fingerprint (from eval-mesh) to seed_set and override priming where necessary.
2. Run floating-point baseline (FP32 or BF16) to generate canonical outputs and internal trace (logits, top-k tokens per step).
3. Run Quantized Emulator against the same probes. If kv_cache_modeling=="exact-sim", emulate cache reads/writes; else apply cache-decay model.
4. Compute fidelity metrics: token-divergence (KL and token-mismatch rate), response-syntactic-distance (BLEU/ROUGE heuristics), and functioncall-structure-delta (for tool-calling).
5. If any metric breaches configured thresholds, auto-generate an RHB and escalate per policy.

Fidelity metrics and thresholds (examples)

- Token mismatch rate: fraction of sample tokens not in FP baseline top-1 (Alert if > divergence_threshold).
- KL over logits: mean KL across steps (Alert if > 0.18).
- Response structure flip: % of probes where functioncall schema or JSON validity changed (Alert if > 0.02).
- Latent-behavior drift: embedding cosine drift of final states (Alert if > 0.12).

Regression Hypothesis Bundle (RHB) schema

The RHB is a standardized artifact produced as a JSON-LD (consumed by issue trackers and triage dashboards). The key fields listed below must be present in the bundle; simplified here for human review.

Table: RHB fields and triage actions

| field | example | triage owner | action on fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| title | "q4f -> q4f-v2: functioncall fidelity regression on payments prompts" | model-owner | assign model regression ticket |
| probe_ids | ["seed-123","seed-54"] | applied-ml | reproduce locally |
| primary_signal | "token-mismatch-rate" | applied-ml | run targeted stress probes |
| delta_snapshot | "/artifacts/q4f/v2/compare-2026-02-10" | SRE | pull logs & kernel traces |
| top_hypotheses | ["quant-rounding-bias", "kv-cache-loss"] | applied-ml | prioritize by score |
| suggested_mitigations | ["increase precision for attention kernels", "use cache-stabilizer rewrite"] | model-owner | patch & re-run QSFS |
| impact_estimate | "0.6% requests downgraded for payments flow" | product | decide rollout delay |
| blocker_flag | "true" | release_coord | block rollout if true |

Hypothesis scoring and prioritization

- Each hypothesis scored by: signal-strength (0–1), reproducibility (0–1), surface-risk (0–1). Composite score = weighted sum (0.5*signal + 0.3*repro + 0.2*risk).
- Triage guidelines: focus first on hypotheses with composite score > 0.6 and reproducibility > 0.7.

Automated escalation rules

- If blocker_flag==true OR top_hypothesis composite score > 0.8 -> auto-create high-priority regression incident and tag SRE/model-oncall.
- If token-mismatch-rate > 2x divergence_threshold across critical probes -> notify product & customer-success.

Integration points with existing pipelines

- eval-harness: QSFS is a pluggable stage in pre-promotion pipelines. Use the eval-harness adapter to surface metrics to the eval-mesh and metrics-store.
- quantization-profiles catalog: QSFS reads canonical quant recipes; results write back suggested profile adjustments.
- regression-triage: RHBs are posted to the regression queue with labels: quant-shadow, simulator, auto-rhb.

CLI examples
sections.heading: Probe types generated

sections.body: redwood-qsf simulate --profile q4f-default --seed-set small-core-100 --kv-cache-modeling approximate --temperature 0.0 --runcount 3 --out-dir /tmp/qsf/run-042
sections.heading: Run a quick smoke sim against a small seed set

sections.body:
redwood-qsf package-rhb --in /tmp/qsf/run-042 --title "q4f-v2 smoke" --upload --notify applied-ml

Promotion checklist (pre-release gate)

1. QSFS run completed with rerun_count >= 3 for release-candidate seeds.
2. No metric breaches OR documented mitigations in RHB.
3. Mitigation verification run shows reduction in relevant signals by >= 50%.
4. RHB accepted by model owner and SRE.
5. Release coordination updated (if blocker_flag true, release blocked until root cause resolved).

Operational roles and SLAs

- QSFS owner: eval-harness team. Response SLA for triage requests: 24 business hours.
- Model owner: respond to RHB assignments with initial ack within 8 business hours.
- Applied-ML: investigative owner for hypotheses with reproducibility >= 0.7.

Failure modes and mitigation patterns (short list)

- Non-reproducible drift (low reproducibility score): increase rerun_count and switch kv_cache_modeling to exact-sim.
- Cryptic embedding drift: run embedding-level saliency probes and per-layer quant-activation histograms.
- Functioncall schema flips: add precision guard for decoder logits and widen functioncall-token threshold.

Appendix A — Example RHB snippet (human-readable)

{
  "title": "q4f-v2: rerank drift for billing prompts",
  "primary_signal": "token-mismatch-rate",
  "divergence": 0.083,
  "top_hypotheses": ["attention-scale-truncation","quantized-softmax-loss"],
  "suggested_mitigations": ["upgrade attention kernel to q8a for critical layers","apply softmax smoothing"]
}

Note: the actual RHB artifact is a structured JSON-LD object; the snippet above is for readability in this doc.

Related pages and references

- Quantization profile catalog and naming conventions: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow-to-prod continuity guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Change history

- 2025-11-12: Draft created (Maya Patel).
- 2025-12-15: Incorporated Evan Chen feedback: added kv_cache_modeling modes.
- 2026-02-10: Published: added automated escalation rules and RHB schema (Sofia Ramos review).

Contact and feedback

For questions, suggested improvements, or to add a seed set to the QSFS catalog, open a ticket in the eval-harness board or DM @Maya.Patel on internal chat.

payload.page_title: Prompt sharding and cache-aware stability evaluation protocol

sections.body: This document defines a repeatable evaluation protocol for measuring prompt-level output stability when prompts are sharded (split across segments), when prefix and KV caches are active, and across quantized model variants. The protocol is intended for applied ML engineers onboarding new models into Redwood’s serving fleet and for regression triage when a change in runtime (kernels, batching, quantization) correlates with output drift.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Provide a deterministic, low-noise benchmark to compare semantic stability across model variants and runtime configs.
- Surface regressions caused by caching differences, prompt segmentation, and quantization.
- Produce actionable diagnostics (delta examples, attention/kv-dumps, similarity matrices) to guide model/runtime remediation.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Applies to autoregressive text generation and chat-style models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder where applicable).
- Not intended for pure embedding-only workloads (see embedding stability spec).
- Routine use: onboarding new model version, validating quantization profile, or triaging a regression flagged by QA or customers.
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Prompt sharding: splitting a single prompt into multiple chunks that are sent as separate requests or streamed segments to the runtime. Common for very long contexts or when prefix caching is leveraged.
- Cache-aware mode: evaluation runs where the runtime is configured to populate and reuse prefix/KV cache between segments or across repeated requests.
- Stability: measured as semantic agreement between outputs given equivalent intent; metrics described below.
sections.heading: Key terms and definitions

sections.body:
1) Candidate selection
   - Pick a representative prompt set (N >= 200 recommended). Use a mix of short, medium, and long prompts and include edge cases: multi-turn chat fragments, code blocks, bullet lists, and HTML fragments.
   - Label prompts with modality tags and expected length bucket (short <128 tok, medium 128-2048, long >2048).

2) Baseline generation (canonical run)
   - Run prompts end-to-end on the reference model variant with cache disabled (cold start) to obtain baseline outputs. Record seeds, tokenizer, model hash, runtime version.
   - CLI example: python eval_runner.py --config configs/ps_stability_baseline.yaml --run-id baseline-2026-02-14

3) Sharded runs
   - For each prompt, generate outputs under two sharding strategies:
     a) Segment-by-sentence: split on sentence boundaries (try to keep segment sizes ~256–512 tokens)
     b) Fixed-window: split into equal token windows with 25% overlap
   - For each strategy, run in: cache-disabled and cache-enabled modes. Capture per-segment outputs and final assembled output.

4) Quantization and runtime variants
   - Repeat sharded runs on each model variant of interest (fp16, int8, quantized-llm-configA). Ensure identical decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop tokens).
   - Record kernel/runtime version, kernel flags (use_batched_kv, fused_attention), and hardware type.

5) Deterministic decoding and sampling controls
   - For stability-focused comparisons prefer deterministic decoding (temperature=0, do_sample=false). If sampling is required for downstream fidelity tests, run an additional sampled pass with fixed RNG seed.

6) Metrics and thresholds
   - Surface-level metrics (per-prompt):
     * Token-level edit distance (Levenshtein) normalized by output length
     * N-gram overlap (BLEU/ROUGE) between baseline and candidate assembled outputs
     * Semantic similarity: cosine(sim(embed(baseline)), embed(candidate)) using the reference embedding model (thresholds defined below)
     * Structural agreement: alignment of stop tokens, list lengths, JSON schema conformance (where applicable)
   - Aggregate metrics (recommended reporting): mean, median, 95th percentile of normalized edit distance; fraction of prompts with semantic similarity < 0.90; fraction with structural breaks (e.g., truncated JSON).
   - Alert thresholds (suggested defaults):
     * Mean normalized edit distance increase > 0.03 compared to baseline -> warning
     * >5% prompts with semantic similarity < 0.90 -> needs-investigation
     * Any prompt with structural break (JSON invalidation, or missing required fields) -> P0 triage

7) Diagnostics produced per failing prompt
   - Raw outputs for baseline and each variant (per-segment and assembled)
   - Token alignment visualization (side-by-side diff)
   - Attention/KV dump (where supported) for segments showing divergence (save to /mnt/evals/kv-dumps/{run-id}/{prompt-id})
   - Embedding similarity heatmap across prefixes and segments
sections.heading: High-level protocol (steps)

sections.body:
run_name: "prompt_shard_stability.baseline"
model: "gptx-7b-fp16"
max_tokens: 256
decoding:
  temperature: 0.0
  do_sample: false
shard_strategy: none
cache_mode: disabled
prompts_source: "datasets/prompt_shard_suite/2026-01.jsonl"
output_dir: "results/ps_baseline/"
sections.heading: configs/ps_stability_baseline.yaml

sections.body:
run_name: "prompt_shard.int8.cache_enabled"
model: "gptx-7b-int8"
max_tokens: 256
decoding:
  temperature: 0.0
  do_sample: false
shard_strategy: fixed_window
shard_overlap: 0.25
cache_mode: enabled
kernel_flags: ["use_batched_kv", "fused_attention_v2"]
prompts_source: "datasets/prompt_shard_suite/2026-01.jsonl"
output_dir: "results/ps_int8_cache/"
sections.heading: configs/ps_shard_cache_int8.yaml

sections.body: python eval_runner.py --config configs/ps_stability_baseline.yaml --workers 16 --seed 12345
sections.heading: run baseline

sections.body: python eval_runner.py --config configs/ps_shard_cache_int8.yaml --workers 32 --seed 12345 --collect-kv-dumps
sections.heading: run int8 shard + cache

sections.body:
- results/{run-id}/outputs.jsonl  # per-prompt assembled outputs
- results/{run-id}/segment_outputs/    # per-segment artifacts
- results/{run-id}/metrics_summary.csv
- results/{run-id}/kv-dumps/
- results/{run-id}/similarity_matrices/{prompt-id}.png
sections.heading: Result artifacts

sections.body:
1) Automatic triage
   - The harness produces a ranked list of prompts by delta severity (composite score combining edit distance, semantic similarity, and structural break flags).
   - If any P0 flags (structural breaks) are present, page oncall-sre + model-owner.

2) Reproduce locally
   - Re-run the failing prompt with the exact run-id, kernel flags, and model hash on a dev cluster node with debug logging enabled.
   - Use --collect-kv-dumps and set REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 to capture runtime assertions.

3) Narrowing hypotheses
   - Compare cache-disabled vs cache-enabled runs to see if divergence appears only when cache is used -> suspect KV caching bug or cache key collision.
   - Compare fp16 vs quantized variants to isolate quantization-induced tokenization/rounding regression.
   - If divergence occurs only under sharding strategies, inspect segment assembly: ensure no dropped tokens at boundaries and consistent tokenizer state.
sections.heading: Analysis and triage playbook

sections.body:
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Eval team (Priya Rao)
- Secondary: Runtime QA (Carlos Medina)
- Expected SLAs: onboarding runs (<= 2k prompts) should complete end-to-end within 24 hours on a standard eval cluster. Triage response for P0 stability regressions: 4 hours.
sections.heading: Ownership and SLAs for evaluation runs

sections.body:
- No structural break alerts across a 1k prompt representative suite.
- Mean normalized edit distance delta <= 0.02 relative to baseline for FP16->candidate path.
- <2% prompts with semantic similarity < 0.90 for sampled suite.
- KV dump size within expected range (no unexpected MVCC growth).
sections.heading: Quality gates for model onboarding (must pass all)

sections.body:
- Symptom: Assembled output truncated when sharded but fine in non-sharded run
  - Check shard_overlap settings; confirm tokenizer boundary splitting does not drop separators.
  - Confirm that the runtime passes the correct attention_mask/position_ids across segments.
- Symptom: Small token-level differences amplified in semantics for long outputs
  - Check floating point determinism flags and quantization config (per-layer scale mismatch).
- Symptom: Divergence only when cache_enabled
  - Reproduce with cache disabled to validate; if confirmed, capture KV dumps and compare cache keys for equality.
sections.heading: Troubleshooting checklist (common failure modes)

sections.body:
- Add a stability dashboard tile in Redwood Console under "Evals / Prompt Shard Stability" that shows: mean normalized edit distance over time, % prompts with semantic similarity < 0.90, counts of structural breaks by model/version/runtime.
- Weekly triage report: top 10 failing prompts, diffs, and remediation status (fix merged / workaround / accept).
sections.heading: Dashboarding and reporting

sections.body:
- The prompt suite may contain customer-derived traces for regression triage. Mark any dataset that contains customer data with confidentiality: restricted and follow the customer-masking checklist before sharing outside the triage group.

Appendix A: Example token-alignment diff output (text)
--- baseline:
The list includes: 1) apple, 2) banana, 3) cherry.
--- candidate:
The list includes: 1) apple, 2) banana 3) cherry.

Note the missing comma after 'banana' which causes JSON-serializers downstream to fail when the output is assembled into a list.

Appendix B: Minimal embed similarity script (bash)

python - <<'PY'
from openai_embedding_client import embed_text
import json
A = embed_text('baseline output')
B = embed_text('candidate output')
from numpy import dot
from numpy.linalg import norm
print(dot(A,B)/(norm(A)*norm(B)))
PY

sections.body:

- Production prompt catalog (see related page)
- Runtime kernel flags doc: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling (internal)

sections.body:

- Carlos Medina (Runtime QA), carlos@redwood.ai

sections.body:

payload.page_title: Probe Hedge Allocator and Degradation Mitigation Manual

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This manual describes the Probe Hedge Allocator (PHA): a runtime-aware subsystem in the eval harness that proactively allocates and schedules evaluation probes to detect, contain, and mitigate fidelity degradation across private, dedicated, and hosted inference tiers. The PHA is designed to hedge coverage for slices that are most likely to show regression when model variants, quantization profiles, or serving kernels change.

Intro / Motivation
------------------
Given that regressions frequently emerge from interactions between model quantization, KV-cache behavior, and workload priming, we need an automated allocator that:
- Prioritizes probes by predicted information gain rather than raw frequency.
- Distributes probe replicas across runtime variants (float32, int8/4x, mixed-precision) and regions for early divergence detection.
- Triggers lightweight mitigations (dynamic fallback, probe re-synthesis) when drift is detected.

Scope
-----
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- The allocation policy and scoring heuristics for probes.
- Operational runbook for handling hedged-probe alerts.
- Integration points with the eval harness, telemetry bridge, and model promotion pipelines.
- YAML config examples and a validation checklist.
Not covered: deep statistical investigation techniques (see regression-triage docs) and offline annotator calibration workflows.

Terminology
-----------
- Probe: a single input (with metadata) used to evaluate model behavior.
- Hedge: creating multiple, staggered replicas of a probe across variants/regions.
- Fidelity delta: metric representing semantic divergence (see Metrics section).
- Probe-band: logical grouping of probes that share a slice/signature (e.g., “payment-instructions_en_US_long”).

Ownership
---------
- Product owner: Maya Patel (Applied ML)
- Implementing team: Eval Platform (eng-applied-ml)
- Oncall: Eval-Oncall rotation (see team wiki for calendar)
- Escalation: first to Eval Platform SRE, then to Runtime Model Ops if quantization or kernel root cause suspected.

Design goals and constraints
---------------------------
- Fast detection: median divergence detection within 15 minutes for high-priority slices.
- Low cost: hedge allocations should increase probe traffic by no more than 8% for top 500 slices during normal hedging.
- Isolation: hedged probes must not affect production customer traffic; use separate shadow tokens and rate-limits.

Metrics and SLOs
---------------
Primary metrics (collected per probe-band and model-version):
- Fidelity Delta (FD): symmetric token-level and embedding cosine divergence composite. (lower is better)
- Divergence Rate (DR): fraction of probes exceeding FD > threshold.
- Time-to-detect (TTD): time from a change (deployment/quantization) to when DR crosses alert threshold.
- Hedge Cost Uplift (HCU): additional token/compute cost from hedging.
sections.heading: This document covers

sections.body:
- TTD: 95th percentile <= 20 minutes for priority bands.
- DR alert threshold: FD >= 0.22 for textual slices or embedding cosine <= 0.88.
- HCU: <= 8% for top-500 bands, <= 15% for all bands in a confined rollout window.

Allocation policy (high-level)
-----------------------------
1. Score probe-bands by a combination of:
   - Historical volatility (weight 0.35)
   - Business priority (weight 0.30)
   - Cross-variant sensitivity (weight 0.25)
   - Recent production error signals (weight 0.10)
2. Select top-K bands per evaluation window (K configurable).
3. For each selected band, allocate hedged replicas across a taxonomy of runtime variants:
   - canonical-fp32 (baseline)
   - quant-int8 (default quant profile)
   - quant-int4-mixed (aggressive)
   - low-latency-kernel (kernel variant B)
   - region-mirror (if multi-region enabled)
4. Orchestrate staggered execution and compare outputs using fidelity rules described below.

Pseudocode (policy)
-------------------
```
for window in rolling_windows:
  bands = fetch_band_scores(window)
  selected = top_k(bands, k=WINDOW_CONFIG.k)
  for band in selected:
    variants = select_variant_set(band)
    for v in variants:
      schedule_probe_replica(band, variant=v, stagger=rand(0,STAGGER_MAX))
```

Fidelity comparison rules
-------------------------
- Primary comparator: composite FD = 0.6 * normalized_token_edit_distance + 0.4 * (1 - cosine_embed).
- For function-call or structured outputs: apply field-level equivalence with stricter thresholds (FD_field <= 0.12).
- Acceptable variance window: if replica outputs diverge but pass semantic equivalence (QA passes), do not alert.

Shutdown and mitigation strategies
--------------------------------
sections.heading: SLOs (targets)

sections.body:
- Soft-mitigation (automated): increase sampling to 3x for the affected band and capture extended debug trace (KV-cache snapshot, seed, full telemetry).
- Autoswap: route subsequently scheduled probes to fallback variant (canonical-fp32) while human review occurs.
- Canary-quarantine: mark latest model/quant artifact as quarantined in the artifact registry and block promotion pipelines.
- Alert owner and create incident with prefilled triage template.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)
---------------------------------
1. Alert fires: DR > threshold for a band.
2. Oncall: acknowledge within 10 minutes in PagerDuty and open a triage ticket.
3. Run lightweight triage commands:
   - CLI: evalctl probe inspect --band <band> --last 60m
   - CLI: evalctl probe compare --band <band> --variants all --format json
4. If FD confirms regression in quant variants but not canonical-fp32:
   - Trigger autoswap: evalctl hedger autoswap --band <band> --target canonical-fp32
   - Notify Model-Ops and set artifact quarantine flag: model-registry tag set --id <artifact> --tag quarantine
5. If all variants diverge from expected golden outputs: escalate to Applied ML for root cause hypothesis (prompt sensitivity, seed changes, tokenization drift).
6. Postmortem: attach probe traces, hedger logs, and telemetry to the incident and link to regression-triage docket.

Validation & test harness integration
-----------------------------------
- Shadow run mode: PHA must be exercised in shadow for every rollout. Test checklist:
  1. End-to-end scheduling works under synthetic load (5000 probes/s for 10m).
  2. Comparators produce stable FD values under controlled perturbations.
  3. Autoswap triggers in the sandbox and respects rate-limits.
- Unit tests: score normalization, variant selection heuristics, and stagger calculation.
- Integration tests: gated in CI with a smoke job that runs PHA across a minimal model set.

YAML config example
-------------------
Below is a representative hedger config used by the eval orchestrator (values annotated):

```yaml
hedger:
  window_seconds: 600            # evaluation window
  k_top_bands: 250              # number of bands to hedge each window
  max_stagger_seconds: 45       # jitter to reduce simultaneous stress
  variant_sets:
    default: ["canonical-fp32", "quant-int8", "low-latency-kernel"]
  cost_budget_pct: 0.08         # HCU budget
  alerting:
    fidelity_threshold: 0.22
    min_alert_volume: 3
```

CLI examples
------------
- Inspecting allocations in last window:
  evalctl hedger status --window 10m --json
- Forcing a temporary hedge for a band:
  evalctl hedger force-hedge --band payment-instructions_en_US_long --variants quant-int8,low-latency-kernel --ttl 1h

Alerting and observability
-------------------------
sections.heading: Automated actions when divergence conditions met

sections.body:
- Probe-band heatmap (DR over time)
- FD distribution histogram by variant
- Hedge Cost Uplift time series and budget burn rate
- Replica failure rate and scheduling latency
sections.heading: Dashboard panels to include in the default hedger view

sections.body:
1. hedger.fd.high: when DR for any priority band > 0.05 sustained for 15m.
2. hedger.hcu.burn: when HCU > configured budget for 30m.
3. hedger.autoswap.rate: when autoswap events exceed 5 in 1 hour (indicates instability).

Telemetry & audit
----------------
sections.heading: Baked alert rules (examples)

sections.body:
- full request/response (sanitized PII)
- model artifact id and runtime kernel id
- KV-cache diagnostics snapshot (if available)
- execution trace id and machine metadata
All artifacts stored in probe-archive with 90-day retention for internal investigations.

Release checklist & promotion gates
----------------------------------
sections.heading: Captured artifacts for every hedged replication

sections.body:
- Run a 48-hour shadow trial with full telemetry enabled.
- Confirm HCU remains below specified budget in a representative workload sample.
- Ensure automated autoswap reversions are tested end-to-end in staging.
- Obtain sign-off from Applied ML, Runtime, and SRE owners (names recorded in sign-off log).

Appendix A: Sample triage template (prefilled)
---------------------------------------------
Title: [Auto] Hedger alert - <band> - <artifact-id>
Severity: P2
Summary: DR crossed threshold in quant variants; canonical-fp32 shows [pass|fail].
sections.heading: Before enabling PHA for a new model-family or quant-profile

sections.body:
- quant-precision drift (quantization mapping mismatch)
- priming/seed variation affecting KV-cache
- tokenization or normalization bug in preprocessor
Immediate actions taken: autoswap -> canonical-fp32; captured extended traces; quarantined artifact.
Next steps: run focused replay job, re-evaluate quant-profile sensitivity, roll forward with revert if necessary.

Appendix B: Quick debugging commands
-----------------------------------
- Compare sample outputs: evalctl probe compare --band <band> --variants quant-int8,canonical-fp32 --sample 20 --output table
- Dump KV cache snapshot for a replica: evalctl probe debug --trace <trace-id> --dump-kv

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary: Eval Platform Slack channel #eval-hedger (pings to PagerDuty)
- Model-Ops lead: Diego Ramos (diego@redwood.com)
- Applied ML lead: Maya Patel (maya@redwood.com)

Change log
----------
- 2026-09-15: Initial draft (Asha Menon)
- 2026-10-10: Added autoswap flow and YAML config defaults (Diego Ramos)
- 2026-11-02: Finalized FD comparator and SLO targets; publish (Maya Patel)

Related reading
---------------
- regression-triage/playbook for automated-regression-bisect (see internal docket)
- quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026.json

End of manual
sections.heading: Hypotheses

payload.page_title: Eval mesh topology and slotting cookbook

sections.body: This cookbook defines the recommended topology, slotting strategies, and operational patterns for the eval mesh used across Redwood’s evaluation fleet. The document covers: mesh topology patterns, slot types and sizing; the slot allocation algorithm; cost and fidelity accounting; backfill and rebalancing strategies; safety and privacy gates for shadow workloads; and an operational runbook for deploying topology changes.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Provide a predictable, cost-aware mapping from eval workloads (probes, shadow traffic, backfills) to scarce evaluation capacity.
- Minimize eval latency for high-priority probes while maximizing overall probe coverage within budget.
- Ensure safe rollouts and auditable chargebacks for tenant-aware evals.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Evaluation platform engineers (owners of eval-orch and shadow-mesh).
- Onboarding engineers preparing probe manifests and budgets.
- SREs responsible for eval fleet capacity and cost allocation.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- eval-orch: central orchestrator that assigns probes to slots and emits allocation events.
- probe-fabricator: generates synthetic probes and seeds shadow traffic.
- shadow-mesh: per-cluster runtime that executes shadow workloads; supports isolation modes (tenant, mixed, anonymized).
- telemetry-ingest: collects token-level latency/cost/time-series for evals.
- eval-ledger: accounting service that records slot consumption and cost attributions.
sections.heading: Key services and components

sections.body:
1) Slot: a reserved execution slot on the eval mesh. Slots have attributes: tier, cpu/gpu profile, qps limit, and cost weight.
2) Probe class: a logically grouped set of probes (e.g., functioncall-stability, longcontext-coherence, embedding-drift).
3) Fidelity budget: the allocation of high-fidelity slots for a probe class over a time window.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
A) Hierarchical mesh (default) — used for most workloads:
   - Global control plane (eval-orch) + regional shadow-mesh clusters.
   - Each regional mesh exposes three slot pools: fast (low-latency), steady (balanced), bulk (throughput-optimized).
   - Routing policy: prefer local fast -> local steady -> cross-region steady -> bulk.

B) Isolated shadow mesh (sensitive tenants) — for regulated customers:
   - Dedicated shadow cluster with tenant-only slots and KMS-protected probes.
   - No cross-tenant colocation; telemetry scrubbed at source.
sections.heading: Topology patterns (recommended)

sections.body:
| slot_type | cpu/gpu | qps_limit | median_latency_target | cost_weight | recommended_use_cases |
| fast      | 1xA100 | 50       | < 40ms                | 5x         | interactive probes, micro-canaries |
| steady    | 1xA100 | 200      | < 120ms               | 2x         | baseline continuous probes        |
| bulk      | 2xA100 | 1000     | best-effort            | 1x         | backfills, large-scale simulations|
sections.heading: Slot types and sizing (reference table)

sections.body:
1. Ingest probe manifest with metadata: priority (P0..P3), fidelity_required (high/medium/low), probe_weight, tenant_id, SLA_window.
2. Compute effective score = priority_weight * fidelity_multiplier / expected_tokens_per_probe.
3. Run candidate selection: try to place in same-region fast pool if score >= fast_threshold; otherwise steady; if no fit and probe is low-fidelity, schedule into bulk with sampling.
4. Perform cost check against probe class fidelity budget in eval-ledger; if budget overrun, enqueue for token-sampled run or reject with recommendation.
sections.heading: Slot allocation algorithm (summary)

sections.body:
- priority_weight: P0=1.0 (critical), P1=0.6, P2=0.3, P3=0.1
- fidelity_multiplier: high=1.0, medium=0.6, low=0.2
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate (for bulk): default 0.05 (5%)
sections.heading: Allocation heuristics and thresholds (tunable knobs)

sections.body:
- Eval-ledger records: slot_id, probe_manifest_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_processed, cost_estimate.
- Monthly billing export includes: tenant_id, probe_class, total_tokens, slot-weighted-cost.
- Fidelity budget alerts: generate when projected spend > 80% of allocated monthly fidelity budget for probe class.
sections.heading: Cost and fidelity accounting

sections.body:
- Trigger conditions: underutilization > 20% for 15m OR overload (queue depth > 2000).
- Backfill steps:
  1) Identify candidate low-priority low-fidelity probes for bulk migration.
  2) Apply progressive sampling ramp (0% -> 5% -> 25% over 30m) with telemetry gates.
  3) Monitor fidelity signal (response-stability-index, latency-tail) — abort if degradation > configured delta.
- Rebalancing (auto): every 10 minutes, eval-orch computes target distribution and migrates slots with live cutover window of 2 minutes.

Safety, privacy, and gating:
- All shadow traffic must be redacted by probe-fabricator before entering telemetry-ingest.
- Sensitive-probe flag triggers isolated shadow-mesh placement.
- Rollout gating: new topology rules must pass canary on 3 regional meshes for at least 24h with no fidelity or latency regression > 2x baseline.

Operational runbook: topology change flow
1) Draft topology change PR (config: pools, thresholds, weightings) and post to #eval-ops.
2) Create an experiment manifest in eval-orch with scope=canary (regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1).
3) Dry-run allocation for 24h (simulation mode) and gather: slot fill curves, projected ledger spend, telemetry delta.
4) If dry-run passes, enable canary with 1% of global probe volume for 24h.
5) Escalation criteria (immediately rollback if any fires):
   - fidelity_delta > 3% for P0 probes
   - latency tail (p99) increase > 150ms for fast slots
   - spending rate > 2x projection
6) Gradually increase canary (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with 12h observation windows between steps.
sections.heading: Backfill and rebalancing policy

sections.body:
---
slot_pools:
  - name: fast
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 50
    weight: 5
    allocation_threshold: 0.7
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: steady
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 200
    weight: 2
    allocation_threshold: 0.3
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: bulk
    gpu: 2xa100
    concurrency: 1000
    weight: 1
    sampling_rate: 0.05
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
---
sections.heading: Example slotting config (YAML example)

sections.body:
- probe_id: pc-2026-485
- probe_class: longcontext-coherence-v2
- priority: P1
- fidelity_required: high
- expected_tokens: 1200
- sensitive: false
- owner: search-team@redwood.ai

Telemetry and alerting knobs to configure for topology rollouts:
- response-stability-index (RSI) delta alert: > 2x baseline -> sev-2
- p99 latency increase (fast slots): > 150ms -> sev-2
- fidelity-budget burn rate: projected > 80% -> paging to cost-ops
- slot-fill anomaly (< 10% utilization across 30m) -> investigate potential overprovisioning
sections.heading: Probe manifest fields (example)

sections.body:
1) Check eval-orch allocation logs for allocation_reject reasons.
2) Query eval-ledger for probe_manifest_id and cost budget status.
3) Inspect shadow-mesh metrics for slot health (oom_count, preemptions, avg_qps).
4) If privacy gating blocked allocation, confirm probe redaction passed (probe-fabricator logs).
sections.heading: Debugging checklist (when probes are not scheduled or fail)

sections.body:
- Goal: reduce cost for continuous functioncall-stability probes by 18% while preserving p99 latency for P0 canaries.
- Action: introduced a new steady pool with 1.5x concurrency and weight=1.8, enabled progressive bulk sampling for low-fidelity sub-slices.
- Result: after staged rollout (1% -> 20% -> 100%), observed 17.9% cost reduction and p99 for P0 canaries remained within 8ms of baseline.
sections.heading: Rollout example (real case study)

sections.body:
- Owners: eval-platform team (primary), evaluation-costing (secondary).
- Oncall: eval-sre rotation (pager: #eval-oncall).
- Escalation path: eval-oncall -> eval-platform -> platform-sre -> eng-lead.

Appendix A — tuning knobs and recommended defaults:
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate: 0.05
- fidelity_alert_pct: 80
- rebalancing_interval_minutes: 10

Appendix B — links to related docs:

payload.page_title: Latency Sensitivity Eval Protocol for Routing and Fallback Policies

sections.body: This document describes the evaluation protocol used to measure and qualify model variants and serving configurations for latency-sensitive workloads. The goal is to produce an operational signal that directly informs traffic routing and automatic fallback policies in Redwood's smart routing layer. It covers metric definitions, workload synthesis, test harness configuration, pass/fail thresholds, and an incident triage runbook for latency regressions.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Many customer-facing features require a sub-100ms median response time or predictable tail latency to maintain UX.
- Model choices (size, quantization), runtime kernel selection, KV-cache hit patterns, and batching behavior all interact to create latency regressions that are invisible to token-count-only evaluations.
- Automated routing and fallback should be driven by a reproducible eval signal that closely mimics production request characteristics.
sections.heading: Background and motivation

sections.body:
- Applies to: model variants intended for low-latency endpoints (chat-completion, single-turn generation with short context), runtime tunables that affect single-request latency (batching, prefetch, kernel/path selection), and routing/fallback policy parameters.
- Excludes: large-batch throughput-only benchmarks, long-context (> 8k) full-document generation stress tests (covered by separate bench).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1) Per-request P95 latency: end-to-end time from API ingress to first-byte-of-response (ms).
2) Cold-start latency: latency when no warm worker has the model loaded or KV cache is empty (ms).
3) Steady-state latency: median and P95 after warmup period (ms).
4) Amplification factor (AF): ratio of P95 under production-mixed traffic to P95 under synthetic single-client baseline. Used to quantify sensitivity to interleaving workloads.
5) SLO delta: change in SLO attainment compared to baseline model/config (percentage points).
sections.heading: Key definitions and metrics

sections.body:
- Target median (50th): <= 80ms for short-chat endpoints (configurable per product).
- Target P95: <= 180ms.
- Acceptable cold-start: <= 400ms.
- AF threshold for auto-rollback: > 1.5 triggers investigation; > 2.0 blocks rollout.
sections.heading: Minimum SLOs used by this protocol

sections.body:
- Primary prompt set: 1k anonymized short-turn prompts sampled from production (max tokens: 64). Prompts are stratified by client product, region, and token distribution.
- Adversarial prompt subset: 200 prompts with long-token prefixes, syntactic noise, and content that stresses decoding loops.
- Synthetic client mix: a multi-client interleaving generator with 50 concurrent virtual clients, configurable think-time distribution (exponential mean = 200ms).
- Background noise profile: 10% of requests are long-context (> 2048 tokens) to simulate multi-tenant interference.
sections.heading: Test corpus and traffic profiles

sections.body:
---
harness: latency-sensitivity-v1
clients: 50
think_time_ms_mean: 200
prompt_set: s3://redwood-evals/latency/short-chat-1k-v2.json
model_variant: rwinf-7b-q8
batch_policy: continuous
kv_cache_mode: enabled
warmup_requests: 500
measurement_window_sec: 600
collect: [p50, p90, p95, p99, mean, throughput, cpu, gpu_util, memory]
---
sections.heading: Harness configuration (example YAML)

sections.body:
1. Provision test cluster matching the target deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). Use the infra profile documented in /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/test-cluster-profiles.
2. Pre-load models and warm KV caches using warmup_requests. Confirm worker processes are up and the model is resident in GPU memory.
3. Start the synthetic client generator with the primary prompt set and background noise profile.
4. Run for measurement_window_sec (recommended 10 minutes for small variants, up to 30 minutes for larger configs).
5. Aggregate metrics and compute AF relative to baseline. Baseline is the currently promoted model+config for the route.
6. If metrics cross thresholds defined under 'Pass/fail criteria', mark the run as failed and trigger the triage workflow.
sections.heading: Execution steps (numbered procedure)

sections.body:
- Hard fail: P95 > 200ms OR AF > 2.0 OR cold-start > 600ms.
- Soft fail (requires engineering review): P95 between 180-200ms OR AF between 1.5-2.0 OR median degradation > 10%.
- Canary gating: For canary rollouts, combine this harness signal with production real-user telemetry for 1 hour before advancing traffic if any soft-fail metrics present.
sections.heading: Pass/fail criteria and gating rules

sections.body:
- If hard fail: route traffic away from the model variant immediately (automatic rollback) and mark variant unhealthy in the routing registry.
- If soft fail: reduce traffic to variant by 50% and add a retry fallback (fast-path to baseline variant) for requests with strict latency budget.
- If AF indicates susceptibility to multi-tenant interference: set conservative batching knobs and enable per-customer QoS isolation in Dedicated deployments.
sections.heading: How latency signals map to routing and fallback policies

sections.body:
- Always run the harness for both float and quantized builds. Quantization may improve median latency but can worsen P95 due to kernel path mismatches.
- Record kernel selection logs (kernel_id, torch/llvm path) and include in eval artifact. Use the profiling-playbook to map slow paths back to kernel candidates.
sections.heading: Quantization and kernel interaction notes

sections.body:
- Each run must produce a single artifact tarball with: harness-config.yaml, raw-metrics.jsonl, aggregated-summary.csv, kernel-selection.log, and reproducer-script.sh. Upload to s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/latency/<run-id>/.
- Create a Confluence run summary page using the template in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/run-summary-template. Required fields: run-id, cluster-profile, model-variant, pass/fail, owner, link to artifacts.

Incident triage runbook (when a promoted variant shows a latency regression in prod):
1. Immediate mitigation (first 5 minutes): increase routing weight to baseline model; if autos-rollback is enabled, the router will reduce traffic automatically. Notify on-call via Slack channel #prod-latency.
2. Collect traces: enable request tracing for affected route and collect first-byte timing, kernel selection trace, and KV-cache hit logs for a 5-minute window.
3. Re-run harness with identical cluster profile and collect AF. If AF reproduces: escalate to serving-runtime oncall.
4. If AF does not reproduce: capture production request samples (privacy-preserving sampling; redact PII) and run through the harness with identical concurrency/think-time distribution.
5. Postmortem: owner creates a postmortem page including root cause hypothesis, timeline, and remediation (config change, kernel patch, model rollback). Link to regression triage playbook and schedule a follow-up regression test after remediation is applied.
sections.heading: Artifact and reporting requirements

sections.body:
- Eval owner: Applied ML Evaluations team (primary contact: Elena Gupta).
- Serving runtime owner: eng-serving-runtime (contacts: Marcus Lee).
- Platform & routing owner: eng-platform (contacts: Tara O'Connell).
- On-call: per the oncall rota in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations.

Checklist before promoting a model/config (pre-promotion verification):
- [ ] Pass latency harness under target cluster profile
- [ ] Quantized and float builds evaluated and artifacts uploaded
- [ ] Canary: run 50% traffic for 1 hour with live telemetry and no hard-fail events
- [ ] Kernel-selection review for uncommon slow-paths
- [ ] Owner sign-off and release notes recorded

Appendix: example CLI commands
- Run harness locally (short smoke test):
  ./eval-harness run --config harness-config.yaml --dry-run=false --warmup 100 --window 60

- Upload artifacts:
  aws s3 cp artifacts/<run-id>.tar.gz s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/latency/<run-id>/ --acl private

- Query aggregated metrics (jq):
  cat aggregated-summary.csv | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | .[1:-1] | map(split(","))'
sections.heading: Ownership and responsibilities

sections.body:
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- /confluence/eng-platform/rollouts/canary-deployment-guidelines
sections.heading: References and related pages

sections.body:

- 2025-12-10: added AF metric and gating rules after review
- 2026-02-03: tightened P95 thresholds for short-chat endpoints and clarified artifact requirements

payload.page_title: Federated Eval Orchestration and Privacy Budgeting Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-----
This playbook describes a federated evaluation orchestration pattern and an accompanying privacy budgeting model for running distributed evals across Dedicated, Private, and Hosted environments. It targets teams that need to: (1) evaluate models across siloed customer workloads, (2) preserve differential privacy and data minimization guarantees, and (3) preserve capacity and cost SLOs while obtaining statistically useful signals.

Motivation
----------
As Redwood supports federated and private deployments, evaluators increasingly need aggregated signals from heterogenous tenants without moving raw user data to central storage. A federated eval approach reduces data movement, improves regulatory compliance, and enables per-tenant calibration. However, it introduces new operational concerns: orchestration latency, heterogeneous compute availability, skewed sample distributions, and the need to account for privacy "budget" consumption across many small experiments. This document defines patterns, configuration, and an operational runbook.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
- Goals:
  - Provide a repeatable orchestration pattern for federated evals that works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
  - Define a privacy budgeting abstraction that teams can use to reason about cumulative information leakage from repeated evals.
  - Offer scheduling and cost controls so evals do not violate production SLOs or incur unexpected costs.
- Non-goals:
  - This playbook is not a full cryptographic DP primer. Use this alongside the Security team's DP guidance for formal proofs.
  - We do not prescribe model training workflows. This targets evaluation and telemetry only.

Key concepts and terminology
----------------------------
- Federated Eval Node: customer-controlled evaluator instance that runs workload probes against a model and emits sanitized, aggregated metrics.
- Coordinator: centralized orchestration service that schedules federated eval jobs, collects metadata, and enforces privacy budgets and quotas.
- Privacy Budget: a per-customer and per-experiment quota (measured in epsilon-like units) that limits how much information an eval can reveal about raw user data.
- SLO Guardrails: limits on CPU/GPU utilization, request QPS, and latency impact so eval runs do not impair production serving.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1) Coordinator service (runs in Redwood control plane):
   - Registers eval specs, assigns job IDs, tracks budgets, aggregates metadata, and stores per-job manifests.
   - API endpoints: POST /v1/fed-evals (create), GET /v1/fed-evals/{id} (status), POST /v1/fed-evals/{id}/complete (submit summary).
2) Federated Eval Agent (runs in customer Dedicated/Private environment or on sandboxed host):
   - Pulls job manifests, executes probes locally, computes local aggregates, applies noise/sanitization, and submits only summary artifacts.
3) Result Aggregator (control plane):
   - Accepts per-node summaries and computes final population-level metrics, confidence intervals, and cross-tenant reports.

Orchestration and scheduling policies
------------------------------------
- Priority classes:
  - critical: must-run for compliance or safety, preemptible only with explicit owner approval.
  - standard: routine evals for performance/cost monitoring.
  - exploratory: low-priority experiments with strict cost caps.
- Backoff and retry policy:
  1) Coordinator schedules up to 3 attempts spaced with exponential backoff (initial 30s).
  2) If nodes report resource contention, Coordinator reschedules to a softer window (off-peak) and reduces sample size.
- Capacity-aware placement:
  - Agents report available GPU minutes and QPS headroom. Coordinator adjusts sample sizes and selects nodes that meet requested headroom thresholds.

Privacy budgeting model
----------------------
- Each federated eval job declares: privacy_label (purpose), sensitivity_level (low | medium | high), and requested_epsilon (numeric string).
- Budget enforcement rules:
  - Per-tenant rolling budget window: 30 days.
  - Default epsilon caps: low=0.5, medium=0.2, high=0.05.
  - Coordinator rejects or asks for explicit owner approval when requested_epsilon exceeds remaining budget.
- Sanitization primitives recommended on Agents:
  - Local aggregation with counts and clipped contributions.
  - Add Laplace/Gaussian noise calibrated to requested_epsilon.
  - Thresholding: require minimum local sample size Nmin before releasing any summary.

Operational runbook: day-of-run checklist
----------------------------------------
1) Create eval manifest with fields: job_id, probes[], privacy_label, requested_epsilon, target_nodes[].
2) Coordinator validates resource quotes and budgets -> returns scheduled window and sample_size suggestion.
3) Notify tenant SRE/owner and request acceptance if requested_epsilon > 0.1.
4) Agents pull manifest and perform a dry-run smoke check (3 probe samples) against a read-only test endpoint.
5) Execute full run. Agents upload compressed summary (sha256) to aggregator.
6) Aggregator computes population-level statistics and stores job artifact.
7) Auto-generate report and flag if any metric deviates > 3 sigma from baseline.

Incident / failure modes and mitigation
--------------------------------------
- Node fails mid-run:
  - Mitigation: Coordinator marks node as partial and rebalances sample to other participants while respecting budget.
- Excessive latency on Agents causing production impact:
  - Mitigation: Immediate agent throttling, abort job, alert oncall, rollback probe frequency.
- Privacy budget overrun attempt:
  - Mitigation: Coordinator refuses job and records audit event; require manual override with compliance sign-off.

Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards
-----------------------------
- Orchestration SLOs:
  - Job acceptance latency: 99th percentile < 4s for manifest validation.
  - Completion success rate: >= 97% across scheduled nodes for standard jobs.
- Privacy and correctness KPIs:
  - Budget violation rate: target 0%.
  - Fraction of reports passing sanity checks: >= 99%.
- Recommended dashboards:
  - Fed Eval Overview (jobs by privacy_label, budget consumption heatmap).
  - Agent Health (node CPU/GPU headroom, last heartbeat).
  - Aggregation Integrity (submitted SHA256 vs canonical).

Configuration examples
----------------------
- Eval manifest (YAML):
```yaml
job_id: fed-eval-2026-187
privacy_label: usage-telemetry
sensitivity_level: medium
requested_epsilon: "0.15"
priority: standard
target_nodes: [tenant-az-1, tenant-eu-3]
probes:
  - name: answer-quality-probe
    samples: 200
    path: /v1/generate
    timeout_ms: 5000
```

- Agent local constraints table:
| key | description | default | notes |
|-----|-------------|---------|-------|
| gpu_headroom_minutes | Minutes of GPU available for evals | "120" | Agents must report as integer minutes |
| min_local_sample | Minimum local samples before reporting | "50" | Prevents low-N leakage |
| noise_mechanism | Laplace|Gaussian | "Gaussian" | Calibrated per requested_epsilon |

Privacy review checklist (pre-launch)
------------------------------------
1) Confirm privacy_label and business justification.
2) Ensure requested_epsilon <= remaining budget or signed exception exists.
3) Verify Nmin and clipping thresholds configured on agents.
4) Confirm audit logging to central control plane is enabled.
5) Register the job in the security review queue if sensitivity_level == high.

Appendix: common CLI commands and snippets
------------------------------------------
- Submit a federated eval (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/fed-evals -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @manifest.yaml

- Retrieve job status:
  curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/fed-evals/fed-eval-2026-187/status

- Quick sanity check (agent):
  python -m redwood.fed.agent \n    --manifest manifest.yaml \n    --dry-run

Related docs and references
---------------------------
- See Eval Mesh and Workload Fingerprinting (internal) for node capability discovery.
- Security DP primer and the Security team's DP evidence repo for formal guarantees.

Ownership and next steps
------------------------
- Owners: Applied ML Eval Platform (primary), Security (privacy budget policy), Eng SRE (agent health).
- Next steps (roadmap):
  - Q2 2026: automated budget reconciliation API and per-tenant quota UI.
  - Q3 2026: integrate cryptographic aggregation primitives (secure aggregation) as opt-in.

Contact
-------
If you have questions about implementing federated evals or need an exception for privacy budgets, contact Maya Patel (maya.patel@redwood.ai) or raise an issue in #eval-platform on Slack.
