payload.page_title: Evaluation Provenance Ledger and Mixed-Precision Rollout Manifest

sections.body:
Defines a canonical provenance ledger format for evaluation artifacts and prescribes a guarded rollout checklist for mixed-precision (quantized) deployments. The goal is reproducible artifact lineage, rapid triage of regressions introduced by precision changes, and clear telemetry to drive safe rollouts.
Overview
This document defines the evaluation provenance ledger (EPL) schema, storage conventions, and an operational manifest for rolling mixed-precision model variants (e.g., FP16 -> INT8 or hybrid quant) through our eval and shadow environments before production promotion. It bridges eval-harness outputs, model-onboarding checkpoints, and runtime telemetry used by regression triage.

Scope
- Applies to all evaluations and probes used for model promotion, shadow validation, and regression bisecting for mixed-precision and quant-migration efforts.
- Covers: provenance records produced by the eval-harness, artifact storage paths, hash and signing conventions, telemetry fields required by triage runbooks, and the staged rollout checklist.
- Excludes: training data lineage (handled by Data Platform) and customer PII transformation rules (see privacy sandbox docs).

Why a ledger matters
- Reproducibility: Every eval artifact must map to an immutable record so a failing probe can be replayed against the exact artifact and runtime.
- Triage speed: Standardized fields let the regression-hunting automation correlate anomalies to runtime/kernel/quant changes.
- Auditing: Rollout manifest provides a compact audit trail for mixed-precision migrations required by compliance.

EPL (Evaluation Provenance Ledger) record format
- Each evaluation run MUST emit an EPL record and push it to the artifacts index. The record is a small YAML/JSON metadata file stored next to artifacts. Example (YAML):

  eval_id: "epl-2026-000124"
  timestamp: "2026-02-09T21:16:03Z"
  probe_set_id: "priming-cohort-v3"
  model_suite: "redwood-small-7b"
  model_commit: "6a3b9c2"
  model_build_tag: "redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01"
  quant_profile_version: "qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2"
  runtime_fingerprint: "runt-fw-1.8.2+kernels-2026-01-20"
  runtime_bin_sha: "sha256:4f9a8e..."
  seed_and_rng: "seed=20260209-42"
  dataset_hashes:
    - "prompts:sha256:ab12..."
    - "labels:sha256:9f3d..."
  batch_profile: "microburst-16-lowlatency"
  kv_cache_config: "enabled,cache_ttl=30m"
  host_gpu_arch: "nvidia-h100-80gb"
  docker_image: "redwood/eval-runner:v1.27"
  artifacts_url: "s3://eval-artifacts/epl-2026-000124/"
  metrics_summary:
    - "embedding_stability:0.012"
    - "coherence_delta:-0.03"
    - "latency_p95_ms:128"
    - "token_cost_delta_per_1k:0.74"

sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- All hashes use sha256 and are hex-prefixed.
- quant_profile_version must reference a formal quant profile artifact from the quant registry.
- runtime_fingerprint encodes serving runtime major/minor, kernel set date, and any experimental flags.
- signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized YAML; signing key is the eval-harness service key (rotated quarterly).

Storage and naming conventions
- Artifact path template: s3://eval-artifacts/{year}/{model_suite}/{eval_id}/
- EPL metadata is saved as metadata.yaml next to artifacts and copied into the artifacts index database.
- Retention: metadata kept indefinitely; large artifacts kept for 90 days by default, with TTL extensions for promoted runs.

Searchable index fields (required)
- eval_id, model_suite, model_commit, quant_profile_version, probe_set_id, timestamp, host_gpu_arch, runtime_bin_sha, artifacts_url.
- Index entries MUST include a small metrics vector (embedding_stability, coherence_delta, latency_p95_ms) for fast queries.

Rollout manifest: staged promotion for mixed-precision variants
Purpose: Reduce blast radius when deploying quantized variants and ensure each stage is reversible with traceable provenance.

Rollout stages (numbered checklist)
1) Local dev & micro-evals
   - Owner: model-onboarding team
   - Run: full EPL metadata produced for the quant profile against a mini-probe set (N=500).
   - Acceptance: no coherence_delta worse than -0.05; embedding_stability <= 0.02.
2) Shadow (isolated shadow mesh)
   - Owner: eval-harness + serving-runtime
   - Run: shadow traffic replay for 48 hours with replica ratio 1:1000; collect EPL and streaming telemetry.
   - Acceptance: pass functional sentinels (safety/hedge tests), latency_p95 within 1.25x baseline, no token_cost_delta > +1.5x.
3) Canary (tenant-limited rolling canary)
   - Owner: platform ops
   - Run: 48–72 hours, ramp to 3% traffic segmented by low-risk tenants; EPL records must link to each canary snapshot.
   - Acceptance: per-tenant quality thresholds: NPS-equivalent probe acceptance rate >= 98%, embedding drift < 0.03, no SEV on functioncall stability.
4) Multi-tenant confidence window
   - Owner: product + platform
   - Run: 7 days at 10–20% traffic; additional human-in-the-loop review for flagged probes.
   - Acceptance: no priority regressions, ops runbook readiness validated.
5) Full promotion
   - Owner: release lead
   - Run: promote artifact tag to catalog and mark EPL provenance as promoted (promoted=true). Update retention policy to 1 year.

Rollback triggers (automated)
- Any SEV-level alert mapped to the promoted artifact_runtime_bin_sha within the last 2 hours.
- embedding_stability delta > 0.05 vs baseline for 5-minute rolling window.
- sustained latency_p95 > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.

Rollback procedure (numbered)
1) Mark artifact as blocked in the model catalog and set promoted=false.
2) Trigger automated routing policy: shift traffic to the last known good commit according to EPL history.
3) Notify stakeholders: #ops-oncall, model-owner, product. Include eval_id and artifacts_url in message.
4) Open regression investigation ticket and attach EPL metadata, telemetry snapshot, and failing probe list.

Triaging with the EPL: a step-by-step example
1) Detection: alert for rise in functioncall failure rate. Alert payload includes runtime_bin_sha and recent eval_ids.
2) Correlate: query the artifacts index for eval runs with matching runtime_bin_sha and quant_profile_version within the last 7 days.
3) Reproduce: fetch metadata.yaml and artifacts_url for the top candidate eval_id, reproduce the run locally using docker_image and seed_and_rng.
4) Isolate: run the same probe set under FP16 and the candidate quant profile; collect metric diffs.
5) Hypothesis: if failure maps to a kernel mismatch, escalate to kernel team; if mapping to quant_profile_version, use quant rollback checklist.

Telemetry fields required by regression automation
- eval_id (string)
- runtime_bin_sha (string)
- quant_profile_version (string)
- host_gpu_arch (string)
- probe_set_id (string)
- embedding_stability (float)
- coherence_delta (float)
- functioncall_error_rate (float)
- latency_p95_ms (float)
- token_cost_delta_per_1k (float)

Operational playbook snippets
- Quick repro CLI (example):
  docker run --rm -v /tmp/artifacts:/artifacts redwood/eval-runner:v1.27 \
    --eval-id epl-2026-000124 --probes /artifacts/prompts.json --model-tag redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01 \
    --quant-profile qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2 --seed 20260209-42 --out /artifacts/replay_result.json

- Checking a provenance record: (jq-friendly example)
  aws s3 cp s3://eval-artifacts/2026/redwood-small-7b/epl-2026-000124/metadata.yaml - | yq e . - && jq .metrics_summary replay_result.json

Security and signing
- All EPL records for canary or promoted runs MUST be signed by the eval-runner service using the eval-harness key.
- Access to artifact buckets requires role-based ACLs: read for platform and model-onboarding; write only by eval-harness service principal.

Governance and review cadence
- Every quarter, the model-onboarding and quant teams run a review of promoted EPL records and collect lessons into a quarterly migration report.
- Any promoted quant profile with two or more production incidents in a quarter must be paused and triaged under the cross-team incident process.

Appendix: Example queries and dashboards
- Minimal dashboard panels to create in Grafana:
  - "EPL Promotions": count of promoted=true by week, filterable by model_suite and quant_profile_version.
  - "Embedding Stability Heatmap": avg embedding_stability by probe_set_id and quant_profile_version.
  - "Runtime Fingerprint Error Correlation": time-series of functioncall_error_rate annotated with runtime_bin_sha changes.

- Helpful index queries (Elasticsearch-style):
  POST /epl-index/_search
  {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"runtime_bin_sha": "sha256:4f9a8e..."}}, {"range": {"timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d/d"}}}]}}}

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (Applied ML - Eval Harness)
- Secondary: Diego Morales (Model Onboarding)
- Oncall escalation: see /oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process for paging details.

Change log
- 2026-01-12: Draft created (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-01-28: Added signing and storage constraints (reviewer: Maya Chen).
- 2026-02-10: Added rollout acceptance numbers and automation-triggered rollback rules (reviewer: Liam O'Connor).

Related references
- quant-profile registry: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles (internal index)
- model catalog tagging guidelines: /product-docs/requirements/model-catalog-tagging
- regression triage runbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026

If you are implementing EPL emission in a new eval runner, open a PR that includes: schema validation tests, signing integration, and at least one sample metadata.yaml for a real probe run.

payload.page_title: Eval Budget Ledger and Cost Attribution Framework

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Eval Budget Ledger: a lightweight, canonical accounting model and operational framework for tracking, attributing, and governing the cost of evaluation work (shadow runs, probes, synthetic workloads, and human review) across the eval harness. It standardizes cost buckets, attribution rules, reporting artifacts, and a minimal runbook for triaging unexpected spend. The ledger enables reproducible cost rollups for feature teams, platform owners, and finance.

Goals
-----
- Provide a single source-of-truth CSV/JSON artifact (the ledger) for every eval campaign.
- Define deterministic attribution rules to map compute, human labeling, and storage costs to owning teams and probes.
- Enable near-real-time spend dashboards and budget alerts tied to probes, model variants, and environments (shadow/staging/prod).
- Reduce surprise spend from large synthetic sweeps and regression investigations; support pre-commit budget gating.

Definitions
-----------
- Probe: An atomic evaluation input or workload slice submitted to the eval harness.
- Campaign: A collection of probes executed as part of a single objective (e.g., shadow rollout of model-v2, quantization stress sweep).
- Ledger row: A single line in the canonical CSV representing cost attribution for one probe execution.

Ledger schema (CSV columns)
--------------------------
The ledger is produced by the eval orchestrator after each batch and stored in S3 and the eval index. Each ledger row is CSV with these columns (pipe-delimited in examples below for readability):

- ledger_id (string): UUID for the row.
- campaign_id (string): stable id for the campaign.
- probe_id (string): stable id for the probe.
- model_variant (string): e.g., redwood/gptx-8b-q4_latest.
- environment (string): shadow|staging|prod.
- start_ts (ISO8601): run start time.
- end_ts (ISO8601): run end time.
- compute_seconds (float): wall-clock GPU/CPU seconds consumed attributed to this probe.
- gpu_type (string): e.g., A100-80GB, L4x.
- memory_gb_seconds (float): memory usage * seconds (for cross-instance memory costs).
- tokens_in (int): input tokens.
- tokens_out (int): output tokens.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (float): fraction for reuse-based discounts.
- human_label_seconds (float): paid human reviewer seconds attributable.
- storage_gb_months_fraction (float): short-lived artifact storage prorated to run.
- infra_cost_usd (float): computed infra cost allocated to row (see cost model).
- human_cost_usd (float): human labeling cost.
- total_cost_usd (float): infra_cost_usd + human_cost_usd + amortized tooling.
- owning_team (string): team slug owning the campaign (e.g., search-platform).
- billing_tag (string): optional billing tag for downstream finance mapping.
- notes (string): free text for special adjustments or credits.

Cost model and attribution rules
--------------------------------
1) Compute pricing table (example):

| resource | unit | nominal_price_usd | comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A100-80GB | per GPU-hour | 3.20 | spot pricing baseline for eval fleet |
| L4x | per GPU-hour | 1.10 | cheaper short-live experiments |
| vCPU | per vCPU-hour | 0.05 | for non-GPU workloads |
| RAM | per GB-hour | 0.002 | memory charge for long-running jobs |

2) Compute allocation: infra_cost_usd = sum(resource_seconds * price_per_unit_hour / 3600) adjusted by kv_cache discount. For probes that benefit from prefix/KV cache, apply a KV discount factor: cost *= (1 - kv_cache_hit_ratio * kv_cache_savings). Default kv_cache_savings = 0.45.

3) Human labeling: human_cost_usd = human_label_seconds * human_rate_usd_per_second. Default human_rate_usd_per_second = 0.004 (equivalent to $14.4/hour for contractor labeling).

4) Storage and tooling amortization: short-lived artifacts (replays, logs) are prorated and summed into storage_gb_months_fraction * storage_unit_price_usd. Tooling and infra overhead (e.g., eval queue, orchestrator overhead) is allocated to rows as a percent uplift (default 5%) and recorded in notes.

Ownership and governance rules
------------------------------
- Campaign owner (owning_team) is responsible for setting a campaign budget and tagging critical probes with high-priority flags.
- Platform (eval-harness) owns the compute_price table and publishing weekly baseline rates to the ledger generator.
- Finance owns final mapping of billing_tag to GL codes.

Operational artifacts and examples
--------------------------------

sections.body:

123e4567|camp-202602|probe-009|redwood/gptx-8b-q4|shadow|2026-02-10T14:02:03Z|2026-02-10T14:02:09Z|6.1|A100-80GB|49.6|152|420|0.38|0.0|0.00002|0.0054|0.0000|0.0054|search-platform|GL-APPL-011|kv-cache applied

Quick CLI to produce per-campaign rollup (example SQL using ledger table):
1) Per-campaign cost: SELECT campaign_id, SUM(total_cost_usd) AS campaign_cost_usd, COUNT(DISTINCT probe_id) AS probes FROM eval_ledger WHERE start_ts >= '2026-02-01' AND environment = 'shadow' GROUP BY campaign_id;
2) Team allocation: SELECT owning_team, SUM(total_cost_usd) FROM eval_ledger WHERE start_ts >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY owning_team;

Budget gating and alerting
-------------------------
- Preflight: campaign owners must declare a soft_budget_usd before launching non-trivial campaigns (> $5000 expected). The orchestrator rejects submission without a soft_budget or explicit approval for campaigns estimated > $25,000.
- Alerts: platform publishes per-campaign and per-team burn-rate metrics to Grafana. Alert thresholds: 50% of soft_budget (warning), 85% (action required), 100% (auto-pause candidate).
- Auto-pause policy: When a campaign crosses 100% and has no explicit approve_overage tag, orchestrator moves non-critical jobs to paused state and notifies owners via Slack and email. Critical jobs (marked critical=true) continue but generate P0 paged messages to the campaign owner.

Runbook: Investigating an unexpected spike
-----------------------------------------
1) Identify the campaign(s) with increased burn (Grafana or ledger query).
2) Drill into probe-level ledger rows for top-K cost contributors: SELECT probe_id, model_variant, sum(total_cost_usd) FROM eval_ledger WHERE campaign_id = 'camp-202602' GROUP BY probe_id ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 50;
3) Check model_variant token stats and kv_cache_hit_ratio: sudden token_out increases or cache_hit drops are common causes.
4) If compute_seconds look anomalous, check orchestration logs for retries or timeouts (orchestrator/job-runner). If human_cost spikes, check labeling batch sizes or misconfigured annotator pools.
5) If budget was exhausted and auto-pause triggered, owners should: a) mark urgent probes as critical if necessary; b) request funding via the campaign's Jira billing request; c) schedule a short review to adjust probe sampling.

Integration notes
-----------------
- The ledger writer is integrated into the eval-orchestrator post-processing stage (hook: /eval/orchestrator/postprocess->ledger-writer).
- A small shim (ledger-normalizer) converts raw runtime traces into the ledger schema and applies price tables fetched from SSM periodically.
- For Private deployments, the ledger generator accepts a custom pricing file and billing_tag mapping. Private deployments must opt-in to sending ledgers to Redwood; default retention is 90 days unless overridden by customer contract.

Rollout plan
------------
1) Q1 2026: pilot with three product teams (search-platform, chat-core, insights) using a nightly shadow campaign.
2) Q2 2026: add automated preflight enforcement and Grafana dashboards; finance mapping for billing_tag.
3) Q3 2026: enforce soft_budget for all campaigns over $2,000; export periodic reports to cost-center owners.

Metrics to monitor
------------------
- Daily eval spend (USD) - global and per-team.
- 7d rolling average cost per probe and cost per 1k tokens.
- Top-50 probes by cost (weekly).
- Fraction of campaigns with declared soft_budget.

Open questions and future work
-----------------------------
- Incorporate token-based QoS pricing (discounts for batched micro-inference).
- Experiment with dynamic kv_cache_savings per-model instead of a fixed default.
- Better human cost modeling for in-house vs vendor labelers.

Appendix: sample Python snippet (ledger row enrichment)
------------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Example ledger row (CSV)

sections.body:
from datetime import datetime
import uuid

def compute_infra_cost(gpu_seconds, gpu_type, kv_hit_ratio, price_table, kv_savings=0.45):
    base_hour_price = price_table[gpu_type]
    cost = gpu_seconds / 3600.0 * base_hour_price
    cost *= (1 - kv_hit_ratio * kv_savings)
    return round(cost, 6)

row = {
    'ledger_id': str(uuid.uuid4()),
    'campaign_id': 'camp-202602',
    'probe_id': 'probe-009',
    'model_variant': 'redwood/gptx-8b-q4',
    'environment': 'shadow',
    'start_ts': datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z'
}

FAQ
---
Q: How are cross-team shared probes charged?
A: The campaign owner selects a billing_tag and can add split percentages to rows (stored in notes). We recommend assigning shared probes to a platform cost pool (owning_team: platform) and then splitting via internal chargebacks in finance.

Q: Can customers running private deployments see per-probe costs?
A: Yes; private deployments can opt-in and provide a custom price table. Ledger output is identical but stored in the customer's S3.

Contact and ownership
---------------------
- Doc owner: Priya Kapoor (applied-ml infra).
- Platform contact (ledger implementation): Miguel Torres.
- Finance contact (cost mappings): Dianne Wu.

payload.page_title: Latency-Quality Slice Optimizer Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a repeatable, slice-driven evaluation and promotion workflow that balances latency SLOs and output quality when deploying quantized or heterogeneous model variants.
- Reduce regressions by combining targeted slice benchmarking, telemetry contracts, and automated gating.

Scope and audience
- Applies to model onboarding, private and dedicated deployments, and hosted canary rollouts.
- Intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and product owners.

Definitions
- slice: a named subset of production traffic grouped by intent, length, or feature flags.
- latency SLO: 95th percentile server-side model generation latency budget for a route.
- quality delta: measured expected change in task-specific metric vs baseline model.

Key SLOs and thresholds
- Global production latency SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for interactive text routes.
- Quantized candidate guardrail: quality delta <= 2.5% relative drop on primary slice metric OR absolute metric delta defined per slice.
- Regression alarm: any slice with quality drop > 5% or p95 latency increase > 30% triggers immediate rollback.

Slice catalog (example)
- onboarding-guidance: short instruction following prompts, expected median tokens 12. Primary metric: accuracy@top1.
- long-context-support: multi-turn doc summarization, median tokens 1200. Primary metric: coherence score.
- embeddings-search-q: short queries for vector similarity, median tokens 8. Primary metric: embedding cosine stability.
- api-batch-worker: high-throughput noninteractive batch calls. Primary metric: throughput and tail latency.

Telemetry and signals required
1) Per-slice quality metrics (task metric, confidence distribution, top-k disagreement).
2) Per-slice latency histogram and p50/p95/p99.
3) Token economy: generation tokens and input tokens per request.
4) Feature tags: model variant id, quant profile id, hardware type, route id.
5) Drift indicators: prompt fingerprint rate change, anchor-response divergence.

Evaluation harness configuration examples
- When adding a new candidate, create a harness job with the following attributes:
  - deterministic seed sets for 3 replicate runs
  - slice weightings matching production traffic fractions or importance weights
  - synthetic amplification for rare slices until N=500 example coverage

YAML snippet for an eval job (illustrative)
```
job_name: latency_quality_slice_eval
model_variant: candidate-v2
replicates: 3
slices:
  - name: onboarding-guidance
    weight: 0.35
  - name: long-context-support
    weight: 0.25
  - name: embeddings-search-q
    weight: 0.25
  - name: api-batch-worker
    weight: 0.15
metrics:
  - name: primary_task_metric
    compare: relative
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    compare: absolute
augmentation:
  rare_slice_min_examples: 500
```

Promotion gating and automated policy (high level)
1. Run harness with baseline model and candidate concurrently. Produce per-slice report with confidence intervals and p95 latency.
2. Apply gate rules in order: safety checks -> latency gates -> quality gates -> cost appreciations.
3. If all gates pass, schedule canary rollout with 5% traffic for 4 hours and expanded telemetry retention.
4. If any gate fails, run targeted regression triage (see Runbook) and block promotion until triage resolves causes and a new candidate is evaluated.

Gate examples
- Safety checks: zero high-severity safety sentinel hits across 3 replicates.
- Latency gate: p95(candidate) <= max( p95(baseline) * 1.15, absolute_slo )
- Quality gate: per-slice primary_task_metric delta >= -2.5% for critical slices, >= -5% for noncritical slices.

Regression triage runbook (summary)
1. Triage kickoff: create incident in tracker, tag model id and quant profile. Notify owner_team and oncall.
2. Reproduce: run harness with failing slice example set and deterministic seed. Capture full token-level diffs and KV-cache traces.
3. Isolate: compare candidate vs baseline on short micro-benchmarks: 1) tokenizer alignment, 2) decoding detokenized mismatch, 3) top-k logit shifts.
4. Test hardware sensitivity: replay eval on alternate device types and with and without kernel fallback.
5. If quantization suspected: run full-precision shadow and mixed-precision variants to narrow failure mode.
6. Repair options: prompt rewrite, quant profile relax, small fine-tune, or rollback. Document chosen remediation path and validation evidence.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples
- Trigger a slice evaluation run: rci eval run --job latency_quality_slice_eval --model candidate-v2 --slices onboarding-guidance,long-context-support
- Fetch per-slice report: rci eval report --job-id 0xabc123 --format table
- Promote to canary: rci rollout create --model candidate-v2 --percent 5 --duration 4h --observability retention=72h

Operational best practices
- Keep slice definitions small and orthogonal: prefer intent-based slices over ad hoc query buckets.
- Maintain a slice ownership map and ensure one owner per slice.
- Refresh rare-slice seed sets monthly or when production distribution changes > 10%.
- Archive long-context examples with token boundaries and session context to enable deterministic replay.

Ownership and escalation
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Eval Platform team (contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai).
- Primary oncall: eval-platform-sre rotation.
- Escalation: after 30 minutes unresolved, escalate to runtime-performance team lead and product owner.

References and related artifacts
- See evaluation orchestration policy and quant profile synthesis doc in related pages for integration details.
- Repository: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness (eval job templates and YAML schemas).

Change log
- 2026-01-18: initial draft and adoption for Q1 model promotions.
- 2026-02-12: tightened latency gate formula and added rare slice amplification guidance.

Appendix: example slice acceptance table
- For each slice provide: slice_name, primary_metric, acceptance_threshold, p95_latency_threshold, owner. Maintain this table in the slice registry.

End of document

payload.page_title: Telemetry-driven Eval Prioritization and Hotspot Triage

sections.body:
Summary
This document describes a telemetry-first system for prioritizing offline and online evaluation jobs and a structured hotspot triage playbook for high-impact model behavior regressions. It targets the evaluator orchestration layer and SRE/Applied-ML engineers who run and act on model quality telemetry for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Motivation
- The eval backlog grows faster than evaluation capacity. Manual triage leads to missed regressions and wasted compute on low-impact slices.
- Telemetry (production errors, user rejections, SLA anomalies) is an early indicator of quality regressions but needs automated translation into eval work.
- We need a deterministic, auditable prioritization pipeline that: (1) converts telemetry to eval tasks, (2) assigns cost-aware priority, and (3) feeds actionable triage runbooks to on-call and ML engineers.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Surface the top-K evaluation tasks that reduce user-impact most per compute dollar.
  - Ensure high-recall capture of hotspots without overwhelming evaluators.
  - Provide an operator-facing triage checklist with concrete rollback/fallback actions.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a model promotion gate (that remains the model-onboarding pipeline).
  - It does not supersede security or privacy reviews for customer data.

Principles
1) Signal-first: prioritize signals with clear business impact (error rates, retention drops, user-text flags).
2) Cost-awareness: include token/throughput cost estimates in prioritization.
3) Explainability: each prioritized eval job must include the telemetry-derived rationale and suggested slices.
4) Fast feedback: support micro-canaries and quick smoke evals (<30m) before full-scale runs.

Telemetry signals (inputs)
- Production traces: streaming error labels (500-series), latency p99/p50 spikes, timeouts.
- User feedback: explicit thumbs-down, A/B experiment metrics (CTR/retention deltas).
- Quality analytics: semantic drift detectors, embedding-distance anomalies, stability score drops.
- Routing & capacity: fallback events (requests routed to cheaper model variants).

Signal enrichment steps
1) Attach context: request metadata (model version, route, top-k prompts), tenant_id, and sequence length buckets.
2) Cluster related events: temporal proximity (5–15m windows), similar prompt fingerprints (edit distance or embedding cosine > 0.92).
3) Score impact: compute an impact score (0–100) combining user count, error severity, and retention delta.

Priority scoring algorithm (overview)
- Inputs: impact_score, estimated_eval_cost (core-hours or token-cost), urgency_multiplier (customer SLA tier), seasonality_factor.
- Priority = (impact_score * urgency_multiplier * seasonality_factor) / (1 + log(1 + estimated_eval_cost))
- Normalization: scale to 0–100 and bucket into: critical (>80), high (60–80), medium (30–60), low (<30).

Eval task generation
1) Auto-slice suggestion: generate 3–7 candidate slices using clustering (intent, length, locale, prompt-token prefix).
2) Quick smoke: spawn a 30m micro-eval on a 500–2k sample (approx 5–20k tokens) to confirm signal.
3) Full evaluation: if smoke fails, schedule full eval with stratified sampling across traffic segments.

Hotspot triage playbook (operator steps)
1) Acknowledge: Owner (on-call ML or SRE) acknowledges the prioritized task in the evaluation dashboard within 30 minutes for critical tasks.
2) Run smoke eval: launch the micro-sample smoke eval. If pass -> mark as false-positive and document reasoning.
3) If smoke fails: run a targeted full eval job and fetch comparison baselines (previous model version and quantized variant).
4) Determine root cause categories (choose one primary):
   - Model drift / distribution shift
   - Quantization-induced degradation
   - Serving KV-cache/latency artifact
   - Prompt-processing bug (pre/post-processing mismatch)
   - Data corruption / formatting errors
5) For each root cause, follow the remediation checklist below.

Remediation checklists (short)
- Model drift:
  - Compare top-k token distributions and embedding centroids versus baseline.
  - Re-run eval with increased context/contextual shots.
  - If confirmed, create model-promotion hold ticket; notify product and release manager.
- Quantization-induced degradation:
  - Re-run on full-precision replica and mixed-precision replicas.
  - If degradation isolated to q4/q8 profile, revert to higher-fidelity profile for affected routes and open quant-team ticket.
- KV-cache / latency artifact:
  - Check per-token latency, cache hit rates, and request-shard mapping.
  - Warm caches for affected routes and schedule a controlled roll-forward.
- Prompt-processing bug:
  - Replay raw request through offline preprocessing; compare outputs.
  - Patch preprocessor and deploy a canary.
- Data corruption:
  - Validate ingestion pipelines and normalization; block bad batches and backfill missing fields.

Escalation and rollback policy
- Critical priority: if a full eval shows regression (>5% degradations on primary metric for top-tier customers), perform an emergency rollback to the last certified model and notify Incident Response.
- High priority: consider partial route-level fallback to a previous variant; schedule a postmortem if rollback is performed.

Operational configurations (table)
| Config name | Default | Range | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke_eval_sample_size | 1000 | 500–5000 | sample count for micro-evaluations |
| smoke_eval_duration | 30m | 5m–120m | duration limit before automatic cancel |
| eval_cost_threshold_usd | 200 | 50–2000 | above threshold requires manager approval |
| critical_priority_threshold | 80 | 70–100 | score threshold for critical routing |
| max_parallel_smoke_jobs | 20 | 1–100 | global concurrency cap |

Automation and tooling hooks
- Orchestration: eval-orch service (internal) integrates with telemetry bus and can enqueue tasks into the evaluator fleet.
- Dashboard: "Eval Hotspots" view shows live prioritized queue, rationale, sample prompts, and quick-run buttons.
- CLI examples:
  - Queue a micro-smoke: evalctl run --slice-id S12345 --mode smoke --sample 1000
  - Fetch rationale: evalctl show --task T98765 --rationale

Metrics and SLOs for the pipeline
- Time to acknowledge (critical): 30 minutes (target 90th percentile).
- Time to smoke result: 45 minutes from enqueue (including scheduling).
- False positive rate for prioritized tasks: <20% (measured quarterly).
- Coverage: >95% of telemetry events with impact_score >= 40 must surface a prioritized eval job or a documented suppression rule.

Ownership and contact list
- Primary owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team lead: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime Reliability (team lead: Miguel Santos)
- Pager rotations and on-call: see /confluence/eng-oncall/oncall-rotations for links.

Audit and compliance notes
- All eval jobs spawned from customer traffic must log the minimal request fingerprint and must not store PII in evaluation payloads. The eval-orch enforces scrubbing policies described in the privacy contract.

Appendix: example prioritized payload (human-readable)
- Alert ID: ALERT-2026-1421
- Rationale: p99 latency spike for route /chat/stream; 12k impacted users, 0.7% retention drop over 1h window
- Suggested slices: long-context > 1024 tokens, locale: en-US, intent: summarization
- Estimated eval cost: $340 (full), $28 (smoke)
- Priority score: 87 (critical)

Related work and references
- See evaluator interchange format and federation spec for task serialization.
- See drift detection and embedding stability guidelines for signal extraction patterns.

Revision history
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft by Eleanor Ruiz.
- 2026-02-10: Added smoke eval parameters and CLI examples (reviewers: Miguel Santos).
- 2026-03-01: Published after review; added escalation thresholds and audit notes.

payload.page_title: Distribution Stability Eval and Response Playbook

sections.body: This playbook describes Redwood's standardized process for evaluating distribution stability (inputs, embeddings, outputs) and the operational response for detected deviations. It is intended to connect evaluation harness outputs, production telemetry, and remediation actions so teams can act consistently across model types and deployment modes.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Applied ML engineers maintaining model quality
- SREs and platform engineers managing observability and alerts
- Owner teams performing model rollouts and post-deployment verification
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- Detect meaningful distribution changes with low false-positive rate
- Maintain model calibration within expected bounds for customer-facing metrics
- Provide automated safe mitigations and clear handoffs for human investigation
sections.heading: High-level goals

sections.body:
- Token-level PSI: alert if PSI > 0.25 over 24h window
- Embedding median cosine shift: alert if median shift > 0.08 over 1h window
- Token KL divergence: alert if KL > 0.5 on sampled prompts
- Scalar calibration gap: alert if absolute gap > 0.06 on labeled validation tasks
- Feedback-derived error rate: alert if 7-day rolling error-rate > 2x baseline
- Traffic anomalies: 3-sigma change in route traffic or sudden spike in latency
sections.heading: Core signals we monitor (defaults)

sections.body:
1) Scheduled stress evaluations: the eval-harness runs daily stress sweeps and produces artifacts (sampled prompts, metrics CSVs, and summary HTML). These artifacts are uploaded to s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/date/.
2) Shadow sampling: during rollouts, the harness collects 14-day shadow traffic and computes baseline distributions to register with the model registry.
3) Scenario suites: teams author scenario YAMLs that the harness runs to simulate edge cases; scenario outputs are stored alongside baseline artifacts.
sections.heading: How the eval-harness integrates

sections.body:
- Aggregation windows: 1h for embedding medians, 4h for token-level checks, 24h for PSI and calibration summaries.
- Sampling policy: default 1% of traffic for embeddings snapshots; up to 10% for flagged routes. Prioritize enterprise tenants and newly introduced route_tags.
- Storage & retention: raw sampled embeddings in Parquet (hourly), aggregated metrics in ClickHouse (90-day TTL), and full harness artifacts preserved for 90 days in S3.
sections.heading: Signal computation and aggregation

sections.body:
- PSI with adaptive bucketing for token categories and prompt length buckets.
- Median cosine shift with trimmed mean to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
- KL divergence for token outputs computed on stratified prompt sets.
- MMD with RBF kernel on embeddings for workloads with continuous shifts.
- Confidence calibration metrics: ECE (expected calibration error) and class-wise calibration for classification-like tasks.
sections.heading: Detectors and algorithms (recommended set)

sections.body:
- Warning (P2): metric exceeds investigation threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.15) but under page threshold. Logged to Slack channel with link to harness artifact.
- Page (P1): metric exceeds page threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.25 OR calibration gap > 0.06) and impacts high-priority tenant or high-traffic route. Triggers PagerDuty.
- Critical (P0): sustained degradation for >4 hours, customer-facing failures, or safety guardrail violations. Requires immediate cross-team war room.
sections.heading: Alert lifecycle and severity classification

sections.body:
1) Confirm alert details and sampling window. Attach harness artifact and recent sampled inputs.
2) SRE: validate system health (latency, error rates, GPU/memory utilization, recent deploys).
3) Applied-ML owner: review sample outputs in the harness UI and check calibration dashboard.
4) If correlated with recent deploy, consider immediate rollback or traffic-pin to previous version.
5) If systemic input shift (e.g., sudden change in prompt shape), update sampling filters and tag incident for retraining consideration.
sections.heading: First-response checklist (0-30 minutes)

sections.body:
- Traffic pin: rollback traffic split to previous model_version for impacted routes for up to 2 hours unless manually cleared.
- Apply latest-calibration: post-hoc calibration transform can be injected in runtime for scalar outputs if artifact exists and owner approves.
- Fallback model route: switch to conservative model variant when safety guardrail triggers.
- Throttle non-critical routes: reduce background sampling and batch sizes to preserve capacity.
sections.heading: Automated mitigations (safe-by-default)

sections.body:
- If calibration plus small corrective data does not restore metrics in 72 hours, plan for targeted fine-tuning.
- Sample requirement guidance: collect minimum 5k validated examples for small distribution shifts; 20k+ for broader domain shifts. Prioritize label quality and tenant representation.
- Retraining options: domain-adaptive fine-tuning, LoRA-style adapters, or retrieval-augmented fine-tuning depending on task and data characteristics.

Onboarding checklist for new model versions (minimum gating):
- Telemetry schema validated and test messages flowing into telemetry topics.
- 14-day shadow evaluation via eval-harness with stress scenarios executed.
- Baseline distributions and calibration artifacts registered in the model registry.
- Drift detectors configured and initial thresholds set; PagerDuty routing updated with owner contacts.
sections.heading: When to retrain or fine-tune

sections.body:
- Run a daily stress sweep: redwood-eval-harness run stress-sweep --model {model_version} --suite default --out s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/
- Generate a drift report: redwood-eval-harness report-drift --model {model_version} --window 24h --algorithms psi,median-embedding,kl --out ./drift-report.pdf
- Inspect last calibration artifact: redwood-model-registry get-calibration --model {model_version} --latest
sections.heading: Example commands and quick references

sections.body:
- Primary: applied-ml oncall (applied-ml@redwood.com) — analysis, calibration artifacts, scenario ownership.
- Platform/SRE: eng-sre oncall (eng-sre@redwood.com) — telemetry, alerting, and rollback automation.
- Product/security: looped in for high-impact or regulated-customer incidents.
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation contacts

sections.body:
- Postmortem required within 7 days for incidents that triggered manual mitigation or customer impact. The postmortem must include timeline, root cause hypothesis, sample artifacts, corrective actions, and updated thresholds.
- Store postmortem artifacts under /incidents/distribution-stability/{incident_id}/ and link to model registry entry.
sections.heading: Post-incident workflow

sections.body:
- Quarterly stability drills: run a simulated shift (synthetic prompts + embedding perturbation) and validate detection time and false positive rate.
- Monthly threshold review: applied-ml and eng-sre review detector thresholds for top 10 models by traffic.

Appendix: decision heuristics summary:
- If metric is marginally above threshold but no customer impact: monitor and increase sampling for 24h.
- If correlated with new deploy: prefer rollback + forensic harness run over immediate retraining.
- If calibration-only fix succeeds: publish new calibration artifact and monitor for 72h before closing incident.
sections.heading: Maintenance and exercises

sections.body:
- 2025-09-20: Created (Diego Alvarez)
- 2025-11-12: Added severity tiers and automated mitigation policies (Priya Nair)
- 2026-01-28: Updated sampling guidance and onboarding checklist (Jared Lim)

payload.page_title: Cohort-aware priming and probe generator handbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document describes the Cohort-Aware Priming (CAP) probe generator: a reproducible pipeline for synthesizing evaluation probes that reflect live runtime cohorts, prioritize quantization compatibility checks, and produce compact, high-value probe bundles for continuous validation and regression triage. The goal is to make probes that mirror the actual mix of requests hitting Redwood inference so that we surface regressions that matter to customers.

Goals
-----
- Reduce false positives from generic probe suites by conditioning probes on runtime cohorts.
- Prioritize probes that stress quantized execution paths and KV-cache interactions.
- Produce stable probe fingerprints that can be replayed across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.
- Enable automated gating rules tied to measurable deltas (coherence, embedding drift, latency).

Terminology
-----------
- Cohort: a grouping of requests sharing runtime telemetry signatures (e.g., avg tokens, model variant, user-intent tag).
- Priming: minimal context added to a probe so the model follows a schema (few-shot examples, system instructions).
- Probe bundle: a curated set of input prompts + expected signal assertions used by the eval harness.
- Quant-compat probe: probe designed to exercise quantized code paths and mixed-precision fallbacks.

Design overview
---------------
1) Telemetry fingerprinting: sample production traces (anonymized) to compute cohort signatures: sequence length distribution, function-call rate, KV-cache hit-rate proxy, and predominant model family.
2) Cohort selection policy: use stratified sampling to choose top N cohorts by traffic (default N=6) plus two long-tail cohorts by entropy score.
3) Probe synthesis: for each cohort, generate probe families: surface-form probes (user utterances), structural probes (table generation, JSON output), and guardrail probes (safety/PII checks). Each probe is primed using cohort-specific fewshots and context length that mirrors the cohort’s median.
4) Quant conditioning: augment ~30% of each cohort's probes with quant-compat scaffolding (edge priming, tokenized adversarial sequences, tiled sparse attention patterns) to stress quant kernels.
5) Validation & fingerprinting: execute probes across a baseline (float) binary and candidate quant/configurations; capture metrics and hash fingerprints for result stability tracking.

Probe generator pipeline (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
1. Extract telemetry snapshot: run `probe-gen collect` for a 24-hour window. Output: telemetry_fingerprint.csv.
2. Construct cohorts: `probe-gen cohortize --top 6 --entropy-longtail 2 --out cohorts.yaml`.
3. Synthesize seed prompts per cohort: `probe-gen synth --cohorts cohorts.yaml --variants 200 --quant-augment 0.3`.
4. Filter duplicates & canonicalize: `probe-gen normalize --dedup --tokenize-bpe`.
5. Bake probe bundles: `probe-gen package --format evbundle --out /artifacts/probes/<date>/`.

Configuration example (evbundle manifest)
----------------------------------------
A minimal evbundle manifest used by the eval harness: (JSON shown as text)

```
{
  "bundle_name": "cap-2026-01-20",
  "cohort": "assistant-longcontext-1",
  "seed_model": "redwood/rlhf-45b-v2",
  "probe_count": "320",
  "quant_aug_percent": "30",
  "assertions": ["coherence_score", "embedding_cos_sim", "token_growth", "latency_p99"]
}
```

Validation matrix (table)
-------------------------
| Metric               | Check type       | Baseline threshold | Allowed delta | Action on breach |
|----------------------|------------------|--------------------|---------------|------------------|
| Coherence (C-score)  | semantic         | >=0.93             | -0.03         | Block rollout, open regression ticket |
| Embedding drift      | numeric (cos)    | >=0.96             | -0.02         | Run embedding-rebase job |
| Latency P99 (ms)     | perf             | <=200              | +40ms         | Notify infra, canary to lower tier |
| Token growth         | cost             | <=1.12x            | +0.08x        | Toggle prompt condensation heuristics |
| Quant fuzziness rate | fidelity         | <=2.5%             | +1.0%         | Mark suspect, increase label budget |

Metric definitions and capture notes
------------------------------------
- Coherence (C-score): aggregate of semantic-similarity (BERTScore/embedding) and task-specific pass rate normalized to [0,1]. Compute over 3 random seeds to reduce variance.
- Embedding drift: mean cosine similarity between baseline embeddings and candidate. Use anchored reference set maintained in S3 `s3://redwood-eval/anchors/`.
- Quant fuzziness rate: percent of probes where candidate output deviates from baseline beyond semantic threshold AND changes tokenization length by >5%.

Gating and rollout policy
------------------------
1. Local validation: every probe bundle must pass local smoke (10% of probes) against float baseline with no regressions.
2. Shadow canary: deploy candidate in shadow across 2% of traffic shaped to selected cohorts. Collect probe metrics for 48 hours.
3. Automatic gate rules (examples):
   - If Coherence delta < -0.02 and quant_fuzziness > 3% -> FAIL
   - If Latency P99 increases by >30ms but coherence delta >= -0.01 -> ALERT (manual triage)
   - If Embedding drift > 0.03 -> RUN embedding-rebase workflow and block rollout until reviewed
4. Escalation: fail gates create a ticket in #eval-regressions with prefilled diagnostics and links to artifact bundles.

Operational runbook (when a CAP probe bundle flags a regression)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Triage lead (owner: applied-ml-evals) acknowledges within 1 business hour.
2. Attach failing probe bundle and run `eval-harness replay --bundle <id> --compare baseline`. Collect full traces.
3. Classify failure: perf | quant | prompt-priming | data-shift. Use the taxonomy in the "failure-classifier" tool.
4. If quant-related: run rerun with higher precision fallback and per-layer logging: `runtime-debug --quant-logging on --layers all`.
5. If primordial prompt-priming issue: regenerate priming with expanded examples and re-run 100-sample smoke.
6. Apply short-term mitigation: automatic fallback to float or alternative model variant per the rollout policy.
7. Long-term action: open ADR if recurring across 3 releases or a customer-facing incident triggers SLA.

Example probes (illustrative)
----------------------------
- Surface-form: a user asks for multi-step plan with a 2048-token context and two function calls. Priming includes system instruction to prefer structured JSON output.
- Structural: generate a 12-row markdown table with nested bullet items; checks include exact-table-shape assertion.
- Quant-compat: adversarial tokenization sequence (e.g., long repeated unicode blocks) to force kernel path divergence.

Sample CLI session
------------------
$ probe-gen collect --window 24h --out tele_snapshot.csv
$ probe-gen cohortize --in tele_snapshot.csv --top 6 --out cohorts.yaml
$ probe-gen synth --cohorts cohorts.yaml --variants 150 --quant-augment 0.3 --out /tmp/cap-bundle

Notes on privacy and production data
-----------------------------------
- Telemetry snapshots MUST be anonymized: remove user IDs, IPs, and redact PII from prompts. Use `telemetry-redact v2` before running cohortize.
- Long-tail cohorts sample less frequently but may contain more safety-sensitive probes; route those bundles through the safety sandbox before any automated gating.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: Applied ML & Evals (team alias: applied-ml-evals@redwood.internal)
- Oncall/triage: eval-oncall rotation (see /confluence/people-ops for schedule)
- Infra/Runtime contact: runtime-kernel@redwood.internal

Review cadence and maintenance
-----------------------------
- Probe bundles are regenerated weekly for high-traffic cohorts and monthly for long-tail cohorts.
- Reviewers should audit the quant-augmentation heuristics quarterly and update the `quant-compat` template if kernel changes occur.

Appendix: quick heuristics for probe prioritization
--------------------------------------------------
- Rank probes by (expected unit-cost * failure-impact). Failure-impact is estimated from customer-facing features touched by the cohort.
- Prefer compact probe families (<= 400 tokens) for latency-focused cohorts; prefer longcontext probes for memory/KV-cache cohorts.

Related artifacts and links
-------------------------
- Ev-harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Quant shadow playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026
- Telemetry redaction tool: git+ssh://git.redwood/internal/telemetry-redact

Change log
----------
- 2025-12-15: Created initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2026-01-20: Formalized gating thresholds and added quant-conditioning section (reviewers: Anika Rao, Diego Morales)

payload.page_title: SLO-driven eval gating and quantization handoff playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines an SLO-driven gating strategy for automated evaluation pipelines and prescribes the operational handoff for quantized model artifacts into shadow and production-serving lanes. The goal is to prevent quantization or performance regressions from reaching customers while enabling fast, reproducible promotion for models that meet both quality and latency/cost objectives.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all model promotions that include a quantized artifact (int8, 4-bit, hybrid-mixed precision) or runtime kernel/packing changes.
- Covers: automated eval gates (pre-promotion), manual triage escalation, shadow deployment gating, and final rollout controls.
- Excludes security-only certification (handled by security-and-compliance).
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Eval Gate: A checkpoint in the CI/eval pipeline that requires pass/fail criteria before artifacts move downstream.
- Promotion Candidate: A model version + quant artifact produced by the quantization pipeline.
- Shadow Lane: Isolated serving environment with production-like traffic for fidelity and performance validation.
- Delta SLO: The allowed deviation from baseline for a given metric (e.g., -1.5% mean accuracy).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
| Metric                        | Baseline (prod model) | Allowed Delta (gate) | Action on breach       | Monitoring source           |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Mean ROUGE / BLEU / F1        | 0.78                  | -0.015               | Block promotion        | eval-summaries, slices API  |
| Latency P95 (ms)              | 180                   | +40ms                | Block promotion        | perf-traces, runtime-metrics|
| Token cost / 1k tokens (USD)  | 0.032                 | +10%                 | Warn + require signoff    | cost-ledger                 |
| Response Stability Index (RSI)| 0.94                  | -0.02                | Block promotion        | stability-service           |
| Functioncall success rate     | 99.6%                 | -0.5%                | Manual triage            | functioncall-metrics       |
sections.heading: SLO matrix (examples)

sections.body:
1. Unit-level evals (fast): run on PR; must pass regression sentinel tests and tokenization sanity checks. Failure: block PR merge.
2. Slice-level evals (medium): run in CI-eval cluster against prioritized slice set (latency-sensitive, high-value intents). Failure: create regression ticket; require owner triage and signoff to proceed to shadow.
3. Shadow smoke (slow): promote candidate to shadow lane with 1% production traffic multiplexed for 24–72 hours. Monitor SLOs; any block-level metric breach for > 30 minutes triggers automatic demotion.
4. Final rollout: if shadow passes, schedule staggered rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with canary hold windows and automatic rollback on live regressions.

Quantization handoff checklist (artifact producer responsibilities):
- Produce deterministic artifact bundle: model.card, quant.metadata.json, kernel-config.yml, and checksums.
- Attach eval manifests: commit hash for eval harness, slice-set id, random seeds used, and perf seed trace.
- Run local safety checks: tokenization parity, functioncall smoke, and small-sample coherence tests.
- Upload artifact to artifact repo with tag: quant/<model>-<version>-<quant-profile>-<date>. Example: quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112
sections.heading: Gating rules (high-level)

sections.body:
---
artifact_tag: "quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112"
producer: "quant-team/autoquant-v2"
eval_manifest: "evals/manifest/2026-01-10-quick.json"
required_gates:
  - unit_sentinels
  - slice_regressions
  - shadow_smoke
promotion_policy:
  shadow_duration_hours: 48
  canary_steps: [5, 25, 100]
  rollback_on: [response_stability_index, p95_latency, mean_fidelity]
---

Operational runbook: step-by-step
1) Submit artifact: producer uploads artifact and triggers "eval-harness run" with tag.
   CLI: eval-harness run --artifact quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --slices priority-slice-set --parallel 12
2) Fast gate: unit tests and sentinel checks run (target: < 30 minutes). If any sentinel fails, pipeline creates an automated regression incident and marks the artifact failed.
3) Slice gate: run full slice suite (target: 2–6 hours). Summary report posted to /evals/reports/<artifact_tag>.
4) If slice gate passes, orchestrator triggers shadow promotion job. Shadow config: 1% traffic, 48h, telemetry piped to shadow namespace.
5) Monitoring and alerting: paging thresholds are configured in monitoring-playbooks:
   - RSI drop >= 0.02 sustained for 30m -> P1 on-call page
   - Latency P95 exceed baseline + 40ms for 4 consecutive 5m windows -> P1
   - Token cost > baseline + 15% for 1h -> SRE on-call.
6) Failures during shadow: run quick rollback script and open triage.
   CLI: eval-harness rollback --shadow quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --reason "p95_latency"
7) After successful shadow, schedule canary rollout with annotated ticket linking eval report, perf traces, and signoffs.
sections.heading: Handoff YAML (example)

sections.body:
- Block-level metric breach? -> Immediate demotion and assign regression-owner -> create incident -> run bisect (if multiple quant profiles) -> if root cause is quant param, attempt localized re-quant or adjust kernel config.
- Cost regression only? -> Flag for product + finance review; require explicit product signoff to proceed.
- Small quality delta within allowed but customer-sensitive slice affected? -> Run targeted human review on slice, consider per-tenant hold.
sections.heading: Triage decision tree (condensed)

sections.body:
- Quantization team: produce artifacts, include metadata, respond to quant-specific failures.
- Applied ML / Eval team: owns eval manifests, slice prioritization, and gate automation.
- SRE: owns rollout orchestration, shadow routing, and emergency rollback tooling.
- Product owner: approves cost deviations and tenant-risk signoffs.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- eval_summary_url (string)
- delta_metrics: {"rsi": "-0.006", "p95_latency_ms": "+12"} (as JSON blob in report)
- perf_trace_id
- artifact_checksums
sections.heading: Metrics to publish with every promotion candidate (minimum)

sections.body:
- Non-deterministic eval results across seeds: increase sample seeds to 10 and run multi-seed aggregator; check for tokenization nondeterminism.
- Latency regression only on long contexts: add context-limited micro-bench and consider KV cache tuning or kernel selection override.
- Functioncall mismatch after quantization: run functioncall-priming harness and verify call-signature fidelity; if failing, mark quant profile as unsuited.
sections.heading: Common failure modes and remediations

sections.body:
1. Set routing to previous stable artifact: routingctl set-default <service> --artifact <stable-tag>
2. Pause ongoing shadow/canary promotions.
3. Open incident with tags: quant, regression, auto-rollback.
4. Triage owner runs bisect on quant parameter set and uploads findings to incident.
sections.heading: Fast rollback checklist (emergency)

sections.body:
- Artifact tag:
- Eval run id and link:
- Shadow duration and traffic: (hours, %)
- Key delta metrics (table): RSI, P95 latency, top-5 slice regressions
- Risk notes and mitigation plan:
- Approvals: quant lead, applied-ml lead, SRE lead, product manager

Appendix: example eval-harness commands and useful endpoints
- Start controlled eval: eval-harness run --artifact <tag> --slices <slice-set> --output /evals/reports/<tag>.json
- Promote to shadow: eval-orchestrator promote --artifact <tag> --lane shadow --traffic 1% --duration 48h
- Query stability: curl -s "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/slices/<slice-id>/stability?artifact=<tag>"
sections.heading: Promotion signoff template (required in ticket)

sections.body:
- Eval orchestration: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-workflow-optimizer-for-mixed-slo-scenarios-2026
- Quant safety baseline: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow deployment pattern: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/shadow-deployments
sections.heading: References and related policies

sections.body:
- 2025-09-12: Created initial draft (Marisol Chen)
- 2025-10-23: Added shadow demotion windows and RSI thresholds (review feedback)
- 2026-01-18: Aligned monitoring thresholds with SRE playbooks and added rollback CLI example (Rina Sato)

Contact: marisol@redwood-inference.internal for questions or proposed updates.

payload.page_title: External Adapter Evaluability Contract and Certification

sections.body:
Overview:
This page defines the evaluability contract, minimum test matrix, and certification workflow for external model adapters and third-party model bundles that Redwood Inference may host or enable via Dedicated/Private deployments. The goal is to ensure adapters are predictable, testable, and safe to run through our eval harness, quantization profile tooling, and production-facing regression triage pipelines.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any external adapter, model wrapper, or conversion artifact submitted by partners or third-party vendors for use in Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private modes.
- Covers behavior-level evaluation (quality), perf-level evaluation (latency/throughput), and operational evaluation (memory, KV cache correctness, failure modes).
- Does not replace product-specific acceptance criteria (service owners may add stricter domain requirements).

Why a contract matters:
1. Third-party adapters often introduce opaque preprocessing, tokenization mismatches, or kernel incompatibilities that create subtle quality regressions after quantization or at different sequence lengths.
2. A repeatable contract enables automated certification in our CI, preventing onboarding regressions and shortening review cycles.
3. It provides clear triage playbooks when regressions surface in production.

Definitions:
- Adapter: a packaging layer that converts a published model checkpoint into Redwood-serving artifacts (tokenizer, model config, conversion metadata).
- Evaluability: the property that an adapter exposes deterministic inputs/outputs for the eval harness and provides telemetry hooks required by Redwood tooling.
- Certification: successful completion of all gates in the test matrix and signoff by the model onboarding owner.

Ownership and roles:
- Partner / Vendor: provides adapter artifacts, conversion notes, and a minimal test manifest.
- Model Onboarding Team: gatekeeper for certification, coordinates evaluations and manual review.
- Eval Platform / CI Owners: run automated harness, collect telemetry, and provide artifacts for SRE and Quantization teams.
- Security & Compliance: reviews any restricted data handling or KMS/HSM interactions.

Certification gates (must pass all):
1) Sanity and determinism gate
   - Run the canonical smoke-suite (100 deterministic prompts).
   - Requirement: 100% successful runs (no crashes), response latency within baseline bounds (<= 2x reference unconstrained), and deterministic tokenization for identical inputs.

2) Tokenization & detokenization fidelity
   - Verify round-trip detokenization across a representative set of multilingual and edge-case tokens (control list provided by eval team).
   - Requirement: character-level equivalence for canonical examples; documented divergences permitted only if annotated in adapter manifest.

3) Eval harness integration gate
   - Adapter must expose an evaluation manifest (see example below) readable by the eval harness.
   - Must pass the functional evals: intent-preservation, hallucination-control, and slot-filling where applicable.

4) Quantization compatibility gate
   - Run quantized inference profiles (8-bit, 4-bit configurations supported by runtime).
   - Metrics: semantic-similarity delta <= configured QoQ threshold (default: 0.06 embedding cosine drop or 3% generation quality delta on chosen metric); memory and peak GPU allocations within expected budget.

5) Performance & throughput gate
   - 95th percentile token latency and median throughput tests across short (16 tokens), medium (256 tokens), and long (2048 tokens) contexts.
   - Requirement: 95th-pct latency within SLO for targeted deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). See table below.

6) Stability and failure-mode gate
   - Injected fault tests: OOM, corrupted KV cache, network flakiness, and abrupt process restart.
   - Requirement: adapter should fail gracefully, return structured errors, and not corrupt shared caches. Recovery path documented.

7) Telemetry & observability gate
   - Adapter must emit adapter_id, model_version, tokenizer_version, quant_profile_id, and deterministic request hash in traces/metrics.
   - Must provide mapping to Redwood standard metric names: redwood.adapter.version, redwood.eval.loss_estimate, redwood.quant.status.

Certification test matrix (summary table):
| Gate | Example tests | Pass criterion | Owner |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| Sanity | smoke-suite (100 prompts) | no crash, tokenization deterministic | Partner / Eval CI |
| Tokenization | round-trip tests for 24 languages | character equivalence or documented note | Partner / Onboarding |
| Functional eval | intent-preservation, factuality probes | PASS on primary slice set (>= 90% of probes) | Eval Team |
| Quantization | 8-bit/4-bit replay tests | semantic delta <= 0.06 | Quant Team |
| Perf | 16/256/2048 token runs | latency SLOs (see SLO table) | Perf Bench |
| Stability | OOM and restart tests | clean failure + documented recovery | SRE / Onboarding |

SLO reference (deployment class targets):
- Hosted API (free/standard tiers): median token latency < 40ms (short context), 95th < 225ms; throughput targets vary with plan.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU): median token latency < 25ms (short context), 95th < 150ms.
- Private on-prem (customer-configurable): target baseline provided during onboarding; certification verifies against declared baseline.

Promotion and release workflow (high level):
1. Partner submits adapter bundle + manifest to the onboarding repo and opens an onboarding request ticket.
2. Eval CI automatically schedules: smoke-suite, tokenization checks, and functional evals on sample probes.
3. Quant team runs parallel quant compatibility sweep; perf bench runs on matching hardware sizing.
4. If all gates pass: Onboarding owner creates a candidate release and tags for shadow experiments.
5. Shadow canary: run production-weighted shadow for 72 hours on non-critical traffic or replayed workload.
6. Monitoring window: evaluate response stability index (RSI) and telemetry adherence.
7. Final signoff: onboarding owner + SRE + Quantization lead.

Automated CI recipe (examples):
- Example adapter manifest (YAML snippet to include in bundle):
  ---
  adapter_id: "vendor-x/adapter-bert-slim-v1"
  model_family: "bert-qa"
  tokenizer: "sentencepiece-v2"
  supported_quant_profiles: ["int8-default","q4f_fast"]
  smoke_suite_hash: "sha256:..."
  test_seed_list: ["seed-a","seed-b"]

- CI job names and brief behavior:
  - adapter-smoke: runs smoke-suite and tokenization checks; exit non-zero on mismatch.
  - adapter-functional: runs eval harness scenarios and produces a JSON artifact with metrics.
  - adapter-quant-sweep: compiles quantized artifact variants and runs replayed probes.
  - adapter-perf-bench: runs block-throughput runs on target hardware and uploads trace files.

Telemetry contract (fields and semantics):
- redwood.adapter.id: stable string identifier for the adapter (immutable per release).
- redwood.adapter.artifact_hash: SHA256 of the packaged artifact (used in reproducibility).
- redwood.quant.profile: quantization profile id used for inference.
- redwood.evaluator.manifest_version: manifest schema version that was used to orchestrate the evaluation.
- request.eval_request_hash: deterministic hash for the request payload used in the harness.

Regression triage and rollback playbook (short):
1. If production detects a rise in regression alerts tied to adapter_id, immediately trigger the adapter-failure playbook.
2. Snapshot failing request hashes and surface them to the model-oncall queue.
3. Run binary-bisect using archived artifacts and replay against the quantized artifact variants to isolate commit/quant-change.
4. If root cause is adapter change, rollback to the previous certified adapter artifact and open an RCA.

Onboarding checklist (must be included in the PR):
- adapter bundle (weights, tokenizer, conversion notes)
- adapter manifest (schema v2)
- smoke-suite seed file and expected artifacts
- minimal functional probe set and expected metrics
- declared quant profiles and memory budgets
- documented recovery steps for OOM or cache corruption

Failure modes and escalation notes:
- Non-deterministic tokenization: reject the bundle until tokenization library is stabilized or adapter provides mapping tables.
- Excessive semantic drift after quantization: mark as conditional-pass with enforced shadowing for 14 days and higher telemetry sampling.
- Telemetry omissions: certification blocked until required fields emitted.

Example commands and artifacts for reviewers:
- Run smoke suite locally (dockerized):
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work redwood/eval-runner:stable 
    --adapter /work/adapter-bundle.tar.gz --smoke-seed /work/smoke-seed.json 

- Generate evaluation manifest (local helper):
  rwd-evalgen manifest create --adapter-id vendor-x/adapter-bert-slim-v1 --probes probes/primary.json --out manifest.yaml

Appendix A: Minimal manifest schema (human-readable)
- manifest_version: v2
- adapter_id: string
- model_family: string
- tokenizer: string
- quant_profiles: list[string]
- smoke_suite_hash: string
- probes: list["path/to/probe.json"]

Appendix B: Common triage templates
- Incident title: "Adapter regression: {adapter_id} semantic delta spike"
- Initial triage checklist:
  1) Confirm adapter_id and artifact_hash.
  2) Run adapter-smoke locally and attach logs.
  3) Run quant replay for reported probe hashes.

Related resources:
- Onboarding PRD (internal link)
- Quantization profiles catalog (internal link)
- Eval harness runner CLI docs (internal link)

Notes and change log:
- 2025-11-04: v1 created (Priya Nair).
- 2026-02-18: updated quant thresholds and telemetry field names (Mei Chen, Quant Team).

Contact: model-onboarding@redwood.ai for requests and reviewer assignment.

payload.page_title: Counterfactual Traffic Synthesis and Stability Protocol for Eval Harness

sections.body:
Summary:

This document defines a reproducible protocol and tooling approach for generating counterfactual and synthetic traffic to stress-test model serving and evaluation infrastructure. The protocol focuses on producing stable, explainable variations of live traffic for: 1) regression detection, 2) caching/kv-cache sensitivity tests, 3) quantization/precision shock tests, and 4) routing and fallback validation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Why this exists:
- Live traffic is the gold standard but cannot always be replayed (privacy, PII, consent) or deterministically modified.
- Random synthetic traffic misses critical corner cases and distributional shifts.
- Counterfactual traffic (systematically altered real or simulated requests) bridges the gap: it preserves semantics while enabling controlled perturbations to probe failure modes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied-ML engineers, SREs, model-onboarding owners, and QA.
- Scope: eval harness integrations (eval-mesh), synthetic traffic service (traffic-synth), and downstream triage runbooks.
- Excluded: labeling guidelines for human annotators (handled in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Key definitions:
- Counterfactual Traffic: requests derived from canonical examples with targeted perturbations (e.g., role swaps, locale swaps, long-context insertion).
- Synthetic Shadow: traffic generated to imitate structural properties (token length, entity density) of a production route without using PII.
- Amplification Factor: multiplier applied to rare-slice traffic to increase statistical power when evaluating regressions.

High-level architecture:
- eval-mesh: orchestrates eval jobs and routes to target serving endpoints (hosted/dedicated/private).
- traffic-synth: independent microservice that composes counterfactuals and emits injections to eval-mesh or canary proxies.
- kv-cache-proxy: optional inline proxy to emulate and flush customer KV cache behaviors.
- quant-simulator: module that wraps model variants (float32->int8 quant) to compare outputs without changing live model binary.

Design principles:
- Determinism where possible: seeds + cataloged perturbation rules produce repeatable traffic.
- Observability-first: every synthetic request carries trace metadata (synth.catalog, perturbation.seed, amplification.id).
- Minimal fidelity loss: preserve original semantic intent of examples to avoid false positives.
- Safety and privacy: no PII copied from production; use token-level anonymization + synthetic named entities.

Catalog of perturbation families (examples):
1) Entity-level swaps: replace named entities with same-type synthetic tokens (e.g., COMPANY_X -> COMPANY_SYNTH).
2) Context elongation: insert benign long context passages to stress KV cache and long-context execution path.
3) Role inversion: flip question/answer framing to catch degenerative behavior in instruction-following models.
4) Locale and formatting: switch date/number formats, RTL language insertion, and timezone offsets.
5) Adversarial punctuation/noise: insert seldom-used unicode or tokenization traps.
6) Quantization stress: force sequences known to amplify FP error (dense numerical tables, alignment tokens).

Sampling strategies:
- Stratified-Aware Sampling: sample from production strata (route, customer-tier, model-version) proportionally, then amplify rare slices by Amplification Factor (AF).
- Edge-Amplify: identify slices with <1% frequency and apply AF 50–200x for statistical power.
- Counterfactual Pairs: always generate a (control, perturbed) pair to compute delta metrics per request.

Configuration table (recommended defaults):
Route/Workload Config YAML (example):
---
name: marketing-chat-route
seed_corpus: s3://eval-corpora/marketing-seed-v2.jsonl
perturbation_families: [entity_swaps, context_elongation, locale_swaps]
sample_strategy: stratified-aware
amplification_factors: {rare_slice: 100, default: 1}
batch_size: 128
duration: 2h
send_mode: shadow (no client-visible effects)
observe_metrics: [latency_p50, latency_p95, rsi, match_rate, token_delta]
---

CLI & examples:
- Generate a reproducible counterfactual run locally (dev):
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 42 --dry-run

- Push a 2-hour shadow stream to eval-mesh for canary:
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 20260214 --duration 2h --send-mode shadow --target eval-mesh:9090

- Quick curl to submit single counterfactual pair to eval-mesh (JSON):
curl -X POST https://eval-mesh.internal/api/v1/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trace_id":"synth-0001","seed":123,"control":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results."},"perturbed":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results with extra accounting table appended."},"tags":{"family":"context_elongation","amplification":"1"}}'

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Response Stability Index (RSI): median absolute token-wise divergence between control and perturbed outputs. Alert if RSI > 0.12 for any amplified slice.
- Latency SLO regression: no more than +10% increase in route p95 latency under synthetic load vs baseline for burst sized up to batch_size*4.
- Semantic match_rate: fraction of perturbed outputs that preserve required intent labels (e.g., intent classification) — target > 0.92 for production promotion.
- Token delta: expected token increase per perturbation family; validate against a 3-sigma envelope built from historical runs.

Experiment / promotion checklist (canary procedure):
1) Local dry-run: run --dry-run and validate traces and perturbation coverage.
2) Shadow targeted canary (1% production RPS equivalent): send to eval-mesh -> observe metrics for 2h.
3) Amplified slice validation: for each rare slice with AF>1, ensure RSI < threshold and match_rate > 0.92.
4) Cross-model comparison: run quant-simulator variants (FP32 vs quant) on same stream and compute per-token delta; flag if > 0.08 for high-sensitivity routes.
5) Rollout decision: if all acceptance criteria pass, mark model as promotion-ready in onboarding matrix.
6) Post-promotion scan: run an overnight full-shaped synthetic sweep (AF=10 for rare slices) and collect stability artifacts.

Triage playbook (when synthetic run flags a regression):
1) Attach run metadata and open a regression issue with tag: eval:counterfactual. Include: config, seed, amplification id, and example (control, perturbed, model outputs).
2) Reproduce with same seed in dev environment. If non-deterministic, capture run logs and escalate to runtime team.
3) Bisect by perturbation family: run traffic-synth with single family enabled to isolate failure mode.
4) Run quant-simulator for quant regressions; if behavior diverges only in quant variant, escalate to model-ops + quant teams.
5) If divergence correlates with KV-cache eviction patterns, enable kv-cache-proxy with deterministic TTL=0/1 toggles to reproduce.
6) Document root cause, mitigations (e.g., prompt normalization, tokenizer glue fixes, caching TTL changes), and remediation timeline.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Traffic-synth: owned by applied-ml (oncall: applied-ml@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.5% availability for dev runs.
- Eval-mesh ingestion: owned by eng-platform (oncall: eng-platform@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.9% for evaluation ingestion.
- Triage and model promotion decisions: model-onboarding team.

Observability and artifacts to capture for every run:
- Trace ID list and sampling map (CSV).
- Per-request control/perturbed outputs (ndjson).
- Metric timeseries for RSI, latency percentiles, match_rate.
- Token-level diffs for top-k diverging examples.
- Run manifest (config + git sha + synth version).

Privacy & safety controls:
- No PII rule: any seed corpus coming from production must pass scrubbing + synthetic-entity-replacement before ingestion.
- Safety review checkpoint: any amplification >100x on slices with user-visible outputs requires a safety review from Research safety lead.

Appendix A — Example perturbation rule (JSON):
{
  "id": "entity_swap_company",
  "description": "Swap organization entities with synthetic names preserving token-length distribution.",
  "patterns": ["ORG", "COMPANY"],
  "replacement_pool": ["AcmeSyn", "BetaWorks", "NovaGrid"],
  "seeded": true
}

Appendix B — Common failure signatures and quick remediation:
- High RSI with low token delta: likely a model policy/decoding change. Remediation: check decoding params, temperature, and any soft-prompt patches.
- High token delta + latency spike: batching/backpressure interaction; remediate via batch tuning and autoscaling policy.
- Failures isolated to quant-simulator: investigate quant profile, re-run per-workload quant-tuner.

Links and references:
- eval-harness overview: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- Regression triage handbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026
- Quant profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

Contact:
- Primary author: Aisha Malik (aisha@redwood.internal)
- Applied-ML oncall: applied-ml@redwood.internal

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft
- 2026-01-20: added quant-simulator integration and RSI acceptance thresholds
- 2026-02-14: finalized canary checklist and privacy controls
