payload.page_title: End-to-End Deployment Quality Contract and Operations Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the end-to-end quality contract for promoting a model artifact through Redwood’s deployment pipeline (shadow -> canary -> GA) and the operational playbook for detecting, triaging, and remediating regressions that violate that contract. It codifies the evaluation gates across: eval-harness checks, prompt set coverage, quantization profile verification, runtime telemetry SLOs, and regression-triage escalation paths.

Scope
-----
Applies to: production model promotions across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Exclusions: low-risk internal experiments that do not serve customer traffic and models with explicit "research-only" labels.

Goals
-----
- Provide a deterministic acceptance workflow that prevents quality regressions for customers.
- Ensure fast, reproducible triage when regressions occur.
- Balance unit-cost improvements (quantization, batching) with strict quality and latency contracts.

Quality Contract (gates and pass criteria)
----------------------------------------
Each promotion must pass the following gates before moving to the next stage. Failure to meet any gate requires documented mitigation and an approver sign-off (owner or product manager).

1) Eval-harness functional & safety suite (pre-promotion)
   - Smoke tests: 0 failing critical tests (CLI: redwood-eval run --suite smoke).
   - Slice-based acceptance: per-slice accuracy/precision recall within baseline delta: <= 2% absolute drop for high-priority slices.
   - Safety sentinels: zero critical safety hits for production prompt set (see appendix for sentinel list).

2) Prompt-set coverage and stability (pre/promotion shadow)
   - Coverage: production prompt-set coverage >= 90% of top-50 workload intents and >= 75% of long-tail probe classes.
   - Stability: Response Stability Index (RSI) ratio >= 0.98 against promoted baseline over 10k sample traffic replay.

3) Quantization & artifact verification (pre-promotion & shadow)
   - Quantized artifact MAPE (mean absolute pct error) on logits/embedding similarity metrics <= 0.5% for encoder outputs, <= 1.5% for logits on generative tasks unless exempted.
   - KV-cache fidelity check: top-k next-token distribution similarity >= 99% on warm sequences.

4) Runtime SLO and cost envelope (canary)
   - Latency: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 180ms for standard request shape (seq_len=512) on canary capacity.
   - Error budget: request_error_rate <= 0.5% (5xx or internal errors) during canary window.
   - Cost: token-cost-per-1k (inference) not exceed baseline + 12% unless approved by cost owner.

5) Post-Canary Quality Signal (canary -> GA decision)
   - Quality regression rate: regressions per 10k requests <= 1 (where regression = semantic correctness drop by eval harness metric defined per workload).
   - Human-in-the-loop sample pass-rate: >= 95% on 200 random canary responses labeled by annotators for intent correctness.

Gate checklist table (copyable)
--------------------------------
| Gate | Must-pass criteria | Tooling/Command | Owner |
|------|--------------------|-----------------|-------|
| Eval-harness smoke | 0 critical fails | redwood-eval run --suite smoke | eval-onboarding team |
| Slice acceptance | Per-slice delta <= 2% | redwood-eval slice-compare --baseline X | applied-ml |
| Quant verification | MAPE thresholds | quant-checker run --artifact a.pt | infra-quant team |
| Canary SLOs | Latency/error/cost | telemetry/alerts dashboard | SRE/Platform |
| Human sample | 95% pass | sampling-runner collect --n 200 | customer-success |

Promotion workflow (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Author creates model promotion PR and attaches promotion manifest (model id, quant profile, eval snapshot id, prompt coverage report).
2. Automated CI runs eval-harness full-suite on shadow artifact; results posted to PR.
3. If green, deployment to shadow routing (no customer traffic) for 6–24 hours with telemetry capture.
4. Canary deploy (5–10% traffic split) for 2–24 hours depending on traffic variance; realtime checks run.
5. If canary meets post-canary quality signals, schedule GA rollout incrementally; otherwise rollback to previous artifact immediately and trigger triage.

Canary sizing rules and ramp schedule
-------------------------------------
- Default canary: 5% traffic for 2 hours -> check automated gate metrics; if stable, increase to 20% for 4 hours -> check again -> GA.
- For high-risk changes (quantization, architecture updates, prompt-engineering), use conservative ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 10% with longer observation windows (12–24h at each step).
- Traffic shaping: prefer homogeneous slices for canary routing (non-sampled, high-volume intents) to avoid noisy long-tail signal.

Telemetry, metrics, and alerting (must be wired prior to canary)
----------------------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (ms)
- request_error_rate (%%)
- quality_regressions_per_10k (count) — measured by eval returns and sentinel mismatches
- embedding_drift_score (cosine delta) — exponential-weighted moving average (EWMA window=1 day)
- token_cost_per_1k (USD)
sections.heading: Core metrics (reported per route/model)

sections.body:
- Sev-1 (Pager): quality_regressions_per_10k > 5 for 30m OR request_error_rate > 2%% for 15m -> pager SRE + applied-ml oncall.
- Sev-2 (High): latency_p95 > 2x baseline for 30m OR embedding_drift_score > 0.12 (absolute) for 2h -> slack alert to model-owners and SRE.
- Sev-3 (Medium): incremental token_cost drift > +20%% vs baseline over 24h -> billing-notification + product.

Regression triage playbook (oncall steps)
-----------------------------------------
1. Detect: Pager fires or customer reports. Record incident id and triage channel (incident-{model}-{ts}).
2. Snapshot: Capture model artifact id, promotion manifest, latency/quality dashboards, and last successful baseline id. CLI: redwood-metrics snapshot --model MODEL_ID --since "-1h" --out /tmp/snap.json
3. Reproduce locally: Run smoke suite and failing prompt slices in local eval-harness (redwood-eval replay --input failing-requests.json --artifact ARTIFACT_ID).
4. Blame bisect: If change set contains multiple commits, perform binary promotion bisect using CI promotion snapshots. Use redwood-bisect --candidates LIST --metric 'quality_regressions_per_10k' --target-threshold 1.
5. If quantization suspected: run quantized replay and float baseline comparison (quant-replay --float baseline.pt --quant candidate.q.pt).
6. Rollback plan: If can’t mitigate quickly, rollback to previous artifact ID and pin canary route to old model. Notify customers per escalation template.

Detailed triage decision tree (short)
--------------------------------------
- If errors are 5xx/internal: prioritize SRE stack traces and runtime logs (likely infra).
- If semantic regressions without errors: focus on eval-harness diffs, prompt/coverage mismatches, or quant artifacts.
- If regressions only on long-tail slices: gather sample frequency and consider targeted prompt rewrites or slice-focused canary with higher observation window.

Quantization-specific acceptance and recovery checks
-----------------------------------------------------
| Check | Threshold | Recovery action |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| Embedding cosine retention | >= 0.995 vs float | Recompute quant profile or fallback to mixed-precision variant |
| Output distribution MAPE | <= 1.5% | Increase precision or enable per-layer calibration |
| KV-cache hit parity | >= 99% | Re-evaluate cache serialization and dequant path |
sections.heading: Alert thresholds and severities

sections.body:
- Automated fallback: route 100% of affected route to float variant within 2 minutes (automated rollback policy).
- Postmortem: quant team runs quant-sensitivity routine and updates the quant-profile registry with failing fingerprints.

Human labeling and escalation matrices
--------------------------------------
- Human label runs: sample 200 responses from canary window; labelers use rubric 'intent-correct/partial/incorrect' and 'harmful/unsafe/ok'.
- Escalation: if labeled incorrect >= 5 in 200 (<= 95% pass) -> open a quality incident; notify product and CS and pause GA.

Operational runbook links and artifacts
--------------------------------------
- Runbook: applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026
- Canary dashboard name: /dashboards/model-canary/{{model_id}}/overview
- CI artifact storage: s3://redwood-artifacts/promotions/{{promotion_id}}/

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Model owner: person listed in promotion manifest (mandatory).
- Applied ML oncall: paged via SRE rotation.
- Quantization owner: infra-quant team (pager via #infra-quant).
- Customer-impact escalation: Customer Success oncall -> product -> legal for high-severity incidents.

Postmortem and continuous improvement
-------------------------------------
- Every production regression that exceeds Sev-2 must have a postmortem within 5 business days with: timeline, root cause, action items, owner, and verification plan.
- Feed triage learnings into: prompt-set extension (new probes), eval-harness test updates, and quant-profile adjustments.

Appendix: Example commands and JSON snippets
--------------------------------------------
1) Promotion manifest example (promotion-manifest.json):
{
  "model_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2",
  "artifact_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0",
  "quant_profile_id": "q_profile_2026-02",
  "eval_snapshot": "snapshot-2026-02-09-17",
  "owner": "asha.patel@redwood.ai"
}

2) Run a pre-promotion eval suite:
$ redwood-eval run --artifact rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0 --suite full --out reports/2026-02-10.json

3) Trigger a bisect (automated):
$ redwood-bisect --metric quality_regressions_per_10k --candidates artifacts/list.txt --baseline artifact:prev

4) Snapshot telemetry:
$ redwood-metrics snapshot --model rwd-llm-3b-v2 --since "-6h" --out /tmp/canary-snap.json

Definitions and glossary
------------------------
- Response Stability Index (RSI): a composite metric that compares normalized token-level distributions, semantic embedding distances, and function-call signature parity between two artifacts. Range 0–1 (1 = identical).
- Regression: measurable drop in task-specific eval metric or human-label pass rate compared to baseline beyond configured threshold.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-02-10: Initial draft (Asha Patel).
- 2026-02-20: Added quantization thresholds and automated fallback policies (Lucia Fernandez).
- 2026-03-02: Adjusted canary ramp rules and human sampling size (Jonah Kim).

Notes and references
---------------------
- See allied docs: applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026 for synthetic evaluation specifics.
- For security and privacy guidance during shadowing, consult security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/shadow-deployment-privacy-guidelines.

payload.page_title: runtime-fingerprint-onboarding-and-shadow-compatibility-checklist-2026

sections.body:
Overview:

This document defines the runtime fingerprinting and shadow-compatibility checklist used by Model Onboarding and the Eval team to verify that a model artifact is compatible with Redwood serving runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private) and safe to promote into production shadowing. The goal is to capture deterministic and non-deterministic runtime signals so teams can anticipate quality regressions introduced by kernels, quantization, KV cache differences, tokenizers, and batching behavior.

Motivation:

- Models with identical weights can behave materially differently under different runtime stacks (quant kernels, mixed precision, sequence-length optimizations).
- Late-stage surprises (coherence drops, hallucination shifts, functioncall decoding errors) are expensive in production.
- A standardized fingerprint and gating checklist reduces promotion risk and speeds onboarding.

Definitions:

- Runtime fingerprint: A compact set of telemetry artifacts (microbench responses, slice-anchor outputs, determinism seeds, tokenization examples, KV-cache delta signatures) that characterize how a model behaves under a given serving runtime and configuration.
- Shadow compatibility: A boolean decision to allow traffic mirroring to a candidate model in shadow mode (non-traffic-affecting) based on fingerprint proximity to the baseline and passing quality & stability gates.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to all models entering Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.
- Required for: major model upgrades (architecture, tokenizer, quant profile), quant-shadow cohorts, and migrations between runtime families (e.g., cuBLAS->kernel-optimizer).

High-level process (1-line):

1) Generate fingerprint artifacts -> 2) Run deterministic microbench & slice probes -> 3) Compare against baseline fingerprint -> 4) Run shadow cohort with telemetry gating -> 5) Promote or rollback.

Runtime fingerprint components (required):

- Tokenization signature: token ids & byte offsets for 150 canonical prompts (see tokenization sample list below).
- Microbench harness: per-kernel per-sequence-length stepwise log-prob arrays for 12 synthetic prompts (3 seeds each).
- KV-cache delta signature: hashed set of KV-cache root-diffs captured at step 8 and step 64 for long-context models.
- Determinism seeds: deterministic log-probability vectors for 20 seed values and a variance summary.
- Functioncall trace baseline: canonical functioncall examples (3 variants per function) with expected JSON schema shapes.
- Embedding drift snapshot: average cosine to production embedding centroid for 50 anchors.

Fingerprint generation checklist (detailed steps):

1. Prepare artifact bundle:
   - Create model artifact with pinned weights + tokenizer + quant profile (if applicable).
   - Tag artifact: service_name:model_name:artifact_hash (e.g., redwood-search:reranker:v2:sha256:abcd).

2. Run tokenization signature job:
   - Command: ./tools/tokenize-signer --model-artifact <artifact_tar> --seed-corpus samples/token-sample-150.json --out token-signature.json
   - Confirm: no unknown token warnings, consistent header fields.

3. Execute microbench harness:
   - Run: redwood-eval --harness microbench --artifact <artifact> --sequence-lengths 32,128,512 --seeds 42,101,202 --output microbench.json
   - Verify: p95 step latency per token and stepwise log-probs exist for each kernel path.

4. Capture KV-cache deltas (for models with > 128 context):
   - Run an 80-step generation, sample cache dumps at step 8 & 64 using the runtime hook (see runtime-ops docs).
   - Produce hashed delta signature: sha256(kv_step8 || kv_step64).

5. Determinism sweep:
   - Run 20 fixed-seed generations and compute variance per token position. Save as determinism.json.

6. Functioncall baseline validation:
   - Execute 9 functioncall prompts. Confirm JSON schema compliance and consistent argument ordering for positional APIs.

7. Embedding centroids:
   - Compute 50-anchor embeddings, compare cosine distribution vs baseline. Save embedding-snapshot.json.

Shadow compatibility checklist (gating thresholds):

- Tokenization: 0 unknown-token warnings; average tokenization length delta <= 2 tokens for same prompt set.
- Determinism: per-token variance median <= 1e-6; max per-token variance threshold = 1e-4.
- Microbench log-prob drift: KL divergence (candidate || baseline) across microbench seeds <= 0.015.
- Embedding drift: median cosine similarity >= 0.985 to production centroid.
- Latency p95: <= 120 ms (hosted dev tier), <= 80 ms (dedicated SLO class A) for seq=128 tests.
- KV-cache delta entropy: hashed-diff Hamming distance <= 0.02 (normalized) from baseline.
- Functioncall schema match: 100% pass. Partial schema drift must have documented migration plan.

Gating policy (pass/fail rules):

1) HardReject: any Functioncall schema mismatch or unknown-token warnings -> block shadowing.
2) SoftReject: microbench KL > 0.03 or embedding median cosine < 0.97 -> require remediation and re-run.
3) ConditionalPass: minor token-length delta or marginal latency increase (<= 10% over baseline) -> allow limited shadow cohort with shortened TTL and tighter telemetry.

Shadow cohort orchestration (operational steps):

1. Create shadow cohort config (example YAML below).
2. Start redwood-shadow-runner in mirror mode for 1% of traffic, forward responses to observability sink only (no user exposure).
3. Enable additional probes: priming-cohort, cornercase-sampler, and latency-tail-capture for the candidate artifact.
4. Monitor rolling windows: 5m/30m/24h for SLI deltas and the fingerprint re-check every 30 minutes.
5. If any HardReject triggers, immediately stop mirroring and cut a rollback ticket.

Example shadow cohort config (shadow-cohort.yaml):

service: redwood-chat
model_artifact: redwood-chat:assistant-xl:sha256:ef12ab34
cohort:
  mirror_ratio: 0.01
  ttl_hours: 24
  extra_probes:
    - priming-cohort
    - latency-tail-capture
    - functioncall-monitor
  telemetry_sinks:
    - redwood-observability:eval-ingest
    - s3://prod-eval-archives/sha256/ef12ab34
gating:
  tokenization_delta_max: 2
  microbench_kl_threshold: 0.015
  embedding_cosine_min: 0.985
  p95_latency_max_ms: 120

Operational monitoring (metrics and dashboards):

- Core SLIs to visualize in the shadow dashboard:
  - eval.fingerprint.tokenization.delta (per-hour)
  - eval.fingerprint.kl_microbench (per-probe)
  - eval.embedding.cosine.median (hourly)
  - runtime.latency.p95.seq128 (5m/30m)
  - eval.functioncall.schema_fail_rate (rolling 1h)
  - eval.kvcache.hamming_norm (delta signature score)

- Alerting rules (default):
  - Severity P1: any HardReject -> Pager to ModelOnboard-1 oncall.
  - Severity P2: microbench KL > 0.03 sustained for 30m -> Slack alert to #model-onboarding and ticket auto-created.
  - Severity P3: latency p95 > SLO + 20% sustained for 1h -> email to owners.

Rollout and rollback criteria (decision table):

| Outcome | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| All gates pass | Promote to 10% live traffic after 24h | ModelOnboard Team Lead |
| ConditionalPass | Extend shadow to 48h with 0.5% mirror and run compensating probes | Eval Lead |
| SoftReject | Block promotion, open remediation ticket, require re-fingerprint after fix | Model Owner |
| HardReject | Stop mirror immediately, revert to baseline artifact, run incident review in 48h | SRE + Model Onboard |

Example CLI commands (common operations):

- Generate fingerprint: ./ci/fingerprint-run --artifact sha256:ef12ab34 --out /tmp/fingerprint_bundle.zip
- Start mirror: ./tools/redwood-shadow-runner --config shadow-cohort.yaml --start
- Run local microbench: redwood-eval --harness microbench --artifact ef12ab34 --out microbench.json
- Re-run deterministic sweep: python ./scripts/determinism_sweep.py --artifact ef12ab34 --seeds 0..19 --out det.json

Telemetry artifacts and storage policy:

- Fingerprint bundle (token_sign, microbench, kv_delta, determinism, embedding-snapshot) is stored in S3 under prod-evals/<artifact_hash>/fingerprint-YYYYMMDD.zip for 1 year.
- Short-term telemetry (5m/30m windows) retained in Prometheus for 90d; aggregated monthly rollups in BigQuery for 3 years.

Checklist to sign off onboarding (pre-shadow):

- [ ] Artifact uploaded with pinned tokenizer + quant profile hash.
- [ ] Tokenization signature generated and validated.
- [ ] Microbench harness executed for required sequence lengths and seeds.
- [ ] KV-cache deltas captured for long context models.
- [ ] Determinism sweep variance within threshold.
- [ ] Embedding snapshot compared; median cosine >= threshold.
- [ ] Functioncall baseline passed 100%.
- [ ] Shadow cohort YAML reviewed by SRE and Eval teams.
- [ ] Dashboards & alerts configured and tested in staging.
- [ ] Ownership recorded in the model registry with contact info.

Ownership and contacts:

- Model Onboarding Lead: Maya Chen (author) — @mchen
- Eval Lead: Arjun Patel — @apatel
- Runtime SRE: Lina Gomez — @lgomez
- Observability Owner: Sofia Martinez — @smartinez

Appendix: tokenization sample list (first 8 of 150):

1) "Translate to Spanish: The server returned an unexpected error code 503."
2) "Summarize the following legal clause: The purchaser warrants..."
3) "Compose a subject line for a password reset email for a fintech app."
4) "Extract dates and amounts from: Invoice #4312 dated 2025-03-01 for $4,200."
5) "Convert this markdown into JSON: - name: 'Redwood' - role: 'inference'"
6) "Functioncall test: create_event(title="Team sync", time="2026-01-15T10:00Z")"
7) "Long-context priming: [repeat a 800-token primer about prior conversation state]"
8) "Edge-case prompt: <script>alert(1)</script> What is the safe sanitized output?"

Notes and future work:

- Track a compact fingerprint vector embedding to allow fast nearest-neighbor comparisons across artifacts (outstanding infra ticket INF-2026-114).
- Add automated suggestion engine that maps fingerprint deltas to likely causes (quant kernels, tokenizer change, or decoding differences).

Related artifacts and references:

- Service: redwood-eval (internal) - eval harness repository: git+ssh://git.redwood/internal/eval-harness
- Runtime ops: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/release-notes
- Model registry: https://registry.redwood.internal/models

Revision history:

- 2025-11-12: Created (Maya Chen).
- 2026-01-04: Thresholds tightened for embedding cosine after cross-team review (Arjun Patel).
- 2026-02-15: Added KV-cache delta hashing procedure and sample YAML (Sofia Martinez).

payload.page_title: Quant Impact Synthesis for Prompt Families

sections.body:
A practical framework for synthesizing and reporting the impact of quantization across semantically grouped prompt families. Enables model-onboarding, shadow-evals, and regression triage teams to surface prompt-specific failure modes introduced by lower-precision artifacts.
Purpose and scope

This document defines an operational procedure and a scoring artifact - the Quant Stability Index (QSI) - for synthesizing quantization impact across prompt families. It is intended for evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and SRE teams performing shadow and canary rollouts of quantized model artifacts (dedicated or private deployments).

Why prompt families?

- Prompt families are clusters of prompts that share semantic intent, response style, or API route (for example: 'single-turn summarization', 'multi-turn clarification', 'code generation', 'customer-support templates').
- Quantization does not affect all prompt families equally; identifying family-specific regressions focuses triage and mitigations (fallback to float, cache bypassing, or better quant profiles).

High-level workflow

1) Define prompt families and representative shards (seeded examples).
2) Generate baseline golden outputs with a float32 reference model.
3) Run parallel eval-harness against candidate quantized artifacts.
4) Compute family-level metrics and the Quant Stability Index (QSI).
5) Prioritize families with QSI below thresholds for triage and corrective actions.
6) Produce an artifact (CSV + JSON) to attach to the model promotion ticket.

Definitions

- Prompt family: a labeled group of prompts sharing intent/style/route.
- Seed set: 100-2,000 canonical examples per family (stratified by length and few-shot contexts).
- Candidate artifact: a quantized model build being evaluated (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-q5_1).
- Reference: approved float model (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-fp32) used to generate baselines.
- QSI (Quant Stability Index): composite score (0-100) indicating fidelity preservation; higher is better.

Quant Stability Index (QSI) - formula and interpretation

Compute per-family QSI as a weighted composite of primary metrics. Use the following canonical weights (configurable):

- Response Fidelity Score (RFS): 0-100, measures semantic alignment with reference using ensembled comparators (embedding cosine + ROUGE-L + model-proxy edit distance). Weight: 0.6
- Latency Delta Penalty (LDP): normalized 0-100 penalty for relative latency change when quantized artifact uses different kernel paths. Weight: 0.15 (penalty reduces QSI)
- Tokenization/Truncation Failure Rate (TFR): 0-100 penalty for increased truncations or tokenization mismatches. Weight: 0.15
- Determinism/Stability Score (DSS): 0-100, measures sampling variance across seeds/passes (lower variance yields higher DSS). Weight: 0.1

QSI = round(clamp( RFS*0.6 + (100 - LDP)*0.15 + (100 - TFR)*0.15 + DSS*0.1 , 0, 100), 2)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- QSI >= 92: green - quant artifact acceptable for canary; proceed with standard rollout.
- 85 <= QSI < 92: yellow - acceptable for shadow or limited canary with aggressive monitoring and fallback.
- QSI < 85: red - requires remediation; do not promote to production.

Representative metrics and thresholds (example)

Metric | Measurement | Alert threshold
- RFS (family median) | embedding cosine delta vs reference (0-1) converted to 0-100 | drop > 4 points (i.e., cos delta > 0.04)
- LDP | p50 latency increase (%) | > 15%
- TFR | fraction of responses truncated or token mismatch | > 1.5%
- DSS | coefficient of variation of semantic similarity across 5 seeds | > 8% (lower is better)

Note: These numeric thresholds are starting points. Owners should calibrate per-product SLOs.

Prompt family selection and seed generation

- Start with product-owned route mapping: pull traffic sample t for each API route over 30 days and perform k-means on encoded prompts to suggest families.
- Human-in-the-loop curation: product/PSM annotators validate families and seed examples.
- Stratify seeds by: short vs long context, presence of code blocks, special tokens, and multimodal attributes (if applicable).
- Minimum seed size: 200 examples per family recommended for stable QSI; 100 allowed for low-risk families.

Operational configuration (eval-harness integration)

Use the eval harness job template 'quant-family-synthesis' in eval-mesh. Example YAML config (attach to job):

job_name: quant-family-synthesis
reference_model: redwood/llama-70b-fp32
candidates:
  - redwood/llama-70b-q5_1
  - redwood/llama-70b-q4f
prompt_families: /datasets/prompt-families/v2/manifest.json
seeds_per_family: 300
concurrency: 48
random_seeds: [42, 123, 777, 2026, 31415]
metrics: [embedding_cosine, rouge_l, latency_ms, truncation_flag]
report_artifact: s3://eval-artifacts/quant-synthesis/${JOB_ID}/report.json
sections.heading: Interpretation guidance

sections.body:
- Small runs (100 seeds/family): 2-4 GPU-hours on r-infer-gpu-k80 equivalent; good for quick checks.
- Medium runs (300 seeds/family): 8-24 GPU-hours depending on candidate count and concurrency.
- Large runs (1k seeds/family): schedule during non-peak; use dedicated pools.

Failure modes and triage playbook

1) Low RFS concentrated in specific family
   - Reproduce on a smaller canonical subset.
   - Inspect top-k output diffs and annotate failure types (hallucination, brevity, style shift).
   - Check quant-profile mismatch (e.g., outlier layer collapse) using quant-tuner diagnostics.

2) High latency delta for quant candidate
   - Confirm kernel selection and fallback paths in runtime telemetry (runtime-telemetry/logs).
   - If new kernel chosen, retest with kernel pinning or different batch sizing.

3) Elevated truncation/TFR
   - Re-check tokenizer compatibility and sequence length rounding.
   - Test with 'preserve-prefix' caching disabled to ensure KV artifacts not causing truncation.

4) Non-deterministic variance (low DSS)
   - Increase sampling seeds and test temperature/sampling configuration parity with reference.
   - If variance persists, inspect quant rounding behavior across batches and across GPU types.

Remediation options (ordered by cost/impact)

- Adjust quant profile (increase bits for sensitive layers).
- Use hybrid quant (higher precision for output layers).
- Enable per-route float fallback for affected families (routing policy change).
- Increase cache-preservation or use cache-priming for long-context families.
- Roll back to previous artifact and open a quant-fix ticket.

Reporting artifact and onboarding checklist
sections.heading: Suggested compute targets and runtimes

sections.body:
- report.json (per-family QSI and per-metric breakdown)
- diffs/ (example input, reference output, candidate output for top 20 failures per family)
- seeds_manifest.csv (family, seed_id, length_tokens, tags)
- job-config.yaml (the eval job config used)
sections.heading: Every synthesis run must produce a single ZIP containing

sections.body:
1) QSI green for > 90% of families and no red critical families.
2) For yellow families, owner signs off on monitoring + fallback plan.
3) Attach report ZIP to model promotion ticket and tag owners.

CLI snippets and quick commands

- Run local quickcheck (100 seeds):

evalctl run --job quant-family-synthesis --config quickcheck.yaml --target candidate:redwood/llama-70b-q5_1

- Summarize QSI from report.json:

python tools/qsi_summarize.py --report report.json --out summary.csv

Ownership, cadence and SLAs

- Owner: Applied ML - Model Reliability (team: applied-ml/reliability). Primary contact: Aisha Kumar.
- Quarterly review of family manifests and thresholds.
- SLA: synthesis run for a new candidate within 48 hours of artifact availability for high-priority models.

Appendix A - Example QSI output (human-readable excerpt)

Model: redwood/llama-70b-q5_1
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist for model promotion (Gated steps)

sections.body:
- summarization_short: QSI=94.2, RFS=95.1, LDP=3.2, TFR=0.2, DSS=96.5
 - longform_assist: QSI=82.4, RFS=78.3, LDP=12.1, TFR=1.8, DSS=85.0
Run id: job-2026-03-10-5b9f
Notes: longform_assist needs hybrid quant for final layers or per-route float fallback.

Appendix B - Common pitfalls and tips

- Do not rely solely on token-level metrics; small semantic shifts often appear only in embedding comparisons or targeted unit tests.
- Validate multi-turn coherence explicitly for families that use KV caching - quantized KV layout changes can surface as coherence regressions.
- Favor reproducible seeds and attach random seeds to the artifact for future bisecting.

Related resources

- quant-profile-synthesis playbook (internal)
- eval-mesh job templates and sample manifests
- model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook (for promotion gate mapping)

If you have questions or need the family clustering helper, ping applied-ml/reliability in Slack or file a request to the eval-harness queue.

payload.page_title: Embedding Stability and Versioning Guidelines

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This guideline documents how Redwood evaluates, monitors, and promotes embedding model versions with a focus on representation stability, backwards compatibility, and the interaction between quantization and downstream retrieval/semantic search behavior. It applies to vector models used for search, deduplication, ranking features, and clustering.

Scope: applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Excludes one-off feature embedding transforms that are not used in production retrieval/ranking.

Goals

- Define reproducible stability metrics and thresholds for embedding drift across versions and quantization profiles.
- Provide a promotion checklist and gating rules for pushing new embedding model versions to production.
- Describe monitoring, alerting, and fast rollback procedures for embedding regressions.
- Document experiment and offline eval harness steps to ensure parity across environments.

Key definitions

- Embedding drift: statistical shift in embedding-space relationships between two model variants measured on a representative probe set.
- Representation fidelity: preservation of semantic neighbor relationships measured via Recall@k and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR).
- Quantization delta: change in cosine similarity distributions introduced by weight/activation quantization measured per workload.

Representative metrics and how to compute them

1) Pairwise similarity change (median and 90th percentile):
   - For each probe vector x from baseline model M0 and candidate M1, compute cosine(M0(x), M1(x)). Report median and 90p.
   - Python snippet:

   ```python
   import numpy as np
   from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

   sims = cosine_similarity(emb0, emb1).diagonal()
   median = np.median(sims)
   p90 = np.percentile(sims, 90)
   ```

2) Retrieval fidelity (Recall@k, MRR):
   - Use a representative retrieval workload (see Probe Sets section). Query with the same prompts/documents against both models and measure Recall@1/5/10 and MRR of ground-truth items.

3) Neighbor rank drift:
   - For each item, compute the rank position of its top-k neighbors under M0 and M1. Report the distribution of rank displacement.

4) Cluster stability (ARI / silhouette change):
   - When embeddings are used for clustering, compare Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between cluster assignments from M0 and M1 on the probe corpus.

Gating thresholds (configurable per workload)

| metric                         | warning threshold | critical threshold | measurement window |
|--------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| median cosine (self)           | >= 0.92           | < 0.88             | probe set (N=5k)   |
| p90 cosine (self)             | >= 0.98           | < 0.95             | probe set (N=5k)   |
| Recall@10 (relative)          | >= -1.0%          | < -3.0%            | evaluation suite    |
| MRR (relative)                | >= -0.8%          | < -2.5%            | evaluation suite    |
| avg neighbor rank displacement| <= 3 positions    | > 8 positions      | probe set (N=5k)   |
| quantization median delta     | <= 0.02 cosine    | > 0.05 cosine      | quant test set     |

Note: thresholds above are defaults. Product workloads (search, recommendations) must set stricter or looser thresholds based on human-in-the-loop validation and user impact analysis.

Probe sets and synthetic workload construction

- Representative probe sources: production anonymized query logs (sampled with privacy filters), canonical documents (FAQ, KB, product descriptions), developer-curated edgecase bundles (typos, code snippets, cross-lingual examples).
- Size and stratification: default N=5,000 with stratified buckets: 50% high-frequency queries, 30% mid-tail, 20% long-tail/edge cases. For multilingual workloads ensure language parity in each bucket.
- Include labeled ground-truth nearest neighbors for at least 2,000 items for Recall and MRR calculations.

Promotion checklist (pre-canary)

1. Automated offline eval: pass all gating thresholds on probe set and evaluation suite.
2. Human review: sample 200 items from high-delta bucket and perform pairwise semantic rating (same / similar / different). Accept at least 92% same/similar for search workloads.
3. Quantization verification: if candidate uses quantization, run quantization delta checks and synthetic cache/kv-access simulations.
4. Latency/cost smoke: verify p95 token/embedding latency and per-embedding cost estimates.
5. Canary config prepared: traffic split, rollback flag, observability hooks.

Canary rollout and monitoring (production)

- Canary duration: minimum 24 hours or 100k queries, whichever is longer.
- Observability hooks to enable: per-request cosine delta percentiles, Recall@10 sampled telemetry, per-tenant/route error rates, and token/embedding latency histograms.
- Continuous gating during canary: if any critical threshold is crossed for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows, automatically trigger rollback. Warnings should notify owner and on-call.

Alerting and SLOs

- Alert types:
  - Warning alert: metric crosses warning threshold for 2 windows -> PagerDuty P2 to owner.
  - Critical alert: metric crosses critical threshold for 3 windows -> PagerDuty P1 and automatic rollback.
  - Drift growth alert: trend-based alert if median cosine declines by > 0.5% day-over-day for 3 days.

SLO guidance: Embedding models should target:
- Retrieval recall degradation <= 1% relative to baseline (monthly average).
- Median cosine self-similarity >= 0.90 across promoted versions.

Quantization-specific checks

- Run separate quantization delta tests: compare float baseline -> quantized candidate on both microbenchmarks and probe suite. Record distribution of cosine deltas and per-query rank shifts.
- If quantization introduces systematic bias (e.g., compresses magnitudes or reduces inter-class margin), require additional human validation and re-evaluation of dimensionality reduction/normalization steps.

Offline eval harness integration steps

1. Add probe set to eval-harness: include baseline embeddings and candidate outputs with deterministic seeding.
2. Run the 'embedding-fidelity' job which computes all metrics and writes a summary artifact to the promotion bucket.
3. Produce a regression report: metric deltas, flagged items (top 500 highest displacement), and human sample results.

Regression triage playbook (high-level)

1. Detection: automated monitor surfaces a regression (critical alert).
2. Initial containment: immediately switch affected traffic to baseline model using routing policy.
3. Triage steps:
   a) Run nondestructive diff - compute top-1 mismatches and p95 delta buckets.
   b) Correlate with recent infra or quantization deploys, tokenizer changes, or preprocessor updates.
   c) If quantization involved, run float vs quantized comparison to isolate quant delta.
   d) If tied to prompt/context distribution shift, snapshot distribution and escalate to product/analytics.
4. Remediation: rollback candidate or hotfix preprocessing/model code.

Ownership and roles

- Model owner: responsible for offline evals, promotion checklist, and human review samples.
- Observability/Platform: implement metrics, alerts, and canary routing.
- SRE: ensure rollback paths and traffic controls are tested in game-days.
- Product: approve impact assessment when user-facing retrieval is degraded.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1. On critical alert, Acknowledge and escalate to model owner and on-call.
2. Immediately enable routing override to baseline (console / CLI):
   - CLI example: redwood routing set --model-group emb-search --version baseline --force
3. Collect debug artifacts: sampled queries, embedding vectors from both models (first 1k), and metric snapshots.
4. Start triage: run offline embedding-fidelity job against the collected samples.
5. If rollback confirmed, open postmortem and schedule follow-up: re-run promotion checklist and add failing items to probe corpus.

Appendix: sample config (promotion.json)

{
  "probe_set": "emb-search-5k-v1",
  "baseline_model": "emb-v2-float",
  "candidate_model": "emb-v3-qat",
  "gating": {
    "median_cosine": 0.90,
    "recall10_relative": -0.01,
    "quant_delta_cosine": 0.03
  },
  "canary": {
    "min_duration_hours": 24,
    "min_queries": 100000,
    "rollback_on_critical": true
  }
}

References and links

- Related promotion playbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Quantization stability guide: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025
- Regression triage handbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Revision history

- 2026-02-15: initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-22: added gating thresholds and quantization section (reviewers: L. Chen).
- 2026-03-02: incorporated SRE rollback CLI and clarified canary windows (published).

payload.page_title: egress-contract-testbed-and-provisioning-harness

sections.body:
Blueprint and runbook for the multi-account egress contract testbed used to validate tenant-level egress SLAs, to provision ephemeral egress infrastructure via Terraform, and to integrate tests into CI/CD. Includes validation criteria, rollout/rollback steps, and monitoring/telemetry guidance.
Overview

This document describes the Egress Contract Testbed and Provisioning Harness: a repeatable test environment and IaC patterns for validating per-tenant egress contracts (bandwidth, NAT/HTTP success, routing correctness, and billing labels) across multi-account GPU workloads. The harness has three goals:

- Validate network-level SLOs before tenant onboarding and before major infra changes.
- Provide an automated, canary-style provisioning flow for ephemeral NAT/egress gateways used in CI.
- Offer a runbook for triage, rollback, and CI integration so changes are exercised automatically.

Design principles

1) Infrastructure-as-tests: treat egress behavior as a contract validated by automated CI that runs Terraform + active traffic tests.
2) Least privilege topology: ephemeral NAT/Gateway instances created in tenant accounts with time-limited roles and strict egress ACLs.
3) Observable assertions: every validation run emits metrics, traces, and artifacts for audit and billing reconciliation.
4) Safe rollouts: every Terraform change is gated by a contract test pass and a canary promotion policy.

Scope and when to use
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- New tenant onboarding requiring egress SLOs or bandwidth guarantees.
- Infra changes that affect NATs, proxies, routing, or BGP adverts.
- CI/CD validation for new Terraform modules that touch egress components.

High-level components

- Terraform provisioning modules (module.egress-testbed): creates ephemeral NAT gateway(s), a test VPC peering, IAM roles for the test harness, and a metrics exporter.
- Traffic generator (egress-checker): containerized test runner that issues HTTP/TCP workloads, measures throughput, success rates, and tail latency.
- Shadow-router (optional): a programmable virtual router that allows injecting route perturbations for resilience testing.
- Test orchestrator (buildkite / GitHub Actions): runs plan/apply + egress-checker, collects artifacts, and publishes pass/fail.
- Observability sink: Prometheus metrics, traces (jaeger compatible), and artifacts stored in S3/GCS for forensic review.

Contract validation matrix (example)

| Contract | Success criteria (CI) | Alert threshold | Artifact |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Per-tenant HTTP success | 99.95% 2m rolling window | <= 99.90% fail -> alert | egress-checker HTTP log + response histogram |
| Sustained bandwidth (burst) | >= 600 Mbps for 60s (burst tier) | < 580 Mbps -> fail test | iperf log + pcap sample |
| NAT session capacity | 120k concurrent ephemeral sessions | < 110k -> fail | netstat snapshot + exporter metrics |
| Labeling and billing tags | All egress flows contain expected X-Client-Tag header or NAT-tag | any missing tags -> fail | packet capture + tag report |

Terraform module usage (example)

Note: the module is intentionally minimal — real usage in tenant onboarding pipelines should supply account IDs, CIDR ranges, and TTLs for ephemeral resources. Example snippet for the test harness:

```hcl
module "egress_testbed" {
  source              = "git::ssh://git.internal.redwood/infra/terraform-modules.git//egress-testbed"
  tenant_account_id   = var.tenant_account_id
  region              = var.region
  allowed_destinations = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  ephemeral_ttl_hours = 4
  nat_instance_size   = "c6g.large"
  enable_shadow_router = true
  labels = { workload = "egress-contract-test" }
}
```

CI/CD integration

- Pipeline steps (Buildkite example):
  1. terraform init + fmt + validate
  2. terraform plan (submit artifact)
  3. gated approval (if applies to prod-like accounts)
  4. terraform apply (ephemeral resources)
  5. run egress-checker suite against the testbed (3 parallel scenarios: http, udp/bandwidth, route-perturbation)
  6. aggregate metrics and publish results to test report artifact
  7. terraform destroy (if run was ephemeral) or tag for promotion if passing and requested
sections.heading: Use the harness for

sections.body:
$ export TENANT=123456789012
$ export REGION=us-west-2
$ terragrunt apply -target=module.egress_testbed --terragrunt-non-interactive
$ docker run --rm -e TARGET_IP=$(terraform output -raw nat_ip) ghcr.io/redwood/egress-checker:stable --profile http,bandwidth,tagging --out /tmp/egress-result.json

Validation criteria and gating policy

- All three scenario groups (HTTP, bandwidth, tagging) must report PASS.
- If any scenario FAILs: pipeline marks change as failed, creates a rollback job, and notifies owners (pager duty and #infra-egress).
- For infra changes touching production NATs, run the same contract tests in a scheduled preflight window (see Runbook).

Runbook: triage and rollback (on test failure)

1. Inspect CI artifacts: /buildkite/artifacts/<run-id>/egress-result.json and pcap samples in S3.
2. Look at Prometheus metrics for exporter (egress_testbed:success_rate, egress_testbed:bandwidth_mbps).
3. If failure is reproducible locally: run the same terraform apply in a subordinate test account and reproduce.
4. If Terraform change caused failure: revert the PR or terraform apply the previous state (see fast rollback steps below).
5. If network route issue: use shadow-router to reapply baseline routes, or de-register BGP announcements that were recently added.
6. Notify stakeholders: #infra-egress, oncall (paging), and the tenant owning the change.

Fast rollback steps (Terraform-focused)

- If ephemeral testbed: simply `terraform destroy` to remove resources.
- If runway change in shared modules: 1) run `terraform state pull` and detect resource diff; 2) apply saved plan from before the PR (pipeline stores last known-good plan); 3) promote previous module tag in module registry and re-run apply.

Metrics and alerting

Recommended metrics to emit from the egress-testbed exporter:
- egress_testbed:http_success_rate (gauge, 0-100)
- egress_testbed:bandwidth_mbps (gauge)
- egress_testbed:nat_sessions (gauge)
- egress_testbed:tag_coverage_pct (gauge)
- egress_testbed:test_duration_seconds (histogram)
sections.heading: Command-line to run locally (example)

sections.body:
- ALERT EgressContractFailure WHEN egress_testbed:http_success_rate < 99.9 for 5m FOR 1m
- ALERT EgressBandwidthDrop WHEN egress_testbed:bandwidth_mbps < 80% of contract_burst for 2m

Ownership and run cadence

- Owner: Network Platform (eng-infra/networking)
- Secondary: GPU Fleet (eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity) for tenant impact analysis
- Scheduled runs: nightly in staging accounts; preflight runs before any ci-cd promotion touching egress modules; weekly canary in prod-mirroring account.

Security and IAM model

- Provisioned roles use short-lived credentials minted by the central provisioning service.
- Ephemeral NATs created with a least-privilege role: no access to customer data, only to tagging and metrics write.
- All pcap artifacts are stored in encrypted buckets with lifecycle 30 days, tagged with run-id and owner team.

Testing matrix and acceptance checklist

1. Module plan + lint: terraform validate + tflint + tfsec (no high severity findings).
2. Provisioning smoke: nat_ip responds to ICMP and metadata endpoint configured.
3. HTTP contract: 2m window at 1-3 rps, 99.95% success.
4. Burst contract: iperf runs at configured bandwidth for 60s.
5. Labeling test: random header injection and NAT-tag confirmation.
6. Billing reconciliation: ensure exported tag summary matches the billing-collector mapping.

Operational notes and gotchas

- Be careful with ephemeral_ttl_hours: long-lived ephemeral NATs can accidentally get picked up by billing reports.
- Shadow-router increases test complexity; isolate it from production BGP sessions.
- On AWS, NAT instance vs NAT gateway cost/behavior differs; our module defaults to instance for testbeds to allow packet capture.

Appendix A — example egress-checker CLI output (truncated)

{
  "run_id": "bk-20260130-1467",
  "http_success_rate": 99.97,
  "bandwidth_mbps": 612.4,
  "nat_sessions": 121200,
  "tag_coverage_pct": 100
}

Appendix B — escalation contacts

- Primary oncall: Network Platform (pager: +1-555-0101)
- Secondary: GPU Fleet lead (slack: @diegom)
- Billing integrator: Finance-Cloud tags (email: cloud-billing@redwood.com)

Appendix C — links and references

- See related runbooks for preflight and rollback: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook
- Terraform modules repo: git.internal.redwood/infra/terraform-modules (private)
- Buildkite pipeline templates: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/buildkite-gpu-provisioning-gate-and-canary-strategy

Revision history

- 2025-02-14: created by Sofia Kline (initial draft)
- 2025-08-10: added shadow-router section and iperf-based burst test (review by Liam Chen)
- 2026-01-30: finalized gating policy and CI artifacts standardization (reviewers Priya Rao, Diego Martinez)

payload.page_title: Annotator Ops — Incident Response, Escrow & Quality Containment Procedure

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the operational procedure for annotation workforce incidents that threaten eval integrity or production-quality guardrails. It covers detection signals, immediate containment steps, escrowing of contested annotation assets, short-term remediation, and post-incident review requirements. The goal is to preserve evaluation provenance, minimize label corruption, and restore trustworthy evaluator/annotator state within defined SLOs.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: in-house annotators, managed third-party vendors, and contractor annotator pools used for probes, prompts, and gold labels associated with evaluation assets.
- Not in scope: model training data acquisition pipelines (separate data governance policy), provider-only telemetry incidents that never touch human labels.

Definitions:
- Contested asset: any probe, prompt, or annotation bundle suspected of compromise (e.g., sudden label drift, coordinated low-agreement).
- Escrow: a write-once, access-controlled snapshot of contested assets and associated metadata (annotator ids, timestamps, session logs).
- Quarantine cohort: subset of annotators or probes suspended from routing while investigation occurs.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Lead (IL) — typically the applied-ml oncall or annotation steward. Owns containment, escalation, and sign-off.
- Annotation Steward — operational owner for the annotator pool; responsible for escrow snapshot and vendor coordination.
- Quality SME — product/ML engineer who assesses quality impact and approves remediation.
- Security Liaison — engages if there is suspected malicious activity or PII leakage.
- Legal/Compliance — engaged for regulatory incidents or customer-sensitive content.

Detection signals (examples):
1) Sudden drop in inter-annotator agreement (IAA) for a probe family: >= 15 percentage points relative to 7-day rolling baseline.
2) Spike in label entropy or label-flip rate: > 3x normal for same slice.
3) Anomalous annotator session behavior: >= 4 short sessions (< 2 minutes) followed by many identical labels.
4) External report: customer or internal reviewer flags consistent mislabeling on high-sensitivity probes.

Immediate containment checklist (TL;DR for first 30 minutes):
1. Triage: IL declares an annotation integrity incident and sets severity (Critical | High | Medium | Low).
2. Quarantine: stop routing new assignments to suspect annotators / vendor cohort and mark related probes as contested.
3. Escrow snapshot: create a timestamped, immutable export of contested assets and session logs (see Escrow procedure).
4. Notify: page Quality SME and Security Liaison if PII or malicious indicators are present.
5. Communication: update an incident thread in the eval-ops channel and record short summary in the incident tracker.

Escrow procedure (runnable steps):
- Precondition: annotator telemetry retention must include session_id, worker_id (pseudonymized), assignment_id, start/end timestamps, and raw label payload.
- CLI snapshot example (internal tooling):
```
# create escrow bundle for probe-family "account-auth" between timestamps
eval-escrow create --probe-family account-auth --from 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-06-01T06:00:00Z --output /escrow/2026-06-01-account-auth.tar.gz
eval-escrow attest --bundle /escrow/2026-06-01-account-auth.tar.gz --owner maya.chen@redwood.ai
```
- Access control: escrow bundles are stored in S3 bucket redwood-escrow-{env}, encrypted with KMS key arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/escrow. Access requires IL + Annotation Steward approval in the access request system.
- Retention: contested escrow bundles are retained for 180 days by default; longer retention requires Legal approval.

Containment decision matrix (where to route probes during incident):
| Severity | Immediate routing behavior | Notes |
| Critical | Pause all related probe traffic to hosted eval mesh | Only synthetic can continue for unaffected families |
| High | Route to shadow-only (no production scoring) | Enables triage without production impact |
| Medium | Reduce sampling rate by 90% and flag outputs | Conservative approach for borderline cases |
| Low | Continue with increased monitoring | Alert Quality SME for manual checks |

Triage investigation steps (hour 0–6):
1. Recompute slice-level metrics (IAA, label entropy, repeat-label frequency) for contested assets.
2. Compare session fingerprints against baseline: IP geography, browser agent, session cadence.
3. Re-annotate a 5–10% stratified random sample with trusted annotators (blind duplication) to estimate contamination.
4. If contamination > 10% of sample, escalate to Remediation; otherwise close as false alarm with notes.

Remediation playbook (when contamination confirmed):
1. Rollback and scrub: remove contested labels from active evals and flag impacted results.
2. Re-annotation: schedule re-labeling with trusted annotator cohort; use double-blind consensus (N=3) for high-sensitivity slices.
3. Quarantine annotators: disable accounts and preserve telemetry for forensics.
4. Vendor action: if vendor-managed, move to contractual remediation path and apply holdback clauses as required.
5. Model/Metric impact: recompute key eval metrics and publish delta report to stakeholders.

Quality SLOs and thresholds (operational targets):
- Detection SLA: Contested-signal alert acknowledged by IL within 30 minutes in 90% of incidents.
- Containment SLA: Quarantine and escrow snapshot completed within 60 minutes for Critical/High incidents.
- Resolution SLA: Re-annotation workflow started within 72 hours for impacted high-sensitivity probes.
- Root-cause review: Post-incident review published within 7 calendar days.

Forensic artifacts and mandatory evidence set (for every incident):
- Escrow bundle (labels, session metadata, assignment traces)
- Snapshot of eval-mesh requests/response logs correlated by probe_id
- Annotator roster snapshot and policy state at incident time
- Re-annotation sample results and reconciliation notes
- Communication log and approvals for access to escrow

Communication checklist (stakeholder cadence):
- T+0 (initial): short incident page and triage classification to eval-ops channel and IL pager.
- T+6 (status): preliminary contamination estimate and containment actions to product and ML lead.
- T+72 (remediation start): plan for reannotation and expected customer-facing impact.
- T+7 (postmortem): published RCA and action items.

Post-incident review template (minimum sections):
1. Executive summary
2. Timeline of detection → containment → remediation
3. Root cause analysis (human error / tooling / vendor / adversarial)
4. Evidence bundles (links to escrow and forensic logs)
5. Cost and coverage impact (probe counts, affected evals, annotated hours)
6. Action items (owners, deadlines, verification criteria)
7. Preventative controls to be implemented (triage automation, sampling rules, SLA changes)

Preventative controls (recommended):
- Active telemetry fuzzing: randomized blind checks routed to internal trusted annotators at a 0.5% sampling rate.
- Agreement sentinel triggers: automatic incident creation when IAA delta > 12 pts for a probe family.
- Vendor audit clause: quarterly quality attestations and a minimum double-annotation rate for sensitive slices.
- Annotator identity hygiene: pseudonymization + rotating worker identifiers to reduce targeted collusion risk.

Operational runbook snippets (automation examples):
- Auto-create incident when metric crosses threshold (pseudo-DSL):
```
on metric("probe.IAA.delta") > 12 pts for 1h -> create incident(type=annotation-integrity) -> attach telemetry bundle
```
- Reannotation workflow kickoff (HTTP API):
POST /internal/reannotation/start
Body: {"probe_family":"account-auth","sample_size":250,"consensus_policy":"n=3-majority"}

Audit and compliance notes:
- Any incident affecting customer-sourced probes must notify Legal within 24 hours.
- Retention of escrow bundles for customer-impacting incidents extends to 7 years if requested by Legal/Compliance.

Open questions and future work:
- Automated label provenance hashing for faster integrity checks (prototype Q3 2026).
- Standard vendor SLAs for annotation speed vs. double-annotation guarantees.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline (illustrative):
- 10:03 UTC: monitoring alert triggered (IAA delta = 18).
- 10:07 UTC: IL acknowledged, quarantined vendor cohort, paused probe routing.
- 10:25 UTC: escrow bundle created and attested.
- 13:00 UTC: re-annotation pilot of 200 items with trusted cohort; contamination = 14%.
- 14:30 UTC: remediation plan approved; re-annotation scheduled, vendor contract notified.
- 2026-03-22: Postmortem published with action items to add sentinel-based auto-triage.

Appendix B — Example evidence JSON schema (for tooling integration):
{
  "probe_id":"string",
  "bundle_id":"string",
  "captured_at":"ISO-8601 timestamp",
  "annotator_ids":["pseud-1","pseud-2"],
  "raw_labels":"base64 or path to object store"
}

Related artifacts and recommended links:
- Evaluator onboarding & certification curriculum (link in related_pages)
- Probe asset deprecation & redistribution policy (link in related_pages)

Owner and contact:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml) — maya.chen@redwood.ai
- Secondary: Ravi Kapoor (annotation steward) — ravi.kapoor@redwood.ai

Change history:
- 2026-03-15: Initial draft.
- 2026-04-12: Added escrow CLI examples and retention clarifications.
- 2026-06-01: Updated SLAs and communication cadence based on Q2 incident drills.

payload.page_title: multi-probe-failure-classifier-and-automated-mitigation-manifest

sections.body:
Summary

This document specifies the Multi-Probe Failure Classifier (MPFC) and the accompanying automated mitigation manifest. MPFC is a lightweight, explainable classifier that aggregates heterogeneous probe signals (functional, coherence, latency, token-economy, and quant-sensitivity probes) to categorize degradations and drive deterministic mitigation actions. The goal is to reduce time-to-recovery for production quality incidents while limiting blast radius for safety and customer-facing regressions.

Scope

- Applies to all model-serving promotion targets (hosted, dedicated, and private) where probe telemetry is ingested into the central eval mesh.
- Focused on runtime performance and output quality regressions that can be observed via probe families (see Definitions).
- Not intended for manual labeling pipelines, data privacy incidents, or infra-only failures (see Exception list).

Definitions

1. Probe: an automated query or synthetic interaction designed to exercise a specific slice of behavior (e.g., few-shot instruction consistency, long-context coherence, embedding similarity).
2. Signal: a numerical or categorical feature emitted by a probe (e.g., pass/fail, perplexity delta, embedding cosine, token delta).
3. Failure class: high-level category assigned by MPFC (coherence-drift, hallucination-spike, latency-tail, quant-artifact, behavioral-flip, routing-fallback).
4. Mitigation: an automated operational action (e.g., rollback, throttle, route-to-variant, degrade-quant, increase-batch-window, open-chan).

Failure taxonomy and classifier design

- Coherence-drift: Multi-turn context coherence drops, measured via turn-level coherence score delta > 8% and increase in repetition metric.
- Hallucination-spike: Increased factually-incorrect outputs flagged by synthetic fact-check probes (false positive rate increase > 5% absolute).
- Latency-tail: P95 latency > 800ms or P99 > 2s for gen endpoints serving SLO-sensitive routes.
- Quant-artifact: Sudden rise in token-level inconsistency between float and quant shadow runs (disagreement ratio > 3%).
- Behavioral-flip: Deterministic change in a labeled prompt family where label accuracy drops > 7%.
- Routing-fallback: Increased fallback-to-secondary-model events > 4% of traffic.

Classifier inputs and feature engineering

- Inputs (examples): ["p95_ms", "p99_ms", "coherence_delta_pct", "repetition_score_delta", "fp_rate_delta", "token_disagreement_pct", "fallback_rate", "embedding_shift_cosine", "kvcache_hit_rate"].
- Time windows: compute short (5m), medium (1h), and trend (24h) aggregates. Classifier uses delta between short and trend windows to detect sudden shifts.
- Explainability: MPFC outputs a top-3 contributing signals per classification for operator triage.

Alerting and thresholds

- Severity levels: P1 (customer-impacting, auto-mitigation allowed), P2 (degrades SLOs, require review before mitigation), P3 (informational).
- Example thresholds (configurable per-service):

| Metric | P1 threshold | P2 threshold | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (ms) | >1200 | 800-1200 | SLO-sensitive routes only |
| coherence_delta_pct | >10% | 5-10% | measured on prioritized slices |
| fp_rate_delta | >6% abs | 2-6% abs | applies to fact-check probes |
| token_disagreement_pct | >5% | 2-5% | comparing quant vs float |

Automated mitigation flow (high level)

1. Detection: Probe mesh emits a trigger event when classifier score >= configured severity threshold.
2. Enrichment: MPFC fetches recent traces, model version tags, rollout state, shadow cohort metrics, and last-deploy commit.
3. Scoring: Compute confidence and top-3 reasons; determine allowable mitigations based on service policy.
4. Action: Execute mitigation (examples below). Actions are conditionally gated by safety checks and cooldown windows.
5. Post-action evaluation: Run focused sanity probes (micro-slice) against mitigated traffic and hold for 10 minutes. If metrics improve, create an incident record and schedule manual review; if not, revert mitigation.

Mitigation action catalog (examples)

- Route-to-variant: Move 30%→0% traffic to the variant causing issues and redistribute to stable baseline.
- Auto-rollback: Switch active model version to previous stable version if regression type in [behavioral-flip, hallucination-spike] and confidence > 0.9.
- Degrade-quant: For quant-artifact class, switch to higher-precision quant or fallback to float path for 10% of requests.
- Throttle/buffer: For latency-tail, enable increased batching up to 2x and return 503 on overflow edges to protect SLOs.
- Canary-throttle: Reduce canary weight from x% to x/2% and trigger shadow replay for failing probes.

Runbook: step-by-step automated mitigation procedure

1. Receive MPFC P1 event -> run enrichment and compute mitigation candidates.
2. Verify no active security flags in last 24h (if flags present, escalate to SRE + Security and do not auto-mitigate).
3. If confidence >= 0.9 and policy allows auto-rollback, trigger rollback via deployment api:

   curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/deployments/rollback
   -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN'
   -d '{"service":"text-gen","target_version":"v1.14.2","reason":"mpfc-auto-rollback"}'

4. If mitigation is route-to-variant, call traffic-router patch with safety envelope: reduce by 30% max per minute and monitor micro-probes.
5. Post-action: run 3 focused probes from the failing slice and wait 10 minutes. If all three pass thresholds, create a templated incident and page the owner_team with summary and top-3 reasons.
6. If the mitigation fails to improve metrics after 2 attempts, escalate to on-call product+ml owner.

Configuration reference (example service-level manifest)

| field | type | allowed values | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| service | string | service name | none | logical service id to apply MPFC |
| severity_policy | object | P1/P2/P3 buckets | company-default | mapping of classifier score -> actions |
| auto_mitigate | boolean | true/false | false | global opt-in toggle per service |
| cooldown_minutes | integer | 0-1440 | 30 | cooldown between mitigations |
| allowed_actions | list | [rollback,route,degrade-quant,throttle] | [route,throttle] | permitted automated actions |

Safety and constraints

- Auto-mitigation is disabled for services with high-risk labels (safety, compliance, billing).
- Any rollback that changes persisted state or customer-visible outputs requires a must-pass sanity probe set.
- Rate-limited: max 2 auto-mitigations per 24h per service to avoid flapping.
- All automated actions produce an audit event with owner, reason, and pre/post snapshots.

Testing and validation

- Unit tests: deterministic classifier tests covering synthetic failure injections.
- Integration: run MPFC in dry-run mode for 14 days against shadow traffic; compare suggested mitigations with human decisions.
- Game-day: quarterly simulation where we inject a quant-artifact and validate full mitigation loop (detection->action->post-eval->audit).

Observability and dashboards

- Dashboard panels: active mitigations (last 24h), classifier confidence histogram, top failure classes by service, mitigation success ratio.
- Logs: structured mitigation_event records with fields {service, action, confidence, reasons, pre_metrics, post_metrics}.

Ownership and SLOs

- MPFC owner: Applied ML Platform (owner on-call = applied-ml-platform-oncall).
- SLOs: detection latency < 2m (time from probe emission to classifier decision) 99% of the time; auto-mitigation success rate > 75% for P1 events where auto-mitigation is allowed.

Rollout checklist

1. Dry-run for 14 days with mitigation suggestions logged (no actions).
2. Enable auto-mitigations for internal-only services with rollback allowed (canary cohort = 5%).
3. Expand to external services with progressively larger cohorts after manual review cycles.
4. Publish runbook and add training for on-call teams.

Governance and review cadence

- Monthly review of mitigation audit logs and false-positive/false-negative cases.
- Quarterly policy review to adjust thresholds and allowed actions.

Appendix A — example classifier output (JSON snippet)

{
  "service": "text-gen-prod",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-10T12:03:22Z",
  "class": "coherence-drift",
  "confidence": "0.93",
  "top_reasons": ["coherence_delta_pct:12.4%", "repetition_score_delta:9.1%", "kvcache_hit_rate:-6.8%"],
  "suggested_actions": ["route-to-stable", "run-sanity-probes"]
}

Appendix B — exceptions list

- Any service with label: "privacy-sensitive" or "regulatory-bound".
- Incident with correlated security signals (escalate to Security).

References

- Applied-eval mesh spec (internal)
- Regression impact index and prioritization framework (see related_pages)

Contact

- Primary owner: Aisha Khan (applied-ml-platform)
- Pager: #applied-ml-oncall

payload.page_title: Contrastive probe assembly and sweeping guidelines

sections.body:
Overview

This guideline defines a contrastive, instrumented approach to assembling probe families and sweeping them through the eval mesh so we can detect subtle regressions, quantization sensitivity, and prompt coverage gaps before promoting model artifacts to production. It ties together probe fabrication, priority-led scheduling, quantization-aware sampling, and rapid regression triage hooks into a single operational playbook.

When to use this document

- New model onboarding where prompt families are large or heterogeneous
- Quantization or mixed-precision migration projects that require targeted sensitivity checks
- Routine sweep windows for high-risk services (high revenue or high regulatory sensitivity)
- After a rollout that impacted tail behavior or embedding stability

Terminology

- probe family: a group of related prompts and expected outputs designed to exercise a behavior class
- conductor: the service that assembles and schedules probes (service name: probe-conductor)
- sweep: a single pass of a probe family across one or more model variants and runtime configurations
- anchor set: small, stable sub-sample used as baseline for absolute deltas
- fidelity gate: a quantitative rule that must be satisfied before promotion

Principles

- contrast-first: always include at least one contrasting probe per family to expose symmetric failure modes
- telemetry-driven: scheduling and priority are driven by recent production telemetry and heatmaps
- quant-aware: include quant and kv-cache variants in every sweep for cache-sensitive workloads
- fast-fail triage: attach automated triage metadata so a triage runbook can start within 5 minutes of a failing sweep

Probe assembly pipeline (conductor flow)

1. Input collection
   - Sources: production slow traces, human-reported failures, synthetic slice generator, localization team submissions
   - Minimum metadata: tenant id, endpoint route, approximate token budget, expected response anchor or rubric id

2. Canonicalization and normalization
   - Strip ephemeral user identifiers, canonicalize dates, normalize numbers to ranges
   - Tag probes with slice tags, complexity score (0.0-1.0), and cache sensitivity flag

3. Contrast insertion
   - For each positive probe add 1-2 contrast probes that change a single variable (role, numerical value, negation)

4. Prioritization and batching
   - Assign priority using scoring: priority = production-frequency*0.6 + failure-likelihood*0.3 + business-impact*0.1
   - Conductor groups probes into batches respecting per-model token budgets and latency targets

5. Export to sweep manifest
   - Manifest fields: probe_id, family, priority, anchor_id, batch_hint, streaming_required(true|false), quant_variants [q4h, q5, fullfp], routes [text-gen, chat, rerank]

Sweeping strategy

- Sweep windows
  - Canary sweeps: after model build and before canary deploy, run full anchor set plus high-priority families (expected run time < 30 min)
  - Nightly sweeps: run extended families across quant variants and stored shadow pool (run time 2-6 hours)
  - Emergency sweeps: ad-hoc runs targeted to failing families with accelerated triage hooks

- Variant matrix
  - Always include: production full-fp baseline, quant candidate(s), kv-cache-on, kv-cache-off
  - Optional: reduced-batching runtime, dedicated-gpu profile, burst-mode routing simulation

Quality guardrails and gates

- Primary quantitative gates (per-family)
  - anchor accuracy delta: absolute delta <= 2.0% on anchor metric (classification EM/ROUGE/CIDER as appropriate)
  - response-stability-index (RSI): RSI <= 0.15 for text-generation families
  - embedding-stability: mean cosine similarity vs baseline >= 0.985 for embedding families
  - latency SLO: p95 <= 250 ms for interactive families when run against dedicated runtime profile
  - token-economy: median token cost per probe change <= 20% vs baseline for production routes

- Promotion policy
  - All fidelity gates must pass for canary promotion unless explicitly waived by the product owner with a documented risk acceptance
  - A single failure in a high-severity family triggers a blocked promotion and automatic assignment to regression-triage queue

Quantization-aware assembly notes

- Include a quant sensitivity tag at probe level when probes include long-context triggers, functioncall sequences, or structured outputs
- For each quant sweep, compute: token-level divergence histogram, per-token entropy delta, and functioncall-argument mismatch rate
- If more than 5% of probes exceed token-level divergence threshold 0.12 then mark quant candidate as high-risk

Regression triage hooks and automation

- triage metadata that must be attached to every failing sweep
  - failing_probe_ids, stack snapshot id, model-artifact-id, runtime-config-id, last-successful-artifact-id, diffed-anchor-output
- automatic bisect starter
  - On failure, conductor enqueues a bisect job against previous 5 artifacts using the causal-regression harness; label assigned: auto-bisect-queued
- human-in-the-loop escalation
  - If auto-bisect is inconclusive after 3 rounds, create a regression issue in tracker with triage payload and assign to owner team

Operational runbook (fast path)

1. detect: conductor sweep fails gate for family X and posts event to #probe-alerts
2. auto-bisect: system starts bisect across last 5 artifacts, posts progress to alert thread (expected 15-45 minutes)
3. enrich: triage assistant attaches recent production traces and top-10 similar probes to the issue
4. owner review: owner reviews bisect result and decides rollback or mitigation within SLA (4 hours for critical families)
5. rollback: if rollback chosen, trigger artifact rollback pipeline and ramp-down promotion window

Example sweep manifest table

| field | example value | notes |
|-------|---------------|-------|
| probe_id | pf-20251112-042 | probe conductor id |
| family | payment-confirmation-ambiguity | logical family |
| priority | 0.82 | computed score |
| quant_variants | [fullfp, q4h] | encoded as list |
| anchor_id | anchor-042 | reference anchor |
| batch_hint | tokens<=2048 | used by conductor |

CLI and API examples

- schedule a sweep via conductor REST endpoint (curl example)

  curl -s -X POST 'https://internal-api.redwood/probe-conductor/v1/sweeps' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SVC_TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"manifest_ref": "manifests/pf-20251112-042.json", "priority_override": "high"}'

- view sweep status (jq-friendly)

  curl -s 'https://internal-api.redwood/probe-conductor/v1/sweeps/pf-20251112-042/status' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SVC_TOKEN' | jq '.progress, .failures'

Example YAML manifest (minimal)

  ---
  manifest_id: pf-20251112-042
  owner: ml-probes
  probes:
    - probe_id: pf-042-a
      family: payment-confirmation-ambiguity
      priority: 0.82
      quant_variants: [fullfp, q4h]
      streaming_required: false

Telemetry and dashboards

- required telemetry emitted by conductor for every sweep
  - sweep_id, probe_id, family, model_artifact, runtime_profile, token_count, p95_latency_ms, rsi, embedding_cosine_mean, gate_pass(boolean), failure_reason
- dashboards to create
  - Probe heatmap by family and region (last 30d)
  - Quant sensitivity scatter (entropy delta vs token divergence)
  - Auto-bisect success rate and mean time to first bisect result

Ownership and escalation

- owner: ml-probes (primary), applied-ml-oncall (secondary)
- escalation path:
  - 0-1 hour: paging to applied-ml-oncall if family tagged critical
  - 1-4 hours: owner team review and rollback decision window
  - >4 hours: engage platform-sre and product owner

Appendix A: telemetry schema (line-delimited JSON example)

  { sweep_id: pf-20251112-042, probe_id: pf-042-a, model_artifact: model-v1.12.3, runtime: dedicated-gpu, rsi: 0.12, p95_latency_ms: 220, gate_pass: true }

Appendix B: decision checklist for marginal failures

- Is the failure localized to quant variant only? If yes, consider targeted rollback of quant candidate
- Does production telemetry show correlated increase in user-visible errors? If yes, prioritize rollback
- Can we mitigate with prompt rewrite or caching tweak? If yes, schedule short-lived route patch and re-run partial sweep

Notes and references

- See related operational contracts: /applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/response-stability-index-calibration-and-deployment-2026 and /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-sequencer-and-fallback-orchestration-2026 for integration points
- This guideline is intentionally prescriptive about manifest fields to keep conductor outputs stable for automation and triage tools

Document history

- author: Maya Chen, created 2025-11-12
- review: Diego Alvarez (2025-12-03), Priya Natarajan (2026-01-24)

End of document
