payload.page_title: Benchmark Data Validation & Review Checklist (Latency/$ Report)

sections.body:
This checklist defines the minimum validation and review steps required before Redwood Inference publishes any benchmark-derived numbers (web table, PDF, blog charts, sales enablement). It is designed to:
- Prevent accidental cherry-picking or misconfigured runs.
- Detect missing regions/models and instability (variance) early.
- Standardize outlier handling and rerun criteria.
- Ensure public artifacts are reproducible and safe (redacted), with a clear sign-off trail.

This document applies to the **Latency/$ Benchmark Report** and any subsequent refreshes/addenda.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- **Run**: One execution of a workload against a specific (model, region, deployment mode, hardware profile, config).
- **Sweep**: A set of runs covering a region×model matrix.
- **Manifest**: The canonical machine-readable record for a run (config, environment, inputs, timestamps, commit SHAs, metrics pointers).
- **Derived dataset**: Aggregated outputs used in public claims (latency/$, $/1M tokens, p50/p95, throughput).
- **Stability gate**: Automated rule that triggers reruns or blocks publish when variance exceeds thresholds.
sections.heading: Definitions (quick)

sections.body:
[ ] 1. Run manifests for all runs included in the report (including reruns).
[ ] 2. Raw logs/metrics pointers referenced by manifests (stored per retention policy).
[ ] 3. Derived dataset (CSV + JSON) with schema version and generation timestamp.
[ ] 4. Data dictionary / metric definitions used for computation (must match methodology page).
[ ] 5. Validation report (automated checks output + manual reviewer notes).
[ ] 6. Redaction report confirming removal of sensitive identifiers in public artifacts.
sections.heading: Required artifacts (must exist before review)

sections.body:
- Models: (list in release ticket / methodology lock)
- Regions: NA/EU/APAC where available
- Deployment mode(s): Hosted (default), and if applicable Dedicated/Private notes
- Workloads: prompt set version(s), concurrency tiers, context-length buckets
sections.heading: Populate the expected set for the specific release

sections.body:
[ ] The expected matrix is written down (link to the release ticket / commit tag).
[ ] Each published table/chart references only a single locked matrix (no ad-hoc additions).
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
Hard-block conditions (must be resolved or explicitly removed from scope with PMM+tech lead approval):
[ ] Any expected region is missing for a model that is otherwise published.
[ ] Any expected model is missing for a region that is otherwise published.
[ ] Any expected workload tier (e.g., concurrency level) is missing for a (model, region) entry.

Acceptable exceptions (must be documented in the “Release Notes / Caveats” section of the report):
- Region temporarily unavailable due to capacity constraints AND removed consistently across all models for that section.
- Model not supported in a region (documented limitation with date).
sections.heading: A2. Missing region/model detection (hard block)

sections.body: [ ] A one-paragraph explanation is included for each exception, with an internal link to the incident/ticket and the date.
sections.heading: Documentation requirement

sections.body:
Each manifest must include, at minimum:
- Run identity: run_id, sweep_id, start/end timestamps (UTC)
- Code provenance: benchmark harness git SHA, runner image digest, config file checksum
- Environment: cloud provider, region, instance type/GPU SKU, driver/CUDA/runtime versions
- Model: model_id, model version/revision, quantization profile (if any)
- Serving config: batching on/off + parameters, caching policy + parameters, max tokens, streaming on/off (if applicable)
- Workload: prompt_set_id + version, token distribution settings, concurrency level, request rate (if rate-driven)
- Warmup: warmup duration/requests and exclusion policy
- Metrics pointers: paths/URIs to raw logs and summarized metrics
- Cost inputs: pricing table version, currency, cost attribution source
sections.heading: B1. Manifest schema validation (automated)

sections.body:
[ ] Manifest passes schema validation with **zero** missing required fields.
[ ] Manifest includes runner image digest (not just a tag).
[ ] Manifest includes the benchmark harness git SHA (not “dirty”).
[ ] All referenced raw metric URIs resolve and are accessible to the review group.
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
For each sweep, randomly sample at least 5% of runs (minimum 5 runs) and confirm:
[ ] Model ID/version matches the published label.
[ ] Region matches the published label.
[ ] Concurrency tier and token limits match the methodology.
[ ] Caching/batching policy matches the methodology (or is explicitly marked as an experimental addendum).
[ ] No “debug” flags were used (e.g., reduced iterations, disabled kernels, forced low batch).
sections.heading: B2. Config integrity (manual spot checks)

sections.body:
[ ] No negative or zero values for latency, throughput, or cost.
[ ] p95 >= p50 for all entries (if violated: investigate aggregation bug or mixed populations).
[ ] Throughput is within plausible range for the hardware tier (flag extreme values for review).
[ ] Cost-per-token and $/1M tokens are within plausible bounds (flag order-of-magnitude errors).
sections.heading: C1. Basic sanity checks

sections.body:
[ ] latency/$ is consistent with its definition (units and directionality). Confirm the report uses one label consistently (e.g., “lower is better” vs “higher is better”).
[ ] If both throughput and latency are reported, ensure they were measured over the same window (post-warmup).
[ ] If streaming metrics are included, confirm whether latency is time-to-first-token (TTFT) vs end-to-end; ensure charts do not mix definitions.
sections.heading: C2. Cross-field invariants

sections.body:
[ ] Deduplicate runs: no identical (model, region, workload, timestamp window) counted twice unless clearly labeled as separate replicates.
[ ] Remove partial runs: any run with aborted execution, missing metrics, or known infra incident overlap must be excluded.
[ ] All exclusions are logged with reason code (see Section F).
sections.heading: C3. Duplicate and partial runs

sections.body: Outliers can occur due to queueing effects, transient network issues, kernel selection changes, or noisy neighbors. We do not remove outliers to “improve” results; we remove them only when we can attribute them to non-representative run conditions or obvious measurement errors.
sections.heading: D1. Outlier policy (default)

sections.body:
1) Prefer **rerun** over exclusion when instability is detected.
2) Exclude only when one of the following is true:
   - Known incident overlap (capacity disruption, elevated 5xx/429, runner error).
   - Measurement artifact (missing warmup exclusion, timestamp misalignment, corrupted metrics file).
   - Manifest indicates mismatched config vs methodology.
sections.heading: Default policy

sections.body:
[ ] Outliers are flagged automatically using a robust rule (see D2), but removal requires an explicit reason.
[ ] Any excluded run has a reason code and linked evidence (ticket/incident/log snippet).
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
- Within each (model, region, workload tier), compute median and MAD (median absolute deviation).
- Flag runs where p95 latency deviates by > 3.5 MAD from the median.
- Also flag cost anomalies where $/1M tokens deviates by > 3 MAD.
sections.heading: Use a robust detector for triage (not auto-exclusion)

sections.body:
[ ] Flagged outliers are reviewed by the benchmark owner (Applied ML) and one runtime reviewer.
[ ] The number of flagged runs and resolution outcome is recorded in the validation report.
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
- Each (model, region, workload tier) must have at least **3 valid replicates**.
- Replicates must be non-overlapping in time (avoid back-to-back runs only).
sections.heading: Unless otherwise specified in the methodology lock

sections.body: [ ] Replicate count meets minimum for every published cell.
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
Trigger reruns when any of the following is true within a (model, region, workload tier):
- p95 latency coefficient of variation (CV) > **7%** across replicates
- OR median p95 differs by > **10%** between two consecutive sweeps in the same day
- OR throughput CV > **8%** (if throughput is used in narrative claims)
sections.heading: E2. Variance thresholds (auto-rerun)

sections.body:
1) Rerun up to 2 additional replicates.
2) If instability persists, escalate to Runtime + Infra to diagnose (queueing, kernel changes, capacity).
3) If unresolved within timeline, either (a) remove the cell from publication, or (b) publish with a clearly labeled “higher variance” caveat (requires PMM + tech lead approval).
sections.heading: Rerun protocol

sections.body:
[ ] Stability gates executed and results attached to the validation report.
[ ] Any “publish with variance caveat” is pre-approved and mirrored across all assets (web + PDF + enablement).
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
For refreshes or v1.1+ updates:
- If latency/$ changes by > **15%** for a previously published (model, region) cell, require a short root-cause note (expected vs unexpected).
sections.heading: E3. Regression guardrails vs last published version (refreshes)

sections.body: [ ] Large deltas are explained (e.g., new runtime version, different GPU SKU, different prompt set, pricing update).
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
Maintain an exclusion log for auditability. Minimum columns:
- run_id
- (model, region, workload tier)
- exclusion_reason_code (INCIDENT, CONFIG_MISMATCH, CORRUPT_METRICS, PARTIAL_RUN, OTHER)
- reviewer
- link_to_evidence (incident/ticket/log)
- date
sections.heading: F. Exclusion log (required format)

sections.body:
[ ] Exclusion log exists and is stored alongside derived datasets.
[ ] Exclusions are reflected consistently (no excluded run appears in any chart/table export).
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
Public exports (CSV/JSON) and any embedded examples must not include:
- Customer identifiers, org IDs, API keys, request IDs that can be correlated externally
- Internal hostnames, fleet IDs, or instance IDs
- Raw prompts that contain customer data (prompt sets must be synthetic/approved)
sections.heading: G1. Redaction checklist (hard block)

sections.body:
[ ] Redaction step executed on all public artifacts.
[ ] A reviewer (Security/Compliance partner) confirms the redaction report.
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
[ ] All metric definitions in assets match the methodology page (names + units).
[ ] Any comparative language (e.g., “faster”, “cheaper”, “best”) is either removed or explicitly scoped with substantiation and disclaimers.
[ ] Charts include required footnotes/disclaimers (variance, workload definition, date range, hardware notes).
sections.heading: G2. Claims alignment checklist

sections.body: Sign-off is required before publishing (web and PDF). The validation report must include names + dates.
sections.heading: H. Sign-off roles (who approves what)

sections.body:
- Applied ML (Methodology & Data): Owns dataset correctness and adherence to methodology
  - Primary: Jonas Weber or Claire Dubois
  - Delegate: Rina Kobayashi
- Runtime (Serving correctness/perf): Confirms runtime config integrity and investigates anomalies
  - Primary: Noah Patel
- Infra/Fleet (Region capacity realism): Confirms region sweeps ran under intended capacity conditions
  - Primary: Vanessa Ortiz
- Finance/Metric definition (Latency/$ computation): Confirms cost inputs and normalization rules
  - Primary: Nadia Rahman
- Security/Compliance (Artifact safety): Confirms redaction and no sensitive leakage
  - Primary: Naomi Feldman
- Legal (Claims/disclaimers): Approves comparative phrasing and required disclaimers
  - Primary: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes
- PMM (Launch asset consistency): Confirms messaging matches approved scope and caveats
  - Primary: Soojin Lee

payload.page_title: Prompt heuristics: templates and failure cases (2026)

sections.body:
h1. Overview
This page consolidates Redwood Inference prompt heuristics, copy/paste templates, and known failure cases for common short instruction tasks:
* binary/multiclass classification
* extractive structured output (JSON)
* rewrites with a constrained style

It is derived from applied experiments and is intended to be broadly reusable (not a personal scratchpad). The focus is pragmatic: maximize reliability under latency and parsing constraints, especially for streaming responses.

h2. Scope and non-goals
* In scope: prompt patterns for 0–3 shot tasks; output formatting constraints; example ordering; streaming-safe delimiters; canonicalization rules.
* Out of scope: full benchmark harness design, model-specific finetuning, or long-form agent prompting.

h2. Current recommendations (TL;DR)
1. Prefer short, explicit role + constraints over long rationale priming for latency-sensitive tasks.
2. For structured extraction, enforce a strict JSON-only contract and include canonicalization rules (e.g., strip currency symbols).
3. Use explicit block delimiters (XML-ish tags) to reduce boundary confusion in streaming.
4. Avoid chain-of-thought prompting. If you need justification, request a one-line "reason" field explicitly (and only when downstream accepts it).

h1. Tested heuristics (what worked, what didn’t)
h2. H1: Explicit role + short constraints beat long rationale priming
* Finding (2026-03): Consistently true for classification + extraction at low shot counts.
* Rationale: Long explanations increase variance and can bleed into the response format.

h2. H2: Example ordering effects (positive-first vs negative-first)
* Prior observation: negative-first examples caused borderline positives to flip negative in 3-shot classification.
* Updated finding (2026-03): ordering effects shrink substantially if:
  * labels are defined once and constrained to an explicit set
  * the final answer is requested under a fixed key (e.g., "Label:" on its own line)
  * examples are symmetric in length and style
* Practical recommendation: still default to positive-first for binary sentiment-like tasks, but treat ordering as a tunable parameter rather than a rule.

h2. H3: Delimiter tokens matter for streaming
* Finding: using explicit tags (e.g., <EXAMPLE>…</EXAMPLE>) reduced malformed structured outputs in streaming compared to freeform separators (e.g., "### EXAMPLE").
* Recommendation: standardize on tag-based delimiters for any prompt that must be parsed.

h2. H4: JSON constraints reduce verbosity and improve parse success
* Finding: "Return EXACT JSON" with an explicit schema reliably reduces paraphrasing.
* Caveat: Without canonicalization instructions, models will often preserve currency symbols or units.

h1. Standard templates (copy/paste)
All templates below are designed to be streaming-friendly and parser-friendly.

h2. Template A — extraction to strict JSON (1-shot)
Use for invoices, receipts, order summaries, and any simple entity/field extraction.

{code}
You are a concise extractor.
Return EXACTLY one JSON object and nothing else.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: {"product":"...","price":"...","quantity":"..."}
sections.heading: Schema (all values are strings)

sections.body:
- price: digits and decimal point only (e.g., "7.25"); strip currency symbols and commas
- quantity: digits only when present; otherwise "unknown"

<EXAMPLE>
Text: "Bought 3 packs of AA batteries (Model X) for $9.99 each"
Output: {"product":"AA batteries (Model X)","price":"9.99","quantity":"3"}
</EXAMPLE>

Now extract from the input below.
Text: "<INPUT_TEXT>"
sections.heading: Canonicalization rules

sections.body: {code}
sections.heading: Output

sections.body:
* The canonicalization block is required if downstream expects normalized numerics.
* If you need multiple items, define an array schema explicitly (and update parsers accordingly).

h2. Template B — classification with tag separators (up to 3-shot)
Use for sentiment/triage/moderation-style labeling.

{code}
You are a brief classifier.
Valid labels: POSITIVE, NEGATIVE.
Return the label only.

<EXAMPLE>
Input: "Loved the service, will come back!"
Label: POSITIVE
</EXAMPLE>
<EXAMPLE>
Input: "Item arrived broken and no reply from support."
Label: NEGATIVE
</EXAMPLE>
<EXAMPLE>
Input: "Average experience, shipping slow but product ok."
Label: NEGATIVE
</EXAMPLE>

Input: "<INPUT>"
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
{code}

Optional hardening line (use when the model keeps adding explanations):
* "Do not output any other words, punctuation, or JSON. Output only POSITIVE or NEGATIVE."

h2. Template C — rewrite to tone (zero-shot)
Use for customer comms rewrite, concise summaries, or tone adjustments.

{code}
You are a rewrite assistant.
Rewrite the following customer message to be formal and concise (one sentence).
Do not add new facts.

Message: "<MSG>"
sections.heading: Label

sections.body:
{code}

h1. Known failure cases and mitigations
h2. F1: Currency symbol leakage in extraction
* Symptom: price values include "$" (or other currency symbols), breaking numeric parsers.
* Example input: "Total: $12.00"
* Bad output: {"price":"$12.00"}
* Mitigation: include canonicalization rule "digits and decimal point only" and provide a 1-shot example that demonstrates stripping symbols.

h2. F2: Example-order bias in borderline classification
* Symptom: borderline positives label as NEGATIVE more often when first example is negative.
* Updated mitigation: enforce "Return the label only" plus symmetric examples; consider adding a neutral/borderline example if task allows (but beware label leakage if the dataset distribution is skewed).

h2. F3: Streaming truncation causing malformed JSON
* Symptom: missing closing brace or partial object when network interrupts or token boundaries cut awkwardly.
* Mitigations:
  1. Keep examples short (< 50 tokens per example for extraction).
  2. Put schema and constraints immediately before the answer.
  3. Prefer one JSON object (not pretty-printed) to reduce token count.
  4. If the client supports it, validate braces and retry once with a "repair" prompt.

h2. F4: Rationale/chain-of-thought contamination
* Symptom: model outputs reasoning text even when asked for JSON/labels.
* Mitigation: remove chain-of-thought priming; explicitly forbid additional text.
* Policy note: Do not request chain-of-thought in production prompts. If justification is needed for UX, request a separate field like "reason" and treat it as non-authoritative.

h2. F5: Extra keys added to JSON output
* Symptom: model adds fields like "currency":"USD" or "confidence":0.82.
* Mitigations:
  * "Return EXACTLY the keys in the schema; do not add any other keys."
  * Provide an example where an extra key would be tempting but is omitted.
  * In downstream parsing, reject unknown keys (preferred) or ignore them (only if product tolerates it).

h1. Mini-results summary (internal quick evals)
These are small-sample directional results intended to guide defaults; they are not full benchmarks.

h2. Setup
* Tasks: binary sentiment classification; receipt-like extraction
* Temperatures: 0.0, 0.2, 0.7
* Few-shot: 0, 1, 3
* Runs per cell: N=50 (updated from earlier N=20 scratch runs)

h2. Highlights
* Extraction:
  * Temp=0.0 + strict JSON + canonicalization rules: price normalization correctness ~96% (previously ~89% without canonicalization).
  * Temp=0.2 increases symbol leakage and key drift; only use if you accept retry/repair logic.
* Classification:
  * Role-only + "label only" constraint: stable across 0–3 shot.
  * Adding short explanations after examples increased variance and increased non-compliant outputs (extra text).

h1. Operational checklist (before shipping a prompt)
1. Define the output contract unambiguously (label-only or strict JSON schema).
2. Add canonicalization rules for any field with units/symbols (currency, dates, counts).
3. Keep examples short and stylistically symmetric.
4. Add hard-stop constraints: "Return only X" / "Return EXACT JSON".
5. Test with streaming on/off and validate parse success.
6. Log representative failures (input, prompt, raw output, model/version, temperature) to the evals tracker.

h1. Open questions / follow-ups
* How much do these behaviors shift across quantization variants (int8 vs int4) in hosted environments?
* For multi-label classification, what is the best delimiter strategy for preventing label drift (comma-separated vs one-per-line)?
* For extraction involving multiple currencies, what is the policy: preserve currency code as separate field vs normalize to a base currency?

h1. Change log
* 2026-03-12: Standardized on <EXAMPLE> tag delimiters; added canonicalization rules section; updated mini-results to N=50 per cell; clarified policy to avoid chain-of-thought prompting.
* 2026-02-25: Initial consolidation from applied-ml experiments and failure logs.

payload.page_title: Quantization Regression Thresholds (Quality Policy)

sections.body:
This page defines Redwood Inference’s quality policy for *quantization-related changes* (e.g., enabling a new Quantization Profile, updating profile artifacts, changing kernel selection for quantized paths). It specifies:
- Required evaluation suites and minimum coverage
- Acceptable regression thresholds (by task family)
- Statistical methods and pass/fail rules
- Automatic block criteria (pre-publish) and automatic rollback triggers (during canary/beta)

The intent is to reduce cost/token while keeping output quality within agreed bounds and ensuring regressions are detected quickly, are attributable, and are reversible.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
**In scope:**
- Any new or updated quantization profile intended for publication in the Quantization Profile Library
- Any runtime or kernel-path change that affects quantized execution correctness or output distribution
- Any control-plane/routing behavior that can silently change the applied precision path for a route

**Out of scope:**
- Non-quantization model changes (handled by Model Onboarding Quality Policy)
- Prompt changes unrelated to quantization (handled by Prompt Set Governance)
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- **Baseline:** The current default serving configuration for a model variant (typically FP16/BF16 or existing approved path) with quantization feature disabled.
- **Candidate (Quantized):** A specific quantization profile version applied to the same model variant.
- **Task family:** Group of eval tasks with similar sensitivity (e.g., Code, RAG QA, Safety).
- **Primary quality metric:** The metric used as the go/no-go gate for a given suite.
- **Non-inferiority margin (NIM):** Maximum allowed degradation versus baseline.
- **Canary:** Controlled rollout phase where a small fraction of traffic uses the profile under strict monitoring.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body: All quantization profile publications must run the following suites **per model variant** and **per supported context-length regime** (see “Context-length bins”).
sections.heading: Required evaluation suites (minimum)

sections.body:
**Goal:** Catch broad instruction-following degradation.
- Coverage: general assistant tasks (writing, extraction, reasoning-lite, formatting)
- Primary metric: pairwise win-rate vs baseline (LLM-judge) + tie-rate reporting
- Minimum samples: 400 prompts per context-length bin
sections.heading: A) Redwood Core Prompt Set (RCPS)

sections.body:
**Goal:** Detect retrieval-augmented QA / grounded answering issues.
- Coverage: short-context QA + long-context QA (with provided context)
- Primary metric: exact match / F1 where applicable; otherwise judge-based groundedness
- Minimum samples: 250 prompts per relevant bin
sections.heading: B) Redwood RAG/QA Set (RRQS)

sections.body:
**Goal:** Ensure function/tool calling and JSON validity aren’t impacted.
- Coverage: function call selection, argument formatting, schema compliance, constrained decoding
- Primary metric: schema-valid rate + exact-match on tool name/required args (where defined)
- Minimum samples: 200 prompts
sections.heading: C) Redwood Tool Use / Structured Output Set (RTUS)

sections.body:
**Goal:** Prevent regressions in refusals and safety policy adherence.
- Coverage: refusal correctness, policy-compliant redirection, harmlessness
- Primary metric: safety violation rate (SVR)
- Minimum samples: 300 prompts
sections.heading: D) Redwood Safety & Policy Set (RSPS)

sections.body:
**Goal:** Catch long-context and summarization drift.
- Coverage: summarization, multi-doc synthesis, long instruction retention
- Primary metric: judge-based quality + factuality spot-check (automated heuristics)
- Minimum samples: 150 prompts
sections.heading: E) Customer-like Long-Context Stress Set (LCS)

sections.body:
Run suites in bins that reflect serving constraints and known sensitivity:
- **Short:** 0–1k input tokens
- **Medium:** 1k–4k input tokens
- **Long:** 4k–max_supported_by_profile input tokens

If a profile is only approved up to a max context (per schema constraints), runs beyond that max are not required, but must be explicitly documented in the profile’s “known_caveats”.
sections.heading: Context-length bins

sections.body: All thresholds below apply to **Candidate vs Baseline** comparisons using the statistical procedure in “Statistical method & decision rule”.
sections.heading: Acceptance thresholds (by task family)

sections.body:
**Interpretation:** Candidate must not be worse than Baseline by more than the margin.

| Task family | Primary metric | Threshold (Candidate vs Baseline) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| General instruction (RCPS) | Win-rate (judge) | Δwin_rate >= -1.5 percentage points AND lower 95% CI bound >= -3.0 pp | Also track tie-rate; large tie shifts can indicate mode collapse |
| RAG/QA (RRQS) | EM/F1 (or groundedness judge) | EM/F1: Δ >= -1.0 pp; Groundedness: Δwin_rate >= -1.0 pp | If using judge, must include “hallucination flag rate” |
| Tool/Structured (RTUS) | Schema-valid rate | Δvalid_rate >= -0.3 pp AND valid_rate >= 99.0% absolute | Any increase in invalid JSON/tool args is high severity |
| Code (if model supports code) | pass@1 (unit tests) | Δpass@1 >= -1.0 pp | Use fixed deterministic harness where possible |
| Safety (RSPS) | Safety violation rate (SVR) | ΔSVR <= +0.0 pp (no increase tolerated) | Safety is hard-gated; any increase blocks |
| Long-context summarization (LCS) | Judge win-rate + factuality heuristics | Δwin_rate >= -2.0 pp AND no >+0.5 pp increase in factuality error heuristic rate | Long-context is more variable; require extra monitoring in canary |
sections.heading: Table: Non-inferiority margins (allowed degradation)

sections.body:
Regardless of task family, the following are *hard blocks*:
- **Refusal drift:** refusal_rate changes by more than **±3.0 pp** on RCPS unless explained by prompt-set composition
- **Toxicity / policy flags:** any increase in RSPS SVR (see table)
- **Format compliance:** RTUS schema-valid rate falls below **99.0%** absolute
- **Determinism / correctness:** any runtime correctness failures, NaNs, or output truncation attributable to quant path
sections.heading: Secondary “sanity” thresholds (hard blocks)

sections.body:
- Prefer **paired** comparisons: same prompts, same decoding params, Baseline vs Candidate.
- Default decoding for policy gates: temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_tokens per suite spec.
- For tool/structured tasks, use the same constrained decoding settings in both arms.
sections.heading: Evaluation design

sections.body:
- Use a **blinded pairwise** judge prompt (no mention of “quantized”).
- Compute **win-rate** as wins / (wins + losses), with ties reported separately.
- Estimate uncertainty via **paired bootstrap** over prompts (10,000 resamples).
- Decision rule:
  - Pass if Δwin_rate meets the threshold AND the lower bound of the 95% CI is above the CI condition in the table.
  - If CI crosses the margin but point estimate passes: mark as **Borderline** and require either (a) increased sample size, or (b) canary only with stricter rollback triggers.
sections.heading: Judge-based metrics (win-rate)

sections.body:
- Use **paired bootstrap** for EM/F1 differences and valid-rate differences.
- For pass@1 with deterministic tests, use a **paired sign test** when applicable; otherwise bootstrap.
- Decision rule:
  - Pass if Δmetric meets the margin and 95% CI supports non-inferiority.
sections.heading: Discrete metrics (EM/F1, valid rate, pass@1)

sections.body:
We gate at the **suite/task-family** level, not per individual prompt. To reduce false positives:
- Use suite-level aggregate metrics.
- If a suite fails narrowly, rerun with +50% samples once (single retry). No repeated retries beyond that.
sections.heading: Multiple comparisons handling

sections.body:
A profile cannot be published to the library unless the following artifacts are attached to the publish request (or linked in the registry entry):
- Eval run IDs for each required suite + context bin
- Summary table with Baseline vs Candidate metrics, deltas, and CIs
- Top 20 “largest delta” prompts (wins→losses) for RCPS and RSPS
- RTUS invalid-output examples (if any), including model outputs
- Perf summary (p50/p95 latency, throughput, VRAM) for supported GPU SKUs from perf suite
sections.heading: Required reporting artifacts (for publication)

sections.body:
Publication is automatically blocked if any of the following occur:
1) Any suite fails the thresholds in the “Acceptance thresholds” table.
2) RSPS SVR increases by any amount.
3) RTUS schema-valid rate < 99.0% absolute.
4) Any **correctness** errors in runtime integration tests (e.g., NaNs, invalid logits, crash, repeated fallback loop).
5) Candidate is marked compatible with a hardware class but fails perf suite smoke checks (e.g., OOM at stated max context).

**Owner:** Applied ML (quality) is responsible for enforcing blocks in the publish pipeline. Runtime and Platform own correctness and compatibility test enforcement.
sections.heading: Automatic block criteria (pre-publish)

sections.body: During canary (perf-canary or design partner beta), quantization enablement must be configured with *fast rollback* and monitored with automated triggers.
sections.heading: Canary/beta rollback triggers (automatic)

sections.body:
These are evaluated over rolling windows and compared to the route’s own baseline window (or a matched control route):
- **Quality guardrail alert:** any RSPS-derived safety signal increase above **0.0 pp** (block + immediate disable)
- **Judge win-rate drift (if online judge sampling enabled):** Δwin_rate < **-3.0 pp** over a 2-hour window with >=200 judged pairs
- **Customer reported regression:** P0/P1 support ticket attributed to quantization on the route (manual trigger to disable within SLA)
sections.heading: Online quality triggers

sections.body:
If any of the following are exceeded, **automatically disable the profile on the route** and page on-call (per severity):
- **p95 decode latency:** +8% relative increase sustained for 15 minutes (per route/model/region)
- **5xx rate:** +0.2 pp absolute increase sustained for 10 minutes
- **Fallback rate:** >1.0% of requests falling back due to incompatibility, load, or runtime rejection (indicates misconfig or profile issue)
- **OOM / runtime error rate:** any sustained non-zero OOM attributable to quant path (threshold: >0.05% for 5 minutes)
sections.heading: Reliability & performance triggers

sections.body:
- **SEV-1 (immediate disable + page):** Safety signal regression, elevated 5xx, crash/OOM spike
- **SEV-2 (auto disable + ticket):** p95 regression >8%, fallback_rate >1%
- **SEV-3 (investigate, may keep canary):** borderline win-rate drift without other issues
sections.heading: Severity mapping

sections.body:
A candidate is **Borderline** if it:
- Passes point estimates but fails CI conditions, or
- Has a small regression near the margin on a critical suite (RRQS/RTUS/RSPS/LCS)
sections.heading: “Borderline” handling policy

sections.body:
- They are labeled **experimental** in the library
- Enablement is restricted (allowlist + canary-only)
- Rollback triggers are configured at the stricter setting:
  - p95 decode latency trigger becomes **+5%**
  - win-rate drift trigger becomes **-2.0 pp**
  - fallback_rate trigger becomes **>0.5%**
sections.heading: Borderline candidates may proceed only if

sections.body:
- **Applied ML (Selene Huang / Arjun Desai):** owns thresholds, suite definitions, and final publish decision.
- **Eval Harness (Olivia Grant):** owns correctness of evaluation tooling and judge prompts.
- **Serving Runtime (Mateo Alvarez / Noah Patel / Hiro Tanaka):** owns runtime correctness, determinism guarantees, and kernel-path safety.
- **Platform Control Plane & Routing (Priya Natarajan / Ethan Park / Mina Haddad):** owns route-level enablement controls, compatibility enforcement, and kill-switch.
sections.heading: Change control & ownership

sections.body:
1) Be proposed via PR to this policy page
2) Include rationale and impact assessment
3) Be reviewed by Applied ML sponsor + Runtime sponsor + Platform sponsor
sections.heading: Any change to thresholds must

sections.body:
- RCPS: 400 per context bin
- RRQS: 250 per relevant bin
- RTUS: 200 total (not bin-split unless tool usage is long-context)
- RSPS: 300 total
- LCS: 150 total

If compute is constrained, prioritize: RSPS, RTUS, RCPS (Short/Medium), RRQS (Short/Medium), then LCS.
sections.heading: Appendix A: Recommended minimum sample sizes (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Increased formatting errors (missing braces/quotes, invalid tool args)
- Hallucinated citations or groundedness drift in RAG prompts
- Subtle refusal boundary changes (over-refusal or under-refusal)
- Long-context degradation (lost constraints, repetition, early truncation)
- Distribution shifts that show up as higher tie-rate but lower win-rate on edge prompts
sections.heading: Appendix B: Known failure modes to watch for in quantized runs

sections.body:
1) Disable profile at the route level (preferred)
2) If widespread or unclear blast radius, activate the global kill-switch
3) File incident or incident-adjacent ticket with:
   - quant_profile_id
   - model_id + variant
   - route_id(s), region(s), deployment tier
   - start time, trigger metrics, and example request IDs

Reference: Rollback Procedure for Quantization Profiles (see related pages).

payload.page_title: Priming Entropy Consumption and Slice Resilience Manifest

sections.body:
Overview
This document defines the Priming Entropy Consumption (PEC) methodology and the Slice Resilience Manifest — a compact set of measurement standards, probe construction rules, and rollout controls used across Redwood's eval harness, prompt sets, and quantization onboarding workflows. The goal is to quantify how much "priming entropy" a prompt family consumes, audit its impact on generation coherence under quantization, and provide actionable remediation and rollback guidance for model promotion.

Why this matters
- Priming (few-shot examples, system content, or long context) consumes model entropy and can amplify quantization-induced degradation or KV-cache fragmentation.
- Teams need a shared signal to: prioritize probe creation, set canary pass/fail rules, and choose quant-fallback thresholds.

Key terms
- Priming Entropy (PE): estimated bits-of-uncertainty consumed by the priming text measured by cross-entropy delta vs. a neutral baseline.
- PEC score: a normalized 0–1 metric representing priming entropy per 1k tokens (higher = more priming cost).
- Slice Resilience: probability that a workload slice preserves fidelity (coherence and factuality) after quantization or caching changes.

High-level requirements (manifest)
1) Every prompt family must publish a PEC score and a Slice Resilience band before promotion to staging/dedicated.
2) Eval harness integrations must run PEC-measured probes during shadow and canary phases.
3) Quantization gates: if mean Slice Resilience drops below 0.92 for an anchored slice, the quantized artifact fails fast and triggers a rollback.
4) Cache-sensitivity contract: if KV-cache hit-rate delta > 6% and resulting fidelity drop > 2.5% absolute, the change must be gated behind an A/B with explicit fallback.

Metrics and thresholds (recommended defaults)
- PEC score thresholds: low (<0.12), medium (0.12–0.35), high (>0.35). Use these bands to determine probe prioritization.
- Fidelity (coherence) delta: tracked as mean pairwise semantic similarity and human anchor score. Guardrail: absolute delta <= 0.03 for low PEC, <=0.05 for medium PEC, <=0.08 for high PEC.
- Quant-fallback threshold: when fidelity delta > 0.06 OR Slice Resilience < 0.92 for priority slices.
- Latency budget impact: if priming increases per-request tokenization time by >15ms median or tail by >40ms P95, flag as performance risk.

Probe construction rules (how to build PEC probes)
- Minimum probe set: 200 seed prompts per slice (stratified by language, intent, and long-context presence).
- For each seed, create 5 perturbations: token masking, paraphrase, adversarial noise, shortened-context, and extended-context.
- Annotate probes with: expected anchor output (gold or exemplar), PEC category, and cache-sensitivity tag (hot/cold).
- Each probe must include an evaluation script that calculates: cross-entropy vs baseline, semantic similarity (embedding cosine), hallucination flags, and token-count sensitivity.

Integration with the eval harness
1) Runner configuration example (text):
   - service: eval-mesh
   - slot: mixed-fidelity
   - priority: PEC-high > functional > perf
   - replay-mode: stochastic-seed=42
2) Scheduling guidance:
   - PEC-high families run on every quant-shadow build and on canary 0.5% traffic slices.
   - PEC-medium families run nightly in shadow; promote to canary if stable for 3 consecutive runs.

Canary matrix and rollout controls
- Canary cells (example):
  | Cell | Traffic | Quant-profile | PEC focus | Pass criteria |
  |------|---------|---------------|-----------|---------------|
  | A1   | 0.1%    | int8-pt       | high PEC  | SliceRes >=0.94 AND fidelity delta <=0.05 |
  | B1   | 1%      | int8-pt + cache| medium PEC| SliceRes >=0.96 AND latency delta <10ms |
  | C1   | 5%      | bf16 fallback | low PEC   | No critical regressions; automated monitoring OK |
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - Any cell where priority slices see Slice Resilience degrade >0.04 within first 24 hours -> immediate rollback.
  - If human annotator disagreements cross 12% for safety-labeled probes, pause rollout and escalate to Applied ML oncall.

Quantization and KV-cache interactions
- Measurement protocol:
  1) Run unquantized baseline on representative workload (1K warmup requests + 10K sample window).
  2) Run quantized artifact with identical replay seeds.
  3) Compare PEC-normalized fidelity and token-efficiency (tokens/response).
- Known behaviors to watch for:
  - High-PEC prompts often expose per-head rounding sensitivity (manifest as terse hallucination regressions).
  - KV-cache fragmentation may amplify effective PEC (more cache misses = less context reuse).
- Mitigations:
  - Quantization-aware prompt rewrites: compress examples, canonicalize tokens that increase entropy (dates, random IDs).
  - Automatic fallback: route PEC-high requests to bf16 profile when latency budget permits.

Runbook: regression triage for PEC-related failures
1) Detection:
   - Alert tags: pec-fidelity-drop, pec-cache-regen, pec-latency-spike.
   - Run automated diff between baseline and candidate for top 20 failing probes.
2) Triage steps (ordered):
   a) Confirm repro with deterministic seed in the eval harness.
   b) Inspect PEC score delta per probe and cache hit-rate changes.
   c) If quantization-induced: rerun with per-layer mixed-precision to isolate layer(s).
   d) If prompt-induced: attempt prompt contraction (strip non-essential priming) and re-eval.
   e) Record root cause in the Regression Huntbook entry and attach annotated probe set.
3) Escalation matrix:
   - If Slice Resilience < 0.88 for priority slices -> escalate to Applied ML (pager) and block promotion.
   - If degradation is confined to non-critical language slices -> product owner decides risk acceptance (documented).

Operational ownership and SLAs
- Owners:
  - Probe stewardship and PEC computation: Applied ML (Elena Chen).
  - Eval harness integration: Eval Platform (Marco Ruiz).
  - Quantization gating and artifact ops: Runtime QE (Aisha Patel).
- SLA targets:
  - PEC score computation latency <= 6 hours for new probe families in nightly pipeline.
  - Canary alerting latency <= 5 minutes for Slice Resilience breaches in production canaries.

Appendix: examples and CLI snippets
- PEC computation (pseudo-CLI):

payload.page_title: Priming Context Probes and Quant-Failure Scan Protocol

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the Priming Context Probe Suite (PCPS) and an automated Quant-Failure Scan Protocol (QFSP) used during model onboarding and periodic stability checks. PCPS is a compact, prioritized catalog of prompt probes designed to exercise contextual priming behaviors (temperature sensitivity, prompt-order invariance, prefix caching interactions, instruction anchoring) across production traffic slices. QFSP is the associated runnable workflow that runs PCPS across quantized artifacts to detect failure modes introduced by precision reduction, KV-cache truncation, and kernel-selection fallbacks.

Scope

- Applies to any model artifact considered for promotion to hosted/dedicated/private serving.
- Intended for both pre-promotion (onboarding) and continuous monitoring (nightly or on-change).
- Focus areas: contextual priming behaviors, instruction-following durability, multi-shot coherence, and quant-specific degradation.

Goals

1. Provide a deterministic, small-footprint probe suite that captures early-warning signals for priming regressions.
2. Automate cross-artifact comparisons (fp16 -> int8/4-bit) with clear pass/fail thresholds and triage steps.
3. Minimize compute cost while maintaining high signal-to-noise for production-relevant failure modes.

Priming Context Probe Catalog (PCPS)

Each probe below is labeled with: probe_id, intent, probe_description, expected_behavior, and measurement. The canonical catalog lives in the eval repository under evals/pcps_catalog/ and is synced to the onboarder. Examples:

- probe_id: PCPS-001
  intent: instruction-anchoring
  description: "Anchor instruction after long irrelevant preamble, measure instruction recall and obedience."
  expected_behavior: "Last-instruction takes precedence; core instruction executed within first 3 lines of response."
  measurement: "InstrRecall@3: binary (1/0) if instruction executed in top-3 lines; Score: BLEU-like against oracle."

- probe_id: PCPS-007
  intent: prefix-cache-sensitivity
  description: "Send two equivalent prompts A and A+prefix (prefix cached). Compare tokens-per-second and output divergence."
  expected_behavior: "Semantically equivalent; small token-level divergence (<4%) and latency delta within batching SLO."
  measurement: "DKL(output_dist(A) || output_dist(A+prefix)), latency_delta_ms"

- probe_id: PCPS-014
  intent: multi-shot-context-coherence
  description: "3-shot with varied ordering; require answer stability across permutations."
  expected_behavior: "Top-1 intent preserved across shots; instability budget <= 12% across permutations."
  measurement: "AgreementRate across 6 permutations"

Runner & Orchestration

- Implementation: evaluator-runner service (eval-runner) with adapters for private/dedicated artifacts. The runner accepts a probe batch JSON and returns per-probe metrics and raw outputs.
- Invocation (example):

  curl -X POST https://eval-runner.internal/api/v1/run
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${EVAL_TOKEN}'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"artifact_uri":"s3://models/redwood/llama-3-8b-int8-v2","probe_set":"pcps_v1","seeds":[42,314],"sampling":{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95}}'

Evaluation Outputs (JSON snippet)

  {
    "artifact_uri": "s3://models/redwood/llama-3-8b-int8-v2",
    "run_id": "pcps-2026-05-03-01",
    "results": [
      {"probe_id":"PCPS-001","instrRecall@3":"0","bleu":0.12,"notes":"instruction truncated by tokenizer"},
      {"probe_id":"PCPS-007","dk_llr":0.06,"latency_delta_ms":14}
    ]
  }

Metrics and Pass/Fail Thresholds

We use three tiers of signal: green, amber, red. Each probe maps to a metric and thresholds defined below.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Metric                      | Green (pass)            | Amber (investigate)        | Red (block/promote fail)
  --------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------
  InstrRecall@3               | >= 0.95                 | 0.85 - 0.95                | < 0.85
  AgreementRate (multi-shot)  | >= 0.90                 | 0.75 - 0.90                | < 0.75
  DKL (A vs A+prefix)         | <= 0.03 nats            | 0.03 - 0.08               | > 0.08
  Latency delta (ms)          | <= 25ms                 | 25 - 75ms                 | > 75ms
  Quant-induced BLEU drop     | <= 0.04                 | 0.04 - 0.12               | > 0.12

Quant-Failure Scan Protocol (QFSP)

QFSP runs PCPS across a matrix of artifacts (float -> fp16 -> int8 / 4-bit / hybrid quant) and quant kernels. It is implemented as a CI job (eval-quant-scan) and a nightly orchestrator (scan-orch). The protocol:

1) Prepare matrix:
   - Artifacts: {fp32, fp16, int8, int4-hybrid}
   - Kernels: {fast-kernel, safe-kernel, fallback-cuda}
   - Cache configurations: {kv_cache_full, kv_cache_trimmed}
2) Run PCPS with deterministic seeds (seed list is defined per artifact in evals/pcps_catalog/config.toml).
3) Collect metrics and produce a delta matrix against golden_reference (last promoted fp16 artifact).
4) Apply scoring rules: any red in per-probe threshold blocks promotion; >=2 amber probes escalate to quant-triage.
5) If blocked, open triage ticket with artifacts, raw outputs, and prioritized probes.

Automated Triage Heuristics

- If InstrRecall failures correlate with tokenization mismatch (token length delta > 8%), tag with reason: tokenization.
- If DKL spikes only under trimmed KV cache, mark as kv-cache-sensitive; schedule a shadow run with larger cache window.
- If quant-induced BLEU drop concentrated on numerical/temporal probes, mark as numeric-precision-degradation and recommend mixed-precision fallback.

Onboarding Checklist (model promotion pipeline)

Use this checklist as part of the onboarding PR for model promotion to staging/production. Responsible: model-onboarding owner (eng applied-ml).

- [ ] PCPS run (all probes) completed and results attached to PR.
- [ ] QFSP run across supported quantization targets completed.
- [ ] No red probes. Any amber probes must have a proposed mitigation plan.
- [ ] Performance regression check: latency at target QPS within 10% of baseline.
- [ ] Resource footprint verified (Vram and CPU) and cost estimate updated.
- [ ] Security review: no sensitive training artifacts in outputs (sanity check via content-sanitizer).
- [ ] Evals artifacts (raw outputs) uploaded to eval-store with retention tag onboarding-30d.

Runbook: When a Quant Block Occurs

1) Pager (oncall-evals) receives automatic card via triage bot when QFSP finds a red probe.
2) Oncall steps:
   a) Validate artifact URIs and seeds by re-running the failing probes locally:

      evalctl run --artifact s3://models/redwood/<artifact> --probes pcps_v1 --seeds 42,314 --out /tmp/pcps-debug.json

   b) Inspect raw outputs and tokenize both golden and candidate outputs:

      python -m evals.tools.token_compare /tmp/golden.json /tmp/pcps-debug.json --show-diff

   c) If tokenization mismatch: escalate to tokenizer-team and attach token diffs. If matched, continue triage.

3) If kv-cache sensitivity suspected, run shadow with KV window increased to +25% and compare.
4) If quant fallback required, revert to mixed-precision profile and run PCPS to confirm signal removal.
5) Document resolution in the triage ticket and change ticket status to resolved only when no red probes remain or a rollback path exists.

Integration with Evals and Monitoring

- PCPS outputs are ingested into the eval-metrics datastore (timeseries) with tags: artifact_uri, quant_level, kernel, kv_config, probe_id.
- Dashboards: pcps-health (SLO view), quant-scan-deltas (matrix heatmap), and probe-explorer (search by probe_id).
- Alerts: alert when any probe enters red for >= 2 runs within 24h or when aggregated Quant BLEU drop exceeds 0.08.

Configuration snippets

- probes config (evals/pcps_catalog/config.toml):

  [[probe_sets]]
  name = "pcps_v1"
  probes = ["PCPS-001","PCPS-007","PCPS-014","PCPS-021"]
  seeds = [42,314]

- promotion job (example YAML):

  jobs:
    - name: eval-quant-scan
      runs-on: runner-highmem
      steps:
        - run: evalctl run --artifact ${{ env.ARTIFACT }} --probes pcps_v1 --seeds 42,314 --out results.json
        - run: evalctl analyze --input results.json --baseline s3://evals/golden/fp16-latest

Ownership and SLA

- Owner: Applied ML / Evals team (eng-applied-ml). Primary contacts: Lina Zhou (author), Marco Hernandez (senior reviewer).
- Expected cadence: Onboarding run per promotion; nightly QFSP across high-risk artifacts (defined in evals/high_risk_list.tsv).
- SLA for triage: initial ack within 4 hours for red-blocking regressions; full investigation within 72 hours.

Appendix: Example probes (full text)

- PCPS-021: numeric-stability-probe
  Prompt: "You are a calculator. Compute 17 * 23 and explain if rounding matters."
  Oracle: "391"
  Failure modes: off-by-one, floating-point notation (3.91e2) that downstream parsers cannot parse.

- PCPS-033: temporal-normalization
  Prompt: "If today is 2026-05-03, what is the date 90 days from now?"
  Oracle: 2026-08-01
  Notes: quantized artifacts sometimes prefer relative-date heuristics and can drift when tokenization splits date components.

Contact and references

- Author: Lina Zhou (lina.zhou@redwood.ai)
- Eval runner repo: git+ssh://git.redwood.internal/evals-runner.git
- Catalog: evals/pcps_catalog/README.md

Revision history

- 2026-02-15: Draft created (L. Zhou)
- 2026-03-22: Added automated triage heuristics and thresholds (M. Hernandez)
- 2026-05-03: Finalized runbook and SLA language; published (L. Zhou)

payload.page_title: Stratified Weighted Sampling Protocol and Annotation Guidelines

sections.body: This document defines a repeatable, auditable protocol for constructing stratified and weighted evaluation samples from production traffic, synthetic generators, and offline data stores. The protocol is intended for benchmark teams, annotation leads, and the eval-harness integration owners. It standardizes stratification keys, weight computation, sampling cadence, and annotation instructions to reduce sampling bias, ensure stable metric estimates, and enable quicker regression root-cause analysis.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to prompt set generation and benchmark creation for: quality regressions, latency-aware stress tests, and privacy-preserving shadow evaluations.
- Covers both production-derived sampling and synthetic augmentation pipelines.
- Does not replace model-specific acceptance criteria; it produces statistically-grounded test corpora to feed the eval harness.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1. Produce evaluation samples with a known sampling distribution and explicit weights so downstream metrics can be unbiasedly estimated.
2. Ensure representation of rare but critical slices (e.g., long-context, non-English, domain-specific tokens) with minimum sample counts.
3. Support automated re-sampling for continuous evaluation while preserving longitudinal comparability.
sections.heading: Goals and success criteria

sections.body:
- Primary stratification keys (in order): workload_type, token_length_bucket, user_tier, locale, prompt_template_id.
- Secondary keys (used for targeted oversampling): failure_history_flag, privacy_sensitive_flag, embedding_similarity_cluster.
sections.heading: Stratification design (high level)

sections.body:
- token_length_bucket: short(0-64), medium(65-512), long(513-2048), xlong(2049+).
- minimum_per_stratum: default 100; for high-risk domains (privacy_sensitive_flag=true) minimum 500.
sections.heading: Practical defaults

sections.body:
- Base weight w_i = 1 / P(sample_i) where P(sample_i) is the probability assigned by the sampler.
- When combining production and synthetic examples, normalize weights by source fraction f_source so that aggregated estimates are unbiased: w_i' = w_i * (1 / f_source).
- Truncation: cap weights at 20x the median weight in the sample to limit variance; record a weight_truncation_applied flag.
sections.heading: Weighting logic (summary)

sections.body:
1. Define target population and the time window (owner: benchmark lead). Example: production traffic between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28.
2. Extract candidate universe with required metadata columns: event_id, timestamp, workload_type, token_count, user_tier, locale, prompt_template_id, failure_history_flag, privacy_sensitive_flag, embedding_cluster_id.
3. Compute stratification keys and assign each candidate to a stratum.
4. For each stratum: determine sample quota q_s = max(minimum_per_stratum, proportional_allocation * global_budget).
5. Within stratum, draw a simple random sample without replacement. If stratum population < q_s, mark as underpopulated and fill remaining quota using nearest-neighbor strata (document fallback list).
6. Compute raw weights and apply truncation/shrinkage.
7. Output sample manifest (CSV/Parquet) and sampler metadata JSON (see example below).
sections.heading: Sampling procedure (operational steps)

sections.body:
- sample_id
- event_id
- stratum_id
- raw_weight
- adjusted_weight
- source (production|synthetic|archival)
- sample_reason (e.g., stratified, oversample, fallback)
sections.heading: Sampler manifest fields (required)

sections.body:
sampler_policy:
  name: stratified_weighted_v1
  time_window: "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z/2026-02-28T23:59:59Z"
  global_budget: 25000
  stratify_by:
    - workload_type
    - token_length_bucket
    - user_tier
    - locale
  minimum_per_stratum: 100
  special_oversamples:
    privacy_sensitive_flag: 500
    failure_history_flag: 300
  weight_truncation_factor: 20
  source_fractions:
    production: 0.7
    synthetic: 0.2
    archival: 0.1
sections.heading: Example sampler YAML (canonical)

sections.body:
-- Candidate extraction for the sampler
SELECT
  event_id,
  occurred_at as timestamp,
  workload_type,
  CASE WHEN token_count <= 64 THEN 'short' WHEN token_count <= 512 THEN 'medium' WHEN token_count <= 2048 THEN 'long' ELSE 'xlong' END as token_length_bucket,
  user_tier,
  locale,
  prompt_template_id,
  failure_history_flag,
  privacy_sensitive_flag,
  embedding_cluster_id
FROM production_events
WHERE occurred_at >= '2026-02-01' AND occurred_at < '2026-03-01'
  AND workload_type in ('chat', 'completion', 'rerank');
sections.heading: SQL extraction example (Postgres-compatible)

sections.body:
- Provide annotators with the full conversation context where available. If context is truncated, mark context_truncated=true.
- Use a 5-point quality scale for open-ended generation: 1 (nonsensical), 2 (incorrect), 3 (adequate), 4 (good), 5 (expert-level).
- For safety-related annotations use binary flags (unsafe_content=true/false) with a short rationale field.
- Required annotator metadata: annotator_id, experience_level, language_proficiency, annotation_timestamp.
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) target: Cohen's Kappa >= 0.6 per major slice; if below, increase adjudication rate.

Table: sample QC thresholds

| Metric | Acceptable | Concern threshold | Action on breach |
|--------|------------|-------------------|------------------|
| IAA (major slices) | >= 0.6 | 0.45 - 0.6 | Increase adjudication to 20% |
| Missing context flag rate | <= 5% | 5% - 15% | Re-run extraction; investigate truncation rules |
| Weight truncation fraction | <= 5% | 5% - 20% | Adjust stratification or increase global budget |
| Percentage synthetic | <= 40% | > 40% | Re-evaluate source fractions; label metrics accordingly |
sections.heading: Annotation guidelines (short)

sections.body:
- The eval harness expects input manifests with adjusted_weight and will compute weighted averages for scalar metrics: metric_hat = (sum_i adjusted_weight_i * y_i) / (sum_i adjusted_weight_i).
- For slice-level estimates, use Horvitz-Thompson estimator with provided inclusion probabilities. Provide a wrapper function in the eval-harness repo: compute_weighted_slice_metrics(manifest_path).
sections.heading: Integration with eval-harness and metrics math

sections.body:
- Sampling dashboard: strata fill rates, underpopulated strata, weight distribution histogram, fraction of truncated weights. Alert if >10% of strata are underpopulated for two consecutive runs.
- Annotation dashboard: IAA per slice, annotation velocity, backlog. Alert when average annotation latency > 72 hours.
sections.heading: Monitoring and dashboards (required)

sections.body:
1. If a regression is detected with high weight concentration (top 5% weights contribute > 50% of variance): flag weight_quality_issue and kick off data review.
2. Recompute metrics excluding top-0.5% weights to test sensitivity. Document results in the regression ticket.
3. If underpopulated slices correlate with regression, schedule an urgent re-sample with expanded quota for affected slices.
sections.heading: Triage and regression playbook (short runbook)

sections.body:
- Benchmark lead: owns sample definition and target population (role: applied-ml lead).
- Sampler owner (platform team): owns sampler tooling, manifests, and automation.
- Annotation lead (data ops): owns annotation schema, IAA monitoring, and adjudication rules.
- Review cadence: quarterly review of stratification keys and once-per-major-release sanity check.

Appendix: example manifest header (CSV)

sample_id,event_id,stratum_id,raw_weight,adjusted_weight,source,sample_reason,prompt_text,locale,token_count
sections.heading: Ownership and cadence

sections.body:
- Why weights instead of pure stratified quotas? Using explicit inclusion probabilities preserves unbiasedness for aggregated metrics and allows flexible post-hoc reweighting when combining heterogeneous sources.
- Why cap weights? Extremely large weights inflate variance and make point estimates unstable; capping preserves signal while limiting estimator variance.
sections.heading: Notes and rationale

sections.body:
- Use the eval harness wrapper compute_weighted_slice_metrics for metric calculations.
- For privacy-preserving sampling variants (DP-aware), see the private sampling appendix in the model-onboarding space (linked in related_pages).
sections.heading: Related artifacts and pointers

sections.body:
- Primary author: Elena Kim (elena.kim@redwood.ai)
- Sampler owner: Jonah Park (jonah.park@redwood.ai)
- Annotation ops: Maya Singh (maya.singh@redwood.ai)
sections.heading: Contact and escalation

sections.body:
- 2026-02-10: Initial publication.
- 2026-03-01: Added weight truncation guidance and integration notes for eval-harness.

payload.page_title: Multimodal Weak-Supervision Evaluation & Augmentation Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a repeatable process for constructing, augmenting, and evaluating multimodal (text + image / layout / audio) workloads using weak supervision signals. It is intended for ML engineers and evaluation owners who are onboarding models that accept or produce multimodal outputs, and for teams responsible for regression triage and embedding/quantization stability tests.

Goals:
- Define a defensible, low-cost pipeline for generating labeled multimodal test sets using weak supervision sources (heuristics, retrieval, synthetic generators).
- Provide annotation and adjudication guidance to ensure high signal-to-noise in critical slices.
- Integrate multimodal tests into the eval harness with clear pass/fail criteria and quantization sensitivity checks.
- Provide a rapid triage path for regressions that surface on augmented slices.

Scope and constraints:
- Works for: image+caption, document PDF layout+text, video-keyframe+transcript, and audio+transcript evaluation flows.
- Not intended for: full end-to-end multimodal dataset labeling at scale (use an MDS program for that). This playbook prioritizes targeted slices where weak supervision buys >10x labeling efficiency.

Definitions:
- Weak supervision sources: heuristics, programmatic labeling functions, model-derived pseudo-labels, retrieval heuristics from existing corpora.
- Slice: a semantically coherent subset of traffic (e.g., receipts with small fonts, hand-written forms, low-light images).
- Anchor examples: high-confidence human-labeled examples used to calibrate weak labels.

High-level process (summary):
1. Define target slices and acceptance metrics.
2. Assemble seed corpus and weak supervision functions.
3. Generate pseudo-labeled candidates and score label confidence.
4. Select stratified samples for human annotation and anchoring.
5. Calibrate and synthesize augmented prompt/perturbation variants.
6. Integrate into eval harness, run baseline and quantized variants.
7. Monitor slice-level metrics; trigger regression triage when thresholds are crossed.

1) Slice definition and acceptance metrics
- Owner: evaluation lead (example: @eval-lead).
- For each slice, record: name, description, cardinality estimate, priority (P0–P3), success metrics.
- Example slice table (markdown):
| slice | description | estimate | priority | primary metric | threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| low-light-images | photos with avg luminance < 0.15 | ~12k | P0 | grounding_precision@0.9 | >0.88 |
| tiny-font-receipts | receipts with font-size < 8pt | ~3k | P1 | ocr_character_f1 | >0.92 |

Primary metrics (examples):
- grounding_precision: fraction of generated references that correctly localize image regions / assets.
- alignment_f1: for structured outputs (tables, forms) compare predicted spans to reference spans via F1.
- hallucination_rate: percent of responses containing non-supported facts (determined by anchor verification).
- retrieval_ndcg@k: relevance for retrieval-backed captioning or context insertion.
- tokenized_error_rate: for transcriptions and OCR.

2) Weak supervision sources and scoring
- Types: heuristic (regex/OCR heuristics), retrieval (nearest-neighbor from labeled seed), model pseudo-labels (teacher models), synthetic (rendered templates / TTS / image perturbations).
- Each source must emit: label, confidence_score (0–1), provenance tag.
- Combine using a simple calibrated aggregator (logistic stacking or majority voting with source weights).
- Minimal metadata for a weak label must include: source_name, label_schema_version, confidence, seed_anchor_id (if derived).

3) Candidate generation and confidence calibration
- Use the following pipeline:
  a. Pull seed corpus (specify query or dataset id).
  b. Apply labeling functions in parallel, collect outputs.
  c. Compute source-level reliability using anchor examples; derive calibrated confidence (Platt scaling or isotonic regression recommended).
  d. Assign final pseudo-labels and stratify by confidence bucket: high (>0.85), medium (0.6–0.85), low (<0.6).

YAML example for labeling function registration (include in eval-harness config):
```yaml
labeling_functions:
  - id: regex-amount-usd
    type: heuristic
    description: "extract monetary amounts preceded by $ or USD"
    params: {pattern: "(?<=\$)\\d+(?:\\.\\d{2})?"}
    weight: 0.6
  - id: teacher-captioner-v2
    type: model
    model_ref: "models/vision-caption/teacher-v2@2025-10-01"
    weight: 0.9
```

4) Annotation and adjudication protocol
- Target throughput: annotate 200-500 anchors per slice initially.
- Annotation roles:
  - Annotator: apply label schema to sample items; mark uncertainties.
  - Adjudicator: resolves disagreements for anchor set; documents decision rationale.
  - Reviewer: periodic quality audit (10% random sample).
- Annotation guidelines must include: clear pass/fail criteria, examples of borderline cases, and a short checklist for each item.
- Dispute resolution: when annotator/adjudicator disagree > 8% across a batch, pause and update labeling functions.

Label schema example (flat list encoded as JSON lines in the annotation tool):
- label_id: grounding_ok
  description: "Model correctly identifies image region(s) referenced in text."
- label_id: partial_grounding
  description: "Some referenced regions correct, but missing others."
- label_id: hallucination
  description: "Output asserts content not present in the image or document."

5) Augmentation and perturbation generation
- Augmentations: scale/rotate_crop, synthetic_noise (jpeg/artifacts), contrast_low, OCR_blur, paraphrase_text, context_dropout (remove retrieved context to test hallucination).
- For each augmentation, define an expected metric delta tolerance (e.g., grounding_precision drop < 0.06 for P0 slices).
- When applying augmentations, preserve anchor IDs and provenance so regressions can be traced.

6) Integration with the eval harness
- Create a harness job per slice with the following knobs: model_variant, quant_setting, batch_profile, inference_timeout_ms.
- Example CLI run (eval harness):
  ./eval-harness run --suite multimodal/low-light-images.yaml --model-ref models/multi/serving-v3 --quant=8bitq

- Required outputs from harness: per-example predictions, per-example confidence, slice-level aggregated metrics, per-perturbation breakdown, and a compact diagnostics bundle (top-20 failure examples with metadata).

7) Quantization and runtime sensitivity checks
- For each slice run: fp16 (baseline), int8-quant (profiled), q4_0 (if supported). Compare primary metrics and compute sensitivity score:
  sensitivity = max(0, baseline_metric - quant_metric) / baseline_metric.
- Thresholds: sensitivity >= 0.10 for P0 slices triggers an investigation.
- If quantization increases hallucination_rate by > 5 percentage points, mark as high risk and block auto-promotion.

8) Regression detection and triage flow
- Alerting: slice-level metrics are pushed to RedMetrics. Create alerts when:
  - metric delta > threshold for consecutive 3 runs, or
  - a single run contains >0.5% of traffic with confidence < 0.2 and a matching failure signature.
- Triage quick-path (15–30 minute):
  1. Confirm failure in eval harness using the model commit hash.
 2. Compare anchor examples: did anchors flip labels? If yes, rollback candidate change.
  3. Run quantization-free baseline to check if error is quant-induced.
  4. Check weak supervision provenance: did a labeling function drift?
  5. If not resolved, escalate to regression team with diagnostics bundle.

9) Promotion and canary rules
- Promotion gating: a slice fails promotion if any P0 slice metric is below threshold OR quantization sensitivity > limits.
- Canary rollout plan: 20% traffic for 24h -> 50% for 24h -> full rollout, with slice-level monitoring at each step. Auto-fallback policy: revert to previous model if any P0 slice metric regresses > 0.05 absolute.

10) Ownership, roles and SLAs
- Evaluation lead: owns slice definitions, acceptance thresholds (SLA: respond to triage within 24h).
- Regression on-call: 4-person rotation in eng-platform; SLA: initial investigation within 2h for P0 alerts.
- Annotation ops: manage annotation throughput and anchor quality; SLA: replenish anchors weekly for high-traffic slices.

Appendix A — Example failure diagnostics bundle fields (CSV friendly):
- example_id, slice, augmentation_tag, model_ref, quant_setting, baseline_metric, current_metric, confidence, labeling_provenance, anchor_label, annotator_notes

Appendix B — Quick checklist before trusting weak labels for promotion:
- Anchor coverage >= 200 examples per P0 slice.
- Weighted aggregator AUC >= 0.92 on anchor holdout.
- No single source >80% of labels unless source is verified teacher model.
- Documentation for each labeling function present in the eval-harness config.

Appendix C — Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Mode: heuristic overfitting (heuristic matches artifacts of training data). Mitigation: randomize and add negative examples to seed.
- Mode: retrieval mismatch (retrieved context from wrong domain). Mitigation: domain-aware retrieval filters and reranking.
- Mode: quantization-induced hallucination. Mitigation: force higher-precision for decoding layer or apply targeted calibration.

References and related pages:
- See also: eval-harness synthetic-workload-profiles, model promotion matrix, and regression-triage playbooks (linked above).

Contact and incremental updates:
- Maintainer: Priya Nair (pri@redwood.ai).
- Suggested cadence: monthly review of high-priority slices and after every major model promotion.
- Change log: 2026-01-12 initial published; 2026-02-18 updated quant sensitivity thresholds and added adjudication throughput targets.

payload.page_title: Annotator Economics and Probe Retention Policy

sections.body: This document defines Redwood Inference's policy for annotation economics (how we compensate human annotators and run quality control) and the lifecycle and retention policy for probe artifacts used across evals, model onboarding, and regression triage. The goal is to make probe stewardship predictable, cost-aware, privacy-compliant, and operationally auditable.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all probe artifacts generated or ingested by Applied ML and Evals teams, including synthetic probes, user-derived probes (anonymized), adversarial test cases, and annotator labels stored in central probe repositories.
- Includes guidance for annotator pay bands, QA pass thresholds, annotation latency targets, storage tiers, deletion/archival procedures, and exception handling.
- Excludes ephemeral debug probes created only in local development that are not pushed to shared repositories.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Probe: an input (prompt, conversation, multimodal input) together with metadata and (optionally) reference labels used for evaluation.
- Annotator: a human contributor who provides labels, ratings, or quality judgments for probes. Includes internal annotators and vetted external vendors.
- Probe Artifact: files and records (JSON/YAML/CSV and attachments) stored in the probe catalog.
- Hot Storage: fast-access storage used by eval harnesses and live shadowing.
- Cold Storage: lower-cost blob storage (S3 Glacier/nearline) for archival.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Applied ML (Probe Stewards): maintain probe taxonomy, label schema, and retention metadata fields. Primary owner of this policy.
- Data Platform: implements storage lifecycle rules, access controls, and cost reports.
- Vendor Management: negotiates vendor rates, SLAs, and compliance attestations.
- Security & Privacy: approves retention periods for customer-derived probes and redaction procedures.
sections.heading: Roles & Responsibilities

sections.body:
- Payment model: per-labeled-item with QA-tier multiplier. Final payout = base_rate * (1 + qa_bonus) where qa_bonus depends on audit pass rate.
- Base rate bands (USD per judgment, approximate ranges):
  * Simple binary label: $0.06 - $0.12
  * Multi-class single-turn: $0.20 - $0.45
  * Multi-turn dialog (per-turn): $0.40 - $1.10
  * Complex reasoning / chain-of-thought annotation: $1.50 - $4.00
- QA multiplier:
  * Audit pass >= 98%: +12% bonus
  * 95% <= pass < 98%: +6% bonus
  * 90% <= pass < 95%: +0% bonus
  * pass < 90%: action: retraining and partial rework; pay withheld until rework passes.
- Minimum effective hourly guarantee for internal annotators: $18/hr equivalent (useful for long tasks with many micro judgments).
- Vendor SLA expectations: average label latency < 48 hours for standard tasks, < 24 hours for high-priority probes. Penalties apply for repeated misses.
sections.heading: Annotator economics (recommended bands and pay model)

sections.body:
1) Sentinel audits: 5–10% of items randomly selected for gold checks per batch.
2) Inter-annotator agreement (IAA): report Cohen's Kappa or Krippendorff alpha per task; threshold: Kappa >= 0.65 for promotion to production probes.
3) Review pipeline: failed sentinels trigger reviewer queue; repeated failures escalate to vendor management.
4) Annotator feedback loop: weekly calibration sessions and example-led remediation.

Probe metadata and minimum schema (fields required in probe catalog):
- probe_id (string), created_by (string), created_at (YYYY-MM-DD), source (synthetic | shadow | customer), sensitivity_level (public | internal | restricted), retention_tier (hot | cold | delete_on_criteria), labels (list), annotator_id (string|vendor-id), qa_pass (true|false), qa_notes (string), last_accessed (YYYY-MM-DD), linked_eval_id (string), embargo_until (YYYY-MM-DD|null).
sections.heading: Quality control and instrumentation

sections.body:
- Hot (default for newly created probes): 180 days from created_at unless promoted. Accessible to eval harness and shadowing pipelines.
- Cold: 3 years from created_at. Moved to cold after 180 days of inactivity or explicit archival. Retrieval windows: 24–72 hours.
- Delete-on-criteria: immediate deletion after fulfillment of legal/contractual erasure requests or on-demand for restricted customer data after NDA review.
- Permanent archive: select seed sets (curated benchmarks) may be retained indefinitely; these must have explicit product owner approval and an associated retention waiver.
sections.heading: Retention policy (default tiers and TTLs)

sections.body:
- All customer-derived probes default to sensitivity_level=restricted unless redacted and approved by Privacy.
- Annotator access: annotators should not see raw PII. Use programmatic redaction and privacy-preserving interfaces.
- Access logs: every read/write/restore from cold storage must be logged with user, action, and timestamp. Audit log retention: 2 years.
sections.heading: Data access and privacy controls

sections.body:
| Component | Unit | Qty | Unit Cost (USD) | Monthly Cost (USD) | Notes |
| Hot object storage | GB | 2,500 | 0.024 | 60 | S3 standard-like tier used by evals |
| Cold archival | GB | 12,000 | 0.004 | 48 | Glacier-like pricing |
| Retrieval API / egress | ops | 4,000 | 0.002 | 8 | peek/replays by evaluation harness |

| QA review labor | hours | 200 | 45 | 9,000 | internal reviewers and calibration |
| Total (example) | | | | 69,116 | Budget planning input |

Operational runbook: enforcement and typical procedures
1) Daily job: retention-enforcer runs at 02:00 UTC. Steps:
   a) Query probe_catalog for items where retention_tier=hot AND created_at < now() - 180d AND last_accessed < now() - 90d.
   b) For candidates, create a move-to-cold task and notify probe steward slack channel (#probe-stewards).
   c) When moving to cold, update retention_tier and set last_moved_to_cold timestamp.
2) Weekly audit: run a probe-ttl-audit report listing items scheduled for deletion within 30 days. Notify owners.
3) Deletion procedure (manual gating for restricted):
   1. Verify legal/customer erasure token.
   2. Run redact-and-delete CLI (example below).
   3. Append deletion event to retention_audit_log.
sections.heading: Cost estimation and example table (monthly cost model)

sections.heading: S3 lifecycle example (JSON snippet for Data Platform)

sections.body:
- Annotation throughput (labels/day) by vendor and task type. Target: sustained throughput with <15% variance week-over-week.
- QA pass rate (gold sentinel pass %) per batch. SLO: >= 95%.
- Average time-to-label (mean and p95). Target: mean < 24h for standard tasks.
- Probe catalog storage by tier (GB) and monthly cost. Budget variance alert: >10% increase month-over-month triggers finance review.
- Retention compliance rate: % of probes older than TTL that are still in hot storage (target < 1%).
sections.heading: Metrics and dashboards (what to monitor)

sections.body:
1) Probe steward drafts task spec and rough complexity estimate.
2) Run pilot with 500 items and measure median time-per-item and QA pass rate.
3) Compute effective hourly equivalent and map to base_rate band.
4) Submit vendor rate change request with evidence (pilot metrics).
5) After 2 successful pilot batches (consistent IAA and QA), promote task to production pricing.
sections.heading: Onboarding and pay adjustment flow for new tasks

sections.body:
- Retention waivers must be recorded as a short-form ADR in Applied ML with owner signoff and expiration date.
- Emergency retention freeze (e.g., ongoing incident triage): applied-ml-oncall may freeze deletion for up to 30 days; approval and rationale logged.
sections.heading: Exception handling and retention waivers

sections.body:
- Monthly compliance digest emailed to Security & Privacy and Finance summarizing retention transitions, deletions, vendor spend, and active waivers.
- Random third-party audit: once per year, a vendor (approved by Legal) may audit probe handling.
