payload.page_title: Slice Synthesis Governance and Localization Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the governance process and technical procedure for synthesizing evaluation slices and localized derivative probes used in continuous evals, stress benchmarks, and production shadowing. It defines responsibilities, sampling budgets, quality gates, telemetry contracts, and localization constraints to ensure probes remain representative and safe across languages, regions, and product features.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers
- Evaluator / probe authors
- Product QA and Safety stewards
- Model-onboarding owners

Scope:
This document covers:
- Derivative probe generation (seed mutation, paraphrase, noise injection).
- Cross-locale and dialect localization rules.
- Sampling governance (budgets, quotas, retention).
- Telemetry and metadata contract for probes and synthetic examples.
- Quality guardrails and automatic rejection criteria.
Not in scope: human annotation instructions (see related annotation charters) and private customer data handling (see privacy-first-shadow-eval-and-dp-certification).

Definitions:
- Seed: a canonical prompt or user-exemplar used to generate derivative probes.
- Derivative probe: any synthetic or transformed prompt created from a seed (paraphrase, translation, noise-perturbed, adapter-context).
- Slice: a labeled subset of workload defined by intent, complexity, or locale (e.g., billing-clarification, spanish-colloquial, long-context).
- Localization family: group of locales/languages sharing a translation and cultural adaptation policy (e.g., en-US/en-GB -> English family).

Governance principles:
1) Traceability: Every derivative probe must include provenance metadata: seed_id, generator_version, transformation_chain, author, and creation_timestamp.
2) Minimal human cost: Favor automatic synthesis when quality gates pass; preserve human review for high-risk slices or customer-impacting features.
3) Budgeted sampling: Each team has a monthly synthesis budget in tokens and probe-counts; budget exhausted => escalation to evaluator lead.
4) Local fidelity: For localization families, include at least one native-speaker validation sample per slice for languages with >1% of traffic.

Metadata (telemetry) contract (required fields):
- probe_id (string)
- seed_id (string)
- slice_tags (list)
- generator (string) e.g. "paraphrase-v2" or "translate-bridge-en-to-es"
- generator_version (string)
- transform_chain (string) e.g. "seed->synonym-perturb(0.2)->paraphrase-v2"
- locale (string) e.g. "es-419"
- estimated_token_cost (int)
- human_review_status (enum) {none, sampled, approved, rejected}
- provenance_url (string) link to source artifact in eval-mesh or storage
- safety_review_tag (string) optional safety label if flagged

Sampling and budget rules:
- Default budget per owning team: 5k probes / month or 1M tokens, whichever is first.
- High-risk slices (financial instructions, legal guidance) capped at 500 auto-synth probes / month unless human-reviewed.
- Localization multiplier: for locales marked as "high fidelity" (top 10% traffic), synthesize a 1:1 ratio to en seeds; for low-traffic locales, cap at 10% of en volume.
- Retention policy: keep synthesized probes and metadata for 24 months. Older probes must be archived with audit trail.

Quality gates (automated):
Run in order; failure at any gate marks the probe as "rejected-automated" and triggers triage.
1) Tokenization sanity: probe must tokenize without OOV errors and token count <= 4x seed length.
2) Semantic-presence check: intent classifier confidence >= 0.7 for target slice.
3) Toxicity filter: run safety classifier v3; toxicity score < 0.2 or flagged for human_review_status.
4) Model-consistency smoke: run lightweight evaluator (evaluator-lite) against production model and baseline model: normalized response similarity >= 0.65 (unless slice expects diversity).
5) Locale fluency spot-check: language identification must match locale with confidence >= 0.9.

Quality gates (human):
- Any probe failing automated gates but within salvage thresholds (e.g., toxicity between 0.2-0.35) is queued for human review.
- Human review checklist: fluency, cultural appropriateness, PII leakage, and instruction preservation. Use the HumanReview UI in eval-mesh (link in related_pages).

Derivation strategies (examples):
- Paraphrase ensemble: 3 paraphrase models (paraphrase-v1/v2/paraphrase-light) with disagreement pruning: keep probes where at least 2 models agree on intent classifier.
- Translation bridge: seed->translate(en->pivot_lang)->paraphrase->back-translate->normalize. Include intermediate artifacts for audit.
- Noise injection: controlled character/token-level perturbations to simulate ASR/typo errors; parameterize by noise_rate (0.01, 0.05, 0.1).

Procedure: Creating a new localized slice (step-by-step)
1) Define slice in the slice registry: slug, owner_team, acceptance_criteria, and initial seed list (minimum 20 seeds).
2) Create a synthesis job in probe-orch with parameters: generator_set, locale_targets, noise_profile, and sampling_budget. Example CLI: 
   probe-orch create --slice billing-clarification --seeds seeds/billing-clarity-2025.json --generators paraphrase-v2,translate-bridge --locales en-US,es-419 --budget 200
3) Probe-orch emits artifacts to s3://eval-mesh/synth/{slice}/{job_id}/ including metadata.json and samples.csv.
4) Run auto-gates: call eval-harness auto-gate --input s3://eval-mesh/synth/{job_id}/metadata.json --out s3://eval-mesh/synth/{job_id}/gated.json
5) If any probes are queued for human review, assign to a reviewer via the HumanReview UI and mark status.
6) Approve and promote a subset (minimum 200 approved probes) to the probe registry for continuous evals.

Role and ownership matrix:
- Slice owner: owns definition, acceptance criteria, and seed list. (Team-level)
- Probe author: initiates synthesis jobs and triage. (Applied ML / Evaluator)
- Quality steward: signs off on human-reviewed probes for high-risk slices. (Safety / Product)
- Telemetry owner: ensures probes emit required metadata. (Observability / Eng-DE)

Metrics and SLOs for synthesis pipeline:
- Gate processing latency: 95th percentile <= 2 minutes per probe for automated gates.
- Human review turnaround: median <= 48 hours for sampled probes.
- Rejection rate (automated): target < 12% for low-risk slices; < 6% for seeded QA sets.
- Localization coverage: top-10 locales must reach 95% of planned probe volume within 7 days of job completion.

Example metadata JSON (single-line, stored in metadata.json):
{"probe_id":"probe-20260115-0001","seed_id":"seed-billing-0007","slice_tags":["billing","clarification","long-context"],"generator":"paraphrase-v2","generator_version":"2.1.0","transform_chain":"seed->paraphrase-v2->noise(0.01)","locale":"es-419","estimated_token_cost":18,"human_review_status":"none","provenance_url":"s3://eval-mesh/synth/billing-20260115/job-7/probe-0001.txt"}

Interoperability notes (integration with quantization profiles and runtime):
- Mark probes with a "quant_sensitivity" tag when probes exercise long-context or high-precision numeric outputs. This flag must trigger the quant-impact-synthesis pipeline (see quantization-profiles directory) to validate behavior under int8/int4 artifacts.
- For probes in dedicated/private workloads, ensure the provenance_url points to private storage and that telemetry respects customer-data redaction policies.

Triage playbook for regression signals (quick steps):
1) Alert from evaluation-dashboard identifies a slice-level quality drop > 5% compared to baseline.
2) Kick off synthetic-bisect: re-run the slice with multiple random seeds and generator_versions to determine whether regression is generator- or model-driven.
3) Check derivation metadata for generator_version drift or locale mapping changes.
4) If candidate root cause is quant-related, add quant-sensitivity-tagged probes to the failing cohort and re-evaluate under quantized artifacts.
5) If human-safety issue found, escalate to Safety oncall and freeze synthetic generation for affected slice.

Rollout and deprecation policy:
- New slice must run in shadow for 2 weeks with continuous monitoring and a minimum of 1k interactions.
- Deprecate a slice only after: owner_team sign-off, archival of artifacts, and update to slice registry.

Appendix: example slice registry table (column descriptions)
- slug: short identifier for the slice (string)
- owner: Owning team
- seeds_count: initial seed count
- target_locales: comma-separated locale list
- risk_level: low|medium|high
- last_audit: YYYY-MM-DD

References and links:
- Eval Mesh: internal portlet for artifact storage and orchestration.
- HumanReview UI: link in top nav > Evaluations > HumanReview.
- Related docs: localization-translation-guidelines, probe-curation-stewardship-and-annotation-charter.

Contact:
For questions or to request increased synthesis budget, open a ticket in #eval-synthesis-support or email maya.singh@redwood-inference.com.

payload.page_title: probe-lifecycle-and-annotation-economics-playbook-2026

sections.body:
Summary
This playbook describes the lifecycle, scheduling, and cost-accounting model for evaluation probes used across Redwood's eval harness. It combines operational rules, annotation economics, automated retirement policies, and quantization-aware handling to help teams run targeted, repeatable probes while keeping cost and label quality under control.

Audience
- ML engineers and evaluators who author/maintain probes
- Platform engineers who operate the eval scheduler and probe runner
- Product owners who require cost and coverage reporting

Scope
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Probe life stages (authoring → active → stale → retired)
- Annotation budgeting and pay rates, including SLA expectations for human review
- Scheduling windows, priority tiers, and run quotas
- Cost model: compute + annotation + storage attribution
- Quantization and model-variant sensitivity experiments for probes
- Automated triage signals and handoff to regression teams

1) Definitions
- Probe: A single, repeatable evaluation workload unit (prompt + expected checks + metadata).
- Probe Bundle: A logical group of probes used to exercise a slice (e.g., long-context, safety, coherence).
- Run: One execution of a probe against a target model/version with a specific config.
- Annotator Task: Human-labeling task derived from probe output for quality measurement.

2) Probe lifecycle (authoring to retirement)
- Authoring: Create probe with complete metadata (owner, business-impact, weight, tags, target-matrix). Use the probe template below.
- Review: 1 asynchronous reviewer + auto-lint. Criteria: reproducibility, determinism seed, clear pass/fail checks.
- Activation: Mark probe active and assign schedule tier (real-time / daily / weekly / monthly).
- Monitoring: Track run success rate, variance, token-cost, and annotation disagreement.
- Aging: If a probe has not triggered an annotator task and has <1% coverage drift for 90 days, it transitions to stale.
- Retirement: Owner or probe-committee retires the probe after stakeholder sign-off. Store archived probe with retention tags for 18 months.

3) Probe metadata template (YAML)
- For authoring, include the following fields in the probe manifest (example):

---
probe_id: "projX_longcontext_042"
owner: "team-language-infra"
business_impact: "high"
slice_tags: ["long-context", "kv-cache-sensitive"]
weight: 2
priority_tier: "daily"  # one of real-time/daily/weekly/monthly
seedable: true
expected_checks:
  - check_type: "semantic_equivalence"
    threshold: 0.82
run_configs:
  - model_family: "redwood-7b-opt"
    quant_profile: "int8-ev"
    context_length: 4096
---

4) Scheduling and quotas
- Priority tiers and default run quotas per probe bundle:
  - real-time: max 2 runs/minute, 95% of requests < 100ms scheduling latency
  - daily: up to 2,000 runs/day per bundle
  - weekly: up to 10,000 runs/week per bundle
  - monthly: up to 100,000 runs/month per bundle
- Backpressure policy: If aggregate queue latency > 5s for 3 consecutive minutes, degrade monthly → weekly → daily runs by 50% until recovery.

5) Annotation economics and budgeting
- Cost components per probe run: compute_cost + storage_cost + expected_annotation_cost*annotation_probability. Annotation probability is determined by sampling rate and sentinel triggers.
- Default annotation sampler: stratified sample 2% of runs for high-impact probes, 0.2% for low-impact. Increase sampling when variance > 0.05 (normalized score).
- Annotator pay bands (example internal rates):
  - QA/Junior annotator: $0.18 / labeled item
  - Senior annotator / adjudicator: $0.45 / disputed item
  - Specialist (safety/legal): $1.25 / review when escalated
- Budget allocation formula (string version):
  - monthly_annotation_budget = sum_over_probes(estimated_monthly_runs * sample_rate * pay_rate)
- Example: 10k runs/month * 2% sample * $0.18 = $36/month for that probe bundle.

6) Quality guardrails and thresholds
- Primary metrics to monitor per probe: pass_rate, semantic_similarity_mean, token_cost_per_run, annotator_disagreement_rate.
- Alert triggers (auto-created):
  - Pass rate drop > 6% absolute within 48h → create incident in eval-oncall (severity P2).
  - Annotator disagreement > 12% for two consecutive sample windows → escalate to triage board.
  - Token cost increase > 30% vs rolling-14d median → cost-owner notification.

7) Quantization-aware probe handling
- When evaluating quantized model variants, tag the probe run with quant_profile and track delta metrics (degradation vectors): semantic drift, hallucination-likelihood, latency delta.
- If semantic_similarity_mean drops by > 0.04 vs float baseline for > 5% of run samples, automatically flag for targeted re-annotation.
- Recommended experiment pattern: shadow-run quantized variant alongside float baseline with 5x sample multiplier on corner-case probes for first 72h.

8) Automated triage signals and handoff
- Triage signals (generated by telemetry pipeline): sudden pass_rate drop, sample variance spike, annotator disagreement, cross-slice correlation with infra incidents.
- Triage flow (automated):
  1. Signal detected → create Triage Issue in "eval-triage" board with prefilled diagnostics (probe_id, model_version, run_config, recent diff, telemetry links).
  2. On-call evaluator ACKS within 60 minutes.
  3. If not ACKed, escalate to ML infra oncall.
  4. If confirmed regression, create regression-bisect job and assign to regression team.

9) Regression bisect integration checklist
- Minimum reproducer: probe manifest + deterministic seed + model binary or docker tag + config file.
- Attach logs: token-level outputs, top-k logits (if enabled), KV cache metrics, latency breakdown.
- Run the automated-bisect command (example):

redwood-eval bisect --probe projX_longcontext_042 --from v2026-01-20 --to v2026-02-10 --output /tmp/bisect-report.json

10) Ownership and escalation matrix
- Probe owner: maintains manifest, signs off on retirement, first responder for probe-level failures.
- Eval oncall: responsible for triage and first-pass investigation (1-hour SLA).
- Regression squad: owns bisect and patching if code/model regression identified (72h remediation target for P1 regressions).
- Platform cost team: monthly reconciliation of annotation and compute spend vs budget.

11) Reporting and dashboards (minimum set)
- Probe Health dashboard (by bundle): pass_rate, sample_rate, annotator_disagreement, avg_token_cost, run_count_7d.
- Cost attribution table: probe_id → compute_cost_last_30d → annotation_cost_last_30d → total_cost.
- Freshness table: last_run, last_annotation, days_since_last_success.

12) Operational recipes (how-to)
- Author a new probe:
  1. Fork probe-template.yaml in the probe repo.
  2. Populate metadata and smoke-tests.
  3. Submit PR; include 1 reviewer and 1 cross-team reviewer if business_impact==high.
  4. Merge and mark active via the console tag.

- Increase sampling temporarily for a suspect model: CLI example:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
    -d '{"probe_bundle":"projX-longcontext","sample_multiplier":5, "reason":"quant-experiment-2026-02"}'
    https://console.internal.redwood/api/eval/sample-control

- Archive a stale probe:
  1. Owner files retirement request.
  2. Probe committee reviews.
  3. If approved, set status: retired and set retention=18 months.

13) Cost-saving heuristics and knobs
- Apply cache-aware downsampling for probes that drive redundant KV cache fills.
- Use lower-fidelity quant probes (int8) for daily health checks, reserve float runs for weekly deep checks.
- Promote probe weights to reduce unnecessary runs: increase weight on high-value probes and reduce frequency for low-impact ones.

14) Example SQL for monthly annotation budget report (string):
SELECT probe_id, SUM(runs) as runs_30d, AVG(sample_rate) as avg_sample, SUM(sample_rate * runs * pay_rate) as est_annotation_cost FROM probe_runs WHERE run_ts > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY probe_id ORDER BY est_annotation_cost DESC;

15) Appendices
A. Probe health SLA table:
- Active probes: scheduling latency p95 < 2s, run success rate > 98%
- Annotation turnaround: 95% labeled within 48 hours for sampled items
- Triage ACK: 60 minutes

B. Retention and privacy notes:
- Probes labeled as containing PII must use the privacy-redaction pipeline before any human annotation. See privacy-and-dp guidelines.
- Archive only non-sensitive artifacts; sensitive outputs must be purged after 90 days unless retained for a legal hold.

C. Contacts
- Probe platform owner: infra-probe-owners@redwood.ai
- Eval oncall rotation: eval-oncall@redwood.ai
- Annotation ops: annotation-ops@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Longtail Failure Fusion & Rollback Codex

sections.body:
Summary

This codex describes a prescriptive, reproducible procedure for fusing longtail failure signals across the eval harness, production shadow runs, prompt/embedding drift detectors, and quantization compatibility telemetry to reach an operational rollback decision. The document synthesizes rules for signal weighting, minimum evidence requirements, automated and manual rollback triggers, and post-rollback verification steps. It is intended for oncall engineers, applied-ML owners, and SREs who participate in regression triage.

Scope

- Applies to model-serving regressions (hosted/dedicated/private) impacting: generation coherency, functioncall correctness, embedding stability, semantic drift, and major cost anomalies caused by quant migrations.
- Excludes: single-request infra failures (network flaps), transient infra-only node failures covered by infra runbooks.

Primary owners and run participants

- Primary owner: Model Reliability (eng) — contact: @marisol.chen
- Triage coordinator: oncall-applied-ml
- SRE partner: oncall-sre
- Notify: product-owners for services with >10% user impact or revenue-path customers.

Signals and authoritative data sources

1) Eval Harness (eval-mesh)
   - Key metrics: fidelity_delta (Fdelta), response_stability_index (RSI), slice_failure_rate (SFR)
   - Data latency: 2–10 minutes for continuous probes, batch horizon 1–4 hours

2) Shadow / Shadow-orchestrator
   - Key metrics: live_regression_score (LRS), percentile disagreement (pDisag), functioncall-failures per 1000 (FC_1k)
   - Config: shadow cohorts must reflect the affected tenant mix; see section "Shadow cohort hygiene"

3) Telemetry from Runtime (probe-farm, kv-cache-trace)
   - Key metrics: kvcache_miss_rate, tokenization_anomalies, tail_latency_p99

4) Quant path and artifact health (quant-scheduler)
   - Key metrics: quant_loss_proxy (QLP), quant-round-trip-error (QRTE), observed compression ratio (CR)

5) Customer / Canary feedback (customer-reported defects, canary errors)
   - Structured via support tickets tagged regression-triage and in Slack channel #regressions-ops

Fusion rules (how signals are combined)

Principle: prefer signal breadth over depth for longtail regressions — a weak signal across many orthogonal sources is more actionable than a single strong metric from a brittle probe.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
||Signal source||Typical weight||Minimum sample size||
|Eval Harness (slice-anchored)|0.30|>= 50 probes per slice|
|Shadow (live)|0.28|>= 1000 requests in cohort|
|Runtime telemetry|0.18|>= 5000 tokens across traces|
|Quant artifact|0.14|>= 3 model variants tested|
|Customer reports|0.10|>= 2 independent tickets|
sections.heading: Evidence model (numeric weights)

sections.body:
- For each signal compute a normalized anomaly score in [0,1] where 0 = no anomaly and 1 = severe. (Normalization procedure is documented in Appendix A.)
- Fusion score = sum(weight_i * normalized_score_i).
- Action thresholds:
  - Fusion score < 0.25: Monitor. Open triage ticket but no rollback.
  - 0.25 <= Fusion score < 0.50: Elevated investigation. Consider targeted canary/patch.
  - Fusion score >= 0.50: Strong candidate for rollback or traffic re-routing. Proceed to rollback runbook.

Minimum evidence gates (hard requirements before automated rollback)

1) Shadow-orchestrator cohort must show pDisag >= 0.12 AND LRS >= 0.35 for the affected slice, or
2) Eval-mesh fidelity_delta >= 0.18 on at least two orthogonal slices (e.g., intent-slice + functioncall-slice), or
3) Quant-loss-proxy > 0.20 AND QRTE producing >1% top-k misrank compared to baseline.

If none of the minimum gates are satisfied, rollback should not be automated. Manual rollback is allowed with oncall + model-owner approval (see manual approval checklist).

Automated rollback triggers (when CI/CD integration permitted)

- A scheduled anomaly aggregator service (regression-blender) will compute fusion scores every 5 minutes. If fusion score >= 0.60 AND at least one minimum evidence gate is true, trigger automated rollback preflight (not final rollback):
  1. Open an incident ticket with pre-filled diagnostics and a pre-rollback plan.
  2. Run targeted canary unroute to baseline for 5% of traffic for 10 minutes.
  3. If the canary unroute reduces fusion score by >= 50%, proceed to full rollback. Else escalate to manual triage.

Manual rollback decision checklist

- Required participants: oncall-applied-ml, model-owner, oncall-sre.
- Checklist items (all must be considered; at least 4/6 must be positive to proceed):
  1. Does the fusion score >= 0.50? (Yes/No)
  2. Is there corroborating customer impact (support tickets or telemetry)?
  3. Can a partial rollback (per-region or per-tenant) reduce risk to observability?
  4. Has a quant migration been applied recently to this model build?
  5. Are there known infra anomalies that could confound signals?
  6. Has the baseline passed the same evaluation probes within the last 24 hours?

Rollback runbook (step-by-step)

1) Pre-rollback: Verify signals and capture a debug snapshot
   - Execute: rwd-eval query --slice <slice-name> --window 60m --format json > /tmp/slice_snapshot.json
   - Run: rwd-shadow snapshot --cohort <cohort-id> --duration 10m --out /tmp/shadow_snapshot.json

2) Partial mitigation (fast path, recommended)
   - Option A (routing): Reduce traffic to the suspect model by 30% for 10 minutes via traffic-router:
     traffic-router scale --model <model-id> --percent-decrease 30 --duration 10m --reason "regression-fusion"
   - Option B (fallback): Enable functioncall-strict-fallback policy:
     rwd-config set routing.fallback_policy functioncall_strict --enable true --ttl 600

3) Full rollback (if indicated)
   - Promote previous stable model version: rwd-deploy promote --model <model-id> --version <baseline-version> --force --annot "auto-rollback-fusion"
   - Verify: wait until rwd-deploy status --model <model-id> shows all pods at Ready and new baseline traffic distribution >= 95%

4) Post-rollback verification (10m, 30m, 2h checks)
   - Run the same eval probes used in the detection path and compare Fdelta/RSI. Expect fusion score drop >= 0.5 within 30 minutes.
   - Confirm p99 latency, kvcache_miss_rate and error budget consumption back to baseline.

Communication and stakeholders

- Triage ticket template must include: fusion_score, per-signal normalized values, top 3 affected slices, example failing probes (id + text), and snapshot links. Use the incident template /templates/regression-codex.md
- Slack: post initial alert to #regressions-ops and tag @model-owner and @sre-oncall.
- Customer-facing comms: if impacted tenants >10% or revenue-path customers affected, follow the customer comms playbook and notify CS within 30 minutes.

Postmortem and blameless analysis

- If rollback occurred, open postmortem within 48 hours. Include: root-cause hypothesis, probe artifacts, quant artifacts (if applicable), and timeline with fusion_score and per-signal graphs.
- Add remediation actions to the Regression Debt backlog and assign owners.

Example incident (short walkthrough)

- Timeline:
  - 01:10: regression-blender fusion_score = 0.62 (quant QLP 0.22, shadow LRS 0.4, RSI 0.25)
  - 01:15: automated preflight reduces suspect model traffic by 5% -> fusion drops to 0.58
  - 01:25: canary unroute 10% traffic -> fusion drops to 0.28 -> rollback promoted baseline at 01:40
  - 02:15: all verification probes show expected RSI improvement, postmortem opened.

Appendix A — Normalizing signals (procedure)

1) For each metric compute z-score using rolling 30-day mean and std. Convert z to a sigmoid-normalized score in [0,1] with scaling tuned per metric.
2) Clip outliers at 99.9 percentile to avoid single-probe domination.

Appendix B — Sample config snippets

- Eval probe registration (example YAML):
  ---
  probe_name: "functioncall-critical-anchored"
  slices: ["functioncall", "finance-instruction"]
  frequency: 5m
  min_samples: 50
  acceptance_criteria:
    - metric: fidelity_delta
      threshold: 0.12

- Regression blender config (JSON-like):
  {
    "fusion_weights": {
      "eval_mesh": 0.30,
      "shadow": 0.28,
      "runtime": 0.18,
      "quant": 0.14,
      "customer": 0.10
    },
    "fusion_interval_seconds": 300,
    "automated_preflight": {
      "canary_percent": 5,
      "canary_duration_secs": 600,
      "rollback_threshold": 0.5
    }
  }

Appendix C — Quick CLI checklist for oncall

- Capture snapshots:
  rwd-eval query --slice <slice> --window 60m --format json > /tmp/snap.json
  rwd-shadow snapshot --cohort <cohort> --duration 10m --out /tmp/shadow.json
- Check fusion score:
  rwd-blender score --model <model-id> --window 15m
- Trigger partial traffic reduction (manual):
  traffic-router scale --model <model-id> --percent-decrease 30 --duration 10m --reason "manual-triage"

Related docs and ownership

- See also: eval-mesh operational guide, quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol, and shadow-orchestrator cohorting best practices.
- This codex will be reviewed quarterly by Model Reliability and SRE; ownership: Model Reliability (eng).

Revision history

- 2026-11-05: Created by Marisol Chen.
- 2026-12-18: Weighting updates after shadow cohort experiment (reviewers: Diego).
- 2027-02-14: Added automated preflight and canary verification steps.

payload.page_title: Automated Regression Bisect and Blame Assistant Playbook

sections.body: This playbook describes an automated workflow for detecting, bisecting, and attributing model regressions across Redwood Inference's evaluation, onboarding, and production promotion pipelines. It formalizes the components of the automated bisect (regress-bisect), the blame-assistant heuristics, alerting thresholds, CI integrations, and an operator runbook for triage teams. The goal is to reduce mean time-to-blame (MTTB) from hours/days to under 90 minutes for high-severity regressions.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to regressions impacting core ML quality signals (semantic accuracy, hallucination rate, safety metrics), performance regressions (median/tail latency, OOMs), and cost regressions (token cost/per-response increases).
- Covers regressions introduced by: model weights, tokenizer/tokenization changes, quantization/precision profile changes, runtime kernel updates, prompt/template changes, and dataset/annotation updates used in eval harness.
sections.heading: Scope and motivation

sections.body:
1) Regression detection: an automated alert where a monitored metric crosses a configured threshold relative to a baseline (rolling 14d median).
2) Bisect window: the time range over which candidate commits/artifacts are evaluated to locate the first-change likely to have introduced the regression.
3) Blame Assistant: a heuristics engine that ranks likely root causes (model, quant, runtime, prompt, eval data) and attaches confidence scores and evidence artifacts.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
1. Detection: nightly and continuous eval jobs compute metric deltas (accuracy, safety, latency) and write alerts to the monitoring topic (kafka://eval-regressions).
2. Triage autopilot: a Lambda/runner creates a regression incident and triggers regress-bisect with the default bisect window (7 days). The incident contains metric diffs, failing slices, recent deployments, and a seed prompt set that reproduces the failure.
3. Bisect: regress-bisect runs binary search across candidate commits/artifacts in parallel using isolated eval sandboxes (shadow jobs). Each candidate executes the same evaluation harness and computes delta metrics.
4. Blame: the blame-assistant gathers bisect outputs, metadata (model hash, quant profile, runtime version, prompt revision), and applies attribution heuristics to produce a ranked list of root-cause hypotheses.
5. Operator review & remediation: triage team reviews the top hypothesis, performs remediation steps (rollback or hotfix), and updates the incident and regression dashboard.
sections.heading: High-level flow

sections.body:
| Metric type | Baseline comparator | Alert threshold | Severity |
|-------------|--------------------|-----------------|----------|
| Semantic accuracy (in-domain) | 14d rolling median | delta <= -3.5 percentage points | P1 |
| Hallucination rate | 14d rolling median | delta >= +5 percentage points | P1 |
| Safety fail rate (policy) | 7d rolling median | delta >= +2 percentage points | P1 |
| Median latency (p50) | 7d rolling median | increase >= 30% and > 50ms | P2 |
| Tail latency (p99) | 7d rolling median | increase >= 50% or > 200ms | P1 |
| Memory/OOMs | run count baseline | > 3 OOMs/hour | P1 |
| Token cost / response | 14d rolling median | increase >= 10% | P2 |
sections.heading: Automated detection thresholds (starting defaults)

sections.body:
- bisect_window: 7d
- parallel_jobs: 4
- timeout_per_candidate: 45m
- min_repro_rate: 60% (candidate must reproduce failing slice in >= 60% of runs to be considered a hit)
- eval_seed_set: top 250 prompts from the failing slice (sliced by user_intent and context_length)
- isolation: ephemeral VMs with pinned runtime: we run candidate against identical hardware profiles
sections.heading: Bisect configuration (regress-bisect defaults)

sections.body:
```
{
  "job_name": "regress-bisect-2026-02-10-ashap",
  "bisect_window_start": "2026-02-03T00:00:00Z",
  "bisect_window_end": "2026-02-10T00:00:00Z",
  "parallelism": 4,
  "seed_prompts": "s3://eval-seeds/failing_slice_124.json",
  "metrics": ["sem_accuracy", "hallucination_rate", "p50_latency", "p99_latency"],
  "min_repro_rate": 0.6
}
```
sections.heading: Sample bisect job JSON (used by orchestrator)

sections.body:
The blame-assistant creates hypotheses with confidence and supporting evidence. Example heuristics (ordered by priority) and what to look for:

- Model hash change: if the bisect narrows to a candidate where only the model artifact differs from prior good candidate. Evidence: model SHA, model card differences, per-layer norm changes > 2x. Confidence++ if failing tokens align with embeddings drift.
- Tokenizer change: evidence from tokenization mismatch rates, token length distribution shift, increased unk/token-splitting counts, snapshot diff of tokenizer files. Confidence++ if failure tokens show different segmentation.
- Quantization profile change: evidence includes quant profile ID, quant calibration logs, increased numeric error on synthetic probes, and reproduction only under quantized variant. Confidence++ if unquantized candidate passes.
- Runtime kernel or kernel flags: evidence from runtime version, kernel flags diff, CPU/GPU driver changes, and regression reproduces with runtime X but not with runtime X-1. Confidence++ if p99 latency shifts and memory allocation traces differ.
- Prompt/template changes: evidence from repo diff of prompt templates, mapping of prompt version to failing seeds, and operator-introduced changes in PRs correlated to bisect window.
- Eval harness changes (scoring/counting): evidence includes scorer version, label mappings, and unit-test failures in eval harness.

Each hypothesis includes: hypothesis_id, primary_cause, confidence_score (0-100), supporting_artifacts (list of URLs), reproducibility_rate, suggested_next_steps.
sections.heading: Blame-assistant heuristics and evidence types

sections.body:
1. Acknowledge incident in PagerDuty and link to regression incident page.
2. Confirm the alert: examine the failing slice and verify reproduction locally using the provided seed prompts.
   - CLI: evalctl reproduce --seed s3://eval-seeds/failing_slice_124.json --model latest --runs 20
3. If the reproduction rate < min_repro_rate, mark as intermittent and run extended-run (200 runs) to gather more signal.
4. Kick off regress-bisect (if not already running):
   - CLI: regress-bisect start --incident-id R-2026-0210-124 --window 7d --parallel 4
5. Review bisect progress and artifacts every 15 minutes. Common statuses: searching, candidate_evaluating, candidate_confirmed, bisect_complete, bisect_failed.
6. When blame-assistant returns primary hypothesis with confidence >= 70%: follow suggested remediation.
   - Model change -> rollback to previous model (documented below) OR initiate a model-patch PR to fix the specific failure cases.
   - Quantization -> re-evaluate quant config or pin to previous quant profile until patch is available.
   - Runtime -> coordinate with eng-serving-runtime and infra to roll back kernel flags or drivers.
7. After remediation, run the full smoke eval set + production shadow checks and mark incident resolved if metrics return within acceptable bounds.
8. Post-incident, file a regression root-cause analysis (RCA) in the incident page with timeline, chosen remediation, and follow-up actions (e.g., additional gates, new unit tests).
sections.heading: Operator runbook (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Model rollback (hosted):
  - API: POST /admin/models/rollbacks {"model_id": "m-1234", "target_version": "v1.2.3"}
  - CLI: rwinfctl model rollback m-1234 v1.2.3 --reason "regression: sem_accuracy drop"
  - Policy: For P1 regressions with confidence >= 80% on model cause, deploy rollback within 30 minutes after approvals from Eng Lead and Product.

- Quant profile pin (dedicated/private):
  - Update deployment config: set quant_profile: "qp-2025-11-08-stable"
  - Redeploy with canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% if passes smoke checks.
sections.heading: Rollback commands and policies

sections.body:
- CI: regress-bisect is triggered automatically for PRs that touch model onboarding, tokenizer, quantization profiles, and runtime flags when candidate metric changes exceed PR-level thresholds.
- Canary gating: any model promoted to dedicated or private must pass the regression-slice battery (50 critical slices) and show no >2% drop on sem_accuracy slices.
- Slack and Tickets: regress-bisect posts to #ml-regressions and creates a Jira ticket with tags: regression:automated, incident_id.
- Observability: all bisect artifacts (raw outputs, per-prompt diffs, memory traces) are uploaded to s3://regress-artifacts/<incident_id>/ and indexed in the regression dashboard.
sections.heading: Integrations and automation notes

sections.body:
- Non-deterministic failures: stochastic sampling in generation can reduce reproducibility — increase eval runs and seed temperature to 0.0 for deterministic reproduction when possible.
- Cross-tenant noise: regressions that only appear under specific tenant prompts require tenant-aware slicing and permissioned access to seed data.
- Performance cost: running parallel bisects is GPU/CPU intensive. Use cost-budget guardrails and restrict parallelism for low-severity incidents.
sections.heading: Known limitations and caveats

sections.body:
- Add unit tests in the eval-harness for any new prompt template or scoring change touching policy-sensitive signals.
- Add synthetic micro-probes that target known brittle tokens and check tokenization/quantization sensitivity on every model promotion.
- Expand blame-assistant signals: integrate model-introspection features (per-layer activation drift) and automated significance testing (bootstrap confidence intervals).
sections.heading: Follow-up and hardening recommendations

sections.body:
- Regression dashboard: https://console.internal/regressions/dashboard
- Eval harness repo: https://git.internal/redwood/eval-harness
- regress-bisect service runbook: https://console.internal/runbooks/regress-bisect
sections.heading: Related pages and artifacts

sections.body:
- Primary owner: Applied ML team (owner: Asha Patel)
- Secondary owners: Eng Serving Runtime (on kernel/runtime causes), Eng Infra (on driver/VM host causes), Product (on user-facing impact decisions)
- SLA for P1 regressions: acknowledge within 15 minutes, first triage within 60 minutes, MTTB target < 90 minutes.

Appendix: quick CLI reference

- Start a manual bisect: regress-bisect start --incident-id <id> --window 7d --parallel 4 --seeds s3://eval-seeds/<file>
- Check bisect status: regress-bisect status --incident-id <id>
- Fetch artifacts: regress-bisect fetch-artifacts --incident-id <id> --dest ./artifacts/<id>
- Run a local reproduce: evalctl reproduce --seed <s3://...> --model <model_ref> --runs 50

Appendix: example blame-assistant output (JSON snippet):

```
{
  "incident_id": "R-2026-0210-124",
  "hypotheses": [
    {"id": "h1", "primary_cause": "quant_profile_change", "confidence": 82, "evidence": ["s3://regress-artifacts/R-2026-0210-124/quant-probe.csv"], "repro_rate": 0.95},
    {"id": "h2", "primary_cause": "tokenizer_update", "confidence": 35, "evidence": ["https://git.internal/diffs/tokenizer/commit-abc"], "repro_rate": 0.22}
  ]
}
```

End of playbook. For questions or to propose changes to thresholds/policies, open a PR against the eval-harness playbooks directory or contact the Applied ML on-call.

payload.page_title: Regression triage playbook for Optimize configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization)

sections.body: This playbook standardizes how we investigate quality regressions that appear after an Optimize configuration change (batching policy updates, prefix/KV caching settings, or quantization profile switches). It is written for Applied ML oncall / Evals owners, with clear handoffs to Runtime and SRE.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- **A quality gate fails** (smoke or full gate) for a proposed Optimize change.
- **Online canary signals degrade** after a gated change is applied (e.g., increased refusals, task success drop, or customer-reported behavior change).
sections.heading: This playbook is used in two primary situations

sections.body:
- Deep performance tuning (covered by Runtime perf runbooks).
- Model onboarding or prompt set curation (covered by prompt-set ownership docs).

---
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
1. **Treat output regressions as real until proven flaky.** Cost optimizations can produce subtle output changes; avoid dismissing failures as “noise” without evidence.
2. **Reproduce on the same model + runtime + hardware SKU.** Quantization regressions are often hardware- and kernel-path dependent.
3. **Prefer smallest reproducible case.** Reduce to a single prompt (or a small handful) that reliably shows the delta.
4. **Capture artifacts early.** Most time is lost when we cannot reconstruct the exact diff/baseline or request context.

---
sections.heading: Triage principles

sections.body:
- Gate run ID (or rollout/canary ID)
- Change type: batching / caching / quantization
- Model: {model_family, model_version}
- Route/account tier (self-serve vs enterprise)
sections.heading: Collect

sections.body:
- Gate run timed out, infra errors, missing artifacts, GPU starvation
- Flake score elevated; repeated runs disagree
sections.heading: Indicators

sections.body:
- If infra/timeouts: follow **Runbook: Optimize quality gate failures** and re-run with same inputs.
- If inconsistent results: proceed to **Flakiness vs real regression** section.
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body:
- **Long-context prompts** (e.g., > 8k tokens) often implicate KV-cache or quant kernels.
- **Tool/function calling or structured output** often implicates decoding differences (temperature/top_p changes via batching policy side effects).
- **Safety/refusal behavior** changes often implicate subtle logit differences with quantization.
sections.heading: Step 2 — Is the regression isolated to a known category?

sections.body:
- Suspect **batch scheduling / continuous batching / decode** → Runtime (Sofia Ivanova / Mateo Alvarez)
- Suspect **prefix/KV cache correctness** → Runtime caching (Omar El-Sayed / Noah Patel)
- Suspect **quant correctness / kernel path** → Quant (Grace Kim / Arjun Desai)
- Suspect **eval harness / scoring** → Evals (Olivia Grant / Jonas Weber)
- Suspect **production signals / canary pipeline** → SRE + Rollouts (Sean Gallagher / Paula Mendes)

---
sections.heading: Step 3 — Choose owner and escalation path

sections.body: Copy the following into the incident/ticket and attach links as available.
sections.heading: Required artifacts checklist (collect first)

sections.body:
- Optimize recommendation ID (if applicable)
- Config diff (exact)
- Baseline config reference (exact)
- Gate policy used (smoke-only vs smoke+full; thresholds version)
- Apply path: one-click vs auto-apply vs manual change
sections.heading: A) Optimization change metadata

sections.body:
- Gate run ID(s), including retries
- Prompt set IDs and suite versions used
- Sampling parameters: sample size, seed, stratification (if any)
- Scoring version(s): rubric/metric bundle version
- Flake score and rerun/aggregation outcome
sections.heading: B) Gate run / eval metadata

sections.body:
- Model identifier and commit/hash if applicable
- Tokenizer version (if pinned)
- Runtime build version
- Quantization profile name + parameters (e.g., weight-only int8, kv-cache quant on/off)
- GPU SKU (e.g., A100-80GB, H100, L4) and driver/CUDA version
sections.heading: C) Model/runtime/hardware provenance

sections.body:
- 5–20 prompts that demonstrate the regression (or 1 prompt if it’s a hard repro)
- Baseline outputs + optimized outputs
- Decoding parameters used (temperature/top_p/max_tokens/stop)
sections.heading: Minimum

sections.body:
- Logprobs (if available) for the first N tokens
- Token-level diff (baseline vs candidate)
- Any error traces (timeouts, OOM, retries)
sections.heading: Preferred for root cause

sections.body:
- Canary cohort definition and traffic %
- Time window and region
- Online quality metrics deltas (task success, rubric proxy, refusal rate)
- Latency/cost deltas (to rule out overloaded conditions)

---
sections.heading: E) Online (if canary)

sections.body: The goal is to reproduce the regression **outside of production traffic** while matching runtime behavior.
sections.heading: Minimal reproduction setup

sections.body:
Use the gate run inputs as ground truth.

**Inputs needed:** gate_run_id OR (baseline_config_ref + candidate_config_ref + prompt_set_id)
sections.heading: 1) Reproduce from a gate run (preferred)

sections.body:
1. Fetch gate run details and artifacts.
2. Identify the smallest failing suite/prompt subset.
3. Run the harness locally or in a sandbox GPU job using the exact config and model version.

Example (pseudocode CLI; update to current harness tooling):
- `eval-harness gating fetch --gate-run-id <ID> --out ./gate_run_<ID>`
- `eval-harness replay --input ./gate_run_<ID>/repro.json --max-prompts 20 --dump-token-diffs true`

What “good” looks like:
- You can show an identical (or highly similar) score delta.
- You can reproduce the qualitative failure on at least 3 prompts.
sections.heading: Procedure

sections.body: If the regression is reported by a customer or detected online, capture an anonymized reproduction.
sections.heading: 2) Reproduce from a production request

sections.body:
1. Pull a representative request payload (anonymized/redacted) + decoding params.
2. Replay against baseline and candidate configs in the same region and GPU class when possible.
3. Compare outputs and (if enabled) logprobs/token-level diffs.

Example request reproduction template (store as a text artifact, not as nested JSON in this page):
- model: <model>
- prompt/messages: <redacted>
- decoding: temperature=<>, top_p=<>, max_tokens=<>, stop=<>
- baseline_config_ref: <>
- candidate_config_ref: <>
- region + gpu_sku: <>

---
sections.heading: Procedure

sections.body:
- **Non-determinism increase:** larger batch sizes can change ordering/latency; if timeouts or streaming truncation occur, output may change.
- **Decode parameter coupling bug:** some batching paths may incorrectly merge per-request decoding params.
- **Resource contention:** larger microbatches increase memory pressure → OOM fallback paths → degraded quality.
sections.heading: Common failure modes

sections.body:
1. Confirm decoding params are identical baseline vs candidate per request.
2. Confirm max_tokens/stop are not hit earlier due to timeouts.
3. Compare token counts and finish reasons.
4. If failure is only under high concurrency, reproduce with load (small load test) rather than single-request replay.
sections.heading: Checks

sections.body:
- Output differences correlate with concurrency or batch size.
- Any evidence of OOM, fallback kernels, or streaming truncation.
sections.heading: Escalate to Runtime when

sections.body:
- **Incorrect cache keying / collisions:** wrong reuse across prompts/routes.
- **Cache invalidation errors:** stale KV cache used after config/model changes.
- **Long-context degradation:** cache policies may change attention behavior indirectly when combined with specific runtime paths.
sections.heading: Common failure modes

sections.body:
1. Disable cache and confirm regression disappears (A/B run: cache on vs off).
2. Test with long-context prompts and forced cache boundaries.
3. Verify that model version and tokenizer match between cached and uncached runs.
4. Verify prefix caching boundaries align with prompt formatting (chat templates are frequent culprits).
sections.heading: Checks

sections.body:
- Regression appears only when cache is enabled.
- Failures are prompt-template dependent.
sections.heading: Escalate to Runtime caching when

sections.body:
- **Kernel-path dependent correctness issues** (GPU SKU specific).
- **Outlier sensitivity**: some prompts become brittle; failures may concentrate in “hard cases.”
- **Safety/refusal shifts** due to logit perturbations.
sections.heading: Common failure modes

sections.body:
1. Reproduce on the same GPU SKU as the failing run.
2. Compare outputs with logprobs if possible; identify early divergence token.
3. Run a small sweep of prompt lengths (short vs long) to see if divergence correlates with context length.
4. Validate that the quant profile is compatible with the model family and runtime build.
sections.heading: Checks

sections.body:
- Regression is GPU-SKU-specific or only appears under long context.
- Divergence is consistent and starts early in generation.

---
sections.heading: Escalate to Quant owner when

sections.body: We consider a gate failure “likely flaky” only if we can demonstrate instability across reruns and no consistent qualitative failure.
sections.heading: Flakiness vs real regression

sections.body:
- Re-run outcomes oscillate pass/fail with overlapping confidence intervals.
- The failing prompts vary widely across reruns.
- The flake score is above the current quarantine threshold.
sections.heading: Indicators of flakiness

sections.body:
1. Rerun the same suite with fixed seed and fixed sampling.
2. Increase sample size (within budget) to reduce variance.
3. Look for a stable subset of prompts that consistently regress.
4. If none exists and infra is healthy, file a prompt-set flakiness issue and consider quarantine.

Quarantine criteria (guideline; confirm against current policy):
- Suite repeatedly fails reproducibility checks AND causes alert storms.
- Suite exhibits high variance without stable failing prompts.
sections.heading: Procedure

sections.body:
- Mark suite as quarantined with a reason code.
- Ensure gates fall back to remaining required coverage.
- Create follow-up task to repair suite (owner + SLA).

---
sections.heading: Actions if quarantined

sections.body: When escalating, include a compact packet so Runtime/SRE can act quickly.
sections.heading: Standard “regression packet” (attach to ticket)

sections.body:
- Summary: <one paragraph>
- Impact: gate blocked apply / canary degraded / customer report
- Change type: batching/caching/quant
- Model + version: <>
- GPU SKU + region: <>
- Baseline config ref: <>
- Candidate config ref: <>
- Gate run ID(s): <>
- Prompt set(s): <>
- Minimal repro prompts: <link or inline list>
- Output comparison: <link to diffs>
- Evidence of determinism: stable across reruns? yes/no
- Logs/traces: <links>
- Initial hypothesis: <1–2 bullets>

---
sections.heading: Template

sections.body: Overrides are allowed only under the exception policy. This section is guidance for triage; always follow the policy for approval and audit requirements.
sections.heading: Guidance for “fix vs override” decisions

sections.body:
- Regression reproduces consistently on a small prompt set.
- Regression affects core task success, safety, or structured output correctness.
- Root cause likely correctness (cache collision, quant kernel bug).
sections.heading: Recommend “fix / block apply” when

sections.body:
- Evidence strongly supports false positive (flaky suite) OR regression is isolated to a non-critical edge case with documented customer acceptance.
- A rollback/fallback plan exists and is tested.
- The override includes an explicit expiration and a follow-up issue.

---
sections.heading: Consider a time-bound override only when

sections.body:
- For gate failures affecting multiple teams, open a single tracking ticket and tag:
  - Evals (Applied ML)
  - Runtime owner for the change type
  - SRE if there are pipeline/timeout issues
- Post a short update in the relevant channel with:
  - Gate run ID
  - Model + config diff summary
  - Current status (repro achieved? suspected cause?)
  - Next action + owner

---
sections.heading: Communication and handoffs

sections.body:
- **Only fails in EU-West**: likely capacity/timeouts or region-specific GPU mix; involve SRE.
- **Only fails on long-context prompts**: KV cache boundaries or quant kernel path; involve Runtime/Quant.
- **Scores drop but outputs look “fine”**: scoring/rubric mismatch; verify metric bundle version and rubric calibration.
- **Refusal rate spikes**: small logit perturbations from quant; verify safety evaluation subset and compare early-token divergence.

---
sections.heading: Appendix: Common symptoms and what they usually mean

sections.body:
- 2026-02-22: Added explicit artifact checklist for GPU SKU + runtime build; clarified flakiness vs real regression criteria; added regression packet template.
- 2026-02-05: Initial published version aligned to gating MVP (smoke + full gates) and first limited production rollout.

payload.page_title: Live Regression Experiment Runner: spec-and-runbook-2026

sections.body: This document specifies the design, configuration, and operational runbook for the Live Regression Experiment Runner (LRER). LRER is an executable orchestration layer that runs short-lived, hypothesis-driven regression experiments against live or shadow traffic to validate regressions, quantify impact, and produce triage artifacts for debugging. It connects the eval harness, prompt/benchmark catalog, and model-onboarding outputs to produce deterministic, auditable experiment runs.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Goals:
  - Run reproducible, short-duration experiments (minutes to hours) against representative traffic slices to confirm suspected regressions.
  - Produce structured artifacts suitable for automated bisect, blame, and trigger remediation playbooks.
  - Integrate with quantization and kv-cache variants to surface compatibility failures.
- Non-goals:
  - LRER is not a replacement for full-scale shadow promotion; it is a fast validation tool for targeted triage.
sections.heading: Goals and non-goals

sections.body:
1. Telemetry spike or quality alert where the regression index indicates an emergent delta.
2. After a model or quantization rollout when automated sentinels report fidelity degradations for a slice.
3. For candidate patch validation (prompt rewrite, quant profile tweak) before promoting a canary.
sections.heading: When to use LRER

sections.body:
- Controller service (lrer-controller): accepts experiment manifests and schedules runner tasks. Owned by Applied ML platform team.
- Worker pool (lrer-worker): executes experiments against configured targets (shadow, private bucket of synthetic probes, live-sampled traffic).
- Artifact store: S3-style bucket with standardized result schema and provenance metadata.
- Alerting hooks: posts to regression-queue and creates a triage incident if run confirms an actionable regression.
- Integrations: eval-harness (probe execution), prompt registry (probe templates), quant-profiles service (variant matrix), telemetry (metrics/trace ingestion).

Experiment manifest: required fields (YAML example)
---
experiment_id: "rgr-20260915-42"
owner: "service-team-name"
trigger_reason: "embedding-stability-drop:cohort:billing_api"
start_time: "2026-09-15T16:00:00Z"
duration: "00:30:00"
mode: "shadow"   # shadow | live-sampled | synthetic
traffic_source:
  type: "sampled"
  fraction: 0.01
probes: ["billing-edgecase-primers:v1", "fewshot-invoice-parse:v2"]
variants:
  - name: "baseline"
    model_ref: "service-a:v2026-09-01"
  - name: "candidate-quant"
    model_ref: "service-a:quant-v2"
  - name: "kv-cache-off"
    model_ref: "service-a:v2026-09-01"
    runtime_flags: ["disable-kv-cache"]
metrics: ["response-stability-index", "answer-coherence", "token-likelihood-delta"]
acceptance_criteria:
  response-stability-index.delta: -0.03   # candidate must not drop by more than 3%
  latency.p50.delta_ms: 100
  failure_rate.absolute: 0.005
tags: ["suspected-regression","billing"]
---
sections.heading: High-level architecture

sections.body:
- Runner will clone probes listed to a local ephemeral execution context.
- For shadow mode, requests are forked to baseline and candidate variants; only baseline responses are returned to the caller.
- For live-sampled mode, the runner will forward a configurable fraction of traffic to candidate paths. A kill-switch is wired to the controller (instant stop on safety thresholds).
- Synthetic mode executes stored probe sets against variants with deterministic RNG seeds.
sections.heading: Execution semantics

sections.body:
- experiment_id (string)
- timestamp (string)
- variant (string)
- probe_id (string)
- request_hash (string)
- response_tokens (integer)
- rsi_score (float)  # response-stability-index
- coherence_score (float)
- latency_ms (integer)
- traces (list)  # list of trace ids (as strings)
- warnings (list)
- failure_class (string)  # e.g., quant-exception, tokenize-failure, runtime OOM
- provenance (string)  # git hash / runtime binary id
sections.heading: Result artifact schema (flattened JSON fields)

sections.body:
- If any variant has response-stability-index drop > 4% vs baseline for >= 5 probes in the run => create regression incident and escalate to owner.
- If latency.p95 increases > 300 ms => auto-stop and annotate with latency-failure.
- If failure_rate > 1% absolute => auto-stop and mark as critical.

Operational runbook: step-by-step
1) Triage lead kicks off LRER run via UI or CLI: lrer run --manifest s3://manifests/rgr-2026.yaml
2) Controller schedules workers in the nearest region to the service to reduce network variance.
3) Worker executes probes and pushes partial artifacts to Artifact store every 2 minutes.
4) Controller computes provisional metrics in-stream and checks thresholds.
5) If thresholds crossed, controller will: a) stop experiment; b) post to #regression-queue w/ link to artifact; c) create triage ticket with prefilled hypothesis template.
6) If run completes without crossing thresholds, controller stores final artifact and posts a run summary.
sections.heading: Telemetry and alerting thresholds (default)

sections.body:
- observed_delta: "response-stability-index -0.05 for cohort:billing_api"
- candidate_variant: "candidate-quant"
- suspect_change_list: ["quant-profile-update v2", "kernel-update 2026-09-03"]
- top-failing-probes: ["billing-edgecase-primers:v1"]
- suggested-next-step: ["run per-probe bisect", "run probe with kv-cache-on/off"]
sections.heading: Hypothesis template (filled automatically)

sections.body:
- LRER produces artifacts compatible with the automated-bisect assistant (see related pages). After a failing LRER run, the bisect assistant can spawn a binary-search across model-revision ranges and quant profiles.
- Chained experiments: manifests can reference previous run artifacts to seed new probe selections. Example use-case: isolate whether a degradation is due to tokenization, quant, or prompt change.
sections.heading: Bisect and experiment chaining

sections.body:
- All live-sampled runs require owner-team approval and a maximum sampling fraction of 5% by default.
- Any run that may return customer-identifiable data to the candidate path must run in shadow or synthetic mode; privacy review required for live-sampled.
- Rate limiting: LRER respects service route quotas and will never exceed a safe-percentage of route capacity (default 2% of RPS).
sections.heading: Quality guardrails & safety controls

sections.body:
- LRER consults the quant-profile registry to build the variant matrix. If a candidate quant profile is not present, the run will fail-fast.
- Probes must reference canonical prompt-set ids from the prompt registry. Probes that exercise long-context behavior should declare context_length and warmup_steps.
sections.heading: Integration notes for quantization profiles and prompts

sections.body:
- Service owner: the team that owns the upstream API (required field in manifest). Responsible for triage actions.
- LRER platform oncall: Applied ML platform SRE rotates 24/7 and is responsible for runner health and emergency kill-switch.
- Escalation path: Service owner -> Applied ML lead -> Platform SRE -> Eng SRE.
sections.heading: Operational ownership and escalation

sections.body:
- Per-run report (auto-generated): run-summary.md, artifacts.json.gz, top10-failing-probes.csv, trace-links.txt.
- If an incident is created, an immediate "micro-postmortem" (1-page) is required within 24 hours by the service owner.
- If LRER identifies quant-induced failures, require a quant safety checklist sign-off before re-rollout: includes cross-tenant privacy scan, numeric-stability test, and memory/regression smoke.
sections.heading: Post-run artifacts and required follow-ups

sections.body:
- run_success_rate (target >= 98%)
- avg_run_latency (median time to complete a 30-minute run)
- artifact_upload_error_rate (target < 0.5%)
- time_to_incident_create (target < 3 minutes on threshold breach)
sections.heading: Operational metrics to monitor for LRER service health

sections.body:
- Worker OOM during quant tests: 1) check worker logs for CUDA OOM; 2) reduce batch_size or switch to lower-precision quant profile; 3) re-run synthetic mode.
- High variance in latency_p95 across baseline vs candidate: 1) confirm same region execution; 2) run synthetic-mode with empty network to isolate runtime overhead; 3) capture perf traces.
- Missing probes: ensure prompt registry permissions and that the probe version exists.
sections.heading: Troubleshooting cheatsheet

sections.body:
- LRER manifests and controller code are owned by Applied ML platform (team: applied-ml-platform).
- Any change to default safety thresholds requires a cross-team review from Security and Eng SRE.
- Annual audit of artifact retention and privacy compliance is performed by Security.
sections.heading: Change history and governance

sections.body:
- Start a run: lrer run --manifest s3://manifests/rgr-20260915-42.yaml --dry-run=false
- Abort: lrer abort --experiment-id rgr-20260915-42 --reason "latency spike"
sections.heading: A) CLI examples

sections.body:
---
experiment_id: "quick-debug-0001"
owner: "platform-team"
mode: "synthetic"
probes: ["edgecase-minimal:v1"]
variants:
  - name: "baseline"
    model_ref: "service-a:canary"
  - name: "candidate"
    model_ref: "service-a:canary-quant"
duration: "00:05:00"
---
sections.heading: B) Minimal manifest for quick debug

sections.body:
- Applied ML lead: Priya Nair (priya@redwoodai.com)
- Platform SRE primary: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwoodai.com)
- LRER owner Slack: #lrer-platform
sections.heading: C) Contacts

This spec is intended to be a living document. Create a doc update whenever thresholds, sampling policies, or integrations change.
