payload.page_title: Latency SLO alignment for perf baselines (Q1 2026)

sections.body: This page defines how **Q1 2026 performance baseline metrics** (bench harness / perf-canary) map to **production latency SLO dashboards and alerting**.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
1) Treating benchmark deltas as production incidents (false pages).
2) Ignoring benchmark deltas that predict real user-facing SLO risk.

This is an alignment doc (definitions + mapping + operational policy). It does **not** replace:
- The baseline methodology (see Q1 2026 perf baseline plan).
- The company-wide perf regression policy/thresholds.
sections.heading: The goal is to prevent two common failure modes

sections.body:
Perf-suite runs are controlled, reproducible, and carry a run manifest (ADR-0172). Key metrics:
- **TTFT (Time To First Token)**: server-side time from request accepted by Redwood API gateway (benchmark client uses direct internal endpoint) to first token being available to stream.
- **First-token-on-wire (FTOW)**: time to first byte written to the server’s streaming transport (when available). Used to catch streamer/backpressure issues.
- **TPOT (Time Per Output Token)**: mean time per generated token during decode, excluding prefill. Reported as ms/token.
- **Throughput**: tokens/sec (decode and/or total), and requests/sec for embeddings.
- Percentiles: **p50/p95/p99**, with explicit sample size and warmup procedure.
sections.heading: Baseline / perf-suite metrics (engineering benchmark semantics)

sections.body:
- Region: at minimum **us-east** and **eu-west**.
- Hardware SKU: H100 / A100 / L40S (as applicable).
- Deployment mode: hosted, dedicated (where supported by harness env).
- Workload shape: chat streaming, long-context prefill, tool/function calling (bursty), embeddings high-QPS.
- Cache mode: **cold** (no prefix/KV reuse) vs **warm** (explicit cache reuse scenario).
sections.heading: Perf-suite cohorts are defined by

sections.body:
Production SLOs are end-to-end and include shared infrastructure and client-facing behaviors.

Canonical views (names may vary by Grafana folder; see “Dashboard mapping” below):
- **Request latency** (non-streaming): time from request received at edge/API gateway to full response completed.
- **Streaming start latency**: time from request received to first chunk delivered to client (proxy-inclusive).
- **Streaming steady-state**: effective token cadence / time between chunks (proxy-inclusive); typically tracked via server-side token timestamps and streaming flush events.
- **Saturation & queueing**: scheduler queue wait, batch assembly time, GPU saturation signals.
sections.heading: Production SLO metrics (user-impact semantics)

sections.body:
- Region, customer tier (hosted vs dedicated), and route type (chat/generate/embeddings).
- In some dashboards: model family or model id for top N models.
sections.heading: SLOs are segmented by

sections.body:
- **Perf baseline regressions** should primarily gate runtime releases (CI/perf-canary) and trigger engineering triage.
- **SLO alerting** should page/on-call based on **production impact**, not on benchmark-only signals.
sections.heading: Key principle: Baselines inform releases; SLOs page on user impact

sections.body: - A large, consistent regression in the representative suite is a **leading indicator**. It should trigger targeted production checks (see playbook below), but should not automatically page SRE unless production SLOs also degrade.
sections.heading: However

sections.body:
The table below defines which production SLO views correspond to each perf-suite cohort, and what “alignment” means.

Alignment does NOT imply exact numeric equality. Benchmarks are run in controlled environments and typically exclude:
- Client overheads
- Edge routing variability
- Multi-tenant contention beyond the harness scenario

Instead, alignment means:
- The same latency components are being measured (TTFT maps to streaming-start, TPOT maps to steady-state decode cadence), and
- The same traffic shape segment is represented (short prefill vs long prefill, bursty vs steady).
sections.heading: Dashboard mapping (SLO views ⇄ baseline cohorts)

sections.body:
| Perf-suite cohort (representative suite) | Baseline metrics (primary) | Production SLO dashboard view (primary) | Production filter / cohort definition | Notes / gotchas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat streaming (short prompt, variable decode) | TTFT p95/p99, TPOT p95/p99, FTOW p95 | API Streaming SLO: Chat – “Time to first chunk” + “Token cadence” | route=chat/completions (streaming=true), prompt_tokens in small/medium bins | TTFT vs FTOW can diverge when proxy buffering changes; prefer FTOW if available for streamer regressions. |
| Long-context summarization (large prefill, modest decode) | TTFT p95/p99 (prefill-dominated), queue_wait p95, batch_assembly p95 | API Latency SLO: Generate – “p99 latency by prompt length” + Scheduler Queueing panel | route=responses/generate, prompt_tokens in high bin (e.g., >8k / >16k) | Production often shows stronger tail effects from cache misses and noisy neighbors; benchmark cold/warm must be compared separately. |
| Tool / function calling (bursty multi-turn) | TTFT p99 under concurrency ramps, overload/drop counters | API Reliability + Latency: Chat – “burst cohorts” + Overload / Load-shed counters | route=chat/completions, tool_calls present OR multi-turn session id present; concurrency spikes | In production this is correlated with customer app behavior; use burst-cohort dashboard not global p99. |
| Embeddings (high-QPS small payload) | req/s, p95 latency, saturation indicators | Embeddings SLO: “p95 latency” + “throughput (req/s)” | route=embeddings, small payload bins | Throughput-first; latency can stay flat until saturation, then cliff. Watch utilization + queueing. |
sections.heading: Table: Workload cohort mapping

sections.body:
| Perf-suite cache mode | What it represents | Production proxy | How to compare |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold | No prefix/KV reuse; worst-case per-request compute | Cache miss / low-reuse workloads; new sessions | Compare to production cohorts where cache hit rate is low; don’t blend with warm. |
| Warm | Explicit prefix/KV reuse; best-case for repeated prefixes | High-reuse workloads (agent loops, repeated system prompts) | Compare to production when cache hit rate is high. Use as a “ceiling”, not a global expectation. |
sections.heading: Table: Cache mode mapping

sections.body: SLO thresholds are a product/reliability contract. Updating them requires the standard SLO change process (RFC + stakeholder approval).
sections.heading: Baseline changes should NOT automatically change SLO thresholds

sections.body:
- detect regressions,
- validate improvements,
- and support release signoff.
sections.heading: Perf baselines are engineering targets to

sections.body:
- **Do not** “fix” a perf regression by relaxing production SLO alerts.
- **Do** update perf gating thresholds when the baseline anchor changes (e.g., new golden build), per perf regression policy.
sections.heading: Therefore

sections.body:
- It may justify tightening perf gating thresholds (to prevent backsliding).
- It does not require tightening production SLO alerts unless there is an explicit product decision to improve the customer contract.
sections.heading: If perf-suite shows a sustained improvement

sections.body:
If perf-suite shows regression but production SLOs are stable:
- Treat as engineering triage (owner: runtime/perf-bench).
- Investigate whether the regression is in a segment not currently dominant in production.
- Add/adjust production cohort dashboards if the segment is missing.

If perf-suite shows regression and production SLOs also degrade:
- Treat as production incident per on-call policy (page based on SLO breach / error budget burn).
- Use perf-suite artifacts to accelerate attribution (kernel selection, scheduler queueing, etc.).
sections.heading: When baseline regressions occur

sections.body:
1) **Informational / triage channel (no page):**
   - Minor perf regressions within noise model or limited to a single run.
   - Routed to: #eng-perf-triage (or equivalent).

2) **Action required (no immediate page):**
   - Sustained regression beyond threshold (per perf regression policy), but no production impact observed yet.
   - Routed to: #eng-perf-triage + owner mention (runtime on rotation).
   - Expectation: open a Linear issue, link run manifest + traces.

3) **Page-on-call (rare):**
   - Only when coupled with production SLO breach / rapid error budget burn OR when a release gate is violated on a release branch that is actively being rolled.
   - Paging is owned by the production on-call policy, not by perf-canary alone.
sections.heading: Perf-canary alert classes

sections.body:
- Benchmark fleets are more sensitive to environmental variance than production.
- Paging on benchmark-only signals creates alert fatigue and slows incident response.
sections.heading: Why we keep perf-canary from paging by default

sections.body: Use this when a baseline regression is detected (nightly or release gating) and you need to decide whether to engage SRE/on-call.
sections.heading: Operational playbook: “Perf baseline moved — do we expect SLO impact?”

sections.body:
- Verify the run manifest cohort: model, region, SKU, workload, cache mode.
- Confirm the metric boundary (TTFT vs FTOW vs request latency).
sections.heading: Step 1 — Confirm cohort + metric boundary

sections.body:
- GPU clock drift / power management differences
- Co-tenancy on benchmark fleet
- Container placement / NUMA differences
- Warmup procedure drift

If suspected, follow the profiling playbook and re-run with isolation settings.
sections.heading: Common causes of benchmark-only shifts

sections.body:
Use the mapping table above.
- Filter by region and route type.
- If available, filter by model id/family.
- Use prompt-length bins where applicable.
sections.heading: Step 3 — Find the matching production cohort dashboard

sections.body:
If production total latency is flat but baseline TTFT worsened:
- Check production scheduler queue wait and batch assembly; sometimes production routing shifts load away.
- Check cache hit rates; a regression in cold-path may be masked by higher warm reuse.
sections.heading: Step 4 — Compare components, not just totals

sections.body:
- If production SLO/error budget is burning: page per standard process.
- If not: open an engineering issue; tag runtime owners; optionally create an SRE follow-up task if dashboard coverage is missing.
sections.heading: Step 5 — Decide escalation

sections.body: To make the mapping workable, both systems must share stable tags.
sections.heading: Required tagging for alignment (dashboards & baseline runs)

sections.body:
- region
- hardware_sku
- model_id (and model_family)
- workload_id (chat_streaming / long_prefill / tool_bursty / embeddings_high_qps)
- cache_mode (cold/warm)
- runtime_build_id
- scheduler_policy_id
sections.heading: Baseline run tags (minimum)

sections.body:
- region
- route
- deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated) where feasible
- model_id for top N models (best effort)
- prompt_length_bin and output_length_bin for chat/generate
- streaming=true/false

If any of the above tags are missing, file an observability gap issue (owner: Observability / SRE) and annotate the baseline report with the limitation.
sections.heading: Production metric tags (minimum)

sections.body: Because baselines are controlled runs with different overheads and different tail-risk characteristics. SLOs represent customer experience under real routing, retries, and multi-tenant behavior.
sections.heading: Why don’t we set SLO thresholds directly from baseline numbers?

sections.body: Prefer **FTOW** (first token on wire) when available; otherwise use **TTFT** but treat proxy buffering as a potential source of mismatch.
sections.heading: Which baseline metric is the closest to “streaming start latency” in production?

sections.body: Yes, often. Baseline work frequently reveals missing segments (e.g., long-prefill prompt bins) and missing component breakdowns (queue wait vs compute). That’s a dashboard improvement, not an SLO contract change.
sections.heading: Do we ever change SLO dashboards based on baseline work?

sections.body:
- SLO dashboards, alerting policy: **Eng-SRE / Observability** (primary: Aisha Bello; backup: Sean Gallagher)
- Perf suite definitions + baseline cohorts: **Serving Runtime / Perf Benchmarks** (primary: Rina Kobayashi; methodology: Claire Dubois)
- Scheduler instrumentation used for component mapping: **Serving Runtime** (primary: Sofia Ivanova)
sections.heading: Ownership

sections.body:
- 2026-02-05: Added FTOW guidance for streamer regressions; clarified paging rules for perf-canary.
- 2026-01-14: Added cache mode mapping and production proxy guidance.
- 2025-12-18: Initial publication for Q1 2026 baseline alignment.

payload.page_title: Error Budget Policy and Enforcement (Hosted vs Dedicated)

sections.body: This page defines Redwood Inference’s canonical **error budget policy** for tiered SLOs (Hosted and Dedicated) and how we **enforce** it via burn-rate alerting, incident thresholds, mitigation expectations, and release/deploy gates.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Make SLO adherence measurable and comparable across teams and regions.
- Create predictable operational behavior during reliability regressions (latency spikes, 5xx bursts, stream disconnects).
- Align Product SLAs/expectations with engineering measurement and operational controls.
sections.heading: This policy exists to

sections.body:
**In scope (Q1 2026 program phase):**
- Tiers: **Hosted (shared)**, **Dedicated (reserved capacity)**
- Services/paths: API Gateway, Routing/Control Plane policy evaluation, model serving request path, telemetry needed to compute SLIs
- SLIs: success rate (non-5xx), latency percentiles, streaming reliability (disconnect/error events)

**Out of scope (referenced for future work):**
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) enforcement gates (we still recommend adopting the same SLI semantics).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
For a given SLO over a reporting window, the **error budget** is the allowed amount of “bad” events (or time) before an SLO is breached.

- For an **availability / success-rate SLO** (e.g., 99.9%):
  - Error budget fraction = (1 - SLO)
  - Example: SLO 99.9% → error budget = 0.1% of requests may be “bad” in the window.

- For a **latency SLO** (e.g., p95 < threshold):
  - Error budget is the allowed fraction of requests exceeding the threshold percentile SLO (as computed by the approved SLI formula).

- For **streaming reliability**:
  - Error budget is the allowed fraction of streams with server-side disconnect/error classifications (per the streaming SLI spec).
sections.heading: Error budget

sections.body:
- **Primary window:** rolling **28 days** (standard SLO/error budget window)
- **Fast window (operational):** rolling **7 days** for early warning and quicker recovery expectations

Dashboards show both; policy enforcement keys off the 28-day budget unless explicitly stated.
sections.heading: We use two windows for reliability management

sections.body:
SLI semantics (inclusions/exclusions) are defined in: *SLI Specification: API Gateway and Routing*.

At a high level, budgets count:
- Server-side 5xx errors (gateway, routing, serving) for success-rate SLIs
- Latency as measured end-to-end at the defined measurement points
- Streaming disconnect/error events classified as server-initiated or server-fault

Budgets do **not** count (unless explicitly included by the SLI spec):
- Client aborts (e.g., client closes connection)
- Invalid requests (4xx validation errors)
- Rate-limited requests (429) — tracked separately as capacity signals
- Retries/fallback attempts are accounted for as defined in the SLI spec (avoid double counting)
sections.heading: What counts against the budget

sections.body:
Burn rate is how fast we are consuming error budget relative to the allowed rate.

- Burn rate = (observed bad-event rate) / (allowed bad-event rate)
- Burn rate of **1.0** means we are spending budget exactly at the sustainable rate.
- Burn rate of **10** means we are spending budget 10× too fast and will breach quickly.
sections.heading: Burn rate

sections.body:
We operate in three states per **(tier, region, endpoint class)** SLO:

| State | Definition (28-day window unless noted) | Operational expectation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GREEN | Budget remaining >= 50% and no active high burn alerts | Normal operations |
| YELLOW | Budget remaining 10–49% OR sustained moderate burn | Mitigate and de-risk releases |
| RED | Budget remaining < 10% OR active high burn OR SLO breach | Reliability-first; enforce gates and incident rules |
sections.heading: Policy: states and thresholds

sections.body:
- We track state at both **tier-level rollups** and **regional breakdowns**; gating uses the tier-level rollup with safeguards to avoid hiding regional burns.
- Dedicated accounts may have **account-level** SLO views. Enforcement is still tier-based unless an explicit account-specific contract addendum exists (handled via exception process).
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body: We use **multi-window burn-rate alerts** to catch both fast regressions and slow burns (ADR-0143).
sections.heading: Burn-rate alerting (multi-window)

sections.body:
For each SLO, we configure burn-rate alerts at two severities:

**SEV2 (fast burn / imminent breach)**
- Condition: burn rate >= **14×** for **1h** AND >= **6×** for **6h**
- Interpretation: at this rate, a 28-day budget can be exhausted in ~2 days (or faster depending on thresholds).

**SEV3 (slow burn / needs attention)**
- Condition: burn rate >= **3×** for **6h** AND >= **1×** for **3d**
- Interpretation: not an immediate outage, but we will breach without mitigation.
sections.heading: Standard burn-rate alert set

sections.body:
- **SEV2** pages the owning on-call rotation (SRE primary + service owner) and posts to #eng-sre and the service channel.
- **SEV3** posts to Slack and creates an incident candidate; paging is optional based on time-of-day rules and recent history.
sections.heading: Paging and routing

sections.body:
- Alerts group by: tier, region, endpoint class, and “dominant failure mode” (error vs latency vs stream)
- We do not page per model or per customer. Contributing dimensions are available via dashboard drill-down.
sections.heading: To avoid alert storms

sections.body: We do not want every SLO alert to become a full incident, but we also need predictable escalation.
sections.heading: When burn triggers an incident

sections.body:
An incident **must** be opened when any of the following is true:
1) **SEV2 burn-rate alert** fires for a tier rollup (Hosted or Dedicated) and persists for **>15 minutes** after initial triage.
2) Any SLO enters **RED** due to budget remaining < 10% *and* the current burn rate is > 1× (i.e., still degrading).
3) Customer-impact signals indicate sustained impact (CS escalation, status page criteria met) even if burn-rate alert is suppressed (e.g., telemetry gaps).

Incident execution details live in: *Error Budget Breach Incident Process*.
sections.heading: Incident trigger rules

sections.body:
- Incident Commander (IC)
- Comms Lead (if customer-facing impact)
- Scribe
sections.heading: Required roles (minimum)

sections.body: When a tier is **YELLOW or RED**, the default posture is **mitigation-first**.
sections.heading: Mitigation expectations (what “good” looks like)

sections.body:
1) Confirm SLI validity (data quality, tagging, sampling) and identify dominant failure mode.
2) Determine blast radius (tier, region(s), endpoint class, top contributing routes/models).
3) Apply first-line mitigations (see below) and decide whether to roll back recent changes.
4) Decide on customer comms threshold and engage CS as needed.
sections.heading: The on-call team should

sections.body:
- **Rollback / disable recent rollout** (preferred when a clear change correlates with burn)
- **Traffic shaping / overload shedding**
  - protect Dedicated capacity first when Dedicated SLOs are at risk
  - enforce per-tenant limits and drop/queue best-effort Hosted traffic where appropriate
- **Routing policy adjustments**
  - shift traffic to healthier region(s) when policy allows
  - adjust fallback to compatible model variants (ensure SLI accounting remains correct)
- **Capacity actions** (in partnership with Infra)
  - add headroom to affected pools
  - shift capacity from non-critical workloads
- **Degrade non-critical features**
  - disable expensive inference options, lower max tokens, reduce parallel tool calls
  - note: any change must be evaluated for correctness and communicated if it changes product behavior

For step-by-step actions, use: *Error Budget Breach Mitigation Runbook* and *Capacity Mitigation Guidelines for SLO Events*.
sections.heading: Depending on failure mode

sections.body: If a tier is burning budget, shipping more changes increases risk. Our policy is to **slow down change** when reliability is degraded while keeping an explicit path for emergency fixes.
sections.heading: Philosophy

sections.body:
1) **Warn-only**: CI/CD posts warnings and requires an acknowledgement for high-risk deploys.
2) **Soft gate**: blocks “non-critical” deploys unless a mitigation checkbox + on-call approval is attached.
3) **Hard gate**: blocks all non-emergency deploys when a tier is in RED or budget exhausted.

As of **2026-02-21**, default posture:
- Hosted: Soft gate in YELLOW; Hard gate in RED
- Dedicated: Hard gate in RED; Soft gate in YELLOW for control plane/routing/serving changes

(Exact implementation follows the deploy-gate design and the release gate owner’s config.)
sections.heading: We support three phases

sections.body:
- New feature rollouts affecting request path (gateway, routing, serving)
- Kernel/runtime upgrades, model version changes, quantization profile changes
- Policy changes that increase load (batching config, concurrency limits)
sections.heading: Unless approved as emergency

sections.body:
- Rollbacks and mitigations
- Observability fixes required to restore SLI correctness

sections.heading: Allowed changes include

sections.body:
1) Create an emergency deploy entry (ticket/template in the release system) including:
   - impacted tier(s)/region(s)

2) Get approval from:
   - On-call IC (if incident open) OR SRE primary
   - Owning EM (or delegate) for the service
3) Execute deploy with enhanced monitoring; annotate dashboards.
4) Document outcome in the incident timeline.

All emergency overrides are logged and reviewed weekly by SRE leadership.
sections.heading: To perform an emergency deploy during a hard gate

sections.body: Escalation is based on tier and burn severity.
sections.heading: Escalation ladder

sections.body:
- Primary: Service owner on-call + SRE primary
- Engage within 30 minutes:
  - Routing owner (Mina Haddad) if routing/fallback involved
  - Control plane owner (Ethan Park) if policy eval or config pushes involved
  - Telemetry owner (Logan Wright) if data quality/SLI validity concerns

- Escalate to SRE Director (Sean Gallagher) if:

sections.body:

- Follow tiered comms guidance; avoid mixing Hosted and Dedicated messaging unless necessary

sections.body: Exceptions are sometimes necessary (e.g., regulatory deadlines, urgent customer commitments, or infrastructure migrations). Exceptions must be explicit and time-bound.

sections.body:

- VP Infra & Reliability (Neha Kapoor) for high-risk exceptions (Dedicated RED, or repeated exceptions)

sections.body:
If an SLO is breached (budget exhausted) OR if SEV2 burn occurs, the owning teams must:
- Produce a post-incident write-up (or attach to existing incident) within **5 business days**
- Include:

payload.page_title: Rollout SLOs and Alert Thresholds for Model Version Changes

sections.body:
h1. Purpose
This page defines the minimum SLOs and alert thresholds that MUST be used (or made stricter) in any production rollout plan for a model version change.

h1. Scope
Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (unless customer-specific SLOs are stricter).

h1. Required monitoring windows
* Canary decision window: 30 minutes minimum
* Ramp step window: 30 minutes minimum (or 2x the p95 request duration, whichever is larger)
* Full rollout validation window: 24 hours after reaching 100%

h1. Required metrics and thresholds
Rollout plans MUST include a table of pass/fail thresholds for the metrics below, at minimum.

h2. Reliability
* 5xx rate (gateway + router combined)
  * Pass: <= baseline + 0.05% absolute over 30 min
  * Fail: > baseline + 0.20% absolute over 15 min
* Timeout rate
  * Pass: <= baseline + 0.03% absolute over 30 min
  * Fail: > baseline + 0.10% absolute over 15 min
* Admission rejects (saturation/backpressure)
  * Pass: <= 0.5% over 30 min
  * Fail: > 2.0% over 10 min

h2. Latency
* p95 end-to-end latency (non-streaming)
  * Pass: <= +5% vs baseline over 30 min
  * Fail: > +10% vs baseline over 15 min
* Time-to-first-token (streaming)
  * Pass: <= +10% vs baseline over 30 min
  * Fail: > +25% vs baseline over 15 min
* Long-tail latency
  * Fail condition: p99 > 2.5x baseline for 10 min

h2. Capacity/efficiency
* GPU utilization saturation
  * Fail condition: sustained > 92% for 15 min with rising queue time
* Tokens/sec/GPU
  * Pass: >= baseline - 3% over 60 min
  * Fail: < baseline - 8% over 30 min
* Cache hit rate (prefix/KV)
  * Pass: within -5% absolute of baseline over 60 min
  * Fail: within -15% absolute of baseline over 30 min

h2. Quality guardrails (required even if fallback hides errors)
* Internal eval regression delta
  * Pass: >= baseline - 0.3 (normalized score)
  * Fail: < baseline - 0.7
* Customer-reported quality issues
  * Fail condition: 2+ independent customer reports with reproducible prompts within 24 hours

h1. Required alert bundle
During any ramp above 0%, enable the rollout_slo_guard alert bundle scoped to:
* model alias
* version id
* region

The bundle MUST page SRE oncall for any fail threshold and MUST notify #eng-platform and #eng-runtime for elevated error/timeout alerts.

h1. Rollback guidance
A rollout plan MUST map each fail threshold to an explicit action:
* Automatic fallback (router) OR
* Manual rollback (restore prior policy) OR
* Pause and investigate (only allowed for non-customer-impacting signals)

h1. Notes for Dedicated and Private
* Dedicated: use customer-specific SLOs if stricter; include per-customer dashboards.
* Private: if customer has pinned versions, ensure rollback procedures are documented and customer-approved.
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Cache Efficiency Guardrail SLO Proposal (Prefix + KV Cache)

sections.body:
This page proposes **internal cache-efficiency guardrail SLOs** for Redwood’s prefix cache and KV cache telemetry. These are **not customer-facing SLAs**. The intent is to:

- Detect regressions that materially increase cost/latency (e.g., prefix cache disabled, version mismatch causing systematic misses, eviction pressure spikes).
- Provide consistent triage signals for SRE + Runtime + Telemetry.
- Avoid paging on **expected workload shifts** (prompt mix changes, model/route traffic migrations, new customer onboarding).

Guardrail SLOs are evaluated per environment (prod, canary), deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and region with strict cardinality controls.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
We are rolling out new cache telemetry (hit/miss counters, miss-reason taxonomy, eviction/pressure indicators, and wasted prefill). This telemetry enables us to:

- Separate “cache got worse” from “workload changed.”
- Attribute drops to actionable reasons (capacity pressure, TTL expired, policy disabled, hash mismatch, version mismatch).
- Set conservative, low-noise alerts tied to burn-rate style evaluation.
sections.heading: Background / Why now

sections.body:
- This does not define any contractual or customer-reported SLA.
- This does not require new eviction algorithms or cache policy rewrites.
- This does not attempt to enforce a single hit-rate target across all workloads; targets are **guardrails + anomaly detection**.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
**Prefix cache:** Cache of canonicalized prompt prefixes used to accelerate prefill for repeated/overlapping prompts.

**KV cache reuse:** Reuse of attention KV states across turns/requests where compatible (implementation-dependent; see ADR).

**Wasted prefill:** Prefill tokens computed that do not contribute to subsequent decode speedups due to cache miss/eviction/disabled policy. Wasted prefill is a leading indicator of cost regressions even when latency impact is masked by batching.

**Guardrail SLO:** Internal target with operational response policies (page/ticket/observe), intended to prevent silent unit-cost regressions.
sections.heading: Terms and definitions

sections.body:
- Interpretable and joinable with route/model context.
- Low-cardinality (bucketed by request shape; allowlisted route/model identifiers).
- Robust to sampling (ratio metrics + volume gates).
sections.heading: The SLIs below are chosen to be

sections.body:
**Definition:**
- Numerator: prefix cache *reused tokens* (or reused prefix span) attributed to requests.
- Denominator: eligible prefill tokens (tokens that could have been accelerated by prefix cache given policy + canonicalization).

**Why token-weighted:** It aligns with cost impact (prefill dominates GPU time for long prompts).

**Primary breakdowns (guardrailed):**
- model_family, model_version (allowlisted), region, deployment_mode
- route_group (hashed/allowlisted), prompt_length_bucket
sections.heading: SLI 1: Prefix Cache Hit Rate (token-weighted)

sections.body:
**Definition:**
- Numerator: KV cache reused tokens/steps (as defined in ADR; excludes retries double-counted)
- Denominator: eligible decode tokens/steps

**Notes:** KV reuse is workload-specific; thresholds should be conservative and primarily used for **regression detection** and **miss-reason diagnosis**, not absolute performance scoring.
sections.heading: SLI 2: KV Cache Reuse Effectiveness

sections.body:
**Definition:**
- Numerator: wasted_prefill_tokens
- Denominator: total_prefill_tokens

**Interpretation:** Wasted prefill rising indicates we are doing expensive prefill work without reuse benefits (common causes: eviction pressure, policy disabled, canonicalization/hash mismatch, version mismatch).
sections.heading: SLI 3: Wasted Prefill Ratio

sections.body:
These are supporting signals used to classify incidents and tune recommendations:
- eviction_events_rate (by eviction_reason)
- prefix_cache_bytes_used / max_prefix_cache_bytes (utilization)
- kv_cache_pressure_gauge (normalized)

We do not set a single global SLO on these gauges; instead they are used as alert qualifiers and to suggest remediation (increase cache size, adjust TTL, routing locality, etc.).
sections.heading: SLI 4: Eviction / Pressure Indicators (supporting, not SLO’d)

sections.body: These initial targets are intentionally conservative and should be revisited after 2–4 weeks of production baselining.
sections.heading: Proposed guardrail targets (initial)

sections.body:
These evaluate at the service level per region + deployment mode, with traffic volume gates.

1) **Prefix Hit Rate (token-weighted)**
- Guardrail: Do not regress by more than **20% relative** from trailing 7-day baseline for the same region + deployment_mode + model_family.
- Absolute floor (only if eligibility is high): if eligible_prefill_tokens_per_5m is high and hit rate < **0.10**, treat as a likely regression.

2) **Wasted Prefill Ratio**
- Guardrail: Do not increase by more than **+8 percentage points** from trailing 7-day baseline (same breakdown as above).
- Absolute ceiling: if wasted prefill ratio > **0.35** for 30m with sustained volume, open an incident ticket (page only if paired with cost/latency impact).

3) **KV Reuse Effectiveness**
- Guardrail: Do not regress by more than **25% relative** from trailing 7-day baseline (KV behavior is more variable; regressions should be validated against prompt mix).
sections.heading: Global (prod) guardrails

sections.body:
For canary, we want sensitivity with low blast radius:
- Trigger if prefix hit rate regresses **>15% relative** vs control (same workload) for 15m with adequate volume.
- Trigger if wasted prefill increases **>5 percentage points** vs control for 15m.
sections.heading: Canary guardrails (release safety)

sections.body:
- p95 latency regression beyond perf-canary thresholds OR
- cost-per-1k-tokens proxy regression (when available) OR
- miss reasons indicate systemic failure (policy_disabled, version_mismatch, hash_mismatch dominating).
sections.heading: Canary failures should block rollout when coupled with

sections.body: We treat the guardrails as “error budgeted” to avoid alert fatigue.
sections.heading: Error budget policy (internal)

sections.body:
- Primary window: **28 days**
- Secondary windows: 7 days, 1 day (for fast detection)
sections.heading: Error budget windows

sections.body:
- Volume gate is met (see below)
- Telemetry quality is healthy (no pipeline drop indicators)
- Guardrail threshold is violated (relative to baseline or vs control)
sections.heading: A minute consumes budget when all of the following are true

sections.body:
- >80% remaining: no action (observe)
- 50–80% remaining: file investigation ticket to Runtime/Platform (non-urgent)
- 20–50% remaining: escalate to oncall lead for prioritization in sprint
- <20% remaining: declare reliability initiative and schedule remediation (may include config changes, routing policy adjustments, cache sizing)

Note: We do not want the “budget” to imply customer SLO compliance; it is used to prioritize engineering work.
sections.heading: Budget actions

sections.body: 1) **Page (P1/P2) only for likely systemic regressions**
sections.heading: Alert classes

sections.body:
- Sustained violation (multi-window) AND
- High confidence signal (volume gate + telemetry healthy) AND
- Strong indicator of platform regression (miss_reason spike in policy_disabled/version_mismatch, or near-zero hit rate with high eligibility)

2) **Ticket (P3) for slow burns / optimization opportunities**
- Relative regressions without clear systemic cause
- Wasted prefill increase without latency impact
- Elevated eviction pressure correlated with specific model/region

3) **Noisy/anomalous (auto-silence)**
- Low volume
- Known maintenance windows
- Known workload migration events (route moved, model rollout in progress) unless canary/control comparison indicates a true regression
sections.heading: Page criteria (must meet all)

sections.body:
These are expressed as intent; implementation may vary between Prometheus/Mimir/etc.

A) Prefix hit-rate “near-zero” (page)
- Condition: hit_rate < 0.02 for 15m
- AND eligible_prefill_tokens > threshold (per region, tuned)
- AND miss_reason not dominated by ttl_expired (to avoid paging on short-TTL workloads)
- Response: page SRE oncall + Runtime oncall; link to dashboard + runbook

B) Wasted prefill spike (ticket)
- Condition: wasted_prefill_ratio increases > +10pp vs 7d baseline for 60m
- AND eligible_prefill_tokens above threshold
- Response: create ticket to Runtime + Platform; attach top miss reasons + top affected routes (allowlisted)

C) Version mismatch misses spike (page in Dedicated/Private; ticket in Hosted)
- Condition: miss_reason=version_mismatch share > 0.20 for 30m
- AND model rollout event detected OR model_version cardinality increases
- Response: Dedicated/Private page (risk of customer-visible cost change); Hosted ticket unless correlated with latency regression

D) Telemetry pipeline health (page to Telemetry)
- Condition: cache metric ingestion drop > X% vs expected for 10m (see pipeline runbook)
- Response: page Telemetry oncall; suppress cache-efficiency pages until data quality restored
sections.heading: Initial alert rules (recommended)

sections.body: To avoid paging on workload shifts, the guardrail system uses:
sections.heading: Volume gates and anti-noise mechanisms

sections.body:
- eligible_prefill_tokens_per_window exceeds a per-region threshold
- AND request_count_per_window exceeds minimum for stable ratios

This prevents small tenants/routes from causing noisy ratio swings.
sections.heading: Alerts only evaluate when

sections.body:
- region
- deployment_mode
- model_family (and optionally model_version when stable)
- prompt_length_bucket

We avoid comparing across different prompt-length mixes by using token-weighted ratios and bucketed baselines.
sections.heading: We compare against trailing baselines on

sections.body:
- policy_disabled / version_mismatch / hash_mismatch: high confidence regression signals
- ttl_expired: often workload/config-driven; default to ticket
- capacity/eviction_pressure: usually infra/config; ticket unless broad and severe
sections.heading: We require miss reasons to classify the event

sections.body:
During planned rollouts (runtime release, model version change, route migration):
- Prefer canary vs control comparisons rather than baseline comparisons.
- Temporarily downgrade some alerts to tickets unless near-zero hit rate is observed.
sections.heading: 4) Change windows / rollout awareness

sections.body:
If ingestion-side cardinality guards or sampling changes cause partial drops, we suppress cache-efficiency pages until:
- required tags are present at expected rates
- counters/histograms pass sanity checks (no unexpected resets)
sections.heading: 5) Telemetry data-quality gating

sections.body:
- Hit-rate trends + baseline overlays
- Wasted prefill trend + correlation with eviction/pressure
- Miss reason breakdowns
- Top affected model_family/region/deployment_mode

**Owning teams:**
- SRE (alert rules, operational response): Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant
- Runtime (instrumentation correctness, cache behavior): Omar El-Sayed / Sofia Ivanova
- Telemetry (ingestion, cardinality guards, sampling): Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
sections.heading: Dashboards (spec in eng-platform) should support

sections.body:
1) Check telemetry pipeline health (avoid chasing missing data).
2) Confirm whether change correlates with rollout/migration (release calendar).
3) Use miss reasons to classify:
   - policy_disabled: validate flags/config; check gateway route settings
   - version_mismatch: validate model rollout + routing compatibility; check join keys
   - hash_mismatch: validate canonicalization version; check prompt hashing deployment
   - capacity/eviction_pressure: validate cache sizing, TTL, and routing locality
4) Mitigate:
   - rollback recent runtime/model changes if canary indicates regression
   - adjust cache size/TTL within safe limits
   - adjust routing locality policy (region affinity) if cross-region mix increased
   - open follow-up to Optimize recommendations pipeline if pattern is customer-actionable

See: eng-platform/runbooks/cache-telemetry-pipeline-incident-runbook
sections.heading: When alerts fire

sections.body:
1) Week 0 (staging + canary):
- Enable guardrail dashboards
- Enable canary vs control alerts (ticket-only)
- Validate volume gates + data-quality gating

2) Week 1 (prod silent):
- Record guardrail metrics; no paging
- Establish 7-day baseline and identify expected diurnal patterns

3) Week 2 (prod ticketing):
- Turn on ticket alerts for wasted prefill + relative regressions
- Iterate thresholds to minimize false positives

4) Week 3 (prod paging, limited):
- Turn on paging only for near-zero hit rate and clear systemic miss-reason spikes
sections.heading: Rollout plan

sections.body:
- What is the best global eligibility definition for prefix cache across streaming chat (ensuring retries are excluded) and for batched prefill?
- Should Dedicated customers have per-customer guardrails (restricted dashboards) or remain aggregated by deployment_mode+region?
- How should we incorporate cost-per-token proxies into paging decisions (requires consistent unit cost estimates)?
sections.heading: Open questions

sections.body:
Approve this as the initial SRE policy for cache-efficiency guardrails, with explicit commitment to:
- Conservative paging (only high-confidence systemic regressions)
- Baseline-based thresholds rather than absolute hit-rate targets
- Two-week production baselining before tightening thresholds
sections.heading: Proposed decision

sections.body:
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (required)
- Runtime: Sofia Ivanova or Omar El-Sayed (required)
- Telemetry: Nadia Rahman (required)
- Product (inform): Paula Mendes
sections.heading: Approvals

payload.page_title: Emergency change guardrails (SLO + error budget)

sections.body: These guardrails define how to make emergency changes safely during active incidents and/or while error budgets are constrained.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body: **Stabilize first, then optimize.** Prefer rollbacks and low-risk mitigations to large behavioral changes.
sections.heading: Core principle

sections.body:
- Request success rate (2xx/5xx) by region for Hosted API
- p95 end-to-end latency by region
- Streaming disconnect rate
- Runtime crash-loop / restart rate
- GPU queue depth
sections.heading: Required monitoring checks (before + after any emergency change)

sections.body:
- **Tier 0 (lowest risk):** rollback to last known good, turning off a feature flag, traffic shift within same model family
- **Tier 1:** runtime config changes that affect batching/caching limits
- **Tier 2:** code changes to scheduler/kernels; changing default kernel selection
- **Tier 3 (highest):** changes that affect request semantics, auth, billing, or cross-region routing
sections.heading: Risk tiers for emergency changes

sections.body:
- Tier 01: approvals per EPC policy (IC/SRE + Runtime/Platform)
- Tier 2: requires explicit Runtime EM approval in addition to IC/SRE approval
- Tier 3: requires VP Engineering (or delegate) approval unless it is a pure rollback
sections.heading: Approval escalation by risk tier

sections.body:
If the Hosted API SLO error budget burn is above 2x normal (week-to-date):
- default to Tier 0 mitigations
- require canary in one cell for at least 10 minutes before expanding
- require explicit rollback readiness confirmation (tag + command)
sections.heading: Error budget constraints

sections.body:
1. Only one change in flight per region at a time (avoid confounding).
2. Every change must have a named owner and a named verifier.
3. Expand rollout only after the verifier states the gate metrics are improving or flat.
sections.heading: Change sequencing rules during active Sev1

sections.body:
- The incident timeline must capture the change time and observed effect
- EPC record must include: risk tier, approvals, and verification evidence
sections.heading: Documentation requirements

payload.page_title: Hosted API SLOs: Enterprise Route Tiers (Hot-route capacity protection)

sections.body: This document defines **per-route SLOs and error budget policy** for Redwood Inference’s **Hosted API** as it relates to **hot-route capacity protection** (tier-aware quotas, priority routing, and controlled shedding).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Explicitly define **enterprise vs best-effort** expectations for the highest-traffic routes.
- Make overload behavior **measurable and supportable** (clear SLIs + dashboards + alerts).
- Align alerting to overload protection so we page on **enterprise degradation**, not expected best-effort shedding.
sections.heading: The intent is to

sections.body:
**In scope**
- Hosted API routes: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v1/completions`.
- Tiered behavior: **Enterprise (Protected)** vs **Best-effort (Standard/Self-serve)**.
- SLOs for **availability**, **latency**, and **overload responses (429)**.
- Alert thresholds and error budget burn policy.

**Out of scope**
- Dedicated and Private SLOs (tracked separately).
- Model-quality or semantic correctness SLIs.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
We classify requests into one of the following tiers at the gateway/policy engine:
- **Enterprise (Protected):** SLA-bearing tenants and allowlisted enterprise accounts for protected routes. These requests receive priority admission and are protected during fleet pressure.
- **Best-effort:** all other traffic. Best-effort may be throttled earlier and more aggressively to preserve fleet health and enterprise budgets.
sections.heading: Route tiers

sections.body:
- Fleet-wide traffic concentration (hot routes)
- High enterprise SLO/SLA coupling
- Known overload blast radius
sections.heading: Protected routes are selected based on

sections.body:
- `/v1/chat/completions` (includes streaming)
- `/v1/embeddings`
- `/v1/rerank`
- `/v1/completions` (legacy; still used by some enterprise SDKs)
sections.heading: Current protected route set

sections.body:
Requests may be rejected with HTTP **429** for:
- **Quota/rate limit enforcement** (tenant policy)
- **Overload shedding/admission control** (fleet protection)

We distinguish causes via standardized reason code headers/payloads (see Support doc for exact fields). For SLO accounting, we treat quota-throttled and overload-shed requests differently by tier (see SLI rules below).
sections.heading: Overload / throttling semantics

sections.body: All SLIs are computed per **route x region x tier** using the standard metrics set.
sections.heading: SLIs (what we measure)

sections.body:
**Definition:** percentage of requests that return an eligible success response.

- Success codes: `2xx` (and `3xx` if any internal redirects apply; typically none)
- Failures: `5xx`, `408`, `499` (client disconnect) are counted as failures unless explicitly excluded by route-specific rules below.

**Tier handling of 429:**
- **Enterprise:** `429` due to *overload shedding/admission control* counts as **unavailable** (because enterprise is protected; overload shed should be rare and indicates under-provisioning or misconfiguration).
- **Best-effort:** `429` due to overload shedding/admission control does **not** count as unavailable (it is expected behavior under pressure). Quota/rate-limit 429s are not counted as availability failures for either tier.

**Note:** 429 classification must be based on the reason code emitted by gateway/policy engine, not inferred from rate.
sections.heading: 1) Availability SLI (server success)

sections.body:
Latency is measured at the gateway edge (request receive to first byte / completion) and reported as:
- **TTFB (time-to-first-byte)** for streaming endpoints.
- **E2E response time** for non-streaming.

We maintain distinct latency SLO targets per tier and route (see tables below).
sections.heading: 2) Latency SLI

sections.body: Not a customer-facing SLO, but required for on-call safety.
sections.heading: 3) Overload activation SLI (operational)

sections.body:
- **shed_rate** (fraction of requests rejected due to overload by tier)
- **admission_control_active** (boolean/ratio time in state)
- **queue_depth / scheduler_lag** for the backing pools

These drive alerts and annotations on the enterprise SLO dashboards.
sections.heading: We track

sections.body:
- SLOs are evaluated over a **rolling 28-day window**.
- Unless specified, targets apply per region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).
- We define both **p95 and p99** latency objectives for enterprise; best-effort uses p95 as primary.
sections.heading: General notes

sections.body:
| Route | Tier | Availability SLO | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | Enterprise (Protected) | 99.95% | 429 overload-shed counts as failure. Quota 429 excluded. |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | Best-effort | 99.5% | 429 overload-shed excluded from availability; still tracked separately. |
| `/v1/embeddings` | Enterprise (Protected) | 99.95% | Batch requests included. |
| `/v1/embeddings` | Best-effort | 99.5% | 429 overload-shed excluded. |
| `/v1/rerank` | Enterprise (Protected) | 99.9% | Lower traffic; still protected. |
| `/v1/rerank` | Best-effort | 99.5% | 429 overload-shed excluded. |
| `/v1/completions` | Enterprise (Protected) | 99.9% | Legacy route; fewer dependencies but included for enterprise compatibility. |
| `/v1/completions` | Best-effort | 99.0% | Best-effort only; deprecation path in progress. |
sections.heading: Availability SLOs by route and tier

sections.body:
- **Chat streaming:** TTFB p95/p99
- **Non-streaming:** E2E p95/p99

| Route | Tier | Latency SLO (primary) | Latency SLO (secondary) | Measurement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming) | Enterprise (Protected) | TTFB p95 ≤ 450ms | TTFB p99 ≤ 900ms | Gateway TTFB |
| `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming) | Best-effort | TTFB p95 ≤ 900ms | (informational) p99 ≤ 1800ms | Gateway TTFB |
| `/v1/chat/completions` (non-streaming) | Enterprise (Protected) | E2E p95 ≤ 1.8s | E2E p99 ≤ 3.5s | Gateway E2E |
| `/v1/embeddings` | Enterprise (Protected) | E2E p95 ≤ 350ms | E2E p99 ≤ 800ms | Gateway E2E |
| `/v1/embeddings` | Best-effort | E2E p95 ≤ 700ms | (informational) p99 ≤ 1.5s | Gateway E2E |
| `/v1/rerank` | Enterprise (Protected) | E2E p95 ≤ 550ms | E2E p99 ≤ 1.2s | Gateway E2E |
| `/v1/rerank` | Best-effort | E2E p95 ≤ 1.2s | (informational) p99 ≤ 2.5s | Gateway E2E |

**Notes / caveats**
- Latency SLOs assume nominal prompt and response sizes. Excessive prompt length or extreme max_tokens increases may be subject to policy limits; those requests are still included in latency metrics unless explicitly rejected by policy.
- Where fallback is permitted (route/model policy), latency SLI measures the actual served path; dashboards must annotate fallback activations.
sections.heading: Latency objectives are defined in terms of

sections.body:
For an SLO target **T** over a 28-day window:
- Error budget = **1 − T**
sections.heading: Error budget calculation

sections.body:
- 99.95% availability ⇒ 0.05% error budget (≈ 21.6 minutes of downtime equivalent over 28 days)
- 99.5% availability ⇒ 0.5% error budget
sections.heading: Examples

sections.body:
- route
- region
- tier
sections.heading: We track budgets separately per

sections.body:
**Enterprise (Protected) routes**
- If burn is elevated, the default stance is **protect SLOs over throughput**.
- Allowed mitigations (in priority order):
  1) Tighten best-effort admission control thresholds (shed earlier)
  2) Temporarily reduce best-effort burst allowances
  3) Increase enterprise reserved capacity / pool weights (if available)
  4) Enable guarded fallback policies where contractually allowed
  5) As last resort: temporary enterprise throttling with exec/on-call approval and proactive comms

**Best-effort routes**
- Best-effort can be shed under pressure; we do not page purely on best-effort 429 shedding.
- If best-effort availability drops due to 5xx (not 429 overload-shed), we investigate as a normal reliability regression.
sections.heading: Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)

sections.body:
For enterprise protected routes, any of the following triggers a “stop the line” review in the weekly reliability sync (or async in #eng-sre if urgent):
- Availability error budget burn ≥ **50%** in 7 days
- p99 latency SLO violated for ≥ **2 hours** in a day (sustained)
- Overload shedding observed for enterprise traffic (non-zero sustained) outside planned game day / load test windows
sections.heading: Budget stop-the-line triggers

sections.body:
- Page on **enterprise** impact (availability/latency) and on conditions that predict imminent enterprise impact.
- Do not page on expected best-effort shedding unless it indicates misconfiguration or runaway protection (e.g., shedding at low utilization).
- Use multi-window burn rate to avoid flapping.
sections.heading: Alert principles

sections.body:
- **Page (Sev2):** 28d SLO burn rate with multi-window thresholds
  - Fast burn: 5m and 1h windows > **14x** budget burn
  - Slow burn: 30m and 6h windows > **6x** budget burn
- **Ticket:** 2h and 1d windows > **2x** burn
sections.heading: For each protected route x region

sections.body:
- **Page (Sev2):** p99 latency SLO violated for **15 minutes** AND admission control active (or queue depth high)
- **Ticket:** p95 latency SLO violated for **60 minutes**
sections.heading: For each protected route x region

sections.body:
These are predictive/guardrail alerts. Configure as:
- **Page (Sev2):** enterprise overload shedding sustained
  - enterprise `shed_rate` > **0.1%** for **10 minutes** (any protected route)
- **Ticket:** best-effort shedding unexpectedly high at low utilization
  - best-effort `shed_rate` > **20%** for **15 minutes** AND GPU utilization < **65%** (indicates policy mis-tuning or signal errors)
- **Ticket:** queue depth / scheduler lag sustained without corresponding shedding
  - queue depth > threshold for **10 minutes** with `admission_control_active=false` (indicates missing trigger wiring)
sections.heading: Overload protection operational alerts

sections.body:
- Primary: **#eng-oncall** and SRE pager rotation
- Secondary: **#eng-platform** for policy/gateway issues, **#eng-runtime** for scheduler lag/queue depth anomalies
sections.heading: Paging routing

sections.body:
- Availability by tier (enterprise vs best-effort)
- Latency p95/p99 by tier (and TTFB for streaming)
- 429 rate split by reason code (quota vs overload)
- shed_rate and admission_control_active
- queue depth and scheduler lag for backing pools
- Annotations for config changes, feature flag toggles, fallback activation

See the dashboard spec for panel/query naming conventions.
sections.heading: Every protected route must have

sections.body:
- **Enterprise 429 overload-shed:** treat as incident-worthy and investigate capacity signals, admission thresholds, route budgets, and pool weights.
- **Best-effort 429 overload-shed:** expected under pressure; use this to validate the protection is working (enterprise should remain stable).
- **Quota 429 (any tier):** not an SLO failure; route to Support/Solutions for policy adjustment if needed.
sections.heading: How to interpret 429s for SLOs

sections.body:
- Feature flag + region canary
- Dashboard annotation
- Rollback plan
- Confirmed alert routing and runbook link in incident-bot message
sections.heading: Changes that affect enterprise SLOs require

sections.body:
- SLO definitions and alert policy: **SRE (Rafael Mendes / Aisha Bello)**
- Metric correctness and tagging: **Telemetry (Logan Wright)**
- Enforcement behavior (429 reason codes, gateway semantics): **API Gateway (Amara Diallo)**
- Priority routing/admission control behavior: **Smart Routing (Mina Haddad)**

payload.page_title: Hosted rollouts: SLO metrics and alerts (cohort-specific)

sections.body: This page defines the SLO signals, cohort-specific metrics, and alerting guidance for **Hosted canary rollouts** (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Detect real customer impact quickly (error/latency/timeouts) **per cohort** (baseline vs canary).
- Provide safe defaults for **auto-stop/auto-rollback** wiring without creating alert storms.
- Standardize dashboard panels and queries used during beta and GA.

This page is SRE-owned, but it is intended for product engineers, on-call responders, and support.
sections.heading: The goal is to

sections.body:
- **Hosted routes** using the canary rollout workflow.
- Cohort tagging emitted by the data plane and aggregated by telemetry.
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Dedicated/Private rollouts (separate SLO policy; signals may be similar but dimensions differ).
- Deep quality-eval gates (optional/manual in GA; future automated gates will be a separate doc).
sections.heading: Does not cover

sections.body:
- **Rollout**: A controlled change for a Hosted route that shifts traffic from a baseline config/model version to a canary config/model version.
- **Cohort**: The request classification for metric attribution:
  - `cohort=baseline`
  - `cohort=canary`
- **Rollout step**: A configured canary percentage (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with a required soak window.
- **Active rollout**: A rollout in `running` (or `paused`) state where traffic is being split and telemetry should include `rollout_id`.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
All metrics used for cohort SLO comparisons MUST be available with these dimensions:
- `route_id` (or stable route name)
- `region`
- `cohort` (baseline|canary)
- `rollout_id` (present only for active rollouts; see below)
sections.heading: Required dimensions for cohort comparisons

sections.body:
- `model_id` / `model_version` (preferred for dashboards, not for paging alerts)
- `status_code_class` (2xx/4xx/5xx) or `error_class`
sections.heading: Optional dimensions (use carefully)

sections.body:
1) `rollout_id` MUST be emitted only when the request is evaluated under an **active rollout**.
2) Alerts MUST NOT page on `rollout_id` dimension by default. Page on `route_id + region` with cohort split as a breakdown.
3) Avoid paging on `tenant_id` or `api_key_id`. Tenant-specific issues should be triaged via logs/traces after the page.
4) Traces: sample at higher rate only for active rollouts (see “Beta tuning”).
sections.heading: To avoid unbounded time-series growth

sections.body: We page on **customer-impacting** signals, and use cohort deltas to determine whether the canary is responsible.
sections.heading: Golden signals (cohort-specific)

sections.body:
1) **Request success / server errors**
   - `http_requests_total` split by `cohort` and `status_code_class`
   - Primary: 5xx rate (server errors)

2) **Timeouts / cancellations**
   - `request_timeouts_total` or `http_requests_total{error_class=timeout}`
   - Also track upstream provider timeouts separately where available

3) **Latency**
   - `request_latency_ms` histogram (p50/p95/p99)
   - For chat/streaming routes, track:
     - Time to first token (TTFT)
     - Token throughput (tokens/sec) where available

4) **Capacity/overload symptoms** (non-paging by default, but used for diagnosis)
   - queue depth, shed/429, GPU saturation, batcher stall metrics
sections.heading: Signals

sections.body:
- **Global route SLOs**: protect customers regardless of rollouts (existing Hosted route SLOs).
- **Rollout cohort SLOs**: protect against canary-specific regressions during rollout steps.
sections.heading: We run two tiers of SLO logic

sections.body:
These are used for **auto-stop/auto-rollback** evaluation and for non-paging warnings.

Target values below are defaults; the orchestrator may apply stricter per-tier policies.

A) Canary error budget guard
- Metric: `canary_5xx_rate` vs `baseline_5xx_rate`
- Stop if either condition is true:
  1) Absolute canary 5xx rate exceeds **0.8%** for **5 minutes**, AND baseline is <= 0.5%
  2) Canary 5xx rate is **>= 2.0x** baseline for **10 minutes** (requires minimum sample size)

B) Canary timeout guard
- Stop if canary timeout rate exceeds **0.3%** for **5 minutes** OR is **>= 2.0x** baseline for **10 minutes**

C) Canary p95 latency regression guard
- Stop if canary p95 latency is **>= baseline p95 + 250ms** for **10 minutes**
- OR relative regression **>= 25%** for **10 minutes**
- Notes:
  - Use **p95** for gating; p99 is too noisy at small canary percentages.
  - Apply minimum sample size requirements (see below).

D) Minimum sample size (anti-flap)
sections.heading: Rollout cohort SLO targets (for stop/rollback gating)

sections.body:
- Require `canary_requests >= 2,000` OR `canary_rps >= 5` sustained during the evaluation window.
- If below minimum, orchestrator should:
  - continue soaking (do not advance)
  - do not auto-rollback based solely on noisy ratios
sections.heading: For any cohort comparison evaluation window

sections.body: Paging should reflect **broad customer impact** or clear production risk. We avoid paging on “expected” canary deltas at low traffic.
sections.heading: Paging alerts (SRE on-call)

sections.body:
- Page on **route-level customer impact** (not per rollout).
- Use cohort breakdown to accelerate diagnosis.
- For beta: prefer **one page + guided runbook** over many hyper-specific pages.
sections.heading: Alert philosophy

sections.body:
These are the default monitors for Hosted rollouts-enabled regions.

1) Hosted route elevated 5xx (page)
- Scope: `route_id + region`
- Condition:
  - 5xx rate >= **1.0%** for **10 minutes** AND total RPS >= **20**
- Annotation: include cohort breakdown (baseline vs canary) in the alert payload.

2) Hosted route elevated timeouts (page)
- Scope: `route_id + region`
- Condition:
  - timeout rate >= **0.5%** for **10 minutes** AND total RPS >= **20**

3) Hosted route latency regression (page)
- Scope: `route_id + region`
- Condition:
  - p95 latency >= **+400ms** above 7d rolling baseline for **15 minutes**
- Notes:
  - This is intentionally route-level, not cohort-level.
  - Cohort charting determines whether canary is culprit.

4) Rollout safety system unhealthy (page)
Pages the owning infra/SRE rotation if the safety mechanisms are failing:
- Orchestrator cannot evaluate stop conditions (metric query failures) for > **10 minutes** for >= **3** active rollouts
- Data plane not emitting cohort tags for > **5 minutes** in a region with active rollouts
sections.heading: Paging alert set (recommended defaults)

sections.body:
These alerts should notify the rollout owner channel (and optionally open an internal ticket) without paging SRE.

1) Canary cohort regression warning (notify)
- Triggered for an active rollout step when any of:
  - canary 5xx rate >= 0.8% for 5m (even if route-level 5xx is below paging)
  - canary p95 latency >= +250ms for 10m
- Routed to:
  - #eng-platform and #eng-sre (beta)
  - plus the owning team’s oncall channel post-GA

2) Cohort sample size insufficient (notify)
- Canary < minimum sample size for > **30 minutes**
- Recommendation: consider increasing canary percentage, extending soak, or scheduling during higher traffic.

3) Split mismatch detection (notify)
- Observed canary share deviates from configured canary percentage by > **20% relative** for > **10 minutes** (e.g., expecting 25% but seeing <20% or >30%)
- This is usually a routing/cohorting bug or region skew; see runbook.
sections.heading: Non-paging alerts (warnings / ticket)

sections.body: The examples below are written in pseudo-PromQL style for clarity. Adjust to the telemetry backend syntax.
sections.heading: Suggested queries (implementation-agnostic)

sections.body:
- canary_5xx_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="canary",status_class="5xx"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="canary"}[5m]))
- baseline_5xx_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="baseline",status_class="5xx"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="baseline"}[5m]))
sections.heading: 5xx rate per cohort

sections.body: - canary_timeout_rate = sum(rate(request_timeouts_total{cohort="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="canary"}[5m]))
sections.heading: Timeout rate per cohort

sections.body:
- canary_p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{cohort="canary"}[10m])) by (le))
- baseline_p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{cohort="baseline"}[10m])) by (le))
sections.heading: p95 latency per cohort

sections.body:
- observed_canary_share = sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort="canary"}[10m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[10m]))
- desired_canary_share = configured value from control plane (emit as metric or query from orchestrator)
sections.heading: Split share observed vs desired

sections.body:
Even though rollout_id is useful for debugging, paging on it creates:
- duplicate pages for multi-route rollouts
- pages for low-traffic rollouts with noisy ratios
- churn when rollouts advance steps
sections.heading: 1) Do not page on rollout_id

sections.body:
- If minimum soak time is 15 minutes, then cohort regression checks should use **>= 10 minutes** windows.
- Avoid 1–2 minute windows for p95/p99; they will flap on moderate traffic.
sections.heading: 2) Use evaluation windows that match soak times

sections.body:
A regression ratio (2x baseline) is meaningless if canary has 50 requests.
- For beta, treat sample-size failures as “extend soak” rather than “stop”.
sections.heading: 3) Enforce sample-size gates

sections.body:
During beta, it is acceptable to add temporary suppressions:
- if a customer runs highly bursty traffic
- if the canary percentage is <5% and traffic is low

Document suppressions in the rollout activity timeline and in #eng-sre.
sections.heading: 4) Suppress known-noisy rollouts

sections.body:
Multi-region traffic makes early cohort comparisons harder.
- Prefer starting a rollout in a single region (if customer routing allows), then expand.
sections.heading: 5) One region at a time (when possible)

sections.body:
- small canary percentages (1%/5%)
- lower traffic (design partners)
- more frequent config changes
sections.heading: During beta we expect

sections.body:
- Default canary gates should bias toward **pause** rather than immediate rollback at tiny sample sizes.
- Increase trace sampling only for active rollouts:
  - baseline: 0.1–0.5%
  - canary: 1–2% (cap absolute spans/sec)
- Keep warning thresholds slightly more sensitive than paging thresholds, but ensure they are gated by minimum sample size.
sections.heading: Recommended beta settings

sections.body:
For each `route_id + region` with an active rollout, dashboards should include:
- Requests/RPS split baseline vs canary (stacked)
- 5xx rate baseline vs canary (overlay)
- Timeout rate baseline vs canary (overlay)
- p50/p95 latency baseline vs canary (overlay)
- TTFT (if streaming) baseline vs canary
- Tokens/sec (if available) baseline vs canary
- Split mismatch panel: observed vs desired canary share
- Orchestrator decisions: last evaluation outcome, last action (advance/pause/rollback)
sections.heading: Dashboard panels (standard)

sections.body:
1) Check route-level impact first (global 5xx/timeout/latency). If route is unhealthy, prioritize restoring service.
2) Split by cohort:
   - If **only canary** is degraded, coordinate with rollout owner to **pause/rollback**.
   - If both cohorts are degraded, treat as route/platform incident (capacity, upstream, region).
3) Validate observed split vs configured split (mismatch can masquerade as canary regression).
4) If orchestrator metric evaluation is failing (timeouts/query errors), disable auto-actions (pause automation) and drive manual rollback if needed.

Reference: confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split
sections.heading: When paged for Hosted route impact during an active rollout

sections.body:
- SRE owner: **Aisha Bello** (signals/alerts), **Sean Gallagher** (paging policy)
- Telemetry owner: **Logan Wright** (tagging/aggregation)
- Routing owner: **Mina Haddad** (cohorting/split enforcement)
- Product policy owner: **Paula Mendes** (guardrail defaults)
sections.heading: Ownership and change management

sections.body:
- SRE + Product sign-off
- a beta validation note (at least 2 design partners or 2 weeks of internal dogfood)
- an update to orchestrator default config and release checklist
sections.heading: Any changes to default thresholds require

sections.body:
- Canary 5xx: >0.8% for 5m (with baseline <=0.5%) OR >=2x baseline for 10m
- Canary timeouts: >0.3% for 5m OR >=2x baseline for 10m
- Canary p95 latency: >= +250ms OR >=25% regression for 10m
- Minimum sample: canary_requests >= 2,000 per window OR canary_rps >= 5 sustained
sections.heading: Cohort guardrails (auto-stop/rollback evaluation)

sections.body:
- Route 5xx >= 1.0% for 10m @ RPS>=20
- Route timeouts >= 0.5% for 10m @ RPS>=20
- Route p95 latency >= +400ms over rolling baseline for 15m
- Safety system unhealthy: cohort tags missing or orchestrator evaluation failing at scale
sections.heading: Paging (route-level)

payload.page_title: Demo Environment SLOs, Error Budgets, and Escalation (Sales Demo Tenant)

sections.body:
This page defines service-level objectives (SLOs) and internal service-level commitments for Redwood’s **Sales Demo Environment** ("demo tenant"). The demo environment must be reliable enough for AE/SE live demos, while staying safe (synthetic data only) and cheap to operate.

**Important:** These targets are for *internal reliability management*. They are not customer-facing SLAs and should not be quoted as contractual commitments.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- **Demo Inference API** (hosted API entrypoint + routing + model pinning/fallback behavior for demo routes)
- **Streaming** behavior (time-to-first-token and disconnect rate)
- **Console Demo Views** (dashboards, rollout view, tracing/error analysis pages used in the talk track)
- **Telemetry ingestion for demo** (synthetic traffic → events → dashboards)
- **Demo reset + healthcheck** (SE-facing reset command and healthcheck report)

Out of scope (tracked, but not SLO-blocking):
- Non-demo tenants
- Non-critical Console pages not used in demo talk track
- Long-term analytics retention for the demo org beyond what’s needed to demonstrate features
sections.heading: In scope (what we measure and page on)

sections.body:
- **Demo environment / demo tenant:** The isolated Redwood org + projects reserved for scripted demos. All traffic and datasets are synthetic.
- **Availability:** Requests succeed without server errors and without quota/capacity rejection beyond defined thresholds.
- **Dashboard freshness:** The time between a synthetic event occurring and it being visible in Console.
- **Demo window:** 08:00–18:00 local time in NA/EU regions on weekdays. We still run monitoring 24/7, but escalation urgency differs.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Any SE can run a live demo end-to-end with **no manual fixes** (no quota edits, no emergency reroutes, no "empty dashboard" moments).
- A demo failure should be **rare** and have an obvious fallback path (backup screenshots/recording).
- When something is broken, the system should fail **predictably** with clear healthcheck output and known remediation.
sections.heading: Reliability goals (what "good" looks like)

sections.body:
- **Demo Inference Gateway** (routing, auth, rate limit decisions): Eng Platform + SRE
- **Demo Model Routes** (pinned versions + safe fallback policy): Routing team (Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon)
- **Console Demo Dashboards + Rollouts UI:** Console team (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin)
- **Telemetry Ingestion + Cost/Latency pipelines:** Telemetry (Logan Wright / Mei Lin)
- **Synthetic Traffic Generator:** Eng Platform (Mei Lin) + SRE for scheduling/alerts
- **Reset + Healthcheck tooling:** Eng Platform (Devon Price) + SE owner (Markus Klein)
sections.heading: Primary components and owners

sections.body: The table below lists the targets used for monitoring, error budget burn, and escalation.
sections.heading: SLOs and internal SLAs

sections.body:
| Metric | SLO target | Measurement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Availability (2xx + expected 4xx) | 99.5% monthly | Per-request, demo routes only | Excludes client-cancelled requests. Expected 4xx includes auth failures for intentionally-invalid-key test only when triggered by the script. |
| p95 latency (end-to-end) | \u2264 1.8s monthly | Gateway receive → first byte response | Normalized on demo routes with pinned models. |
| p99 latency (end-to-end) | \u2264 3.0s monthly | Same as above | Used as a guardrail; not the primary SLO. |
| 5xx rate | \u2264 0.3% monthly | Per-request | Any sustained spike pages SRE. |
| 429 rate | \u2264 1.0% monthly | Per-request | We expect some burst control during synthetic traffic; sustained 429s during demo window are a Sev2. |
sections.heading: 1) Demo Inference API (non-streaming)

sections.body:
| Metric | SLO target | Measurement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Streaming availability | 99.0% monthly | Successful stream completion | A completion counts when the server finishes the stream or a graceful client cancel occurs after receiving \u2265 1 chunk. |
| Time-to-first-token (TTFT) p95 | \u2264 1.2s monthly | Request start → first chunk | Customer-facing demos are sensitive to TTFT. |
| Stream disconnect rate | \u2264 0.5% monthly | Unexpected disconnects | Measured for demo routes only; excludes intentional network test steps. |
sections.heading: 2) Demo Streaming API

sections.body:
| Metric | SLO target | Measurement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Console demo view availability | 99.5% monthly | Successful page load (HTTP + API deps) | Scoped to demo-critical views: Usage (cost/latency), Errors, Traces, Rollouts. |
| Dashboard freshness (p95) | \u2264 10 minutes | Event time → visible in graphs | The primary goal is to avoid empty graphs during a live walkthrough. |
| "Empty dashboard" incidents | 0 during demo window (goal) | SE-reported + automated checks | Any occurrence triggers follow-up even if self-resolved. |
sections.heading: 3) Console demo dashboards and views

sections.body:
| Metric | Target | Measurement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Reset end-to-end duration | \u2264 5 minutes (p95) | Reset command start → success | Reset includes: project cleanup, key rotation (if scheduled), seed config re-apply, traffic generator verification. |
| Healthcheck correctness | 100% (goal) | Automated validation | Healthcheck must flag: quota exhaustion risk, model pin invalid, telemetry ingestion lag, missing seeded entities. |
| Parallel demo readiness | \u2264 2 concurrent demos per region (baseline) | Capacity + quota checks | Scaling beyond baseline is planned work; see capacity runbook. |
sections.heading: 4) Demo reset + healthcheck

sections.body: We use error budgets to balance changes (new demo scenarios, Console tweaks, model updates) against stability.
sections.heading: Error budget policy

sections.body:
- **Monthly error budget** (calendar month) is the primary accounting period.
- During heavy demo periods (quarter-end), we may also monitor **weekly burn rates** and temporarily tighten gating.
sections.heading: Budget periods

sections.body:
We track burn against the primary availability/freshness SLOs above.

1) **Info threshold: 1x burn rate (projected to exhaust budget by end of month)**
   - Action: Post status note in #demo-oncall and tag owners. Confirm dashboards, streaming, and reset health.

2) **Warn threshold: 2x burn rate (projected to exhaust within ~2 weeks)**
   - Action: Freeze non-essential demo changes (deck-dependent UI tweaks, new scenario additions). Require SRE sign-off for demo-tenant deploys.

3) **Critical threshold: 5x burn rate (projected to exhaust within ~3–5 days)**
   - Action: Demo environment enters **stability mode**:
     - No feature work; only reliability fixes.
     - Disable risky experiments (non-critical canaries for demo routes).
     - Ensure backup assets are up to date (screenshots/recording).
     - Daily standup in #demo-oncall until burn is below 2x.
sections.heading: Burn-rate thresholds and actions

sections.body:
The following changes require either an SE dry-run or explicit go/no-go in #demo-oncall:
- Updates to **pinned model versions** or fallback routing rules
- Quota/rate-limit policy changes for demo org/projects
- Console changes affecting demo-critical pages (Usage, Errors, Traces, Rollouts)
