payload.page_title: Marketplace SKU Catalog v2 (AWS + GCP) — Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Add-ons

sections.body: This document defines Redwood Inference’s **Marketplace SKU Catalog v2** for AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Map cleanly to Redwood’s internal billing meters and entitlements (no “special marketplace-only plans” in product).
- Support enterprise procurement patterns (usage-based, commits, reserved capacity, and Private licensing).
- Reduce buyer confusion by aligning names across clouds: **Hosted** vs **Dedicated** vs **Private**, plus add-ons.
sections.heading: The catalog is designed to

sections.body:
- SKU naming conventions
- Inclusions/exclusions
- Marketplace billing dimensions → internal meters
- Entitlement semantics used by provisioning and metering

---
sections.heading: This is the source of truth for

sections.body:
**In scope:**
- Hosted API (usage-based) SKUs
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) SKUs
- Private deployment (license) SKUs
- Compliance + observability add-ons sold via marketplace

**Out of scope (handled via private offers / order forms as needed):**
- Custom model onboarding fees
- One-time professional services
- Complex multi-year ramp schedules (documented in private offer templates)

---
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- AWS Marketplace product/offer UIs (title length limits, readability)
- GCP Marketplace listings (SKU + plan naming constraints)
- Internal billing catalog (stable identifiers)
sections.heading: We need names that work in

sections.body: - **Redwood Inference <Product> — <Plan>**
sections.heading: Format

sections.body:
- “Redwood Inference Hosted — Pay-as-you-go”
- “Redwood Inference Dedicated — Reserved GPU Capacity”
- “Redwood Inference Private — VPC/On‑prem License”
sections.heading: Examples

sections.body:
- Use **Hosted / Dedicated / Private** as top-level taxonomy.
- Avoid hardware jargon in the SKU name (hardware is a capacity attribute in Dedicated entitlements).
- Avoid absolute claims (e.g., “HIPAA compliant”) in any SKU name.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: - **RI-MP-<PRODUCT>-<PLAN>-V2**
sections.heading: Internal canonical code used across systems

sections.body:
- PRODUCT ∈ {HOSTED, DEDICATED, PRIVATE, ADDON}
- PLAN is short and stable (PAYG, COMMIT, RESERVED, LICENSE, COMPLIANCE, RETENTION, AUDIT)
sections.heading: Where

sections.body:
- RI-MP-HOSTED-PAYG-V2
- RI-MP-DEDICATED-RESERVED-V2
- RI-MP-PRIVATE-LICENSE-V2
- RI-MP-ADDON-COMPLIANCE-V2
sections.heading: Examples

sections.body:
- Cloud-specific SKU identifiers (AWS “dimensions”, GCP “billing dimensions/SKUs”) map to these canonical codes.
- v2 codes must not be reused once deprecated.

---
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
**Intended buyer:** PLG teams + procurement-led usage-based purchases.

**Included:**
- Hosted inference endpoints (chat/text generation, embeddings, reranking where enabled)
- Streaming responses
- Basic usage analytics in Console
- Standard support (best-effort, business hours) unless upgraded via Support policy (not a marketplace SKU in v2)

**Excluded (unless separately contracted):**
- Dedicated data isolation / dedicated GPU pools
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) at-rest for hosted (Private offers/Private deployment only)
- Custom SLAs beyond standard platform targets
sections.heading: Hosted (Redwood API)

sections.body:
**Intended buyer:** teams needing predictable throughput, isolation, and SLA-backed performance.

**Included:**
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) tied to an org and region
- Dedicated autoscaling policy within reserved capacity; burst capacity only if contracted
- Console observability + per-model dashboards

**Excluded:**
- On-prem delivery
- Air-gapped environments
sections.heading: Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated)

sections.body:
**Intended buyer:** regulated enterprises and platform teams requiring VPC/on-prem options and customer-managed networking.

**Included:**
- Private control plane option (VPC) and/or on-prem package (as applicable to the purchased SKU)
- Audit logging features (base) and integration guidance
- Key management integration options (KMS/HSM integrations depend on deployment mode)

**Excluded:**
- Hardware procurement for on-prem (unless separately contracted)
- Customer-specific compliance attestations

---
sections.heading: Private (Redwood Private)

sections.body: All marketplace billing must map to the following internal meters.
sections.heading: Billing meter taxonomy (internal)

sections.body:
- **meter.hosted.tokens.prompt**: prompt/input tokens (counted per request)
- **meter.hosted.tokens.completion**: completion/output tokens (counted per request)
- **meter.hosted.embeddings.units**: embedding units (1 unit = 1,000 tokens embedded, rounded up)
- **meter.hosted.rerank.requests**: rerank requests (per call)
sections.heading: Hosted meters

sections.body:
- **meter.dedicated.gpu_hour**: GPU-hours consumed within a dedicated pool (by hardware class)
- **meter.dedicated.reservation.month**: reserved capacity commitment (monthly)
sections.heading: Dedicated meters

sections.body:
- **meter.private.platform.month**: platform license fee (monthly)
- **meter.private.nodes.month**: optional node-based licensing if applicable (monthly)
sections.heading: Private meters

sections.body:
- **meter.addon.compliance.month**: compliance bundle subscription (monthly)
- **meter.addon.audit_export.month**: audit log export feature (monthly)
- **meter.addon.retention_ext.month**: extended retention (monthly)
sections.heading: Add-on meters

sections.body:
- Marketplace dimension → internal meter mapping must be **1:1** wherever possible.
- If a marketplace requires multiple dimensions (e.g., prompt vs completion), both must be present and reconciled daily.
- Rounding rules must be consistent across clouds and align to internal invoice logic.

---
sections.heading: Metering principles

sections.body: The tables below define the canonical v2 SKUs. Cloud-specific identifiers are recorded in the AWS/GCP offer structure docs; this doc defines the canonical catalog and mapping expectations.
sections.heading: SKU catalog (v2)

sections.body:
| Customer-facing SKU name | Canonical code | Marketplace billing model | Marketplace dimensions (conceptual) | Internal meter mapping | Entitlements granted | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redwood Inference Hosted — Pay-as-you-go | RI-MP-HOSTED-PAYG-V2 | Usage-based | Prompt Tokens (1K), Completion Tokens (1K), Embeddings Units, Rerank Requests | meter.hosted.tokens.prompt; meter.hosted.tokens.completion; meter.hosted.embeddings.units; meter.hosted.rerank.requests | Hosted API access; standard rate limits per org tier | Default marketplace entry SKU; no minimum commit. |
| Redwood Inference Hosted — Committed Spend | RI-MP-HOSTED-COMMIT-V2 | Contract (commit drawdown) | Commit Amount ($) and/or Token Unit bundle (per marketplace constraints) | Internal ledger draws down against hosted meters above | Hosted API access; higher default quotas; invoice via marketplace | Use for customers requesting predictable monthly commit through marketplace. Structure differs by AWS vs GCP constraints; canonical code stays stable. |
sections.heading: A) Hosted SKUs

sections.body:
- Includes Redwood model catalog access as exposed in Hosted API.
- Does **not** include dedicated capacity; customers must purchase Dedicated for isolation and guaranteed throughput.
sections.heading: Hosted inclusions/exclusions clarifications

sections.body:
| Customer-facing SKU name | Canonical code | Marketplace billing model | Marketplace dimensions (conceptual) | Internal meter mapping | Entitlements granted | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redwood Inference Dedicated — Reserved GPU Capacity | RI-MP-DEDICATED-RESERVED-V2 | Contract (monthly reservation) | Reserved Capacity (monthly) + Optional GPU-hours overage (if allowed) | meter.dedicated.reservation.month (+ meter.dedicated.gpu_hour for overage where applicable) | Dedicated pool entitlement (region, hardware class, size); SLA profile flag | Hardware class (e.g., L4/A10/A100/H100) is an entitlement attribute; do not encode into SKU name unless a marketplace requires separate dimensions. |
| Redwood Inference Dedicated — Usage Overages (Add’l GPU-hours) | RI-MP-DEDICATED-OVERAGE-V2 | Usage-based (only when paired with reserved) | GPU-hours | meter.dedicated.gpu_hour | Allows burst/overage billing when enabled on the org | This SKU is optional and should not be public unless a partner portal requires it; typically enabled via private offer. |
sections.heading: B) Dedicated SKUs

sections.body:
- “Reserved” implies capacity allocation + predictable throughput targets; exact SLO language is governed by the contract/offer.
- Dedicated does not imply Private networking; for VPC/on-prem requirements, use Private.
sections.heading: Dedicated inclusions/exclusions clarifications

sections.body:
| Customer-facing SKU name | Canonical code | Marketplace billing model | Marketplace dimensions (conceptual) | Internal meter mapping | Entitlements granted | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redwood Inference Private — VPC/On‑prem License | RI-MP-PRIVATE-LICENSE-V2 | Contract (monthly/annual) | Platform License (monthly/annual) | meter.private.platform.month | Private deployment entitlement; private control plane flags; support routing tag | Deployment mode (VPC vs on-prem) is captured as an entitlement attribute and provisioning workflow selection. |
| Redwood Inference Private — Node-Based License (Optional) | RI-MP-PRIVATE-NODES-V2 | Contract (monthly) | Licensed Nodes (count/month) | meter.private.nodes.month | Node-count cap for licensed clusters | Only used when customer licensing requires node-based constraints (primarily on-prem). Prefer platform-only license when possible. |
sections.heading: C) Private SKUs

sections.body:
- “Private” includes customer-managed networking and elevated security controls, but does not automatically grant specific regulatory certifications.
- Audit logs are available in all tiers; advanced export/retention features are add-ons (below).
sections.heading: Private inclusions/exclusions clarifications

sections.body:
Add-ons are intended to be attachable to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (subject to deployment compatibility). If a marketplace cannot express “attachable,” we list them as separate purchasable plans and enforce compatibility via entitlement checks.

| Customer-facing SKU name | Canonical code | Marketplace billing model | Marketplace dimensions (conceptual) | Internal meter mapping | Entitlements granted | Inclusions | Exclusions/notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compliance Bundle (Marketplace) | RI-MP-ADDON-COMPLIANCE-V2 | Contract (monthly) | Compliance Bundle (monthly) | meter.addon.compliance.month | compliance_bundle=true | Security documentation bundle access workflow, compliance feature flags (where applicable), and faster security review path | Does not confer customer compliance; evidence access may be gated and requires approved contacts. |
| Audit Log Export | RI-MP-ADDON-AUDIT-V2 | Contract (monthly) | Audit Export (monthly) | meter.addon.audit_export.month | audit_export=true | Export audit logs to customer SIEM/storage destinations supported by deployment mode | Availability varies by deployment type; enforce via entitlement compatibility matrix. |
| Extended Retention | RI-MP-ADDON-RETENTION-V2 | Contract (monthly) | Retention Extension (monthly) | meter.addon.retention_ext.month | retention_extended=true | Increased retention for logs/telemetry per policy | Does not override legal hold requirements; retention maxima depend on product constraints and published policy. |
sections.heading: D) Add-on SKUs (attachable)

sections.body:
- Compliance Bundle: Hosted ✅ / Dedicated ✅ / Private ✅
- Audit Log Export: Hosted ⚠️ (limited) / Dedicated ✅ / Private ✅
- Extended Retention: Hosted ✅ / Dedicated ✅ / Private ✅

(⚠️ = supported only for specific data types or regions; refer to the Security Packet and Data Handling doc.)

---
sections.heading: Compatibility matrix (enforced by entitlement service)

sections.body:
- Prompt tokens billed to **meter.hosted.tokens.prompt**.
- Completion tokens billed to **meter.hosted.tokens.completion**.
- Marketplace “per 1K tokens” dimensions are computed as: `ceil(tokens / 1000)` for billing units *only if required by marketplace*; internal raw tokens are still stored for analytics and reconciliation.
sections.heading: 1) Hosted token mapping

sections.body:
- 1 embedding unit = **1,000 tokens embedded**, rounded up per request.
- Internal records store raw token count + computed units for marketplace reconciliation.

payload.page_title: Fidelity migration impact matrix and pricing heuristics

sections.body: Playbook and decision matrix to guide product and commercial teams when migrating customers between fidelity tiers (e.g., high, standard, low). Includes impact matrix, quantitative heuristics used for pricing adjustments, rollout steps, telemetry requirements, and risk mitigations.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Purpose
This document provides a repeatable playbook for assessing the customer and system impact when migrating a tenant’s inference consumption between fidelity tiers. It combines an operational impact matrix (technical and customer-facing effects) with concrete pricing heuristics and a phased migration plan. The goal is to enable predictable economics while limiting customer disruption and preserving SLOs.

Scope
- Applies to migrations across fidelity bands within Redwood’s consumption model (e.g., High-Fidelity -> Standard, Standard -> Low-Fidelity).
- Relevant to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; where private deployments have separate contractual constraints, use the appendix guidance.
- Intended audience: product managers, solutions engineering, account teams, billing, and SRE.

Definitions
- Fidelity tier: Operational profile that trades response quality characteristics (sampling, decoding, quantization, KV cache aggressiveness) for cost/latency. Typical tiers: High, Standard, Low.
- Migration: A change to the effective fidelity tier for a tenant (per-route or global).
- Fidelity delta: Observable changes in output quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxy, hallucination rate, perplexity drift, or domain-specific accuracy).

Impact Matrix (technical / customer / commercial)
Format: rows = Migration type, columns = Expected system CPU/GPU impact, Latency, Token cost delta, User-facing quality risk, Customer billing change, Recommended guardrail.

| Migration | GPU utilization | 95p latency | Cost per 1k tokens | Output quality risk | Billing delta | Guardrail |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| High -> Standard | -20% to -35% | -10% to -25% | -28% | Small drop; risk on long-context summarization | -25% | Canary 1% traffic, track domain prompts |
| Standard -> Low | -30% to -50% | -15% to -40% | -40% to -55% | Medium; increased token repetition, factuality regressions | -45% | Run A/B on synthetic prompts, revert on >5% metric degradation |
| High -> Low (fast path) | -45% to -70% | -25% to -60% | -60%+ | High; possible unacceptable regressions for sensitive workflows | -60%+ | Only for non-transactional routes or explicit customer opt-in |
| Low -> Standard | +15% to +30% | +8% to +20% | +30% | Quality improvement measurable; risk of increased cost | +28% | Phased uplift with cost alerts and budget caps |

Note: values above are workload-sensitive. Always run synthetic replay (see telemetry section) before schedule.

Quantitative Pricing Heuristics
We use a set of heuristics to translate expected runtime delta into an adjustment to per-token pricing or to recommended credits/discounts for migration windows. Heuristics are intentionally conservative to avoid revenue loss from quality-related churn.

1) Baseline compute cost mapping
- Measure steady-state per-token GPU seconds over representative 24h window.
- Map GPU seconds to unit cost using committed pricing for the deployment (hosted vs dedicated).

2) Apply fidelity multiplier (example):
- High: 1.00 (reference)
- Standard: 0.72 (+/- 0.06)
- Low: 0.42 (+/- 0.08)
These multipliers are validated monthly against production telemetry; treat as soft knobs.

3) Convert to billable price adjustment
- If migration reduces compute by X%, then per-token price is reduced by max(X - 5%, floor 10%), where 5% accounts for overheads not realized as direct savings.
- For increases in fidelity, recommend a surcharge calculated as ceil((observed cost increase + 3% ops premium) * 100)/100 to nearest cent per 1k tokens for advertised pricing.

4) Migration crediting
- For customer-facing migrations (where perceived drop might reduce retention), offer a one-time credit sized at 10% of the first-month expected spend differential for migrations that exceed a projected 20% quality regression risk.

Decision rules (binary)
- If projected output-quality delta (measured by the evaluation harness) > 7% on critical prompt set => require explicit customer approval and Solutions Eng sign-off.
- If projected cost savings < 8% => do not auto-migrate; consider opt-in only.

Telemetry & Evaluation Requirements
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Synthetic replay of at least 50k representative requests or 72 hours of sampled production traffic (whichever is larger).
- Evals: domain prompt set (owner-provided) + Redwood baseline prompt set. Key metrics: fidelity_score, hallucination_rate, latency_p95, token_cost_estimate.
- Dashboard: per-route change visualization, diff histograms for token counts and latency, sliding 24/168h windows.

Migration Playbook (operational steps)
1) Prepare:
  - Owner: Product / Solutions Eng
  - Collate domain prompt set (min 100 canonical prompts) and representative traffic sample (see telemetry).
  - Estimate cost delta via offline simulator (use cost-sim SDK v2).
2) Synthetic run (preflight):
  - Run A/B: 10% traffic routed to candidate tier for 48 hours. Capture fidelity metrics and customer-facing regressions.
  - Monitor: fidelity_score drop, error rates, latency p95, requests with >3 repeated tokens.
3) Canary expansion:
  - If preflight passes thresholds (fidelity_score drop <= 4% and no customer errors) expand to 33% for 72 hours.
4) Billing and pricing action:
  - Apply temporary dual-billing window: customer billed at midpoint price for 2 billing cycles while retention and usage observed; credit if churn signals triggered.
5) Full rollout:
  - Increase to 100% in 24-48 hours with automated rollback triggers.
  - Post-rollout: 14-day monitoring window with weekly review.
sections.heading: Before approving a migration produce

sections.body:
- fidelity_score drop > 7% sustained for 6 hours
- new error.rate increase > 2x baseline
- customer-initiated escalation recorded

Customer communication templates
- Pre-migration (email/in-console): clear summary of expected changes, scheduled window, cost impact (estimated), opt-out instructions, contact for support.
- Post-migration: operational summary with before/after metrics and applied credits if any.

Pricing examples (scenarios)
- Scenario A: Customer A (Standard -> Low): baseline monthly spend $50k. Projected token cost reduction 45%. Heuristics: reduce per-token price by 40% (since >8% and accounting for overheads). Offer 10% one-time credit ($5k) if fidelity delta on domain set >10%.
- Scenario B: Customer B (High -> Standard, non-critical): baseline $12k. Projected compute saving 30%. Per-token price reduced by 25% and no credit; add a 2-month observation billing band and telemetry reports.

Risk & Mitigations
- Regressions for long-context chains: use targeted fallback policy for routes with long sequences (route-level 'high-fidelity' pin).
- Unexpected billing disputes: require ledger export and spend-simulator runbooks to be part of migration packet.
- Model drift: include monthly re-eval cadence for migrated tenants for first 6 months.

KPIs to evaluate migration program
- Migration success rate: % migrations completed without rollback within 14 days (target >= 90%).
- Net dollar retention impact for migrated customers at 90 days (target >= -2%).
- Average cost savings realized vs simulated (target within +/- 8%).
- Time to rollback when automated trigger fires (target < 10 minutes).

Operational ownership and contacts
- Product (Fidelity Programs): Maya Chen (owner) — maya@redwood.example.com
- Solutions Engineering: Liam Patel — liam@redwood.example.com
- Billing & Revenue Ops: Sofia Martinez — sofia@redwood.example.com
- SRE escalation: Ethan Brooks — ethan@redwood.example.com

Appendix A — Private deployments and contractual constraints
- Private deployments may require contract amendment for any fidelity-based pricing changes. Work with Legal and Commercial to produce one-off amendments. For on-prem, the migration must be scheduled with a 4-week lead time and a signed change order.

Appendix B — Example cost-sim snippet (pseudo-JSON)
{
  "route": "chat-v1/assistant",
  "baseline_seconds_per_token": "0.0032",
  "candidate_multiplier": "0.72",
  "estimated_monthly_tokens": "1_200_000_000",
  "projected_monthly_cost": "$X"
}

Appendix C — Fast checklist (one-pager)
- [ ] Domain prompts collected and validated
- [ ] Synthetic replay configured (>=50k requests)
- [ ] Preflight A/B run (10% traffic) complete and passing
- [ ] Canary (33%) complete and passing
- [ ] Billing plan updated and communications drafted
- [ ] Rollback configured with automated alerts

Notes and change log
- 2027-08-09: Initial draft and internal review.
- 2027-10-01: Added explicit billing band and credit heuristics after pilot with three customers.
- 2028-01-15: Clarified rollback thresholds and added private-deploy constraints.

Related artifacts
- Cost-sim SDK v2 runbook (internal link)

payload.page_title: Microbundle Crediting Playbook and PRD

sections.body:
Microbundle Crediting Playbook and PRD

Summary
-------
This document defines the Microbundle Crediting model (short: Microbundles), the product requirements for self-serve developers, the billing and reconciliation rules, and an operational playbook for rollout and rollback. Microbundles are small, attachable credit packs (fractional token/feature credits) intended to enable low-friction feature gating, inexpensive development experimentation, and per-route micropricing for high-cardinality use cases (edge agents, mobile SDKs, and partner integrations).

Goals
-----
- Enable customers to purchase and allocate small units of consumption-credit (microbundles) to routes, features, or teams.
- Support fractional consumption (credits consumed at 0.001-credit granularity) to keep costs commensurate with short-lived/low-volume workloads.
- Provide transparent metering and reconciliation with accuracy SLOs suitable for billing (monthly reconciliation) and near-real-time UX (estimate & reserve APIs).
- Offer a simple self-serve console and API for buying, gifting, and allocating microbundles.

Non-goals
---------
- Not intended to replace enterprise reserved capacity or large token bundles.
- Does not include long-term commitment discounts at launch (that is a later phase).

Definitions
-----------
- Microbundle: A purchasable pack that carries N credit units and meta-tags (feature tag, route tag, expiration).
- Credit unit: The internal currency used to pay for generation, embedding, or reranking operations. 1 credit unit is decoupled from tokens; conversion is defined per model/profile.
- Fractional credit: We charge/consume credits at 0.001 precision to support micro-usage.

Design overview
---------------
High-level: customers buy microbundles via the Console or Billing API. Microbundles are recorded on the customer account and can be: assigned to routes, gifted between subaccounts, or consumed directly by passing a bundle_id in the request header. The runtime will prefer bundle meter consumption when present, falling back to normal per-token billing when exhausted or absent.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- bundle_id: UUID that maps to a bundle ledger entry.
- allocation: assignment of bundle_id to a route/team with an optional monthly cap.
- reserve_token API: short reservation token that guarantees credit for a single request (used by offline/mobile flows).

Microbundle tiers (initial public offering)
----------------------------------------
| Tier name | Credits | Typical use case | Price (USD) | Expiry |
|-----------|---------|------------------:|-----------:|--------|
| nano      | 10      | quick dogfooding / API keys for PoC | $0.49  | 90d |
| small     | 100     | small feature trial or sandbox | $3.99   | 180d |
| devbox    | 1,000   | light developer-heavy testing | $29.99  | 365d |
| team-mini | 10,000  | small team experiments | $249.00 | 365d |

Note: pricing above is list; final prices subject to regional taxes and currency rounding. Implementation will support promo codes and partner grants.

Metering rules and conversion semantics
--------------------------------------
1) Consumption path: when a request includes header X-Redwood-Bundle-ID: <bundle_id>, the serving runtime will perform these steps in order:
   a) Check allocation for route/model compatibility.
   b) Estimate credit cost using the model performance profile (credits_per_token or credits_per-inference).
   c) Attempt to reserve fractional credits from the bundle ledger atomically.
   d) If reservation succeeds, proceed and debit on completion; if it fails (insufficient), fall back to per-token charging.

2) Estimation examples (JSON):
```json
{
  "model": "rwkv-34b-quant",
  "input_tokens": 64,
  "output_tokens_estimate": 128,
  "credits_per_token": 0.0025,
  "estimated_credits": 0.48
}
```

3) Fractional rounding: We store ledger balances as integers in milli-credits (1 credit = 1000 milli-credits). All reservations and debits are in milli-credits to avoid floating point issues.

Billing & reconciliation SLOs
----------------------------
- Real-time estimate accuracy: estimate vs actual debit should be within +/-15% on median workloads (measured per model-profile) for the 30-day canary window.
- Billing accuracy (ledger correctness): 99.995% monthly accuracy for credits debited vs consumption events (target for production).
- Reconciliation latency: all debit events must be visible in billing ledger within 60 seconds of request completion.

Required telemetry (minimum)
- metric: microbundle.estimate_median_error (target < 15%)
- metric: microbundle.debit_latency_seconds.p95 (target < 2s)
- metric: microbundle.ledger_discrepancies_monthly_count (target < 5 for global accounts)
- logs: reservation.debug logs with bundle_id, route, estimate, reserved_milli_credits

Console & API UX
----------------
sections.heading: Key constructs

sections.body:
- Billing -> Microbundles page: purchase flow, apply promo, view history.
- Route management: ‘assign microbundle’ modal with cap & expiry.
- Usage insights: per-bundle consumption timeline and per-route spend breakdown.

API surface (initial)
- POST /v1/microbundles/purchase {tier, quantity, promo_code?} -> 201 { bundle_ids[] }
- POST /v1/microbundles/{bundle_id}/allocate {route_id, monthly_cap_milli_credits?} -> 200
- GET /v1/microbundles/{bundle_id}/ledger -> 200 {balance_milli_credits, history[] }
- POST /v1/microbundles/estimate -> 200 {estimated_milli_credits} (public preview)

Example: reserve flow (CLI)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/microbundles/estimate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input_tokens":32,"expected_output":64}'
```

PRD acceptance criteria (must pass to ship)
-------------------------------------------
1) End-to-end flow: purchase -> allocate -> consume -> ledger debit verified in billing within 60s.
2) Console pages ship with purchase and allocation UI (QA checklist attached).
3) Estimate accuracy median error < 15% for eight representative models (small, medium, large).
4) Service-level dashboards and alerting enabled (see telemetry).
5) Can be toggled per-customer via feature-flag (allowlist for early customers).

Rollout plan and canary metrics
-------------------------------
Phase 0: internal dogfood (2 weeks)
- Enable feature-flag for internal accounts. Target metrics: estimate_error_median < 18%, debit_latency_p95 < 2s.

Phase 1: Invite-only customers (4 weeks)
- 5–10 customers, nightly reconciliation checks.
- Measurement windows: 7-day rolling for estimate error and ledger discrepancy rate.

Phase 2: Gradual public rollout (8 weeks)
- 10% percent traffic first week, 25% second week, 50% third week, 100% final week.
- Automatic gating: if ledger_discrepancies_monthly_count > 10 or debit_latency_p95 > 5s, pause rollout and revert traffic to non-bundle charging.

Rollback & incident playbook
---------------------------
1) Detect: alert triggered (discrepancy count or debit latency).
2) Mitigate: toggle feature-flag to disable bundle acceptance at the routing tier (runtime will fallback to per-token charging).
3) Assess: run reconciliation job to enumerate affected bundle_ids and estimate exposure.
4) Communicate: incident channel #inc-billing and customer success notify affected customers within 24h.
5) Remediate: apply corrective ledger adjustments and issue credits as necessary.
6) Postmortem: 72-hour review with engineering, product, SRE, and billing.

Security and compliance considerations
------------------------------------
- Bundle metadata and ledger entries must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed).
- Audit log: every debit, reservation, and allocation change must be retained for 13 months for billing disputes.
- RBAC: only billing admin roles and route-owners may allocate bundles.

Open questions (to resolve before GA)
------------------------------------
- International pricing and currency rounding strategy for sub-dollar microbundles.
- Legal wording for expiry and refund policy for unused microbundles.
- Interplay with enterprise reserved capacity: can we auto-fallback to reserved capacity without double-billing?

Ownership and timeline
----------------------
- Product owner: Asha Patel (product)
- Engineering lead: Diego Morales (billing infra)
- SRE / Observability: Nora Ahmed
- Estimated milestones: prototype & internal dogfood complete by 2028-07-12; invite-only by 2028-08-09; GA targeted 2028-10-01 (subject to acceptance criteria).

Appendices
---------
A) Sample ledger entry (CSV columns): bundle_id, timestamp, event_type, milli_credits_delta, resulting_balance_milli, request_id, model_profile
B) QA checklist highlights: purchase redemption test, concurrent reservation stress test (10k/s), reconciliation end-to-end test (100k events), security KMS key rotation impact test.

Notes and references
--------------------
- See related: product-overview/deployment-surface-consumption-pricing-implications-2026 for consumption impacts on pricing tiers.
- See token-bundle-flex-enterprise-metering-2026-08-20 for large-bundle metering patterns and differences.

payload.page_title: Feature-level microbundle pricing experiments playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook describes the approach, experiment designs, measurement plan, and rollout steps for per-feature microbundle pricing experiments. The goal is to enable incremental monetization of discrete fidelity features (e.g., response-volatility-control, structured-output hooks, session-anchored embeddings) by offering tiny, composable bundles that developers can opt into. This document focuses on experiment hygiene, metric definitions, sample pricing matrices, simulation queries, and a safe rollout path for Hosted and Dedicated customers.

Background and motivation

- Problem: Many customers only need a small subset of high-cost fidelity features. Current tiered SKUs (e.g., Fidelity Bronze/Silver/Gold) are coarse and force overpayment or multiple product integrations.
- Hypothesis: Offering per-feature microbundles priced at sub-dollar-per-100k-token increments will increase revenue from low-volume customers and improve conversion from free trials without materially degrading unit economics or SLOs.
- Constraints: Pricing experiments must preserve existing customer SLAs and should be revenue-neutral in early A/B phases to avoid commercial disruption.

Objectives and success criteria
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Achieve a 10–15% increase in ARPU among developer-tier customers who enable >=1 microbundle within 90 days of availability.
2) Maintain hosted inference 99.9% 95th-percentile token-latency baseline for customers enabling microbundles.
3) Demonstrate microbundle gross margin > 35% in simulation tests before GA.
sections.heading: Primary objectives (OKR-aligned)

sections.body:
- Adoption rate: percent of eligible customers who enable >=1 microbundle within 30 days.
- Incremental revenue: net new revenue attributable to microbundles (USD) measured monthly.
- Retention delta: 90-day retention difference between adopters and matched control.
- Cost delta: average per-token cost delta for adopters (runtime + infra amortized).
- SLA impact: change in 95th p50/p95 token latency, OOM/eviction rates for impacted pools.

Microbundle taxonomy (examples)

- Low-cost feature microbundles (target price $0.20–$2 / 100k tokens):
  - Structured-output hook (JSON schema enforcement)
  - Soft-stop hallucination penalty (lightweight reranker)
  - Small-session pinned embeddings (per-session retention 1–2 keys)

- Medium-cost microbundles (target price $2–$10 / 100k tokens):
  - Deterministic sampling / constrained decoding primitives
  - Enhanced KV-cache persistence (session-hardened warm cache)

- High-cost microbundles (target price $10–$50 / 100k tokens):
  - Response-volatility-control (heavy reranker + cross-attention adapters)
  - Multimodal-attachment-fusion (extra compute for small images/metadata)

Experiment designs

1) Pricing A/B (Revenue-neutral pricing test)
- Setup: Randomly assign new developer signups to control (no microbundles; existing tiers) or experiment (see microbundle opt-in modal). For the experiment cohort, show suggested microbundles with prices and a free 14-day trial credit for the first microbundle.
- Sample size: minimum 1,200 signups per arm to detect a 7% ARPU lift with 80% power.
- Duration: 90 days.
- Measurement: tracking of adoption rate, incremental revenue, and retention delta.

2) Feature-only opt-in (Product-led adoption)
- Setup: Enable microbundle toggle in Console -> Developer Sandbox. No forced price shown for first 30 days; instead show a consumption quota limit and notification of impending charge.
- Duration: pilot 30–60 days.
- Measurement: friction-to-adopt (time-to-first-use), conversion to paid after quota.

3) Price elasticity ladder (staged price exposure)
- Setup: For experiment cohort, randomly assign one of three suggested price points per microbundle (low/medium/high).
- Measurement: discrete demand curve per feature; track marginal adoption drop per 10% price increase.

Measurement plan and instrumentation
sections.heading: Success metrics (measured per cohort)

sections.body:
- event.microbundle.shown (user_id, signup_cohort, bundle_id, suggested_price, ui_context)
- event.microbundle.enrolled (user_id, bundle_id, start_ts, trial_end_ts, pricing_tier)
- event.microbundle.usage (user_id, bundle_id, tokens_consumed, model_variant, runtime_pool)
- metric.runtime.cost_per_token (by model_variant, pool, minute)
- metric.latency.p95_tokens (by customer_id, route, model_variant)

Suggested SQL queries (example)

1) Adoption rate by cohort (Postgres-like):
SELECT cohort, bundle_id, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS adopters, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens
FROM microbundle_events
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-12-01' AND '2027-01-10'
GROUP BY cohort, bundle_id;

2) Incremental revenue estimate (simple model):
-- assumes price USD per 100k tokens, prorated by tokens_consumed
SELECT cohort, bundle_id, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens,
       SUM((tokens_consumed/100000.0) * price_per_100k) AS revenue_estimate
FROM microbundle_usage JOIN microbundle_catalog USING (bundle_id)
GROUP BY cohort, bundle_id;

Cost simulation steps

1) For each bundle, compute worst-case per-token cost: runtime + infra overhead + routing credit.
2) Simulate 95th percentile session retention impact (KV cache warmup) using existing workload traces (use the simulation harness from eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
3) Run Monte Carlo on adoption percentiles (5/25/50/75/95) to estimate margin sensitivity.

Sample pricing matrix (illustrative)

| bundle_id | short_desc                        | price/100k | expected_cost/100k | margin_est | notes |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|------------|--------------------|------------|-------|
| B-JSON1   | Structured-output (light)         | $1.50      | $0.70              | 53%        | low CPU, small cost delta |
| B-KV1     | Session pinned embeddings (small) | $2.50      | $1.20              | 52%        | increases memory usage per session |
| B-RER1    | Soft reranker (light)             | $5.00      | $3.20              | 36%        | higher CPU; monitor p95 latency |

Customer-facing UX patterns

- Console: "Add microbundle" flow inside route and project settings. Display estimated incremental cost per 10k tokens and projected monthly spend given last 30-day usage.
- API: Allow billing_action="enable_microbundle" on per-route creation. Document the feature in SDKs with example JSON payload:

{
  "route": "/chat",
  "microbundles": ["B-JSON1", "B-KV1"]
}

- Usage billing: Microbundles appear as separate line items in Billing -> Usage with a descriptive label and cost-per-usage.

Safeguards and guardrails

- Default caps: Any newly-enabled microbundle defaults to a 30-day usage cap of $5 for free-trial cohorts. Admins can raise caps.
- SLA isolation: Microbundle-enabled traffic is routed to dedicated soft pools tagged with "microbundle-experiment" to avoid cross-tenant P95 regressions.
- Automated rollback thresholds: If any of the following occur during experiment window, pause new enrollments and trigger review:
  - p95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline for experiment cohort
  - error rate (5xx) delta > 0.5% absolute
  - infra cost per-token unexpectedly increases > 30% vs simulated estimate

Rollout and lifecycle plan

1) Internal alpha (0–4 weeks): small developer pilot (10 customers). Validate instrumentation and billing events. Owners: Product (Ava), Eng Runtime (Ethan), Billing (Priya).
2) Beta experiment (4–12 weeks): A/B pricing ladder and feature-only opt-in across new signups. Minimum sample size rules apply.
3) Analyze results and tune prices (weeks 12–16): compute elasticity and run margin sims.
4) Gradual GA (weeks 16–28): enable in Console, create migration guide for existing customers, add UI education. Offer opt-out windows for Dedicated customers.

Owners and responsibilities

- Product (owner): Ava Martinez — experiment design, success criteria, go/no-go.
- Eng Runtime: Ethan Kim — routing, pool tagging, p95 monitoring.
- Billing & Revenue Ops: Priya Patel — usage line-itemization, invoices, revenue measurement.
- Analytics: Jordan Lee — experiment instrumentation, cohort analysis, SQL queries.
- Legal & Compliance: review pricing language and contracts pre-GA.

FAQ and open decisions

- Q: Should microbundles be available to Dedicated customers at GA?
  - A: Dedicated customers require contract amendments. Default GA will be Hosted only; Dedicated enablement will be opt-in via sales playbook.

- Q: How do we prevent abuse (e.g., switch between cheap microbundles to exploit fallback)?
  - A: Enforce per-route entitlement and minimum billing period per bundle (30 days). Track abusive patterns and escalate to SRE/Trust.

Related pages

- /product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/entropy-based-fidelity-credit-allocator-2026-10-14
- /product-docs/product-overview/consumption-playground-developer-onboarding-overview-2026-03-22
- /eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/simulation-harness-intro

Appendix: example rollout checklist (numbered)

1. Verify telemetry is live for event.microbundle.* (Analytics sign-off).
2. Deploy UI modal with A/B assignment flags (DevEx sign-off).
3. Provision microbundle routing pools with isolation tags (Eng Runtime).
4. Set trial credit caps and billing line-item templates (Billing Ops).
5. Run initial 10-customer alpha for 2 weeks and collect p95/5xx metrics.
6. Proceed to Beta only if SLA regressions are within thresholds.

Document change log

- 2026-11-20: created by Ava Martinez (initial draft).
- 2026-12-18: added simulation steps and SQL examples (Jordan Lee).
- 2027-01-11: updated rollout cadence and sample pricing matrix; switched status to in_review.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Micro-Fidelity Migration and Hybrid Pricing Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook provides a step-by-step operational and commercial plan for migrating customers from coarse-grained token billing and large-bundle fidelity SKUs to a micro-fidelity, hybrid-pricing model. The goal is to reduce friction for mid-market customers migrating from hosted to Dedicated or Private deployments while protecting Redwood economics and preserving predictable unit costs.

Audience:
- Product managers owning pricing and packaging
- Solutions Engineers / Sales Engineers executing migrations
- Account teams for customer communications
- Finance for revenue recognition impacts
- Billing & metering engineers for implementation details

Objectives:
- Provide a repeatable migration path with playbook steps and run rates.
- Define a hybrid pricing construct that combines base capacity + micro-fidelity credits.
- Ensure observability signals and guardrails to detect revenue or quality regressions.
- Offer recommended incentives and temporary discounts for migrations.

Background and motivation:
Many mid-market customers rely on bundled token credits and per-tenant fidelity SKUs that are inflexible for incremental usage patterns. Customers hesitate to commit to Dedicated capacity without a predictable marginal cost for higher-fidelity requests. The micro-fidelity model decomposes fidelity (compute/latency/quality) into small, billable credit units customers can attach per-route or per-model.

High-level hybrid pricing model (recommended):
- Base reservation: monthly committed capacity (vCPU/GPU units) with guaranteed throughput SLA.
- Included credit bucket: X micro-fidelity credits/month (consumed first).
- On-demand micro-credits: per-1k-token equivalent credit price for bursts and higher-fidelity model variants.
- Fallback pricing: guaranteed cost ceiling via auto-fallback to standard model variants when on-demand credit spend would exceed configured monthly cap.

Core micro-credit definitions and examples:
- Micro-fidelity credit (MFC): unit that maps to compute/latency premium for a request. 1 MFC ~= baseline for 1k standard tokens at standard quality.
- Example tiers: low-fidelity = 0.25 MFC/1k tokens, standard = 1 MFC/1k tokens, premium = 3 MFC/1k tokens.

Sample pricing table (examples for guidance only):
| Component | Metric | Pricing example | Notes |
|----------|--------:|----------------:|-------|
| Base reservation | GPU-hour equivalent | $12,000 / month | 1x p3.2xlarge equivalent; guaranteed 95th %-ile latency SLO |
| Included credits | MFC / month | 100,000 MFC | Applies across tenant; resets monthly |
| On-demand MFC | MFC / 1k tokens | $0.0009 / MFC | Metered at request time |
| Cost ceiling | Monthly spend cap | Customer-configured | Auto-fallback triggers at cap |

Migration playbook (sales + SE + engineering):
1) Pre-migration audit (SE + account):
   - Collect current token usage: 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day histograms by route and model.
   - Collect peak concurrency and latency-sensitive routes.
   - Identify top 10 prompt templates driving premium fidelity.
   - Deliver a migration readiness score (green/amber/red).
2) Plan and propose (SE + product + finance):
   - Map historical usage to MFC consumption using conversion factors (use 1 MFC/1k tokens baseline; adjust for model variants).
   - Propose a base reservation sized for 75th percentile baseline throughput.
   - Propose included credits at 40% of expected monthly MFC burn to encourage predictable commit.
   - Simulate monthly cost under 3 consumption scenarios (conservative, expected, high). Attach example spreadsheet export.
3) Pilot (2–4 weeks):
   - Enable micro-credit meter in a sandpit tenant.
   - Route 20% of traffic to micro-fidelity-priced variants with observability flags.
   - Capture quality metrics (BLEU-like scoring, embedding drift, or customer-specific evals).
   - Validate billing events and invoice lines in staging billing pipeline.
4) Full migration rollout (4–8 weeks):
   - Gradual ramp: 20% -> 50% -> 100% traffic shift with checkpoints.
   - Enable cost ceiling auto-fallback and alerting for >10% variance vs forecast.
   - Apply any agreed migration credits or temporary discounts as contract adjustments.
5) Post-migration evaluation (30/60/90 days):
   - Review MFC utilization, cost per 1k tokens, and customer quality SLAs.
   - Update recommended included credit levels and reserved capacity if patterns diverge.

Implementation requirements (billing & metering):
- Metering lane must emit per-request MFC usage with the following fields: tenant_id, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, mfc_consumed, timestamp.
- Billing pipeline must support aggregation by tenant-month and export a line-item per MFC category.
- Console must display three cost projections: current month burn, forecast at current rate, and worst-case cap.
- Audit logs for migration promotions and discount adjustments.

SLOs, observability & alerts:
- Billing accuracy: <0.1% reconciliation drift between meter and invoice for migrated accounts (30-day rolling).
- Quality regression: customer-specific eval A/B delta no worse than -2% from baseline for the first 30 days.
- Cost variance: alert if monthly spend > 15% above pilot forecast within first 60 days.
- Latency SLO: reserved capacity routes maintain 95th %-ile latency below target (per-customer SLO).

Incentives and commercial constructs:
- Migration credit: one-time 10% MFC top-up applied first month for eligible mid-market customers.
- Ramp discount: first 3 months, on-demand MFCs billed at 90% list for customers that commit to a 6-month base reservation.
- Quality credits: conditional refunds if measured quality metrics drop below agreed thresholds after migration (per contract).

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpectedly high MFC burn increases customer churn.
  Mitigation: Cost ceiling auto-fallback and pre-migration simulations; clear comms on estimated worst-case spend.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to meter mismatch.
  Mitigation: Pilot reconciliation, invoice preview, and 30-day dispute SLA handled by billing ops.
- Risk: Customer perceives complexity.
  Mitigation: Offer a managed migration option (SE-led) and pre-packaged migration templates.

Rollout timeline and milestones (quarterly cadence):
- Q4 2026: Billing pipeline MVP and console cost projections.
- Q1 2027: Pilot with 5 mid-market customers and refine conversion factors.
- Q2 2027: Launch public pricing page and self-serve migration templates.
- Q3 2027: Expand to Dedicated and Private deployments; add on-prem metering connector.

Ownership and contacts:
- Pricing design: Product (Ava Patel)
- Migration operations: Solutions Engineering (Sana Mehta)
- Billing & metering implementation: Eng infra (Diego Ramirez)
- Finance approvals: Finance (Jin Park)

Appendix A — Example conversion logic (pseudocode):
- baseline_mfc = tokens_k * variant_multiplier
- variant_multiplier examples: {"low": 0.25, "standard": 1.0, "premium": 3.0}
- apply_customer_adjustment = baseline_mfc * customer_quality_factor

Appendix B — Example console screenshots (text descriptions):
- Billing preview panel: shows included credits, month-to-date MFC burn, forecast, and cap slider.
- Migration dashboard: per-route MFC burn heatmap, top 5 prompt templates by spend, quality delta sparkline.

Related docs and references:
- Pricing concepts and SKU glossary (link to internal pricing glossary).
- Per-tenant fidelity credit framework (reference: internal design doc).
- Graceful fidelity degradation PRD (reference: internal PRD).

Next steps and approvals required:
- Product to finalize list price for MFC (target: Feb 28, 2027).
- Billing and console teams to complete MVP by Mar 15, 2027.
- Pilot cohort selection and legal contract addendums by Mar 31, 2027.

Document revision history:
- 2026-11-20: Initial draft created by Ava Patel.
- 2027-01-10: Added sample pricing table and pilot checklist.
- 2027-02-15: Incorporated reviewer feedback; promoted to in_review.

payload.page_title: GCP Marketplace: SKU & Billing Dimensions (v2)

sections.body:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s GCP Marketplace SKU structure and the billing/metering dimensions used for GCP Marketplace reporting. It is the source of truth for:
- How GCP Marketplace “plans/SKUs” map to Redwood products (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and add-ons.
- Which usage dimensions we report to Google, with units, rounding rules, and source-of-truth meters.
- Integration expectations for Procurement + Metering flows (subscription → entitlement → org provisioning → usage reporting → reconciliation).

This is GCP-specific; AWS offer structure and dimensions are covered separately.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Ensure Marketplace SKUs map cleanly to Redwood internal billing meters (no ambiguous dimensions).
- Keep billing semantics procurement-friendly (predictable invoicing, clear unit definitions).
- Define reporting cadence, idempotency, and reconciliation rules that satisfy GCP Marketplace requirements and reduce customer billing disputes.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Final price points, discounting, or private offer terms (owned by Partnerships + Finance/Legal).
- Detailed UI copy for listing pages.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
For Redwood on GCP Marketplace (SaaS), the customer procures a plan that creates an entitlement. Redwood must:
1) Validate entitlement status during onboarding.
2) Map the entitlement to a Redwood org.
3) Report usage against the entitlement (for usage-based dimensions) OR rely on subscription charges (for fixed/contract dimensions).
sections.heading: Product + Plan model (SaaS)

sections.body:
During provisioning and ongoing metering, Redwood stores the following identifiers:
- GCP entitlement resource name ("gcp_entitlement_id"): the canonical key for metering attribution.
- GCP consumer billing account/project identifiers as provided by procurement payloads (for support + reconciliation).
- Redwood org_id and (optionally) a marketplace_subscription_id to support multi-subscription edge cases.
sections.heading: Key identifiers we store

sections.body:
- Entitlement propagation may be delayed; onboarding UX must provide retry guidance.
- Entitlement may be reassigned/updated (e.g., plan change); metering attribution must follow the current active entitlement.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
We publish three primary purchase paths, aligned to internal packaging:
1) Hosted API (usage-based)
2) Dedicated (subscription + optional overage)
3) Private (subscription; usage may be “$0 metered” for auditability depending on plan)

Add-ons are attachable where allowed by GCP Marketplace plan structure:
- Compliance Pack (security/compliance features + evidence access + extended retention options)
- Observability Retention (extended logs/metrics retention)
- Premium Support (SLA/support tier)
sections.heading: SKU / plan taxonomy (GCP)

sections.body:
- Product family prefix: “Redwood Inference”
- Plan names: “Hosted”, “Dedicated”, “Private”, plus tier markers (e.g., Standard/Enterprise) where needed.
- Usage dimensions: lowercase snake_case; stable over time (do not rename once launched).
sections.heading: Naming conventions (GCP-facing)

sections.body: The table below is the authoritative set of GCP Marketplace billing dimensions and their mapping to Redwood internal meters.
sections.heading: Billing dimension catalog (GCP)

sections.body:
- Units must be unambiguous and consistent across docs, console, and invoices.
- Dimensions should be low-cardinality and stable (avoid per-model dimensions; model choice is a Redwood config, not a billing dimension).
- Where volume is large (tokens), we report in “1K” units to reduce event volume while preserving accuracy.
sections.heading: Dimension requirements

sections.body:
| GCP dimension | Unit | What it covers | Redwood internal meter | Rounding/aggregation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| hosted_input_tokens_1k | 1 = 1,000 input tokens | Prompt/input tokens for chat/text generation, including system + developer messages | tokens_in | Aggregate hourly; round up to nearest 1K per hour per org+entitlement |
| hosted_output_tokens_1k | 1 = 1,000 output tokens | Completion/output tokens for chat/text generation (including streaming) | tokens_out | Aggregate hourly; round up to nearest 1K per hour per org+entitlement |
| hosted_embeddings_1k_tokens | 1 = 1,000 tokens embedded | Tokens processed by embedding endpoints (input text tokens) | embedding_tokens | Aggregate hourly; round up to nearest 1K per hour per org+entitlement |
| hosted_rerank_1k_items | 1 = 1,000 items reranked | Number of documents/items evaluated by rerank endpoints | rerank_items | Aggregate hourly; round up to nearest 1K per hour per org+entitlement |
sections.heading: Hosted API (usage-based) dimensions

sections.body:
- “Tokens” are counted using the serving model’s tokenizer, consistent with Redwood API usage analytics.
- For multi-part requests (tool calls, structured output), token counting follows the same accounting as existing Redwood hosted billing.
- If a request fails before inference begins (e.g., auth/validation), no usage is reported.
- If inference begins and fails mid-stream, usage is based on tokens actually generated and delivered (best effort); partial tokens are included.
sections.heading: Hosted notes

sections.body:
Dedicated on Marketplace is primarily subscription-priced (capacity reservation). We support optional overage/burst dimensions when contractually enabled.

| GCP dimension | Unit | What it covers | Redwood internal meter | Rounding/aggregation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| dedicated_capacity_month | 1 = 1 month | Reserved capacity subscription (GPU pool + isolation + SLA tier per plan) | dedicated_capacity_months | Charged via marketplace subscription; no usage reporting required for base reservation |
| dedicated_burst_gpu_hours | 1 = 1 GPU-hour | Approved burst usage beyond reservation (if enabled) | dedicated_burst_gpu_hours | Aggregate daily; report within 24h; round to 0.1 GPU-hour |
| dedicated_egress_gb | 1 = 1 GB | Customer-approved billable egress (rare; only if explicitly included in offer) | network_egress_gb_billable | Aggregate daily; round up to 0.1 GB |
sections.heading: Dedicated (subscription + optional overage) dimensions

sections.body:
- By default, Dedicated plans should avoid surprise variable charges; burst/egress dimensions must be explicitly enabled in the offer and reflected in customer-facing FAQs.
- Capacity “size” (e.g., GPU type/count) is captured in the plan configuration, not as a usage dimension.
sections.heading: Dedicated notes

sections.body:
Private is typically billed as a platform subscription (license + support). Some enterprise customers prefer “$0 usage reporting” for auditability; if used, those dimensions must remain non-billable and clearly documented.

| GCP dimension | Unit | What it covers | Redwood internal meter | Rounding/aggregation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| private_platform_month | 1 = 1 month | Private control plane subscription (VPC/on-prem package as scoped) | private_platform_months | Charged via marketplace subscription |
| private_compliance_pack_month | 1 = 1 month | Compliance add-on (controls, evidence access, audit log integrations, retention options) | compliance_pack_months | Charged via marketplace subscription |
| private_observability_retention_month | 1 = 1 month | Extended observability retention add-on | observability_retention_months | Charged via marketplace subscription |
sections.heading: Private (subscription) dimensions

sections.body: - Any “usage” within Private (tokens, embeddings) is governed by the customer’s own infra capacity; we do not bill per token for Private unless explicitly structured as a hybrid offer.
sections.heading: Private notes

sections.body:
- Hosted dimensions: report aggregated usage at least hourly; target is within 2 hours of usage.
- Dedicated overage dimensions (if enabled): report daily; target within 24 hours.
- Backfill window: support at least 72 hours of late reporting for delayed event pipelines and reconciliation.
sections.heading: Reporting cadence and windows

sections.body:
Metering events must be idempotent. Requirements:
- Use a deterministic idempotency key per (entitlement, dimension, time_bucket) to prevent double charges on retries.
- Retry on transient errors (429, 5xx) with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Hard-fail and alert on repeated authorization errors (401/403) or malformed payloads.
sections.heading: Idempotency and retries

sections.body:
- Redwood internal billing meters remain the source of truth for customer-visible usage analytics in the console.
- Marketplace reporting is a downstream projection; discrepancies must be explainable via logs and time buckets.
- Persist a metering ledger entry for every reported bucket with: entitlement id, org id, dimension, quantity, bucket start/end, report timestamp, response status.
sections.heading: Source of truth and auditability

sections.body:
- Entitlement is ACTIVE, and
- Entitlement is linked to exactly one Redwood org (or an explicitly selected org in multi-org edge cases).
sections.heading: Usage must only be reported when

sections.body:
- Do not report usage.
- Console should show a blocking error with “Verify subscription” retry, and a path to support.
sections.heading: If entitlement is missing/unknown

sections.body:
- Compute tokens_in and tokens_out per request.
- Attribute usage to the request’s billing org.
- Resolve org → active gcp_entitlement_id.
- Aggregate into hourly buckets:
  - hosted_input_tokens_1k = ceil(sum(tokens_in) / 1000)
  - hosted_output_tokens_1k = ceil(sum(tokens_out) / 1000)

Rationale: rounding at the hourly bucket (not per request) reduces rounding error while keeping volume low.
sections.heading: Hosted: chat/text generation

sections.body:
- Use embedding_tokens (tokenizer-consistent token count).
- Aggregate hourly:
  - hosted_embeddings_1k_tokens = ceil(sum(embedding_tokens) / 1000)
sections.heading: Hosted: embeddings

sections.body:
- Count rerank_items as the number of documents/items scored.
- Aggregate hourly:
  - hosted_rerank_1k_items = ceil(sum(rerank_items) / 1000)
sections.heading: Hosted: rerank

sections.body:
Only applicable for offers that explicitly include burst overages.
- Measure burst_gpu_hours from scheduler/runtime utilization attribution (dedicated pool only).
- Aggregate daily:
  - dedicated_burst_gpu_hours = round(sum(burst_gpu_seconds) / 3600, 1)
sections.heading: Dedicated: burst usage

sections.body:
- Subscription add-ons (compliance/retention/support) should be represented as separate monthly subscription dimensions when supported by the plan structure.
- Do not attempt to meter add-ons by feature usage (e.g., “audit log exports”); keep procurement simple.
sections.heading: Add-ons

sections.body:
- Marketplace charges are issued by Google under the customer’s GCP billing account.
- Redwood usage in the console is near-real-time; Marketplace invoicing may lag due to reporting and billing cycles.
- Token usage is reported in 1K-token units (input and output separately).
- Customers can reconcile by comparing:
  - Console usage export (tokens_in/tokens_out by day)
  - Marketplace invoice line items for the corresponding dimensions
sections.heading: Customer-visible billing semantics (what Support/Sales can claim)

sections.body:
1) Confirm the entitlement id and billing org mapping (multi-subscription issues are the #1 cause).
2) Pull metering ledger entries for the disputed period (dimension + quantity + bucket timestamps).
3) Compare against console usage export for the same org and period.
4) If we under-reported: backfill within the allowed window.
5) If we over-reported due to duplication: identify duplicate idempotency key collision; coordinate correction path with Finance/Legal (see RevRec notes).
sections.heading: When a customer reports a mismatch

sections.body:
- Subscribe in GCP Marketplace test environment; entitlement becomes ACTIVE.
- Link entitlement to a new Redwood org and to an existing org (both paths).
- Generate traffic for each Hosted endpoint type (chat, embeddings, rerank).
- Verify within 2 hours:
  - Usage appears in Redwood console
  - Metering ledger has reported buckets
  - GCP Marketplace shows expected dimensions
- Negative tests:
  - Entitlement inactive → usage not reported
  - Retry storms (simulate 429/5xx) → no duplication
  - Entitlement propagation delay → onboarding guidance is correct
sections.heading: Testing checklist (pre-submission)

sections.body:
- Confirm final plan count and whether GCP listing will use separate plans per tier (Standard vs Enterprise) or a single plan with private offers.
- Confirm whether any Dedicated offers require overage dimensions at launch; default recommendation is “no” unless strongly requested by procurement.
- Confirm whether Premium Support is sold as a Marketplace add-on (monthly) or handled off-marketplace.
sections.heading: Open questions / follow-ups

sections.body:
Any changes to dimension names, units, or rounding rules require:
- Approval from Product (Packaging), Finance (RevRec), and Engineering (Billing/Metering)
- A migration plan that preserves backwards compatibility for existing Marketplace entitlements
- Update to customer-facing Marketplace FAQ + docs site pricing/packaging page
sections.heading: Change control

payload.page_title: Entropy-based fidelity credit allocator: product brief and rollout playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes the Entropy-Based Fidelity Credit Allocator (EFCA), a product component that dynamically assigns finite fidelity credits to tenant requests based on request entropy, service-level objectives (SLOs), and marginal economics. EFCA is intended to reduce customer-visible fidelity regressions while improving token cost efficiency across hosted and dedicated deployments.

This brief includes: rationale, allocation mechanics, API/contract examples, policy knobs, rollout plan, observability requirements, SLO impact analysis, and pricing examples.

Goals

- Protect response quality for high-information requests while reducing average per-token cost.
- Provide deterministic, auditable credit allocation that maps to existing billing/crediting systems.
- Enable gradual rollout with telemetry and regression guardrails.

Scope

- Applies to: hosted API and Dedicated (gateway layer). Not enabled for Private VPC until customer consent and contract amendment.
- Applies to fidelity-sensitive features: multishot chat, code generation, and structured output where fidelity materially affects correctness.
- Not a replacement for fidelity bundles or flat per-token pricing; EFCA augments existing bundles with behavior-driven credit steering.

Key definitions

- Fidelity credit: unit used by runtime to select higher-cost execution paths (larger model variant, less quantization, longer KV cache retention). One credit ~= 1 premium token-worth-of-cost in baseline economics.
- Request entropy: a scalar estimate of the information content of the request payload and context window (0..1). Higher entropy means more uncertain and high-value text.

Design principles

1. Signal-first: use robust, explainable signals (entropy, historical route fidelity, tenant fidelity SLAs).
2. Marginal economics: allocate credits where marginal improvement in quality justifies marginal token cost.
3. Auditable decisions: every allocation decision must emit an allocation record for billing and audits.

Allocation mechanics (high level)

1. Input signals per request: request_entropy, tenant_priority_score, route_fidelity_budget, recent_quality_trend, fallback_compatibility_flags.
2. Score = w_e * entropy + w_p * priority + w_q * quality_trend (weights configurable per tenant pool).
3. Compute marginal_expected_quality_gain(score) using an internal mapping model (calibrated by lab evals).
4. If marginal_expected_quality_gain * value_per_quality_point >= marginal_cost_of_credit, allocate N credits (0..max_per_request).

Policy knobs (examples)

- w_e, w_p, w_q: weights for entropy, priority, and quality trend (float).
- max_credits_per_request: integer cap (default 10).
- fallback_reserve: percentage of tenant daily credits reserved for emergency fallbacks (default 5%).
- entropy_thresholds: low/medium/high buckets that map to default allocation bands.

API and allocation record contract

Allocation is exposed as a synchronous pre-filter endpoint used by the routing/gateway layer. Contract (JSON example):

Request (POST /v1/allocator/allocate)
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "route": "chat.v1",
  "request_entropy": 0.73,
  "context_length": 2048,
  "priority": "standard",
  "recent_quality_trend": -0.02
}

Response
{
  "allocation_id": "alloc-20261014-abc",
  "credits_allocated": 4,
  "allocation_reason": "entropy_high_margin_positive",
  "predicted_quality_gain": 0.12,
  "estimated_extra_cost_tokens": 520,
  "expires_at": "2026-10-14T12:14:23Z"
}

Every allocation must produce an allocation record for billing and audit topics in the following minimal shape (pub/sub JSON string):
- allocation_id, tenant_id, route, credits_allocated, baseline_variant, allocated_variant, reason, marginal_cost_est, predicted_quality_gain, timestamp, trace_id

Configuration examples (gateway feature flag + tenant override)

1) Global feature flag (yaml):
features:
  efca_enabled: true
  efca_default_weights:
    w_e: 0.7
    w_p: 0.2
    w_q: 0.1
  efca_max_credits_per_request: 10

2) Tenant override (json stored in tenant config service):
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "efca_enabled": true,
  "weights": {"w_e":0.8, "w_p":0.15, "w_q":0.05},
  "max_credits": 6,
  "fallback_reserve_pct": 0.05
}

Observability and telemetry requirements

- Surface the following dashboards: allocation-rate, credits_consumed_per_tenant, average_predicted_quality_gain, allocation_reasons_breakdown, chargeback_estimate_by_route.
- Alert if: daily credits consumption > 120% of forecast, average_predicted_quality_gain drops below 0.03 for 24h, or allocation error rate > 0.5%.
- Add taggable traces: allocation_id and trace_id must propagate through gateway -> runtime -> billing pipeline.

SLO and gating criteria for rollout

- Quality regressions: no customer-facing drop > 5 percentage points in eval pass rate on critical prompt sets for any top-10 tenant during canary.
- Latency: pre-filter allocation latency must be < 12ms p95 in hosted mode. If allocation latency causes overall request p95 to exceed SLO by > 5%, disable synchronous allocation and fall back to sampled async allocation.
- Cost: predictable billing — forecasted marginal spend must be within +/- 10% of actual spend for the first 30 days for canary tenants.

Rollout plan (phased)

Phase 0: Lab (complete)
- Generate calibration datasets linking entropy to quality gains for target models and sequence lengths.
- Build mapping models and sanity checks.

Phase 1: Internal canary (2 weeks)
- Enabled for internal tenants and Redwood-owned demo accounts. Validate allocation records, telemetry, and billing pipeline.

Phase 2: Opt-in customer canary (4–6 weeks)
- Invite 5 customers across SMB and mid-market with different workload shapes. Collect objective evals (pre/post) and revenue impact. Baseline: 2M tokens/day combined.

Phase 3: Default-on for new tenants / opt-out for existing (8 weeks)
- Roll EFCA as default for new tenants. Provide easy tenant override and UI in Console.

Phase 4: Enterprise expansion and Private deployment consent (Q3-Q4)
- Offramp for regulated customers: EFCA can be disabled or run in dry-run mode with allocation records only.

Risk analysis and mitigations

- False positives (allocating credits where no quality improvement): Keep conservative mapping model and cap max_credits_per_request. Review high-frequency reasons.
- Billing disputes: Provide allocation record exports and a Console view of allocation decisions. Implement reconciliation job to compare estimated marginal cost vs actual billing.
- Latency impact: implement fast-path cache for recurring allocation decisions keyed by (tenant, route, entropy_bucket).

Pricing and billing ties

- EFCA does not change baseline token pricing. Instead, credits map to premium charge events. Billing schema: for each allocation record, emit a provisional charge_line with {tenant_id, allocation_id, estimated_extra_cost_tokens}. Final charge reconciled daily with actual runtime cost multipliers.
- Playbook for refunds: if predicted_quality_gain < 0.02 and estimated_extra_cost_tokens > 250, mark allocation as eligible for automated credit refund and notify tenant.

Examples (worked scenarios)

1) High-entropy code generation request
- entropy 0.92, tenant standard plan, predicted_quality_gain 0.18 -> allocate 8 credits -> runtime uses a less-quantized variant and extended KV retention -> customer sees fewer compile/regression failures.

2) Low-entropy routinized text completion
- entropy 0.12, predicted_quality_gain 0.01 -> allocate 0 credits -> cost saved, output identical quality.

Operational runbooks (short)

- Allocation spread spike (>200% of forecast): 1) notify billing and SRE, 2) set tenant-level throttle to cap daily credits, 3) enable aggressive entropy thresholds for 1 hour. Owner: billing (pager duty).
- Allocation endpoint errors >0.5%: 1) flip gate efca_enabled=false globally, 2) fail-open to 0 credits, 3) paged to runtime-oncall. Owner: eng-platform.

Open items and product decisions required

- Accounting model: reconcile provisional credit charges into token billing buckets vs new fidelity SKU. Decision owner: finance.
- Console UX: build allocation audit timeline in Console. Decision owner: DX/Product.
- Lab calibration cadence: re-evaluate mapping model quarterly or when new major model variant is onboarded. Owner: applied-ml.

Appendix: calibration example (pseudo)

- Lab eval summary mapping: for model variant A -> quality_gain per added credit approximated by a logistic curve fit on labeled evals.
- Example mapping table (excerpt):
| entropy_bucket | avg_quality_gain_per_credit | recommended_credits |
| low (0-0.33)   | 0.02                       | 0                      |
| medium (0.34-0.66)| 0.06                     | 2                      |
| high (0.67-1.0) | 0.15                       | 6                      |
