payload.page_title: Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products

sections.body:
This page defines Redwood Inference’s standard rules for **discounts** and **credits** for usage-based products (Hosted API, Dedicated burst/overages where applicable, and any token/embedding-based SKUs). The goals are:
- Protect revenue integrity and margin while enabling reasonable commercial flexibility.
- Ensure discounts/credits are **consistently applied to the same meters** customers see.
- Maintain **audit-ready** approval trails for RevRec (ASC 606) and internal controls.

This policy applies to all Redwood employees and contractors involved in quoting, contracting, billing, customer support remediation, and pricing experiments.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Hosted API usage SKUs (e.g., billed tokens, embeddings units, rerank units, request-based SKUs if/when used).
- Dedicated: usage-based components (e.g., burst GPU-seconds above commit) and one-time credits applied to invoices.
- Promotional/free-trial credits, contractually committed credits, and goodwill/service credits.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- Standard list pricing definition (see Pricing & Packaging overview pages).
- Non-usage products (e.g., fixed-fee Private platform licenses) except where explicitly included in an Order Form.
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
- **Meter / billable unit:** The unit recorded by billing telemetry and used to produce invoices. Example: **billed_tokens** for Hosted API.
- **Raw tokens vs billed tokens:** Raw tokens may include uncached or pre-dedupe counts. **Billed tokens** are the invoicing unit after billing rules (dedupe/idempotency, cache-hit attribution rules, etc.). Credits and discounts apply to **billed** usage only.
- **Discount:** A reduction in price per unit (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a percentage reduction on usage charges.
- **Credit:** A dollar value that offsets charges on invoices (a “coupon” balance). Credits have **no cash value** and are not refundable unless required by contract or law.
- **Service credit:** A credit issued for SLA/non-conformance or billing errors.
- **Promotional credit:** A credit granted for trial, marketing campaigns, partnerships, or sales incentives.
- **Contracted credit:** A credit explicitly included in an Order Form/MSA as part of commercial terms.
sections.heading: Definitions (use these terms consistently)

sections.body:
1. **All discounting and credits must be recorded in systems of record** (Deal/Account + Billing) and have an approver trail.
2. **No retroactive price changes** to already-invoiced usage without Finance + Legal approval and a documented RevRec assessment.
3. **Credits apply to billed usage as computed by billing meters** (not customer-estimated counts).
4. **Discount stacking is limited** (see “Stacking rules”). Any exception is an exception request.
5. Credits must have an **expiry date** unless explicitly waived by Finance (rare; requires CFO approval).
6. Any term that could be interpreted as “free usage” must include a clear definition of **the exact meter(s)** and the application order (see “Contract language requirements”).
sections.heading: Policy summary (non-negotiables)

sections.body:
- Must be implemented via standard plan configuration.
- Must be accessible/consistent across similarly situated customers in that plan tier.
- Any deviation from published plan discounting is treated as a **commercial exception**.
sections.heading: A) Public/self-serve plan discounts

sections.body:
- **Unit price override** for specific meter(s) (preferred).
- **Percent discount** applied to usage subtotal (acceptable only if explicitly tied to the same meter set).
- **Tiered volume pricing** by monthly usage (requires Product + Finance review because it changes packaging).

Not allowed without CFO + GC approval:
- “Most favored pricing” commitments.
- Open-ended “meet/beat competitor” clauses.
- Retroactive price matching.
sections.heading: Allowed structures

sections.body:
- Must have a defined start/end date.
- Must define what happens after the promotion ends (auto-revert to list/contract rate).
sections.heading: C) Time-bounded promotional discount

sections.body: Purpose: reduce onboarding friction or enable evaluation.
sections.heading: 1) Promotional / trial credits

sections.body:
- Default expiry: **90 days** from grant date.
- Not transferable; not redeemable for cash.
- Intended to offset **usage charges** only; cannot offset fixed recurring platform fees unless explicitly approved.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: Purpose: negotiated commercial term.
sections.heading: 2) Contracted credits (Order Form)

sections.body:
- Must be explicitly stated in the Order Form: amount, expiry, eligible meters, and application order.
- Finance must confirm RevRec treatment before signature (variable consideration constraints).
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: Purpose: remediation for SLA incidents, billing disputes, or significant product issues.
sections.heading: 3) Service / goodwill credits

sections.body:
- Must reference an incident/ticket and include a rationale and calculation.
- Expiry default: **12 months** (unless customer requires shorter/longer; Finance approval needed).
- Should not be used to “quietly” replace missing product functionality; escalate to Product leadership if recurring.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
Unless otherwise specified in the Order Form, credits apply to:
- Hosted API: **billed_tokens** (prompt + completion, including tool/structured output tokens per meter spec)
- Embeddings: **billed_embedding_units** (per embeddings meter definition)
- Rerank: **billed_rerank_units**

Credits do **not** apply to:
- Taxes, regulatory fees, or pass-through charges
- Dedicated reserved commits (monthly minimums), unless explicitly stated
- One-time professional services fees
sections.heading: Eligible meters

sections.body:
On each invoice, the billing system applies adjustments in this order:
1. **Included usage** in the customer’s package/free tier (if applicable)
2. **Contracted unit prices** (including any negotiated discount)
3. **Credits** (promotional/contracted/service), applied to the eligible usage subtotal
4. Taxes and non-creditable line items

Important: credits offset charges; they do **not change recorded usage quantities**.
sections.heading: Application order (standard)

sections.body: If the meter spec distinguishes cached vs uncached billed tokens, credits apply to the final **billed** quantities after cache and dedupe logic. Any customer-visible statement about caching must use approved language from Legal (see related page).
sections.heading: Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens

sections.body:
- Discounts for Dedicated should generally be expressed as changes to **commit level** or **unit price for burst usage** (if burst is enabled).
- Credits may be applied to burst usage invoices or as an invoice-level service credit.
- Credits should not be used to effectively reduce a committed minimum without Finance approval; that changes contract economics and RevRec.
sections.heading: Dedicated usage: credits and discounts

sections.body:
- Default: **one commercial discount** (unit price override or percent discount) may be active per meter at a time.
- Promotional credits may coexist with negotiated unit pricing.
- Additional stacking (e.g., unit price override + invoice percent discount + marketing credits) requires an exception approval.
sections.heading: Stacking rules

sections.body:
- Promotional/trial credits: **90 days**
- Service credits: **12 months**
- Contracted credits: as negotiated, but must be specified
sections.heading: Default expiry

sections.body:
- Expired credits cannot be reinstated without CFO approval.
- Credits are non-refundable. Any customer request for refund/cash equivalent must be routed to Legal + Finance.
sections.heading: Expiry handling

sections.body: Expired unused credits may have accounting implications (breakage). Finance will determine treatment based on credit type and contract terms. Do not promise outcomes to customers.
sections.heading: Breakage and RevRec note

sections.body:
This section is not a full accounting memo; it lists operational requirements.
- **Discounts and contracted credits** are part of the arrangement consideration and can affect transaction price.
- **Service credits** related to SLA or service shortfalls are generally treated as a reduction of revenue (contra revenue) for the impacted period/customer.
- Any material change to pricing terms (including credits granted outside standard policy) may require:
  - A RevRec assessment (materiality, variable consideration constraint)
  - A contract modification evaluation
  - Documentation for auditors (who approved, why, and when)

Finance owner for RevRec decisions: **Emily Stone**. Escalate early if the proposed adjustment is large or spans multiple months.
sections.heading: Revenue recognition (ASC 606) guidance (operational)

sections.body:
Any Order Form/MSA language that introduces discounts or credits must specify:
- Credit amount (USD) and whether it is promotional/contracted/service
- Expiry date and non-transferability
- Eligible products/meters (e.g., billed_tokens)
- Application order (what it offsets; whether it can offset fixed fees)
- Dispute window and billing dispute process

Use the clause library and approved definitions in: **Usage-based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook**.
Legal owner: **Sofia Mendes**. Do not draft “custom” credit language in email.
sections.heading: Contract language requirements (must-haves)

sections.body:
Approvals are required **before** sending a quote/Order Form, and before issuing credits that affect an invoice (unless covered by pre-approved support remediation bands).

Table: Approval requirements (minimum)

| Change type | Threshold (USD impact) | Who can approve | Required documentation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Unit price discount (standard band) | <= $25k ARR equivalent or <= 10% effective discount | CRO (Jordan Blake) + Finance delegate (FP&A) | Deal record + pricing rationale |
| Unit price discount (non-standard) | > 10% or impacts gross margin model | CFO (Laura Bennett) + CRO | Deal record + margin impact summary |
| Promotional/trial credits | <= $10k total per account per quarter | CRO or CPO delegate + Finance delegate | Deal record + campaign/justification |
| Promotional/trial credits | > $10k per quarter | CFO + CRO | Written justification + expected conversion plan |
| Service credits (billing dispute / SLA) | <= $5k per invoice | Support manager + Finance (RevRec) | Support ticket + incident/billing evidence |
| Service credits | > $5k per invoice or retroactive beyond 1 billing cycle | CFO + GC (Michael Grant) + RevRec | RevRec assessment + legal review |
| Any retroactive repricing (changing unit rates for past usage) | Any | CFO + GC + RevRec | RevRec memo + customer comms plan |
sections.heading: Approval matrix (discounts and credits)

sections.body:
- “ARR equivalent” is computed from trailing 30-day usage annualized at proposed pricing.
- Pricing experiments may have separate pre-approvals; see experiment guardrails pages. Individual exceptions within experiments still require documentation.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
For every discount/credit, record:
- Account name, billing account ID, and contract/Order Form reference
- Adjustment type (discount vs credit) and subtype (promotional/contracted/service)
- Amount (USD) and expiry
- Eligible products/meters
- Approver(s) and date
- Rationale and links to supporting evidence (ticket, incident, email approval)
sections.heading: What must be recorded

sections.body:
- **HubSpot** (Deal/Company): store commercial terms summary and attach approvals.
- **Billing system** (ledger/credits module): create the credit grant with expiry and eligibility flags.
- **Support system (Jira)**: for service credits, link the customer ticket to the credit grant ID.
- **Confluence**: if the exception sets a precedent or affects policy, add a short addendum under “Exception log” below.
sections.heading: Where to record

sections.body:
Use this process for anything outside the policy (stacking beyond rules, unusual expiry, retroactive adjustments, meter-specific carve-outs, etc.).

1. Create an exception request (HubSpot note + internal ticket). Include:
   - Proposed term(s)
   - Estimated $ impact and customer rationale
   - Whether it changes past invoices
   - Whether it changes which meters are eligible
2. Obtain approvals per matrix (Finance + GTM; Legal if contract language changes).
3. Finance/RevRec confirms accounting treatment if needed.
4. Implement:
   - Update Order Form language (if contracted)
   - Configure billing (credit grant / rate override)
   - Notify Support/CS of customer-facing explanation
5. Verify on **invoice preview** before sending to customer.
sections.heading: Exception process

sections.body:
- Never promise that Redwood will “match their internal token counts.” Instead explain billed vs raw tokens and provide usage exports.
- Avoid implying that caching “doesn’t count”; use the approved caching language.
- For disputes, acknowledge the concern, provide the reconciliation approach, and if issuing a service credit, describe it as a one-time remediation.
sections.heading: Customer communication guidelines (internal)

sections.body:
- Grant: $2,000 promotional credit, expires in 90 days
- Eligible: Hosted API billed_tokens + embeddings units
- Unit pricing: standard list
- Expected outcome: offset first month’s overage during onboarding
sections.heading: Example 1: Promotional credit for a POC

sections.body:
- Trigger: confirmed double-counting bug for streaming retries
- Remediation: credit equal to overbilled amount for the impacted invoice period
- Required: Support ticket, query evidence, RevRec sign-off, and customer communication stating the credit is specific to the identified issue
sections.heading: Example 2: Service credit for metering bug impact

sections.body: - 2026-02-22: Clarified that credits apply to **billed tokens** (post-dedupe/cache attribution) to align with meter hardening work and reduce invoice disputes. Owner: Finance/RevRec.
sections.heading: Exception log (policy-impacting only)

sections.body:
- Finance policy owner: **Laura Bennett (CFO)**
- RevRec/accounting owner: **Emily Stone**
- Legal language owner: **Sofia Mendes** (Commercial), **Michael Grant** (GC)
- GTM owner: **Jordan Blake (CRO)**
- Product owner (Hosted API pricing/metering): **Nikhil Sharma**
sections.heading: Owners and escalation

sections.body:
- A customer requests retroactive repricing, refund, or cash payout.
- A proposed discount/credit changes meter definitions or conflicts with published usage definitions.
- The adjustment is large enough to be material or would set a precedent.
sections.heading: Escalate immediately if

payload.page_title: Consumption prepaid collateral bundles & trial mechanisms (product brief)

sections.body:
Summary

This brief defines the product concept, requirements, and rollout plan for a new pricing construct: prepaid collateral bundles (PCB) that customers purchase as locked credits to cover reserved capacity, burstable consumption, and trial allowances. The goal is to provide customers predictable economics for adoption, protect Redwood from uncollectible usage, and enable frictionless trials with configurable safety controls.

Goals

- Enable predictable short-to-medium term revenue by letting customers prepay for capacity or credit pools.
- Reduce fraud/chargeback exposure for large trial activations and high-burst customers.
- Make trials and onboarding smooth: automatic trial-to-paid conversion with configurable grace periods.
- Provide clear UX and reconciliation pathways so finance and customer success can explain charges.

Scope

In scope: design of PCB SKUs, API surface for creating/redeeming collateral bundles, billing reconciliation logic, UI flows for sales and self-serve, rules for expiration/refunds, SLOs and telemetry.
Out of scope: wholesale changes to invoicing cadence, international tax treatment (handled by existing billing stack), on-prem private deployment billing connectors (future phase).

Definitions

- Collateral bundle (CB): a purchasable item representing prepaid credits (token-credits + optional reserved capacity hours).
- Collateral ledger: immutable event log of deposits, redemptions, refunds, and expirations.
- Trial collateral: temporary CB granted to new customers for evaluation; tracked separately for conversion rules.
- Reserved capacity carveout: portion of a CB that guarantees dedicated capacity for a time window.

High-level product hypothesis

If customers can prepay collateral in discrete bundles with clear conversion rules and guardrails, we will increase early revenue recognition, reduce overage disputes, and increase conversion from trial to paid usage while limiting exposure to high-cost bursts.

Requirements (PRD style)

1) SKU model and UI
  - 3 initial SKUs: Starter-CB (100k tokens), Grow-CB (1M tokens + 10 reserved GPU-hours), Enterprise-CB (5M tokens + 100 reserved GPU-hours).
  - Each SKU has: price_usd, token_quantity, optional_reserved_capacity_hours, expiration_days, refundable_percent.
  - UI: Billing > Prepaid Credits page to purchase, view balance, and configure auto-topup thresholds.

2) API surface (stable public endpoints)
  - POST /v1/bundles.create => create collateral bundle (payment & ledger entry)
  - GET /v1/bundles/{id} => retrieve bundle metadata and remaining balance
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/redeem => redeem credits for request (internal use by runtime router)
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/convert => convert trial collateral to paid order (on acceptance)
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/refund => issue refund according to refundable_percent and policy
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
{
    "sku": "Grow-CB",
    "customer_id": "acct_01Gq2x...",
    "payment_method_id": "pm_0a1b2c",
    "metadata": { "sales_rep": "sr-122" }
  }

3) Runtime integration and prioritized routing
  - Router must accept an optional header X-Prepaid-Bundle: {bundle_id} to consume from a specific CB.
  - If a request cannot be fulfilled due to reserved capacity limits, runtime should fall back per routing policy (e.g., use hosted pool and mark as overage against CB if allowed).
  - Redemption semantics: atomic decrement of token count and reserved hour counters, with idempotency and optimistic locking.

4) Reconciliation and ledger
  - All bundle events generate ledger entries: DEPOSIT, REDEEM, EXPIRE, REFUND, CONVERT.
  - Daily reconciliation job aggregates ledger to billing invoices and posts to AR system. Jobs must be idempotent and have auditable run logs.

5) Trials and conversion rules
  - Trial CBs: expire in 30 days, refundable_percent = 0, conversion window = 72 hours after trial acceptance.
  - Auto-convert behavior (opt-in): if trial usage exceeds threshold (e.g., 75% of trial tokens), optionally create a paid Grow-CB and apply remaining usage to it.

6) Refund & expiration policy
  - Prepaid collateral expires after expiration_days; default = 365 days for paid SKUs.
  - Refunds allowed within 14 days for self-serve; refunds incur 2% processing fee + prorated usage deduction. Enterprise refundable_percent is negotiable.

7) Accounting & revenue recognition notes (for finance)
  - Use deferred revenue accounting: deposit -> liability; redeem -> recognized revenue based on usage mapping by day. Provide daily export CSV with ledger events.

8) Telemetry & SLOs
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly for bundles APIs.
  - Runtime redemption latency: 95th percentile < 20ms when bundle header present.
  - Reconciliation run success rate: daily job must succeed 7/7 days per week; any missed run triggers oncall paging for finance oncall.
  - Metrics to emit: bundle_deposits, bundle_redemptions, bundle_refunds, bundle_expirations, avg_redeem_latency_ms.

Design details (Design Spec highlights)

- Authorization model: bundles belong to customers; bundle_id can be scoped to an API key or tenant. Only authorized service accounts may redeem reserved_capacity hours.
- Atomic redemption: implement via single-row DB transaction with version column to avoid double-spend (SQL pseudo):
  UPDATE prepaid_bundles SET token_balance = token_balance - :tokens_requested, version = version + 1 WHERE id = :id AND version = :expected_version AND token_balance >= :tokens_requested;
- Fallback rules: define per-bundle policy flags: allow_overage (boolean), prioritize_reserved (boolean). If allow_overage=false and reserved capacity exhausted, return HTTP 429 with error code PREPAID_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED.

UX flows

1) Self-serve purchase
  - Customer clicks Buy > selects SKU > enters payment > purchase completes > bundle deposit credited and visible in Billing UI.
  - UI shows countdown for expiration and breakdown (tokens vs reserved hours).

2) Sales-assisted onboarding
  - Sales creates ephemeral trial CB via Sales Console with trial flags and fixed conversion options. CSM monitors trial usage and triggers conversion playbook if adoption signals pass.

3) Trial-to-paid conversion (playbook)
  - If customer requests conversion, use POST /v1/bundles/{trial_id}/convert which will attempt to create an equivalent paid CB and mark trial CB as converted. Notify finance and CSM.

Rollout plan and milestones

Phase 0 (Q3 2026) - Design & API MVP
  - Finalize SKU definitions and edge-case policies.
  - Implement bundles.create and bundles.get, minimal UI for Billing > Prepaid Credits.
  - Enable trial CB creation via Sales Console only.
  - Telemetry instrumentation for redemption latency and deposit counts.

Phase 1 (Q4 2026) - Runtime integration & self-serve
  - Runtime redemption integration and X-Prepaid-Bundle header support.
  - Self-serve purchase flow and auto-topup UI.
  - Reconciliation export to finance in CSV format.

Phase 2 (Q1 2027) - Enterprise features
  - Refund negotiation flow, invoiced purchase support, and reserved capacity SLA add-ons.
  - Advanced reporting dashboards for CSM/Finance.

Operational runbook (high level)

- Pager triggers: reconciliation failure, daily job misses, unusually high redemption error rate (>0.5% of redeems failing due to DB conflicts), or API error rate spike >3% sustained 5 min.
- Troubleshooting steps:
  1) Check ledger job logs in /jobs/recon and restart job with dry-run flag.
  2) Validate DB replica lag; if lag > 30s, route to infra and pause redemptions for safety.
  3) If double-spend suspected, run diff of ledger vs runtime redemption events and reconcile manually.

Security and compliance notes

- All billing and sensitive payment metadata is stored in PCI-compliant payment gateway; Redwood stores only bundle metadata and ledger events (no raw card data).
- Audit logs: every bundle API call must include caller_id and be logged to long-term audit storage (retention 7 years for enterprise customers on request).

Business & commercial considerations

- Pricing sensitivity experiments: run A/B tests on refundable_percent and expiration_days to measure conversion uplift vs revenue leakage.
- Accounting conservative default: if in doubt, mark expired prepaid as unredeemable after 365 days; sales can negotiate exceptions via ticketing.

Open questions (to resolve before Phase 0 dev kickoff)

- Long-tail SKUs: should we allow custom SKU builder in UI or require Sales to request engineering?
- Cross-tenant redemption: allow child-workspaces to share a single CB? (enterprise asked for this).
- Tax handling & regional pricing: require finance sign-off for multi-currency SKUs.

Ownership and contacts

- Product lead: Maya Chen (product)
- Engineering lead: Daniel Ruiz (eng-platform)
- Finance liaison: Sofia Alvarez (finance-legal)
- CSM lead: Priya Nair (customer-success)

Next steps

1) Review this brief with finance and legal by 2026-08-22.
2) Finalize SKU pricing sheet and publish to internal pricing catalog.
3) Kick off API design sprint (2 weeks) and schedule runtime integration spike.

Appendix
sections.heading: Example create request (JSON)

sections.body:
- date, bundle_id, customer_id, event_type, tokens_delta, reserved_hours_delta, balance_tokens, balance_reserved_hours, ledger_sequence_id

FAQ

Q: Can bundles be transferred between accounts?
A: Not in Phase 1. Transfer requests require sales/finance manual process.

Q: What happens if a bundle purchase charge fails after deposit was created?
A: Create attempts are idempotent; failed payments roll back the DEPOSIT event and create a FAILED_DEPOSIT entry for diagnostics.

payload.page_title: AWS Marketplace Offer Structure (Redwood Inference) — Offer Types, Dimensions, Metering, and Submission Artifacts

sections.body:
This page documents how Redwood Inference is packaged and sold via **AWS Marketplace**, including:
- Supported **offer types** (public + private offers)
- **Contract and usage dimensions** used for pricing and billing
- How we implement **AWS metering and entitlements**
- A checklist of **required AWS submission fields and attachments**

This is the source of truth for Partnerships/GTM, Product, Billing Engineering, and Finance/Legal during offer creation and marketplace submissions.

---
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body: Redwood Inference is offered on AWS Marketplace as a **SaaS** product (not AMI or container image distribution).
sections.heading: Scope (AWS Marketplace)

sections.body:
1) **Public offer** for self-serve usage-based procurement (Hosted).
2) **Private offer** for negotiated terms (committed spend, enterprise add-ons, and Dedicated/Private deployments).
sections.heading: We support the following purchasing motions

sections.body:
- Distributing the inference runtime as an AMI/EKS add-on via Marketplace (packaging handled via Redwood Private contracting; Marketplace can be used for procurement/invoicing only).

---
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body: AWS supports multiple pricing models for SaaS. We use two, depending on SKU.
sections.heading: AWS Marketplace offer types we use

sections.body:
**When to use:**
- PLG + procurement-friendly motion for Redwood Hosted API
- Customers who want to pay via AWS bill without negotiating custom terms

**Pricing model:**
- Usage-based (metered)

**Customer experience:**
- Customer subscribes in AWS Marketplace
- Redirected to Redwood registration/fulfillment URL
- Redwood validates the AWS subscription and provisions/links the Redwood org
- Usage is metered to AWS Marketplace based on consumption

**Notes:**
- Public offers must be simple and unambiguous. Minimize dimension count.
- Avoid claims that require qualification (e.g., “lowest cost”) in listing copy.
sections.heading: 1) Public offer (standard listing)

sections.body:
**When to use:**
- Enterprise procurement requiring negotiated discounts, payment terms, or commitments
- Dedicated capacity reservations
- Redwood Private licensing + support/compliance add-ons

**Pricing model options we use:**
- Contract (committed spend) with dimensions for prepaid units
- Usage-based (metered) + negotiated rates/discounts (if required)
- Hybrid structures (committed + overage) when contractually necessary

**Notes for private offers:**
- Private offers should map to internally-supported meters and limits.
- Ensure the subscription still provisions correctly via the same fulfillment flow.
- All negotiated terms must be approved per discount and legal guardrails.

---
sections.heading: 2) Private offers (negotiated)

sections.body:
- **Hosted (Redwood API):** usage-based
- **Dedicated:** contract + (optional) usage add-ons; entitlements represent capacity reservation and included tokens
- **Private (VPC/on-prem):** contract; procurement/invoicing via AWS, delivery via Redwood (not AWS infrastructure)

AWS Marketplace listings/offers must remain consistent with the SKU catalog in:
- `marketplace-sku-catalog-v2`

---
sections.heading: We align AWS Marketplace packaging to Redwood product lines

sections.body:
AWS Marketplace billing requires **dimensions** (named line items) that are either:
- **Metered** (reported via AWS Marketplace Metering Service), or
- **Entitlement/contract units** (granted via AWS entitlements for a contract term)
sections.heading: Dimensions: AWS contract + metered usage

sections.body:
1) **Mirror internal meters.** A dimension must map cleanly to a Redwood billing meter.
2) **Prefer token-based units.** Use tokens/embeddings as the primary unit for Hosted.
3) **Limit dimension count.** Too many dimensions increases buyer confusion and mapping errors.
4) **Separate add-ons only when needed.** Only split compliance/support/retention into separate dimensions when it is required for procurement or revenue recognition.
5) **Avoid “unmeterable” promises.** Dedicated/Private still needs a measurable commercial unit (commit units, capacity reservation units, or platform license units).

---
sections.heading: Dimension design principles

sections.body: The exact dimension IDs/names must match the AWS product configuration and internal billing catalog identifiers.
sections.heading: Standard dimensions (current)

sections.body:
| Dimension (AWS) | Unit | Internal meter | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `hosted_input_tokens` | 1K tokens | `hosted.tokens.input` | Metered. Includes prompt/system/user tokens. |
| `hosted_output_tokens` | 1K tokens | `hosted.tokens.output` | Metered. Includes assistant tokens. |
| `hosted_embeddings` | 1K embedding units | `hosted.embeddings.units` | Metered. Used for embedding endpoints. |
| `hosted_rerank_units` | 1K rerank units | `hosted.rerank.units` | Metered. For reranking models/routes. |
sections.heading: Hosted (usage-based) — Public offer

sections.body: - If we must reduce dimensions for AWS simplicity, we can collapse to `hosted_tokens_total` (input+output), but this reduces transparency and may conflict with internal pricing levers.
sections.heading: Guidance

sections.body:
Dedicated is primarily sold as a reservation/commit. In AWS Marketplace this is represented as contract dimensions.

| Dimension (AWS) | Unit | Internal mapping | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `dedicated_commit_units` | $1 of commit | `commit.usd` | Contract dimension. Represents committed spend applied to usage on the dedicated pool. |
| `dedicated_capacity_reservation` | 1 reservation | `dedicated.reservation` | Optional. Used only when buyer requires line-item capacity reservation. |
| `dedicated_overage_tokens` | 1K tokens | `dedicated.tokens.overage` | Optional metered dimension if contract allows overage beyond commit. |
sections.heading: Dedicated (reserved capacity) — Private offers

sections.body:
- Prefer **commit-only** + internal enforcement of included usage when possible.
- Use overage dimension only if the private offer explicitly permits it.
sections.heading: Guidance

sections.body:
Private is licensed; delivery is Redwood-controlled. AWS Marketplace is used as the procurement channel.

| Dimension (AWS) | Unit | Internal mapping | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `private_platform_license` | 1 license-month | `private.license.month` | Contract dimension. Covers control plane/runtime license. |
| `private_support_tier` | 1 support-month | `support.tier.month` | Contract dimension. If support must be separated for procurement. |
| `compliance_addon` | 1 addon-month | `addon.compliance.month` | Optional. Only if sold separately. |
sections.heading: Private (VPC/on-prem) — Private offers

sections.body:

---
sections.heading: Guidance

sections.body:
1) **Subscribe:** Customer subscribes to the AWS Marketplace product/offer.
2) **Fulfillment:** AWS redirects to Redwood’s fulfillment URL with customer identifiers.
3) **Entitlement check:** Redwood verifies subscription/contract entitlements and links them to a Redwood org.
4) **Usage:** Customer uses Redwood API/Console as normal.
5) **Metering:** Redwood reports usage to AWS Marketplace (for metered dimensions) and enforces entitlements/contract constraints.
sections.heading: High-level flow

sections.body:
- **AWS Marketplace Entitlement Service**
  - Used to fetch contract entitlements for a given customer + product code.
  - Redwood caches entitlements with periodic sync and on-demand re-check during provisioning.

- **AWS Marketplace Metering Service**
  - Used to submit hourly/daily usage records per dimension.
  - Redwood’s billing pipeline aggregates usage events and posts metering records with idempotency keys.
sections.heading: AWS services used

sections.body:
- **Entitlement Sync Job**
  - Pull-based sync of AWS entitlements to Redwood’s billing catalog.
  - Requirements: retries, idempotency, and alerting for propagation delays.

- **Marketplace Entitlement Verification API**
  - Called by Console onboarding to validate subscription status.
  - Returns actionable error codes (e.g., subscription not found, pending propagation, already linked).

- **Billing Dimension Mapper**
  - Canonical mapping from AWS dimension name → Redwood internal meter.
  - Must be versioned and tested; mismatches cause buyer billing confusion and support escalations.
sections.heading: Redwood internal components (names used in engineering/docs)

sections.body:
- Default cadence: **hourly aggregation**, with backfill support for late events.
- Idempotency: use a deterministic key per (customer, dimension, hour window).
- Rounding: report units in **1K token increments** (rounded up per hour window) unless contract requires a different policy.
sections.heading: Metering frequency and aggregation

sections.body:
- **Entitlement propagation delay:** show “Try again in a few minutes” + provide a retry button and support link.
- **Metering submission errors:** retry with exponential backoff; alert if error budget exceeded.
- **Dimension mismatch:** block metering submission and page Billing Eng; do not silently remap.
sections.heading: Failure modes and expected handling

sections.body:
- 99.9% of metering records submitted within 6 hours of usage window close.
- <1% of new subscriptions experience provisioning delay >15 minutes due to entitlement sync.

payload.page_title: Customer Fidelity Credit Portability Framework

sections.body:
Purpose and scope

This document describes the Customer Fidelity Credit Portability Framework: the rules, primitives, and operational playbooks that allow customers to transfer, convert, or reconcile fidelity credits (promotional, escrowed, or purchased) between Redwood deployment surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and across billing constructs. The framework targets commerce and product teams, billing engineers, and solutions engineers enabling predictable customer migrations and minimal friction for enterprise transitions.

Goals

- Reduce friction for customers migrating workloads between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private by providing predictable credit handling.
- Ensure correct accounting and minimal financial exposure for Redwood.
- Provide deterministic UX and API primitives for credit visibility, conversion, and rollback.
- Minimize manual billing operations and exception cases.

Non-goals

- This doc does not replace contract-level legal terms for enterprise discounts or bespoke financial instruments.
- It does not define new pricing tiers; it defines mapping and operational rules for credit portability only.

Definitions and primitives

- Fidelity Credit: A unit representing monetary or usage value issued to a customer that can be applied toward Redwood consumption. Types: Promotional, Escrowed, Purchased, Insurance Credits.
- Portability: Movement of credit value between account constructs (e.g., hosted account -> dedicated tenant) without changing the underlying monetary backing unless conversion occurs.
- Conversion Rate: A deterministic multiplier used when mapping credit value across different pricing surfaces to reflect differing unit economics (e.g., hosted per-token price vs dedicated reserved capacity).
- Escrow Bucket: Temporary holding state for credits pending migration, approval, or reconciliation.

High-level portability modes

1) Direct Pass-through
   - Credits remain denominated in Redwood currency and are moved 1:1 between account constructs.
   - Use-case: Small customers moving between hosted sub-accounts under the same billing entity.
   - Constraints: Only allowed when pricing tiers and entitlement structures match.

2) Conversion-on-Move
   - Credits are converted using an agreed conversion rate at the time of migration.
   - Use-case: Hosted (per-token) credits converted to Dedicated capacity credits or vice versa.
   - Conversion is timestamped and recorded for audit.

3) Escrow-with-Approval
   - Credits are placed in an Escrow Bucket pending finance approval when policy or contract deviations are detected.
   - Use-case: Customer with promotional credits tied to Hosted wants to move to Private where legal/compliance prevents full pass-through.

Conversion model and formulas

- Conversion must be deterministic. The canonical conversion formula: converted_value = original_value * conversion_multiplier - conversion_fee
- Conversion multiplier is determined by lookup table (managed in Pricing Catalog service) keyed by (from_surface, to_surface, date).
- Conversion_fee is applied only when the portability causes a measurable economic delta (e.g., converting promotional credits into committed capacity).

Pricing catalog sample (table)

From | To | Multiplier | Fee
-----|----|------------|-----
Hosted (per-token) | Dedicated (reserved credits) | 0.85 | $0.00 (applied by default)
Hosted | Private (on-prem credit) | 0.70 | $0.00 (requires legal approval)
Purchased bundle | Hosted | 1.00 | $0.00
Escrowed promotional | Any | variable | subject to approval

(Notes: Applied multipliers are reviewed quarterly by Pricing Ops; fees may be negotiated for large enterprise transfers.)

Audit and accounting guarantees

- Every portability transaction creates a signed ledger entry with fields: transaction_id, customer_id, source_bucket, destination_bucket, original_amount, conversion_multiplier, converted_amount, operator_id, timestamp, and policy_id.
- Ledger entries are immutable and stored for minimum 7 years per finance policy.

Customer UX and API primitives

- Console flow: "Migrate credits" modal available on Billing -> Credits page for eligible accounts. Steps: 1) Select source bucket, 2) Select destination surface, 3) Preview conversion (shows multiplier, fees), 4) Acknowledge terms, 5) Initiate migration.
- API: POST /v1/billing/credits/migrate {source_bucket_id, destination_surface, amount, metadata} -> returns migration_preview_id and estimated_conversion. POST /v1/billing/credits/migrate/confirm {migration_preview_id} -> executes migration.
- Webhooks: credit_migration.requested, credit_migration.completed, credit_migration.rejected.

Operational playbooks

1) Self-serve migration (automated)
   - Preconditions: customer has single billing entity, no security/legal constraints, conversion multiplier defined, projected converted_amount <= $250k.
   - Steps: 1) Customer initiates via console or API; 2) System validates entitlements and pricing mappings; 3) System executes conversion and emits webhooks; 4) Customer receives final invoice adjustment if needed.

2) Escrow and manual approval
   - Preconditions: cross-entity move, legal constraints, high-value (> $250k), or promotional credits flagged as non-portable.
   - Steps: 1) Credits moved into Escrow Bucket with status=PENDING_APPROVAL; 2) Notifications to Finance and Legal; 3) Review with customer; 4) Approve -> execute conversion or Reject -> return credits to origin with audit note.

3) Rollback and dispute handling
   - If a post-migration reconciliation detects a mismatch, the system supports: automatic rollback (if within 72 hours and destination usage < 10% of migrated credits) or dispute workflow (Finance case created, customer credited pending resolution).

Edge cases and guardrails

- Multi-tenant mappings: Individual sub-account credits cannot be ported across top-level billing accounts without written authorization.
- Time-bounded promos: Promotional credits with expiry shorter than 90 days are non-portable by default.
- Negative balance protection: Conversion cannot create negative reserved capacity entitlements. Any residual shortfall triggers an invoice event.
- Tax and regulatory: Movement of credits that change tax treatment require Finance sign-off; Private/on-prem transfers typically require additional compliance checks.

Telemetry and observability

Instrument all migration flows with the following metrics: credit_migration_attempts, credit_migration_success, credit_migration_fail_reason, average_conversion_multiplier, escrow_pending_count. Provide per-customer logs and an aggregated weekly dashboard in Redwood Console (Billing -> Credit Portability).

Policies and approval matrix

- Auto-approve threshold: <= $250k and same billing entity.
- Finance review threshold: > $250k and <= $2M.
- Executive/Legal review: > $2M or cross-jurisdiction movement to Private/on-prem.

Implementation plan and milestones (Q4 2026 -> Q1 2027)

1) Q4 2026 (Pilot)
   - Implement conversion catalog and immutable ledger.
   - Expose API preview endpoint and console migration modal (alpha).
   - Run pilot with 3 enterprise customers migrating Hosted->Dedicated.
2) Q1 2027 (General availability)
   - Add escrow approval workflow, notification plumbing (Slack + email), and webhooks.
   - Integrate with billing engine and reconciliation jobs.
3) Q2 2027 (Scale & compliance)
   - Support Private/on-prem transfers with legal workflow templates and multi-jurisdiction tax handling.

Rollout checklist for launch

- [ ] Conversion catalog seeded for top 10 SKUs.
- [ ] Console preview + confirm modal QAed and accessibility tested.
- [ ] API contract versioned and documented in developer docs.
- [ ] Escrow notification runbook created and routed to Finance and Legal channels.
- [ ] Audit retention storage provisioned and encryption validated.

Open questions and decision points

- Should conversion multipliers decay over time to reflect pricing changes, or remain snapshot-based at migration time? Recommended: snapshot-based with clear timestamps.
- What is the appropriate commercial rebate (if any) for customers who initiated migration within 30 days of a major pricing change? Finance to propose a template.

Appendix: Example migration transcript (Hosted -> Dedicated)

1) Customer requests migration of $100,000 hosted credits to Dedicated.
2) Pricing catalog multiplier for date 2026-11-01 is 0.85. Estimated converted credits = $85,000 equivalent reserved capacity.
3) System creates ledger entry TX-20261101-0001, moves funds, emits webhooks.
4) Customer consumes Dedicated capacity; monthly reconciler validates usage and final invoice adjusts for residual rounding differences.

Contacts and owners

- Product owner: Maya Chen (product)
- Billing engineering: Diego Ramirez (engineering)
- Finance liaison: Anika Patel (finance-legal)
- Legal: Ethan Lowe (legal)

Related artifacts and links

- Pricing catalog location: /internal/pricing/catalog (read-only)
- Billing engine runbooks: /eng-infra/runbooks/billing-reconciler
- Migration pilot notes: /product-docs/roadmap-and-themes/credit-portability-pilot-2026-notes (internal)

Change log

- 2026-10-25: Document created (Maya Chen).
- 2026-11-12: Added operational playbooks and approval thresholds (Maya Chen).

payload.page_title: SLO-driven fractional capacity pricing playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines a new pricing and packaging offering: SLO-driven fractional capacity bundles. The objective is to let customers purchase fine-grained capacity commitments (fractional GPU / shard equivalents) that are priced and SLA'd based on declared latency and throughput SLOs. The model aims to bridge the gap between per-token usage pricing and large reserved capacity contracts by offering a predictable cost ladder tied to operational SLOs and automatic fallback rules.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Goals:
  - Provide a predictable, lower-friction alternative to multi-month Dedicated contracts for teams that need capacity predictability tied to latency SLOs.
  - Increase conversion from self-serve to committed revenue by offering smaller commit sizes and SLO-backed discounts.
  - Expose clear levers (frac-capacity size, SLO target, burst window) that map directly to unit costs and throttling behavior.
- Non-goals:
  - Replace Dedicated annual contracts for very large enterprises.
  - Support every legacy billing model immediately; this playbook focuses on the fractional-capacity product and migration story.
sections.heading: Goals and non-goals

sections.body:
- Mid-market product teams with stable but moderate traffic (1k-50k requests/day) who need latency guarantees but not full reserved racks.
- Platform teams prototyping SLO-aligned internal chargeback models.
- ML-driven SaaS apps that want predictable per-session economics for conversational features.
sections.heading: Target customers

sections.body:
- Current options: Hosted per-token pricing (high variance) and Dedicated reserved capacity (high commitment). Customers repeatedly ask for an intermediate product that reduces cost variance without needing large commits.
- Observability and routing capabilities (our smart routing, fallbacks, and prefix-caching) make it feasible to offer fractional guarantees while preserving global availability with graceful degradation.
sections.heading: Background and motivation

sections.body:
- SKU: frac-capacity-{unit} (unit = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 of a session-equivalent shard). Each SKU pairs with an SLO profile (e.g., p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms) and a burst window (requests/min).
- Bundles: customers pick a bundle of N units for a billing period (monthly, quarterly) and declare an SLO profile. The system reserves proportional scheduling capacity and provides a discount vs on-demand per-token pricing.
- Fallback policies: if capacity is saturated, requests are subject to automatic fallback rules: lower-cost model variant, queued low-priority lane, or best-effort on-demand routing. These fallbacks are governed by the purchase’s fallthrough policy selected at purchase time (conservative / balanced / aggressive).
sections.heading: Product offering (high level)

sections.body:
1) Capacity accounting: track fractional allocations per tenant across GPU pools. Implementation notes: use the existing capacity ledger with a new fractional shard abstraction.
2) SLO enforcement: integrate with routing policy to prefer frac-capacity pool for qualifying requests and measure p95/p99 at the token and request level.
3) Billing & metering: create a monthly metering record for committed units vs consumed units, apply discounts and overage rules.
4) Telemetry: surface per-customer SLO compliance, fallback counts, and cost delta vs on-demand in Console.
5) Compatibility: support Hosted and Dedicated (Dedicated maps fractional units to dedicated pool partitions; Hosted maps to shared fractional tenancy).
sections.heading: Technical requirements (summary)

sections.body:
- Base on-demand rate (example): $0.0008 / token (reference).
- Fractional bundles: pricing is a function of unit size, SLO tier, and term commitment. Example table (displayed as ASCII table):
  | Bundle unit | SLO tier | Term | Discount vs on-demand | Effective unit price (example) |
  |-------------|----------|------|----------------------|-------------------------------|
  | 0.1         | p95-200ms| monthly | 12%                 | $0.000704 / token             |
  | 0.25        | p95-200ms| monthly | 18%                 | $0.000656 / token             |
  | 0.5         | p99-500ms| quarterly | 25%               | $0.0006 / token               |
  | 1.0         | p99-250ms| annual | 38%                 | $0.000496 / token             |
Notes on pricing: discounts increase with larger fractional units, tighter terms, and willingness to accept higher fallthrough aggression. The pricing engine will parameterize by observed utilization and historical fallback cost to keep revenue neutral during initial rollout.
sections.heading: Pricing & discount model (examples)

sections.body:
- SLOs are expressed as request-level latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and optional throughput floor (rps).
- Enforcement is conservative: routing prioritizes SLO-compliant pools but will not preempt other high-importance tenants; instead it routes to configured fallbacks once queue depth or expected latency exceeds thresholds.
- Violations: if monthly SLO compliance drops below contracted coverage (e.g., 99.9% of requests within declared p95), customers receive a credit formula (see Billing section).

Billing, credits and overage rules:
1) Committed charge: monthly invoice line for purchased units.
2) Consumption reconciliation: measured consumed tokens routed via fraction pool are billed at discounted rate up to committed units.
3) Overage: consumption beyond committed units is billed at a pre-agreed overage rate (e.g., on-demand + 10%).
4) SLO credit: if SLO compliance falls below threshold, apply credit equal to X% of the committed charge for the affected period (formula: committed_charge * max(0, (target_compliance - observed_compliance) / target_compliance) * SLA_factor).
sections.heading: SLO mapping and enforcement details

sections.body:
- New Console page: "Fractional Capacity" under Billing & Capacity. Views: active bundles, SLO health heatmap, fallback counts, projected month-end consumption delta.
- Alerts: default alert if observed compliance < target by 0.5% for 12h. Owners: customer-success + infra-oncall.
sections.heading: Console and telemetry changes (UX notes)

sections.body:
1) Pilot: Q2 2027 — small set of mid-market beta customers on Hosted with manual provisioning and heavy SE support.
2) Automation: Q3 2027 — full self-serve sign-up, Console UX, and automated capacity ledger integration.
3) Dedicated support: Q4 2027 — map fractional units to dedicated partitions and allow migration.
4) General availability: targeted for early 2028 after 3 months of adoption metrics and reliability KPIs.
sections.heading: Rollout & migration plan (recommended)

sections.body:
- For customers on per-token: offer a conversion tool to estimate monthly committed units from historical 90-day usage and target SLO, with recommended initial bundle and a 30-day evaluation term.
- For Dedicated customers: allow conversion of a subset of reserved racks into fractional units for internal chargeback and new product lines.
sections.heading: Migration guidelines for existing customers

sections.body:
- Commercial: conversion rate from self-serve to fractional bundles, ARR from fractional products, average committed unit size.
- Reliability: SLO compliance >= 99.5% for pilot group, fallback rates < 5% of requests.
- Financial: realized ASP vs forecast within ±8%, overage revenue within forecast caps.

payload.page_title: commercialization-playbook-optimize-conductor-fidelity-addons-2029-02-09

sections.body: This playbook describes the commercialization strategy, product packaging, pricing mechanics, and launch operations for Redwood Optimize 'Conductor' and its associated Fidelity Add‑Ons. It is intended for product managers, sales engineering, pricing, and GTM teams coordinating the cross-functional launch and early commercial expansion.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Redwood Optimize Conductor: orchestration and policy engine that executes model selection, batching, and cache coordination across multi-variant deployments.
- Fidelity Add‑Ons: per-tenant optional bundles that trade unit-cost for output fidelity and latency guarantees (e.g., Fidelity Shield, Deterministic Routing, Hot-KV Retention).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Redwood Optimize has matured from an internal optimizer into a modular commercial product. Conductor is the central orchestration component customers adopt to achieve cross-model cost targets and fidelity SLOs. Early adopters requested licensed fidelity controls (to lock outputs, pin KV caches, or preemptively allocate reserved micro-burst capacity). This playbook turns those capabilities into GTM-ready SKUs and outlines rollout controls to balance revenue with operational risk.
sections.heading: Background

sections.body:
1. Launch Conductor with a clear baseline SKU and three additive Fidelity Add‑Ons that are easy to sell and instrument.
2. Provide deterministic billing primitives so finance and customer success can reconcile cost savings vs charges.
3. Define rollout guardrails (canary segments, quota limits, automatic rollback criteria).
4. Establish success metrics and playbooks for onboarding, escalations, and migrations.
sections.heading: Objectives

sections.body:
- AI-native startups that require predictable per-route fidelity for PLG growth.
- Mid-market teams optimizing inference spend across dozens of model variants.
- Enterprises with contractual fidelity and latency guarantees for regulated workflows.
sections.heading: Target customer profiles

sections.body:
- Engineering: single API to express fidelity policies with runtime enforcement, reduces fragmentation of in-house schedulers.
- Platform/Infra: lowers average cost per token via cross-model KV reuse and safe batching while enabling tiered SLOs.
- Finance/GTM: productized add‑ons that capture value from customers who trade cost for reliability.
sections.heading: Value propositions (by persona)

sections.body:
(Use the table below as canonical SKU description for contracts and billing systems)

SKU | Short name | Unit | Description | Default inclusion
---|---:|---:|---|---
OPT-CONDUCTOR | Conductor | monthly seat / tenant | Core orchestration engine, includes policy primitives, telemetry, and basic autoscaling integration | Included in Optimize core tier (or add-on for hosted customers)
FID-SHLD | Fidelity Shield | percent-of-usage crediting + surcharge | Guarantees top-k stability for route prompts (measured by response re-rerun similarity). Applied as billing multiplier when limits exceeded. | Optional add-on
FID-ROUTE | Deterministic Routing | per-request overlay credit | Routes requests to deterministic inference lanes with reserved KV warmers. Charges per-request for deterministic lanes. | Optional add-on
FID-HOTKV | Hot-KV Retention | GB-month + per-surge fee | Increased KV cache retention and pre-warming for tenant-specific prefixes to reduce cold token latency. | Optional add-on
sections.heading: Product definitions and SKUs

sections.body:
- Conductor baseline: charged as fixed monthly tenant product fee plus a small per-route decision token charge (0.1 cents per policy decision).
- Fidelity Shield: charged as usage multiplier (e.g., +15% to tokens billed under shielded routes) with a monthly cap. Optionally sold as a firm per-route SLA price for enterprise customers.
- Deterministic Routing: sold as micro‑SKU per-request overlay (e.g., $0.002 per routed request), measured on routed count.
- Hot-KV: charged as tiered GB-month (0–50GB = $X/GB, 50–250GB = $Y/GB) plus pre-warm operations fee for bursts.
sections.heading: Pricing models and examples

sections.body:
{
  "customer_id": "acct_123",
  "sku": "FID-ROUTE",
  "period": "2029-02",
  "units": "4350",
  "unit_price_usd": "0.0020"
}
sections.heading: Example billing snippet (JSON for billing system ingest)

sections.body:
- Starter Optimize: Conductor included with limited policy rate (5k decisions/day), no add‑ons. Ideal for trials and PLG users.
- Scale Bundle: Conductor + Fidelity Shield (discounted when purchased together), includes 100k policy decisions/day and 5GB Hot-KV.
- Enterprise Fidelity: Custom pricing with deterministic routing SLAs, reserved KV capacity, and a seat for SRE integration. Includes implementation support and 6-month usage refund SLA for failing SLOs.
sections.heading: Packaging guidance and recommended bundles

sections.body:
1) Fidelity SLA definitions: define measurement method, sampling windows (30m), and remediation credits (pro-rated product credit).
2) Data residency on Hot-KV: specify whether KV storage is tenant-isolated and encryption at-rest policy.
3) Capacity overrun: automatic throttling vs paid pre-warm option.
4) Termination and migration assistance: outline export format for cached KV prefixes and policy definitions.
sections.heading: Contract & legal notes (clauses to include in the exhibit)

sections.body:
1. Staged rollout phases:
   a. Alpha (internal + 2 customers): manual enablement, close SRE monitoring, 24/7 on-call for first 2 weeks.
   b. Beta (selected customers, <20 tenants): feature-flagged in console, billing in sandbox only, success rep onboarding.
   c. GA (public purchase): backfill documentation, default quotas applied, support SLAs live.
2. Canary segmentation rules:
   - Start with non-critical routes that account for <5% of tenant token volume.
   - Disable add-ons automatically if error rate delta > 0.5% or average latency increase > 60ms sustained over 10 minutes.
3. Automated rollback triggers (runtime):
   - Policy decision runtime exceptions > 0.1% across requests for 5 consecutive minutes.
   - Memory pressure on KV nodes > 75% for > 5 minutes.
   - Billing meterfeed anomalies (negative credits or >200% spike) trips a hold on add-on billing pipeline.
sections.heading: Operational rollout and guardrails

sections.body:
1. Pre-sales: run the Conductor readiness assessment (see Appendix A). Capture route shapes, expected qps, model variants.

payload.page_title: SLO-backed Pricing & Bundled Capacity PRD

sections.body:
Overview

Problem statement:
Redwood customers pay for capacity and tokens, but many enterprise teams ask for predictable cost behavior tied to operational outcomes (latency SLOs, error budgets, and availability). Current unit-based pricing does not capture the value of: (1) guaranteed latency/availability for critical routes, (2) bundled tooling (Optimize features, caching, and rollout controls), and (3) simpler accounting for reserved capacity + burst. This PRD proposes an SLO-backed pricing model and bundle constructs that map directly to customer SLAs and internal cost/accounting needs.

Objective (what success looks like)
- Launch 3 new bundled SKUs that combine reserved capacity, SLO guarantees, and optional Optimize features by Q2 2026.
- Achieve 20% uplift in MRR from existing Dedicated customers migrating to SLO Bundles within 12 months of GA.
- Reduce billing disputes for latency incidents by 60% in pilot customers (tracked via billing-support ticket tags).

Non-goals
- This PRD does not change hosted API per-token public pricing. It targets Redwood Dedicated and Private customers and reserved-capacity commitments.
- It does not include fine-grained per-prompt quality/loss adjustment billing (that is future work).

Target customers
- Enterprise product teams requiring contractual latency SLAs (e.g., e-commerce search, realtime assistants).
- Platform teams buying Dedicated pools who want simplified internal chargebacks.
- High-volume customers seeking operational credits for Optimize and cache features.

Success metrics
1. Commercial: number of customers on SLO Bundles, conversion rate from existing Dedicated contracts, ARR growth attributable to bundles.
2. Operational: mean time to billing dispute triage, percent of requests meeting SLOs per billing cycle, utilization of bundled Optimize credits.
3. Product: number of rollout features enabled via bundles, NPS lift for customers on bundles.

User stories
- As a Platform lead, I want a contract that guarantees 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for a dedicated pool so I can commit internal SLAs to product teams.
- As a Finance lead, I want a single invoice line for reserved capacity + Optimize credits to simplify chargeback.
- As an SRE, I want automatic fallback policies and documented incident remedies included in the contract so customers know how Redwood will remediate SLO slippage.

Requirements
Functional requirements:
1) SKU model: create three SKUs — Base (SLO-Lite), Performance (SLO-Standard), Enterprise (SLO-Premium).
2) Each SKU must expose a clear set of SLOs (latency p95 & p99, availability, token throughput) and corresponding financial remedies (credits).
3) Bundles include a configurable number of Optimize credits (tokens of Optimize actions: auto-batching suggestions, model-quantization assessments, and caching reserved units).
4) Contracts must enumerate: model families covered, maximum sequence length, region(s), and supported fallback variants.
5) Billing system must issue pro-rated credits automatically when SLO breaches are validated.
6) Console UI: new Billing > Bundles page to create and manage bundles, view SLO compliance charts, and export monthly compliance reports.

Non-functional requirements:
- Telemetry: system must capture per-request latency, model variant, routing policy, and pool id for all requests covered by bundles (retention 12 months).
- Reporting latency: SLO compliance dashboard must refresh hourly and allow export of monthly CSVs for billing reconciliation.
- Security: contract metadata and bundle assignments must respect RBAC and be available to customer-admins only.

Pricing constructs and examples
Principles:
- Bundle price = reserved-capacity fee + SLO premium + amortized Optimize credits.
- SLO premium scales with the aggressiveness of latency targets and criticality (SLO-Premium > SLO-Standard > SLO-Lite).
- Clear, auditable metrics must tie SLO breaches to financial remedies.

Example pricing table (illustrative; final commercial pricing TBD):

| SKU | Pool GPU Equivalent | Monthly base | SLO p95 (tokens/ms) | Optimize credits / month | Expected effective per-1M tokens |
|-----|---------------------|--------------:|--------------------:|--------------------------:|-------------------------------:|
| SLO-Lite | 1 x A100 | $18,000 | p95 <= 220ms | 1,000 | $850 |
| SLO-Standard | 2 x A100 | $32,000 | p95 <= 120ms | 5,000 | $720 |
| SLO-Premium | 4 x A100 | $60,000 | p95 <= 60ms | 20,000 | $640 |

Financial remedies model
- For each calendar month, compute SLO compliance window and percent of covered requests meeting the SLO. If compliance < 99.9% for a given p95 target, issue tiered credits: 0.5% invoice credit for compliance in [98.0%,99.9%), 2% for [95.0%,97.99%), and 5% for <95%. Credits are applied automatically and visible in the Bundle invoice line item.

Telemetry and validation plan
Required events and attributes (minimum):
- request.id, timestamp, pool_id, model.name, model.variant, seq_len, tokens_generated, latency_ms, route_policy, response_status, cache_hit (bool).
- Aggregations: hourly p50/p95/p99 by pool_id + model.variant + route_policy.
Validation flow:
1) Billing runs nightly to compute hourly aggregates;
2) For each bundle contract, compute monthly compliance and generate preliminary credit amount;
3) SRE/finance review automated preliminary credits (3 business days) before finalizing;
4) Customer receives notification and invoice adjustment at month end.

Console & API changes
- API: POST /v1/bundles to create bundle, GET /v1/bundles/{id}/compliance returns monthly compliance CSV link. Example payload snippet:

{
  "bundle_name": "Acme-Performance-2026",
  "pool_id": "pool-xyz-123",
  "sku": "SLO-Standard",
  "models": ["redwood-rlm-v2", "llama-3-sim"],
  "regions": ["us-west1"],
  "start_date": "2026-01-01"
}

- UI: New Bundles management page under Billing. Key screens: Bundle detail, SLO compliance chart (hourly p95 heatmap), Optimize credit consumption, Invoice preview.

Rollout plan
Phase 0 — Design & agreements (Q4 2025)
- Finalize SKUs and credit mechanics with finance and legal. Prototype compliance pipeline in staging.
- Obtain pilot commitments from 3 existing Dedicated customers.

Phase 1 — Pilot (Q1 2026)
- Launch pilots with 3 customers (one per SKU). Validate telemetry, credit calculations, and customer reporting.
- Collect pricing feedback and refine commercial remedies.

Phase 2 — GA (Q2 2026)
- GA launch to new Dedicated contracts and Private deployments. Update sales collateral and renewals playbooks.
- Migrate existing high-value Dedicated customers via opt-in upgrade offers.

Phase 3 — Expansion (H2 2026)
- Add per-route SLO attachments, support for multi-region SLA stitching, and small-batch spot pooling.

Migration and customer communications
- Customers on legacy Dedicated will receive tailored transition offers: price-match for first 6 months or pro-rated credits.
- Sales playbook includes: comparison worksheet, step-by-step migration checklist, and a red-team Q&A for legal.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product: Maya Chen (PRD owner)
- Eng/Runtime: Ethan Park (implementation lead)
- Eng/Billing: Diego Alvarez (billing integration)
- Finance: Priya Natarajan (pricing & legal prep)
- SRE: Arjun Rao (telemetry & validation)

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Telemetry gaps cause disputed credits. Mitigation: 30-day staging telemetry verification window and manual reconciliation workflow.
- Risk: Overly aggressive SLOs increase infra cost. Mitigation: SLO calibration experiments in pilot and automated suggestion engine in Optimize.
- Risk: Complexity for customers to interpret credits. Mitigation: clear invoice line items, monthly compliance CSV, and customer success onboarding sessions.

Open questions
- Should host-level per-token discounts be applied inside bundles for extremely high utilization (>80%)? (Finance input required)
- How to support multi-tenant Dedicated pools where multiple customers share a pool? Need an isolation/measurement model.

Appendix A — Example monthly compliance CSV columns
- bundle_id, month, pool_id, model, region, total_requests, pct_meeting_p95, pct_meeting_p99, computed_credit_percent, credit_amount_usd

Appendix B — Sample contract clause (billing remedy)
- "Redwood will use observable telemetry to compute monthly SLO compliance. If the Bundle fails to meet the agreed p95 latency target, Customer will receive a credit applied as a reduction to the next invoice as described in the Financial Remedies Model."

Next steps
- Align pricing bands with finance and legal by 2025-11-30.
- Begin staging telemetry instrumentation and billing pipeline prototypes by 2025-12-15.
- Confirm pilot customers and schedule kickoff by 2026-01-15.

References
- Packaged tiers & credit conversion guidelines (internal)
- Redwood Optimize product overview (internal)
- Dedicated capacity reference architecture (internal)

payload.page_title: Service-tier surge scenario playbook and launch checklist

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines policies, automated controls, and an operational checklist for handling surge events that impact Redwood service tiers (Developer, Standard, Reserved). It focuses on minimizing customer-visible failures, preserving SLOs, and making predictable commercial decisions (credits, throttles, and fallback). This document combines product requirements, rollout checklist, runbook actions, and pricing impact guidelines for engineering, product, SRE, and GTM teams.

Goals
-----
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs for each tier when possible.
- Provide deterministic fallback behavior (variant, fidelity, region) within 200ms decision latency.
- Ensure cost/backstop actions are transparent and reversible.
- Reduce manual escalation during surges through automation and clear ownership.

Scope and definitions
---------------------
- Surge event: a tenant- or system-wide increase in request volume or token rate that causes capacity pressure for >2 minutes.
- Service tiers: Developer (best-effort), Standard (SLO-targeted), Reserved (dedicated capacity + SLA).
- Fidelity fallback: reducing model variant or quantization level to preserve throughput.
- Credit event: a post-facto customer credit to compensate SLA violations.

Signals and thresholds (product requirements)
-------------------------------------------
- Per-route call rate (requests/sec) sustained > 3x baseline for 2 minutes triggers tier evaluation.
- Aggregate token-per-second (TPS) across a host pool exceeding safe_utilization_threshold (75%) for >30s triggers autoscaling and pre-fallback checks.
- Error rate > 1% (5xx or model timeouts) for >60s escalates to incident path.
- Latency p99 surpassing tier SLO + 50ms for 3 minutes triggers automated fidelity fallback.

Configuration table (example values)
-----------------------------------
| parameter | Developer | Standard | Reserved |
|-----------|-----------|----------|----------|
| p99 latency SLO | 600ms | 200ms | 100ms |
| safe_utilization_threshold | 80% | 75% | 70% |
| max-fallback-depth | 2 variants | 1 variant | 0 variants |
| auto-scale cooldown | 45s | 30s | 15s |
| burst-credit-policy | none | 10% credits/day | contractual |

Automated decision flow (high level)
----------------------------------
1) Detect surge via telemetry (ingest from runtime observability).
2) Apply local autoscaling (policy per pool). If scaling meets demand within 90s, action = monitor.
3) If scaling insufficient and p99 > threshold, trigger graded fallback: Developer -> aggressive quantized variant; Standard -> single-step usage of fallback variant + token batching policy; Reserved -> regional failover only.
4) If error-rate remains > 1% after fallback, route to degraded-mode: enqueue noninteractive requests, mark route degraded, notify SRE and account team.
5) If SLA breach confirmed, open credit review workflow.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Detection and initial triage (oncall SRE)
   - Action: Validate alerts (console dashboards + /api/v1/health-code).
   - Command: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/status | jq '.pools[] | select(.util>0.75)'
   - Owner: SRE team.
2. Engage autoscaling (automated by control plane)
   - Verify: autoscaler events in last 2 minutes.
   - Command: rwctl autoscaler status --pool <pool-id> --last 120s
   - If autoscaler failed: escalate to infra-oncall (Slack: #infra-oncall).
3. Apply fidelity fallback (product-controlled)
   - Trigger: product toggle for route-level fallback ("/api/v1/config/routes/<route>/fallback").
   - Example payload (curl):
     curl -X PATCH https://operator.redwood.internal/api/v1/routes/route-id -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"fallback":"quantized-x4"}'
   - Owner: runtime/product oncall.
4. Controlled throttles and enqueueing
   - Use rate-limit policy: route->policies->burst_throttle = 100r/s default, reduce to 50r/s.
   - Owner: SRE + product.
5. Customer communication and crediting
   - Trigger: Confirmed SLO breach for Standard or Reserved for >60 minutes.
   - Notify: Customer success to draft status update using template: "We detected increased latency affecting X between T1 and T2; actions taken: autoscale, fallback; next steps..."
   - Credit initiation: file ticket to billing with incident id, impact window, and credit calculation (see pricing section).

Escalation matrix and owners
---------------------------
- Stage 0 (automated): runtime control plane (autoscaler/fallback). Owner: runtime-engineering.
- Stage 1 (oncall SRE): verify and execute manual mitigation. Owner: eng-sre.
- Stage 2 (product + account): route prioritization, customer comms, credit decision. Owner: product + customer-success.
- Stage 3 (legal + finance): contractual Reserved SLA breaches. Owner: finance-legal.

Pricing and credit guidance (product & billing)
--------------------------------------------
- Developer tier: no SLA credits. For widespread developer tier disruption, offer goodwill credits (manual approval by customer-success).
- Standard tier: automated credit slab based on severity tier:
  - Severity A (SLO miss 1–4 hours): 5% of daily token spend for impacted route.
  - Severity B (SLO miss 4–12 hours): 15% of daily token spend.
  - Severity C (>12 hours): case-by-case escalation to finance.
- Reserved tier: refer to contract; default action: activate contractual credit pipeline and schedule post-incident RCA within 3 business days.

Credit calculation example (Standard)
----------------------------------
- Impact window: 2026-10-12 12:00 -> 2026-10-12 16:00 (4h).
- Daily token spend for route: $2000/day.
- Severity B credit = 15% of daily = $300.

Rollout checklist (product + eng)
--------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:

- [ ] Implement telemetry alerts and dashboard widgets (p99, util, errors).
- [ ] Add fallback variants to model-variant registry and test in canary.

- [ ] Create customer communication templates (developer, standard, reserved).

- [ ] Verify autoscaler cooldown and fallback execution under load.
- [ ] Confirm billing automation can create credit tickets.
- [ ] Inform sales and customer-success of behavior and sample messaging.
sections.heading: Launch day

sections.body:
- [ ] Review actual surge incidents and tune thresholds.
- [ ] Run tabletop incident with product, SRE, CS teams.
- [ ] Decide on conservative defaults for next quarter.

Testing and simulation plan
--------------------------
- Synthetic load generator: use loadrunner-redwood (docker image rw/loadrunner:2026-09) to replay token patterns.
- Test scenarios: gradual ramp x3, spike x10, regional outage with traffic shift.
- Acceptance criteria: autoscaler recovers within 120s for Standard; fallback triggers and reduces p99 by >=20%.

Telemetry and dashboards (observability requirements)
--------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Post-launch (30 days)

sections.body:
- Per-pool utilization heatmap (1s granularity).
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 + error-rate trend with annotated fallback events.
- Autoscaler events timeline correlated with instance churn.
- Cost delta panel (estimated $/min) while fallback is active.
Retention and alerting: 30d high-resolution for troubleshooting; 365d aggregated for post-incident review.

Documentation and API surface (developer-facing)
---------------------------------------------
- Endpoints:
  - GET /v1/routes/<route>/status -- returns current fallback/limit state.
  - PATCH /v1/routes/<route>/config -- set fallback policy (product-only).
  - POST /v1/incidents/surge -- manual incident trigger (GTM/CS).
- Example SDK snippet (python):
  from redwood import RoutesClient
  rc = RoutesClient(api_key=REDWOOD_KEY)
  rc.update_config(route_id, {"fallback":"quantized-x2", "burst_throttle":50})

Open questions and decisions (to be resolved by Q4 2026)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Should Developer tier receive automated soft-fallbacks to preserve platform stability? (tradeoff: customer surprise).
- Define exact credit percentages for cross-tenant incidents vs single-tenant incidents.
- Whether to surface real-time remaining burst credits to customers in Console.

Appendix A — sample incident timeline
-----------------------------------
- 10:01: alert: pool util 82% (sustained 45s)
- 10:02: autoscaler invoked (failed to allocate GPU due to quota)
- 10:03: product toggle applied: Standard routes -> fallback quantized-x1
- 10:04: p99 reduces from 320ms -> 220ms, errors steady at 0.2%
- 10:10: provisioned additional capacity, fallback removed at 10:12
- Post-incident: credit ticket created, customer-success notified, RCA scheduled.

Contacts and ownership
----------------------
- Product owner: Priya Nair (product)
- Runtime engineering: Marco Alvarez (runtime)
- SRE oncall rota: eng-sre@redwood.internal
- Customer Success lead: Sana Iqbal
- Billing contact: billing-ops@redwood.internal

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-10-10 — initial draft by Priya Nair.
- 2026-10-15 — incorporated SRE thresholds and autoscaler notes (Marco Alvarez).
- 2026-10-21 — finalized credit slabs and launch checklist; published.
