payload.page_title: Developer Economics and Ecosystem Plugins Roadmap — Q1 2029

sections.body:
Summary:

This document describes the strategic roadmap, core requirements (PRD), high-level design decisions, and commercialization plan for the Developer Economics and Ecosystem Plugins initiative for Q1 2029. The initiative aims to grow developer adoption, monetize third-party plugin integrations, and surface actionable consumption insights so product teams can optimize cost/latency tradeoffs for developer-led workloads.

Why this initiative now:
- We observe a 45% year-over-year growth in API signups but only 12% conversion to paid tiers for plugin-enabled flows.
- Customers have requested a clearer way to attach third-party plugin costs to consumption and to receive packaged pricing for plugin-enabled workflows.
- Enabling an ecosystem of plugins increases stickiness and drives higher average revenue per developer (ARPD) if we provide clear commercial primitives and telemetry.

Goals (success criteria):
1. Increase paid conversion for developer accounts that try plugins from 12% to 22% within six months of GA.
2. Launch a plugin billing primitive and attribution surface that yields >= 90% cost-allocation accuracy for plugin-invoked tokens.
3. Integrate consumption telemetry into Console insights for plugin flows with < 2.5% sampling overhead.
4. Introduce two commercial plugin packaging options and secure pilot customers for each (at least 3 pilots).

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: hosted plugin registry, per-plugin consumption attribution, new packaging SKUs for plugin-augmented routes, Console UX for plugin economics, SDK hooks for plugin tracing, and a billing export for partner settlements.
- Out of scope: on-prem/private plan billing adapters (handled in a later wave), marketplace payments processing, and fully managed plugin hosting (partners self-host).

Principles guiding design:
- Developer-first: minimal friction to try and compose plugins from the Console and SDK.
- Transparent economics: customers should see line-item plugin cost impact in the same flow as model tokens.
- Low overhead: telemetry and attribution must not add measurable latency to the critical path.
- Composability: support multi-plugin chains with deterministic attribution heuristics.

Roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- Q1 2029 (this doc):
  - Finalize plugin billing primitive spec and attribution algorithm.
  - Build plugin registry MVP with metadata and verification tags.
  - Implement SDK tracing hooks and Console consumption insights for plugin flows (beta).
  - Define two packaging SKUs: Plugin-Add-on (per-call marginal), and Plugin-Bundle (monthly seat + capped tokens).
  - Begin partner pilots (3 selected ISVs).

- Q2 2029:
  - GA plugin registry and billing primitive; enable per-plugin line items in invoices.
  - Launch partner settlement export and pilot partner payout templates.
  - Add predictive cost estimates to Console for plugin-enabled routes.

- Q3 2029:
  - Integrate plugin consumption insights into Optimize recommendations.
  - Expand packaging templates and self-serve partner onboarding.

- Success metrics to track each quarter:
  - Paid conversion uplift for plugin-enabled developer cohorts.
  - Accuracy of plugin cost attribution vs partner-reported usage.
  - Latency overhead introduced by tracing (P95).
  - Number of pilots converted to commercial contracts.

PRD: core requirements (brief):
A. Billing primitive and attribution algorithm (MUST):
   - Assign token consumption and runtime costs to the invoking plugin(s) with deterministic rules for multi-plugin chains (e.g., last-invoker wins, or weighted by time-in-plugin).
   - Provide an API to fetch attributed consumption per-tenant, per-route, per-plugin for arbitrary date ranges.
   - Ensure attribution accuracy > 90% on synthetic tests and > 85% on production shadow runs.

B. SDK and runtime hooks (MUST):
   - SDKs (JS, Python) expose a simple plugin invocation API that attaches plugin_id and correlation_id to requests.
   - Runtime accepts plugin metadata and emits a lightweight trace event at plugin entry/exit.

C. Registry and verification (SHOULD):
   - Registry stores plugin metadata: name, vendor, semantic tags, cost model (per-call or per-token), verification status, docs link.
   - Allow partners to self-submit manifests and request verification badges.

D. Console & telemetry (MUST):
   - Console shows per-plugin consumption, estimated token cost, percent of total route spend, and trend charts.
   - Provide downloadable CSV/JSON exports suitable for finance reconciliation.

E. Pricing & packaging (MUST/SHOULD):
   - Define two SKU families: per-call marginal (Plugin-Add-on) and subscription bundles (Plugin-Bundle).
   - Pricing rules must allow: per-tenant overrides, trial credits, and per-plugin revenue share settings for partner settlements.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Attribution model: deterministic weighting vs probabilistic sampling. Deterministic models are easier to reason about for billing but can misattribute in complex async plugin graphs. We will implement a deterministic last-invoker weighting with a later plan to support time-weighted attribution for long-running plugins.

- Telemetry overhead: trace events should be encoded in compact binary and sampled at a low default rate (1%) with an adjustable tenant-level sample rate. For billing accuracy we run deterministic attribution on all billed requests but run tracing only for diagnostics.

- Security and confidentiality: plugins may receive user data. The registry will surface a "data sensitivity" flag and partners must declare processing requirements. Billing metadata must not leak customer PII; only plugin_id and cost metrics are stored in billing exports.

Pricing & packaging (commercial brief):
- Plugin-Add-on (per-call marginal):
  - Charged on top of standard token costs. Simple per-call fee or per-token multiplier published in registry.
  - Ideal for low-frequency, high-value integrators (e.g., external search, knowledge connectors).
  - Billing flow: plugin fee + tokens consumed by plugin + base route tokens.

- Plugin-Bundle (subscription):
  - Monthly seat or route-level subscription that bundles a token allowance and plugin runtime credits. Overage rates apply above allowance.
  - Discounts for annual contracts and for multi-plugin bundles.
  - Offer a standard contract template for partner revenue share (e.g., 70/30 split after threshold).

- Pilot commercial terms (Q1):
  - Offer partners 6-month pilot with waived listing fees, reduced 10% revenue share for first 3 months, and co-marketing credit.

Console UX and developer flows (high level):
1. Discover: Developer navigates registry, reads plugin docs and cost model.
2. Try: Click "Try in sandbox" launches quick demo with sample tenant credits.
3. Instrument: SDK call attaches plugin metadata and correlation id.
4. Observe: Console insights display plugin cost breakdown and allow exporting the data.
5. Commercialize: In Console, enable "Add plugin bundle" to route and buy the SKU.

Launch plan (detailed Q1 -> GA):
1. Beta (internal + partners) — weeks 1–8:
   - Release registry MVP and SDK hooks to partners; enable shadow billing exports for validation.
   - Run synthetic tests and two partner pilots.

2. Public beta — weeks 9–16:
   - Open registry to limited developers, add Console insights, enable trial SKUs.
   - Collect feedback and refine attribution heuristics.

3. GA (target by end of Q2):
   - Turn on billing primitive for paying tenants, publish official docs and contract templates, enable partner settlement exports.

Rollout and rollback steps (operational):
1. Feature flags: all components behind feature flags scoped by tenant.
2. Shadow mode: run attribution in shadow for 2–4 weeks before billing activation.
3. Monitor: Key alerts — attribution mismatch rate >10%, sample trace latency P95 increase >10ms, Console export failures >0.5%.
4. Rollback: disable billing routing and revert tenant flag; schedule hotfix and run tenant reconciliation.

Open questions for leadership (to resolve before Q1 dev start):
- Acceptable default revenue share for partner plugin bundles (proposal: 70/30 after $X threshold).
- Minimum attribution accuracy threshold required for switching from shadow to billed mode (proposal: 90%).
- Tolerance for Console sampling overhead (proposal: default 1%, configurable).

Risks and mitigations:
- Misattribution causing billing disputes: mitigate with extended shadow runs, partner reconciliation exports, and a 30-day safe window where invoices are informational only.
- Latency regressions from tracing: use sampling and offload heavy telemetry work to async pipelines.
- Partner fraud / misdeclared cost models: implement registry verification badges and periodic partner audits.

Ownership and contact points:
- Product lead: Aisha Patel (primary)
- Engineering lead: Liam Chen (runtime & SDK hooks)
- Partnerships & bizdev: Maria Gonzalez (partner pilots)
- Billing & finance liaison: Ethan Brooks

Appendix: short tables and examples

| 12345 | chat.route.create | plugin.search.v1 | 2029-01-05 | 420 | 0.36 | deterministic-last-invoker | abc-123 |

Sample SDK call (JS):
```
const res = await Redwood.plugins.invoke({
  plugin_id: 'plugin.search.v1',
  correlation_id: 'abc-123',
  input: {
    prompt: 'Summarize meeting notes',
  }
});
```

Related docs and references:
- Developer consumption sizing and packaging playbook (product docs).
- Billing export schema (finance internal).
- Registry verification policy (partnerships).

Next steps (this week):
1. Product to confirm revenue share floor with finance and partnerships.
2. Engineering to draft the billing primitive API and estimate implementation effort (T-shirt sizing).
3. Partnerships to identify candidate pilots and prepare initial manifests.

payload.page_title: Service Boundary Fidelity Transition Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
=======
This playbook defines the product and operational plan for transitioning tenant traffic across service boundaries as we introduce fidelity-tier boundaries and per-route fidelity controls. It consolidates product overview context, minimum viable requirements (PRD), a high-level design spec, a staged roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging implications, and release notes/communications to customers. The intent is to provide a single source of truth for product, engineering, and GTM teams executing the transition.

Goals
-----
- Ensure predictable user experience when fidelity boundaries are applied across service tiers.
- Provide clear SLOs and rollback criteria to protect revenue and quality.
- Minimize customer friction through phased rollout and transparent billing mapping.
- Enable platform teams to implement controls without ad-hoc service changes.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Per-route fidelity controls exposed in the Redwood API and Console.
- Runtime routing from hosted->dedicated/private variants when fidelity conflicts arise.
- Billing mapping from fidelity tiers to existing token/credit models.
- Telemetry and QA/eval capture for quality regressions.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- New model variant marketplace onboarding flow (separate PRD).
- Deep kernel/runtime optimizations for quantization (runtime/infra teams own).

Product requirements (PRD) — minimum viable
-----------------------------------------
1) API surface
   - Add `fidelity` optional field on generation and embeddings routes (enum: low, standard, high, ultra).
   - Backwards compatibility: default behavior = `standard` when omitted.
   - Per-route account config: owners can set a `fidelity_cap` and `fidelity_floor` in Console and via the admin API.

2) Billing & metering
   - Each fidelity tier maps to a multiplier on token-based billing: low=0.6x, standard=1x, high=1.6x, ultra=2.2x.
   - Credits and quota consumption must be visible in Console per-route and per-token class.

3) Guardrails and safety
   - Quality regression detection: sample 0.1% of requests with golden prompt sets (configurable per account).
   - Automatic rollback trigger if regression rate > 3% for 24h on a route or if customer complaint >= 5 in 7 days.

4) Rollout controls
   - Canary by tenant subset: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with manual approval gates.
   - Per-tenant opt-out window for 30 days after first enforcement.

Design summary (high-level)
---------------------------
- Control Plane: extend route configuration model with fidelity fields and pricing mapping. Console exposes UI and API endpoints.
- Data Plane / Runtime: route table contains (route_id, fidelity_cap, assigned_variant). Routing policy evaluates fidelity requirement then picks compatible model variant and runtime pool.
- Observability: add fidelity dimension to existing per-token metrics, latency histograms, cost attribution, and loss/regression dashboards.

Service boundary behaviors (examples)
------------------------------------
- If a request requests `ultra` but tenant `fidelity_cap` is `high`, the runtime will:
  1) If compatible higher-precision variant available on the same tier, serve it and bill at `high` pricing.
  2) Else, follow fallback policy (either downgrade to `high` or error depending on tenant policy).

Detailed config table (reference)
--------------------------------
| Field | Type | Description | Default | Owner |
| route.fidelity | enum | Requested fidelity level | standard | product |
| route.fidelity_cap | enum | Maximum fidelity allowed for route | ultra | product |
| route.fidelity_floor | enum | Minimum fidelity guaranteed | low | product |
| pricing.multiplier | float | Multiplier applied to token price for tier | see mapping | finance |

YAML example (route config)
---------------------------
```
route_id: sales-chat
fidelity: high
fidelity_cap: ultra
fidelity_floor: standard
billing_tag: per-tenant-abc
```

Rollout plan and timeline
-------------------------
Phase 0 — Engineering & QA (Weeks 0–6)
1. Implement API schema changes and Console mockups.
2. Runtime handling for fidelity flagging and fallback policies.
3. Integrate telemetry dimensions and create baseline dashboards.
4. Internal E2E tests with synthetic workloads and golden prompts.

Phase 1 — Beta customers (Weeks 7–12)
1. Invite 6 existing enterprise customers across industries (SaaS, fintech, healthcare).
2. Run 6-week controlled experiment: 10% of traffic opt-in.
3. Weekly quality reviews and billing reconciliation.

Phase 2 — Gradual ramp (Weeks 13–22)
1. Open to self-serve tenants with console opt-in.
2. Canary rollout for hosted regions (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with monitoring gates.
3. Publish pricing guidance and migration FAQ.

Phase 3 — Enforcement & defaults (Weeks 23+)
1. Make fidelity enforcement the default for new tenants.
2. Continue monitoring and runbook updates.

SLOs, metrics and alerting
--------------------------
Primary SLOs (product-facing)
- Fidelity correctness: 99.5% of requests are served with an allowed fidelity within 250ms decision time.
- Quality regression SLO: False positive regression triggers <= 1/month; regressions detected correctly >= 95%.

Operational metrics to instrument
- Per-route fidelity distribution (percent of tokens/requests by tier).
- Cost delta per-tenant week-over-week.
- Latency added by fidelity evaluation step.
- Golden set evaluation pass-rate and regression ratio.

Alerting configuration (examples)
- P0: Regression ratio > 3% for 24h on a route -> page SRE + oncall PM.
- P1: Billing multiplier mismatch detected for a tenant -> Slack alert and ticket.

Pricing and packaging implications
---------------------------------
- Introduce Fidelity Credits as a visible billing abstraction: customers can purchase bundles that guarantee `high` fidelity up to X tokens per month. Unused high-fidelity tokens do not rollover.
- Migration offers: 3-month introductory discount (20% off fidelity multipliers) for tenants who accept automated fidelity enforcement.
- Enterprise add-on: fidelity insurance that guarantees auto-rollbacks if quality drops (legal & finance approval required).

GTM and customer communications
------------------------------
- Documentation: Console help article and migration FAQ published at time of Beta open.
- Email cadence: initial invite -> onboarding guide -> 2-week status -> 30-day opt-out reminder.
- Sales enablement: one-pager mapping fidelity tiers to common customer workloads (search, summarization, code-gen).

Release notes (intended content for public release)
--------------------------------------------------
- Feature: Per-request fidelity control and per-route fidelity caps.
- Benefit: Lower cost options for latency-sensitive workloads and high-quality tiers for revenue-critical paths.
- Migration: Default remains unchanged; new console options available for interested customers.
- Known limitations: fidelity decisions will not be supported for streaming fallback during v1.0.

Rollback and incident playbook (short)
------------------------------------
1. Detect regression via golden-set or customer report.
2. If regression meets rollback criteria (see PRD), perform immediate rollback to previous fidelity mapping and notify customer.
3. Post-incident: run root cause analysis, update acceptance tests, and schedule hotfix if needed.

Ownership and stakeholders
--------------------------
- Product owner: Dana Chen (product)
- Engineering owners: Marco Ruiz (serving-runtime), Priya Desai (data-plane)
- SRE escalation: Liam O'Connor (eng-sre)
- Finance & Pricing: Daniel Nguyen (finance)

payload.page_title: adaptive-fidelity-market-experiments-roadmap-2028-q1

sections.body:
Overview:

This roadmap describes a coordinated program of market-facing experiments and internal simulations to validate adaptive fidelity bundles (high/medium/low output fidelity) combined with dynamic pricing and onboarding flows. The goal is to identify product-configurations that maximize net revenue per request while maintaining customer-visible SLOs for latency and quality. This is a product + go-to-market initiative with heavy engineering support (Optimize + Serving Runtime + Console).

Goals:
- Establish 3 fidelity tiers (High, Medium, Low) with clear cost-to-quality tradeoffs and price points for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Prove a neutral-to-positive overall revenue impact (net revenue per token) for at least two customer segments within 12 weeks of experiment start.
- Keep customer-facing SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms and quality regressions < 1.5% (measured by eval prompt sets) per route.
- Define rollout criteria and automation for per-route fidelity recommendations in Redwood Console.

Hypotheses to validate (examples):
1) Many customers will accept a Medium fidelity default for background tasks if price is ~30% lower and latency improves 10–20%.
2) For chat/interactive routes, a "smart fallback" that reduces fidelity only when p99 latency >400ms will improve availability without measurable quality loss.
3) A meterable fidelity credit (small upfront credit applied to Medium/Low) will increase adoption without materially increasing churn.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: Hosted API customers (self-serve + SMB sales-assisted) and Dedicated customers with opt-in via Console. Private on-prem deployments are excluded from initial experiments.
- Constraint: Experiments must not violate enterprise customers’ pinned-variant constraints; enterprise routes that explicitly pin model variants will be excluded.
- Data handling: All A/B data and logs will follow existing telemetry and privacy policies; no customer user data leaves the platform for analysis except aggregated metrics.

Definitions (for this program):
- Fidelity tiers:
  - High: full-precision variants (FP16/AMP, no aggressive quantization), highest output consistency. Target use: core chat, compliance-sensitive outputs.
  - Medium: optimized kernels + int8/4 quantization with tuned temperature/profile. Lower cost, slightly higher variance. Target: background summarization, search snippets.
  - Low: aggressive quantization (int4 / 3-bit profiles), energy-optimized kernels. Target: bulk embedding-like tasks where latency matters more than nuance.

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Primary: Net revenue per 1M tokens served (USD), measured weekly, segmented by customer cohort.
- Secondary: 1) p95 request latency across routes; 2) eval-set quality delta per route (population-weighted); 3) Adoption rate of Medium/Low across eligible routes; 4) Change in churn rate for test cohorts.

Experiment pillars and milestones (12-week cadence):
1) Simulation and off-line modeling (Weeks 0–3)
   - Run high-fidelity cost/latency simulator with representative workload traces (samples from June–Oct 2027).
   - Parameters: batch size distribution, sequence length percentiles (P50/P90/P99), kv-cache hit rates.
   - Deliverable: Simulation report with expected per-token cost delta and p95/p99 latency projections for each fidelity tier.

2) Internal pilot (Weeks 3–6)
   - Select 3 internal product routes and 5 partner customers (opt-in) for closed beta.
   - Implement per-route fidelity controls and Console UI to toggle defaults.
   - Run canary traffic at 5% for 2 weeks, monitor latency, errors, and eval divergence.
   - Deliverable: Pilot post-mortem with recommended price points.

3) Public A/B experiment (Weeks 6–12)
   - Roll out to a randomized subset of self-serve customers grouped by profile (startup, midmarket, infra teams).
   - Experiment arms: Control (no change), Medium-default (price -30%), Smart-fallback (High default with fidelity reduction on pressure).
   - Monitor: SLOs, quality deltas, revenue, adoption.
   - Deliverable: Decision memo recommending 0/1 scale decisions (deploy, iterate, or rollback).

Roadmap timeline (high level):
- 2028-01-10: Roadmap published (this doc).
- 2028-01-17 to 2028-02-07: Simulation runs and analysis (Engineering lead: Arjun Rao).
- 2028-02-07 to 2028-02-28: Internal pilot + Console toggles (Console PM: Leila Hassan).
- 2028-02-29 to 2028-03-20: Public A/B with weekly checkpoints (Go-to-market: Samir Kaur).
- 2028-03-27: Final decision reviews and rollout plan for Q2 2028.

Ownership and roles:
- Product lead: Priya Nair (owner of roadmap, decision authority).
- Experiment engineering lead: Arjun Rao (eng-serving-runtime).
- Console/productization: Leila Hassan (eng-developer-experience).
- Optimize heuristics and simulations: Ethan Morales (eng-platform / Optimize).
- Data & metrics: Li Wei (analytics), responsible for experiment instrumentation and dashboards.
- Legal & pricing: Marisol Perez (finance-legal) for compliance and contract language updates.

Rollout criteria and decision gates:
- Safety gate (pre-A/B): Simulation must show p95 latency within 10% of baseline for each candidate route under expected load.
- Quality gate: Eval-set regression for any route must be < 1.5% (absolute) for Medium tier in the pilot.
- Revenue gate: Expected net revenue per 1M tokens must increase or be neutral for at least one target cohort in simulation.

Console UX and API changes (summary):
- New per-route fidelity default control with three radio options (High/Medium/Low).
- New global account-level preference to express cost-sensitivity (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive).
- Telemetry: additional fields in usage events: fidelity_tier, simulated_cost_saved_usd, fidelity_reason (default|fallback|user_override).
- API: PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} body will accept "default_fidelity": "high|medium|low". Example:

  PATCH /v1/routes/abc123
  Content-Type: application/json

  {
    "default_fidelity": "medium"
  }


Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers perceive fidelity downgrades as quality regressions.
  Mitigation: Conservative defaults, clear Console messaging, 2-week opt-out grace, and fine-grained route-level opt-out.
- Risk: Unexpected p99 latency regressions on long-sequence requests when using aggressive quantization.
  Mitigation: Smart-fallback rules (detect rising p99 and switch to higher fidelity variant), automated rollback on SLO breach.
- Risk: Billing edge cases and disputes.
  Mitigation: Pre-release billing FAQ and small credit applied to initial adoption cohorts; finance-legal to provide T&Cs update.

Data and metrics instrumentation (required dashboards):
- Per-fidelity tier: cost-per-token estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, eval-quality-delta.
- Route-level adoption metrics: percent routes with Medium/Low default, top 50 routes by volume that chose Medium/Low.
- Cohort revenue dashboard: segmented by company size and industry vertical.

Appendix A — Simulation parameter table (example):

| Parameter | Baseline | Medium | Low | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Average per-token cost (USD) | 0.0016 | 0.00112 (-30%) | 0.0008 (-50%) | Kernel & quantization assumptions
| p95 latency (ms) | 240 | 200 (-17%) | 170 (-29%) | Measured on sample traces; p99 will be monitored
| Eval-quality delta (relative) | 0.0 | -0.8% | -2.4% | Weighted on conversational eval set

Appendix B — Example acceptance checklist for pilot routes:
1) Route has automated eval set integrated into CI (yes/no).
2) Baseline telemetry available for 30 days (yes/no).
3) Customer route owner opt-in confirmed (yes/no).
4) Billing credit applied and visible in Console (yes/no).
5) Rollback policy configured and tested (yes/no).

References and related materials:
- Simulation harness: internal repo redwood/optimize/sim-v2 (design doc link in Dev wiki).
- Observability contract spec: /product-docs/design-specs/quality-gates-and-observability-contract-spec-2027-04-05
- Prior work: graceful-fidelity-degradation-prd-2026-09-07

Next steps (action items within 7 days):
1) Engineering to schedule simulation runs and surface initial cost model by 2028-01-17 (Assignee: Arjun Rao).
2) Console team to prototype per-route toggle and API contract by 2028-01-24 (Assignee: Leila Hassan).
3) Analytics to prepare standard dashboards and signup opt-in flow reports by 2028-01-24 (Assignee: Li Wei).

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.com)
- Escalation: Head of Product (Samir Kaur) if rollout decision needs exec arbitration.

Document history:
- 2027-11-20: Draft created by Priya Nair.
- 2027-12-10: Internal review with Eng + Optimize; updated simulation scope.
- 2028-01-10: Finalized and published (this edition).

payload.page_title: Feature Waves and Go-to-Market Playbook — Q3 2026

sections.body: This document outlines the Feature Waves for Q3 2026 and a prescriptive Go-to-Market (GTM) playbook for launching the next set of Redwood Inference product capabilities. It covers product scope, measurable success criteria, rollout phases, pricing/packaging impacts, monitoring and SLO targets, launch gating, and ownership.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Objective: Deliver three prioritized feature waves that increase hosted API ARR, improve Dedicated utilization, and accelerate Private deployment adoption for regulated accounts.
- Timebox: Q3 2026 (planned cadence: Wave A launch week of 2026-07-12).
- Audience: Product, Growth, Engineering, SRE, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success.
sections.heading: Context and intent

sections.body:
- Host API Revenue (net-new): +18% month-over-month across Q3 driven by Wave A/B feature adoption.
- Dedicated Capacity Utilization: increase committed utilization from 62% -> 78% by 2026-09-30.
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) for customers on Private: reduce median onboarding time from 21 days -> 10 days.
- Quality guardrail: fewer than 0.5% increase in generation error-rate within 30 days post-launch per model route.
sections.heading: Goals & Success Metrics

sections.body:
- PLG engineers (small/medium apps) — prioritize Wave A low-friction features and SDKs.
- Platform & Security buyers (enterprise) — prioritize Wave C private deployment and compliance packaging.
- Embedded AI product teams — prioritize Wave B cost/perf controls and model variants.

sections.body:
| Wave | Primary Features (owner) | Primary KPI | Target SLO / Perf Target | Pricing impact |
|------|-------------------------|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|
| Wave A (Q3 start) | SDK streaming primitives + standardized prompt templates (owner: DX team) | # API calls with streaming >= 2x baseline | 95th p95 latency <= 450ms (1k tokens) | Minor: no pricing change; feature flag gating |
| Wave B (mid-Q3) | Cost-aware batching & adaptive quantization advisory (owner: Optimize team) | Per-token cost reduction observed in A/B test >= 12% | 99% of requests below cost-SLO with <2% latency tail regressions | Introduce optional per-route optimization add-on (beta pricing) |
| Wave C (late-Q3) | Private deployment quickstart + certified compliance bundle (owner: Private deployments team) | # Private pilots -> paid conversions within 90 days >= 40% | On-prem bootstrap time <= 48 hours for certified configs | New enterprise packaging; platform fee + deployment license (see Pricing section) |

(Notes: Table rendered above as ASCII for Confluence; owners are team leads.)
sections.heading: Feature Waves (high level)

sections.body:
1) Pre-launch (T-6 to T-2 weeks)
   - Complete product-signoff checklist (owners signoff: PM, Eng, SRE, Security).
   - Create feature flags: ff.streaming_v2, ff.adaptive_batch_v1, ff.private_quickstart_v1.
   - Prepare SDK changelog and migration guide (DX).
   - Set up A/B experiment: sampling rule (1% control, 49% baseline, 50% variant) for Wave B cost experiment.
2) Limited rollout (T-2 to T+2 weeks)
   - Enable for internal + partner accounts, Solutions Engineering-run pilots.
   - Monitor: latency_p95_by_route, error_rate_by_route, cost_per_1k_tokens.
   - Weekly quality reviews; rollback threshold: error_rate increase > 0.8% absolute or latency_p95 regress > 30% relative.
3) Open rollout (T+2 to T+8 weeks)
   - Gradual ramp to 100% for hosted customers per routing policy; provide migration CLI (redwood migrate-streams).
   - Announce public docs + quickstart templates; launch self-serve opt-in for optimization add-on.
4) Enterprise enablement (post T+8 weeks)
   - Dedicated & Private sales motions: package templates, pricing worksheets, compliance evidence bundles.
   - Offer day-2 runbook and 90-day SLA uplift conversations (SRE & Sales).
sections.heading: Rollout plan (detailed)

sections.body:
- Blocking criteria (must be green before open rollout):
  - Stability: <0.2% production error-rate attributable to feature on internal canary fleet for 7 consecutive days.
  - Performance: p95 latency within 10% of baseline for 99% of routes (where baseline is previous quarter median).
  - Security & compliance: Customer-data-handling review completed and ATO checklist signed by Security.
  - Documentation: SDK migration guide, quickstarts, sample prompts, and runbook published.
sections.heading: Release gating & launch criteria

sections.body:
- Wave A: No price change; included in hosted API tier. Market message focuses on DX/velocity benefits.
- Wave B: Introduce a new optional "Optimize Add-on" priced as a % discount on per-token billing when the system applies adaptive quantization/batching. Initial beta pricing: 8% of token spend as monthly surcharge that guarantees >=10% realized cost reduction under benchmarked workloads.
- Wave C: Enterprise Private package has two components: platform license (one-time onboarding fee + monthly platform fee) and deployment license (per-node or per-GPU). Suggested list: onboarding $25k, platform $5k/month, node license $2k/month (negotiable). Include standard SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) mapped to response times and retention.
sections.heading: Pricing & packaging considerations (product notes)

sections.body:
- Solutions Engineering (SE) checklist for demos:
  - Demo 1 (DX-focused): show streaming + prompt templates; demo script: 10–12 steps with prepopulated prompts.
  - Demo 2 (Optimize-focused): run live cost comparison with and without adaptive batching using benchmark dataset (privacy-safe).
  - Demo 3 (Private-focused): show quickstart deployment on a sandbox VPC with KMS integration.
- Customer objection handling:
  - "Will these features increase costs?" -> Walk through Optimize add-on model: surcharge only when system applies optimizations; show expected cost delta and rollback option.
  - "How do we validate accuracy regressions?" -> Point to regression harness and quality guardrails (prompt sets + golden outputs).

sections.body:
- Dashboards to create/update:
  - "Wave A - Streaming adoption" (owner: DX) — metrics: streaming_success_rate, stream_connect_latency, average_stream_tokens.
  - "Wave B - Cost optimization" (owner: Optimize) — metrics: realized_cost_saved_pct, batching_rate, quantization_failures.
  - "Wave C - Private onboarding" (owner: Private deployments) — metrics: bootstrap_time_median, infra_errors_per_bootstrap, compliance_check_pass_rate.
- Alerts & SLOs:
  - streaming_success_rate < 99% for 5m -> pager (severity P2) to DX oncall.
  - realized_cost_saved_pct < 6% for 1h during beta -> notify Optimize PM and SRE (investigate parameter tuning).
  - bootstrap_time_median > 72 hours -> SRE ticket automation and SE outreach.
sections.heading: Monitoring & Observability changes

sections.body:
- Hypothesis: Adaptive batching + quantization advisory reduces observable per-token spend by >=12% without user-visible quality regressions.
- Metric definitions: cost_per_1k_tokens = (infrastructure_costs_allocated / tokens_generated) * 1000; quality_regression = BLEU/ROUGE-based delta + manual spot checks on 500 prompt pairs.
- Experiment duration: 28 days with daily reporting. Success threshold: >=12% median cost reduction and <=0.5% regression signal in quality harness.
sections.heading: Data & experiment plan (Wave B cost experiment)

sections.body:
- Dependency: kernel-level quantization support must ship from runtime team by 2026-06-15 for Wave B to meet schedule.
- Risk: performance regressions when applying heavy adaptive batching for small (<64 token) requests. Mitigation: per-route sampling and fallback.
- Risk: enterprise purchase cycles may delay Wave C revenue realization. Mitigation: early pilot discounts + documented onboarding SLAs.

Ownership, milestones, and timeline:
- PM leads: Priya Nair (Wave planning), Jordan Blake (Wave B PM), Sofia Martinez (Wave C PM).
- Engineering owners: DX (SDKs), Optimize (cost tools), Private deployments (onboarding).
- Key milestones:
  - 2026-05-15: Feature design freeze for Wave A.
  - 2026-06-15: Runtime quantization kernel availability.
  - 2026-07-12: Wave A limited rollout (partner pilots).
  - 2026-08-02: Wave B experiment starts.
  - 2026-09-20: Wave C enterprise pilot cohort onboarded.

Appendix A — API surface & CLI changes (examples):

- CLI: redwood optimize analyze --route <route_id> --profile perf -> outputs suggested batch/quantization profile JSON.

Appendix B — Templates and artifacts to publish:

payload.page_title: Tailored SLO Transition Toolkit for Enterprise Clients

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook is a product-focused toolkit for enterprise customers who are migrating inference workloads between Redwood deployment modes (hosted -> Dedicated or hosted -> Private). It defines a repeatable process to translate customer-facing SLOs into platform controls, consumption profiles, and pricing guardrails. The goal is to ensure predictable latency, cost, and availability during and after migration while minimizing production impact.

Audience
- Product managers and solution architects leading migrations
- Customer success and solutions engineering
- Platform and runtime engineers responsible for capacity and rollout

Scope
- Migration modalities covered: Hosted -> Dedicated, Hosted -> Private (VPC/on-prem).
- SLO types addressed: p50/p95 latency, per-request fidelity, availability (monthly uptime), error budget burn, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Not in scope: model retraining, dataset migrations, or legal/compliance contract changes (handled by other teams).

Goals and Success Criteria
- Clear mapping from customer SLOs to Redwood controls (routing policies, capacity reservations, fallback rules).
- Migration playbooks with <2% regression in p95 latency for 90% of customers within 48 hours of switchover.
- Cost-estimation accuracy <= 12% vs. measured 30-day post-migration consumption for standard conversational workloads.

Key Concepts
- SLO translation: converting an abstract SLA (e.g., \"95% requests under 150ms\") into technical knobs (instance size, batching targets, KV cache policy, model variant).
- Fidelity envelope: an agreed set of model/quantization variants allowed for a tenant during capacity constraints.
- Consumption contract: a committed capacity profile (reserved-GPU-hours, warm-pools) tied to billing and graceful degradation behavior.

SLO Translation Matrix (example)
This table provides an example mapping of customer SLOs to Redwood controls and the verification signals we use.

| Customer SLO | Redwood Controls | Verification Signals | Notes |
|-------------|------------------|----------------------|-------|
| p95 latency <= 200ms | Dedicated pool with 2:1 reservation; small-batch target 16 tokens; KV cache TTL 2h | p95 request latency, queueing ratio, batch sizes | Start with 1.5x headroom for first 48h |
| Availability 99.9% | SLA-backed route with dual-region fallback | error rate, failover latency, health checks | Enable automatic region failover for critical routes |
| Cost target: < $0.75 / 1k tokens | Route to quantized variant for non-critical paths; enable adaptive batching | per-token cost, sample quality evals | Quality gate required for quantized variant before enabling |

Migration phases
1) Intake & assessment (owner: solutions engineering)
   - Gather production traffic profile (sequence-length distribution, tokens per request, concurrency, peak shapes).
   - Obtain target SLOs and cost constraints from the customer.
   - Baseline measurements from hosted: 14-day traces + synthetic QPS ramp.

2) Design & capacity plan (owner: product + platform)
   - Run capacity simulation using the customer profile; recommend pool sizes, autoscaling thresholds, and warm-pool budgets.
   - Compute cost-sim and produce 3 consumption options: conservative, balanced, and aggressive.
   - Select fallback model variants and define fidelity envelope.

3) Preflight validation (owner: platform + runtime)
   - Create a staging tenant in Dedicated/Private and run 48-hour shadow traffic replay.
   - Verify SLOs: p50/p95 latency, correct batching behavior, and KV cache hit rate.

4) Canary rollout (owner: solutions engineering + SRE)
   - Gradually shift 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% traffic over KPI gates (latency, error rate, cost).
   - Monitor for anomalies for 24 hours after each step, revert on defined thresholds.

5) Post-migration stabilization (owner: customer success + platform)
   - 30-day monitoring window with weekly reconciliations and cost tuning.
   - Transition to normal support and budgeting cadence.

Pre-migration checklist (minimum required)
- [ ] Production traffic histogram (7-day, 30-day) uploaded to migration ticket
- [ ] Customer SLOs and target cost constraints documented and agreed
- [ ] Model variant compatibility matrix finalized (quantized/float16/float32)
- [ ] Security & network prerequisites validated (VPC peering, firewall rules)
- [ ] Key rotation and KMS access for Private deployments verified
- [ ] Billing & contract addendum approved if reserved capacity is required

Canary gating thresholds (example)
- Latency: p95 increase <= 10% vs hosted baseline per canary step
- Errors: request error rate increase <= 0.1% absolute
- Cost: projected effective $/1k tokens not exceed agreed consumption option by >20%
- Quality: evaluation prompts pass fidelity gate (acceptance threshold configurable, default: 95% similarity by rubric)

Rollback and fallback policies
1) Immediate fallback to hosted route if any gate is violated during canary.
2) If fallback unavailable (e.g., network failure in customer VPC), engage emergency route: model variant in Dedicated pool + reduced concurrency (throttled to safe QPS).
3) Post-rollback root-cause analysis within 48 hours following the incident retros.

Telemetry and verification
- Required telemetry signals to collect during migration: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, model variant usage, error type breakdown, per-route cost metrics.
- Alerting: temporary migration policy alerts for \"SLO drift\" (p95 latency > threshold), \"cost-exceed\" (consumption-run-rate > expected by 25%), and \"quality-regression\" (eval similarity below gate).
- Reconciliation cadence: daily for first 7 days, weekly for next 3 weeks.

Pricing and packaging implications
- Consumption options (decision knobs):
  - Reserved capacity (monthly commitment): lowest unit cost, requires 30-day lead time for provisioning.
  - Warm-pool subscription (short-term buffer): medium unit cost, flexible up/down monthly.
  - On-demand bursts: highest unit cost, used for occasional traffic spikes.
- Addenda: migrations that require Dedicated pools should include a migration fee to cover pre-provisioning and runbook engineering (typically 10–15% of first-month reserved cost).
- Billing reconciliation: for first billing cycle post-migration, provide a line-item report comparing projected vs actual consumption with suggested tuning actions.

Sample pricing decision table
| Consumption option | Best for | Expected unit cost delta vs hosted | Recommended contract term |
|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Reserved capacity | Predictable, 24/7 traffic | -20% | 12 months |
| Warm-pool subscription | Variable daytime workloads | -8% | 1–3 months |
| On-demand bursts | Spiky, unpredictable | +30% | none |

Ownership & stakeholder matrix
- Migration lead: Solutions Engineering (primary contact)
- Platform provisioning: Eng Platform
- Runtime tuning and model compatibility: Serving Runtime team
- SLO verification and SRE gating: Eng SRE
- Billing adjustments and contract changes: Finance & Legal

Risk register and mitigations (top risks)
- Unexpected p95 regressions: Mitigation: conservative headroom and quick rollback policy.
- Quality regressions with quantized variants: Mitigation: gated local evals + sample A/B tests before canary.
- Billing disputes due to consumption variance: Mitigation: pre-migration cost-sim, post-migration line-item reconciliation, and credits as required per contract.

Roadmap & milestones for the toolkit (product view)
- Q2 2027: Publish toolkit, add migration-automations to Console (guided wizard).
- Q3 2027: Telemetry templates in Console (preflight upload + trend analytics).
- Q4 2027: Automated cost-simulator in Console with contract-ready export.
- Q1 2028: Policy-driven canary automation (gates + auto-fallback) for standard enterprise bundles.

Release notes (initial release v1.0)
- v1.0 (2027-04-11): Initial publish of Tailored SLO Transition Toolkit. Includes translation matrix templates, migration playbook, canary gating thresholds, and pricing decision guidance.
- v1.1 (2027-06-20): Added warm-pool pricing guidance, updated canary thresholds based on first 10 migrations, and published evaluation rubric for quantized variants.

Appendix: Example console snippet (policy JSON as example)
Note: the snippet below is an illustrative example that operators can paste into the Console policies UI.

POLICY: DedicatedRoutePolicyExample
- route: tenant-abc-dedicated
- reservation: 2 x a100-40g
- autoscale_min: 2
- autoscale_max: 8
- batching_target_tokens: 16
- kv_cache_ttl_seconds: 7200
- fallback_route: hosted-tenant-abc
- canary_steps: [1,5,20,100]

Acceptance checklist before closure
- [ ] 30-day post-migration cost report delivered to customer
- [ ] No unresolved SLO violations older than 7 days
- [ ] Runbook updates merged and Console guided-wizard entry created
- [ ] Account moved to standard billing cadence

References and related materials
- Hosted -> Dedicated transition playbook (internal)
- Capacity simulator reference guide (internal)
- Quantization evaluation rubric (internal)

Contact
Product owner: Lena Park (product@redwood.ai)
Solutions eng lead: Marco Diaz (solutions@redwood.ai)

Change log
- 2027-04-11: v1.0 published (initial toolkit).
- 2027-06-20: v1.1 updated with warm-pool pricing and thresholds after empirical tuning.

payload.page_title: Lab-driven feature experiments roadmap Q4 2028

sections.body:
Overview

This document defines the roadmap, governance model, and operational playbook for Redwood's Lab-Driven Feature Experiments program (the Lab). The Lab is a small-batch, safety-and-cost-aware environment for validating product and runtime changes that impact inference economics, fidelity, and developer ergonomics prior to wider rollout.

Goals

- Accelerate validated learning about feature value and economics using constrained, instrumented experiments.
- Reduce rollout risk for changes that affect cost per token, latency SLOs, or model output fidelity.
- Create repeatable guardrails and telemetry for feature-level decisions (accept, iterate, rollback).

Scope

- In-scope: model variant pilots, quantization profiles, batching and caching policies, routing heuristics, SDK UX changes that affect request surface, and console telemetry experiments.
- Out-of-scope: major infra (fleet resizing), customer-facing billing model changes, and any experiment that requires global data residency changes. Those require separate enterprise review.

Key success metrics (per-experiment)

1) Primary business metric (one only): e.g., increased API conversion or reduced per-token cost for sample workload. Target specified in experiment brief.
2) Performance safety metrics (must not regress):
   - Median tail latency (p95) change <= +10% vs baseline
   - Error rate (5xx/4xx) increase <= 0.5 percentage points absolute
   - KV cache hit rate impact documented if relevant
3) Fidelity safety metrics:
   - BLEU/ROUGE/LLMScore change <= threshold defined per prompt set (default: 2% absolute)
   - Regression alerting bound: any metric drop > 3% triggers immediate pause
4) Cost/Economics:
   - Estimated per-token cost delta documented in experiment brief
   - Burn budget cap enforced (see Cost and resourcing)

Quarterly roadmap (Q4 2028)

- Week 1-3 (Oct): Establish baseline telemetry dashboards and canonical prompt-sets for three product verticals (Search, Automated Support, Content Gen). Owners: Product–Asha, Signals–Sophie.
- Week 4-6 (Nov): Run small-batch quant-fallback experiments (2 model variants * 3 quant profiles) on dedicated lab cluster. Deliverable: per-variant fidelity matrix and cost delta table. Owners: Applied ML–Miguel, Runtime–Raj.
- Week 7-10 (Nov-Dec): SDK surface experiment: streaming chunk sizes and default retry policy change. Canary to 2% of traffic via dev sandbox tokens. Deliverable: conversion vs latency trade-off report. Owners: Developer DX–Kara.
- Week 11-12 (Dec): Governance review, consolidate results, decide promotion candidates for production canary or return to iteration.

Experiment lifecycle and governance

- Proposal: submit an Experiment Brief (single-page) with hypothesis, primary metric, safety criteria, data retention, owners, and budget. Template below.
- Approval: Experiment Review Board (ERB) approves experiments with one of: green (go), conditional (go with guardrails), or deny. ERB membership: Product Lead (chair), Applied ML, Runtime, Security, Finance.
- Run: experiments run on the Lab cluster or sandbox routes depending on risk. All experiments must include automated telemetry and a rollback flag.
- Review: post-run review within 5 business days with artifacts: raw telemetry, analysis notebook, and promotion recommendation.
- Promotion: promotion to production requires an explicit promotion PRD that maps metrics to production SLOs and cost commitments.

Experiment brief template (single page)

- Title
- Owner and team
- Background and hypothesis
- Primary metric and success threshold
- Safety metrics and hard stop thresholds
- Estimated cost delta and burn budget (USD/month or tokens/month)
- Duration and traffic target (sandbox %, reserved pool)
- Data retention and PII considerations
- Rollback criteria and owner contact

Runbook / step-by-step (numbered)

1) Create Experiment Brief and attach canonical prompt set and baseline snapshots.
2) Submit ERB request (email + link) and allow 48 business hours for approval; emergency experiments can request expedited review.
3) Provision lab resources via the Lab provisioning CLI:
   - CLI example: redwood-lab provision --cluster lab-q4-2028 --variant v01 --quant-int8 --budget 5000
4) Deploy experiment and enable telemetry collector with tags: experiment-id, owner, vertical.
5) Monitor dashboards for safety thresholds; on breach, execute: redwood-lab rollback --experiment <id> --reason "safety-threshold-breach"
6) Run until pre-declared minimum sample size or duration achieved.
7) Produce post-run report and present to ERB for promotion decision.

Telemetry and dashboards (minimum required)

- Top-level: primary metric trend, median and p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, KV/cache hit ratio.
- Fidelity: prompt-set-specific scoring charts and confusion breakdowns.
- Economics: estimated per-request cost and projected monthly run-rate.

Cost and resourcing

- Each experiment must declare a hard burn budget. Default sandbox budget: $5k/month. Any experiment expecting > $20k must receive Finance sign-off.
- Lab clusters are billed to an internal cost center; chargeback to product teams occurs monthly.

Architecture / reference configuration (table)

Service | Purpose | Default config | Owner
------- | ------- | -------------- | -----
lab-cluster-q4 | isolated GPU pool for small-batch pilots | 4 x A100-80GB, preemptible | eng-infra
lab-routing-proxy | routes sandbox tokens | rate-limit 100rps | eng-platform
telemetry-collector | ingest and annotate experiment traces | retention 90d, schema v2 | signals
variant-orchestrator | manage model variant routing and fallback | canary 2%, fallback policy: immediate | runtime

Promotion criteria to production canary

- Primary metric meets or exceeds success threshold with 95% confidence.
- No safety metric breaches during full experiment window.
- Performance headroom validated on production-like load (stress test p99 < 1.2x baseline).
- Cost delta within committed commercial bounds.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Unanticipated fidelity regressions in long tail prompts. Mitigation: extended long-tail prompt set run and manual review by Applied ML.
- Risk: Cost overrun. Mitigation: hard burn budget and automated budget-enforcement hooks.
- Risk: Security/data exposure. Mitigation: experiments default to synthetic or scrubbed prompt-sets; PII experiments require Security sign-off.

Appendix: sample experiment config (YAML)

experiment_id: lab-q4-2028-quant-01
owner: asha.patel@redwood.com
variant: gptx-mini-v1
quant_profile: int8-safety-1
traffic_target: 1%
duration_days: 14
burn_budget_usd: 3000
primary_metric: "support-ticket-resolution-rate"

Related artifacts and links

- Canonical prompt-set repo: github.com/redwood-inference/lab-prompt-sets
- Telemetry dashboard: /dashboards/lab-experiments/q4-2028
- ERB meeting notes (template): /product-docs/roadmap-and-themes/erb-meeting-notes-template

Contact and ownership

- Program owner: Asha Patel (Product Lead) — asha.patel@redwood.com
- Applied ML lead: Miguel Ramirez — miguel.ramirez@redwood.com
- Runtime liaison: Rajiv Menon — rajiv.menon@redwood.com

Document change log

- 2028-10-02: created by Asha Patel
- 2028-11-15: added telemetry requirements and lab CLI example (reviewer: Sophie Chen)
- 2028-12-12: finalized Q4 run schedule and ERB membership (reviewers: Miguel Ramirez, Jonah Li)

payload.page_title: Sunset Strategy and Migration Playbook for Model Variants

sections.body:
Purpose
This playbook defines Redwood's standard process for sunsetting (deprecating) model variants and migrating traffic/customers to successor variants or fallback models. It is intended for product managers, engineering, SRE, customer success, and legal/compliance when a model variant reaches end-of-life (EOL) or is being replaced for cost, quality, or licensing reasons.

Scope
- Applies to public and dedicated model variants listed in the Redwood model catalog.
- Excludes emergency security removals (see Incident Response Security runbook).
- Covers technical migration, billing adjustments, communications, monitoring, and rollback.

Goals and success metrics
- Minimize customer impact: <95% of active routes migrated within 30 days of migration window start.
- Quality safety net: model-output regression rate <1.0% (as measured by defined eval set).
- Availability: no increase in 99th percentile latency greater than 20% during migration windows.
- Billing correctness: 100% of migrated routes billed to the successor variant or fallback by close of billing cycle following cutover.

Preconditions (must be completed before announcing sunset)
1. Successor variant selected and validated in the staging environment.
2. Compatibility matrix completed (tokenization, supported functions/tool-calling, max sequence length).
3. Regression test report (eval harness) showing parity or documented deltas and mitigation.
4. Billing mapping defined (old variant -> new variant / credit conversion).
5. Customer-impact list exported (active tenants, routes, critical SLAs).
6. Legal review complete for licensing changes.

Timeline and Phase Checklist
- Phase 0: Planning (T-60 to T-30 days)
  - Owner: Product PM
  - Tasks: select successor, run regression/eval, prepare compatibility matrix, draft customer notice, schedule SRE/CS working session.
- Phase 1: Announcement (T-30 days)
  - Owner: Go-to-market & CS
  - Tasks: send formal notice to affected customers, publish public deprecation notice page, set in-console sunset banner for impacted routes.
- Phase 2: Migration Window (T-30 to T+30 days)
  - Owner: CS + Engineering
  - Tasks: enable migration tooling, assist customers with testing, open migration tickets, monitor KPIs.
- Phase 3: Cutover & Billing Transition (T+30 days)
  - Owner: Billing + SRE
  - Tasks: automated cutover of non-responsive tenants (if allowed), finalize billing mapping, update catalog.
- Phase 4: Post-Cutover (T+30 to T+60 days)
  - Owner: Product + SRE
  - Tasks: collect telemetry, run postmortem, remove variant from public catalog, archive artifacts.

Ownership and escalation
- Product PM: overall program owner, stakeholder communication, final approval for cutover.
- Eng-SRE: migration tooling, routing policies, automated fallback flow.
- Customer Success: coordinate customer migration plans, SLA negotiation, issue triage.
- Billing & Finance: price/credit mapping, invoice adjustments, reconciliation.
- Legal & Security: confirm compliance and license termination conditions.
- Escalation: Pager duty for Migration SRE rotation; create incident channel #migration-eol in Slack.

Communication templates (shortened)
- Customer Notice Subject: Important: Redwood is retiring model variant [VARIANT_NAME] on [DATE]
- Body: "We are retiring [VARIANT_NAME] on [DATE]. Your routes using this variant will be able to switch to [SUCCESSOR_NAME] with identical API contracts. If you prefer, Redwood will schedule a migration session with your CS representative. Details: [link to migration guide]."
- In-console banner: "[VARIANT_NAME] will be retired on [DATE]. Click to view migration options."

Technical migration steps (engineers)
1. Validate that successor model variant is compatible:
   - Tokenizer check: ensure same token mapping for sentinel tokens.
   - Function/tool compatibility: run smoke tests for tool-calls and streaming.
2. Create a migration plan for each tenant route (RouteID list).
3. Use migration API (example):
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/migrations \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"route_ids": ["route-123"], "from_variant": "v1-small-quant", "to_variant": "v2-core-q4", "dry_run": true}'
4. Run dry-run and collect perf/quality samples into /tmp/migration-samples.
5. If dry-run passes, schedule a canary subset (5% traffic) and observe for 48 hours.

Canary and rollback policy
- Canary size: default 5% of traffic or up to 3 enterprise tenants (whichever smaller).
- Canary SLO gates (must pass to expand):
  - 99th percentile latency increase < 15%.
  - Error rate increase < 0.5% absolute.
  - Eval regression delta < 0.5% in key prompt set.
- Rollback triggers:
  - Any customer-impacting error > 1% for 15 minutes.
  - Quality regressions discovered by CS for a paying tenant.
- Rollback process:
  1. Pause migration orchestration.
  2. Re-route canary traffic back to previous variant.
  3. Open an incident and assign to migration SRE.
  4. Product to convene mitigation review within 8 hours.

Monitoring and dashboards
- Minimum dashboards to create/update prior to migration:
  - Migration progress dashboard (routes migrated, percent complete).
  - Per-variant latency & error heatmap.
  - Customer-impact dashboard (top 10 tenants by errors during migration).
- Example queries (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - error_rate_by_variant = sum(rate(request_errors_total{variant!=""}[5m])) by (variant) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (variant)
  - p99_latency_migration = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{migration_window="true"}[5m])) by (le, variant))
- Alerts:
  - migration_error_rate_high: alert if error_rate_by_variant for successor > 1.5x baseline for 10m.
  - migration_latency_regression: alert if p99_latency_migration > baseline_p99 * 1.2 for 15m.

Billing & credits handling
| Scenario | Action | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer migrates voluntarily before cutover | Bill successor variant from migration date | Billing | Preserve prorated credits where applicable |
| Customer remains on deprecated variant after window (no response) | Auto-migrate to fallback variant if policy allows; otherwise disable route per contract | Product + Legal | For enterprise, require explicit approval before disabling |
| Pricing changes between variants | Issue pro-rated invoice adjustment or one-time credit | Finance | Communicate in announcement letter |

Data retention and audit
- Archive logs and sample outputs for all migration dry-runs and canaries for 90 days in the migrations bucket: s3://redwood-archives/migrations/{variant}/{date}/.
- Export audit trail: who performed migration, timestamp, tool versions. This must be attached to the migration ticket.

Postmortem and learning loop
- Owner: Product PM
- Deliverable within 14 days of cutover: Postmortem doc with root cause, impact, mitigations, and action items. Include customer feedback summary.
- Feed action items into roadmap: tag as high/med/low and assign owners.

Operational playbook quick checklist (for on-call)
- Verify migration window is active and banners are visible.
- Confirm SRE migration job queue is empty after cutover.
- Validate billing mapping for at least 3 customers.
- Run smoke test script against 10 migrated routes.

Appendix A — Example migration CLI snippets
- Dry run:
  redwoodctl migrate --routes-file routes.csv --from v1-small-quant --to v2-core-q4 --dry-run --output migration-report.json
- Execute migration (canary 5%):
  redwoodctl migrate --routes-file routes.csv --from v1-small-quant --to v2-core-q4 --canary 5 --notify cs-team

Appendix B — Communication timeline checklist
1. T-30: Email notice and in-console banner (public doc published).
2. T-21: Host migration office hours (recording linked).
3. T-7: Reminder; targeted outreach to high-usage tenants.
4. Cutover: Final confirmation 24 hours before.
5. T+7: Follow-up with migrated customers and CS satisfaction survey.

FAQ (select)
- Q: Can customers opt-out of auto-migration?
  A: Enterprise customers can request an exception; it requires a signed amendment. Self-serve customers are subject to the public policy.
- Q: Are token counts preserved across variants?
  A: Tokenization differences are listed in the compatibility matrix; migration tooling rewrites static prompt templates where safe.

Document maintenance
- Review cadence: annual or whenever a major serving change occurs.
- Next scheduled review: 2027-09-20.

Related artifacts and links
- Compatibility matrix (link to internal file)
- Migration API spec (internal link)
- Billing mapping spreadsheet (internal finance link)

Owners and contact points
- Product PM: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@redwood.ai)
- Migration SRE Lead: Priya Nair (on-call pager)
- Customer Success Lead: Diego Martinez

End of document.

payload.page_title: Serving Tier Evolution: Consumption, Migration, and Pricing Playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines an operationally actionable approach for evolving Redwood Inference serving tiers over the next 12–18 months. It combines product strategy (tier definitions, pricing signals), migration mechanics (customer-facing plans and engineering rollout steps), and operational guardrails (SLOs, capacity commitments, monitoring) to keep customer applications stable while improving cost-to-serve and unit economics.

Goals:

- Reduce hosted per-token cost for high-throughput customers by 18–25% through tier consolidation, predictable bundles, and improved batching defaults.
- Provide a low-friction migration path for customers to move between tiers with clear billing, SLO, and tooling guarantees.
- Minimize churn and support overhead during changes by offering canary windows, opt-in accelerators, and automatic fallbacks.

Context and drivers:

1) Market: customers increasingly require predictable monthly ocost commitments tied to SLOs rather than pure burst pricing.
2) Platform: recent runtime optimizations (KV cache improvements, quantization recommendations) enable new cost bands with minimal quality regressions.
3) Sales: enterprise customers ask for clearer upgrade/migration policy between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Guiding principles:

- Backwards compatibility: any tier change must preserve API, response semantics, and existing client SDK contracts.
- Observable economics: customers must be able to see the cost impact of tier changes in the Console before committing.
- Safe rollout: production changes must include automated fallback to prior tier variants when latency or error budgets are violated.
- Migration symmetry: every upward move (to higher capacity or lower latency tier) must have a symmetric downgrade path.

Tier definitions (canonical):

We define three consumer-facing serving tiers that map to internal capacity and routing policies. Table below is illustrative — concrete numeric bands will be assigned per-region in the pricing exercise.

| Tier name | Target customer profile | Key guarantees | Typical use cases | Commitment model |
|-----------|------------------------|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Standard | Startups, dev & test | < 500ms median, best-effort batching | Chatbots, dev APIs, prototypes | Pay-as-you-go or monthly credits |
| Predictable | Mid-market apps with steady throughput | 95th pct latency SLO, 10% cost discount vs Standard | SaaS features, background generations | 3–12 month creditized commitments with rollover |
| Enterprise Dedicated | High-throughput, regulated workloads | Latency & availability SLAs (SLA credits), network isolation | Legal/financial production services | Reserved capacity (monthly/annual), optional on-prem packaging |

Migration strategy and timeline (12 months):

1. Q1 — Pilot: select 8 existing Predictable and 3 Enterprise customers to participate in an early migration pilot. Collect telemetry (latency, cost per 1M tokens, error rates) and customer qualitative feedback.
2. Q2 — Console tools: ship an in-Console migration preview that simulates 30/60/90-day cost and SLO implications and exposes a one-click scheduled migration window.
3. Q3 — Opt-in accelerator: automated batching/quantization recommendations for customers that accept migration; include a reversible rollout that can be reverted within 24 hours.
4. Q4 — Broad rollout: new sign-ups default to the updated tier map; legacy customers receive a multi-month campaign with optional incentives to migrate.

Rollout playbook (engineering + customer success):

- Pre-rollout checklist (owner: product + eng-platform):
  - Confirm telemetry instrumentation: per-route token counts, model variant mapping, latency percentiles, KV cache hit-rate.
  - Capacity safety nets: ensure fallback routes and variant compatibility exist for top 20 routes by traffic.
  - Billing simulation: generate per-customer cost delta reports for the past 90 days.

- Migration run steps (customer success lead):
  1. Run Console migration preview with customer and share simulated bill.
  2. Schedule migration window (2–4 hours low-traffic).
  3. Enable staging route on Predictable/Enterprise variant and run 5% traffic for 48 hours.
  4. If errors or latency SLOs exceed thresholds, automatically revert and open an incident (see incident template below).
  5. Post-migration: 30-day quality check and credit reconciliation.

CLI / API examples (for engineering ops):

# Preview migration for route
redwood migrate-preview --route-id r_12345 --target-tier predictable --lookback 90

# Schedule migration window
redwood migrate-schedule --route-id r_12345 --target-tier predictable --start 2026-06-14T00:00:00Z --duration 4h

Pricing and packaging considerations:

- Commitment tiers must be creditized: customers pre-pay for a bundle of tokens and receive preferential routing and burst retention.
- Flexible rollover: unused committed tokens roll into a six-month buffer to reduce churn/complaints at quarter boundaries.
- Add-on: latency buffer entitlement for Enterprise customers that receive automatic rerouting to higher-cost variants if SLOs are in danger.

Sample customer scenarios (illustrative):

| Customer profile | Current spend | Migration offer | Expected delta (monthly) | Notes |
|------------------|---------------|-----------------|-------------------------|-------|
| Growth SaaS | $25k | Move to Predictable with 6mo credits | -12% | Reduced per-token cost, small config change
| AI-native startup | $2k | Stay Standard + optimize batching | -18% | No commitment required
| Regulated fintech | $120k | Enterprise Dedicated reserved capacity | +5% (but stable) | SLA + isolation required

SLOs, monitoring, and rollback triggers:

- Tier-level SLOs (examples):
  - Standard: 95% requests < 800ms, availability 99.5%
  - Predictable: 95% requests < 500ms, availability 99.8%
  - Enterprise Dedicated: 99% requests < 350ms, availability 99.95%

- Rollback triggers (auto):
  - 5xx rate increases > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 30 minutes.
  - P50/P95 latency regression exceeding tier SLO by > 30% for 30 minutes.
  - KV cache hit-rate drop > 20% resulting in >5% token-cost increase.

Ownership and approvals:

- Product: Aisha Patel (owner) — product direction and migration policy.
- Eng-Platform: Daniel Kim — migration tooling, traffic shaping, rollout automation.
- Eng-SRE: Marina Kuznetsova — SLO definitions, rollback automation, incident playbook.
- Sales & CS: assigned AE/CSM per customer — commercial negotiation and scheduling.

Risk register and mitigations:

- Risk: Unexpected quality regressions after applying quantization or batching optimizations.
  - Mitigation: Canary at 5–10% traffic with automated quality-eval checks; require manual opt-in for hallucination-sensitive routes.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to opaque cost simulations.
  - Mitigation: Provide downloadable cost-simulation spreadsheets and a 30-day window for credits/reconciliation.
- Risk: Capacity contention during major migrations.
  - Mitigation: Stagger migrations by region and use a dynamic token-admission policy to protect legacy routes.

Incident template (to be used if rollback is triggered):

1. Summary: one-line description (e.g., "Predictable migration r_12345 reverted due to latency spike").
2. Start time / end time.
3. Impacted customers and routes.
4. Immediate mitigation: rollback to previous tier variant.
5. Data collected: traces, p50/p95/p99 latency, error traces, KV cache metrics.
4. Postmortem owner and timeline for mitigation.

Communications and GTM:

- Messaging pillars: clarity (cost & SLO effects), control (Console preview + opt-in), safety (rollbacks & credits).
- Customer comms cadence: pre-announce (8 weeks), migration invite (4 weeks), migration reminder (7 days, 48 hours, 4 hours), post-migration survey (7 days, 30 days).
- Sales enablement: one-pager playbook with sample scripts, objection handling, and a calculator for conversion economics.

Appendix: Console UX notes and data exports:

- Migration preview must show: current bucketed token consumption, simulated post-migration latency distribution, 30/60/90 day cost projection, and a downloadable CSV containing per-route deltas.
- Telemetry export columns: route_id, route_name, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, errors_5xx, time_window_start.

Next steps / decisions required:

- Approve numeric pricing bands for Predictable and Enterprise tiers per-region (finance + pricing).
- Sign-off on the rollback triggers and automatic revert windows (eng-sre + legal).
- Pilot customer list and incentive packages (sales + customer success).

Document change log:

- 2025-10-15: Draft created by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-18: Added migration playbook and CLI examples (review feedback incorporated).
- 2026-02-25: Updated SLO bands and rollback thresholds following eng-sre review.

Related artifacts / links:

- Migration preview design mocks: product-docs/design-specs/migration-preview-console-mockups-2025-11
- Cost-simulation notebook: product-docs/requirements/cost-simulation-notebook-2025-09
- Quantization safety checklist: product-docs/requirements/quality-aware-quantization-rollout-prd-2026-12-01

For questions or to propose changes, contact the document owner (Aisha Patel) or add comments on this page.
