payload.page_title: unified-edge-to-cloud-prd-rollout-2028-04-18

sections.body: This PRD and rollout playbook describes the product scope, requirements, design constraints, and step-by-step launch plan for the "Converged Edge-to-Cloud" inference offering. The goal is a single developer-facing package (API + runtime configuration + billing model) that allows customers to run Redwood inference consistently across lightweight edge appliances and the hosted/dedicated cloud surface with predictable SLAs and cost controls.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Increasing demand for latency-sensitive, privacy-preserving use cases (on-device scoring, kiosk assistants, regulated industrial inference).
- Customers want a single contract and SDK that abstracts runtime location while preserving SLOs and cost transparency.
- Competitive differentiation: ship a first-class hybrid experience with automated fallback, delta-model sync, and unified observability.
sections.heading: Why this project now

sections.body:
1) API/SDK surface updates to support location hints (edge/preferred-region/fallback-policy).
2) Runtime packaging for validated edge appliances (NVIDIA Jetson Orin family, selected Intel/AMD servers with discrete GPUs, and lightweight CPU-only devices), including quantization profiles and preforked KV cache snapshots.
3) Hybrid cache coordinator integration to maintain prefix/KV coherency between edge caches and cloud caches.
4) Billing + metering rules for hybrid consumption (local compute credits, sync delta charges, and cloud fallback token billing).
5) Console UX for per-tenant edge fleet management, rollout controls, and fidelity knobs.
6) Observability and quality monitoring: edge telemetry ingestion, synthetic prompt set regression checks, and drift detection.
sections.heading: Scope (what's in)

sections.body:
- Support for fully air-gapped on-prem appliance installs (handled in Private wave).
- Marketplace bundling or reseller pricing (handled by GTM in Phase 2).
sections.heading: Out of scope (for Phase 1)

sections.body:
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency for edge-local requests <= 60ms for short completions (<128 tokens) on validated appliances.
- Availability: Fleet-level uptime for edge nodes >= 99.5% calendar-month.
- Cost delta: Average per-token cost for hybrid workloads competitive with cloud-only by <= 15% after local compute credits applied.
- Quality: No more than 1.5% regression in evaluation prompt-set for quantized variants deployed to edge compared to cloud baseline.
- Adoption: 10 paying customers with production edge deployments within 6 months of launch.
sections.heading: Goals and success metrics (KPIs)

sections.body:
- As an ML engineer, I want to pin a model variant to run locally on kiosk hardware and fall back to cloud if local capacity is saturated.
- As a platform engineer, I want console controls to rollback fidelity settings for a set of devices by region.
- As a finance lead, I want clear monthly metering rows that separate local compute credits from cloud token billing for chargeback.
sections.heading: User stories (representative)

sections.body:
- RQ-01: SDK accepts location hints and fallback policy flags with input validation and documented defaults.
- RQ-02: Edge runtime image with validated quantization profiles for each supported model family and hardware profile.
- RQ-03: Delta sync protocol to update small model patches (<200MB) without full model replacement.
- RQ-04: Hybrid cache coordinator that guarantees eventual KV prefix consistency and TTL-based eviction policy tuned for edge capacity.
- RQ-05: Telemetry pipeline extension to tag edge-originated traces and expose token-level cost attribution.
- RQ-06: Billing rules engine update to support local compute credits, monthly device allowances, and on-demand fallback token charges.
- RQ-07: Console flows for fleet onboarding, per-device rollout groups, and canary controls (percent-based, geo-based, and tag-based).
sections.heading: High-level requirements (must-have)

sections.body:
- Memory: Edge runtime must operate with a peak resident set <= 9GB for the baseline quantized variant on the target device class.
- Boot time: Local model serving process must be ready (accept queries) within 90s after appliance reboot.
- Security: All edge images must support disk encryption at rest and TLS1.3 mTLS to Redwood control plane. Key management must integrate with customer KMS in Private wave; for Phase 1 use Redwood-managed ephemeral keys with audit logging.
- Upgrade model: Rolling in-place updates preferred; fallback to blue-green for devices that support container orchestration.
sections.heading: Non-functional constraints and design constraints

sections.body:
| Hardware class | Model family | Quant profile | Expected P95 <128 tokens | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Jetson-Orin (NX) | LLaMA-like 7B | int8-q4 | 58ms | validated reference image v1.0 |
| Intel NUC (i7, 16GB) | Small LLMs (3B) | int8-q4 | 85ms | CPU-only baseline; recommend 2 threads per request |
| AWS Graviton (edge region) | 7B quantized | bf16-fp16 mix | 70ms | cloud-side instance; for hybrid testing only |
sections.heading: Compatibility matrix (validated hardware/profiles)

sections.body:
- Use a delta-model sync instead of full pull to avoid network egress spikes and to enable rapid rollbacks.
- Implement a lightweight local controller (single binary) that handles routing: local -> cloud fallback -> queued local retry. This keeps the SDK surface minimal and avoids complex client-side logic.
- Favor quantization profiles that prioritize quality above raw throughput for Phase 1; provide an "aggressive-cost" profile in Phase 2.
sections.heading: Design notes (key decisions and rationale)

sections.body:
- New request fields (SDK v2.5+):
  - location_hint: ["edge-local", "region:us-west-2", "cloud-preferred"]
  - fallback_policy: {"mode": "immediate|queue|failover", "max_cloud_tokens": 5000}  # represented as JSON in SDK
sections.heading: API / SDK changes (example)

sections.body:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
resp = client.generate(
  model="rw-7b-q4-edge",
  prompt="Summarize the last 10 messages",
  location_hint="edge-local",
  fallback_policy={"mode":"immediate","max_cloud_tokens":2000}
)
```
sections.heading: Example usage (pseudo-code)

sections.body:
1) Alpha (internal + 2 customers) — 8 weeks
  - Deliver edge runtime v1 images for Jetson NX and NUC, SDK v2.5 beta, basic console fleet view.
  - Acceptance: internal synthetic suite and two pilot customers validated.
2) Private Beta (10 customers) — 12 weeks
  - Add telemetry ingestion for edge traces, cost attribution, and delta sync resiliency tests.
  - Onboard billing rules for compute credits and per-device allowances.
  - Acceptance: automated regression tests pass; customers complete standard onboarding checklist.
3) Public GA — 6 weeks after Beta (contingent on metrics)
  - Full console UX, documentation, runbooks, and sales collateral.
  - Tiered pricing and packaging available (see Pricing implications).
sections.heading: Rolling launch plan (phased)

sections.body:
- Canary knobs: percent rollout (1%, 5%, 25%), geo filter, device-tag filter.
- Health checks during canary: p95 latency, error rate, model-quality delta on synthetic prompts.
- Automatic rollback triggers: 2x increase in error-rate over baseline OR 3% absolute regression in quality checks OR sustained p95 > 2x target for 30 minutes.
sections.heading: Canary and rollback controls

sections.body:
- Synthetic prompt set: 500 prompts per customer partitioned by features (QA, instruction, multi-turn). Run locally and in cloud; track loss and answer similarity (ROUGE/BLEU or embedding-based cosine).
- Edge heartbeat: 60s cadence metric with last-seen and resource snapshot. Alert if offline > 10 minutes for > 2% of fleet.
- Cost dashboards: per-device, per-route, and aggregated monthly views with drilldowns to token-level attribution.
sections.heading: Observability and quality guardrails

sections.body:
- Pricing primitives: monthly device allowance (credits), local compute credits (per-second or per-request), fallback cloud token usage (per-token rate).
- Example SKU: Edge Starter — up to 50 devices, 10k local compute credits/month, fallback at cloud rates + 10% admin fee.
- Finance requirement: must expose line-itemized export for chargeback and metered billing with invoice tagging for local vs cloud consumption.
sections.heading: Billing and packaging implications (summary)

sections.body:
- Onboarding checklist (operator):
  1) Register tenant and enable Edge feature flag.
  2) Provision device certificate via console and verify mTLS handshake.
  3) Push initial model delta and validate sample prompts.
  4) Set rollout group and start 1% canary.
- Incident response playbook summary:
  - If fleet-level p95 > threshold: increase fallback to cloud for affected groups, notify SRE and product owner, open incident ticket with root-cause label "edge-performance".
  - If delta sync fails: hold rollout, serve from previous model snapshot, and engage build/release to repackage delta.
sections.heading: Runbooks and day-2 ops (high level)

sections.body:
- SDK, runtime images, and console controls released to internal staging environment.
- End-to-end tests verifying: location hint routing, fallback behavior, delta sync, and telemetry tagging.
- Billing records generated for hybrid usage in a sandbox tenant and reconciled with Finance.
- Runbook and customer-facing docs drafted and peer-reviewed.
sections.heading: Acceptance criteria (definition of done)

sections.body:
- Risk: Edge device heterogeneity leads to inconsistent quality.
  - Mitigation: Validate a narrow set of reference appliances for Phase 1 and expose an "unsupported" warning in SDK.
- Risk: Network partitions cause heavy cloud fallback and cost spikes.
  - Mitigation: Default fallback policy for edge devices is backoff + queueing; provide cost-safes in console (per-device token caps).
- Risk: Model drift due to different quant profiles on edge.
  - Mitigation: Periodic quality sampling and rollback automation; ensure quant profile labels in model registry.
sections.heading: Risks and mitigations

sections.body:
- Product lead (overall): Maya Patel
- Eng owners: Runtime team (Amber Zhou), SDK/API (Noah Grant), Billing (Priya Shah)
- SRE/Infra: Omar Reyes
- Go-to-market: Anika Bose
sections.heading: Stakeholders and owners

sections.body:
1) Final definition and granularity of "local compute credit" (per-second vs per-inference).
2) Whether to allow customer-managed KMS for key material in Phase 1 (security trade-offs).
3) Exact default fallback policy — immediate vs queued with bounded cloud token cap.
sections.heading: Open questions (must resolve before Beta)

sections.body:
- Example device provisioning flow (CLI):
```
redwood device provision --tenant acme --device-id kiosk-42 --profile jetson-nx --cert-path ./kiosk-42.crt
```
- Example delta patch upload (CLI):
```
redwood models delta-upload --model rw-7b --patch ./rw-7b-patch-v1.2.delta --target-profile jetson-nx
```
- Reference test matrix location: confluence://product-docs/requirements/edge-validation-test-matrix (TBD)
sections.heading: Appendix (examples and reference commands)

sections.body:
- Expand supported appliance list and introduce an aggressive cost profile.
- Allow fully air-gapped installs with customer-provided KMS.
- Integrate with Redwood Optimize to propose on-device fidelity knobs automatically based on workload patterns.
sections.heading: Notes for go-forward (Phase 2 possibilities)

payload.page_title: PRD: Shadow Traffic for Quality Eval Metrics (Console & Rollouts)

sections.body:
Teams trust Redwood for safe rollouts based on latency/cost/error SLOs, but still lack a production-safe way to detect *quality* regressions (correctness, safety, instruction following, format adherence) when changing models/versions/quantization/prompt templates. This PRD proposes **Shadow Traffic**: duplicate a sampled subset of live requests to one or more candidate variants, score outputs asynchronously, and surface **quality deltas** alongside existing performance and error metrics—without affecting the user-visible response.

Shadow Traffic is designed to work across **Hosted**, **Dedicated**, and **Private** deployments using existing routing/rollout primitives (route configs, canaries, A/B) and Redwood’s eval-harness scoring templates.

---
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Run offline prompt sets that do not match production distribution.
- Manually sample production logs and run ad-hoc eval scripts (slow, non-deterministic, often violates retention policies).
- Deploy canaries and hope user feedback/support tickets surface regressions.
sections.heading: What customers do today

sections.body:
- Quality regressions often show up only under real production context (long contexts, tool outputs, domain-specific formats).
- Customers cannot accept user-visible risk during testing.
- Platform teams need consistent metrics and governance across many routes/teams.
sections.heading: Why this fails

sections.body:
- “We can’t justify switching models without a quality dashboard we trust.”
- “We need a pre-flight quality gate during rollouts—not a postmortem.”
- “We need strict retention/redaction; we cannot store prompts indefinitely.”

---
sections.heading: Customer pain (verbatim themes)

sections.body:
1. **Production-safe quality measurement**: shadow requests must never change user-visible responses and must be fail-open.
2. **Statistically meaningful deltas**: confidence intervals and minimum sample guidance built into the experience.
3. **Rollouts integration**: attach shadow experiment results to canary/A-B rollouts and support regression alerts.
4. **Minimal overhead**: strict budgets for latency impact, telemetry cardinality, and scoring compute.
5. **Security + compliance by default**: data minimization, redaction, short retention defaults, audit logs.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Full offline replay for arbitrary historical traffic beyond short retention.
- Executing arbitrary customer-supplied eval code inside Redwood (v1 focuses on Redwood-provided metrics + bring-your-own prompt sets via eval-harness where supported).
- Automatic rollback based on quality signals at launch (advisory-first; revisit post-beta).

---
sections.heading: Non-goals (v1)

sections.body:
**Jobs to be done**
- Compare candidate vs control quality during model/version/prompt changes.
- Understand *why* quality changed (examples, segments, rubric breakdown).
- Confidently recommend ship/rollback.

**Pain points**
- Offline eval sets miss production edge cases.
- Hard to correlate quality with latency/cost changes.
- Requires building internal pipelines.
sections.heading: Persona A: ML Engineer (Quality owner)

sections.body:
**Jobs to be done**
- Roll out changes safely across routes and teams.
- Enforce governance (sampling caps, data handling policies, RBAC).
- Avoid performance regressions and metrics stack overload.

**Pain points**
- High-cardinality metrics melt dashboards.
- Shadowing can create unpredictable cost if unbounded.
- Needs auditability and kill switches.
sections.heading: Persona B: Platform Engineer (Inference platform owner)

sections.body:
**Jobs to be done**
- Ensure shadow path does not impact user path.
- Detect scoring pipeline degradation (lag, backlog) and respond.

---
sections.heading: Persona C: SRE / Observability Engineer

sections.body:
1. **Create shadow experiment on a route**
   - As an ML Eng, I choose a route, specify sampling %, select 1–2 candidate variants (model version or config), and start.
2. **View quality deltas with confidence intervals**
   - As an ML Eng, I see rubric scores and heuristic metrics comparing control vs candidates over time and by segment.
3. **Drill into examples**
   - As an ML Eng, I can view redacted prompts/outputs (where allowed) for a small sample of flagged cases.
4. **Attach to rollout**
   - As a Platform Eng, I run a canary rollout and view shadow quality signals in the rollout timeline.
5. **Governance + safety**
   - As a Platform Eng, I cap sampling and scoring budgets per org/tenant and can disable shadowing instantly.

---
sections.heading: User stories

sections.body:
- Shadow traffic routing policy attached to a **route** and/or **rollout**.
- Deterministic request fingerprinting + bucketing for consistent comparisons.
- Async scoring pipeline for a default metric bundle (see below).
- Console UI: create experiment, results dashboard, drilldown examples (permission-gated), export.
- Alerting for quality regressions and scoring pipeline health.
- Hosted, Dedicated, Private support with environment-appropriate retention/storage defaults.
sections.heading: In-scope

sections.body:
- Unlimited number of candidates per experiment (v1: max 2 shadow variants per control).
- Arbitrary custom metrics plugins executed inside Redwood.

---
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
- **Control**: the variant that serves the user response.
- **Shadow variant**: candidate variant that receives mirrored requests but does not serve responses.
- **Shadow experiment**: configuration + time window + scoring rubric version.
- **Quality delta**: difference in metric distributions between control and candidate with confidence bounds.

---
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Create shadow experiment from:
  - A route (standalone), or
  - A rollout object (canary/A-B), linked for traceability.
- Required fields:
  - Control target (route current target)
  - Shadow targets (1–2)
  - Sampling rate (default 1%, configurable with caps)
  - Fingerprinting key selection (default: stable hash of normalized prompt + request metadata; excludes raw PII fields)
  - Runtime guardrails (timeouts, circuit breaker behavior)
  - Scoring bundle + rubric version pin
- Optional fields:
  - Segment filters (e.g., request_type=chat vs completion; region; model family)
  - Request field allowlist for storage (Dedicated/Private may expand)
  - Customer-defined tags (restricted list; validated against cardinality policy)
sections.heading: 1) Experiment configuration

sections.body:
- Fail-open: shadow failures must not affect the user-visible path.
- Strict timeouts on shadow requests.
- Backpressure + circuit breaker:
  - If shadow queue backlog or shadow target error rate exceeds thresholds, auto-disable shadow forwarding for that experiment (with audit event + banner in Console).
- Streaming support:
  - Control response streams as normal.
  - Shadow captures are bounded (e.g., up to N tokens or until timeout) with explicit “partial_capture” markers.
sections.heading: 2) Shadow routing behavior

sections.body:
- Default capture: minimal fields needed for scoring (see “Data handling” section).
- Redaction pipeline applied before persistence.
- Retention defaults:
  - Hosted: short retention (default 7 days for scored aggregates; 24–72 hours for sampled examples).
  - Dedicated: configurable retention windows with org admin approval.
  - Private: customer-controlled storage location and retention; support “no examples stored” mode.
sections.heading: 3) Data capture & privacy

sections.body:
- Asynchronous scoring with retry/dedupe.
- Support:
  - Heuristic metrics (fast, deterministic)
  - Model-graded rubric metrics (slower, costed)
- Store:
  - Per-request scores (short retention)
  - Aggregates by time window + safe dimensions (longer retention)
- Rubric version pinning:
  - Experiment results always labeled with rubric version; comparisons across rubric versions are not shown by default.
sections.heading: 4) Scoring pipeline

sections.body:
- “Shadow Experiments” page: create, list, status, last data received, scoring lag indicator.
- Results view:
  - Metric deltas with confidence intervals
  - Trend over time (hour/day)
  - Segment filters (cardinality-safe)
  - Clear “not enough samples yet” states with guidance
- Examples drilldown:
  - Permission-gated (RBAC + audit)
  - Redacted views by default; download/export gated by role
- Rollout integration:
  - Rollout timeline shows linked shadow experiment status and top regressions.

---
sections.heading: 5) Console UX (v1 must-haves)

sections.body: v1 ships a **default metric bundle** intended to cover common regression types while keeping costs and ambiguity manageable.
sections.heading: Default quality metric bundle (v1)

sections.body:
1. **Format adherence**
   - Checks: valid JSON, required keys present, schema match, no extraneous text.
   - Inputs: output text; optional schema.
   - Caveat: strict schemas can over-penalize benign variations.

2. **Refusal rate (proxy)**
   - Detect refusals using pattern + classifier heuristics.
   - Caveat: false positives for safe disclaimers.

3. **Tool/function calling structure validity** (if applicable)
   - Valid tool name + arguments parse + required args.

4. **Length/verbosity drift**
   - Mean/median output tokens; tail behavior.
   - Used as a diagnostic, not a “quality score.”

5. **Error-classification deltas**
   - Increase in empty outputs, truncation markers, partial streaming captures.
sections.heading: A) Heuristic metrics (low cost, deterministic)

sections.body:
1. **Instruction following (rubric score 1–5)**
   - Model-graded rubric prompts tuned for general instruction compliance.
   - Requires stable rubric model/version.

2. **Safety / policy compliance (rubric score + flags)**
   - Detects unsafe content categories and refusal appropriateness.
   - Output: categorical flags + score.

3. **Grounding/faithfulness proxy (where applicable)**
   - For requests with provided context: checks whether answer cites/uses given context.
   - Note: v1 is a proxy, not a formal factuality guarantee.
sections.heading: B) Model-graded metrics (higher cost; async)

sections.body:
- Domain-specific correctness (requires custom evals; roadmap).
- Full jailbreak robustness testing (separate security program).

---
sections.heading: v1 metric exclusions (explicit)

sections.body:
v1 supports a restricted set of dimensions for aggregation:
- route_id (bucketed where needed)
- deployment_mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- region
- request_type (chat/completions/embeddings where relevant)
- model_id (control + shadow)
- rubric_version
- outcome (success/error/timeout/partial_capture)
sections.heading: Dimensions & segmentation (cardinality-safe)

sections.body:
- customer_user_id
- prompt_id (unless bucketed/coarsened)
- raw customer tags beyond an allowlisted set

---
sections.heading: Explicitly not supported as aggregation dimensions in v1

sections.body:
- At least **3 beta customers** actively running shadow experiments weekly.
- Customers can make a ship/rollback decision using the dashboard within **< 30 minutes** of review time.
- At least **2 documented saves** where shadow metrics caught a regression before user exposure.
sections.heading: Product success (beta)

sections.body:
- **User-path impact**:
  - p99 latency impact on control path: **<= 1%** at default sampling.
  - No increased error rates attributable to shadowing.
- **Shadow path reliability**:
  - Shadow forwarding success rate (when enabled): **>= 99%** excluding shadow target errors.
  - Scoring pipeline: **95% of scored results available within 30 minutes** (target; measure separately by metric type).
- **Observability safety**:
  - No sustained metrics cardinality alerts from enabling shadow traffic under recommended configs.
sections.heading: Technical success

sections.body:
- Confidence intervals shown for all primary deltas.
- Clear UI indicators for: insufficient sample size, scoring lag, partial captures, rubric version.

---
sections.heading: Trust & interpretability

sections.body:
- Finalize ADRs (routing placement, telemetry model).
- Define metric bundle v1 and rubric versioning policy.
- Sign off retention/redaction defaults with Security.
sections.heading: Phase 0 (Requirements + architecture) — 2 weeks

sections.body:
- Shadow routing MVP + deterministic bucketing.
- Telemetry events v1 + basic aggregates.
- Scoring pipeline for heuristics + 1 model-graded rubric (instruction following).
- Internal dogfood on Redwood-owned tenants; weekly review.
sections.heading: Phase 1 (MVP + dogfood) — 4–6 weeks

sections.body:
- Console create/view flows + example drilldowns.
- Attach to rollouts (timeline + linkage).
- Regression alerts (advisory) + scoring lag alerts.
sections.heading: Phase 2 (Console + alerts + rollout integration) — 4 weeks

sections.body:
- Overhead benchmarks + backpressure tuning.
- Expanded rubric set (safety + format adherence + faithfulness proxy).
- Docs + SDK support; enablement.

---
sections.heading: Phase 3 (Hardening + GA readiness) — 4–6 weeks

sections.body:
**Principles**
- Shadow testing creates real incremental cost (extra inference on shadow targets + scoring compute + storage).
- Packaging should encourage safe use (sampling caps) while aligning with value.

**Proposed packaging direction (subject to PM-1845 decision)**
- Hosted:
  - Included: heuristic metrics + limited sampling caps.
  - Add-on: model-graded scoring pack (billed per scored request or per 1K scored requests) with higher retention.
- Dedicated:
  - Included: shadow routing + heuristics.
  - Add-on: model-graded scoring (bundled commit) + higher retention and examples.
- Private:
  - Base: feature available; scoring options depend on deployment constraints.
  - Add-on: compliance pack for extended audit/retention controls where needed.

**Console cost transparency requirements**
- Experiment creation flow must estimate incremental costs:
  - Shadow inference cost (by sampling % and target type)
  - Scoring cost (heuristic vs model-graded)
  - Storage/retention cost impact (if applicable)

---
sections.heading: Pricing & packaging assumptions (v1)

sections.body:
- Clear upcoming model/version/quantization change (time-bound decision).
- Willing to run shadow experiments for at least 2–4 weeks.
- Has a defined “quality owner” and a platform admin to configure policies.
- Accepts default rubric metrics (or can map them to internal expectations).
sections.heading: Beta selection criteria

sections.body:
1. **Northstar Customer Support AI** (Dedicated prospect / early adopter)
   - Why: high sensitivity to instruction following + safety; needs quality gates for upgrades.
   - Ask: “shadow evals during rollout” aligns directly.

2. **Aurora DevTools** (high-volume, cost-sensitive)
   - Why: can validate sampling guidance and cardinality safety under load.
   - Focus: dashboards, segmentation, cost transparency.

3. **HelioFin RegTech** (regulated fintech)
   - Why: validates retention/redaction defaults, audit logs, and Private/Dedicated controls.
   - Focus: “no examples stored” mode, auditability, data residency constraints.
sections.heading: Proposed beta candidates

sections.body:
- Dedicated Slack/CS channel + weekly check-ins.
- Preconfigured dashboards + alert templates.
- Guidance on sampling rates and minimum sample sizes.
sections.heading: Beta commitments (what we provide)

sections.body:
- Beta customers can run experiments without Redwood engineer intervention.
- No Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents attributable to shadow traffic for 30 days.
- Documented playbook for enable/disable and troubleshooting.

---
sections.heading: Exit criteria for GA

sections.body: - Shadow artifacts may contain customer prompts/contexts and model outputs (potentially sensitive).
sections.heading: Data classification

sections.body:
- Redaction: configurable allowlist + truncation + hashing of stable identifiers.
- Retention: short by default; longer retention requires explicit tenant setting and role.
- Access: RBAC-gated; example drilldowns require elevated permission; all access is audited.
- Export: disabled by default for Hosted; configurable for Dedicated/Private.
sections.heading: Default controls

sections.body:
- Support local storage backends and customer-managed keys.
- Support SIEM export of audit events.
- Allow disabling model-graded scoring if compute or policy prohibits.

---
sections.heading: Private deployment considerations

sections.body:
1. **Risk: Shadowing impacts tail latency or overloads data plane**
   - Mitigation: strict timeouts, async processing, circuit breaker, sampling caps, perf canary gates.

2. **Risk: Telemetry cardinality explosion**
   - Mitigation: dimension allowlist, bucketing, server-side enforcement, pre-launch review with Observability.

3. **Risk: Misleading metrics (false positives / poor calibration)**
   - Mitigation: ship limited, well-defined bundle; label metrics as “proxy”; require confidence intervals; include example-driven diagnostics.

4. **Risk: Privacy/regulatory violations**
   - Mitigation: default short retention, redaction-first storage, RBAC + audit, tenant-level opt-outs.

---
sections.heading: Risks & mitigations

sections.body:
- Control plane shadow policy schema + validation (Platform Control Plane).
- Smart routing mirroring + deterministic bucketing (Routing).
- Telemetry event schemas + pipelines (Telemetry/Analytics).
- Scoring workers + eval-harness integration (Applied ML/Evals).
- Console UI + APIs + RBAC (Console & Tooling).
- SRE guardrails, dashboards, and alerting policy (SRE/Observability).

---
sections.heading: Dependencies

sections.body:
1. What is the default sampling % for Hosted vs Dedicated (1% vs 0.5%) given expected scoring costs?
2. Should we allow >2 shadow variants in v1 for enterprise tenants, or hold for v2?
3. Which rubric model(s) are acceptable for model-graded scoring in Private deployments (customer-supplied vs Redwood-supplied) and how is that configured?
4. What is the GA stance on “automatic rollback” using quality signals: remain advisory, or allow opt-in thresholds?
5. What is the default behavior for storing examples (off by default vs on with strict retention) by deployment mode?

---
sections.heading: Open questions

sections.body:
- [ ] Shadow policy create/update audited (who, when, what changed)
- [ ] Kill switch per-tenant and per-experiment
- [ ] p99 overhead validated under perf canary suite
- [ ] Scoring lag dashboards + alerts + runbook links
- [ ] UI shows confidence intervals and minimum sample guidance
- [ ] Cardinality enforcement validated with synthetic worst-case tags
- [ ] Retention/redaction defaults signed off by Security and documented
sections.heading: Appendix: v1 requirements checklist (for launch readiness)

payload.page_title: Streaming session fidelity tiers — PRD, pricing & go-to-market launch playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This document describes the product requirements, technical design constraints, pricing model, SLOs, roadmap and the go-to-market (GTM) playbook for Streaming Session Fidelity Tiers — a capability that allows customers to select, negotiate, and pay for different fidelity (quality/latency/cost) operating points for long-lived streaming sessions. The goal is to productize a predictable, monetizable streaming surface that balances developer ergonomics, customer economics, and Redwood's serving costs.

Why this exists:
- Customers building interactive experiences (voice assistants, real-time summarization, multi-turn assistants, collaborative editing) need predictable streaming latency and cost for session-oriented workloads.
- Current per-token pricing and ad-hoc fallback behaviors create unpredictable bills and poor developer UX for long sessions with bursty traffic.
- Fidelity tiers let customers trade quality/cost with explicit SLAs and usage credits tied to session duration and streaming shape.

Scope (what's included):
1) API surface for declaring session fidelity tier at session creation and mid-session negotiation.
2) Pricing & packaging model (per-session credits, time-decayed token allowances, streaming duration discounts).
3) Runtime contract: SLOs (median p50/p90 latency, token throughput, availability), documented fallback policies, and observability hooks.
4) Console UX: per-session cost preview, telemetry, and fidelity insights.
5) Billing hooks & metering: credit accounting, prorated adjustments, and refunds for SLA breaches.

Out of scope:
- Deep model architecture changes or new model training.
- On-prem Private deployments beyond billing API stubs (Private customers will receive contract templates in a follow-up).

Product requirements (PRD):
- Requirement 1: Fidelity Tier Definitions
  * Bronze — low-cost, high-latency-friendly: up to 3x token latency vs baseline, aggressive quantized/fast fallback paths. Lower quality; best-effort availability.
  * Silver — balanced: target latency within 1.3x baseline, default caching & batching enabled, standard fallback.
  * Gold — premium: latency within 1.0x baseline, reserved capacity path, lower eviction for KV cache, prefer higher-fidelity quantization or float where available.
- Requirement 2: Session Contract API
  * POST /v1/sessions (payload includes fidelity_tier, expected_duration_minutes, max_stream_rate_tokens_per_sec)
  * PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/negotiation to upgrade/downgrade fidelity mid-session with a nonce-based confirmation flow for billing changes.
- Requirement 3: Credit & Metering Model
  * Sessions consume Session Credits (SC). SC consumption = base_credit_per_minute[fidelity] * applied_duration_factor * shape_multiplier.
  * Shape multipliers account for burst vs. steady token rate (burst multiplier up to 2.5x).
  * Tiered discounts apply at duration thresholds: 0–15m (no discount), 15–120m (5% discount), >120m (12% discount).
- Requirement 4: SLOs & SLA compensation
  * Gold: p50 <= 120ms, p90 <= 250ms; availability 99.95%. SLA credit formula: prorated SC refund equal to estimated affected tokens * 1.5.
  * Silver: p50 <= 200ms, p90 <= 500ms; availability 99.9%.
  * Bronze: p50 <= 400ms, p90 <= 900ms; availability 99.5%.
- Requirement 5: Observability & Developer Feedback
  * Per-session telemetry: average token latency, p50/p90, kv-cache hit rate, model-variant fallback count, and credit burn rate.
  * Console must show a live cost preview and an estimated completion cost when session created and periodically during session.
- Requirement 6: Safety & Quality Guardrails
  * Automatically escalate to a sandboxed low-fidelity variant on safety or hallucination regressions. Guardrail metrics must trigger a telemetry event and a developer-facing explanation.
- Requirement 7: Billing & Contracting
  * Billing export includes per-session SC debits, prorations on fidelity changes, and SLA credit adjustments. Exports must be consumable by finance-run reconciliation jobs.

Technical design summary:
Runtime routing and enforcement:
- Sessions are first-class objects with associated metadata (fidelity_tier, expected_duration, credit_bucket_id). Routing policy uses fidelity_tier to pick serving lanes: reserved-lane (Gold), mixed-lane (Silver), opportunistic-lane (Bronze).
- A session coordinator component (new microservice) tracks session lifetime, enforces credit burn rules, and applies shape multipliers in real time. The coordinator also emits telemetry and enforces mid-session fidelity changes.

Cache & batching considerations:
- Gold sessions pin a higher share of KV cache and receive preferential small-batch packing to keep p50 low.
- Bronze sessions are eligible for aggressive pooling with higher batch sizes and longer scheduling windows.

Model variant strategy:
- Maintain compatibility matrix mapping fidelity tier -> allowed model variants and quantization levels. Example: Gold -> fp16 / 8x4 quant; Silver -> 4-bit + modest dequant; Bronze -> aggressive 4-bit / int8 variants.

Configuration snippet (example session creation body):

{
  "model": "redwood-llama-xxl-v2",
  "fidelity_tier": "silver",
  "expected_duration_minutes": 45,
  "max_stream_rate_tokens_per_sec": 25,
  "billing": { "credit_bucket": "acct-1234-prod" }
}

Operational & SRE requirements:
- Metrics to surface: per-session credit-burn-rate, p50/p90 token-latency, session-churn-rate, blocked-negotiations.
- Alerting thresholds: Gold p90 latency > 300ms for 5m -> P1 paging; Silver p90 > 700ms for 10m -> P2; Bronze p90 > 1200ms -> P3.
- Runbook: automatic downgrade flow where a session is proactively downgraded to next-lower fidelity if latency breach persists > 2 minutes and customer consent flag is false. Runbook must include customer notification and SLA credit recording steps.

Pricing & packaging (examples):
- Pricing primitives:
  * Session Credit (SC) unit — base price $0.06 / SC (examples below compute SC required).
  * Base credits per minute: Bronze 0.4 SC/min, Silver 1.0 SC/min, Gold 2.4 SC/min.
  * Shape multipliers: steady = 1.0, bursty = 1.6, spiky = 2.2.

Pricing examples table:
| Fidelity | Expected duration | Base credits | Shape | Estimated SC | Estimated list price (USD) |
| Gold | 60m | 2.4 SC/min -> 144 SC | steady -> x1.0 | 144 SC | $8.64 |
| Silver | 60m | 1.0 SC/min -> 60 SC | bursty -> x1.6 | 96 SC | $5.76 |
| Bronze | 20m | 0.4 SC/min -> 8 SC | spiky -> x2.2 | 17.6 -> 18 SC | $1.08 |

Commercial packaging options:
- Self-serve: session credits top-up in Console; customers estimate costs with the session preview UX.
- Committed bundles: monthly SC commitments with volume discounts (tiered).
- SLA-backed contracts: enterprise customers can purchase dedicated Gold lanes as part of Redwood Dedicated with custom price per SC and contractual uptime.

Roadmap & milestones (Q3–Q4 2026):
1) Q3 2026 (alpha): API schema + coordinator prototype, console cost preview MVP, internal SRE runbook.
2) Q4 2026 (beta): public API, billing exports, small set of enterprise pilot customers (3–5), initial pricing tiers.
3) Q1 2027 (GA): full GTM playbook, console UX polished, cross-product packaging (Optimize + Console), marketplace listing for dedicated Gold lanes.

GTM and launch playbook (high level):
1) Pilot selection: recruit 3 pilot customers across verticals (voice, SaaS assistants, enterprise search). Focus pilots on Gold and Silver lanes.
2) Measurement plan: define adoption and success metrics — pilot retention rate, average SC per session, SLA breach frequency, revenue per pilot.
3) Developer outreach: SDK samples, quickstarts (Node, Python), and a replayable developer sandbox with synthetic streaming traffic.
4) Sales & packaging: pricing calculator, playbook for customer negotiations, standard SLA language and contract addendum templates.
5) Support & onboarding: dedicated SE hours for pilot customers, runbook handed to support with escalation paths.

Launch checklist (pre-GA):
- [ ] API spec published and SDKs (JS/Python) implemented.
- [ ] Billing export schema validated with Finance.
- [ ] Console cost preview integrated with per-session telemetry.
- [ ] 3 pilot customers onboarded and running synthetic load tests.
- [ ] SRE alerts and automatic downgrade runbook validated in staging.
- [ ] Pricing tiers and credit economics validated against serving-cost model.
- [ ] Security review and privacy checklist completed.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: Dedicated lane capacity and scheduler improvements (team: eng-serving-runtime).
- Dependency: Billing/export pipeline (team: finance & eng-infra).
- Risk: If model fallback quality regresses at lower fidelity, developers may see poor UX; require a shadow-eval pipeline to detect regressions early.
- Risk: Complexity of mid-session upgrades could produce billing disputes — mitigations: nonce-confirm flows, clear console audit trail, and automated reconciliation jobs.

Release notes summary (alpha -> beta):
- Alpha release (internal) — introduced session object, fidelity labels, prototype coordinator, and console preview.
- Beta release (external pilots) — full metering, billing export, SLA reporting, and mid-session negotiation support.

Ownership and contacts:
- Product lead: Priya Patel (owner)
- Engineering leads: Marco Chen (runtime), Lina Rodríguez (billing & metering)
- SRE: Evan Murphy
- Sales & GTM contact: Jasmine Park

Next steps (immediate):
1) Align with runtime team on reserved-lane resource guarantees and scheduling primitives.
2) Draft API spec RFC and circulate to reviewers (Marco, Lina, Evan) for feedback by 2026-06-25.
3) Build coordinator MVP and integrate with staging telemetry by 2026-07-31.

Appendices:
A. Example billing export row (CSV):
session_id,customer_id,fidelity_tier,start_ts,end_ts,duration_minutes,shape_multiplier,sc_consumed,price_usd,slas_breached,slacredit_usd
sess-9a7c,acct-1234,gold,2026-08-01T10:01:00Z,2026-08-01T11:01:00Z,60,1.0,144,8.64,false,0.00

B. Developer SDK example (Node pseudocode):
const session = await client.sessions.create({ model: 'redwood-llama-xxl-v2', fidelity_tier: 'gold', expected_duration_minutes: 45 });
session.on('costUpdate', (preview) => console.log('Estimated cost', preview.estimated_usd));

C. Open questions for review:
- How should we price cross-tenant shared sessions for multi-actor collaborative flows?
- Do we want a hard cap on shape multipliers per tenant to limit abuse?
- What are acceptable guardrail thresholds for automatic downgrade without customer consent?

Please review the attached API RFC draft and cost model spreadsheet (links to be attached in the Confluence UI).
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: PRD: Optimize Quality Guardrails — Mandatory Quality Gating for Config Changes

sections.body:
Redwood Optimize can recommend cost-saving configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles) that can materially affect model outputs. This PRD defines **mandatory quality evaluation gates** that must pass before Optimize can apply any supported config change to production traffic (automatically or via one-click). The intent is to prevent silent quality regressions while keeping developer experience fast via tiered gates (smoke → full) and clear override policy with auditability.

**This PRD is for Hosted API gating enforcement.** Dedicated will follow after GA; Private will be manual-first with documentation and UI surfaces.

---
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body: Optimize today can surface recommendations that improve unit economics but may change output quality. Without systematic gating, we rely on post-deploy detection (customer complaints, ad-hoc monitoring) and reactive rollbacks.
sections.heading: Problem

sections.body:
- Quantization profile changes impacting long-context or rare-token behavior
- Batching policy changes changing effective scheduling / latency distribution and causing timeouts, truncation, or downstream tool-calling failures
- Prefix/KV caching settings changing behavior under partial prefix matches or cache eviction edge cases

We need **consistent, measurable, enforceable** guardrails that:
1) block known-bad changes before they reach full traffic,
2) remain fast enough to preserve Optimize’s “one-click value,” and
3) provide a complete audit trail for regulated / enterprise workflows.

---
sections.heading: Common regression modes

sections.body:
- **Prevent silent quality regressions** caused by cost optimizations by introducing required quality gates.
- **Define consistent pass/fail criteria** using offline evals and (where applicable) online canary signals.
- **Enforce gating at the right boundaries** (defense-in-depth): block Apply and block rollout promotion.
- **Make safe-by-default the fastest path**: provide tiered gates and clear guidance.
- **Traceability and auditability**: record what changed, why, what ran, results, and who approved/overrode.

---
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Fully automated gating for Redwood Private / on-prem deployments (we will support manual workflows + documentation only).
- Overhauling model onboarding or prompt set authoring processes (we integrate with existing eval harness and curated prompt sets).
- Building a new online experimentation system (we integrate with existing Rollouts canary workflows and telemetry).

---
sections.heading: Non-goals (initial release)

sections.body:
- **Application Engineer / ML Engineer (self-serve):** wants one-click apply for cost savings without breaking their app.
- **Platform Engineer (enterprise):** wants predictable guardrails, audit logs, and strong defaults.
- **Applied ML / Evals owner:** wants rigorous metrics, variance handling, and prompt set coverage control.
- **SRE / Oncall:** needs operational visibility and low-noise alerting (flake detection, timeouts, failure spikes).

---
sections.heading: Personas & primary users

sections.body:
**As an engineer**, when Optimize suggests a config change, I can click “Apply,” and Redwood will:
1) automatically run required quality gates for the proposed diff,
2) show pass/fail + key deltas and artifact links,
3) block apply if gates fail (or require an override with justification).

**Success looks like:** I can safely adopt a recommendation within a predictable time budget, with clear confidence signals.
sections.heading: US1 — One-click apply (Interactive)

sections.body:
**As a platform team**, I can opt into “auto-apply” for certain recommendation types and routes, but only if:
- required gates pass, and
- a canary rollout policy is attached (where applicable), and
- auto-rollback triggers exist.

**Success looks like:** cost savings accrue continuously without quality regressions and with an auditable trail.
sections.heading: US2 — Auto-apply (Policy-driven)

sections.body:
**As an oncall or eval owner**, when a gate fails I can quickly determine whether it is:
- a true regression,
- an eval flake / insufficient sample, or
- an infra / capacity issue (timeouts, region GPU scarcity),
with direct links to artifacts and recommended next steps.
sections.heading: US3 — Gate failure triage

sections.body:
**As an authorized approver**, I can approve a time-bound override when business needs require it, with:
- reason code + free-text justification,
- expiration date,
- required follow-up task (e.g., rerun full gate, create bug ticket), and
- audit log export compatibility.

---
sections.heading: US4 — Override with accountability

sections.body:
Optimize recommendations that propose a diff in one or more of:
1) **Batching policy updates**
   - max batch size, continuous batching toggles/limits, queueing thresholds
2) **Prefix/KV caching settings**
   - prefix cache enablement, cache size/eviction tuning, KV reuse policies
3) **Quantization profile changes**
   - profile selection per model family and GPU SKU (e.g., FP16 → INT8, or INT8 variant A → variant B)
sections.heading: Supported config change types (in-scope)

sections.body:
- Prompt/template changes, tool definitions changes, safety policy changes
- Switching to a different base model family (handled via existing model rollouts + model eval policy)

---
sections.heading: Out of scope for gating MVP

sections.body:
- Any supported config change must create a **Gate Run** record.
- The Optimize “Apply” action must be **blocked** unless the gate run is **Passed** or a valid **Override Granted** exists.
- Enforcement must be **server-side** (not only UI), with clear machine-readable failure reasons.
sections.heading: R1 — Gating must be mandatory before production apply

sections.body:
- **Smoke gate (fast):** small prompt subset, high-signal checks; aims to catch obvious regressions quickly.
- **Full gate:** larger coverage across prompt sets and metrics, with stronger variance controls.

Default behavior by change type (MVP defaults; configurable in v1):
- Batching + cache diffs: Smoke gate required; Full gate required for enterprise tiers and/or risky knob changes.
- Quantization profile diffs: Smoke gate + Full gate required by default.
sections.heading: We will support at least two tiers

sections.body:
- Gate results must report:
  - baseline config used,
  - proposed config diff,
  - metric deltas vs baseline,
  - confidence/variance signals (per eval methodology),
  - flake score / rerun count.
- Pass/fail decisions must use thresholds defined in: `quality-gate-metrics-and-thresholds-v1`.
sections.heading: R3 — Pass/fail criteria and variance handling

sections.body:
- Default baseline is the **current production config** for the same route/model/version.
- Quantization baseline must also match **hardware SKU** (GPU type) and supported execution path.
- Baseline must be immutable for the duration of a gate run; if baseline changes mid-run, rerun is required.
sections.heading: R4 — Baseline selection rules

sections.body:
- A config change cannot be promoted from canary to 100% if gates are failing.
- Rollout controller must:
  - halt promotion on gate failure,
  - optionally trigger rollback to baseline for configured routes,
  - notify owners via configured channels.
sections.heading: R5 — Rollout coupling (canary & promotion)

sections.body:
- Override capability must be restricted (RBAC), time-bound, and audited.
- Override must require:
  - owner (requester), approver, reason code, text justification,
  - expiration (default 72 hours; max allowed per policy),
  - follow-up task link (ticket).
sections.heading: R6 — Overrides (exception policy)

sections.body:
- Optimize recommendation view must display:
  - gate status (Not started / Running / Passed / Failed / Overridden / Expired),
  - top-level summary (1–3 key metrics),
  - artifact links (eval report, prompts, traces),
  - clear call-to-action (Run gates / View results / Request override).
- Apply button behavior:
  - enabled only when Pass or Override Granted,
  - disabled with tooltip + blocking reasons otherwise.
sections.heading: R7 — Console/Optimize UX requirements

sections.body:
- Gate-run events must be emitted to:
  - audit log (enterprise exportable),
  - metrics/tracing for operational monitoring.
- Required minimal audit events:
  - gate_started, gate_completed, gate_passed, gate_failed,
  - override_requested, override_granted, override_denied, override_expired,
  - apply_blocked_due_to_gate.

---
sections.heading: R8 — Observability & audit trail

sections.body:
- Supported diffs: batching, caching, quant profile
- Gate tiers: smoke + full
- Mandatory gating enforcement at Apply boundary
- Rollout promotion blocked on gate failure
- Minimal UI surfaces in Console/Optimize for status + artifact links
- Overrides enabled for restricted approvers with expiration + audit events
- Basic flake handling: rerun policy + flake score surfaced
sections.heading: MVP (Limited production rollout target: 2026-02)

sections.body:
- Per-route / per-tier configurable gate policy (e.g., enterprise requires full gates)
- Better guidance and guardrails: “risk level” classification of diffs (static validation)
- Quarantine workflow for flaky prompt sets + admin tooling
- Expanded online canary quality signals (where reliable) and tighter coupling with rollback triggers
- Stronger reporting: cost saved vs quality protected dashboards

---
sections.heading: v1 (GA target: 2026-03+)

sections.body:
- Inputs to policy selection (MVP):
  - change type (batch/cache/quant)
  - account tier (self-serve vs enterprise)
  - route criticality flag (optional, default false)
- Outputs:
  - required gate tier(s)
  - timeout budget per tier
  - retry/rerun limits
sections.heading: Gate policy selection

sections.body:
- NotStarted → Pending → Running → (Passed | Failed | Canceled)
- OverrideRequested → (OverrideGranted | OverrideDenied)
- OverrideGranted → (Expired)
sections.heading: Gate run state must include

sections.body:
- Smoke gate target runtime: **≤ 20 minutes p95** (excluding queue time)
- Full gate target runtime: **≤ 120 minutes p95**
- Hard timeouts must be enforced; timeouts are treated as failures with clear reason codes (distinguish infra vs quality).
sections.heading: Execution constraints

sections.body:
- QUALITY_REGRESSION
- INSUFFICIENT_CONFIDENCE / HIGH_VARIANCE
- EVAL_FLAKE_DETECTED
- EVAL_TIMEOUT
- EVAL_INFRA_ERROR
- BASELINE_NOT_AVAILABLE
- CONFIG_DIFF_INVALID / UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION

---
sections.heading: At minimum

sections.body:
- **Cost saved (realized):** incremental $ savings / token or per route after gated changes ship (tracked weekly).
- **Quality protected:**
  - # and % of proposed changes blocked due to quality regression
  - reduction in customer-reported quality incidents attributable to Optimize changes
- **Adoption:** % of Optimize recommendations that complete gating and ship (by change type)
sections.heading: Outcome metrics (business & user)

sections.body:
- Gate pass rate (smoke / full) by model family and change type
- Gate execution latency p50/p95 (queue + run time)
- Flake rate and rerun frequency (by prompt set)
- False positive rate (manually confirmed non-regressions) and top drivers
- Override rate, average override duration, overrides without follow-up completion

Initial targets for limited rollout (go/no-go inputs; subject to final sign-off):
- Smoke gate completion p95 ≤ 30 minutes end-to-end (including queue)
- Full gate completion p95 ≤ 3 hours end-to-end
- Flake rate ≤ 5% of runs requiring >1 rerun
- Override rate ≤ 2% of applied changes (excluding pre-approved internal testing)

---
sections.heading: Guardrail health metrics (operational)

sections.body:
- Enable gating in staging for synthetic + internal test routes.
- Run shadow gate runs for common Optimize recommendations (do not block apply yet).
- Validate baseline selection, artifact links, and failure reason clarity.
sections.heading: Phase 0 — Internal staging (2026-01)

sections.body:
- Turn on enforcement (block apply) for select internal workloads.
- Add oncall runbook and dashboard.
- Measure flake rate and tune thresholds/prompt sets.
sections.heading: Phase 1 — Internal beta (2026-01 to 2026-02)

sections.body:
- Hosted API only.
- Start with:
  - a subset of routes (low/medium criticality)
  - a subset of accounts (opt-in + a small default cohort)
- Enforce gating for all in-scope diff types.
- Require full gates by default for quant profile changes.
sections.heading: Phase 2 — Limited production rollout (2026-02)

sections.body:
- Expand to broader route coverage.
- Enable per-tier policy defaults (enterprise stricter).
- Begin Dedicated default integration plan; Private manual workflow surfaced in Console.
sections.heading: Phase 3 — GA (2026-03+)

sections.body:
- Feature flag gating enforcement per account/route.
- If gating system instability causes widespread blocking (infra), allow temporary “monitor-only” mode, but keep audit logging and require explicit approval for switching modes.

---
sections.heading: Rollback strategy

sections.body:
- **Eval Harness:** trigger API, artifact storage, rerun aggregation, flake score.
- **Optimize service:** config diff schema, gate state machine persistence, apply-time enforcement.
- **Rollout controller:** promotion gating + optional rollback triggers.
- **Console:** UX surfaces for status/results/override request.
- **Observability pack:** metrics/traces + dashboards and alerts.
- **Policy/RBAC:** override approver roles and audit log export.

---
sections.heading: Dependencies

sections.body:
- **Eval flakiness blocks legitimate savings.** Mitigation: flake scoring, rerun policy, quarantine workflow; keep smoke gates high-signal.
- **Gate latency slows down developer workflow.** Mitigation: tiered gates; smoke-first; dedicated eval capacity pools; p95 targets tracked.
- **Baseline drift causes inconsistent comparisons.** Mitigation: baseline pinning per gate run; rerun on baseline change.
- **Overuse of overrides erodes protections.** Mitigation: strict RBAC, time bounds, audit review, override rate alerts.
- **Config diff invalid combinations.** Mitigation: static validation before expensive evals; clear rejection reasons.

---
sections.heading: Risks & mitigations

sections.body:
1) For each in-scope config diff type (batch, cache, quant), Optimize can initiate a gate run and persist results.
2) Apply is blocked server-side when gates are failing or missing; clear reason codes returned.
3) Console/Optimize shows gate status, key deltas, and artifact links.
4) Rollout controller blocks canary promotion when gates fail.
5) Override flow exists, is RBAC-restricted, time-bound, and emits audit events.
6) Observability dashboards show gate funnel and failure/flake breakdown; alerts exist for failure spikes and sustained infra timeouts.
7) End-to-end integration test covers: propose diff → run gates → pass/fail → apply allowed/blocked → override → apply allowed.

---
sections.heading: Acceptance criteria (MVP)

sections.body:
- Final default thresholds and minimum sample sizes per gate type (Applied ML to finalize in thresholds doc).
- Which batching/caching knobs qualify as “risky” and should require full gates by default (Runtime to provide initial classification).
- Online canary quality signals: which are reliable enough to block promotion vs advisory only (SRE + Applied ML alignment).

---
sections.heading: Open questions

sections.body:
- **Gate Run:** A single evaluation execution for a proposed config diff compared against a pinned baseline.
- **Smoke Gate:** Fast, high-signal eval subset intended to catch obvious regressions.
- **Full Gate:** Broader eval suite intended to provide high confidence for production rollout.
- **Override:** Time-bound exception allowing apply despite failed/missing gates, with audit trail and follow-up.
sections.heading: Appendix: terminology

payload.page_title: Adaptive Cost SLOs PRD: dynamic cost-aware routing and autoscaling

sections.body: This Product Requirements Document (PRD) describes the Adaptive Cost SLOs feature: a unified mechanism that allows customers and platform operators to express and enforce cost targets (per-token cost, $/inference, monthly spend cap) alongside traditional latency and availability SLOs. The feature coordinates model routing, quantization profile selection, batching policies, and autoscaling gestures to meet cost objectives while preserving correctness and reliability.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Provide a first-class declarative API and Console UX for defining cost SLOs at the token, route, and customer namespace levels.
- Implement runtime enforcement that adjusts routing (model variant selection), batching, KV/prefix cache policies, and instance sizing to meet cost targets without violating hard latency SLOs.
- Surface per-request and aggregated cost explainability (why a request incurred a cost outcome).
- Enable safe rollouts with canary experiments and guardrails to prevent quality regressions.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- This PRD does not change basic pricing tiers or the billing engine; it provides cost-target-driven routing and controls only.
- It will not replace manual reserved capacity contracts; Dedicated will still allow explicit capacity pinning.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
- Customers increasingly want predictable inference economics. Many ask for a way to cap or target unit costs for high-volume features (e.g., embeddings at scale, token-heavy summarization).
- Current levers (quantization profiles, manual model selection, batching knobs) are powerful but disconnected and require deep runtime knowledge.
- Adaptive Cost SLOs aggregates those levers with a policy layer and closed-loop control to meet cost targets at scale.
sections.heading: Background and motivation

sections.body:
- Product engineers: set per-route cost budget to keep feature unit economics stable during peak load.
- Platform/FinOps: enforce company-wide monthly spend caps or set conservative SLOs for dev/staging vs. prod.
- SRE: ensure that cost-induced runtime changes do not violate latency or error SLOs.
sections.heading: User personas & primary use cases

sections.body:
- Policy API: A new CostSLO object, configurable via Redwood API and Console. Fields include: scope (route|model|namespace), target_type (per_token|per_inference|monthly_cap), value (numeric), latency_guard_ms (hard latency bound), priority (enum: latency_first|cost_first|balanced), fallback_policy (list of fallback actions).
- Controller: A control-plane loop that computes recommended runtime configurations every 30s per SLO. Recommendations include model_variant, max_batch_size, KV_cache_policy (aggressiveness), allocation_hint (vCPU/GPU type).
- Enforcement: The serving runtime consumes recommendations and attempts adjustment via safe actions: prefer cheaper model variant, increase batching within latency bounds, enable higher quantization, or route to Dedicated reserved pool.
- Explainability: Each request's metadata will include the active CostSLO id and a short rationale: e.g., "selected-variant:llama-13b-q4_0- for 22% lower token cost; batch-size increased 2x; latency impact estimated +12ms (within guard)".
sections.heading: High-level design overview

sections.body:
FR-1: API - Create/Read/Update/Delete CostSLOs. Example API payload:
- POST /v1/cost_slos
  {
    "scope": "route:/v1/embeddings",
    "target_type": "per_inference",
    "value": "0.0035",
    "latency_guard_ms": 150,
    "priority": "cost_first"
  }
FR-2: Console - Cost SLO editor with live simulation of historical traffic showing projected compliance, and an impact preview (estimated latency/cost tradeoffs).
FR-3: Enforcement - The controller must emit a plan change at most once per 30s per SLO and annotate the plan with expected cost delta and estimated error/regression risk.
FR-4: Fallbacks - If enforcement would violate latency_guard_ms for >1% of requests in a 5m window, revert to previous plan and raise an alert.
FR-5: Reporting - Per-route daily compliance report (compliant/violations, 95th percentile cost, root-cause tags).
FR-6: Audit - All plan changes must be stored in a time-series config log for 90 days.
sections.heading: Functional requirements (FRs)

sections.body:
NFR-1: Controller decision latency must be <1s for computing a plan per SLO.
NFR-2: Introduced runtime overhead must add <1% p99 tail latency at steady state.
NFR-3: Config data and logs must be encrypted at rest and accessible via existing audit log APIs.
sections.heading: Non-functional requirements (NFRs)

sections.body:
- Cost compliance SLO: Monthly target satisfied if 95% of per-inference costs are <= target_value across the billing window.
- Hard latency guard: No more than 1% of requests exceed latency_guard_ms after enforcement; immediate rollback if >5% in a 5m window.
sections.heading: SLO/threshold definitions (example)

sections.body:
- CostSLO object (fields): scope, target_type, value, latency_guard_ms, priority, fallback_policy[], enabled, tags[].
- Example CLI: redwood cost-slo create --scope route:/v1/chat --target_type per_token --value 0.00025 --latency_guard 120 --priority balanced
sections.heading: API surface and examples

sections.body:
1) Create Cost SLO: Guided wizard with traffic sampling slider and recommendation engine that suggests an initial policy (e.g., prefer quantized small casting).
2) Simulate: Run a historical simulation for the last 7/30/90 days. UI shows projected violations and an impact heatmap (latency vs. cost).
3) Deploy: Stage to canary (1% traffic) for 24h with automatic rollback conditions.
4) Promote: If canary passes (no regressions, cost delta within expected range), promote to full rollout and schedule a post-rollout review.
sections.heading: Console UX & workflows

sections.body:
- M0 (2025-12-15): API schema and Console mockups complete.
- M1 (2026-02-01): Controller prototype + simulation pipeline. Limited internal testing with two pilot customers.
- M2 (2026-03-15): Runtime enforcement in staging; canary tooling and rollback hooks implemented.
