payload.page_title: Private VPC Terraform Modules (Alpha) — Release Notes

sections.body: This page tracks the **Alpha** release notes for the **Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules** (AWS-only). The alpha module suite provides Redwood-validated defaults for the foundational networking and security footprint required to run **Redwood Private** in a customer-managed VPC (with EKS assumed in the reference architecture).
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Reduce pilot risk by standardizing **subnet layout**, **routing/NAT strategy**, **VPC endpoints**, and **logging defaults**.
- Provide a supported baseline for installer prerequisites (endpoints/DNS/egress) and predictable day-2 operations.
- Keep the surface area opinionated with documented extension points.

---
sections.heading: Alpha focus areas

sections.body:
**Module suite version:** v0.1.0-alpha (initial tagged alpha)

**Support stance:** Alpha is supported for **design partners and guided pilots** only. Changes may be breaking between alpha versions; customers must pin versions.

---
sections.heading: Current Alpha Version

sections.body: The suite is published as composable Terraform modules (repository: `redwood-terraform`). Names below reflect the module intent; refer to the repo README for exact paths.
sections.heading: Included Modules (v0.1.0-alpha)

sections.body:
- VPC creation (IPv4)
- Subnet layout: **public** and **private** subnets across 2–3 AZs (configurable)
- Route tables with a Redwood-standard split between public ingress and private workloads
- NAT strategy options:
  - **One NAT per AZ** (recommended default for availability)
  - **Single NAT** (opt-in cost-saving mode, documented trade-offs)
sections.heading: Provides

sections.body: - Defaults are aligned to the **AWS Private VPC Reference Architecture (EKS)** and Redwood Private installer expectations for egress and control plane reachability.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- Interface endpoints (configurable set) with opinionated defaults for Redwood Private usage:
  - `ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr` (required for image pulls in private-only environments)
  - `sts` (commonly required depending on runtime/installer auth patterns)
  - `logs` (CloudWatch Logs)
  - Additional commonly used endpoints (as supported by region)
- Gateway endpoint:
  - `s3` (recommended for private egress reduction and reliability)
- Optional flags for **private DNS behavior** and documented constraints/anti-patterns.
sections.heading: Provides

sections.body: - Redwood Private installer includes preflight checks/warnings when critical endpoints are missing or private DNS is misconfigured.
sections.heading: Installer alignment

sections.body:
- VPC Flow Logs with a secure-by-default posture
- Destination options:
  - CloudWatch Logs (default)
  - S3 (customer-owned bucket, recommended for longer retention)
- Recommended baseline retention defaults (customer-overridable) and fields required for security investigations.
sections.heading: Provides

sections.body:
- Cluster/node egress patterns (least-privilege by default, with documented exceptions)
- Load balancer/ingress boundaries (when applicable)
- VPC endpoint access boundaries
sections.heading: Provides opinionated SG templates/patterns for

sections.body: - Make secure networking the default while reducing pilot friction. Where strict least-privilege is impractical, the module includes a documented “operability override” path.
sections.heading: Design intent

sections.body:
- An IAM role and policy scaffold for the **installer execution role**
- Support for **permission boundaries** and customer IAM integration
- Documented expectations for who assumes the role and when (CI runner vs human operator vs customer automation)
sections.heading: Provides

sections.body:
- Outputs and routing hooks intended to integrate with customer-managed VPN/DX without embedding provider-specific assumptions
- Clear docs on where customers extend vs where Redwood validates
sections.heading: Provides

sections.body:
- Example environment layout and `tfvars` patterns appropriate for design partners
- Minimal “happy path” example aligned to the deployment guide
sections.heading: Includes

sections.body:
- Automated checks (fmt/validate/lint/security scan) and provider pinning
- Integration test harness that can stand up and tear down an ephemeral VPC to validate expected outputs
- Release tagging + changelog generation workflow (alpha-grade)

---
sections.heading: Includes

sections.body:
**Terraform:** 1.6+ (recommended)

**AWS Provider:** 5.x (pinned in the repo for reproducibility)

**AWS Regions:** Any commercial region supporting the required endpoints; customers must validate endpoint availability per region.

**Assumed platform constraints:**
- Reference architecture assumes **EKS** and standard AWS VPC primitives.
- Redwood Private installer expects private subnets with controlled egress and access to required AWS services (typically via endpoints).

---
sections.heading: Compatibility (Alpha)

sections.body: - None (initial alpha tag).
sections.heading: v0.1.0-alpha

sections.body:
Alpha versions may introduce breaking changes without GA-level deprecation windows. Customers must:
- Pin module versions (do not track `main`).
- Treat upgrades as change-managed events (see the upgrade/rollback runbook).

---
sections.heading: Important note for all Alpha versions

sections.body: This alpha intentionally does not cover every enterprise topology. Known constraints:
sections.heading: Known Limitations (v0.1.0-alpha)

sections.body:
- **IPv6 is not supported** in the alpha modules.
- **Transit Gateway (TGW)** and complex hub-and-spoke routing are not modeled; use extension points and document the delta for Redwood review.
- No first-class support for multi-VPC/multi-account network perimeters beyond documented patterns.
- DNS advanced patterns (split-horizon with multiple resolvers, custom resolver endpoints) are not fully templated; only guidance is provided.
sections.heading: Networking / Topology

sections.body:
- Endpoint sets are opinionated and region-dependent; customers may need to add endpoints for organization-specific controls.
- Private DNS toggles can cause subtle breakage if combined with custom DNS forwarding; follow the deployment guide and installer preflight output.
sections.heading: Endpoints / Egress

sections.body:
- Flow logs are covered; additional sources (e.g., Route 53 Resolver query logs) are **guidance-only** and not uniformly implemented across all customer DNS patterns.
- SIEM forwarding is supported via customer-owned destinations and patterns, but is not turnkey.
sections.heading: Logging / Auditability

sections.body:
- IAM scaffolding is designed for the Redwood installer integration; it is not a complete enterprise IAM framework.
- Organizations with strict SCPs/permission boundaries may require tailoring; this is expected and is part of pilot onboarding.
sections.heading: IAM

sections.body:
- Ephemeral integration tests may run nightly or on-demand rather than on every PR due to time/cost; refer to CI docs for current gating.

---
sections.heading: Testing

sections.body:
Use the day-2 runbook for the full procedure. At a minimum:
1. **Pin module versions** in Terraform (`ref`/`version`) and commit the lockfile.
2. Run `terraform plan` and review for:
   - Subnet CIDR changes
   - NAT gateway replacement
   - Route table churn
   - Endpoint recreation
3. If any of the above appear, coordinate with Redwood (Infra + Private Deployments) before applying.
sections.heading: Upgrade Guidance (Alpha)

sections.body:
- Prefer additive changes.
- Avoid renaming resources in-place; use state mv only with Redwood guidance.

---
sections.heading: Recommended practice during alpha

sections.body:
- **Design partners** and customers in a Redwood-guided pilot.
- Internal Solutions Engineering / Pro Services deployments.
sections.heading: Who this is for

sections.body:
1. Post in Slack: `#eng-private-deployments` with:
   - AWS region
   - Module version
   - Which example you started from
   - Sanitized `terraform plan` diff (no account IDs / sensitive CIDRs)
   - Installer preflight output (if applicable)
2. For blockers impacting a pilot timeline, open a Linear ticket under the VPC modules epic and tag:
   - Infra: Irene Choi
   - Networking: Victor Alvarez
   - Security: Marcus Lin (if IAM/logging boundaries)
3. If an active pilot is down, follow the SRE escalation route for Private deployments via the on-call channel (Solutions Eng can coordinate).
sections.heading: How to get help

sections.body:
- Module usage aligned with the reference architecture and deployment guide
- Debugging endpoint/DNS/NAT issues surfaced by installer preflight
- Safe upgrade review for alpha versions
sections.heading: What we can support in alpha

sections.body:
- Significant topology deviations (TGW hub/spoke, multi-account perimeters)
- Custom DNS infrastructures requiring resolver endpoints/forwarding chains
- Deep SIEM pipelines beyond recommended destinations

---
sections.heading: What typically requires a paid services engagement

sections.body:
- Missing `ecr.*` interface endpoints or private DNS misconfiguration → installer fails pulling images.
- Intermittent DNS resolution in private subnets due to resolver settings/forwarders → manifests as flaky control plane communications.
- Single NAT in multi-AZ environments leading to unexpected outage blast radius.
- Overly permissive egress rules added ad-hoc to “fix” endpoint issues; later fails security review.
sections.heading: Appendix: Common Pilot Failure Modes (Observed)

sections.body:
- Deployment guide (alpha)
- Logging defaults and SIEM hooks
- IAM boundaries guidance

---
sections.heading: See also

sections.body:
- Initial publication of AWS VPC foundation modules (VPC/subnets/routing)
- Endpoint module with private DNS options and documented constraints
- Flow logs module with destination options (CloudWatch Logs/S3)
- Security group patterns for private deployments
- IAM scaffold for installer execution role with permission boundaries
- Optional VPN/DX hooks (placeholders)
- Example environments and alpha quickstart structure
- CI validation + integration test harness + release tagging workflow

payload.page_title: Optimize Conductor 2.0 - Release Notes and Migration Guide

sections.body:
Summary

This document describes the Redwood Optimize Conductor 2.0 release: what changed, why it matters, SLO and billing impacts, rollout and migration steps, and operational notes for customers and internal teams. Optimize Conductor 2.0 introduces workload-aware multi-pass optimization, a pluggable estimator for hybrid deployments, and default telemetry schemas for per-route cost attribution. The release is focused on reducing per-token inference cost for conversational workloads while preserving quality SLAs.

Highlights

- Workload-aware multi-pass optimization: a new orchestration layer that simulates alternate batching, quantization, and cache policies across historical traces and recommends per-route profiles.
- Hybrid estimator plugin: customers running Dedicated + Private topologies can use the new estimator to predict cross-environment cost tradeoffs and warm-capacity benefits.
- Observability schema v2: standardized telemetry fields for capture of per-variant latency, KV cache hit rates, and token-level cost estimates (see Telemetry changes section).
- Migration assistant CLI: a guided CLI and UI assistant that validates a tenant’s usage traces, runs a sandboxed simulation, and produces recommended policy bundles with confidence bands.
- Compatibility and fallbacks: automatic fallback rules to Produce Conductor 1.x profiles when runtime compatibility or regression risks are detected.

Why this release?

Customers have asked for more deterministic cost reductions without manual tuning. Optimize Conductor 2.0 is intended to:

- reduce average per-token serving cost for chat-like flows by 8–22% in early benchmarks,
- shorten time-to-safe-rollout (canary → A/B → 100%) via integrated simulation-driven confidence scores, and
- provide clearer observability to map cost changes to specific configuration deltas.

What’s changed (detailed)

1) Multi-pass optimization engine
- Runs a sequence of optimizers (batch sizing, prefix caching, quantization profile selection, KV eviction policy) against a tenant’s trace in a sandbox.
- Produces an ordered set of recommended policy bundles with: expected cost delta, expected latency delta (p50/p95), and a confidence score derived from simulation variance.
- Output format (JSON example):

  {
    "bundle_id": "optc-202612-sandbox-01",
    "candidate_policies": ["batch-128","q8_2","prefix-kv-enabled"],
    "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-12.4",
    "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "210",
    "confidence": "0.87"
  }

2) Hybrid estimator plugin
- Extensible plugin API that accepts per-region capacity profiles and returns cross-topology allocations.
- Useful for customers who split traffic between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Sample CLI call: redwood-optimize simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator --trace traces/2026-11-01.json

3) Observability schema v2
- New required telemetry fields: optimize.bundle_id, optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, optimize.kv_hit_rate, optimize.batch_shape.
- Backwards compatibility: the ingestion pipeline will accept v1 telemetry but only the new dashboards and reports will show v2 fields.

4) Migration assistant CLI/UI
- Provides an automated sequence: validate traces → run sandbox sim → produce recommended bundles → run offline regression evals → generate rollout plan.
- CLI example (high level):

  # validate traces and run simulation\  redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://bucket/trace-2026-10-15.json\  redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --policy-bounds "{\"min_batch\":32,\"max_batch\":256}"

- The UI exposes an interactive confidence slider for selecting more conservative vs aggressive bundles.

SLO and billing impacts

- Expected unit economics: Early benchmarks across 6 representative tenants show mean cost reduction 12% (range 8–22%) with p95 latency change within +/- 10% of baseline for the chosen conservative bundles.
- Billing: There is no immediate change to billing metrics or pricing SKUs. Cost savings are realized through optimization of runtime configuration and will show up as lower consumption in token/cpu/GPU usage reports.
- SLA considerations: Teams must validate per-tenant latency/p95 and function-call integrity. Optimize Conductor 2.0 includes a safety gate that will not permit an automatic rollout if p95 regression > 15% in the sandbox regression evals.

Upgrade and migration plan (for customers)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Prepare (owner: customer success / solutions engineering)
- Gather a 7–14 day usage trace covering representative traffic (session length distribution, model variants, peak windows).\- Ensure trace contains at least 50k inference requests or the migration assistant will flag low-confidence recommendations.
- Confirm tenant has a staging route (non-production) that can proxy 5–10% of live traffic for A/B tests.

2) Simulate and validate (owner: customer success + tenant engineering)
- Run the migration assistant simulate command to generate candidate bundles.
- Review recommended bundles and associated confidence scores.
- Run offline regression evals against a fixed prompt set to verify functional parity (owner provides known-good prompts for critical flows).

3) Canary rollout (owner: tenant engineering + Redwood SRE)
- Apply conservative bundle to 1–2 production routes at 1–5% traffic.
- Monitor optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, request.latency_p95, model.output_consistency metrics for 24–72 hours.
- If p95 regression remains < 10% and no functional regressions detected, proceed to A/B.

4) A/B and ramp (owner: customer success + Redwood product)
- Ramp to 25–50% traffic, compare endpoint KPIs, and collect user-facing error rates.
- Typical ramp cadence: double traffic every 12 hours if all checks pass.

5) Full rollout and post-rollout audit (owner: customer success + finance)
- Ramp to 100% when confidence remains high.
- Generate a 7-day post-rollout audit report showing realized cost delta and latency impact.

Rollback criteria
sections.heading: Recommended staged migration (small-to-large tenants)

sections.body:
- p95 latency regression > 15% vs baseline for the route during the canary or A/B.
- Any functional regression detected by the offline regression evals (semantic inconsistency, hallucination increase measured by test oracle).
- KV/cache hit rate drop > 30% causing unexpected cost increases.

Operational runbook (SRE)

Owner: eng-sre
sections.heading: Immediate rollback triggers

sections.body:
- optimize.simulation_confidence < 0.5 for a recently applied bundle → alert to product/sre.
- optimize.estimated_cost_usd increases > 10% over rolling 24h → alert to billing-ops.
- request.latency_p95 increases > 12% over baseline → page oncall.
- optimize.kv_hit_rate falls below configured threshold for a route → run cache debug runbook.
sections.heading: Monitoring checklist (alerts to configure)

sections.body:
1) Identify affected routes using optimize.bundle_id in logs.
2) Use the simulation sandbox to replay a representative subset of traffic.
3) If rollback is required: redwood-optimize migrate rollback --tenant TENANT_ID --bundle BUNDLE_ID
4) Open an incident and follow standard oncall postmortem cadence if the cause is not apparent.

Compatibility and fallbacks

- Compatibility matrix: Conductor 2.0 supports runtime agent versions >= 3.2.2. If a route uses agent < 3.2.2, the migration assistant will recommend a v1-compatible bundle and include an upgrade path.
- Fallback behavior: If a live trial detects functional regressions, the platform will automatically apply the last-known-good bundle for that route and create a high-visibility ticket to the product owner.

Telemetry and dashboard changes (what product teams should know)

- New Optimize dashboards (Console):
  - Per-tenant Optimization Summary (shows realized vs estimated cost deltas, per-route confidence scores).
  - Bundle Explorer (lists applied bundles, simulation metadata, and rollback events).
  - Regression surface map (maps prompts/paths that failed offline regressions).

- Telemetry ingestion notes: SDKs and ingestion pipelines must emit the optimize.* v2 fields. Agents older than 3.2.2 will continue to emit v1 fields; the ingestion layer will backfill where possible but v2-only reports require agent upgrade.

Administrative and billing notes

- There is no separate paid SKU for Optimize Conductor 2.0 during the initial preview period. Usage of the migration assistant sandbox is metered and shown as an internal optimization run in the tenant’s console.
- Finance ops will track realized savings as part of monthly consumption reports. For enterprise customers on committed Dedicated plans, Optimize-driven savings will be reconciled as operational improvements and reflected in future commit discussions.

Known limitations and gotchas

- Small tenants (fewer than 50k requests in the trace window) should expect lower-confidence recommendations; consider a longer trace window.
- Extremely bursty traffic patterns can reduce optimizer confidence; the migration assistant offers a conservative bundle option for these tenants.
- The sandbox simulation assumes identical model weights and versioning; if a tenant uses rapidly changing model variants, freeze model rollouts during sandbox runs.

Support and escalation

- Primary contact: customer-success-optimize@redwood.ai (for migration coordination)
- SRE escalation: oncall-sre@redwood.ai (pager contacts in internal roster)
- Engineering bug reports: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/issues (label: conductor-2.0)

Owners and contacts

- Product manager: Ava Nguyen (owner)
- Engineering lead: Diego Martinez
- Customer success lead: Maya Patel
- SRE lead: Liam O'Connor

Appendices

A — Example recommended bundle (full JSON)
{
  "bundle_id": "optc-202612-conservative-001",
  "policies": {
    "batch": 64,
    "quantization": "q8_2",
    "prefix_kv_enabled": true,
    "kv_eviction_policy": "lru_time_based_1h"
  },
  "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-9.8",
  "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "195",
  "confidence": "0.78"
}

B — CLI checklist for migration assistants
- Ensure trace is complete and covers peak windows.
- Run redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://...
- If validation passes, run redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator
- Review candidate bundles and run offline regression evals
- Execute canary rollback plan if any regression triggers occur

C — Release timeline
- 2026-11-15: internal alpha completed
- 2026-11-22: customer preview starts (select tenants)
- 2026-12-01: general availability (GA) and documentation published

D — Links (internal)
- Migration assistant repo: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/migration-assistant
- Telemetry schema v2 reference: /product-docs/design-specs/optimize-telemetry-schema-v2

payload.page_title: Console Simulated Traffic Runner — Release Notes 1.0

sections.body:
This document contains the release notes for Console Simulated Traffic Runner (STR) v1.0 — a developer-facing, browser-integrated tool for producing realistic, configurable synthetic traffic against Redwood inference routes from the Console. STR v1.0 is intended to accelerate on-boarding, load-testing, and fidelity regression experiments without requiring customers to run external traffic generators.

Key goals for 1.0:
- Provide a lightweight, zero-install traffic simulator embedded in Console for rapid developer experiments.
- Support representative traffic shapes: conversational sessions, bursty transactional requests, batched embedding requests, and long-generation streams.
- Emit telemetry compatible with production consumption metrics so experiments mirror billing and SLO signals.
- Offer safe modes (read-only, cost caps) to prevent runaway charges in self-serve accounts.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Console UI: New "Simulate Traffic" tab on Route detail pages with pre-built scenarios and a configurable scenario editor.
- Scenario library: 12 curated scenarios (e.g., ─ low-latency chat, high-throughput batching, heavy-KV eviction, streaming long-context) plus the ability to define custom sequences.
- Execution engine: In-Console runner that executes HTTP/SDK-compatible requests against the selected route with control over concurrency, arrival distribution (poisson, fixed, burst), and sequence length.
- Cost & SLO preview: Each scenario shows estimated token cost, projected p50/p95 latency impact, and error-rate delta based on historical baseline.
- Telemetry integration: STR streams experiment telemetry to the same ingestion pipeline as production, tagged with experiment_id. Telemetry includes per-request timing, token counts, retry events, fallback occurrences, and model-variant selection.
- Safety controls: Per-experiment budget caps, per-account max concurrency defaults, and an optional confirmation step for any scenario that could exceed a configured monthly cost threshold.
sections.heading: Change summary (what's new)

sections.body:
- Engineers can validate performance and fidelity trade-offs early in feature development without needing a separate load-test environment.
- Product and SRE teams gain consistent signals from experiments because measurements use production-grade telemetry and cost models.
- Sales and Customer Success can demonstrate predictable migration scenarios to Dedicated and Private customers during onboarding.

Supported platforms and limits in 1.0:
- Availability: Hosted Console only (Global region). Private Deployment support is planned for 2.0.
- Max concurrent virtual clients per experiment: 200.
- Max sustained request rate per route from STR: 1,200 rps (soft limit; subject to route quota).
- Max scenario length (in tokens generated per session): 8,192 tokens.
sections.heading: Why this matters

sections.body:
- name: scenario_name — (string) human-friendly label.
- arrival_pattern: poisson|fixed|burst — (string) selects arrival distribution.
- concurrency: (integer) simulated parallel clients.
- payload_template: (string) templated request body supporting variables ({{user_id}}, {{seed_prompt}}).
- token_budget: (integer) cap on tokens for experiment (safety).
- model_variant: (string) explicit variant OR leave blank for routing policy.
- duration_seconds: (integer) duration of the run.
sections.heading: Configuration reference (table)

sections.body:
1) Navigate to Console → Routes → <your-route> → Simulate Traffic.
2) Choose a curated scenario (e.g., "Chat: bursty onboarding") or Create New.
3) Adjust concurrency and token_budget. If you exceed your default budget cap, the Run button will be greyed out until you acknowledge the cost.
4) Click Run and observe live telemetry in the experiment panel.
sections.heading: Quickstart (Console)

sections.body:
- The Console exposes a one-time experiment token for CLI-driven orchestration (intended for CI integration). Example:
  1) Request an experiment token from Console (POST /api/console/experiments/token)
  2) Run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/experiments/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer <EXPERIMENT_TOKEN>' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","scenario":"chat-burst","concurrency":50,"duration_seconds":300}'
sections.heading: CLI (beta) example (curl)

sections.body:
- STR uses the same tokenization and cost model as production billing. Experiment telemetry includes experiment_id and scenario_name tags so team owners can aggregate cost and latency impacts in dashboards.
- Experiment events are sampled by default at 100% for the experiment lifecycle and retained for 7 days in product tiers; longer retention is available via Optimize add-on.
sections.heading: Telemetry and cost alignment

sections.body:
- Running STR does not modify production route quotas but will be subject to rate-limiting if a route is under global contention. STR will gracefully back off and report fallback events.
- STR supports a "canary" target option: tagged requests that are routed to a variant pool (canary) so teams can validate variants without impacting the main fleet.
sections.heading: SLO & safety interactions

sections.body:
- No config changes required to routes. STR calls the route endpoints exactly as a customer client would; existing access controls (API keys, per-route tokens) are used.
- Admins can disable STR per account from Console → Settings → Experimentation to prevent usage in regulated tenants.
sections.heading: Upgrade/migration notes for existing teams

sections.body:
- 2026-09-15: Internal beta (Redwood employees + select partners).
- 2026-09-29: Early access for self-serve accounts.
- 2026-10-01: Public launch (GA) — feature enabled by default for all hosted accounts.
sections.heading: Rollout and availability timeline

sections.body:
- Product owner: Sofia Chen (product) — sofia.chen@redwood.ai
- Engineering: Marco Ruiz (eng-platform) — @mruiz
- SRE & telemetry: Jamie Patel (eng-sre) — @jpatel
sections.heading: Owners and contacts

sections.body:
- STR issues requests using the same REST/SDK surface as documented for hosted inference. If the route supports function/tool-calling and streaming, STR can simulate both.
- For streaming scenarios, STR simulates slow and fast producers to reproduce partial-response conditions.
sections.heading: SDK and API compatibility notes

sections.body:
1) Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) are not supported in 1.0. Do not rely on STR measurements for air-gapped performance planning.
2) STR executes experiments from Console-hosted agents; cross-region latency skew may affect measurements for routes pinned to a specific region. Document observed region offset in experiment notes.
3) Very high-fidelity fidelity regressions that depend on customer data integrations (e.g., embeddings backed by customer-owned vector DB) will be approximate unless the customer integrates the data into the scenario template.
4) Cost-estimates are conservative projections based on the last 30d median token size; actual billing may vary for dynamic or multi-model routing policies.
sections.heading: Known limitations and caveats

sections.body:
- Experiment stalls at "Initializing": check that the route has a valid active model and that the account has remaining token budget.
- Observed fallback spikes: examine the experiment timeline for rate-limit or variant-fallback tags; reduce concurrency or switch to canary variant pools.
- Telemetry not visible in dashboards: confirm experiment_id tag inclusion and that the account's telemetry ingestion is enabled. Contact SRE if missing events are systemic.
sections.heading: Troubleshooting (common issues)

sections.body:
- All simulated requests are stamped with an experiment tag to prevent accidental ingestion into customer logs and to mark any resulting outputs as non-production in downstream pipelines.
- Experiment tokens are single-use and short-lived (default TTL: 10 minutes).
- Admins can configure retention and disable experiment telemetry at account level for regulated customers.
sections.heading: Security and compliance

sections.body:
- In-Console guided tour (Simulate Traffic → Tour).
- Workshop: "Using STR to size Dedicated capacity" — hands-on lab content in Learn Portal (internal).
- API reference: Console Experiment API (internal link).
sections.heading: Documentation and training resources

sections.body:
- Private Deployment agent for on-prem performance parity (v2.0).
- Scenario provenance: recording seed prompts and deterministic replay for fidelity reproduction (v1.2).
- Integration with Optimize to automatically suggest batching and quantization settings from experiment results (v1.3).

Appendix: experiment JSON example
{
  "scenario_name": "chat-burst-onboarding",
  "arrival_pattern": "burst",
  "concurrency": 75,
  "duration_seconds": 180,
  "payload_template": "{\"input\": \"Hello, I need help onboarding\"}"
}

If you find issues or need higher-capacity trials for enterprise demo, contact the product owner or join #console-sim-runner on Slack.
sections.heading: Feedback and next steps (planned improvements)

sections.body:
- 2026-09-15 — v1.0 initial GA (S. Chen): Public launch and documentation published.
- 2026-10-01 — v1.0.1 (S. Chen): Adjusted cost estimation algorithm to include variant routing overhead in estimates.

payload.page_title: Optimize Conductor 4.0 release notes and migration guide

sections.body:
Overview

This document describes the Optimize Conductor 4.0 release: feature highlights, API and UX changes, SLO and cost implications, a step-by-step migration and rollout checklist for customers and internal teams, and known issues and rollback procedures. Optimize Conductor 4.0 ships a new multi-tenant optimization engine, deep integration with the Fidelity Advisor, and kernel-aware scheduling to reduce per-token cost while preserving observed fidelity.

Goals of the release

- Reduce average per-token inference cost for mixed conversational workloads by 15–35% depending on traffic shape.
- Enable live fidelity negotiation between the Optimize Advisor and the serving runtime for dynamic, SLO-aware routing.
- Provide robust, telemetry-first migration paths for existing Conductor 2.x/3.x customers with minimal service disruption.
- Expose a stable API and a migration shim to preserve backwards compatibility for SDKs and partner integrations.

What’s new in 4.0 (high level)

1) Multi-tenant optimization engine
- A federated optimizer that maintains per-tenant batching and caching policies with a global capacity-aware admission controller.
- Benefits: better cross-tenant utilization, fewer cold-start penalties for low-volume tenants.

2) Kernel-aware scheduling and quantization profiles
- Scheduler now uses model architecture and target hardware metadata (kernel fingerprints) to select quantization and execution paths per-batch.
- Benefits: improved throughput for quantized variants, automatic fallbacks to safe execution paths under load.

3) Fidelity Advisor v2 integration
- Live API that negotiates fidelity targets per-request with the serving runtime. Fidelity policies are evaluated against real-time telemetry and historical customer thresholds.
- Benefits: observable, auditable fidelity decisions and automated crediting adjustments.

4) Hybrid KV-prefetch cache coordinator
- Local-prefetch proxy and a cloud-coordinated KV cache eviction protocol reduce repeated KV misses for session-heavy conversational workloads.

5) Telemetry and cost-normalization changes
- New per-route cost attribution fields (cost_estimate, cost_adjuster_id).
- Streaming telemetry schema v3 (see Observability section below).

6) Console UX and API changes
- New Optimize Conductor UI: per-tenant policy editor, rollout simulator, and a migration dashboard.
- API: /optimize/v4/policies, /optimize/v4/migrate, /optimize/v4/simulate

Compatibility and deprecations

- Backwards compatibility: SDKs calling /optimize/v3 will be routed to a compatibility shim which preserves prior semantics for 12 months post-release. We recommend migrating to v4 within 90 days for full performance benefits.
- Deprecated: legacy batch policy fields 'batch_target_ms' and 'kv_strategy: legacy' are deprecated and will be removed in 2029-10-01.

Important SLO and performance notes

- Expected latency impact: median generation latency unchanged for steady-state traffic; p95 may improve for quantized-optimized paths but can increase during initial migration windows by ~5–10% while batchers warm.
- Cost impact: measured 15–35% savings in mixed chat + embeddings workloads in beta; savings are sensitive to session affinity and average prompt length.
- Telemetry SLO: optimize-conductor ingestion should achieve 99.9% delivery for telemetry events; customers relying on fidelity negotiation should ensure <500ms telemetry propagation to meet tight latency SLOs.

Release compatibility matrix (summary)

- Conductor 2.x -> 4.0: Must run migration shim; recommended staged canary rollout (see checklist).
- Conductor 3.0 -> 4.0: Direct upgrade supported; run the compatibility tests in the migration playbook.

Migration plan and checklist (recommended approach)

Ownership: product -> release manager; eng-platform -> rollout; eng-serving-runtime -> runtime compatibility; customer-success -> customer comms.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Preparation (2 weeks before canary)
- Identify tenants for staged rollout; prefer 5–10% of traffic slice for initial canary.
- Verify that the customer has telemetry-forwarding >= 99% and healthchecks for /v1/health of local-prefetch proxies.
- Run preflight simulator: curl -X POST /optimize/v4/simulate -d '{"traffic_profile":"tenant-sample"}' and confirm cost_estimate delta.

2) Canary (1 week)
- Deploy Optimize Conductor 4.0 to a single region and enable only non-critical tenants.
- Monitor p50/p95 latency, KV miss rate, policy decision error rates, and fidelity negotiation failures.
- Keep compatibility shim active for any SDKs hitting /v3.

3) Gradual rollout (2–6 weeks)
- Increase traffic in doubling increments (10% -> 20% -> 40% -> 80% -> 100%), waiting for stable telemetry after each step (minimum 24 hours).
- Validate cost and quality metrics against baseline.

4) Post-rollout verification (2 weeks)
- Run fidelity regression suites (PRD test harness) and collect customer-reported regressions.
- Disable compatibility shim after confirming zero critical regressions for 14 days.

Migration checklist (detailed)

- [ ] Run preflight simulation and capture cost_estimate baseline.
- [ ] Ensure customers have updated SDKs supporting v4 or confirm compatibility fallback is acceptable.
- [ ] Confirm telemetry schema v3 ingestion is enabled for the tenant.
- [ ] Validate KMS/HSM policies for any encrypted KV prefetch state.
- [ ] Coordinate canary window with customer success for high-value accounts.
- [ ] Record rollback points (cluster snapshots, config versions).

API changes and examples
sections.heading: Phases
New endpoints (examples)

sections.body:
- rwdctl optimize migrate --tenant t-123 --target 4.0 --dry-run

Console changes and operator guidance

- New migration dashboard: shows per-tenant cost delta, fidelity regression flags, and a staged rollout controller.
- Operators should use the simulator to sanity-check policy updates before committing to tenant production.

Observability and telemetry details

Telemetry schema v3 highlights: new fields
- cost_estimate (float): in USD per 1000 tokens estimated by optimizer
- cost_adjuster_id (string): id of the cost normalization rule applied
- fidelity_decision_id (string): cross-reference to Fidelity Advisor decision traces

Recommended dashboards and alerts
- Dashboards: Optimize Conductor 4.0 -> Per-tenant cost trends, Batch utilization heatmap, Fidelity decision trace viewer.
- Alerts (examples):
  - fidelity.negotiation.failures > 1% in 5m -> Sev2 (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
  - kv.miss_rate increase > 2x baseline in 10m -> Sev2 (owner: eng-platform)
  - telemetry.ingestion.failures > 0.1% in 15m -> Sev1 (owner: eng-sre)

Quality and evaluation guidance

- Run the packaged regression harness: tests/regression/optimize_v4/ which includes synthetic traffic shapes: conversational-heavy, short-prompt-burst, embedding-only, mixed-transactional.
- Evaluation metrics to track: response_consistency, hallucination_rate (if available), latency_p95, per_token_cost.

Known issues and limitations

- During heavy partitioning events the hybrid KV-prefetch coordinator may temporarily increase tail latency by up to 40% until evictions stabilize. Workaround: toggle prefetch:fallback_to_local = true.
- Some edge model variants with custom CUDA kernels may not yet benefit from kernel-aware scheduling; consult the compatibility matrix.
- Console migration dashboard can display stale cost deltas for tenants with infrequent traffic; use the simulate endpoint for accurate dry runs.

Rollback plan

- If p95 latency or fidelity regressions exceed defined thresholds during canary:
  1) Pause rollout and revert policy updates via /optimize/v4/policies rollback API.
  2) If regression persists, scale back to previous conductor image using cluster snapshot and disable multi-tenant optimizer feature flag.
  3) Notify customer-success and schedule a hotfix window.

Security and compliance notes

- Conductor 4.0 requires that any prefetch cache state persisted to disk is encrypted with customer KMS keys for customers with restricted confidentiality settings.
- Audit logging: all fidelity negotiation decisions are written to the audit log stream with retention consistent with customer's compliance tier.

Customer communication and enablement

- Outbound comms: send migration playbook and preflight checklist to customers 10 business days before planned migration.
- Include an optional 30-minute technical review call for enterprise customers during canary.

Appendix A: Backwards compatibility shim behavior

- The compat shim translates /optimize/v3 semantics to v4 with the following rules:
  - Legacy batch_target_ms -> batch_budget_ms mapping with normalization factor 0.8.
  - Explicitly disables kernel-aware scheduling for shimmed requests to preserve latency characteristics.
  - Returns a deprecation header: X-Optimize-Deprecation: v3-compat; replacement: /optimize/v4

Appendix B: Telemetry migration sample

- Example event (schema v3):
  {
    "timestamp":"2028-09-15T14:32:05Z",
    "tenant_id":"t-123",
    "route":"/v1/generate",
    "cost_estimate":0.0024,
    "fidelity_decision_id":"fd-789",
    "batch_id":"b-456"
  }

Contacts and ownership

- Release owner: Priya Ramakrishnan (product)
- Runtime compatibility: Anika Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- Rollout and infra: Marcus Liu (eng-platform)
- Customer enablement: Diego Alvarez (customer-success)

Document history

- 2028-09-15: Draft created by Priya Ramakrishnan
- 2028-09-18: Internal review and expanded migration checklist (reviewers: Diego, Maya)
- 2028-09-20: Published after resolving compatibility shim behavior notes

payload.page_title: Optimize 1.3 release notes — Performance Profiles & Cost Telemetry

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document summarizes the Redwood Optimize 1.3 release (GA: 2026-02-20). Optimize 1.3 introduces Performance Profiles, Telemetry-based Cost Estimator, latency-tier presets for the Console, and several SDK/CLI usability improvements. The release targets customers using Redwood Optimize to tune Dedicated and Hosted inference for predictable unit economics and simplified rollout of quantization/batching recommendations.

Highlights
----------
- Performance Profiles (feature flag: optimize.performance_profiles): per-model, per-workload profiles that capture measured latency/throughput/cost at multiple sequence-length distributions. Profiles power auto-suggestion rules and the new cost estimator.
- Telemetry-based Cost Estimator: end-to-end estimator that uses historical request shape telemetry (prefix length, tokens-per-request, hit rates) to produce monthly cost projections and sensitivity analyses.
- Latency-tier Presets in Console: new predefined profiles (S0: <50ms p95, S1: <120ms p95, S2: <250ms p95) that automatically tune batching and cache TTL recommendations.
- SDK v0.18.0: new Optimize client with async estimate_cost() and get_performance_profile() helpers; breaking rename of estimate() -> estimate_cost().
- CLI: redwood optimize export-profile <model> -> writes a reproducible YAML profile used for Dedicated scheduling.
- Migration & compatibility: recommended default quantization profiles unchanged; deprecated optimize.legacy_hint removed (see Migration notes).

What’s new (detailed)
---------------------
1) Performance Profiles
   - Description: Profiles record observed stat distributions for: sequence_length, tokens_generated, request_rate (qps), prefix_cache_hit_rate. Each profile stores measured p50/p95 latencies and per-token GPU time across representative buckets (short/medium/long).
   - Storage: profiles are stored in the customer namespace (s3-backed), versioned, and visible via Console and API.
   - API preview: POST /v1/optimize/profiles {"model":"redwood-7b-v1","workload":"chat-short"} -> returns profile id and recommendations.
   - Owner: Optimize team (owner: Deepa Nair).

2) Telemetry-based Cost Estimator
   - Inputs: time window (default 30d), model(s), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated), commitment tier, sequence-length histogram.
   - Output: month-over-month projection (USD), token breakdown (input/system/output), sensitivity table (how cost changes if average tokens/request increases by +10/25/50%).
   - Accuracy caveats: estimator factors in measured batching efficiency and prefix cache hit rate; for cold-start or sparse telemetry customers, the estimator uses conservative defaults (see config below).
   - Console: new "Cost Projection" panel on Optimize pages with download CSV button.

3) Latency-tier Presets
   - Presets: S0 (ultra-low latency), S1 (balanced), S2 (cost-efficient). Each preset maps to batching window targets, max batch size, and prefix_cache_TTL suggestions.
   - Implementation: presets are applied as heuristics on top of Performance Profiles and can be overridden by route-level policy.

4) SDK & CLI changes
   - SDK v0.18.0: function rename estimate() -> estimate_cost(); new async wrapper; returns structured CostEstimate object. See SDK guide for migration snippet.
   - CLI: new export-profile command produces a YAML suitable for Dedicated scheduler. Example: redwood optimize export-profile redwood-13b-v2 --window 7d --out profile.yaml

Migration notes and breaking changes
----------------------------------
- Deprecated field removed: optimize.legacy_hint (previously used for heuristic-only recommendations). Action: remove any usages in saved route configs. Failure to remove will return 400 in API calls that include the field.
- SDK rename: update code references estimate() -> estimate_cost(). Simple search-and-replace sufficient for most codebases.
- Profile format changes: profile v1 -> v2 adds buckets for "prefix_cache_hit_rate". Dedicated scheduler accepts both v1 and v2, but v1 profiles will be automatically converted on import with a best-effort fill (read-only). We recommend re-exporting profiles after conversion.

Configuration snippets and examples
----------------------------------
- Console: Toggle Performance Profiles via Admin -> Optimize feature flags -> optimize.performance_profiles (default: off for existing tenants; on for new tenants).

- Example API request (cost estimate):

  Content-Type: application/json

    "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
    "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
    "window_days": 30,
    "sequence_histogram": {"short": 0.7, "medium": 0.25, "long": 0.05},
    "commitment_tier": "std-monthly-1"
  }

{

    "sensitivity": {"+10%_tokens_per_request": 12650.35}

- SDK migration example (Python):

  cost = optimize_client.estimate(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=30)
  # after
  cost = await optimize_client.estimate_cost(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=30)

Rollout plan
------------
- Canary: 2026-02-18 -> enable Performance Profiles for 10 pilot tenants (selection criteria: medium-sized Dedicated customers with diverse request shapes). Monitor p95 latency impact and console correctness.
- Gradual rollout: 2026-02-20 -> enable for new tenants and opt-in for existing tenants via Console.
- Full enforcement: 2026-03-10 -> deprecate legacy_hint on route configs (400 returned if present).

SLOs and observability
----------------------
- Optimize service SLO unaffected: 99.9% availability for API endpoints.
- Cost estimator-specific: 99% of estimates generated within 2s for inputs with cached Performance Profiles; 95% within 5s for uncached inputs.
- Telemetry metrics exposed: optimize.profile_generation.count, optimize.estimate_latency_ms.p95, optimize.estimate_cache_hit_rate. Dashboards: /dashboards/optimize/1-3-release-estimates

How to opt-in / try it today
---------------------------
1) Console: Admin -> Feature flags -> toggle optimize.performance_profiles -> follow "Enable" flow to accept data-sharing for profile generation.
2) API: POST /v1/optimize/profiles?action=generate with model + window_days.
3) CLI: redwood optimize export-profile --generate redwood-7b-v1 --window 7d --out my-profile.yaml

Owner and support
-----------------
- Product owner: Deepa Nair (Optimize)
- Engineering lead: Samir Gupta (Optimize infra)
- Support: support@redwood.ai (use tag: optimize-1.3)
- Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/optimize-profile-generation-runbook

Known issues and limitations
---------------------------
- Cold telemetry causes conservative cost projections (noted in UI). We plan a future release (1.4) to add synthetic workload injection to reduce conservatism.
- Some legacy Dedicated accounts with strict region restrictions may see profile import failures due to S3 path policies; workaround: use CLI export/import via local file.

Full changelog (selected)
------------------------
- 1.3.0 (2026-02-20): GA release. Added Performance Profiles, Cost Estimator, Console presets, SDK 0.18.0, CLI export-profile.
- 1.3.0-rc1 (2026-02-10): Canary with 10 tenants; fixed profile-merge race leading to duplicate buckets.

Feedback and next steps
-----------------------
- We're actively collecting feedback via the Optimize workspace channel and customer QBRs. Priorities for 1.4: synthetic workload generation, improved estimator calculus for multi-model ensembles, and automated rollback suggestions when recommendations cause SLA regressions.

Appendix: reproducible profile YAML example
-----------------------------------------

workload: chat-short
buckets:
  - name: short
    pct: 70

  batching: {max_batch_size: 128, target_window_ms: 8}

If you need help migrating or want the Optimize team to run a custom projection for your account, contact Deepa or open a ticket with support (tag: optimize-1.3).

payload.page_title: Hosted Inference: Cost-Fallback & Telemetry Normalization 1.2 Release Notes

sections.body:
Release 1.2 introduces the Cost-Fallback policy engine for hosted inference and a normalized telemetry pipeline for cost attribution. This release improves transparency for fallback events, aligns billing signals with runtime decisions, and reduces cost overcounting in multi-variant fallthrough scenarios.
Cost-Fallback engine: deterministic policy layer that chooses fallback variants based on a configurable cost threshold and fidelity constraints.
Telemetry Normalization v1: a new pipeline stage that deduplicates token-attribution events across model-variant handoffs and retries.
Per-request fallback annotations surfaced in Console and API response headers for easier auditing and customer diagnostics.
New billing hook: optional trial-mode mode that simulates invoicing changes for 30 days without affecting charges.
Updated SDKs: client-side flag to opt into fallback transparency headers (Python/Node 1.2.0+).
Runtime and billing are backward compatible. Customers using legacy billing callbacks should update their webhook consumers to accept the new 'x-redwood-fallback-reason' header. SDK upgrades are recommended to get transparent fallback headers; however, clients that do not upgrade will continue to receive previous response shapes with reduced visibility.
| Area | Change | Customer Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serving runtime | Cost-Fallback engine enabled by default for low-tier routes | Potentially different model variants selected under peak load | See rollout controls and opt-out guide below |
| Billing & metering | Telemetry Normalization deduplicates attribution events | Near-term apparent drop in 'per-token' invoiced events on reconciliations (expected) | Billing simulator available; reconciliations will align within billing cycle |
| Console | New fallback timeline and per-request annotations | Additional UI column and export fields | Minor learning curve; docs + quickstart provided |
| SDKs | Response header additions and opt-in flags | No functional breakage, richer diagnostics | Upgrade SDK to 1.2.0+ for full experience |
1) 2026-06-30: Canary rollout on 5% hosted traffic in us-west-2.
2) 2026-07-07: Observability window review; extend to 25% if no regressions.
3) 2026-07-14: Billing reconciliation test with sandbox customers.
4) 2026-07-21: Full enablement for hosted API worldwide with migration window.
5) 2026-08-01: Billing switch: normalization applied to customer invoices (retroactive disclaimers applied for trial-mode customers).
Step 1: Review the Cost-Fallback policy defaults in Console > Routing > Fallback Policies and note any routes with custom targeting.
Step 2: For enterprise contracts with explicit variant lock requirements, open a support ticket to pin variant selection or opt-out of the Cost-Fallback engine.
Step 3: If you have downstream billing webhooks, update consumers to parse and ignore unknown headers; optionally implement handling for 'x-redwood-fallback-reason'.
Step 4: Enable Billing Simulator in Console > Billing > Simulators for a 30-day trial of normalized billing to preview impact (no real charges).
Step 5: Upgrade client SDKs to 1.2.0+ to receive fallback annotations in response headers and to toggle client-side annotation flags where necessary.
| Config | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| fallback.cost_threshold_pct | 20 | Percentage over baseline cost allowed before fallback triggers |
| fallback.fidelity_floor | medium | Minimum fidelity required for fallback target variants |
| telemetry.dedup_window_ms | 250 | Time window for de-duplicating token attribution events |
| billing.simulator.enabled | false | Admin toggle to run invoicing preview without charges |
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- New emitted events: 'fallback.choice', 'fallback.eviction', 'telemetry.normalization.delta'.
- Console dashboards: 'Fallback Rate by Route', 'Normalized vs Raw Token Delta'.
- Alerts added: 'Fallback rate > 15% for 5m' (severity P2), 'Normalization delta > 10% for a billing window' (severity P3).
Action: On elevated fallback rates investigate KV-cache hit rates, variant capacity, and cost profiles. Telemetry Normalization alert indicates reconciliation variance; if triggered, contact billing-ops before making routing changes.
1) Toggle 'fallback.enabled' to false at service-level (Console or API) to stop policy-based variant selection.
2) Revert telemetry normalization by setting 'telemetry.normalization.enabled' to false in Admin feature-flags (safe for 1-hour windows).
3) If invoice anomalies occur, enable billing.simulator and run reconciliation; contact finance-ops to freeze invoice dispatch.
4) Post-mortem: collect last 72h of 'fallback.choice' and 'telemetry.normalization.delta' events and file incident per oncall runbook.
- In rare cases (multi-region failover + retry storm) deduplication may undercount attribution; SREs will apply a temporary increased dedup_window_ms.
- SDKs older than 1.1.5 will not expose new header metadata; these clients will see reduced visibility into fallback decisions.
- Customers using third-party metering proxies that rely on raw token events should use the Billing Simulator to validate before full migration.
Q: Will normalized telemetry change what I'm billed?
A: Normalized telemetry reconciles attribution to avoid double-counting across retries and handoffs; legitimate usage is preserved, but line-item distribution may shift. Use the Billing Simulator to see projected changes.

Q: Can I disable Cost-Fallback for specific routes?
A: Yes — Console supports per-route override. For contracts that require strict variant selection, contact your account team to set enforcement rules.

Q: What if normalization causes a >15% delta during initial invoices?
A: We will not auto-bill unilaterally. Billing ops will notify impacted customers during the migration window and apply manual reconciliations as needed.
- 2026-07-09: Run 72h reconciliation job for canary tenants and publish findings.
- 2026-07-18: Deliver support knowledge base article and customer comms template.
- 2026-08-05: Retrospective with stakeholders to capture improvements for 1.3.
Product owner: Aisha R. Morales (aisha.morales@redwood.ai)
Engineering lead: Marcus Li (marcus.li@redwood.ai)
SRE oncall: paged via #sre-oncall
Billing ops: billing-ops@redwood.ai
Support: support@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Edge Deployment: Consumption & Packaging Guidance

sections.body:
Overview

This document explains recommended consumption patterns, packaging options, and operational requirements for customers deploying Redwood inference at the edge (VPC-edge appliances, on-prem appliance, and lightweight cloud-edge regions). It is intended for product managers, solutions engineers, and the dedicated/private deployment teams who design packaging and pricing for edge use cases.

Goal and scope

- Goal: Provide prescriptive guidance that balances predictable economics, SLOs, and customer rollout friction for edge-style deployments.
- Scope: Applies to small-to-medium edge sites (single node to 4-node clusters) and distributed edge fleets with regional management. Does not replace Dedicated/Hosted economics guidance; it complements them.

Key design principles

1) Predictable unit metrics: prefer per-instance or per-site capacity metrics (concurrent sessions, reserved vGPU units) over purely per-token billing for edge customers.
2) SLO-aligned packaging: offer SKU variants tied to latency and availability SLOs (e.g., "Edge Standard" vs "Edge SLO+"), with explicit throttling and fallback behavior.
3) Operational simplicity: reduce on-site configuration needed; provide sane defaults for batching, KV caching, and quantization.
4) Graceful degradation: include automatic fallback to lower-cost/compatibility model variant and a controlled degradation policy to preserve uptime.

Recommended packaging primitives

- Site Reservation (monthly): commits to N reserved vGPU units (e.g., small=1, medium=2, large=4). Includes baseline throughput, priority routing, and access to remote control plane.
- Per-Request Add-on: optional metered overage for burst traffic (per-100ms inference unit).
- SLO Add-on: paid feature adding 99.9% availability SLA and 95th percentile per-request latency caps with penalty credits.
- Telemetry Retention Tiers: default 7d, premium 90d for diagnostics and audits.

Suggested SKU examples (illustrative)

| SKU | Reserved vGPU | Target QPS | 95p Latency SLO | Telemetry | Monthly price (USD) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Edge Small | 1 | 15 | <250ms | 7d | 3,500 |
| Edge Medium | 2 | 40 | <200ms | 30d | 7,500 |
| Edge High SLO | 4 | 120 | <120ms | 90d | 22,000 |

(Prices are example guidance for sales/solutions engineering; final pricing to be validated in GTM motions.)

Operational configuration defaults

- Kernel/Runtime: enable continuous batching with max_batch_size=64 for text-gen workloads and dynamic_batch_timeout_ms=5 for low-latency sites.
- KV Cache: enable local prefix/KV caching with eviction TTL=12h for conversational workloads.
- Quantization profile: recommend int8 dynamic quantization for Llama-family models; fallback to int8+KV-aware execution for long context workloads.
- Memory limits: set per-container token buffer ceiling at 512k tokens to avoid OOM during spike patterns.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
---
edge_site:
  reserved_vgpu: 2
  runtime_defaults:
    max_batch_size: 64
    dynamic_batch_timeout_ms: 5
    kv_cache_enabled: true
    kv_cache_ttl_hours: 12
    quant_profile: int8-dynamic
  telemetry:
    retention_days: 30
    sampling_rate: 0.2
  fallback_policy:
    - when: cpu_util > 85%
      action: shift-to-compat-variant
    - when: network_latency > 300ms
      action: circuit-breaker-throttle
---

Rollout checklist for new edge customers

1. Pre-sales sizing & spike analysis: collect 7-day traffic trace or synthetic peak tests.
2. Default package selection: map required QPS and latency to SKU; confirm telemetry needs.
3. On-site validation: install appliance, run smoke test suite (see CLI commands below), validate model variants and KV-caching.
4. Canary traffic: route 5–10% of production traffic for 24–72 hours to the site and monitor error budget usage.
5. Full cutover and monitoring: enable customer-facing DNS and begin normal routing; maintain enhanced analytical sampling for 72 hours.
6. Post-cutover review: run performance report and capture lessons in the customer folder.

Smoke test CLI examples

- Install verification: redwoodctl edge status --site SITE_ID
- Latency sanity: redwoodctl benchmark --site SITE_ID --model MODEL --duration 60s --qps 10
- KV caching check: redwoodctl inspect-kv --site SITE_ID --model MODEL

SLO definitions and monitoring signals

- Latency SLO (95th): measured as server-side response completion time from request receipt to final token emitted.
- Availability SLO: percent of successful RPCs over rolling 30-day window.
- Error budget policy: If error budget < 25% over a 7-day window, trigger remediation runbook and consider temporary capacity boost.

Important thresholds (default)

- 95p latency target: Edge Small <250ms, Edge Medium <200ms, Edge High SLO <120ms.
- CPU utilization watermark for scaling decisions: 70% (soft), 85% (hard).
- Network latency threshold for remote control plane failover: 300ms.

Billing and metering notes

- Primary metering: reserved vGPU units as the committed unit. This allows customers to predict monthly spend.
- Overage billing: measured in 100ms “inference units” for additional usage beyond reserved capacity.
- Cross-charge for telemetry storage and extended retention as separate line item.

Fallback and graceful degradation policy

- First-tier: model variant fallback (e.g., reduce context length or move to a sparsely-quantized variant) while preserving API contract.
- Second-tier: request shedding with informative 503 including Retry-After and diagnostics token.
- Third-tier: circuit-breaker engages, redirecting to remote-hosted instance (if allowed by customer policy).

Security and compliance considerations

- Default: encrypt all data-at-rest with customer KMS integrated to HSM when available.
- Network: site must provide egress rules allowing control-plane webhooks and telemetry uplinks. Optionally support fully air-gapped installs with offline license key exchange.
- Audit: generate deployment and model-change audit logs retained according to telemetry tier.

Ownership and escalation

- Product owner: Aisha Patel (Edge packaging and economics).
- Solutions engineering: Marcus Chen (customer sizing & onboarding).
- Private Deployments engineering: Jordan Li (installer, runtime tuning).
- Escalation path: SE -> Private Deployments oncall -> SRE platform lead (pager).

Open questions (to resolve before GTM)

1. Final price anchoring for APAC channel partners (currency and margin adjustments).
2. Specific penalty terms for SLO add-on in multi-site failover scenarios.
3. Precise telemetry egress bandwidth caps for low-connectivity sites.

Appendices

A. Related configuration templates: refer to /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging for installer manifests.
B. Benchmark harness: reference the eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite repo for workload profiles and synthetic traces.

Notes

This guidance should be used as the canonical playbook when preparing offers and scopes for edge-style private deployments. Sales and solutions engineers must confirm price and SLA language with finance and legal before committing to customer contracts.

payload.page_title: Developer Fidelity Alignment: Integrator Kit & Onboarding Playbook

sections.body:
SUMMARY
This playbook describes the "Integrator Kit" approach to align developer expectations for response fidelity across Local Developer Runtimes, Hosted Redwood API, and Dedicated/Private deployments. It combines a lightweight SDK, telemetry contract, sample fidelity test-suite, migration checklist, and commercial guidance so partner integrations ship with predictable quality and predictable cost. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction, avoid repeat regressions caused by quantization/sequence-length interactions, and surface cost/latency trade-offs early in customer engagements.

AUDIENCE
- Platform and product engineers integrating with Redwood APIs or embedding Redwood SDKs in developer tooling.
- Solutions engineers and customer success teams onboarding customers migrating from local dev or self-hosted inference to Redwood hosted/dedicated modes.
- Developer advocates and partner engineers building Marketplace connectors.

GOALS
- Provide a small, reproducible fidelity test-suite engineers can run locally and in CI to measure parity across runtimes (local sim -> hosted -> dedicated).
- Define a telemetry contract (minimum signals) for debugging fidelity regressions and cost attribution.
- Document a step-by-step migration checklist with clear ownership, gating criteria, and rollback signals.
- Offer packaging & pricing guidance for integrators choosing default fidelity presets.

SCOPE AND NON-SCOPE
- In-scope: text generation/chat fidelity alignment, short-form embeddings, and reranking flows. Includes SDK samples for JS/Python, CI integration patterns, and observability dashboards.
- Out-of-scope: full model training workflows, custom model adapters for third-party LLM vendors (see third-party-model-adapters-design).

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
1) Quick start (integrator kit contents)
2) Fidelity test-suite and metrics
3) Telemetry contract (required signals)
4) Migration checklist (canary -> rollout -> rollback)
5) Packaging & pricing guidance
6) Design notes and engineering requirements
7) Roadmap and release notes
8) Appendix: API examples and CI snippets

1) QUICK START: WHAT'S IN THE INTEGRATOR KIT
- SDK bundle: lightweight NPM/PyPI packages (redwood-integrator-js, redwood-integrator-py) that wrap the Redwood API and provide fidelity-preserving defaults (max_tokens caps, deterministic sampling presets, KV cache warmup helpers).
- Fidelity test-suite: 150 curated prompts covering conversational, multi-turn, and long-context edge cases plus expected-checksum responses for deterministic configurations.
- CI integration recipe: GitHub Actions + CircleCI templates to run suite against multiple endpoints.
- Telemetry schema: example events, recommended tags, and a sample Grafana dashboard JSON.
- Migration checklist: owner roles, canary size guide, SLO regressions to watch, and cost-guard rails.

2) FIDELITY TEST-SUITE AND METRICS
Short description: The suite is intentionally small and deterministic so it can run quickly in CI while being sensitive to common regressions (tokenization differences, sampling temperature, quantization-induced word-choice drift).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- pass_rate (percentage of prompts matching expected-checksum under deterministic settings)
- token_delta_median (median difference in token count produced vs reference)
- semantic_similarity_median (embedding cosine median when run with canonical embed model)
- latency_p95 (milliseconds)
- cost_per_prompt_usd (estimated token pricing model)

Example expected outputs: the suite includes a JSONL file (checked-in to integrator-kit repo) where each row contains prompt_id, prompt_text, canonical_response_checksum, canonical_embedding_vector_id. CI uses the checksum and similarity thresholds to triage failures.

3) TELEMETRY CONTRACT (MINIMUM SIGNALS)
All Redwood integrations running in production must emit the following minimum signals to the customer's telemetry and to Redwood's observability pipeline (customer-permissioned):
- request_id (string)
- model_id (string)
- model_variant (string)
- runtime_mode (local|hosted|dedicated|private)
- sequence_length_in, sequence_length_out (integers)
- latency_ms (integer)
- tokens_input, tokens_output (integers)
- sampling_seed (if provided), temperature, top_p (floats)
- batch_size (integer)
- quantization_profile (string)
- fidelity_flag (string) - e.g., fidelity:high|medium|low
- test_suite_prompt_id (optional) - when running regression suite
- checksum_match (bool) - when applicable
These fields are sufficient for us to triage: (1) fidelity regressions, (2) cost spikes, and (3) sizing/latency anomalies.

Suggested tagging: tenant_id, route_id, environment (dev|staging|prod), sdk_version.

4) MIGRATION CHECKLIST (OWNER + STEP-BY-STEP)
Owners: Solutions Engineering (lead), Product Engineering (runtime), Customer Success (communication).
Pre-Canary
1. Confirm customer use-cases and target SLOs (latency p95 <= X ms, semantic_similarity_median >= 0.88, error_rate <= 0.5%).
2. Run fidelity test-suite against customer's local runtime and record baseline metrics.
3. Configure integrator SDK with "preserve-determinism" mode and run suite against Redwood hosted sandbox.
4. Validate telemetry contract is enabled and flowing to sandbox dashboards.

Canary (10% traffic or 50k monthly tokens, whichever is smaller)
1. Create canary route with identical config to production route except model_variant pinned to canary.
2. Monitor pass_rate, semantic_similarity_median, latency_p95, and cost_per_prompt every 30 minutes for first 24 hours.
3. Set automated abort triggers: pass_rate drop >= 5 percentage points, semantic_similarity_median delta >= 0.05, latency_p95 increase >= 30%. If triggered, abort and rollback to previous variant.

Rollout
1. If canary is healthy for 72 hours, schedule linear rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 12-hour observation windows.
2. After each step, run full fidelity test-suite in production traffic shadow mode (run requests in shadow and evaluate checksums without affecting response path).
3. Finalize rollback window for 72 hours post-100% rollout.

Rollback signals
- sustained semantic_similarity_median drop > 0.03 for 24h, or
- increased user-facing error rate > 1% for 30 minutes, or
- unexpected cost uplift > 20% for 1 hour.

5) PACKAGING & PRICING GUIDANCE
Default packaging suggestions when recommending fidelity presets to customers:
- "Balanced" preset: medium caching, mixed quantization (8-bit for matmul-heavy layers), sampling temp 0.7. Good for low-latency chat; recommended for self-serve.
- "High-fidelity" preset: reduced quantization, conservative pruning, pre-warmed KV cache, deterministic sampling for key routes. Recommended for enterprise workflows with strict semantic parity needs.
- "Economy" preset: aggressive quantization, higher batch sizes, fallback to lower-cost variant for non-critical routes. Recommended for high-throughput vectorization workloads.

Commercial notes: provide a fidelity addon SKU (monthly) that bundles: 1) additional fidelity test runs per month, 2) extended observability retention (90 days), 3) access to model-variant compatibility support. Pricing examples should tie to committed tokens and observability retention tiers. Include credit-based pilot pricing for initial integration (e.g., 200k tokens free + 30-day fidelity triage support).

6) DESIGN NOTES AND ENGINEERING REQUIREMENTS
High-level requirements (must be met by product engineering to support Integrator Kit):
- Runtime: provide an API parameter "preserve_determinism" that enforces fixed seeds, disables non-deterministic kernels, and returns canonical tokenization metadata.
- Telemetry: expose an ingestion endpoint for integrator-sdk telemetry with per-tenant sampling controls.
- Sandbox: maintain a sandbox model_variant pinned to a known config for integration tests.
- Canary tooling: automated route duplication and linear rollout orchestration (existing rollout API extension).
- Cost calculator: API-based estimator endpoint that accepts expected token histogram and returns per-prompt cost across model variants.
sections.heading: Key metrics (computed per run)

sections.body:
- All telemetry carrying test_suite_prompt_id or checksum_match must be flagged as test data and not included in persistent eval datasets unless explicit consent is provided.
- Keys used in integrator SDK must support scoped TTLs and route-limited scopes to limit blast radius during canaries.
sections.heading: Minimal security/ops constraints

sections.body:
| Setting | Purpose | Recommended default | Owner |
|---------|---------|---------------------|-------|
| preserve_determinism | Ensure repeatable outputs for regression checks | true (for test runs) | runtime team |
| fidelity_preset | High/Medium/Low fidelity cost tradeoffs | Medium | product |
| max_tokens_per_prompt | Safety and cost guard | 1024 | solutions eng |
| kv_cache_warmup | Pre-warm cache to reduce first-token latency | enabled | runtime |
| telemetry_sample_rate | Controls volume of telemetry | 100% for canary, 1% for production | eng-sre |

7) ROADMAP & RELEASE NOTES
sections.heading: Requirements table (configurable knobs)

sections.body:
- Q4 2026: publish integrator-kit SDKs and fidelity test-suite; create hosted sandbox variant and provide pilot credits.
- Q1 2027: rollout preserve_determinism API parameter and basic canary automation in Console.
- Q2 2027: fidelity-addon SKU launch with observability retention tiers and automated fidelity advisor in Console.

Release notes (v1.0 — 2026-10-12):
- Deliverables: integrator-kit repo, fidelity-test-suite (150 prompts), sample Grafana dashboard, GH Actions recipe, pricing pilot guidelines.
- Known limitations: deterministic checks currently only supported on select model families; embedding-based similarity uses reference embed model ID and must be gated per-customer.

8) APPENDIX: API EXAMPLES AND CI SNIPPETS
A. Example API snippet (Python) — deterministic test run\
```python
from redwood_integrator import RedwoodIntegrator
client = RedwoodIntegrator(api_key="REDACTED", preserve_determinism=True)
resp = client.generate(route_id="acme-chat", prompt="Summarize the customer's account notes.", max_tokens=256, model_variant="sandbox-fid-v1")
print(resp.text)
sections.heading: Roadmap (near term)

sections.body:
```
B. GitHub Actions matrix example (run tests against local and hosted):
```yaml
name: fidelity-ci
on: [push]
jobs:
  run-suite:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        runtime: [local, hosted]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run fidelity suite
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          ./tools/run_fidelity_suite.sh --runtime ${{ matrix.runtime }} --report results/${{ matrix.runtime }}.json
```

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q: What if a customer's local runtime inherently differs (different tokenizer)?
A: We require the Integrator Kit to include a tokenizer compatibility check. If mismatch is unavoidable, document the delta in the integration notes and prefer embedding-based similarity thresholds over checksum checks for content-sensitive routes.

Q: Can we run full fidelity checks on production traffic?
A: Never mutate production responses. Use shadowing to run checks in parallel and report checksum_match without impacting live responses.

OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS
- Product lead: Priya Nandakumar (product)
- Runtime engineering steward: Jian Li (eng-serving-runtime)
- Solutions engineering lead: Eliot Harper (customer-success)
- Pricing & packaging: Marisol Velez (go-to-market)

APPROVALS
- Approved by: Product Council (2026-11-02)
- Pilot cohort: 3 customers (beta) launched 2026-12-01

RELATED PAGES AND REFERENCES
- Developer consumption scenarios catalog (see related_pages)
- Onboarding and cost advisor playbook (see related_pages)
- Third-party model adapters design spec (for vendor adapter guidance)

CHANGELOG
- 2026-10-12: v1.0 initial publish — integrator-kit assets and CI recipes.
- 2026-12-01: added canary abort triggers and concierge pilot pricing.
- 2027-01-05: updated telemetry contract with fidelity_flag and sampling guidance.

END OF DOCUMENT
