sections.body: Title: Developer Consumption Scenarios Catalog (2026)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This catalog describes common developer integration patterns for Redwood Inference, recommended defaults, performance expectations, pricing implications, and product requirements that the product and engineering teams should support. It is intended to guide SDK documentation, onboarding templates, and cost/latency calculators in the Console and Optimize product.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Product managers and technical writers building onboarding flows
- Solutions engineers and SEs onboarding new customers
- SDK and runtime engineers implementing defaults and telemetry
- Sales engineers advising customers on SLA and pricing choices
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body: We observed five consistent consumption archetypes across customers during Q4 2025 and H1 2026: transactional chat, bulk/async summarization, embedding-heavy search, high-throughput reranking, and multimodal enrichment pipelines. Each archetype has distinct latency SLOs, cost sensitivity, and recommended serving configuration. Supporting clear first-class paths for each will reduce time-to-first-success and lower surprise bills.
sections.heading: Executive summary

sections.body:
1) Transactional chat (conversational UI)
   - Description: Low-latency request/response flows where each request should return a coherent multi-turn response in <200ms P95 for simple prompts and <600ms for long-context turns. Typical for in-app assistants, chatbots, and support UIs.
   - Recommended model variants: conversational-1-small (dev), conversational-1 (default), conversational-1-fp16 (low-latency).
   - SLOs & KPIs: P95 latency target 150–600ms depending on fidelity; error rate <0.5%; context length up to 4k tokens.
   - Default runtime config: streaming enabled, continuous KV caching per session (TTL 30m), batch-size target 8, max-batch-wait 8ms.
   - Cost sensitivity: medium. Recommend dynamic quantization for dev/test; for production prefer fp16 on Dedicated.
   - Pricing guidance: favor per-token pricing with optional concurrency-based discounts for high-throughput chat channels.

2) Bulk/async summarization (document pipelines)
   - Description: Large documents or corpora processed asynchronously. Latency tolerance measured in minutes rather than milliseconds; cost per unit is primary metric.
   - Recommended model variants: summarization-1-medium, summarization-1-quantized-8bit.
   - SLOs & KPIs: throughput (docs/hour), cost per doc, end-to-end latency 1–30 minutes depending on pipeline batching.
   - Default runtime config: large-batch worker pools, aggressive batching (batch-size 64–256), prefix caching disabled across unrelated requests, prefer quantized variants.
   - Cost sensitivity: high — recommend Schedule Jobs + Dedicated Reserved capacity with burst credits.
   - Pricing guidance: use token-bundle discounts and reserved-capacity packages; suggest customers use Redis pre-chunking to reduce token count.

3) Embedding generation at scale (search & vector DB population)
   - Description: Massive embedding workloads for indexing, similarity search, and vector database ingestion. IO-bound and typically offline or streaming.
   - Recommended model variants: embeddings-2-highthroughput, embeddings-2-quantized.
   - SLOs & KPIs: embeddings/sec, token efficiency, batching efficiency. Aim for >10k embeddings/hour per GPU worker for medium-size vectors.
   - Default runtime config: streaming-batch worker with per-request batching window 100–250ms, compacted batching to match vectorizer memory constraints.
   - Cost sensitivity: very high — customers should use Optimize recommendations to enable mixed-precision and larger batch sizes.
   - Pricing guidance: meter by 1) per-embedding unit with tiered volume discounts, or 2) per-job credits for offline cron jobs.

4) Reranking / kNN re-ranker (low-latency re-score)
   - Description: Small inputs with compute-heavy scoring (e.g., scoring 100 candidates). Requires stable latency and predictable cost.
   - Recommended model variants: reranker-1-small (fast), reranker-1 (balanced).
   - SLOs & KPIs: P95 latency <250ms for up to 100 candidates; per-request cost per 100 candidates target.
   - Default runtime config: vectorized scoring kernels, dedicated CPU offload for lightweight prefiltering, batch-size 1 with internal micro-batching for candidates.
   - Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Encourage model distillation or candidate pruning upstream.
   - Pricing guidance: recommend a per-request pricing add-on for high-candidate re-rank workloads or a candidate-count multiplier in billing.

5) Multimodal enrichment pipelines (OCR + LLM + embeddings)
   - Description: Pipelines combining document OCR, image embeddings, and LLM enrichment. These are compositional and often cross service boundaries.
   - Recommended model variants: multimodal-lite (edge), multimodal-core (cloud).
   - SLOs & KPIs: end-to-end pipeline latency; component reliability; per-document cost.
   - Default runtime config: orchestration via Redwood Conductor patterns, per-stage SLOs, and fallback to lower-fidelity model variants.
   - Cost sensitivity: mixed. Visual pre-processing is often dominant cost.
   - Pricing guidance: bundle consumption across stages into a single per-document credit to simplify billing and reduce surprise.
sections.heading: Catalog of scenarios (high-level)

sections.body:
- Table represented as plain text for Confluence import. Columns: Scenario | Default Model | Batch Strategy | Cache | Typical P95 Latency | Recommended Billing Mode
- Row 1: Transactional chat | conversational-1 | small continuous batching (8) | session KV cache (30m) | 150–600ms | per-token + concurrency discount
- Row 2: Bulk summarization | summarization-1-quant | large batches (64–256) | none | minutes | reserved capacity / token bundles
- Row 3: Embeddings | embeddings-2-qtz | medium batch (50) | no | seconds to minutes | per-embedding unit (volume tiers)
- Row 4: Reranking | reranker-1 | micro-batching internally | ephemeral | <250ms | per-request candidate multiplier
- Row 5: Multimodal | multimodal-core | stage-oriented batching | stage caches | variable | bundled per-document credit
sections.heading: Per-scenario recommended defaults (table)

sections.body:
- SDK defaults: expose a scenario preset parameter (e.g., scenario="chat-transactional") that applies recommended model, max_tokens, KV cache TTL, and batching hints.
- Console: add a Consumption Scenario Selector in onboarding with example throughput, estimated cost per 1k requests, and a toggle for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Optimize: ensure Optimize suggests quantization profiles per scenario and shows estimated cost savings and fidelity delta.
sections.heading: Implementation notes for SDKs and Console

sections.body:
1. Scenario presets in SDKs and Console (MVP): provide 5 presets mapped to runtime configs and telemetry tags.
2. Billing meter updates: support candidate-count multiplier for reranking and a per-document bundled credit for multimodal pipelines.
3. Telemetry: add scenario tags to all traces, token meters, and cost attribution so Console can show per-scenario costs.
4. Onboarding templates: produce quickstart repos for each scenario with sample data, infra Terraform for Dedicated testing, and a Q/A checklist.
sections.heading: Product requirements (high-level PRD bullets)

sections.body:
1) Customer selects scenario in Console or via SE flow.
2) Console pre-populates recommended model and capacity; shows simulated cost for 1k requests/day.
3) Customer runs sample traffic generator (included in quickstart) for 24h in staging.
4) Solutions engineer reviews telemetry: P95 latency, batching efficiency, token ratio.
5) If cost > expectation, enable Optimize recommendations: quantize, increase batch size, or enable fallback variants.
6) After acceptance, transition to Dedicated (optional) with reserved capacity sizing guide.
sections.heading: Operational playbook (onboarding sequence)

sections.body:
- UX simplicity vs configuration granularity: presets must be opinionated but not block advanced users.
- Pricing complexity vs fairness: bundling simplifies bills but must remain transparent for high-volume users.
- Default SLOs must be conservative so early adopters don't observe large regressions.
sections.heading: Design constraints and trade-offs

sections.body:
- Q1 2026: Launch SDK scenario presets + Console selector (MVP).
- Q2 2026: Telemetry tagging by scenario, consumption cost breakdown in Console.
- Q3 2026: Billing primitives for candidate multipliers and per-document credits.
- Q4 2026: Optimize integration that recommends scenario-specific quantization profiles and simulates fidelity impact.
sections.heading: Roadmap & next steps (quarterly milestones)

sections.body:
- Time-to-first-success: median time from signup to serving first 1k requests with stable SLOs (target <72 hours).
- Per-scenario cost accuracy: discrepancy between estimated and actual cost for first 30d (target <15%).
- Onboarding churn: percentage of customers that abandon after staging (target <10%).

Release notes snapshot (v0.1 - published 2026-01-15):
- Introduced Developer Consumption Scenarios Catalog and SDK scenario presets for chat, summarization, embeddings, reranking, and multimodal pipelines.
- Console: added onboarding selector that simulates cost and pre-configures runtime defaults.
- Telemetry: initial scenario tagging implemented for hosted API.

sections.body:
- Product owner: Marina Ortega (product)
- Engineering lead (SDKs): Evan Liu (engineering)
- Optimize integration: Priya Nair (engineering)
- Solutions engineering contact: Jamie Brooks (customer-success)

sections.body:

- Terraform patterns: internal repo: infra/terraform/dedicated-sample

Appendix: Example CLI snippet (chat transactional preset)
$ redwood-cli create-inference-job --scenario chat-transactional --model conversational-1 --concurrency 20 --kv-cache-ttl 1800

JSON example (preset manifest)
{
  "preset": "chat-transactional",
  "model": "conversational-1",

payload.page_title: Session Resilience: Onboarding & Fallback Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended onboarding path, configuration checklist, SLO mapping, and operational runbook for session resilience and automatic fallback behavior for Redwood Inference customers and internal integrations. It is written for product managers, reliability engineers, and solutions engineers who are responsible for onboarding customers to high-availability conversational workloads and validating fallback guarantees.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist to map customer SLAs to Redwood runtime policy and route configuration.
- Define fallback tiers, compatibility constraints, and fallback sequencing to minimize user-visible errors and cost spikes.
- Specify test cases, telemetry panels, and alert thresholds used to verify resilience before and after go-live.
- Assign ownership and rollback criteria for any canary or staged rollout that modifies fallback behavior.

When to use this playbook
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. A customer with conversational workloads requests SLA-backed resilience or dedicated capacity.
2. An internal team needs to modify fallback ordering, add a new variant, or tune eviction/evacuation settings.
3. Running a canary rollout of fallback policy changes across regions or tenant tiers.

Key concepts and components

- Redwood Runtime (service name: redwood-runtime): token-serving engine that performs KV cache management and batching.
- Route Router (service name: route-router): policy engine that selects target model variants and fallback chains.
- Fallback Orchestrator (service name: fallback-orchestrator): coordinates in-flight session transfers and state hydration across variants.
- KV Cache Coordinator: shared prefix cache used to accelerate warm sessions; eviction policy matters for resilience.
- Variant Compatibility Matrix: a customer-visible matrix describing which models are compatible as fallbacks (format provided below).

SLO and tier mapping (recommended defaults)

| Customer SLA Tier | Target p99 Latency | Availability SLO | Fallback aggressiveness | Cost tolerance |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Development / PoC | <= 500ms | 99% | Low (best-effort) | Low |
| Production (Standard) | <= 300ms | 99.9% | Medium (soft fallbacks) | Medium |
| Production (High) | <= 120ms | 99.95% | High (aggressive, multi-variant) | High |

Mapping notes: For High-tier customers we recommend reserved Dedicated capacity or pinned warm pools to reduce eviction-driven fallbacks.

Fallback sequencing and compatibility
sections.heading: Use this playbook when

sections.body:
1. Primary model variant (pinned to customer's tenant config)
2. Warm-variant (same architecture, lower precision quantization)
3. Regional-compatible variant (same coupling & tokenizer, possibly smaller context window)
4. Cost-tier fallback (smaller model with documented expected regressions)
5. Degraded response mode (short, deterministic response or transparent error)

Compatibility matrix example (deliverable to customer during onboarding):

| Primary Variant | Warm Variant | Regional Variant | Cost Fallback | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rdx-7b-16k-fp16 | rdx-7b-16k-q4 | rdx-7b-8k-fp16 | rdx-3b-8k-q4 | Warm retains KV cache; regional requires tokenization check |

Configuration checklist for onboarding (must complete before entitlement)

1. Service-level checks
   - Confirm tenant placement: hosted | dedicated | private.
   - Confirm model variants to register and pin order in the fallback chain.
   - Validate quota and burst capacity options are configured for the customer.
2. Runtime and network checks
   - Verify KV cache footprint for the tenant (recommended: reserve 1–2 GB per 100k active sessions).
   - Ensure cross-region replication is enabled if regional fallbacks are used.
   - Validate TLS/KMS integration for private deployments.
3. Observability and alerts
   - Create dashboards: Session Health (active sessions, warm hits, fallback rate), Latency P99/P50, Eviction rate.
   - Create alerts: fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5m (SEV3), p99 latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 10m (SEV2), warm-hit ratio < 60% for 15m (SEV2).
4. Contract and communications
   - Agree on documented degradations for tiered fallbacks and tie to billing credits.
   - Populate customer-facing compatibility matrix in the onboarding packet.

Operational validation tests (pre-go-live)

Perform the following tests in a staging environment that mirrors production traffic patterns:
- Warm-hit regression test: simulate warm workload and assert warm-hit ratio >= 80% within 30 minutes after ramp.
- Eviction stress test: ramp token churn to trigger eviction and assert fallback chain proceeds without session loss.
- Regional failover test: simulate region outage and validate fallback to regional-compatible variants with < 2% request failure.
- Fidelity check: run 500 sample prompts through each fallback variant and compute top-level quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE or domain-specific metric).

Test automation snippet (curl example)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/sessions/test-fallback -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt": "Test fallback behavior: echo session id", "session_id": "staging-validate-01", "simulate": "eviction_spike"}'

Expected responses: 200 with fallback headers X-Model-Variant and X-Fallback-Reason when a fallback occurred.

Monitoring and dashboards
sections.heading: Standard fallback chain (default policy)

sections.body:
- Session Health: active sessions, sessions created/min, sessions evicted/min.
- Warm Cache: warm-hit %, average KV latency, eviction queue length.
- Fallback Metrics: fallback_count, fallback_rate, fallback_path_distribution.
- Latency & Errors: p50/p95/p99 latencies, 5xx rate, client timeouts.

Alert thresholds (recommended)

- fallback_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> Pager to SRE oncall (SEV3)
- p99 latency > SLO * 1.3 for 10m -> SEV2 escalation to runtime team
- eviction_queue_length > 1000 for 5m -> SEV2 to infra and runtime
- sudden increase in cost per token > 50% vs baseline for 1h -> billing & product notify

Canary and rollout guidance

When changing fallback policies or adding new fallback variants, follow this phased rollout:
1. Internal canary: 0.5% of traffic routed to canary policy within non-customer-facing sandbox tenants for 24–48h.
2. Beta tenants: select 2–3 low-risk customers (with agreed rollback) for 48–72h.
3. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over a minimum of 7 days, with automated abort on metric regressions.
sections.heading: Minimum dashboard panels

sections.body:
- fallback_rate increases > 2x baseline and absolute > 1% for 10m.
- p99 latency regresses > 20% and absolute > SLO for 15m.
- end-to-end user error rate increases > 0.5% absolute for 30m.

Rollback procedure (owner: runtime oncall)

1. Pause rollout and remap affected routes to previous policy via route-router CLI:
   route-router promote --route <route-id> --policy previous-policy --reason "rollback due to fallback regression"
2. Trigger eviction stabilization: increase warm-pool retention by 2x for affected tenants for 30 minutes.
3. Open incident bridge and notify customer success/customer contact.
4. Post-rollback validation: run smoke tests and confirm warm-hit ratio and latency back to baseline.

Customer communication template (outbound)

Subject: Update: Resilience policy change and temporary rollback

Hi <CustomerName>,

We observed elevated fallback rates after the recent resilience policy change and have paused the rollout for your tenant. We reverted to the previous fallback configuration to ensure session continuity. Our team will investigate and follow up with a technical summary and next steps.

Ownership and escalation

- Product owner: Priya Shah (product) — responsible for policy decisions, customer communications, and contractual mapping.
- Runtime owner: Engine Runtime Team (engineering) — responsible for code changes and runtime knobs.
- SRE: Platform SRE on-call — responsible for alerts, incident coordination, and hotfix rollbacks.
- Customer Success: assigned CSM — responsible for customer notifications and SLA credit reconciliation.

Appendix A: Recommended default knobs and values

| Knob | Default value | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| warm_pool_retention | 45m | Balances memory cost with warm-hit likelihood |
| kv_cache_size_per_tenant | 2GB per 100k sessions | Empirical baseline from production telemetry |
| fallback_evaluation_window | 5s | Time to wait for model to respond before trying next fallback |
| fallback_backoff | exponential, start 100ms | Prevent cascading bursts to fallback variants |
| session_transfer_timeout | 10s | Timeout for orchestrated state hydration between variants |

Appendix B: Deliverables for customer onboarding packet

- Compatibility matrix (CSV) for chosen model variants
- Observability dashboard links and alert subscriptions
- Documented fallback degradations and expected UX impact per tier
- Test schedule and acceptance criteria checklist

Appendix C: Helpful links and internal references

- Runtime architecture: /eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/overview
- Route policy reference: /eng-platform/systems-and-services/route-router-spec
- Evacuation protocol: /eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/session-evacuation-and-eviction-protocol-spec-2026-03-30

Change history

- 2025-08-21: Initial authoring (Priya Shah).
- 2025-11-05: Added canary guidance and automated abort criteria (reviewers: Mei Wong).
- 2026-01-10: Updated knobs and alert thresholds after Q4 resiliency postmortem (Liam O'Connor).

End of document.

payload.page_title: Partner Technical & Commercial Onboarding Guide

sections.body:
Overview:

This document is a combined technical and commercial onboarding guide for platform partners (ISVs, channel partners, and system integrators). It codifies the minimal requirements, SLOs, integration steps, and commercial checkpoints required to move a partner from initial engagement to production launch on Redwood Inference. The goal is to standardize the experience so partners meet performance/compliance expectations while minimizing engineering hand-hold time.

Audience:
- Partner engineering managers and integration engineers
- Redwood partner managers and solutions engineers
- Sales and legal teams finalizing commercial terms

Goals:
- Deliver a repeatable 8-week onboarding path for non-enterprise partners and a configurable 12–16 week path for enterprise integrations.
- Ensure measurable performance: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for transactional routes in hosted mode (see SLOs).
- Validate commercial readiness: billing setup, SKU mapping, crediting and contract sign-off.

Scope and partner types:
- ISVs integrating Redwood API directly into a product (primary focus).
- Channel partners white-labeling Redwood-powered features.
- System integrators deploying Redwood Private for regulated customers.

Required preconditions (check before kickoff):
1) Signed NDA and partner intake form completed by partner manager.
2) Partner has a technical contact and schedule for weekly syncs.
3) Billing entity exists or a purchase order path is identified (finance).
4) For Private deployments: network reachability test and customer KMS details available.

Ownership matrix:
| Activity | Redwood owner | Partner owner | Escalation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Technical integration (API keys, test creds) | Partner Solutions (eng) | Partner engineering lead | Partner manager -> AM
| SLO validation & perf testing | Eng-Platform (Benchmarking) | Partner QA | SRE oncall
| Contract & billing | Finance & Sales Ops | Partner procurement | Legal
| Security review & data handling | Security & Compliance | Partner security lead | Security director

Key SLOs and thresholds (integration stage vs. post-launch):
- Integration stage (verification tests):
  - 95th percentile tail latency for test suite (end-to-end): <= 350ms
  - Error rate during synthetic load tests: < 0.5%
- Production SLOs (post-launch):
  - 95th percentile request latency: <= 250ms (transactional routes)
  - Uptime: 99.9% monthly for hosted integrations; Dedicated SLA will be contract-specific
  - Token cost variance: observed unit cost within +/-15% of projected estimate in the first 30 days

Onboarding flow (8–16 week template):
1) Kickoff (week 0) — kickoff deck, success criteria, communication channels.
2) Discovery (week 0–1) — traffic profile, peak QPS, typical sequence length, and privacy constraints.
3) Sandbox integration (week 1–3) — partner implements requests against Redwood sandbox API keys; sample test suite executed.
4) Performance validation (week 3–4) — run perf harness (see Commands) and adjust batching/kv caching settings.
5) Commercial finalize (week 4–5) — SKU mapping, billing method, early-consumption credit if applicable.
6) Security & compliance review (parallel, week 2–6) — SOC/pen test checklist and data residency confirmation.
7) Canary launch (week 5–8) — 1–5% traffic, monitor SLOs, escalate on regression.
8) Production rollout (week 8+) — phased traffic increase with rollback gates.

Technical integration checklist:
- API credentials: obtain partner sandbox key and production key.
- Model selection: confirm model variant(s) (e.g., redwood-rlhf-7b-q4f) and fallback variants.
- Batching strategy: sample batch_size and max_latency tradeoffs documented.
- KV/prefix cache: identify session prefixes for caching and TTLs.
- Observability: configure per-route telemetry in Console; enable traces and token-level cost snapshots.
- Webhooks & tooling: configure event webhooks for usage alerts and quota notifications.

Perf harness (commands):
- Synthetic runner (example):
  ./perf-runner --target https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/generate \n    --key REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY \n    --concurrency 50 --rps 300 --duration 300 --sequence-distribution profiles/short-medium.json

- Sample cURL for a streaming conversational route:
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}" -X POST \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the quarterly results."}],"stream":true}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions

Commercial and billing checklist:
- SKU mapping: map partner features to Redwood SKU(s). Typical mapping examples included in appendix.
- Discounting: determine early-adopter credits and overage rate tiers.
- Entitlements: confirm which routes are included in the base SKU vs. paid add-ons (e.g., dedicated warm capacity).
- Quota setup: set soft quotas for first 30 days with alerting at 70%/90%.

Security & compliance checkpoints:
- Data handling: confirm PII/no-PII policy and whether request/response logging is permitted for evals.
- Access control: RBAC role assignments for partner SREs (read-only by default).
- Audit logging: ensure audit logs forwarded to partner or partner-managed SIEM if required.
- Private deployment specifics: KMS integration test, HSM handshake, network peering checklist.

Canary and rollback gates (operational criteria):
- Canary metrics evaluated every 30 minutes for 24 hours: latency, error rate, token cost per minute.
- Automatic rollback triggers: sustained 95th percentile latency above SLO for 30 minutes, or error rate >1% for 15 minutes.
- Manual rollback: Partner requests immediate rollback via support channel; SRE executes session evacuation plan.

Go-live checklist (must be green):
- All integration tests passing in production keys.
- Billing entity active and invoice test completed.
- SLO dashboard created and subscribed for alerts.
- Security sign-off completed.
- Runbook created and shared with partner for first 72 hours post-launch.

Post-onboarding: metrics & cadence:
- Weekly health sync for first 4 weeks; then biweekly for 2 months; monthly thereafter until business metrics stabilize.
- Reported metrics: per-route latency, per-tenant token cost, quota burn rate, incidents and degradations.
- Quarterly business review: consumption vs. forecast and fidelity adjustments.

Templates and artifacts (links to internal templates):
- Kickoff deck template: confluence://templates/partner-kickoff-deck
- Integration test suite: git://infra/partner-integration-tests (see README)
- Billing SKU template: confluence://templates/partner-sku-mapping

Appendix A — Example SLA lines (sample text for inclusion in partner contract):
- Redwood will provide hosted inference availability of 99.9% measured monthly. Credits are applied when availability falls below the threshold: 5% credit for 99.0–99.9%, 15% for 98.0–99.0%.
- SLO for transactional 95th percentile latency: 250ms. Measured for endpoints designated as "transactional" in the onboarding form.

Appendix B — Example SKU mapping (sample):
| Feature | Redwood SKU | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Chat API (up to 4k tokens) | sku-chat-std | Base entitlement in Starter plan
| Chat API (up to 32k tokens) | sku-chat-large | Add-on for enterprise-grade sessions
| Dedicated warm capacity | sku-dedicated-warm-1 | Monthly reserved GPU pool

Appendix C — Troubleshooting quick commands:
- Dump active sessions for tenant:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" https://console.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/${TENANT_ID}/sessions\n
- Force-evacuate sessions for a canary rollback:
  ./evacuate-sessions --tenant ${TENANT_ID} --grace-period 30 --dry-run=false

Contact and escalation list:
- Partner Solutions (primary): solutions-partners@redwood.ai, on-call: +1-555-0123
- Benchmarking & Performance: perf-eng@redwood.ai
- Commercial & Billing: partner-billing@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: secops@redwood.ai

Revision history:
- 2026-11-05: Initial published (Aisha Patel)
- 2027-02-10: Clarified SLA credit bands and added canary rollback triggers (Marcus Nguyen)

End of document.

payload.page_title: Synthetic consumption scenarios playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook documents a standardized approach for generating, running, and interpreting synthetic consumption scenarios to evaluate SLA sensitivity, cost exposure, and fidelity degradation risk across Redwood’s deployment surfaces (hosted, dedicated, private). It complements the lab-driven experiments used by Research and the developer sandbox artifacts used by DX. The goal is to create reproducible scenario artifacts and a lightweight simulation harness that product, SRE, and sales engineers can use during onboarding, capacity planning, and pricing negotiations.

Scope and intended audiences

- Scope: scenarios that exercise per-token cost, tail-latency SLOs (P95/P99), KV cache hit-rate dynamics, and fallback behaviors for multi-variant routing. Includes synthetic traffic, session-based conversational traces, and embedding spike simulations.
- Audiences: product managers, solutions engineers, SREs, pricing analysts, and field sales engineers.

Why synthetic scenarios matter

1. Surface non-linear cost behaviors caused by batching, prefix reuse, and KV cache churn.
2. Validate fallback economics when primary variants are preempted or out of capacity.
3. Provide deterministic inputs for pricing simulations and contractual SLA sizing.

Core components of the playbook

1) Scenario Catalog (canonical set)

- conversational-burst: short interactive sessions with high-turn counts (10–50 turns) per session; 80% of sessions are under 2s target latency; median tokens per turn: 64; use-case: chat assistants.
- transactional-hf: high-frequency single-turn calls with small prompts and strict P95 <= 200ms; tokens per request: 8–32; use-case: realtime search rerank and LLM-assisted autocompletion.
- longform-stream: single long responses streamed in chunks; typical response length: 1024–4096 tokens; use-case: summarization and content generation.
- embedding-spike: sudden burst of batched embedding creation (10k–100k vectors) lasting 5–30 minutes; use-case: reindexing and bulk ingestion.
- mixed-fidelity: mixture of high-fidelity (e.g., large variant) and low-fidelity calls with weighted routing to test fallback economics.

Each scenario artifact includes: synthetic traffic generator configuration (load shape, percentiles), seed prompt sets (10–100 canonical prompts), and an acceptance checklist.

2) Metrics and SLO mappings

- Latency: P50, P95, P99, tail-latency spikes (5-min windows). SLO targets: transactional-hf P95 <= 200ms (hosted), conversational-burst P95 <= 500ms (dedicated SLA tier).
- Cost: tokens-per-minute / effective $/1M tokens at current SKU rates. Include delta when fallback to lower-cost variants occurs.
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity vs baseline prompts; pass/fail thresholds for quality gates (e.g., semantic-similarity >= 0.87).
- Cache: KV-cache hit rate, prefix reuse %, and eviction rate per 5-min window.
- Availability: percent successful responses and defined error budget consumption over scenario window.

3) Simulation methodology (step-by-step)

1. Select scenario artifact from the Catalog.
2. Pin model variants and runtime knobs (batch size, max tokens, quantization profile) in the config table below.
3. Run a dry-run at 5–10% scale to validate traffic generator and telemetry hooks.
4. Execute the full-scale run for a minimum of 60 minutes (recommended 3 hours for longer steady-state metrics).
5. Run a correlated quality evaluation on sampled outputs (sample size: 500 responses).
6. Produce the scenario report and SLA sensitivity matrix.

4) Recommended configuration table (canonical defaults)

| parameter | hosted default | dedicated default | rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| request_batch_size | 8 | 32 | Dedicated pools can group larger batches to increase throughput |
| quantization | int8 | int8 | Cost-forward default; evaluate quality gates post-run |
| kv_cache_enabled | true | true | Preserves session prefix reuse economics |
| prefetch_window_ms | 50 | 30 | Lower for dedicated to favor throughput |
| fallback_policy | variant-priority | variant-priority-with-regional-fallthrough | Provide more resilience for dedicated customers |
| telemetry_sample_rate | 1.0 | 1.0 | Full sampling for scenario runs; reduce for production |

5) Acceptance checklist for scenario artifacts

- [ ] Traffic generator validated with dry-run.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards defined and linked (latency, cost, cache, quality).
- [ ] Sampling seed and randomization seeds recorded in artifact.
- [ ] Reproducibility steps logged (config hash, runtime commit).
- [ ] Quality gate pass for sampled outputs.

6) SLA sensitivity matrix (examples)

- transactional-hf: increasing concurrency from 100 to 1000 at fixed per-request tokens increases P95 from 120ms to 410ms and increases cost by +18% due to smaller batch efficiency; recommend adjusting batch sizing or reserving warm capacity at concurrency > 600.
- conversational-burst: introducing 25% session churn (frequent session creation) drops KV hit rate from 78% to 42%, increasing median token cost by 12% and P99 by 90ms; mitigation: session locality routing and sticky cache anchors.

7) Common experiments and what they reveal

- Quantization toggles: toggling int8->float16 for select variants to quantify quality delta vs cost savings.
- Batch shape sensitivity: sweep batch sizes and request shapes to identify knee points in latency vs throughput.
- Fallback pressure test: simulate full-capacity of primary variant and enable regional fallthrough to measure failover latency and cross-variant quality impact.
- Cold-start warmup: measure latency and token overhead for model cold starts across dedicated pools after 15m idle.

8) Runbook: interpreting results and recommended actions

1. If P95 breaches target but cost remains low, tune batch sizing and prefetch_window_ms.
2. If cost spikes while latency is stable, inspect KV eviction rate and prefix churn—consider increasing cache TTL for long sessions.
3. If quality gates fail after quantization, rollback quantization profile for the affected variant and open a quality regression issue with Model Onboarding team.

9) Ownership and cadence

- Scenario artifacts: owner = Product Experiments (product-experiments@redwood.com).
- Lab runs and long-duration tests: owner = Applied ML & Evals.
- SRE checks and capacity recommendations: owner = eng-sre.

Quarterly cadence: catalog refresh and re-run of top 5 scenarios aligned with pricing reviews and major model variant changes.

10) Telemetry and dashboard recipes (examples)

- Dashboard: consumption-sim-ops (Grafana) – panels: P95 latency, P99 latency, token-rate, cost-rate, KV hit rate, error-rate.
- Query examples (PromQL-like pseudocode):
  - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - kv_hit_rate = rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])

11) Artifact template and CLI snippet

- artifact.yaml (minimal):
  name: conversational-burst-2027-03-run
  scenario: conversational-burst
  seed_prompts: ./seeds/conversational-burst/seed-100.jsonl
  traffic_shape: {rps: 120, burst_profile: exponential, duration_mins: 180}
  variants: [gptx-large-v1-quant, gptx-small-v1-quant]
  knobs: {batch_size: 16, kv_cache_enabled: true, telemetry_sample_rate: 1.0}

- Run (local harness):
  ./sim-harness run --artifact artifact.yaml --telemetry destination=grafana/consumption-sim-ops --commit $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

Appendix A — Example scenario report outline

- Executive summary (1 paragraph)
- Key findings (bulleted)
- SLA sensitivity matrix (table)
- Cost delta summary ($/1M tokens baseline vs observed)
- Quality sample notes and failing prompts
- Recommended mitigations and owners

Appendix B — Troubleshooting tips

- Partial telemetry: verify telemetry_sample_rate and OTEL exporter configuration.
- Non-reproducible noise: lock random seeds and verify artifact.yaml commit hash.
- Unexpected quality drift: compare outputs against golden baseline and open a Model Onboarding ticket with evidence.

Contact and next steps

For help running scenarios or onboarding scenario artifacts into the catalog, contact product-experiments@redwood.com. The catalog is reviewed quarterly—submit new scenario proposals as PRs to the canonical git repo (internal) with a triage note and a representative seed set.

payload.page_title: Onboard: SLO-first Packaging Playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook describes the SLO-first packaging model for onboarding new developer and mid-market customers to Redwood Inference. It provides a prescriptive set of packaging defaults, onboarding steps, telemetry and rollout guidance designed to reduce cost uncertainty while guaranteeing customer-facing latency/availability objectives. Use this when negotiating early SLAs, designing onboarding flows, or creating customer-specific packaging addenda.

Goals

- Make service-level objectives the primary axis for packaging and entitlements.
- Reduce cost uncertainty by exposing clear tradeoffs between SLO tiers and cost levers (batching, KV caching, quantization).
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist that product, solutions, and customer success can follow for 48–72 hour time-to-first-SLO (customer-visible).
- Ensure safe rollouts with telemetry, rollback triggers, and canary guardrails.

Audience

Product managers, solutions engineers, customer success, account executives negotiating Dedicated/Private contracts, and developer onboarding engineers.

Scope and non-goals
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Hosted and Dedicated onboarding paths.
- Default packaging configurations and SLO mappings.
- Onboarding runbook and telemetry requirements.
- Pricing buckets tied to SLOs and predictable capacity commits.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- Detailed legal contract language (finance/legal will publish templates).
- Deep runtime kernel tuning steps (see eng-serving-runtime docs).

SLO-first packaging model overview

We define three canonical SLO tiers customers can select during onboarding. Each tier maps to a set of default runtime and packaging configurations, and a cost multiplier relative to baseline usage pricing. Teams can override defaults for enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments.

Table: Canonical SLO tiers

| Tier name | Availability SLO | P95 latency target (text gen) | Default runtime profile | Typical customer size | Notes |
|-----------|------------------:|-----------------------------:|------------------------|---------------------|------:|
| Bronze    | 99.5%             | 800 ms                      | shared-hosted, opportunistic batching | small dev teams, PoC | cost-first, longer coldstart windows |
| Silver    | 99.9%             | 350 ms                      | hosted with prefix-KV cache, medium batching | early production apps | balanced cost/latency |
| Gold      | 99.99%            | 120 ms                      | Dedicated warm capacity, reserved KV, strict batching caps | mission-critical, scale | SLA-backed availability and latency |

Defaults and packaging primitives

Each tier exposes configurable primitives that materially impact unit economics. Default values for each tier are documented in the table below. These defaults are opinionated; use engineering review for bespoke allocations.

Table: Default primitives by tier

| Primitive | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
|-----------|--------|--------|------|
| Max batch size | 64 | 32 | 16 |
| Prefix KV cache TTL | 10m | 60m | 6h |
| Quantization profile | fp16 | int8-mixed | int8+llm-quant |
| Warm capacity percent | 0% | 30% | 80% |
| Reserved concurrency | burst | 200 r/s | 2k r/s |

Pricing model and packaging SKUs

High-level pricing approach: map expected steady-state consumption to an SLO SKU. Each SKU consists of: base monthly fee (for dedicated/warm guarantees), per-token variable price, and an SLO credit that limits behavior under overload. Example SKU (Silver):

- base_fee_monthly: $1,200 (stringified in contract)
- per_token_rate: $0.0006 per token
- on_slo_mitigation: traffic reprioritization + adaptive batching

Note: Concrete USD values are negotiation starting points — product/pricing must sign off on any discounting above 15%. Finance owns final published SKUs.

Developer onboarding checklist (48–72 hour target)

1. Initial scoping call (owner: solutions engineering).
   - Confirm target SLO tier, expected peak qps, concurrency pattern, and security requirements.
   - Capture model family and sequence length distribution.
2. Provisioning (owner: infra ops/product).
   - For Hosted: allocate namespace, default runtime profile per chosen tier.
   - For Dedicated: reserve GPU pool and warm capacity; create tenant routing policy; configure KMS if requested.
3. Baseline traffic replay and smoke tests (owner: onboarding eng).
   - Run synthetic traffic generator with representative prompts (use playbook prompts-store).
   - Verify p95 latency and error budget burn over 1–4 hours.
4. Telemetry and tracing hooks (owner: observability/product).
   - Ensure tenant export of token-level telemetry, p95/p99 latency metrics, and request traces to customer's telemetry workspace (if configured).
5. Cost forecast and packaging sign-off (owner: solutions/product).
   - Use the cost simulator (CLI example below) to estimate 30/60/90 day spend given projected traffic.
6. Go-live and canary (owner: SRE/onboarding eng).
   - Canary 5% traffic for 2 hours with active rollback monitors.

Example: cost simulator CLI snippet
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body: redwood-cost-sim --tokens 10000000 --tier silver --sequence-avg 128 --output report.json
sections.heading: CLI: simulate cost for 10M tokens/month at Silver defaults

sections.body:
{"scenario":"silver-default-10m","monthly_cost_usd":"7200","base_fee":"1200","variable":"6000"}

Telemetry, observability and rollback triggers

Required telemetry exports for onboarding must be configured before removing canary protection. At minimum:

- token_count (per request), request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), request_error_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, warm_capacity_utilization.
- SLO burn rate alert: when error budget consumption > 10% per 10-minute window for > 2 windows, trigger automated rollback to previous runtime profile.
- Cost-exposure alert: projected monthly cost increase > 15% vs signed forecast for sustained 60 minutes.

Table: Alert thresholds (recommended)

| Alert | Threshold | Action owner | Automated action |
|-------|----------:|--------------|------------------|
| P95 latency > target + 20% | sustained 5m | SRE | throttle and scale-up signal |
| Error rate > 0.5% | sustained 10m | Oncall | fallback to lower fidelity variant |
| KV hit rate < 10% | 30m window | Runtime eng | suggest cache-warm job |
| Cost drift > 15% projection | 60m | Customer success | send usage hold and flag to AE |

Rollout phases and gating

Phase 0 — Discovery: collect traffic patterns, negotiate tier.
Phase 1 — Provisioned canary: 5% traffic routed for 2–4 hours, full telemetry.
Phase 2 — Gradual ramp: 20% for 12 hours, then 100% if stable.
Phase 3 — Harden + review: 72-hour post-go-live review with performance and cost readouts.
sections.heading: Output (example JSON)

sections.body:
- P95 and error budget within 125% of target for duration of canary.
- No more than 5% cost overshoot vs forecast during canary.

Engineering contacts and ownership

- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product) — overall playbook steward.
- Solutions eng lead: Diego Martinez — onboarding scoping and customer templates.
- Runtime liaison: Elliot Ng (eng-serving-runtime) — implementation of tiered defaults and rollback hooks.
- Observability: Priya Raman (eng-platform) — telemetry export onboarding.

API example: SLO binding request (HTTP JSON)

POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/slo-binding
Content-Type: application/json
sections.heading: Gates before moving from Phase 1 to Phase 2

sections.body:
{"slo_tier":"silver","target_p95_ms":"350","max_monthly_tokens":"20000000","preferred_runtime_profile":"silver-default-2026-11"}

Operational notes and known tradeoffs

- Stronger SLOs (Gold) typically increase unit cost by 2–4x for the same token volume due to warm capacity and reduced batching. Communicate this clearly during pricing conversations.
- For customer workloads dominated by long sequences (avg sequence > 1024 tokens), Gold may require model variant pinning or quantization profile adjustments.
- On Dedicated, reserved KV cache TTLs should be conservatively lowered before any mass migration to avoid cache stampedes.

Open decisions

- Whether to expose an automated SLO-negotiation UI in Console that maps observed workload to a recommended tier (product to decide by 2027-01-15).
- How to standardize discounting policy tied to multi-year Dedicated commitments (finance/product ongoing).

KPIs and success metrics

- Time to first customer-visible SLO (target <= 72 hours).
- Fraction of onboards that hit forecasted cost within ±15% at 30 days (target >= 80%).
- Post-onboard SLO compliance at 90 days (fraction of customers meeting their tier's SLOs, target >= 95%).

Related docs

- /confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-to-private-migration-performance-playbook-prd-2026-05-17.json
- /confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/migration-pricing-pathways-hosted-to-dedicated-2027-11.json
- /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tenant-onboarding-telemetry-template.json

FAQ

Q: Can a customer change tiers mid-cycle?
A: Yes. Tier changes are permitted at the start of the next billing cycle unless otherwise negotiated. Mid-cycle emergency downgrades may be applied with prorated credits.

Q: What happens if SLOs are violated due to third-party model regressions?
A: We route to fallback variants and open an incident. The SLO review will distinguish between platform and model-level causes; customer credits follow the contractual SLA process.

Appendix: minimal JSON contract snippet for SKU assignment

{"sku_id":"silver-onboard-2026-1","tier":"silver","base_fee_monthly":"1200","per_token_usd":"0.0006","slo_p95_ms":"350"}

If you have questions about tailoring this playbook for a customer, contact the product owner or add to the playbook issues tracker (link: /confluence/product-docs/roadmap-and-themes/playbook-issues).

payload.page_title: Model Bridge Marketplace: Warm-Capacity Subscriptions — Product Brief & PRD

sections.body:
Summary:

This document defines the product brief, high-level PRD, design constraints, pricing constructs, and launch plan for the Model Bridge Marketplace Warm-Capacity Subscriptions. The feature introduces a marketplace of third-party and Redwood-verified model variants where customers can purchase warm-reserved execution capacity in subscription bands that attach to model SKUs. The goal is to provide lower cold-start latency, predictable cost for heavy callers, and a commercial path to monetize curated variants with managed warm capacity.

Background and Problem Statement:

- Customers using model variants (open or partner models) encounter two friction points: variable cold-start latency for spiky traffic and opaque unit economics across variant and capacity choices.
- Enterprise customers have expressed willingness to pay for predictable latency and throughput guarantees for specific model variants used in core product flows.
- There is no single product that combines a marketplace (variant discovery + licensing) with an attached, metered warm-capacity subscription offering and a clear UX for developer selection and routing.

Value Proposition:

- For Developers: simple discovery and one-click attach of warm-capacity plans to a model variant with client SDK flags and telemetry hooks for preflight checks.
- For Platform/Operators: improved capacity predictability and autoscaling smoothing via long-lived reservations; better ability to schedule heavy-tail workloads onto dedicated pools.
- For Redwood: new recurring revenue from subscription bands, increased adoption of curated variants, and reduced tail latency incidents.

Goals and Non-Goals (success criteria):

Goals:
1. Deliver warm-capacity attach UX and billing for model variants (MVP) within Q4 2026.
2. Achieve 50% reduction in cold-start tail (95th percentile) for customers using subscriptions vs baseline.
3. Secure at least 5 pilot customers on paid plans within 90 days post-launch.

Non-Goals:
- This PRD does not include a full decentralized billing marketplace or revenue split automation for third parties in MVP (commercial reconciliation will be manual).
- It does not replace Dedicated reserved GPU contracts. Warm capacity is a software reservation layer on top of Hosted pools.

User Personas and Journeys:

- Small SaaS Engineer (Self-serve): discovers a high-performance summarization variant in the marketplace, attaches a Bronze warm band, toggles preflight checks in SDK, and validates latency improvements in Console.
- Platform SRE: maps warm subscriptions to a predictable capacity class; uses Console dashboards to see warm utilization and make scheduling changes.
- Revenue Ops: validates invoices and reconciles marketplace partner payouts (manual for MVP).

PRD — Requirements (MUST/HIGH/MED/LOW):

MUST:
- Marketplace listing model variant metadata: name, version, memory footprint, token throughput estimate, certified latency profile (cold and warm), and vendor attribution.
- Subscription SKU model: tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with defined reserved concurrency, soft headroom, and expected 95p tail latency improvement.
- Attach API: endpoint to attach/detach a subscription to a tenant+route (REST + SDK). Example payload:

POST /v1/marketplace/attach
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_123",
  "route_id": "payments-summarize",
  "variant_sku": "open-summarizer-v2-gold",
  "subscription_sku": "warm-gold-100"
}

- Routing policy: requests matching a route with an attached warm subscription must preferentially route to warm pools; on exhaustion, fallback to recommended compatible variants with documented SLA degradation.
- Billing integration: capture subscription SKU, start/end timestamps, and pro-rated charges for partial periods into the billing ledger.

HIGH:
- Console UI: discovery catalog, attach flow, warm-capacity utilization graph (per-tenant, per-variant).
- Telemetry: preflight latency probe and gateway metrics that tag requests as Warm vs Cold.
- Alerts: when warm subscription utilization exceeds 85% for >15m.

MED:
- Automated partner revenue split UI for future integration (data model only in MVP).
- SDK helper that toggles warm-only routing for test mode.

LOW:
- Allow customers to self-serve nominee partner payouts and reconciliations.

Design Spec — Architecture Overview:

Key components (MVP):
- Marketplace Catalog Service (catalogsvc): stores variant metadata, SKU definitions, pricing. Exposes read APIs for Console and SDK.
- Subscription Manager (submgr): authoritative ledger of tenant subscriptions, entitlements, and soft-headroom config. Integrates with Billing Service for charges.
- Warm Pool Orchestrator (wpo): maps subscriptions to warm pool capacity classes and ensures pool reservation via scheduling hints.
- Routing Gate (router): runtime decision point that prefers warm pools when entitlement exists and enforces fallback policies.
- Console UX and SDK feature flags.

Data Contracts and Example JSONs:

Variant metadata example:
{
  "variant_sku": "open-summarizer-v2-gold",
  "model_name": "open-summarizer-v2",
  "memory_gb": "24",
  "throughput_tps": "18",
  "certified_warm_95p_latency_ms": "120",
  "certified_cold_95p_latency_ms": "800",
  "vendor": "OpenCommunity",
  "compatible_hardware": ["A100-40GB","H100-80GB"]
}

Subscription SKU table (text table):
| SKU | Reserved concurrency | Soft headroom | Target 95p warm latency | Monthly list price (USD) |
|-----|----------------------|---------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|
| warm-bronze-10 | 10 | +2 | 250ms | $1,200 |
| warm-silver-50 | 50 | +5 | 160ms | $5,000 |
| warm-gold-100 | 100 | +12 | 120ms | $9,000 |

SLOs and metrics to track (MVP):
- Warm 95p latency per variant and per tenant — target per SKU declared in catalog.
- Warm subscription utilization: % of reserved concurrency utilized over sliding 5m and 1h windows.
- Warm fallback rate: fraction of requests that fell back to non-warm due to exhaustion. Target: <5% for normal operation.

Operational Runbook Excerpts (On-call SRE):

1) Symptom: Console shows warm-subscription utilization >95% for >30m and multiple tenants report increased cold starts.
   - Step 1: Identify impacted warm pool and check "wpo" scheduling backlog. CLI: curl -s https://internal-api/wpo/pools?pool_id=<pool>
   - Step 2: Temporarily increase soft headroom for affected subscriptions (submgr API) and notify customers.
   - Step 3: If scheduling backlog persists >1h, trigger capacity bump playbook (see Runbooks/terraform-and-iac).

2) Symptom: Billing records missing subscription start events.
   - Step 1: Check submgr write-ahead log for recent failed transactions.
   - Step 2: Reconcile with Console attach audit events and create manual invoice if necessary. Owner: Revenue Ops.

Security and Compliance Considerations:

- Marketplace listings must include allowed-data-usage flags and required contract attachments for partner-owned variants. Any variant flagged "restricted" must not be discoverable by public tenant catalogs.
- Audit logs for attach/detach operations must be retained for 13 months (complies with existing retention policy).

Roadmap & Milestones (high-level):

1) Q4 2026 (MVP): Catalog read/write, subscription attach API, routing preference to warm pools, billing capture (manual reconciliation), Console attach flow (beta). Pilot with up to 5 customers.
2) Q1 2027: Partner revenue split automation, Console warm utilization dashboards, SDK helpers, partner onboarding guide.
3) Q2 2027: Dynamic price bands, auto-scale warm-headroom based on seasonality signals, per-route fidelity negotiation with warm-aware fallback.

Pricing and Packaging:

Pricing principles:
- Simple predictable bands that map to developer mental models (Bronze/Silver/Gold).
- List price includes a committed monthly fee for reserved concurrency; overage pricing is per-request at a discounted hosted token rate.
- Enterprise customers can negotiate dedicated bundles and private warm allocations (out-of-scope for MVP billing automation).

Example pricing scenarios (text table):
| Customer | Variant | Reserved | Monthly | Expected unit cost improvement |
| Acme Inc | open-summarizer-v2 | 50 (silver) | $5,000 | ~30% lower per-token latency cost at 95p |
| RetailCo | vendor-qa-v1 | 10 (bronze) | $1,200 | improved UX for checkout summaries |

Commercial notes for Sales and Revenue Ops:
- Pilot pricing will include a 3-month discounted rate at 50% list for early adopters.
- Revenue Ops will manually reconcile partner payouts in MVP; contracts must be attached before listing is published.

Launch Checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Catalog CRUD endpoints implemented and documented.
- [ ] Subscription attach/detach API + SDK wrappers.
- [ ] Router changes deployed behind feature flag.
- [ ] Billing ledger capture and invoice test harness.
- [ ] Console attach flow + warm-utilization widget (beta).
- [ ] Pilot onboarding doc and partner contract template.
- [ ] Runbook added to eng-platform/runbooks.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Feature flag gated end-to-end flows exist and are exercised by automated e2e tests covering attach->route->billing paths.
- Pilot tenants report a measurable 95p latency improvement vs baseline for at least 3 variant SKUs.
- Billing records appear in ledger for each attach action within 5 minutes.

Release Notes (Draft for internal release):

Model Bridge Marketplace — Warm-Capacity Subscriptions (Internal Beta) — 2026-11-01
- Introduces marketplace catalog and subscription SKU model with attach API.
- Adds routing preference for warm subscriptions and console attach UX (beta).
- Billing ledger capture enabled for subscription SKUs (manual reconciliation).
- Known limitations: partner payouts are manual; autoscaling warm-headroom not yet implemented.

Open Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Warm pool overcommit leading to higher-than-expected fallbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults on soft headroom and 85% utilization alerting.
- Risk: Confusion between Dedicated and Warm subscriptions. Mitigation: Console UX education, rename terms internally in docs.

Ownership and Contacts:
- Product Owner: Elena Rodriguez (product)
- Engineering Lead: Marcus Lee (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE Contact: Priya Nair (eng-sre)
- Revenue Ops: Jonah Kim (finance-legal)

Appendix — Example CLI snippets and SDK flags:

Attach via CLI (example):
redwood marketplace attach \
  --tenant acct_123 \
  --route payments-summarize \
  --variant open-summarizer-v2-gold \
  --sku warm-silver-50

SDK preflight example (python):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="x")
client.marketplace.attach_preflight(route="payments-summarize", variant="open-summarizer-v2-gold")

Document links and further reading:
- See Console mockups in the design repository and Pilot onboarding checklist in /product-docs/roadmap-and-themes.

This product brief is intended to be the single source of truth for the Model Bridge warm-capacity pilot. Revisions will be tracked and reviewers listed above will sign off before GA.

payload.page_title: Hosted-to-Private Migration Assistant — Release Notes v1.0

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document records the v1.0 release of the Hosted-to-Private Migration Assistant (Migration Assistant). The Migration Assistant is a product-side, self-service tool that automates and guides migration of customer workloads from Redwood hosted inference to a Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem bundle). This release targets enterprise customers with predictable traffic patterns and a first-class path for security review and compliance.

Key highlights (v1.0)
--------------------
- Dry-run simulation engine that predicts cost and latency changes for a representative workload.
- Traffic replay service for staged validation using customer-provided traces (anonymized).
- Configuration translator: converts hosted inference route configs into Private manifest drafts (YAML).
- Rollout orchestration with canary, gradual ramp, and automated fallback to hosted endpoints.
- CLI and web console flows with built-in preflight checks and an audit-ready migration log.
- Integrations: KMS key registration guide, private network validation checks, and IAM role templates.

Why this matters
-----------------
Customers frequently request a low-risk, observable way to move to Private deployments for compliance or data residency reasons. Previously migrations required significant manual work across networking, model pinning, cost-model validation, and on-prem packaging. The Migration Assistant reduces friction by codifying best-practice migration steps and automating error-prone conversions.

Audience and scope
-------------------
- Primary audience: Customer Platform Engineers and SREs working with Redwood enterprise accounts.
- Secondary audience: Solutions Engineers and Account Leads supporting migrations.
- Scope: Inference routes serving token-based text generation, chat, and embedding endpoints. Does not bundle on-prem hardware provisioning (that remains a separate engagement).

Compatibility and prerequisites
-------------------------------
- Supported models: Redwood-verified open models and customer-provided containerized models where the same model artifacts are available to the private runtime.
- Minimum Redwood Console version: 2028-05-01.
- Required customer inputs: sample traffic (1M tokens or representative subset), route config JSON, target network CIDR, KMS metadata.
- Network prerequisites: VPN or Direct Connect configured; egress rules validated for model and telemetry endpoints.

SLOs and success criteria for migrations
----------------------------------------
- Validation pass rate >= 95% for preflight checks.
- Simulation drift: predicted latency within +/- 15% of observed on first canary.
- Rollout success: >= 99% of requests served from Private after ramp, or automatic fallback completes within configured timeout.

What’s included in this release
-------------------------------
1) CLI: redwood-migrate v1.0
   - Commands: init, simulate, translate, dry-run, canary, promote, rollback
   - Example: redwood-migrate simulate --route-id r-1234 --trace-file sample-trace.json --output report.json
2) Console workflows
   - Migration workspace with step-by-step wizard and visual diff of translated config
3) APIs
   - POST /migrations (create)
   - GET /migrations/{id}/status
   - POST /migrations/{id}/actions (canary, promote, rollback)
4) Artifacts
   - Generated migration manifest (YAML) and an accompanying audit bundle (ZIP) that contains simulation reports, CLI outputs, and preflight logs.

Preflight checks (run automatically)
----------------------------------
1. Model compatibility: runtime-level compatibility check for model ops and quantization profile.
2. KV and prefix cache expectations: validates whether cache warmup is needed and estimates warmup tokens.
3. Network connectivity: port and routing checks against supplied CIDRs.
4. Secret bindings: KMS availability and role binding tests.
5. Consumption policy mapping: maps hosted quotas and token bundles to Private capacity estimates.

Migration manifest example (YAML excerpt)
----------------------------------------
```yaml
migration:
  route_id: r-1234
  target: private-vpc-az1
  model_pin: open-7b-quant-v2
  traffic_split:
    - canary: 5%
    - ramp: [5, 25, 50, 100]
  preflight_checks: [model_compatibility, network_connectivity, kms_bindings]
  rollback_policy:
    on_error: fallback-hosted
    timeout_minutes: 20
```

Runbook: recommended migration flow
-----------------------------------
1. Kickoff and scoping (Solutions Eng + Customer)
   - Confirm objectives, rollback SLA, and audit requirements.
2. Prepare inputs
   - Customer supplies route config, sample trace, and network/KMS metadata.
3. Simulate (local + cloud)
   - Run redwood-migrate simulate and review the generated cost/latency report.
4. Translate and review manifest
   - Use the console diff to validate translated resources and secret mappings.
5. Dry-run (no traffic)
   - Deploy artifacts to private test environment and run internal smoke checks.
6. Canary (live)
   - Start with configured canary percent; measure telemetry for 2x SLO window.
7. Promote or rollback
   - Promote after stability checks pass; otherwise trigger automated rollback.
8. Post-migration audit
   - Generate the migration bundle and upload to customer compliance repo.

Operational commands and examples
--------------------------------
- Start a canary: redwood-migrate canary --migration-id m-20280612-01 --percent 5
- Promote: redwood-migrate promote --migration-id m-20280612-01
- Force rollback: redwood-migrate rollback --migration-id m-20280612-01 --reason "latency spike"

Known issues and limitations (v1.0)
----------------------------------
- Edge case: models using custom CUDA kernels that are not present in the Private runtime will fail model_compatibility check. Manual kernel packaging is required.
- Trace fidelity: highly bursty production traces require sampling; simulation accuracy degrades for highly tail-heavy workloads.
- RBAC: migration actions require admin-level role in both hosted account and private control plane. Documented workarounds exist in the operations guide.

Security and compliance notes
-----------------------------
- All uploaded traces are anonymized client-side by the CLI before upload (PII redaction defaults enabled).
- Migration audit bundles are signed with Redwood KMS and retained for 365 days by default; retention settings configurable per customer.
- KMS integration requires the customer to provide a key ARN (AWS) or equivalent metadata for on-prem HSM registration.

Telemetry and observability
--------------------------
The Migration Assistant emits the following telemetry namespaces: migration.events, migration.simulation, migration.rollout. Default retention for migration traces is 90 days. Built-in dashboards: Migration Overview, Canary Health, Simulation vs. Observed Delta.

Rollout and deprecation plan
----------------------------
- v1.0 rollout: gradual launch to enterprise beta cohort (June 2028), followed by general availability (GA) on 2028-07-15.
- Deprecations: none planned for v1.x. Breaking changes will follow a 60-day deprecation notice.

Support and escalation path
---------------------------
- First line: Solutions Engineering (SE) assigned to the account.
- Second line: Private Deployments Engineering oncall (eng-private-deployments).
- Escalation: open a ticket with priority P0 when rollback fails to complete within configured timeout. Include migration-id and audit bundle.

Appendix: sample simulation report excerpt
-----------------------------------------
{
  "route_id": "r-1234",
  "simulated_qps": "120",
  "predicted_95_latency_ms": "230",
  "predicted_cost_delta_pct": "-18%"
}

Contact and ownership
---------------------
Product owner: Aisha Kumar (product)
Engineering owner: Marco Ruiz (eng-private-deployments)
Migration Assistant CLI maintainer: Ling Zhao (eng-infra)

Related documentation
---------------------
- Private deployment onboarding checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deployments-onboarding-checklist
- Hosted-to-dedicated transition playbook: /confluence/product-docs/product-overview/hosted-to-dedicated-transition-playbook-2026-06-30

Change log (high level)
-----------------------
- 2028-06-10: v1.0 internal candidate build completed.
- 2028-06-12: v1.0 published (GA cohort schedule published to TechOps).

If you need a hands-on migration run, contact the Migration Specialist team via the Console support channel and reference the migration-id from your workspace.

payload.page_title: Fidelity & Cost Telemetry Advisor: Launch Brief and Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This brief defines the product scope, acceptance criteria, launch steps, and go-to-market signals for the Fidelity & Cost Telemetry Advisor (FCTA) — a lightweight advisor service surfaced in Console and via API that recommends fidelity (model variant, quantization, batching) and pricing/packaging guidance based on live telemetry and customer goals. The target release is a controlled launch to pilot customers with a wider availability in Q3 2026.

Background and problem statement:
- Customers struggle to tune fidelity vs. cost tradeoffs for production inference. Current approaches are manual (trial-and-error) or require deep engineering investment.
- Platform telemetry contains rich signals (latency distributions, token-per-request distributions, KV cache hit rates, warm-start ratios, error rates) that can be turned into actionable fidelity recommendations.

Goals and non-goals:
1. Goals:
   - Surface per-route fidelity recommendations that reduce per-token cost by 10–30% while keeping customer-defined quality constraints (BLEU/ROUGE/QA delta) within tolerance.
   - Provide clear, actionable rollout steps (canary traffic split, metric watchers, rollback triggers).
   - Integrate with pricing engine to estimate monthly $ savings and recommended packaging options (microbundle, warm-capacity suggestion).
2. Non-goals:
   - This release will not provide automated model-level retraining nor automated quantization of customer models.
   - The advisor will not automatically change production traffic (manual approval required).

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Pilot adoption: 6 pilot customers onboarded within 8 weeks.
- Cost impact: mean recommended cost delta of -18% (median).
- Safety: <2% of recommendations that trigger a critical quality regression in monitored prompt sets during pilot.
- UX: >70% of pilot users follow the advisor rollout playbook for at least one route.

High-level user experience:
- Console: Route details -> "Fidelity Advisor" tab shows current telemetry snapshot, recommendation card with expected cost delta, quality risk score, and one-click exportable rollout checklist.
- API: POST /v1/advisor/evaluate with route_id and target_goal -> returns a list of discrete recommendation objects (variant, quant profile, batch_size, cache_policy) plus estimated monthly delta.

Functional requirements (priority ordered):
1) Telemetry ingestion and enrichment (MUST)
   - Ingest the following signals at 1m granularity: p50/p95 latency, tokens/request histogram, kv-cache-hit-rate, warm-start-rate, concurrency, error-rate by status code.
   - Augment with model profile: architecture family, seq-length-distribution, quantization-capable-flag.
2) Recommendation engine (MUST)
   - Rule-based baseline engine that encodes guardrails (latency SLO, quality shield thresholds).
   - Scoring model component (LOWER PRIORITY) that ranks options by cost/quality pareto front.
3) Console surface (MUST)
   - Recommendation card, confidence band, expected cost delta, manual rollout checklist export (markdown/JSON).
4) Pricing integration (MUST)
   - Call pricing service to simulate monthly billing under recommended config and present delta and suggested packaging options.
5) Rollout playbook (MUST)
   - Provide numbered rollout steps with explicit SLO checks and rollback criteria.
6) Audit & approval (MUST)
   - Store recommendations and owner approvals in the audit log (immutable for 90 days).
7) Safety testing harness (SHOULD)
   - Run recommended config against a sampled prompt set (tenant-mapped) in a sandbox and compute quality deltas before approval.
8) Multi-tenant isolation (MUST)
   - Ensure no cross-tenant telemetry mixing; customer data stays scoped to tenant.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency of generating a recommendation: < 2s for common routes, < 10s for heavy analytic routes.
- Storage: telemetry retention 90 days in hot store, 13 months in cold store.
- Availability: 99.9% for advisor API during business hours, 99.5% globally.
- Security/compliance: support KMS-encrypted tenant ids and RBAC for action approvals.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Start with deterministic rules (quantize when token-lengths < 1024 and latency headroom > 20ms) to reduce initial ML model complexity and increase explainability.
- Use conservative default confidence bands: only recommend aggressive quant or variant demotion when sandbox pass-rate > 95%.
- Cost simulations will be approximate at launch (rounded to the nearest dollar for the customer view) and will include a margin of safety (+5%) in the presented savings.

Example recommendation (JSON snippet):
```
POST /v1/advisor/evaluate
{
  "route_id": "tenant-1234/route-payments",
  "target_goal": "cost-minimize",
  "constraints": { "max_quality_delta": 0.02, "latency_p95_target_ms": 250 }
}

RESPONSE 200
[
  {
    "recommendation_id": "rec-20260530-01",
    "variant": "redwood-compat-7b-quant8",
    "batch_size": 8,
    "kv_cache_policy": "prefix-cache:enabled",
    "expected_monthly_delta_usd": "-1200",
    "confidence": "high",
    "sandbox_pass_rate": "98%"
  }
]
```

Rollout checklist (exportable):
1. Create canary route with 5% traffic -> owner: eng-platform oncall
2. Monitor p50/p95 latency and quality monitors for 48 hours (triggers: latency_p95 > baseline + 20%, quality_regression > 1%) -> owner: route-owners
3. If safe, increase to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if no triggers.
4. Post-rollout: schedule 7-day cost and quality review and update alert thresholds.

Packaging & pricing guidance (customer-facing options):
- Microbundle suggestion: If expected monthly savings > $1000, recommend microbundle upgrade for reduced per-token price.
- Warm capacity suggestion: If recommendations increase peak concurrency stability and customer has frequent traffic spikes, recommend a warm-capacity subscription estimate with monthly delta.

Pricing estimator table (display formatting shown as plain text):
| Scenario | Current monthly $ | Recommended monthly $ | Estimated savings | Suggested package |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Low-volume sandbox | 1,200 | 950 | 250 | none |
| Mid SaaS app | 6,400 | 5,120 | 1,280 | microbundle-standard |
| High-throughput | 35,000 | 28,000 | 7,000 | warm-capacity-committed |

Release plan and timeline (high level):
- Week 0–4: Build telemetry adapters, rule engine prototype, console UX mockups. Owned by: eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, product UX.
- Week 5–8: Integrate pricing simulator, audit logging, and sandbox harness. Security review and RBAC scoping.
- Week 9: Onboard 3 internal beta tenants.
- Week 10–14: Pilot with 6 external customers. Collect feedback, measure KPIs.
- Week 15: Wider availability gating decision. Launch comms and pricing page updates.

Owner & runbook responsibilities:
- Product (Maya Patel) — overall program owner and PM for pilot coordination.
- Eng-serving-runtime — telemetry adapter and low-latency recommendation endpoint.
- Eng-platform — Console tab and rollout automation hooks.
- Eng-infra/security — KMS, RBAC, audit-log storage.
- Customer Success — pilot recruiting and onboarding playbook.

Operational runbook (short):
1. If advisor API error-rate > 2% for 10m, escalate to eng-serving-runtime oncall and switch advisor UI to "temporarily unavailable" mode.
2. If cost estimator deviates from billing by >10% for 3 customers, open an incident and pause billing-linked recommendations until corrected.
3. For quality regression incidents traced to advisor recommendations, roll back route configuration and flag the recommendation as failed. Notify product and research.

Dependencies and open questions:
- Pricing service endpoints and SLA for simulation calls (work with finance).
- Tenant-specific prompt sets for sandbox safety tests (agreement from customers required).
- Definitive success thresholds for quality metrics across verticals (PLG SaaS vs. regulated enterprise).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-aggressive recommendations causing quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative confidence bands, mandatory sandbox pass and manual approval.
- Risk: Billing mismatch leading to customer distrust. Mitigation: use conservative rounding and a disclaimer; prioritize reconciliations and telemetry alignment.

Appendix — Minimal acceptance checklist (for launch):
- Telemetry signals available for pilot tenants (yes/no)
- Pricing simulator integrated and vetted by finance (yes/no)
- Console UX validated in user tests (3 participants) (yes/no)
- Audit log writes verified for 90-day retention (yes/no)
- RBAC and approval flow reviewed by security (yes/no)

Related artifacts and links:
- Design spec: /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/prescriptive-fidelity-advisor-design-2026-08-24
- PRD: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-fidelity-decision-service-and-sdk-2028-04-11
- Pricing integration spec: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/pricing-simulator-api-spec-2026-04-12

Contact: Maya Patel (product) — for questions, pilot enrollment, or clarifications.
