payload.page_title: Tiered Evaluation Orchestration and Label-Refresh Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines a tiered evaluation orchestration pattern and an automated label-refresh loop for long-tail prompt coverage, focused on mixed-mode deployments (hosted, dedicated, private). It prescribes how to prioritize evaluation resources, run quantization-aware regressions, and triage failures back into an automated labeling and resampling pipeline. The intent is to keep production quality stable while minimizing eval cost and human labeling overhead.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Production workloads are long-tailed: a small fraction of prompts account for most customer pain.
- Evaluations must balance fidelity (expensive, exact reproductions) with throughput (cheap, wide coverage).
- Quantization and model forks (e.g., quantized variants) introduce subtle failure modes that only surface with targeted prompt resampling.
sections.heading: Why this matters

sections.body:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, evaluation owners, QA engineers, model-serving SREs, and solutions engineers supporting Private deployments.
- Scope: continuous eval orchestration, prompt resample prioritization, label-refresh automation, quantization-aware gating and regression triage. Does not cover billing, customer communication templates, or security incident response (see related pages).
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
1) Eval Orchestrator (service: evald) — schedules and prioritizes evaluation jobs across three tiers: rapid-smoke, focused-slice, and fidelity-replay.
2) Resample Prioritizer (service: samplecraft) — scores prompt/document slices for human labeling or synthetic augmentation.
3) Label Refresh Pipeline (job: label-refresher) — batches human tasks and applies labels back to the eval corpus with provenance.
4) Regression Triage Assistant (tool: triage-assist) — links failing slices to potential root causes: prompt drift, quantization delta, KV-cache mismatch, or model-version idiosyncrasy.
5) Telemetry connector — maps production traces and error tags back to eval slices.
sections.heading: Components overview

sections.body:
- Tier 1: Rapid-smoke (low-cost, high-frequency)
  - Purpose: detect large regressions quickly after a build or config change.
  - Characteristics: synthetic seeds + small high-impact prompt sets, latency < 5 min, cost < 2% of full eval budget.
  - Use cases: pre-commit smoke, post-deploy quick sanity checks.

- Tier 2: Focused-slice (medium-cost, targeted)
  - Purpose: validate behavior on high-risk slices (business-critical customers, high-error cohorts, long-context sequences).
  - Characteristics: human-labeled reference answers, ensemble comparators, targeted metrics (semantic-f1, calibration, hallucination score).
  - Use cases: canary promotions, quantization candidate validation.

- Tier 3: Fidelity-replay (high-cost, low-frequency)
  - Purpose: reproduce exact production traces with live KV/state, full RNG seeds, and quantized/FP variants for root-cause analysis.
  - Characteristics: exact sequence lengths, real traffic mirrors, token-level diffs, full telemetry correlation.
  - Use cases: regression postmortems, model certification for Private deployments.
sections.heading: Tier definitions and when to use them

sections.body:
- Input signals (scored, 0–100): production error rate delta, traffic weight, novelty score (NLP embedding distance to training set), last-labeled-at (recency penalty), and quantization-sensitivity score.
- Score formula (example): 0.4*error_delta + 0.25*traffic_weight + 0.2*novelty + 0.1*quant_sensitivity + 0.05*recency_boost.
- Buckets: High (>70), Medium (40–70), Low (<40).
- Actions: High -> immediate human labeling batch + Tier 2 eval; Medium -> synthetic augmentation + Tier 1; Low -> deferred sampling for periodic scans.
sections.heading: Prioritization policy (Resample Prioritizer)

sections.body:
1) Telemetry ingestion: production traces tagged with slice-id and anomaly flag are forwarded to samplecraft.
2) Prioritization: samplecraft assigns bucket and creates labeling tasks via the labeling vendor API (or internal labeling UI).
3) Human labeling: label-refresher batches tasks in 200–500 units, includes guardrail checks (consistency spot-checks, gold-standard insertion rate 5%).
4) Label quality: labels pass when inter-annotator agreement (IAA) > 0.75 for categorical tasks or correlation > 0.85 for scalar metrics.
5) Recompute slice baselines: new labels are versioned and pushed to the eval corpus.
6) Trigger focused eval: Tier 2 evals run automatically for updated slices; if threshold breach occurs, open a triage runbook.
sections.heading: Automated label-refresh loop (operational steps)

sections.body:
- Tier 1 smoke pass: semantic-stability delta <= 0.08 (absolute) vs. baseline; latency p95 < 2x baseline.
- Tier 2 pass: semantic-F1 >= baseline - 0.03 AND hallucination-rate <= baseline + 0.02.
- Tier 3 certification: token-diff ratio <= 1.5% on certified prompt set; KPIs: pass rate >= 95% across certified slices.
- Labeling SLA: 95% of high-priority labeling tasks completed within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Gating thresholds and SLOs (example numbers)

sections.body:
- Every quantization candidate must run a focused-slice eval that includes: long-context (>4k tokens) prompts, high-KV-cache reuse prompts, and prompts that previously exhibited token-level divergence.
- Capture and compare intermediate logits snapshots where supported; if absolute logit drift above 0.2 occurs on top-10 tokens for >5% of slices flag as high-risk.
- For mixed-precision deployments, ensure ensemble testing (FP16 baseline + quantized variants) on Tier 3 replay before promotion.
sections.heading: Quantization-aware checks

sections.body:
1) Dev publishes candidate -> Tier 1 smoke executes.
2) If smoke passes, automated scheduling runs Tier 2 focused-slice for quantization and edge-case slices.
3) Passing Tier 2 triggers a controlled Tier 3 replay (gold-standard certification), or for low-risk changes a fast-promote to canary.
4) Canary monitors real traffic for 48–72 hours with telemetry hooks; automated rollback if error_delta > 1.5x or customer-facing regressions detected.
sections.heading: Acceptance and promotion flow (condensed)

sections.body:
1) Run triage-assist to collect diffs: token-level diffs, logit-drift summary, top-k answer divergence, and KV-cache hit-rate in replay.
2) Map failure signatures to root-cause classifiers (known classes: quantization, prompt-truncation, tokenization drift, RNG/seed mismatch, model-abi mismatch).
3) If classifier confidence < 0.6, escalate to a human investigation and create a regression incident.
4) Create reproducible fidelity replay job (Tier 3) with telemetry link and annotated hypothesis list.
5) Run controlled experiments: swap quantized kernels, toggle KV-cache modes, and sweep model compilation flags. Record results in a structured triage table.

Triage table (example columns, described):
- experiment-id, hypothesis, knobs-changed, pass/fail, notes, investigator, linked-artifacts.

Operational runbook: step-by-step for on-call (short):
1) Alert receives: eval-alert team->oncall.
2) Run quick-smoke job: evalctl run --suite rapid-smoke --candidate <id> --baseline <id> --timeout 10m.
3) If smoke fails, pin candidate in rollout system and mark canary:do-not-progress.
4) Kick off Tier 2 focused eval with label-refresh trigger.
5) If triage indicates quantization, run quant-sanity script: ./tools/quant-sanity --candidate <id> --slices important-slices.yaml.
6) Document findings in triage incident and route to model-onboarding and runtime-kernel teams.
sections.heading: Regression triage playbook (on Tier 2/3 failure)

sections.body:
- Quick smoke run:
  evalctl run --suite rapid-smoke --candidate rwm-2026-003 --baseline rwm-stable-2026-01 --out /tmp/smoke.json

- Focused job config (YAML):
  name: focused-slice-job
  candidate: rwm-2026-003
  slices: [enterprise-critical, long-context-8k, kv-heavy]
  labels_required: true
  parallelism: 8
  posthooks: [label-refresh, triage-notify]
sections.heading: Example CLI and YAML snippets (textual)

sections.body:
- Insert gold items at a 5% rate per batch.
- If a worker fails >2 gold items in the same batch, reject and reassign their tasks.
- Compute batch IAA and only accept batch if IAA >= 0.75.
sections.heading: Label quality checks (pseudo rules)

sections.body:
- Eval Orchestrator (evald): team - applied-ml-evals (owner: Evan Liu)
- Label Refresh (label-refresher): team - data-ops (owner: Marta Kovacs)
- Regression Triage Assistant: team - runtime (owner: Sofia Martinez)
- Oncall escalation channel: #eval-triage and pager duty evals-oncall rota
sections.heading: Ownership and contacts

sections.body:
- Related: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026 (interchange formats)
- Related: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol-2026 (quant repair)
- Related: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook (profiling guidance)

Appendix A: Common failure signatures and first actions (short catalogue):
- High token-diff concentrated in suffix region -> likely context-truncation or alignment mismatch. Action: run replay with extended context tokens and check tokenization mapping.
- Broad semantic drift across slices but low token-diff -> possible calibration or distributional shift. Action: run focused-slice with alternative temperature and sampler settings.
- Instability only in quantized runtimes -> run quant-sanity sweep and compare logits snapshots.

Appendix B: Example acceptance checklist for promoting quantized variant:
- [ ] Tier 1 smoke: pass
- [ ] Tier 2 focused: semantic-F1 delta <= -0.03
- [ ] Tier 2 hallucination: <= baseline + 0.02
- [ ] Tier 3 fidelity: token-diff <= 1.5% on cert set
- [ ] Labeling IAA >= 0.75 on all new slices
- [ ] Post-canary telemetry stable for 72 hours

- Contact: evan.liu@redwood.ai for operational questions, priya.desai@redwood.ai for process questions.

payload.page_title: Console UX Spec: Retention Settings + Compliance Downloads

sections.body: This document specifies the **Redwood Console** experience for configuring and validating **Retention Controls** and for initiating/downloading baseline **Compliance Reporting Pack** artifacts.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Viewing current **effective retention** by data class (and by region when supported)
- Editing retention within tier guardrails (min/max TTL) with clear warnings and prerequisites
- Understanding and exporting **change history** for retention settings
- Downloading exports required for security reviews (retention config export, audit-log templates link) and initiating a **Compliance Reporting Pack** generation

This is a UX and interaction spec; exact schema validation is owned by the retention policy service and documented in `retention-policy-schema-and-validation`.

---
sections.heading: The Retention Settings page is the primary UI for

sections.body:
1. Make retention settings **discoverable and safe**: clear defaults, guardrails, and plain-language explanations.
2. Enable Security Admins to **self-serve** common changes (e.g., set request logs to 7 days) without Support involvement.
3. Reduce security-review churn by enabling fast **exports and downloads** that map to the baseline evidence pack.
4. Provide auditors and read-only stakeholders with **clear evidence**: effective settings, scope, and change history.
5. Prevent misconfiguration by surfacing prerequisites (e.g., content logging disabled) and consequences (e.g., reduced debuggability).
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Full custom report builder; direct integration to external GRC platforms beyond download/export.
- Per-field redaction controls (handled under logging standards).
- Building a standalone audit-log UI; we link to audit-log exports/templates.

---
sections.heading: Non-goals (v1)

sections.body:
- **Security Admin (customer):** owns retention configuration and evidence generation.
- **SRE/Platform Admin (customer):** cares about debuggability, incident response, and operational impact of short retention.
- **Auditor/Compliance Analyst (customer):** read-only verification of controls, wants a clean export.
- **Redwood GRC (internal):** supports compliance pack requests and standard evidence delivery.

---
sections.heading: Primary personas

sections.body: - **Console → Organization Settings → Security & Compliance → Retention**
sections.heading: Location

sections.body:
1. Overview banner (deployment/tier context, last updated, holds)
2. Retention table (data classes + values + status)
3. Edit panel / modal (per data class, optionally per region)
4. Change history (auditable log of configuration changes)
5. Exports & Compliance Pack (download actions + pack status)

---
sections.heading: Subsections within the page

sections.body:
Console uses role-based access. Page access and actions:

| Role | View retention | Edit retention | View change history | Export retention config | Generate/download compliance pack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Org Owner | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Security Admin | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Compliance Admin | Yes | Limited (see below) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| SRE Operator | Yes | No (default) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Read-only Auditor | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | No |
sections.heading: Roles (customer-facing)

sections.body:
- Can adjust retention **within default ranges** but cannot:
  - Enable storage of prompts/completions where the product requires separate feature enablement
  - Create or release holds (handled via legal hold workflow)
sections.heading: Limited edit for Compliance Admin

sections.body:
- Redwood Support and GRC may need read-only access for troubleshooting evidence requests.
- Internal access is controlled via separate internal RBAC; do not expose internal-only controls in customer UI.
sections.heading: Internal access (Redwood)

At top of page, show a compact context block:

payload.page_title: Session Evacuation and Eviction Protocol Spec

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This design specification defines the Session Evacuation and Eviction Protocol (SEEP), a deterministic runtime policy and associated control plane/agent contracts for moving or terminating conversational sessions when physical or logical serving capacity changes. SEEP ensures customer-facing session continuity goals are balanced with infrastructure safety, cost controls, and predictable developer-facing semantics.

Motivation and goals
--------------------
- Reduce user-visible errors (Partial responses, broken websockets, abruptly ended sessions) during planned maintenance, scaling events, or overloaded nodes.
- Provide deterministic, testable behaviors for session takeover, graceful evacuation, and controlled eviction.
- Define a telemetry contract so downstream product and SRE teams can evaluate impact to SLAs and unit economics.
- Keep developer surface minimal: a small set of statuses and webhooks/streaming events that SDKs can observe and act on.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Real-time conversational session evacuation and eviction for hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Node-initiated evacuation (drain + migrate), controller-initiated evacuation (region failover), and aggressive eviction for capacity emergency.
- Telemetry and observability signals needed for SLOs and billing reconciliation.
sections.heading: In-scope

sections.body:
- Long-running offline batch migration of embeddings/long-term KV stores (handled by cache lifecycle team).
- Application-level retry logic (consumer SDKs should use the provided events; app-specific retry strategies are not prescribed here).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Session: a conversational context with a session_id and associated KV/decoder state stored in the session-store and optionally in node-local KV cache.
- Evacuation: proactive process where a node coordinates moving an active session to another node and updating routing state so new requests are routed correctly.
- Eviction: forced termination of a session when no migration path is available or policy prefers termination (cost/priority/tenancy).
- Drain window: configured time budget for graceful evacuation (default 8s for low-latency, 30s for long-running sessions).
- Priority hints: tenant metadata used to select which sessions to keep when resources are constrained (e.g., enterprise tier, SLA tags).

High-level architecture
-----------------------
sections.heading: Out-of-scope

sections.body:
- router-service: global request router; maintains mapping of session_id -> node_id and handles route changes.
- session-agent (node-local): manages KV cache, in-flight token emission, and coordinates evacuation/eviction with the controller.
- evacuation-coordinator: control-plane controller that orchestrates drain, migration, and final state transitions.
- session-store: durable store for session canonical state (cold copy) and migration journal.
- telemetry-proxy: funnel for structured telemetry events (metrics, traces, structured logs) from session-agent and coordinator.

Event sequence diagrams (text)
----------------------------
1) Planned node maintenance (drain)
- operator triggers maintenance -> evacuation-coordinator marks node_id as DRAINING.
- evacuation-coordinator requests router-service to stop new allocations to node_id and to return list of active sessions (streaming).
- session-agent receives DRAIN signal and begins per-session evacuation in parallel, honoring priority hints.
- For each session: session-agent writes migration intent to session-store, streams session-state to target node(s) using the migration API, updates router-service with new mapping when migration ACK returned.
- Once all sessions are migrated or drain-window expires, node marks DRAIN_COMPLETE and controller moves node to maintenance.

2) Emergency eviction (capacity pressure)
- Node under severe memory/CPU pressure triggers local eviction policy.
- session-agent evaluates eviction candidates by (priority -> last-active -> estimated cost-to-migrate).
- For selected sessions: session-agent emits 'eviction.advised' event to telemetry-proxy, then attempts a fast checkpoint to session-store. If checkpoint fails or cost>threshold, session_agent emits 'eviction.forced' and transitions session to TERMINATED with reason code.

Policy model and decision graph
------------------------------
sections.heading: Services and components referenced in this spec

sections.body:
1. Regional controller emergency flag (highest precedence).
2. Tenant priority hint (enterprise > paid > freemium).
3. Session SLA tag (e.g., response-consistency-sla: 99.5%).
4. Session idle-time and recent token-rate.
5. Estimated migration cost (bytes to transfer + deserialization cost).
sections.heading: Policy inputs (ordered by precedence)

sections.body:
- MIGRATE -> attempt graceful transfer to target node (preferred).
- STALL -> permit the current node to finish tokens but block new requests (used during short drains).
- TERMINATE -> close the session and persist the terminal marker (eviction).

API contract: session-agent <-> evacuation-coordinator (HTTP + streaming)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- POST /v1/nodes/{node_id}/evacuate  (controller -> node): triggers drain, body: {"drain_window_s":<int>, "policy_override": <string|null>}
- GET /v1/nodes/{node_id}/sessions?status=active (controller -> router-service): streaming list of session_id, priority, last_active, size_bytes
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/migrate (agent -> controller/target): body: { "target_node": "node-99", "checkpoint_uri": "s3://sessions/...", "mode": "copy|move" }
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/terminate (agent -> controller): body: { "reason": "eviction_forced|evacuation_timeout|policy_terminate", "user_visible_msg": "optional" }

Configuration table (defaults and allowed ranges)
------------------------------------------------
| key | default | valid values | description |
|----|---------:|--------------|------------|
| session.eviction.drain_window_s | "8" | "1..300" | Graceful drain time per node for low-latency clusters.
| session.eviction.max_concurrent_migrations | "32" | "1..500" | Max parallel migrations a node can attempt.
| session.eviction.priority_weights | "enterprise:100,paid:60,free:10" | comma-separated weights | Weighting for selection.
| session.eviction.fast_checkpoint_threshold_bytes | "1_048_576" | bytes | Sessions larger than this will prefer MIGRATE with snapshot vs inline transfer.

SLOs and thresholds
-------------------
- Migration success rate: >= 99.5% for planned drains (measured over daily windows).
- User-visible abrupt-termination rate due to evacuation: <= 0.05% of active session starts per month.
- Average additional tail latency introduced by evacuation activities: <= 5ms p95.

Telemetry and observability contract
----------------------------------
All session-agent and evacuation-coordinator events MUST be emitted to telemetry-proxy with the following minimal structured schema (JSON log):
- event.type (string): one of ["evacuation.start","session.migrate.attempt","session.migrate.success","session.migrate.fail","session.evict.advised","session.evict.forced","evacuation.complete","evacuation.timeout"]
- event.ts (ISO8601)
- node.id, session.id, tenant.id
- reason_code (if applicable)
- estimated_migration_bytes, actual_migration_bytes
- migration_duration_ms
- outcome (migrated|terminated|stalled|failed)

Metrics (prometheus counters/gauges) to be emitted by session-agent:
- seep_migrations_total{outcome="success|fail|partial"} (counter)
- seep_evictions_total{reason="policy|emergency|quota"} (counter)
- seep_migration_duration_seconds (histogram)
- seep_migration_queue_length (gauge)

Alerting and dashboards
- Pager alert: seep_migrations_total{outcome="fail"} rate > 1% over 15m => P1 to runtime-sre.
- Dashboard: per-tenant migration success rate, per-region drain completion latency histogram, and eviction counts by reason.

Operator runbook (high level)
----------------------------
1. Planned maintenance: trigger controller API -> verify router-service stops new allocations -> monitor seep_migration_queue_length and migration success events.
2. If migration failures spike: abort remaining migrations and mark node for emergency evacuation with policy_override: "suppress-migration" to avoid cascading failures.
3. If user-visible termination breaches SLO: initiate retrospective (ticket), enable increased drain_window for the affected cluster, and schedule canary maintenance.

Rollout and migration plan
-------------------------
- Canary (stage): implement protocol in dev cluster; run 10% of internal traffic with drain_window=30s for 2 weeks. Run synthetic churn tests with the migration harness.
- Beta (staging): enable in staging and run an 8-week soak with tenant-priority simulation (mix matching enterprise/freemium ratios).
- GA (hosted): default drain_window=8s for low-latency clusters; allow per-tenant overrides for Dedicated customers via account settings.

Backward compatibility and SDK guidance
--------------------------------------
- SDKs should handle the following session status codes sent over streaming: ACTIVE, DRAINING, MIGRATING, TERMINATED.
- On MIGRATING, SDKs MUST retry open requests within 500ms and reconnect using the session_id; router-service should direct to new node.
- Applications that require absolute continuity (no replays) should mark sessions with "persistence: true" and will be placed in a protected priority bucket (note: larger migration cost).

Testing matrix
--------------
1. Unit tests: policy decision graph permutations with mocked inputs.
2. Integration tests: controller + router + two node session_agent migration flows (happy and failure paths).
3. Chaos test: random node kill during migration and verify migration journal recovery (target success rate >= 99%).
4. Load test: synthetic churn at 5x peak expected tenant churn. Validate migration queue length and p95 migration_duration under threshold.

Security and compliance considerations
-------------------------------------
- Migration checkpoints and snapshots MUST be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed keys) and signed for integrity.
- Evacuation events with tenant metadata are considered sensitive and are routed through the telemetry-proxy with access controls; PII must be redacted before emission.

Ownership and maintenance
------------------------
- Feature owner: Priya Shah (serving-runtime).
- Primary review/approver: Daniel Kim (runtime-sre).
- Runtime implementation: eng-serving-runtime/session-agent team.
- Observability and alerts: eng-platform/dashboards team.

Appendix: sample migration request (YAML)
--------------------------------------
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: MigrationRequest
session_id: sess-01AF3C
source_node: node-12
target_node: node-99
mode: move
checkpoint: s3://session-checkpoints/prod/2026-03-30/sess-01AF3C.chk
priority: enterprise
notes: "drain by controller: node maintenance 2026-03-30T22:00Z"
---

References
----------
- Session resilience PRD: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-session-resilience-and-fallback-contract-2026-08-03
- Migration journal design (eng-serving-runtime): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/migration-journal

payload.page_title: Progressive variant rollouts and compatibility matrix spec

sections.body:
Specification for progressive model variant rollouts, compatibility gating, and a canonical compatibility matrix used by Redwood’s serving platform to safely release model variants across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
Background: As Redwood expands model offerings (quantized variants, instruction-tuned checkpoints, and architecture forks), product teams must be able to roll variants to subsets of traffic without risking regressions. This spec defines the gating rules, compatibility matrix, and orchestration primitives that the Redwood platform will provide.

Scope: Applies to model variant rollouts that change any of: tokenizer version, model architecture family (e.g., transformer block changes), KV cache layout, quantization format, or callable tool schemas. Includes Hosted API and Dedicated. Private customers may opt-in to use the same control plane primitives.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Provide deterministic compatibility checks that prevent unsafe variant assignment to previously cached KV/embedding workloads.
- Define rollout gates (syntactic, perf, quality) that are enforced automatically for canary and percent-rollouts.
- Expose a concise compatibility matrix for model owners and platform engineers.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- This spec does not change model training or evaluation pipelines.
- This does not propose new model format standards (that is a separate infra initiative).
- Product: Asha Patel (owner)
- Serving runtime: Marcus Liu
- Eng-sre: Sofia Ramirez
- Applied ML / Onboarding: Ethan Cho
- Console & Rollouts UX: Priya Desai
- Enterprise GTM: Lucas Meyer
1) Safety: The platform must block variant assignment when incompatibility risk is detected (e.g., tokenizer mismatch, cache layout change).
2) Observability: Rollout must emit per-variant metrics: latency p50/p95, error rate, per-token cost, and quality deltas on a curated prompt set.
3) Granularity: Support routing by percent, by customer (account_id), and by route (API key + model route).
4) Fallbacks: Automatic, fast fallback to the last-known-good variant on errors or on defined SLO breaches.
5) Compatibility API: A read-only endpoint that returns the compatibility matrix for any model family.
6) Manual override: Admins can create emergency rollbacks with one-click in Console.
7) Private deploy opt-in: Private deployments must be able to opt-out of platform gating while still consuming the compatibility matrix as guidance.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body: Columns: variant_id | model_family | tokenizer_version | kv_layout | quant_format | tool_schema_hash | compatible_with_previous_kv (yes/no) | notes
sections.heading: Compatibility matrix format (canonical)

sections.body:
- v1.0.0 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v2 | kv-v1 | fp16 | ts-abc123 | yes | baseline
- v1.1.0-quant | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v2 | kv-v1 | int8-q4 | ts-abc123 | yes | quantized weights; safe for cached prefixes
- v2.0.0 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v3 | kv-v2 | int8-q4 | ts-def456 | no | tokenizer and kv_layout changed; must invalidate prefix cache
- v2.0.1 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v3 | kv-v2 | int8-q4 | ts-def456 | yes | minor patch to cache checksum logic
Access pattern: GET /compatibility/model-family/{family} -> returns list of rows as above. Console will render as table and include links to model-onboarding pages.
sections.heading: Example rows

sections.body:
1) Compatibility service: A central read-only service (compat-service) stores canonical rows and exposes an HTTP API and internal gRPC API. It is the source of truth for gating.
2) Admission controller: The serving control plane queries compat-service at the time of assignment. If 'compatible_with_previous_kv' is 'no' and assignment would route traffic with cached prefixes, the admission controller either: a) blocks assignment, or b) requires explicit cache invalidation in rollout plan.
3) Rollout engine changes: The rollout engine will add a 'compatibility_check' phase before traffic shifts and during scheduled canary evaluation windows.
4) Metrics pipeline: During canary we evaluate quality using a lightweight prompt set (default 50 prompts) executed asynchronously and compared against a baseline using automatic metrics (perplexity/ROUGE/ROUGE-L/semantic-similarity) and hand-curated business metrics where available.
5) UI: Console shows per-variant compatibility flags, matrix link, and a one-click 'invalidate cache and continue' flow that triggers a controlled cache purge job.
sections.heading: High-level design

sections.body:
- compat-service storage: Postgres table with row-level version and 'effective_from' timestamps.
- Atomic rollout changes: Rollout engine persists desired-state in a config store (etcd) and coordinates canaries via leader election.
- Backward-compatibility modes: 'strict' (default) blocks unsafe assignments; 'permissive' allows assignment but will route only to new sessions. Private deployments default to permissive unless configured.
sections.heading: Implementation details

sections.body:
- compat-service read API is internal-only and authenticated via mTLS.
- Audit logs written to central audit-log store for every variant assignment decision.
sections.heading: Security considerations

sections.body:
[
  {
    "variant_id": "v2.0.0",
    "model_family": "redwood-rlhf-7b",
    "tokenizer_version": "tok-v3",
    "kv_layout": "kv-v2",
    "quant_format": "int8-q4",
    "tool_schema_hash": "ts-def456",
    "compatible_with_previous_kv": "no",
    "notes": "requires prefix invalidation or routing to new sessions only"
  }
]

Rollout config (YAML) example for canary with explicit cache invalidation:
---
rollout_name: rl-7b-v2-canary
model_family: redwood-rlhf-7b
variant: v2.0.0
strategy:
  - step: canary
    percent: 5
    duration_minutes: 60
    compatibility_action: invalidate_prefix_cache
  - step: ramp
    percent: 50
    duration_minutes: 240
    compatibility_action: validate_metrics
  - step: full
    percent: 100
    duration_minutes: 0
    compatibility_action: none
---
CLI: rwdctl rollout create --file rl-7b-v2-canary.yaml
sections.heading: Example compatibility API response (JSON snippet)

sections.body:
1) Author prepares variant and publishes to model catalog with compatibility rows.
2) Run automated compatibility check: rwdctl compat check --family redwood-rlhf-7b --variant v2.0.0. Address any 'no' flags.
3) Create canary with 'compatibility_action=invalidate_prefix_cache' if necessary.
4) Monitor for 60 minutes primary metrics (latency p95, errors) and run quality prompt set jobs.
5) If quality delta > threshold (see metrics_and_slos), automatically rollback.
6) If stable, continue ramp steps.
7) Post-rollout: create release note entry and pin variant as stable in the catalog.
sections.heading: Rollout procedure (recommended)

sections.body:
- Hot split of dedicated pools: for Dedicated nodes with long-lived sessions, the system prefers session-aware routing to avoid state mismatch.
- Private deployments with permissive mode: an explicit 'force' parameter is required to bypass strict gating.
sections.heading: Edge cases

sections.body:
- Latency: p95 increase <= 20% relative to baseline or absolute p95 <= 300ms (whichever is tighter per route)
- Errors: 5xx increase <= 0.1 percentage point absolute
- Quality: Semantic-similarity delta on evaluation prompt-set >= -0.03 (cosine sim) OR business-critical prompt pass-rate >= baseline - 2ppt
sections.heading: Primary SLOs during rollout windows

sections.body:
- Any single route exceeds latency SLO for 3 consecutive windows (window = 5 minutes)
- Error delta exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive windows
- Quality probe failure rate > 10% in canary window
sections.heading: Rollout thresholds (automatic rollback triggers)

sections.body: - All per-variant telemetry shall be stored with variant tags for 90 days in metrics store. Prompt-set evaluation artifacts retained for 30 days by default.
sections.heading: Telemetry and storage

sections.body:
1) Pager triggers: spike in errors or rollout rollback event.
2) Triage: identify variant_id and affected routes with 'rwdctl rollout status --id <id>'.
3) Immediate mitigation: trigger rollout rollback (rwdctl rollout rollback --id <id>) OR trigger emergency fallback policy to baseline variant.
4) If issue is cache incompatibility: run 'rwdctl cache purge --scope=affected-customers --variant <old>' only after coordinating with product to accept transient cold-start costs.
5) Postmortem: owner_team opens a postmortem within 48 hours and tags the rollout with incident id.
6) Prevent recurrence: add additional compatibility unit tests to the model onboarding harness.
- [ ] Compatibility matrix entry exists for the new variant
- [ ] Automated compat check passes or explicit cache invalidation plan approved
- [ ] Canary prompt-set defined and uploaded
- [ ] SLO thresholds configured for the route
- [ ] Fallback variant tagged and healthy
- [ ] Monitor dashboards pinned and alerting validated
Next engineering work: implement compat-service migration script, add 'compatibility_action' to rollout engine, and add Console UI for one-click cache invalidation. Product will schedule an internal pilot with two active customers in Dedicated by Q3 2026.
sections.heading: On-call steps for rollout incidents

sections.body:
1) Standardize 'kv_layout' semantic versioning across model-owners.
2) Decide retention for prompt-set results for compliance and debugging.
3) Define default compatibility_policy per region (latency-sensitive regions may prefer permissive mode).
