payload.page_title: Third-Party Model Adapters and Runtime Contracts: Design Patterns and Integration Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This design spec describes a set of standardized adapter patterns and runtime contract primitives for integrating third-party (external) model endpoints into Redwood Inference. The objective is to enable safe, observable, cost-predictable, and fallback-ready use of non-Redwood models (partner-hosted or customer-hosted endpoints) while preserving platform SLOs and billing/crediting models.

Goals
-----
- Define a minimal runtime contract that every third-party model adapter must implement (capabilities, health, performance, metadata).
- Provide configuration patterns for fidelity/economics negotiation, graceful fallback, and adaptive routing.
- Specify telemetry, tracing, and billing signal requirements to maintain observability parity with native models.
- Offer a rollout and validation playbook for onboarding new adapters.

Non-Goals
---------
- This spec does not mandate how external providers internal model serving should be implemented.
- It does not replace contractual/legal terms for third-party SLAs; it defines technical primitives for runtime behavior.

Key terminology
---------------
- Adapter: Lightweight runtime component in Redwood that translates Redwood inference requests to a third-party model API and normalizes responses.
- Runtime contract: A set of API endpoints / metadata and behavioral guarantees the adapter exposes to the Redwood runtime.
- Variant: Model variant in Redwood’s catalog; an adapter-backed variant is a variant that proxies to an external model.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1) Registration: Admin registers an adapter-backed variant in the model catalog with an adapter descriptor (endpoint, auth, capacity hints, supported features).
2) Adapter runtime: The adapter runs as a sidecar or managed connector in the serving plane and exposes the standardized contract endpoints to the Redwood routing layer.
3) Request path: Routing -> Adapter contract API -> third-party model -> Adapter normalizes output -> Redwood runtime continues (KV cache, batching, post-processing).
4) Telemetry flow: Adapter MUST emit the standardized telemetry events (latency, token counts, fidelity flags) to Redwood observability ingest endpoints.

Adapter contract: required endpoints and fields
----------------------------------------------
The adapter must implement the following HTTP endpoints. Each endpoint is described in the table below. The adapter may be implemented as a container sidecar in Dedicated/Private deployments or as a hosted connector for Hosted variants.

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose | Required fields (JSON) | Response example notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| /health | GET | Liveness & readiness probe | {"uptime_s": number, "status": "ok|degraded|down", "version": string} | Used by router; TTL 5s recommended |
| /capabilities | GET | Declared features | {"max_seq": number, "supports_streaming": bool, "supported_ops": ["generate","embed","chat"]} | Used at registration and periodic refresh |
| /infer | POST | Primary request path | {"request_id": string, "input": object, "mode":"sync|stream", "budget_ms": number, "fidelity_hint": "high|medium|low"} | Adapter returns normalized out object and token counts |
| /metrics-enqueue | POST | Push telemetry events | {"request_id": string, "latency_ms": number, "tokens_in": number, "tokens_out": number, "model_variant": string} | Reduces sampling mismatch with native runtime |
| /fallback-surface | GET | Adapter-provided fallback recommendations | {"compatible_variants": [string], "confidence_score": 0.0-1.0} | Used by policy engine when errors/latency exceed thresholds |

Configuration table: adapter descriptor (catalog fields)
-----------------------------------------------------
- variant_id (string): Redwood catalog id for the adapter-backed variant.
- adapter_endpoint (url): Base URL for adapter contract endpoints.
- auth_type (enum): oauth2 | api_key | mTLS.
- capacity_hint (object serialized string): e.g., "p50_latency_ms=120;p99_latency_ms=800;throughput_rps=50".
- cost_profile (string): cost-per-token or per-call template to feed billing/crediting engine.
- fidelity_profile (string): which fidelity tier this adapter maps to for billing purposes.

Performance SLOs, thresholds, and graceful degradation
-----------------------------------------------------
- Target SLOs (adapter must support): p50 <= 150ms; p90 <= 300ms; p99 <= 1200ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens).
- If runtime sees end-to-end latency > configured budget_ms or /health reports status != ok, routing policy must mark variant as degraded and consult /fallback-surface.
- Fallback policy precedence: 1) local cached response, 2) alternative adapter-backed variant with same fidelity, 3) Redwood native lower-cost variant with fidelity negotiation, 4) synthetic short-response (graceful degradation).

Telemetry and observability requirements
--------------------------------------
- Every /infer call must enqueue a metrics event via /metrics-enqueue within 2s of completion. Telemetry fields: request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, success|error, error_class.
- Traces: adapters should propagate inbound trace headers (x-trace-id) and attach outbound traces to Redwood tracing system.
- Sampling: Default 100% token accounting for billing; sampling for detailed request traces may be configurable.

Security, data handling, and compliance constraints
--------------------------------------------------
- Customer data residency rules must be enforced: adapter deployments in Private mode MUST not route PII to external-hosted adapters without explicit contract.
- Authentication: mTLS is preferred for Dedicated/Private. OAuth2 with short-lived tokens acceptable for hosted connectors; tokens must be rotated every 24 hours in production by default.
- Audit logs: adapters must provide a pullable audit log (S3/HTTPS) or stream to Redwood audit ingest with event types: model_call, config_change, health_change.

Adapter contract extension points (optional)
-----------------------------------------
- Output post-process hooks: adapter may declare post-processing templates (JSON schema) that Redwood will apply for normalization.
- Model explainability: adapters can optionally expose a /saliency endpoint returning token-level attributions; Redwood will surface this only for customers with enabled privacy consent.

Example adapter config (catalog entry)
-------------------------------------
{ "variant_id": "ext-llm-acme-3b", "adapter_endpoint": "https://acme-adapter.example.net/v1", "auth_type": "mTLS", "capacity_hint": "p50_latency_ms=120;p99_latency_ms=900;throughput_rps=30", "cost_profile": "per_token:0.00002", "fidelity_profile": "medium" }

Onboarding and validation playbook
--------------------------------
1) Pre-onboard review: Security, Legal and Product complete checklist (data residency, liability, SLA alignment).
2) Registration: Add descriptor to model catalog in staging.
3) Smoke tests (automated): health, capabilities, infer correctness, telemetry push.
4) Performance tests: run the benchmarking suite for target token lengths (32/128/512) and record p50/p90/p99.
5) Fidelity evaluation: run representative prompt-set evals (calibration dataset) to capture quality delta vs Redwood baseline.
6) Billing test: exercise cost_profile and ensure billing engine ingests metrics events and calculates credits properly.
7) Canary rollout: route 1% traffic with automated rollback on regressions (latency or quality).
8) Full launch: move to production catalog and enable 100% routing.

Automated tests and gating
-------------------------
- Gate: no adapter variant allowed to reach >5% production traffic unless p90 latency within 2x of advertised capacity_hint p90 AND fidelity delta (measured metric) within configured tolerance.
- CI artifacts: performance CSV, fidelity evaluation report, telemetry verification JSON, security checklist signed.

Compatibility and migration considerations
----------------------------------------
- Backwards compatibility: adapters that implement /capabilities v1 must continue supporting legacy fields for 6 months with deprecation warnings in /health.
- Migration: provide a transition SDK that maps older request envelopes to new contract fields and rewrites cost_profile templates.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Product: owner of catalog and onboarding playbooks (owner_team: product).
- Runtime: eng-serving-runtime owns adapter runtime integration, routing, and policy enforcement.
- Observability: eng-platform owns telemetry ingestion, dashboarding, and alerting.
- SLAs: adapters SHOULD declare their own SLA; Redwood will surface status but will only guarantee Redwood-level SLOs for native variants unless contractual SLA exists.

Rollout roadmap and milestones (quarterly cadence)
--------------------------------------------------
- Q4 2026: spec sign-off, reference adapter SDK, telemetry contract implementation, staging onboarding of 2 partners.
- Q1 2027: integrate billing/crediting signals and end-to-end canary tooling; onboard 3 additional partners.
- Q2 2027: privacy-residency enforcement, mTLS automation, and ally program for certified adapters.

Related risks and mitigations
---------------------------
- Risk: External provider latency causes customer-visible SLO violations.
  Mitigation: aggressive degrade-and-fallback policy + preflight performance caps.
- Risk: Billing fraud / metric mismatches.
  Mitigation: cross-validate adapter telemetry with Redwood edge sampling and require signed metrics batches from adapter.

Next steps and action items
--------------------------
- Product: finalize spec and coordinate security/legal checklist by 2026-11-15.
- Eng-serving-runtime: implement adapter router stubs and /health polling by 2026-12-01.
- Eng-platform: add telemetry schema and dashboards for adapter-backed variants by 2026-12-10.

Appendix: quick-checklist for adapter readiness
----------------------------------------------
- [ ] /health implemented and returns status==ok
- [ ] /capabilities populated (max_seq, supports_streaming)
- [ ] /infer accepts budget_ms and fidelity_hint
- [ ] Telemetry events sent to /metrics-enqueue
- [ ] Auth configured and rotating per policy
- [ ] Performance reports uploaded to onboarding bucket

References
----------
- Runtime architecture (internal): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- Billing/crediting contract: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process
- Telemetry schema v2: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts

Contact
-------
For questions about this spec, contact Priya Rao (Product) or Evan Turner (Eng-serving-runtime).

payload.page_title: Quantization rollout, observability & billing hooks — design spec

sections.body:
Overview

This design spec describes how Redwood will orchestrate a controlled rollout of model quantization variants while ensuring: (1) comprehensive observability to detect quality regressions early, (2) billing hooks that correctly surface changed unit economics to customers, and (3) customer-facing communication and migration tooling. The spec focuses on hosted and dedicated deployments; private deployments will be covered by a companion ops-runbook.

Goals

- Safely enable per-tenant or per-route quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) with automatic fallbacks.
- Produce telemetry sufficient to detect quality drift within 30 minutes of rollout changes for any tenant.
- Expose billing events and cost delta estimates in the console and usage exports so customers can decide when to opt-in/out.
- Provide an automated preflight simulation to estimate latency, memory, and token-cost changes for a tenant before migration.

Non-goals

- This spec does not define new quantization kernels or low-level runtime execution optimizations (runtime team responsibility).
- It does not replace contractual changes for SLA/price adjustments; it provides signaling hooks and recommended contract text for commercial teams.

Background and motivation

Quantization reduces memory and compute cost but can change output distributions (fidelity) and latency characteristics. Customers with tight quality constraints need: (1) rigorous observability to detect regressions; (2) billing transparency when unit costs change; and (3) safe rollback and migration pathways. Existing model-variant rollouts handle code-level switches, but quantization introduces unique telemetry and billing semantics that must be integrated with Redwood Optimize and Console.

Key concepts

- Quantized variant (q-variant): A model binary compiled/quantized to a lower precision (e.g., int8, int4).
- Preflight simulation: Synthetic or replayed workload run that produces latency/memory/cost delta estimates and a shadow-quality score.
- Telemetry gate: A set of signals (metrics + regressions) used to automatically pause or rollback a rollout.
- Billing hook: Event emitted when a tenant's effective per-token cost or capacity credit changes due to quantization.

Design overview

1) Rollout model

- Variants are deployed per-route (API route) with tenant-specific policy override. Default policy is tenant-opt-in.
- Rollouts support staged canary: internal canary (eng-prod), external canary (select customers), gradual percentage-based ramp, and tenant-initiated migration.
- Each rollout includes an associated "quantization profile" meta-record: precision, expected throughput improvement, estimated cost multiplier, and known limitations.

2) Observability and telemetry gating

- Minimum telemetry produced for every q-variant invocation:
  - token_count (input + output)
  - latency_p99, latency_p95, latency_p50 (per route, per tenant)
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio (where applicable)
  - top_k_token_prob_shift (approx metric computed from shadow-eval; see QA below)
  - perplexity_delta (shadow vs baseline)
  - deterministic-safety-check-failures (count)

- Derived signals and thresholds (defaults):
  - quality_regression_alert if shadow-quality-drop > 3% on a route over a 30-minute window.
  - latency_regression_alert if latency_p95 increases by > 50ms and p95 baseline was < 300ms.
  - cost_delta_notice if effective per-token cost changes by > 10%.

- Telemetry collection details:
  - Streaming traces should tag invocations with variant_id, rollout_id, tenant_id, route_id, and inferred-fidelity-tier.
  - Shadow-eval: For external canaries and staged rollouts, a sample of requests (configurable, default 1%) are evaluated against baseline full-precision model to compute fidelity metrics off-path. These shadow-evals are sampled asynchronously and do not affect live latency.

- Automated gating:
  - Each active rollout has a gating policy (json). Gate checks run every 5 minutes and compute statistical significance (Welch t-test) between baseline and q-variant on the past 30 minutes. If any gate condition trips, the rollout is automatically paused and an incident-style notification is created with recommended rollback steps.

3) Billing hooks and semantics

- When a tenant receives traffic served by a q-variant, Redwood must:
  a) Calculate the rendered cost-per-token (C_token) used for billing and UI. Default: C_token(q-variant) = C_token(baseline) * cost_multiplier(profile).
  b) Emit a BillingEvent with the following attributes: tenant_id, rollout_id, variant_id, effective_cost_multiplier, timestamp, estimated_monthly_savings (based on last 7 days consumption).

- Billing integration points:
  - Real-time console: display effective per-route cost delta.
  - Ingestion pipeline: BillingEvents feed usage reconciliation and downstream billing batch (daily).
  - Alerts: If the billing delta is negative (unexpected cost increase) above threshold, create immediate PagerDuty alert.

- Customer-visible notices:
  - Console banner when a tenant is on a q-variant for more than 1 hour: "This route is using a quantized variant that reduces compute cost by ~X% and may change output fidelity. See migration details."
  - Billing exports include both baseline-equivalent tokens and effective tokens for reconciliation.

Config schema (example)

- rollout_policy.json (fields):
  - "rollout_id": string
  - "route_id": string
  - "variant_id": string
  - "target_percentage": integer (0-100)
  - "shadow_sample_rate": float (0-1)
  - "gating_policy_id": string
  - "billing_mode": ["pass-through", "adjusted"]  // pass-through uses baseline pricing; adjusted applies multiplier
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
rollout_id: qroll-2027-04-21-42
  route_id: /v1/chat/completions
  variant_id: gptx-q8-2027-03
  target_percentage: 25
  shadow_sample_rate: 0.02
  gating_policy_id: gp-quant-std
  billing_mode: adjusted

Rollout steps (operational playbook)

1. Preparation (preflight)
  1.1. Create quantization profile and register variant_id.
  1.2. Run preflight simulation for the customer or tenant: replay last 24h sample calls or run synthetic prompt set to estimate latency/cost/fidelity deltas.
  1.3. Produce a preflight report: expected p95 latency change, estimated monthly savings, shadow-quality-score. Deliver to customer console.

2. Internal canary (multi-team)
  2.1. Deploy to internal canary pool (eng-prod).
  2.2. Observe telemetry for 48h.
  2.3. Approve or abort based on gating policy.

3. External canary (selected customers)
  3.1. Notify customers via console and email (template provided).
  3.2. Ramp target_percentage to 10% for 24-72h.
  3.3. Gate checks run every 5 minutes.

4. Gradual ramp
  4.1. Increase target_percentage in steps (10, 25, 50, 100) with minimum 2h at each step.
  4.2. If gating policy trips at any step, automatically pause and notify SRE/owner.

Observability & dashboards

- New dashboard tiles (Console + internal Grafana):
  - Per-route per-tenant fidelity heatmap (shadow-quality-score over time).
  - Cost delta timeline (estimated vs realized).
  - Rollout health timeline with gating decision markers.
  - Latency distribution overlay baseline vs q-variant.

- Alerts and PagerDuty:
  - quality_regression_alert => P2 (pager duty after 15m sustained).
  - latency_regression_alert => P3.
  - billing_delta_negative_alert => P1 (immediate).

SLOs and thresholds (suggested defaults)

- Shadow-quality-drop tolerance: <= 2% for internal canary, <= 3% for external canary, <= 5% for production ramp.
- Latency p95 increase tolerance: <= +20% or +50ms (whichever is smaller) during canary.
- Detection window: 30 minutes for automated gating; 7 days for billing reconciliation checks.

Testing, QA and metrics validation

- Unit tests: gating policy evaluation logic, billing event emission, edge-case missing telemetry.
- Integration: End-to-end test that simulates a 10k-req/hour tenant with shadow-evals enabled and asserts that: billing events are emitted, preflight report is produced, and that gate trips when intentional regression injected.
- Chaos testing: Inject synthetic noise in shadow-eval metrics to validate false-positive rate.

Customer communication and migration UX

- Preflight report displayed in Console with a single-click "Schedule migration" that triggers tenant-initiated ramp.
- Email + Console templates for external canary invitations.
- Billing FAQ text included in migration flow; template for Account Execs for larger customers.

Data retention and privacy considerations

- Shadow-eval artifacts that include customer prompt/response pairs must be subject to PII scrubbing and retained per Data Retention policies (default 30 days for preflight artifacts; longer only with explicit consent).

Ownership and rollout governance

- Feature owner: runtime-variant-team (primary).
- Observability/gating service owner: eng-platform (secondary).
- Billing pipeline integration: finance-legal (contract), billing-engine (implementation).
- Product comms: product-marketing (external).

Open questions and risks

- Calibration of shadow-quality-score: which metric best correlates to customer satisfaction across varied prompt sets? (Action: run multi-tenant correlation study Q2 2027).
- Should we offer an automated opt-out window that refunds a proportional credit if quality regressions are detected post-migration? (Commercial decision).

Appendices

A. Example gating policy (gp-quant-std)
  - window_minutes: 30
  - sample_minimum: 500 requests
  - metrics: ["shadow-quality-drop", "latency_p95_delta"]
  - thresholds: {"shadow-quality-drop": 0.03, "latency_p95_delta": 0.05}

B. Preflight report sample fields
  - baseline_p95_latency_ms
  - qvariant_p95_latency_ms
  - estimated_monthly_savings_usd
  - shadow_quality_score
  - confidence_interval

Contact and next steps

- Proposed timeline: prototype (Q2 2027), internal canary (Q3 2027), external canary (Q4 2027).
- Action items: design review (this doc), implementation RFC from runtime team, billing-engine API contract, Console UX mockups.

For discussion at the next cross-functional rollout sync.

payload.page_title: Design Spec: Marketplace subscription → org provisioning flow (AWS + GCP)

sections.body:
This document specifies the end-to-end onboarding flow for customers purchasing Redwood Inference through AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace.

The flow begins at **marketplace subscription/contract acceptance** and ends at **first successful API key creation and first successful request**. It covers:
- Entitlement verification (AWS/GCP)
- Redwood org provisioning and linking to a marketplace identity
- SKU/plan mapping and initial quota/limits
- Console UX and error handling
- Edge cases: existing orgs, multiple subscriptions, delayed entitlement propagation, region/residency constraints

Primary goal: reduce marketplace onboarding friction while preserving correctness for billing/metering and security expectations.

---
sections.heading: 1. Summary

sections.body:
1) **Time-to-first-success**: minimize time from marketplace purchase to first successful Redwood API request.
2) **Correctness**:
   - Correct plan/SKU mapping to internal billing meters.
   - Idempotent org provisioning.
   - Accurate entitlement state and lifecycle handling.
3) **Resilient UX**:
   - Clear error states with retry guidance.
   - Support for entitlement propagation delays.
4) **Enterprise-ready**:
   - Support procurement-led buyers who start in the marketplace before having a Redwood org.
   - Provide a clean path for customers who already have a Redwood org.
sections.heading: 2.1 Goals

sections.body:
- Implementing marketplace listing copy, screenshots, or pricing (covered elsewhere).
- Implementing the metering pipeline itself (this spec consumes the SKU → meter mapping).
- Solving all identity management problems (SCIM/SSO) during this flow; those can occur after the org exists.

---
sections.heading: 2.2 Non-goals

sections.body:
- **Procurement-led buyer (Enterprise IT/Procurement):** subscribes in marketplace first, then delegates to an engineer.
- **Developer/ML engineer:** wants a fast “subscribe → API key → curl works” path.
- **Solutions engineer / CS:** needs deterministic troubleshooting steps when entitlements lag.
sections.heading: 3.1 Personas

sections.body:
1) Marketplace listing → “Set up your account” / “Configure” deep link to Redwood Console
2) Email from Redwood (optional; depends on marketplace capabilities and customer-provided contact)
3) Direct Console entry point: `console.redwoodinference.com/marketplace`

---
sections.heading: 3.2 Entry points into Redwood

sections.body:
- **Marketplace provider**: `aws` or `gcp`.
- **Entitlement**: a provider-specific proof that the customer has an active subscription/contract.
- **Entitlement identity**:
  - AWS: typically a **CustomerIdentifier** (from AWS Marketplace Metering / Entitlement APIs).
  - GCP: typically an **Entitlement Resource Name** (e.g., `projects/.../entitlements/...`) plus associated account/project signals.
- **Marketplace subscription**: a purchase/contract that maps to one or more Redwood SKUs.
- **Redwood org**: the customer’s tenant in Redwood.
- **Org linking**: associating an existing or new Redwood org with a marketplace entitlement identity.
- **Plan assignment**: applying SKU-derived limits/features to the org (Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons).

---
sections.heading: 4. Key concepts and definitions

sections.body:
1) Customer subscribes in AWS/GCP Marketplace.
2) Customer clicks “Set up your account” and arrives at Redwood Console marketplace entry.
3) Console collects minimal info (email, org name) and requests entitlement verification.
4) Backend validates entitlement with marketplace provider.
5) Backend provisions new Redwood org and links it to the entitlement identity.
6) Backend assigns plan/SKU(s) and default limits.
7) Console prompts user to create first API key.
8) Console shows a “Try your first call” panel; user sends first request.
sections.heading: 5.1 Happy path (new customer)

sections.body:
1) Customer subscribes in marketplace.
2) In Console, user signs in and chooses “Link subscription to an existing org”.
3) Entitlement verification succeeds.
4) Backend links entitlement identity to the selected org and updates plan/SKU(s).
5) User creates/uses existing API key and proceeds.

---
sections.heading: 5.2 Happy path (existing Redwood org)

sections.body:
**URL**: `/marketplace/start?provider={aws|gcp}&token={provider_token}`

**Purpose**: confirm we can parse the provider context, explain steps, and start verification.

**UI elements**
- Header: “Finish setting up Redwood Inference”
- Stepper (4 steps): Verify subscription → Create/link org → Create API key → First request
- Primary CTA: “Verify subscription”
- Secondary CTA: “I’m already a Redwood customer”

**Copy (guidance)**
- “Marketplace entitlements can take a few minutes to propagate. If verification doesn’t succeed immediately, you can retry without losing progress.”

**Validation**
- If `provider` missing/unknown: show error “Marketplace provider not recognized” with link to docs and support.
- If `token` missing: show “This link is incomplete. Return to the marketplace and click Set up your account.”

---
sections.heading: 6.1 Screen A — Marketplace landing

sections.body:
**Behavior**
- On click, Console calls backend verification endpoint.
- Show spinner and log a telemetry event (see §10).

**UI states**
1) Verifying…
2) Verified
3) Not found / pending propagation
4) Found but not eligible (e.g., expired, wrong product)

**Retry UX**
- If pending propagation: show “We don’t see your entitlement yet. This can take up to 15 minutes.”
- Provide “Retry” button and “Troubleshoot” link.
- After 3 retries, surface a compact troubleshooting checklist:
  - Confirm you subscribed to the correct offer
  - Confirm you are using the same marketplace account that subscribed
  - Wait and retry (entitlements can be delayed)
  - Contact support with a correlation ID

---
sections.heading: 6.2 Screen B — Verify subscription (in progress)

sections.body:
**Entry condition**: entitlement verification succeeded.

**Choice**
- Option 1 (default): “Create a new Redwood organization”
  - Fields: Org name, Primary region (if applicable), Admin email (prefilled if signed in)
- Option 2: “Link to an existing organization”
  - Requires user to be signed in.
  - Dropdown of orgs user belongs to.
  - If user lacks permissions, show “You need Org Admin permissions to link a marketplace subscription.”

**Notes**
- Region selection (Hosted): defaults to nearest region, but must respect marketplace eligibility/residency constraints (see §8.6).
- For Dedicated/Private SKUs: show info panel “A Redwood Solutions Engineer will contact you to finalize deployment details. You can still create an org now to start the process.”

---
sections.heading: 6.3 Screen C — Create or link org

sections.body:
**Behavior**
- Console calls backend “provision/link” endpoint with the verified entitlement.
- Backend is required to be idempotent.

**UI**
- Progress text:
  1) Creating your organization
  2) Linking marketplace subscription
  3) Applying plan and limits
  4) Finalizing
- If step fails, show error and safe retry (“Retry provisioning”).

**Operational hint**
- Always display a **Provisioning Correlation ID**.

---
sections.heading: 6.4 Screen D — Provisioning (in progress)

sections.body:
**Default**: create a key scoped to the org.

**Fields**
- Key name (default: “Marketplace onboarding key”)
- Permissions preset:
  - Default: “Standard (chat + embeddings)” for Hosted
  - Dedicated/Private: default “Limited until deployment is active” (if relevant)

**Output**
- Show key once with copy-to-clipboard.
- Provide links to SDK quickstarts.

**Guardrails**
- If org policy requires SSO/SCIM before API keys (rare): show a blocking message and route to support/SE. (We should avoid this default for marketplace buyers; call out to Security/Product if needed.)

---
sections.heading: 6.5 Screen E — Create first API key

sections.body:
- Provide a minimal curl snippet using the new API key.
- Show “Test connection” button that performs a lightweight request (e.g., list models or a small completion) to confirm end-to-end success.
- Display usage metering note:
  - “Usage from marketplace subscriptions is billed via {AWS|GCP} Marketplace. You can also view usage details in Redwood Console.”

---
sections.heading: 6.6 Screen F — First request / success

sections.body: This section describes the intended contract; exact path names may change, but semantics must remain.
sections.heading: 7. Backend API contract (console ↔ control plane)

sections.body:
**Endpoint**: `POST /api/marketplace/entitlements/verify`

**Request (conceptual)**
- `provider`: `aws|gcp`
- `provider_token`: opaque token from provider deep link
- `request_id`: client-generated UUID

**Response**
- `status`: `VERIFIED | PENDING | NOT_FOUND | INELIGIBLE | ERROR`
- `entitlement_id`: internal stable ID (present for VERIFIED/PENDING)
- `provider_entitlement_ref`: provider reference (string)
- `sku`: marketplace SKU identifier
- `plan_preview`: display-only label (e.g., “Hosted API – Usage Based”)
- `retry_after_seconds`: optional for PENDING
- `correlation_id`: always

**Error codes** (normalized)
- `MP_INVALID_TOKEN`
- `MP_ENTITLEMENT_NOT_FOUND`
- `MP_ENTITLEMENT_PENDING`
- `MP_ENTITLEMENT_EXPIRED`
- `MP_PRODUCT_MISMATCH`
- `MP_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`
sections.heading: 7.1 Verify entitlement

sections.body:
**Endpoint**: `POST /api/marketplace/provision`

**Request (conceptual)**
- `entitlement_id`
- One of:
  - `create_org`: org_name, admin_email, preferred_region
  - `link_org`: org_id
- `idempotency_key`: UUID (required)

**Response**
- `org_id`
- `org_slug`
- `linked`: `true|false`
- `plan_applied`: string (e.g., “marketplace-hosted-usage-v2”)
- `limits_applied`: display string (exact quotas are internal; show customer-friendly summary)
- `next_steps`: string list (e.g., “Create API key”, “Invite team members”)
- `correlation_id`

**Idempotency requirement**
- Same `(entitlement_id, idempotency_key)` must produce the same `org_id` and not create duplicates.
sections.heading: 7.2 Provision or link org

sections.body:
Use existing API key creation endpoint; the console should prefill name and then route to existing API key UI.

---
sections.heading: 7.3 Create API key (existing)

sections.body:
**Problem**: After subscribing, the marketplace entitlement may not be visible immediately.

**Behavior**
- Verification returns `PENDING` when the provider token is valid but no active entitlement is yet retrievable.
- Console instructs retry, shows a reasonable upper bound (“up to 15 minutes”), and provides correlation ID.
- Backend also runs a sync job that will reconcile entitlements periodically (out of scope here but must exist).

**SLO target (product)**
- 95% of new subscriptions verifiable within 10 minutes.
sections.heading: 8.1 Entitlement propagation delay

sections.body:
**Behavior**
- Verification returns `NOT_FOUND` with hint: “This setup link must be opened by a user with access to the subscribing marketplace account.”
- Provide troubleshooting steps and correlation ID.
sections.heading: 8.2 User clicked setup link from a different marketplace account

sections.body:
**Scenario**: customer tries to link a second marketplace subscription to the same org.

**Policy**
- Allow multiple subscriptions per org only if SKUs are compatible (e.g., Hosted usage SKU + Compliance add-on). Disallow conflicting base plans.

**UX**
- If compatible: show “We’ll add this subscription to your org” summary.
- If incompatible: block with a clear reason and link to support/AE.
sections.heading: 8.3 Existing Redwood org already linked to a different subscription

sections.body:
**Scenario**: a second user attempts to set up after someone already completed provisioning.

**Behavior**
- `POST /verify` returns VERIFIED with metadata indicating “already linked” (or `POST /provision` returns existing org)
- Console shows:
  - “This subscription is already linked to organization: {org_name}.”
  - If user has access, offer “Go to org”.
  - If not, show “Request access from an org admin or contact support.”
sections.heading: 8.4 Subscription already linked to an org

sections.body:
**Behavior**
- Console always sends an idempotency key.
- Backend returns the same org.
- Console resumes from the current state.
sections.heading: 8.5 Duplicate org creation attempts / refresh during provisioning

sections.body:
**Principles**

payload.page_title: Cost Shield: Burst Protection Reservation Pricing (Design Spec)

sections.body: This design spec defines Cost Shield — a reservation-based burst protection and pricing model for Redwood Dedicated and Private customers. Cost Shield is a packaging and control layer that (1) guarantees short-duration capacity headroom for spiky traffic, (2) limits unexpected per-token costs during bursts, and (3) enables predictable unit economics for customers migrating from hosted pay-as-you-go to Dedicated capacity.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Provide a low-friction, credit-backed burst protection product that reduces cost volatility for customers with bursty workloads.
- Integrate with Dedicated pool autoscaling and warm capacity features to ensure a fast, controlled footprint for bursts without excessive overprovisioning.
- Expose simple UX and API primitives for applying burst credits, viewing credit burn, and configuring policy-level limits.
- Ensure accurate telemetry for billing reconciliation, SLO compliance, and product analytics.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Cost Shield is not intended to replace long-term reserved capacity or sustained throughput commitments.
- It will not change underlying model execution kernels or per-token micro-optimizations.
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
- Burst Credit: Prepaid units (token-equivalent credits) that can be consumed when a tenant exceeds their steady-state committed capacity. Each credit corresponds to a fixed number of token-equivalents depending on the packaging.
- Shield Window: The short time window (default 5–15 minutes) during which reserved headroom is guaranteed to be available for bursts.
- Protection Threshold: The percent of committed baseline utilization above which burst credits are eligible to be applied (default 80%).
- Soft-Fallthrough: Automatic fallback behavior to compatible cheaper model variants or preemptible capacity when credits are exhausted and a fallthrough policy is configured.
sections.heading: Key concepts and terminology

sections.body:
1) Pricing/Packaging requirements:
  - Offer three Cost Shield SKUs: Bronze (small), Silver (medium), Gold (large). Each SKU defines: monthly credit allotment, Shield Window, and guaranteed headroom in vGPU-equivalent throughput.
  - Allow one-time top-ups and scheduled monthly renewals tied to the billing cycle.
  - Credits expire on a rolling 12-month schedule by default (configurable per account for enterprise).

2) Behavioral requirements:
  - When a tenant’s baseline throughput utilization > Protection Threshold, incoming requests may draw from Burst Credits to expand capacity within Shield Window.
  - The runtime MUST prioritize requests according to configured SLAs: e.g., route transactional routes ahead of background batch routes when credits are limited.
  - If credits are exhausted, and no soft-fallthrough is configured, requests are throttled according to the tenant’s configured throttling policy.

3) Observability and billing telemetry:
  - Emit per-tenant events: credit_allocated, credit_consumed, credit_topped_up, credit_expired, credit_balance_snapshot. Events must include timestamp, request_id batch_id (if applicable), route_id, model_variant, tokens_consumed, and estimated cost delta.
  - Billing integration must be able to reconcile credits consumed vs per-token charges within +/-1% for monthly invoices.

4) API / Admin UX:
  - Console: new Cost Shield dashboard that shows current credit balance, projected burn rate (based on 7/30/90-day patterns), recent credit events, Shield Window utilization heatmap, and recommended SKU.
  - REST API: endpoints to get balance (GET /v1/cost-shield/{tenant}), top-up (POST /v1/cost-shield/{tenant}/topup), attach/detach SKU (PATCH /v1/cost-shield/{tenant}), and simulate burn (POST /v1/cost-shield/{tenant}/simulate).

5) Runtime changes (serving surface):
  - Admission control layer: add a Cost Shield admission policy that checks: baseline_utilization, protection_threshold, current_credit_balance, route_priority, and applicable Shield Window.
  - Scheduler: when credits are eligible, the scheduler may provision short-lived warm instances or reassign queued requests to maintain latency SLOs for covered traffic up to guaranteed headroom.
sections.heading: Product requirements (high level)

sections.body:
1. Request arrives at front-door routing.
2. Router computes projected baseline utilization for tenant (sliding-window exponential smoothing, default 5m window).
3. If projected > Protection Threshold, call Cost Shield service to attempt to reserve credits for this request batch.
4a. If reservation succeeds, mark request as 'shielded' and schedule on reserved headroom path (fast lane).
4b. If reservation fails and soft-fallthrough configured, route to fallback model or preemptible pool.
4c. Otherwise respect tenant throttling policy and return 429 or best-effort response based on route.
sections.heading: Admission control flow (high level)

sections.body:
- Baseline: Tenant A has committed capacity of 100 tokens/s. Bronze SKU gives 100k credits/month, Shield Window = 10 minutes, guaranteed headroom = 25 tokens/s.
- If Tenant A experiences a 10-minute spike to 350 tokens/s, the runtime will grant up to guaranteed headroom (25 tokens/s) immediately if credits exist; the remainder will be routed through soft-fallthrough or throttled.
- Credit consumption formula (simplified): credits_used = sum_over_requests(tokens * model_weight) * SKU_multiplier. SKU_multiplier adjusts for model class (e.g., 1.0 for base Llama-class, 1.8 for very-large variants).
sections.heading: Credit accounting model (examples)

sections.body:
- credit_allocated: "tenant=acme, sku=bronze, window_start=2028-01-12T15:34Z, tokens_reserved=24000, headroom_tokens_per_sec=25"
- credit_consumed: "tenant=acme, route=transaction, model=redwood-2-small, tokens=1523, credits=1523"
sections.heading: Telemetry schema (stringified event examples)

sections.body: - GET /v1/cost-shield/{tenant} response: {"balance": "124000", "sku": "bronze", "shield_window_minutes": "10", "headroom_tps": "25", "protection_threshold_pct": "80"} (JSON string fields in API will be numeric in implementation; the console will render for humans.)
sections.heading: API contract details (example payloads)

sections.body:
- Setup flow: Admin chooses SKU -> system estimates projected monthly burn given current usage -> shows recommendations and a one-click preview simulation for a previous burst window.
- Incident view: Console card visible in tenant health panel showing active shield events, active credits consumption timeline, and recent fallthroughs to cheaper models.
sections.heading: UI wireframes and console flows (summary)

sections.body:
Phase 0 (pilot, Q1 2028):
- Pilot with 5 existing Dedicated customers (SRE + Customer Success-managed onboarding). No self-serve purchases. Manual reconciliation for billing.

Phase 1 (self-serve beta, Q2 2028):
- Expose SKU selection in console for Dedicated customers. Automated billing enabled for Bronze/Silver. Gold requires sales approval.
- Add soft-fallthrough and recommended policy templates.

Phase 2 (general availability, Q3 2028):
- Full public SKU purchase for Dedicated and Private (enterprise-managed) with configurable expiry windows and enterprise-specific contract terms.
- Add usage-based auto-topup option and programmatic webhooks for credit events.
sections.heading: Rollout plan and gating

sections.body:
- Product SLO: Cost Shield accounting must be 99.9% accurate for credit balance updates (latency under 2s) and 99.99% available for reads.
- Billing risk: Ensure reconciliation pipeline with billing service validates consumed credits to within +/-1% of on-chain per-token costs for monthly invoices.
- Abuse risk: Implement per-tenant hard caps and anomaly detection. If a tenant shows sustained >10x weekly spikes, the system should flag and require sales/CS review prior to further automated top-ups.
sections.heading: SLOs and risk considerations

sections.body:
- Cost Shield metadata is account-level billing metadata and inherits tenant confidentiality settings. All API calls must be authenticated and authorized via existing tenant-scoped RBAC.
- Audit logs for credit events stored for 13 months by default (extendable for enterprise customers).
sections.heading: Security and compliance

sections.body:
- Alert: credit-processor-lag > 10s -> page oncall-costshield primary -> check message queue length and executor health.
- Playbook: If credits appear overconsumed, trigger immediate partial rollback (prevent further allocations), fetch event stream for last 60 minutes, reconcile with billing export, and notify Customer Success.
sections.heading: Operational runbook (summary)

sections.body:
- SKU granularity: Do we allow per-route SKUs for advanced customers? (Tradeoff: complexity vs precise economics.)
- Expiry policy default: 12 months vs 24 months for enterprise.
- Model weighting table: Who owns and maintains SKU_multiplier values for new model variants? Recommend Research/Applied ML maintain proxied weights and Product owns governance.
sections.heading: Open questions and decisions to make

sections.body:
- Product owner: Asha Patel (product). Engineering owners: Rajiv Menon (serving runtime), Eleanor Chen (billing/console integration).
- Next milestones: prototype admission-control hook (Q1 2028), telemetry schema reviewed and signed off (by 2028-02-10), pilot onboarding checklist completed (by 2028-03-01).

Appendix A — Example billing scenarios (illustrative):

- Scenario 1: Predictable lumpy traffic (announcements, campaigns). Bronze SKU reduces invoice spikes by pre-absorbing 60–80% of burst cost for a nominal monthly fee.
- Scenario 2: Frequent microbursts (chatty agents). Silver SKU recommended; combined with auto-topup it smooths monthly spend while protecting latency-sensitive routes.

Appendix B — Related artifacts and references:

- Warm capacity subscriptions product brief (link in related_pages).
- Dedicated pool autoscaling spec (see eng-infra/team-wiki).
- Billing reconciliation playbook (finance-and-legal/billing).
sections.heading: Ownership and next steps

sections.body:
- 2027-11-18: Initial draft (Asha Patel).
- 2027-12-22: Added telemetry schema and API contract examples (Eleanor Chen).
- 2028-01-19: Incorporated pilot rollout plan and SLOs; moved to in_review.

payload.page_title: Service Catalog Contract and Integration Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook defines the canonical service catalog contract for model and variant metadata and documents recommended integration patterns for runtime, Dedicated, Private deployments, and Console authoring. The catalog centralizes: model variant mappings, compatibility profiles, region/availability constraints, SLO class assignments, and operational metadata used by routing and cost-aware features.

Purpose and scope:

- Establish a single, versioned API surface for catalog CRUD operations.
- Provide concrete integration recipes for each consumer type (runtime, console, dedicated, on-prem).
- Describe rollout, monitoring, and security requirements to avoid inconsistent behavior across services.
- Scope excludes billing pipeline implementation and model training lineage.

Key principles:

1) Single source of truth: catalog entries are authoritative for routing, routing fallbacks, and console metadata.
2) Backwards-compatible evolution: additive fields only; breaking changes require major versioning.
3) Fast propagation: normal writes should be visible to runtime consumers within the defined change propagation SLO.

High-level API contract (summary):

- Base path: /api/catalog/v1/entries
- Operations: list, retrieve by id, create, update (patch), soft-delete
- Modes: read-only (runtime), read-write (authoring), bulk import (onboarding)
- Auth: bearer tokens with role claims controlling write vs read access
- Versioning: Accept-Version header; default v1; support feature-flagged v1.1 for opt-in fields

Canonical entry fields (human-readable form):

- id: stable string identifier (e.g., gv-2026-0001) 
- name: human-friendly model name (namespace/name)
- variants: list of variant identifiers mapped to binary artifacts (variant IDs only)
- compatibility_profile: tag describing latency/cost compatibility (e.g., low-latency/high-cost)
- regions_allowed: list of region identifiers where routing is permitted
- cost_multiplier: decimal multiplier applied by routing/cost algorithms (optional)
- deprecation_date: ISO date when the model is scheduled for retire (optional)
- bindings: pointers to external integrations (encrypted references only)

API semantics and examples (pseudo-examples):

- List call with filters: GET /api/catalog/v1/entries?compatibility_profile=low-latency&region=us-west1 returns a paged list of matching entries. Use page_token and page_size for pagination.

- Create flow (authoring): POST /api/catalog/v1/entries with canonical entry payload. On success return 201 and Location header.

- cURL example (authoring):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" -H "Accept-Version: v1" -X POST https://catalog.internal.redwood/api/catalog/v1/entries -d 'id: gv-2026-0001, name: redwood/gpt-3.8-f, variants: [f32, f16-q4], compatibility_profile: low-latency, regions_allowed: [us-west1]'

Integration patterns (detailed):

1) Runtime (eng-serving-runtime) - read-only cache

- Behavior: runtime processes consume a read-only snapshot. Snapshots are refreshed on a schedule (default 30s) and via a change-stream subscription (Kafka).
- Cache invalidation: entries with a higher semantic version trigger immediate refresh. Runtime must support last-known-good fallback to a pinned catalog file for >5m outages.
- Observability: runtime traces must include catalog_snapshot_version and entry_ids used for routing decisions.

2) Console and authoring services - managed write path

- Writes are mediated by an authoring service that enforces schema validation and a soft-approval workflow: draft -> approved -> published.
- Approval requirements: at least one applied-ml reviewer for compatibility changes and one eng-infra reviewer for region/binding changes.

3) Dedicated customer pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) - sync model

- Dedicated: a periodic export job writes approved entries for the customer to an encrypted customer-specific location. A tenant-local registry in the Dedicated control plane consumes the export and exposes a local read-only API.
- On-prem: installers accept a signed catalog manifest pointer argument (installer flag: --catalog-import). The import validates signatures and applies entries into the local registry.

Versioning, compatibility and rollout:

- Additive-first policy: new fields are added as optional. Renames or semantic changes require a major version (v2).
- Soft-deprecation: set deprecation_date. Consumers should stop routing to entries older than deprecation_date + 30 days.
- Canary rollout process for schema changes: enable Accept-Version opt-in for small percentage traffic (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Wait 24 hours between steps and validate metrics and contract tests.

SLOs and Monitoring:

- Catalog API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Latency SLO: p95 GET /entries/{id} < 50ms in-region.
- Change propagation SLO: 120 seconds (time from publish to runtime visibility).

Key alerts:

- P1: API error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes or availability drops below 99.9%.
- P2: Change propagation lag > 10 minutes for > 5% of updates.

Instrumentation requirements:

- All writes must emit events to the catalog-change topic with schema version and correlation id.
- Runtimes must log catalog_snapshot_version in request traces and measurement tooling must correlate generation metrics with catalog versions.

Security and RBAC:

- Roles: catalog-reader, catalog-writer, catalog-admin.
- Writer endpoints require catalog-writer role; approval flows require catalog-admin for publish actions.
- Sensitive bindings MUST be stored encrypted in KMS and not returned in GET response bodies. GET responses may include a sentinel flag like "has_sensitive_bindings=true".

Testing and validation:

- Schema unit tests and contract tests must be added to the authoring CI pipeline.
- Integration test harness: staging runtime runs against a synthetic catalog with varied compatibility profiles and region constraints.
- Load testing: verify list/pagination performance with up to 100k entries at 200 RPS target.

Migration and deprecation plan (recommended timeline):

- Phase 0 (planning): publish schema docs and runbook.
- Phase 1 (30 days): run catalog service in read-only mode for runtime; no authoring writes except imports. Collect compatibility gaps.
- Phase 2 (30-60 days): enable feature-flagged authoring for internal teams (v1.1). Run canaries and expand test coverage.
- Phase 3 (60-120 days): open write access to broader teams with approval gating for region/binding changes; begin tenant sync for Dedicated.

Deprecation notice policy:

- Minimum notice: 90 days for model deprecation windows.
- Automation: the authoring service should trigger console notifications and email to owning teams and affected tenants when deprecation_date is set.

Pre-deploy checklist:

- Schema published and contract tests added to CI.
- Authoring UI wired to validator and approval service.
- RBAC policies created in IAM and tested.
- Runtime caching library implemented with last-known-good fallback.
- Dashboards: Catalog API availability, change lag, cache hit ratio.
- Security review signed off by security-and-compliance.

Owners and contacts:

- Product owner: Asha Patel (product).
- Technical owner: Daniel Kim (eng-platform).
- Applied ML contact: Marta Gonzalez (applied-ml).

Appendix: canonical schema (human-readable summary)

- required fields: id, name, variants, compatibility_profile
- optional fields: regions_allowed, cost_multiplier, deprecation_date, bindings

Example operational commands (migration):

- Export approved entries for tenant mycorp to encrypted storage: 
  tools/catalog_export.py --tenant mycorp --approved --out gs://redwood-tenant-manifests/mycorp/catalog-YYYY-MM-DD.gpg

- Import a signed manifest to an onprem installer: 
  ./installer --catalog-import gs://redwood-tenant-manifests/mycorp/catalog-YYYY-MM-DD.gpg --verify-signature

References and related pages:

- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (runtime cache and fallback details).
- product-docs/requirements/multimodel-pipeline-orchestration-prd-2026-01-12.json (multi-model orchestration constraints).

Revision history:

- 2026-10-15: initial draft by Asha Patel.
- 2026-11-10: added SLOs and canary rollout process after eng-platform review.
- 2026-12-01: clarified migration checklist and approval gating (current status: in_review).

payload.page_title: Quickstart Templates v1 — Launch Metrics & Telemetry Specification

sections.body:
This document defines the metrics, telemetry events, and traffic tagging required for the **Quickstart Templates v1** launch (RAG + Agents templates across Python and TypeScript). The goal is to measure adoption, activation, and ongoing retention while respecting privacy constraints and avoiding high-cardinality analytics.

**Primary use cases**
- Measure funnel from docs/CLI to “first successful request”.
- Attribute API traffic to template-generated apps (opt-in) to assess retention and quality.
- Quantify support deflection (lower ticket rate / faster time-to-resolution) over time.

**Non-goals (v1)**
- User-level session replay, prompt content capture, or any collection of customer data beyond minimal operational/attribution fields.
- Perfect causal attribution across all acquisition channels (we will prioritize docs → CLI → API request instrumentation).

**Owners**
- Spec owner: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API PM)
- Implementation liaison: Logan Wright (Telemetry platform)
- DevEx implementation: Monica Patel (templates), Dana Lo (TS)
- Privacy/Security review: Marcus Lin
- Support KPI alignment: Dev Patel / Priya Shah

---
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
**Time-to-First-Success (TTFS)**
- **Definition:** time between a developer starting a template (CLI init or repo template usage) and their first **successful** Redwood API request from that template app.
- **Target (launch):** p50 ≤ 15 minutes, p90 ≤ 45 minutes (internal beta baseline to be captured).
sections.heading: North Star KPI

sections.body:
1) **Template Activation Rate**
- **Definition:** % of template starts that reach First Success within 24 hours.
- **Segments:** language (py/ts), template type (rag-agent), acquisition channel (docs vs github).

2) **Doctor Pass Rate**
- **Definition:** % of `doctor` runs that end with “healthy” status (API connectivity + env validated + collector reachable when configured).

3) **Streaming Readiness Rate (where applicable)**
- **Definition:** % of first success requests using streaming that complete without disconnect/reconnect errors.
sections.heading: Activation KPIs

sections.body:
1) **Template-tagged Weekly Active Apps (WAAs)**
- **Definition:** number of distinct template app install IDs that generate ≥ 1 successful request in a rolling 7-day window.
- **Note:** Requires opt-in traffic tagging (see “Traffic tagging”).

2) **D7 / D30 Retention (tagged apps)**
- **Definition:** % of apps active in week 0 that are active again in week 1 (D7) / week 4 (D30).
sections.heading: Retention KPIs

sections.body:
1) **Support Ticket Rate per 1k template starts**
- **Definition:** count of template-related tickets / (template starts / 1000).
- **Source:** Support tagging + analytics.

2) **Top Failure Modes (by event + error taxonomy)**
- **Definition:** distribution of failure categories for first-run requests (auth, quota, network, tool schema, retrieval empty, exporter misconfig).

---
sections.heading: Support & Quality KPIs

sections.body:
We will measure the following funnel steps. Each step is backed by one or more telemetry events.

1) **Discovery**
- Developer views template docs page or README.

2) **Start**
- Developer scaffolds a project via CLI or GitHub template.

3) **Configure**
- Developer sets API key and required env (model, base URL, etc.).

4) **Verify (Doctor)**
- Developer runs `doctor` to validate env/API connectivity (recommended but not required).

5) **Run Local**
- Developer starts the app locally and makes a request.

6) **First Success**
- The template app makes its first successful inference request to Redwood.

7) **Ongoing Usage**
- Subsequent successful requests in later days/weeks.

---
sections.heading: Funnel definition (canonical)

sections.body:
1) **Opt-in traffic tagging**
- Template-origin tagging MUST be **off by default** for requests that traverse customer corporate proxies that may reject unknown headers.
- Templates SHOULD provide a simple switch (env var) to enable tagging.

2) **Privacy + data minimization**
- Do NOT send prompts, tool arguments, retrieved documents, PII, or customer identifiers.
- Do NOT log API keys or bearer tokens.
- Any “install/app identifier” must be a randomly generated UUID stored locally in the template project.

3) **Cardinality control**
- No dynamic IDs in metric label sets.
- Any identifiers used for analytics must be stored in event payloads (analytics system), not as metric dimensions.

4) **Consistency across languages**
- Python and TypeScript templates MUST emit the same core event names and required fields.

---
sections.heading: Telemetry principles & constraints

sections.body:
All events are emitted to Redwood’s analytics pipeline (Console/Analytics) as discrete events.

**Naming convention**
- Prefix: `quickstart_` for template/quickstart events.
- Use snake_case.

**Field conventions**
- `template_id`: stable string identifier for template family, e.g. `rag-agent`.
- `template_language`: `python` | `typescript`.
- `template_version`: semver string (e.g. `1.0.0`).
- `scaffolder`: `cli` | `github`.
- `install_id`: random UUID generated on init; stored in local project file (e.g. `.redwood/template.json`).
- `project_hash`: optional stable hash derived from (install_id + repo path) used only for dedupe; must not contain user path strings.
sections.heading: Event taxonomy

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_docs_view`
- **When:** docs page for templates is loaded (docs-site instrumentation).
- **Required fields:** `page_path`, `referrer_domain` (domain only), `utm_source` (if present), `utm_campaign` (if present)
- **Notes:** avoid full URLs beyond path; do not capture query strings other than UTM.

**Event:** `quickstart_docs_click_install`
- **When:** user clicks CLI install / repo link.
- **Required fields:** `target` (`cli_install` | `github_repo` | `walkthrough`), `page_path`
sections.heading: 1) Docs / discovery

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_template_init`
- **When:** CLI `init` completes successfully OR (if feasible) a first-run script in GitHub template runs.
- **Required fields:** `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`, `scaffolder`, `install_id`
- **Optional fields:** `os_family` (windows/macos/linux), `node_major` or `python_major_minor`

**Event:** `quickstart_template_init_failed`
- **When:** CLI init fails.
- **Required fields:** `template_id` (if known), `scaffolder`, `error_category`, `error_code`
- **Allowed categories:** `dependency_install`, `filesystem_permissions`, `network`, `unknown`
sections.heading: 2) Start / scaffold

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_env_check`
- **When:** template app starts up and validates required env vars.
- **Required fields:** `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`, `install_id`, `env_status` (`ok` | `missing_required` | `invalid_value`)
- **Optional fields:** `missing_fields` (comma-separated allowlist: `REDWOOD_API_KEY,REDWOOD_MODEL,REDWOOD_BASE_URL,OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`)
sections.heading: 3) Configuration / environment

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_doctor_run`
- **When:** CLI `doctor` is executed.
- **Required fields:** `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`, `install_id`
- **Optional fields:** `checks_run` (comma-separated), `duration_ms`

**Event:** `quickstart_doctor_result`
- **When:** `doctor` finishes.
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `result` (`healthy` | `degraded` | `unhealthy`)
- **Optional fields:** `failed_checks` (comma-separated allowlist: `api_key,api_reachable,model_access,otel_collector_reachable,dns,tls,clock_skew`)
sections.heading: 4) Doctor

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_first_success`
- **When:** first successful inference request is completed from a given `install_id`.
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`, `request_mode` (`sync` | `streaming`)
- **Optional fields:** `model_family` (e.g. `llama`, `qwen`, `mistral`), `region` (Redwood region code), `latency_ms_bucket` (bucketed)

**Event:** `quickstart_request_failed`
- **When:** a request fails before first success (or any time, sampled).
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`, `error_category`, `http_status`
- **Allowed `error_category`:** `auth`, `quota`, `rate_limit`, `network`, `timeout`, `stream_disconnect`, `tool_schema`, `tool_execution`, `retrieval_empty`, `retrieval_error`, `otel_export_error`, `unknown`
- **Optional fields:** `retry_attempts` (bucketed: 0,1,2,3+)

**Event:** `quickstart_request_success`
- **When:** successful requests after first success; sampled to control volume.
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `template_id`, `template_language`, `template_version`
- **Sampling:** 1% default (configurable); always emit `quickstart_first_success` regardless of sampling.
sections.heading: 5) API request outcomes (template app)

sections.body:
**Event:** `quickstart_deploy_selected`
- **When:** user selects a deploy recipe (e.g. Fly.io, Render, Docker, k8s) from README or CLI.
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `deploy_target` (`docker` | `flyio` | `render` | `kubernetes` | `other`)

**Event:** `quickstart_template_upgrade`
- **When:** CLI upgrade command runs successfully (v1 may be deferred; include only if shipped).
- **Required fields:** `install_id`, `from_version`, `to_version`

---
sections.heading: 6) Deploy / upgrade

sections.body: Traffic tagging is used to allow Console analytics to filter and report on template-generated traffic.
sections.heading: Traffic tagging (API gateway attribution)

sections.body:
- Must be **opt-in** and easy to disable.
- Must not include sensitive data.
- Must be stable across retries and streaming reconnect.
- Must be compatible with Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private when possible.
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body:
When tagging is enabled, the template app will include the following headers on Redwood API requests:
- `X-Redwood-Template-Id: rag-agent`
- `X-Redwood-Template-Version: 1.0.0`
- `X-Redwood-Template-Lang: python` (or `typescript`)
- `X-Redwood-Template-Install-Id: <uuid>`

**Important:** `X-Redwood-Template-Install-Id` is used for analytics correlation and MUST NOT be promoted to metric dimensions.
sections.heading: Header conventions (v1)

sections.body:
- Env var: `REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1` enables header tagging.
- Default: disabled.
- If a request fails due to proxy/header rejection (4xx at proxy), templates should log a user-facing warning suggesting disabling tagging.
sections.heading: Enable/disable behavior

sections.body:
- Gateway will allowlist these headers and persist them into request metadata for analytics (not logs by default).
- For Private deployments, customers can choose to drop these headers at ingress; templates should continue functioning.

---
sections.heading: Gateway handling

sections.body: Dashboards will be built in Console/Analytics and must be reviewable by DevEx, PM, and Support. This section defines each dashboard, required charts, and filters.
sections.heading: KPI dashboard definitions (Console)

sections.body:
**Primary questions:** Are templates being started? Are users reaching first success quickly?

**Charts**
1) Template Starts
- Metric: count of `quickstart_template_init`
- Breakdown: `template_language`, `scaffolder`

2) Activation Rate (24h)
- Metric: % of `install_id` with `quickstart_first_success` within 24h of init
- Breakdown: `template_language`

3) TTFS (p50/p90)
- Metric: distribution of (first_success_ts - init_ts)
- Breakdown: `template_language`

4) Doctor Health Outcomes
- Metric: count of `quickstart_doctor_result`
- Breakdown: `result`

**Filters**
- Date range
- Language
- Template version
sections.heading: Dashboard 1: “Quickstart Templates — Adoption & Activation”

sections.body:
**Primary questions:** Where do users fail before first success and how do we fix it?

**Charts**
1) Top error categories
- Metric: count of `quickstart_request_failed` before first success
- Breakdown: `error_category`

2) Rate limit / quota issues
- Metric: count of `quickstart_request_failed` where `error_category in (rate_limit, quota)`
- Breakdown: `http_status`, `template_language`

3) Streaming disconnect rate
- Metric: `stream_disconnect` / total streaming attempts
- Breakdown: language

4) Tool schema failures
- Metric: count of `tool_schema`
- Breakdown: template_version
sections.heading: Dashboard 2: “Quickstart Templates — Failure Modes (First Run)”

sections.body:
**Primary questions:** Do template apps keep using Redwood?

**Prereq:** tagging enabled by developer (header-based attribution).

**Charts**
1) Weekly Active Apps (tagged)
- Metric: distinct `install_id` with ≥ 1 successful request (rolling 7d)

2) D7 / D30 retention
- Metric: cohort retention based on first success week

3) Token economics (tagged traffic)
- Metric: tokens in/out aggregated for tagged traffic
- Breakdown: model_family (coarse)

---
sections.heading: Dashboard 3: “Quickstart Templates — Retention (Tagged Apps)”

sections.body:
- `quickstart_request_success`: sampled at 1% (configurable).
- `quickstart_request_failed`: emit at 100% until first success; after first success sample at 10%.
- `quickstart_first_success`: always emit.
- CLI events: always emit (low volume).

---
sections.heading: To avoid excessive telemetry volume

sections.body:
- Docs-site analytics: `quickstart_docs_*` events.
- CLI telemetry: `quickstart_template_init`, `quickstart_doctor_*`.
- Template runtime telemetry: `quickstart_env_check`, `quickstart_first_success`, `quickstart_request_*`.
- Gateway attribution: header allowlist and metadata persistence for Console filtering.
sections.heading: Sources

sections.body:
- Primary key: `install_id` (UUID, generated at init).
- We DO NOT attempt to correlate to a Redwood user identity at v1 in this spec. Account-level rollups can be derived from request auth on the backend (internal only).

---
sections.heading: Correlation strategy

sections.body:
**Must-haves**
- No prompts, documents, tool args, or file paths in telemetry payloads.
- No full URLs (only docs page path + referrer domain).
- No IP addresses captured in template-side telemetry.
- Install ID is random UUID; not derived from hostnames, usernames, or repo paths.

**Review gates**
- Security review sign-off (Marcus Lin) for field allowlist.
- Observability review sign-off (Allison Grant) to ensure no high-cardinality metric labels.
- Support review (Dev Patel) to ensure error categories align with troubleshooting taxonomy.

---
sections.heading: Privacy, security, and compliance checklist

sections.body:
1) GitHub template starts: do we have a reliable mechanism to emit `quickstart_template_init` without CLI? (Option: a one-time “postinstall” script that is clearly disclosed and can be disabled.)
2) Private deployments: do customers want the ability to disable all analytics events while still allowing OTel traces/metrics? If so, define `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE=off|minimal|full`.
3) Versioning: confirm whether template version should reflect repo release tag or CLI scaffold version stamp (prefer scaffold stamp written into project).

---
sections.heading: Open questions (to resolve before GA)

sections.body:
- 2025-03-11: Made traffic tagging explicitly opt-in; clarified header set and proxy compatibility rationale.
- 2025-03-03: Added retention dashboard definitions and sampling guidelines.
- 2025-02-14: Initial v1 spec drafted for PM-912.
