payload.page_title: Adaptive Token Budgeting and Pricing Modes — Design Spec

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This design spec describes the Adaptive Token Budgeting subsystem and associated Pricing Modes to make per-route and per-tenant token economics flexible, predictable, and SLO-aligned. The goal is to enable customers and internal systems to select tradeoffs between latency, cost, and quality through an explicit budgeting API and backend billing primitives.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Config surface for routes and tenants to express token budgets and pricing mode.
- Runtime enforcement and accounting hooks in the serving runtime to decrement budgets and emit metrics.
- Billing integration that maps budget consumption to invoiceable units and credits.
- UI/Console representation and rollout steps.

Non-goals: internal-only rate limiting (existing quota system remains); deep ML model changes; user-facing experiments outside configured modes.

Background and motivation

Redwood currently charges primarily per-token and via reserved capacity contracts. Customers building latency-sensitive features request more predictable per-route economics tied to SLOs (e.g., 95th percentile latency < 120ms) and per-feature budgets (e.g., chat sessions capped at 1,000 tokens/day). Existing approaches are either too coarse (account-level token bundles) or too brittle (static per-request limits).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Explicit budgets that can be bound to a route, API key, or tenant.
- Pricing modes that change how budget consumption maps to billable tokens (flat token accounting, SLO-backed creditization, and hybrid subscription models).
- Runtime signals (latency, tail, error-rate, model fallback) to dynamically adjust effective spend rates to protect SLOs and cost targets.

Goals and success metrics
sections.heading: Adaptive Token Budgeting introduces

sections.body:
1) Allow product teams and customers to declare per-route/tenant token budgets and pricing mode.
2) Ensure billing accuracy within 0.5% of serving accounting for budgets-enabled routes.
3) Reduce cost-per-request for bursty workloads by >= 12% via intelligent remapping (within 6 months of rollout).
4) Provide tooling to convert current token bundles into budgeting constructs with < 5% migration delta.
sections.heading: Primary goals

sections.body:
- Percentage of paid requests routed through a pricing-mode (target 30% in 6 months).
- Billing reconciliation delta (target <= 0.5%).
- Customer-reported latency regressions attributable to budgeting toggles (target < 1%).

High-level design
sections.heading: Success metrics (sample)

sections.body:
- Budgeting API (admin): /v1/budgets (create, update, delete, preview)
- Enforcement library: thin runtime hook inside the serving runtime to decrement budgets, consult pricing mode, and emit accounting events
- Pricing Engine: maps accounting events to billing line-items according to mode and rules
- Console: UI to visualize budgets, projected spend, and SLO impact
- Reconciliation service: asynchronous job that verifies usage events against billing tables nightly
sections.heading: Components

sections.body:
1) fixed_token: straightforward tokens-in/tokens-out pricing. Accounting event = tokens_consumed.
2) slo_credits: budgets are denominated in SLO credits. Credits are consumed at a variable rate based on runtime signal (e.g., high tail latency -> credit burn increases). Billing maps credits to invoiceable token-equivalents at periodic conversion.
3) buffered_subscription: subscription seat or capacity that provides a discounted effective per-token rate after a fixed monthly commitment; budget prevents overspend beyond allowed burst credits.
4) hybrid: per-route rules that mix modes (e.g., warm path fixed_token, cold path slo_credits).

Configuration model (example)
sections.heading: Pricing modes (supported)
Config object (JSON example)

sections.body:
| field | type | description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| route | string | Route path or matcher |
| scope | enum | route|key|tenant |
| mode | enum | fixed_token|slo_credits|buffered_subscription|hybrid |
| budget_amount | integer | numeric budget for period in mode units |
| budget_period | string | ISO period for budget reset |
| slo_target | object | SLO target(s) used for adjustment decisions |
| fallback_policy | enum | allow|throttle|fallback| |
| adjustment_policy | object | Runtime adjustment tuning parameters |

Runtime enforcement and events

At request completion, the serving runtime will emit an accounting event to the Budgeting topic (Kafka):
- event fields: timestamp, route_id, tenant_id, api_key, tokens_input, tokens_output, model_variant, latency_ms, status, applied_mode, effective_budget_units_consumed
sections.heading: Config table

sections.body:
1) Lookup budget config by route/key/tenant precedence.
2) Evaluate adjustment_policy against observed signals (latency_ms, error_rate).
3) Compute effective_consumption = base_token_count * mode_multiplier (mode-dependent).
4) Atomically decrement budget; if insufficient, apply fallback_policy.
5) Emit accounting event and metrics (budget_remaining, burn_rate, last_adjustment).
sections.heading: The Enforcement library behavior (pseudocode)

sections.body:
- fixed_token: 1.0
- slo_credits: variable (1.0 -> 3.0 depending on stress signals)
- buffered_subscription: 0.6 (discount factor) until subscription cap reached

API and Console UX
sections.heading: Mode multipliers (example)

sections.body:
- POST /v1/budgets  -> create or preview config
- GET /v1/budgets/{id} -> current state and projected spend
- PATCH /v1/budgets/{id} -> change mode/budget/fallback
- POST /v1/budgets/{id}/preview -> simulate N requests and report cost & SLO impact
sections.heading: Admin API endpoints (surface)

sections.body:
- Budget Summary (percentage consumed, forecasted burn)
- What-if Preview (simulate different traffic shapes and adjustment settings)
- Billing Impact (translated to invoiceable units)

Telemetry and SLOs
sections.heading: Console screens

sections.body:
- redwood.budget_remaining{route,tenant,mode} gauge
- redwood.budget_burn_rate_per_min{route,tenant,mode} gauge
- redwood.budget_adjustments_total{route,tenant,policy} counter
- redwood.budget_denied_requests_total{route,tenant,reason} counter
- redwood.budget_accounting_delta{route,tenant} gauge (nightly reconciliation diff)

SLO contracts and enforcement policies (recommended defaults):
- p95_latency_ms <= 120 for latency-sensitive chat routes
- error_rate <= 0.5%
- budget_reconciliation_delta <= 0.5% monthly

Billing integration and invoice mapping
sections.heading: Metrics to emit per budget-enabled route (prometheus names)

sections.body:
- fixed_token: invoice line = tokens_consumed * token_rate
- slo_credits: invoice line = credits_converted * credit_conversion_rate (conversion window: daily close)
- buffered_subscription: base_monthly_fee + overage = (committed_tokens*discount_rate) + overage_tokens*standard_rate

Reconciliation and auditing
sections.heading: Mapping rules (examples)

sections.body:
1) Aggregate accounting events and produce aggregate consumption per budget id.
2) Cross-check against billing ledger; compute budget_accounting_delta.
3) If delta > 0.5%, create an investigation ticket and tag affected customers.

Rollout plan

Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks):
- Internal pilot with platform routes only.
- Validation of enforcement hooks and event schema.
- Manual reconciliation checks.

Phase 1 (beta customers, 8–12 weeks):
- Onboard 3–5 customers across use cases (chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Enable only fixed_token and buffered_subscription modes initially.
- Provide migration tool to translate token bundles.

Phase 2 (SLO-backed modes, 12–16 weeks):
- Open slo_credits and hybrid mode.
- Monitor billing delta and tail latency.
- Add UI previews and automated conversion tool.
sections.heading: Nightly job responsibilities

sections.body:
- Full rollout, doc updates, and pricing page changes.
- SLA and support plan updates.

Migration and backward compatibility

- Existing token bundles: migration tool will compute an equivalent budget in fixed_token mode; customers can opt-in to change modes.
- Fallback: default to existing quota system when budget system is unavailable (circuit breaker).

Security, privacy, and compliance

- Budget configs considered customer metadata — include KMS-backed storage for sensitive fields.
- Accounting events contain no PII; API keys are hashed before being emitted to Kafka.
- Audit logs retained consistent with data-retention policy; include export path for compliance customers.

Operational runbook (short)
sections.heading: Phase 3 (GA)

sections.body:
1) budget_accounting_delta > 0.5% for > 24h -> paging to Billing SRE
2) budget_denied_requests_total spike -> page Platform Oncall (possible config bug)
3) nightly_reconciliation_job_fail -> page Data Platform
sections.heading: Common alert triggers

sections.body:
1) For mis-billed customer: run manual aggregate and create invoice credit; revert budgets if rollout caused regression.
2) For enforcement hotpath failures: toggle budgeting circuit-breaker for affected cluster; monitor error rates.

Security review checklist: handled (encryption at rest, encrypted audit trail, role-based UI access).

Open design questions and tradeoffs

- Conversion cadence for slo_credits -> invoiceable tokens (daily vs hourly).
- Precise conversion algorithm: linear vs tiered conversion rates under stress.
- UI UX: how much control to expose to customers for adjustment policy tuning.

Risks

- Misconfiguration could cause customer downtime (mitigation: preview + safeties).
- Billing reconciliation complexity increases (mitigation: nightly reconciliation and manual override).

Ownership and next steps
sections.heading: Quick recovery steps

sections.body:
- Product: Asha Iyer (spec lead)
- Engineering: Daniel Kline (runtime), Priya Nair (billing engine)
- SRE/Billing: Evan Zhou
sections.heading: Owners

sections.body:
1) Finalize event schema and enforcement library API.
2) Implement budget create/preview API and Console mockups.
3) Prepare pilot plan and select internal routes.

Appendices

Appendix A — Example CLI commands
$ redwood admin budgets create --route "/v1/chat" --mode slo_credits --budget 10000 --period P1M --slo.p95_latency_ms=120

Appendix B — Example accounting event (JSON)
{"timestamp":"2026-12-12T08:23:12Z","route":"/v1/chat","tenant_id":"acct_1234","tokens_input":12,"tokens_output":128,"latency_ms":98,"status":"ok","applied_mode":"slo_credits","effective_budget_units_consumed":64}

Appendix C — QA checklist
- Unit tests for enforcement library multipliers and atomic decrement
- Integration test with billing conversion job
- End-to-end simulation with what-if traffic shapes
- Console preview matches server-side projection within 2%

References
- product-pricing/ratecard (internal)
- /confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/token-bundle-flex-enterprise-metering-2026-08-20
- /confluence/product-docs/requirements/per-route-slo-creditization-and-billing-prd-2027-09-15
sections.heading: Next steps (first 30 days)

payload.page_title: Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA) — Design Spec

sections.body:
This document specifies the end-to-end user experience for **Hosted canary rollouts** in Redwood Console (GA scope): creating a rollout, progressing traffic steps, pausing, requesting/receiving approvals, and rolling back. It includes screen-by-screen behavior, validation rules, empty/error states, and the key UI-to-backend interactions.

Hosted canary rollouts enable customers to safely introduce a new model version/config on a **Hosted route** by gradually shifting a percentage of traffic from a **baseline** (current production) to a **canary** (new version/config), with policy guardrails and automatic stop/rollback based on SLO signals.
sections.heading: 1. Overview

sections.body:
- Provide a **GA-ready wizard** to create a canary rollout on a Hosted route.
- Provide a **Rollout details** experience that supports: start, step forward, pause/resume, rollback, and approvals.
- Provide **clear metrics comparisons** between baseline and canary cohorts.
- Surface **policy guardrails** (max step size, min soak, approvals required) clearly and early.
- Provide **auditable, customer-visible activity timeline** (who did what, when, and why where available).
sections.heading: 1.1 Goals

sections.body:
- Automatic dynamic optimization (bandits) or step sizing.
- Full automated quality gating as a hard requirement (quality inputs may be displayed/linked if customer provides them).
- Dedicated/Private rollout UX parity (ensure concepts and language don’t block future parity).
sections.heading: 1.2 Non-goals (GA)

sections.body:
- **Operator / ML engineer**: wants to ship a new model version safely and quickly with clear rollback.
- **Platform admin / security**: needs approvals, auditability, and predictable controls.
- **SRE / on-call**: needs obvious stop reasons, safe backout, and consistent incident breadcrumbs.
sections.heading: 1.3 Primary personas

sections.body:
- **Route**: a Hosted API route (e.g., `support-agent-prod`) configured with a model + settings.
- **Baseline**: the currently active model version/config that receives non-canary traffic.
- **Canary**: the proposed model version/config to test.
- **Cohort**: baseline vs canary request group (deterministic assignment).
- **Step**: a planned traffic percentage and soak duration (e.g., 5% for 30 minutes).
- **Soak**: the time the system should run at a step before allowing progression.
- **Guardrails**: policy constraints (step size limits, min soak time, approvals).
- **Stop condition**: thresholds on SLO signals that automatically pause or rollback.

---
sections.heading: 1.4 Definitions (customer-visible terminology)

sections.body:
1) **Route details page** → “Rollouts” tab → “Create canary rollout”
2) **Console global navigation** → “Rollouts” (new top-level page for tenants with feature enabled) → “Create rollout”
sections.heading: 2.1 Entry points

sections.body:
- **Rollouts list** (table view): all rollouts for the tenant; filters by route/status.
- **Create rollout wizard** (multi-step): route selection → choose baseline/canary → schedule → guardrails/approvals → review.
- **Rollout details**: current step, controls (start/step/pause/rollback), timeline/activity, metrics comparison.

---
sections.heading: 2.2 Main screens

sections.body:
- The UI is gated behind `hosted_canary_rollouts_enabled` (tenant-level flag).
- If the feature is disabled:
  - Hide “Rollouts” nav and route tab.
  - If user hits a deep link, show an access page: “Rollouts not enabled for this workspace” with “Contact support” CTA.
sections.heading: 3.1 Feature availability

sections.body:
The UI must preflight and clearly message permission failures.
- **Create rollout**: requires `rollouts.create`.
- **Start rollout**: requires `rollouts.start`.
- **Progress step / change traffic**: requires `rollouts.progress`.
- **Pause/resume**: requires `rollouts.pause` / `rollouts.resume`.
- **Rollback**: requires `rollouts.rollback`.
- **Approve** (if required by policy): requires `rollouts.approve` (e.g., “rollout-approver” role).

UX rule: If the user lacks permission for an action, the action button is hidden where possible; otherwise disabled with tooltip “You don’t have permission to do this. Ask an admin to grant: <permission>.”

---
sections.heading: 3.2 RBAC actions (high-level)

sections.body:
- Keep a **sticky right-side summary panel** with key selections: route, baseline, canary, schedule, guardrails, approval requirement.
- Validate early and inline; reserve blocking errors for final “Review & confirm”.
- Every step supports **Back/Next**; `Next` is disabled until required fields are satisfied.
- Save as draft only if we can reliably persist partial configuration; GA behavior: do not persist until final submit. (Follow-up: draft saving.)
sections.heading: Wizard design principles

sections.body: **Purpose:** Choose the Hosted route to roll out.
sections.heading: Step 1: Select route

sections.body:
- Searchable dropdown/table list of Hosted routes.
- Route row shows: route name, current model, region mode (single/multi), last updated.
sections.heading: UI elements

sections.body: - Route (exactly one).
sections.heading: Required input

sections.body:
- Route must be Hosted (not Dedicated/Private).
- Route must be eligible for rollouts (backend provides `rollout_eligible: true/false` and a reason).
sections.heading: Validations

sections.body: - If no Hosted routes exist: “No Hosted routes yet” with CTA “Create route”.
sections.heading: Empty state

sections.body:
- If routes cannot be fetched: inline error with retry.
- If selected route becomes ineligible after selection (rare): show blocking banner “This route can’t be rolled out right now: <reason>.” Provide “Choose another route”.
sections.heading: Error state

sections.body: **Purpose:** Define the baseline and the target canary configuration.
sections.heading: Step 2: Choose baseline & canary

sections.body:
- Two side-by-side cards:
  - **Baseline** card (read-only by default; prefilled with current route config)
  - **Canary** card (select model version/config)
sections.heading: UI layout

sections.body:
- Baseline defaults to current pinned model version/config on the route at time of wizard load.
- If the route uses “floating” model aliasing (e.g., `llama-3.x-latest`), show a warning: “Baseline uses a moving target. Pin a version for predictable rollouts.” Provide inline action “Pin baseline to current resolved version” (if user has permission).
sections.heading: Baseline rules

sections.body:
- Choose model (catalog) and version.
- Choose config differences (where supported): quantization/profile, max tokens, safety settings, tool-calling toggles (exact set based on current Hosted route configuration options).
sections.heading: Canary selection

sections.body: - Canary model + version.
sections.heading: Required fields

sections.body:
- Canary must be compatible with route mode (e.g., chat vs completion).
- Canary cannot be identical to baseline; if identical, show inline error “Canary matches baseline. Choose a different version or configuration.”
- Backend policy preflight can mark certain combinations as denied (e.g., disallowed model family); surface error as “Not allowed by workspace policy: <message>.”
sections.heading: Validations

sections.body: **Purpose:** Define step progression plan.
sections.heading: Step 3: Traffic schedule

sections.body:
- Preset schedule templates (radio buttons):
  - Conservative: 1% → 5% → 10% → 25% → 50% → 100%
  - Standard: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%
  - Custom: editable step list
- Step list table:
  - Step #
  - Canary traffic %
  - Soak duration (minutes/hours)
  - “Requires approval” indicator (derived; see Step 4)
sections.heading: UI elements

sections.body:
- Default template = “Standard”. Default soak time per step = 30 min (adjustable).

Validation rules (UI + backend):
- Percent must be integer 0–100.
- Steps must be strictly increasing, ending at 100%.
- Minimum 2 steps (GA requirement: at least one canary step before 100%).
- Max number of steps: 10 (to reduce complexity).
- Policy constraints:
  - Max step jump (e.g., cannot go 5% → 50% if max jump is 25%).
  - Minimum soak time per step (e.g., at least 15 minutes).
sections.heading: Defaults

sections.body:
- Show a “Policy guardrails” callout at the top of this step:
  - “Max step increase: <X>%”
  - “Minimum soak: <Y> minutes”
  - “Approvals required: <Yes/No> (see next step)”
sections.heading: Policy messaging

sections.body:
- If a step violates policy, show red inline error on that row, and disable Next.
- If backend policy service is unavailable, allow user to continue but show blocking validation at Step 5 (Review) before submission. Copy: “We couldn’t verify policy guardrails right now. You can continue, but you won’t be able to start the rollout until validation succeeds.”
sections.heading: Error states

sections.body: **Purpose:** Configure stop conditions and understand approvals required.
sections.heading: Step 4: Guardrails & approvals

sections.body:
1) **Automatic stop / rollback**
2) **Approval gates**
3) **Notifications** (GA-lite: choose recipients or default workspace notification settings)
sections.heading: Sections

sections.body:
- Toggle: “Automatically pause on SLO breach” (default ON)
- Toggle: “Automatically rollback on severe breach” (default ON if policy allows)
- Threshold preview (read-only defaults may be policy-controlled):
  - 5xx error rate delta (canary vs baseline)
  - Timeout rate
  - p95 latency regression
sections.heading: UI toggles and fields

sections.body: - Customers can select from “Default (recommended)” vs “Custom thresholds” only if they have `rollouts.thresholds.edit` permission and workspace policy allows customization.
sections.heading: Recommended GA interaction

sections.body:
- Thresholds must be within allowed bounds (policy-defined min/max).
- If customer selects “Custom” but lacks permission, revert to Default and show toast “Custom thresholds require admin permission.”
sections.heading: Validation

sections.body:
UI:
- Section header: “Approvals”
- If policy requires approvals for certain actions (e.g., starting rollout, moving beyond 25%, rolling back): show a non-editable summary list:
  - “Start rollout: approval required”
  - “Increase traffic above 25%: approval required”
  - “Rollback: approval required” (if applicable)
- If approvals are optional (policy allows): provide toggle “Require approval to progress steps” with explanation.
sections.heading: 4.2 Approval gates

sections.body: - The wizard does not collect approver names; approvals are role-based (rollout-approver). We display: “Any user with the Rollout Approver role can approve.”
sections.heading: Interaction detail

sections.body:
- Default behavior: notify workspace admins + rollout creator.
- Optional: add additional emails/users (if supported by existing notification system).
sections.heading: 4.3 Notifications

sections.body:
**Purpose:** Final validation and commit.

UI:
- Read-only summary of:
  - Route
  - Baseline config
  - Canary config
  - Traffic schedule
  - Stop/rollback settings
  - Approval requirements
- “Create rollout” button.
sections.heading: Step 5: Review & confirm

sections.body:
- Re-run policy evaluation for:
  - Create
  - Start eligibility (even if not starting now)
  - Schedule compliance
  - Approval requirements
- Confirm route has not materially changed since Step 2:
  - If baseline differs from current route config, show a blocking warning: “This route changed since you started the wizard.” Options:
    - “Update baseline to current route” (recommended)
    - “Continue with original baseline” (requires explicit confirm; may be denied by policy)
sections.heading: Submit-time validations (must be blocking)

sections.body:
- After create: redirect to Rollout details page with a success banner “Rollout created. Ready to start.”

---
sections.heading: Success

sections.body:
- Title: “Canary rollout: <route name>”
- Status pill: Draft / Running / Paused / Waiting for approval / Rolled back / Completed / Failed
- Key metadata row:
  - Baseline version
  - Canary version
  - Current canary %
  - Current step soak remaining (if applicable)
  - Created by + timestamp
sections.heading: 5.1 Page header

sections.body: Actions displayed depend on state and permissions. Buttons should be consistent in placement to reduce operational mistakes.
sections.heading: 5.2 Primary action bar

sections.body:
- **Start rollout** (Draft)
- **Request approval** (if required and user lacks approve permission)
- **Approve** / **Reject** (visible to approvers when approval is pending)
- **Increase traffic (Next step)** (Running)
- **Pause** (Running)
- **Resume** (Paused)
- **Rollback** (Running/Paused/Waiting)
sections.heading: Common actions

sections.body: - Rollback requires confirmation modal and typed route name for rollouts above 25% (policy-driven).
sections.heading: Destructive action protection

sections.body:
1) **Overview** (default): step progression + current health
2) **Metrics**: baseline vs canary comparisons
3) **Timeline & activity**: customer-visible timeline and audit-like log
4) **Settings** (read-only summary for GA; editing post-create is out of scope except rollback/stop toggles if permitted)

---
sections.heading: 5.3 Main content tabs

sections.body:
- Step indicator: “Step 2 of 5”
- “Canary traffic: 25%”
- Soak timer: “Soak: 18m remaining (min 30m)” or “Soak complete”
- Health snapshot (last 15m):
  - error rate delta
  - p95 latency delta
  - timeouts delta
sections.heading: At top of Overview

sections.body:
When user clicks “Increase traffic”:
1) If min soak not satisfied, block and show message: “Minimum soak time not reached. Try again in <time>.”
2) If next step exceeds an approval threshold:
   - If user is approver: show confirm modal “Approve and apply next step (50%)?”
   - If user is not approver: clicking triggers “Request approval” flow (see Section 7)
3) On success: show toast “Traffic updated to 50% canary.”
sections.heading: 6.2 Progressing to next step

sections.body: - Show blocking modal with the policy message and a link “View policy details” (opens a side panel with the evaluated constraints and suggested resolution).
sections.heading: If the policy engine denies the step

sections.body:
Pause is always immediate (no approval unless policy requires it).
- Modal copy:
  - Title: “Pause rollout?”
  - Body: “Traffic will remain at the current split until you resume or rollback.”
  - Optional field: “Reason (shown in timeline)”
sections.heading: 6.3 Pausing

sections.body:
Resume re-enters Running state without changing traffic.
- If resume is denied by policy, show banner with the denial reason.

---
sections.heading: 6.4 Resume

sections.body: Approvals are modeled as explicit workflow states and actions.
sections.heading: 7. Approval flows (request, approve, reject)

sections.body:
- Starting the rollout
- Increasing traffic above a threshold
- Rollback
- Disabling auto-rollback (if allowed at all)

The UI must treat approvals as **hard gates**:
- Non-approvers can initiate a request but cannot proceed.
sections.heading: Approvals may be required by policy for

sections.body:
- Clicking a gated action (Start / Next step / Rollback)
- Dedicated “Request approval” button in header when state is Waiting for approval
sections.heading: Entry points

sections.body:
- Action requested (read-only): e.g., “Increase traffic to 50%”
- Optional message: “Context for approver”
- Notify: default approver group (read-only) + optional additional recipients
sections.heading: Modal fields

sections.body:
- Rollout enters **Waiting for approval** state.
- Banner appears: “Waiting for approval to increase traffic to 50%.”
- Activity log entry is appended.
sections.heading: After submit

sections.body:
- Banner with requested action and message.
- Buttons: “Approve” (primary) and “Reject” (secondary).
sections.heading: Approver sees

sections.body:
- Shows what will happen (traffic change or rollback) and any risk callouts (e.g., “Traffic will go from 25% → 50%.”)
- Optional reason/comment (logged).
sections.heading: Approve modal

sections.body: - Required reason (logged and visible to requester).
sections.heading: Reject modal

sections.body:
- If approved: the system performs the requested action and returns to Running/Paused as appropriate.
- If rejected: system returns to prior state (e.g., Running at current split) and displays banner “Approval rejected: <reason>.”

Edge case: approval expires
- If policy includes an approval TTL (optional): show “Approval request expired” and require a new request.

---
sections.heading: Post-action behavior

sections.body: - Header action bar: “Rollback”
sections.heading: Rollback entry points

sections.body:
- Title: “Rollback canary rollout?”
- Explanation: “This will route 100% of traffic back to baseline and end the rollout.”
- Options (radio):
  1) “Rollback to baseline (100%)” (default)
  2) “Rollback to previous step” (only if supported by orchestrator; if not supported, omit)
- Optional reason field (shown in timeline)
- If policy requires approval: modal becomes “Request rollback approval” for non-approvers.
sections.heading: Rollback modal

sections.body:
- Status becomes “Rolled back”.
- Show persistent banner: “Rolled back to baseline at <timestamp>.”
- Primary CTA becomes “Create new rollout” (pre-fills route and baseline).
sections.heading: After rollback

sections.body:
- The page shows a high-severity banner:
  - “Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach” OR “Rolled back automatically due to severe SLO breach”
  - Include: metric(s) that triggered, time window, and link “View details in Metrics”.
- In Timeline, record an entry with actor = “System” and include trigger details.

If the system fails to evaluate metrics (e.g., telemetry outage):
- Do not auto-rollback purely due to missing data.
- Optionally auto-pause if policy says “pause on unknown” (default OFF for GA). If paused, banner: “Paused because metrics are temporarily unavailable.”

---
sections.heading: When stop conditions trigger

sections.body: Help users decide whether to proceed, pause, or rollback by comparing cohort health and performance.
sections.heading: 9.1 Purpose

sections.body:
- Time range selector: last 15m / 1h / 6h / custom
- Region selector (if multi-region): All regions (default) + per-region breakdown
- Cohort legend: Baseline (blue) vs Canary (orange)
sections.heading: 9.2 Layout

sections.body:
- Request rate (RPS)
- 5xx error rate
- Timeout rate
- Latency p50/p95
- Tokens/sec or throughput proxy (where available)
sections.heading: Charts (GA-required)

sections.body: - “Compare cohorts over the same time window. Small canary sizes may produce noisy metrics.”
sections.heading: Guidance text (compact)

sections.body:
- If canary traffic is 0% (Draft): show empty state “No canary traffic yet. Start the rollout to see comparisons.”
- If data is delayed: show banner “Metrics may be delayed by up to 2 minutes.”
- If baseline or canary has insufficient volume: show warning “Low sample size — interpret with caution.”
sections.heading: 9.3 Empty and partial states

sections.body:
- Telemetry unavailable: show error panel with retry; keep Rollout controls available.
- Region mismatch: if a region has no canary capacity, show “No canary traffic in <region> (capacity not available)” and link to troubleshooting.

---
sections.heading: 9.4 Error states

sections.body:
- Provide a chronological story of the rollout.
- Mirror audit events at a user-friendly level (without exposing sensitive internal IDs).
sections.heading: 10.1 Timeline goals

sections.body:
- “Rollout created” (actor + timestamp)
- “Rollout started (1% canary)”
- “Traffic increased to 5%”
- “Paused by <user> (reason)”
- “Approval requested for 50% step”
- “Approved by <user>” / “Rejected by <user> (reason)”
- “Auto-paused due to p95 latency regression” (System)
- “Rolled back to baseline” (manual/system)
sections.heading: 10.2 Timeline entries (examples)

sections.body:
- Each entry expands to show:
  - Actor
  - Action
  - Optional comment/reason
  - Links: “View metrics around this time” (applies a time window)
sections.heading: 10.3 Interaction details

sections.body:
- Timeline retains entries for at least the rollout’s lifetime + standard Console retention; audit logs follow security retention policy (separate).

---
sections.heading: Retention note

sections.body: This section defines user-facing error strings and where they appear.
sections.heading: 11. Validation & error messaging (canonical list)

sections.body:
- Route required: “Select a route to continue.”
- Canary required: “Select a canary model and version.”
- Canary equals baseline: “Canary must differ from baseline.”
- Invalid schedule: “Steps must increase and end at 100%.”
- Policy denied: “Not allowed by workspace policy: <policy_message>.”
sections.heading: 11.1 Wizard validations

sections.body:
- Min soak not met: “Minimum soak time not reached. Try again in <time>.”
- Approval required: “Approval required to proceed. Request approval to continue.”
- Action conflict (optimistic concurrency): “Rollout changed while you were viewing this page. Refresh and try again.”
- Data plane enforcement issue (rare but critical): “Traffic split could not be applied. Rollout is paused. Contact support if this persists.”
sections.heading: 11.2 Runtime validations

sections.body:
- Inline field errors for user-correctable issues.
- Page-level banner for state issues (policy, approvals, system actions).
- Blocking modal for destructive actions and gated approvals.

---
sections.heading: 11.3 Standard error UI patterns

sections.body:
- All charts and status indicators must have text equivalents.
- Buttons must include clear labels (avoid ambiguous “Continue” in action bar; use “Increase traffic”, “Rollback”, etc.).
- Confirmation dialogs must use explicit language (“Rollback to baseline”) and never default to destructive without a clear primary/secondary distinction.

---
sections.heading: 12. Accessibility & safety

sections.body: This section is descriptive (not an API spec) to ensure UX assumptions are supported.
sections.heading: 13. UI ↔ backend integration (contract expectations)

sections.body:
- Create rollout with baseline/canary configs + schedule + guardrails.
- Policy evaluation endpoint that returns:
  - Allowed/denied
  - Denial reason suitable for end-user display
  - Derived constraints (max jump, min soak, approvals required)
- Rollout state machine with explicit states:
  - Draft, Running, Paused, WaitingForApproval, Completed, RolledBack, Failed
- Action endpoints:
  - start, progress_to_step, pause, resume, request_approval, approve, reject, rollback
- Event emission for timeline + audit logs.
- Metrics tagging by rollout_id + cohort (baseline/canary) with controlled cardinality.
sections.heading: 13.1 Required backend capabilities

sections.body:
- Rollout details page should poll state every 10–15s while Running/WaitingForApproval, and every 30–60s otherwise.
- Metrics view should query with a small delay to avoid flicker; show “updated <time> ago”.

---
sections.heading: 13.2 Loading & polling

sections.body:
1) Do we support “Rollback to previous step” in GA, or always rollback to baseline 100%?
2) Should approvals be step-specific (approve exactly 50%) vs approve “progress step” generically? (Current design assumes step-specific.)
3) Do we need a “dry run” preview showing expected cohort counts per region? (Likely post-GA.)
4) Should we expose cohort assignment method details (hash key) in UI? (Current: no, keep internal; expose only behavior guarantees.)

---
sections.heading: 14. Open questions / follow-ups

sections.body: “Canary traffic is real production traffic. Start with a small percentage and ensure stop conditions are enabled.”
sections.heading: A.1 Risk warning (schedule step)

sections.body: “Canary volume is low. Metrics may be noisy; consider increasing canary traffic gradually or extending soak time.”
sections.heading: A.2 Low sample size warning (metrics)

sections.body: “Your workspace policy blocked this action. If you believe this is incorrect, contact an admin or support and include the rollout ID.”
sections.heading: A.3 Policy denial help

payload.page_title: Variant hot-swap: zero-downtime model variant hot-swap design spec

sections.body:
Overview
======
This design spec describes the Variant Hot-Swap system: a runtime capability that allows swapping a serving model variant with zero client-visible downtime and bounded impact to SLOs. Hot-swap covers both in-place binary/weights replacement on a host and coordinated cross-host handoff for multi-replica services. The goal is to support fast rollbacks, emergency variant patches, and model upgrades without dropping connections or causing request errors.

Context and motivation
----------------------
- Customers require predictable service levels during model rollouts. Traditional rolling restarts or drain-and-replace strategies cause request queueing, increased latency, or transient errors.
- We already support progressive rollouts (canaries, staged traffic shifting). Hot-swap is a complementary capability targeted at: emergency rollbacks, tiny-critical fixes to a model in prod, and metadata-driven in-server variant swaps for affinity-sensitive sessions.

Goals
-----
1. Zero client-connection interruption for active sessions during a variant swap.
2. Maintain per-tenant latency 95th percentile within a configurable delta (default +200ms) during swaps.
3. Guarantee token-consistency for streaming sessions: no duplicated or missing tokens delivered to the client.
4. Support seamless rollback to the previous variant within 30s under normal conditions.
5. Provide observability hooks and automated runbook triggers on SLO deviations.

Non-goals
---------
- Solving stateful model weight warmup for very large models (>1TB) in sub-minute timelines. For very large variants, hot-swap will default to a staged cross-host approach rather than in-memory replace.
- Replacing major architecture changes that require incompatible runtime kernels; those will use progressive rolling upgrade paths.

Stakeholders and ownership
--------------------------
- Product: Model delivery and runtime experience (primary contact: Elena Moreno).
- Engineering: Serving runtime (owner), rollout orchestration, and SRE (SLO/alerting).
- Applied ML: Variant packaging constraints and validation tests.
- Customer Success: Communication templates for emergency changes.

High-level design
-----------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- HotSwap Controller (stateless service): accepts swap requests, validates policy, coordinates with orchestrator.
- Local Swap Agent (per-host): performs in-memory swap when safe, handles KV-cache migration, and sequences drain flags for local threads.
- Session Coordinator (distributed): ensures streaming sessions' token state is checkpointed and resumed without duplication across variant boundaries.
- Fallback Manager: enforces automatic rollback policies if SLO/health signals cross thresholds.

Sequence flows (in-place hot-swap)
---------------------------------
1. Operator or automated job creates a HotSwap request with target variant id, prewarm hints, and rollout policy.
2. HotSwap Controller verifies compatibility matrix and quota checks.
3. Controller instructs candidate hosts' Local Swap Agent to prewarm weights into an isolated address space (worker pool).
4. Local Swap Agent loads weights into standby workers, runs validation prompt set (configurable), and warms KV caches for prefix patterns if provided.
5. When 90% of standby workers pass validation, Controller issues a coordinated handoff:
   a. Mark new workers as READY and old workers as TRANSITIONING.
   b. Session Coordinator freezes streaming token emission checkpoint per-session.
   c. Router starts routing new requests to READY workers.
   d. For active streaming sessions, last-token markers are emitted, session state copied to new worker, and emission resumes.
6. Local Swap Agent retires old workers post-grace period and releases memory.

Cross-host staged hot-swap (for large variants)
-----------------------------------------------
- If in-place memory constraints prevent instant replacement, the Controller performs a staggered handoff: bring up READY workers on different hosts, start routing a subset of new sessions, migrate long-lived sessions in small batches, and finally decommission old capacity.

Configuration table: key knobs
----------------------------
| config_name | default | description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| swap.max_downtime_ms | 200 | Soft upper bound for allowed p95 delta during swap |
| swap.prewarm_timeout_s | 60 | Time to wait for prewarm/validation before abort |
| swap.stream_checkpoint_mode | full | \"full\" or \"light\" checkpointing for streaming sessions |
| swap.rollback_on_slo | true | Whether to trigger automatic rollback on SLO breach |
| swap.max_parallel_sessions_migrate | 50 | Max concurrent session migrations per host |

Example HotSwap request (YAML)
------------------------------
```yaml
variant_id: v3.2.1-patch
prewarm_hints:
  - prompt_set: safety-smoke-10
  - warm_prefixes: ["/chat/", "/assist/"]
rollout_policy:
  strategy: in_place
  max_concurrent_migrations: 40
  p95_latency_delta_ms: 200
  abort_on_error: true
```

Failure modes and mitigations
-----------------------------
- Prewarm failure (OOM or validation fail): abort swap, mark variant as failed; send automatic rollback and create incident if >3 hosts failed.
- Partial migration stalls: backoff and reduce batch size; route new sessions away from affected hosts.
- Token duplication on streams: Session Coordinator enforces idempotent markers; API layer verifies last_token_id before resuming.
- Sudden SLO regressions: Fallback Manager initiates rollback and throttles new requests for affected tenant(s).

Observability and telemetry
-------------------------
Mandatory metrics (exported by Local Swap Agent and Controller):
- hot_swap.start_count, hot_swap.success_count, hot_swap.abort_count
- hot_swap.prewarm_latency_seconds (histogram)
- host.swap_memory_peak_bytes
- session.migrated_count, session.migration_latency_seconds
- per-tenant.p95_latency_delta_during_swap_ms (derived)
sections.heading: The hot-swap capability is a multi-layer system composed of

sections.body:
- hot_swap.abort_rate > 5% in 10m -> Pager to serving-runtime-oncall
- per-tenant.p95_latency_delta_during_swap_ms > config.swap.max_downtime_ms -> Auto-rollback and SRE runbook

API contract and admin UX
------------------------
sections.heading: Alerts and runbook triggers

sections.body:
- POST /hot-swap -> submit request; returns job id
- GET /hot-swap/{id}/status -> progress, per-host status
- POST /hot-swap/{id}/abort -> abort and rollback
Admin UX elements: validation results, per-host prewarm logs, and a safe-preview mode that runs validation without committing swap.

Runtime compatibility matrix (summary)
-------------------------------------
- In-place hot-swap supported: small->medium variants (<120GB resident) on kernels v2.1+.
- Cross-host staged hot-swap required for >120GB or incompatible kernel combos.
- Quantized variants: hot-swap allowed if kernel supports identical inference path; otherwise staged path.

Testing strategy and acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------
1. Unit tests for Local Swap Agent state transitions.
2. Integration: synthetic traffic runner with streaming sessions verifies no token duplication and p95 within configured delta across 1000 simulated long-lived sessions.
3. Chaos tests: randomly kill workers during handoff; system must rollback cleanly and record artifacts.
4. Performance: cold prewarm + swap on standard host must complete within prewarm_timeout_s for 95% of runs.
Acceptance: in 10 controlled rollouts, 0 client-visible disconnects and p95 within configured delta for 9/10 runs.

Rollout plan
-----------
- Phase 1 (canary): internal tenants only; runbook and monitoring enabled; 2-week window.
- Phase 2 (beta): selected customers opt-in for emergency hot-swap; gather telemetry and refine config knobs.
- Phase 3 (GA): enabled for all dedicated and hosted clusters with safe defaults and opt-out for tenants that request scheduled rolling upgrades.

Operational runbook (high-level)
-------------------------------
1. Check job status in Controller UI.
2. If prewarm failing: examine host logs, memory, and validation harness results.
3. On SLO breach: trigger abort -> Controller posts abort -> Fallback Manager starts rollback.
4. Postmortem: collect hot_swap.* metrics, agent logs, session checkpoint traces, and create incident summary.

Open design issues and follow-ups
--------------------------------
- Edge-case: long-running streaming sessions with external side effects (webhooks). Need a policy for tie-breaker: prefer session affinity vs. external-side-effect consistency.
- Validation set coverage: how to identify a minimal smoke set that covers critical safety/fidelity regressions for hot-swap. Responsible: Applied ML to own and curate.

References
----------
- Progressive variant rollouts (compat matrix) — see related page.
- Canary scheduler economics and rollback spec — see related page.

Appendix: small glossary
-----------------------
- READY worker: process/worker that has loaded a new variant and passed validation but not yet serving live traffic.
- TRANSITIONING worker: worker in the process of handing off state and draining outstanding requests.
- Session Coordinator: distributed component that manages streaming token checkpoints to coordinate migration.
sections.heading: HotSwap API endpoints (REST)

payload.page_title: Unit Economics Dashboard (Internal) — Drilldown UX Spec (v1)

sections.body:
This document specifies the Console UX for the internal **Unit Economics** dashboard v1, with emphasis on the filter bar, drilldown navigation, top-N tables, and empty/error-state behavior.

Primary metric: **Blended $/1M output tokens** (finance-aligned). Users can drill down by:
- Model (incl. model version and quantization profile)
- Region
- Customer tier (Self-serve / Dedicated / Private / Enterprise)

Non-goals (v1): external customer-facing cost views; automated optimization actions.

---
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Confirm unit cost trends are explainable and reconcile to spend inputs.
- Pull quarter-to-date (QTD) summaries with clear caveats.
- Identify unit-cost outliers by region/tier/model.
sections.heading: Finance (CFO/FP&A)

sections.body:
- Prioritize cost optimization work based on impact size and affected segments.
- Detect regressions after runtime/infra/model changes.
sections.heading: Product (Console/Optimize)

sections.body:
- Triage anomalies: missing tokens, dimension coverage gaps, and cost spikes.
- Validate whether caching/batching/quantization changes moved economics.

---
sections.heading: Engineering (Telemetry/Runtime/SRE)

sections.body:
- Console left nav (internal-only): **Analytics → Unit Economics**
- Deep links from alerts/runbooks (when data quality issues fire)
sections.heading: Entry points

sections.body:
1) **Overview** (default)
   - KPI tiles (current window)
   - Time series
   - Top-N tables (Models, Regions, Tiers)

2) **Drilldown detail** (one pattern, parameterized by dimension)
   - Dimension header (e.g., Model: `rw-mistral-7b`)
   - Time series + breakdowns of remaining dimensions
   - Supporting signals panel (cache hit rate, batching efficiency, avg output length, streaming share, quant profile mix)

---
sections.heading: Pages (v1)

sections.body: Filter bar is pinned at top of page content.
sections.heading: Global filter bar (applies to Overview + Drilldowns)

sections.body:
1) **Time range** (required)
   - Defaults: Last 7 days
   - Presets: Last 24h, Last 7d, Last 30d, QTD, Custom
   - Custom supports start/end date-time; timezone selector defaults to **UTC** with a visible indicator.

2) **Model** (optional, multi-select)
   - Values from canonical model identifier mapping.
   - Display label: marketing alias (if present) + internal id in tooltip.
   - Selecting a model narrows tables and time series.

3) **Model version** (optional, conditional)
   - Enabled when exactly one model is selected.
   - Default: All versions.

4) **Quantization profile** (optional)
   - Default: All
   - Allowed values are from controlled vocabulary (per telemetry standard). Unknown/other values grouped as `Other/Unknown`.

5) **Region** (optional, multi-select)
   - Uses normalized canonical region names (e.g., `us-east`, `eu-west`).
   - Unknown values grouped as `Unknown` and are selectable.

6) **Customer tier** (optional, multi-select)
   - Values: Self-serve, Dedicated, Private, Enterprise
   - Tooltip clarifies derivation (billing/contract/routing flags).

7) **Advanced** (collapsible)
   - Streaming: All / Streaming only / Non-streaming only
   - Compare to: Previous period (same duration) [toggle]
sections.heading: Filters (left to right)

sections.body:
- Any change applies immediately (no “Apply” button) with debounce (300–500ms) to avoid rapid refetch.
- Show a small “Updating…” indicator in the filter bar while requests are inflight.
- URL is the source of truth for filter state (shareable deep link). Query params:
  - `from`, `to`, `tz`, `models`, `version`, `quant`, `regions`, `tiers`, `streaming`, `compare`
- Provide “Reset to defaults” action.
sections.heading: Filter interaction rules

sections.body:
- If selected filters yield >N series (e.g., >25 in a chart), show a warning and force aggregation (see Chart section).
- If the user selects a combination known to be slow (e.g., long custom range + high-cardinality breakdown), show inline guidance: “Try narrowing the time range or selecting fewer dimensions.”

---
sections.heading: Guardrails

sections.body: Tiles show the current time window and (if enabled) delta vs previous period.
sections.heading: 1) KPI tiles (Overview + Drilldown)

sections.body:
- **Blended $/1M output tokens**
- **Total output tokens**
- **Total attributed cost ($)**
- **Data completeness** (percent of expected hourly partitions present)
sections.heading: Required tiles (v1)

sections.body:
- $/1M output tokens: show with 2 decimals if >= $1, else 4 decimals (e.g., $0.1234).
- Deltas: show % change with sign.
- Tooltips:
  - Define blended cost and scope.
  - Link: “Metric definition” → metric dictionary page.
sections.heading: Tile formatting

sections.body: Default chart: **Blended $/1M output tokens over time** (hourly for <= 72h; daily otherwise).
sections.heading: 2) Time series chart

sections.body:
- “Group by” (single dimension) dropdown on Overview: None (default), Model, Region, Customer tier.
- On Drilldown pages: group-by defaults to the *remaining* most relevant dimension (see drilldown sections).
sections.heading: Controls

sections.body:
- If group-by is None: single line.
- If group-by is set: multi-line chart limited to top 10 by output tokens; remaining grouped into “Other”.
- Hover tooltip shows:
  - $/1M output tokens
  - output tokens
  - attributed cost
  - completeness/confidence indicator for that bucket
sections.heading: Chart behaviors

sections.body: - If “Compare to previous period” is enabled, show dashed line(s) for previous period with same color family.
sections.heading: Comparison mode

sections.body: Three tables on Overview (stacked). Default sort: highest attributed cost ($) descending.
sections.heading: 3) Top-N tables

sections.body:
- **Top Models**
- **Top Regions**
- **Top Customer Tiers**
sections.heading: Tables

sections.body:
1) Name (dimension value)
2) Blended $/1M output tokens
3) Output tokens
4) Attributed cost ($)
5) Cache hit rate (if available)
6) Batching efficiency (if available)
7) Streaming share
8) Data completeness
sections.heading: Common columns (v1)

sections.body:
- Cache hit rate: displayed as %; tooltip clarifies KV/prefix cache definition.
- Batching efficiency: displayed as %; tooltip clarifies definition (effective utilization vs ideal).
- Streaming share: % of requests that were streaming.
sections.heading: Column definitions

sections.body:
- Rows are clickable to drill down (see Drilldown navigation).
- Column sorting enabled for: $/1M, output tokens, cost, completeness.
- Pagination: default 10 rows, expandable to 25/50.
- Search within dimension values for Models and Regions.
sections.heading: Table interaction

sections.body:
- No customer identifiers in any table.
- Suppress buckets with extremely low volume to avoid over-interpretation and potential leakage:
  - If a row has < 0.5% of total output tokens for the view (or < configurable absolute minimum), display it aggregated into “Other” (exact threshold TBD with Finance/Security).

---
sections.heading: Privacy & sensitivity

sections.body:
- `/internal/unit-economics` (Overview)
- `/internal/unit-economics/model/<model_id>`
- `/internal/unit-economics/region/<region_id>`
- `/internal/unit-economics/tier/<tier_id>`
sections.heading: Drilldown pages use the same route with typed parameters

sections.body:
- Clicking a row in any Top-N table navigates to the corresponding drilldown.
- Clicking a legend item in the chart (group-by mode) navigates to that drilldown (if dimension is eligible).
sections.heading: Entry actions

sections.body: - `Unit Economics` → `Model: rw-llama3-70b` (or Region/Tier)
sections.heading: At top of drilldown detail

sections.body:
- Drilldown retains all global filters (time range, quant profile, streaming, etc.).
- Drilldown implicitly pins the selected dimension value; it is shown as a “locked” pill in the filter bar with an “X” to remove and return to Overview.

---
sections.heading: Context preservation

sections.body:
- Model display name (alias + id)
- Optional subheader chips: selected model version, selected quant profile
sections.heading: Header

sections.body:
1) KPI tiles (same as Overview)
2) Time series chart (default group-by: **Region**) with toggle to switch group-by to Customer tier
3) Breakdown tables:
   - “Regions for this model” (top 25)
   - “Customer tiers for this model” (all tiers)
   - If model version is not pinned: “Model versions for this model”
   - If quant profile is not pinned: “Quant profiles for this model”

Supporting signals panel (right rail or below, depending on screen width):
- Cache hit rate trend
- Batching efficiency trend
- Avg output length (tokens) trend
- Prefill/decode ratio (if instrumented)
- Notes: “Signals are diagnostic; attribution is directional.”
sections.heading: Primary content

sections.body: - Region canonical name (e.g., `eu-west`) + tooltip listing underlying mapped providers/labels.
sections.heading: Header

sections.body:
1) Time series chart (default group-by: **Model**)
2) Tables:
   - “Models in this region”
   - “Customer tiers in this region”
   - “Quant profiles mix in this region”
sections.heading: Primary content

sections.body: - If the region has known cost-rate-card updates in the selected window, show “Rate card changed on <date>” with link to methodology note.
sections.heading: Region caveat callout (inline)

sections.body: - Tier name + tooltip describing derivation and edge cases.
sections.heading: Header

sections.body:
1) Time series chart (default group-by: **Model**)
2) Tables:
   - “Models for this tier”
   - “Regions for this tier”
   - “Quant profiles for this tier”
sections.heading: Primary content

sections.body:
- Dedicated/Private tiers may have more pronounced idle cost allocation effects; add a persistent info note linking to ADR.

---
sections.heading: Tier caveat callout (inline)

sections.body:
- **No data**: query returned zero rows for the selected filters.
- **Partial data**: some expected hourly partitions missing OR missing critical dimensions above threshold.
- **Stale data**: data freshness SLO violated (e.g., latest hour not loaded by target time).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Use skeleton loaders for tiles and tables.
- Time series shows a faint placeholder grid with “Loading data…” label.
- Preserve previous data on minor filter tweaks when possible; show “Updating…” to reduce perceived flicker.
sections.heading: Loading states

sections.body:
- Title: “No unit economics data for this selection”
- Body copy:
  - “Try widening the time range or removing one or more filters.”
  - If streaming-only is enabled: “Streaming-only views may have limited coverage for older periods.”
- Actions:
  - Button: “Reset filters”
  - Link: “View pipeline status” (links to internal observability dashboard)
sections.heading: Show a dedicated empty state panel

sections.body:
When completeness < target (thresholds per SLO doc):
- Show a **yellow banner** at top of page:
  - “Data is incomplete for the selected time range (X% of expected hours present). Values may change after backfill.”
  - Link: “See runbook”
- In charts/tables, show a small “Low confidence” indicator next to affected series/rows.
sections.heading: Partial data state (incomplete coverage)

sections.body:
- Show **red banner**:
  - “Data is stale (latest hour: <timestamp UTC>).”
  - Link: “Incident channel / runbook”
sections.heading: When latest data is older than freshness target

sections.body:
- Display a non-blocking error toast plus a full-width error panel if content cannot load.
- Panel includes:
  - “We couldn’t load unit economics data.”
  - “Request ID: <id>”
  - “Retry” button
  - Link to runbook
sections.heading: If API returns an error

sections.body:
If a high fraction of rows have `Unknown` for a critical dimension (region/tier/model):
- Show an inline warning in the relevant table header:
  - “High ‘Unknown’ coverage for Region (12%). Investigate region normalization.”
  - Link to region normalization plan and/or runbook.

---
sections.heading: Dimension coverage issues

sections.body:
To avoid misinterpretation (per internal visualization guidelines):
- Always display metric unit in labels: “$/1M output tokens”.
- Use consistent number formatting across tiles, charts, and tables.
- For very small denominators:
  - If output tokens < minimum threshold for the row, show $/1M as “—” and tooltip: “Insufficient volume for stable unit cost.”
- Deltas should be suppressed when the previous period has insufficient volume.
sections.heading: Formatting, rounding, and interpretation safeguards

sections.body:
- “Blended $/1M output tokens includes allocated compute + shared overhead per the finance methodology. It is not the marginal cost of an additional request.”

---
sections.heading: Required tooltip copy (v1)

sections.body:
- Page is behind an internal feature flag and RBAC check.
- If a user lacks access:
  - Show “You don’t have access to Unit Economics.”
  - Provide instructions: “Request access via #internal-tools-support” (or internal request system).
  - Do not reveal any metric values.

---
sections.heading: Permissions and access control UX

sections.body:
- Keyboard navigation must work for filter bar controls and table row drilldowns.
- Color choices for multi-series charts must be color-blind safe; do not rely on color alone for compare mode (use line style).
- Tooltips must be accessible (focus-triggered, not hover-only).

---
sections.heading: Accessibility and usability requirements

sections.body:
- Page view: Overview vs drilldown type
- Filter change events (time range, dimension filters, compare toggle)
- Drilldown click source (table vs chart)
- Export actions (if added later)
- Error/empty-state occurrences with reason code

---
sections.heading: Log the following events (internal analytics)

sections.body:
1) Minimum volume thresholds for suppressing unstable $/1M values (row-level). Owner: Marissa Cole + Laura Bennett.
2) Default timezone: keep UTC only vs allow local timezone selection. Owner: Chloe Martin.
3) Compare-mode defaults: always off vs remembered per user. Owner: Product.
4) Confidence indicator computation details (completeness + unknown coverage) and exact thresholds. Owner: Allison Grant + Caleb Johnson.
5) Whether “Model version” should be exposed as a first-class filter on Overview (vs drilldown-only). Owner: Marissa Cole.

---
sections.heading: Open questions / decisions needed

sections.body:
- Banner (incomplete): “Data is incomplete for the selected time range ({{completeness}}%). Values may change after backfill.”
- Banner (stale): “Data is stale (latest hour: {{timestamp}}).”
- Empty state title: “No unit economics data for this selection”
- Empty state helper: “Try widening the time range or removing one or more filters.”
- Tooltip (metric): “Blended $/1M output tokens includes allocated compute + shared overhead per the finance methodology. It is not marginal cost.”
sections.heading: Appendix A: UI copy strings (v1)

sections.body:
- Output tokens: total metered output tokens attributed to the selection.
- Attributed cost ($): allocated cost for the selection per the attribution model.
- Cache hit rate: fraction of tokens served with KV/prefix cache reuse (definition may vary by runtime path).
- Batching efficiency: utilization proxy representing effective batching vs ideal scheduling.
- Completeness: percent of expected hourly partitions present for the bucket.
