payload.page_title: Offline observability bundle packaging (air-gapped/on-prem) — Private minimum pack

sections.body: This page defines how Redwood packages and delivers the **Private observability minimum pack** for **offline / air-gapped on-prem** environments.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Ensure customers can install a supported baseline observability setup without outbound internet.
- Provide a deterministic, verifiable artifact bundle (images + dashboards + rules + configs) that can be mirrored into a customer registry.
- Make upgrades/rollbacks safe: versions are pinned, manifests are checksummed/signed, and compatibility constraints are documented.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Customer-specific dashboard customization in the bundle.
- Long-retention or federation “premium” observability features.
sections.heading: Non-goals (v1)

sections.body:
- Customer platform / infra teams operating Redwood Private in on-prem or restricted networks.
- Redwood Solutions Engineering and Support assisting air-gapped installs.
- Redwood Private Deployments engineers maintaining the offline packaging.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- The official offline bundle produced by Redwood release tooling for a specific Redwood Private release.
- Mirroring into a customer-managed registry (Harbor/Artifactory/ECR-on-VM/etc.) using standard tools (skopeo/crane/docker).
- Helm-based installation via `redwood-private-installer` and `redwood-helm-charts` with offline overrides.
sections.heading: We support

sections.body: - Customer-built images or repackaged dashboards/rules not matching the bundle manifest (unless explicitly approved in a support engagement).
sections.heading: We do not support

sections.body: The offline observability bundle is versioned alongside Redwood Private.
sections.heading: Bundle versioning

sections.body:
- Bundle filename: `redwood-private-observability-offline-bundle-<private_version>-<bundle_build>.tar.zst`
- Example: `redwood-private-observability-offline-bundle-1.18.0-b3.tar.zst`

The bundle is considered compatible only with the matching Redwood Private version (see “Compatibility & upgrades”).
sections.heading: Naming convention

sections.body:
The offline bundle contains **three classes** of artifacts:

1) Container images (OCI)
- Required images for the minimum-pack observability components.
- Redwood-owned images (where applicable) plus pinned upstream images.

2) Grafana dashboards
- JSON dashboards in a versioned directory.
- Provisioning metadata for folder placement and datasources.

3) Prometheus rules
- Alerting rules and recording rules shipped as YAML.
- Rules include runbook links and are aligned to the Private alert severity taxonomy.
sections.heading: Bundle contents

sections.body:
- `manifest/`
  - `bundle-manifest.json` (list of artifacts and digests)
  - `bundle-sbom.spdx.json` (SBOM for images + key files)
  - `SHA256SUMS`
  - `cosign.bundle.sig` (signature payload; see “Signing & verification”)
- `images/`
  - `index.json` (mapping of source image -> digest -> target tag suggestion)
  - `oci/` (OCI image layout) OR `docker-archive/` (depending on release tooling)
- `grafana/`
  - `dashboards/private-min-pack/<version>/*.json`
  - `provisioning/` (folders + dashboard providers)
- `prometheus/`
  - `rules/alerts/*.yaml`
  - `rules/recording/*.yaml`
- `logging/`
  - `collector/` (default config snippets)
  - `pipelines/` (Loki/ELK/Splunk examples; templates)

Note: Exact layout may evolve, but `manifest/bundle-manifest.json` is the source of truth for what the bundle contains.
sections.heading: Top-level structure (logical)

sections.body: The minimum pack is designed to work with customer-run Prometheus/Grafana, but our offline bundle ships a supported baseline “batteries included” stack for on-prem installs when customers do not already have standard tooling.
sections.heading: Container images to mirror (minimum pack)

sections.body: The following images are included and must be mirrored into the customer registry if deploying the included components:
sections.heading: Image set (baseline)

sections.body:
- `quay.io/prometheus/prometheus:<pinned>`
- `quay.io/prometheus/alertmanager:<pinned>`
- `quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter:<pinned>`
- `quay.io/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator:<pinned>` (if using the operator path)
- `grafana/grafana:<pinned>`
sections.heading: Core observability

sections.body:
- `registry.k8s.io/metrics-server/metrics-server:<pinned>` (only if enabled by values)
- `registry.k8s.io/kube-state-metrics/kube-state-metrics:<pinned>`

Logging (default collector; see ADR-022):
- `grafana/loki:<pinned>` (optional; enabled when using the bundled Loki path)
- `grafana/promtail:<pinned>` OR `grafana/alloy:<pinned>` (depending on bundle revision)
- `otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:<pinned>` (optional; only if OTLP export is enabled)
sections.heading: Kubernetes metrics

sections.body: - No additional Redwood application images are introduced by the observability bundle; it only references metrics/logs emitted by existing Redwood Private components.
sections.heading: Redwood components (for dashboards/rules parity)

sections.body:
- All images are pinned by **digest** in `manifest/bundle-manifest.json`. Tags are advisory.
- If your environment forbids external registries, mirror all images to a single internal registry namespace (recommended).
- If you already operate Prometheus/Grafana, you may disable bundled deployment and use only dashboards/rules. In that case, you still need to ensure your existing versions meet the compatibility matrix below.
sections.heading: Image set notes

sections.body:
These are the minimum supported upstream versions for air-gapped installs using the minimum pack artifacts.

- Kubernetes: 1.26–1.30
- Prometheus: >= 2.45 (recommended 2.50+)
- Alertmanager: >= 0.26
- Grafana: >= 10.4
- Loki (if enabled): >= 2.9

If customers run older versions, dashboards may fail to render, PromQL may error, or alert expressions may be invalid. Support may ask you to upgrade tooling before triaging Redwood-specific issues.
sections.heading: Compatibility matrix (minimum supported versions)

sections.body: Air-gapped installs require customers to validate artifact integrity.
sections.heading: Signing & verification

sections.body:
The bundle includes `manifest/SHA256SUMS` covering:
- The compressed bundle file (when distributed as a single archive)
- `bundle-manifest.json`
- All dashboard JSON files
- All Prometheus rule YAML files
sections.heading: Checksums

sections.body:
1. Extract bundle: `tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xvf redwood-private-observability-offline-bundle-<ver>.tar.zst`
2. Verify checksums:
   - `cd manifest && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`
sections.heading: Customer verification (example)

sections.body:
Redwood signs the bundle manifest using Sigstore/cosign.

Verification steps (connected environment, recommended before moving into the air-gap):
- `cosign verify-blob \
    --certificate-identity "redwood-releases@redwoodinference.com" \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
    --signature manifest/cosign.bundle.sig \
    manifest/bundle-manifest.json`
sections.heading: Signatures

sections.body: - Redwood can provide an offline verification packet (certificate + Rekor inclusion proof) per release if required by customer policy. Coordinate via Solutions Engineering.
sections.heading: Air-gapped verification

sections.body:
When mirroring, ensure the final registry references match the digests in the manifest.
- Acceptable: retagging while preserving digest.
- Not acceptable: rebuilding images or mirroring via a process that changes layers.
sections.heading: Image digest enforcement

sections.body: Customers should mirror images from the bundle into an internal registry accessible by the cluster.
sections.heading: Mirroring images into a customer registry

sections.body:
- `skopeo` (preferred for air-gapped mirroring)
- `crane` (OK)
- `docker load` + `docker push` (works, slower; avoid for very large bundles)
sections.heading: Recommended tools

sections.body:
- Internal registry: `registry.customer.local/redwood-observability`
- Bundle extracted to `/bundles/obs/`
sections.heading: Assumptions

sections.body:
1) Authenticate to internal registry:
- `skopeo login registry.customer.local`

2) Iterate images from `images/index.json` (scripted by customer; Redwood installer also supports a mirror command in some environments):
- For each entry, copy digest-pinned image:
  - `skopeo copy --all \
      oci:/bundles/obs/images/oci/<image_path>@sha256:<digest> \
      docker://registry.customer.local/redwood-observability/<name>:<tag>`

3) Validate digests:
- `skopeo inspect docker://registry.customer.local/redwood-observability/<name>:<tag> | jq .Digest`
- Compare to `bundle-manifest.json`.
sections.heading: Procedure

sections.body:
If the bundle ships `docker-archive/` tarballs:
- `docker load -i images/docker-archive/prometheus.tar`
- `docker tag <loaded_image_id> registry.customer.local/redwood-observability/prometheus:<tag>`
- `docker push registry.customer.local/redwood-observability/prometheus:<tag>`
sections.heading: Example: mirror using docker-archive

sections.body: Use this when the customer already has a standard observability stack.
sections.heading: Mode A: Use customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana

sections.body:
- Install Redwood dashboards and Prometheus rules from the bundle into the customer stack.
- Configure datasource names and scrape configs to match Redwood expectations.

Key values (examples; exact keys may vary by chart version):
- `observability.enabled=true`
- `observability.prometheus.deploy=false`
- `observability.grafana.deploy=false`
- `observability.dashboards.install=true`
- `observability.rules.install=true`
sections.heading: Required actions

sections.body: Use this when the customer requests a turnkey supported stack.
sections.heading: Mode B: Deploy bundled Prometheus/Grafana (baseline)

sections.body:
- Mirror images to internal registry.
- Provide image registry override values.
- Ensure storage classes and PVC sizing meet minimums.
sections.heading: Required actions

sections.body:
- `global.imageRegistry=registry.customer.local`
- `observability.prometheus.deploy=true`
- `observability.grafana.deploy=true`
- `observability.prometheus.retention=15d` (default)
- `observability.prometheus.storage.size=200Gi` (default baseline; see sizing guidance)

Note: If NetworkPolicies are enabled in the cluster, you must allow Prometheus scrapes of Redwood namespaces (see Day-2 runbook).
sections.heading: Key values (examples)

sections.body: - `grafana/dashboards/private-min-pack/<version>/`
sections.heading: Location in bundle

sections.body:
- Runtime overview (golden signals, token throughput, batching/KV cache, GPU utilization)
- Control plane health (gateway/auth/policy/config services)
- GPU & node resources (GPU saturation, memory pressure, node exporter)
- Queueing/backpressure (request queue depth, throttling, 429s)
- Error analysis (5xx, upstream dependency errors, restart loops)
sections.heading: Dashboards included (v1 minimum set)

sections.body:
- Grafana provisioning (file-based) for bundled Grafana.
- ConfigMap import (Kubernetes) for customer-managed Grafana, if they accept provisioned dashboards.
sections.heading: Installation patterns

sections.body: - Prometheus datasource named `Prometheus` (default) OR override via values.
sections.heading: Datasource expectations

sections.body:
- `prometheus/rules/alerts/`
- `prometheus/rules/recording/`
sections.heading: Location in bundle

sections.body:
- Alerts are designed for bounded cardinality in customer Prometheus.
- SLO burn alerts are included where feasible; some are disabled by default to avoid paging noise.
- Every alert includes:
  - A short summary
  - Severity (`sev1`, `sev2`, `sev3`)
  - A “what to do first” hint
  - A runbook link (internal by default; externalized in customer-facing docs)
sections.heading: Rule design notes

sections.body: Upgrade the observability bundle in lockstep with Redwood Private **minor** releases unless release notes explicitly declare compatibility.
sections.heading: Golden rule

sections.body:
- Supported: `1.18.x` -> `1.19.x` (standard minor upgrade)
- Supported: patch upgrades within the same minor (`1.18.0` -> `1.18.3`)
- Not supported without review: skipping more than one minor version (e.g., `1.17` -> `1.19`)
sections.heading: Supported upgrade paths

sections.body:
- New or renamed metrics (dashboards and rules will be updated accordingly).
- Alert threshold tuning and enable/disable defaults.
- Dashboard panel queries and variable naming.
- Upstream image pins (Prometheus/Grafana/Loki).
sections.heading: What can change across versions

sections.body:
- Stable metric names for top-level golden signals.
- Stable dashboard UIDs within a major release line.
sections.heading: We aim to preserve

sections.body:
- They are called out in the Redwood Private release notes.
- A migration note is included in the bundle manifest metadata.
sections.heading: When breaking changes occur

sections.body:
- Also rollback dashboards/rules to the previous bundle version.
- Keep Prometheus TSDB data; do not delete PVCs unless instructed.
- If alert noise spikes after rollback, temporarily disable the `SLO burn` group until rules are aligned.
sections.heading: If you rollback Redwood Private

sections.body: These defaults are chosen to be safe for typical Private footprints and are validated in reference environments.
sections.heading: Storage and sizing defaults (baseline)

sections.body:
- Retention: 15 days
- Storage: 200Gi (PVC), expandable
- CPU/memory: 2 vCPU / 8Gi baseline (scale up with scrape volume)
sections.heading: Prometheus

sections.body: - Storage: optional (PVC) if persisting dashboards/users; otherwise ephemeral is acceptable for bundled dashboards.
sections.heading: Grafana

sections.body:
- Buffering defaults are tuned to avoid unbounded memory usage.
- If the customer requires “no log loss,” enable disk-backed buffering and ensure adequate node storage.

For detailed sizing by request volume, see the Infra runbook for Prometheus/Grafana sizing.
sections.heading: Logging collector

sections.body:
1) “We need all artifacts as a single signed tarball”
- Supported. Redwood ships a single compressed bundle plus checksum and signature metadata.

2) “We cannot run Grafana in-cluster; must use central Grafana”
- Supported in Mode A. Provide dashboards as JSON plus provisioning guidance.

3) “We must forward logs to Splunk/ELK; no Loki allowed”
- Supported. Use the `logging/pipelines/` templates and configure collector output accordingly.

4) “No outbound DNS / egress”
- Supported. Ensure charts do not reference external image registries; set `global.imageRegistry` and mirror all digests.
sections.heading: Common customer constraints and recommended responses

sections.body:
- [ ] `sha256sum -c` passes for all files in `manifest/SHA256SUMS`.
- [ ] Bundle manifest signature verified (connected environment) OR offline verification packet delivered.
- [ ] All included images mirrored; digests match manifest.
- [ ] Installer preflight checks pass (storage class, PVC provisioning, NetworkPolicy reachability).
- [ ] Prometheus scrapes Redwood targets (no `up == 0` for Redwood jobs > 5m).
- [ ] Grafana dashboards render and show non-empty panels after generating sample traffic.
- [ ] At least one alert can be triggered in staging via failure injection (scrape failure or simulated 5xx).
sections.heading: Before handing off to customers / declaring readiness

sections.body:
- Dashboards empty: confirm datasource name and Prometheus job labels; check scrape permissions (NetworkPolicies).
- Prometheus OOM / TSDB churn: reduce scrape interval, increase resources, and verify cardinality constraints; confirm no high-cardinality labels were enabled.
- Log pipeline backpressure: increase buffers, reduce batch size, confirm sink auth (Splunk HEC token / ELK credentials).

See: Private observability Day-2 runbook for step-by-step triage.

3) Generate `bundle-manifest.json`, SBOM, and checksums.
4) Sign manifest; publish bundle to the customer delivery channel.
5) Validate in reference air-gapped environment (see validation plan).

payload.page_title: On‑prem upgrade bundle format (air‑gapped) — Redwood Private

sections.body: Redwood Private on‑prem (including fully air‑gapped environments) upgrades are delivered as a **single, self‑contained upgrade bundle**. The bundle includes all artifacts required by the installer to validate, plan, and execute an upgrade **without reaching the public internet**.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Bundle packaging requirements and directory layout
- The **manifest** (what it must contain and how it’s validated)
- Checksums and signature verification requirements
- Offline dependency handling (container images, Helm charts, CLIs)
- How `redwood-private-installer` locates, verifies, and uses bundles
sections.heading: This document defines

sections.body:
- **Bundle**: A `.tar.zst` (preferred) or `.tar.gz` archive containing a manifest and all upgrade artifacts.
- **Artifact**: A file or OCI object required for upgrade (charts, images, binaries, migration jobs).
- **Mirror**: Customer-managed offline registry/repository (e.g., Harbor, Artifactory, Nexus).
sections.heading: Terminology

sections.body:
We publish two bundle flavors. Both share the same manifest schema.

1) **Offline bundle (recommended)**
- Contains **all** OCI images (as tar archives) and Helm charts.
- Installer can load/push images to a local registry and install charts without any external fetch.

2) **Mirror-assisted bundle**
- Contains charts and metadata, but images are expected to already exist in the customer mirror.
- Manifest includes required image digests; installer verifies presence by digest.
sections.heading: Supported bundle types

sections.body:
1) **Deterministic**: A bundle uniquely identifies the release and artifact digests.
2) **Verifiable**: Bundle must pass checksum + signature verification before use.
3) **Complete**: For Offline bundles, no network fetch is required after verification.
4) **Auditable**: Installer writes verification and consumption results into the upgrade audit trail.
sections.heading: High-level invariants (must hold)

sections.body: - `redwood-private-upgrade-bundle_<privateVersion>_<k8sMinor>_<arch>_<buildId>.tar.zst`
sections.heading: Recommended naming convention

sections.body: - `redwood-private-upgrade-bundle_1.18.0_k8s-1.29_amd64_b20250614.3.tar.zst`
sections.heading: Example

sections.body:
After extraction, the bundle must have this top-level structure:

```
./
  manifest.json
  manifest.sig
  checksums.sha256
  charts/
    redwood-private-<version>.tgz
    redwood-private-crds-<version>.tgz
  images/
    index.json
    oci/
      redwood-control-plane_@sha256-....tar
      redwood-data-plane_@sha256-....tar
      redwood-migrations_@sha256-....tar
      ...
  binaries/
    redwood-private-installer_<version>_<os>_<arch>
    kubectl_<version>_<os>_<arch>   (optional)
    helm_<version>_<os>_<arch>      (optional)
  docs/
    release-notes.md
    upgrade-notes.md
  licenses/
    THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt
```
sections.heading: Bundle directory layout

sections.body:
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, and `checksums.sha256` are mandatory.
- `images/` is mandatory for Offline bundles; optional for Mirror-assisted bundles.
- `binaries/` may include a pinned installer build, but the bundle can also be consumed by a separately distributed installer as long as compatibility checks pass.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- File name: `manifest.json`
- Encoding: UTF‑8
- JSON object (schema validated by installer)
sections.heading: Format

sections.body:
The installer treats these fields as required and **blocking** if missing.

- `bundle_format_version`
  - String; current value: `"1.0"`
- `bundle_id`
  - String; unique id (e.g., build id)
- `created_at`
  - RFC3339 timestamp
- `private_version`
  - The Redwood Private platform version contained in this bundle
- `upgrade_paths`
  - Supported source versions (initially N‑1 → N is the default)
- `kubernetes_compatibility`
  - Supported K8s minor versions (e.g., `1.28`, `1.29`)
- `artifacts`
  - Lists charts/images/binaries by name, version, and digest
- `signing`
  - Signature metadata (key id, algorithm)
sections.heading: Required fields

sections.body:
- `release_channel` (e.g., `stable`, `beta`)
- `notes` (short summary)
- `known_issues` (links/ids)
- `support_bundle_tags` (what to include in support bundles)
sections.heading: Recommended fields
Manifest example (abridged)

sections.body:
- Reject unknown `bundle_format_version` values.
- Reject bundles whose `private_version` is not compatible with the installer’s supported range.
- Enforce `upgrade_paths.supported_sources` / `blocked_sources` (see compatibility policy).
- Validate that every artifact referenced exists and matches the expected digest.
sections.heading: The installer MUST

sections.body:
- File name: `checksums.sha256`
- Format: standard `sha256sum` output (`<sha256>  <relative-path>`)
- Must include:
  - `manifest.json`
  - All chart tarballs under `charts/`
  - All image tars under `images/oci/` (Offline bundles)
  - Any binary under `binaries/` shipped in the bundle
  - Any `docs/` content is optional (non-blocking if missing unless referenced by manifest)
sections.heading: checksums file

sections.body:
```
9f2d...  manifest.json
b18a...  charts/redwood-private-1.18.0.tgz
c91c...  charts/redwood-private-crds-1.18.0.tgz
0d77...  images/oci/redwood-control-plane_@sha256-....tar
f3a1...  binaries/redwood-private-installer_0.31.0_linux_amd64
```
sections.heading: Example

sections.body:
- The installer verifies SHA256 for each referenced artifact.
- Any mismatch is **blocking** and must fail before prechecks/plan generation.
sections.heading: Verification behavior

sections.body:
- File name: `manifest.sig`
- Signature covers the bytes of `manifest.json` (exact file contents).
- Signature algorithm: **ed25519**
sections.heading: Signature file

sections.body:
- Redwood publishes release public keys out-of-band to on‑prem customers as part of the Private onboarding package.
- Customers configure trusted keys on the operator host (or inside the installer container) prior to upgrade.
sections.heading: Trust model

sections.body:
1) `--trusted-keys <path>` (file containing one or more public keys)
2) `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_TRUSTED_KEYS_PATH` (env var)
3) Default path: `/etc/redwood-private/trust/keys/`
sections.heading: The installer searches keys in this order

sections.body:
- Signature verification is **blocking**.
- `signing.key_id` in the manifest must match an available trusted key id.
- Installer records key id and verification result in upgrade audit logs.
sections.heading: Verification requirements

sections.body:
- `images/oci/*.tar` are OCI image tarballs.
- `images/index.json` maps human names to digests and tar paths (installer uses this for fast validation).
- Installer can either:
  - Load into container runtime (e.g., `containerd`) and re-tag, or
  - Push directly to a customer registry mirror.

Required: all images referenced by charts must be present by digest.
sections.heading: Offline bundle

sections.body:
- Bundle omits image tar files.
- Manifest lists all required images + digests.
- Installer verifies images exist in the configured mirror registry **by digest**.
- If the mirror serves tags only, operator must ensure tags resolve to the declared digests.
sections.heading: Mirror-assisted bundle

sections.body:
- Must be shipped as `.tgz` under `charts/`.
- The bundle should include a CRDs chart separately (`redwood-private-crds`) when CRDs must be applied ahead of control plane rollout.
sections.heading: Helm charts

sections.body:
- For air‑gapped environments, we recommend shipping a pinned installer binary in `binaries/`.
- Optional: include `kubectl` and `helm` to avoid relying on host tooling.
sections.heading: CLIs and tools

sections.body: The installer supports two primary modes: **path-based** and **directory discovery**.
sections.heading: How the installer locates bundles

sections.body:
- Archive:
  - `redwood-private-installer upgrade --bundle /path/to/bundle.tar.zst`
- Extracted dir:
  - `redwood-private-installer upgrade --bundle-dir /path/to/extracted/`
sections.heading: Operators provide the bundle archive or extracted directory

sections.body:
- If `--bundle` is provided, installer extracts to a working directory under:
  - `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/redwood-private/bundles/<bundle_id>/`
- If `--bundle-dir` is provided, installer uses it read-only and writes state elsewhere.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
If no explicit bundle flag is passed, installer searches:
1) `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_BUNDLE_DIR`
2) `/opt/redwood-private/bundles/current/`

Discovery requires `manifest.json` at the root.
sections.heading: Directory discovery (fallback)

sections.body:
1) **Locate bundle** (path/discovery)
2) **Read manifest** and validate schema
3) **Verify signature** of `manifest.json`
4) **Verify checksums** of referenced artifacts
5) **Compatibility gate**
   - Source version must be in `supported_sources` and not in `blocked_sources`
   - K8s minor must be supported
6) **Artifact availability checks**
   - Offline bundle: ensure all required `images/` and `charts/` exist
   - Mirror-assisted: verify mirror contains all required digests
7) **Proceed to prechecks / plan**

If any step fails, the installer must stop before making changes.
sections.heading: Installer performs these steps in order (all are auditable)

sections.body: For on‑prem, images typically must be pushed to a local registry.
sections.heading: Operator configuration: offline registry and mirrors

sections.body:
- `--registry-mirror <host:port>`
- `--registry-username <user>` / `--registry-password-file <path>`
- `--registry-ca-file <path>` (private CA)
- `--registry-insecure` (not recommended; restricted environments only)
sections.heading: Installer flags (common)

sections.body:
- For Offline bundles, installer loads and pushes **by digest**, then configures chart values to reference the mirror.
- For Mirror-assisted bundles, installer validates image digests exist before continuing.
sections.heading: Expected behavior

sections.body:
| Failure | What it means | Typical remediation |
|---|---|---|
| `SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED` | Bundle may be tampered with or wrong key configured | Confirm trusted key set; re-download bundle; verify key id; avoid copying through systems that modify files |
| `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` | A file differs from expected SHA256 | Re-transfer with binary-safe method; validate storage integrity; re-fetch bundle |
| `MISSING_ARTIFACT` | Manifest references a file not present in the bundle | Wrong bundle version or incomplete extraction; re-download and re-extract |
| `UNSUPPORTED_UPGRADE_PATH` | Source version not supported | Use supported N‑1 release first or contact Support for an assisted multi-hop plan |
| `MIRROR_DIGEST_NOT_FOUND` | Mirror does not contain required image digest | Push images to mirror (or use Offline bundle); ensure digest retention is enabled |
sections.heading: Failure modes and operator remediation

sections.body:
- Store bundles in a WORM-capable or access-controlled location (auditors frequently request evidence of what was installed).
- Keep `manifest.json`, `checksums.sha256`, and `manifest.sig` together; do not rename files.
- Prefer `.tar.zst` for large bundles (faster and smaller for offline transfer).
- Ensure your transfer mechanism preserves file integrity (avoid email/IM attachments; use SFTP, signed artifact channels, or physical media with verification).
sections.heading: Operational guidance

sections.body:
- Bundle signatures are the primary integrity control; checksums provide defense-in-depth and earlier corruption detection.
- Customer environments may require that bundles are scanned prior to import. The manifest can be used as an input inventory for scanners.
- The installer must emit audit events for: bundle verification start/finish, key id used, and bundle id/private version consumed.
sections.heading: Security and compliance notes

sections.body: tarzstd -d -c bundle.tar.zst | tar -xvf -
sections.heading: Extract (tar.zst)

sections.body: sha256sum -c checksums.sha256
sections.heading: Quick local checksum verification

sections.body:
cat manifest.json | jq .
```
sections.heading: Optional: inspect manifest

sections.body:
- Bundles are forward-compatible within a major installer line when `bundle_format_version` is unchanged.
- If the installer reports `UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE_FORMAT`, update the installer to the minimum version referenced in release notes.

(Installer compatibility enforcement is described in the upgrade plan / rollback ADR and the Private release gating policy.)
sections.heading: Appendix B: Bundle compatibility with installer versions

payload.page_title: Offline dependency curation and binary slimming guidelines

sections.body:
Summary

This document describes the recommended process for creating minimal, auditable offline artifacts for Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The guidance covers: curation of third‑party dependencies, binary slimming techniques, SBOM generation and signing, runtime compatibility hardening, and field validation/rollback considerations. The goal is reproducible, minimal-footprint deliverables that operators can install in air-gapped or restricted environments with clear forensic evidence.

Scope and intended audience

- Scope: build artifacts (binaries, wheel files, container image layers, model weight archives, and ancillary runtime shims) that are intended for offline delivery to customer-controlled infrastructure.
- Audience: release engineers, on‑prem packaging engineers, operator/systems integrators, security/compliance reviewers.

Principles and objectives

1. Minimal trusted surface: include only the code and runtime components required for the supported feature set and SLO targets.
2. Reproducibility: every offline bundle must be provably rebuildable from source under a documented build matrix (compiler, toolchain, model version).
3. Auditable provenance: SBOMs, signature manifests, and a small evidence bundle (build logs + checksums) accompany each release artifact.
4. Deterministic compatibility: runtime shim + quantization metadata to ensure model weights run on target accelerators without runtime code changes.

Owners and contact

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments / Packaging team
- Primary contact for implementation questions: priya.nair@redwood.ai
- Security reviewer: evelyn.park@redwood.ai

Prerequisites and inputs

- Upstream components: pinned git commit/tag for each dependency (git:// or HTTPS), upstream license files, and upstream SBOM if available.
- Build environment: sealed builder VM/container definition (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS base, glibc 2.35, GCC 12 or clang 15) captured as part of the evidence bundle.
- Model artifacts: signed model weights archive and quantization profile (see subsection below).

High-level workflow (numbered steps)

1. Dependency inventory and initial pruning
   - Run dependency discovery on the full build graph (language-specific): pipdeptree for Python, mvn dependency:tree for Java, ldd/objdump for native binaries.
   - Mark direct dependencies vs transitive. Mark optional and development-only packages.
   - Create initial allowed_list.txt containing direct runtime deps and explicitly required transitive deps.

2. Static analysis and runtime tracing
   - Static: run a static analyzer to detect unused symbols and large transitive pulls (e.g., cargo-tree features, pip optional extras).
   - Dynamic (recommended): run a representative synthetic workload in an instrumented environment to trace imported modules, opened shared libraries, and loaded plugins. Capture traces.

3. Binary slimming and artifact reduction
   - For Python: produce a wheel that excludes tests, examples, and optional extras. Use auditwheel to repair manylinux wheels but remove development extras. Use pip --no-deps and re-bundle only needed wheels.
   - For native libs: strip symbols (strip --strip-unneeded) and use objcopy to remove debug sections. If using musl builds for smaller images, include musl static runtime only when target requires it.
   - For containers: prefer multi-stage builds that copy only the application artifact and runtime dependencies into the final image. Use distroless / scratch base images when possible.
   - For model weights: store deltas/quantized weights separately from the serving binary; provide a small bootstrap loader that validates quantization metadata.

4. Compatibility shim & runtime contract
   - Provide a minimal runtime shim that implements a narrow API contract (e.g., /v1/infer shim used by systemd service). The shim decouples the model loader from the heavy runtime and makes hotpatching safer.
   - Document ABI/expectations in runtime_contract.txt: supported libc, required kernel features (e.g., io_uring), GPU driver versions, and required device nodes.

5. SBOM, signing, and evidence bundle
   - Generate SBOMs in SPDX and CycloneDX formats for all artifacts. Include package checksums (sha256), origin URL, and build recipe.
   - Sign artifacts and SBOMs with Redwood release key and produce a detached signature (RFC 4880 or PKCS7).
   - Evidence bundle must include: reproducible build recipe, builder VM image reference and checksum, CI build logs (condensed), and a reconciliation matrix mapping each file to an SBOM entry.

6. Validation and field smoke tests
   - Deploy artifact to an isolated test host (airgapped mimic) and run the smoke checklist: startup, health endpoint response, small inference workload, memory and open file descriptor inspection, and a basic latency profile.
   - Validate SBOM entries and signatures; ensure checksums match.

7. Release and operator handoff
   - Publish artifact to the release asset bucket (signed, offline-friendly layout) and populate operator handoff package with: install script, operator checklist, rollback artifact, and forensic evidence bundle.

Binary slimming techniques (detailed)

- Symbol dead stripping: use -ffunction-sections and -Wl,--gc-sections where supported. Combine with link-time optimization to reduce code size.
- Granular feature flags: build logical subcomponents as optional features and disable everything not required for the shipped configuration. Document which features are enabled via features.json.
- Compressed overlay: provide an optional compressed, read-only overlay for rarely used helper utilities; the operator can expand these on demand.
- Filesystem exclusion table: explicit list of excluded paths (tests/, docs/, examples/, benchmarks/) applied by the packaging stage.

SBOM and signing checklist (table style)

Component | SBOM required | Signature | Evidence
--- | ---: | ---: | ---
Application binary | yes | yes | build_recipe.txt, build_log_excerpt
Python wheels | yes | yes | wheel_hashes.txt
Container image layers | yes | yes | layer_manifest.json
Model weights | yes | yes | quant_profile.json, weight_manifest
Builder VM | optional (hash) | yes | vm_manifest.json

Runtime validation matrix (example)

- Kernel: 5.15+ for io_uring features (required for async IO path).
- glibc: 2.33+; if below, must deploy musl static variant.
- NVIDIA driver: 525.x+ for cuBLAS kernels used in the runtime (if GPU mode).
- CUDA: 11.8+ and matching cuDNN as specified in runtime_contract.txt.

Operator installation checklist (short)

1. Verify artifact checksums and detached signatures.
2. Confirm SBOM matches expected inventory and all licenses are acceptable.
3. Dry-run install to ephemeral namespace.
4. Run smoke tests (health, small inference, metrics export).
5. Snapshot logs and collect evidence bundle for customer acceptance.

Rollback and emergency procedures

- Ship a paired rollback artifact with every release: a lightweight manifest pointing to the previous known-good artifact bundle plus a verified reinstall script.
- If reduced functionality is detected after install, operators must: 1) scale service to zero to preserve state; 2) apply rollback artifact; 3) collect forensic evidence (dmesg, health endpoint dumps, last N inference traces) and upload to the secure evidence bucket.

Integration with upgrade-and-rollback playbooks

- This guideline is designed to be compatible with the existing orchestrated rollforward/rollback framework (see related pages). The packaging pipeline emits the compatibility metadata consumed by the canary controller and automated rollback artifact producers.

Appendix A — Example build snippets
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
FROM ubuntu:22.04 AS builder
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential python3-dev
WORKDIR /src
COPY . /src
RUN ./build.sh --target-bundle

FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc
COPY --from=builder /src/out/app /usr/local/bin/app
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/app"]
sections.heading: Minimal multi-stage Dockerfile (excerpt)

sections.body:
cyclonedx-py --format json --output sbom.json --include-licenses

Example signature command (detached, GPG):

gpg --output sbom.json.sig --detach-sign --armor --local-user release@redwood.ai sbom.json

Appendix B — Common pitfalls and mitigations

- Pitfall: large transitive dependency introduced by a minor version bump. Mitigation: add automatic pre-merge check that compares dependency tree size and flags +10% changes.
- Pitfall: non-reproducible builds due to timestamps. Mitigation: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and use deterministic archivers (tar --sort=name --mtime).
- Pitfall: runtime failure due to missing kernel feature. Mitigation: include runtime feature probe in operator preflight and provide static fallback if probe fails.

Revision history

- 2026-01-15 (Priya Nair) — initial published draft.
- 2026-03-10 (Priya Nair) — added SBOM signing examples, expanded rollback checklist and validation matrix.

Related resources

- See the related pages list at the top for airgap delivery and image signing playbooks.

End of document

payload.page_title: Runtime Artifact Provenance and Service Allowlist

sections.body:
This guide defines the runtime artifact provenance model and the operator-maintained service allowlist required for Redwood on-prem packaging. It standardizes:

- artifact metadata (what we record),
- cryptographic signing and attestation processes (how we prove authenticity),
- local verification playbooks (how operators validate before deploy), and
- the service allowlist lifecycle (how services are authorized to run in customer air-gapped or VPC-managed runtimes).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Field operators performing image bake and install
- Release engineers responsible for packaging and attestation
- Security reviewers and compliance teams validating supply-chain evidence
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body: Applies to all on-prem runtime artifacts distributed as part of Redwood Private (control plane agents, runtime images, model bundles, pinned kernels, and local operator tooling). Does NOT cover third-party OS updates (see customer node OS patch policy).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- artifact: any binary, container image, or model bundle that will be installed on customer runtime nodes.
- provenance: metadata that links an artifact back to a build, signer, and verification snapshot.
- attestation: signed statement (and optional predicate) asserting an artifact's properties (build ID, SBOM reference, approved model hash).
- allowlist: curated list of service identifiers (binary SHA256 or container image digest) permitted to execute within the runtime sandbox.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) Minimal trusted surface: provenance must identify the build pipeline and an authorized signer.
2) Deterministic verification: verification steps are automated and repeatable by field operators.
3) Forensic-friendly: telemetry and retention policies preserve enough signals to reconstruct an install timeline for 90 days.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
- name: Artifact filename or image tag
- kind: container | binary | model-bundle
- build_id: CI pipeline run id (e.g. rwd-ci/2026-1023)
- digest: sha256:... (container/image digest or artifact SHA256)
- signer: principal who signed (service account or HSM key id)
- signature: base64 signature reference or external attestation link
- sbom_ref: link to SBOM (cyclonedx/spdx) stored in evidence bucket
- build_time_utc: 2026-01-12T15:23:00Z
- provenance_version: v1 (this document)
- approved_for: list of release channels (onprem-stable, onprem-candidate)
- allowed_services: list of service IDs for initial allowlist population
sections.heading: Provenance metadata schema (human-readable table)

sections.body:
---
name: rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz
kind: binary
build_id: rwd-ci/2026-01234
digest: sha256:8d1f3a...
signer: ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026
signature: s3://rwd-evidence/attestations/rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.sig
sbom_ref: s3://rwd-evidence/sboms/rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.cdx.json
build_time_utc: 2026-01-10T21:08:00Z
provenance_version: v1
approved_for: [onprem-stable]
allowed_services: [rwd-agent, rwd-qos-proxy]
---
sections.heading: Example provenance manifest (YAML snippet)

sections.body:
1) Build pipeline produces artifact and SBOM and records build_id.
2) CI uploads artifact and SBOM to internal artifact registry and registers a provisional provenance manifest.
3) Release engineer triggers attestation: signing key managed in HSM (key id format ksm://hsm-prod/keys/...). Use cosign-compatible workflow; tooling wraps HSM signing.
4) Attestation is pushed to evidence storage (S3/GCS or customer-staged object store) and provenance manifest is updated with signature ref.

Commands (example, adapt per-field tooling):
sections.heading: Signing and attestation flow (operator-facing)

sections.body:
$ rwd-verify --artifact rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz --manifest provenance.yaml
expected output: OK: signature verified by ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026
sections.heading: verify digest and signature locally

sections.body: $ curl -fsS $(jq -r .sbom_ref provenance.yaml) | jq '.components[] | select(.license==null)'
sections.heading: fetch SBOM and quick-check for unexpected packages

sections.body:
1) Confirm manifest provenance_version == v1.
2) Confirm digest matches artifact on disk: sha256sum <file> == digest in manifest.
3) Validate signature against authorized signer key id. Reject if signer not in authorized_signers list.
4) Fetch SBOM and quick audit for banned packages or unexpected runtimes.
5) Validate allowed_services entries map to services in deployment manifest.
6) Record verification result to local operator journal and push minimal telemetry envelope (verification success/failure, build_id, digest) to evidence collector (see telemetry section).
sections.heading: Local verification playbook (pre-install checklist)

sections.body:
- Initial population: During package creation, product leads propose allowed_services; security reviews and field testing gate inclusion.
- Approval: Change proposal goes through release-candidate signoff and is recorded in the allowlist ledger (signed change log stored alongside provenance).
- Operator application: Operators deploy allowlist to the tenant's policy service before first runtime start. The runtime enforces execution by digest comparison.
- Emergency exemption: Operators may temporarily permit a service via a signed operator-exemption token (time-limited, max 4 hours) and must file a post-mortem within 48 hours.
sections.heading: Service allowlist lifecycle

sections.body: rwd-agent|binary|sha256:8d1f3a...|initial deploy|release-engineering@redwood.com|2026-01-12T22:00:00Z
sections.heading: service-id | kind | digest | reason | approved_by | approved_at

sections.body:
- At exec-time the runtime resolver: computes artifact digest -> checks allowlist -> verifies signature cache.
- If either check fails, the runtime denies exec and emits a denial reason to local audit socket.
- A degraded mode exists where the runtime runs minimal quarantined process with network disabled for debugging; this mode requires operator manual approval and records full forensic telemetry.
sections.heading: Enforcement model (runtime)

sections.body:
- Minimum telemetry emitted on verification: build_id, digest, signer_id, verification_result (pass|fail), timestamp, operator_id (if manual).
- Retention window for full verification envelopes: 90 days (default).
- Anonymized digest index (sha256 prefixes) retained 365 days for cross-tenant threat hunting (where customer consented).
- Evidence storage policy: SBOMs and attestations are immutable and versioned for 3 years (to support compliance audits).
sections.heading: Telemetry and retention (forensics-aware)

sections.body:
- Upgrades must pass provenance verification against the target allowlist entry before swap.
- Rollbacks re-apply previously-approved allowlist values and must re-run provenance verification for the rollback artifact (digest and signature).
- If rollback artifact provenance is missing, operators must:
  1) halt automated rollback,
  2) escalate to release team, and
  3) only permit manual rollback with signed operator exemption + recorded justification.
sections.heading: Upgrade and rollback interactions

sections.body:
1) Preflight: rwd-verify --artifact <file> --manifest provenance.yaml
2) Apply allowlist: rwd-allowlist apply --file allowlist.txt --env tenant-1234
3) Start runtime: rwd-runtimectl start --env tenant-1234
4) Validate runtime acceptance: rwd-runtimectl status --env tenant-1234 | grep -E "allowlist|verification"
5) If verification fails, collect traces: rwd-collect-trace --selector verification_failure --out /tmp/forensic-<ts>.tgz and open an object in the evidence bucket.
sections.heading: Operator runbook (quick steps)

sections.body:
- Verification latency: median 1.5s, p95 5s for local verification against cached signer keys.
- Evidence upload: attestation upload must complete within 60s of signing step in CI.
- Operator manual-exemption window: max 4 hours; approval recorded and telemetry emitted immediately.
sections.heading: SLOs and operational thresholds

sections.body:
- Document owner: Maya Thompson (eng-packaging)
- Primary on-call for signing/evidence: release-team-oncall@redwood.com
- Security escalation: sec-ops@redwood.com (pager)

Appendix A — Example audit evidence entry (JSON envelope, single-line):

{"timestamp":"2026-01-12T22:01:05Z","build_id":"rwd-ci/2026-01234","artifact":"rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz","digest":"sha256:8d1f3a...","signer":"ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026","verification_result":"pass","operator":"auto-ci"}

Appendix B — Troubleshooting matrix (common failures):

- signature mismatch: verify HSM key mapping and that artifact digest was not truncated in transit.
- sbom missing: block install; request SBOM from release owner and attach as urgent evidence.
- allowlist absent: reject install; check allowlist ledger for pending approvals.
sections.heading: Owner and escalation

sections.body:
- 2026-01-15: created by Maya Thompson (initial schema and verification playbook).
- 2026-02-10: tightened telemetry retention defaults and added operator-exemption process.
sections.heading: Change log notes

sections.body:
- See model-artifact-supplychain-and-image-attestation-spec for detailed SBOM and attestation predicate formats.
- See container-image-signing-and-verification-playbook for container-specific cosign examples.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Hardware Root-of-Trust Provisioning and Supply Chain Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents a repeatable, auditable process to provision hardware root-of-trust (HRoT) keys, verify firmware supply chain integrity, and maintain chain-of-custody evidence for Redwood Private on-prem appliance deliveries. It is intended for the Private Deployments Field Engineering, On‑Prem Packaging, and Security teams.

Scope: Applies to all customer appliances that include a protected key store (TPM2/HSM/SE), signed firmware, and a Redwood-supplied OS image. Excludes customer-managed HW without Redwood-supplied firmware.

Goals
- Ensure devices boot only trusted, signed images (secure boot enforced).
- Maintain provable chain-of-custody for device key material and firmware artifacts.
- Provide a minimal operator procedure for provisioning, verification, and recovery during field installs.
- Integrate with our evidence collection and audit logging pipeline for compliance requests.

Owner and escalation
- Document owner: On‑Prem Packaging Team (owner_onprem@redwood.ai).
- Security contact: Product Security (ps-team@redwood.ai).
- Field escalation: Field Engineering Lead (field-lead@redwood.ai).
- SLA for support: 24×7 for P1, response within 1 hour.

Key terms and components
- HRoT: Hardware Root of Trust (device-bound key pair provisioned into TPM/HSM/SE).
- Provisioning Authority (PA): Redwood role responsible for generating and signing device manifests and firmware (service: provisioning.redwood.internal).
- Device Manifest: JSON artifact that binds hardware identifiers to expected firmware hashes and vendor attestation statements.
- Chain-of-Custody Log: Append-only log (S3-compatible) holding signatures and handoff events for each device batch.

High-level flow
1. Vendor manufacturing -> initial device hardware IDs (serial, HW UUID) and vendor attestation statements.
2. Redwood PA creates device manifests and generates provisioning requests.
3. Devices shipped to field with sealed provisioning token (optional) or provisioned in factory.
4. Field operator executes provisioning checklist; device performs TPM-backed key injection or HSM pin provisioning.
5. Post-provision verification: secure-boot measurement, firmware hash match, and chain-of-custody upload.
6. Acceptance tests and handoff to Customer Success.

Pre-deployment requirements (vendor checklist)
| Item | Required format | Responsible | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Device serial and HW UUID export | CSV (serial, hw_uuid, mac, batch_id) | Vendor | No duplicates, signed by vendor key (PEM) |
| Firmware signed binary | COSE signature over image | Vendor | Verified by Redwood root key; RFC-compliant signature |
| Secure element provisioning support | TPM2 or secure element driver | Vendor | tpm2_pcrread produces expected PCRs |
| Transport packaging tamper-evidence | Tamper sticker ID list | Vendor | Sticker IDs included in chain-of-custody CSV |

Artifact formats and example
- Device manifest (example):
{
  "device_serial": "RWD-APPL-000123",
  "hw_uuid": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-11ec-8fea-0242ac120002",
  "batch_id": "batch-2026-02-01-az1",
  "bootloader_hash": "sha256:3a1f...",
  "kernel_hash": "sha256:7b4c...",
  "firmware_signer": "vendor-a@example.com",
  "attestation_statement_uri": "https://vendor.example.com/attestations/RWD-APPL-000123.sig"
}

Operator provisioning checklist (field)
1. Verify vendor CSV and chain-of-custody signatures:
   - Command: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-coc/batch-2026-02-01/csvs/vendor-list.csv .
   - Validate signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify vendor-ca.pub -signature vendor-list.sig vendor-list.csv
2. Connect to device console and confirm HW UUID:
   - Command: sudo redwood-util device-info --serial
   - Expected output contains hw_uuid from vendor CSV.
3. If using sealed provisioning token: unlock token with operator OTP (single-use).
4. Run provisioning agent: sudo redwood-provision --manifest ./RWD-APPL-000123.manifest.json --mode=field
5. Confirm TPM key present: tpm2_getpubek && tpm2_readpublic -c 0x81010001
6. Verify secure boot measurement matches manifest: redwood-verify-image --manifest ./RWD-APPL-000123.manifest.json
7. Upload local evidence bundle: tar czf evidence-RWD-APPL-000123.tgz /var/log/redwood-provision && curl -X POST -F file=@evidence... https://ingest.redwood.internal/coc/upload

Acceptance criteria (field)
- Device boots to Redwood OS login within 90 seconds.
- Secure-boot chain validated: bootloader_hash and kernel_hash match manifest.
- TPM-backed device key available and exported public-key uploaded to PA.
- Evidence bundle present in chain-of-custody S3 and associated to device_serial.

Telemetry and SLOs
- Provisioning success rate per batch: target 99.5% (alert if < 98%).
- Average field provisioning time: target <= 20 minutes per device.
- Evidence upload latency: target < 5 minutes.
- Telemetry coverage: boot measurement + provisioning logs + transport tamper flag.

Security controls and KMS integration
- Root signing keys are stored in HSM (AWS CloudHSM / on-prem HSM). Production signing operations require 2/3 operator approval for new vendor roots.
- Device certificates are X.509 with CN=device_serial and EK binding. Private keys never leave TPM or HSM.
- Key rotation policy: PA rotates intermediate signing keys every 12 months; root keys rotate every 24 months with documented rollback window.

Firmware rollout and canary strategy
- Canary batch size: 1% of devices in a controlled site (min 3 devices).
- Rollout stages: canary -> staged (10%) -> broad (50%) -> full (100%).
- Monitoring signals: boot-failure-rate, request-latency, kernel oops count.
- Automatic halt on: >2% increase in boot failures vs baseline sustained for 15 minutes.

Rollback and recovery procedures
1. If a firmware canary fails verification repeatedly: trigger halt and notify Product Security and Field Engineering.
2. Remote rollback path (if supported): sign and publish previous manifest with role=recovery, then trigger remote update via management plane.
   - Example command: redwood-update --device RWD-APPL-000123 --manifest recovery-manifest.json --force
3. Manual recovery: instruct operator to boot to recovery USB image with signed kernel and run redwood-recover --restore-factory-keys.
4. If device key is suspected compromised: place device into quarantine and schedule secure erase and re-provision.

Audit evidence and compliance package
- Evidence artifacts per device: vendor CSV (signed), manifest (signed by PA), provisioning logs (signed), evidence bundle (uploaded), tamper-sticker photo (optional).
- Retention: chain-of-custody logs retained 7 years for regulated customers (configurable per contract).
- Sample audit export command:
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-coc/batch-2026-02-01/evidence/RWD-APPL-000123.tgz ./ && tar -tvzf evidence-RWD-APPL-000123.tgz

Operational runbook: common failure modes and remediations
- Failure: TPM provisioning fails with PCR mismatch.
  - Check vendor manifest PCR expectations vs device PCR: tpm2_pcrread sha256: tpm2_pcrread sha256:all
  - Remediation: attempt re-provision, if persistent, return device to vendor and mark batch for investigation.
- Failure: Evidence upload fails due to TLS cert validation.
  - Check system time and CA bundle: date && ls /etc/ssl/certs && curl -v https://ingest.redwood.internal/health
  - Remediation: temporarily store evidence locally and retry; escalate if fails >30 min.
- Failure: Secure boot validation mismatch after field update.
  - Compare manifest hashes to image on device: sha256sum /boot/bootloader.bin && grep bootloader_hash manifest.json
  - Remediation: if image diverged and not signed by vendor/PA, isolate and investigate for tampering.

Change control and vendor onboarding playbooks
- New vendor onboarding requires: SOX/ISO supplier attestation form, test batch (10 devices) shipped to Redwood lab, manifest schema verification, and shared private key exchange process to support signature verification.
- Vendor must support: online attestation statements (HTTPS), per-device signed manifests, and an offline revocation list endpoint.

Testing and CI hooks
- CI pipeline must: verify signed firmware artifacts using the PA public key before releasing images to customers. Sample CI step (Bash):
  openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pa-root.pub -signature firmware.img.sig firmware.img || exit 1
- Reproducible build policy: all firmware builds must produce deterministic artifacts with recorded build environment (docker hash, buildargs) stored with the manifest.

Appendices
A. Minimal manifest schema (required fields): device_serial, hw_uuid, batch_id, bootloader_hash, kernel_hash, firmware_signer, attestation_statement_uri, manifest_signature.
B. Useful commands: tpm2_getcap -c handles | tpm2_readpublic -c 0x81010001 | redwood-verify-image --help
C. Contacts and ticket templates: use `PROV-<BATCH-ID>` prefix for all JIRA tickets; include: device_serial, manifest_sha256, evidence_s3_path, contact_field_engineer.

Related documents
- On-presence attestation checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/ephemeral-boot-and-attestation-playbook-2026
- Private deploy telemetry & ingestion contract: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026

Revision history
- 2026-02-15: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-22: Added CI examples and canary thresholds (reviewers: Priya Shah).
- 2026-03-02: Hardened rollback steps and updated SLOs (approved).

payload.page_title: Field certification, tenant burn-in, and operator runbook for private deployments

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines the field certification and tenant burn-in program for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem), plus an operator runbook to guide installation teams through post-install validation, acceptance, and safe handoff to steady-state operations. It is intended for field engineers, SREs, integration engineers, and customer success teams.

Scope
- Applies to all private deployments delivered with Redwood-managed control plane or customer-managed control plane.
- Covers hardware and firmware verification, runtime sanity tests, tenant-specific workload burn-in, telemetry contract validation, licensing and KMS key rotation, and defined acceptance criteria for Customer Acceptance Testing (CAT).

Assumptions and prerequisites
- Operator has network access to customer telemetry endpoints as specified in the integration contract.
- Images and packages are signed (see container-image-signing-and-verification-playbook).
- Required keys and certificates are provisioned in the target KMS/HSM and accessible to the installation environment.

Approval and ownership
- Program owner: eng-private-deployments Field Engineering (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Certification authority: Security & Compliance (reviewer: Dr. Lena Fischer)
- Final acceptance signer: Customer Success lead for the customer account

High-level workflow (summary)
1. Pre-flight verification (lab)
2. Field install and bootstrap
3. Hardware & firmware attestation
4. Runtime smoke and KV/Prefix cache warmup
5. Tenant-specific synthetic burn-in (hours or days depending on SLAs)
6. Telemetry validation and evidence collection
7. CAT sign-off and handoff to operations

Detailed procedures

1) Pre-flight verification (lab stage)
- Duration: 2–8 hours per image revision.
- Steps:
  a. Verify signed images match shipped digest: sha256 checksums for every artifact.
  b. Run the offline acceptance harness: run the included sim-workload-suite for 90 minutes at nominal QPS and 30 minutes at 2x expected QPS.
  c. Execute KV cache persistence tests: write/read sequences for 1M keys simulated across shard boundaries.
  d. Run thermals/thermal-cycling in lab for new hardware SKUs: 3 cycles at 80% sustained GPU utilization.
- Exit criteria: all tests green; any critical failure escalated to Release Engineering.

2) Field install & bootstrap checklist
- Owner: Field Engineer (primary), Customer Onsite Technician (secondary).
- Minimum checklist (operator marks pass/fail):
  - [ ] Rack/power verification and PDU mapping matches network diagram.
  - [ ] Firmware baseline (BMC, NIC, GPU firmware) recorded in deployment manifest.
  - [ ] Network ACLs and BGP/peering verified for control-plane proxies.
  - [ ] Local time/sync (NTP/PTP) configured and validated.
  - [ ] HSM/KMS connectivity verified with sample signing operation.
  - [ ] Image accounts and service tokens installed to ephemeral operator account.

3) Hardware & firmware attestation
- Procedure:
  1. Run attestation tooling (hw-attestctl attest --output json) and capture signed statement.
  2. Validate measured boot log and firmware signatures match manifest.
  3. Record telemetry: serial numbers, SKU, NIC MACs, PCB revision, firmware versions.
- Failure modes and mitigations:
  - If measured boot fails: collect logs and isolate node; do not join node to cluster.
  - If firmware mismatch: consult firmware-rollback policy and vendor-supplied signed images.

4) Runtime smoke and KV/prefix cache warmup
- Goals: confirm runtime can load models, serve requests, and persist KV metadata without errors.
- Commands (example snippets):
  - curl -X POST https://local-runtime/healthz -H 'Authorization: Bearer <op-token>'
  - rdbtool kv-sanity --endpoint https://local-kv --verify 10000
- Smoke test checklist:
  - [ ] Model load success for primary model variant (<= 30s cold load).
  - [ ] Inference query at 1 qps/replica returns 95% < 350ms.
  - [ ] KV read/write P99 < 25ms for local SSD-backed KV.

5) Tenant-specific synthetic burn-in (critical section)
- Purpose: expose model-serving, routing, caching, and multitenancy isolation issues prior to production traffic.
- Duration guidance:
  - Small tenants (<= 10 RPS): 6–12 hours.
  - Medium tenants (10–200 RPS): 24–72 hours.
  - Large tenants (> 200 RPS): 72–168 hours with scheduled load ramps.
- Synthetic workload design:
  - Use the tenant's representative prompt set (provided during onboarding) plus fuzzed sequences to exercise length distributions.
  - Include a 10% injection of adversarial/edge prompts to check guardrails.
  - Ramp profile: 0→25% QPS 30 minutes, hold 1h; 25→75% 2h; 75→100% 1h; maintain 100% for X hours as per tenant size.
- Observability checks (automated):
  - Model error rate (bad-inference or empty responses) < 0.5%
  - Token-level cost variance within expected bounds ±15%
  - KV cache hit-rate target: >= 65% after warmup for prefix-heavy workloads
  - Tail latency SLOs: P95 < 300ms, P99 < 700ms (adjust per SLO matrix)
- Operator actions on alarm:
  1. If error rate spikes > 1% for 10 minutes: pause synthetic load, collect core dumps, escalate to runtime-engineering.
  2. If P99 increases by >2x baseline: enable fallback model variant routing and notify customer success.

6) Telemetry validation and evidence collection
- Required telemetry streams:
  - Inference traces (sampling 1/1000 requests or 1% whichever is higher).
  - Token accounting (per-request token counts, model id, quantization flag).
  - Hardware telemetry (GPU temp, power, ECC/memory errors).
  - Network metrics (egress RTT, packet drops), and control-plane heartbeats.
- Evidence bundle to produce for CAT:
  - Signed attestation statement (hardware + firmware).
  - Burn-in report (load profile, duration, pass/fail with timestamps).
  - Observability extract: p95/p99 latencies, error rates, KV hit rates, per-tenant token accounting for the burn-in window.
  - Container/image digests and deployment manifest.
- Storage format: compressed tar.gz with SHA256 checksum and two copies: one uploaded to customer evidence bucket and one retained in Redwood secure evidence store for 90 days.

7) Licensing and KMS rotation (during pre-handoff but part of certification)
- Steps to rotate operator license and customer KMS keys post-install:
  1. Generate ephemeral rotation token (use operator-rot-tool rotate --mode ephemeral).
  2. Push new key material to HSM via vendor API; confirm key id and wrap key metadata.
  3. Run integration smoke to decrypt a sample secret and sign a token.
  4. Record rotation event to audit log and tag evidence bundle.
- Rollback: if new key fails validation, revert to previous key and schedule controlled re-rotate with vendor support.

8) Customer Acceptance Testing (CAT) and handoff
- CAT acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied):
  - Hardware attestation present and signed.
  - Burn-in completed with no critical failures and all telemetry targets met.
  - Security checklist: KMS attested, agent/collector configured, RBAC bindings verified.
  - Performance checklist: P95 and P99 within SLO band per customer SLA.
- Handoff artifacts provided to customer: operator runbook, evidence bundle, support contact matrix, and rollback playbook.
- Sign-off template: Customer Success provides signed acceptance email referencing the evidence bundle digest and the date/time.

Operator runbook (post-CAT steady-state checks)
- Daily checks (5–10 minutes) by operator or automated job:
  - Verify control-plane heartbeats for all tenants.
  - Ensure telemetry ingest rate is within expected window (alert if < 60% of expected).
  - Check for any ECC or GPU hardware errors reported in last 24h.
- Weekly checks:
  - Refresh of agent TLS certs in staging and canary.
  - Review top-20 slow queries and token cost drift.
- Incident quick actions (first 30 minutes):
  1. If runtime is unresponsive: run safe-degrader (runtimectl degrade --mode read-only) to preserve state while maintaining basic API surface.
  2. If KV corruption suspected: snapshot current state, enable read-only mode, initiate kv-verify job.
  3. If thermal event: move traffic away from affected node(s) and coordinate with field replacement.

Upgrade and rollback guidance (concise)
- Recommended pattern: automated canary → staged rollout → safety window → full rollout.
- Safety gates prior to stage promotion:
  - Canary stable for 2h at canary traffic or 1k requests (whichever greater) with no more than 0.2% error increase.
  - Telemetry ingestion continuity and auto-scaling behaved within thresholds.
- Immediate rollback triggers:
  - Canary error increase > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - P99 latency regression > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Rollback procedure summary:
  1. Pause further promotions.
  2. Promote previous revision for affected replicas using operator canary control panel.
  3. Run smoke tests and confirm with APM traces that service recovered.
  4. Open RCA ticket and engage release engineering.

Checklist: Field certification acceptance matrix (table)
- Represented here as a plain ASCII table for portability. Operators must produce a matrix with checkmarks as part of evidence.

Item | Responsible | Target | Pass criteria
-----|-------------|--------|------------
Hardware attestation | Field Eng | Before join | Signed statement present
Image digests verified | Field Eng | Pre-boot | sha256 match for all images
Model load smoke | Runtime Eng | Post-bootstrap | Primary model loads in <=30s
Synthetic burn-in | Field Eng | Per SLA | Pass per tenant size guidance
Telemetry contract | Observability | During burn-in | Required streams present and sampled
KMS validation | Security | Pre-handoff | Decrypt/sign test succeed
CAT sign-off | Customer Success | Post-burn-in | Signed acceptance and evidence uploaded

Evidence retention and compliance
- Retain evidence bundles for 90 days in secure store; snapshot metadata retained for 3 years per contract.
- For regulated customers, escalate to compliance team for longer retention windows and provide audit-ready exports.

Templates and automation (links and CLI examples)
- burnin-runner.yaml (sample job config)
  - description: config for tenant synthetic run including ramp profile, prompt sets, and fuzz rules.
  - required fields: tenant_id, prompt_set_id, qps_profile, duration_hours, edge_injection_pct
- Example command to run a burn-in job:
  rdb-burnin submit --tenant tenant-123 --config burnin-runner.yaml --report-out /tmp/burnin-report.tar.gz

Troubleshooting guide (common issues)
- Model fails to load intermittently: check model shard mapping and GPU memory pressure; run gpu-mem-profile and compare to model footprint matrix.
- KV read errors under load: inspect disk IO wait and concurrent garbage collection; consider increasing local IO throughput or moving shards.
- Telemetry gaps: ensure agent has outbound connectivity to ingest endpoints and verify agent policy for sample rate.

Postmortem and RCA expectations for certification failures
- Any certification failure that blocks CAT must produce a 48h preliminary incident report with: timeline, impact, immediate mitigations, owner, and next steps. Full RCA within 7 business days.

Appendices
A. Example burn-in ramp profile YAML (simplified)
---
qps_profile:
  - duration_mins: 30
    target_qps_pct: 25
  - duration_mins: 60
    target_qps_pct: 75
  - duration_mins: 120
    target_qps_pct: 100
edge_injection_pct: 10
prompt_set_id: promptset-tenant-123
---

B. Acceptance email template
Subject: CAT Acceptance - <customer> - <deployment-id>
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
We have completed field certification and tenant burn-in for deployment <deployment-id>. Evidence bundle digest: <sha256>. All acceptance criteria met as of <datetime>. Please reply to confirm acceptance.

C. Contact matrix
- Field Eng (on-call): +1-555-0101, field-eng@redwood.ai
- Runtime SRE: runtime-sre@redwood.ai
- Customer Success: cs-team@redwood.ai

D. Quick links
- Related runbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/field-ops-checklist-model-swap-rollback-cookbook-2026

Change log
