payload.page_title: Model weights rolling refresh and local cache sizing recommendations

sections.body: This document provides an operator-focused playbook for safely performing rolling refreshes of model weight artifacts and for sizing the local model-weights cache on on-prem / air-gapped private deployments. It covers goals, risk model, telemetry and SLOs, a step-by-step rolling update procedure, sizing guidelines and worked examples, rollback triggers, and verification checks for day-2 operations.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Field operators and site reliability engineers responsible for private deployments
- Release engineers coordinating model artifact updates
- Support engineers validating customer acceptance after a refresh
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body: Model weight refreshes (new model versions, quantized artifacts, or security-patched artifacts) are high-impact operations for private deployments. Improper refreshes can cause repeated cold-starts, evict critical KV cache entries, and cause tail-latency regressions. A carefully controlled rolling refresh plus conservative local cache sizing reduces customer-visible disruptions while still allowing frequent model updates.
sections.heading: Why this matters

sections.body:
- Goal: Replace weights with minimal 99th-percentile latency regression (<10% relative) and no more than 1% sustained error-rate increase per tenant during the operation.
- Constraint: Limited local disk and memory on edge appliances; intermittent upstream connectivity for air-gapped refreshes.
- Safety: Any automated step must be reversible; manual approval gates for major-architecture swaps (e.g., FP16->quantized INT8).
sections.heading: Goals and constraints

sections.body:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Operations (oncall: private-deploy-ops).
- Release owner: model-onboarding team (contact: model-release@redwood.example.com).
- Escalation path: operator -> field-ops lead -> SRE -> oncall product-eng. See related_pages for contact pages.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor before, during, and after refresh:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for inference calls per tenant and per route.
- Error rate: HTTP 5xx and application-level model failures (tokenization/decoding errors).
- Cold-starts per minute: number of new model-container initializations.
- Disk pressure: % used of weights-cache mount; inode exhaustion.
- Memory pressure: RSS and OOM events on runtime processes.
- Avail: service healthy checks and per-model readiness probes.
SLO thresholds used by operators: p99 increase <10% (relative), error-rate delta <1% absolute, cold-start rate <3/min per node during steady state.

Local model-weights cache sizing recommendations (summary table):
- Small footprint sites (single-rack, latency-sensitive dev sites): allocate 2x working-set weights on disk, 1x working-set in RAM for memory-mapped access.
- Medium sites (2–8 GPU nodes): allocate 1.5x working-set on disk, 0.75x working-set in RAM.
- Large sites (>=8 GPU nodes, multi-tenant): allocate 1.2x working-set on disk, 0.5x working-set in RAM and rely on shared NFS/central storage for cold artifacts.
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation

sections.body:
| Site class | Typical concurrent models | Per-model artifact size | Working set (models) | Disk buffer | Recommended disk cache | Recommended RAM for mmap | Notes |
| Small | 1–3 | 18 GB | 2 | 36 GB | 72 GB | 18 GB | Single-rack dev / proof-of-concept |
| Medium | 4–16 | 18 GB | 6 | 36 GB | 108 GB | 12 GB | Production pilot clusters |
| Large | 16+ | 18–140 GB | 10 | 40 GB | 220 GB | 30–60 GB | Multi-tenant with varied model sizes |
sections.heading: Sizing table (worked example)

sections.body:
- estimated_working_set = sum(peak_concurrent_models_expected * per_model_size)
- disk_cache = round_up(estimated_working_set * disk_multiplier + disk_buffer)
- ram_mmap = round_up(estimated_working_set * ram_multiplier)
Suggested multipliers: disk_multiplier = 1.2 (large) to 2.0 (small), ram_multiplier = 0.5 (large) to 1.0 (small).
sections.heading: Sizing formula (operators)

sections.body:
1) Validate artifact integrity: verify PGP signature and checksum of model artifact bundle.
2) Confirm storage availability: free_space >= disk_cache + 10% slack.
3) Confirm runtime compatibility: artifact schema vX <= supported_runtime_schema_vY.
4) Snapshot existing state: collect KV-cache manifests, running container PID lists, and model readiness endpoints.
5) Scheduling window: confirm maintenance window and stakeholder notification.
6) Rollback plan: pre-stage previous artifact and test local restore on a non-production node.

Rolling refresh procedure (safe-by-default, minimal disruption):
1) Stage artifacts to a central staging bucket accessible to nodes (airgap: ship via OTA bundle and verification script).
2) On each node, in a staggered sequence (one node every N minutes depending on cluster size), perform:
   a) Pause new model placements: set cluster routing weight to 0 for node (or cordon node in k8s).
   b) Drain in-flight requests: wait for active_request_count == 0 or timeout (recommended 30s–90s).
   c) Fetch && verify artifact bundle: verify checksum + signature.
   d) Place artifact into local weights cache under a new versioned directory (do not overwrite in-place).
   e) Restart model runtime process with versioned artifact path (graceful reload path preferred to full restart).
   f) Run smoke tests: send sample prompts (happy path + 2 regression prompts) and validate outputs and latency.
   g) If smoke tests pass, reintroduce node to routing pool (uncordon) and monitor for 10 minutes for tail-latency regressions.
   h) If smoke tests fail or tail latency spikes > p99 threshold, trigger automatic rollback for that node.
3) Continue sequence across nodes until zero nodes remain on old version.
4) Post-refresh validation: run tenant-level synthetic workloads for 30–60 minutes and verify telemetry targets.
sections.heading: Preflight checklist (required)

sections.body:
- Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node-name>
- Drain: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
- Install artifact (example): /opt/redwood/bin/install_weights.sh --bundle /staging/model-v2.bundle --dest /var/lib/redwood/weights/model-v2 --verify
- Restart runtime: systemctl restart redwood-runtime.service
- Smoke test example (curl): curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/predict -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq '.latency_ms, .status'
sections.heading: Commands and examples (kubernetes-based appliance example)

sections.body:
- Node-level rollback: if smoke tests fail, restore previous symlinked artifact and run graceful-reload; if reload not supported, restart runtime with previous binary.
- Cluster-level rollback: if systemic regression is observed across >25% of nodes, immediately stop rolling updates, mark release as suspect, and coordinate a cluster rollback via the release owner.
- Eviction storms: if disk pressure causes weights eviction during refresh, pause rollout and increase disk cache or reduce resident working set by temporarily reducing model placements.
sections.heading: Rollback and failure modes

sections.body:
- preload_on_start: boolean (true recommended) — preload weights into mmap to avoid high-latency first requests.
- mmap_prefault_pages: integer — number of pages to prefault at startup to reduce first-request tail latency (default 0; 65536 for high-memory nodes).
- max_concurrent_reload: integer — limit concurrent reloads on a node to avoid OOM.
- background_eviction_threshold_pct: 75 — start background eviction only above this disk usage to avoid premature churn.
sections.heading: Operational safety knobs and runtime flags

sections.body:
1) Acceptance synthetic suite (provided by model-onboarding): pass rate >= 99/100 prompts.
2) Latency: p99 not exceed pre-release baseline by >10%.
3) Resource stability: no OOMs; no sustained CPU > 85% for >5 minutes.
4) Telemetry: ensure logs include "weights:loaded:OK" per node in the last 5 minutes.
sections.heading: Verification and acceptance tests (post-refresh)

sections.body:
- Never overwrite existing weight directories in-place; use versioned directories and atomically switch symlinks. This avoids partial artifact corruption on interruption.
- Prefer graceful reload hooks over full process restart to retain warmed KV-caches where possible.
- For air-gapped sites, include a small bootstrap agent that can verify and stage bundles offline; operators reported a 40% reduction in human errors when using a signed bundle installer.

Appendix A: Example artifact layout on node:
/var/lib/redwood/weights/
  model-v1/ (sha256-abc...)
  model-v2/ (sha256-def...)
  current -> model-v1

Appendix B: Quick checklist for small sites (1–3 nodes):
- Pre-copy bundle to all nodes via scp; verify checksums locally.
- Stagger refresh with 30–60s between nodes.
- Keep a local fallback copy of previous artifact on each node for immediate rollback.

Appendix C: Contact and reference links:
- Model release playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/operator-handback-and-custodian-rollforward-playbook-2026
- KV-cache migration guide: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025

If you discover gaps or want this procedure automated in the operator toolkit, open a PR against infra-operator-scripts and tag eng-private-deployments@redwood.example.com.
sections.heading: Operational tips and lessons learned from field installs

payload.page_title: Offline artifact delivery and model refresh operator runbook

sections.body:
Summary

This runbook describes the operator-level steps, verification checks, and rollback procedures for delivering model artifacts to air-gapped or VPC-private Redwood Private deployments and performing a safe model refresh (hot-swap or staged rollout). It covers secure artifact packaging, transport validation, HSM/KMS verification, on-host ingestion, staged rollout patterns, automated health checks, and troubleshooting. Intended audience: field operators, platform engineers, and customer SREs running private deployments.

Goals and SLOs

- Goal: Replace a model bundle in an offline/private environment with minimal downtime and provable integrity.
- SLO: Model refresh completion within the operator maintenance window (default 30 minutes for small changes, 90 minutes for full model swap) 95% of the time.
- Safety constraints: No automatic switch to a new artifact unless all verification gates pass.

Ownership

- Primary executor: Field Operator / Platform Engineer (on-call operator).
- Reviewer/approver: Deployment Custodian (customer or Redwood field lead).
- Backup: Remote Escalation to Redwood Private Deployments team (pager).

Prerequisites and environment checklist

1) Pre-flight (remote before artifact export):
   - Confirm approved change request: CR-ID (vendor or customer) and signed acceptance.
   - Verify package manifest and signed digest are present in the artifacts registry (S3, GCS, or internal registry).
   - Ensure operator has the following: dev laptop with USB-A/USB-C transfer tools, signed access token (expiration >= 6 hours), and the vendor-supplied manifest.

2) Target environment (on-prem or VPC):
   - KV-store (redis) and serving runtime versions must match compatibility matrix (see Compatibility table below).
   - Node-level disk free >= 50GB (recommended) and memory headroom for model load (see resource table).
   - HSM/KMS accessible: either network HSM (for VPC) or local hardware token (for airgapped sites) with operator key escrow details.

Compatibility table (example)

| Component | Minimum supported | Verified for this run | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Serving runtime | 1.8.2 | 1.9.0 | Runtime picks specific kernels for quantized models |
| KV cache format | v2 | v2 | v2->v3 migrations require pre-warm step |
| Model bundle format | rbf-2025-10 | rbf-2026-01 | rbf-2026-01 supports delta patches |
| On-host agent | 3.4.x | 3.4.1 | Feature flag for atomic-swap required |

Artifact packaging requirements

Each model bundle must include the following files at top level of the artifact tarball (.tar.gz or .zip):
- model.bin (binary weights or shard list)
- model.metadata.json (see example below)
- model.manifest.sig (detached signature; signed by Redwood release key or customer-signed key)
- checksums.sha256 (SHA-256 sums of artifact contents)
- compatibility.txt (runtime and kv-cache constraints)

Example model.metadata.json (operator should validate locally):

```
{
  "model_name": "rw-opt-13b-q4_0",
  "variant": "quantized-q4_0",
  "version": "2026-05-01",
  "shards": 4,
  "size_bytes": 14000000000,
  "created_by": "redwood-release-bot@redwood.ai",
  "notes": "delta-patch-ready"
}
```

Transport and delivery patterns

There are three recommended delivery methods depending on customer connectivity:

A) Encrypted network transfer (VPC with egress to secured artifact gateway):
   - Use the internal artifact gateway with TLS mutual auth. Transfer command (example):

   curl --key operator.key.pem --cert operator.crt.pem --cacert gateway-ca.pem \
     -F "artifact=@/tmp/rw-opt-13b-q4_0-2026-05-01.tar.gz" \
     https://artifact-gateway.internal.redwood/api/v1/upload

   - Verify gateway returned upload_id and that server-side checksum matches checksums.sha256.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Export artifact from build farm to an encrypted thumbdrive using vendor tooling. Use LUKS or BitLocker with a randomly generated passphrase exchanged via an out-of-band channel (phone or secure chat with OTP).
   2. Maintain chain-of-custody log: operator name, time, thumbdrive ID, CRC of transfer.

C) Shuttle appliance (for large datasets > 100GB):
   - Use Redwood-certified shuttle appliance. Follow appliance manifest signing flow and use the provided transfer client (shuttle-client v2+).

Signature and integrity verification (mandatory)

All artifact arrivals must pass cryptographic checks before ingestion. Steps:
1) Verify checksums: `sha256sum -c checksums.sha256` should report `OK` for every file.
2) Verify detached signature: `openssl cms -verify -in model.manifest.sig -content model.metadata.json -CAfile release-certs.pem` (or use `gpg --verify` for GPG-signed manifests).
3) Verify manifest fields against a local allowlist (expected model_name, version range, shard count).
4) HSM/KMS verification: if the artifact is encrypted with customer key, run `kms-client decrypt --key-id alias/customer-model-key --input model.bin.enc --output model.bin` and validate HMAC in `checksums.sha256`.

On-host ingestion sequence (safe mode)

1) Quiesce new traffic: set runtime flag `--accept-new-models=false` and drain short-lived requests. This preserves in-flight responses and keeps cold starts predictable.
2) Create a staging directory with unique timestamp: `/var/lib/redwood/staging/model-2026-05-01-timestamp/`
3) Copy artifact to staging and run verification steps from previous section on-host.
4) Unpack into staging and run container-level smoke load: `./bin/model-verify --warm --max-requests 20 --kv-preload` (the agent provides this helper). Expected exit code 0.
5) Validate runtime telemetry: check `model_load_time < 60s` and `initial_memory_rss < 90% of node free memory` in agent logs.

Staged rollout patterns (choose one)
sections.heading: B) Physical transfer (airgapped sites)

sections.body:
1. Add new model to the runtime but keep traffic weight = 0.
   2. Configure synthetic traffic generator to send 1% of production-equivalent traffic (10 qps or min(1% of avg qps, 20 qps)).
   3. Observe SLOs for 30 minutes: latency p95 < 2x baseline, error rate < 0.5%.
   4. If stable, increase weight in exponential steps (1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with 15–30 minute observation windows.

B) Atomic swap (fast path for non-breaking quantization fallback):
   - Perform a single atomic endpoint switch after pre-warm. Requires `--atomic-swap` enabled. Backup snapshot is kept for 15 minutes before garbage collection.

Automated health checks and telemetry gating (must pass before advancing)

- Health checks: `model_ready` metric, `kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.6`, `latency_p95 < baseline * 1.5`, `error_rate < baseline + 0.25%`.
- Telemetry sources: per-node agent, control-plane trace, and synthetic client.
- Gate: all checks must be green for two consecutive windows to proceed.

Rollback and emergency backout
sections.heading: A) Canary (recommended for critical customers)

sections.body:
1) If canary/atomic swap fails, immediately set traffic weight back to previous model (control-plane API call). Example API call:

POST https://control-plane.internal.redwood/api/v1/models/{endpoint}/traffic-shift
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "from": "rw-opt-13b-q4_0:2026-05-01",
  "to": "rw-opt-13b-q4_0:2026-04-15",
  "weight": 100
}

2) If node-level memory pressure or OOM observed, execute emergency kill (on operator judgement) and restart runtime with previous snapshot: `systemctl restart redwood-runtime && /usr/local/bin/redwood-restore --snapshot /var/backups/model-snapshot-2026-04-15.tar.gz`

Forensic evidence collection (post-failure)

- Save staging directory, `/var/log/redwood/agent.log` (last 5000 lines), and `journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "-2h" > /tmp/runtime-journal.log`.
- Preserve checksums and manifest, and forward to Redwood forensic bucket (via secured transfer) within the customer-approved retention policy.

Operator checklist (short)

1) Confirm CR and maintenance window.
2) Validate artifact signature and checksums.
3) Quiesce new connections and stage artifact.
4) Run container smoke tests and telemetry validations.
5) Execute canary or atomic swap as per policy.
6) Observe telemetry gates, then ramp to 100% if green.
7) If failure, perform rollback steps and collect forensic data.

Troubleshooting and common failure modes

- Failed signature verification: ensure operator has the correct release-certs.pem. If missing, escalate to Release Engineering.
- HSM decryption timeout: Check network path to KMS, verify operator token validity, and re-run with `--kms-retry 3`.
- High cold-start latency: ensure KV preload completed and increase pre-warm threads `--prewarm-threads` by +2.
- Serving runtime rejects shards: verify `shards` count in model.metadata.json and confirm shard placement in `/etc/redwood/shard-map.json`

Audit and evidence log format (minimum fields)

- operator, timestamp (UTC), artifact_id, transfer_method, signature_key_id, preflight_checks_passed (true/false), canary_result (pass/fail), rollback_invoked (true/false)

Sample audit line (CSV)

operator,timestamp,artifact_id,transfer_method,signature_key_id,preflight_checks_passed,canary_result,rollback_invoked
mtthompson,2026-05-12T11:05:12Z,rw-opt-13b-q4_0-2026-05-01,physical,B2F3-RELEASE-2026,true,pass,false

Related pages and references

- /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026
- /confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-acceptance-and-smoke-validation-2026
- KMS/HSM operator quick reference (internal link)

Appendix: quick commands
sections.heading: Immediate rollback (fast)

sections.body: sha256sum -c checksums.sha256
sections.heading: Verify checksum

sections.body: openssl cms -verify -in model.manifest.sig -content model.metadata.json -CAfile /etc/redwood/release-certs.pem -out /dev/null && echo "signature OK"
sections.heading: Verify signature (CMS)

sections.body:
mkdir -p /var/lib/redwood/staging/model-2026-05-01-timestamp && tar -xzvf /tmp/artifact.tar.gz -C /var/lib/redwood/staging/model-2026-05-01-timestamp && /usr/local/bin/model-verify --path /var/lib/redwood/staging/model-2026-05-01-timestamp

Change log and revision history

- 2026-02-10: Initial draft by Maya Thompson.
- 2026-03-18: Added canary gating metrics and telemetry thresholds (reviewer Arjun Patel).
- 2026-05-12: Hardened HSM validation steps and added physical transfer chain-of-custody template (reviewer Sofia Kim).
sections.heading: Unpack into staging and run verify helper

payload.page_title: Offline bundle format and manifest (Redwood Private on-prem/air-gapped)

sections.body:
This page defines the **offline bundle** file format used to install or upgrade **Redwood Private** in **air-gapped / offline** environments. It specifies:
- Bundle layout (directory structure + required artifacts)
- The **bundle manifest** (schema + hashing requirements)
- SBOM inclusion/pointers
- Compatibility rules (forward/backward)
- Size and packaging constraints for common offline transport workflows

This page is the source of truth for what the installer expects on disk. Signing and verification behavior is defined in the design doc and ADR (linked above).

---
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Enable offline install/upgrade with **no network fetches** (installer must operate fully from the bundle).
2. Provide a deterministic, machine-verifiable inventory of contents (hashes + versions).
3. Support cryptographic signing of the manifest (integrity + provenance).
4. Support incremental evolution of the bundle format without breaking older installers.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Customer-provided signing roots / customer-signed bundles (tracked as a future plan).
- Fully standardizing on one container transport format for all customers; we support a small set with clear rules.

---
sections.heading: Non-goals (initial phase)

sections.body:
- **Bundle**: The offline artifact delivered to customers (a directory or an archive that expands to a directory).
- **Bundle root**: Top-level directory containing manifest and artifact subdirectories.
- **Manifest**: Canonical file inventory and metadata; is the unit that is signed.
- **Build ID**: Unique identifier for the release build producing the bundle.

---
sections.heading: Terminology

sections.body:
The bundle MUST expand to a single directory (the bundle root) containing the following top-level files:
- `manifest.json` (required)
- `manifest.sig` (required for signed bundles; optional only for explicitly approved break-glass bundles)
- `README.txt` (required; short human instructions, version, and support pointers)
sections.heading: Bundle root requirements

sections.body:
- `manifest.certchain.pem` (optional; included when verification expects an embedded certificate chain)
- `SBOM/` directory (optional; when SBOM is embedded rather than referenced)

The installer MUST be pointed at the bundle root directory (not at an archive). Customers may transport bundles as an archive (e.g., `.tar.zst`) but MUST extract prior to install.

---
sections.heading: Optional

sections.body:
A valid bundle contains the following directories under the bundle root:

1) `install/`
- Contains installer entrypoints and helper binaries/scripts used by Redwood Private installation and preflight.

2) `charts/`
- Helm chart tarballs (`.tgz`) required for Redwood Private components.

3) `images/`
- Offline container images in one of the supported forms (see “Container images” section).

4) `artifacts/`
- Redwood runtime artifacts required for on-prem serving (e.g., engine plugins, tokenizer assets, compatibility shims).

5) `config/`
- Offline install configuration defaults, schema files, and example values.
sections.heading: Required directories

sections.body:
- `models/` (optional in initial phase; when present, includes model weights or model bundles for customers approved for offline model transport)
- `deps/` (optional; OS/package dependencies only when explicitly required for a specific on-prem installer path)
- `SBOM/` (optional; embedded SBOM documents)
sections.heading: Optional directories

sections.body: The following is an illustrative example. Exact filenames vary by release.
sections.heading: Example tree

sections.body:
- `manifest.json`
- `manifest.sig`
- `README.txt`
- `install/`
  - `redwood-private-installer-linux-amd64`
  - `redwood-private-installer-linux-amd64.sha256` (optional convenience checksum; not a substitute for manifest hashes)
  - `plugins/` (optional)
- `charts/`
  - `redwood-private-1.32.0.tgz`
  - `redwood-observability-1.32.0.tgz`
  - `redwood-gateway-1.32.0.tgz`
- `images/`
  - `oci-layout/` (preferred)
    - `index.json`
    - `blobs/sha256/...`
  - `images.lock` (required; references image digests; also included in manifest)
- `artifacts/`
  - `runtime/`
    - `engine-plugins-2026.01.0.tar.zst`
    - `tokenizers-2026.01.0.tar.zst`
  - `compat/`
    - `k8s-migrations-2026.01.0.tgz`
- `config/`
  - `values.schema.json`
  - `values.offline.example.yaml`
- `SBOM/` (optional)
  - `sbom.spdx.json`
  - `sbom.cyclonedx.json`

---
sections.heading: Bundle root

sections.body:
- Exactly one platform installer binary is REQUIRED for supported platforms (initial support: Linux amd64; Linux arm64 optional by release).
- Any required helper binaries MUST be included locally; the installer must not download dependencies in air-gapped mode.
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- Filenames are included in manifest and MUST match exactly (case-sensitive).
- Executable bit must be preserved by the customer’s transfer/extract tooling. README.txt includes extraction guidance.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: - Helm chart tarballs (`.tgz`) for all components referenced by the release.
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- Chart versions and `appVersion` MUST align with the bundle `release.version` metadata in `manifest.json`.
- The installer reads charts from this directory only; it must not attempt to pull charts from remote repos.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: - An offline image store plus a lock file.
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
1) **OCI image layout** (preferred)
   - Stored under `images/oci-layout/`
   - The manifest MUST include the top-level `index.json` hash plus blob hashes.
2) **Docker image tar archives** (supported only for customers with existing docker load workflows)
   - Stored as `.tar` under `images/docker-archives/`
   - The manifest MUST include sha256 hashes for the tar files and the expected image digests.
sections.heading: Supported formats (one of)

sections.body:
- `images/images.lock` is REQUIRED.
- It contains the authoritative list of image references and immutable digests (e.g., `registry.redwoodinference.com/redwood/gateway@sha256:...`).
- The lock file itself is hashed and listed in `manifest.json`.
sections.heading: Lock file

sections.body:
- Tags are allowed in lock entries for readability but digests MUST be present and treated as authoritative.
- The bundle MUST include all images referenced by charts/values for the default offline install path.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: - Runtime-dependent assets needed for the release (engine plugins, tokenizer assets, migration packages, etc.).
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- Artifacts must be referenced by exact filename and sha256.
- Where possible, artifacts should be compressed using `.tar.zst` for size efficiency.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: - Offline example values files and schemas used for validation.
sections.heading: Required

sections.body: - These files are treated as install inputs and MUST be hashed.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
SBOM is REQUIRED at the release level, provided either:
- Embedded in the bundle at `SBOM/` and referenced from the manifest with hashes, OR
- Referenced externally via a pointer in the manifest (pointer MUST include content hash), for customers who prefer separate SBOM distribution channels.

---
sections.heading: SBOM (`SBOM/` or external reference)

sections.body:
- `manifest.json` (required)
- `manifest.sig` (required for normal releases)

The signature covers the canonical bytes of `manifest.json` (canonicalization rules are owned by ADR-0147; this page specifies the semantic schema).

---
sections.heading: Files

sections.body: `manifest.json` MUST be a UTF-8 JSON document.
sections.heading: Manifest schema (semantic specification)

sections.body:
- `schema_version`: Version of the manifest schema (e.g., `"1.0"`).
- `bundle`: Bundle identity fields (id, format version).
- `release`: Redwood Private release metadata (version, channel).
- `build`: Build provenance metadata (build id, timestamps, repo SHAs).
- `artifacts`: List of all files/artifacts covered by the manifest, including their hashes.
- `sbom`: SBOM pointer(s) and hashes.
sections.heading: Required top-level fields

sections.body:
- `compatibility`: Installer version constraints and upgrade/downgrade rules.
- `notes`: Human-readable summary (kept short; do not include secrets).
sections.heading: Recommended/optional top-level fields

sections.body:
- `path`: Relative path from bundle root using `/` separators.
- `sha256`: Lowercase hex sha256 digest of the file content.
- `size_bytes`: File size in bytes.
- `type`: One of: `installer`, `helm_chart`, `image_lock`, `image_store`, `runtime_artifact`, `config`, `sbom`, `model`, `dep`, `other`.
sections.heading: Each artifact entry MUST include

sections.body:
- `media_type`: Helpful descriptor (e.g., `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`, `application/gzip`).
- `image_digests`: For image stores/archives, a comma-separated list of image digests expected to be present.
- `chart`: For charts, `name` and `version` as a single string `"<name>@<version>"`.
sections.heading: Optional per-artifact fields (when applicable)

sections.body:
- `sbom.primary_path` (relative path) OR `sbom.primary_uri` (external location)
- `sbom.primary_sha256`
sections.heading: The manifest MUST include at least one SBOM reference

sections.body:
- `sbom.formats` as a comma-separated list (e.g., `spdx-json,cyclonedx-json`)
- `sbom.secondary_paths` as a comma-separated list of additional embedded SBOMs
sections.heading: Optional

sections.body:
If present, `compatibility` MUST include:
- `min_installer_version`: Minimum installer version required to verify/install this bundle.
- `max_tested_installer_version`: Highest installer version validated during CI for this release (informational).
- `downgrade_policy`: `forbid` or `allow_with_flag` (default: `forbid`).

---
sections.heading: Compatibility section
Manifest example (illustrative)

sections.body:
- `sha256` is the required hash algorithm for all artifacts.
- Hashes MUST be computed on the exact bytes of the file as stored in the bundle.
- For archives (e.g., `.tgz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar`), hash the archive file itself (not expanded contents).
sections.heading: Hashing requirements

sections.body:
- Repackaging archives can change bytes and invalidate hashes.
- “Smart unzip” or antivirus tools can modify files or strip executable bits.

---
sections.heading: Common transfer pitfalls to call out in support

sections.body:
- Installers MUST fail closed if required fields are missing or any required artifact hash mismatches.
- Installers MUST ignore unknown fields (forward-compatible) unless the field is explicitly declared “critical” by installer version.
sections.heading: General rule

sections.body:
- `schema_version` uses `MAJOR.MINOR` semantics.
  - MINOR increments may add optional fields or new artifact types.
  - MAJOR increments may introduce breaking changes; will require a new minimum installer version.
sections.heading: Manifest schema versioning

sections.body:
- `bundle.format_version` is an integer representing the on-disk layout expectations.
- The installer MUST check `bundle.format` and `bundle.format_version` and error if unsupported.
sections.heading: Bundle format versioning

sections.body:
- New `type` values may be added. Installers should treat unknown `type` values as `other` for display/inspection, but still enforce hash verification for those files if they are referenced in `artifacts`.

---
sections.heading: Artifact type extensibility

sections.body:
- Secure file transfer to a staging host inside the enclave
- Removable media with filesystem limits (notably FAT32 4 GiB file limit)
- Offline scanning/ingestion systems with maximum object size policies
sections.heading: Air-gapped customers frequently move bundles via

sections.body:
- Target bundle size (typical release, excluding optional models): **≤ 60 GiB**.
- Hard limit for standard supportability: **≤ 120 GiB**.
- If a release would exceed 120 GiB, Release Engineering must:
  - Provide a documented split-bundle strategy OR
  - Obtain explicit Product + Security approval with customer-specific guidance.
sections.heading: Redwood guidance

sections.body:
If split delivery is used, the following rules apply:
- Each part must be independently hashable and referenced from the manifest.
- The installer must support a deterministic reassembly method (documented in README.txt).
- Split bundle mechanics MUST NOT change the bytes of `manifest.json` post-signing.

Note: Current default path is single bundle directory; split delivery is supported only for approved customers and must be coordinated with Solutions/PS.

---
sections.heading: Split bundle policy (when needed)

sections.body:
`README.txt` MUST include:
- Product + release version
- Bundle ID + build ID
- Minimum installer version
- Simple extraction guidance (including preserving executable bits)
- Primary verification command (e.g., `installer inspect --verify`)
- Log locations for verification failures
- Support escalation pointers

Do not include secrets, internal URLs that won’t resolve in air-gapped environments, or customer-specific tokens.

---
sections.heading: README.txt requirements (customer-facing summary)

sections.body:
1. Required top-level files exist: `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `README.txt`.
2. All `artifacts[].path` entries exist on disk and are within the bundle root (no `..` traversal).
3. All artifact hashes and sizes match.
4. `schema_version`, `bundle.format`, and `bundle.format_version` are supported.
5. `images/images.lock` exists and is included in `artifacts`.
6. SBOM is present (embedded or pointer) and hash is verifiable.
7. No network fetch is required for default offline install path.

---
sections.heading: A bundle is considered well-formed if

sections.body:
- Standardizing model transport under `models/` (including chunking and license attestation).
- Optional inclusion of per-artifact `sha512` for customers requiring dual-hash policies.
- Formal definition of “critical unknown fields” (installer behavior) tied to schema version.

---
sections.heading: Open items / future extensions

sections.body:
- Format/layout + installer expectations: **Eng Private Deployments** (Ethan Park)
- Manifest schema + canonicalization: **Deterministic policy/manifest engineering** (Jordan Lee) in collaboration with Release Eng
- Signing and key management: **Release Engineering / Security Engineering** (Connor O'Brien, Marcus Lin)
- Docs and customer guidance: **DevEx** (Kira Thompson)
sections.heading: Ownership

payload.page_title: tenant-sla-decomposition-and-resilience-profiling-playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook describes a pragmatic approach to decomposing customer-facing SLAs into measurable component-level SLOs for Redwood Private deployments, and a resilience profiling process that operators and SREs can run during onboarding, capacity planning, and major upgrades. It targets multi-tenant VPC and air-gapped on-prem installations where tenant isolation, predictable latency, and cost containment are primary concerns.

Goals
- Convert business SLAs (uptime, p99 latency, throughput) into component SLOs.
- Produce a resilience profile per tenant that identifies dominant failure modes and right-sized guardrails.
- Provide a reproducible test and remediation runbook for operators and field engineers.
- Ensure rollback and fallback policies are covered by SLA mapping.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) installations where tenants are mapped to virtual deployment namespaces.
- Assumes standard Redwood runtime components (edge-gateway, tenant-router, model-service, kv-cache, routing-orchestrator) and standard observability stack (metrics: Prometheus; traces: Jaeger/OpenTelemetry; logs: central ELK/Cloud logging).
- Not a workload-specific guide; replace workload-specific thresholds (sequence length, token rate, concurrency) with tenant-specific profiling values gathered during onboarding.

Key terms
- Business SLA: commitment to the customer (e.g., "99.95% success and p99 inference latency < 250ms for <=512 tokens").
- Component SLO: internal target for a single subsystem (e.g., model-service p99 < 120ms).
- Resilience profile: summary of how a tenant’s workload reacts to component degradation (latency vs. throughput curves, cold-start sensitivity, cache-hit dependence).

Owner and escalation
- Playbook owner: Runtime Resilience Team (runtime-resilience@redwood.internal).
- Day-2 ops owner: Private Deployments Field Ops (pd-field-ops@redwood.internal).
- Oncall escalation: see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.

SLA decomposition pattern (high level)
1. Capture the business SLA: uptime, latency bounds (p50/p95/p99), throughput or concurrency caps, and any region/residency constraints.
2. Identify critical request path and map to components: ingress -> edge-gateway -> tenant-router -> model-service -> kv-cache (optional) -> tokenizer -> response aggregation.
3. Assign per-component SLOs using conservative headroom (recommended: business p99 * 0.5 for model-stage components; see table below).
4. Define error budgets and automated fallback policies for each SLO.
5. Validate decomposition via synthetic and recorded-replay profiling under representative load.

Recommended SLO decomposition table (example)
- Business SLA: p99 inference latency < 250ms for <=512 tokens.

| Component | Example SLO | Rationale / Notes | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| edge-gateway (ingress & TLS) | p99 < 30ms | Termination and rate-limiting; must be small fraction | infra-sre |
| tenant-router (routing + auth) | p99 < 20ms | Route selection + tenant ACL checks | runtime-team |
| model-service (GPU infer) | p99 < 150ms | Bulk of token generation; scale horizontally | runtime-team |
| kv-cache (prefix/KV caching) | p99 < 10ms (cache hit) | Cache hits significantly reduce model work | runtime-team |
| tokenizer / postproc | p99 < 15ms | CPU-bound transforms | infra-sre |
| network (inter-host) | p99 < 20ms | Inter-node RPCs; depends on placement | infra-network |

Notes on headroom: choose component targets so their sum + inter-component overhead <= business SLA. For high-variance workloads (long tails), increase model-service headroom or enable micro-batching to reduce variance.

Resilience profiling procedure (runbook)
1. Prepare: ensure the tenant has a representative prompt set and traffic profile. Collect: typical sequence length distribution, top-k model variants, per-call token counts, burst patterns.
2. Baseline capture (no fault): run 30-minute steady-state load at 100% of expected normal concurrency; collect p50/p95/p99, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
3. Stress steps (progressive):
   a. Increase concurrency to 1.5x and 2x normal; observe latency and error rates.
   b. Introduce synthetic network latency of +10ms/+25ms on inter-host links; observe impact on p99.
   c. Drop KV cache hit ratio by simulating cache cold starts (evict and prime); measure additional latency.
   d. Simulate model-service CPU/GPU slowdowns: cap GPU frequency or inject per-call CPU delay.
   e. Toggle quantization fallback (if tenant uses multiple quantized variants) to measure quality-latency tradeoff.
4. Canary failure modes: incrementally kill 1/3 of model-service replicas and observe graceful degradation and autoscale behavior.
5. Regression validation: replay recorded traffic through a candidate upgrade in an isolated canary to assert SLO adherence.

Data to collect during profiling
- Metrics: per-component latency histograms, per-replica CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, request-failure-type breakdown.
- Traces: end-to-end traces that can be filtered by tenant-id and operation-id.
- Artifacts: sample request/response pairs, cache hit logs, model logits for quality regressions.

Resilience profile output (artifact)
- A one-page summary that includes:
  - Tenant ID and workload class (interactive, batch, batched-interactive).
  - Baseline SLO attainment and error budget consumption.
  - Dominant failure modes (e.g., cache cold-start, model-service tail, network contention).
  - Recommended mitigations (config knobs and infra changes).
  - Risk level (Low / Medium / High) and suggested guardrail adjustments.

Mitigations catalog (examples)
- KV cache: increase memory allocation for tenant namespace; enable persistent warming pool; set cold-start TTLs.
- Model-service: pre-warm model instances for high-SLA tenants; reduce batch sizes to lower p99 at cost of throughput; set instance affinity to reduce inter-host network hops.
- Edge-gateway: add request coalescing for identical warm prefixes; tune rate limits for bursty clients.
- Autoscaler: lower decision window to respond faster for high-burst tenants; tie burst capacity to committed reserved capacity where available.

SLA-aware rollout and rollback steps (upgrade path)
1. Pre-upgrade profiling: capture resilience profile for production tenant traffic.
2. Offline regression harness: run upgrade image in isolated lab with replay of captured traffic for 2x normal concurrency for 1 hour.
3. Staged canary: deploy to 5% of capacity (non-reserved), run production traffic routing for 30–60 minutes while monitoring SLO signals and error budgets.
4. If any of these trip:
   a. Automatically route affected traffic to compatible lower-cost model variant (if configured) or to dedicated reserved pool.
   b. Trigger rollback if p99 exceeds business SLA by >25% for 10 consecutive minutes or error rate spike > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
5. Post-rollback: preserve traces/logs and attach to incident record; run targeted profiling to find root cause.

Runbook checks and alarms (SLO guardrails)
- Alerts to fire:
  - model-service_p99 > configured-component-slo * 1.5 for 5 minutes -> P1 to runtime oncall.
  - end-to-end_p99 > business-sla * 1.25 for 10 minutes -> P0 escalation and automatic traffic fallbacks.
  - KV-cache_hit_ratio < baseline * 0.6 for 10 minutes -> P2 with automated warming job queued.
- Automated responses: scale-up policy, traffic-steer to regional fallback, enable temporary batching-mode for throughput protection.

Configuration checklist (recommended defaults)
| Config | Recommended default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| model-service_min_replicas | 3 | Keep >=3 for shardable stateful models to survive single-node loss |
| model-service_target_cpu_util | 60% | Tune down for low-latency tenants |
| kv-cache_initial_size_mb | 1024 | Increase for high-throughput tenants |
| autoscaler_evaluation_window_secs | 30 | Short windows for bursty interactive workloads |
| edge_gateway_rate_limit_burst | 200 | Per-tenant token bucket burst cap |

Tenant onboarding checklist (profiling-driven)
1. Collect sample traffic and run baseline profiling.
2. Generate resilience profile and map to business SLA.
3. Apply tuned component SLOs into tenant config (via control-plane API).
4. Configure alarms and automated fallbacks in console (see Redwood Console -> tenant <id> -> Guardrails).
5. Schedule periodic re-profiling (quarterly or after major workload changes).

Templates and artifacts
- Resilience profile template (copy into customer ticket): include baseline metrics chart, failure-mode heatmap, and mitigation table.
- Canary gating checklist: automated tests (latency regression, quality regression using stored prompts), manual signoff owners.
- Incident attachment template: include replay inputs, delta in cache-hit ratio, and model logits for top 10 failing examples.

Operational notes and gotchas
- Quantization fallbacks can change quality; always attach model-eval prompts to canary run to detect subtle output regressions.
- For air-gapped sites, ensure reroute policies consider limited fallback capacity and longer lead time for manual remediation.
- Reserved capacity tenants: align autoscaler policies to not evict reserved pool during multi-tenant pressure.

References
- See related runbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-burst-forecast-and-guardrails-playbook-2026
- Private deployment onboarding runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026
- Observability configuration standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards

Appendix: example CLI commands
- Run synthetic baseline:
  rdw-infer-bench --tenant-id tenant-123 --concurrency 50 --duration 1800 --profile-out tenant-123-baseline.json
- Deploy canary and route 5% traffic:
  rdw-deploy canary --image v2026-03-01 --namespace tenant-123-canary
  rdw-traffic-route set --tenant tenant-123 --percent-canary 5

Revision history
- 2026-01-12: created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-02-10: added automated rollback thresholds (Rafael Ortega).
- 2026-03-02: clarified SLO decomposition defaults and added config checklist (Priya Nair).

payload.page_title: Offline Swarm Deployment and Rollout Playbook (VPC & On‑Prem Hybrid)

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook documents a validated pattern we call the 'Offline Swarm' — a hybrid private deployment topology for customers that require local inference pods with a lightweight, optionally offline control plane. It covers prerequisites, reference topology, operator-driven rollout steps (canary -> ramp -> full), safe upgrade and rollback procedures for stateful model artifacts and KV caches, post-deployment acceptance tests, and required customer readiness checks. Intended audience: private-deploy field engineers, site reliability engineers (SREs), and customer operators.

Goals and constraints
- Goal: deploy/upgrade inference capacity into a customer VPC or air-gapped site with zero-customer-data-exfiltration risk and minimal disruption to traffic.
- Constraint: some sites operate with intermittent connectivity to Redwood control plane (heartbeat window >= 1h).
- SLOs: production inference endpoints SHOULD meet customer SLOs: p50 < 40ms (small models), p95 < 200ms (medium models), p95 < 450ms (large models) under normal traffic patterns.

Scope
- Applies to: VPC-hosted private deployments and on-prem airgapped sites using the Redwood lightweight operator.
- Not covered: full multi-region public cloud control-plane deployments (use dedicated operator playbooks instead).

Reference topology (textual diagram)
- Local operator (k8s-operator-lite) on management plane (non-privileged)
- Inference pod group(s) (model-runtime) per tenant, with local KV cache and ephemeral model shard store
- Local telemetry forwarder with buffered store-and-forward to central telemetry gateway (optional)
- Optional on-site artifact registry / airgap bundle server (signed images and model weights)

Requirements: customer readiness checklist
| Category | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control connectivity | Periodic outbound TLS to redwood-control.redwood.ai:443 (heartbeat) OR operator in fully-offline mode | Allowlist for artifact fetch from operator only |
| Hardware | 2 x inference GPUs per tenant-class, 64GB system RAM, 2x 10Gb NIC | NVMe local cache, 4+ GPUs for medium/large models |
| Storage | 500GB ephemeral model store | 2TB with snapshotting for high-throughput deployments |
| KMS / key boundary | Customer KMS (AES-256) available for config secrets | HSM integration for signed image attestation |
| Network | VPC subnet with egress control, private peering for telemetry | BGP path for cross-site fallback |

Important notes:
- If site is fully airgapped, follow the airgapped-bundle recipe (see "Artifact bundle & attestation" section) and schedule operator handshake windows for manual attestations.

Artifact bundle & attestation
- Build signed bundles locally or provide signed model artifacts through our secure transfer template. Each bundle MUST include: model sha256, quantization profile tag, runtime-compatibility manifest (v2), and an operator-manifest.yaml with desired model-weight placement strategy.
- Signing: use customer key (recommended) or Redwood-signed attestation when under managed contract.

Operator configuration matrix (example)
| Config key | Example value | Notes |
| operator.mode | offline | offline | 
| operator.heartbeat_interval | 15m | Pulls control intents when available |
| operator.model_prefetch | 2 | Number of model weights to pre-warm per node |
| operator.kv_eviction_seconds | 3600 | Keep prefix caches warm for 1h |
| runtime.max_live_requests | 200 | Per-GPU soft limit |

Pre-deployment validation steps (run by field engineer)
1) Verify customer network egress/allowlist: curl --head https://redwood-control.redwood.ai/health or validate offline mode.
2) Validate hardware inventory: lspci | grep -i nvidia; check NVMe SMART for > 1M IO cycles remaining.
3) Confirm signed bundle integrity: sha256sum model.tar.gz && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature model.tar.gz.sig model.tar.gz.
4) Run smoke container: docker run --rm --read-only --network=host redwood/runtime-check:stable sh -c 'redwood-health --check-kv --check-gpu'

Rollout procedure (operator-driven, recommended cadence)
- Roles: field-engineer (executes operator commands), operator (customer operator), SRE-on-call (Redwood on-call for escalation).
- Canary (T+0): Deploy operator-mode=offline or connected to control plane in read-only. Push model bundle to 1 node:
  1. put operator into maintenance state (operatorctl set-mode canary)
  2. operatorctl apply-bundle --bundle ./signed-bundle.tar.gz --target nodes=node-01
  3. Monitor: runtime/latency p50/p95, kv/hit-rate, GPU temperature. Accept if p95 within 20% of baseline and no OOMs for 10m.
- Shadow traffic (T+1h): mirror 10% of live traffic to canary pod for 2 hours. Required checks: correctness score vs eval prompt set >= baseline - 0.02 absolute.
- Gradual ramp (T+6h): increase traffic in steps: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows at each step.
- Full enroll: when ramp steps pass acceptance gates, mark deployment stable and schedule post-deploy snapshot.

Acceptance gates (automated)
- Perf gate: p95 latency delta <= +25% vs baseline OR absolute p95 under model-class SLOs.
- Quality gate: automated evals on 200 prompt-set samples: mean quality metric delta <= 0.015.
- Resource gate: no GPU mem exceedance > 90% for more than 2 consecutive 1-minute intervals.

Backout & rollback cookbook
- Immediate rollback (triggered by operator or SRE): operatorctl rollback --to-previous --preserve-kv=true. This performs an atomic model pointer switch; model weights are not removed to speed rolling back.
- For stateful KV inconsistencies: follow the KV reconciliation procedure:
  1. Quiesce writes (operatorctl quiesce-tenant <tenant>)
  2. Snapshot current KV: operatorctl kv snapshot --out kv-snap-<ts>.tar.gz
  3. Reconcile by replaying prefetched prefixes from snapshot to nodes marked healthy.
- Evidence preservation: collect /var/log/redwood/operator.log, model load traces, GPU telemetry (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv), and a TLS packet capture (if allowed) for the timeframe of the incident.

Upgrade choreography for model runtime and kernel bundles
1) Preflight: operatorctl validate-runtime-bundle --bundle runtime-bundle.tgz (checks kernel ABI, cuDNN, and kernel selectors).
2) Canary roll: upgrade operator on 1 node, run two inference passes with canary model, validate correctness.
3) Staged roll: waves of 3 nodes with 10–15 minute soak per wave.
4) Post-upgrade: run KV validation job (operatorctl kv-validate --threshold 0.999).

Special case: offline-only sites (no outbound connectivity)
- Use signed-artifact USB / airgapped bundle transfer. All operator commands MUST be executed locally by a customer operator. Redwood provides a signed manifest and verification tool (redwood-offline-verify).
- Scheduled manual attestations: field engineer and customer operator must co-validate bundle checksum and signature. Record attestations in ticket system (include signed manifest).

Monitoring & observability contract
- Local metrics to collect (minimum): runtime.request.latency p50/p95, runtime.kv.hit_rate, node.gpu.utilization, node.gpu.temperature, model.load.time.
- Local retention: minimum 7 days granular metrics; aggregated rollups for 90 days. For airgapped sites, use buffered forwarder to central telemetry when connectivity resumes.

Operator runbook excerpts (quick commands)
- Apply bundle: operatorctl apply-bundle --bundle /opt/artifacts/signed-bundle.tar.gz --target node-02
- Force rollback: operatorctl rollback --to-previous --reason "regression-detected"
- Quiesce tenant writes: operatorctl quiesce-tenant tenant-42

Post-deploy acceptance tests (automated):
- run-eval-runbook --prompts=canary-200.json --baseline-id=canary-baseline-2025 --assert-quality-delta 0.02
- perf-check --rps 20 --duration 300 --assert-p95 < 1.25*baseline

Ownership and escalation
- Deployment owner: eng-private-deployments field-delivery (oncall rota: field-eng@redwood.ai).
- Escalation to SRE oncall if any of the following for > 15 min: sustained p95 > SLO, two or more node OOMs, KV corruption detected.

Runbook appendix: artifact verification examples
> Verify signature:
> openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature signed-bundle.tar.gz.sig signed-bundle.tar.gz

> Check GPU status (example):
> nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used,temperature.gpu --format=csv

References and further reading
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026 for airgap packaging specifics.
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025 for state migration patterns.

Revision history
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-02-01: Field validation and operator command updates (Marco Rivera, Claire Nguyen).

Document feedback
Please send feedback or suggested edits to eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai or propose changes via the Confluence edit flow.

payload.page_title: VPC crossconnect operational escape-hatch playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents an operator-focused "escape hatch" for private deploys using VPC crossconnects (peerings, Dedicated Interconnect, or private WAN fabric). It is intended for urgent mitigation when crossconnect or inter-region control-plane degradation threatens tenant SLAs or causes KV-cache divergence and routing blackholes. The goal is to describe safe, reversible operator actions that preserve tenant data integrity and minimize customer impact until engineering or networking can resolve the underlying fabric issue.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Control plane region-to-region RPC error rate > 5% sustained for 3 minutes and auto-fallback did not preserve throughput.
- Data-plane RTT degradation > 100 ms p95 between local tenant proxy and remote model shard AND packet loss > 2%.
- Crossconnect BGP session drops to < 80% adjacency or route flaps causing > 30% request errors to a tenant for > 2 minutes.
- KV cache inconsistency alerts (kv-cache-reconcile-failures) observed on > 5% of backend pods after a partial network partition.

Prerequisites and safety constraints
-----------------------------------
Operators must confirm the following before executing any escape-hatch steps:
1) Incident owner assigned and pager notified. (Run: incident assign <oncall-team>)
2) Maintenance window permission if a tenant-facing interruption is expected.
3) Backups and forensic snapshots: ensure latest telemetry and artifacts are preserved (see Evidence collection).
4) Immutable rollback path exists for any configuration change (route or policy).

SLOs and thresholds referenced
----------------------------
- Control plane availability objective: 99.95% per region.
- Tenant e2e latency target for private VPC: p95 < 150 ms.
- Immediate mitigation threshold (escape hatch): error rate spike > 5% or p95 latency > 250 ms.

Immediate containment (first 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------
1) Quick triage: determine containment domain (control plane vs data plane). Run the following queries in observability:
   - metrics.query("sum(rate(rpc_errors_total[1m])) by (region)")
   - metrics.query("histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region))")
2) If BGP adjacency unstable: do NOT withdraw all routes. Instead, isolate the failed adjacency and move traffic to configured fallback peers using controlled route-preference changes.
3) Announce to affected operators and customers: use the Customer Communication Template (section below).

Operator actions (ordered, reversible steps)
-------------------------------------------
This sequence is intentionally conservative; each step is reversible and documented with the rollback command. Execute one step at a time and wait 60–120 seconds for telemetry to settle before proceeding.

1) Place region-level traffic into safemode degrader (non-destructive)
   - Purpose: throttle or queue new long-running requests to prevent cascading resource pressure.
   - Command: operatorctl region-safemode enable --region <REGION> --throttle 0.3
   - Validation: watch request_shed_rate and queue_depth metrics.
   - Rollback: operatorctl region-safemode disable --region <REGION>

2) Promote local fallback model variants for latency-sensitive tenants
   - Purpose: steer tenant routing to locally pinned model variants (smaller or quantized) to reduce cross-region calls.
   - Command: operatorctl model-rollout promote --tenant <TENANT> --variant local-quantized-v1 --priority emergency
   - Validation: per-tenant latency and token-cost metrics; ensure responses remain within business rules.
   - Rollback: operatorctl model-rollout demote --tenant <TENANT> --variant local-quantized-v1

3) If BGP route instability continues, perform a controlled route-preference shift (BGP local-pref bump) to prefer alternate transit
   - Purpose: avoid total path loss and maintain forward progress.
   - Safety: only change local-pref for affected prefixes; set a TTL for the change (10 minutes) to auto-revert.
   - Example command (network automation): terraform apply -var 'prefixes=["10.40.0.0/16"]' -var 'local_pref=200' -target module.bgp.policy --auto-approve
   - Rollback: Revert terraform change or run: terraform apply -var 'local_pref=100' -target module.bgp.policy --auto-approve

4) If KV cache divergence detected, trigger a staged resync sequence
   - Detect: run kvctl check --scope region --since 15m. Look for > 0.5% missing keys per shard.
   - Stage 1 (non-blocking): kvctl repair --shard <SHARD> --mode incremental --rate-limit 200/s
   - Stage 2 (if Stage 1 insufficient): kvctl repair --shard <SHARD> --mode snapshot-restore --window 10m (this will cause increased I/O; schedule with care)
   - Validation: kvctl check should return zero divergence and kvcache_sync_lag < 30s.
   - Rollback: Cancel long-running repair: kvctl cancel --task <TASK_ID>

5) Operator emergency proxy (temporary local-only proxy)
   - Purpose: short-circuit crossconnect for a small set of tenants by running a local proxy that honors token scope but pins to local compute.
   - Command (deploy): kubectl -n operator apply -f manifests/emergency-proxy-<tenant>.yaml
   - Manifest notes: proxy must run with read-only mount to local KV snapshot and NOT accept config pushes.
   - Rollback: kubectl -n operator delete -f manifests/emergency-proxy-<tenant>.yaml

Routing rollback decision matrix
-------------------------------
Use this matrix to select whether to change route preferences or keep trying application-level mitigations.

- Symptom: transient packet loss (1–3%), small RTT increase (10–50 ms) -> Avoid routing changes; use safemode and model promotion.
- Symptom: sustained packet loss (>3%) OR route flaps across multiple peers -> Perform route-preference shift for affected prefixes.
- Symptom: full adjacency down -> Activate alternate transit and, if unavailable, place affected tenants into planned outage with customer notice.

Evidence collection (mandatory before destructive actions)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Snapshot control-plane RPC logs (last 60m): logctl export --service control-plane --since 60m --out /tmp/cp-logs-<ts>.tar.gz
2) Capture BGP RIB and adjacencies: netctl bgp dump --peer all > /tmp/bgp-<ts>.txt
3) Store KV-head checksums: kvctl checksum --all > /tmp/kvck-<ts>.json
4) Ingest the artifacts into incident blobstore: incident upload /tmp/*-<ts>* --tag <INCIDENT_ID>

Customer communication templates
-------------------------------
sections.heading: Use this playbook when ANY of the following are true

sections.body:
- Subject: [Incident <INCIDENT_ID>] Temporary service routing mitigation in <REGION>
- Body: We are currently mitigating a networking disruption affecting private VPC crossconnects in <REGION>. Short-term mitigations are in place to preserve availability; you may see elevated latency or degraded throughput for a subset of requests. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Owner: <NAME>.

Full outage cadence: first notice (T+0), follow-ups (T+30m), T+2h engineering summary. Use incidentctl notify-customer --id <INCIDENT_ID> --template mitigation-update

Telemetry queries and dashboards (quick list)
-------------------------------------------
- Control plane error spikes: metrics.query("sum(rate(control_plane_rpc_errors[1m])) by (region)")
- BGP churn: metrics.query("rate(bgp_updates_total[5m])")
- KV divergence: metrics.query("sum(kv_cache_drift_shards_total{status=\"diverged\"})")
- Request p95 e2e: metrics.query("histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,tenant))")
- Recommended dashboards: "VPC Crossconnect Health", "KV Consistency Overview", "Safemode Events"

Post-incident remediation checklist
----------------------------------
1) Root cause analysis: assign RCA owner and timeline within 48 hours.
2) Remove temporary route preferences and confirm BGP stability for 24 hours.
3) Run full KV reconciliation and snapshot verification.
4) Convert any emergency-proxy usage into a controlled, documented feature if repeatedly used.
5) Update this playbook with lessons learned.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- First responder (oncall-networking): Pager: #network-oncall. Primary Slack: #network-ops.
- Control plane engineering lead: Priya Sundaram (priya@redwood.ai)
- SRE incident commander: Matteo Fischer (matteo@redwood.ai)
- Customer success escalation for major customer impact: Sana Ortiz (sana@redwood.ai)

Appendix: sample commands and quick references
--------------------------------------------
- Check BGP adjacency: netctl bgp show peers --peer <PEER_IP>
- Dump RIB for prefix: netctl bgp rib --prefix 10.40.0.0/16
- Trigger kv incremental repair: kvctl repair --shard sh-42 --mode incremental --rate-limit 200/s
- Promote emergency variant for tenant: operatorctl model-rollout promote --tenant acme-corp --variant low-latency-edge-v2 --priority emergency

Change log
----------
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft (A. Patel).
- 2026-03-05: Added KV resync staging and evidence collection steps (reviewers: M. Ruiz, E. Park).

Notes and safe-guards
---------------------
- Never perform a global route withdraw as a first step. Global withdrawals have historically caused multi-region evictions and lengthy recoveries.
- Prefer application-level mitigations (safemode, model promotion, emergency proxy) before fabric-level manipulations except when data-plane is fully severed.
- All terraform or network automation changes must include a TTL tag so that accidental permanent preference changes are avoided.

Document links and references
----------------------------
- See also: operator-handback-and-custodian-rollforward-playbook (operator procedures).
- Observability guides: "VPC Crossconnect Health" dashboard in Dashboards library.
- KV consistency design doc: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kv-cache-consistency-design-2025.json

End of playbook.

payload.page_title: Operator kickoff, compliance acceptance, and customer handoff playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the coordinated steps for a successful operator kickoff, compliance acceptance testing (CAT), and handoff to the customer operations team for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates pre-flight checks, packaging attestations, day-2 responsibilities, upgrade/rollback acceptance criteria, and a minimal evidence catalog required for compliance review.

Scope:
- Applies to all Private deployments delivered by Redwood Inference: VPC-hosted control plane, delegated/federated control plane, and fully on-prem air-gapped installations.
- Targets deployments where a formal customer handoff and compliance attestation is required (regulated industries: finance, healthcare, government).

Owner and stakeholders:
- Document owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel)
- Primary stakeholders: Field Operators, Platform Engineering, Security & Compliance, Customer NOC
- Approvers: Head of Customer Success, Compliance

Acceptance gates and timeline:
1. Preflight complete: network, hardware, KMS, and model artifact integrity checks passed.
2. Compliance Acceptance Test (CAT): telemetry contract and evidence bundle validated.
3. Operator kickoff: on-site/remote knowledge transfer & runbook validation.
4. Formal handoff: customer signs acceptance certificate; Redwood hands over operator playbooks and support SLAs.

Preflight checklist (condensed):
| Area | Minimum requirement | Owner |
|------|---------------------|-------|
| Hardware | Node count >= requested capacity; accelerator firmware signed and latest LTS | Customer/Field Ops |
| Network | BGP/peers configured; egress policy and MTU validated; < 50ms intra-region RTT | Customer Network |
| KMS/HSM | Key provisioning, attestation, and rotation schedule defined | Security Team |
| Model Artifacts | Signed manifests; SHA256 checksums for each artifact | Platform Engineering |
| Telemetry | Agent installed; metrics ingress verified; retention policy agreed (90d default) | Platform & Customer NOC |

Detailed operator kickoff procedure:
1. Schedule a 4-hour kickoff session with participants listed in the "Owner and stakeholders" section.
2. Walk through operator runbooks: startup, graceful degradation, and model swap.
3. Run smoke workload (see "Smoke test" below) and validate SLOs.
4. Confirm alerting and SLO dashboards are accessible to customer observers.
5. Sign the Operator Readiness Sheet (template in "related_pages").

Smoke test (example commands):
- Verify model endpoint responds:
  - curl -X POST https://<tenant-proxy>/v1/generate -d '{"input":"smoke test"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Validate latency and throughput baseline (sample PromQL):
  - avg_over_time(redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds{job="serving",tenant="customerX"}[5m]) < 0.5

CAT (Compliance Acceptance Test) checklist:
- Telemetry contract verification:
  - Metrics: per-tenant token_count, request_latency_histogram, kv_cache_hit_ratio
  - Logs: redwood.request.{request_id} with redacted PII fields
  - Evidence: end-to-end signed telemetry manifest and sample retention export
- Evidence bundle (minimum):
  - Signed node inventory (CSV)
  - Firmware/BIOS attestation report
  - KMS provisioning snapshot
  - Model artifact manifest and checksums
  - Telemetry sample export (7 days) with hash
  - Operator Readiness Sheet (signed)

Upgrade and rollback acceptance criteria:
- Upgrade acceptance:
  - Canary run (10% traffic) for 30 minutes with zero fatal errors and less than 5% latency regression vs baseline.
  - KV cache warming period observed; no more than 2% request failures during warmup window.
- Rollback triggers:
  - Any fatal error impacting >1% of requests for 5 continuous minutes.
  - SLO breach: 99th percentile latency increase > 2x baseline for >10 minutes.
- Rollback procedure (condensed):
  1. Trigger orchestration: scale down new model pods to 0, increase previous version to desired capacity.
  2. Re-attach model artifact snapshot and validate checksums.
  3. Verify KV cache convergence and run smoke tests.
  4. Preserve forensic logs; assemble rollback evidence bundle.

Operator responsibilities (first 30 days):
- Nightly health checks (automated): disk pressure, GPU temperature, process restarts
- Weekly artifact refresh validation and signature verification
- Monthly compliance snapshot export and evidence handover
- On-call escalation: Tier 1 operator -> Platform Oncall -> Security (for integrity incidents)

Runbook snippets (examples):
- Force graceful model rollback via CLI:
  - redwoodctl rollout rollback --tenant customerX --model-id model:v2 --reason "latency-regression"
- Collect forensic evidence for upgrade failure:
  - redwoodctl collect evidence --tenant customerX --since "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" --out /tmp/evidence.tar.gz

Acceptance certificate template (to be signed by customer):
- Customer: <customer-name>
- Deployment id: <deployment-id>
- Deployment type: VPC | On-prem
- Preflight completed: yes/no
- CAT completed: yes/no
- Operator kickoff: date/time
- Signed by: <customer-ops> / <redwood-rep>

Related artifacts and attachments:
- Example telemetry manifest (JSON) — attach signed export
- Operator Readiness Sheet (spreadsheet)
- Sample evidence bundle checklist (archive)

Escalation and post-handoff support model:
- 30-day hypercare window: Redwood provides 24/7 operator-to-operator escalation for critical incidents.
- After hypercare: standard enterprise SLA applies; quarterly QBRs and runbook reviews.

Change log:
- 2026-02-12: Draft created by Aisha Patel
- 2026-04-03: Added smoke test PromQL and CLI examples (reviewer: Luca Bianchi)
- 2026-10-05: Expanded CAT evidence list and updated upgrade acceptance thresholds (reviewer: Mei Chen)

Appendix A — Telemetry contract (minimal required metrics):
- redwood_inference_requests_total (labels: tenant, route, model_version)
- redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket (labels: tenant, route, model_version)
- redwood_kv_cache_hits_total and redwood_kv_cache_misses_total (labels: tenant, model_version)

Appendix B — Evidence bundle manifest example (one-line JSON):
{"deployment_id":"dep-12345","collected_at":"2026-10-05T14:00:00Z","items":["node-inventory.csv","firmware-report.pdf","telemetry-sample.ndjson"]}

Contact:
- Primary author: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- Field operator lead: Luca Bianchi (luca@redwood.com)
- Compliance lead: Mei Chen (mei@redwood.com)
