payload.page_title: Immutable rollback artifact catalog and attestation manifest

sections.body:
Overview

This runbook defines the catalog format, attestation manifest, and operator procedures used to produce, verify, and preserve immutable artifacts for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended to:

- Ensure rollback operations are forensic-friendly and reproducible.
- Provide a canonical manifest schema and signing/verification recipes.
- Specify retention, evidence packaging, and roles for operator and customer-facing rollbacks.

Scope

Applies to: private-control-plane builds, runtime container images, model weight bundles, quantization artifacts, runtime configs, and migration/upgrade bundles used during stateful upgrades and rollbacks for Private Deployments. Excludes ephemeral telemetry logs (see related telemetry retention pages).

Why immutable artifacts and attestation?

1. Reproducibility: exact content/hashes allow deterministic rollbacks to prior working state.
2. Forensics: full evidence capture (hashes, signatures, provenance) supports incident investigations and customer audits.
3. Safety: signed attestation prevents accidental or malicious substitution of rollback artifacts.

Definitions

- Artifact: any binary or bundle (container image, model weights tar.gz, config archive).
- Catalog entry: a single row in the artifact catalog describing an artifact and its metadata.
- Attestation manifest: signed metadata document describing the artifact catalog for a release or checkpoint.
- Evidence bundle: packaged artifacts + manifest + verification receipts used for rollback or audit.

Catalog schema (canonical fields)

We require every private-deploy artifact to be published with a catalog entry that includes the following fields. Operators must not omit fields marked REQUIRED.

| Field | Type | REQUIRED | Description |
|-------|------|----------|------------|
| artifact_id | string | REQUIRED | Unique stable identifier: <service>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDD>-<hash-prefix> |
| artifact_type | enum | REQUIRED | one of: container, model-weights, quant, config, migration-bundle |
| version | string | REQUIRED | semantic or internal version (e.g. 2025.11.03-rc4) |
| sha256 | hex | REQUIRED | SHA-256 of the artifact file (lowercase hex) |
| size_bytes | integer | REQUIRED | File byte size |
| storage_uri | string | REQUIRED | canonical URI where artifact is stored (s3://, gs://, file://) |
| build_id | string | OPTIONAL | CI build identifier that produced artifact |
| builder | string | OPTIONAL | team/service responsible for build |
| provenance | string | OPTIONAL | URL or identifier for provenance bundle (build logs, recipe) |
| signature_kms_key | string | OPTIONAL | KMS key id used to sign this artifact (if signed) |
| attestation_id | string | REQUIRED | reference to the attestation manifest that certified the catalog |
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
artifact_id,artifact_type,version,sha256,size_bytes,storage_uri,build_id,builder,provenance,signature_kms_key,attestation_id
core-runtime-container,container,2026.01.14-rc1,a3f4...7c5e,124578312,s3://redwood-prod/artifacts/runtime:2026.01.14-rc1,ci-14522,serving-runtime,http://ci.company/build/14522,projects/redwood/kms/rs-1,attest-2026-01-14-rc1

Attestation manifest (schema and examples)

The attestation manifests are the authoritative signed documents that reference a set of catalog entries. Format: YAML or JSON. Required top-level fields: attestation_id, timestamp_utc, produced_by, catalog_digest, artifacts (list), signatures (list).
sections.heading: Sample catalog row (CSV-like)

sections.body:
---
attestation_id: attest-2026-01-14-rc1
timestamp_utc: "2026-01-14T03:12:41Z"
produced_by: "/teams/serving-runtime/ci-14522"
catalog_digest: sha256:a7b...9f0
artifacts:
  - artifact_id: core-runtime-container
    artifact_type: container
    version: "2026.01.14-rc1"
    sha256: a3f4...7c5e
    storage_uri: s3://redwood-prod/artifacts/runtime:2026.01.14-rc1
  - artifact_id: transformer-weights-v2
    artifact_type: model-weights
    version: "v2-quant"
    sha256: b6d2...12ff
    storage_uri: s3://redwood-prod/models/transformer/v2-quant.tar.gz
signatures:
  - signer: "projects/redwood/kms/rs-1"
    signature: "base64:..."
    method: "kms-sign"
---

Catalog digest calculation

- Sort canonical artifact entries by artifact_id.
- Serialize minimal fields (artifact_id|artifact_type|version|sha256|storage_uri) as newline-joined rows.
- Compute SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes and hex-encode. The attestation.manifest.catalog_digest must match this value.

Signing and verification recipes

We support two signing methods depending on deployment sensitivity: KMS/HSM signing (preferred for Private Deploys) and GPG for lower-sensitivity field operators.

KMS/HSM signing (recommended)

- Sign (example using Google Cloud KMS-style CLI):
  1) Export manifest bytes: cat attestation.yaml > attestation.raw
  2) gcloud kms keys versions sign --key=rs-1 --location=global --keyring=redwood --key-version=1 --input-file=attestation.raw --signature-file=attestation.sig
  3) Store signature (base64) in attestation.yaml.signatures[].

- Verify (example):
  1) Fetch public key from key management service.
  2) Use kms verify or a local crypto library to validate attestation.raw against attestation.sig.
  3) Recompute catalog_digest and verify artifact sha256 values by downloading artifact headers (or entire file).

GPG signing (fallback for air-gapped operator environments)

- Sign: gpg --armor --output attestation.sig --detach-sign attestation.yaml
- Verify: gpg --verify attestation.sig attestation.yaml

Operator rollback runbook (forensic-preserving path)

1) Triage and decision
   - Confirm rollback is allowed per customer SLA and change window. Check operator change log and customer notification channel.
   - Obtain attestation_id for the target checkpoint.

2) Enter evidence mode (do not modify production logs except to record actions)
   - Tag the incident in telemetry (incident-id).
   - Snapshot current running state: record node images, running artifact IDs, KV cache digests, and relevant config versions.

3) Prepare evidence bundle
   - Create a directory: /evidence/<incident-id>/pre-rollback
   - For each artifact in attestation.artifacts: fetch artifact header, compute sha256 locally, and store a verification receipt file named <artifact_id>.receipt with fields: storage_uri, expected_sha256, observed_sha256, downloaded_bytes, verification_time_utc.
   - Save attestation.yaml and attestation.sig alongside receipts.

4) Lock-change and schedule rollback maintenance window
   - Notify oncall and customer. Acquire operator approval (2-person rule: requester + approver). Record approver names in evidence bundle metadata.json.

5) Execute rollback (safe path)
   - Use orchestrator operator tool (example command):
     rwd-operator rollback --attestation attest-2026-01-14-rc1 --dry-run=false --preserve-kv=true --evict=false --evidence-dir=/evidence/<incident-id>/rollback
   - For stateful services follow stepwise model:
     a) Drain traffic from target nodes.
     b) Stop runtime.
     c) Replace runtime artifacts with ones referenced in attestation (verify SHA-256 before starting).
     d) Start and monitor health probes for 30m (SLO target: 99% success for critical API endpoints).

6) Post-rollback evidence preservation
   - Package /evidence/<incident-id> as a tar.gz and store in secure evidence bucket with immutability flags (WORM) for retention period (see policy).
   - Attach signed manifest and verification receipts to the incident ticket and customer notification.

7) Forensics and follow-up
   - If rollback was triggered by suspected tampering, escalate to Security & Compliance and preserve network captures per legal checklist.

Sample verification receipt (JSON text file saved per artifact)

{
  "artifact_id": "transformer-weights-v2",
  "storage_uri": "s3://redwood-prod/models/transformer/v2-quant.tar.gz",
  "expected_sha256": "b6d2...12ff",
  "observed_sha256": "b6d2...12ff",
  "downloaded_bytes": "412345678",
  "verification_time_utc": "2026-02-14T02:03:12Z"
}

Retention and evidence policy (summary)

- Evidence bundles for rollbacks must be retained for a minimum of 3 years for regulated customers and 180 days for standard customers.
- Evidence storage must be immutable (object lock / WORM) and encrypted at rest with customer or provider-managed keys per deployment contract.
- Access to evidence buckets requires RBAC: role=incident-evidence-reader or incident-evidence-admin and always audited.

Roles and responsibilities

- Operator (field operator / SRE): prepare evidence bundle, execute rollback, verify artifacts and record receipts.
- Release owner (team): ensure artifact catalog is accurate, produce attestation manifests during release CI.
- Security & Compliance: preserve chain-of-custody for suspected tampering and approve long-term retention exceptions.

Automated checks (CI hooks)

- CI must produce attestation manifests for any private-deploy release candidate and store them in the signed-attestations registry.
- Pre-deploy gate: catalog_digest must match CI reported digest and all artifacts must have sha256 present.
- Post-deploy monitor: continuous verifier agent should sample deployed nodes every 6 hours and verify running artifact sha256 against attestation stored in registry. Alerts if mismatches are found.

Appendix A — quick checklist for operators (one-page)

1) Verify attestation exists and signature verifies.
2) Snapshot current state and create evidence directory.
3) Compute local sha256 for each artifact referenced.
4) Acquire 2-person approval; set maintenance window.
5) Run rwd-operator rollback with evidence-dir.
6) Monitor health probes for 30m; escalate on errors.
7) Archive evidence bundle with immutable storage and link to ticket.

Appendix B — example attestation verification script (bash)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ATT=attestation.yaml
SIG=attestation.sig
sections.heading: Example (YAML)

sections.body: kms-verify --key projects/redwood/kms/rs-1 --input $ATT --signature $SIG || { echo "signature invalid"; exit 2; }
sections.heading: Verify signature (example using kms-verify binary)

sections.body:
echo "attestation verified"

Related pages and links

- See: /eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/model-artifact-supplychain-and-image-attestation-spec-2026 (artifact provenance requirements)
- See: /eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/forensic-friendly-rollback-protocol-and-telemetry-preservation-playbook-2026 (incident preservation guidance)

End of document.
sections.heading: For each artifact, curl --head storage_uri and compute sha256 on the downloaded file header/body as required.

payload.page_title: Offline Upgrade Validation Harness and Simulated Workload Suite

sections.body:
Summary:

This page describes the offline upgrade validation harness and simulated workload suite used to validate private deployments before field upgrades or model swaps. The harness lets operators perform deterministic, repeatable validations of control-plane changes, runtime binary upgrades, model quantization swaps, and KV-cache migrations without impacting production tenants. It encodes a set of workload profiles, failure injection scenarios, telemetry assertions, and acceptance criteria required for sign-off.

Goals and scope:

- Provide an automated, reproducible validation path for upgrades that cannot be fully exercised in production canaries (air-gapped QA).
- Validate performance regressions (p50/p95/p99), correctness of model outputs for a set of golden prompts, and KV-cache consistency during stateful migrations.
- Exercise network/egress/fallback policies, tenant isolation rules, and KMS/HSM integrations in a safe sandbox.
- Produce an evidence bundle (logs, traces, metrics, artifacts) suitable for compliance audits and customer acceptance tests (CATs).

Out of scope:

- Non-deterministic A/B experimentation across live traffic.
- Long-term capacity soak tests longer than 72 hours (these are executed in separate stress labs).

Audience:

This document is intended for:
- Operators and SREs responsible for private deployment upgrades.
- Field engineers executing customer upgrades and runbook authors.
- Release engineers validating binary and package images.

High-level architecture of the harness:

1) Controller: a containerized orchestration component that coordinates profile playback, failure injection, and artifact collection.
2) Workload generator: pluggable modules that emulate request patterns for text generation, chat, embeddings, and KV-access at configurable QPS and token distributions.
3) Failure injector: network latency/jitter, process restarts, OOM simulation, GPU thermal spikes (simulated via throttling), and KMS latency stubs.
4) Telemetry validator: a rules engine that consumes traces/metrics/logs and evaluates pass/fail assertions.
5) Evidence bundler: packages logs, trace snapshots, diffs of golden outputs, and a human-friendly summary for sign-off.

Prerequisites and environment:

- Offline validation cluster that mirrors customer topology (minimum: 3 control-plane nodes, 6 worker nodes with representative GPU types).
- Ingested model artifacts: both current and candidate model binaries / quantized variants.
- Sample tenant configs and KV snapshots exported from production (sanitized).
- Network replay facility or traffic generator with TLS termination mirroring customer certs.
- Secrets: test KMS keys or HSM simulator. Ensure keys are marked test and are not customer secrets.

Workload profiles (bundled):

Each profile is a YAML file included in the suite. Profiles represent realistic mixes of requests and token distributions. Representative profiles: 

- small-text-search (embeddings-heavy): 100 QPS, 90% 128-token prompts, 10% 512-token prompts, embeddings batch size 32.
- conversational-saas (chat-heavy): 40 QPS, average 6 messages/session, 30% streaming responses, 15% function-calls.
- bursty-webhook (burst patterns): base 5 QPS with bursts to 800 QPS for 30s every 10m (tests autoscaling and burst policies).
- large-gen (long-context): 10 QPS, 80% requests with 2048 tokens output, intensive KV-cache usage.

Example profile snippet:

---
profile_name: large-gen
qps: 10
sequence_length:
  input: 512
  output: 2048
mix:
  generation: 95
  embeddings: 5
kvs:
  prefix_hit_rate: 0.65
  kv_ops_per_request: 2
---

Failure scenarios and injection matrix:

- Network partitions: simulate partial control-plane -> worker plane partitions and assert TLS fallback and routing policies.
- Slow KMS: add 200–1000ms latency to KMS calls and assert request error-rates remain below 0.5% for SLA-backed customers.
- GPU eviction simulation: sequentially drain and taint worker GPU slots and validate tenant failover and graceful degradation.
- KV inconsistency: introduce out-of-order KV-appends to check convergence and correctness of model state after catch-up.
- Model artifact corruption: feed an intentionally truncated model file and validate runtime rejects with clear error and falls back.

Telemetry assertions and acceptance criteria:

The telemetry validator enforces assertions at both service and tenant granularity. Key assertions: 

- Latency SLOs: generation p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms for small-text-search profile; p50 <= 250ms, p95 <= 1200ms for large-gen (these are validation targets, not guaranteed production SLOs).
- Error budget: end-to-end error rate (5xx or explicit runtime rejects) < 0.3% during the validation window.
- Token accounting: per-tenant token counts and cost ledger must match simulated inputs within 0.5%.
- Output fidelity (golden prompts): normalized token-level diff (BLEU-like) <= 2% on curated evaluation set after model swap. Any regression > 2% triggers hold.
- KV consistency: after simulated migration, sample 1000 state keys and assert deterministic values match pre-migration baseline.

Acceptance checklist (automated and manual steps):

Automated gating: 
1. All telemetry assertions are green.
2. Evidence bundle generated and checksum verified.
3. No fatal runtime rejects in error logs.

Manual review gating (operator):
1. Compare golden prompt diffs and confirm no semantic regressions.
2. Verify rollout playbook steps and human approvals are recorded.
3. Sign the CAT (Customer Acceptance Test) artifact when deploying to a customer.

Rollback triggers and automated backout policy:

- Immediate automatic rollback if any of the following are observed during a staged upgrade: crash-looping control-plane node, >1% sustained increase in p99 latency for two consecutive 10-minute windows, or token accounting discrepancy > 1% for billing-critical tenants.
- If rollback triggers, the harness executes these steps:
  1) Quiesce new client connections.
  2) Re-point traffic to previous model binary snapshot or previous container image.
  3) Restore KV snapshot and replay any missing operations.
  4) Re-run golden prompt set and validate parity.
  5) Generate a rollback report and mark run as failed for release dashboard.

Example rollback command sequence (CLI):

# Gracefully mark candidate version as draining
redwoodctl candidate set-drain --version v2026.03-candidate --reason "telemetry-regression"

# Roll traffic back to previous stable image
redwoodctl rollout promote --from v2026.02-stable --to production --force --note "auto-rollback"

Evidence bundle and audit artifacts:

The harness produces a bundle in S3-compatible storage (or local object store for air-gapped runs). Bundle contents:
- logs/ (structured logs from controller, generators, runtime)
- traces/ (Jaeger trace captures around failures)
- metrics/ (Prometheus scrape dumps)
- golden-diffs/ (per-prompt diffs and similarity scores)
- kv-checksums.csv (sampled pre/post migration)
- run-report.json (summary metadata, pass/fail flags, checklist status)

The run-report is machine-readable for the release pipeline; a human-friendly SUMMARY.txt is also included.

Sanitization and customer data handling:

- Use only sanitized exports from production. Replace PII using redaction toolchain (script: scripts/sanitize-export.sh).
- Generate synthetic tenant identifiers. Do not run with customer KMS keys; use test keys or HSM simulator.

Packaging and CI integration:

- The harness is shipped as a Helm chart (chart/harness/) and a CLI artifact (bin/validation-runner). CI job definitions (Jenkins / GitHub Actions) live under infra/pipelines/validate-upgrades.yaml.
- Typical pipeline steps: build artifacts -> create validation cluster -> deploy harness -> run suite -> collect evidence -> mark release pass/fail.

Runbook (step-by-step):

1) Prepare: ensure sanitized KV snapshot is uploaded and candidate images are available.
2) Bootstrap cluster: helm install harness --values ci/values-qa.yaml
3) Start profile: validation-runner start --profile large-gen --duration 60m --evidence-bucket s3://redwood-validation/runs/2026-03-01-abc
4) Monitor: tail logs and telemetry dashboard; the telemetry validator posts status to /status endpoint.
5) On success: download evidence bundle, attach to release ticket, notify release owner for manual review.
6) On failure: trigger automated rollback, collect post-rollback evidence, and open incident if regressions persist.

Operational ownership and SLAs for validation runs:

- Owner: eng-private-deployments upgrade team. Primary on-call: @upgrade-squad (rotating).
- Target run time for a standard validation (1 hour profile): full run + evidence packaging completes in <= 120 minutes. If packaging takes longer, pipeline marks run degraded.

Metrics the team dashboards should include:

- Run success rate (7d/30d)
- Median evidence bundle creation time
- Average validation runtime per profile
- Number of auto-rollbacks triggered and root-cause categories

Known limitations and future work:

- The harness currently simulates GPU thermal events through throttling rather than physical power cycling; we plan to integrate with rack-level testbeds for hardware-induced faults in 2026 Q3.
- Long-duration soak tests and regulatory customer-specific CAR tests are executed in separate labs (link to scheduling page required).

Appendices:

A. Example golden prompt verification script (bash):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in golden-prompts/*.jsonl; do
  jq -c . $f | while read -r j; do
    prompt=$(echo "$j" | jq -r .prompt)
    expected=$(echo "$j" | jq -r .expected)
    got=$(curl -sS -X POST https://runtime.test.local/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d "{\"prompt\":\"$prompt\"}")
    sim=$(python3 tools/token_similarity.py --expected "$expected" --actual "$got")
    echo "$f,$sim" >> results.csv
  done
done

B. Sample profile directory layout:

/profiles/
  large-gen.yaml
  conversational-saas.yaml
  small-text-search.yaml

C. Contact and escalation:

- Upgrade lead: Aisha Kumar (aisha@redwood.ai)
- On-call rotation: upgrade-squad@pager.redwood.ai
- Security contact for sanitized data questions: Priya Shah (priya@redwood.ai)

D. Quick links:

- Release playbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026
- CI pipelines: infra/pipelines/validate-upgrades.yaml
- Artifact storage policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention

payload.page_title: Safe patch and firmware rotation playbook for private deployments

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a safe, repeatable process for performing host OS patches, accelerator firmware updates, and associated runtime library rotations for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for field operators and SREs responsible for day‑2 maintenance where the goal is to apply security and firmware updates with minimal customer impact and clear forensic evidence in case of rollbacks.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to private deployments that run the Redwood runtime on customer-managed infrastructure (VPC leases or on‑prem racks).
- Covers node-level OS package upgrades, GPU/accelerator firmware upgrades, and model-serving runtime library (inference engine) swaps that require coordinated node restarts.
- Not intended for control-plane-only control updates; see operator control-plane swap guides for those procedures.

Owner and roles:
- Owner: Private Deployments Engineering (oncall: eng-private-deployments-team)
- Operator: Field operator or customer operator performing hands-on steps.
- Reviewer: SRE runbook reviewer for post‑operation evidence and timelines.
- Escalation path: oncall -> runtime-leads -> security (if firmware revocation or supply chain issue suspected).

Preflight checklist (must be satisfied before any patch window):
1) Customer acceptance and maintenance window confirmed in writing.
2) Telemetry baseline capture completed (see Observability section).
3) Backup snapshots completed for persistent runtime state and KV caches where applicable.
4) Model artifact and runtime image provenance verified (signed hashes, attestation).
5) Rollback artifacts produced and staged (firmware images, package repo pointer, runtime image tag).
6) Operator has access to emergency escape route (console, IPMI/iDRAC/BMC, or equivalent).

Minimal risk table (quick reference):
| Component | Risk level | Typical impact | Rollback speed estimate |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| OS kernel/packaged deps | Medium | service restart, glibc ABI regressions rare | 15–45m per node |
| Accelerator firmware | High | degraded performance or hardware unavailability | 30–120m per node (depends on vendor tools) |
| Inference runtime library | Medium–High | model-serving failures or quantization mismatches | 10–60m per node |

Staged procedure (operator runbook):
1. Preflight verification (parallelizable):
   - Confirm customer maintenance window and SLO exceptions.
   - Snapshot runtime state: run snapshot script: 
     curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" https://localhost:5600/api/v1/operator/snapshot > /tmp/runtime-snapshot-$(date -I).json
   - Record baseline telemetry (30 minutes of representative traffic): export metrics to archive: 
     prometheus-cli snapshot --range=30m --out=/tmp/telemetry-baseline-$(date -I).tar.gz

2. Canary node update (single zone, 1 node of smallest footprint):
   - Drain ingress: mark node Unschedulable and wait for in-flight KV/cache flush.
   - Apply OS package updates using the curated repo + APT/YUM wrapper: 
     /opt/redwood/bin/apply-packages --repo=https://repo.redwood.local/private/patches/2026-02 --dry-run=false
   - If accelerating firmware: push firmware via vendor tool with attach logs to evidence bundle. Example vendor command (pseudo): fwupdater --host $BMC --image fw-2026.02.bin --verify-sig --apply
   - Restart runtime process and verify health endpoints: curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || rollback-step
   - Run post-canary smoke tests (see Test matrix).
   - Monitor telemetry for 30 minutes. If no regressions, continue.

3. Zone rollout (parallel within safety limits):
   - Schedule waves with a maximum of N concurrent nodes where N is set by capacity and customer SLA (default N=2 for high-risk firmware).
   - For each node in the wave: drain -> apply -> restart -> smoke test -> uncordon.
   - Maintain rolling prefix/KV cache shard consistency by staggering waves to avoid global cache thrash.

4. Runtime library swap (if required):
   - Use canary image tag and feature-gated rollout via the control-plane (image tags: redwood/runtime:stable-202602-canary)
   - Allow 5–10% traffic to canary path, observe quality/regression metrics, then progress to 25%, 50%, 100%.

Rollback triggers and immediate actions (TRIGGERS are monitored automatically where possible):
- Trigger examples:
  - Latency p95 increase > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes.
  - Error rate increase > 1% absolute or 3x relative baseline.
  - Accelerator device failing to initialize or absent from device list.
  - Model outputs failing integrity checks (tokenization mismatch, nan logits).
- Immediate actions:
  1. Pause the rollout (stop further waves).
  2. Revert control-plane image tag if runtime library caused regression.
  3. For firmware: put impacted nodes into maintenance mode and re-flash previous firmware image using staged rollback artifact.
  4. Notify customer stakeholders via templated message (see Communication templates).
  5. Open an incident record and attach snapshot evidence bundle.

Rollback procedure (firmware-focused):
1) Identify affected nodes using telemetry tags and device IDs.
2) For each node: instruct BMC to re-image or apply staged firmware image with verification flags. Example pseudo-command: 
   bmcctl --host $BMC --user $OP --apply /opt/rollback/fw-2025.11.bin --verify --force-if-unsigned
3) Validate device presence and driver handoff: dmesg | grep -i accel; redwood-admin device list --json
4) Restart runtime and run full smoke and regression test suite.
5) Preserve forensic evidence (firmware update logs, signed hashes, control-plane job ID) and attach to incident.

Observability and telemetry (what to capture):
- Mandatory metrics: request_latency_p95, request_error_rate, device_online_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_quality_regression_score.
- Logs: firmware_update_* logs, system journal, kernel oops, vendor device logs.
- Traces: distributed traces for representative requests to detect tail latency regressions.
- Evidence bundle format: 
  - /evidence/<date>/telemetry-baseline.tar.gz
  - /evidence/<date>/firmware-apply-logs.tar.gz
  - /evidence/<date>/snapshots/runtime-snapshot.json

Test matrix (smoke and verification):
1) Health endpoints: /health, /ready, runtime-admin/kv-status
2) Functional smoke: Gen small/medium/large requests and compare tokenization and top-5 logits against baseline hashes.
3) Performance smoke: 100 synthetic requests with production concurrency distribution; assert p95 < baseline*1.5
4) Device verification: run vendor diag and ensure pass status = true

SLO impact and customer communication:
- Typical maintenance window template: clear statement of expected maximum interruption (e.g., "Best effort: <5m per node; worst case: node offline up to 60m while firmware reflash completes").
- Any anticipated SLO excursions must be pre-approved; update customer SLA sheet and notify account owner.

Communication templates (short):
- Pre-window: "Redwood will perform scheduled firmware/security patching on <date> between <start> and <end>. We expect nominal impact; in the unlikely event of rollback we will follow our incident playbook and provide updates."
- On-deviation: "We have paused the rollout due to observed regression in zone <zone>. Immediate rollback is in progress. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Post-completion: "Maintenance completed. Attached evidence bundle. Please file any post-check concerns within 72 hours."

Post-operation review and evidence retention:
- Create an internal review ticket with attached evidence bundle and performance charts.
- Required fields in the review ticket: operator, start/end times, artifacts applied (package/firmware/runtime tag), telemetry diff summary, rollback occurrences and root-cause hypothesis.
- Retention: evidence bundle kept for 180 days for regulated customers (longer per contract).

Appendix A — Emergency escape actions (fastest path):
- If device-level failure prevents safe reflash, isolate node from load (force-evict) and mark as quiesced in operator console. Prepare same-day physical RMA process as described in the field hardware handbook.

Appendix B — Vendor-specific notes (examples):
- Vendor A (AccelX): requires BMC session with token renewal every 10 minutes during flash. Use accelx-fwcli --keepalive 600. Failure modes: incomplete flash leaves device in "fallback" mode; manual force-recovery required.
- Vendor B (MatrixAccel): supports A/B firmware partitions; rollback is quick but needs driver handshake. Always wait for driver-bound metric before uncordon.

References and related docs:
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/container-image-signing-and-verification-playbook-2026

Contacts:
- Primary runbook owner: eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai
- Oncall: pager: #eng-private-deployments oncall

- 2026-02-15: Initial draft by Ava Martinez
- 2026-03-04: Added rollback triggers and evidence retention guidance (reviewers: Jordan Li, Priya Shah)
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Private Deployments: Upgrade Go/No-Go Checklist (Enterprise)

sections.body: This checklist is the required go/no-go gate for upgrading an *enterprise* Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). It defines the minimum validations, evidence, and sign-offs required before starting the maintenance window, and the stop/rollback criteria during execution.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
Applies to any customer production Private environment upgrade of: (a) control plane components (operator, controller, API gateway), (b) serving runtime/data plane images, (c) cluster dependencies shipped by Redwood (ingress, cert-manager bundles, logging agents), or (d) installer/upgrade tooling.

> Policy dependencies: This page is the operational gate, but approvals/comms requirements are defined in the Change Management Policy and Planned Maintenance Comms SOP. Security-specific sign-off requirements are defined in Secure SDLC: Security Sign-off for Customer Deployments. SLO/error budget checks are defined in Planned Change SLO / Error Budget Review Requirements.

---
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1. Create a change request ticket using the Private Upgrade Change Request template (Jira internal-support).
2. Name a single *Change Owner* (usually Private Deployments on-call or the assigned Solutions/Delivery engineer).
3. Confirm customer-side *Change Approver* and *Operator* contacts (who will be present in the window).
sections.heading: A) Change record + ownership

sections.body:
1. Record current versions: installer, operator/controller, runtime images, chart versions.
2. Confirm target versions and the exact upgrade path (no skipping major versions unless explicitly supported).
3. Confirm model/runtime compatibility notes for the customer’s pinned models.
sections.heading: B) Version + compatibility

sections.body:
1. Confirm backups exist and are recent for:
   - Control plane config state (values files, helm releases, operator CRs)
   - Any Redwood-managed persistent volumes (if present)
   - Customer-provided external dependencies are documented (DB, SSO, KMS)
2. Validate rollback artifacts are available locally: previous installer bundle, previous image tags, and prior values files.
3. Ensure a rollback decision point is explicitly called out in the window plan (see “In-window gates”).
sections.heading: C) Backups + rollback readiness

sections.body:
Run the standard preflight and attach the output to the change ticket:
- Cluster capacity and node readiness checks
- Storage class/PV health
- DNS and egress reachability (if images are pulled during window)
- TLS/certificate expiration checks
- Required Kubernetes API versions present (no deprecated APIs that will break charts)
sections.heading: D) Preflight validations (attach evidence)

sections.body:
1. Confirm dashboards/alerts are visible to Redwood during the window (temporary access granted if needed).
2. Confirm the following signals are available:
   - Control plane API error rate
   - Inference request error rate (5xx)
   - P95 latency for primary routes
   - GPU utilization and OOM/restart rates

---
sections.heading: E) Observability readiness

sections.body: The Change Owner must explicitly record “GO” in the change ticket after confirming all items below.
sections.heading: Go/No-Go gate (must be completed at window start)

sections.body:
- Change Management approvals completed (see policy for approvers by risk level).
- SRE SLO/error budget review completed (or documented risk acceptance).
- Security sign-off completed if triggered (auth/RBAC/audit/TLS/dependency changes).
- Customer Success owner acknowledges comms plan and customer readiness.
sections.heading: 1) Required sign-offs (links required)

sections.body:
- Maintenance notice sent according to comms SOP (timing + channel).
- During-window escalation path confirmed (Redwood + customer).
- “All clear” message drafted for post-window.
sections.heading: 2) Customer communications ready

sections.body:
- Preflight output has no *red* blockers; any *yellow* warnings have an owner and mitigation.
- No open P0/P1 incidents on Redwood side that would reduce ability to respond/rollback.
- If a change freeze is active, an exception is approved and linked.

---
sections.heading: 3) Final technical readiness

sections.body:
- Operator/controller pods Ready
- Control plane API healthy (no sustained 5xx)
- No unexpected restart loops
sections.heading: Proceed only if all are true within 10 minutes

sections.body:
- Runtime pods Ready and stable (no crashloops)
- Can complete a synthetic inference request on each region/cluster segment
- Customer confirms application-level smoke test passes
sections.heading: Proceed only if all are true within 15 minutes

sections.body:
Hold for 30 minutes of steady state with alerting enabled and monitored.

---
sections.heading: Gate C: Verification window

sections.body:
Rollback should be initiated if any of the following occurs and cannot be resolved quickly:
- Sustained inference 5xx above customer’s baseline +5% for >5 minutes
- P95 latency regression >30% for >10 minutes on the primary routes
- Authentication failures (SSO/JWT validation) or RBAC denial spikes
- Audit log pipeline breaks (if contractual requirement)
- Control plane cannot reconcile/upgrade further

---
sections.heading: Rollback criteria (immediate NO-GO / trigger rollback)

sections.body:
- Preflight output
- Version matrix (from/to)
- Rollback plan (commands + expected time)
- Links to SLO/error budget check and any risk acceptance
- Security sign-off (or “not required” rationale)
- Copy of customer comms and confirmation of receipt
sections.heading: Evidence to attach to the change record

sections.body:
Primary: Private Deployments
Consulted: SRE, Security & Compliance, Customer Success
sections.heading: Ownership

payload.page_title: Rollback semantics and hooks (Redwood Private upgrades)

sections.body: This page defines **rollback semantics** for Redwood Private upgrades and the **hook contracts** used by the installer and Helm charts to rollback safely and deterministically.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Provide clear **entry points** for rollback across phases (precheck → backup → control plane → data plane).
- Define a **hook interface** for components (control plane services, data plane workloads, storage/migrations) to participate in rollback.
- Make rollback **safe by default**, **idempotent**, and **auditable**.
- Document how to handle **partial upgrades**, **schema migrations**, and **model cache/state**.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Full blue/green cutover for every Private environment (see ADR).
- Guarantee rollback after every possible irreversible data migration (we require explicit “rollback supported” signaling per release).

---
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body:
- **Upgrade attempt**: one execution of an upgrade plan by the private installer.
- **Upgrade state**: persisted record of plan version, steps executed, artifacts, and checkpoint outputs.
- **Rollback**: coordinated process to restore the deployment to the **previous known-good version (N-1)** using stored state + backups + component hooks.
- **Control plane (CP)**: Redwood Private control plane services (API, auth, scheduler/orchestrator, console backend, upgrade controller).
- **Data plane (DP)**: model serving runtime, routers, worker pools, ingress sidecars, and per-model caches.
- **Rollback supported**: release declares that rollback from N to N-1 is supported given the documented constraints.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Default supported upgrade path is **N-1 → N**. Rollback is **N → N-1**.

---
sections.heading: Version convention

sections.body:
1. **No automatic rollback without operator confirmation**, except when explicitly configured (`--auto-rollback-on-failure`) and only before “Point of No Return” (see below).
2. Rollback must be **deterministic**: given the same stored upgrade state and artifacts, rollback performs the same actions in the same order.
3. Rollback must be **idempotent**: re-running `rollback` after a failure must either continue safely or no-op completed steps.
4. Rollback must preserve **auditability**:
   - Emit audit log events for rollback start/stop and per-stage outcomes.
   - Store the rollback run log and final outcome in the support bundle.
5. Rollback must favor **availability over performance**: safe/known-good configuration first; optimization re-tuning later.

---
sections.heading: Rollback invariants (must always hold)

sections.body:
**When:** prechecks or artifact validation fails before any Kubernetes resources or databases are modified.

**Semantics:** No rollback is needed. Installer prints a failure summary and remediation steps.

**Required behavior:**
- Persist a failed upgrade attempt record (for audit/support).
- Do not modify the stored “current version” pointer.
sections.heading: 1) Pre-deploy / “no changes applied”

sections.body:
**When:** some CP/DP resources have been updated, but we have not performed any irreversible schema changes.

**Semantics:** Rollback is supported via:
- Reverting Helm releases to previous chart/app versions.
- Restoring config/state from saved checkpoints.
- Clearing/reconciling caches.

**Default behavior:** Offer rollback interactively; allow `--auto-rollback-on-failure`.
sections.heading: 2) In-place changes applied, but before the Point of No Return

sections.body:
**When:** a step marks PoNR reached (typically schema/data migration that is not guaranteed reversible).

**Semantics:** Rollback may still be possible, but only with **explicitly supported** restore paths:
- Full database restore from backup snapshot taken at the start of the upgrade attempt.
- “Down migrations” only if the release provides them and they are declared safe.

**Required behavior:**
- Installer must require explicit confirmation with a typed acknowledgement:
  - `--confirm-rollback-after-ponr "I UNDERSTAND THIS MAY CAUSE DATA LOSS"`
- Installer must print a prominent warning describing potential data loss and downtime.

---
sections.heading: 3) After the Point of No Return (PoNR)

sections.body:
- Operator: `redwood-private rollback` (recommended).
- Operator: `redwood-private upgrade --rollback` (roll back the most recent attempt).
- Automation: `--auto-rollback-on-failure` (only pre-PoNR).
- SRE/Support guided recovery (manual steps may be required for PoNR scenarios).

Rollback should be recommended (but not auto-triggered) when:
- CP health checks fail for > 10 minutes after upgrade.
- DB migration step exceeds configured timeout AND cannot be safely resumed.
- DP error rates exceed rollback thresholds during the upgrade window (see SRE runbook).

---
sections.heading: Rollback may be initiated by

sections.body:
The installer persists an **upgrade state record** (stored in the private installer state store; mirrored in the support bundle) containing:
- Upgrade attempt ID
- Previous version (N-1) + target version (N)
- Artifact digests (charts/images/bundles) for both N-1 and N
- Completed steps and timestamps
- Checkpoint outputs (e.g., Helm revision numbers, migration IDs applied, config snapshots)
- PoNR flag + the step that set it
sections.heading: Persisted upgrade state (required for rollback)

sections.body:
- Helm release name + namespace + revision for CP and DP releases
- DB migration baseline (last applied migration ID at start)
- Backup snapshot IDs and verification status

---
sections.heading: Minimum required checkpoint outputs

sections.body:
Rollback is driven by a set of hooks executed by the installer and/or Helm. Hooks are used to:
- Quiesce traffic
- Prevent concurrent writes
- Restore prior configuration
- Roll back schema changes (when supported)
- Reconcile runtime caches
sections.heading: Hook model

sections.body:
1. `rollback.pre` (quiesce & safety gates)
2. `rollback.restore` (revert versions and restore state)
3. `rollback.post` (health checks, cleanup, unlock)
sections.heading: Hooks are executed in phases

sections.body:
- Be **idempotent**.
- Have a **bounded runtime** and a clear timeout.
- Produce structured output for logs (stdout/stderr) and an explicit exit code.
- Avoid printing sensitive values (secrets, tokens). Print resource names/IDs only.

Hook input context (conceptual; passed via env vars/args depending on implementation):
- `UPGRADE_ATTEMPT_ID`
- `FROM_VERSION` (N)
- `TO_VERSION` (N-1)
- `PONR_REACHED=true|false`
- `BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_IDS` (if applicable)
- `DRY_RUN=true|false`
sections.heading: Each hook must

sections.body:
- **Success**: installer continues.
- **Retryable failure**: installer may retry (default: 3 retries with exponential backoff) if hook is marked retryable.
- **Fatal failure**: installer stops and instructs operator to run manual recovery.
sections.heading: Hook result semantics

sections.body:
- **Helm hooks** for Kubernetes resources and Jobs.
- **Installer-managed hooks** for environment-level tasks (artifact switching, bundle validation, backup restore orchestration).

We standardize on these labels/annotations for Kubernetes Jobs used as rollback hooks:
- `redwood.ai/hook-type: rollback`
- `redwood.ai/hook-phase: pre|restore|post`
- `redwood.ai/hook-component: control-plane|data-plane|db|cache|network`
- `redwood.ai/hook-timeout-seconds: "600"` (string because annotations)

---
sections.heading: Components participate in rollback via

sections.body: Rollback ordering must prevent partial incompatibilities. Ordering is:
sections.heading: Ordering rules (deterministic rollback)

sections.body:
1. **Acquire upgrade lock** (prevent parallel upgrades/rollbacks).
2. **Freeze external automation** (e.g., disable GitOps reconciliation if configured; print operator instructions).
3. **Quiesce traffic**:
   - Option A (preferred): set DP routers to “drain mode” (stop accepting new requests; allow in-flight completion).
   - Option B: apply ingress maintenance policy (return 503 with retry-after) when drain mode is unavailable.
4. **Pause background jobs**:
   - Scheduled evals
   - Model warmers/prefetchers
   - Token accounting batch jobs
sections.heading: Phase A — Safety gates (`rollback.pre`)

sections.body:
5. **Control plane rollback first** (CP must be compatible with DP rollback actions and migration tooling):
   - Roll back CP Helm release(s) to prior revision OR apply pinned N-1 artifacts.
   - Wait for CP readiness gates.
6. **Database/schema handling** (see “Schema migrations” section):
   - If PoNR not reached: ensure no further migrations run; restore baseline-compatible settings.
   - If PoNR reached: restore from snapshot and verify.
7. **Data plane rollback**:
   - Roll back DP chart revisions to N-1.
   - Disable any N-only features in DP config.
8. **Model cache/state reconciliation**:
   - Clear or invalidate caches that may contain N-only formats.
   - Rebuild indices lazily post-rollback.
sections.heading: Phase B — Restore (`rollback.restore`)

sections.body:
9. **Health checks**:
   - CP API readiness + auth readiness
   - DB connectivity
   - DP readiness + basic inference smoke test (if enabled)
10. **Unquiesce traffic** (drain off / ingress restored).
11. **Unlock + finalize**:
   - Persist rollback outcome
   - Emit audit events
   - Print operator summary and next steps
sections.heading: Phase C — Post checks (`rollback.post`)

sections.body:
- Stop and print the **exact failing step**, last successful checkpoint, and a one-command retry.
- If failure occurs after traffic is quiesced, keep traffic quiesced unless operator opts out.

---
sections.heading: If any step fails

sections.body:
A “partial upgrade” is any attempt where at least one of these occurred:
- CP Helm revision changed
- DP Helm revision changed
- DB migration executed
- Config/state schema changed

Rollback uses the persisted step list to determine what to revert.
sections.heading: Partial upgrades: how rollback behaves

sections.body:
- If only **DP** steps ran (CP untouched), rollback may still roll back DP first, but must confirm CP compatibility (the compatibility policy gate must pass for N-1 DP with N CP).
- If **DB migrations** executed, rollback must consult PoNR and migration metadata (see below).
- If **artifact mismatch** is detected (e.g., chart digest differs from recorded), rollback stops and requires operator to provide correct artifacts or bundle.

---
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: Schema migration behavior is the most common PoNR driver.
sections.heading: Schema migrations (DB) and rollback

sections.body:
- **Reversible**: safe down-migration supported and tested.
- **Forward-only but compatible**: old application version can run against the new schema (backward compatible).
- **Irreversible**: cannot guarantee old version correctness; PoNR is reached.
sections.heading: Each release must classify migrations as one of

sections.body:
- We default to **forward-only but backward compatible** migrations.
- PoNR is set only when a migration is marked **irreversible**.
sections.heading: Default policy

sections.body:
1. **Reversible**
   - Run down migrations as part of `rollback.restore`.
   - Must be idempotent and guarded by migration IDs.

2. **Forward-only but compatible**
   - Do not run down migrations.
   - Ensure CP/DP config is set to N-1 values.
   - Keep schema as-is; N-1 services must be confirmed compatible.

3. **Irreversible (PoNR)**
   - Restore DB from backup snapshot taken at upgrade start.
   - Warn operator about data loss since snapshot time.
sections.heading: Rollback behavior by category

sections.body:
- Migration runner must enforce lock timeouts and bounded blocking.
- Migrations must have explicit per-step timeouts and emit progress.
- Installer must capture:
  - starting migration ID
  - ending migration ID
  - whether PoNR was reached

---
sections.heading: Required guardrails

sections.body: Model cache issues are a frequent rollback footgun because cache formats, quantization metadata, or routing tables can change between versions.
sections.heading: Model cache/state during rollback

sections.body:
- **KV/prefix caches** (in-memory, per-pod): safe to drop.
- **Disk caches** (PVC-based): may contain versioned formats.
- **Global model registry metadata** (DB/object store): must remain consistent with CP version.
sections.heading: Cache types

sections.body:
- In-memory caches are always dropped by restarting DP pods during rollback.
- Disk caches are handled based on declared compatibility:
  - If cache format is **backward compatible**: preserve PVCs.
  - If cache format is **not guaranteed compatible**: invalidate by bumping cache namespace key or deleting cache directories (preferred) rather than deleting PVCs.
sections.heading: Rollback policy

sections.body:
- `model_id`
- `model_version`
- `runtime_cache_schema_version`

On rollback, the runtime must:
- Set `runtime_cache_schema_version` to the N-1 value.
- Avoid reading N-formatted cache entries.
sections.heading: DP cache keys must include

sections.body:
Rollback may temporarily increase cold-start latency due to cache invalidation. This is expected.

---
sections.heading: Operator-facing note

sections.body: Charts must implement rollback-safe behavior.
sections.heading: Helm hook specifics (Kubernetes)

sections.body:
- Any hook Job must:
  - specify `activeDeadlineSeconds`
  - be restartable or safe to re-run
  - have clear logs and exit status
- Pre-delete hooks must not delete shared state unless explicitly intended.
- Chart changes must avoid schema assumptions that prevent N-1 resources from applying.
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body:
- Use a separate “rollback coordinator” Job triggered by the installer that:
  - sets a ConfigMap flag `redwood.ai/upgrade-mode: rollback`
  - runs component hooks in order (or triggers component jobs)
- Use readiness gates that can be satisfied on N-1.

---
sections.heading: Recommended Helm patterns

sections.body:
- `redwood-private rollback` rolls back the latest upgrade attempt by default.
- `redwood-private rollback --attempt <id>` targets a specific attempt.
- `redwood-private rollback --dry-run` prints planned actions and validations.
sections.heading: Commands

sections.body:
- Attempt ID
- From/to versions
- Whether PoNR was reached
- Backups involved
- Step-by-step progress with explicit component names
sections.heading: Rollback output must include

sections.body:
1) Validate rollback artifacts (N-1 bundle) ... OK
2) Acquire upgrade lock ... OK
3) Drain ingress ... OK
4) Rollback control-plane (helm revision 42 -> 41) ... OK
5) DB restore required (PoNR reached) ... restoring snapshot snap-0f12ab... OK
6) Rollback data-plane (helm revision 108 -> 107) ... OK
7) Invalidate model disk cache namespace ... OK
8) Health checks ... OK
9) Restore ingress ... OK

Result: ROLLBACK_SUCCEEDED (duration 18m32s)

---
sections.heading: Example (abbreviated)

sections.body:
- Hooks marked retryable may be retried up to 3 times.
- If a retryable hook still fails:
  - installer stops
  - prints the next safe manual action
  - leaves the system in the safest known mode (typically traffic quiesced)
sections.heading: Failure handling and retry semantics

sections.body:
- GitOps controller continuously re-applies N resources.
- DB snapshot restore fails due to storage constraints.
- Artifact mirror lacks N-1 images/charts.

---
sections.heading: Manual intervention examples

sections.body:
- `private.upgrade.rollback.started`
- `private.upgrade.rollback.step.completed`
- `private.upgrade.rollback.failed`
- `private.upgrade.rollback.completed`
sections.heading: Rollback must emit audit events (minimum)

sections.body: - `attempt_id`, `from_version`, `to_version`, `ponr_reached`, `environment_id`, `operator_identity`, `artifact_digests`
sections.heading: Required event fields (high level)

sections.body:
- upgrade/rollback plan artifacts
- installer logs
- per-hook job logs
- the final state record

---
sections.heading: Support bundle must include

sections.body:
A Private release may claim “rollback supported” only if:
- Compatibility policy includes N ↔ N-1 checks for CP/DP components.
- Migrations are classified and documented (reversible / compatible / irreversible).
- Backup snapshot strategy is validated for supported storage backends.
- CI includes at least one N-1 → N → N-1 cycle in an ephemeral environment.

---
sections.heading: Release requirements to claim “rollback supported”

sections.body:
Below is a representative Kubernetes Job hook template used by charts. (Exact fields may vary by chart; follow current chart conventions.)

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: redwood-rollback-db-check
  namespace: redwood-system
  labels:
    redwood.ai/hook-type: rollback
    redwood.ai/hook-phase: restore
    redwood.ai/hook-component: db
  annotations:
    redwood.ai/hook-timeout-seconds: "900"
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 900
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: rollback-db
          image: registry.redwood.ai/private/db-tools:${IMAGE_TAG}
          args: ["rollback", "--attempt", "$(UPGRADE_ATTEMPT_ID)"]
          env:
            - name: UPGRADE_ATTEMPT_ID
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: redwood-upgrade-state
                  key: attempt_id

---
sections.heading: Appendix A — Hook interface example (Job template)

sections.body:
- CP cannot become ready within the documented timeout and logs indicate config/schema mismatch.
- DP error rate stays above the upgrade alert threshold after the stabilization window.
- Migration is stuck and cannot safely resume.
sections.heading: Roll back when

sections.body:
- Only one DP pool is failing readiness (try pool-level remediation first).
- A precheck warning is triggered post-upgrade (address warning; do not rollback).

For detailed alert thresholds and escalation rules, see the SRE runbook: “upgrade-related alerts and mitigation.”
sections.heading: Do NOT roll back immediately when

payload.page_title: Orchestrated control-plane swap and fallback playbook

sections.body:
Purpose and scope

This playbook defines a repeatable, low-risk process to orchestrate a control-plane swap between Redwood's hosted control plane and a customer-private control plane (or between two private control-plane versions) with explicit fallback and rollback steps. It covers: pre-swap readiness checks, phased swap orchestration, KV cache handover, traffic steering, verification gates, automated rollback triggers, and post-swap evidence collection. This document is intended for operators, field engineers, and SREs responsible for private deployments.

When to use this playbook

- Planned upgrades to control-plane software where a full in-place upgrade is impractical (major version or architecture change).
- Emergency diversion from hosted control plane to private control plane (or vice-versa) for customer isolation or regulatory requirements.
- Migration between control-plane clusters for scale, geo-failover, or tenancy rebalancing.

Key services referenced

- control-plane-api: the HTTP/GRPC endpoint handling tenant and model routing policy decisions.
- runtime-proxy: the data-plane proxy used at customer VPC edge to route inference traffic.
- operator-agent: the field operator service that performs image swap, config apply, and evidence bundle collection.
- kv-store (redis-ephemeral / s3-backed snapshot): stores runtime ephemeral state and prefix/KV caches.
- telemetry-gateway: aggregates traces, metrics, and log events for SLO validation.

SLOs and safety thresholds (gates)

- Successful RPC error-rate during canary window must remain < 0.5% (control-plane-api).
- 99th percentile control-plane latency must not increase by > 40% compared to pre-swap baseline.
- KV cache warmup hit-rate target >= 65% after model handover within 15 minutes.
- No more than 2% of tenants may exhibit critical inference latency regressions (>500ms increase) during the swap.

Pre-swap checklist (operator must verify)

1. Backups & evidence
   - Take a snapshot of control-plane database and model-variant manifest: operator-agent cli: run "operator-agent snapshot --target control-plane-db --tag pre-swap-<date>".
   - Export KV cache manifest and last-consistent cursor for each tenant: "kvctl export --out pre-swap-kv-manifest.json".
2. Capacity & compatibility
   - Confirm target control-plane nodes meet runtime compatibility matrix (see table below).
   - Reserve burst capacity of at least 20% in the serving cluster to avoid overload during cache miss storms.
3. Observability & test harness
   - Ensure telemetry-gateway retention window covers pre-swap baseline metrics.
   - Provision a synthetic workload (see Quick test harness) with representative sequence lengths and request mix.
4. Communication
   - Notify customer NOC and internal stakeholders; create incident runbook with oncall escalation list.

Compatibility matrix (example)

| Component | Minimum supported version | Recommended version | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| control-plane-api | v2.8.0 | v3.0.x | v3.0 adds policy caching improvements; requires runtime-proxy >= v1.4 |
| runtime-proxy | v1.3.2 | v1.5.x | v1.5 contains KV handoff endpoint and improved timeout handling |
| operator-agent | v0.9.0 | v1.1.x | operator-agent v1.x supports evidence bundle compression |
| kv-store | redis 6.2+ or s3 snapshot | redis 7.x | When using redis, enable AOF snapshots for quick restore |

Phased orchestration (high-level)

1) Canary phase (single-tenant/small slice)
   - Select canary tenant(s) using: high-traffic + tolerant=FALSE labels. Canary traffic should represent 1-3% of typical load.
   - Steps:
     a) Deploy control-plane software to new cluster (or enable secondary control plane) in standby mode.
     b) Configure routing policy rule: traffic for canary tenant -> new-control-plane endpoint. Use routing policy key: "swap-canary-<id>".
     c) Start synthetic workload and watch SLOs for 10 minutes.
     d) Validate KV cache warmup and inference tail latency.

2) Incremental rollout (progressive tenant fanout)
   - Expand to 10% of tenants over next 30 minutes if metrics remain green. Each expansion step: 10 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100% using predefined tenant cohorts.
   - At each step, validate: error-rate < 0.5%, p99 latency delta < 40%, KV warmup >= 65%.

3) Full swap and quarantine windows
   - Once at 100% and stable for 60 minutes, mark new control plane as primary and trigger a final state sync.
   - Hold a 2-hour quarantine window during which a coordinated rollback is still considered low-impact.

Automatic rollback triggers

If any of the following occur within the defined observation window, execute an immediate rollback to the previous control plane and follow the rollback evidence checklist:

- Total error-rate exceeds 1.5% for the canary group for > 3 minutes.
- p99 latency increases by > 100% for more than 5 minutes.
- KV warmup hit-rate below 40% after 15 minutes for more than 5 tenants.
- More than 5 tenants report inference failures measured by application-level 5xx rates.

Rollback sequence (fast path)

1. Freeze routing changes: set routing policy to failover -> previous-control-plane. Command:
   - curl -X POST https://control-plane-admin.internal/apply-routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer <operator-token>' -d '{"mode":"failover","target":"previous-control-plane"}'
2. Scale down new control-plane traffic adapter to drain connections: "kubectl scale deployment cp-adapter-new --replicas=0 -n redwood-control"
3. Restore KV snapshot if necessary: "kvctl import --from pre-swap-kv-manifest.json --apply"
4. Rehydrate evidence bundle: operator-agent collect --tag pre-swap-<date> --include logs,metrics,traces
5. Notify stakeholders: runbook-trigger email templates located at /templates/rollback-notify.md

Post-rollback diagnostics

- Collect control-plane-api logs (last 2 hours) and grep for errors with code >= 500.
- Correlate telemetry-gateway traces to identify tail latency causation.
- Run model-sanity test suite against both control-plane versions to detect behavioral differences.

Operator CLI quick commands (examples)

- Start a canary swap:
  operator-agent start-swap --target new-control-plane --tenants canary-list.json --dry-run=false --evidence-tag pre-swap-<date>
- Monitor swap progress:
  operator-agent status --swap-id <id> --format table
- Force immediate rollback:
  operator-agent rollback --swap-id <id> --reason "metric-trigger" --collect-evidence

KV cache handover considerations

- Strategy A: live stream bulk prefetch
  - Pre-compute top-K prefixes per-tenant and seed target runtime-proxy via kvctl seed --manifest pre-swap-kv-manifest.json.
  - Advantages: faster warmup. Disadvantages: bandwidth and storage transient spike.

- Strategy B: on-demand lazy warming with throttled misses
  - Allow misses to fall back to model origin with a throttled concurrent limit to protect model backend.
  - Advantages: minimal up-front cost. Disadvantages: higher initial latency for some tenants.

Decision guidance: use Strategy A for latency-sensitive workloads with predictable prefix distributions (chatbots, search reranking). Use Strategy B when bandwidth or storage for full prefetch is constrained.

Observability checklist (what to watch)

- control-plane-api: RPC error-rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GC pause spikes.
- runtime-proxy: connection churn, per-tenant KV hit-rate, serialization errors.
- telemetry-gateway: missing spans, ingestion lag > 30s triggers alert.
- infra: CPU steal, node OOMs, disk IO saturation.

Synthetic test harness (quick)

1. Use the canonical synthetic client: redwood-test-client v1.2.
2. Load pattern: 60% short requests (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens).
3. Run in three phases: baseline (15m), canary (10m), expanded (continuous during rollout).

Evidence and audit bundle (required)

- Must include: control-plane-db snapshot id, kv manifest, operator-agent action log, telemetry slice (baseline and during swap), pod-level logs for cp-adapter and runtime-proxy, incident timeline.
- Bundle format: tar.gz with JSON manifest describing included files and checksums. Command to collect: "operator-agent collect-evidence --swap-id <id> --out /tmp/swap-evidence-<id>.tar.gz"

Troubleshooting playbook (short)

- Symptom: KV warmup low despite prefetch
  - Check redis AOF/memory pressure; ensure eviction policy is not aggressive. Run: "redis-cli INFO MEMORY" and "kvctl show-evictions --tenant <id>".
- Symptom: sudden p99 tail spike
  - Check for long GC pauses in control-plane API pods (describe pod, jstack if possible), and review recent kernel updates or node-level maintenance.
- Symptom: gradual increase in error-rate after 30m
  - Inspect model-variant manifest divergence and verify model artifact checksums across clusters (sha256).

Roll-forward (if canary passed and gradual rollout completed)

- Finalize primary assignment in the global routing table and mark old control plane as read-only for 24 hours.
- Schedule decommission window for the old control plane only after 7 days of stable telemetry and no rollback incidents.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall: private-deployments-sre@redwood.internal).
- Secondary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-lead@redwood.internal).
- Escalation: Platform Pager (pager redwood-platform) -> Site Reliability Lead.

Related artifacts and references

- Upgrade decision record: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/incremental-stateful-upgrade-strategy-2027
- KV migration playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025
- Operator CLI reference: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operator-cheat-sheet-for-field-installations-2027

Revision history

- 2027-11-02: Drafted by Maya Chen.
- 2028-03-12: Reviewed and published; added automated rollback triggers and more detailed KV handover guidance.

payload.page_title: Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract

sections.body:
Overview
This document defines the artifact shepherding contract for staged rollouts and rollbacks on Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It formalizes the signals, gating thresholds, operator procedures, and evidence-retention requirements that must be satisfied for a model or runtime artifact to progress through canary -> ramp -> full release, and the exact steps to safely rollback. It applies to control-plane and data-plane artifacts (serving runtime binaries, model bundles, quantized weights, kernel patches, operator images).

Scope
- Applies to all private-deploy customer environments managed by Redwood (VPC and on-prem packaged installs).
- Covers: artifact signing & provenance, preflight validation, canary orchestration, automated and manual rollback triggers, post-rollback forensic evidence collection.
- Excludes: customer-managed model training pipelines and customer-owned third-party appliances (see related_pages for handoff guidance).

Goals
- Minimize customer-facing impact during upgrades.
- Ensure deterministic rollback that preserves customer state and audit evidence.
- Provide clear, reproducible operator playbook for on-call and field engineers.

Key roles and ownership
- Release Owner (engineering): owns stage gating, artifact bundles, and the rollout schedule.
- Field Operator (operator / customer engineering): executes rollout and rollback in the customer environment and performs local verification.
- SRE Oncall: monitors platform-level SLOs and authorizes emergency rollback if automated circuits do not trigger.
- Security/Compliance Reviewer: verifies artifact provenance (signatures, SBOM) for regulated customers before ramp.

Prerequisites (pre-release checklist)
1. Artifact packaging: each bundle must include a signed manifest (COSE/PKCS7) and SBOM. The manifest contains: semantic_version, checksums (sha256), compatible_runtime_ids, and rollback_guard_tags.
2. Operator tools: field environment must have redwoodctl >= 1.12.0 installed, with operator credentials and a valid operator-session token.
3. Telemetry contract: customer telemetry export must include these metrics at 30s resolution: request_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tok_per_request, model_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.
4. Backup: snapshot of KV cache and stateful operator artifacts taken and stored off-host. Snapshot command: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.

Staged rollout strategy (canonical flow)
1) Canary (0 -> 2%):
   - Deploy artifact to a small canary cohort (2% traffic or 1 small tenant, whichever is more conservative).
   - Retain both old and new model weights and the ability to route by tenant.
   - Minimum dwell time: 30 minutes or 10k requests, whichever is reached first.
   - Automatic gating checks (see gating criteria) run continuously.
2) Ramp (2% -> 25%):
   - Increase traffic in timed increments: 2% -> 10% -> 25% over 2 hours, pausing 20 minutes at each step to validate.
   - At each pause, run the full validation suite: synthetic traces, baseline eval prompts, and production smoke queries as described in Validation section.
3) Broad roll (25% -> 100%):
   - Continue to 50% then 100% only after passing two consecutive ramp windows with green signals and signoff from Release Owner.

Gating criteria (automated triggers)
- Abort and immediate rollback if any of the following are observed during a dwell window:
  - Absolute error-rate increase: model_error_rate increases by >0.5 percentage points and the delta is statistically significant with p<0.01 over the last 30 minutes.
  - Latency degradation: p95_latency_ms increases by >50% or exceeds 500ms sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Token budget regressions: tok_per_request increases >25% without commensurate quality improvement (see quality checks).
  - KV cache regressions: kv_cache_hit_rate drops by >15% leading to >10% increase in back-end load.
  - Resource saturation: GPU utilization >95% on primary nodes for >5 minutes.
- Soft warning thresholds: p50 latency increase >20%, error-rate increase >0.2pp — these notify SRE and Release Owner and pause automatic ramps pending review.

Manual rollback criteria (operator discretion)
- Single-customer severe error (data corruption, PII exposure), or customer SLA breach.
- Failed dependency rollout (e.g., operator CRD changed and was not applied correctly).
- Security or compliance compromise detected in SBOM or signature validation.

Rollback procedures (ordered checklist)
1. Initiate rollback command (preferred automated path if gated):
   - redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots
2. If automated rollback fails or is unavailable, perform explicit operator fallback:
   - Step A: Quiesce incoming traffic to the affected tenant cohort: redwoodctl traffic set-weights --deployment <id> --weights old:100,new:0
   - Step B: Restore model artifact and runtime image from signed archive: redwoodctl image install --from s3://redwood-artifacts/<artifact>-vX.Y.Z --verify-signature
   - Step C: Apply operator manifest rollback: kubectl -n redwood operator set image redwood-operator=redwood/operator:<previous-tag>
   - Step D: Rehydrate state from snapshot if required: redwoodctl snapshot restore --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD --target <deployment-id>
3. Post-rollback verification (must complete before closing incident):
   - Verify all gating metrics are within pre-release baseline for 60 minutes.
   - Run smoke test suite (listed in Validation).
   - Confirm no loss of persistent requests and that KV cache coherence is restored.
4. Evidence capture: collect operator logs, artifact manifests, signature verification output, and telemetry windows for the entire rollout and rollback period. Store in the evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD/. Preserve for minimum 90 days for regulated customers.

Validation and acceptance tests (examples)
- Baseline eval prompts: 200 prompt set used to compare semantic deviation. Pass criteria: mean semantic-similarity drop <0.02 measured with the approved comparator model.
- Synthetic throughput run: 30-minute steady-state at 1.5x expected QPS with 95th percentile latency < configured SLO.
- End-to-end trace checks: sampled requests must show no >2% increase in external service calls (upstream indices, database) attributable to artifact change.

Telemetry and monitoring contract
- Required dashboards: "Artifact Rollout Overview", "Canary Health Summary", "KV Cache Drift", and "Model Quality Regression".
- Alerting: automated must-fail alerts for gating criteria must notify SRE, Field Operator, and Release Owner via the oncall channel and create a paging incident if severity is P1.
- Sampling: preserve full traces for 2 hours, aggregated metrics for 30 days, and raw request logs for 7 days by default. For customers with compliance needs, extend to 365 days as per their telemetry SLA.

Forensic and audit tasks after rollback
- Freeze related telemetry windows for the duration of the investigation.
- Generate artifact provenance report: include manifest signatures, uploader identity, and SBOM diff between versions.
- If data exposure is suspected, follow the private-deploy evidence-preservation playbook (see related_pages).

Post-release remediation and learnings
- Required deliverables within 72 hours of rollback: a short incident brief (what changed, why gate failed, immediate fixes), and a remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Release Owner must create a follow-up action ticket for any required runtime or model quantization adjustments.
- If rollback was triggered by quality regression, add failing prompts to the guarded prompt set and schedule a regression evaluation in the next model onboarding sprint.

Appendix A — Example gating table (human-readable)
Rows: Metric | Baseline | Abort delta | Soft warning
- model_error_rate | 0.6% | +0.5pp (abort) | +0.2pp (warn)
- p95_latency_ms | 180ms | +50% or >500ms (abort) | +20% (warn)
- kv_cache_hit_rate | 72% | -15pp (abort) | -8pp (warn)
- gpu_util | 65% | >95% sustained 5m (abort) | 80% (warn)

Appendix B — Quick CLI cheatsheet
- Create snapshot: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-$(date +%F)
- Start canary: redwoodctl rollout start --deployment <id> --artifact <artifact-uri> --stage canary --canary-percent 2
- Check rollout status: redwoodctl rollout status --deployment <id>
- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <previous-semver>

Appendix C — Escalation matrix
- 0–15 minutes: Field Operator triages and attempts automated rollback.
- 15–60 minutes: SRE oncall engaged; Release Owner notified.
- >60 minutes or data-loss event: Executive on-call and Security engaged, customer CS lead notified.

References and related pages
- See related_pages for the forensic rollback protocol and operator handshake runbooks.
- SBOM and signature guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/artifact-signing-guidelines (internal link).

Revision history
- 2026-02-15: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2026-06-01: Added telemetry contract and gating percentiles (reviewers: Liam O'Rourke).
- 2026-08-03: Tightened canary dwell time and added evidence retention for regulated customers (reviewers: Priya Singh, Diego Morales).
