payload.page_title: Private Deploy Telemetry & Integration Contract

sections.body:
Overview:

This document defines the telemetry and integration contract that Redwood Inference requires for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for customer SREs, network/security teams, and Redwood delivery engineers. The goal is to create a predictable, auditable, and minimally invasive telemetry footprint so Redwood and the customer can operate and troubleshoot the private deployment while meeting privacy and compliance constraints.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: telemetry (metrics, traces, logs), health probes, control-plane callbacks, auth for observability endpoints, retention and encryption requirements, and validation tests used during onboarding and day-2 operations.
- Audience: customer platform/SRE, customer security/compliance, Redwood deployment engineers, Redwood Support.

Design principles:
- Minimum viable telemetry: only collect what is necessary for runbookable alerts and SLA verification.
- Data minimization: avoid customer PII in telemetry; use hashed or redacted identifiers where possible.
- Configurable retention and egress: customers may opt to keep telemetry inside their VPC or allow Redwood to ingest metrics over an authenticated channel for operational support.
- Deterministic schema: metrics, span names, and log keys must follow the schemas below to allow Redwood tooling to parse and generate alerts automatically.

Prerequisites (customer responsibilities):
1) Network connectivity: (if choosing Redwood-managed observability) allow outbound TLS egress to the Redwood observability endpoint (host: obs.redwood-inference.internal OR customizable host supplied by the customer) on port 443. Alternatively, customers must provide an HTTP(S) endpoint that conforms to the schema below.
2) TLS & Auth: TLS 1.2+ enforced. Mutual TLS (mTLS) for high-sensitivity customers; otherwise Bearer token with rotating key is acceptable.
3) Time sync: NTP within ±5s across nodes.
4) Minimal system permissions: service account that can write to the provided observability endpoint and read local runtime logs.

Telemetry types and required fields:
1) Metrics (Prometheus-style time series recommended)
   - Required metric names and labels:
     - redwood.runtime.request_count{model,route,status_code} (counter)
     - redwood.runtime.request_latency_ms{model,route,p95_bucket} (histogram/summary)
     - redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio{model,route} (gauge)
     - redwood.node.cpu_utilization{node_id,zone} (gauge)
     - redwood.node.gpu_memory_used_mb{node_id,gpu_index} (gauge)
   - Labels guidance:
     - model: model identifier (e.g., gptq-13b-v1). Use the customer-visible name; avoid user IDs.
     - route: API route name (e.g., /v1/generate or /v1/chat).
     - status_code: 200, 503, 429, etc.

2) Traces (OpenTelemetry compatible)
   - Required spans and attributes:
     - Span: redwood.request (root span) with attributes: request.id, model, route, input_tokens, output_tokens, upstream_fallback (boolean), cache_hit (boolean).
     - Child spans: redwood.kv_cache.lookup, redwood.batch.serialize, redwood.kernel.exec with attributes: duration_ms, gpu_id, batch_size.
   - Sampling: default 1% sample of all requests; 100% sample of requests with status_code >= 500 and of requests explicitly flagged in the test harness. Customers may raise sampling to 10% for onboarding windows.

3) Logs
   - Structured JSON logs preferred. Log fields required for server logs:
     - timestamp (ISO8601), level (INFO/WARN/ERROR), service (e.g., runtime-agent), node_id, request_id (if request-scoped), message, error_code (if present), stack (if error).
   - Sensitive data handling: request.payload must NOT contain raw user input. If request-level context is required for debugging, the customer must supply a redacted payload or a hashed token that maps locally to the raw data under customer control.

Delivery models (customer selects one):
A) Customer-hosted observability (recommended for high compliance):
   - All telemetry is written to customer-managed endpoints inside the VPC. Redwood will provide the expected schemas and alert rules as files. Redwood support connects via ephemeral bastion and shared playbook.

B) Hybrid: Metrics & health probes are exposed to customer endpoints; Redwood ingests anonymized metrics via a secure egress channel for SLA verification. Traces and logs remain customer-hosted unless explicit permission is granted.

C) Redwood-managed ingestion: Customer allows outbound telemetry to obs.redwood-inference.internal using mTLS. This model is used for customers who want Redwood to manage alerting and incident response.

Auth and certificate management:
- mTLS: preferred for Redwood-managed ingestion. Customer provides CA or Redwood provides CSR flow and short-lived certs.
- Bearer tokens: rotate every 30 days. The token rotation endpoint is: POST /api/v1/telemetry/rotate on the customer control plane for exchange.

Schema examples:
- Metric export (Prometheus exposition format example):
  # HELP redwood_runtime_request_count Total number of requests served
  # TYPE redwood_runtime_request_count counter
  redwood_runtime_request_count{model="gptq-13b-v1",route="/v1/generate",status_code="200"} 1245

- Trace span example (OTLP JSON snippet):
  {
    "name": "redwood.request",
    "attributes": {
      "request.id": "req-2f8b",
      "model": "gptq-13b-v1",
      "route": "/v1/chat",
      "input_tokens": 32,
      "output_tokens": 128,
      "cache_hit": false
    }
  }

- Log example (single line JSON):
  {"timestamp":"2026-02-10T18:32:04Z","level":"ERROR","service":"runtime-agent","node_id":"node-17","request_id":"req-2f8b","message":"KERNEL_OOM during kernel.exec","error_code":"KERNEL_OOM"}

Operational SLOs and alerting matrix (minimum):
| Signal | SLO / Threshold | Alert | Owner |
|-------|----------------|-------|-------|
| request_success_rate (30d rolling) | >= 99.5% | page on < 99.0% | Customer SRE + Redwood on-call |
| tail_latency_p99 (in ms) | <= 2000ms for 90% of routes | alert when p99 > 4000ms for 10m | Customer SRE |
| node.cpu_utilization | <= 85% sustained | page at 95% for 5m | Customer SRE |
| kv_cache_hit_ratio | >= 70% for cacheable routes | warn below 50% for 30m | Redwood support |

Note: For customers using Redwood-managed ingestion, Redwood will create these alerts and share alert playbooks. For customer-hosted metrics, Redwood will provide the Prometheus alert rules and Grafana dashboards as IaC.

Onboarding validation checklist (run as part of deployment acceptance tests):
1) Metrics scrape: Verify Prometheus scrape of runtime endpoints returns required metrics and labels.
2) Trace sampling: Confirm traces are exported and sampled at 1% with rule exceptions.
3) Log schema: Validate structured logs against schema using the provided JSON Schema file (redwood-telemetry-log-schema-v1).
4) End-to-end test: Execute a synthetic request that triggers kernel.exec and verify corresponding metric increment, trace span, and log entry appear within 60s.
5) Auth & certs: Rotate telemetry token and verify 401 -> 200 transition on key update.

Upgrade and rollback considerations for telemetry:
- During upgrades, retain dual-schema compatibility for 2 minor releases. All new metric names must be introduced alongside the old names for 30 days with telemetry tags indicating version.
- Rollback steps must include backfilling any missing metric where a rename occurred: a shim exporter can write the legacy metric name for 48 hours after rollback.

Day-2 operational playbook excerpt (high level):
1) Incident triage:
   - Step 1: Confirm alerts (metrics/trace/log).
   - Step 2: Identify node and request_ids via traces or logs.
   - Step 3: If kernel OOM or node-level resource saturation, scale GPU pool or trigger failover policy (see customer-specific HA doc).
   - Step 4: If unavailable, engage the Redwood on-call via the secure channel and provide sanitized request_ids and time windows.

2) Routine maintenance:
   - Rotate telemetry tokens on a 30-day cadence.
   - Verify scraping and ingestion post-maintenance within 15 minutes.
   - Run the synthetic end-to-end test after each major package upgrade.

Data retention and compliance options:
- Default retention: metrics 90 days (aggregated to 1d after 30 days), traces 30 days (sampled), logs 30 days.
- Customer can request retention changes; any retention >365 days requires a compliance exception and approval from legal/security.

Escalation and ownership:
- First responder: Customer SRE (documented in the customer runbook supplied at handoff).
- Second line: Redwood deployment engineer (on-call) with access to anonymized telemetry and runbook.
- Third line: Redwood runtime engineering for kernel-level faults.

Deliverables from Redwood to customer:
- Prometheus scrape configuration (YAML) and alert rule set.
- Grafana dashboards (JSON) for runtime, nodes, and caches.
- Trace sampling and span processor config (OTLP/collector config).
- Telemetry validation harness (Python script) used during onboarding.

Appendix A — Example Prometheus job snippet:
  scrape_configs:
    - job_name: "redwood-runtime"
      static_configs:
        - targets: ["10.0.2.15:9100"]
      metrics_path: /metrics
      scheme: https
      bearer_token_file: /etc/redwood/telemetry-token

Appendix B — Minimum dashboard panels to include:
- Requests per second (per model)
- P95/P99 latency (per route)
- KV cache hit ratio over time
- GPU memory used and utilization per node
- Trace-error waterfall for failed requests

Related pages:
- Link: eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-acceptance-and-smoke-validation-2026 (for full acceptance tests)
- Link: eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026 (for day2 automation)

Contact and support:
- Primary delivery contact: samira.patel@redwood.ai
- Escalation channel: private-deploy-onsite-slack (invite provided during onboarding)

Revision history:
- 2026-02-12: Created by Samira Patel
- 2026-03-01: Clarified sampling guidance and added hybrid model option

payload.page_title: Field Acceptance & Safety Certification Playbook for Offline (Air‑gapped) Deploys

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines the field acceptance and safety certification criteria for offline / air‑gapped private deployments of the Redwood runtime. It is intended for delivery engineers, customer site operators, and SREs who perform the final acceptance verification and produce evidence for compliance packages.

Scope

- Applies to: on‑prem or isolated VPC deployments where control‑plane connectivity is intentionally restricted (air‑gapped or dark site).
- Excludes: hosted Redwood API, fully connected Dedicated deployments.
- Goal: provide a deterministic, repeatable test suite and sign‑off template to ensure the deployment meets safety, availability, and traceability requirements prior to customer handover.

Quick summary of acceptance outcomes (must all PASS to sign off)

1) Functional health: all core services report healthy and APIs respond to local queries.
2) Safety resilience: node restart, power loss, and network partition recovery tested.
3) Observability: required telemetry artifacts produced and retained locally as evidence.
4) Security baseline: image signatures validated, KMS/HSM handshake validated (when applicable), minimal privileged access verified.
5) Performance sanity: representative inference workload meets configured SLOs for p50/p95/p99.

Roles and responsibilities

- Delivery Engineer (owner): run acceptance suite, collate artifacts, mark preliminary PASS/FAIL.
- Customer Site Operator: provide physical access and power/networking support, verify facility safety steps.
- SRE Field Reviewer: audit evidence, approve final certification.
- Product Security: validate signature / KMS evidence if restricted.

Prerequisites (before starting the playbook)

- Images delivered and verified by checksum/signature. Provide signed manifest (sha256) in /opt/redwood/manifests/.
- Hardware included in the delivery manifest and power/cooling validated by customer on site.
- Basic network cabling and switch configuration completed. Out‑of‑band management (BMC) reachable from operator network.
- Local admin user created: redwood-admin (sudo without password restricted by time window).

Required artifacts to produce during the run (evidence bundle)

- signed-manifest.txt (sha256 checksums + signer identity)
- health-checks.json (service health endpoints snapshot)
- telemetry-snapshot.tar.gz (metrics/ logs / traces for the test window)
- firmware-and-drivers.txt (nvidia-smi / lspci / dmidecode outputs)
- power-fail-recovery.log (step trace for power tests)
- acceptance-signoff.md (signed by delivery engineer and customer operator)

Service names referenced in this playbook

- redwood-runtime.service (primary inference runtime)
- redwood-agent.service (node agent handling KV cache and local routing)
- control-plane-proxy (local proxy for private control plane connectivity, may be disabled in true airgap)
- kv-cache-daemon (local at-rest cache service)
- node-watchdog.service (operator safety watchdog for unattended reboots)

Acceptance tests (step‑by‑step)

1) Baseline verification (10–20 minutes)
   a) Verify signed images: sha256sum -c /opt/redwood/manifests/signed-manifest.txt
      - Expected: all OK. Document signer and checksum.
   b) Validate service units: systemctl status redwood-runtime redwood-agent node-watchdog
      - Expected: active (running) for each. Capture `systemctl show -p ActiveState,MainPID` output.
   c) Health endpoint checks: curl --unix-socket /var/run/redwood.sock http://localhost/health | jq .
      - Expected: {"overall":"ok","components":[...] }

2) Functional smoke (20–40 minutes)
   a) Local inference request: use the bundled smoke client. Example: /opt/redwood/bin/smoke-client --model local-l2 --prompt "Hello" --max-tokens 16
      - Expected: valid token stream within 200ms median for small model; capture output (stdout) to health-checks.json.
   b) KV cache warmup: run 100 short requests and confirm cache hit rate > 60%. Use /opt/redwood/bin/cache-stats --window 60s.

3) Performance sanity (1–2 hours depending on hardware)
   a) Run the workload profile supplied for the customer (profile file location: /opt/redwood/tests/profiles/<customer>-baseline.yaml).
   b) Observe p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization. SLO targets for acceptance (configurable per contract):
      - p50 inference latency: <= 35ms (small L1 models)
      - p95 inference latency: <= 90ms
      - p99 inference latency: <= 250ms
      - throughput stability: <10% jitter over 15 min window
   c) Collect metrics: curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep -E "(inference_latency|gpu_util|cache_hit)" > metrics.txt

4) Safety & resilience tests (sequential; coordinate with customer operator)
   Note: these tests intentionally induce disruptions. Ensure customer signs the safety waiver section in acceptance-signoff.md before proceeding.

   a) Graceful node restart
      - Command: sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "5m" --no-pager > restart-recovery.log
      - Acceptance: runtime resumes within configured restart window (default 60s) and recovers KV state; no data corruption in local cache.

   b) Simulated power failure (controlled)
      - Procedure: use remote PDU to cut power for a single node for 30s, then restore.
      - Acceptance: node boots to operational state within site SLA (default 10 minutes), node-watchdog performed expected reboot, logs captured to power-fail-recovery.log.

   c) Network partition/failover
      - Procedure: isolate tenant network from site management network for 90s. If control-plane-proxy is enabled, confirm the runtime can continue processing local queued requests and that fallback policies engage.
      - Acceptance: no more than 1% request failure during partition; queued requests are replayed; alerts fired into local alerting backend. Capture partition-recovery.log.

   d) Disk corruption detection (read-only simulation)
      - Procedure: mount a loop device with read-only flag to simulate partial disk failure for /var/lib/redwood/cache.
      - Acceptance: runtime detects read-only filesystem, transitions affected services to degraded mode and emits evidence to health-checks.json.

5) Security & image attestation tests (30 minutes)
   a) Verify image signature with customer KMS/HSM or provided signer. Command example: cosign verify-blob --key /opt/redwood/keys/cosign.pub /opt/redwood/images/redwood-runtime.tar.gz
      - Expected: verification success.
   b) RBAC smoke: attempt an elevated operation from non-admin account; expect denial. Capture sudoers and audit logs.

Observability and evidence capture (always collect)

- Metrics snapshot: /opt/redwood/bin/dump-metrics --output telemetry-snapshot/metrics.prom
- Log snapshot: tar -czf telemetry-snapshot/logs.tar.gz /var/log/redwood/* (include system/journal logs for the test window)
- Traces: if local jaeger-enabled, export span collection: /opt/redwood/bin/export-spans --window 30m --out telemetry-snapshot/traces.jaeger
- Attachments: hardware outputs: nvidia-smi -q > firmware-and-drivers.txt; dmidecode > firmware-and-drivers.txt (append).

Minimum telemetry retention for certification: 90 days local + offsite transfer instructions included in runbook if customer requests.

Failure modes and rollback criteria

- If more than one of (power fail, network partition, disk failure) causes permanent data loss or unrecoverable runtime state, abort acceptance.
- If performance SLOs fail for p99 by >40% consistently after tuning, classify as FAIL and open a ticket to Eng Platform for remediation with priority P1.
- For security verification failures (image signature mismatch, unexpected privileged processes), stop and revert to verified images.

Safe rollback checklist (if required)

1) Quiesce incoming traffic at local load balancer.
2) Snapshot local KV state (if possible): /opt/redwood/bin/kv-snapshot --out /tmp/kv-snap-<ts>.tar.gz
3) Restore verified image from signed-manifest to node: /opt/redwood/bin/apply-image --manifest signed-manifest.txt
4) Bring up services in dependency order: redwood-agent -> kv-cache-daemon -> redwood-runtime.
5) Re-run smoke tests and attach artefacts.

Sign‑off template (fill in fields, append signatures)

- Deployment id: <deployment-id>
- Customer: <customer-name>
- Site: <site-location>
- Hardware kit id: <kit-id>
- Delivery Engineer: <name> (signature)
- Customer Operator: <name> (signature)
- SRE Reviewer: <name> (signature)
- Acceptance result: PASS | FAIL
- Notes: freeform field for deviations, mitigations, follow-ups.

Common troubleshooting commands and expected artifacts

- Check GPU: nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/gpu.txt (verify driver >= 515.0)
- Runtime logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -o short-precise --since "1 hour" > /tmp/runtime.log
- KV cache status: /opt/redwood/bin/cache-stats --json > /tmp/cache.json
- Heartbeat: curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/redwood.sock http://localhost/health | jq .uptime

Safety and physical site considerations (non‑technical)

- Ensure qualified electrical staff performs power PDU tests.
- Follow local permits and safety rules for on-site battery/UPS maintenance.
- All induced failure tests must have a signed waiver before execution.

Appendix A — Example commands (copyable)

1) Verify manifest: sha256sum -c /opt/redwood/manifests/signed-manifest.txt > /tmp/manifest-verify.out 2>&1
2) Health check: curl --unix-socket /var/run/redwood.sock http://localhost/health | jq . > /tmp/health.json
3) Export metrics: curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep inference_latency > /tmp/inference-metrics.txt
4) Create evidence bundle: tar -czf /tmp/acceptance-bundle-<deployment-id>.tgz signed-manifest.txt /tmp/health.json telemetry-snapshot/* firmware-and-drivers.txt power-fail-recovery.log

Appendix B — Minimum hardware/firmware table (acceptance baseline)

- Minimum GPU driver: 515.0
- Minimum CUDA toolkit: 11.7
- Disk: NVMe >= 1TB per node (mirrored or enterprise grade)
- RAM: >= 256GB per inference node for large models; smaller models may accept 128GB
- BIOS: latest vendor-recommended revision; secure boot optional but recommended
- TPM/KMS recommended for image attestation

References and related runbooks

- Ephemeral boot and attestation (onprem packaging): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/ephemeral-boot-and-attestation-playbook-2026
- Field operational runway and safety windows: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/field-operational-runway-and-safety-windows-2026
- Controlled rollforward & rollback guidance: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/orchestrated-rollforward-and-customer-safeguards-2026

Change history

- 2025-07-10: Created by Priya Natarajan (initial draft).
- 2025-09-02: Added performance sanity thresholds and KV cache guidance (reviewer: Carlos Mendez).
- 2026-02-12: Updated safety test windows and added evidence retention guidance (reviewer: Aisha Rahman).

End of document

payload.page_title: Private deploy acceptance and smoke validation playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the minimum acceptance and smoke validation steps for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, deployment engineers, and customer success engineers who perform the final handoff and post-install verification. The goal is to provide a reproducible, time-boxed validation runbook that ensures the control plane, runtime, networking, security and observability are functioning to minimal SLAs before marking a deployment as ‘accepted’.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to: VPC-based private deployments and fully on-prem packages deployed by Redwood delivery teams or partner integrators.
- Not intended for: deep performance tuning or long-term capacity testing (see separate perf-suite docs).
- Timebox: full acceptance run should be completable in 3–8 hours depending on environment and scale.

Quick summary of gates (acceptance criteria):
1) Control plane API: POST /v1/models/list returns 200 and <= 500ms median response within acceptance window.
2) Runtime health: all runtime agents report healthy and KV cache warm success for at least 3 recent requests.
3) Networking: egress and ingress ACLs allow required ports; inter-pod latency < 2ms in same AZ and < 20ms cross-AZ (target).
4) Observability: telemetry pipeline ingestion within 60s, 99th percentile metric latency < 120s.
5) Security: KMS integration confirmed and test key can be used to encrypt/decrypt a sample token.

Pre-flight checklist (1 hour)
- Confirm inventory: list of hosts, instance types, network CIDRs, control-plane endpoints, cluster IDs.
- Credentials: deployment admin account, KMS access, mock-customer API key created for testing.
- Telemetry: Prometheus endpoint, tracing collector endpoint, log forwarding destination verified.
- Backups: snapshot/backups taken for relevant volumes before running tests.

Minimum hardware & software baseline (table)
(Use this as the initial acceptance baseline; larger deployments require updated baselines in the customer requirements doc.)

| Component | Minimum spec (single AZ small) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane VM | 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM | Control plane services run on this host (API, auth, UI) |
| Runtime worker (per GPU node) | 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 1xA10/RTX6000 or equivalent | Adequate for single-model small-load smoke tests |
| Storage | 200 GB SSD | OS + model artifacts cache |
| Network | 1 Gbps internal | Bandwidth affects throughput testing |

Network and firewall validation (required checks)
- Required ports and protocols:
  - TCP 443 (control plane API ingress)
  - TCP 1443 (agent to control-plane gRPC)
  - UDP/TCP 514/1514 (optional syslog/secure logging)
  - TCP 9090 (Prometheus, metrics read-only)
  - TCP 9411 (Zipkin/Jaeger collector)
- Firewall test procedure (3 steps):
  1. From a customer app host: curl -v https://<control-plane-host>/health should return HTTP 200.
  2. From each runtime host: nc -zv <control-plane-host> 1443 (expect success).
  3. From telemetry host: curl -sS http://<prometheus-host>:9090/-/healthy (expect 'Prometheus is Healthy').

Baseline performance expectations (smoke targets)
- Single-token generation (small model): median latency <= 150 ms, 95th <= 400 ms.
- 512-token generation (larger model): median per-token latency consistent with model profile; goal: first-token within 500 ms on warm cache.
- KV cache hit rate: after warm-up sequence, expect >= 70% prefix cache hit rate for synthetic replay prompts.

Acceptance test sequence (ordered, time-boxed)
1) Control plane health and auth (15–30min)
   - Verify API health:
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" https://<control-plane>/v1/health
     Expected: {"status":"ok","services":["api","auth","db"]} and HTTP 200.
   - Verify auth: create a short-lived token via POST /v1/admin/tokens and perform a sample model list call.

2) Runtime and model load (30–60min)
   - Deploy a canary model variant (small open model recommended).
   - Verify agent registration: on each runtime node run:
     sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
     Expected: active (running) and no crashes in last 5m.
   - Trigger model load via API and validate model-state:
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" -d '{"model":"canary-small","action":"load"}' https://<control-plane>/v1/models/manage
     Expected: 200 and status 'loaded' for all targeted agents.

3) Telemetry and tracing verification (15–30min)
   - Emit a trace via test client that calls model generate endpoint with tracing enabled; confirm trace shows through control-plane -> router -> runtime.
   - Confirm metrics appear in Prometheus within 60s. Use query: up{job=~"redwood.*"} and expect target count == deployed services.

4) Smoke generation test (30–60min)
   - Run the canonical smoke script (example below) from a client host that uses the test API key. Execute 3 phases: cold, warm, and concurrency.
   - Expected results: no 5xx errors, success rate >= 99%, median latency <= smoke targets above.

5) Security integrations (15–30min)
   - KMS: encrypt/decrypt roundtrip using the configured key.
   - Secrets: attempt a test rotation of a short-lived secret and validate runtime picks up rotated secret without restart (if configured).

6) Observability retention and alerts (15min)
   - Trigger a synthetic error and ensure alert rule fires to the configured PagerDuty/Slack channel.
   - Confirm log timestamps and trace IDs correlate across services.

Smoke script examples and CLI snippets
- Minimal smoke curl for generation (small model):

  curl -s -X POST https://<control-plane>/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"canary-small","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}' | jq .

  Expected minimal response: JSON containing "text" and a non-empty "request_id".

- Automated smoke runner (python pseudo):
  # ./scripts/smoke_runner.py --count 200 --concurrency 5 
  # Validations: status==200, latency distribution logged to /tmp/smoke-report.json

Prometheus queries to validate (examples)
- Control plane API availability:
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane",status=~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane"}[5m]))
  -> Expect >= 0.995 during acceptance run.
- Runtime agent health:
  count(up{job="redwood-agent"} == 1) == <expected-agent-count>
- Model load latency (histogram):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_load_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) < 10

Rollback and failure isolation criteria
- Immediate rollback triggers (stop acceptance and roll back to previous stable config):
  - >1% 5xx rate on control plane APIs for 10 consecutive minutes.
  - Any runtime node repeated crash-loop within 5 minutes after model load.
  - KMS failures preventing encryption/decryption for 5 consecutive test calls.
- Partial rollback actions:
  1. Remove canary model from routing and restore previous routing weights.
  2. Drain and restart affected runtime nodes (one at a time).
  3. If control plane is impacted, switch to read-only mode and fail traffic to dedicated fallback region (if configured).

Escalation and ownership
- Primary owner during acceptance: private-deploy delivery engineer (tagged on deployment ticket).
- Engineering on-call: redwood-eng-oncall@redwood.ai (pager duty).
- Security contact for KMS/SEV: security@example-redwood.ai (for encryption and secrets incidents).
- When to escalate to core runtime team: model load latency > 2x baseline and sustained for 15m.

Acceptance sign-off
- Required approvers: Delivery Engineer, SRE Approver, Customer Success Engineer.
- Sign-off checklist items (each must be checked in the ticket):
  - [ ] API health verified
  - [ ] Runtime agents healthy and model loaded
  - [ ] Smoke generation tests passed (attach /tmp/smoke-report.json)
  - [ ] Metrics ingested and alert verified
  - [ ] KMS/Secrets validated
  - [ ] Backups/snapshots confirmed

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands
- Check agent logs:
  journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 500 --no-pager
- Inspect model cache state (on runtime node):
  /opt/redwood/bin/modelctl status --model canary-small --json
- Force a cache warm for a prefix set:
  /opt/redwood/bin/cache-warm --model canary-small --prefix-file /tmp/prefixes.txt

References and related pages
- See private-deploy field compatibility matrix for scaled baselines: /eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-field-compatibility-matrix-2026
- Day2 telemetry and acceptance checklist: /eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026

Document maintenance
- Owner: eng-private-deployments (delivery squad).
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after any major control-plane/runtime release.
- Last full review: 2026-02-10 (document updated to add KMS validation step and Prometheus queries).

payload.page_title: Private Deploy Field Compatibility Matrix and CAT (Customer Acceptance Tests) - 2026

sections.body:
Overview:

This document provides a pragmatic compatibility matrix and a runnable Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) checklist for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem) of Redwood Inference. It aggregates constraints and tested compatibility across: OS/kernel, GPU models and drivers, container runtimes, networking (VPC/NAT/MTU), storage tiers and mount options, KMS/HSM integration, observability agents, and upgrade/rollback constraints. The goal is to give engineering and sales teams a single reference to determine whether a prospective customer environment is supported, requires mitigations, or is unsupported.

When to use this page:
- Pre-sales validation for dedicated/private offers
- Onboarding architecture review with customer infra teams
- Day‑2 operations planning for upgrades/migrations

Compatibility summary (status legend):
- SUPPORTED: Redwood has validated and recommends this configuration for production.
- SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS: Works but with tradeoffs (reduced throughput, feature flags disabled, additional runbook steps).
- UNSUPPORTED: Not recommended; significant engineering effort required.

High-level compatibility matrix (text table):

| Component category | Key items tested | Recommended versions / settings | Status | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Host OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 8.9, Rocky 8.6 | Ubuntu 22.04 preferred; kernel >= 5.15 | SUPPORTED | We test packages on these images. Custom kernels require validation. |
| GPUs | NVIDIA A10, A100 40GB, H100, RTX 6000 | Driver 525+ (A100 use 520/525+, H100 535+), CUDA 11.8+ | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | H100: require runtime build with newer attention kernels; contact Redwood for optimized image. |
| Container runtime | containerd 1.6+, Docker 20.10+ (runtime: runc/CRI) | Use containerd for cluster installation; Docker supported for single-host. | SUPPORTED | We ship OCI images.
| Orchestration | Kubernetes 1.25–1.29 | kubelet flags: --feature-gates=..., runtimeClass enabled | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | Older K8s may need custom admission.
| Networking (VPC) | Private subnet w/ NAT, egress via managed NAT gateway | MTU >= 1500, bandwidth >= 10 Gbps for medium clusters | SUPPORTED | For burst workloads use dedicated egress links. |
| MTU and tunneling | VXLAN/GRE overlay | MTU 1400+ recommended; fragmentation causes latency | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | If MTU < 1400 expect ~10–30% throughput drop. |
| Storage | Local NVMe (>= 1 TB for model cache), NFS backed by EBS/CSI | XFS recommended for NVMe; ext4 ok for experimental | SUPPORTED | NFS: ensure fsync latency < 10ms for prompt-serving. |
| KMS / HSM | AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, BYO-HSM (PKCS#11) | TLS mutual auth, key rotation window: 90d | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | BYO-HSM requires a tested connector (scheduling & failover runbook). |
| TLS | TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3 | Prefer TLS1.3, ciphers: ECDHE+AESGCM | SUPPORTED | Mutual TLS required for some private control-planes. |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus, Grafana | otel-collector v0.60+, prometheus 2.40+ | SUPPORTED | Sampling and PII redaction required for regulated customers. |
| RBAC / IAM | OIDC & SAML SSO | OIDC preferred for short-lived tokens | SUPPORTED | SAML still supported via SSO proxy. |
| Quantized runtimes | int8/4-bit quantization pipelines | Requires runtime flags and validated model artifacts | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | Certain attention kernels revert to slower paths; test with cust prompts. |

Operational thresholds and Day‑2 constraints:

- Minimum telemetry retention for root-cause: 7 days full-span traces, 30 days aggregated metrics.
- Alerting thresholds (recommendation):
  - P95 serving latency > 250ms for 60s => page SRE team
  - Token error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m => trigger rollback plan
  - OOM events > 1/hour per node => scale policy or instance type change

Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) checklist (runnable steps):

1) Environment validation (infra):
   - Confirm OS kernel:
     uname -a
   - Confirm GPU presence and drivers:
     nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv
   - Check available NVMe capacity and latency:
     lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT
     sudo fio --name=nvme-latency --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=4 --time_based --runtime=30

2) Container and networking validation:
   - Validate MTU and path MTU discovery:
     ip link show && ip route get 8.8.8.8
   - Simple network throughput test (iperf3):
     iperf3 -c <server> -P 8 -t 30

3) Model-serving smoke test (single-host):
   - Pull Redwood runtime image and run quick generator test:
     docker run --rm -e RW_API_KEY=test -p 8000:8000 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:stable-2026-01 
     curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-open-compat","prompt":"Say hi"}' | jq

4) Observability and audit trace validation:
   - Confirm metrics exported to Prometheus:
     curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep redwood_runtime
   - Verify trace export to OTLP collector using sample trace generator (curl to /v1/trace/test)

5) KMS integration test:
   - Rotate test key with 1-hour TTL and attempt signing operations via runtime CLI. Confirm logs show key usage and no timeouts.

Upgrade and rollback constraints (practical runbook summary):

- Pre-upgrade gating checks (all must pass):
  1. No active canary > 5% of production traffic for 10m.
  2. All nodes have < 10% CPU pressure and < 70% GPU memory used.
  3. Telemetry ingestion backfill window healthy (no API backlog).

- Online upgrade pattern (recommended for K8s):
  1. Canary deploy new runtime to 1 node / 5% capacity. Run CAT subset of tests for 15 minutes.
  2. If canary OK, gradually increase 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m observation windows.
  3. If token-error-rate increases or latency regressions exceed thresholds, trigger immediate rollback.

- Rollback checklist (if upgrade fails):
  1. Shift traffic to previous model variant via routing policy.
  2. Re-provision previous runtime image on failed nodes and validate model cache warmup.
  3. Run smoke test suite; collect and attach logs and traces to incident ticket.

Known incompatibilities and mitigation strategies:

- Low MTU networks (MTU <= 1400):
  - Effect: Increased fragmentation, higher per-token latency and throughput loss.
  - Mitigation: Enable jumbo frames on overlay or pin runtime to host networking where possible.

- Custom or older CUDA stacks (CUDA < 11.5):
  - Effect: Unsupported kernel paths; quantized runtime will fallback to slower code paths.
  - Mitigation: Upgrade drivers and CUDA where possible; otherwise schedule a performance tuning engagement.

- HSM behind network proxies with aggressive timeouts:
  - Effect: Key operations timeout during bursty workloads.
  - Mitigation: Tune proxy idle/timeouts and add local caching layer for key material with strict TTL.

Acceptance metrics and sign-off:

- Minimum performance sign‑off (example for medium deployment):
  - 95th percentile latency for 1k token prompt: < 600ms
  - Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent small requests (2–8 tokens output) with <10% degradation from baseline
  - Error budget: token error rate < 0.5% in steady-state test window

- Customer sign-off steps:
  1. Run CAT (items 1–5) with Redwood Solutions Engineer present.
  2. Validate upgrade/rollback dry run with simulated traffic.
  3. Approve cutover schedule, maintenance window, and post-cutover monitoring runbook.

Ownership and escalation paths:

sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Optimization Config Audit Events (Safe Apply + Rollback)

sections.body:
This document specifies the audit log event taxonomy for **Optimization Config** lifecycle actions used by Safe Apply + Rollback (batching, caching, and quantization profiles). The goal is to ensure:
- Traceability: who did what, when, and to which scope (tenant/model/region/deployment).
- Non-repudiation and forensic value (request identifiers, actor identity, diff hash).
- Compliance alignment: exportable to customer SIEM, consistent retention, and least-privilege enforcement.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- **Hosted API** and **Dedicated** (Redwood-managed control plane)
- **Private** deployments (operator-managed; same event schema, with deployment-specific differences called out below)
sections.heading: This spec applies to

sections.body:
- **Optimization Config**: a versioned object representing runtime optimization knobs (e.g., batching heuristics, cache toggles, quantization profile selection).
- **Config Version**: immutable version record. Rollbacks always select a previous immutable version.
- **Active Version**: the version currently applied for a given scope.
- **Scope**: the blast radius target for apply/rollback (tenant, model, region; optionally environment and deployment mode).
- **Rollout**: a staged apply operation, potentially including canary % and gating.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Audit events are emitted by the **Optimization Config Service** (control plane) and **Rollout Controller**.
- Events are written to the central Audit Log pipeline with **at-least-once** delivery semantics. Consumers must de-duplicate by `event_id`.
- Ordering is **best-effort** across services; do not assume strict ordering. Use `occurred_at` + `rollout_id` + `request_id` for correlation.
sections.heading: Event delivery guarantees

sections.body:
- Default retention: **400 days searchable** in Redwood systems.
- Export: events are available to enterprise customers via SIEM export connectors (see related page: Audit Log Export Pipeline).
- Extended retention (enterprise add-on): **up to 7 years** in cold storage (export-only; not necessarily searchable in Console).
sections.heading: Redwood-managed (Hosted/Dedicated)

sections.body:
- Default on-box retention for the audit sink is **30 days** (operator-configurable).
- Customers are expected to forward to their SIEM for long-term retention.
- Redwood support may request exports during escalations; customers control access.
sections.heading: Private deployments

sections.body:
- Viewing audit events in the Console requires `audit.events.read`.
- Triggering apply/rollback requires optimization operator permissions (see RBAC bundle); audit logging does **not** grant action permissions.
sections.heading: RBAC

sections.body: All Optimization Config audit events MUST include the required fields below.
sections.heading: Common schema (all events)

sections.body:
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string (UUID) | Unique per event for de-duplication. |
| `event_name` | string | Must match taxonomy below. |
| `event_version` | string | Schema version for the event payload, e.g. `"1.0"`. |
| `occurred_at` | string (RFC3339) | UTC timestamp. |
| `severity` | string | `INFO` \| `WARN` \| `ERROR`. |
| `actor_type` | string | `user` \| `service` \| `system`. |
| `actor_id` | string | User ID or service principal ID. |
| `actor_email` | string | For `user`; empty string for service/system. |
| `actor_display_name` | string | Human-readable name when available. |
| `authn_method` | string | e.g. `sso`, `api_key`, `service_token`. |
| `rbac_roles` | string | Comma-separated roles effective at action time (snapshot). |
| `request_id` | string | Control-plane request ID. |
| `trace_id` | string | Distributed trace correlation ID (if available). |
| `source_ip` | string | Client IP when present; may be empty for internal services. |
| `user_agent` | string | Client UA for Console/API; may be empty for internal services. |
| `org_id` | string | Redwood org/account identifier. |
| `tenant_id` | string | Tenant identifier (may equal org for single-tenant accounts). |
| `deployment_mode` | string | `hosted` \| `dedicated` \| `private`. |
| `environment` | string | `prod` \| `staging` \| `dev` (for private, operator-defined). |
| `scope` | string | Canonical scope string; see Scope encoding below. |
| `optimization_config_id` | string | Stable config object ID. |
| `optimization_config_version_id` | string | Version being referenced by the event (see per-event semantics). |
| `idempotency_key` | string | If provided by client; else empty string. |
| `result` | string | `success` \| `failure` \| `partial` \| `queued`. |
sections.heading: Required fields (MUST)

sections.body:
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | Operator-provided reason or system reason. |
| `change_summary` | string | Short summary for humans; avoid secrets. |
| `diff_hash` | string | Deterministic hash of normalized diff (for integrity). |
| `from_version_id` | string | Prior active version (promotion/rollback/apply). |
| `to_version_id` | string | New target version (promotion/rollback/apply). |
| `model_id` | string | If scoped to model. |
| `region` | string | e.g. `us-east-1`. |
| `cluster_id` | string | Dedicated/private cluster identifier when applicable. |
| `rollout_id` | string | Applies to rollout-related events. |
| `canary_percent` | string | Percent as string to keep schema simple; e.g. `"5"`. |
| `gate_set` | string | Gate set identifier; e.g. `"default-prod"`. |
| `gate_summary` | string | Human-readable summary of gate results (no nested structures). |
| `error_code` | string | Stable internal code; e.g. `"VALIDATION_SCHEMA"`. |
| `error_message` | string | Sanitized message (no secrets). |
sections.heading: Optional fields (SHOULD when available)

sections.body: `scope` MUST be encoded as a stable, parseable string to avoid nested structures:
sections.heading: Scope encoding (canonical string)

sections.body: `tenant={TENANT_ID};model={MODEL_ID|*};region={REGION|*};route={ROUTE|*}`
sections.heading: Format

sections.body:
- Tenant-wide: `tenant=t_123;model=*;region=*;route=*`
- Model in region: `tenant=t_123;model=llama-3-70b;region=us-east-1;route=*`
- Specific route override: `tenant=t_123;model=llama-3-70b;region=us-east-1;route=/v1/chat/completions`
sections.heading: Examples

sections.body: Event names are namespaced under: `optimization_config.*`
sections.heading: Event taxonomy

sections.body:
1) `optimization_config.version.created`
- Emitted when an immutable config version is created.
- `optimization_config_version_id` = newly created version.
- SHOULD include `diff_hash` if created by editing from a base version.

2) `optimization_config.version.validated`
- Emitted when validation is executed (schema + semantic checks).
- `result` may be `success` or `failure`.
- On failure, include `error_code` and sanitized `error_message`.

3) `optimization_config.version.promoted`
- Emitted when a version is promoted to be eligible/visible as “candidate for apply” (promotion semantics defined by control plane policy).
- `from_version_id` may be empty.
- `to_version_id` = promoted version.
sections.heading: Version lifecycle

sections.body:
4) `optimization_config.rollout.started`
- Emitted when safe apply begins for a scope.
- MUST include `rollout_id`, `from_version_id`, `to_version_id`.
- SHOULD include `canary_percent` and `gate_set`.

5) `optimization_config.rollout.gate_evaluated`
- Emitted after each gate evaluation interval (or significant gate decision).
- `result` can be `success` (gate pass), `failure` (gate fail), `partial` (insufficient data), or `queued`.
- MUST include `rollout_id`.
- SHOULD include `gate_summary`.

6) `optimization_config.rollout.paused`
- Emitted when rollout is paused (manual or automatic on gate fail).

7) `optimization_config.rollout.completed`
- Emitted when rollout completes and target version is active for the scope.
- `result` = `success`.

8) `optimization_config.rollout.failed`
- Emitted when rollout fails irrecoverably (e.g., validation regression discovered mid-rollout, controller error).
- `result` = `failure`.
- Include `error_code`/`error_message`.
sections.heading: Apply / rollout

sections.body:
9) `optimization_config.rollback.requested`
- Emitted when a rollback is initiated (Console button/API).
- `from_version_id` = currently active version at time of request.
- `to_version_id` = requested prior version.
- SHOULD include `reason`.

10) `optimization_config.rollback.executed`
- Emitted when rollback is executed and control plane considers the rollback applied (per rollback semantics).
- `result` may be `success` or `partial` (e.g., some shards pending) depending on runtime reporting.

11) `optimization_config.rollback.failed`
- Emitted when rollback cannot be executed.
- Include `error_code`/`error_message`.
sections.heading: Rollback

sections.body:
12) `optimization_config.action.denied`
- Emitted when an actor attempts create/apply/promo/rollback without permissions.
- `result` = `failure`.
- MUST include `error_code` = `RBAC_DENIED`.
sections.heading: Access control / policy enforcement

sections.body:
| Event | Additional required fields |
|---|---|
| `optimization_config.version.created` | `optimization_config_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.version.validated` | `optimization_config_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.version.promoted` | `to_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollout.started` | `rollout_id`, `from_version_id`, `to_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollout.gate_evaluated` | `rollout_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollout.paused` | `rollout_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollout.completed` | `rollout_id`, `to_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollout.failed` | `rollout_id`, `error_code` |
| `optimization_config.rollback.requested` | `from_version_id`, `to_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollback.executed` | `from_version_id`, `to_version_id` |
| `optimization_config.rollback.failed` | `from_version_id`, `to_version_id`, `error_code` |
| `optimization_config.action.denied` | `error_code` |
sections.heading: Minimum additional fields required on top of Common Schema

sections.body:
- Do NOT log prompt contents, model outputs, raw payloads, access tokens, API keys, or private URLs.
- `error_message` must be sanitized; prefer `error_code` for programmatic troubleshooting.
- `change_summary` should describe high-level intent (e.g., “Enable prefix cache for chat routes”) without embedding customer data.
sections.heading: PII / secrets guidance

sections.body:
- Export format is JSON Lines (one JSON object per line) with the fields above.
- Field names are stable and snake_case.
- `rbac_roles` is included as a snapshot to support post-hoc authorization review.
- Customers frequently filter by: `tenant_id`, `deployment_mode`, `scope`, `event_name`, `to_version_id`, and `request_id`.

payload.page_title: Orion Defense  Redwood Private requirement: closed network / offline deployment

sections.body:
h1. Context
Orion Defense is pursuing an on-prem deployment of *Redwood Private* for workloads in a controlled environment. Their terminology is *closed network* and *classified enclave*.

h1. Requirement summary (customer stated)
* Deployment mode: Redwood Private (on-prem Kubernetes).
* Network policy: the cluster must have *no outbound internet routes* (customer phrase: "no outbound" / "closed enclave").
* Software delivery: Redwood must provide an *offline installer bundle* including container images, Helm charts, and a bill of materials (BOM).
* Verification: supply-chain metadata required (image digests, SBOM where available, signature verification process).
* Logging: audit logs must be exportable to customer SIEM without contacting external endpoints.

h1. Notes / clarifications
* Orion does allow internal PKI/OCSP endpoints, but *not* public OCSP/CRL checks.
* Time sync is internal only.
* Outbound access via a corporate proxy is *not* permitted in the enclave.

h1. Risks
* Any implicit dependency on external registries or package repositories will fail.
* Any background job that attempts outbound connectivity will be flagged by Orion security monitoring.

h1. Next steps
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Customer requirements: minimum hardware, network, and security checklist for private deployments

sections.body:
Summary:

This document captures the minimum customer-side requirements and a compact pre-deployment checklist for Redwood Private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It is intended for customer cloud/platform engineers, SREs, and security teams to verify readiness before a Redwood Private installation or Dedicated integration. The guidance is intentionally conservative: meeting these minimums ensures we can achieve baseline SLOs (99.5%% availability for control plane APIs, 95th percentile p99 token latency targets depending on model class) and run standard day-2 operations (monitoring, upgrades, rollback).

Scope:
- Applies to: Redwood Private Control Plane (VPC-hosted or customer-managed) and On‑Prem inference clusters (in customer datacenter or private cloud).
- Excludes: downstream application-specific scaling beyond baseline capacity (see capacity planning notes in Appendix).

Owner and escalation:
- Redwood contact: Solutions Engineer (assigned per engagement).
- Customer owner: Platform/SRE primary and secondary contacts (provide on kickoff).

Minimum hardware requirements (baseline node roles and counts):

Note: these minimums assume a small production deployment supporting ~5–10QPS of medium-length generation (seq len ~1024). For larger workloads request sizing guidance from Redwood Solutions.

| Role | Minimum nodes | CPU | RAM | Disk (type) | Network |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Control plane (K8s master/control-plane) | 3 | 4 vCPU | 16 GB | 100 GB (SSD) | 1 Gbps redundant |
| Inference worker (GPU) | 2 | 16 vCPU | 64 GB | 1 TB NVMe | 25 Gbps recommended |
| Inference worker (CPU-only, small loads) | 2 | 12 vCPU | 48 GB | 500 GB NVMe | 10 Gbps |
| Storage / artifact nodes (model registry, artifacts) | 1–2 | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 2 TB SSD or NFS | 1–10 Gbps |
| Logging / metrics collectors | 2 | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 500 GB SSD | 1 Gbps |

Hardware notes and recommendations:
- GPU supported list (minimum recommended): NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 40GB (preferred: A100 for heavy models). For quantized LLMs on Ampere-class cards A30/A10 acceptable for small-medium models.
- Disk: NVMe preferred for model load latency; spinning disks for cold storage only. Use RAID1/10 or cloud-managed persistent disks with IOPS guarantees.
- CPU flags: ensure host kernel has the latest performance patches and configured with transparent hugepages=never for predictable latency.

Network requirements (VPC and on-prem common checklist):

Mandatory network features:
- Private control plane requires stable IPs or DNS entries for: control-plane-api, model-registry, console, metric-ingest.
- Low-latency fabric between inference workers and artifact storage. Recommended intra-cluster latency <500us; network MTU >= 9000 (jumbo frames) where supported.
- Bandwidth: GPU workers should have >=25Gbps NICs; CPU-only workers >=10Gbps.

Firewall and port rules (customer-managed edge and internal firewalls):
- Required inbound/outbound rules between components (examples):
  - Control Plane API: TCP 8443 (HTTPS) inbound from customer admin CIDR + Redwood ops CIDR (if hybrid).
  - Node-to-node gRPC: TCP 50051–50060 (cluster internal) — open within VPC/subnet only.
  - Metrics/Tracing: TCP 9090 (Prometheus pull) or outbound 4317/4318 (OTLP) to configured collectors.
  - SSH for support: TCP 22 (only via bastion; permit Redwood ephemeral IPs when support is active).

DNS, certificate, and TLS requirements:
- Wildcard or explicit DNS entries for control plane endpoints. DNS TTL <= 300s recommended for failover.
- TLS: mTLS for inter-service traffic is strongly recommended. Control plane and console must present certificates from a customer-managed CA or an allowed public CA.
- Cert rotation plan: provide API for cert refresh (ACME or manual) and document expiry/rotation windows.

Security and compliance checklist:
- Identity and access:
  - RBAC: K8s RBAC enabled for control-plane. Cluster admin accounts limited to platform owners.
  - Service accounts: use bound service accounts and least privilege IAM roles in cloud environments.
- Key management:
  - Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, or HSM) required for encryption of model material and secrets at rest. Provide KMS access policy at least for encryption/decryption.
- Audit logging and retention:
  - Audit logs must be exported to a customer SIEM or cloud logging with retention policy aligned to compliance requirements (default: 90 days).
- Data residency and separation:
  - For regulated customers, provide VPC/subnet isolation for tenant workloads. Ensure no model artifacts or prompt logs cross configured boundaries without explicit consent.

Pre-deployment checklist (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff and contact list: confirm customer SRE, security contact, and RW lead.
2. Inventory and credentials: provide cloud account IDs, VPC/subnet IDs, bastion access, and KMS ARNs.
3. Network validation: customer runs the basic connectivity tests below and provides results.
4. Hardware verification: confirm GPU types, NIC speeds, and disk IOPS numbers (run fio if needed).
5. Certificate and DNS: provide TLS certs (or CSR process) and DNS delegation/records.
6. Security review: share network diagram and IAM policies for assessment.
7. Scheduling: agree on install window and maintenance/upgrade windows.

Connectivity validation commands (examples to run from a customer bastion host):
- DNS: dig +short control-plane.example.internal
- Port test: nc -vz control-plane.example.internal 8443
- Bandwidth test (between worker nodes): iperf3 -c <peer> -P 8 -t 30
- Disk IOPS sample: fio --name=randread --ioengine=libaio --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=4 --runtime=30 --group_reporting

Validation tests (post-install smoke tests):
- API health: curl -k -s https://control-plane.example.internal:8443/healthz should return HTTP 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}.
- Model pull: request a small model install and verify model registry reports state=ready within configured timeout.
- Inference loop: submit a 64-token generation to a lightweight model and verify latency < baseline (see appendix baseline numbers).
- Metrics visibility: Prometheus target list must include all exporter endpoints; no scrape errors older than 5 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (minimum to sign-off):
- All pre-deployment checklist items validated.
- Smoke tests pass in two consecutive runs spaced 30 minutes apart.
- Security and audit logs successfully delivered to customer logging with expected fields (timestamp, principal, action, resource).
- Backup snapshots for artifact storage completed and verified.

Day-2 operations and upgrade guidance (high level):
- Monitoring and alerting:
  - Critical alerts: control-plane unavailable, model-pull failrate >2%% over 10m, GPU OOM events, persistent scrape errors.
  - Suggested SLOs: control-plane p99 API latency < 500ms; model-pull success rate >= 99%%.
- Routine maintenance:
  - OS and driver patching: schedule during agreed maintenance window, cordon and drain worker nodes before driver/OS upgrades.
  - Model updates: treat model updates as application deploys; run canary to 10%% of serving capacity then ramp.
- Upgrade procedure (short checklist):
  1. Announce window to stakeholders and disable auto-scaling for the window.
  2. Snapshot artifact stores and backup etcd (if K8s control plane managed by customer).
  3. Upgrade control-plane services one at a time with health checks between steps (healthz and readiness probes).
  4. Upgrade inference runtime kernel and drivers on a drained node, validate model load, then uncordon.
  5. Run regression smoke tests and monitor for 30–60 minutes.
  6. Rollback immediately if any critical SLO breaches occur or if >5%% request error rate persists for >15 minutes.

Rollback strategy (guiding rules):
- Fast rollback is allowed for control-plane changes or runtime driver patches if smoke tests fail. Use previously tested image tags or snapshots.
- For model rollout regressions, immediately revert routing to previous model variant and scale up previous variant capacity if necessary.
- Keep at least two prior well-known-good control-plane images and model variants available for rollback.

Operational runbook excerpts (what to provide to oncall):
- Incident: Control plane 503s observed across zones — immediate steps:
  1. Check control-plane pods: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide; detect CrashLoopBackOffs.
  2. Inspect control-plane logs: kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --since=10m.
  3. Validate etcd/DB connectivity and disk pressure.
  4. Notify Redwood support and attach kubectl output bundles.

Appendix A — Baseline latency and load numbers (example):
- Small model: p95 response < 80ms, p99 < 200ms on CPU-only worker.
- Medium model: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms on single A10 GPU.
- Model pull: median model pull time (artifact load to worker) < 45s for 2GB model from local NVMe.

Appendix B — Example minimal IAM policy (cloud):
- Provide a yaml snippet with permissions required by the control plane (S3:GetObject, S3:PutObject, kms:Decrypt).

Appendix C — Contact matrix and runbook links:
- Redwood SRE runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/redwood-private-sre-runbook (internal)
- Onsite escalation: provide customer-specific phone and pager contacts in the deployment intake form.

Notes and change history:
- 2024-08-12: Initial draft, A. Patel.
- 2024-11-05: Added GPU guidance and MTU recommendations, L. Chen review.
- 2025-02-07: Hardened security checklist and added rollback thresholds after customer pilot, Marisol Rivera.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This page describes the customer-facing requirements and the operator runbook for performing model quantization and compatibility validation in Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It covers acceptance criteria, staged rollout steps, preflight checks, monitoring thresholds, and explicit rollback triggers. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable process that protects customer SLAs and preserves model quality while enabling cost-efficient quantized execution on heterogeneous GPU/CPU fleets.

Scope

- Applies to model artifact updates that introduce any quantized weight formats (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, or mixed-precision) or kernel ABI changes that affect runtime compatibility.
- Targets Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Hosted/Dedicated customers should reference the hosted quantization guidance instead.
- Intended audience: Field operators, SRE/Platform on-call, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers during handoffs.

Why this matters

- Quantization reduces memory and cost but can alter numeric characteristics and performance. A structured validation prevents regressions in latency, throughput, and output quality.
- Private deployments often contain heterogeneous accelerators (A100, H100, inferred ARM CPUs). Compatibility mismatches occur when kernels or compilation artifacts do not match target microarchitectures.

Acceptance Criteria (customer-facing)

Use the following acceptance thresholds for a quantized model variant to be considered "ready" for staged rollout to production tenants:

1) Quality (functional):
   - Task accuracy / F1 / BLEU / ROUGE: not worse than baseline model by more than 1.5 absolute points for critical prompt set; or relative drop <= 3% if metric is ratio-based.
   - Latent semantic similarity (embedding-based): average cosine similarity to baseline embeddings >= 0.985 on the customer prompt set.

2) Latency and throughput:
   - p95 generation latency at customer sequence length baseline: increase <= 15% compared to baseline run.
   - Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <= 10% under the target batch profile.

3) Resource and thermal behavior:
   - GPU memory usage reduced as expected by quantization profile (documented in the quant-profile YAML).
   - No sustained thermal throttling or preemption events during synthetic burn-in runs.

4) Stability:
   - No hard crashes, CUDA driver errors, or kernel OOMs during a 4-hour burn-in with representative traffic.
   - KV-cache eviction patterns are compatible (see KV cache compatibility checklist).

Preflight checklist (operator)

- Operator ownership: assign a primary operator and a secondary on-call.
- Artifact verification: verify model bundle signature and provenance chain (SHA256 + cosign signature).
- Quantization profile: confirm quantization YAML is present and matches runtime capability matrix.
- Runtime compatibility table: confirm target runtime binaries (libredwood_runtime.so) and kernel variants are present for target hardware.
- Customer telemetry contract: confirm telemetry level required by customer (sampling rate, PII redaction) is enabled.

Minimum test matrix (must pass all items)

| Test case | Description | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Unit smoke | Load model, run a minimal token generation | returns tokens, no errors |
| Synthetic throughput | Run load generator (k6/locust) at target qps | throughput within 10% |
| 4-hour burn-in | Continuous traffic representative of production | no crashes, no OOM |
| Prompt-set regression | Run customer prompt set (50–200 prompts) | quality thresholds met |
| Embedding parity | 1000 sample vectors from customer corpus | cosine >= 0.985 |
| KV-cache survival | Warm cache then run eviction scenarios | no correctness issues |
| Telemetry sanity | Ensure traces, metrics, and logs emitted | sample rate observed |

Staged rollout plan (recommended)

1) Canary (internal): deploy quantized variant into an isolated canary tenant on the same hardware family.
   - Duration: 6–12 hours of synthetic + limited real traffic.
   - Validation: monitor latency p95, error rate, resource metrics.

2) Customer trial: enable quantized variant for 1–3 low-risk customer tenants with automatic fallback to baseline if metrics cross thresholds.
   - Duration: 24–72 hours.
   - Operators should run the prompt-set regression daily and compare results to baseline.

3) Gradual fan-out: increase tenant count by factors of 2 every 24 hours while monitoring.

4) Cutover: after 1 week of steady metrics, allow customer to opt in for full conversion. Maintain a 48-hour manual-backout window.

Operator rollout commands (examples)

- Verify artifact signature:

```
sha256sum model.quantized.tar.gz
cosign verify --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/model-signing model.quantized.tar.gz
```

- Stage to canary runtime:

```
redwoodctl deploy model --bundle model.quantized.tar.gz --profile quant-profile.yaml --target canary-tenant --strategy staged
```

- Activate trial for customer tenant (example):

```
redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-quant --rollout 10%
```

Rollback triggers and automation

Automated rollback should trigger when any of the following are observed for the affected tenant(s) within a 30-minute window unless overridden by a named approver:

- p95 latency > configured SLO + 25% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Error rate increase >= 1 percentage point and absolute error rate > 0.5% (application-level errors).
- Quality regression observed on daily prompt-set exceeding acceptance thresholds.
- Any hard runtime crash (segfault, driver panic, fatal kernel error).

Rollback steps (manual override)

1) Pause new traffic to the quantized variant:
   - redwoodctl rollout pause --model model-v2-quant --tenant tenant-1234
2) Re-route traffic to previous model:
   - redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-baseline --rollout 100%
3) Preserve artifacts and logs: collect model bundle, runtime logs, and kernel traces and attach to incident ticket.
4) If kernel/driver panic suspected, escalate to infra and file a field incident with detailed environment capture (dmesg, nvml logs, kernel oops)

KV cache compatibility notes

- Quantized models may change KV cache layout if activations are stored in lower precision. The runtime includes an on-disk compatibility tag at model bundle root: `kv_cache_compat: v2`. Operators must verify that target runtime supports the tag.
- If tag mismatch is detected, the runtime will refuse to mount existing cache by default; to preserve cold-start behavior, perform a warm-up pass to rebuild KV caches.

Quantization profile example (quant-profile.yaml)

```
model:
  name: model-v2
  variant: int8-quant
quantization:
  algorithm: blockwise-8bit
  per_channel: true
  calibration: dynamic
runtime_requirements:
  - kernel_variant: f16-accel-h100
  - min_compute_capability: 8.0
  - kv_cache_compat: "v2"
perf_expectation:
  p95_latency_pct_increase: 12
  throughput_drop_pct: 7
```

Telemetry & SLOs to monitor

- Metrics (emit at request-token granularity): request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_bytes_total, kernel_errors.count
- Traces: sampling for cold-start request and first 10 tokens; attach model_id and quant_profile label.
- Logs: structured operation logs including artifact_sha, operator_id, tenant_id, node_id.
- Alert thresholds (suggested):
  - latency_p95 > baseline*1.25 -> Sev3 alert to oncall + operator
  - kernel_errors.count > 0 -> Sev2, immediate paging to infra
  - quality_regression.daily > threshold -> owner notification and ops review

Evidence for customer acceptance handoff

- Signed model bundle + checksum file.
- Burn-in run report (CSV) with latency, throughput, memory, and error metrics.
- Prompt-set regression report (diffs and sample outputs).
- Embedding parity report (summary stats and histogram).
- Telemetry contract verification (sampling rate and PII redaction snapshot).

Operator escalation matrix

1) Operator on-call (primary) — troubleshoot and execute rollback if needed.
2) Platform SRE — investigate kernel/driver failures.
3) Solutions Engineer (customer-facing) — coordinate customer communication.
4) Security/Legal (if telemetry/PII exposure suspected)

Postmortem and evidence preservation

- If rollback occurs, create a postmortem within 72 hours including timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigations. Attach: model bundle, runtime logs, kernel traces, alert graphs, and the acceptance test artifacts.

Appendix A — Example prompt-set regression runner (CLI)

```
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
python tools/prompt_regression_runner.py \
  --model-endpoint https://private-runner.local/tenants/tenant-1234/model-v2-quant \
  --prompts prompts/customer-critical-50.json \
  --output reports/quant_regression.csv
```

Appendix B — Common failure modes and mitigations

- Symptom: p95 latency spikes after quantized rollout.
  - Likely causes: suboptimal kernel variant selected, increased serialization overhead, or KV-cache rebuilds.
  - Mitigation: pin alternative kernel_variant in runtime config, increase batching window temporarily, or roll back.

- Symptom: embedding cosine drift below threshold.
  - Likely causes: calibration dataset mismatch or per-channel quantization error.
  - Mitigation: re-run calibration with customer corpus, increase calibration samples, or disable per_channel quantization.

- Symptom: GPU OOMs on some nodes only.
  - Likely causes: driver/kernel mismatch or firmware variation.
  - Mitigation: isolate affected nodes, run driver/firmware validation harness, move tenants off node.

Owners and contacts

- Document owner: Ava Patel (eng-serving-runtime) — ava.patel@redwood.ai
- Primary SRE contact: Miguel Santos — miguel.santos@redwood.ai
- Solutions Engineer lead: Lina Zhou — lina.zhou@redwood.ai

Related reading

- See also on-prem packaging and air-gap artifact delivery, KV cache migration playbooks, and the runtime kernel compatibility matrix.

Change log

- 2026-01-12: Initial draft created by Ava Patel.
- 2026-04-07: Added KV cache compatibility section and automated rollback triggers (reviewers: Miguel Santos).
- 2026-06-10: Finalized acceptance thresholds and appended CLI examples (publish).
