payload.page_title: VPC multitenant failure-domain hardened operator playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook defines operator procedures and hardened configuration recommendations to detect, contain, and recover from VPC-level failure domains in multitenant private deployments. It is intended for Redwood operators, field engineers, and SREs responsible for private VPC and on-prem tenant fleets.

Goals:
- Minimize customer-visible impact when a VPC-level failure (network partition, AZ outage, BGP flaps, service subnet corruption) occurs.
- Provide deterministic detection, containment, and rollback patterns that work across hosted, dedicated, and private control planes.
- Preserve tenant data integrity (KV caches, session state) and avoid cascading model-swap regressions.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: VPC-sited control/data plane failures that affect one or more tenants in a private deployment. Includes cross-VPC routing incidents, NAT/gateway failures, and service-subnet reachability loss.
- Audience: Field operators, on-call SREs, Private Deploy Ops, Customer Engineering. Not intended for pure hardware/BIOS-level recovery (see HW EOL guide).

Key terminology:
- Failure domain: a bounded set of hosts or network paths whose outage causes correlated tenant impact.
- Safemode: an automated degradation policy that reduces non-essential services (batching, telemetry sampling, model rollouts) to protect SLOs.
- KV sticky state: in-memory prefix/KV caches bound to model-serving processes; must be reconciled before cutovers.

High-level failure model and invariants:
1) Fail-stop network partitions (e.g., subnet route removed) should be isolated to a single failure domain; automated traffic steering must avoid spilling load to degraded domains.
2) Model swap/quantization operations must not be in-progress during a domain recovery; operator tooling must detect in-flight swaps.
3) Observable invariants: token latency p50/p95 increases by >2x, KV miss rate rises >15%, and model error/regression alerts trigger are strong indicators of a domain boundary breach.

Pre-deployment hardening checklist (table):
| Area | Required config | Rationale | Owner |
|------|-----------------|-----------|-------|
| VPC routing | BGP session keepalive 10s, bgp-multipath enabled, two transit gateways per region | Reduce single-BGP-session impact | Network team |
| Subnet layout | Service subnets paired across AZs, /26 minimum per service role | Limits blast radius | Infra |
| Control-plane proxies | Dual HA proxies with health-check TTL 5s | Fast failover for control-plane RPCs | Private Deploy Ops |
| KV persistence | Snapshot interval 60s for critical tenants, WAL retention 5x longer than upgrade window | Prevent state loss on eviction | Runtime team |
| Telemetry | Sampling 100% for error traces during incidents, token-level summaries every 30s | Faster triage | Observability team |

Configuration recommendations (concise):
- CIDR and routing: reserve a /20 per tenant-burst-block, implement strict subnet ACLs to prevent cross-tenant lateral movement.
- NAT gateway: deploy at least two NAT endpoints per AZ with dynamic route preference and health-based failover.
- Egress policing: apply tokenizable egress rate limits per tenant to prevent noisy neighbor amplification during repair.
- Control-plane endpoints: use TLS client cert authentication + mTLS between operator tools and control-plane with short-lived cert lifetimes (1h) for operator sessions during emergencies.

Operator guardrails and safemode triggers:
Safemode should be engaged automatically when any two of the following are true for a 3m window:
- p95 latency for text-generation API > 800ms and increased >2x from baseline
- KV cache miss rate > 15% sustained
- Drop in successful model response rate > 5% absolute
When safemode engages, the platform should: reduce batch sizes by 50%, disable non-critical telemetry streams, pin model variants to last-known-good, and refuse new model rollouts.

Incident detection play (quick triage):
1) Alert ingestion: triggers from the VPC router, NAT gateway, or control-plane health-checks alert the on-call.
2) Initial triage (first 5 minutes): confirm scope (single tenant vs. multiple tenants vs. full-VPC) using origin tags and tenant mapping.
3) Containment (10–20 minutes): attach traffic cordon to affected failure domain: remove route advertisement to external regions and route via transit gateway failover.

Step-by-step containment and recovery (operator runbook):
1) Classify incident: network-only | control-plane-only | mixed.
2) If network-only:
  a) Check BGP session state: `show bgp summary` and look for flaps.
  b) If BGP flap identified, increase hold-time to safe value and enable path damping for impacted session.
  c) Rehome NAT for affected subnets to alternate AZ NAT using `ip route` failover recipes.
3) If control-plane-only:
  a) Verify proxy health and restart proxies in degraded order: read-only proxies first, then read-write.
  b) Freeze model rollouts: `redwoodctl rollout freeze --scope=tenant` and confirm no in-flight artifacts.
4) Mixed incidents: escalate immediately to senior network + runtime engineer and run parallel steps above.
5) State reconciliation: rehydrate KV from last snapshot to a staging object store, run KV consistency check (sha256 checksums) and only reattach to live processes after verification.

Upgrade & rollback considerations during/after failures:
- Never perform stateful model swap or quantization during an active failure domain. Maintain an automated gate that checks: error budget consumption < 25% and no safemode engagement for 30m.
- Rollback recipe (if an upgrade caused the failure):
  1) Pin traffic to previous model tag using traffic-weighting: `redwoodctl traffic pin --model previous-tag --weight 100`
  2) Reconcile KV caches by performing a local warm-up run (seed 10% of common prefixes) before unfreezing rollouts.
  3) Run smoke generator across all tenants that saw the upgrade; compare token-level p50/p95 and rejection rates to baseline.

Testing and validation playbook (preproduction & field tests):
- Synthetic tests: run coordinated multi-tenant synthetic traffic with 10–30% tail-load spike to validate eviction windows.
- Chaos tests: scheduled chaos drills that simulate single-subnet route removal, NAT failure, and AZ probe loss. Use a canary tenant to validate rollback flow.
- Onboarding acceptance test (OAT): operator must pass a 3-hour injection window verification where safemode is exercised and recovery completed within RTO objective.

Telemetry and alerting (recommended sets and thresholds):
- Metrics to ingest: p50/p95/p99 latency per tenant, KV miss %, model error ratio, bgp session flaps per minute, NAT failed translations/sec.
- Alerts:
  - P95 latency > 800ms for 3m -> P1 to oncall (pager)
  - BGP session flaps > 5 in 2m -> P1 network paging
  - KV miss rate > 15% for 5m -> oncall slack + runbook link

Post-incident checklist and postmortem structure (within 48 hours):
1) Timeline reconstruction with delta-synchronized logs (include control-plane RPCs, NAT metrics, bgp summaries).
2) Root cause hypothesis and evidence table (logs, packet captures, traceroutes).
3) Mitigations applied, duration, customer impact (minutes, percent of calls failed).
4) Action items with owner and ETA.

Escalation matrix and ownership:
- First-line: Private Deploy Operators (oncall rotation)
- Second-line: Runtime Engineers (model/KV) and Network on-call
- Third-line: SRE Incident Commander + Customer Engineering for high-severity customer impact
- Contact procedures: use incident channel `#inc-private-vpc` and escalate to paging list if P1 after 10m.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets:
- Freeze rollouts:
  ```
  redwoodctl rollout freeze --scope=tenant --tenant-id t-1234 --reason "vpc-failure-engaged"
  ```
- Pin traffic to previous model:
  ```
  redwoodctl traffic pin --tenant t-1234 --model v1.9.2 --weight 100
  ```
- KV snapshot and verification (conceptual):
  ```
  redwoodctl kv snapshot --tenant t-1234 --since "-2m" --out s3://private-artifacts/t-1234/snap-20260621
  redwoodctl kv verify --snapshot s3://private-artifacts/t-1234/snap-20260621 --sha256 <expected>
  ```

Appendix B — Example safemode YAML (operator-editable):
| key | value | description |
|-----|-------|-------------|
| safemode.enabled | true | master enable flag |
| safemode.triggers.latency_p95_ms | 800 | p95 threshold to evaluate |
| safemode.actions.reduce_batch_pct | 50 | how much to reduce batching |
| safemode.actions.freeze_rollout | true | prevents new model rollouts |
Example YAML snippet:
```
safemode:
  enabled: true
  triggers:
    latency_p95_ms: 800
    kv_miss_percent: 15
  actions:
    reduce_batch_pct: 50
    freeze_rollout: true
    telemetry_sampling: 0.1
```
Related references and reading:
- VPC tenant commissioning guide (operator handbook)
- Tenant eviction and safe-state sanitization playbook
- Regional model fallback topology (design doc)

Owner and contact:
- Document owner: Leila Chen (Private Deploy Ops) 
- Operational owner: Private Deploy SREs (oncall)

Revision history:
- 2026-02-15: created (Leila Chen)
- 2026-04-02: added safemode action set and triggers (Marco Alvarez)
- 2026-06-21: clarified KV snapshot verification and added rollback recipe (Priya Natarajan)

payload.page_title: Runtime cost / SLO balancing and eviction policy playbook

sections.body:
SUMMARY
This playbook defines an operator-facing, testable procedure for balancing runtime cost controls against latency and availability SLOs in private VPC/on‑prem deployments. It prescribes an eviction policy taxonomy, decision thresholds, telemetry contracts, and runbook steps for safe enforcement and rollback. It focuses on tenant-facing inference services (runtime-proxy, gpu-scheduler, kv-cache) and is intended for field operators, SREs, and operator automation engineers.

Why this exists
- Private deployments often run heterogeneous workloads with conflicting economics: some tenants require low p95 latency, others tolerate higher latency but need high throughput.
- When capacity or thermal constraints occur, automated eviction/throttling mitigations protect critical SLOs but must avoid unnecessary cost overruns and customer impact.
- This playbook provides a deterministic policy set operators can deploy and a validation checklist for upgrades.

Scope
- Applies to: VPC / on‑prem Redwood Private environments, dedicated GPU clusters managed by runtime-controller and tenant-quota-service.
- Not covered: model artifact build pipelines, long-term billing reconciliation (finance maintains separate docs).

Goals
1) Protect critical latency SLOs (p95 <= configured target) for priority tenants while containing GPU spend growth.
2) Provide predictable, auditable eviction decisions with forensic telemetry.
3) Ensure safe rollback and customer notification paths.

Key concepts and terminology
- Priority class: tenant priority label (critical | standard | best-effort). Set by customer contract via onboarding.
- Eviction window: short timeframe (usually 60–300s) where tenant tokens / requests are preferentially throttled or rejected.
- Graceful degradation: service-level fallback (quantized model, lower beam, reduced response length).
- Burst absorber: a local admission controller that uses token-bucket + predictive de‑queueing to smooth spikes.

SLO / cost mapping matrix (example)
| Priority | Target p95 latency | Allowed throughput loss | Preemptible GPU use | Billing tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| critical | <= 120ms | 0% | no | SLA: gold |
| standard | <= 250ms | up to 10% | yes (if warm) | SLA: silver |
| best-effort | <= 500ms | up to 30% | yes (immediate) | SLA: bronze |

Eviction policy taxonomy
1. Soft throttling (request-level): reduce admission via burst absorber. Preferred initial step.
2. Graceful fallback (model-level): switch to a quantized or truncated variant with known cost profile.
3. Tenant-level preemption: move non-critical tenant workloads to preemptible nodes / spot capacity.
4. Eviction (hard): terminate or deny new requests until load reduces. Use with explicit operator approval for critical tenants.

Decision thresholds (recommended starting point)
- Node GPU utilization sustained > 88% for 3 minutes -> trigger soft throttling for best-effort tenants.
- p95 latency for priority class critical exceeds target by >20% for 90s -> escalate to graceful fallback for non-critical replicas; notify oncall.
- Control-plane queue depth > 10k and mean request wait > 250ms -> enable tenant-level preemption policies.
- Thermal throttling (hardware telemetry) detected on > 1/3 of nodes in a zone -> immediate admission control and operator alert.

Telemetry and observability contract (what must be emitted)
- Per-tenant: p50/p95/p99, request rate, rejection rate, average token cost, model variant in use, priority_class label. Emit at 10s resolution.
- Per-node: GPU util, memory pressure, temperature, power draw, active model slots, last eviction timestamp. Emit at 5s resolution for critical nodes.
- Control-plane: admission decisions (reason code), last policy evaluation, operator override flag.
- Audit logs: immutable entries for any hard eviction or tenant preemption including timestamp, initiator (auto/operator), justification, and trace id.

Operator runbook: handling an ongoing capacity/latency incident
1) Triage (0–3 minutes)
   a) Confirm alert: check runtime-dashboard, per-tenant p95, node GPU util.
   b) Identify impacted priority classes (query: tenant-quota-service /api/v1/tenants?priority=true).
2) Apply safe mitigations (3–10 minutes)
   a) Enable soft throttling via: curl -X POST "https://control-plane.local/api/adm/burst-absorber" -d '{"action":"enable","scope":"best-effort"}'
   b) Flip graceful fallback flag for target tenants:
      - CLI: rctl tenant set-variant --tenant-id TID --variant quantized-small --timeout 10m
   c) Monitor p95 over 30s windows. If p95 improves, continue observation.
3) Escalate to preemption (10–30 minutes)
   a) If sustained GPU util > 90% and latencies remain degraded, enact tenant preemptions using the preemption API with a dry-run first:
      - rctl preempt --target-class best-effort --dry-run=true
   b) Notify stakeholders (email + slack #ops) with template: "Preemption dry-run performed at TIMESTAMP for class best-effort. See trace TR-XXXX."
4) Hard eviction and customer communication (30+ minutes)
   a) Only with operator approval and when other mitigations failed. Record justification and runbook checklist in incident ticket.
   b) Execute: rctl eviction start --tenant-id TID --reason "capacity-critical" --expected-duration 15m
   c) Generate audit package and notify customer success to issue escalation communication.

Post-incident forensics and cost reconciliation
- Produce an incident report with: timeline, policy decisions, telemetry extracts (per-tenant, per-node), and cost delta for the interval.
- For each hard eviction, attach: operator approval snapshot, preemption dry-run results, and the rollback sequence used.

Safety nets and rollback patterns
- Operator override: any automated eviction can be paused with the operator-override flag (control-plane API). Overrides must be time-limited (max 1h) and logged.
- Canary: test eviction policy in a canary namespace for 24h with synthetic load before wide rollout. Use tenant-sim harness (see testing).
- Automatic revert: if p95 for priority-critical increases by > 15% post-policy change, automatic rollback to last policy config after 60s.

Testing and validation checklist (pre-deploy)
1) Unit tests for policy evaluation logic (simulate load patterns).
2) Integration tests: end-to-end with runtime-proxy, gpu-scheduler, and tenant-quota-service using staged models.
3) Chaos tests: simulate node loss, thermal events, and control-plane network partition. Verify correct admission and audit logs.
4) Cost simulation: run a 6h synthetic workload to model GPU-hour impact of policy choices.

Example policy config (YAML)
policy_name: balanced-2026
description: "Default policy for mixed-priority clusters"
priority_classes:
  - name: critical
    p95_target_ms: 120
    preempt_allowed: false
  - name: standard
    p95_target_ms: 250
    preempt_allowed: true
  - name: best-effort
    p95_target_ms: 500
    preempt_allowed: true
admission_controls:
  burst_absorber:
    enabled: true
    token_rate: 1000
    burst_size: 2000
eviction_rules:
  - trigger: node_gpu_utilization
    threshold: 88
    sustained_seconds: 180

Operator CLI quick reference
- Check per-tenant latency: rctl metrics tenant p95 --tenant TID --window 1m
- Toggle soft throttling: rctl admission set --burst-absorber {enable|disable} --scope {best-effort|standard|all}
- Start preempt dry-run: rctl preempt --target-class best-effort --dry-run

Rollout and change process
1) Draft policy PR in config-repo. Include test plan and cost simulation output.
2) Create canary namespace in staging; run 24h synthetic load (synth-tool run --policy balanced-2026 --namespace canary).
3) After successful canary, schedule progressive rollout to one cluster at a time during low-business-hours.
4) Post-rollout: collect telemetry for 72h and sign off if stable.

Ownership and escalation
- Policy owner: runtime-ops (oncall: runtime-ops@redwood.example.com)
- SRE escalation: eng-sre oncall if incident impacts multiple clusters or region.
- Customer communication: customer-success pager and account lead for any tenant-facing hard eviction.

Templates
- Customer notification (short): "We applied temporary capacity measures that may have affected non-critical requests; your SLA for critical requests remains intact. Contact cust-success@redwood.example.com with ticket ID."
- Incident recording checklist: incident_id, start_time, policy_version, affected_tenants, mitigation_steps, approval_signatures.

Appendix: example telemetry query (Influx/PromQL style)
- p95 per tenant: max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[1m])) by (le, tenant))[5m:1m])
- node GPU util: avg(node_gpu_utilization{zone=~"us-*"}) by (node)

References and related docs
- Onboarding contract fields that define priority_class (see customer-requirements-library).
- Runtime admission control API spec (internal link).

FAQ
Q: Can we evict critical tenants?
A: Only with explicit operator approval and documented justification. In most cases we prefer graceful fallback or preemption to spot instances.

Q: How do cost savings measure against customer impact?
A: All policy changes require a cost delta simulation; production change must include SLA impact analysis.

CONTACTS
- Policy author: Priya Raman (priya.r@redwood.example.com)
- Reviewers: Carlos Mendes, Alison Wu

CHANGE LOG
- 2026-01-15 Created initial draft.
- 2026-03-22 Added thermal and telemetry requirements.
- 2026-06-03 Finalized thresholds and operator CLI commands.

payload.page_title: Customer data migration and acceptance playbook for private deployments

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end process, runbook steps, verification checks, and rollback strategies for migrating customer data (model artifacts, KV caches, tenant metadata, and telemetry pointers) into Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is written for field engineers, customer success leads, and SREs involved in a migration engagement.

Scope
- Applies to private deployments delivered by Redwood (VPC-hosted private control plane and fully on-prem bundles).
- Covers: data export from source environment, transfer packaging, validation, staged import, acceptance testing, and coordinated rollback.
- Excludes: deep schema changes to customer application databases (coordinate separately with customer DB team).

Owners and stakeholders
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Ava Martinez)
- Primary implementers: Field Ops / Deployment Engineers
- SRE support: Platform Oncall for migration window (pager)
- Security reviewer: Security & Compliance (must approve transport plan if customer data classified sensitive)
- Customer primary: named contact in onboarding ticket

Pre-migration checklist (must be green before any data movement)
1) Acceptance window scheduled and approved by customer and Redwood PM.
2) Signed data transfer agreement if data classification is PII/sensitive.
3) Snapshot retention policy agreed (number of backups, retention TTL).
4) Capacity reservation: GPU/CPU, storage, egress bandwidth verified.
5) Key rotation/crypto plan approved for transit (TLS + signed manifests).
6) Test tenant created in target environment and smoke-tested.
7) Monitoring & tracing hooks instrumented in target (request/response latency, KV miss/hit, token accounting).

High-level migration phases
1. Plan & dry-run
2. Export & package
3. Transfer & verify integrity
4. Staged import to test tenant
5. Functional verification & acceptance tests
6. Cutover to production tenant
7. Post-migration monitoring and cleanup

Detailed runbook steps
Phase 1 — Plan & dry-run (owner: Customer Success + Field Ops)\- Confirm data components to migrate: model files (weights), tokenizer and vocab, KV cache snapshots, tenant metadata (routing rules, quotas), eval/quality baselines, telemetry pointers.\- Produce a Migration Plan doc: file inventory, expected sizes, checksums, transfer windows, and rollback points.\- Perform a dry-run with a 10% subset of data into a test tenant. Capture timings and failure modes.

Phase 2 — Export & package (owner: Customer Success / Customer IT)\- Recommended export format: gzipped tarball with a signed manifest.json that includes sha256 checksums and schema version. Example manifest entry:
  {
    "path": "models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt",
    "sha256": "<hex>",
    "size_bytes": "123456789",
    "type": "model"
  }
- For KV caches: produce both a flat snapshot and an incremental WAL if supported. Label snapshot with sequence ID.
- Encryption: use customer-provided KMS envelope encryption or PKCS7 with our field tooling. Transport keys are rotated per migration.

Phase 3 — Transfer & verify integrity (owner: Field Ops)\- Transfer options (choose based on environment):
  - Secure SFTP (for on-prem to Redwood VPC) with IP allowlist
  - HTTPS multipart upload to pre-signed target bucket (for VPC-hosted private control plane)
  - Physical shipment for extremely large datasets (follow hardware courier runbook)
- Verification steps: validate manifest signatures, verify sha256 for each file. Any mismatch: quarantined and re-requested from source.

Phase 4 — Staged import to test tenant (owner: Field Ops + Runtime Team)\- Import order (strict):
  1) Tenant metadata and routing rules (so services know where to route requests)
  2) Model artifacts (weights + tokenizer) — register model in model-catalog with provisional version tag
  3) KV cache snapshots — load as read-only first, warm-up using background rehydrate jobs
  4) Eval baseline and quality checks (register prompt sets and expected metrics)\- Runtime flags to use during staged import:
  - --model-register-mode=provisional
  - --kv-load-mode=readonly
  - --rehydrate-workers=4
  - --disable-autoscaler=true

Phase 5 — Functional verification & acceptance tests (owner: Customer Success + QA)
- Test categories and example checks:
  - Connectivity: ping endpoints, validate TLS cert chain.
  - Authentication: token exchange flow for customer's IAM integration.
  - Model correctness: canonical prompt set (20–50 items) should return matching outputs within quality tolerance thresholds.
  - Latency & throughput: 95th percentile latency must be within agreed SLO delta vs baseline (table below).
  - KV cache hit rate: expected warm hit rate > 60% within 2 hours of warm-up.
  - Billing / metering: per-token accounting sanity check against simulated traffic.

Acceptance criteria table
| Signal | Requirement | Measurement window | Action if fail |
|--------|-------------|--------------------|----------------|
|Model functional pass rate| >= 95% on canonical prompts| 1 hour | Fail and rollback to last stable model|
|95p latency delta| +<20% vs baseline| 1 hour | Investigate autoscaler and routing|
|KV cache warm hit rate| >= 60% within 2 hours| 2 hours | Trigger background rehydrate, extend warm window|
|Telemetry completeness| >99% traces & metrics ingested| 30 minutes| Re-check ingestion pipeline and backfill missing spans|
|Metering reconciliation| <1% token accounting drift| 24 hours| Start billing investigation and hold invoices|

Phase 6 — Cutover to production tenant (owner: Field Ops + SRE)\- Pre-cutover checklist: all acceptance tests green; snapshot of test and pre-production manifests archived; rollback snapshot taken and hash-signed.\- Cutover method options:
  1) DNS switch / routing table update to point traffic at new tenant (preferred for VPC control plane)
  2) Blue/Green tenant swap using the platform’s tenant-routing feature
  3) Gradual traffic ramp using percentage-based routing (canary)
- Cutover steps (canary example):
  1) Route 1% traffic for 10 minutes. Monitor critical signals (errors, latency, model outputs).
  2) If green, increase to 10% for 20 minutes.
  3) Continue 25% -> 50% -> 100% with at least two monitoring windows per step.
- Post-cutover: mark provisional model versions as active and update model-catalog and billing tags.

Phase 7 — Post-migration monitoring and cleanup (owner: SRE + Customer Success)\- Minimum 72-hour elevated monitoring with daily sync calls.\- Run sanity reconciliation jobs: metric comparison, token billing reconciliation, config drift checks.
- Clean up provisional artifacts after 30 days if no issues (automatically archive).

Rollback strategies and safe abort points
- Abort during transfer: stop imports and request re-transfer; no state change in target.
- Abort after staged import but before cutover: mark import as quarantined and keep imports read-only; restore previous routing.
- Abort during canary: immediately shift traffic back to previous tenant and mark the incident for postmortem.
- Full rollback: use the pre-cutover snapshot manifest to restore model catalog and KV snapshots. Restoration checklist:
  - Verify restoration manifest checksums.
  - Re-enable autoscaler and health checks.
  - Communicate with customer and open a rollback RCA ticket.

Operational tooling and commands (examples)
- Verify manifest sha256:
  cat manifest.json | jq -c '.files[]' | while read f; do sha256sum "$(echo $f | jq -r .path)" | grep "$(echo $f | jq -r .sha256)" || echo "mismatch:$f"; done
- Import model (field CLI):
  redwoodctl model import --tenant $TENANT --path models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt --tag provisional-2026-03-15
- Load KV snapshot as readonly:
  redwoodctl kv load --tenant $TENANT --snapshot kv-20260315.tar.gz --mode readonly

Telemetry & observable signals to watch (real-time)
- Request error rate (5xx and internal errors)
- Model output regression signals (semantic drift detector events)
- KV cache miss ratio and rehydrate job backlog
- Autoscaler activity and container restart rate
- Token accounting deltas between gateway and billing service
- Ingestion lag for traces/metrics (should be < 60s for critical spans)

Security and compliance considerations
- Ensure all transfer endpoints are in allowlists and logs retained per retention policy.
- For regulated customers, ensure audit events are exported to customer SIEM (via syslog or secure forwarder).
- If migration includes customer secrets, use HSM-backed envelope keys; log key usage to audit trail.

Rollforward and incremental migration pattern (when dataset too large)
- Use incremental WAL + snapshot approach: seed with a full snapshot, then apply ordered WAL batches until cutover window.
- Validate ordering invariants by sequence numbers in manifests and ensure idempotency by consumer.

Common failure modes and remediation (quick reference)
- Mismatch checksums: re-run export, verify source FS integrity.
- Slow rehydrate: increase rehydrate-workers, or temporarily route low-latency traffic to model variant without cache dependency.
- Hidden model regressions: run a wider evaluation prompt set and if failures exceed threshold, rollback model and start postmortem.

Communication plan
- Pre-migration: share schedule and expected customer impact with all stakeholders 72 hours in advance.
- During migration: hourly updates to customer during critical windows; immediate alert on any failed acceptance gate.
- Post migration: 72-hour handoff call, weekly summary for first 30 days.

Appendices
A) Minimal technical artifact checklist (table)\| Artifact | Required | Example path | Notes |
| Model weights | yes | models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt | Prefer quantized artifacts if customer uses reduced footprint |
| Tokenizer | yes | models/llama-v2-7b/tokenizer.json | Must match model hash |
| KV snapshot | conditional | kv-snapshots/tenant-20260315.tar.gz | Include WAL batches if >0 |
| Manifest | yes | manifest.json | Signed and sha256-verified |

B) Escalation matrix
- Field Ops lead -> SRE oncall -> Platform Engineering -> Head of Customer Success -> Security (if sensitive data)

C) Related runbooks and reference pages
- Post-installation telemetry and acceptance checklist (see related pages)
- Incremental stateful upgrade strategy

Document change log
- 2026-03-15: created (Ava Martinez)
- 2026-04-02: added WAL incremental guidance (Priya Rao)
- 2026-05-02: tightened acceptance thresholds and added telemetry signals (Diego Huang)
