payload.page_title: Runbook: Redwood Private Control Plane Restore

sections.body: This runbook describes how to restore the **Redwood Private control plane** from a previously created backup artifact.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Restore prerequisites (cluster, tooling, access, keys)
- Restore modes (in-place vs. new cluster)
- Bootstrap order and dependency sequencing
- Validation (functional + data integrity)
- Abort/rollback criteria
- How to confirm **tenant configuration** and **routing policies** are restored correctly
sections.heading: It covers

sections.body:
- Redwood SRE / Private Deployments teams running DR drills or assisting customers
- Customer platform teams operating a supported Redwood Private deployment

---
sections.heading: This runbook is intended for

sections.body:
- Restoring Redwood control-plane state captured by the Redwood backup toolkit (configuration database, control-plane object/state, release metadata, policy/config state)
- Restoring Kubernetes objects that are part of the Redwood control plane where the toolkit includes them (via manifests/Helm values, as applicable)
- Post-restore validation for:
  - Tenant inventory and tenant-level configuration
  - Routing policies (model pins, fallback rules, regional/capacity policies)
  - Control-plane API readiness for normal operations
sections.heading: In scope (this runbook)

sections.body:
- Kubernetes cluster disaster recovery via **etcd snapshot restore** (see: `eng-infra/runbooks/restore-k8s-cluster-from-etcd-snapshot`)
- Data-plane customer application recovery (data plane is designed to be redeployable; see: `runbook-data-plane-state-backup`)
- Restoring external dependencies not managed by Redwood (e.g., customer-managed DNS provider, external IdP settings) except as validation checkpoints

---
sections.heading: Explicitly out of scope

sections.body:
**Primary on-call / escalation:**
- SRE lead: Sean Gallagher
- Control plane engineering: Ethan Park
- Security review (keys/encryption): Marcus Lin / Hanae Suzuki
- Release/packaging (air-gapped bundles): Connor O'Brien

**Customer-facing execution (when applicable):**
- Solutions lead: Markus Klein

---
sections.heading: Roles and ownership

sections.body:
- Backup **manifest** (JSON) that includes:
  - backup_format_version
  - platform_version
  - timestamp
  - artifact checksums
  - encrypted payload metadata (cipher, envelope/KMS info)
- Backup **payload** (encrypted tarball or equivalent)
- Access to the **backup storage backend** (S3/NFS/GCS or offline bundle)

If you cannot validate checksums/signatures *before* restore, stop and escalate.
sections.heading: You must have

sections.body:
- **VPC / cloud**: IAM role/credentials to read backup bucket and use KMS key (Decrypt)
- **On-prem / air-gapped**: local artifact access + signature verification keys/materials

Security requirement: backups must remain encrypted end-to-end; do not manually decrypt to disk unless explicitly required by a documented break-glass procedure.
sections.heading: Depending on environment

sections.body:
**A. Restore into a clean cluster (recommended for DR drills and most incidents)**
- New Kubernetes cluster is provisioned and reachable
- The correct Redwood Private version is available (installer + charts) and matches compatibility policy

**B. In-place restore (only when explicitly approved)**
- The existing cluster is stable enough to run restore tooling
- You have confirmed what will be overwritten and have a rollback plan
sections.heading: Choose one restore mode

sections.body:
- The restore workflow enforces compatibility checks between the backup format and the target platform version.
- If the installer reports a format/version mismatch:
  - Do not bypass by hand-editing the manifest.
  - Escalate to Control Plane Engineering (format migration may be required).

---
sections.heading: 4) Versions are compatible

sections.body:
- Restores are **destructive** to control-plane state. Treat restore as a change with the same rigor as a production deployment.
- Always restore into a clean namespace/cluster when possible.
- Avoid mixing partial data sources (e.g., restoring DB from backup but leaving old policy config CRs in place).
- If you suspect cluster-level corruption, do not proceed with application-level restore until infra confirms cluster integrity.

---
sections.heading: Safety / risk notes

sections.body:
- Environment name:
- Restore mode: (clean cluster / in-place)
- Backup ID / timestamp:
- Backup storage backend (S3/NFS/offline bundle):
- Manifest path:
- Payload path:
- Target Redwood Private version:
- KMS key ID (if applicable):
- Target cluster context (kubectl context name):
- DNS plan (same hostname vs. temporary hostname):

---
sections.heading: Record these in the incident/DR ticket before starting

sections.body:
Follow this order to avoid common failure modes (including missing CRDs and webhook ordering issues):

1. **Pre-flight checks** (cluster connectivity, storage access, key access, version compatibility)
2. **Install/verify CRDs and core control-plane scaffolding** (no restore yet)
3. **Restore control-plane datastores and state** using the installer restore workflow
4. **Bring up control-plane services** (API, controllers) in a controlled manner
5. **Post-restore reconciliation** (controllers reconcile desired state)
6. **Validation** (health, tenant configs, routing policies, smoke checks)
7. **Cutover** (DNS/TLS, routing) if restoring into a new cluster

---
sections.heading: High-level restore sequence (bootstrap order)

sections.body:
- Announce in the relevant channel and update the incident timeline.
- Freeze changes:
  - Pause automated rollouts
  - Disable scheduled backups temporarily (avoid confusing signals)
  - Confirm no ongoing upgrades

---
sections.heading: If this is production or a customer-assisted restore

sections.body:
- `kubectl config current-context`
- `kubectl get nodes`
- `kubectl get ns`
sections.heading: Run

sections.body:
- API server is unstable (timeouts)
- Nodes are NotReady and not actively being repaired
sections.heading: Abort if

sections.body:
Expected namespaces vary by install, but typically include:
- `redwood-system` (or customer-specific equivalent)
- `redwood-observability` (if observability pack installed)

If restoring into a clean cluster, namespaces may not exist yet. That is OK.
sections.heading: 1.2 Confirm required namespaces and baseline components

sections.body:
- Verify manifest checksums match payload.
- If using an offline bundle, verify signature and checksum manifest per packaging doc.

Typical commands (examples; adjust to your environment and tooling):
- `redwood-private backup verify --manifest ./backup-manifest.json --artifact ./backup.enc.tar`

If verification fails, **stop** and obtain a known-good backup.
sections.heading: 1.3 Validate backup artifact integrity (required)

sections.body:
For KMS envelope encryption, ensure the restore identity can call Decrypt on the key.
- Cloud: confirm IAM policy includes `kms:Decrypt` for the key and the bucket read permissions.
- On-prem HSM: confirm client configuration and key slot availability.
sections.heading: 1.4 Validate key access (KMS/HSM)

sections.body:
- KMS is unavailable and you do not have an approved break-glass plan.

---
sections.heading: Abort if

sections.body: This step prevents a common on-prem failure mode where the restore re-applies custom resources before their CRDs exist.
sections.heading: Step 2 — Install CRDs and baseline chart scaffolding (do not restore yet)

sections.body: Install the CRDs for the target Redwood version. Use the supported installation path (Helm/installer).
sections.heading: 2.1 Install Redwood control-plane CRDs

sections.body:
- `helm repo update`
- `helm upgrade --install redwood-crds redwood/redwood-crds -n redwood-system --create-namespace --version <TARGET_VERSION>`
sections.heading: Example (Helm-based installs)

sections.body: - `kubectl get crds | grep -i redwood`
sections.heading: Validate CRDs exist

sections.body: - CRDs fail to install or are an unexpected version.
sections.heading: Abort if

sections.body: Install charts/components required to run restore jobs/hooks (RBAC, service accounts, configmaps, job templates).
sections.heading: 2.2 Install minimal control-plane chart prerequisites

sections.body: - `helm upgrade --install redwood-control-plane redwood/redwood-control-plane -n redwood-system --version <TARGET_VERSION> -f values.yaml --set restore.enabled=true`
sections.heading: Example

sections.body:
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get sa,role,rolebinding`
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get jobs`

---
sections.heading: Validate

sections.body: Use the supported installer restore command. Do not hand-apply objects unless explicitly instructed by engineering.
sections.heading: Step 3 — Execute restore workflow

sections.body:
If supported by the installer version, generate a restore plan:
- `redwood-private restore plan --manifest <PATH> --target-cluster <CONTEXT>`
sections.heading: 3.1 Dry-run / plan (recommended)

sections.body:
- Which components will be overwritten
- Any required manual steps (e.g., external DNS)
sections.heading: Review for

sections.body:
Typical command shape (examples; flags vary by version):
- `redwood-private restore apply --manifest <PATH_TO_MANIFEST> --artifact <PATH_OR_URI_TO_ARTIFACT> --namespace redwood-system`
sections.heading: 3.2 Run restore

sections.body: - `redwood-private restore apply --manifest s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/manifest.json --artifact s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/payload.enc.tar --kms-key <key-arn> --namespace redwood-system`
sections.heading: For S3-backed artifacts

sections.body: - `redwood-private restore apply --manifest ./manifest.json --artifact ./payload.enc.tar --offline --namespace redwood-system`
sections.heading: For air-gapped restores

sections.body:
- Fetches artifact(s) from storage
- Validates checksums
- Decrypts payload in-memory / ephemeral workspace
- Restores control-plane datastore snapshot(s)
- Rehydrates platform configuration state (including tenant config and routing policy objects)
- Emits a restore report (store it in the ticket)
sections.heading: What this step does (conceptually)

sections.body:
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -w`
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get jobs`
- `kubectl -n redwood-system logs job/<restore-job-name> --tail=200`
sections.heading: Watch jobs/pods

sections.body:
- Decryption failures that indicate wrong key or tampered artifacts
- Persistent RBAC permission errors (fix RBAC, then re-run from a clean state)
- Database restore fails with data corruption errors

---
sections.heading: Abort criteria (immediate)

sections.body:
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get deploy`
- `kubectl -n redwood-system rollout status deploy/<name>`
sections.heading: 4.1 Confirm control-plane deployments are healthy

sections.body:
- `kubectl -n redwood-system get pods | egrep -i "controller|webhook|api"`

If controllers are crashlooping, check:
- Missing secrets references (expected if secrets are references-only; see validation)
- Misconfigured external endpoints (IdP, KMS, object storage)

---
sections.heading: 4.2 Confirm webhooks/controllers are running

sections.body: Record results in the restore report / incident ticket.
sections.heading: Validation checklist (required)

sections.body:
1. Kubernetes health:
   - No CrashLoopBackOff in `redwood-system`
   - Core services Ready
2. Control-plane API health:
   - `curl -k https://<control-plane-endpoint>/healthz` returns OK (or equivalent)
3. Backup status endpoint (if enabled):
   - Confirm the platform reports the restored last-known backup metadata as expected (do not treat this as proof of restore correctness; it is an indicator).
sections.heading: A) Basic health and readiness

sections.body:
- Confirm schema migrations did not run unexpectedly (compare platform version from manifest to running version)
- Confirm expected counts of key entities (tenants, routes, policies) are non-zero and plausible
sections.heading: Perform the supported read-only checks

sections.body: Goal: ensure tenant inventory and tenant-level settings (authz, quotas, pinned models, rate limits, routing configuration) match the pre-incident state.
sections.heading: C) Tenant configuration verification (must-pass)

sections.body: - `redwood-private admin tenants list`
sections.heading: Using the supported admin tooling/API (examples)

sections.body:
- Tenant count matches expectations
- Critical tenants present (top customers / internal tenants)
sections.heading: Validate

sections.body:
For 3–5 representative tenants (including at least one “most complex” tenant):
- `redwood-private admin tenants get --tenant <TENANT_ID>`
sections.heading: C.2 Spot-check tenant configuration

sections.body:
- Correct tenant status (enabled/disabled)
- Correct quota / rate limit values
- Correct auth settings (OIDC issuer URL, audience, required claims) where applicable
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body: Backups should not embed raw secret material unless explicitly configured; most environments store **references**.
sections.heading: C.3 Confirm secrets handling is correct

sections.body:
- Secret references resolve (KMS/HSM reachable; external secret manager reachable)
- No unexpected plaintext secrets exist in restored objects
sections.heading: Validate

sections.body:
- Do not proceed to cutover.
- Fix external secret integration first.
sections.heading: If secret references fail to resolve

sections.body: Routing policies are a primary restore correctness signal because they directly affect inference behavior.
sections.heading: D) Routing policies verification (must-pass)

sections.body:
- `redwood-private admin routing policies list`
- Or via API: `GET /admin/routing/policies`
sections.heading: Examples (names vary by implementation)

sections.body:
- Policies exist for expected tenants
- Default global policy is present
sections.heading: Validate

sections.body:
For each of the same 3–5 tenants:
- Confirm pinned model versions (e.g., `model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct@<version>`)
- Confirm fallback chain ordering (primary → secondary variant → last-resort)
- Confirm any region/capacity tier routing rules match pre-incident configuration
sections.heading: D.2 Verify model pins and fallbacks

sections.body:
- Policies restore but are not applied due to controller reconciliation failures
- Policies applied but model version IDs differ from what tenants expect
sections.heading: Common failure modes

sections.body:
- One chat completion request
- One embedding request (if used)
sections.heading: Run a minimal end-to-end inference call per tenant

sections.body:
- Requests are authorized correctly
- Request is routed to the expected model
- Latency is within reasonable bounds for a cold start
- No repeated fallback due to missing capacity (unless expected)
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Restore duration and outcome metrics present
- Control-plane error rate normalizing
- No sustained authz failures

---
sections.heading: E) Observability signals (recommended)

sections.body:
If restoring into a clean cluster and you need to move production traffic:

1. Use a **temporary hostname** first (e.g., `cp-restore.<domain>`).
2. Validate using the checklist above.
3. Confirm TLS certificates are valid for the cutover hostname(s).
4. Switch DNS (or load balancer target) to the restored control plane.
5. Monitor:
   - Control-plane 5xx rate
   - Auth failures
   - Tenant request success
sections.heading: Cutover procedure (new cluster restores)

sections.body:
- If DNS cutover causes failures, revert DNS immediately to prior endpoint while you diagnose.

---
sections.heading: Rollback (cutover-specific)

sections.body:
- Artifact integrity verification fails
- Decryption fails due to wrong key or tampered artifact
- Restore tool reports an unsupported version/format and no migration path is approved
- Control-plane services cannot reach required external dependencies (KMS/secret manager/object storage) and you cannot remediate quickly
sections.heading: Abort immediately if

sections.body:
**New cluster restore (preferred):**
- Rollback is typically “do not cut over” or “revert DNS,” then re-run restore in a fresh environment.

**In-place restore:**
- You must have captured pre-restore snapshots (or an equivalent rollback point) before running restore.
- If a restore partially applies:
  - Stop controllers to prevent drift
  - Escalate to Control Plane Engineering for the cleanest recovery path

Important: Avoid manual, piecemeal rollback of restored objects unless directed by engineering; it often creates a harder-to-debug mixed state.

---
sections.heading: Rollback options

sections.body: - Errors like “no matches for kind …” or “resource mapping not found”
sections.heading: Symptoms

sections.body:
- Ensure CRDs are installed for the target version (Step 2.1)
- Re-run restore from a clean state
sections.heading: Fix

sections.body: - Restore job logs show `Forbidden` errors (list/get/patch)
sections.heading: Symptoms

sections.body:
- Apply the recommended RBAC from the Helm values / chart templates
- Confirm service account is correct
- Re-run restore
sections.heading: Fix

sections.body: - Timeouts or throttling during decrypt
sections.heading: Symptoms

sections.body:
- Confirm KMS availability and quotas
- Ensure retry/backoff settings are enabled in the restore tooling
- If KMS is down, stop and follow incident process (do not implement ad-hoc encryption changes)
sections.heading: Fix

sections.body: - Tenants exist but requests route to defaults
sections.heading: Symptoms

sections.body:
- Check controller reconciliation logs
- Confirm policy CRs exist and are in Ready state
- Ensure any dependent resources (model catalog entries, capacity tiers) are present in the restored environment

---
sections.heading: Fix

sections.body:
1. Re-enable scheduled backups (if disabled) and confirm next run is successful.
2. If this was a DR drill:
   - Capture RTO (time from start to validated readiness)
   - File follow-ups for any manual steps that should be automated
3. Update the DR readiness dashboard signals:
   - last_restore_drill_success
   - restore_drill_latency
   - backup_job_success_rate

---
sections.heading: Post-restore actions

sections.body:
- Restore command invocation (sanitized)
- Restore report output from `redwood-private restore apply`
- Logs for restore job (last ~500 lines)
- Validation checklist results (tenants + routing policy spot checks)
- If cutover occurred: DNS change record + monitoring screenshots
sections.heading: Attach or link

payload.page_title: Intermittent WAN Degradation — Operator Runbook for Private Deployments

sections.body:
Summary:

This runbook describes detection, mitigation, and post-incident steps for intermittent WAN degradation affecting Redwood Private deployments (VPC-connected or on-prem control plane bridges). It focuses on preserving SLOs, minimizing model-serving disruption, safe traffic steering, and safe rollback/upgrade behavior when WAN links fluctuate.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments with hybrid control planes (VPC+edge), air-gapped bridges, and VPC-peered tenant topologies.
- Covers symptoms related to intermittent increased latency, packet loss, asymmetric routing, and short network partitions (seconds to minutes).
- Not intended for full datacenter failure: see Disaster Recovery runbooks for regional failover.

Owner & escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Operations (oncall: #pod-privops)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (oncall: #sre-oncall)
- Pager: +1-555-0102 (privops)
- If customer impact > 10% of tenant requests or SLA breach suspected, escalate to Engineering Manager (Elena Martinez) and Customer Success lead (Ravi Kumar).

SLOs and impact thresholds (operational):
- Healthy: control-plane request p95 <= 250 ms, tokenized inference p95 <= 400 ms.
- Degraded: sustained >20% increase above baseline latency OR packet loss >3% for >= 60s.
- Critical: sustained packet loss >10% or periodic disconnects causing >1% of requests to error for >= 5 min.

Signals & detection (alarms):
1) Automated alerts:
   - Telemetry: control-plane RPC error-rate spike, model-serving tail-latency increase, and KV-cache miss storm.
   - Network sensors: BGP flaps, interface errors, RTT jump, interface input errors.
   - Ingest: increased retransmits and TLS session resets reported by edge proxies.
2) Customer reports: elevated 5xx errors, streaming timeouts.
3) Synthetic checks: cross-region / tenant health checks failing intermittently.

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alarm: check telemetry dashboards (Redwood Console -> Private Deployments -> Tenant X -> Latency & Errors).
2) Verify scope: identify affected tenants, control-plane nodes, and AZs. Use redwood-ctl status --tenant <id> --scope network to list impacted routes.
3) Capture artifacts:
   - redwood-ctl trace capture --duration 120s --include=network,proxy,kv
   - tcpdump on affected interface: sudo tcpdump -i <iface> -w /tmp/wan-issue.pcap (rotate after 2 min)
4) Check provider signals: cloud provider network health dashboard, router BGP peer status, WAN provider NOC bulletins.

Tiered response (action matrix):
- Tier 1 (Transient blips, <60s): monitor and annotate incident. Increase sampling on traces but avoid changing config.
- Tier 2 (Degraded, 60s–10m): apply graceful traffic throttles and reroute noncritical traffic. Notify CS for impacted tenants.
- Tier 3 (Critical, >10m or SLA risk): execute traffic steering to alternate control-plane region or enable degraded-mode serving. Consider controlled rollback of recent changes.

Immediate mitigations (playbook):
1) Reduce noisy background traffic:
   - Apply egress rate limit for telemetry-heavy collectors to 20% of baseline: redwood-ctl policy apply --path /telemetry/ingest --egress-cap 20%
   - Temporarily disable scheduled large-model preloads (model prefetch) via config flag: set config.model_prefetch=false for affected clusters.
2) Prefer local inference paths:
   - If model artifact exists locally on edge nodes, shift routing to local-only mode: redwood-ctl route set --tenant <id> --prefer-local true
   - Confirm KV cache hits: redis-cli -h <kv-host> INFO and check keyspace hits/misses.
3) Reroute control-plane to alternative region (safe fallback):
   - Only for tenants with fallback allowed in config.json: if fallback_enabled == true then execute: redwood-ctl failover start --from-region A --to-region B --tenant <id>
   - Use canary traffic percentage (start 5%) and watch error rates for 3 minutes.
4) Switch to degraded-mode policy for latency-sensitive endpoints:
   - Replace full response streaming with chunked summary responses (low-bandwidth fallback).

Safe traffic steering checklist (detailed):
1) Authorization & customer consent: verify tenant contract allows cross-region steer and notify CS with template (see templates section).
2) Capacity check: ensure target region has at least 1.5x measured peak qps reserved for tenant during failover window. Use capacity query: redwood-ctl capacity query --region B --reserve 1.5x --tenant <id>
3) Consistency considerations: model versions pinned? If target region runs a quantized variant, enable quality guardrail: redwood-ctl quality-check --model <model-id> --baseline <tenant-prompt-set>
4) KV cache warmup: pre-warm top-1000 keys with redwood-ctl cache prewarm --keys-file top_keys.txt --region B
5) Monitor: increase tracing to p100 sampling for the tenant during steer.

Model-serving and KV cache considerations:
- Avoid simultaneous model hot-swap during network instability. Hot-swap increases remote fetches and can amplify traffic.
- If large model layers are fetched over WAN, defer model downloads; prefer fallback quantized variants located locally.
- KV cache eviction policy: if eviction storms occur, throttle write-back via circuit breaker config: set config.kv.circuit_breaker_window=30s

Upgrade & rollback safety guidance (when WAN is unreliable):
- Postpone planned upgrades for control-plane or model hot-swap until link stability >= 30 min.
- If an upgrade caused the issue: perform incremental rollforward to previous stable build per the orchestrated-rollforward-and-customer-safeguards playbook.
- Rollback checklist:
  1) Verify stored artifacts and signatures: gpg --verify <artifact>.sig <artifact>
  2) Initiate controlled rollback targeting 10% of nodes as canary: redwood-ctl deploy rollback --target-percent 10 --reason "WAN_degradation"
  3) Monitor service-level metrics for 5 minutes before widening.

Customer communication templates (shortened):
- Initial alert (CS -> customer): "We are investigating intermittent network disruptions affecting inference latency for your tenant. Our team has applied traffic isolation measures and will notify you with updates every 15 minutes."
- Failover notification: "We are proactively steering traffic to an alternative control plane in <region>. You may observe brief consistency artifacts for pinned model versions. Estimated mitigation time: 30–45 minutes."

Post-incident actions (before incident close):
1) Collect all artifacts: pcaps, redwood-ctl traces, probe results, BGP logs, provider tickets.
2) Conduct a 30-min blameless incident review within 72 hours. Include: timeline, mitigation effectiveness, customer impact, and recommended preventive work.
3) Recommended follow-ups (backlog items):
   - Implement adaptive telemetry sampling to prevent noisy collectors from amplifying WAN saturation.
   - Add health-check that tracks asymmetric packet loss and route divergence.
   - Create automation to prewarm KV cache for tenants with fallback flags.

Runbook validation tests (quarterly):
- Synthetic scenario: inject 5% packet loss on control-plane interface for 5 minutes and validate:
  - automated alert triggers,
  - runbook mitigations complete without human-only steps within 10 minutes,
  - customer notification template is sent by CS automation.
- Chaos test: scheduled WAN flaps (BGP withdraw/announce) in staging for 3 AZs. Validate canary failover and rollback timeline.

Appendix: sample troubleshooting commands and expected outputs:
- Quick health checks:
  - redwood-ctl status --verbose --tenant <id>
  - curl -sS https://private-ctrl.<region>.internal/health | jq .
  - iperf3 -c <peer> -t 10 (target throughput / latency)
- Adjust iptables to drop 1% traffic for test: sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 1%
- Capture example edge proxy error: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/edge-proxy.log | grep "upstream reset"

Customer requirements summary (minimums for predictable private behavior):
| Category | Minimum requirement | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| WAN SLA | 99.95% with jitter < 30 ms p95 | Stable link reduces transient failovers |
| Layer 2/3 MTU | 1450–9000 (consistent across path) | Avoids fragmentation for model artifact streaming |
| BGP | Static or BGP with eBGP timers >= 3s and graceful restart | Prevents rapid flaps that trigger control-plane failover |
| KMS latency | <= 150 ms p95 to KMS endpoints | Key operations should not be intermittently slow |
| Local storage | 400 GB free on edge nodes (per model pool) | Allows local model replica and cache warmup |

Ownership and contacts:
- Field operator lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- SRE escalation: Mateo Rivera (mateo@redwood.ai)
- Customer Success: Ravi Kumar (ravi@redwood.ai)
- Playbook reviewers: Elena Martinez, Priya Singh

Related artifacts and links:
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-consistency-chaos-validation-and-rollback-matrix-2028
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026

Revision history:
- 2025-01-14: Created by Aisha Patel
- 2025-06-12: Expanded steering checklist and added model-serving KV cache guidance (reviewers: Ravi Kumar, Elena Martinez)

End of runbook.
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Runbook: Offline bundle signature/manifest verification failures (Redwood Private)

sections.body: This runbook is used by SRE/Support/PS to diagnose and resolve **offline bundle verification failures** for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), especially in **air-gapped** environments.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Bundle manifest integrity (hashes)
- Manifest signature validity (trusted key, signature matches manifest)
- Certificate validity window checks (not-yet-valid / expired)
- Downgrade/replay protection (signed version + local install state)

**Safety principle:** installer verification is designed to **fail closed**. Do not bypass verification except via an approved break-glass process.

---
sections.heading: Verification covers

sections.body:
Typical user-facing errors during `preflight` / `install` include:
- **HASH_MISMATCH**: One or more artifacts do not match the manifest digest.
- **MANIFEST_PARSE_ERROR**: Manifest cannot be parsed or canonicalization mismatch.
- **SIGNATURE_INVALID**: Signature does not match the manifest.
- **SIGNATURE_EXPIRED** / **CERT_EXPIRED**: Signing cert chain is expired.
- **SIGNATURE_NOT_YET_VALID**: System time is behind the signing validity window.
- **UNKNOWN_SIGNING_KEY**: Signature is valid but key is not trusted by local trust store.
- **MISSING_SIGNATURE_FILE**: `manifest.sig` / envelope file missing.
- **DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED**: Bundle version is lower than installed state.

---
sections.heading: Symptoms (what you will see)

sections.body:
1) **Customer + environment**
   - Customer name/account, deployment type (on-prem / VPC), cluster distro/version
   - Air-gapped constraints (no outbound, limited time sources, approved crypto requirements)

2) **Bundle + installer**
   - Bundle filename and full path (as received)
   - Bundle version / build ID (if known)
   - Installer version (`redwood-private-installer --version`)

3) **Execution context**
   - Command used (preflight/install flags)
   - Exact error output (copy/paste), including error code if present

---
sections.heading: Collect these upfront to avoid back-and-forth

sections.body:
On the target host (or a similar host with the same trust store), run:
1) Version + environment:
- `redwood-private-installer --version`
- `uname -a`
- `date -u`

2) Inspect bundle:
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /path/to/redwood-private-offline-bundle.tgz`

3) Verify bundle signature + manifest hashes:
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /path/to/redwood-private-offline-bundle.tgz --verify --verbose`

Save the full output for attachment to Support.
sections.heading: Step 1 — Run inspect + verify (non-destructive)

sections.body:
- Installer logs: `/var/log/redwood-private-installer/installer.log`
- Verification logs: `/var/log/redwood-private-installer/verify.log`
- Local audit events (JSONL): `/var/log/redwood/audit/audit.log`

If logs are missing, re-run the failing command with debug logging:
- `RWI_LOG_LEVEL=debug redwood-private-installer preflight ...`
sections.heading: Default paths (may vary by distro/packaging)

sections.body:
1) Hash mismatch / bundle tampering / transfer corruption
2) Not-yet-valid / expired (time and validity windows)
3) Unknown key (trust store/key rotation)
4) Signature invalid (wrong signature, wrong manifest, or canonicalization mismatch)
5) Downgrade blocked (replay/downgrade protection)

---
sections.heading: Use the first matching bucket

sections.body: The bundle contents (or extracted artifacts) do not match the signed manifest digests.
sections.heading: What it usually means

sections.body:
- Corruption during file transfer (USB drive, SCP retry, proxy tooling)
- Bundles extracted and re-packed
- “Helpful” unzip/tar tooling altering files (line endings, permissions, truncation)
- Partial file copy (disk full)
sections.heading: Common causes

sections.body:
1) Verify the bundle as-is:
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /path/to/bundle.tgz --verify --verbose`

2) Compute the bundle file hash and compare to what Redwood published (if provided out-of-band):
- `sha256sum /path/to/bundle.tgz`

3) Check disk space and copy integrity:
- `df -h`
- `ls -lh /path/to/bundle.tgz`
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Re-transfer the bundle using a binary-safe method:
  - Prefer `scp`/`rsync` with verification over ad-hoc drag/drop tools.
  - If using removable media, copy to local disk first and re-run `sha256sum`.
- Do **not** modify bundle contents. Do not re-tar/re-zip.
- If customer must stage bundles through multiple hops, require a checksum verification at each hop.
sections.heading: Fix / remediation

sections.body:
- Hash mismatch persists across multiple independent transfers.
- Multiple customers report mismatches for the same bundle build ID.
sections.heading: Escalate if

sections.body:
- Create Support ticket (severity based on impact) and tag: `private-offline-signing`.
- Include: bundle build ID, installer version, failing artifact path(s), and verify.log.

---
sections.heading: Escalation path

sections.body:
- **NOT_YET_VALID:** the system clock is behind the signing validity window (common in air-gapped environments without NTP).
- **EXPIRED:** signing certificate chain expired, or bundle is beyond allowed verification window (policy).
sections.heading: What it usually means

sections.body:
1) Capture system time:
- `date -u`
- If available: `timedatectl status`

2) Identify the error subtype in logs:
- Look for `SIGNATURE_NOT_YET_VALID`, `SIGNATURE_EXPIRED`, `CERT_EXPIRED` in `/var/log/redwood-private-installer/verify.log`.
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Correct the host time using the customer-approved time source.
  - If the environment forbids NTP, coordinate with the customer to update time via their standard process.
- Re-run verification after time is corrected.

**Diagnostics-only override:** Some installer builds support a time override flag for debugging (does not change system time). Use only to validate hypothesis and capture evidence.
- Example: `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle ... --verify --time-override "2026-02-01T12:00:00Z"`

If the override makes verification pass, you have confirmed time skew as root cause.
sections.heading: Fix / remediation (NOT_YET_VALID)

sections.body:
- Confirm whether the customer is attempting to install an older bundle beyond the supported window.
- If bundle is legitimately current but cert is expired:
  - Treat as a release/signing incident.
  - Escalate immediately to Release Engineering + Security Engineering.
sections.heading: Fix / remediation (EXPIRED)

sections.body:
- Release Eng: Connor O'Brien
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin

---
sections.heading: Escalation path

sections.body: The signature is cryptographically valid, but the public key is not in the installer’s trusted key set.
sections.heading: What it usually means

sections.body:
- Customer installer is older than the key rotation
- Customer did not update the offline trust store bundle
- Trust store file path misconfigured
sections.heading: Common causes

sections.body:
1) Verify output should indicate:
- Signature valid
- Key ID / fingerprint present
- Failure: `UNKNOWN_SIGNING_KEY`

2) Identify trust store source:
- Check installer config (if used) and logs for the trust store path.
- Common locations:
  - Embedded: `redwood-private-installer` ships with a default trust set
  - External: `/etc/redwood/trust/redwood-bundle-signing-keys.pem`

3) Validate the installer version supports the rotated key:
- `redwood-private-installer --version`
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Update installer to the minimum version required for the bundle (preferred).
- If customer uses an external trust store, deliver the updated trust store file via their approved offline process.
- Re-run `bundle inspect --verify`.
sections.heading: Fix / remediation

sections.body:
- For air-gapped customers, plan trust store updates as part of the same media shipment as the bundle whenever possible.
- Do not add ad-hoc keys without a documented key-rotation/trust-store procedure.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- If this occurs right after a Redwood rotation event, cross-check the key rotation runbook and ensure comms went out.

---
sections.heading: Escalation path

sections.body:
- Manifest was modified (even whitespace/ordering matters if canonicalization is enforced)
- Signature file does not correspond to the manifest (mismatched pair)
- Bundle was partially rebuilt/repacked by a third party
- Bug in older installer regarding canonicalization/parsing
sections.heading: What it usually means

sections.body:
1) Confirm manifest + signature are present and match expected layout:
- Bundle should include `manifest.json` and `manifest.sig` (or the documented envelope).

2) Re-run verify with verbose:
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle ... --verify --verbose`

3) Check for parsing errors:
- `MANIFEST_PARSE_ERROR`, `CANONICALIZATION_MISMATCH`, `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Ensure the bundle is directly from Redwood release artifacts.
- Ensure no intermediate system auto-edits JSON (avoid manual edits, avoid “formatters”).
- Upgrade installer if the error is linked to known canonicalization fixes.

Escalate if
- Signature invalid for a newly published release artifact.
- Multiple environments fail on the same artifact.
sections.heading: Fix / remediation

sections.body:
- Release Engineering + Security Engineering (treat as potential supply-chain incident until proven otherwise).

---
sections.heading: Escalation path

sections.body: The bundle version is lower than what is recorded as installed on the host/cluster, and downgrade is blocked by policy.
sections.heading: What it usually means

sections.body:
- Error includes `DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED` and shows installed version vs bundle version.
- Identify local install state record from logs (location may vary by installer):
  - Common: `/var/lib/redwood-private-installer/state.json`
sections.heading: Confirm

sections.body:
- Use a supported rollback procedure from the compatibility matrix.
- If customer needs emergency rollback:
  - Engage Support + on-call SRE to validate approved rollback path.
  - Do not delete/modify install state files as a workaround.

---
sections.heading: Fix / remediation

sections.body:
1) Command output:
- `redwood-private-installer --version`
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle ... --verify --verbose`
- `date -u`

2) Logs:
- `/var/log/redwood-private-installer/installer.log`
- `/var/log/redwood-private-installer/verify.log`
- `/var/log/redwood/audit/audit.log` (verification events only, if large)

3) Bundle metadata:
- Bundle filename + size
- Bundle version/build ID (from inspect output)

4) If available, generate a support bundle:
- `redwood-private-installer support-bundle --output /tmp/redwood-support-bundle.tgz`

---
sections.heading: Attach the following (redact customer secrets as required)

sections.body:
Verification outcomes should generate a local audit event indicating:
- Outcome: success/failure
- Failure reason code (e.g., HASH_MISMATCH, UNKNOWN_SIGNING_KEY)
- Bundle version/build ID
- Key ID (fingerprint) when applicable
- Whether break-glass was used
sections.heading: Audit expectations (Private / offline)

sections.body:
- Confirm audit logging is enabled for the deployment.
- Capture installer logs and escalate to the installer team.

---
sections.heading: If audit events are missing

sections.body: **Goal:** Provide a narrow, auditable path for critical restore scenarios when verification cannot be performed.
sections.heading: Break-glass (bypass) guidance — restricted use

sections.body:
- Only with explicit customer acknowledgement and Redwood approval (per exception process).
- Must produce explicit warnings + audit markers.
- Must create a Support ticket and capture evidence.
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
1) Open/associate a Support ticket (SUP-xxxxx) and document impact, urgency, and why verification cannot proceed.
2) Obtain approval per exception policy (Security leadership + Release Eng as required).
3) Run installer with break-glass flag and ticket annotation (flag name may vary by installer version):
- Example: `redwood-private-installer install --bundle ... --airgapped --break-glass-skip-bundle-verification --break-glass-ticket SUP-xxxxx`
4) Confirm audit log includes break-glass marker.
5) Follow-up remediation: restore normal verification by installing a properly signed bundle and removing any temporary overrides.

If any uncertainty exists, stop and escalate to Security Engineering.

---
sections.heading: Process (high-level)

sections.body:
- Severity based on install blockage / production impact
- Tag: `private-offline-signing`
- Attachments: verify output + logs + support bundle
sections.heading: Open Support ticket with

sections.body:
- Signature invalid for an official Redwood release artifact
- Cert expired unexpectedly for current release
- Widespread unknown-key after rotation without comms
- Suspected key compromise
sections.heading: Escalate immediately if

sections.body:
- Release Engineering: Connor O'Brien
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin
- SRE/on-call: Sean Gallagher / Neha Kapoor (exec sponsor)

---
sections.heading: Contacts/owners

sections.body:
- [ ] Capture installer version and system UTC time
- [ ] Run `bundle inspect --verify --verbose`
- [ ] Categorize failure (hash/time/key/signature/downgrade)
- [ ] Collect logs and (if available) support bundle
- [ ] Apply remediation for the bucket
- [ ] Re-run verify to confirm resolution
- [ ] If unresolved in 30 minutes or signs of release-wide issue, escalate to Release Eng + Security Eng

---
sections.heading: Operator checklist (copy/paste)

sections.body:
- Hash mismatch after transfer → re-transfer + verify checksums at each hop; avoid repacking.
- Not-yet-valid → fix system time; confirm no restricted time source issues.
- Unknown key → update installer/trust store post-rotation.
- Signature invalid → ensure manifest/signature pair is intact; upgrade installer for canonicalization fixes.
- Downgrade blocked → use supported rollback/compatibility procedure; do not delete state.
sections.heading: Appendix: Common root causes and fast fixes

payload.page_title: operational-handshake-and-validator-catalog-2026

sections.body:
Overview

This runbook defines the operational handshake and validator catalog used during private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments. It is intended for Operator/Field teams, Solutions Engineering, and SREs who perform acceptance, day‑2 validation, and controlled cutovers to production traffic. The goal is to provide a single, repeatable validation checklist that: (1) verifies networking, security and runtime invariants; (2) exercises the runtime and model swap paths with canary traffic; and (3) provides clear rollback triggers and remediation guidance.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood Private deployments: VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed data plane, and air‑gapped on‑prem appliances.
- Covers pre-install validation, post-install smoke tests, canary traffic plan, performance regression checks, and rollback criteria.
- Does NOT replace security compliance evidence artifacts (see customer-requirements library) but references the minimum evidence required for acceptance.

Owner & Roles

- Owner: Deployment Engineering (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary runbook operator: Field Operator / Site Reliability Engineer
- Secondary: Solutions Engineer (customer side) for on-site coordination
- Escalation: Oncall SRE -> Runtime Lead -> Head of Private Deploys (see Escalation section)

Preflight / Prerequisites

Before running validators, confirm:

- Customer network ACLs and BGP/VPC routes are applied per the commissioned design.
- KMS/HSM endpoints reachable from operator VLANs and test service account has encrypt/decrypt privileges.
- Minimum hardware + firmware baseline validated against the compatibility matrix (GPU driver, CUDA/ROCm version, BIOS/firmware).
- Time sync (NTP/PTP) drift < 500ms across control and data nodes.
- Inventory snapshot (serials, NIC MACs, disk UUIDs) uploaded to ticketing system for forensic traceability.

Validator Catalog (operator-friendly table)

| Check | Command / Tool | Expected Result | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Network path to control-plane API | curl -k https://{{control_plane_ip}}/healthz | 200 + JSON {"status":"ok"} | Validate route tables, firewall policy, and proxy ACLs; run traceroute and tcpdump |
| KMS envelope encrypt/decrypt | redwood-kms-tool verify --endpoint {{kms}} --key-id kv-1 | encrypt/decrypt roundtrip < 500ms and success code | Check KMS IAM, VPC endpoints, DNS, and customer firewall; fallback: use ledger-encrypted keystore for acceptance |
| GPU driver / CUDA compatibility | dpkg -l | nvidia-driver >= 525 and CUDA 12.x OR rocm >= 6.x | Reinstall certified driver image; isolate node from pool and re-run burnin |
| Image signature verification | cosign verify --key public.pem image.tar.gz | signature valid, provenance matches release tag | Re-download signed image, verify root of trust; if persistent, escalate to supply-chain security |
| Model artifact checksum / provenance | sha256sum model.tar.gz && cat provenance.json | checksums match release manifest; provenance contains signed build id | Failure -> quarantine artifact and fetch canonical artifact from model registry |
| KV cache warmup smoke | curl -X POST {{runtime}}/v1/cache/warm -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | cache hit rate increase of >10% in 5m window | If miss-rate persists, verify model-to-cache mapping and network between workers |
| Cold start latency test | pb-runner --seq 2048 --qps 1 | p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms (baseline) | If regressions, collect runtime profile and compare to baseline; may require rollback of runtime build |
| TLS certificate chain validation | openssl s_client -connect {{endpoint}}:443 -servername host | full chain validated, no SHA1 intermediates | Replace cert, validate intermediates; check OCSP/CRL reachability |
| Audit log forwarding | tail -n 100 /var/log/redwood/audit.log | recent entries for install actions, no permission failures | Fix agent config and restart collector; ensure log retention policy met |

Acceptance Criteria (binary pass/fail per section)

- Critical validators (network, KMS, image signature) must pass 100%.
- Performance validators (latency/throughput) must be within defined guardrails relative to the customer profile:
  - Latency guardrails: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms under canary load (see Performance Baseline).
  - Throughput: sustained QPS within 10% of committed throughput for dedicated pools under synthetic profile.
- Canaries: at least 30 minutes of canary traffic with < 0.5% error rate and no steady increase in 99th percentile latency.
- Security: KMS envelope rotation validated end-to-end and audit events present.

Performance Baseline (example values, tune per-customer)

- Canary profile: 10 concurrent sessions; 1.5 RPS per session; sequence length distribution 512/2048/4096 token buckets.
- Expected results for medium model (16GB KV per replica):
  - Steady-state throughput: 45 req/s per replica
  - Token generation latency: p50 90ms, p95 260ms (generator only)

Runbook: Field Validation Procedure (numbered)

1. Preflight: Review installation ticket and confirm prerequisites checklist (network, KMS reachable, inventory uploaded).
2. Smoke install: Deploy runtime image to a single validation node in the tenant pool. Run image-signature + driver + cert validators.
3. Control-plane handshake: Execute control-plane API health, and create a temporary test-tenant with restricted quota.
4. Artifact validation: Pull the model artifact and verify checksum/provenance.
5. Warmup: Trigger KV-cache warmup and confirm cache hit-rate and memory usage remain within expected bounds.
6. Canary start: Route 1% of production traffic (or synthetic canary profile defined above) to the validation tenant. Monitor for 30m.
7. Performance sweep: Run the cold-start latency and throughput synthetic tests; collect perf profiles and compare to golden baselines.
8. Security checks: Validate KMS key usage logs, certificate chain verification, and audit log forwarding.
9. Acceptance decision: If all critical validators and canary performance pass, schedule incremental traffic ramp per the traffic migration matrix.
10. Post-cutover: After reaching 100% traffic, run a second sweep of performance validators for 2 hours to detect latent regressions.

Rollback Triggers (automated + operator-observed)

- Error rate > 2% sustained for 10 minutes on production routes originating from the new deployment.
- 99th percentile latency regression > 30% compared to baseline for > 5 minutes.
- KV-cache corruption or state divergence detected (inconsistent model responses across replicas).
- Failures in KMS envelope operations or certificate chain validity errors.

Rollback Procedure (fast, auditable)

1. Initiate Safemode: operator sets tenant to safemode which pauses new model swaps: `redwood-ctl tenant update --id {{tenant}} --safemode=true`.
2. Traffic re-route: shift traffic back to previous revision via control-plane: `redwood-ctl traffic-shift --from={{new}} --to={{prev}} --weight=100` (automated orchestration preferred).
3. Verify: confirm error rate returns to baseline and latency stabilizes within 10 minutes. Collect diagnostic bundles `redwood-ctl collect-diagnostics --tenant {{tenant}} --since "-15m"`.
4. Snapshot & Quarantine: snapshot runtime state and quarantine artifact versions for forensic analysis.
5. Postmortem initiate: create incident with labels `private-deploy-regression` and assign to runtime lead.

Remediation Playbook Examples

- Networking regression: If packet loss or MTU mismatch is detected, isolate node, confirm jumbo frame settings and BGP adjacencies, then reintroduce to pool after validation.
- KMS intermittent: fallback to cached symmetric wrap with strict TTL; escalate to cryptography team if KMS SLA cannot be met for 30 minutes.
- Performance regression tied to driver mismatch: pause scheduling on heterogeneous GPU node type and trigger immutable rollback to previous image.

Telemetry & Alerts (minimum metrics to emit)

- metrics.runtime.request_count (per model, per route)
- metrics.runtime.error_count (per error class) – Alert: error_rate > 1% sustained 5m (warning), > 2% 10m (critical)
- metrics.runtime.latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99) – Alert: p99 > baseline * 1.3 (critical)
- metrics.kvcache.hit_rate – Alert: hit_rate drop > 20% relative to baseline during warmup window
- audit.kms.operation – Alert: KMS failures > 5 in 10m

Evidence & Reporting (for Customer Acceptance)

- Upload the following artifacts to the deployment ticket before handoff:
  - inventory.csv (hardware identifiers)
  - topology.json (VPC/BGP routes snapshot)
  - diagnostic bundle tarball from the validation node
  - signed model provenance and checksums
  - canary perf report (pdf) with latency histograms and QPS timeline

CLI & Example Commands

- Health check: `curl -sS https://{{control_plane_ip}}/healthz | jq`
- Canaries: `redwood-ctl canary start --tenant {{tenant}} --profile canary-small --duration 30m`
- Collect diagnostics: `redwood-ctl collect-diagnostics --tenant {{tenant}} --out /tmp/diag.tar.gz`

Change Log

- 2026-02-15: Created initial runbook (A. Patel)
- 2026-06-02: Added KV-cache warmup rules and canary profile updates (M. Chen)
- 2026-09-10: Tightened latency guardrails and added KMS envelope remediation (L. Rodriguez)

Related Pages & References

- Customer acceptance & smoke validation checklist (see related pages)
- Private deploy operational hardening and safe migration playbook
- Model artifact provenance and signing policy

Appendix: Quick Templates

- Minimal acceptance email snippet: "Acceptance: All critical validators passed; canary run 30m; performance within guardrails. Proceeding to staged ramp as per migration matrix. Signed: <operator>"
- Evidence bundle structure (zip): `inventory.csv`, `topology.json`, `canary_report.pdf`, `diag.tar.gz`, `provenance.json`

For questions or deviations from this runbook, open a deviation request and tag the runtime lead for approval.

payload.page_title: field-ops-checklist-model-swap-rollback-cookbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook documents a prescriptive, field-ops focused checklist for performing model swaps (hot model activation / traffic cutover) in private/VPC and on‑prem deployments, plus automated and manual rollback procedures. It is intended for SREs, field engineers, and customer success engineers executing model rollouts in production or controlled staging environments.

Scope

- Applies to model binary swaps that change serving artifacts (model weights, quantization profile, kernel variant) without topology changes.
- Includes simple router-level cutovers and multi‑service switchover where model-router, kv-cache-proxy, and latency‑sensitive request paths are involved.
- Excludes full infra upgrades (kernel/os/persistent-storage schema changes), which are covered by the incremental stateful upgrade strategy.

Definitions

- Model swap: replacing a model version in the serving runtime and routing a portion or all of traffic to it.
- Canary: < 5% traffic to new model for validation.
- Rollback: reverting routing and model artifacts back to a previous, known-good model.

Owners & Roles

- Primary: Field SRE (oncall) — executes cutover and monitors telemetry.
- Secondary: Model Ops — verifies model artifact integrity and QA metrics.
- Tertiary: Customer Success / Solutions Eng — coordinate with customer for external validation.
- Escalation: Runtime Team Lead (pager) for persistent availability degradations.

Service names used in this doc

- model-router (control-plane routing service)
- serving-runtime (GPU inference service)
- kv-cache-proxy (shared KV cache layer)
- control-plane-agent (local node agent for artifact pulls)
- rdwctl (CLI used by field teams to operate Red­wood services)

SLOs & Safety Thresholds (pre-cutover validated)

- 95th perc latency (token gen) <= 150 ms
- Error rate <= 0.5% (5xx / total requests)
- KV cache miss ratio <= 10% (expected baseline)
- GPU utilization (p95) <= 78% under steady load
- Disk pressure: node disk usage < 85%
- Model artifact checksum must match signed manifest (SHA256).

Pre‑cutover checklist (must be green before any traffic shift)

1. Artifact validation (Model Ops)
   - Manifest signed and verified: `rdwctl artifact verify --model vX.Y --manifest /tmp/manifest.json`
   - Check model size and quantization metadata.

2. Capacity validation (SRE)
   - Canary nodes available and tainted for canary traffic.
   - Sufficient spare GPU capacity: `kubectl top nodes | grep gpu` shows >= 10% spare headroom.

3. Observability validation (oncall)
   - Dashboards for model-router, serving-runtime, and kv-cache-proxy instantiated for model swap window.
   - Traces: set new trace tag `model.version=vX.Y` in sampling.

4. Traffic & routing validation (control-plane)
   - Route policy exists for canary: `rdwctl routing show canary-vX.Y`
   - Fallback route configured to previous model variant on latency/error triggers.

5. Runbook & communications
   - Stakeholders notified via #field-deploys and incident bridge (Zoom link pinned).
   - Schedule maintenance window if swap > 10% traffic or if customer requires.

Validation matrix (quick reference)

| Validation area | Green condition | Action if amber | Severity threshold for rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Latency | p95 <= 150ms | Tighten canary -> pause | p95 increase > 50% over baseline for 5m |
| Error rate | < 0.5% | Pause + investigate logs | error rate > 1.5% for 3m |
| KV miss ratio | <= 10% | Increase TTL or degrade canary | sustained > 25% for 5m |
| GPU saturation | p95 <= 78% | Scale up pods | p95 > 90% for 5m |
| Disk | usage < 85% | Clear temp artifacts | usage >= 95% |
Step‑by‑step model swap procedure (canary -> ramp -> full)

1. Stage artifact on control-plane agents
   - `rdwctl artifact stage --model vX.Y --nodes nodegroup-canary`
   - Confirm checksums: `rdwctl artifact verify --model vX.Y --checksum <sha256>`

2. Prepare canary environment
   - Label canary pods: `kubectl label pod <pod> redwood/canary=true`
   - Ensure probe timeouts/thresholds are conservative (liveness 10s, readiness 5s).

3. Activate canary routing (0->5% traffic)
   - `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --add-canary vX.Y --weight 5`
   - Start a scripted smoke test suite targeting canary endpoints (see Smoke tests below).

4. Observe for 10 minutes (minimum) across the validation matrix
   - Use dashboards and alert queries (listed later).
   - If any amber condition, reduce to 0% and collect debug artifacts.

5. Ramp plan (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Incremental steps: increase weight in controlled windows (recommended 10–20 minutes between steps).
   - At each step: run short A/B latent comparison latency tests and distributional checks on outputs.

6. Finalize cutover and drain previous version
   - After stable 30+ minutes at 100%, deprecate old model: `rdwctl routing remove --route model-router/main --model vX-previous`
   - Begin artifact cleanup on nodes: `rdwctl artifact prune --older-than 30d`

Automated rollback triggers (configure in model-router policy)

- Rollback trigger if any of the following sustained for configured window (defaults shown):
  - Error rate > 1.5% for 3 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous model.
  - p95 latency increase > 50% relative to baseline for 5 minutes -> pause + rollback.
  - KV miss ratio > 25% for 5 minutes -> pause and investigate, followed by rollback if not resolved in 10 minutes.
  - GPU p95 > 90% for 5 minutes -> scale action; if scale fails, rollback.

Automated rollback action sequence (runtime)

1. model-router sets traffic to previous model (atomic routing change).
2. control_plane_agent signals serving-runtime to garbage-collect new artifact.
3. Alert fires to oncall and incident bridge created automatically.

Manual rollback cookbook (when automation is disabled or muted)

1. Halt new traffic immediately: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --weight 0 --model vX.Y`
2. Repoint route to previous model: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --model vX-previous --weight 100`
3. Verify serving-runtime replicas are healthy: `kubectl get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide`
4. Rehydrate caches if necessary: `rdwctl cache prewarm --model vX-previous --targets nodegroup-production`
5. Collect artifacts for postmortem: `/opt/redwood/logs/*model-swap* /var/log/serving-runtime/*`

Post‑rollback verification checklist

- Confirm SLOs returned to baseline for 15 minutes.
- Confirm KV cache hit ratio returned to baseline.
- Confirm GPU utilization stabilized.
- Open a postmortem ticket in JIRA and attach collected artifacts.

Smoke tests (example suite)

- Latency probe: 100 short prompts across 10 clients, measure p50/p95/p99.
- Output validation: deterministic prompts from `eval/prompt-sets/sanity` compared via token-diff
- Resilience test: burst traffic + small percentage of malformed requests to validate errors are isolated.

Telemetry queries & dashboards (examples)

- Error rate (PromQL): `sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests_total{code=~\"5..\"}[1m])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests_total[1m]))`
- p95 token latency (Histogram): `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version))`
- KV miss ratio: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))`
- Artifact pull failures per node: `increase(control_plane_agent_artifact_pulls_failed[10m])`

Logging & diagnostic collection

- Quick bundle: `rdwctl diag collect --start \"2026-09-15T10:00:00Z\" --end \"2026-09-15T10:30:00Z\" --out /tmp/swap-diag.tar.gz`
- Logs to include: serving-runtime, model-router, kv-cache-proxy, control-plane-agent, system journal.

Safety notes & tips from field experience

- Prefer conservative readiness timeouts for new models: they often compile kernels on first inference and may temporarily increase latency.
- Always have an immediate cache-prewarm strategy: a cold kv-cache commonly causes transient high latencies and elevated error rates.
- If running with quantized models, include quantization fallback policies in routing metadata to avoid silent correctness regressions.

Escalation & communications template

- Bridge title: \"Model Swap Incident — <customer-name> — vX.Y\"
- Initial message (pinned): problem summary, current impact (users affected, %traffic), mitigation action taken, next steps, runbook link.
- Owners: Field SRE, Model Ops, Customer Success.

Postmortem & follow‑ups

- Required within 72 hours for any rollback or incident with > 5 minutes of customer impact.
- Attach: artifact manifests, diag bundle, timeline of routing weights, and root cause hypothesis.
- Action items: label owner, target date, and link to validation tests added to CI model-onboarding.

Appendix: CLI snippets and sample routing YAML

- Sample routing change (YAML):
```yaml
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: main-model-route
spec:
  primaryModel: vX-previous
  canaries:
    - model: vX.Y
      weightPercent: 5
  rollbackTriggers:
    latencyP95IncreasePercent: 50
    errorRatePercent: 1.5
```

- rdwctl quick commands:
  - Stage: `rdwctl artifact stage --model vX.Y --nodes nodegroup-canary`
  - Activate canary: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --add-canary vX.Y --weight 5`
  - Force rollback: `rdwctl routing rollback --route model-router/main --to vX-previous --reason \"p95 spike\"`

Related pages

- See also: post-installation acceptance checklist, incremental stateful upgrade strategy, private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook.

Contact

- Owner: Ava Martinez (Field SRE) — ava.martinez@redwood.ai
- Runtime Team Pager: #ops-pager

Document change log

- 2026-02-10 — Created by Ava Martinez (draft)
- 2026-06-02 — Added automated rollback triggers and telemetry queries (review: Darren Kline)
- 2026-09-15 — Expanded manual rollback steps and diagnostic collection (approved)

payload.page_title: Operational Compendium: Policies, Procedures, and Templates

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This compendium collects Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standardized templates for access & permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and common internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers executing routine operational decisions.

Scope: Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with Redwood systems, finances, or data. Exceptions require documented approval from the owning team and Finance or Legal where indicated.

Owner and maintenance: The Finance & Legal team maintains procurement, expenses, and vendor-management sections. People Ops maintains travel and people-facing templates. Security owns access, permissions, and data management sections. Contact: policies@redwood-inference.com.

Policy matrix (high level)
- Access & Permissions: Role-based access by default; principle of least privilege; periodic review cadence. Owner: Security.
- Change Management: Risk-based RFCs and release windows with automated gating for production. Owner: Eng Platform.
- Data Management: Classification, retention, encryption, and deletion standards. Owner: Security & Data Compliance.
- Procurement & Expenses: Approval thresholds, preferred vendors, centralized PO process. Owner: Finance.
- Vendor Management: Risk assessment, contract minimums, periodic review. Owner: Finance & Legal.
- Travel: Pre-approval, per diem, booking guidance, and expense reconciliation. Owner: People Ops.

Section 1 — Access & Permissions
1.1 Principles\- All access requests must be justified with a business reason, TTL (time-to-live) when temporary, and an owner.\- Use "rbac.redwood-inference.com" for role assignments (internal IAM).\- Privileged roles (e.g., infra-admin, db-admin, kms-admin) require manager + security approval.

1.2 Provisioning workflow (standard)
1) Employee/contractor requests access via Access Request Form (template below).
2) Request is routed to the resource owner for approval within 48 hours.
3) Security performs Privilege Review for sensitive scopes (PII, keys, production DB).
4) Provision automated via SCIM/Okta connector where supported. Manual grants logged in the access audit tracker.

1.3 Periodic review\- Quarterly role review for all production-facing roles.
- Annual audit for all users with access to PII or export-controlled data.

1.4 Emergency escalation\- Security on-call must be notified immediately for suspected misuse. Communicate via #security-incident and PagerDuty.

Section 2 — Change Management
2.1 Change classification\- Minor: non-customer-impacting configuration or documentation changes. No RFC required; pre-commit CI and canary deploy recommended.\- Major: code or infra changes that may impact latency, billing, or availability for customers. Requires RFC, rollout plan, and release window.\- Critical: security patches, data-migration fixes, or incidents requiring immediate action; follow incident process and retrospective.

2.2 RFC and release process (major changes)
1) Author prepares RFC in the RFC template (title, summary, risk classification, rollback plan, testing matrix).
2) Stakeholders: Eng Platform, SRE, Product, Security, and Finance (if cost impact). Send RFC for 72-hour review unless expedited.
3) Pre-release checklist: unit/integration tests, perf test (latency & throughput baseline), canary target (min 1% traffic), monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds.\4) Release window: standard weekday 09:00–17:00 PT unless otherwise approved. Emergency releases isolate after-hours approvals policy.

2.3 Post-deploy validation\- 60-minute observation for canary; metrics tracked: error rate (<0.1%), p50/p95 latency within baseline +20%. If threshold exceeded, rollback immediately.

2.4 Change rollback SLOs\- Time-to-rollback target: 30 minutes for high-severity regressions, 4 hours for functional regressions affecting fewer than 5% of customers.

Section 3 — Data Management
3.1 Classification\- Public: safe to publish.\- Internal: accessible by employees.\- Confidential: PII, customer data, model-training datasets, and export-controlled data.

3.2 Retention and deletion\- Hot logs: 90 days.\- Backups (encrypted): 365 days.\- Long-term archives: up to 7 years (subject to legal holds).\- Data deletion requests: follow data subject request (DSR) playbook; acknowledged within 3 business days.

3.3 Storage and encryption\- All Confidential data must be encrypted at rest with KMS keys (customer-managed where requested in Private deployments). TLS 1.2+ for in-transit.

3.4 Access for analytics and dev\- Use anonymized or synthetic datasets when possible. Any request to copy production data for dev/analytics must be approved by Data Compliance and logged with a TTL.

Section 4 — Procurement & Expenses
4.1 Approval thresholds (effective 2026)\- <= $5,000: direct manager approval.\- $5,001–$50,000: Director + Finance approval.\- $50,001–$250,000: VP-level approval + Finance.\- > $250,000: Executive committee (CEO/CFO) + Legal + Finance.

4.2 Purchase order (PO) process\- All vendor spend requires a PO issued through the Procurement portal (procurement.redwood-inference.com) before goods/services begin, except for recurring cloud bills covered under the Cloud Subscription policy.

4.3 Preferred vendors and exceptions\- Finance maintains a preferred-vendor registry (cloud partners, software, professional services). Exceptions require a Vendor Exception Form and procurement committee approval.

4.4 Expense policy highlights\- Employee reimbursements must be submitted within 30 days.\- Non-itemized alcohol is disallowed on expense reports without Executive approval.\- Corporate card policy: cards issued at manager discretion; employees must reconcile monthly.

Section 5 — Vendor Management
5.1 Onboarding minimums\- Contract must include: data protection addendum (DPA), security SOC2 or equivalent evidence where applicable, liability and indemnity clauses, termination & data return instructions.

5.2 Risk assessment matrix (summary)
- Low: SaaS with no sensitive data (quarterly review).\- Medium: SaaS with internal data or vendor personnel access to non-sensitive systems (biannual review).\- High: Any vendor with access to PII, production systems, or model-training data (triannual review + penetration test evidence).

5.3 Offboarding checklist
1) Revoke all credentials and API keys.
2) Confirm data export and secure deletion per contract.
3) Update inventory and notify teams.

Section 6 — Travel & Business Expenses
6.1 Pre-approval and booking\- All overnight travel requires manager approval in Travel Portal. Book via our Travel partners (TravelPortal.redwood-inference.com) to ensure insurance and preferred rates.

6.2 Per diem and reimbursement\- Domestic: $75/day meals; International: follow per-country rates in Appendix A. Receipts required for meals > $25.\- Lodging: book standard rooms; any upgrade requires manager approval and justification.

6.3 Safety and insurance\- All employees traveling for work are covered by company travel insurance. Emergency assistance contact: travel-assist@redwood-inference.com.

Section 7 — Templates (copy & paste)
7.1 Access Request Form (example fields)
- Requester name:
- Email:
- System/resource requested:
- Role required (read/write/admin):
- Business justification:
- TTL (dates):
- Approving manager:

7.2 Change RFC template (header fields)
- Title:
- Author:
- Proposed date:
- Risk classification (minor/major/critical):
- Rollout plan and canary strategy:
- Backout plan and estimated RTO/RPO:
- Metrics to monitor (names of dashboards/alerts):

7.3 Procurement Request template
- Requestor:
- Vendor name:
- Description of goods/services:
- Estimated total cost:
- Budget code / cost center:
- Approvals required (list):

Section 8 — Responsibilities and contacts
- Finance (procurement, invoices): finance-ops@redwood-inference.com\- Security (access, data): sec-ops@redwood-inference.com\- People Ops (travel, HR templates): people-ops@redwood-inference.com\- Eng Platform (RFCs, release windows): platform@redwood-inference.com

Appendix A — International per-diem quick table (examples)\- US: $75/day meals\- UK: £60/day meals\- Germany: €65/day meals\- India: ₹2,500/day meals

Appendix B — Example CLI snippets
- Generate access ticket (placeholder):
  curl -X POST https://access.redwood-inference.com/api/v1/requests -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"resource":"db-production","role":"read","ttl":"72h"}'

Appendix C — Audit & reporting cadence\- Monthly: Finance reports (open POs, recurring spend).\- Quarterly: Vendor risk reviews and access certification.\- Annually: Full policy review and tabletop exercises.

Change log
- 2025-07-15: Initial draft (Priya N.).
- 2025-11-02: Procurement thresholds updated (Finance).
- 2026-01-12: Clarified change rollback SLOs and added emergency escalation contacts.

Notes and references
- See related policies for detailed SOC2 control mapping and DSR playbook.
- Templates can be copied into Google Drive template library for use in requests and RFCs.

End of compendium.
