payload.page_title: Access and Procurement Journey Guide

sections.body:
Overview

This guide consolidates company-wide policies and operational procedures for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel. It is intended for requesters, approvers, and process owners. The procedures below balance speed, least-privilege, and auditability.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party service accounts.
- Excludes project-level transient experiments explicitly funded and documented by a product sponsor; such exceptions must be logged with legal and people-ops.

Key principles

- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required and set expirations where possible.
- Separation of duties: approvals should cross function (requester -> manager -> finance/security as applicable).
- Auditability: every access or procurement must have a ticket and cost center.
- Data classification: handle data according to classification (Public / Internal / Restricted / Regulated).

1) Access and Permissions lifecycle

Summary: standardized request -> justification -> owner approval -> provisioning -> periodic review.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requester: initiates the request with justification and cost center.
- Manager: verifies business need and duration.
- Resource Owner (service or team owning the resource): approves technical scope and least-privilege mapping.
- Security (for Restricted/Regulated or cross-org access): performs a risk review.
- IT/Platform: performs provisioning and documents ticket.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
| Resource type | Approval chain | Max duration without reapproval | Escalation owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GitHub repo (read) | Manager -> Repo owner | 90 days | Eng Platform |
| Production database (read) | Manager -> Data owner -> Security | 30 days | Head of Security |
| Dedicated GPU cluster | Manager -> Infra cost owner -> Finance | 30 days | SRE lead |
sections.heading: Approval matrix (example)

sections.body:
1. Requester opens an Access Request ticket (Jira template: ACCESS-REQUEST) and selects resource and classification.
2. Include explicit justification, required TTL (time-to-live), and cost center code.
3. Manager approves in Jira; if approval is not provided within 48 hours, request auto-escalates to manager's manager.
4. Resource owner confirms mapping to least-privilege roles and approves.
5. IT/Platform performs provisioning and posts the provisioning record + checklist to the ticket.
6. On expiry, access is automatically revoked. Requests for extension require a new approval.

Temporary & emergency access

- Emergency access is permitted via the Emergency Access workflow (Jira tag: ACCESS-EMERGENCY).
- Emergency grants are time-limited (max 8 hours) and must be documented in the ticket with a postmortem within 72 hours.

Periodic review

- Quarterly entitlement sweep: owners must review active grants and close or re-scope stale entries.
- KPIs: 95% of grants have an expiry <= 90 days; 100% of production DB users reviewed monthly.

2) Change management (applies to infra, runtime, and data schemas)

Goals: prevent outages, enable rapid but safe changes, preserve rollback capability.
sections.heading: Standard request flow (numbered)

sections.body:
- Normal Change: non-prod schema tweaks, config-safe changes. Plan in CHG board and notify affected teams.
- High-Impact Change: production schema changes, runtime kernel upgrades, or infra replacements. Requires two approvers (owner + SRE) and a rollout window.
- Emergency Change: mitigations for P1/P0 incidents; follow emergency change process and complete post-change review.
sections.heading: Change types and thresholds

sections.body:
- Description of change, affected services, rollback plan, scheduled window, test plan, and owner.
- Impact analysis: latency/cost/availability and which customers are affected.
- Communication plan: status channel, pre/post messages, and runbook links.

Execution and rollback

1. Schedule change in the change calendar and create CHG ticket.
2. Notify stakeholders 72 hours before window for High-Impact; 24 hours for Normal.
3. Execute in the approved window; monitor predefined SLOs and business metrics.
4. If metrics cross thresholds (see SLOs table), trigger rollback and incident process.
sections.heading: Change submission checklist (short)

sections.body:
- API P50 latency > 2x baseline for >5 minutes -> rollback.
- Error rate > 0.5% for read APIs or >0.2% for write APIs for >3 minutes -> rollback.

3) Data management and classification
sections.heading: SLO thresholds for automated rollback examples

sections.body:
- Public: non-sensitive material (marketing collateral).
- Internal: operational data for day-to-day engineering and product work.
- Restricted: PIIs, internal strategy, or data requiring contractual controls.
- Regulated: data subject to compliance regimes (HIPAA, GDPR special category) and additional contractual controls.
sections.heading: Classification model

sections.body:
- Public: no restrictions.
- Internal: stored in company storage with access controls; retained 3 years unless otherwise required.
- Restricted: encryption-at-rest and in transit mandatory; access only via approved IAM roles; must be cataloged.
- Regulated: additional contractual clauses; processing locations limited by region; subject to audits annually.

Data retention and deletion

- Default retention: 3 years for Internal, 7 years for business-critical financial records, as legal requires for Regulated.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Deletion template (see Templates section).

4) Procurement and expenses
sections.heading: Handling rules by class (brief)

sections.body:
1. Request: Initiator files a Purchase Request (PR) with justification, vendor, estimated COS, and cost center.
2. Manager approval: verifies budget and business need.
3. Procurement review (Finance procurement team): validates vendor onboarding status, commercial terms, and PII handling.
4. Contracting: Legal reviews terms for spend > $50k or any vendor storing Regulated data.
5. Purchase order & payment: Finance issues PO and processes invoice.
sections.heading: Procurement lifecycle (high-level)

sections.body:
- <$1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance reviewer.
- $25,000–$50,000: Manager + Procurement lead + Finance signoff.
- >$50,000: Manager + Procurement lead + Legal + Executive sponsor.
sections.heading: Approval thresholds (example)

sections.body:
- Corporate card: for travel, subscriptions <= $2,000/yr, and low-value operational purchases.
- Personal reimbursement: itemized receipts required, submit within 30 days.
- Audit: Finance runs monthly card reconciliations and random expense audits quarterly.

Vendor onboarding & risk assessment
sections.heading: Card and expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Vendor contact and legal entity details.
- Data handling classification: does vendor process Restricted or Regulated data?
- Security review: evidence of SOC2 or equivalent for vendors with access to Internal/Restricted data.
- Contract terms: data processing addendum (DPA), liability caps, termination rights.
- Payment terms, PO requirements, and escalation contacts.
sections.heading: Checklist

sections.body:
- Low: SaaS tools with no Internal data access (no DPA).
- Medium: tools that store Internal data; require DPA and standard security checklist.
- High: vendors processing Restricted/Regulated data; require SOC2/ISO evidence, legal review, and quarterly security attestations.

5) Travel & out-of-region work
sections.heading: Vendor risk levels (summary)

sections.body:
- All business travel requires a Travel Request with estimated cost and safety assessment for the destination. Managers approve travel; trips with cost > $5k require finance review.
- Travelers must register high-risk trips with people-ops and complete any location-specific compliance training.
sections.heading: Booking and approvals

sections.body:
1. Submit expense via the Expense system with receipts and cost center.
2. Manager reviews and approves within 10 business days.
3. Finance processes reimbursements on the next payroll cycle if submitted by the cutoff.
sections.heading: Expense reimbursements (high-level)

sections.body:
- Per diem follows national guidelines for the travel country; lodging should use preferred suppliers when available.
- Upgrades (e.g., business class) require approval from an Executive sponsor for trips > 8 hours one-way.

6) Templates and artifacts (appendix)
sections.heading: Per diem and lodging rules

sections.body:
- ACCESS-REQUEST (Jira template): fields - requester, resource, justification, TTL, cost center, classification.
- PURCHASE-REQ (Procurement form): fields - item, vendor, estimate, cost center, approver chain.
- DATA-DELETION-REQUEST (Form): fields - dataset id, reason, owner, retention exemption.
- TRAVEL-REG (Form): fields - itinerary, risk assessment, approver, emergency contact.

Example JSON snippet for a Purchase Request (for automation):

{
  "requester": "<name>",
  "vendor": "<vendor-name>",
  "estimated_amount_usd": "<amount>",
  "cost_center": "<code>",
  "data_classification": "Internal/Restricted/Regulated"
}

Governance & enforcement

- Policy exceptions must be documented and approved by people-ops + finance + legal (if applicable).
- Violations (misuse of cards, inappropriate access, or unapproved vendor data use) trigger an investigation and remedial actions which may include revocation of access or disciplinary steps.

Operational metrics to track (examples)

- Mean time to provision access (target < 48 hours).
- Percentage of access requests with explicit TTL (target 100%).
- Vendor onboarding cycle time (target < 15 business days for low/medium risk).
- Monthly travel expense reconciliation lag (target < 10 days).

Related resources and references

- RBAC & Privilege Review process: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/privilege-review-process
- Procurement FAQ and PO template: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/po-templates
- Change calendar and CHG board: /confluence/eng-platform/change-calendar

Revision history

- 2024-06-12: Initial draft (Priya Raman).
- 2024-11-15: Added emergency access process and SLO rollback thresholds (review: Ethan Cole).
- 2025-01-29: Updated procurement thresholds and vendor risk criteria (review: Marta Ivanova).

Contact and ownership

- Document owner: people-ops (policy-ops@redwood.example).
- For access questions: access-ops@redwood.example.
- For procurement questions: procurement@redwood.example.

End of guide.

payload.page_title: Redwood enterprise procedures kit — company operations (2026)

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document centralizes company-wide operational policies and ready-to-use process templates covering access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended as the canonical reference for operational owners, approvers, and team leads.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and suppliers who request access, make changes to production systems, handle company data, engage vendors, or incur business travel/expenses. Exceptions must be approved by the owner_team (finance-legal) and recorded in the exceptions register.

Principles
- Least privilege and auditable approvals for access.
- Risk-proportional controls: higher risk => higher review/fail-safe.
- Single source of truth for templates to speed approvals and audits.
- Clear ownership for every control and handoff.

Owners and escalation
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner: Maya Chen).
- Operational owners: People Ops (travel & people-related expenses), Eng-SRE (change management for infra), Eng-Platform (deployment change policies), Procurement (vendor onboarding), Security (data classification & RBAC design).
- Escalation channel: #ops-escalation (Slack); for regulatory incidents notify security@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com.

1) Access & Permissions
Summary: RBAC-based model with centralized requests through the Access Request Portal (ARP). Temporary elevation via Just-In-Time (JIT) access is encouraged.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requester: provide justification and duration.
- Approver: manager or service owner depending on resource type.
- IAM admin: perform provisioning and maintain audit logs.
sections.heading: Responsibilities

sections.body:
| Resource type | Approver | Max default duration | Escalation threshold |
|---------------|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Non-prod cloud project | Team manager | 90 days | Security review if > 30 days or cross-team |
| Prod read-only role | Service owner | 30 days | Security review if > 30 days |
| Prod write / admin role | Service owner + Security | 7 days | Required approval from Eng-SRE for > 7 days |
| Vendor access (limited) | Procurement + Service owner | 14 days | Contract/DPAs required for > 30 days |
sections.heading: Access categories and approval matrix (summary)

sections.body:
1. Submit ARP form including business justification, requested resources, and duration.
2. Auto-notify approver(s); if multi-approver, require all approvals.
3. IAM admin provisions account/role and tags request id for audit.
4. Access automatically expires at the requested end date; reminders sent 7 days before expiry.
sections.heading: Request process (high level)

sections.body:
1. Request JIT via ARP with short justification and immediate timeline.
2. Approver reviews and sets a task window; JIT sessions are logged and session recordings retained for 90 days.
sections.heading: Temporary elevation/JIT steps

sections.body:
- Quarterly reviews for all active Prod admin roles.
- Annual certification for vendor accounts.

2) Change Management
Goal: enable fast, safe, and auditable changes across infra and product services.
sections.heading: Access review cadence

sections.body:
- Standard change: pre-authorized, repeatable operational tasks (e.g., routine scaling) — no CAB required but must follow runbook.
- Normal change: requires change ticket, impact assessment, approver sign-off, and scheduled window.
- Emergency change: implemented to remediate incidents. Post-implementation review required within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
- Title
- Owner/Requester
- Change category (standard/normal/emergency)
- Impact assessment (services/users, rollback plan)
- Scheduled window
- Validation plan / smoke tests
sections.heading: Change request template (short)

sections.body:
- Normal change: Service owner + Eng-SRE (for infra) or Product owner (for API) depending on impact.
- High-impact (customer-facing outage risk): CAB approval required. CAB meets twice weekly; use asynchronous voting for low-latency approvals.
sections.heading: Approval matrix

sections.body:
1. Open change ticket in Change Management system (link: /tools/change).
2. Fill template, attach runbook, assign approvers.
3. Complete pre-change checklist (backups, canary, synthetic checks).
4. Execute in maintenance window.
5. Run validation tests.
6. Close ticket with outcomes and metrics (latency, error rate).
sections.heading: Implementation steps (normal change)

sections.body:
1. Tag ticket as EMERGENCY; notify on-call and #incident.
2. Implement mitigation with minimum scope.
3. After stabilization, conduct a post-implementation review within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Emergency change protocol

sections.body:
- Production major releases blocked on high-traffic holidays (list maintained by Product).
- Routine changes allowed in designated windows: Mon–Fri 02:00–06:00 UTC and Sat 08:00–12:00 UTC (exceptions handled by CAB).

3) Data Management
sections.heading: Change windows and blackout periods

sections.body:
- PUBLIC: no restrictions.
- INTERNAL: default for business documents.
- RESTRICTED: PII, customer data, proprietary model weights.
sections.heading: Classification scheme (three levels)

sections.body:
- RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, stored in approved buckets, and access controlled via RBAC with explicit justification.
- Export/egress of RESTRICTED data requires a Data Use Request and DSA review (Data Security & Assurance).

Retention and deletion
- Logs (diagnostic): 180 days by default, extendable to 365 days upon SRE request.
- Backups: retention per service SLA; restore tests quarterly.
- Customer data retention: as per contract or 7 years max unless otherwise specified.
sections.heading: Data handling requirements

sections.body:
1. Contain and preserve evidence.
2. Notify Security and Legal within 24 hours.
3. Conduct forensics; follow regulatory notification timelines.
sections.heading: Data breach steps (summary)

sections.body:
- Every dataset must include: owner, classification, retention policy, last updated, and approved uses.

4) Procurement & Expenses
sections.heading: Data labeling and metadata requirements

sections.body:
1. Need identification and owner assignment.
2. Create Purchase Request (PR) using Procurement template (see Templates section).
3. Competitive sourcing required for purchases > $50k.
4. Procurement team reviews vendor compliance (security, SOC2, DPAs) and negotiates terms.
5. Purchase Order (PO) issued; vendor onboarding completed.
sections.heading: Procurement lifecycle

sections.body:
- Up to $2,500: Team lead approval.
- $2,500–$50,000: Department head + Procurement review.
- > $50,000: VP approval + Procurement + Legal.
sections.heading: Approval thresholds (summary)

sections.body:
- Use corporate card for approved travel with pre-approval.
- Expense report due within 14 days of trip end.
- Receipts required for any individual expense > $25.
- Per diem model: US domestic $75/day (meals & incidental), international vary by country — check Finance portal.

Reimbursements and audit
- Finance reserves the right to audit expense claims for 12 months.
- Non-compliant claims will be remediated with manager and may lead to revocation of card privileges.

Procurement request example (JSON snippet to paste into PR form):
```
{
  "requester": "Name",
  "department": "Engineering",
  "description": "GPU cloud capacity: 4 x A100 reserved for Q1 experiments",
  "estimated_cost": "48,000",
  "vendor": "CloudCompute Inc.",
  "business_justification": "Prototype + evaluation for Dedicated offering",
  "approval_chain": ["team-lead", "procurement"]
}
```

5) Vendor Management
sections.heading: Card and travel expenses

sections.body:
1. Complete vendor intake form and risk assessment.
2. Verify security posture (SOC 2, ISO, pen-test results if applicable).
3. Data processing addendum (DPA) and contractual terms signed by Legal.
4. Create vendor record in Vendor Registry with owner and contract dates.
5. Provision necessary access and limit by least privilege.
sections.heading: Vendor onboarding checklist

sections.body:
- Key vendors must have a documented SLA and escalations.
- Quarterly vendor review for strategic vendors; annual review for others.
sections.heading: SLAs and monitoring

sections.body:
- Revoke all accounts and access within 48 hours of contract termination.
- Verify data return/destruction per contract.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Pre-approval: All business travel requires a Travel Request in the Travel Portal and manager pre-approval.
Booking: Use preferred travel vendors for corporate rates; personal arrangements reimbursable only with prior approval.
Safety & compliance: Follow local guidance and travel advisories; register high-risk travel with People Ops.
sections.heading: Offboarding

sections.body:
- Lodging: reasonable nightly rate per city band (see Finance portal).
- Meals: per diem or itemized receipts.
- Ground transport: ride-share or economy car rental.

Travel emergency support: 24/7 travel assistance is available via travel-support@redwood.com.

7) Internal Templates (canonical templates to use)
- Access Request (ARP) template (fields: requester, resource, duration, justification, approver).
- Change Request template (fields: owner, impact, rollback, validation, stakeholders).
- Procurement Request (PR) template (fields: requester, vendor, cost, justification, approvals).
- Vendor Intake form (fields: vendor, controls checklist, contracts, risk rating).
- Travel Request template (fields: traveler, dates, destination, business purpose, manager approval).
sections.heading: Expense categories and caps

sections.body:
--Start ARP--
Requester: Jane Doe
Resource: prod-ml-models S3 bucket (RESTRICTED)
Duration: 7 days
Justification: Investigate model drift for customer incident #1234
Approver: Service owner (ML Infra), Security (if > 3 days)
--End ARP--

Governance and audit
- All actions (access grants, change tickets, procurement approvals) must be tagged with policy id and retained per retention rules.
- Internal audit cadence: semi-annual for access controls, quarterly for change management evidence, annual for procurement/vendor compliance.

Amendments and exceptions
- To request an exception, submit an Exception Request with rationale, compensating controls, and expiration date. Exceptions expire automatically unless renewed via the same process.

FAQs (short)
Q: Who signs off on vendor DPAs?
A: Legal in coordination with Procurement.
Q: How long are access request logs retained?
A: 365 days for provisioning logs; session recordings for 90 days.

Contacts
- Policy owner: maya.chen@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com
- Travel support: travel-support@redwood.com

Related pages and references
- Central policy index: /confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025
- Change management runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/change-management
- Data classification guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention

Revision history
- 2025-11-15: Created by Maya Chen (finance-legal).
- 2026-02-10: Updated access durations and procurement thresholds; added JIT access section.

End of document

payload.page_title: Ops Orchestra: Company-wide Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, and Travel Procedures

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This document (Ops Orchestra) defines the canonical, company-wide procedures for access and permissions, change management, data classification & handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding & management, travel policy, and a small library of standard templates. It is intended for managers, approvers, and people-ops/finance partners who execute or govern cross-functional operational processes.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors that require platform, finance, or HR-related access or services. Exceptions must be approved by the relevant owner_team and logged in the change registry.

Owners and SLAs
- Document owner: finance-legal
- Primary operational leads: Security (access changes), Eng-SRE (infrastructure change runs), Finance (procurement/expenses), People-Ops (travel & benefits)
- Target SLA for routine approvals: 72 business hours
- Emergency/expedited approvals: same-day (see Emergency change section)

1) Access & Permissions
1.1. Access model
- Roles: Employee, Contractor, Service (machine identity), Admin
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP) is required for all roles. Role permissions must be justified in the access request ticket.
- Temporary access: granted using time-bound roles (max 14 days for privileged work).

1.2. Request and approval flow
1. Submit access request via internal access-portal (link: /internal/tools/access-portal). Include: owner, justification, resources, duration, and approver group.
2. Security review: Security reviews high-scope requests (production, key stores, billing).
3. Grant: System auto-provisions where templates exist; otherwise manual provisioning by Cloud Ops within SLA.
4. Verification: Requester confirms access; owner_team marks request closed.

1.3. Access matrix (example)
| Resource class | Typical roles allowed | Approval required | Max duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production inference cluster | Platform-engineer, Release-engineer | Security + Team Lead | 7 days (expirable) |
| Billing and invoices | Finance, Accounting | Finance Manager | 30 days |
| Audit logs / SIEM | Security | Security Lead | 14 days |
| Private console (VPC) | Customer Success (with customer consent) | Security + Customer Success Director | 14 days |

1.4. Periodic review
- Quarterly entitlement review for Admin and privileged roles. Teams must certify access within 10 business days of quarterly notification.

2) Change Management
2.1. Classification
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved templates, no downtime (automated).
- Normal change: scheduled, requires change ticket and 72-hour review window.
- Emergency change: unplanned, immediate action required to restore availability or reduce security risk. Must be retrospectively reviewed by CAB.

2.2. Change Advisory Board (CAB)
- Membership: Eng-SRE, Platform, Security, Product, and one Finance/Legal representative.
- Weekly meeting cadence for normal changes; emergency convened ad-hoc.
- Approval criteria: risk, roll-back plan, test plan, owner, monitoring & alerting updates.

2.3. Change request template (required fields)
- Title
- Owner & approvers
- Type (standard/normal/emergency)
- Rollout window & maintenance window
- Backout/rollback plan
- Canary/verification steps and SLOs to observe
- Impacted services and customers

2.4. Deployment checklist (example)
1. Create change ticket in change-registry (link: /internal/tools/change-registry).
2. Attach runbook and rollback commands.
3. Confirm tests in staging and smoke tests.
4. Schedule and notify stakeholders 48 hours before the window.
5. Execute canary rollout; monitor latency/error metrics for 30 minutes.
6. Proceed to full rollout if health criteria met, otherwise initiate rollback.

3) Data Classification & Management
3.1. Classification levels
- Public: Safe for external publication.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data; limited sharing outside Redwood prohibited.
- Confidential: Business-sensitive data (contracts, pricing, non-public benchmarks).
- Restricted: Regulated or customer-sensitive data (PII, PHI, encrypted customer payloads).

3.2. Handling rules by class
- Storage: Restricted must be stored in customer-dedicated or encrypted buckets with KMS key rotation; Confidential must use company-managed encryption.
- Access: Restricted requires two-factor and documented business justification.
- Transit: TLS 1.2+; internal tunnels must be encrypted and use mutual authentication where possible.
- Retention: See table below.

3.3. Retention & Disposal (summary)
| Data class | Default retention | Disposal action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | N/A | No action required |
| Internal | 3 years | Archive to long-term internal store, remove direct access |
| Confidential | 7 years | Secure delete and log shred event |
| Restricted | Customer-specific / regulatory | Follow customer or legal retention schedule; certify deletion with KMS key rotation |

3.4. Data breach playbook (high level)
1. Contain: Isolate affected resources.
2. Notify: Security incident channel and CISO.
3. Assess: Determine scope and classification of exposed data.
4. Remediation: Revoke credentials, rotate keys, patch vulnerability.
5. Notification: Legal decides customer/regulator notifications.
6. Post-incident: Postmortem and remediation tracking.

4) Procurement & Expenses
4.1. Procurement thresholds & approval matrix
- Purchase Request (PR) < $5,000: Manager approval (auto in procurement system).
- $5,000 – $50,000: Finance Manager + Procurement review.
- $50,000 – $250,000: Procurement Director + Legal review.
- > $250,000: VP-level approval and board notification for multiyear commitments.

4.2. Preferred vendors and vendor rationalization
- Teams should use preferred vendors list in procurement portal. If a new vendor is required, request a Vendor Exception with justification and complete the risk questionnaire.
- Vendor Exception approvals target SLA: 5 business days.

4.3. Expense policy highlights
- Travel expenses must include original receipts for amounts > $75.
- Per diem and caps: domestic $80/day, international $120/day unless pre-approved.
- Pre-approval: Any trip with total estimated cost > $2,000 requires manager + Finance pre-approval.

4.4. Purchase order & invoice flow (example)
1. Create PR in procurement system with line items and cost center.
2. Procurement reviews contracts, confirms compliance and insurance.
3. Contract owner (Legal) signs if required.
4. PO issued to vendor; invoice matched in AP and paid per vendor terms.

4.5. Template: minimal Purchase Request JSON (for internal procurement portal)
{
  "title": "[short description]",
  "requested_by": "user@example.com",
  "cost_center": "ENG-PLATFORM",
  "amount": "$[amount]",
  "vendor": "VendorName",
  "justification": "[business reason]"
}

5) Vendor Onboarding & Management
5.1. Onboarding checklist (must-complete before PO issuance)
- Vendor risk questionnaire completed and scored.
- Security controls validated: SOC2 or equivalent, encryption-at-rest, vulnerability disclosure policy.
- Contractual terms (SLA, liability caps, data residency) negotiated.
- Approved insurance certificates on file.
- Finance payment terms and tax forms collected.

5.2. Ongoing vendor review
- Quarterly business reviews for strategic vendors.
- Annual security re-attestation for vendors holding Confidential or Restricted data.
- Termination checklist: data return/secure deletion, credential revocation, final invoice reconciliation.

6) Travel & Meetings Policy
6.1. Booking and approvals
- All business travel should be booked via the company travel portal (link: /internal/tools/travel).
- Manager approval required for all travel. International travel requires People-Ops pre-check for visa and safety guidance.

6.2. Health, safety, and insurance
- Company travel insurance covers itinerary-based medical and evacuation for approved trips. Register your travel itinerary in travel-portal to enable support.

6.3. Sustainable travel guidance
- When feasible, prefer direct flights with lower emissions (use carbon-light options in travel portal). Combine trips for adjacent meetings rather than separate travel instances.

7) Templates & Forms (library)
- Access request template: /templates/access-request.md (example fields: resource, justification, approvers, duration)
- Change request template: /templates/change-request.md
- Purchase Request JSON template: (see section 4.5)
- Vendor risk questionnaire: /templates/vendor-questionnaire.pdf

8) Exceptions, Escalations, and Audit
- Exceptions: Submit policy exceptions to finance-legal with documented business justification and compensating controls. Exceptions have a 6-month default expiry unless renewed.
- Escalations: Use the incident/escalation matrix for operational disputes; unresolved cases route to Director-level owners.
- Audit: Teams must retain change and procurement records for at least 3 years and be able to produce them for internal or external audit.

9) Frequently asked operational scenarios (quick answers)
- Need temporary production access for a P0 fix? Open an Emergency change and tag Security + Eng-SRE, provide rollback and verification steps.
- New contractor requiring billing console access? Use contractor role template and limit to 14 days; require Finance sponsor and sign-off.
- Vendor wants to store customer payloads? Require Restricted data handling controls and a customer-approved data processing addendum (DPA).

10) Change log & related artifacts
- Major revisions: 2026-09-12: Added vendor re-attestation cadence and procurement thresholds update.
- Artifact links: change-registry, procurement-portal, access-portal, vendor-portal (internal links in system).

Appendix A: Contacts and escalation list
- Security (access changes, incidents): security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Procurement & Vendor ops: procurement@redwood.ai
- Finance (expenses): expenses@redwood.ai
- People-Ops (travel & visas): people-ops@redwood.ai
- CAB coordinator: cab@redwood.ai

Appendix B: Short CLI snippets
- Revoke an API key (example):
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"key_id":"abcd-1234"}'

- Query change registry for open emergency changes:
  curl -sS https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/changes?status=emergency | jq '.'

Appendix C: Quick checklist PDF export (one-pager summary)
- Use the export template in /templates/ops-onepager.docx to produce a manager-facing checklist for onboarding new hires, vendors, or services.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Ops Authorization and Stewardship Playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates cross-functional policies and prescriptive procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and employee travel. It is designed for product, engineering, security, finance, and people-ops partners to reduce ambiguity, accelerate approvals, and maintain audit-ready trails.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who request access to production systems, submit change requests, incur company expense, or handle regulated data. Exemptions require an explicit written approval from Security + Finance.

Principles

- Least privilege by default: grant minimal access required for the task and return access immediately on task completion.
- Separation of duties: approvals and implementers should not be the same person for high-risk requests.
- Risk-based gating: use thresholds (financial, data sensitivity, availability impact) to escalate approvals.
- Auditability: every approval path must result in a ticket, timestamp, and approver identity.

Roles and responsibilities

1. Requester: initiates request, provides justification, and declares data types involved.
2. Approver: assigned based on the approval matrix below. Responsible for validation and sign-off.
3. Implementer: executes the change or provisioning after approval.
4. Auditor/Reviewer: periodic reviewer (security/finance) who samples completed changes and access grants.
5. Steward: owner of a product or data domain (e.g., API Product Owner, Data Steward) who approves sensitive-data requests.

Access and permissions
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Role-based access (RBAC) is the default. Roles map to named collections in the access catalog: read-only, engineer, infra-admin, sre-oncall, billing-view, privacy-analyst.
- Temporary elevated access is provided via time-limited grants (TTL) and must include justification and expiry.
sections.heading: Access model

sections.body:
1) Create an access ticket in the internal system (prefix: ACCESS-). Include: systems, role, business justification, duration, and stewardship approvals if data is sensitive.
2) Auto-check: system runs a policy engine to detect conflicts or need for steward approval.
3) Approval: routed to manager for low-risk requests, to product steward for data-involving requests, and to Security for infra-admin.
4) Grant: implementer or automation applies the role; ticket updated with TTL and revocation schedule.
sections.heading: Request flow

sections.body:
apiVersion: rwd.v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: analytics-billing-read-2025
subjects:
  - type: User
    id: user:maya.chen@redwood.ai
roleRef:
  name: billing-view
  namespace: analytics
expires_at: 2025-06-15T23:59:00Z
sections.heading: Example RBAC binding (YAML) for internal catalog

sections.body:
- rwdctl access request --role infra-admin --systems cluster-1 --reason "deploy hotfix" --duration 4h
- rwdctl access revoke --ticket ACCESS-2345

Approval matrix (financial & risk thresholds)

| Request type | Threshold | Approver | Implementer restriction | Audit requirement |
|--------------|-----------|----------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| Standard access | <= 30 days, no sensitive data | direct manager | self or automation | ticket + manager signoff |
| Elevated infra access | any duration | Security (2FA) + manager | automation only | ticket + security attestation |
| Sensitive data access | any duration | Data Steward + Security | steward-coordinated | ticket + data access log enabled |

Change management
sections.heading: Quick CLI example (internal tooling)

sections.body:
- Routine: low-risk config changes, no customer impact, implemented during business hours.
- Standard: requires change ticket, test plan, rollback steps, and reviewer. Allowed outside change window with manager approval.
- Major: large schema migrations, model weight changes, or infra reboots that may impact latency/availability. Must be scheduled in the approved maintenance window and require cross-team signoffs.

Change request checklist (must be attached to every CHANGE- ticket):
- Summary and owner
- Impact analysis (services and customers affected)
- Test plan and verification criteria
- Rollback steps (including data migration reversion if applicable)
- Scheduled window and communication plan
- Post-change verification tasks and monitoring dashboards
sections.heading: Change windows and classification

sections.body:
1) Triage via oncall channel.
2) Emergency approval from SRE lead or Security (phone/DM acceptable).
3) Implement change with post-facto ticket created within 24 hours and full RCA within 72 hours if the change caused customer-visible impact.

Data management and stewardship

Classification: all datasets must be classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Regulated. The steward must be named in the dataset registry.
sections.heading: Emergency changes

sections.body:
- Confidential data must never be copied to personal devices or third-party services without a signed DPA and explicit steward approval.
- Backups containing Regulated data must use customer-specific encryption keys and be listed in the custody register.
- Analytics sampling and production logging must redact PII at ingest where feasible.
sections.heading: Data handling rules

sections.body:
- Quarterly automated access certification for all Confidential/Regulated datasets.
- Ad-hoc reviews for projects flagged by security or privacy.

Procurement and expenses (guidelines)
sections.heading: Data access review cadence

sections.body:
- Up to $1,000: Manager approval (one approver).
- $1,001 to $25,000: Manager + Finance reviewer.
- Over $25,000: Manager + Finance + Executive sponsor (VP-level) + Legal for contract review.
sections.heading: Approval thresholds for spend (examples)

sections.body:
1) Create procurement request (PROC-) with cost center, justification, and vendor.
2) Finance performs budget check and routes for required approvals.
3) Contracts team reviews any vendor with PII or model hosting.
4) Purchase order (PO) issued and copy attached to PROC- ticket.
sections.heading: Procurement flow

sections.body:
- Employees must submit receipts within 14 days. Card charges auto-flagged for review if over $500.
- Per diem and travel reimbursement defined in the Travel section below.

Vendor onboarding and management

Minimum vendor checklist before provisioning production access or sending data:
1) Completed security questionnaire (SSQ) and evidence (SOC 2 report or equivalent).
2) Signed DPA (if processing customer data) and appropriate data residency annotations.
3) Contract review by Finance + Legal with indemnities and termination rights.
4) Vendor account owner assigned and a quarterly health review scheduled.
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Access review every 90 days.
- Contract renewal at 60 days before expiry with risk re-assessment.
- Offboarding steps: revoke credentials, remove integrations, validate data deletion per DPA, and archive evidence.

Travel policy summary
sections.heading: Ongoing vendor controls

sections.body:
- Domestic travel under $1,500: Manager approval.
- International travel or travel > $1,500: Manager + People Ops approval.
- All travel that includes customer meetings must include a security pre-clearance check if devices with access to internal systems will be used.
sections.heading: Booking and approvals

sections.body:
- Use preferred vendors where available. Receipts required for accommodations and transportation.
- Lost baggage or itinerary changes must be reported to People Ops within 48 hours.

Templates and internal forms
sections.heading: Per diem and accommodation guidance

sections.body:
- Access request (ACCESS-) template:
  * Title: ACCESS-<system>-<role>-<short-reason>
  * Requester: name + email
  * Justification: business need and expiry
  * Data involved: classification
  * Approvals required: manager, steward, security

- Change request (CHANGE-) template:
  * Title: CHANGE-<service>-<summary>
  * Owner: name + pager
  * Impact: brief list of affected services
  * Test & rollback plan: steps and verification criteria

- Procurement (PROC-) template:
  * Title: PROC-<vendor>-<purpose>
  * Cost center:
  * Budget owner:
  * Quote & attachments: link to vendor quote and SSQ

Example expense email subject: "Expense Submission: Conference travel (May 2025) — Maya Chen — $1,142.50"

Operational tools and integrations

- Tickets: internal JIRA/ServiceDesk instance (ticket prefix mapping: ACCESS-, CHANGE-, PROC-, VEND-).
- Automation: rwdctl and workflows in the console to apply RBAC TTLs.
- Logs & audit: all access grants and change approvals stream to Splunk and stored for 13 months for compliance reviews.

Appendix: sample approval matrix (text table)

| Action | Low risk | Medium risk | High risk |
|--------|---------|------------|----------|
| Access grant | manager | manager + steward | security + product steward |
| Infra change | oncall approval | SRE lead + manager | SRE lead + Security + Product owner |
| Vendor contract | Finance | Finance + Legal | Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor |

Revision history

- 2024-08-15: First published by Maya Chen.
- 2025-05-10: Expanded vendor onboarding checklist and added RBAC YAML example (editor: Carlos Rivera).

Related references

- See: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/runbook (for technical RBAC implementation)
- See: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/maintenance-windows (for scheduling maintenance)

Contact points

- Security policy questions: security@redwood.ai
- Procurement & contracts: procurement@redwood.ai
- People Ops (travel & expenses): people-ops@redwood.ai

This playbook will be reviewed annually or on significant organizational change.

payload.page_title: Operational Flows and Policy Gallery

sections.body: This page consolidates company-wide operational flows and reusable policy artifacts relating to access and permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended as a single-entry reference for teams to discover the canonical process, required approvals, and the standard templates used by Redwood Inference.
sections.heading: Purpose and scope

sections.body:
- Engineering, Product, Security, Finance, People Ops, and Procurement partners.
- Team leads and managers who approve access, spend, or changes.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
| Area | Owner | Target SLA / Thresholds | Key system | Approval path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & Permissions | Security + IT | Standard request: 48 hours; Elevated: 5 business days; Emergency: <4 hours | IdentityHub (IAM) | Manager -> Security reviewer -> IAM admin |
| Change Management | Eng-Platform | Standard change window: 02:00–05:00 PST; Emergency changes: immediate runbook | OpsChange | Change owner -> CAB -> Release manager |
| Data Management | Security + Data Platform | Retention: 1y/3y/7y by classification; Backup RPO 24h | DataLake / Vault | Data owner -> Security review |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance-Legal | < $5k: manager; $5k–$75k: procurement; > $75k: exec | ProcureFlow, Spendly | Req -> Procurement -> Finance -> Exec (if needed) |
| Vendor Management | Procurement | Onboarding: 7–14 days | Vendor Portal | Security review -> Procurement -> Contracting |
| Travel & Expenses | People Ops + Finance | Per-diem and policy; pre-approval for > $2k | Spendly | Traveler -> Manager -> Finance |

Note: See "Templates" section at the end for direct links to request and approval forms.

1) Access & Permissions (Identity lifecycle)
sections.heading: Summary (quick reference)

sections.body: Redwood centralizes identity and access control to IdentityHub. All access must follow least-privilege principles and be tied to an owner and business justification. Temporary elevated access must have an expiration.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requester: submits request in IdentityHub with justification and business owner.
- Manager: approves role change and validates business need.
- Security reviewer: performs risk review for privileged access (SRE/infra, customer data, KMS/HSM).
- IAM admin: applies the change and documents in the audit log.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
1. Requester files an Access Request in IdentityHub with resource, role, justification, and requested duration.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, escalate to manager's skip-level.
3. If the role is privileged, Security reviewer has 2 business days to respond; may place conditions (MFA, limited scope).
4. IAM admin provisions access. Provisioning events must include ticket ID and expiration.
sections.heading: Standard process (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- 90% of standard requests fulfilled within 48 hours.
- Emergency access (investigations, P1 incidents): target same-day (4 hours) turnaround via on-call IAM admin and Security Pager.
- Monthly audit: all privileged roles reviewed quarterly.
sections.heading: SLOs and monitoring

sections.body:
- Emergency access uses the Emergency Access Runbook (link: OpsChange/Emergency-Access-Runbook). Every emergency grant must be accompanied by an audit ticket and post-incident access review within 7 days.

2) Change Management (Services & Infra)
sections.heading: Exceptions and emergency process

sections.body: To minimize risk from configuration and code changes by standardizing assessment, scheduling, and rollouts.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk, follow templated rollout (e.g., dependency bumps, non-prod config changes).
- Normal changes: require CAB review; typically feature deploys, infra patches.
- Emergency changes: require immediate action; follow Emergency Change runbook and postmortem.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
- Standard changes: no CAB if they match the Standard Change Catalogue and use a validated automation playbook.
- Normal changes: submit in OpsChange 72 hours before planned window. CAB meets daily for fast lanes and weekly for large changes.
- Change window: default maintenance window 02:00–05:00 PST; services with global usage must consult SRE before scheduling.
sections.heading: Approval matrix and windows

sections.body:
- All normal and emergency changes must include a rollback plan and a success metric (SLO delta or error rate).
- If errors exceed alert threshold (error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline), trigger rollback and incident response.
sections.heading: Rollback policy

sections.body:
- Owner must run the Post-Change Checklist in OpsChange within 4 hours of completion and mark the change as successful or failed.

3) Data Management (Classification, Retention, Access)
sections.heading: Post-change verification

sections.body:
| Classification | Examples | Default retention | Access controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Marketing assets | 0 | Read-only public URLs |
| Internal | Documentation, non-sensitive logs | 3 years | Corporate SSO with RBAC |
| Confidential | Customer PII, analytics with identifiers | 7 years | Justified access, strict logging, DLP |
| Restricted | KMS keys, secrets, regulated customer data | As required by contract | Restricted to named individuals, HSM/KMS controls |
sections.heading: Classification table

sections.body:
- PII and Confidential datasets require a documented Data Processing Agreement and must be stored only in Vault-backed buckets with encryption at rest.
- Backups: daily snapshot with retention according to classification. Restore drills: annually for Restricted data, bi-annually for Confidential.
sections.heading: Data handling requirements

sections.body:
- Automated retention policies are enforced via DataLife jobs. Data owners must declare retention period at onboarding.
- Deletion requests use the Data Deletion Template and are tracked in the Data Deletion Register.
sections.heading: Retention and deletion

sections.body:
- Schema migrations that touch production must be submitted to Data Platform and follow the Migration Review workflow (submit migration PR, canary run, monitoring).

4) Procurement & Expenses
sections.heading: Data change control

sections.body:
- <$5,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow (Spendly card optional).
- $5,000–$75,000: Procurement team approval + Finance-Legal review (Supplier terms assessment).
- >$75,000: Procurement + Finance-Legal + Executive approval (SVP or CFO).
- Capital spend: follow Capitalization policy; enter requisition with finance tag.
sections.heading: Procurement thresholds and approvals

sections.body:
- For purchases > $50k, obtain at least 2 competitive quotes and document selection rationale in ProcureFlow.
- Risk scoring: Procurement assigns a Vendor Risk Score (1–10). Any vendor with score >=7 triggers Security review and may require SOC2/ISO evidence.
sections.heading: Competitive sourcing and vendor evaluation

sections.body:
- Use Spendly to submit expense reports. Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Per-diem for domestic travel: $75/day lodging cap: $250/night without pre-approval.
- International travel: pre-approval required for trips exceeding $2,000.
sections.heading: Expense reimbursement rules (high level)

sections.body:
- Monthly reconciliation between ProcureFlow and accounting.
- Random sample expense audits quarterly (finance + internal audit).

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding checklist (7–14 day target):
1. Vendor request created in Vendor Portal (ProcureFlow) with SOW/quote.
2. Procurement performs commercial review and risk scoring.
3. Security runs technical and compliance review (SOC2/penetration test evidence as required).
4. Legal reviews contract terms and data processing clauses.
5. Finance provisions payment terms and payment method.
6. Account team verifies go/no-go.
sections.heading: Audit and controls

sections.body:
- Standard contract must include: data residency clause, breach notification timeline (<=72 hours), liability caps, and SLA definitions (uptime, support response).
- For production services that affect customer traffic, require 99.9% uptime SLA and a runbook integration.
sections.heading: Contractual controls and SLAs

sections.body:
- On contract end, Procurement triggers Offboarding Checklist: license termination, access revocation in IdentityHub, data return or secure deletion, final invoice settlement.

6) Travel policy (concise)
sections.heading: Offboarding and termination

sections.body: - Any trip expected to exceed $2,000 requires manager & finance pre-approval via Spendly.
sections.heading: Pre-approval

sections.body: - All employees traveling on business automatically receive Redwood travel insurance and are covered under the company incident response procedures.
sections.heading: Travel safety and insurance

sections.body: - Use company preferred vendors where available. Personal upgrades should not be charged to company cards without explicit manager approval.
sections.heading: Booking and allowable expenses

sections.body:
- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip completion. Late submissions may delay reimbursement.

7) Templates and artifacts (canonical)
sections.heading: Expense timelines

sections.body:
- Access Request Template (IdentityHub Request Form) -> /confluence/templates/access-request-template
- Change Request Template (OpsChange Change Form) -> /confluence/templates/change-request-template
- Data Deletion Request -> /confluence/templates/data-deletion-request
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist -> /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Low-value Purchase Requisition (<$5k) -> /confluence/templates/requisition-lowvalue
- Expense Report Template (Spendly) -> /confluence/templates/expense-report-template
sections.heading: Available templates (ProcureFlow / Confluence Templates)

sections.body:
- Minimal change request example (YAML):
---
title: "Upgrade dependency X"
components: [service-a, service-b]
window: "2026-09-01T02:00:00-07:00 to 2026-09-01T05:00:00-07:00"
rollback: "helm rollback v1"
owner: "team-service-owner@example.com"
---
sections.heading: Example JSON/YAML snippets

sections.body:
- Policy exceptions must be recorded using the Exception Request Template and approved by the policy owner. Exceptions are logged and reviewed quarterly.
- Non-compliance (unapproved access, unauthorized spend) escalates to the owner_team and may be subject to disciplinary action per HR policy.
sections.heading: Audit and enforcement

sections.body: - Each area above has an associated runbook stored in OpsChange and linked from this page. Runbooks include command snippets, contact on-call rotation, and verification checks.
sections.heading: Operational readiness and playbooks

sections.body:
- 2026-02-10: Created by Maya Chen (initial gallery and templates).
- 2026-05-12: Procurement thresholds updated; added vendor risk scoring (Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-08-01: Added emergency access SLA details and retention clarifications (Samira Patel).
sections.heading: Change log for this page

payload.page_title: Operations Ecosystem Handbook: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, and Templates

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide operational policies for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It provides consistent decision thresholds, owners, and step-by-step procedures teams must follow.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors unless a separate customer contract or legal requirement overrides a default. Exceptions must be documented and approved via the Risk & Exceptions process.

Owners and escalation
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy maintenance).
- Operational owners: Engineering (access provisioning & change review), Eng-SRE (production change approvals and runbooks), People Ops (travel and expense policies), Procurement (vendor onboarding and purchase approvals), Security (data classification and sensitive approvals).
- Escalation path: Team Lead -> Platform Security -> Director of Eng-SRE -> VP Finance -> Chief Legal Officer.

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: Access decisions balance speed and principle of least privilege. All access is logged and reviewed. Access requests and approvals must use the central Access Request system (Jira ticket prefix ACCESS-) unless an emergency process is invoked.

Key definitions
- Standard access: Non-privileged accounts, code repositories, and internal tools. Approval by team lead.
- Privileged access: Root, database admin, KMS/HSM operations, production SSH. Requires security review and a privileged access request.
- Emergency access: Short-term elevated access for critical incidents. Must be documented retroactively within 24 hours (see Emergency Access process).

SLAs and thresholds
- Standard requests: resolved in 3 business days (SLA).
- Privileged requests: resolved in 5 business days, security review required.
- Emergency requests: acknowledged within 1 hour, granted only when approved by on-call Eng-SRE and Platform Security.

Standard process (day-to-day)
1. Open ACCESS-<team>-<short-desc> ticket and select template (standard | privileged | emergency).
2. Attach justification, business owner, and requested duration.
3. Team lead + security approver approve via ticket workflow.
4. Provisioning performed by identity team or delegated approver.
5. Ticket automatically moves to access review queue after provisioning for periodic audit.

Emergency access process (incident-driven)
1. Pager duty alert -> engineer requests emergency access via Slack emergency channel and creates ACCESS-EMERG ticket within 1 hour.
2. On-call Eng-SRE + Platform Security must approve in Slack with reference to ticket id.
3. Access is granted with an expiration (default 4 hours).
4. Post-incident: engineer must provide root cause and list of commands executed in the ticket. Security performs retroactive audit within 72 hours.

Periodic reviews
- Quarterly: Team leads must certify all privileged accounts assigned to their teams.
- Annual: Org-level access review and remediation plan coordinated by Security.

2) Change Management
Intro: All changes that affect production availability, security posture, or billing/cost must follow the Change Process. The change categories below determine approval and testing requirements. Use CHG- prefix in Jira.

Change categories and requirements
- Standard change (low risk): Non-prod config updates, documentation, minor infra changes. Require peer review and automated CI checks. Can be scheduled without further approvals.
- Significant change (medium risk): Deployments to production affecting >5% of traffic or changes to model serving config (batch sizes, KV cache behavior). Require canary rollout plan, owner sign-off, SLO impact analysis, and Ops reviewer.
- Major change (high risk): Migrations, database schema changes, KMS rotations, network or IAM redesigns. Require formal RFC, impact analysis, test plan, rollback plan, and Director-level approval.
- Emergency change: Patches required to restore service. Emergency changes allowed only during incident with on-call approval and must be documented and post-reviewed.

Mandatory artifacts for Significant & Major changes
- Change RFC (short): Purpose, owners, impact scope, rollback plan, test matrices, runbook steps.
- Canary plan: Traffic percentage schedule, monitoring windows (min 30 minutes), success/failure criteria mapped to SLOs.
- Rollback trigger conditions: latency increase >25% vs baseline for 3 consecutive sampling windows, token error rate increase >2x, or customer-impacting 5xx spike.

Change approval cadence and SLAs
- Standard: peer review and automated checks; deploy in next scheduled window.
- Significant: 48-hour review window; schedule deploy in next maintenance window.
- Major: minimum 7-business-day review and Exec sign-off.
- Emergency: retro-review within 72 hours; change ticket must contain executed commands and postmortem linkage.

3) Data Management and Retention
Intro: Data classification and retention must meet legal, security, and product needs. Follow the Data Classification Matrix and retention baseline below. For any contract-specific retention, legal overrides the baseline.

Classification (examples)
- Public: Docs intended for public consumption.
- Internal: Non-sensitive internal docs, logs with no PII.
- Confidential: Business sensitive, performance dashboards with customer identifiers.
- Sensitive/PII: Customer personal data, secrets, private keys.

Retention baseline table
- Application logs (non-PII): 90 days.
- Metrics & observability raw data: 365 days aggregated (retention at the raw sample level 90 days).
- Crash reports and incident recordings: 365 days.
- Customer PII: default retention 2 years after last active transaction or contract termination unless legal requires a different period.
- Audit logs (security, IAM): 7 years (retention required for compliance audits).

Data access and handling rules
- PII access must be restricted to named roles and require privileged access ticket.
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with KMS-managed keys; customer keys may be used in Private deployments.
- Backups: daily backups for production databases with 30-day rolling retention, longer where contracts require.

Delete and retention processes
1. Data owners file a Data Deletion Request (DDR-<product>) with scope and query.
2. Legal reviews for contractual obligations.
3. Engineering executes deletion scripts in a sandbox environment and provides proof-of-delete report.
4. Production deletion executed during maintenance window and verified by Security.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Intro: Procurement protects Redwood’s financial commitments and enables predictable vendor management. The Procurement team manages vendor contracts, POs, and payment approvals. Employee-level expenses follow the People Ops expense policy.

Approval thresholds
- <$5,000: Team lead approval (submit PRQ ticket).
- $5,000–$50,000: Procurement and Finance approval required.
- >$50,000 or multi-year commitments: VP-level approval and legal review.

Purchase steps for non-contracted buys
1. Create PRQ-<team>-<purpose> in procurement queue with justification, cost center, and vendor details.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor, validates pricing, and if needed requests vendor security questionnaire.
3. Finance issues PO after approvals.
4. Vendor onboarding (see Vendor Management checklist) prior to going-live.

Expense policy highlights (employee reimbursements)
- Reimbursable timeframe: submit within 60 days of expense date.
- Meal per diem: domestic $70/day; international per diem follows government guidance and must be pre-approved.
- Lodging: reasonable economy/business class for customer meetings; upgrades require justification and Director approval.
- Personal expenses will be denied (e.g., minibar charges).

Procurement SLA targets
- Standard requests under $5k: 5 business days.
- $5k–$50k: 10–15 business days depending on vendor response.
- >$50k: variable; procurement will provide an estimated timeline within 3 business days.

5) Vendor Management
Intro: Vendors that access Redwood systems or customer data must go through Vendor Risk and Onboarding. The goal is to reduce operational, security, and contractual risk.

Onboarding checklist (minimum)
- Completed Vendor Intake form with contract term, contact points, and scope.
- Security questionnaire (SIG or equivalent) completed and scored by Security.
- Contract with liability clauses and data processing addendum (DPA) where applicable.
- SLA definitions: uptime targets, support windows, escalation contacts, and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Access model: least privilege, time-bound credentials, and visibility in vendor inventory.

Vendor SLA & KPIs (recommended defaults)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for core infra vendors; for non-critical SaaS, negotiable.
- Response: 4-hour acknowledgement for Severity-1 incidents; 24-hour initial response for Severity-3.
- Security: annual penetration test report or SOC2 Type II preferred for vendors handling PII.

Periodic review and offboarding
- Quarterly: procurement tracks vendor spend and risk flags.
- Annual: security re-evaluation for vendors with access to PII.
- Offboarding steps: revoke credentials, certify data returns or deletion, and close vendor record in procurement system.

6) Travel and Remote Work Expenses
Intro: Travel must align with business need and minimize cost. People Ops approves travel and maintains travel booking partners.

Pre-approval and timelines
- Domestic travel: team lead approval at least 5 business days before travel.
- International travel: People Ops and manager approval at least 15 business days before travel (visa timelines may require more lead time).

Airfare and lodging guidance
- Air: economy or basic economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or coach-plus for flights over 6 hours with Director pre-approval for upgrades.
- Hotel: business-standard hotels; avoid extended-stay unless meeting multi-day onsite requirements.

Safety and duty of care
- People Ops maintains emergency contact lists and travel insurance guidance.
- Employees traveling to regions with security advisories must register with People Ops and receive manager approval.

7) Templates and Reusable Artifacts
Intro: Below are the canonical templates teams must use. These reduce review friction and ensure consistent evidence for audits. Each template is available in the central Templates library (link in related pages).

Access Request (sample fields)
- Title: ACCESS-<team>-<purpose>
- Requester: name + employee id
- Business owner: name + team
- Access type: standard | privileged | emergency
- Resources requested: list with exact identifiers (e.g., vault://secrets/production)
- Duration: start and end date (default 90 days for privileged)
- Justification: business impact if denied

Change Request RFC (short)
- Title and owner
- Summary of change
- Impacted services and customer impact
- Test plan and rollback steps
- Canary schedule and success metrics
- Approval checklist (peer, ops, security, legal if applicable)

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (sample)
- Intake form link: [procurement intake]
- Security questionnaire: attached
- Contract signed: yes/no
- PO created: yes/no
- Access assigned: list resources and expiration
- SLA recorded in vendor portal: yes/no

Expense Reimbursement Form (required fields)
- Employee name, ID, cost center
- Date(s) of expense
- Merchant and expense category (travel/meal/lodging/supplies)
- Amount and currency
- Receipt attachment (required for >$25)
- Approval chain (manager, finance)

8) Audit, Exceptions, and Continuous Improvement
- Exceptions: submit Risk Exception Form with justification; CFO + Security approve exceptions >90 days. All exceptions must have a renewal date.
- Audits: Procurement, Security, and Finance coordinate annual internal audits. Audit findings get tracked in the Audit Tracker and assigned remediation owners.
- Continuous improvement: A cross-functional Ops Review committee meets monthly to triage policy gaps, implement improvements, and publish quarterly updates to this handbook.

Quick reference table (decision thresholds)
- Access standard SLA: 3 business days | privileged SLA: 5 business days | emergency: 1 hour
- Procurement approval: < $5k team lead | $5k–$50k procurement+finance | >$50k VP+legal
- Change review: standard (peer), significant (48 hours), major (7 business days)
- Data retention baseline: logs 90d | metrics aggregated 365d | audit logs 7y | customer PII default 2y

Contact and support
- Primary policy contact: finance-policy@redwood.com
- Procurement queue: prq@redwood.com (PRQ- prefix in Jira)
- Access requests: access-requests@redwood.com (ACCESS- prefix)
- Security escalations: security-oncall@pager.redwood.com

Appendix: Example CLI snippets
- Create a privileged access ticket (example):
  curl -X POST https://jira.redwood.internal/rest/api/2/issue -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"fields": {"project":{"key":"ACCESS"}, "summary":"Request privileged DB access - analytics", "issuetype":{"name":"Task"}, "description":"Requester: Priya Shah\\nBusiness owner: Marcus Leung\\nResources: db-prod.redwood:analytics\\nDuration: 90 days"}}'

- Sample deletion proof-of-delete output (format):
  deleted_records: 12345
  query: "DELETE FROM events WHERE created_at < '2023-01-01' AND team = 'alpha'"
  executed_by: automation-deleter-02
  timestamp: 2025-09-12T02:34:00Z

Revision history
- 2025-06-12 (Priya Shah): Initial draft and baseline thresholds published.
- 2025-10-04 (Marcus Leung): Added Emergency Access flow and tightened privileged request SLA.
- 2026-02-18 (Priya Shah): Updated procurement thresholds and travel per diem rates; clarified data retention baseline.

End of document
