payload.page_title: Authorization Patterns and Financial Guardrails — Company Ops Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines company-wide operational patterns for authorization, purchasing and expense guardrails, change control, data classification and retention, vendor onboarding, and business travel rules. The objective is to enable efficient day-to-day operations while preserving risk controls, auditability, and predictable approval paths.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors with company accounts, and business units that initiate procurement, vendor relationships, or system changes. Exceptions are handled through the Exceptions process (see Governance).

Principles

- Least privilege for systems and data; role-based access where possible.
- Separation of duties for approvals over financial thresholds.
- Time-bound access and documented justification for elevated permissions.
- Proportional vendor review based on risk and spend.
- Clear SLOs for access and procurement workflows to reduce operational friction.

1) Access & Permissions

Goal: Fast, auditable access provisioning with risk-calibrated approvals.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requestor: Submits access request with business justification and expected duration.
- Manager: Verifies job need and approves low-medium risk requests.
- System Owner (service owner): Confirms access scope and approves.
- InfoSec: Approves access to Confidential/Restricted data or privileged infra.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Low-risk (read-only, public/internal data): fulfillment SLO 24 business hours.
- Medium-risk (write permissions, non-production infra): fulfillment SLO 48 business hours.
- High-risk (production admin, Confidential/Restricted data): fulfillment SLO 72 business hours + InfoSec review.
- Emergency access: documented emergency request, <8 hours review window; must be revoked and post-reviewed within 3 business days.
sections.heading: Access classification and SLOs

sections.body:
1. Developer requests read access to analytics dashboard (Low-risk) -> Manager approve -> Automated provisioning.
2. SRE requests production kube-admin (High-risk) -> Manager + System Owner + InfoSec -> Time-limited token via PAM.
sections.heading: Approval paths (examples)

sections.body:
- Role templates: use pre-defined role templates (engineering-read, engineering-write, infra-operator) to minimize bespoke grants.
- Time-boxed grants: default 30 days for temporary elevated access unless extended with renewed justification.
- PAM integration: all production admin activity must go through privileged access management tooling with session recording where available.

2) Change Management

Purpose: Control risk from code, infra, and configuration changes while enabling frequent safe delivery.
sections.heading: Provisioning patterns

sections.body:
- Standard (pre-authorized routine changes): scheduled, low impact. No CAB approval required.
- Normal (non-emergency changes): require change ticket, testing evidence, and CAB review for higher-risk changes.
- Emergency: expedited review path; post-implementation review mandatory.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
1. Create change ticket in Jira with owner, rollback plan, test artifacts, and monitoring playbook.
2. Run automated pre-flight checks (unit tests, integration smoke, canary gates).
3. If categorized Normal and impact > medium, include CAB review. CAB meets weekly; emergency CAB convenes ad-hoc.
4. Implement staged rollout: dev -> canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks and automatic rollback on failure thresholds.
sections.heading: Process

sections.body:
- Any change that impacts data classification boundaries (e.g., changes to KMS usage, S3 bucket ACLs) requires Security sign-off.
- Rollback trigger: >1% error rate increase sustained for 5 minutes, or >25% latency regression for two consecutive monitoring windows.

3) Data Management
sections.heading: Risk thresholds and gating

sections.body:
- PUBLIC: intended for public release. No special controls.
- INTERNAL: company-internal information; avoid public disclosure.
- CONFIDENTIAL: personal data, customer data, PII, sensitive business info. Requires encryption at rest and in transit.
- RESTRICTED: highest-risk material (regulated financial records, legal investigations, unreleased M&A data). Access by explicit approval only.
sections.heading: Classification levels

sections.body:
- HR records: 7 years (HR must request archive with retention justification).
- Financial records: 7 years for audit.
- Product telemetry: default 1 year unless product team declares longer retention for analytics (requires Data Steward approval).
- Backups and logs: 90 days hot, 2 years cold archive unless restricted by regulatory requirements.
sections.heading: Retention & archival

sections.body:
- All CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest using company KMS.
- Customer keys (where offered) must be managed via customer-provided KMS or HSM integration.
sections.heading: Encryption & keys

sections.body: - Default storage is in approved cloud regions (US, EU regions listed in the region whitelist). Transfers outside approved regions require Data Steward sign-off and legal review.
sections.heading: Data movement and allowed regions

sections.body:
- All accesses to CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data must be logged and retained for at least 2 years for audit.

4) Procurement & Expenses
sections.heading: Data access auditability

sections.body:
- <$2,500: Card purchase or manager approval.
- $2,500–$25,000: Manager + Finance team approval (purchase request in procurement system).
- $25,001–$250,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement team + Legal (contract review).
- >$250,000: Executive sponsor sign-off (VP/Head) + Procurement + Legal + Finance.
sections.heading: Approval matrix (monetary thresholds)

sections.body:
1. Complete Purchase Request form with business justification, supplier, SOW/quote, expected dates.
2. Procurement evaluates supplier risk and competitive alternatives.
3. Legal reviews contracts for liabilities, IP, and data protection clauses.
4. Finance approves budget and issues PO.
sections.heading: Procurement steps

sections.body:
- Standard invoice terms: net 30 unless negotiated.
- Finance will not process invoices without matching PO and receiving confirmation unless pre-approved.
- For subscriptions, vendor must provide annual SOW and renewal notice 60 days before renewal.
sections.heading: Payment and invoicing

sections.body:
- Personal card reimbursements: submit receipts within 30 days; expenses older than 90 days require justification and may be declined.
- Per-diem: domestic $75/day for meals, international $85/day unless local per-diem schedule applies.
- Lodging caps: domestic standard rate $250/night, high-cost market (SF, NYC, LON) cap $350/night with manager pre-approval.
- Ground transportation: preference for ride-share or public transit when practical; car rentals require justification.

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Tier 1 (Low-risk, < $25k annual): standard onboarding, SIG-Lite questionnaire.
- Tier 2 (Medium-risk, $25k–$250k or access to INTERNAL/CONFIDENTIAL data): full security questionnaire, basic financial viability check, contract review.
- Tier 3 (High-risk, > $250k or access to RESTRICTED data): SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, penetration test evidence, security addendum, and board-level review for strategic vendors.
sections.heading: Risk tiers and review requirements

sections.body:
1. Business Sponsor submits Vendor Intake form (name, scope, expected spend, data types).
2. Procurement assigns risk tier and issues vendor questionnaire.
3. Security evaluates responses; request additional controls if necessary.
4. Legal negotiates contract and SOW.
5. Procurement issues PO and records vendor in vendor registry.
6. Vendor access provisioning is time-limited and monitored; credentials are rotated on a schedule.
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist

sections.body:
- Standard data processing agreement (DPA) mandatory for any vendor processing personal or customer data.
- Insurance: minimum commercial general liability and cyber insurance coverage required for Tier 2+.
sections.heading: Contractual guardrails

sections.body:
- At contract termination: procurement triggers offboarding checklist including account termination, data return/destruction certification, and license revocation.

6) Travel Policy & Expense Templates
sections.heading: Offboarding

sections.body:
- Travel must be booked with corporate travel portal or approved agency for insurance coverage.
- International travel requires manager and Security brief for high-risk countries (see travel whitelist/blacklist).
sections.heading: Booking and approvals

sections.body:
- Submit expenses within 30 days of travel completion. Finance reviews and processes within 10 business days after submission when complete.

Personal travel combined with business: must clearly separate business expenses and non-reimbursable personal costs.
sections.heading: Expense submission cadence

sections.body:
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency assistance for approved business travel.
- Travelers must register trips with Security prior to departure for visits to high-risk regions.

7) Templates and Forms (links)

- Access Request Form: /confluence/templates/access-request-form (use this for all access grants).
- Purchase Request Form: /confluence/templates/purchase-request-form (mandatory for > $2,500).
- Vendor Intake & Risk Assessment: /confluence/templates/vendor-intake-risk.

- Travel Expense Template: /confluence/templates/travel-expense-template
- Change Ticket Template (Jira): project=CHG, include fields: owner, rollback plan, health-checks, monitoring links.

8) Governance, Ownership and Exceptions
sections.heading: Travel safety & insurance

sections.body:
- Finance owns procurement policies and approval matrix maintenance.
- Security owns data classification, KMS policies and vendor security requirements.
- People-ops and Legal support travel and contract policies respectively.
sections.heading: Ownership

sections.body:
- Submit an Exception Request with rationale, compensating controls, duration, and owner.
- Exceptions are reviewed by a cross-functional committee monthly. High-risk exceptions (>90 days or involving RESTRICTED data) require executive sponsor and Legal approval.
sections.heading: Exception process

sections.body:
- Quarterly audits of procurement spend against PO compliance.
- Annual vendor risk re-assessment for Tier 2/3 vendors.
- Post-incident reviews are required for any access, change, or vendor incident impacting Confidential/Restricted data.

Appendix: Quick-reference tables
sections.heading: Audit and continuous improvement

sections.body:
| Amount | Approver chain | Notes |
|-------:|----------------|-------|
| <$2,500 | Manager | Card purchase allowed |
| $2,500–$25,000 | Manager + Finance | PO recommended |
| $25,001–$250,000 | Manager + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Contract review required |
| >$250,000 | Exec sponsor + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Board-level approval for strategic spend possible |
sections.heading: Monetary approval quick table

sections.body:
- PUBLIC: no controls
- INTERNAL: RBAC + audit logs
- CONFIDENTIAL: Encryption + KMS + logging
- RESTRICTED: Explicit approval + limited audience + legal oversight

Contact and escalation
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Finance: finance@redwood.example.com
- InfoSec: security@redwood.example.com
- Security Operations (urgent): #sec-ops or pager on-call

Revision history
- 2024-10-21: Created by Sofia Alvarez.
- 2024-11-30: Updated approvals and onboarding checklist after procurement retrospective.
- 2025-01-18: Added travel per-diem caps and updated vendor tier thresholds.

Notes
- This playbook is intended to be a living document. Teams should propose changes via PR into the policies repository or by filing a Governance suggestion in the PULSE board.

payload.page_title: Access Provisioning and Spend Journeys (Company Playbook)

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook centralizes company-wide routines for: access and permissions, change control, data handling, procurement and expense requests, vendor onboarding, and travel approvals. It is intended for requestors, approvers, finance, security, and operations teams.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors that require systems access, make purchases on behalf of Redwood, or manage configuration changes to production or corporate systems. Exceptions must be approved by Finance + Security.

Principles (short)
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required.
- Clear ownership: every access/expense/change has a named owner.
- Auditability: decisions and artifacts are retained for 3 years (longer for regulated customers).
- Separation of duties: requester ≠ approver for material spend and production changes.
- Risk-based controls: higher-risk assets require additional validation.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Requestor: submits request with business justification and expiry.
- Approver: validates business need and policy compliance.
- Provisioner: implements the access, change or purchase. For infra changes, this is the engineering owner.
- Finance: validates budget and PO requirement for purchases > $5,000.
- Security: performs risk review for access to sensitive assets (PCI/PHI/Customer PII).
- Vendor Ops: manages supplier onboarding and contract records.

1) Access & Permissions: request-to-provision workflow
A. Access categories
- Standard internal apps: Google Workspace, Slack, Okta-managed SSO apps.
- Sensitive systems: production clusters, customer data stores, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
- Service accounts and API keys

B. Request flow (numbered steps)
1. Requestor fills the Access Request form in the internal portal. Required fields: owner, justification, asset identifier (service name), role, required duration, and risk notes.
2. Automated validation: system checks manager alignment, existing approvals, and if request touches sensitive assets.
3. Approver(s) notified: manager for standard access; manager + security for sensitive. Approvals are timeboxed to 48 hours.
4. Provisioner executes via IaC or identity provider. Provisioning must include an audit tag: "provisioned_by=<engineer>" and expiry metadata.
5. Post-provision review: owner confirms least-privilege within 7 days.
6. Revocation: requests with duration automatically expire; ad-hoc revocations are processed within 4 business hours for sensitive assets.

C. Example Access Request JSON (for integration):
{
  "request_id": "REQ-2026-0123",
  "requestor": "alice@example.com",
  "asset": "redwood-prod-cluster-3",
  "role": "read-only",
  "justification": "Support ticket #45121 - debug customer issue",
  "expiry": "2026-03-31"
}

D. Minimum approval matrix (table as text)
- Manager approval: any standard internal app.
- Manager + Security: access to customer data, KMS, or production write access.
- Manager + Security + Infra Eng lead: service accounts, long-lived keys (>90 days), or configuration write for core infra.

E. Access reviews
- Quarterly automated recertification for all roles.
- Monthly manual review for owners of assets classified high or critical.

2) Change Management (applies to infra and critical apps)
A. Change types
- Routine (low risk): config changes with no customer impact.
- Standard (planned): scheduled deploys within existing CI/CD gates.
- Emergency: rollbacks or fixes for live incidents.

B. Change lifecycle (numbered)
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) in the change tracker. Include: impact statement, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, and approver list.
2. Risk assessment: automated scoring based on affected services, blast radius, and user counts. Score > 7 requires Security + SRE signoff.
3. Approval: standard changes require SRE or owning eng manager; high-risk changes require cross-team approval and a canary plan.
4. Execution: operator runs the change following the runbook (include CLI snippets or playbook links).
5. Post-deploy verification: health checks and metric baselines for 60 minutes; if deviations exceed thresholds (5% traffic error rate increase or 30% latency tail degradation), initiate rollback.
6. Post-change review: update CR with lessons learned within 3 business days.

C. Emergency changes
- Emergency changes may bypass normal lead times but must be documented in the tracker within 24 hours and reviewed by the incident review board within 72 hours.

3) Data Management (classification & retention)
A. Classification levels
- Public: safe to publish externally.
- Internal: company-only, low sensitivity.
- Confidential: product roadmaps, non-public contracts.
- Restricted: customer PII/PHI, payment data — requires encryption at rest, access controls, audit logs.

B. Retention & deletion
- Default retention: documents and logs - 3 years.
- Customer PII/PHI: retention per contract or legal requirement; ensure secure deletion procedures and certs of destruction.

C. Data handling rules
- No customer data in personal devices or uncontrolled cloud storage.
- Use approved S3 buckets with encryption-and-logging policy for backups.

4) Procurement & Expenses
A. Purchase thresholds and approvals (table as text)
- <= $500: Manager approval.
- $501–$5,000: Manager + Finance cost center approval.
- > $5,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement (PO required).
- > $50,000: Procurement lead + Legal + Finance (contract & SLAs required).

B. Request-to-purchase flow (numbered)
1. Submit Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement portal with business justification, vendor, estimated cost, and budget code.
2. Finance validates budget availability within 2 business days.
3. Procurement reviews vendor terms and recommends PO or contract.
4. Once approved, Procurement issues a PO and Finance arranges payment terms.

C. Expense reporting and travel
- All expenses recorded within 10 business days of transaction. Receipts required for any expense > $25.
- Corporate card use: allowed for approved subscriptions and travel only. Disputes to be raised within 30 days.

5) Vendor Management
A. Onboarding checklist (numbered)
1. Vendor risk classification (low/medium/high) based on access and data processing.
2. Security questionnaire and evidence collection (SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports as relevant).
3. Contract template with data handling and breach notification clauses; Legal review required for high-risk vendors.
4. Technical integration: restrict network access to least-privilege IP ranges, short-lived credentials, and dedicated service accounts where possible.
5. SLA & monitoring: define uptime, support channels, escalation points, and regular review cadence.

B. Offboarding
- Revoke all credentials, confirm return or destruction of data, and archive contract artifacts. Vendor Ops must complete offboarding checklist within 5 business days.

6) Travel Policy (brief)
- Approvals: Manager pre-approval required for any travel. Trips with reimbursement > $2,000 require Finance pre-approval.
- Per-diem & limits: domestic hotel limit $250/night; international evaluated per region (Finance provides country caps).
- Booking: use corporate travel vendor where available; exceptions require manager justification.

7) Templates & Forms (links and examples)
- Access Request Form: internal portal link (use template ID: ARF-2025).
- Purchase Request Template: include vendor, justification, budget code, and anticipated SOW.
- Change Request Template: include test plan, rollback, and impact matrix.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: checklist with required evidence fields.

8) Escalation & Audit
- Escalate unresolved approval delays > 72 hours to the team director.
- Security incidents involving vendor or data must follow the Incident Response policy and be reported to Security Pager within 1 hour.
- Audit cadence: internal audit team runs an annual review; targeted audits occur after significant incidents.

9) Metrics & KPIs to monitor
- Time-to-provision (median target: 24 hours for standard apps).
- Time-to-approve purchases (median target: 3 business days).
- Quarterly access recertification completion rate (target: 95%).
- Number of emergency changes and post-change rollback rate (target rollback < 5%).

Appendices
A. Example CLI snippet to revoke an API key (for infra owners)
$ redwoodctl keys revoke --key-id=svc-abc-123 --reason="project-complete"

B. Sample approval language (copy-paste for approvers)
"I approve this request as the owner/manager. I confirm budget and business justification, and I understand the access will expire on the date specified."

C. Frequently Asked Questions (short)
Q: Who to contact for fast-track access?
A: Managers may request an expedited path; security must approve for sensitive assets. Fast-track is intended only for critical customer-impact scenarios.

D. Change history
- 2025-03-02: Playbook created (Asha Patel).
- 2025-10-15: Added vendor onboarding checklist (Priya Desai).
- 2026-02-14: Updated thresholds and revocation SLAs (Liam Torres).

References
- Incident Response (security-and-compliance/incident-response-security)
- Authorization Lifecycle (policies-and-process/authorization-lifecycle-and-procurement-patterns-2029)
- Procurement templates (policies-and-process/templates)

Contact
For questions or proposed updates, email policy-ops@redwood.ai or open a PR against the central playbook repository.

sections.body:
Overview:

This handbook centralizes company-wide procedures, approval templates, and operational checklists for core administrative processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It exists to reduce ambiguity, accelerate approvals, and ensure consistent auditing evidence for internal and external compliance reviews.

Scope:

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and temporary staff across global offices.
- Covers systems and services owned by Redwood (hosted control plane, internal admin consoles, identity providers, finance systems, contract repositories).
- Does NOT replace product-level runbooks for service incidents; see eng-sre runbooks for operational incident playbooks.

Key Definitions:

- RBAC: Role-Based Access Control.
- Approver: The role authorized to approve a request (manager, data owner, or finance approver).
- Change Window: Approved schedule during which non-emergency changes may be applied.
- Data Classification: Public / Internal / Confidential / Regulated.

1) Access & Permissions

Objective: Grant least privilege access, enforce separation of duties, and provide an auditable trail for approvals and role changes.

Policy summary:

- All access requests must be submitted through the Access Request form (Confluence link in templates).
- Default assignment model: role templates mapped to groups in our IdP (Okta).
- Elevated (admin) access requires manager + owner_team approval and a 90-day review cadence.
- Temporary access must include an expiration date; max duration by default is 30 days without additional justification.

RBAC matrix (summary):

| Role                     | Typical privileges                              | Approver required            | Review cadence |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|----------------|
| employee                | Standard product and internal tools access       | Manager                      | 12 months      |
| devops                  | Deployment pipelines, infra config read/write    | Infra owner + manager        | 3 months       |
| service-admin           | Service-level admin on specific service          | Service owner                | 90 days        |
| security-admin          | IAM, audit logs, policy edits                    | Security lead + CISO         | 90 days        |
| finance-admin           | Billing/expense systems, vendor payments         | Finance director             | 6 months       |

Access request procedure (step-by-step):

1. Submit Access Request through the Access form; include justification and expected duration.
2. Auto-notification to direct manager for approval.
3. If role is elevated, route to owner_team for second approval.
4. Provisioning is executed by automated provisioning service (Provisioner v2) after approvals are recorded.
5. The request and approval chain are archived in the Audit Log for 7 years.

Access change and removal:

- On termination or role change HR triggers automatic deprovisioning workflow via the HR -> IdP connector (target: within 4 hours).
- Managers must review their direct reports’ privileged access quarterly; exceptions documented in the quarterly-attestation template.

2) Change Management

Goal: Minimize risk from configuration and code changes while enabling predictable deployment velocity.

Change categories:

- Standard change: Low risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates, patching).
- Normal change: Requires RFC and approval (e.g., service config changes, infra instance type changes).
- Emergency change: Applied in response to an incident; must be post-facto documented within 24 hours.

RFC process (normal changes):

1. Create RFC in Change Tracker with summary, impact assessment, rollback plan, test criteria, and owners.
2. Security and SRE review for risk and operational impact.
3. Approval required from Change Board (CDO/Lead SRE + Service Owner) during weekly change board.
4. Schedule for approved Change Window and publish runbook.
5. Post-change validation and close RFC (pass/fail + metrics).

Change window and blackout periods:

- Change windows are Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00 local time except during Q4 product launches and major marketing events; teams must consult the company calendar for blackout dates.

Change rollback thresholds (examples):

- If request causes error rate > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes, initiate automatic rollback.
- If latency P50 increases by > 40% for > 10 minutes, Service Owner must evaluate rollback.

3) Data Management

Purpose: Reduce data exposure and ensure compliant handling of regulated and customer data.

Data classification policy:

- Public: Information intended for public release.
- Internal: Operational and non-sensitive business data.
- Confidential: Employee PII, customer metadata, non-public financials.
- Regulated: Data subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., EU personal data, healthcare).

Handling rules (high level):

- All Regulated or Confidential data must be stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.3).
- Production datasets with PII require a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and explicit data owner sign-off prior to sharing.
- Minimum necessary principle: copies and exports must be limited and logged.

Retention and deletion:

- Default retention: logs 1 year, analytics 3 years, financial records 7 years.
- Data destruction must follow the Secure Deletion checklist and be signed off by data owner.

Data access reviews and audits:

- Data owners must conduct access reviews every 6 months.
- All data access to regulated datasets requires Just-In-Time (JIT) approval and session recording for auditable access.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Objective: Standardize purchasing and expense approvals to control spend and maintain vendor compliance.

Approval thresholds (functional summary):

- <$2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance lead approval.
- >$25,000: Director-level approval + procurement review; >$100,000 requires exec sponsor.

Procurement process (recommended):

1. For recurring SaaS or one-off purchases, create a Purchase Request in the Procurement system with business justification, vendor, estimated cost, and GL code.
2. Finance validates budget and requests competitive bid if > $25k (min 2 bids).
3. Legal conducts contract review for vendor agreements storing data or providing cloud services.
4. Procurement issues PO; Finance schedules payment terms and coding.

Expenses policy highlights:

- Reimbursements within 30 days via Expensifier; receipts required for any claim >$25.
- Per diem for travel (see Travel section) or actuals with receipts.
- Corporate cards to be used per-corporate-card SOP; misuse may lead to remediation or loss of card privileges.

5) Vendor Management

Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, continuity, and contractual expectations.

Vendor lifecycle stages:

- Intake and classification: Technical/non-technical, data handling level, and risk category (low/medium/high).
- Security review: Questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ or vendor-specific) and control mapping.
- Contracting: Standard contract templates; include SLAs, indemnities, data handling, and termination clauses.
- Onboarding: Credentials, contacts, escalation paths, and SSO where possible.
- Ongoing monitoring: Quarterly performance & security reviews for high-risk vendors.

Vendor SLA baseline (recommended):

| Vendor risk | Uptime SLA | Security artifacts | Review cadence |
|------------|-----------:|-------------------|----------------:|
| Low        | N/A        | Basic questionnaire | Annual        |
| Medium     | 99.5%      | SOC2 Type II or equivalent | Semi-annual |
| High       | 99.9%      | SOC2 + penetration test | Quarterly     |

Termination and offboarding:

- Offboarding checklist: credential revocation, data return or certified deletion, final invoice reconciliation, and closure confirmation.
- Data escrow: required for strategic vendors where data continuity risk exists.

6) Travel Policy

Objectives: Keep travel purposeful, minimize cost variance, and protect employee safety.

Booking and approvals:

- Domestic travel requires manager pre-approval for trips >1 night.
- International travel requires manager + People Ops pre-approval; consult travel risk guidance.
- Preferred vendors and negotiated rates should be used where available.

Allowed spend & per diems (summary):

- Air: economy coach for trips <6 hours; premium economy or business requires director-level approval.
- Hotels: mid-range business hotels. Maximum nightly rate guidance by city in the Travel Rate Card (attached).
- Meals: Per diem tiered by location; itemized receipts required for expense claims >$75.

Safety and emergency protocol:

- Employees traveling internationally must register trip details with People Ops and have access to emergency contact numbers.
- In evacuations or geopolitical escalations, follow the People Ops crisis procedures.

7) Internal Templates & Forms

Included templates (attached in Confluence as page attachments):

- Access Request (form)
- Change RFC Template (with risk table and rollback plan)
- Data Sharing Agreement checklist
- Purchase Request and PO template
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (vendor-questionnaire-template.docx)
- Travel pre-approval and expense claim form

8) Roles & Responsibilities

- People Ops: Governance for employee lifecycle, travel approvals, termination flows.
- Finance & Procurement: Budget validation, PO issuance, vendor payments, expense policy enforcement.
- Security & Compliance: Data classification guidance, vendor security reviews, and access audits.
- Service Owners: Approve changes, own runbooks, and sign off on access to service-level admin roles.

9) Escalation & Audit Trails

- All policy exceptions must be requested via the Exceptions form and require an owner_team sponsor + Security/Finance sign-off. Exceptions are time-boxed and expire unless renewed.
- Audit logs for access, provisioning, procurement, and change approvals are retained according to retention schedule and available for compliance review.

10) Appendix: Example forms and checklists

- Quick checklist: New vendor onboarding (10 steps) — intake, classification, questionnaire, contract, SSO, test integration, SLA confirmation, billing setup, data transfer method, monitoring schedule, offboarding plan.
- Change RFC quick test cases: include a smoke test command, validation query examples, and rollback command snippets.

Smoke test example (pseudo-CLI):

- curl -sS https://internal-status.redwood/api/v1/health | jq .service_status
- run perf-check --target service-x --p50-threshold 200ms --max-tokens 512

Document governance and revision history:

- This manual is owned by People Ops. Major revisions require cross-functional review (Security, Finance, Legal, and Product as needed).
- Revision log: 2024-11-02 Initial publication; 2025-06-18 Updated procurement thresholds and travel rate card locations.

Contact & ownership:

- Primary owner: Maya Patel (People Ops) — maya.patel@redwood.ai
- Security reviewer: Ethan Chen — ethan.chen@redwood.ai
- Finance reviewer: Sofia Martinez — sofia.martinez@redwood.ai

Related references:

- See also: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build for change pipeline guidance; /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging for log retention details.

sections.body:
Summary

This page is the company-wide reference for core operational guardrails and common workflows (Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel policy, and internal templates). It consolidates decision criteria, approval thresholds, roles, and step-by-step procedures so teams can operate consistently while enabling rapid product delivery. Use this hub as the canonical source for operational patterns; for team-specific deviations request an exception (see Governance & Exceptions).

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Covers cross-functional processes that impact security, finance, or customer data.
- Does not replace product-team implementation guides; it standardizes approvals, controls, and handoffs.

Principles

1. Least privilege by default: grant only the access necessary for a defined task and duration.
2. Clear separation of duties: custody (people who operate) vs. control (people who approve).
3. Risk-based approvals: higher risk requires more stringent approval paths.
4. Auditability and traceability: all requests must be recorded in the authoritative workflow system.
5. Continuous improvement: metrics collected for bottlenecks and policy tuning.

Key Roles and Owners

- Requestor: the employee initiating an action (access request, change, purchase, travel).
- Approver: person with delegated authority to approve based on thresholds (manager, finance approver, security reviewer).
- Owner Team: team responsible for operating a service or dataset (documented in service catalog).
- Control Owner: centralized team accountable for the policy (Finance & Legal for procurement; Security for access; Data Governance for data policies).
- Approvals Admin: platform team that maintains forms and workflows (IT/Platform).

Access and Permissions

Overview
- Access is managed centrally via the identity provider (IdP) and group memberships. Privileged access (production, PII datasets, KMS) requires additional approvals and periodic recertification.

Access Tiers and Approval Requirements

| Tier | Target Resources | Approval Path | Duration | Recertification |
|------|------------------|---------------|----------|----------------|
| Tier 1 (Standard) | Corporate apps (email, wiki, Slack) | Manager | 1 year auto-expiry | Annual manager recert |
| Tier 2 (Privileged) | Production consoles, deploy pipelines | Manager + Service Owner | 90 days | Quarterly recert by service owner |
| Tier 3 (Sensitive) | PII datasets, KMS, private customer environments | Manager + Service Owner + Security | 30 days | Monthly recert + audit |

Request Workflow (Access)

1. Requestor opens the Access Request form in the IT portal and selects resource and tier.
2. Automated checks run (manager mapping, MFA status, current memberships).
3. Approver(s) review in-place; approvers must add justification when granting Tier 2/3.
4. Provisioning webhook updates group membership in IdP; provisioning logs appended to audit store.
5. Expiry reminder sent 14 days before expiration; auto-remediate if not recertified.

Change Management

Purpose
- Ensure safe, auditable changes to production systems while enabling rapid delivery. Changes are categorized by risk and must follow an approval and rollout plan.

Change Categories and Gates

- Standard Change: low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config tweaks, security patching windows).
- Minor Change: single-service change; requires Service Owner sign-off and smoke tests.
- Major Change: cross-service or customer-impacting; requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) review and rollback plan.
- Emergency Change: must follow Emergency CAB retrospective within 48 hours.

Change Process (high level)

1. Create change ticket with description, scope, rollout plan, backout procedure, monitoring plan, and owner.
2. Automated risk scoring computes initial category (based on blast radius, data sensitivity, customer impact).
3. If Major, schedule CAB and notify stakeholders; Minor and Standard follow simplified approval.
4. Execute in an approved window; monitor metrics and error budgets.
5. Complete post-deploy checklist and link to deployment artifact.

Data Management

Guiding Policies
- Data classification: All data must be labeled (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted).
- Data access control maps to classification. Sensitive or Restricted data requires explicit data access request and auditing.
- Backups and retention schedules are defined per dataset owner.

Data Handling Checklist

- Verify classification and legal constraints.
- Ensure encryption at-rest and in-transit for Confidential/Restricted.
- Confirm retention policy and data deletion process.
- Log access and set alerts for anomalous access patterns.

Procurement & Expenses

Purchase Thresholds and Approvals

| Amount (USD) | Approval Required | Procurement Involvement |
|--------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| <= 1,000 | Manager | No vendor setup required |
| 1,001 - 25,000 | Manager + Finance Approver | Procurement validates T&Cs |
| > 25,000 | Manager + Finance Director + Legal | Procurement-led RFP / Contract review |

Preferred Procurement Flow

1. Use the Purchase Request template in the approvals system.
2. Attach quotes, justification, and budget code.
3. Procurement validates vendor, tax status, and standard contract requirements.
4. Finance issues PO; vendor onboarding collects W-9 / VAT details and security questionnaire as applicable.

Expense Policy Highlights

- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days with receipts.
- Travel per-diem follows published bands; exceptions require manager + finance sign-off.
- Corporate cards are issued on manager recommendation and subject to monthly reconciliation.

Vendor Management

Onboarding Steps

1. Requestor raises Vendor Onboarding ticket with scope and contact.
2. Procurement runs vendor risk classification (Low/Medium/High).
3. High-risk vendors require security questionnaire, SOC report, and legal review.
4. Contract sign-off tracked in central contract repository with expiration reminders.

Ongoing Vendor Controls

- Quarterly review for high-risk vendors.
- SLAs and escalation paths documented in the contract.
- Access for vendor employees follows Tier 2/3 approval paths; vendor accounts are time-limited.

Travel Policy (Business Travel)

Booking and Approvals
- Travel must be pre-approved in the Travel Request form. Approvals require manager sign-off and travel budget confirmation.
- Preferred booking channels (partner travel portal) should be used for corporate rates and insurance coverage.

Expenses and Safety
- Employees are expected to follow lowest reasonable cost standards consistent with safety and schedule.
- Emergency travel deviations require post-hoc manager and finance approval.

Templates and Reference Forms

- Access Request (IT Portal): fields: requestor, resource, justification, tier, duration, manager, service owner.
- Purchase Request (Finance Form): fields: requestor, vendor, amount, budget center, quotes, approver chain.
- Vendor Risk Questionnaire (link): short-form and long-form variants.
- Travel Request Form: destination, dates, purpose, budget code, approver.

Example: Minimal Purchase Request JSON (copy into Purchase Request form if using API)

{
  "requestor": "name@example.com",
  "vendor": "Acme Cloud Services",
  "amount_usd": "7500",
  "budget_code": "ENG-OPS-2026",
  "justification": "Reserved capacity for Q2 load testing",
  "approvers": ["manager@example.com", "finance-approver@example.com"]
}

Governance & Exceptions

- Requests for policy exceptions must be submitted to the Control Owner via the Exception Request form and include compensating controls, risk assessment, and expiry date.
- Exceptions are reviewed monthly by a cross-functional panel (Security, Finance, Legal, Requesting Team).

Metrics and SLAs for the Hub

- Target approval times: Access Tier 1 = 24 hours, Tier 2 = 3 business days, Tier 3 = 5 business days.
- Procurement turnaround: <= 5 business days for <= $25k with complete docs.
- Vendor onboarding for high-risk vendors: target 30 days.

Operational Runbooks (Quick Links)

- Access: How to request access, how to recertify, emergency access escalation.
- Change: CAB scheduling, template for postmortem and rollbacks.
- Procurement: How to run an RFP and attach contracts.
- Vendor: Onboarding checklist and sample SLA contract clauses.

Retention and Audit

- All approvals, change tickets, vendor contracts, and travel approvals are retained per the retention catalog (default 7 years for contracts and financial artifacts; 3 years for routine change tickets).
- Audit logs for access and data access are stored in the centralized audit store with immutable retention.

How to Use This Hub

1. Start with the relevant template linked from the Templates section.
2. Follow the workflow steps and attach required artifacts.
3. If uncertain about risk classification, contact the Control Owner (Finance & Legal for procurement or Security for access).

Appendix: Quick Approval Matrix (human-readable)

- Low-risk access & purchases: manager-only approval.
- Medium-risk (service-impacting or > $1k): manager + functional approver.
- High-risk (PII/KMS or > $25k): manager + finance director + legal + security as applicable.

Contact and Escalation

- Finance & Legal (Control Owner for procurement): finance-legal@redwood.com
- Security (Control Owner for privileged access): security-ops@redwood.com
- Platform & IT (workflows & templates): platform-it@redwood.com

Related artifacts and downloads

- Purchase Request template (embedded).
- Vendor questionnaire (PDF).
- Access recertification playbook (runbook link).

Change log

- 2025-03-12: Created by Asha Menon.
- 2025-11-05: Procurement approval thresholds updated (Finance).
- 2026-02-20: Added Tier 3 access recertification cadence and sample JSON for Purchase Request.

payload.page_title: Unified Access, Change, and Procurement Manual

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This manual consolidates core company-wide processes that span access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy touchpoints, and common internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for cross-functional operators (engineering, security, finance, and people-ops) to coordinate low-friction, auditable, and compliant workflows.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems.
- Covers lifecycle of requests: request -> approval -> fulfillment -> audit / revoke.
- Excludes specialized procedures documented on team-level pages (e.g., onprem packaging runbooks).

How to use this document
------------------------
- Follow the numbered processes for operational tasks.
- Use templates in Section "Library: Templates" for consistent submissions.
- Raise exceptions via the Risk & Exceptions flow (see "Related pages").

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
| Process | Primary owner | SLA (target) | Escalation owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & permissions (standard) | IAM Platform | 48 business hours | Security Oncall |
| Emergency access (break-glass) | Security | immediate (0–2 hours) | SRE Lead |
| Change approvals (non-prod) | Engineering Change Board | 72 hours | Eng Platform Manager |
| Change approvals (prod) | Change Advisory Board (CAB) | 5 business days | CTO Office |
| Procurement (standard) | Procurement / Finance | 5 business days | Head of Finance |
| Vendor onboarding | Vendor Management | 7 business days | Legal Counsel |
| Expense reimbursements | Finance | 5 business days after submission | Finance Ops Lead |

1) Access & Permissions
-----------------------
Intro: Access requests should follow least-privilege principles. Roles are used where possible; adhoc grants must be timeboxed. All requests must include business justification and expiry.

Access classification
- Role-based: Preferred for services and groups (e.g., "redwood-data-analysts").
- Scoped token: Short-lived tokens for CI/CD jobs with automated rotation.
- Temporary elevation: Emergency / break-glass with audit.

Standard request flow (non-emergency)
1. User submits Access Request via the Access Portal (link: /confluence/eng-infra/access-portal). Include: resource, role, justification, org owner.
2. IAM Platform validates request (owner contact check).
3. Approver (owner_team lead) approves or rejects.
4. IAM Platform fulfills and assigns expiry (default 30 days for temporary requests).
5. Automated audit entry created in Audit Log stream.

Emergency (break-glass)
1. User requests emergency token via Security Slack channel + short form.
2. Security grants short-lived token (1 hour) and notifies CAB.
3. Post-incident: owner files retrospective and either approves extension or revokes.

RBAC examples and CLI snippets
- Grant role: redwoodctl iam grant --user priya.kapoor@redwood.ai --role redwood-data-analyst --resource dataset:traffic-logs
- Revoke role: redwoodctl iam revoke --user alice@redwood.ai --role redwood-maintainer

Access review cadence
- Quarterly review for high-privilege roles (SLA: 14 days to remediate mismatches).
- Annual org-wide certification for contractors.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Principles
- Changes are categorized by risk: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, EMERGENCY.
- Changes must include test plan, rollback plan, and observability signals.
- Production-facing changes require CAB approval; non-prod changes follow lightweight review.

Change request template (YAML example)
---
title: "upgrade-runtime-kernel-2026-02"
owner: "eng-platform"
category: "PROD"
risk: "MEDIUM"
planned_window: "2026-02-15T02:00:00Z/2026-02-15T04:00:00Z"
rollback_plan: |
  1) Disable new kernel via flag
  2) Redeploy previous image from tag v1.12.3
test_plan: |
  - end-to-end smoke: 100 requests/min for 15 minutes
observability: |
  - latency p95 < 200ms; error rate < 1%
---

Standard change workflow
1. Create change request in the Change Tracker with attached runbook and test artifacts.
2. Peer review and automated CI verification.
3. CAB reviews HIGH/PROD changes; non-PROD can be approved by owner.
4. Schedule during approved windows; notify affected teams.
5. Execute, monitor metrics and rollback if thresholds breached.
6. Post-change review within 5 business days.

Rollback thresholds (examples)
- Latency p95 increases by >2x for 5 minutes -> initiate rollback.
- Error rate >3% sustained for >2 min -> rollback.

3) Data Management
------------------
Classification levels
- PUBLIC: safe for external disclosure.
- INTERNAL: business data that is non-sensitive.
- CONFIDENTIAL: PII, model weights, customer data. Access requires justification, approved storage and encryption.

Storage & retention rules
- CONFIDENTIAL data must be stored in encrypted buckets with KMS-managed keys; retention default: 3 years unless contractually specified.
- Logs containing PII must be purged or redacted within 90 days.

Data handling checklist for new dataset
1. Classify dataset using Data Classification form.
2. Confirm legal/regulatory constraints with Legal.
3. Provision storage in approved project and enable server-side encryption.
4. Register dataset in the Data Catalog (link: /confluence/data-catalog).

Sample Data Classification table
| Field | Example | Classification | Storage requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user_email | alice@example.com | CONFIDENTIAL | encrypted, access limited |
| telemetry_id | abc123 | INTERNAL | review quarterly |
| model_logits | float[] | CONFIDENTIAL | store in project with key rotation |

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Principles
- Central procurement ensures contract review, cost optimization, and vendor consolidation.
- Expense policy focuses on reasonableness and receipts for reimbursement.

Procurement flow (typical)
1. Team raises Purchase Request in Procurement Portal: justification, budget code, expected vendor.
2. Procurement verifies vendor, checks existing contracts, and obtains quotes.
3. Finance approves spend against budget.
4. Legal reviews contract if > $50k or if clauses flagged.
5. Procurement issues PO and tracks delivery.

Expense submission checklist
- Submit within 30 days of expense.
- Include itemized receipt and expense category.
- Use corporate card for business travel where available.

Per diem and travel guidance (high level)
- Domestic travel: meals up to $75/day.
- International: country-specific per diem on Travel Portal.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business only with pre-approval.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Onboarding steps
1. Vendor Intake form: business case, regulatory needs, data access requirements.
2. Security assessment: fill vendor security questionnaire.
3. Contracting & SLAs: Legal drafts contract and defines SLAs and termination clauses.
4. Technical onboarding: assign minimal-access accounts and run PoC in sandbox.
5. Quarterly vendor review for strategic vendors.

Vendor risk categories & controls
- Low risk: SaaS with no customer data access. Controls: basic vendor profile and PO.
- Medium risk: vendors processing internal data. Controls: SOC2 report, contract clauses, least privilege.
- High risk: vendors accessing customer data or models. Controls: formal security assessment, encryption in transit+rest, dedicated VPC peering if required.

6) Travel Policy Highlights
--------------------------
- All work travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Portal.
- Travelers must submit expenses and trip summary within 10 business days of return.
- International travel with customer-sensitive data must consult Security for device posture.

7) Library: Templates
---------------------

payload.page_title: Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle and Procurement Alignment — Playbook and Templates

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle used at Redwood Inference and prescribes how access decisions, change management, data handling, procurement approvals, and vendor onboarding must align. The goal is to reduce blast radius, maintain auditable approvals, and ensure procurement decisions reflect operational security and least-privilege requirements.

Intended audience:
- Engineering managers and platform owners
- Security reviewers and compliance owners
- Finance and procurement teams
- People Ops for role updates and offboarding

Scope:
- All systems and services that store or process customer or internal data (hosted, dedicated, private)
- User access patterns (person, service account, CI/CD token)
- Hardware and software procurement that will be onboarded to production or private deployments

High-level Principles:
1) Least-Privilege by Default: every grant should be scoped to the minimum resource and time necessary.
2) Explicit Approval and Traceability: all requests require approver identity, business justification, and expiration.
3) Separation of Duties: procurement approvals and technical provisioning require independent reviewers.
4) Continuous Verification: periodic entitlement review, automated attestations where possible.
5) Procurement Security Gate: any vendor or purchase that touches customer data or infra must pass a security checklist before ordering.

Definitions (short):
- Entitlement: permission granted to a principal to access a resource.
- Owner: the team responsible for the resource and first point of contact for approvals.
- Sensitive Resource: any asset categorized as PII, IP, or production-infrastructure.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Requester: initiates access or procurement request with justification and expected duration.
- Resource Owner: validates technical need, selects grant scope, defines SRE/DR contact.
- Security Reviewer: evaluates the request for exposure, vendor risk, and compliance.
- Procurement/Finance Approver: verifies budget, contract terms, and vendor eligibility.
- People Ops: ensures role changes and terminations trigger entitlement revocation.

Access Lifecycle (Detailed Procedure):
1) Request Phase (Tooling: Access Portal / ServiceNow integration)
   - Requester populates: resource identifier (ARN or service name), purpose, least-privilege role, requested duration, and business justification.
   - Request must reference the ticket ID for any procurement tied to the access (e.g., new VM or external vendor account).

2) Approval Phase (two-step minimum for sensitive resources)
   - Step 1: Resource Owner approves scope & duration. For role-specific grants, the owner must select a pre-approved role template.
   - Step 2: Security Reviewer validates risk and selects compensating controls (MFA requirement, IP allowlist, monitoring hooks).
   - Step 3: Finance/Procurement approves if the access requires a new subscription, vendor account, or billed service.

3) Provisioning Phase (automation encouraged)
   - Automated provisioning preferred: IAM policy generated from templates, short-lived credentials, and audit log enablement.
   - Manual provisioning requires the provisioning engineer to attach the request ticket and record the change ID.

4) Active Use & Monitoring
   - All granted entitlements produce an audit event captured in the central logging pipeline.
   - Teams must create alerting for anomalous privilege elevation and high-volume data exports tied to newly-issued entitlements.

5) Expiration & Review
   - Every temporary grant is auto-expired at its requested end date.
   - Permanent grants must have an explicit quarterly attestation by the resource owner.
   - Annual entitlement review: owners receive the entitlement roster and must attest by the SLA date. Non-attested entitlements will be flagged for revocation.

6) Revocation & Offboarding
   - People Ops triggers revocation for terminated employees within 2 hours for production and 24 hours for non-prod.
   - For vendor contracts ending, the vendor account must be revoked and any keys rotated within 5 business days.

Change Management Intersection:
- Any change to access patterns that affects production or sensitive resources must follow the change control matrix: change category (minor/major/emergency), required approvers, rollout window, and backout plan.
- Example: Adding a new role that provides read access to billing data is a "major" change — requires Resource Owner, Security, and Finance signoff plus a canary rollout to a single user for 48 hours.
- Emergency changes (security patching, immediate revocation) must be recorded retroactively with documented justification and post-change review within 48 hours.

Procurement Alignment Checklist (applies pre-order):
- Does this purchase create new identities or vendor-managed accounts that will access Redwood infrastructure? If yes, attach vendor security checklist.
- Does the vendor process customer data? If yes, require contract clause with data processing addendum (DPA) and encryption requirements.
- Follow cost thresholds for approvals:
   - Under $5k: Team lead approval (documented in ticket).
   - $5k–$50k: Finance + Procurement approval.
   - >$50k: Finance + Procurement + VP-level approval and legal review.
- If hardware (GPU/servers) is procured for Dedicated or Private, include a network segmentation plan and KMS/HSM integration notes.

Vendor Security Gate (required artifacts before onboarding):
- Completed vendor security questionnaire and attestation to standards (ISO/ SOC / relevant checklist).
- Evidence of data handling controls: encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, logging retention.
- Contact matrix for incident response and escalation windows.
- Proof of required certifications or SOC2 reports if handling customer data.

Templates and Example Artifacts (copy/paste friendly fields):
1) Access Request Template (fields to capture in portal):
   - requester_name
   - team
   - resource_id (service/ARN)
   - access_role_template (link to role library)
   - justification (business)
   - desired_duration (ISO 8601)
   - linked_procurement_ticket (optional)
   - risk_mitigation (monitoring/MFA)

2) Procurement Fit-Gap Table (to be attached to vendor requests):
   - column headers: requirement | vendor_compliance | notes | evidence_link
   - sample rows: encryption-at-rest | yes/no | algorithm & key ownership | link-to-report

3) Approval Matrix (example):
   - team-lead: approve purchases <$5k and non-sensitive grants
   - procurement: approve purchases $5k–$50k and confirm vendor onboarding steps
   - finance-director: approve >$20k ongoing subscriptions
   - security: mandatory approver for any resource marked Sensitive or vendor-managed account
   - legal: mandatory for all customer-data-handling vendors and contracts >$50k

Operational Runbook Snippets (for oncall SREs):
- Revoke compromised key:
  1) Identify key ID and associated principals.
  2) Create revocation ticket in "Access Portal" referencing incident ID.
  3) Rotate any dependent keys, notify asset owner and security.
  4) Document actions and mark the incident for postmortem if exposure to customer data occurred.

- Emergency vendor account disablement:
  1) Security issues escalated to vendor-contact; disable account via vendor console or block IP ranges.
  2) Provision temporary alternative if service is essential; route traffic to fallback vendor if configured.
  3) Engage Legal and Procurement within 4 hours for contract remediation.

Data Management and Retention (short):
- Access decisions must reference the data classification for the resource. Data classification labels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Retention policies are applied at the dataset level; procurement of storage services requires agreeing to retention, deletion, and e-discovery terms.

Monitoring, Metrics & SLOs:
- Entitlement Review SLA: resource owners must attest to entitlements within 30 days of the attestation request (SLO 90%).
- Offboarding Revocation SLA: 2 hours for production accounts (SLO 99%), 24 hours for non-prod (SLO 95%).
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist Completion: 10 business days target from purchase approval to live onboarding (SLO 80%).

Audit and Evidence Collection:
- Every approval path must produce an immutable ticket with approver identity, timestamps, and justification.
- Security keeps 3 years of entitlement change logs for audit and internal review.

Example CLI snippets and IAM policy examples (illustrative):
- Short-lived token creation (example):
  $ accessctl issue --principal user:marcus --role read-only:billing --expires 72h --ticket TKT-12345

- Sample minimal IAM policy (text):
  {
    "Version": "2022-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["billing:GetInvoices"],
        "Resource": ["arn:redwood:billing:prod:::invoices/*"]
      }
    ]
  }

Rollout and Adoption Plan:
1) Q2 2024: Pilot with Platform and Finance teams for procurement gating and short-lived access.
2) Q3 2024: Enforce automated expirations and connector integrations with People Ops.
3) Q4 2024: Expand enforcement to Dedicated and Private deployment onboarding flows.
4) Ongoing: Quarterly training for managers and procurement; update templates based on audit feedback.

Escalation Paths & Contacts:
- Security Pager: sec-oncall@redwood.example (for immediate exposure)
- Procurement Ops: procurement@redwood.example
- People Ops: peopleops@redwood.example
- Security Owner (document owner): aisha.morgan@redwood.example

Related policies and references:
- RBAC and Authentication Standards (/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth)
- Procurement Playbook (see procurement team pages)
- Change Management Matrix (/confluence/policies-and-process/change-management-matrix)

Appendix: Example attestation email (one-click):
Subject: Quarterly Entitlement Attestation — Resource: billing-service
Body: Please confirm the list of active users and approve or mark for revocation. Link: <attestation-link>

Document maintenance:
- Owner (Security) will review annually or after any audit finding.
- Proposed changes appear as PRs in the policy repo; major updates require cross-functional signoff from Security, Finance, and People Ops.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Operational Commons and Process Patterns 2026

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates company-wide process patterns and canonical templates that operational teams (finance, security, people-ops, engineering, and product) should follow when executing cross-functional activities: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the internal templates used to standardize execution.

Audience: All Redwood employees who own or execute operational processes, and technical leads who implement controls in services and tools.

Scope: Applies to all corporate functions and product teams operating under Redwood Inference legal entities. This is the canonical set of process patterns; local variations require documented exceptions and a risk-owner signoff.

-----

1) Access & Permissions

Goal: Grant least privilege access quickly while maintaining auditability and fast recovery for incidents.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Access Owner: Team manager (regionally delegated)
- Access Audit Owner: Security Team
- Provisioning Tool Owner: Eng-Platform

Pattern: Request -> Approve -> Provision -> Review
sections.heading: Key Roles and Owners

sections.body:
1. Submit access request via the Access Request form (Confluence template: "access-request-template") with justification and least-privilege role.
2. Manager-level approval required for all role grants; for admin-level roles, security review is mandatory.
3. Eng-Platform or HR (for people systems) performs provisioning within 48 business hours.
4. Access grants automatically expire after 90 days unless renewed.
5. Quarterly review: Security runs an automated orphan-account and role-scope report; team managers must attest within 14 days.
sections.heading: Procedure (standard)

sections.body:
- Provisioning SLA: 48 business hours for standard requests, 5 business days for sensitive roles.
- Periodic Audit: Quarterly attestation, monthly automated scans.
sections.heading: SLA and Controls

sections.body:
- Emergency access (break glass) requires written post-facto justification within 24 hours and is logged to the central audit log.

-----

2) Change Management (services, infra, and major configs)

Goal: Minimize unexpected impact from changes while enabling rapid iteration on serving stacks and business systems.
sections.heading: Revocation and Emergency Access

sections.body:
- Fast-track: Non-customer-facing, low-risk changes (doc updates, non-prod infra tuning).
- Standard: Routine production changes with rollbacks and monitoring in place.
- Major: Schema migrations, model rollouts, capacity-related infra changes, changes affecting SLAs.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
- Fast-track: Owner approval + automated CI checks.
- Standard: Owner + peer reviewer + responsible SRE on-call signoff. Rollout plan and rollback playbook required.
- Major: Owner + Eng-Platform + Product + Change Advisory Board (CAB) signoff. CAB meets twice weekly; emergency CAB can be convened.
sections.heading: Approval Matrix

sections.body:
1. Describe change, impact, and rollback plan in the change request template.
2. Pre-deploy canary in a controlled slice (1–5% traffic or designated test cluster).
3. Instrumentation: Ensure tracing, profiling, and key metric dashboards are updated.
4. Run smoke tests and the regression prompt-set where model-serving behavior might change.
5. Perform progressive rollout using feature flags and monitor error budget and latency SLOs for 30 minutes after each step.
6. If any threshold breach occurs, trigger automatic rollback and page the on-call.
sections.heading: Deployment checklist (for Standard and Major)

sections.body:
- Latency increase > 20% from baseline for 5 minutes -> immediate rollback.
- Error rate > 1% for 3 minutes -> rollback + incident review.

Change windows: Standard business hours preferred; Major changes require notified maintenance windows and customer-facing communications.

-----

3) Data Management (classification, retention, handling)

Principles: Minimize retained PII, apply defense-in-depth, and document lineage for datasets used for training/eval.
sections.heading: Escalation thresholds (example)

sections.body:
- Public: Documentation, marketing assets.
- Internal: Product specs, runbooks, non-PII operational data.
- Restricted: Customer data, secrets, regulated datasets.
sections.heading: Classification tiers

sections.body:
| Data Type | Retention Default | Access Pattern | Owner |
| Customer logs (non-PII) | 180 days | Read for support & SRE | Customer Success |
| Customer PII | 90 days (default) | Minimal, audited | Security |
| Model training datasets | 365 days (review) | Restricted; request-based | Applied ML Team |
| Audit logs | 2 years | Security & Compliance | Security |
sections.heading: Retention and Access Rules (summary table in plain text)

sections.body:
- All Restricted data must be stored in approved repositories (VPC-only buckets, customer-dedicated storage) and encrypted at rest with KMS keys.
- Masking/pseudonymization is required before using customer telemetry for model training unless explicit consent/contractual terms allow.
- Data deletion requests must be tracked via the Data Deletion Request template and completed within contractual timelines.
sections.heading: Data Handling Requirements

sections.body:
- Every dataset used for model onboarding must include a provenance document: source, transformation steps, retention policy, and contact owner.

-----

4) Procurement & Expenses

Objective: Streamline purchases and expense reimbursement while providing delegation controls and budget visibility.
sections.heading: Lineage and Provenance

sections.body:
- <= $5,000: Team manager approval.
- $5,001–$50,000: Department head approval + procurement review.
- > $50,000: VP-level approval + legal/compliance review.
sections.heading: Purchase thresholds and authority matrix

sections.body:
1. Create a Purchase Request (PR) using the Purchase Request template with business justification, budget code, and vendor info.
2. Procurement verifies vendor due diligence checklist (insurance, security posture questionnaire if needed).
3. Procurement creates PO and routes to vendor.
4. Finance records the commit against the budget and tracks payments.
sections.heading: Approved procurement flow

sections.body:
- Reimbursable items: travel, client entertainment (with receipts and business justification), approved training.
- Non-reimbursable: personal expenses, fines, or items without documentation.
- Expense submission: within 30 days of expenditure; late submissions require manager exception.
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Any trip > $2,500 requires explicit manager and travel coordinator approval and a travel safety review for international travel.

-----

5) Vendor Management

Vendor lifecycle stages: Selection -> Contracting -> Onboarding -> Monitoring -> Offboarding
sections.heading: Travel approvals

sections.body:
- Legal & security review (standard clause checklist).
- SOC2 or equivalent evidence for vendors handling Restricted data.
- Financial health check for long-term commitments.
sections.heading: Minimum due diligence checklist (selection stage)

sections.body:
- Signed contract with SLAs and termination rights.
- Security questionnaire and remediation plan.
- Contact and escalation list (vendor-side and Redwood-side).
sections.heading: Onboarding artifacts required

sections.body:
- Strategic vendors: quarterly business reviews (QBRs).
- Operational vendors: monthly KPI review and incident syncs as needed.
sections.heading: Monitoring cadence

sections.body:
- Data return or certified deletion; revoke credentials and ensure accounts terminated.
- Final invoice reconciliation and retention of contract for 7 years (per legal retention schedule).

-----

6) Travel & Event Policy (high-level)

Principles: Safety first, cost-consciousness second, equitable access to travel for required business needs.
sections.heading: Offboarding checklist

sections.body:
- Use approved travel portal; economy class for flights under 5 hours, premium economy or business only with pre-approved manager exception.
- Hotel selection must use corporate rates when available.
sections.heading: Booking rules

sections.body:
- International travel requires manager approval and travel safety check for high-risk countries.
- Emergency travel assistance details and insurance coverage are available through People Ops.
sections.heading: Safety & Approvals

sections.body: - Meal per diem caps differ by region; itemize expenses and provide receipts for amounts over $75 USD equivalent.
sections.heading: Expenses and per diems

sections.body:
- Additional procurement flow required for significant spend on booths or sponsorships. See Procurement section.

-----

7) Internal Templates and Checklists (where to find them)
sections.heading: Conference sponsorships and exhibitor booths

sections.body:
- access-request-template (Access & Permissions)
- change-request-template (Change Management)
- procurement-purchase-request (Procurement & Expenses)
- vendor-onboarding-pack (Vendor Management)
- data-provenance-checklist (Data Management)
- travel-approval-form (Travel)
- post-incident-review (Incident Response)
sections.heading: Canonical templates (use and link names)

sections.body:
- Teams must not create local forks of templates without documenting the differences and obtaining an owner-team signoff.
- All templates have a metadata header that includes template owner, last revision date, and related policy link.

-----

Governance and Exceptions
sections.heading: Template usage rules

sections.body:
1. Document the exception request using the Exception Request template, including risk assessment and mitigation.
2. Route to owner_team and governance board (depending on risk tier).
3. Approval requires a documented compensating control and an expiration date.
sections.heading: Exception process

sections.body: - Policy and templates review cadence is annual. High-risk controls (access, data handling) are reviewed semi-annually.
sections.heading: Periodic review cycle

sections.body:
- Time-to-provision (median hours) for access requests.
- Change success rate (percentage of changes with no rollback).
- Vendor security compliance coverage (%) for vendors handling Restricted data.
- Expense processing time (median days).

Appendix: Example change request checklist (text)
1. Change summary and owner contact.
2. Impact analysis and affected services list.
3. Rollback steps with clear commands or runbook references.
4. Monitoring dashboards and metric thresholds.
5. Communication plan (internal and customer-facing if relevant).
sections.heading: Metrics and KPIs (suggested)

sections.body:
- Policy curator: Priya Natarajan (finance-legal)
- Access & Security escalation: Marta Alvarez (Security)
- Procurement lead: Evan Chen (Finance)
- Change CAB coordinator: Liam O'Connor (Eng-Platform)
sections.heading: Contact and ownership matrix

sections.body:
- 2025-10-15: Created by Priya Natarajan.
- 2026-01-10: Added data retention defaults and travel threshold updates (reviewers: Evan Chen, Marta Alvarez).
- 2026-02-01: Published as company policy and linked canonical templates.
sections.heading: Revision history

- Company Ops Index (search: company-operations-reference-2025)

End of document.
