payload.page_title: Foundation controls and processes: access, change, data, procurement & travel

sections.body: This playbook collects Redwood Inference’s baseline, cross-functional controls and step-by-step processes for: access & permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the canonical operational reference for engineering, product, people-ops, and finance teams.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or customer data.
- Operational exceptions (e.g., security incident response) are handled by the Security incident process; see related pages.
- Owners listed below are accountable for maintaining each section and ensuring team-level procedures map to these standards.
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required and use temporary elevated access where practical.
- Segregation of duties: approvals should not be self-authorized for procurement, vendor onboarding, or high-risk changes.
- Auditability: every approval and change must be traceable in systems that retain logs for the retention period defined in Data Management.
- Cost-awareness: procurement and expense approvals must reference budget lines and expected ROI.
sections.heading: Key principles

sections.body:
- Admin group: role-based group with elevated configuration privileges (e.g., network-admin, infra-admin).
- High-risk change: any change that may impact production latency, security posture, or customer data availability.
- Sensitive data: PII, customer secrets, or regulated data subject to additional controls described below.
sections.heading: Definitions (short)

sections.body:
Owner: Security (operational policies maintained jointly with People Ops)
Purpose: Centralize how access is requested, approved, and revoked to reduce blast radius and support audits.
sections.heading: Access & permissions

sections.body:
1) Request: employee or contractor opens an access request via the Access Portal (internal URL: /access-portal) and identifies the resource, justification, and duration (if temporary).
2) Manager approval: direct manager must approve role justification and provide a business justification in the request.
3) Owner approval: resource owner (service or team owner) must sign off for production and sensitive resources.
4) Security review: for requests involving customer data or elevated privileges, Security performs a risk review (within 48 hours).
5) Provision: IAM system (OKTA + internal RBAC) provisions access; request and approval chain are recorded.
6) Scheduled review: access with duration > 90 days is automatically included in quarterly access reviews.
sections.heading: Standard process for granting access

sections.body:
- Revocation should be initiated by manager or security via the Access Portal. Offboarding triggers automatic deprovisioning: accounts, keys, VPN tokens, and cloud roles are revoked within 2 hours of HR offboard confirmation.
- Emergency access: just-in-time (JIT) admin elevations are provided via the Privileged Access system and expire within the session window (default 4 hours). All JIT sessions are logged in SIEM and reviewed weekly.
sections.heading: Revocation and emergency access

sections.body:
Owner: Eng Platform / Eng SRE (policy maintained with Product)
Purpose: Ensure predictable, auditable changes to systems and services while minimizing customer impact.
sections.heading: Change management

sections.body:
| Type | Examples | Approval required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard (low-risk) | routine configuration updates, non-prod infra patching | Auto-approved via change queue; notify SRE team |
| Normal (moderate-risk) | model rollout, database schema migration | Manager + service owner approval; change ticket in CHG system |
| High-risk / Emergency | production DB rollback, broad network change | SRE on-call + Eng Platform lead approval; Emergency CAB post-facto review |

Pre-deployment checklist (Normal + High-risk):
- Impact analysis documented on the change ticket
- Backout plan and validation steps included
- SLA/RPO/RTO implications enumerated
- Load, canary, and smoke test schedules defined
- Communication plan with customer-facing teams (Support, CS)
sections.heading: Change classification table

sections.body:
- Normal changes should target low-traffic windows or use progressive rollout (canaries at 1%, 10%, 50%).
- Canary metrics: error rate, tail latency (p99), token drop rate for inference services. Canary fails when error rate or p99 latency increases by > 25% relative to baseline for 10m.
sections.heading: Change windows and Canary policy

sections.body:
- All High-risk changes require a postmortem within 72 hours and a closure signoff from the change owner.
- Monthly change audit report is distributed to Eng leadership.
sections.heading: Post-change reviews and audits

sections.body:
Owner: Security + Data Governance
Purpose: Define lifecycle for all company and customer data to meet compliance, privacy, and operational needs.
sections.heading: Data management and retention

sections.body:
- Public: documentation intended for public consumption
- Internal: operational data not containing PII or secrets
- Sensitive: PII, model training data tied to customers, API secrets
- Regulated: data covered by contractual/regulatory controls (e.g., GDPR special categories, HIPAA)
sections.heading: Data classification levels

sections.body:
| Data type | Retention | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audit logs | 2 years (compressed) | Security |
| Billing & invoices | 7 years | Finance |
| Backups (non-sensitive) | 30 days rolling | Eng Infra |
| Customer model inputs (sensitive) | Configured per contract; default 30 days | Product / Legal |
sections.heading: Retention matrix (summary)

sections.body:
- Must be approved via an elevated access workflow (see Access & permissions).
- Access requires MFA, device posture check, and mandatory data handling training.
- Sensitive exports are encrypted with customer-specific keys where required.
sections.heading: Access to sensitive data

sections.body:
- Secure wipe procedures for cloud storage and on-prem disks are documented in Eng Infra runbooks.
- Deletion requests (customer or internal) are processed within 30 days unless contractual restrictions apply.
sections.heading: Data disposal

sections.body:
Owner: Finance (procurement team)
Purpose: Ensure cost control, vendor compliance, and transparent approvals.
sections.heading: Procurement & expenses

sections.body:
1) Low-value purchases (< $5,000): budget owner approval via procurement system.
2) Mid-value purchases ($5,000 – $50,000): budget owner + Finance procurement lead approval.
3) High-value purchases (> $50,000): VP-level signoff + Legal review for contract terms.
sections.heading: Procurement thresholds and approval matrix

sections.body:
1) Raise PR in Procurement Portal with cost center and business case
2) Procurement validates vendor and checks existing contracts or preferred suppliers
3) Finance budgets against runway/OKR allocations and approves/rejects within 3 business days
4) Purchase order (PO) issued and vendor notified
sections.heading: Purchase request workflow

sections.body:
- Travel expenses are reimbursed per Travel Policy below; employees must submit within 30 days with receipts.
- Card usage: corporate cards must be reconciled weekly. Misuse or repeated exceptions will trigger review by Finance and People Ops.
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
Owner: Procurement + Legal
Purpose: Standardize vendor risk assessment, onboarding, contract lifecycle, and periodic review.
sections.heading: Vendor management and onboarding

sections.body:
- Category A (Strategic/High-risk): vendors handling customer data, infra providers, or critical software (renewal cadence, quarterly business reviews, SLA penalties).
- Category B (Business-support): SaaS tools without customer data, moderate risk (annual review).
- Category C (Low-cost / Consumable): office supplies, low-risk services (procurement-approved catalog).
sections.heading: Vendor classification and controls

sections.body:
1) Vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire + SOC2/ISO reports)
2) Legal contract negotiation with appropriate data processing addenda (DPA)
3) Finance sets payment terms and PO process
4) Procurement adds vendor to vendor registry and assigns owner
5) Quarterly health checks and SLA monitoring configured
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist (Category A)

sections.body: - Contracted vendors must provide a data export and deletion plan. Procurement coordinates with Eng and Security to revoke access and rotate shared credentials.
sections.heading: Termination and offboarding

sections.body:
Owner: People Ops + Finance
Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective travel practices that balance employee comfort and budget discipline.
sections.heading: Travel policy (concise)

sections.body:
- Booking: employees should use the approved travel portal. Air travel in economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Per diem: meal caps are country-specific and listed in the Travel Templates appendix.

payload.page_title: Operational Catalog: Access Lifecycle, Change Controls, Data Stewardship, and Supplier Onboarding

sections.body: This document consolidates company-wide operational policies and repeatable procedures governing: access and permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel, and the standard templates teams must use. It is intended as the canonical cross-functional catalog for engineering, product, security, finance, and people-ops.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems or data. Exceptions must be approved by Finance-Legal and Security.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required for the role and timeboxed when possible.
- Separation of duties: requests that change financial or production states must involve at least two independent approvers.
- Auditability: every privilege change, production change, procurement, and vendor onboarding event must create an auditable ticket with owner, justification, and artifacts.
- Risk-based controls: controls scale with data sensitivity and financial exposure.
sections.heading: Summary of Key Principles

sections.body:
- Catalog owner: Nina Patel (Finance-Legal) — nina.patel@redwood.ai
- Access governance: Security (team alias: security@redwood.ai) — primary contact: Marcus Liu
- Change management operations: Eng Platform (eng-platform@redwood.ai) — primary contact: Sofia Romero
- Procurement & vendor coordination: Finance (procure@redwood.ai) — primary contact: Ethan Park

1) Access & Permissions
sections.heading: Owners and Contacts

sections.body: Access lifecycle is managed through the Access Request System (ARS), group-managed identity (GMI) roles, and short-lived elevated sessions (just-in-time). All non-public systems require an ARS ticket ID embedded in the access grant.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requester: provides business justification, scope, and duration.
- Approver: manager-level for standard access; system owner for high-sensitivity assets.
- Access Review Owner: a designated manager or system owner who runs quarterly reviews.
sections.heading: Roles and Responsibilities

sections.body:
| Access Level | Example Systems | Approval Required | Max Duration |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Standard employee | Slack, Google Drive (non-sensitive folders) | Manager | 1 year |
| Elevated dev | Internal staging clusters, debug consoles | Manager + System Owner | 30 days |
| Production operator | Prod serving runtime, deployment API | System Owner + SRE on-call | 7 days |
| Sensitive data access | PII datasets, audit logs | Data Steward + Security | 14 days |
sections.heading: Access Categories and Approval Matrix

sections.body:
1. Create ARS ticket with justification and target resources.
2. Manager approves (auto-notify system owner if required).
3. Access is provisioned via GMI and an audit log entry is created.
4. Ticket must be tagged with a re-review date and auto-closure if timeboxed.
sections.heading: Request Flow (standard)

sections.body:
- Use Break-Glass form (link in ARS) and notify Security + SRE immediately.
- All break-glass grants are time-limited to 4 hours and must be converted to formal ARS request within 24 hours with post-incident justification.
sections.heading: Emergency access (break-glass)

sections.body:
- Quarterly entitlement reviews for all groups.
- Automated orphan account detection runs weekly; remediation tickets assigned to the account owner with 7-day SLA.
sections.heading: Access Review and Remediation

sections.body:
```
Title: Access request — [system] — [purpose]
Requester: [name]
Justification: [business need, minimal scope]
Target resources: [resource identifiers]
Duration: [days]
Approvers: [manager email, system owner]
```

2) Change Management
sections.heading: Sample Access Request Template (to paste into ARS)

sections.body: Ensure predictable, observable, and reversible changes to production and critical systems while minimizing customer-facing disruptions.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Standard (pre-approved low risk): routine config changes, small infra tweaks.
- Normal: requires review and approval via Change Request (CR).
- Emergency: immediate fixes for P1/P0 incidents; follow-up CR required.
sections.heading: Change Categories

sections.body:
1. Submit CR in the Change Tracker with impact assessment, rollback plan, test cases, deployment window, and monitoring plan.
2. Engineering change owner schedules review with affected service owners.
3. CAB review required for changes with: cross-team impact, data migrations, vendor contracts, or >$50k monthly spend impact.
4. After approval, schedule deployment within allowed windows (see Deployment Windows).
5. Post-deploy verification (smoke tests) and CR close-out within 48 hours.
sections.heading: Change Request Process (Normal changes)

sections.body:
- CR form with owners and stakeholders.
- Runbook snippet for deployment and rollback.
- Test checklist and automated test links.
- Observability hooks (dashboards/alerts) to verify success.
sections.heading: Required Artifacts for every Normal CR

sections.body:
- Low-risk infra: Mon–Thu 10:00–18:00 PT.
- High-risk / customer-facing services: default weekend or off-peak windows agreed with SRE.
- Emergency changes allowed outside windows with on-call approval.
sections.heading: Deployment Windows and Service Hours

sections.body:
```
Change ID: CR-########
Rollback owner: [name]
Trigger(s) for rollback: [error rates, latency, failed smoke]
Estimated rollback time: [minutes]
Rollback steps: [commands/steps]
Verification after rollback: [checks]
```
sections.heading: Rollback Plan Template (short form)

sections.body:
- CR review SLA: 3 business days for Normal changes.
- Emergency follow-up CR: create within 24 hours.
- Post-deploy verification: complete within 48 hours.

3) Data Management and Classification
sections.heading: Change KPIs and SLAs

sections.body:
- Public: safe for external distribution.
- Internal: company-internal operational data.
- Confidential: business-sensitive data (contracts, customer metadata).
- Restricted: PII, PHI, regulated data requiring enhanced controls.
sections.heading: Data Classification Levels

sections.body:
- Encryption at rest and in transit required for Confidential and Restricted.
- Access controls: RBAC + just-in-time for Restricted.
- Logging: all Restricted data access must emit fine-grained audit events retained 2 years.
- Data minimization: services must not store Restricted data unless approved by Data Steward.
sections.heading: Handling Requirements by Class

sections.body:
- Default retention for Internal data: 2 years.
- Confidential: 3–7 years depending on contract/legal requirements.
- Restricted: retention determined by legal/data steward; default 7 years.
sections.heading: Retention Policy

sections.body:
- Data Stewards: designate classification, retention, and approved consumers.
- Platform teams: enforce technical controls (encryption, logging).
- Security: periodic audits and policy exceptions handling.
sections.heading: Data Lifecycle Responsibilities

sections.body:
- Report data incidents to security@redwood.ai immediately.
- Triage, impact assessment, and notification per incident response policy.

sections.heading: Data Incident Handling

sections.body:

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
sections.heading: Company Card and Delegation

sections.body:
- Tier 1 (Strategic/High risk): hosts customer data, manages production services. Requires Security review, SOC2 + contract addenda.
- Tier 2 (Moderate risk): business tools with access to internal systems. Requires DPIA and standard contract.
- Tier 3 (Low risk): marketing suppliers, consultants. Standard MSA acceptable.

1. Vendor profile in Vendor Registry (legal name, tax id, primary contact).
2. Risk assessment completed by Procurement + Security.
3. Contract with data processing addendum if applicable.
4. Approved purchase order and payment terms.
5. Technical onboarding and least-privilege integration plan.
6. Regular review cadence defined (quarterly for Tier 1, annually for Tier 2).
sections.heading: Onboarding Checklist (minimum)

sections.body:
- Ensure deprovisioning checklist executes: revoke keys, remove service accounts, terminate access, confirm data disposition or return per contract.

6) Templates & Required Forms (links to systems are referenced by name)
- Access Request (ARS): use the ARS form. Include resource IDs and expiry.
- Change Request (CR): use Change Tracker CR template. Attach rollbackplan and tests.

payload.page_title: Cross-Functional Authorization Lifecycle and Spend Coordination Playbook

sections.body: This playbook describes an integrated operating model for: (1) authorizing access and permissions across systems, (2) orchestrating change approvals that affect access or spend, and (3) coordinating procurement, vendor onboarding, and travel/expense flows so that authorization decisions and financial commitments are aligned and auditable.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- System owners and service teams
- People Operations and Finance approvers
- Security and Compliance reviewers
- Platform and SRE teams that implement RBAC and entitlement plumbing
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body:
- Access request lifecycle (request → approval → provision → review → revoke) for internal systems and cloud resources.
- Change management gating when requests require config changes, role updates, or service-level modifications.
- Procurement workflows tied to access (licenses, reserved capacity, dedicated GPU commitments).
- Vendor onboarding steps that require system access, data access agreements, and expense/payment terms.
- Travel & expense approvals where access or vendor relationships are created as a result of travel.
sections.heading: This document covers company-wide processes for

sections.body:
- Least privilege by default: default access is no access; approvals must justify elevated scopes.
- Separation of duties: requestors cannot be sole approvers where spend or data sensitivity is material.
- Auditability: actions must be traceable to an approver, ticket, and artifact (PO, contract, NDA).
- Single source of truth: Authorization decisions must be recorded in the central entitlement system and mirrored in the ticketing system.
- Risk-based controls: High-sensitivity data and high-dollar spend require additional reviewers.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
- Entitlement: a permission or role granted to a principal (user, service account).
- Approver: person or role authorized to approve a request.
- Sensitive Data: data labeled Confidential or Restricted in the data classification catalog.
- Material Spend: any commitment > $50,000 or multi-year contract.
sections.heading: Definitions (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Service Owner (team): owns the resource, ensures periodic access reviews, produces justification for approvals.
- Requestor: initiates the access/change/procurement request with necessary justification and cost code.
- Approvers:
  - Line Manager: approves role-based low-risk access (< 30 days).
  - Security Reviewer: required for any access to Sensitive Data.
  - Finance Approver: required for any procurement or material spend.
  - Legal: required for vendor contracts, NDAs, and custom terms.
- Platform/SRE: implements technical provisioning after approval and updates inventory.
- Vendor Management: coordinates onboarding and contract signatures.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
1) Initiation: requestor files a ticket in the central intake template (see Templates section) and selects request type: Access | Change | Procurement | Travel. Mandatory fields: resource, justification, duration, cost center, sensitivity flag, business owner.
2) Automated triage: the entitlement system inspects resource and assigns required approvers based on rules (data sensitivity, environment: prod vs non-prod, and dollar thresholds).
3) Approvals sequence:
   a) Line manager signs off for role-fit and business need.
   b) Security reviews if sensitivity flag >= Confidential.
   c) Finance reviews if request includes purchase or is tied to a budget.
   d) Legal only if vendor or contract is involved.
4) Provisioning: Platform/SRE or the automated agent provisions role (IAM change, service account, token issuance) using audited pipelines. Provisioning must attach ticket ID and artifact links.
5) Validation: Requestor confirms access and performs a short acceptance test within 48 hours.
6) Periodic review and expiry: Temporary access expires automatically at the requested end date. Permanent role grants are subject to quarterly access reviews by the Service Owner.
7) Revocation: Revocation requests should follow the same ticket pipeline and be prioritized as P1 for ex-employees and contractor offboarding.
sections.heading: Access request workflow (detailed)

sections.body:
- Any access or permission change that modifies production behavior or increases blast radius must be accompanied by a Change Request (CR) and follow the CR approval board (CRB) schedule.
- CR classification:
  - Minor: role rename, non-prod resource permission change – can be scheduled without CRB if low risk.
  - Major: any permission to read/write Sensitive Data in prod, changes to network allowlists, or multi-tenant routing – requires CRB review and a rollback plan.
- Required CR artifacts: impact statement, test plan, rollback procedure, monitoring checklist, and contact list.
sections.heading: Change management alignment

sections.body:
| Classification | Examples | Approvers required | Typical retention in ticketing system |
|---------------|----------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Public        | Marketing assets | Line manager | 180 days |
| Internal      | Design docs, internal metrics | Line manager | 365 days |
| Confidential  | Customer PII, internal PII | Line manager + Security | 3 years |
| Restricted    | Regulated customer data, financial reports | Line manager + Security + Legal | 7 years |
sections.heading: Data classification table (guide when deciding approvals)

sections.body:
- Preliminary: business case and budget code assigned by the Requestor.
- Procurement intake: submit PO request including vendor name, SOW, estimated value, renewal terms, and required access scope.
- Vendor risk review: Vendor Management runs an InfoSec questionnaire for external access, data handling, and SOC reports.
- Contracting: Legal negotiates, signs NDA, and finalizes T&Cs.
- Access provisioning: once contract signed, create a vendor identity (least-privileged), restrict to necessary IP ranges and time windows, enable session recording where applicable.
- Payment & invoicing: Finance ensures PO matches invoice before payment.
- Onboarding closure: Vendor Management closes the onboarding checklist and updates the vendor registry.
sections.heading: Procurement and vendor onboarding checklist

sections.body:
- Separate vendor identities; no sharing of Redwood employee accounts.
- Time-bound credentials with automatic expiry and step-up authentication for sensitive actions.
- Network segmentation and allowlists per project.
- Logging and session recording retained per the data classification retention policy.
sections.heading: Vendor access controls (minimum technical controls)

sections.body:
- If travel leads to a vendor agreement or material procurement (e.g., edge-hosted hardware), the traveler must submit a pre-travel authorization: estimated spend, expected vendor engagements, and data/access implications.
- Post-travel: expense reports must reference the ticket/PO or contract that resulted from the trip. Travel that results in vendor onboarding must trigger the vendor onboarding checklist.
sections.heading: Travel & expense interplay with access/vendor flows

sections.body:
- Access request template (ticket): fields = requestor, service, resource path, justification, duration, cost code, sensitivity flag, business owner, requested permissions.
- Procurement intake form (CSV/JSON snippet):
  {
    "vendor": "ExampleCo",
    "estimated_value": 12000,
    "currency": "USD",
    "cost_center": "ENG-PLATFORM",
    "po_required": true
  }
- Vendor onboarding checklist (checkboxes): Business case, NDA signed, SOC 2 evidence, Access scope defined, PO created, Monitoring configured.
- Change Request template: impact, rollback, monitoring, test results, deployment window, contacts.

Audit, monitoring and metrics:
- Audit trail requirements: every approval and provisioning action must write an immutable record to the entitlement audit log with fields: request_id, actor, action, timestamp, justification.
- Key metrics to track monthly:
  - Mean time to approve (MTTA) – target <= 24 hours for non-sensitive requests.
  - Mean time to provision – target <= 4 hours after final approval for automated flows.
  - Percent of temporary access expired on schedule – target >= 99%.
  - Number of emergency revocations per quarter – target <= 3 (investigate root cause if > 3).
sections.heading: Templates (centralized artifacts)

sections.body:
- Urgent revocation (ex-employee with prod access):
  1) Open emergency ticket and tag as P0.
  2) Notify Security and SRE on-call via page.
  3) Revoke sessions globally, rotate shared keys, and disable accounts.
  4) Validate no active sessions and confirm with HR.
- Vendor breach response (vendor account suspected compromise):
  1) Suspend vendor identity and isolate associated resources.
  2) Engage Vendor Management and Legal; require vendor to provide incident report and mitigation timeline.
  3) Initiate customer-impact assessment if applicable.
sections.heading: Operational playbooks (quick runbooks)

sections.body:
- Phase 1 (0–30 days): Publish templates, run two cross-functional workshops (Security, Finance, Legal, Platform) and update ticket intake forms.
- Phase 2 (30–90 days): Configure automated approvers and entitlement rules in the central system; run a dry run with three pilot teams.
- Phase 3 (90–180 days): Company-wide rollout, mandatory training module for managers, and first quarterly access review.
sections.heading: Training and rollout plan

sections.body:
- Tickets and approvals retained according to data classification table.
- Contracts and POs retained per Finance retention policy and Legal guidelines.
sections.heading: Retention and records

sections.body:

payload.page_title: Rights and Risks Alignment Manual

sections.body: This manual defines a single, company‑wide pattern for aligning access and permissions, change approvals, data handling expectations, procurement thresholds, vendor risk decisions, and travel expense governance. It is intended for stakeholders who approve access, manage vendor relationships, run platform changes, or sign off on spend.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems.
- Covers systems managed by Hosted, Dedicated and Private teams (internal and customer environments).
- Does NOT replace team‑specific operational runbooks; instead it provides the canonical authorization and risk model teams should import into local procedures.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1) Least privilege by default: grant the minimum role required for 90% of daily work.
2) Segregation of duties: approval chains must separate requesters from approvers for critical actions.
3) Risk‑based accuracy: higher risk assets require stronger controls (2FA, approved devices, KMS‑wrapped keys).
4) Single source for approvals: use the Company Access Portal (CAP) for all access requests and the Procurement Portal for spend.
sections.heading: Principles (short)

sections.body:
- Tier 1 — Low impact: read access to public/internal docs, non‑prod dashboards. Approver: Manager. Review cadence: annual.
- Tier 2 — Operational: write access to non‑production systems, basic production monitoring. Approver: Service Owner + Manager. Review cadence: quarterly.
- Tier 3 — Sensitive: production write, secret access (API keys, DB write), vendor integrations. Approver: Service Owner + Security Reviewer + Finance (if cost). Review cadence: monthly.
- Tier 4 — Elevated: access to PII/regulated datasets, KMS key material, ability to deploy to customer VPCs. Approver: Exec Sponsor + Security + Legal + Finance. Review cadence: monthly; emergency access requires post‑hoc audit.
sections.heading: Authorization tiers (table described)

sections.body:
1) Initiate request in CAP with: requester, justification, scope, required duration (one‑off, 30/90/365 days or indefinite with quarterly review), and risk assessment answers.
2) Manager auto-approves for Tier 1 within 48 hrs.
3) For Tier 2–4, the approval chain is auto-notified; approvers have 72 hrs to respond.
4) If an approver rejects, the request returns to requester with required changes.
5) After approval, IAM issues the entitlement and records the change in the Audit Ledger (immutable entry with request id).
6) Access is time‑boxed; expiration triggers an automated review reminder 7 days before expiry.

Change management summary (SRE + platform integration):
- All planned production changes must use the Change Request (CR) flow in the Change Registry and follow these thresholds:
  - Routine (low‑risk): config tweaks, non‑customer facing infra changes. Owner to notify on-call and deploy. Post‑deploy review within 48 hrs.
  - Standard (medium): schema changes, scaling policies, model rollout to staging. Requires peer review, safety smoke tests, canary percent <= 5% for 24 hours.
  - Major (high): API contract changes, data migrations, model rollouts to production >5% traffic, or infra upgrades that impact SLA. Requires CR with approvals: Service Owner, Eng SRE, Security, Product, and Finance for cost > $10k.
- Change freeze windows: last 3 business days of every quarter and major release dates (documented on Team Roadmaps).
- Emergency changes: Follow the Emergency CR path — immediate approver notification by PagerDuty; postmortem required within 5 business days.
sections.heading: Access request workflow (numbered)

sections.body:
- Public: documentation intended for external consumption. Storage: general bucket, no restrictions.
- Internal: company internal docs, non‑sensitive metrics. Storage: corporate GCS/Azure Blob with standard encryption at rest.
- Confidential: customer non‑PII, non‑regulated business data. Access: Tier 3 controls, logged, KMS for secrets.
- Restricted: PII, regulated customer data, HIPAA/CCPA scope. Access: Tier 4, strict RBAC, HSM/KMS, network segmentation (VPCs), mandatory audit logging and quarterly attestation.
sections.heading: Data classification and handling (short table style)

sections.body:
- All restricted data must be stored in approved environments only (see Appendix: Approved Data Stores).
- Export of confidential or restricted data outside Redwood requires Data Owner + Legal + Security approval and an executed DPA if third‑party.
- Backups containing restricted data must use customer‑segregated keys and have a retention policy consistent with the customer's contract.
sections.heading: Data handling rules (bullets)

sections.body:
- Micro Purchases: <= $1,000 — Manager approval in Procurement Portal.
- Standard Purchases: $1,001–$25,000 — Manager + Finance approval; procurement handles vendor setup.
- Strategic Purchases: $25,001–$250,000 — Manager + Finance + Legal + Procurement Sourcing; requires vendor risk assessment.
- Enterprise/Capital: > $250,000 — Executive sponsor + VP Finance + Legal + Procurement; board notification for multiyear commitments > $1M.
- POs: All purchases > $5,000 require a PO.
- Expense submissions: employees must attach receipts in the Expense Portal within 60 days. Per‑diem rates are published separately; use corporate cards for travel when possible.
sections.heading: Procurement and expenses (approval thresholds)

sections.body:
- Low (L): SaaS with no customer data access (e.g., marketing SaaS). Controls: standard contract, annual review.
- Medium (M): Vendors that process internal non‑sensitive operational data or limited customer metadata. Controls: SOC2 or equivalent, annual contract review, standard DPA.
- High (H): Vendors with access to PII, regulated data, or that run inside customer‑facing infrastructure. Controls: SOC2 + contractual SLAs, penetration test report, annual on‑site/in‑depth review, segmentation verification.
sections.heading: Vendor management and risk tiers

sections.body:
1) Business Owner submits Vendor Intake form in Procurement Portal.
2) Procurement runs vendor questionnaire + basic risk scoring.
3) Security reviews for High/Medium vendors.
4) Legal negotiates contracts and DPAs.
5) Finance approves payment terms and wiring details.
6) IAM and Service Owner configure minimal access and set review cadence.
sections.heading: Vendor onboarding checklist (condensed)

sections.body:

payload.page_title: Enterprise Process Library and Operational Blueprints

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the company-wide operational policies and standardized procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and common internal templates. It is intended as the single-source reference for teams implementing or auditing cross-functional workflows.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and contingent workers across global regions. Exceptions must be approved by the owning team and recorded in the policy exceptions tracker.

Principles

- Safety-first: Preserve customer and company data confidentiality and integrity by default.
- Least privilege: Access granted only for specific, timeboxed tasks.
- Clear ownership: Every process step must name an accountable role.
- Auditability: Actions and approvals must be traceable in company systems.
- Efficient operations: Balance control with predictable SLAs to avoid operational friction.

Governance and Owners

- Policy Owner: Finance & Legal (primary), Security (technical guidance), People Ops (people/process enforcement).
- Executive Sponsor: VP Operations.
- Operational Owners and Contacts:
  - Access & Permissions: Access Administration (access-admin@redwood.example.com)
  - Change Management: Platform Engineering (change-mgr@redwood.example.com)
  - Data Management: Data Stewardship (data-steward@redwood.example.com)
  - Procurement & Expenses: Procurement (procurement@redwood.example.com)
  - Vendor Management: Vendor Risk & Compliance (vendor-risk@redwood.example.com)
  - Travel & Expenses: People Ops (travel@redwood.example.com)

1) Access & Permissions

Summary: Use least privilege and time-limited approvals for systems. Primary identity provider is Okta; resource-specific access is governed via AWS IAM, GCP IAM, and internal RBAC in the Redwood Console.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Requestor: employee or manager who requests access.
- Approver: role owner (service owner) or delegated approver.
- Access Admin: implements changes in IAM/Okta and records audit entries.
- Privileged Access Reviewer: security team member for periodic reviews.
sections.heading: Roles and Authority

sections.body:
1. Standard (non-privileged) access: Raise request in Jira (project: ACCESS-REQ) or via self-service Confluence form. Manager approval required. SLA: implemented within 24 hours for routine requests.
2. Privileged access (production systems, secrets, or escalation tooling): Requestor must provide justification, duration, and rollback plan. Approval chain: manager -> service owner -> security (Privileged Access Board). SLA: 72 hours target for approvals; emergency access via break-glass flow (see Emergency Access Runbook link).
3. Temporary access: Requests may include expiry (default 7 days). Access Admin will configure automatic expiration where supported.
sections.heading: Standard request flows

sections.body:
- Quarterly privileged access review owned by Security.
- Semi-annual standard access recertification owned by managers; automated reminders issued via Okta.
sections.heading: Access reviews and recertification

sections.body:
- MFA enforced for all interactive accounts (Okta verify or hardware token).
- Password managers (company-approved) required for shared credentials; avoid manual sharing.
- Secrets stored in company KMS/HSM-backed vault (HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS).

2) Change Management

Purpose: Ensure controlled, auditable changes to production and customer-facing systems while minimizing outage risk.
sections.heading: Minimum technical controls

sections.body:
- Standard Change: Pre-approved, documented repeatable change (e.g., scheduled config refresh). No CAB approval required if checklist met.
- Normal Change: Requires RFC in Jira (project: CHG-RFC), impact assessment, test plan, backout plan, and CAB approval if risk > low.
- Emergency Change: Urgent fixes to mitigate active incidents; must use Emergency Change workflow and be reviewed post-implementation.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
1. Create RFC in CHG-RFC with owner, roll-out window, test plan, backout plan, and stakeholders.
2. Review window: 48 hours for Normal Changes.
3. CAB: Weekly standing CAB for non-emergency approvals; security and SRE must attend for high-risk changes.
4. Implementation: follow deployment checklist; observe monitoring and alert windows.
5. Post-deploy verification & close RFC.
sections.heading: Process Summary

sections.body:
- RFC triage: 24-48 hours.
- Emergency change post-mortem: within 72 hours of change.
sections.heading: SLOs & thresholds

sections.body:
- All RFCs logged in Jira (CHG-RFC) with owner and links to runbooks.
- Deployment metadata must include build SHA, model variant, runtime config, and canary percent where applicable.

3) Data Management
sections.heading: Tooling & Audit

sections.body:
- Public: Allowed for public distribution.
- Internal: Default for non-sensitive company information.
- Restricted: Customer data, contracts, and PII that require access controls.
- Confidential: Legal, M&A, or regulated data with strict handling and retention.
sections.heading: Classification

sections.body:
- Public: No special controls.
- Internal: Store in company-managed drives; standard backups.
- Restricted: Encrypt at-rest and in-transit, access via least privilege, logging enabled, DLP policies enforced.
- Confidential: Access on approved devices only, dual approval for exports, mandatory legal review for sharing outside company.
sections.heading: Handling rules by class

sections.body:
- Audit logs: 1 year (full retention); aggregated metrics kept 3 years.
- Financial/contract records: 7 years per finance policy.
- Customer datasets used for evaluation: retention limited to project duration + 90 days unless contract states otherwise.
sections.heading: Retention & deletion

sections.body:
- Data exports to vendors require vendor classification and approved data processing agreement (DPA).
- Encrypted transfer only (TLS 1.2+). Use secure SFTP or signed API endpoints.
sections.heading: Data movement & third parties

sections.body:
- Any suspected data leak reported to Security in 1 hour.
- Incident response runbook invoked; notifications per Legal/Compliance templates.

4) Procurement & Expenses
sections.heading: Data incidents

sections.body:
- Purchase < $5,000: Department Manager approval. Target processing SLA: 48 business hours.
- $5,000 - $50,000: Director approval + Procurement review. SLA: 5 business days for standard vendor contracts.
- > $50,000 or multi-year commitments: VP approval + Legal sign-off + Procurement lead. SLA: 10-21 business days depending on negotiation complexity.
sections.heading: Procurement thresholds and approval matrix

sections.body:
- All vendor contracts with data handling, indemnity, or IP clauses must be routed to Legal.
- Standard purchasing templates (NetSuite PO, SOW template) are required for commitments > $25k.
sections.heading: Contracting & legal review

sections.body:
- Employees must submit expense reports within 7 days of trip completion.
- Receipts required for items > $25.
- Corporate card allowed for travel and vendor meals only; personal reimbursements require manager approval.
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Vendor onboarding into AP requires completed W-9 (US) or equivalent tax form, banking details verified, and PO or approved contract attached.
- Invoice payment terms default to Net 30 unless negotiated.

5) Vendor Management and Risk Assessment
sections.heading: Vendor payments and fiscal controls

sections.body:
1. Vendor intake form in Confluence/Procurement portal.
2. Business justification and owner.
3. Security questionnaire if vendor processes Restricted/Confidential data.
4. DPA and liability review by Legal.
5. Insurance and SOC 2/ISO evidence where applicable.
6. Approved by Procurement and Legal.
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist (minimum)

sections.body:
- Tier 1 (High risk): Vendors processing customer data or offering critical infrastructure. Controls: annual penetration test evidence, SOC2 Type II, formal SLA, and quarterly performance reviews.
- Tier 2 (Moderate): Vendors with internal access or moderate data. Controls: security questionnaire, semi-annual review.
- Tier 3 (Low): Standard SaaS with no sensitive data. Controls: standard contract review and annual renewal check.
sections.heading: Risk tiers and controls

sections.body:
- Revoke access within 24 hours of contract end.
- Retrieve company assets and credentials.
- Confirm data deletion per contract (evidence uploaded to vendor portal).

6) Travel Policy (high level)
sections.heading: Offboarding

sections.body:
- All international travel requires trip request submitted to People Ops with manager approval at least 14 days in advance.
- Domestic travel: manager approval suggested 7 days in advance.
sections.heading: Booking and approvals

sections.body:
- Economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business for flights over 6 hours or for VP+ roles with pre-approved exceptions.
- Use company-approved hotels and negotiated rates where available.
sections.heading: Preferred vendors and class of service

sections.body:
- Meals: per diem $75/day domestic, $100/day international (adjusted per country where policy provides).
- Incidentals require receipts for reimbursement.
sections.heading: Per diem and reimbursements

sections.body:
- Submit receipts and expense report within 7 days of trip completion.
- People Ops audits 10% of travel reports quarterly for policy compliance.
sections.heading: Expense submission and audit

sections.body:
- Employees traveling to high-risk geographies must enroll in the company travel safety program and notify People Ops.

7) Internal Templates and Quick References
sections.heading: Safety & security

sections.body:
- Access Request Template (ACCESS-REQ form)
- RFC Template (CHG-RFC) with rollout and roll-back checklist
- Vendor Intake Form and Security Questionnaire
- Standard Procurement SOW and PO Checklist
- Expense Report Template and Corporate Card Usage Guide
- Incident Notification Templates for Data and Security events

How to use templates: Create a copy of the canonical template page, fill required fields, attach artifacts (test results, screenshots), and link the artifact in the Jira ticket.

8) Exceptions, Waivers, and Continuous Improvement

- Exceptions: Must be requested via the policy exceptions tracker and include mitigation plans, owner, and expiration date. Executive approval required for exceptions > 90 days.
- Periodic review: This document will be reviewed annually by Finance & Legal with input from Security and People Ops.
- Continuous improvement: Teams should file process improvement requests in the OPERATIONS-IMPR Jira board.

Appendices

A. Contact directory: (roles repeated)
- Access Admins: access-admin@redwood.example.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Vendor Risk: vendor-risk@redwood.example.com
- Travel/People Ops: travel@redwood.example.com
- Security incident reporting: security-alerts@redwood.example.com

B. Quick SLAs summary:
- Standard access requests: 24 hours
- Privileged access requests: 72 hours (target)
- RFC triage: 24-48 hours
- Procurement < $5k: 48 business hours
- Vendor onboarding (Tier 1): 10 business days typical

C. Links and References:
- Central Policy Index: /confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025
- Emergency Access Runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/emergency-access
- RFC project board: https://jira.redwood.example.com/projects/CHG-RFC
sections.heading: Included templates (links to Confluence templates)

sections.body:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Ava Martinez (initial consolidated library).
- 2026-02-15: Expanded procurement thresholds and added vendor tiering (edited by Ava Martinez).

If you have questions about scope, exceptions, or implementation guidance, contact the policy owner (finance-legal) or one of the operational owners listed above.

payload.page_title: Access & Procurement Fabric: Guidelines, Workflows, and Templates

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the 'fabric' that ties together access and permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and the internal templates used to operationalize these processes. It is intended for request owners, approvers, people-ops, security, finance, and engineering managers.

Scope

- All employees, contractors, and third-party vendors requesting access to Redwood systems or requesting procurement/expenses.
- All changes to production services that require approvals or coordination with SRE, security, or product.
- Vendor lifecycle from intake to offboarding.

Principles

1. Least privilege first: grant the minimum rights required and require periodic recertification.
2. Single source of truth: all approvals and requests are recorded in the Ops Portal (internal).
3. Separation of duties: procurement approvals are separate from access approvals.
4. SLA-driven responsiveness: preset SLAs for different request types.

Owners & Escalation Paths

- Access & Permissions: Owner - People Ops (owner: Laura Chen). Escalation: People Ops Lead -> Security Manager (Greta Andersson) -> CFO on exceptions.
- Change Management: Owner - Eng Platform (owner: Mateo Rios). Escalation: Platform Lead -> Eng SRE -> CTO for high-risk rollouts.
- Procurement & Expenses: Owner - Finance (owner: Arjun Mehta). Escalation: Finance Manager -> Head of Finance -> CFO.
- Vendor Onboarding: Owner - Security & Legal joint (owner: Priya Nair).

SLAs and Targets

- Standard access request (non-privileged): target 3 business days.
- Privileged access (admin, production DB, infra): target 5 business days + security review.
- Procurement request (<= $5k): target 2 business days.
- Procurement request (>$5k): target 5 business days + legal/vendor review.

Access & Permissions Lifecycle

1. Request submission: submit via Ops Portal -> Select request type: Access - Application / Access - Infra / Temporary Privilege.
2. Tiered approval: Manager -> App Owner -> Security (if privileged) -> People Ops finalization.
3. Provisioning: automation kicks a runbook (where available) or IT team performs manual provisioning.
4. Recertification: automated reminders at 90/180 days depending on sensitivity; revocation if not recertified.
5. Emergency access: time-limited approval via 'just-in-time' (JIT) workflow; all sessions audited and recorded.

Access Request Example (Ops Portal JSON payload)

{
  "request_type": "access",
  "resource": "project-redwood-prod-db",
  "role_requested": "db_reader",
  "justification": "Support analytics job for Q4 cost report",
  "requested_by": "jordan.kim@redwood.com",
  "manager_approval": "pending"
}

Approval Matrix (Summary Table)

| Request Type | Approver Chain | Financial Threshold | Security Review Required | Typical SLA |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Non-privileged access | Manager -> App Owner | N/A | No | 3 business days |
| Privileged access | Manager -> App Owner -> Security -> People Ops | N/A | Yes | 5 business days |
| Purchase <= $5k | Manager -> Finance approver | $0 - $5,000 | No | 2 business days |
| Purchase > $5k | Manager -> Finance -> Legal (+Vendor Security if SaaS) | > $5,000 | Yes | 5 business days |
| Vendor onboarding | Vendor Lead -> Security -> Legal -> Finance | Varies | Yes | 10 business days |

Change Management (Engineering and Platform)

- All changes to production services must be registered in the Change Log (Ops Portal -> Changes).
- Change categories: Standard (pre-approved low risk), Normal (planned, requires change review), Emergency (unplanned, requires post-facto review).
- Change Review Board (CRB): weekly meeting for Normal changes that could impact availability or cost. CRB membership: Platform Lead, SRE, Security, Product Owner.

Change Request Checklist

1. Title and short description.
2. Risk assessment (low/medium/high).
3. Rollout plan and migration steps.
4. Backout plan and expected recovery time.
5. Monitoring & alerting hooks.
6. Stakeholder notifications (customers if needed).

Data Management & Classification

- Data classification levels: Public, Internal, Sensitive, Regulated.
- Handlers must label datasets and S3 buckets with classification tags and retention policies.
- Access to Sensitive/Regulated data requires additional approvals, data processing agreement (if external), and encryption at rest and transit.

Procurement & Expenses Workflow

1. Create procurement ticket in Ops Portal and attach vendor quote.
2. Include business justification and expected budget line (GL code).
3. Manager approval required for all purchases.
4. Finance performs spend validation and issues PO for approved vendors.
5. For SaaS vendors, require security & privacy questionnaire completion before PO if handling company data.

Procurement Approval Thresholds (Quick Reference)

- Up to $500: Manager discretionary; submit expense form and receipt.
- $501 - $5,000: Manager approval + Finance routing.
- $5,001 - $50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review.
- > $50,000: Exec sponsor + Finance + Legal + Procurement committee.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (minimum)

- Intake form completed with vendor contact and scope.
- Business justification and SOW or quote attached.
- Security questionnaire (SIG or vendor-specific) completed.
- Data processing agreement signed if vendor processes personal data.
- Procurement/PO issued and vendor entered into vendor registry.
- Key rotation and access expiry timeline agreed.

Vendor Offboarding

- Notify vendor of contract termination in accordance with contract terms.
- Revoke all credentials and API keys.
- Collect confirmation of data deletion or return per DPA.
- Update vendor registry and archive contract documents.

Travel & Expense Guidelines (high level)

- Preferred travel booking channels: company travel partner or expense portal.
- Per diem and meal caps referenced on the Expense Template.
- Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Higher-risk travel to regulated regions requires Security review and travel authorization form.

Templates (attached in the portal)

- Access Request Form (template ID: AR-2026): for employee and contractor access requests.
- Procurement Request Form (PR-2026): captures cost center, GL code, justification, vendor details.
- Vendor Intake Checklist (VI-2026): minimal fields for security and legal gating.
- Change Request Template (CR-2026): includes rollback plan and monitoring.
- Travel Authorization & Expense Template (TE-2026): per diem rates and receipt checklist.

Template Example (Procurement Request YAML)

requester: jordan.kim@redwood.com
department: Engineering
vendor: Acme Analytics
amount: 4200
gl_code: 5102
justification: Quarterly license for data pipeline profiling tool
required_by: 2026-02-01
approvers:
  - manager: rachel.turner@redwood.com
  - finance: arjun.mehta@redwood.com

Operational Playbook (step-by-step for a typical purchase)

1. Requester opens PR-2026, attaches quote and security questionnaire (if SaaS).
2. Manager approves in Ops Portal and selects GL code.
3. Finance reviews and either approves or requests clarifications.
4. If vendor handles data, Security triggers vendor review (up to 5 business days).
5. Legal drafts or reviews contract and DPA where necessary.
6. Finance issues PO and instructs Accounts Payable on payment terms.
7. Post-procurement: procurement record updated and vendor added to registry.

Audit & Reporting

- Quarterly audits on access recertification and high-value procurement (> $25k).
- Finance publishes a monthly spend dashboard by department and vendor.
- Security publishes a vendor risk dashboard showing outstanding questionnaires and remediation status.

Common Questions & Answers

Q: How do I get emergency access to production for a customer-critical fix?
A: Use the JIT workflow in Ops Portal and select Emergency access. The request will route to the on-call SRE and Security for immediate review; approvals can be retrospective but must include a full post-mortem within 3 business days.

Q: Who pays for consultant travel?
A: Consultant travel must be included in the SOW and pre-approved by Finance; expense claims must follow the standard expense template and manager review.

Change History

- 2025-08-12: Created by Nina Kowalski.
- 2025-11-03: Added vendor onboarding checklist and procurement thresholds (reviewers: Arjun Mehta).
- 2026-01-15: Published: clarified SLAs and added JIT access flow.

Related resources (internal links)

- Ops Portal: https://internal.ops-portal.redwood.corp/
- Vendor Registry: https://internal.vend-registry.redwood.corp/
- Security Questionnaire (SIG): https://internal.security.redwood.corp/sig

Appendix A — Example Ticket Titles

- "Access request: project-redwood-data-warehouse - db_reader"
- "Purchase request: Acme Analytics license - $4,200"
- "Change request: kube-node-autoscaling rollout - Normal"

Appendix B — Contacts

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (Laura Chen)
- Finance: finance-requests@redwood.com (Arjun Mehta)
- Security: security-ops@redwood.com (Greta Andersson)
- Legal: legal@redwood.com (Priya Nair)

payload.page_title: Passport to Access, Change, Vendor & Travel Operations

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates company-wide operational policies for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding/management, and travel. It provides prescriptive workflows, approval matrices, owners, and reusable templates for consistent execution across teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to: All Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or representing Redwood externally.
Applies to systems: Cloud accounts, on-prem infrastructure, Redwood Console, internal business systems (finance, HR, ticketing), and private deployments where Redwood personnel provide support.
Exclusions: Tactical team-level processes that do not touch company identity, financial approvals, or customer-sensitive data.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege by default: Roles must grant the minimum permissions needed for the job.
- Explicit approval trail: All access, changes, and vendor contracts must be traceable to an approver.
- Risk-based controls: Higher-sensitivity assets require stronger controls (MFA, periodic certification, contractual SLAs).
- Periodic review: Access and vendor risk assessments on a defined cadence.

Roles & Ownership (quick reference)
-------------------------------
- People Ops: Access policy governance, onboarding/offboarding audit, role catalog maintenance.
- Security: RBAC design, privileged access reviews, vendor security questionnaires.
- Finance & Legal: Procurement thresholds, contract sign-off, vendor PO issuance.
- Team Leads: Day-to-day access approvers, change approvers within scope, expense approvers.
- IT/Platform: Implement access grants (IAM), change rollouts for infra services, monitoring.
- Vendor Manager: Vendor onboarding, SLA tracking, quarterly business reviews (QBRs).

Access & Permissions
--------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default. No permanent user-level "root" accounts; break-glass exceptions require formal approval.
- MFA is required for all interactive accounts; keys rotating every 90 days for service principals.
- Sensitive resource classification: Confidential (customer PII, private keys), Internal, Public. Confidential resources require two-step approval.

Onboarding flow (standard user)
1. Request: Team lead fills Access Request Template (see Appendix). Submit via ticketing system with business justification.
2. Approval: People Ops + Team Lead sign-off for standard roles. Security review required for access to Confidential resources.
3. Provisioning: IT/Platform uses iamctl to create role bindings. Example commands:
   - iamctl create-role-binding --principal user:alice@redwood.ai --role data-analyst --scope project:telemetry
   - iamctl grant --service-account svc-reporting --role read-only-storage
4. Record: Ticket updated with grant details and entitlement expiration if temporary.

Temporary elevated access & emergency escalation
- Temporary access is granted for a maximum of 7 days by default. Extensions require re-approval.
- Emergency (break-glass) process:
  1) Engineer requests emergency access via the incident channel, tagging security and oncall.
  2) Security issues a one-time ephemeral token (valid 2 hours) and logs the request in the incident ticket.
  3) Post-incident: Owner must file a retrospective and certify that temporary credentials were revoked within 24 hours.

Periodic reviews
- Quarterly role entitlement review (People Ops + Team Leads).
- High-privilege users review every 30 days (Security owner).
- Automation: iamctl export-entitlements --since 90d | ./scripts/entitlement-audit.sh

Change Management
-----------------
sections.heading: Policy summary

sections.body:
- Standard: Pre-approved, low-risk routine changes (config tweaks, minor infra scaling) executed via CI with no extra approval.
- Normal: Planned changes that require RFC, owner approval, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency: Unplanned changes to restore service (follow emergency access flow above).

Approval matrix (examples)
- Low risk (<$5k impact, non-customer facing): Team Lead approval.
- Medium risk (>= $5k or customer-facing impact): Team Lead + Platform owner.
- High risk (security or PII impact, infra changes affecting >1 region): Team Lead + Security + Platform + People Ops for communications.

Change request process (normal change)
1. Create RFC in the change registry with: description, rollback plan, test plan, impact window, owner.
2. Review: Platform/Service owner performs technical review within 48 hours.
3. Approve: Approvals collected (digital sign-off in the ticketing system).
4. Schedule: Schedule in maintenance calendar and notify affected stakeholders 72 hours prior.
5. Execute & Validate: Runbook executed, smoke tests, and post-deploy verification.
6. Close: Post-change report filed within 24 hours of completion.

Emergency changes
- Tag RFC as EMERGENCY and follow 2-hour post-incident postmortem SLA. Root cause and mitigations must be documented.

Data Management
---------------
sections.heading: Change types

sections.body:
- Confidential: Customer PII, private keys, audit logs. Encryption at rest + access limited to named roles. Retention policy: default 7 years for audit logs, PII retention per contract.
- Internal: Company emails, internal metrics. Retention: 2 years unless business need.
- Public: Marketing materials, public docs. No special retention.
sections.heading: Classification levels

sections.body:
- Confidential data must not be used in development environments without masking. Use synthetic datasets or the data-masking service (maskit).
- Backups containing Confidential data must be encrypted and stored in the locked vault bucket (s3://redwood-vault).
- Data access requests for Confidential data require Data Steward approval and a documented business justification.

Data deletion and retention
- Data deletion requests are processed by the Data Steward team within 30 calendar days.
- Retention exceptions require approval from Legal + Data Steward and must be logged.

Procurement & Expenses
----------------------
Approval thresholds (examples)
- <$1,000: Team Lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Team Lead + Finance reviewer.
- >$25,000: Finance + Legal + VP-level approval.

Procurement flow (vendor goods/services)
1. Requisition: Requester files a Purchase Request (PR) with justification, cost center, and preferred vendor.
2. Finance review: Finance validates budget availability and assigns a PO number for approved requests.
3. Legal review: For contracts > $25k or handling Confidential data, Legal performs standard review.
4. PO issuance & payment: Accounts payable issues PO and processes payment upon invoice receipt.

Expense policy highlights
- Travel: Book through approved travel partner or travel@redwood.ai. Personal upgrades must be paid out-of-pocket.
- Per diem: US domestic: $75/day; International: country-dependent (see Appendix).
- Receipt requirements: All expenses >$25 require scanned receipt.

Vendor Management
-----------------
Onboarding checklist
1. Vendor intake form submitted (business case, contact, services provided).
2. Security questionnaire (SIG-lite) completed and reviewed by Security.
3. Contract terms reviewed by Legal (include data residency, breach notification SLA, indemnity).
4. PO or contract signed and linked to vendor record.
5. Vendor added to vendor registry and scheduled for first QBR within 90 days.

SLAs & monitoring
- Standard vendor SLA expectations: 99.5% uptime for production services, 24h initial response for critical incidents.
- Vendor Manager maintains vendor scorecard: availability, response SLAs, quarterly NPS.

Offboarding
- Termination checklist: confirm data return or secure deletion, revoke credentials, close open POs, final invoice reconciliation, document lessons learned.

Travel Policy (summary)
----------------------
Booking rules
- Use corporate travel portal for flights/hotels. Exceptions require manager approval.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; premium economy allowed for flights > 6 hours with approval.

Reimbursement and per diem
- Use expense system to submit within 30 days of travel.
- Meals and incidental receipts must be itemized for claims above per diem.

Health & safety
- Employees traveling to high-risk countries must register with People Ops and complete safety training.
- Company will not approve travel to locations flagged in the Travel Risk Matrix without exec sign-off.

Communications & Templates
-------------------------
sections.heading: Handling rules

sections.body:
- Access Request Template (fields: requester, role, justification, expiry)
- Vendor Risk Assessment checklist (SIG-lite excerpt)
- Change Request (RFC) template with rollback steps and smoke tests
- Travel approval form with destination risk and itinerary summary

Appendix A — Access Request Template (example)
---------------------------------------------
Requester: __________________
Team: ______________________
Requested role(s): ___________
Business justification: _______
Requested duration (if temporary): __days
Approvals: Team Lead / Security (if needed) / People Ops

Appendix B — Vendor Risk Assessment (excerpt)
--------------------------------------------
- Does vendor store Confidential data? (Y/N)
- Data residency requirements satisfied? (Y/N)
- Has vendor completed SOC2 or equivalent? (Y/N)
- Incident notification SLA <= 72 hours? (Y/N)
- PII handling: encryption at rest/in transit? (Y/N)

Appendix C — Sample RFC YAML
---------------------------
```yaml
id: RFC-2025-045
title: Migrate telemetry workers to new autoscaler
owner: samira@redwood.ai
risk: medium
impact_window: 2025-08-14T01:00Z/2025-08-14T03:00Z
rollback_steps:
  - scale down new autoscaler
  - revert deployment image to v1.12.2
smoke_tests:
  - curl -f https://telemetry.redwood.ai/health
  - check metrics: telemetry_items_processed > 100/min after 10m
approvals: [team_lead, platform_owner]
```

Operational SLAs & KPIs
----------------------
- Access provisioning: 95% of standard role requests fulfilled within 2 business days.
- Change review SLA: Technical review completed within 48 hours for planned changes.
- Vendor QBR cadence: first QBR within 90 days of onboarding; quarterly thereafter.

Governance & Exceptions
----------------------
- Exceptions to these policies require documented approval from People Ops + Security + Finance, and must include a sunset date.
- Noncompliance escalations: team lead -> department head -> People Ops -> Legal. Repeated violations may result in access suspension.

How to use this playbook
------------------------
- Copy templates from the Appendix to create tickets.
- Follow the approval matrix above; when in doubt, escalate to Security or People Ops.
- For system-level changes, create an RFC and reference this playbook in the ticket.

Document maintenance
--------------------
Owner: People Ops
Review cadence: Annual full review; targeted updates when regulatory or business changes occur.
Change log: See page history for detailed edits.

Contacts
--------
- People Ops (access policy): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security (privileged access): security@redwood.ai
- Finance (procurement): procurement@redwood.ai
- Vendor Management: vendors@redwood.ai
