payload.page_title: Request-to-Contract Playbook: Access, Procurement, Vendor & Travel Guidance

sections.body: This playbook documents a single, cohesive operational flow from an internal request (access, expense, travel, or procurement) through approval to execution and contract closeout. It is intended for managers, requestors, finance partners, security, and vendor teams. The goal is to reduce cycle time, centralize audit evidence, and ensure consistent risk controls for vendor onboarding and sensitive access.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and partners requesting:
  - System access and elevated permissions
  - Hardware or software procurement (including cloud credits and ML instance reservations)
  - Vendor engagements (SOWs, MSA, pilots)
  - Business travel and associated expense requests
- Excludes: petty cash reimbursements under $50 (see Finance petty-cash policy).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Principle of least privilege for access requests.
- Segregation of duties across requestor, approver, and approver-within-security/finance for high-risk actions.
- Evidence-first procurement: every spend must have a request, approval, and an owner.
- Centralized vendor records and contract indexing for discoverability and audits.
sections.heading: Key principles

sections.body:
- Follow the numbered workflow for the request type.
- Use the included templates (Access Request, Procurement Request, Vendor Checklist, Travel Pre-Approval) and attach to the ticket.
- Escalate via the incident-channel if approvals exceed SLA windows.

1) Roles & Responsibilities (high level):
- Requestor: initiates request, provides justification, attaches attachments, and responds to clarifying questions.
- Line Manager / Budget Owner: confirms business need and approves budget.
- Finance Approver: verifies budget coding and cost center alignment.
- Security Reviewer: reviews access requests with sensitive scopes, approves vendor security posture for contracts.
- Procurement / Legal: reviews contract terms above threshold or non-standard terms.
- Vendor Owner: Redwood employee who will own the vendor relationship and renewal.
sections.heading: How to use this playbook

sections.body:
- Access request <= 30 days: Requestor (R), Manager (A), Security (C), IT Ops (I)
- Purchase order <= $10k: Requestor (R), Manager (A), Finance (C), Procurement (I)
- Contract > $50k or data-bearing vendor: Requestor (R), Manager (C), Finance (C), Legal (A), Security (A)

2) Access & Permissions Workflow:
Purpose: Provide a fast, auditable process for granting, reviewing, and revoking access.
SLOs: initial decision within 2 business days for standard requests; expedited same-day for critical production emergency access.
sections.heading: RACI at a glance (examples)

sections.body:
1. Requestor submits "Access Request" form in company service portal. Required fields: system, role, justification, duration (if temporary), data sensitivity classification.
2. Automated pre-checks: portal validates requestor's manager, current last access review date, and whether request is for privileged tooling.
3. Manager approval: manager verifies business justification and duration.
4. Security review (if sensitive or privileged): security annotates required controls (MFA, IP restrictions, log forwarding) and approves or requests mitigations.
5. IT ops executes access change and documents ticket with audit evidence (user added, policy applied).
6. Scheduled re-certification: all temporary elevated accesses auto-expire; permanent roles appear on quarterly access review reports.
sections.heading: Step-by-step

sections.body:
- Immediate revocation for terminated employees or contractors (HR/IT automation).
- For inactive accounts > 90 days, access is automatically disabled pending owner review.

Access Request template (example YAML snippet to paste into a ticket):
---
request_type: access
requestor: maya.patel@redwood.ai
system: model-inference-console
role_requested: inference-operator
justification: Debugging production latency spikes during rollout
duration_days: 14
data_classification: internal
approvals_required: [manager, security]
attachments: [runbook-link, incident-id]
---

3) Change Management (service & infra changes):
Purpose: Ensure changes are planned, communicated, and reversible while minimizing production impact.
sections.heading: Revocation policy

sections.body:
- Standard: pre-approved, low-risk operational changes (e.g., routine backup config tweak). Notified via changelog.
- Normal: scheduled planned changes requiring CAB sign-off for changes > scheduled window or affecting >1 region.
- Emergency: unplanned changes to restore service. Post-facto review required.
sections.heading: Change categories and approvals

sections.body:
1. Submit Change Request with: scope, rollback plan, impact analysis, execution window, monitoring plan, owner.
2. Risk assessment by SRE: categorize as low/medium/high. High requires legal/SEC review if data-bearing.
3. CAB review: for medium/high, present during weekly CAB meeting or urgent CAB if timeline short.
4. Approval: CAB decision recorded with explicit owners and fallbacks.
5. Execute during scheduled window; SRE monitors and records metrics (error rate, latency, token throughput).
6. Post-change review: publish brief change summary and lessons learned within 3 business days.
sections.heading: Change process (normal)

sections.body:
1. Declare emergency in the incident channel.
2. Authorize a single emergency owner (normally SRE on-call).
3. Execute rollback-first strategy where possible; capture all actions for post-facto review.
4. Within 48 hours, produce a Change Review document linking to incident postmortem.

4) Data Management Requirements:
- Data classification: public / internal / restricted / regulated. All vendor contracts must include data classification mapping and handling clauses.
- Minimum controls for restricted data: encrypted-at-rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, customer-managed keys (if required), access logs retained 365 days.
- Data retention and deletion: owners must document retention periods in the request; automated deletion or archival workflows must be in place for regulated datasets.
sections.heading: Emergency change playbook

sections.body:
- Does vendor process restricted or regulated data? (Y/N)
- Can the vendor sign required BAA / DPA? (Y/N)
- Encryption and key management options documented.
- Location of data centers and EU-residency alignment noted.

5) Procurement & Expenses:
sections.heading: Data checklist for vendor onboarding

sections.body:
- Up to $5k: Manager sign-off.
- $5k - $50k: Manager + Finance approval; Procurement looped for vendor setup.
- > $50k: Manager + Finance + Legal + Procurement + Security (if data handled).
sections.heading: Procurement thresholds and approval matrix

sections.body:
1. Requestor files Procurement Request with business case, estimated TCO, preferred vendor, and draft SOW (if applicable).
2. Finance verifies budget and cost center.
3. Procurement evaluates vendor, requests commercial terms, and runs economical comparisons.
4. Legal negotiates terms; execute MSA/PO.
5. Finance issues PO and creates cost coding.
6. Vendor setup: Procurement creates vendor record, tax/ACH info, and ensures onboarding documents are stored in the contract index.
sections.heading: Contracting steps (request to contract)

sections.body:
- All travel must be pre-approved via Travel Pre-Approval form for reimbursement eligibility.
- Per diem rules: domestic $75/day, international variable by region (see Travel appendix).
- Card usage: corporate card holders may transact up to $10k per month per card; above that requires pre-approval from Finance.
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
{
  "request_type": "procurement",
  "requestor": "liam.chen@redwood.ai",
  "vendor": "Acme-ModelOps",
  "estimated_annual_cost": "42000",
  "business_case": "Managed model monitoring integration for inference quality alerts",
  "approvals_required": ["manager","finance","procurement"]
}

6) Vendor Management Lifecycle:
Stages: request -> security & risk review -> commercial negotiations -> onboarding -> quarterly review -> renewal/exit.
sections.heading: Procurement request JSON example (paste into portal)

sections.body:
- Initial vendor questionnaire (standard 40-question assessment) for any vendor with production access or data handling.
- For vendors processing regulated data, require SOC2 Type II or equivalent and a dedicated security review.
- Pilot engagements limited to 3 months by default unless otherwise approved.
sections.heading: Security & risk gating

sections.body:
- Signed MSA or PO
- Vendor contact and escalation matrix
- Security questionnaire completed and approved
- Data processing addendum (if required)
- Payment and tax forms on file
- Assigned Redwood vendor owner
sections.heading: Vendor onboarding checklist (required artifacts)

sections.body:
- Vendor owner completes a short quarterly health check: uptime SLA conformance, incidents in period, cost vs. value memo, renewal recommendation.

7) Travel & Expense Guidance:
Pre-approval required for any travel outside your home region or for travel where cost > $750.
sections.heading: Quarterly vendor review

sections.body:
- Use the corporate travel portal for flights and hotels where available.
- Economy for flights under 8 hours; premium economy / business for flights > 8 hours when approved.
- Hotels: select one-star-tier above the venue minimum for safety and proximity.
Expense submission: attach receipts, conference agenda, and pre-approval ID. Submit within 14 days of trip completion.
sections.heading: Travel booking guidance

sections.body:
- Expenses submitted without pre-approval may be denied or routed for manager remediation with potential payroll offsets if non-reimbursable.

8) Templates & Forms (attached here as examples to copy):
- Access Request (fields: requestor, system, role, justification, duration, approvers)
- Procurement Request (fields: requestor, vendor, TCO, contract term, approvals)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (link to central questionnaire)
- Travel Pre-Approval (fields: traveler, purpose, budget code, estimated cost, manager approval)

9) Audit, Reporting & Metrics:
- Monthly procurement spend report by cost center and vendor owner.
- Quarterly access review results with remediation counts (goal: <=5 exceptions per quarter).
- Vendor risk dashboard: number of vendors processing regulated data, pending questionnaires, and high-risk escalations.

10) Escalation & Exceptions:
- If approvals exceed SLA (2 business days for access, 5 business days for procurement < $50k), the requestor may ping the appropriate approver and escalate to the owner team lead.
- Exceptions to policy must be documented with a temporary exception request and retained in the contract index. Exceptions expire within 90 days unless renewed.

Appendix A — Example RACI table (ascii):
Role             | Requestor | Manager | Finance | Procurement | Legal | Security | IT/Ops
-----------------|-----------|---------|---------|-------------|-------|----------|--------
Access (standard)| R         | A       | I       | I           | I     | C        | R
Procure <$5k     | R         | A       | C       | I           | I     | I        | I
Contract >$50k   | R         | C       | C       | C           | A     | A        | I

Appendix B — Sample evidence checklist for audits:
- Access tickets with approval chain and timestamps.
- Signed MSAs or PO attachments in contract index.
- Vendor security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence if applicable.
- Travel pre-approval forms and receipts.
- Change requests with risk assessment and post-change notes.
sections.heading: Noncompliance and recovery

sections.body:
- Document owner: Finance-legal Ops (Maya Patel).
- Review cadence: annual policy review (owner initiates in Q4) or sooner when regulatory change occurs.
- Change log: record substantive updates in the portal changelog with links to versioned artifacts.
sections.heading: Ownership & maintenance

sections.body:
- Contract index (internal link)
- Security questionnaire (internal link)
- Finance portal / expense submission
- IT service portal (access requests)
sections.heading: Related resources and links

sections.body:
- policy-questions@redwood.ai (for interpretations)
- procurement@redwood.ai (vendor & procurement questions)
- security@redwood.ai (access and vendor security)

End of playbook.

payload.page_title: integrated-ops-toolkit-access-to-travel-2029

sections.body:
Overview
=======
This document is a single, practical toolkit combining company-wide procedures and forms for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel policies. It is designed for cross-functional teams (engineering, finance, security, people-ops) to follow a consistent, auditable process. Use the templates and checklists below when opening requests or executing approvals.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Relevant for hosted, dedicated, and private deployment engagements.
- Auditable by Security and Finance during reviews and audits.

Goals
-----
- Reduce approval latency for low-risk requests while enforcing controls for regulated activities.
- Provide templates that standardize requests and vendor assessments.
- Ensure data handling and retention align with classification levels.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy custodianship).
- Operational owners: Security (access, data classification), Eng-SRE (change runbooks), Procurement (vendor onboarding).
- Escalation path: requestor -> requestor's manager -> owner_team lead -> Head of Finance/Head of Security as required.

Quick reference: decision matrix
--------------------------------
| Area | Low risk (auto/manager) | Medium risk (2 approvers) | High risk (committee) |
| Access to internal services | Manager approval | Security + Manager | Security Committee |
| Change to runtime infra | N/A | Eng-sre + Product | Emergency CAB |
| Vendor procurement (<= $25k) | Procurement manager | Procurement + Finance | Legal + Exec |
| Travel reimbursement (<= $1,000) | Manager approval | Finance + Manager | Exec approval |

Access & permissions procedure
------------------------------
1) Request initiation
   - Use the Access Request template in the Request Tracker (confluence link: /requests/access).
   - Required fields: service name (e.g. redwood-control-plane, serving-runtime), role requested, business justification, data access level.
2) Data classification check
   - Classify data involved: PUBLIC | INTERNAL | RESTRICTED | REGULATED. See Data Management section for retention and handling rules.
3) Approval and provisioning
   - Low risk: manager approves in the Request Tracker; IAM ticket is auto-created and provisioned by platform-auth bot (approx latency: 4 hours).
   - Medium/high risk: Security review completed within 2 business days. Provisioning requires documented justification and an expiration (default 90 days unless otherwise approved).
4) Post-provision audit
   - Automated weekly IAM delta report to owners; access with no activity for 60 days is flagged for review.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
policy: |
  version: 1
  statement:
    - effect: allow
      action: ["kv:Read", "object:Get"]
      resource: "arn:redwood:storage:us-west-2:account:embeddings/*"
      condition: { "StringEquals": { "redwood:Role": "ml-researcher" } }

Change management (engineering systems)
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Minimize service disruption while enabling frequent, auditable deployments.

Change categories
- Standard change: pre-approved, repeatable (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal change: requires review and scheduled window.
- Emergency change: applied outside normal windows; post-facto CAB review required.

Procedure (normal change)
1) Create a Change Request ticket in CHANGE-BOARD with: summary, impact analysis, rollback plan, monitoring playbook, owner, and target window.
2) Peer review: two engineers (one from owning service) review design.
3) Security review if data-scope includes RESTRICTED/REGULATED.
4) Canaries: deploy to 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Metrics to monitor: latency p50/p95, error rate, token throughput, KV cache hit rate.
5) Full rollout: expand in windows (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated health gates.
6) Post-deploy: complete change ticket with metrics and retrospective if SLO breach or unexpected errors.

Telemetry gates (example thresholds)
| Metric | Canary threshold | Full rollout threshold |
| error_rate | < 0.5% | < 0.7% |
| p95_latency | < 800ms | < 1.2s |

Rollback steps (if threshold exceeded)
1) Trigger automated rollback: revert to previous model revision or config snapshot.
2) Notify oncall via PagerDuty runbook for serving-runtime.
3) Open postmortem within 48 hours if rollback occurred.

Data management: classification and retention
-------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Grant read-access to embeddings store

sections.body:
- PUBLIC: No restrictions. Retention: business default.
- INTERNAL: Access by employees only. Retention: 2 years default unless specified.
- RESTRICTED: Encrypt at rest with customer KMS, access-by-approval; retention: 7 years for auditable datasets.
- REGULATED: Subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., GDPR/CCPA financial/personal data). Retention: per contract.

Data retention policy examples
| Data type | Classification | Default retention | Owner |
| logs (application) | INTERNAL | 365 days | Eng-SRE |
| customer-audit-logs | REGULATED | 7 years | Security + Finance |
| embeddings derived from customer data | RESTRICTED | contract dependent | Research + Legal |

Procurement and vendor management
---------------------------------
sections.heading: Classification levels and handling rules

sections.body:
- <= $2,500: Team budget owner sign-off (submit PR in Procurement system).
- $2,500–$25,000: Procurement + Finance approval.
- > $25,000: Legal review + Exec sponsor.

Vendor onboarding checklist
1) Business case and budget entry.
2) Security questionnaire (SSQ) completed: must score > 75% for low risk.
3) Contract template: use Standard SaaS Agreement (procurement library).
4) Data processing addendum (DPA) required if vendor handles RESTRICTED/REGULATED data.
5) KMS/HSM integration review if vendor will hold keys.
6) Insurance and SOC2 evidence collected.
7) Operational contacts & escalation list captured in vendor record.

Vendor scorecard fields (example)
- Security posture (SOC2, encryption)
- Data residency and compliance (regions, DPA)
- Financial stability (3-year run rate)
- Support SLAs and escalation channels
- Price & terms (TCO, termination)

Templates (to copy into the Procurement system)
- Vendor Scorecard CSV: vendor_name,security_score,dpa_required,annual_cost,sla_hours
- Contract clause snippet for data returns: "Upon termination, vendor will securely delete or return all customer data within 30 days and certify deletion."

Travel and expenses policy (concise)
-----------------------------------
sections.heading: Procurement thresholds & approvers

sections.body:
- Be economical; default to economy-class travel for flights < 6 hours.
- Use preferred vendors and booking portal for company rates.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.

Travel approval flow
1) Submit Travel Request form with purpose, itinerary, estimated cost, and approver (manager).
2) Travel > $1,000 requires Finance review. International travel with customer data access requires Security sign-off.
3) After travel: submit Expense Report with receipts within 7 business days. Expenses older than 30 days require CFO approval.

Per diem and limits (examples)
| Item | Limit | Notes |
| Meals | $75/day domestic | Higher for high-cost cities with prior approval |
| Lodging | $250/night domestic | Book in business rate; exceptions require manager approval |
| Ground transport | Actuals | Use shared rides when practical |

Expense templates and checklist
- Expense report fields: traveler, dates, client, purpose, line-item costs, receipts attached.
- Required receipt checklist: date, vendor, amount, card last4. Missing receipt action: manager justification + traveler attestation.

Audit & monitoring
------------------
- Monthly audit: Finance runs random sample of 5% of expense reports and 10% of vendor invoices.
- Quarterly access audit: Security reviews all accounts with RESTRICTED/REGULATED access.
- Change audit: Eng-SRE publishes quarterly change logs and incident rollups to the SRE dashboard.

Operational templates (copyable)
-------------------------------
1) Access Request (example text)
   - Summary: [one-line]
   - Service: [service name]
   - Role: [role]
   - Justification: [why access is needed]
   - Duration: [expiry date or permanent]
   - Data classification: [PUBLIC/INTERNAL/RESTRICTED/REGULATED]
2) Change Request (example text)
   - Summary, Impact, Rollback plan, Metrics to monitor, Owner, Rollout windows
3) Vendor Onboarding (example checklist)
   - Business case, SSQ score, DPA present, Contract signed, Escalation contacts
4) Travel Request (example text)
   - Traveler, Dates, Purpose, Estimated cost, Manager approver

Related procedures and links
---------------------------
- Security runbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security
- Procurement catalog and templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement
- Eng-SRE change runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

Appendices
---------
A. Example change ticket template (markdown)
```
Title: [service] – [change short summary]
Owner: [name]
Impact: [high/medium/low]
Rollback: [steps]
Canary plan: [traffic %, duration, metrics]
Monitoring: [dashboard links]
```

B. Vendor SSQ highlights (key questions)
- Encryption at rest/in transit? KMS integration?
- SOC2 Type II? Last audit date?
- Data residency and subprocessors?

C. Contact matrix
- Finance: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security-ops@redwood.com
- Platform-auth (provisioning): platform-auth-bot@redwood.com
- Oncall (serving-runtime): pagerduty "serving-runtime"

Change history
--------------
- 2025-08-12: Initial draft published by Priya Singh.
- 2025-11-03: Added vendor scorecard and SSQ threshold.
- 2026-02-10: Clarified travel approval thresholds and retention table.

payload.page_title: cross-company-operating-guides-2026

sections.body: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data governance, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It is intended as the single canonical reference for cross-functional teams and approvers.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or who conduct business on Redwood’s behalf.
- Describes mandatory approval matrices, minimum technical controls, and operational workflows.
- Distinguishes low-risk day-to-day actions from high-risk production changes and vendor commitments.
sections.heading: Scope and intent

sections.body:
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team).
- Day-to-day steward: IT & Security for access/data controls; Procurement for spend and vendor onboarding; People Ops for travel & expenses.
- Review cadence: annual review by owners; ad-hoc updates when legal/regulatory changes occur.

1) Access & Permissions (IAM)
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, enforce account hygiene, and provide repeatable provisioning/deprovisioning.
sections.heading: Governance and ownership

sections.body:
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Use standardized roles in the Identity Service (identity.redwood.internal). No permanent account should hold both Admin and Finance privileges.
- Provisioning flow (standard):
  1. Create Access Request using the Access Request template (link below).
  2. Manager approval required for non-admin roles. Security approval required for any IAM role granting write access to production namespaces.
  3. Provisioned by IT within SLA: 2 business days for non-prod, 4 hours for urgent prod if approved.
- MFA: Required for all interactive logins and CLI sessions; hardware 2FA is required for nominal admin roles.
- Account review: Quarterly access reviews; role owners must attest via the Access Attestation spreadsheet.
sections.heading: Key controls

sections.body:
```yaml
user: jane.doe@redwood.ai
request_reason: "Feature debugging - investigate latency regression in model-serving"
roles_requested:
  - svc-kv-readonly
  - dev-sandbox-writer
expiration: 2025-04-10
manager_approval: pending
security_approval: required
```

2) Change Management
All changes touching production systems follow the change process below. Non-production changes should follow lightweight review.
sections.heading: Example access request (YAML snippet)

sections.body:
- Standard change: Pre-approved, repeatable, documented maintenance (e.g., routine infra patching). CAB not required.
- Minor change: Low-risk config or code change; requires owner + SRE approval.
- Major change: Schema migrations, model rollouts, infra upgrades affecting >1 service; requires CAB approval and rollout plan.
sections.heading: Change categories and approval thresholds

sections.body:
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) using the CR template. Include rollback plan, test plan, blast radius, and monitoring playbook.
2. Owner and SRE review (48 hours). If Major, schedule for next CAB meeting (weekly).
3. Pre-production validation: run regression suite described in the CR and attach the logs.
4. Approve and schedule the window. Production change window: 02:00–04:00 UTC (default) unless business needs dictate otherwise.
5. Execution: one authorized executor only; notify #oncall and #incidents channels.
6. Post-change verification: run smoke checks and report using the post-change checklist within 2 hours.
7. If degraded, perform rollback steps defined in the CR and escalate per the incident playbook.
sections.heading: Process (numbered steps)

sections.body:
- Change approval SLA: 48 hours for Minor, 7 business days for Major (from submission to scheduled window).
- Post-change verification: 95% of changes must have green smoke checks within 2 hours.

3) Data Management and Classification
sections.heading: SLOs related to change process

sections.body:
- Restricted: Customer PII, payment data, export-controlled models. Encrypt at rest and in transit; access by exception only.
- Internal: Business operations data, internal dashboards. Encrypted at rest; access on need-to-know basis.
- Public: Documentation and marketing materials.
sections.heading: Classification labels

sections.body:
- Customer PII: default retention 90 days unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Logs: short-term debug logs 30 days; aggregated observability metrics retained 13 months.
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Request template and log to the governance tracker.
sections.heading: Retention and deletion

sections.body:
- Critical data (config, metadata, model artifacts) backed up daily with immutable snapshots; restore RTO target: 4 hours; RPO: 1 hour for critical objects.
- Annual restore rehearsals and quarterly partial restores for selected datasets.
sections.heading: Backups and DR

sections.body:
- Keys managed through Redwood KMS (kms.redwood.internal) or customer KMS for Private deployments. All production keys rotate at least every 12 months.

4) Procurement & Expenses
sections.heading: Encryption and key management

sections.body:
- <$5,000: Manager approval.
- $5,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- >$25,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review; Procurement team involvement required.
- Recurring subscriptions: treated like contracts and reviewed annually by Procurement.
sections.heading: Approval matrix (high level)

sections.body:
1. Submit Purchase Requisition with vendor, scope, and budget code.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor risk (SOC2, contracts) and creates PO.
3. Finance processes invoice on receipt and matches to PO.
sections.heading: Purchasing flow

sections.body:
- Corporate p-cards: restricted to approved cardholders and limited to <$5k per transaction by default.
- Travel advances: require People Ops approval and reconciliation within 30 days.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
sections.heading: Card and expense policies

sections.body:
- Confirm vendor legal entity and W9/W8 status.
- Security posture: ask for SOC2 Type II or equivalent; if not available, require risk assessment by Security.
- Contractual terms: data processing agreement, SLAs, data residency clauses if applicable.
sections.heading: Minimum due diligence checklist

sections.body:
1. Business sponsor completes Vendor Intake form.
2. Procurement runs due diligence and assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High).
3. Legal negotiates contract terms; Security ensures technical controls are adequate.
4. Vendor is added to vendor registry with owner and renewal date.
sections.heading: Onboarding steps (simplified)

sections.body:
- Quarterly reviews for strategic vendors; annual reviews for medium/high risk vendors.
- SLA targets documented in the vendor record; breach triggers escalation and remediation plan.

6) Travel Policy (business travel)
sections.heading: Vendor performance and reviews

sections.body:
- All trips must be pre-approved in Travel Request system with estimated cost and business justification.
- Use company-preferred vendors where available.
sections.heading: Booking and approvals

sections.body:
- Per diem standard rates mirror US GSA rates for domestic travel unless a negotiated vendor rate applies.
- Receipts required for any single expense >$75. Reimbursements submitted within 60 days.
sections.heading: Per diem and reimbursement

sections.body:
- If an employee is involved in an incident while traveling, notify People Ops immediately and file an Incident Report in the HR portal.

7) Standard Templates and Examples (links and text snippets)
- Access Request template: https://confluence.internal.redwood/access-requests (use the YAML example above as canonical).
- Change Request template: include intent, blast radius, rollback plan, and smoke tests.
- Vendor Intake template: fields for legal entity, contact, product, risk tier, SOC2 link.
- Expense report template: CSV and PDF forms available at Finance shared drive.
sections.heading: Safety and incident reporting

sections.body:
- Title, owner, impacted services (e.g., model-serving-api, kv-store, config-service)
- Test plan attached (unit, integration, e2e)
- Rollback steps validated in staging
- Monitoring and alerts configured for the window
- Communications plan for customers and internal stakeholders

Appendix A — Definitions and abbreviations:

- RPO: Recovery Point Objective

payload.page_title: Controls Symphony: Access, Procurement & Operational Patterns

sections.body:
Purpose

This playbook unifies the company-wide operational controls for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel approvals, and reusable templates. It is intended for cross-functional use (Engineering, Security, Finance, People Ops, and GTM) to reduce friction, shorten approval cycles, and ensure auditable, repeatable decisions.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood systems, cloud accounts, and corporate processes.
- Covers identity and access provisioning, privileged access, approved change windows, data classification and retention, procurement up to $2M, vendor onboarding and offboarding, and company travel expense policies.

Principles (summary)

- Least privilege by default: grant only what’s needed for 90-day periods.
- Separation of duties: approvals require distinct reviewers for budget/technical/security where applicable.
- Traceability: every access/grant/change/procurement decision must have a ticket (Jira/Concur/Contract ID).
- Risk-tiered controls: higher risk → stricter approvals and mandatory security review.

Ownership matrix

| Domain | Primary owner | Secondary owner | SLA for requests |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Access & Permissions | Identity & Access Team | Team Engineering Manager | 3 business days (standard) / 8 hours (urgent) |
| Change Management | Platform Ops | Service Owner | 48 hours pre-notice for standard changes |
| Data Management | Data Governance | Security | 5 business days for classification requests |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance Ops | Requesting Manager | 5 business days for approvals under $25k |
| Vendor Management | Procurement | Legal | 10 business days for standard vendors |
| Travel & Expenses | People Ops / Finance | Manager | 3 business days prior for international travel |

Access & Permissions (detailed)

1) Onboarding/Offboarding

- New hire access is initiated from People Ops via the Onboarding Jira template (ONB-Create-Access). Identity & Access provisions core accounts (Okta, GCP, AWS, GitHub) after background check and completion of policy acknowledgements.
- Offboarding checklist (mandatory): revoke SSO sessions, remove SSH keys, disable cloud console roles, rotate shared keys if user had privileged access, and log completion in ONB-Offboard ticket.

2) Role-based access and temporary elevation

- Define roles in the Roles Catalog (roles.redwood.internal). Use IAM groups mapped to job functions.
- For temporary privileged access (break-glass), request through the BreakGlass form; approvals required from Service Owner + Security Approver. Maximum duration: 8 hours. All activity must be audited and forwarded to Security within 24 hours.

3) Privileged key management

- Never store non-rotating private keys in user home directories. Use Vault (hashicorp) for secrets and HSM/KMS for production server keys. Automatic rotation schedule: 90 days for service keys, 30 days for developer tokens.

Change Management (process)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Create a change request in Jira (CHG-XXXX) with description, impacted services, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Classify change: Standard (no downtime), Planned (may affect SLOs), Emergency (security/production incident).
sections.heading: Steps for standard and emergency changes

sections.body:
- Standard change: Service Owner approval.
- Planned change: Service Owner + Platform Ops + optional Security review (if data-in-path).
- Emergency change: Triage with Oncall + Post-incident RFC within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Approval matrix

sections.body:
- Planned changes with potential customer impact must be announced on #status and scheduled on the status page 48 hours prior.

Data Management (summary & configs)
sections.heading: Notifications

sections.body:
- Public: No restrictions.
- Internal: Company employees only.
- Confidential: Access by role; encryption at rest & in transit required.
- Regulated: PII / PHI / Financial; additional contractual controls.
sections.heading: Classification levels

sections.body:
| Data Type | Retention | Responsible |
|---|---:|---|
| Application logs (non-PII) | 90 days | Eng SRE |
| Audit logs (IAM, Admin) | 3 years | Security |
| Customer datasets (regulated) | As contract requires | Customer Success + Legal |
sections.heading: Retention table

sections.body:
- All regulated and confidential data must be stored in customer-specific buckets with encryption (AES-256) and access logging enabled.
- Data exports must be approved by Data Governance and logged. Use the Data Export Request template (templates/data-export-request.md).

Procurement & Expenses (workflow & thresholds)
sections.heading: Data handling rules

sections.body:
- < $5,000: Manager approval in Concur.
- $5,000–$50,000: Manager + Finance Ops approval.
- $50,000–$500,000: Procurement + Finance Ops + Legal review (if contract).
- > $500,000: Executive procurement review + Legal + CFO sign-off.
sections.heading: Quick rules

sections.body:
1. Create a Purchase Request (PR) in Procurement tracker with business justification, preferred vendor, and budget code.
2. Finance Ops validates budget and assigns spend category.
3. Procurement engages vendor, negotiates terms, and routes contract to Legal if any custom terms.
4. PO issued only after approvals are complete.
sections.heading: Process (numbered)

sections.body:
- Per diem and travel class are defined in the Travel section. Receipts required for expenses > $25. Reimbursement submitted in Concur within 60 days. Expenses submitted after 120 days may be denied.

Vendor Management (lifecycle)
sections.heading: Expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Tier A (Critical): Access to production systems or regulated data. Mandatory SOC2/ISO assessment and annual review.
- Tier B (Standard): Business tools with no regulated data access. Annual attestation.
- Tier C (Low): Non-critical vendors (marketing assets, event services). Procurement checklist only.
sections.heading: Vendor risk tiers

sections.body:
- Business case and sponsor identified.
- Security questionnaire completed (vendor-security-questionnaire-v2.xlsx).
- Contract template used: contracts/vendor-standard-agreement.docx.
- Validate insurance and IP clauses.
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist

sections.body:
- Revoke vendor credentials and SSO.
- Disable API keys and rotate any shared secrets.
- Archive contract and record termination date.

Travel & Expenses (summary)

- Booking: Use Redwood Travel Portal (Concur). Manager approval required for air travel. Economy preferred under 6 hours; Premium Economy permitted for flights over 10 hours with manager consent.
- International travel: submit itinerary and local emergency contact 10 business days prior. Security review required for travel to high-risk countries (see Travel Risk Matrix).
- Expense categories: meals, lodging, ground transport, incidentals. Alcohol must be reasonable and documented.

Templates and Reusable Artifacts

- templates/onboarding-access-checklist.md
- templates/data-export-request.md
- templates/vendor-security-questionnaire-v2.xlsx
- templates/purchase-request-form.json
- templates/travel-itinerary-declaration.txt

Governance & Continuous Improvement

- Quarterly review cadence: Owners will meet monthly and produce a consolidated control report quarterly for the Audit Committee.
- Key metrics tracked: average access request time, number of emergency changes, procurement cycle time, vendor risk remediation rate. Target goals: access requests <= 3 days (90th percentile), procurement cycle <= 10 business days for <$50k.

Audit & Evidence collection

- Required evidence: Jira change tickets, Concur expense records, signed contracts, IAM grant logs, Vault access logs. Store evidence links in the Control Evidence tracker (controls-evidence.redwood.internal).

Appendix A — Example change request (sample JSON)

{
  "change_id": "CHG-2029-0001",
  "service": "inference-runtime",
  "type": "planned",
  "owner": "eng-platform@redwood.internal",
  "scheduled_window": "2029-02-17T02:00:00Z",
  "rollback_plan": "revert image tag to v1.12.3 and restart service",
  "test_plan": "smoke tests (latency < 150ms) and synthetic traffic at 10% of normal",
  "approvals": ["service-owner", "platform-ops", "security-if-data-in-path"]
}

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets

- Revoke AWS role (example): aws iam remove-role-from-instance-profile --instance-profile-name prod-app --role-name temp-debug-role
- Vault read (example): vault kv get secret/service/prod-db-creds

Frequently asked questions

Q: Who can approve vendor contracts?
A: Procurement can approve standard contracts up to $50k. Legal review required for custom terms. Executive approval required above $500k.

Q: What to do for product emergency changes during off hours?
A: Execute emergency change with Oncall and document in CHG ticket; produce post-incident RFC within 72 hours.

Related pages and links

- Central policy index: /confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025
- Roles Catalog: https://roles.redwood.internal
- Control Evidence tracker: https://controls-evidence.redwood.internal

Contact points

- Identity & Access: iam-support@redwood.internal
- Procurement & Vendors: procurement@redwood.internal
- Data Governance: datagov@redwood.internal

Change history

- 2028-11-15 — Initial draft, Isha Raman
- 2028-12-22 — Added vendor tiering and updated procurement thresholds (reviewers: Diego Alvarez, Maya Chen)
- 2029-02-10 — Published with travel policy updates and templates added

payload.page_title: Authorization Flowbook — Access, Procurement & Travel

sections.body:
Summary:
This Flowbook consolidates company-wide procedures for granting access and permissions, approving changes, managing data and retention, processing procurement and expenses, onboarding vendors, and authorizing business travel. The intent is to provide a single, actionable reference for requesters, approvers, and operational teams so approvals are fast, auditable, and aligned with security and budget guardrails.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who request access to systems, submit purchase requests, propose configuration or code changes, or travel on company business.
- Excludes purely personal reimbursements (see People Ops T&E exceptions) and one-off low-value reimbursements under $25.

Principles:
1) Least privilege: Grant the minimum access required and review every 90 days for non-admin roles.
2) Separation of duties: Requesters cannot self-approve purchases, access, or change deployments that materially affect their own services.
3) Risk-based approvals: Higher risk (data access, high dollar spend, code push to prod) requires stronger review.
4) Auditability: All requests must include business justification and be logged in central systems (AccessHub / ProcPortal).

Roles and Ownership:
- Requester: initiates the request with justification, cost center, and business owner.
- Approver: the named manager or cost-center owner; senior approver required for high-risk items.
- Security owner: reviews data-access and vendor security questionnaires.
- Procurement: validates vendor terms and preferred supplier status for purchases > $5k.
- Finance: verifies budget and issues PO for approved purchases.
- IT Ops / SRE: executes access provisioning, change coordination, and rollback if needed.

Access & Permissions:
Request flow:
1. Create an access request in AccessHub with: resource, role, duration, justification, business owner, and confidentiality level.
2. Immediate manager approval required for all requests.
3. Security owner review for any request that: grants access to PII, allows export, or touches model training data.
4. Audit tag assigned if request is >90 days or privileged.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Resource classification | Typical approver | Security review required | Auto-expiry |
|------------------------|------------------|-------------------------|-------------|
| Public docs            | Manager          | No                      | 365 days    |
| Internal non-sensitive | Manager          | No                      | 90 days     |
| Confidential (PII)     | Manager + SecOps | Yes                     | 30 days     |
| Admin/system-level     | Manager + IT Ops | Yes                     | 14 days     |

Re-certification:
- Every 90 days an automated recertification email is sent for non-admin roles. Unattended roles will be disabled after 14 days of non-response.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Temporarily granted via Emergency Access form with post-hoc justification and 24-hour security debrief. Any break-glass must be recorded and reviewed within 3 business days.

Change Management:
Change categories:
- Routine: low-risk config changes (non-prod) — schedule in regular maintenance window, manager approval.
- Standard: pre-approved, repeatable changes (e.g., certificate rotation) — CAB notification.
- Significant: code or infra changes impacting production — requires SRE sign-off and change runbook.
- Emergency: incident-driven changes — use Emergency Change process and record rollback plan.

Change procedure (significant changes):
1. Create Change Request (CR) in ChangeTracker with: description, owners, rollback plan, risk assessment, and test plan.
2. SRE and Product sign-off required.
3. Schedule canary and phased rollout with feature flags; communicate to oncall.
4. Post-deploy validation tasks and metrics to confirm behavior.
5. Post-change review within 5 business days; capture learnings in ChangeTracker.

Rollback criteria:
- Error rate > 1% above baseline for 10 minutes, latency SLO breach > 50ms increase, or critical customer impact. Pre-deploy canary thresholds must be defined in the CR.

Data Management:
Classification levels:
- Public: safe for external distribution.
- Internal: Redwood operational content; acceptable for internal collaboration.
- Confidential: employee PII, customer data, model training datasets.
- Restricted: regulated data (PCI, HIPAA).

Storage and handling rules:
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved buckets with customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and VPC-only access.
- Mask or tokenize PII before exporting from platform systems.
- Data retention: standard logs 90 days; model training datasets retention to be defined per project (default 2 years). Exceptions require Data Steward approval.

Data access review:
- Any dataset that contains Confidential or Restricted data must have an explicit Data Owner and an access approval recorded in AccessHub.

Procurement & Expenses:
Thresholds and approvals table:
| Amount (USD) | Required approvers | Procurement involvement |
|--------------|--------------------|------------------------|
| <$1,000      | Manager            | Optional               |
| $1,000–$5,000| Manager + Finance  | Procurement advisory   |
| $5,000–$50,000 | Manager + Procurement + Finance | Procurement required |
| >$50,000     | Exec sponsor + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Procurement & Legal required |

Preferred vendors and contract reuse:
- Procurement maintains a Preferred Supplier list. For common categories (cloud, GPUs, security tooling), use pre-negotiated contracts when possible to speed approvals.

Purchase flow (typical):
1. Requester submits Purchase Request in ProcPortal including SOW, vendor info, and business justification.
2. Procurement validates vendor terms and negotiates as needed for >$5k.
3. Finance confirms budget.
4. Legal reviews contract when >$50k or if non-standard clauses present.
5. PO issued; vendor is approved for payment.

Expense & Travel policy (high level):
- All business travel requires pre-approval via TravelRequest with estimated cost and trip purpose.
- Use company booking tool for flights; seat-class policy: economy for flights < 6 hours, premium-economy or equivalent on longer flights with manager approval.
- Per diem and per-trip lodging caps are published on the travel portal and vary by region (sample table below).

Travel caps by region (sample):
| Region | Daily per diem | Hotel cap/night |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| US     | $75            | $250            |
| EMEA   | 55 EUR         | 180 EUR         |
| APAC   | 8,000 JPY      | 25,000 JPY      |

Reimbursement timeline:
- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip end with receipts attached. Finance processes standard claims within 7 business days. Non-compliant items may be denied.

Vendor Management:
Onboarding checklist (minimum items):
- Vendor profile in VendorRegistry (legal name, tax ID, address).
- Security questionnaire completed (AIC or equivalent).
- Data processing agreement (DPA) signed if vendor processes Confidential or Restricted data.
- Insurance certificates verified for material engagements.
- SLAs and escalation contacts recorded.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual security attestation for vendors handling Confidential data.
- Quarterly contract performance review for strategic suppliers.

Templates and Examples:
- Purchase request JSON (sample):
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.com",
  "cost_center": "AI-TEAM-01",
  "vendor": "CloudGpus Ltd",
  "amount": "15000",
  "justification": "Dedicated GPU pool for model benchmarking"
}

- Access request example (form fields): resource, role, start_date, end_date, business_justification, approvals (manager, security if required).

- Change request checklist: description, owners, test plan, canary plan, rollback steps, monitoring runbook, communication list.

Operational controls and automation:
- All request systems must emit an event to the central audit log with metadata: request_id, requester, approvers, timestamps, and attachments.
- Automated guardrails: requests exceeding policy thresholds trigger a hold and a notification to Procurement and Security.

Exceptions and escalation:
- To request an exception (policy deviation), open an Exception Request in the Policy Portal with rationale, compensating controls, and a 90-day review cadence.
- Appeals: a three-person committee (Finance, Security, and Requester’s leader) reviews exceptions within 5 business days.

Enforcement and compliance:
- Random quarterly audits will be performed against a sample of access, procurement, and travel records. Findings may lead to disciplinary action or process revisions.

Appendix A — Quick links (internal):
- AccessHub: https://internal.accesshub.redwood/requests
- ProcPortal: https://internal.procportal.redwood/purchase-requests
- ChangeTracker: https://internal.change.redwood/changes
- VendorRegistry: https://internal.vendorregistry.redwood/vendors

Appendix B — Contact matrix:
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance: finance-ops@redwood.com
- Security: secops@redwood.com
- Travel support: travel@redwood.com

Revision history:
- 2026-06-15: Initial published version (A. Patel).
- 2026-09-01: Updated travel caps and procurement threshold clarifications (reviewers: D. Kim, S. Martinez).

Related resources and next steps:
- For implementers: integrate request webhooks to central audit log and enable automated expiry on AccessHub.
- Recommend cross-functional tabletop exercise to validate Emergency Change and Break-Glass procedures within the next quarter.

End of Flowbook.

payload.page_title: entitlements-and-purchase-pathways-playbook-2030

sections.body:
Overview
=======

Purpose: This playbook consolidates company-wide procedures for entitlements (access and permissions), change governance, data handling expectations, procurement and expense approvals, vendor lifecycle management, and travel approvals. It is intended for all Redwood employees and contractors who request or approve resources, commit changes to production, or manage third-party relationships.

Scope: Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployment teams, platform and infra teams, procurement interactions, people-ops travel arrangements, and any third party that will access Redwood systems or customer data.

Quick links: Access Portal (Okta + Access Request), VendorHub (procurement back-end), ExpenseFlow (employee expenses), Legal intake form, Security questionnaire (security.redwood.local).

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------

- Requestor: person initiating an access, change, purchase, vendor relationship, or travel booking. Responsible for completeness and business justification.
- Manager/Approver: direct manager who validates business need and budget availability.
- Approving Officer (Finance/Procurement): validates procurement thresholds, tax, and vendor classification.
- Security Reviewer: evaluates data access risk and mandatory controls (SOC2, encryption, contract clauses).
- Legal Reviewer: reviews contract terms for vendor agreements above threshold or with custom IP/data terms.
- Proc Ops (Vendor Onboarding): completes supplier setup, obtains W-9/COI as applicable.

Principles
----------

- Least privilege: grant minimal entitlements required for the job and set automatic expiration where practical.
- Segregation of duties: approval and provisioning paths must not be owned by the same individual for medium/high risk requests.
- Evidence-first approvals: all approvals must be attached to the request in VendorHub or Access Portal.
- Risk proportionality: stricter controls for vendors with data access, privileged infra access, or requests above financial thresholds.

Access & permissions (entitlement lifecycle)
-------------------------------------------

1) Request process

- Use the Access Portal (accessible from the Redwood Console > Tools > Access Request).
- Provide: justification, target systems (service name and environment), requested role (exact RBAC role), duration, and manager approval.
- For long-lived roles (>90 days), supply quarterly business justification and add reviewer in Access Portal.

2) Approval matrix (summary)

- Day-to-day access to non-prod systems: manager approval.
- Prod read-only access: manager + security notification.
- Prod privileged/infra access (SSH, K8s-admin, DB write): manager + security + infra-owner approval.
- Emergency elevated access: break-glass procedure (see Runbook ID: RG-2026-breakglass).

3) Provisioning and deprovisioning

- Provisioning is automated via Okta + Terraform runbooks (Infra-IAC). On approval, provisioning SLA is 2 business days for standard requests, 8 hours for emergency sprints.
- Access expirations are enforced: default 30 days for contractor requests, 90 days for internal hires unless renewed.

4) Periodic review

- Quarterly access attestation: team owners must validate active entitlements and remove stale accounts. Failure to respond triggers automated revocation notices.

Change management
-----------------

Scope: Any modification to production services, infra provisioning, IAM policies, or customer-facing configuration.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Standard change: pre-approved, repeatable changes (e.g., routine OS patching via controlled pipeline). Requires change ticket and notification to SRE runbook subscribers.
- Normal change: requires Change Review Board (CRB) approval for higher impact (planned releases that affect SLAs). CRB meets twice weekly.
- Emergency change: immediate fixes that must follow the emergency roll-forward checklist and be retroactively documented in the change ticket.
sections.heading: Change categories and approval paths

sections.body:
- Quarterly freeze: last two business days of each quarter are freeze windows for major releases unless exception approved by CTO and SRE lead.
- High-risk releases: require canary rollout and 30% traffic validation for 24 hours before full rollout.
sections.heading: Change windows and freezes

sections.body:
1. Change owner and contact
2. Rollout and rollback plan with automation steps
3. Expected impact and post-deploy validation steps
4. Backout criteria and timeline
5. Stakeholder notification list

SLOs and audit

- All normal changes must have an associated ticket and be auditable for 12 months.
- Emergency changes must be documented within 48 hours.

Data management and classification
--------------------------------
sections.heading: Change request minimum content (ticket)

sections.body:
- Public: content intended for public consumption.
- Internal: operational information not intended for external distribution.
- Confidential: employee, business, or customer information that requires access controls.
- Restricted: regulated or highly sensitive data (PII, payment data, health data) that requires encryption at rest and in transit, strict access controls, and audit logging.
sections.heading: Classification levels

sections.body:
- Confidential & Restricted: store only in approved systems (Redwood Console vaults, encrypted S3 with KMS). No vendor transfer without security and legal sign-off.
- Data retention: default retention for logs is 90 days; for customer-facing telemetry retention follows contractual obligations.
- Data deletion: use Data Erasure Request form and verify via automated deletion job.

Procurement and expenses
------------------------
sections.heading: Handling rules (summary)

sections.body:
| Amount (USD) | Approvals required | Notes |
|--------------|-------------------|-------|
| < 2,500 | Manager | Auto-approval in VendorHub if budget tag present |
| 2,500 – 50,000 | Manager + Finance | Finance checks budget and tax classification |
| > 50,000 | Manager + Finance + Procurement + Legal | Requires exec sponsor and procurement intake form |
sections.heading: Purchase approval thresholds (effective)

sections.body:
1. Create a request in VendorHub including business justification, vendor name, SOW/quote, and budget tag.
2. Attach vendor compliance docs (SOC2, ISO, insurance certificate) when available.
3. Finance validates budgets and tax treatment within 3 business days.
4. Procurement routes to Legal for >50k or non-standard T&Cs.
5. Once approved, Procurement issues purchase order and coordinates supplier setup.
sections.heading: Procurement steps (numbered)

sections.body:
- Use ExpenseFlow, attach receipts within 30 days of expense. Per diem caps: domestic $150/day, international $250/day unless pre-approved. Card use: corporate cards are preferred for travel; personal card reimbursements require manager approval.

Vendor management lifecycle
--------------------------
sections.heading: Expense reimbursement

sections.body:
- Initial intake: vendor submitted via VendorHub, 1 business day acknowledgement.
- Risk assessment: Security performs questionnaire review; expect 5-7 business days for standard vendors, 15-20 days for those handling Restricted data.
- Contracting: Legal drafts/negotiates terms; standard NDA/SOW templates for low-risk vendors. Time: 5–15 business days depending on terms.
- Procurement & finance: vendor setup (W-9/COI), tax classification, payment terms.
sections.heading: Onboarding checklist (timeline expectations)

sections.body:
- Low risk (no data access): PO, standard SOE, vendor contact, invoice cadence.
- Medium risk (limited data access): PO, signed DPA, security questionnaire, SOC2 Type II preferred.
- High risk (customer data or privileged infra access): PO, DPA, SOC2 Type II or penetration test report, system access plan, contractual breach notification clause, indemnity terms.
sections.heading: Minimum vendor requirements by risk tier

sections.body:
- Termination checklist: revoke credentials, recover assets, enforce data return/deletion, final invoice reconciliation, and a post-termination confirmation from vendor. Procurement must retain termination evidence for 7 years.

Travel policy (high level)
-------------------------

Booking: Use Travel Portal (linked from Redwood Console). Lowest reasonable fare policy applies for economy class. Business class requires exec-level pre-approval for travel over 8 hours.

Approvals: Manager approves travel requests in Travel Portal. International travel must include security and people-ops notification if travel is to high-risk countries listed by People Ops.

Per diems and expenses: See ExpenseFlow caps. Receipts required for all items >$25.

payload.page_title: Employee Mobility and Systems Access Framework

sections.body:
Summary
This playbook defines a single, company-wide framework for (1) granting and revoking system access, (2) managing employee travel and mobility, and (3) standardizing procurement, vendor onboarding, and expense workflows. It consolidates existing practices into a cohesive reference intended for hiring managers, system owners, people-ops, security, finance, and employees who travel or contract vendors.

Purpose
- Reduce friction for legitimate business activity while maintaining least-privilege controls.
- Clarify responsibilities, SLAs, and templates for access requests, change approvals, procurements, and travel.
- Provide operational playbooks for emergency access, contractor offboarding, vendor assessments, and cross-border data handling.

Scope
Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors, vendors and contingent workers that interact with Redwood production or sensitive data. Components covered: IAM & permissions, temporary access (bastion/sudo), change management for infra and app-level changes, procurement (cards and POs), vendor onboarding & assessment, travel booking & reimbursable expenses, and internal templates.

Key Definitions
- System Owner: person accountable for access decisions on a service (usually the service lead or product manager).
- Requester: employee initiating an access/procurement/travel request.
- Approver: manager/role required by the workflow.
- Privileged Access: any access that allows production-side data exfiltration, administrative actions (root/sudo), secrets management, or billing.

Roles & Responsibilities
- People-Ops: policy owner, onboarding/offboarding orchestration, travel policy administration.
- Security: approves privileged access patterns, runs periodic access reviews, maintains exception register.
- Finance: approves procurement thresholds, conducts vendor payment setup.
- Managers (requester’s manager): approve routine access and travel.
- System Owners: approve service-level permissions, attest periodic access reviews.

Access & Permissions
Principles
1. Least privilege by default.
2. Temporary access for non-routine tasks.
3. Separation of duties: provisioning and approval should be distinct roles.

Access Request Process (standard flow)
1. Employee files request via Access Portal (Confluence form -> OKTA ticket).
2. Request must include purpose, duration, and scope (specific resources).
3. Manager approves (within 48 hours).
4. System Owner confirms service-level needs (SLA 3 business days).
5. Security performs a risk check if request involves Production or Sensitive data.

Approval Matrix (representative thresholds)
- Non-sensitive SaaS (e.g., Slack channels): manager approval.
- Internal dev environments: manager + system owner.
- Production access or secrets: manager + system owner + Security.
- Cross-account/cloud console access: manager + System Owner + SRE + Security.

Temporary Access Rules
- Default duration: 8 hours for ad-hoc troubleshooting, 30 days for development contractors.
- Extensions require renewal through the Access Portal with justification.
- All temporary sessions must be recorded (session recording where available) and audited weekly.

Privileged Key & Secret Management
- Secrets stored only in approved vaults (KMS/HSM + central secrets manager).
- Permanent secrets rotate every 90 days; service-account keys rotate every 60 days.
- No long-lived personal API keys for production.

Emergency (Break-glass) Access
1. Initiate incident channel and tag security on-call.
2. Security issues one-time elevated token via emergency delegation service (valid for 1 hour).
3. Requester documents actions within 24 hours and files a retrospective.

Periodic Reviews
- Quarterly access attestation: System Owners must confirm active users and roles.
- Monthly privileged user audit by Security.

Change Management
Change Types
- Routine: application config changes that do not touch production data (low risk).
- Standard: planned infra or app changes with predefined runbooks (medium risk).
- Emergency: changes necessary to remediate incidents (high risk).

Change Advisory Board (CAB)
- Weekly CAB for standard changes. Representation: Engineering (serving-runtime/infra), Security, SRE, Product.
- CAB template: change id, owner, start/end window, rollback plan, impact matrix, monitoring/alerts.

Change Workflow (standard change)
1. Submit RFC in the Change Portal with risk score and rollout plan.
2. Stakeholders comment within 48 hours.
3. CAB approves or requests mitigation steps.
4. Deploy during agreed maintenance window.
5. Post-deploy verification and rollback capability confirmed.

Rollback & Postmortem
- Every standard and emergency change must include a clear rollback plan.
- If an emergency change occurs, a postmortem indexed in Confluence must be filed within 5 business days.

Change Exceptions
- Exceptions are timeboxed and recorded in the Access Exception Registry with an owner and an expiry (max 30 days unless reapproved).

Data Management
Data Classification
- Public: information safe to disclose.
- Internal: non-sensitive company data.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, regulated info, or secrets.

Handling Rules
- Restricted data requires encryption at rest and in transit, access limited to approved roles, and cannot be stored in personal cloud drives.
- Cross-border transfer of Restricted data requires Legal sign-off and documented data flow map.

Retention & Deletion
- Default retention: product logs 90 days, backups 180 days unless business/legal require longer.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) workflow in the Privacy Portal.

Backups & Recovery
- Backups must be encrypted, stored in a separate account, and tested quarterly for restore capability.

Procurement & Expenses
Procurement Routing
- Low-value purchases (< $2,500): corporate card or manager approval.
- Mid-value purchases ($2,500–$50,000): Procurement Request (PR) + Finance Manager approval.
- High-value purchases (> $50,000): PR + Finance Director + VP approval; competitive quotes required.

Purchase Process
1) Create PR with line items, business justification, budget code, and vendor contact.
2) Procurement verifies supplier PO terms and conflict-of-interest checks.
3) Finance approves and issues PO or instructs corporate card charge.

Expense Reimbursement
- Use Expense System with photographed receipts. Meals per diem: domestic $75/day, international varies by region (see Expense Matrix link).
- Per diem and lodging max rates published annually.

Corporate Cards & Controls
- Cardholders have monthly limits set by Finance. Card transactions over $5,000 require pre-authorization.
- Misuse results in revocation and HR disciplinary review.

Vendor Management
Onboarding Checklist
1) Business justification & approved PO.
2) Security assessment: questionnaire covering SOC2/ISO, data handling, penetration testing history.
3) Legal review & signed contract (includes security addendum).
4) Finance vendor setup and tax forms.

Third-Party Risk Assessment
- Vendors categorized by access & data exposure (Low, Medium, High).
- High-risk vendors require annual security attestation, penetration test evidence, and right-to-audit clauses.

Contract SLAs & Escalation
- Contracts > $100k or >12 months must include SLA metrics (uptime, response time), financial remedies, and an executive escalation path.

Vendor Offboarding
- Deprovision access within 24 hours of contract end.
- Reclaim assets and ensure data destruction or return per contract.

Travel & Employee Mobility
Booking and Approval
- Employees request travel via Travel Portal with manager approval. Travel booking must use preferred vendors for negotiated rates.
- Non-standard travel requires pre-approval from Finance and People-Ops.

Safety & Duty of Care
- People-Ops publishes travel advisories. Employees must register international travel and carry emergency contact info.
- For high-risk locations, security will require a travel safety plan and may restrict travel.

Reimbursement & Allowed Expenses
- Reimbursable: airfare (economy or business for flights >6 hours with manager approval), lodging, ground transport, meals (see per diem).
- Non-reimbursable: in-room entertainment, personal expenses, fines.

Remote Work & Mobility
- For long-term remote work or relocation, use the Remote Work Request form: includes stipend, hardware shipping, tax implications, and local labor compliance checks.

Templates & Examples
Included templates (attached as documents in the Confluence page):
- Access Request form (fields: requester, manager, system, scope, duration, business justification).
- Change Request (RFC) template with risk score and rollback plan.
- Procurement Request template (line items, budget, vendor).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSAQ) checklist.
- Travel Pre-approval & Expense form.

Example: Minimal Access Request (copy/paste)
```
Requester: Priya.Shah@redwood.com
Manager: Maria.Gupta@redwood.com
System: analytics-reporting-prod
Scope: read-only on analytics schema; no export
Duration: 14 days
Business justification: validate report queries for Q4 billing reconciliation
```

Enforcement & Exceptions
- Non-compliance discovered during audit will trigger remediation steps: 1) immediate revocation if critical; 2) remediation plan within 5 business days; 3) disciplinary review if repeated misuse.
- Exception process: submit Exception Request with scope, owner, compensating controls, and expiry. Security reviews exceptions monthly.

Metrics & Reporting
- Monthly reports: number of open access requests, average approval time, number of privileged accounts, vendor risk distribution.
- Quarterly KPIs: mean time to grant access (target <72 hours), privileged access reduction (target -10% year/year).

Appendix A — Contacts and Escalation Points
- People-Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security On-call: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Travel Desk: travel@redwood.com

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets and sample policy (service account rotation)
- Rotate key (example):
ssh into key-rotation-host && ./rotate_service_key --service analytics --env prod --rotate-days 60

- Sample retention YAML (apply in infra repo):
retention:
  logs_days: "90"
  backups_days: "180"
  sensitive_data_flag: "true"

Change Log
- 2028-11-07: Created by Priya Shah (people-ops).
- 2029-02-13: Revised procurement thresholds and travel per diem schedule; added vendor offboarding SLA.

Related resources
- Access Portal: [Confluence > Access Portal] (internal link)
- Change Portal: [Confluence > Change Requests] (internal link)
- Procurement Catalog: [Finance > Procurement] (internal link)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: [Security > VSAQ] (internal link)

This framework is a living document maintained by People-Ops in coordination with Security and Finance. For questions or to request updates, contact people-ops@redwood.com.

payload.page_title: Access, Change & Procurement Playbook — Compact Guide

sections.body:
Purpose
  This compact playbook consolidates Redwood Inference company-wide policies and operational patterns for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel expense handling, and the canonical templates teams should reuse. It is designed for day-to-day reference by engineering, product, security, people-ops, and finance teams. Use this as an operational checklist and a set of enforced thresholds; it links to detailed procedures where required.

  Scope
  - Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors, and vendors with company accounts or physical access.
  - Covers lifecycle from request -> approval -> provisioning -> review for access; request -> approval -> rollout -> post-change verification for changes; request -> approval -> purchase -> invoice for procurement; and vendor security/contract checks before onboarding.
  - Exceptions must follow the Risk & Exceptions workflow (security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions) and be timeboxed.

  Owners and escalation
  - Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
  - Day-to-day steward: Security (access operations)
  - Procurement contact: Procurement Manager (procurement@redwood.ai)
  - Emergency on-call: Eng SRE rotation (see eng-sre/oncall-rotations)

  Access lifecycle summary
  1) Request: Use the central Access Request form (internal link: /forms/access-request). Always include justification and data classification of resources requested.
  2) Approval matrix: Requests require one of the following approvers depending on resource tier:
     - Tier 1 (public docs, non-sensitive tools): Team lead or manager. SLA: 48 business hours.
     - Tier 2 (internal systems, non-production infra): Product/Engineering manager + Security approval. SLA: 72 business hours.
     - Tier 3 (production systems, customer data, KMS/HSM, admin roles): Manager + Security review + Finance if billing impact. SLA: 5 business days.
  3) Provisioning: Automated where possible (IAM flows). Manual steps must be tracked in the ticket. Record the provisioning ticket ID in the access request.
  4) Review & recertification: Quarterly recertification for Tier 3 and semi-annual for Tier 2. All teams run a role-review runbook before offboarding events.
  5) Emergency access: Temporary elevated access issued via Break-Glass process. Emergency access screenshots, reason, and postmortem must be attached to the original request within 48 hours.

  Access controls & thresholds (table)
  | Resource class | Example services | Default TTL | Approval required |
  |---|---|---:|---|
  | Tier 1 (Low) | Public docs, marketing tools | 90 days | Team lead |
  | Tier 2 (Moderate) | Staging clusters, internal dashboards | 30 days | Manager + Security |
  | Tier 3 (High) | Production GPU clusters, KMS, customer data | 7 days (renew) | Manager + Security + Finance |

  Change policy at-a-glance
  - All changes that affect production paths, security posture, or billing above $10k/month must enter the Change Review workflow.
  - Types of changes:
    a) Standard changes: Pre-approved and recurring (e.g., routine infra patching). Require CAB notification only.
    b) Normal changes: Require pre-approval, rollout plan, backout plan, and post-change verification.
    c) Emergency changes: Bypass normal CAB timelines with documented justification and a post-implementation review within 72 hours.

  Change process (numbered)
  1. Create change ticket in the Change queue with classification, impact analysis, rollback plan, owner, and proposed window.
  2. Peer review & security review: Security approves if any sensitive data, network, or IAM changes are included.
  3. CAB review: Weekly CAB meets for Normal changes. Approvals logged in the ticket.
  4. Runbook execution: Follow the runbook for the service, including pre-checks and canary rollout (10% traffic for 30 minutes typical).
  5. Verification & close: Post-change verification checklist completed and attached to the ticket. Record any incidents in oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.

  Data classification
  - PUBLIC: Intended for public disclosure. No special handling.
  - INTERNAL: Company operational data. Access controlled but not regulated.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, PII, financials. Strong access controls and encryption required.
  - RESTRICTED: Regulated data (e.g., health, payment card). Requires compliance controls and restricted hosting.

  Handling rules (bullets)
  - All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using company-approved KMS.
  - Data minimization: Only store fields required for the purpose. Retention schedules must be applied per the Data Retention matrix.
  - Data export: Exports of CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data require Security + Legal approval and an approved export ticket.

  Purchasing thresholds & approval
  - Low-touch purchases (< $2,500): Team budget owner approval. Use corporate card or expense report.
  - Mid-tier purchases ($2,500 - $50,000): Manager + Procurement approval and standard PO.
  - High-value purchases (> $50,000): Procurement + Finance + Legal. Contract review required.

  Procurement process (steps)
  1. Initiate PR (Purchase Request) with justification, GL code, and vendor details.
  2. Procurement evaluates vendor terms, compliance evidence, and price competitiveness.
  3. Finance validates budget availability and issues PO.
  4. Receipt and invoice matching: AP validates and follows 3-way match.

  Expense policy highlights
  - Travel per diem: see travel policy summary below. Personal expenses are non-reimbursable.
  - Receipts required for all expenses > $25. Use the Expense system with proper GL coding.

  Onboarding checklist
  - Vendor intake form completed with business case and data access requirements.
  - Security questionnaire: Vendor must complete the security questionnaire if they process CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data.
  - Contract & SOW: Legal negotiates terms, includes data protection addenda and breach notification timelines.
  - Access controls: Least-privilege IAM accounts, dedicated service accounts, and timeboxed credentials where possible.

  Vendor risk thresholds
  - Low: SaaS without data access. Approval: Procurement.
  - Medium: SaaS with internal data access. Approval: Procurement + Security.
  - High: Processes CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data or has system access. Approval: Procurement + Security + Legal + Exec sponsor.

  Travel guidelines
  - Booking: Use approved travel portal. Economy or equivalent for domestic travel; premium economy for flights over 6 hours with manager approval.
  - Pre-approval: All travel above $1,000 requires manager pre-approval.
  - Per diem: Meals up to $75/day; incidentals up to $25/day. Exceptions require manager approval.

  Expense submission timeline
  - Submit within 30 days of expense. Late submissions may be denied without manager exception.

  Reusable templates
  - Access request subject: [Access Request] <Resource> — <Justification>
  - Change ticket name: [Change][<Service>] <Short summary> — rollout <date>
  - Purchase request template (CSV fields): requester, vendor, justification, gl_code, cost_estimate, contract_required (yes/no)

  Sample Access Request (copyable)
  -------------------------------
  Title: [Access Request] S3 project-buckets — analytics team
  Requested by: <name>
  Resource: s3://redwood-analytics/project-buckets
  Tier: Tier 2
  Justification: Required for daily ETL runs producing product analytics. No PII expected; storing aggregated metrics.
  Duration: 90 days
  Approvers: Team lead; Security if escalated

  Sample Change Checklist (to attach to ticket)
  - Pre-change snapshot/backups taken: yes/no
  - Rollout window: HH:MM UTC
  - Canary % and duration: 10% for 30m
  - Rollback plan: exact steps + owner
  - Post-change verification metric(s): error-rate <= 0.5%, latency within SLO

  Exceptions
  - Requestors may ask for exceptions using the Risk & Exceptions form. Exceptions must include duration, compensating controls, owner, and sunset date.

  Escalation ladder (short)
  1. Team lead
  2. Service owner
  3. Security / Procurement
  4. Head of Finance/Legal (for vendor/contract issues)

  Related references
  - Detailed procurement SOP: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-sop-2025
  - Vendor security questionnaire: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-questionnaire
  - Data retention matrix: /confluence/policies-and-process/data-retention-matrix
  - Change CAB calendar: /confluence/eng-platform/cab-schedule

  Revision history
  - 2025-07-15: Initial compact playbook published (Maya Chen)
  - 2025-11-02: Added emergency access SLA & updated procurement thresholds (Liam O'Connor)
  - 2026-02-10: Clarified vendor risk thresholds and added sample templates (Sofia Ramirez)
