payload.page_title: Authorization Workflows and Travel Templates — Operational Guide

sections.body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This page defines standardized authorization workflows, approval thresholds, vendor onboarding steps, travel approval templates, and associated operational procedures for Redwood Inference. It is intended for employees, managers, finance, security, and platform teams who participate in access approvals, change management, procurement, vendor management, and corporate travel.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood entities worldwide and covers: access & permissions requests; change approvals for infra and application deployments; procurement & expense approvals; vendor onboarding & renewals; and company-sponsored travel bookings and reimbursements.

Ownership
---------
- Document owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
- Primary contributors: Security (IAM), Eng-SRE, People Ops, Procurement
- Stakeholders: Product, Eng-Platform, Customer Success

Quick links
-----------
- Access request form (IAM Service): https://console.redwood.internal/iam/requests
- Procurement system (ProcureFlow): https://procureflow.redwood.internal
- Vendor onboarding (VendorHub): https://vendorhub.redwood.internal
- Expense system (ExpenseTrack): https://expenses.redwood.internal

1) Roles and responsibilities
----------------------------
- Requester: initiates requests (access, change, purchase, travel).
- Manager/Team Lead: verifies business justification and approves up to their approval limit.
- Security/IAM: verifies least-privilege assignments, performs risk review for privileged access.
- Procurement: validates vendor contracts, PO issuance, and vendor financial checks.
- Finance: verifies budget availability and final reimbursement.
- Legal: reviews non-standard contract terms, NDAs, data processing agreements.

2) Access & permissions workflow
--------------------------------
Principles: least privilege, role-based assignments, short-lived elevated access, auditability.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Tier 0 — Public/Read-only: no approval required for public docs.
- Tier 1 — Standard user: manager approval within 48 hours SLA.
- Tier 2 — Elevated (service accounts, admin console): manager + IAM review, 72-hour SLA.
- Tier 3 — Sensitive & Privileged (KMS keys, production DB write): manager + IAM + Security + VP signoff, 7-day SLA.
sections.heading: Access tiers

sections.body:
1. Requester files a request in IAM Service with justification, scope, and duration.
2. Manager reviews and either approves or returns for clarification within 48 hours.
3. For Tier 2/3, IAM performs a risk check and documents exceptions in the audit log.
4. Provisioning automation (when available) creates the account/role and notifies Requester.
5. Access is automatically time-limited; renewal requests follow the same workflow.
sections.heading: Request process (standard)

sections.body:
- Business justification clearly stated and linked to ticket or JIRA.
- Access duration <= 30 days unless approved as recurring.
- Principle of least privilege applied (no 'owner' role unless necessary).
- MFA enabled and device compliance validated via Intune or device inventory.
sections.heading: Elevated access checklist (for approvers)

sections.body:
- IAM Service will auto-expire temporary access at the end of the requested window.
- SLA targets: standard requests 48 hours, elevated 72 hours, privileged 7 days.
- Weekly orphaned-account report produced to eng-sre@redwood.internal.

3) Change management (infra & app changes)
-----------------------------------------
sections.heading: Automated controls and SLAs

sections.body:
| Tier | Impact | Examples | Approvers | Typical lead time | Rollback SLA |
|------|--------|----------|----------|------------------:|------------:|
| C1   | Low    | Config tweak, non-prod deploy | Team lead | 0–24h | 30m |
| C2   | Medium | Production bugfix, schema migration (non-destructive) | Team lead + Eng-SRE | 24–72h | 60m |
| C3   | High   | Version upgrades, DB migrations, infra changes | Eng-SRE + Product + Security | 72h+ | 30m guaranteed |
sections.heading: Change tiers and approval matrix

sections.body:
- Rollback procedure documented and tested.
- Monitoring playbook with key metrics and alert thresholds (latency, error-rate, CPU).
- Stakeholder notification list (SLACK channel, oncall).
- Scheduled maintenance window (if customer-facing).
sections.heading: Pre-change checklist (must be attached to change ticket)

sections.body:
1. Create change ticket in ChangeBoard with planned window, impact, approvals, rollback plan.
2. Run preflight smoke tests in staging; attach logs.
3. Execute during approved window with one engineer owning runbook.
4. Monitor metrics and escalate to oncall per runbook if thresholds exceeded.
5. Close ticket with post-change summary and incident link if any anomalies occurred.
sections.heading: Change execution steps (standard)

sections.body:
- Emergency changes require Eng-SRE + incident commander signoff post-facto; must be documented within 24 hours.

4) Data classification and handling
---------------------------------
sections.heading: Emergency changes

sections.body:
- Public: safe to publish.
- Internal: Redwood internal use; no PII.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or proprietary models.
- Restricted: regulated data subject to contractual or legal restrictions.
sections.heading: Data classes

sections.body:
- Encryption at rest via KMS required for Confidential and Restricted.
- Access limited to Tier 2/3 and logged.
- Backups encrypted and stored in region-specific buckets matching data residency requirements.
sections.heading: Handling rules by class

sections.body:
- Retention baseline: logs 90 days, backups 180 days, product telemetry 2 years (unless contract specifies otherwise).
- Data deletion requests must follow the Data Subject Request SOP (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-subject-requests).

5) Procurement, expenses, and approval thresholds
------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Data retention & deletion

sections.body:
- <= $1,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow.
- $1,001–$25,000: Manager + Procurement review.
- $25,001–$250,000: Director + Procurement + Finance.
- > $250,000: VP + Legal + Procurement + CFO approval.
sections.heading: Approval thresholds (examples)

sections.body:
1. Requester creates a requisition in ProcureFlow with business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement validates vendor, performs legal/financial checks and obtains quotes if required.
3. Finance verifies budget availability and issues PO.
4. Vendor receives PO and onboarding begins via VendorHub.
sections.heading: Procurement workflow (vendor purchase)

sections.body:
- Use ExpenseTrack to submit receipts within 10 business days of expense.
- Per-diem and policy caps: domestic lodging up to $275/night unless pre-approved; international per-diem per country schedule in ExpenseTrack guidelines.
- Unauthorized spend (personal entertainment, family members, luxury upgrades) is not reimbursable without prior approval.

6) Vendor onboarding & lifecycle
------------------------------
sections.heading: Expense policy (travel & misc)

sections.body:
- Completed VendorHub intake form and company W-9 or local equivalent.
- Proof of insurance (if applicable), references, and SOC2 or equivalent report for vendors handling Confidential/Restricted data.
- Signed MSA and applicable DPA/Privacy Addendum reviewed by Legal.
sections.heading: Vendor onboarding minimum requirements

sections.body:
- Low risk: commodity vendors (office supplies) — ProcureFlow + basic vetting.
- Medium risk: SaaS vendors with internal access — SOC2 assessment and Standard Contract.
- High risk: vendors with access to customer data or production systems — Security questionnaire + on-site review + encrypted connection requirements.
sections.heading: Vendor risk tiers and controls

sections.body:
- Contract expiration notice triggers 90/60/30-day reminders to vendor owner.
- Renewal requires business justification, cost analysis, and Security re-assessment for data-handling changes.

7) Travel policy and approval templates
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Ensure safe, cost-effective travel with clear approval and reimbursement paths.
sections.heading: Contract renewal checklist

sections.body:
- All business travel must be pre-approved in TravelBoard (link: https://travelboard.redwood.internal) with estimated cost and budget code.
- Manager approval required for trips <= 5 days. Director approval required for international travel or trips > 5 days.
sections.heading: Pre-approval requirements

sections.body:
- Use company travel partners for flights and hotels when available.
- Economy or premium-economy for flights under 8 hours; manager approval needed for upgrades.
- Use company-preferred hotels; exceptions require explanation.
sections.heading: Standard travel booking guidelines

sections.body:
"Trip purpose: [brief business objective]
Dates: [start] to [end]
Estimated cost: $[amount]
Budget code: [code]
Business justification: [1–2 sentences]
Risk considerations: [health/visa/travel advisories]
Approvals: Manager: [name], Director: [name if required]"
sections.heading: Travel approval template (copy into TravelBoard comments)

sections.body:
- People Ops maintains an emergency travel roster and will coordinate evacuation or emergency support for employees in high-risk regions. Contact emergency@redwood.internal.

8) Templates and sample artifacts
--------------------------------
Include these templates in the page attachments and in Template Library:
- Access request template (IAM): fields: requester, resource, duration, justification, JIRA link.
- Change ticket template (ChangeBoard): fields: scope, impact, rollback, test plan, owner, stakeholders.

payload.page_title: Request Flows and Vendor Management Blueprint

sections.body: This blueprint codifies company-wide procedural flows for three common cross-functional operations: access & permissions changes, procurement and expenses, and vendor onboarding (including travel-related approvals). It is intended to be a single reference for requestors, approvers, and operational teams. It emphasizes principles of least privilege, auditability, separation of duties, and risk-proportionate review.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and short-term vendors.
- Covers: Okta/SSO group membership requests, privileged (sudo/K8s/DB) access, change management for production services, purchase requests, vendor onboarding/security review, corporate travel approvals and expense reimbursement.
- Excludes: HR-only processes (benefits, payroll) and customer data access requests governed by contract addenda (see related_pages).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum role required and set explicit time-to-live when feasible.
- Two-approver model for privileged changes: manager + owning service/product/security reviewer.
- Auditability: all requests must create a tracked ticket (Jira or Procurement Portal) with clear justification and link to approvals.
- SLAs:
  - Standard access requests: respond within 3 business days.
  - Escalation for critical access: initial response within 4 hours, resolution or temporary mitigation within 24 hours.
  - Procurement approval (<= $5k): 5 business days. $5k–$50k: 10 business days. > $50k: 20 business days + procurement committee cadence.
sections.heading: Principles and SLAs

sections.body:
- Requestor: initiates the ticket with justification, cost center, and expected TTL for access.
- Manager: verifies business need and cost center.
- Security Team: reviews privileged access and vendor security posture.
- Procurement (Finance) Team: executes purchase, contract review, and vendor payments.
- IT/Platform: enacts access changes and monitors expirations.
- Legal: reviews contracts for enterprise vendors or data sharing agreements.

1) Access & Permissions Request Flow (Okta / Internal RBAC)
A. Request submission (Jira access-request template or via Self-Service Portal):
  - Required fields: requestor, manager, justification, resource (service name e.g., inference-runtime-prod), role (e.g., read-only, deploy, db-admin), TTL (if temporary), business owner, risk classification.
  - Attachments: training completion proof (if required), signed NDA for external contractors.
B. Automated validations:
  - Portal checks: ensure requestor is manager-approved in HR system and cost center present.
  - TTL enforcement: default TTL for elevated roles = 7 days unless longer period justified.
C. Approval chain:
  1. Manager approval (manager of requestor).
  2. Service/Product owner approval (if different).
  3. Security review for roles with sensitive scope (e.g., DB admin, SSH, K8s cluster-admin).
D. Implementation & Audit:
  - IT/Platform applies changes via IaC or identity provider automation (Okta group provisioning).
  - Ticket must include implementation record and link to user provisioning audit log.
  - Automated reminders sent 3 days before TTL expiration.
E. Emergency access (break-glass):
  - One-time emergency elevation can be granted with after-action review within 48 hours. Emergency title must include "EMERGENCY" and be tagged for security postmortem.

2) Change Management for Production Services
- Change window: routine non-disruptive changes occur Mon–Fri 03:00–06:00 UTC when possible; disruptive changes require scheduled maintenance with 72h customer/internal notice.
- Risk classification:
  - Low: config tweaks with <1% user impact forecast.
  - Medium: rolling deploys that touch stateful services.
  - High: schema migrations, cross-region DNS changes, or leader election changes.
- Approval & testing:
  1. Dev team runbook + preflight checklist (unit + canary + e2e where applicable).
  2. SRE review for medium/high risk.
  3. Change scheduled in the calendar and communicated to #sre-oncall, #product-updates.
- Rollback: every high/medium change must include a tested rollback plan and a verification checklist for post-rollout validation (latency, error rate, key traces).

3) Procurement & Expenses (high-level rules)
- Thresholds and approvals:
  - <= $5,000: Requestor -> Manager -> Procurement auto-approve.
  - $5,001–$50,000: Requestor -> Manager -> Procurement (finance review) -> Contract owner if recurring.
  - > $50,000: All above + Procurement Committee review + Legal sign-off.
- Purchase types and templates:
  - One-time purchases: use the Procurement Portal form; attach quote and cost center.
  - SaaS subscriptions: require security self-attestation (see vendor onboarding) and renewal cadence.
  - Capital requests: submit CAPEX form (Finance) and include depreciation schedule.
- Payment terms and invoices:
  - Standard net-30 unless negotiated. All invoices routed to AP via procurement ticket with PO number.
- Expense reimbursement:
  - Submit receipts in Expensify within 30 days. Missing receipts require manager exception.
  - Per diem and mileage: follow company scale. Current mileage rate: 0.655 USD/mile.
sections.heading: Roles & Ownership

sections.body:
| Spend band | Approval chain | Typical SLA | Docs needed |
|-----------:|----------------|------------:|------------|
| <= $5k | Manager -> Procurement | 5 business days | Quote/receipt, cost center |
| $5k–$50k | Manager -> Procurement -> Finance | 10 business days | Vendor security attestation, quote |
| > $50k | Committee + Legal | 20 business days | Contract, SOC2 or equivalent, legal redlines |

4) Vendor Onboarding & Security Checklist
- Tiering by data exposure:
  - Tier A (restricted): vendors that handle customer PII, model weights, or infra with access to production systems. Require SOC2 Type II, penetration test report, contract MR, and use of customer-approved key management (KMS/HSM) if handling secrets.
  - Tier B (internal-confidential): vendors that process internal analytics, require security questionnaire and encryption-in-transit.
  - Tier C (public): marketing, event vendors; basic company insurance & tax form.
- Onboarding steps (checklist):
  1. Business sponsor opens vendor request in Procurement Portal with SOW/quote.
  2. Procurement triage: confirm spend band and request security tier.
  3. Security team performs questionnaire and provides required controls (SLA, encryption, incident response).
  4. Legal reviews & signs contract; include data processing addendum if Tier A/B.
  5. IT/Platform configures network & access (VPC peering, firewall rules) where necessary.
  6. Finance sets up payment terms and cost center mapping.
- Required minimums for Tier A:
| Requirement | Expectation |
|-------------|-------------|
| SOC2 Type II | Report within last 18 months or compensating controls |
| Incident response | 24/7 email + 2 business hour SLA for critical incidents |
| Data handling | Encryption at rest and in transit; data deletion policy defined |

- Deprovisioning: vendor termination checklist includes revoking access, cert/key rotation, verifying data deletion, and final invoice reconciliation.

5) Travel & Expense Policy (operational alignment)
- Approval flow: Requestor -> Manager -> Finance reviewer (if > $2k or > 5 people) -> People Ops (if international visas needed).
- Booking: employees are encouraged to use the corporate travel portal for preferred vendors and negotiated rates. Exceptions require manager + travel admin approval.
- Reimbursement timelines: 30 days submission; reimbursements processed within next payroll cycle.
- Safety & compliance: employees traveling to restricted countries must consult with Security & People Ops 10 business days before travel.

Templates and Forms (links & sample fields)
- Access Request (Jira template): fields={requestor, manager, resource, role, justification, TTL, business owner, CI/CD impact, attachments}.
- Procurement Portal: fields={project, cost-center, frequency, vendor-tier, SOW, quote, security-tier}.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: standard 40-question form (available as spreadsheet in /confluence/security-and-compliance/).
- Travel Request: fields={purpose, dates, attendees, estimated cost, manager approval}.

payload.page_title: Enterprise process safeguards and operational templates

sections.body:
Overview:
This page collects company-level safeguards, approval flows, and reusable templates for core operational processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single, authoritative reference for owners and approvers so decisions are consistent, auditable, and aligned with Redwood’s security and financial controls.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with company systems or incurring company spend.
- Exceptions require an approved Risk Exception (see "related_pages") and a documented compensating control.

Owners and escalation:
- Process owner: Finance & Legal (policy stewardship, escalation on spend and vendor risk).
- Operational steward: People Ops (access provisioning cadence, travel approvals).
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (RBAC, system hardening, data classification).
- Escalation: Finance > Head of Finance > Legal Counsel for contract or regulatory questions.

1) Access & Permissions (Summary and checklist)
Purpose: Enforce least-privilege while supporting developer velocity.
Minimum controls:
- All human identities must authenticate via SSO (Okta).
- Service accounts require a documented owner and will follow a 90-day key rotation cadence.
- MFA required for privileged roles (admin, infra, billing).

Provisioning process (standard):
1. Submit access request in the Access Portal with justification and duration.
2. Manager approves via the portal.
3. System owner validates scope (1 business day SLA).
4. Access is granted; audit log entry created and emailed to requestor.

Deprovisioning:
- Offboarding flow triggers immediate removal of SSO sessions and revocation of API keys.
- Contractors: access expires automatically on contract end date; extend only with manager + security approval.

Role definitions (short table):
| Role | Typical responsibilities | Example systems |
|-----|------------------------|----------------|
| Viewer | read-only access for troubleshooting | Dashboards, logs |
| Contributor | deploy and change non-prod configs | CI, staging clusters |
| Admin | manage production infra and secrets | Prod clusters, KMS |

2) Change Management (Safe rollout pattern)
When required: Any change impacting production config, schema, model serving behavior, or cost > $5,000 monthly expected increase.
Principles: small, reversible, and observable changes.
Approval workflow:
- Minor (non-prod or config-only, low risk): developer -> peer review -> automated tests -> rollout.
- Major (schema changes, infra scaling, model variant switch): developer -> tech lead -> SRE owner -> change advisory board (CAB) approval window.
Canary + rollback steps (recommended):
1. Deploy canary to 1% of traffic for 30 minutes.
2. Monitor: latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost variance, key user journeys.
3. If metrics within thresholds, increase to 10% for 1 hour.
4. Full rollout and post-rollout review within 48 hours.
Thresholds:
- Latency: less than 15% change to P95 relative to baseline.
- Errors: < 0.5% increase in error rate.
- Cost: < 10% unexpected per-token cost increase.

3) Data Management (Classification + lifecycle)
Classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Restricted: customer PII, regulated datasets, private keys. Stored in encrypted buckets with strict RBAC.
- Confidential: internal financials, roadmaps, unreleased models.
Retention: store only as long as business need. Default retention: logs 90 days, analytics 2 years, backups 3 years (encrypted).
Data access request: include business justification, data fields required, expected duration, and mitigation plan. Security must sign off for Restricted data.
Secure transfer: use SFTP or vetted vendor integrations (see vendor management).

4) Procurement & Expenses (Controls and thresholds)
Approval thresholds (examples):
- <$2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,000–$25,000: Department head + procurement notification.
- >$25,000: Finance + Legal review; require PO and vendor credit check.
Process:
1. Raise a Purchase Request in the procurement system with justification, budget code, and vendor info.
2. Procurement validates quotes and negotiates terms.
3. PO issued; vendor onboarding (see vendor section).
Expense reporting: receipts required within 7 days for travel; corporate card reconciliation monthly.

Travel policy (summary):
- Book with approved travel vendors or use the company travel portal.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business class with Director+ approval for international >6 hours.
- Per diem and meal caps defined on the travel expense form.
- Safety and incident reporting requirement: contact People Ops immediately for emergencies.

5) Vendor management (Risk and onboarding)
Risk tiers: low, medium, high (based on data sensitivity, access to systems, financial exposure).
Onboarding checklist:
- Contract signed and stored in central repository.
- Security questionnaire completed for medium/high risk.
- Approved SLA and exit plan.
- Designated vendor owner in the product or platform team.
Quarterly vendor review: owners must attest to current risk posture and usage.
Termination: ensure data return/destruction is verified and certificates of destruction retained.

6) Templates & Forms (Quick links and samples)
Included templates (attached here as inline text snippets):
- Access request template:
  - Requestor name: 
  - System or role: 
  - Justification: 
  - Duration: 
  - Manager approval: 

- Change advisory form (summary):
  - Change owner: 
  - Risk category: low/medium/high
  - Rollback plan: 
  - Monitoring checklist: metrics and alert thresholds

- Vendor onboarding checklist (fields): vendor name, risk tier, contract expiry, data access required, security questionnaire status, PO number.

Example: simple JSON snippet for a change submission (CLI-friendly):
{
  "change_id": "chg-2025-001",
  "owner": "team-service",
  "risk": "medium",
  "canary_percentage": "1",
  "rollback_command": "kubectl rollout undo deployment/service --namespace=prod"
}

Audit & reporting:
- Monthly access review: managers must certify active access lists for their teams.
- Quarterly vendor risk attestation by vendor owners.
- Change log retention: all approved changes and CAB minutes retained for 3 years.

Enforcement & exceptions:
- Non-compliance discovered via audit will trigger remedial action and may include revocation of access, retraining, or remedial procurement steps.
- Risk exceptions must be entered into the Risk Exception register and include compensating controls and an owner and expiry date.

Related resources and links:
- Access Portal (SSO requests): /internal/access-portal
- Procurement system: /internal/procurement
- Vendor repository: /internal/vendor-portal
- Incident response and security runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-process

Revision history:
- 2024-02-15: Initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2024-09-01: Added canary thresholds and vendor onboarding checklist (reviewers: Diego Martinez).
- 2025-10-10: Updated procurement thresholds and travel guidance (reviewers: Rina Okafor, Evan Zhou).

Contact for questions: policy@redwood.ai (Finance & Legal policy inbox).

payload.page_title: Company Operations Process Crosswalk & Template Kit

sections.body:
Overview

This page consolidates company-wide policies and operational processes into a single crosswalk, with ready-to-use templates for common actions: access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. Its primary goal is to reduce ambiguity by: (1) clarifying ownership and approvals for routine decisions, (2) providing step-by-step procedures for common tasks, and (3) publishing canonical templates and checklists that teams can copy.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood corporate and product teams unless a separate customer- or regulation-specific exception exists.
- Does not replace role-specific runbooks (e.g., SRE incident runbooks); it provides the governance layer and standardized forms.

Document structure

1) Roles & ownership matrix
2) Access & permissions: request, review, audit
3) Change management: standard and emergency paths
4) Data management: classification, handling, retention
5) Procurement & expenses: thresholds, PO and card usage
6) Vendor management: onboarding and risk checklist
7) Travel policy: booking, approvals and reimbursement
8) Templates and examples (copyable blocks)
9) Governance and review cadence

1) Roles & ownership matrix

- Document owner: People Ops (process maintenance, templates).
- Access approvals: Team Manager -> Service Owner -> Security for sensitive resources.
- Procurement approvals: Requester -> Manager -> Finance for up to $10k; Manager + Finance -> Legal for > $10k.
- Change approvals: Service Owner -> Change Approver (SRE/Platform) -> Production Change Window.
- Vendor onboarding: Procurement lead -> Security -> Legal signoff -> Contracting.

Owners and definitions

- Requester: person initiating request (access, purchase, travel).
- Service Owner: team designated owner for a given service or dataset.
- Approval Authority: role with explicit delegation to approve (manager, finance partner, security reviewer).

2) Access & permissions

Principles

- Principle of least privilege: grant minimum permissions for a defined period.
- Time-bound access: temporary access must have an expiry and be audited.
- Segregation of duties: no single person should perform production change and approval concurrently unless designated as emergency on-call.

Standard access request flow (non-sensitive resources)

1. Requester files an Access Request via the Access Portal (or Workday form for people & payroll access). Required fields: requester, resource name, reason, duration, intended actions.
2. Team Manager reviews, confirms business justification, and either approves or requests changes.
3. System Owner enforces configuration change and records grant in the access registry.
4. Automated audit job generates monthly access snapshot; owners must attest quarterly.

Access approval matrix (simplified)

| Resource type | Approver | Typical duration | Extra controls |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Non-prod compute (dev/test) | Team Manager | 30 days | Token/SSH rotation on handoff |
| Production application access | Service Owner + SRE | 14 days | MFA mandatory, session recording |
| Sensitive dataset (PII/PHI) | Security + Data Owner | 7 days | Data access agreement, DLP enabled |
| Cloud infra (IAM role) | Infra Owner + Security | 1 day | Just-in-time (JIT) + ephemeral creds |

Access review cadence

- Quarterly attestation by owners for all production and sensitive access.
- Automated reminders at 21, 14, and 7 days before temporary grants expire.
- Emergency access (see change mgmt) requires post-hoc audit within 72 hours.

3) Change management

Change categories

- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized items with documented rollback (e.g., config tweaks, capacity scaling).
- Normal change: larger changes requiring approval and scheduling (e.g., model rollout, infra upgrades).
- Emergency change: required to remediate incidents and restore service quickly.

Standard change process

1. Submit change request in Change Tracker (title, impact, rollback plan, owner, start/stop window).
2. Change Approver (SRE lead) reviews risk and schedules during a change window.
3. Pre-change checklist completed (backups, runbook, monitoring set).
4. Execute change and mark status.
5. Post-change verification and update the runbook.

Emergency change flow

1. During an incident, the incident commander may declare emergency change.
2. Implement fix with minimal required approvers (on-call, service owner).
3. File retrospective and change ticket within 24 hours.
4. Conduct post-implementation review and root cause analysis (RCA) within 7 days.

Rollback criteria and metrics

- Automatic rollback if error rate exceeds 5% for 5 minutes or latency increases 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Owners must define service-level rollback triggers in the change request.

4) Data management

Classification labels

- Public: intended for public consumption. No controls required beyond retention policy.
- Internal: Redwood-internal; retention per team defaults.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (e.g., financial plans, contracts). Access restricted to business need.
- Sensitive (PII/PHI): regulated; must follow encryption, approved processing, and minimization.

Handling and storage rules

- All Sensitive data must be stored in approved encrypted stores; keys managed by KMS.
- Export of Sensitive data requires Data Owner signoff and documented business justification.
- De-identification preferred before analysis; use tokenization or irreversible hashing when possible.

Retention and deletion

- Default retention: 36 months for Internal and Confidential unless business reason.
- Sensitive data: follow legal/regulatory retention schedules (e.g., payroll/tax data per country law).
- Data deletion requests: owner completes deletion ticket; infra runs deletion within SLA (standard: 10 business days).

Data access request form (example fields)

- Dataset identifier
- Purpose of access
- Duration requested
- Export required (yes/no)
- Reviewer comments

5) Procurement & expenses

Principles and thresholds

- Use company purchasing card for business travel and low-value purchases (< $2,500) when approved by manager.
- Purchase orders (POs) required for vendor spend > $10,000.
- Capital expenses and multi-year contracts require Finance and Legal review.

Procurement flow (standard vendor purchase)

1. Requester submits Procurement Request form with business justification and budget code.
2. Manager approves. If > $10k, Finance assigns procurement lead and Legal is notified.
3. Procurement lead obtains quotes (if applicable), negotiates terms, and requests Legal review.
4. Once contract executed, Procurement issues PO and informs requester.

Expense report guide (high-level)

- Submit receipts within 30 days of transaction.
- Cardholders must reconcile monthly.
- Meal per diem: $75 USD/day domestic; receipts required for single-meal transactions above $75.
- Lodging: economy or standard business class; exceptions require manager pre-approval.

PO template (copyable snippet)

{
  "po_number": "PO-XXXX-YYYY",
  "vendor_name": "Vendor, Inc.",
  "description": "Software subscription (annual)",
  "amount": "$XX,XXX",
  "billing_terms": "Net 30",
  "owner": "Team / Service Owner"
}

6) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist (minimal)

- Business justification and confirmed budget code.
- Security questionnaire completed (vendor risk level: low/medium/high).
- Data flow diagram if vendor will process company data.
- Contract with appropriate clauses (DPA, security, breach notification).
- Insurance verification and contact points.
- Kickoff meeting with SLAs and escalation contacts.

Vendor risk decisions

- Low risk: SaaS with no company data (e.g., public marketing tools). Procurement lead can complete onboarding.
- Medium risk: SaaS where company data is processed; Security review required.
- High risk: Vendors with access to PII/PHI or production systems; Requires Legal + Security + Procurement approval.

Periodic review

- High-risk vendors reviewed annually. Medium-risk every 18 months. Low-risk every 36 months.

7) Travel policy (quick reference)

Booking and approvals

- Domestic travel: manager approval required; use preferred booking partners for corporate rates.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval; check visa and vaccination requirements.

Allowed expenses and limits

- Economy airfare standard; Premium economy allowable with manager pre-approval for flights > 8 hours.
- Ground transportation: rideshare or standard car service; receipts required.
- Per diem for meals as described in Expenses section.

Safety and duty of care

- Register travel with People Ops for international trips.
- Emergency contact and nearest embassy or consulate info must be provided for travel over 72 hours.

8) Templates and examples

- Access Request form (fields): requester, resource, justification, duration, owner, approver, business impact.
- Procurement Request form (fields): requester, budget code, vendor, estimated amount, justification, preferred vendor contact.
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (bulleted).
- Change Request template: title, owner, window, rollback, monitoring, test plan.
- Expense report sample line: {date, merchant, category, amount, project_code, receipt_link}.

9) Governance, metrics and review cadence

- Quarterly review cycle: People Ops maintains templates and collects feedback; Security and Finance run focused reviews on schedule.
- KPIs to track: average procurement lead time (target: < 10 business days), percent of access requests with time-bound expiry (target: 100%), number of emergency changes per quarter (target: trend down).
- Exceptions: Requests for permanent deviations must be logged as exceptions and approved by People Ops + relevant owner; exceptions are time-limited and reviewed semi-annually.

Appendices and links

- Access Portal: https://access.redwood.local (internal)
- Change Tracker: https://changelog.redwood.local (internal)
- Procurement Request Form: https://forms.redwood.local/procurement (internal)
- Data classification reference: confluence/security-and-compliance/data-classification

Change log

- 2024-05-20: Initial draft published.
- 2025-10-01: Updated procurement thresholds and vendor review cadence.

How to use these templates

- Copy the relevant template block into your team page and update service-specific fields (service owner, SLAs, contact points).
- Submit changes to this crosswalk via the PR template in People Ops (link above); all submissions will be reviewed and merged by People Ops and Security as appropriate.

Contact

- People Ops (process owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai

sections.body:
Overview

This document provides a unified, company-wide protocol for operational controls that span access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, and travel rules. It consolidates commonly used templates, decision thresholds, and step-by-step flows so teams can follow consistent processes and auditors can validate controls.

Goals
- Reduce approval friction for low-risk changes while preserving strong controls for sensitive assets.
- Provide clear, auditable trails for procurement and vendor decisions.
- Standardize role-based access tiers and self-service patterns.
- Ensure data classification drives handling and retention decisions.

Scope
Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors interacting with Redwood systems or representing Redwood in procurement or travel. Exceptions require documented risk sign-off from Finance-Legal and Security.

Owner & Escalation
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (primary), Security (co-owner for data/access sections)
- Day-to-day operations: Shared Services (procurement/expenses), IT Ops (access provisioning), SRE (change management for production systems)
- Escalation: Director, Finance -> VP Ops -> Legal Counsel for contract exceptions

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access with tiered approvals and automated reviews.

Roles and tiers
- Tier 0 (Public): Documentation, non-sensitive marketing assets. Justified by system owner.
- Tier 1 (Internal): Internal dashboards, code repos without prod secrets. Auto-approval by manager for onboarding. Quarterly review.
- Tier 2 (Restricted): Production systems metadata, customer metadata (non-PII). Requires manager + system owner approval. Monthly review and IAM recertification.
- Tier 3 (Sensitive): PII, Secrets, KMS/HSM access, audit logs. Requires manager + system owner + security approver. 30-day emergency token TTL.

Provisioning workflow (standard)
1. User submits access request using the Access Portal (access.redwood.internal). Include justification, requested tier, and duration.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, request escalates to manager's manager.
3. System owner validates least-privilege and either approves or requests scope reduction.
4. Automation provisions access and records grant ID in IAM audit log.
5. Scheduled recertification emails sent based on tier cadence.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Submit Break-Glass request via PagerDuty incident with ticket link. Security will issue a time-limited token (max 24 hours) after documented justification. Post-incident, owner must run a retrospective and revoke or rationalize further.

Access review matrix (summary table)
| Asset class | Example services | Approval chain | Review cadence | Retention of evidence |
|-------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|----------------------|
| Public | Marketing site | Manager | Annual | 1 year |
| Internal | Internal dashboards | Manager | Quarterly | 1 year |
| Restricted | Prod read-only | Manager + Owner | Monthly | 3 years |
| Sensitive | KMS, DB write | Manager + Owner + Security | Monthly | 7 years |

2) Change Management
Purpose: Ensure predictable rollout of changes to infra, runtime, and customer-facing systems.

Change classes
- Standard (low risk): Pre-authorized routine ops (e.g., adding capacity, package updates with green tests). No CAB needed.
- Minor: Non-customer-impacting changes requiring owner approval and automated canary.
- Major: Customer-facing or schema/DB migrations, requires CAB review and rollout plan.
- Emergency: Mitigation of active incidents; follow post-facto CAB review.

Change process (major change checklist)
1. Author prepares Change Request (CR) in Change Tracker including impact analysis, rollback plan, test plan, and monitoring playbook.
2. Submit CR at least 72 hours before planned window.
3. Engineering owner coordinates a pre-CAB review with SRE and Security.
4. CAB meeting: Approvers = Service Owner, SRE Lead, Prod Support, Security Rep, and Product Owner. Decision documented.
5. If approved: schedule in maintenance window, assign runbook author and observers.
6. Execute with live monitoring and rollback guardrails. Capture incident metrics.
7. Post-change review within 48 hours summarizing variance from plan and action items.

Rollback criteria (example)
- Error rate > 3x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes OR
- p95 latency exceeds SLO by 2x for 5 minutes OR
- Any customer-facing data loss or corruption detected.

3) Data Management and Classification
Policy summary
- Data is classified at creation: Public, Internal, Restricted, Sensitive. Classification governs storage, transit encryption, and retention.
- Sensitive data requires encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS for Private deployments) and strict access controls.

Data handling rules (quick reference)
- Transit: TLS 1.2+ required for all external traffic; internal calls must use mTLS.
- At rest: AES-256 or better. DB backups with separate key lifecycle.
- Logging: PII must be redacted before ingestion into observability systems.
- Retention: Default retention is 3 years for Restricted, 7 years for Sensitive unless legal hold applies.

Data classification decision tree (example)
1. Does the data identify an individual? -> Yes => Sensitive or Restricted.
2. Is it covered by contract/regulation (GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA)? -> Yes => Sensitive.
3. Is it telemetry or aggregated metrics? -> Likely Internal.

4) Procurement & Expense Controls
Procurement thresholds and required approvals
- < $5k: Team lead approval; use corporate P-card where available. Purchase must attach quote and purpose.
- $5k–$50k: Procurement ticket + Finance approval; at least one competitive quote preferred.
- $50k–$250k: Procurement + Finance + Legal review for contracts. Vendor security questionnaire required.
- > $250k: Leadership approval (Director+) and VP-level review; full procurement RFP recommended.

Expense categories and documentation
- Travel: itemized receipts required; per-diem caps applied by region.
- Software subscriptions: submit seat count and renewal terms 30 days before expiry.
- Capital vs. expense: Finance will classify per capitalization policy and notify requestor.

Vendor security & procurement checklist (minimum)
1. Completed Vendor Intake Form (VIF) with scope and contact information.
2. Security questionnaire or SIG profile.
3. Proof of insurance & SOC2 or equivalent where applicable.
4. Contract with standard Redwood terms; deviations require Legal sign-off.
5. Procurement entry in vendor registry and assigned owner.

Template: Procurement request fields (for portal)
- Project name
- Business owner
- Estimated annual spend
- SOW/contract link
- Data access required (Yes/No; if yes, classify data)
- Security assessment result link

5) Vendor Lifecycle Management
Stages: Evaluate -> Onboard -> Monitor -> Offboard

Evaluate (selection)
- Use standard RFP template for >$50k. Score vendors on security, cost, SLAs, and integration complexity.
- Shortlist 2–3 vendors when practical.

Onboard
- Assign internal vendor owner and designate integration engineer.
- Configure least-privilege access in a dedicated service account; no shared credentials.
- Register vendor in Vendor Registry with onboarding artifacts.

Monitor
- Quarterly risk review for strategic vendors; annual for tactical vendors.
- Track SLA performance, security posture changes, and cost trends.

Offboard
- Revoke credentials, certificates, and application tokens.
- Confirm data deletion/return per contract.
- Perform final security scan and closure checklist.

6) Travel & Expenses (key rules)
- Business class travel permitted for flights >8hrs economy alternative required if <8hrs. Exceptions require Director approval.
- Hotel standard: business or mid-range corporate rates; upgrades require justification.
- Per-diem: set by region (refer to Travel Rates appendix). Receipts required for expense reports > $25.
- International travel: complete pre-approval and security briefing if traveling to high-risk countries.

Expense submission workflow
1. Submit expenses with receipts within 15 calendar days of trip.
2. Manager approves within 7 days or escalates.
3. Finance processes reimbursement within standard payroll cycle.
4. Excess or unusual expenses flagged for audit.

Templates and attachments
- Access request template (fields)
- Change Request (CR) template and checklist
- Vendor Intake Form (VIF) sample
- Procurement request form JSON example:
{
  \"project\": \"Example Integration\",
  \"owner\": \"team@example.redwood\",
  \"estimated_annual\": \"18000\",
  \"data_access_required\": \"Yes\",
  \"classification\": \"Restricted\"
}

Audit and Reporting
- All approvals and artifacts must be retained in the central Governance bucket with indices for at least the retention period specified by the control (see Access review matrix).
- Monthly operational dashboard: open change requests, outstanding procurement approvals, and active emergency access tokens.
- Annual independent audit: Finance & Legal coordinate with Security to validate vendor and access controls.

Exceptions and re-evaluation
- Exceptions follow an Exception Request process: submit business justification, compensating controls, and a time-bound approval (max 12 months). Legal & Security must co-sign.
- Policy review cadence: Every 12 months or after a major incident.

Appendix: Quick links
- Access Portal: https://access.redwood.internal
- Change Tracker: https://change.redwood.internal
- Procurement Portal: https://procure.redwood.internal
- Vendor Registry: https://vendors.redwood.internal
- Travel Rates & Per-diem: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-rates-2028

Contact for questions
- Finance-Legal policy owner: policy-owner@redwood.com
- Security co-owner: security-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement helpdesk: procure-help@redwood.com

End of document

payload.page_title: Request Lifecycle and Controls Catalog — 2026

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This catalog defines the lifecycle for operational requests and the associated control gates across Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, and Travel. It provides standardized request forms, approval matrices, SLAs, and template artifacts to reduce tribal knowledge and speed consistent decisions.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor agents who submit or approve requests for: system access, configuration changes, data uses, purchases, vendor engagements, and company travel. Exceptions must be approved by the owning function and recorded in the exception registry.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege and just-in-time access.
- Separation of duties for financial and security-critical approvals.
- Automated enforcement where possible; manual review when risk exceeds automation thresholds.
- Clear SLAs and escalation paths for business continuity.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Requester: initiates the request with required justification and attachments.
- Approver: designated role(s) who evaluate and approve/reject per the approval matrix.
- Owner/Maintainer: team that implements the request (SRE, infra, facilities, travel ops).
- Security Reviewer: performs data/privacy/security review when flagged.
- Finance Reviewer: approves expenditures above configured thresholds.
- Legal Reviewer: reviews contracts, vendor terms, and high-risk data-sharing agreements.
- Compliance & Audit: retains records and performs periodic reviews.

Access & Permissions (IAM)
-------------------------
Purpose: Standardize requests for cloud/console/API access and role grants.

Access request flow (standard)
1. Requester completes Access Request form in ProcureFlow/IAM Portal including justification, duration, resource scope, and owner.
2. Auto-validation run by IAM Service: checks policy templates and existing memberships.
3. If low-risk (pre-approved role & <30 days) automatic grant occurs; otherwise routed to Approver(s).
4. Security Reviewer is added if role includes sensitive scopes (PII, audit logs, production write).
5. Owner executes grant and documents ticket ID.

SLAs and thresholds
- Standard requests: 24 business hours.
- High-priority (production incident): 4 hours (phone + portal).
- Emergency after-hours: on-call approver phone escalation; retrospective approval within 24 hours.

Approval matrix (examples)
| Resource category | Typical approver(s) | Security review required | Auto-grant allowed? | Max duration |
|-------------------|---------------------|-------------------------:|--------------------:|------------:|
| Non-prod read-only| Team lead            | No                      | Yes                 | 90 days     |
| Non-prod write    | Team lead + SRE      | No                      | Conditional         | 30 days     |
| Prod read         | Product manager + SRE| Conditional              | No                  | 30 days     |
| Prod write        | Product manager + SRE + Security | Yes         | No                  | 7 days      |
| Audit logs access | Security + Compliance| Yes                     | No                  | 7 days      |

RBAC templates (recommended labels)
- role:data-scientist: read-only datasets + dev compute
- role:inference-operator: production inference write, model deploy APIs
- role:observability-reader: metrics/logs read-only (no PII)

CLI example (request automation)
```
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
rlctl access-request --user alice --role inference-operator --resource project:redwood-prod --duration 6h --reason "investigating latency spike"
```

Change Management
-----------------
Scope: configuration changes to infra, runtime, CI/CD pipelines, production model rollouts, and security controls.

Change categories
- Standard (low-risk, pre-authorized routine changes)
- Normal (planned changes requiring approval and scheduling)
- Emergency (out-of-band fixes for incidents)

Normal change process (numbered)
1. Create RFC in Change Registry (ticket template: ChangeRequest). Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, schedule, owners.
2. Technical review by SRE/Platform and dependency owners.
3. Security and compliance review if change touches data control plane or auth.
4. Scheduled maintenance window and stakeholder notification.
5. Execute change and mark lifecycle states: planned -> staging -> validation -> production -> closed.

Emergency change flow
- On-call SRE follows emergency authorizer list (Primary SRE on-call, then Engineering Manager, then CTO).
- Execute emergency fix and attach retrospective within 48 hours.
- Post-incident RFC must be submitted within 5 business days.

Change guardrails
- All production changes must have automated rollback steps and observability runbooks attached.
- No schema-changing data migrations in production without dry-run and 2 approvers.

Data Management
---------------
Data classification
- Restricted (PII, PHI, financial records): encryption at rest and in transit, access by exception only.
- Internal (product telemetry, internal notes): restricted to employees, aggregated exports require approval.
- Public (marketing materials): permitted for external distribution.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: product telemetry 90 days (hot), 365 days (cold); logs 180 days.
- Restricted data retention must be approved by Data Governance and Legal.
- Data deletion requests follow standard ticketed workflow and are recorded in the Data Deletion Log.

Data use approvals
- Any project that trains models on customer data must complete a Data Use Assessment and obtain Legal + Security signoff.
- Example: dataset_redwood_customers_2025 requires DU-approved contract & KMS policy.

Encryption and key management
- All production encryption keys must be provisioned via KMS/HSM. Key rotation every 90 days for high-sensitivity keys.

Procurement & Expenses
----------------------
Procurement thresholds and approvals
| Amount band (USD) | Required approvals | Procurement channel |
|-------------------:|--------------------|-------------------|
| <$2,500            | Manager            | Card/ExpensesApp  |
| $2,500–$25,000     | Manager + Finance  | ProcureFlow (PO)  |
| $25,000–$250,000   | Manager + Finance + Procurement | ProcureFlow + Contracting |
| >$250,000          | Exec sponsor + Legal + Procurement | Strategic sourcing |

Preferred procurement flow
1. Create Purchase Request with justification, budget code, and vendor information.
2. Finance validates budget and is assigned approver.
3. Procurement reviews for preferred vendors and negotiates T&C if applicable.
4. PO is issued; vendor onboarding checklist triggered for new vendors.

Expense policy
- Employees should expense costs within 60 days. Card disputes must be filed within 90 days.
- Travel bookings: Economy or lowest reasonable fare; upgrade only with exec approval.

Vendor Management
-----------------
Vendor risk levels and onboarding checklist
- Risk levels: Low, Medium, High (based on data access, control plane integration, criticality).
- Onboarding steps for new vendor (checklist):
  1. Business justification and owner assignment.
  2. Security questionnaire (VendorRisk) completion.
  3. Contract with minimum security clauses (encryption, breach notification, subprocessor list).
  4. Procurement creates PO and payment terms.
  5. Technical integration review and test plan.
  6. Compliance records stored in Vendor Registry.

Contractual minimums (summary)
- Data processing agreement for any vendor handling customer data.
- Right to audit clause for high-risk vendors.
- Minimum 30-day termination notice and documented exit plan for critical services.

Vendor monitoring
- Quarterly review for medium/high vendors; monthly health checks for critical platform vendors.
- Maintain scorecard: uptime, incident response time, patch cadence, security findings.

Travel Policies
---------------
Pre-approval and booking
- All travel reimbursed must be pre-approved by the Requester’s manager in the TravelPortal.
- Book through TravelPortal or approved agency for company liability coverage.

Per diems and allowable expenses
- Domestic: meals up to $75/day; Lodging: reasonable single occupancy rate.
- International: per-region rates available in TravelPortal templates.
- Alcohol may be expensed only while entertaining clients with prior manager approval.

Safety and emergency
- Employees traveling to countries with Level 3 or higher travel advisories require Security team approval.
- Emergency contact: travel-support@redwood.com and on-call security phone.

Templates & quick artifacts
--------------------------
Included templates (stored in Templates folder in ProcureFlow)\- Access Request form (JSON/YAML example below)
- Purchase Request form
- Change Request (RFC) template
- Vendor Onboarding checklist
- Data Use Assessment template

Access Request JSON example
```
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.com",
  "role": "inference-operator",
  "resource": "project:redwood-prod",
  "duration_hours": 6,
  "justification": "Investigating model latency spike",
  "approvals_required": ["product_manager", "sre"]
}
```

Purchase Request example fields
- requester_email, vendor_name, item_description, estimated_cost, budget_code, justification, required_by_date, attachments

Escalation and exceptions
-------------------------
- Escalation path for stalled requests: Requester -> Approver -> Owner team lead -> Function head -> People Ops / Finance escalation.
- Exceptions to policy must be documented with risk assessment and approved by the responsible function head and Risk Committee.

Auditability and retention
-------------------------
- All approvals and artifacts are recorded in ProcureFlow and retained for a minimum of 7 years for procurement; access logs retained per Data Retention schedule.
- Regular audits: Quarterly spot-checks for access grants and annual vendor compliance review.

Adoption and tooling notes
------------------------
- Automate low-risk grants via IAM Service and ProcureFlow integrations.
- Integrate VendorRisk and Contracting with ProcureFlow to enforce policy gates before POs are issued.
- Use AuditExports to feed SIEM for all privileged access events.

Related pages and references
--------------------------
- /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/standard-rbac-2024.json
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-change-retro-2025.json
- /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement-and-expenses/purchase-guidelines-2025.json

Revision history
---------------
| Date | Author | Notes |
|-----|-------|------|
| 2025-11-12 | Priya N. Rao | Initial draft and consolidation of cross-functional request flows. |
| 2025-12-18 | Marcus Li | Added SLA targets and RBAC templates. |
| 2026-02-08 | Sofia Alvarez | Updated procurement thresholds and vendor onboarding checklist. |

payload.page_title: Policy & Process Almanac: Company-wide Standards and Templates

sections.body:
Overview:

This document is the single-source reference for company-wide policies and process templates across Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel, and Internal Templates. Intended audience: people-ops, finance, engineering, product, security, and managers who must follow or approve cross-functional requests.

Goals:
- Provide clear, actionable procedures for common requests and approvals.
- Reduce turnaround time by standardizing thresholds, owners, and templates.
- Ensure security and compliance controls are applied consistently.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and people with accounts on Redwood-managed systems.
- Exceptions require documented approval via the Exceptions process (see Escalation & Exceptions).

Quick policy matrix (summary):
| Domain | Primary owner | Typical SLA / Threshold | Key artifacts |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Access & Permissions | people-ops / security | Standard requests: 3 business days; Emergency elevated access: 2 hours | Access request template, RBAC group list |
| Change Management | eng-platform | Normal changes: 5 business days pre-notice; Major infra changes require CAB approval | Change request template, rollback playbook |
| Data Management | security / finance-legal | Data deletion requests: 10 business days; Retention: defined per classification | Data classification matrix, retention schedule |
| Procurement & Expenses | finance-legal | Purchases <$5k: 3 business days; >$50k: exec approval + 20 business days | PO template, vendor evaluation checklist |
| Vendor Management | finance-legal / security | New vendor onboarding: 15 business days | Vendor questionnaire, contract template |
| Travel | people-ops / finance-legal | Pre-approval: 5 business days; Expense submission: within 15 days of return | Travel request & expense templates |

1) Access & Permissions
Principles:
- Principle of least privilege by default.
- Temporary elevation preferred over long-lived high privileges.
- All privileged access requires an owner and an audit TTL.

Role definitions (examples):
- Reader: read-only to resources; auto-approver via manager.
- Contributor: ability to create resources; manager + tech lead approval.
- Admin: elevated privileges; security review + VP approval for permanent access.

Standard request flow (self-service for most):
1. Employee opens Access Request using the access_request template (link in Templates section).
2. Manager verifies business justification and approves in the system.
3. Technical owner approves (for contributor/admin).
4. Provisioning occurs via IaC or identity provider (IdP) automation.
5. Access is auto-expired after TTL unless renewed via a documented review.

Access thresholds requiring extra review:
- Any request granting "Admin" or "Privileged" role on production systems requires security review.
- Cross-tenant/VPC access requires network security sign-off and on-call notification.

Example CLI request (for advanced teams using the RBAC API):
```
curl -X POST https://identity.redwood.example/api/v1/access-requests \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user":"alice@redwood.com","role":"prod-db-contributor","expiry":"2026-04-15","justification":"incident debug"}'
```
RBAC groups (current canonical list):
- redwood-readonly
- redwood-devs
- redwood-prod-ops
- redwood-admins
(Updates to the canonical list must be proposed via the Change Management process and documented in the RBAC registry.)

2) Change Management
Change types and required approvals:
- Minor (non-production config changes, docs): owner approval.
- Standard (code deploy, infra config): owner + release manager approval.
- Major (schema migrations, network changes, infra rollouts): CAB approval (weekly CAB meeting).
- Emergency (P1/P0 incidents): follow the Incident Commander's emergency change flow; retrospective required.

Change lifecycle checklist (before scheduling):
- Define impact window and rollback plan.
- Confirm pre-deployment validation tests.
- Notify stakeholders via the release calendar (email + Slack channel).
- Schedule change outside blackout windows unless emergency.

Pre-approval windows and SLAs:
- Standard changes: submit 5 business days before planned date.
- Major changes: submit 10 business days before planned date.
- The CAB meets every Tuesday at 09:00 PT; decisions recorded in the change tracker.

Rollback policy:
- Every change must include a tested rollback procedure that can be completed within the rollback window (target: 60 minutes for infra rollbacks).
- If rollback cannot be completed automatically, include manual runbook steps with required on-call contacts.

Change request template (brief):
- Title, owner, scope, start/end window, rollback steps, validation plan, stakeholder list, risk level.

3) Data Management
Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: safe to share externally. Retention: 3 years unless specified.
- INTERNAL: company-internal; retention as required by business.
- CONFIDENTIAL: PII, financials, customer data; retention per legal & contract.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (HIPAA, PCI, etc.) — special handling and encryption at rest + in transit.

Retention & deletion:
- See the Data Retention Schedule table below for defaults. Deletions must be recorded in the Data Deletion Log.

Data retention schedule (examples):
| Data class | Default retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Public assets (marketing) | 3 years | Marketing lead |
| Internal analytics | 2 years | Data Platform team |
| Customer logs (non-PII) | 1 year | Customer Success |
| Customer PII | as contracted; minimum 7 years | Legal 

Encryption & key management:
- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted with customer-managed keys where contractually required.
- KMS usage: AWS KMS + HSM integration for private deployments; key rotation every 365 days recommended.

Data transfer checklist (example YAML template for cross-region movement):
```
transfer_request:
  owner: eng-data-platform
  source: us-west-2-pipeline
  destination: eu-central-1-lake
  data_class: INTERNAL
  approval: [security, legal]
  date_required: 2026-04-01
```

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement tiers & approval matrix:
| Tier | Value | Approver(s) |
|---|---:|---|
| Tier 1 | <$5,000 | Requester manager |
| Tier 2 | $5,000 - $50,000 | Manager + Finance (budget owner) |
| Tier 3 | >$50,000 | Director + Finance + Legal review (if third party) |

Purchase order (PO) process:
1. Raise a PO request in the procurement tool with supplier info and SOW.
2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO.
3. Contracts team reviews if third-party software/service.
4. Supplier receipt must match PO; invoices routed to AP for three-way match.

Expense policy (travel and non-travel):
- Employees must submit expenses within 15 calendar days of transaction.
- Meals and incidental per diem capped per location (see Travel section).
- Unapproved or late submissions may be delayed or denied.

Allowed payment methods:
- Company card: primary for travel and approved subscriptions.
- Personal reimbursements: supported with receipts and manager approval.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding checklist (new vendor):
1. Vendor Profile: legal name, tax ID, region.
2. Security Questionnaire: SOC 2/ISO attestation or complete CAIQ.
3. Contract review: legal and procurement.
4. Risk assessment: data access, SSO, encryption requirements.
5. PO / payment terms setup.

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low: consultants without access to customer data — standard contract.
- Medium: vendors with limited system access — SSO + scoped permissions + annual review.
- High: vendors with customer data or production access — security controls, quarterly audits, and encryption requirements in contract.

Renewal & offboarding:
- Notify stakeholders 60 days before contract end for renewals.
- Offboarding checklist includes termination of all credentials, return/destruction of data, and deletion from asset registry.

6) Travel Policies
Booking & approvals:
- Use the corporate travel tool for all business travel.
- Domestic trips <48 hours require manager pre-approval. International travel requires security & people-ops notification.

Per diem & reimbursements:
- Per diem rates follow the government locality table adopted by Redwood; see travel-per-diem template.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business requires director approval.

Expense submission steps:
1. Submit expense within 15 days of return with itemized receipts.
2. Manager approves in expense system.
3. Finance processes payment on the next payroll cycle.

Safety & emergency contact:
- Before international travel, register trip with people-ops and provide emergency contact information.

7) Internal Templates & Quick Links
Included templates (copy/paste into the request tools):
- Access request template: (fields) requester, manager, role, expiry, justification, technical owner.
- Change request template: (fields) title, owner, windows, rollback steps, validation steps.
- Vendor onboarding checklist (as described above).

Sample Access Request (one-line):
Title: Temporary PROD DB Contributor
Requester: alice@redwood.com
Manager: bob@redwood.com
Role: prod-db-contributor
Expiry: 2026-04-12
Justification: customer incident debug

8) Roles & Ownership (contact pointers)
- people-ops: people-ops@redwood.example (policy questions, travel, benefits)
- finance-legal: procure@redwood.example (POs, vendor contracts)
- security: sec-eng@redwood.example (access reviews, data policy)
- eng-platform: infra@redwood.example (change board, release calendar)

9) Escalations & Exceptions
Exception request process:
1. Submit an Exceptions Request document with justification and compensating controls.
2. Owner team reviews within 5 business days.
3. If risk > medium, route to the Cross-Functional Exceptions Panel (CFEP) for final decision.

Emergency escalation flow (P0/P1):
- Page on-call via PagerDuty -> Incident Commander -> Notify CTO and Head of Security -> Temporary emergency change allowed with post-incident CAB review.

Appendix: Useful links and artifacts
- Access request template: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change request tracker: /confluence/tools/change-tracker
- Data retention schedule: /confluence/policies-and-process/data-retention-2025
- PO template: /confluence/templates/purchase-order
- Vendor questionnaire (CAIQ): /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-caiaq

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12: Created by Priya Menon; initial policy draft.
- 2026-02-20: Added procurement tiers and vendor renewal timings (reviewers Marco Alvarez, Sofia Patel).
- 2026-03-05: Finalized RBAC group canonical list and CLI example; published.

End of document.

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our standard operating procedures for employee access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expense approvals, vendor onboarding, and employee travel. It is designed as a single "concierge" reference for stakeholders who coordinate cross-functional approvals and execution (line managers, people-ops, finance, security, and legal).

Principles
- Least privilege: Grant only the minimum access required for a task and review quarterly.
- Clear accountability: Every request must have a named approver and an operational owner.
- Auditability: Decisions, approvals, and evidence (receipts, contracts, IAM logs) must be retained per retention rules.
- Risk-tiered control: Higher value / sensitive activities require stricter review and formal sign-off.

1) Access & Permissions Lifecycle
Intro: Applies to all access requests for cloud consoles, production systems, data stores, internal tools, and third-party SaaS.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Submit request through Access Portal (Confluence link + internal form). Include: justification, duration, resources, data categories.
2. Manager approval (explicit) within 72 hours.
3. Security review for requests involving sensitive or regulated data (PII, PHI, PCI).
4. IAM provisioning & automation executes change; owner confirms access.
5. Scheduled review dates added (default 90 days) with auto-expiration.
sections.heading: Request flow (standard)

sections.body:
- Owner submits an emergency ticket in PagerDuty with category "BreakGlass" and tags the security oncall.
- Temporary access granted for a maximum of 12 hours, logged and must be reconciled with a post-incident justification within 24 hours.
sections.heading: Emergency access flow (break glass)

sections.body:
- Tier 1 (non-sensitive tooling, read-only): manager approval.
- Tier 2 (write access to production-adjacent infra): manager + platform lead.
- Tier 3 (access to PII/regulated systems, production writes): manager + security + legal where contract/regulatory scope applies.
sections.heading: Permission Tiers and Approvals

sections.body:
- Request form copy, approval chain, policy link, IAM ticket id, and audit log export (CSV) uploaded to the ticket before closure.

2) Change Management (software + infra)
Scope: Applies to changes that modify runtime behavior, data schemas, deployments, infra configuration, or access patterns.
sections.heading: Required evidence and logging

sections.body:
- Standard (pre-approved routine ops): follow runbook, update change log.
- Minor (low risk): RFC + reviewer signoff; can be scheduled in maintenance window.
- Major (high risk, data migration, schema change, infra reconfiguration): full RFC, cross-team review, dry run in staging, canary rollout plan, rollback procedure.
- Emergency: declared by oncall; must be postmortem'd and converted into a formal RFC within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Change categories

sections.body:
- <= $500 infra spend & non-customer facing: team lead
- $500–$5,000 or schema changes affecting <1% of users: infra manager + SRE
- > $5,000 or customer-impacting: infra manager + SRE + Product + Finance (if budgetary)
sections.heading: Change approval matrix (example)

sections.body:
- All major changes require documented canary metrics, automated health checks, and a single-button rollback where possible.
- If a rollback is executed, follow the Incident Report template and schedule an RCA within 3 business days.
sections.heading: Rollout & rollback

sections.body:
- Default maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC.
- Exceptions must be approved 72 hours in advance and include a fallback plan.

3) Data Management & Classification
sections.heading: Change window guidance

sections.body:
- Public: safe to publish. Retention: optional.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal use. Retention: 1 year unless otherwise noted.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (contracts, roadmaps). Retention: 3 years.
- Regulated: PII, PHI, PCI. Retention and handling per legal/regulatory requirements; encrypt at rest & in transit.
sections.heading: Classification levels

sections.body:
- Regulated data must be stored in approved encrypted stores (KMS-backed) and access limited to Tier 3.
- De-identification is required before data leaves secure environments for analysis.
- Backups: encryption enabled; retention schedules must be documented and reviewed annually.
sections.heading: Handling rules

sections.body:
- Logs (system): 90 days raw, 1 year aggregated
- Audit trails (access): 3 years
- Employee records: 7 years post-employment
- Vendor contracts: 7 years after contract end

4) Procurement & Expense Approval Patterns
sections.heading: Data retention & deletion schedule (summary table)

sections.body:
- Purchase <= $1,000: Requester + Manager approval (Procurement team notified).
- $1,001–$10,000: Manager + Finance reviewer (PO required).
- > $10,000: Manager + Finance + VP-level sign-off + Legal review for vendor contracts.
sections.heading: Spending thresholds and approvers (quick reference)

sections.body:
1. Complete Purchase Requisition form (link in header). Include justification, GL code, budget owner.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO for approved requests.
3. Vendor invoices to be directed to procurements@redwood.com with PO number.
sections.heading: Procurement workflow

sections.body:
- Cardholders must reconcile monthly. Attach receipt PDFs for any charge > $25.
- Personal expenses are prohibited. Card use for travel and subsistence only unless preapproved.
- Missing receipt: manager signoff + lost-receipt affidavit.
sections.heading: Corporate card & expense policy highlights

sections.body:
- Travel: GL 6001.
- Contractor services: GL 5202.
- Cloud infra: GL 6105.

5) Vendor Onboarding & Ongoing Governance
sections.heading: Expense coding examples (for AP)

sections.body:
1. Initiation: Requester submits Vendor Onboarding Form including SOW, security questionnaire, and expected spend.
2. Procurement review: Finance validates budget and PO terms.
3. Security assessment: security team runs the Vendor Risk Questionnaire (VRQ). High-risk vendors require a full security assessment and a SOC2 or equivalent.
4. Legal review: contract terms, SLAs, liability clauses.
5. Account provisioning: least-privilege accounts issued and a named owner assigned.
6. Go-live: monitor first 30 days and schedule a 90-day checkpoint.
sections.heading: Onboarding steps (minimum)

sections.body:
- Low: non-production SaaS with no sensitive data. Controls: standard contract + annual review.
- Medium: services that process internal data. Controls: VRQ, annual questionnaire, limited access scopes.
- High: vendors that handle regulated data or critical infrastructure. Controls: SOC2, penetration test evidence, quarterly reviews, contractual security SLAs, right-to-audit clause.
sections.heading: Vendor risk tiers and controls

sections.body:
- Disable accounts and revoke keys.
- Verify data deletion or return per contract.
- Ensure final invoice & PO closure.
- Update asset & vendor registry.

6) Travel & Remote Work Expense Guidance
sections.heading: Termination checklist (vendors)

sections.body:
- All international travel requires manager + people-ops pre-approval.
- Travel estimated > $2,500 requires VP-level sign-off.
sections.heading: Pre-approval

sections.body:
- Book through corporate travel portal. Use preferred vendors where available.
- Per diem for meals: $75/day domestic, $100/day international (or actuals with receipts).
sections.heading: Travel booking & per diem

sections.body:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must check-in with People Ops and register with the travel security provider.
- For work requiring visas or formal letters of invitation, allow 4–6 weeks lead time.
sections.heading: Safety & compliance

sections.body:
- Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of trip completion. Exceptions require manager approval.

7) Internal Templates & Quick Checklists
A. Access Request checklist (copy into Access Portal):
- Reason for access
- Resources requested (list)
- Duration (start/end)
- Business sponsor + Manager name
- Data categories involved
- Approval evidence uploaded

B. Vendor Onboarding templated fields (YAML example):
---
vendor_name: ""
vendor_type: "" # SaaS / Contractor / Hardware
estimated_annual_spend: ""
data_access: "" # none / internal / regulated
security_documents: ["SOC2", "PenTest"]
owner: ""
---

C. Change RFC minimum sections:
- Summary
- Owner & stakeholders
- Risk assessment
- Rollout plan & canary metrics
- Rollback procedure
- Schedule & maintenance window

D. Expense submission template (email subject):
Expense: <Your Name> - <Trip/Reason> - <MM/YYYY> | PO: <PO# if applicable>

8) Ownership & Escalation Matrix
sections.heading: Expense submission timeline

sections.body:
- Access control operations: Security (IAM team)
- Change approval board: SRE + Platform leads + Product
- Procurement: Finance + Procurement ops
- Vendor risk & contracts: Legal + Security
- Travel & People Ops: People Ops + Finance
sections.heading: Summary of primary owners

sections.body:
1. Attempt resolution with the owner.
2. If unresolved in 48 hours, escalate to team manager.
3. If unresolved in 5 business days or high-risk, escalate to Director-level.

Appendix: Useful links & CLI examples
- Access Portal: https://internal.redwood.com/access-portal
- Vendor Onboarding form: https://internal.redwood.com/vendor-onboard
- Example audit export command (AWS):
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ConsoleLogin --start-time 2025-01-01 --end-time 2025-06-01 --output json > login-audit.json
sections.heading: Escalation steps

sections.body:
- Procurement ops: procurements@redwood.com
- Security intake: security-intake@redwood.com
- People Ops travel desk: travel@redwood.com

Revision history
- 2024-10-15: Initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2025-03-12: Added Emergency access clarifications and vendor risk tiers (Rosa Kim)
- 2025-06-10: Updated procurement thresholds and travel pre-approval workflow (Diego Hernandez)

End of document
