payload.page_title: GPU local sim-runner and canary eval playbook

sections.body:
Overview
========
This playbook describes the "GPU Local Sim-Runner" used by Redwood Inference engineering teams to generate realistic synthetic inference traffic for capacity testing, canary evaluation, and local debug. The goal is to provide a repeatable, low-cost way to validate scheduling, batching, KV cache behavior, and cost signals before touching production GPU pools. It covers architecture, CI integration, example workload specs, Terraform/IaC snippets, SLOs to validate, and an incident checklist.

Scope
-----
- Intended audience: infra engineers, SREs, runtime engineers, and QA where GPU behavior matters.
- Environments: developer laptop devbox (cpu-only), ephemeral CI GPU pool (Buildkite/GHA runner), on-prem test-cluster, and sandbox cloud GPU account.
- Not covered: full production rollout steps for Dedicated customers. See related product docs for that.

Goals and acceptance criteria
-----------------------------
- Validate queue/backpressure and eviction behavior under realistic inferencing patterns.
- Surface regressions in latency tail (P95/P99) and token-cost changes ahead of release.
- Run nightly and pre-deploy canaries that mimic tenant mixes (short-chat, long-context, streaming).
- Cost guardrails: any simulated run that exceeds budget triggers an automatic teardown and Slack alert.

SLOs and metrics we check
-------------------------
- P50/P95/P99 latency (ms) for simulated single-request and multi-request workloads.
- Token cost delta (simulated estimated tokens) vs baseline (should not increase > 6% for patch releases).
- Batch size distribution and percent of requests batched > target (target: 65% for throughput mode).
- GPU util and memory headroom (keep < 92% sustained utilization during canaries).

Architecture (logical)
---------------------
- Sim-Runner CLI: accepts workload spec (JSON/YAML) and emits request traces to the test endpoint.
- Orchestrator: CI job or local runner that provisions ephemeral test targets (via Terraform module) and collects artifacts to object storage.
- Metrics exporter: lightweight sidecar/agent that scrapes runtime metrics and pushes to our Prometheus/Grafana test cluster.
- Analysis job: converts traces to canary report and uploads to the Canary Dashboard.

Testbed components and ownership
--------------------------------
| Component | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| sim-runner (bin/sim-runner) | Generate requests, control QPS, sequence length, jitter | eng-serving-runtime |
| tf-module/gpu-sandbox | Create ephemeral GPU nodes, node pool, VPC peering | eng-infra |
| ci/jobs/canary | Orchestrate provisioning, run sim, collect metrics | eng-infra/ci |
| metrics-exporter | Export local metrics to test Prometheus | eng-sre |

Local developer quickstart
-------------------------
1. Pull the repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/gpu-sim-runner.git
2. Install: make install (creates virtualenv and installs bin/sim-runner)
3. Start a local test target (CPU devbox): ./bin/sim-runner --serve-local --port 8080 &
4. Run a short workload: ./bin/sim-runner run --spec examples/short-chat.json --target http://localhost:8080 --qps 50 --duration 2m
5. Inspect logs and artifacts in ./artifacts/<timestamp>

Example workload spec (short-chat.json)
---------------------------------------
{
  "name": "short-chat-50qps",
  "mix": [
    {"type": "chat", "prompt_length": 16, "response_length": 32, "weight": 0.8},
    {"type": "embed", "size": 512, "weight": 0.2}
  ],
  "qps": 50,
  "duration_seconds": 120,
  "jitter_pct": 10
}

CI integration (Buildkite / GitHub Actions)
-------------------------------------------
- We run two classes of CI jobs: quick smoke (on CPU runners) and full canary (on ephemeral GPU sandboxes).
- Full canary triggers: merges to main for runtime, quantization, or kernel selection changes; scheduled nightly for critical branches.

Example Buildkite job snippet (gpu-sandbox canary)
--------------------------------------------------
steps:
  - label: "gpu-canary: provision"
    command: |
      scripts/provision-sandbox.sh --tf-module tf-module/gpu-sandbox --env canary-$BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER
  - label: "gpu-canary: run sim"
    command: |
      ./bin/sim-runner run --spec ci/workloads/sha-mix.json --target $SANDBOX_ENDPOINT --qps 200 --duration 900 --report artifacts/report.json
    plugins: [docker#v3.7.0]
  - wait
  - label: "gpu-canary: analyze & teardown"
    command: |
      scripts/analyze-report.sh artifacts/report.json || echo 'analysis failed'
      scripts/teardown-sandbox.sh --env canary-$BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER

Terraform / IaC example (ephemeral sandbox module)
--------------------------------------------------
- Module name: tf-module/gpu-sandbox
- Intent: small, short-lived clusters for canaries (1-4 nodes), preconfigured with sandbox subnet and minimal IAM.
- Minimal variables table:
| variable | type | default | description |
|---|---:|---|---|
| cluster_name | string | "sim-canary" | name of GKE/EKS cluster or instance group |
| node_count | number | "2" | default node count for canary runs |
| gpu_type | string | "nvidia-a10" | accelerator SKU |
| preemptible | bool | "true" | allow preemptible/spot nodes to save cost |
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
module "gpu_sandbox" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com:redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//gpu-sandbox?ref=v1.2.0"
  cluster_name = "${var.env}-canary"
  node_count = 2
  gpu_type = var.gpu_type
  preemptible = true
}

Cost and safety controls
------------------------
- Budget limit: $30 per canary by default. If provisioning estimate > budget, the job fails fast.
- Max runtime: 30 minutes for ephemeral clusters; CI job has a hard timeout of 45m.
- Auto-teardown: scripts/teardown-sandbox.sh must run even on analysis failure (use Buildkite hooks or GHA always:).

Canary evaluation procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------
1. Create unique env id: CANARY_YYYYMMDD_<build>.
2. Provision terraform sandbox: scripts/provision-sandbox.sh --env $CANARY_ID.
3. Wait for nodes ready (health check endpoint, expected time ~ 3-6m).
4. Run sim-runner with canonical workload for the patch: ./bin/sim-runner run --spec ci/workloads/canary-core.json --qps 180 --duration 15m --report artifacts/report.json.
5. Collect metrics: prometheus scrape, logs, and artifacts.
6. Generate canary report: scripts/analyze-report.sh artifacts/report.json -> artifacts/canary-report.html.
7. Gate policy: if P99 latency increases > 10% OR token-cost delta > 6% -> fail and open a blocker ticket on Phabricator/Jira with artifacts.
8. Teardown sandbox regardless of pass/fail.

Alerts and dashboards
---------------------
- Canary Dashboard: Grafana dashboard id 1203 (canary/sim-runner). Shows latency histograms, batch-size distribution, GPU util heatmap, and token-cost trend.
- Slack channel: #infra-gpu-canaries receives pass/fail posts with a link to the artifacts archive.
- Alert rules (Prometheus):
  - canary_p99_regression: (increase >10% vs baseline) for 1 evaluation -> Severity: high, notify #infra-oncall and owner.
  - canary_cost_spike: (token_cost_delta > 6%) -> Severity: medium, notify eng-infra and runtime owners.

Runbook: when a canary fails
----------------------------
1. Triage the report: look at artifacts/canary-report.html and compare to last-green baseline.
2. Identify root signal: increased batching? kernel change? quantization profile? memory swap?
3. If root cause is infra (TF/driver/kernel), open an incident and page eng-sre.
4. If root cause is runtime code: revert canary branch or trigger canary rollback.
5. Run a reduced test locally to reproduce iteratively: low-qps with verbose logging.
6. Once resolved, re-run the canary and attach a short postmortem to the original ticket.

Troubleshooting checklist
-------------------------
- Provisioning failed: check Terraform plan logs, quota errors, and service account IAM (tf-module/gpu-sandbox/iam-policy).
- Excessive P99 with low GPU util: likely small batch sizes or KV cache misses — enable profiling (./bin/sim-runner --profile) and capture NVTX traces.
- OOM on node: reduce worker concurrency or choose larger GPU SKU; ensure preflight memory check is enabled in script.
- Cost overruns: abort and tag test-run as "budget-exceeded"; examine workload spec for QPS/duration mistakes.

Developer troubleshooting commands
--------------------------------
- Start sim-runner locally (verbose): ./bin/sim-runner --spec ci/workloads/debug-long.json --target $ENDPOINT --qps 10 --duration 300 --verbose
- Collect NVTX traces: export SIM_NVTX=1 && ./bin/sim-runner run ... (then run nvprof on the node).

Oncall escalation matrix
------------------------
- 1st: owning runtime engineer (pager duty team: runtime-eng)
- 2nd: eng-sre lead oncall
- 3rd: infra-eng manager

Retention and artifacts
-----------------------
- Canary artifacts are retained for 14 days in S3://redwood-canary-artifacts/. Use scripts/fetch-artifacts.sh to pull them locally.

Appendix A: canonical workload recipes
-------------------------------------
- short-chat: 50 QPS, 16 token prompts, 32 token responses (good for smoke tests).
- long-context: 10 QPS, 2048 prompt tokens, 1024 response tokens (stress KV/cache and memory).
- mix-tenant: multi-weighted mix of chat/stream/embed to exercise routing and batch formation.

Appendix B: changelog
----------------------
- 2024-05-10: initial draft and prototype runner (Asha Patel).
- 2024-09-12: added HCL tf-module snippet and budget guardrails (Marcus Lee).
- 2025-11-02: moved to published, tightened cost-control defaults to $30 and reduced max runtime (Evelyn Chen).

Contacts and ownership
----------------------
- Primary owner: eng-infra (oncall: #infra-oncall)
- Runtime integration: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-eng@redwood.com)
- CI ownership: eng-infra-ci

Related pages
-------------
See related pages in page metadata for provisioning modules, GPU forecasting, and ephemeral GPU pools for additional reference.

End of playbook
sections.heading: Snippet (HCL)

payload.page_title: Private Release Gating & Change Management Policy

sections.body:
This policy defines the **minimum required gates** and **change-management workflow** for shipping Redwood Private releases (VPC and on-prem/air-gapped). The goal is to make upgrades **safe by default**, reduce upgrade-related incidents, and ensure we produce **auditable artifacts** (plan, prechecks, backup/restore status, approvals, and communications).

This page is normative. Teams may add stricter checks; exceptions require formal approval (see “Exceptions”).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Redwood Private control plane + data plane releases shipped via:
  - `redwood-private-installer` upgrade workflows
  - Helm chart updates (`redwood-helm-charts`)
  - Terraform module updates (`redwood-terraform`) impacting version pinning or artifact sources
  - Platform version compatibility/policy updates in `redwood`
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Redwood hosted API releases
- Pure documentation-only releases
sections.heading: Does not apply to

sections.body:
- **Private release**: A versioned set of artifacts (installer, charts, images, migrations, compatibility policy) intended for customer-managed environments.
- **Upgrade plan**: A generated, persisted, auditable plan describing staged steps, required artifacts, dependencies, and rollback entry points.
- **N-1 → N**: Supported default upgrade path for initial GA. (Multi-hop may be supported case-by-case.)
- **Blocking precheck**: Must pass to proceed. Failure requires remediation or approved exception.
- **Warning precheck**: Does not block, but must be acknowledged in the change record.
- **Change record**: Single source of truth for a planned customer upgrade (internal ticket + attached artifacts).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
A Private release or customer change event may proceed only if all of the following are satisfied:
1) **Supported upgrade path** is enforced by compatibility policy (default: N-1 → N).
2) **Upgrade plan** is generated and stored (no “imperative-only” upgrades).
3) **Blocking prechecks** pass.
4) **Backup** completes successfully (or an approved alternative is documented).
5) **Approval gates** are completed (Release Engineering + SRE; Security as required by risk score).
6) **Customer communications** are sent per risk score and timeline.
7) **Rollback readiness** is verified (rollback command available, rollback hooks present, post-rollback checks defined).
8) **Auditability** requirements are met (installer logs + audit events retained, support bundle includes upgrade traces).
sections.heading: Policy summary (required gates)

sections.body:
- **Release Engineering (required)**: validates release artifact integrity, CI evidence, and packaging.
  - Default: Connor O’Brien (delegate: Devon Price)
- **SRE (required)**: validates operational safety, monitoring/alerting, rollback readiness.
  - Default: Sean Gallagher (delegate: Rafael Mendes)
sections.heading: Required approvers

sections.body:
- **Security/Compliance (conditional)**: required for regulated environments, backup/restore changes, audit event schema changes, or any change involving secrets/KMS.
  - Default: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin
- **Infrastructure (conditional)**: required for changes impacting storage backends, networking, or cluster requirements.
  - Default: Irene Choi / Victor Alvarez
sections.heading: Conditional reviewers (by risk score)

sections.body: Use the following rubric to determine communication timelines, approvals, and additional safeguards.
sections.heading: Risk scoring (customer environment)

sections.body:
- **Impact**
  - 1: Control-plane-only minor patch, no migrations, no Helm ordering changes
  - 2: Rolling restart of data plane or minor migration, expected <5 min disruption to management operations
  - 3: Schema migrations, control-plane/data-plane sequencing changes, or any change with potential inference impact
- **Complexity**
  - 1: Single component update, no dependency changes
  - 2: Multiple components, Helm hooks/order changes, or new prechecks
  - 3: New backup mechanism, rollback semantics change, or artifact source/mirror changes
- **Environment sensitivity**
  - 1: Non-regulated VPC; standard connectivity
  - 2: Regulated VPC (audit/SIEM requirements) or customer has strict maintenance windows
  - 3: On-prem/air-gapped, or customer has hard change-control gates (e.g., CAB), or evidence retention requirements
sections.heading: Risk score = Impact (1–3) + Complexity (1–3) + Environment sensitivity (1–3)

sections.body:
- **Low (3–4)**: Standard gates
- **Medium (5–6)**: Standard + enhanced comms + rollback drill (tabletop)
- **High (7–9)**: Standard + Security review + pre-upgrade readiness meeting + explicit rollback rehearsal plan

Record the score and tier in the change record.
sections.heading: Risk tiers

sections.body:
Before a Private release is marked “eligible for customer upgrades”, Release Engineering must attach evidence of:
- **CI evidence**: private installer integration test matrix coverage (minimum baseline below)
- **Compatibility policy update**: supported upgrade paths explicitly enumerated
- **Changelog**: customer-facing highlights + known issues + upgrade notes
- **Rollback contract**: unchanged or explicitly documented (if changed, requires SRE + Security review)
sections.heading: Release readiness requirements (pre-cut)

sections.body:
- Kubernetes versions: current supported set (see test matrix page)
- Scenarios:
  - N-1 → N happy path upgrade
  - Precheck failure injection (at least one blocking check)
  - Migration lock timeout simulation (ensures safe defaults / bounded timeouts)
  - Rollback invocation after a simulated mid-upgrade failure
sections.heading: Minimum CI baseline (must pass)

sections.body:
- Target environment identifiers (customer, region/site, VPC vs on-prem)
- Target versions (current → desired)
- Risk score + tier
- Proposed maintenance window
- On-call coverage plan
sections.heading: Create a change record (internal ticket) and attach/link

sections.body:
- Generate plan:
  - `redwood-private upgrade plan --from <current> --to <target> --output plan.json`
- Review plan for:
  - Artifact list completeness (images/charts/migrations)
  - Stage ordering: control plane completes before data plane rollouts
  - Defined rollback entry points and post-rollback verification steps
- Store artifacts:
  - Attach `plan.json` and human-readable summary to the change record
sections.heading: 2) Generate and review the upgrade plan (required)

sections.body:
- Execute:
  - `redwood-private upgrade precheck --plan plan.json --output precheck-report.json`
- Attach the report to the change record.
sections.heading: 3) Run prechecks (required)

sections.body:
(See full spec for details; below is the policy baseline.)
- **Kubernetes health**: all nodes Ready; no critical system pods CrashLoopBackOff; API server reachable
- **Control-plane connectivity**: installer can reach control-plane endpoints (or local on-prem endpoints)
- **RBAC/auth**: service accounts and cluster roles present; OIDC/SSO reachability validated when configured
- **Storage headroom**:
  - Persistent volumes used by databases/stateful components have ≥20% free space AND ≥10 GiB free (whichever is larger)
  - Snapshot target has sufficient space (backend-specific)
- **DB connectivity + privileges**: migration user can acquire required locks; bounded lock timeout configured
- **Version compatibility**: policy evaluation confirms supported path (default: N-1 → N)
- **Artifact availability**:
  - Online: registry/chart repo reachable
  - Offline: bundle present and checksum/signature verified
- **TLS/DNS**: certificates not expiring within 14 days; required SANs present; DNS resolution passes for internal endpoints
sections.heading: Blocking prechecks (must pass)

sections.body:
- Non-critical capacity warnings (e.g., <30% cluster headroom)
- Optional integrations temporarily unreachable (e.g., SIEM forwarder, non-blocking webhooks)
- Non-default configuration drift detected (requires “acknowledge + document”)
sections.heading: Warning prechecks (must be acknowledged)

sections.body:
- Backup must complete successfully **before** executing any irreversible step (e.g., non-backward-compatible migration).
- Execute via installer:
  - `redwood-private backup run --plan plan.json --output backup-report.json`
- Backup requirements:
  - Encryption enabled (KMS/HSM where applicable)
  - Restore procedure documented and available to operators
  - Retention: minimum 7 days for standard; 30 days for regulated unless customer policy requires longer
- Attach `backup-report.json` and backup location metadata to the change record.
sections.heading: 4) Backup and restore readiness (required)

sections.body:
Approvals required before “apply” begins:
- **Release Engineering approval** (required):
  - Confirms artifacts match release manifest
  - Confirms CI baseline met
  - Confirms offline/air-gapped bundle verification (if applicable)
- **SRE approval** (required):
  - Confirms prechecks are clean (or acceptable warnings are acknowledged)
  - Confirms monitoring/alerts in place for the window
  - Confirms rollback path is viable and documented
- **Security/Compliance approval** (conditional):
  - Required for High risk tier
  - Required for changes to audit events, backup handling, encryption defaults, or secret material

Approval must be recorded in the change record with approver name + timestamp.
sections.heading: 5) Approval gates (required)

sections.body: Communications requirements depend on risk tier.
sections.heading: 6) Communications (required)

sections.body:
- Post to `#eng-releases` and `#eng-oncall` at least:
  - T-24h for Medium/High
  - T-2h for Low
- Include: customer/site, window, versions, on-call lead, rollback trigger criteria, links to change record.
sections.heading: Internal comms (all tiers)

sections.body:
- **Low**: notify customer contact at least **48 hours** prior (or per contract), confirm window.
- **Medium**: notify **5 business days** prior; include expected operator actions and verification checklist.
- **High**: notify **10 business days** prior; schedule readiness call; confirm evidence expectations (audit logs, backup proof, rollback plan).

##### Customer email template (copy/paste)
Subject: Redwood Private maintenance window: upgrade to <VERSION>

Hello <Customer Team>,

We are planning a maintenance window to upgrade your Redwood Private deployment from <CURRENT_VERSION> to <TARGET_VERSION>.

- Proposed window: <DATE/TIME> (<TIMEZONE>)
- Expected impact: <e.g., control plane restart; inference data plane unaffected / short rolling restarts>
- Preconditions: We will run preflight checks (cluster health, storage capacity, connectivity) and take a backup prior to any migration.
- Rollback: If we detect upgrade failure conditions (see below), we will initiate a rollback to <CURRENT_VERSION> and validate service health.
sections.heading: Customer comms

sections.body:
- Control plane healthy and responding
- Data plane readiness checks passing
- Upgrade audit events present for compliance logging (if applicable)
sections.heading: Success criteria

sections.body:
- Persistent elevated error rate in control plane beyond <THRESHOLD> for > <DURATION>
- Migration step exceeds safe timeout or fails idempotency checks
- Readiness gates fail for > <DURATION>

Please reply with confirmation of the window and any change-control requirements we should align to.

Thank you,
<Redwood Contact>
sections.heading: Rollback trigger criteria (examples)

sections.body:
- Start upgrade:
  - `redwood-private upgrade apply --plan plan.json --state-dir <path> --output upgrade-report.json`
- Requirements during execution:
  - Operator follows plan ordering; no manual step skipping without SRE approval
  - Health checks after each stage (control plane, then data plane)
  - If any blocking invariant fails, pause and escalate (see “Stop conditions”)
sections.heading: 7) Execute upgrade (during window)

sections.body:
Stop and escalate to SRE + Release Engineering if any occur:
- Control plane unavailable >10 minutes without clear forward progress
- Migration step exceeds declared plan timeout or reports lock contention beyond thresholds
- Repeated crash loops for upgrade jobs/hooks
- Artifact mismatch detected (digest differs from manifest)
- Unexpected data plane impact (elevated inference errors) during upgrade window
sections.heading: 8) Stop conditions and escalation

sections.body:
- Page SRE on-call (Private)
- Notify Release Engineering in `#eng-releases`
- Update customer status if Medium/High tier
sections.heading: Escalation

sections.body:
Rollback must be treated as an operational procedure with equivalent rigor.
- Invoke rollback only using supported tooling:
  - `redwood-private upgrade rollback --state-dir <path> --output rollback-report.json`
- Rollback requirements:
  - Uses stored upgrade state to ensure deterministic step reversal
  - Executes rollback hooks in defined order
  - Verifies post-rollback health checks (control plane + data plane)
- Attach rollback report and final status to the change record.
sections.heading: 9) Rollback policy (when invoked)

sections.body:
For every customer upgrade event, the following must be retained and attachable for support/compliance:
- Upgrade plan (`plan.json`) + human summary
- Precheck report (`precheck-report.json`)
- Backup report (`backup-report.json`) + backup identifiers
- Upgrade execution report (`upgrade-report.json`) and/or state machine logs
- Rollback report if used (`rollback-report.json`)
- Installer logs (sanitized) and referenced artifact manifests
- Audit log events for: upgrade started, prechecks pass/fail, backup completed, upgrade completed/failed, rollback invoked/completed
sections.heading: Auditability and evidence retention

sections.body:
- Default: 30 days internal retention for upgrade artifacts
- Regulated customers: align to contract; if unspecified, 90 days recommended
sections.heading: Retention guidance

sections.body:
- Update change record with final status, duration, and any deviations
- If any incident occurred (customer-visible impact or rollback), file an incident and link it
- Record “lessons learned” and precheck gaps for backlog triage
sections.heading: Within 2 business days of completion

sections.body:
Exceptions are allowed only when documented and approved.
- Who can approve exceptions:
  - Release Engineering lead + SRE lead (both required)
  - Security/Compliance additionally required for regulated/high-tier customers
- Valid exception examples:
  - Emergency security patch where full comms timeline is not possible
  - Customer-mandated window with reduced lead time
  - Temporary CI gap with compensating controls (e.g., dedicated staging rehearsal)
sections.heading: Exceptions

sections.body:
- Which gate is being bypassed
- Why it is safe to proceed
- Compensating controls
- Rollback plan and stop conditions
sections.heading: Exception request must include

sections.body:
- [ ] Risk score + tier recorded
- [ ] Upgrade plan generated and attached
- [ ] Blocking prechecks passed; warnings acknowledged
- [ ] Backup completed; restore path documented
- [ ] Approvals captured (RelEng + SRE; Security if required)
- [ ] Customer notified per tier
- [ ] On-call coverage confirmed
- [ ] Upgrade executed with stage verification
- [ ] Rollback readiness confirmed; rollback executed if needed
- [ ] Artifacts retained; support bundle includes upgrade traces
sections.heading: Appendix A: Change record checklist (operator-facing)

sections.body:
Channel: #eng-releases (cc #eng-oncall)

Private upgrade scheduled
- Customer/site: <NAME> (<VPC/ON-PREM>)
- Window: <START–END> <TZ>
- Version: <CURRENT> → <TARGET>
- Risk tier: <LOW/MED/HIGH> (score: <n>)
- On-call lead: <NAME>
- Plan + prechecks: <LINK>
- Rollback trigger criteria: <BULLETS>
sections.heading: Appendix B: Internal Slack announcement template

sections.body:
- Policy owner: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien)
- Operational owner: SRE (Sean Gallagher)
- Next review date: 2025-09-30 (or sooner if we have a P0/P1 upgrade incident)

payload.page_title: Production Change Management Policy

sections.body:
This policy defines the minimum process and approvals required for production changes at Redwood Inference. The objective is to reduce customer impact from planned changes and ensure we capture sufficient evidence, rollback planning, and communications.

This applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments (including customer-managed clusters).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- *Change record*: the system-of-record ticket for the change (Jira for support/operations changes, Linear for engineering work, with a Jira change record if customer production is affected).
- *Risk level*: Low/Medium/High/Critical based on blast radius and reversibility.
- *Go/No-Go gate*: explicit confirmation at start of window that prerequisites are met.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1. Change record with scope, owner, and timeline.
2. Rollback plan (time-to-rollback estimate required).
3. Monitoring plan (what signals are watched, by whom).
4. Customer communications plan if there is customer-visible impact or a maintenance window.
5. Evidence attached: preflight outputs, screenshots/links to dashboards, relevant test results, and approvals.
sections.heading: Required elements for every production change

sections.body: Examples: documentation-only, internal tool changes without customer impact.
sections.heading: Low

sections.body: Examples: changes behind a feature flag; reversible config changes; single-tenant changes with fast rollback.
sections.heading: Medium

sections.body: Examples: multi-component changes; schema migrations; upgrades to customer production Private clusters; changes to auth/RBAC; changes requiring coordinated downtime.
sections.heading: High

sections.body: Examples: irreversible changes; upgrades during peak traffic; changes during active incident; changes that affect multiple enterprise customers simultaneously.
sections.heading: Critical

sections.body: - Engineering peer approval OR team lead approval.
sections.heading: Low

sections.body:
- Owning team lead
- On-call/SRE notified
sections.heading: Medium

sections.body:
- Owning team lead
- SRE approver (named individual)
- Customer Success approver if customer-facing
- Security approver if security triggers are met
sections.heading: High

sections.body:
- Director-level engineering approver
- SRE approver
- Security & Compliance approver
- Customer Success approver
sections.heading: Critical

sections.body:
Security sign-off is required when the change affects any of the following for a customer production environment:
- Authentication, SSO, token validation, signing keys, or session handling
- RBAC policy defaults, permission boundaries, or privileged service accounts
- TLS configuration, certificate automation, or trust stores
- Audit logging pipeline, retention, or integrity controls
- Introduction of new third-party dependencies/images
- Network boundaries (ingress/egress controls)
sections.heading: Security triggers (require Security & Compliance sign-off)

sections.body:
- Alters scaling behavior, autoscaling policy, or load shedding
- Changes core request routing, fallback policies, or region-level capacity
- Modifies alerting/monitoring or disables alerts for a window
- Has any planned downtime or performance regression risk
sections.heading: SRE review is required when the change

sections.body:
If the change is customer-visible (maintenance window, risk of degraded service, or known downtime), the change record must include:
- Customer notification timing and channel
- Internal comms plan (who is on bridge, where to post updates)
- An all-clear message plan
sections.heading: Communications requirements

sections.body:
For High/Critical changes, the Change Owner must explicitly record a GO/NO-GO decision at window start including:
- Confirmation approvals are complete
- Confirmation rollback is ready
- Confirmation monitoring is in place
- Confirmation customer comms are sent and acknowledged where applicable
sections.heading: Go/No-Go gate requirement

sections.body: Exceptions (including change freeze overrides) require explicit approval and must be linked from the change record.
sections.heading: Exceptions

payload.page_title: Respond, Recover, Review: Incident Playbook and Game Day Syllabus

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes a single, opinionated lifecycle for incidents at Redwood: Respond → Recover → Review. It consolidates triage ladders, step-by-step containment and recovery runbooks, a postmortem template, on-call rotation rules, and a reproducible game day syllabus for team readiness. Use this as the canonical operational path for any incident affecting customer-facing inference services or control plane components.

Scope
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private control plane services.
- Excludes non-prod test environments (see team wiki for staging incident guidance).

Quick definitions
- Incident: any event causing customer-visible degradation, increased error rates, latency SLO breaches, or data integrity issues.
- Major incident: multi-region outage, sustained latency SLO violations >30m, or data loss.
- Bridge: primary coordination channel (Slack #inc-bridge by default).

Roles & ownership
1) Incident Commander (IC): owns triage decisions, public comms, and rollback choices. Usually senior SRE or on-call service owner.
2) Bridge Operator: runs the bridge, collects evidence, and creates updates. Typically the on-call SRE.
3) Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): runtime, networking, database, billing, security.
4) Customer Liaison: customer-success engineer for customer-impacted incidents.
5) Postmortem Author: the person who documents the timeline and actions within 72 hours.

Triage decision ladder (first 15 minutes)
1) Detect: alert fires or customer report.
2) Acknowledge: on-call sets initial status in the bridge within 5 minutes.
3) Classify: apply the impact matrix (below) and decide major vs minor.
4) IC assignment: if major, escalate to IC immediately; if minor, on-call handles.
5) Stabilize: execute containment runbook snippets.

Impact matrix (short)
| Customer Impact | Traffic impact | SLO impact | Classification |
|-----------------|----------------|------------|----------------|
| Single customer, degraded responses | <1% traffic | None/very small | P2 |
| Multiple customers, increased latency | 1-10% traffic | SLO at risk | P1 |
| Widespread errors or region down | >10% | SLO breach | Major/P0 |

Immediate containment runbook (first 30 minutes)
1) Put a short-status placeholder: "Investigation underway; initial mitigation in progress."
2) Turn off automated scaling/burst if it's causing churn (CLI: redwood infra scale --service <svc> --mode paused).
3) Apply quick-filters: route new traffic to fallback model variant or healthy region per routing policy. Example: set routing policy via console -> Traffic -> Fallback: small-model-v1.
4) If CPU/GPU exhaustion: evict long-running jobs and enable preemptible fallback pools. Command sample: kubectl cordon <node> && redwood node-drain --evict-long-kv --force.
5) If memory leakage suspected: restart the service with crash-loop protection removed: systemctl restart redwood-runtime-<svc> or k roll restart <deployment>.

Evidence & data collection checklist
- Timestamped alert bindings (incident open time)
- Grafana dashboards: latency-by-route, token-throughput, GPU-utilization, queue-depth
- Recent deployments and rollouts (git commit hashes, canary IDs)
- Error traces and most frequent exceptions
- Customer reports and sample request IDs

Mitigation -> Recovery (30m–4h)
1) Confirm root cause hypothesis with focused tests (run replay on canary).
2) If workaround available (e.g., rollback to previous build or pin to non-quantized model), implement with a canary and 10% traffic test.
3) Monitor for regression for at least two SLO windows (typical windows: 1m/5m/1h depending on metric).
4) If fix is code-level, create a hotfix branch, CI run, and deploy via canary. Tag changelog with incident ID.
5) When stable for recovery SLOs, prepare rollback of temporary mitigations.

Communication templates
- Internal bridge update (concise):
  [HH:MM UTC] STATUS: Investigating | IMPACT: region us-west high latency | ACTION: routing fallback enabled to us-east | OWNER: @oncall-sre | NEXT: 15m update

- Customer status (public/private):
  Subject: Incident [INC-<id>] - Latency degradation affecting inference API

  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We're actively investigating an issue causing increased latency for text-generation requests in us-west. Our on-call team has enabled automatic routing to alternate regions and a fallback model to reduce impact. We will provide the next update by <ETA 15m>.

  What we're doing: diverting traffic, monitoring failover, validating results.
  What you can expect: service restored for most requests within 30-60 minutes; a follow-up report will be sent when the cause is identified.

  Incident ID: INC-<id>

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Operations

- Status page template (short):
  Title: Partial outage: inference API (us-west)
  Impact: Increased latency; some requests may time out
  Update: Investigating; fallback routing applied
  Next update: in 15 minutes

Postmortem template (to publish within 72 hours)
1) Title: Postmortem - INC-<id> - one-line summary
2) Severity: P0/P1/P2
3) Date opened / closed / duration
4) Services affected and customer impact (list customers if high impact)
5) Timeline (table of events with HH:MM UTC, actor, action, outcome)
6) Root cause analysis (clear technical narrative)
7) Mitigations implemented during incident (short-term)
8) Permanent remediation and owners (action, target date)
9) Detection gaps and monitoring improvements
10) Communication review (what worked, what didn't)
11) Follow-ups and acceptance criteria for closure
12) Links to evidence (dashboards, logs, commits)

On-call rotation & handoff rules
- Shift length: 1 week primary (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC) for SREs; 4-week rotation for on-call leads.
- Swap policy: swaps must be posted to #oncall-swaps and acknowledged by the replacing engineer at least 24 hours prior.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled in Slack or Handoff doc):
  - Current active incidents (IDs and short status)
  - Outstanding action items with owners
  - Known risky changes scheduled in next 24h (deploys, infra changes)
  - Personal contact preference and escalation path

Game day syllabus (90–120 minutes; bi-quarterly)
Purpose: exercise the full Respond→Recover→Review flow under controlled conditions. Rotate inject owners across teams.

1) Pre-work (30m):
   - 5m brief: objectives and scale of injected failure
   - 10m runbook review: triage ladder & containment runbook reviewed by IC
   - 15m environment prep: pre-populated incidents, synthetic traffic, and test telemetry enabled

2) Active exercise (45–60m):
   - Inject: simulate throttling of control-plane API + region CPU spike
   - Observe: on-call detects via alert and opens bridge (goal: <5m)
   - Respond: assign IC, run containment steps, and roll fallback routing
   - Recover: perform targeted rollback or config change; validate with synthetic transactions

3) Debrief and scoring (20–30m):
   - Runbook adherence (0-10): extent to which steps were followed
   - Communication clarity (0-10): clarity and cadence of updates
   - Time-to-detect, time-to-ack, and time-to-recover metrics captured
   - Improvement actions captured as JIRA tickets tagged game-day/<date>

Game day evaluation rubric (examples)
- Detection (0-5): alert fired and was noticed within 5m (5pts).
- Role clarity (0-5): IC and bridge operator were assigned within 3m (5pts).
- Containment effectiveness (0-10): mitigation reduced customer error rate by >75% in one SLO window (10pts).
- Recovery correctness (0-10): rollback or patch restored service without data loss (10pts).
- Communication (0-5): internal and customer message templates used correctly (5pts).

Runbook governance & change control
- Owners: every runbook must list a primary owner and at least one reviewer.
- Review cadence: owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any relevant production change.
- Versioning: runbook edits must include changelog entry and incident tags when used in a real event.

Operational dashboards & useful queries
- Main dashboards: Service Overview, Latency by Route, Model Token Cost, GPU Utilization, Queue Depth.
- Useful queries (examples):
  - Top error types: SELECT error, count(*) FROM logs WHERE service='inference' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY error LIMIT 20
  - 95th latency by route: grafana/latency?panel=95p-by-route

Appendix: SLOs and escalation thresholds
| Service | SLO (p95) | Warning threshold | Escalation threshold |
|---------|----------:|------------------:|---------------------:|
| Text-generation API | 200ms | 120% of SLO for 10m | 150% of SLO for 5m |
| Embeddings API | 150ms | 120% for 10m | 150% for 5m |
| Control plane API | 100ms | 120% for 10m | 150% for 3m |

Escalation matrix (summary)
- P2: notify team slack + on-call (no IC)
- P1: IC assigned, bridge opened, customer liaison notified
- P0 (major): Exec notif (paging), incident war room, external status page update every 15m

Document maintenance
- Owner: Asha Patel (eng-sre)
- Review cycle: annual mandatory review; otherwise update after any game day or major incident.

Related resources
- See also: incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024, incident-metrics-and-evidence-collection-standard-2025
- Templates folder: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/templates

Last reviewed: 2025-02-20 by Diego Martinez
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: PLG Signal Data Handling and Retention Policy

sections.body:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s data handling, privacy safeguards, access controls, and retention standards for the **PLG-to-sales signal routing** project.

The goal of the PLG signal pipeline is to surface *account-level* indicators that a self-serve customer may benefit from sales-assisted upgrades (Dedicated/Private) while minimizing data collection, reducing spam/false positives, and meeting Redwood’s privacy and compliance obligations.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Data collected and processed to generate **PLG Signals** (threshold + intent signals).
- Storage and access of signal artifacts in analytics datasets and HubSpot.
- Retention, deletion, and audit requirements for this pipeline.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- General product telemetry retention policies not specific to PLG signals.
- Customer content processing policies for model inputs/outputs (handled by separate product and security policies).
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
The PLG signal pipeline processes **customer-sensitive operational data**.
- Default classification for signal datasets and payloads: **Restricted (customer-sensitive)**.
- HubSpot records created/updated by this pipeline are also treated as **Restricted**, due to commercial sensitivity and potential contact association.
sections.heading: Data classification

sections.body:
1. **Account-level by default:** signals are generated at org/account (and optionally workspace) level, not tied to named end users.
2. **Data minimization:** only capture the minimum fields needed to detect a signal and route ownership.
3. **No customer content:** do not store prompts, completions, embeddings, file contents, or payload samples as part of the signal pipeline.
4. **Aggregations over raw events:** route aggregated counts/rates and short reason strings instead of raw event streams.
5. **Separation of duties:** only a small set of roles can access restricted analytics tables; sales users see only what is needed to act.
6. **Retention with purpose:** keep raw data only long enough to score signals and audit pipeline correctness.
sections.heading: Design principles (must-haves)

sections.body: PLG signals are computed from product and web telemetry, aggregated into daily/weekly windows.
sections.heading: What data is used for PLG signals

sections.body:
**Account identifiers**
- Redwood internal identifiers: org_id, workspace_id
- Account metadata: plan_tier (trial/free/paid), region, billing_customer_id (internal key only)

**Usage aggregates (non-PII, account-level)**
- Tokens: tokens_in, tokens_out (daily/weekly totals)
- Requests: request_count, streaming_request_count
- Spend: spend_usd (daily/weekly), spend_velocity (week-over-week change)
- Reliability: 429_count, 5xx_count, timeout_count, error_rate
- Performance aggregates: p50/p95 latency buckets (no request payloads)
- Quota/limit indicators: quota_exhausted_events count

**Account expansion aggregates**
- workspace_count, new_workspace_count (windowed)
- org_member_invite_count (aggregate count)

**Intent signals (web/docs/product interactions) — aggregated**
- Page/view events aggregated by page category (e.g., “Dedicated docs”, “Private/VPC docs”, “Security FAQ”, “Pricing page”)
- Download or request events for security artifacts (e.g., SOC2 request initiated) aggregated as a boolean/count

**Routing/support context**
- Existing CRM owner ids (if present)
- Existing customer flag (to coordinate CS vs Sales)
- Suppression flags (e.g., recently contacted, do-not-contact)
sections.heading: Allowed data elements (approved)

sections.body:
Do **not** collect, store, or route the following in PLG signal datasets or into HubSpot via this pipeline:
- Prompt text, completion text, embeddings vectors, uploaded files, tool/function call arguments, or any customer content.
- API keys, access tokens, refresh tokens, signing secrets.
- Full IP addresses or precise device fingerprints.
- Raw user identifiers (email, full name) originating from product telemetry.
- Fine-grained event trails that reveal individual user behavior (e.g., “User X viewed page Y at timestamp Z”).
- Freeform notes that include sensitive customer data (health, payment card data, credentials, etc.).

Exception handling: If a new signal proposal requires a prohibited element, it is blocked by default and must go through a documented privacy review and explicit Security + Legal approval (see “Security sign-off checkpoints”).
sections.heading: Prohibited data elements (not allowed)

sections.body:
1. **Telemetry / analytics warehouse**
   - Stores aggregated usage + intent inputs and computed signal outputs.
   - Signal outputs are maintained as a dedicated dataset/table family for auditability and backfills.

2. **Signal scoring and routing service**
   - Processes aggregates, computes score/qualification, and sends minimal payloads to HubSpot.
   - Must be stateless beyond short-lived queues and retry buffers.

3. **HubSpot**
   - Stores a small set of company-level properties representing: latest signal type, score, timestamps, and recommended next action.
   - Creates timeline notes and tasks that reference signal types and aggregates.
sections.heading: Where data is stored (systems of record)

sections.body:
- Prefer **company-level** properties (Company object) for signals.
- Do not create new Contacts from telemetry.
- If a Contact already exists (e.g., self-serve signup contact), tasks may be associated to the company and optionally the existing primary contact, but the signal payload must remain account-level.
sections.heading: When routing to HubSpot

sections.body:
- plg_signal_latest_type (enum)
- plg_signal_latest_score (numeric)
- plg_signal_latest_window (e.g., “7d”, “30d”)
- plg_signal_latest_summary (short controlled string, e.g., “Sustained 429s + spend velocity”)
- plg_signal_latest_detected_at (timestamp)
- plg_signal_suppressed_until (timestamp)
sections.heading: Approved HubSpot fields (examples)

sections.body:
- Use templated text.
- Include only **aggregated metrics** (e.g., “429s in last 7d: 54”, “spend WoW: +62%”).
- Avoid referencing any individual user’s activity (e.g., “Alice looked at the security page”).
sections.heading: Notes/tasks should

sections.body: Retention is defined for (a) raw-ish input event tables, (b) aggregated inputs, (c) signal outputs, and (d) HubSpot artifacts.
sections.heading: Retention policy

sections.body:
**A) Web/docs intent events (raw event logs): 90 days**
- Purpose: support scoring, debug attribution, and resolve false positive reports.
- After 90 days, raw event logs must be deleted or transformed into non-identifying aggregates.

**B) Product usage telemetry used for scoring (raw operational logs): 90 days**
- Purpose: recompute signals for short backfills and validate pipeline.
- Note: separate platform logging policies may retain operational logs longer; PLG signal datasets must not extend this retention by copying raw logs.

**C) Aggregated inputs (daily/weekly rollups): 18 months**
- Purpose: trend analysis, model/threshold tuning, and auditability.
- Aggregation must not include prohibited fields.

**D) PLG Signal outputs in analytics (qualified + unqualified scored records): 18 months**
- Purpose: conversion attribution, suppression logic, and audit.
- Records should be keyed by org/account id and signal_type + window_start.

**E) HubSpot company properties: while account is active; review at 24 months inactivity**
- Purpose: sales execution.
- Inactivity review: if an account is inactive for 24 months (no product usage and no active sales process), RevOps should purge PLG signal properties and timeline notes created by this pipeline.

**F) HubSpot tasks created by this pipeline: follow HubSpot standard task retention; close-out required within 30 days**
- Sales/CS process requirement (not a deletion requirement): tasks must be completed/closed or explicitly snoozed with a reason to reduce clutter.
sections.heading: Standard retention periods

sections.body:
- Raw web/docs events: 90 days
- Raw usage telemetry copied into PLG datasets: not allowed (use aggregates)
- Aggregated inputs: 18 months
- Signal outputs: 18 months
- HubSpot properties/notes: active lifecycle; purge review after 24 months inactivity
sections.heading: Retention table (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Read access limited to:
  - Telemetry & Analytics Engineering (e.g., Logan Wright’s team, named analysts)
  - Security/Compliance reviewers as needed for audit
  - RevOps/Business Systems for troubleshooting (time-bound)
- Access mechanism:
  - Role-based access control (RBAC) with least privilege
  - Quarterly access review by Security + Data/Analytics owner
sections.heading: Analytics datasets (restricted)

sections.body:
- HubSpot access is governed by Sales Ops and Security controls.
- PLG signal properties are visible to Sales/CS roles that need to act.
- Any export of HubSpot data for analysis must follow restricted data handling standards and approved destinations.
sections.heading: HubSpot access

sections.body:
- HubSpot integration uses OAuth with the minimal required scopes.
- Tokens and client secrets must be stored in the approved secrets manager (no plaintext in code, CI logs, or dashboards).
- Rotation:
  - OAuth refresh tokens: rotate at least every 180 days or upon incident
  - Secrets: rotate within 7 days after any suspected exposure
sections.heading: Service accounts and secrets

sections.body: The pipeline must maintain sufficient auditability without collecting sensitive customer content.
sections.heading: Logging, monitoring, and auditability

sections.body:
- Structured logs for routing actions (created/updated company, created task, suppressed) keyed by internal org_id and HubSpot company id.
- Log redaction for any accidental payload inclusion.
- Metrics and alerts for:
  - HubSpot 429/5xx rates
  - Dropped/failed updates
  - Event lag and backlog
  - Task creation volume (to detect spam regressions)
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body: - Router service operational logs: 30 days (unless security incident requires longer retention under incident response procedures).
sections.heading: Audit retention for system logs

sections.body:
- Customer request to delete PLG signal artifacts (e.g., contract requirement)
- GDPR/CCPA data subject request (DSAR) for personal data
- Correction request for inaccurate account metadata impacting routing
sections.heading: Supported request types

sections.body:
1. **Intake**
   - Requests must be routed to Security/Privacy via the standard channel (Legal/Privacy queue) and assigned an owner.
   - Record: requester, organization, scope (analytics, HubSpot, both), deadline.

2. **Identify identifiers**
   - Use internal org_id and known CRM identifiers.
   - Do not rely on end-user emails from telemetry (not collected by design).

3. **Delete from analytics**
   - Delete PLG signal outputs for the org_id (all windows) within 30 days unless contract specifies shorter.
   - Delete aggregated input rows if they are uniquely tied to the org_id.
   - Ensure derived tables/materializations are also purged.

4. **Delete from HubSpot**
   - Clear PLG signal properties on the Company object.
   - Remove timeline notes created by the pipeline where feasible.
   - Close associated tasks with a neutral internal reason (e.g., “Data deletion request processed”).

5. **Verification and audit record**
   - Provide an internal completion note including timestamps and tables/objects affected.
   - Retain only the minimum audit evidence required (no customer content).
sections.heading: How to process deletion requests (procedure)

sections.body:
If a customer reports incorrect signal-driven outreach (false positives):
- Apply suppression immediately if needed.
- Investigate using aggregated records and pipeline logs.
- If the issue is caused by misattribution (e.g., mismapped domain), correct mapping and backfill.
sections.heading: Corrections

sections.body:
1. Adding any new input data field to the signal schema.
2. Adding any new intent source (docs instrumentation, marketing site tracking changes).
3. Changing retention durations.
4. Changing what is written into HubSpot (new properties, freeform text, new associations).
sections.heading: Security/Privacy approval is required for

sections.body:
- Update the relevant ADR/schema doc and open a review in #eng-security.
- Security reviewer (Marcus Lin or delegate) validates prohibited-data compliance.
- Privacy approver (Dr. Aisha Rahman) signs off on minimization + retention.
- Legal (Michael Grant) consulted for policy/contract changes, DSAR obligations, or new tracking categories.
- Compliance (Olga Petrov) consulted when changes impact SOC2 evidence expectations.
sections.heading: Approval steps

sections.body:
- Any pipeline change that violates “Prohibited data elements” is a release blocker.
- Exceptions must be documented with:
  - Business rationale
  - Alternative options considered
  - Compensating controls
  - Explicit written approval from Security + Legal
sections.heading: Enforcement and exceptions

sections.body:
Owner: Security & Compliance (primary), with shared operational ownership by Telemetry & Analytics.
- Review cadence: every 6 months, or immediately after a privacy incident, customer complaint, or material change to intent sources.
sections.heading: Owner and review cadence

sections.body:
- Security/Privacy approvals: Dr. Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin
- Analytics pipeline owner: Logan Wright
- HubSpot/business systems owner: David Kim
- Sales Ops (routing/ownership): Isabelle Laurent
