sections.body:
Overview

This page documents a recurring cross-team on‑call skill sprint combined with a curated scenario library and associated artifacts (runbook checklists, postmortem template, rotation guidance, game‑day scoring, and status/customer comm templates). The intent is to reduce bus factor, improve triage speed for LLM serving incidents, and surface gaps proactively through structured practice.

Use this as the canonical playbook for running 1-week oncall skill sprints and for running game‑day simulations that reflect production failure modes.

Goals
- Decrease mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR) for common serving incidents by 25% over 6 months.
- Ensure at least two engineers per service have runbook-level competency.
- Discover missing runbook steps, telemetry gaps, and permission blockers.
- Create reusable customer‑safe status templates and evidence artifacts for postmortems.

Scope
- Applies to: runtime, autoscaling, KV cache, routing, quantization and model-quality degradations, rate-limiting, and multi-tenant isolation incidents.
- Excludes: infrastructure-level cloud provider maintenance (see cloud-accounts playbook) and data-breach/legal escalations (see security-and-compliance).

Who should run this
- Program owner: Oncall Enablement (eng-sre).
- Facilitator: SRE engineer assigned to that sprint.
- Participants: Engineers from serving-runtime, infra, platform, and customer-success on rotation.

High-level cadence
- Sprint frequency: monthly cross-team sprint (one team rotates to facilitate per month).
- Sprint duration: 5 business days (Monday onboarding -> Friday retro + evidence deliverables).
- Game-day: optional Saturday simulation (2–4 hours) for high-stakes scenarios.

Roles & responsibilities
- Sprint owner: schedule, invite participants, reserve sandbox, publish objectives.
- Facilitator: coordinate scenarios, ensure safe environment, perform runbook invocations.
- Service steward: primary on-call owner for scenario subject matter expertise and acceptance criteria.
- Observer / Scorer: captures metrics, timelines, and runs scoring sheet.

Rotation model (example)
- Each team contributes 2 engineers per sprint. Swaps are scheduled at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Pairing matrix (example):
  - Week 1: Serving Runtime (owner) + Platform (partner)
  - Week 2: Infra (owner) + Customer Success (partner)
- Handoff signoffs recorded in Slack channel #oncall-sprints and attached to this page.

Sprint process (detailed)
1) Pre-sprint (T minus 5 days):
   - Sprint owner publishes objectives and recommended reading (relevant runbooks, dashboards, previous postmortems).
   - Participants confirm sandbox access and role assignments.
   - Facilitator provisions a non-prod tenant that mirrors production telemetry (traffic shape + KV cache).
2) Day 1 — Onboarding & priming:
   - 60–90 minute kickoff: architecture review, SLOs, and threat model for chosen scenario.
   - Quick tour of alerting playbooks, dashboards, and incident command flow.
3) Days 2–3 — Shadow & paired triage:
   - Participants shadow a simulated pager (rotating primary).
   - Perform triage steps using runbook; toggles made only in sandbox.
   - Observers capture timestamps for MTTA/MTTR and decision points.
4) Day 4 — Independent run & evidence capture:
   - Participants run scenario without facilitator coaching.
   - Each run produces: timeline, key findings, telemetry gaps, suggested runbook edits.
5) Day 5 — Retro, action items, and postmortem draft:
   - Facilitated retro (30–45m) with scoring sheet review.
   - Owner creates postmortem draft and ownership for action items.

Scenario Library (select entries)
- Scenario: KV cache eviction cascade\  Severity: Sev 2\  Trigger: Sudden full-node restart + cache warmup miss rate > 85%\  Expected impact: Increased latency on generation requests, SLO degradation within 10 minutes\  Key runbook: runtime/kv-cache-eviction-checklist\  Game-day script (short):
  1. Inject node restart in sandbox cluster.
  2. Flood traffic with long-context requests to exercise kv miss behavior.
  3. Observe latency, evictions per node, and autoscaling decisions.\  4. Mitigation steps: route traffic to warm pools, trigger KV warmup job, scale compute, and enable progressive throttling.

- Scenario: Autoscaler oscillation under burst traffic\  Severity: Sev 2\  Trigger: synthetic spike followed by rapid drop causing flapping between scale actions\  Expected impact: Throttled requests, increased CPU load, burst billing risk\  Key runbook: infra/autoscaler-flap-mitigation\  Game-day script: trigger programmed traffic spike, verify rollback cool-down settings, validate autoscaler metrics and guardrails.

- Scenario: Model-quality regression (inference artifacts)\  Severity: Sev 1 (customer visible quality regression)\  Trigger: New model rollout without canary due to mislabelled tag\  Expected impact: Incorrect outputs, user-visible failures, potential SLA impact\  Key runbook: product/model-rollout-emergency-rollback\  Game-day script: simulate a canary failure, execute rollback path, validate both quality metrics and customer comms.

Runbook checklist (template)
- Title: [service] — short description
- Pager summary: one-sentence symptom and immediate impact
- Initial triage (1–5 min):
  - Check alerts and incident signals (pager, dashboard, logs).
  - Identify affected regions/tenants.
  - Capture initial MTTA timestamp.
- Containment (5–30 min):
  - Route traffic to fallback model/region if available.
  - Enable basic rate-limits or circuit-breakers.\  - Record actions in incident log.
- Mitigation (30–180 min):
  - Apply temporary config change or rollback.
  - Scale resources or trigger warmups.
  - Validate error rate and latency metrics.
- Recovery & verification (post mitigation):
  - Confirm SLOs returning to normal for at least 30 minutes.
  - Run smoke tests against customer-facing endpoints.
- Closure & evidence (within 24 hours):
  - Publish timeline, artifacts, and preliminary postmortem draft.
  - Assign action items and owners.

Postmortem template (required fields)
- Title
- Date and incident ID
- Severity classification (and why)
- Summary (one paragraph)
- Timeline (table-like plaintext with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (clear 3-level decomposition)
- Corrective actions (owner, ETA, verification)
- Preventative actions (owner, ETA)
- Customer impact summary and credits (if any)
- Evidence artifacts: links to logs, dashboards, incident channel transcript
- Approval and publish status

On‑call handoff checklist
- Confirm active alerts are captured and assigned.
- Share recent deploys and config changes.
- Hand over any in-progress action items and owners.
- Validate that runbook links are accessible to the incoming oncall.
- Confirm staging/production credentials and sandbox links.

Operational thresholds & SLOs (examples)
- Generation latency (p95) target: 250ms (SLO), 500ms (SLO burn threshold).
- Error rate (5xx) SLO: <= 0.2% per minute; alert at 0.5% sustained 10m.
- Model-quality drift: human-eval failure rate increase > 5% triggers incident review.
- KV miss rate: alert at > 15% sustained for 5 minutes.

Status page & customer comm templates
- Major outage (initial public message):
  - Title: Major degradation affecting text generation in US region\  - Body: We are aware of an issue affecting text generation in the US region impacting some customers. Our engineering team is investigating. We will post updates every 30 minutes. (Avoid technical root cause until verified.)
- Customer update (progress):
  - Title: Update — mitigation in progress\  - Body: We have identified increased KV miss rates causing latency and are routing traffic to warm pools while scaling capacity. Estimated timeframe: 30–90 minutes. Next update: [time].
- Resolution message:
  - Title: Issue resolved — text generation restored\  - Body: The underlying issue was a cache warmup regression after a node restart. Traffic has been routed and latency metrics are stable. Full postmortem forthcoming.

Game‑day playbook and scoring
- Objectives: validate runbook completeness, telemetry coverage, permissions, and communication templates.
- Metrics captured: MTTA, MTTR, number of manual workarounds, runbook edit count.
- Scoring rubric (example):
  - MTTA < 5m: 3 points
  - MTTR < 30m: 3 points\  - Runbook edits > 1: 2 points\  - Customer comm ready and approved: 2 points\  - Evidence artifacts uploaded: 1 point
- Passing threshold: >= 8 points.
- Debrief: 30–60 minutes with facilitator, steward, and observers. Action items captured in tracker and prioritized into the tribal backlog.

Artifacts & evidence required after sprint
- Completed incident timeline (plaintext or CSV).
- Runbook edits committed as PRs (link).
- Postmortem draft with assigned owners for corrective actions.
- Scoring sheet and lessons learned doc.

Permissions & sandboxing guidance
- Use the oncall-sprint sandbox tenant (request via infra@redwood).
- No changes to production allowed during simulations. If a simulation requires production toggles, explicit approval from service steward and SRE director required.

Related pages
- runtime/kv-cache-eviction-checklist (link placeholder)
- infra/autoscaler-flap-mitigation (link placeholder)
- product/model-rollout-emergency-rollback (link placeholder)

Review cadence and ownership
- This page: owned by Oncall Enablement (eng-sre). Review quarterly or after any Sev1.
- Sprint artifacts: steward must resolve action items within 30 days or file an exception with their manager.

Appendix: quick commands & dashboards
- Check CPU and autoscaler events (kubectl & cloud CLI examples):
  - kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime -o wide\  - gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"name~'runtime'\"\\- Dashboards: Runtime - Latency (p50/p95), KV hit/miss, Model QPS by variant.

If you have questions or want to schedule an upcoming sprint, ping #oncall-sprints or email oncall-enablement@redwood.com.

payload.page_title: Oncall Decision Briefs and Severity Calibration

sections.body:
Summary:
This page is a compact, action-oriented set of decision briefs for oncall leads and bridge operators to calibrate incident severity, accelerate correct containment actions, and produce consistent customer communications. It contains: a severity calibration matrix tuned for LLM serving, short decision briefs per common signal, a 10-step incident containment runbook skeleton, rotation expectations and handoff checklist, a library of lightweight game-day scenarios, and ready-to-send status & post-incident templates.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Redwood Inference public-facing services and customer-dedicated model pools.
- Intent: reduce ambiguity during initial 0–30 minute response window; help oncall quickly select severity, route resources, and produce customer-safe notices.

Quick definitions:
- Pager: immediate interrupt for a responder.
- Bridge: the primary coordination channel (Zoom + Slack bridge).
- IC: Incident Commander.
- SLO breach: measurable deviation for latency, availability, or quality.

Severity calibration matrix (use within first 10 minutes):
| Severity | Observable signal (example) | Immediate action (first 10m) | Pager? | Exec notify? |
|---|---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| Sev 1 (Critical) | Multi-region 5xx surge > 3x baseline OR >2% customer-impacting errors for 15m | Open bridge, notify SRE and sysadmin, failover/rollback to previous model, trigger capacity uplift | Yes (all hands) | Yes (CTO, Head of SRE) |
| Sev 2 (High) | Sustained 99.9th percentile token latency increase >2x for >10m OR major customer tenant errors | Open bridge, short-term throttles, enable cached responses, engage model team | Yes | No (exec watch) |
| Sev 3 (Medium) | Intermittent latency spikes, elevated error traces localized to a pool | Triage oncall, collect traces, apply targeted restarts, monitor | Maybe (rotation-dependent) | No |
| Sev 4 (Low) | Degraded observability, single non-prod pool flake, or advisory quality regression | File ticket, schedule follow-up, run diagnostic job | No | No |

How to pick the right severity (decision brief):
1) Measure customer impact: count of affected requests, percentage error rate, and whether any SLA/commitment is violated.
2) Confirm signal covariance: is latency accompanied by increased CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache evictions, or network errors?
3) Consider blast radius: single tenant, single region, or global?
4) Choose severity that matches SLO impact and blast radius; document reasons on the bridge.

Immediate containment runbook (0–30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge pager within 2 minutes and post initial stub in bridge: cause-known? impact-estimate? immediate-actions? IC: <name>.
2. Collect telemetry: run quick queries (examples below).
3. Isolate scope: identify affected model, region, and tenant(s).
4. If errors > threshold or global latency: route traffic to standby region or compatible model variant.
5. Apply temporary rate-limiting per-tenant or increase token budget for critical customers.
6. If KV cache thrash: increase cache size or flush hot keys; roll-back recent cache config changes.
7. If GPU saturations: scale up Dedicated pool or enable burst capacity; drain noisy pods.
8. If model quality regression suspected: switch to previous model version (pin) and disable canary.
9. Validate core functionality with synthetic smoke tests (examples below).
10. Stabilize and move to recovery playbook; document timeline.

Quick telemetry commands (examples for bridge use):
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=model-x -o wide
- ./infra/ops/bin/query_metrics --metric=token_latency_99 --window=10m --service=serving
- curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.redwood/api/pools/active | jq
- python tools/run_smoke.py --endpoint=https://host/compose --prompt-file=smoke/prompts/basic.json

Validation & smoke tests (3 checks):
- Latency smoke: execute 20 small inference requests, confirm p50 < expected and p99 < threshold.
- Throughput smoke: run a 60s burst to confirm autoscaler behavior and observe error rate.
- Quality smoke: run 10 golden prompts from eval set and diff token-level outputs vs baseline.

Handoff and rotation expectations:
- Primary oncall should hold the bridge for first 30–60 minutes. After stabilization, IC names the continuity owner for long-tail remediation.
- Handoff checklist (pre-handover): current severity, actions taken, open tasks, key leads and their contact, expected next check-in time, link to postmortem stub.
- Shadow policy: second-level oncall must be shadowing high-severity incidents until bridge is closed.

Game-day scenario library (pick 1–2 per 90m drill):
- Scenario A: Global KV cache evictions triggered by heavy prompt prefixes; objective: restore tail latency to 95% of baseline in 30m. Success criteria: p99 latency reduced to target and no customer SLA violations.
- Scenario B: Canary model rollout introduces hallucination spike for a subset of prompts; objective: detect quality regression, rollback, and verify. Success: rollback within 15m, zero impacted customers in next hour.
- Scenario C: Bursty token flood from multi-tenant misconfiguration leading to GPU saturation; objective: apply tenant throttles and bring utilization under 85% in 20m.
- Scoring rubric: detection time (0–10), containment time (0–20), correctness of customer comms (0–5), post-incident documentation (0–5).

Customer & status page templates (use during first 60 minutes):
- Short status (public):
  Title: "Partial service disruption affecting model inference in <region>"
  Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Resolved
  Impact: "Some customers may experience increased latency or errors for text generation in <region>."
  Next update: "<time in UTC; e.g., 2026-01-15T15:45Z>"

- Internal customer notice (email/CSR):
  Subject: [Incident] Degraded inference throughput in <region> — immediate actions taken
  Body: "Timeline: <brief timeline>. Impact: <who/what>. Actions taken: switched traffic to fallback model, enabled per-tenant throttles. Next steps: continuing validation and a follow-up at <time>. If you see critical customer impact, reply to this thread and we will prioritize outreach. — Oncall team"

Post-incident (30–120 minutes after stabilization):
- Evidence collection: attach traces, dashboard snapshots (token_latency, error_rate, cpu/gpu_util), and command history.
- Immediate remediation tickets: create JIRA with severity, owner, ETA for fix and link to postmortem.
- Postmortem stub: use the Incident comm and postmortem framework page (link included below) and ensure RCA distinguishes cause vs trigger.

Calibration checklist for oncall leads (weekly):
- Review all Sev1/Sev2 incidents from last week and confirm severity assignments.
- Re-run 1 game-day scenario with the current oncall roster.
- Audit status page templates used and sample the last 3 customer notices for tone and completeness.
- Confirm runbook commands remain executable and update credentials if needed.

Runbook maintenance rules:
- Every change to a critical runbook requires a PR, peer reviewer, and one successful game-day validation.
- Runbooks older than 180 days must be flagged for review.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Incident comm & postmortem framework: <confluence://incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026>
- Triage for degraded latency and SLO regression: <confluence://triage-for-degraded-latency-and-slo-regression-2024>
- Operator competency & evidence handbook: <confluence://operator-competency-incident-evidence-handbook-2025>

Ownership and escalation paths:
- Primary: Serving SRE (oncall rotation) — first responder & bridge operator.
- Secondary: Runtime team — model/pool experts.
- Tertiary: Customer success for high-touch customers and legal for any regulatory-impacting incidents.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft by Lina Rodriguez.
- 2025-05-04: added KV cache guidance and smoke tests (reviewers updated).
- 2026-01-15: calibration checklist and new game-day scenarios added (published).

Notes for readers:
- Use this page as a living playbook; pick the severity conservatively if in doubt and prioritize customer safety.
- If you have changes, open a PR against the runbook repository and ping the reviewers listed on this page.

payload.page_title: Serving incident orchestration for model degradations

sections.body: This playbook describes orchestration, runbooks, communications, and post-incident practices for operational incidents that manifest as model degradations: sustained latency regressions, throughput collapses, KV-cache corruption, and measurable model-quality regressions (e.g., hallucination rate or prompt-set failures). It focuses on incidents affecting Redwood inference serving (hosted, dedicated, private) and assumes responders have access to the Console, telemetry dashboards, and the serving runtime control plane.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Scope: incidents where one or more model endpoints or model variants experience degraded performance or quality that impacts customer SLOs or causes meaningful customer errors.
- Intent: provide a repeatable, low-friction path from detection to recovery and learning. Priorities are: safety (prevent customer data loss), restore service (meet SLOs), reduce blast radius, and learn.
sections.heading: Scope and intent

sections.body:
1) Sev1 — Full service outage or >50% of requests failing or >2x median latency across all regions for >5 minutes. Immediate bridge and customer notification.
2) Sev2 — Significant degradation for a subset of customers or a single region (e.g., sustained 5–10x p95 latency increase, backlog growth). Start bridge within 15 min.
3) Sev3 — Localized quality regressions (model outputs failing quality checks), slow error increases, non-customer-visible degradations. Begin triage during working hours.
sections.heading: Classification matrix (severity mapping)

sections.body:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns orchestration, communications, and triage prioritization. Typically on-call service owner or SRE.
- Service Owner: primary model/endpoint engineer. Owns technical mitigation and rollback.
- Bridge Operator: runs the conference bridge / status page updates.
- Escalation Liaison (Customer Success): handles customer comms for enterprise customers.
- On-call Data Scientist: validates model-quality regressions and run evaluation harnesses.
sections.heading: Roles & responsibilities

sections.body:
- Alerts: p95 latency > 2× baseline for 5 minutes; error-rate spike > 1% absolute; KV-cache miss rate > 20% leading to CPU/GPU increase.
- Console signals: per-route token-rate drop, sudden increase in request retries, or autoscaler thrash events.
- Quality monitors: prompt-set eval failure rate > 4% on production canary.
- Customer reports via support or status page.
sections.heading: Detection & initial signals (examples)

sections.body:
1) Detect and declare incident: responder acknowledges alert in 5 minutes. If metrics cross Sev1 thresholds, IC declares Sev1.
2) Stand up bridge: Bridge Operator starts bridge (Zoom/Meet) and ticket in tracker (include live links).
3) Initial triage (first 15 minutes): determine blast radius, rollback options, safe mitigations.
4) Mitigate & restore (15–90 minutes): apply short-term mitigation (route traffic away, scale up reserved pool, swap model variant).
5) Stabilize & monitor (90–240 minutes): watch SLOs return to normal across 2× measurement window.
6) Close & learn (post-recovery): IC assigns postmortem owner within 24 hours.

Runbook: high-latency spike affecting hosted endpoints (quick checklist)
1) Evidence collection (first 5 min):
   - Check Console: per-model p50/p95/p99, active requests, queue length.
   - Run: Grafana query for p95 by region and model: "sum by(region, model) (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m]) ))"
   - Check autoscaler events: rapid scale-outs/scale-ins.
2) Immediate mitigations (choose one based on blast radius):
   - Route traffic to a compatible model variant with known performance profile. Command: rdctl route set --route <route-id> --variant <variant-id> --weight 100
   - Pin customers to Dedicated pools if available: Console -> Customers -> Fast Switch -> Dedicated
   - Temporarily disable streaming/chunking on heavy routes to reduce scheduling overhead.
3) If KV-cache miss storm detected:
   - Rehydrate hot prefix caches: exec on cache-repopulate job: kubectl -n serving run cache-repop --image=infra/cache-pop --env PREFIX_LIST=/opt/hot-prefixes
   - If cache corruption suspected, pause writes and roll forward from last known-good snapshot: rdctl cache restore --snapshot <snapshot-id>
4) If autoscaler thrash:
   - Lock min/max pool sizes for the affected pool to current safe values via infra control plane.
   - Temporarily switch to reserved capacity for critical customers.
5) When latency is reduced to within SLO for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows, begin controlled rollback of temporary mitigations.

Runbook: model-quality regression (e.g., hallucination or prompt-set failures)
1) Triage classifier: check evaluation harness for failing prompt sets and production canary outputs.
2) If regression is only in a canary: stop rollout and revert to previous model variant.
3) If regression is in production: throttle traffic, enable safe-mode (strict decoding constraints, lower temperature), and route high-value customers to vetted variants.
4) Data collection: collect 1k sample inputs/outputs, flag for red-team review, and run against eval harness.
sections.heading: Incident lifecycle (high-level steps)

sections.body:
- Generation latency SLO (p95): 500ms for hosted small models, 1.2s for long-context variants.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for hosted API (critical routes).
- Model-quality guardrail: canary pass rate >= 98% on core prompt-set.
- Alert thresholds: p95 > 2× baseline for 5m -> Sev2; p95 > 3× baseline for 5m or error-rate > 5% -> Sev1.
sections.heading: SLOs & thresholds (reference)

sections.body:
- Status page short: "Degradation affecting text-generation endpoints in us-west-2. Engineers investigating. Some customers may experience elevated latency or failures. Updates at 30-minute cadence."
- Enterprise template (first notice):
  Subject: Incident affecting inference latency (US-West)
  Body: "We are currently investigating an incident impacting inference latency for model <model-name> in US-West. Impact: elevated p95 latency and increased request errors for a subset of requests. Actions: routing traffic to alternate variants and scaling dedicated pools for impacted customers. ETA for next update: 30 minutes. If you require a dedicated channel, reply to this message and we will open a customer bridge."
- Internal bridge message (standup):
  "IC: <name>. Current status: Sev2. Impact: p95 x5 for route /v1/generate. Mitigations in progress: variant swap and cache rehydration. Owner: <service-owner>. Next update in 15 minutes."

Postmortem template (required fields) — publish within 72h:
- Title (one-line)
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Timeline (UTC) with bullet timestamps
- Impact (customers, routes, metrics)
- Root cause analysis (technical and organizational factors)
- Mitigations applied during incident
- Remediation plan (owner + ETA)
- Follow-ups and action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
- Postmortem reviewers

On-call rotations, handoffs, and expectations:
- Primary on-call: 1-week rotation (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC). SREs and owners swap weekly.
- Secondary/reserve: assigned for 24/7 coverage escalation.
- Handoff checklist (before shift end): active incidents, outstanding actions, customer escalations, link to bridge and runbook, list of temporary mitigations.
- Quiet window: prefer handoffs outside of expected maintenance or game-day windows.

Game day plan (quarterly, 90–120 minutes exercise)
- Objective: validate detection and response to a model-quality regression introduced in a canary rollout and a simultaneous KV-cache miss storm.
- Participants: on-call SRE, service owner, on-call data scientist, customer liaison, bridge operator.
- Scenario steps:
  1) Seed canary with failing prompt-set (automated).
  2) Trigger cache eviction on a test pool.
  3) Observe alerts (must fire within 5 minutes) and require team to follow runbook.
  4) Evaluate time-to-recovery and communications.
- Scoring: detection (0–5), triage accuracy (0–5), mitigation correctness (0–10), communications clarity (0–5).
sections.heading: Communications templates (status page & enterprise notice)

sections.body:
- rdctl list models --region us-west-2
- rdctl swap-variant --route <route> --from <old> --to <new>
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=runtime --since=10m | grep "backpressure"
- grafana link: Console -> Dashboards -> Serving -> p95 by model
sections.heading: Operational tooling & quick commands (reference)

sections.body:
- Every runbook section must have an owner and a last-reviewed date. This playbook is reviewed quarterly by the Eng SRE and Serving Runtime teams.
- Postmortem owners must close follow-ups or convert them into roadmap tickets within 30 days.

Appendix A — example evidence table (for postmortem)
| Item | Where to find | Example query/command | Notes |
| Timeline logs | /var/log/serving/events | grep "2027-02-09T" /var/log/serving/events | include request ids |
| Metrics | Grafana serving cluster | see dashboard: p95-by-model | export CSV at time window |
| Cache snapshot | S3://redwood-cache/snapshots/ | rdctl cache list-snapshots | pick most recent <snapshot-id> |

Appendix B — escalation matrix quick reference:
- 0–15 minutes: on-call primary (ack & bridge)
- 15–45 minutes: SRE + service owner engage; escalate to IC if unresolved
- >45 minutes or customer-impacting SEV1: Paging to Engineering Director and Customer Success lead.
sections.heading: Runbook hygiene and ownership

sections.body:
- Serving runtime architecture (link): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- SLO and error budget playbook: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Model onboarding and QA: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
sections.heading: References & related pages

sections.body:
- 2026-11-15: Created by Asha Kapoor
- 2027-02-10: Reviewed and published after game-day validation (reviewers: Miguel Santos, Riley Chen, Priya Nair)

This document is intended as an operational reference. If you are the on-call first responder, follow the shortest path to restore service and then enable learning via the postmortem template.

payload.page_title: On-Call Operator Lifecycle, Incident Orchestration, and Customer Briefing Kit

sections.body:
Purpose
This document is a concise, prescriptive playbook for on-call operators managing Redwood Inference serving incidents. It focuses on lifecycle expectations (before, during, after), rapid orchestration patterns for common LLM-serving failures, and a customer briefing kit that CSRs and on-call leads can use verbatim. It is intended for SREs, Platform Engineers, Incident Commanders, and Customer Success liaisons.

Scope
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments of Redwood inference runtime.
- Covers incidents that affect availability, latency SLOs, cost anomalies, and model output quality regressions.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks; use this as the canonical orchestration template and communication source.

Key definitions
- Operator: the on-call engineer responsible for initial triage and first containment.
- Incident Commander (IC): owns the incident lifecycle and cross-team orchestration.
- CSR Liaison: Customer Success engineer responsible for external customer communication.
- Severity (S): S0 (outage), S1 (major degradation), S2 (partial impact), S3 (informational / maintenance).

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
- API 95th latency SLO: 250ms for text-generation small models, 95th < 250ms. Alert: sustained 95th > 400ms for 3m.
- Token generation error rate: SLO 0.1% 5m rolling. Alert: error_rate > 0.5% for 5m.
- KV cache miss amplification: baseline miss ratio < 6%. Alert: baseline miss ratio rises above 20% for 10m.
- Cost per 1k tokens deviation: baseline +/- 30% for 15m triggers investigation.

Operator lifecycle checklist (Before shift)
1) Run pre-shift health checks (5 min):
   - Confirm PagerDuty mobile subscription and Slack availability.
   - Open Metrics dashboard: "Serving / Latency", "Token Costs", "Cache Miss Ratio".
   - Confirm daily golden synthetic checks green (chat-sim / embedding-sim).
2) Warm-handoff (if taking over):
   - Review previous 24h incidents in the on-call summary.
   - Announce presence in #oncall-handoff Slack channel with the standard template: "Oncall: Maya now on duty until 08:00 UTC".
3) Shadowing & Mentoring: new operators must shadow 2 live shifts and attend a 2-hour runbook lab before primary rotation.

Initial detection and first 10 minutes (fast triage stencil)
1) Confirm the alert source and validity:
   - Is this from synthetic canaries, customer telemetry, or user reports? Link: <pagerduty-incident-url>.
2) Classify severity using the impact matrix (latency + error + customer traffic).
3) If S0 or S1, acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and start an incident bridge.
4) Capture evidence within first 5 minutes:
   - Timestamped screenshots of dashboards.
   - API traces for a sample request (trace_id).
   - Representative logs (service, model-server, gpu-host).
5) Execute rapid containment (see containment patterns).

Containment patterns (prescriptive)
- Pattern A — Model fallback:
  1) If a model flavor (e.g., quantized variant) is failing, switch traffic to the most recent verified stable variant per the model-catalog:
     - CLI: curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/route/switch" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","target_model":"model-v2-stable"}'
  2) Validate synthetic check returns green within 2 minutes.
- Pattern B — KV cache eviction and warm-warm restore:
  1) Identify cache churn: query metrics (datadog): metric:runtime.kv_cache.evictions{service:encoder} by host.
  2) If eviction rate > 1000/min on a node, cordon instance and boot a replacement from the warm pool:
     - kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && terraform apply -target=module.warm_pool.instance
- Pattern C — Throttling / backpressure mitigation:
  1) Apply admission control to non-critical customers and routes using rate-limit policy rollback:
     - Console action: Routes > /v1/embeddings > set burst=50/s steady=20/s for tier:free.

Escalation matrix (primary contacts and ownership)
- Incident Commander: oncall-ic rotation (PagerDuty role). Responsibilities: declare severity, manage bridge, approve mitigations.
- Runtime Lead: eng-serving-runtime (pager, slack #runtime-oncall).
- Network & Cloud: eng-infra oncall (pager).
- Customer Success Liaison: customer-success oncall (Slack #customer-ops).
- Legal / Comms (for incidents with regulatory/customer data exposure): security-and-compliance lead (email/phone).

Runbook excerpts: common LLM-serving incident types
1) High tail latency (95th spikes)
   - Quick checks: CPU/GPU saturation, host GC cycles, OOMs, queue length.
   - Commands:
     - kubectl top pods --namespace=runtime | grep model-server
     - datadog query: avg(last_5m):gpu.utilization{cluster:prod} by {pool}
   - Remediations (in order):
     a) Redirect traffic to lower-cost region or dedicated pool with headroom.
     b) Enable autoscale burst (console) for affected model route.
     c) If memory thrash: restart model-server pod on a rotated node.
2) Model quality regression (sudden hallucination/formatting errors)
   - Evidence to collect: failing prompt set IDs, sample outputs, model version, tokenization artifacts.
   - Immediate mitigation: route to previous model snapshot and open a model regression ticket to Applied ML.
   - Customer-facing line: "We observed an unexpected change in model outputs for a short window; we have rolled back to a verified snapshot and are investigating root cause."
3) Cost anomaly / token-spike
   - Check: per-route token count and new spikes in request length.
   - Temporary policy: throttle high-volume customers and enable per-request token caps.
   - Longer term: enable prompt-length enforcement and add quota notifications.

Customer briefing kit (templates with placeholders)
- Immediate acknowledgement (within 30 minutes of S0/S1):
  Subject: "Redwood status: Incident acknowledged — [short impact summary]"
  Body: "Hello <CustomerName>,
  We detected an issue affecting <product-area> beginning at <start-time-UTC>. Impact: <brief-impact>. We have an incident active and are working to restore service. Next update expected in 30 minutes.
  Incident ID: <PD-12345>
  IC: <IC name> (oncall@redwood.internal)
  Regards,
  Redwood Support Team"

- Follow-up update (once containment complete):
  Subject: "Redwood status: Containment in place — <summary>"
  Body: "Hello <CustomerName>,
  We have implemented <mitigation> at <time-UTC>. Impact is reduced to <new-impact>. We are now collecting detailed evidence and will provide root cause within 48–72 hours.
  Temporary mitigations applied: <list>.
  Next update: <ETA>.
  - <CSR name>"

- Post-incident customer report (formal): include timeline, impact quantification, root cause analysis, remediation, and preventive actions. Use the Postmortem template below and attach anonymized evidence.

Postmortem template (timing expectations)
- Draft Summary within 72 hours (initial incident sketch).
- Full postmortem (with RCA and action items) within 7 business days for S0/S1.
- Must include: timeline of events, evidence artifacts, contributing factors, corrective actions (owner + due date), regression test updates, risk assessment, and customer impact table.

Evidence collection checklist (must be added to the incident artifact bundle)
- Links to dashboard snapshots (png) for latency, errors, cache miss ratio.
- Representative request traces (3 samples with trace_ids).
- Model and runtime version hashes.
- Config snapshots for load-balancer and route policies.
- PagerDuty timeline export and bridge transcript.
- Any customer-reported payloads (sanitized).

Game day and training plan (quarterly cadence)
- Quarterly simulated incidents with mixed scenarios: cache-eviction storm, regional network partition, and model-quality regression.
- Roles scheduled: IC, runtime-ops, infra, CSR, legal observer.
- Scoring rubric: mean time to acknowledge (goal <2m), mean time to contain (goal <15m), customer comm delay (<30m), evidence completeness score (>90%).
- Post-game-day: 1-hour retrospective and remediation backlog grooming.

Rotation policy and handoffs
- Primary on-call shifts are 12 hours for Engineering SREs (08:00–20:00 UTC or 20:00–08:00 UTC) with one weekend rotation per quarter.
- Backup on-call: staggered 4-hour overlap at shift change.
- Handoff protocol: outgoing operator prepares a 15-minute handoff message covering open alerts, degraded routes, and ongoing mitigations. Handoff must be posted to #oncall-handoff channel and pinned.

Runbook governance and change control
- Every runbook referenced in this page must contain an owner tag and last-tested date.
- Runbooks older than 180 days are flagged for review.
- Substantive changes require a doc-review and a shadowed runbook test in a staging game-day.

Security and compliance considerations
- If incident involves potential data exposure, classify as security-sensitivity S and escalate to Security & Compliance immediately. Do not include any PII in external comms; use sanitized examples only.

Appendix: Quick reference templates and CLI snippets
- Acknowledge incident (PagerDuty): pd trigger --service "serving-api" --title "Latency spike" --severity high
- Snapshot dashboards (Datadog): datadog snapshot create --board "Serving|Latency" --start -10m --end now --output /tmp/latency.png
- Sample Slack update (to #customer-ops): "INC <PD-12345> S1: latency 95th 600ms since 13:11 UTC. Containment: routing change to dedicated-pool-3 in progress. IC: Maya. CSR: Priya. Next update: +20m."

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: Maya Chen (eng-sre). Maintenance cadence: quarterly review.
- Next scheduled game-day: 2026-05-15.

Related artifacts and links
- Model-serving runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Incident evidence standard: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-collection-standard-2025

Version history
- 2024-05-12: Created by Maya Chen.
- 2025-11-03: Expanded containment patterns and added cost anomaly play.
- 2026-02-14: Published with updated rotation policy and game-day schedule.

payload.page_title: External status protocol and runbook for multi-tenant incidents

sections.body:
SUMMARY
This playbook defines the external status protocols, approved customer communication templates, and operational runbook for multi-tenant incidents that impact Redwood Inference hosted APIs or Dedicated clusters. It is intended for oncall engineers, SRE bridge operators, customer success, and incident commanders.

SCOPE AND INTENDED USE
- Applies to incidents where one or more customers experience degraded latency, errors, or data-loss risk from hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments with observable customer impact.
- Excludes purely internal developer outages with zero customer-facing impact (see internal-only runbook).
- Use when incident severity >= S2 (see Severity mapping).

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES
- Incident Commander (IC): oncall SRE or senior engineer (primary decision-maker for containment and external comms).
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge and coordinates cross-team contributors.
- Customer Success Lead (CSL): owns customer-facing messaging and coordinates targeted customer outreach for impacted tenants.
- Model Owner / Serving Team: owners of the model-serving stack (model-serving team).
- Communications Reviewer: product marketing or legal for escalated enterprise disclosures (if required).

SEVERITY MAPPING (quick reference)
- S1 — Critical: Broad outage impacting >20% of requests or >5 customers with >30% error rates for >5 minutes. Triggers immediate exec alert and public status page incident.
- S2 — Major degradation: Significant latency or error rate increase for a subset of customers (>5% of requests or 1–5 customers affected) for >15 minutes. Triggers status page incident and targeted customer notices.
- S3 — Minor or single-customer impact: Latency or quality regressions affecting a single customer or non-critical degradation (work with CS for customer notice).

SLOs / ALERT THRESHOLDS (service-level examples)
| Service | SLO (p99 latency) | Alert threshold | Error budget policy |
| inference-gateway | 300 ms | p99 > 1200 ms for 5m | Pause non-critical experiments at 50% burn |
| model-serving | 75 ms per-token | p99 > 500 ms for 2m | Auto-fallback to smaller variant at 75% burn |
| router-api | 200 ms | p99 > 800 ms for 10m | Scale routing pods; escalate to infra |
NOTE: Table above is a plain-text representation — use monitoring dashboards for current SLO telemetry.

INITIAL BRIDGE AND RESPONSE PROCEDURE (first 15 minutes)
1) Acknowledge: PagerDuty/Slack alert acknowledged by first responder in 2 minutes.
2) Bridge up: Bridge Operator creates incident bridge (Zoom + Slack channel) and posts initial summary. Use channel name: #bridge-<short-service>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.
3) Triage: IC classifies severity (S1/S2/S3) within 10 minutes and assigns roles.
4) Customer signal: CSL prepares initial status page and customer notification drafts using templates below.
5) Containment plan: list immediate mitigations (see containment checklist).
6) Evidence capture: collect logs, traces, backend metrics, and top-50 request traces to evidence bucket (S3 path pattern: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/).

CONTAINMENT CHECKLIST (pick applicable steps quickly)
- Fail open to bulkhead-similar region: route traffic to fallback-region (region fallback policy).
- Activate model fallback: switch traffic from large-llm to quantized or smaller variant via router-api: POST /control/fallback?service=model-serving&variant=lite.
- Increase autoscaling target for inference-gateway by +50% (k8s HPA or cluster autoscaler).
- Disable non-essential batch jobs (analytics-ingest, background-aggregator) to free GPU/CPU.
- Purge or temporarily bypass KV cache if stale/poisoned: cache-ops flush-key-prefix --prefix=user-cache-<tenant-id>.

EXTERNAL STATUS PAGE PROCESS
- When to publish: Publish to public status page for any S1 and S2 incidents; optional for S3 when multiple customers affected.
- Status page ownership: Bridge Operator initiates the status update; CSL reviews before publish.
- Frequency: initial update within 15 minutes of incident classification; follow-ups every 30 minutes while active, then every 2 hours during stabilization; final resolution update when incident is resolved and postmortem scheduled.

PUBLIC STATUS TEMPLATES (replace tokens in {{double-braces}})
- Initial (S1/S2):
  Title: Degraded performance for Redwood inference API - detection ongoing
  Body: We are investigating increased error rates and elevated latency for the Redwood Inference API that may affect model responses and embeddings for some customers. Our oncall team has identified impacted regions: {{regions}} and is actively working on mitigation. No data loss has been detected at this time. Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner. Incident ID: {{incident-id}}.

- Update (stabilizing):
  Title: Mitigation in progress — partial recovery observed
  Body: We have implemented mitigations ({{mitigation-actions}}) and are seeing partial recovery in {{regions}}. Some requests may still experience increased latency. We will continue monitoring and provide another update by {{time}}. A targeted customer notice has been sent to affected tenants.

- Resolved:
  Title: Incident resolved — service normal
  Body: The incident impacting {{services}} has been resolved at {{timestamp}}. All systems are operating within normal parameters and SLOs are recovering. We are scheduling a post-incident report and will reach out to any customers who experienced sustained impact.

CUSTOMER EMAIL / CSR TEMPLATE (targeted notice for impacted customers)
Subject: Service impact affecting your Redwood Inference requests — incident {{incident-id}}
Body: Hello {{customer-name}},

We detected an incident that affected your requests between {{start}} and {{end}} against {{service-or-route}}. Our team applied the following mitigations: {{mitigation-actions}}. Based on initial analysis, the incident resulted in {{high-level-impact}} (e.g., higher latency, partial errors). We will follow up with a post-incident summary and actionable recommendations within 72 hours. If you need an immediate technical lead, reply and we will schedule a dedicated call.

RUNBOOK: TROUBLESHOOTING MATRIX (by symptom)
- Symptom: High p99 latency on inference-gateway  Causes to check: CPU saturation on gateway pods, network egress issues, backend model-serving queue depth > 500.  Steps: 1) kubectl top pods -n serving | sort -r; 2) check gateway logs for 502/504 spikes; 3) scale replicas: kubectl scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=<current*1.5>.
- Symptom: Increased 5xx from model-serving  Causes: model process crashes, OOM errors, model KV cache poisoning.  Steps: 1) check pod restarts: kubectl get pods -n model-serving -o wide; 2) inspect logs /var/log/model-serve.log; 3) roll model instance: /ops/rollout model-serving --selector=canary=false --max-surge=1.
- Symptom: Erratic user-specific errors  Causes: tenant config changes, prompt injection, corrupted tenant cache.  Steps: 1) isolate tenant traffic by routing to a dedicated lane; 2) flush tenant KV cache; 3) open high-priority support ticket to CSL.

ESCALATION MATRIX
- If containment not achieved within 30 minutes for S1: escalate to Head of SRE and oncall infra; issue an exec notification (email + Slack #exec-alerts).
- If third-party dependency (e.g., cloud provider networking) is suspected: open a provider support ticket and attach incident evidence bundle immediately.
- For potential data exposure: pause customer notifications until Security is engaged and legal is consulted (see security-and-compliance data-exposure SOP).

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS AND EVIDENCE RETENTION
1) Immediate capture: store logs/traces and a short incident chronology in s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/chronology.txt.
2) Postmortem draft: IC + Bridge Operator draft within 72 hours. Use postmortem template: executive summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation and long-term fixes, owners, ETA.
3) Evidence retention: retain raw traces for 90 days, aggregate metrics for 1 year. PII or customer-sensitive logs are archived with restricted access.
4) Customer follow-up: CSL to send tailored postmortem or summary within 72 hours to impacted customers, and schedule one-on-one calls for enterprise accounts as needed.

ONCALL ROTATION AND HANDOFFS (practical notes)
- Primary oncall: 7x24 primary rotation with 1-week shifts. Secondary oncall: 1-week shadow rotation for escalations.
- Handover checklist: unresolved incidents, active mitigations, pending postmortem actions, customer callbacks scheduled, links to active bridges. Use the template: Handover: <incidents>, <actions>, <blocked-by>.
- Escalation points: if primary cannot make a decision within 20 minutes, the secondary steps in as IC.

GAME DAY EXERCISES (recommended cadence)
- Quarterly full-scale game day that simulates a multi-tenant latency storm affecting router-api + model-serving. Objective: practice status page cadence, targeted customer comms, and model-fallback automation.
- Focused exercises monthly for new joiners to practice bridge operator responsibilities and evidence capture.

METRICS FOR COMMUNICATION (what to include in updates)
- Impacted customers count and representative tenant IDs (anonymized for public updates).
- % of requests failing and p99 latency relative to baseline.
- Mitigations applied and immediate effect (e.g., p99 improved from 1.4s -> 420ms).

AUDIT AND APPROVALS
- All public status updates must be approved by IC and CSL before publishing. For enterprise customers, postmortem and remediation plan must be reviewed by Security if data exposure or regulatory impact is suspected.

APPENDIX: CLI SNIPPETS AND LINKS
- Create bridge (internal tool): rwi bridge create --service model-serving --severity S1 --owner @aisha
- Evidence bundle upload: rwi incident evidence upload --id {{incident-id}} --path /tmp/evidence.tar.gz --s3 s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{{incident-id}}/
- Model fallback trigger (internal API): curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/rollout/fallback -d '{"service":"model-serving","variant":"lite"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

DOCUMENT HISTORY AND NOTES
- Created: 2026-03-15 by Aisha Patel
- Major revision: 2026-09-10 — added customer email templates and clarified evidence retention policy.

RELATED DOCUMENTS
- See onboarding checklist for new bridge operators, incident postmortem template, and data-exposure SOP in the security-and-compliance space.

END OF DOCUMENT

payload.page_title: Multichannel status orchestrator and translated templates

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the Multichannel Status Orchestrator pattern and provides a catalog of pre-approved, translated status templates for use on the Redwood status page, email, SMS, and account-level in-product notices. It standardizes sequencing, severity mapping, escalation ownership, and localization to ensure fast, consistent, brand-safe communications during operational incidents.

Audience
- On-call SREs and ops bridge leads
- Customer Success (CS) incident liaisons
- Legal and PR for high-severity incidents
- Product and platform owners responsible for downstream status updates

Scope and goals
- Cover: status page messages, customer emails, SMS alerts, in-console banners, and partner notifications.
- Goals: speed (first public notice <= 10 min for Sev1/S3P), tone consistency, accurate scope, and multilingual coverage for EN/ES/FR (priority) + fallback guidance for other languages.

When to use this orchestrator
1) Any incident with customer-facing impact (latency, errors, throttling, model quality) that meets our customer-impact tiers.
2) Planned maintenance affecting customers for >15 minutes.
3) When a single channel update (status page only) is insufficient — use multichannel for incidents hitting enterprise customers or when SLO crediting is possible.

Ownership and run ownership model
- Primary owner: Incident Bridge Lead (typically on-call SRE).
- Secondary owner (communication execution): On-call CS liaison.
- Legal/PR consulted for Sev1 external statements.
- Template maintenance: CS content guild; updates every quarter or after each major incident.

Severity mapping and timing commitments
| Severity | Redwood label | First public update target | Follow-up cadence | Channels to use |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| Sev1 / P0 | outage (critical customer impact) | <= 10 minutes | 30 min until stable, then hourly | Status page + Email + SMS + In-console banner + Slack enterprise channel |
| Sev2 / P1 | partial outage / high error rate | <= 30 minutes | 1 hour | Status page + Email + In-console banner |
| Sev3 / P2 | degraded latency/quality | <= 60 minutes | 4 hours | Status page + In-console banner |
| Maintenance | scheduled maintenance | 72 hours notice + reminder 2 hours prior | N/A | Status page + Email for affected customers |

Runbook: step-by-step communications workflow (bridge lead)
1. Confirm impact and scope with service owner (who does what, which customers affected).
2. Classify severity using the incident severity decision ladder (see related runbook).
3. Prepare first-public-message using the Short Notice template (English).
4. Post to Status Page (see API example below) and create an update draft for CS email/SMS channels.
5. Assign CS liaison to send targeted emails to enterprise tenants (copy includes timeline and mitigation).
6. If multilingual is required (see language matrix below), trigger translation pipeline (CS guild) and include translated messages in next update.
7. Schedule and post regular updates per the cadence. Ensure every update includes: what changed, current impact, mitigation steps, customer action (if any), ETA or next update window, and link to the status page.
8. Close the incident with a final summary (postmortem anchor) and publish a follow-up message containing root cause (when available) and remediation/fixes.

Status page API example (curl)
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"service":"inference-api","impact":"partial_outage","title":"Elevated 5xx errors affecting text-generation","body":"We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting text generation requests. Tokenization paths are being validated. More details will follow.","severity":"high" }'

Template catalog: Short Notice (English)
- Title: "Investigating elevated errors affecting [service]"
- Body (first public): "We are currently investigating elevated errors affecting [service]. Some requests may fail with 5xx responses or experience increased latency. Engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update by [time window]."
- Actions for customers: "No action required right now. If you see persistent failures, contact support with request IDs."

Template catalog: Escalated Notice (English)
- Title: "Partial outage impacting [feature] — mitigation in progress"
- Body (follow-up): "We have identified a regression in [component]. A mitigation (fallback to model vX) is rolling out. Impact is reduced for most customers but persists for a subset. Estimated time to mitigation: ~ [ETA]."

Multilingual translated templates (examples)
- Spanish (ES):
  - Title: "Investigando errores elevados que afectan a [service]"
  - Body: "Actualmente estamos investigando errores elevados que afectan a [service]. Algunas solicitudes pueden fallar con respuestas 5xx o experimentar mayor latencia. Los ingenieros están investigando activamente. Publicaremos una actualización antes de [time window]."
- French (FR):
  - Title: "Investigation d'erreurs élevées affectant [service]"
  - Body: "Nous enquêtons actuellement sur des erreurs élevées affectant [service]. Certaines requêtes peuvent échouer avec des 5xx ou subir une latence accrue. Les ingénieurs enquêtent activement. Nous publierons une mise à jour avant [time window]."

Language matrix and precedence rules
- Priority locales: en-US (default), es-ES, fr-FR. For enterprise customers with tenant locale preference: use tenant locale if available.
- If a translation is not available within the first update window, post English with a short apology line: "Localized message forthcoming — English update provided below."

Channel-specific formatting notes
- SMS: keep <= 320 characters; include link to status page and support contact.
- Email: include incident ID, impact table (affected regions/tenants), and recommended mitigations for customers. Use the Email Notice template.
- In-console banner: include short call-to-action (CTA) and link to status page. Do not include internal debugging details.

Email Notice template (example)
Subject: "[Incident ID] — Impact to [service] (updates every 30m)"
Body:
Hello [Customer name],

We want to let you know that you may experience [brief impact description]. Our engineering teams are actively investigating and we will provide updates every [cadence].

What we know: [bullet list of affected regions / endpoints / tenant subsets]
What we're doing: [bullet list of mitigation steps]
If you need immediate assistance: contact support@redwood.ai with Incident ID [incident id].

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Incident Team

Customer tiers and communication escalation matrix
| Customer tier | Channel | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise (contracted) | Email + Phone + Status page + Account PM | CS Liaison + Bridge Lead |
| Self-serve paying | Status page + Email | Bridge Lead + CS Broadcast |
| Free / trial | Status page | Bridge Lead |

Translation pipeline and turnaround SLA
- Rapid translation SLA for priority locales: 20 minutes for short notices (<=120 words) via CS guild rotation.
- Non-priority locale request: create ticket to Content Ops for 24–72 hour translation turnaround.
- If machine translation is used for immediate needs, the message must be labeled: "Machine translation — human review pending."

Templates for legal / PR review
- Use the Legal Review short-form: include impact facts, customer exposure (yes/no), and whether data loss is suspected. Submit PR/Legal at legal@redwood.ai with subject line: "LEGAL REVIEW REQUEST — Incident [ID]".

Post-incident cadence and postmortem inclusion
- Final customer-facing post: publish "Incident resolved" update within 24 hours with a summary and link to the postmortem.
- Postmortem must contain a customer-facing executive summary (2–3 paragraphs) and a technical appendix. CS authors the customer-facing summary.

Example status messages (full templates)
- SMS (short): "[INCIDENT ID] We are investigating elevated errors in [service]. Details: [short url to status]."
- In-console banner: "We are currently experiencing degraded [service]. See status.redwood.ai for updates."

Triage checklist for translation decisions (bridge lead)
1. Confirm affected customer list and locale preferences.
2. If >5 enterprise customers in same locale are affected -> require human translation.
3. Else: post English + note about localization.
4. Trigger CS guild if human translation required.

Governance and quality control
- Quarterly audit: sample 10 incidents and validate message timeliness, localization correctness, and adherence to templates.
- Incident communications training: mandatory for bridge leads and CS liaisons (1x per quarter).
- Template change process: propose PR in the content repo, two reviewers required (CS lead + SRE comms owner).

Appendix A — Example incident lifecycle timeline (Sev1)
- T+0m: Detection, bridge stood up, impact confirmed.
- T+5m: First public status page post (short notice).
- T+10m: Targeted enterprise email drafted and approved.
- T+30m: Mitigation rolling for subset; status page update + SMS to contracting customers.
- T+120m: Stabilized for 95% of traffic; hourly updates continue.
- T+24h: Incident closed, final summary posted, postmortem assigned.

Appendix B — Sample status page payload (JSON)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-20260208-1234",
  "service": "inference-api",
  "severity": "high",
  "title": "Investigating elevated 5xxs for text-generation",
  "body": "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting text-generation. More details to follow."
}

Appendix C — Contacts and escalation list
- On-call Bridge Lead: pager (primary on-call)
- CS Liaison: cs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- PR: pr@redwood.ai

Change log
- 2024-11-14: Drafted by Lauren Chen.
- 2025-06-03: Added French templates and updated SLA for translations (Marco Ruiz).
- 2026-02-08: Revised cadence and included SMS character guidance (Aisha Patel).

Related pages
- Incident severity decision ladder (link internal)
- Postmortem style guide
- Customer escalation contacts directory

End of document

payload.page_title: Pagerless Escalation and Shadow Ops Handbook

sections.body:
Overview

This handbook documents the Pagerless Escalation pattern and the Shadow Ops role used for low- and medium-severity degradations where immediate interrupting pages are unnecessary or counterproductive. It defines the decision criteria, communication templates, role responsibilities, automated signals, and game-day exercises to validate the pattern.

Why we use pagerless escalation
- Reduce alert fatigue for noisy, transient signals (e.g., short-lived 5xx bursts, KV cache warm-up spikes).
- Reserve pagers for incidents requiring synchronous coordination (high-severity/Customer-impacting).
- Improve signal triage fidelity by enriching alerts with context before human interrupt.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood-hosted runtime and Dedicated control-plane alerts categorized as Severity 3 and Severity 4 in our incident taxonomy.
- Does NOT apply to: security breaches, data-loss events, full-region outages, or SLA-violating incidents (Severity 1 or 2).

Key concepts and definitions
- Pagerless Alert: An automated alert that posts to #ops-notifications with a synthesized summary, suggested runbook link, and a list of likely remediation steps. No pager is fired automatically.
- Shadow Ops: A rotating, lightweight operative (not full responder) who monitors pagerless alerts, performs preliminary analysis, and escalates when human coordination is required.
- Mobilization Bridge: A temporary collaboration channel (Slack huddle + Zoom bridge) opened when escalation criteria are met.

Roles and responsibilities
| Role | Primary responsibilities | Escalation contact |
| Shadow Ops | Monitor pagerless alerts, confirm signal validity, attempt quick mitigations, update status doc | Primary oncall (if escalated) |
| Shadow Lead (senior) | Final decision to escalate to bridge, coordinate customer comms if needed | SRE oncall, Incident Commander |
| Primary Oncall | Runs bridge, coordinates engineers, executes major mitigations | Engineering oncall roster |
| Customer Success | Prepare customer-facing notices if bridge opens | Customer Success Manager |

Decision criteria: when to remain pagerless vs escalate
1. Stay pagerless when all of the following are true:
   - Incident classified Severity 3 or 4.
   - Signal includes a clear, single-service scope (not cross-region).
   - Estimated customer impact < 5% of active requests or limited to internal telemetry.
   - Automated mitigations or cache warming can be attempted without cross-team coordination.
2. Escalate to a Mobilization Bridge when any of the following occur:
   - Error rate sustains > 10% for 5 minutes after automated throttles/buffering.
   - SLO for critical path (p99 latency or availability) is projected to be breached within 15 minutes.
   - Multiple services begin failing concurrently or multiple customers report matching errors.

Pagerless flow (step-by-step)
1. Detection: Alerting platform (Prometheus/Alertmanager) fires a pagerless alert into #ops-notifications and creates an incident stub in the incident tracker (Jira/IR-XXXX). Alert contains: concise summary, core metrics (30s/5m/1h), top 3 correlated traces, proposed runbook link.
2. Auto-enrichment: Alert processor attaches recent traces, mapping to model-serving shard, last deploy, and recent kernel/quantization changes.
3. Shadow Ops pickup (within 3 minutes): Rotating Shadow Ops acknowledges the alert in Slack and updates the incident stub with initial triage notes.
4. Quick mitigations (if applicable, within 10 minutes): Restart worker pool on affected shard, enable fallback model variant, purge stale cache prefix. Shadow Ops documents commands used.
5. Observe (10–30 minutes): If metrics recover to < threshold for 15 minutes, mark incident as "resolved without pager" and close stub after a 1-hour observation window.
6. Escalate: If criteria in "Decision criteria" are met, Shadow Ops notifies Shadow Lead and requests bridge. The Shadow Lead confirms and triggers pager and bridge.

Templates and automation
- Slack message template (pagerless alert to #ops-notifications):
  > [pagerless] IR-XXXX | service: runtime-ingest | 5xx rate 7.2% (5m) | affected region: us-west-2 | suggested mitigations: restart-pool, enable-fallback-model | link: <incident-stub-link>

- Incident stub fields (minimum):
  - title (string)
  - severity (S1..S4)
  - observed_at (ISO timestamp)
  - affected_services (CSV)
  - initial_metric_snapshot (30s/5m/1h)
  - enrichment_links (traces, logs, recent-deploys)
  - actions_taken (chronological bullet list)

Runbook excerpt: common quick mitigations
1. Restart worker pool (stateless replicas):
   - CLI: rdxctl cluster restart --service runtime-ingest --shard X
   - Expected result: drop in 5xx within 60–120s as unhealthy nodes recycle
2. Enable fallback model variant:
   - Console: model -> runtime-ingest -> Switch to variant fallback-v1
   - Note: fallback reduces quality but often restores availability quickly
3. KV cache purge for prefix storm:
   - CLI: rdx-cachectl purge --prefix project123:prompt_cache --region us-west-2
   - Caution: large purges may cause CPU spikes; stagger if > 10M keys

Customer communication guidance (pagerless incidents)
- If resolved without pager: No external communication required. Document internally and include a one-paragraph summary in the weekly operations digest.
- If bridge opens or incident affects > 5% of customers: Customer Success drafts an outbound notice using the template below and coordinates approval with Shadow Lead.

Customer notice template (short outage)
Subject: Redwood Inference brief impact to request processing in us-west-2
Body: We observed elevated error rates for request processing in us-west-2 between 2026-11-15 03:12 UTC and 2026-11-15 03:32 UTC. Our automated mitigations (pool restart and fallback model enable) restored service. We do not expect data loss. If you saw degraded responses, please contact your CSM.

Status page messaging (when bridge opens)
- Status title: Elevated error rates in us-west-2 (Runtime Ingest)
- Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors and latency.
- Current status: Investigating (Engineering mobilized)
- Next update cadence: Every 20 minutes until mitigation confirmed

Game day exercises (to validate the pattern)
1. Objective: Validate that Shadow Ops can detect, mitigate, and decide not to escalate for a synthetic Severity 3 event.
2. Injected signal: Simulate a 5xx spike on a single shard for 12 minutes.
3. Success criteria:
   - Shadow Ops acknowledges within 3 minutes
   - Quick mitigations executed within 8 minutes and documented
   - No bridge opened and incident closed after 1-hour observation window
4. Post-exercise deliverable: 1-page summary, runbook adjustments, and lessons learned logged to the incident learning catalog.

Rotation and coverage guidance
- Shadow Ops is a 1-week rotating role drawn from oncall teams. Typical rotation: Mon 00:00 UTC to Mon 00:00 UTC.
- Shift responsibilities: 30-minute response SLA to acknowledge; 10-minute SLA to attempt allowed quick mitigations.
- Training: New Shadows complete an onboarding lab focused on common mitigation commands and the alert enrichment UI.

Metrics and reporting
- Tracked KPIs (weekly):
  - Pagerless incident count
  - Pagerless escalation rate (percentage that required bridge)
  - Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for pagerless alerts
  - % of pagerless incidents that later become S1/S2 (should be < 1%)

Postmortem and learning cadence
- Any pagerless incident that escalates to bridge must follow the standard postmortem template (timeline, detection path, root cause, action items).
- Quarterly synthesis: Operations synthesizes recurring pagerless themes and recommends runbook/alert tuning.

Runbook governance and review
- Owners must review Shadow Ops runbooks annually or after any escalated incident.
- Shadow Lead runs monthly quick-practice drills and reports drift or stale commands to the runbook owner.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for Shadow Ops (printable)
1. Read alert summary and incident stub.
2. Confirm recent deploys and top correlated traces.
3. Attempt quick mitigation (choose 1): restart-pool, enable-fallback, purge-prefix.
4. Update incident stub with time-stamped actions.
5. Observe for 10–30 minutes. If recovery, mark resolved-without-pager and close after observation window.
6. If criteria met, notify Shadow Lead and request bridge.

Appendix B — Runbook links and automation endpoints
- Incident tracker template: https://jira.internal/redwood/IR-XXXX
- Alert enrichment UI: https://opsui.internal.redwood/alerts/enriched
- Pagerless automation config (example):
  {
    "alert_type": "pagerless",
    "escalate_thresholds": {"error_rate_pct": 10, "slo_projection_minutes": 15},
    "shadow_ack_timeout_s": 180
  }

Contacts
- Shadow program owner: Maya Patel (pagerless@redwood.com)
- Shadow Lead rotation: see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rotation-schedule
- Incident commander escalation: ic-escalate@redwood.com

Revision history
- 2026-03-01: Created (Maya Patel)
- 2026-07-12: Added KV purge caution and expanded quick mitigation list (Liam Chen)
- 2026-11-15: Clarified escalation thresholds and added game-day template (Aisha Gomez)

payload.page_title: Error Budget Arbitration and Cross-Service Routing Runbook

sections.body: This runbook defines the procedures for arbitrating shared error budgets across multiple Redwood services, applying automated and manual traffic-routing policies, and documenting decisions during cross-service reliability events. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and service owners who operate multi-tenant or interdependent inference services (Hosted API, Dedicated routing, Private gateways).
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Ensure predictable, auditable decisions when error budgets are scarce.
- Provide a clear sequence of automated mitigations and human arbitration steps.
- Minimize customer impact while preserving critical SLAs for prioritized workloads.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Applies to services that either: (a) share a physical pool (GPU cluster, region) or (b) are connected by request routing policies (fallbacks, canaries, model variants).
- Not intended for pure data-plane failures (network fabric outages) — those follow incident runbooks.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Primary owner: SRE Platform (oncall rotation: platform-sre@example.redwood)
- Service owners: owning team for each affected service
- Arbitration lead: senior SRE on duty (escalation step after 20 minutes if automated mitigations insufficient)
- Executive stakeholder: Product reliability lead (notify for >2 hour service degradation or repeated arbitration events)
sections.heading: Owner / Roles

sections.body:
- Active SLO dashboards (per-service and pooled-resource level) with: availability, p95 latency, error rate
- Error budget ledger accessible in the Console and via API (ledger.redwood.internal/v1/error-budgets)
- Current routing policy manifests stored in git (infra/routing-policies/)
- Oncall Slack channel and incident channel templates ready: #sre-arbitration, #incident-<service>
sections.heading: Prerequisites / Telemetry to have available

sections.body:
1) If pooled error budget >20% remaining: allow standard autoscaling and routing fallbacks.
2) If pooled error budget between 5–20% remaining: apply automated conservative routing and inform arbitration lead.
3) If pooled error budget <5% remaining OR p95 latency >SLO x 2: trigger manual arbitration and progressive traffic reduction for least critical routes.
sections.heading: Decision matrix (abbreviated)

sections.body:
- Tier 0: AuthN/AuthZ, Billing, Control-plane (must be preserved when possible)
- Tier 1: Customer-facing inference endpoints with enterprise SLAs (Dedicated customers pinned to capacity)
- Tier 2: Public Hosted API free/low-tier routes, internal batch jobs, non-critical analytics
sections.heading: Priority tiers (for arbitration)

sections.body:
1) Throttle low-priority rate-limited keys by applying quota reduction policy (CLI example below).
2) Increase batching threshold for meeting non-latency-sensitive workloads using batching-flow controller.
3) Redirect traffic to quantized model variants for routes flagged as tolerant to quality tradeoffs.
4) Activate regional spillover: shift traffic from the hot region to healthy region(s) subject to data residency constraints.
sections.heading: Automated mitigations (order of operations)

sections.body:
- Reduce quota for a key (example):
  $ redwoodctl quotas update --key k_abc123 --qps 10 --reason "arb throttle: pooled EB <10%"

- Apply routing override (gitops manifest snippet, YAML):
  # infra/routing-policies/overrides/arb-2026-02-10.yaml
  routeOverrides:
    - service: inference-public-v1
      action: reduce-weight
      weight: 20
      reason: "arb - preserve Tier 1 capacity"
sections.heading: CLI & API examples

sections.body:
- Pooled error budget remaining (percent):
  sum(service:eb_remaining_percent{pool="gpu-eu-west"}) by (pool)
- If pooled_eb_percent < 10% for 10m -> fire arbitration-tier-warning alert (Severity: P2)
- If pooled_eb_percent < 5% for 5m or p95_latency > 2 * SLO for 5m -> fire arbitration-required (Severity: P1)
sections.heading: Prometheus queries and alerts to drive arbitration

sections.body:
1) Triage (0-10 minutes):
   - Acknowledge the alert in #sre-arbitration and create an incident stub (use /incident create).
   - Post initial private summary: affected pools, pooled EB %, top 3 impacted services, impact window estimate.
2) Gather (10-25 minutes):
   - Pull ledger entries for the last 24h for each service: (API: /v1/error-budgets/{service}/history)
   - Confirm if any enterprise Reserved Capacity blocks reductions (check Dedicated contracts dashboard).
   - List current routing overrides and canary rollouts that could be reverted.
3) Execute automated mitigations (25-40 minutes):
   - Apply the mitigations in the Automated mitigations section, smallest blast radius first.
   - Record each change in the incident notes (who, what, why, manifest commit hash).
4) Arbitration (40-90 minutes):
   - If mitigations insufficient, convene arbitration: service owners + arbitration lead + product SLA owner.
   - Use the Priority tiers table to evaluate candidate reductions.
   - Make a single explicit routing decision: e.g., reduce hosted-public weight by 40% and redirect to rate-limited queue.
   - Announce decision with timeline and rollback criteria.
sections.heading: Manual arbitration procedure (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Post-change verification window: 10 minutes for latency metrics, 30 minutes for error-rate stabilization.
- Rollback criteria (automated): if p95 increases > 20% after change or error budget consumption accelerates, revert manifest.
- Manual rollback: authorization required by arbitration lead and service owner. Document reason and time.

Post-event artifacts (what must be produced within 24 hours):
- Incident summary in Confluence (fill the Incident Evidence template). Include: timeline, decision log, manifest commits, cost impact estimate, and follow-ups.
- Update error-budget ledger with arbitration decisions (fields: decision_id, services_impacted, delta_eb_alloc, rationale).
- Open follow-up actions (Jira tickets) for remediation: capacity changes, SLA renegotiation, or automation improvements.
sections.heading: Rollback and verification

sections.body:
- Channel: #sre-arbitration
- Message:
  [ARBITRATION] Pool gpu-eu-west pooled_eb=3.2% -> reducing hosted-public weight by 35% to protect Tier1 Dedicated customers.
  Owner: @priya.menon, Action window: 40m, Rollback criteria: p95 > SLO * 1.2 after 10m.
  Commits: infra/routing-policies/overrides/arb-2026-02-10.yaml (sha: a1b2c3d)
sections.heading: Example arbitration message (Slack template)

sections.body:
- All arbitration decisions must be accompanied by a git manifest commit and at least one Restore/Undo manifest created at the time of change.
- Arbitration events that result in customer-visible degradation require a post-incident review (PIR) within 3 business days.
- Repeated arbitrations (>3 in a 30-day rolling window) trigger a Reliability Initiative and capacity remediation plan owned by SRE Platform + affected service teams.
sections.heading: Governance & auditability

sections.body:
- Auto-suggest routing overrides based on historical quality sensitivity (Q-Score) per route.
- A command to generate rollback manifest automatically when applying an override.
- Better ledger UI: show per-service contribution to pooled consumption and projected time-to-exhaustion under current trends.

Appendix: Sample SLO / Error budget table (example for an inference service)
| Metric | SLO | Window | Error budget (tokens) | Alert threshold |
|--------|-----|--------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| Availability | 99.95% | 30d | 435 min downtime | EB<10% -> warn |
| p95 latency | 350ms | 30d | N/A | p95>700ms -> P1 |
| 5xx error rate | 0.5% | 30d | 135k errors | EB<5% -> arbitration |
sections.heading: Automations to implement (roadmap items)

sections.body:
- Platform SRE Pager: +1-555-0110 (PagerDuty: platform-oncall)
- Arbitration Slack: #sre-arbitration
- Incident template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-template (use when creating the PIR)
sections.heading: Contacts and escalation links

sections.body: This runbook was authored to codify how we make tradeoffs when multiple services draw from shared capacity or pooled error budgets. The emphasis is on small blast-radius automation followed by rapid human arbitration with clear audit trails. The team should review this runbook quarterly and after any arbitration that required manual escalation.
sections.heading: Notes and rationale

sections.body:
- Error budget ledger API docs: /internal/api/error-budgets
- Routing policy gitops README: infra/routing-policies/README.md
- SLO definitions and ownership: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/slo-catalog
