payload.page_title: Incident Orchestration Decision Canvas and Runbook

sections.body:
Overview

This page documents a combined decision canvas and runnable playbook for on-call responders at Redwood Inference. The intent is to give a clear, SLO-driven decision process that: 1) shortens time-to-containment, 2) reduces noisy escalations, and 3) improves evidence collection for post-incident analysis. Use this page as the primary guide when an active incident affects customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, or Private control plane).

Scope

- Applies to incidents that impact latency, availability, correctness (quality regressions), or billing/quotas for inference endpoints.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks for deployment, onboarding, or infra reconfiguration; it is the orchestration layer to choose which runbook and communications path to use.

Quick facts and SLO thresholds (production)

- Availability SLO: 99.95% (per-region, 30d rolling).
- Latency SLO: p99 < 350ms for short-form generate endpoints; p99 < 700ms for long-sequence pipelines.
- Error budget alert: Trigger when 7-day rolling availability drops below 99.9% or error-rate increase > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.
- Severity mapping:
  - Sev-0: Global outage impacting >50% of traffic or all control plane requests – page exec & Exec Bridge.
  - Sev-1: Major degradation (SLO breach risk within 1 hour) impacting production customers – Incident Bridge.
  - Sev-2: Partial degradation or isolated customer impact – Slack triage and owner-led response.
  - Sev-3: Minor non-customer impacting issues, backlog tickets.

Roles & ownership

- First Responder (Pager): Acknowledge within 5 minutes. Primary responsibilities: initial triage, evidence collection, stabilize or escalate.
- Incident Lead (IL): Assumes orchestration for incident run until handoff. Owns timeline, communications cadence, and action tracking.
- Engineering SRE: Implements mitigations, applies capacity or routing changes, validates fallbacks.
- Product/CS Liaison: Drafts customer-facing messages and pulls impacted customer list.
- On-call Manager: Ensures correct escalation, rotates relievers if incident extends beyond shift.

Decision Canvas: How to pick the remediation path

Use the following questions in order. Answer quickly and use the branching guidance to select the right runbook and comms path.

1) Detect: Is this an alert (automated) or a customer report?
  - If alert and metric crosses severity thresholds (see Quick facts), continue.
  - If customer report and localized: start Sev-2 triage; verify scope via request logs.

2) Scope: Is impact region-wide or customer-scoped?
  - Region-wide -> consider routing, capacity, or control-plane failure runbooks.
  - Customer-scoped -> follow escalation matrix to platform & account teams; consider temporary exception or throttling.

3) Velocity: Is the degradation rapidly worsening (exponential error growth or rising latency trend)?
  - If yes -> escalate to Incident Lead and open a dedicated bridge.

4) Containment feasibility: Can we reduce blast radius with routing flags, model-fallback, or circuit-breakers?
  - If yes -> implement containment (see Containment steps). If not, escalate to infrastructure leads.

5) Recovery path: Is a fast rollback or failover available (canary rollback, previous model version, or alternate region)?
  - If yes -> run Recovery Execution template.
  - If no -> run Mitigation & Stabilization template and plan RTO > 1 hour.

Runbook templates (copyable blocks)

A) Containment (apply immediately if feasible)
1. Toggle prefix/KV cache passthrough for the affected model pool (console CLI: redwood cache set --pool <pool> --mode passthrough).
2. Apply route-level throttles to limit new sessions to 30% of normal traffic for the affected pool.
3. Activate model-fallback: route low-priority traffic to quantized/compatible variant.
4. If OOM or GPU errors present, drain impacted nodes from serving group and shift traffic to standby capacity.

B) Recovery Execution (rollback/failover)
1. Verify available previous model or deployment snapshot timestamped in the catalog.
2. Initiate canary rollback using the Console: rollouts create --service <svc> --target <version> --canary 10%.
3. Monitor p95/p99 latency and error-rate for 5 minutes. If stable, ramp to 50% for 3m, then full.
4. If rollback fails, revert and fallback to circuit-breaker + staging capacity.

C) Mitigation & Stabilization (when rollback not possible)
1. Temporarily increase autoscale target for Dedicated pools by +25% (owner: infra).
2. Reduce model max_tokens/sequence on heavy pipelines to reduce per-request work.
3. Enable degraded-mode responses: include structured field "warning": "degraded_serving" for downstream clients.
4. Open ticket for engineering change and assign immediate action items with owners and ETA.

Containment checklist (evidence to collect before modifying production)

- Incident timestamp, originating alert ID, scope (regions/tenants), and request sample.
- Relevant metric graphs (latency p50/p95/p99, errors, qps) and trace ids for 3 sample requests across affected timeframe.
- Cluster/node logs (stderr/stdout), GPU OOM messages, scheduler traces.

Status page & customer comms templates

Use these templates on the Status Page (internal canonical copy) and for customer emails/CS messages. Personalize the placeholders (<...>).

Initial acknowledgement (public status page and customer CS)
"We are aware of an issue affecting the Redwood inference API in <region>. Our engineering team is investigating. Impact: increased latency and request failures for some customers. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Reference: <incident-id>."

Status update (20-60 minute cadence while active)
"Update: Engineering identified a high-error-rate condition tied to <root_cause_short>. We’ve applied a containment step to reduce customer impact by <percent_reduction>% and are validating service behavior. Next update in 30 minutes or after major progress. Impacted customers: <list or 'subset of customers'>. Reference: <incident-id>."

Resolution (final)
"Resolved: The issue affecting inference requests in <region> has been resolved at <time>. Root cause: <short_rca>. Mitigation: <actions taken>. If you continue to experience problems, please contact support with reference <incident-id>. A technical postmortem will be published to customers within 48 hours if they were materially affected."

Internal incident comms cadence (recommended)
- 0-10m: Acknowledgement to core Slack incident channel and create bridge.
- 10-30m: First status update with containment steps completed.
- Every 30m while active: update with metrics and current next-action.
- On resolution: brief summary and link to postmortem draft.

On-call rotation, escalation matrix and shadowing

- Primary responder: 8-hour rotation (08:00–16:00; 16:00–00:00; 00:00–08:00). Relievers shadow for first 48h of a long-running incident.
- Escalation contact order: Primary Pager -> On-call team lead -> SRE Principal -> Head of Infra. Contact details are maintained in the oncall roster.
- Shadowing policy: New responders shadow for 2 full shifts and run tabletop drills before independent paging.

Game days and readiness drills

- Frequency: Quarterly game days per region; monthly tabletop for new hires.
- Exercise types: network partition simulation, multi-model quality regression, capacity exhaustion, and downstream dependency failure.
- Scoring: time-to-detect, time-to-contain, customer-impact reduction, and completeness of evidence collected.

Postmortem and action tracking (must-haves)

1. Postmortem timeline with timestamps for detection, triage, containment, full recovery, and communications.
2. Root cause analysis: a clear causal chain (not just symptoms).
3. Corrective actions: owner, ETA, and verification steps.
4. Customer impact summary and whether credits/notifications are required.
5. Postmortem review meeting scheduled within 7 days and linked in the document.

Evidence collection template (minimum)

- Alert IDs and monitoring graphs (PNG links).
- 3 representative request traces with full call-stack and headers redacted.
- Configuration snapshot (model version, routing rules, autoscale parameters).
- Deployment history for last 24 hours.

When to convert to a public postmortem

- Convert when > 10% of customers or any enterprise customer experienced latency or failures for more than 1 hour, or if the incident required a region-level failover. Publish a customer-facing summary within 48 hours and a full internal RCA within 7 days.

Operational notes & dos-and-don’ts

- Do: Keep the Incident Lead role single-threaded for coordination.
- Do: Avoid broad-spectrum rollbacks without canary validation.
- Do: Use structured ‘degraded-mode’ flags in responses to allow downstream graceful degradation.
- Don’t: Make unilateral security or data-retention changes during an incident.
- Don’t: Use the status page for internal technical noise; keep it high level and customer-centric.

Appendix: CLI snippets and common commands

- Create bridge: redwood bridge create --incident <incident-id> --severity <sev> --owner <il-name>
- Toggle model fallback: redwood routes update --route <route> --fallback-version <id>
- Snapshot deployment: redwood deployments snapshot --service <svc> --out /tmp/snapshot-<ts>.json

Related pages and references

- SLO and error budgeting guidance: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2024
- Incident lifecycle templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-lifecycle-orchestration-templates-2025
- Runbook maintenance policy: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-retention-and-responder-onboarding-handbook-2026

Document maintenance

- Owner: Engineering (oncall-playbooks squad). Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev-1 incident.
- Last reviewed: 2025-02-03.

End of document."

payload.page_title: On-call Accountability Guide and Escalation Scenarios

sections.body: This document defines who is accountable during incidents, concrete escalation scenarios, triage and remediation checklists, on-call rotation guidance, and reproducible game day exercises. It is intended for engineers, SREs, and on-call responders who will execute runbooks and communicate with internal and external stakeholders.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services (api.redwood.internal, inference-gw, router, kv-cache).
- Covers severity classification, primary/secondary responsibilities, escalation paths, status page updates, and post-incident follow-up.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks (links in Related pages).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Act with ownership: responders should act until a handoff is explicit.
- Fast, clear communication: update channels every 15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1 until recovery.
- Avoid cognitive overload: prefer escalation to an IC when scope grows beyond one responder.
sections.heading: Principles (short)

sections.body:
1) Detection & Alerting: PagerDuty alerts + automated monitoring (CloudWatch/Prometheus).
2) Triage (first 10 minutes): confirm scope, impact, and assign primary responder.
3) Containment (15–60 minutes): mitigate customer impact (fallbacks, routing, scale-up).
4) Remediation (hours): deploy fixes, rollbacks, or configuration changes.
5) Recovery confirmation: validate SLOs and monitor for regressions.
6) Post-incident: blameless postmortem, RCA, and action items.
sections.heading: Incident lifecycle (high level)

sections.body:
- Primary Responder (PR): first engineer to acknowledge alert. Responsibilities: collect logs, run triage checklist, apply short-term mitigations, own incident channel.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates multi-team activity for Sev0/Sev1. Responsibilities: communication cadence, prioritization, deciding customer comms, engagement of execs if needed.
- SRE Owner: owns platform-level remediations (autoscaling, capacity, network).
- Service Lead / Oncall SME: subject-matter expert for the affected service.
- Communications Lead: drafts external status updates and customer notifications.
- Postmortem Author: writes the formal incident report.
sections.heading: Roles & responsibilities

sections.body:
- Sev0 (P0) — System-wide critical outage: >50% of requests failing or >90% latency regression across regions for >5 minutes. Action: immediate IC, executive notification.
- Sev1 (P1) — Customer-impacting outage: significant subset of customers degraded (>10%). Action: IC if escalation needed; hourly exec updates after 1 hour.
- Sev2 (P2) — Partial degradation: single region or non-critical functionality affected. Action: PR-led containment, oncall SME engaged.
- Sev3 (P3) — Minor impact: edge errors, limited customers, or operational tasks. Action: ticketation and fix during normal hours.
sections.heading: Severity definitions and thresholds

sections.body:
| Trigger / Time | Primary responder action | If unresolved after | Escalate to | Channel |
|----------------|-------------------------|---------------------|-------------|---------|
| PagerDuty alert acknowledged | Run triage checklist | 10 minutes | Service Lead | #svc-<name>-incidents |
| Impact confirmed (Sev1/Sev0) | Call an IC and create incident channel | 15 minutes | Incident Commander | #incidents |
| No progress on mitigation | Notify SRE Owner, request capacity increase/fallback | 30 minutes | Platform Oncall | #sre-oncall |
| Exec notification required | IC to inform Head of Eng & CEO | 60 minutes (Sev0) | Exec on-call | direct pager/email |
sections.heading: Escalation matrix (text table)

sections.body:
- Confirm what is failing (API endpoints, model quality, embeddings, telemetry).
- Confirm blast radius (regions, accounts, routes).
- Check recent deploys/rollouts (Console rollouts page).
- Capture logs and span traces: link to the tracing session and relevant logs.
- Verify capacity signals: GPU utilization, queue depth, OOMs.
- Apply immediate mitigations: route to fallback model, scale replicas, enable read-only mode.
- Create incident channel and update PagerDuty incident with notes and links.

Runbook starter (generic, can be copy-pasted into service runbooks):
1) Validate alert: `kubectl get pods -n <ns>`; `kubectl logs -f <pod>`; `curl -sv https://api.redwood.internal/health`
2) Check autoscaling: `kubectl describe hpa <svc>` or `cloudctl describe autoscaler <svc>`
3) Check GPU health: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` (on-host) or open telemetry panels.
4) Roll back recent deploy: follow CI/CD rollback docs; prefer config toggles if possible.
5) Apply circuit-breaker: update router config to reduce new sessions to degraded path.
6) If kernel OOMs: capture core and escalate to infra kernel team.
sections.heading: Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

sections.body:
Scenario A — Inference gateway returning 500s across region after a config rollout:
- Triage: PR checks recent rollout id (Console) -> matches 12:05 deploy.
- Action: Immediately rollback to prior revision (CI/CD rollback step).
- Escalation: If rollback fails in 15 minutes, IC calls SRE Owner to route traffic to standby region and open cloud provider ticket.
- Customer comms: initial status set to "investigating" within 20 minutes, follow-up every 30 minutes until recovery.

Scenario B — Model quality regression (higher hallucinations) observed by automated evals:
- Triage: Confirm eval set regressions and ratio of affected requests.
- Action: Pin customers to verified model version; disable auto-routing to the new model.
- Escalation: Notify ML model onboarding and product leads if >5% error rate.
- Customer comms: targeted notification to affected customers via email template (see example).

Scenario C — Network partition between control plane and VPC-hosted private deployment:
- Triage: Confirm routes and BGP sessions, check VPC flow logs.
- Action: Failover to Private control plane snapshot or instruct customer to use local endpoints per private deployment runbook.
- Escalation: Engage Private deployments oncall and account owner.
sections.heading: Example escalation scenarios (concrete)

sections.body:
- Internal updates (Sev0/Sev1): every 15 minutes until containment; every 30 minutes during remediation.
- External status page cadence: initial update within 20 minutes, follow-ups at 40 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours, and when resolved.
sections.heading: Communication cadence and templates

sections.body:
- Initial short update (public status page):
  Subject: Incident — API request failures affecting <region>
  Body: "We are investigating increased error rates for the Redwood API impacting <region>. Our engineers are actively triaging. We will provide an update by <time>. Impact: some requests may fail with 500 errors."

- Targeted customer email (example):
  Subject: Service interruption affecting your Redwood inference requests
  Body: "Hi <CustomerName>, we’re investigating an issue impacting inference requests in <region>. We’ve rolled back a deployment and are monitoring recovery. No customer data exposure has been detected. We’ll follow up within 60 minutes. If you have immediate concerns, reply or open a ticket at <support link>."

- Post-resolution update:
  Body: "The issue has been resolved by <action taken>. We are completing a post-incident review; a preliminary RCA will be published within 72 hours. We apologize for the impact."

Escalation call templates (IC -> Exec):
- Short briefing format (5 lines):
  1) What happened (time, services affected).
  2) Current impact (customers, % requests failing, business exposure).
  3) What we’ve done (mitigations applied).
  4) Next steps and ETA.
  5) Decision needed from execs (if any).
sections.heading: Status page & customer message templates (placeholders)

sections.body:
- Shifts: weekly rotations for SREs and service oncalls (Mon 9am local).
- Handoff notes: outgoing oncall must post a handoff message with known issues, active incidents, and monitoring dashboards. Use the template in the team wiki.
- Handoff checklist:
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule membership.
  - Confirm Slack notification routing.
  - Verify telemetry dashboards are accessible.
  - List ongoing work that may affect availability (ongoing rollouts, infra changes).
sections.heading: On-call rotation and handoff guidance

sections.body:
- Objective: validate the incident lifecycle, communication cadence, and runbook efficacy; measure time-to-detect and time-to-recover.
- Frequency: quarterly for SRE, semi-annual per service owner.
- Roles: designate a facilitator, observers (measurements), responders (rotate).
- Example exercises:
  1) Simulated config rollout causing 50% error rate — test rollback and cross-region failover.
     - Success criteria: rollback completed <15 minutes, public status updated in <20 minutes.
  2) Artificial model-quality regression — test model pinning and customer notifications.
     - Success criteria: affected customers identified and pinned within 30 minutes.
  3) Control plane latency spike — test alerting thresholds and IC activation.
     - Success criteria: IC created and incident channel opened within 10 minutes.
- Post-game-day: produce a short report with timings, gaps, and action items.
sections.heading: Game day exercise playbook (reproducible)

sections.body:
- Incident triage note posted to incident channel within 1 hour.
- Preliminary RCA summary published within 72 hours (draft by IC + responders).
- Full postmortem (blameless) published within 7 days with owners for each action item and deadlines.
- Action items tracked in the engineering backlog and reviewed in the next team retro.
sections.heading: Post-incident process and timelines

sections.body:
- Time to acknowledge (target <5 min).
- Time to containment (target P0 <30 min, P1 <60 min).
- Time to recovery (target P0 <2 hours).
- Number of pages per incident.
- Communication latency (time between incident detection and first public update).
sections.heading: Operational metrics to track per incident

sections.body:
- ICs and PRs should nominate at least one deep action item for each Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- The SRE management team consolidates recurring action items into quarterly reliability initiatives.
sections.heading: Ownership and continuous improvement

sections.body:
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/api-gateway-recovery
- /confluence/eng-platform/incident-command-cheat-sheet
- /confluence/eng-infra/capacity-scaling-guidelines

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and runbook links
- Rollback (CI): `ci rollback --service inference-gw --to-revision <rev>`
- Create incident channel: `/incident create \"<short title>\" --severity P1` (Slack bot)
- PagerDuty escalation: `pd incidents acknowledge <id>`
- Example logs query (ELK): `timestamp:[now-15m TO now] AND status:500 AND service:inference-gw`
sections.heading: Related pages (examples)

sections.body:
- Owner: eng-sre (policy owner); please review annually or after any Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- For edits: submit a PR to the Confluence doc with reviewers listed above.

payload.page_title: Operational Playbook: Unified Runloop and Postmortem Rubric

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook defines a single, auditable runloop for incidents at Redwood Inference that unifies: on-call rotations, bridge/bridge-operator responsibilities, runbook-driven remediation steps, game-day simulations, status page messaging, and a measurable postmortem quality rubric. The goal is predictable, low-friction incident handling and continuous improvement across SRE, Serving, and Platform teams.

Audience and scope
- Primary: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Core Product engineers on pager.
- Secondary: Support/Customer Success for customer comms and account escalation.
- Applies to: service availability, latency SLO regressions, data-path correctness (prefix/KV cache), capacity exhaustion, and control plane failures.

Key definitions
- Runloop Operator: the person running the live bridge, responsible for status updates and coordination.
- Bridge Channel: #incident-ops (Slack) and dedicated Zoom bridge.
- Tiered SLO classes: Critical (SLO 99.99), High (99.95), Standard (99.9).
- Severity mapping:
  1. Sev0 — complete outage for >= 5% customers or global control-plane failure.
  2. Sev1 — significant degradation (P95 latency > 2x SLO or error rate causing user-visible failures).
  3. Sev2 — partial impact to subset of customers or non-critical functionality.

Incident lifecycle (high-level runloop)
1) Acknowledge (0-5 minutes)
   - Pagered engineer acknowledges in-monitoring alert and posts in #incident-ops with short summary: service, symptoms, first-detected timestamp.
   - Runloop Operator opens incident in our incident tracker (use template: incident.create --service <name> --class <Critical|High|Standard>).
2) Triage and classification (5-15 minutes)
   - Confirm scope (region, model family, customer subset).
   - Map to SLO class and set severity. If severity escalation is needed, page SRE lead and product on-call.
3) Containment (15-60 minutes)
   - Execute targeted runbook for the symptom (see example runbooks below).
   - If no runbook exists, capture steps attempted and enable mitigation flags (traffic shaping, heavier caching, temporary fallback model) per policy.
4) Restoration (30-180 minutes)
   - Restore service incrementally where possible. Validate with synthetic traffic and user-facing checks.
   - Update status page (see templates) every 30 minutes for critical incidents until mitigated.
5) Remediation and fix tracking (within 72 hours)
   - Assign remediation owner and open a ticket in the remediation tracker. High-severity incidents require a remediation plan within 7 calendar days.
6) Post-incident review (within 3 business days)
   - Postmortem draft in Confluence using the template in this doc. Use the Postmortem Quality Rubric for acceptance.

Runbook examples (copyable templates)
- Symptom: Regional 5xx spike for model inference (Region: us-west-2)\  1. Verify metrics: errors by model, host, and region (cli: redwood-metrics query --metric inference_errors --by host,model,region).\  2. If host-level error rate > 20% for a host group, drain new requests from that host pool: redwood-ctl pool drain --pool <pool-id>.\  3. If KV-cache errors visible in logs, flip prefix-cache-rollover flag: redwood-config set prefix_cache_fallback=true.\  4. If rollout-related (new model variant), rollback to previous variant via canary rollback: redwood-deploy rollback --model <model-id> --version previous.\  5. Validate with synthetic load (curl -sS https://internal-health/model_probe | jq .latency)

- Symptom: Progressive P95 latency increase (SLO class: High)\
  1. Check batching histogram and queue lengths on serving nodes. Look for sustained queueing (Q > 8ms per request).\  2. Temporarily reduce max_batch_size for impacted model: redwood-ctl model-config set --model <id> max_batch_size=8.\  3. If latency persists, enable local-prefetch cache and measure effect.\  4. If under capacity stress, trigger autoscale burst: redwood-scale trigger --pool <dedicated-pool> --burst 20%.

Severity decision ladder (quick checklist)
- Sev0: Trigger Exec review, page CTO, activate customer war room. Update status page within first 10 minutes.
- Sev1: Page SRE lead and Product on-call. Bridge Operator posts status every 30 minutes.
- Sev2: Triage on-call only; cadence 60–120 minutes for customer comms.

On-call rotation and expectations
- Rotation model: Primary (7-day shift) + Secondary (7-day shadow) per platform region.
- Handover: Daily standup in #oncall-handoff at 09:00 local; handover note must contain outstanding incidents, maintenance windows, and noisy alerts.\- Escalation contacts:
  - Primary on-call: pager (primary), slack DM, phone.
  - Secondary on-call: notified after 15 minutes if acknowledgement not seen.\  - Engineering lead: notified if issue unresolved for 60 minutes or severity upgraded.
- Time commitment: expected to be available within 15 minutes of pager during shift; long-running restoration requires rotation swapping with lead agreement.

Game-day simulation guide (quarterly schedule)
- Frequency: Quarterly full-team simulation + monthly micro-sims for critical subsystems.
- Typical 4-hour game-day agenda:
  1. 0:00 — Inject: synthetic degradation (e.g., region blobstore latency and KV cache evictions).
  2. 0:05 — Pager triggers and primary acknowledges.
  3. 0:10 — Bridge stands up and status page skeleton posted.
  4. 0:20 — Engineering executes runbook or improvises mitigation.
  5. 1:30 — Restore and validate; runbook updates captured.
  6. 2:00 — Post-game retro using postmortem rubric; assign follow-ups.
- Scoring: time-to-ack, time-to-first-status-post, time-to-restoration, and quality of postmortem (rubric score).

Status page and customer comms templates
- Status page cadence: initial acknowledgement within 10 minutes for Sev0/Sev1, subsequent updates every 30 minutes for Sev0 and 60 minutes for Sev1.
- Status update template (short):
  - Title: Partial degradation of inference API in us-west-2\
  - Incident ID: INC-2025-####\
  - Time: 2025-07-14T15:10Z\
  - Summary: We’re investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting inference requests in us-west-2. Root cause under investigation.\
  - Impact: Some customers experience increased errors and higher latency. Persisting requests may be retried automatically by SDKs.\
  - Next update: 2025-07-14T15:40Z\
  - Contacts: support@redwood.ai for account-specific concerns.
- Customer severity email (when incident hits paid customers):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Impact (INC-2025-####)\
  Body: Dear <Customer>,\n\  We are investigating an issue affecting inference latency and error rates for requests routed to us-west-2. Our on-call and platform engineers are actively mitigating the issue. We will provide updates at least every 30 minutes until resolved. For urgent account-level concerns, please reply to this message or reach out to support@redwood.ai.\n\  — The Redwood Inference Team

Postmortem Quality Rubric (acceptance criteria)
- Sections required: Summary, Timeline (UTC), Detection, Impact, Root Cause Analysis, Containment & Recovery steps, Remediation plan, Owner(s), Action items with due dates, Follow-up verification plan.\- Rubric scoring (0-4 scale per criterion):
  1. Completeness (required sections present) — 0..4\  2. Timeline fidelity (timestamps and evidence links) — 0..4\  3. RCA quality (one true root cause, not multiple surface causes) — 0..4\  4. Mitigation clarity (playbook or config changes captured) — 0..4\  5. Remediation tracking (owner & due date assigned) — 0..4\  6. Preventative engineering (tests/monitoring added) — 0..4\- Acceptance threshold: total >= 18 out of 24 for publication to the learning archive. If score < 18, PM/owner must iterate within 5 business days.

Remediation tracker (text table)
| ID | Owner | Type | Due | Status |
| R-2025-001 | Priya Nair | Config change (prefix-cache) | 2025-07-21 | In progress |
| R-2025-002 | Miguel Alvarez | Scale policy update | 2025-07-28 | Open |
| R-2025-003 | Ruth Kim | Integration test (model rollback) | 2025-08-04 | Open |

Evidence collection checklist
- Collect: alert IDs, raw request IDs, host logs (rotate to secure bucket), metrics query ranges, API traces, and the first-detection signal.\- Standard CLI commands to capture evidence:
  - redwood-logs fetch --service inference --since 2025-07-14T15:00Z --filter "error" > /tmp/inference-errors.log\  - redwood-metrics query --metric request_latency --agg p95 --from 2025-07-14T14:30Z --to 2025-07-14T16:00Z > /tmp/latency-p95.csv\  - redwood-traces export --span inference --txn <trace-id> --out /tmp/trace.json

Governance and SLAs for follow-ups
- High-severity remediation plan posted: within 7 calendar days.\- Code/infra fixes targeted for merge within 30 days and rollout within 60 days unless exception granted by SRE Manager.
- Quarterly summary of published postmortems and outstanding remediations shared with leadership.

Runbook hygiene and ownership
- Each team owning a service must maintain runbooks in this directory with explicit owner and last-verified date.
- Runbooks are validated in every quarterly game-day; failures in runbook efficacy require an immediate runbook update and a follow-up ticket.

Appendix: quick checklists and contact matrix
- Quick triage checklist (for first responder):
  1. Acknowledge and declare bridge.
  2. Identify affected region(s)/model(s).
  3. Confirm severity and page escalation if needed.\ 4. Post initial status.
- Contact matrix (order):
  1. Primary on-call (pager).
  2. Secondary on-call (after 15 min).\ 3. SRE Lead (after 60 min or immediate for Sev0).

Notes and change log
- 2025-02-10: Playbook created by Priya Nair.
- 2025-07-14: Added postmortem rubric and remediation SLAs; updated status templates to require 30-minute cadence for Sev0.

Related resources
- Template: incident.postmortem.template (Confluence)

payload.page_title: Staged restoration schedule and customer quiet-window templates (2026)

sections.body: This document describes Redwood's staged restoration approach for multi-service incidents, the associated quiet-window practice for customer communications, and reusable status page and customer templates. It codifies responsibilities, timing windows, verification gates, and escalation thresholds to reduce noisy updates during large recoveries while preserving transparency and compliance.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Restore customer-facing functionality in prioritized stages with safety gates.
- Reduce customer confusion and churn by consolidating updates into structured quiet windows.
- Provide ready-to-send status and email templates to minimize drafting time during incidents.
- Ensure on-call teams have clear verification checklists and rollback criteria.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body: This playbook applies to incidents impacting Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, console availability, or billing/usage reporting services. Use for partial or full degradations where staggered restoration reduces blast radius.
sections.heading: Applicability

sections.body:
1) Primary on-call (Responder): initial triage, mitigation, and first updates.
2) Secondary (Support): service-level mitigation and cross-team coordination.
3) Incident Commander (IC): orchestrates staged restoration schedule, approves quiet windows, makes go/no-go decisions.
4) Communications owner: drafts status and customer emails using templates below.
sections.heading: Key roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Error rate > 5% for > 3 minutes on critical route -> urgent incident (stage 0).
- Median latency > 750ms for > 10 minutes -> consider partial throttling and stage-based recovery.
- Token processing backlog > 10 minutes average -> trigger cache warmup and staged capacity increase.
sections.heading: SLO and threshold triggers for staged restoration

sections.body:
Phase 0 — Containment (0–20 minutes):
- Reduce blast radius: disable autoscaling policies that exacerbate thrash, apply circuit breakers per service.
- Short customer notice: initial status posted (see template A).
- IC assignment mandatory.

Phase 1 — Stabilize core control plane (20–60 minutes):
- Restore control-plane APIs and monitoring; ensure events are flowing.
- Verify internal health checks:
  - kubectl get pods -n <namespace> -l app=<service> --field-selector=status.phase=Running
  - curl -sS https://internal-health/<service>/live | grep OK
- If checks fail, remain in containment and escalate to platform infra.

Phase 2 — Gradual customer traffic re-introduction (60–180 minutes):
- Reopen traffic for low-priority routes or small customer cohorts (canary groups).
- Monitor KPIs for 3x the usual check interval before widening.
- Execute cache/KV warmups and pre-populate common prompt prefixes where applicable.

Phase 3 — Bulk restore + verification (3–12 hours):
- Progressive scaling to full capacity with automated throttling fallback.
- Run synthetic workload sweep: 50 requests/min across top 100 prompt templates.
- Confirm error rate below 1% and P95 latency within SLOs before marking restored.

Phase 4 — Closure and follow-up (>12 hours):
- Publish final status and postmortem timeline.
- Coordinate with Customer Success for high-touch outreach.
sections.heading: Staged restoration phases (recommended cadence)

sections.body:
- Definition: A quiet window is a pre-approved time window during active restoration where customer-facing updates are batched to reduce churn and confusion.
- Typical cadence: IC approves quiet windows of 30–90 minutes during phases 1–3.
- When to use: multi-service rollouts, cascading capacity throttles, or when frequent partial changes would create contradictory messages.
- Exceptions: security incidents, legal/regulatory impacts, or new PII exposures always require immediate notification.
sections.heading: Quiet-window practice (purpose and cadence)

sections.body:
- Communications owner posts an initial notice that updates will be provided at fixed intervals (e.g., every 60 minutes) and lists the next expected update time.
- Emergency channel (internal Slack #incident-critical) remains open for internal stakeholders and affected large customers.
- If situation materially changes (customer data exposure, full outage of SLA-bound service), quiet window is lifted and immediate update sent.
sections.heading: Quiet-window rules

sections.body:
- Title line: short and factual (e.g., "Degraded: Inference API elevated error rate").
- Affected services: list with product-impact tags (API, Console, Billing).
- Impact: brief customer-facing description and user-facing symptoms.
- Current status: staging phase and expected next update time.
- Actions underway: short bullet points of mitigation.
- Owner and contact: names and ‘urgent’ contact link or email.

Template A — Initial status page (short):
- Title: "Investigating: Increased error rate for /v1/generate"
- Body: "We are aware of elevated error rates for text generation requests. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We'll post updates every 60 minutes or sooner if there is a material change."
- Next update: ISO timestamp

Template B — Quiet-window update (scheduled):
- Title: "Monitoring: Partial recovery in canary cohort"
- Body: "We have reintroduced a fraction of traffic to a small cohort and are monitoring key metrics (error rate, P95 latency). No action required from customers. Next scheduled update in 60 minutes."

Template C — Customer email (high-touch):
- Subject: "Redwood incident update — [short description] — ongoing"
- Greeting: "Hello <CustomerName>,\nOur engineering team is currently restoring service for <affected feature>. We understand the impact and are prioritizing your traffic. The next planned update is at <time>. For questions, reply to this message and your account team will respond."
sections.heading: Status page messages (components)

sections.body:
- Synthetic test sweep: all 200-sample requests return successful status.
- Telemetry sanity: error rate < 1% for 30 minutes, P95 latency within SLO.
- KV/Cache warm: tail-latency stable and cache-hit rate > 85%.
- Billing/usage reporting validated for delayed batches.
sections.heading: Verification checklist (pre-announce stage completion)

sections.body:
- Any major customer cohort reports repeated errors > 3 occurrences in 10 minutes.
- Error rate doubles or P95 increases > 50% relative to baseline during widening.
- Unrecoverable dependencies fail health checks.
sections.heading: Rollback / abort criteria during staged rollouts

sections.body:
- Run an annual staged-restoration game day with a simulated cross-region capacity loss. Include communications drills for quiet-window templates.
- Success metrics: time to first canary traffic (< 90 minutes), mean time to full restore (target < 6 hours), and correctness of status messaging (peer-reviewed).
sections.heading: Game day and training guidance

sections.body:
1) Record timeline with exact timestamps for each phase change.
2) Assign action owners and target remediation dates.
3) Include communications audit: what updates were sent and to which customers.
4) Retrospective game-day to validate changes if remediation impacts operational playbook.
sections.heading: Post-incident actions and postmortem checklist

sections.body:
- Link: internal runbook index (search: "staged restore").
- Link: incident-comm-templates collection.

Appendix: quick health-check commands and samples:
- Check core pods: kubectl get pods -n inference -l tier=backend
- Perform a synthetic generation: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
- Verify queue depth: curl -s https://internal-metrics/queues | jq '.inference_queue.depth'
sections.heading: Related links and references

sections.body:
- 2024-11-12: created by Aisha Malik (initial draft).
- 2025-06-03: added quiet-window templates and verification gates (reviewed by Daniel Park).
- 2026-02-03: formalized SLO thresholds and game-day guidance (approved).

payload.page_title: Stability Ops Accelerator and Operator Runloop

sections.body:
Overview
========
This document defines the Stability Ops Accelerator: a compact, operator-focused incident process and runloop optimized for model-serving platforms. It consolidates the incident lifecycle, operator runbooks, rotation scheduling rules, game-day scenarios, status page automation patterns, and customer comm templates into a single, prescriptive reference intended for SREs, service owners, and response engineers.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood inference production services (hosted, dedicated, private control plane).
- Covers incidents that affect latency, throughput, correctness (model quality), and availability of inference endpoints.
- Excludes: deployment planning, long-term roadmap decisions, and non-production labs.

Quick summary (one-line)
------------------------
When an SLO or customer-impacting signal trips, follow the 3-stage runloop: Acknowledge -> Contain -> Restore; escalate using the Ordered Escalation Ladder; use templates to drive customer comms and capture evidence for the postmortem quality gate.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Operator (primary responder): owns initial acknowledgement, triage, and executing containment runbook steps.
- Bridge lead (senior SRE): orchestrates cross-team coordination, external comms, and decisions about rollbacks/fallbacks.
- Service owner (team lead): approves high-impact changes, provides product context and customer impact assessment.
- On-call escalation tier (tier-2/3): provides specialist remediation (runtime kernels, model variants, infra).
- Incident comms owner (customer success / bridge lead): drafts status page and customer messages.

Incident lifecycle (detailed steps)
----------------------------------
1) Alert & acknowledge (T+0 to T+5)
   - Pager triggers; operator acknowledges within 5 minutes.
   - Record the alert ID and initial hypothesis in the incident channel.
2) Initial triage (T+0 to T+15)
   - Confirm customer impact using metrics: requests/sec, 95/99 latency, error rate, tokens/sec, KV-cache hit rate.
   - Classify severity (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) using definition table below.
3) Containment (T+15 to T+60)
   - Apply immediate mitigations from containment runbooks (scale up, fallback to cheaper model, activate read-only caches, rate-limit or burst-throttle ingress).
   - If multi-region, failover policy executes per the routing playbook.
4) Restoration (T+1h onward)
   - Implement targeted fixes (kernel/driver restart, cache purge+warm, model rollback, config patch).
   - Run smoke tests on a controlled traffic slice; slowly ramp traffic back using canary policy.
5) Stabilize & close (post-restoration)
   - Confirm SLOs are restored for a minimum observation window (30–60 minutes).
   - Collect evidence, save logs, and open a postmortem.

Severity classification (reference)
----------------------------------
| SEV | Symptom examples | Customer impact threshold | Immediate action |
|-----|------------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| SEV1 | Total outage for >3% of active tenants in a region | Customer API returns 5xx or no responses | Bridge, exec-notify, global failover |
| SEV2 | Latency spike >2x baseline for 10+ minutes for high QPS endpoints | Significant degradation for key customers | Containment runbooks, regional failover |
| SEV3 | Single-tenant QoS regression or degraded quality for low traffic | Isolated impact, elevated errors | Owner triage, scheduled fix window |

Runbook catalog (core entries)
-----------------------------
- model-serving-degradation: latency and cold-KV-cache runbook
  - Symptoms: 95th latency increasing, KV-cache hit rate < 70%, CPU on worker nodes > 90%
  - Immediate steps: switch to reduced-length generation model variant; enable prefix caching; increase batch timeout to 25ms
  - Escalation: owner -> runtime-kernels -> infra-networking

- kernel-crash-and-oom: node-level fatal errors and OOMs
  - Symptoms: pod restarts, CUDA OOM logs, kernel-level crashes in /var/log
  - Immediate steps: cordon node, restart runtime on new worker, purge large KV entries, set eviction policy to LRU-fast

- ttl-cache-poisoning: corrupted prefix or evicted warm cache causing repeated slow-paths
  - Steps: rotate cache namespace, run controlled rewarm script, throttle traffic to rewarm target nodes

Example runbook table (condensed)
--------------------------------
- Name: model-serving-degradation
  Owner: eng-serving-runtime
  Pager: #oncall-ml-serving
  Primary mitigation: model-variant-fallback, KV-cache-rewarm
  Time-to-contain target: 30 min

Rotation scheduling and fairness rules
------------------------------------
- Primary constraint: no engineer should have more than one critical pager shift within a 7-day window.
- Shift length: 8-hour blocks for primary operators; 24-hour for tiered on-call (overlap handoff at 08:00 UTC).
- Swap rules: allow one self-swap per 30-day period; swaps must be recorded in the oncall roster and approved by rotation owner.
- Auto-scheduling algorithm (summary): round-robin across on-call pool with weighted fairness (weights by recent load: recent-shifts*1.2). This yields ~10% bias to less-burned responders to maintain knowledge spread.

Game days: scenarios and rubrics
--------------------------------
Purpose: validate operator runloop, cross-team handoffs, and containment runbooks. Rundays are quarterly.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- KV cache warm-loss: synthetic traffic removes cache entries and forces cold paths (focus: cache rewarm, traffic shaping).
- Multi-model-fallback stress: primary model overloaded, require fallback and correctness checks (focus: A/B routing, quality regression detection).
- Throttle storm / noisy neighbor: noisy tenant consumes capacity, triggers autoscaler and backpressure (focus: admission control, tenant isolation).
sections.heading: Core scenarios (rotate each quarter)

sections.body:
- Acknowledge within 5m: 10 points
- Contain within SLA targets (see runbook): 40 points
- Customer comm posted within 15m if SEV1/2: 20 points
- Evidence capture complete and postmortem opened within 4h: 20 points
- Coordination and handoff quality (subjective): 10 points
Pass threshold: >=75 points.

Status page automation patterns
------------------------------
We maintain an automated status pipeline to reduce noise and speed transparent comms. The recommended pattern:
1) Use an internal incident registry (inc-registry service) to create incident records.
2) A small automation lambda (node/python) composes status page messages and pushes to the public status page API and to the incident channel.
3) Templates are chosen by severity and updated by the comms owner.
sections.heading: Grading rubric (pass/fail metrics)

sections.body:
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Model serving latency spike - us-west1","impact":"partial_outage","updates":[{"body":"We are investigating elevated latencies for text generation endpoints in us-west1. Operators are containing traffic and activating fallback models.","status":"investigating"}] }'

Customer communication templates (copy-and-send)
-----------------------------------------------
- Initial SEV1 notice (public):
We are currently investigating elevated latencies and failed responses for text generation endpoints in the us-west1 region. Our engineers are actively containing the issue by routing traffic to healthy model variants and rewarming caches. We will provide updates every 15 minutes or sooner as significant milestones occur.

- Customer-visibility update (15m):
Update: We have put a mitigation in place that reduces error rates by ~65% and latency by ~30% for affected calls. Work continues on a full restoration; we estimate a further 45–90 minutes to complete verification and traffic ramp.

- Post-incident customer summary (post-closure):
Summary: On YYYY-MM-DD at HH:MM UTC we detected elevated latencies for hosted generation endpoints in us-west1 impacting ~X% of requests. Root cause: cache eviction cascade combined with model variant overload. Mitigation: triggered fallback to smaller model variant and rewarm pipeline; system restored by HH:MM UTC. Action items: (1) increase default cache retention for hot prefixes, (2) add model-variant warm replicas, (3) alert thresholds to include KV-cache-hit-rate.

Postmortem template and quality gate
------------------------------------
Use the postmortem template integrated with the postmortem tracker. Minimum required fields:
- Title, incident ID, SEV, start/end timestamps
- Chronology (timeline of key events, 5–10min granularity for first hour)
- Impact statement (customers affected, business impact)
- Root cause analysis (one-paragraph hypothesis, evidence, instrumentation links)
- Mitigations and timeline (what changed during incident)
- Long-term action items with owner and ETA (must include at least one owner with target completion < 90 days)
- Postmortem quality gate checklist (signed off by Bridge lead and service owner):
  - Evidence attached (logs, graphs)
  - Correlating alerts and traces present
  - Customer comms thread linked
  - Action items assigned and visible in tracker

Runbook maintenance and ownership
--------------------------------
- Owners must review their runbooks quarterly and after any SEV1/SEV2 incident.
- Deprecated runbooks are archived with a migration note.
- Runbook change log must include: date, author, summary of change, reviewer.

Appendix: operator cheat-sheet (condensed)
-----------------------------------------
- First 5 minutes: acknowledge, open incident channel, post initial comm, capture hypothesis.
- First 30 minutes: contain using the runbook, apply mitigations, escalate if blocked.
- After restore: gather evidence, open postmortem, schedule action item review with service owner within 3 business days.

Appendix: example Slack messages
-------------------------------
sections.heading: Minimal example (curl) to update status API

sections.body: [INC-12345] SEV1: Elevated latency in us-west1 for text-gen endpoints. Operator @aisha acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: KV cache miss storm; switching to model-variant-v2 for 10% traffic now.
sections.heading: Initial alert channel message

sections.body:
Investigating: Elevated latencies for text-generation in us-west1. We are containing impact and will post updates every 15 minutes.

Maintenance of this document
---------------------------
Owner: eng-serving-runtime documentation lead.
Review cadence: annually and after any major incident.
Feedback: file an update request in the doc comments or ping #runbook-maintainers.
sections.heading: Customer public status snippet (short)

payload.page_title: Incident Response Apprenticeship & Evidence Lab

sections.body: This document defines a reproducible apprenticeship for new oncall responders and a standardized evidence-lab process for collecting forensic artifacts during LLM-serving incidents. It combines a staged training curriculum with concrete runbook exercises, an evidence checklist scoped to model serving (KV caches, token traces, model eval diffs), and templated customer and status-page messaging. The goal is to reduce time-to-competence for junior responders and improve the fidelity of post-incident analysis by ensuring consistent artifact capture.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all responders operating Redwood inference-hosted and dedicated clusters (hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments under Redwood ops support).
- Exercises include performance degradations, model-quality regressions, capacity saturation, quota-related throttles, and multi-region failover.
- Does NOT replace existing critical-runbooks (use those for immediate remediation). This training sits alongside runbook library and augments evidence capture.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- New responder reaches "independent responder" (can run triage, operate bridge, and capture required evidence) within 6 supervised incidents or 4 game days.
- Post-incident files include a verified evidence bundle with logs, traces, tokenized model outputs, snapshot of eval-run prompts, and SLO telemetry.
sections.heading: Key outcomes

sections.body:
1) Apprentice (new oncall trainee):
   - Observe 2 live incidents before active participation.
   - Run the Evidence Checklist during supervised incidents.
2) Mentor (senior oncall or SRE):
   - Provide live guidance, review apprentice evidence bundles, and sign-off on competency milestones.
3) Bridge Operator:
   - Operates incident bridge, leads comms cadence, and coordinates customer status updates.
4) Incident Commander (IC):
   - Drives restoration decisions, approves rollbacks and safety gates, owns postmortem assignment.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Stage 0: Orientation (reading + self-paced labs)
  - Read: Incident process overview, runbook quick-start, status page policy.
  - Lab: Simulated alert walkthrough (1 hour).
- Stage 1: Shadowing (observe two incidents)
  - Focus: signal identification, evidence checklist familiarization.
- Stage 2: Guided response (mentor present)
  - Lead triage for low-severity events, capture evidence bundle, draft customer notice.
- Stage 3: Independent response (mentor on-call but not direct)
  - Lead medium-severity triage and bridge operations. Mentor reviews artifacts.
- Assessment: Practical exam during a scheduled game day scenario (see Game day design).
sections.heading: Apprenticeship curriculum (stages)

sections.body:
1) Alert ingestion and enrichment:
   - Automatic enrichers attach: alerting_rule, service_owner, last_deploy, recent_rollout_tags, and model_version.
2) Initial classifier (5 mins):
   - Confirm: impact (internal svc only / customer-facing), affected regions, model(s) implicated.
   - If SLO breach or >5% customer request failures -> escalate to Bridge.
3) Evidence capture (first 10 mins): run Evidence Checklist.
4) Containment vs. Remediation plan (IC decision):
   - Contain: throttles, route to fallback model variant, capacity scale-up.
   - Remediate: diagnostics, model rollback, configuration tweak.

Evidence Checklist (must be attached to incident before bridge close):
- Time-windowed logs (service logs, orchestrator events) covering -5m to +30m around alert.
- Traces (sampled spans) for top 5 p99 requests by latency.
- Metrics snapshot: p50/p90/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, enqueue depth, KV cache hit-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, host-level memory.
- KV cache diagnostics: top keys by size and miss-rate, cache eviction spikes.
- Model inference artifacts:
  - Tokenized model outputs for 10 representative requests (input, output tokens, temperature, model version, quantization profile).
  - Eval-set diffs: latest eval score and delta vs baseline (if available).
- Network / infra artifacts: netstat / iostat snippets or cloud provider instance events if applicable.
- Deployment context: last_deploy_commit, rollout-id, feature-flag state.
- Human notes: chronology, hypothesis, remediation actions, who executed them.
sections.heading: Incident intake & triage flow (compact)

sections.body:
- Preserve: do not truncate original log files; copy a time-bounded slice to the incident bundle.
- Signing: bundle owner (IC or Bridge Op) must add a small memo with the list of files and SHA256 checksums. Example: sha256sum incident-2025-02-01-evidence.tar.gz
- Access controls: mark evidence bundles as restricted in the incident tracker if they contain customer PII or redact per Data Handling policy.

Sample runbook excerpt: KV cache saturation (novel LLM-serving specifics)
- Trigger: alert if KV_cache_miss_rate > 20% AND p99 latency > 2s for 5 continuous minutes.
- Priority: P1 (customer-impacting).
- Immediate steps:
  1) Run: rbctl cache inspect --service=model-infer --window=10m --top=50 > /tmp/kv-top.txt
  2) Check cache eviction log: curl -sS https://ops-api.local/cache/events?since=10m | jq .
  3) If eviction spike present, increase cache capacity (temporary): infra-autoscaler scale cache-pool --replicas +1 --reason "KV-surge"
  4) If increase not possible, route traffic to smaller window model variant: routing-cli set-route --service model-infer --variant model-v2-small --weight 100 --reason "fallback due to KV saturation"
- Capture evidence: attach rbctl outputs, cache-top, eviction events, and the routing change audit log.

Customer and status page message templates (concise examples):
- Initial public status (short):
  Title: "Degradation: text-generation latency elevated in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated latency affecting text generation API in us-west-2. Impact: increased response times and occasional timeouts. Mitigation: routing to fallback variant and scaling. Next update: 30 minutes."
- Intermediate update (medium):
  Title: "Mitigation in progress: fallback routing and capacity increases applied"
  Body: "We have applied fallback routing to model-v2-small and increased Dedicated cache capacity. Error rates have reduced from 6% -> 2.1%. We are continuing diagnostics; ETA for full restoration: 2 hours. Customers on Dedicated will see reduced throughput while safety checks run."
- Full resolution notice (detailed):
  Title: "Resolved: latency normalized"
  Body: "Root cause: KV cache eviction surge due to a malformed batch workload after a merchant rollout. Mitigations: roll back merchant rollout, increased cache pool temporarily, and deployed a request-size validation gate. We collected a full evidence bundle. If you saw degraded outputs, please open a support ticket quoting incident ID. Post-incident review scheduled: YYYY-MM-DD."
sections.heading: Forensics & chain-of-evidence guidance

sections.body:
- Automated first-ack (bot): "INCIDENT [INC-2025-0123] acknowledged: KV cache miss spike in us-west-2. Bridge: #inc-2025-0123. Initial triage started by @bridge-op."
- Manual bridge post (template): "Status: Mitigating. Action: Fallback routing to model-v2-small applied at 15:03 UTC. Observed: p99 latency down from 2.6s to 1.1s. Next: Observe for 20m then decide rollback."
sections.heading: Example Slack bridge snippets and automation

sections.body:
- Objective: Validate apprentice's ability to run triage, collect evidence, operate the bridge for 30–60 minutes, and produce a customer-facing timeline.
- Scenario examples:
  1) Synthetic traffic spike with malformed batch payloads causing cache churn.
  2) Silent regression: small eval delta (5%) in reranking model leading to increased user complaints (requires correlation between KL eval drop and downstream error rate).
- Scoring rubric (pass thresholds):
  - Evidence completeness: 80%+ items present (pass)
  - Time-to-initial-bridge (under escalation): < 8 minutes (pass)
  - Customer message clarity: reviewer score >= 4/5 (pass)
  - Root-cause hypothesis & remediation proposal: feasible and safety-aware (pass)
sections.heading: Game day exercise design (assessment-style)

payload.page_title: On-call Scheduling Equity & Rotation Fairness

sections.body: This document defines Redwood's principles, operational rules, and concrete procedures for designing fair, equitable on-call rotations across engineering teams. It complements technical runbooks and incident playbooks by ensuring the human element (load distribution, swap mechanics, crediting, training cadence) is treated consistently and transparently.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Psychological safety: avoid punitive scheduling, enable swaps without stigma, and protect time off.
- Predictability: publish rotations and expected load in advance so engineers can plan.
- Measurability: track on-call load and crediting with simple metrics that are reviewed monthly.
- Equity: distribute higher-impact shifts (nights, holidays, long-duration incidents) more evenly over time.
- Remediation: provide time and support after difficult incidents (post-incident rest and pairing).
sections.heading: Goals and principles

sections.body:
- Applies to all engineering teams with production on-call responsibilities (Serving Runtime, SRE, Platform, Private Deployments).
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks or incident escalation matrices; this document governs people/processes around schedules and fairness.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Primary on-call: first responder for pager alerts and incident triage.
- Secondary on-call: backup for escalations after the primary acknowledges.
- Pager density: average number of P1/P2 alerts per 7-day period for a rotation slot (tracked per service).
- On-call credit: a points system used to quantify burden for each shift (see table below).
sections.heading: Key Definitions

sections.body:
1) Shift length and cadence:
   - Default shift: 1 week for Primary (Monday 00:00 UTC through Sunday 23:59 UTC).
   - Night-only rotations (where applicable): 7 nights, 00:00–08:00 local shift.
   - Max consecutive shifts: 2 consecutive primary weeks unless opt-in approved by manager.

2) Maximum weekly on-call load:
   - No engineer should exceed 25% of total primary weeks in a rolling 12-month window unless explicitly opted-in.
   - When a team has fewer than 6 eligible engineers, People Ops will initiate a backfill discussion with managers.

3) Swap and carry rules:
   - Swaps are permitted with 48-hour minimum notice for primary week swaps; emergency swaps allowed by manager or rotation owner.
   - Carryover compensation: if a swap results in an engineer taking >50% of a particularly noisy week after swap, the original owner receives 1.0 on-call credit and the swap-taker receives 1.5 credits (see credits table).

On-call crediting system (purpose: objective fairness accounting)
| Shift type | Base credit | Incident multiplier | Example note |
|-----------|-------------|---------------------|--------------|
| Standard week (primary) | 1.0 | 1.0 | baseline |
| Night week (primary) | 1.25 | 1.0 | nights counted higher |
| Holiday week (company-declared) | 1.5 | 1.0 | US major holidays |
| Week with >3 P1s | 1.0 | 1.5 | multiplier applied post-week |
| Major incident (SEV1 lasting >4h) | additional 1.0 | n/a | added to credits for that engineer
sections.heading: Rotation design rules (hard constraints)

sections.body:
| Rule | Value | Owner / Notes |
|------|-------|--------------|
| Default primary shift | 1 week | People Ops & Team Leads |
| Max consecutive primary weeks | 2 | People Ops | Opt-in allowed |
| Swap notice (standard) | 48 hours | Engineers | Use /oncall swap-requests channel |
| Emergency swap path | Manager or Rotation Owner approval | People Ops handles exceptions |
| Post-incident rest window | 24–72 hours | Manager + SRE Lead | For SEV1 responders
sections.heading: Operational table (quick reference)

sections.body:
1) Rotation creation (rotation owner responsibility):
   a) Define eligible roster and publish 90-day calendar.
   b) Annotate expected pager density for that service (low/medium/high).
   c) Set blackout dates where applicable (major conferences, CTO vacation windows).

2) Swap workflow (engineer-initiated):
   1. Create a swap request using the On-call Bot: /oncall swap @alice for week 2025-06-08
   2. Confirm acceptance by both parties in Slack within 48 hours.
   3. Update the rotation tool (rota.redwood.internal) and notify rotation-owner channel.
   4. The swap triggers automated credit adjustments in People Ops ledger.

3) Emergency swap (manager/owner):
   - Manager opens a ticket to People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) and pings rotation-owner. People Ops logs the exception and adjusts credits accordingly.

4) Post-incident relief & pairing:
   - For any SEV1 where an engineer had >2 hours of continuous triage, the manager must schedule one day of focused coding-free pairing or rest in the following 7 days. Pairing can include knowledge transfer for runbook improvements.
sections.heading: Procedures (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Monthly fairness job (run by People Ops) computes: per-engineer rolling 12-month credit totals, average pager density per slot, and outlier detection (top and bottom 5%).
- Escalation: If an engineer is in the top 5% of credits, rotation-owner and manager schedule a remediation meeting within 7 days to rebalance future rotations.
- Opt-in and opt-out: engineers can opt-in for above-average on-call loads for compensation (extra PTO day or monetary stipend); opt-out requires manager sign-off and must not leave team below minimum coverage.
sections.heading: Fairness mechanisms and automated checks

sections.body:
- Credits per engineer (rolling 12 months) — target mean and variance by team.
- Pager density by rotation slot (P1/P2s per week).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) while on primary on-call.
- Incidents per shift and cumulative incident duration.
- Post-incident rest usage rate (percentage of SEV1s that received scheduled rest).
sections.heading: Metrics and reporting (what we track)

sections.body:
- Frequency: quarterly team game days focused on high-burden services.
- Scope: simulated P1s that exercise the entire runloop (pager, bridge, rollback).
- Participation: every engineer must participate in at least one team game day per 12 months; People Ops and team leads ensure equitable assignments.
- Debrief: each game day produces a 1-page debrief with remediation items and impact on credits if game day uncovered chronic load imbalance.
sections.heading: Game day & training cadence (to reduce inequitable burden)

sections.body:
- For planned maintenance that intersects multiple on-call shifts, rotation owners must notify affected engineers 14 days in advance and publish a customer-facing status page schedule draft 7 days prior.
- If maintenance falls on a holiday week (1.5 credit), rotate ownership to minimize repeated holiday burden for the same engineer across a 12-month window.
sections.heading: Customer communications and scheduling conflicts

sections.body:
- Swap request (Slack):
  "Hey @oncall-bot, I need to swap my primary week 2025-06-08. Willing to take 2025-07-06 in exchange. @bob please confirm."

- Manager escalation email (People Ops):
  Subject: Emergency on-call swap request for team Runtime – week 2025-06-08
  Body: "Manager: Priya Nair. Reason: family emergency. Affected engineer: @alice. Request: swap to @bob. Please approve and adjust credits."

- Post-incident rest note (for DEBRIEF):
  "SEV1 on 2025-02-21 — primary responder @charles had 6 hours of continuous triage; scheduled 1 day of rest on 2025-02-25 and paired knowledge transfer on 2025-02-26."
sections.heading: Examples (templates)

sections.body:
- People Ops performs quarterly audits. Repeated non-compliance (e.g., consistently exceeding max consecutive shifts without opt-in) will be raised to the manager and Engineering leadership.
- Exceptions for small teams (<6 eligible engineers) are permitted with a mandatory remediation plan to grow the eligible roster or hire backfill.
sections.heading: Enforcement and exceptions

sections.body:
- Rota tool: rota.redwood.internal (API available at https://rota.redwood.internal/api/v1). Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROTATOKEN" https://rota.redwood.internal/api/v1/rotations/team-runtime
- On-call Bot Slack commands: /oncall swap, /oncall schedule, /oncall credits @me
- Fairness job: runs on the 1st of each month and writes to People Ops ledger (spreadsheet + internal database).
sections.heading: Implementation notes (tools & automation)

sections.body:
- Policy owner: People Ops (Maya Chen).
- Execution owner: Rotation owners (team SRE leads).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review (People Ops + Eng SRE + Legal for compliance impacts).

Appendix A: Example credit ledger CSV format (header row)
- engineer_email,team,week_start,week_end,shift_type,base_credit,incident_credit,total_credit,notes

Appendix B: Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Can I sell my on-call shift?
A: No. Selling shifts for money outside company opt-in programs is prohibited. All swaps must be tracked in the rota tool.

Q: What counts as a holiday week?
A: Company-declared holidays (see HR calendar). Local public holidays that are not company-declared are treated as standard weeks unless the team agrees otherwise.

Q: How are credits converted to compensation?
A: Credits are primarily used for internal fairness tracking. Opt-in compensation programs (extra PTO or stipend) are handled by People Ops and require manager approval.
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation matrix for this policy

sections.body:

sections.body:
Post‑Incident Learning Codex: Handoff, Synthesis, and Customer Briefing Patterns

Summary
This playbook documents a standardized, auditable process for converting operational incidents into durable organizational learning. It covers immediate triage-to-handoff checklists for on‑call rotations, artifact collection and retention, a concise postmortem cadence, and reusable customer communication templates. The goal is faster restoration during incidents, higher quality postmortems, and improved readiness across rotations.

Scope
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated services (latency, errors, throughput, availability).
- Not for design discussion artifacts (those belong in product-docs).
- Includes guidance for private deployments when Redwood support is the primary responder.

Goals
- Ensure every incident produces a minimal, searchable artifact set within 24 hours.
- Drive a 25% reduction in repeat incidents for the same root cause class within 6 months.
- Shorten the time to first customer notification to 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2 events.

Ownership & Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, owns timelines and customer comms until handoff.
- Bridge Operator: maintains the incident bridge (Slack channel, Zoom), updates status page and artifacts.
- Postmortem Owner: drafts the postmortem and assigns action items within 72 hours.
- Documentation Steward: ensures runbooks and KB entries are updated postmortem.
- Customer Liaison: handles external customer messages and escalations.

Triggering events (examples)
- SLO breach: 99th percentile latency > 500ms for 5 consecutive minutes for model inference endpoint.
- Error spike: 5x baseline 5xx rate sustained for > 10 minutes.
- Capacity constraint: GPU pool utilization > 90% with queue > 60s for > 5 minutes.
- Data plane failure: inability to reach KV cache across region.

Immediate (first 0–30 minutes) checklist
1. IC acknowledges incident and posts summary to bridge with: Impact, Hypothesis, First actions, Owner list.
2. Bridge Operator opens standard bridge channel: #bridge-incident-YYYYMMDD and pins these artifacts: runbook used, SLO dashboard link, status page draft.
3. Triage responders collect a quick snapshot (commands below) and upload to incident artifacts bucket.
4. Customer Liaison drafts and sends Initial Status (template in Templates section) within 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2.
5. If degradation continues past 30 minutes, IC escalates to senior oncall and notifies SRE lead.

Snapshot commands (run immediately)
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference > /tmp/incident-pods.txt
- kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=10m > /tmp/incident-logs-10m.txt
- curl -s 'https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(request_latency_ms[5m])' > /tmp/latency-metrics.json
- redis-cli -h cache-01.redwood.local INFO > /tmp/redis-info.txt

Handoff checklist (shift or ownership transfers)
- Time of handoff (ISO 8601)
- Summary of what’s known and what’s being worked
- Active mitigations and why they matter
- Remaining risks and what to test next
- Where artifacts are stored (S3 path or Confluence page)
- Postmortem Owner assigned (name + ETA for draft)
- Communication status: customers notified? internal comms sent?

Post‑incident artifact checklist (minimal required set)
- Incident timeline (UTC) with 1‑minute granularity where available
- Bridge chat export (Slack/Zoom transcript)
- Snapshot files (pods, logs, metrics, redis/info) and collector commands used
- Runbooks invoked (link + version)
- SLO dashboards and alert graphs (PNG)
- Final incident commander notes (hypothesis and key decisions)
- Customer messages and support ticket IDs

Artifact naming and storage convention
- S3 path: s3://incidents/YYYY/MM/DD/incident-<short-id>-<service>/
- Files: <timestamp>-<service>-<artifact-type>.log or .png (example: 2025-03-18T15:12Z-inference-pods.txt)
- Confluence: page title: "Incident <short-id> — <service> — Brief"

Postmortem cadence and expectations
- 24 hours: IC publishes incident brief in Confluence with timeline and artifact links.
- 72 hours: Postmortem Owner posts first draft with root cause hypothesis and corrective actions.
- 7 business days: Postmortem final draft complete, actions assigned and scheduled.
- 30 days: Follow-up review to validate fixes and close action items.

Postmortem structure (minimum required sections)
1. Summary (one paragraph)
2. Impact (users, customers, SLOs)
3. Timeline (ordered events, UTC)
4. Root cause analysis (evidence-backed)
5. Corrective actions (owner, ETA, verification steps)
6. Preventative actions (what changed in runbooks/SRE playbooks)
7. Lessons learned and TL;DR for execs

Prioritization rubric for corrective actions
- P0: fixes required to restore SLOs or remove single points of failure (implement within 7 days)
- P1: prevent recurrence for the same customer class (30 days)
- P2: documentation, observation, or low-effort reliability improvements (90 days)

Customer communication templates (copy/paste, replace placeholders)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
"We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latency for the inference API in <region>. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Current hypothesis: cache mismatch between autoscaled pools. Next update: <ETA or time>. Incident ID: <incident-id>. Contact: <support-email>"

Ongoing status (every 30–60 minutes until resolved):
"Update: We are currently applying an increase in capacity and validating request queue drain. Impact: ~<percent>% of requests affected. Mitigation steps taken: <list>. Next update: <ETA>. Incident ID: <incident-id>"
sections.heading: Initial status (to be sent within 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2)

sections.body:
"Resolved: The issue affecting inference latency and errors in <region> has been resolved as of <time> UTC. Root cause: <short cause>. Customer impact: <summary>. Follow-up: A postmortem will be published at <link> within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, please contact <support-contact>."

On‑call cross‑training and knowledge retention
- Shadowing requirement: every new oncall must complete 3 shadowed incidents and run 2 sandbox drills in the first 60 days.
- Mini‑game days: monthly 90‑minute scenarios run by SRE lead; attendance required for oncall rotation.
- Playbook updates: Documentation Steward to update runbook within 5 business days after postmortem if a procedural change is required.

Game day and training schedule template
- Week 1: Intro & tooling (1h) – dashboard walkthrough, artifact collection commands.
- Week 2: Simulated silent degradation scenario (2h) – focus on detection and customer comms.
- Week 3: Bridge ops and status page drills (1h) – practice templates and automation.
- Week 4: Deep dive retro (1h) – review simulated incident and update runbooks.

Automation & validation hooks
- On bridge creation, a bot auto-generates: incident short-id, S3 artifact path, and drafts initial status with the template.
- Runbook verification job (nightly) executes smoke checks and records pass/fail in the incident artifacts bucket.
- Postmortem checklist automation: a GitHub actions workflow creates issues for each corrective action with labels and due dates.

SLOs and thresholds referenced in this playbook
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inference 99p latency (regional) | 99% <= 300ms | 99p > 500ms for 5m |
| Inference error rate (5xx) | <= 0.5% | 5xx > 1.5% baseline*5 for 10m |
| GPU pool utilization | N/A | util > 90% and queue > 60s for 5m |

*Baseline calculated as 30‑day rolling mean.

Success metrics for the playbook
- Time to initial customer notice: target < 15 minutes (measured across SEV1/SEV2 incidents).
- Postmortem completion rate: 95% of incidents have a draft within 72 hours.
- Action closure rate: 80% of P0/P1 items closed or scheduled within 30 days.

Retention, tagging and searchability
- All incident artifacts must include tags: incident-id, service, region, severity, postmortem-owner.
- Confluence pages must include the label: incident-archive and the S3 path for artifacts.
- Search tip: use the incidents index (Confluence macro) or query the S3 index with the incident-id prefix.

Appendix A — Minimal incident timeline example
- 2025-03-18T15:12Z: Alert fired – inference-99p latency > 500ms.
- 2025-03-18T15:14Z: Bridge opened, initial status published.
- 2025-03-18T15:20Z: Cache cluster restart attempt, partial improvement.
- 2025-03-18T15:48Z: Autoscale policy invoked; queue draining begins.
- 2025-03-18T16:10Z: 99p latency back under threshold; monitoring for regression.

Appendix B — Postmortem quick checklist (one‑page)
- [ ] Publish incident brief (24h)
- [ ] Assign Postmortem Owner (72h)
- [ ] Draft corrective actions with owners and ETAs (72h)
- [ ] Schedule 30‑day follow up to validate fixes
- [ ] Update runbooks and label changes in Confluence

Related pages and links
- Incident comms & postmortem framework (link above)
- Runbook retention and responder onboarding handbook (link above)
- SLO dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/slo

Contacts
- Oncall Slack: #oncall-inference
- Support email: support@redwood.com
- Pager duty escalation: +1-800-555-0123 (for SEV1 pager escalation)

Revision history
- 2025-03-18: Created by Maya Rodriguez
- 2025-06-02: Added automation hooks and SLO table (reviewers: Ethan Cole)
- 2025-11-10: Updated cadence and retention policy (reviewers: Priya Nair, Sara Kim)

End of document
