payload.page_title: Responder Guidance and Simulation Labs with Templates

sections.body:
Summary:
This document is a compact, operational reference for responders, rotation leads, and incident controllers. It combines: severity definitions and triage ladders, a quick-run containment checklist, standardized status page and customer communication templates, a blameless postmortem timeline, and a small library of hands-on simulation (game-day) scenarios and lab steps. Designed to be printed on a single page for pager responders and expanded in linked runbooks for each service.

Goals and intended audience:
- Goals: reduce time-to-stable, standardize communications, ensure actionable post-incident follow-up, and improve responder readiness through repeatable simulations.
- Audience: primary on-call responders (SRE/Platform, Serving Runtime, Infra), incident commanders, product-support liaisons, and on-call rotation managers.

Definitions and severity matrix (quick reference):
| Severity | Impact description | Target initial response | Example triggers |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Sev0 | System-wide outage affecting >95% of traffic / external customer blocking | 5 minutes | API unavailable, entire region down |
| Sev1 | Major feature degradation affecting >20% of traffic or high error rates | 15 minutes | Tokenization failures, model-serving OOMs |
| Sev2 | Partial degradation or performance regression for specific customers/routes | 30 minutes | Elevated tail latency for specific model variants |
| Sev3 | Non-urgent bugs, monitoring alerts without immediate customer impact | Next business window | Single-customer integration failures |

Responder roles and responsibilities (cheat sheet):
1) Incident Commander (IC) — owns scope, prioritization, and timeline. Starts the incident in PagerDuty channel and chooses communications cadence.
2) Lead Responder / Troubleshooter — runs technical containment and root-cause hypothesis. Runs diagnostics and coordinates hotfixes.
3) Communications Liaison — drafts status page and customer messages; coordinates with CS/Legal for sensitive incidents.
4) Oncall Owner / Rotation Lead — validates handoffs, ensures postmortem and follow-up action items are created.
5) Shadow/Support — additional engineers for focused subsystems (GPU pool, routing, cache).

Initial triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge and declare: IC acknowledges in PagerDuty and opens incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>), sets severity level.
2. Triage signals: collect these immediately: traffic/ingress graphs, error-rate, rate-limited metrics, GPU utilization, queue lengths, platform autoscaler events, recent deploys.
3. Containment decision: decide one of: continue mitigation while maintaining production, roll back last deploy, failover to fallback model, or throttle/route traffic away from affected region.
4. Evidence capture: snapshot logs, capture stack traces, save request IDs, and export a short list of representative problematic requests (see Evidence checklist below).
5. Stakeholder notice: Communications Liaison posts a short status page entry (template below) and pings CS/Account teams for customers on live SLAs.

Containment patterns and commands (common actions):
- Quick rollback: git tag -> trigger rollback pipeline: ci rollback --env prod --to <last-good-commit>
- Scale up worker pool (short-lived): rwctl cluster scale --role serving --count +50 --reason "incident: <id>"
- Isolate noisy tenants: routing rule: rwctl route update --service serving --match "tenant_id:123" --action divert:staging
- Kill runaway jobs: kubectl -n serving get pods -l job=kv-cache | xargs kubectl delete pod

Evidence checklist (what to collect and where):
- Timestamped metrics windows (5/15/60 minute snapshots) from Grafana or BigQuery.
- Representative request IDs and model prompts/outputs (sanitize PII).
- Node-level profiles: nvidia-smi, dmesg, and kernel OOM logs.
- Deployment history (git commit hashes, image digests).
- Autoscaler/cluster events and scheduler logs.

Escalation ladder (who to call and when):
1. If Sev0 or escalation within 15 minutes: oncall-frontend, oncall-coresvc, oncall-gpu, and the Engineering Director (pager).
2. If containment not achieved in 60 minutes: page CTO or oncall-ops-lead for cross-team resource allocation.
3. For data-exfil or compliance-sensitive incidents: Communications Liaison pages Security and Legal immediately and mark confidentiality:restricted.

Status page and customer communication templates (short-form):
- Status page short update (first publish):
  Title: "Investigating: Elevated errors for text-generation API in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated 500 errors impacting text-generation endpoints in us-west-2. A subset of requests are experiencing timeouts and failed responses. Our on-call team is actively triaging and will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impact: some customers may see errors or increased latency. Workaround: retry after 5s."

- Internal CS escalation (Slack DM / Email):
  Subject: [Incident <id>] Text-gen errors in us-west-2 — initial notice
  Body: "Current impact: 25% error rate for text-generation for customers in us-west-2. Affected APIs: /v1/generate. Estimated time-to-next-update: 30 min. Suggested customer guidance: advise retry with exponential backoff; escalate if SLA-critical. Point-person: <Communications Liaison> (<handle>)."

Customer-facing status update (progress/mitigation):
  "Update: We have isolated the issue to the routing layer for GPU pool A and implemented a temporary routing fallback; error rates have decreased from 25%->3% for most customers. We are monitoring latency and plan a gradual traffic reintroduction once stable. Next update in 60 minutes."

Postmortem and follow-up process (timeline and checklist):
1) Incident close and initial notes: IC marks incident as 'resolved' in PagerDuty and creates a skeleton postmortem within 48 hours.
2) Evidence & timeline: collect 5/15/60 minute metric snapshots, logs, and runbook actions. Add a precise timeline (iso8601 timestamps) of actions taken.
3) Root-cause analysis: at least two engineers should propose and review hypotheses; include reproduction steps where possible.
4) Severity review & SLO impact: calculate error budget consumption and customer impact.
5) Action items: assign owners with deadlines and include verification steps.
6) Blameless review meeting: schedule within 7 days, invite rotation leads, product impacted owners, and CS liaison.
7) Postmortem publication: public internal doc + summary to Customer Success if customers were impacted.

Postmortem template (one-line fields for quick copy):
- Title: "Postmortem: <short-desc> — Incident <id>"
- Summary: brief one-paragraph impact and resolution.
- Timeline: bullet list with exact timestamps.
- Root cause: single sentence.
- Corrective actions: list with owner and due-date.
- Verification plan: how to prove the fix works.
- Lessons learned: two to four bullets.

Simulation labs (game-day catalogue and steps):
Purpose: validate runbooks, exercise cross-team comms, and test fallback behaviors without customer impact. Each lab is designed to be completable in a 90-minute session.
Library (three starter scenarios):
- Lab A: "GPU pool noisy neighbor" — simulate a tenant that exhausts KV cache and triggers autoscaler thrash. Objectives: verify isolation rules, throttle policy, and rapid tenant diversion.
  Steps: 1) Create test load on tenant X using load-generator. 2) Observe autoscaler oscillation. 3) Apply diversion rule: rwctl route update --match tenant:X --divert staging. 4) Validate reduced error rate and no regression on other tenants.
- Lab B: "Model rollout regression" — deploy a new quantized model variant that increases tail latency. Objectives: validate canary rollback, metrics-based automatic fallback, and canary burn-in checks.
  Steps: 1) Deploy canary at 5% traffic. 2) Monitor tail-latency and token-per-second metrics. 3) Automatically trigger model fallback if p95 latency > 600ms for 5 minutes. 4) Confirm rollback and redeploy with fix in staging.
- Lab C: "Control-plane region failover" — simulate a region-level dependency failure and validate cross-region routing. Objectives: test DNS failover, cache warmup plan, and customer notices.
  Steps: 1) Announce maintenance window to participants. 2) Simulate API gateway failover in us-east-1 -> fail to us-west-2. 3) Observe cache cold-start effects and measure recovery time. 4) Post customer-facing status updates at T+15 and T+60.

Game-day runbook scorecard (metrics to capture):
- Mean Time To Detect (MTTD) during lab.
- Mean Time To Contain (MTTC): from detect -> containment action.
- Accuracy of status updates (were updates timely and accurate?).
- Follow-up action completion rate within 30 days.

Runbook hygiene checklist (what every service runbook should include):
- Owner, escalation contacts, runbook last-updated timestamp.
- Minimum diagnostic commands (kubectl, rwctl, log queries).
- Severity-specific containment steps (Sev0/1/2).
- Rollback and failover playbooks (including required approvals).
- Post-incident verification tests.

Rotation rules and on-call best practices (practical guidance):
- Shift length: default 7 days. Avoid >14 consecutive on-call days.
- Handoffs: always include a 15-minute overlap with written notes and a quick sync if high-noise.
- Quiet windows: define a monthly "no-incident-hiring" blackout to avoid scheduling big changes during critical events.
- Secondary coverage: every primary on-call must designate a backup for critical windows.

Artifacts retention and evidence storage policy:
- Short-term artifacts (logs, dumps) kept for 30 days in incident bucket incident-logs/<id>.
- Long-term artifacts (sanitized traces, postmortems) saved to Confluence and long-term storage for 2 years.

Quick-reference checklist for responders (one-liner items):
- Acknowledge, declare severity, create channel, tag IC, capture request IDs, post status, apply containment, collect artifacts, escalate if >60m, create postmortem skeleton.

Templates and copy bank (snippets to copy/paste):
- Status short: "We are investigating increased errors for <service> in <region>. Impact: <summary>. Next update: <ETA>."
- Status resolved: "Resolved: Root cause was <brief>. Customer impact has ended; we are running verification checks. Full postmortem to follow."
- CS notice subject: "[Incident <id>] <service> elevated errors — customer advisory"

Appendix: Technical quick-commands (examples responders use often):
- Dump logs for request ID: logcli query 'request_id="<id>"' --from -5m --to now --limit 1000 
- Show GPU metrics (last 15m): grafana api /api/datasources/proxy/1/query?from=-900000&to=now&query=nvidia_utilization
- Apply diversion rule: rwctl route update --service serving --match 'tenant_id:<id>' --action 'divert:staging'

Related runbooks and references:
- Link to service-specific runbooks (see Service Directory)
- Postmortem examples and action tracker template

Ownership and governance:
- Document owner: Incident Ops (rotation lead).
- Review cadence: quarterly review by rotation leads; immediately after any Sev0/1 incident.

Feedback and improvements:
If you run a simulation, add the scorecard results to the Game-Day Tracker and propose new lab scenarios to the Incident Ops board.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Customer Bridge Timeline and SLA Remediation Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the customer bridge activation, timeline, and SLA remediation calculation for long-tail or high-impact incidents affecting Redwood Inference customers. It is intended for on-call operators, SREs, customer success managers (CSMs), and legal/exec comms. The goal is to ensure consistent, timely customer communication and a transparent remediation calculation when SLAs are impacted.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Audience: on-call SREs, bridge leads, CSMs, support engineers, account executives, legal.
- Purpose: standardize who does what and when during multi-hour or multi-tenant incidents; provide ready status and email templates; give a defensible, auditable SLA remediation calculation that can be shown to customers and finance.
sections.heading: Audience and purpose

sections.body:
1) Service severity triggers:
   - Severity A (outage) — >5 minutes of global unavailability for hosted API endpoints OR >2% customer impact as measured by error-rate spike above baseline.
   - Severity B (sustained degradation) — p99 latency breach for >30 minutes or error rate elevated >1% for >30 minutes.
2) SLA/contract triggers: any incident that pushes a customer’s monthly availability below their contracted SLA (e.g., 99.95% availability) for the current billing period.
3) Customer escalation: an enterprise customer requests a bridge or legal requests preservation of evidence.
sections.heading: Activation criteria (when to open a customer bridge)

sections.body:
- Bridge Lead (assigned by on-call): coordinates timeline, messages, stakeholder invites, and decision authority for public updates.
- Technical Responder(s): own containment and remediation steps, provide estimates to bridge lead.
- Customer Liaison (CSM): owns customer-specific comms and post-incident reconciliation.
- Legal: verifies wording for regulated customers and signs off on remediation/comms when sensitive data or contractual terms are involved.
- Communications Owner (Go-to-market / PR): for incidents likely to require public blog posts or press coordination.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
| Time after activation | Owner | Action | Output / Example |
|-----------------------|-------|--------|------------------|
| 0-5 min | On-call pager | Acknowledge pager, confirm activation | Conference bridge (Zoom/Meet) and Slack #bridge-channel |
| 5-15 min | Bridge Lead | Initial triage summary & impact estimate | Short status posted to status.redwood.ai and internal incident doc |
| 15-30 min | Technical Responder | Containment attempt (rollback/scale/bypass) | Failover or mitigation implemented (with commands) |
| 30-60 min | Bridge Lead + Customer Liaison | Customer-facing initial status | Initial template (see below) published + targeted email to impacted AEs/CSMs |
| 60-240 min | All | Regular updates every 30-60 minutes | Update cadence recorded; estimated ETA for recovery |
| Recovery | Technical Responder | Confirm recovery and validation | Monitoring checks green for 2x p99 window |
| +24-72 hours | CSM + Bridge Lead | Post-incident reconciliation and remediation calculation | Draft remediation proposal and schedule customer call |
sections.heading: Bridge timeline template (use immediately on activation)

sections.body:
- Tone: factual, concise, non-speculative. Avoid root-cause statements until validated. Use legal-safe phrasing: "We are investigating a service degradation affecting inference requests."
- Minimum contents of each public update: incident summary, scope/impact, mitigation in progress, next ETA, and a link to the status page.

Templates (copy-and-paste, replace placeholders):
1) Initial status page / email (30–60 min):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Degradation Affecting Inference API
sections.heading: Status cadence and content guidance
Body

sections.body: The service issue affecting the Inference API has been resolved as of {time UTC}. We validated recovery across {regions} and are monitoring closely. Impact summary and remediation calculation will be provided within 48–72 hours. If you experienced customer-facing impact, your CSM will reach out to coordinate next steps.
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
- Principle: credits are computed per-customer, pro-rated for the portion of the billing period where actual availability < contractual SLA.
- Inputs required (collect at time of incident closure):
  - Customer contract SLA (A_sla) e.g., 99.95%
  - Billing period total minutes (M_period) e.g., 30 days = 43200 minutes
  - Customer observed downtime minutes (D_obs) = total minutes during billing period where service was unavailable for that tenant (use request logs and tenant ID filtering).
- Formula (credit percent of monthly fee):
  - Availability observed: A_obs = 1 - (D_obs / M_period)
  - If A_obs >= A_sla -> no credit.
  - If A_obs < A_sla -> Credit% = min(100, (A_sla - A_obs) / A_sla * 100)
- Example: 1-hour (60 min) tenant-affecting outage in a 30-day billing period with SLA 99.95%:
  - D_obs = 60
  - M_period = 43200
  - A_obs = 1 - (60/43200) = 0.998611 -> 99.8611%
  - A_sla - A_obs = 0.000539 or 0.0539 percentage points -> Credit% = (0.000539 / 0.9995) * 100 ≈ 0.05396% of monthly bill. Round to two decimals for customer-facing proposal.
- Rounding and minimums: finance requires credit proposals to be rounded to two decimal percent and minimum credit offered is $5 or 0.01% equivalent, whichever is higher.
sections.heading: SLA remediation calculation (auditable)

sections.body:
- If incident is severity A affecting >5% of total traffic OR enterprise customer SLA breach -> automatic remediation review and phone call by CSM within 24 hours.
- If incident results in data loss or customer data exposure -> escalate to Legal + Exec and stop public language until approved.
- For minor transient spikes (<15 minutes, <0.5% impact) -> customer notification via status page only; remediation assessed in monthly review.
sections.heading: Remediation decision matrix (high level)

sections.body:
1) Within 24 hours: Bridge lead publishes incident chronology (who/what/when) — owner: Bridge Lead.
2) Within 48–72 hours: CSM drafts remediation proposal and credit calculation — owner: CSM + Finance review.
3) Within 5 business days: Post-incident review (internal) with SRE, Product, CSM; produce action items and assign owners.
4) Within 10 business days: Draft postmortem prepared and peer-reviewed; follow remediation schedule.

Evidence collection checklist (mandatory for remediation decisions):
- Request logs (tenant ID filtered) covering the incident window.
- Monitoring graphs: p95/p99 latency, error rates, host counts.
- Deployment and scaling events (timestamps & commands).
- Relevant runbook invocations and commands executed by responders.
- Communications archive (status page updates, emails to customers).
sections.heading: Post-incident workflow and deliverables (owner & timeline)

sections.body:
1) Identify top failing route(s) with request-id sampling.
2) Isolate knobs: reduce concurrency, enable fallback model variant, apply KV cache bypass/eviction plan.
3) If a deployment caused regression: rollback to last known healthy model version and monitor for 10 minutes.
4) If scaling is root cause: trigger emergency capacity (Dedicated burst or increase autoscaler target) and notify capacity@redwood.internal.

Customer comms escalation templates (CSM -> AE -> Customer):
- Short escalation email to AE: "Heads up: Incident {incident-id} impacting {customer-name}. CSM will follow up with details and remediation proposal within 48 hours."
- Phone script for enterprise call: open with apology, factual timeline, mitigation steps, remediation proposal, and expected follow-up. Keep duration <= 30 minutes for first call.
sections.heading: Runbook quick-steps (technical containment)

sections.body:
- Frequency: quarterly cross-functional drills focusing on long-tail incidents and multi-tenant remediation calculations.
- Participants: on-call SRE, CSM, Finance rep, Legal, and an Exec sponsor.
- Metrics to practice: evidence collection time (target < 4 hours), remediation proposal time (target < 48 hours), and customer ack time (target < 24 hours).

sections.body:

- Updates: timestamped bullets with concrete mitigations.
sections.heading: Templates for the status page (short form)

sections.body: - All bridge decisions must be recorded as timestamped entries in the incident doc, including who approved remediation and the inputs used for the SLA credit calculation. Attach finance-ticket number when credit is applied.

Appendix A — Template remediation worksheet (CSV columns):

payload.page_title: Availability Classification and Restoration SOP

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a single, pragmatic standard operating procedure (SOP) for classifying availability incidents, restoring service, and coordinating communications. It consolidates triage steps, restoration runbooks, status page templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation responsibilities, and a repeatable game-day exercise plan.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Inference public API endpoints, dedicated tenant ingress, and the control plane used by Private deployments. Does NOT replace model-serving specific runbooks (see related runbooks in eng-serving-runtime).

Definitions and Severity Classification

1) Severity levels (availability-focused)
   - Sev-1 (Critical): Global or multi-region service outage causing API request failure for >50% of production requests or blocking all reads/writes for a paid customer. Objective: restore within 60 minutes or follow escalation policy.
   - Sev-2 (High): Significant degradation (latency > 3x SLO or 50–80% error rate) affecting multiple customers or a single enterprise customer with dedicated capacity. Objective: interim mitigation within 4 hours.
   - Sev-3 (Medium): Partial degradation localized to a region, single service, or non-blocking errors (e.g., 10–30% increased error rate). Objective: remediation within 48 hours.
   - Sev-4 (Low): Operational anomalies, alerts without customer impact, or routine maintenance tasks. Objective: address in normal sprint cycle.

SLOs and Alert Thresholds (excerpt)

| Component | 99th latency | Error rate alert | SLO target |
|-----------|-------------:|-----------------:|-----------:|
| Public API (text-generation) | 600ms | >5% over 5m | 99.9% availability monthly |
| Embeddings endpoint | 400ms | >3% over 5m | 99.95% availability monthly |
| Control plane (auth/keys) | 200ms | >1% over 5m | 99.99% availability monthly |

Ownership and Roles

- Incident Commander (IC): First responder from engineering-oncall who takes coordination lead for the active incident.
- Service Owner: Team that owns the failing service (e.g., runtime-serving, routing, queue-proxy).
- Communications Lead: Eng-SRE or Customer Success rep who drafts customer-facing messages.
- Pager: The on-call engineer(s) for the implicated service.
- Exec Liaison: Senior engineering manager notified for Sev-1 and prolonged Sev-2 incidents.

Triage Matrix (quick guide)

1) Initial detection (automated alert, pager, or customer report)
   - Validate: Confirm alert signal (check metrics, logs, recent deploys).
   - Classify: Use error footprint + business impact to assign severity.
   - IC assigned: Pager duty system auto-assigns; if unclear, the first responder becomes IC for first 15 minutes.

2) If Sev-1 or unresolved after 15 minutes: escalate to on-call SRE lead and notify Exec Liaison.

Standard Restoration Procedure (step-by-step)

A) Containment (first 10–30 minutes)
   1. Apply temporary traffic routing: divert traffic to fallback model variant or region. CLI example:

   # Toggle routing policy to fallback pool
   redwoodctl routes set --service public-api --policy fallback-pool

   2. Disable autoscale policies that may worsen instability.
   3. If root cause unknown, enable verbose trace sampling for 5–10 minutes and capture core dumps/heap profiles.

B) Remediation (30–180 minutes)
   1. Identify root component: check metrics dashboards (latency, error rate, queue depth), recent deploys, config changes, and infra events.
   2. If a recent deploy is suspected, perform a fast rollback:

   # Roll back to previous model-served revision
   redwoodctl deploy rollback --service runtime-serving --to-revision v2025-01-10-rc3

   3. Apply config toggles (e.g., reduce batch size, force synchronous KV cache bypass) per component runbooks. See runbook links in "Runbook mapping" below.

C) Recovery validation (post-remediation)
   1. Run synthetic health checks across regions and client SDKs.
   2. Confirm ticketing and monitoring show metrics returning to baseline for two consecutive 5-minute intervals.
   3. If service remains degraded, escalate to engineering incident review for next actions (hotfix/patch or capacity change).

Runbook mapping (quick links)

- runtime-serving: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook (real runbook id)
- routing-and-traffic: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/traffic-shift-and-fallback
- control-plane: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging
- infra (GPU fleet): /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity

Communications and Status Page Templates
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- T+15m: Short summary of what is known + next 30m plan (post to #incidents slack and update internal status doc).
- T+60m: Detailed update with mitigations applied and customer impact estimate.
- T+240m: Restoration confirmation + next steps and ETA for full remediation.
- Post-incident: Postmortem link + summary (within 72 hours).

Public status page template (JSON snippet for status pipeline)

{
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "components": ["public-api", "embeddings"],
  "impact": "Some customers are experiencing increased latency and errors when calling the text-generation and embeddings endpoints.",
  "updates": [
    {"time": "2025-02-12T14:12:00Z", "message": "Identified elevated error rates; applying routing fallback to reduce customer impact."},
    {"time": "2025-02-12T15:05:00Z", "message": "Traffic routing applied. Observing reduced error rates; monitoring for stabilization."}
  ]
}

Customer email template (short)

Subject: Service impact update — Redwood API (partial degradation)

Hello,

We are investigating an issue impacting text-generation and embeddings. Some requests may fail or experience higher latency. We have implemented traffic fallback to reduce customer impact and are actively monitoring. We will provide a follow-up update by 15:05 UTC.

If you are seeing a critical production impact, reply to this message and we will prioritize a direct escalation.

— Redwood Inference Support

Postmortem and RCA Requirements

- Timeline: Include exact times for detection, mitigation steps, and full restoration.
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (logs, traces, config diffs).
- Contributing factors and corrective actions with owners and due dates.
- Severity validation against classification matrix.
- Lessons learned and detection improvement tasks (alerts, dashboards).
- Publish draft within 72 hours (IC) and final postmortem with action items closed or scheduled within 30 days.

On-call Rotations and Handoff Expectations

- Primary on-call rotation: team-managed weekly schedule. Engineers should ensure runbook access and up-to-date contact info in PagerDuty.
- Handoff checklist (on shift start/end):
   1. Review active incidents and oncall board.
   2. Confirm access to runbook links and escalation contacts.
   3. Note any scheduled maintenance and expected noisy alerts.
- Escalation triggers: failure to acknowledge pager in 5 minutes, unresolved Sev-1 after 15 minutes.

Game-day exercise plan (quarterly)

Objective: Validate the end-to-end incident workflow, including detection, routing fallbacks, public communications, and postmortem cadence.
sections.heading: Internal status updates cadence (IC responsibility)

sections.body:
- Frequency: Quarterly (every 3 months).
- Duration: 90 minutes + 30 minutes debrief.
- Participants: On-call engineer, Eng-SRE lead, Service Owner, CS Communications Lead.
sections.heading: Exercise cadence and roles

sections.body:
1) Inject simulated increased error rate in staging which mimics a regression from a recent deploy.
2) On-call must detect via alert, assign IC, and execute containment (traffic shift) within 20 minutes.
3) Communications Lead publishes a status page update and internal incident note.
4) Team performs rollback in staging and validates recovery.
5) Debrief covers timeline, missed alerts, and improvement items.

Runbook governance and health checks

- Every runbook referenced here must be reviewed at least once per quarter by the Service Owner.
- Runbook validation checklist: accuracy of commands, recent owner contact, and a working verification command or synthetic check.

Escalation Matrix (condensed)

| Trigger | Primary | Escalate after | Next | Exec notify |
|--------:|:--------|:--------------:|:-----|:-----------:|
| Pager unacked | On-call | 5 min | Team lead | No |
| Sev-1 unresolved | IC | 15 min | SRE Lead | Yes (phone) |
| Customer P1 reported | CS Lead | immediate | IC + SRE Lead | Yes |

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and artifacts to capture

- redwoodctl logs tail --service runtime-serving --since 10m --level error
- Capture core dumps: /var/crash/core-<pid>.tgz
- Snapshot of queue depth: redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --window 5m

Document maintenance

Owner: Eng-SRE.
Review cadence: annually for classification thresholds; quarterly for runbook links and playbook commands.

Related resources

- Incident comm and postmortem framework (internal link).
- Runtime profiling playbook (internal link).
- SLO and error budget guide (internal link).

Revision history

- 2024-11-10 — Created by Aisha Kapoor (initial draft).
- 2025-01-15 — Reviewed and expanded restoration steps (Priya Nair).
- 2025-02-12 — Published with status page templates and game-day plan (Diego Martinez).

payload.page_title: Rapid escalation routing playbook and multi-audience status canvas

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines a fast, deterministic escalation routing layer for incidents that require cross-functional coordination, and a set of status templates mapped to audience lanes (customers, internal engineering, executive stakeholders, and security/legal). It is intended for on-call engineers, bridge operators, SREs, and customer success leads.

Scope
- Applies to incidents impacting: API availability, sustained latency / SLO regressions, data-plane integrity, and model-quality regressions with customer impact.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance (use Maintenance Status SOP) and low-impact alerts that fit the Operational Alert handbook.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-action for Sev-1 / Sev-2 to under 5 minutes.
- Provide clear, audience-tailored status messaging within 20 minutes of bridge creation.
- Ensure single-source-of-truth (bridge) and automatic routing to the right escalation lanes.

Key concepts
- Escalation lanes: pre-defined recipient groups (On-call Service Owner, Incident Engineering Pool, Customer Success Triage, Legal & Security standby, Executive Liaison).
- Routing policies: rules that map signals and tags to escalation lanes (signal = SLO breach, error spike, KV cache eviction storm, model-sampling drift).
- Bridge templates: standardized meeting/bridge artifacts pre-populated with incident metadata.
- Audience lanes (status canvas): distinct status message templates for Customers, Internal Eng, Executives, and Security.

Escalation routing matrix (high-level)
| Trigger | Primary lane | Fallback lane | Pager policy | Owner if no ack (10m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| API 5xx > 1% sustained 5m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to SRE lead |
| P95 latency > SLO x2 for 10m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to Platform SWE |
| KV cache evictions > threshold | Incident Engineering Pool | Storage team | Pager + Slack | Escalate to Runtime Lead |
| Model quality regression (regression-detector) | Model Onboarding Oncall | Applied ML | Email + Pager (if customer-facing) | ML Lead |

Routing policy implementation notes
- Signals are tagged at ingestion (kafka topic or alertmanager webhook) with metadata: service, region, model_tag, severity_guess, suspected_component.
- A central routing service (incident-router) evaluates rules and calls PagerDuty / Slack / Email based on lane policies.
- All escalations create a bridge document and populate the status canvas skeleton via API.

Runbook: first 10 minutes (operator checklist)
1) Acknowledge the primary pager (0–2 minutes). Record time in the bridge header.
2) Confirm customer impact using metrics dashboards: request-rate, 5xx, p95, error types (2–5 minutes).
3) If the outage meets Sev-1 or Sev-2 criteria, kick off the standard bridge (use bridge-template: rapid-escalation).
4) Tag the bridge with: severity, suspected-component, affected-regions, customer-facing-flag, and impacted-models.
5) Populate the Customer Status lane (see Status templates) and post first customer-facing note within 20 minutes.
6) Assign primary owner and secondary (backup) in the bridge.
7) Enable data collection hooks: capture request traces, logs slice, model-run inputs, and a copy of the most recent deployment manifest.

Bridge operator responsibilities
- Keep the bridge single-threaded: avoid parallel fragments. Use threads for deep-dive subteams.
- Maintain timeline entries (who did what, exact timestamps).
- Coordinate evidence snapshot uploads to the incident artifact store with labels for later postmortem indexing.
- Execute rollback/hotfix policies only with owner and SRE approval.

Audience-specific status canvas (templates)
- Customer lane (external, plain language):
  - Title: [Company] API Degraded — Region {region} — {short impact summary}
  - Body: "We are investigating increased errors for requests in {region}. Impact: customers may see timeouts or 5xx responses. We have an active incident (INC-{id}) and will post updates at least every 30 minutes. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff; set lower concurrency per client while we stabilize."
  - Tone: transparent, non-technical, action oriented.

- Internal Engineering lane (technical):
  - Title: [INC-{id}] {service} — Bridge open — {severity}
  - Body: include: service dashboards links, alert rules firing, recent deploy hashes, KV cache stats, stack traces, and temporary mitigation steps.
  - Tone: explicit about hypotheses, actions run, and next steps.

- Executive lane (briefing):
  - Title: Service Impact — High level summary (INC-{id})
  - Body: impact summary (customers affected estimate), business impact (percent of traffic), ETA for next update, mitigation in progress, and ask (need exec comms approval / sales outreach).
  - Tone: concise, risk-focused, no technical jargon.

- Security & Legal lane:
  - Title: Potential Data / Compliance Impact — {INC-{id}}
  - Body: short description of suspected scope, data classes at risk, immediate containment actions, and request for legal review.
  - Tone: factual and conservative.

Status cadence and templates
- Initial announcement: within 20 minutes of bridge creation. Use Customer lane template if customers affected.
- Regular updates: every 30 minutes while active, then every 60 minutes as stabilization proceeds.
- Post-incident notification: final status and mitigation summary within 24 hours.

Customer comm templates (examples)
- Initial (20m):
"We've detected elevated errors for requests to Redwood's Text Generation API in {region}. Our engineering team is actively investigating (INC-{id}). We will post an update within 30 minutes. If you need immediate support, contact your CSM or open a support ticket with priority 'Incident'."

- Follow-up (60m):
"Update on INC-{id}: Root cause hypothesis: {brief hypothesis}. Mitigation in progress: {actions}. Partial restoration observed in {region}; customers may see intermittent errors. Next update in 30 minutes."

- Resolution (final):
"INC-{id} resolved at {time}. Impact: {summary of impact and affected customers}. Root cause: {root cause}. Actions taken: {mitigation and long-term fixes planned}. If you experienced data loss or customer-facing regressions, contact support at [support@redwood.ai]."

Escalation decision ladder (who calls the execs / sales / legal)
1) If >5% traffic impacted for >30 minutes -> notify Sales Leadership and CSMs.
2) If PII/exfiltration suspected -> notify Security & Legal immediately (pager) and set confidentiality to restricted.
3) If SLA credit or regulatory report likely -> notify Finance & Legal and prepare remediation plan.

On-call rotations, handoffs and expectations
- Primary on-call model: blended SRE + product-service rotation. Typical cadence is 1 week for primary on-call, with 48h shadowing for new members.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled in the handoff channel):
  - Current open incidents and statuses.
  - Recent deploys (last 24h) and known risky changes.
  - Nightly synthetic job health and anomalies.
  - Any escalations to watch.
- Quiet-window policy: no non-emergency merges within the on-caller's first 24 hours and last 12 hours of a shift.

Game day exercises and drills
- Quarterly scenario: Multi-region latency spike with KV cache evaporation. Objectives: validate routing rules, status canvas timelines, and rollback procedures.
- Annual scenario: Model-quality regression affecting top-tier customers. Objectives: exercise product/machine-learning coordination, customer comms, and regulatory escalation.
- Scoring rubric: time-to-bridge, time-to-first-customer-note, time-to-restore, and postmortem action completion rate.

Post-incident process and template
- Within 48 hours: write a 1,000–1,500 word postmortem with the following sections: Summary, Timeline, Impact, Root Cause Analysis (5 whys), Mitigations (short-term and long-term), Action owners, and Customer communications chronology.
- Postmortem quality gate: at least one cross-functional reviewer from SRE, Product, and Customer Success.
- Action completion tracking: actions are tracked in the incident tracker board with due dates and owners; unresolved actions >90 days require escalation to the CTO for review.

Evidence & SLO artifact checklist
- Metrics and dashboards snapshot URLs (UTC timestamps).
- Alertmanager/Signal ingestion raw payloads.
- Request-level traces for 10 representative requests during the incident window.
- Deployment manifests and model checksum at time of incident.
- Customer impact table (tenant IDs, request volume, percent of traffic).

Rollback and hotfix authorization matrix
| Type | Who can authorize | Required approvals | Communication step |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Hotfix to config (non-code) | On-call Owner | SRE lead | Post to bridge + changelog |
| Code rollback (service) | Service Owner + SRE lead | Product Director | Notify Exec lane and customers if >10% traffic |
| Model rollback / hotpatch | Model Oncall + Applied ML lead | Security review if data-sensitive | Coordinate with CSMs before large customer-facing change |

Operational KPIs to track (post-incident)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev-1: target < 3 minutes.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) for Sev-1: target < 45 minutes.
- Customer update latency (time to first external message): target < 20 minutes.
- Postmortem completion within 72 hours: target 100% for Sev-1, 75% for Sev-2.

Ownership and contacts (examples)
| Responsibility | Team | Primary contact | Pager |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Incident bridge ops | SRE | oncall-bridge@redwood.ai | Pager: incident-ops |
| API service owner | Platform | api-owner@redwood.ai | Pager: api-service |
| Model incidents | Applied ML | ml-oncall@redwood.ai | Pager: ml-oncall |

Related runbooks and references
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-and-retention-playbook-2025
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/first-five-minutes-operator-cookbook-and-csr-scripts-2026
- See: Maintenance Status SOP (internal)

Appendices
A. Incident-router rule examples (pseudo-JSON)
  - "if alert.labels.component == 'kv-cache' AND alert.value.evictions > 100000 -> route: incident-engineering-pool"
B. Bridge template fields (minimum): Incident ID, Severity, Affected services, Primary owner, Timeline, Evidence links, Customer impact table.

Document ownership and updates
- Owned by: SRE Incident Response Guild.
- Review cadence: bi-annual or after any Sev-1 where MTTR > target.
- Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 (see reviewers above).


Playbook for deterministic escalation routing, audience-specific status templates, operator checklists, rotation and game-day guidance, and post-incident process tailored for multi-audience communications.

payload.page_title: Bridged Incident Dossier and Closure Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
======
This page defines the "Bridged Incident Dossier" (a compact, standard incident artifact created during bridged/major incidents) and the playbook for moving from active response to closure. The dossier is a lightweight single-file story containing the timeline, evidence, impact calculation, customer-status artifacts, and closure criteria required for handoff to the post-incident review team and downstream stakeholders.

Why this exists
----------------
- Reduce friction during handoff from incident responders to postmortem authors.
- Standardize evidence collection so enterprise/regulatory audits have consistent artifacts.
- Provide templated customer- and exec-facing messages that can be quickly adapted.
- Make SLA credit calculations and remediation actions reproducible.

Scope
-----
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- All production degradations or outages that open a bridged incident (severity P1/P0/P1-high).
- Multi-tenant incidents where customer impact or SLA credit may be required.
Excludes: simulated game-days, maintenance windows (unless unexpected regressions occur).

Owners and roles
----------------
- Incident Commander (IC): owns dossier creation and earliest artifact completeness.
- Evidence Scribe: collects logs, traces, and KV cache snapshots.
- Bridge Operator: owns the bridge, recording timestamps and participant list.
- Customer Liaison (CL): drafts customer-facing templates and posts status updates.
- Postmortem Lead: owns closure, root cause analysis, and action-tracking after the incident is stabilized.

Bridged Incident Dossier: minimum contents checklist
--------------------------------------------------
The dossier must contain the following sections (presented here as a checklist to be completed during the bridge):
- Incident metadata: incident id, service(s) affected (service slugs), IC, bridge link, start and end times (UTC), incident severity.
- Short summary (1–3 sentences): what happened, user-visible impact.
- Timeline (annotated): at least 10 timestamps or major events with actor and rationale.
- Evidence packet pointers: links to logs, traces (trace IDs), perf dashboards, flamegraphs, and representative request samples.
- Metrics snapshots: pre-incident baseline and peak-impact metrics (error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput).
- Customer impact matrix: list of affected tenants, estimated % of requests impacted, and any MV/paid customers flagged for escalation.
- Temporary mitigations executed: config changes, fallbacks, throttles, reroutes.
- Stability decisions: rollbacks, model fallback triggers, autoscale events.
- Status page artifacts: final customer message versions, status-page ids, and timestamps of publication.
- SLA and credit calculation worksheet: inputs and computed credit amount (if applicable).
- Post-incident next steps: owners and target dates for remediation.

Bridged incident flow (quick reference)
-------------------------------------
1) Bridge open and IC assignment (T0). IC posts bridge link and basic metadata to incident system.
2) Evidence Scribe attaches initial artifacts: timestamped metrics snapshot and 3 representative logs.
3) Customer Liaison drafts an initial "we are investigating" status and posts truncated status to the status page.
4) Containment & mitigation loop: apply mitigations (circuit breakers, model fallback) and measure impact.
5) If mitigation successful, mark Stabilized and start Dossier completion and scheduled handoff to Postmortem Lead.
6) If mitigation fails or incident escalates, maintain bridge until recovery and then proceed to dossier close.

Triage and containment runbook excerpt (for model-serving latency SLO regressions)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Detect: alert when p99 latency > 1.5x SLO for 10 minutes and error rate > 0.5%.
- Immediate steps (first 10 minutes):
  1. IC: confirm alert validity, note thresholds that fired in dossier.
  2. Scribe: capture a 5-minute window of perf metrics and top 10 traces: CLI:
     curl -s "https://dash.internal/services/metrics?service=runtime&from=-5m&to=now" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > metrics-5m.json
  3. Runtime lead: examine KV cache eviction graphs and hot-shard counts.
  4. Apply fast mitigation: switch routing policy to regional fallback with query cap-of-50% (temporary).
- If errors persist after 15 minutes: consider model quantization rollback (two-step):
  a) Re-route 10% of traffic to cold model variant for verification.
  b) If verified healthy, escalate to 50% over 10 minutes.

Evidence collection template (copy into dossier)
------------------------------------------------
Table: (paste into the dossier as rows)
- metric_snapshot_pre: /dash/snapshots/2026-03-12-09-00.json
- metric_snapshot_peak: /dash/snapshots/2026-03-12-09-12.json
- representative_trace_ids: [span-12345, span-12398, span-12411]
- log_archive_links: /logs/incidents/INC-2026-0041/2026-03-12-bridge.tar.gz
- kv_cache_state: /artifacts/kv/kv-state-2026-03-12.tar.gz
- config_changes: list of commands and Git commit SHAs (see example below)

Example commands to capture config and state
------------------------------------------
- Capture running config (k8s):
  kubectl -n redwood get deploy serving-runtime -o yaml > serving-deploy-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).yaml
- Snapshot Redis/KV metadata:
  redis-cli --rdb rdb-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).rdb
- Preserve active model weights/variant pointer:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/serving/current/variant.json ./variant-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json

Customer/status page messaging (templated)
----------------------------------------
Use these short, editable templates for status-page posts and CS notifications. Replace bracketed tokens.
- Initial public status (First 15 minutes):
  Title: "Degraded inference latency in [region] — investigating"
  Body: "We are investigating reports of increased latency for inference requests in [region]. Our engineers have opened an incident (ID: [INC-ID]) and are actively investigating. We will post updates every 15 minutes or when there is a material change."
- Stabilized public status:
  Title: "Service stabilized — continued monitoring"
  Body: "We mitigated the issue impacting inference latency in [region]. We are monitoring to ensure steady performance and will publish a technical postmortem within 72 hours."
- Customer follow-up (direct to affected tenants):
  Subject: "[INC-ID] — Summary and next steps for [tenant]"
  Body: "Hi [Tenant Name],
We observed [estimated %] of your requests were impacted between [Tstart] and [Tend]. The root cause was [brief cause]. We applied [mitigation]. Our remediation plan is: 1) [action 1], 2) [action 2]. Your assigned CSM is [CSM name]."

SLA credit quick method (example)
--------------------------------
When an outage qualifies for a credit under our SLA, calculate using the service-level definition and time window:
- Inputs (must be present in dossier): incident start, incident end, total customer requests in window, measured impact % for that customer.
- Example computation:
  - Customer total monthly billable requests: 120,000
  - Impact window: 2 hours = 2/720 of monthly window (approx).
  - Estimated impacted requests: 120,000 * (2/720) * 0.6 impact = 200 requests
  - Credit policy: credit = pro-rated fee for impacted requests (finance formula reference F-002).
Record the full worksheet in the dossier and attach finance approval link.

Closure criteria (must be satisfied before postmortem handoff)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Incident is stabilized: p99 latency <= SLO for a sustained 30-minute window.
- Dossier completion: at least 80% of the checklist present and timestamped artifacts uploaded.
- Customer communications: public status updated and CS notifications sent for flagged tenants.
- Action owners assigned for remediation items with target dates.
- Finance notified if SLA credit may be required.

Post-incident retrospective & game-day integration
------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
1. Incident timeline readout (10 minutes, IC)
2. Evidence review (10 minutes, Scribe)
3. Root cause language (15 minutes, technical owners)
4. Actions and owners (15 minutes)
5. Lessons learned and playbook changes (20 minutes)
6. Optional game-day run (20 minutes) — attempt the top mitigation step in a synthetic environment if safe.

Runbook retirement and continuous improvement
--------------------------------------------
- Each bridged incident that results in a new remediation >3 person-days creates a task to update the runbooks the mitigation touched.
- Runbook change owner must submit a PR to the runbook repo within 7 days, with a short changelog entry describing the update.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
-----------------------------------
- Executive one-pager template: attach as "exec-brief.md" in the dossier.
- Postmortem rubric and severity-to-action mapping: link "/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-rubric-2025"
- Dossier starter JSON (machine readable) for automation:
  { "incident_id": "[INC-ID]", "start_time": "[T0]", "severity": "P1", "owner": "[IC]" }

RACI (abridged)
---------------
- Responsible: IC, Evidence Scribe, Bridge Operator
- Accountable: SRE Lead
- Consulted: Runtime Engineering, Product (if config changes affect features)
- Informed: Customer Success, Legal (if regulatory / data exposure)

Examples and corner cases
------------------------
- Silent degradation detection: if anomaly detection flagged gradual p99 drift over 3 hours (no bridge opened), run the "silent incident" lightweight dossier and schedule a remediation game-day.
- Multi-region failover: if failover to secondary region was performed, attach traffic split charts and extra verification traces for the secondary region.

Appendix: common short commands and snippets for Scribes
------------------------------------------------------
- Capture top error traces (temporary):
  curl -s "https://traces.internal/api/search?service=runtime&minDuration=200&limit=20" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > top-traces.json
- Export SLO dashboard snapshot via CLI:
  slo-cli snapshot --service runtime --output slo-snapshot-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).png

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary contact for dossier process questions: Aisha Patel (pager: pagerduty)
- Escalation to SRE lead: Diego Morales

Notes
-----
This playbook favors rapid, repeatable evidence collection and small standardized message templates to reduce cognitive load on responders during high-stress bridged incidents. Keep the dossier concise — the goal is a single coherent artifact that supports postmortem recommendations, SLA computations, and customer trust restoration.

payload.page_title: Triage playbook for model-quality regressions and CSR templates

sections.body:
Summary:
This document explains the operational process for detecting, triaging, and recovering from model-quality regressions (MQRs) that materially affect customer-facing outputs. It includes runbook steps, ownership, on-call rotation guidance, game day scenarios for MQRs, postmortem checklist, and customer/CSR notification templates.

Scope:
- Applies to any regression that changes generation quality: hallucinations, large accuracy drops, safety/TOX outputs, or systematic formatting errors for production models served by Redwood.
- Excludes infra-only outages where model execution returns but request routing/latency is the primary cause; see latency playbooks for those flows.

Objectives:
1. Rapidly detect and contain regressions to minimize customer impact.
2. Provide clear ownership and escalation rules between Serving, Applied ML, and SRE.
3. Maintain transparent customer communication and post-incident learning.

Key contacts and ownership:
- First responder (FR): oncall serving-runtime engineer (primary)
- Applied ML triage lead (AMLT): Applied ML team member (secondary)
- SRE escalation owner: SRE oncall (tertiary)
- Customer success liaison (CSL): assigned CSR for impacted accounts
- Pager rotation: eng-sre oncall schedule (see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations)

SLO and thresholds for triggering this playbook:
- Quality SLOs: measured per-eval-suite or per-customer prompt set. Trigger if:
  - Absolute metric drop > 8% (e.g., exact match/ROUGE/F1 depending on suite) over 1 hour compared to baseline, OR
  - Burst of customer complaints (>=3 distinct customers complaining about similar failure mode within 30 minutes), OR
  - Safety threshold breach: >1% toxic responses in production sampling window.

Automatic detection signals (examples):
- Canary evaluation failure (continuous eval alerts)
- Regression alerts from Redwood Optimize monitors (quality drift detector)
- Unexpected prompt-set eval failures after a rollout
- Customer reports via support channels tagged as "model-quality"

Immediate runbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge and declare incident
   - FR acknowledges pager within 5 minutes. Set bridge (Zoom/Jira/Slack huddle) and incident Slack channel #incident-mqr-<id>.
   - Use incident classification: MQR-1 (safety-critical), MQR-2 (major quality degradation), MQR-3 (minor / localized).
2) Quick scope and containment
   - Collect sample failing inputs/outputs and timestamps.
   - Check last deploys/rollouts: matching model version, quantization profile, kernel changes, or routing rules in the last 24 hours.
   - If issue maps to a specific rollout/config change, immediately enact rollback to previous pinned model variant (see rollback checklist below).
3) Notify Applied ML and Customer Success
   - Ping AMLT and CSL on-call. Provide sample artifacts and initial classification.
4) Apply short-term mitigations (if rollback not feasible)
   - Route affected traffic to a fallback model variant (lower-recall but safer/older model) via smart routing rules.
   - Increase sampling and enable verbose logging for the impacted routes.

Rollback checklist (if root cause is a recent model or config change):
- Confirm baseline model hash/version to roll back to.
- Validate rollback model passes smoke evals (canary prompts).
- Ensure KV cache or prefix cache is invalidated appropriately if required.
- Coordinate with infra/SRE for deployment window (aim for immediate out-of-band rollback).
- Communicate rollback start in incident channel and to CSL for customer notices.

Deep triage (30–180 minutes):
- AMLT performs targeted evals on prompt sets showing failure modes.
- FR gathers system telemetry: model version, GPU nodes, kernel versions, quantization flags, and request routing metadata.
- SRE checks runtime logs for memory corruption, OOM patterns, or precision-induced anomalies.
- If a data-related issue is suspected (label drift, tokenizer changes), involve Data Platform and Product for evaluation.

Decision ladder for broadened escalation:
1) If rollback/fallback eliminates customer impact -> transition to recovery & monitoring.
2) If rollback not possible and impact > MQR-2 -> open major incident and include CTO/Head of Applied ML in bridge.
3) If safety-critical outputs present -> notify Legal and Security immediately and follow restricted comms path.

Customer and CSR communication templates
- Use these templates as plain text in Support and Status updates. Customize per customer severity and SLA. Always include: what happened, who is affected, what we're doing, and expected next update time.

Template A: Initial short notice (within 30–60 minutes)
Subject: [Redwood] Investigation under way for model output quality affecting [service]
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},
We’re contacting you because we are investigating an issue that may affect the quality of outputs from {ModelName} for requests sent after {ISOtimestamp}. Our engineers are actively investigating and we may route traffic to a fallback model to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs. We will send another update within 60 minutes.
If you notice any critical safety issues, please contact your CSR immediately (direct line: {CSRPhone}).
– Redwood Operations

Template B: Follow-up notification (after rollback/fallback)
Subject: [Redwood] Mitigation applied for model quality issue affecting {ModelName}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},
We applied a mitigation at {ISOtimestamp} that routes traffic for {ModelName} to a safe fallback variant while we complete root-cause analysis. Impacted requests should resume normal quality within the next 5–15 minutes. We will share a detailed incident report after the investigation completes.
– Redwood Operations & Applied ML

Template C: Post-incident summary (to customers and CSRs)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident report: model-quality regression for {ModelName} (incident {IncidentID})
Body:
Summary:
- Incident window: {Start} – {End}
- Affected models/routes: {ModelName}/{Route}
- Root cause: {Short description}
- Remediation: {Rollback / Fix applied}
- Customer impact: {Description and metrics}
- Mitigations taken: {List}
Next steps:
- Permanent fix ETA: {Date}
- Monitoring improvements: {List}
We appreciate your patience and will reach out to impacted accounts directly with any follow-up.
– Redwood Operations

Postmortem and learning checklist (owner: incident owner, due within 7 days):
1) Evidence collected: logs, eval run outputs, model hashes, sampling artifacts.
2) Timeline constructed with decision points and communications.
3) Root cause hypothesis and validation steps documented.
4) Action items defined with owners and deadlines (e.g., revert rollback automation, improve canary suite).
5) Add regression tests to eval harness and link to CI (owner AMLT).
6) Publish postmortem to Confluence and tag related pages.
7) If customer-facing, coordinate customer call scheduling with CS.

On-call rotation guidance specific to MQRs:
- Serving oncall: primary pager for 0–60 minutes after detection. Must be able to perform rollbacks and routing changes.
- AMLT oncall: secondary pager, expected to be available within 30 minutes for evals.
- SRE: tertiary pager for infra-related escalations.
- Shift handoff: include open incident ID, current classification, mitigation state, and outstanding postmortem tasks.

Game day scenarios (recommended quarterly):
1) Canary-eval regression after staged rollout: practice identifying failing prompts, performing rollback, and updating routing rules.
2) Safety spike simulation: generate synthetic toxic outputs and exercise restricted comms and Legal/Security handoffs.
3) Silent-degradation: only 5% of requests fail quality checks — test detection sensitivity and sampling rules.

Metrics and dashboards to monitor (minimum):
- Quality SLO score (per-route and global) with 5/15/60-minute windows.
- Canary evaluation pass rate (per-deploy).
- Customer complaint rate for model-quality tag.
- Fraction of traffic on fallback variants.

Runbook snippets (CLI / API)
- Route traffic to fallback variant (example):
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routing/override -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"model-v1.3-fallback","duration_minutes":60}'

- Trigger immediate canary eval (example):
  redwood-eval run --suite=canary-small --model=model-v1.4 --output=canary-output.json

Operational improvements (post-incident backlog suggestions):
- Harden rollback automation to validate canary smoke tests automatically.
- Expand canary prompt sets to include recent customer prompts and safety-focused cases.
- Improve sample retention for quick evidence collection (increase to 24h for quality incidents).
- Add routing telemetry tag for every request to trace policy decisions.

Appendix A: Incident severity examples
- MQR-1 (Safety-critical): Generation yields unsafe content (toxicity, privacy leak) for multiple customers or a high-severity single-customer incident. Immediate Legal and Security involvement.
- MQR-2 (Major quality drop): Systematic accuracy drop impacting many customers; performance still usable but degraded.
- MQR-3 (Localized): Single-customer or single-route degradation with limited blast radius.

Appendix B: Evidence collection checklist
- Sample inputs and outputs (CSV/JSON)
- Model version/hash and rollout ID
- Eval outputs for canary and baseline
- Routing configuration at the time of incident
- Host/runtime telemetry (GPU logs, kernel versions)

Related pages and references:
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/canary-design
- /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-03: Added rollback checklist and CLI snippets (review: Marco Sandoval).
- 2026-02-14: Expanded game day scenarios and added communication templates (review: Lena Nguyen).

End of document.

sections.body:
Overview:

This document defines a structured Responder Apprenticeship program for new and rotating responders. The apprenticeship combines shadowing, active pairing, formal handover checklists, and a set of reusable customer-voice templates (status page, email, and support chat) tailored for LLM inference incidents (latency, model-quality regressions, KV cache thrash, and capacity blips). The goal is to accelerate operational readiness, reduce noisy escalations, and standardize customer communications while preserving empathetic tone and technical accuracy.

Scope:
- Applicable to all SREs, on-call engineers, platform responders, and solutions engineers participating in on-call rotation.
- Focus areas: detection triage, containment, restoration, post-incident handoff, and customer comms.

Goals and success metrics:
- Time-to-first-meaningful-action (TFMA) for apprentices: target < 10 minutes during supervised shifts (game-day measured).
- Handover completeness rate: > 95% of checklists completed for each incident.
- Customer-template adoption: 100% of external status updates originate from provided kits for incidents with customer impact.

Roles & ownership:
- Program owner: Maya Chen (observability & oncall enablement).
- Lead mentor: Diego Morales (SRE).
- Buddy mentors: platform and runtime engineers assigned 1:1.
- Leadership sponsor: Head of Eng SRE.

Curriculum overview (8-week apprenticeship):
1) Week 0 — Orientation (self-study):
   - Read: incident lifecycle, runbook index, SLOs, and the team Slack triage channel norms.
   - Watch: 2 recorded bridge runs and 1 postmortem walkthrough.
2) Weeks 1–2 — Shadowing (observational):
   - Shadow 4 on-call shifts (night/day mix).
   - Tasks: observe triage, listen on bridge, compile 3 questions per incident.
3) Weeks 3–4 — Paired response (active):
   - Pair with mentor on 6 shifts. Apprentice performs initial triage steps with mentor approval.
   - Mentor checks handover checklist live and completes annotations.
4) Weeks 5–6 — Autonomy with review (semi-independent):
   - Apprentice is primary responder on 4 shifts; mentor acts as observer.
   - After each shift, debrief using the incident evidence template.
5) Weeks 7–8 — Certification & capstone game-day:
   - Participate as primary responder in a scheduled capstone game-day focusing on KV cache/cache-eviction and capacity-throttle scenarios.
   - Pass rubric: TFMA, checklist adherence, communication quality.

Shadowing schedule template (example):
- Day shift: 09:00 - 17:00 PT (2h overlap with mentor; apprentice observes 1 active incident).
- Night shift: 20:00 - 04:00 PT (paired bridge duty; apprentice reduces interruptions).

Handover checklist (must be completed on every responder handoff):
- Incident ID and severity level
- Brief description of symptoms and affected routes/models
- Detection timestamps: first alert, first response, first mitigation
- Actions taken so far (commands, restarts, rollbacks) with runbook links
- Temporary mitigations and known side-effects
- Current hypothesis and next diagnostic steps
- Ownership of long-running tasks and who will follow up (pager + Slack handle)
- Customer-facing status and templates used (link to Customer-Voice Kit)
- Evidence snapshot location (metric dashboards, traces, logs, sample request IDs)
- Suggested postmortem owner and timeline

(Use the following compact table as a quick checkbox for handovers in the bridge):
| Field | Example / Command | Completed? |
| Incident ID | INF-2026-1234 | [ ] |
| Severity | Sev2 - elevated latency | [ ] |
| Affected Model/Route | text-gen:openmodel-6b / embeddings | [ ] |
| Evidence URL | grafana/app?panel=latency | [ ] |
| Temporary Mitigation | scale-up pool, enable prefix-cache | [ ] |

Triage decision ladder (quick reference):
1. Is the issue customer-facing or internal-only? If customer-facing, escalate to on-call lead and prepare a customer template.
2. Can a rollback/model-variant fallback restore acceptable behavior within 10 minutes? If yes, proceed and monitor.
3. If not, apply containment (rate limits, route isolation, revert batching change) and open a mitigation task.

Game-day design (capstone):
- Duration: 3 hours. Scenario mix: KV cache eviction storm, noisy neighbor GPU saturation, model quality regression due to new weights.
- Metrics to monitor: 95th/99th p99 latency, queued requests, GPU util, error-rate per model.
- Evaluation rubric: TFMA, checklist compliance, comms clarity, root-cause reasoning.

Post-incident debrief template (for apprenticeship):
- Summary (one-sentence)
- Timeline (bullet list of key events with timestamps)
- Actions taken and outcome
- What worked / didn’t work (freeform)
- Follow-ups assigned (owner + due date)
- Learning for the apprenticeship curriculum

Customer-Voice Kit (ready-to-use templates)
1) Status page short update (public):
   - Title: Degraded API latency impacting text-generation routes
   - Body: We are investigating elevated latency affecting text-generation endpoints in our hosted region (us-west-2). Some requests may experience delays or timeouts. Our on-call team is actively mitigating the issue; updates will be posted here every 30 minutes.
   - Impact field: Partial outage for text generation; embeddings and non-latency-sensitive routes unaffected.
   - ETA: Initial mitigation expected within 60 minutes.

2) External email template (customers affected by SLA-sensitive incidents):
   - Subject: Incident INF-2026-1234 — Latency impacting inference throughput
   - Body: Hello <CustomerName>,

Our team is investigating an issue impacting inference latency for text-generation routes in us-west-2. We have activated mitigation steps (scaling and prefix-caching) and are monitoring for improvement. We will provide an update within 30 minutes and a post-incident summary once services are stable. If you require assistance or a dedicated bridge, reply to this message and we will escalate.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Ops Team

3) Support chat / CSR quick response (concise):
   - "Thanks for reporting — we're on it. The issue is impacting generation latency; our on-call team is working on containment and we'll update you in ~30m. Can you share any affected request IDs?"

Escalation thresholds (apprentice-specific guidance):
- Immediately page mentor if: TFMA > 20m, severity escalates to Sev1, or rollback risks data loss.
- Notify product/solutions if customer-visible KPI drop > 10% or any enterprise customer reports failures.

Evidence collection checklist (minimal set to attach to postmortem):
- Grafana: latency and request-rate panels (screenshot)
- Traces: 3 representative traces for p99 failures
- Logs: error buckets and a sample of request payloads (sanitized)
- Model artifacts: model version, quantization profile, recent rollout ID

Mentor feedback rubric (pass/fail criteria for certification):
- Technical: correct use of runbooks, evidence collection, and diagnostic commands.
- Operational: follows handover checklist, keeps bridge concise, and documents actions.
- Communication: clear customer updates, correct escalation, and calm bridge facilitation.

Onboarding admin checklist for program owner:
- Assign mentor and buddy within 3 business days of enrolment.
- Schedule game-day in week 8 and reserve a staging cluster for realistic simulation.
- Add apprentice to on-call channel read-only for observational weeks.

References and links:
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index (internal)
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026.json
- Evidence collection standard: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-chain-and-forensic-runbook-2025.json

Appendix: example diagnostic commands and artifacts to memorize
- Check route health: curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health/text-gen
- Snapshot KV cache stats: redis-cli --csv INFO keyspace | grep evicted
- GPU pool utilization: rci gpunode top --pool inference-dedicated

Revision history:
- 2025-03-14: Drafted initial curriculum and checklist (Maya Chen)
- 2025-06-02: Added customer-voice templates and mentor rubric (Diego Morales)
- 2026-02-10: Formalized capstone game-day and certification criteria (Maya Chen)
