payload.page_title: First Principles Triage and Runbook Ops Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook codifies a first-principles approach to triage, containment, restoration, and post-incident evidence capture for Redwood's serving and orchestration systems. It standardizes decision-making heuristics (not rote checklists) so responders can make consistent, auditable choices during high-uncertainty incidents.

Intended audience:
- Primary: first responders, on-call engineers, SRE rotation leads
- Secondary: incident commanders, support leads, product liaisons

Scope:
- Applies to production-hosted and dedicated Redwood inference endpoints, routing/control plane, autoscaler, and KV-cache services.
- Excludes: developer sandboxes, local dev workflows, and customer-managed private control planes (see reference runbooks in eng-private-deployments).

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Restore meaningful customer traffic within SLO-defined windows (see SLOs section).
  - Preserve forensic evidence for regulatory & billing audits.
  - Make triage decisions that minimize blast radius and enable progressive escalation/fallback.
- Non-goals:
  - Exhaustive troubleshooting of non-production issues.
  - Replacing service-specific runbooks (this is a guiding framework that links to those runbooks).

Severity classification (quick reference):
1) Sev0 / Major outage: >50% of customer requests failing or systemic data corruption; requires bridge within 15 minutes.
2) Sev1 / Major degradation: latency SLOs breached for >10% of tokens or persistent error-rate spike >5% for 15+ minutes.
3) Sev2 / Partial: isolated region/tenant impact; elevated errors for a single model or capacity pool.
4) Sev3 / Informational: low-impact regression, non-urgent customer report.

SLOs and restoration windows (example):
- Token-latency p95: 300ms target, SLO window: 30d; breach defined as p95 > 400ms for >1h with customer impact.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Restoration windows: Sev0 — bridge and public status within 15 min, functional recovery target 2h; Sev1 — alert & triage within 30 min, recovery target 6h; Sev2 — triage within 2h, recovery 24h.

Decision heuristics (first principles):
1) Protect evidence: if incident may affect billing/integrity, snapshot logs/KV-store and capture crashdumps before mass restarts.
2) Minimize user blast radius: favor traffic-shaping, rate-limits, or routing to degraded-but-safe model variants over full service shutdown.
3) Prefer reversible changes: configuration toggles and rate limits over irreversible migrations.
4) Escalate early: if triage confidence < 60% after 30 minutes at Sev0/Sev1, call an Incident Commander.

Roles and responsibilities (one-line):
- First Responder: acknowledge alert, collect evidence, make safe containment moves.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinate cross-functional response, customer messaging, and retrospective ownership.
- Service Owner: domain SME, implements and validates fixes.
- SRE Lead: approves large-scale rollbacks and capacity changes.
- Communications Lead: drafts public and customer templates.

Runbook anchor procedure: initial 18-minute triage (used as a mental model)
1) 0:00–0:02 — Acknowledge, set bridge channel, post short status: severity estimate, likely impacted services, initial mitigation (if any).
   - Slack template: "[ACK] Sev{n} — {service} — initial triage in progress. Bridge: {link}."
2) 0:02–0:06 — Evidence capture: collect latest logs (last 30 minutes), snapshot KV-cache metadata, export controller metrics, and note any recent deploys/rollouts.
   - CLI snippets:
     ```bash
     # capture last 30m logs for service
     rbctl logs service/my-service --since 30m > /tmp/my-service-logs.txt
     # snapshot kv cache metadata
     rbctl kv snapshot --service my-model-pool --out /tmp/kv-snap.json
     ```
3) 0:06–0:12 — Rapid hypothesis generation: enumerate top 3 root causes (capacity, recent deploy, upstream network, data corruption).
4) 0:12–0:18 — Containment action 1: implement the least disruptive mitigation from the hypothesis list (example: switch traffic to warm pool, apply per-tenant rate-limits, disable caching layer write-behavior). Record the exact command and operator.
5) Post-18: If restored, proceed to evidence hardening and RCA. If not, escalate to IC.

Containment play examples (choose lowest-privilege/reversible):
- Re-route traffic to compatible model variants (CLI):
  ```bash
  rbctl traffic update --route /v1/generate --to model:llama-2-13b-quant --weight 100
  ```
- Apply a per-tenant throttle for noisy tenants:
  ```bash
  rbctl quota set --tenant tenant-123 --requests-per-minute 2000
  ```
- Disable aggressive KV writes temporarily:
  ```bash
  rbctl feature disable kv_writeback --service my-cache
  ```

Evidence capture checklist (always capture in order):
- Timestamps and timezone-normalized event windows.
- Full request-id traces for a representative sample (min 5).
- Controller and node-level metrics (CPU, GPU mem, queue length) spanning -60m..+15m around incident start.
- Snapshot of active rollouts and model version pins.
- Any relevant billing/usage spikes.
- Export of error payloads and stack traces.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- If containment not effective after 30m at Sev0/1 -> IC + SRE Lead + Product PM on-call.
- If evidence indicates data integrity risk -> Inform Security and Legal (follow security-and-compliance incident runbook).
- If customer-sensitive data is suspected -> mark confidentiality: restricted and follow chain-of-custody.

On-call rotation and mentorship guidance (unique element):
- Rotation model: two-week primary on-call + four-week secondary; shadow week for new hires before primary.
- Mentorship pairing: every new on-call engineer is paired with a mentor for the first 3 rotations; mentor runs a 60-minute pre-rotation walkthrough covering common runbooks and CLI exercises.
- Post-shift debrief: primary fills a 10-min structured debrief form in the bridge after each shift (what alerts fired, any runbook gaps, triage confidence).

Game day playbook (90-minute template):
- Objective: validate triage heuristics and evidence capture under simulated KV-cache corruption and aggressive autoscaler oscillation.
- Pre-game: schedule with all participating teams, pre-seed synthetic load, and mark customer impact as simulated.
- Scenario timeline:
  - 0–10m: inject synthetic errors at controller and amplify a slow build-up of queue length.
  - 10–25m: expect first-responder to follow initial 18-minute triage; verify evidence artifacts exist.
  - 25–45m: require the IC to authorize a traffic-shift to warm pool and a rollback of the latest model rollout.
  - 45–75m: validate rollback, run a smoke test suite, and confirm metrics restore.
  - 75–90m: structured retro and runbook updates.

Status page & customer comm templates (editable):
- Public status (short):
  "We are investigating elevated request errors affecting text generation in US-East. Impact: intermittent failures for some customers. Mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes."

- Incident page (long):
  "Timeline: 10:14 UTC — Elevated 5xx rate observed; 10:20 UTC — bridge stood up; 10:27 UTC — initial containment: traffic routed to warm pool; 11:07 UTC — rollback of model rollout; 11:45 UTC — services stable; 12:00 UTC — full validation completed. Customer impact: intermittent request failures for ~18% of requests between 10:14-11:07 UTC. Root cause: faulty model rollout interacting with KV-cache eviction logic. Next steps: harden rollout gating and add KV eviction anomaly detection."

- Customer email template (concise):
  "Subject: Incident affecting Redwood text-generation in US-East — [Resolved]

  Hi {customer_name},

  We experienced intermittent errors impacting text-generation requests in US-East from {start_time} to {end_time}. We restored service by routing traffic to a warm pool and rolling back a model rollout. Your account saw {approximate_percent}% failed/latency-impacted requests. We will follow up with an RCA and proposed mitigations by {date}. If you require credits or a dedicated call, reply to this message and we will schedule it."

Post-incident workflow (team actions):
1) IC prepares a one-page incident chronicle within 24 hours and shares with stakeholders.
2) Evidence handoff: all captured artifacts uploaded to the incident bucket with checksum and chain-of-custody note.
3) Technical RCA: service owners produce detailed analysis (3–7 business days recommended).
4) Remediation plan: prioritized action items with owners and ETA (target: at least one mitigating fix within 7 days).
5) Follow-up customer communication: scheduled by Customer Success with IC input.

RCA example structure (required fields):
- Summary (one paragraph)
- Impact window and affected tenants
- Root cause analysis with evidence links
- Contributing factors
- Corrective and preventative actions (owner + ETA)
- Lessons learned and runbook updates made

Runbook governance and upkeep:
- Every runbook referenced from this playbook must have an owner and a quarterly review date.
- After every Sev0/1 incident, update the runbook within 10 business days or create a backlog ticket linking to the incident.
- Maintain a runbook change log at the top of each runbook with dates, approver, and short rationale.

Appendix: quick forensic commands and artifact locations
- Export controller metrics: `rbctl metrics export controller --from "-60m" --to "+15m" --out /tmp/controller-metrics.csv`
- Collection bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/incident-{incident_id}/artifacts/ (ensure checksum.md5 is present)
- Evidence retention: default 90 days for standard incidents, 365 days for any incident that may affect billing or legal obligations.

Notes and references:
- Related SOPs: security-and-compliance/incident-response-security, eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides
- See also: postmortem templates (incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026) and on-call mentorship materials in eng-sre/team-wiki.

Revision history:
- 2024-04-15: initial draft (Aisha Thompson)
- 2024-09-10: expanded evidence checklist and CLI snippets (Daniel Cho)
- 2025-11-02: added mentorship pairing and game-day template; clarified SLO restoration windows (Priya Nair)

Contact and escalation list (on-call directory links):
- Primary SRE rotation: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rotation-directory
- IC on-call schedule: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/ic-schedule

End of playbook.

payload.page_title: Oncall handoff pulse and customer message canvas

sections.body: This document defines a compact, repeatable oncall handoff 'pulse' protocol and an associated customer message canvas used for SLA-sensitive incidents. It is designed for frontline operators, incident commanders, and SREs to accelerate warm-handoffs, standardize what evidence to collect, and provide pre-approved customer status templates for each incident phase.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Scope: all Redwood public and enterprise-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated routing, and Private control plane).
- Audience: oncall operators, bridge leads, SREs, support on-call, and customer success liaisons.
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
- Handoffs are a high-risk time for information loss and slow restoration.
- Customers require consistent, SLA-aligned messaging.
- Engineers need a minimum set of evidence to triage and produce regulatory artifacts.
sections.heading: Why this exists

sections.body:
1) Pulse: a 5-minute structured handoff exchange capturing state, evidence, and next actions.
2) Quiet window: a 10–30 minute period after a handoff where only critical changes are made; used to stabilize and prevent oscillation.
3) Evidence bundle: minimal artifacts required to validate severity and timeline for post-incident review.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
- Sev-1: Full outage impacting >10% of customers or any enterprise SLA breach.
- Sev-2: Significant degradation (latency SLO degradation >50th percentile) or partial regional outage.
- Sev-3: Minor degradation or isolated tenant impact.
sections.heading: Severity mapping (for pulse context)

sections.body:
1. Attest (30s): outgoing operator states: "I am handing off; current incident state: SEV-X; bridge open; primary hypothesis: <one-line>".
2. Evidence check (90s): outgoing lists evidence bundle items present (see Evidence collection table).
3. Actions and blockers (60s): outgoing reviews in-flight actions, who is owning them, and blockers.
4. Timeboxing and quiet window (30s): agree the next 15/30 minute quiet window and who will break it.
5. Acceptance (30s): incoming confirms understanding, repeats 1–2 critical next steps aloud, and declares a new heartbeat schedule.
6. Update status page & CSR (remaining time): outgoing or incoming (pre-agreed) posts the next public update.

Evidence collection (minimum required for SLO and postmortem):
- Requested artifacts (collect and attach to the incident ticket):
  * Time range (UTC) for observed deviation.
  * Aggregated 1m and 5m latency histograms for affected endpoints (csv).
  * Recent autoscaler events (timestamped).
  * Host / GPU node IDs and kube pod IDs (for Dedicated/private).
  * Model variant used (name + version + quantization profile).
  * Representative request/response sample (anonymized) showing failure or degradation.
  * Error traces (stack traces, grpc/HTTP codes), and cold start counts.
  * Any recent config/rollout IDs (canary id, rollout job id).
sections.heading: Pulse protocol (5-minute structured handoff)

sections.body:
| field | why it matters | command / link |
|---|---|---|
|Time range|Bounds the incident window|N/A|
|Latency histograms|Proves SLO regression|curl https://observability/api/latency?s=...|
|Autoscaler events|Shows capacity churn|kubectl get events --namespace=inference|
|Node/pod IDs|Ties to infra failures|kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=...|
|Model variant|Identifies model-level regressions|cat /deploys/current_model.txt|
|Request sample|Reproduces customer impact|Extract via internal trace ID payload|

Note: paste the above as plain text in the ticket if attachments are delayed.

Status page and customer message canvas (SLA-sensitive templates):
- Template rules: keep messages factual, avoid speculation, and include: impact, affected region/tenants, mitigation steps underway, ETA or next update window, and a contact/CSR escalation path.

Initial acknowledgement (within 15 minutes for Sev-1, 30 minutes for Sev-2):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident — {service} {SEV-1/2} — {short summary}
sections.heading: Evidence table (copy into incident ticket)

sections.body:
We are aware of an issue impacting {service}.
Impact: {brief, e.g. "Some API requests return 500 / Observed latency > 2s for <region>"}.
Customers affected: {public / list enterprise tenants when known}.
What we are doing: {brief bullet list of immediate mitigation actions}.
Next update: {T+15 / T+30 / promise window}.
Contact: {csr-email and status page link}.
sections.heading: Message body

sections.body: Subject: [Redwood] Incident update — {service} — current state
sections.heading: Stabilization update (during quiet window)

sections.body:
Summary of changes since last update. Attach evidence snapshot (latency percentile snapshot). If rollback or fallback executed, list rollout id and who initiated.

Post-incident status and customer reconciliation (within SLA window per contract):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — {service} — post-incident summary
sections.heading: Message body

sections.body:
Root cause (as-of current understanding): {one-paragraph}.
Impact summary: total minutes degraded/outage, tenants affected, and credits (if applicable).
Evidence: attach evidence bundle (histograms, traces, and representative request/responses).
Next steps: remediation, follow-ups, and expected timeline for long-term fixes.

Handoff checklist (what the incoming must verify within first 10 minutes):
- Confirm bridge URL and ticket link is reachable.
- Confirm severity mapping and whether SLA credit process is triggered.
- Validate evidence bundle presence or initiate collection.
- Confirm owner for: model rollback, autoscaler tuning, routing policy change.
- Confirm customer comm schedule and who is authoring the public update.
sections.heading: Message body

sections.body:
- Quiet window default: 15 minutes after each handoff for Sev-1, 10 minutes for Sev-2.
- Only break quiet window for: new evidence changing hypothesis, confirmed mitigation efficacy (rollback success/failure), or safety/regulatory requirement.
- Anyone breaking the quiet window must call 'breaking quiet' in the bridge and update ticket with reason.

Game day plan: Pulse Drill (30–60 minute exercise to validate handoffs):
Purpose: exercise the 5-minute pulse handoff under load with simulated evidence delays.
sections.heading: Quiet-window rules and exceptions

sections.body:
- Incident conductor (1): runs timeline and injects faults.
- Bridge operators (2): outgoing and incoming.
- Customer comm (1): drafts and publishes status updates.
- Evidence steward (1): simulates delayed logs/attachments.
sections.heading: Roles

sections.body:
1. Inject simulated latency spike in Europe region.
2. Outgoing operator runs first pulse, collects partial evidence.
3. After 5 minutes, outgoing hands off per protocol; incoming performs acceptance.
4. Evidence steward releases delayed artifacts after 8 minutes; teams must update ticket.
5. Run through two handoffs and a forced quiet window break.
sections.heading: Scenario steps

sections.body:
- All handoffs completed within 5 minutes.
- Status page updated within required windows.
- Evidence bundle at least 80% complete by T+20.
sections.heading: Success criteria

sections.body:
- Oncall operator: first responder and ticket maintenance.
- Service steward (team owning service): technical ownership after stabilization.
- Bridge lead / incident commander: coordinates cross-team actions.
- Customer Success: external comms and SLA reconciliation.
- Security: loop in if data exposure is possible.
sections.heading: Escalation and ownership matrix (quick reference)

sections.body:
1. Incident ticket updated with final evidence bundle (within 48 hours).
2. Postmortem draft (blameless) created within 72 hours and assigned reviewers.
3. Remediation actions tracked as tasks with owners and target dates (linked in ticket).
4. SLA credit assessment completed and communicated per contract.

Appendix A — Quick copy-paste status templates:
- ACK template (Sev-1):
[ACK] We are investigating increased error rates in {service} in {region}. We will update within 15 minutes.

- UPDATE template (mid-incident):
[UPDATE] Mitigation applied: {action}. Observed effect: {latency P95 down from X to Y}. Next update: {T+30}.

- RESOLVE template:
[RESOLVED] The incident affecting {service} has been resolved. Root cause: {short}. Impact: {duration and tenants}. Full post-incident report: {link}.

Appendix B — Example CLI snippets for evidence extraction:
- Latency snapshot (example): curl -s "https://observability/api/latency?s=2026-03-01T12:00:00Z&e=2026-03-01T12:30:00Z&service=inference" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > latency.csv
- Pod list for a rollout: kubectl get pods -n inference -l rollout=canary-2026-03 -o wide
sections.heading: Post-incident artifacts and timeline for closure

sections.body:
- 2025-11-12: Document created by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-03-02: Updated quiet-window defaults and added Pulse Drill game-day steps.
sections.heading: Change log

sections.body:
- Owner: SRE Ops (oncall-and-incident-response).
- Training: all oncall operators must complete Pulse Drill at least twice per 6 months.
sections.heading: Ownership and training

sections.body: - Send suggested edits or additional templates to the oncall playbook Slack channel (#oncall-playbook) or file changes as PRs to the runbook repository.
sections.heading: Feedback and improvements

payload.page_title: On-call Shadow Labs and Continuity Manifest

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the On-call Shadow Lab program and the accompanying Continuity Manifest used to validate responder readiness, handoff fidelity, and incident continuity for Redwood Inference. The Shadow Lab program runs scheduled, low-risk experiments (synthetic signals and twilight incidents) against staging and canary surfaces to exercise runbooks, rotation handoffs, and customer communication paths.

Goals

- Verify that every on-call rotation has at least one active shadowing trainee per cycle.
- Prove runbooks, automation, and status-page tooling through repeatable synthetic-signal scenarios.
- Validate handoff fidelity and evidence capture for postmortems and regulatory audits.
- Reduce time-to-stabilize for tiers 0–2 incidents by 30% across the next two quarters.

Program overview

1) Shadow Labs (weekly): lightweight, scheduled exercises where an experienced responder (mentor) pairs with a trainee (shadow) and performs a simulated detection and triage using non-production signals. Exercises focus on one play at a time (e.g., KV cache miss storm, batching-pressure, N+1 latency).
2) Synthetic Signal Days (monthly): automated scenarios injected against isolated canaries that generate realistic observability signals (SLO deviation, error spikes, missing traces). These are run under a test-ops guard and always target staging/canary routes.
3) Continuity Manifest (quarterly): a checklist-driven audit verifying runbooks, rotation contact lists, backup responders, and status page templates are current.

Roles and responsibilities

- Lead Responder (mentor): prepares scenario, reviews evidence, signs off on trainee readiness. Ownership: eng-sre.
- Shadow Trainee: performs triage and executes runbook steps under mentor guidance. Ownership: rotating engineers/ML engineers.
- Continuity Owner: owns the quarterly Manifest and remediation tracking. Ownership: platform-ops.
- Status Page Operator: maintains status page templates and triggers customer messages if scenario crosses customer-impact threshold. Ownership: customer-success on-call.

On-call shadow lab schedule (recommended cadence)

- Weekly shadow session (1 hour): 1 mentor + 1 trainee. Focus: single runbook execution, handoff practice.
- Monthly synthetic scenario (2 hours): test automation team runs scripts; on-call participates.
- Quarterly continuity audit (half day): review manifest items, rotate backup responders, update runbooks.

Synthetic Signal Catalogue (table)

Name | Source | Target SLO | Detection threshold | Expected response time | Owner
KV-Cache-Pressure | canary-kv | p50 tail latency < 250ms | 10% requests failing TTL errors for 3m | ack: 2m, mitigation: 15m | eng-serving-runtime
Batch-Throttle | canary-batcher | 95th latency < 500ms | batching latency >200% baseline for 5m | ack: 5m, mitigation: 20m | eng-platform
Auth-Token-Expiry | canary-auth | availability 99.9% | token-validation errors > 0.5% for 5m | ack: 2m, mitigation: 10m | eng-sre

Runbook template (single-file canonical pattern)

Every runbook used in Shadow Labs should follow the template below. This ensures consistent evidence collection and easy automation integration.

- Runbook title: short, unique
- Service / component: service name(s) and route(s) affected
- Severity tiers and customer impact mapping
- Detection signals: metrics, logs, traces to check (include dashboard urls)
- Initial triage checklist (numbered):
  1. Confirm alert validity and time window.
  2. Identify impacted routes and customers via request tags.
  3. Check autoscaling and queue length metrics.
  4. If model-related, check kv-cache size and recent model-rollout history.
- Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1. Apply fast rollback to previous model variant (if applicable).
  2. Increase worker pool or scale burst group. CLI:
     curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/ops/scale?pool=ingest&delta=+2" \n  3. Enable prefix-KV bypass (short-lived) and monitor error rate.
- Verification steps: smoke tests and SLO checks (include target metrics).
- Evidence capture checklist: screenshots of dashboards, links to logs (packet id, trace id), pager ids, bridge transcript.
- Post-incident next-steps and owners.

Incident handoff and continuity rules (manifest items)

The Continuity Manifest is a simple checklist to be completed at handoff and during audits. Key items:

- Rotation roster verified (primary + backup) with phone and escalation order.
- Runbooks validated for current top-10 incident classes.
- Status page templates checked and test-sent to internal channel (no external publish).
- Backup responder health: confirm 2 responders in different regions with VPN access.
- Automation playbooks functional (CI smoke for runbook runner).

Handoff procedure (5-step sequence)

1. Outgoing responder posts concise status: current state, mitigation in progress, >customer impact? Y/N, tasks outstanding.
2. Incoming responder reviews runbook & evidence links, acknowledges within 5 minutes.
3. Confirm pager/bridge access and test a single quick command (e.g., get cluster health).
4. Update rotation calendar and mark handoff complete in the oncall ledger.
5. If escalations expected, notify Customer Success and Legal (if SLA breach likely).

Status page and customer comms templates

Use these concise, staged templates tailored to the incident tier. Keep language factual and avoid conjecture.

- Short incident announcement (initial)
  Title: Service degradation for <service-name> in <region>
  Body: We are investigating elevated error rates impacting <subset-of-customers>. We have engaged the on-call team and will provide updates within 30 minutes.

- Update (staged)
  Title: Update: mitigation in progress for <service-name>
  Body: We are deploying mitigations and observing partial improvement. A portion of requests are still affected. Next update in 30 minutes or on progress.

- Resolution
  Title: Resolved: <service-name>
  Body: The issue has been resolved at <time>. Root cause: <short summary>. Impacted customers: <list>. Postmortem will be published in X business days.

Sample internal pager message (short)

[ALERT] KV-Cache-Pressure canary-kv p50 latency spike > 250ms (3m window)
Triage: runbook: kv-cache-pressure
Action: scale ingest pool + enable bypass
Owner: @oncall-engineer | Bridge: #bridge-1245

Postmortem / evidence checklist

- Incident timeline with timestamps (UTC).
- Evidence: dashboard links, logs (trace ids), bridge transcript, customer messages.
- Root cause hypothesis and validation steps performed.
- Rollback/mitigation timeline and why chosen.
- Action items with owners and due dates (include verification plan).
- Regulatory evidence pack (if customer-impacting): signed by Continuity Owner.

Game day scoring and pass/fail criteria

- Completion of runbook steps within target windows (ack within 5m, mitigation attempted within 20m).
- Quality of evidence captured (screenshots, links) scored 0–5.
- Handoff fidelity (outgoing: 5 checks present) scored pass/fail.
- Customer comms template used correctly (language and cadence).
- Overall pass = 80%+ on combined criteria. Failures create a remediation ticket assigned to continuity owner.

Onboarding a new responder (quick checklist)

1. Shadow two weekly labs (observe and run one under mentor).
2. Pass a synthetic-signal scenario with independent execution and evidence capture.
3. Confirm access to bridge, status page, and runbook editor.
4. Sign the Continuity Manifest and provide emergency contact.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and integrations

- Trigger a test status page update (internal test endpoint):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d '{"status":"internal-test","message":"shadow-lab ping"}' https://status-internal.redwood/api/v1/test-publish

- Fetch recent bridge transcript:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-bridge-logs/bridge-1245/transcript.txt - | tail -n 200

- Evidence automation: add evidence link to incident ticket (example):
  curl -X POST https://internal-issue.redwood/api/issue/12345/evidence -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"link":"https://dash.redwood/model/trace?id=abc123","note":"kv-cache smoke check"}'

Ownership and contact points

- Continuity Owner: Maya Carter (platform-ops) | maya.carter@redwood.com
- Program Lead: Elena Park (eng-sre) | elena.park@redwood.com
- Status Page Operator: Customer Success on-call (rotating)

Related artifacts and links

- Central runbook index: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks-index
- Oncall ledger and rota: /tools/oncall/rota
- Synthetic scenario repo: git@github.com:redwood/ops-synthetic-labs.git

Notes and next steps

- Immediate: run first synthetic scenario for batcher on 2026-03-07 and notify oncall roster.
- Q2 OKR: reduce median mitigation time by 30% using Shadow Lab remediation tickets.

Document history

- 2025-09-12: created by Elena Park
- 2025-12-08: added synthetic scenarios catalog (Ravi Nair)
- 2026-03-01: continuity manifest updates and new status templates (S. Liu)

End of document

payload.page_title: incident-symphony-runbook-and-notice-kit

sections.body:
Overview:

This page defines the 'Incident Symphony' playbook: a prescriptive orchestration pattern for multi-team incidents where coordinated, time-boxed work and clear comms keep customers informed while engineers restore service. It pairs a lightweight role choreography with templates (status page + customer notices), concrete first-responder commands, and a repeatable game-day scenario to validate readiness.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, service owners, product on-call, support leads, oncall engineers.
- Applies to: service outages and degradations affecting production inference, embeddings, or API availability across hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Not for: low-level CI/CD failures that do not affect customer traffic.

Key principles:
- Clear roles and short cadence: assign a Conductor (IC equivalent) within 3 minutes of a page.
- Communication-first: aim to publish a status update within 10 minutes for any P2+ event.
- Contain then remediate: focus first on customer impact surface (routes, rate limiting, fallbacks), then identify root cause.
- Keep changes reversible: prefer routing changes and configuration toggles over destructive fixes during incident.

Severity table (quick reference):
|| Severity || Customer impact || SLA risk || Typical response || Time-to-first-update ||
|| Sev 1 || Total outage for > 1% customers or majority of requests failing || High || Bridge + IC + Exec notice || 10 minutes ||
|| Sev 2 || Partial service degradation (latency spikes, increased errors) || Medium || Triage + containment plan || 15 minutes ||
|| Sev 3 || Isolated error, single-region, nonblocking || Low || Owner-led fix || 60 minutes ||

Roles (musical metaphor):
- Conductor (Incident Commander): single point for decisions and customer-facing updates.
- Section Leads (Service Owners): one per impacted service (eg. runtime, routing, database).
- Instrument Leads (Engineers): hands-on triage and mitigation for a slice of the system.
- Scorekeeper (Scribe): records timeline, actions, and publishes postmortem draft skeleton.
- Audience & Comms (CSR/Liaison): crafts status page and customer notices.

Triage checklist (first 0-15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge the pager and declare the incident in Slack #ops-emergency.
2. Conductor creates the incident channel and pins this runbook.
3. Section Leads join and report an initial hypothesis in the channel.
4. Scorekeeper begins a timeline document and copies the Incident Summary template below.
5. Publish an initial status page entry (see templates).

Immediate actions (containment patterns):
- High latency / token amplification: temporarily route heavy customers to lower-seq-length model variant, enable prefix cache.
- Model OOMs / GPU failures: evict affected worker pool, scale up standby pool, enable routing fallback to CPU-quantized model.
- Persistent 5xx from runtime: set autoscale burst to 0 and route to healthy region; if global, initiate circuit-breaker to degrade non-critical routes (embeddings batch jobs).
- Excessive KV cache misses: restart cache proxy with warmup mode, throttle internal replays.

Runbook commands (examples):
- Check service pods and recent restarts:
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
  kubectl -n redwood describe pod <pod-name>
- Inspect GPU node health:
  redwoodctl nodes status --region us-west-2 --filter gpus
- Query error-rate from tracing backend (example):
  curl -s 'https://observability/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total{job=runtime,error!=""}[5m])' | jq
- Extract recent model load errors from logs:
  rg "Model load failed|KV cache corruption" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 200

Rollback and routing safe-play actions:
1. Prefer routing changes that are explicitly reversible: scale policy, model alias switch, region preference.
2. Example alias switch (imaginary CLI):
  redwoodctl routing set-alias model:prod:model-v2 model-v1 --reason "fallback for latency spike" --author $ME
3. Canary rollback pattern: route 10% traffic for 10 minutes, observe tail latency and 5xx ratio, then expand or rollback.

Escalation matrix (timeboxes):
- 0-10m: declare incident, initial update (Conductor).
- 10-30m: if no containment achieved, escalate to Platform SRE lead and open executive thread.
- 30-60m: if customer impact continues, prepare external customer notice (CSR lead) and schedule Exec update.

Status page templates (copy/paste and fill placeholders):
- Investigating:
  Title: "Investigating — Elevated error rates affecting inference API"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated errors for the Inference API affecting some requests in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively diagnosing the issue. Impact: some requests return 5xx or experience delayed responses. Next update: in 10 minutes. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff.
  
- Degraded / Partial outage:
  Title: "Partial degradation — Inference latency increased"
  Body: "We identified a service degradation impacting latency for text-generation requests for a subset of customers. We have reduced traffic to the affected worker pool and enabled fallback model variants while we remediate. Impact: increased latency up to XXs for affected requests. Next update: in 30 minutes.
  
- Resolved:
  Title: "Resolved — Inference API"
  Body: "The underlying issue has been resolved and normal service has been restored. Root cause: <summary>. Mitigation: <actions>. We will publish a post-incident report within 72 hours.

Customer notice email (short form):
Subject: Service degradation affecting Redwood inference — update
Hi <Customer>,
We wanted to let you know we are experiencing elevated errors/latency impacting the Inference API in <region>. Our team is actively working to resolve this and we have implemented fallback routing to reduce impact. We will follow up with a full post-incident summary. If you have an active outage, please reply to this message and we will prioritize.

Game-day scenario (exercise):
Objective: validate multi-region restoration and communications under a synthetic backend failure that triggers failover and routing changes.
Preconditions: standby region with 2 healthy worker pools, canary model variant available, synthetic traffic generator configured.
Steps:
1. At T0 simulate a GPU node retirement in primary region.
2. Observe autoscaler behavior and routing changes.
3. Conductor times to first update and validates status page publishing.
4. Section Leads perform a safe alias switch to canary, then measure error-rate and latency.
Scoring rubric:
- Publish initial status update within 10m: 10 points
- Containment (restore <5xx to baseline) within 30m: 20 points
- Successful reversible routing change without data loss: 30 points
- Post-exercise postmortem drafted within 48h: 10 points

Postmortem template (to be filled by Scorekeeper):
- Title and incident id
- Summary (1–2 sentences)
- Impact (customers affected, runtime window, quantifiable metrics)
- Timeline (minute-resolution actions and decisions)
- Root cause analysis (why the change happened and underlying systemic gap)
- Corrective actions (short, medium, long-term) with owners and due dates
- Validation plan (how we will prove the fixes work; include metrics and test plans)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups

On-call rotation & handoff checklist:
- Handoff should include: active incidents, muted alerts, known degradation, outstanding rollouts, and upcoming maintenance.
- Recommended shift length: 7 calendar days per on-call (primary), with 24-hour overlap handoff window on day 1 and day 7.
- Shadowing requirement: new on-call should shadow 3 rotations before taking primary.
- Handover message template (Slack pinned):
  - Current status: <OK/Degraded/Incident>
  - Active incidents: <id + brief>
  - Runbooks/links: <links>
  - Known flaps: <services>

Post-incident verification (72h):
- Owner runs the validation plan and reports pass/fail in the postmortem.
- Observability team runs a targeted alert sweep for anomaly recurrence.

Attachments and links:
- Dashboard: https://observability/dashboards/inference-slo
- Incident template: /confluence/templates/incident-timeline
- Routing CLI docs: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/routing-cli

Appendix — common quick fixes (copyable snippets):
- Clear KV proxy cache and warm:
  redis-cli -h kv-proxy flushall && curl -X POST https://internal/kv-warmup
- Temporarily increase concurrency for model pool:
  redwoodctl pools update runtime-v2 --concurrency 128 --region us-east-1

Notes and governance:
- All Sev 1 incidents require a postmortem with at least one cross-team reviewer and owner timelines tracked in the corrective actions table.
- This runbook should be exercised at least twice per year via game days.

Contact and escalation directory:
- Platform SRE oncall: pager +1-555-0101, Slack @platform-oncall
- Runtime service owner: @runtime-team
- CSR lead: csr@redwood.com

End of document.

payload.page_title: First Five Minutes Operator Cookbook and CSR Scripts

sections.body:
Overview
========

This page captures a compact, actionable playbook for the first five minutes of any on-call activation plus a set of short Customer Support Representative (CSR) scripts and status templates. The goal is to reduce time-to-stabilize by standardizing immediate operator actions, clarifying responsibilities, and providing repeatable customer-facing messaging. This doc is intended for first responders, bridge operators, and support agents.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
- Pager or monitoring alert for production-facing service impacting customer requests (latency, errors, capacity).
- Customer-reported outage escalated to on-call.
- Any incident declared P1 / Sev-1 by SRE or product steward.

Key principles (quick)
----------------------
- Acknowledge fast: an initial, accurate status reduces duplicate work and calms stakeholders.
- Observe first, act second: gather evidence quickly before sweeping changes.
- Contain, then mitigate: prioritize actions that prevent damage or wide impact.
- Communicate clearly: internal and external messages should be short, factual, and time-boxed.

Operator checklist: 0–5 minutes (ordered)
---------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge and declare scope (0:00–0:30)
   - Accept the pager in the on-call system and record timestamp.
   - Post a 1-line bridge message in the designated channel: "Investigating: [service] alert — initial triage started (T+0m)."
   - Set incident priority level per SLO impact matrix.

2. Quick evidence snapshot (0:30–1:30)
   - Grab dashboards: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), error rate, request rate for the last 15 minutes.
   - Check recent deploys / rollouts (last 30–60 minutes): deploy pipeline, Canary status.
   - Collect top-5 logs errors (grep/ELK) and top N failing endpoints.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=svc=api -o wide
   - curl -sS "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/query?query=rate(request_errors[1m])" | jq .
   - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/last-hour/ . --include '*api-*' --profile oncall

3. Rapid containment (1:30–3:00)
   - If obvious noisy neighbor or hot loop, apply a short-lived rate limit until mitigation: e.g., Traffic Control: svc-level rate to 50% for 10m.
   - If a model variant or recent canary looks correlated, switch routing to last-known-good variant using the routing control plane: "route set my-service -> model:v42 --weight 100 --dry=false".
   - If persistent cache corruption suspected, toggle read-through-only mode and invalidate affected prefixes.

4. Escalate and assign roles (3:00–4:00)
   - Confirm primary bridge operator and assign a restoration owner.
   - Page +1 domain expert if not already on bridge (kernel/scheduling, runtime, infra, product steward).
   - Start an evidence capture thread: list of the artifacts being collected and where.

5. External and internal one-liners (4:00–5:00)
   - Internal: short summary in bridge + SLO impact matrix level.
   - External (CSR): use the short template (below) to let affected customers know we are investigating and will provide updates.

Decision ladder: when to rollback, route, or throttle
----------------------------------------------------
- Rollback immediately if a single recent deploy correlates with error spike and automated canary indicated failure.
- Route fallback if model variant/region shows degradation but alternative variant is healthy.
- Throttle/rate-limit when resource exhaustion or noisy-neighbor behaviors cause transient spikes.

Quick runbook authorship checklist (for the operator modifying runbook during incident)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Keep a one-line summary of what changed and why.
- Add a short "If you see X do Y" step at the top for next responders.
- List the exact commands used (no shorthand).
- Timestamp actions and add links to evidence artifacts (dashboards, logs).
- Mark the runbook change as draft and flag for post-incident review.

CSR scripts and customer-facing templates
----------------------------------------
Principles for customer messages: be human, brief, factual, and set expectations. Use the "What we know / What we are doing / When next update" format. Avoid technical jargon for general customers.
sections.heading: Example commands

sections.body: - "Hi — thanks for reporting. We are aware of an issue affecting [feature/service]. Our engineering team is investigating; we will update you within 30 minutes or sooner with next steps. If you can share a request id, timestamp, or example payload, that helps our triage. — Redwood Support"
sections.heading: CSR initial inbound template (use within first 5 minutes)

sections.body:
- Title: "Partial degradation of [service] in [region]"
- Body: "We are investigating increased errors for requests to [service]. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Current action: on-call team has started triage and containment. Next update: in 30 minutes."

Private customer SLA/NDA-sensitive template (for enterprise accounts):
- "Redwood Incident Reference: RWI-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN> — We are investigating an issue impacting [customer-specific surface]. Our engineering and account teams are engaged and will provide a detailed update in 30 minutes. For immediate questions please reply to this thread or contact your account manager."

Short escalation message for execs (1 line)
- "Severity [1/2] incident impacting [service]; mitigation in progress; ETA unknown. Primary owner: @name. Bridge: #ops-bridge."

Evidence collection quick list
------------------------------
- Alert trigger timeline (monitoring).
- Request traces for 10 representative failing requests.
- Sample logs (first 100 errors).
- Recent deploy hashes and canary stats.
- CPU/GPU utilization across serving fleet, KV cache statistics.

Game-day micro-drill: 5-minute focus
------------------------------------
Run this 15–20 minute exercise weekly to practice the first-five-minutes flow. Roles: pager receiver, bridge operator, CSR, domain expert.
1) Fire a synthetic alert: p99 latency spike + 5% error rate.
2) T+0: Pager receiver acknowledges, posts bridge message, collects dashboards. (3 min)
3) T+3: Bridge assigns owner, attempts containment (route fallback). (5 min)
4) T+8: CSR posts public status page and notifies enterprise account leads.
5) Debrief (5–10 min) focusing on speed of acknowledgement, quality of evidence, and message clarity.

Post-incident micro-postmortem template (to start within 24 hours)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
- Title: Incident RWI-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN> — short summary
- Impact: customer-visible symptoms, affected services, regions, % requests impacted
- Timeline: bullets with timestamps for key events (pager, containment, mitigation, full restore)
- Root cause hypothesis (initial)
- Actions taken (with command or config lines used)
- Immediate remediation and durable fixes proposed
- Owner list and ETA for each fix
- Follow-up eval: add regression test or synthetic monitor to catch the issue pre-production
- Lessons learned and blameless notes

Runbook maintenance and lifecycle for first-5m steps
---------------------------------------------------
- Every runbook referenced from this playbook must include: owner, last-runbook-test date, and a 2-line quick action summary.
- Quarterly review: runbooks with no test in 90 days are flagged and an owner is assigned 30 days to remediate.

Operational SLO thresholds referenced
------------------------------------
- API 99th latency SLO: 500ms — degradation -> Sev-2; outage -> Sev-1.
- Error rate SLO: 0.5% 5m rolling — sustained >2% -> Sev-1.
- Request drop / throttling: any unauthenticated region-wide drop >1% sustained -> Sev-1.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- On-call rotations: see team rota in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rotation-playbook-skills-matrix-and-postmortem-rubric-2024 (link).
- Primary owners by area: serving-runtime: @samir, infra: @marco, product-steward: @evelyn.

Related artifacts and links
--------------------------
- Incident command playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024 (link)
- Postmortem template and archive: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026 (link)
- Status page guidance: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/customer-comm-tonebook-and-staged-status-templates-2026 (link)

Appendix: Sample quick commands and snippets
------------------------------------------
- Force traffic to fallback model variant (control-plane CLI):
  redwood route update --service my-service --variant model:fallback-v1 --weight 100 --reason "Immediate containment"

- Short script to snapshot top error messages (bash):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  timeframe="15m"
  jq -r '.events[].message' /var/log/service/errors.log | head -n 100 > /tmp/incident-errors-$(date +%s).log

- Minimal evidence JSON payload example for postmortem:
  {
    "incident_id": "RWI-20260301-01",
    "first_alert": "2026-03-01T09:12:00Z",
    "impact": "p99 latency up to 1.8s; 6% error rate for 8m"
  }

Notes and next steps
--------------------
- After restoring service, ensure runbook authorship checklist is followed and a postmortem is drafted within 24–48 hours.
- Add this playbook to the new responder apprenticeship syllabus for onboarding.

Document history
----------------
- 2025-11-06: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-03-01: Updated with CSR templates and game-day micro-drill (reviewers: Marco, Evelyn, Samir)

payload.page_title: On-call exercise curriculum and status template bundle

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines a repeatable on-call exercise curriculum (game-days + tabletop), the responder rota templates, runbook validation checklist, and a small bundle of customer- and status-page templates intended for fast, consistent external communication. It is designed for teams operating Redwood’s model-serving infrastructure and is explicitly scoped to operational readiness (not hiring or policy).

Scope and intended audience

- Scope: full lifecycle of on-call readiness exercises and the artifacts produced (rotas, runbooks, evidence, customer notices).
- Audience: SREs, service owners, support leads, and engineering team leads who run or participate in exercises.

Goals

1. Ensure responders can stabilize common failure modes within SLO objectives.
2. Validate runbook correctness and handover clarity.
3. Practice customer-facing status communication and cadence.
4. Create reproducible artifacts (evidence packages) for compliance and postmortem analysis.

Exercise curriculum overview

- Types of exercises
  - Simulation (live traffic replay to staging): validates autoscaling, throttling, and cache behavior.
  - Tabletop (lead facilitation, no live infra): policy and decision-path validation.
  - Injected-failure game day (chaos experiments in a sandboxed cluster): tests fallback routing and KV cache recovery.
  - Customer-comm drill (status page + incident notification cadence): exercises external messaging.

- Cadence recommendations
  - Quarterly: one injected-failure game day per critical service.
  - Monthly: tabletop for cross-team coordination and runbook review.
  - After each major release: focused simulation for features touching routing, caching, or quantization.

Exercise planning checklist (pre-game)

1. Define objective (e.g., validate canary fallback within 90s).
2. Identify scope (services, environments, traffic subset).
3. Assign roles: facilitator, incident commander (IC), bridge operator, service steward, reporter.
4. Produce an evidence plan (logs, traces, KV cache snapshots, request samples).
5. Publish safety guardrails (blast radius, kill-switch, rollback plan).
6. Notify stakeholders and schedule a 30-minute pre-brief.

Role definitions and rota templates

- Key roles
  - Incident Commander (IC): overall decision authority for the exercise or live incident.
  - Bridge Operator: runs the incident conference bridge / status page posts.
  - Service Steward: subject-matter owner for the failing service or model.
  - Recovery Engineer: implements fixes, rollbacks or mitigations.
  - Customer Liaison: crafts and approves public notifications for customers.

- Example 4-week on-call rota format (CSV-friendly)

| week_start | primary_oncall | secondary_oncall | bridge_operator | notes |
| 2027-01-03 | Priya Nair | Miguel Alvarez | Jordan Kim | primary covers hosted-api
| 2027-01-10 | Arun Khatri | Elena Park | Tessa White | primary covers dedicated capacity

(Teams should store rotas in the shared schedule system and link to the runbook for each service.)

Incident lifecycle & runbook validation pattern

1. Detection: alert fires -> initial triage within first 2 minutes.
2. Triage: IC assigns severity and service steward within 5 minutes.
3. Containment: short-term mitigations (rate-limit, fallback region) within SLO window.
4. Remediation: code/infra changes or rollback.
5. Recovery: verify metrics and synthetic tests pass.
6. Handover: formal postmortem evidence package created and the incident is closed.

Runbook validation checklist (for each runbook)

- Header metadata present: owner, last updated date, slack channel, escalation contacts.
- SLOs and customer impact thresholds defined.
- Clear decision ladder: when to escalate, when to rollback.
- Repro steps for common faults (eg. cache thrash, GPU OOM, model quality regression).
- Minimal commands and examples: kubectl, curl, analysis queries.
- Post-exercise smoke test and verification steps.

Example runbook excerpt: KV cache eviction spike
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: - Sudden drop in token throughput with increased 5xx errors and large KV_cache_miss ratio (>40%).
sections.heading: Incident signal

sections.body:
1. Set primary route to fallback-model-1 and reduce batch sizes.
2. Run: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=cache | grep Evicted
3. Check Redis/remote-KV latency: curl -s http://kv-proxy:9090/metrics | grep kv_latency_ms
4. If whether the KV store is saturated, toggle read-only mode: curl -X POST http://kv-admin/ro-mode
5. Notify bridge and begin customer comm script (see templates below).

Postmortem evidence package (minimum)

- Timeline (UTC) with automated metric spikes and human actions.
- Relevant traces (trace IDs list).
- Logs: filtered by request IDs and pod names.
- Snapshots: KV cache size and configuration, model versions deployed.
- Configuration diffs if a recent deploy exists.

Customer-facing status templates (copy-and-paste ready)

1) Status page initial notice (short)
- Title: Degraded response times for hosted API
- Body: We are investigating increased latency affecting text generation for a subset of requests. Users may see slower responses or occasional 5xx errors. Our team has identified a service-dependency impacting KV cache performance and is actively working on containment. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
- Severity: partial_degradation

2) Status page update (investigation)
- Title: Active mitigation in progress
- Body: We have applied a traffic routing change to fall back to model-variant B for affected requests and reduced batching to lower pressure. Error rates are down ~60%; latency is improving but not yet back to baseline. Estimated next update: 60 minutes.

3) Customer notification (email) — brief
Subject: Service update: latency affecting model responses
sections.heading: Immediate actions (IC / Service Steward)

sections.body:
Hi —
We experienced elevated latency impacting a subset of text generation requests between 14:12–14:45 UTC. We applied a routing mitigation and validated recovery at 14:53 UTC. No data was lost.
If you rely on strict latency, consider pinning to a dedicated capacity plan or enabling our reduced-batch routing config (see KB: /internal/ops/reduced-batch-config).
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support

Internal status post template (Slack / Ops bridge)

- Subject: [INCIDENT] {service} {severity} — short summary
- Body:
  - Detection time: {UTC}
  - Current state: {investigating | mitigating | recovered}
  - Action taken: {fallback routing applied, batch size reduced, canary rolled back}
  - Assigned: IC={name}, Steward={name}, Bridge={name}
  - Next update: +30m or on state change

Post-exercise & post-incident learning loop

1. Capture a 1–2 page incident summary with root cause hypothesis and what worked/who was impeded.
2. Upload evidence package to the incident folder and tag the postmortem ticket.
3. Runbook edits: assign owner to implement fixes within 7 business days or raise a backlog ticket.
4. Training update: schedule a targeted 60-minute lab for any recurring tooling gaps.
5. Metrics review: check for false-positive alerts and adjust thresholds.

Table: SLO examples and action thresholds

| SLO name | Target | Alert threshold | Action |
| API p95 latency | < 200ms | p95 > 350ms for 5m | Trigger incident, notify IC |
| Model-serving error rate | < 0.5% | 5xx > 2% for 3m | Route to fallback-model, engage steward |
| Embedding throughput | >= 500 qps | sustained drop > 50% | Check autoscaling and GPU health |

Game day safety principles

- Always run destructive experiments in a sandbox or staging cluster unless pre-authorized.
- Provide a live kill-switch and a tested rollback plan before injecting faults.
- Limit blast radius to a single customer tenant where possible during partial tests.
- Keep customer liaison in the loop for any public-impacting simulations.

Evidence retention and postmortem governance

- Evidence packages must be retained for 12 months for auditability.
- High-severity incidents (SEV2/SEV1): postmortem published within 7 business days; follow-up action owner assigned.
- Quarterly executive digest to summarize recurring failure modes and remediation progress.

Appendix: links and artifacts (examples)

- Runbook template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-template-2025
- Incident evidence repository: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/editor
- Shared rota calendar: https://calendar.redwood.ai/oncall

Contact and ownership

- Document owner: Samantha Lee (slee@redwood.ai)
- Primary maintainers: eng-sre team
- Review cycle: yearly or after any SEV1 incident

payload.page_title: Developer Oncall Field Manual — Status Scripts & Postmortem Cadence

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This manual is a compact, developer-focused reference for first responders and bridge operators who run, stabilize, and close incidents affecting inference traffic. It combines:
- A concise incident lifecycle that matches our incident tooling and status page model.
- Reusable Slack + status-page message templates for internal and customer communication.
- Practical runbook actions for common LLM-serving degradations (latency SLO regressions, 5xx bursts, KV-cache storms, and throttling).
- A lightweight postmortem cadence and evidence checklist to ensure corrective action and measurable risk reduction.

Why this doc exists
- Reduce cognitive load for developer-oncall: follow-step guidance with safe defaults.
- Standardize external messaging to avoid conflicting customer updates.
- Make post-incident learning reliable: evidence captured during the first hour so root causes are reproducible.

Ownership & contact matrix
------------------------
- Primary owner (oncall bridge): Bridge Conductor (role).
- Primary technical responder: Service Owner oncall (team-specific pager).
- Escalation: Runtime Engineering (pager), SRE Escalation (pager).
- Executive notification: Director of Eng (on severe incidents only).

Quick contact (for bridge operator)
Role | Primary | Backup
-----|---------|-------
Bridge Conductor | marcos-bridge@redwood.ai | ops-bot@redwood.ai
Service Owner | svc-owner@redwood.ai | team-oncall@redwood.ai
Runtime Eng | runtime-pager@redwood.ai | runtime-backup@redwood.ai
SRE Escalation | sre-lead@redwood.ai | sre-oncall@redwood.ai

Incident lifecycle (concise)
---------------------------
1) Detect
   - Signals: SLO alert, synthetic failure, external customer report, monitoring anomaly.
   - Default detection channel: PagerDuty -> Slack #incidents -> start bridge.
2) Acknowledge (first 10 minutes)
   - Bridge Conductor acknowledges incident in PagerDuty and posts initial status.
   - Triage with Service Owner to classify impact (P0/P1/P2).
3) Stabilize (first 60 minutes)
   - Apply pre-approved mitigations from runbooks.
   - If mitigation reduces customer impact, escalate to restoration.
4) Restore
   - Apply permanent or near-term fixes (rollbacks, config flips, capacity augment).
   - Monitor SLOs and customer signals.
5) Postmortem & Corrective Actions
   - 24h quick blameless summary; 7-day deep postmortem for P0/P1 incidents.

Severity definitions & SLAs (selected)
------------------------------------
- P0: Platform-wide outage affecting >= 10% of production tokens or persistent > 30s request latency for > 5% of requests for 15+ minutes.
- P1: Significant degradation for a subset of customers or sustained error-rate increase > 3% above baseline for 10+ minutes.
- P2: Localized impact, single-region or tenant, intermittent errors or performance blips.

SLO examples (for runtime teams)
Metric | Target | Alert threshold
-------|--------|----------------
Gen latency (p95, 2k tokens) | <= 350ms | p95 > 450ms for 5m
End-to-end 5xx rate | <= 0.5% | 5xx > 1.5% for 3m
KV cache miss ratio | <= 8% | miss ratio > 15% for 10m

Runbook: Rapid KV cache storm (common failure pattern)
----------------------------------------------------
Goal: Reduce fanout and restore tail latency while preserving customer throughput.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Confirm: check cache miss ratio + recent redeploys.
   - Metrics: cache_miss_ratio (dash), latency_p95_by_model.
2. Short-term (first 5-15m): enable per-model conservative caching policy.
   - CLI: rcli cache set-policy --model <model> --policy conservative
3. Reduce batching window for affected workers (reduces tail latency).
   - k8s: kubectl -n runtime patch deploy worker-<pool> --patch '{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"worker\",\"env\":[{\"name\":\"BATCH_WINDOW_MS\",\"value\":\"50\"}] }]}}}}'
4. If CPU saturates: divert traffic to smaller sequence-length tuned model variant.
   - Routing command: rcli route set --service inference --model <model>-latency-variant
5. If instability persists >30m, engage Runtime Eng for emergency capacity scale (add GPU pool).

Runbook: 5xx burst (model OOM or library crash)
---------------------------------------------
1. Identify top failing path: Sentry + access logs.
2. If model OOM suspected, set fallback-mode: use quantized variant and pin instance reuse:
   - rcli runtime set --fallback-model <model>-q4 --reuse-kv true
3. If crash on new deploy: roll back to last known-good image.
   - k8s: kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=<rev>
4. Post-restore: increase crashloop backoff and mark deploy for postmortem.

Safe internal messaging (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------
- Bridge message (Slack #incidents):
  "INCIDENT | [P0/P1] | <short summary>\n   Bridge: @bridge-conductor-name\n   Impact: <high-level customer-facing impact>\n   Next update: in 15 minutes or when customer-visible state changes."

- Pager/owner ack snippet:
  "Acknowledged. Triage in progress. Primary lead: @svc-owner. Running runbook: <name>."

Customer-facing status page templates
------------------------------------
Use the short template for the first public notice; expand in subsequent updates.
1) Initial public status (short):
   "Redwood Inference is investigating elevated errors affecting text-generation requests in us-west-2. We are actively triaging and will provide updates within 15 minutes. Impact: a subset of customers may experience increased latency or 5xx responses."
2) Follow-up status (if mitigated):
   "We have identified a KV cache warm-up pattern causing tail latency. We applied conservative caching and reduced batch windows; error rates have decreased. We are monitoring; no customer action required. ETA for full restoration: 1-2 hours."
3) Post-incident summary (public):
   "Incident on YYYY-MM-DD caused by a cache storm triggered by a model routing change. Mitigations included policy rollback and conservative caching. Root cause analysis and mitigation plan published (internal)."

Slack templates (bridge -> cs/comm)
---------------------------------
- For CS teams (internal):
  "CS-ALERT: [INCIDENT P1] <short summary>. Expected customer impact: <list>. Suggested response lines: <one-sentence guidance>. Contact bridge: @bridge-conductor."
- For Execs (private channel):
  "Exec Notice: P0 incident impacting production inference (start: <time>, scope: <percent tokens>). Remediation in progress. Will escalate if > 90 minutes."

Postmortem cadence & artifact checklist
--------------------------------------
- P0/P1: 7-day deep postmortem required. 24-hour blameless incident summary published to #postmortems within 24h.
- P2: Quick 72h summary with owner action item list.

Required postmortem evidence (must be attached)
- PagerDuty timeline export (CSV)
- Bridge Slack transcript (first 24 minutes)
- Monitoring graphs: latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cache miss ratio for the affected timeframe
- Deploy history (git SHA + k8s revision)
- Synthetic test results run across affected endpoints

Postmortem template (short)
- Title, Impact summary, Detection timeline, Root cause, Mitigation, Action items (owner + due date), Postmortem author, Triage reviewer.

On-call rotation & human factors guidance
----------------------------------------
- Standard rotation: 7-day oncall for engineers. Short swaps allowed with 48h notice and replacement documented on the rota.
- Shadowing: 2-week shadow window for new oncallers.
- Handover: at shift start, the previous oncaller must post a 10-line summary: outstanding tickets, ongoing experiments, flagged deploys.
- Burnout safeguards: max 3 consecutive weeks as primary oncall. Temporary augment budget available (1 engineer/day) for high-severity incidents lasting >72h.

Game days and simulation design (recommended)
-------------------------------------------
- Cadence: quarterly game days per team; 2 focused scenarios per game day (one KV-cache-style, one capacity-throttle).
- Objectives: validate runbook actions under stress, verify bridge messaging templates, measure MTTR and evidence capture.
- Scoring (simple):
  - Detection time (0-10)
  - Acknowledge & bridge up (0-10)
  - First mitigation applied (0-10)
  - Evidence completeness (0-10)
  - Customer messaging accuracy (0-10)
- Post-game deliverable: improvement backlog + 1 targeted automation (e.g., auto-cache-policy flip, synthetic alert refinement).

Runbook hygiene & governance
---------------------------
- Every runbook must have: owner, last-run timestamp, last-validation timestamp.
- Validation: runbook dry-run during team game day at least once every 6 months.
- Decommission: runbooks not executed or validated for 18 months must be archived and reviewed before reuse.

Escalation SLA (internal)
------------------------
- P0: bridge up within 5 minutes, Runtime Eng oncall paged within 7 minutes.
- P1: bridge up within 10 minutes, Service Owner paged within 15 minutes.
- P2: triage within 30 minutes.

Appendices
---------
A) Commands quick reference
- rcli cache set-policy --model <model> --policy conservative
- rcli route set --service inference --model <model>-latency-variant
- kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=<rev>
- rcli runtime set --fallback-model <model>-q4 --reuse-kv true

B) Customer messaging examples (copy-paste-ready)
- Initial: "We’re investigating increased error rates affecting generation in <region>. We will update in 15 minutes."
- Mid-incident: "Mitigation applied. Error rates decreased by ~80% vs peak; monitoring to confirm full restoration (ETA 1–2h)."
- Closure public: "Root cause identified as a cache warming pattern; mitigation plan implemented. We will roll out a permanent fix by <date>. Contact support@redwood.ai for tenant-specific impact."

C) Postmortem owner rotation (process)
- The service owner assigns a postmortem author within 48 hours. If unassigned, Bridge Conductor defaults as author.
- Action items must have owners and target completion dates; overdue items reviewed at weekly reliability sync.

Revision history
---------------
- 2026-01-12 — created by Marcus Nguyen (published)
- 2026-04-02 — reviewer feedback: clarified KV-cache thresholds and added CLI snippets (Priya Raman)
- 2026-06-15 — added game-day scoring rubric and tightened escalation SLA (Ethan Cole)

Related reference pages
- Bridge conductor script and legal-safe phrasing (link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/bridge-runway-stabilization-sprint-playbook-2029)
- Forensic evidence & deploy history (link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-chain-and-forensic-runbook-2025)

End of manual
------------
For questions or to propose changes, open a PR against this page and ping @Marcus in #ops-docs.

payload.page_title: Incident Anticipation and Rapid Triage Sprint Guide

sections.body: This guide prescribes a compact, repeatable process to anticipate common failure modes, run short triage sprints, and deliver consistent customer-facing status updates. It is targeted at responders (first-on-call engineers, SRE/Platform), service owners, and the incident bridge operator. Use this as a canonical checklist for incidents where fast containment and measured customer comms are the priority (Priority P1/P2).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to Redwood inference services: API gateway, serving runtime, autoscaler, and KV cache layers.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks; instead, it prescribes the sprint and coordination primitives used to invoke runbooks and communicate externally.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1) Restore a safe operating envelope within 15 minutes for P1 events (partial or full service outage).
2) Provide a clear status narrative to customers and leadership within 30 minutes.
3) Capture structured evidence for a postmortem within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Key objectives

sections.body:
- First Responder: acknowledge alerts, run diagnostics, escalate to Bridge if unresolved in 10 minutes.
- Bridge Operator: orchestrates communications, opens bridge (Zoom/Slack huddle), publishes status page updates, owns incident timeline.
- Service Owner: advises on rollback/runbook steps, signs any tenant-impacting changes.
- SRE Lead: approves cross-service mitigations (traffic shifts, capacity reallocation).
sections.heading: Roles & responsibilities (quick reference)

sections.body:
| Severity | Symptoms | Immediate target | Bridge required |
| P0 | Total outage affecting >= 90% of traffic | 15 min restore or mitigation | Yes (full incident bridge) |
| P1 | Significant degradation impacting core customers | Contain in 15 min, restore in 1 hour | Yes |
| P2 | Partial, non-critical degradation | Fix within 24 hours | Optional |
(When in doubt classify conservatively — prefer P1 for multi-tenant customer-facing regressions.)

Rapid Triage Sprint — checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge & annotate: first responder sets incident labels (service, region, error class) in the incident tracker and records initial symptoms (top logs, recent deploys).
2) Bridge & channel: Bridge Operator creates incident channel (Slack #bridge-<id>) and a temporary doc (Incident Sprint Sheet) with visible fields: severity, impacted customers, start time, first actions.
3) Quick smoke tests: run the canonical health-check and the top 3 synthetic queries used in SLO monitoring.
4) Verify recent changes: CI/CD deploys (last 60m), infra changes, config pushes.
5) Execute containment if safe: scale up dedicated pool, disable autoscaler bursts, or activate read-only mode for internal control plane. Document every step.
sections.heading: Incident classification matrix (summary)

sections.body:
- When a triage sprint identifies a root cause candidate, follow "One-Action Rule": take one safe mitigation (e.g., redirect traffic) and observe for five minutes. No two independent risky changes in parallel.
- Push results to the Incident Sprint Sheet with precise command lines and config diffs. Include expected rollback steps.
sections.heading: Runbook invocation pattern (how to call service runbooks)

sections.body:
1) T+0–10m: Escalate to Bridge if triage unresolved.
2) T+10–30m: Bring in Service Owner and SRE Lead.
3) T+30–60m: Executive on-call notified for P0/P1 if customer impact persists; start cross-service mitigation run.
sections.heading: Escalation ladder (timed)

sections.body:
- Snapshot logs (5 minute windows) for gateway, runtime, autoscaler.
- Capture top 20 noisy stack traces and error keys.
- Snapshot metrics (qps,  p50/p95 latency, error rate) and recent config state (feature flags, host pools).
- Preserve the failing VM/container/actor for postmortem if possible.

Status page & customer communications templates (use verbatim where applicable):
Template: Short initial status (for status.redwood.ai and customer emails)
Subject: "[Status] Degraded inference responses — investigating (service: <service>, region: <region>)"
sections.heading: Evidence collection & quick-forensics checklist

sections.body:
We are aware of degraded responses affecting <service> in <region>. Our engineers are investigating. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Next update: <T+30m>. If you are seeing significant customer impact please reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai with your tenant id.

Template: 30-minute update (if mitigations in progress)
Subject: "[Update] Mitigation underway — partial recovery observed"
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
Mitigation: We have applied <mitigation> (e.g., increased dedicated pool, routed traffic away from noisy host). We are seeing partial recovery: success rate improved from X% to Y% and latency p95 reduced from A ms to B ms. We continue to monitor across regions. Estimated next update: <T+60m>.

Template: Post-incident customer summary (short)
Subject: "[Resolved] Service disruption affecting <service> — summary and impact"
sections.heading: Body

sections.body: Summary: The incident began at <start time> and was resolved at <end time>. Root cause: <short cause>. Impact: <brief impact numbers> (e.g., 12% of requests failed, customers in EU-1 experienced elevated latency). Mitigation: <actions taken>. Actions we will take: <1–3 concrete actions and timeline>. If you need tenant-specific evidence contact your CSM.
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
Purpose: validate rapid triage and status cadence without disrupting production.
Plan (45–90 minutes):
- Pregame: select an injected failure (e.g., KV cache eviction storm, autoscaler underrun, model fallback error) and verify synthetic monitors fire.
- Execution: first responder runs through the Rapid Triage Sprint checklist; Bridge Operator publishes two status updates (initial & 30m).
- Postgame: 30 min retrospective focusing on comms clarity and time-to-first-action.
Metrics to capture: time-to-ack, time-to-bridge, time-to-first-mitigation, quality of status message (peer-rated).
sections.heading: Game day / Simulation playbook (biweekly micro-sprints)

sections.body:
- Primary oncall: 7-day cadence for responders in SRE/Platform team.
- Secondary: 7-day cadence offset by 3 days to ensure overlap.
- Bridge duty: weekly rotation for engineers signed up on Bridge roster.
sections.heading: Rotation cadence & handoff template

sections.body:
1) Confirm no active incidents or hand over open bridges with a summary.
2) Share any ongoing mitigations, TTLs on rate limits, and next scheduled tasks.
3) Update the oncall calendar and incident tracker with notes.
sections.heading: Handoff checklist (before stepping down)

sections.body:
- Title, severity, start/end timestamps, services impacted, customer impact notes.
- Timeline: minute-level timeline for first hour, 5–15 minute buckets thereafter.
- Root cause analysis: short causal chain and why safeguards failed.
- Remediation plan: owner, priority, due date.
- Lessons learned & runbook updates required (link to runbook).
- Evidence attachments: logs, dashboard snapshots, code/config diffs.
sections.heading: Postmortem scaffold (must be completed within 72 hours)

sections.body:
- Every runbook must declare: owner (persona), last-reviewed date, and a test vector (synthetic query and expected response).
- Quarterly review: owners run a live validation during a game day.
- Deprecation policy: if no owner or no test vector for >6 months mark runbook for retirement.
sections.heading: Runbook hygiene & ownership

sections.body:
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target: < 2 minutes for pager alerts.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM): < 15 minutes for P1.
- Post-incident action completion rate: 100% tracked to owners within 30 days.

Appendix: Useful commands & dashboards (examples)
- CI/CD: curl -sS https://ci.redwood.ai/api/v1/latest-deploys?service=<service>
- Health checks: curl -sS https://<service>.<region>.redwood.ai/ready | jq .status
- Dashboards: torq.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime-overview and torq.redwood.ai/d/alerts/incident-runner
