payload.page_title: Service Outage Coordination and Stakeholder Briefing Kit

sections.body:
Summary

This kit centralizes procedures, templates, and checklists for coordinating a multi-team service outage at Redwood Inference. It is intended for Incident Leads, Communication Leads, SRE responders, Customer Success, and Product managers who must rapidly align external and internal communications while preserving incident evidence and SLO context.

Purpose

- Provide a single source of truth for: incident coordination timeline, stakeholder briefings, external status updates, and post-incident handoff.
- Reduce variance between incidents so that customers and executives receive clear, consistent, and timely information.

Scope

Applies to all incidents that meet Severity S0–S2 (see definitions below). Minor operational items (S3) should still use the internal incident-to-task flow but do not normally require external comms unless customer impact is observed.

Key Principles

1. Fast alignment over perfect detail: publish an initial external status within 15 minutes for S0/S1/S2 incidents.
2. Single source of truth: the Incident Lead owns the incident timeline and status page copy.
3. Clear ownership of comms: Communication Lead drafts external messages; Customer Success reviews for customer-specific impacts.

Incident coordination workflow (high level)

1) Detection & Triage (0–5 minutes)
   - Pager/alert to on-call responder.
   - On-call responder confirms reproducibility and initial impact.
   - If confirmed and impact >= S2, escalate to Incident Lead.

2) Mobilize (5–15 minutes)
   - Incident Lead declares incident, assigns roles (Incident Lead, Comm Lead, Primary Responder, Secondary Responder, Scribe).
   - Create incident run channel (Slack #incident-<service>-YYYYMMDD-001).
   - Open incident doc in the incident tracker (link template provided in Appendix).

3) Notify & Publish Initial Status (<=15 minutes for S0–S2)
   - Comm Lead prepares initial status using the template below and posts to status.redwood.ai and customer-facing channels.
   - Internal all-hands notification to execs and product-owner mailing list.

4) Contain & Mitigate (15–90 minutes)
   - Run troubleshooting playbooks.
   - Execute mitigations (rollbacks, routing changes, capacity surge) as approved by Incident Lead.
   - Log actions in timeline with timestamps and owners.

5) Recovery & Verification (90–240 minutes)
   - Validate service health and SLO metrics for 15–30 minutes before declaring recovery.
   - Comm Lead updates status with mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem.

6) Close & Postmortem (within 72 hours)
   - Incident Lead files a post-incident summary.
   - Postmortem reviewers assigned; learnings scheduled into the roadmap or runbook backlog.

Roles & responsibilities

- Incident Lead (usually senior SRE or service owner)
  - Declares incident severity and timeline, approves external messages, coordinates escalations.

- Communication Lead (SRE + Customer Success rotation)
  - Drafts and publishes status page updates, customer emails, and exec briefs.

- Primary Responder(s)
  - Executes technical mitigations and documents commands/actions.

- Secondary Responder
  - Shadow and pick up tasks or take over if primary becomes unavailable.

- Scribe
  - Maintains the incident timeline, captures logs, and preserves evidence for postmortem.

Severity definitions & SLO impact

- S0: Complete outage impacting all customers or critical internal systems; targeted human response immediately.
- S1: Major degradation affecting a subset of customers or some critical functionality; high priority.
- S2: Partial degradation with increased error rates/latency but workarounds exist; requires attention.
- S3: Functional degradation with limited or no customer impact; tracked as an engineering ticket.

Table: quick reference (as plain text)

Severity | Typical symptoms | Initial comms required | SLA impact threshold
S0 | 100% errors or unavailable | Status page + email + outreach | Major SLA breach, exec notified
S1 | Large fraction customers affected | Status page + scheduled updates | Potential SLA exposure
S2 | Partial errors/latency | Status page entry + internal brief | Monitor for SLA drift
S3 | Low impact | Internal ticket | No SLA impact

Immediate actions (first 15 minutes)

1. Confirm incident and severity.
2. Incident Lead: create channel and incident doc.
3. Comm Lead: draft initial status (see template).
4. Primary Responder: capture `top`/`iostat`/`nvidia-smi` and save output to incident doc.
5. Scribe: begin timeline with timestamps and owners.

External communications cadence and templates

Guidelines
- Use clear, non-technical language for customers; include technical details in an "Expanded Details" section for interested engineering contacts.
- Every external update should include: impact summary, affected services/customers, mitigation steps in-progress, ETA for next update.
- Publish updates on the status page first, then mirror to email/slack/CS signals as appropriate.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Title: Service disruption impacting <service-name>
Status: Identified
Started: <ISO timestamp>
Impact: Users may experience <description of impact>. We are investigating and will provide updates every <N> minutes.
Mitigation: Our engineers are actively investigating.
Next update: <time window, e.g., 30 minutes>
sections.heading: Initial status (status page) template (use plain text)

sections.body:
Subject: Incident affecting <service-name> – we are investigating

Hi <CustomerName>,

We are investigating an issue impacting <service-name> that may affect your requests. Our team is actively working on mitigation and we will share updates via https://status.redwood.ai.

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with details and an ETA as soon as possible.

— Redwood Inference Support

Periodic update template (status page)

Status: Investigating / Mitigating / Identified
Update time: <ISO timestamp>
Summary: Short recap of progress since last update.
Actions taken: List of mitigation steps and owner initials.
Next update: <time or ‘when more info available’>

Final update template

Status: Resolved
Resolved: <ISO timestamp>
Summary: Brief explanation of root cause and remediation applied.
Customer impact: Which customers/features were affected and duration.
Follow-up: Postmortem will be published to <link> within <X> business days.

Internal briefing: executive one-pager (30–60 lines max)

- Incident ID: INC-<service>-YYYYMMDD-xxx
- Severity: S0|S1|S2
- Start/End times: <ISO> / <ISO or ongoing>
- Impact summary: concise sentence(s) describing customer/business impact
- Root cause hypothesis: short bullet(s)
- Actions taken: top 3 mitigations and outcomes
- Customer outreach: who was contacted and when
- Next steps: postmortem owner and ETA, compensation evaluation if applicable

Post-incident handoff checklist (prior to closing ticket)

1. Ensure system metrics are stable for 30 minutes (error rate and latency).
2. Archive logs and attach to incident doc (retention policy note: preserve logs for 90 days).
3. Identify action items and owners; create tickets with priority and due dates.
4. Schedule postmortem review session within 72 hours.

Game day & rotation tie-ins

- Quarterly game days will exercise the coordination flow in this kit; rotation teams should use the exact templates and timing windows to validate SLAs and comms latency.
- New on-call hires must shadow two incidents and run one tabletop exercise before independent rotation.

Appendix A: escalation contacts (plain table)

Role | Name | Pager / Slack handle | Backup
Incident Lead | Aisha Patel | pager: pg-aisha | Marcus Chen
Comm Lead | Lucia Romero | slack: @lucia | Darren O'Neill
On-call SRE | rotation | rotation | rotation
Customer Success Pager | cs-pager | cs@redwood.ai | account-ops

Appendix B: sample status page JSON payload (example for engineering use only)

{
  "incident_id": "INC-service-20260120-001",
  "status": "identified",
  "started_at": "2026-01-20T10:12:00Z",
  "summary": "Service generation requests are returning 5xx errors for some regions.",
  "updates": [
    {"at": "2026-01-20T10:15:00Z", "message": "Investigating - engineering triage in progress"}
  ]
}

Appendix C: common troubleshooting commands (copy into incident doc)

- Kubernetes: kubectl -n <ns> get pods -o wide
- Logs: rg -n "ERROR|exception" /var/log/service/*.log | head -n 200
- GPU health: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv

Retention & evidence handling

- All incident artifacts (timelines, logs, runbook snapshots) must be stored in the incident repo for at least 90 days.
- For incidents with customer data exposure, follow security-and-compliance/data-incident-guidance and mark the incident confidentiality as restricted.

Governance & continuous improvement

- Every S0/S1 incident triggers a mandatory postmortem review with exec presence.
- Action items from postmortems must be tracked in the engineering backlog and triaged by owners within two sprints.

How to use this kit in a live incident

1. Read the Immediate actions section and choose the correct template for comms.
2. Use the incident channel naming convention to ensure discoverability.
3. Keep messages short and time-stamped; the scribe should post the timeline to the incident doc every 15 minutes.

Document maintenance

- Owner: Incident Response Guild (eng-sre).
- Review cadence: annual or after any S0 incident.
- Suggested updates: add service-specific mitigations and contacts per-quarter.
sections.heading: Customer email (short) template

payload.page_title: Observer lifecycle and incident runloop for LLM serving

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the end-to-end observer lifecycle and incident runloop for Redwood's model-serving surface (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and bundles runbooks, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation guidance, game day templates, and status/ customer communication examples. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, support, and product owners.

Scope: model-serving API endpoints, inference runtime clusters, KV/prefix caching, routing/fallback policies, and the components that directly impact inference SLOs (p95 latency, error-rate, availability). This doc does NOT cover: billing incidents, non-inference control plane failures, or infra provider outages (those are covered under eng-sre/runbooks).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Runbook: High-latency model-serving cluster (below)
- Postmortem template (section: Postmortem & RCA)
- Status templates (section: Status & customer comms)

1) Roles and responsibilities

- Primary on-call (Responder): first investigator and owner of the incident until carrier handoff. Responsible for initial triage, mitigation, and comms.
- Bridge operator (if invoked): runs the incident bridge, coordinates stakeholders, and keeps a public running summary.
- Escalation on-call (Area owner): team-level escalation for service-specific fixes (e.g., runtime, routing, infra).
- SRE incident lead: validates mitigations, authorizes wider mitigations (e.g., autoscaler changes, capacity swaps).
- Customer-facing comms (Support / CS): drafts and publishes customer messages using the status templates.

2) Severity classification and SLO thresholds

We use a simple three-tier severity system for model-serving incidents. Severity should be assigned during triage and visible on the incident ticket and status page.

Severity | Definition | Target response | Escalation window
---------|------------|-----------------|-------------------
P1       | Large-scale outage: >25% of production requests affected OR p95 latency >5x SLO for >5 min | Acknowledge within 2 min | Escalate to SRE & product within 10 min
P2       | Partial outage / customer impact: single region or class degraded, p95 latency 2–5x SLO | Acknowledge within 15 min | Escalate within 60 min if unresolved
P3       | Localized or performance regression with mitigation available; no major customer disruption | Acknowledge within 2 hours | Triage in next business day
sections.heading: Quick links

sections.body:
- p95 latency: 250 ms (hosted small models)
- error-rate: <0.2% (5xx + timeouts measured at API edge)
- availability: 99.95% monthly

3) Incident lifecycle and runloop (step-by-step)

1. Signal and detection
   - Alerts originate from metrics (Prometheus), tracing anomalies (Jaeger), and customer reports. Priority to signals that touch p95 and error-rate.
   - Initial evidence to capture: top-5 alert graphs, time window, affected regions, model(s), recent deploys, and increase in queue depth.

2. Acknowledge & declare
   - Primary on-call acknowledges the alert in the paging system within the severity window.
   - If P1/P2, stand up incident bridge (Zoom/Google Meet) and create the incident ticket in Jira/Status (template).

3. Triage (first 10 min)
   - Determine blast radius: region(s), customer subsets, models, routing tiers.
   - Check recent deploys: Git commit, rollout ID. If deployment <15 minutes prior, suspect rollout.
   - Check autoscaling events, GPU preemption events, and queue backlog.

4. Mitigate (minutes -> hours)
   - Preferred mitigations: graceful fallback to compatible model variant, reduce QPS via routing policy, enable prefix cache, increase concurrency on affected nodes, or scale reserve pool.
   - If mitigation applied, verify p95 and error-rate returning toward SLO.

5. Stabilize & communicate
   - Once p95 within acceptable range or a durable mitigation is in place, move to ‘stabilize’. Post an initial status update: summary, impact, next steps, ETA for mitigation, and owner.

6. Recovery & post-incident work
   - After service is stable for the confirmation window (30–60 minutes), close the incident with a remediation plan and schedule a postmortem.

4) Decision ladders & escalation matrix (cheat-sheet)

- If p95 > 2x SLO for >10 min AND error-rate increasing: escalate to SRE incident lead.
- If queue depth > 10x baseline and tail latency rises: trigger capacity augmentation (add reserved nodes) and notify infra.
- If rollout suspected: immediately pause rollout and roll back if safe.

5) Runbook: High-latency model-serving cluster (operational run steps)

Scope: used by on-call for cross-region high p95 or persistent tail latency.
sections.heading: SLOs (example)

sections.body:
1. Collect evidence (commands/queries):
   - kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=model-serving -o wide
   - prometheus query: rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) and topk(10, increase(request_errors_total[5m]))
   - curl -sS "https://observability.internal/api/top-traces?service=model-serving&window=5m"
2. Check recent rollouts:
   - deployctl history runtime/model-serving --since 30m
3. Inspect node resources:
   - nvidia-smi (on affected nodes)
   - kubectl describe pod <pod> | egrep -i "OOM|Evicted|Preempt"
4. Apply quick mitigations:
   - Toggle runtime-routing to fallback pool: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/route/update -d '{"policy":"fallback","target_pool":"reserve"}'
   - Increase concurrency for model-serving: k8s patch deployment runtime/model-serving -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"inference","env":[{"name":"MAX_CONCURRENCY","value":"64"}]}}]}}}'
5. Verify: run synthetic load for the affected model variant (locally or from staging runner) and measure p95.
sections.heading: Immediate checklist (order matters)

sections.body:
- p95, p50, p99 latency for affected model(s)
- API 5xx & 429 counts (edge and runtime)
- Queue depth and average queue time
- CPU/GPU utilization by node pool

6) Runbook: Capacity exhaustion and noisy neighbor containment

Symptoms: increasing queue length, marginal requests failing with timeouts, noisy processes consuming GPU memory.
sections.heading: Important metrics to include in the incident ticket

sections.body:
1. Identify noisy pod(s): kubectl top pod --all-namespaces --containers | sort -r -k3
2. Throttle noisy customers via routing tags: controlplane route throttle --tag customer:cust-123 --rate 10rps
3. Spin up reserved nodes (if autoscale not available): terraform apply -var='reserved_pool=3' -target=module.gpu_pool
4. Schedule controlled eviction for confirmed memory leaks (drain node and cordon).

7) Postmortem & RCA process (requirements and template)
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Postmortem draft due: within 72 hours of incident stabilization for P1/P2; within 14 days for P3.
- Action items assigned with owners and deadlines within the postmortem.
- Severity re-evaluation: PM and SRE must agree on severity and external communications.
sections.heading: Timeline requirements

sections.body:
- Title (concise)
- Incident ID, Severity, Start/End timestamps
- Summary: 2–3 sentence impact statement
- Timeline: minute-level timeline for first 60 minutes, then hourly
- Root cause: contributing factors, single root cause statement
- Corrective actions: short-term mitigations + long-term fixes (owner + due date)
- Follow-up: automation, test coverage, monitoring additions, runbook updates
- Customer impact and communications log (include status page and support tickets)

8) On-call rotations, handoffs, and tooling
sections.heading: Postmortem template (use as checklist)

sections.body:
- Primary rotation cadence: 1-week primary, 1-week secondary (shadow), then 2 weeks off.
- Handoff window: 30-minute overlap between shifts for verbal handoff and ticket review.
- Coverage for holidays: distributed on-call with explicit backup; team lead must approve changes 1 week in advance.
sections.heading: Rotation policy (recommended)

sections.body:
- Review open incidents and priority tickets
- Check ‘health check’ dashboard: tail latency, error-rate, queue backlog, GPU pool utilization, status-page open incidents
- Confirm calendar availability and Slack contact info
sections.heading: Handoff checklist

sections.body:
- Acknowledge page: pagerctl ack <alert-id>
- Open incident ticket: incidentctl create --service model-serving --severity P1 --summary "<short>"
- Mute noisy alert rule: alertctl mute --rule <rule-name> --expires 15m (document reason)

9) Game day playbook (quarterly exercise template)

Goals: validate runbooks, test capacity augment workflows, exercise customer comms and incident bridge procedures.

Duration: 4 hours (wall time)
Participants: at least 2 on-call engineers, 1 SRE incident lead, 1 product lead, 1 support rep
sections.heading: On-call tooling quick commands

sections.body:
- Sudden p95 spike in US-West after a model rollout
- Reserve pool exhausted with queuing in Dedicated customers
- Cache invalidation leading to mass cold starts and tail latency increase
sections.heading: Scenarios (pick 2 per game day)

sections.body:
1. Pre-brief: scope and inject points, safety checklist (no real customer traffic will be impacted—use staging or canary traffic).
2. Inject: simulated traffic pattern or toggle a feature flag to emulate failure.
3. Observe: measure detection time, triage time, mitigation time.
4. Review: collect timings, update runbooks, publish a 1-page after-action note.

10) Status page & customer communication templates
sections.heading: Game day checklist

sections.body:
- Be timely, factual, and concise.
- Use three updates: Acknowledged, Mitigating, Resolved.
- Include impact scope, affected models/regions, workaround, ETA if known, and owner contact.
sections.heading: Status page principles

sections.body:
- Acknowledged (first post):
  Title: Elevated inference latency impacting hosted API (US-West)
  Body: We are investigating elevated p95 latency for text generation requests in US-West beginning at 2026-01-12T11:04Z. Impact: ~35% of requests experiencing elevated tail latency. Owner: Alex Chen. Next update: 11:20Z.

- Mitigating (follow-up):
  Title: Mitigation in progress — routing to reserve pool enabled
  Body: We have enabled fallback routing to a reserve node pool which has reduced the observed p95 by ~60%. We continue monitoring. Some customers on Dedicated may see brief increased queuing. ETA to stabilize: 30–45 minutes.

- Resolved:
  Title: Resolved — latency returned to expected levels
  Body: The fallback routing and a rollout pause resolved the incident. No further action required. We are scheduling a postmortem and will publish details within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Status page examples (short)

sections.body: Subject: Incident update — Inference latency (region US-West)
sections.heading: Customer email template (for affected large customers)

payload.page_title: Cross-Functional Incident Rehearsal and Customer Liaison Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable, cross-functional incident rehearsal (game day) and operational playbook that foregrounds the Customer Liaison role. It covers the lifecycle from detection to postmortem for incidents that materially affect customer-facing inference throughput, latency SLOs, or safety/fidelity regressions.

Audience: SRE, Platform, Support, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Customer Success.

Scope: Tiered incidents that meet the criteria in the Incident Classification Matrix below (Severity 1/2/3 definitions). This playbook focuses on coordination patterns, customer status messaging cadence, role responsibilities, and rehearsal scenarios.

When to use this playbook

- Use as the runbook for multi-team incidents affecting customer SLAs, persistent latency regressions, or sustained model-quality regressions.
- Use as the template for scheduled game days and for onboarding customer liaison participants.

Incident classification matrix\n
| Severity | Customer impact examples | Immediate actions | SLO/threshold examples | Typical escalation path |
|---------:|-------------------------|-------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| Sev 1 | Platform outage for hosted API (multiple regions) or Dedicated capacity unavailable | Bridge & all-hands, customer status within 15m | Availability < 99.5% or P99 latency > 5s global | Pager -> SRE lead -> Eng oncall -> Exec notif |
| Sev 2 | Significant feature degradation affecting subset of customers | Triage, partial mitigation, status within 30m | Error rate spike > 5% sustained, single-region P95 latency > 3s | Pager -> Platform -> Customer Liaison -> Product |
| Sev 3 | Intermittent customer-facing anomalies, low-impact regressions | Owner assigned, customer outreach as needed | Error rate < 1% but user-visible | Slack alert -> Product/Support owner |

Roles and responsibilities

1) First Responder (FR): Acknowledges pager, collects signals, performs initial isolation.
2) Bridge Lead (BL): Runs the incident bridge, manages the timeline, and coordinates technical responders.
3) Customer Liaison (CL): Primary interface with customer success and affected customers. Crafts status page and email templates; owns customer-facing timing and tone.
4) Engineering SME: Implements fixes, triage, hotfixes, and rollback decisions.
5) Ops/Infra Lead: Evaluates capacity/fleet impacts and triggers failover or autoscaling policies.
6) Postmortem Author: Captures timeline and RCA within 72 hours.

Customer Liaison normative behavior

- Immediately after Bridge is stood up, CL posts initial customer-facing statement: acknowledgement, estimated scope, and next update window.
- Use empathetic language; avoid technical jargon in public statements. Example template in the Communications Templates section.
- Coordinate all external communications through the Support lead and the Legal/PR escalation path for regulated customers.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 minutes)

1. Confirm incident severity using the Incident Classification Matrix.
2. Gather key telemetry: P95/P99 latencies, error rates, request volume, KV cache hit rates, model-serving queue depth.
3. Capture impacted routes/models/customers.
4. Determine immediate mitigation: route traffic to fallback model, increase burst capacity, or enable cached responses.
5. CL posts initial status update (see templates).

Containment and mitigation run steps (example ordered list)

1. Stop-new-deploys: Initiate emergency change freeze in CI/CD.
2. Scale mitigation: Trigger autoscaling group increase or warm spare pool.
3. Model fallback: Switch affected route to verified lower-latency model variant with documented quality delta.
4. Traffic shaping: Apply rate-limits or queue backpressure for noisy tenants.
5. KV cache invalidation only if necessary and with caution (note: invalidation can increase load).
6. If root cause appears to be kernel/cuda or host-level degradation, move workload to healthy hosts and coordinate with cloud provider.

Runbook snippets and useful commands

- Dashboards to open: /dashboards/inference-overview, /dashboards/latency-by-model, /dashboards/cache-hit-rates, /dashboards/slo-violations
- Example kubectl to identify pod restarts: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide --show-labels | grep serving
- Example curl health check: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/healthz?model=redwood-l1
- Redis cache hit rate query (PromQL): sum(rate(redis_command_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(redis_command_calls_total[1m]))

Customer status page cadence and templates
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Timing: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes (Sev1), updates at predictable intervals (every 30–60 minutes for active incidents), and resolution notice within 30 minutes of service restoration.
- Content: short headline, impact summary, mitigation steps, next update ETA.
- Tone: accountable, clear, and non-technical for public posts.

Public status template (short)

- Title: We are investigating elevated API errors affecting text generation in US region
- Time: 2026-03-05 14:07 UTC
- Impact: Customers in the US region may experience increased error rates and longer response times.
- Mitigation: Traffic is being routed to healthy capacity and a rollback to last-known-good model is in progress.
- Next update: 15–30 minutes

Customer email template (for impacted customers)

Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood inference (US region)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re currently investigating an issue impacting inference requests in the US region that may cause higher error rates and slower responses for some requests. Our SRE and Platform teams have an active bridge and are executing mitigations to restore service.

What we’re doing: routing requests to fallback capacity and rolling back a recent model variant to a verified version.

Next update: We will follow up in ~30 minutes or sooner with progress. If you require immediate assistance, reply to this email and we will prioritize you for direct support.

Thanks for your patience,
Customer Liaison, Redwood Inference

Internal Slack broadcast template

#incident-sev1: Initial ack — Bridge: <link> | Impact: US region errors | CL: @Priya | Next update in 15m

Postmortem guide and required artifact checklist
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
- Preliminary timeline (published inside 24 hours)
- Full postmortem with RCA and mitigations (within 72 hours)
- Action items with owners and dates (tracked in the incident backlog)
sections.heading: Required deliverables (due timeline)

sections.body:
1. Summary (one-paragraph customer-facing)
2. Impact (who/what/when)
3. Timeline (UTC timestamps; include monitoring alerts and key commands executed)
4. Root cause analysis (include why detection/mitigation failed)
5. Corrective actions (short-term & long-term)
6. Confidence & test plan for each corrective action
7. Follow-ups and owners (Jira/Issue IDs)

Game day (rehearsal) plan template

Objective: Validate cross-functional choreography (SRE + Platform + Support + CL) for model-serving outages and customer comms.

Duration: 120–180 minutes
sections.heading: Postmortem structure (use for every Sev1/2)

sections.body:
- Bridge Lead (SRE)
- Customer Liaison (CS or Support)
- Engineering SME (Platform/Serving)
- Observability engineer
- Product owner and Solutions Engineer
sections.heading: Participants and pre-reads

sections.body:
1. Warm-up (10m) — Review roles, tools, and playbook pages.
2. Scenario kickoff (5m) — Inject a simulated upstream model artifact corruption that causes model mismatch and elevated error rates for a subset of customers.
3. Active response (60–90m) — Teams run the incident, practice mitigation (roll back model, adjust routing), and exercise the CL templates.
4. After-action (30–45m) — Immediate hot-wash: capture timeline, identify gaps in tooling/permission, and log action items.
5. Retro (15–30m) — Assign owners for improvements and schedule follow-ups.
sections.heading: Exercise flow

sections.body:
- Initial customer acknowledgment posted within target window (0/5)
- Technical mitigation applied and validated (0/10)
- Postmortem skeleton published within 24h (0/5)
- Clear owner assignment for all action items (0/5)

On-call rotation guidance and handoff checklist
sections.heading: Scoring rubric (example)

sections.body:
- Primary pager: 7 days (preferred) or 14 days max
- Secondary/backup: 14 days
sections.heading: Rotation lengths

sections.body:
- Confirm coverage and contact details in the rota tool.
- Share outstanding low/medium action items and any running tickets.
- Verify access to key runbooks and dashboards.
- CL handover: the outgoing Customer Liaison shares open customer tickets and scheduled notifications.
sections.heading: Handoff checklist (pre-shift)

sections.body:
- Document any incidents/near-misses that occurred during shift.
- Update on-call notes page with ongoing mitigations and ETAes.
- Acknowledge receipt in the rota tool.

Training and onboarding for Customer Liaisons

- New CLs complete two shadowing sessions across two live rotations and one replayed game day.
- Required reading: incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026 (internal), SLO definitions, and the customer-communication-tonebook.

Tooling and permissions matrix (table as text)

- PagerDuty: ack/resolve (roles: FR, BL) | Owner: SRE | Permission: oncall group
- Statuspage: publish/update (roles: CL) | Owner: Support | Permission: status-editor
- Jira: create incident tasks (roles: BL/PO) | Owner: Eng Ops | Permission: incident-writer
- Observatory dashboards: read/update (roles: all responders) | Owner: Observability | Permission: team-read

Appendix A — Contact and escalation list

- SRE lead: @liam.oconnor and +1-415-555-0172
- Platform lead: @alyssa.park and +1-650-555-0138
- Support escalation: support-escalation@redwood.com
- Security/Legal escalation: sec-legal@redwood.com (use for regulated-customer disclosures)

Appendix B — Glossary of common terms

- CL: Customer Liaison
- BL: Bridge Lead
- KV cache: Key-Value cache used for prefix caching
- P95/P99: 95th/99th percentile latency

Related pages and references

- See internal runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-library
- SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2025
- Postmortem rubric: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

Revision history

- 2025-11-03 — v0.1 created by Priya Nambiar (initial cross-functional rehearsal concept)
- 2026-01-14 — v0.3 updated with Customer Liaison templates after pilot game day
- 2026-03-05 — v1.0 published: added runbook snippets, rotation guidance, and scoring rubric

If you have questions or suggested edits, ping @Priya on Slack or open an edit request on this page.

payload.page_title: Operator shadow simulator and incident communication templates

sections.body:
A practical program and set of templates to accelerate new responders from shadow to independent operator using synthetic stress simulations, a measurable progression matrix, and customer-facing status templates tailored to model-inference incidents.
Overview

This page defines the Operator Shadow Simulator (OSS) program: a lightweight, repeatable set of synthetic incident exercises, paired with a structured shadow-to-solo progression, and standard customer/stakeholder communication templates. The OSS purpose is to:

- Verify operator proficiency on common Redwood serving incidents (throttling, KV-cache churn, multi-model fallbacks, and model-quality regressions).
- Provide a painless cadence for shadowing, knowledge transfer, and graded solo signoff.
- Ensure consistent, brand-safe external communications and status page updates during incidents.

Scope

Applicable to: oncall responders across SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Customer Success who will act as first- or second-line operators. Not intended for product design or long-format postmortems (separate process).

Program components

1) Synthetic stress scenarios (OSS scenarios)
   - KV-cache cold-start spike: simulate high prefix miss rates across multiple tenants.
   - Throttle/backpressure burst: backend GPU pool saturates causing 429/503 surface area.
   - Model-variant fallback cascade: primary model unavailable, fallback to quantized variant with longer latency.
   - Quality regression smoke test: controlled prompt set returns measurable quality drop (BLEU/ROUGE-style metric simulated).

Each scenario includes: objective, preconditions, injected signals, verifier checks, and expected operator actions.

2) Shadow-to-solo progression matrix (Operator progression)
   - Stage 0 — Orientation (0–2 days): read key runbooks, walk through runbook playflows, observe two live incidents.
   - Stage 1 — Guided shadow (1–2 weeks): shadowing shifts with checklist signoffs; complete OSS scenario A and B under guidance.
   - Stage 2 — Supervised practice (1 week): lead two OSS exercises with a mentor watching; fill evidence form.
   - Stage 3 — Solo signoff (pass criteria): independent response to a synthetic exercise and one low-impact live incident under review.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Timely acknowledgment (under 2 minutes).
- Accurate severity classification and correct paging path.
- Correct containment action (e.g., capacity isolation, traffic shaping, rollback or model swap).
- Clean evidence chain (logs, traces, alert IDs) submitted within 30 minutes of stabilization.

Roles & responsibilities

- New responder: complete OSS orientation materials and schedule shadow shifts.
- Mentor (experienced operator): run through scenarios, provide real-time feedback, sign off evidence form.
- Rotation lead (oncall manager): approve solo signoff and update rota.
- Incident commander (IC): owns escalation during live incidents and coordinates customer comms.

OSS scenario example: KV-cache cold-start spike

Objective: Verify operator can identify cache-miss driven latency spike and perform a controlled cache-warmup + autoscaler adjustment without causing broad restarts.

Preconditions: Synthetic traffic generator enabled against staging pool; monitoring dashboards show 95th percentile latency rising; cache hit ratio drops below 60%.
sections.heading: Progression criteria (pass/fail signals)

sections.body:
1. Spike in 'kv_cache_miss_rate' for tenant T01 to 75% for 10 minutes.
2. Increased 'inflight_requests_per_gpu' metric crossing 90% threshold.
sections.heading: Injected signals

sections.body:
- Operator escalates to SLO-tier 2 within 10 minutes.
- Performs controlled cache-warmup script (oss/cache-warmup.sh) without restarting serving processes.
- Confirms 95th percentile latency reduces by at least 30% within 15 minutes.
sections.heading: Verifier checks (pass criteria)

sections.body:
1. Acknowledge page and join bridge.
2. Run 'k8s get pods' and locate impacted node(s).
3. Check dashboards: kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_miss_rate, inflight_requests_per_gpu.
4. Run cache-warmup script:

   # Example cache warmup command (staging)
   ./oss/scripts/cache-warmup.sh --tenant T01 --model redwood-base-1 --duration 300

5. If warmup has no effect after 10 minutes, scale up pool by +1 instance (follow autoscale SOP).
6. Document all commands and timestamps to evidence form.

Automation hooks

- The OSS harness posts a synthetic incident ticket to the responder Slack channel and triggers the oncall pager for realistic timing.
- Each run auto-creates a case in JIRA with prefilled template for evidence capture.

Operator resilience scorecard (post-exercise)

- Acknowledge time: 0–2 min — green; 2–5 min — yellow; >5 min — red.
- Containment correctness: pass/fail with notes.
- Evidence completeness: % of required fields completed.
- Communication clarity: mentor-rated 1–5.

Simulation logistics and cadence

- Monthly OSS run for each oncall rotation block (default: first week of rotation).
- Ad-hoc OSS runs may be scheduled by rotation leads for remediation.
- Game-day frequency: quarterly cross-team full-day exercise focusing on multi-service orchestration.

Grading and certification

- Passing two OSS scenarios + mentor approval => certified to respond as second-line.
- Passing three scenarios + one live low-impact incident => eligible for solo oncall.
- Certifications tracked in People Ops training profile.

Communication templates

Below are canonical, brand-safe templates for incident updates. Always: brevity, what we know/ don’t know/ next steps, impact, ETA, contact. Tailor tone to customer impact and confidentiality level.

1) Initial customer-facing status (public status page)

Title: Degraded inference latency — <region> (investigating)
Time: 2026-02-10T14:05Z
Summary: We are investigating elevated latency for inference requests in <region>. Impact: a subset of customers may see increased response times and occasional 429 errors.
What we know: Latency increase observed in the serving pool handling redwood-base-1.
What we don’t know: Root cause (investigation ongoing).
Next steps: Ops are running cache-warmup and checking autoscaling behavior. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or when the customer impact changes.
Contact: status@redwood.ai and support portal link

2) Internal bridge announcement (Slack / Bridge topic)

[INCIDENT START] 2026-02-10 14:05 UTC — Latency spike: region-nyc-1
Impact: 95th latency ↑ 220% for tenant subset T0xx. Errors: intermittent 429s.
Bridge: <link>
IC: @oncall-sre
Actions underway: cache warmup, pool scale +1, model fallback readiness.
Requested inputs: service owners for model-serving and GPU-pool.

3) Customer update (email for affected customers)

Subject: Update — Inference latency in <region> (Feb 10)
Hello,
We experienced elevated inference latency affecting some requests in <region>. Our team identified sustained cache miss rates and is executing a staged warmup and scale-up. We expect a meaningful improvement within 30 minutes. We’ll follow up with a summary once resolved. Sorry for the disruption — we know how important low latency is and we’re taking steps to prevent a recurrence.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Support Team

4) Status resolved (status page + internal)

Title: Resolved — inference latency in <region>
Time: 2026-02-10T15:12Z
Summary: The latency spike has been resolved. Root cause: cache churn on the serving pool amplified by a synthetic load pattern. Remediation: completed cache warmup and scaled pool for short window. Next steps: post-incident action items and follow-up scheduled.

Mini post-incident template (15-minute synth postmortem)

1. Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-NNN
2. Timeline (HH:MM UTC): pager -> bridge -> mitigation -> resolve
3. Impact summary: which tenants, SLOs breached (if any)
4. Root cause hypothesis: short paragraph
5. Immediate remediation taken
6. Action items (owner, due date)
7. Communication summary

Runbook & checklist index (quick links)

- KV-cache cold start: oss/runbooks/kv-cache-coldstart
- Throttle/backpressure: oss/runbooks/throttle-backpressure
- Model-fallback: oss/runbooks/model-fallback-and-compatibility
- Quality-regression: oss/runbooks/quality-regression-triage

Pager criteria (table)

| Severity | Symptom examples | Page to | SLA / Time to action | Primary owner |
| P0 | Complete region outage; 100% errors | oncall-sre + eng-platform | 1 min | Eng SRE |
| P1 | SLO breaches, 95th latency > 2x baseline, customer-impacting errors | oncall-sre | 2 min | Serving Runtime |
| P2 | Increased error rate for subset of tenants; performance degradation | oncall-ops | 15 min | Platform Ops |
| P3 | Non-urgent config drift, alerts with noisy telemetry | oncall-dev | 1 business day | Service Owner |

(Use judgment; when in doubt, page the next higher severity.)

Evidence collection checklist

1. Alert IDs and timestamps.
2. Bridge link and participants.
3. Top 3 stack traces / error messages.
4. Relevant metric snapshots (PNG or dashboard links).
5. Commands executed and outputs (copy/paste).
6. Logs: correlate span IDs and request IDs.
7. Customer tickets opened/impacted tenants listed.

After-action items + prevention library

- If root cause is cache churn, add a low-latency warmup window to autoscaler runbooks.
- If model fallbacks are frequent, publish a compatibility matrix for model variants and CPU/GPU profiles.
- Track mean time to evidence (MTTEv) as metric for operator readiness; goal < 45 minutes for P1s.

Onboarding tasks for new responders

1. Read the top-5 runbooks listed above.
2. Complete two OSS shadow exercises as observer.
3. Run one supervised simulated incident and submit evidence.
4. Pass mentor signoff and complete certification survey.

Retention & continuous improvement

- Rotation leads must schedule a retro after each OSS run to capture easy wins and adjust scenarios.
- Maintain a library of anonymized incident timelines for training.

Appendix: sample automatic evidence form (fields to populate)

- Incident ID
- Start time (UTC)
- Acknowledge time (UTC)
- Initial severity
- Summary of symptoms
- Commands executed (copy/paste)
- Metric screenshots (links)
- Resolution steps
- Postmortem owner (name)

Appendix: CLI snippets and links

- List pods by label:
  kubectl get pods -l app=serving-runtime -n redwood-prod
- Check autoscaler status:
  kubectl describe hpa serving-runtime-pool -n redwood-prod
- Query cache metrics (Prometheus example):
  prometheus_query 'kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant="T01"}'

Questions or improvements? Contact the rotation lead or send feedback to oncall-process@redwood.ai.

Document history

- 2025-09-01: Created by Priya Desai.
- 2026-02-10: Updated templates and progression matrix (Marcus Liu review).

payload.page_title: SRE Response Playbook: Rotations, Runbooks, Postmortems & Game Days

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operational response for production incidents: on-call rotation rules, primary runbook patterns, postmortem requirements, game day guidance, and status / customer-communication templates. Use this as the canonical reference for SREs, platform engineers, and on-call responders.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: All production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, inference runtime).
- Audience: SREs, platform engineers, incident commanders (ICs), triage engineers, support engineering, and engineering managers.

Key contacts and channels
-------------------------
- PagerDuty services:
  - Redwood - Serving (pd-service: redwood-serving-pd)
  - Redwood - Control Plane (pd-service: redwood-controlplane-pd)
  - Redwood - Networking (pd-service: redwood-net-pd)
- Slack channels:
  - #sre-oncall (primary incident comms)
  - #infra-ops (secondary escalation)
  - #eng-announce (for broad service-impact notices)
- Email alias for external-facing comms: status@redwood.ai

SLOs and critical thresholds (examples)
-------------------------------------
- redwood-api-gateway: P95 latency < 150ms, error rate < 0.5% per 5m.
- redwood-serving (generation): P95 time-to-first-token < 220ms, tail latency (99th) < 2.0s.
- embeddings-service: 99.9% availability monthly.

Alert severity and initial responder actions
------------------------------------------
- Sev 1 (P0) — outage impacting > 30% of traffic or critical loss of inference: immediate PD page to primary on-call. Escalation timeline: 2 min (phone), 5 min (SMS), 10 min (manager).
  1) Acknowledge the page within 2 minutes.
  2) Join incident bridge: https://meet.redwood.ai/incident (IC will create private conference on start).
  3) Post initial status to #sre-oncall and tag @oncall-lead.
  4) Execute the relevant runbook (see Runbook catalogue).
- Sev 2 (P1) — degraded performance or partial outage: PD to primary, respond within 15 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P2) — non-urgent bugs and single-customer issues: triage during business hours, PD to secondary only if escalation needed.

Escalation matrix
-----------------
- Primary -> Secondary -> Engineering Manager -> Platform Lead -> CTO (if > 4 hours unresolved for Sev 1).
- Example contacts:
  - Primary on-call: pd: redwood-serving-pd -> contact via PD; Slack: @primary_oncall.
  - Secondary on-call: pd: redwood-serving-pd-backup.
  - Platform escalations: @platform-lead on Slack.

Incident commander (IC) protocol
--------------------------------
1) Confirm incident and classify severity.
2) Set communication cadence (every 15m for P0/P1, hourly for P2).
3) Assign roles: Scribe, Communications lead, Mitigation lead, Postmortem lead.
4) Track actions in the incident doc (create Google doc using template link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-doc-template).
5) When mitigated, ensure customer-facing status update is issued and postmortem is assigned.

Runbook pattern (standardized)
-------------------------------
Every service runbook should follow this structure. Runbooks live in the Runbooks directory and are referenced from alert payloads.

- Title: Service name + runbook (e.g., redwood-serving - cold-start-high-latency)
- Pager triggers: alert IDs and severity mapping.
- Impact: short description of visible user impact.
- Quick checklist (immediate actions): 5 bullet checklist with commands.
- Diagnostics: key dashboards, queries, and commands.
- Mitigation steps (ordered): step-by-step reversible actions.
- Post-incident steps: metrics to collect, log pulls, and handoffs.
- Owner and last review date.

Sample runbook excerpt: redwood-serving - high-tail-latency
---------------------------------------------------------
Impact: Customers see increased token latency for >10% of requests, generation stalls observed.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Acknowledge alert in PD.
2) Check autoscaler and GPU pool health: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-serving
3) Verify example request path on canary node: curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
4) Check worker metrics dashboard: Grafana -> Serving / Tail latency (last 15m)
sections.heading: Quick checklist

sections.body:
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep redwood-serving
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c inference-runtime --since=15m | grep -E "error|timeout"
- curl -sS "https://metrics-api.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"
sections.heading: Diagnostics (commands) - run in sequence

sections.body:
1) If autoscaler failing: restart HPA controller: kubectl rollout restart deployment/hpa-controller -n infra
2) If single node noisy: cordon + drain then redeploy: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
3) If kernel OOM and memory pressure: scale down batch size on model variant (see config: /configs/quantization-profiles/low-memory.json)
sections.heading: Mitigation steps

sections.body:
- Collect logs for 1 hour before/after remediation.
- Export traces for 99th percentile requests.
- Create postmortem doc within 72 hours.

On-call rotation rules
----------------------
- Rotation length: 7 days (Mon 00:00 UTC -> Sun 23:59 UTC).
- Shift handover window: 30 minutes overlap; outgoing on-call must provide a 15 minute summary in #sre-oncall.
- Primary and secondary assigned; primary handles PD pages, secondary handles edge escalations and backups.
- Time-off and coverage: swap requests must be recorded in the oncall calendar and a note posted to #sre-oncall at least 24 hours prior.
- Follow-the-sun: North America and Europe teams coordinate swaps during holidays; APAC coverage is arranged by request.

Game day program (quarterly)
----------------------------
Purpose: Validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, and surface gaps in tooling and observability.
sections.heading: Post-incident tasks

sections.body:
- Define scope (which service(s) to simulate).
- Book participants: SREs, product engineer(s), support, and security if required.
- Prepare injectable failure (e.g., node reboot, API rate limiter misconfiguration).
- Create a game day doc with objectives and success criteria.
sections.heading: Planning checklist (6 weeks out)

sections.body:
- Time-box the scenario to 90 minutes.
- Use a dedicated Slack channel: #game-day-YYYY-QX.
- Track timeline and actions in the game day doc; require at least one mitigation attempt per team.
sections.heading: During the exercise

sections.body:
- What went well
- Observability gaps discovered
- Runbook updates required (link to PR)
- Action owner and ETA for remediation

Postmortem and RCA requirements
------------------------------
- Postmortem must be created for any Sev 1/Sev 2 incident with customer impact.
- Timeline: draft within 72 hours; final postmortem published within 14 days.
- Template fields (required):
  - Title
  - Incident ID
  - Date/time window
  - Summary (one paragraph)
  - Impact (customers affected, revenue impact if known)
  - Timeline (minute-level for first 2 hours, then high-level)
  - Root cause analysis
  - Mitigations during incident
  - Long-term fix and owners
  - Action items with owners and due dates
  - Metrics to validate fix
  - Lessons learned

On-call playbook for managers (brief)

payload.page_title: Operator Experimentation Lab and Incident Hypothesis Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines a lightweight, repeatable process for treating incidents as hypotheses and running short, instrumented experiments during low-impact windows (the "Operator Experimentation Lab"). The intent is to accelerate learning about failure modes, reduce blast radius through controlled shadow ops, and produce higher-quality postmortems with actionable remediation steps.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to oncall engineers, SREs, service owners, and platform operators across Redwood Inference.
- Focused on transient degradations, KV-cache regressions, routing fallbacks, and autoscaling edge cases. Not intended for full SEV1 outages that require immediate containment.
sections.heading: Scope and intended audience

sections.body:
- Experiment window: a scheduled 30–90 minute slot where controlled tests run against non-production or canary slices.
- Hypothesis incident: an observed signal with a testable root-cause hypothesis (e.g., "throttle surge + slow kernel selection causes >200ms tail in region-us-west2").
- Shadow ops: executing corrective or investigative actions in a non-customer-facing mode (mirror traffic, dark-launch toggles, non-committed rollouts).
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
1) You have an incident signal below SEV1 where the triage team has time to validate a hypothesis (SLO regression <20% customer impact).
2) There is ambiguity in root cause and a short live test could disambiguate between causal factors (e.g., kernel choice vs. batching policy).
3) The service owner approves a shadow operation and there is a clear rollback path.
sections.heading: When to use this playbook

sections.body:
1. Author hypothesis: one-sentence hypothesis and expected observable metric delta (e.g., "Expose quantized kernel v2 reduces p50 latency by 15% for seq_len<=512").
2. Scope traffic: select canary tenant(s) or synthetic traffic. Note tenant IDs or synthetic job IDs.
3. Impact assessment: estimate expected customer impact (tokens dropped, failed requests). If >5% chance of visible customer errors, abort.
4. Approval: service owner + oncall lead sign-off. Record in this doc: approvers and timestamp.
5. Safety hooks: monitoring alerts, automated rollback play, and circuit-breaker thresholds.
6. Runbook and observer assignment: owner for the experiment, observer(s) who will collect traces and evidence.
sections.heading: Operator Experimentation Lab checklist (pre-experiment)

sections.body:
1. Prepare environment: confirm canary routing, synthetic harness, and observability dashboards (latency, errors, cpu/gpu utilization, KV-hit-rate).
2. Baseline capture (T-10m): record key metrics for 10 minutes before change. Use /metrics/export job id or dashboard snapshot.
3. Apply change to canary (T0): annotate change in experiment log, note git commit/infra diff, and add a short tag to tracing.
4. Monitor (T0 to T+30m): continuous watch for degradations, collect flame graphs and kernel-level traces if tracing flags are enabled.
5. Quick decision gate (T+15m): if any safety hook trips, roll back immediately and proceed to containment notes.
6. Ramp / revert (T+30m): either ramp to additional canaries if safe, or revert and capture post-change metrics.
7. Evidence capture and synthesis: collect traces, heap profiles, kernel selection logs, and summarize in the experiment result section.

Templated experiment metadata (table-style listing to copy into incident ticket):
- experiment_id: OPX-YYYYMMDD-<short>
- hypothesis: <one sentence>
- owner: <name + pager>
- scope: <tenant IDs or synthetic jobs>
- baseline_snapshot: <dashboard link or metrics export id>
- commit/ref: <git sha or infra diff URL>
- start_time: <RFC3339>
- end_time: <RFC3339>
- safety_thresholds: <e.g., error_rate>0.5% OR latency_p95>1200ms>
- rollback_plan: <step list>
sections.heading: Experiment execution procedure (numbered steps)

sections.body:
- Containment step (fast path):
  1) Disable canary routing: run "redwoodctl route set --service <svc> --route canary:false"
  2) Scale down new kernel pods: "kubectl scale deployment/<svc>-kernel --replicas=<prev> -n infra"
  3) Clear KV prefix cache if suspect: "redis-cli --eval scripts/evict_prefix.lua <prefix>"

- For autoscaler anomalies:
  1) Pin desired replicas: "kubectl patch hpa/<svc> -p '{\"spec\":{\"minReplicas\":X}}'"
  2) Force warm pool allocation: trigger "infra warmup --pool <pool-id> --count N"
sections.heading: Runbook templates included (copyable snippets)

sections.body:
- Frequency: monthly 90-minute lab per team + quarterly cross-team coordination game-day.
- Attendees: oncall engineers, SRE, runtime team, product owner (optional), incident commander (rotating).
- Objectives: validate a single hypothesis end-to-end, practice safe rollback, measure time-to-evidence.
- Scoring: 1) did the experiment run to completion? 2) was rollback executed within threshold if required? 3) evidence quality (traces + repeatability).
sections.heading: Game-day design for experiments and shadow ops

sections.body:
- One-line summary of what happened and whether hypothesis was supported.
- Evidence list: traces, metric diffs, kernel logs, commit ids.
- Remediation plan with owner and ETA (patch, config change, longer-term architecture).
- If experiment failed to discriminate, list next hypotheses and planned experiments.
- Attach experiment metadata table (above).
sections.heading: Postmortem and hypothesis reporting requirements (minimums)

sections.body:
- Lab owner is the oncall lead for the week or designated lab coordinator.
- Observers: at least one SRE and one runtime engineer for kernel-level experiments.
- Paging policy: during lab windows, critical paging remains unchanged. Non-critical alerts may be muted with explicit approval.

Customer communications and status page templates (minimal safe language):
- Internal short blurb (to internal channels):
  "We observed an elevated p95 latency in region-us-west2. We are running a controlled canary experiment to validate a kernel optimization and will revert automatically if safety thresholds are hit. No customer-facing errors expected at this time."

- Public status page (concise):
  "Investigating: We are validating a mitigation for elevated inference latency in us-west2. Customer requests remain largely served; some requests may experience transient slower responses. We will provide updates in the next 30 minutes."

- Customer-sensitive template for enterprise tenants (CS/AE use):
  "We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests in us-west2. Our engineering team is running a controlled canary to test a mitigation; we do not expect data exposure or request loss. We will share findings and mitigation ETA within 2 hours. If you see increased errors, please open a support ticket and reference OPX-<id>."

Measurement and observability checklist (metrics to capture):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (inference and backend), error rate, token drop rate, request throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, kernel selection distribution, batching size histogram.
- Trace tags to include: experiment_id, canary=true, kernel_variant, tenant_id.
sections.heading: Rotation and staffing guidance for lab runs

sections.body:
1) If error_rate > 0.5% for 5m OR latency_p95 > SLA_threshold for 5m -> escalate to incident commander and rollback.
2) If resource saturation (GPU mem > 90% or OOMs) -> immediate rollback and page infra team.
3) If hypothesis supported and improvement >10% p95 with no safety trips -> schedule rollout plan and a postmortem write-up.
sections.heading: Decision gates and escalation ladder (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Experiment owner must post a 2-paragraph summary and evidence to the incident ticket within 24 hours.
- Full postmortem (if experiment touched production or surfaced customer impact) due in 72 hours.
- Action items assigned in GH issues or internal tracker with owner and due date; engineering manager verifies closure during weekly triage.

Appendix A — Example incident-to-experiment flow (short narrative):
1) Signal: automatic SLO alert for p95 increases in us-west2.
2) Triage: oncall gathers traces, hypothesizes that new batching policy is increasing tail.
3) Decision: run experiment using shadow traffic vs. canary tenant; approved by service owner.
4) Experiment: change batching policy on canary, monitor 30 minutes, safety hooks OK.
5) Outcome: p95 improved 12% on canary, no increase in errors. Hypothesis supported.
6) Postmortem: schedule rollout with staged canaries and monitor.

Appendix B — Links and references:
- Runbook template repo: https://git.internal.redwood/runbooks/experiment-templates
- Observability dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/ops/experiment-lab
- CLI: redwoodctl docs: https://docs.internal.redwood/redwoodctl

Contact for improvements: Maya Chen (pager: maya-oncall), SRE runbook curator team.

payload.page_title: Rapid Stabilization Cadre: Protocols and Template Kit

sections.body:
Overview

This page documents the 'Rapid Stabilization Cadre' (RSC) pattern: a compact, cross-functional responder unit that executes a time-boxed containment sprint for high-severity incidents affecting Redwood Inference’s serving surface. The kit includes invocation criteria, a three-phase sprint checklist, handoff protocols for on-call rotations, a postmortem rubric tailored to sprint incidents, a short game-day syllabus, and ready-to-send status page / customer comms templates.

Goals
- Restore acceptable service levels within the first 60 minutes for Sev-1 and within 3 hours for complicated multi-region outages.
- Contain customer impact and preserve forensic evidence for later RCA.
- Produce a clear handoff artifact and postmortem within defined SLAs.

Scope
- Applies to incidents impacting production inference latency SLOs (>25% of requests > 2x latency SLO), availability SLOs (>1% error rate sustained over 5 minutes for multi-tenant endpoints), or large-scale KV/cache corruption events.
- Not intended for feature regressions isolated to a single non-prod environment.

Who is in the Cadre
| Role | Typical owner | Responsibility | Pager role |
|------|---------------|----------------|------------|
| Cadre Lead | oncall-team-member (primary) | Runs the sprint, triages scope, coordinates stakeholders | Pager: primary |
| Runtime Engineer | eng-serving-runtime | Kernel/scheduling and GPU-runtime mitigations | Pager: secondary |
| SRE/Service Owner | eng-sre | Capacity and traffic shaping, infra fallbacks | Pager: secondary |
| Observability Lead | eng-platform | Rootcause signals, traces, and synthetic checks | Pager: optional |
| Customer Liaison | customer-success | Customer notices and SLA liaison | Pager: on-call CS for enterprise customers |

Ownership and escalation chain
- Cadre Lead is responsible for declaring sprint phases and driving the artifact. If a Cadre Lead is unavailable within 5 minutes after page, escalate to the oncall duty manager.
- Engineering manager of implicated service must be notified within 30 minutes for Sev-1 events.

Sprint model: three phases (time-boxed)
1) Phase A — Rapid Containment (0–20 minutes)
   - Primary objective: stop the customer-visible blast radius and collect triage evidence.
   - Steps (quick checklist):
     1. Acknowledge page, set status "Investigating" on the status page.
     2. Run immediate health checks: runbook id RSC-01-coldstart-checks.
     3. Snapshot critical observability: traces (last 30 minutes), error logs, kernel/gpu metrics, KV cache metadata. Store to /tmp/incident_evidence/<incident-id>.
     4. Apply containment knobs in order (documented below). If knob applied, annotate timeline.
     5. If containment fails within 20 minutes, declare Phase B.

   - Containment knobs (ordered, fast to slow):
     - Short-circuit to read-only cache mode (if supported).
     - Route traffic to regional fallbacks (policy: prefer non-affected region within 10s).
     - Scale up short-lived dedicated capacity (burst pool) for top-tier customers.
     - Apply temporary rate-limits for anonymous/unpaid tiers.

2) Phase B — Rapid Stabilization (20–60 minutes)
   - Primary objective: restore service to SLO window (latency and availability) with minimal customer functionality loss.
   - Steps:
     1. Confirm containment knobs took effect and validate via synthetic probes (green for core path).
     2. Run targeted mitigations: kernel parameter adjustments, KV cache flush with safe filter, model fallback to pinned variant.
     3. If running fallbacks, activate traffic mirroring to measure quality delta.
     4. Coordinate with Customer Liaison for enterprise customers: send initial customer comm (template below).
   - Success criteria to exit Phase B: core customer flows pass acceptance tests for 2 consecutive cycles (5m).

3) Phase C — Operate and Transition (60–180 minutes)
   - Primary objective: Harden fix, schedule longer remediation, prepare handoff/runbook update.
   - Steps:
     1. Freeze any broad rollouts and block auto-rollbacks until postmortem.
     2. If hotfix needed, prepare canary hotfix with rollback plan.
     3. Extend evidence collection and tag artifacts for enterprise/regulatory retention.
     4. Prepare handoff artifact for the rotation coming on duty (see Handoff Artifact section).

When to invoke the Rapid Stabilization Cadre
- Invocation triggers (any of the following):
  - Latency SLO breach resulting in >25% requests above 2x latency target for >5 minutes.
  - Availability SLO breach >1% total error rate sustained for >5 minutes across a region.
  - Model-serving correctness regression affecting >5% of A/B eval prompt set for a production model.
  - Detection by synthetic monitors of catastrophic KV inconsistency.

Runbook invocation checklist (must be completed in the first 12 minutes)
1. Acknowledge on-call page and post the initial incident stub in the incident channel (format below).
2. Capture incident-id: rsc-YYYYMMDD-XXX and create artifact directory.
3. Attach critical traces/logs and run the -evidence-gather script:
   bash /usr/local/bin/collect-incident-evidence --id ${INCIDENT_ID} --out /tmp/incident_evidence/${INCIDENT_ID}
4. Apply Phase A containment knobs (ordered above).
5. Mark timeline entries on the incident document with timestamps and owner.

Handoff artifact: what to produce before handing to next rotation
- One-page incident summary (Markdown): cause hypothesis, actions taken, containment knobs applied (with timestamps), current SLO status, business impact estimate (e.g., % customers affected), and next steps.
- Evidence bundle link (s3 path) with retained logs and a hash manifest.
- Postmortem owner assignment and a target postmortem publish date (default: 7 business days).
- Updated runbook checklist if a new mitigation sequence was used.

On-call rotation & cadence changes (operational governance)
- RSC cadence: on-call rotations should ensure at least two engineers are RSC-ready per shift (primary + backup).
- Weekly stabilization office hour: 60min slot for recent incidents triage and runbook pruning; mandatory for all oncall leads.
- Shadow requirement: new responders must participate in 2 supervised RSC activations before being primary.

Postmortem rubric and deadlines
- SLA for postmortem draft: 7 business days (owner must create draft).
- Final postmortem: 14 business days with reviewer signoffs.
- Postmortem must include: timeline (minute resolution for first 90 minutes), hypothesis and evidence, root cause(s) by category (infra/runtime/model/config), customer impact quantification, and 3 concrete action items (owner + due date).
- Severity classification and required detail:
  - Sev-1 (prod outage impacting >10% of customers): full RCA, exec summary, and compliance evidence bundle.
  - Sev-2 (partial degradation): condensed RCA and runbook update.
  - Sev-3 (minor/contained): optional lightweight review at weekly office hour.

Game day syllabus (RSC-focused)
- Objective: validate the entire sprint flow end-to-end.
- Frequency: quarterly for RSC, with synthetic blast tests and a KV-corruption simulated exercise.
- Minimum exercise tasks:
  1. Simulate a regional latency storm and exercise Phase A containment knobs.
  2. Execute hotfix canary workflow and rollback.
  3. Perform handoff to an out-of-shift rotation and validate artifact quality.
  4. Run the postmortem rubric and produce draft within 48 hours.

Status page and customer comms templates
- Status page — three canonical states: Investigating, Identified, Mitigated, Resolved. Use the short-form template below for the initial public update.

Initial status page entry (public)
Title: Degraded inference latency for hosted-api in us-west-2
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency on text generation endpoints in us-west-2.
Customer guidance: We are actively investigating and may route traffic to healthy regions; no action required from customers.
Estimated next update: 30 minutes

Enterprise customer email template (initial)
Subject: Incident rsc-{{incident_id}}: Degraded inference latency — initial notice
Hi {{customer_name}},

We’re investigating an issue causing degraded inference latency for hosted API traffic in us-west-2. Our Rapid Stabilization Cadre has been activated and is executing containment and stabilization. At this time we estimate a potential impact window of 30–90 minutes for affected requests.

What we’re doing:
- Containing impact with regional routing and temporary rate-limits for non-paid tiers.
- Collecting forensic evidence and monitoring synthetic tests.

Immediate customer action: none. We’ll provide an update within 30 minutes. If you need live updates or a dedicated liaison, reply to this email and we’ll escalate.

Regards,
Marta Silva
Redwood Inference — Customer Reliability Team

Post-update (resolved) template — status page
Title: Resolved: Degraded inference latency in us-west-2
Status: Resolved
Impact: Root cause: memory pressure in serving runtime triggered GC that slowed KV lookups. We have rolled back a config change and restored normal latency.
Customer guidance: No action required. We will publish a postmortem with timeline and action items within 7 business days.

Forensic evidence preservation and compliance notes
- Evidence retention: default retention for incident evidence bundle is 90 days; for Sev-1 incidents retention is 1 year.
- When handling customer-sensitive data, ensure evidence is stored in customer-specific, access-restricted buckets and flagged with appropriate classification labels.

Runbook lifecycle and pruning
- Any runbook step invoked during an RSC sprint must be reviewed within 72 hours and either accepted into the canonical runbook or retired with rationale.
- Runbook owner must add a short changelog entry and link to the incident postmortem.

Metrics and SLOs to track for cadence health
- Mean time to containment (MTTC) target: <= 25 minutes for Sev-1.
- Mean time to stabilization (MTTS) target: <= 60 minutes for Sev-1.
- Postmortem lead time adherence: 95% of postmortem drafts created within 7 business days.

Appendix A — Incident channel stub (copy/paste)
Incident: rsc-{{incident_id}}
Severity: Sev-1 / Sev-2
Impact: brief one-line impact summary
Start: {{ISO timestamp}}
Cadre lead: @username
Current status: Investigating
Containment knobs applied: (list)
Evidence bundle: s3://redwood-incidents/{{incident_id}}
Next update: +30m

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: collect-incident-evidence --id ${INCIDENT_ID} --s3 s3://redwood-incidents/${INCIDENT_ID} --include traces,logs,kernel-metrics
sections.heading: collect evidence (example)

sections.body:
ops-route-adjust --from-region us-west-2 --to-region us-east-1 --policy emergency-fallback

Appendix C — Example timeline fragment (format for postmortem)
\- 00:00 Pager received by Cadre Lead
\- 00:03 Initial status page posted (Investigating)
\- 00:08 Containment: route to fallback region; synthetic checks pass
\- 00:22 Stabilization: pinned to fallback model variant; KPIs return to SLO

How to get help or suggest improvements
- File PR against the runbook repo: gitlab.redwood/infrastructure/runbooks (label: rsc).
- For policy changes or cadence adjustments, bring a proposal to the weekly stabilization office hour.

Document change log
- 2025-11-12 — Created by Marta Silva (initial draft).
- 2026-02-10 — Added evidence retention rules and updated MTTC/MTTS targets (reviewers: Ethan Brooks, Priya Natarajan).
