payload.page_title: Rotation Engagement Handbook and Status Automation Guide

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This handbook codifies Redwood Inference’s approach to on-call rotations, incident classification, runbook structure, postmortem practice, and automated status page communications. It is intended for SREs, service owners, engineers, support, and product managers who participate in incident mitigation and outward communications.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deploy agents). Excludes experimental sandbox clusters unless their failure can affect customer-facing capacity.

Key principles
--------------
- Safety first: protect customer data and restore availability; mitigation > perfection.
- Clear roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, Primary Engineer, Secondary / Escalation.
- Timeboxing: accelerate triage, minimize cognitive load with templates and automation.
- Learning: every Sev1/Sev2 incident requires a postmortem with action items and owners.

Severity taxonomy and SLO guardrails
-----------------------------------
- Sev1 (P0): Production service unavailable or correctness severely degraded for > 2 minutes; customer-impacting across multiple customers or critical customers. Target response: page within 2 min, mitigation path within 15 min.
- Sev2 (P1): Significant degradation for a subset of customers or major feature (e.g., streaming broken) with customer workarounds. Target response: page within 15 min, mitigation within 1 hour.
- Sev3 (P2): Minor degradation, non-urgent bugs, or single-customer impact with workarounds. Follow regular operational cadence.

Representative SLOs (exposed in SLO dashboard)
------------------------------------------------
- Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly for production region endpoints.
- Median (p50) inference latency for short prompts: < 200 ms; p95 < 1200 ms.
- Control plane API success rate: 99.9% over 24h.

Incident lifecycle: quick-run checklist
--------------------------------------
1) Detect & Page: Alerts route to on-call (PagerDuty) with runbook link.
2) Triage (0–10m): Determine severity, impact, and immediate mitigation (e.g., rollback, scaling).
3) Assign roles (10m): IC, Primary Engineer, Communications Lead, SRE support.
4) Mitigate (15–60m): Apply mitigation steps until service is acceptably degraded or recovered.
5) Stabilize (60–240m): Post-mortem draft, hotfix rollout and verification.
6) Close & document (24–72h): Finalize postmortem, complete action items.

Runbook template (required header for all runbooks)
---------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- runbook_id: short dashed identifier (e.g., runtime-gpu-oom)
- service_owner: team name and primary contact
- pager_policy: who is paged and escalation windows
- severity_association: default severity mapping
- impact_checks: short list of queries to confirm impact
- safe_mitigation: list of mitigations that are reversible

Example runbook: inference-runtime-high-cpu
-----------------------------------------
Summary: High CPU on inference runtime nodes causing elevated latency and request queueing.
sections.heading: Every runbook must start with these fields

sections.body:
- Grafana: inference-runtime/cpu_utilization > 90% (5m)
- Alerts: recurrence of queue_backlog > 200 requests
- Customer reports: ticket/Slack channel #support-api showing 4+ reports in 10 min
sections.heading: Impact checks

sections.body:
1) Increase replica count (k8s HPA override): kubectl -n inference patch deployment runtime --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":5}]'
2) Scale up GPU pool (infra-ops): runbook-scripts/scale-gpu-pool --cluster-prod --count +2
3) Unload large batch jobs: identify active jobs and trigger graceful drain: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/jobs/drain?job_id=...
4) Apply traffic-shed rule (traffic router): restrict non-critical routes to 10% traffic
Escalation matrix: Primary -> Secondary -> SRE Lead -> On-call Manager.
sections.heading: Immediate safe mitigation (in order)

sections.body:
- p95 latency back under threshold for 10 continuous minutes
- No error rate spike in last 5m

Incident roles and responsibilities (concise)
-------------------------------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): owns decisioning and triage step. Usually oncall primary or designated senior engineer.
- Primary Engineer: deepest subject expert for the affected service. Executes runbook steps.
- Secondary / Backup: fills in if Primary unavailable, and prepares rollback plan.
- Communications Lead: owns status page and customer messages, coordinates with customer-success for key accounts.
- Postmortem Author: drafts the timeline and root cause analysis.

Communication templates (status page + customer-facing)
------------------------------------------------------
Use these as starting templates. Replace bracketed fields before publishing.
- Initial public status (short):
  Title: [Major outage] Hosted API: increased latency / partial outage
  Body: We are investigating reports of increased latency affecting text generation in region [us-west-2]. Affected customers may experience delayed or timed-out responses. Our engineers are actively investigating. Next update: in 15 minutes.
- Update (mitigation in place):
  Title: Mitigation applied — traffic routed to fallback model variant
  Body: We have applied a mitigation that routes traffic to a compatible fallback model for a subset of requests to reduce latency while we continue to investigate the root cause. Some requests may receive differences in output quality. We will provide a root cause analysis in the postmortem.
- Resolved:
  Title: Resolved — Hosted API latency issue
  Body: The issue has been resolved. We reverted the temporary routing and verified p95 latency for short prompts is within targets. We will publish a detailed postmortem within 72 hours.

Internal Slack comms template (to #incidents channel)
----------------------------------------------------
[SEV{level}] [service] - short summary\- IC: @handle – Primary: @handle – CL: @handle\- Impact: summary (regions/customers)\- Mitigation: summary\- Next update in 15m or at {time}

Status page automation (example API calls)
-----------------------------------------
We use the Status API (internal) for programmatic updates. Example curl for initial incident post:

curl -X POST "https://status-internal.redwood.dev/api/v1/incidents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"[Investigating] Increased latency in hosted-api-us-west-2","service_ids":["svc-hosted-api-usw2"],"status":"investigating","impact":"partial"}'

Tip: integrate the above into incident responders (PagerDuty webhooks) so an alert automatically posts a skeleton incident that IC can edit.

Postmortem checklist and template
--------------------------------
Required for Sev1/Sev2. Document the following as plain text in the postmortem doc:
- Incident ID and timeline (UTC timestamps)
- Detection path (monitoring, customer report, CI)
- Impact summary and customers affected
- Root cause analysis (what failed and why)
- Remediation and long-term fix plan with owners and due dates
- Action items tracked in backlog; link to ticket(s)
- Severity assessment and SLO impact calculations (token counts, error minutes)
- Lessons learned and follow-up game-day exercise suggestion
sections.heading: Post-mitigation checks

sections.body:
- Draft: within 72 hours of incident resolution
- Finalized with reviewers: within 7 calendar days

Rotation and scheduling policy (practical rules)
-----------------------------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week (Mon 00:00 UTC — Sun 23:59 UTC) for primary oncall. Secondary rotation offset by 1 week.
- Handover notes: outgoing oncall must publish a 10-minute handoff summary in the oncall board including outstanding incidents, maintenance windows, and infra churn.
- Time off & exemptions: request 14 days ahead. For extended leave (> 4 weeks), team adjusts rotation or assigns merchant oncall.
- Escalation fast path: if primary does not acknowledge page within 5 minutes, PD escalates to secondary. If no ack in 15 minutes, escalate to SRE Lead.

On-call fatigue and safety measures
----------------------------------
- Nighttime escalation limits: high-frequency non-critical alerts are grouped and swept at 06:00 local unless a human indicates immediate need.
- Silent-maintenance windows: planned changes that may trigger alerts must include a maintenance window in PD to suppress notifications.
- Incident credit & compensations: engineers receive an incident-response credit for severe incidents (tracked by people-ops).

Game days and simulation blueprint
----------------------------------
Goal: validate runbooks, automation, rotas, and communications under pressure.
Frequency: quarterly for platform-wide, monthly for critical services.
Sample half-day agenda (4 hours)
1) Kickoff (15m): objectives and rules of engagement.
2) Scenario execution (90m): seeded synthetic failure (e.g., control-plane DB latency spike).
3) Observability & mitigation (60m): participants execute runbooks and post status updates.
4) Debrief (45m): what worked, what failed, action items assigned.
Deliverables: runbook updates, automation tweaks, and an executive summary submitted to leadership.

Metrics we track for oncall health and incident quality
------------------------------------------------------
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev1: target < 2 min.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM): target < 20 min for Sev1.
- Postmortem completion rate within 7d: 100% for Sev1, 90% for Sev2.
- Number of false-positive high-priority alerts per quarter (goal < 5).

Operational tooling and recommended automations
---------------------------------------------
- PagerDuty integration: automated escalation policies and PD -> Status API webhook.
- Incident skeleton creation: webhook places a draft incident and runbook link in the incident doc store.
- Automated runbook health checks: weekly synthetic probes that exercise the mitigation steps (e.g., run the scale-gpu-pool script in dry-run).
- Postmortem stub automation: when an incident closes, create a postmortem stub in the docs with required sections prefilled.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Oncall program lead: SRE Manager (operational ownership for rotation rules and tooling).
- Incident policy owner: Head of Reliability (policy approval and SLA alignment).
- Runbook shepherds: each service owner is responsible for their runbooks and must review them quarterly.

Appendices
---------
A) Quick comms cheatsheet
- When to use customer-facing status: any Sev1 or customer-impacting Sev2.
- Use internal-only Slack for triage details. Always keep the public status non-technical.

B) Example escalation command snippets
- Check runtime pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o wide
- Tail logs: kubectl -n inference logs -f pod/inference-runtime-abc123

C) Postmortem rubric (how reviewers score the document)
- Completeness (timeline, impact) 0–5
- Root cause clarity 0–5
- Actionability (concrete fixes with owners) 0–5
- Communication quality (timeliness of status updates) 0–5

D) Contact matrix (rotating oncall aliases)
- primary-oncall@redwood.dev (PagerDuty alias)
- secondary-oncall@redwood.dev
- ops-cs@redwood.dev (customer success)

Document maintenance
--------------------
- This handbook is reviewed quarterly by the oncall program lead and after every Sev1. Runbook owners should confirm runbook accuracy at least once per quarter.

Related resources
-----------------
- Incident command playbook and escalation matrix (linked in related_pages)
- Oncall simulation cookbook (game day scenarios)
- SLO & error budget dashboards

End of document

payload.page_title: On-call contingency catalog for degraded embeddings and RLHF regressions

sections.body:
SUMMARY:
This document defines the contingency catalog, triage flows, runbooks, escalation matrix, status-page and customer-communication templates specifically for incidents that manifest as degraded embeddings or regressions introduced by RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) tuning or model rollouts. It complements general incident playbooks by focusing on symptom patterns unique to semantic encodings and quality regressions in production inference.

SCOPE:
- Services: embedding-service (embedder-v1, embedder-v2), rerank-service, semantic-search, similarity-indexer, recommendation pipelines that use embeddings, and downstream model pipelines that rely on RLHF-tuned chat models.
- Audience: on-call engineers, ML engineers, product owners, SREs, customer success engineers, and incident bridge operators.
- Excluded: hardware-only failures (power/network), general latency-only SLO breaches that have no quality signal. Those are handled by standard oncall playbooks.

GOALS:
1) Restore customer-facing semantic fidelity within 60 minutes for P0 regressions (see severity table).
2) Provide consistent, evidence-backed customer communications within 2 hours of detection.
3) Ensure reproducible rollback or mitigation paths that preserve user data and minimize model drift.

SEVERITY DEFINITIONS (specific to embedding / RLHF incidents):
- Sev P0 (Critical): Large-scale quality regression causing >10% customer-visible semantic failures (document retrieval miss-rate increase, embeddings similarity drop, classification accuracy regression on monitored prompt-sets) OR production RLHF rollout causing hallucinations or safety policy violations. Immediate bridge.
- Sev P1 (High): Noticeable quality degradation for a subset of customers or models (5–10% regression on canaries) or indexing throughput severely impacted by embedding failures.
- Sev P2 (Medium): Small degradation detected by internal evals or telemetry; no immediate customer impact but trending.
- Sev P3 (Low): Investigations, tooling, or model-improvement tasks with no current impact.

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES:
- Bridge Operator (first-tier): oncall engineer from eng-sre. Starts bridge, runs initial hypothesis checklist, coordinates comms.
- ML Triage Lead: ML engineer responsible for the model family (embeddings/rlhf). Runs evaluations, comparisons, and produces evidence for rollback decisions.
- Runtime SRE: owns serving runtime metrics, autoscaling, and cache invalidation.
- Indexing Owner: owns the similarity-indexer and reindexing procedure.
- Customer Liaison: CS engineer who drafts customer messages and liaises with account teams for impacted customers.
- Incident Commander: assigned for P0/P1 incidents; rotates from senior SRE/ML.

EARLY DETECTION SIGNALS (examples):
- Drop in retrieval NDCG (canary prompt-set) by >7% in 15 minutes.
- Sudden rise in semantic-distance variance between persisted embeddings and live embeddings (KS test p < 0.01).
- Increase in rerank-service false negatives on golden queries.
- Customer reports: consistent incorrect recommendations, high churned query failure rate, or safety policy flags.

EVIDENCE COLLECTION CHECKLIST (first 20 minutes):
1) Capture timestamps for when alerts began (UTC).
2) Snapshot canary evaluation results (embed-canary-suite). CLI: curl -sS https://embedder/api/v1/canary | jq .results > canary.json
3) Export sample inputs (redact PII) and their live embeddings and historical embeddings.
4) Check model and artifact versions: model-id, weights-hash, tokenizer version, quantization profile.
5) Confirm deployment events in CI/CD: recent rollout IDs from deployment-service.
6) Check inference logs for increased error rates, timeouts, or OOMs.
7) Validate KV cache state and prefix-hits: cache-hit ratio drop may surface changed embedding dimensionality or hash mismatch.
8) Verify indexer health: pending reindex backlog, failed shards, or index version mismatch.

DECISION LADDERS (triage -> remediation):
- If median canary score falls by >8% and rollout ID matches a recent model promotion -> trig rollback to previous model variant.
- If mismatch between tokenizer/token-version -> hotfix: toggle fallback tokenizer path and invalidate affected cache prefixes.
- If indexer backlog is high and embedding generation is healthy -> scale indexer, queue backfill, and post temporary advisory to customers.
- If regression only appears in RLHF conversations (hallucinations/safety flags) -> disable RLHF tuning flag for the model (config toggle) and revert to supervised baseline.

MITIGATION RUNBOOKS (ordered quick-actions):
1) Immediate containment (performed by Bridge Operator):
   - Add incident tag to service: curl -X POST https://infra/api/tag -d '{"service":"embedding-service","incident":"IN-XXXX"}'
   - Pin traffic to previous model variant via routing override: api gateway -> set route weight 100% to model:vX
   - Bump canary evaluation cadence to 1/min for 30 minutes.
2) Reproduction (performed by ML Triage Lead):
   - Run embed-canary-suite against model:vX (live) and model:vX-1 (baseline). Command: ./tools/run_canary --suite embed-canary --model model:vX --out out_vX.json
   - Compute similarity deltas and annotate failing queries.
3) Rollback (if decision ladder triggers):
   - Submit rollback via deployment-service with pre-filled template: rollback-template.json.
   - Revalidate indexer after rollback by running a 1% sample reindex and verifying NDCG.
4) Temporary customer shielding (if immediate rollback impossible):
   - Route affected customers to a compatibility layer (feature-flagged local fallback) that serves cached embeddings for frequently-seen queries.
   - Apply per-tenant throttles to limit noisy traffic contributing to indexer backlog.
5) Long-term remediation:
   - Post-incident: add new regression tests, extend canary prompt-sets, retrain with targeted human feedback, and adjust RLHF reward shaping to reduce regressions.

ESCALATION MATRIX (summary):
- T+0–15m: Bridge Operator + Runtime SRE.
- T+15–45m: Add ML Triage Lead and Indexing Owner.
- T+45–120m: Escalate to Incident Commander and Product Owner; draft customer comm.
- >120m: Executive notification and cross-functional war room.

STATUS PAGE TEMPLATES (short and actionable):
- Short public status (1–2 sentence):
  "We are investigating reports of degraded search and recommendation results for some customers. Some requests may return less relevant results. Our engineers are triaging; updates at 1-hour cadence."

- Expanded public update (situation + mitigation):
  "Update 2: We identified a model variant rollout that caused decreased embedding quality for a subset of queries. We have routed traffic away from the new variant and are validating baseline model results. If you rely on semantic search or recommendations, you may observe intermittent quality differences while we complete the validation. We expect an additional update in ~60 minutes."

- Internal customer-facing template (email for impacted customers):
  Subject: Incident IN-XXXX: Temporary degradation in semantic search/recommendations

  Hi <Customer Contact>,

  We detected a regression affecting the relevance of semantic search and recommendations for some queries. Our engineers have identified the likely cause (recent model promotion) and have routed traffic to a stable model variant to limit impact. We will follow up with a post-incident summary within 72 hours that includes root cause, mitigation steps taken, and credits if applicable.

  Immediate impacts: decreased relevance, delayed reindex for new data.
  Mitigation: traffic re-route, temporary use of cached embeddings for frequent queries.
  ETA for return to baseline: 1–3 hours (subject to validation).

  If you see specific queries that are producing incorrect results, please send redacted examples to <cs-team@redwood.ai> and we will prioritize.

  Regards,
  Customer Liaison

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS (within 72 hours):
- Full postmortem with timeline, root cause, and mitigations. Use template: postmortem-structured.md.
- Add failing queries (anonymized) to embed-canary-suite.
- Create an alert-to-action rule: when canary NDCG drops >5% for 10m, auto-scale indexer and open a bridge.
- If RLHF tuning introduced a safety regression, freeze RLHF experiments for the model family until a safety review completes.

REPRODUCTION AND EVAL CHECKS (commands and thresholds):
- Run: python evals/embed_regression_check.py --baseline model:vX-1 --candidate model:vX --suite embed-canary --alpha 0.05
- Thresholds: if candidate median NDCG < baseline NDCG - 0.05 (5 points) -> fail. If p-value < 0.01 -> high confidence.

GAME DAY EXERCISES (recommended quarterly):
- Exercise A: Canary-failure scenario. Simulate a 10% drop in canary NDCG and practice rollback, comms, and reindex sanity check. Duration: 3 hours.
- Exercise B: Indexer-throttle scenario. Create synthetic burst traffic causing index backlog; practice flow-control, per-tenant shielding, and prioritized backfills. Duration: 4 hours.
- Exercise C: RLHF-safety scenario. Inject prompts that trigger safety flags in a canary RLHF model; practice disabling RLHF flag and rolling back. Duration: 2 hours.

ON-CALL ROTATION GUIDELINES (fairness + handoff):
- Minimum experience for ML Triage Lead: 6 months on the model family.
- Shadowing: new oncall engineers shadow three incidents (at least one game-day) before independent rotation.
- Handoff doc: outgoing oncall must provide: active incidents list, recent canary results, cache invalidation state, and pending rollouts.
- Fairness: block consecutive weekend oncalls to max 2 per quarter; implement a credits system for extra shifts redeemable for time off.

SLOS AND MONITORING RECOMMENDATIONS (concrete thresholds):
- Canary NDCG (embed-canary-suite): p95 >= baseline - 0.02 for healthy. Alert if 5-minute rolling drop >0.03.
- Embedding generation success rate: >= 99.5%. Alert if < 99.0% for 5 minutes.
- Index backlog: < 10k pending documents. Alert if > 50k for 10 minutes.

PLAYBOOKS FOR COMMON ROOT CAUSES (quick reference):
- Model artifact divergence (weights/tokenizer mismatch): rollback, re-run validation, tighten CI check for tokenizer compatibility.
- Quantization/precision bug: pin quantized profile in runtime and route to non-quantized serving while patching kernels.
- Inference cache inconsistency: invalidate prefix and rebuild for affected tenants, add schema version to cache keys.
- RLHF reward shaping regression: revert tuning batch and create unit tests for known safety prompts.

DOCUMENTATION AND OPERATIONS RUNSHEET (for Incident Commander):
- Timeline template (UTC):
  00:00 - Detection and bridge creation (who)
  00:05 - Evidence snapshot (who)
  00:15 - Preliminary hypothesis and mitigation (who)
  00:45 - Escalation decision (who)
  02:00 - Customer notice (who)
  24:00 - Postmortem draft (owner)

METRICS TO ATTACH TO POSTMORTEM (minimum):
- Canary NDCG time series with annotated events.
- Fraction of traffic shifted to fallback variant.
- Number of impacted customers and top-5 tenants by request volume.
- Time-to-rollback, time-to-recover, and time-to-first-customer-notification.

APPENDIX: TOGGLE AND CLI SNIPPETS
- Toggle RLHF for model: curl -X POST https://config/api/feature-toggle -d '{"model":"model-family-x","rlhf_enabled":false}'
- Query canary: curl -sS https://embedder/api/v1/canary | jq .results
- Reindex 1% sample: python tools/reindexer.py --percent 1 --index semantic-index-v2

REVISION HISTORY:
- 2026-02-15: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft).
- 2026-02-22: Added escalation matrix and templates (reviewers: Marco Rossi, Elena Kim).
- 2026-03-01: Published after security review and small edits to SLO thresholds.

CONTACTS:
- ML Triage Lead on-call alias: ml-triage-oncall@redwood.ai
- Runtime SRE on-call alias: runtime-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Customer Success liaison: cs-briefing@redwood.ai

END OF DOCUMENT

payload.page_title: Oncall handshake procedures and automated status flows

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines the "handshake" and continuity procedures for on-call rotations and a companion set of deterministic automated status flows that reduce human overhead during incident startup. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, customer success, and anyone who will author or consume engineer-to-customer communications during outages.

Goals

- Ensure reliable, brief, repeatable handoffs between on-call shifts and between teams.
- Minimize time-to-first-public-communication by automating status page updates and internal paging where safe.
- Provide templated, role-specific communications for initial, cadence, and resolution updates.
- Capture ownership and escalation rules so incidents progress without decision paralysis.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood public-facing production services and model inference endpoints in hosted and Dedicated deployments. Excludes purely internal tooling flagged non-customer-impacting by the service owner.

Definitions

- Handshake: the short, written + verbal exchange that confirms ownership and context between outgoing and incoming on-call engineers.
- Incident Automation Flow: a set of automated steps (alerts -> runbook -> status update) that run with minimal human intervention until escalation thresholds are reached.
- Incident ID: standardized identifier: RWI-{YYYYMMDD}-{SEQ} (generated by incident manager).

Roles & Responsibilities

- Primary On‑Call (POC): first responder; responsible for initial triage and containment.
- Incident Commander (IC): takes ownership if incident escalates beyond containment (typically after 20 minutes or at SLO breach risk).
- Incident Communicator (IComm): owns public status updates and customer comms; liaises with Customer Success for major-impact incidents.
- SRE Lead / Pager Duty Escalation: coordinates multi-team mobilization and postmortem assignment.
- Outgoing On‑Call: completes handshake checklist and documents outstanding work.

Handoff (Handshake) Checklist — mandatory before leaving shift

1. Open the incident management page for any active incidents and confirm ownership. If no incident, perform a shift transfer note.
2. Provide a 5–10 minute verbal summary to incoming on-call with these items: active incidents, key mitigation state, recent alerts suppressed, and any scheduled tasks that may affect availability.
3. Post a written handoff into the team channel using the template below. Include: timestamp, active incidents (IDs), mitigation actions performed, outstanding actions, and CI/CD or infra changes in last 24 hours.
4. Confirm monitoring alarms and alert forwarding are functioning: check latest PagerDuty/Alertmanager health check, and validate status webhook delivery.
5. If any incident is active and not yet assigned an IC, ensure the IC field is set. If no IC yet, agree on escalation trigger (time or threshold).

Handoff template (team channel)

- Shift: <incoming_name> from <HH:MM> UTC
- Outgoing: <name> at <HH:MM> UTC
- Active incidents: RWI-20260210-03 (investigating)
- Summary: brief one-paragraph status
- Actions performed: list
- Outstanding: list
- Alerts muted: list
- Notes: runbook pointers, on-call runbook path, links

Automated Status Flows (design & examples)

We use deterministic automation to ensure rapid public-facing communication and to reduce the cognitive load on first responders. Automation is gated by safety checks: it will not publish customer-impact statements without two independent signals (alert + metric breach) unless an IC authorizes. Flows are implemented as idempotent steps in our incident manager.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: 1. detected -> 2. triaged -> 3. investigating -> 4. mitigated -> 5. resolved -> 6. postmortem
sections.heading: Flow states (canonical)

sections.body:
- detected: alert from Alertmanager (error rate > 5% or latency p95 > 3s for 5m)
  - action: create incident ID and page POC, attach initial event snapshot to incident. No public message yet.

- triaged: POC confirms customer impact (metric + user-visible errors)
  - action: if metric breach confirmed, post internal 'investigating' draft and notify IComm; if both conditions true, automation will create a status-page draft and push to 'pending' state.

- investigating: IC or POC marks incident as investigating or automation auto-promotes after N minutes with confirmed impact.
  - action: publish status page 'Investigating' with template A (see below). Start 15-minute cadence timer.

- mitigated: measurable improvement (error rate halved or latency back to within SLO for 10m)
  - action: update status to 'Identified' or 'Monitoring' depending on confidence, change cadence to 30 minutes and include mitigation notes.

- resolved: SLOs restored for 30 minutes and root cause identified or a patch deployed
  - action: publish 'Resolved' notice and schedule postmortem assignment.
sections.heading: Trigger examples and automated actions

sections.body:
- two independent signals: alert + metric breach OR alert + customer complaint URL
- no unreviewed deploys in last 15 minutes for the implicated service (checks CI metadata)
- no active PII/secure-data breach tags detected by the incident classifier

Status page templates

Use the following templates verbatim; IComm may add customer-specific detail but must not alter the severity tag without IC approval. Replace placeholders in double braces.

Template A — Initial public notice (Investigating)

Title: {SERVICE} — Investigating degraded performance ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Next update: ~15 minutes
Notes: We are aware of increased error rates affecting {REGION or ROUTE}. Engineers are investigating and we will post updates here.

Template B — Identified / Mitigated

Title: {SERVICE} — Mitigation in progress ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Identified / Under monitoring
Impact: A subset of requests to {ENDPOINT} were affected; mitigation deployed to {REGION}.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Notes: Traffic has been rerouted and error rate has decreased. We are monitoring and expect to provide an update in 30 minutes.

Template C — Resolved

Title: {SERVICE} — Resolved ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Resolved
Impact: Customer-facing impact has been resolved.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Notes: Root cause: brief summary. Remediation: what was changed. Postmortem: link (pending).

Customer-facing email/SMS/CS template (short)

Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {SERVICE} degraded (update)\n
Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

We are aware of degraded performance impacting {SERVICE}. Our engineering team is investigating and we will follow up with another update in ~15 minutes. For updates see: {STATUS_PAGE_LINK} or reply to this message.

— Redwood Inference Support

Customer-facing enterprise template (for large customers; longer form)

Subject: Enterprise notice — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} affecting {SERVICE}

Hi {{CS_LEAD_NAME}} and team,

Summary: brief one-line summary of impact.
Current state: Investigating / Identified / Resolved
Timeline: key timestamps (detection, triage start, mitigation start)
Mitigations in place: list
Action requested: e.g., please confirm whether you’re seeing errors and share logs if relevant.
Contacts: IComm name and on-call primary contact.

SLO and escalation thresholds (examples)

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms (global)
- Error SLO: failed requests < 0.5%
- Automated publish threshold: error rate > 5% for 5m OR p95 latency > 3s for 5m.
- IC escalation: 20 minutes after triaged state OR when SLO breach risk > 2x baseline.

On-call rotation best practices (practical rules)

- Shift length: standard 8 hours weekday, 12 hours weekend (follow people-ops policy for overtime).
- Pair handoffs for the first week of new hires: outgoing must shadow the incoming for >= 1 hour.
- Limit concurrent maintenance tasks during shift transitions: no risky deploys within 30 minutes of handoff.
- Rotation ownership: each service must have a documented owner and backup (name + PD escalation in the runbook).

Game day curriculum (90-minute template)

1. 0–10m: Setup and roles assigned (IC, IComm, SRE Lead).
2. 10–25m: Inject simulated detection (synthetic traffic causing error spike).
3. 25–45m: Validate automation: ensure detection -> incident created -> status draft created.
4. 45–70m: Force escalation by simulating SLO breach; practice customer comms and cross-team coordination.
5. 70–90m: Post-exercise review and actions: assign 3 concrete fixes and owners.

Postmortem and follow-up process

- Postmortem owner: SRE Lead must assign within 48 hours.
- Draft deadline: 7 business days.
- Required sections: summary, timeline, impact (customer-visible), root cause analysis (5 whys or equivalent), mitigations (short-term), systemic recommendations, and action owners with due dates.
- Severity mapping required for executive summaries: Sev-1 (major outage impacting >25% of customers or >1 region for >30 mins), Sev-2 (partial degradation), Sev-3 (minor).

Runbook maintenance and retirement

- Every runbook must have a "last validated" timestamp and a tester name. Runbooks older than 12 months require revalidation before they can be used as automation targets.
- Runbook retirement process: add "deprecated" tag, schedule an owner to migrate callers, and archive old playbooks with cross-links.

Metrics we capture on every incident

- Time to acknowledge (goal < 2 minutes)
- Time to first public communication (goal < 15 minutes when automation gates satisfied)
- Time to mitigation (goal depends on service tier, e.g., < 60 minutes for core inference)
- Mean time to restore (MTTR)
- Postmortem action completion rate (target 95% on-time)

Appendix: automation snippets and examples

Example: create an incident in our incident manager (pseudo-curl)

```
curl -X POST "https://inc-man.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"inference-api","title":"Investigating increased error rate","detected_at":"2026-02-12T14:03:00Z","metrics":{"error_rate":0.072}}'
```

Example: update status page draft (idempotent)

```
curl -X PATCH "https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/drafts/{{DRAFT_ID}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status":"investigating","body":"...templated body..."}'
```

Example: incident handoff message (Slack formatting)

```
/incident-handshake \nshift_incoming: @alice \nshift_outgoing: @priya \nactive_incidents: RWI-20260212-01 (investigating) \nnotes: failover applied to cluster-3, next check in 15m
```

Ownership and links

- Playbook owner: Priya Menon (SRE)
- Escalation and PD config: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024
- Status page automation: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/status-page-integration
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

Revision history

- 2024-05-15: Created (Priya Menon).
- 2025-11-10: Added automation safety gates and enterprise email templates (reviewers: Carlos Ruiz).
- 2026-02-12: Clarified handoff templates and updated game day curriculum (last_updated by Priya Menon).

payload.page_title: Rapid Handoff SOP for Multi-Region Incidents

sections.body:
Summary

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the rapid handoff and orchestration process for incidents that affect services across multiple regions (e.g., us-west + eu-central). It codifies timing expectations, handoff signals, decision ladders, runbook checkpoints, and customer-facing status templates so cross-region responders can coordinate with minimal overhead. Use this page as the canonical reference during multi-region degradations, full-region outages, and cross-region failovers.

Goals

- Restore customer-visible availability and reduce mean time to restore (MTTR).
- Ensure clear ownership for each affected service and geographic region.
- Avoid duplicated work and split-brain decision-making across regions.
- Provide consistent, timely customer communication from the earliest detection.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to any incident that meets one or more of the following: cross-region traffic routing issues, regional capacity loss, multi-region KV-store inconsistency, or simultaneous SLO regressions across regions.
- Not for single-service, single-region minor degradations where local runbooks and on-call ownership suffice.

Roles and responsibilities

- Bridge Operator (primary): owns the unified incident bridge, timeline, and public status page messages. Typically the on-call SRE for the primary impacted service.
- Regional Lead (one per affected region): coordinate triage and local mitigations in-region; report regional state to the bridge.
- Service Owner: technical owner for the product/service surface (model-serving, auth, routing, etc.). Responsible for action items and RCA.
- Escalation Liaison: senior eng/sre who facilitates cross-team decisions (fallbacks, cross-region failover approvals).
- Customer Comms Lead (CS/PR): drafts and approves external customer messages when severity > Sev2.

RTO / SLO thresholds and escalation triggers

- Sev1 (Full outage / widespread customer impact): any region with >= 50% reduction in successful request rate or latency > 5x baseline for 10+ minutes. Escalate to org-level bridge.
- Sev2 (Partial outage / degraded): user-facing errors or latency spikes affecting a subset of customers or routes. Requires cross-region check within 15 minutes.
- Escalate automatically to Escalation Liaison at T+30 minutes if mitigation unclear.

Rapid handoff timeline (T = detection time)

1) T+0 — Detect & Acknowledge (0–3 minutes)
   - Alerting system triggers cross-region page; first responder acknowledges in pager.
   - Bridge Operator creates/claims the incident bridge channel (Zoom/Slack bridge).
   - Post initial internal acknowledgement to status page: use template "initial_acknowledge" (see Customer comms).

2) T+3 — Bridge Formation & Roles (3–8 minutes)
   - Bridge Operator assigns Regional Leads and Service Owner in bridge.
   - Each Regional Lead posts current regional health summary: traffic, error rate, recent deployments.
   - If known, mark any automated failovers / scaling actions already executed.

3) T+8 — Rapid Triage (8–20 minutes)
   - Establish whether incident is a single-failure propagated via control plane (routing, DCS), or independent per-region failures.
   - If control-plane or shared dependency implicated, treat as unified incident and escalate to Org-level coordination.

4) T+20 — Decision Point (20–30 minutes)
   - Decide: (A) proceed with cross-region failover, (B) implement region-isolated mitigations, or (C) take a coordinated rollback.
   - Escalation Liaison must be involved for option A or C.

5) T+30+ — Stabilize & Handback (30 minutes onward)
   - Bridge Operator assigns post-stabilization owner and records action items.
   - If handing control back to regional ops, perform a formal Handoff Checklist (below).

Handoff Checklist (use before releasing bridge)

- Confirm observed customer impact and verify metrics baseline. (Bridge Operator)
- Confirm that all immediate mitigation actions are documented in the incident timeline. (Regional Leads)
- Validate that no outstanding cross-region decision remains (failover, rollback). (Escalation Liaison)
- Assign long-running action items with owners and due dates. (Service Owner)
- Schedule follow-up postmortem meeting within 48–72 hours. (Bridge Operator / Service Owner)

Decision ladder (who approves what)

- Local mitigations (scale, restart, config tweak): Regional Lead.
- Cross-region traffic shift / DNS failover: Escalation Liaison + Service Owner sign-off.
- Customer-impacting rollbacks: Service Owner + Product Manager + Escalation Liaison.

Bridge operator runbook quick commands

- Create bridge channel: /incident create --service=<service> --regions=us-west,eu-central --sev=1
- Attach runbook: /incident attach-runbook <runbook-id>
- Notify exec channel: /incident notify-exec --summary "Multi-region routing degradation"

Evidence collection checklist (must be captured in timeline)

1) Timeline entries for each action (timestamped): detection, ack, mitigations, role assignments.
2) Key system graphs: per-region request rate, error rate, P50/P95 latency, queue depth.
3) Recent deploys or infra changes in the prior 60 minutes.
4) Network/bgp/dns changes, cloud region health notices.

Customer communication templates

- initial_acknowledge (internal & status page)
  "We have detected an issue affecting [SERVICE] impacting traffic in multiple regions. Our engineers are investigating. We will provide an update within 15 minutes. (Incident ID: [INCIDENT_ID])"

- ongoing_update (public)
  "Update: We are investigating elevated errors/latency affecting [SERVICE] across [REGIONS]. Current mitigation: [ACTION]. Next update in 30 minutes or earlier if there is a change."

- mitigation_progress (public)
  "Update: We have implemented [MITIGATION] which has reduced error rates by ~[PERCENT]. We continue to monitor and will provide a status when the issue is fully resolved."

- resolved (public)
  "Resolved: The issue affecting [SERVICE] across [REGIONS] has been resolved at [TIME UTC]. Root cause: [SHORT RCA]. Customers may need to retry in-flight operations; none of the user data was lost. A postmortem will be posted within 72 hours."

Status page guidance

- Post the initial_acknowledge as soon as the bridge is created (T+0–3).
- For Sev1 incidents, use the public status page and include a severity tag and affected regions.
- Update cadence: 15 minutes for the first hour, then 30 minutes until resolved.

Postmortem rubric and template (to be completed within 72 hours)

- Title: [Service] — Multi-Region Incident — [Date]
- Summary: two-paragraph summary of what happened and customer impact.
- Timeline: annotated time-stamped actions (raw evidence snippets).
- Impact: affected customers, latency, error counts, duration.
- Root cause analysis: Causal chain and contributing factors.
- Corrective actions: prioritized list with owners and target dates (P0/P1/P2).
- Learnings and follow-ups: process changes, monitoring gaps.

Game day checklist for multi-region scenarios

- Pre-game: identify 2 services and mark Regions A/B as simulated failure targets. Ensure valid canary traffic generators.
- During game: practice bridge creation, assigning Regional Leads, and executing a DNS/traffic shift.
- Validate: status page templates, exec notifications, and customer comm approval flow.
- Post-game: generate a short retro and update this SOP with any gaps discovered.

Rotation and handoff best practices

- Handoffs should be intentional: 5–10 minute synchronous overlap for critical incidents.
- Use a "brief, readback" pattern: outgoing oncall states the current hypothesis, outstanding actions, and next expected check-in time. Incoming oncall reads back to confirm.
- Maintain up-to-date personal runbook links in the oncall profile card.

Failure modes and mitigation patterns (examples)

- Control-plane cascade: prioritize isolating shared control-plane services (config store, routing layer) and execute region-level circuit breakers.
- KV-store split-brain: suspend cross-region writes and promote read-only routing to healthy regions until reconciliation.
- Network blackhole in a region: shift traffic via CDN/origin routing and coordinate with cloud provider for region-level diagnostics.

Appendices

- Appendix A: Example Handoff Slack script
  "
  [OUTGOING] 14:35 UTC — Handoff to @incoming
  Hypothesis: routing control-plane N+1 failure in us-west causing 502s.
  Actions taken: scaled router pool x2, disabled canary config v42, started failover per runbook.
  Outstanding: DNS TTL propagation expected until 14:50 UTC.
  Next check-in: 14:40 UTC.
  [INCOMING] 14:36 UTC — Readback: Confirmed.
  "

- Appendix B: Quick approvals matrix (names and escalation phone numbers)
  "Service Owner: @svc-owner (pager)
  Escalation Liaison: @sre-lead (pager)
  Customer Comms Lead: cs-lead@example.com
  "

- Appendix C: Runbook links (insert canonical runbook links here)
  "Routing runbook: [link:routing-runbook]
  KV reconciliation: [link:kv-reconcile]"

Notes and governance

- This SOP is reviewed quarterly and after every Sev1 multi-region incident.
- Major changes (new failover strategy, DNS architecture changes) must be approved by the SRE leadership team and documented here.

Contact and escalation directory

- Bridge Operator rotation: see /oncall/rotations (internal link).
- To request an urgent cross-region test or game day, file an RFC in the #ops-scheduling channel.

Revision history

- 2026-04-15 — created by Asha Patel (published).
- 2026-06-28 — clarified decision ladder and added evidence checklist (review: Miguel Torres).
- 2026-09-10 — updated customer comm cadence and handoff checklist after game day (review: Claire Nguyen).

Related guidance

- See also: incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024, oncall-playbook-rotation-handoff-and-simulation-scenarios-2026, service-stability-orchestration-handbook-incident-scripts-and-rotation-playbook-2026.

payload.page_title: Incident Execution Guide, Runbooks, and Communication Templates

sections.body: This page is an operational playbook for executing incidents from detection through postmortem and remediation. It standardizes roles, runbook structure, alert thresholds, communication templates, rotation rules, and game day exercises. Use this guide as the canonical source for incident execution across Redwood Inference services.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted and Dedicated/Private control-plane services that impact customer-facing inference APIs, console, or billing.
- Excludes routine CI failures and development branch problems (handled by triage owners).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Incident: any event causing customer-visible degradation or data/control plane impact for >30s or impacting >0.5% of requests in a region for >5 minutes.
- Severity levels: P0 (system down or data loss), P1 (significant customer impact), P2 (degraded performance impacting SLAs), P3 (minor or isolated issues).
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
1) Detection & Alerting
   - Sources: Prometheus alerts, tracing-based anomaly detectors, Synthetics (every region), customer-reported tickets, platform health probes.
   - Automatic triage: Alerts with matching runbook tags are routed to oncall via PagerDuty with escalation policies defined below.
2) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Pager acknowledges, documents initial symptoms in the incident channel (Slack #inc-<service>-<region>).
   - If impact meets P1/P0 criteria, auto-page Incident Commander (IC) and notify Product/Customer Success.
3) Containment & Mitigation
   - IC assigns roles and calls for mitigation steps. Mitigation goal: stop customer impact, minimize blast radius, restore availability.
4) Restoration
   - Validate service health across regions, update status page, and begin traffic rehoming if required.
5) Post-incident review
   - Capture timeline within 48 hours; full postmortem completed in 7 business days with action items and owners.
sections.heading: Incident lifecycle (high level)

sections.body:
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads incident, sets priorities, owns the incident timeline, and makes rollout/fallback decisions. (Default: SRE oncall lead).
- Communications Lead: Owns customer-facing comms, status page updates, internal summaries. (Default: oncall primary until handed to PM/CS).
- Engineering Owner(s): Service-owner engineers who run remediation steps and confirm fixes.
- Support Liaison: Triage customer tickets, surfaces relevant customer impact details.
- War Room Coordinator: Creates and moderates incident Slack channel, ensures notes and recordings are captured.
sections.heading: Roles & responsibilities

sections.body:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary oncall for SREs, 1 week secondary. Follow policy: maximum 6 consecutive weeks oncall per year per engineer.
- Handoff checklist (to run at every rotation swap):
  1. Confirm PagerDuty schedule and escalation contacts.
  2. Confirm access (kube, cloud console, logs-bucket).
  3. Review 3 most recent active runbooks and ongoing incidents.
  4. Share any planned maintenance windows.
- Handoff message example:
  "Handoff: @alice -> @bob. Primary oncall for inference-core this week. No active incidents. Known maintenance: database patch Thursday 02:00 UTC. Key dashboards: /dashboards/inference-overview. PD escalation: pd://redwood/inference-primary.
sections.heading: On-call rotations and handoffs

sections.body:
- Title (service-region-tag)
- Purpose and scope
- Owner & reviewers (team email + schedule)
- Triggers (alerts / symptoms that should cause invocation)
- Pre-flight checks (e.g., verify region, check KV cache status)
- Step-by-step mitigation (numbered, idempotent steps)
- Validation (how to confirm success)
- Rollback / fallback plan
- Post-incident tasks & references
sections.heading: Runbook structure (required fields)

sections.body:
---
Title: inference-api-high-5xx-us-east-1
Owner: inference-svc-team@redwood.com
sections.heading: Sample runbook (truncated)

sections.body:
- prometheus: inference_api_5xx_rate > 0.5% (5m)
- synthetic: /health returns 500 from 3 probes in 2 regions
sections.heading: Triggers

sections.body:
1) Confirm the alert: grep "5xx" /var/logs/inference/* | tail -n 200
2) Check deployment health: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "CrashLoop|0/"
3) If new deploy in last 30m: rollback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=<previous>
4) If not deploy-related: scale down suspect node pool: gcloud container clusters resize <cluster> --node-pool=<pool> --num-nodes=<reduced>
5) Purge local KV caches on affected hosts: redis-cli -h <host> FLUSHDB (only if cached keys are ephemeral)
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- requests_p95 latency returns below 400ms across 5 minutes
- 5xx rate < 0.1% for 10 consecutive minutes
---
sections.heading: Validation

sections.body:
- 5xx error rate: trigger if >0.5% requests for 5m (P1), >2.0% for 2m (P0).
- Latency: p95 > 1000ms for 5m -> investigate P1. p99 > 2s for 3m -> P0.
- Queue backpressure: queued requests > 5k in a region -> P1.
- Synthetic failures: 3 region probes failing in 5m -> P1.
sections.heading: Alert thresholds and metric guidelines (examples)

sections.body:
- Primary oncall (first 5 minutes)
- After 5 minutes with unresolved mitigation: escalate to secondary oncall + IC auto-notify
- After 15 minutes for P0 events: page Engineering Director + Head of SRE + Customer Success lead
sections.heading: Escalation matrix (summary)

sections.body:
- Use status.redwood.ai for public status. For Dedicated/Private customers also use ticketing system and account-level email templates.

Templates (copy/paste and fill placeholders)
1) Initial acknowledgement (15 minutes):
Subject: [Incident] Redwood Inference – {service} experiencing errors in {region}
sections.heading: Status page and customer comms templates
Body
Body

sections.body:
The incident impacting {service} in {region} is resolved as of {time UTC}.
Impact summary: {duration, affected customers, root cause (initial)}
Follow-up: A full post-incident review will be published when complete with action items and timelines.
Contact: support@redwood.ai
sections.heading: Body

sections.body:
- Keep language non-technical and candid.
- Include impact, work underway, ETA (if available), and mitigation steps.
- Mark updates with timestamps and an internal incident id.
- For sensitive incidents (data loss, security), route updates through Security & Legal for approval.
sections.heading: Customer status page content guidelines

sections.body:
- Draft timeline (owner: IC) due within 48 hours — includes minute-level timeline, alerts, and remediation steps taken.
- Full postmortem document due within 7 business days. Postmortem must include: summary, timeline, root cause analysis (5 whys / RCA), corrective actions (owner and ETA), and verification plan.
- Postmortem review: mandatory review meeting attended by IC, owners, SRE manager, and PM.
- Action tracking: add all remediation tasks to the incident JIRA/project board with labels: incident-<id>, postmortem, blocker. Owners must provide progress updates weekly until complete.
sections.heading: Post-incident review process

sections.body:
- Quarterly regional failover exercise (target: rotate primary traffic across regions without customer downtime).
- Monthly mini-simulations: single-service degradation with 30-minute time-boxed resolution.
- Annual full-stack P0 simulation conducted with exec observers.
sections.heading: Game day program (recommended cadence)

sections.body:
- Runbook gaps report, playbook updates, training assignments.
- Scorecard: average MTTR, missed steps, communication quality (customer-facing clarity).
sections.heading: Game day outputs

sections.body:
- Ownership: every runbook must list an owner and two reviewers. Runbooks are reviewed quarterly.
- Retirement: deprecated runbooks archived with reason and date.
- PR process: runbook edits are submitted via docs repo PR; urgency edits allowed with follow-up review within 5 business days.
sections.heading: Runbook maintenance & governance

sections.body:
- Block high-stress sequences: restrict scheduled changes during primary oncall week unless emergency.
- Offer 4 hours backup time after P0 events for rest & paperwork (approved by manager).
sections.heading: Oncall wellbeing and limits

sections.body:
- Useful CLI snippets:
  - View recent deploys: kubectl -n inference rollout history deployment/inference-api
  - Force rollback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=<rev>
  - Query error rate: prometheus-query 'sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="inference"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference"}[5m]))'

- Example incident timeline (abbreviated):
  00:00 Alert fires: 5xx rate spike detected (0.8%)
  00:02 PagerDuty acknowledged by oncall
  00:06 Triage finds suspect deploy 00:45 UTC -> rollback initiated 00:07
  00:14 Error rate begins to decline -> p95 latency improving
  00:20 Traffic normalized; status page updated to "Partial degradations being mitigated"
  01:10 Incident declared resolved; IC closes incident and assigns postmortem owner

- Postmortem template header (to copy into PRD):
  Title: {incident-id} – {short summary}
  Severity: {P0/P1/P2}
  Timeline owner: {name}
  Root cause: {summary}
  Corrective actions: - {action} (owner, ETA)

Contact matrix & escalation contacts (always keep PD entries up to date):
- SRE primary: oncall-sre-primary@redwood.ai
- Engineering director: director-eng@redwood.ai
- CS incident liaison: cs-liaison@redwood.ai
sections.heading: Appendices

- /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks

payload.page_title: SLO-driven automated fallthrough and incident playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document defines an SLO-driven incident response pattern we call the "fallthrough flow": automated detection of SLO boundary crossings, progressive mitigation (automated routing and model fallbacks), and human-run escalation/playbooks where automation cannot resolve the issue. It combines end-to-end runbooks, on-call rotation guidance, game day scenarios, status page and customer communications templates, and a postmortem checklist.

Scope
-----
- Services: model-serving (hosted and dedicated), routing layer, cache services (prefix/KV), and the control plane that performs routing and rollouts.
- Intended for incidents that originate from performance or availability regressions that cause SLO boundary crossings (latency, request error rate, embedding failure rate).
- Not intended for security incidents (see security-and-compliance incident playbooks).

When to apply this playbook
--------------------------
Apply when an automated SLO alert triggers (see SLO table below) or when an on-call detects a customer-impacting degradation. For minor anomalies that do not cross SLOs, follow the local diagnostics flow and file an RCA if recurring.

SLOs and severity mapping
-------------------------
| SLO Category | Target | Alert trigger | Severity |
|--------------|--------|---------------|----------|
| p95 latency (text-gen) | < 300 ms | p95 > 600 ms for 5m | Sev-2 |
| p99 latency (text-gen) | < 900 ms | p99 > 1800 ms for 2m | Sev-1 |
| Request error rate | < 0.5% | 1% sustained for 5m | Sev-1 |
| Embedding failure rate | < 0.2% | 0.5% sustained 10m | Sev-2 |
| Control plane API availability | 99.9% monthly | 5min outage | Sev-1 |

Severity definitions (quick)
- Sev-1: Broad customer impact or production outage (multiple customers/regions failing). Immediate all-hands escalation.
- Sev-2: Significant degradation affecting a subset of customers or elevated error/latency but partial functionality.
- Sev-3: Localized issue, non-critical, triage during office hours.

Automated fallthrough flow (overview)
------------------------------------
1) Detection: SLO alerting triggers via Prometheus/Alertmanager (SLO bridges into Alertmanager rules).
2) Automated mitigation: playbook-runner executes pre-configured actions for the matched service and severity. Typical actions (in order):
   - Activate per-customer model fallback (route to a compatible model variant with lower latency/quantizations).
   - Enable aggressive prefix/KV cache priming for affected route.
   - Apply temporary throttling/burst control to limit new requests (protect downstream).
   - If control-plane unavailable, promote a cached routing policy (local policy file) to avoid dependency calls.
3) Notification: PagerDuty alert to primary on-call, Slack incident channel created, status page incident draft created.
4) Human escalation: If automation resolves within the auto-resolve timeout (default 7 minutes), automation posts a closure note. Otherwise, escalate to Sev-1 runbook.

Automated mitigation examples (commands)
- Promote a fallback model via rcli (Redwood CLI):
  rcli rollout promote --service model-router --from live --to fallback-low-latency --reason "auto-slo-fallthrough"

- Enable KV caching warmup for route:
  rcli cache enable --route /v1/generate --ttl 3600 --mode warmup

- Apply throttling at gateway:
  rcli gateway throttle --route /v1/embeddings --rate 200rps --burst 400

Sev-1 incident runbook: high p99 latency across region
----------------------------------------------------
Immediate actions (first 10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and create an incident channel: #incident-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>-<id>.
2) Post the short incident summary to the channel with the SLO breaches and region(s) affected.
3) Run quick health checks (commands):
   - kubectl get pods -n model-serving -l app=model --output wide
   - rcli metrics query --expr "avg_over_time(model_p99_latency[5m])" --service model-serving
   - curl -sS https://status.redwood.example/api/v1/incident-drafts | jq .
4) If automation has already applied fallbacks, confirm fallback status: rcli rollout status --service model-router
5) If error rate also elevated, capture sample failed requests (request ids) and attach to the incident channel.

Diagnostics (5–30 minutes)
- Check resource saturation: nvidia-smi on affected nodes, node CPU/memory, network errors in dmesg.
- Check model runtime logs for OOM, kernel errors, or compilation failures.
- Verify upstream dependencies (S3, control plane, KMS) with synthetic checks.
- If KV cache hit rate dropped, run: rcli cache stats --route /v1/generate

Mitigation options (ordered by risk)
1) Scale up dedicated pool for the model: rcli capacity add --pool model-pool-4x --count 2
2) Reduce model concurrency/sequence length defaults for new requests (config change): update config at /configs/model-serving/runtime.yaml and apply: rcli config apply --file runtime.yaml
3) Rollback to previous model revision: rcli model rollback --service model-serving --to revision-20260201
4) If control-plane dependent routing failing, swap to static routing: rcli routing set-static --service model-router --file static-routes.json

Rollback guidance
- Preconditions: validate that the target revision was healthy (pass smoke tests). Run: rcli model smoke-test --revision revision-20260201 --tests basic-gen,embed
- Rollback steps: 1) Schedule a rolling rollback with canary 10%. 2) Wait 2 minutes, evaluate p95/p99. 3) Ramp to 100% if stable.

Post-incident (within 24–72 hours)
- If automation resolved the incident without human intervention, author must still file a short incident note with cause and what automation did.
- For Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents: file a full postmortem (template below) within 72 hours and declare an owner for action items.
- Runbook update: if an automated action misfired or made the incident worse, immediately add a gated rollback step to the automation and mark the runbook for review.

Runbook: high p99 latency (example)
- Owner: runtime-team@redwood.example
- Primary TLDR: p99 latency > 1800ms across region for 2m. Follow automated fallthrough, then escalate to human if unresolved.
- Dashboard: [Model Serving - Latency] (grafana://dashboards/model-serving-latency)
- Steps:
  1) Confirm SLO and scope.
  2) Execute automated fallthrough (if not already executed).
  3) Capture traces for 5 requests: rcli trace tail --service model-serving --limit 5
  4) If CPU/GPU saturation: add capacity (see mitigation options).
  5) If tracing shows KV cache misses as root cause: warm caches and consider cache policy change.
  6) If third-party dependency (S3, KMS) is slow: engage infra-oncall and consider short-circuiting calls.

On-call rotation and handoff checklist
------------------------------------
- Recommended rotation: primary on-call 7 days, secondary 7 days, SRE duty engineer 1 week; overlap handoff windows of 30 minutes.
- Handoff checklist (to be posted in calendar invite):
  - Current incidents and their status.
  - Outstanding action items and owners.
  - Any scheduled rollouts or canaries in-flight.
  - Paging schedule and escalation policy.
  - Link to rotation roster: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/roster-2026

Game day scenarios and exercises
------------------------------
We run quarterly game days. Scenarios to include:
- Model-wide p99 latency spike caused by new kernel path. Objective: validate fallback automation and rollback steps.
- Control plane API outage simulated for 15 minutes. Objective: validate static routing promotion and degraded-mode behavior.
- Multi-region partial blackout (eg: simulated AZ failure). Objective: validate cross-region routing and customer-safe fallbacks.
- Silent regression: 10% increase in model hallucination rate (quality). Objective: validate quality alerting and rollback to previous model.

Status page and customer communications templates
----------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Title: Degraded model-serving latency in us-west-2 - Impact: Some hosted inference requests experience elevated latency or failures.
- Affected Services: Hosted text-generation (model: redwood-llama-13b-quant).
- Start time: 2026-02-10T09:12:00Z
- Next update: 2026-02-10T09:27:00Z
- Mitigation: Automated fallbacks and cache warmups applied. Scaling in progress.
sections.heading: Status page draft (short form)

sections.body:
Subject: Service impact affecting inference latency (region: us-west-2)
Hi <CustomerName>,
We are investigating an incident affecting inference latency in us-west-2 that may impact requests to hosted text-generation models. Our automated mitigation has been applied and we are actively scaling capacity. We will post updates on https://status.redwood.example and notify you as we have a resolution.
If you require assistance or have a critical workload, reply to this email and our customer success team will prioritize you.
Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support

Slack templates for incident channels
- Initial post (pinned):
  > Summary: p99 latency breach in us-west-2 for model-serving.
  > SLOs: p99 > 1800ms.
  > Immediate actions taken: automated fallback promoted, cache warmup, gateway throttling.
  > Commands to run: rcli rollout status --service model-router
  > Owner: @runtime-oncall

- Ongoing updates: timestamped short notes listing new diagnostics and mitigations. Avoid long paragraphs.

Postmortem template (required for Sev-1/Sev-2)
-----------------------------------------------
- Title:
- Incident ID:
- Status: draft | reviewed | closed
- Timeline (UTC): bullet list with timestamps and short events.
- Impact: systems/customers/regions affected, estimated % of requests impacted.
- Root cause analysis: concise causal chain with evidence.
- Why it wasn't detected earlier: instrumentation gaps.
- Action items: each with owner, due date, risk level.
- Follow-up verification plan: smoke tests, scheduled audit.
- Lessons learned.

Runbook maintenance and governance
--------------------------------
- All runbooks must be reviewed quarterly and after any Sev-1 incident.
- Automation scripts referenced by a runbook must include a canary check and a manual abort flag.
- Ownership: runtime-team owns model-serving runbooks; eng-sre owns oncall rotations and escalation policies.

Appendix A: Example incident log entry (copy into incident channel)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
[2026-02-10 09:12:04 UTC] ALERT: p99 latency exceeded threshold in us-west-2 (p99=2.2s). Automation triggered: fallback promoted to fallback-low-latency.
[2026-02-10 09:15:30 UTC] Action: fallback at 100% confirmed; p99 decreased to 980ms.
[2026-02-10 09:35:00 UTC] Action: scaled model pool by 2 instances; p99 stable at 320ms.

Appendix B: Quick reference commands
----------------------------------
- rcli rollout status --service model-router
- rcli model rollback --service model-serving --to <revision>
- rcli cache stats --route /v1/generate
- kubectl logs -n model-serving <pod> --since=10m

Contact matrix (escalation)
--------------------------
- Primary on-call: runtime-oncall@pagerduty (page immediately)
- Secondary on-call: eng-sre@pagerduty
- Incident commander rotation: see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/ic-rotation

Document history
----------------
- 2025-11-15: Created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-01-20: Added automated mitigation examples and CLI snippets (reviewers: Ethan Rivera).
- 2026-02-10: Clarified rollback guidance and added game day scenarios (reviewers: Priya Natarajan, Liam O'Connor).

References and related pages
---------------------------
- SLO policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-policy-2025
- Runtime runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Routing and control plane playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/routing-playbook
