payload.page_title: Operator Competency & Incident Evidence Handbook

sections.body: This handbook prescribes the operator competency levels and the Incident Evidence Package (IEP) lifecycle used by Redwood Inference for on-call and incident response. It standardizes what to collect during and after an incident, how to store and name artifacts, who owns retention decisions, and how operator skills are assessed and renewed. The audience includes bridge operators, incident commanders, SRE managers, compliance, and customer success.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Ensure reproducible, auditable evidence for postmortems and customer/regulatory requests.
- Keep bridge operators prepared through a clear competency path and game-day practice.
- Reduce time-to-evidence after incidents and lower risk of incomplete investigations.
sections.heading: Why this exists

sections.body:
- Applies to incidents impacting Redwood-hosted public endpoints and customer-facing Dedicated/Private services when Redwood manages evidence.
- Routine maintenance with no customer-facing impact is out of scope.
sections.heading: Applicability

sections.body:
- Band 0 / Observer: Reads runbooks, shadows bridges. Training: 1 shadow shift.
- Band 1 / Operator: Executes standard bridges, collects IEP items. Training: checklist + supervised run.
- Band 2 / Senior Operator: Runs multi-region bridges, prepares IEP for IC. Training: proctored sim + mentor sign-off.
- Band 3 / Lead: Coaches operators, validates evidence completeness on high-impact incidents. Training: demonstrated leadership in multiple incidents and game-days.
- Band 4 / Incident Commander: Owns tactical decisions and customer escalations. Training: proctor assessment and leadership endorsement.
sections.heading: Operator competency bands (short)

sections.body:
- Badges issued after assessment and logged in the SRE credential registry.
- Renewal cadence: Bands 0-1 yearly; Bands 2-4 every 6 months or after major platform changes.
- Failed assessments require a documented remediation plan and retest window (30 days).
sections.heading: Badge lifecycle and renewal

sections.body:
- Incident identifier, start and end timestamps, and bridge id.
- Chronological timeline of status updates and actions.
- Metrics snapshots: p50/p95/p99 and error rates for relevant signals.
- Representative logs: -15m to +30m around incident start (sampling allowed with justification).
- Traces/spans for affected request flows.
- Relevant config/deploy markers: commit id, deploy id, feature-flag state.
- Copies of status page messages and customer comms.
- Evidence manifest: list of artifacts, storage URIs, and checksums.
sections.heading: Incident Evidence Package (IEP) minimum contents

sections.body:
1) Export bridge transcript and note bridge id.
2) Capture a metrics snapshot covering the incident window.
3) Export logs for the time window; filter for errors/timeouts but include context lines.
4) Export traces with higher sampling for the first 30 minutes.
5) Record deploy/config state and capture diffs where applicable.
6) Save drafts of status page and customer messages.
7) Publish evidence manifest to the secure evidence bucket and record checksums.

Example commands (illustrative, edit per service):
- Metrics: ri-cli metrics export --service "$SERVICE" --from "$INC_START" --to "$INC_END" --out /tmp/metrics-$INCIDENT.json
- Logs: ri-cli logs export --service "$SERVICE" --from "$INC_START" --to "$INC_END" --filter "error OR timeout" --out /tmp/logs-$INCIDENT.tgz
- Traces: ri-cli traces export --service "$SERVICE" --window "$INC_START/$INC_END" --out /tmp/traces-$INCIDENT.json
- Bridge transcript: bridgectl export --id $BRIDGE_ID --format text --out /tmp/bridge-$INCIDENT.txt
sections.heading: Immediate collection checklist (run on bridge)

sections.body:
- All IEP artifacts must be stored under s3://ri-incident-evidence/<year>/<incident-id>/
- Filenames: <incident-id>__<artifact-type>__<short-desc>__v<1>.<ext>
- Example: 2025-03-10-INC-8421__logs__ingest-api__v1.tgz
sections.heading: Storage and naming standards

sections.body:
- IEP metadata and timelines: 7 years.
- Aggregated metrics and summaries: 7 years.
- Raw logs: 1 year unless escalated to legal hold.
- Traces: 90 days full fidelity, 2 years sampled summaries.
- Screenshots and customer comms: 7 years.
- PII or customer data: retention governed by contract and legal guidance.
sections.heading: Retention (summary)

sections.body:
- Evidence Custodian approves retention exceptions and legal holds.
- Access requires an evidence request ticket with justification; presigned URLs expire by default after 72 hours.
- All access is audited; audit records are attached to the evidence manifest.
sections.heading: Governance and access control

sections.body:
- Deletion of evidence requires approval from the Evidence Custodian and Legal.
- Legal holds suspend deletion and retention timers until Legal clears the hold.
sections.heading: Legal holds and deletion

sections.body:
- The postmortem author must link to the IEP artifacts and manifest URIs.
- IEP completeness verification must occur within 72 hours of incident closure; missing artifacts escalate to the SRE manager.
sections.heading: Postmortem responsibilities

sections.body:
- Minimum cadence: quarterly simulations per team; monthly for high-risk services (business-critical or frequently failing systems).
- Each game-day requires operators to: run a bridge, capture a full IEP, draft a status page message, and complete a rubric.
- Passing game-day simulations contribute to badge renewal requirements.
sections.heading: Game-day integration and operator fitness

sections.body:
1) Candidate schedules a 60-90 minute proctored simulation.
2) The simulation includes triage, bridge ops, evidence collection, and comms.
3) Proctor scores the candidate against a standardized rubric and records pass/fail and notes.
4) On pass, update badge status; on fail, issue remediation plan and retest window.
sections.heading: Assessment workflow (proctored sim)

sections.body:
- Sev1 (complete outage or multi-tenant impact): Full IEP + extended logs + raw traces + deploy diffs + regulatory packet as needed.
- Sev2 (partial outage or degraded SLOs): Full IEP + representative logs + sampled traces.
- Sev3 (localized degradation): Compact IEP (metadata, metrics, minimal logs).
sections.heading: Severity guidance for evidence depth

sections.body:
1) Stakeholder opens evidence-request ticket using the template.
2) Evidence Custodian validates scope within 24 hours.
3) Custodian provides presigned URIs or schedules a secure review session.
4) Access is logged; ticket closed after verification or when legal hold is applied.
sections.heading: Evidence request process (short)

sections.body:
- IEP completeness within 72h for Sev1/Sev2: target 98%.
- Internal evidence access SLA: 24 hours.
- Badge renewal on time: 95% of operators.

Appendix: templates and short samples
- Status page short template (public):
  Title: Service Degradation — [service-name]
  Impact: Customers may experience increased latency in [region].
  Started: [ISO timestamp]
  Updates: Every 30 minutes until resolved
  Current: Mitigation underway

- Customer notification (CS/Enterprise):
  Subject: Incident [incident-id] — [service-name] — Impact & Next Steps
  Body: We observed an incident beginning at [time] impacting [scope]. Actions taken: [summary]. Postmortem ETA: [date]. Contact: [CS lead].
sections.heading: KPIs and targets

sections.body:
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@redwood.ai>
- Evidence Custodian: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@redwood.ai>
sections.heading: Contacts and governance (short)

sections.body:
- 2024-11-20: Created by A. Patel
- 2024-12-15: Clarified traces retention and evidence manifest format
- 2025-03-10: Added game-day cadence and updated badge renewal intervals

End of handbook.
sections.heading: Revision history

payload.page_title: stabilization-runloop-rotation-index-and-customer-briefs-2024

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Stabilization Runloop used for first 90 minutes of an operational incident, the Responder Rotation Index (role matrix and handover rules), a compact Evidence Cookbook for collecting defensible data during live incidents, plus ready-to-send customer-facing status templates for the status page and email/Slack.

Scope: Applies to all incidents impacting Redwood hosted inference, dedicated pools, or private deployments where customer-visible SLOs (latency, availability, embeddings correctness) are degraded. This is not a replacement for per-service runbooks; it is the cross-service stabilization scaffold to be used for multi-service degradations and escalations.

Ownership and contacts

- Incident Commander (IC): role assigned per incident, default escalation to oncall SRE.
- Bridge Operator: Engineering oncall who manages the bridge/Slack channel and status updates.
- Service Stewards: owners of affected services (listed in service catalog).
- Evidence Custodian: the investigator responsible for capturing and preserving logs/traces/artifacts.

If IC unknown, page on-call rota: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations-index (canonical).

Stabilization Runloop (0–90 minute scaffold)

1) First 5 minutes — Acknowledge & classify
   - Acknowledge pager and immediately open incident bridge (Zoom/Slack Huddle).
   - IC posts short incident summary to #incidents and triggers the Notification Ladder.
   - Classify impact: Severity-1 (Service down), Severity-2 (SLO degradation), Severity-3 (partial/isolated).
   - Record initial hypothesis (one-line) and begin Evidence Cookbook checklist.

2) Minutes 5–20 — Contain and prioritize
   - IC defines containment objective (e.g., prevent error amplification, reduce traffic, disable problematic route).
   - Apply safe mitigations: route failover, short-term rate limits, circuit-breakers, scaling spot instances.
   - Bridge Operator posts customer-facing interim message (see templates).

3) Minutes 20–45 — Diagnose and validate mitigation
   - Evidence Custodian collects logs, trace IDs, request/response samples, and KV-cache snapshot if applicable.
   - Attach diagnostics to incident ticket (Incident ID).
   - If mitigation effective, transition to ‘stabilized’ state and monitor for recurrence for 30–60 minutes.

4) Minutes 45–90 — Remediate and prepare recovery steps
   - Plan rollback or patching steps if mitigation is temporary.
   - If code or model change is implicated, freeze further rollouts and enable model fallback to previous verified variant.
   - IC schedules follow-up action owners and post-incident blameless RCA lead.

Rotation Index: Roles & Handoff Rules

- Incident Commander (IC): single owner for decision authority. Handover rule: new IC must be explicitly accepted on the bridge and announce time of handover.
- Bridge Operator: responsible for status messages, stakeholder pings, and customer notices. Handover rule: share latest message draft and last timestamp of customer update.
- Technical Lead(s): service-specific engineers. Handover rule: summarize tests run and next required action.
- Evidence Custodian: ensures artifacts are stored and preserved. Handover rule: provide storage path and list of preserved artifacts.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Active mitigations (what, who, when applied)
2. Observed impact and metrics at handover
3. Pending actions and blockers
4. Next scheduled status update time

Evidence Cookbook (what to collect, where, and why)

Collect early, collect often. Preserve raw artifacts before running destructive remediation when possible. If live remediation must occur, snapshot before mutation.
sections.heading: Handover checklist (always read out loud on bridge)

sections.body:
- Incident ID and timeline (UTC).
- Pager payload and originating alert rule.
- Top 100 error logs (timestamped) from affected services (JSON format).
- Representative request/response pairs with headers and model outputs (redact user PII).
- Trace spans (trace IDs) covering failure path (link to APM dashboard).
- Token-level runtime metrics for LLM requests (latency, tokens emitted, backend queue time).
- KV cache stats and recent cache hit/miss samples (if applicable).
- GPU/host telemetry at incident window (GPU utilization, memory, XLA failures).
- Rollout/CI history for the last 24h (deploy IDs, model version, quantization profile).
- Network flow captures or LB logs if packet-level issues suspected.

Storage and retention
- Upload artifacts to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/{incident-id}/evidence (or internal equivalent).
- Tag artifacts with incident-id and evidence-custodian name.
- Retain critical artifacts for 90 days by default; escalate to security if retention needed longer for compliance.

Chain of custody notes: record who pulled/exported data and the precise commands used. Example:
- Command: aws s3 cp /var/log/service/error.log s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1234/evidence/error.log --profile incident-custodian

Postmortem & Blameless RCA process
sections.heading: Minimum artifact set (Evidence Custodian priority)

sections.body:
- Any customer-visible SLO breach lasting > 5 minutes.
- Any incident with an SLA credit or legal/regulatory impact.
sections.heading: Triggers for postmortem

sections.body:
1. Summary: 3-sentence incident synopsis and customer impact.
2. Timeline: concise, minute-level timeline of key events.
3. Root cause: single sentence plus supporting evidence.
4. Contributing factors: systemic/process/code/model items.
5. Remediations: short-term and long-term with owners and ETA.
6. Follow-ups: list of tracked action items in Jira with owners.
7. Lessons learned and monitoring improvements.

Game-days and simulation guidance
sections.heading: Postmortem template (must be filled within 7 business days)

sections.body:
- Validate Stabilization Runloop timings (ack -> bridge -> first customer notice).
- Exercise Evidence Cookbook collection under time pressure.
- Verify rotation handovers and noisy-channel reduction (fewer than 3 concurrent messengers).
sections.heading: Objectives for exercises

sections.body:
- KV-cache mismatch causing degraded latency for tail queries.
- Model rollout causing hallucination/regression in a targeted prompt set.
- Multiregion failover with partial capacity loss in a primary region.
sections.heading: Recommended scenarios (quarterly)

sections.body:
- Time-to-first-bridge (target < 4 minutes)
- Time-to-interim-customer-notice (target < 15 minutes)
- Evidence completeness (required artifacts captured)
- Number of simultaneous communicators (target 1–2)

Status Page & Customer Brief Templates

Use plain, non-technical language for public pages. Keep customer notices short, factual, and updated at predictable cadence (every 15–30 minutes while active).
sections.heading: Scoring rubric

sections.body:
- Title: Incident: High Latency for Model Generation
- Short summary: We are investigating increased latency for text generation in our hosted API. Some requests may return slowly or time out.
- Impact: A subset of customers in us-west-2 may see generation latency over 5s.
- ETA: We are actively diagnosing; next update in 30 minutes.
- Mitigation: We have applied a temporary routing change to reduce error amplification.
sections.heading: Public status page template (short)

sections.body:
- Subject: Redwood status update — degraded inference latency (Incident INC-1234)
- Body: Hello — We are investigating a latency issue affecting text generation. Our engineers have applied a temporary routing change and are collecting diagnostics. We will post another update in 30 minutes. If you rely on low-latency endpoints, please consider using the regional failover option or pinning to dedicated capacity.

Internal short message (Bridge Operator to #incidents):
- [INC-1234] S2: High tail latency RN. Mitigation applied: routing to fallback pool. Evidence custodian: @sam. Next update: +30m.

Escalation Ladder (summary)

1. Oncall SRE (automated pager)
2. Service Steward and Technical Lead
3. Senior SRE (on-call escalation)
4. Head of Platform (for customer SLA/regulatory impact)

SLO & alert thresholds (examples)

- Generation latency p95 > 2s for 2 minutes: P1 alert to oncall (Pager).
- Error rate > 5% for 5 minutes: P1 alert.
- KV cache eviction rate spike > 10x baseline for 60s: P2 alert.

Runbook snippets (examples to copy into service runbooks)

- Rotate service to fallback pool:
  curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/services/{service}/route -d '{"pool":"fallback-1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"

- Snapshot recent logs (last 30 minutes):
  journalctl -u redwood-service --since "30 minutes ago" -o json > /tmp/redwood-logs-INC-1234.json

- Export trace spans for ID TRACE-####:
  apm-cli export --trace-id TRACE-#### --out s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1234/evidence/trace-TRACE-####.json

Appendix: Helpful links and templates

- Incident ticket template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-ticket-template
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/editor
- Evidence upload bucket instructions: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/evidence-handling

Change history

- 2024-09-18: Document created by Maya Chen.
- 2025-03-04: Added Evidence Cookbook minimum artifact set and updated customer message cadence (reviewers: Liam Patel, Rosa Nguyen).

Contact for questions: oncall@redwood.ai or @maya.chen on Slack.

payload.page_title: Triage-to-Rehabilitation Incident Lifecycle Playbook

sections.body: This playbook documents the end-to-end incident lifecycle used at Redwood Inference: triage -> containment -> stabilization -> rehabilitation -> postmortem. It prioritizes rapid customer impact reduction, clear ownership handoffs, and measurable verification of follow-up actions. Use this as the canonical runbook for production-facing serving incidents (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to production services supporting inference requests, embedding pipelines, and the control plane.
- Intended audience: first responders, SREs, product incident leads, Customer Success reps acting as customer liaisons.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Severity levels: S1 (major outage, multi-region customer impact), S2 (single-region high-impact), S3 (degraded but non-critical).
- Triage: initial acknowledgement and impact assessment (first 0-10 minutes).
- Containment: actions to stop escalation of impact (10-45 minutes).
- Stabilization: hold state where customer-visible impact is removed and safe rollouts are prepared (45 minutes - 6 hours).
- Rehabilitation: engineering fixes, rollbacks, capacity restores, tests, and canary rollouts (6 hours - 14 days).
- Verification: completed validation of post-incident actions (up to 30 days depending on action).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) Triage (0-10 minutes)
   - Goals: acknowledge pager, determine severity, create incident channel, assign Incident Commander (IC).
   - Targets: pager ack <= 3 minutes; incident declared/dismissed <= 10 minutes.
   - Outputs: incident channel, initial impact statement, link to core dashboards.
2) Containment (10-45 minutes)
   - Goals: stop customer-facing degradation.
   - Typical actions: enable circuit-breakers, route to fallback models, disable noisy tenants, short-term scaling or region failover.
   - Targets: reduce error rate by >= 80% or bring latency within SLO within 45 minutes.
3) Stabilization (45 minutes - 6 hours)
   - Goals: stabilize metrics, lock mitigations, avoid repeated flips.
   - Outputs: pinned temporary config, adjusted alerts to avoid noisy pages, scheduled rehab plan.
4) Rehabilitation (6 hours - 14 days)
   - Goals: implement engineering fix, full capacity restore, regression test, and safe rollout.
   - Outputs: PRs, canary runs, monitoring dashboards with new detectors.
5) Postmortem & Prevention (publish within 7 days for S1/S2)
   - Goals: blameless root-cause analysis, SMART action items with owners and verification dates.
sections.heading: Incident lifecycle (phase goals and timeboxes)

sections.body:
- First Responder: acknowledges page, performs quick triage checks, posts initial notes in channel.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, decides containment strategy, owns executive comms drafts.
- SMEs: runtime, model-serving, infra, networking, observability.
- Customer Liaison: Customer Success/Account lead who owns external messaging and customer follow-up.
- SRE Lead: monitors elapsed time against escalation thresholds and triggers exec notifications if needed.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Health checks and high-level signals:
  1) Platform health: curl -s https://status.redwood-inference.internal/api/health | jq .
  2) Alert stream: check pager history and alerting dashboard
  3) Per-region error rates: /dashboards/serving/errors?window=5m
- Quick interrogations (commands):
  - kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide --selector=service=api | grep CrashLoopBackOff
  - redis-cli -h kv-cache INFO memory
  - rwictl deployments list --region us-west
sections.heading: Core runbook checks (first 10 minutes)

sections.body:
- Route traffic to fallback model (quantized/smaller):
  rwictl route set --model redwood-small-q8 --percent 100 --selector region=us-west
- Scale worker pool (temporary):
  terraform apply -var='worker_count=64' modules/serving/scale.tf
- Isolate tenant causing noisy behavior: update access control list or temporarily disable tenant key.
- Evict KV cache prefix if cache thrash is suspected: redis-cli -h kv-cache EVAL \"return redis.call('del', KEYS[1])\" 1 prefix:key
sections.heading: Common mitigations (examples)

sections.body:
Trigger | Immediate Action | Rationale
"Tail latency > 3x baseline for core endpoints" | Reduce max_seq_length to 512 for affected routes and enable prefix caching | Lowers average CPU/GPU work per request
"Pod OOMs on model decoder" | Cordon node, restart affected pods, failover to warm spare pool | Prevents repeating OOMs and isolates faulty node
"Error rate concentrated in single tenant" | Throttle or disable tenant traffic, open support ticket for tenant owner | Restores service for other customers quickly
sections.heading: Containment decision matrix (text table)

sections.body:
- If mitigation fails to reduce impact within 30 minutes -> escalate to Eng SRE lead and Product on-call.
- If we have sustained customer impact > 3 hours -> notify Exec on-call and Customer Success Director.
- For S1 incidents, prepare an initial executive brief within 60 minutes.
sections.heading: Escalation thresholds

sections.body:
- Default: primary-week / secondary-week pairing. Primary receives pages; secondary maintains situational awareness and performs escalations when requested.
- High-traffic windows (holidays, launches): use micro-shifts (12-hour shifts) with 30-minute overlap for handoff.
- Handoff checklist (must be posted in incident channel):
  1) Current impact summary (one-liner)
  2) Mitigations in place and who applied them
  3) Outstanding actions with owners and ETA
  4) Dashboards & links (latency, errors, pods, routing rules)
  5) Next scheduled check-in time and on-call contact handles
sections.heading: On-call rotation patterns and handoffs

sections.body:
- Cadence: quarterly SRE-led drills; annual cross-functional customer-impact simulation.
- Scenario templates: KV-cache thrash under synthetic load, model-quality regression after a release, autoscaler misconfiguration, multi-region routing failure.
- Exercise runbook:
  1) Announce scope and objectives 24 hours in advance to participating teams.
  2) Execute scenario with synthetic traffic and faults.
  3) Capture timeline and decisions in the incident channel (source of truth).
  4) Score outcomes: time-to-detect, time-to-recover, correctness of mitigations.
  5) Produce remediation actions and update runbooks within 2 weeks.
sections.heading: Game day exercises and validation

sections.body:
- Collect artifacts: logs, traces, deployment events, alert history, canary reports.
- Build timeline: minute-level for first hour; 5-15 minute buckets thereafter.
- Identify root cause(s), contributing factors, detection gaps, and mitigation gaps.
- Define action items (owner, due date, verification criteria).
- Publish on Confluence and schedule verification review meeting.
sections.heading: Postmortem (blameless) checklist

sections.body:
- Short (status header):
  "Investigating elevated error rates for text-generation API in us-west — engineers are working on mitigations."
- Medium (status body/update):
  "We are investigating elevated error rates and latency on the text-generation endpoint in the US-West region. Mitigation in progress: traffic is being routed to a fallback quantized model while engineering investigates the root cause. Next update: 30 minutes."
- Long (post-incident summary):
  "Root cause: memory growth in the model decoder after a kernel patch caused OOMs on serving nodes. Fix: reverted kernel patch, deployed memory-accounting telemetry, and completed a canary rollout. Impact: 2028-02-14 02:12 UTC to 2028-02-14 04:47 UTC. Customers affected were contacted directly. Follow-ups: automated memory sampling and post-deploy smoke tests scheduled."
sections.heading: Status page and customer communication templates

sections.body:
- Initial contact (short):
  "We are investigating an issue affecting text-generation latency in your region. Mitigation applied to reduce impact. We will update you within 30 minutes. — Redwood Incident Team"
- Follow-up with remediation summary:
  "Action taken: routed traffic to a quantized fallback model reducing error rate by 92%; reverted a kernel change that correlated with increased memory usage. Long-term fix ETA: 10 business days. We will proactively coordinate billing adjustments if applicable."

Governance, runbook hygiene, and metrics:
- Ownership: every runbook must list an owner and a quarterly review date at the top of the page.
- Runbook retirement: if a runbook is not exercised in 12 months, it must be reviewed for relevance or archived.
- Action verification: owners must report action status in the Reliability Dashboard until marked verified.
- Key metrics to track post-incident: time-to-detect (TTD), time-to-contain (TTC), time-to-recover (TTR), number of mitigations applied, and number of customer-impacting requests.

Appendix: copy/paste channel snippets
- INCIDENT header (copy into channel):
  "INCIDENT: [One-line summary] | IC: @username | Severity: S1/S2 | Impact: [customers/percent] | Mitigation: [short description]"
- HANDOFF snippet (at time of handoff):
  "HANDOFF: Summary: [one-liner]; Mitigations: [list]; Outstanding: [actions with owners]; Next check: [time]; Owner: @username"
sections.heading: Customer liaison templates (for Account Managers)

sections.body:
- Recommended labels: incident-lifecycle, runbook, oncall, game-day, status-page
- Suggested reviewers: Daniel Kim, Priya Shah, Alex Nguyen

End of playbook. For questions or to propose edits, ping @maya.patel or open an edit request on the page.
sections.heading: Document metadata guidance (for page header)

payload.page_title: Shift orchestration and status canvas

sections.body:
Overview

This page documents the Shift Orchestration pattern and the Status Canvas: a lightweight, modular approach to on-call handoffs, live incident status updates, and customer-facing messages. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incident windows, accelerate safe stabilization, and produce consistent artifacts for post-incident review.

Scope and audience
- Audience: first/second-line responders, incident commanders, bridge operators, on-call engineers, SRE leads, customer success when escalation is active.
- Scope: active incident lifecycle (ack -> contain -> stabilize -> restore -> retrospective) and the handoff/state model used inside and across shifts.

Key principles
1. Minimal, shared state: handoffs must surface only the essential facts (impact, hypothesis, next action, blockers).
2. Modular status text: compose updates from reusable sentence fragments (the Status Canvas) to avoid inconsistent messaging under pressure.
3. Timeboxed cadence: fixed checkpoints (10m, 30m, 60m, then hourly) for internal and external updates.
4. Champion ownership: a named Incident Commander (IC) owns the public narrative; the bridge operator owns the timeline/triage log.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): owns decision-making, public status updates, escalation decisions.
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge, posts comms to Slack/status page, maintains triage log.
- Primary Responder: works contained area (service, model, infra).
- Secondary/Support: deeper debug, infra changes, runbook actions.
- Customer Liaison (CS/Success): owns customer-specific comms where required and ensures SLA/regulatory notes.

Shift handoff checklist (state canvas)
For every rotation, leave a single-line subject and a structured canvas in the handoff channel or incident tracker. Required fields:
1) Active incident? (yes/no)
2) Incident ID(s) / Bridge link (URL)
3) Impact summary (1 sentence)
4) Current hypothesis and known mitigations
5) Actions in-flight and authors (command + ETA)
6) Blockers / resource needs
7) Followup / post-incident actions due to next shift

Example handoff (paste into #oncall-handoffs):
- Active incident: yes
- Bridge: https://meet.example/bridge/INC-2026-137
- Impact: API 503s for embedding endpoints in us-west; estimated 65% of customer requests failing.
- Hypothesis: model cache eviction + rate limiter misconfiguration causing backend queue overflows.
- Actions: rolling cache-size increase (alice) — ETA 12m; temporary QPS cap (bob) — completed.
- Blockers: capacity for canary pool exhausted; infra request filed (#1234).
- Next shift notes: continue cache monitor for 30m post-rollout; begin RCA prep.

Incident lifecycle: step-by-step
1. Acknowledge (T+0–10m)
  - Pager duty: responder acknowledges within 5 minutes.
  - Bridge is stood up and pinned in #incident-bridge.
  - IC and Bridge Operator are declared in the first 10 minutes.
  - First internal status posted to internal channel.
2. Triage & containment (T+10–30m)
  - Run the relevant containment runbook. See quick links below.
  - If customer-impacting, prepare a short external status (see Status Canvas fragments).
3. Stabilize (T+30–90m)
  - Apply mitigations and monitor key SLOs (latency, error-rate, successful tokens).
  - If mitigation fails, escalate to platform/infra and consider fallback model variant.
4. Restore & validate (T+90–240m)
  - Run smoke tests and validate end-to-end flows.
  - Update customers and close bridge when validated.
5. Retrospective (post-incident)
  - Collect timeline, artifacts, logs, config diffs, and runbook versions.
  - IC ensures postmortem draft within 72 hours; final review within 14 days.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
| Metric | Alert threshold | Initial action | Owner |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| API error rate (5m) | > 5% | Pager to pager-team | svc-owner |
| Tail latency (p95) | > 1.5s | Notify oncall | oncall-responder |
| Embedding 503 rate | > 3% | Bridge & start triage | IC |

Communications: the Status Canvas
The Status Canvas is a set of modular sentence fragments that are combined to form consistent updates. Use the minimal appropriate fragments for brevity.

Fragments — Impact level (choose one):
- minor: "A subset of requests are experiencing increased latency; no customer-facing errors observed."
- elevated: "Some customers may see errors or degraded responses; a remediation is in progress."
- critical: "A significant portion of traffic is failing; we have opened an incident and are actively working to restore service."

Fragments — Action (choose one):
- investigating: "Our team is investigating the root cause and collecting logs and traces."
- mitigating: "We are applying mitigations (temporary routing and capacity adjustments) to limit impact."
- rolling-back: "We are rolling back the most recent configuration change to restore baseline behavior."
- fallback: "We are routing affected requests to a compatible model variant while we resolve the primary issue."

Fragments — ETA / next update (choose one):
- eta-10m: "Expect an update in ~10 minutes."
- eta-30m: "Expect an update in ~30 minutes as we validate mitigations."
- eta-hourly: "We will provide hourly updates until resolution."

External status templates (examples)
- Initial external (elevated/critical):
  "[Time UTC] Status: {impact-fragment} {action-fragment} {eta-fragment} We will provide updates via this status page and direct customer messages as appropriate. (Incident ID: INC-2026-137)"

- Follow-up / Resolution:
  "[Time UTC] Update: service behavior has returned to baseline following {short-action-summary}. We are monitoring for recurrence and will publish a post-incident summary within 14 days. (Incident ID: INC-2026-137)"

Channel and cadence guidance
- Internal bridge channel: #incident-bridge-{id} (private) — use for operational chatter, temporary config commands, and triage logs.
- Public status page: update at T+30m for customer-visible incidents and then hourly.
- Customer notices: CS owns targeted emails or account-level notices; IC approves the message.
- Slack posting template (bridge operator):
  "INC-2026-137 — {short-impact} — {link to status} — IC: @user — Next update: {time}"

Automation snippets (examples)
- curl JSON payload to update our status service:
  curl -X POST https://status.redwood.example/api/v1/incidents \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${STATUS_TOKEN}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"incident_id":"INC-2026-137","impact":"elevated","message":"We are mitigating increased errors for embeddings; expect update in 30m."}'

- PagerDuty escalation API example (short):
  curl -X POST https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents \
    -H 'Authorization: Token token=${PD_TOKEN}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"incident":{"type":"incident","title":"Embedding 503 spike","service":{"id":"PABC123"}}}'

Runbook references (quick links)
1. Embeddings 503 containment runbook — /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/embeddings-503-containment
2. KV cache eviction playbook — /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
3. Rate-limiter rollback SOP — /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/rate-limiter-rollback

Game day & run drills (recommended cadence)
- Quarterly: full multi-shift incident sim (4-hour exercise) with enforced handoffs and public status updates.
- Monthly: 90-minute targeted drills (e.g., cache eviction, model fallback).
- Post-drill: update runbooks and publish a one-page drill summary.

Artifacts required for post-incident review
- Complete triage timeline (timestamps, actor, actions)
- Runbook versions executed and diffs (commit IDs)
- Logs, traces, and sample request ids (anonymized if necessary)
- Status page messages and CS communications
- Short list of remediation and owners (owner + due date)

Handoff best practices (practical tips)
- Use the canvas template; avoid freeform — structured state reduces rework.
- Attach one validation screenshot or short metric chart showing pre/post mitigation effect.
- Mark any ongoing customer communications and pin the message to the channel.
- If escalation is pending (e.g., infra approval), include the request link and SLA for approval.

Appendix: short checklists
- Ten-minute checklist:
  1) Confirm bridge URL and participants.
  2) Define IC and Bridge Operator.
  3) Post brief internal status and triage hypothesis.
  4) Identify immediate mitigations.
- Handoff checklist (5 items):
  1) Bridge link and incident ID.
  2) Short impact sentence.
  3) Primary action in-flight and ETA.
  4) Blockers and required approvals.
  5) Next shift explicit owner.

Related pages and references
- Incident comm and postmortem framework — /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- First responder playbook — /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/first-responder-playbook-and-runbook-pruning-guidelines-2024

Ownership and review cadence
- Document owner: engineering / ops-runbook squad.
- Review cycle: quarterly or after any major incident exercise.

Contact and feedback
- For feedback or improvement proposals, open a PR against the runbook repo or ping #oncall-runbook-maintainers.

payload.page_title: Service Stewardship: Rotations, Crisis Comms, and Postmortem Workflow

sections.body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood's operational guidance for service stewardship: how teams schedule and run on-call rotations, conduct fast triage, execute customer and status communications during incidents, and run the postmortem process with a bias for learning and closure. It is intended for primary responders, rotation leads, product owners, and the incident communications cadre.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-ack and time-to-stable for customer-impacting incidents.
- Provide clear ownership for every phase of an incident (detect, contain, restore, notify, learn).
- Standardize customer-facing communications to protect trust while avoiding premature technical statements.
- Ensure postmortems turn into concrete, tracked action items and that runbooks remain current.

Who this applies to
- Engineering responders (SRE, serving runtime, infra, platform)
- Customer Success for customer comms & severity alignment
- Product and Security for impacted product decisions and regulatory evidence

High-level incident lifecycle (one-line)
1) Signal received -> 2) Triage & classify severity -> 3) Contain & mitigate -> 4) Restore service -> 5) Customer & internal comms -> 6) Postmortem & follow-up

Severity definitions (team-canonical)
- Sev 1 (Critical): System-wide or multi-region outage with >50% of customers affected, immediate executive notification. Target: page within 3 minutes, first bridge in 10 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): Major functionality degraded for a subset of customers or significant error-rate increase. Target: page within 10 minutes, bridge within 30 minutes.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized degradation with feature impact; handled by on-call with async updates.
- Sev 4 (Low): Non-customer-impacting alerts, maintenance tasks, or noise.

Ownership matrix (quick reference)
| Responsibility | Primary | Secondary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pager handling & triage | Rotation responder | Rotation lead | Acknowledge within target
| Bridge operator (status updates) | Rotation lead | Customer Success rep | Start bridge for Sev1/2
| Customer status drafts | Customer Success | Rotation lead | Use templates below
| Postmortem lead | Rotation lead | Product owner | Postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/2

On-call rotation design
- Rotation length: standard is 1 week for SRE/serving-runtime primary rotation. Exceptions must be documented: long rotations (2+ weeks) require manager approval and backup schedule.
- Handoff window: 15-minute overlap at handoff for privileged roles (e.g., bridge operator, steward).
- Secondary (follow-the-sun): For multi-region coverage, primary rotates in region; secondary is on-call in next region to ensure 24h coverage.
- Time-off & fairness: Each engineer should have at least 4 weeks between hard-week rotations; rotation lead monitors load and can request swaps.

Creating a rotation entry (procedure)
1) Add entry in the oncall-schedule calendar (Team Schedules -> Redwood Oncall) with name, start/end, backup name, and contact methods.
2) Add runbook link to the calendar entry under "runbook_url" field.
3) Notify primary, secondary, and Customer Success via Slack #rotations and email 72 hours before start.
4) Rotation lead runs quick sanity check of runbook (smoke commands) within 48 hours prior.

Runbook hygiene & required sections
Every runbook must include the following sections and be validated annually:
- Overview and owner (team and person)
- Signal sources and alert thresholds
- Quick triage checklist (top 6 checks with commands)
- Containment steps (rate limiting, circuit-breakers, fallbacks)
- Restore steps (hotfix, rollback, scaling actions)
- Mitigation workarounds for customers
- Runbook test instructions (how to validate)
- Recent changes (changelog)
- Last test date and next review date

Quick triage checklist (copyable)
1) Confirm alert: identify metric/trace/trace-id and time window.
2) Check upstream dependencies (redis, kv-store, model-serving pool) via dashboards.
3) Determine blast radius: services, regions, tenant scope.
4) If blast radius > threshold, raise severity and call bridge.
5) Apply short-term containment (rate limit, disable feature flag).
6) Start thread for follow-up actions and evidence collection.

Bridge & comms play (immediate actions)
- Who to start bridge: rotation lead. If unavailable, primary responder starts.
- Bridge template: title, severity, time-of-detect, immediate impact, owner, link to runbook, next update ETA.
- Update cadence: every 15 minutes for Sev1; every 30 minutes for Sev2 until stable.

Status page templates
Public status page (short form)
- Title: [Region] Degraded API latency impacting customers
- Time detected: 2026-08-27T14:21 UTC
- Impact: Increased request latency for text-generation endpoints in us-west1. Some requests are timing out; retries may succeed.
- Current status: Engineers are investigating; mitigation in progress.
- Next update: 2026-08-27T14:40 UTC

Private customer notice (for affected customers)
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference latency (us-west1)
Body: Dear <Customer Name>,
We’re investigating elevated latency for the text-generation endpoints in us-west1 that may cause timeouts for some requests. Our SREs have applied temporary throttling and are rolling a mitigation across the cluster. We will provide our next update by <time>. If you see sustained errors, please reply to this thread or reach out to your CSM. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Escalation and executive notification
- Auto-escalation: Mute escalations for noise but ensure Sev1 triggers SMS to on-call, rotation lead, and the Pager Duty exec list.
- Exec brief: For Sev1 incidents lasting >30 minutes, rotation lead prepares a 4-line executive summary: (1) impact, (2) root cause hypothesis, (3) mitigation in place, (4) next steps and ETA.

Postmortem workflow (required for Sev1/2; recommended for Sevs 3 when customer impact is >1 tenant)
1) Triage owner publishes initial incident timeline in the incident doc within 24 hours.
2) Postmortem lead schedules the postmortem meeting within 72 hours (invited teams: engineering, product, customer success, security if applicable).
3) Draft postmortem sections: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root cause analysis (5 whys / fishbone), Contributing factors, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Preventative controls.
4) Action items are added to the central tracker (Jira project INF-OPS) with required SLA: one high/critical action within 2 weeks, others triaged into roadmap.
5) Postmortem must be published to the internal incident archive no later than 7 days after the incident and linked from the runbook.

Postmortem quality rubric (used by reviewer)
- Complete timeline with evidence (logs, traces, metrics): Pass/Fail
- Clear root cause analysis (not just symptom): Pass/Fail
- Concrete, assigned corrective actions with dates: Pass/Fail
- Learnings that change runbooks/process: Pass/Fail
- Stakeholder communication included: Pass/Fail

Game day (exercise) playbook
- Frequency: each service should run a game day annually, SRE-organized. Critical services should run semi-annually.
- Scope: exercises should include KV cache thrashing, autoscaling failure, network partition, and model-serving cold-cache scenarios.
- Pre-game checklist: runbook smoke tested, backups verified, participants and observers assigned, customer comms templates validated.
- Instructor-led script: one-page scenario with expected failure points and scoring rubric.
- Post-exercise retro: 3 actions max with owners and deadlines; update runbooks within 14 days.

Forensics & evidence collection
- What to collect: full request traces (sampled ID list), service logs, autoscaler events, kernel metrics, and model-serving GPU telemetry.
- Retention: preserve a compressed evidence bundle for 90 days in the incident bucket with labels: incident-id, severity, service.

Runbook testing cadence
- Weekly smoke checks for critical-runbooks (automated where possible).
- Quarterly manual validation by rotation lead.
- Annual full-runbook audit by engineering reliability QA.

Customer credits & remediation policy (summary)
- Credits: apply per the customer SLA policy when service-level availability falls below contracted SLA per month. Technical team recommends remediation steps; Customer Success owns credit comms.
- Temporary workaround: rotation lead documents mitigation and timeline; CSM drafts customer message. Legal is looped for enterprise customers before final message if credits are proposed.

Template snippets (copy/paste)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: "[BRIDGE] Sev{level} - {service} - {short-impact} - Bridge: {link} - Owner: @{owner} - Next update: +15m"
sections.heading: Bridge start message (Slack)

sections.body: "Update: Engineers have identified a partial region-level degradation affecting {service}. We have applied temporary throttling and are monitoring. No customer data exposure is suspected. Next update in 15 minutes."
sections.heading: Public status update

sections.body:
- INF-1234: Increase autoscaler cooldown from 30s -> 90s to reduce oscillation. Owner: @alex. ETA: 2026-09-15.

Maintenance: How to retire/update this doc
- Owner (eng rotation lead) must review annually or after every Sev1/2 incident.
- Any runbook changes discovered in postmortem are applied within 14 days and validated by the next rotation.

Appendix: Useful commands and dashboards
- Dashboards: Runtime-Latency, ModelPool-Utilization, Edge-Errors, Redis-Client-Errors
- Useful CLI checks:
  - curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/v1/ping
  - rtx tail --service serving-runtime --since 5m | jq '.level=="error"'
  - k get hpa -n serving-runtime

Contacts
- Incident mailbox: incidents@redwood.ai
- Pager duty escalation list: pd-sev1@redwood.ai
- Rotation QA: rotations@redwood.ai

Related pages and artifacts
- Maintain runbook links in the team runbook index and ensure the runbook id is on your calendar entry.

Document history
- 2025-03-12: Created by Priya Nandakumar.
- 2025-11-02: Added postmortem quality rubric (reviewers: Ethan Cole).
- 2026-09-01: Expanded game-day scenarios and evidence retention window (updated by Mariana Ruiz).

payload.page_title: Tribe Liaison & Status-Wire Protocol: Incident Playbook

sections.body:
Overview:
This playbook defines the Tribe Liaison role and the Status-Wire communication protocol used for coordinated incident response across teams (platform, runtime, SRE, customer success, and engineering tribes). It is intended for incidents with cross-team impact (multi-service degradation, multi-region latency spikes, or model-quality regressions affecting production).

Purpose:
- Reduce cross-team friction and duplicated messaging during incidents.
- Provide a repeatable activation workflow for public and customer-facing communications.
- Offer templates and checklists for rapid, consistent status updates and post-incident evidence collection.

When to activate the Status-Wire:
1) Any P0 or P1 incident declared by SRE / Incident Commander.
2) Sustained SLO deviation > 5 minutes affecting > 1 customer or > 10% of traffic.
3) Model-quality regression that causes repeated error responses or hallucination rates above threshold.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): overall incident authority; owns triage decisions and escalation to execs.
- Tribe Liaison (TL): single named engineer from each affected tribe. TLs consolidate technical findings and represent their team on the Status Wire. Responsible for:
  - Rapidly validating impact and proposed mitigations for their domain.
  - Contributing one-line status and next steps for each wire update.
  - Collecting evidence artifacts (logs, traces, perf snapshots).
- Bridge Operator: manages the incident bridge, recording timeline and action items.
- Communications Lead (Comms): drafts customer-facing updates, coordinates legal/compliance review if required.
- Customer Success Rep: prepares prioritized customer impact list and coordinates direct outreach where needed.

Activation checklist (first 10 minutes):
1. IC declares incident and sets severity.
2. Pager alert: On-call SRE acknowledges and opens bridge.
3. IC assigns an engineered TL per affected tribe (platform, runtime, model-infra, console).
4. Bridge Operator posts Status-Wire channel link (Slack #status-wire-<incident-id>) and pins initial incident summary.
5. TLs post immediate 1-line: "{team}: impact (yes/no), likely root area, immediate mitigation". Example: "Runtime: partial KV-cache eviction causing 40% increased tail latency; restarting cache nodes as mitigation"
6. Comms drafts and posts first customer notice (see templates).

Escalation matrix (quick reference):
| Role | Primary | Secondary | Escalation threshold | Contact method |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Incident Commander | SRE Lead on-call | Eng Director on-call | >30 minutes to containment | Pager / Phone |
| Tribe Liaison | Team on-call engineer | Team tech lead | No mitigation found in 20 minutes | Slack DM / Pager |
| Comms Lead | Support Ops | Head of CS | Customer SLA breach or regulatory impact | Slack / Email |

Runbook snippets (copy into service runbooks):
- inference-gateway:
  1) Check service health: curl -fsS https://health.redwood.internal/inference-gateway/metrics || true
  2) Query recent traces: otel-cli query --service inference-gateway --last 15m
  3) If error-rate > 2% and tail-latency > 800ms, toggle canary fallback: curl -XPOST https://admin.redwood.internal/route/fallback -d '{"route":"/generate","model":"gptx-small-fallback"}'
- kv-cache:
  1) Inspect eviction log: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id=\"kv-cache\"" --limit 200
  2) Rehydrate hot-keys from snapshot: /opt/tools/kv-rehydrate --snapshot s3://redwood-cache/snaps/latest --keys hot-keys.txt

Status-Wire messaging cadence:
- Initial (T+10m): Brief impact, services affected, immediate mitigations in progress, expected next update in 30 minutes.
- T+30m: Progress update including measurable signposts (error-rate, latency, traffic diverted) and next steps.
- Every 30—60m afterward: update until containment. Shorten cadence to 15 minutes if customer-impacting or high uncertainty.
- Containment achieved: merge into final incident summary and begin postmortem timeline.

Customer-facing templates (copy/paste-ready):
- Short status page entry (public):
  Title: "Degraded API latency for text generation — investigating"
  Body: "We are investigating increased latency affecting text-generation API requests in US-West. Impact: intermittent delays up to ~4s for a subset of requests. Current actions: rolling restart of KV cache nodes and routing a portion of traffic to fallback model variants. Next update: in 30 minutes. Affected customers will receive direct notices if they meet SLA thresholds."

- Email / CS message (for affected customers):
  Subject: "Service update: transient delays for Redwood text generation — {incident-id}"
  Body: "Hi {customer_name},

We are actively responding to an incident affecting text-generation latency in {region}. Some requests are experiencing elevated latency or transient errors. Our SRE and runtime teams have deployed mitigations (cache restarts and traffic routing) and are monitoring recovery. We will provide another update at {time} or sooner if status changes. We apologize for the disruption and will share a detailed post-incident report within 72 hours.

If you require escalation or mitigation assistance (e.g., pinning model variants or temporary throttling), reply to this message and your Customer Success lead will coordinate.

— Redwood Support"

Game day and simulation plan (quarterly):
- Objective: exercise cross-tribe coordination and Status-Wire to validate SLAs and communications.
- Frequency: quarterly for SRE + product-critical tribes; monthly light drills for new joiners.
- Duration: 90 minutes.
- Roles assigned in advance: IC, Bridge Operator, 3 TLs, Comms, CS.
- Scenario example: synthetic KV eviction at scale causing 30% tail latency increase and 5% error-rate.
- Success criteria: containment within 45 minutes, customer-facing update within 10 minutes, complete evidence capture (traces/logs/metrics) uploaded to incident ticket.

Post-incident evidence & postmortem template:
- Attachments required in postmortem: timeline (with T+ minute markers), logs (last 60 minutes per service), relevant traces (span IDs), Mitigation steps, Root cause analysis, Action items with owners and SLA for completion.
- Postmortem outline (use this header structure):
  *Summary*
  *Impact* (customers, SLOs)
  *Timeline* (bullet list with timestamps)
  *Root Cause*
  *Contributing factors*
  *Immediate remediation*
  *Long-term fixes*
  *Action items (owner + due date)*
  *Verification plan*

On-call rotation fairness & handoff checklist:
- Primary rotation length: 9 days (3-person rotation recommended for fairness).
- Shadowing: new on-call engineers shadow for 2 rotations.
- Handoff checklist (mandatory before shift end):
  1) Confirm no ongoing incidents assigned.
  2) Share any active mitigations, experiments, or rollouts in last 12 hours.
  3) Verify Escalation list and on-call contacts are up-to-date.
  4) If any open action items: add clear owner and ETA.

Bridge & tooling references:
- Incident bridge template: Zoom link pinned in channel; Google Doc timeline template: https://docs.internal.redwood/incident-timeline-template
- Dashboards:
  - SRE Living Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/ll1/sre-living-dashboard
  - Model Quality Monitor: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/mq/model-quality
  - Token-level cost/latency: Console -> Observability -> Token Insights
- Runbook registry: Confluence runbook index (add link to service runbook pages).

Quick checklist for the Tribe Liaison (TL):
1) Join bridge and post one-line status.
2) Verify logs and traces for your domain and attach evidence to bridge notes.
3) Propose emergency mitigation and estimate time-to-contain.
4) Commit to follow-up artifact (e.g., heap dump, timeline snippet).

Appendix: sample Slack status-wire message (copy-paste)
```
[Status-Wire] Incident: INF-2026-842
IC: @sre-oncall
Services: inference-gateway (P), kv-cache (P)
Runtime: Restarting 2/3 cache replicas; expected partial recovery in ~12m. Error-rate peaked at 4.1%; tail latency 95p=950ms. Next update in 30m.
TLs: @runtime-tl (runtime), @platform-tl (platform), @modelinfra-tl (model)
```

Operational notes & governance:
- All incident owners must file a postmortem for P0/P1 incidents within 72 hours of containment.
- Action items must be tracked in the central incident board and have clear owners and due dates.
- Quarterly reviews: the Incident Review Council will audit a sample of postmortems for completeness and follow-through.

Related pages and references:
- Incident evidence collection standard, SLO definitions, Runbook registry.

Contact & ownership:
- Primary owner: Leah Park (SRE, Incident Ops)
- Secondary owner: Marcus Chen (Runtime)

payload.page_title: Bridged Restoration Playbook for Traffic Spikes and Noisy Neighbors

sections.body:
Overview:
This playbook defines a pragmatic, low-latency response for incidents caused by sudden traffic spikes and 'noisy neighbor' behaviors that degrade Redwood inference performance for one or more tenants. It covers detection signals, a prioritized containment ladder, traffic-routing mitigations, customer/status templates, on-call responsibilities, game-day simulation steps, and post-incident follow-ups. The goal is to restore broad service health quickly while preserving data integrity and providing clear communications to customers and stakeholders.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to degradation events where latency SLOs or request errors increase across one or more model-serving clusters due to imbalanced tenant traffic or noisy workloads (e.g., long-sequence bulk requests, high concurrency bursts, or runaway retries).
- Not intended for software-only bugs (see separate code-regression runbooks) or hardware failures where evacuation/repair is required.

Key service targets and SLO thresholds (for on-call decisioning):
- P50 latency target: <= 180ms (informational)
- P95 latency SLO: < 850ms (SLO)
- Error rate SLO: < 0.5% 5m rolling
- Degradation alert thresholds (auto-alert rules):
  - Latency p95 > 900ms sustained for 3m -> P1 alert
  - Error rate 5m > 2% -> P1 alert
  - Queue length > 500 requests on a node pool -> P2 alert

Symptoms that indicate noisy-neighbor / traffic-spike incident:
1) Sudden ingress increase from a small set of API keys/accounts.
2) Elevated KV cache misses combined with long tail latencies.
3) One or two model-serving pods/instances consuming >70% GPU memory or >85% SM utilization while others are relatively idle.
4) Retrying clients or reconnect storms visible in request logs.

Detection & initial triage (first 10 minutes):
1. Acknowledge alert and open an incident channel (Slack #ops-bridge-<incident-id> and create incident in PagerDuty).
2. Triage officer captures initial signals:
   - Top 10 source API keys over last 5 minutes (monitoring query)
   - Top 5 node pools by CPU/GPU utilization
   - Per-region request rate and P95 latency deltas
3. Decide containment vs. full mitigation based on blast radius. If impact is localized to a customer or a single node pool, prefer containment.

Containment ladder (ordered by safety & speed):
1) Rate-limit / apply ingress throttles to offending API key(s).
   - Short-term target: reduce offending client concurrency by 80%.
   - Command example (internal traffic-shaper):
     adminctl throttle --api-key <KEY> --concurrency 10 --duration 15m --reason "auto: noisy neighbor containment"
2) Apply per-account token bucket limits at the edge (NGINX/LB) and enforce burst/steady rates.
3) Move noisy traffic to degraded-capacity lane (lower-priority pool) and apply model-fallback if necessary.
   - Use routing tag: noisy-neighbor => route to low-pri pool
4) Temporarily scale up dedicated GPU workers if autoscaling is slower than needed (fast path only when containment insufficient).
5) Evict long-running KV-cache-heavy requests or cancel queued requests from offending sources.
6) If the noisy tenant is high-value and containment would violate contractual terms, coordinate with CS/AM for soft-limits and manual throttling.

Operational checklist (actions and owners):
- Triage owner (SRE on-call): run initial monitoring queries and populate incident channel with top metrics.
- Runtime owner (Serving team): validate node health and identify overloaded pods for isolation.
- Network/Edge owner (Infra): implement edge rate-limits and block rules if necessary.
- CS/AM (Customer Success): identify impacted customers and prepare messaging if public-facing.

Speed commands and monitoring queries (copy/paste):
- Top API keys by RPS (PromQL):
  topk(10, sum by (api_key) (rate(requests_total[1m])))
- Node pool GPU utilization (Grafana query): filter by cluster:_cluster and avg_over_time(nvml_gpu_utilization[1m]) > 80
- Cancel in-flight requests (internal):
  adminctl cancel-requests --filter "api_key=<KEY> AND duration>120s" --dry-run
- Apply routing tag to re-route traffic:
  adminctl route set --api-key <KEY> --route-tag noisy-neighbor --duration 30m

Traffic routing and isolation table (operators):
| Condition | Action | CLI / Dashboard location | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single API key >50% cluster RPS | Apply per-key throttle (concurrency cap) | Edge dashboard -> Rate limits OR adminctl | Offending flow limited; cluster p95 improves |
| Many small keys showing aggregate increase | Create rate-limit policy by org | infra-console -> traffic-policies | Aggregate load reduced, fairness improved |
| Specific node pool saturated | Drain new requests, move routing | k8s: cordon/evict + adminctl route | Reduce hot-spot, allow eviction to catch up |

Escalation matrix (time-boxed):
- 0–10m: Triage owner determines containment step; notify on-call manager if P1.
- 10–20m: If no improvement after containment, page Runtime owner and Infra lead.
- 20–40m: If still degraded and customer-impact >10% of requests, escalate to Head of SRE and CS lead for customer comms.
- 40m+: Consider wider mitigations: cluster-level Autoscale burst, redirect traffic to alternate region, or soft failover to Redwood Dedicated.

Customer and status communications (templates):
- Status page short update (public):
  Title: Degraded inference performance in <region> due to high request volume
  Body: Our teams are investigating elevated request rates affecting inference latency for some customers in <region>. We have implemented temporary rate limits and routing changes to stabilize performance. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Impact: some requests may experience higher latency or receive transient failures.

- Customer-facing email/snippet (for impacted customers):
  Subject: Temporary throttling applied to stabilize inference performance
  Hi <CustomerName>,
  We detected unusually high request volumes originating from activity linked to your API key that contributed to broader latency increases in <region>. To protect platform stability we have temporarily applied a rate cap to your traffic for 15 minutes while we investigate. No data has been lost. If this disruption causes critical business impact, reply and we will prioritize a tuned mitigation.

- Internal incident update template (first 30 min):
  - Detection: timestamp + alert name
  - Scope: affected clusters / % of traffic affected
  - Actions taken: containment step and time
  - Next steps: further mitigations and owners
  - ETA for next update: +30m

Post-incident assessment checklist (immediately after P0 cleared):
1. Capture final metrics (p95, error rate, top API keys) for the incident window.
2. Identify root cause: spike pattern, client bug, abusive traffic, or valid workload change.
3. Determine whether new guardrails (per-key quotas, fair-share routing) are required.
4. If customer-caused, coordinate with CS for remediation plan and potential billing/credit.

Postmortem & remediation (owners & timeline):
- Incident author: SRE triage owner (write the postmortem within 72 hours).
- Required sections: timeline, detection, impact, root cause analysis, corrective actions, preventive actions, roll-forward plan, and verification steps.
- Priority remediation timeline:
  - Hotfixes (<=7 days): apply emergency throttles and improve alert thresholds.
  - Short-term fixes (<=30 days): add per-account rate limiting and traffic-shaping rules.
  - Long-term engineering work (<=90 days): routing fairness algorithm, autoscale policy refinement, and improved per-tenant telemetry.

Game-day simulation plan (quarterly practice):
- Objective: practice identifying and containing noisy-neighbor incidents without customer-impact.
- Roles to seat: Triage owner (SRE), Runtime owner (Serving), Infra (Edge), CS on-call, PagerDuty coordinator.
- Scenario outline:
  1) Synthetic traffic generator ramps a single API key to 60% cluster RPS over 2m.
  2) Monitoring triggers latency p95 alert and queue-length alert.
  3) Triage owner must identify offending key within 5 minutes and apply first containment step in 10 minutes.
  4) Serving team practices moving noisy traffic to degraded pool and validates that lower-priority pool degrades gracefully.
- Success criteria: mean time to containment < 15m and restoration of p95 < 850ms within 25m.

Validation and runbook retirement criteria:
- This runbook is validated if used during one real incident or two game-day exercises in a 12-month window.
- Retire when: the platform routing layer enforces per-tenant fairness automatically AND we have monitoring proving no single key can exceed 30% cluster RPS for 6 months.

Appendix A — sample PromQL and SQL checks:
- Top keys by 5m RPS (PromQL):
  topk(20, sum by (api_key) (rate(requests_total[5m])))
- Error rate (SQL for audit):
  SELECT api_key, count(*) as errors FROM request_logs WHERE status >= 500 AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 20;

Appendix B — quick reference commands (for SREs):
- adminctl throttle --api-key <KEY> --concurrency 10 --duration 15m --reason "noisy containment"
- adminctl route set --api-key <KEY> --route-tag noisy-neighbor --duration 30m
- adminctl cancel-requests --filter "api_key=<KEY> AND duration>120s" --confirm
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

Appendix C — ownership & contacts:
- On-call SRE: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
- Serving runtime lead: runtime-team@redwood.ai
- Network/infra lead: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
- CS escalation: cs-escalations@redwood.ai

Related reading and links:
- See internal routing policies: infra-console -> Traffic Policies
- See postmortem template: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

Document maintenance:
- Author: Aisha Patel (SRE)
- Review cadence: annual review and after any noisy-neighbor incident.

End of playbook.

payload.page_title: Incident evidence chain and forensic runbook

sections.body:
Summary
This runbook defines the incident evidence chain and forensic procedures for Redwood Inference. It describes what to preserve, how to collect evidence reliably, who owns each step, and how evidence is stored for post-incident analysis and regulatory review. The goal is to preserve actionable telemetry and system state without delaying customer-facing remediation or violating privacy controls.

When to use this document
- Use when an incident involves: data integrity questions, possible security compromise, unexplained model quality regressions, or any situation where later forensic analysis is required.
- If the incident is purely a transient metric blip with obvious root cause (e.g., planned capacity maintenance announced beforehand), follow the standard incident command playbook instead.

Principles
- Capture early: first 15 minutes matter.
- Minimize blast radius: collection should not exacerbate the incident.
- Chain of custody: every snapshot must be tagged with who collected it, why, and cryptographic checksums where feasible.
- Privacy-first: redact or avoid collecting customer PII unless absolutely required and approved by security/legal.

Roles and ownership
- Incident Commander (IC): overall owner of incident response and evidence decisions for the incident. Typical role: SRE on-call lead.
- Forensic Lead: security engineer or senior SRE responsible for evidence collection and preservation.
- Telemetry Engineer: owns access to observability tools (Datadog, Loki, Splunk) and runs bulk exports.
- Platform Engineer: runs live-system snapshots (heap/VM/gcore) where permissible.
- Legal & Security Liaison: approves sensitive evidence collection and external requests.

Immediate steps (0–15 minutes) — evidence-first checklist
1) Declare evidence mode: IC sets incident bridge topic and announces "EVIDENCE MODE" in the bridge, which signals minimal state mutation.
2) High-level metadata capture (IC or Forensic Lead):
   - Incident ID, start timestamp, primary affected service(s), customer-impact flag.
   - Save as incident-metadata.json. Example content: {
     "incident_id": "INC-20260120-1234",
     "start_ts": "2026-01-20T14:12:03Z"
   }
3) Telemetry snapshot (Telemetry Engineer):
   - Export 30m windows of relevant metrics and traces centered on detection time. Preferred formats: JSON for traces (Jaeger/Zipkin), CSV/JSON for metrics.
   - Command example (Datadog API):
     curl -s -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/query" "-d "{\'from\':<ts>,\'to\':<ts>}"" -H 'DD-API-KEY: <redacted>'
4) Logs (Telemetry Engineer):
   - Pull logs for implicated service instances for window (-30m, +30m). Use indexed queries and export to object store.
   - Example Loki query: {job="inference-runtime", level="ERROR"} |= "timeout" | json
   - Store exported logs at s3://redwood-forensics/<incident_id>/logs/
5) Live-system snapshot (Platform Engineer, with Forensic Lead approval):
   - When safe and necessary, capture: process list, open sockets (ss -tunap), GPU state (nvidia-smi -q), thread stacks (gdb/gcore), running containers (docker ps --no-trunc), and kernel dmesg.
   - Minimal command set:
     sudo ss -tunap > /tmp/<incident_id>-sockets.txt
     sudo nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/<incident_id>-gpu-state.xml
     sudo gcore -o /tmp/<incident_id>-pid <pid>  (only for root cause capture; avoid on high-latency prod tiers)
6) KV cache and model artifacts (Serving/Platform Engineer):
   - Snapshot model artifact versions, model config, and a checksum of model weights. Record quantization/serve pipeline used.
   - Example: sha256sum /opt/models/release-v12/model.bin > /tmp/<incident_id>-model-sha256.txt

Chain of custody and metadata tagging
- Every artifact stored in object store must be accompanied by a small metadata JSON that includes: collector, timestamp, purpose, commands-run, checksum, access-list.
- Naming convention: <incident_id>/<artifact_type>/<hostname>-<timestamp>-<short-hash>
- Example metadata file: /s3/redwood-forensics/INC-20260120-1234/logs/collector-metadata.json

Preservation and storage policy
- Short-term: all artifacts are immutable in s3://redwood-forensics/<incident_id>/ and preserved for 90 days.
- Long-term retention: items marked as legal evidence are moved to secure evidence vault with 7-year retention and HSM-backed checksums.
- Access control: default: read-by-role (Forensic Lead, IC, Legal, Security). Requests for other access must be logged and approved.

Evidence formats and minimum required fields
- Logs export (JSON lines): timestamp, host, service, level, trace_id, span_id, message, raw_payload (if allowed).
- Traces: full trace with spans; include span tags for model_id and request_size.
- Metrics: time-series with host and service dimensions labeled.
- Heap/core dumps: store compressed, provenance metadata, do not upload to public cloud without explicit approval.

Customer-facing communication templates (short, factual)
- Initial notice (when customer impact confirmed):
  Subject: Redwood Incident INC-{{incident_id}} – service impact
  Body: "We are investigating an issue affecting inference responses in region {{region}}. Our SRE team has activated evidence preservation and is working on restoration. No action is required from your side; we will follow up with timelines and mitigation steps within 60 minutes. If you need an incident contact, reply to this message."
- Investigation update (optional):
  "Update: We have captured necessary telemetry and isolated the affected fleet. A mitigation is in progress. We will provide a technical summary in the post-incident report."
- Post-incident summary: include non-sensitive findings, mitigation steps taken, and customer-facing remediation guidance. Avoid including raw logs or PII.

Post-incident process and postmortem requirements
1) Postmortem author: assigned by IC within 48 hours.
2) Required sections: summary, timeline, evidence artifacts list (with object store paths), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (with owners and due dates), verification plan.
3) Evidence appendix: list of preserved artifacts and their checksums (sha256).
4) Action items: track in the company issue tracker; every high/critical incident must have at least one preventative action with owner and ETA.

Forensic analysis playbook (when security compromise suspected)
- Immediately escalate to Security Liaison. Security will:
  - Freeze affected accounts and suspend automation that could mutate evidence.
  - Start a parallel secure evidence export into the secure evidence vault (encrypted with customer-specific KMS if necessary).
  - Collect network captures (only where lawful and approved): tcpdump on affected hosts with strict retention and access controls.
- Legal must be consulted before any external notifications that could disclose details of the investigation.

Automated capture scripts and examples
- We maintain a small toolbox in Git: infra/forensics-scripts. Key scripts:
  - capture-metrics-windows.sh: exports Datadog metrics to JSON and uploads to S3.
  - snapshot-service-state.py: collects ps, ss, docker/containerd metadata, nvidia-smi output, and zips artifacts.
Example capture-metrics-windows.sh (trimmed):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
INCID=$1
FROM_TS=$(date -u -d "-30 minutes" +%s)
TO_TS=$(date -u +%s)
curl -s -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/query" -H 'DD-API-KEY: $DD_API_KEY' -d "{\"from\":$FROM_TS,\"to\":$TO_TS}" > /tmp/${INCID}-metrics.json
aws s3 cp /tmp/${INCID}-metrics.json s3://redwood-forensics/${INCID}/metrics/${INCID}-metrics.json

Testing the runbook (game day plan)
- Quarterly game day: sim scenario where a model-serving node misbehaves and evidence must be preserved.
- Objectives: validate that telemetry exports complete in <15 minutes, that object store paths match metadata, and that access controls prevent unauthorized reads.
- Scoring rubric: completion of snapshots (30 pts), metadata completeness (30 pts), correct chain-of-custody (20 pts), successful postmortem with action items (20 pts).

Appendix A — quick commands and queries
- Export traces (Jaeger): curl -s "http://jaeger-query:16686/api/traces?service=inference-runtime&start=<start>&end=<end>" > /tmp/traces.json
- Loki bulk export example: loki_query='\"{job=\\\"inference-runtime\\\"} |= \\\"error\\\"\"'
  curl -G -s http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range --data-urlencode "query=$loki_query" --data-urlencode "start=$START" --data-urlencode "end=$END" > logs.json
- Compute sha256: sha256sum /opt/models/release-v12/model.bin > /tmp/model-sha256.txt

Appendix B — minimum SLOs for evidence procedures
- Telemetry snapshot completion: 95% of exports must complete within 15 minutes of request.
- Metadata attachment: 100% of artifacts uploaded to object store must have an accompanying metadata JSON.
- Chain-of-custody logging: every artifact access must be logged and retained for 180 days.

References and related docs
- See incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024 for parallel incident orchestration responsibilities.
- See eng-infra/retention-policies-2024 for data retention and deletion schedules.

Change log
- 2025-09-15: Created (initial draft).
- 2026-01-20: Updated to add GPU/state capture guidance and legal escalation flow.
