payload.page_title: Mobilization Roles Checklist and Template Archive

sections.body: This document consolidates our incident mobilization lifecycle, concise role checklists for responders, and a curated archive of status / customer communication templates. It is intended for oncall responders, bridge operators, SRE leads, and engineering managers who participate in incident activation or customer-facing communications.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all service-impacting incidents affecting hosted API, Dedicated, or Private control plane surface areas.
- Focuses on rapid mobilization (first 0–60 minutes) and stabilization 60–240 minutes.
- Not a replacement for individual runbooks — this is a lightweight orchestration layer and template set.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1) Automatic triggers:
   - SLO breach: 99th percentile latency > 2x target for 10m or error rate > 1% for 5m (see SLO matrix).
   - PagerDuty alert severity = P0 or P1 (automated).
2) Human triggers:
   - Product/CS escalates customer-impacting behavior.
   - Large-scale regression detected in monitoring or Canary pipeline.
sections.heading: When to mobilize (decision criteria)

sections.body:
1) Acknowledge & Stabilize (0–10m)
   - First responder acknowledges in PagerDuty, confirms incident title & severity.
   - Minimal immediate mitigations (traffic shaping, circuit-breaker flip, remove problematic hosts).
2) Mobilize Bridge & Core Roles (10–30m)
   - Stand up an incident bridge (Zoom/Google Meet/Slack huddle).
   - Assign on-bridge roles using the Role Matrix below.
   - Post initial status update to status.redwood.com (Status Page templates section).
3) Triage & Remediation (30–120m)
   - Execute runbooks, collect evidence, escalate to platform teams if needed.
4) Stabilize & Customer Communication (120–240m)
   - Confirm mitigation, route-fix or rollback as needed, prepare customer notices.
5) Recovery Verification & Close (240m+)
   - Validate SLOs returning to acceptable range for rolling 24h window, close incident, start postmortem.
sections.heading: High-level mobilization lifecycle (phases)

sections.body:
| Role | Primary responsibilities | Typical owner | Backup |
|------|------------------------:|---------------|--------|
| Incident Commander (IC) | Decision authority, escalation to execs, postmortem sponsor | SRE lead oncall | Eng manager oncall |
| Bridge Operator | Manage bridge, record timeline, coordinate communication | Oncall SRE | Support engineer |
| Primary Responder | Troubleshoot service, run mitigations, implement hotfix | Service owner oncall | Secondary service oncall |
| Triage Analyst | Collate logs/metrics, correlate alerts, run diagnostic queries | Observability engineer | DevOps engineer |
| Customer Liaison | Draft and publish customer-facing messages, handle CS requests | Customer Success rep | Account manager |
| Runbook Executor | Execute specific runbook steps (rollback, scale, config) | Service oncall | Platform operator |
sections.heading: Role matrix (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Incident Commander checklist:
  1. Confirm incident scope & severity.
  2. Assign bridge and roles.
  3. Decide on initial mitigation direction (throttle, degrade, rollback).
  4. Schedule 15m cadence updates.
- Bridge Operator checklist:
  1. Start bridge and record bridge link in incident ticket.
  2. Note participants and roles.
  3. Take running notes and generate timeline entries.
- Customer Liaison checklist:
  1. Use template (section: Status page & customer comm templates) to publish initial notice within 30m.
  2. Coordinate with IC for messaging cadence and escalation to named account managers.
sections.heading: Quick checklists (to print/use as Slack checklist)

sections.body:
1) Create incident ticket in Jira (project: RED-OPS-INC). Title format: [SEV{0|1}] <service> — <short summary>.
2) Create bridge (preferred: Slack huddle link or Meet link) and paste in ticket.
3) Tag PagerDuty escalation channel and ping assigned IC. Use: /pd trigger <incident-key> if needed.
4) Attach runbook link(s) for the affected service to the ticket.
5) IC assigns roles; Bridge Operator records timeline entries.
6) Runbook Executor performs steps exactly as written and records commands & outputs in the ticket.
sections.heading: Runbook activation procedure (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Check pod health (Kubernetes):
  kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=service=<service-name> -o wide
  kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod-name> --since=10m | tail -n 200
- Restart service instance (safe restart pattern):
  kubectl rollout restart deployment/<service-deployment> -n redwood-serving --request-timeout=30s
- Query KV cache hit ratio (PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_runtime_kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Trigger PagerDuty acknowledgement (CLI):
  pd incidents acknowledge <incident-id> --message \"Acknowledged by <your-name> — mobilizing team\"
sections.heading: Runbook snippets & safe commands (examples)

sections.body:
- Initial status (public status page) — template A (use within 30 min):
  Title: Degraded performance for Redwood API (region: us-west-2)
  Impact: Intermittent elevated latency causing timeouts for a subset of requests.
  Time: <ISO timestamp>
  What we know: We are investigating increased 99th percentile latency. Early signs point to autoscaling saturation on the model-serving pool.
  Next update: <time +30m>
  Contact: support@redwood.ai (for customers with dedicated support, see direct account contact).
- Customer-facing email (for affected enterprise accounts):
  Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API in us-west-2 — initial update
  Body: Hello <Customer-Name>,
  We are writing to let you know we are actively investigating an issue impacting requests to Redwood API in us-west-2. Our engineering team has mobilized and is executing mitigations. We will share an update in 30 minutes. If you have an active support case, we will update it directly.
  — Redwood Inference Ops Team
- Post-incident follow-up (summary template):
  Title: Post-incident summary — <incident-id>
  Summary: Short description, impact, duration, customers impacted (list), root cause summary, immediate mitigations, long-term fix plan, ETA for fix.

Game day: rapid mobilization lab (90–120 minute template)
Objective: Practice the first 60 minutes of mobilization, with focus on comms, role assignment, and runbook fidelity.
sections.heading: Status page & customer communication templates

sections.body:
- 0–10m: Inject alert (SRE exercise channel), PD pages go out.
  - 10–20m: Stand up bridge, assign roles.
  - 20–50m: Execute primary mitigations (scale, circuit-break, rollback).
  - 50–70m: Publish customer notice and status page entry.
  - 70–90m: Close simulated incident, run short postmortem.
sections.heading: Schedule

sections.body:
- First public status published within 30m.
  - Bridge had role assignments recorded.
  - No unauthorized config changes.
  - Evidence artifacts (logs, metrics snapshots) attached to the incident ticket.
sections.heading: Scoring criteria (pass/fail)

sections.body:
- Collect timeline from bridge and ticket.
- Export relevant dashboards (99/95/50 latency, error rate, KV cache, autoscaler events).
- Archive key logs (10m before — 30m after incident peak) to S3: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/logs/
- Save runbook execution transcript as part of ticket attachments.
- Assign postmortem author within 72 hours and target publish in 7 calendar days.
sections.heading: Postmortem & evidence collection checklist

sections.body:
- Exec notify (email + Slack #exec-ops) when: incident duration > 120m AND more than 3 enterprise customers impacted or revenue-sensitive route degraded.
- Legal and security notification: trigger when data exposure is suspected (follow security escalation SOP).
sections.heading: Escalation windows & executive notification thresholds

sections.body:
- Document owner: Incident Response team (primary: Elena Brooks).
- Maintainers: Oncall SRE rotation and Observability guild.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review aligned to postmortem synthesis and SLO retrospectives.

Appendix — template catalog (catalog entries and intended use):
| Template id | Purpose | Use window | Destination |
|-------------|---------|------------|-------------|
| tpl-initial-30 | Initial public status page | within 30m | status.redwood.com/public |
| tpl-enterprise-email | Email for named customers | initial + ongoing | direct email to account teams |
| tpl-postmortem | Post-incident report | after recovery | internal wiki + customers if requested |
| tpl-bridge-note | Bridge operational note | during incident | incident ticket timeline |
sections.heading: Ownership & maintenance

sections.body:
- Service runbook examples: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/<service-name>-runbook
- Incident evidence S3 policy: s3://policies/incident-evidence-policy.md
sections.heading: Related runbooks and links

sections.body:
- 2024-10-15 — Created by Elena Brooks (published).
- 2025-02-03 — Templates updated: added PromQL query and game day scoring rubric.
sections.heading: Change log

payload.page_title: Oncall readiness, SLO drills, and customer notification playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's oncall readiness program focused on: SLO-based drills, consistent runbook usage, and standardized customer communications. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) for high-severity incidents while preserving clear, timely customer-facing updates.

Scope

- Applies to production customer-facing services: API gateway, runtime serving layer, model catalog, embedding/embedding service, and the Console.
- Covers incident triage, escalation, internal comms, customer/status page updates, post-incident reviews, and game-day exercises.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks; instead complements them with a standard escalation and comms pattern.

Quick links (operational)

- PagerDuty: pd://redwood-production
- Status page: https://status.redwoodinference.internal (internal-only)
- Runbook repository: git@repo:redwood/runbooks.git
- Slack channels: #oncall, #incident-ops, #cust-comm

Severity taxonomy and thresholds

We use a four-level severity model tied to customer impact and SLOs. All incidents must be classified within the first 15 minutes.

1) Sev 0 (Critical) — system-wide outage or large customer impact
   - Symptoms: API error rate > 10% global for 5+ minutes OR region-wide unavailability OR sustained >50% SLO breach risk.
   - Pager: immediate page to primary oncall + escalation to engineering leadership. Target MTTR: 60 minutes.

2) Sev 1 (High) — significant degradation affecting many customers
   - Symptoms: latency p95 >2x baseline AND affecting >25% of requests OR model-serving errors cluster.
   - Pager: primary oncall. Target MTTR: 180 minutes.

3) Sev 2 (Medium) — localized degradation or single-customer impact
   - Pager: notify oncall via channel, optional page if not acknowledged. Target MTTR: 24 hours.

4) Sev 3 (Low) — informational, non-urgent issues or scheduled maintenance
   - Handled in backlog; update status page when relevant.

Roles and responsibilities

- Primary Oncall (Engineering): first responder, triage, and runbook execution.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, decides severity, and approves customer messages for Sev1/Sev0.
- Triage Engineer: collects logs, traces, and initial metrics; creates incident record.
- Comms Lead (Customer Success / IC): drafts status page and customer messages; coordinates with legal if data exposure suspected.
- Escalation Owner (Engineering Lead): implements code/fix or rollback and owns rollout plan.
- Postmortem Owner: ensures follow-up actions and tracks them to completion.

Oncall rotation and handoff (standard practice)

- Rotation length: 1 week for production oncall, 2 weeks for secondary/backfill.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack at shift start and end):
  1) Confirm Slack/Ding/PD notifications are working.
  2) Verify runbook repo is reachable and pull latest changes: git fetch origin/main && git pull.
  3) Snapshot open incidents and outstanding action items in #oncall-handoff thread.
  4) Confirm contact details for your rotation teammate (mobile and email).

- Warm handoff process: on last day of shift, the outgoing oncall posts a final summary of active alerts, mitigations in progress, and observed anomalies. The incoming oncall must acknowledge and ask clarifying questions within 15 minutes.

Paging and escalation timings

- Initial page: 0 minutes. If not acknowledged in 5 minutes -> escalate to secondary.
- If still not acknowledged in 15 minutes -> page engineering lead.
- For Sev0 incidents, immediately page on-call + engineering leadership and call the IC.

Runbook usage and template (how to run a runbook)

General guidance: Always work from the canonical runbook in the runbook repo. If a runbook is out of date, annotate and file a maintenance ticket.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Purpose: One-sentence description of the incident type covered.
- Detection: Metric/alert that should trigger this runbook (include alert name and thresholds).
- Impact assessment: list of systems/customers affected and quick commands to verify.
- Quick mitigation steps: minimal actions to restore service (prefer config toggles/traffic-shifts over code changes).
- Full remediation steps: longer-term fixes or rollbacks with safety checks.
- Post-incident checks: verification commands and dashboards to observe.
- Owner and runbook last-updated date.

Example: Latency spike runbook (abridged)

1) Detection:
   - Alert: api-latency-p95 > 1200ms for 3m
   - Verify: curl -sS https://api.redwoodinference.internal/health | jq .latency_p95

2) Quick mitigation:
   - Check autoscaling: kubectl get hpa -n serving; if replica count stable, scale deployment: kubectl scale deploy/serving-blue --replicas=8 -n serving
   - If related to batching: toggle batching profile to conservative: /ops/batching toggle --profile conservative --service serving

3) Full remediation:
   - Roll back the latest model-variant rollout: ./deploy/rollout rollback --service serving --to=stable
   - Recompile optimized kernels if CPU/GPU saturation observed: follow kernel compile playbook in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling

4) Post-incident checks:
   - Verify p95 latency back to baseline for 15m.
   - Monitor errors and token-per-second metrics for 60m.

Customer-facing communication templates

Use these templates as the basis for status page and direct customer comms. The Comms Lead must edit and approve before publishing. Keep messages clear, factual, and free of speculation.

Status page incident (short)

- Title: [Investigating] Intermittent API errors affecting generation endpoints
- Impact: A subset of API requests may return 500 errors or time out. Affects ~30% of requests across regions.
- Next update: in 30 minutes
- Update example: 2025-03-15T14:20Z — We have identified a service degradation impacting generation endpoints and initiated a rollback of the recent model rollout. Our engineering team is monitoring recovery.

Direct customer message (email/CS rep template)

Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API responses — update

Hello <CustomerName>,

We are investigating an incident that may cause intermittent 500 errors and timeouts when calling the Redwood API. Our oncall team has put mitigations in place and we are monitoring recovery. We will provide another update within 30 minutes.

Impact: you may see failed requests or delays for requests routed to the affected variant.

If you have a production-critical integration and need assistance: reply to this email or contact your Customer Success representative.

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

Commands and artifacts for comms lead

- Compose status page JSON (example snippet):
{
  "status": "investigating",
  "components": ["API"],
  "incident_updates": [{"body": "Investigating increased 500 errors on generation endpoints.", "created_at": "2025-03-15T14:20:00Z"}]
}

- Slack update: /topic status: Investigating API errors — rollback in progress.

Postmortem and action tracking (RCA checklist)

Postmortem must be filed within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev0 incidents and include:

- Summary: concise incident overview (what, when, impact).
- Timeline: ordered events with timestamps and actors.
- Root cause analysis: 5 whys + contributing factors.
- Mitigations implemented during incident.
- Long-term actions (owner and due date).
- Postmortem severity and lessons learned.

RCA checklist: verify instrumentation coverage, reproduce in staging where safe, confirm alert thresholds, and schedule follow-up engineering review.

Game day program (SLO drills)

Purpose: validate we can detect, escalate, and communicate incidents quickly and that runbooks are accurate.
sections.heading: Runbook template (use as header in each service runbook)

sections.body:
- Quarterly company-wide game day (table-top style) led by Eng SRE.
- Monthly team-level drills (2 hours) covering a single service and the comms template.
- Participants: oncall engineers, secondary, engineering lead, product owner, and customer success.

Example drill (90 minutes)
- 00:00 — Inject synthetic latency (or simulated alert) into serving metrics.
- 00:05 — Oncall is paged; triage starts.
- 00:15 — IC declared; comms lead drafts status page entry.
- 00:30 — Mitigation (traffic shift to warm pool) executed.
- 00:50 — Recovery verified; postmortem owner assigned.
- 01:30 — Retrospective and runbook edits.
sections.heading: Cadence and roles

sections.body:
- Acknowledge time < 3 minutes
- Severity classification accuracy > 90%
- Comms sent within 30 minutes of IC declaration
- Runbook fidelity score (did steps match observed behavior?) — pass/fail

Monitoring, dashboards, and SLOs
sections.heading: Game day evaluation criteria

sections.body:
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for production generation endpoints
- Latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for text-generation calls (90% of traffic)
- Embedding correctness: regression test suite pass rate >= 99% on model updates
sections.heading: Key SLOs (examples)

sections.body:
- Global overview: total requests, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec
- Model health: recent rollouts, variant split, and rollback status
- Resource saturation: GPU utilization, OOM events, queue length

Alert hygiene and tuning

- Every alert must map to an SLO or a clear operational signal (no alert should exist without an owner).
- Alert thresholds must include suppression windows and runbook links.
- Quarterly review of noisy alerts: if an alert fires more than 10 times per month, file a tuning ticket.

Post-incident follow-up and tracking

- Use the incident tracker board (Jira project: OPS-INCIDENTS) to create a parent ticket for each Sev1/Sev0 with linked remediation tasks.
- Track actions to completion and review in the monthly reliability meeting.
- For every change to a runbook, add a one-line changelog entry at the top and increment the version.

Appendices

A) Sample kubectl and tracing commands
- kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n serving logs deployment/serving-blue --tail 200 | grep ERROR
- ./tools/trace-query --trace-id <trace-id> --service serving

B) Status page examples and language matrix (short/medium/long)
- Short: Investigating — intermittent API errors affecting generation endpoints.
- Medium: Our oncall team has identified an increase in 500 responses for generation endpoints, likely related to a model rollout. We are rolling back and monitoring recovery. Next update in 30 minutes.
- Long: We have identified a service degradation following a model variant rollout that affects a subset of requests. Mitigation (rollback) is in progress. There is no evidence of data loss. We will provide a timeline and RCA after stabilization.

C) Quick checklist for IC when data exposure suspected
- Contact Security and Legal immediately.
- Freeze logs/archives for the affected window.
- Use template: "Potential data exposure — contact security immediately" in Slack and PD.

D) Runbook maintenance SLA
- Owners must review and sign off runbooks quarterly. Missing owner triggers escalation to service lead.

Contact list (oncall escalation)

- Oncall team alias: oncall@redwoodinference.internal
- Escalation lead: eng-lead@redwoodinference.internal
- Customer comms: cust-success@redwoodinference.internal

Revision history

- 2024-05-10: Created by Ava Martinez
- 2024-11-02: Added game-day cadence and SLOs (reviewers: Liam O'Connor)
- 2025-03-15: Updated comm templates and paging timings (reviewers: Priya Singh, Noah Patel)

Related reading

- eng-serving-runtime kernel-and-scheduling best practices
- oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024
- product-docs/release-notes/model-rollout-guidelines

If you have feedback or suggested edits, please open a pull request against the runbook repo or tag @AvaMartinez in #oncall.

payload.page_title: post-incident-action-triage-and-closure-playbook

sections.body:
Overview
-------
Purpose: Provide a single, prescriptive playbook for converting an incident into a closed, audited post-incident action package that meets operational, customer, and (when required) regulatory evidence requirements. This playbook covers triage decisions, evidence assembly, action assignment, validation, and formal closure so teams can consistently ship durable improvements after SLO regressions, model-quality incidents, capacity outages, and security-relevant events.

Scope
-----
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Trigger an SLO breach or customer-visible outage.
- Require a postmortem per the incident classification policy (sev2+ or customer-impacting sev3).
- Impose regulatory evidence needs (e.g., enterprise customers requesting timeline/evidence).

It does NOT replace the immediate incident-runbook steps used during active mitigation; rather it formalizes the post-incident work that follows stabilization.

Owners and Roles
----------------
- Incident Lead (IL): responsible for the post-incident timeline, facilitating RCA tasks, and certifying closure.
- Evidence Curator (EC): collects logs, traces, and exports artifacts in audit-ready formats.
- Remediation Owner (RO): implements code/config changes and tracks remediation tasks.
- QA Validator (QA): owns test plans validating fixes and regression non-repro.
- Customer Liaison (CL): drafts customer communications and coordinates sign-off when customers require tailored notices.
- SRE Review Board (SRB): periodic gate that reviews high-severity incident closures and verifies evidence completeness.

When to Open a Post-Incident Package
------------------------------------
1) Stabilization complete and IL marks the incident as resolved in the status system.
2) Incident classified as requiring postmortem per incident policy.
3) Any customer requests for detailed evidence or credits.

Immediate Post-Incident Triage Checklist (first 24 hours)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm stabilization artifacts: final incident timeline, mitigations applied, current service state.
2. Create Post-Incident Package (PIP) in the incident tracker with tags: incident-id, service, sla-impact, customer-impact.
3. Assign Evidence Curator and Remediation Owner.
4. Run the Evidence Collection Runbook (see section below) and capture artifact links in the PIP.
5. Schedule a 60-minute RCA kickoff with IL, EC, RO, QA within 48 hours.
6. If customer-impacting, CL prepares initial customer notification draft and shares with IL for approval.
7. Check for any regulatory notification obligations and escalate to Legal/Security if present.

Evidence Collection Runbook (EC tasks)
--------------------------------------
Goal: create a reproducible, auditable artifact bundle that includes timeline, logs, traces, configuration state, and human decisions.
Minimum artifact set (all items must be recorded as links in the PIP):
- Incident timeline (ISO8601 timestamps) with actor and command-level entries.
- Aggregated logs covering -15m to +60m around the first alert.
- Trace spans (sampled and full spans where possible) for affected requests.
- KV cache and prefix cache snapshots if the incident involves model serving cache anomalies.
- Deployment metadata: image/tag, git-commit, rollout policy, feature flags state.
- Autoscaling/queue metrics and capacity snapshots.
- Relevant config files (yaml/json) and the applied diff against last known-good.
- Dashboard snapshots (PNG) and metric queries (copyable).
- Customer-facing evidence: anonymized request examples (redacted PII per data policy).
- Slack/PagerDuty bridge transcripts and summary of manual interventions.
- Any security alerts or IDS/IPS logs if security-sensitive.
sections.heading: This document applies to incidents that

sections.body:
- Export logs as newline-delimited JSON compressed with gzip.
- Save traces as Jaeger/Zipkin JSON exports where supported.
- Add a manifest.json (top-level) listing each artifact with short description and SHA256. Example manifest entry: "{"path": "artifacts/aggregated-logs.gz", "desc": "app logs -15m:+60m", "sha256": "..."}" (store the manifest as plain text in the PIP).
- If customer requests: produce a redacted artifact bundle and obtain Legal approval prior to sharing.

RCA Workshop (recommended agenda, 90 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Objectives (5m): scope and expected deliverables.
2. Timeline review (10m): IL/EC walk through the minute-level timeline.
3. Evidence walkthrough (20m): EC shows traces/logs, highlighting root signals.
4. Hypothesis generation (15m): team lists candidate root causes and contributing factors.
5. Experimentation plan (10m): quick checks and reproduction tasks for RO/QA.
6. Remediation plan (20m): define actions, owners, priority, and estimated effort.
7. Closure criteria and follow-up cadence (10m): decide QA gates and SRB review schedule.

Action Item Template (to copy into PIP)
-------------------------------------
- id: ACTION-<incident-id>-<n>
- title: short descriptive title
- owner: <team/name>
- priority: P0 | P1 | P2
- due_date: YYYY-MM-DD
- description: one-paragraph summary of the change
- repo/PR: link to change or ticket
- test_plan: short bullets of validation steps
- rollback_plan: how to revert if regression occurs
- evidence_required: list of artifacts that prove the fix works

Example Action Item (text form)
- id: ACTION-INC-20240915-1
- title: Fix cache-eviction race in kv-cache service
- owner: serving-runtime-team/Jordan
- priority: P0
- due_date: 2024-10-02
- description: Correct ordering in eviction code path to prevent stale prefixes from triggering high-latency fallbacks.
- repo/PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/1234
- test_plan: unit tests for eviction ordering, integration job simulating high-concurrency prefix churn, synthetic load test verifying no SLO regressions for 72h.
- rollback_plan: revert PR and re-deploy previous image; pre-approved hotfix pipeline exists.
- evidence_required: augmented traces showing no repeated cache-miss storms and metric SLO delta < 0.1%.

Validation and QA Gates
----------------------
- QA must author a short test report capturing: test inputs, expected outputs, results, and timestamped evidence artifacts.
- For model-quality incidents include an eval harness run (link to eval job id), with before/after metric slices and prompt set examples.
- Define a hold window: do not perform large rollouts for 48 hours after deployment unless SRB approves.

Closure Criteria
---------------
sections.heading: Evidence packaging guidelines

sections.body:
1. All action items are either deployed and validated or have documented exception notes with SRB sign-off.
2. Evidence manifest is complete and artifacts are stored in the secure evidence bucket.
3. Postmortem document (narrative + timeline + RCA + action items) is published in Confluence and linked from the PIP.
4. Customer Liaison confirms any required customer messages have been sent and acknowledged when necessary.
5. If incident had regulatory implications, Legal or Security stamps the package as compliant.
6. IL marks the PIP as closed in the incident tracker and notifies SRB for periodic sampling review.

Postmortem Narrative Structure (recommended headings)
---------------------------------------------------
- Summary (1–2 paragraphs)
- Impact (customers/SLO/latency/cost) with concrete numbers and time ranges
- Timeline (minute-level) with key decision points
- Root cause analysis (clear statement of root cause + contributing factors)
- Actions (table/list of action items with owners and due dates)
- Validation plan and evidence links
- Lessons learned and prevention strategies
- Appendices: raw artifact links, scripts used for analysis, and customer communication copies

Sample Internal Customer Communication (short)
-------------------------------------------
Subject: Incident INC-20240915 — brief impact summary and remediation plan\nHello —
On 2024-09-15 we observed degraded generation latency for the Redwood API impacting ~3% of requests for 37 minutes. Our mitigation restored stable throughput. Root cause: race condition in kv-cache eviction that produced repeated cache-miss storms under a high prefix churn workload.
Planned remediation: code fix deployed to staging and a P0 action item targeted for 2024-10-02. We will send a detailed follow-up including evidence once the remediation is validated.
If you need a formal redacted artifact package for compliance review, contact the support lead at support@redwood.ai.

Sample Customer-Facing Template (for customers requesting evidence)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Hi <CustomerName>,
We appreciate your patience. We have created a redacted evidence bundle for INC-20240915 that includes: timeline, anonymized request examples, and deployment metadata. To comply with our data policy we have redacted fields identified in the bundle. Please confirm your preferred secure transfer method (S3 or signed portal link).

Operational Play Integrations
----------------------------
- Game Days: include a PIP readiness drill once per quarter where teams run through the entire pack creation process under a 90-minute timebox. The drill is graded on completeness of manifest, reproducibility of a short RCA, and timeliness of action assignment.
- Rotation Handoff: on-call rotations should include a 15-minute shadow specifically to review open PIPs. Any PIP older than 7 days without an owner escalates to the oncall manager.
- Status Page/Communication Workflow: if the incident required a public status page update, include the status update ID and changelog entry in the PIP. Use the cURL snippet below to fetch the public change:

cURL example to retrieve status entry (internal status API):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN" "https://status-api.internal.company/incidents/INC-20240915"
sections.heading: A PIP can be closed only when all of the following are met

sections.body:
service:"redwood-api" AND event.type:"request" AND response.status:[500 TO 599] AND @timestamp:[now-1h TO now]

For model-eval regressions, example eval command (internal harness):
./eval-harness/run_eval.sh --job-id eval-20240915 --subset problematic-prompts --output results/inc-20240915.json

Regulatory and Legal notes
-------------------------
- If incident may trigger contractual SLA credits, coordinate with Finance & Legal before issuing customer credits.
- For regulated customers (Finance/Healthcare), prepare both a redacted bundle and an audited bundle. Audited bundles must be stored with immutability flags and legal approval.

Archival and Retention
---------------------
- PIP artifacts are retained in the secure evidence bucket for 7 years for regulated incidents, and 1 year for routine incidents.
- Manifests and postmortem narratives remain in Confluence indefinitely but with access controls.

SRB Sampling and Continuous Improvement
--------------------------------------
- SRB samples closed PIPs monthly; sampled items are scored on evidence completeness, clarity of RCA, and whether actions reduced recurrence risk.
- Scores feed a quarterly remediation velocity metric reported to eng leadership.

Appendix: Quick checklist for Incident Lead before marking PIP closed
------------------------------------------------------------------
1. All action items have owners and statuses.
2. Evidence manifest present and links validate to existing objects.
3. QA test report(s) attached with pass/fail and artifacts.
4. Customer messages sent or CL documented reason for no-customer notification.
5. SRB or Legal approval attached if required.
6. PIP closure note published in Confluence and incident tracker.

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary contact for this playbook: Maya Patel (Lead, Incident Ops) — maya.patel@redwood.ai
- SRB inbox: srb@redwood.ai
- Evidence storage owner: infra-artifacts@redwood.ai

Change log
----------
- 2024-09-15: Initial draft and operationalisation following sev1 kv-cache incident.
- 2025-11-02: Added manifest/sha guidance and SRB sampling process.

payload.page_title: Responder knowledge curation and rotation compact guide

sections.body:
Purpose
This compact guide describes how responders should curate incident knowledge, execute rotations, run lightweight postmortems, and use standardized customer and status-page templates. It’s intended for primary on-call engineers, secondary responders, incident commanders, and the SRE rotations manager.

Quick summary
- Goal: reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for recurring patterns by 30% over 3 months through better knowledge capture and rotation hygiene.
- Scope: all production incidents that meet alert thresholds for latency, error-rate, or capacity (see SLO thresholds below).
- Owners: on-call (primary), SRE rotations manager (rotation schedule), incident-retrospective lead (postmortem quality).

When to use this doc
- Any multi-person incident (severity P1/P2) longer than 15 minutes.
- Regression patterns detected by automated SLO regression alerts, or repeating alerts from the same service within 7 days.

SLOs and thresholds (reference)
| Service | SLO (p99 latency) | Error-rate target | Alert threshold |
| Redwood-API-gen | 200ms | <0.5% | p99 > 300ms for 5m OR errors > 1% for 1m |
| Embedding-pipeline | 500ms | <1.0% | latency > 900ms for 10m OR 5% queued tokens |

Incident lifecycle (compact)
1) Detect & Notify
   - Pager triggers to #oncall with runbook link. Pager includes runbook id, sample alerts, and top-2 logs.
2) Triage (primary on-call) — first 10m
   - Identify blast radius (service, region, endpoints).
   - Determine owner: 'compute', 'runtime', 'network', or 'customer-config'.
   - Execute immediate mitigations: scale-up, rate-limit, routing fallback. Document each action in incident timeline.
3) Escalate (if >10m unresolved)
   - Contact secondary, then incident commander. Use matrix below.
4) Contain & Restore (15–90m)
   - Follow runbook checklist for the service category. If unknown pattern, run the regression triage checklist.
5) Synthesize knowledge (post-containment)
   - Create a one-paragraph incident summary and one actionable next-step list (5 items max).
6) Postmortem and rotation handoffs (within 72h)
   - Lightweight postmortem must be drafted within 72 hours; owner assigned to finalize within 7 days.

Escalation matrix (compact)
1. Primary on-call (first 10m): attempt containment.
2. Secondary on-call (10–20m): deeper debugging and mitigations.
3. Incident Commander (20–60m): coordinates cross-team actions, customer comms.
4. Platform lead / SRE manager (60m+): exec decision on rollbacks, customer exec notification.

Contact/roles list
- Primary on-call: resolves or escalates.
- Secondary: supports root cause debugging.
- Incident Commander (IC): single point for decisions and customer comms.
- Communications lead: crafts status page and customer messages.
- Postmortem owner: writes final RCA and follow-ups.

Immediate runbook checklist (pattern-based)
Use this checklist when the alert matches a known pattern. If not, shift to regression triage flow.
- Verify monitoring (Grafana /datadog) is accurate.
- Capture a p99/p95/p50 snapshot and recent deployment IDs.
- Check model-serving nodes: `rmi list --service redwood-runtime | grep unhealthy`
- If CPU/GPU saturation: trigger scale policy `infra autoscale --service runtime --up 2`
- If errors spike and correlate with new deploy: roll back to last stable tag `kubectl set image ...`

Regression triage checklist (unknown pattern)
1. Collect evidence: traces, example requests, logs. Use `logs query --svc <svc> --last 30m --filter error`.
2. Identify change vectors: deploys, config changes, infra events, third-party failures.
3. Reproduce locally with traffic replay (if safe) or synthetic requests.
4. If reproducible: implement temporary routing or throttling as containment.
5. Record hypothesis and test results in the timeline.

Postmortem template (lightweight)
- Title: [Service] outage YYYY-MM-DD
- Severity: P1/P2
- Summary (one para): what happened, customer impact, duration
- Timeline (bullet list): ordered actions with timestamps and owners
- Root cause hypothesis: short statement
- Evidence: logs, traces, graphs (links)
- Corrective actions (5 items max): owner + ETA
- Preventative work: larger initiatives for backlog
- Lessons learned (3 bullets): what to change in runbook/alerts/rotations

Postmortem quality bar
- Draft within 72 hours, owner assigned.
- Include at least one reproducible signal and a concrete test to prevent regression.
- Scorecard (0–5): completeness, evidence, actionability, timeline clarity, follow-up closure. Aim >=4.

Rotation hygiene (compact rules)
- Shift length: 1 week primary, 1 week secondary.
- Warm handoff: 30-minute overlap between shifts for the first day of the week.
- Shadowing: new on-call must shadow 2 incidents before independent shifts.
- Knowledge curation: every on-call shift must add/update at least one runbook note or create a ‘playbook snippet’ (max 300 words) describing the incident pattern and mitigation.
- Escalation practice: if the same service has 3 incidents in 14 days, that service goes on a 30-day ‘watch list’ and gets a game-day.

Game day playbook (30–60 minute exercise)
- Objective: validate runbook accuracy and handoffs for a single regression pattern.
- Participants: primary, secondary, IC, communications, product representative.
- Scenario (example): p99 latency spike in Redwood-API-gen after a config rollout.
- Steps:
  1) Inject synthetic alert and start timer.
  2) Primary executes runbook; log actions.
  3) Secondary attempts deeper debugging.
  4) IC practices communications and status update cadence.
  5) After-action (15m): capture gaps, assign remediation tasks.

Status page and customer communication templates
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Title: Partial degradation — Redwood-API-gen (region: us-west-2)
- Impact: Customers in us-west-2 may experience elevated request latency and failed streaming responses.
- Current status: Mitigation in progress — traffic routed to fallback model instances.
- ETA: initial mitigation applied; full restoration target 90 minutes.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or on notable progress.
sections.heading: Status page (short form)

sections.body:
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood-API-gen in us-west-2 — ongoing mitigation
Hi <CustomerName>,
We’re investigating an issue impacting Redwood-API-gen in us-west-2 that may cause higher latency and occasional failures. Our on-call team has applied a routing mitigation and is continuing work to fully restore service. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you rely on streaming responses for production traffic, please toggle fallback routing (instructions link).
Regards,
Redwood Inference Operations

Communication cadence (IC responsibilities)
- IC posts initial status within 15 minutes.
- Periodic updates every 30 minutes while unresolved.
- Post-incident summary within 72 hours; customer-facing RCA within 7 days for P1 incidents.

Knowledge curation steps (concrete)
1) Immediately after containment: fill the incident summary section in the incident document (one para + five bullets).
2) Within 24 hours: add a short playbook snippet to the service runbook describing the observed signal and the successful mitigation command(s).
3) Within 72 hours: create the lightweight postmortem and link graphs and traces.
4) Before rotation end: ensure follow-ups have owners and estimated completion dates.

Sample timeline entry (format to copy into incident doc)
- 2025-02-10T14:05Z — Alert: p99 latency spike for Redwood-API-gen (primary on-call: linh). Pager sent to #oncall.
- 2025-02-10T14:12Z — Primary investigated, found config rollout at 14:00; scaled runtime +2 nodes (`infra autoscale`).
- 2025-02-10T14:28Z — Secondary engaged. IC declared a P1. Traffic shifted to fallback. Latency improving.
- 2025-02-10T15:20Z — Service restored to SLO. Mitigation confirmed. Created incident summary.

Runbook maintenance & ownership
- Every runbook must list a runbook owner and a last-updated timestamp.
- Owners are responsible for: post-game-day updates, triage notes, and verifying rollback instructions.
- Repo: runbooks are stored in Confluence and mirrored to /docs/runbooks repo nightly.

Escalation and debrief checklist for IC (post-incident)
- Confirm that customer comms were sent and queued for postmortem inclusion.
- Ensure all timeline entries have timestamps and owners.
- Assign postmortem owner and set review meeting (if scorecard <4).
- If the incident is recurring, schedule a game-day within 14 days.

Appendix: common mitigation commands
- Check node health: `nodes get --region us-west-2 --service redwood-runtime`
- Temporary scale up: `infra autoscale --service runtime --up 2 --reason "incident"`
- Rollback last deploy: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n production`
- Re-route traffic: `route update --service redwood-api-gen --to fallback-cluster`

Notes and governance
- This guide is intentionally compact to be usable in high-pressure contexts. Teams should expand service-specific steps into their runbooks.
- Every on-call rotation lead should review this guide quarterly and propose changes through the runbook governance process.

End of document

payload.page_title: Field Operator Stabilization Procedures and Customer Briefs

sections.body:
Summary:

This runbook documents a compact, operator-focused stabilization runloop for first 10–30 minutes of any service-impacting event that primarily affects inference traffic (latency spikes, KV cache evictions, model-serve OOMs, and mass rate-limit bursts). It includes a clear triage ladder, step-by-step actions for the field operator, templates for customer-facing comms, a short post-incident evidence checklist, and a game-day syllabus to keep operator skills fresh.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Enable an on-call operator (primary or secondary) to quickly stabilize traffic, limit blast radius, and produce consistent customer status updates while evidence is collected for later RCA.
- Scope: Production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted inference API (hosted/dedicated), routing/fallbacks, KV caching layers, batch router, and model-serving runtime. Not intended for low-priority config requests or non-prod environments.

Key contacts and ownership:

- Primary operator: on-call SRE (PagerDuty escalation)
- Escalation owners: Serving Runtime (team-serving-runtime), Platform (team-platform), SRE (eng-sre), Customer Success (cs-respond), Security (security-ops)
- Slack channels: #oncall-ops (primary), #platform-alerts (secondary)
- PagerDuty escalation policy: "Inference API — Primary" -> "Inference API — Secondary" -> "SRE Shift Lead"

Severity mapping (quick reference):

1. Sev1 (Critical) — System-wide outage or p99 latency > 5s for > 5 minutes, customers experiencing failed requests or large-scale degraded throughput.
2. Sev2 (Major) — Significant latency/regression affecting a subset of customers or increased error rates (5–20% error rate sustained > 10 minutes).
3. Sev3 (Minor) — Transient errors, single-customer impact, or degradations with automated fallback in effect.

SLOs to use during triage:

- Hosted text-generation API: availability 99.95% monthly; p99 latency target < 400ms (tokens streaming excluded).
- Dedicated customer pools: throughput-based SLOs agreed per contract (reference customer SLA doc).
- KV cache hit-rate baseline: > 65% for high-read workloads; immediate declines below 40% indicate cache eviction storms.
- Error budget threshold for immediate escalation: remaining error budget < 10% for the rolling 30d window.

Operator stabilization runloop (first 10 minutes):

1) Acknowledge and collect signals (0–2 min)
   - Acknowledge PagerDuty and join bridge/Slack.
   - Record initial symptom set: service(s), region(s), observed metrics (p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue depth), and time window.
   - Commands to run immediately:
     - curl -sS https://status.redwood.com/health | jq .
     - kubectl --context=prod get pods -n inference -l app=inference-gateway -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoop|Evicted"
     - grafana quick checks: open dashboard "Inference — p99 latency by region" and snapshot if possible.

2) Contain the blast radius (2–6 min)
   - If KV cache eviction spike: temporarily reduce cache churn by throttling autoscaler for model-onboarding jobs and apply cache warming (see KV cache warm command below).
   - If p99 latency spike caused by noisy tenant: apply tenant-aware rate limit:
     - rctl set-tenant-rate --tenant-id <TENANT> --per-sec 5
   - If model-serving OOMs: switch traffic to compatible fallback model variant (policy: model-variant-fallback v1.2) via the router:
     - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/router/switch -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-compat-v1.2"}'
   - If ingress/backpressure in batch-router: decrease batch size and enable immediate draining:
     - POST /api/v1/batch-router/drain?mode=fast

3) Stabilize throughput (6–12 min)
   - Re-route a small % (5–10%) of traffic to a warm standby region or a lower-cost variant to relieve the hot path. Use canary routing when available.
     - routectl split --from inference-gateway:us-east-1 --to inference-gateway:us-west-2 --percent 10
   - Turn on additional logging for affected services for 10 minutes to capture evidence, then set back to info.

4) Customer comms and status (within 15 min)
   - Publish an initial status note (short form) within 10–15 minutes to status.redwood.com and post in #oncall-ops with copy for the Customer Success team. Use the template below.
   - If customer-impacting: escalate to CS and prepare tailored notices for top affected customers using the customer-brief template.

Short-form status template (initial):

Title: Incident — [Service] degraded in [region]\Status: Investigating\Impact: Elevated latency and 5xx errors for subset of API requests; customers may see request failures or slow responses.\ETA: Initial triage complete; further updates every 30 minutes or on change.\Owner: Asha Mehta (on-call)\Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/<INCIDENT_ID>

Long-form customer brief (CS-ready) — example:

Subject: Service degradation affecting inference requests in us-east-1\\nHi <CustomerName>,

We’re currently investigating elevated latency and a higher-than-normal error rate that may affect inference requests to us-east-1. Our SREs have contained the issue and rerouted a portion of traffic; we expect partial stabilization within the next 30 minutes. We will provide a follow-up update with root-cause analysis and remediation steps once available.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Rerouted ~10% of traffic to us-west-2 (reduced pressure).
- Applied tenant-level rate limiting to high-volume tenants identified in the event.

If you are seeing failed requests, please provide request IDs and sample timestamps — we will prioritize debugging.

Regards,
Redwood SRE & Customer Success

Evidence collection checklist (before postmortem) — minimum required:

- Metric snapshots: p95/p99 latency, error-rate, request volume from Grafana (time window +/- 30m)
- Service logs: 10-min log slice from all affected inference-gateway pods
- Router traces: sampled traces for 5 failed requests (trace IDs)
- Deployment state: git commit hashes and rollout timestamps for any recent changes
- Eviction/OOM artifacts: kube events, node-level logs if applicable

Post-incident tasks (within 24–72 hours):

1. Create an incident record using the incident template (see below) and link evidence artifacts.
2. Run a prioritized RCA. If RCA requires cross-team investigation, assign action items and owners with due dates.
3. Check error budget implications and notify finance/product if SLA credits may be triggered.

Incident record template (to attach to postmortem):

- Incident ID: <INCIDENT_ID>
- Severity: Sev1/Sev2/Sev3
- Start / End time (UTC): <start> / <end>
- Impact summary: short paragraph
- Timeline (minute-level for first 60 minutes; coarse after): bullet list
- Evidence collected: list of saved metrics, logs, traces and links
- Corrective actions taken during incident: bullet list
- Postmortem owner: <Name>
- Action items: owner, description, due date, status

Postmortem rubric (what matters):

- Focus on facts: timeline, evidence, and decision points.
- Evaluate detection and mitigation latency: how long between signal and first containment?
- Quantify customer impact: requests impacted, customers affected, revenue/SLA exposure.
- Validate action items meet the SMART criteria and have owners + deadlines.

Runbook publishing checklist (for any change):

- Author and reviewer assigned.
- Test commands and rollback steps verified in a staging runbook drill.
- Add one example customer comm and one internal Slack snippet.
- Mark confidentiality and link to any affected cust-SLA references.

Game-day syllabus (30–60 minute labs run quarterly):

- Scenario A — KV eviction cascade: simulate eviction by saturating cache-writer job; validate throttling and cache-warm steps.
- Scenario B — Noisy tenant throttling: create synthetic traffic from tenant emulator; validate tenant-rate controls and customer notices.
- Scenario C — Model OOM fallback: intentionally trigger OOM on model-serving runtime and observe routing to compatible model variant.
- Scenario D — Multi-region partial outage: disable us-east-1 ingress and verify split routing and customer status updates.

Each game-day includes: pre-game checklist, operator roles (primary/secondary/bridge), 1-hour controlled window, and a 30-min retro capturing evidence for the postmortem template.

Escalation matrix (quick view):

- If within first 10 minutes the operator cannot reduce error rate or latency by 50%: escalate to Serving Runtime lead (pager: team-serving-runtime).
- If security artifact suspected (e.g., abnormal auth failures): escalate to Security immediately and mark confidentiality: restricted.
- If > 30 minutes without stabilization on a Sev1: notify Exec on-call and Customer Success for customer outreach.

CLI snippets and useful commands (operators):

- KV cache warm: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/cache/warm -d '{"scope":"global","keys":10}'
- Snapshot metrics to S3: curl -X POST https://metrics.redwood.internal/snapshot -d '{"dash":"inference-p99","window":"30m"}'
- Rotate inference router: routectl rotate --service inference-gateway --mode soft

Operational notes and common pitfalls:

- Avoid full rollback of serving runtime in first 15 minutes unless it's the only evident cause — prefer routing to fallbacks first.
- Don’t mass-scale down nodes during an ongoing OOM event — that can increase eviction churn.
- Always preserve raw logs before truncation for legal and compliance evidence retention.

Retention and evidence policy pointers:

- Incident artifacts required for Sev1: full logs and traces retained for 180 days.
- For Sev2: retain 90 days.
- For Sev3: retain 30 days.

Appendix: short checklist for the operator to post (single-line items):

- Acknowledge PD and join bridge
- Collect initial metrics snapshot
- Contain blast radius (rate-limit / re-route / drain)
- Publish initial status (status.redwood.com)
- Collect evidence (logs, traces, commits)
- Escalate as needed per matrix
- Create incident record and assign postmortem owner

Related pages and references: refer to dashboards and runbooks in the "eng-sre" space for detailed dashboards, and to the Customer Success sprint playbook for templated customer notifications.

Document owner: Asha Mehta (eng-sre)

Last reviewed: 2026-02-10

payload.page_title: On‑call Transition Cookbook and Blameless Postmortem Cadence

sections.body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This page codifies a repeatable, SLO-driven approach for on‑call transitions, escalation ladders, and a blameless postmortem cadence. It is designed for engineers, SREs, and on‑call leads who perform handoffs, run game days, and own incident learning loops.

Scope: applies to Redwood Inference production services (hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments) and covers: rotation transitions, short‑form handoff artifact, escalation timers, evidence collection, postmortem schedule, and customer status / status page templates.

Principles
----------
- SLO first: incidents are triaged against customer‑facing SLOs (availability and latency) and classification is driven by SLO impact.
- Time‑boxed actions: fast containment is prioritized; long investigations are deferred to postmortem.
- Psychological safety: no individual blame; focus on systemic causes and actionable remediation.
- Repeatability: written artifacts + runbook links must always accompany major handoffs.

Key SLOs and thresholds (for triage)
-----------------------------------
| SLO | Target | Triage threshold | Escalation severity |
|----|-------:|------------------:|-------------------:|
| Hosted API availability | 99.95% monthly | < 99.5% sustained 10m | Sev2 / Sev1 if customer outage |
| P95 generation latency (region) | < 250 ms | > 400 ms 5m window | Sev2 |
| Embeddings throughput (per-dedicated pool) | 95% of provisioned | < 80% throughput 10m | Sev3/Sev2 |
| Error rate (5xx) | < 1% | > 3% 5m rolling | Sev2/Sev1 |
\nRotation transition checklist (10-minute template)
--------------------------------------------------
The on‑going oncall (OOO) briefly documents the following in the team Slack #oncall-handoff and attaches a short handoff artifact to the rotation calendar event. Use the checklist below — aim for 10 minutes.

1) Current state summary (1–2 lines): services impacted, customer visible symptoms, any workarounds in place.
2) Active pages/tickets: PD incidents and JIRA IDs.
3) What I did in the last hour: mitigations, restarts, config changes, rollbacks.
4) What I intend to do next (if known) and blockers.
5) Key dashboards/queries: link(s) to the SLO dashboard, rate-limited query, and trace.
6) Runbooks attached (copy links): e.g., Runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
7) Evidence bundle location: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id> or /mnt/incident-evidence/<incident-id>
8) Confidence level and suggested escalation (ack windows, owners).

Example handoff message (Slack)
-------------------------------
[HANDOFF] 2026-02-03 09:50 UTC
- Summary: ~30% 5xx on hosted-text-gen-east; customers see streaming truncation.
- Active: PD#1234 (ack), JIRA INC-987
- Last hour: restarted model pool A, disabled auto-batching; latency p95 improved ~20% but errors persist.
- Next: coordinate canary rollback (owner: @diego), investigating kernel OOMs (link).
- Runbooks: kv-cache-eviction, model-fallback-policy. Evidence: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/INC-987

Escalation ladder and timers
---------------------------
- Pager acknowledgment target: 5 minutes (primary)
- Initial mitigation window: 15 minutes (if unresolved, escalate to secondary)
- Cross-team engagement: 30 minutes (platform, model-team, SRE)
- Customer status decision point: 45 minutes (if customer impact confirmed)

Escalation flow (summary): Primary -> Secondary -> Team Lead -> Oncall SRE -> Engineering Director. For customer-impacting Sev1s, trigger Incident Bridge and notify CS/Support within 30 minutes.

Containment runbook quick actions (top-level)
--------------------------------------------
1) Reduce blast radius: temporarily throttle trafffic, shift routing to a healthy region, or disable non-essential features.
2) Switch traffic to a compatible model variant (fallback): document fallback in the timeline.
3) Revert recent deploys or config churn if the timeline indicates correlation.
4) If OOMs or GPU kernel errors, drain affected nodes and re-schedule workloads. Use drain script:
```
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
okctl node drain --id i-0abc123 --reason "OOM during inference" --timeout 600
```
\nEvidence collection and preservation (must do within first hour)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Save logs (kubectl logs --since=1h or equivalent), traces, and the current SLO dashboard snapshot to the evidence bucket.
- Capture sample requests that reproduce the error (sanitize PII).
- Tag all evidence with incident-id and owner. Failure to preserve evidence can block postmortem analysis.

Postmortem cadence and ownership
-------------------------------
- Triage postmortem required if incident meets any of:
  - Customer‑facing outage (any SLA credit exposure)
  - Sev1 or prolonged Sev2 (> 4 hours)
  - Repeating root cause across 3 incidents in 30 days

- Timeline:
  - 0–48 hours: containment and evidence collection (operational owners)
  - 72 hours: preliminary timeline and a blameless incident summary (to #postmortems)
  - 7 calendar days: draft postmortem authored (owner: incident commander)
  - 14 calendar days: postmortem review meeting (participants: incident owner, SRE, affected service leads)
  - 30 days: action item close or re-assess (owner assigned)

- Roles:
  - Incident Commander (IC): runs the incident and is responsible for the timeline and initial writeup.
  - Evidence Lead: ensures logs, traces, and reproductions are saved.
  - RCA Lead: performs deeper analysis and drafts contributing cause matrix.
  - Action Tracker: ensures remediation tasks have clear owners and dates.

Blameless postmortem scaffold (required sections)
------------------------------------------------
- Summary (2–4 sentences)
- Impact (users, SLOs, revenue/customers)
- Timeline (bulletized, timestamps in UTC)
- Root cause (contributing causes + evidence)
- Remediation: short term (within 7d) and long term (within 90d)
- Preventative metrics and tests (what we'll add to detect recurrence)
- Owners and acceptance criteria for each action
- Lessons learned and open questions

Meeting templates and psychological-safety checklist
--------------------------------------------------
Before the postmortem review meeting, the IC must:
- Share the draft with the reviewer list at least 48 hours ahead.
- Flag any security/customer sensitive sections to Legal/Compliance.
sections.heading: Drain node (example)

sections.body:
- Start with facts and timeline, not names.
- Invite questions about systems and decisions; avoid assigning blame.
- Confirm each action has an owner and a deadline.
sections.heading: During the meeting

sections.body:
- Explicitly state "this is a blameless postmortem" at the meeting start.
- Use neutral language: "contributed to" vs "caused by".
- Encourage junior engineers to speak; the facilitator should call on quieter participants.

Game day (chaos) playbook for oncall skill growth
--------------------------------------------------
Frequency: quarterly per team.
Goals: practice evidence collection, handoffs, and force‑test runbooks.
sections.heading: Psychological-safety checklist (short)

sections.body:
1) 15m scenario brief (injects and objectives)
2) 30–60m incident response (live)
3) 30m hotwash (what worked, what didn’t)
4) 30m action creation and runbook updates

Scenarios to rotate: KV cache eviction, model quantization regression, regional routing failure, capacity exhaustion in dedicated pools. Each scenario must have a realistic timeline and clear termination criteria.

Status page and customer communication templates
------------------------------------------------
Decision rule: publish to status.redwood.ai if customer visible impact or any ongoing mitigation that takes >30 minutes. For high severity incidents always publish within 45 minutes.

Status page template (short)
- Title: Degraded generation in US‑East (ongoing)
- Affected: Hosted text generation API
- Time identified: 2026-02-03 09:05 UTC
- Current status: Identified — Mitigation in progress
- Next update: 2026-02-03 10:00 UTC
- Details: We are seeing an elevated 5xx rate for text generation in the US‑East region. Teams are investigating and have routed traffic away from impacted nodes. No data loss reported.

Customer support email (initial)
Subject: Service degradation impacting text generation in US‑East
sections.heading: Minimum agenda

sections.body:
Hello,

We are investigating an issue affecting text generation in the US‑East region. You may experience errors or increased response times. Our teams are actively mitigating and we will send an update within 45 minutes. We apologize for the disruption.

— Redwood Inference Support Team

Customer follow‑up template (30m)
- What changed since last update: e.g., rolled back canary, reduced traffic to region A (impact reduced 40%)
- Expected next steps and ETA (if known)
- Contact for escalations: support@redwood.ai (include account manager if enterprise customer)

Runbook hygiene and ownership matrix
-----------------------------------
- Every runbook must include: owner, last run date, test instructions, rollback steps, and a short SR (safety review) note.
- Review cadence: critical runbooks (SLO‑impacting) reviewed quarterly; lower‑risk annually.

Example runbook metadata table
ID | Name | Owner | Last tested | Next review
RB-041 | kv-cache-eviction | Marcus Patel | 2026-01-15 | 2026-04-15
RB-058 | model-fallback-policy | Lena O'Neill | 2025-11-10 | 2026-02-10

Automations and small helpers
-----------------------------
- Automated evidence snapshot: trigger via /incident snapshot <incident-id> to save dashboards and traces to the evidence bucket.
- Slack bot handoff: /handoff create will auto-post the 8‑point checklist to #oncall-handoff and attach the calendar event.

Appendices
---------
A. Quick decision ladder (cheat sheet)
- If SLOs violated and customers impacted: declare Sev1, start bridge, notify CS within 30m.
- If internal-only impact with degradation: Sev3/Sev2 depending on duration and scope.

B. Useful commands and snippets
- Collect recent logs (k8s): kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=text-gen --since=30m > /tmp/textgen-logs-30m.log
- Capture traces (example): go-trace-collector --service hosted-text-gen --start 2026-02-03T08:50:00Z --end 2026-02-03T09:10:00Z --out traces/INC-987.json

C. Related pages
- Runbook library: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Incident evidence retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/incident-evidence-policy

If you have improvements to this cookbook, open PR on the runbook repo or ping the SRE rota lead.

payload.page_title: Concierge On‑Call Playbook: Quiet Windows and Customer Status Scripting

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the ‘Concierge’ on‑call experience — a structured runbook and communications framework for handling low‑severity but customer‑facing incidents during quiet windows (overnight, weekends, public holidays) and for scripted status escalations. The goal is to preserve trust with clear, human‑centered status updates while keeping operational overhead low.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood production inference services (api-gateway, runtime-fleet, kv-cache, routing‑mesh) and to customer‑facing status flows initiated by SLO deviations, capacity blips, or model-quality regressions that do not require a full bridge.

Owner: Customer Success (Concierge Squad) + Oncall Operations

Key principles
- Empathy first: surface clear impact and next steps, not internal diagnostics.
- Minimal noise: aggregate notifications where appropriate to avoid waking multiple stakeholders.
- Fast stabilization then transparency: prioritise quick mitigation (reroute, throttle, fallback model) before detailed forensics.
- Escalate early when customer business flows are at risk.

When to use this playbook (decision ladder)
1) Alert detected: SLO or customer signal crosses low/medium threshold (see thresholds table).
2) Triage: operator confirms impact (single-region, capacity spike, elevated latency (p50>target*2) but <30% error rate).
3) If human‑facing and within quiet window, invoke Concierge Playbook. If severity escalates to 30%+ error or region outage, follow full incident bridge runbook.

Thresholds (summary)
| Signal | Low | Medium | Bridge trigger |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 99th latency (model-generation) | >2000ms | >3500ms | persistent >5000ms or customer-reported outage |
| Error rate (5m rolling) | 0.5% | 2% | >5% |
| KV cache miss rate | +10pp from baseline | +25pp | sustained >40pp or cascading retries |

Concierge operator responsibilities
- Acknowledge within 10 minutes.
- Run quick mitigation checklist (below).
- Post an initial customer‑facing status update within 30 minutes during quiet windows.
- Keep updates at 30‑60 minute cadence until stabilized or fully escalated.
- Create a short incident stub in the Incident Log and hand over to the owning SRE team if follow‑up is required.

Quick mitigation checklist (order of operations)
1. Validate the alert: verify graphs in dashboards (per-route latency, token throughput, GPU utilization) and confirm customer impact.
2. Apply safe mitigation: per-route fallback to smaller model / cached response, enable burst capacity if available, temporarily increase concurrency limits for affected routing tier.
3. Throttle noisy tenants: if multitenant noisy‑neighboring behavior is detected, apply tenant-level rate limit and notify tenant owner.
4. Evict/refresh KV cache prefix if prefix hot‑spotting is identified (use cache-evict --prefix <key> with ttl 60s).
5. If mitigation is successful, track changes in the Evidence section and prepare handback notes.

Customer‑facing status templates
- Initial: "We are investigating increased request latency affecting some API calls in <region>. Our engineers are applying targeted mitigations; we will update again within 30 minutes. Impact: degraded latencies for a subset of requests. No widespread outage detected."
- Follow up (mitigated): "Mitigation in place: requests are routing to a lower-latency model variant and queuing pressure reduced. Latency is improving. We will keep monitoring and follow up with a short summary in the next 2 hours."
- Follow up (escalate to bridge): "Impact is broader than initially assessed; we are escalating to a full incident bridge and will provide more frequent updates. We expect an extended restoration window. Next update in 15 minutes."
- Resolution summary: "Root cause summary and customer impact: <one‑paragraph plain English summary>. Remediation steps taken: <bulleted list>. Action items and owner(s): <bulleted list>. If you require credits or tailored remediation, reply to this thread and we will connect you with your Customer Success lead."

Slack and Pager templates
- Slack (internal #ops-alerts): "[Concierge] Acknowledged: latency spike in us‑west‑1 for route /v1/generate. Mitigations: fallback to small model, increased burst capacity. Monitoring: p99 down 60% from peak. Will update in 30m. Owner: @oncall-operator"
- Pager/Phone (escalation): "Concierge oncall: brief summary, mitigation applied, escalation needed? yes/no. Contact matrix in Handoff section."

Status page rules and cadence
- If the bridge is not required and mitigation is in place within 60 minutes, we post an advisory (status.redwood.ai: Partial Degradation) with a 1h update cadence.
- If a bridge is opened, follow the Incident Communication SOP for status page and press templates.
- Template fields required: impact_summary, affected_regions, affected_endpoints, mitigation_steps, next_update ETA, incident_id.

Handoff procedure (Concierge -> SRE/Service Owner)
1. Create Incident stub: short summary, timelines, dashboards, mitigation steps, runbook steps already executed, artifacts (logs, core indicators).
2. Tag owning service and @svc-oncall.
3. Transfer in Slack DM + Incident Log entry: include link to status page and customer message thread.
4. If owner team needs deeper analysis, SRE takes over and updates the incident status to Bridge.

Postmortem and follow‑up requirements
- For incidents handled completely within Concierge and resolved within 3 hours with no customer credit requests: create a short postmortem stub (one page) summarizing timeline, root cause hypothesis, action items. Owner must close within 7 days.
- For incidents requiring bridge or customer credits: follow the full postmortem process (90-day remediation plan, exec summary, customer outreach script).

Game day scenarios (quarterly, run by Concierge Squad)
- Scenario A: Overnight KV cache stampede — simulate sudden miss-rate increase causing latency blips. Objective: measure time-to-first-mitigation and customer update quality.
- Scenario B: Noisy tenant causing route starvation — exercise throttling and tenant notification cadence.
- Scenario C: Model variant rollback during quiet window — validate automated rollback + status message sequencing.

Playbook run cadence and ownership
- Concierge Playbook owner: Customer Success (Concierge Squad).
- Quarterly review with SRE and Eng Platform to update thresholds and mitigation knobs.
- Game days: Concierge leads quarterly; SRE provides technical observers and grading.

Evidence and artifacts (what to collect)
- Dashboards: p50/p90/p99 per-route latency, error rate, GPU utilization, KV miss rate.
- Logs: correlated request ids for impacted windows.
- Change events: autoscaling, model rollouts, config pushes during incident window.

Operational configuration table (reference knobs)
- autoscale.burst_enabled: true|false
- routing.fallback_model: <model-id> (example: rdx-small-1)
- per_tenant.rate_limit: 100–500 rps (configurable)
- cache.eviction_ttl_seconds: 60–300

Handoff checklist (brief)
1. Incident stub in Incident Log (link).
2. Customer thread with most recent status messages.
3. Mitigations executed and who executed them.
4. Dashboards and links to artifacts.
5. Suggested owners and priority of follow ups.

Appendix: Checklist for status language (tone and content)
- Keep it customer-centric: start with the impact and affected functionality.
- Use plain language: avoid internal acronyms unless they help clarify.
- Provide next-step ETA and what customers can do (workarounds).
- Close with how customers can reach their account team for tailored support.

Templates and example timelines (sample incident)
- 00:00 Alert triggered (p99 > 3500ms). Operator acknowledges 00:07.
- 00:20 Mitigation: fallback model applied; p99 improving. Post initial customer message 00:25.
- 01:00 System stable; monitoring for 60 minutes. Post mitigation update 01:10.
- 02:00 Incident closed; create stub and short postmortem 02:15.

Contact matrix (concierge escalation)
- Concierge operator -> oncall SRE (pager) if bridge required.
- Concierge operator -> platform oncall (Slack @platform-oncall) for autoscaling failures.
- Concierge operator -> Account Manager for high-touch customers (phone).

Change log
- 2024-11-18: Created playbook (Priya R.).
- 2025-03-12: Updated thresholds and added game day scenarios (Liam O'C.).

Related links
- Internal incident log: /dash/incidents
- Status page publisher doc: /confluence/product-docs/publish-status-updates

End of document
