payload.page_title: incident-preboarding-and-rapid-escalation-manual

sections.body: This page codifies a compact, reusable incident preboarding process and a rapid escalation manual for Redwood Inference on-call operators. It is intended to reduce time-to-stable for common serving and routing incidents by standardizing pre-incident checks, triage steps, escalation thresholds, customer notifications, and game-day exercises.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- First responders and on-call SREs
- Bridge operators / duty leads
- Product engineers called for escalations
- Customer Success/Support for customer notices
sections.heading: Who should use this doc

sections.body:
1) Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recover (MTTR) for latency and availability incidents.
2) Provide low-friction templates for the first 30 minutes of an incident (preboarding and initial comms).
3) Ensure consistent on-call handoffs and measurable follow-ups (postmortem + action tracking).
sections.heading: Primary goals

sections.body:
- Applies to Redwood hosted inference services (inference-gateway, routing-proxy, kv-cache, model-runtime).
- Not intended to replace service-specific deeper runbooks; those live under eng-serving-runtime/runbooks.
- This is not a legal or customer SLA explanation; use finance-and-legal templates for credits and contractual language.
sections.heading: Scope and non-goals

sections.body:
- Primary owner: SRE team (Pager: eng-sre-oncall)
- Escalation owner: Runtime Reliability (oncall: runtime-lead)
- Communications owner: Customer Success (oncall: cs-bridge)
- Exec escalation: Head of Production (oncall: prod-head)

Preboarding checklist (to run at sign-on or before a high-risk deploy):
- Confirm your PagerDuty roster and replacement on call.
- Confirm you have access: VPN, KMS keys, Debug bastion, Slack #incident, PagerDuty, Status Page admin.
- Load basic dashboards: "service-slo-overview", "token-latency-by-route", "error-rate-heatmap".
- Warm up common troubleshooting commands (see "Operator quick commands").
- Verify that postmortem template and a JIRA incident-ticket are ready (ticket prefix: INC-).
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation contacts

sections.body:
1) Signal detection: automated SLO alert, customer report, or internal alert.
2) Acknowledge: on-call acknowledges in PagerDuty within 3 minutes for P0/P1.
3) Preboard (first 5 minutes): collect evidence, set bridge, record timeline.
4) Triage (5–15 minutes): classify impact, determine quick mitigations.
5) Mitigate (15–60 minutes): execute fixes or fallbacks, engage owners.
6) Stabilize (60+ minutes): confirm SLO recovery and route traffic back.
7) Communicate: send status page updates and customer templates per cadence.
8) Review: run postmortem within 72 hours and track action items to closure.
sections.heading: Incident lifecycle (concise numbered workflow)

sections.body:
- P0 (SEV-0) — Platform outage: >30% of requests failing or latency >5x SLO for >5 minutes. Target MTTA: 1 minute, MTTR: 30 minutes.
- P1 (SEV-1) — Significant degradation: 5–30% of requests affected or sustained 2x latency for >5 minutes. Target MTTA: 3 minutes, MTTR: 2 hours.
- P2 (SEV-2) — Minor degradation or partial functional loss for a subset of tenants. MTTA: 30 minutes, MTTR: 24 hours.
- P3 (SEV-3) — Minor bug/feature regression with no immediate customer impact.

Rapid escalation matrix (use this table to decide whom to call and when):
| Time since detection | Trigger condition | Action | Escalation target | Notes |
|----------------------|-------------------|--------|-------------------|-------|
| 0–5m | P0 detection | Acknowledge & open bridge | On-call (primary) | DM runtime-lead in Slack #runtime-critical |
| 5–15m | No quick mitigation or impact grows | Page runtime-lead and product-owner | runtime-lead + product-owner | Consider traffic re-routing/fallback |
| 15–30m | SLO not recovering | Exec escalation (prod-head) + CS-bridge | prod-head, cs-bridge | Prepare customer comms and legal hold if needed |
| 30–60m | Ongoing customer-visible outage | Open cross-functional incident with engineering and support | All hands page | Trigger public status page updates and SOC brief |

Note: use PagerDuty for signal, Slack for rapid thread, and bridge (Zoom/Jitsi) for coordination. Place artifacts (logs, graphs) in the incident ticket.

Triage runbook: initial evidence and quick checks (first 10 minutes)
- Step 0: Capture scope: "Which services?" (inference-gateway, routing-proxy, kv-cache, model-runtime).
- Step 1: Validate SLO metric sources: Grafana dashboard (service-slo-overview), logs (elk/inference-logs), and tracing (jaeger).
- Step 2: Run automated checklist commands (examples):
  - Check gateway pods and recent restarts: kubectl -n production get pods -l app=inference-gateway -o wide
  - Check error ratios in last 5m: curl -s "http://monitoring/api/alerts?service=inference-gateway&window=5m" | jq .
  - Check KV cache eviction rates: curl -s http://kv-metrics/api | jq '.evictions_1m'
  - Confirm model runtime health: ssh runtime-bastion "systemctl status model-runtime || journalctl -u model-runtime -n 200"
- Step 3: Identify if a rollback or fallback can be applied quickly (traffic shift to previous model version, disable caching optimization).
- Step 4: If mitigation is not obvious, escalate per matrix and collect logs for postmortem.

Operator quick commands (cheat-sheet)
- Open bridge: ./scripts/open-bridge --incident INC-<id> --topic "inference outage"
- Post status update: ./scripts/statuspage post --component inference-gateway --status investigating --message "Investigating elevated errors"
- Rotate traffic to previous model (example): rd-ctl route set-weight --service inference-gateway --version v2025-09-20 --weight 100
- Flush KV cache for tenant (example): curl -X POST https://kv-cache.internal/flush?tenant=acme-corp --header 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

Status page templates (examples used by CS or Bridge operator)
- Initial: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "investigating",
  "message": "We are investigating elevated error rates impacting text generation. Impacted users may see failed requests or increased latency. We will update when we have more information."
}
- Update: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "message": "Mitigation in progress: traffic diverted to fallback model version v2025-09-20. Some requests may still fail intermittently. Next update in 30 minutes."
}
- Resolved: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "operational",
  "message": "Issue resolved. All services normal. Root cause investigation is ongoing and will be summarized in the postmortem."
}
(Replace values with real incident id and summary.)

Customer comms templates (concise, plain-language):
- Short initial email to affected customers:
  Subject: Redwood Inference – Service Interruption Update (INC-12345)
  Body: Hello <Customer>,
  We are aware of an issue affecting text generation for some requests. Our engineers are actively investigating. You may see errors or higher latency. We will provide our next update within 30 minutes. If you have critical workloads, please reply to this message and we will prioritize your tenant.
  — Redwood Inference Support

- Resolution notice to customers:
  Subject: Redwood Inference – Incident Resolved (INC-12345)
  Body: Hello <Customer>,
  The incident affecting text generation has been resolved at 2025-06-10T14:45Z. We restored traffic to the primary runtime and have confirmed system health. We are preparing a postmortem and will share findings and mitigations within 72 hours.
sections.heading: Priority definitions and SLO thresholds

sections.body:
- Title: INC-12345 — Elevated error rate impacting inference-gateway
- Timeline: (UTC timestamps, system detected, acknowledged, mitigation started, resolved)
- Impact: number of affected requests, percent of customers impacted, duration, SLO miss details
- Root cause: concise statement and supporting evidence (logs, diffs, commits)
- Contributing factors: list of 2–4 items (eg, config rollout, autoscaler threshold, false-positive alert)
- Corrective actions (owner, due date): eg, pin autoscaler version (owner: infra-team, due: 2025-07-01)
- Validation: how we will verify the fix (synthetic tests, canary metrics)
- Follow-ups: link to JIRA and next review meeting

Game-day & simulation plan (30–90 minute exercise template):
- Objective: validate that the on-call team can detect, escalate, and restore service within SLO targets using the preboarding steps.
- Participants: 1 bridge operator, 2 SREs (primary & secondary), 1 runtime engineer, 1 CS liaison.
- Scenario examples: high KV cache eviction causing 3x latency; model runtime OOM during peak; routing-proxy partial outage creating 50% of tenants with 500 errors.
- Schedule (example 60m):
  - 0–5m: Inject signal (monitoring alert + synthetic failing requests)
  - 5–15m: Triage & collect evidence. Bridge opens and status posted.
  - 15–30m: Apply mitigation (traffic shift, restart runtime, increase capacity).
  - 30–45m: Validate mitigation and prepare customer comm.
  - 45–60m: Debrief and write quick learning note; create postmortem ticket if relevant.
- Scoring rubric: detection time, acknowledgement time, mitigation time, customer comm quality. Capture metrics and iterate.

payload.page_title: First-Response Cadre Playbook and CSR Status Lattice

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes the role, responsibilities and procedures for the "First-Response Cadre" (FRC) — the set of people who take immediate action for service signals before the full incident bridge is established. The goal is fast containment, evidence capture, and clear handoff to the incident bridge or service steward. This doc also includes a structured lattice of customer status templates (CSR templates) for common impact tiers.

Audience: oncall engineers, bridge operators, CSRs, SRE leads.

Key objectives
- Acknowledge and classify alerts within 2 minutes for P0/P1 signals.
- Contain customer-visible impact within 30 minutes when possible.
- Preserve forensic evidence (logs, traces, KV snapshots) before remediation alters state.
- Provide consistent customer-facing status lines using the CSR lattice below.

Roles and contacts
1) First Responder (FR) — primary oncall engineer who opened the alert.
   - Responsibility: initial triage, short-term containment, evidence snapshot.
   - Contact: #oncall (Slack), PagerDuty: redwood-prod-oncall
2) Bridge Operator (BO) — sets up and runs the bridge if incident escalates.
   - Responsibility: run the timeline, coordinate cross-team ops.
   - Contact: #bridge-ops
3) Service Steward (SS) — owner of the failing service.
   - Responsibility: hold long-running remediations, postmortem lead.
4) CSR Liaison — customer success liaison for customer-facing comms.
   - Responsibility: select and publish CSR template, route customer questions.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Signal arrival
   - Monitor/alerting systems: Prometheus Alertmanager, Sentinels (latency monitors), LogAnvil (error spikes).
   - FR acknowledges in PagerDuty within 2 minutes.
2. Rapid Triage (0–10 minutes)
   - Determine scope: single region vs global; single-customer vs multi-tenant.
   - Quick checks: deployment events, recent model rollouts, autoscaling events, or noisy neighbors.
   - Evidence capture checklist (run immediately):
     a) Dump top 200 error traces: curl -s "https://loganvil/api/v1/query?service=...&top=200" > evidence/traces-$(date +%s).json
     b) Snapshot KV cache metrics (hit/miss rates) and TTL distributions.
     c) Record in-bridge timeline: timestamp, FR name, hypothesis.
3. Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - Apply short-term mitigations: route traffic to fallback model, disable new rollouts, scale up inferencers, toggle prefix caching.
   - If containment succeeds, mark status as "stabilized" and proceed to incident creation in the bridge if required.
4. Bridge & Escalation (30+ minutes or immediate for P0)
   - BO establishes bridge using template: conference link, triage doc, runbook links, and customer comm ID.
   - Assign action owners and target SLAs for restoration steps.
5. Recovery & Validation
   - Verify steady-state across regions and tenants for at least two 5-minute windows.
6. Postmortem
   - SS leads the write-up within 72 hours; postmortem must include timeline, root cause, action items, and regression tests.

Triage decision ladder (condensed)
- If 95th percentile latency > 2x SLO across >10% of hosts -> escalate to P1.
- If sustained error-rate > 3% for requests over 10 minutes OR confirmed data loss affecting customers -> P0.
- If single-tenant impact and rate-limited -> P2 (service owner to coordinate).

Sample Runbooks (excerpts)
A) KV Cache Eviction Spike
- Trigger: cache eviction rate > 1000 evictions/min and cache hit ratio drops by >15%.
- Steps:
  1) Pause any recent quantization rollouts: infra rollback command.
  2) Temporarily increase cache capacity by 25% for affected shard group: k8s patch.
  3) If autoscaler misbehaving, cascade to manual scale up: runbook/kvs/manual-scale.
  4) Observe 10m; if hit ratio returns above baseline, plan a targeted rollout fix.

B) Model-quality regression (RLHF/eval failure)
- Trigger: quality monitors detect +10% failure rate against golden prompt-set.
- Steps:
  1) Route traffic to previous model version variant with fallback policy.
  2) Open regression ticket and attach evaluation artifacts and seed prompts.
  3) Notify product and research: sr_research@redwood.ai.

On-call rotations, handoffs and etiquette
- Rotation length: 7-day primary oncall blocks with 14-day shadow rotation for junior engineers.
- Handoff checklist (to be posted in Slack at shift change):
  - Confirm no active P0/P1 incidents assigned.
  - Share list of ongoing maintenance windows and scheduled rollouts.
  - Leave brief notes on hotspots (e.g., "KV shard 3 showing elevated GC, watch eviction rate").
- Quiet-window protocol: no major rollouts within primary oncall's first 12 hours unless pre-approved by SRE lead.

Game day design and scoring
- Frequency: quarterly team-wide game days; smaller tabletop run twice monthly for new hires.
- Scenario types: total-threshold outage, progressive degradation (latency oscillation), model-quality regression, cross-region failover.
- Scoring rubric (0–10) per scenario:
  - Detection speed (0–3): time from simulated fault to acknowledged alert.
  - Containment (0–3): mitigation applied correctly within target window.
  - Communication (0–2): customer status + internal bridge notes clarity.
  - After-action (0–2): quality of post-game retro and actionable items.

Postmortem rubric (must-haves)
- Executive summary (1–2 paragraphs)
- Chronological timeline with timestamps and evidence links
- Root cause analysis (5 whys or causal graph)
- Impact and blast radius calculation (tenant list, % of traffic, duration)
- Action items with owners and due dates (no more than 5 high-priority.
- Regressions/test coverage added and verification plan
- Severity classification and whether SLA credits are applicable

SLOs and thresholds (examples)
- Text generation latency SLO: p95 < 300ms (global), p99 < 750ms (regional)
- Error rate SLO: <0.5% (5m rolling) ; Alert if >1% sustained for 5 minutes
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for Redwood API (hosted)

CSR (customer status) lattice (templates)
- Tier A: brief holding message (for initial, uncertain impact)
  Subject: [Redwood] We are investigating degraded service for text-generation
  Body: We are aware of an issue affecting text-generation latency for some customers. Our engineers are investigating. We will provide updates in 30 minutes or sooner. No action required from customers at this time.

- Tier B: intermediate update (confirmed impact, mitigation in progress)
  Subject: [Redwood] Mitigation in progress for reduced throughput
  Body: We have identified a cause for reduced throughput in region us-west-2 and are applying a mitigation. Some requests may receive slower responses or fallbacks to a compatible model. We expect improvement within 60 minutes. If you require assistance, contact support@redwood.ai.

- Tier C: resolved (post-recovery)
  Subject: [Redwood] Issue resolved — text-generation service restored
  Body: The incident impacting text-generation has been resolved as of 15:24 UTC. We confirmed normal traffic patterns for 30 minutes and will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours. We apologize for the disruption.

Customer comms templates (CSR examples)
- Short in-incident update (10–30 min cadence):
  "We are continuing to investigate; current mitigation is to route affected requests to the fallback model. Next update in 30 minutes or when there is a material change."

- Escalation / SLA credit notice: include incident ID, duration, affected tenants, and next steps. Use legal@redwood.ai for approvals.

Operational checklists
- Evidence collection checklist (first 15 minutes): traces, sample requests/IDs, model version, deployment id, recent config changes (last 60m), KV cache snapshot.
- Post-incident closure checklist: confirm monitoring stable for 2x SLO window, close incident in PagerDuty, file postmortem draft and schedule review.

Appendix: quick commands & links
- Establish bridge: /tools/bridge/new --template "frc-standard" --service text-generation
- Snapshot logs: curl -s "https://loganvil/api/v1/query?service=text-generation&since=15m" > /tmp/tg-evidence.json
- Rollback model: rdm model rollback --service text-generation --to-version v2026-10-11

Ownership & escalation matrix (summary)
- Level 1 (FR): primary oncall -> #oncall; handles triage and containment.
- Level 2 (BO+SS): bridge operator and service steward -> run bridge and coordinate longer-term mitigations.
- Level 3 (Exec): SRE Director and Product Lead -> invoked for severe multi-customer P0s > 3 hours.

Related docs
- Incident command playbook and escalation matrix (link above)
- Runbook library: repo:/runbooks/oncall

Revision history
- 2025-06-12: Created (Maya Chen)
- 2026-11-03: Added CSR lattice and expanded game-day scoring (Maya Chen)

End of document

payload.page_title: Surge Capacity Sprint Playbook: Retail & Marketing Traffic Spikes

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines the on-call procedures, runbooks, communication templates, and post-incident analysis steps for rapid capacity surges driven by retail or marketing campaigns (flash sales, promotional emails, sponsored ad pushes). It focuses on containment, fast-path capacity ramp, graceful degradation for non-critical features, and customer communication. Use this when traffic grows 2x+ above normal sustained TPS for >5 minutes or when latency SLOs cross the warning threshold for core APIs.

Scope and assumptions

- Scope: Redwood public API endpoints (generation, embeddings, streaming), regional load balancers, autoscaler control plane, KV cache layer, and customer-facing status page.
- Assumptions: Autoscaling is enabled for affected fleets; dedicated capacity customers may be exempt; telemetry (awssignals / prometheus) is operational.
- Exclusions: Internal CI jobs, scheduled maintenance windows, or slow-degrading experiments are handled by separate maintenance runbooks.

Severity classification (specialized for surge events)

1) Surge-S1 — transient spike: short-lived spike ( < 10 minutes ), no SLO breach, warnings in latency percentiles.
2) Surge-S2 — sustained surge: >= 2x baseline for >= 10 minutes, 95th percentile latency > SLO but error rate < 0.5%.
3) Surge-S3 — capacity saturation: error rates > 0.5% and client-visible failures or denied capacity.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

1. Acknowledge alert and create an incident channel (Slack #inc-surge-<region>-<time>) and Zoom bridge.
2. Capture starter evidence (one-line): "What, where, when, impact" and pin to channel.
3. Identify the signal: traffic volume, RPC queue depth, GPU utilization, autoscaler events, upstream DDoS protection logs.
4. If traffic originates from a single customer or IP bloc, flag for tenant-aware mitigation (see Tenant Containment).
5. Start customer-facing status notice (template below) in draft.

Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Lead (first on-call): overall coordination, declaring severity, and customer notices.
- Capacity Engineer: tune autoscaler, provision burst pools, and perform pool-level restarts if needed.
- Routing/Edge Engineer: validate LB health, remove noisy backends, apply traffic shaping.
- Product Owner (on-call for product): approve graceful-degradation choices and feature toggles.
- Customer Success/Support Liaison: prepare customer-specific comms for affected accounts.

Containment steps (Surge-S2 / Surge-S3)

1) Fast-fail non-essential routes
   - For routes serving analytics, batch embeddings, or background tasks, toggle feature_gate=defer_background (example CLI):
     rdc toggle-feature --route "/v1/embeddings/batch" --flag defer_background --until 1h
   - Immediately disable optional streaming websockets for low-tier traffic.

2) Tenant containment
   - If a single tenant causes the spike: apply tenant throttles (soft limit 20 rps) and move to a dedicated rate-limited pool.
   - Commands:
     - List top tenants by qps: curl -s https://telemetry.internal/api/top-tenants | jq '.'
     - Apply throttle: rdc tenant-rate --tenant <id> --limit 20

3) Scale-up and pre-warm
   - Trigger manual burst capacity for the affected region (owner: Capacity Engineer).
   - AWS example: runbook includes IaC shortcut: terraform apply -var=\"burst=true\" -target=module.pools.burst
   - Pre-warm caches: run cache-warm job for the top N prefixes for expected inputs.

4) Backpressure and client hints
   - Emit 429 with Retry-After for best-effort degradations. Prefer 202/accepted for queued batch work.

Recovery and restoration steps

1. Confirm saturation has reduced for >2 consecutive 5-minute windows (traffic and GPU util).
2. Remove temporary throttles and feature gates in reverse order (document each change in channel).
3. Drain and decommission temporary burst nodes once warm utilization < 50% for 15 minutes.
4. Run sanity checks: sample a set of golden prompts across model families and validate p99 latency and correctness.

Operational playbook snippets and commands

- List affected autoscaler events: rdc autoscaler events --region us-west-2 --since 30m
- Promote burst pool: rdc pool promote --name burst-usw2 --until 02:00
- Re-route traffic away from unhealthy LB: rdc lb adjust --lb api-west --remove backend-id=be-1234

Customer and public status templates

Internal short status (first 15 minutes)

"Status: We are investigating a traffic surge impacting inference latency for US-West customers. Core APIs are slower than normal; some batch requests are queued. Incident lead: @<name>. Next update: in 15 minutes."

Public status page (short)

Title: "Degraded performance for inference in US-West due to unexpected traffic surge"
Impact: "Some requests may experience elevated latency or temporary queueing. A subset of background jobs may be delayed."
Mitigation: "We have enabled temporary burst capacity and are throttling non-essential routes to restore responsiveness."
Updates: "We will post updates every 15 minutes."

Customer-specific email template (for high-touch accounts)

Subject: "[Action Required] Temporary throughput controls during US-West traffic surge"
Body: "Hello <CustomerName>, we detected a significant traffic surge impacting your region and have applied temporary throughput controls to protect availability. Recommended actions: reduce parallel client threads and defer large batch submissions for 30–60 minutes. Our team is actively scaling and will follow up when controls are removed. — Redwood Inference Support"

Game day scenarios and exercises (recommended cadence: quarterly)

Scenario A — "BlackFriday Sim": synthetic traffic ramp 10x baseline with multi-tenant noisy neighbor injection. Objectives: verify tenant containment automation, autoscaler burst IRS, and status cadence.
Scenario B — "Promo Blast": A single high-traffic tenant ramps to 5x; objective: confirm tenant throttle workflow and customer comm loop.
Scenario C — "Cache Eviction Storm": KV cache misses lead to GPU pressure; objective: validate cache-warm and pre-warm scripts and golden prompt verification.

Exercise checklist (for each game day)

- Pre-game: validate telemetry pipelines, create synthetic keys, and reserve burst quota.
- During: time-boxed changes, one change per 5 minutes, record timestamps.
- Post-game: run the postmortem template below and publish learnings.

Post-incident analysis and postmortem template
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Incident timeline (UTC) with exact actions and authors.
- Telemetry graphs: TPS, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, GPU util, queue depth, autoscaler events.
- List of toggles/throttles and exact CLI commands used.
- Customer impact list (accounts with failed requests or elevated latencies).
- Root cause hypothesis and severity rationale.

Postmortem sections (copy into a standard page)

1. Summary — 1–2 sentence description and business impact.
2. Timeline — minute-by-minute sequence.
3. Impact — systems, customers, SLO breaches.
4. Root cause analysis — technical explanation and evidence.
5. Actions planned — owner, due date, verification criteria.
6. Retro notes — what worked, what didn't, and recommended game-day changes.

Example postmortem action items

- Automate tenant throttling into the autoscaler pipeline (owner: eng-serving-runtime; due: 2026-04-15).
- Instrument early-warning signal: moving-average QPS over 3 minutes (owner: eng-sre; due: 2026-03-31).
- Add a customer-visible field to status notices for high-touch accounts (owner: customer-success; due: 2026-04-07).

Runbook governance and maintenance

- This playbook must be reviewed after every Surge-S2 or Surge-S3 incident and during quarterly game days.
- Runbook owner: Capacity Engineering Guild. Review cadence: quarterly.

Appendix: quick decision ladder (one-liners)

- If p99 latency > 2x SLO and error rate < 0.5%: flip non-essential feature gates and trigger burst pool.
- If error rate > 0.5%: apply tenant containment and consider regional traffic re-route.
- If burst pool fails to provision in 10 minutes: escalate to infra on-call and prepare customer credit assessment.

Links and references

- Autoscaler runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/ci-cd-and-build/autoscaler-runbook-2025
- Tenant containment procedure: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/tenant-containment-manual-2024

Contact matrix (escalation)

- 0–10 minutes: Incident Lead (oncall-primary)
- 10–30 minutes: Add Capacity Engineer and Routing Engineer
- 30+ minutes: Pager to Eng Director and Customer Success Director

Change log

- 2026-01-15: Created by Priya Nambiar.
- 2026-02-10: Added tenant containment CLI snippets (reviewer: Liam).
- 2026-03-05: Added public status templates and game-day scenarios (reviewer: Sofia).

payload.page_title: Responder Operations Manual: Synthesized Procedures and Communication Templates

sections.body:
Summary

This document is a concise, operational manual for responders responsible for stabilizing Redwood Inference services during customer-impacting events. It synthesizes guidance across detection, triage, containment, stabilization, restoration, post-incident analysis, on-call rotations, and customer communications. The goal is fast, repeatable decision-making with clear accountability and artifact collection for downstream audits and postmortems.

Who should read this
- Primary: on-call responders and bridge operators (SRE, serving runtime, infra).
- Secondary: product incident liaisons, customer success leads, and engineering managers who will review postmortem artifacts.

Scope and goals
- Scope: production-facing degradations that affect latency, throughput, error rates, model quality regressions, or core control plane availability. Not a replacement for component-specific runbooks; see component runbook index for low-level commands.
- Goals: minimize customer-visible impact, preserve forensic evidence, communicate clearly, and generate a postmortem-ready artifact set.

Roles & responsibilities
- Bridge Operator (Bridge): runs the incident bridge, coordinates updates, and owns customer-facing cadence until handoff.
- Stabilizer: executes corrective actions (scaling, cache flushes, partial rollbacks) and reports progress.
- Escalation Owner: senior engineer who approves rollbacks, infra changes, or legal/security engagements.
- Scribe: records timeline, hypotheses tested, and telemetry snapshots.
- Customer Liaison: prepares and posts external status updates and coordinates with CS.

Incident lifecycle (high-level)
1) Detect: automated alert or customer report. Evidence: alert URL, example request IDs, and sample failing responses.
2) Acknowledge & Create Bridge: owner creates a bridge with subject line prefix: [STAB] <service> <symptom>.
3) Triage: classify severity, impact scope, and likely components (runtime, cache, control plane, network).
4) Contain: apply non-destructive mitigations to stop escalation (rate limit, circuit-break, disable integrations).
5) Stabilize: targeted fixes, Canary rollback, route traffic away, or scale capacity.
6) Recover: restore normal traffic patterns and monitor for regressions.
7) Post-effect: collect artifacts, runbook updates, and schedule postmortem.

Severity definitions and decision thresholds
- Sev3 (minor): small set of customers affected, degraded P95 latency > target by 2x for 5+ minutes.
- Sev2 (major): broad customer impact, error rate spike > 1% absolute or 5x baseline for 5+ minutes, or sustained P95 degradation > 3x.
- Sev1 (critical): total or near-total outage for a region or platform-wide control plane failure.

10-minute stabilization checklist (run immediately once bridge is up)
1) Bridge URL, pager owner, and short subject in bridge title.
2) Quick evidence capture: list 3 representative request IDs, link to alert, and paste CLI output for service status.
3) Short customer-facing statement: "We are investigating elevated errors/latency for <service>. Initial mitigation in progress."
4) Apply containment: incremental throttles, disable non-essential integrations, or move traffic to healthy pool.
5) Identify one tactical action to try next (scale, cache clear, rollback).

Decision matrix (text table)
Trigger | Immediate containment | Next action owner
"Error rate spike > 5x" | Activate per-tenant throttles; enable degraded-mode | Stabilizer
"KV cache hot miss storm" | Reduce TTLs; promote healthy cache nodes | Stabilizer
"Model quality regression (high hallucination)" | Route to validated fallback model; pause model rollout | Escalation Owner

Escalation ladder (contact sequence)
1) On-call responder (primary pager)
2) Service lead (phone)
3) Platform SRE lead (if >15 minutes without stabilization)
4) CTO/VP Eng (for Sev1 or sustained outage >60 minutes)

Customer-facing status templates
- Initial (first 15 minutes):
Subject: Service degradation for <service> — investigating
Body: We are investigating elevated errors/latency affecting <service> in <region>. Engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will post an update within 15 minutes.

- Update (progress):
Subject: Update: <service> degradation — partial mitigation in place
Body: We implemented <mitigation>. Error rate reduced from X% to Y%. Some customers may still see intermittent issues. ETA for full restoration: ~30 minutes.

- Resolution:
Subject: Resolved: <service> — normal operation restored
Body: The issue impacting <service> has been resolved as of <timestamp UTC>. Root cause analysis is underway; we will follow up with a postmortem. If you continue to see issues please reply to this message or open a support ticket.

- Follow-up postmortem notice:
Subject: Postmortem scheduled for <service> incident on <date>
Body: We will publish the postmortem by <date>. Action items and mitigation plan will be included.

Evidence & artifact checklist (required for all Sev2/Sev1)
- Alert URL(s) and timestamps
- Representative request IDs and full request/response payloads (redact PII)
- Dashboard links pinned to the bridge
- Core dump/log bundles or AWS/GCP diagnostic snapshots
- A list of commands executed (with timestamps) and the person who ran them

Minimum runbook fragments to attach for common faults
- High error rate:
  - Commands: "kubectl get pods -n serving"; "rds-cli describe-connections --filter service=<service>"
  - Dashboards: Serving P95 latency, error-rate by model, recent deploys table
- Cache storm:
  - Commands: "redis-cli INFO"; "prometheus query: sum(rate(redis_command_duration_seconds_count[1m])) by (instance)"
  - Short fix: "Increase read-replicas; evict largest keys carefully using ITERATE/EVICT script"
- Model quality regression:
  - Commands: "rollout manager rollback --model <id> --to-version <prior>"; add telemetry for model-score drift

Postmortem & follow-up process
- Timeline: publish draft within 72 hours; final postmortem and action item list within 10 business days.
- Required sections: Summary, Impact, Root cause, Timeline of decisions, Mitigations applied, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Detection gap, Preventative measures.
- Severity review committee: for Sev1 incidents, at least one SRE, one product manager, and one CS lead must review the draft.

On-call rotation guidance and handoff checklist
- Rotation length: typical 7 days for primary responder, 14 days for supporting buckets.
- Shadowing: new responders shadow for 2 full rotations before independently owning critical bridges.
- Handoff checklist (to be run at shift change):
  1) Confirm no active bridges or escalate if unresolved.
 2) Share list of outstanding action items (owner + ETA).
 3) Provide any live tickets or ongoing communications with customers.
 4) Confirm monitoring subscriptions and pager escalation targets.

Game day recipes (low-overhead exercises teams can run monthly)
- KV cache eviction storm: simulate cache thrash against staging cluster, practice containment (throttle, promote replicas). Success criteria: restore P95 within 20 minutes without full restart.
- Canary model rollback: rollout a model with injected bad responses, validate rollback steps and customer routing. Success criteria: rollback completes and no customer requests hit faulty model after 10 minutes.
- Rate-limit cascade: artificially apply a tenant-level throttle and verify upstream controllers obey circuit-breakers and SLOs. Success criteria: no global outage; automated alerts produce a useful signal.

Evidence collection SOP for audits and enterprise customers
1) Export dashboards as PNG and CSV and upload to bridge notes immediately.
2) Attach zipped log bundle with a README of time windows used.
3) Sanitize customer data using the sanitization script: "scripts/sanitize-logs --from <t1> --to <t2> --redact-keys email,ssn"

Maintenance windows and restoration cadence (policy)
- Rolling maintenance: prefer rolling capacity upgrades with live health checks.
- Forced restoration windows: for customer-impacting fixes that require downtime, coordinate with CS and give minimum 72 hours notice for enterprise customers.

Appendix: sample internal bridge transcript template
- Header: Bridge URL, Incident ID, Severity, Initial symptom
- Timeline entries: timestamp | actor | action | result | evidence link
  - Example: 2026-02-05T15:12Z | Maya Chen | scaled serving pool +20% | P95 reduced 35% | link to dashboard

Appendix: quick commands and common dashboards (copy-paste)
- Get serving pods: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide
- Check autoscaler: redwoodctl autoscale status --service <service>
- Prometheus query: sum(rate(http_server_errors_total[1m])) by (service)

Related resources and ownership
- Component runbook index: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/index
- SLO & escalation policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2025
- Playbook maintenance: owners of this document should review after every Sev2/Sev1 and update within 7 days.

End of document

payload.page_title: Cobalt bridge operator manual and escalation FAQ

sections.body: This page documents the 'Cobalt' bridge variant: a pre-authorized, lightweight incident bridge pattern for short-duration multi-team escalations (SRE + Customer Success + Platform). Cobalt is intended for events where rapid coordination and a single accountable bridge operator are required, but a full executive bridge is not yet warranted.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Reduce time-to-first-action for customer-impacting spikes by 40% compared to ad-hoc DMs.
- Provide a minimal, repeatable operator checklist that works across multi-tenant model-serving and dedicated capacity incidents.
- Standardize customer-facing status templates for low-latency public updates.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
1) Any incident where a single bridge operator plus SRE and CS must coordinate live for >15 minutes and <3 hours.
2) Latency SLO breach affecting >=5% of active requests for 10 minutes.
3) Repeated 503 errors on generation endpoints with no clear single-service root cause.
4) Customer-visible errors reported by multiple unrelated tenants.
sections.heading: When to open a Cobalt bridge (criteria)

sections.body:
- Regulatory/legal-impacting incidents (open a formal executive bridge).
- Long-running outages expected >3 hours (escalate to full incident command).
- Incidents confined to a single repo-level rollout where the owning team can manage via their team runbook.
sections.heading: When NOT to open a Cobalt bridge

sections.body:
1) Acknowledge and claim the Cobalt bridge in PagerDuty; set bridge channel to #cobalt-bridge-<region> and create the temporary bridge channel.
2) Triage initial impact: run `cobalt-scan` (internal CLI) to collect top signals: request-rate, 99th/95th latency, CPU/GPU utilization. Example: `cobalt-scan --service=serving-runtime --window=10m`
3) Post initial customer-facing status (see templates below) within 10 minutes of bridge open.
4) Convene SRE + CS + Platform in the bridge channel and assign roles: operator (single), comms, evidence collector, remediation lead.
5) Execute fast mitigations in order (see ordered checklist below). Track each action in the incident timeline.
6) If mitigations fail within 30 minutes and incident severity increases, escalate to a full Incident Command (see Escalation Matrix).
7) When service is stabilized, run the Cobalt closure checklist and schedule a 24–72 hour follow-up: short incident review (not a full postmortem unless required).

Fast mitigation ordered checklist (apply top-to-bottom until impact reduces):
- Step 1: Apply circuit-breaker routing to reduce noisy tenancy: `route-weight set --service=frontdoor --tenant=NOISY_TENANT --weight=0.0`
- Step 2: Temporarily pin affected requests to a lower-cost variant with higher concurrency limits.
- Step 3: Scale up Dedicated pool by +20% using the autoscale override API.
- Step 4: Enable KV-cache fallback for common prefixes (reduce model decode work).
- Step 5: Throttle non-critical background jobs that consume KV/cache bandwidth.
sections.heading: Operator playbook (step-by-step)

sections.body:
| Severity | Trigger window | Initial responder | Escalation target |
|---|---:|---|---|
| P3 (cobalt) | 10–30m customer impact <10% | Bridge operator + SRE | Keep as Cobalt; optional EM notify |
| P2 (cobalt->ic) | >30m or impact >=10% | Bridge operator + SRE + CS | Incident Commander (IC) -> full bridge |
| P1 (exec) | region-wide outage, high business impact | IC + Exec comms | Exec bridge, on-call leadership, legal as required |

Note: escalation must be enacted automatically if metrics cross thresholds; the bridge operator declares escalation and tags PagerDuty with `escalation:automatic` when threshold is exceeded.
sections.heading: Escalation matrix (severity thresholds and handoffs)

sections.body:
- Bridge operator: single point of coordination, owns the bridge lifecycle.
- Remediation lead: drives technical fixes and rollbacks.
- Comms lead: crafts public and customer notices using templates below.
- Evidence collector: captures logs, traces, and KV/cache snapshot for post-incident analysis.

Evidence collection checklist (minimum items to attach to incident):
- Timeline (UTC) of actions and observed metrics (10m resolution).
- `serving-runtime` traces for 5 example failed requests (include request_id).
- Hotspot profile: GPU/CPU per-host over the incident window (top 10 hosts).
- KV cache hit-rate and eviction logs.
- Snapshot of routing table and weight overrides.

Status page & external customer templates (use verbatim, fill placeholders):
- Initial public status (within 10m):
"We are experiencing elevated latency on model inference in <region>. Our team is actively investigating. No customer data loss is expected. Updates every 15 minutes."

- Follow-up (when mitigation in progress):
"We have applied targeted routing and capacity measures to reduce impact. Some customers may see improved latency. We will provide another update at <hh:mm UTC>."

- Resolution message:
"The service is restored in <region>. Root cause analysis will be published to affected customers within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, please open a ticket with request_id=<REQUEST_ID>."
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities (one-liners)

sections.body:
"Hi <Customer Name>,
We detected elevated latency affecting your requests originating from <region>. Our on-call team opened a Cobalt bridge and applied routing mitigations; you should see improvements. We will follow up with a root cause summary within 72 hours.
Regards,
Redwood Support"

Status page payload example (JSON, for automation):
`{
  "page": "status.redwood.ai",
  "component": "model-inference/<region>",
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "update_body": "Elevated latency observed; mitigation in progress (Cobalt bridge open).",
  "notify_customers": ["tenant:12345"]
}`

Game day checklist (30–60 minute exercise to validate Cobalt flows):
- Pre-game: pick a low-risk service and schedule a 60m slot; notify observers.
- Inject: small, targeted latency spike via controlled canary traffic to the chosen service.
- Operator: open Cobalt bridge, run `cobalt-scan`, post initial status.
- Roles: verify SRE/CS/Platform assignment and comms cadence.
- Exercise automation: confirm `route-weight set` and autoscale override runbook succeed.
- Evidence: collect logs and validate evidence collector template.
- Retro: 30m retro using the template at the end; publish findings.
sections.heading: Customer-specific email snippet (short)

sections.body:
1) Update timeline and outstanding actions.
2) Confirm next check-in times and escalate points.
3) Transfer ownership in PagerDuty and Slack bridge with `@handoff` message including summary.
4) If remaining risk exists, schedule a 1-hour watch with a named owner.
sections.heading: Handoff checklist (end of shift or operator transfer)

sections.body:
- `cobalt-scan` — collects telemetry and writes a YAML summary to `/tmp/cobalt-<timestamp>.yml`.
- `route-weight` — routing control utility (see `route-weight --help`).
- `status-publish` — posts to status page using the JSON payload format above.
- `evidence-collector` — wrapper that bundles logs/traces and uploads to secure incident vault.
sections.heading: Automations and tooling (quick reference)

sections.body:
- Cobalt incidents that lasted >30 minutes or resulted in customer-visible errors require a short incident review (template linked).
- If the review surfaces a systemic risk (rollout bug, scaling misconfiguration), escalate to a full postmortem and include affected model versions and rollout IDs.
- All Cobalt evidence bundles must be retained for 180 days and classified internal.
sections.heading: Runbook retention and post-incident follow-up policy

sections.body:
Q: Can we use Cobalt for a planned maintenance window?
A: No — use maintenance channels; Cobalt is for unplanned rapid coordination.

Q: Who authorizes a Cobalt bridge closure?
A: The bridge operator closes the bridge after remediation lead confirms stable metrics for 10 consecutive minutes and comms lead has posted an external status.

Q: How do we decide between Cobalt and a full Incident Command?
A: Follow the Escalation Matrix thresholds. If impact is trending upward or customer SLA exposure is high, escalate.
sections.heading: FAQ (quick answers)

sections.body:
- Incident timeline template: `/templates/cobalt/timeline.md`
- Evidence bundle uploader: `/tools/evidence-collector`
- Bridge operator quick-start cheatsheet: `/playbooks/bridge-quickstart`
sections.heading: Related templates and links

sections.body:
- Document owner: Maya Chen (SRE, Incident Ops).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P2/P1 escalation where Cobalt was used.

Time (UTC) | Action | Actor | Notes
-----------|--------|-------|------

2024-09-14T10:05Z | Cobalt bridge opened | Bridge operator | #cobalt-bridge-us

End of document."

payload.page_title: Status Page and Incident Comms: Guidance for Rollout-Related Issues

sections.body:
h1. Purpose
This page explains when a rollout issue should be communicated via the status page and how to coordinate communications during a rollback or prolonged fallback.

h1. Definitions
* Rollout issue: any degradation caused by a planned model version change, routing change, or runtime configuration update.
* Incident: a customer-impacting event that meets the incident declaration criteria.

h1. When to post a status page update
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
* Any widespread Hosted API impact lasting > 15 minutes (elevated 5xx, timeouts, or severe latency)
* Any Dedicated customer experiences SLA-impacting degradation and requests formal comms
* Any Private customer experiences impact outside the approved change window
* A rollback is initiated after > 25% traffic ramp OR after any customer notification has been sent

h1. Required content of a rollout-related status update
sections.heading: Post a status page update if any of the following occur

sections.body:
* What users are experiencing (symptoms)
* Impacted surfaces (Hosted/Dedicated/Private, regions, request types)
* Current mitigation (automatic fallback active, manual rollback in progress, traffic capped)
* Next update time (commit to a timestamp)
* Where customers can get support

h1. Coordination model
* Incident Commander (IC): owns the status page message content and cadence.
* Customer Success: owns account-specific communications for Dedicated/Private.
* Engineering owner: provides technical updates and ETA for rollback.

h1. Rollback comms
sections.heading: Include

sections.body:
1. Notify #incidents and #support with a short summary and mitigation step.
2. Update the rollout plan with the rollback trigger and time.
3. If the status page is used, explicitly state that we reverted to the prior model version (avoid internal ids unless customers pin versions).

h1. After-action requirements
If a rollout issue required status page comms, the associated postmortem MUST link to:
* the rollout plan
* router policy ids (old/new)
* the thresholds that triggered rollback
* customer communications artifacts (tickets/emails)

payload.page_title: Planned Maintenance and Change Communications

sections.body:
h1. Summary
This page defines RedwoodInferences requirements for communicating planned maintenance and production changes that may impact customers. It also describes internal communication expectations for changes with no expected customer impact.

h1. Scope
Applies to production changes for Hosted API and Console. For Private deployments, coordinate with Customer Success and follow the customer-specific comms plan.

h1. When customer communications are required
Customer communications are required if any of the following are true:
* Any expected downtime, degraded performance, or increased error rates
* Any planned breaking change to APIs, SDK behavior, auth, rate limits, or quotas
* Any change that may cause delayed/duplicate billing events or usage reporting gaps
* Any region-level maintenance that reduces redundancy

h1. Lead time requirements
* Minor maintenance (no downtime expected, small perf risk): publish status page notice \u2265 24 hours before start.
* Major maintenance (possible downtime/degradation): publish status page notice \u2265 72 hours before start and email impacted customers.
* Emergency maintenance: publish as soon as practical with clear reason and mitigation.

h1. Required information in customer-facing comms
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. What is happening (plain language)
2. Expected impact (what will customers observe)
3. Start time, end time, and timezone
4. Affected products (Hosted API, Console) and regions
5. Mitigation steps customers can take (if any)
6. Where to get updates (status page link)
7. How to contact support (support email / portal)

h1. Internal communications (always required)
For all production changes, post a heads-up in #eng-releases with:
* Change record link
* Owner and approver(s)
* Services/regions
* Canary plan
* Rollback trigger

h1. Status page workflow
1. Draft maintenance notice using the template below.
2. Have on-call IC or SRE on-call review for accuracy when the change is SLO-sensitive.
3. Publish and schedule updates at least every 60 minutes during the window (or more frequently if issues).

h1. Template: Maintenance notice
Title: Planned maintenance for {Product} in {Region}
Body: We will perform planned maintenance on {date/time}. During this window, you may experience {impact}. We will post updates at {status page link}. If you need assistance, contact {support}.

h1. Post-maintenance closure
After completion, publish a final update including:
* Confirmation that maintenance is complete
* Any residual customer actions required
* Summary of observed impact (if any)

h1. Related pages
* Production Change Management Standard (v2)
* Rollback and Post-change Validation
