payload.page_title: Dedicated Capacity Usage Meter Definition (GPU-seconds)

sections.body:
This document defines how Redwood Inference meters **Dedicated Capacity** usage for billing, revenue recognition support, and customer-facing usage reporting. The unit for Dedicated usage is **GPU-seconds**.

This definition is intentionally precise because small ambiguities (e.g., how idle time is counted, autoscaling transitions, or node flaps) can create invoice disputes and RevRec risk.

**Audience:** Finance/RevRec, Legal, RevOps, Product, and Engineering (Telemetry + Control Plane).

---
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Dedicated GPU pools provisioned to a single customer (data isolated).
- Metered usage for:
  - Overage beyond reserved commits (if applicable)
  - Burst capacity (if enabled)
  - Usage visibility and forecasting (even when fully covered by commit)
- Per-pool and per-day aggregation for invoices and usage exports.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- Hosted API token/request meters (see Hosted API meter spec).
- Private/on-prem deployments where billing is license/support-based (separate contract terms).

---
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
A **Dedicated Pool** is an isolated capacity group (e.g., `pool_id`) for a customer in a region, with a GPU type and an autoscaling policy.

**Examples:**
- `acme-prod-us-east-1-a100-80gb`
- `zenchat-eu-west-1-l40s`
sections.heading: Dedicated Pool

sections.body: A **Reserved Commit** is the contracted baseline capacity the customer pays for regardless of utilization.
sections.heading: Reserved Commit (Commercial)

sections.body:
- **Committed GPUs per pool** (e.g., 8x A100) with a fixed monthly fee.
- Optional **Burst**: additional GPUs beyond commit billed by usage.

Important: The **GPU-seconds meter measures usage**, but the customer may still pay for unused reserved capacity via their commit fee. Unused reserved capacity is not refunded unless explicitly stated in the Order Form.
sections.heading: Common contract structures

sections.body: A **GPU-second** is one GPU allocated to the customer’s Dedicated pool for one second.
sections.heading: GPU-second (Meter Unit)

sections.body:
- Let `allocated_gpus(t)` be the number of GPUs in the pool that are in an **Allocated** state at time `t`.
- Over a billing interval `[T0, T1)`, usage is:

`gpu_seconds = ∫(from T0 to T1) allocated_gpus(t) dt`

This integrates across autoscaling changes; a pool can contribute varying GPU counts over time.
sections.heading: Formal definition (per pool)

sections.body:
A GPU is **Allocated** to a pool if it is:
- Provisioned and attached to the customer’s Dedicated pool, and
- In a serving-capable state (including warm standby), such that Redwood holds it exclusively for that pool.
sections.heading: Allocated GPU (Operational)

sections.body:
- **Active/Serving** nodes (taking traffic)
- **Warm/Ready** nodes (ready to serve, held for fast scale-up)
sections.heading: Allocated includes

sections.body:
- **Provisioning** (cloud instance requested but not yet attached to the pool)
- **Deallocating/Terminating** (released from pool; see end-time rule below)
- **Maintenance/Unavailable** where Redwood has removed the GPU from the customer pool (counts as not allocated)

---
sections.heading: Allocated excludes

sections.body: To eliminate ambiguity and reduce over/under-counting during autoscaling transitions, GPU-seconds v2 uses control-plane state transitions as the primary signal.
sections.heading: State model and timing rules (GPU-seconds v2)

sections.body:
A node/GPU allocation for a pool should be modeled with these timestamps:
- `allocated_at`: time the GPU becomes allocated to the pool (exclusive hold begins)
- `deallocated_at`: time the GPU ceases to be allocated to the pool (exclusive hold ends)
sections.heading: Control-plane states (simplified)

sections.body: - Count GPU-seconds from `allocated_at` (inclusive) to `deallocated_at` (exclusive).
sections.heading: Metering rule

sections.body:
Set `allocated_at` at the first time the node meets BOTH:
1) Control plane assigns it to the pool (pool attachment is complete), AND
2) Node reports `READY` (or equivalent) to the pool manager.

Rationale: we do not bill the customer for time prior to the pool actually holding the GPU for them.
sections.heading: Effective allocation start (allocated_at)

sections.body:
Set `deallocated_at` at the first time any of these occurs:
- Control plane detaches the node from the pool, OR
- Node is marked `UNALLOCATED` / `RELEASED` by the pool manager, OR
- The node is placed into a Redwood maintenance quarantine (not exclusive to the customer)

Rationale: once Redwood no longer holds the GPU exclusively for the customer’s pool, it should not be billed.
sections.heading: Effective allocation end (deallocated_at)

sections.body:
- If a node temporarily stops heartbeating but remains assigned to the pool, it remains allocated **up to a maximum grace period**.
- Default grace period: **120 seconds**.
- After grace period, the node is considered **not allocated** until it returns to `READY`.

This rule prevents billing from continuing indefinitely due to missing telemetry while still tolerating short blips.

---
sections.heading: Handling node flaps and missing heartbeats

sections.body:
- Raw computation: second-level intervals derived from `(allocated_at, deallocated_at)`.
- Storage/aggregation for billing export: minute-level rollups (sum of seconds), then daily/monthly totals.
sections.heading: Meter granularity

sections.body:
- Internal storage retains integer GPU-seconds.
- Customer-facing exports may include minute-level rows; totals are exact sums (no rounding beyond integer seconds).
sections.heading: Rounding

sections.body:
GPU-seconds are computed and reported **per pool**. Invoice presentation may group pools by:
- Customer account
- Region
- GPU type
- Contract line item

---
sections.heading: Per-pool aggregation

sections.body:
1) **Commit fee** (fixed): based on committed GPUs and term
2) **Usage overage** (variable): based on metered GPU-seconds above included amount (if applicable)
sections.heading: Dedicated bills are typically composed of

sections.body:
- `included_gpu_seconds` = `committed_gpus * seconds_in_billing_period`
- `billed_overage_gpu_seconds` = `max(0, metered_gpu_seconds - included_gpu_seconds)`
sections.heading: Definitions used in invoicing

sections.body: - Some contracts treat commit as “reserved access” and do not define an “included” usage bucket; in those cases, GPU-seconds are used for transparency and forecasting, and overage billing may be driven only by burst usage. Always reconcile to the Order Form.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body: Burst means the pool is allowed to scale above its committed GPU baseline.
sections.heading: Burst rules (if enabled)

sections.body:
- GPUs within committed baseline are covered by commit fee.
- GPUs above committed baseline contribute to **burst GPU-seconds**, billed at the burst overage rate.
sections.heading: Billing behavior

sections.body:
- We compute total `metered_gpu_seconds`.
- We also compute `burst_gpu_seconds` by subtracting baseline capacity per second:

`burst_gpu_seconds = ∫ max(0, allocated_gpus(t) - committed_gpus) dt`

If `committed_gpus` changes mid-period (contract amendment), apply the new baseline effective at its contract start time.
sections.heading: Operationally

sections.body:
Idle time is billed when the GPU is allocated to the customer pool, regardless of request volume.

This is intentional and aligns with the Dedicated product promise: capacity is held for the customer to guarantee throughput/latency.

---
sections.heading: Idle accounting

sections.body:
- Pool holds 4 GPUs continuously from 10:00:00 to 11:00:00

`gpu_seconds = 4 GPUs * 3600 seconds = 14,400 GPU-seconds`

If the customer’s commit is 4 GPUs:
- `included_gpu_seconds` for that hour = 14,400
- `billed_overage_gpu_seconds` = 0
sections.heading: Example 1: Fixed 4-GPU pool for 1 hour

sections.body: Committed baseline = 2 GPUs.
sections.heading: Example 2: Autoscaling up/down with burst enabled

sections.body:
- 12:00:00–12:10:00 allocated 2 GPUs
- 12:10:00–12:25:00 allocated 6 GPUs
- 12:25:00–12:30:00 allocated 3 GPUs
sections.heading: Timeline

sections.body:
- Pool configured with min size 2 GPUs; receives no traffic for 6 hours
- GPUs remain `READY`
sections.heading: Example 3: Warm/Ready capacity (no traffic)

sections.body:
- `gpu_seconds = 2 * (6 * 3600) = 43,200 GPU-seconds`

Rationale: Redwood is reserving and operating capacity.

---
sections.heading: We still bill

sections.body:
If a scale-up is requested at 09:00 but the node attaches and becomes READY at 09:06:
- Do NOT bill 09:00–09:06
- Bill from 09:06 onward
sections.heading: 1) Provisioning delays

sections.body:
If a node stops accepting traffic at 18:00:00 (draining) but remains exclusively held and attached until 18:05:00:
- Continue billing until deallocation (18:05:00)
sections.heading: 2) Deallocation during draining

sections.body:
If a node heartbeats are missing for 45 seconds but it remains assigned and returns to READY:
- Continue billing (within grace period)
sections.heading: 3) Temporary health flaps

sections.body:
- Stop billing after 120 seconds of missing heartbeat
- Resume when READY returns
sections.heading: If missing for 5 minutes

sections.body:
Usage events must be idempotent.
- Dedupe key (conceptual): `(pool_id, node_id, allocated_at, deallocated_at, meter_version)`
- Any replays/backfills must not double-count.
sections.heading: 4) Control plane retries / duplicate events

sections.body: If committed GPUs change mid-period, baseline subtraction for burst calculations must apply the correct baseline per second (effective date/time from the amendment).
sections.heading: 5) Mid-month contract changes

sections.body:
- The invoice line item must reference the amendment effective date.
- Reconciliation exports must retain the baseline schedule used.
sections.heading: Finance requirement

sections.body:
If Redwood removes capacity from the customer pool (maintenance quarantine, hardware failure replacement):
- Stop billing for the removed GPUs at quarantine time.
- If contract includes uptime/SLA credits, handle separately per SLA policy; do not “silently” adjust the meter.
sections.heading: 6) Maintenance and Redwood-caused unavailability

sections.body: Dedicated pools currently bill in whole GPUs unless explicitly contracted otherwise.
sections.heading: 7) Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) / fractional GPUs

sections.body:
- The meter must support fractional `allocated_gpus(t)`.
- GPU-seconds become a real number (still aggregated precisely).
- Contracts and invoices must explicitly define fractional units.
sections.heading: If fractional allocations are introduced

sections.body:
If a customer has pools in multiple regions and traffic fails over:
- Meter each pool independently.
- If failover causes temporary double allocation (both pools held), both are billed unless contract includes explicit DR standby provisions.

---
sections.heading: 8) Cross-region failover

sections.body: - Control plane pool membership and readiness transitions.
sections.heading: Primary signals (v2)

sections.body:
- A stable reconciliation table/export including:
  - `account_id`, `pool_id`, `region`, `gpu_type`
  - `meter_version`
  - `gpu_seconds_total`, `burst_gpu_seconds` (if applicable)

payload.page_title: Billing Adjustments, Credit Memo & Invoice Dispute SOP

sections.body:
Overview

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describes the end-to-end process for handling billing adjustments, credit memos, and customer invoice disputes. It clarifies ownership, expected timelines, accounting treatment, and controls to ensure accurate revenue recognition and timely customer service. This document applies to all Redwood Inference invoiced customers and internal chargeback corrections.

Scope

- Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private billing events (usage, reserved capacity, overages, and manual credits).
- Excludes refunds for hardware procurement; hardware/vendor refunds follow procurement SOPs.

Definitions

1) Invoice dispute: A formal challenge by a customer about an invoice line or total.
2) Credit memo: An accounting document issued to reduce receivable/invoice amount.
3) Billing adjustment: Internal change to a posted invoice or account (example: misapplied credits, duplicate charges).
4) AR hold: Temporary suspension of collection while dispute is being investigated.

Responsibilities and RACI

- Customer Success: First-line intake for disputes and communication owner until resolution.
- Billing & Finance (AR team): Owns investigation, approves accounting entries, issues credit memos and posts adjustments.
- Legal: Reviews disputes that meet contract escalation criteria or potential legacy liability.
- Sales/Account Exec: Confirms contract terms and pricing for commercial exceptions.
- Engineering/Platform: Provides usage logs, model-run traces, and config snapshots for technical disputes.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Receive dispute: Customer Success (R) / Billing (A)
- Investigate: Billing (R) / Engineering (C) / Sales (C)
- Approve credit: Billing Finance (A) / Legal (C for >$50k or multi-period)
- Issue credit memo: Billing Finance (R/A)
- Post accounting entry: Finance GL Team (R)

SLA Targets

- Acknowledgement to customer: within 24 business hours.
- Initial investigation complete: within 5 business days.
- Resolution (credit issued or decision communicated): within 15 business days for standard disputes.
- Complex/escalated disputes involving contract/legal review: target 30 calendar days.

Intake and Triage (Step-by-step)

1) Intake: Customer opens a ticket via Support Portal or emails billing@redwood.ai. Customer Success creates a Dispute Case in the Billing Disputes queue with the following minimum fields: customer_id, invoice_id, disputed_amount, reason_code (choose from: usage_discrepancy, pricing_error, duplicate_charge, credit_application, tax_issue, other), and supporting documents.

2) Triage by Customer Success (within 24 business hours):
   - Verify receipt and confirm customer contact details.
   - Assign priority code: P1 (>= $50k or business-impacting), P2 ($5k–$50k or product-impacting), P3 (< $5k).
   - For P1/P2, notify Billing & Finance and Sales immediately.

3) Create investigation ticket in Finance case system (NetSuite/Chargebee/AR sub-ledger) and link to Support ticket.

Investigation Checklist (Billing & Finance)

For each dispute, follow these steps and document findings in the finance case record:

- Step A: Validate invoice data
  - Confirm invoice date, billing period, plan/sku, rate card used, and tax calculation.
  - Verify invoice was generated against customer-specified pricing table and approved contract amendment (if any).

- Step B: Reproduce usage charge (if applicable)
  - Request engineering export: usage_details.csv containing columns: timestamp, model_id, cpu_gpu_seconds, tokens_in, tokens_out, route_id, request_id.
  - Use the following sample SQL to cross-check billed tokens against usage exports:

    SELECT invoice_id, SUM(billed_tokens) as billed_tokens, SUM(actual_tokens) as actual_tokens
    FROM billing_exports
    WHERE customer_id = '<<customer_id>>' AND invoice_period = '<<YYYY-MM>>'
    GROUP BY invoice_id;

- Step C: Check for applied credits or promos
  - Confirm if automatic credits (trial credits, promotional discounts, reserved capacity amortization) were applied.

- Step D: Check for double billing / system error
  - Search for duplicate invoice numbers or repeated job runs within 1 hour of each other.

Approval Matrix and GL Treatment

- Credits under $1,000: Billing Finance Lead approval.
- Credits $1,000–$50,000: Finance Manager + Billing Lead approval.
- Credits >$50,000 or multi-period impact: Finance Director + Legal review required.
sections.heading: RACI summary

sections.body:
- Issuing a credit memo that reduces Accounts Receivable (AR):
  - Debit Revenue Reduction (GL 4012)
  - Credit Accounts Receivable (GL 1201)

- If cash was already collected and refund is required:
  - Debit Cash/Bank (GL 1001)
  - Credit AR (GL 1201) and record refund reason code.

Revenue recognition impact

- Short-term billing corrections (credit memo applied within same reporting period as invoice): recognize as contra-revenue in the same period.
- Adjustments that affect prior-period recognized revenue (post-close): require an adjusting journal entry and disclosure per accounting policy. Legal and Finance must be notified; threshold for disclosure: cumulative impact > $250k.

Issuing a Credit Memo

1) Prepare credit memo form in AR system with: credit_memo_id, original_invoice_id, credit_amount, reason_code, approver_id, accounting_impact (GL lines), and memo_text.
2) Attach supporting documents: investigation summary, engineering usage extracts, and customer confirmation message.
3) Post the credit memo and generate PDF copy for customer.
4) Notify Customer Success and Sales that the credit has been issued and update case status to Resolved.

Dispute Escalation to Legal

Escalate to Legal when any of the following criteria are met:
- Potential liability or credits > $50,000.
- Dispute involves contract interpretation (billing term ambiguity, SLA credits claimed beyond standard policy).
- Customer threatens litigation or contract termination.
sections.heading: Accounting entries (examples)

sections.body:
- Provide formal response templates, evaluate contract language, and recommend hold/settlement terms.

Special Cases and Examples

Example A — Usage discrepancy (customer claims over-billing):
1. Engineering provides request-level logs and token counts for the disputed window.
2. Billing Finance recalculates billed tokens using rate card; discrepancy confirmed = 2% billed overage due to parser bug.
3. Approver signs credit for the prorated overage. Credit memo issued and contra-revenue posted.

Example B — Contracted reserved capacity misapplied:
1. Sales confirms a signed PO for Dedicated capacity with a different amortization start date.
2. Billing identifies 3 months of misapplied usage at on-demand rates.
3. Finance issues credit for differential and adjusts future invoices to reflect correct amortization.

Controls and Audit Trail

- Every credit memo must reference an investigation case id and have at least one supporting document attached.
- Approvals recorded via e-signature or system approval workflow.
- Quarterly audit: Random sample of 10% of credit memos and top-10 credits by dollar value reviewed by Internal Audit and Head of Finance.

Reporting and Metrics
sections.heading: Legal will

sections.body:
- Open disputes (count) and age distribution
- Time to resolution (median and 90th percentile)
- Total credits issued (YTD) and as % of gross billings
- Top 10 dispute reasons by volume and by amount
sections.heading: Key metrics maintained in the Billing Dashboard

sections.body:
SELECT reason_code, COUNT(1) AS disputes, SUM(credit_amount) AS total_credit
FROM `redwood-billing.procedures.credit_memos`
WHERE DATE(issued_at) BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY total_credit DESC;

Operational Checklist for Customer Success (closing loop)

1. Confirm customer received credit memo PDF.
2. Confirm invoice status is Updated/Closed in the customer portal.
3. Update renewal or committed capacity calculations if dispute impacts committed usage.

Access, Segregation of Duties, and System Notes

- Billing creation and approval capabilities are separated: AR clerks can draft credit memos but cannot approve above their approval limit.
- Journals that impact prior-period revenue require Director-level signoff.
- System logs retained for 7 years in accordance with retention policy.

Customer Communication Templates (summary)

- Acknowledgement (24h): "We received your dispute for invoice INV-<<id>>. Our team is reviewing and will update you within 5 business days. Case: CASE-<<id>>."
- Resolution with credit: "We issued credit memo CM-<<id>> for $<<amount>>. Attached is the PDF and applied ledger entries. If you have questions, contact billing@redwood.ai."

FAQ (short)

Q: Will a dispute place my account on hold?
A: Only if the dispute is P1 or there is an active AR hold by the finance team. Customer Success will notify you.

Q: Does a credit memo change my contract?
A: No — credit memos correct invoicing or compensate for operational errors; contract terms remain unchanged unless accompanied by a signed amendment.

Appendix A — Credit Memo CSV template

credit_memo_id,original_invoice_id,customer_id,credit_amount,reason_code,approver_id,issued_at,memo_text
CM-2026-001,INV-2026-1405,CUST-492,$2,500,usage_discrepancy,FIN-MGR-12,2026-03-01,"Prorated overcharge for token parsing bug"

Appendix B — Contact Directory

- Billing & AR: billing@redwood.ai (team alias)
- Customer Success (billing queue): cs-billing@redwood.ai
- Finance Escalation: finance-escalate@redwood.ai
- Legal Intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Engineering Oncall (billing exports): infra-billing-oncall@redwood.ai

Change Log

- 2026-02-10: Created by Elena Martinez (Billing Lead).
- 2026-03-02: Updated approval matrix and SLA targets after Finance leadership review.

Related Policies and Links

- See: Chargeback and internal billing guidelines (internal page) for inter-company billing adjustments.
- See: Contract terms exceptions policy for credit approvals tied to commercial concessions.

End of document

payload.page_title: Pricing change notice and revenue reconciliation procedure

sections.body: This procedure defines the cross-functional steps required when changing pricing or billing terms for Redwood Inference customers, and the downstream revenue recognition (RevRec) and forecasting adjustments required. The goal is to: (1) ensure consistent legal and procurement approvals; (2) provide deterministic notification timelines to customers and internal teams; (3) produce auditable RevRec adjustments and journal entries; (4) update FP&A forecasts and committed capacity accounting.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all changes that modify customer-facing pricing, billing cadence, or contract charge quantities: rate card changes, discounts, credits, one-time fees, term amendments, capacity commits, and early termination fees.
- Exclusions: purely marketing price lists that do not change existing contracts, internal list-price experiments (<72 hours) with no customer impact.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Pricing Change: any modification to the monetary terms in an executed agreement or an active billing relationship.
- Amendment Effective Date: the date the new pricing/billing terms take legal effect.
- Billing Cutoff Date: final invoice date using old pricing.
- RevRec Adjustment Window: 90 days post-amendment for accounting adjustments and catch-up.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
- Sales: initiates pricing change request, completes commercial justification.
- Legal: drafts amendment and approves final contract language.
- Procurement (customer side): confirms customer acceptance and PO alignment (if applicable).
- Finance (Revenue Operations / RevRec): validates accounting treatment, prepares journal entries, issues billing adjustments.
- FP&A: updates forecasts and model assumptions.
- Billing/Payments (Finance Ops): executes invoices/credit memos and updates billing system.
- Customer Success: communicates operational impact and coordinates customer acceptance.
sections.heading: Owners and responsibilities (high level)

sections.body:
1) Internal approval target: all pricing changes must have commercial, legal, and finance approval 10 business days before Amendment Effective Date.
2) Customer-facing notice: standard notice is 30 days prior to Amendment Effective Date for recurring price increases or structural changes.
3) Emergency/expedited changes: approval window can be shortened to 3 business days with Executive sponsor approval; Finance must manually validate RevRec impact before go-live.
sections.heading: Notice triggers and SLAs

sections.body:
- Confirm product/sku mapping for affected charges.
- Provide expected billing delta by customer (monthly run rate delta).
- Confirm if change affects committed capacity or reserved billing.
- Attach customer PO or email acceptance (if required).
- Select Amendment Effective Date and propose Billing Cutoff Date.
sections.heading: Pre-change checklist (Sales lead)

sections.body:
1) Sales uploads Pricing Change Request (PCR) into Contract Intake Workspace (Confluence template link) containing: customer, contract id, old/new rates, effective dates, reason, revenue owner, and estimated MRR/ARR impact.
2) Legal reviews draft amendment and flags any non-standard clauses.
3) Finance (RevRec) assesses accounting treatment and flags any immediate revenue deferral or acceleration needs.
4) Procurement or Customer Success obtains formal customer acceptance signature or PO.
5) Final sign-off recorded in the PCR and the amendment executed.

Billing execution and RevRec steps after amendment effective date:
1) Billing/Payments: generate invoice run using new rates on or after Billing Cutoff Date. Issue any automated proration rules per billing system policy.
2) RevRec (Revenue Operations): calculate the revenue impact by identifying the overlap period where the old rate was previously recognized and the new rate applies.
3) If a retrospective correction is required (e.g., retrospective credit or back-billed invoice), Finance must: a) prepare credit memos or invoices, b) record corresponding journal entries, and c) document rationale in the PCR.
sections.heading: Approval workflow (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Simple recurring price increase (prospective): Recognize revenue per normal schedule; adjust future forecasts. No retrospective RevRec entry required if amendment is prospective.
- Mid-term rate change with retroactive billing (customer approved back-billing): Recognize additional revenue when invoiced; if payment expected after period end, record receivable and assess collectibility. Consider ASC 606 guidance on contract modifications.
- One-time credits or refunds: Issue credit memo and reduce recognized revenue in the RevRec Adjustment Window. Document control: link credit memo to amendment id.
sections.heading: Accounting treatment guidance (common scenarios)

sections.body:
- Prospective increase (no retro): No adjustment to historical entries.
- Retroactive billing issued for Jan-Mar period and invoiced in May:
  Debit: Accounts Receivable $30,000
  Credit: Revenue (prior periods catch-up) $28,000
  Credit: Deferred Tax/Other adjustments $2,000  (if tax or timing)
- Issuing customer credit for overbilling:
  Debit: Revenue Reduction/Contra-Revenue $5,000
  Credit: Accounts Receivable or Cash $5,000
sections.heading: Sample journal entries (illustrative)

sections.body:
- FP&A must update recurring revenue models within 5 business days of amendment execution. Updates include: monthly run-rate, churn adjustments, committed capacity revenue schedules, and GAAP vs. cash waterfall.
- For material amendments (>5% of ARR per customer or >$250k ARR delta), FP&A and RevOps must produce a reconciliation memo and present in the next Finance weekly forecast review.
sections.heading: Forecasting & FP&A alignment

sections.body:
- Revenue Operations runs the Pricing Change Reconciliation report (PCRR) each month which includes: list of amendments executed, effective dates, invoiced deltas, outstanding credit memos, and pending disputes.
- Reconciliation queries (example SQL-like pseudo-query):
  SELECT contract_id, amendment_id, effective_date, sum(new_amount - old_amount) as monthly_delta
  FROM billing_events
  WHERE effective_date BETWEEN :start_date AND :end_date
  GROUP BY contract_id, amendment_id

- Automation: Revenue Ops maintains a mapping table of amendment ids to invoice ids used in automated reconciliation scripts. Exceptions feed a ticket to RevRec for manual review.
sections.heading: Reporting and reconciliation controls (monthly cadence)

sections.body:
- Price increase notification subject: "Notice: Updates to your Redwood Inference pricing effective [DATE]"
- Template bullet points to include: brief rationale, affected SKUs, Amendment Effective Date, Billing Cutoff Date, contact for questions, link to amendment document, and instructions for PO updates.
sections.heading: Customer communication templates (condensed)

sections.body:
- Day 0–5 post-amendment: Billing/Payments handles invoice issuance and straightforward disputes.
- Day 6–30: RevRec and Sales resolve pricing discrepancies and approve credit memos.
- >30 days: Escalate to Head of Finance and General Counsel for disputed legacy billing beyond standard Credit Policy window.

Controls, audit trail and evidence retention:
- All pricing changes must be stored in Contract Intake Workspace and linked to: executed amendment PDF, PCR ticket, customer acceptance artifact, and invoice/credit memo ids.
- Retain evidence for 7 years for audit purposes per company policy.
sections.heading: Escalation matrix

sections.body:
- PCR Confluence template: [link to template]
- Amendment checklist (embedded): 1) commercial summary, 2) legal clause exceptions, 3) RevRec sign-off, 4) invoices to be reissued, 5) communications log.
- Sample credit memo JSON (billing system snippet):
  {
    "customer_id": "CUST-12345",
    "amendment_id": "AMEND-2026-004",
    "amount": "-5000.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "reason_code": "PRICE_CORRECT"
  }
sections.heading: Templates and artifacts (links and examples)

sections.body:
- If a pricing change triggers a change in committed capacity, coordinate with Infrastructure Finance to update committed GPU reservation invoicing and capacity reporting.
- Apply rounding and proration rules consistently: default to bill on a per-day proration basis for mid-cycle changes unless customer requests otherwise.
- Where possible, prefer prospective amendments to avoid complex retroactive accounting and customer disputes.
sections.heading: Operational notes and best practices

sections.body:
- Time-to-approval (goal: <10 business days)
- % of pricing changes requiring retrospective correction (goal: <5%)
- Average time to clear pricing disputes (goal: <15 business days)
- Forecast delta accuracy after pricing changes (goal: <2% variance reported vs. revised forecast)

Appendix A — Example calculation:
- Customer A had $100k monthly at old rate. On 2026-03-01 rate increased to $110k monthly. Amendment Effective Date: 2026-03-01. Billing Cutoff Date: 2026-03-01.
  - If change is prospective only: March invoice reflects $110k; no historical adjustments.
  - If back-billed for Feb at new rate and customer approved: Additional invoice for Feb delta = $10k.

Appendix B — Contact list:
- RevRec (Revenue Operations): revrec@redwood.com (owner: Maya Patel)
- Billing/Payments: billing@redwood.com
- Legal Contracts: legal-contracts@redwood.com
- FP&A: fpna@redwood.com
- Customer Success: cs-ops@redwood.com
sections.heading: KPIs and monitoring

sections.body:

- 2026-03-20: Updated emergency change SLA and sample journal guidance after external audit request.
- 2026-05-03: Clarified forecasting update timelines and added PCRR monthly control requirement.

payload.page_title: Subscription billing cutover and revenue timing policy (2027)

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines Redwood Inference’s policy for (A) determining the timing of revenue recognition for subscription and usage contracts and (B) the operational cutover steps for migrating or launching subscription billing systems (including contract amendments, plan changes, and vendor- or in-house billing engine replacements). It is intended for Finance, Legal, Revenue Operations, Product, and Engineering teams involved in contract lifecycle and billing operations.

Scope

- Applies to all customer contracts that include subscription fees, recurring usage components, or multi-element arrangements sold or amended after 2024-01-01.
- Excludes one-off professional services invoices governed by separate SOWs (see Professional Services invoicing policy).
- Covers hosted Redwood API subscriptions, Dedicated capacity reservations, and Private deployment license/maintenance arrangements.

Principles

1. Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize as obligations are satisfied.
2. Billing timing (invoice issuance) and revenue recognition date may differ; policy distinguishes cash/billing cadence from revenue earn-in.
3. Conservatism on bundling: when product features are materially distinct, allocate and recognize separately unless contractually debundled.

High-level policy rules

- Initial subscription term: Recognize recurring service revenue ratably over the contract term starting from the customer’s contract effective date or service commencement date, whichever is later.
- Upfront implementation fees: Capitalize and recognize over the estimated period of benefit (default: 24 months) unless the fee is for a distinct service; then recognize when delivered.
- Usage-based fees: Recognize in the month the usage is earned (metered usage period) once reliable usage metrics are available and validated.
- Multi-element arrangements: Allocate transaction price based on standalone selling prices (SSP). If SSP not available, use best estimate hierarchy (list price, adjusted price of similar customer).
- Deferred revenue cutoff: Invoices that cover future periods must be recorded to deferred revenue and recognized ratably.

Billing cutover: goals and SLAs
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Zero customer-facing downtime for billing continuity.
- No more than one billing cycle of divergence between invoicing system and revenue accounting (target: <30 days reconciling difference).
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Cutover runbook execution window: typically scheduled during low-traffic weekend.
- Reconciliation tolerance: post-cutover reconciliation mismatch must be <0.5% of ARR or $50k (whichever is smaller) within 14 calendar days.
- Final invoice re‑issuance window: customer-impacting invoices reissued within 7 business days when required.

Roles and ownership

- Finance (Revenue Accounting): policy owner; decision rights for recognition.
- Legal: contract language and change approvals; confirms effective dates.
- RevenueOps / Billing Platform: executes cutover and customer communications.
- Product/Engineering: provides data extracts, API endpoints, usage logs, and implements migration hooks.

Cutover checklist (pre, during, post)

Pre-cutover (30–7 days before)
1. Confirm master contract list and effective dates with Legal and Sales.
2. Freeze rate table changes; record SSPs for new plans.
3. Align sample of 50 customers across systems (CRM, previous billing engine, ledger) for test reconciliation.
4. Prepare export of historical deferred revenue balances by contract.
5. Stakeholder sign-off: Finance, Legal, RevenueOps, Product.

During cutover (execution weekend)
1. Put read-only locks on customer billing accounts in legacy system where possible.
2. Execute data export: customers, active contracts, billing schedules, usage windows, credits/adjustments.
3. Import into new system; run automated integrity checks (record counts, checksum on monetary totals).
4. Run parallel invoice generation for one pilot cohort (25–100 customers).
5. If pilot passes, flip traffic per the rollback plan.

Post-cutover (day 1–30)
1. Full reconciliation: deferred revenue opening balance, invoices issued vs. expected, unapplied payments.
2. Resolve exceptions and record corrective journal entries with approval (see Journal entries section).
3. Customer communications for any reissued invoices or proration adjustments.
4. Post-mortem and final sign-off by Finance.

Approval matrix (excerpt)

| Change type | Threshold | Approver | Finance review SLA |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| New SKU / pricing tier | Any | RevenueOps + Finance | 3 business days |
| Contract amendment that accelerates revenue recognition | > $100k total | Finance Director + Legal | 5 business days |
| One-time implementation fee recognition policy waiver | > $50k | Head of Finance | 2 business days |

Journal entry examples (illustrative)

1) Monthly recognition for a $12,000 annual subscription billed annually (invoice date 2026-01-01, term: 12 months):

- On invoice issuance (2026-01-01):
  DR Accounts Receivable $12,000
  CR Deferred Revenue $12,000

- Monthly (recognition entry each month, 2026-01-31, etc.):
  DR Deferred Revenue $1,000
  CR Subscription Revenue $1,000

2) Usage invoice (recognized same month):
  DR Accounts Receivable $3,250
  CR Usage Revenue $3,250

3) Corrective entry post-cutover (to move $14,500 from misclassified revenue back to deferred for period mismatch):
  DR Retained Earnings (correction) $14,500
  CR Subscription Revenue $14,500
  DR Deferred Revenue $14,500
  CR Accounts Receivable $14,500

Exception handling and common failure modes

- Missing contract effective date: hold invoices until Legal confirms; if ambiguity persists beyond 5 business days, default to invoice date for recognition and flag for contract remediation.
- Usage lag: if usage metrics are delayed >7 days, defer recognition until validated; estimate only with documented rationale and Finance Director approval.
- Customer disputes: place invoice on hold and create a dispute ticket; revenue recognition continues unless the dispute impacts collectibility (see credit risk policy).

Contract amendments and renewals

- Renewals that are materially identical to prior terms: continue ratable recognition without reallocation.
- Amendments that change scope or price: reassess for new performance obligations; if additional deliverables are distinct, allocate incremental consideration.
- Early termination: recognize any remaining deferred revenue for services not to be performed in accordance with the contract termination terms unless refund obligation exists; apply customer credit or refund per contract.

Templates and artifacts (appendix)

- CSV template: contract-export-template.csv (columns: contract_id, customer_id, effective_date, term_months, billing_frequency, annual_price, currency, sku_id, deferred_balance)
- Reconciliation workbook: revrec-cutover-recon.xlsx (sheets: summary, detail_by_contract, exceptions)
- Change request form: billing-change-request.md (fields: requestor, business justification, financial impact, rollback plan)

Operational playbook snippets (CLI / SQL)

- Example SQL to extract active subscriptions:
  SELECT contract_id, customer_id, start_date, end_date, billing_frequency, amount FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'active';
- Checksum example (python):
  import csv
  total = sum(float(r['deferred_balance']) for r in csv.DictReader(open('contract-export-template.csv')))
  print(f"Deferred total: {total:.2f}")

Risk controls and audit evidence

- Every cutover requires a signed Cutover Approval Form retained in the finance project folder.
- Audit trail: keep exports, import logs, checksum reports, and reconciliation workbooks for 7 years.
- Sample-based audit: Finance will sample 5% of active contracts (min 50) post-cutover for verification.

Communication plan

- Internal: daily standups during the cutover week; status updates to stakeholders via #revops-cutover Slack channel.
- External (customers): proactive email 7 days prior if invoices or payment methods may be reissued; follow-up within 48 hours for impacted customers.

Appendix A — Decision tree (short)

1. Is the charge recurring? Yes -> ratable recognition. No -> evaluate distinct delivery.
2. Is usage metered? Yes -> recognize on usage period once validated. No -> consider upfront/one-time rules.

Owners and contacts

- Policy owner: Priya Raman, Director, Revenue Accounting (finance@redwood.ai)
- Billing platform lead: Omar Li, RevenueOps (revops@redwood.ai)
- Legal contact: Asha Kapoor, Counsel (legal@redwood.ai)

Revision history

- 2025-11-12: Created by Priya Raman (draft)
- 2026-02-18: Major update to cutover SLA and reconciliation tolerances (reviewers: Miguel Santos, Ellen Wu)
- 2026-03-01: Published

Related policies

- Professional services invoicing policy
- Credit risk and DSO policy
- Procurement contract approval matrix

Questions and escalation

For questions or to request an exception, submit a Billing Change Request and tag the policy owner. Exceptions require documented business justification and approval from Head of Finance.

payload.page_title: ClearEdge Health (2027) — Weekly invoicing, PO fingerprint, and net terms (RevRec/Billing)

sections.body:
h1. Overview
This page documents the *finalized* billing + invoicing requirements for *ClearEdge Health* for the 2027 pilot, including weekly invoice cadence, PO identifier requirements (including *po_fingerprint*), and agreed payment terms.

This supersedes earlier guidance circulating in the June 2027 email thread; the key changes are called out in the *Change log*.

h1. Scope
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
* Customer: ClearEdge Health
* Deal/CRM: DEAL-8742
* Region: US
* Pilot duration: 12 weeks (unless amended)

h1. Final commercial terms (billing-impacting)

payload.page_title: Marketplace RevRec & Invoicing Notes (AWS + GCP)

sections.body:
This page documents Redwood Inference’s revenue recognition and invoicing implications for AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace (GCP Marketplace) transactions, including:
- How we recognize revenue for usage-based and contract-based marketplace purchases
- How marketplace fees (revenue share) are recorded
- How refunds/credits are handled (and what we can/can’t do within each marketplace)
- How to reconcile marketplace reporting to Redwood internal billing/metering

This is an internal Finance + Legal reference intended to be consistent with ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles. It is not customer-facing.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Hosted API (usage-based)
- Dedicated (reserved capacity contracts) when transacted via marketplace (where supported)
- Private (platform fee + support) when transacted via marketplace (typically via private offers)
- Compliance / support add-ons sold as separate dimensions/SKUs
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- Direct (non-marketplace) contracts and invoicing (see standard Order Form + invoicing runbook)
- Technical metering implementation details (see Billing Catalog + Marketplace Metering docs)
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
- Marketplace “Seller of Record”: AWS/GCP is the billing party to the end customer; Redwood receives net proceeds.
- Marketplace “Private Offer”: negotiated pricing/terms within marketplace tooling; acceptance and billing occurs through AWS/GCP.
- Entitlement: the marketplace subscription record used to provision/limit Redwood usage.
- Metering dimension: the billable unit reported to AWS/GCP (e.g., tokens, requests, capacity-hours), mapped from Redwood internal meters.
- Net proceeds: amount remitted to Redwood after marketplace revenue share and (where applicable) taxes handled by marketplace.
sections.heading: Definitions and key objects

sections.body: In most marketplace scenarios Redwood is the primary party delivering the service (we host/operate the inference platform) and AWS/GCP facilitates procurement and billing. However, the end customer is billed by the marketplace and the marketplace collects consideration.
sections.heading: Principal vs agent (gross vs net)

sections.body:
- We record revenue on a gross basis for the service delivered to the customer, with marketplace revenue share recorded as a selling expense (or contra-revenue only if required by local statutory guidance).
- We record Accounts Receivable against the marketplace (not the end customer) to the extent a receivable exists based on reports/remittance timing.

If a specific private offer or marketplace program introduces conditions that materially change control indicators (e.g., marketplace controls pricing and has primary responsibility for delivery), Finance must re-assess principal/agent for that program/region.
sections.heading: Policy position (default)

sections.body:
1) Usage-based (Hosted API) via marketplace
- Performance obligation: stand-ready access to API + actual usage (tokens/embeddings/reranks).
- Recognition: as usage occurs (typically daily), based on Redwood internal metering as the system of record, reconciled to marketplace metering reports.
- Cutoff: revenue accrued through period-end for delivered usage regardless of when marketplace remits cash.

2) Committed spend / contract dimensions (where offered)
- If structured as a committed spend with consumption over time:
  - Recognize revenue as usage occurs up to the committed amount.
  - Unused committed amount: generally deferred and recognized over the contractual period if stand-ready access is the performance obligation, subject to breakage assessment.
- If the marketplace product is a fixed subscription for a term (e.g., “Platform fee per month”):
  - Recognize ratably over the subscription term.

3) Dedicated capacity reservations
- Performance obligation: reserved capacity (stand-ready) and related platform access.
- Recognition: ratably over the reservation term (monthly straight-line), unless the contract specifically ties consideration to delivered capacity-hours and metering supports it.
- Overages (burst capacity) if separately metered: recognize as used.

4) Private deployments (Private / VPC / on-prem package)
Marketplace structures vary; common patterns:
- Subscription (platform fee): recognize ratably over term.
- Professional services (if included): recognize as delivered based on hours/milestones; ensure SKU/offer distinguishes services from subscription where required.
- Support add-ons: ratably over term.
sections.heading: Revenue recognition timing by purchase type

sections.body:
If an offer bundles multiple components (e.g., “Private Platform + Support + Compliance Add-on”), Finance must ensure:
- Separate line items/dimensions exist where practical.
- Standalone selling prices (SSP) are documented for allocation when components are bundled.

As a guardrail for marketplace packaging: avoid bundling implementation services into marketplace SKUs unless the marketplace supports clear separation and the legal terms align.
sections.heading: Multiple performance obligations and allocation

sections.body:
- AWS/GCP revenue share is recorded as a marketplace fee expense (typically within Sales & Marketing or Cost of Revenue depending on policy; Redwood default is Sales & Marketing unless the program is treated as a distribution channel cost directly tied to delivery).
- Record fee based on marketplace statements (not estimates), unless cutoff requires accrual.

Recommended accounts (illustrative; use current COA names in NetSuite):
- Revenue: Marketplace - Hosted Usage / Marketplace - Subscriptions
- Contra/Expense: Marketplace Fees
- Receivable: Due from Marketplace
- Cash: Marketplace Remittances
sections.heading: Marketplace fees and cost treatment

sections.body:
- The marketplace invoices the customer. Redwood does not issue an invoice to the customer for marketplace-billed usage/subscriptions.
- Redwood may provide a “billing support letter” or usage summary for customer procurement, but it must not be presented as a tax invoice.
sections.heading: Who invoices the customer

sections.body:
- Usage reports (tokens, requests, model family, environment) from Redwood Console
- Mapping of Redwood usage categories to marketplace dimensions (for customer chargeback)
- Remittance timing expectations and support escalation contacts
sections.heading: Permitted (on request)

sections.body:
- Re-issuing marketplace invoices with Redwood branding
- Making commitments about marketplace tax treatment (VAT/GST) beyond directing customers to AWS/GCP invoice documentation
sections.heading: Not permitted (without Legal approval)

sections.body:
- Customers typically do vendor onboarding with AWS/GCP, not Redwood.
- For Private Offers, customers may request Redwood W-9/W-8 or SOC documentation; coordinate via Security/Compliance and Legal, and clarify that billing is via marketplace.
sections.heading: Purchase Orders (POs) and vendor onboarding

sections.body:
- Refunds/credits to marketplace customers must be processed through the marketplace mechanisms, not through Redwood’s direct invoicing.
- Redwood may provide service credits inside Redwood (e.g., additional usage allowance) only if consistent with:
  - Marketplace policies
  - The customer’s private offer terms
  - Revenue recognition guidance (credits may reduce transaction price)
sections.heading: General rule

sections.body:
- Customer claims unexpected spend due to misconfiguration
- Metering mismatch (Redwood vs marketplace)
sections.heading: Common scenarios

sections.body:
1) Support confirms incident/dispute scope and time window.
2) Billing Engineering validates internal metering and dimension mapping for the subscription entitlement.
3) Finance determines whether an adjustment is warranted.
4) If warranted:
   - Prefer marketplace credit/refund path (AWS/GCP credit memo equivalent), following marketplace seller workflows.
   - If marketplace cannot issue retroactive adjustments for certain dimensions, Legal + Finance decide on an alternative (e.g., issuing a future-period discount via private offer amendment).
sections.heading: Process

sections.body: - Refunds reduce revenue in the period identified (or as a subsequent event if applicable), with corresponding reduction in receivable from marketplace.
sections.heading: Accounting

sections.body:
- Marketplace cancellations generally stop future billing but do not automatically refund past periods.
- For prepaid/annual private offers, refunds depend on private offer terms and marketplace policy.
sections.heading: Subscription cancellations

sections.body: - If a refund is approved, reverse deferred revenue for the remaining term and reduce receivable/cash accordingly.
sections.heading: Accounting

sections.body:
- Avoid marketplace “$0 with credits” structures that are ambiguous for revrec.
- If a marketplace trial is offered:
  - Ensure the trial is clearly separate from paid subscription/usage.
  - Track conversion and start date of paid entitlement.

If Redwood grants credits inside the Redwood platform (non-marketplace):
- Treat as variable consideration / discount, and ensure it is reflected in net revenue where it impacts the transaction price.
- Do not represent internal credits as marketplace credits.
sections.heading: Policy

sections.body:
- Redwood internal metering is the operational source of truth for usage delivered.
- Marketplace reports are the commercial source of truth for amounts billed/collected.
- Reconciliation is required at least monthly, and weekly during launch/transition periods.
sections.heading: Source of truth

sections.body:
For each marketplace (AWS, GCP) and each SKU/dimension:
- Units billed (marketplace) vs units metered (Redwood)
- Gross billed amount (marketplace) vs gross revenue recognized (Redwood)
- Marketplace fees (per statement) vs accrued fees
- Net remittance vs cash received
- Open receivable balance vs “due from marketplace” aging based on remittance schedule
sections.heading: Minimum reconciliation outputs (monthly close)

sections.body:
1) Extract Redwood internal usage summary by marketplace entitlement
- Group by: marketplace (AWS/GCP), seller account, entitlement ID, SKU, dimension, day/month

2) Extract marketplace statements
- AWS: metering/billing reports + disbursement/remittance reports
- GCP: marketplace earnings and billing exports (as provided by partner portal)

3) Map dimensions
- Use the approved SKU mapping catalog (v2) as the only mapping reference.
- Any unmapped dimensions or new SKUs must be flagged to Product + Billing (risk of misbilling and incorrect revrec).

4) Investigate exceptions
sections.heading: Recommended workflow

sections.body:
- Entitlement propagation delay (usage occurred before marketplace recognized subscription)
- Dimension mismatch due to SKU rename or legacy listing
- Partial-day proration differences for subscription start/end
- Currency conversion differences (if marketplace bills in local currency but Redwood books in USD)

5) Close and post entries
- Accrue revenue to match delivered usage and/or ratable subscription periods.
- Accrue marketplace fees if statements lag close.
sections.heading: Common exception categories

sections.body:
- >1.0% variance in units or revenue per SKU/month: escalate to Billing + Partnerships and open a tracking ticket.
- Any customer-impacting misbilling: coordinate with Support and Legal before issuing marketplace adjustments.
sections.heading: Exception thresholds and escalation

sections.body:
- Finance (RevRec): owns close and final numbers
- Billing Engineering: owns meter/dimension correctness
- Partnerships: owns marketplace portal processes and submissions
sections.heading: Owners

sections.body:
- Expect overlap where customers are on legacy SKUs while new SKUs are live.
- Finance must ensure:
  - Legacy SKUs remain mapped to internal meters until fully sunset
  - Revenue reporting separates legacy vs v2 SKUs for at least 2 quarters post-launch
  - Any customer migration (private offer amendment or subscription change) is documented for revrec (contract modification assessment)
sections.heading: During listing refresh and SKU migration

sections.body:
- If the change adds distinct services at SSP: treat as separate contract.
- If the change modifies price/term for the same service: account as contract modification with cumulative catch-up or prospective treatment as appropriate.
sections.heading: Contract modification guidance

sections.body:
- Gross usage billed: $100,000
- Marketplace fee: $15,000
- Net remittance expected: $85,000
sections.heading: Assume

sections.body:
- Dr Due from Marketplace $100,000
- Cr Marketplace Revenue $100,000

When marketplace fee statement is issued (or at month-end if known):
- Dr Marketplace Fees Expense $15,000
- Cr Due from Marketplace $15,000
sections.heading: At month-end (accrual based on usage delivered)

sections.body:
- Dr Cash $85,000
- Cr Due from Marketplace $85,000
sections.heading: Upon cash remittance

sections.body:
- Annual platform subscription: $240,000
- Start date: Feb 1

At contract start (if billed/recognized via marketplace subscription):
- Dr Due from Marketplace $240,000
- Cr Deferred Revenue $240,000
sections.heading: Assume

sections.body:
- Dr Deferred Revenue $20,000
- Cr Subscription Revenue $20,000
sections.heading: Monthly recognition

sections.body:
- Ensure segregation of duties: offer creation (Partnerships) vs revrec policy (Finance) vs system mapping changes (Engineering).
- Maintain evidence for:
  - SKU mapping approvals
  - Contract terms (private offer PDFs/portal exports)
  - Marketplace statements and remittance reports
  - Reconciliation workpapers and variance investigations
sections.heading: Controls and audit considerations

sections.body: - Store reconciliation workpapers and marketplace statements in the Finance close folder for the fiscal year (minimum 7 years, or per corporate retention policy).
sections.heading: Retention

sections.body:
1) Confirm new SKUs/dimensions launched this period; verify mapping exists.
2) Pull Redwood usage by entitlement for the month; validate totals to internal dashboards.
3) Pull AWS/GCP billing + remittance statements.
4) Complete reconciliation and investigate variances above threshold.
5) Post revenue accruals/deferrals and marketplace fee accruals.
6) Tie out Due from Marketplace to expected remittance schedule.
7) Document any refunds/credits approved and confirm they were processed through marketplace.
sections.heading: Operational checklist (monthly close)

sections.body:
- RevRec owner: Emily Stone
- Pricing/Finance sponsor: Laura Bennett
- Commercial counsel: Sofia Mendes
- Billing/metering: Cole Summers
- CRM/process coordination (deal ops visibility): Isabelle Laurent
sections.heading: Contacts

sections.body:

- 2026-01-21: Initial publication for marketplace listing refresh launch prep.

payload.page_title: Invoice "Overage Adjustment" After Quota Threshold Change — Proration & Rate-Lookup RCA (2026)

sections.body:
A dedicated-plan customer (Maple Health) reported an unexpected invoice increase immediately after changing their quota threshold from **1M tokens to 2M tokens** via the Console UI on **2026-03-09**. The subsequent invoice generated on **2026-03-10** included a large line item labeled **"overage adjustment"**.

Engineering confirmed the charge was caused by a **rate-lookup fallback to a legacy/default mapping** during a narrow failure window in the quota metadata write path. The invoicing pipeline proceeded using the fallback rate rather than retrying rate lookup after metadata became available.

Finance issued a manual credit and Engineering shipped a hotfix to prevent recurrence.

---
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Customer: **Maple Health**
- Tier: **Dedicated**
- Environment: **prod (us-east)**
- Affected model(s) observed in ledger context: **gpt-4o-mini**
- Primary artifact: **invoice_82419** (customer-provided PDF referenced in ticket)
sections.heading: Customer & Scope

sections.body:
- Customer received an invoice containing an **"overage adjustment"** line item for **~1.1M tokens** at an unexpectedly high/legacy rate.
- No service downtime was reported; impact was limited to **billing correctness and customer trust**.
sections.heading: Impact

sections.body:
- We identified **7** other accounts with quota updates during the same failure window.
- **0** additional incorrect invoices were ultimately issued (either no invoice generated in the window or invoices were generated after metadata became consistent).

---
sections.heading: Additional exposure (post-incident audit)

sections.body:
- **2026-03-09 17:42** — Console quota change event recorded for Maple Health (quota_update by user@maplehealth.com).
- **2026-03-09 (deploy window)** — Invoicing job **v2.3.1** running; quota metadata store experienced intermittent **HTTP 500** responses.
- **2026-03-10** — Invoice generated; includes **"overage adjustment"** line item.
- **2026-03-11** — Support engineering flags known proration edge case: rate/proration lookup can fall back when quota metadata is missing.
- **2026-03-12** — Finance places provisional credit hold pending confirmation.
- **2026-03-15** — Root cause confirmed: quota update event emitted, metadata write failed transiently, invoicing job proceeded with fallback.
- **2026-03-18** — Hotfix deployed: invoicing job **v2.3.2** (retry rate lookup; block fallback on proration-required paths).
- **2026-03-19** — Manual credit issued to Maple Health; customer notified with explanation and prevention steps.
- **2026-03-21** — Completed audit for similarly timed quota updates and reconciled ledgers.

---
sections.heading: Timeline (UTC)

sections.body:
When the customer increased their quota threshold, the system should:
1) persist the new quota configuration and effective date metadata,
2) emit/consume an update event, and
3) compute proration using the correct rate schedule for the billing period.

During the **2026-03-09 deploy window**, the quota metadata store returned **HTTP 500** for a short interval. The quota-service still emitted the update event, but the metadata write was not committed in time for the invoicing job’s rate/proration computation. The invoicing job **v2.3.1** then:
- retried the invoice job itself, but
- did **not** retry the downstream rate/proration lookup sufficiently, and
- fell back to a default/legacy mapping when quota metadata was missing.

This produced a line item labeled **"overage adjustment"** at the incorrect rate.

---
sections.heading: What Happened (Technical)

sections.body:
**Primary root cause:** Invoicing job **v2.3.1** treated missing quota metadata as a non-fatal condition and used a **default/legacy rate fallback** rather than enforcing consistency (retry/backoff) for proration-required invoices.

**Contributing factors:**
- Intermittent metadata store **500s** during a deploy window.
- A brittle contract between quota-service metadata persistence and the invoicing pipeline’s assumptions about metadata availability.
- Insufficient alerting on "fallback rate mapping used" events (logged but not paged/alerted).

---
sections.heading: Root Cause

sections.body:
- Finance issued a **manual credit** for the incorrect portion of the "overage adjustment" line item (issued **2026-03-19**).
- Customer received:
  - confirmation that the charge was due to an internal proration/rate-lookup error,
  - credit confirmation details, and
  - a summary of prevention steps (hotfix + monitoring).

---
sections.heading: Customer Resolution

sections.body:
- **Invoicing job v2.3.2** (deployed **2026-03-18**):
  - Retries rate/proration lookup with exponential backoff when quota metadata is missing.
  - Prevents use of legacy/default fallback mapping for proration-required paths; instead marks invoice generation as "retryable" until metadata is available or a max retry threshold is exceeded.
  - Adds structured logging for "metadata missing" and "fallback prevented" outcomes.
sections.heading: Engineering changes (deployed)

sections.body:
- New metric: `invoicing.rate_lookup.fallback_attempted` (should be ~0)
- New alert: page on sustained nonzero fallback attempts over 5 minutes in prod.

---
sections.heading: Monitoring/alerting (added)

sections.body:
When a customer reports a sudden post-quota-change invoice increase with an "overage adjustment" line:
1) Check whether a quota threshold change occurred within 48 hours before invoice generation.
2) Ask Engineering to confirm whether metadata was missing/fallback used.
3) If confirmed, issue a manual credit and tag it as: **Billing correction — proration/rate lookup**.
sections.heading: Finance & RevRec Guidance (Operational)

sections.body:
- Invoice ID (e.g., invoice_82419)
- Ledger snapshot (line item details)
- Console quota change timestamp
- Region/environment
- Confirmation of invoicing job version

---
sections.heading: Minimum evidence to capture (for audit)

sections.body:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Support ticket | SUP-92477 |
| Customer | Maple Health |
| Tier | Dedicated |
| Region | us-east |
| Console quota change | 2026-03-09 17:42 UTC |
| Invoice generated | 2026-03-10 |
| Line item label | "overage adjustment" |
| Token quantity referenced | ~1.1M tokens |
| Invoicing version observed | v2.3.1 |
| Fix version | v2.3.2 |

---
sections.heading: Appendix A — Key Data Points

sections.body:
This incident was a **billing correctness bug**, not a pricing/policy change.
- Policy: proration must reflect the correct rate schedule and effective dates for quota changes.
- Bug: missing metadata led to an incorrect legacy/default rate mapping being applied.

For any future disputes, reference the support ticket and this RCA for justification of credits/refunds when the fallback path is implicated.
sections.heading: Appendix B — Notes on Policy vs. Bug

payload.page_title: Finance operational scenarios checklist: commitment & contingency

sections.body:
Summary:
This document is an operational checklist for cross-functional finance scenarios that commonly affect forecasting, procurement commitments, contract ingestion, and revenue recognition handoffs. It codifies decision thresholds, owner responsibilities, approval gates, and escalation paths for three high-impact scenarios: rapid usage ramp (hosted API/dedicated capacity), mid-contract price change requests, and supplier procurement delays that affect committed capacity.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise and dedicated-capacity commercial contracts, purchase orders (POs) that exceed $50k or any that create capital or recurring commitments, and procurement requests that could materially affect quarterly forecasts.
- Not intended for purely internal one-time purchases under $5k (use procurement self-serve).

Principles:
- Forecast accuracy matters: changes to committed spend must be reflected in the rolling 12-week cash and MRR forecast within two business days of approval.
- Single source of truth: the contract ingestion system (ContractDB) remains definitive for billing and revrec triggers.
- Fast, auditable decisions: every commitment action must be logged with approver, date, and reason.

Primary owners and contacts:
- Finance (Forecasting & RevRec): Evelyn Cho (forecast_owner@redwood.example), backup: Maya Singh.
- Procurement: Liam O'Connor (procurement_lead@redwood.example).
- Legal (Commercial Contracts): Priya Raman (legal_contracts@redwood.example).
- Sales / Customer Success: account executive or CSM owning the customer relationship.

Scenario matrix (decision table):
| Scenario                                | Trigger threshold                         | Required approvals                         | Forecast action                      |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Rapid usage ramp (hosted API)          | >20% week-over-week growth or +$100k/mo   | Finance + Sales lead                        | Reforecast immediate 12-week cadence  |
| Dedicated capacity commit              | Contracted GPU commit > $250k annualized  | Finance + Procurement + Legal               | Add to committed revenue queue (RevRec) |
| Supplier delay affecting delivery      | Delay > 30 days or < 80% capacity         | Procurement + Engineering + Finance        | Apply contingency buffer, notify sales |

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Pre-commit approval (for any new commitment > $50k):
   1.1 Sales or Product submits Commitment Request Form (Confluence link + ContractDB stub).
   1.2 Procurement validates vendor terms and lead time.
   1.3 Finance runs cash-impact and P&L sensitivity (3 scenarios: base, -20% revenue, +30% cost).
   1.4 Legal reviews commercial terms for data/residency/KMS/HIPAA clauses.
   1.5 Approval: Finance director and Procurement lead must countersign; Legal signs if contractual exceptions exist.
   1.6 Upon approval, Procurement creates PO and uploads signed contract into ContractDB; update forecast spreadsheet and internal dashboards.

2) Forecast update cadence and artifacts:
   - Triggered updates: within 2 business days after any approval or material amendment.
   - Weekly rolling forecast: 12-week rolling forecast updated every Friday EOD and published to Finance dashboard.
   - Required artifacts: signed contract, PO number, projected monthly burn schedule, capacity mapping (if hardware), and revrec trigger mapping.

3) Contract ingestion to billing & RevRec mapping (checklist):
   - Verify contract exists in ContractDB with correct effective and term dates.
   - Confirm billing cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) in contract metadata.
   - Map contract line items to billing codes and billing service identifiers used by BillingEngine.
   - Mark revrec trigger: performance obligations identified and assigned to RevRec owner.
   - File an ingestion ticket to BillingOps with contract id and expected first invoice date.

Escalation & exception matrix:
| Issue                                  | Escalation chain (1 -> 2 -> 3)            | SLA for resolution                         |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Contract ingestion mismatch             | BillingOps -> Finance RevRec -> Legal     | 3 business days                            |
| Unplanned cost overrun (>15% of PO)    | Procurement -> Finance -> COO             | 2 business days                            |
| Customer requests early termination    | Sales -> Legal -> Finance                 | 5 business days                            |

Operational examples (sample run):
- Example A: Customer requests dedicated 50-GPU pool; procurement estimates 8-week lead time and $420k annual. Flow: Sales opens Commitment Request -> Procurement validates vendor -> Finance models cash impact -> Legal approves terms with KMS clause -> Approvals captured -> PO issued -> Contract ingested -> Forecast updated.

Metrics and SLOs to track (finance dashboard):
- Time from approval to forecast update: target <= 2 business days.
- Contract ingestion lag (signed -> BillingEngine ticket): target <= 3 business days.
- % of monthly variance explained by committed changes: target > 90% (explainable activity).
- Number of unapproved commitments discovered in audits: target 0.

Templates, CLI snippets, and config examples:

  customer_name,contract_id,product_line,annual_value,po_number,effective_date,term_months,owner,email

Audit and retrospectives:
- Quarterly audits: Finance will run a committed-spend vs. recognized revenue audit and publish variance notes.
- Postmortem: if a commitment causes >$200k unplanned cost or >10% forecast miss, run a cross-functional postmortem within two weeks.

payload.page_title: Capacity cost hedging and billing coordination guide

sections.body: This guide describes Redwood Inference's standardized approach for aligning capacity purchasing (GPU/pool reservations and cloud commit tiers), short‑term hedging strategies, and billing/revenue-recognition coordination. The goal is to reduce P&L volatility from usage seasonality and to ensure procurement, legal, finance, and product teams share a synchronized playbook for commits, overage handling, and invoice timing.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated capacity products; Private deployments follow a separate procurement cadence but should reference the hedging principles below.
- Covers forecasting windows of 1 month, 3 months, and 12 months.
- Includes guidance for monthly usage commits, reserved GPU capacity, spot/burst usage policies, and contract features that materially affect revrec (e.g., non-refundable prepayments, renewal triggers).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Baseline Commitment: recurring reserved capacity (monthly or annual) with a fixed price and term.
- Hedge Reserve: an incremental short-term capacity reservation (1–3 months) used to smooth cost for anticipated spikes.
- Overage Pool: metered usage billed at overage rates when actual consumption exceeds committed capacity.
- True‑up window: the period after which usage is reconciled and credits/debits applied.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
1) Visibility and single source of truth: Finance owns the committed-capacity ledger in the finance data warehouse; product/infra feed daily usage estimates into it.
2) Risk sharing: Tiered commitments should align incentives—teams with product roadmap-driven demand (e.g., Search team) should internalize part of hedging cost.
3) Minimizing revrec complexity: Prefer prepaid, short-term hedges over long multi-year irregular payments unless contractually necessary.
4) Operational simplicity: Standardize three hedging instruments: monthly hedge blocks, quarterly top-up, and burst credits.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
- Finance (Owner): final forecast signoff, commit economics analysis, and revrec guidance.
- Procurement: negotiates vendor terms, PO issuance, and manages supplier credit and invoices.
- Legal: reviews contract clauses that affect recognition (non-refundable, termination penalties, service credits).
- Product/Infra: provides demand signals, seasonality drivers, and validates performance requirements.
- Sales: communicates customer-facing contract terms that interact with capacity (enterprise reserved pools).
sections.heading: Roles and ownership

sections.body:
1) Inputs (daily): API token usage by SKU, median/95th p50/p95 tokens per request, mean session length, number of concurrent sessions.
2) Aggregation (weekly): compute 3-week trailing average and 98th percentile daily peak.
3) Rolling forecast buckets:
   - Short (0–30 days): p95 daily peak scaled by planned launches and promotions.
   - Medium (30–90 days): trailing average plus planned cadence impact (feature flags, marketing).
   - Long (90–365 days): conservative CAGR applied to baseline plus pipeline-sourced enterprise commitments.
sections.heading: Forecasting model (operational)

sections.body:
- Monthly Hedge Block: purchase when short forecast variance > 15% vs baseline for next 30 days. Typical size: 20–50% of expected incremental peak.
- Quarterly Top-up: used if medium forecast projects > 20% sustained increase for 60+ days.
- Burst Credits: vendor-managed spot capacity; use when short, unexpected spikes < 7 days.
- Trigger example: If expected 30‑day additional token volume > 10B tokens (~$xxk cost), open Monthly Hedge approval.
sections.heading: Suggested hedging instruments and thresholds

sections.body:
1) Weekly cadence: Product/Infra provides a 30-day demand delta to Procurement by Monday 10:00 PT.
2) Procurement evaluation: same-day tiered sourcing (internal reserved pool vs. cloud provider commit) with 24–48 hour turnaround for standard monthly hedges.
3) PO issuance: standard template (see appendix) — include term, price, termination notice (60 days), and true-up window.
4) Invoice routing: route hedging invoices to Finance CC procurement@redwood.ai and attach PO number; flagged hedging invoices are reconciled to the commit ledger within 3 business days.
sections.heading: Procurement sync and PO cadence

sections.body:
- Payment terms: prefer net-30 for hedges; prepaid monthly hedges allowed with clear revrec note.
- Refundability: Obtain explicit language for refunds or reallocation in case of cancelled product launches.
- Capacity transfer: include clause allowing internal re-assignment of reserved capacity across Redwood-owned projects.
- Termination & penalties: cap termination penalties; define force majeure and migration assistance.
- Usage metrics & reporting: define the metric vendor will report for capacity consumption and the cadence (daily/weekly).
sections.heading: Contract considerations (legal checklist)

sections.body:
- Hedge accounting approach:
  - Prepaid monthly hedges are treated as deferred revenue and recognized as monthly cost of goods sold (COGS) as capacity is consumed or as time‑based amortization if capacity is fungible and time-bound.
  - Non-refundable upfront multi-month hedges follow the revenue recognition policy: amortize over contractual service period unless a delivered performance obligation exists earlier.
- Invoicing timing: Finance must match hedge invoices to commits within the same month; mis-matched items are placed on a 1-cycle exception report for review.
- Example: $120k prepaid hedge for 3 months → recognize $40k/month as cost and amortize deferred revenue accordingly unless usage allocation requires different treatment.

Operational playbook: step-by-step (example: 30-day spike mitigation)
1) Trigger: Product alerts 7-day rolling usage > 130% of baseline for two consecutive days.
2) Action: Product files Demand Delta ticket and tags procurement + finance with forecast delta and required start date.
3) Procurement: evaluates Monthly Hedge Block vs burst credits; if hedge chosen, draft PO and route for approval.
4) Finance: performs quick economic check (IRR impact, revrec implications) and approves up to the threshold ($50k) or escalates otherwise.
5) Execution: procurement issues PO, vendor confirms, invoice routed, and capacity is allocated.
6) Post-mortem: within 10 business days after spike, Product and Finance co-author a short RCA and cost allocation note.
sections.heading: Billing and revenue recognition coordination

sections.body:
- Auto-approve (Procurement + Finance): hedges <= $50,000 and duration <= 3 months.
- Director-level approval: $50,001–$250,000 or <12 month term.
- VP/CFO approval: > $250,000 or multi-year commitments.
sections.heading: Approval thresholds (examples)

sections.body:
- Calculation inputs: baseline tokens/day = 5B, expected spike average = 9B tokens/day for 30 days.
- Incremental tokens = (9B - 5B) * 30 = 120B tokens.
- If vendor committed price = $0.0000125 per token reserved, hedge cost ≈ 1,500,000 (120B * 0.0000125).
- Finance will compare the above to expected overage pricing and potential lost revenue from throttling to decide whether to hedge.
sections.heading: Example calculations

sections.body:
| Item | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Short-term hedge trigger | +15% 30-day variance | Measured vs baseline commits |
| Hedge minimum size | $5,000 | Avoid micro-POs |
| True-up cadence | Monthly | Reconcile commits to usage |
| Invoice routing SLA | 3 business days | To commit ledger |
sections.heading: Configuration table (recommended defaults)

sections.body:
- Example SQL to surface 30-day delta (internal warehouse):
  SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(tokens) as tokens_per_day
  FROM analytics.api_usage
  WHERE sku IN ('hosted-gen', 'dedicated-gpu')
  AND ts >= current_date - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY day
  ORDER BY day desc;

- Procurement CLI example (prototype) to open a hedge request:
  redwood procurement create-hedge --term monthly --start 2026-09-01 --amount 200000 --reason \"Search release Q3\" --owner product-search@example.com
sections.heading: Data and tooling snippets

sections.body:
- Hedge effectiveness: (avoided overage spend - hedge cost) / hedge cost, measured quarterly. Target > 20% positive contribution.
- Forecast accuracy: mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for 30-day window; target < 12%.
- Invoice reconciliation SLA: percent reconciled within 3 business days; target 95%.
sections.heading: Reporting and KPIs

sections.body:
- After any hedging event > $50k or any false positive hedge (unused capacity > 40%), Product and Finance must produce a 10-slide retrospective: why forecast missed, what signals were available, and recommended model changes.

Appendix A — Standard PO template fields:
- PO title, PO number, vendor legal entity, capacity description (units and pricing), start/end dates, termination notice, refund/reassignment clause, invoice instructions, GL codes.

Appendix B — RevRec references:
- See revenue-recognition/internal-policy-2025 for detailed guidance on amortization vs usage-based recognition.

Appendix C — Escalation contacts:
- Finance: priya.nair@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Legal: contracts@redwood.ai
- Product Ops: product-ops@redwood.ai
sections.heading: RCA and continuous improvement

sections.body:
- Dedicated capacity cost allocation playbook (link internal)
- Contracting governance for capacity commits (link internal)
sections.heading: Related pages and links

sections.body:
- 2026-03-15: created by Priya Nair (initial draft)
- 2026-06-02: updated with procurement CLI and KPI targets

End of document.
