payload.page_title: Forecasted Demand Hedging and Contract Flexing Procedure

sections.body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard process for hedging forecasted demand, flexing (adjusting) contractual capacity commitments, and reconciling invoices to revenue recognition triggers. It covers operating principles, decision gates, an actionable runbook for procurement and finance, example scenarios with numeric impacts, and the technical hooks with our Billing Service and RevRec Engine. The procedure balances operational flexibility with revenue accounting controls to avoid surprise recognition or cash shortfalls.

Goals

- Reduce mismatch between forecasted consumption and committed capacity cost by at least 60% over a 12-month window.
- Ensure contract flex changes are compliant with revenue recognition rules (ASC 606 / IFRS 15 analogs used by RevRec Engine).
- Standardize a cross-functional decision path (Finance, Procurement, Product, Sales) for adjustments to commitments and pricing holdbacks.
- Maintain clear audit trail for external audits and internal forecasting.

Scope
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- All capacity and committed GPU reservations (Dedicated) and multi-month buy commitments across hosted/dedicated/private products.
- Procurement actions that change monthly committed spend by > $25,000 or change capacity by > 10% of the existing commitment.
- Forecast adjustments that materially change monthly revenue recognition by +/- 5% of forecasted recognized revenue.
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Routine one-off purchase orders under $5,000.
- Non-capacity software licenses without revenue recognition implications.

Key definitions

- Forecast Hub: Central forecasting dataset and UI used by Finance and Product.
- Commitment Window: Time interval (typically monthly) covered by a reserved capacity contract.
- Hedging Action: Any change intended to reduce the financial exposure from forecast variance (e.g., structured discounts, staged ramping, convertible credits).
- Contract Flexing: Formal amendment to an existing capacity contract to scale up/down committed units or adjust price.
- Pricing Holdback: Portion of invoiced amount deferred or conditioned on future usage milestones to align with RevRec triggers.

Roles & ownership

- Finance (Forecasting Lead): owns Forecast Hub, computes hedging recommendation, approves accounting impact. Primary contact: Priya Nambiar.
- Procurement: negotiates contract amendments and issues purchase orders in ProcureFlow. Primary contact: Marcus Lee.
- Product: validates technical capacity requirements and rollout schedule. Primary contact: Dana O'Connor.
- Legal: reviews material contract terms and amendment language. Primary contact: Arjun Patel.
- Billing Engineering: implements holdbacks and invoice metadata in Billing Service / Commitments API. Primary contact: Linh Tran.
- RevRec (Accounting Systems): configures revenue recognition rules and updates RevRec Engine. Primary contact: Miguel Santos.

Operating principles

1) Use conservative forecast bands: base / expected / upside with 40/35/25% weighting for procurement planning.
2) Prioritize flexibility over lowest initial unit cost when forecast uncertainty > 15% (measured as rolling 90-day MAPE).
3) Ensure every contract amendment includes metadata fields: amendment_reason, effective_date, capacity_delta, price_delta, pricing_holdback_percent, and accounting_treatment (defer/recognize).
4) Surface any proposed contract flex that changes RevRec recognition by > 5% of monthly revenue to Finance leadership for pre-approval.

Decision thresholds and gates

- Forecast accuracy SLO: Forecast Hub 30-day MAPE <= 15%. If violated for two consecutive periods, trigger mandatory hedging review.
- Contract flex threshold: capacity_delta >= 10% OR monthly committed cost delta >= $25,000 -> requires Finance + Procurement + Legal approval.
- Holdback threshold: pricing_holdback_percent > 10% -> requires RevRec sign-off.

Operational procedure (step-by-step)

1) Weekly Forecast Review (Finance)
   - Run Forecast Hub report: rolling 30/90-day MAPE, demand distribution (p50/p75/p90), and open commitments.
   - If 30-day MAPE > 15% OR p90 demand > committed capacity by > 20% within next 60 days, create a Hedging Recommendation.

2) Hedging Recommendation (Finance -> Product, Procurement)
   - Document options: (A) convert spot to short-term ramped commit; (B) add staged capacity with 30-day opt-out; (C) negotiate convertible credit (credit applied to future overage).
   - Include estimated P&L impact and RevRec treatment using scenario modeling (base/expected/upside). Attach model export (.csv).

3) Cross-functional Review Meeting (Ad hoc, required within 3 business days)
   - Attendees: Finance forecasting lead, Procurement rep, Product manager, Legal reviewer, Sales if customer-facing.
   - Approve one option and set action owner and timeline. Record decision in Forecast Hub as "Hedging Action ID".

4) Procurement Execution
   - Procurement creates amendment draft in ProcureFlow with amendment metadata pre-filled.
   - Legal reviews and clears final language within 48 hours for standard amendments.
   - Procurement issues PO / amendment and updates Commitments API with new capacity and holdback fields.

5) Billing & RevRec Implementation
   - Billing Engineering adds pricing_holdback_percent and holdback_conditions to invoices via Billing Service metadata.
   - RevRec updates RevRec Engine configuration: mapping amendment ID to accounting treatment and sets recognition schedule.
   - Finance validates journal entries in FDW (Finance Data Warehouse) and confirms deferred revenue balances.

6) Reconciliation (monthly, Finance)
   - Match invoices to commitments using Commitments API: ensure invoice_amount - holdback = recognized revenue per RevRec schedule.
   - Run a reconciliation report and flag any mismatches > 2% of invoice_amount.

7) Post-Implementation Review (30 days after amendment)
   - Measure actual cost vs. modeled cost and forecast variance. Capture lessons learned in Forecast Hub and tag the Hedging Action ID.

Templates & required fields
sections.heading: Exclusions

sections.body:
| field | required | description |
| amendment_id | yes | Unique amendment identifier (amend-YYYYMMDD-XXXX) |
| amendment_reason | yes | e.g., "hedge demand variance" |
| effective_date | yes | YYYY-MM-DD |
| capacity_delta | yes | positive or negative integer (GPUs) |
| price_delta | yes | decimal USD per unit |
| pricing_holdback_percent | conditional | integer 0-100; percent of invoice to holdback |
| holdback_conditions | conditional | free text; milestone or usage-based conditions |
| accounting_treatment | yes | "defer" | "recognize" |

Example amendment JSON to write to Commitments API (example snippet)
{
  "amendment_id": "amend-20270112-001",
  "effective_date": "2027-02-01",
  "capacity_delta": "+64",
  "price_delta": "-1.25",
  "pricing_holdback_percent": "10",
  "holdback_conditions": "10% held until 30-day cumulative usage >= 80% of new capacity",
  "accounting_treatment": "defer"
}

(Procurement should copy the snippet into ProcureFlow's amendment payload editor; Billing Engineering will ingest the same amendment_id.)

Accounting impact and controls

- Any amendment with accounting_treatment == "defer" must map to a deferred revenue schedule in RevRec Engine. Deferred balances should be reviewed by accounting weekly until fully recognized.
- Journal entry controls: dual review required for any amendment that increases deferred revenue by > $50,000. Approvers: Finance Lead + Controller.
- Audit trail: all amendments must include a linked Hedging Action ID and the Forecast Hub model export. Keep records for 7 years.

Monitoring, metrics, and SLOs

- Forecast Hub accuracy SLO: 30-day MAPE <= 15% (owner: Finance).
- Commitment invoice reconciliation SLO: monthly reconciliation mismatch < 2% (owner: Finance Ops).
- Amendment processing SLA: Procurement + Legal signoff within 72 hours for standard templates (owner: Procurement).
- Billing metadata ingestion SLA: Billing Service must surface new amendment metadata within 24 hours of Commitments API update.

Alerts (examples)

- Alert: "Forecast Hub MAPE breach" -> trigger: MAPE > 15% for 2 consecutive windows -> action: auto-create Hedging Action, notify Finance/Procurement/Product via Operations Slack channel #finance-procure-alerts.
- Alert: "Reconciliation delta" -> trigger: month-end mismatch > 2% -> action: Finance Ops page on-call and hold further procurement until remediation.

Example scenarios (numeric)

Scenario A: Upside demand outpaces forecast
- Current committed monthly cost: $400,000 for 256 GPUs.
- Forecast p90 indicates need for +64 GPUs in 45 days (expected additional monthly cost $120,000).
- Procurement negotiates staged 30-day opt-out ramp for +32 GPUs immediately and +32 GPUs after 30 days, pricing_holdback_percent = 10%.
- Modeled result: cash outlay month 1 increases by $60k, holdback $6k deferred; RevRec Engine recognizes incremental revenue when usage milestone met.

Scenario B: Demand shortfall
- Committed monthly cost: $300,000; near-term usage shows -20% vs commit.
- Hedging action: negotiate convertible credit equal to 50% of unused capacity that can be consumed over next 90 days or applied to overage at 80% face value.
- Accounting: convertible credit treated as contra-revenue when applied; initial recognition follows guidance in RevRec Engine based on when credit is consumed.

Governance and escalation

- Any dispute between Procurement and product about technical necessity escalates to Head of Platform (final arbiter for capacity need).
- Any change with revenue recognition impact > $250k requires Controller and CFO approval prior to execution.

Rollout checklist (first 90 days)

- Week 0: Publish this procedure and run a training session with Procurement, Finance Ops, Billing Engineering, and Legal.
- Week 2: Integrate amendment metadata schema into ProcureFlow and Commitments API.
- Week 4: RevRec Engine staging config updated to accept amendment_id mapping.
- Week 6: End-to-end test with a simulated amendment and reconciliation.
- Week 12: First post-implementation review and KPI check-in; iterate templates as needed.

Related pages and artifacts

- Forecast Hub home: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/forecast-sensitivity-and-contract-alignment-playbook-2025
- Capacity contracting governance: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/capacity-contracting-financial-governance-2026
- Commitments API developer guide: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/commitments-api-reference

Appendix A: Quick CLI snippet for Commitments API (curl)

curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwoodinfra.local/commitments/amendments -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"amendment_id":"amend-20270112-001","effective_date":"2027-02-01","capacity_delta":64,"price_delta":-1.25,"pricing_holdback_percent":10,"accounting_treatment":"defer"}'

Appendix B: Audit checklist (for Finance Controller)

- Verify amendment has Hedging Action ID and Forecast Hub export attached.
- Confirm Journal entries created / staged in FDW match RevRec schedule.
- Ensure dual approvers present for high-value deferrals.
- Confirm ProcureFlow contains signed amendment PDF and legal signoff.

Document owner and contact

Finance Forecasting Lead: Priya Nambiar (priya.n@redwoodinfra.com). For operational questions contact Procurement: procurement-ops@redwoodinfra.com.

Revision history

- 2026-11-15: Created by Priya Nambiar (initial draft).
- 2027-01-20: Added amendment metadata schema and example scenarios (reviewers Marcus Lee, Dana O'Connor).
- 2027-02-10: Published and marked internal after Governance review.

payload.page_title: Variable-capacity cashflow smoothing and collection playbook

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook describes the operational procedures, decision thresholds, and accounting guidance for smoothing cashflow and managing collections for customers on variable-capacity contracts (metered usage, burst pools, or hybrid reserved + overage billing). It aligns procurement, contracting, billing ops, revenue recognition, and forecasting so that short-term cash disruptions from large usage swings are controlled while preserving customer relationships.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: provide standardized steps to minimize month-to-month cash volatility from variable-capacity customers and reduce days-sales-outstanding (DSO) for high-usage accounts.
- Scope: applies to all enterprise and MID-MARKET customers where monthly usage can exceed committed tiers by >25% in a single month. Excludes pure self-serve free-tier accounts unless flagged by finance ops.

Principles:
- Predictability first: prefer small, contractual monthly true-ups over ad-hoc large invoices.
- Risk-based controls: escalate highest-risk accounts earlier (PSA score >= 70, see Risk Scoring below).
- Customer-first collections: use graduated, account-managed contact before legal escalation.

Key stakeholders and ownership:
- Finance Ops (billing): owner for invoicing cadence, aging reports, and credit holds. Service: rwb-billing (internal microservice).
- Revenue Accounting: owner for RevRec entries and deferred revenue adjustments.
- Sales Ops / Account Executive: owner for customer communication and contract concessions.
- Procurement (customer side interface): coordinates escalation for large enterprise customers.
- Legal: sign-off for contract amendments > $250k MRR impact.

Risk Scoring (input to cadence):
- Usage volatility (30/90 day variance): >50% = 30 pts
- Outstanding balance / ARR ratio: >5% = 20 pts
- Payment history: 1 late pay in 12 months = 10 pts, 2+ = 25 pts
- Contractual dispute history: each dispute = 15 pts
- Total score >= 70 => High risk, 40-69 => Medium, <40 => Low.

Operational thresholds and SLOs:
- Invoice generation SLA: billing run must issue preliminary invoice within 72 hours of month close (owner: Finance Ops).
- True-up cadence for variable accounts: default monthly; optional biweekly when forecast delta > 30%.
- DSO target: 35 days company-wide; High-risk accounts target: <25 days.
- Credit hold threshold: unpaid aging > 45 days AND balance > $25k (except with AE exceptions).

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Pre-close forecasting adjustment (day -5 relative to month close):
   - Finance Ops pulls usage signal from telemetry (service: rwb-usage-collector) and compares to committed tiers.
   - If projected overage > 25% of committed band, flag account and notify AE + Revenue Accounting.

2) Proactive mini-invoice offer (day -3):
   - For accounts with projected >50% overage, offer a biweekly invoice or interim true-up. AE negotiates options and signs in Salesforce (sf-opportunity ID appended to billing ticket).

3) Final invoice and allowances (day 0 to +3):
   - Issue final invoice in rwb-billing. Attach usage report CSV and reconciled mapping to contract line-items.
   - Revenue Accounting determines recognition split: immediate recognition for usage-billed items; deferred for prepayments per policy (see Accounting examples).

4) Collections cadence (post-invoice):
   - Day 1-14: automated payment retry (2 attempts) + first reminder email (Finance Ops).
   - Day 15-30: AE outreach + second reminder; account risk score recalculated.
   - Day 31-45: Senior AE + Finance Ops coordinated call; consider payment plan.
   - Day 46-60: Credit hold triggered if threshold met; notify Legal and Procurement contacts.
   - Day 61+: Legal collections and possible contract enforcement (requires Legal + Revenue Accounting sign-off).

Escalation matrix (owners and SLAs):
- Finance Ops: issue invoices and runage reports within 72h of close.
- AE: first personalized outreach within 7 days of overdue.
- Sales Ops: approve payment plans up to $100k and duration up to 90 days.
- Legal: approve escalation to collections for >$250k outstanding or repeated defaults.

Accounting guidance (examples):
- Scenario A: Metered overage invoice sent and paid within term:
  - Invoice creates AR at invoice date. Once cash collected: Debit Cash; Credit AR. Revenue recognized per usage delivered.
- Scenario B: Prepaid reserved pool with monthly true-up and credit applied:
  - On prepayment: Debit Cash; Credit Deferred Revenue. 
  - On monthly true-up (usage consumed): Debit Deferred Revenue; Credit Revenue (when performance obligation satisfied).
- Scenario C: Credit memo for billed dispute resolved in favor of customer:
  - Issue credit memo referencing invoice_id. Accounting: Debit Revenue (reversal); Credit AR/Cash depending on follow-up.

Example invoice timing table (recommended):
| Customer risk | Forecast delta | Suggested cadence | Credit policy |
| High         | >50%           | Biweekly or immediate true-up | Strict: hold >45d & >$25k |
| Medium       | 25-50%         | Monthly + optional interim | Moderate: hold >60d |
| Low          | <25%           | Monthly (standard)           | Standard: hold >90d |

Integration with forecasting and procurement:
- Forecasts must ingest committed capacity + rolling 90-day usage to generate cashflow curves. Finance Forecasting team will apply a smoothing algorithm (exponential smoothing with alpha=0.25 default) to produce the monthly cash impact used in run-rate forecasts.
- Procurement alignment: when a customer requests increased capacity, Sales Ops must issue a Capacity Change Request (CCR) that includes an updated procurement authorization and revised billing terms. CCRs > $250k ARR require procurement checklist and Legal review.

Monitoring, alerts, and dashboards:
- Dashboards (owner: Finance Analytics):
  - Monthly usage delta heatmap (by customer, product).
  - Aging buckets: 0-30,31-60,61-90,90+ with drilldown to AE.
  - Cashflow smoothing impact simulation panel.
- Alerts (owner: Finance Ops):
  - Usage spike alert: projected >100% month-over-month (severity P1).
  - Aging threshold breach: high-risk account hits 30 days overdue (severity P2).

Sample CLI snippets (internal tooling):
- Export usage for account 12345 for month:
  $ rwb-billing export-usage --account 12345 --month 2028-12 --format csv
- Create interim invoice:
  $ rwb-billing create-invoice --account 12345 --period 2028-12 --type interim --notify ae:jon.doe@example.com

Record retention and evidence for audits:
- Keep usage CSV, invoicing run log, AE email trail, and CCR approvals for a minimum of 7 years for enterprise customers. Evidence folder naming convention: /evidence/{account-id}/{year-month}/.

Appendix: common questions
Q: When do we move an account to reserved-only?
A: Consider reserved-only when an account’s monthly overage has occurred in 3 of 6 months and the ARR impact of reserving reduces expected unit cost by >15%. Sales Ops evaluates and drafts an amendment.

Q: Who approves discounts applied to interim invoices?
A: Discounts >10% must be approved by Head of Revenue (Finance + Sales sign-off).

Related policies and pages:
- Commitment usage reconciliation SOP (link above).

payload.page_title: Scenario-Based Budget Ramp and Contingency Guidelines

sections.body:
Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference's operational guidance for building scenario-based budget ramps, aligning procurement and contract commitments with forecast scenarios, and executing contingency controls for revenue recognition and billing events. The goal is to provide a repeatable framework teams can use to translate product/usage signals into finance actions while minimizing surprise impacts to cash, committed capacity, and revrec timing.

Scope
Applies to: finance, product managers, commercial operations, procurement, legal, and engineering leads who own capacity or purchasing decisions. Covers: quarterly and annual forecasting cadence, intra-quarter model updates, procurement gating for reserved capacity, and recognition/billing triggers tied to contract terms. Does not replace formal contract review with legal or the revenue recognition policy in revrec-and-billing.

Key definitions
- Budget ramp: planned change in spend (opEx or committed CapEx) from one fiscal period to the next tied to growth scenarios.
- Contingency wallet: a short-term reallocation of operating funds reserved for urgent capacity or contract coverage.
- Trigger event: measured condition (metric or date) that requires a pre-defined finance action.

Overview of the scenario approach
1) Baseline (Base case): best-estimate forecast built from current ARR/usage, average ticket size, and trend smoothing over the trailing 12 weeks. Used for monthly operating liquidity and headcount planning.
2) Accelerated growth (Upside): 20–60% higher usage across one or more products; used to size fast-follow capacity, temporary burst pool, and short-term procurement approvals.
3) Contraction (Downside): 15–40% lower usage; used to identify reducible discretionary spend and deferred capacity commitments.
4) Stress (Adverse): 40%+ deviation or major contract churn event; triggers immediate executive review and formal contingency actions.

Assumptions and inputs (what teams must provide)
- Product leads: projected monthly active usage and feature launch dates impacting token volumes.
- Commercial: pipeline coverage and likely conversion windows by cohort.
- Eng infra: lead time on GPU capacity (typical procurement + deployment = 8–12 weeks for dedicated pools; 1–3 days for hosted autoscale changes).
- Procurement/legal: minimum notice periods and penalty clauses in supplier agreements.
- Finance: unit economics assumptions (cost/token, amortization windows for reserved capacity, and recognition windows).

Example thresholds and trigger matrix
- Green: +/- 10% of Base — no action, update forecast at next monthly cadence.
- Amber: +/- 10–30% — Finance & Product triage; if Upside, provision 25% of projected burst capacity in a contingency wallet; if Downside, pause discretionary hire and freeze non-critical procurement.
- Red: >30% deviation or contractual breach risk — Exec review within 48 hours; possible re-negotiation of capacity commitments and initiation of revenue recognition impact assessment.

Procurement alignment and gating rules
1) Local purchases (< $15k): follow standard procurement workflow and do not require scenario approval.
2) Medium purchases ($15k–$150k): require finance sign-off against the current Base and Upside scenarios; include a clause for adjustable delivery dates where possible.
3) Large/committed purchases (>$150k or multi-month GPU pool reservations): must be approved by VP Finance and Head of Engineering and accompanied by a scenario exposure statement.
4) Reserved capacity clause check: procurement must flag any multi-quarter commitments with early termination penalties and notify finance for revrec modeling.

Contract clauses to watch (procurement & legal checklist)
- Billing cadence vs performance window: confirm the invoice schedule and the service delivery window to align with revrec rules.
- Capacity overprovisioning: seek proportional billing clauses (pay-for-usage over baseline) or negotiated credits for idle reserved units.
- Force majeure and termination rights: ensure negotiated notice periods match operational lead times.
- Auto-renew and evergreen clauses: procurement must prevent unintentional rollovers without a 60-day notice to finance.

Revenue recognition and billing policy alignment guidance
- For reserved capacity with upfront payments: finance must evaluate whether payments meet ASC revenue criteria for deferred revenue or should be amortized over the delivery period. Attach a one-line summary to any purchase request >$150k indicating expected revrec treatment (deferred / recognized upon delivery / hybrid).
- For usage-based billing with volume discounts: include modeled discount tiers in the forecast scenario matrix and document the recognition impact for each tier.
- Contract amendments: any amendment that materially changes term or price must be tagged in the CRM and trigger a revrec review within 5 business days.

Monthly operational checklist (minimum required actions)
1) Finance: refresh Base/Up/Down scenarios with latest trailing 12-week consumption and AR cadence.
2) Product: submit any new launches or deprecations with expected token delta.
3) Procurement: surface any near-term renewals (>30 days until renewal) with exposure notes.
4) Legal: confirm any change to notice periods or penalties in active negotiations.
5) Execs: review Amber/Red triggers and sign off on contingency draws.

Contingency wallet governance
- Size: typically 3–8% of quarterly operating budget, adjustable by exec decision.
- Use cases: emergency burst GPUs, one-off credits to customers to prevent churn, bridging early vendor invoices.
- Approval flow: pull requests up to $50k approved by Head of Finance; $50k–$250k requires VP Finance; >$250k requires CFO and CEO.
- Replenishment: wallet replenished on the next monthly close if Base scenario is met or earlier if approved by CFO.

Decision matrix example (tabular view)
Event | Immediate owner | Default action | Documentation required
--- | --- | --- | ---
Upside +25% sustained for 2+ weeks | Product + Finance | Allocate burst pool; open procurement ticket for transient GPUs | Usage report, PO request, contingency draw memo
Downside -20% for 1 month | Finance + People Ops | Freeze hiring and non-essential spend | Revenue forecast revision, hiring freeze notice
Supplier contract with early termination penalty | Procurement + Legal | Negotiate penalty reduction or credit | Contract redline summary, financial exposure calc

Forecast ingestion example (YAML)
forecast_period: 2026-Q1
models:
  - name: base
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 1,200,000
      average_ticket: 0.0025
  - name: upside
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 1,600,000
      average_ticket: 0.0022
  - name: downside
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 900,000
      average_ticket: 0.0030

Runbook: urgent funding request for capacity (<= 72 hours)
1) Product files emergency capacity request in procurement portal with supporting usage spike data and estimated cost.
2) Finance validates unit economics and authorizes contingency draw in writing.
3) Procurement issues expedited PO and confirms vendor lead time and billing milestone.
4) Legal confirms no contract clauses prevent fast-start invoicing and documents any temporary amendment.
5) Engineering stands up burst capacity and provides completion notice to Finance for revrec alignment.

Owner and cadence
- Primary owner: VP Finance (overall governance and approval ladder).
- Secondary owners: Head of Procurement, Head of Product, Head of Engineering.
- Review cadence: monthly operational check-in; quarterly executive scenario review aligned with board materials.

Reporting and artifacts to attach to approvals
- Scenario exposure summary (one page): quantifies Base/Upside/Downside cash and revrec impact.
- Procurement exposure ledger: active commitments, renewal dates, penalty windows.
- Revrec quick memo: expected recognition treatment and timing for any >$150k commitments.

Appendix A — Example approval email template (for contingency draw)
Subject: Contingency Draw Request — Q1 Burst GPUs — $75,000
Recipients: VP Finance, Head of Procurement, Head of Product

Appendix B — Quick checklist for product launches with procurement impact

payload.page_title: Forecast-to-Invoice Reconciliation: Workflow and Controls

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the operational workflow, controls, and escalation paths for reconciling committed forecasts (contracts, pipeline commitments, reserved capacity) to issued invoices and recognized revenue. It applies to monthly and quarterly close activities and to ongoing procurement-billing alignment for Dedicated and Private deployments. The objective is to ensure accuracy of billing, timely dispute resolution, and that revenue recognition inputs to RevRec are traceable to signed commercial terms.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer contracts that generate recurring or usage-based revenue (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployments, professional services).
- Bridges three teams: Revenue Operations (Revenue Ops), Billing & AR, and Procurement/Contracting (Sales Ops & Legal as needed).

Key definitions:
- Forecast Commitment: Contractual or sales-committed quantity/value used in forecasts (e.g., committed monthly reserved capacity $/GPU/hr).
- Billing Event: Trigger that generates invoiceable usage (monthly metered, committed overage, one-time setup).
- Invoice-to-Forecast Delta: (Invoiced Amount - Forecasted Amount) / Forecasted Amount.
- Material Variance Threshold: Any Invoice-to-Forecast Delta > 5% or $5,000 (whichever is lower) is material and requires root-cause and remediation.

Owners and Roles:
- Finance (Billing & AR): Issue invoices, route disputes, maintain AR ledger. Primary owner for reconciliations and month-end invoice postings.
- Revenue Ops: Map contract terms to billing product SKUs, maintain forecast model and committed MRR/ARR.
- Procurement & Legal: Review and approve contract amendments that change billing triggers.
- Finance Systems (FP&A/Platform): Maintain GL codes, post adjusting entries, and update forecast rollups.

Cadence and Workflow (high level):
1) Daily: Near-real-time reconciliation dashboard updated from billing system (Stripe/Zuora/GCP Marketplace). Exceptions flagged for >10% daily movement.
2) Weekly: Revenue Ops and Billing run a delta report by customer, product, and contract. Variances >5% are triaged.
3) Monthly close window (Day -5 to Day +7): Formal forecast-to-invoice reconciliation, ownership sign-off, and posting of any adjusting journal entries before cutoff.
4) Quarterly: Deep-dive of recurring variance patterns and contract amendment sampling.

Detailed procedure: Monthly reconciliation (step-by-step)
1. Export datasets (Day -5):
   - Billing system: invoices, credit memos, unapplied payments for the prior month (CSV).
   - Revenue Ops: forecast committed amounts by customer and SKU (CSV).
   - Contracting: signed SOWs/amendments for the period (PDF links).

2. Normalize and join (Day -4):
   - Normalize SKUs and GL mapping using the canonical product mapping table (ProductCode -> GL Account).
   - Join on (CustomerID, ContractID, BillingPeriod).
   - Compute Invoice-to-Forecast Delta and create exception list.

3. Triage exceptions (Day -3 to Day -2):
   - Auto-resolve rules (no human action required): small rounding differences (< $50), unapplied payments that clear within AR workflow, known timing differences (trial-to-paid transition).
   - Manual review triggers: Material variance threshold breach, credit memos > 10% of invoice, unexpected SKUs billed. Assign to owner.

4. Root-cause and corrective actions (Day -2 to Day 0):
   - Common root causes: mis-mapped SKU, late contract amendment, usage meter misconfiguration, duplicate invoice.
   - Corrective actions: issue credit memo, reissue corrected invoice, adjust forecast and note in contract metadata, or post adjusting journal entry.
   - All corrective actions must include an audit comment referencing the ContractID and TicketID.

5. Sign-off and posting (Day 0 to Day +2):
   - Billing & AR owner posts final invoices/credit memos. FP&A posts adjusting journal entries with reference in the supporting schedule.
   - Revenue Ops approves the reconciliation schedule by customer and marks closed.

Escalation matrix: 
- Day 0 unresolved -> Escalate to Revenue Ops lead.
- Day 3 unresolved and material -> Escalate to Head of Finance and Legal (if contractual).
- Disputes involving > $50k or contractual interpretation -> Legal & Sales leadership review; temporary hold on revenue recognition pending resolution.

Controls and thresholds:
- Material variance threshold: >5% or $5,000.
- Invoice posting SLA: all corrected invoices/credit memos must be issued within 5 business days of identification.
- RevRec hold threshold: disputes > $50,000 or >20% of expected recognized revenue for the customer in the period.
- Audit trail: Every reconciliation row must have references for ContractID, InvoiceID, AR Ticket ID, and owner initials.

Integration points and datasets:
- Billing platform (Zuora/Stripe): Invoices, credit memos, payment records; export via API /billing/v1/invoices?period=YYYY-MM.
- Forecast model (internal db): committed_mrr table (CustomerID, ContractID, SKU, CommittedAmount, EffectiveDate).
- Contract repository (DocStore): canonical PDF link and amendment history.
- GL posting system (NetSuite/QuickBooks): Journal entry API endpoints for adjustments.

Example exception report (CSV columns):
CustomerID,ContractID,BillingPeriod,ForecastedAmount,InvoicedAmount,DeltaPct,RootCause,Owner,Status,Notes
ACME-001,CTR-2025-447,2026-06,12000,13800,15.0,Overage/UsageMeter,RevenueOps,in_review,"Investigating meter config; preliminary credit memo planned"

Templates and examples:
- Journal entry example (JSON payload to GL API):
{
  "date": "2026-06-30",
  "lines": [
    {"account": "Revenue-Deferred-400", "debit": "1800"},
    {"account": "Revenue-Recognized-401", "credit": "1800"}
  ],
  "memo": "Adjusting entry: reconcile forecast vs invoice for CTR-2025-447"
}

- Contract billing mapping table (sample):
| Contract Clause | Billing Trigger | SKU | GL Account | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------------|-----|------------|-------|
| Monthly reserved capacity | Monthly committed charge | RDW-DED-RES | 40110 | Applies when customer pins capacity |
| On-demand API tokens | Metered usage per 1k tokens | RDW-HOST-TOK | 40120 | Metered usage reported daily |

Exception handling examples:
- Duplicate invoice discovered: immediate cancellation note, reissue corrected invoice; log incident in Billing Queue with TicketID and tag 'duplicate-invoice'.
- Contract amendment effective mid-month: pro-rate invoice and tag both affected periods; update forecast and create audit entry linking to signed amendment PDF.

RevRec linkage and audit requirements:
- Every recognized revenue amount used for GAAP RevRec must be traceable to (a) a signed contract or amendment, (b) the posted invoice or approved credit memo, and (c) the reconciliation supporting schedule.
- The monthly reconciliation workbook is the single source of truth for differences and must be archived for 7 years.

Automation and tooling recommendations:
- Implement continuous reconciliation using a nightly ETL job that writes exception rows to a triage queue (e.g., Jira project: FNY-BILL).
- Add validation rules to the Revenue Ops product mapping service to reject unmapped SKUs at contract onboarding.
- Build a simple UI for Billing owners to apply common corrections (issue credit, re-bill) that records approval metadata.

Checklist before close (Day -1):
- [ ] Export billing and forecast datasets
- [ ] Run normalization script and generate exception CSV
- [ ] Triage and assign all exceptions > material threshold
- [ ] Confirm all planned corrective actions have tickets and owners
- [ ] Final sign-off from Billing & Revenue Ops leads

Audit & evidence retention:
- Reconciliation workbook (PDF), invoice PDFs, credit memos, contract PDFs, and Journal Entry IDs must be uploaded to the DocStore with naming convention: "recon/{YYYY-MM}/{CustomerID}/{ContractID}".
- Retention: 7 years for GAAP/audit purposes; 2 years for operational artifacts for internal reference.

Related references:
- Revenue recognition policy (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revenue-recognition-policy-2025)
- Invoice posting and cutoff SOP (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/invoice-posting-and-cutoff-sop-2026)
- Contract amendment SOP (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-amendment-billing-cutover-2025)

Change history:
- 2026-03-12: Document created by Maya Shah.
- 2026-05-10: Added RevRec hold threshold and automation recommendations (reviewer: Evan Brooks).
- 2026-07-20: Updated SLA timing and archival path for DocStore (reviewers: Liam Chen, Rosa Delgado).

Contact for questions:
- Maya Shah (Finance Manager) - maya.shah@redwood.com
- Revenue Ops: revops@redwood.com
- Billing & AR: billing@redwood.com

payload.page_title: Procurement-to-Cash Controls and Forecast Reconciliation Runbook

sections.body:
Overview

This runbook defines the controls and operational procedures that connect procurement events, contractual milestones, billing triggers, and revenue recognition forecasts for Redwood Inference. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and revenue operations stakeholders who manage: vendor and customer contracts, invoice routing, forecasting inputs, and recurring billing pipelines.

Scope

- Applies to all customer contracts, procurement commitments, and vendor invoices that have direct or indirect impact on revenue recognition, cash collection, or the revenue forecast (ARR, MRR, and deferred revenue balances).
- Covers the end-to-end procurement-to-cash (P2C) path for both Hosted API and Dedicated/Private contract types.
- Excludes payroll and taxes (handled by People Ops and Tax).

Goals and success metrics

- Ensure >99% accuracy between contract terms and billing triggers prior to invoice issuance.
- Reduce forecast adjustment churn to <1% of ARR per month attributable to contract mis-mapping.
- Maintain an audit trail linking each revenue recognition entry to a contract clause and an executed procurement event.

Ownership and primary contacts

- Finance (Revenue Ops) — primary owner for forecast reconciliations, revrec entries, and reporting. (Contact: Miguel Torres)
- Legal — owner of contract clause interpretation and amendment approvals. (Contact: Elena Karpova)
- Procurement — owner of vendor commitments, PO issuance, and supplier controls. (Contact: Aisha Patel)
- Billing/Payments — owner of invoice generation, payment capture, and disputes. (Contact: Ravi Menon)

Key controls (high level)

1) Contract-to-billing mapping: every executed contract must include a billing trigger table (see template in Appendix) and a unique Contract ID (CID) that surfaces in the billing system.
2) Purchase Order (PO) linkage: supplier and customer POs must be linked to the CID or internal commit ID before processing.
3) Approval gates: revenue-impacting discounts, credits, or credit notes require delegated approval documented in the contract system.
4) Forecast feed locking: once a monthly forecast window is closed, upstream contract changes that affect closed months must post an adjustment memo and be flagged for FP&A review.
5) Audit trail: all revrec entries must reference a source: CID, invoice ID, and journal entry.

Procedure: Contract ingestion and initial mapping (step-by-step)

1. Contract executed (Legal stamps signed copy) -> Legal uploads signed contract to Contract Repository and assigns CID.
2. Legal populates the Contract Metadata form (contract type, start/end dates, billing cadence, termination/renewal clauses, standard revrec code) and flags any non-standard terms.
3. Revenue Ops receives CID and performs a contract mapping review within 3 business days: confirm billing cadence, milestone vs. usage billing, and discount schedules.
4. If contract is non-standard, Revenue Ops runs a RevRec impact assessment and produces an implementation checklist. Legal/Revenue Ops agree on billing trigger mapping before the contract is activated in the Billing system.

Billing trigger mapping table (required content in contract metadata)

| Procurement/Contract Event | Billing Trigger Type | Billing System Field | RevRec Recognition Policy |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Annual prepay (customer pays upfront) | Upfront invoice | invoice.type = "prepay"; invoice.schedule = "single" | Recognize ratably over service term (ASC 606: performance obligations) |
| Monthly metered usage | Usage invoice | invoice.metric = "tokens"; invoice.period = yyyy-mm | Recognize as invoiced (when performance obligation satisfied) |
| Dedicated reserved capacity (commit) | Periodic recurring invoice | invoice.type = "subscription"; invoice.terms.cadence = "monthly" | Recognize monthly as service delivered |
| One-time professional services | Milestone invoice | invoice.type = "milestone"; invoice.milestone_id = MID | Recognize on completion of milestone or per acceptance criteria |

Note: Contracts with mixed billing (prepay + usage) must list both rows and include a primary CID-level mapping.

Forecast reconciliation cadence and runbook
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Owners: Revenue Ops + Sales Ops
- Inputs: latest closed invoices, adjustments (credit notes), newly executed contracts (CID additions), churned accounts, payment failures flagged by Billing.
- Outputs: delta report for FP&A, flagged exceptions (contracts with missing billing triggers), and updated MRR/ARR metrics in the Forecasting dashboard.
sections.heading: Weekly cadence (operational)

sections.body:
- Pre-close checkpoint (T-5 business days): Revenue Ops publishes the contract change log for the month and any expected adjustments.
- Close window (T-2 to T+3 days): FP&A ingests revised inputs and posts final month-end revenue recognition journal entries.
- Post-close review (T+10): Finance runs a reconciliation: deferred revenue opening balance + billings - recognized revenue = deferred revenue closing balance. Discrepancies >0.5% require a root-cause memo.

Runbook: Weekly forecast reconciliation (detailed)

1. Pull datasets:
   - SQL: SELECT cid, start_date, end_date, billing_cadence, price_day, amount FROM contracts WHERE state = 'active';
   - Invoices API: /v1/invoices?status=posted&period=YYYY-MM
   - Billing adjustments: export credit_notes.csv from Billing portal.
2. Join by CID, aggregate billings by period, compare to forecast bucket for same period.
3. Flag items where abs(billing - forecast) > $5,000 OR >5% of forecast bucket.
4. Investigate flagged items: common root causes include unlinked PO/CID, unprocessed amendment, or manual credit memo.
5. Resolution: document fix in the exception tracker and update forecast for next weekly run.

Billing and revenue recognition escalation matrix

- Level 1 (Billing ops): invoice formatting, payment posting, charge sequencing. SLA: 1 business day.
- Level 2 (Revenue Ops): revrec policy questions, mapping disputes, reclassification requests. SLA: 3 business days.
- Level 3 (Legal / FP&A): contract interpretation, significant policy exceptions (> $50k impact) or audit escalations. SLA: 5 business days.

Controls for procurement spend that impacts revenue forecasts

- Commit-to-PO principle: Any procurement commitment over $50k that would materially affect unit economics or forecasted cost of goods sold must be routed through Finance and documented with an impact memo.
- Vendor refunds/credits: Credit memos issued by suppliers that affect recognized revenue or cost allocations must be approved by Procurement and Finance before posting.
- Capital vs. expense gating: Onboarding expenses (e.g., on-prem packaging with >12 month life) must be filtered through the capitalization workflow. See Appendix B for the capitalization decision checklist.

Audit and evidence requirements

Each monthly revrec posting must include links to: signed contract (CID), invoice(s), payment confirmation (if cash basis), and a short audit justification note. Standard evidence folder naming convention: /evidence/revrec/YYYY/MM/CID-<cid>.zip

Common exceptions and how to resolve them

- Missing CID on invoice: Attach signed contract to invoice in Billing and re-run invoice validation.
- Discount applied but not approved: Open a variance ticket and reverse invoice; require Sales and Finance approval for reissue.
- Duplicate invoice: Flag in Billing system and create a credit memo referencing original invoice ID.

Appendix A — Contract metadata template (fields required)

- CID (string)
- Customer name (string)
- Contract type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Start date / End date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Billing cadence (monthly / quarterly / annually / usage)
- Billing triggers (description + mapping table)
- RevRec policy (text reference to internal policy code)
- Owner (Sales owner, Revenue Ops owner)

Appendix B — Capitalization decision checklist

1. Is the asset expected to provide economic benefit > 12 months? (Y/N)
2. Is the total cost > $5,000? (Y/N)
3. Is the asset a component of an installable on-prem package delivered to a customer? (Y/N)
4. If two or more answers are Yes, route to Capitalization committee for approval.

Appendix C — Example remediation SQL (use with care)

-- Find invoices with no CID linked
SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, total_amount FROM invoices WHERE cid IS NULL AND status = 'posted' LIMIT 100;

-- Aggregate billed vs forecast by month
SELECT date_trunc('month', invoice_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) as billed, f.forecast_value
FROM invoices i
JOIN forecasts f ON date_trunc('month', i.invoice_date) = f.month
GROUP BY 1, f.forecast_value
ORDER BY month DESC;

Operational notes and tooling

- The Forecasting dashboard is the single source of truth for MRR and ARR; Revenue Ops is responsible for publishing the weekly snapshot every Monday by 09:00 PT.
- Use the Exception Tracker (Spreadsheet link stored in Team Drive) to drive investigations. Each exception must have a documented owner and resolution ETA.
- Critical escalations should be opened in the Finance Slack channel #finance-ops-escalations and must include CID, invoice id, and a 1-paragraph summary.

Change log

- 2026-01-10 — Initial published version (Miguel Torres).
- 2026-02-15 — Added weekly runbook steps and billing trigger table; added reviewers (Aisha, Ravi, Elena).

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Legal, Revenue Ops, Procurement, and Billing for input when developing this runbook.

payload.page_title: Blended Cost Methodology v1 (Unit Economics Dashboard)

sections.body:
This document defines the Finance-aligned methodology for computing **Blended Cost per 1M Output Tokens** (“blended $/1M output tokens”) as used in Redwood’s internal **Unit Economics Dashboard**. It is intended to:
- Provide a consistent metric definition that reconciles (within agreed tolerances) to Finance reporting and infrastructure spend inputs.
- Establish the source of truth for the GPU cost rate card and its update/versioning cadence.
- Specify allocation rules (including shared overhead and idle capacity treatment) so cross-team analysis uses the same assumptions.
- Define required reconciliation checks and sign-off gates for executive reporting.

This is **v1** of the methodology. Changes must follow the versioning process described below.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
**Blended Cost per 1M Output Tokens**

**Formula:**
- **Blended $/1M output tokens** = (Allocated cost in USD / Total output tokens) * 1,000,000

**Unit:** USD per 1,000,000 output tokens.
sections.heading: Primary KPI

sections.body:
- Tokens generated by the model and returned to the caller in both streaming and non-streaming responses.
- Tokens generated for tool/function-call structured outputs when they are part of the model’s generated output.
sections.heading: Included

sections.body:
- Input/prompt tokens.
- Tokens generated internally but not returned due to request cancellation, truncation before delivery, or transport errors (unless explicitly flagged as delivered; see “Known limitations”).
sections.heading: Excluded

sections.body: - Platform metering pipeline (token counters emitted by gateway/runtime) aggregated hourly.
sections.heading: Token measurement source

sections.body:
- GPU compute cost applied via standardized hourly **GPU rate card** (provider/region/capacity type).
- Approved, explicitly enumerated “serving overhead” adders applied as a percentage of GPU compute (see Overhead policy).
sections.heading: Included costs (v1)

sections.body:
- Corporate overhead not attributable to serving (e.g., G&A).
- R&D/training spend.
- One-time incident costs unless explicitly incorporated into the rate card for the month/quarter.
sections.heading: Excluded costs (v1)

sections.body:
- **Model** (and version / quantization profile)
- **Region** (normalized canonical region)
- **Customer tier** (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)
sections.heading: The dashboard supports drilldowns by

sections.body:
- Company-wide (all tiers)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private separation
- Region rollup (e.g., NA/EU) for exec narratives

**Important:** The KPI is reported as a blended measure, not a marginal cost. Shifts in traffic mix, idle allocation, and rate card changes can move the KPI even if runtime efficiency is flat.
sections.heading: Finance reporting commonly requires rollups

sections.body:
**Source:** Token metering pipeline aggregates (hourly)
- Required dimensions (v1): model_id, model_version (or equivalent canonical), region_canonical, customer_tier, streaming_flag, quantization_profile.
- Completeness requirements are governed by the Unit Economics Pipeline SLO page.
sections.heading: A) Token denominators

sections.body:
**Source:** Finance GPU cost rate card (versioned)
- The rate card provides an hourly USD rate by:
  - cloud/provider
  - region
  - GPU type (where applicable)
  - capacity type (on-demand vs reserved/committed vs dedicated pool)

**Provenance:** The rate card is derived from a combination of invoices, cloud billing exports, and committed contract schedules.
sections.heading: B) GPU cost inputs

sections.body:
**Source:** Infra capacity telemetry + scheduler utilization reports
- Used to estimate how many GPU-hours to attribute to each segment.
- Utilization is used for allocation of shared pools and idle capacity treatment.
sections.heading: C) Capacity accounting / utilization

sections.body:
**Source:** Finance-approved overhead policy (v1)
- Overhead adders are used only where direct invoiced attribution is not available or would be unstable at hourly granularity.
sections.heading: D) Overhead adders

sections.body: The allocation model assigns GPU-hours and cost to segments (model/region/tier) using token-weighted and pool-aware logic.
sections.heading: Allocation model (v1)

sections.body:
- **Hosted shared pools** (multi-tenant GPU fleets)
- **Dedicated pools** (customer-reserved GPU pools)
- **Private deployments** (customer VPC/on-prem; cost model differs)

Each pool has its own allocation rule.
sections.heading: Costs are grouped into pools prior to allocation

sections.body:
- Allocation basis: **output tokens by segment** within the pool, within the hour.
- If a segment is missing required dimensions (e.g., region unknown), it is allocated to “unknown” and excluded from segment drilldowns until remediated. Finance rollups must include “unknown” to avoid undercounting.
sections.heading: Hosted shared pools

sections.body:
- Allocation basis: **contracted capacity** first, then actual utilization where available.
- v1 approach:
  - If dedicated GPU-hours are explicitly tracked: allocate direct GPU-hours to that customer tier/region, then distribute to models by output token share within that customer’s traffic.
  - If not explicitly tracked: allocate cost based on reserved capacity hours (contract schedule) regardless of utilization; see Idle capacity treatment.
sections.heading: Dedicated pools

sections.body:
- v1 dashboard reporting:
  - Where Redwood bears infrastructure cost (managed private): treat as a separate pool and allocate similarly to Dedicated.
  - Where customer bears infrastructure cost (on-prem): **excluded from GPU cost numerator**; output tokens may be present for product analytics, but Finance KPI reporting should exclude these rows to avoid distorting company blended cost.
sections.heading: Private deployments

sections.body:
Idle capacity is a first-order driver of blended cost and must be consistent with Finance.

v1 policy:
- **Hosted shared pools:** idle GPU-hours are allocated across segments in the pool proportional to output tokens for the hour (i.e., idle cost is blended into unit cost).
- **Dedicated pools:** idle cost is treated as part of the customer’s pool cost (reflecting the reserved nature of the contract). If traffic is low, unit cost increases; this is expected.
sections.heading: 3) Idle capacity treatment

sections.body: - This aligns with how Finance interprets committed capacity costs: the cost exists regardless of utilization.
sections.heading: Rationale

sections.body:
Overhead is applied as an adder on GPU compute cost for each pool.

v1 overhead adders:
- Hosted shared pools: +X% (Finance-controlled value set per quarter)
- Dedicated pools: +Y% (may differ due to support/ops overhead)
- Private managed: +Z%

Note: Specific percentages are maintained in the rate card version notes and are not duplicated here to avoid stale documentation.
sections.heading: 4) Overhead policy (v1)

sections.body:
- **Monthly refresh** for invoice/billing alignment.
- **Quarterly lock** for executive KPI decks and board reporting.
sections.heading: Rate card update cadence

sections.body:
- Each rate card release is versioned (e.g., 2025Q4, 2026Q1).
- The Unit Economics Dashboard must:
  - Persist the rate card version used for any aggregate.
  - Allow Finance to rerun historical periods using the version in effect at the time (reporting stability).
sections.heading: Versioning rules

sections.body:
- Monthly rate updates are effective at the start of the month in **UTC**, unless otherwise specified in the release note.
- Finance reporting may use month boundaries in Pacific Time for close processes; where required, Finance will specify a “reporting calendar” mapping. Default dashboard time boundaries remain UTC.
sections.heading: Effective dates

sections.body: Finance requires that the KPI is defensible and reconcilable to spend inputs and platform metering.
sections.heading: Reconciliation methodology

sections.body:
1) **Token denominator reconciliation**
   - Compare aggregated output tokens from the unit economics tables vs the canonical metering totals for the same window.
   - Expected variance: <= 0.5% for stable periods; investigate if > 1%.

2) **Cost numerator reconciliation**
   - Compare allocated GPU cost totals vs cost pool totals from the rate card * GPU-hours inputs.
   - Expected variance: 0% after deterministic allocation (any difference indicates missing rows or join/filter bugs).

3) **Spend-to-billing sanity check (monthly)**
   - Compare total allocated compute cost vs cloud billing exports/invoices for the month.
   - Tolerance: Finance-defined; typically within 2–5% depending on invoice timing, credits, and accrual estimates.

4) **Customer-tier split reasonableness**
   - Validate that Hosted/Dedicated/Private pool totals align with internal tagging and contract schedules.
   - Spot check a sample of known Dedicated customers monthly.

5) **Outlier review**
   - Top-N segments by unit cost and by token volume.
   - Verify that spikes correspond to known events (rate changes, utilization drops, region incidents, model rollouts).
sections.heading: Reconciliation checkpoints (v1)

sections.body:
- Rate card version and change log
- Reconciliation report output (tokens + cost + variances)
- List of known data quality incidents affecting the window (with impact estimate)
sections.heading: For each monthly/quarterly reporting cycle

sections.body:
This dashboard metric is **cost-based**. It is not directly netted against:
- customer credits
- pricing discounts
- promotional programs

FP&A may separately compute contribution margin metrics that incorporate revenue. Do not mix definitions in executive narratives without explicit labeling.
sections.heading: Treatment of credits, discounts, and revenue

sections.body:
- Data freshness SLO is met for the reporting window.
- Dimension completeness meets thresholds (region/model/tier not missing beyond threshold).
- Streaming and non-streaming token parity checks pass.

When these gates fail, the dashboard must either:
- show a “data confidence” warning and block export to KPI pack, or
- require an explicit Finance override with a recorded reason.
sections.heading: The KPI is considered Finance-reportable only if

sections.body:
- Methodology owner: **FP&A (Rishi Malhotra)**
- Finance sponsor: **CFO (Laura Bennett)**
- Engineering owners:
  - Token metering correctness: **Nadia Rahman / Telemetry & Analytics**
  - Aggregation job + warehouse views: **Logan Wright / Platform Engineering**
  - Dashboard surfaces: **Console & Tooling**
sections.heading: Operational cadence and ownership

sections.body:
1) Finance publishes rate card update (if applicable)
2) Engineering validates ingestion of new rate card version
3) Reconciliation report run and reviewed
4) Finance sign-off recorded; KPI pack sources updated
sections.heading: Monthly process

sections.body:
- Streaming delivery edge cases: If the client disconnects mid-stream, “generated” vs “delivered” token semantics may diverge depending on runtime path. v1 uses “delivered” where instrumented; otherwise defaults to runtime counter. This is tracked as an instrumentation gap.
- Private/on-prem cost exclusion: On-prem deployments where the customer bears infra cost are excluded from the cost numerator; tokens may still appear for operational visibility.
- Timezone boundary mismatches: Dashboard defaults to UTC hourly rollups; Finance month-close may require alternate boundaries.
sections.heading: Known limitations (v1)

sections.body:
- inclusion/exclusion rules
- idle capacity treatment
- overhead adders
- rate card provenance or versioning

must be documented as a methodology update and, where material, accompanied by an ADR and a backtest showing impact on prior periods.
sections.heading: Any changes to

sections.body:
- **Output tokens:** Tokens returned to the caller as part of model output.
- **Blended cost:** Average cost including idle and shared overhead allocations.
- **Pool:** A grouping of capacity/cost that shares an allocation rule (hosted shared, dedicated, private).
- **Rate card:** Finance-maintained table mapping capacity inputs to hourly USD cost assumptions.
sections.heading: Appendix A: Glossary

sections.body:
Do:
- Always label the metric as **blended** and specify the time window and rate card version.
- Use drilldowns to identify cost drivers (region mix, quant profile changes, caching/batching changes).

Don’t:
- Compare two windows without checking for rate card version changes.
- Interpret a unit cost move as purely runtime regression without verifying utilization and traffic mix.
sections.heading: Appendix B: Reporting guidance (do’s and don’ts)

payload.page_title: Supplier Payment Terms, Budget Tiering, and Approval Patterns

sections.body: This document defines standardized patterns for supplier payment terms, ties procurement approval tiers to budget ownership, and prescribes authorization steps to reduce fiscal risk. It is intended for finance, procurement leads, purchasing approvers, and partnering engineering/product teams who request supplier commitments.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Reduce invoice disputes and late-payment costs by standardizing payment term negotiations.
- Ensure budget accountability by mapping approval tiers to specific budget owners and forecast windows.
- Provide a clear, auditable purchase and payment workflow for obligations that impact revenue recognition or multi-month commitments.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Applies to all vendor agreements, purchase orders (POs), subscriptions, and capacity commitments with total expected spend > $5,000 annualized.
- Excludes petty cash, corporate card purchases under $1,000, and pre-approved SaaS subscriptions with centralized subscriptions program.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
1) Budget-first: No commitment is valid until associated budget is confirmed for the fiscal period (capex or opex).
2) Tiered approvals: Higher fiscal impact requires broader review (procurement + finance partner + legal for contract language).
3) Standard terms default: Use standard Redwood payment terms and amendments only with finance approval.
4) Clear ownership: Each PO must list a Budget Owner (name + cost center) and a Contract Owner.
sections.heading: Key Principles

sections.body:
- Net 30 (preferred) for US and EU suppliers.
- Net 14 for one-time consultants and contractors where earlier payment accelerates delivery and vendor discounts apply.
- Net 45 only if vendor provides at least 2% discount for early payment or extended delivery milestones justify the timing.
- Prepayment (up to 50%) permitted only for hardware/on-prem installs with explicit milestone schedule and finance escrow account.

Decision Matrix: budget tiers and required approvers

| Fiscal Impact (Annualized) | Approval Chain (order) | Procurement Steps | Contracts Review |
|---------------------------:|------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| $1k - $5k                 | Requestor -> Manager   | Create PO -> Procurement review optional | No legal review |
| $5k - $50k                | Requestor -> Manager -> Budget Owner -> Procurement | Mandatory PO -> Procurement negotiates terms | Legal review if custom T&Cs |
| $50k - $250k             | Requestor -> Manager -> Finance Partner -> Procurement Head | Sourcing process, multiple quotes recommended | Legal review required; commercial team notified |
| > $250k                  | Requestor -> Manager -> Finance Director -> VP/Head of Business Unit -> CFO sign-off | Executive sourcing, vendor risk review, finance modeling | Legal + Security + Compliance sign-off |

Note: For Dedicated Capacity contracts and multi-year commitments, use the >$250k flow regardless of annualized amount.
sections.heading: Standard Payment Terms (default)

sections.body:
1. Requestor fills the procurement intake form with justification, deliverables, and preferred payment schedule. Include estimated annualized cost and budget center.
2. Manager approves and confirms there is a product/engineering or go-to-market need.
3. Budget Owner verifies available forecast capacity for the relevant fiscal window and either confirms budget or proposes a reforecast.
4. Procurement validates vendor: financial stability, sanctions check, payment currency, and collects at least one certificate of insurance for professional services > $25k.
5. Procurement negotiates standard payment terms. Any deviation requires documented finance sign-off with reason.
6. If required by tier, Legal reviews terms and negotiates liability/indemnity/CIP/KMS clauses.
7. PO issued, vendor acknowledges, and Service Commencement Date (SCD) is recorded in PO metadata.
8. For multi-period or subscription deals, schedule quarterly budget reviews and automated usage metering to feed the committed spend into rolling forecasts.

Table: Approval thresholds (concise)

| Threshold | Minimum Approvers | Additional Controls |
|----------:|------------------|---------------------|
| <$5k     | Manager          | Standard vendor check |
| $5k–$50k | Manager, Budget Owner | PO required; procurement notified |
| $50k–$250k | Finance Partner, Procurement Head | 2 vendor quotes; legal review if custom terms |
| >$250k   | Finance Director, BU VP, CFO | Executive approval; board notification if strategic multi-year |
sections.heading: Procedural Steps (numbered)

sections.body:
- Scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, termination for convenience (30–60 days), SLAs if applicable, IP assignment for custom work, data handling and residency clauses, indemnity caps aligned to budget tier, audit rights (for >$50k), and payment schedule tied to milestones.

PO Template (JSON example to paste into the procurement system):

```json
{
  "po_number": "AUTO-GEN",
  "vendor": "<vendor_name>",
  "amount": "<annualized_amount>",
  "currency": "USD",
  "budget_owner": "Name (Cost center)",
  "contract_owner": "Name (email)",
  "payment_terms": "Net 30",
  "service_commencement": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "notes": "Attach SOW and security questionnaire link",
  "approvals": ["manager_approval_id", "budget_owner_id"]
}
```
sections.heading: Default Contract Clauses (checklist to include in SOW/PO)

sections.body:
- If a supplier requires non-standard payment terms (e.g., Net 90), procurement must run a cost-of-capital calculation and obtain Finance Director approval.
- Emergency procurements (urgent infra/hardware to restore production) may be escalated to SRE + Procurement Head; documented after-action PO must be created within 5 business days.
sections.heading: Exceptions and Escalation

sections.body:
- All POs with multi-month impact must be mapped to monthly forecast lines. Procurement will add committed spend to the rolling 12-month forecast during the weekly forecast refresh.
- For Dedicated Capacity contracts, finance will create a committed capacity ledger entry and amortize cost across recognized months in the forecast model.
sections.heading: Budgeting and Forecast Implications

sections.body:
- % of POs issued with standard payment terms (target: >= 90%).
- Average days-payable outstanding for non-enterprise vendors (target: 28–32 days).
- Number of budget reforecasts triggered by procurement (>5% of BU forecast).
- Number of exceptions requiring executive sign-off.
sections.heading: Metrics and Reporting (monthly cadence)

sections.body:
- Procurement: process owner and vendor diligence (R/A).
- Finance Partner: budget verification and forecasting (R).
- Legal: contract review for custom terms (C).
- Requestor (Product/Eng): requirements and acceptance (I).
sections.heading: Owner and RACI (single-line entries)

sections.body:
1) Week 1–2: Communicate new patterns and thresholds to all BU finance partners and procurement sprints channel.
2) Week 3–4: Training sessions for managers and requestors (recordings uploaded).
3) Week 5–ongoing: Start enforcing PO gates at the procurement system for thresholds above $5k; collect feedback and adjust.

Appendix A — Example scenarios:
- Example 1 (SaaS seat renewal, $42k/year): Requestor submits renewal. Manager approves. Budget Owner confirms opex capacity. Procurement negotiates Net 30 and discount. PO executed with standard SOW. No legal review required.
- Example 2 (On-prem hardware, $320k one-time): Enterprise procurement flow initiated. Finance models capex vs opex impact. Legal and Security run concurrent reviews. Executive sign-off obtained. Payment: 30% deposit (escrowed), remainder by milestones.

Appendix B — Quick checklist for requestors (bulleted):
- Attach business justification and desired start date.
- Identify budget owner, cost center, and GL code if known.
- Attach vendor tax and payment instructions, W-9/EU VAT if applicable.
- Indicate whether vendor requires any special security or residency terms.
sections.heading: Rollout and Training Plan

sections.body:

- PO system instructions: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/po-system-user-guide
- Standard contract templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/standard-templates-2024

payload.page_title: Vendor performance and revenue impacts guideline

sections.body: This guideline defines how vendor performance (delivery, SLAs, and invoicing accuracy) is measured and how those measurements are mapped to revenue recognition and billing controls at Redwood Inference. It provides a governance model, KPI thresholds, procurement-to-finance handoffs, and an escalation path when vendor performance could materially affect timing or amount of revenue.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to all third-party vendors that supply: Dedicated capacity (GPU pools), runtime software (licensed inference components), and professional services tied to customer commitments.
- Does NOT replace contractual clauses; it operationalizes contract triggers into procurement and revenue processes.
- Owned by Finance (Revenue Operations) with procurement and legal co-ownership for vendor terms.
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Vendor Performance Incident (VPI): any event where vendor delivery or invoicing deviates from contract terms by an amount causing potential revenue impact > $10k or delay > 7 days.
- Billing Exception: invoice mismatch > 2% of expected amount or with unsupported line items.
- Service Delivery SLA: contractually defined metric (e.g., 99.5% availability for Dedicated capacity over a 30-day window).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) Procurement team:
   - Primary owner for vendor selection, SOW acceptance, and PO issuance.
   - Maintain vendor profiles in VendorCentral (internal registry), including primary contact, backup contact, contract ID, and escalation matrix.
   - Tag every contract with RevRec-impact: none / low / medium / high.
2) Legal team:
   - Validate contract clauses for acceptance criteria, change-order flow, and termination rights that affect revenue timing.
3) Finance (RevOps):
   - Maintain revenue recognition mapping and enforce billing acceptance criteria prior to invoice posting.
   - Maintain the Vendor Performance Ledger (VPL) and calculate monthly adjustments.
4) Product/Engineering (for technical delivery):
   - Provide delivery evidence (deployment manifests, capacity proofs, release notes) required for milestone-based recognition.

KPI table (monthly cadence) — how we score vendors and the resulting action:
| KPI | Metric | Threshold (green) | Warning (amber) | Fail (red) | Action when amber | Action when red |
|-----|--------|------------------:|------------------:|-----------:|-------------------|------------------|
| SLA Compliance | % of required uptime/throughput | >= 99.5% | 98.0% — 99.49% | < 98.0% | Procurement notice + 1 remediation cycle | Trigger VPI, notify Finance, pause milestone recognition |
| Delivery Timeliness | % of milestones delivered on time | >= 95% | 80% — 94% | < 80% | Request recovery plan and ETA | Escalate to Legal / Contract remedy evaluation |
| Invoice Accuracy | Error rate vs PO | <= 2% | 2.1% — 5% | > 5% | Request corrected invoice; hold non-disputed lines | Withhold invoice payment; finance adjustment and possible credit notes |
| Support Responsiveness | MTTR for Sev2/Sev3 | <= 8 hours | 8 — 24 hours | > 24 hours | Escalation to vendor AM | Contractual SLA credit request + evaluate substitution |

Mapping vendor KPIs to revenue recognition and billing controls:
- Contracts with milestone-based revenue: Revenue is recognized only after product/engineering provides evidence artifacts (deployment manifests, signed acceptance, smoke test results). If vendor KPI is red for Delivery Timeliness or SLA Compliance that affects the milestone, Finance will delay recognition and record a potential deferral.
- Subscription / capacity reservations (Dedicated): If a vendor outage causes customer-facing capacity degradation for > 14 aggregated customer-days in a month, Finance will calculate billable credits per contract and adjust revenue in the month of impact.
- Invoicing exceptions: Any Billing Exception in excess of $5k triggers a temporary payment hold for the disputed amount and initiates a joint procurement/finance investigation.

Procedures (procurement -> finance handoff):
1) Prior to PO: Procurement tags the contract with RevRec-impact and uploads the contract to ContractVault with required milestone artifacts defined.
2) At delivery/milestone completion: Engineering uploads evidence to EvidenceStore and notifies Procurement + Finance via the VPL workflow.
3) Finance validates evidence and checks vendor KPIs for the trailing 30 days. If any relevant KPI is red, Finance issues a Revenue Delay Notice (RDN) and logs an adjustment.
4) Invoice processing: Finance compares invoice to PO and EvidenceStore. Discrepancies > 2% create a Billing Exception ticket in FinanceOps.
5) Month-end: Vendor Performance Ledger is reconciled; deferred revenue and credits are posted against GL accounts: 2200 (Deferred Vendor Services) and 5300 (Vendor Credits).
sections.heading: Governance model and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Day 0: Procurement files VPI and notifies Vendor AM and Finance.
- Day 3: Vendor must submit remediation plan and ETA.
- Day 7: If plan is insufficient or no progress, Legal and Revenue Operations hold a joint review and determine contract remedies (credits, penalties, or substitution).
- Day 14+: If unresolved and revenue impact threshold breached, Finance files a RevRec Impact Notification to the CFO and pauses affected revenue until remedied.
sections.heading: Escalation matrix and timelines

sections.body:
- Scenario A: A Dedicated GPU vendor misses 10% of committed hours in a month (SLA Compliance = 89%). Action: VPI -> calculate per-customer credits; defer 100% of impacted month revenue for affected customers until crediting evidence posted; escalate to Legal for contract remedy assessment.
- Scenario B: A software vendor issues an invoice with unsupported license lines ($12k). Action: Payment hold on $12k, open Billing Exception, require vendor-corrected invoice and evidence of license entitlement.
sections.heading: Example scenarios (operationalized)

sections.body:
- Procurement pre-PO checklist: RevRec-impact tag, required evidence artifacts, acceptance tests, SLA clauses, primary contact, backup contact, billing cadence.
- Evidence artifact list (for milestone recognition): deployment manifest, test run IDs, signed acceptance email (product manager), smoke-test logs, capacity allocation receipts.
- Finance validation checklist: PO match, EvidenceStore confirmation, KPI check (VPL snapshot), invoice metadata verification, GL mapping, tax treatment confirmation.
sections.heading: Templates and checklist (appendix)

sections.body:
- VPL is reconciled weekly and a monthly Vendor Performance Report is published to the Finance-Procurement dashboard.
- All evidence artifacts are retained for 7 years in ContractVault (as required for audits).
- Changes to thresholds or RevRec-impact categorizations must be approved by Head of RevOps and Procurement Director.
sections.heading: Reporting and auditability

sections.body:
- This guideline is reviewed quarterly by the cross-functional Vendor Governance Committee.
- Emergency changes (for regulatory or major customer contract impacts) can be fast-tracked with CFO approval.
sections.heading: Change control and review cadence

sections.body:
- Document owner: Aisha Patel, Head of Revenue Operations (aisha.patel@redwood.com)
- Procurement lead: Carlos Mendez (carlos.m@redwood.com)
- Legal contact: Sana Iqbal (sana.iqbal@redwood.com)

Appendix A — Sample GL posting entries (narrative):
- On deferral: DR 4000 Contract Revenue (reversal) / CR 2200 Deferred Vendor Services (deferred obligation)
- For vendor credit: DR 5300 Vendor Credits / CR 2100 Accounts Payable
