payload.page_title: Contract Amendments and CapEx-to-OpEx Shift Procedure (Policy + Checklist) 2026

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines the standardized process for (1) assessing and approving contract amendments that change payment or delivery terms, and (2) handling transfers of capitalized project spend (CapEx) to operating expense (OpEx) when contracting or procurement events trigger a change in accounting treatment. The goal is to preserve revenue recognition integrity, maintain auditability, and provide a repeatable, cross-functional checklist for finance, legal, procurement, and engineering stakeholders.

Scope
Applies to: all Redwood contracts, purchase orders, and procurement commitments where either: a) the counterparty or contract amendment changes payment terms, milestones, or deliverables that impact timing of cash or revenue recognition; or b) procurement originally requested as capital expenditure is later reclassified to OpEx as a result of contract structure, term, or usage-based billing.

Definitions
- Amendment: any signed change to an executed contract that alters price, term, scope, or payment structure.
- CapEx-to-OpEx shift: the reclassification of previously anticipated capitalizable costs into operating expense based on contract use, contract term, or accounting guidance.
- Revenue Trigger Event: a contractual change that affects when revenue can be recognized (for example, shifting from milestone-based invoicing to usage-based invoicing).

When this doc should be invoked
- Legal proposes an amendment that extends a term, removes a milestone, or introduces a recurring/usage billing model.
- Procurement or engineering requests scope changes that convert a deployable asset into a hosted/subscription service.
- Account team renegotiates payment terms (e.g., prepay to net-60 or net-90).
- Finance identifies an existing PO or commitment that no longer meets capitalization criteria.

Policy (high-level)
- No contract amendment that materially affects revenue timing or capitalizability may be executed without completing the Contract Amendment & CapEx Review (CACR) checklist below.
- Ownership: Finance owns accounting treatment decisions and final sign-off on CapEx-to-OpEx reclassifications. Legal owns contract language and risk assessment. Procurement owns PO issuance and version control. Sales/account owners must initiate amendment requests and provide commercial context.

Approval Matrix (thresholds)
Use the following approval tiers for amendments and reclassification:

| Amendment or Reclassification Value | Required Approvals | Documentation Required | SLA to Decision |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| <= $50k                             | Account Manager + Procurement Lead | Signed amendment draft, CACR checklist | 5 business days |
| $50k - $250k                        | + Finance Manager | As above + impact revenue memo | 7 business days |
| $250k - $1M                         | + Head of Finance + Legal Counsel | As above + accounting memo + tax brief | 10 business days |
| > $1M                               | + CFO + General Counsel + Revenue Ops | Full financial model, audit trail, exec approval | 15 business days |

Step-by-step Procedure (numbered)
1. Initiation
   - Trigger: Account, Procurement, or Legal flags an amendment or a reclassification need.
   - Submit: Initiator fills the 'Amendment Request Form' (Confluence link) and attaches draft amendment, original contract, and PO/commitment.

2. Triage (Procurement)
   - Procurement verifies contract versions, PO numbers, and vendor details.
   - Assigns a procurement ticket and notifies Finance and Legal.

3. Financial Impact Assessment (Finance)
   - Determine if amendment changes: timing of invoicing, deliverables tied to milestones, capitalization criteria, or unlocks right-of-use assets.
   - If CapEx to OpEx is suspected, Finance completes the 'CapEx Reclassification Assessment' worksheet (spreadsheet template). Key fields: original capitalizable cost basis, remaining useful life, reason for reclassification, and expected P&L impact.

4. Legal Review (Legal)
   - Legal assesses risks, change in liability profile, termination rights, and ensures amendment language has clear billing and acceptance criteria.

5. Cross-Functional Decision (Finance + Legal + Procurement + Sales)
   - Convene if approval tier requires. Finance documents accounting expected treatment (capitalization vs. expense), and Revenue Ops assesses revrec impact (deferred revenue, milestone deferral, or immediate recognition).

6. Documentation and Approvals
   - Attach the completed CACR checklist, financial memos, and legal redlines to the procurement ticket.
   - Collect sign-offs per Approval Matrix. Obtain e-signature if required by policy.

7. Post-Approval Actions
   - If reclassification approved: Finance posts journal entries and updates fixed-asset or expense schedules.
   - Procurement issues updated PO or credit/debit notes.
   - Revenue Ops updates revenue forecasts and deferred revenue schedules.
   - Legal archives executed amendment and updates contract register.

8. Audit Trail and Closeout
   - All artifacts (forms, memos, approvals, accounting entries) must be archived in the contract folder (document management) and linked in the procurement ticket. Retain per retention policy (7 years).

CACR Checklist (condensed)
- [ ] Amendment draft attached and versioned
- [ ] Original contract & PO attached
- [ ] Initiator notes scope change and commercial rationale
- [ ] Finance impact worksheet completed
- [ ] Revenue Ops impact documented (deferred revenue or timing)
- [ ] Legal risk memo attached with redlines
- [ ] Approval signatures collected per Approval Matrix
- [ ] Journal entry or asset schedule updated (if applicable)
- [ ] Document stored in contract registry (link)

Accounting Treatment Guidance (practical examples)
1) Example: Milestone invoicing removed and replaced by monthly usage fees
   - Impact: revenue recognition likely shifts to over-time; may increase deferred revenue if prepayments remain. Finance must quantify remaining performance obligations and update revenue curves.
   - Suggested entry: move recognized revenue from milestone buckets to subscription revenue accounts across remaining term; adjust deferred revenue schedule.

2) Example: Capital procurement reclassified as OpEx because the item is a managed service rather than a company-owned asset
   - Impact: remove asset capitalization entry, reverse amortization schedules, and expense previously capitalized amounts to P&L in period of reclassification (unless guidance requires prospective treatment). Document tax implications.

Sample Journal (simplified)
- Reverse capitalization (one-time adjustment)
  DR Accumulated Depreciation - Equipment  120,000
  DR Loss on Reclassification               30,000
  CR Fixed Asset - Equipment               150,000

- Subsequent: expense recognized monthly as part of Hosting/Services expense

Revenue Recognition Notes
- Revenue Ops must re-evaluate the 'satisfaction of performance obligations' when contract scope or billing frequency changes.
- If an amendment increases the term but removes customer acceptance milestones, revenue may require recognition over time (ASC 606 principles).

Roles & Responsibilities (short)
- Finance: final accounting judgment, journal entries, financial memos, capital policy interpretation.
- Legal: contract language and risk acceptance; ensures amendment protects company interests.
- Procurement: ticketing, PO updates, supplier notifications, contract registry updates.
- Sales/Account: commercial rationale and customer negotiation context; ensures customer-signed amendment is uploaded.
- Revenue Ops: revenue modeling, deferred revenue schedules, and forecast adjustments.

Escalation Path
- Day 0-7: Procurement owner coordinates.
- If decision requires >7 business days, escalate to Head of Finance and Legal Counsel.
- For >$1M or material customer disputes, schedule an executive review with CFO and GC within 3 business days of escalation.

Appendix A: Amendment Request Template (text)
- Contract ID: __________
- Counterparty: __________
- Amendment summary: one-paragraph commercial description
- Reason for amendment: __________
- Value impact (ARR/One-time): __________
- Suggested accounting treatment: CapEx / OpEx / No change
- Business owner: __________

Appendix B: Quick Examples of Accepted Evidence
- Signed redline PDF with e-signature trace
- Accounting memo with calculations and reference GL codes
- Procurement ticket ID and PO change history

Related documents and references

- Contract template library: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-template-library-2025
- Procurement PO guidelines: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/procurement-playbook-2024

Notes for auditors
- All reclassifications must include a business justification and be signed by Head of Finance. Post-close adjustments will be labeled and retained as audit workpapers.

Document history
- Created by: Sofia Martinez (Finance) on 2025-11-18
- Reviewed: Daniel Cho (Legal), Priya Nair (Revenue Ops), Margaret Liu (Procurement)
- Published: 2026-01-20

sections.body:
Summary
This playbook documents the approved procedure for handling pricing variances discovered during procurement and the conditions and operational steps to accelerate billing (shorten payment terms or issue interim invoices) for contracted Dedicated and Hosted customers. It clarifies roles, thresholds, required artifacts, operational SLAs, and accounting (revrec) treatment.

Purpose
- Reduce time-to-billing when price or volume changes require invoice timing adjustments.
- Provide a consistent approval and audit trail so revenue recognition remains compliant with ASC 606 and internal control standards.
- Minimize customer disruption while protecting company margin and cash flow.

Scope
Applies to: dedicated-capacity and hosted subscriptions, multi-month purchase orders, professional services add-ons, and third-party hardware/software pass-throughs where a pricing variance or accelerated billing is requested. Excludes pure one-time refunds and simple credit memos processed under the existing billing adjustments SOP.

Definitions
- Pricing variance: any negotiated deviation from the originally executed contract pricing (discount increases, fee add-ons, or material scope changes > 5% of contract value).
- Billing acceleration: moving invoice issuance earlier than originally scheduled, shortening payment terms (e.g., Net30 -> Net15), or issuing interim milestone invoices.
- Material change threshold: dollar-amount or percentage that requires tiered approvals (see matrix).

Owners and RACI
- Requestor (R): Sales / Customer Success / Solutions Engineering initiates the request and uploads the change packet.
- Legal (A/R): Reviews contract language and approves amendments. (Accountable for contract form).
- Finance Ops (A/C): Reviews accounting impact, approves billing timing and revrec treatment, issues invoices. (Consulted on margin and cash flow).
- Procurement (C): For pass-throughs or vendor pricing changes, verifies PO alignment.
- CRO/Sales Leader (I/A): Approves commercial concessions above delegated limits.
- Audit & Compliance (I): Receives final artifact for internal control records.

Approval Matrix (text table)
- Tier 0: Non-material variance (< $5k or < 5% of MRR) -> Sales Ops approval. Finance Ops notified within 3 business days.
- Tier 1: Minor variance ($5k–$50k or 5%–20% of MRR) -> Sales Leader + Finance Ops approval. Legal informed.
- Tier 2: Major variance ($50k–$250k or 20%–50% of MRR) -> CRO + Finance Ops + Legal signoff; Procurement review if pass-through.
- Tier 3: Strategic (> $250k or > 50% of MRR) -> Executive review (CFO + Chief Legal Officer + CRO). Requires written memo and finance modeling.

Pricing Variance - Required Artifacts
1) Change packet (uploaded to Contracting JIRA ticket): redline amendment, summary memo from Account Executive, customer approval email.
2) Updated pricing schedule (CSV) showing prior vs. proposed pricing by SKU and usage band.
3) RevRec impact memo (Finance Ops template) with estimated revenue and timing delta.
4) Procurement confirmation for any third-party cost changes (vendor notice, updated PO).

Billing Acceleration Triggers
- Trigger A (Operational): customer requests earlier billing to match internal capital planning. Allowed for Tier 0–1 with Sales Ops + Finance Ops signoff.
- Trigger B (Contractual): contract amendment explicitly permits milestone or accelerated billing. Billing proceeds per amendment.
- Trigger C (Risk Mitigation): vendor price increases that would retroactively reduce margin and where contract allows pass-through; accelerated billing considered to lock in pre-increase rates (requires Procurement + Finance Ops approval).
- Trigger D (Cash/Collection risk): customer downgrade or late-payment history; billing acceleration may be used as a credit control measure subject to CRO and Finance Ops approval.

Operational Procedure (step-by-step)
1) Initiation: Requestor opens a Contracting JIRA (project: CONTRACT-CHANGE) with label "pricing-variance" and attaches the change packet.
2) Triage (SLA: 2 business days): Sales Ops assigns Tier and routes to Finance Ops & Legal. Automated notifications are sent to reviewers.
3) Analysis (SLA: 5 business days for Tier 0–1, 10 business days for Tier 2–3): Finance Ops completes revrec memo and margin impact. Legal drafts amendment redline.
4) Approval: Approvers sign in the Contracting system. Electronic signatures permitted for Tier 0–1; Tier 2–3 require recorded meeting approval and an executive memo.
5) Billing Setup (SLA: 2 business days after approval): Finance Ops creates new invoice schedule in the billing system (Billing Service v2) and sets payment terms. If acceleration is approved, update AR aging buckets and notify Treasury for cash forecasting.
6) Notification: Customer is sent a formal notice with updated invoice and payment terms; customer confirmation required for Net-change in payment terms.
7) Recording & Archive: Save final amendment, invoices, and revrec memo to the Contracts bucket (S3 path: s3://redwood-contracts/archived/2026/) and add link to the JIRA ticket. Compliance closes loop.

Accounting and RevRec Guidance
- Shortening payment terms alone does not change revenue recognition timing; revrec follows performance obligations. However, if acceleration triggers earlier invoicing for a deliverable already satisfied by Redwood, Revenue may be recognized earlier — Finance Ops must consult ASC 606 checklist and document justification in the revrec memo.
- Deposit accounting: accelerated prepayments that create a contract liability must be tracked in the Billing Service as "deferred_revenue_accelerated" and reconciled monthly.
- Hedge scenarios: when vendor cost increases are passed through, record an offsetting COGS entry immediately on invoice issuance and document margin pass-through in the revrec memo.

System Controls and Audit Trail
- Mandatory fields in Contracting JIRA: requestor, estimated variance amount, requested acceleration date, link to amendment draft, assigned approvers.
- Billing Service audit log must contain: billing change id, approver id, timestamp, previous payment terms.
- Monthly sampling: Audit & Compliance will sample 10% of accelerated billing cases for the quarter and report exceptions.

Sample billing API snippet (Billing Service v2)
```
POST /v2/invoices
{
  "customer_id": "cust_1234",
  "contract_id": "ctr_5678",
  "invoice_schedule": "accelerated",
  "payment_terms": "Net15",
  "line_items": [ { "sku": "dedicated-gpu-hr", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 50000 } ],
  "approval_reference": "CONTRACT-CHANGE-9876"
}
```

Exceptions and Escalations
- If Legal determines the amendment introduces unacceptable legal risk, the request is rejected and a remediation plan must be produced within 7 business days.
- If Finance Ops is asked to accelerate billing but cannot reconcile the revrec impact, Finance Ops must escalate to the CFO within 48 hours.

Templates and Checklists (links)
- RevRec impact template: /templates/finance/revrec-impact-template.xlsx
- Amendment redline template: /templates/legal/amendment-redline.docx
- Billing acceleration request checklist: /templates/procurement/billing-acceleration-checklist.md

Metrics and SLAs
- Triage SLA: 2 business days.
- Approval SLA: 5 business days (Tier 0–1), 10 business days (Tier 2–3).
- Billing execution SLA: 2 business days after approval.
- Success metrics: percentage of accelerated bills issued within SLA (> 95%), number of revrec restatements related to acceleration (target 0).

Related Procedures
- See: commitment-lifecycle-credit-and-sunsetting-policy (revrec lifecycle) and purchase-requisition-risk-tiering-sla-and-escalation (procurement risk) for upstream inputs.

Revision history
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-02: Added Tier 3 executive review requirement (reviewers: Santiago Ruiz, Priya Kapoor).
- 2026-05-03: Updated SLAs and added Billing Service API snippet; set confidentiality to restricted.

Appendix: Quick decision flow (text)
1) Is the variance material? -> Yes -> follow Tier matrix; No -> Sales Ops handles.
2) Does the customer require earlier invoicing? -> Yes -> follow Billing Acceleration Triggers.
3) Is there vendor pass-through? -> Yes -> Procurement verifies and Finance adjusts COGS.

Document owner contact
- Maya Chen (Finance Operations) — maya.chen@redwood.com
- For legal questions: legal-ops@redwood.com

End of document

payload.page_title: purchase-requisition-risk-tiering-sla-and-escalation-2026

sections.body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the purchase requisition risk-tiering model, target SLAs for approvals and purchase order issuance, and the escalation ladder for exceptions. It standardizes how requisitions flow from request to commitment so finance, procurement, and legal can reliably map commitments to revenue recognition and vendor onboarding steps.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference business units when creating purchase requisitions and committing to vendor spend, including Hosted, Dedicated, and Private product teams.
- Includes SaaS subscriptions, cloud spend, hardware purchases, contract services, and multi-year commitments.
- Excludes petty cash and expense reports (handled in expense policy).

Definitions:
- Requisition (Req): Initial request by a requester to purchase goods/services.
- Commitment: Binding financial obligation created when a PO is issued or contract signed.
- Risk Tier: Categorization of requisitions by commercial, compliance, and financial risk.
- SLA: Target time interval for each approval step.

Risk Tiering Matrix (determinants and examples):
| Tier | Total Value (net ARR equivalent) | Key Risk Flags | Typical Approval Path | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 - Low | < $10k | Standard SaaS, single-year, pre-approved vendor list | Manager -> Finance automated approval (48h) | Fast-track, auto-PO where applicable |
| Tier 2 - Moderate | $10k - $100k | Multi-year <=2yrs, new vendor, minor IP/data access | Manager -> Procurement -> Finance (72h) | Standard SOW, credit check, basic vendor form |
| Tier 3 - High | $100k - $1M | Multi-year >2yrs, custom work, data residency, or requiring SLA/insurance | Manager -> Procurement -> Legal -> Finance (7 business days) | Requires contract review, security questionnaire |
| Tier 4 - Strategic | > $1M or material vendor | Any strategic vendor, significant security/compliance or offshore data flow | Exec sponsor + Procurement -> Legal -> CFO (variable; target 14 business days) | Requires board-level notification for > $5M or strategic platform commitments |

Requisition lifecycle and SLAs (targets):
1. Request creation: requester fills requisition template in Procurement Portal; checklists populate for required attachments (SOW, MSA, security questionnaire).
2. Manager review: 24–48 hours to confirm need and budget center.
3. Procurement intake: triage and assign risk tier within 48 hours of manager approval.
4. Legal intake (if required): review kickoff within 1 business day after procurement assignment.
5. Contract review cycle: target 5 business days for Tier 2, 7 business days for Tier 3, 14 business days for Tier 4 (measured from first legal review assignment to redline complete).
6. Finance approval and PO issuance: target 24–48 hours after contract sign-off or approved requisition for auto-POs.

Approval routing rules (examples and exceptions):
- Auto-approvals: Items on the pre-approved catalog and Tier 1 requisitions under $2k are auto-approved by Finance if budget center has available funds.
- Delegated approvals: Managers may delegate approvals to designated deputies during leaves; delegation must be recorded in the Procurement Portal.
- Cross-charge and internal transfers: If the spend is internal redistribution (e.g., cloud chargeback), follow internal chargeback form and finance acceptance before PO.

Escalation ladder and steps (operational procedure):
1. If any step misses SLA, the current owner must escalate to the next-level owner within 24 hours, documenting the reason in the requisition notes.
2. Escalation path by missed SLA: Procurement Lead -> Procurement Manager -> Finance Ops Lead -> Head of Procurement -> CFO (for Tier 4 or > $500k).
3. For legal bottlenecks longer than SLA, legal assigns an owner and must provide a 24-hour remediation plan or suggest an interim mitigation (e.g., redline with conditional sign-off, playbook-approved fallback clause).
4. For security/compliance blockers, Security Review Board is convened within 48 hours by Procurement Lead.

Vendor due diligence checklist (minimum items by tier):
- Tier 1: W-9/Entity name, verification in vendor registry.
- Tier 2: Vendor questionnaire, basic SOC/ISO attestation if available, commercial references.
- Tier 3: Full security questionnaire, legal entity verification, insurance certificates, data flow map, and KYC.
- Tier 4: In-depth security assessment, on-site or detailed architecture review, exec sponsor sign-off, and backup vendor contingency plan.

Integration with Contracts, Revenue Recognition, and Billing:
- All commitments created via PO or executed contract must be recorded in the Contract Management System (CMS) with the following tags: vendor_id, contract_value, start_date, end_date, commitment_type. These tags are required for RevRec automation.
- Mapping examples: one-time professional services = recognized as % completion per SOW; multi-year committed capacity (Dedicated) = amortized monthly; committed discounts = recorded as deferred revenue adjustment by Finance RevRec team.
- Trigger rules: PO issued without an executed MSA for a Tier 3/4 vendor triggers legal hold and deferred PO state; Finance will not recognize revenue or bill customers on any deliverables tied to non-executed contractual dependencies.

PO JSON example (for automation):
{
  "po_id": "PO-2026-00451",
  "vendor_id": "V-9982",
  "amount": "125000",
  "currency": "USD",
  "tier": "3",
  "sow_reference": "SOW-2026-07",
  "contract_id": "CMS-2026-3342",
  "business_unit": "dedicated-capacity",
  "approval_history": ["mgr:2026-01-12T09:12Z","procurement:2026-01-15T13:20Z","legal:2026-01-20T15:42Z","finance:2026-01-21T10:03Z"]
}

(Automation note: approval_history is an array of strings in the CMS; logging timestamps enables SLA measurement and invoice matching.)

Monitoring, KPIs, and dashboards:
- Key metrics to track weekly: median time to triage, median legal review time by tier, percentage of requisitions meeting SLA, number of escalations by reason, vendor onboarding lead time.
- Targets: 90% of Tier 1 approved within 72 hours; 75% of Tier 2 approved within 7 days; 60% of Tier 3 within 14 days.
- Dashboards: Procurement Portal should expose filters for business_unit, tier, pending_days, and approval_owner. Finance and Legal each have a dedicated RevRec/Contract dashboard for contract tagging completeness (>98% target).

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- Requester: Completes requisition, attaches SOW/requirements.
- Manager: Validates need, confirms budget center, first approver.
- Procurement: Triage, vendor diligence, routing to Legal/Finance, SLA steward.
- Legal: Contract review, redline ownership, risk mitigation.
- Finance: Budget validation, PO issuance, RevRec alignment.
- Security: Assessment owner for data-handling vendors.

Exception handling examples (common scenarios):
- Rush procurement for pilot requiring >$100k within 3 business days: require Exec sponsor email, Procurement-approved expedited intake, and Legal fast-track checklist.
- Vendor refuses standard MSA change that affects RevRec: Procurement escalates to CFO, Legal documents risk, Finance may require escrow or alternate billing terms.

Change control and continuous improvement:
- Procurement will run a quarterly SLA retrospective. Action items are tracked in the procurement backlog and prioritized by impact to RevRec and go-live blockers.
- Any changes to tier thresholds or approval owners must be approved by Head of Procurement and CFO and published with a 30-day notice.

Appendix A — Requisition template checklist (fields):
- Requester name; date; business_unit; budget_center; cost_center_code; vendor_name; vendor_entity_id; estimated_amount; currency; justification; required_by_date; attachments (SOW, security questionnaire, PO template).

Appendix B — CLI snippet for procurement portal (example):
# Create requisition (example CLI)
redwood-proc req create \n  --requester "alice@redwood.ai" \n  --business-unit "dedicated-capacity" \n  --vendor "V-9982" \n  --amount 125000 \n  --currency USD \n  --tier 3 \n  --attachments ./SOW.pdf,./security-questionnaire.pdf

Contacts and owners:
- Procurement operations (primary): procurement-ops@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Finance PO operations: finance-po@redwood.ai
- Escalation: head-of-procurement@redwood.ai

Revision history:
- 2026-01-10: Initial published by Priya Nair.
- 2026-02-12: Added expedited intake steps for pilots and clarified SLA targets after Q4 retrospective (Ethan Cole).
- 2026-03-02: Updated legal review SLAs and RevRec trigger rules (Mariana Ruiz).

Related documents and links:
- Procurement vendor onboarding playbook (see related_pages)
- Contract risk tiering guidance
- RevRec mapping standards and contract tagging guide

Approved by: CFO (documented approval recorded in Procurement Portal).

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines a compact, company-wide set of controls, operational procedures, and reusable templates for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended to be a single-pane reference for engineering, product, finance, security, and people teams.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved third parties.
- Covers corporate systems, customer-facing services, and internal tooling unless a specific system-level exception exists.

Principles
- Least privilege: Access is granted for the minimum set of permissions required to perform a role.
- Separation of duties: Approval, execution, and audit functions are segregated where practical.
- Auditability: All requests, approvals, and non-trivial changes must be recorded in the canonical systems.
- Risk proportionality: Controls scale with sensitivity and business impact.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose
Provide an auditable, role-oriented approach to granting, reviewing, and revoking access across cloud consoles, internal apps, admin systems, and on-prem resources.

Key roles and responsibilities
- System Owner: Defines required roles and least-privilege permissions for their service.
- Access Requestor: Employee or contractor requesting access.
- Approver: Role owner or manager required for approval (see approval matrix).
- Access Coordinator (IAM team): Executes access grants, logs changes, and schedules reviews.

Standard process (new access)
1. Submit a request using the Access Request template in the Templates section.
2. Requestor provides justification, duration (if temporary), and scope.
3. Service owner or manager reviews and approves in the identity system (IAM ticket).
4. Access Coordinator performs the grant, records the grant ticket ID, and notifies requestor.

Temporary access and emergency escalations
- Temporary access (<= 14 days) can be approved by the service owner with a mandatory expiry timestamp.
- Emergency access (e.g., SEV-level incidents) requires post-facto approval within 48 hours and must include explanation and a rollback plan.

Periodic entitlement reviews
- Quarterly automated entitlement reports are generated by IAM and distributed to service owners. Owners must attest within 10 business days.
- Any un-attested entitlements are reviewed by the security team and may be revoked pending investigation.

Access thresholds (examples)
- Admin-level cloud console access: executive approval + security review.
- Database write access to production: service owner + SRE lead approval.
- Read-only observability access: manager approval.

2) Change Management
Definitions
- Standard change: Low-risk changes that follow an approved runbook (no CAB required).
- Significant change: Changes affecting production behavior, schema migrations, or capacity planning (CAB required).
- Emergency change: Time-sensitive changes to mitigate active incidents.

Change request workflow
1. Create a change ticket in the change management system with: scope, rollback plan, monitoring plan, and scheduled window.
2. Classification: change owner tags the ticket as Standard/Significant/Emergency.
3. For Significant changes, submit to the weekly CAB 72 hours before the window with required artifacts.
4. CAB members: SRE, Security, Service Owner, Product Lead, and an independent reviewer.
5. Post-change validation: owner runs the checklist and records metrics.

Emergency change handling
- Emergency changes must be logged immediately with the ‘emergency’ tag and documented within 24 hours.
- Retrospective review required within 5 business days.

Rollback and safety checks
- All significant changes must include: pre-change backup snapshot ID, automated health checks, and a clearly documented rollback command sequence.

3) Data Management
Classification and handling
- Data classification levels: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED.
- Minimum handling requirements:
  - PUBLIC: no special controls.
  - INTERNAL: logging enabled, TLS in transit.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: encryption at rest, access limited to role list, masking for non-product contexts.
  - RESTRICTED: HSM/KMS-backed encryption, strict access reviews, prohibited export without explicit legal sign-off.

Retention & deletion
- Default retention: product logs 90 days; metrics 365 days; backups 30 days unless longer retention approved by service owner.
- Data deletion requests must follow the Data Deletion Request template and are executed within the agreed SLA (typically 14 days).

Data transfer and third-party processors
- All cross-border data transfers must be documented and approved by Legal.
- Vendors handling RESTRICTED data require a Security Assessment and a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

Encryption and key management
- All sensitive production data must be encrypted at rest using company-managed KMS keys.
- Key rotation: annually or immediately after suspected compromise.

4) Procurement & Expense Policy
Approval matrix (summary)
- <= $2,000: Direct manager approval.
- $2,001 – $25,000: Manager + Finance approver.
- $25,001 – $250,000: Head of function + Finance director.
- > $250,000: Executive sponsor + VP Finance + Legal review.

Procurement process (vendor or capex)
1. Complete Procurement Request template with business justification, budget code, and expected contract term.
2. Procurement team validates budget availability and recommends supplier shortlist.
3. For software subscriptions or cloud spend > $10k/year, include an ops/security impact summary.
4. Legal reviews and signs contracts > $25k or any contract containing data clauses.

Employee expenses (travel & expense reports)
- Employees should use the company expense system and submit receipts within 14 days.
- Per diem / caps: see Travel section below.
- Non-compliant expenses (e.g., personal entertainment not pre-approved) are denied by Finance and will be recovered.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding checklist (essentials)
- Business justification & owner identified.
- Security assessment: at minimum a questionnaire; for high-risk vendors an architecture review.
- Contract template with SLA, termination, and data clauses.
- PO issued and budget tagged.

Risk tiers and controls
- Tier 1 (High risk, e.g., stores RESTRICTED data): Full SOC2 or equivalent, quarterly security reviews, contract with explicit breach obligations.
- Tier 2 (Medium risk): Annual security attestations, contractual SLAs, limited data access.
- Tier 3 (Low risk): Standard procurement terms, no sensitive data access.

Vendor review cadence
- Quarterly health checks for Tier 1, annual review for Tier 2, biennial for Tier 3.

Offboarding and contract closeout
- Revoke all credentials and API keys within 24 hours of termination.
- Validate data return/destruction per contract.
- Capture lessons learned in the Vendor Offboarding form.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Booking & approvals
- All business travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Request template.
- Use the corporate booking portal where available for negotiated rates.

Allowed expenses and limits
- Air travel: economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy allowed for flights > 6 hours with manager approval.
- Hotel: up to $250/night in primary metro areas; manager approval required for higher rates.
- Meals: up to $75 per day; itemized receipts required.

Insurance and emergency assistance
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency repatriation for approved trips.
- For high-risk or travel to restricted countries, contact Security and People Ops at least 14 days before travel.

International travel and visas
- Travelers are responsible for securing required visas; People Ops will reimburse visa fees with receipts.

7) Internal Templates (canonical forms)
All templates are available in the central templates library. Included examples below (snippet).

Access Request template (snippet)
- Requestor: [name]
- System: [service name]
- Role requested: [role]
- Justification: [business reason]
- Duration: [permanent | temporary (end date)]
- Approver: [manager/service owner]

Change Request checklist (snippet)
- Change ID: [auto-generated]
- Owner: [name]
- Type: [Standard|Significant|Emergency]
- Rollback steps: [commands/checklist]
- Health checks: [metrics to validate]

Procurement Request template (snippet)
- Requestor: [name]
- Budget code: [GLXX]
- Supplier: [vendor name]
- Term: [months/years]
- Business justification & expected ROI: [text]

Vendor Onboarding checklist (snippet)
- Vendor name: [name]
- Tier: [1|2|3]
- Data access required: [NONE|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|RESTRICTED]
- Security assessment link: [url]

8) Governance & Review
- Policy owner for this document: Finance & Legal (operational custody), with cross-functional editorial ownership by Security and People Ops.
- Review cadence: annual formal review, quarterly check-ins for critical sections (access, change, data).
- Exceptions: documented exceptions require a written risk acceptance and senior sponsor.

Appendix: Contact points & links
- Access/IAM team: iam-team@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com
- Travel & People Ops: travel@redwood.com / people-ops@redwood.com
- Templates library (canonical): /confluence/templates/ops-forms

Change log
- 2026-09-15: Initial release.
- 2026-12-10: Updated procurement approval thresholds and added emergency access post-facto window.
- 2027-02-02: Clarified retention defaults and added vendor offboarding timing requirements.

sections.body:
Overview
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describes Redwood Inference's end-to-end triage for procurement items that require legal review or cross-functional escalation. The goal is to reduce cycle time, ensure appropriate risk controls for contracting and billing, and provide clear ownership and SLA targets for each review tier.

Scope
- Applies to all vendor engagements, SOWs, license purchases, hardware leases (including GPU reservations), SaaS subscriptions, and professional services agreements initiated via Procurement.
- Excludes low-value purchases that follow the corporate purchasing card (P-card) policy (see Finance policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/p-card-guidelines).

Definitions
1) Low-risk procurement: Purchase value <$25k, no data access, vendor uses standard market terms, no cross-border data transfer.
2) Medium-risk procurement: $25k–$250k, includes limited data access (non-sensitive), or requires limited bespoke terms (payment schedules, warranty clarifications).
3) High-risk procurement: >$250k, access to customer data or models, on-prem or network connectivity required, escrow/KMS requirements, change to indemnity/limitation clauses, or vendor requested data residency exceptions.
4) Contracting Owner: Procurement lead assigned to the purchase.
5) Legal Triage Owner: Commercial counsel assigned to initial review.

Decision Matrix (quick reference)
| Value band | Data access | Special clauses requested | Initial path | SLA (initial review) | Escalation
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| <$25k | None | Standard T&C | Procurement approval | 2 business days | Procurement Manager
| <$25k | Non-sensitive | Minor clarifications | Procurement + Legal FYI | 3 business days | Legal (if changes requested)
| $25k–$250k | Non-sensitive | Payment / warranty edits | Legal triage | 5 business days | Senior Counsel
| >$250k or any sensitive data | Any | Any bespoke confidentiality / KMS / escrow | Legal + Security + Finance | 10 business days | GC + Head of Procurement + Security

Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Procurement Request Intake
   a. Requestor opens a PR in the Procurement system (Jira/Workday) with required attachments: vendor quote, SOW, standard T&C, and vendor risk questionnaire.
   b. Procurement Owner tags the request with one of the risk bands and assigns Contracting Owner.
2. Automated Pre-checks (Procurement)
   a. Validate vendor is in the approved vendor list and has completed KYC.
   b. Run vendor risk scan (third-party risk tool) — attach report.
3. Legal Triage (Commercial Counsel)
   a. Counsel performs 3-screen review: (1) identify material exposures (indemnity, liability caps, warranty, IP, data access); (2) verify billing & rev-rec implications (see RevRec checklist below); (3) recommend standard redlines.
   b. Counsel applies template responses from the Clause Library for common items (data transfer addendum, limited indemnity, software license grant).
4. Cross-functional Review (when required)
   a. Security: Required for any network connectivity, data access, KMS/escrow, or on-prem deployments. Security lead must sign off within 3 business days of assignment.
   b. Finance: Required for contracts with atypical billing cadence, revenue-sharing, or subscription modifications; Finance must verify revenue recognition implications and billing trigger alignment.
   c. Product/Platform: Required for technical SOW accuracy and operational acceptance criteria for managed services.
5. Negotiation & Approval
   a. Procurement leads negotiations on non-legal commercial terms; legal negotiates legal language.
   b. For high-risk contracts, the final approval requires sign-off from Head of Procurement, Commercial Counsel, and Director of Finance.
6. Execution & Post-signature Controls
   a. Store executed contract in the contract repository (DocuSign + ContractDB) and tag with metadata (see Contract Metadata section).
   b. Trigger supplier onboarding checklists: finance onboarding (AP routing), security onboarding (vulnerability scan), and ops onboarding (service acceptance).

Contract Metadata (required fields stored in ContractDB)
- contract_id: unique Redwood identifier (e.g., RDW-CTR-2026-000123)
- vendor_legal_name
- purchasing_owner: "team/person"
- commercial_owner: "Procurement lead"
- legal_owner: "Commercial counsel"
- start_date / end_date / renewal_terms
- not_to_exceed_value / committed_spend_line_items
- billing_trigger: invoicing cadence and event that triggers rev-rec (see billing examples)
- data_classification_and_controls: none | non-sensitive | regulated | restricted
- kyc_status: complete | incomplete
- escrow_or_kms_required: yes | no
- confidentiality: internal | restricted | customer-only
- signed_copy_link: internal URL to storage

Revenue Recognition & Billing Checklist (Finance items to confirm before legal approval)
- Identify performance obligations and the billing trigger for each (e.g., access to API endpoints vs. delivery of physical hardware).
- Confirm whether contract changes the timing of revenue recognition (advance payments, non-refundable fees, milestone billing).
- Map invoicing cadence to subscription terms; attach billing examples:
  Example 1: Monthly subscription — bill in arrears on 1st of following month; revenue recognized ratably over month.
  Example 2: Annual prepay — bill at execution; revenue recognized ratably over 12 months.
  Example 3: Hardware + installation SOW — hardware recognized at delivery; installation revenue recognized over acceptance period (SOW acceptance).

Service Level Targets for Reviews
- Procurement initial intake validation: 1 business day.
- Legal initial triage (see Decision Matrix): 2–10 business days depending on band.
- Security review when required: 3 business days.
- Complete negotiated contract to signature for medium-risk: target 15 business days; high-risk: target 30 business days.

Escalation Contacts
- Procurement Manager: Maya Thompson — procurement@redwoodinference.com — primary for intake issues.
- Legal: Diego Morales — diego.morales@redwoodinference.com — commercial counsel.
- Senior Counsel / GC: Eleanor West — eleanor.west@redwoodinference.com — escalations for policy exceptions.
- Finance RevRec: Priya Singh — priya.singh@redwoodinference.com — billing/revrec edge cases.
- Security: Jin Park — jin.park@redwoodinference.com — data and network escalations.

Exception Handling & Emergency Procurement
- Emergency procurement (e.g., critical hardware replacement) may be approved by Head of Procurement + Head of Finance with retroactive legal review. Document the emergency rationale and complete a post-facto risk assessment within 5 business days.
- For multi-year commitments with budget implications, Procurement must coordinate with Budget Owners and FP&A to surface commitment in the next forecast cycle.

Template Clauses (common redlines and recommended language)
1) Limitation of Liability (recommended cap): "Except for willful misconduct or breach of confidentiality, liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 1,000,000 or (ii) the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim."
2) Data Processing Addendum (DPA) pointer: "Attach DPA described in Appendix A; vendor must support EU SCCs and provide KMS integration details for customer-managed keys where required."
3) Escrow/KMS: "For on-prem or model-hosting arrangements where customer datasets or model weights may be subject to e-discovery or regulatory requests, vendor must provide an escrow arrangement or KMS integration documented in Schedule 3."

Audit & Reporting Requirements
- Quarterly procurement compliance report to Finance and Legal: list of executed contracts > $100k and any deviations from SOP.
- Monthly aging report of contracts in negotiation (by risk band).
- Post-mortem on all high-risk negotiations that exceeded 30 business days: root cause and action items.

Appendix A: Sample Legal Redline Checklist (for counsel)
- Verify IP ownership and license grants.
- Check indemnity and carve-outs for open-source dependencies.
- Confirm limitation of liability and insurance obligations.
- Ensure confidentiality duration and return/destruction procedures.
- Confirm termination for convenience and transition assistance obligations.

Appendix B: Example CLI snippet to tag a contract in ContractDB (internal tool)
$ contractdb tag add --id RDW-CTR-2026-000123 --label "data:non-sensitive" --field billing_trigger="monthly_in_arrears" --owner procurement/maya.thompson

Related Documents & References
- Procurement playbook (sourcing to recognition): /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/sourcing-to-recognition-control-catalog-and-procurement-playbook-2025
- Contract clause inventory: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-clauses-escrow-kms-data-residency-2026
- RevRec examples and policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/subscription-billing-cutover-and-revenue-timing-policy-2027

Change History
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-08: Added Decision Matrix and revrec checklist (review by Priya Singh).
- 2026-01-09: Published after Security review and updated SLA targets.

Owners & Maintenance
- Document owner: Head of Procurement (Maya Thompson).
- Document steward for updates: Commercial Counsel (Diego Morales).
- Review cadence: annual or on material policy change.

This SOP is the authoritative procedure for procurement legal triage and escalation. Any deviations must be documented as an exception and approved by the GC and Head of Finance.

payload.page_title: Capacity Contracting and Financial Governance Guidance

sections.body:
Purpose:

Provide concrete governance for how Redwood ties multi-month capacity contracts to budgeting, procurement, legal review, and revenue recognition. This guidance is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales, and Platform teams responsible for capacity commitments.

Executive summary:
- Treat all multi-month reserved GPU capacity agreements as cross-functional commitments that require synchronized forecasting, procurement timing, and revrec mapping.
- Establish predictable thresholds and a clear approval chain to protect financial runway while enabling sales to secure competitive terms for customers.
- Define operational steps to recover value from unused capacity and to limit exposure from long-term discounts.

Definitions and thresholds:
- Normalized Capacity Unit (CU): defined as a normalized GPU serving slot used for financial planning.
- Strategic Commitment: any deal or purchase that meets one or more: total contract value >= $300,000; term >= 12 months; or new private deployment requiring managed control plane.
- Short Commitment: term < 12 months and value < $300,000.

Forecasting requirements:
1) Data inputs and owners:
   - Sales: deal pipeline and expected go-live dates (weekly updates).
   - Product: expected feature-driven demand multipliers for each customer cohort (quarterly).
   - Eng-SRE: measured CU utilization by cluster and projected p95 latency impact (daily metrics, monthly summary).
   - Finance: converts utilization into cashflow impacts and runway scenarios (monthly).
2) Minimum forecast horizon: 12 months rolling, with a 24-month strategic view for any Strategic Commitment.

Procurement and purchase timing:
- Preferred procurement window: align purchases to next fiscal quarter planning cycle unless emergency scale required by SRE.
- For Strategic Commitments, procurements should start RFP and pricing negotiation at least 60 days before the expected capacity start date.
- Payment options must be assessed for their RevRec impact: prepaid discounts versus monthly billing. Finance will simulate cashflow and deferred revenue impacts before approval.

Approval matrix (roles and thresholds):
- Procurement lead: approves Short Commitments up to $300k total value.
- Finance Director: approves Strategic Commitments below $1M and certifies runway impact.
- CFO: approves Strategic Commitments >= $1M or any deal that reduces runway coverage below the target threshold defined by Finance.
- Legal: must sign off on termination, exit, data residency, and SLA credit language for all Strategic Commitments.

Contract language standards (minimum required clauses):
- Service start definition: explicit acceptance tests or go-live criteria that trigger the start of service and billing.
- SLA credit mechanics: clear measurement window, credit calculation, and dispute resolution timing.
- Reuse and allocation: where permissible, include a clause allowing Redwood to reallocate or resell unused committed capacity after a notice period, subject to customer privacy constraints.
- Buyout option: standardized buyout formula for early termination to avoid open-ended exposure.

Revenue recognition guidance:
- Prepaid capacity fees: record as deferred revenue and recognize ratably over the contractual service period beginning at the service start.
- Monthly invoiced capacity: recognize as revenue in the period services are rendered.
- Implementation fees for private deployments: recognize on delivery milestones if separable; otherwise, amortize over the contractual period.
- Discounts tied to term length: clearly map discount percentage to gross contract value, and reflect the net price in revrec modeling.

Unused capacity and breakage mitigation:
- 0	60 days after go-live: account teams and SRE collaborate to migrate eligible workloads into the committed pool.
- 61	120 days: Finance and Sales may offer transferable credits for other internal customers or partner marketplace placement where contract permits.
- >120 days: leadership decision to apply a contractual buyout, marketing resale, or write-down. All outcomes must be recorded in the Contract Exceptions log.

Discount policy and controls:
- Standard term discounts (illustrative): 12 months = 8% max; 24 months = 16% max; 36+ months = 20% max.
- Any nonstandard commercial terms or increased discounts require a Contract Exceptions entry and sign-off from Finance Director and Legal Counsel.

Operational runbooks (step-by-step):
- Monthly alignment runbook (owner: Finance)
  1. Pull pipeline from CRM and map to expected CU start dates.
  2. Reconcile with SRE utilization dashboard and compute additional CU needs.
  3. Publish Capacity Funding Memo: required funding, recommended payment terms, and runway impact.
  4. If procurement is recommended, open Jira procurement ticket and attach Capacity Funding Memo.
- Contract close runbook (owner: Legal + Finance)
  1. Validate contract metadata: start date, billing cadence, termination language, and SLA definitions.
  2. Confirm RevRec treatment and chart of accounts mapping.
  3. Enter the contract into the RevRec system with monthly recognition schedule.

Reporting and KPIs:
- Monthly Capacity Financial Report must include: total committed CUs, utilization rate, deferred revenue for capacity, runway coverage months, and top 10 at-risk contracts.
- KPIs: coverage ratio (target >= 6 months), average utilization by cluster (goal > 70%), breakage rate (goal < 5% of committed spend).

Escalation and exceptions:
- If coverage ratio drops below 4 months, Finance and Procurement execute an emergency review and produce mitigation options within 7 business days.
- All Contract Exceptions are reviewed quarterly by a cross-functional panel (Finance, Legal, Sales, Eng-SRE).

Implementation actions (next 90 days):
- Update the standard contract template to add reuse and buyout language (owner: Legal).
- Automate the CU conversion step inside the Forecast workbook using per-route telemetry APIs (owner: Finance + Eng Platform).
- Pilot a transfer-credit program for internal teams to absorb unused capacity (owner: Revenue Ops).

Revision history:
- 2026-01-10: Document created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-01: Clarified procurement windows and added buyout guidance.

Primary contacts and owners:
- Finance owner: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.example)
- Procurement contact: Evan Park (epark@redwood.example)
- Legal contact: Priya Natarajan (pnatarajan@redwood.example)

End of guidance.

payload.page_title: Contract Pricing Escalation & Billing Rules Engine — Playbook

sections.body: Summary: This playbook defines the Contract Pricing Escalation and Billing Rules Engine used by Redwood Inference to: (1) apply contractually-accurate pricing changes to invoices, (2) route pricing disputes and exceptions to the correct finance/legal/ops owners, and (3) ensure revenue recognition and billing automation behave predictably across hosted, dedicated and private deployment billing models. Scope and applicability: - Applies to all customer contract amendments, price adjustments, promotional credits, and capacity/commitment modifications for hosted API, Dedicated and Private products. - Excludes one-off partner integrations handled by Partner Ops (see related pages). - Effective for deals with signature date >= 2026-01-01; legacy deals are managed per Contract Amendment SOP. Goals and success metrics: - Automation coverage: 80% of routine price-change events should be handled end-to-end by the rules engine without manual intervention. - Billing accuracy: < 0.5% invoice adjustment rate caused by pricing logic errors. - Dispute SLA: 2 business days Triage, 10 business days Resolution for standard pricing disputes. Key concepts and definitions: - Pricing Rule: A discrete rule that maps contract terms (tier, region, feature flags, commitment band) to invoice line pricing and metadata. - Effective Window: Start/end timestamps when a pricing rule is valid for usage correlation. - Billing Token: Atomic meter unit used in invoicing (tokens for generation, embedding units, dedicated-GPU-hours). - Escalation Path: Pre-defined sequence of owners for exceptions (Billing Ops -> RevRec -> Legal -> Sales). Owners and contact points: - Billing Rules Engine Owner: Finance Systems (primary) — lead: Ethan Calder — billing-systems@redwood.ai - Legal Approval for Contract Changes: Legal Counsel — lead: Sofia Martinez — legal-contracts@redwood.ai - Revenue Recognition Owner: RevRec Team — lead: Daniel Cho — revrec@redwood.ai High-level architecture: - Ingestion: Contract ingestion service (contracts-api) converts signed contract PDFs/CLM entries into canonical JSON terms. - Rule Compiler: Translates contract terms into executable pricing rules applied by the Billing Rules Engine. - Execution: Billing Engine applies rules to usage events; results are stored in the invoice staging table and reconciled with ledger. - Observability: Per-customer rule application trace stored in the rules-audit index (retention 365 days). Example pricing-rule snippet (YAML): --- rule_id: dedicated-commit-band-42 priority: 200 match: product: dedicated region: eu-west-1 commitment_band: 1000-4999 actions: unit_price: 1.75 # USD per GPU-hour apply_credit: false revrec_mapping: committed_revenue effective_window: start: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z end: 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z --- Escalation matrix (rule exception types): 1) Mismatch between contract and compiled rule (Validation Error) - Auto-notify: Billing Systems + Legal (within 1 hour) - Triage owner: Billing Systems (2 business hours) - Escalate to Legal after 1 business day if unresolved 2) Disputed invoice due to price interpretation (Customer Dispute) - Auto-notify: CS Rep + Billing Ops + Sales AE - Triage owner: Billing Ops (2 business days) - Secondary: RevRec review if revenue impact > $10,000 3) Rule executable failure (Runtime) - Pager: On-call Billing SRE (pager after 10 minutes) - Fallback: Apply previous known-good rule and create corrective invoice if necessary Change control and approvals: - Minor pricing adjustments (<= 5% of contract list price and no revrec mapping changes): Finance Systems approval only (ticket in FIN-BILL queue). - Material changes (> 5% or any revrec mapping change): Legal + RevRec + Finance Systems sign-off. Sales Ops must attach ACORD form for delegated discounts. - All approved changes must be timestamped and stored in contracts-audit with the signer, ticket id, and rationale. Billing reconciliation & cutover checklist (when a rule changes mid-billing-cycle): 1) Freeze rule generation timestamp (T0) and snapshot current rule set. 2) Run pre-cutover dry-run against the billing-staging dataset. 3) Compare delta: - Net invoice delta <= $2,000 or <= 0.5% of run total -> allow automated cutover. - Otherwise -> require manual review and scheduled cutover window. 4) Post-cutover: auto-generate corrective invoices for retroactive deltas that meet schedule policy. Revenue recognition alignment: - Each pricing rule must declare revrec_mapping: committed_revenue | usage_revenue | other_specified. - Deferred revenue entries generated by the Billing Engine must include a source_rule_id and contract_signature_date. - RevRec team runs monthly reconciliation comparing rules-audit with general ledger; exceptions flagged for investigation within 5 business days. Dispute handling and customer credits: - Dispute window default: 60 days from invoice date unless contract specifies otherwise. - Temporary credits may be issued by Billing Ops up to $5,000 for low-risk disputes; amounts above require RevRec + Legal approval. - Credits must be delivered as invoice adjustments (negative invoice lines) or account-level credits with an expiry date. Operational runbook (common procedures): - Validate new contract ingestion: 1. Pull contract from CLM (contracts-api). 2. Run contract-compiler dry-run. 3. Check rule compilation log for warnings (SEV>0). 4. Approve and tag with approval ticket (FIN-BILL-XXXX). - Emergency rollback of a rule set: 1. Open FIN-BILL incident and notify RevRec + Legal. 2. Switch billing-engine to last-known-good ruleset (older snapshot). 3. Reprocess invoices affected during failure window and notify stakeholders. Audit, controls and evidence collection: - All rule changes must be logged in contracts-audit with: actor, timestamp, before/after JSON, approval ticket id. - Quarterly internal audit will sample 10% of rule changes, focusing on material discounts and revrec mapping changes. - Evidence retained for 7 years for regulated customers; default retention is 3 years. Appendix A — Threshold reference table: | Threshold name | Trigger | Unit | Owner | |---------------|---------:|------:|------------------| | Material Change | > 5% price delta | % | Legal + RevRec | | High Revenue Impact | > $10,000 | USD | RevRec | | Auto-credit ceiling | <= $5,000 | USD | Billing Ops | | Dispute window | 60 | days | Billing Ops | Appendix B — Example scenarios: - Scenario 1: Customer upgrades Dedicated commitment mid-month. Steps: Sales creates amendment, Contract ingestion runs, Billing Rules Engine compiles new rule with effective start aligned to amendment time. Dry-run performed; if delta small, automatic cutover; else scheduled cutover and customer notified. - Scenario 2: Promotional credit applied retroactively. Steps: Sales Ops creates promo ticket, Legal validates T&C, Billing Ops issues adjustment invoice with negative line and expiry metadata. RevRec maps to other_specified revenue. Related artifacts and links: - contracts-api onboarding guide (internal link) - FIN-BILL queue playbook (Jira board FIN-BILL) - RevRec monthly template (spreadsheet) Revision history: - 2025-11-15: Initial draft (Priya Nair) - 2026-01-28: Added automated cutover thresholds and YAML example (Ethan Calder) - 2026-02-20: Hardened dispute SLAs and retention notes (Sofia Martinez) Questions or change requests: Open a request in the FIN-BILL Confluence comments or file a Jira ticket (FIN-BILL) and tag the Billing Rules Engine owner.

payload.page_title: Contract Change Financial Impact Playbook

sections.body:
Overview
=======

Purpose: This playbook describes the cross-functional procedure for assessing the financial impact of contract changes (amendments, addenda, credits, term extensions, early terminations, SOW changes) and operationalizing updates into the budget, forecast, procurement system, and revenue recognition. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Sales Operations, Procurement and Revenue Operations.

Scope: Applies to all customer and vendor contract changes that: (a) alter committed revenue/expense by >= $25,000 annualized, or (b) change billing timing by more than 30 days, or (c) modify contract term by > 90 days. Lower-value changes may follow an abbreviated path in Section: "Quick Path".

Principles
----------
- Single source of truth: Contract system (DocuSign/CLM) + Billing system (Stripe/Zuora) + Forecast (Adaptive/Anaplan) must be consistent.
- Fast, auditable decisions: Target review SLA is 5 business days for standard amendments, 10 business days for complex amendments.
- Clear ownership: Each amendment must have a named Financial Reviewer and Legal Reviewer recorded in the contract record.
- RevRec-first mindset: Changes are evaluated with ASC 606 (or local GAAP equivalent) impact as the gating criterion for recognition and deferral treatment.

Key Stakeholders and Roles
--------------------------
- Requesting Team (Sales/Procurement) — owns business justification and customer communication.
- Legal — validates contractual language and signs the amendment.
- Finance (RevRec) — determines revenue recognition impact and accounting treatment.
- FP&A — updates forecast and budget, communicates variance to owners.
- Billing/Revenue Ops — updates billing system, issues credits/invoices, and ensures collections mapping.
- Procurement (vendor-side changes) — mirrors process for cost-side impact.

Definitions
-----------
- Amendment: any signed document that changes price/term/delivery of an existing contract.
- Material Change: change meeting scope thresholds in Scope section.
- Billing Trigger: the event that drives invoice issuance (e.g., effective date, milestone completion).

Decision Matrix (text table)
---------------------------
This table should be reproduced in the contract record as a checklist.

| Change Type | Material Threshold | Accounting Gate | Primary Reviewer | SLA |
|------------|--------------------|-----------------|------------------|-----|
| Price increase / decrease | >= $25k ARR | Assess for contract modification under ASC 606; remeasurement or cumulative catch-up | Finance (RevRec) | 5 biz days |
| Term extension / contraction | > 90 days | Evaluate effect on performance obligations and timing of recognition | Finance (RevRec) | 7 biz days |
| Billing schedule change (defer/accelerate) | Any change > 30 days | Determine whether contract consideration remains the same and if modification leads to variable consideration | Finance + Billing Ops | 5 biz days |
| Credit / refund request | Any | Assess whether credit is a separate transaction or reduces consideration | Finance + Legal | 5 biz days |
| SOW / deliverable re-scope | Any | Determine whether scope change creates new distinct performance obligations | Finance + PM | 10 biz days |

Procedure: Contract Change Review (detailed)
-------------------------------------------
1. Intake and triage (Requesting Team)
   - Create amendment record in CLM within 1 business day, attach redline and business rationale.
   - Tag the record with estimated financial impact (must be a number or range).
   - Assign primary Financial Reviewer (FP&A or RevRec) and Legal Reviewer in the CLM.

2. Legal review (Legal)
   - Confirm amendment language is executable and capture effective date, termination provisions, and any warranty/penalty clauses.
   - If new terms change risk profile, escalate to Security/Compliance.

3. Accounting impact analysis (Finance — RevRec)
   - Within SLA, run a modification assessment aligned to ASC 606 checklist:
     a. Is there a separate distinct good/service?
     b. Does the change add a distinct price that reflects standalone selling price?
     c. Does performance obligation period change?
   - Outcome: (i) No change to recognized revenue (operational update only), (ii) Prospective treatment (future billing adjusted), (iii) Cumulative catch-up (unless contract scope indicates otherwise).
   - Document: accounting memo (one paragraph) and store in CLM record.

4. Forecast and budget update (FP&A)
   - If material, update the rolling forecast and mark variance reason code: "Contract Amendment".
   - Recalculate ARR / TCV impact and update pipeline/commit numbers.
   - Communicate changes to Sales leadership and Customer Success if renewal/health is impacted.

5. Billing system execution (Billing/Revenue Ops)
   - Translate amendment into billing instructions: invoice schedule, credit memos, proration rules.
   - Implement credits or invoices only after Finance memo sign-off.
   - For refunds/credits > $10k, require Treasury approval for cash impact.

6. Procurement (vendor-side changes)
   - Mirror the steps above for supplier contract changes.
   - Ensure PO amendments are issued before accepting changed supplier on new terms.

7. Close and audit trail
   - Mark record as "Complete" in CLM and attach all artifacts (signed amendment, accounting memo, billing ticket, forecast update).
   - Update monthly contract-change register owned by Finance Ops.

Quick Path: Low-value changes (< $25k ARR and no timing change)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- Sales/Procurement may route to an expedited review: Legal notification + Billing Ops update with a single-step Finance acknowledgement email. Target SLA: 2 business days.

Templates and Examples
---------------------
- Accounting memo template (one-paragraph): "Contract ABC amendment increases monthly fee from $X to $Y effective DATE. Assessment: There is no new distinct performance obligation; the amendment is a contract modification accounted for prospectively; deferred revenue change = $Z. Reviewer: NAME, DATE."

- Billing instruction example (free text to Billing Ops):
  "Apply prorated credit of $2,400 on invoice 2026-001 for period 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30. Issue one-time invoice of $12,000 on 2026-05-01 for new service. Reference contract: C-2026-589."

Accounting and RevRec Notes (practical rules)
---------------------------------------------
- Use the following fast checks: if price change is for a distinct add-on with standalone price -> treat as separate contract; if the change modifies remaining promised goods/services -> treat as contract modification.
- For term > 12 months additions that include discounts, compute implicit rate and compare to historical ARR to determine variable consideration constraints.
- All cumulative catch-ups must be approved by Accounting Manager and recorded in the close period following sign-off.

Systems and Tags
----------------
- CLM: DocuSign + ContractWorkbench (contract-id). Required fields on amendment record: financial-impact-estimate, finance-reviewer, legal-reviewer, revrec-treatment, billing-ticket-id.
- Forecast system: Tag change with variance code "CONTRACT_AMENDMENT" and include CLM id.
- Billing system: All credits must reference both invoice-id and CLM-id.

SLAs and Escalation Path
------------------------
- Standard escalation: 48 hours after SLA breach -> Finance Manager; 72 hours -> Head of Finance; 5 business days -> CFO notification for enterprise accounts.

Audit Controls and Evidence
---------------------------
- Required artifacts for audit: signed amendment, accounting memo, updated invoice(s) or credit memos, FP&A forecast snapshot before/after, email approvals when applicable.
- Retain artifacts for minimum 7 years per company retention policy.

Operational metrics to track
--------------------------
- Median time to close amendment (target: <= 5 business days).
- % of amendments triggering cumulative catch-up.
- Number of forecast adjustments attributable to contract changes (monthly).
- Billing exceptions created per quarter.

Appendix: Checklist (to paste into CLM record)
---------------------------------------------
1. Amendment uploaded to CLM with business rationale.
2. Financial estimate entered.
3. Legal and Finance reviewers assigned.
4. Accounting memo attached.
5. Billing ticket created and linked.
6. Forecast updated (if material).
7. Signed amendment stored and record closed.

Owners and Contacts
-------------------
- Finance (RevRec lead): Priya Kapoor (priya.kapoor@redwood.com)
- FP&A: Ethan Morales (ethan.morales@redwood.com)
- Legal: Marta Alvarez (marta.alvarez@redwood.com)
- Billing Ops: Sarah Nguyen (sarah.nguyen@redwood.com)

Related reading
---------------
- Forecast sensitivity and contract alignment playbook (linked)
- Contract amendment accounting procedure (linked)

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-10-12: Created by Jordan Liao (initial draft).
- 2026-01-08: Added Quick Path and adjusted SLAs after pilot.
- 2026-03-15: Published with reviewer approvals and template examples.

Notes and next steps
--------------------
- Pilot: Finance Ops will run a 3-month pilot (Apr–Jun 2026) tracking time-to-close and the percentage of amendments requiring cumulative catch-up.
- Action: Integrate CLM required fields into the DocuSign template by end of Q2 2026.

payload.page_title: Integrated Cashflow Scenario Playbook for Commitments and Billing

sections.body:
Purpose and scope

This playbook explains how Finance, Legal, Procurement and Sales coordinate to produce consistent cashflow forecasts, billing schedules, and revenue recognition outcomes for contracts that include committed or reserved capacity ("Dedicated" offers). It consolidates common scenarios, decision triggers, required metadata, and example journal entries. Use this document when closing or amending capacity commitments, planning forecast scenarios, or preparing monthly close adjustments.

Key objectives
- Ensure forecasts match contractual billing triggers and the timing of service performance.
- Standardize handoffs between Sales / Solutions / Procurement and Finance.
- Reduce last-minute forecast corrections at month-end by defining inputs, owners and SLAs.
- Provide reproducible templates for scenario-driven cashflow analysis.

Audience
- Finance (FP&A, RevRec, Accounting)
- Legal and Contracts team
- Sales and Solutions Engineering
- Procurement and Billing Operations
- Customer Success (for acceptance and onboarding timing)

Definitions and required contract metadata
- Committed Monthly Fee: fixed monthly charge for reserved capacity (USD).
- Minimum Contract Term: length in months.
- Start of Service (SoS): date when customer can begin production on provisioned capacity.
- Acceptance Date: date when customer confirmatory acceptance or automatic acceptance criteria are met.
- Billing Trigger: event that causes an invoice (e.g., SoS, contract effective date, first usage).
- Non-Refundable Setup: portion of fee invoiced/recognised upfront.

Every contract record in the CRM (and downstream contract database) must include these fields: contract_id, customer_tier, committed_monthly_fee, minimum_term_months, setup_fee_usd, billing_trigger, start_of_service_date, acceptance_criteria, cancellation_terms, payment_terms_days.

Ownership and SLAs
- Sales: populate contract metadata and tag deal as DEDICATED in CRM at contract signature (SLA 24 hours).
- Legal: verify contract metadata and mark exceptions if billing deviates from standard templates (SLA 48 hours).
- Procurement/Billing Ops: convert contract into subscription record and schedule first invoice (SLA 3 business days after SoS or billing trigger).
- RevRec: verify recognition method and provide forecast impact to FP&A (SLA 2 business days after invoice is scheduled).
- FP&A: update cashflow forecast and scenario models (SLA weekly cadence, and special ad hoc within 2 business days of material contract changes).

Scenario matrix (summary)
|| Scenario || Forecast impact || RevRec trigger || Billing cadence || Primary owner ||
| New Dedicated Contract (standard) | +Committed monthly revenue starts on SoS; one-time setup cash inflow on setup_fee | Revenue ratably over contract unless setup_fee non-refundable (see contract) | Monthly in advance or upfront per contract | Sales -> Billing Ops |
| Contract Amendment (term/fee change) | Delta applied pro‑rata from amendment effective date | RevRec adjusts prospectively; catch-up adjustments if prior invoices were incorrect | Adjusted monthly invoices or credit/memo | Sales + RevRec |
| Early Termination (customer pays termination fee) | Immediate cash inflow (termination fee) and loss of future committed revenue | Termination fee recognized on receipt if not performance-based; remaining prepayments reviewed for refund liability | One-time invoice | Legal + Finance |
| Conversion from Trial / POC to Committed | Forecast steps up over provisioning timeline | Recognize when acceptance and billing trigger met; if trial fees credited, apply credit mechanics | Typically monthly forward billing | Sales + Customer Success |

Detailed procedures and checklists
1) New Dedicated Contract — from signature to first recognized revenue
   a) At signature (Sales): tag CRM record with committed_monthly_fee, minimum_term_months, setup_fee_usd, billing_trigger and expected SoS.
   b) Legal: confirm billing_trigger language ("upon provisioning", "upon acceptance", or "on effective date"). If nonstandard, create a Contract Exception and notify RevRec.
   c) Solutions/Infra: open onboarding ticket (JIRA/Runbook) to provision capacity. Provisioning ETA must be captured in CRM within 24 hours.
   d) Customer Success: capture acceptance criteria and plan acceptance call; set tentative acceptance date.
   e) Billing Ops: schedule first invoice based on billing_trigger. If billing_trigger = SoS and provisioning is ahead of schedule, Billing Ops waits for documented Acceptance Date.
   f) RevRec: determine recognition policy: typically ratable over the minimum_term_months starting on SoS or Acceptance Date. For any non-refundable setup_fee, tag as "setup_revenue" and recognize per contract terms (either upfront or amortized).
   g) FP&A: insert contract cashflows to short-term forecast using scheduled invoice dates and payment terms (use expected collection delay of payment_terms_days plus processing lag of 3 business days).

2) Amendment workflow — mid‑contract fee or term change
   a) Sales must create an amendment record and mark the amendment_effective_date.
   b) RevRec computes prospective revenue delta and any catch-up adjustments for previously billed periods (generate journal entries for credits/debits).
   c) Billing Ops issues credit or debit memos for historical corrections; confirm customer acceptance of any credits.
   d) FP&A updates scenario models and publishes an updated cashflow delta to Treasury.

3) Early termination and settlement
   a) Legal validates termination fee per contract.
   b) Billing Ops issues settlement invoice.
   c) RevRec assesses whether remaining prepayments are refundable or should be recognized as termination income.
   d) FP&A models future cash shortfall and flags to leadership if >5% of quarterly forecast; scenario to be published within 24 hours.

Forecast templates and modeling inputs
- Minimum input columns (CSV): contract_id, customer_name, product_line, committed_monthly_fee_usd, setup_fee_usd, minimum_term_months, start_of_service_date, acceptance_date, billing_trigger, payment_terms_days, currency, region, sales_owner, contract_owner.
- Suggested FP&A model tabs: ActiveContracts, Amendments, Terminations, CollectionsLag, FX assumptions, DeferredRevenueSchedule.

Sample calculations
- Monthly recognized revenue (ratable basis):
  recognized_monthly = committed_monthly_fee_usd * proportion_of_service_days_in_month
  Example: committed_monthly_fee = 120,000 USD/year => 10,000 USD/month. If SoS is on the 11th of a 30-day month: proportion = (30 - 10)/30 = 20/30 => first month recognized = 6,667 USD.
- Deferred revenue on setup_fee if amortized over term:
  deferred_setup_monthly = setup_fee_usd / minimum_term_months

Example journal entries (illustrative)
- On invoice issuance (monthly in advance):
  DR Accounts Receivable 10,000
  CR Unearned Revenue (Deferred Revenue) 10,000

- On monthly recognition (ratable):
  DR Unearned Revenue 10,000
  CR Service Revenue 10,000

- On setup_fee received and recognized upfront (non-refundable):
  DR Cash 25,000
  CR Service Revenue 25,000

Note: These entry examples are illustrative. RevRec and Accounting must validate against GAAP/IFRS and consult external or internal accounting counsel for complex arrangements.

Controls and review checklist for monthly close
- Verify all dedicated contracts with SoS within the month are present in RevRec tracker (owner: RevRec).
- Reconcile invoices scheduled vs. invoices issued (owner: Billing Ops). Threshold: 100% of scheduled invoices must be issued or have a documented exception.
- Cash collection lag: Flag any invoice unpaid after payment_terms_days + 10 days as delinquent; escalate to AR collector.
- FX remeasurement: apply monthly FX spot to AR balances by region and post P&L impact (owner: Accounting).

Procurement / Purchase Order alignment (when applicable)
- If enterprise customers require PO-based invoicing: Sales must capture PO number and PO billing cadence. Billing Ops must verify PO acceptance before scheduling the first invoice.
- For capitalized or pass-through procurement charges (hardware, installation partners): Procurement must map vendor invoices to contract_id and tag as reimbursable if contract specifies.

Exception handling and contract deviations
- Contracts that deviate from the standard (custom billing cadence, multi-year prepaid with unique refund mechanics) must be escalated to RevRec and Legal and marked with label CONTRACT_EXCEPTION in CRM.
- Exception SLAs: initial assessment within 48 hours; treatment (revrec policy) published within 5 business days.

Reporting and dashboards
- Weekly FP&A feed: new committed ARR, churned committed ARR, expected cash in next 30/60/90 days.
- Monthly close package: deferred revenue rollforward, contract amendment summary, and top 10 forecast deltas with root-cause.
- Alerts: Treasury receives an automated alert when expected cash inflows > $250k shift vs prior forecast (owner: FP&A).

Appendices
A. Quick checklist for Sales at signature
- Populate all required CRM fields (see section above).
- Attach signed contract PDF and mark "DEDICATED" tag.
- Notify Solutions for provisioning with expected SoS.

B. CSV import template (column header row)
- contract_id,customer_name,product_line,committed_monthly_fee_usd,setup_fee_usd,minimum_term_months,start_of_service_date,acceptance_date,billing_trigger,payment_terms_days,currency,region,sales_owner,contract_owner

C. Useful links
- RevRec policy central: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/revrec-policy-central-2025
- Forecasting model: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/forecast-model-download
- Billing runbook: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/billing-ops-runbook

Contact and escalation
- Primary RevRec contact: Omar Rizvi (revrec@redwood.com)
- Billing Ops lead: Priya Nair (billing-ops@redwood.com)
- Finance escalation: Maya Chen (fpande@redwood.com)

Revision history
- 2026-02-01: Created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2026-03-05: Published after review by Daniel Park and Sofia Alvarez; clarified amendment catch-up process and added acceptance checklist.

End of playbook
