payload.page_title: Operational Procurement-to-Revenue Handoff Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the operational workflow, controls, and checklists for progressing a purchase or customer contract from procurement/contract signature through billing and revenue recognition (RevRec). It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, sales operations, and engineering program managers who participate in customer onboarding, vendor procurement, or contract amendments that impact invoicing or revenue timing.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Applies to: customer contracts, marketplace channel agreements, and capitalized procurement where invoicing or revenue recognition is impacted (Hosted API credits, Dedicated/Private Reserved capacity deals, platform add-ons).
- Excludes: one-off expense purchases < $5k (see Procurement Low-Value Flow).
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: - Misaligned contract and procurement handoffs are the largest single source of billing delays and RevRec misstatements. Clear checklists and GL mappings prevent missed milestones, incorrect billing cadence, and audit friction.
sections.heading: Why this matters

sections.body:
- Billable Event: a contract-trigger (activation, delivery milestone, committed capacity start) that creates an invoice obligation.
- Revenue Trigger: the specific condition that permits recognizing revenue (often delivery, customer acceptance, or right-to-invoice).
- Deferred Revenue: amounts invoiced or paid where revenue recognition is deferred due to unmet performance obligations.
sections.heading: Key definitions (quick reference)

sections.body:
1. Contract owner / AE (Sales): ensures signed SOW/Order Form with commercial terms and activation dates entered into Salesforce and attaches executed document to the opportunity.
2. Legal: validates required contract clauses (data residency, escrow, KMS, indemnities).
3. Procurement (vendor side) / Sales Ops (customer side): creates procurement ticket and routes to Finance for billing configuration.
4. Finance (Billing & RevRec): configures billing schedule, GL mappings, and RevRec treatment.
5. Engineering Program Manager (for Dedicated/Private): validates deployment readiness and capacity start date.
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation

sections.body:
- Contract metadata captured in Salesforce: billing entity, legal entity, currency, payment terms, taxation flags, SOW attachment.
- Payment terms: Net 30 / Net 45 / prepay; record expected invoice cadence.
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears, monthly in advance, annual upfront — specify in opportunity.
- Activation trigger: automatic on provisioning / manual on customer acceptance — record explicit wording.
- Pricing components: recurring subscription, usage (tokens/embedding units), overage rates, discounts, credits.
- SLA credits and penalty clauses: route to Finance for contra-revenue treatment guidance.
- Data residency and export restrictions: label contract confidentiality if required.
- Revenue accounting flags: deferred revenue allowed? Capitalizable costs? (Finance to advise).
sections.heading: Procurement and Contract Checklist (pre-billing)

sections.body:
1. Signed contract uploaded (Sales): attach executed PDF to opportunity in Salesforce and set Opportunity Stage = "Contracted - Billing Ready".
2. Legal sign-off complete (Legal): update "contract_review" field and set confirmation in the opportunity comments.
3. Sales Ops creates Billing Configure ticket in Zendesk (Billing queue) with the following payload:
   - Opportunity ID, Executed Contract URL, Billing entity, Currency, Payment terms, Invoice recipient, Tax exemption docs, Expected start date, Pricing schedule CSV.
4. Finance Billing reviews within 2 business days and responds with:
   - Required missing items (if any) or "Billing Ready" and assigned Invoice Template.
5. Technical activation check (Engineering): confirm "Capacity Start Date" or "Service Live Date" in the ticket.
6. Invoice creation: First invoice generated according to cadence; if annual upfront, ensure RevRec journal setup in RevRec system (NetSuite/Zuora).
7. RevRec classification: Finance marks revenue as Recognize Now / Deferred with journal entry template included in ticket.
8. Post-invoice validation: Sales Ops confirms customer acceptance and verifies invoice arrived.
sections.heading: Operational flow (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Recurring hosted API revenue: recognized over service period (time-based), unless the contract has usage-based provable completion events.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: recognized monthly when dedicated capacity is delivered and available to customer; if deployment delayed >14 days, defer revenue until capacity window open.
- One-time setup professional services: recognized on customer acceptance sign-off or when deliverables transferred, per SOW.
- Credits and refunds: recorded as contra-revenue; material credits must be escalated to Finance Manager for approval.

Table: Billing triggers and RevRec action (ASCII table)
| Contract Type                | Bill Trigger                      | RevRec Treatment               | Owner        | SLA
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------|-----
| Hosted API subscription     | Start date or provisioning        | Recognize monthly over period | Finance      | 2d
| Dedicated Reserved Capacity | Customer capacity start timestamp | Recognize when available      | Eng + Finance| 3d
| Annual prepaid contracts    | Invoice on day 0                  | Defer, recognize monthly      | Finance      | 5d
| Professional services       | Customer acceptance sign-off      | Recognize on acceptance       | PM / Finance | 7d
sections.heading: Revenue Recognition Rules (summary)

sections.body:
- Purchase Value < $5k: low-value procurement flow (no contract required). Buyer records PO in Coupa and tags finance for FY overhead allocation.
- $5k – $50k: requires Procurement review and Finance notification; one procurement approver + line manager.
- $50k – $250k: requires Procurement lead, Finance & Legal review.
- > $250k: requires VP Finance approval and Legal executive sign-off.

Clause checklist for Legal (to be confirmed before Billing Ready):
- Customer billing entity and tax ID present
- Invoicing address and electronic invoicing consent
- Payment terms explicitly stated
- Termination and refund language (impact on deferred revenue)
- Escrow/KMS/data residency clauses if flagged
- Confidentiality / data processing addendum attached if needed
sections.heading: Thresholds and approval matrix (procurement side)

sections.body:
- Example Billing Configure ticket body (CSV-friendly):
  {
    "opportunity_id": "O-12345",
    "executed_contract_url": "https://redwood.atlassian.net/...",
    "billing_entity": "Redwood, Inc.",
    "currency": "USD",
    "payment_terms": "Net 30",
    "invoice_recipient": "finance-billing@example.com",
    "expected_start_date": "2027-02-01",
    "pricing_schedule": "monthly:4999;usage:per_token:0.0006"
  }

- RevRec journal template (example narration):
  Debit: Deferred Revenue (liability)
  Credit: Revenue - Hosting (income)
  Narration: "Release of deferred annual hosting for Acme Corp. — Feb 2027"
sections.heading: Templates and examples (snippets)

sections.body:
- Finance runs a monthly Revenue Trigger audit: sample 10% of recently contracted deals and confirm ticket-to-invoice-to-RevRec mapping. Exceptions reported as tickets to finance-ops and legal.
- Billing SLA: Billing Configure tickets should be actioned within 2 business days; exceptions are tracked in the monthly ops dashboard.
- Quarterly spot-check: Legal & Finance to sample high-risk clauses (KMS, escrow, data residency) and ensure special handling is applied (restricted invoice routing, separate legal entity billing).
sections.heading: Monitoring and controls

sections.body:
- Missing invoice recipient / tax docs: remediation = Sales Ops pause provisioning and open ticket to collect docs; Finance to delay invoice until resolved.
- Activation date mismatch: remediation = engineering confirms logs and issues playbook checklist; Finance adjusts first invoice and posts correction entry if necessary.
- SLA credit disputes: apply contra-revenue entry and require credit memo; if material (>5% of contract value) escalate to VP Finance.

Appendix A — GL mapping quick-reference (example):
- Hosted subscription revenue -> GL 4100
- Usage revenue (tokens/units) -> GL 4120
- Professional services revenue -> GL 4300
- Deferred revenue (liability) -> GL 2200
- Credits / refunds -> GL 4900

Appendix B — Contacts and ownership
- Billing & RevRec (Finance): billing-team@redwood.example.com
- Legal Contracts: contracts@redwood.example.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Engineering Activation Leads: eng-activation@redwood.example.com
sections.heading: Common failure modes and remediation

sections.body:
- 2026-11-15: Initial draft by Maya Rodriguez
- 2026-12-10: Added GL mapping and thresholds (review by Ethan Kim)
- 2027-01-10: Published with SLA metrics and ticket template updates (approved by VP Finance)
sections.heading: Revision history

sections.body:
- Sourcing-to-recognition control catalog (procurement) — see related_pages
- Chargeback and internal billing guidelines — see related_pages

If you have questions or need a walk-through for a live deal, open a Billing Configure ticket and add the "revrec-onboarding" tag so Finance will prioritize the request.

payload.page_title: Forecast Revote and Contract Trigger Procedures

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This page defines the operational process for (1) triggering a forecasting "revote" when material changes or risks to revenue/expense projections occur, and (2) the threshold-based contract review and procurement actions that must happen as a result. The aim is to ensure alignment between FP&A, Sales/Revenue Ops, Legal, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (RevRec) teams so decisions are timely, auditable, and minimize revenue leakage or compliance risk.

Scope

- Applies to all ARR/commit/one-time contract changes and material forecast updates for Redwood product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes forecasting events impacting expected revenue >= defined thresholds, material cost changes affecting gross margin, and contract amendments that change billing cadence, payment terms, or data-residency requirements.
- Excludes routine sales discounts under delegated approval authority (< $25k ARR impact and within discount matrix).

Definitions

- Revote: A formal re-forecasting process where owners re-submit expected revenue or expense numbers for a given period and obtain explicit FP&A sign-off.
- Contract Trigger: A procurement/legal/finance review required when a contract or amendment crosses a pre-defined financial or policy threshold.
- Materiality thresholds: numeric thresholds (see Decision Matrix) that drive approvals and handoffs.

Decision Matrix (summary)

| Trigger Type | Metric | Action Required | Primary Owner | Escalation/Approver |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Forecast variance | Quarter-to-date revenue variance >= 10% | Revote opened; weekly re-forecast cadence | FP&A (Forecast Manager) | Finance Director (+ Product lead if product variance) |
| New contract / amendment | Annual contract value (ACV) >= $250,000 | Legal + Procurement review; commercial terms worksheet | Sales Ops | Legal Counsel + VP Finance |
| Billing cadence change | Any change from annual to monthly or vice versa | RevRec assessment; billing system change request | Billing Ops | RevRec Manager + Finance Director |
| Data residency / KMS clause | Any customer-requested region or KMS requirement | Security/Compliance review; contract appendix | Legal + Security | Head of Security + Legal Director |
| Capital/one-time hardware spend | Purchase >= $100,000 | Procurement RFQ + budget commit | Purchasing | CFO approval |

When to open a Revote
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1. Quarter-to-date revenue deviates from last published forecast by >= 10%.
2. Customer churn with ARR impact >= $100k for the quarter.
3. Multiple large bookings (> $250k ACV) are delayed beyond the quarter cutoff.
4. Contract amendments change pricing, billing frequency, or introduce non-standard payment terms.

Procedure: Revote Workflow (step-by-step)

1. Detection and Triage
   - Trigger sources: Sales Ops daily pipeline report, billing exceptions, account executive notification, automated variance alert from forecasting tool.
   - FP&A Forecast Manager logs the revote in the Forecast Tracker (Google Sheet + Jira: FIN-REVOTE-YYYYMMDD).

2. Initial Assessment (24 business hours)
   - FP&A runs a variance breakdown: by account, product, geography, and sales stage.
   - Responsible: Forecast Analyst prepares a one-page memo summarizing causes and initial recommended outlook.

3. Convene Revote Working Group (within 48 hours)
   - Attendees: Forecast Manager (chair), Sales Ops rep, Account Owner(s), Product/Engineering if product-issue driven, Billing Ops, RevRec.
   - Output: Revised P50 and P90 forecasts for the impacted time window and a list of mitigation actions.

4. Documentation and Approval (72 hours)
   - Forecast Manager publishes revised forecast and submits for approval to Finance Director.
   - Finance Director must approve or reject; if rejected, escalate to VP Finance.

5. Communication and Systems Update
   - On approval, Forecast Manager updates the canonical forecast, notifies Execs via the weekly FP&A digest, and files the revote package in the Forecast Archive (shared drive).
   - Billing Ops and RevRec evaluate downstream impacts (billing dates, recognition schedule) and issue change requests to the billing system and GL mapping.

Contract Trigger Procedures

When a contract or amendment meets a trigger in the Decision Matrix, follow the steps below. The objective is to ensure consistent commercial terms, appropriate legal review, and correct RevRec treatment.

1. Intake and Triage
   - Sales Ops submits a Contract Intake form (template in Templates/contract-intake.csv) and attaches proposed SOW/Amendment.
   - Procurement coordinates vendor or third-party evaluation when a hardware or services procurement is part of the deal.

2. Commercial Terms Worksheet
   - Sales Ops populates the Commercial Terms Worksheet (required for ACV >= $50k). Fields: customer name, ACV, billing frequency, payment terms, RPO, termination, pass-through costs, data residency, KMS, warranty SLA.

3. Legal Review and Redlines
   - Legal uses the worksheet to determine clause needs. Standard turnarounds: 3 business days for standard deals, 7 business days for complex deals (KMS, data residency, escrow).

4. RevRec & Billing Assessment
   - RevRec Manager reviews for revenue timing and contract boundaries. If billing cadence changes or variable consideration is introduced, RevRec must sign off before countersignature.

5. Procurement & Payment Terms
   - Procurement validates any vendor-related spend or pass-through costs. For purchase commitments >= $100k, Procurement obtains competitive bids where applicable.

6. Approvals and Countersignature
   - Final approvals per Decision Matrix; Legal files executed contract and notifies Finance and Billing. Countersignature may be delayed only under documented risk mitigation.

Templates and Artifacts (locations)

- Contract Intake Template: /templates/contract-intake.csv
- Commercial Terms Worksheet: /templates/commercial-terms-worksheet.xlsx
- Forecast Tracker (canonical): Drive > Finance > Forecasts > Forecast-Canonical-YYYY.xlsx
- Revote Jira epic prefix: FIN-REVOTE-

Roles & Responsibilities

- Forecast Manager (FP&A): Owner of revote cadence, publishes canonical forecast, coordinates working group.
- Sales Ops: Submits intake forms, provides account-level detail and pipeline status.
- Legal: Reviews contract language, produces redlines, maintains contract repository.
- Procurement: Handles vendor evaluation and purchase order issuance.
- RevRec (Accounting): Certifies recognition treatment, updates revenue schedules.
- Billing Ops: Executes billing system changes and invoice timing updates.

Audit Trail and Controls

- Every revote must have an artifact bundle: notification email thread, one-page memo, revised forecast file, Jira ticket, and list of approvals. Store bundle in Forecast Archive for 7 years.
- Contract redlines and executed copies must be stored in the Contract Repository (DocStore ID required).
- Automated alerts: Forecasting tool sends an immutable snapshot (CSV) to Archive on any revote event.

Sample thresholds (operational reference)

- Forecast revote: revenue delta >= 10% QTD OR absolute ARR change >= $100k.
- Legal review: ACV >= $250k OR any non-standard clause (data residency/KMS/escrow).
- Procurement RFQ: purchase or pass-through cost >= $100k.
- RevRec pre-approval: any change to billing cadence or variable consideration.

Checklist (pre-approval)

- [ ] Contract Intake form complete and attached
- [ ] Commercial Terms Worksheet populated
- [ ] Forecast impact assessed and documented
- [ ] Legal redlines attached or waived in writing
- [ ] RevRec sign-off obtained for recognition timing
- [ ] Procurement bids attached (if applicable)
- [ ] Finance/Director-level approval recorded

Example: Contract language snippet (recommended clause for monthly-to-annual changes)

"If Customer elects to change billing cadence from annual to monthly, any prorations, refunds, or payment deferrals must be documented in an amendment. Changes to billing cadence will be reviewed by Finance and RevRec to confirm revenue recognition treatment; no change will be implemented without written approval from the RevRec Manager."

Edge cases and escalation guidance

- Multiple simultaneous triggers: if a revote coincides with a contract > $250k that also changes data-residency, create a joint working group including Legal, Security, FP&A, and Sales.
- Emergency cutover: for urgent remediation (security, SLA breaches) that require immediate contract amendment, Legal may provisionally approve emergency language with post-hoc FP&A and RevRec review within 5 business days. Document rationale in the Contract Repository.

Operational calendar and SLAs

- Revote detection to Working Group convened: SLA = 48 business hours.
- Forecast Manager to publish revised forecast: SLA = 72 business hours.
- Legal turnaround (standard): 3 business days; complex: 7 business days.
- Procurement RFQ cycle: typical 10 business days for standard procurements.

Reporting and KPIs

- Revote frequency by quarter (% of weeks with revote activity).
- Time-to-approve (median) for revisions and contract triggers.
- Forecast accuracy delta before/after revote.
- Percentage of deals requiring RevRec rework post-signature.

Frequently asked questions

Q: Who owns the canonical forecast during a revote?
A: FP&A (Forecast Manager) retains ownership; inputs come from Sales Ops and account owners.

Q: Can Legal sign a contract if RevRec hasn’t approved the recognition treatment?
A: No—RevRec approval is required whenever billing cadence or variable consideration is altered.

Related policies and references

- Forecast sensitivity and contract alignment playbook (see related pages).
- Contract sourcing, pricing & billing SOP (procurement).
- Revenue recognition policy (Accounting Manual section 4.2).

Contacts

- Forecast Manager: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- RevRec Manager: revrec@redwood.ai

Revision history

- 2025-11-12: Document created by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-02: Updated thresholds after FP&A review (Marcus Lee).
- 2026-01-18: Added emergency escalation language and SLAs (Sofia Hernández).

Attachments

- Templates: contract-intake.csv, commercial-terms-worksheet.xlsx
- Example revote memo: revote-sample-memo.pdf

payload.page_title: Commercial discounts governance and approval matrix — guidance for forecasting, contracts, and billing

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the governance, approval matrix, and required accounting and forecasting treatments for commercial discounts and one-off pricing concessions at Redwood Inference. It connects contract-level decisions to procurement and forecasting processes and prescribes the billing and revenue recognition (revrec) handling required to keep forecasts, SOWs, and GL entries consistent.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: provide a single-source policy for how discounts are requested, approved, documented, and reflected in forecasts and revenue recognition.
- Scope: applies to all customer-facing commercial discounts (list price reductions, promotional credits, implementation discounts, free-trial conversions, and market-development funds) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings. Includes sales, customer success, finance, legal, and procurement interactions.

Definitions
- Net Price: list price less approved commercial discounts.
- One-off credit: single invoice credit applied for retention or remediation.
- Promotional credit: time-bound credit used for trial/POC conversions; typically expires after 90 days.
- Billing trigger: event that starts invoicing (e.g., contract signature, provisioned capacity, first API request).
- Revenue trigger: performance obligation satisfaction event for revrec determination.

Key principles
1) Separation of commercial and accounting approvals
   - Commercial teams (Sales/CS/Go-to-market) drive negotiation and propose discounting rationale.
   - Finance (Revenue Operations) validates accounting treatment and ensures revenue recognition integrity.
   - Legal ensures contract clauses align with approved commercial terms.
2) Forecast first, finalize later
   - All discount proposals that materially (>5% ARR impact or >$50k annual value) change forecasted net revenue must be entered in the Forecast Adjustment Log (FAL) before signature.
3) Short-lived credits must be instrumented
   - Promotional credits must include explicit expiration and usage caps in contract exhibits to prevent open-ended liabilities.

Approval matrix (quick reference)
- Discount type: Standard list discounts (up to 15%) -> Approver: Sales Manager (auto-approve in CPQ).
- Discount type: Strategic/renewal discounts (15%–30%) -> Approver: Head of Revenue + Finance (email approval recorded).
- Discount type: >30% or ACV > $250k with discount -> Approver: CRO + CFO + Legal sign-off required; requires documented business case in Deal Approval Portal.
- One-off credits for remediation < $25k -> Approver: CS Manager.
- One-off credits >= $25k -> Approver: CS Head + Finance.

Approval matrix (table - text format)
| Discount band | Decision owner | Required artefacts | Accounting owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–15% | Sales Manager (CPQ) | Quote in CPQ | RevOps | Auto-approved via CPQ ruleset |
| 15–30% | Head of Revenue + Finance | Deal memo (Deal Portal) | RevOps | Requires forecast adjustment entry |
| >30% or ACV>$250k | CRO + CFO + Legal | Business case + Legal termed amendment | RevOps + Treasury | Requires executive record and SSO sign-off |

Request and documentation workflow (numbered SOP)
1. Sales rep opens Deal Approval Portal entry with: customer, list price, requested discount, term, ARR/ACV impact, suggested billing trigger, and proposed contract clause (if non-standard).
2. Generate CPQ quote draft, attach to Deal Approval Portal.
3. If discount triggers Finance review (per matrix), RevOps assigns a ticket; Sales cannot share final contract until RevOps approves forecast treatment.
4. Legal drafts amendment or exhibit; Finance signs off on the wording required for revrec (see Section: Contract language for revrec).
5. Once all approvals are captured, update Forecast Adjustment Log (FAL) with expected ARR impact and expected billing/recognition dates.
6. Procurement and Revenue Operations create billing schedule in Stripe/Billing system and set GL mapping.

Contract language guidance for revrec and billing triggers
- Always include: "Billing Trigger" and "Revenue Recognition Trigger" as discrete clauses. Example snippet: "Billing will commence on the later of (a) signature date or (b) provisioning of Dedicated capacity. Revenue will be recognized ratably over the contracted service term from the revenue trigger date unless otherwise specified per Section X."
- For promotional credits: include an exhibit specifying credit amount, expiration date, and applicability (applies to invoice # or product SKU).
- For multi-element deals (e.g., implementation + dedicated capacity + premium support), use explicit deliverable definitions and assign revenue allocation percentages in an attached Schedule.

Forecasting and GL mapping rules
- Short-term forecast adjustments: FAL entries are visible to FP&A and product finance. Add the following fields in the FAL entry: expected billing start, expected billing cadence, expected ARR delta, probability (sales stage), revrec method (ratable / milestone), GL accounts for deferred revenue and recognized revenue.
- GL mapping: standard SaaS mapping applies. Examples:
  - Deferred Revenue: 2400
  - Subscription Revenue: 4001
  - One-off professional services: 4105
  - Promotional Credits (contra revenue): 4200
- Example calculation (promotional credit applied at signing):
  Example: Customer signs a 12-month Hosted plan at list $120,000 (monthly $10,000), promotional credit $12,000 applied at signing as invoice credit. Net invoice on month 1 = $0; months 2–12 = $10,000. Accounting: recognize subscription revenue ratably $120,000/12 = $10,000 per month; apply contra revenue entry for $12,000 recognized in month 1 as reduction of billed revenue and amortize the credit over same term if credit is to be applied pro rata (documented in contract). If credit is a one-time bill credit that only reduces invoice 1, record a contra-revenue of $12,000 in month 1 and adjust cash/AR accordingly. Consult RevOps on scenario.

Procurement interactions and templates
- Procurement is involved for integration/implementation discounts when a 3rd-party vendor or internal service must be purchased to fulfill the deal. Proc must:
  - Validate supplier onboarding (if vendor is required).
  - Confirm PO requirements and lead times in SOWs.
- Template checklist for procurement-triggered discounts:
  - SOW attached (Y/N)
  - External supplier required (Y/N) -> vendor name and onboarding status
  - Estimated vendor cost and margin impact
  - Payment terms to vendor vs customer terms alignment

Revenue recognition decision tree (short)
1. Is there a distinct performance obligation? -> Yes: allocate transaction price. No: treat as combined service.
2. Is discount contingent on future activity? -> Yes: treat as variable consideration; use expected value method and constrain estimates when necessary.
3. Is billing in arrears or in advance? -> Adjust timing of deferred revenue and invoicing entries accordingly.

Operational controls and required system changes
- CPQ must enforce discount bands and flag deals that require escalated approvals.
- Deal Approval Portal must capture all artifacts and approval audit trail.
- FAL must be integrated into forecasting model (monthly sync) and surfaced to FP&A with probability-weighted scenarios.
- Billing systems must support invoice credits and contra-revenue GL mapping; Stripe/Billing templates should be updated with new credit types: promo_credit, remediation_credit, reseller_margin_adjust.

Escalation and exceptions
- Exceptions to the approval matrix require an exception memo submitted to Finance with CRO/CFO signoff; exception memos are retained for audit for 7 years.
- Immediate remediation credits (customer incident) may be provisionally issued by CS up to $5k and must be logged in the Incident Credits Log within 48 hours; any credit > $5k requires Finance approval before issuance.

Audit and reporting
- Monthly reports: pipeline impact from approved discounts, realized discount rate (ACV-weighted), number of exception memos, and remaining deferred revenue attributable to credits.
- Quarterly audit: Internal Audit will sample 10 deals (> $50k) each quarter to confirm approval trails and GL treatment.

Appendices
A. Sample CPQ approval comment template
  - "Reason for discount: [strategic/renewal/retention]
  - Expected ACV impact: $[amount]
  - Forecast entry ID: FAL-[YYYY]-[NNNN]
  - Approvals captured: [names]"

B. Example phrasing for invoice credit exhibit
  - "Company will provide a promotional invoice credit in the amount of $X to be applied against the first invoice. The credit expires if not applied within 90 days of execution and is non-transferrable."

C. Quick checklist for RevOps before invoice issuance
- Confirm approved discount attached to CPQ quote.
- Verify FAL entry and expected billing cadence.
- Confirm GL coding for deferred revenue and contra entries.
- Ensure legal exhibit is attached to contract for promotional credits.

Owners and contacts
- Policy owner: Priya Desai (Finance — RevOps) — priya.desai@redwood.ai
- Legal reviewer: Evan Li (Legal) — evan.li@redwood.ai
- Procurement contact: Marta Kovacs (Procurement) — marta.kovacs@redwood.ai

Revision history
- 2026-01-15: Policy drafted (Priya Desai).
- 2026-02-05: Incorporated feedback from Sales and RevOps (Liam O'Connor).
- 2026-03-02: Published with final approval from CFO (approved by Sofia Martinez).

Related resources
- Forecast Adjustment Log (FAL) — internal FP&A spreadsheet (link).
- Deal Approval Portal — internal app (link).
- CPQ discount ruleset documentation — internal wiki (link).

End of document

payload.page_title: Usage-Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook (Tokens, Retries, Caching, Credits, Disputes)

sections.body:
This playbook provides Redwood Inference’s approved legal guidance and clause library for **usage-based pricing** across Redwood API (Hosted) and related packaging. It is designed to:
- Ensure **consistent definitions** (tokens, requests, cache hits, retries) across MSAs, Order Forms, pricing pages, and Sales communications.
- Reduce **invoice disputes** by aligning contract language with metering behavior.
- Support **revenue recognition (RevRec)** and audit readiness by defining authoritative sources, dispute windows, and credit/refund mechanics.

This page is **restricted** because it contains clause language and internal positions.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Hosted API usage-based charges (tokens/requests/embeddings units)
- Metered add-ons where usage events are the basis of invoicing
- Dedicated and Private agreements only where they incorporate usage-based overages or burst (primary Dedicated meter definitions live elsewhere)
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Full MSA templates (see Legal templates repository)
- Export-controlled or regulated country-specific addenda (escalate to Legal)
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body: The following definitions should be used as the “source definitions” when drafting or redlining contract language. If a customer demands alternate language, follow the escalation path below.
sections.heading: Definitions (approved internal meanings)

sections.body: **Token** means a discrete unit of text as processed by the applicable model’s tokenization scheme. Tokenization is model-dependent.
sections.heading: 1) “Token”

sections.body:
- Token counts are **model-specific** and may differ between models and versions.
- For chat-style endpoints, token counts may include system/developer messages, tool call payloads, and structured output formatting as applicable.
- We support (and prefer to contract around) **billed tokens** as the invoicing unit, rather than raw “input + output tokens,” because billed tokens reflects caching/discounting rules.
sections.heading: Important internal positions

sections.body:
- **Input Tokens / Prompt Tokens**: tokens attributable to the request context provided by the customer.
- **Output Tokens / Completion Tokens**: tokens generated by the model in response.
- **Billed Tokens**: the token quantity used for billing after applying billing rules (e.g., caching adjustments, promotional discounts, free-tier inclusion), as shown on the invoice and/or usage reports.
sections.heading: Recommended terminology

sections.body: A **Request** is an API call that is accepted by Redwood’s service and results in an attempt to process the call (including streaming requests). Do not tie “request” to “successful response” unless Product/Finance explicitly approves.
sections.heading: 2) “Request”

sections.body: **Usage Report** means Redwood’s reported usage as displayed in the Console, invoice detail, or usage export/API. Contract language should clarify which report is authoritative for billing.
sections.heading: 3) “Usage Report” / “Usage API”

sections.body: - For contracts: define that **Redwood’s invoice and supporting usage report** is the authoritative basis for fees, subject to the dispute process.
sections.heading: Internal preference

sections.body: Caching may reduce compute performed by Redwood. Contract language must avoid obligating Redwood to charge based on compute cost; instead, define how caching affects billed tokens.
sections.heading: 4) “Caching” / “Cache Hit”

sections.body:
- We may apply **cache-hit attribution** to reduce billed usage for eligible cached content, as described in product documentation.
- Caching behavior can change over time as the service is optimized; the contract should permit evolution while maintaining transparency via reports.
sections.heading: Internal position

sections.body:
- **Client side** (customer’s SDK/app retries)
- **Server side** (Redwood retries/fallback routing to preserve availability)
sections.heading: Retry can occur on

sections.body:
- We aim to bill **once per logical request** where retries are transparently handled under the same idempotency key.
- If the customer does not use idempotency keys and submits duplicate requests, those may be billable.
sections.heading: Internal positions

sections.body:
For any Order Form/SOW with usage-based fees, include:
1) Usage unit definition (tokens, embeddings units, requests, GPU-seconds if applicable)
2) Billing measurement and reporting source (invoice + usage report)
3) Caching and retries treatment (at least at a high level)
4) Dispute window + audit mechanics (reasonable; avoids open-ended re-billing risk)
5) Credits/refunds policy (when available; how applied)
6) Change management notice (especially if customer requests strict metering invariants)
sections.heading: Required building blocks

sections.body:
- Timezone for daily usage exports (default: UTC) if customer cares about day-level reporting
- Explicit acknowledgment that tokenization differs by model and may evolve with model upgrades
sections.heading: Optional but recommended

sections.body: Use the below clauses as starting points. Do not materially alter without Legal review.
sections.heading: Clause library (approved language)

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Usage is measured in tokens processed by the applicable model. A token is a unit of text determined by the model’s tokenization scheme. Fees are calculated based on the number of billed tokens reported by Redwood for the applicable billing period. Token counts may vary by model and model version.”

**Negotiation notes:**
- If customer requests a fixed tokenization algorithm, respond that tokenization is model-dependent and tied to the model provider’s implementation.
- If customer requests billing purely on input+output tokens, steer to “billed tokens” and point to reporting transparency.
sections.heading: A. Usage unit (Tokens) — baseline clause

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“A request is an API call accepted by the service for processing. Requests that are duplicated by Customer (including due to Customer retries without an idempotency key) may be counted as separate requests.”
sections.heading: B. Usage unit (Requests) — when included

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“For streaming responses, usage is measured based on tokens processed and reported by Redwood for the request. If a streaming connection is interrupted, Redwood may report usage for tokens processed up to the point of interruption.”

**Negotiation notes:**
- Avoid promising that interrupted streams are always free; we can grant credits case-by-case.
sections.heading: C. Streaming responses — how to describe

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Where the service supports tool/function calling or structured output, tokens attributable to tool call inputs/outputs and associated formatting may be included in token usage as reported by Redwood.”
sections.heading: D. Tool/function calling and structured output

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Redwood may employ caching and other optimization techniques. Usage reports may distinguish cached and non-cached usage. Redwood may apply billing adjustments (including reduced billed tokens) for eligible cached content as described in Redwood documentation. Optimization techniques may change over time.”

**Alternative clause (customer requests explicit fairness statement):**
“Redwood will not charge more than once for the same logical request submitted with the same idempotency key, and may reduce charges when caching is applied, as reflected in the usage report.”
sections.heading: E. Caching treatment

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Customer is responsible for implementing idempotency keys for retryable requests. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid duplicate billing for server-side retries performed under the same logical request identifier. Customer-submitted duplicate requests may be billable.”

**Negotiation notes:**
- Do not guarantee “no double billing ever.” Instead: “commercially reasonable efforts” + dispute process.
sections.heading: F. Retries and idempotency

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Fees are based on Redwood’s measurement systems and usage records. Redwood will provide usage reporting via invoice detail, Console, or usage export/API. In the event of conflict, the invoice and supporting usage report for the billing period will control, subject to Customer’s dispute rights.”
sections.heading: G. Measurement system and authoritative records

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Customer must notify Redwood in writing of any good-faith dispute regarding an invoice within thirty (30) days of the invoice date, describing the basis for the dispute in reasonable detail. If Customer does not dispute an invoice within this period, the invoice will be deemed accepted.”

**Fallback positions:**
- 45 days: acceptable for larger enterprise if requested.
- 60+ days: requires CFO (Laura Bennett) approval due to RevRec and cash collection risk.
sections.heading: H. Dispute window (recommended default)

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Credits, if any, are applied to future invoices unless otherwise required by law. Except as expressly provided in the Agreement, fees are non-refundable.”

**Optional add-on (when SLA credits apply):**
“Service credits are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet a service level, and will be calculated and applied as described in the applicable SLA.”
sections.heading: I. Credits and refunds (usage-based)

sections.body:
**Approved clause (standard):**
“Redwood may update its measurement and reporting systems from time to time. Redwood will not materially increase charges due solely to a measurement change without providing prior notice and an opportunity to review supporting reporting for the change.”

**Internal guidance:**
- If the customer requests strict “no metering changes” language, escalate; this conflicts with ongoing hardening efforts (shadow-billing compare, meter v2) and can create operational risk.
sections.heading: J. Meter changes and notice

sections.body:
**Position:** We support OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but tokenization/attribution can differ by model and implementation.
**Response:** Offer transparency: billed tokens reported; provide sample usage exports; consider adding a “reporting parity” exhibit if necessary (requires Product + Eng + Legal review).
sections.heading: 1) “Tokens must match OpenAI exactly.”

sections.body:
**Position:** If compute is performed, some usage may be reported.
**Response:** Use idempotency + commercially reasonable efforts clause. Offer a credits mechanism for verified platform-caused duplicate charges.
sections.heading: 2) “Do not charge for retries / failed requests.”

sections.body:
**Position:** Caching may reduce billed tokens depending on eligibility and product policy.
**Response:** Use caching clause; avoid hard commitments. If needed for the deal, define a limited-term promotional adjustment with Finance sign-off.
sections.heading: 3) “Caching must always reduce price.”

sections.body:
**Position:** Generally no.
**Response:** Offer 45 days; if deal size justifies, escalate to CFO/GC with RevRec impact assessment.
sections.heading: 4) “Dispute window must be 90 days.”

sections.body:
**Position:** No direct customer access to raw multi-tenant logs.
**Response:** Provide usage exports, reconciliation support, and audit reports as appropriate; reference access-controls policy.
sections.heading: 5) “Audit rights to inspect raw logs.”

sections.body:
Finance operates a month-end close process with a usage data freeze window and controlled backfills.
- Contract language should not obligate real-time corrections for late events.
- Use the dispute clause and reconciliation process to handle exceptions.
sections.heading: Month-end close and late-arriving events

sections.body:
- Default approach is **forward-looking fixes** with audit trail.
- Retroactive invoice changes require Finance + Legal approval.
sections.heading: If Redwood discovers a metering bug

sections.body:
If contract or procurement asks for a customer-facing explanation:
- Sales should use the approved FAQ language (see Sales Enablement page) and avoid promising exact token parity or “never bill on retries.”
sections.heading: Customer communications

sections.body: Use this section for routing redlines or customer questions.
sections.heading: Escalation path (when to pull in Legal/Finance/Engineering)

sections.body:
- Any requested change to dispute windows, audit rights, or refundability language
- Requests for “most favored nation” pricing tied to token definitions
- Contractual commitments about caching or retry billing behavior
sections.heading: Escalate to Commercial Counsel (Sofia Mendes)

sections.body:
- Any language that constrains Redwood’s ability to modify measurement systems
- Any customer request for regulatory/compliance commitments tied to billing logs
- Any threat of litigation or formal audit request
sections.heading: Escalate to GC (Michael Grant)

sections.body:
- Requests for extended dispute windows beyond 45 days
- Any proposal for retroactive rebates/true-ups
- Any complex credits structure (rollover, non-expiring, transferable)
sections.heading: Escalate to RevRec/Accounting (Emily Stone)

sections.body:
- Material concessions affecting revenue recognition or collection
- Any exception involving significant credits/refunds or contractual refund obligations
sections.heading: Escalate to CFO (Laura Bennett)

sections.body:
- Customer requires a written description of metering behavior for retries/streaming/tool calls
- Customer reports discrepancy between invoice and usage export needing technical reconciliation
- Customer requests special export formats/timezone/day-boundary logic
sections.heading: Escalate to Engineering (Nadia Rahman / Logan Wright)

sections.body:
1) Confirm the usage unit(s) match the product packaging (tokens vs requests vs embeddings)
2) Confirm “billed tokens” language is used where available
3) Ensure retries/idempotency clause is included if customer is retrying or using streaming
4) Confirm dispute window is 30 days (or approved exception)
5) Confirm credits policy matches Finance policy and RevRec requirements
6) Link to usage reporting source and avoid promises of exact parity with other providers
sections.heading: Before sending paper

sections.body:
Use only when procurement requires a detailed exhibit; keep it concise.

**Exhibit X — Usage Definitions (Example)**
- “Billed Tokens” means the token quantity reported by Redwood for billing, which may account for caching adjustments and promotional inclusions, as reflected in Redwood’s usage report.
- “Idempotency Key” means a unique identifier provided by Customer to allow safe retries without duplicate logical charges.
- “Cache Hit” means a request (or portion thereof) served from Redwood-managed cache, which may be reported as cached usage and may be billed differently as reflected in the usage report.
sections.heading: Appendix: example exhibit (usage definitions)

sections.body:
- 2026-02-24: Updated retry/idempotency position to align with metering hardening work and shadow-billing compare; clarified streaming interruption treatment; added meter-change notice clause.
- 2026-01-10: Added caching clause options and dispute window negotiation guidance.
sections.heading: Change log

sections.body: For questions or proposed edits to this playbook, contact Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel) and tag Emily Stone (RevRec) for changes that affect billing acceptance, dispute windows, or credits/refunds mechanics.
sections.heading: Questions

payload.page_title: Commitment Approval Queue and Legal Handshake — Cross-functional SOP

sections.body:
Overview:
This document defines the operational flow, responsibilities, SLAs, and handoff artifacts for purchase commitments that require legal contract review and create revenue recognition/billing implications. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales/Account Management, and Engineering teams who originate or manage commercial commitments.

Scope:
- Covers commitments that create a contractual obligation (subscription, reserved/dedicated capacity, multi-year commitments, SOWs, and enterprise support contracts).
- Excludes purely internal purchase orders (hardware/software purchases with no customer contract).

Goals:
- Ensure commitments are approved and recorded in forecasts within defined timelines.
- Standardize the legal handoff so contract language does not delay billing or revrec.
- Define a clear queue/triage and escalation path for approvals and exceptions.

Key Definitions:
- Commitment: Any customer or partner agreement creating a multi-period obligation or payment schedule (subscription, reserved capacity, committed spend).
- Revenue Trigger: The point at which Finance is authorized to record deferred revenue and/or issue invoices.
- Legal Handoff: The formal transfer of contract artifacts (redlines, signature pages, SOWs) from Legal to Finance/Revenue Ops and Procurement.

Approval Matrix (thresholds and approvers):
| Commitment Value (ARR equivalent) | Required Approvals | Primary Approver SLA | Notes |
|----------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------|-------|
| <= $50,000                       | Deal Owner + Finance | 3 business days     | Standard billing terms template OK |
| $50,001 - $250,000               | Deal Owner + Finance + Legal | 5 business days | Legal review required for non-standard clauses |
| $250,001 - $1,000,000            | Deal Owner + Finance + Legal + Sales Director | 7 business days | May require procurement/PO coordination for customers with procurement constraints |
| > $1,000,000                     | Deal Owner + CFO + GC + Sales VP | 10 business days | Executive notification; procurement may require additional KYC/credit checks |

Required Artifacts for Legal Handoff (attach to the approval ticket):
- Fully executed contract or final redline PDF (signed pages if available)
- Statement of Work (SOW) or Order Form with line-item billing cadence
- Pricing worksheets and discount approvals (signed pricing attestation)
- Customer billing/legal contact and invoicing address (including billing email and PO requirements)
- Implementation acceptance criteria (if recognized on delivery/milestones)
- Any compliance or data residency attachments (if applicable)

Operational Workflow (numbered procedure):
1. Origin: Sales/Account Manager creates an approval ticket in the procurement/commitments queue (JIRA ticket type: COMMITMENT-REQ) using the template below.
2. Finance Triage (within 2 business days): Finance validates that the commitment is reflected in the latest forecast bucket and assigns a forecast owner. If the commitment is material to forecast variance (>5% of ARR bucket), Finance flags for Forecast Committee review.
3. Legal Review (standard SLA: 5 business days): Legal triages for non-standard clauses (IP, indemnity caps, data residency, escrow, KMS). Legal provides either: approved contract, commentary with required edits, or escalates to GC for >$1M deals.
4. Procurement/PO Coordination (if customer requires PO): Procurement issues internal PO or confirms external PO flow to Accounts Receivable.
5. Signature & Artifact Collection: Once signed, Sales uploads the executed contract and the signature page into the ticket and moves the ticket to the "Handoff to Revenue Ops" status.
6. Revenue Ops/Billing (within 3 business days of handoff): Revenue Ops validates recognition model (subscription vs. milestone), assigns revenue recognition code, and creates the billing schedule in the billing system (NetSuite/Stripe/Zuora integration).
7. Forecast Update & Recognition Trigger: Finance updates MRR/ARR forecasts and, if recognition criteria are met, records a deferred revenue schedule. Any exceptions (e.g., acceptance criteria not met) are noted and posted to the contract record.
8. Post-Mortem: For any deal that misses SLAs or causes >10% forecast variance, the cross-functional team runs a 10-day incident review.

JIRA Ticket Template (COMMITMENT-REQ):
- Summary: [Customer] - [Product/Capacity] - [Currency Amount] - [Contract Type]
- Fields: Customer legal name; Sales Owner; Deal Value (ARR/EAC); Renewal/Start/End Date; Billing cadence; Required PO? Y/N; Attachments: draft contract, pricing sheet, SOW.
- Workflow statuses: New -> Finance Triage -> Legal Review -> Procurement (if PO) -> Handoff to Revenue Ops -> Billing Scheduled -> Closed

Legal Review Prioritization Rules:
- Expedited (48 hours): Security incident remediation agreements, legal holds, and customers requiring urgent cutoff dates.
- Standard (5 business days): Most SaaS/reserved capacity agreements using approved templates.
- Extended (10 business days): Complex multi-party agreements, export controls, or material IP transfers.

Escalation Path:
1. If Legal review exceeds SLA, Legal lead notifies Sales leader and Finance lead within 24 hours after SLA breach.
2. If procurement PO is delayed >7 business days, Procurement lead notifies Sales Ops and the customer procurement contact.
3. For high-value deals (> $1M) in active exception, the GC + CFO schedule a 1:1 review within 48 hours of escalation.

Revenue Recognition Checklist for Revenue Ops (required for RevRec posting):
- Contract type confirmed: Subscription / Usage / Milestone / One-time.
- Billing cadence: Monthly / Quarterly / Annual / Milestone-based.
- Start date for recognition: Signed date / Service start / Acceptance sign-off.
- Performance obligations explicitly listed in contract and mapped to revenue schedule.
- External customer PO or billing requirements documented.
- Any customer acceptance criteria or holdbacks captured with expected dates.
- GL codes and deferred revenue accounts assigned.

Sample Approval Matrix Table (CSV-friendly):
threshold,approvers,legal_sla,finance_sla,notes
50000,Sales Owner;Finance,3bd,2bd,standard template ok
250000,Sales Owner;Finance;Legal,5bd,2bd,legal review required
1000000,Sales Owner;CFO;GC;Sales VP,10bd,3bd,exec review

Common Exceptions and How to Handle Them:
- Customer requires campus/department-specific PO: Procurement to create a PO template and confirm split-invoicing if required.
- Data residency clauses or KMS requirements: Flag to Security & Compliance and Legal; include expected 10 business day review window.
- Discounting beyond approved threshold: Sales must attach Pricing Exception Approval signed by Revenue Operations + Finance.

Operational Metrics and Reporting:
- KPI 1: % of commitments processed within SLA (target: 95%).
- KPI 2: Average Legal review time (target: <= 4 business days for standard deals).
- KPI 3: Time from signature to first invoice (target: <= 5 business days).
- KPI 4: Number of forecast adjustments attributable to post-signature changes (target: < 3% monthly).

Roles & Responsibilities (short list):
- Sales/Deal Owner: Initiate ticket, attach artifacts, drive customer signature.
- Legal: Provide contract review, flag non-standard terms, sign-off on final language.
- Finance: Triage commitments, update forecasts, own revrec treatment.
- Procurement: Ensure PO flow, vendor/customer procurement onboarding if required.
- Revenue Ops/Billing: Create billing schedules, issue invoices, maintain recognition schedules.

Backout / Remediation Steps (if a signed contract cannot be recognized immediately):
1. Tag contract as "Pending Acceptance" in the system with reason code (e.g., implementation dependency).
2. Finance records a note and defers recognition; Revenue Ops schedules first invoice to be blocked until acceptance.
3. Account Manager to provide weekly status updates until acceptance criteria are met.
4. If outstanding beyond 90 days, escalate to Sales Director and Finance for resolution; consider credit memo or amendment.

Appendix A — Example Clause Language to Avoid (Legal Notes):
- Open-ended indemnities or unlimited liability without caps.
- Ambiguous acceptance criteria that delay start date determination.
- Auto-renewal terms without clear notice periods (Finance needs clear renewal triggers for forecasting).

Appendix B — Quick Contact Roster:
- Finance Triage: finance-triage@redwood.ai
- Revenue Ops: revenue-ops@redwood.ai
- Legal Intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai

Change Log:
- 2026-01-12: Document created by Daniela Martinez.
- 2026-03-18: Added expedited legal SLA rules and JIRA template fields (review: Marcus Lee).
- 2026-09-02: Updated approval thresholds and post-signature SLA targets; clarified RevRec checklist (review: Priya Raman, Olivia Chen).

Related Documents:
- procurement/supplier-onboarding-and-invoice-routing-2026.json
- revrec-and-billing/chargeback-and-internal-billing-guidelines-2026.json

Notes for implementers:
- Use the COMMITMENT-REQ ticket exactly; missing attachments are the leading cause of SLA misses.
- Maintain an automated dashboard (Looker/Metabase) showing ticket age by stage; Finance and Legal leads must review weekly.

payload.page_title: Oddball Onboarding Reminders and Quirky Notes

sections.body: This is an intentionally informal, slightly silly companion document to the official onboarding checklist. It lives in scratchpad because some of these notes are purely cultural or useful only to folks who like to ask "where did they hide the spare HDMI?". Use with discretion.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Capture oddball-but-useful local knowledge that helps new hires settle in faster.
- Offer a few lightweight rituals and office norms that are not in the formal handbook.
- Surface small operational tips that save time (e.g., where the spare dongles live, how to reset the office espresso, who to ping for a standing desk).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body: New hires should complete the canonical onboarding checklist first (HR/IT/Manager items). After the essentials, skim this doc for practical pointers and local flavor. It's intentionally casual — things change often and not everything here is official policy.
sections.heading: Quick intro (1 paragraph)

sections.body:
1. Office practicalities
2. Daily rituals and unwritten norms
3. Tech and desk tips
4. Emergency and first-aid oddities
5. Small procedures and who-knows-what

1) Office practicalities
- Key locations:
  - Snacks/communal fridge: small freezer shelf labeled "donut concessions" (please replace what you take).
  - Spare HDMI / dongles: labeled bag in meeting room B cabinet (top shelf).
  - Print toners and stationery: supplies closet, second shelf, behind the green plant box.
- Kitchen/coffee notes:
  - Espresso machine: short press of the silver button, then long press to purge steam. If it makes a high squeal, flip the red switch behind the unit (ask Facilities if unsure).
  - Refrigerator etiquette: label your food with name + date. Food older than 7 days goes to "community science" (i.e., compost).

2) Daily rituals and unwritten norms
- Standups: 9:30am sharp for most engineering squads; if you are late, DM your squad lead rather than interrupting the thread.
- Meeting rooms: toggle "Do Not Disturb" on the door if you need private whiteboard time; otherwise move to the lounge.
- Lunch culture: Taco Tuesday is unofficial but highly encouraged. If you win the taco duty raffle, you own one pack of hot sauce.

3) Tech and desk tips
- Spare power strip: under the "tool cart" by the big ficus (yes, that ficus).
- Desk plant care: water weekly (small cup), rotate to the window side every two weeks. The office plant-care rota lives in Confluence: company-handbook/office-plant-care.
- VPN quirks: if your private deployment demo fails to reach staging, try toggling the lightweight VPN profile (Profile: redwood-lite) before opening a ticket. This sometimes clears stale routes after laptop sleep.
- Local dev trick: ssh-agent sometimes gets confused after laptop lid suspend. Run:
  ```
  eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"; ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
  ```

4) Emergency and first-aid oddities
- First-aid kit: top drawer in reception desk — bandages, antiseptic wipes.
- AED: wall by the main stairs, second floor. The AED signage is slightly faded; we will replace by Q3 but for now note the location.
- If the fire alarm tests at 9:02am: this is usually a scheduled alarm test on Wednesdays; if it occurs outside normal maintenance windows, follow evacuation procedure and report to Safety Lead.

5) Small procedures and who-knows-what
- Printer jam ritual: open back door, gently pull paper toward you, then press the big green "reset" button for 3s. If the jam persists, email facilities@redwood.com and include a photo.

payload.page_title: Ten-Step Restoration Sprint & Shadow Mentoring Handbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook describes a focused, repeatable Ten-Step Restoration Sprint used during multi-system outages and pairs that operational flow with a structured shadow-mentor program to accelerate oncall proficiency. It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, service owners, and SRE mentors.

Scope: Applies to production incidents that meet SLO-impacting criteria (see SLO thresholds section). Not intended for low-severity config errors or scheduled maintenance.

Owner: Eng SRE team. Primary contact: oncall-lead@redwood.example.com.

Quick links: runbook library, status page templates, postmortem template, incident evidence checklist.

Audience and roles

- Incident Initiator: the first person to acknowledge the alert and call the bridge.
- Bridge Operator: facilitates the incident bridge, coordinates comms, and enforces the Ten-Step Sprint cadence.
- Primary Resolver: service owner(s) leading technical work for the impacted service(s).
- Secondary Resolvers: cross-functional engineers called in to assist (networking, infra, runtime).
- Shadow: junior responder who observes and documents actions during the sprint.
- Mentor: senior SRE who leads post-incident coaching and retro facilitation.

How to use this document

- Use the numbered Ten-Step Sprint for initial restoration (first 60–90 minutes).
- Run the shadow mentoring checklist in parallel to create training artefacts.
- After containment, follow the Post-Incident Evidence & Draft Postmortem template included below.

SLO thresholds that trigger Ten-Step Sprint

| Severity | Symptom | SLO impact | Trigger |
|---------|---------|------------|---------|
| Sev1 | Total region outage for hosted API | >= 99.5% reduction in success rate for 5+ minutes | Auto-trigger after 3x alert flood or manual bridge |
| Sev2 | Significant latency increase | > 200ms p95 increase across customer requests for 15+ minutes | Review/bridge by oncall |

Ten-Step Restoration Sprint (primary runbook)

1) Acknowledge & Bridge (0–5m)
   - Incident Initiator: acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and create a bridge (Zoom/Google Meet).
   - Bridge Operator: open the incident channel (#inc-xxxx) and post initial status: impacted services, region, estimated blast radius, primary contact.
   - Shadow: note timestamps, alert IDs, and initial metrics snapshot.

2) Quick Impact Triage (5–10m)
   - Primary Resolver: confirm service(s) affected using dashboards (console/model-serving, ingress, and edge metrics).
   - Bridge: classify impact (regional vs. global, data plane vs. control plane).
   - Output: short impact statement to stakeholders.

3) Stabilize Traffic (10–20m)
   - If applicable, apply graduated traffic control: rate-limits, scaled back routing policies, or traffic-division to healthy regions.
   - Use fallback model variants or reduced sequence length mode where supported to temporarily reduce CPU/GPU pressure.

4) Hotfix Window (20–40m)
   - Primary Resolver and Secondary Resolvers: run validated mitigation steps from specific service runbooks (see related runbook IDs).
   - Keep changes small, reversible, and documented in the incident channel.

5) Validate Restoration (30–50m)
   - Run synthetic probes against restored endpoints. Confirm p95/p99 latency and error-rate trends returning to baseline.
   - Shadow: capture pre/post metric snapshots and the commands used.

6) Customer Status & Tiered Notifications (immediately after validation)
   - Bridge Operator: publish customer-facing status update using the template below.
   - For enterprise customers impacted by the incident, trigger account-level outreach per the escalation matrix.

7) Stabilization Monitoring (50–90m)
   - Maintain increased sampling and tracing for 3x normal volume for 90 minutes.
   - Set temporary alerts at tighter thresholds (e.g., 50% of SLO slack) to catch reversion.

8) Evidence Collection & Triage for Postmortem (start while stabilizing)
   - Collect logs, traces, config diffs, rollout metadata, and full command history. Attach artifacts to the incident ticket.
   - Shadow: curate a short evidence index with direct links.

9) Restore Normal Ops & Runbook Handover (90–120m)
   - Roll back temporary mitigations and revert traffic controls when confident.
   - Primary Resolver: schedule a 60-minute triage deep-dive with the mentor and product owner within 48 hours.

10) Close Bridge & Draft Postmortem (post sprint)
   - Bridge Operator: move the channel to read-only and create a draft postmortem using the included template.
   - Mentor: assign action owners with clear SLAs for mitigation items.

Shadow-Mentor Program (parallel process)

Purpose: Turn incidents into repeatable learning opportunities and accelerate new responder ramp.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Record timestamps for each decision and action.
- Note who is contacted and the exact commands or consoles used.
- Capture any runbook gaps or ambiguous steps.
- Collect a short list of 3 teachable moments for the retro.
sections.heading: Shadow checklist (during sprint)

sections.body:
- Within 48 hours: review the evidence index and draft postmortem with the shadow.
- Within 7 days: run a 30–60 minute learning session with the wider oncall rota covering the teachable moments and suggested runbook updates.
- Ensure at least one runbook edit or clarification is merged per incident for which the shadow prepared artifacts.

Escalation matrix (quick reference)

- Local service issue -> Primary Resolver -> Service Lead (15 min)
- Cross-service or infra -> Add Secondary Resolver(s) + SRE oncall (10 min)
- Prolonged SLO loss > 1 hour -> Paging to Eng Director + Product Ops (escalate at 60m)
- Customer-impacting > 4 hours -> Executive status + CS/AE briefing (escalate at 4h)

Status Page & Customer Comms Templates

Public status template (to be posted on status.redwood.example.com):
- Title: Incident - {service} - {brief cause} (Region)
- Impact: Short sentence (e.g., "Customers in us-west experienced elevated errors and increased latency between 12:03–12:45 UTC.")
- Current status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Restored / Monitoring
- Next update: {time + 30m}
- Notes: High-level mitigation steps and workarounds.
sections.heading: Mentor responsibilities (post sprint)

sections.body:
- Subject: Incident update — {service} — {short impact statement}
- Body: One-sentence impact, actions taken, ETA for more info, contact person (SRE lead and AM), apologies and credit guidance (if applicable).

Post-Incident Evidence & Draft Postmortem Template

1) Summary (1–3 sentences): What happened and visible customer impact.
2) Timeline: concise, timestamped actions (use ISO-8601).
3) Root cause hypothesis / final root cause: technical summary.
4) Contributing factors: people, process, tooling, and telemetry gaps.
5) Mitigation and long-term fixes: owner and ETA.
6) Customer impact and remediation: crediting plan, customer comms sent.
7) Evidence index: links to logs, traces, recordings, rollout IDs, and config diffs.
8) Retrospective notes and teachable moments.

Runbook governance and ownership

- Each service runbook must list a primary owner, secondary owner, and last-tested date.
- Runbooks must include safe roll-forward and roll-back commands and a quick-impact checklist.
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly for high-risk services, bi-annual for others.

Game-day & Mentored Simulation schedule

- Quarterly Game-Days: 3 planned scenarios per quarter (network partition, kv-cache storm, auth tier regression). At least one scenario must use the shadow-mentor pairing.
- Shadow simulations: monthly 60-minute labs where a shadow leads a mini-restoration and a mentor grades the artifacts produced.

Metrics and KPIs to track program health

- Mean Time To Restore (MTTR) — target: reduce by 20% year-over-year.
- Shadow ramp time — % of shadows qualified to be solo oncall within 4 months.
- Runbook churn — number of runbook edits per incident (target: >=1 edit/incident).
- Postmortem completion rate — 100% for Sev1/Sev2 within 7 days.

Appendices

A. Evidence collection checklist (CLI commands and dashboards)
- curl and synthetic probe examples, steps to download logs from logging cluster, query examples for traces, recommended span sampling rates.

B. Restorative CLI snippets (examples with placeholders)
- Rollout rollback:
  gcloud run services update-traffic SERVICE --to-revisions REVISION --region REGION
- Temporary rate-limit (kong example):
  curl -X POST https://api-gateway/config -d '{"limit":100}'

C. Customer status example (realistic copy)
- \"12:10 UTC — We are investigating increased error rates for text-generation in us-west. Our mitigation is to route new requests to our fallback model variant which reduces throughput but restores successful responses. Next update: 12:40 UTC.\"

D. Learning outcomes rubric for mentors
- Level 1: Shadow can summarize timeline and reproduce evidence index without guidance.
- Level 2: Shadow can perform 30% of mitigation steps under supervision.
- Level 3: Shadow can lead a mini-sprint with a mentor ready to intervene.

E. Change log
- 2025-11-02: v0.1 created by Priya Nair.
- 2026-01-05: clarified enterprise escalation thresholds (reviewer: Ethan Murphy).
- 2026-03-15: added evidence collection CLI snippets and learning rubric (reviewer: Lina Kovács).

Related resources

- Runbook index (link to internal runbook library)
- Incident postmortem template (link)
- Status page authoring guide (link)

End of document.
