payload.page_title: Third-Party Integration Audit, Access, and Retention Policy

sections.body:
Summary

This policy defines mandatory controls and end-to-end procedures for onboarding, operating, and decommissioning third-party integrations (3P connectors, vendor APIs, partner systems) with respect to access control (RBAC), authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC checks, incident response integration, and compliance evidence collection. It applies to all product and infrastructure integrations that exchange or access Redwood Inference customer or production data.

Scope

- In-scope: any integration that reads, writes, proxies, or requests metadata from production services, including SaaS connectors, hosted vendor agents, and partner-managed webhooks.
- Out-of-scope: internal tools that never connect to customer or production data channels (documented exceptions require risk approval).

Goals and non-goals

- Goals: ensure least-privilege access, consistent audit trail and immutable evidence, clear retention and data residency mapping, fast investigative workflows for incidents, and defensible compliance posture for audits (SOC2/ISO).
- Non-goals: prescribe vendor procurement decisions or pricing; those remain with Finance/Procurement.

Roles and responsibilities

- Security (owner): policy custodian; approves security evidence packages; runs periodic sampling reviews.
- Integrations/Product (requester/owner): submit onboarding package, implement required logging hooks, maintain connector config.
- Eng-Infra (ops): configure audit collectors, retention enforcement, and secure network egress controls.
- Legal/Compliance: define preservation holds, retention overrides for legal requests.

Authentication and RBAC requirements

1. Minimized privileged identities
- All third-party integrations must use dedicated service identities (no shared human credentials).
- Each connector gets a unique long-lived client-id and short-lived credential pattern when supported (preferred: OIDC + short-lived TLS or mTLS).

2. Authorization model
- Integrations are assigned one of three roles: read-only, write-limited, or admin-proxy. Default is read-only.
- Role mapping is configured via the authz-service and enforced at the API gateway level (authz-service policy id: AZ-THIRD-PARTY-01).

3. Approval and attestation
- Every new integration requires approval from the owning product manager and security; approval recorded in the integration registry (registry ticket ID required).
- Quarterly attestation: owners must re-affirm the necessity and RBAC scope of active integrations.

Audit logging requirements

- All integration activity must emit structured audit events to the centralized audit pipeline (service name: audit-collector). Required fields: timestamp, service, connector_id, actor, action, resource, request_id, source_ip, success/failure, change_summary (free text max 1024 chars).

- Logging format (JSON example)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-01T12:00:00Z",
  "service": "ingest-api",
  "connector_id": "stripe-sync-abc123",
  "actor": "svc-thirdparty-stripe",
  "action": "create_customer",
  "resource": "customer:cus_9z8y",
  "request_id": "req-6b4f",
  "source_ip": "203.0.113.42",
  "success": true,
  "change_summary": "created customer with email redacted@example.com"
}

- SLOs and availability
- Audit events must arrive at audit-collector within 30s for 99% of events. Missing or delayed telemetry must trigger an integration health alert routed to #integrations-ops.

- Tamper-resistance
- Raw audit streams are append-only and backed by immutable object storage (WORM) for high-sensitivity connectors when required by policy. All logs are signed with a rotating key via KMS to provide provenance.

Data residency and retention matrix

- Default retention policy (applies unless overridden by contract or legal hold):

Table: retention matrix
Service / Log type | Typical retention | Minimum retention | Encryption | Owner
authz-service (access grants) | 365 days | 90 days | AES-256 + KMS | security
audit-collector (structured events) | 2 years | 1 year | AES-256 + KMS | eng-infra
request-traces (full traces/spans) | 90 days | 30 days | AES-256 at rest | eng-platform
third-party-payloads (raw vendor payloads) | 180 days | 30 days | Customer-region KMS | integrations/product
compliance-evidence-bundles | 7 years | 3 years | AES-256 + HSM-wrapped keys | compliance

- Residency mapping
- Integrations must declare the geographic regions where data will be stored or transmitted during onboarding. For EU/UK customer data, default storage must be in eu-* regions unless contractually waived.

- Cross-border replication
- Cross-region replication of logs or payloads is allowed only with documented business justification and signed data processing addendums. Replication requests require security and legal approval and are tracked in the registry.

Secure SDLC controls for connector code

- All code shipped by Redwood that interfaces with third-party vendors (connectors, agents) must follow these checks before production deployment:
  1. Static application security testing (SAST) pass with zero critical findings.
  2. Dependency vulnerability policy: no unpatched critical CVEs; high-severity must have documented mitigation and scheduled patch window.
  3. Secrets scanning: no hard-coded secrets in repo or builds.
  4. Integration tests that exercise happy and failure paths for auth and error reporting.
  5. Security review: triage within 5 business days; approvals logged in PR and integration registry.

- Third-party vendor-supplied agents installed in customer networks must have a documented SBOM and supported upgrade path; unsupported binaries are disallowed by default.

Incident response and investigation workflow

- Detection and triage
  1. Integration health alerts (failed token refresh, high error rate, missing audit events) are paged to on-call via PagerDuty with severity mapping: SEV2 (service degradation) or SEV1 (suspected data exfiltration).
  2. On-call collects evidence using standardized collector scripts and documents actions in the incident ticket.

- Evidence preservation
  1. Immediately snapshot relevant logs, connector configs, and audit-collector streams to an evidence bucket with legal hold tag.
  2. If exfiltration suspected, engage Legal and Forensics; preserve network captures and, if available, encrypted key manifests.

- Notification and containment
  1. Containment options: rotate connector credentials, revoke tokens at gateway, isolate connector IP ranges, or disable connector at config management. Which action to take is decided by security on-call in consultation with product owner.
  2. Post-containment verification includes ensuring no further unauthorized activity for 24 hours and that audit event arrival returns to baseline.

Compliance evidence workflow (for audits)

- Evidence package components
  - Integration registry export (approved connectors with rationale), role-to-permission maps, audit event extracts (time-bounded), retention policy records, KMS key rotation logs, and attestation records.

- Packaging process (standardized)
  1. Request: Compliance requests evidence via the evidence intake form; security-owner assigns a package owner.
  2. Collection: use the evidence-orch service to pull signed audit slices and attachments into a sealed evidence bundle (bundle id included).
  3. Verification: reviewer checks signatures and manifest; discrepancies trigger a remediation runbook.
  4. Delivery: deliver sealed bundle through the secure transfer mechanism (SFTP with mutual TLS or the compliance portal).

Risk exceptions and temporary access model

- Exception framework
  - Short-lived exceptions (<= 30 days) are recorded with an explicit compensating control (e.g., additional logging, network isolation) and must have a designated approver from Security and Product.
  - Long-lived exceptions (> 30 days) require risk committee review and legally binding justification.

- Emergency temporary access
  1. Security-approved emergency tokens are issued with a maximum lifetime of 8 hours and always require requestor identity and justification logged in the registry.
  2. All emergency tokens are rotated immediately after use and subject to audit.

Operational checklists (onboarding, decommissioning)

- Onboarding checklist (product/integrations owner)
  1. Fill integration registry form and indicate data residency.
  2. Obtain security approval and assign RBAC role.
  3. Implement structured audit events and test end-to-end flow to audit-collector.
  4. Confirm retention class and encryption key location.
  5. Run security gating pipeline and get SAST/DAST results.

- Decommissioning checklist
  1. Rotate or revoke credentials and remove egress rules.
  2. Export final audit slice and mark evidence bundle.
  3. Apply retention policy for residual artifacts; if deletion requested, follow secure deletion workflow and record proof.

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets

- Exporting a time-bounded audit slice (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_TOKEN" \
    "https://audit-collector.internal/api/v1/export?connector_id=stripe-sync-abc123&from=2025-12-01T00:00:00Z&to=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z" \
    -o stripe-sync-dec-2025-logs.json

- Rotating connector credentials (gateway CLI):
  rwd-gateway rotate-connector --id stripe-sync-abc123 --reason "compromise-suspected" --force

Appendix B: Evidence manifest template (text)

manifest_id: BUNDLE-20260109-0001
created_by: priya.patel@redwood.ai
components:
  - integration_registry_export: path/to/registry.csv
  - audit_slice: path/to/stripe-sync-dec-2025-logs.json
  - kms_rotation_logs: path/to/kms-rotation.log
signature: <base64-signature>

Review cadence and metrics

- Quarterly: sample 10% of active third-party connectors for RBAC and logging completeness.
- Annual: evidence readiness drill (tabletop) with Legal and Compliance.
- KPIs: percentage of integrations with end-to-end structured events (target 100%), average time to produce an evidence bundle (target < 3 business days).

Related documents and references

- See audit-collector onboarding guide, authz-service policy AZ-THIRD-PARTY-01, integration registry template, and secure-sdlc checklist.

Questions and contact

- Policy owner: security@redwood.ai (Priya Patel). For urgent incidents, contact security on-call via PagerDuty (rotations listed in Eng SRE runbook).

Change log

- 2025-09-15: Initial draft and stakeholder review.
- 2025-11-02: Added KMS rotation requirements and retention matrix updates.
- 2026-01-10: Clarified emergency token lifecycle and evidence packaging steps.
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Retention policy schema and validation

sections.body:
This page defines the **Retention Policy** payload schema used by the control plane, the **validation rules** enforced at write-time (API + Console), and tier-specific **min/max TTL** constraints.

The policy is evaluated in the **control plane** and enforced by data-plane purge/TTL jobs. Policy changes are audited, versioned, and exportable for compliance reporting.

**In scope for v1/v1.1:**
- Request/response logs (where logging is enabled)
- Prompts/completions *where stored* (e.g., debugging capture, eval artifacts)
- Audit logs
- Traces and metrics retention for platform telemetry
- Artifacts (eval datasets, red-team prompt sets) where applicable

---
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- **Data class**: a named category of stored data subject to a retention rule (e.g., `audit_logs`).
- **TTL**: time-to-live. After TTL elapses, records become eligible for deletion.
- **Retention rule**: configuration for one data class (TTL + behavior).
- **Legal hold**: suspension of deletion for a defined scope; requires an approved exception workflow.
- **Effective time**: timestamp after which the policy is considered active. Enforcement is best-effort and asynchronous.
sections.heading: Terminology

sections.body:
- Retention applies to **stored data** only. If a data class is not collected/stored, retention settings for that class are treated as **Not Applicable** (see “Disabled logging modes”).
- Purge semantics are **eventual** (asynchronous jobs) and must be **idempotent**.
- Changing TTL to a shorter period does not retroactively “time travel”; it makes older data eligible and is deleted on the next purge cycle.

---
sections.heading: Key semantics

sections.body:
- Global defaults + per-data-class overrides
- Legal hold block (references the exception workflow)
sections.heading: v1 (GA)

sections.body:
- Optional `region_overrides` to allow different TTLs by residency region (only where product tier supports multi-region storage)
- Optional `grace_period_hours` for staged purge after TTL expiry (bounded)
sections.heading: Adds

sections.body:
- v1 payloads remain accepted.
- v1 payloads are normalized internally to the v1.1 model with empty `region_overrides`.

---
sections.heading: Backward compatibility

sections.body:
**Object name:** `RetentionPolicy`

**Notes:**
- The API persists a server-generated `id` and `change_history`. These fields are not required in create/update requests.
- All timestamps are UTC.
sections.heading: RetentionPolicy payload (API/Console)

sections.body:
- `schema_version` (string): `"1.0"` or `"1.1"`
- `tier` (string): `"hosted" | "dedicated" | "private"`
- `effective_at` (string, RFC3339): e.g., `"2025-02-01T00:00:00Z"`
- `rules` (array): per-data-class rule set
sections.heading: Required fields (create/update)

sections.body:
- `name` (string): human-readable label
- `description` (string)
- `region_overrides` (array): v1.1 only
- `legal_hold` (object): hold metadata (see below)

---
sections.heading: Optional fields

sections.body:
- `request_logs` — request/response metadata and payloads *where logging is enabled*
- `prompt_completion_captures` — stored prompts/completions captured for debugging/evals (not ephemeral streaming)
- `audit_logs` — security-relevant administrative events
- `traces` — distributed tracing spans/events
- `metrics` — time-series metrics
- `artifacts_eval_datasets` — eval datasets, red-team prompt sets, and related artifacts stored by Redwood

If a data class is not supported for a given tier/deployment mode, the API rejects it with `unsupported_data_class`.

---
sections.heading: Use the following identifiers verbatim

sections.body: Each entry in `rules` is a `RetentionRule`.
sections.heading: Rule schema

sections.body:
- `data_class` (string, required): one of the canonical identifiers
- `ttl_days` (integer, required): number of days to retain stored records
- `purge_mode` (string, optional): `"scheduled"` (default) | `"expedite"`
- `grace_period_hours` (integer, optional; v1.1): additional delay after TTL eligibility before deletion begins (default 0)
- `notes` (string, optional): internal notes (audited)

`purge_mode` semantics:
- `scheduled`: delete on normal cadence and throttling limits.
- `expedite`: best-effort prioritization in purge queues (subject to platform safety limits; may require approval for large backfills).

`grace_period_hours` constraints:
- 0–72 hours (all tiers). Values outside range are rejected.

---
sections.heading: RetentionRule fields

sections.body: `region_overrides` allows per-region TTL deviations from the base rule for the same `data_class`.
sections.heading: Region overrides (v1.1)

sections.body:
- `region` (string, required): e.g., `"us-east"`, `"us-west"`, `"eu-central"`
- `rules` (array, required): same `RetentionRule` shape but restricted to overriding `ttl_days`, `purge_mode`, and `grace_period_hours`
sections.heading: RegionOverride fields

sections.body:
- Overrides must reference only data classes present in base `rules`.
- Overrides may tighten retention (shorter TTL) or extend retention (longer TTL) **only within tier max/min constraints**.
- If the product tier/deployment does not support multi-region storage, `region_overrides` is rejected with `region_overrides_not_supported`.

---
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body: Legal hold does not change the configured TTL; it suspends deletion for a defined scope.
sections.heading: Legal hold block

sections.body:
- `enabled` (boolean, required)
- `scope` (string, required when enabled): `"tenant" | "data_class" | "time_window"`
- `data_classes` (array of strings, required for scope `data_class`)
- `start_at` (string, RFC3339, required)
- `end_at` (string, RFC3339, optional)
- `reason` (string, required)
- `approved_by` (string, required): approver identity (must match RBAC + approval matrix)
- `ticket_ref` (string, required): link/id to the approved exception (e.g., JIRA/ServiceNow)
sections.heading: Fields

sections.body:
- Legal hold requests are validated against the approval matrix (see “Legal hold and retention exceptions”).
- When enabled, enforcement services must emit a hold signal in metrics and annotate purge job runs.

---
sections.heading: Validation
Example A: Dedicated tenant (v1.1) with region overrides
Example B: Hosted tenant (v1.0) minimal policy
Example C: Legal hold (tenant scope)

sections.body: Validation happens in the control plane on create/update. Any error results in HTTP 400 with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message.
sections.heading: Validation rules (write-time)

sections.body:
- `schema_version` must be a supported value (`1.0` or `1.1`).
- `tier` must match the tenant’s deployment tier.
- `effective_at` must be valid RFC3339.
- `rules` must contain unique `data_class` entries (no duplicates).
- `ttl_days` must be an integer.
sections.heading: 1) Structural validation

sections.body:
The API enforces min/max TTL limits based on tenant tier.

**Table: TTL bounds (days)**
| Data class | Hosted (min–max) | Dedicated (min–max) | Private (min–max) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| request_logs | 1–30 | 1–90 | 1–3650 |
| prompt_completion_captures | 1–14 | 1–30 | 1–3650 |
| audit_logs | 90–400 | 90–730 | 30–3650 |
| traces | 1–30 | 1–90 | 1–3650 |
| metrics | 7–30 | 7–180 | 1–3650 |
| artifacts_eval_datasets | 30–365 | 30–730 | 1–3650 |
sections.heading: 2) TTL bounds (min/max by tier and data class)

sections.body:
- If a tenant is configured for an enhanced compliance package, Security may set stricter minimums for `audit_logs` via server-side policy (not customer configurable).
- For Private deployments, long TTLs are allowed but may be constrained by the customer’s own storage policies and infrastructure limits.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
- `grace_period_hours` must be 0–72.
- `purge_mode` must be `scheduled` or `expedite`.
- `region_overrides` (if present):
  - only allowed for `schema_version` >= 1.1
  - region names must be in the tenant’s allowed region list
  - override rules must reference only data classes present in base `rules`
sections.heading: 3) Cross-field validation

sections.body:
- If `data_class` is unknown: `unknown_data_class`.
- If `data_class` is known but not supported for that tenant/tier: `unsupported_data_class`.
sections.heading: 4) Unsupported or non-configurable classes

sections.body:
- If `tier` does not match tenant tier: `tier_mismatch`.
- Only principals with `retention_policy:write` may create/update policies.
- Updates that shorten `audit_logs.ttl_days` or enable `purge_mode=expedite` for `audit_logs` require elevated permission `retention_policy:privileged_write`.

---
sections.heading: 5) Tier mismatch and permissions

sections.body: Retention does not independently enable data collection. If logging/collection for a data class is disabled elsewhere (tenant logging config, telemetry toggles, or product tier restrictions), retention rules behave as follows:
sections.heading: Handling disabled logging modes / not-applicable classes

sections.body:
- The policy remains **valid** as long as it passes schema + TTL bounds validation.
- Enforcement for that data class returns status **NOT_APPLICABLE** and emits a metric signal (for transparency).
- The Console surfaces a warning: “This data class is not currently collected; retention settings will not have effect until enabled.”
sections.heading: Behavior

sections.body: We currently implement warnings (Console) rather than hard errors for most disabled-collection scenarios to avoid blocking policy templates reused across environments.
sections.heading: Validation warnings vs. errors

sections.body:
- The tenant tier cannot ever produce that data class (e.g., requesting `prompt_completion_captures` on a tier where capture is not available): `unsupported_data_class`.
- The requested configuration is internally contradictory (e.g., `region_overrides` for a single-region tenant): `region_overrides_not_supported`.
sections.heading: Hard errors are raised when

sections.body:
Even when NOT_APPLICABLE, retention configuration changes are:
- recorded in audit logs (`retention_policy.updated` event)
- included in retention configuration exports for compliance reporting

---
sections.heading: Audit requirements

sections.body:
- `invalid_schema_version`
- `tier_mismatch`
- `unknown_data_class`
- `unsupported_data_class`
- `duplicate_data_class_rule`
- `ttl_out_of_bounds`
- `invalid_grace_period`
- `invalid_purge_mode`
- `region_overrides_not_supported`
- `region_not_allowed`
- `override_rule_missing_base_rule`
- `insufficient_permissions`
sections.heading: Common validation failures

sections.body:
```json
{
  "error": "ttl_out_of_bounds",
  "message": "request_logs.ttl_days must be between 1 and 30 for hosted tier",
  "field": "rules[0].ttl_days"
}
```

---
sections.heading: Example response body (illustrative)

sections.body:
- Purge jobs must apply **server-side safety limits** (batch sizes, throttling) to prevent DB pressure.
- TTL enforcement must be observable (e.g., `ttl_lag_seconds`, `purge_failures_total`, `purge_rows_deleted_total`).
- Policy evaluation results are cached in the control plane; cache invalidation occurs on policy update events.

---
sections.heading: Operational notes (implementation constraints)

sections.body:
- Any update creates a new entry in retention policy change history (who/when/what changed).
- For enterprise tenants, changes that reduce retention for audit logs should follow the exception workflow and may require Security approval.

---
sections.heading: Change management

sections.body:
- Schema + validation: Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park) and Security Engineering (Marcus Lin)
- Compliance export usage: GRC (Olga Petrov)
- Purge enforcement and verification metrics: SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant)

payload.page_title: Geo-fenced Access Forensics and RBAC Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines patterns, responsibilities, and step-by-step procedures for investigating and producing compliance evidence when an access event or security incident is constrained by geographic (geo-fenced) residency requirements. It covers how RBAC signals, audit logs, and retention boundaries interact with incident response and secure SDLC controls to produce verifiable artifacts for internal review and external audits.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Scope: incidents where data access or processing may violate geo-residency, cross-border transfer, or regional entitlements (includes customer-configured VPCs, Private deployments, Hosted API requests routed across regions).
- Objectives:
  - Provide a repeatable evidence chain that ties access decisions to principals, policies, and infrastructure location at the time of the event.
  - Minimize evidence sprawl while respecting legal retention constraints and data minimization requirements.
  - Define roles, SLOs, and tool commands for secure collection and packaging of artifacts for auditors.
sections.heading: Scope and Objectives

sections.body:
- Geo-fenced resource: dataset, model endpoint, or storage bucket configured with a residency constraint (e.g., EU-only).
- Primary evidence artifacts: RBAC policy snapshot, access token metadata, audit-log slices (authorization and transport), network egress records, cloud-region metadata, system time synchronization proof, and KMS access logs.
- Evidence envelope: compressed, signed package (SHA256) containing artifacts + manifest + chain-of-custody record.
sections.heading: Key Concepts and Definitions

sections.body:
- Incident Commander (IC): security-oncall (security team) — overall authority for evidence collection within SLO.
- Data Residency Owner: product/security owner for the customer/feature — validates residency policy interpretation.
- Forensics Lead: eng-sre / security operations — collects logs, takes snapshots, and produces the envelope.
- Legal/Compliance Liaison: finance-legal — coordinates disclosure and retention exceptions.
- Deploying Service Owner: eng-platform/eng-private-deployments — provides runtime topology and region mapping.
sections.heading: Ownership and Roles

sections.body:
1) Evidence preservation SLO: initial data-preservation snapshot within 60 minutes of IC assignment.
2) Evidence package delivered to Legal/Compliance for review within 24 hours.
3) Complete chain-of-custody record finalized within 7 calendar days.
Failure to meet SLOs escalates to the Head of Security and the Compliance Director.
sections.heading: SLOs and Timelines

sections.body:
- RBAC policy review gate in SDLC: all changes to region-scoped roles must include a signed review and automated tests validating policy effect on resource filters.
- Immutable audit pipeline: all access events are forwarded to the immutable-audit-store with append-only retention policies and signed timestamps (see Audit Pipeline FAQ).
- Regional telemetry tagging: services must emit a region tag (redwood_region) with requests for routing decisions and post-hoc verification.
- KMS policy templates: regional key usage must be logged and linked to audit entries with KMS key id.
sections.heading: Pre-incident Controls (Secure SDLC and Runtime)

sections.body:
- Detection signals: guardrail alert (data access outside residency), anomalous RBAC grant, cross-region egress spike, or customer report.
- Triage checklist (initial):
  1. Confirm IC and Forensics Lead assignment.
  2. Record the initial detection time and signal source.
  3. Capture transient guardrail artifact (alert id, screenshot).
  4. Flag affected tenants, resources, and region tags.
sections.heading: Detection and Triage

sections.body:
- 1) Live RBAC state snapshot: `redwood-cli rbac snapshot --resource <resource-id> --output rbac-snapshot.json` (includes role mappings, role bindings, attribute filters).
- 2) Auth token metadata: fetch from auth-service token-inspector API for the suspect tokens (redact token values; collect token id, creation, TTL, issuer, scope).
- 3) Immutable audit slice: query immutable-audit-store for events between T-30m and T+30m for the resource and principal. Example query: `SELECT * FROM audit WHERE resource_id = 's3:bucket:customer-foo' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2025-09-01T10:00:00Z' AND '2025-09-01T10:30:00Z'`.
- 4) Network egress and route logs: include NAT/gateway records showing egress region.
- 5) Cloud provider region metadata: map instance IDs to region and AZ at event time via cloud-inventory snapshots.
- 6) KMS access logs: list of decrypt/encrypt operations against region-bound keys.
- 7) System control plane snapshots: model routing policy, routing decisions, and fallback rules in effect.
- 8) Time-source verification: NTP/time-sync check of service nodes (document drift if any).
sections.heading: Evidence Types and Collection Order (preservation-first)

sections.body:
- Envelope contents (recommended):
  - manifest.json (artifact index with SHA256 checksums, timestamps, collector id)
  - rbac-snapshot.json
  - audit-slice.ndjson
  - network-egress.csv
  - cloud-inventory.json
  - kms-access.log
  - response-routing-state.yaml
  - collection-log.txt (human-readable steps and collector assertions)
- Sign the envelope using the Forensics Lead key: `gpg --armor --detach-sign evidence-envelope.tar.gz`.
- Store the envelope in restricted retention-bucket with object ACL 'compliance-evidence' and immutable lock (where supported).
sections.heading: Chain-of-Custody and Evidence Envelope Format

sections.body:
- Steps run from Forensics host with required ephemeral credentials:
  1) Gather artifacts into /tmp/evidence-<incident-id>/
  2) Generate manifest with checksums:
     `find . -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum > manifest.sha256`
  3) Tar, compress, and sign:
     `tar -czf evidence-<incident-id>.tar.gz -C /tmp evidence-<incident-id>`
     `gpg --armor --detach-sign evidence-<incident-id>.tar.gz`
  4) Upload to retention-bucket with server-side-encryption and legal hold tag:
     `aws s3 cp evidence-<incident-id>.tar.gz s3://compliance-evidence-restricted/ --sse aws:kms --tagging \"legalhold=true\"`
sections.heading: Packaging CLI Example (consolidated)

sections.body:
- If evidence contains customer PII in a jurisdiction with strict residency (e.g., EU), perform redaction and store derivatives in-region only. Where legal holds require cross-border transfer for investigation, obtain Legal approval and document the exception in the manifest with justification and duration.
- Default retention for investigation artifacts: 1 year in restricted storage; shorter retention allowed when artifacts are validated and no longer needed for regulatory obligations.
sections.heading: Retention and Minimization Policies (data-residency-aware)

sections.body:
- Within 24 hours the Forensics Lead packages a preliminary envelope and notifies Legal/Compliance and the Data Residency Owner.
- Legal/Compliance performs an accept/reject on cross-border transfer requests. If rejected, evidence must be rebuilt with in-region-only artifacts or with approved redactions.
- Handoff checklist:
  - Verify manifest checksums and signatures.
  - Confirm access control on evidence object (RBAC policy limited to: Legal/Compliance, Security IC, Forensics Lead).
  - Create audit ticket linking incident id to package id.
sections.heading: Evidence Review and Handoff

sections.body:
- Low-risk: no cross-border exposure, only internal access — document and close after 7 days with minimal retention.
- Medium-risk: suspected jurisdictional exposure but mitigations possible (redaction, in-region rebuild) — escalate to Compliance for review; allow temporary restricted transfer pending approval.
- High-risk: confirmed cross-border PII transfer or regulated data exposure — pause automated retention policy, notify external counsel, and follow escalation tree up to CEO if required.
- Keep an exceptions register with: incident id, justification, approver, allowed transfer scope, and expiration date.
sections.heading: Exception and Risk Handling (Risk and Exceptions)

sections.body:
- Completeness: percentage of required artifacts present in envelope (target >= 95%).
- Time-to-preserve: median time from IC assignment to first envelope creation (target <= 60 minutes).
- Integrity: percent of envelopes with valid signatures and checksum verification at handoff (target 100%).
- Residency compliance: percent of cross-border evidence transfers that had explicit Legal approval (target 100%).

Operational Playbook: Step-by-step (concise):
1) IC assigns Forensics Lead and creates incident ticket with residency tag.
2) Forensics Lead runs `redwood-cli rbac snapshot` and collects auth metadata.
3) Pull audit slices and network logs using immutable-audit-store queries.
4) Collect cloud-inventory and KMS logs; perform NTP check.
5) Package artifacts into envelope, generate manifest, sign, and upload to restricted bucket.
6) Notify Legal/Compliance, Data Residency Owner, and Deploying Service Owner.
7) Legal approves or requests redaction/in-region rebuild.
8) Finalize chain-of-custody and close incident when artifacts meet review.

Appendix A — Example manifest.json (excerpt):
{\n  \"incident_id\": \"INC-2025-2345\",\n  \"created_by\": \"forensics.priya\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-09-01T11:12:00Z\",\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    {\"path\": \"rbac-snapshot.json\", \"sha256\": \"<sha256>\"},\n    {\"path\": \"audit-slice.ndjson\", \"sha256\": \"<sha256>\"}\n  ],\n  \"legal_approval\": {\"status\": \"pending\", \"approver\": \"\"}\n}

Appendix B — Quick queries and locations:
- Immutable audit store: https://immutable-audit.internal.redwood/query (requires mfa+security role)
- RBAC snapshot API: https://rbac-api.internal.redwood/v1/snapshot
- Evidence upload bucket: s3://compliance-evidence-restricted (access via `aws s3` with compliance-role)

Appendix C — Frequently asked decisions:
- Q: Can we transfer evidence cross-border for urgent legal analysis?
  A: Only with Legal approval and a documented exception; redactions preferred where possible.

- Q: What if an artifact is missing due to retention TTL?
  A: Record the missing artifact in the manifest, escalate to Forensics Lead and Legal; consider reconstructing from higher-level telemetry if available.
sections.heading: Audit and Evidence Quality Metrics

sections.body:
- RBAC change gate in SDLC (link to engineering workflow)
- Immutable audit pipeline design doc (link to audit-logging/design)
- KMS key usage and regional key policy template (link to secure-sdlc/key-management)
sections.heading: Related Controls and References

sections.body:
- Security Oncall: security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Forensics Lead (rotation): forensics-rotation@redwood.ai
- Legal/Compliance: compliance@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Security Assurance Blueprint for Cross-Border Model Deployments

sections.body: This blueprint defines a repeatable assurance pattern for deploying Redwood model-serving assets across international boundaries while satisfying RBAC, audit logging, data residency, secure SDLC checkpoints, incident response obligations, and compliance evidence requirements. It is intended for platform engineers, compliance owners, and SREs responsible for private or Dedicated deployments that span multiple legal jurisdictions (EU, UK, US, APAC).
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Provide a single mapping that ties each regulatory/contractual requirement to concrete controls and evidence artifacts.
- Standardize deployment-time and post-deploy validation checks to produce audit-ready packages.
- Outline an incident-oriented evidence preservation flow that maintains cross-border chain-of-custody requirements.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Applies to: Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments that process customer data in or across different legal jurisdictions, including model weights, telemetry, and request/response logs.
- Not in scope: purely hosted API requests that do not trigger private-region routing (handled by Hosted API compliance).
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Model-router (service-uid: model-router-prod) — routes requests by region and policy.
- Authz-gateway (service-uid: authz-gw) — central RBAC enforcement point for tenant-level entitlements.
- Audit-collector (service-uid: audit-collector) — immutable log ingestion and short-term secure archive.
- Residency-orchestrator (service-uid: residency-ctl) — placement and retention controller for data and artifacts.
- Evidence-bundler (service-uid: evidence-bundler) — packages evidence artifacts for auditors.
sections.heading: High-level architecture references (services)

sections.body:
- RBAC: enforce attribute-based, tenant-scoped role assignments via Authz-gateway. Evidence: role bindings export (CSV), policy versions (git SHA), JIT activation logs.
- Audit logging: all privileged API calls, configuration changes, cross-region routing events logged by Audit-collector. Evidence: signed log manifests, WORM snapshots.
- Data residency & retention: Residency-orchestrator enforces placement, TTLs, and geo-tags. Evidence: placement manifests, retention policy manifests, hashed sample payloads.
- Secure SDLC gates: model onboarding must pass automated static checks, provenance validation, and quantization-safety tests. Evidence: CI run IDs, SBOM for model artifacts.
- Incident response: preserved forensic artifacts must be timebound and provide chain-of-custody. Evidence: preserved forensic snapshot, signed transfer receipts.
sections.heading: Control mapping matrix (summary)

sections.body:
1) RBAC and entitlements
   - Tenant isolation: no tenant-scoped tenant_admin role may span regions. Enforcement: Authz-gateway denies cross-tenant role assignment.
   - Least privilege baseline: roles must be scoped to least privilege templates (viewer, operator, deployer, security).
   - JIT access: enable ephemeral elevated access with maximum duration 2 hours; require approval via identity provider workflow.
   - Evidence items produced at deploy time: role-bindings-<timestamp>.csv, policy-commit-<git-sha>.txt

2) Audit logging
   - SLO: 99.99% write availability to Audit-collector.
   - Retention: operational logs kept 90 days hot, 3 years cold (region-specific per contract).
   - Integrity: logs must be hashed with SHA-256 and stored in WORM block.
   - Required logged fields: timestamp (UTC), request_id, tenant_id, actor_id, operation, resource, region, outcome, pre-image (if config change).
sections.heading: Detailed requirements and thresholds

sections.body:
{
     "timestamp": "2029-01-10T16:21:03Z",
     "request_id": "req_abc123",
     "tenant_id": "ten-42",
     "actor_id": "svc:deployment-bot",
     "operation": "role.bind.create",
     "resource": "roles/tenant_admin",
     "region": "eu-west-1",
     "outcome": "success"
   }

3) Data residency & retention controls
   - Residency policies must be expressed as declarative manifests attached to tenant configuration.
   - Default retention: 30 days request logs unless a contract requires otherwise.
   - Cross-border transfer rules: explicit opt-in with documented lawful basis. Transfers require a Transfer Manifest signed by Legal and the tenant owner.
sections.heading: Example log schema (single-line JSON example)

sections.body:
---
   tenant_id: ten-42
   allowed_regions: [eu-west-1]
   retention:
     request_logs_days: 90
     model_telemetry_days: 365
   cross_border_transfer:
     allowed: false

4) Secure SDLC checkpoints for model onboarding
   - Gate 1 (source provenance): model origin signed and checksum verified. Evidence: provenance.json, checksum.txt.
   - Gate 2 (security scan): vulnerability scan of model runtime container, policy violations = fail. Evidence: vuln-scan-<id>.json.
   - Gate 3 (behavioral eval): test prompts for PII/safety regression. Evidence: eval-report-<date>.html.
   - Gate 4 (deployment artifact review): SBOM, container image digest, and infra-as-code commit. Evidence: sbom.json, image-digest.txt, deploy-pr-<id>.

5) Incident response & evidence preservation
   - Trigger conditions for cross-border evidence preservation: detection of exfiltration, unauthorized privilege escalation, or model integrity anomalies.
   - Steps (numbered):
     1. Immediately snapshot affected region logs and metadata via Evidence-bundler with read-only transfer.
     2. Apply short-term retention hold (30 days) using Residency-orchestrator.
     3. Notify Legal and Compliance; create secured incident folder with signed manifest.
     4. If transfer to another jurisdiction is required for investigation, produce Transfer Manifest and obtain Legal sign-off.
     5. Hand off artifacts to forensics team with chain-of-custody receipt signed by two approvers.

   - Preservation checklist (minimum evidence set):
     - role-bindings export at T0
     - authz-gateway audit trail (48h surrounding event)
     - audit-collector WORM snapshot containing event window
     - model-router routing decision log and pre-image
     - SBOM + container image digest
sections.heading: Manifest example (YAML)

sections.body:
1) Trigger detection (SRE or automated monitor) -> open incident in IR system with tag cross-border.
2) IR playbook invokes Evidence-bundler endpoint /bundle?incident=<id>&scope=regional.
3) Evidence-bundler produces signed bundle manifest and uploads to secure evidence store with geo-tagging.
4) Compliance owner validates manifest and approves or requests additional artifacts.
5) Evidence-bundler issues transfer receipts if artifacts leave original geo-zone.
sections.heading: Evidence orchestration workflow (typical run)

sections.body:
- Residency-orchestrator CLI example (used by platform operator):
  residencyctl set-tenancy --tenant ten-42 --regions eu-west-1 --retention-logs 90

- Short verification script (bash):
  # verify authz policy applied for tenant
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://authz-gw.internal/api/v1/tenants/ten-42/policies" | jq .policyVersion

Operational ownership matrix (roles -> owners):
- Residency-orchestrator: eng-platform (primary), security (secondary)
- Authz-gateway: eng-infra (primary), security (secondary)
- Audit-collector: eng-sre (primary), security (secondary)
- Evidence-bundler: security (primary), eng-platform (secondary)
sections.heading: Automation snippets and verification checks

sections.body:
1. Confirm tenant residency manifest committed to tenant-config repo (reviewer: eng-platform).
2. Confirm RBAC policy linted and policy-commit SHA recorded.
3. Verify Audit-collector writable and health status green for target region.
4. Run Evidence-bundler dry-run and confirm bundle manifest created.
5. Store pre-deploy artifacts in signed compliance vault with retention metadata.
sections.heading: Rollout and audit verification checklist (pre-deploy)

sections.body:
- Bundle manifest describing artifact contents and checksums.
- Signed log snapshots (WORM) with hash chain.
- RBAC export with timestamps and approver metadata.
- Model onboarding evidence (SBOMs, provenance, eval reports).
- Transfer manifests for any cross-border artifacts with Legal sign-off.
sections.heading: Audit packaging (what to hand to an external auditor)

sections.body:
- Exceptions may be requested when a tenant requires temporary cross-border processing for legitimate business reasons. Exceptions process:
  1) Submit exception request referencing tenant_id, justification, duration, and compensating controls.
  2) Security reviews risk and recommends compensating controls (e.g., additional encryption, in-transit mTLS, bilateral NDAs).
  3) Legal approves Transfer Manifest and signs exception.
  4) Exception recorded in Exceptions Register and evidence artifacts flagged with exception id.
sections.heading: Risk & exceptions governance

sections.body:
- Number of cross-border transfers initiated and approved.
- Number of exceptions open and average time to close.
- Audit bundle generation time (median).
- Percentage of deployments with complete pre-deploy evidence (target 100%).

Appendix A: Example evidence-bundle manifest (excerpt)
{
  "bundle_id": "bun-20290105-9f3a",
  "tenant_id": "ten-42",
  "created_by": "evidence-bundler@redwood.internal",
  "items": ["authz/role-bindings-20290105.csv", "logs/worm-snapshot-20290105.tar.gz"],
  "geo_tags": ["eu-west-1"],
  "signatures": ["sig-1:base64..."]
}

Appendix B: Contacts and escalation
- Security on-call: +1-555-0110 (pager)
- Legal compliance lead: Priya Kapoor (priya.k@redwood.ai)
- Platform product owner: Marco Hernandez (marco.h@redwood.ai)

sections.body:

- 2028-12-10: Added incident preservation checklist (reviewed by Marco Hernandez)
- 2029-01-15: Updated retention defaults and added Transfer Manifest workflow (Legal review)

sections.body:

payload.page_title: Preflight Runtime Certification and Integration Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
======
This playbook defines a standardized preflight certification and integration checklist for new runtime releases, scheduler changes, kernel rollouts, and model-variant onboarding. The goal is to ensure predictable latency, cost stability, and safety of production inference before wide deployment. This document is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and release engineers running final acceptance for any change that touches the serving runtime (kernels, scheduler, KV cache, batching, or model packaging).

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: provide a single source of truth for pre-deploy checks, automated tests, performance gates, and manual sign-offs needed to certify a runtime change.
- Scope: changes to the serving runtime binary, kernel packages, scheduler policy logic, new model variants for hosted/dedicated/private, and instrumentation changes that affect tracing or metrics. Does not cover application-level prompt changes or external orchestration (unless they modify runtime configuration).

Ownership
---------
- Release owner: runtime-release@redwood.internal (primary contact for rollout)
- Test lead: runtime-qe (owns automated suites and correctness baselines)
- SRE guard: eng-sre-oncall (approves capacity and incident readiness)
- Product reviewer: owner from product team for model-variant fidelity gates

Acceptance criteria (high level)
--------------------------------
Provide a boolean pass/fail across functional, performance, reliability and observability. All items below must be green or accompanied by an owner-approved risk waiver documented in the release ticket.

| Area | Minimum requirement | Threshold / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Functional correctness | All unit+integration tests pass in CI with coverage >= 85% for changed modules | CI job: runtime-ci/unit and runtime-ci/integration
| Latency SLO preservation | P50/P95/P99 for canonical workloads within +/- 10% / 15% / 25% of baseline | Baseline is previous GA runtime in canary region
| Throughput | Sustained throughput within 90% of baseline under same concurrency | Measured with the workload generator (see Benchmarking protocol)
| KV cache hit behavior | Prefix caching warmup within expected curve (documented in model onboarding) | Synthetic replay should show cache warming within 60s for standard corpora
| Memory stability | No memory growth observed over 30-minute soak with production-shaped traffic | Heap and GPU memory must remain within configured headroom
| Observability | Traces and metrics include new schema fields and pass compatibility checks | Canary traces must surface trace_id and kernel_hint tags

Preflight automated test matrix
-------------------------------
Run these tests before any canary rollout. All tests should be executed in an isolated canary environment that mirrors production networking and acceleration fabric. Where possible, run with recorded production traffic via telemetry replay.

1. Unit + Integration CI: runtime-ci/{unit,integration,e2e-model-sanity} (automated).
2. Microbench kernel suite: micro-kernel-bench (single-node single-GPU) — verifies per-kernel latency distributions and correctness of outputs across sequence lengths 8/64/512.
3. Mixed-concurrency soak: 30m soak with concurrency ladder (10, 50, 200, 600) using workload-sculptor v2. Capture resource metrics.
4. Prefix/KV warmup replay: run prefix-replay with the top-10k production prefixes. Verify warmup curve against baseline.
5. Observability schema validation: run trace-schema-checker and metric-lint to validate new tags and dimensions.
6. Fault-injection resilience: scheduler-fuzz (bump eviction, inject transient NVLink errors, simulate node preempt). Verify graceful fallback and no request leak.

Integration checklist (manual + automated items)
------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Canary cluster creation: allocate a dedicated canary pool with identical GPU types and network topology.
- [ ] Canary routing rules: route 1% of traffic for 2 hours, then 5% for 4 hours if stable.
- [ ] Canary observability: ensure log retention and tracing are enabled with sampling configured to capture 100% of canary requests.
- [ ] Alerting: enable elevated alert thresholds and create a temporary dashboard for the rollout.
- [ ] Traffic shaping: replay production traffic snapshot for 15 minutes at start of each ramp step.
- [ ] Manual sign-off: QE lead and SRE guard must sign off after the 5% ramp.

Benchmarking protocol (detailed)
-------------------------------
Follow this reproducible protocol for all performance comparisons. Preserve deterministic seeds where applicable.

- Tooling: workload-sculptor v2 (https://internal.tools/workload-sculptor), micro-kernel-bench, trace-collector, perf-compare-tool.
- Baseline: the current production GA runtime version and the same model artifacts.
- Environment: isolated VPC, same GPU SKU, NUMA configuration matching the target fleet.
- Steps:
  1. Provision test nodes matching target GPU topology (same instance type and NVLink config).
  2. Warm cache: run a 5-minute prefix replay at 10% of target throughput.
  3. Run single-node microbench for kernels: collect 10k samples per kernel and compute median and tails.
  4. Run mixed-concurrency soak for 30 minutes. Capture CPU, GPU, mem, kernel latency histograms and queue lengths.
  5. Run distributed throughput run: multi-node with autoscaler disabled to measure throughput headroom.
  6. Report: generate an artifacts bundle (bench-report.tar.gz) with raw traces, histograms, config files and an HTML summary.

Kernel and scheduler validation checklist
----------------------------------------
- Verify kernel hinting compatibility: new kernels must accept the same hint flags or gracefully ignore unknown hints.
- Priority decay behavior: when tenant priorities change under load, ensure short-lived priority spikes do not starve background jobs.
- Preemption safety: preemption must preserve KV cache consistency and avoid partial token emission.
- Admission control: admission controller should trim requests beyond configured thresholds rather than returning 5xx without diagnostics.

Kernel knobs to validate (quick table)
-------------------------------------
| Knob | Purpose | Acceptable delta from baseline |
|---|---|---|
| batch_max_tokens | Controls batching window; impacts latency and throughput | +/- 20% relative to baseline recommendation
| kernel_prefetch_depth | Controls KV prefetch depth | Should not increase GPU memory > 5% in steady state
| scheduler_slot_quantum_ms | Time quantum for slot preemption | Should preserve P99 within 25% of baseline

Profiling playbook (how to capture and interpret traces)
------------------------------------------------------
- Capture commands (example):
  - Start tracing agent: curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/trace/start -d '{"mode":"full","duration_s":300}'
  - Collect kernel-level profiles: micro-kernel-bench --collect-profiles --output profiles.tar.gz
- Sampling guidance: stratified sampling across tenant tiers. For canary, capture 100% traces for 15 minutes, then 1% sampling. For production, keep 0.1% default and increase to 1% when investigating.
- Key signals to inspect:
  1. request.timeline: time spent in admission queue, batching window, kernel dispatch, KV fetch, and token emit.
  2. kernel.latency_by_op: per-op breakdown to spot regressions inside attention or matmul kernels.
  3. gpu.utilization and sm_efficiency: look for saturation or poor utilization with high queue lengths.

Release gating rubric
--------------------
A release can proceed to full rollout only when all of the following are true or have an approved risk waiver recorded in the release ticket:
- Functional tests and kernel correctness checks are green.
- Latency SLO preservation criteria met for P50/P95/P99.
- No unresolved high-severity regressions in soak or fuzz runs.
- Observability compatibility verified and schema changes communicated.
- SRE guard has capacity mitigation plan and rollback playbook attached.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (quick steps)
--------------------------------------------
1. Pause traffic to the canary variant via the router API: curl -X POST https://router.internal/traffic-control -d '{"variant":"canary","state":"paused"}'
2. Scale down canary pool to zero and re-route to baseline version.
3. If requests are stuck in admission queue, initiate queue-dump and cancel pending requests: runtime-admin queue-dump --canary --cancel-pending
4. Reproduce failure in sandbox and collect artifacts for postmortem.
5. Create an incident ticket and start an RCA if P0 or customer-facing impact occurred.

Runbook fragment: diagnosing a latency spike during ramp
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm scope: is the spike limited to canary or global? Check per-route and per-model dashboards.
2. Check admission queue length and batching_window_ms metric.
3. Inspect recent scheduler events for preemption bursts or priority churn.
4. Run micro-kernel-bench against a snapshot of the canary node to check per-kernel regression.
5. If KV cache coldness is suspected, run prefix-replay and compare hit rate curve; if warmup is delayed, consider temporary traffic reroute.

Known issues and tolerations (operational note)
----------------------------------------------
- NVLink transient hiccups can cause short-lived GPU timeouts; scheduler should detect and retry at kernel granularity. Operationally, allow one retry for shortest requests.
- Observability schema change: missing kernel_hint tag will be treated as a warning for 7 days before enforcement.
- Model swap oscillation: if model-variant swap occurs rapidly under autoscaler policy, tighten swap debounce to 60s.

Appendix A: sample canary config (yaml)
-------------------------------------
```
canary:
  cluster: canary-eu-1
  traffic_ramp:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 2h
    - percent: 5
      duration: 4h
  sampling:
    tracing: 100%
    metrics: 100%
  resource_overrides:
    gpu_headroom: 10%
    prefetch_depth: 4
```

Appendix B: useful CLI snippets
-------------------------------
- Start a controlled prefix replay:
  workload-sculptor replay --snapshot top10k-prefixes --rate 500/s --duration 600s --target canary-eu-1
- Collect a bench bundle:
  micro-kernel-bench --nodes 4 --samples 10000 --out bench-report.tar.gz
- Validate trace schema:
  trace-schema-checker --endpoint http://trace-validator.internal --report schema-report.json

References and related pages
---------------------------
- Runtime feature lifecycle and sunset playbook (link above).
- Runtime upgrade validation and canary matrix.
- Kernel hinting compatibility spec.

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-11-03: Created by Linh Tran.
- 2025-12-08: Added kernel knob table and profiling commands (review by Asha Patel).
- 2026-01-12: Clarified rollback steps and added canary YAML (review by Nora Kim).

payload.page_title: Transient Data Escrow and Geo-Fallback Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the operational pattern we call 'Transient Data Escrow' and the associated Geo-Fallback decision and evidence flow. It is intended for security engineers, SREs running private and dedicated deployments, legal/compliance reviewers, and on-call incident responders.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Ensure data required for compliance or incident investigation can be quickly captured without violating residency constraints.
- Provide a predictable, auditable escrow lifecycle with clear retention SLAs and retrieval guarantees.
- Define when and how to trigger cross-region fallback in case of outages, capacity constraints, or legal directives.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Applies to transient inference metadata, request/response traces, and short-lived artifacts (prefix caches, ephemeral keys) produced by Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments.
- Does NOT change long-term retention policies for customer data stored in persistent stores; escrow is a short-term, policy-governed buffer used for evidence packaging.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Escrow bucket: encrypted, timebound storage (object store) in the region designated by the customer's residency profile.
- Escrow artifact: a signed bundle (.tar.gz + manifest) containing data snapshots, provenance metadata, and audit indexes.
- Geo-Fallback mode: policy state where escrow writes will move to a pre-authorized alternate region due to an outage or legal directive.
- Evidence Envelope: the set of audit metadata (signatures, ACL snapshots, decision log entries) required for compliance audits.
sections.heading: Key concepts

sections.body:
- Escrow write latency: 95th percentile < 2s for payloads <= 2MB.
- Escrow retrieval SLA: 99.5% successful retrieval within 2 hours for retained artifacts (TTL > 0).
- Maximum escrow TTL: default 30 days unless a longer retention is explicitly requested and approved by Legal.
- Geo-Fallback decision window: automatic fallback only after >3 consecutive region-level health check failures or an explicit approval from Incident Commander for cross-border fallback.
sections.heading: SLOs and thresholds

sections.body:
- Data Residency Owner: Product Security (primary), Customer Success (secondary).
- Escrow Storage Owner: Eng-Infra (owns bucket provisioning and encryption).
- Oncall Incident Commander: Eng-SRE.
sections.heading: Roles and ownership

sections.body:
| Trigger | Action | Evidence required | Approver |
|---|---|---|---|
| Region outage (>5m degraded control plane) | Buffered writes -> local escrow; attempt immediate retry; if >15m, evaluate Geo-Fallback | Health check logs, decision log | Incident Commander (auto) |
| Capacity constraint causing non-SLA throughput | Degrade non-essential telemetry; route critical evidence to escrow in same residency | Routing logs, capacity alarms | Eng-SRE + Product Security |
| Legal order requiring copy in alternate jurisdiction | Freeze new writes to escrow; create sealed copy and escalate to Legal | Sealed escrow bundle, legal notice | Legal + CISO |

Operational procedure: escrow write lifecycle
1. Ingress: service components create an escrow artifact ID and post payload to the regional escrow gateway endpoint (POST /escrow/v1/artifacts).
2. Signature: gateway signs artifact with region-scoped KMS key and writes to 'escrow-inbound' bucket with lifecycle metadata (owner customer id, retention TTL, purpose tag).
3. Indexing: audit-service indexes artifact metadata and emits an audit event: escrow.artifact.created (includes sha256, size, region, signer-id).
4. Retention enforcement: background job enforces TTL; artifacts reaching TTL are soft-deleted and then hard-deleted after 7-day tombstone window.

Runbook excerpt: immediate retrieval for investigations
- Pager: security-oncall is paged with priority-1 when a legal hold or incident requires retrieval.
- Retrieval steps:
  a. Confirm artifact ID and customer residency profile.
  b. Use admin CLI (example below) to request sealed copy: redwood escrow retrieve --artifact-id <id> --sealed --auth-token $TOKEN --target /tmp/forensic/<id>
  c. Verify artifact signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify region_pubkey.pem -signature <id>.sig <id>.tar.gz
  d. Create Evidence Envelope using evidence-packager (see tooling section).
sections.heading: Decision matrix (summary)

sections.body:
- Post artifact:
  curl -X POST https://escrow.<region>.redwood-internal/api/v1/artifacts \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN' \
    -F 'customer_id=acct-123' \
    -F 'purpose=forensic' \
    -F 'file=@/tmp/trace.json'

- Retrieve sealed artifact:
  redwood-cli escrow retrieve --artifact-id a1b2c3 --sealed --region eu-west-1

Audit and evidence packaging
- Every escrow.artifact.* event must be correlated with the authorization decision that permitted the write. The correlation keys: artifact_id, request_id, principal_id, decision_rule_id.
- Evidence Envelope contents (minimum):
  - artifact.tar.gz (payload)
  - manifest.json (metadata: sha256, size, region, TTL, signer key id)
  - audit.log snippet (authorization events +/- 24 hours)
  - system health snapshot (region health metrics at time of escrow)
  - decision-log entry (why geo-fallback or special retention was used)
sections.heading: CLI examples

sections.body:
{
  "artifact_id": "a1b2c3",
  "customer_id": "acct-123",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "ttl_days": "30",
  "signed_by_kms": "projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/rk/cryptoKeys/escrow-eu"
}
sections.heading: Sample manifest (illustrative)

sections.body:
- Preconditions for automatic fallback:
  1. Persistent region connectivity failure across >= 3 control plane probes spaced 30s apart.
  2. All retry windows exhausted for direct writes (>3 attempts).
  3. Alternate region is pre-authorized in customer's residency metadata (allowed_fallback_regions contains target region).
- Manual fallback (requires approval): use when legal or operational urgency exceeds automatic thresholds. Documented via decision-log entry (decision.owner, reason, timestamp, approver).
sections.heading: Geo-Fallback activation policy (detailed)

sections.body: - When geo-fallback moves escrow writes, the system must include the following in the Evidence Envelope: original region health snapshot, signed decision-log entry, list of artifacts impacted, and the mapping of original artifact IDs to fallback artifact IDs.
sections.heading: Fallback evidence requirements

sections.body:
- Legal Hold request flow:
  1. Legal files hold request with artifact IDs or selectors (customer_id + time window).
  2. Security oncall sets 'hold=true' flag on artifacts via admin API; TTL is set to 'infinite' until release.
  3. Evidence Envelope generation is prioritized and retrieval SLA becomes 1 hour.
- Exception approval matrix:
  - Short extension (<=90 days): Product Security can approve.
  - Long extension (>90 days): Legal + CISO signoff required.

Forensics verification checklist (to accompany evidence delivery):
- [ ] Signatures validate against KMS public keys.
- [ ] Audit events for authorization present and unmodified.
- [ ] Decision log entry present for geo-fallback or TTL extension.
- [ ] Chain of custody recorded in evidence manifest (who retrieved, when, and under which token).
sections.heading: Retention and legal hold exception handling

sections.body:
- Audit query sample (Search for escrow writes for a customer in the last 24h):
  SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE event_type LIKE 'escrow.artifact.%' AND customer_id='acct-123' AND timestamp >= now()-interval '24 hours';
- Health check command (control plane probe):
  curl -fsS https://controlplane.<region>.redwood-internal/health || echo "unhealthy"
sections.heading: Operational tooling and queries

sections.body:
- Escrow buckets must be encrypted with region-scoped KMS keys. Key rotation schedule: every 12 months.
- All artifacts are signed on write; signatures stored alongside artifact in '.sig' files. Verification must use the KMS public key published in the key registry.
- Access control: Only service identities with role 'escrow.writer' may write. Escrow.reader.role is required to retrieve sealed artifacts. RBAC changes affecting escrow roles must go through change-management and produce a signed change event.
sections.heading: Security controls and encryption

sections.body:
- Monthly: simulated geo-fallback drill (non-production customer) to verify decision-log creation, artifact mapping, and retrieval.
- Quarterly: legal hold retrieval rehearsal with Legal and Customer Success to validate retrieval SLA and evidence packaging.

Appendix A: Example retention matrix
| Artifact type | Default TTL | Tombstone window | Retain-on-legal-hold? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inference trace (metadata only) | 30 days | 7 days | Yes |
| Full request/response payload | 14 days | 7 days | Yes |
| Debug dump (large) | 7 days | 7 days | Case-by-case |

Appendix B: Contact list
- Escrow Storage Pager: infra-escrow-oncall@redwood.com
- Security Oncall: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Legal Escalation: legal-escalations@redwood.com
sections.heading: Testing and drills

sections.body:
- 2026-03-01: Created by Ava Martinez (Product Security).
- 2026-06-15: Updated to tighten fallback triggers and clarify evidence envelope (Ravi Patel, Zoë Kline).
sections.heading: Change history

sections.body:
- Geo-smart retention and audit evidence playbook (internal)
- Forensic log preservation and legal hold playbook
