payload.page_title: Feature-Flag Access Governance and Evidence Playbook for Emergency Overrides

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines governance, RBAC controls, audit logging requirements, data residency constraints, SDLC gating, incident response procedures, and compliance evidence packaging for feature-flag emergency overrides (a.k.a. "kill switches" or "emergency features"). It covers both the control plane (console/CLI) and the runtime path (service-level toggles) and is intended for security engineers, SREs, product/platform engineers, and compliance reviewers.

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: Ensure emergency feature-flag overrides can be executed with minimal blast radius, clear authorization, full auditable evidence, and predefined post-incident review steps.
- Scope: Applies to all feature-flag systems used to control inference routing, model selection, rollout gating, telemetry masking, or any change that affects production model outputs and customer data handling across Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Exclusions: Temporary local developer feature flags that do not touch production systems.

Definitions
-----------
- Emergency Override: An action which forces a system to a safe state (e.g., disable a model variant, revert routing to a fallback model, or mute logging to stop PII leakage) outside normal release processes.
- Control Plane Flag vs Runtime Flag: Control plane flags are changed via the console/CLI and affect configurations; runtime flags are evaluated at request time by services.

Principles
----------
1. Least-privilege execution: Only the minimal set of roles can initiate overrides.
2. Two-person controls for high-impact actions: Dual approval for overrides that change data residency, purge logs, or enable broad consumer-facing rollbacks.
3. Immutable audit trail: All override actions are logged to the centralized audit pipeline with immutable retention.
4. Evidence-first practice: Immediate evidence collection is required; evidence packaging must meet audit requirements for regulatory reviews.
5. Post-incident gating: Any override must be followed by RCA, mitigation, and, if required, a policy update in the SDLC.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Security on-call: triage, approve (where designated), validate evidence collection, lead post-incident access review.
- SRE/Runtime owner: perform the override when authorized, execute runbook steps, ensure runtime invariants.
- Product owner: authorize business-impact changes and coordinate customer communications.
- Compliance/Ops: collect and package audit evidence for regulators.
- Feature-flag platform owners: ensure flags support metadata, expiration, scoping, and audit hooks.

RBAC model and matrix
---------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Default deny for override endpoints.
- Role bindings must be timebound for temporary elevation.
- Use attribute-based conditions (e.g., region, environment, incident severity) for scoping.

RBAC matrix (examples)
| Action | Low-impact flags (UI visibility only) | High-impact flags (routing, residency, log purge) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| View flags | ops-reader | ops-reader | Read-only allowed for broad ops team |
| Schedule a disable (non-prod) | ops-engineer | ops-engineer | Non-prod only |
| Initiate emergency override (prod) | - | security-oncall + sre-oncall (approve/execute) | Two-person control enforced |
| Revoke override | security-oncall | security-oncall | Revoke requires single owner to restore |
| Grant temporary elevation | security-admin | security-admin | Must create entitlement ticket with TTL |

Technical controls required
---------------------------
- Flags must carry metadata: owner, intended impact, safe-state description, automated rollback TTL, allowed-roles, and residency-impact tag.
- All override APIs must accept a unique incident_id parameter and optional justification string.
- Feature-flag platform must support policy-based approvals (automated or manual) and emit structured audit events for each state change.

Audit logging requirements
-------------------------
Minimum fields to log for each override event (JSON payload example in Appendix):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_id (SCIM ID or service account)
- actor_role_bindings (list)
- action (e.g., flag.disable, flag.set-safe-state, flag.purge-logs)
- flag_id, flag_key, flag_scope (environments/regions)
- incident_id and justification_text
- approval_trace (if dual approval: approver_id, approver_role, approval_time)
- before_state, after_state (diff blob or pointer)
- retention_policy_applied (which retention rule was referenced)
- audit_store_checksum and storage_path (immutable store)

Logging delivery and retention
- All audit events must be forwarded to the centralized immutable audit store (S3 with Object Lock or equivalent for Private deployments) via the audit edge pipeline within 30s of action.
- Retention baseline: 7 years for actions affecting customer data residency or log purges; 2 years for lower-impact overrides.
- Short-term hot-store (30 days) must support full-text search and correlation with telemetry.

Data residency and retention considerations
----------------------------------------
- Any override that alters data residency (e.g., enable/disable a geo-routing flag) requires pre-approval from Data Governance unless it is a declared emergency with clear mitigation steps.
- If an override causes logs or telemetry to be redirected across jurisdictional boundaries, the override must record the legal_basis field and trigger a compliance notification to Legal.
- For Private deployments, evidence must not leave customer VPC without an explicit signed authorization; use in-situ evidence packaging when required.

SDLC gating and pre-deployment controls
-------------------------------------
Before a flag is used in production with emergency override capability, the following SDLC gates must be passed:
1. Security design review: documented threat model entry with affected data flows.
2. RBAC integration test: e2e tests validating binding enforcement and TTL behavior.
3. Audit pipeline test: simulated override with end-to-end audit record validation.
4. Runbook and rollback verification: rehearsed runbook in staging with game-day exercises.

Incident response: emergency override procedure
---------------------------------------------
1. Triage and decision: Security on-call assesses severity and decides on override necessity.
2. Assign incident_id: Create an incident in the designated tracker and include that id in the override call.
3. Dual approval (if required): Use the policy engine to request/record approver. For high-impact changes, require security-oncall and sre-oncall signatures.
4. Execute override: SRE executes the override using CLI with incident_id and justification.
   - CLI example: redwood-ffctl override --flag model-routing-A --state disabled --incident INC-20270210-17 --justification "stop-PII-exfil"
5. Verification: Confirm after_state and service health metrics for 15 minutes.
6. Evidence collection: Immediately trigger evidence collector (see Evidence Packaging section).
7. Communication: Notify product and legal if residency or contract-bound behaviors are impacted.
8. Post-incident: Create RCA, schedule entitlement attestation, and review RBAC bindings for any temporary elevations.

Evidence collection and packaging
--------------------------------
sections.heading: High-level rules

sections.body:
- Immutable audit event (full JSON payload) from audit store.
- Flag history timeline (60 minutes before through 24 hours after).
- Approval trace records (approver identities and timestamps).
- Related telemetry snapshots: routing tables, active KV cache entries, model versions served.
- Network flows and egress logs (if potential exfiltration).
- If logs were purged or redacted, include pre-purge snapshot and retention policy referenced.
- A signed evidence manifest (SHA256 hashes of artifacts) and storage locations.
sections.heading: Required artifacts to collect within 60 minutes of override

sections.body:
- incident_id
- executive_summary (1–3 sentences)
- artifact_index (list of artifact keys/paths)
- retention_class (regulatory retention to apply)
- chain_of_custody (who accessed evidence)
- reviewer_signoffs

Exception and risk handling
---------------------------
- Pre-approved emergency exceptions: Small set of known and documented override types may be pre-authorized for single-person execution (e.g., kill switch for a telemetry stream known to leak non-customer data). These must be enumerated and time-limited in an exceptions registry.
- High-risk overrides (data-residency change, log-purge) cannot be pre-approved: they always require dual approval and legal notification.
- Risk scoring: Each override must be assigned a risk score (1–100) based on impact vectors: customer-data, residency, availability, reputation. If risk score >= 70, require elevated legal review post-override.

Monitoring and verification
--------------------------
- After any override, apply a 60-minute verification window: health checks, end-to-end request sampling, and audit-event replay must be validated.
- Automated anomaly detection should flag mismatches between expected and observed before_state/after_state for manual review.

Metrics and KPIs
---------------
- Time-to-override (target < 10 minutes for declared emergencies).
- Evidence completeness rate (target 100% for high-impact overrides).
- Number of temporary elevations per quarter (trend downwards).
- Number of post-override entitlements not revoked within 24 hours (target 0).

Operational runbooks and checklists
----------------------------------
- Runbook: emergency-override-execute.md (link to team-runbook).
- Checklist (for executing engineer):
  1. Confirm incident id and severity.
  2. Confirm approver IDs and record approval.
  3. Execute CLI/API with incident_id and justification.
  4. Verify after_state and publish verification snapshot.
  5. Trigger evidence collection job.
  6. Notify stakeholders.

Appendices
---------
Appendix A: Example audit event (JSON snippet)
{
  "timestamp": "2027-02-10T17:42:12Z",
  "actor_id": "scim:users:arjun.patel",
  "actor_role_bindings": ["security-oncall", "prod-ops"],
  "action": "flag.disable",
  "flag_id": "ff-model-routing-A",
  "flag_scope": "prod-us-east-1",
  "incident_id": "INC-20270210-17",
  "justification_text": "Mitigating active PII exfiltration from model outputs",
  "approval_trace": [{"approver_id": "scim:users:maya.chen", "approver_role": "security-oncall", "approval_time": "2027-02-10T17:41:58Z"}],
  "before_state": "enabled",
  "after_state": "disabled",
  "audit_store_checksum": "sha256:abcd...",
  "storage_path": "s3://redwood-audit/2027/02/10/INC-20270210-17.json"
}

Appendix B: CLI examples
- Execute emergency override (with approval stub):
  redwood-ffctl override --flag ff-model-routing-A --state disabled --incident INC-20270210-17 --justification "stop-PII-exfil" --approver maya.chen

Appendix C: Pre-approved exception registry sample
| exception_id | description | allowed_roles | expiry | notes |
| EXC-001 | Telemetry mute for non-customer-internal-only stream | sre-oncall | 2027-06-30 | Single-person allowed; must be recorded |

Related artifacts and links
--------------------------
- Feature-flag platform design doc (link: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/feature-flag-architecture)
- Audit pipeline contract (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025)
- Incident runbook template (link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-runbook-template)

Review cadence and owner
------------------------
- Owner: Security (Arjun Patel).
- Review cadence: Quarterly for policies and after any high-impact override.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-11-15: Created
- 2027-02-10: Published with clarifications on evidence timelines and retention classes

Contact and escalation
----------------------

payload.page_title: Access & Residency Exception Request Process (ARERP)

sections.body: This document defines the Access & Residency Exception Request Process (ARERP) used by Redwood Inference teams to request, evaluate, approve, monitor, and revoke exceptions to RBAC, data residency, and retention policies. ARERP ensures exceptions are timeboxed, risk-assessed, and evidence-backed so the company maintains auditability and minimal exposure.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Temporary changes to role assignments that grant expanded privileges (RBAC exceptions)
- Requests to store or process data in locations outside standard residency zones (Residency exceptions)
- Deviations from documented retention schedules for specific datasets (Retention exceptions)
- Any exception that affects audit logging posture or requires changes to collection/retention of logs
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Requester: Individual or team initiating the exception (owner must be a manager-level engineer or product lead).
- Security Reviewer: Security team member who performs risk assessments and recommends controls.
- Data Privacy Lead: Evaluates residency and legal/regulatory constraints.
- Approver: Designated approver(s) depending on risk tier (see Decision Matrix).
- System Owner: Service/account owner responsible for implementing and reverting changes.
- Audit Owner: Responsible for ensuring evidence (logs, approvals) is retained.
sections.heading: Actors and Responsibilities

sections.body:
1) Exception request form (use template below).
2) Justification and business impact analysis (why required, user/customer impact).
3) Duration requested (start/end dates).
4) Exact scope of privileges or dataset identifiers (resource ARNs / project IDs).
5) Proposed compensating controls (least-privilege narrowing, session timeouts, elevated access via jumpbox, step-up auth).
6) Audit evidence plan: which logs will be captured, retention window, retention location.
7) Data residency impact: countries/regions, contractual/regulatory notes, any DPA or customer-specific requirements.
8) Rollback plan and verification steps.
sections.heading: Submission Requirements (minimum evidence)

sections.body:
- Low Risk: Non-production feature flags, ephemeral developer tooling with read-only access to non-sensitive data. Approver: Team Lead + Security Reviewer.
- Medium Risk: Changes that touch production metadata, limited write access, or residency deviation to a neighboring region. Approver: Product Manager + Data Privacy Lead + Security Reviewer.
- High Risk: Broad write/delete privileges in production, cross-border residency with legal constraints, or retention changes impacting regulated data. Approver: Head of Security + Legal + CTO.
sections.heading: Decision Matrix and Risk Tiers

sections.body:
- Initial triage: security reviewer responds within 24 business hours.
- Medium-risk decision target: 3 business days.
- High-risk decision target: 7 business days.
- Maximum approved duration by default: 30 days (extensions must reapply and include a justification and new evidence).

Template: Exception Request (copy into new request ticket)
---
Title: <short description>
Requestor: <name/team>
Service / Resource(s): <service name, project id, ARNs>
Type: RBAC | Residency | Retention | Mixed
Risk Tier (requester suggestion): Low | Medium | High
Start: YYYY-MM-DD
End: YYYY-MM-DD
Justification: <reason>
Compensating Controls: <list>
Audit Plan: <logs to collect, retention location, owner>
Rollback Plan: <steps to revert>
Stakeholders: <names/emails>
Attachments: <evidence, config diffs, screenshots>
---
sections.heading: Approval SLA and Timeboxes

sections.body:
- Temporary session tokens with 1-hour TTL, enforced MFA
- Restricted egress via proxy/VPC endpoint and allowlist of destination IPs
- Live observability: custom dashboard for the duration, with alerting on anomalous patterns
- Query and write quotas for elevated roles
- Continuous audit stream replicated to secure S3 bucket with immutable retention policy

Audit Evidence Requirements
- All approved exceptions must be accompanied by a single JSON manifest stored in: s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/{exception-id}.json
- Manifest fields (examples): exception_id, requester, approvers, start, end, resources, compensating_controls, evidence_location.
- Required logs: IAM policy change events, STS token issuance, data-access events (read/write/delete), network egress logs for affected hosts.
- Retain audit evidence for the longer of: approved exception duration + 90 days OR base regulatory retention period.

Operational Steps (Request -> Review -> Approve -> Revoke)
1) Requester opens an ARERP ticket in the Exceptions queue and attaches the template.
2) Security Reviewer performs a risk assessment and documents findings in the ticket (including recommended mitigations).
3) Data Privacy Lead reviews residency impact for non-US regions and flags legal constraints.
4) Approver(s) sign off in the ticket and add the exception manifest to the compliance S3 path.
5) System Owner implements changes and notifies Audit Owner who validates logs are being captured and retained.
6) During exception window, Security runs weekly checks for anomalous activity (short checklist below).
7) At end date, System Owner revokes elevated access and performs a verification runbook.
8) Audit Owner runs a reconciliation: confirm manifest, logs, and remediation evidence exist.
sections.heading: Compensating Controls Catalog (examples)

sections.body:
- Verify active sessions for elevated accounts (list).
- Confirm no write/deletes outside declared scope.
- Check network egress to non-allowlisted destinations.
- Ensure alerting thresholds are active and have fired if anomalies detected.

Revocation and Post-Mortem
- Immediate revocation criteria: unexpected data access, exfiltration indicators, elevated auth token used outside scope, or legal request from compliance/legal.
- If revocation occurs early, the Security Reviewer files an incident-security page and triggers the incident response procedures per /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-operational-playbook-2024.
- Post-exception post-mortem required for any exception that: (a) exceeded duration, (b) had a trigger causing revocation, or (c) produced any audit alerts. The post-mortem must include timeline, root cause, and corrective actions.

Periodic Review and Metrics
- Quarterly audit: Security and Internal Audit will sample a minimum of 10% of approved exceptions for full evidence completeness.
- KPIs to track: time-to-decision, number of extensions, incidents triggered during exception, and average time to revoke.

Integration with Secure SDLC
- Exceptions tied to feature rollouts must be requested in tandem with a release ticket and include test plans that validate least-privilege behaviors.
- CI/CD gates will automatically refuse deployments that rely on an active exception unless the manifest exists and approvers are listed in the ticket.

Common Scenarios and Guidance
- Developer needing temporary prod read access: suggest read-only role with session TTL and logging; mark as Low risk.
- Partner integration requiring cross-border storage for a pilot: medium risk; require Data Privacy Lead sign-off and per-customer DPAs.
- Hotfix requiring schema migration with delete privileges: high risk; recommend canary window and DB-level replication snapshot before change.
sections.heading: Weekly Security Checklist (during exception)

sections.body:
| Artifact | Owner | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|
| Exception manifest | Audit Owner | exception_end + 90 days |
| IAM change logs | System Owner / Audit | exception_end + 365 days |
| Data access logs (sensitive datasets) | Data Team / Audit | regulatory minimum (e.g., 7 years) |
| Post-mortem | Security | permanent |

Escalation and Risk Acceptance
- If approvers and stakeholders disagree, Security escalates to Head of Security and Legal for resolution within 48 hours.
- Formal risk acceptance for high-risk exceptions must be recorded in the Risk Register and include a compensating-control verification plan.

Appendices
A. Example manifest JSON (store as .json in S3)
{
  "exception_id": "EX-2026-0123",
  "requester": "team/feature-X",
  "approvers": ["Arjun Patel", "Leah Rogers"],
  "start": "2026-01-15",
  "end": "2026-02-14",
  "resources": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-dataset-X"],
  "compensating_controls": ["mfa", "session-ttl:1h"],
  "evidence_location": "s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/EX-2026-0123/"
}

B. Quick links:
- Exception queue: /jira/EXCEPTIONS (internal)
- Residency matrix: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/residency-matrix-2024
- RBAC guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-guidelines-2025

payload.page_title: Cross-domain security controls mapping and exception workflow

sections.body:
Summary:
This document provides a cross-domain mapping of core security and compliance controls (RBAC & auth, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response, and compliance evidence workflows) and defines a single exception and risk process for deviations. It is intended for Product, Security, Engineering, SRE, and Compliance teams responsible for implementing or assessing controls.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce duplicate control efforts across teams by standardizing control intent, minimal implementation patterns, monitoring signals, and exception handling.
- Scope: All Redwood-hosted and customer-deployed products (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and associated infra components (control plane, serving runtime, data stores, logging pipeline).
- Exclusions: Vendor-managed SaaS where contractual controls replace Redwood implementation — exceptions must be recorded (see Exception Process).

Ownership and SLAs:
- Control owner (security): Security Controls & Compliance Team (owner: Asha Mehta).
- Implementation owners: Service teams (runtime, infra, console, onboardings).
- Review cadence: Quarterly control reviews; RBAC privileged role certification every 90 days.
- Incident SLA (security triage): P1 ack 15 minutes, P1 containment 4 hours; P2 ack 1 hour. Audit evidence requests during audits: initial package within 5 business days.

Controls mapping (high level):
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Control domain           | Purpose                               | Minimal implementation   | Monitoring KPI / Alert threshold                  | Evidence to attach                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RBAC & Authentication   | Ensure least-privilege access          | Centralized IAM (Okta + internal SCIM); role-based groups; MFA | Quarterly privileged access audit; alert if >1 user added to admin role outside JIT window | Role membership export, access request tickets, JIT logs |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Audit Logging           | Immutable action trail for forensics  | Centralized write-once log stream (kinesis -> elasticsearch -> cold S3) with tamper detection | No drop >0.1% of events per hour; missing critical logs for >15 minutes -> page SRE | Retention policy record, SHA256 manifests, ingestion metrics |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Data Residency & Retention | Ensure data stored within contractual boundaries; minimize retention | Region-tagged storage buckets, encryption-at-rest, configurable retention policies per customer | Any cross-region replication record -> review within 24 hours; retention mis-config -> ticket | Data residency maps, retention config, customer contract clause |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Secure SDLC             | Embed security in CI/CD and releases  | PR gating: SAST, dependency-scan, secret-scan; release checklist; canary rollback | Failed SAST block on merge; secret-scan alert -> immediate rollback and rotation | Scan reports, build artifacts, release notes |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Incident Response       | Rapid detection and response          | Central pager (PagerDuty); triage runbooks; evidence preservation steps | P1 ack >15m -> incident commander escalation to CTO; RKPI: MTTR target <6 hours for infra incidents | Incident timeline export, preserved logs, evidence bundle |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Compliance evidence     | Provide auditors and customers required artifacts | Evidence orchestration: per-audit manifest, automated exports (S3), signed snapshots | Evidence completeness for audit requests: 95% in initial package | Evidence manifests, signatures, change-log |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Implementation patterns and examples:

1) RBAC & Auth (implementation pattern)
- Pattern: Centralize identity (Okta) and authorize via a service-level RBAC layer that maps Okta groups to service roles. Use short-lived service tokens with workload identity for intra-cluster auth.
- Privileged access flow: Just-in-time (JIT) elevation via access-request system (request -> approver -> auto-revoke after TTL). TTL defaults: 4 hours for emergency, 1 hour for standard elevated sessions.
- Example IAM snippet (service mapping):

```
# Example role binding (conceptual)
{
  "role": "service-admin",
  "bindings": [
    {"provider": "okta", "group": "redwood:service-admins"}
  ],
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}
```

- Controls: MFA required for all interactive access; passkeys allowed; CLI tokens rotate every 7 days; service-to-service tokens rotate every 30 days.

2) Audit logging (implementation pattern)
- Pattern: Emit structured JSON events with standardized schema (event_type, actor_id, service, resource_id, request_id, timestamp, outcome). All services append request_id headers for traceability.
- Pipeline: service -> kafka -> log-enrichment -> write-once index -> nearline analytics -> cold S3 (retention tiers). Tamper-detection uses periodic manifest hashes and external signing service (HSM).
- Monitoring: Ingestion lag SLO: 120s (90th percentile). Alert: ingestion_lag >300s for 5m -> page on-call.
- Example event schema (short): {"event_type":"auth.grant","actor_id":"user:123","resource":"project:abc"} (keep as single-line JSON in logs).

3) Data residency & retention
- Pattern: Customer data is tagged at create-time with a residency label. Replication disabled by default across regions unless contract allows. Retention policy engine evaluates object TTL and purges after retention window via scheduled job.
- Retention defaults: logs: 365 days (security-critical) / 90 days (standard); customer PII: per contract (commonly 180 days).
- Implementation note: For Private deployments, retention enforcement must be configured via the on-prem settings during install and verified during pre-flight checks.

4) Secure SDLC
- Gates: PR cannot be merged unless pipeline passes: unit tests, SAST, dependency-check, secret-scan. Build artifacts are signed using CI key (rotated quarterly). Release checklist includes: security changelog, rollback instructions, canary percentage, and monitored metrics.
- Canary rollout: default 5% for 2 hours, metrics stable -> 25% for 6 hours -> global. Automatic rollback triggers: error-rate increase >2x baseline AND latency p95 increase >30% during canary window.

5) Incident response security procedures
- On detection: create incident in tracking system (link to runbook), preserve evidence snapshot (logs, VM/docker images metadata, audit stream snapshot).
- For suspected data exfiltration: isolate affected instances, snapshot disks, export logs to immutable store, and notify legal and customer success within 24 hours if contractual breach likely.
- Evidence preservation steps (quick):
  1. Capture timestamps and request_ids.
  2. Lock log write permissions to prevent rotation/overwrite.
  3. Create read-only artifacts in signed S3 with SHA256 manifest.

Exception and risk handling workflow (single canonical process)
1. Request: Service owner files an Exception Request ticket in JIRA with template fields: affected_control, justification, compensating_controls, duration, owner, rollback_condition.
2. Initial review (48 hours): Security triage validates completeness.
3. Risk assessment (5 business days): Security + Infra + Product review residual risk and required compensating controls.
4. Approval: For <30 days, Security Approver may approve. >30 days or cross-region/data-residency exceptions require CISO and Legal sign-off.
5. Mitigations & monitoring: All approved exceptions must have monitoring (alerting thresholds) and a mitigation plan documented. Exceptions are timeboxed and auto-expire.
6. Renewal: Requests to renew must submit 7 business days before expiry; renewals get expedited review but require fresh justification.

Exception decision template (fields):
- id: EXC-2025-####
- service: (service name)
- scope: (controls and resources)
- risk_summary: (text)
- compensating_controls: (list)
- approved_by: (names)
- expires_on: (YYYY-MM-DD)

Operational checklist for auditors / evidence packaging
- Assemble: control mapping matrix (this doc), implementation evidence (config exports), logs (signed manifests), role membership exports, JIT audit log, release artifacts for the period under review.
- Packaging steps (CLI examples):
  1. Export roles: `tools/iam/export-roles --service runtime --out roles.csv`
  2. Snapshot logs: `tools/logs/snapshot --since 2025-08-01 --until 2025-08-31 --sign --out s3://evidence/2025-08-logs`
  3. Generate manifest: `tools/evidence/manifest --path s3://evidence/2025-08-logs > manifest.json`

Change log and governance
- Changes to this mapping require sign-off from Security and at least one impacted service owner. Major changes (affecting residency, retention, or RBAC model) must be communicated two weeks prior to enforcement via company-wide digest and product release notes.

Appendix: Quick reference snippets
- RBAC review schedule (example):
  - Day 0: export admin roles -> Day 7: security review -> Day 10: owner remediation ticket -> Day 30: closure.
- Audit ingestion SLOs: 90th percentile ingestion <120s; error budget: <0.1% lost events/month.

Contact and escalation
- Security controls owner: Asha Mehta (ashamehta@redwood.ai)
- On-call security (PagerDuty): sec-oncall@redwood.ai (see internal rota)
- Legal escalation: legal-escalations@redwood.ai

References
- Internal: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/structured-audit-pipeline-and-query-playbook-2026
- Internal: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/privileged-role-rotation-and-certification-guideline-2025
- External: NIST SP 800-53 (for control mapping inspiration)

Approved: Security leadership (CISO) on 2025-09-10.

Note: This is a living document; teams implementing these patterns should attach concrete implementation pages under the service subspace and link back to this canonical mapping.

payload.page_title: Exception process: emergency unsigned (hotfix) offline bundle for Redwood Private

sections.body:
This page defines the **break-glass exception process** for shipping an **emergency unsigned offline bundle** ("unsigned hotfix bundle") for **Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)** when the standard bundle signing process is unavailable.

**Default policy:** All Redwood Private offline bundles MUST be signed and must fail closed in the installer when signature verification fails.

**Exception:** An unsigned bundle may be shipped only under the strict conditions and approvals below, with mandatory compensating controls, customer communication, and follow-up remediation.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Enable urgent customer impact fixes when signing is temporarily blocked.
- Control and document supply-chain risk.
- Produce auditable evidence for customers and internal compliance.

---
sections.heading: This process exists to

sections.body:
- **Offline bundles** distributed to customers for air-gapped or restricted-network environments.
- **Hotfix** releases required for security vulnerabilities, data loss risk, severe availability incidents, or legal/compliance blockers.
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Standard signed releases.
- Customer-controlled internal artifact repackaging (customer actions outside Redwood distribution).
- Break-glass install flags on the customer side (covered in installer policy and runbooks).

---
sections.heading: Does not apply to

sections.body:
- **Offline bundle:** The packaged set of artifacts used to install/upgrade Redwood Private (installer, charts/manifests, image references, runtime artifacts, model/runtime dependencies, SBOM pointer, etc.).
- **Unsigned hotfix bundle:** An offline bundle that is distributed **without Redwood’s cryptographic signature** due to an exception.
- **Compensating controls:** Additional verification steps (hash validation, controlled distribution, access restrictions, enhanced audit logging) required when signature-based integrity verification is not available.

---
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) **Unsigned offline bundles are prohibited by default.**
2) **Unsigned offline bundles may be shipped only under an approved exception** and must:
   - Be limited in scope, time, and recipients.
   - Use compensating controls described in this document.
   - Include a committed plan and deadlines for a **signed replacement**.
3) Any use of this exception is treated as a **Security/GRC event** and must be recorded for audit purposes.

---
sections.heading: Policy statement

sections.body:
An exception request is eligible only if ALL of the following are true:
- **Customer impact is high/urgent**, e.g.:
  - Critical security vulnerability (actively exploited or high confidence risk).
  - Severity-1 incident impacting production installs/upgrades.
  - Data corruption/loss risk.
  - Regulatory/legal deadline where delay would materially harm customer.
- **Standard signing is blocked** due to one of:
  - Signing key infrastructure outage/unavailability (HSM/KMS access failure).
  - Release pipeline break preventing signing with no timely workaround.
  - Emergency incident response requiring immediate patch distribution before signing path can be restored.
- **No safe alternative exists**, such as:
  - Shipping a signed bundle via an alternate signing environment.
  - Reverting to last known good signed bundle.
  - Using a signed minimal mitigation release.
sections.heading: Acceptable reasons (eligibility criteria)

sections.body:
- Convenience, schedule pressure, non-urgent feature delivery.
- Avoiding a normal security review.
- Shipping unsigned because the signing process is “not finished”.

---
sections.heading: Not eligible

sections.body:
The approvers below provide explicit, recorded approval (ticket + written acknowledgment). Approvals may not be delegated without Security leadership consent.

| Decision / Step | Required approvers | Optional / FYI |
|---|---|---|
| Open exception request + initial triage | Release Eng Lead (Connor O'Brien), Security Eng Lead (Marcus Lin) | Product Owner Private (Vivek Kulkarni), SRE Lead (Sean Gallagher) |
| Risk acceptance to distribute unsigned bundle | Security Exec Sponsor (Dr. Aisha Rahman), GRC Lead (Olga Petrov), Release Eng Lead (Connor O'Brien) | Infra/SRE Exec Sponsor (Neha Kapoor) |
| Customer communication approval (template + recipients) | Product Owner Private (Vivek Kulkarni), Support Readiness Lead (Dev Patel), GRC Lead (Olga Petrov) | Customer Success Lead (Rachel Kim), Solutions Lead (Fatima Noor) |
| Final “go/no-go” on distribution | Security Exec Sponsor (Dr. Aisha Rahman) AND Release Eng Lead (Connor O'Brien) | CEO/Legal only if contractually required |

**Quorum rule:** If any required approver is unavailable, the exception is blocked unless Dr. Aisha Rahman and Connor O’Brien both approve an alternate approver in writing.

---
sections.heading: Approval matrix (who must approve)

sections.body:
For each unsigned bundle exception, the release owner (Release Eng) must produce and store the following:

1) **Exception ticket** (single source of truth)
- Title format: `EXC-UNSIGNED-BUNDLE: <Customer/Segment> <Bundle version> <Reason>`
- Must include: impact, timeline, affected customers, mitigation plan, and risk acknowledgment.

2) **Bundle identity + immutable metadata**
- Bundle version (e.g., `private-2026.01.0-hotfix.1`)
- Build ID / CI run ID
- Git commit SHAs for installer/charts/runtime as applicable
- Artifact list (what is included)
- Intended recipients (named accounts)

3) **Compensating integrity verification package (hash manifest)**
Because signature verification is not available, Redwood must provide a **separate integrity verification package**:
- `SHA256SUMS` (or equivalent) covering:
  - Offline bundle archive
  - Internal bundle manifest
  - Installer binary (if shipped separately)
  - Any chart tarballs or dependency packages
  - SBOM file/pointer artifact if included
- Hashes must be generated on a controlled build runner and verified by a second operator.

4) **Two-person verification record**
- Operator A generates hashes and attaches them to the ticket.
- Operator B independently recomputes hashes from the staged artifacts and confirms match.
- Both sign off with timestamp and workstation/build environment identifier.

5) **Distribution controls record**
- Where the bundle is hosted (internal restricted bucket/release portal)
- Access control list (ACL) snapshot: who can download
- Expiration date for access

6) **Customer communication record**
- Approved message sent, time sent, recipients, and acknowledgement if required.

7) **Remediation plan with deadlines**
- Target date for restoring signing pipeline
- Target date for issuing a signed replacement bundle
- Plan for revocation/withdrawal of unsigned bundle

---
sections.heading: Required artifacts and evidence (must be produced)

sections.body: When shipping an unsigned bundle, Redwood must apply ALL of the controls below.
sections.heading: Compensating controls (required)

sections.body:
- **Limit recipients** to explicitly approved accounts/environments.
- **Limit time window**: bundle access should expire within **7 calendar days** unless re-approved.
- Do not post unsigned bundles to broad download portals or public locations.
sections.heading: 1) Strict distribution limitations

sections.body:
- A hash file (e.g., `SHA256SUMS`) and verification steps.
- A clear statement: “Integrity must be verified before install; do not proceed if hashes do not match.”
sections.heading: Provide customers with

sections.body:
- `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`
- Or `sha256sum <bundle>.tar.zst` and compare with provided value.
sections.heading: Recommended customer commands (Linux example)

sections.body:
- Avoid tools known to mutate archives.
- Prefer binary-safe transport (e.g., secure copy to removable media, verify hashes after transfer).
sections.heading: Customers must be instructed to

sections.body:
- Bundle filename must include `UNSIGNED` (example):
  - `redwood-private-2026.01.0-hotfix.1-UNSIGNED-offline-bundle.tar.zst`
- Include `UNSIGNED_README.txt` at bundle root stating:
  - Why unsigned
  - Required verification steps
  - Expiration / replacement plan
sections.heading: 4) Explicit risk labeling in artifacts

sections.body:
- The installer must continue to **fail closed** on signature verification by default.
- If the customer must proceed without signature validation, this must be handled via the installer’s documented break-glass path (separately governed), and must be logged locally as a break-glass event.

---
sections.heading: 5) Installer behavior

sections.body:
Approvers must acknowledge the following in the exception ticket:

- “We understand that shipping an unsigned offline bundle increases the risk of undetected tampering in transit or at rest.”
- “We confirm that the signed-bundle pipeline is currently blocked and that no safe signed alternative is feasible within the required timeline.”
- “We commit to issuing a signed replacement bundle by <DATE> and to withdrawing the unsigned bundle from distribution by <DATE>.”
- “We confirm compensating controls are in place: restricted distribution, hash-based verification, two-person verification, and documented customer communication.”

---
sections.heading: Risk acknowledgment (required language)

sections.body: Owner: Connor O'Brien (Release Engineering) or delegate on the release train.
sections.heading: Step 0 — Initiate exception

sections.body:
- Severity/impact summary
- Root cause of signing blockage (what failed)
- Why delay is unacceptable
- Proposed unsigned bundle version + recipients
sections.heading: Create the exception ticket and include

sections.body: Owner: Marcus Lin (Security Engineering)
sections.heading: Step 1 — Security triage

sections.body:
- Eligibility criteria
- Threat considerations (tampering, replay/downgrade risk)
- Whether additional controls are required for the specific customer environment
sections.heading: Validate

sections.body:
Owner: Release Engineering

- Produce the bundle using deterministic build steps as usual.
- Generate `SHA256SUMS` for all required artifacts.
- Complete two-person verification.
sections.heading: Step 2 — Prepare unsigned bundle + hash manifest

sections.body:
Owner: Olga Petrov (GRC) to coordinate approvals

- Collect approvals per matrix.
- Ensure risk acknowledgment language is included verbatim.
sections.heading: Step 3 — Obtain approvals

sections.body:
Owner: Vivek Kulkarni (Product Private) + Dev Patel (Support)

Send approved message before sharing download links.
sections.heading: Step 4 — Customer communication

sections.body:
- Reason for unsigned distribution
- Required hash verification steps
- Support contact path
- Replacement plan and expected timeline
sections.heading: Minimum content

sections.body:
Owner: Release Engineering

- Host in restricted location.
- Provide customer with:
  - Bundle
  - `SHA256SUMS`
  - Verification instructions
  - `UNSIGNED_README.txt`
sections.heading: Step 5 — Distribute with access controls

sections.body:
Owner: Release Engineering + Security

- Confirm customer verified hashes and completed install/upgrade.
- Restore signing pipeline.
- Ship signed replacement bundle.
- Withdraw access to unsigned bundle.

---
sections.heading: Step 6 — Track completion + remediation

sections.body: Subject: `[Action required] Redwood Private hotfix bundle integrity verification (unsigned emergency release)`
sections.heading: Template A — Initial notice (email)

sections.body:
- We are providing an emergency hotfix bundle to address <ISSUE>.
- Due to <SIGNING BLOCKER>, this bundle is **unsigned**. This is an exception to Redwood’s standard signed-bundle process.
- Before installation, you must verify integrity using the provided `SHA256SUMS` file:
  1) Transfer both the bundle and `SHA256SUMS` to your offline environment.
  2) Run: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`
  3) Do not proceed if any verification fails.
- We will provide a **signed replacement** by <DATE> and will retire this unsigned bundle by <DATE>.
- If you have any questions or verification failures, contact <Support alias/SE contact> and include the verification output.
sections.heading: Body

sections.body: Subject: `Signed replacement available: Redwood Private <version> offline bundle`
sections.heading: Template B — Follow-up (signed replacement available)

sections.body:
- A signed replacement bundle is now available: <LINK/DELIVERY METHOD>.
- Please prefer the signed bundle for any new installs/upgrades.
- The previous unsigned bundle will be removed from distribution on <DATE>.

---
sections.heading: Body

sections.body: Within **5 business days** after distribution of any unsigned bundle, Release Engineering must schedule and complete a remediation review with Security + GRC.
sections.heading: Remediation requirements (mandatory)

sections.body:
- [ ] Root cause analysis: why signing was blocked (technical + process)
- [ ] Confirm the signed pipeline is restored OR a permanent workaround exists
- [ ] Issue a signed replacement bundle and validate verification end-to-end
- [ ] Withdraw unsigned bundle distribution and document withdrawal date/time
- [ ] Confirm customer has migrated (or documented why not)
- [ ] Update runbooks/tests to prevent recurrence
- [ ] File follow-up tickets for any process gaps (approvals, evidence, access controls)
sections.heading: Remediation checklist

sections.body:
- Link to signed replacement release artifact
- Confirmation of unsigned bundle removal
- Summary of customer outcome (install success + any issues)

---
sections.heading: Evidence to attach after remediation

sections.body:
- Exception tickets and evidence must be retained for **7 years** (or longer if customer contract requires).
- All approvals must be recorded in writing (ticket comments are acceptable if identities are validated).
- Access logs for downloads must be retained for at least **1 year**.

---
sections.heading: Audit and retention

sections.body:
If an unsigned bundle is suspected to be tampered with, leaked, or redistributed beyond approved recipients:
1) Notify Security on-call and Release Engineering immediately.
2) Stop distribution (revoke links/credentials).
3) Initiate an incident: “Potential supply-chain compromise (unsigned bundle exception)”.
4) Provide customers with new verified artifacts and guidance.

---
sections.heading: Escalation and incident handling

sections.body:
**Q: Can we ship an unsigned bundle to keep a release train on schedule?**
No. Schedule pressure is not an eligible reason.

**Q: Can we provide only a single hash of the bundle archive?**
No. At minimum, provide a hash for the archive and the internal manifest; additionally provide hashes for critical install components (installer, charts/deps) to support targeted verification and troubleshooting.

**Q: Can Support approve this exception?**
No. Support participates in readiness and communication, but Security leadership, GRC, and Release Engineering approvals are mandatory.

**Q: Does this change the installer verification policy?**
No. The installer must continue to treat missing/invalid signatures as a failure by default; any customer-side override remains separately governed and must be audited.

payload.page_title: Entitlement Drift Detection & Forensic Readiness Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end detection, alerting, triage, and evidence-packaging processes for entitlement drift (unexpected or unauthorized changes to role bindings, group memberships, service accounts, and temporary elevations). It ties RBAC monitoring to audit logging, data residency constraints, Secure SDLC checkpoints, and incident-response forensics so Redwood can:

- Rapidly detect drift events across control planes (IAM, tenant ACLs, orchestration, model-serving policies).
- Triage and contain drift with minimal blast radius.
- Assemble admissible evidence for legal, compliance, or customer audits while preserving chain-of-custody and residency constraints.

Scope and Audience

This document applies to: production and staging control planes that affect inference access (console, API keys, service identities, feature flags, and model access policies). Primary audience: security operations, SRE, platform engineers, and compliance reviewers.

Definitions

- Entitlement drift: any divergence between an authoritative entitlement state (the desired state recorded in our provisioning system or policy-as-code repo) and the observed effective entitlements in runtime systems.
- Forensic readiness: ability to preserve, collect, and provide trustworthy traces and artifacts to prove what happened and who performed actions.
- Evidence bundle: a time-bound package of logs, snapshots, and metadata used for audits.

Owner & Escalation

- Primary owner: Security Ops (security@redwood.com)
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (platform-sre@redwood.com)
- Escalation: If drift indicates lateral movement or data exfiltration, escalate immediately to Oncall Security Incident Manager and follow the Incident Response Security runbook (/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-process).

Detection & Alerting Strategy

1) Sources to monitor (examples):
   - IAM change events (cloud provider IAM API): CreateUser, UpdateRole, AttachPolicy, AddRoleBinding
   - Internal entitlement service events: group membership writes, delegated-role activations
   - Service account key lifecycle events: key create/delete, key use from new IP ranges
   - Model-serving access grants: model ACL mutations, tenant-level allowlists
   - Feature-flag activations that enable privileged paths

2) Baseline/authoritative state sources:
   - policy-as-code repo (git): /infra/iam/policies and /platform/entitlements (single source of truth)
   - Provisioning system (Terraform state / config management system)
   - Scheduled inventory snapshots of runtime (every 4 hours)

3) Detection rules and thresholds (examples):
   - High-confidence drift: a direct mismatch between git-authoritative policy and runtime within 10 minutes -> SEV2 alert to Security Ops.
   - Medium confidence: unexpected role binding to a high-privilege role (e.g., "platform-admin", "entitlement-owner") without matching approval ticket -> SEV3 alert.
   - Low confidence: ephemeral group membership mismatch for non-critical roles -> metric alert only (dashboard).

4) Alerting channels: PagerDuty for SEV2/SEV1, Slack #sec-ops for SEV3 triage thread, internal dashboard; all alerts must include: detected_delta, authoritative_reference_commit, first_seen, detected_by_query_id, correlation_id.

Monitoring queries (examples)

- Example SQL (audit-event store):
  SELECT event_time, actor, action, resource, region, request_id
  FROM audit_events
  WHERE action LIKE '%role%'
    AND event_time >= now() - interval '1 hour'
    AND (resource_role IN ('platform-admin','dedicated-operator'))
  ORDER BY event_time DESC;

- Example Kibana DSL for role-binding changes: (description) query on event.type: "iam.change" AND change.target: "role_binding" AND NOT metadata.approved_ticket_id:*

Triage Procedure (quick actions)

1) Acknowledge alert and capture correlation_id.
2) Use the diagnostic checklist:
   - Confirm authoritative state: git commit referenced in alert (git show <commit>).
   - Cross-check provisioning system (terraform state list) for drift markers.
   - Pull audit log slice for event_time +/- 30 minutes and for involved principals.
   - Confirm if change was via automation (pipeline run id, CI actor) or manual (user principal).
3) Contain:
   - If automation error: revert via CI rollback and disable failing pipeline; create a revert PR with emergency tag.
   - If manual and unauthorized: revoke the binding (temporary removal) and rotate any affected credentials. Document change in incident ticket.
4) Escalate:
   - If evidence of compromise (unapproved lateral movement, abnormal artifact access): open Security Incident ticket and follow Incident Response Security playbook.

Forensic Evidence Packaging (evidence bundle spec)

Every evidence bundle MUST include the following artifacts and metadata fields. Keep the bundle representation small (tar.gz encrypted) and signed.

- Mandatory artifacts (minimum):
  - Audit log slice in newline-delimited JSON (event_time window +/- 30m)
  - Snapshot of runtime entitlements (CSV) with SHA256 checksum
  - Git reference: repository, commit SHA, and diff of the authoritative policy
  - Provisioning run logs (Terraform apply outputs, CI pipeline run logs)
  - User/session metadata (IP, geolocation, MFA status) pulled from authn provider
  - S3 object store path or forensic bucket pointer where raw artifacts are kept (encrypted at rest)

- Metadata fields to attach to bundle manifest (JSON):
  - bundle_id (UUID), collected_at (UTC ISO8601), collector, retention_tier, region_residency, legal_hold_flag, chain_of_custody (list of actions + actor + timestamp)

- Evidence signature and storage:
  - Sign the bundle with Redwood evidence signing key (KMS key alias: alias/redwood/evidence-signing).
  - Store hot copy minimum 90 days in encrypted forensic S3 bucket (s3://forensics-<region>) with server-side KMS. Cold archive copies moved to WORM storage with 7-year retention where applicable by regulation.

Data Residency & Retention Considerations

- Residency mapping: Each artifact must be labeled with region_residency based on the source system (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). The collector must not move raw PII-containing logs outside their original region unless explicitly permitted.
- Retention policy (default):
  - Hot (fast access): 90 days (for triage and operational forensics)
  - Warm: additional 275 days (total 365 days) for compliance queries
  - Cold/Archive: up to 7 years where required by contract/regulation; otherwise 2 years.
- Deletion/Legal hold: Legal hold flags block retention transitions. Deletion requires: security approval, legal approval, and completion of evidence manifest.

Chain of Custody and Auditability

- Every evidence action (collect, transfer, sign, export) must be recorded in the evidence manifest and in the centralized audit store with following fields: action, actor, timestamp, target_object, justification_ticket.
- Evidence manifests are themselves logged to the immutable-audit-store topic and have unique evidence_id that maps back to the incident ticket.

Integration with Secure SDLC & Model Onboarding

- Preventative controls:
  - All policy changes must pass policy-as-code checks in CI (static analysis rules for least-privilege, role naming conventions, and residency tags).
  - Any change to high-privilege roles requires two approvers and a dedicated release gate in the deployment pipeline.
- Gate validation artifacts: The Secure SDLC gate produces an artifact (gate_proof.json) that must be attached to any evidence bundle created within 72 hours of that gate activation.

Operational Playbook: Step-by-step (fast response)

1) Detect -> page Security Ops with SEV code.
2) Acknowledge & gather: run quick-collection script: ./ops/collect-entitlement-slice.sh --ticket=<id> --window=30m --out=/tmp/evidence-<id>.tgz
3) Reproduce assertion: compare the collected entitlements CSV with git-authoritative CSV: ./tools/compare-entitlements --gold=repo/authoritative.csv --observed=/tmp/entitlements.csv
4) Contain: revoke binding using least-disruptive step (example CLI):
   - gcloud iam roles remove-binding --role=roles/platformAdmin --member=user:jane@redwood.com --project=redwood-prod
   - or internal: rbackctl revoke --binding-id=<binding> --reason="unapproved-drift"
5) Package evidence: run ./ops/package-evidence.sh --input=/tmp/evidence-<id> --kms-alias=alias/redwood/evidence-signing --out=s3://forensics-us-west-2/evidence-<id>.tar.gz
6) Notify legal/compliance and set legal_hold if requested.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Security Ops: lead detection, triage, evidence collection, legal handoff readiness.
- Platform SRE: assist in containment, runbook execution, and rollback.
- Compliance: advise on retention/residency and approve evidence release.
- Engineers (owners of affected services): implement code fixes, follow remediation checklist, and create follow-up PRs.

Post-incident activities

- Post-mortem required for SEV2/SEV1 drift incidents within 5 business days. Include timeline, root cause, fixes, and evidence bundle link.
- Remediation verification: policy-as-code tests added to CI must run successfully for 3 consecutive successful runs before closure.
- Metrics to track: mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) target <= 30 minutes for high-confidence drift, mean-time-to-contain (MTTC) target <= 60 minutes.

Requesting Temporary Exception or Emergency Elevation

- Workflow summary: Exceptions to be requested in the RBAC exception tracker with justification, duration, and compensating controls (MFA required, IP allowlist, session recording). All temporary exceptions auto-expire and require manual extension.
- Evidence requirement: Exceptions must include expected audit events and a snapshot reminder to collect those events at closure.

Appendices

A: Artifact examples
- Sample evidence bundle manifest (fields listed above).
- Example CLI snippets and script headers are kept in /ops/documents/entitlement-playbook-samples/

B: Queries and detector IDs
- Detector IDs: ENT-DRIFT-001 (git-vs-runtime mismatch), ENT-DRIFT-002 (unapproved-high-priv-role), ENT-DRIFT-003 (service-account-key-usage-from-new-region).

C: Compliance mapping
- Map of regulatory retention obligations per region: US (HIPAA/contractual) up to 7y, EU (GDPR) restrict transfer—minimize cross-border artifact movements, APAC depends on contract. Compliance should be consulted for every cross-border evidence export.

Revision history

- 2026-01-12: Created by Eleanor Chen.
- 2026-03-22: Added containment CLI examples and retention tiers (Marco Villanueva).
- 2026-06-30: Hardened evidence signing procedure and updated MTTD/MTTC targets (Priya Kapoor).

Related documents

- See RBAC provisioning automation: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provisioning-and-evidence-automation-2026
- See audit event schema: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025

Contact

- Security Ops (primary): security-ops@redwood.com
- For legal/compliance inquiries: compliance@redwood.com

End of document

payload.page_title: Authorization Evidence Handoff and Escalation Playbook

sections.body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the standard process for assembling, validating, and handing off authorization (RBAC) and residency-related audit evidence to compliance reviewers and incident responders. It covers trigger conditions, artifact templates, SLAs, escalation paths, and an exceptions workflow for cases where evidence cannot be produced within the standard window.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference services and control planes (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes RBAC role assignments, privileged role rotations, access-request logs, audit trails from KMS/HSM, and data residency/retention manifests.
- Not intended for customer-specific contractual negotiations (handled by Legal/RevenueOps).

Definitions and key SLAs:
- Evidence collection SLA: 48 hours for standard requests, 24 hours for high-priority incident-driven requests.
- Audit log retention baseline: 365 days for control-plane logs, 730 days for payment/auth events (where mandated).
- Proof-of-access window: all role assignment events must be exportable for any 90-day window on request.

Owners and roles:
- Requestor: Product or Ops engineer who initiates an evidence request.
- Evidence Collector: Oncall or SRE assigned in the request (security owns coordination).
- Compliance Reviewer: Security Compliance PM (primary reviewer).
- Incident Responder: Eng-sre or Security IR lead for incidents.
- Exception Approver: Head of Security or delegated compliance lead.

Trigger scenarios (examples):
1) Routine audit: Quarterly compliance review for region X.
2) Customer audit: Customer requests proof of data residency and access controls.
3) Incident: Suspected unauthorized access or data exfiltration.
4) Internal exceptions: Change that bypassed standard approvals (emergency access).

Artifact catalog (what to gather):
- RBAC manifest: exported list of roles, role-bindings, effective principals, and start/expiry timestamps. Format: YAML (see example below).
- Access-change log: time-ordered CSV/JSON of grant/revoke events with actor, justification, and ticket ID.
- Privileged-session traces: pii-redacted shell session logs, jump-bastion records, and session duration.
- Audit-index: pointer file (JSON) mapping artifact locations (S3 path, retention tag, checksum).
- Residency manifest: bucket/region mapping, encryption-at-rest metadata, and KMS key IDs.
- Evidence provenance: collection timestamp, collector identity, hash, and collection method.

RBAC manifest example (YAML):
---
roles:
  - name: infra-admin
    id: role-23cd
    scope: org:infra
    bindings:
      - principal: user:anne.redwood@company.com
        assigned_at: 2025-10-01T09:12:33Z
        expires_at: 2026-01-01T09:12:33Z
      - principal: service:ci-bot@redwood
        assigned_at: 2025-11-08T02:00:00Z
    privileged: true

Access-change export (CLI examples):
- Export role bindings for a 90-day window (GCP/AWS examples shown):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/iam --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1707776000000 --filter-pattern "PutRolePolicy" > access_changes_90d.json
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gce_instance" AND protoPayload.methodName:"SetIamPolicy"' --start-time=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z --end-time=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --format=json > access_changes_90d_gcp.json

Data residency manifest template (ASCII table):
| Resource path | Region | Encryption | KMS Key ID | Retention days |
| /s3/redwood-prod/logs | us-west-2 | AES256 | arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd | 730 |
| /gcs/redwood-prod/embeddings | europe-west1 | CMEK | projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/ek1 | 365 |

Evidence collection procedure (step-by-step):
1. Requestor files an evidence request in the Compliance queue (Jira ticket type: COMPL-EVID) with scope, time window, and reason.
2. Security triage: Within 4 business hours the Security Triage lead assigns an Evidence Collector and marks priority (standard / expedited).
3. Collector performs scoped exports using approved tooling (see approved-export-tools below), stamps each artifact with collection metadata, and uploads to the evidence S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<ticket-id>/.
4. Collector populates the Audit-index JSON and attaches it to the Jira ticket.
5. Compliance Reviewer verifies artifacts, requests clarifications if needed, and marks the ticket resolved or escalates.

Approved-export-tools and locations:
- rdb-audit-export (internal CLI) — outputs compressed JSON and attaches checksums.
- kubectl audit-exporter — for k8s RBAC events.
- redwood-log-archiver (internal) — for centralized audit log slices.
- Evidence storage: s3://redwood-evidence (access limited to compliance+security roles via bucket policy).

Validation checklist (minimum):
- [ ] RBAC manifest covers requested time window.
- [ ] All role-change events contain actor and justification.
- [ ] Residency manifest lists all storage resources and their regions.
- [ ] KMS key IDs present and match key registry.
- [ ] Checksums included and validated after upload.
- [ ] Evidence-index.json present in S3 and attached to ticket.

Escalation and exception flow:
- If evidence cannot be produced within the SLA due to log-rotation or retention limits, the Evidence Collector must:
  1. Immediately escalate to the Security Triage lead with reasons and available partial artifacts.
  2. Open an Exception Request (ticket labels: EXCEPTION / AUTH-EVID) with recommended mitigation (e.g., extended retention, rehydration from cold storage).
  3. Exception Approver has 72 hours to approve or require alternative evidence.
- Emergency incident path: If incident responders require evidence for an active breach, Security may invoke expedited collection and short-term emergency access to archived logs (must be recorded and approved post-facto).

Integration with Incident Response:
- Incident responders subscribe to evidence queue; any COMPL-EVID ticket linked to an active incident must be marked with incident ID and prioritized.
- For PII/SEV incidents, collectors must produce redacted artifacts and a redaction map describing removed fields.
- Chain-of-custody: For evidence used in legal or regulatory proceedings, the Collector must collect under the legal hold process and notify Legal immediately.

Common exception scenarios and mitigations (examples):
- Missing historical logs: Mitigate by retrieving from Glacier/Cold archives (may take 24–72 hours). Document retrieval ETA in ticket.
- Encrypted events missing keys: Coordinate with KMS team to (a) check key rotation logs, (b) verify key escrow policies.
- Cross-region exports blocked by network policy: Use staging export host in target region (requires temporary egress exception).

Runbook: Requesting an RBAC exception (step process):
1. Submit COMPL-EVID / EXCEPTION ticket with: affected role, time box, business justification, and risk assessment.
2. Security Triage performs quick risk assessment (<= 8 hours) and assigns temporary mitigations (e.g., scope-limited sessions, additional monitoring).
3. Exception Approver signs off or rejects. Approved exceptions must include compensating controls and a maximum duration (<= 14 days unless renewed).
4. All approved exceptions are recorded in the Exceptions Register (s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/registry.csv).

Checklist: Audit Evidence Package (final deliverable contents):
- Audit-index.json (string map of artifacts)
- RBAC manifest (YAML)
- Access-change export (CSV/JSON)
- Residency manifest (ASCII table or YAML)
- Checksums and provenance file (SHA256)
- Approval logs (ticket history, exception approvals)

Retention and archival policy references:
- Evidence artifacts follow the Evidence Retention policy: evidence-retention-policy-v2 (see product-docs) — default 7 years for high-risk events.
- Short-term exports kept in s3://redwood-evidence/temp/ with auto-delete: 30 days.

Auditability and tooling notes:
- All evidence collection actions must be logged in the collection audit stream (internal topic: audit.collection.events) with fields: collector, ticket_id, timestamp, artifact_path, checksum.
- Periodic validation job (monthly) re-hashes a random sample of artifacts and reports mismatches to the Compliance channel.
- Example validation SQL (run on the audit-index dataset):
  SELECT ticket_id, COUNT(artifact_path) AS artifacts, MAX(collected_at) AS last_collected
  FROM evidence_index
  WHERE collected_at >= '2025-01-01'
  GROUP BY ticket_id
  HAVING artifacts < 3;

References and related pages:
- Exceptions register: s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/registry.csv
- Evidence retention policy: product-docs/evidence-retention-policy-v2
- KMS rotation playbook: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/privileged-role-rotation-and-certification-guideline-2025.json

Appendix A — Example evidence-index.json (schema summary):
- ticket_id: string
- artifacts: list[string] (S3 paths)
- collector: string (email)
- collected_at: timestamp
- checksum: string (sha256)

Appendix B — Quick troubleshooting tips:
- If export tooling fails with "permission denied": verify export role in IAM; temporarily escalate to infra-admin using Emergency Access Flow and record in ticket.
- If checksum mismatch after upload: re-export artifact, re-calc checksum locally, and update evidence-index with new hash; notify Compliance Reviewer.

Contact information:
- Security Triage Slack: #sec-triage (monitored 24/7)
- Compliance mailbox: compliance@redwood.com
- Evidence storage owner: infra-storage@redwood.com

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Security (Priya Shah). Review cadence: annual or after any incident that invokes this playbook.

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Initial published version.
- 2026-02-10: Clarified SLAs for incident-driven evidence and added audit-index schema summary.

payload.page_title: End-to-End Compliance Evidence Blueprint for Model Serving Incidents

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This blueprint defines a reproducible, auditable process for collecting, preserving, and delivering compliance evidence when a model-serving security incident (for example: data exposure, unauthorized inference access, or pipeline compromise) is suspected or confirmed. It ties together RBAC/auth telemetry, audit logs, data residency constraints, secure SDLC artifacts, incident response actions, and exception governance so that evidence can be produced quickly for investigations and regulators while minimizing attack surface and legal risk.

Scope and intent
----------------
- Scope: model-serving infra across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (VPC / on‑prem).
- Intent: provide a single reference for on-call, SRE, security, and compliance teams to preserve an evidentiary record that satisfies internal SLAs and common regulatory requirements (GDPR, SOC-type audits, and contractual data residency constraints).

Key objectives
--------------
1. Minimize time-to-preservation (target: evidence-preserved within 60 minutes of incident identification).
2. Ensure chain-of-custody metadata for all artifacts.
3. Respect data residency and retention policies during evidence handling.
4. Provide a defensible, repeatable packaging format for audit teams and regulators.
5. Define exception and risk-acceptance workflows for constrained environments.

Ownership and contact matrix
---------------------------
- Primary owner: Security Incident Response (security).
- Secondary owners: Eng-SRE (ops), Eng-Serving-Runtime (runtime artifacts), Legal (privacy/regulatory).
- Pager escalation: security-oncall -> incident commander -> CISO (per oncall rota).

Roles and responsibilities (short)
- Incident Responder: initiates preservation, documents chain-of-custody, and coordinates packaging.
- SRE: executes log/metric exports, snapshotting caches, and instance images if required.
- Runtime Engineer: extracts model artifacts, model hashes, and inference cache manifests.
- Legal & Privacy: validates cross-border steps and approves evidence exports where required.

Evidence taxonomy (what to collect)
----------------------------------
- Authentication & Authorization:
  - RBAC change logs (role grants/revocations) with timestamp and actor ID.
  - Token issuance/rotation events (service identity issuance, X.509 events).
- Audit logging:
  - API gateway request logs (request id, client id, route, timestamp, latency, response code).
  - Inference-level logs (minimal prompt/response metadata; NEVER include full customer plaintext prompts unless legal-approved).
  - System-level logs: kube-audit, kubelet, node syslog, cloud-control-plane events where available.
- Model & artifact metadata:
  - Model manifest (model id, version, SHA256 hash, quantization profile).
  - Container image digests and deployment manifests (k8s manifests, Helm values).
- State snapshots:
  - KV cache snapshot (only metadata and cache keys; raw cached customer data requires Legal signoff).
  - Process/thread dumps and core files (if crash is relevant).
- Network & storage traces:
  - Flow logs, VPC/Security Group ACLs at incident window, s3 access logs for relevant objects.
- Identity correlation artifacts:
  - Authentication traces linking user/service identity to requests (session ids, client certs, exchange traces).

Retention and residency rules (guidelines)
-----------------------------------------
- Default evidence retention: 2 years for audit copies, 90 days for hot evidence before cold archival.
- Data residency enforcement: evidence that includes customer data must remain in the originating region unless Legal provides an export authorization.
- Redaction: when evidence contains PII or customer-provided content, redact according to the Data Masking Standard (see related page).

Chain-of-custody manifest (required fields)
------------------------------------------
Each packaged evidence bundle MUST include a plain-text manifest with these top-level fields (one per line):
- incident_id: unique RFC4122 UUID assigned by incident commander
- collected_by: person or service (email)
- collection_time_utc: RFC3339 timestamp
- artifact_list: newline-separated list of artifact filenames included in the bundle
- origin_region: AWS/GCP/Azure region or "on-prem"
- legal_approval: boolean (true/false) and approver name if applicable
- handling_notes: free text field for special handling steps or redaction summary

Example manifest snippet (plain text)
-----------------------------------
incident_id: 2f7e1b9c-4b25-4b6b-9f1a-0a6f4e5c9a11
collected_by: sasha.patel@redwood.ai
collection_time_utc: 2026-12-08T18:42:12Z
artifact_list:
  - authz_roles_2026-12-08.log
  - api_gw_requests_2026-12-08.csv
  - model-manifest-v3.json
origin_region: eu-west-1
legal_approval: true (Priya Nair)
handling_notes: redacted user prompts per legal guidance; cache snapshot trimmed to keys only

Preservation runbook (step-by-step)
----------------------------------
1) Triage and scope: Incident Responder captures initial incident id and brief summary in the incident channel.
2) Preservation trigger: If the incident involves suspected data exposure, run the preservation playbook and mark evidence_hot = true.
3) Short-term snapshot (within 60 minutes):
   - SRE: export API gateway logs for incident window:
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN" "https://logs.redwood.internal/api/v1/export?from=2026-12-08T18:30:00Z&to=2026-12-08T19:00:00Z&app=api-gateway" > api_gw_requests.csv
   - Runtime: capture model manifest and container image digest:
     kubectl -n model-serving get deploy model-foo -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' > image_digest.txt
   - SRE: snapshot k8s events and kube-audit for affected namespace: kubectl get events -n model-serving --since=1h -o yaml > k8s-events.yaml
4) Secure packaging: write manifest, compress artifacts to encrypted archive (AES-256) and store in evidence bucket with restricted ACLs. Example:
   tar czf - api_gw_requests.csv model-manifest-v3.json k8s-events.yaml | gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 -o incident-2f7e1b9c-20261208.tgz.gpg
   gsutil cp incident-2f7e1b9c-20261208.tgz.gpg gs://evidence-prod/eu-west-1/incident-2f7e1b9c/
5) Notify Legal & Privacy for cross-border approval if evidence leaves region.
6) Handoff: update incident tracker with storage path, manifest digest (SHA256), and responsible custodian.

Packaging format and delivery
----------------------------
- Standard bundle naming: incident-<incident_id>-<region>-<YYYYMMDD>.tgz.gpg
- Include checksums: SHA256 manifest and artifact-level checksums.
- Only share decrypted content with Legal/Compliance or external auditors through recorded, access-controlled sessions (e.g., ephemeral session to a dedicated review VM).

Exception and risk-acceptance flow
--------------------------------
Situations may require deviation (for example, on-prem customers disallow remote snapshot export). Follow this flow:
1. Document exception request in the Exception Tracker with justification and risk assessment.
2. Engineer proposes mitigations (on-site retention, remote audit under supervision, data minimization).
3. Security + Legal review and approve/deny. Approval must include a timebound limit and required evidence handling steps.

Integration with secure SDLC and deployments
------------------------------------------
- CI/CD must emit immutable build artifacts and store image digests in the Artifact Registry (artifact->SHA mapping). This allows matching runtime images to source commits during an investigation.
- Pre-deployment: include a "forensics hook" in release templates that records the deployment manifest to the artifact registry with an immutable timestamp.
- Post-deployment testing: smoke tests must capture route-level access logs and synthetic requests that will help determine baseline behavior when investigating anomalies.

Audit and verification (what auditors will look for)
-------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Evidence completeness and timestamps for the incident window.
- Chain-of-custody and manifest integrity (checksums match).
- Residency compliance (evidence did not cross restricted boundaries without approval).
- RBAC changes correlating to the incident (who granted what, when).

Checklist for release with evidence considerations
------------------------------------------------
- Build artifact stored with checksum: yes/no
- RBAC change docs for the release: yes/no
- K8s manifests and Helm values archived: yes/no
- Canary traffic logs available for the release window: yes/no
- Evidence hooks validated in CI: yes/no

Example forensic queries (search patterns)
----------------------------------------
- Locate all requests tied to a principal in a 15-minute window (Elasticsearch):
  GET /_search?q=client_id:svc-account-123 AND @timestamp:[2026-12-08T18:30:00Z TO 2026-12-08T18:45:00Z]&size=10000
- Find RBAC grant events for a user:
  SELECT * FROM authz_events WHERE event_type = 'role_grant' AND target_user = 'alice@acme.com' AND ts > '2026-12-01' ORDER BY ts DESC;

Privacy & redaction notes
------------------------
- Do not include plaintext customer inputs or direct model outputs unless specifically required and approved by Legal. When approved, redact per the Redaction Matrix and record the redaction rationale in handling_notes.
- When evidence includes PII, mark the bundle as "sensitive" and apply additional ACLs and retention limits.

Post-incident evidence lifecycle
-------------------------------
- Day 0–7: Hot evidence retained with restricted access for active investigation.
- Day 8–90: Cold storage in evidence-bucket with logged, but limited, access.
- >90 days: Archive to long-term immutable store (WORM) if required by regulator; otherwise schedule secure deletion per retention schedule.

Training and drills
------------------
- Conduct an annual evidence preservation drill (game-day) that includes cross-team coordination: SRE, Runtime, Security, Legal.
- Maintain a one-page quick reference at /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/evidence-quick-reference for oncall responders.

Appendix A — Quick export commands (examples)
-------------------------------------------
- Export S3 object list for prefix and copy to evidence bucket (awscli):
  aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket customer-logs --prefix "prod/model-foo/2026-12-08/" --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,LastModified:LastModified}' > s3-list.json
  aws s3 cp s3://customer-logs/prod/model-foo/2026-12-08/api.log .
- Create encrypted archive locally and upload:
  tar czf - api_gw_requests.csv model-manifest-v3.json | gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 -o /tmp/incident.tgz.gpg
  aws s3 cp /tmp/incident.tgz.gpg s3://evidence-prod/eu-west-1/incident-2f7e1b9c/

Appendix B — Minimal artifact naming conventions
-----------------------------------------------
- <service>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>.<ext> (e.g., api-gw-requests-20261208-184212.csv)

Related policies and links
-------------------------
- Data Masking Standard (link to internal doc)
- Evidence Retention Policy (link to internal doc)
- RBAC Change Control SOP (link to internal doc)

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-11-08: Drafted initial blueprint (Sasha Patel).
- 2026-12-12: Added KV cache handling guidance and manifest template (reviewers: Priya Nair).
- 2027-01-12: Finalized packaging & cross-border approval flow; published.
