payload.page_title: End-to-End Evidence & Containment Playbook for Cross-Region Inference Incidents

sections.body: This playbook defines the operational steps, evidence requirements, and containment actions for inference-related security incidents that span multiple geographic regions or data jurisdictions ("cross-region inference incidents"). It maps RBAC/auth checks, audit logging retrieval, data residency considerations, secure SDLC artifacts, and compliance evidence packaging into a single end-to-end procedure.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Purpose: Enable fast, defensible incident response and compliance evidence assembly when model-serving or inference requests trigger security concerns across region boundaries.
- Scope: Applies to incidents involving Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) deployments where requests, data, or logs cross jurisdictional boundaries.
- Not in scope: Customer-managed on-prem systems not connected to Redwood telemetry collection (see owner_team escalation).
sections.heading: Purpose and scope

sections.body:
| Role | Team | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Incident Commander (IC) | eng-sre / security (rotating) | Triage ownership, external comms, regulatory notification decisioning |
| Evidence Custodian | security | Assemble packaged evidence, sign-off for retention & export |
| Runtime Lead | eng-serving-runtime | Collect runtime traces, model variant mappings, KV-cache snapshots |
| Audit Logging Lead | eng-infra | Retrieve immutable audit streams and sign timestamps |
| Legal & Compliance | finance-legal | Regulatory notification, data residency approvals, privileged exception review |
| Customer Success | customer-success | Customer comms (if customer visible) and contractual obligations |
sections.heading: Stakeholders and ownership

sections.body:
1) Sev1: Active exfiltration or unauthorized cross-border data access confirmed. Immediate regulator/DAO notification potential.
2) Sev2: Unauthorized inference outputs (PII leakage) suspected but scope unknown.
3) Sev3: Non-customer-impacting auth misconfiguration discovered in routing/policy.
sections.heading: Incident severity classification (quick reference)

sections.body:
1. IC announces incident channel (secure Slack + incident document).
2. Snapshot RBAC state: export relevant policy bindings via internal tool (command example below).
   - Command: redwood-auth export-bindings --scope "<tenant|org|service>" --output /tmp/bindings-$(date +%s).json
3. Lock down privileged paths: perform just-in-time disable on implicated service accounts.
   - Command: iamctl disable --service-account <id> --reason "incident-<id>"
4. Preserve raw audit stream: ask Audit Logging Lead to seal and snapshot the region-specific Kafka topic and immutable object store.

Evidence collection matrix (required for regulatory and audit packages):
- RBAC & Auth artifacts:
  - Current and historical role bindings (exported JSON) for the affected tenant/org/service (retain 2x incident window).
  - Access tokens and token-issuance logs (issue/refresh/rotation events) from authn service.
  - Privilege elevation events (JITA activations) with who/when/for-what.
- Audit logging artifacts:
  - Immutable audit blob range covering T0 - T+48h (UTC). Include structured events (request_id, principal_id, route, model_version, response_size, geoip).
  - Raw transport logs (ingress/egress, LB traces) and service-level traces (span traces) correlated by request_id.
- Data residency and storage artifacts:
  - Storage bucket/object manifests showing residency region tags and object creation timestamps.
  - KMS envelope logs showing key usage and region-bound KMS operations.
- Secure SDLC artifacts (if suspected code/packaging issue):
  - Signed build manifest, container digest, image provenance (SBOM), and CI/CD pipeline run ids for the deployed model-serving revision.
- Incident-specific snapshots:
  - KV cache head snapshots (if model cache reuse may have caused data bleed).
  - Batcher policy state and active batching windows.

Evidence packaging standard (what to deliver to regulators/auditors):
1. Evidence manifest (JSON list) with SHA256 checksums for each artifact and canonical timestamps.
2. Readme describing provenance and chain-of-custody for each artifact.
3. Redacted sample of affected inference requests (PII redaction applied at source) plus algorithm used for redaction.
4. Signed attestation from Evidence Custodian.
sections.heading: Triage checklist (first 30 minutes)

sections.body:
| Artifact type | Minimum retention (internal) | Export allowed? | Storage location | Export notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Audit event blobs | 7 years | Yes (case-by-case, legal sign-off) | immutable-archive/region/{r} | Exports must include signature and manifest |
| RBAC bindings snapshot | 3 years | Yes (redacted) | auth-evidence-store | Must include admin approval |
| Token issuance logs | 1 year | No (sensitive) | secure-log-vault | Export prohibited without court order |
| Build manifests/SBOM | 5 years | Yes | sdlc-provenance-store | Include CI job ids and commit SHAs |
| KV-cache snapshots | 90 days | No (contains potential customer data) | ephemeral-forensics | Only accessible to security + legal w/ approval |
sections.heading: Retention and export rules (table)

sections.body:
- Export recent audit events for request_id X from ES cluster:
  curl -s -u readonly:$(cat /etc/audit/es-readonly-token) "https://es.internal/_search?q=request_id:REQUEST_ID&size=10000" > /tmp/audit-REQUEST_ID.ndjson

- Seal and snapshot Kafka topic (audit-topic-REGION-A) to immutable store:
  kafka-dump --topic audit-topic-REGION-A --from-offset <start> --to-offset <end> --out /tmp/audit-REGION-A-$(date +%s).ndjson
  objectstore put --bucket immutable-archive-region-a /tmp/audit-REGION-A-$(date +%s).ndjson --tag sealed-by=incident-<id>

- Example auth export (RBAC):
  redwood-auth export-bindings --scope tenant:acme-corp --since 2024-11-10T00:00:00Z --output /tmp/acme-bindings.json
sections.heading: Key operational commands and examples (for responders)

sections.body:
- If evidence shows active cross-border data flow with unauthorized principal: immediate partial shutdown of cross-region routing for affected model and region-level failover to region-local variant.
- If only misconfiguration with no confirmed data leakage: apply corrective policy patch (policy id) and schedule a canary verification before re-enabling routing.
- Always prefer region-local fallback when available; document the reason and timestamp.
sections.heading: Containment and fallback policy (decision matrix)

sections.body:
- All artifacts moved to the evidence store must be hashed with SHA256 and timestamped with the internal timestamping service (ts.sign). The Evidence Custodian adds a signed manifest:

  # Example manifest entry (line format)
  sha256:af3b... | audit-REGION-A-1672531200.ndjson | sealed-by:incident-2024-123 | ts:2024-11-15T13:04:00Z
sections.heading: Forensic integrity and cryptographic stamping

sections.body:
- Confidential data confirmed exfiltrated outside authorized jurisdictions: notify Legal within 2 hours and regulators (per region) within 72 hours if required by local law.
- PII exposure limited to <10 users (customer visible): IC to consult Legal; consider deferred notification pending scope confirmation but no later than 48 hours.
sections.heading: Regulatory notification thresholds and timelines

sections.body:
1. If evidence cannot be exported due to data residency policies, Legal must issue an exception request by completing the Exception Request Template and escalate to the cross-functional board within 24 hours.
2. Exception approval requires at minimum: security sign-off, runtime lead mitigation plan, and compliance/legal sign-off (emails archived).
3. All approved exceptions must be logged into the Authorization Exception Register (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/exception-register).
sections.heading: Exception handling and risk acceptance

sections.body:
- 72-hour: Evidence package finalized and handed to Legal; regulatory notification goes out if required. Conduct an initial root-cause hypothesis and short blameless rundown.
- 30-day: Formal Post-Incident Review (PIR) with engineering, security, legal and customer-success. Deliverables: RCA, remediation backlog, policy changes, test-case additions to eval harness, and a compliance evidence audit confirming retention rules were followed.
sections.heading: Post-incident activities (72-hour and 30-day)

sections.body:
- Enforce signed image and SBOM verification at deploy time for the runtime and model-serving artifacts.
- Require staged regional config tests that assert no cross-region data flows in canary mode.
- Add unit/regression tests that assert policy bindings for routing and tenant isolation.
sections.heading: SDLC and prevention controls (recommended)

sections.body:
- Evidence manifest template (JSON sample).
- Exception request template (DOC).
- Sample redaction script (Python) used when preparing PII-sanitized samples.

Appendix A — Quick reference scrubbing example (Python pseudocode):
  def redact_user_text(payload):
      # naive example - run through production redactor with policy id
      return re.sub(r"\b\d{9,}\b", "[REDACTED]", payload)

Appendix B — Contact list (oncall rotation):
1. Security oncall: +1-555-0101 (Slack: #security-oncall)
2. Eng SRE oncall: +1-555-0102
3. Legal urgent: legal-urgent@redwood.ai
sections.heading: Templates and attachments (appendix)

sections.body:
- For permanent runbook templates and export forms see: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/evidence-orchestration-for-model-serving-governance-2026
- See build/SBOM retention policies: /confluence/security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/sdlc-data-residency-audit-artifacts-manifest-2026

sections.body:

- 2025-01-20: Added KV-cache snapshot guidance and retention rules (reviewers Marco, Lina)
- 2025-02-10: Clarified export rules for token logs; published version

End of document.

payload.page_title: Zero‑Trust Incident Evidence Handbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This handbook defines a single, auditable evidence workflow for security incidents in zero‑trust and multi‑tenant contexts. It ties RBAC decisions, audit logs, data residency restrictions, and SDLC controls to a reproducible incident response procedure so security, legal, and customers can independently validate remediation and regulatory artifacts.

Scope
- Applies to incidents that impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability of tenant data or control plane services.
- Covers evidence collection, packaging, retention mapping, access controls for evidence, and sign‑off cadence.
- Not intended for routine operational alerts (handled by oncall runbooks) unless they escalate to an incident.

Audience
Security engineers, incident commanders, SRE oncall, legal/compliance leads, support escalation engineers, and platform product managers.

Key Principles
- Least privilege: evidence access follows RBAC and JIT privilege activation; no broad evidence buckets.
- Immutable sources: use append‑only audit exports and content hashing for chain‑of‑custody.
- Region‑aware packaging: evidence containing PII or regionally regulated telemetry must follow data residency rules when exported.
- Reproducibility: every artifact contains the query, time window, and tool version used to create it.

Owner & Critical Services
- Incident owner: Security Incident Response (SIR) team. Primary contact: Elena Martinez (Security PM).
- Critical services in scope: auth-api (internal), audit-streamer, telemetry-ingest, kv-cache, model-serving-proxy.
- Evidence store: secure-evidence-bucket (S3, KMS encrypted), immutable-audit-store (time-series archive), forensics-host (air‑gapped VM snapshots).

Roles & Responsibilities (table)
- Responders and signers:
| Role | Team | Responsibility | Escalation threshold |
| Incident Commander (IC) | security | Coordinates response, approves evidence release | Sev2 or above |
| Forensic Lead | security | Runs audit queries, exports chain-of-custody | Any suspected data exfil |
| SRE Liaison | eng-sre | Collects system snapshots, CPU/memory traces | Service-level degradation > 10% |
| Legal/Compliance | finance-legal | Advises on disclosure and retention | Data subject request or regulator notice |
| Customer Success | customer-success | Coordinates outbound comms if customer impacted | Confirmed tenant data exposure |

Minimum SLOs for Evidence Package
- Time to initial evidence snapshot: 60 minutes from incident declaration.
- Proof of collection: SHA256 hash and signed manifest within 90 minutes.
- Evidence access provisioning: 15 minutes for JIT approvals for named reviewers.

Incident Evidence Workflow (step-by-step)
1) Incident declaration
   - IC creates the incident ticket and tags it with data sensitivity: {none, low, high, regulated}.
   - If regulated, immediately notify Legal and set package-residency flag.
2) Lockdown & preserve ephemeral state
   - SRE runs snapshot commands and captures process lists, network state, and container IDs. Example CLI snippet:
     - ssh forensics@forensics-host -- sudo ./capture_snapshot.sh --incident $INCIDENT_ID --services "auth-api,audit-streamer"
3) RBAC evidence collection
   - Export role changes and sign-in events for the 72h window prior to incident:
     - audit-query: SELECT * FROM auth_events WHERE (event_type IN ('role_grant','role_revoke','login')) AND ts BETWEEN $T0 AND $T1;
   - Include policy versions and role‑assignment manifests.
4) Audit log extraction
   - Pull immutable-audit-store segments covering the incident window and associated trace IDs.
   - Preserve both raw message stream (gzipped) and a parsed summary (CSV) used for triage.
5) Data residency filter
   - If package-residency=EU, copy artifacts only to eu-evidence-bucket (replication disabled) and log the transfer with KMS key id.
6) Secure packaging & manifest
   - Create manifest.json (required fields: incident_id, created_by, tool_versions, time_window, sha256 list). Example manifest line: {"path":"/evidence/2026-02-02/auth-events-1.gz","sha256":"...","size":"12345"}
   - Sign manifest with k8s-signing-key: kubectl exec signer -- /opt/sign-manifest --manifest manifest.json --key-id evidence-signing-v1
7) Chain-of-custody recording
   - Append manifest entry to chain-of-custody ledger in immutable-audit-store with signature and timestamp.
8) Evidence access control
   - Create a temporary RBAC grant for reviewer group: evidence-reviewers.$INCIDENT_ID with expiry 48 hours. Use JIT activation and require MFA.
9) Review, redact, and release
   - Legal performs PII review and indicates fields requiring redaction. For regulated incidents, an independent auditor must sign off before external disclosure.
10) Archive & retention declaration
   - Archive final package to long-term store with retention labels: retention=incident-class-X (see retention table below).

Evidence Packaging Checklist (required)
- [x] manifest.json signed (signature and public key id)
- [x] audit-store segment (raw) with sha256
- [x] parsed CSV of key events used in investigation
- [x] RBAC dump (policy versions + diffs)
- [x] System snapshot (sha256) and list of hostnames
- [x] Chain-of-custody ledger entry id
- [x] Redaction map (if any) and redaction justification
- [x] Evidence access list and expiry timestamps

Retention Mapping (table)
- retention rules are applied at packaging time and encoded into object metadata.
| Incident class | Retention label | Minimum retention | Access review cadence |
| PII exposure - regulated | incident-class-H | 7 years (or regulator-required) | annual |
| PII exposure - non-regulated | incident-class-M | 3 years | biennial |
| No customer data | incident-class-L | 12 months | biennial |

RBAC & JIT Controls
- Evidence store policy: only evidence-service principal and signer role can write to secure-evidence-bucket.
- Reviewer access is provisioned via evidence-reviewers.$INCIDENT_ID temporary group and enforced by attribute-based conditions: requester.department in {security,legal,compliance} AND request.context.mfa = true.
- JIT activation flow: request -> manager approval (within 15 min) -> IAM issues short token (TTL 48h) -> IAM logs activation to audit-streamer.

Audit Logging & Queries (examples)
- Immutable audit export command (internal tool):
  ./audit-export --service auth-api --from $T0 --to $T1 --format gz --out /tmp/$INCIDENT_ID/auth-audit.gz
- Example quick triage query (SQL on parsed CSV index):
  SELECT user_id, action, ip, ts FROM parsed_audit WHERE trace_id = 'TRACE-1234' ORDER BY ts ASC LIMIT 500;
- Key thresholds to surface in evidence package:
  - Unsuccessful login rate spike: > 5x baseline over 10 minutes
  - Role grant anomalies: any grant where source != automation-bot AND approver IS NULL

Secure SDLC Evidence Linkages
- If the incident traces to a code change, include the following with the package:
  - PR id and merge commit hash
  - Build artifact digest and provenance (CI job id, runner id, environment variables snapshot)
  - Feature flag state during deployment and rollout percentage
- Required attestation: release owner must attest to canary metrics and rollback actions in the incident ticket.

Risk & Exceptions Process
- Risk classification: every incident is assigned a risk score (0–100) by the IC using the scoring rubric attached. High risk (score >= 70) requires board notification and an external auditor engagement.
- Exceptions and evidence withholding:
  - Temporary exceptions to residency can be approved by Legal + CISO only, with compensating controls documented and evidence labeled: "exception-approved-$ID".
  - All exceptions are timeboxed and must include a mitigation roadmap.

Communication & Disclosure
- Internal communication lanes: #incidents (ops), #sec-briefing (security), private channel with Legal.
- Customer notification triggers: confirmed tenant data exposure OR SLA-blind impact. Draft notice template is appended to every incident package and must include the manifest id and access url.

Forensics & Long‑term Validation
- Periodic revalidation: archived packages with incident-class-H are rehashed and validated annually; mismatches trigger re‑ingestion.
- Independent audit: for regulated incidents, we keep an auditor read-only snapshot for 3 years and log every auditor access event in immutable-audit-store.

Appendix A — Incident Scoring Rubric (summary)
- Confidentiality impact: 0–40 points (based on data types exposed)
- Availability impact: 0–30 points (user-facing outages)
- Integrity impact: 0–20 points (model or config tampering)
- Likelihood/velocity: 0–10 points (attack automation, exploitation speed)

Appendix B — Example manifest.json (trimmed)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0142",
  "created_by": "elena.martinez",
  "time_window": "2026-02-02T02:14:00Z/2026-02-02T03:01:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    {"path": "/evidence/INC-2026-0142/auth-audit-1.gz", "sha256": "abc123...", "size": "1,024,000"}
  ],
  "signed_by": "evidence-signing-v1",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ..."
}

Related pages & References
- Security runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-triage
- RBAC policy guide: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/least-privilege-guidelines
- Immutable audit architecture: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/immutable-audit-store-design

Revision history
- 2025-11-18: initial draft (Elena Martinez)
- 2025-12-10: add JIT flow details and retention table (Kofi Mensah)
- 2026-02-02: legal redaction workflow and manifest schema updates (Priya Raman)

Contact
Security Incident Response: sir@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: On‑Call Authorization & Evidence Orchestration Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines on‑call responsibilities, evidence collection sequencing, RBAC containment actions, audit logging queries, and data‑residency considerations for security incidents that require authorization forensics or cross‑region evidence packaging. It is intended for Security on‑call, SRE on‑call, Incident Commanders (ICs), and Legal/Evidence liaisons.

Goals
- Ensure chain‑of‑custody for authorization and access artifacts is preserved for regulatory and legal review.
- Minimize blast radius via rapid RBAC containment patterns.
- Produce audit/evidence bundles that meet internal and external compliance requirements within 24 hours of escalation.

Scope
- Applies to incidents affecting: authn/authz services (authz-service, idp-proxy, token-issuer), service accounts, privileged console access, cross‑tenant model serving requests, and audit pipeline integrity.
- Includes multi‑region evidence handling and data residency constraints for regulated customers.
- Excludes routine access reviews and non‑security change requests.

Ownership and Roles
- Security On‑Call: primary evidence collection, RBAC containment decisions, initial artifact packaging.
- SRE On‑Call: assist with log retrieval (audit-ingest), snapshot VMs or storage, rotate service credentials as directed.
- Incident Commander (IC): authorizes escalations, liaises with Legal/Compliance.
- Legal/Evidence Liaison: validates packaging, issues legal hold requests.
- Customer Success/Account Owner: informed for customer‑impacting retention or residency actions.

Key Services and Artifacts
- authz-service (Kubernetes deployment `authz-prod`): authorization decision logs (decision_id, principal, resource, action, verdict, reason).
- idp-proxy (OIDC fronting service): token issuance records and jwk rotation events.
- audit-ingest (Kafka → ES pipeline): raw event stream name `audit_events_v1`, retention per region.
- evidence-bucket (S3/GCS): immutable evidence archives with kms encryption and locked retention policy.

SLOs and Timelines
- T0 (detection): 0–30 minutes — on‑call acknowledges and begins containment.
- T1 (initial evidence snapshot): within 2 hours — collection of volatile artifacts and audit index ranges.
- T2 (evidence bundle): within 24 hours — packaged, checksummed, and submitted to legal/evidence store.
- T3 (signed chain of custody): within 48 hours — legal holds and provenance assertions completed.

Immediate Containment Checklist (first 30 minutes)
1. Confirm scope and affected principals (users, service accounts, keys).
2. If active exploit suspected: temporarily disable affected identity bindings, enable timebound deny rule for resource(s).
3. If risk to production: apply read‑only or deny policy to model inference routes and admin consoles.
4. Record actions in incident timeline and create evidence marker event (see Audit Query snippet).

Step‑by‑Step Evidence Orchestration (detailed procedure)
1) Triage and Tagging
- Tag incident in PagerDuty with label `authz-forensics` and severity (P0/P1).
- Create incident Jira (or internal ticket) with evidence checklist reference.

2) Volatile Snapshot (SRE + Security) — within 2 hours
- Collect process list and kernel logs on affected nodes:`sudo journalctl -u authz-service --no-pager -o short-iso > /tmp/authz-journal.log`
- Export in‑memory key information if safe: token caches, KV cache pointers (dump KV with `redis-cli --rdb` into evidence-bucket/volatile/).
- Take filesystem and container snapshots (use `crictl` or `docker` snapshot) and store checksums in evidence manifest.

3) Audit Log Range Capture (Security)
- Identify timeline (Tstart, Tend) from detection markers and collect the audit index range from `audit-ingest` (Elasticsearch) for `audit_events_v1`.
- Example ES query (replace placeholders):
{
  "query": {
    "bool": {
      "filter": [
        { "term": { "event_source": "authz-service" }},
        { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "2025-09-30T10:00:00Z", "lte": "2025-09-30T10:45:00Z" }}}
      ]
    }
  },
  "sort": [{"@timestamp": {"order": "asc"}}]
}
- Export results as ndjson and store in evidence-bucket/audit-exports/ with SHA256 checksum.

4) RBAC State Snapshot (Security)
- Export current role bindings and policy documents for the affected tenant(s):
  - For Kubernetes: `kubectl get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings -o yaml --all-namespaces`
  - For IAM (cloud): use Cloud CLI to export iam policy JSON for project/account and write to evidence-bucket/rbac-state/
- Mark any recently changed bindings (last 24–72 hours) and include change request IDs where available.

5) Data Residency and Cross‑Border Considerations
- If evidence includes customer data, consult the Data Residency Matrix (table below) before transferring evidence across regions.
- If evidence must remain in a jurisdiction (e.g., EU), copy artifacts to regional evidence-bucket EU endpoint and set access limitations to Legal+Security only.

Data Residency Matrix (excerpt)
| Artifact type | Preferred storage location | Retention baseline | Access group |
|---------------|----------------------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Token issuance logs | Origin region evidence-bucket (e.g., eu-west-1) | 2 years | Security, Legal |
| Audit ndjson export | Origin region; mirror allowed with approval | 7 years | Security, SRE |
| Volatile VM snapshot | Region of host; do not move across borders | 90 days | SRE, Security |

6) Evidence Packaging and Hashing
- Create manifest file `evidence-manifest.json` containing: artifact list, SHA256 checksums, origin region, collected_by, timestamps.
- Example manifest fields (must be present): `artifact_id`, `path`, `sha256`, `collected_at`, `collector`, `retention_policy_id`.
- Sign manifest using the incident on‑call GPG key and upload (manifest.sig) alongside bundle.

7) Legal Hold and Chain of Custody
- IC requests legal hold by emailing Legal/Evidence Liaison with incident ID and manifest.
- Legal replies with hold ID and required retention window. Attach hold metadata to evidence-bucket object ACL and record in evidence registry.

8) Evidence Delivery and Audit Trails
- For internal audit: deliver signed bundle URL + manifest to Compliance Tracker.
- For external regulators or customers: coordinate with Legal to issue credentialed access (temporary one‑time presigned URL) and audit the access via `audit-ingest` logs.

Escalation and Delegation Matrix
- If evidence contains PII or regulated customer data -> escalate to Legal within 60 minutes.
- If IAM compromise detected -> escalate to Security Lead and revoke affected roles immediately.
- For cross‑region legal conflicts (customer requests data residency) -> escalate to VP Security and Head of Legal.

RBAC Containment Patterns (recommended, reversible)
- Timebound deny: attach temporary deny policy with explicit expiry (e.g., 1 hour) rather than permanent removal.
- Scoped lock: reduce role to `read-only` for affected services using `role-binding patch` and log the action.
- Service account rotation: issue new key pair and rotate consumers via canary path; do not delete old keys until audit export confirmed.

Audit Logging and Provenance Checks
- Always create a marker event immediately after containment action:
  - Event fields: {"event_type":"incident_marker","incident_id": "INC-12345","action":"rbac_containment","actor":"oncall:ap", "timestamp":"..."}
- Verify that the marker is present in the ES index and that the ingest pipeline preserved original timestamps.
- If audit-ingest is compromised, fall back to node level logs and network captures; note divergence in manifest.

Artifact Retention and Deletion Rules
- Default retention: audit ndjson — 7 years; token issuance logs — 2 years; volatile snapshots — 90 days.
- For legal holds, retention overrides baseline and must be honored until release. Record release approval in evidence manifest.

Evidence Submission Checklist (required for closure)
- [ ] Manifest present and signed
- [ ] All artifacts checksummed and uploaded to evidence-bucket
- [ ] Legal Hold ID recorded (if applicable)
- [ ] Chain of custody email thread archived in ticket
- [ ] Access audit log showing only authorized viewers
- [ ] Retention policy ID annotated in manifest

Post‑Incident Actions
- Root cause analysis with model serving, authz, and SRE teams within 72 hours.
- Update RBAC guardrails and automated denial runbooks if applicable.
- Schedule focused canary rollouts to validate rotated credentials.
- Add synthetic audit markers to validate ingest pipeline replay integrity.

Appendices
A. Example evidence-manifest.json (minimal)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2025-0912-01",
  "collected_by": "aisha.patel",
  "artifacts": [
    {"artifact_id":"authz_journal","path":"evidence-bucket/volatile/authz-journal.log","sha256":"<sha256>"},
    {"artifact_id":"audit_export","path":"evidence-bucket/audit-exports/authz-2025-09-30.ndjson","sha256":"<sha256>"}
  ]
}

B. Quick Audit Query Examples
- Marker search (ES): `GET /_search?q=event_type:incident_marker AND incident_id:INC-2025-0912-01`
- Access actor range: `GET /_search` with filter `actor.principal:"service-account:ingest-writer"` and time range.

C. Frequently asked operational questions
Q: Who can approve cross-region evidence movement?
A: VP Security and Head of Legal must sign off; record approval in incident ticket.

Q: What if audit-ingest is unavailable?
A: Use node level logs and network packet captures; note in manifest and escalate to SRE.

Document Change Log
- 2025-03-12: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft).
- 2025-06-01: Added Data Residency Matrix and SLOs (review: Marcus Chen).
- 2025-09-30: Clarified RBAC containment patterns and added manifest signing requirement (review: Lina Gómez).

Related Policies and References
- Event schema contract: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025
- RBAC automation playbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provisioning-and-evidence-automation-2026
- Evidence registry: internal tool `evidence-registry.redwood.local`

If you are on‑call and uncertain about any step, page the Security Lead and Legal immediately. Preserve all timestamps and never overwrite original artifacts.

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the detection, containment, evidence collection, legal-hold procedures, and post-incident validation steps for a confirmed or suspected compromise of privileged cryptographic keys (KMS/master keys, HSM-wrapped keys, or long-lived service credentials) that are used in Redwood Dedicated deployments. It covers tenant isolation and cross-region evidence preservation requirements, and provides concrete CLI/SQL/query examples for collecting admissible forensic artifacts.

Intended audience
------------------
- Security on-call (SecOps) and Forensics engineers
- Dedicated deployment SRE/Support leads
- Legal (incident counsel) and Compliance owners
- Product security and Platform engineering liaisons

Scope and assumptions
---------------------
- Applies to compromised keys used by Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers, and keys used by private control planes associated with Dedicated clusters.
- Includes KMS keys (cloud-managed), HSM-managed key material, and long-lived signing keys (e.g., model-signing, deployment-signing).
- Does NOT replace tenant-specific legal obligations; when a customer requests additional controls, follow customer contract terms and involve Legal.

Priority decision matrix
------------------------
1. Confirmed compromise of a customer-facing key (high): immediate containment and legal hold.
2. Suspected compromise of internal service key (medium): rapid containment and evidence snapshotting.
3. Compromise limited to ephemeral test key (low): local revocation and root-cause analysis.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Incident commander (IC): SecOps on-call (primary) -> contact via #secops-oncall and pager
- Forensics lead: Platform forensics team (evan.zhao@redwood.ai)
- Dedicated SRE contact: Dedicated oncall rotation (dedicated-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Legal counsel (incident): Incident legal rotation; escalate via PagerDuty if PII/regulated data involved

Detection and initial triage (0-30 minutes)
-----------------------------------------
1. Triage signals:
   - Cloud KMS alerts (suspicious key usage outside normal time/region).
   - Unexpected schedule-key-deletion or key-disable API calls.
   - Alert from deployment telemetry: sudden token invalidations, deployment failures citing signing mismatch.
   - Multiple failed signing attempts or JWTs signed by unknown key id.
2. Quick checks (commands):
   - AWS (CloudTrail event lookup):
     aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=<key-id> --start-time "2028-01-11T00:00:00Z" --end-time "2028-01-11T23:59:59Z"

   - GCP (Cloud Audit Logs via gcloud):
     gcloud logging read "protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta" --freshness=1d --limit=200 --format=json | jq '.[] | select(.resourceName|test("<key-name>"))'

   - Snapshot KMS key metadata (AWS example):
     aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key-arn>
     aws kms describe-key --key-id <key-arn> --output json > /tmp/evidence/key-desc-<key-id>.json

3. Initial containment decisions (within 30 min):
   - If key is actively used for signing customer requests, consider immediate key disable/schedule-delete and failover to a rotated key.
   - If disablement would cause customer outage, follow controlled failover: rotate signing endpoints to a pre-provisioned standby key and throttle traffic.

Containment and mitigation (30-120 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Short-term containment options (choose with Legal):
   - Disable key (cloud KMS):
     aws kms disable-key --key-id <key-arn>
   - Schedule deletion (if irrevocable compromise confirmed):
     aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id <key-arn> --pending-window-in-days 7
   - For HSM keys: place the HSM slot into maintenance mode and freeze network access; take HSM management console snapshots.

2. Tenant isolation checklist:
   - Identify affected tenants by correlating API key usage with KMS usage events.
   - Apply per-tenant network ACLs or security group ACLs if shared nodes are impacted.
   - If Dedicated pool is multi-tenant, evict/unbind non-matching tenants and failover their workloads to isolated capacity.

3. Communications (IC responsibility):
   - Notify Legal and Customer Success for affected customers within SLA window.
   - Post incident banner in status.redwood.ai if customer impact is >= partial outage.

Evidence collection and preservation (most-critical section)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Guiding principle: collect immutable copies and preserve provenance. Capture system state, audit logs, configuration, and cryptographic artifacts. Use timeline stamps and manifest to record chain-of-custody.

1. Evidence bundle structure (recommended naming):
   - evidence/<incident-id>/manifest.txt
   - evidence/<incident-id>/cloudtrail-raw.json.gz
   - evidence/<incident-id>/kms-describe-json.txt
   - evidence/<incident-id>/hsm-snapshots/*
   - evidence/<incident-id>/network-captures/*

2. Minimal artifact list (must capture all):
   - Raw audit log slices (CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs) for start_time-48h .. end_time+24h
   - KMS describe and policy documents (get-key-policy, key rotation status)
   - Access control changes (IAM role changes, STS assume-role events)
   - Service logs with signature failures or unexpected key-id headers
   - Running container images and /proc/cmdline for impacted hosts (if safe to snapshot)
   - Memory dump of signing process only when authorized by Legal and Forensics; capture using LiME/volatility guidance

3. Example evidence collection commands
   - CloudTrail (AWS):
     aws s3 cp "s3://cloudtrail-logs/<bucket>/account/<account-id>/" /tmp/evidence/cloudtrail-raw --recursive --exclude "*" --include "*<YYYY-MM-DD>*"

   - Export KMS key policy and aliases (AWS):
     aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-arn> --policy-name default > /tmp/evidence/key-policy-<key-id>.json
     aws kms list-aliases --key-id <key-arn> > /tmp/evidence/key-aliases-<key-id>.json

   - Export rotation and grants:
     aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key-arn> > /tmp/evidence/key-rotation-<key-id>.json
     aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-arn> > /tmp/evidence/key-grants-<key-id>.json

4. Audit log query examples (forensic-grade queries):
   - Identify cross-region access:
     SELECT eventTime, eventName, userIdentity, sourceIPAddress, awsRegion, requestParameters FROM cloudtrail_logs WHERE resource = '<key-arn>' AND eventTime BETWEEN '2028-01-09T00:00:00Z' AND '2028-01-11T23:59:59Z' ORDER BY eventTime DESC;

   - Find STS tokens created using the key:
     SELECT * FROM cloudtrail_logs WHERE eventName = 'AssumeRole' AND requestParameters LIKE '%<key-id>%';

Chain-of-custody and manifest requirements
-----------------------------------------
- Manifest must contain: incident id, collector name, collection timestamps (UTC), checksums (SHA256) for each artifact, storage location (S3 path), encryption method for preserved copies, and who authorized collection.
- Use stamped checksums: sha256sum artifact > artifact.sha256

Legal hold and retention rules (contract-driven)
-----------------------------------------------
- Immediately notify Legal for any key compromise involving customer data or keys attached to customer tenancy.
- Preserve originals for a minimum of 2 years for incidents involving regulated data, unless Legal instructs longer.
- Evidence copies must be stored in an immutable bucket with versioning and MFA delete enabled where available.

Special considerations for data residency and cross-border evidence
-----------------------------------------------------------------
- If evidence includes customer PII governed by residency clauses, consult Data Residency matrix and follow regional export rules before copying logs outside region. Mark artifacts with region tags in the manifest.
- If required, perform remote analysis in-region and ship only derived metadata out-of-region; record the reasoning in the manifest.

Forensics tooling and safe handling
----------------------------------
- Prefer read-only APIs and logging exports. Avoid running intrusive collection on production hosts unless forensics lead authorizes.
- Recommended tooling: AWS CLI, gcloud, jq, tshark (for network pcap), LiME (for memory capture), volatility for analysis, and a documented VM for forensic analysis (offline).

Restoration and system hardening (24-72 hours)
---------------------------------------------
1. Replace compromised key(s) across all consumers and rotate dependent skeleton keys.
2. Re-issue short-lived credentials and rotate any static tokens.
3. For Dedicated clusters, perform an image rebuild for signing services with new keys; ensure reproducible build artifacts with SBOM attached.
4. Introduce additional policy guards: restrict key usage to explicit principals, add region constraints, and require context-based conditions (e.g., source VPC).

Post-incident evidence pack and reporting (72 hours)
--------------------------------------------------
- Prepare an evidence pack for Legal and Compliance containing manifest, executive summary, timelines, root cause analysis, and mitigations applied.
- SLO for the report: initial executive summary within 48 hours; full technical report within 14 business days.

Metrics and detection improvements (closure)
-------------------------------------------
- Create/update detection rules for anomalous KMS usage patterns (international region jump, unusual principal).
- Add a nightly job to verify key policy drift for production keys and alert on policy diffs.
- Track post-incident metrics: mean time to contain (goal < 2 hours), evidence collection completeness (100% of required artifact set), and number of tenants affected.

Runbook appendix (cheat sheet)
-----------------------------
1. Snapshot key metadata (AWS):
   aws kms describe-key --key-id <key-arn> --output json > /tmp/evidence/key-desc.json
   aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-arn> --policy-name default > /tmp/evidence/key-policy.json

2. Disable key (if authorized):
   aws kms disable-key --key-id <key-arn>

3. Export CloudTrail slice (example):
   aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=<key-id> --start-time "2027-11-01T00:00:00Z" --end-time "2027-11-02T23:59:59Z" --output json > /tmp/evidence/cloudtrail-slice.json

4. Generate manifest entry (example):
   echo "artifact: cloudtrail-slice.json
sha256: $(sha256sum /tmp/evidence/cloudtrail-slice.json | awk '{print $1}')
collected_by: $(whoami)
collected_at: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> /tmp/evidence/manifest.txt

Related documents and references
-------------------------------
- Incident evidence coordination playbook (internal): /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-evidence-coordination-for-rbac-audit-and-retention-2026
- Service identity rotation guide: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/service-identity-rotation-and-evidence-playbook-2026
- Data residency decision matrix: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/data-sovereignty-decision-matrix-and-audit-evidence-playbook-2026

Notes and change log
---------------------

- 2027-12-15: Added cross-region evidence handling and manifest schema (review by Marisol Rivera).
- 2028-01-11: Legal hold wording clarified; added CLI examples and retention guidance (review by Liam O'Connor).

End of playbook

payload.page_title: Forensic Log Preservation and Legal Hold Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard operating procedure for preserving forensic logging artifacts and initiating a legal hold during a security incident that may have legal or regulatory implications. It covers: scope, responsibilities, technical collection steps, integrity verification, short- and long-term storage, RBAC controls during evidence handling, and coordination with Legal and Compliance.

Intended audience

- Incident responders (eng-sre, security ops)
- Platform engineers who own logging/export pipelines
- Legal and Compliance contacts handling preservation requests
- Engineering managers coordinating access and custody

Scope

Applies to all production and staging systems that generate audit logs, access logs, request traces, application-level telemetry, and associated artifacts that may be relevant to an incident. This includes:

- API gateway and request audit logs (redwood-gateway-audit)
- Serving runtime telemetry (runtime-metrics and kernel traces)
- Authentication and authorization logs (auth-service, IAM audit)
- Orchestration and scheduling logs (kube-audit, autoscaler events)
- Network flow captures and firewall logs (vpc-flow-logs)
- Customer-facing telemetry when subject to legal hold (consult Legal)

Definitions

- Forensic artifact: any file or record collected for the purpose of investigation or regulatory review.
- Legal hold: an instruction to preserve specific data from normal retention/deletion, initiated by Legal/Compliance.
- Collector: an authorized engineer or security operator who executes the collection steps.

Ownership and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): declares evidence collection, coordinates with Legal, approves access escalations.
- Security Ops: executes collection playbook, ensures integrity, performs initial triage.
- Platform Storage Owner: prepares secured preservation buckets and ensures encryption/KMS.
- IAM/RBAC Owner: applies temporary access changes and documents approvals (break-glass).
- Legal/Compliance: issues the legal hold, defines custodians, and provides retention directives.

Pre-requisites (before collection)

1. Confirm scope and list of systems from IC + Legal.
2. Identify owners and responsible engineers for each system.
3. Ensure a preservation S3 (or cloud equivalent) bucket exists: redwood-preserve-{incident-id} with encryption enabled and restricted ACLs.
4. Ensure an evidence KMS key is provisioned and access is limited to security and legal service principals.
5. Verify audit logging pipelines are writable (no disk pressure) and snapshot capability exists for long-term storage.

High-level collection timeline (SLOs)

- Initial collection (critical artifacts): target within 4 hours of incident declaration.
- Full snapshot of relevant clusters/services: target within 24 hours.
- Evidence integrity manifest produced and stored: within 48 hours.

Step-by-step collection playbook

1) Triage and scope confirmation
   - IC confirms incident ID and legal hold scope.
   - Security Ops creates the preservation bucket and a ticket in the incident tracker with the tag: evidence-preserve/{incident-id}.

2) Lock down retention and prevent automated deletion
   - For each candidate bucket or index, apply an immediate retention override: set lifecycle to "retain" or disable deletion APIs.
   - Example (AWS CLI):
     aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket my-audit-bucket --lifecycle-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ID":"preserve-incident-123","Status":"Enabled","AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload":{"DaysAfterInitiation":36500}}]}'

3) Collect primary artifacts (critical first)
   - API gateway audit (last 30 days and live tail):
     aws s3 cp s3://redwood-gateway-audit/2025/02/ --recursive s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/ingest/gateway-audit/ --profile preserve-role
\   - Kubernetes audit logs: generate a cluster snapshot with kube-audit-collector and compress:
     kubectl --context=prod get events --all-namespaces -o json > prod-cluster-events.json
     tar -czf prod-cluster-audit.tar.gz prod-cluster-events.json /var/log/kube-apiserver/audit.log

4) Capture ephemeral state and KV caches
   - Export model-serving KV caches if relevant (coordination with runtime team). Use runtime export tool: runtimectl export-cache --model-id m-123 --since 2025-01-01 --out cache-export.pb

5) Network-level artifacts
   - If packet captures are required, coordinate with network team:
     tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/incident-123.pcap 'host 10.20.30.0/24'
     gcloud compute scp compute-instance:/tmp/incident-123.pcap . && aws s3 cp incident-123.pcap s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/network/

6) Database and object storage snapshots
   - Request DB snapshot via platform owner. For Postgres: create a read-replica snapshot and export logical dumps:
     pg_dump --host=db-read.prod.redwood.internal --username=readonly --format=custom --file=prod-incident-123.dump --schema=public

Integrity verification and manifest

- For every collected artifact produce a SHA-256 hash and add a line to a manifest file: manifest-INC-2025-02.txt
  Example manifest line: sha256sum prod-cluster-audit.tar.gz  prod-cluster-audit.tar.gz

- Sign the manifest with the collector's GPG key (if available) or store signed approval in the incident ticket.
  gpg --detach-sign --armor manifest-INC-2025-02.txt

- Example manifest header:
  Incident: INC-2025-02
  Collector: asha.patel@redwood.com
  CollectedAt: 2025-02-18T14:23:00Z

Packaging and encryption

- All artifacts MUST be uploaded to the preservation bucket within a directory named by incident ID and collection phase (e.g. s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/phase-1/).
- Apply server-side encryption with evidence KMS key and enforce bucket policy to deny DeleteBucket and DeleteObject unless with break-glass approval.

- Example upload command:
  aws s3 cp prod-cluster-audit.tar.gz s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/phase-1/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01-2345

RBAC controls and emergency access (break-glass)

- Normal principle: least privilege. During preservation the following special rules apply:
  - Create a short-lived "evidence-access" role that grants: s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket for redwood-preserve-{incident-id}, kms:Decrypt on evidence KMS key, and readonly access to index/search artifacts.
  - Access request must include: IC approval, Legal approval, and a Security Manager signature in the incident ticket.
  - All role assumptions are logged and a 24/7 oncall approver is designated.

- Break-glass checklist: time, approver name, justification, artifacts accessed, TTL of credential (max 8 hours), and post-access audit notes.

Legal hold coordination

1. Legal issues hold directive with scope and custodians. Security Ops tags the incident ticket and adds the hold label: legal-hold/INC-2025-02.
2. Custodians are notified with the required actions and stop-delete instructions.
3. Security Ops schedules weekly retention confirmation with Legal until release.

Evidence handoff to Legal or external counsel

- Handoff package should include: artifact tarball(s), manifest (sha256 and signed), collection timeline, collector identities, RBAC/approval log, and storage location.
- Preferred handoff: provide access to the preservation bucket with a time-limited read-only role rather than transferring copies. If copies are transferred, document chain of custody and destroy copies only with Legal approval.

Chain-of-custody form (ASCII table template)

| Item ID | Artifact path | Collected by | Collected at (UTC) | Hash (sha256) | Current Holder | Notes |
|---------|----------------|--------------|---------------------|----------------|----------------|-------|
| 1 | s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/phase-1/prod-cluster-audit.tar.gz | asha.patel | 2025-02-18T14:23:00Z | abcd1234... | redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02 | initial collect |

Retention mapping and cross-region residency

- Legal/Compliance will specify retention periods (e.g., 7 years, 3 years, indefinite). Map retention requirements to storage classes and region restrictions:
  - Short-term (<=90 days): standard encrypted buckets in originating region.
  - Long-term (>90 days): move to dedicated preservation account with cross-region replication disabled if data residency prohibits replication.

- If the incident involves cross-border data, Legal will provide custody restrictions. Preservation buckets may be placed in-region only (e.g., eu-west-1) and access limited to EU-based engineers where required.

Secure SDLC tie-ins and post-incident actions

- Root cause findings that require code or infra changes MUST be triaged through our Secure SDLC process: open an RFC, perform a threat model update, and require change review with Security and SRE.
- Add verification suites to CI that assert: audit logging is enabled, log rotation retains at least N days, and alerting for missing streams is in place.

Evidence review and purge release

- Legal issues a release when the hold is lifted. Security Ops performs a release checklist: verify signed release, document final custody, and either remove retention locks or schedule normal lifecycle.

Audit logging configuration checklist (minimum)

- All services generate structured logs (JSON) with: timestamp, request_id, user_id, service, operation, source_ip, result_code.
- Centralized ingest to the audit pipeline with guaranteed delivery (SQS/Kafka backed) and monitoring on ingestion lag (>5m alerts).
- Retention policies defined per environment and override mechanism for legal hold.

Configuration snippet examples

- Minimal structured audit example (JSON line):
  {"ts":"2025-02-18T14:12:03Z","request_id":"r-7a2f","user":"service-account:ingest","svc":"gateway","op":"POST /v1/generate","src_ip":"198.51.100.23","result":200}

- Simple lifecycle rule example (AWS bucket):
  {
    "Rules": [
      {
        "ID": "preserve-INC-2025-02",
        "Status": "Enabled",
        "NoncurrentVersionExpiration": {"NoncurrentDays": 36500}
      }
    ]
  }

Post-collection audits and logging of access

- All access to preserved artifacts must be logged and reviewed weekly by Security and Legal. Any unauthorized access triggers an immediate re-evaluation of custody and potential re-collection.

Related pages and references

- Incident response playbook (link: confluence://eng-sre/incident-response-playbook)
- Audit logging standards (link: confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/standards)
- RBAC emergency escalation procedure (link: confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/emergency-escalation)

Appendix: common CLI commands and snippets

- Compute SHA-256: sha256sum artifact.tar.gz
- Upload with KMS: aws s3 cp artifact.tar.gz s3://redwood-preserve-INC-2025-02/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <evidence-key-arn>
- Generate signed manifest: gpg --detach-sign --armor manifest-INC-2025-02.txt

Approval and change history

- 2025-02-18: Drafted by Asha Patel (security).
- 2025-03-02: Reviewed by Marco Hernandez (security ops) and Liang Zhou (platform).
- 2026-01-12: Updated retention mapping and cross-region guidance after legal review.

Contact

Security ops oncall: security-oncall@redwood.com
Legal contact: legal-preserve@redwood.com

payload.page_title: Tenant Segmentation Incident: Evidence Handling & Forensic Guidance

sections.body:
Summary:

This page defines the operational runbook and evidence-handling guidance for incidents that impact tenant segmentation or authorization boundaries in Redwood Inference (hosted and dedicated modes). It ties together RBAC containment procedures, audit log capture, cross-region data residency considerations, secure-SDLC remediation requirements, and compliance evidence packaging for regulatory review. Intended audience: Security on-call, SRE, platform engineers, privacy/compliance, and legal.

Goals and scope:
- Contain and isolate affected tenant(s) within 30 minutes of detection for high-impact incidents (see "Severity rubric" below).
- Capture forensically-sound evidence from compute, network, and storage while preserving data residency constraints.
- Produce a packaged evidence artifact suitable for internal RCA and regulator audits within 72 hours.
- Ensure remediation steps are coordinated with release/control gates in the secure SDLC so fixes do not regress production controls.

Terminology:
- Tenant segmentation incident: any event where a tenant's data, requests, or metadata are accessible to another tenant or to unauthorized principals due to an authorization, routing, or configuration failure.
- Evidence artifact: a reproducible bundle of logs, KV snapshots, configurations, and attestations required for investigation and audit.

Severity rubric (examples):
1) Sev1 (Critical): confirmed cross-tenant data exposure (PII or customer-authenticated responses) or broad authorization bypass affecting >10 customers. SLA: contain within 30 min, notify legal and CRO.
2) Sev2 (High): suspected segmentation flaw with limited blast radius (1–10 customers) or authorization misconfiguration that may allow access, not yet confirmed. SLA: contain within 2 hours.
3) Sev3 (Medium): RBAC policy drift or audit-log gaps with no confirmed exposure. SLA: investigate within 24 hours and remediate in next sprint or hotfix depending on impact.

Immediate containment checklist (ordered, numbered):
1) Triage and declare incident severity. Owner: security-oncall. Use PagerDuty group: sec-oncall-tenant.
2) Apply immediate routing policy to redirect affected tenant traffic to safe-handling tier (redwood-routing CLI):
   - Example: redwood-routing set-policy --tenant-id t-012345 --policy isolate --duration 3h
3) Revoke short-lived credentials for affected tenants and for implicated service accounts. Commands:
   - aws sts revoke-sessions --user-id <id> (for AWS SSO: script in /infra-scripts/revoke-sessions.sh)
   - k8s: kubectl delete secret <secret-name> -n <tenant-namespace>
4) If running on Dedicated or Private deployments, escalate to customer infra contact per customer runbook and notify via secure channel (IdP group + encrypted email).

Forensic evidence capture (preservation-first principles):
- Preserve before edit. Never modify disk images, configuration files, or primary audit stores in-place unless required for containment; prefer copies.
- Tag each artifact with an immutable evidence ID and timestamp (UTC). Example format: EVID-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>-<short-hash>.

Required evidence items (minimum):
- Compute snapshot or process list covering the incident window (ps aux, container images list).
- Kernel and application logs: journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-02-10T10:00:00Z" > runtime.log
- Auth events and policy evaluations from the ABAC/RBAC engine (authz-audit service). Query example (internal logging):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_API_KEY" "https://log-api.internal/v1/search?q=tenant:t-012345 AND event:authz_eval&from=2026-02-10T09:50:00Z&to=2026-02-10T10:20:00Z" > authz-events.json
- KV cache snapshots (when applicable) with redaction markers if required by privacy policy. Use redwood-kvctl snapshot --tenant t-012345 --out kv-snapshot.tar.gz
- Network captures limited to headers where full packet capture would violate data residency/PII constraints; when full PCAP is required and allowed, capture using tcpdump -w and store in controlled evidence bucket.

Evidence packaging and metadata table (required fields):
| field | description | example |
| EVID_ID | Unique artifact id | EVID-20260210-authz-9f3a |
| SEVERITY | Declared severity | Sev1 |
| TENANTS | Affected tenants | t-012345, t-078901 |
| REGIONS | Regions where data origin/routing occurred | us-east-1, eu-west-1 |
| DATA_RESIDENCY | Residency constraints | EU_ONLY |
| ARTIFACTS | List of files included | runtime.log, authz-events.json, kv-snapshot.tar.gz |
| HASHES | SHA256 hashes for each artifact | sha256:... |

Storage, encryption, and retention controls for evidence artifacts:
- Evidence artifacts MUST be uploaded to the evidence S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence-prod. Use server-side encryption with KMS: --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-efg.
- For cross-border incidents, use a region-locked bucket mirroring strategy: write-only replication to s3://redwood-evidence-eu for EU-data, with explicit legal hold tag: "legal_hold=true".
- Retention policy applied: evidence-retention=7 years for Sev1, 2 years for Sev2, 6 months for Sev3. See retention config file example:

Retention policy JSON example:
{
  "evidenceBucket": "redwood-evidence-prod",
  "retentionBySeverity": {"Sev1": "2555d", "Sev2": "730d", "Sev3": "180d"},
  "kmsKey": "arn:aws:kms:..."
}

RBAC and auth telemetry required for investigation:
- authz-audit service: full policy evaluation logs and policy-version metadata.
- IAM entitlement change logs (user-provisioning, role-assignments) from entitlement-service.
- OAuth/OIDC token minting logs (token issuance and revocation).
- Admin console session recordings (redwood-admin-activity) limited to metadata per privacy rules.

Data residency and cross-border constraints:
- If the incident involves EU-only tenants (residency label present), evidence must remain in EU zone buckets and access must be granted only to staff with EU processing authorization. See label: residency:EU.
- For hybrid-residency customers, coordinate with Privacy & Legal before any artifact transfer outside permitted zones.

Chain-of-evidence steps (recommended):
1) Assign evidence custodian: security investigator (primary) and SRE (secondary).
2) Create evidence record in internal tracker: evidence-id, artifacts list, custodian, custody log.
3) Collect artifacts using read-only copies and compute SHA256 hashes.
4) Upload to evidence bucket with encryption and immutability flags (if supported).
5) Update custody log with date/time, operator, action, and destination URI.

Secure-SDLC integration and remediation gating:
- All code changes intended to remediate segmentation incidents must pass an elevated review: security-review required + automated policy tests for RBAC regression.
- Pull request checklist additions for remediation PRs:
  - unit/regression tests covering the RBAC policy paths
  - canary rollout plan with feature flag and fallback
  - performance backstop to ensure latency SLOs not violated (99th percentile token latency must remain within baseline + 30%).
- Release blocking criteria: failing evidence-preservation steps or incomplete audit captures are release-blocking until resolved.

Notifications and stakeholders (communication):
- Pager duty groups: sec-oncall-tenant, platform-oncall.
- Slack channels (restricted): #sec-tenant-incidents (read-only for non-stakeholders).
- Notification cadence: initial triage within 15 minutes for Sev1 to legal, C-level ops; hourly updates until containment.

Regulatory and compliance packaging (what to provide to auditors):
- Evidence manifest (CSV) with artifact URIs, hashes, custodian signatures, residency assertions, and legal hold tags.
- Signed preservation affidavit from custodian describing actions taken and timing. Template available as /templates/preservation-affidavit.md.
- Redacted sample of impacted request/response pairs with consistent redaction rules documented in /security/redaction-guidelines.md.

Operational templates and automation (location):
- Collection scripts: /infra-scripts/evidence-collector.sh (invoked with --evid-id).
- Custody tracker template: internal jira template 'EVID-TRACKER'.
- S3 lifecycle and replication manifests: terraform modules under infra/terraform/modules/evidence-buckets.

Post-incident review and risk/exceptions handling:
1) Within 7 days: post-incident review (owner: security manager) with attendees: SRE, product, legal, affected OEMs/customers as needed.
2) Document root cause, sequence-of-events, and permanent remediations in the RCA page.
3) If remediation requires an exception to existing controls (temporary entitlements, expanded cross-region access), file a risk-and-exceptions request using the template at /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/exception-request-template. The request must include compensating controls and an explicit expiration time.

Monitoring and regression detection after remediation:
- Add continuous evals to detect recurring policy overrides: daily authz-audit queries for anomalous policy evaluations.
- Include synthetic tests in the perf suite that simulate tenant boundary checks (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/tenant-isolation-tests).

Appendix A — Example commands and snippets:
- Export authz events: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_API_KEY" "https://log-api.internal/v1/stream?tenant=t-012345&service=authz-audit&from=2026-02-10T09:50:00Z" | jq . > authz-stream.ndjson
- Snapshot KV store (GCP datastore example): gcloud datastore export --kinds=redwood_kv --namespaces=t-012345 gs://temp-evidence/kv-export-20260210
- Evidence upload (AWS example): aws s3 cp authz-events.json s3://redwood-evidence-prod/evid/EVID-20260210-authz-9f3a/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-efg

Appendix B — Ownership and contact matrix:
- Security-oncall: PagerDuty sec-oncall-tenant, primary investigator.
- SRE: platform-oncall, assists with snapshots, network captures, and kube-level containment.
- Privacy & Legal: consult for residency, cross-border transfer, and regulatory notifications.
- Customer Success: coordinates customer communication for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-18: Initial draft (Marta Ruiz).
- 2026-01-09: Added retention policy examples and cross-region replication controls (Ethan Zhao).
- 2026-02-12: Finalized severity SLA and secure-SDLC gating (Priya Menon).

Related artifacts and links:
- /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/least-privilege-evidence-and-access-risk-playbook-2026
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/tenant-isolation-regressions-2025
- /infra/terraform/modules/evidence-buckets (internal repo)

Contact for questions: Marta Ruiz (security) — mruiz@redwood.example.com

payload.page_title: AuthZ Forensic Readiness: Checklist & Evidence Preservation Playbook

sections.body:
Operational playbook to ensure authentication/authorization evidence is captured, preserved, and packaged for security incidents, compliance audits, and legal holds across Redwood Inference deployments (hosted, dedicated, private).
Purpose
This playbook defines the operational controls, runbooks, and packaging standards for authentication and authorization (AuthZ) evidence required during security incidents, regulatory audits, and legal holds. It spans RBAC events, service-to-service auth, token/key lifecycle, audit log persistence, cross-region residency considerations, and integration points with our secure SDLC.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood services and control planes: hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.
- Evidence types covered: access grants/revokes, role changes, token/credential issuance, session starts/stops, policy evaluations, admin approvals, automated provisioning events, and audit pipeline delivery confirmations.
- Not in scope: user-created application payloads (handled by data retention team) except where payloads are directly referenced by auth decisions.

Owners and Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): Security on-call lead (rotating) — overall playbook authority during incidents.
- AuthZ Evidence Custodian (AEC): Identity & Access Management (IAM) engineering — responsible for evidence collection commands, retention, and integrity proofs.
- Audit Pipeline Owner: Observability platform team — ensures delivery of audit events to storage and maintains schema compatibility.
- Legal/Evidence Liaison: Legal & Compliance — authorizes legal holds and external disclosure.
- Oncall SRE: Eng-SRE — executes higher-level capture steps for infrastructure and storage.

Readiness Checklist (pre-incident)
1) Audit Stream Health
   - Verify end-to-end delivery: service -> audit-collector -> immutable-store.
   - SLO: 99.9% event delivery within 60s for auth events.
   - Daily check: `auditctl stream-health --check 24h` (returns delivery latency histogram).
2) Integrity and Signing
   - Ensure audit batches are signed with the current signing key (KMS key id).
   - Key rotation cadence: quarterly, documented in key-rotation-runbook.
3) Retention Baseline
   - Default retention: 3 years for authz decision logs (hosted/US), 7 years for enterprise regulated customers (per contract). See retention matrix in section "Retention Mapping".
4) Forensic Bundles Template
   - A defined JSONL manifest format exists (see example below). Ensure pipeline supports on-demand export.
5) Legal Hold Actionable Pathway
   - Legal holds can be opened by Legal & Security. Verify preservation toggle pathway in evidence-service UI/API.
6) Playbook Drills
   - Quarterly tabletop plus an annual live exercise with oncall and legal.

Immediate Actions When an AuthZ Incident is Suspected
1) Triage and Classification
   - IC assigns severity (S1: active exploitation, S2: suspicious anomalous grants, S3: informational).
   - If S1 or regulatory scope, engage Legal immediately.
2) Stabilize
   - If abuse involves privileged roles, initiate immediate containment: temporary role freeze and JIT disablement for affected roles.
   - Example CLI to freeze role propagation: `iamctl role-freeze --role admin --reason "incident-<id>"`.
3) Evidence Preservation (AEC + Audit Pipeline Owner)
   - Issuing preservation command: `evidencectl preserve --incident incident-<id> --scope authz --from 2024-08-01T00:00:00Z --to now`
   - The command should produce a signed manifest (SHA256 sums) and store a copy in the immutable evidence bucket in the region of origin and a secondary copy in the secure-evidence vault (global).
4) Capture Volatile State
   - Snapshot running session caches and KV-store auth caches: `runtime-snapshot --target kv-auth-cache --output snapshot-<id>.tar.gz`
   - Export current policy engine decision trees: `policyctl export --format yaml > policy-snapshot-<id>.yaml`
5) Audit Log Queries and Exports (examples)
   - Example ES query to find role grant events:
     POST /_search
     {
       "query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"event.type": "auth.role.grant"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-30d"}}}]}}
     }
   - SQL example for clickhouse storage: `SELECT timestamp, principal, action, resource FROM auth_events WHERE event_type='role_grant' AND timestamp >= '2024-08-01'`

Forensic Bundle Format (manifest-first JSONL)
- Each bundle must include a manifest.json (top-level) signed and checksumed. Example manifest fields (line-delimited JSON):
  {"bundle_id":"incident-<id>", "created_by":"evidencectl", "created_at":"2024-08-15T12:34:56Z", "signing_key":"kms://projects/redwood/keys/audit-sign-v2", "items":[{"path":"auth_events_2024-08-15.jsonl.gz","sha256":"...","type":"auth_log","region":"us-west-2"}]}
- All content files appended as compressed JSONL with one event per line.

Chain-of-Custody and Proof-of-Integrity
1) Signatures: Each exported bundle and manifest must be signed using KMS. The signature metadata (key id, signature timestamp) is recorded in bundle metadata.
2) Hashing: SHA256 for files, and a bundle-level Merkle root for all included files where possible.
3) Access Log: Who downloaded or accessed the bundle is recorded in the evidence-access index. Access requires AEC approval and an audit entry is created.

Retention Mapping (summary table described in text)
- Region default: US-hosted: 3 years for auth events; EU-hosted: 5 years where customer-specific contracts require it; APAC: 2 years by default but can be extended per customer SLA.
- Legal holds: supersede default retention and set retention to indefinite until release.
- Short-lived debug traces (token caches, ephemeral traces): 30 days unless escalated.

Integration with Secure SDLC (gates and artifacts)
- Pre-merge checks: every change touching auth code or audit schemas requires an automated schema-compatibility test. CI job: `ci-authz-schema-check`.
- Release gate: releases that modify entitlement logic must include a signed regression test artifact and an evidence export demonstrating no backward-incompatible decision changes against production prompt/decision sets.
- Post-deploy monitoring: anomaly detector (authz-anom) triggers a P1 alert for unusual privilege grant rates (> 3x baseline per 10m).

Evidence Packaging and Handoff to Legal/External Auditors
1) Packaging Steps (AEC):
   - Collect: relevant logs, policy snapshots, role membership lists, session snapshots, deployment manifests for relevant services.
   - Package: bundle into signed manifest + compressed payloads.
   - Verify: compute and publish checksums to the evidence index.
   - Handoff: create an evidence ticket and notify Legal with bundle id and access request template.
2) Redaction: If external disclosure is required, work with Legal to apply redaction rules; maintain an unredacted copy in the secure vault.

Sample Commands and Automation Snippets
- Generate a forensic bundle for the last 72 hours:
  `evidencectl preserve --incident incident-1234 --scope authz --from "now-72h" --format jsonl --dest s3://secure-evidence/incident-1234/`
- Verify manifest signature:
  `evidencectl verify --manifest s3://secure-evidence/incident-1234/manifest.json`
- Toggle legal hold via API (requires legal token):
  `curl -X POST https://evidence.redwood.internal/holds --header "Authorization: Bearer <legal-token>" -d '{"bundle_id":"incident-1234", "reason":"subpoena"}'`

Common Incident Playbook Paths (decision tree summary)
- If unauthorized privilege escalation detected:
  1) S1 path: freeze role propagation, preserve last 90 days of logs, engage Legal, create forensic bundle, initiate customer notification cadence (if PII involved).
  2) S2 path: targeted role revoke, capture policy change event, schedule follow-up audit.
- If potential data residency breach (logs crossing boundary):
  1) Isolate pipeline sink, preserve affected shard, consult Data Residency lead, and escalate to Compliance.

Post-Incident: Evidence Lifecycle and Lessons Learned
- Evidence retention review: after incident close, AEC recommends retention window (standard or extended) in the postmortem.
- Automated evidence summary: evidencectl summarize --bundle incident-1234 > incident-1234-summary.md (attach to postmortem).
- Improvement actions: update CI gates, add specific detection rules, or tighten retention as required.

Appendix A — Example minimal manifest (single-line JSON string representation)
{"bundle_id":"incident-1234","created_at":"2024-08-15T12:34:56Z","created_by":"evidencectl","items":[{"path":"auth_events_2024-08-15.jsonl.gz","type":"auth_log","sha256":"abc123...","region":"us-west-2"}],"signature":"kms-signature-v1"}

Appendix B — Quick references
- Evidence export API: https://wiki-internal/api/evidence-export (internal only)
- IAM runbooks: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provenance-and-retention-framework-2026
- Key rotation runbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-schema-versioning-and-evidence-tagging-2026

Change History
- 2024-08-15: Initial draft (Maya Patel).
- 2024-11-02: Added manifest signing examples and retention matrix updates (Elena Ruiz).
- 2025-02-10: Clarified CI gate requirements and added sample automation snippets (Jonah Kim).
