payload.page_title: Docs site offline edit & atomic commit playbook

sections.body:
Overview
========
This playbook defines the recommended offline editing workflow and the atomic-commit policy for the Redwood docs site. It is intended for the developer experience (DevX) writers, SDK engineers, and contributor tooling owners who need to: prepare content without continuous connectivity, stage large curated snippet bundles, and guarantee atomic updates across the docs site, snippet-store, and snippet validation CI.

Motivation
----------
- Support contributors in low-bandwidth or intermittent network environments (device-only editing, airplane mode, secure sites).
- Prevent partial rollouts (e.g., docs update without required snippet or sample-code update) by enforcing atomic commits across multiple repositories and services.
- Reduce support escalations caused by broken snippets after a partial deploy.

Scope
-----
Applies to: docs authors, SDK sample owners, release engineers, and DX tooling maintainers.
Not in scope: runtime model-serving changes, infra-level network maintenance (see eng-infra runbooks).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Offline edit bundle: a tarball or git bundle that contains content edits, snippet updates, and a manifest describing intended target branches.
- Atomic commit: a deploy step that ensures content + snippet-store + validation tags move from A->B together, or the operation aborts and rolls back.
- Snippet-store: the internal service that hosts canonical code snippets (internal URL: https://snippet-store.redwood.internal).
- Docs canary: a selective rollout to 2% of documentation traffic and the staging subdomain (docs-staging.redwood.com) before a full publish.

Goals and SLAs
--------------
- Docs site availability SLO for the main site: 99.95% (see eng-platform dashboards for exact monitoring).
- Deployment failure rate target: < 1% for atomic publish jobs.
- Mean time to recovery for broken snippets after an atomic publish: < 30 minutes with oncall involvement.

Offline edit workflow (recommended)
----------------------------------
1) Prepare local workspace
   - Clone the docs repo and snippet-store mirrors: git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/docs.git and git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/snippet-store.git
   - Create a working branch: git checkout -b offline/<your-issue-id>

2) Make edits locally
   - Update Markdown/Confluence-sourced files, add or modify snippets in snippet-store/src, update manifest.yaml (see manifest example below).
   - Run local validation: ./tools/local-docs-check --quiet. This runs lint, link-checker, and snippet extraction in offline mode.

3) Create an offline edit bundle
   - Generate a signed bundle: ./tools/mk-bundle --branch offline/<id> --author "Maya Thompson" --sign > offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz
   - The bundle includes: docs patch, snippet-store patch, manifest.yaml, preflight-checks.json, and a GPG signature.

4) Transport bundle to a connected machine (trusted staging)
   - Use a secure transfer mechanism (scp to bastion or upload via private S3) and verify the bundle signature: gpg --verify offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz.sig offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz

5) Validate and submit to the atomic publish job
   - On the connected machine, extract and run: ./tools/verify-bundle offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz
   - If verification passes, push to the release queue: ./tools/submit-atomic --bundle offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz --target-branch release/<date>

Atomic commit policy
--------------------
- Atomic publish job responsibilities:
  - Orchestrate simultaneous PRs/patches across: docs repo, snippet-store, and devx-samples repository.
  - Trigger CI validation pipelines: docs-ci-lint, snippet-ci-tests, sample-integration-tests.
  - Create a single release tag (docs-release/<semver>) only if all checks pass.
  - Deploy to docs-staging and run canary checks.

- Rejection conditions (job will abort and rollback):
  - Any CI job fails (lint/link/snippet-compile/sample-build).
  - Canary validation fails (broken links, snippet mismatch, formatting regressions).
  - Manifest mismatch: required snippet versions not present in snippet-store.

- Rollback behavior:
  - The atomic job never merges individual PRs into production branches. It only merges when everything is green. On failure, it leaves feature branches intact for manual remediation and opens a triage issue with artifacts from the failed run.

Staging and release orchestration
---------------------------------
1) Canary publish (default):
   - Deploy release tag to docs-staging and to 2% of traffic via docs-proxy routing.
   - Run automated acceptance: link-checker, snippet-executor (executes code samples in a sandbox), readability metrics.
   - Notify #docs-canary Slack channel with failure/success summary.

2) Hold period:
   - Default hold: 2 hours for low-risk doc updates, 24 hours for sample or SDK surface changes.

3) Full publish:
   - If canary positive, the atomic job performs the merge to main and tags release. Content is then indexed by search and promoted to docs.redwood.com.

CI checks and snippet validation
--------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:

sections.heading: Required CI checks for atomic publish

sections.body:
- Each snippet must include metadata header: language, runtime, expected-output, and snippet-id. Example header:

  <!-- snippet: id=auth-quickstart lang=python runtime=py3.10 expected-output=OK -->

- CI will reject snippets that: fail to compile/run, exceed runtime limits (120s for full-run tests), or assert outputs that differ from expected-output.

Manifest example (manifest.yaml)
--------------------------------
- purpose: tie docs edits to snippet versions and intended branches
- fields (text):
  - docs_branch: "offline/PR-1234"
  - snippet_store_branch: "offline/PR-1234-snippets"
  - sample_repo_branch: "offline/PR-1234-samples"
  - required_snippet_tags: ["sdk-python@2.3.1", "sdk-js@1.8.0"]
  - author: "Maya Thompson"
  - change_summary: "Update SDK quickstart and python auth snippet for new token flow"

(Refer to the appendix for a YAML example file.)

Rollback and emergency procedures
--------------------------------
- If a problematic publish reaches production: open an incident in PagerDuty with the tag "docs:broken-snippets" and notify #docs-oncall.
- The oncall will run the atomic rollback script: ./tools/atomic-rollback --tag <docs-release/tag> which will revert the release tag and re-deploy the previous release.
- Post-incident steps: create a postmortem in oncall/incidents/docs with timeline, root cause, and corrective actions.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owners:
  - DevX Docs (team alias: devx-docs@redwood.com) — content and editorial responsibility.
  - DevX Tooling (team alias: devx-tooling@redwood.com) — bundle tooling, verify-bundle, and atomic orchestrator.
  - SDK Samples (rotation): assigned sample owners in AUTHORS.md for language-specific snippets.
- Oncall escalation path:
  1) devx-oncall (PagerDuty)
  2) devx-tooling lead (pagerduty escalation rule)
  3) eng-platform (if infrastructure impacts observed)

Appendix: example commands and YAML
-----------------------------------
sections.heading: Snippet validation details

sections.body:
# confirm GPG signature
  gpg --verify offline-bundle-123.sig offline-bundle-123.tar.gz

  # verify bundle contents and run staged checks
  ./tools/verify-bundle offline-bundle-123.tar.gz --run-ci-mock

  # submit for atomic publish (creates combined PRs and triggers CI)
  ./tools/submit-atomic --bundle offline-bundle-123.tar.gz --target-branch release/2026-02-03

Sample manifest.yaml (text):

  docs_branch: "offline/PR-1234"
  snippet_store_branch: "offline/PR-1234-snippets"
  sample_repo_branch: "offline/PR-1234-samples"
  required_snippet_tags:
    - "sdk-python@2.3.1"
    - "sdk-js@1.8.0"
  author: "Maya Thompson"
  change_summary: "Update quickstart for SDK auth changes"

FAQ (short)
-----------
Q: Can I push only docs without snippets?
A: Not under the atomic policy if the manifest declares snippet changes. For pure editorial updates, the atomic job allows docs-only bundles with an explicit no-snippet flag.

Q: What happens if snippet CI times out?
A: The atomic job marks the run as failed and opens a triage issue. For transient CI infra issues, re-run uses the same bundle artifacts.

Q: Where do I get help?
A: Ping #devx-docs in Slack for editorial questions and #devx-tooling for CI/tooling failures. For emergencies use devx-oncall.

payload.page_title: Embedded Team Hiring & Partnership Playbook

sections.body:
Purpose
- This playbook defines a standard hiring, onboarding, and partnership approach for candidates hired into embedded roles: engineers, product managers, designers, and data scientists who will be placed inside product or platform teams but remain connected to a central enabling org. The goal is to reduce ramp time, set predictable expectations for managers and candidates, and preserve consistent quality across decentralized placements.

Scope
- Applies to: Embedded hires (E-embedded) and long-term cross-functional contractors joining product, platform, and data teams.
- Exclusions: Purely central roles (e.g., hiring for people-ops core HR team) and short (<12 week) contractors.

Principles
1) Clarity of scope: hire against an initial 90-day charter with measurable deliverables.
2) Observable outcomes: bias toward work samples and past impact over hypotheticals.
3) Partnership-first: hiring loop must include both hiring manager and a partner (product, infra, design) as interviewers.
4) Inclusion: structured interviews, diverse slates, and calibrated scorecards mitigate bias.

Hiring workflow (high level)
1. Intake & role brief (owner: hiring manager + central recruiter)
   - One-pager: mission of placement, success metrics at 30/60/90 days, required/optional skills, team context, escalation contacts.
   - Candidate profile: seniority band, travel/region constraints, remote vs colocated requirement.
2. Sourcing & shortlisting
   - Minimum slate size: 4 diverse candidates before onloop interviews when possible.
3. Interview loop (see template below)
4. Decision & offer (people-ops approves comp band & equity)
5. Onboarding and 90-day sponsor assignment

Role intake template (deliverables to include in the brief)
- 30-day goals (examples): Setup dev environment, ship first small bugfix or doc change, join oncall shadowing.
- 60-day goals: Deliver initial feature component or experiment, own recurring weekly sync with partner team.
- 90-day goals: Independently land a scoped project with post-deploy metrics and a blameless retro.
- Ramp success metrics: PR merged within 2 weeks; first independent deploy by week 8; oncall readiness by week 12.

Interview loop template (embeds and roles)
- Recruiter screen (30m): logistics, motivation, culture fit
- Work-sample assignment or take-home (optional for senior roles)
- Technical competency (45–60m): hiring manager + team engineer (system design, code review of candidate sample)
- Cross-functional partnership (30–45m): product/design/infra partner checks collaboration and prioritization
- Behavioral & leadership (30m): people manager or senior IC for collaboration examples
- Bar-raiser / calibration interviewer (30m): someone neutral from another org to assess bias and comp

Scoring rubric (sample)
- Each interviewer uses a 1–5 scale with evidence notes. Aggregate pass threshold: mean >= 3.6 and no single interviewer with a 1.
- Competencies (scored separately): Core craft (technical/product/design), Collaboration & Stakeholder Management, Ownership & Impact, Learning Agility, Communication.

DEI guardrails (mandatory)
- Diverse slate policy: at least 30% underrepresented candidates in final 4 when possible.
- Structured question bank supplied to interviewers.
- Interviewer calibration every 2 months for hiring managers who have conducted >4 loops.

Offer & acceptance checklist
- People-ops: confirm comp band, manager: confirm 90-day charter and sponsor, Legal: confirm any contract clauses (NDA, export control).
- Candidate: receives written offer with clear first-day logistics and expected 30/60/90 deliverables.

Onboarding & first 90 days (detailed plan)
- Role sponsor: someone on the host team (peer-level) assigned for 90 days; sponsor runs weekly sync during first 8 weeks.
- First week (Day 1–5):
  - Day 1: Welcome, account access, security & compliance training, team intro readout slot.
  - Day 2–5: Environment setup, mini pairing sessions, first 1:1 with manager (set expectations), meet cross-functional partner.
- Weeks 2–4: Shadowing on-call, ship first small task, feedback checkpoint at week 4 with manager + sponsor.
- Weeks 5–8: Ownership of a scoped feature/experiment; biweekly demo to partner team.
- Weeks 9–12: Handover, production metrics, oncall readiness signoff, end-of-90-day retro and success rubric review.

90-day evaluation (manager + sponsor)
Table (text format)
| Dimension | Evidence | Expected by 90 days | Rating notes |
|-----------|----------|---------------------|--------------|
| Ramp speed | PRs, deploys, code reviews | PR merged within 2 weeks, independent deploy by week 8 | 1–5 |
| Impact | Metrics, feature outcomes | Clear measurable impact (adoption, latency, cost) | 1–5 |
| Collaboration | Meeting notes, stakeholder feedback | Regular partner syncs and positive peer feedback | 1–5 |
| Reliability | Oncall incidents handled, pager response | Participated in oncall rotations; minimal guidance by week 12 | 1–5 |

Manager responsibilities (checklist)
- Prepare the 90-day charter prior to offer acceptance.
- Schedule first-week meetings and assign a sponsor.
- Run weekly 30-minute check-ins for first 8 weeks, then biweekly 1:1s.
- Provide timely feedback: short-form written notes after major milestones (PRs, demos).
- Submit 90-day evaluation to people-ops and file calibration notes.

Manager 1:1 and feedback cadence (recommended)- Weekly 30m manager check-ins for weeks 1–8: focus on blockers, onboarding logistics, psychological safety.- Weekly sponsor syncs (15m) run by sponsor.- Biweekly team sync demos (30m) to align stakeholders.- Formal 30/60/90 feedback checkpoints (written notes) at days 30, 60, 90.

Performance calibration & promotions
- Calibration windows: quarterly (standard) + rolling promotion packet review for exceptional cases.
- Evidence required for promotion: consistent 6–12 month impact, demonstrated leadership in scope expansion, peer & partner endorsements.
- Promotion packet template: summary of impact, before/after metrics, two manager-level endorsements, learning plan for next level.

Probation & remediation
- Probation period: default 90 days with extension possible (max 60 days) when there is a documented improvement plan.
- Remediation steps: document concerns -> create 30/60 day improvement plan with SMART goals -> weekly progress checkpoints -> final assessment.

Operational checklists and templates (links)
- New hire 90-day charter template (copyable).
- Interviewer question bank (structured) and scorecard (spreadsheet).
- Sponsor handoff checklist.
- Sample offer language for embedded placements.

Sample new hire 30/60/90 charter (plain text)
- 30-day: Complete environment setup, write first microservice unit tests, attend three partner planning meetings.
- 60-day: Deliver first scoped experiment, increase test coverage by X%, drive one cross-team sync.
- 90-day: Ship project, monitor initial metrics for 2 weeks, prepare lessons-learned doc and present in retro.

Integrations with existing people-ops processes
- Use People-ops hiring portal to create requisition and track diverse slate compliance.
- Upload 90-day evaluation into the People-ops performance folder.
- Trigger learning resources (role-specific training playlists) automatically on hire.

Escalation & ownership
- Hiring disputes or offer escalations: escalate to Talent Lead (people-ops) -> Head of Recruiting -> CFO for comp exceptions.
- Onboarding blockers that prevent ramping: escalate to host team tech lead and People-ops onboarding coordinator.

Appendix: sample interview scorecard (text)
- Candidate name: ____________________
- Role: ____________________
- Interviewer: ____________________
- Date: ____________________
- Scores (1–5): Core craft: __, Collaboration: __, Ownership: __, Communication: __, Overall: __
- Evidence notes: (3–5 bullet lines)

Related resources
- Onboarding immersion rotation playbook: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026.json
- Role activation & 90-day sponsor playbook: /confluence/people-ops/role-activation-and-90-day-sponsor-playbook-2026.json

payload.page_title: Docs Site Runbook: Publishing, SDK Guides, and Canonical Support Fixes

sections.body:
Purpose:
This runbook consolidates operations and editorial procedures for the Redwood developer documentation site (docs.redwood.ai), with a focus on: SDK guide publication, quickstart/template lifecycle, API example validation, Site CI/CD, and the canonical fixes for the top support issues we see from customers. Use this page as the single source for day-to-day site ops for the DX team and on-call engineers.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: DX engineers, technical writers, on-call eng for docs site incidents, solutions engineers publishing examples.
- Scope: procedures for authoring, validating, publishing, rolling back docs; CI/CD and release checks; canonical fixes for frequent support tickets; monitoring and KPI thresholds.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience docs team (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (pager: #eng-sre).
- Escalation path: docs on-call -> SRE on-call -> Head of DX -> Product (if content change impacts contracts/SLA).

Operating hours and SLA:
- Publishing window: 08:00–20:00 PDT weekdays for non-emergency content changes.
- Emergency fixes: 24/7 (use on-call).
- Target publish success rate: 99% (measured monthly).

Repository and deployment overview:
- Docs repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git (main branch protected).
- CI provider: GitHub Actions (docs-ci).
- Static site generator: Hugo + custom shortcodes and the DX theme.
- CDN: Cloudfront in front of S3 bucket (origin).
- Preview environments: Pull-request preview via netlify-preview (per-PR).

Pre-publish checklist (authors):
1) Lint and link-check: run local script `scripts/validate.sh` (see below).
2) API examples: run the example suite against staging API credentials and ensure no flaky tests.
3) SDK snippets: run unit smoke test: `python -m pytest tests/snippets` or `yarn test:snippets`.
4) Accessibility quickscan: `axe` browser extension or `npm run a11y-check` for pages with interactive components.
5) Metadata: frontmatter contains title, summary, tags, stable-url, and last_updated.

Local validation commands (examples):
```bash
# run static checks
./scripts/validate.sh
# run snippet tests (python SDK)
REDWOOD_API_KEY=$STAGING_KEY pytest tests/snippets/test_py_snippets.py -q
# run linkcheck
hugo --gc --minify && ./scripts/linkcheck.sh public
```

Publishing procedure (major doc or SDK guide):
1) Create a PR against `main` with descriptive title and change summary.
2) Assign reviewers from the reviewers list and any area owner (sdk-guides / product docs).
3) CI runs: lint -> snippet tests -> accessibility -> preview deploy.
4) Reviewer checklist (must be completed before merge):
   - Verify code examples execute against staging API and produce expected responses.
   - Confirm accuracy of SLOs, thresholds, and service names.
   - Validate wording for customer-facing clarity.
5) Merge by a reviewer (no self-merge for public-facing pages).
6) Post-merge: monitor the publish pipeline and CDN invalidation logs.

Rollback procedure (site or page-level):
1) If preview tests fail before merge: fix in branch.
2) If post-merge regression is detected: open an emergency PR reverting the merge and set PR title with `[EMERGENCY-ROLLBACK]` prefix.
3) SRE to coordinate cache invalidation and ensure the S3 origin matches the rollback commit.
4) Run smoke checks from multiple regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).

Post-publish verification (10–15 min after merge):
- Check preview and live URL respond (curl + check status 200).
  `curl -sS -I https://docs.redwood.ai/path | grep HTTP`
- Validate snippet output with `scripts/verify_live_snippets.sh` (compares golden outputs).
- Confirm CDN invalidation completed in CloudFront console.
- Spot-check three pages for formatting on mobile and desktop.

Template for SDK guide (required frontmatter):
- required frontmatter keys: title, description, stable_url, sdk (python|js|go), sdk_version, tags, last_updated
- Example frontmatter: `---
title: "Quickstart: Python SDK v2"
sdk: python
sdk_version: "2.1.0"
---`

Canonical structure for an SDK guide page:
1) Short intro (1–2 paragraphs).
2) Installation snippet.
3) Minimal example with expected output.
4) Common pitfalls and troubleshooting (short bullets).
5) API reference link and changelog notes.
6) Test snippet that can be executed by CI.

API example validation checklist:
- Do examples use stable model names and deterministic seeds where applicable?
- Are environment variables (like REDWOOD_API_KEY) referenced but not leaked?
- Are examples idempotent and safe to run against staging?
- Do examples contain timeouts and retries for network calls?

Top support issues and canonical fixes (current list):
1) Auth failures in examples (most common)
   - Symptom: 401 when running snippets locally.
   - Root cause: author used personal dev key in repo or example references `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but user didn't set it.
   - Canonical fix: Add a clear auth setup section to every SDK guide and include `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<YOUR_KEY>"` in examples; update `scripts/validate.sh` to detect hard-coded keys.
2) Streaming responses hang in previews
   - Symptom: Netlify preview shows spinner indefinitely for streaming examples.
   - Root cause: preview environment blocks WebSocket/stream upgrades or the preview proxy strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers.
   - Canonical fix: Add a fallback non-streaming example and a note in streaming docs explaining preview limitations. File a ticket to SRE to whitelist preview origin if long-term requirement.
3) Mismatched SDK version in snippets
   - Symptom: code uses `client.chat.stream()` which exists only in SDK v3 but page frontmatter claims v2.
   - Root cause: stale copy/paste across versions.
   - Canonical fix: Require `sdk_version` in frontmatter and add CI step to check snippet compatibility against that version by running `npx test-snippets --sdk-version $sdk_version`.
4) Broken links to product pages after model name changes
   - Symptom: 404s to model catalog links in older guides.
   - Canonical fix: Use stable redirectable paths (`/models/{slug}`) instead of raw model names, and add a weekly linkcheck job.

Monitoring, alerts and KPIs:
- Pager triggers: Site 5xx rate > 1% for 5m, Preview deploy failures > 3 in 1 hour.
- Dashboards to check: docs-build-failure-rate, docs-traffic-by-region, snippet-test-failures (per-sdk).
- Monthly KPI: snippet test pass rate >= 98%.

Runbook: common remediation commands and snippets:
- Re-run failed job locally: `GITHUB_ACTIONS=false ./scripts/ci-run.sh --job publish`
- Force CDN invalidation: `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E12345 --paths "/\*"`
- Rebuild preview manually: `./scripts/trigger-preview.sh <pr-number>`

Editorial notes and best practices:
- Keep examples minimal and copy-paste friendly (max 40 lines for a runnable snippet).
- Prefer explicit numeric examples for latency/cost where relevant (`Estimated cost: ~$0.002 per 1k tokens`).
- When documenting SLOs or thresholds, cite service names and owners (e.g., `Serving Runtime (owner: infra/runtime-team) - p99 latency < 350ms`).

Incident debriefs and postmortems:
- For any publish outage > 30 minutes open a postmortem in `confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/postmortems`.
- Include root cause, timeline, impacted pages, and the canonical fix applied.

Appendix: quick links and useful commands:
- Repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git
- CI status: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site/actions
- Preview checks: `./scripts/verify_preview.sh <preview-url>`

If you find gaps in this runbook or new recurring issues, add a short section under "Top support issues" and notify reviewers. This document is reviewed quarterly by the DX owner (owner: Aisha Patel).

sections.body: h1. Overview
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
* Updating the SDK Quickstart to include _streaming_ and _tool/function calling_.
* Aligning Hosted vs Dedicated routing language (including a small cost/latency comparison).
* Publishing two sample apps (React chat UI + serverless/edge proxy) with copy-pasteable examples.

Scope note: this is written as a polished docs-spec/reference for DevX work. Implementation details in linked PRs.

h1. Target audience

* Developers integrating Redwood Inference via the JS or Python SDK.
* DevX maintainers authoring docs for quickstart and examples.

h1. Key decisions (updated)

* The Quickstart must include a minimal streaming example (<= 15 lines) and explicitly demonstrate cancellation.
* The Quickstart must include a minimal tool-calling example. If a single snippet becomes too long, provide two minimal snippets (streaming-only and tool-calling-only) with a short note on combining them.
* Billing copy has been updated: we should not claim “only pay for generated tokens” without qualification. See *Streaming billing copy* below.
* Sample apps will be documented as two code paths: Hosted and Dedicated. The README should make switching explicit (via env vars and a small toggle in the UI for the React sample).

h1. Docs locations (where this content lands)

* Quickstart page (docs site): “Quickstart (2 min)” section
* Examples:
** examples/streaming.md
** examples/tools.md (or examples/functions.md if that’s the established naming)
** examples/batching.md
* FAQ:
** Hosted vs Dedicated routing policy (with a small table)

h1. Quickstart: minimal streaming example (JavaScript)

Below is the current recommended minimal snippet. It demonstrates partial tokens and cancellation while staying small.

{code:javascript}
const controller = new AbortController();
const stream = await client.responses.stream({
  model: "redwood-4.1-mini",
  input: "Summarize this paragraph in one sentence.",
  signal: controller.signal,
});
for await (const event of stream) process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? "");
// cancel if the user navigates away:
controller.abort();
{code}
sections.heading: This page consolidates the current guidance for
Notes for maintainers

sections.body:
1. Show streaming alone (Quickstart).
2. Show tools alone (Quickstart or examples/tools.md).
3. In examples/tools.md, add an “Advanced: tools with streaming” section that explains event sequencing and how to buffer partial arguments.

Implementation guidance to include in the docs (no deep internals):
* Tool arguments may arrive incrementally; accumulate until a “tool_call.complete” (or equivalent) event before executing.
* Always validate tool arguments against the schema before running side effects.
* If emitting structured JSON to the UI, parse only after completion; during streaming show a placeholder state (“Working…”).

h1. Hosted vs Dedicated routing (FAQ-ready)

h2. Summary

* Hosted: simplest integration, shared fleet, best for fast onboarding.
* Dedicated: reserved capacity and stronger control over versions/rollouts, best for predictable latency and regulated workloads.

h2. Routing policy table (example)

|| Dimension || Hosted (shared) || Dedicated (reserved) ||
| Typical onboarding time | Minutes | Days (provisioning + contract/config) |
| Latency variance | Medium (depends on shared load) | Low (reserved capacity) |
| Version control | Model aliases managed by Redwood | Optional pinning + controlled rollout windows |
| Failover behavior | Managed automatically | Configurable (e.g., fallback to Hosted or smaller Dedicated model) |
| Cost model | Pay-as-you-go | Base reservation + usage (per contract) |

h2. Example headers / configuration

Docs must clearly separate what changes between Hosted and Dedicated. Prefer environment variables and a short table.

|| Setting || Hosted || Dedicated ||
| Base URL | https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1 | https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1 (same) |
| Routing selector | none (default) | set routing to a dedicated deployment (header or SDK config) |
| Model name | redwood-4.1-mini (alias) | customer-specific alias or pinned version |

Important: the exact header/config name for Dedicated routing should match the SDK release. Do not publish placeholder header names in the public docs.

h1. Batching examples (JS + Python)

Docs gap addressed: JS batching examples must be present alongside Python.

h2. Conceptual guidance
sections.heading: Recommended docs approach

sections.body:
* You have many small requests that can tolerate a small delay (e.g., embeddings, classification, short completions).
* You want improved throughput and cost efficiency.
sections.heading: Use batching when
Avoid batching when

sections.body:
1. “Quickstart (2 min)” section (install, env vars, run)
2. “Switching routing mode” section (Hosted vs Dedicated)
3. “Common errors” section (auth, rate limits, model unavailable)
sections.heading: README requirements

sections.body:
* Add a minimal Playwright test that asserts tokens append in order during streaming.

h2. 2) Serverless / edge proxy

Goal: a minimal edge function that forwards requests and (optionally) injects routing configuration for Dedicated.
sections.heading: Testing requirement

sections.body:
* Example request forwarding
* Timeouts and cancellation behavior
* Clear warning on logging and PII (do not log prompts/responses by default)
sections.heading: Must include

sections.body:
* If Dedicated returns a retryable error (e.g., transient 503), demonstrate retry with a smaller model alias or a Hosted fallback _only if customer policy allows_.

h1. Error handling section (Quickstart addendum)

The Quickstart should include a small “Errors” section with:
* Common error types (auth, rate limit, model unavailable, transient 5xx)
* A remediation bullet for each
sections.heading: Fallback example (Dedicated capacity exhausted)

sections.body:
* Rate limiting: “Use exponential backoff with jitter. For user-facing flows, consider a smaller or less expensive model alias for retries.”
* Transient 5xx: “Retry with bounded attempts. For critical flows, consider a fallback model per your routing policy.”

h1. Streaming billing copy (updated)

Previous draft phrasing (“only pay for generated tokens”) is too absolute.

Approved safer wording for internal drafts (confirm with Finance/Packaging before publishing externally):
* “In streaming mode, tokens are delivered incrementally as they are generated. Billing is based on usage per your plan; cancellation may reduce output tokens, but request-level minimums and other plan rules may apply.”

Action: before publishing externally, get explicit sign-off from Finance/Packaging on the final sentence.

h1. Model versioning: pinning vs aliases (Dedicated)
sections.heading: Suggested copy (updated)

sections.body:
* Model aliases: stable name that can move to a newer model revision as Redwood rolls out improvements.
* Pinned versions: fixed model revision for maximum repeatability.

sections.body:
1. Test in staging with the new alias target.
2. Roll out with a small percentage of traffic (if supported by customer routing config).
3. Monitor latency and quality; rollback by repointing alias or reverting config.

payload.page_title: Docs-site snippet retirement and translation playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines the process, roles, and technical patterns our Developer Experience (DX) team uses to retire, update, and translate code snippets, API examples, and small how-tos that appear across the docs site, SDK guides, quickstarts, and API reference. It is intended for documentation owners, SDK maintainers, localization partners, and support engineers who propagate canonical fixes into documentation and SDK examples.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Ensure snippet changes are safe, discoverable, and reversible.
- Reduce stale or broken examples across languages by centralizing lifecycle rules.
- Provide a clear translation/localization workflow so localized pages are updated in step with English source edits.
- Maintain a fast path for urgent canonical fixes coming from support/triage.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Single-file snippets embedded in docs, quickstarts, and API examples.
- Language variants (python, javascript, curl) of the same example.
- Snippet metadata, tagging, and canonical source references.
- CI checks that verify snippet compilation or linter rules where possible.
sections.heading: Scope (what this playbook covers)

sections.body:
- Full sample applications (these follow the SDK repo release lifecycle).
- API surface changes that require SDK releases (those coordinate with Engineering Change Control).
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
- Canonical snippet: the primary source snippet maintained in the docs repo (usually under /snippets/).
- Snippet retirement: a formal removal or replacement of a snippet because it is obsolete, insecure, or replaced by a better pattern.
- Localized page: a translated doc page that mirrors an English source.
sections.heading: Key definitions

sections.body:
| Role | Responsibility | Primary contact |
|------|----------------|-----------------|
| Docs owner | Proposes snippet retirement/changes; writes replacement guidance | Priya Raman |
| SDK maintainer | Verifies language samples and raises SDK backport PRs if required | Ethan Morales |
| Localization lead | Coordinates translation updates and timing | Sofia Klein |
| Support escalation | Triggers urgent canonical-fix pathway when snippets cause customer impact | Daniel Park |
| Release coordinator | Approves scheduled doc deploy windows and notifies downstream teams | ReleaseOps Team |
sections.heading: Owners & roles

sections.body:
- Minor fixes (typos, formatting, linter fixes): Docs owner can merge after single reviewer sign-off.
- Behavioral fixes (auth change, example that could produce incorrect results): Docs owner + SDK maintainer must approve.
- Retirement of major example patterns (e.g., removing OAuth snippet): Docs owner + SDK lead + Security review required.

Snippet metadata standard (required front-matter for any canonical snippet):
- id: short-handle (e.g. embed-quickstart-python)
- languages: comma-separated (python,javascript,curl)
- status: canonical | deprecated | retired | experimental
- last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
- owner: team-or-person
sections.heading: Governance & approval thresholds

sections.body:
languages: python,javascript,curl
status: canonical
last_reviewed: 2026-02-10
owner: eng-devx
---

Retirement workflow (recommended cadence: quarterly review for low-risk snippets, immediate for critical fixes):
1) Proposal: Docs owner raises a Snippet Retirement RFC in the docs repo as a PR to /snippets/ with the reason and proposed replacement (if any).
2) Impact analysis: Include a quick search report (grep/graph) listing pages that reference the snippet. Use the internal snippet index: /docs/snippet-index.csv.
3) Classification: Mark the PR as one of: minor, breaking, security. If breaking or security, add label `retire-breaking` or `retire-security`.
4) Review: Required reviewers per classification (see Governance above). Add localized pages to reviewers.
5) Canary deploy: Merge to `canary-docs` and verify CI checks pass (compilation, snippet linters). Notify QA channel.
6) Observability window: Keep the change in canary for 48 hours and collect telemetry: 404s for removed snippet IDs, feedback form hits, and support tickets referencing the example.
7) Full rollout: Schedule to main docs deploy window. Communicate change in the weekly docs digest and to SDK teams.
8) Archive: Move retired snippet file to /snippets/retired/YYYYMMDD-<id>.md and update snippet-index.csv.
sections.heading: id: embed-quickstart-python

sections.body:
- Trigger: Support files a P1 if a snippet causes incorrect behavior in customer production flows (e.g., auth header example that leaks tokens).
- Steps:
  1. Support posts a ticket in #docs-urgent with reference and suggested patch.
  2. Docs owner creates an emergency PR titled `URGENT: canonical fix <id>` and adds `emergency` label.
  3. At least one SDK maintainer validates the fix (this can be a lightweight smoke test).
  4. PR merged to `canary-docs` and released to `main` with override per ReleaseOps policy (no wait window).
  5. Postmortem: owner documents cause and preventive action in the PR.

Translation / localization workflow (synchronization strategy):
- Principle: Localized pages must not lag behind canonical safety fixes. For retirements and security fixes, localized pages must be updated within 7 calendar days.
- Process:
  1) Mark the English PR with label `i18n-update-required` and add a `translation-delta` note in the PR description describing the scope of change.
  2) Localization lead triggers a translation job and assigns translators with a 72-hour SLA for minor textual edits; 7 days for behavioral changes.
  3) Localized PRs should reference the English canonical PR in their description (link to original PR).
  4) If localized content cannot be updated in time for the main deployment (e.g., legal constraints), the English change can be blocked only by Security/Legal; otherwise we proceed and add a localized warning banner automatically using the i18n pipeline.

Snippet tagging, CI and automated checks:
- All snippets must pass automated linters for the language and a lightweight snippet-checker. For languages we support, we run:
  - python: flake8 + snippet-run (virtualenv + run)
  - javascript: eslint + node-run-check
  - curl: http request smoke test (where endpoint public or mocked)
sections.heading: Urgent canonical fix pathway (support-driven)

sections.body:
name: snippet-smoke-checks
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  python-snippets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Run snippet runner
        run: |
          pip install -r tools/snippet-check/requirements.txt
          python tools/snippet-check/run_snippets.py --language python --path snippets/

Propagating canonical fixes to SDK guides and API examples (checklist):
- Create accompanying SDK issue/PR if the change requires an SDK release (auth flows, method names).
- If no SDK code change is required, update SDK guide pages with note: "Updated to reflect docs canonical fix <PR link>".
- Coordinate with SDK maintainers for backports if older major versions require the same fix.
- Add a `support-canonicalized` tag to the support ticket.
sections.heading: Sample GitHub Actions job (snippet smoke check)

sections.body:
- Severity P0/P1: use urgent pathway.
- Severity P2: schedule within 3 business days.
- Severity P3: normal triage (next sprint).
sections.heading: Support & canonical fixes triage matrix

sections.body:
- [ ] Snippet front-matter present and valid.
- [ ] Linter checks pass for all languages in `languages` front-matter.
- [ ] Impact analysis attached (pages list).
- [ ] Localization impact flagged if present.
- [ ] If security-sensitive, security review attached.

sections.body:
- Count of retired snippets per quarter (goal: reduce stale snippet backlog by 50% YoY).
- Number of support tickets referencing snippet examples (goal: 0 for high-severity cases).
- Time-to-fix for emergency canonical fixes (SLA target: < 4 hours for detection-to-canary-merge).

1) Revert PR in the docs repo and deploy to canary.
2) Run snippet smoke checks and open communication in #docs-ops with timeline.
3) If revert fails, contact ReleaseOps to block the main deploy and escalate to Eng SRE.

- Example requiring SDK change: open SDK issue and label `docs-blocker`; docs PR should link to SDK PR.

payload.page_title: Quantization Profiles (Public Docs) — Customer Documentation Plan

sections.body:
This page defines the plan for customer-facing documentation for the Quantization Profile Library (opt-in). The goal is to help customers safely enable quantization profiles per route, understand limitations and compatibility, run appropriate evaluations, interpret observability signals, and roll back quickly if needed.

This is an internal planning doc for Redwood Docs + DevEx and will be used as the source of truth for docs IA, required examples, and cross-team review gates.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
**Primary audiences**
- Software engineers and ML engineers integrating Redwood routes who want to reduce cost/token.
- Platform teams managing production change control (audit logs, RBAC, rollbacks).

**Customer use cases we need to support in docs**
1. Enable an approved quantization profile for a single route (hosted API).
2. Enable profile for a route with region/tier constraints (Dedicated + multi-region hosted).
3. Validate quality and latency before expanding traffic.
4. Diagnose output changes, elevated fallback rate, or latency regressions.
5. Roll back (route-level disable; global kill-switch is internal-only but mention its existence at a high level).
sections.heading: Audience and use cases

sections.body:
- Make it clear this is **opt-in** and **route-scoped** (v1), with baseline behavior unchanged when disabled.
- Provide a simple “happy path” enablement flow with copy-pastable examples (Console + API/SDK).
- Set expectations on **compatibility constraints** and **fallback behavior** (deterministic, baseline precision fallback).
- Provide a lightweight but concrete evaluation best-practices section that customers can follow without needing Redwood internal harnesses.
- Provide troubleshooting steps tied to the actual product signals customers will see (Console warnings/errors, request metadata, audit history, and dashboard panels).
sections.heading: Goals (docs)

sections.body:
- Do not position this as automatic tuning/recommendations (out of scope for v1).
- Do not publish internal-only implementation details (artifact signing specifics, internal service names, kill-switch runbooks).
- Do not promise universal profile coverage across all models/GPU SKUs.
sections.heading: Non-goals (docs)

sections.body:
We need consistent, customer-friendly wording:
- **Quantization profile**: A versioned, Redwood-validated configuration for running a specific model variant using a specific quantization method/precision combination.
- **Profile library**: The set of published profiles per model variant. Customers choose a profile for a route.
- **Route-level enablement**: Profiles are enabled per route, not globally for all tenant traffic (v1).
- **Fallback**: If a request is incompatible (hardware/sequence length constraints) or profile application fails safe checks, Redwood serves using baseline precision for that request (or route) while emitting an event.
sections.heading: Product language and terminology

sections.body:
- Avoid saying “Redwood automatically picks the best profile.”
- Avoid “lossless” claims. Use “aims to preserve quality” and emphasize eval/monitoring.
sections.heading: Avoid ambiguous language

sections.body: We will publish a small cluster of pages under: **Optimize → Quantization Profiles**.
sections.heading: Information architecture (public docs)

sections.body:
**Proposed title:** “Quantization Profiles (Preview/Beta)” (or “Quantization Profiles” once GA)

**Outline**
- What quantization profiles are and why they reduce cost.
- Opt-in and route-scoped behavior.
- High-level lifecycle: published profiles, versioning, deprecations.
- Safety model summary:
  - Compatibility checks before enablement.
  - Deterministic selection.
  - Fallback to baseline.
  - Auditability and change history.

**Callouts**
- “Start with a canary route; expand after evals.”
- “Not all models/regions support all profiles.”
sections.heading: Page 1: Overview (concept + safety model)

sections.body:
**Proposed title:** “Enable a quantization profile for a route”

**Required elements**
- Console walkthrough (with screenshots once UX is final):
  1) Navigate to Route → Performance/Optimize → Quantization
  2) Choose model variant + eligible profiles
  3) Read compatibility warnings
  4) Confirm change (modal) and review expected impact
  5) Verify enablement and view change history

- API example (REST) for updating route config
  - Show setting `quantization_profile_ref` to a specific profile ID/version.
  - Show how to reset to `default` / disable.

- SDK examples
  - Python and TypeScript: configure route setting; retrieve route state; handle incompatibility errors.

**Verification steps**
- Confirm in Console that route shows “Enabled” and which profile is selected.
- Show how to verify in request metadata (e.g., response headers or trace attributes) that a profile was applied vs fallback.
- Show where to find fallback/latency/cost deltas in dashboards.
sections.heading: Page 2: Enablement guide (Console + API/SDK)

sections.body:
**Proposed title:** “Compatibility, constraints, and fallback behavior”

**Include**
- What compatibility depends on:
  - Model ID + model variant
  - Deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private as applicable)
  - GPU class/SKU (expressed as customer-friendly names)
  - Max context / sequence length limits
  - Region constraints (if/when supported in route policy)

- Customer-facing compatibility matrix
  - If we can’t maintain a full matrix, we must at least publish:
    - “Supported GPUs by profile type” (e.g., INT8 supported on X, FP8 on Y)
    - “Max supported context per profile” for popular models
  - Decide format: table in docs + downloadable CSV updated weekly (recommended).

- Fallback semantics
  - Define what happens when incompatible:
    - If enablement time: block with clear error and remediation.
    - If request time: safe fallback to baseline; emit a signal; no infinite retry loops.

- Limitations / known caveats
  - Output differences are possible.
  - Some profiles may be labeled “Experimental” with narrower guardrails.
  - If customers pin to a profile version, it won’t change unless they update.
  - If we ever add “recommended” aliases, document that aliases may move and how we prevent silent changes (see Open Questions).
sections.heading: Page 3: Compatibility + limitations

sections.body:
**Proposed title:** “How to evaluate quality and latency before rollout”

**Customer-friendly guidance**
- Suggested evaluation approach:
  - Identify representative prompts (production samples + edge cases).
  - Run baseline vs profile-enabled comparisons.
  - Use A/B sampling (e.g., 1–5% traffic) with a rollback threshold.

- What to measure
  - Quality: task-specific metrics (pass@k, exact match, ranking metrics) + human review where appropriate.
  - Latency: p50/p95 decode latency and time-to-first-token.
  - Cost: cost/token and throughput.

- Rollout strategy
  1) Enable in staging on a non-critical route
  2) Canary in production (small % traffic)
  3) Expand gradually with monitoring

- Provide explicit “stop conditions”
  - Elevated fallback rate
  - Increased error rate
  - Statistically meaningful quality regression on a defined slice

**Note:** We cannot publish Redwood’s internal thresholds verbatim if they are considered sensitive, but we can publish recommended guardrails (e.g., “predefine acceptable deltas and require sign-off”). We will align with Selene Huang (quality guardrails) on what’s safe to disclose.
sections.heading: Page 4: Evaluation best practices

sections.body:
**Proposed title:** “Troubleshooting quantization profiles”

**Structure: symptom → likely cause → how to confirm → resolution**
sections.heading: Page 5: Troubleshooting + rollback

sections.body:
- Console says profile is incompatible
  - Common causes: wrong model variant, unsupported GPU class, context length exceeds profile limit.
  - Resolution: choose another profile; reduce max tokens/context; use baseline.

- Output quality changed unexpectedly
  - Confirm: compare baseline vs profile, check whether fallback occurred (mixed behavior can look inconsistent).
  - Resolution: disable profile; run eval; contact support with request IDs.

- p95 latency increased
  - Confirm: look at per-route latency panels; check TTFT vs decode; check batching/caching changes.
  - Resolution: disable profile; adjust route concurrency/batching; consult Redwood support.

- Elevated fallback rate
  - Confirm: dashboard panel + route events.
  - Likely causes: requests exceed profile constraints; region/GPU mismatch; deployment drift.
  - Resolution: tighten route constraints; pick compatible profile; disable.

- 5xx errors after enabling
  - Confirm: error class; check if errors correlate with specific profile version.
  - Resolution: disable; provide audit event ID and request IDs to support.

Rollback instructions (customer-actionable)
- Disable at route level (Console + API snippet).
- Verify disablement and that requests are using baseline.
sections.heading: Required symptoms

sections.body:
- “What information to include in a support ticket” checklist:
  - Org/tenant ID
  - Route name/ID
  - Model + variant
  - Profile ID/version
  - Region/deployment mode
  - Approx timeframe
  - Request IDs/traces
  - Observed metrics (fallback rate, p95 latency)
sections.heading: We should also include

sections.body:
We will maintain a single authoritative set of snippets and import them into the docs site.

**REST (pseudo)**
- GET route settings (show current model + quant state)
- PATCH route settings to set profile ref
- PATCH route settings to disable / reset to default

**Python SDK**
- Update route quantization setting
- Validate compatibility result handling
- Verify applied profile via response metadata

**TypeScript SDK**
- Same as Python, plus typing for errors.
sections.heading: Required code/examples (public docs)

sections.body:
- Final field names and error shapes must match control-plane API.
- Confirm the exact response fields that indicate `applied` vs `fallback` vs `disabled`.
sections.heading: Docs dependencies

sections.body: We will mirror Console language in docs to minimize confusion.
sections.heading: Console UX copy and warnings (alignment)

sections.body:
- “This change may affect output quality. Evaluate before ramping traffic.”
- “This profile is only compatible with <constraints>. Requests outside constraints will fall back to baseline.”
- “Pinning a profile version ensures deterministic behavior until you change it.”

We will coordinate final wording with Tessa Morgan (UX lead) and Kenji Nakamura (rollout/controls designer).
sections.heading: Warnings to standardize

sections.body:
**Reviewers required before docs merge**
- Applied ML: Arjun Desai (profiles lead) + Selene Huang (guardrails)
- Runtime: Noah Patel (runtime architect)
- Platform/Console: Chloe Martin (Console backend lead)
- SRE/Release: Connor O'Brien (rollout lead)
- Security/RBAC: Naomi Feldman (RBAC/audit requirements)

**Release stages and docs behavior**
- Beta/allowlist:
  - Docs are public but clearly marked “Beta” with known limitations.
  - Include a “Contact Support to enable” note if feature is behind an allowlist.

- GA:
  - Remove Beta banner.
  - Publish compatibility matrix link and clear deprecation policy.

**Update cadence**
- Compatibility matrix and profile coverage: weekly updates (aligned with profile publishing cadence).
- Troubleshooting section: update after each beta incident/support trend.
sections.heading: Review, launch gating, and update cadence

sections.body:
- ≥80% of beta design partner enablements completed without synchronous Redwood help.
- Reduction in support tickets that are purely “how do I enable/disable?” (shift to higher-signal issues).
- Median time-to-rollback for customers (self-serve) < 10 minutes after following docs.
- Docs telemetry: high completion rates on enablement guide; low bounce on troubleshooting due to missing information.
sections.heading: Success criteria (docs)

sections.body:
1. **Alias semantics:** Will we expose “recommended/latest” aliases in v1 GA or only pinned profile IDs/versions? If aliases exist, we must document how we prevent silent changes (e.g., aliases only change on customer action vs Redwood updates).
2. **Customer-facing compatibility matrix:** What is the minimum viable matrix we can keep current without excessive operational load? (Proposal: publish for top 10 models + major GPU classes first.)
3. **What can we safely publish about quality thresholds?** We should align with Applied ML on whether to include specific numeric deltas or keep it as qualitative guidance.
4. **Request metadata surface:** What is the final customer-visible mechanism to confirm applied profile (headers, response fields, trace attribute)? This must be stable.
sections.heading: Open questions

sections.body:
- (Docs) Elliot Price: draft public docs pages 1–5 and route through review (target by 2025-03-14).
- (DevEx) Monica Patel: finalize Python + TS snippets and ensure they match SDK releases.
- (Console) Chloe Martin: confirm final Console labels, error strings, and change history UX for screenshot capture.
- (Applied ML) Arjun Desai / Selene Huang: approve public-facing evaluation guidance and guardrail language.
- (SRE) Connor O'Brien: verify rollback instructions align with operational reality and dashboards customers can access.
sections.heading: Action items

sections.body:
- Keep customer docs consistent with the PRD’s promise: **opt-in**, **auditable**, **deterministic**, and **reversible**.
- Prefer “how to verify” sections over deep internals; customers need confidence that the setting is actually applied and understand when/why fallback happens.

payload.page_title: Docs Site: SDK release windows, canaries, and hotfix playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This page defines the operational pattern the Docs Site and SDK teams use for planned SDK releases, weekly docs site change windows, canary promotion, and expedited hotfixes. The goal is to minimize user-facing regressions, speed up critical fixes, and keep rollout telemetry auditable. This playbook is intended for library authors, Docs Site maintainers, DevX oncall, and Release Engineers.

When to follow this playbook

- Regular SDK releases (minor/patch) that change public APIs or default runtime behavior.
- Docs Site content or snippet changes that must be synchronized with an SDK release.
- Hotfixes that restore regressions in production (build failures, telemetry regressions, wrong default params).
- Emergency rollbacks when a release causes production errors exceeding alert thresholds.

Release cadence and windows

- Regular release window: Tuesdays 10:00–12:00 PT. Use this window for scheduled minor and patch SDK releases and docs content pushes.
- Docs-only window: Wednesdays 14:00–15:00 PT for non-SDK content updates that still require minimal review.
- Hotfix window: 24/7 — hotfixes may be requested outside scheduled windows but must follow the expedited verification checklist below.

Roles and responsibilities

- Release owner (library author): creates the release PR, runs preflight checks, and opens the rollout ticket.
- Docs Site owner (docs-maintainer): coordinates snippet updates, staging verification, and monitors site health dashboards.
- DevX oncall: monitors canary telemetry and approves promotion; executes rollback when thresholds are met.
- Release engineer: validates CI gates and can trigger the automated promotion pipeline.

Pre-release checklist (required before merging a release PR)

1) Update changelog and API compatibility note. Include the minimal reproduction for behavior changes.
2) Run the local integration matrix: node, python, and go SDK quickstart smoke tests (see sample commands below).
3) Run docs build: ensure snippet extraction and the docs site staging build succeed (docs build exit code == 0).
4) Verify telemetry: run unit and integration tests that exercised telemetry counters and ensure no new missing telemetry keys.
5) Attach a release ticket with: expected impact, canary group definition, and rollback plan.

Canary promotion flow (recommended for all production-impacting changes)

1) Create a canary release artifact tagged with the date and canary identifier (e.g., sdk-js@2.5.1-canary-20250212-rc1).
2) Stage docs site with canary artifact references in a per-canary branch of the staging site.
3) Run the canary smoke suite (minimum: 50 requests across the common endpoints, latency and correctness checks).
4) Monitor the following metrics for 30 minutes:
   - error_rate (requests with 5xx or SDK-level errors) < 0.5%
   - median_latency (p50) change <= +15% relative to baseline
   - token_cost_per_request change <= +30% relative to baseline (for generation endpoints)
   - golden_prompt_accuracy: local eval against 100 golden prompts must not regress >1% absolute
5) If all checks pass, request approval from DevX oncall and merge to main release track. Record approval in the release ticket.

Hotfix (expedited) flow

1) Triage: engineer files an incident ticket and labels it hotfix. Capture: failing endpoint, example request, last-good-artifact, and impact estimate (users/minute affected).
2) Create a hotfix branch off the last-good-artifact and implement the minimal change.
3) Run focused tests: the hotfix test suite must include the failure repro and must pass locally and in CI smoke.
4) Deploy to a canary cohort of 1% traffic for 10 minutes. If no new errors and all validation checks pass, incrementally increase to 10% for 20 minutes.
5) If at any point error_rate > 1% or latency p50 increases > 30% vs baseline, immediately rollback to last-good-artifact and escalate to Incident Commander.

Rollback procedure (when rolling back a failed release)

1) Post the rollback plan in the release ticket and on the incident channel.
2) Run the automated rollback pipeline to restore last-good-artifact.
3) Clear caches (docs snippet cache, CDN edge purge) where applicable.
4) Run post-rollback smoke checks and monitor metrics for 60 minutes.
5) Create a postmortem entry if rollback was performed (link the incident ticket).

Monitoring and SLOs for SDK and Docs changes

- Canary pass rate: target 99% pass for smoke checks prior to promotion.
- Production error rate SLO (post-release 6h window): increase in error_rate must be <= 0.25% absolute from baseline; otherwise trigger rollback.
- Docs build success: 100% during release window. Any docs build failures must block promotion.

Observability and dashboards to watch

- docs-site/staging-builds: build status, snippet-extraction errors, last successful build time.
- sdk/canary-health: error_rate, p50/p95 latencies, token_cost_per_request, golden_eval_regressions.
- synthetic/quickstarts: scheduled runs of the standard quickstarts (node, python, go) every 30 minutes.

Templates and sample commands

- Local quickstart smoke (Node):
  npm ci && npm run smoke -- --endpoint=https://staging.docs.redwood.ai --api-key=${API_KEY}

- Local quickstart smoke (Python):
  pip install -r requirements.txt && python smoke_quickstart.py --endpoint https://staging.docs.redwood.ai --api_key $API_KEY

- Example CI job snippet (concise):
  - name: SDK smoke tests
    run: |
      make smoke-node && make smoke-py && make docs-build

- Canary tagging convention: sdk-{lang}@{version}-canary-{YYYYMMDD}-{build}

Ownership matrix

- Release owner: SDK library team (primary)
- Docs maintenance: Docs Site engineering (primary), DevX (secondary)
- Oncall verification: DevX oncall (primary)
- Rollback execution: Release engineering (primary)

Post-release responsibilities and runbook triggers

- 0–6 hours after release: active monitoring window. Oncall checks dashboards every 15 minutes.
- If error_rate breach occurs: trigger rollback runbook and create an incident ticket.
- >6 hours and <72 hours: monitoring at 1-hour cadence; file a regression ticket if behavioral regressions are observed.

Common pitfalls and canonical fixes

- Problem: snippets in docs reference unreleased helper APIs.
  Fix: add feature gates to the staging build and keep snippet references behind canary tags until SDK promotion.
- Problem: CI passes locally but fails in docs build due to missing environment variables.
  Fix: use the standardized docs stub env and add a gating CI job that runs the docs build with secrets masked.
- Problem: golden prompt regressions aren’t caught until late.
  Fix: add a lightweight golden set for each SDK and run a differential eval in the canary stage.

Appendix: example changelog template

- Title: sdk-{lang} v{major}.{minor}.{patch} — YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: One-line summary of impact.
- Notable changes:
  - Breaking changes: list and migration steps
  - Bug fixes: list of tickets and short descriptions
  - Docs changes: list of pages/snippets updated

Troubleshooting checklist (quick)

1) If docs site staging build fails: check snippet-extraction logs, missing env, and plugin versions.
2) If canary shows increased latency: check kernel selection logs, batching metrics, and upstream model variant routing.
3) If golden accuracy regresses: revert the SDK change and re-run local evals; open an evaluation ticket with the Research Applied ML team.

Contact and escalation

- Primary Slack channel: #devx-release-ops
- Oncall rotation: see /confluence/eng-developer-experience/oncall-and-rotations (link)
- Pager: DevX oncall; Release engineering backup: release@redwood.ai

Change history

- 2024-11-14: Initial draft by Lena Zhou.
- 2025-01-22: Added golden eval thresholds and updated canary timing (Ethan Garcia).
- 2025-02-12: Clarified rollback metrics and added docs-only window (Priya Menon).

payload.page_title: SDK Streaming and Network Simulator Playbook

sections.body: Overview
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This playbook documents an engineer-focused, reproducible local sandbox and network simulation workflow for developing, testing, and debugging Redwood SDKs and API integrations that use streaming, retries, and stateful token-level behavior. It prescribes a lightweight toolchain, canonical examples (Python + Node + curl), CI test harness patterns, and an incident remediation checklist aimed at reducing flakiness in SDK behavior and protecting downstream consumers from regressions.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Provide a repeatable local environment that simulates realistic network conditions (latency, jitter, packet loss) while preserving streaming semantics.
- Offer canonical SDK examples for streaming, chunked responses, and function/tool-calling fallbacks.
- Define CI patterns and synthetic tests to catch common regressions (partial streams, duplicate messages, connection resets).
- Document recommended timeouts, backoff strategies, and SDK-level telemetry points.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body: - SDK maintainers, runtime engineers, developer-experience engineers, and platform integrators.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- Covers the Redwood public REST/SDK streaming flows and the developer-facing SDKs (Python, Node). Does NOT cover Dedicated or Private deployment packaging specifics beyond network differences.

Prerequisites
- Docker (>= 24.0) and docker-compose
- Python 3.10+ with virtualenv support and Node 18+
- access to Redwood dev API key (redwood-dev-*), or a local mock credential for offline mode

Quickstart: Local sandbox with streaming + network simulator
1) Clone the devx-sim repo (internal): git clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-devx-sim.git
2) Start sandbox (single command): docker compose up --build
   - Services started: redwood-mock-api (HTTP + SSE), netem-proxy (Toxiproxy wrapper), sandbox-ui (optional)

3) Configure your client to point at sandbox endpoints:
   - REST endpoint: http://localhost:8080/v1
   - SSE/streaming endpoint: http://localhost:8080/v1/stream
   - Env example (.env.local):
     REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080
     REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-test-key

Canonical examples (snippets)
- Python streaming (requests + SSE parsing):

  import os
  import requests
  from sseclient import SSEClient

  url = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_BASE') + '/v1/stream/generate'
  headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}
  resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True)
  client = SSEClient(resp)
  for event in client.events():
      if event.event == 'message':
          print(event.data)
      elif event.event == 'done':
          break

- Node streaming (fetch + server-sent events via eventsource-js):

  const EventSource = require('eventsource');
  const es = new EventSource('http://localhost:8080/v1/stream/generate', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer local-test-key' } });
  es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('chunk', e.data);
  es.addEventListener('done', () => es.close());

- curl (quick smoke):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer local-test-key" http://localhost:8080/v1/stream/generate -N

Network simulation matrix
- Use the netem-proxy service to alter conditions. The table below is a recommended baseline for tests to include in PR checks:

  | Test name                 | Latency | Jitter | Loss | Reorders | Purpose |
  |--------------------------|---------|--------|------|----------|---------|
  | stable-low-latency       | 10ms    | 2ms    | 0%   | 0%       | fast-path validation
  | high-latency             | 200ms   | 20ms   | 0%   | 0%       | latency-sensitive timeouts
  | intermittent-loss        | 50ms    | 10ms   | 2%   | 0%       | small packet loss handling
  | burst-loss               | 120ms   | 30ms   | 10%  | 5%       | simulate flaky mobile networks
  | reorder-and-jitter       | 80ms    | 80ms   | 0%   | 3%       | ordering and partial-chunk handling

Timeouts, batching, backoff (recommended defaults)
- Use these as starting points in SDKs and allow overrides via client config. Add to SDK docs as parameterized examples.

  | Component          | Default     | Rationale |
  |-------------------|-------------|-----------|
  | connectionTimeout | 10s         | connection establishment under load
  | readTimeout       | 60s (streaming) | long-running streams can be open, but SDK should use heartbeat enforcement
  | requestTimeout    | 120s        | overall request cap for heavy generation
  | maxBatchTokens    | 2048        | default batching to avoid OOMs on 16GB GPU nodes
  | retryBackoffBase  | 200ms       | jittered exponential backoff base
  | retryMaxAttempts  | 5           | covers transient infra failures

CI test harness recommendations
1) Unit tests: isolate serializer, chunk-merger, and retry/backoff logic. Use fake SSE stream generator.
2) Integration tests (job): run two matrix entries: stable-low-latency and intermittent-loss. Assert: no duplicate chunks, final "done" event received, and stream ordering preserved.
3) E2E smoke (gated): one high-latency run against stage-orange (hosted test shard) to validate server-induced delays.
4) Flakiness budget: allow up to 1 flaky run / 100 CI runs; exceed triggers flakiness investigation.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d netem-proxy redwood-mock-api
  export REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8080
  pytest tests/integration/test_streaming.py::test_stream_resilience --maxfail=1 -q

Telemetry and logging guidance
- Emit these SDK-level metrics (tag by client_id and model):
  - stream_open_count (counter)
  - stream_close_count (counter)
  - stream_chunk_bytes (histogram)
  - stream_error_rate (counter + labels: error_type)
  - reconnect_attempts (counter)

- Log shape: JSON lines with these top-level fields: timestamp, client_id, model, request_id, event (open|chunk|error|close), chunk_index, chunk_size, latency_ms, netem_profile. Include sample log line in docs.

Common failure modes and canonical fixes
- Duplicate chunk ingestion:
  - Symptom: consumer observes identical text chunk twice after a reconnect.
  - Cause: server replay + client naive dedupe by content only.
  - Fix: SDK should attach and persist monotonic sequence tokens per stream (sequence_id + offset) and dedupe by (request_id, sequence_id, offset). If sequence metadata missing, fall back to content hashing with sliding window.

- Premature stream close on network blip:
  - Symptom: stream closes with HTTP 499 or socket reset during long generation.
  - Fix: implement soft-reconnect with resume token. Server supports resume token header X-Resume-Token. SDK steps:
    1) On transient network error, attempt_resume = true if resume token present.
    2) Reconnect with header X-Resume-Token: <token> and request resume range.

- Partial JSON messages (chunk boundary splits):
  - Symptom: JSON decoder failure in consumer when a JSON object is split across chunks.
  - Fix: SDK should buffer incomplete frames and only parse after assemble. Provide tolerant parser that recovers from trailing commas and whitespace.

Troubleshooting checklist (Dev-on-call)
1) Reproduce locally using netem profile matching incident.
2) Capture wiretrace (curl -v and tcpdump) and SDK logs.
3) Validate server-side: check request_id, model shard and kv-cache usage.
4) Run checksum of chunks to detect replays/duplicates.
5) If resume tokens were used, verify server accepted resume header.

Docs-site operating procedure for examples and code snippets
- All SDK code snippets in docs must be runnable with a single script in the devx-sim repo. For each docs change that touches code samples:
  - Add an integration test under examples/ that executes the snippet in CI container.
  - Update the snippet’s test-case id in examples/index.yml used by docs build.
  - Warnings: avoid auth leakage — use environment variable placeholders in docs.

Ownership, escalation, and SLAs
- Owners: devx-sdk-team (primary), serving-runtime-team (secondary for server resume/token issues).
- Pager: devx-sdk-oncall rotation; escalate to runtime on-call if server-side resume tokens or kernel-level OOMs suspected.
- Target triage time for production incidents: 30 minutes.

Change log
- 2025-11-20: initial draft with sandbox blueprint and netem-profiles.
- 2026-01-12: added resume token and dedupe guidance after incident INC-2026-0011.
- 2026-02-10: published: added CI job templates and telemetry guidance.

Appendix: Helpful commands
- Start sandbox: docker compose up --build
- Toggle netem profile: curl -X POST http://localhost:8474/profiles -d '{"profile":"burst-loss"}'
- Dump SSE traffic: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer local-test-key" http://localhost:8080/v1/stream/generate -v -N > /tmp/trace.sse

Related pages and references
- See SDK retry/backoff standards (link in related_pages) and runtime resume token spec (internal RFC link).

Contact
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.com)
- DevX Slack: #devx-sdk

payload.page_title: Onboarding Samples & Runtime Accelerator for SDKs

sections.body:
OVERVIEW

Short intro: This page centralizes the "Runtime Accelerator" sample library and onboarding playbook for SDK authors and integrators. It bundles compact, runnable examples (embed-first, generation-first, streaming, and hybrid), publishing and review controls for docs site owners, and a canonical triage map for the top 8 support issues encountered during early SDK adoption.

GOALS
- Reduce time-to-first-success for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs from days to under 2 hours.
- Provide deterministic examples that exercise production runtime features: batching, streaming, KV cache reuse, and error-handling.
- Standardize doc publishing and golden-trace validation so examples stay runnable across runtime releases.

AUDIENCE
- SDK engineers (maintainers and contributors)
- Developer advocates and DX writers
- Solutions engineers onboarding customers

SCOPE & COMPONENTS
1) Sample Library (runnable artifacts)
   - sample-embed-pipeline: small Go + Py examples showing embedding batching and sparse caching.
   - sample-gen-stream: Node + Python streaming example with reconnection and resume tokens.
   - sample-hybrid-search-gen: full end-to-end sample combining embeddings -> reranker -> generator.
2) Quickstart playbooks (this doc)
3) Validation harness: golden traces and CI job definitions (docs-ci/golden-trace-runner)
4) Support canonical fixes mapping

HOW TO USE (QUICKSTARTS)
- Quickstart: minimal generator (Python)
  1. pip install redwood-sdk==2.1.0
  2. export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
  3. python -c "from redwood import Client; c=Client(); print(c.generate('Write a haiku about caching'))"

- Streaming reconnect snippet (Node)
  - key steps:
    1) subscribe to event stream
    2) buffer partial chunks with idempotency token
    3) on disconnect, resume using stream_resume_token
  - sample snippet:
    const c = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
    const res = await c.streamGenerate({ prompt: 'Explain prefix caching', stream: true, resumeToken: lastToken });

PUBLISHING WORKFLOW FOR SAMPLES (docs-site owners)
1. Author creates PR against docs repo and attaches: sample code, Dockerfile (if applicable), and a small smoke test (run-local.sh).
2. CI runs: unit tests, golden-trace runner, and container build smoke.
3. Reviewer (DX writer + SDK maintainer) signs off. Required labels: docs-sample, smoke-tested.
4. Merge window: weekday 09:00–17:00 UTC; if merging outside window, notify #devx-channel.
5. Post-merge: automated job deploys sample to staging and validates canonical traces for latest runtime tag.

GOLDEN TRACE CONTRACTS
| sample | inputs | stable fields | acceptable delta |
| sample-gen-stream | prompt sized 8–128 tokens | token-sequence, complete flag | +/- 2 tokens on final chunk |
| sample-embed-pipeline | 10 short docs | embedding L2-norm | < 0.05 change per model minor bump |

DOCS SLOs & OWNER METRICS
- Example run success rate >= 98% in staging (CI-run) per release.
- Sample smoke time < 90s on standard CI runner (2 vCPU, 8GB RAM).
- Ownership: docs-site engineering (primary), eng-devx (secondary). Contact: samira.patel@redwood.ai

CANONICAL SUPPORT ISSUE MAP (Top 8) — triage + fix
1) Symptom: SDK install fails on Python 3.11 with wheel errors.
   - Cause: missing manylinux wheel for new build; CI omitted universal wheel step.
   - Fix: Add manylinux2014 wheel build target; publish artifact and bump docs with compatibility note.
2) Symptom: Streaming reconnect resumes duplicate tokens.
   - Cause: server-side resume idempotency token mismatch when client retries without checkpointing.
   - Fix: Example updated to persist last_resume_token and deduplicate partial buffers in client.
3) Symptom: Embeddings drift after quantized model upgrade.
   - Cause: incompatible quantization profile in runtime-config.
   - Fix: Add a compatibility shim and note to release notes + recommended profile mapping table.
(remaining items summarized for brevity in doc; full canonical-fixes list maintained in repo under /support/canonical-fixes)

RELEASE-CONTROLLED CONFIG SNIPPET
{
  "sample_ci": "golden-trace-runner: v1",
  "runtime_profile": "embeddings-stable-v2",
  "smoke_timeout": "90s",
  "maintainers": "eng-devx"
}

LOCAL DEBUG & EMULATION
- To run locally: repo contains run-local.sh, which launches a lightweight emulation container (uses runtime-stub:0.3). Example:
  ./run-local.sh sample-gen-stream --env-file .env.local
- Telemetry: enable DEBUG_SAMPLE=1 to surface per-sample telemetry to stdout; do not commit local .env files.

ESCALATION FOR UNRESOLVED SAMPLE FAILURES
1. If CI golden-trace failure persists for > 3 consecutive runs, create a ticket in the docs-support queue and @mention SDK oncall.
2. Attach CI logs, sample id, runtime tag, and the failing golden trace.
3. Oncall process:
   a. confirm whether change originated in runtime or docs.
   b. if runtime: open incident runbook and follow runtime rollback steps.
   c. if docs: revert the sample or patch immediately with smoke test.

MAINTENANCE & ROTATION
- Owners must review each sample on major runtime release or every 6 months, whichever comes first.
- Deprecated samples: add label deprecated-sample and move code to /archive with README describing reason.

RELATED LINKS
- SDK repo: https://git.redwood.ai/sdk
- Golden-trace runner: https://git.redwood.ai/docs-ci/golden-trace-runner
- Support canonical fixes: https://git.redwood.ai/support/canonical-fixes

APPENDIX: CHECKLIST FOR NEW SAMPLE SUBMISSION
1. runnable in CI with a 90s smoke test
2. contains README with expected outputs and golden trace
3. has small deterministic input set
4. includes owner and maintainer contact
5. labeled and linked in this doc

payload.page_title: Quickstart Templates: Docs Information Architecture (IA) Update Proposal

sections.body:
This page proposes an information architecture update to integrate **Quickstart Templates** (RAG + agents) into the Redwood docs in a way that:
- Reduces time-to-first-success for PLG engineers.
- Makes templates discoverable from SDK and API reference pages.
- Clearly explains the difference between **Hosted**, **Dedicated**, and **Private** deployments without duplicating large parts of product documentation.
- Establishes a durable pattern for versioning (latest vs pinned) and template maintenance.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
1) Where templates live in the docs nav
2) The page structure and cross-linking strategy
3) How deployment-mode guidance is presented (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
4) Migration plan and ownership

---
sections.heading: This proposal covers

sections.body:
- **Discoverability:** Templates should be reachable within 1–2 clicks from the docs homepage and directly from SDK docs.
- **Clarity:** Users should immediately understand: “Is this a tutorial? an example? a production-ready scaffold?”
- **Low duplication:** Keep Hosted/Dedicated/Private details canonical in product docs; templates should link out and only include delta guidance.
- **Operational readiness:** Observability, safe defaults, and troubleshooting should be first-class in IA (not buried).
- **Version integrity:** Docs should make it obvious which template version a walkthrough corresponds to, and how to get updates.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Rewriting the entire docs homepage IA.
- Creating separate docs sets per language; language selection should be consistent and lightweight.
- Documenting every deployment provider recipe (Fly/Render/K8s/etc.) as first-class docs pages in v1; we will link to repo recipes.
