payload.page_title: Integrated Career & Operations Handbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
- This handbook consolidates core company-handbook guidance that spans working at Redwood, early-career ladders, benefits enrollment, hiring and onboarding patterns, and the practical mapping of internal tools required for day-to-day work.
- It is designed for new hires, managers, and people-ops partners as a single, prescriptive reference for the first 12 months of employment and for career progression planning.

How to use this document
- Read sections relevant to your role: new hires should start with the 'FastStart' onboarding checklist; managers should review the 'Manager Welcome Kit' and 'Role Sprint' guidance.
- Use the tables and checklists as templates during hiring, onboarding, and L&D conversations.

1. Working at Redwood: Principles and Norms
- Developer-first, production-first culture: prioritize shipping reliably and iterating with data.
- Asynchronous-first communication: explicit expectations for written status, pull request (PR) etiquette, and meeting hygiene.
- Career conversations occur quarterly in IC/manager 1:1s and formally twice per year at checkpoints.

Core norms
1) Psychological safety: encourage questions and signal when things are experimental.
2) Shared ownership: teams own product metrics, SLOs, and operational runbooks.
3) Iterative learning: use retros and experiments to reduce risk.

2. Career Pathways and the Role Sprint Framework
Introduction
- Redwood organizes growth around repeatable, time-boxed "Role Sprints" that combine milestones, skill objectives, and measurable outputs over a 6–12 month cadence. Role Sprints reduce ambiguity and help managers and ICs plan promotions, learning investments, and cross-team moves.

Role Sprint components (required)
- Title & Level objective: succinct statement of expected scope (e.g., "Senior Backend Engineer: owns public API performance for model serving").
- Impact outcomes (3 max): measurable product or operational outcomes.
- Skill checkpoints: core competencies with concrete evidence (code review leadership, architecture decisions, incident response).
- Stretch goal: learning objective aligned to career next-step.
- Success criteria: quantitative and qualitative signals for promotion or completion.

Procedure: running a Role Sprint (numbered steps)
1. Manager and IC draft the Sprint at the quarterly growth sync.
2. Agree on 3 impact outcomes and one stretch goal; record in the personal role-sprint doc.
3. Schedule monthly check-ins and a final review; update evidence in the shared career folder.
4. If outcomes are met early, propose a new Sprint or a calibrated promotion packet.

Example: Role Sprint snapshot
| Field | Example |
| Title | Staff ML Engineer (inference runtime) |
| Impact outcomes | 1) Reduce 95th percentile latency by 20% on two production models. 2) Ship continuous batching feature with documentation. 3) Own post-deploy performance regression plan. |
| Skill checkpoints | Performance tuning, cross-team leadership, PR -> architecture doc authorship |
| Stretch goal | Give internal performance benchmarking talk and mentor two juniors |

3. Hiring & Onboarding: FastStart vs DeepStart
Intro
- We operate two prescriptive onboarding tracks based on role complexity: FastStart (1–6 weeks) for contributor roles with small surface area and DeepStart (6–12 weeks) for cross-functional or platform-heavy roles.

FastStart checklist (for contributors)
1. Pre-start: account provisioning (Okta, GitHub, Slack), hardware request, and first-week calendar sent.
2. Day 1: team welcome, key docs, product overview, and immediate access to staging.
3. Week 1: shadowing sessions, first small PR, internal-tools walkthrough.
4. Week 2–4: ownership of a small bug/feature, first oncall shadow session.

DeepStart checklist (for platform, infra, SRE, product leads)
1. Pre-start: environment mirror setup (local infra VM), extended playbook access, and security brief.
2. Weeks 1–3: cross-team onboarding rotations, architecture deep-dive, observability and runbook access, and test harness setup.
3. Weeks 4–8: lead a small cross-team integration, author runbook addendum, and present a 30-minute tech review.

Standard onboarding deliverables (templates included)
- 30/60/90 day plan (template linked in related pages).
- First deliverable: production-validated PR or runbook contribution.
- Onboarding feedback survey at day 30 and day 90.

4. Benefits & Perks: Enrollment, Checkpoints, and Tips
Enrollment timeline (important dates)
- Day 0–30: automatic invite to benefits portal, default health coverage enrollment window = 30 days.
- Day 31–60: retirement plan auto-enrollment options and meetings with benefits specialist.
- Quarterly: cafeteria-style perks refresh and stipend reauthorization windows.

Quick reference table: major benefits
| Benefit | Enrollment window | Owner/contact |
| Health (medical/dental/vision) | 0–30 days | benefits@redwood.com |
| Retirement (401k / pension) | 0–60 days | finance-benefits@redwood.com |
| Parental leave | Plan at hire; claims after 1 year service | people-ops-leave@redwood.com |
| Hybrid office stipend | Quarterly claim window | ops@redwood.com |

Tips and edge cases
- If you miss the initial 30-day window for health, submit an exception request to people-ops with reason and supporting docs.
- For international hires, country-specific benefits are handled by the local HR lead; refer to the country benefits matrix on the benefits portal.

5. Internal Tools and Access Matrix
Purpose
- Map tools to role owner, access level, and onboarding touchpoint. Keep this matrix updated; it is the authoritative source for access onboarding.

Access matrix (excerpt)
| Tool | Purpose | Default access (new hire) | Manager action required | Onboarding touchpoint |
| Okta | SSO / identity | Provisioned automatically | None | Pre-start email |
| GitHub (org) | Code & PRs | Write access for engineers | Add to org team | Day 1 walkthrough |
| Datadog | Observability & traces | Read for most engineers | Request additional roles | Week 1 observability session |
| GCP Projects | Deploy & infra | No access by default | Request via infra-reqs ticket | DeepStart week 1 |

Self-service CLI examples (copy/paste)
- Request infra project access:
  rdo infra-reqs create --project inference-staging --reason "Sprint work" --approver @infra-oncall
- Create onboarding ticket (people-ops):
  rdo people-ops ticket create --template onboarding --new-hire "Full Name" --start-date 2026-02-15

6. Manager Welcome Kit (30/60/90 for managers)
Manager 30-day priorities
1. Complete manager orientation and legal training.
2. Meet direct reports (1:1s), set initial expectations, and review each direct report's latest role-sprint document.
3. Validate team access matrix and unblock any provisioning.

Manager 60-day priorities
1. Run first performance checkpoint conversations and schedule career check-ins.
2. Ensure team has runbooks for top 3 production services and that oncall rotation is staffed.

Manager 90-day priorities
1. Complete first hiring calibration and interview loop if open roles exist.
2. Create a resourcing and upskilling plan for the next 6 months.

Checklist: new manager handoff
- Confirm org chart and direct-report list.
- Review all open PRs and outstanding incidents.
- Get read-access to the staffing and budget dashboard.

7. Policies, Exceptions, and Escalations
- Role-expense approvals: managers can approve up to $1,500 without VP sign-off. Anything above requires finance-legal review.
- Benefit exceptions: people-ops will adjudicate on a case-by-case basis; typical response time = 7 business days.
- Access exceptions for contractors: require sponsor and infra approval; all exceptions must be time-limited.

Escalation paths (quick)
1. Access/inventory issue -> manager -> people-ops -> infra.
2. Payroll/compensation issue -> payroll -> finance -> people-ops.
3. Security incident involving PII -> security -> legal -> incident-response channel.

8. Ownership and Contacts
- People Ops (owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits specialist: benefits@redwood.com
- Talent & hiring: hiring-team@redwood.com
- Internal tools (oncall): infra-tools@redwood.com

9. Appendix: Templates and Evidence
- 30/60/90 day plan (template): copy to personal folder and share with manager.
- Role-sprint template: link to internal template repo and example.
- Onboarding feedback form: send at day 30 and day 90; people-ops triages results monthly.

Revision history

- 2026-02-10: Added Role Sprint examples and DeepStart checklist after people-ops review.
- 2026-03-01: Finalized manager kit and access matrix; published.

payload.page_title: alert-fatigue-tuning-through-telemetry-deduplication-retrospective

sections.body:
Summary:
This retrospective documents a 10-week experiment (Jul 2025–Sep 2025) where the Platform Observability team applied telemetry-level deduplication and alert grouping to reduce oncall operator cognitive load and alert fatigue. The experiment targeted token-cost, prefix-cache, and tail-latency alerts for multi-tenant LLM inference services. We achieved a 48% reduction in mean-page-rate for platform operators and a 22% improvement in median time-to-action for prioritized incidents.

Context and motivation:
- Background: In H1 2025 we observed rising alert volumes correlated with (a) increased multitenant traffic, (b) higher prefix-cache churn from cache-pinning experiments, and (c) more granular SLI decomposition for token-cost attribution.
- Problem statement: Operators were routinely paged for symptom-level signals (e.g., bursty token-cost deltas, cache eviction churn, per-tenant latency spikes) without an upstream signal tying these to a single root cause. Result: fatigue, slower triage, and blocked customer-facing rollouts.
- Goal: Reduce irrelevant/duplicate alerts by 40% while preserving N-of-1 detection (i.e., still detect real degradations for small-but-critical tenants).

Experiment design (10 weeks):
1) Week 0–2: Baseline collection. We instrumented alert streams and captured pages, tags, and runbook usage.
2) Week 3–6: Deploy telemetry deduplication and grouping rules in the alert router.
3) Week 7–9: Runbook and dashboard changes + targeted operator training.
4) Week 10: Measure outcomes and capture retrospective notes.

What we changed (technical summary):
- Telemetry deduplication layer (Alert Router v2):
  - New pre-filter: dedupe_by_key = [region, tenant_id, model_variant_family, root_cause_hash]
  - Grouping window: 90s for symptom grouping; 10m for cascade grouping.
  - Suppression policy: keep highest-severity alert, suppress duplicates with same root_cause_hash for 15m.
- Root-cause hash derivation: deterministic hash over (top_N_span_tags, failing_component, dominating_metric). Example: sha256(span_tags|component|metric_bucket).
- Alert lifecycle enrichment: enriched alerts now contain a compact causal context (3 fields): probable_cause, affected_tenants_sample, suggested_runbook_link.
- Dashboard changes: created a dedup-aware timeline panel and a grouped incident view.

Concrete rules and examples:
- Prometheus alert example (pre-change):
  ALERT MultiTenant_TokenCost_Surge
  IF increase(token_cost_total[5m]) > 1000 by (tenant_id)
  FOR 2m
  LABELS {severity="warning"}

- Alert Router dedupe policy pseudocode:
  dedupe_key = f"{region}|{tenant_id if single-tenant else 'multi'}|{model_family}|{top_span_tag}"
  if recent_alerts.exists(dedupe_key, window=90s):
    attach_to_existing(alert)
  else:
    route_new(alert)

- Example root_cause_hash derivation (shell pseudo):
  printf "%s|%s|%s" "$top_span" "$component" "$metric_bucket" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12

Metrics collected (baseline vs experiment):
| Metric | Baseline (weekly avg) | Experiment (weekly avg) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pages per oncall shift | 76 | 39 | -48% |
| Distinct incidents (grouped) | 18 | 16 | -11% |
| Mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) | 4.8 min | 3.2 min | -33% |
| Median time to remediation | 22 min | 17 min | -23% |
| False-positive pages (ops adjudicated) | 29% | 12% | -17pp |

Findings and tradeoffs:
- Positive:
  - Significant reduction in noise: operators received fewer low-information pages and had higher confidence in each page's signal.
  - Faster initial triage: grouping reduced duplicate investigations across regional operators.
  - Cost savings: fewer unnecessary escalations and less context-switching; estimated saving ~0.9 FTE-equivalent of operator time/year.
- Negative / risk areas:
  - Rare single-tenant regressions were at risk of being grouped under multi-tenant noise. Mitigation: we added tenant-priority exemptions and a per-tenant safety window (see configuration table).
  - Initial complexity: root_cause_hash generation required careful normalization of span tags; incorrect normalization produced under-grouping.

Operator workflow changes (short):
1. New incident card contains: grouped-alert-id, root_cause_hash, confidence_score, suggested_next_step.
2. Operator verifies grouping by inspecting affected_tenants_sample (first 5 tenants) and the timeline panel.
3. If grouping hides a critical tenant, operator clicks "escalate-single-tenant" which creates an immediate new high-priority incident scoped to that tenant.

Configuration and safety table:
| Setting | Default | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| grouping.window.symptom | 90s | Groups rapid duplicate pages from the same problem | Observability SRE |
| grouping.window.cascade | 10m | Aggregate cascading events into a single incident | Observability SRE |
| suppression.duration.same_root | 15m | Prevent alert storms during noisy recoveries | Observability SRE |
| tenant_priority_exemptions | [enterprise-tier tenants] | Always create distinct incidents for these tenants | Platform Ops |
| per-tenant-safety-window | 5m | Allow early re-surface for high-priority tenants | Platform Ops |

Dashboards and alerting changes (deployment checklist):
1. Deploy Alert Router v2 to staging and enable dedupe=false flag. Run in shadow mode for 48h.
2. Switch on dedupe=true in one regional alert-router (canary). Monitor pages and error rates for 72h.
3. Add "grouped incident" panel to oncall dashboard and validate with two simulated incidents.
4. Promote to all regions and enable tenant-priority exemptions.

Runbook updates (high-level):
- Token-cost surge runbook: add Section 2 showing how to interpret grouped incidents and a button to expand per-tenant view.
- Cache-eviction runbook: include troubleshooting matrix for prefix-cache churn and root_cause_hash examples.
- Tail-latency runbook: define decomposed steps to verify whether grouped alert is region-specific or model-family-wide.

Lessons learned and recommended next steps:
- Always normalize span/tag values before hashing; build a shared normalization library used by instrumentation and alert router.
- Move from hard suppression durations to adaptive suppression: increase suppression during ongoing mitigation and reduce after confirming recovery.
- Improve runbook UX: quick-expand controls that show all suppressed duplicates without needing to open multiple incidents.
- Roll tenant-priority exemptions into billing/SLAs to ensure operational visibility matches business impact.
- Run additional experiments on dedupe thresholds: compare 30s/90s/3m symptom windows for different workload profiles.

Appendix: example queries and scripts
- Grafana grouped timeline (Flux-like pseudocode):
  SELECT time_bucket(1m, event_time) as t, count(distinct root_cause_hash) FROM alerts WHERE environment='prod' AND region='us-west-2' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC

- Example alert router health check (curl):
  curl -sS -XGET http://alert-router.prod.svc/health | jq

- Python snippet: root_cause_hash normalization
  def normalize_span(span):
      # drop numeric ids, trim long tags, lowercase
      out = span.lower()
      out = re.sub(r"tenant_[0-9]+", "tenant", out)
      out = re.sub(r"\b0x[0-9a-f]+\b", "hexid", out)
      return out[:256]

Ownership and follow-ups:
- Action owners:
  - Observability SRE (Diego Alvarez): finalize normalization library and land tooling for root_cause_hash audit.
  - Platform Ops (Priya Nair): extend tenant-priority exemption list and define billing-linked priority table.
  - DX (Maya Chen): update runbooks and oncall dashboard panels.
- Follow-up milestones:
  - Q1 2026: migrate normalization library into telemetry SDK (owner: Observability SRE).
  - 2026-02: run 12-week adaptive dedupe pilot on bursty workloads (owner: Platform Ops).

Appendix B: links and references
- Implementation PRs and runbook diffs: (internal links to repo/PRs)
- Related Confluence pages: fractional-alerting-and-noise-reduction-strategy-2025 (see related_pages)

End of document.

payload.page_title: Path to Impact: New Hire 120-Day Ops & Benefit Orientation

sections.body:
Summary

This playbook provides a practical, step-by-step 120-day onboarding and benefits orientation for new hires at Redwood Inference. It balances immediate operational access, early contribution goals, and benefit enrollment milestones so that new teammates reach sustained impact quickly and with clarity. This page is intended for new hires, hiring managers, people-ops, and assigned buddies.

Who should use this

- New hires entering any technical or cross-functional role.
- Hiring managers coordinating a new hire’s ramp.
- People-ops and IT teams provisioning access and benefits.
- Assigned buddies and mentors who will guide day-to-day integration.

Quick start checklist (first 48 hours)

1) Complete HR welcome form and benefits pre-enrollment.
2) Verify Okta SSO account and set MFA (Authenticator + recovery email).
3) Join core Slack channels: #all, #team-announce, #engineering-ops (or product equivalent).
4) Claim GitHub account and accept org invitation (organization: redwood-inference).
5) Access Confluence and complete the "New Hire Acknowledgements" page.
6) Meet your manager and buddy for a 30-minute kickoff meeting.

First-Week Objectives (days 1–7)

- Administrative: Confirm payroll, health plan enrollment window, and expense policy understanding. Benefits enrollment deadline is 30 days from start date; action required via the People Ops portal.
- Operational: Confirm access to developer tools (GitHub, CI/CD pipeline, internal artifact store), communication tools (Slack, Email), and ticketing (Jira).
- Social: 2 x 1:1 scheduled with cross-functional partners (security, infra, product) and a team intro meeting.
- Learning: Complete the "Security & Data Handling for New Hires" micro-course (approx 90 minutes).

Typical 120-day plan (high-level goals)

Week 1: Setup and context
- Gain required access and complete required trainings.
- Deliver a short "Intro & Goals" doc in Confluence for your manager and buddy.

Weeks 2–4: Small, meaningful contributions
- Own a small ticket/bug or documentation improvement that touches production code or customer docs.
- Demonstrate end-to-end flow: from issue to code to CI to deployment preview.

Months 2–3 (days 31–90): Expand scope
- Drive a cross-team micro-project (e.g., infra monitoring rule, a reproducible integration test, or a product small feature).
- Complete role-specific competency checkpoints (see Role Ladder Summary below).

Months 3–4 (days 91–120): Sustainable ownership
- Transition at least one operational task or area to stable ownership.
- Present a 15-minute "What I shipped" demo in the team retro and capture learnings in Confluence.

Role Ladder Summary (concise guidance)

- IC-1 (Associate): Focus on learning systems, shipping small changes, and addressing code review feedback.
- IC-2 (Engineer): Own feature slices, mentor interns/juniors, and begin owning SLIs for a service.
- IC-3 (Senior): Drive architecture choices, own large cross-cutting projects, and coach peers.
- Staff+ (Principal/Staff): Define roadmaps, represent the company externally, and lead multi-team programs.

Each role ladder includes competency milestones for technical deliverables, cross-team collaboration, impact metrics, and mentoring responsibilities. For detailed competency rubrics, see the related role pages in the Roles & Career space.

Benefits orientation (what to prioritize and how to enroll)

- Health & Dental: Enrollment window is 30 days from start date. Action steps: Log into People Ops portal -> Benefits -> Enroll. Keep receipts for any opt-out paperwork.
- 401(k): Enrollment available immediately; employer match vests over 12 months.
- Wellness stipend: Claim via expense portal (limit $200 / quarter).
- Parental leave & sabbatical: Review policy in Benefits space and discuss eligibility with People Ops for planning.

People Ops contact for benefits: benefits@redwood.com (response SLA: 2 business days).

Access Matrix (who to contact to get things done)

| Resource | Owner / Team | How to request | Expected SLA |
|---------|-------------|---------------|-------------|
| Okta / SSO | IT / People Ops | Auto-provision via offer letter; re-requests: it-requests@redwood.com | 4 business hours |
| GitHub org | Engineering Tools | Manager approves invite; toolchain@redwood.com for escalations | 1 business day |
| Jira project access | Eng Ops | Manager grant + jira-requests@redwood.com | 1 business day |
| Cloud dev environment | Infra | Infra runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking | 2 business days |
| Payroll and tax forms | Finance | Upload to People Ops portal -> Payroll | 3 business days |

Manager responsibilities (must do list)

- Provide a role-specific 120-day success plan within 48 hours of start.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 12 weeks, then switch cadence to biweekly unless mutually agreed.
- Assign a peer buddy and confirm at least two cross-team intros in week 1.
- Ensure the new hire has at least one scoped, ownerable task by the end of week 2.
- Run a 60-day feedback checkpoint and a 120-day review (documented in Confluence).

Buddy responsibilities (day-to-day support)

- Be the go-to person for quick questions about team conventions and tooling.
- Review the new hire’s first small PR and provide actionable feedback.
- Arrange a "Lunch & Learn" or pairing session in the first 30 days.

Hiring handoff checklist (recruiter -> manager -> people-ops)

1) Recruiter: Final offer package confirmed, candidate accepts, send offer metadata to People Ops (title, manager, start date, salary band).
2) Manager: Confirm onboarding buddy and initial 120-day goals.
3) People Ops: Kick off provisioning workflows, benefits pre-enroll email, and welcome calendar invites.
4) IT/Infra: Ensure required service quotas and sandbox access are available by day 1.

Example commands and templates

- Requesting an additional GitHub team: create a Jira ticket using the "Access Request" template with fields: username, team-name, justification.

- Quick CLI snippet to verify Okta session (for engineers):

  $ okta whoami
  email: asha.patel@redwood.com
  status: active

- Template: 120-day goal doc (copy into your team Confluence space)
  - Problem statement
  - Success metrics (quantitative if possible)
  - Key stakeholders and collaborators
  - Timeline and milestones

Operational excellence expectations

- New hires in engineering are expected to understand the team's SLIs within 60 days and to be able to run the standard profiling and local reproduction steps without assistance by day 90.
- Security & compliance trainings must be completed within 14 days of start; completion is required for continued access to production systems.

Escalations and critical contacts

- People Ops (benefits / payroll): benefits@redwood.com (SLA 2 business days)
- IT / Access escalations: it-requests@redwood.com (SLA 4 business hours)
- Security incident triage: security-oncall@redwood.com (pager: see Security oncall rota)

Frequently asked questions (short answers)

Q: How long until I can push to main?
A: No direct pushes to protected branches. New hires should open PRs and request at least one reviewer. Privileged write permissions are granted based on demonstrated review quality and tenure, typically after 90 days.

Q: Who signs me up for health/dental?
A: You enroll yourself via the People Ops portal; People Ops can assist if you miss the 30-day window.

Q: What should I prioritize in week 1?
A: Confirm access, meet your manager and buddy, and ship a small documentation or configuration change to learn the end-to-end flow.

Related documents and where to go next

- New hire orientation and tooling checklist (detailed): /confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024
- Role competency rubrics: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027
- Security & Data Handling training: /confluence/security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/security-training-required
- Benefits & policies main page: /confluence/company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks

Revision history

- 2023-06-15: Created by Asha Patel.
- 2024-07-12: Added Access Matrix and Manager responsibilities (review by Marcus Nguyen).
- 2024-11-10: Updated benefits enrollment timelines and SLAs.

sections.body:
Overview

This manual defines Redwood's cohort-based onboarding approach and the complementary role-activation process that ensures new contributors have the correct privileges, expectations, and growth touchpoints. It consolidates: working-at-Redwood orientation, role ladder activation, benefits signposting, hiring manager responsibilities, and the internal tools access matrix used by IT and People Ops.

Audience
- New joiners across engineering, product, and GTM functions joining cohort onboarding.
- Hiring managers, onboarding buddies, people-ops partners, and IT provisioning engineers.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable cohort experience that accelerates productive contribution within 30 days.
- Ensure role ladders and compensation/benefits visibility are clear by day 15.
- Prevent over- and under-provisioning by standardizing tool access per role and employment type.

Scope and exclusions
- Applies to full-time employees and long-term contractors (>6 months). Short-term contractors, interns, and externals follow the separate contractor onboarding matrix (see related pages).
- Does not replace role-specific technical onboarding delivered by teams (e.g., runtime onboarding, security orientation).

Cohort model (high level)
1. Cohort cadence: new cohorts start every Monday. For hires who join mid-week, assign them to the next cohort or run one-off expedited onboarding (manager decision).
2. Cohort size target: 6–20 contributors per cohort for best interaction.
3. Duration: 4-week orchestrated program with optional 8-week technical deep-dive tracks.
4. Delivery: blended — live orientation sessions (Zoom), recorded modules (LMS), and team-run role shadowing.

Week-by-week cohort outline
- Week 0 (Pre-boarding) — before start date:
  - HR sends employment packet and benefits portal link.
  - IT creates staged accounts in the provisioning queue and sends the new-joiner hardware survey.
  - People Ops assigns cohort number and Slack cohort channel (#cohort-YYMMDD).

- Week 1 — Foundations:
  - Day 1: Welcome session (People Ops) — company mission, values, benefits overview, basic security.
  - Day 2: Manager meeting — role context, 30/60/90 expectations.
  - Day 3: Tools orientation — GitHub, Jira, CI previews, and Redwood Console walkthrough.
  - End of week: Buddy check-in and first-week feedback form.

- Week 2 — Role and Team Integration:
  - Team-specific tech onboarding (data access requests if needed).
  - Role ladder & compensation Q&A (People Ops optional drop-in).
  - Shadowing and pairing assignments begin.

- Week 3 — Execution:
  - First small delivery (bug fix, doc contribution, simple eval).
  - Career conversation with manager to align ladders and growth goals.

- Week 4 — Calibration and Transition:
  - 30-day manager review (documented in People Ops system).
  - Add to continuous learning pathway and schedule 90-day checkpoints.

Role ladder activation process (step-by-step)
1. Role definition and offer: Recruiter confirms level (e.g., IC2, IC3, Manager1) in offer.
2. People Ops creates a role-activation record in HRIS with the level, base comp, and expected promotion horizon.
3. Manager and new hire complete the "Role Expectation Form" by day 7.
4. People Ops schedules a role-ladder orientation slot in week 2.
5. At day 30, manager records initial calibration: confirming level/expectations and scheduling a development plan if needed.

Hiring manager checklist (minimum responsibilities)
- Pre-boarding: confirm equipment and run a short team welcome note.
- Day 1: meet & set 30/60/90 goals in writing.
- Week 2: schedule role ladder Q&A and identify the first pairing partner.
- Day 30: complete the 30-day review and update People Ops.
- Day 90: deliver a competence calibration and identify promotion blockers or support needs.

Internal tools access matrix (standardized defaults)
Note: IT/Provisioning uses this table as the baseline. All requests that deviate must include manager approval and use the Access Exception form.

| System | Full-time Engineer | Product Manager | People Ops | Contractor (long-term) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GitHub (org) | write | write | read | write (limited repos) | Engineers get main repo access by default; contractors restricted to a single repo set. |
| Jira (standard) | write | write | admin | write | Product & Eng: access to private product boards; People Ops limited admin for HR-related projects. |
| Redwood Console (prod) | read | read | read | no | Prod write access requires SRE sign-off and approved RBAC ticket. |
| Internal Wiki | write | write | write | read | Editing rights for full-time staff. |
| Payroll/Benefits Portal | no | no | admin | no | People Ops handles benefits enrollment. |
| AWS Console (prod) | no | no | no | no | Accessed via bastion and approved requests; separate infra process. |

Provisioning SLA and ownership
- Target SLA for baseline provisioning (accounts, laptop, Slack): 5 business days before start date. For late hires this becomes 2 business days after request.
- IT Provisioning team owner: it-provisioning@redwood.internal (SLA owner).
- Escalation: if provisioning misses SLA, hiring manager escalates to People Ops partner and the onboarding program lead.

Benefits and perks signposting (what to expect in week 0–2)
- Benefits enrollment window opens on Day 1 and remains for 30 days. People Ops sends reminders on days 3, 10, and 20.
- Stipends (home-office, learning): auto-eligible after payroll activation; request through internal finance form.
- Parental and caregiver policies summarized with links in the LMS module.

Special cases and exceptions
- Remote-first hires across APAC/EU: tax and benefits packaging will differ; People Ops will provide a jurisdiction-specific packet within 48 hours of start.
- Senior hires (Director and above): many provisioning steps are manual (exec laptop prep, additional security briefings) — onboarding lead will create a bespoke checklist.

Onboarding feedback and metrics (how we measure success)
- Primary metrics: time-to-first-PR, 30-day self-reported readiness, manager 30-day rating (1–5).
- Target goals: 75% of cohorts hit time-to-first-PR within 21 days; average manager 30-day rating >= 4.0.
- Monthly retrospective: People Ops runs a 60-minute cohort retro and submits a short improvement plan.

Security & compliance requirements during onboarding
- All new joiners must complete the Secure SDL course within 7 days.
- MFA must be enabled on all accounts before any write-level repo access is granted.
- Contractors must sign the Contractor Data Protection Addendum before being granted access to internal datasets.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
- Role Expectation Form (Template): /templates/role-expectation-form.docx
- Access Exception Form: /forms/access-exception.pdf
- Cohort feedback survey (LMS): /lms/cohort-feedback
- First-30 Review form (People Ops system): /people-ops/30-day-review

payload.page_title: Tenant initialization and observability orchestration for VPC private deployments

sections.body:
Summary:
This guide describes the recommended operator-driven sequence for tenant initialization (first-boot and ongoing warmstarts) and the observability orchestration that must be applied for Redwood private VPC deployments. It consolidates the operator bundle (preflight, staged model warmstart, KV cache priming, and telemetry gating) into an auditable runbook so field operators and customer operators follow the same safe pattern.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce SLA risk and mean time to healthy (MTTH) for newly commissioned tenants in VPC/private deployments by providing a reproducible initialization flow and a mandatory observability contract.
- Scope: Applies to all private VPC customer installs and self-hosted operator handoffs where Redwood provides the operator bundle (control plane or delegated operator). This does not replace specific customer firewall or change control requirements.

Audience:
Primary: deployment engineers, field operators, customer NOC engineers. Secondary: SREs and product engineers involved in private deploy rollouts.

Owner and escalation:
- Document owner: Engineering — Private Deployments team
- Primary contact for approvals: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Escalation path: Operator on-call -> Private-deploy SRE -> Platform infra -> Product security if telemetry gating is blocked

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Healthy tenant ready to serve production traffic with validated latency SLOs and telemetry within 30 minutes of completion for small-capacity installs (up to 4 GPUs).
- Observability contract satisfied: metrics, traces, and logs are streaming to the tenant-specific ingest endpoint; synthetic probes show end-to-end success 3/3 times.

Prerequisites and preflight checks (operator checklist):
1) Customer connectivity confirmed (BGP/peer, cross-connect tested).
2) KMS/HSM credentials provisioned and validated (KMS handshake successful).
3) Image and artifact signature verification passed (SHA256 match and signature vendor attest).
4) Required quotas/capacity reserved: GPU counts, local disk, and network egress budget confirmed.
5) Telemetry endpoint and redact/PII policy agreed and configured.

Architecture overview (high level):
- The operator bundle performs the following orchestration phases: 1) preflight & attestation, 2) control-plane handshake, 3) tenant core service boot (API gateway, routing), 4) model artifact download & integrity check, 5) staged warmstart (KV cache priming → model weight verifications → model load), 6) telemetry gating and synthetic validation, 7) traffic ramp and handoff.

Operator sequence (detailed steps):
1. Preflight (automated): run ./operator preflight --tenant <TENANT_ID>. This produces a preflight report (preflight-<TENANT_ID>.json) with green/yellow/red indicators.
2. Attestation: verify hardware and image signatures. CLI example:
   curl -sS -X POST https://operator.local/api/v1/attest -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"image":"sha256:..."}'
3. Network handshake: validate cross-connect and DNS entries. Commands:
   - dig +short controlplane.<tenant>.redwood.internal
   - traceroute -m 15 <control-plane-ip>
4. Artifact staging: pull model tarball to cache node, verify signature, and compute model fingerprint. Example bash snippet:
   sha256sum model.tar.gz | tee model.sha256
   gpg --verify model.tar.gz.sig model.tar.gz
5. KV cache priming: run the priming job with a curated prompt set (see 'Priming dataset' below). This step uses controlled synthetic traffic to populate prefix caches and the attention KV store to reduce first-request tail latency.
6. Model warmload: load model into GPU memory in low-priority mode, validate init loss < threshold and run 3 inference sanity checks. If failures occur, operator can fallback to quantized-compatible variant.
7. Telemetry gating: enable full telemetry ingest only after synthetic probe passes. Until then, run in telemetry-buffered mode and hold the metrics export key in operator vault.
8. Traffic ramp: 0→10→50→100% traffic ramp over configurable windows (default 5 min per step). Use circuit-breakers for each step.
9. Handoff: mark tenant state = active and notify account team with the handoff template.

Priming dataset and priming job contract:
- The priming dataset is a curated set of 200 prompts reflecting the customer’s expected prompt patterns (token length distribution, function-calling patterns). The operator must: 1) ensure redaction for PII, 2) run at 0.1 qps to avoid capacity spikes, 3) tag the run as synthetic in telemetry (label synthetic=true).
- The priming job should accept these parameters: dataset_path (S3 URI), concurrency (1–8), qps_target, and max_tokens_per_prompt.

Observability contract (required signals):
- Metrics (every 10s): token_throughput, request_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_memory_utilization, model_load_time.
- Traces: distributed traces must include operator-init-span, model-load-span, priming-job-span, and request-endpoint spans with sampling rate 100% for the initialization window and 1% steady-state.
- Logs: operator and runtime logs must include structured JSON events with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, trace_id, level, component, message, and error_code if applicable.
- Synthetic probes: probe success ratio 100% for 3 sequential probes before telemetry gating.

Healthcheck response schema (example):
{"status":"ok","checks":{"model_loaded":"ok","kv_cache":"primed","telemetry_ingest":"buffering","latency_p95_ms":45}}

(Operators should assert model_loaded == ok and kv_cache in ["primed","partial"] before ramping traffic.)

Acceptance table (operator must validate):
| Item | Target | Pass condition |
|------|--------|----------------|
| Model load time | <= 90s | model_load_time <= 90s |
| kv cache hit rate | >= 70% | kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.7 |
| p95 latency | <= 150ms | request_latency_p95 <= 150 |
| Telemetry delivery | 3/3 probes | probe success == 3 |

Rollout and rollback procedures:
- Controlled rollout: Start with canary tenant routes (5% traffic), monitor SLOs for 10 minutes. If errors or p95 increases > 2x baseline, step rollback procedure.
- Fast rollback: operator trigger ./operator rollback --tenant <TENANT_ID> --to-stamp <ARTIFACT_STAMP>. Rollback reverses model load and re-activates previous kv cache snapshot.
- For stateful kv-cache mismatches: Evict newest cache and re-prime from snapshot. Avoid partial rollback without operator approval.

Observability gating failure modes and remediation:
- Telemetry backpressure: put runtime into telemetry-buffered mode (buffer duration 1h) and continue serving reads-only until ingestion restored. Notify compliance if PII-sensitive fields were buffered.
- Model artifact mismatch: quarantine reload and fall back to quantized-compatible model variant; open a ticket with "model-artifact-integrity" tag.
- KV priming failures: run the priming job with reduced concurrency (concurrency=1) and extended timeout (2x). If still failing, collect pprof and heap profiles and escalate to runtime team.

Automation snippets (Kubernetes job example):
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: tenant-priming-{{TENANT_ID}}
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: priming
        image: registry.redwood/ops/priming:stable
        command: ["/app/priming","--dataset","s3://private-deploy/priming/{{TENANT_ID}}.ndjson","--qps","0.1"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 2

Troubleshooting quick reference (top issues):
- If p95 spikes after handoff: check kv_cache_hit_rate and network egress throttles.
- If telemetry not received: verify agent certificate (openssl s_client -connect telemetry.ingest:443) and operator vault key rotation timestamp.
- If priming job OOMs: increase priming job memory by 1.5x and reduce concurrency.

Validation checklist (operator signoff):
1. All preflight indicators green.
2. Model artifact fingerprint stored in tenant evidence bundle.
3. Synthetic probe pass (3/3).
4. Metrics and trace spans visible in tenant dashboard with correct labels.
5. Handoff notification sent and ticket closed with acceptance tags.

Audit and evidence preservation:
- The operator must archive the following artifacts to the tenant evidence bucket: preflight-<TENANT_ID>.json, model.sha256, priming-job.log, healthcheck.json, and the final handoff email template. Retention default 365 days.

payload.page_title: Onboarding Microlearning & Competency Rubric: Sprint-Based New Hire Path

sections.body: This playbook defines Redwood Inference's microlearning-based onboarding sprint approach and a companion competency rubric for assessing new hire readiness across engineering and product-adjacent roles. It is intended to standardize manager expectations, shorten time-to-impact, and create objective, coachable milestones tied to hiring evidence and early performance conversations.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Scope: Individual contributors (IC) and first-line managers across Engineering, Product, and Developer Experience.
- Audience: hiring managers, people-ops partners, onboarding buddies, hiring panel members, and team leads responsible for 0–90 day programs.
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
- Ramp time: median ‘able-to-own-feature’ reduced from 12 to 9 weeks within 6 months of roll-out.
- Competency coverage: 90% of new hires should score "meets expectations" or above on core rubric by week 12.
- Manager satisfaction: > 80% managers rate the playbook as useful in quarterly survey.
sections.heading: Goals and success metrics

sections.body:
1) Microlearning first: short, focused modules (10–45 minutes) that can be completed asynchronously.
2) Evidence over ceremony: require small artifacts or checkpoints (PR, doc, demo) not passive completion.
3) Manager-enabled, not manager-heavy: provide templates so managers can coach in 1:1 with minimal prep.
4) Cross-functional onboarding: early customer/product context for engineers; early infra/ops basics for product managers.
sections.heading: Design principles

sections.body:
- Microlearning module catalog: short modules with owner, estimated time, and acceptance evidence.
- 14-day sprints: 4 sprints (0–2, 3–4, 5–8, 9–12 weeks) with prioritized learning objectives and artifacts.
- Competency rubric: mapped to hire bands (IC2–IC4) and role families.
- Manager checklist and 1:1 conversation templates.
- Hiring feedback integration: how hiring notes map to initial sprint goals.
sections.heading: Core components (what to expect)

sections.body:
| Module ID | Title | Owner | Time | Acceptance evidence | When recommended |
| ML-01 | Product & Mission Primer | People-Ops / Growth | 20m | Written 3-bullet summary + manager sign-off | Week 0–1 |
| ML-02 | Security & Data Handling at Redwood | Security | 30m | Acknowledgment + 1-sentence example of data flow concern | Week 0–1 |
| ML-03 | Local Dev Environment: Start-to-First-PR | Eng DX | 45m | Merge of a starter PR that runs unit tests | Week 0–2 |
| ML-04 | Serving Runtime Overview | Eng Serving Runtime | 30m | 10-minute demo + 1 Q/A note | Week 1–3 |
| ML-05 | Observability & Tracing Basics | Eng Platform | 25m | Create one trace in staging and link in ticket | Week 2–4 |
sections.heading: Microlearning module catalog (example)

sections.body:
- Sprint 0–2 (Orientation sprint — weeks 0–2)
  1. Complete ML-01, ML-02, ML-03.
  2. Deliverables: 3-bullet product summary (ML-01), security acknowledgment (ML-02), PR merged (ML-03).
  3. Manager check-in: 30 minutes end of week 2; use "Orientation 1:1" template below.
- Sprint 3–4 (Customer & Tooling — weeks 3–4)
  1. Complete ML-04, ML-05.
  2. Deliverables: demo of a runtime flow, link to created trace.
  3. Manager check-in: 30 minutes end of week 4; evaluate early competency with rubric.
- Sprint 5–8 (Ownership & Delivery — weeks 5–8)
  1. Focus on a small, scoped ticket with cross-team impact.
  2. Deliverable: feature PR + design note + 10-minute demo.
  3. Manager check-in and peer feedback collected.
- Sprint 9–12 (Independence & Quality — weeks 9–12)
  1. Deliverable: owner-of-record on a minor feature or an infrastructure improvement.
  2. Final readiness review using the competency rubric.
sections.heading: Sprint structure (recommended cadence)

sections.body:
- Pre-start: review hiring notes, map 3 initial sprint goals, assign buddy.
- Day 1–7: ensure access, schedule orientation, confirm ML module assignments.
- Weekly: 30-minute structured 1:1 using templates; log evidence artifacts to onboarding tracker.
- Week 4 and week 12: perform rubric assessments and upload to the HR LMS.

1:1 conversation templates (short):
- Orientation 1:1 (end of week 2):
  - What surprised you in your first two weeks?
  - Which microlearning felt most useful? Which was unclear?
  - Confirm next sprint deliverables and support needed.
- Competency checkpoint (week 4):
  - Review artifacts from sprints 0–4.
  - Based on the rubric, which 1–2 skills need focus?
  - Agree on measurable action (pairing sessions or shadowing).
sections.heading: Manager responsibilities (checklist)

sections.body:
- Scoring legend: 1 = Needs support; 2 = Developing; 3 = Meets expectations; 4 = Exceeds expectations.
- Core categories (apply to IC engineering roles):
  1. Product context & customer empathy
  2. Dev environment & velocity (can land safe PRs)
  3. System-level understanding (service boundaries, latency/cost tradeoffs)
  4. Quality & observability (tests, traces, runbook updates)
  5. Collaboration & cross-team communication
sections.heading: Competency rubric (sample criteria and scoring)

sections.body:
| Category | Week 4 target (IC2) | Week 12 target (IC2) | Evidence examples |
| Product context | 2 | 3 | 3-bullet summary, customer ticket review |
| Dev velocity | 2 | 3 | Merged PRs with passing CI, simple fix without revert |
| System understanding | 1 | 3 | Diagram in design doc, ability to explain runtime flow |
| Quality & observability | 2 | 3 | Tests added, staging trace present, runbook contribution |
| Collaboration | 2 | 3 | Peer feedback, cross-team ticket ownership |
sections.heading: Sample rubric table (compact)

sections.body:
- Week 4 checkpoint: if two or more categories are scored 1, open an individualized support plan (ISP) with clear actions and owners.
- Week 12 readiness: at least 4 categories must be >= 3 to be considered "independent contributor (meets expectations)".
sections.heading: Scoring process and thresholds

sections.body:
- All acceptance evidence (PR links, demo notes, trace links) must be attached to the onboarding tracker ticket in Jira and summarized in the new hire’s onboarding doc in Confluence.

sections.heading: Evidence requirements and storage

sections.body:
1. The hiring manager transcribes 3 evidence-backed strengths and 1–2 coached development areas from the final interview packet into the onboarding plan within 48 hours of offer acceptance.
2. These become sprint goals with visible owner and measurement (e.g., pair session, specific PR).
3. If the hiring panel rated a candidate as "high potential but limited infra exposure", schedule additional ML infra pairings in sprint 3–4.

sections.body:

2. Owner: hiring manager + people-ops L&D partner.
3. Steps:
  a. 3-day intake meeting to set 30/60/90 day goals.
  b. Assign mentor and weekly focused sessions (30–60m).
  c. Define measurable checkpoints; re-assess after 30 days.
  d. If insufficient progress after 60 days, escalate to people-ops for role fit conversation.

sections.body:

sections.body: This playbook combines two companion needs for new and existing Redwood teammates: (1) a concise, repeatable career-path launchpad that clarifies role-level expectations, promotion signals, mentorship offerings, and leveling checkpoints; and (2) a compact benefits and tools catalog that new hires can use to become operational in their first 30 days. This document is intended for hiring managers, new hires, mentors, and People Ops partners.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Primary owner: People Ops (Priya Nandagopal)
- Promotion requests & calibration: People Ops + Engineering Managers + Product managers for PM/Design roles
- Tools & access issues: IT Services (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Benefits enrollment questions: Total Rewards (owner: Evelyn Chen)

Section 1 — Quick career-path launchpad:
1) Role families and common prefixes:
   - IC (Individual Contributor): IC1, IC2, IC3, IC4, IC5 (senior, staff, principal equivalents)
   - EM (Engineering Manager): EM1, EM2, EM3 (manager, senior manager, director equivalence)
   - PM/DES (Product/Design): PM1..PM4, DES1..DES4

2) Promotion signals (evidence we expect):
   - Impact: measurable product or infra outcomes tied to business metrics or SLOs (examples: 20% reduction in inference cost for a service; +15% query throughput)
   - Scope: cross-team influence (roadmaps, rollout ownership) and mentoring of 2+ peers for mid-to-senior levels
   - Craft: consistent delivery quality, code review leadership, and design artifacts that are followed in production
   - Leadership: for senior IC/EM bands, pattern of mentoring, hiring contributions, and representation in roadmap tradeoffs

3) Example leveling rubric highlights (short):
   - IC2 -> IC3: takes end-to-end feature ownership for a small service; consistently hits deadlines; mentors interns
   - IC3 -> IC4: owns cross-team features, leads design reviews, drives postmortem action items to closure
   - IC4 -> IC5: shapes product/architecture strategy, routinely mentors external teams, and defines technical hiring bar

4) Promotion process (7-step checklist):
   1. Candidate prepares a 1–2 page promotion packet (owner drafts evidence and impact statements)
   2. Manager reviews and adds calibration notes
   3. People Ops schedules a cross-functional calibration panel within 10 business days
   4. Panel provides decision and written feedback (target: 5 business days)
   5. Manager meets with candidate to communicate outcome and growth plan
   6. If promoted, update title and payroll change within next payroll cycle (People Ops)
   7. If delayed or appealed, escalations go to Director of People Ops (Rosa Alvarez)

payload.page_title: Role Transition and Backfill Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's standard process for role transitions (promotions, lateral moves, and exits) and backfills. It consolidates manager, people-ops, and team responsibilities to minimize service disruption, preserve institutional knowledge, and accelerate handovers. Use this as the canonical checklist and timeline for any role change that impacts active workstreams or customer commitments.

When to use this playbook:
- A team member accepts a new internal role (promotion or transfer).
- A headcount is vacated (resignation, termination, or extended leave).
- A manager decides to add or reshape a role and needs to recruit a backfill.

Goals and success criteria:
- Primary services maintain customer SLOs during transition (no >10% sustained latency regression attributable to staffing change).
- Handover completed with no critical knowledge gaps: at least one runbook, one paired session, and an up-to-date task list shared.
- New hire or transferee productive in core duties within their first 30 days (progress tracked by manager checkpoints).

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- People-ops: approve hiring or role change, update Headcount tracker, run offer and onboarding logistics, coordinate cross-team communications.
- Hiring manager / New manager: define role scope, create/update role profile and success criteria, lead interview and selection, run first 90-day plan and weekly 1:1s.
- Outgoing individual (if applicable): deliver handover artifacts, complete knowledge-transfer sessions, tag relevant docs and claims.
- Team peers / domain SME: coauthor runbooks, participate in shadowing, take short-term ownership of critical queues.
- Eng-platform / Infra: (as needed) support access changes, escalate observed regressions to eng-sre.

Standard timeline and checkpoints (typical for voluntary internal transfer):
1) Pre-transition (4+ weeks before move)
   - Manager notifies People-ops and updates internal Headcount tracker.
   - Draft role profile and 90-day success criteria (document link).
   - Identify interim coverage plan for critical on-call or production queues.

2) Announcement & recruitment (3–4 weeks before move)
   - People-ops publishes role opening internally (Greenhouse + internal channel).
   - Manager assembles interview panel and assigns scorecard owners.

3) Selection & offer (1–3 weeks)
   - Offer approved by People-ops; compensation matched to band and precedent.
   - Effective date and reporting line confirmed.

4) Handover period (2 weeks before -> 2 weeks after transfer)
   - Outgoing contributor prepares the Handover Package (see "Handover Package" section).
   - Three paired sessions scheduled (shadowing, runbook walkthrough, escalation scenarios).
   - Access & repo permissions reviewed; entitlement changes requested by manager via the Access request form.

5) Post-transition (0–90 days after transfer)
   - Manager runs 1:1 cadence: weekly for first 30 days, then biweekly until day 90.
   - People-ops schedules 30/60/90 check-ins and nudges training enrollments (compliance, security, platform).

Handover Package (required artifacts) — manager must confirm completion:
- Role summary: one-paragraph scope, primary metrics, and current OKRs.
- Critical systems list: service names, on-call rotations, runbook links, pager severity thresholds.
- Current work-in-progress: JIRA ticket list (links), expected owners, and blockers.
- Key contacts matrix: internal SMEs, external partners, customer owners.
- Access matrix snapshot: repos, dashboards, test environments, and credential handoff notes.
- Known risks & mitigation: backlog items that might cause regressions and proposed owners.

Handover Package template (copy-paste snippet):

--- Handover Summary ---
Role: {ROLE_NAME}
Effective date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
Primary objective: {short description}
Key services: {service-a, service-b}
On-call coverage: {yes/no}  Pager escalation: {SEV1 contact}

WIP tickets:
- [PROJECT-123] Owner: @user  ETA: 2026-03-01
- [PROJECT-456] Owner: @user  ETA: 2026-04-12

Runbooks and dashboards:
- Service A runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/service-a-runbook
- SLO dashboard: Grafana /dashboards/slo-service-a

Known risks:
- Data-migration scheduled for Q2; requires DBA involvement.

---

Communication and announcement checklist:
- Draft public announcement for team and cross-functional partners.
- Update org chart and team page on Confluence.
- Add calendar hold for handover sessions (30–60 min each).
- Notify customers where the role change affects primary contacts (CS/AM to coordinate).

Temporary coverage patterns (examples):
- Short leave (<4 weeks): assign peer as "interim owner" with explicit escalation rights; no new hires unless capacity permanent.
- Extended vacancy (>8 weeks): open backfill requisition with People-ops; consider contractor for critical production work.
- Promotion creating new vacancy: prioritize internal candidate pool to reduce knowledge transfer time.

Interview and evaluation guidance for backfill hires:
- Scorecards must reflect the updated role profile and competency map.
- Include at least one practical exercise or code/design review relevant to the role.
- Interview panel should contain a peer, a manager, and a product or SRE stakeholder where applicable.
- Use rubric: Technical (40%), Systems & Docs (20%), Collaboration & Culture (20%), Problem Solving (20%).

Access and tooling steps (quick reference):
- Greenhouse: create requisition and tag with team, hiring manager, and urgency.
- Okta/SCIM: request role entitlement changes at least 3 business days before effective date.
- Lattice: move performance plan to new manager after transfer; people-ops will coordinate.
- Confluence: update team page and copy runbook ownership to new assignee.

Manager checklist (signed off before day 0):
- [ ] Handover Package uploaded to Confluence.
- [ ] Three paired sessions scheduled and recorded.
- [ ] Interview panel assembled and scorecard ready (for backfill).
- [ ] Access changes requested and temporary credentials issued if needed.
- [ ] Customer and partner notifications drafted.
- [ ] Temporary escalation path assigned and documented.

Risk mitigation playbooks (if transition impacts SLOs):
- If latency or error rate increases >5% above baseline after transition, escalate to eng-sre and invoke the "production-continuity" runbook.
- For high-severity incidents during handover, senior manager must be looped in within 60 minutes.

Templates and examples (links):
- Example Handover Package: /confluence/company-handbook/examples/handover-samples
- Manager communication template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/role-change-announcement

FAQ (common manager questions):
Q: How long should knowledge transfer sessions be?
A: Aim for three 60-minute deep dives plus shorter 30-minute follow-ups. Record sessions when possible and post notes.

Q: What if the role requires specialized hardware or access?
A: Begin entitlement requests early (Okta + infra tickets). For on-prem hardware, engage eng-infra and schedule a provisioning lead time of 2–3 weeks.

Q: Should we always backfill a promoted role?
A: Not always. Managers should review prioritization with their director and People-ops based on capacity, OKR impact, and budget constraints.

Escalation contacts:
- People-ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Eng SRE on-call: pager duty (see on-call roster)
- HR employment questions: hr@redwood.ai

Appendix: Example 30/60/90 checkpoints (manager guidance)
- Day 30: Core service ownership demonstrated (can triage common SEVs), initial OKR intake complete.
- Day 60: Independent ownership for routine deployments and service health, engagement with cross-functional partners established.
- Day 90: Fully operational in role; evidence-based 90-day review and calibration with People-ops.

Document maintenance:
This playbook is owned by People-ops and will be reviewed annually or after every major reorg. Submit suggestions or edge-case reports to the People-ops Confluence page.

payload.page_title: Internal Mobility & Benefits Operations Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook combines guidance on internal mobility (moves, promotions, and role transitions) with the operational details that make benefits and onboarding predictable and fast. It is intended for managers, people-ops partners, hiring managers, and HR operations to run consistent, fair transitions and ensure new joiners and movers receive timely benefits and tooling access.

1) Purpose and Scope
- Purpose: Reduce variance in internal transfers and benefits provisioning, shorten time-to-productivity for movers and new hires, and align promotion decisions to a shared rubric.
- Scope: Applies to all full-time employees and long-term contractors; covers lateral moves, promotions, role changes, exits, benefits enrollment, and core onboarding workflows. Does NOT replace team-level performance conversations or legal contract changes (finance/legal owned).

2) Principles
- Transparency: publish role expectations and promotion rubrics publicly on the People Portal.
- Timeliness: target 7 business days for access provisioning after an accepted transfer/promotion; target 30 days for compensation changes to be reflected in payroll cycles.
- Fairness: calibration across functions by quarterly review cycles with people-ops and department leads.
- Employee-first: minimize blocker work for the individual moving teams; prioritize uninterrupted productivity.

3) Internal Mobility: Types and Process
A. Types of moves
1. Lateral transfer: change of team/title without level change.
2. Promotion: level increase (IC or Manager path).
3. Dual-role / temporary matrix assignment: short-term project-based assignments.

B. Candidate-initiated vs. Manager-initiated
- Candidate-initiated: employee applies via Internal Job Board; manager of receiving team must complete a short-form intake in the People Portal and schedule interviews within 7 business days.
- Manager-initiated: originating manager opens a transfer request; people-ops validates role fit and suggests timeline.

C. Interview loop (standard, 3–4 steps)
1. Intro screen (15–30 min) — hiring manager: focus on role fit and expectations.
2. Technical/functional interviews (1–2 interviews, 45–60 min) — peers: focus on skills and working style.
3. Leadership/peer alignment (30–45 min) — cross-team questions, collaboration examples.
4. Offer & mobility approval — hiring manager + people-ops sign-off; compensation changes routed to Finance.

D. Timelines and SLAs
- Job posting -> first interview: 7 business days target.
- Final decision -> transfer start date: 10 business days target (exceptions for business-critical timing).
- Access and tooling provisioning: complete within 7 business days of start date.

4) Promotion & Leveling Rubric (summary)
- We publish full level profiles on the People Portal; below is the operational summary used in calibration panels. Each promotion decision should reference measurable examples across these dimensions:
  - Impact: demonstrable product/customer outcomes or technical/operational improvements with metrics.
  - Ownership: scope of work, independent project leadership, cross-team coordination.
  - Craft: depth of technical/product craft, decision clarity, quality of deliverables.
  - Mentorship & Collaboration: active coaching/mentorship, influence without authority.
  - Execution: reliability, velocity, and ability to unblock complex deliveries.

Promotion panel composition: hiring manager + previous manager (if applicable) + people-ops partner + cross-functional peer reviewer.

5) Compensation Operations (high level)
- Banding: every role is mapped to a compensation band; band ranges are market-derived and updated annually by People Ops + Finance.
- Review cadence: annual merit cycle in October; ad-hoc market adjustments possible with VP approval.
- Equity refreshes: eligibility at 24 months (standard) or at promotion.
- Pay timing: eligible changes approved before payroll cutoff result in the next monthly payroll; otherwise the following month.

6) Benefits & Perks: Enrollment and Operational Notes
- Core benefits: medical/dental/vision (enrollment window: 30 days from start), 14-week paid parental leave (primary), 6-week paid parental leave (secondary), mental health stipend ($360/year), flexible learning stipend ($1,200/year).
- Sabbatical: eligibility at 36 months; request process: submit a Sabbatical Petition form to people-ops 120 days before intended leave.
- Wellbeing: quarterly wellness days and company-sponsored mental health sessions scheduled by People Ops.
- Commuter & home-office: one-time home office stipend ($800 on new hire milestones) and commuter pre-tax benefit in supported regions.
- Benefits Exception Process: manager + people-ops to submit a Benefits Exception Request; Finance/legal must approve cost > $10k per year.

7) New Hire and Transition Checklist (operational runbook)
A. Pre-boarding (people-ops) — 7–14 days before start
- Create employee record in HRIS and assign employee ID.
- Send offer paperwork and benefits enrollment links.
- Create placeholder accounts in AccessManager for repos, Slack, email (provision on day 1).
- Ship welcome kit: laptop, charger, onboarding guide, and welcome swag (ship 5 business days before start).

B. Day 1 (manager + IT)
- Welcome meeting (30 min) with manager: role context, team norms, 30/60/90 goals.
- IT handoff: verify laptop, VPN, and key tooling access.
- HR intro: benefits demo and payroll setup.

C. First 30 days (manager + buddy + people-ops)
- Weekly check-ins with manager (first 4 weeks).
- Scheduled buddy sessions for product and infrastructure orientation.
- Complete core trainings: security, code of conduct, and data handling.

D. First 90 days (manager)
- Performance checkpoint at 30 and 90 days.
- Goal alignment and first small impact deliverable.

8) Tooling & Access (owners and onboarding steps)
- People Portal (People Ops): job postings, transfer requests, benefits forms. Owner: people-ops.
- AccessManager (IAM): requests for repo, cloud, and production access. Owner: Eng Security. Workflow: submit an access request ticket with manager approval; expect 48–72 hours for standard, 7 days for privileged production access.
- DevSpace (repos and CI): provisioned by eng-platform on first active repo commit. Owner: eng-platform.
- Redwood Console (product-facing operational dashboard): team owners must add new member via team settings; cross-org viewers given read-only by default.
- OnboardKit (task tracker for new hires): auto-populates manager and new hire tasks; People Ops owns template updates.

9) Role Handoffs and Knowledge Transfer Checklist (for movers)
- Document: open-source roadmap items, runbooks, DRI list, active tickets, and recurring meetings.
- Pairing: two-week co-delivery period with overlap where feasible.
- Access: origin manager to maintain access for 7 days post-transition for escalations.

10) Exceptional Flows
- Rapid redeployment: for business-critical reassignments, people-ops will fast-track access in 48 hours and waive standard posting timelines.
- Cross-border transfers: consult Finance and Legal for visa/payroll changes; expect 30–90 day lead time.

11) Ownership and Escalation
- People-ops: program owner for mobility and benefits operations (email: people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: unresolved cases escalate to Head of People within 5 business days.

12) Templates and Attachments (available on People Portal)
- Transfer intake form (fillable).
- Promotion case packet template.
- Benefits exception request form.

13) FAQ (short)
- Q: How long until my new manager assigns me work?
  A: Within 3 business days of official transfer start.
- Q: When will my benefits start?
  A: Benefits enrollment window opens immediately on start; coverage effective the first of the following month unless otherwise specified.
- Q: Who signs off promotions?
  A: Hiring manager + people-ops + cross-functional reviewer + VP (if band/level change requires budget).

14) Related pages
- People Portal: /people-portal/role-profiles
- Internal Job Board: /people-portal/internal-jobs
- Sabbatical policy: /company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks/sabbatical-guidelines

Questions or requests for clarifications: contact people-ops@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Career Lattice and Skill-Badging Program — Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood's Career Lattice and the accompanying Skill-Badging Program. It standardizes role-level expectations, clarifies promotion and rotation processes, and ties skill badges to onboarding, performance calibration, and benefits pathways.

Audience: People managers, individual contributors, people-ops partners, hiring managers, and engineers preparing for role changes or promotions.

Goals

- Make career progression transparent across functions (Engineering, Product, Research, Sales, and GTM).
- Enable horizontal movement (rotations and lateral moves) without penalty to total comp trajectory.
- Provide portable, verifiable skill badges that reflect applied competency rather than tenure.
- Reduce time-to-contribution for internal transferees and new hires by aligning onboarding bundles to lattice tracks.

Scope and Definitions

- "Career Lattice": a multidimensional framework connecting Level (IC/Manager), Functional Specializations (e.g., Serving Runtime, Observability), and Cross-Functional Skills (e.g., System Design, Security).
- "Skill Badge": a lightweight credential issued by People Ops + engineering reviewers to attest to demonstrated competence (evidence-based). Badges are recorded in the internal HR profile and visible to hiring managers.
- This playbook covers: level definitions (L1–L7), promotion cadence, lateral/rotation process, badging criteria, onboarding tie-ins, and tooling integrations.

Level Structure (high level)

- L1 (Associate): Early-career contributors; focus on onboarding, mentorship, and core execution.
- L2 (Engineer / Associate PM): Executes independently on well-scoped work; owns small components.
- L3 (Senior / Staff individual contributor path entry): Leads medium-complexity projects; mentors peers.
- L4 (Senior Staff / Manager): Leads cross-team initiatives or manages teams; defines technical strategy for a domain.
- L5 (Principal / Group Manager): Shapes product/technical direction across multiple teams.
- L6+ (Distinguished / Director+): Company-level impact and strategy.

Sample competency table (use for calibration meetings)

| Dimension | L2 | L3 | L4 | L5 |
|-----------|----|----|----|----|
| Ownership | Owns tasks end-to-end with guidance | Owns components independently | Owns cross-team features and tradeoffs | Shapes org-level priorities |
| Design | Implements straightforward designs | Designs systems for scalability | Architects multi-service flows | Defines technical principles |
| Communication | Clear within team | Influences cross-team discussions | Shapes product requirements with stakeholders | Influences executive audience |

Promotion Process (concise procedure)

1. Candidate raises interest to manager and updates Career Profile (People Ops portal).
2. Manager completes Promotion Nomination form (template) with: scope of work, artifacts (PRs, design docs), 3+ peer reviewer names, impact metrics, and expected level.
3. Peer reviewers provide written feedback via the People Ops review form within 10 business days.
4. Calibration panel (people-ops + cross-functional senior reviewers) meets in monthly promotion windows. Promotion decisions documented in HR system.
5. If approved, onboarding checklist is generated for new level-specific expectations and skill-badge opportunities. Timeline target: decision within 30 days of nomination.

Criteria and Evidence (examples)

- Evidence-based artifacts: merged PRs, production metrics, incident leadership notes, design docs, customer impact summaries, and mentoring examples.
- Minimum impact expectation: at least one measurable cross-team outcome (reliability, latency, cost, adoption) for moves to L4+.
- Time-in-role is advisory, not prescriptive: rapid promotions permitted with strong evidence.

Lateral Moves and Rotations

Principles

- Rotations are encouraged and treated as formal development assignments (3–6 months typical).
- Compensation and continuous benefits remain intact during rotations; compensation reviews align to the receiving role post-rotation based on outcomes.

Process (for internal applicants)

1. Candidate and receiving manager agree on objectives and success metrics; submit Rotation Agreement to People Ops.
2. People Ops validates capacity and confirms reporting/mentorship structures.
3. Rotation kickoff includes a 2-week focused onboarding bundle (see Onboarding tie-ins below).

Skill-Badging Program

Overview: Skill badges are small, earned credentials tied to discrete competencies (e.g., "Production Deployment Ownership", "Large-Scale Embeddings Ops", "Cross-Region Networking for Private Deployments"). Badges are earned through a combination of: documented artifacts, peer review, and a short applied assessment where relevant.

Badge lifecycle

- Nomination: Candidate submits evidence and supporting reviewers.
- Panel review: A triage panel (one senior engineer from the domain, one people-ops reviewer, one cross-functional verifier) evaluates evidence within 7 business days.
- Issuance: Badge appears on internal profile and can be linked in promotion packages. Badges may expire after 24 months for areas with fast-moving tech; renewal requires re-evidence.

Badging examples and acceptance criteria (examples)

- "Service Observability Badge": evidence = design doc + 2 production alerts resolved + postmortem contribution.
- "Deploy Pipeline Steward": evidence = authored CI/CD config, 1 rollout owned, runbook updates.

Onboarding Tie-ins (how new hires use the lattice)

- New hires complete a Role Profile survey during week 1 that maps their prior badges and preferred tracks.
- People Ops assigns an onboarding bundle: required reading, mentor pairing, and an initial small project aligned to the lattice track.
- Within 60 days, hiring manager and new hire propose 90-day success metrics tied to potential badges.

Benefits and Performance Alignment

- Compensation: Promotions follow the published compensation bands per level; skill badges inform merit and bonus calibrations but do not replace formal compensation processes.
- Learning stipends: Badge earners are eligible for an accelerated learning stipend (up to $1,200/year) for role-relevant training.

Tools and Workflow Integrations

- People Ops portal: central repository for profiles, nominations, and badges. (Integration: HRIS must support custom badge fields.)
- GitHub/GitLab: artifact linking required for most badges (PRs, commit hashes).
- Internal Wiki/Confluence: canonical place for design docs and evidence.
- Slack: dedicated #career-lattice channel for badge Q&A and rotation openings.

Governance and Ownership

- Program owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Technical badge stewards: Rotating roster of senior engineers (2 per domain) who serve 6-month terms.
- Review cadence: Quarterly program health review (metrics below) and annual policy refresh.

Metrics and Success Measures

- Time-to-promotion (median). Target: <= 10 months for level-to-level where applicable.
- Percentage of promotions with at least one skill badge on file. Target: 60%+ by end of first year.
- Rotation success rate (rotation converted to permanent placement or marked successful). Target: 70%.

Communications and Rollout Plan

- Phase 1 (Q4 2024): Pilot with Eng platform and People Ops; publish initial 8 badges.
- Phase 2 (Q1 2025): Expand to Product and Research; automation for badge issuance.
- Full rollout (Q2 2025): Company-wide announcement, manager training sessions, and incorporation into performance calibration.

Appendix A: Promotion checklist (manager-facing)

- Updated Career Profile (candidate)
- Promotion Nomination form completed
- 3+ reviewer statements collected
- Artifact links included (PRs, metrics, postmortems)
- Calibration panel submission deadline met

Appendix B: Example Rotation Agreement fields

- Candidate name, current role, receiving manager, rotation length, objectives (3 items), success metrics, mentor assigned, expected end-date.

Questions and escalation

- First point of contact: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- For disputes: escalate to Head of People Ops and a designated cross-functional appeals panel.

Revision history

- 2024-11-03: Playbook created (pilot scope).
- 2025-02-14: Clarified badge lifecycle and added compensation tie-ins.

Related documents

- Role framework and growth paths (see related_pages).
- New hire orientation and tooling guide.
