payload.page_title: Contributor Launch 360 — Toolkit Playbook for Role Handoffs, Benefits, and Career Signposts

sections.body:
SUMMARY
This playbook describes a standardized, cross-functional process we use at Redwood to launch contributors into productive roles quickly and safely. It ties together role handoffs, access to internal tools, benefits activation, and early career signposts. Audience: people-ops, hiring managers, engineering managers, ICs who are onboarding new contributors, and managers executing role transitions.

GOALS
- Reduce time to first meaningful PR or feature by 50% for technical hires.
- Ensure tooling and benefit entitlements are applied consistently within first 5 business days.
- Provide clear career signposts (30/90/180 day) to reduce role ambiguity and improve early retention.

SCOPE
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- New hire (IC & manager) onboarding from offer acceptance through first 6 months.
- Role transitions (internal promotions, lateral moves) requiring access and privileges changes.
- Activation of benefits and payroll entitlements during first pay period.
- Tooling access flows for common services: GitHub, CI runners, Redwood Console, Slack, OKTA, GCP/AWS accounts for Private deployments.

OWNER & STAKEHOLDERS
- Owner: people-ops (Ava Thompson)
- Primary stakeholders: hiring manager (team), eng-dx (developer experience), infra (cloud-accounts), security (rbac-and-auth).

KEY DEFINITIONS
- Contributor Launch 360 (CL360): The combined workflow of role assignment, tool access, benefits activation, and career check-ins.
- Role Handoff: Formal transfer of responsibilities when someone leaves or moves teams.
- Privilege Window: A temporary elevated access period (max 72 hours) for onboarding engineers to run infra setup tasks under supervision.

QUICK START (one-page)
1) Offer accepted: people-ops triggers CL360 workflow in Workflows service (workflow-id: CL360-001).
2) Day 0 (before first day): create GitHub org access, Slack invite, OKTA identity, basic GSuite account.
3) Day 1–5: complete access checklist (sections below), schedule 30-day check-in with manager and peer buddy.
4) Day 30/90/180: run career signpost templates & update role expectations doc in team wiki.

DETAILED CHECKLIST (numbered tasks assigned to owners)
1. people-ops: Create employee record, initiate payroll and benefits enrollment (deadline: before end of first pay period).
2. security: Provision OKTA account, apply baseline RBAC groups (rbac: core-contributor, slack-basic).
3. eng-dx: Grant GitHub repo access (triage and owner repos), CI runner permissions, and sandbox AWS/GCP project with cost tags.
4. infra: If role requires Private deployment access, create VPC scoped service account and add to project-level IAM with least privilege.
5. manager: Assign first sprint ticket, schedule role expectations meeting, introduce to peer buddy.
6. peer buddy: Run tooling walkthrough (Git cloning, local dev sandbox, Redwood Console walkthrough).
7. people-ops + manager: Confirm benefits enrollment and equipment procurement (laptop, docking) within week 1.

ACCESS MATRIX (text table)
Service | Typical first-day entitlement | Provisioning owner | SLA
GitHub (org) | read + repo triage | eng-dx | 4 hours
Redwood Console (dev) | view + token creation | eng-dx | 8 hours
CI runners | submit jobs (non-privileged) | eng-dx | 24 hours
OKTA | identity + 2FA | security | 2 hours
GCP/AWS sandbox | limited project access | infra | 48 hours
Hardware (laptop) | issued | people-ops | 5 business days
Benefits enrollment | initiated | people-ops | 3 business days

PRIVILEGE WINDOWS
- Use case: infra bootstrapping, secrets migration, on-prem install validation.
- Max duration: 72 hours.
- Approval flow: manager -> infra owner -> security reviewer. Approval recorded in the CL360 ticket.
- Rollback: infra must provide automated rollback playbook and test run before window can be granted.

ROLE HANDOFF CHECKLIST (when an incumbent leaves or changes role)
1) Manager files a Role Handoff Request in the RoleOps queue (template: role-handoff-YYYYMMDD).
2) people-ops schedules knowledge transfer sessions (min 2 hours) and documents runbooks in team wiki.
3) eng-dx reassigns repo ownership and updates CODEOWNERS.
4) infra removes elevated privileges and runs an access audit (using AccessAudit tool, export saved to payroll-archive).
5) Security issues final sign-off and closes the handoff ticket.

CAREER SIGNPOSTS (templates & outcomes)
- 30-day: "Foundations" — checklist includes merged PR, completed onboarding tasks, first documentation contribution. Manager outcome: alignment on short-term goals.
- 90-day: "Execution" — deliverable ownership, cross-team collaboration evidence, feedback conversation. Manager outcome: discuss development plan and ladder fit.
- 180-day: "Trajectory" — demonstrable impact, promotion calibration if applicable, stretch assignments. Manager outcome: confirm next 6–12 month objectives.

MANAGER GUIDANCE: ROLE EXPECTATIONS TEMPLATE (fill-in)
- Role name, level and band: ______
- Key deliverables (first 90 days): 1) ______ 2) ______ 3) ______
- Success metrics (OKRs / metrics): ______
- Buddy and stakeholders: ______
- Access required: ______

BENEFITS ACTIVATION (procedural steps)
1) people-ops enters hire into Benefits Portal and sends enrollment email within 24 hours of start.
2) New hire completes forms; people-ops confirms enrollment and sends confirmation.
3) For equipment stipends, people-ops issues a voucher and shipping schedule.
4) For international hires, payroll and tax team coordinate local onboarding (timeline: up to 14 days).

EXAMPLE SCRIPTS & SNIPPETS
- CLI: Create basic sandbox project (GCP example)
```
sections.heading: This playbook covers

sections.body:
gcloud projects create redwood-sandbox-{{employee-id}} --name="sandbox-{{employee-name}}"
gcloud iam service-accounts create sandbox-builder --display-name="Sandbox Builder"
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-sandbox-{{employee-id}} --member="serviceAccount:sandbox-builder@redwood-sandbox-{{employee-id}}.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/viewer"
```
- YAML: Example onboarding ticket payload for Workflows service
```
workflow: CL360-001
assignee: people-ops
employee_id: E-12345
start_date: 2026-01-05
role: Software Engineer II
required_tooling: [github,okta,redwood-console,ci]
```

ESCALATION PATHS
- Day 0–5 access failure: escalate to eng-dx on-call (rota: eng-dx-oncall@redwood.com).
- Benefits not applied by first pay: people-ops escalation to HR lead (hr-lead@redwood.com) and finance.
- Privilege window misuse: security incident process (see Security IR runbook) — immediate suspension and audit.

METRICS & HEALTH DASHBOARD (for people-ops)
- Time-to-first-merge (target: <= 14 days)
- Percentage of hires with full access by day 5 (target: 95%)
- Benefits enrollment completion rate by first pay period (target: 100%)
- Role handoff completeness score (manual audit quarterly, target: 90%)

FAQ
Q: Who is responsible for laptop shipping delays?
A: people-ops owns procurement; infra supports temporary remote development images until hardware arrives.

Q: How do I request a privilege window?
A: Use the RoleOps ticket template and attach the infra rollback playbook. Approval chain: manager -> infra -> security.

Q: Can a contractor receive the same benefits?
A: Contractors receive a subset of the benefits; refer to contract-specific entitlements in the Benefits Portal.

TEMPLATES & RESOURCES (links)
- Role Handoff Request template: /confluence/templates/role-handoff-request
- CL360 Workflows: /internal/workflows/CL360-001
- AccessAudit export: /internal/tools/access-audit
- Developer quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-quickstart

APPENDIX: AUDITABLE FIELDS (what we log)
- OKTA provisioning events (timestamped)
- GitHub org invites and approvals
- Privilege window approvals and duration
- Ticket timeline for CL360 workflow

CHANGE HISTORY
- 2025-11-18: Created by Ava Thompson (baseline launch playbook).
- 2026-02-12: Updated access SLA and added Privilege Window policy after security review.

OWNER CONTACTS
- people-ops: people-ops@redwood.com (Ava Thompson)
- eng-dx: eng-dx@redwood.com (Marcus Lee)
- security: security@redwood.com (Sofia Ramirez)

END OF PLAYBOOK

payload.page_title: Warmup Sequencer and Traffic Fingerprinter — IaC spec & runbook

sections.body:
Overview

This document defines the design, Terraform/IaC module interface, CI/CD pattern, and operational runbook for the Warmup Sequencer and Traffic Fingerprinter system. The goal is to pre-seed GPU KV caches and model contexts in advance of user traffic, using a telemetry-driven fingerprint of tenant traffic to prioritize warmup candidates. The spec covers: service components, IaC modules and variables, SLOs, monitoring/alerts, a safe canary and rollback process, and step-by-step incident procedures.

Goals

- Reduce first-request tail latency for cold model sessions by seeding KV cache and tokenized prefixes.
- Prioritize warmups by traffic similarity so warmest tenants get prewarmed capacity.
- Provide idempotent, auditable IaC modules and a CI/CD pattern to deploy with zero-downtime.
- Expose ownership and telemetry to SRE and infra teams for cost/capacity trade-offs.

Service components (logical)

- warmup-sequencer (K8s service): schedules warmup jobs based on fingerprint scores and capacity budget.
- traffic-fingerprinter (Batch/K8s): ingests sampled request traces, derives compact fingerprints (64-bit), and produces tenant score vectors.
- burst-orchestrator (serverless controller): applies short-term credits when burst triggers are detected.
- prewarm-job-runner (K8s CronJob + GPU node selector): runs ephemeral inference clients that execute warmup prefixes and optionally populate distributed KV cache.
- warmup-metrics-collector (Prometheus exporter): collects warmup latency, success/failure, and tokenized-prefix hit rates.

Key SLOs and thresholds

| Metric | Target | Alert condition |
|---|---:|---|
| First-request latency (p50) for prewarmed sessions | < 120 ms | N/A (informational) |
| First-request latency (p99) for prewarmed sessions | < 700 ms | p99 > 1.5s for 10m |
| Warmup success rate (job-level) | >= 98% | < 95% for 15m |
| Fingerprinter staleness | < 5m | > 10m (pager) |
| Warmup budget spend accuracy | +/- 10% of target budget | variance > 25% (pager) |

Design decisions and rationale

- Fingerprints are compact and privacy-preserving: we compute deterministic, keyed hashes of anonymized request features (model id, average seq_len bucket, token-prefix hash) to avoid storing raw PII.
- Warmup is budgeted per-tenant: a global budget (tokens/sec) and per-tenant soft cap prevent runaway costs.
- Idempotency: each warmup job writes a short-lived marker to DynamoDB/etcd with TTL; duplicate runs detect markers and skip work. This avoids double-charging GPU time.
- Prefer read-only cache warmups where possible (populate LRU cache entries) and avoid generating user-visible side effects.

IaC module interface (Terraform)

Use a dedicated module: tf-module/gpu-warmup-sequencer with the following variables and outputs. The snippet below is a suggested interface example for consumers.

Example: module usage (HCL)

module "gpu_warmup_sequencer" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.internal/infra/tf-modules//gpu-warmup-sequencer?ref=v1.2.0"

  cluster_name            = var.cluster_name
  service_account        = aws_iam_role.warmup_role.arn
  prewarm_node_selector  = { "gpu_type" = "v100" }
  max_concurrent_jobs    = 120
  global_token_budget_tps = 4000
  fingerprint_kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.fingerprint.id
  metrics_pushgateway    = module.metrics.pushgateway_url
  alerting_policy       = module.alerts.warmup_policy_id
}

Module outputs (strings): warmup_service_url, fingerprinter_job_role, iam_policies_applied

Recommended variable defaults

| var | default | notes |
|---|---|---|
| max_concurrent_jobs | 60 | tuned by pool size; override per-region |
| prewarm_node_selector | {"gpu_tier":"inference-warm"} | ensures jobs land on warm pools |
| global_token_budget_tps | 2000 | conservative starting value |

CI/CD and deployment pattern

- Repo layout: infra/modules/gpu-warmup-sequencer, services/warmup-sequencer, services/traffic-fingerprinter.
- CI: Buildkite pipeline with steps: unit tests -> container build -> image promotion -> Terraform plan -> Atlantis apply (when approved).
- Canary pattern: Deploy fingerprinter and warmup-sequencer to a canary namespace with 5% of traffic (simulated or shadowed) for 24 hours. Run telemetry smoke tests and compare warmup success/failure rates.
- Rollback: Terraform destroy is not acceptable for rollback. Use image rollback and scale-down + feature flag (disable-scheduler) accessible to SRE via the admin console.

Prometheus metrics and alert rules (examples)

- warmup_job_latency_seconds_bucket{job="prewarm-job-runner"}
- warmup_job_success_total{result="success"}
- fingerprinter_fingerprint_age_seconds
- warmup_budget_consumed_tokens_per_sec

Alert example (Prometheus Alertmanager rule):

ALERT WarmupJobHighFailureRate
  IF increase(warmup_job_success_total{result="failure"}[15m]) > 0 and
     (sum(increase(warmup_job_success_total[15m])) / sum(increase(warmup_job_success_total[15m]) + increase(warmup_job_success_total{result="success"}[15m]))) > 0.05
  FOR 10m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS {
    summary = "Warmup job failure rate >5% over 15m",
    runbook = "link:/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/warmup-sequencer-traffic-fingerprinter-iac-spec#incident-response"
  }

Runbook: incident response (pager to SRE rotation)

1) Triage & initial checks (15 min)
   - Confirm alert using Grafana dashboard: "Warmup Sequencer Overview".
   - Check fingerprinter staleness: query fingerprinter_fingerprint_age_seconds. If > 10m, escalate pager.
   - Determine blast radius: which regions/tenants are affected? Use warmup_service_url/admin/tenants to map.

2) Immediate mitigation steps (if warmup jobs failing or causing overload)
   - Flip feature flag: disable-scheduler via Admin Console (temporary) to stop new warmup jobs. Command: curl -X POST "$WARMUP_ADMIN/api/v1/flags/disable-scheduler" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
   - Scale down prewarm-job-runner Deployment to 0 and scale warmup-sequencer to 1 replica for debugging: kubectl -n infra scale deploy/prewarm-job-runner --replicas=0
   - If OOM/driver faults observed on GPU nodes, cordon affected nodes: kubectl cordon <node> and drain if necessary. See GPU node troubleshooting below.

3) Recovery & validation (30–60 min)
   - Re-deploy fingerprinter with debug logging (if root cause unknown). Create a short-lived build tag and deploy only to canary.
   - Re-run a small set of synthetic warmup jobs against a sandbox GPU pool to validate end-to-end. Use the diagnostic client: curl -X POST $WARMUP_SERVICE/synthetic/run -d '{"tenant":"test-tenant","prefix":"hello"}'
   - Unlock scheduler after verifying success: re-enable scheduler and gradually increase max_concurrent_jobs by 10% every 5 minutes while watching job success rate & GPU utilization.

4) Postmortem actions (24–72 hours)
   - Capture the following traces: sample job logs (s3://infra-logs/warmup/YYYYMMDD/), fingerprinter outputs, controller metrics.
   - If change caused the incident, prepare an RCA with roll-forward plan. Apply IaC changes using module version pinning.

GPU node troubleshooting checklist

- Symptoms: driver crash, high GPU memory churn, persistent PCIe errors.
- Steps:
  1. kubectl get pods -o wide -n gpu | grep prewarm-job
  2. Check dmesg and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log on the node
  3. Verify CUDA driver versions: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
  4. If node health unstable, cordon + annotate and create support ticket to Hardware team (owner: infra-hw).

Cost and quota controls

- Token budget enforcement: burst-orchestrator reads a monthly token budget and enforces per-tenant TPS using a leaky-bucket algorithm.
- Billing telemetry: warmup_job_token_count exported to billing pipeline with tag warmup=true. Ensure TF module attaches the correct tagging policy (tag:cost_center).

Safety checklist before enabling for a new customer

1. Confirm customer has agreed to warmup budget and tagging in contract.
2. Run the fingerprinting job on 24 hours of sampled traffic and validate fingerprint entropy > 0.7 (avoids everyone mapping to a single bucket).
3. Run synthetic warmup smoke tests against a dedicated sandbox GPU pool.
4. Ensure alerts and dashboards are configured for the customer's region.

Operational ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: infra-inference (pager: #infra-sre)
- Secondary owner: platform-ml (on-call: #platform-ml)
- Hardware escalation: infra-hw@redwood.internal
- Infra IaC contact: Aisha Patel (tf-module steward)

Appendix: example fingerprinter pseudocode (Python)

```
# pseudocode: compute a stable tenant fingerprint
import hashlib

def make_fingerprint(model_id, seq_len_bucket, prefix_hash, salt):
    buf = f"{model_id}:{seq_len_bucket}:{prefix_hash}"
    h = hashlib.blake2b(buf.encode('utf-8'), digest_size=8, key=salt.encode('utf-8'))
    return int.from_bytes(h.digest(), 'big')
```

References and related modules

- tf-module/gpu-warmup-sequencer (module source code)
- services/traffic-fingerprinter (implementation repo)
- dashboards/Warmup Sequencer Overview (Grafana)

Change log

- 2025-07-01: Document created by Sofia Martinez (initial design + IaC interface).
- 2025-08-20: Added Prometheus alert examples and Runbook incident steps (review: Ethan Zhao).
- 2025-10-12: Updated SLO targets and added canary deployment pattern (review: Priya Nair).

payload.page_title: Foundations Toolkit and Role Sprint Handbook

sections.body: This handbook bundles the practical tooling and milestone calendar for new joiners (ICs and first-time managers) and the Role Sprint process we use to accelerate early-career growth. It is intended to be a single reference for people-ops partners, hiring managers, mentors, and new teammates during their first 120 days and beyond.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- New individual contributors (IC1–IC3) and first-time managers.
- Hiring managers and onboarding buddies.
- People-ops and engineering managers who run Role Sprints.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- Tool access and minimal config for day‑one productivity.
- A repeatable 6-week Role Sprint format for skill acceleration.
- An aligned set of role-ladder checkpoints and promotion-ready evidence.
- Benefits and perks orientation checklist relevant to first 120 days.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Owner: People Ops - New Hire Experience (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Operational lead: Asha Mehta (People Ops Partner).
- Tooling owner: Platform Productivity (eng-developer-experience).
- SLA: People-ops acknowledges access requests within 24 hours and resolves standard tool access within 72 hours.

Quick-start checklist (day 0–3):
1) Accounts and access (people-ops action):
   - GitHub (team/org membership), Google Workspace, Slack, Okta enroll, SSO to Console.
   - Confirm access to the following services: repo-read for core infra, onboarding repo write, dev sandbox.
2) Equipment and ergonomics (IT action):
   - Provision laptop, monitor, and dock; ship same-day where regional stock available.
3) Intro sessions (manager action):
   - 30-min role orientation, 60-min product overview, calendar invite for weekly 1:1 cadence.
4) Role Sprint enrollment (manager + mentor):
   - Assign Role Sprint cohort (if applicable) and a primary mentor.
sections.heading: Ownership and SLAs

sections.body:
- Week 0: Getting set up, security training, first demo.
- Weeks 1–2: Shadowing and tiny-owner tasks (bug fix, doc edit).
- Weeks 3–8: Role Sprint (6 weeks) — defined scope, deliverable, and public demo.
- Weeks 9–16: Impact projects and evidence collection for role ladder checkpoints.
sections.heading: First 120-day running plan (summary)

sections.body:
- Objective: 1 focused competency improvement tied to job-level outcomes (e.g., reduce median inference latency by 10% in a small path, or own a documentation chapter and automated test harness).
- Team: new hire (owner), mentor, manager, one reviewer from related team.
- Deliverables:
  1) Sprint brief (1 page): background, goals, success metrics, constraints.
  2) Weekly public standup updates (Slack thread + 1 slide update).
  3) Final demo + PR or doc change + retrospective.
- Evaluation rubric (applied at demo):
  - Outcome alignment (1–5): Did the work map to role outcomes?
  - Quality and craft (1–5): Code/docs meet standards.
  - Collaboration (1–5): Engaged reviewers and cross-team feedback.
  - Velocity/ownership (1–5): Work completed independently and on schedule.
  - Total score guidance: 16–20 = exceeds expectations; 12–15 = meets; <12 = needs follow-up.

Role ladder checkpoints (for IC1–IC3):
- IC1 (Foundational): Demonstrates reliable task completion, basic design awareness, and participates in code review. Evidence: 3+ merged PRs with positive reviews; pair session with mentor.
- IC2 (Developing): Owns a small service or feature, accepts cross-team requests, mentors interns. Evidence: 1+ independent feature, measurable metrics (latency/quality), written post-mortem.
- IC3 (Experienced): Leads medium-scope design, influences roadmap, guides multiple teammates. Evidence: design doc ownership, measurable product impact, consistent peer feedback.

Tools matrix (concise table — use when issuing access requests):
- Tool | Purpose | Typical first-action | Owner
- GitHub | Code hosting and PRs | Fork+build+create PR | Platform Productivity
- Console (Redwood Console) | Observability/rollouts | Link to team dashboard + demo read-only view | Observability Team
- Sandbox (dev env) | Local experimentation | Run sample inference locally | Eng Infra
- Docs repo | Docs and runbooks | Edit onboarding doc and submit PR | Docs Team
- CI/CD (buildkite) | CI pipelines | Trigger baseline test run | Eng Infra

Note: For each tool, the first-action must be completed in week 1 of onboarding. People-ops automates invites via Okta; escalate to people-ops if not received within SLA.
sections.heading: Role Sprint (6-week) format (repeatable)

sections.body:
1) Narrative: 1–2 page summary describing context, actions, and impact.
2) Artifacts: PR links, dashboards, test results, demo recording.
3) Peer feedback: 3+ reviewers' written notes or evaluations.
4) Manager calibration: one-page assessment mapping accomplishments to role ladder outcomes.
sections.heading: Promotion evidence guidance (how to collect and present)

sections.body:
- How to enroll in health, dental, 401(k), commuter/remote stipends.
- Scheduling a benefits Q&A with People Ops: use the Benefits Portal link in the welcome email.
- Parental leave and sabbatical overview: summary + links to full policy pages.

Hiring & onboarding tie-ins (what managers should do before day 1):
1) Define a clear first-120-day plan and Role Sprint objective in the hiring repo.
2) Pre-assign a mentor and share their calendar availability.
3) Add required reading links to the offer email (product overview, architecture primer, code of conduct).
4) Prepare an initial contribution task that is scoped to 1–3 days of effort.

Manager checklist for running Role Sprints (before sprint start):
1) Approve sprint brief and success metrics.
2) Confirm reviewer and demo audience.
3) Reserve 30–45 minutes for final demo and retrospective.
4) Schedule midpoint check-in (week 3).
sections.heading: Benefits & perks orientation (first 2 weeks)

sections.body:
- Title: (short)
- Background: (2–3 sentences)
- Goal: (one measurable outcome)
- Success metrics: (quantified where possible)
- Constraints: (services, time, approvals required)
- Deliverables: (artifacts to produce)
- Estimated time: (hours/days)

Accessibility, reasonable adjustments, and remote-first norms:
- We provide captioned recordings of demos and allow flexible working windows for focused work.
- Request adjustments via people-ops-form@redwood.ai; typical turnaround 5 business days.

Offboarding and knowledge transfer (owners must plan at departure):
1) Handover doc with active work list and who-to-contact.
2) Transfer repo ownership and update runbooks.
3) Revoke tool access via Okta ticket (people-ops triggers, SRE validates).

Appendix: useful links and templates (copy into your onboarding repo):
- Onboarding repo template: /repos/onboarding/new-hire-templates
- Sprint brief template: /docs/templates/role-sprint-brief.md
- Promotion evidence template: /docs/templates/promotion-evidence.md
- Benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example
sections.heading: Sample sprint brief template (paste into onboarding repo)

sections.body:
Q: How often should Role Sprints run for early-career hires?
A: We recommend one Role Sprint during the first 120 days and another within the first year for high-growth plans.

Q: Who signs off if a Role Sprint score is borderline?
A: Manager and People Ops jointly agree on follow-up actions; the hiring manager documents a 6-week remediation plan.

payload.page_title: Cross-Functional Apprenticeship & Starter Toolkit (2026)

sections.body:
A structured 90-day cross-functional apprenticeship program that accelerates new and transitioning contributors through role-specific ladders, integrates benefits orientation, and provides a step-by-step internal tools starter kit. Designed for early-career hires, IC-to-manager rotations, and engineers joining product/platform teams.
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable apprenticeship flow that combines role clarity, hands-on projects, assigned mentorship, and an internal tools ramp to reduce time-to-impact while preserving predictable career progression and benefits alignment. The program balances people-ops guardrails with team-specific learning plans so hiring managers can onboard contributors with consistent experience and measurable outcomes.

Who this is for:
- New full-time hires (engineers, product, SRE, support)
- Internal transferees rotating between functions (e.g., infra -> platform)
- Early-career apprenticeship hires (cohort-based)

Core objectives:
1. Reduce average time-to-productive-contribution from 90 -> 60 days for apprenticeship participants.
2. Provide a documented ramp that explicitly maps to role ladders and promotion criteria.
3. Ensure tool access and baseline security/compliance checks within first 48 hours.
4. Create measurable mentor/mentee commitments (mentor ratio 1:4; 2 weekly touchpoints).

Program structure (90-day phased plan):
Phase 0 (Pre-start, owner: People Ops, timeline: -7 to 0 days):
- Background checks, equipment provisioning, building access, pre-reads distributed.
- Manager shares 90-day plan and first project brief.
- Tools checklist triggered: Okta invite, GitHub org access request, Slack group, console read-only.

Phase 1 (Foundations, owner: Hiring Manager & Mentor, days 0–30):
- Week 1: orientation, security briefing, team rituals, intro tasks (scaffolded).
- Week 2–4: paired onboarding tasks, runbook walkthroughs, first small PR.
- Deliverable: documented "first-30" retrospective and feature stub merged.

Phase 2 (Applied work, owner: Team Lead, days 31–60):
- Rotating small projects with incremental ownership.
- Midpoint check-in: competency rubric review and benefits Q&A session.
- Deliverable: autonomous ownership of a single service/feature for a sprint.

Phase 3 (Ownership & Career sync, owner: Manager, days 61–90):
- Handover autonomy for maintenance tasks; present outcomes to team.
- Career ladder calibration: map observed competencies to role expectations.
- Deliverable: promotion-readiness note or continued development plan.

Role & Career ladder alignment:
- Each apprenticeship cohort is paired with the published role ladder for the target role.
- Managers must attach the relevant ladder link to the 90-day plan and explicitly call out the 3 promotion-critical behaviors expected at the next level.
- Example mapping (engineer apprentice):
  - Level IC1: deliver small features, write unit tests, follow coding standards.
  - Level IC2: own a service component, lead design discussions, mentor interns.

Access & internal tools starter kit (must complete within 48 hours):
- Required access: Okta SSO, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, CI dashboard, Datadog (read), JIRA.
- Security: MFA enabled, company laptop encrypted, mandatory secure-coding checklist.
- Tools onboarding items (owners in parentheses):
  1) Okta & Google account setup (people-ops).
  2) GitHub org + repo permissions request (team repo owner).
  3) CI pipeline read-access and local runner config (devops).
  4) Datadog dashboards and alert subscriptions (SRE).
  5) Local dev environment bootstrap script and sample data (team engineering).

Quick-access table: tool, initial permission, owner, SLA
| Tool        | Initial Permission  | Owner       | SLA to grant |
|-------------|---------------------|-------------|---------------|
| Okta        | SSO user            | People Ops  | 4 hours       |
| GitHub      | org+repo read/write | Team Owner  | 8 hours       |
| Datadog     | read dashboard      | SRE         | 24 hours      |
| CI System   | read logs           | DevOps      | 24 hours      |
| Internal Console | read-only       | Platform    | 48 hours      |

Benefits orientation and mapping:
- New hires receive a benefits onboarding session in week 2 covering healthcare, 401(k), paid time off, parental leave, and commuter/office stipends.
- For apprentices and rotational roles, people-ops provides a benefits mapping note that clarifies stipend eligibility and pro-rated time off.
- Sample benefits mapping (ascii table):
| Employment Type | PTO accrual (yr1) | Health plan eligibility | Office stipend |
|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------------|----------------|
| Full-time FTE   | 15 days           | Day 1                   | $400/quarter   |
| Apprenticeship  | 10 days (prorated) | After 30 days           | $200/quarter   |
| Contractor      | N/A               | No (depends on plan)    | No             |

Hiring manager checklist (pre-start to 90 days):
1. Create role-specific 90-day plan and attach role ladder (day -7).
2. Identify and confirm mentor (ratio <= 1:4) and schedule weekly 1:1s (day -3).
3. Complete tool access requests and verify SLAs (day 0).
4. Run weekly progress syncs with people-ops for first 30 days.
5. Conduct midpoint competency calibration at day 45 and record notes.
6. Final career ladder calibration at day 90 and decide next steps.

Mentor expectations:
- Two weekly touchpoints: one technical pairing session (1 hour) and one career/feedback check (30 minutes).
- Provide code reviews within 48 hours for critical PRs.
- Maintain a short growth log (3 bullet outcomes weekly) to share at mid and end checkpoints.

Governance & compliance:
- All apprentices sign the standard Redwood confidentiality and security onboarding forms before system access.
- Any deviation to advantages (extended stipends, accelerated promotion) must be approved by People Ops and documented in the related_pages field.

Success metrics & reporting (owner: People Ops & Hiring Manager):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (target <= 21 days).
- Time-to-autonomous-ownership (target <= 60 days).
- Mentee satisfaction (pulse survey at days 30/90, target >= 85% positive).
- Mentor load (maintain ratio <= 1:4).

Related resources and templates (appendix):
- 90-day plan template: /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/90-day-plan-template (link internal).
- Role ladder index: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/role-ladders-index (link internal).
- Tool access request form: /internal/self-service/access-requests (link internal).
- Sample onboarding checklist (text file included in team repo).

FAQ (short):
Q: Can apprentices be converted to FTE?
A: Yes. Conversion follows standard hiring/offer process; manager must submit conversion proposal to People Ops with 90-day outcomes.

Q: What if tool access is delayed beyond SLA?
A: Escalate to the tools-owner channel; People Ops will open a support ticket and provide a temporary sandbox where feasible.

Q: How are promotions considered during apprenticeship?
A: Promotions are possible, but require evidence against the ladder behaviors and a cross-functional calibration panel.

Appendix: templates and checklists are available in the team wiki and referenced related pages above. For questions, contact people-ops@redwood.ai or the program lead, Aisha Kumar.

payload.page_title: Satellite Team Tool Access and Mentor Pairing Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines the process, roles, SLAs, and artifacts required to onboard and support satellite teams, project rotations, and short-term contractors who require scoped access to Redwood systems. It pairs an access lifecycle with a mentor pairing program to accelerate impact while maintaining security and cost controls.

Scope
- Applies to any transient or temporary team event lasting between 2 days and 12 months: rotations, shadowing, pilot squads, contractor engagements, and hackweeks.
- Not intended for full-time hire onboarding (see new-hire orientation).
- Covers tool access (Okta, Redwood Console, GCP projects, Vault, Jira, GitHub org), mentor pairing, and deprovisioning.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-meaningful-commit for satellite contributors to under 2 business days for standard access and 4 hours for urgent business-critical cases.
- Ensure least-privilege with automated expiry and quarterly auditability.
- Provide explicit mentor ownership to reduce support load on platform teams.

Ownership and Roles
- Requestor: Team lead sponsoring the satellite access (manager or product owner). Responsible for initial justification and tagging in requests.
- Sponsor (Engineering or Product): Approves scope and duration.
- People Ops (Access Admin): Coordinates approvals, issues Okta group invites, and schedules mentor pairing if requested. SLA: 24 business hours for standard requests.
- Security (Reviewer): Performs risk review for requests with sensitive scope (see Risk matrix below). SLA: 48 business hours.
- Mentor: Senior engineer from host team assigned for 4–8 weeks. Responsible for onboarding, API walkthroughs, and weekly syncs.
- Platform Concierge (eng-platform): Executes provisioning where automation is not available and maintains the access templates.

Access Categories and Typical Entitlements
1) Read-only observer (no write access): Slack channels, Redwood Console read dashboards, project docs.
2) Scoped contributor (code + deployment but restricted): GitHub repo write, non-prod GCP project, test service tokens.
3) Production observer: Read-only access to production dashboards and logs; no deploy. Requires extra approval.
4) Production operator (limited): Deploy privileges for a single microservice / model-serving pool. Requires sponsor and security justification.

Risk Matrix (high level)
- Low risk: access limited to internal docs, non-prod GCP, staging Redwood Console. No Security review.
- Medium risk: write access to code repos, test infra, non-prod secrets. Requires security notification.
- High risk: production secrets, deploy rights, customer data. Requires security review and sponsor sign-off.

Requesting Access: Step-by-step
1. Create a Satellite Access Request in the Access Portal (link: /tools/access-portal). Use the template:
   - Title: [Team] Satellite Access – <Short description>
   - Duration: select end date (maximum 12 months)
   - Scope: choose one or more presets: observer, scoped-contributor, prod-observer, prod-operator
   - Sponsor: add sponsor email
2. Sponsor approves the request in the portal (one click).
3. People Ops validates role mapping and assigns Okta groups within 24 business hours for standard requests. For urgent requests mark "fast-lane" and ping @access-concierge on Slack. SLA: 4 hours for approved fast-lane requests during business hours.
4. Platform Concierge provisions named resources using the appropriate Access Template (see templates table below).
5. Mentor pairing: Requestor selects mentor pairing option in the portal (recommended). People Ops assigns a mentor within 48 hours from the host-team mentor pool.

Onboarding Checklist (Mentor + Mentee) — complete within first 5 business days
1. Kickoff video call (30–45m): introductions, objectives, sprint goals, success metrics.
2. Walkthrough of the primary repo and CI/CD flow.
3. Provide developer sandbox links and test dataset pointers.
4. Demo Redwood Console route for the service(s) in scope.
5. Agree on communication channels and on-call handoffs (if any).
6. Set 1:1 cadence: weekly for first month, then biweekly.

Access Templates (table)

Name | Description | Example Entitlements | Default Duration | Responsible
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
observer | Read-only access for short engagements | Slack read, Console dashboards (read), Docs | 30 days | People Ops
scoped-contributor | Code + non-prod infra access | GitHub write, non-prod GCP project, test Vault tokens | 90 days | Platform Concierge
prod-observer | Read-only prod monitoring | Grafana read, Sentry read, prod logs view | 30 days | People Ops + Security
prod-operator | Limited deploy rights to 1 service | Deploy token restricted to service X, audit logging enabled | 30 days | Sponsor + Security + Platform Concierge

(When copying into Access Portal, choose the template and apply additional constraints.)

Mentor Pairing Program Details
- Purpose: Rapid context transfer, guardrails education, and human escalation path.
- Commitment: Mentor expected to spend 4–6 hours/week for first 4 weeks, then 2 hours/week for the following 4 weeks. Expectation set in mentor roster.
- Mentor compensation: 2 hours/week of mentoring flagged as "time goodwill" and can be logged to team capacity planning.
- Metrics: mentee time-to-first-PR, number of support tickets opened to infra teams, and mentor satisfaction survey after 6 weeks.

Escalation and Support
- First-line: Mentor and sponsor. For access failures, ping #access-ops (Slack) with request ID.
- Second-line: Platform Concierge (oncall rotation listed on the internal roster).
- Security incidents: Immediately email sec-incident@redwood.ai and create incident ticket referencing the request ID.

Automated Deprovisioning and Renewal
- All satellite access is issued with an expiration date. Access Portal will notify requestor and sponsor 7 days before expiry.
- Auto-renewal: requestor can submit renewal up to 14 days before expiry. Renewals require sponsor re-approval. Max cumulative duration is 12 months.
- Early deprovisioning: Sponsor or People Ops can close a request; provisioning automation will revoke tokens and remove Okta group membership within 1 hour of approval.

Audit and Compliance Requirements
- Quarterly audit: People Ops will run an access report for all active satellite grants and send to Security for review.
- Retention: access request records are retained for 3 years.
- Proof of least-privilege: for any prod or high-risk grant, the sponsor must provide a short justification and acceptance of additional monitoring.

Example CLI snippets and YAML for scoped-contributor request (paste into Access Portal advanced field)

---yaml
requester: jane.doe@redwood.ai
team: Data Science – Project Nimbus
scope: scoped-contributor
repos:
  - github.com/redwood/example-repo
nonprod_project: gcp-nimbus-dev
duration_days: 60
mentor_requested: true
---

Quick Troubleshooting (common issues)
- Missing GitHub repo permissions: confirm org membership; if the repo is private, ensure the repo slug is correct.
- GCP project not visible: verify billing account mapping and requestor's email domain.
- Vault tokens failing: rotate token via the Access Portal and confirm environment variable names.

KPIs and Success Criteria
- Primary KPIs: time-to-first-PR, percentage of requests fulfilled within SLA, mentor program NPS.
- Target: 90% of standard requests fulfilled within 24 business hours; mentor NPS >= 8/10.

Offboarding and Lessons Learned
- Offboarding checklist (automated): revoke Okta groups, disable deploy tokens, remove from Slack-private channels, archive any ephemeral GCP projects, and and mark request closed.
- Post-mortem: for engagements > 3 months, mentor must submit a short 1-page summary with wins, blockers, and suggested improvements. This gets added to the Access Portal record.

Appendix: Useful links and templates
- Access Portal: /tools/access-portal
- Mentor roster and sign-up: /people/mentor-roster
- Access templates (raw): /eng-platform/templates/access-templates.yaml
- Emergency contact: security oncall: +1-555-0123 (internal only)

Frequently Asked Questions
- Q: Can a contractor be given permanent access if the engagement extends beyond 12 months?
  A: No — convert to full-time hire or re-issue a new request with full sponsorship and review.
- Q: Who pays for additional GCP costs created by a satellite project?
  A: The sponsoring team covers costs. Chargeback tags are required at provisioning time.

Change Log
- 2027-03-15: Playbook created (Priya Natarajan).
- 2027-05-10: Added fast-lane SLA and mentor compensation guidance (reviewers: Marcus Lee).
- 2027-06-02: Tightened renewal rules and clarified audit cadence (Security input).

payload.page_title: Participant-Led Career Sprints and Access Workbook

sections.body: This workbook formalizes a participant-driven approach to early career momentum at Redwood. It bundles: a repeatable sprint cadence for role-focused development, a prescriptive access and tooling checklist for new and transitioning contributors, and a short manager/mentor playbook to normalize expectations. The workbook is intended for new hires, people managers, mentors, and people-ops partners.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Reduce variability in the first 90 days for engineers, product, and platform contributors.
- Make access provisioning predictable and measurable (target: 48 business hours for full toolset).
- Align career sprint outcomes to competency ladders and role-level expectations.
sections.heading: Why this exists

sections.body:
- Scope: individual contributor onboarding (IC1–IC4), manager onboarding, cross-functional rotation support, and lateral role transitions. Does NOT replace role-specific technical onboarding labs for specialized infra or research tracks.
- Audience: new joiners, hiring managers, buddy/mentor, people-ops, engineering leads.
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
- Sprint: 14 calendar days focused on 1–2 measurable outcomes (e.g., merge a non-trivial PR, ship a docs-first integration).
- Access Bundle: standard set of accounts/entitlements required for a role to be productive (see Access Matrix).
- Activation Window: time between account creation request and completion. Target SLA: 48 business hours.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Document owner: People Ops (Priya Nambiar)
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review with engineering and product DRI (next review: 2026-05-15)
- Escalation path: people-ops -> hiring manager -> Head of People Ops.
sections.heading: Owner and maintenance

sections.body:
1) Kickoff (Day 0–1): participant selects a sprint goal with manager/mentor sign-off. Write a 1-paragraph success criteria.
2) Planning (Day 1–2): list tasks, blockers, and required accesses. Assign a buddy for technical review.
3) Execution (Day 3–12): daily check-ins (asynchronous ok) and two demo moments: mid-sprint and final demo.
4) Review (Day 13–14): public write-up of outcomes, artifacts (PRs, docs, tests), and a 1–3 line reflection.
sections.heading: Sprint design pattern (participant-led)

sections.body:
- New Backend IC: ship a telemetry-enhanced endpoint behind feature flag + add an e2e smoke test.
- Product PM transition: run a 2-week scoped validation session with 5 customers and produce a prioritized decision memo.
- SRE rotation: run a pageload test for a non-critical service and update runbook with three remediation points.

Pre-sprint checklist (manager + people-ops):
1. Confirm role-level Access Bundle assigned.
2. Approve sprint goal and success criteria.
3. Assign buddy and reviewer.
4. Schedule mid-sprint demo slot.
5. Ensure workspace and required infra (test cluster, dataset mocks) available.
sections.heading: Sprint examples (role-aligned)

sections.body:
| Bundle name      | Typical roles           | Minimum entitlements (examples)                                        | Provision SLA |
|------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| Core Contributor | IC1–IC3                 | Okta SSO, GSuite, GitHub (repo-read + team membership), Jira, Slack     | 48 business hrs |
| Engineer Plus    | IC2–IC4                 | + AWS console read, KMS request role, Redwood Console dev project view | 48 business hrs |
| Infra Operator   | SRE/Infra roles         | + Prod VPN, PagerDuty, Cluster admin (scoped)                         | 72 business hrs |
| Manager         | People/Eng Managers     | + Manager dashboards, 1:1 scheduling tools, compensation ladder view   | 48 business hrs |
sections.heading: Access Matrix (standard bundles)

sections.body:
- Account requests: use the "Access Requests" form (URL internal: /tools/access-requests). Include new-joiner email, start date, team, and sprint intent.
- GitHub team invite: /cli (internal) -> `gh org invite --team \"team-name\" user@example.com`
- Okta SWAT ticket: create ticket in Jira project OPS-ACCESS with label `okta-provision`.
- Redwood Console project access: add to project via Console > Projects > Manage > Add Member (role: viewer/dev).
sections.heading: Provisioning details and commands

sections.body:
- Activation Window: target median 24 hrs, p95 < 72 hrs.
- Sprint completion rate: percent of participant-led sprints that meet success criteria within 14 days (target 80%).
- Buddy review turnaround: median 48 hrs.

Role ladder alignment guidance (how sprints map to growth signals):
- IC1: deliver a scoped change with mentor support; demonstrate basic code quality and documentation.
- IC2: independently own an end-to-end small feature, instrumenting metrics and follow-up fixes.
- IC3: lead an integration across teams, propose design tradeoffs, mentor IC1/IC2 contributors.
- IC4+: shape priorities, own cross-product initiatives, and influence roadmap trade-offs.
sections.heading: Service SLA & metrics to track

sections.body:
1. During offer stage: confirm Access Bundle and sprint expectation on offer email.
2. Day 0: set first sprint goal in the candidate's onboarding doc.
3. Day 1–2: unblock access requests and confirm buddy.
4. Mid-sprint: attend the demo and provide documented feedback (use template below).
5. Sprint review: update the individual's onboarding checklist and record signals for calibration conversation.
sections.heading: Manager/mentor playbook (quick steps)

sections.body:
- Sprint goal: (1–2 lines)
- Outcome: (success / partial / blocked)
- Evidence: (links to PRs, docs, dashboards)
- Coaching notes: (3 short bullets)
- Recommended next sprint focus: (1 sentence)
sections.heading: Manager feedback template (use in PR or demo notes)

sections.body:
- Sprint README (1 page): goal, steps, blockers, artifacts, retrospective note.
- PRs and tests: linked to the sprint README.
- Buddy sign-off: one-line confirmation in the README.
sections.heading: Artifacts to capture (required)

sections.body:
- Failure: delayed access prevents execution. Mitigation: escalate to people-ops within 24 hrs; temporarily provide a sandbox environment.
- Failure: ambiguous sprint goal. Mitigation: require manager sign-off on success criteria before Day 2.
- Failure: no buddy engagement. Mitigation: people-ops maintains a rotating on-call buddy roster for core teams.

Onboarding tooling quick-reference (links and what to capture):
- HR / Payroll onboarding: capture W-4 / local tax forms, emergency contact, preferred name. Owner: People Ops.
- Okta: enable MFA, verify SSO groups. Owner: Security.
- GitHub: accept organization invite, set 2FA, join team repos. Owner: Eng Team Admin.
- Redwood Console sandbox: confirm project access and sample request to public models. Owner: Platform.

payload.page_title: Operational Accelerator: Onboarding & Career Skills Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's Operational Accelerator: a combined onboarding, role-progression, and tools-access program designed to reduce time-to-impact for new joiners and provide a repeatable pathway for career growth. It is oriented around 30/60/90 milestones, a lightweight competency matrix, manager and buddy responsibilities, and an explicit tools & benefits checklist to remove operational friction.

Audience:
- New joiners (IC and manager hires)
- Hiring managers and people-ops partners
- Onboarding buddies and mentors
- Team leads responsible for role progression

Goals:
- Standardize first-90-day experience so >80% of hires reach first production change within 45 days.
- Provide transparent promotion indicators tied to measurable outcomes.
- Ensure consistent access to tools (Okta, GitHub, Datadog, Slack, Confluence, Jira, PagerDuty) by day 3.

Owners & escalation:
- Program owner: People Ops Onboarding (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Manager enablement: People Ops Enablement (owner: Marcus Nguyen)
- Tooling & access: IT Access Team (owner: Priya Rao)
- Escalation channel: #onboarding-escalations (Slack) and onboarding@redwood.com

High-level workflow (step-by-step):
1) Offer & pre-boarding (People Ops)
   - Send Welcome Packet (benefits summary, first-week agenda, required compliance training).
   - Provision core accounts (Okta, Google Workspace) and request hardware.
2) Day 0–3: Orientation and access validation
   - Tasks: join Slack, sign up for SSO, clone internal repo, complete security awareness.
   - Access SLA: IT to confirm GitHub/Confluence/Datadog/PagerDuty provisioning within 72 hours; target 95% success.
3) Week 1: Domain ramp and first contribution
   - Assign onboarding buddy for 30 days.
   - Complete role-specific quickstarts (codebase tour, run local server, submit a doc change).
4) Weeks 2–6: Deepening and ownership
   - Participate in at least one cross-team planning meeting.
   - Complete two technical or product learning modules from the Redwood Learning Catalog.
5) Day 45: Manager check-in and readiness review
   - Expected outcome: candidate has made a production-adjacent contribution or owned a small customer-facing task.
6) 60–90 days: Impact & career conversation
   - 90-day review with manager + people-ops to assess competencies and next steps.

Competency Matrix (summary table):
- Technical Craft: Contributes code/architecture for area; demonstrates debugging and testing practices.
- Product Judgment: Understands customer impact and tradeoffs for feature decisions.
- Collaboration: Cross-team communication, effective PRs, constructive reviews.
- Ownership: Delivers end-to-end features or ops enhancements.
- Influence (IC4+): Mentorship, design leadership, measurable improvements in team delivery.

Promotion indicators (what we look for):
- Scope & scale: Breadth of impact beyond single project.
- Autonomy: Consistently delivers with minimal guidance.
- Quality: Ship quality work (low rework, automated tests, monitoring).
- Leadership: Mentors others, leads design reviews, and improves processes.
- Metrics: Demonstrable improvements in KPIs (latency, cost, usage, customer satisfaction).

Manager checklist (first 90 days):
- Before Day 1: Review role onboarding plan and confirm mentor.
- Day 1: 30-minute alignment meeting; set 30/60/90 expectations.
- Weekly: 1:1 touchpoints and blockers log.
- Day 45: Complete readiness form and sign off on first-impact milestone.
- Day 90: Conduct formal 90-day review and update role development plan.

Buddy program (operational details):
- Role: technical and culture partner for 30 days.
- Time commitment: 2–3 hours/week for guided sessions.
- Suggested sessions: code walkthrough, architecture primer, release process demo, benefits intro.

Tools & access checklist (owner: IT Access Team):
- Required by Day 1: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, GitHub read access.
- Required by Day 3: CI/CD pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions runner access), internal dev cluster, local infra secrets (via Vault).
- Optional within Week 1: Datadog dashboard access, PagerDuty on-call shadowing, Analytics console.
- Verification: Use this CLI snippet to validate access: 
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OKTA_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.company/me || echo "Okta failed"

Benefits orientation (first-week actions):
- Enroll in health plan: deadline 30 days (People Ops contact: benefits@redwood.com).
- 401(k) auto-enrollment details and contribution guide.
- Flexible work stipend claim instructions (submit via workplace-portal).

Hiring & interview guidance (for hiring managers):
- Interview loop template (recommended): Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager -> Technical assessment -> System design (for senior roles) -> Behavioral -> Offer debrief.
- Calibration: use canned rubrics for Role Competency, with explicit accept/decline thresholds.
- Time-to-hire target: 30 days from recruiter screen to offer for IC roles.

Sample 30/60/90 milestones (IC example):
- 30 days: Local dev environment up, first merged documentation change, understands main product flows.
- 60 days: Small feature delivered to staging, has created or improved test coverage and runbook.
- 90 days: Owns a feature area bug triage, contributed to a cross-team tech discussion, completed career development check-in.

Career-path sketch (engineering example):
- IC1 (New grad/entry): Focus on individual deliverables and learning.
- IC2 (Experienced IC): Solid delivery, effective PRs, starts mentoring interns.
- IC3 (Senior IC): Broad ownership, system design, influences product decisions.
- IC4 (Staff): Cross-team impact, technical leadership, sizable project alphas.
- IC5 (Principal): Company-level technical leadership and long-term roadmap shaping.
- Manager tracks: EM1->EM2->Senior EM with parallel expectations for team growth, hiring, and people development.

Promotion process (practical steps):
1) Candidate prepares promotion packet: 2–3 examples of impact, metrics, and peer feedback.
2) Manager collects at least 3 reviewer reports and confirms timeline.
3) Calibration panel reviews and recommends decision within 30 days.
4) People Ops communicates outcome and next development plan.

Operational metrics (how we measure success):
- Time-to-first-merge (target: median <= 21 days).
- Access SLA (target: 95% of hires have core tools by Day 3).
- 90-day retention target: >= 95% actively employed and in role.
- Manager satisfaction: post-90-day survey score >= 4.2/5.

Templates & artifacts (links and examples):
- 90-day review template: /confluence/templates/90-day-review
- Promotion packet checklist: /confluence/templates/promotion-packet
- Onboarding playbook checklist (CSV): /confluence/downloads/onboard-checklist.csv

Common failure modes & mitigations:
- Missing access: escalate to IT Access Team within 24 hours and run fallback cloud-based lab access.
- No clear 1:1 cadence: manager must schedule weekly 1:1s in first 30 days or People Ops will assign a coaching session.
- Lack of early impact: assign targeted short-milestone projects with clear acceptance criteria.

Appendix: Sample 90-day readiness form (fields):
- Technical accomplishments (bulleted)
- Customer/product impact (numbers or examples)
- Peer feedback summary (2–3 quotes)
- Areas for development and support requests

- 2026-06-02: Updated tools SLA language and promotion packet flow (reviewers: M. Nguyen, P. Rao)

sections.body: This compact playbook bundles three closely related employee experiences: the first 90 days of onboarding, the 'career safety net' used to manage role transitions and expectations, and a concise internal-tools quickstart required to be productive at Redwood. It is intended for hiring managers, new hires, people-ops partners, and managers handling role transitions.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Reduce time-to-impact for new hires to 30 days for basic production contributors, 60 days for engineers contributing to core runtime, and 90 days for cross-functional ownership of projects.
- Provide a visible, humane set of expectations (the Career Safety Net) for employees facing role changes, performance improvement, or return-from-leave transitions.
- Standardize onboarding tool access so engineering and non-engineering teams can complete the technical checklist in the first week.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:

- Internal tooling access request: https://id.redwood.example/access-requests
- Role ladder reference: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027

1) First-90 Onboarding framework

Intro: The First-90 is split into three clearly defined phases with owner responsibilities and measurable outcomes. Managers must publish a simple 90-day plan for each hire in the onboarding doc within 48 hours of start date.
sections.heading: Quick links (operational)

sections.body:
- Day 0–7: Orientation + Access
  - Outcomes: account creation, README for team, local dev + CI run, one small doc or PR merged.
  - Owner: Hiring manager + buddy.
  - Must-complete checklist items:
    1. HR paperwork completed (People Ops)
    2. Okta + SSO validated and 2FA registered
    3. Internal mailbox and Slack channels joined
    4. Dev environment: run unit tests locally and submit a tiny fix/typo PR

- Day 8–30: Contribution + Feedback
  - Outcomes: shipping a first scoped task (bug fix, evaluation harness test, doc change), first check-in with manager, initial career conversation.
  - Owner: Manager (weekly 1:1)
  - Success metrics: PR landed, code review feedback implemented, buddy signoff on operational readiness.

- Day 31–90: Ownership + Integration
  - Outcomes: ownership of a small feature, runbook or eval suite component; documented handoff for cross-team dependencies.
  - Owner: Manager (biweekly 1:1)
  - Success metrics: service/deck ownership identified, promotion of knowledge via a 30-min team demo, and an updated career plan in Lattice/Growth platform.

2) Career Safety Net (CSN) — humane role transitions and support

Purpose: The CSN is a people-first protocol to support employees who are reassigned, returning from extended leave, or subject to a performance conversation. It codifies expectations, resources, and timelines so transitions are explicit and fair.
sections.heading: Phases and outcomes

sections.body:
- Transparency: clear goals, measurable checkpoints, and written agreements (no surprise change of expectations).
- Time-bounded: typical CSN plans last 6–12 weeks depending on context.
- Support-first: training, mentorship, and reasonable load reduction when appropriate.
- Escalation clarity: defined steps if objectives are not met.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:

- Review date and next steps (promote, extend, role change)

2. If no sustained improvement: formal HR performance process, with People Ops and legal review as needed.

3) Benefits, Perks, and Accessibility highlights

This section captures the practical touchpoints new hires need to use benefits and ensure accessibility needs are handled early. It is a companion to the full Benefits Catalog.

4) Internal tools quickstart (minimal commands and access flow)

Objective: get a new hire capable of completing the Dev + Prod checklist within the first week. This section lists the most common commands, access flows, and troubleshooting tips.

Authentication and identity

payload.page_title: IC Manager Toolbox and Ladder Playbook

sections.body:
SUMMARY
This document describes the 'IC Manager Toolbox' — a curated set of internal tools, permissions, workflows, and career-mapping guidance that enable individual contributors (ICs) to take on manager-like responsibilities for projects, mentoring, and operational ownership without a formal manager title. The playbook explains how ICs get access to tooling, how responsibilities map to career ladders, promotion criteria, and how benefits and perks align with expanded scope.

PURPOSE
- Reduce friction for cross-functional IC ownership (tech leads, project owners, on-call leads) by standardizing access and expectations.
- Make role progression transparent: what skills, deliverables, and operational scope are expected at each IC level when operating with manager responsibilities.
- Preserve clarity between line management duties and IC leadership activities; offer safety rails and escalation paths.

SCOPE AND AUDIENCE
This playbook is for: software engineers, ML engineers, product managers working as ICs, people managers who approve elevated IC privileges, and People Ops. It covers tooling access, permission templates, 90-day onboarding checklists, promotion rubrics, and benefit eligibility related to expanded role scope.

IC MANAGER TOOLBOX — WHAT IT IS
The IC Manager Toolbox is a package of tools and permissions that are granted as a single bundle when an IC is approved for expanded scope for a defined period. Typical capabilities included:
- Project workspace creation and lifecycle ownership in Confluence and Jira.
- Team-level on-call rotation assignment and the ability to create runbooks.
- Budget view-only for assigned feature flags/allocated infra through the Cost Console.
- Ability to create private RFCs and propose policy changes.
- Mentorship hours allocation (formal 1:1 slots and mentee assignments).
- Hiring interview scheduling privileges (panel invites) and interview feedback templates.

TOOLING INVENTORY (QUICK REFERENCE)
| Tool | Purpose | Default Owner | Access Process | Notes |
|-------|---------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| Confluence Team Space | Project docs & runbooks | Eng Platform | Request via "/access create-space" ticket | Template: ic-team-space-v1 |
| Jira Project (read/write) | Task/issue ownership | Eng Platform | People Ops approval + manager signoff | Use board template: feature-owner-board |
| On-call roster manager | Roster edits, runbook updates | SRE | Pager duty group grant | Scoped to services assigned |
| Cost Console (view) | Budget transparency | Finance Ops | Audit request: cost-console-view | No charge modification |
| Interview Scheduler | Candidate scheduling | Recruiting | Self-assign after panel approval | Use interview feedback template |

ACCESS AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW (NUMBERS)
1. Nomination: IC or manager submits an IC Manager Toolbox nomination form (short form: why, scope, duration, expected outcomes).
2. Manager endorsement: direct manager provides endorsement + lists collaborators and expected time allocation.
3. People Ops review: confirms policy alignment, checks capacity and benefit eligibility.
4. Tooling grant: Eng Platform / SRE / Finance apply scoped permissions (7 business days target).
5. Confirmation kickoff: People Ops schedules 30-minute kickoff with IC, manager, and tooling owners.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Objective and target impact (200–400 words)
- Expected duration (3 / 6 / 12 months)
- Time allocation estimate (e.g., 20% mentorship / 10% interviews / 70% IC work)
- List of services or projects in scope
- Manager endorsement (name and signature)

ONBOARDING CHECKLIST (FIRST 90 DAYS)
1. Day 0–3: Confirm toolbox access, create project Confluence space, and import runbook template.
2. Week 1: Hold kickoff meeting with stakeholders; publish 90-day plan on Confluence.
3. Week 2–4: Shadow current on-call lead or manager for operational handover.
4. Month 1: Update runbook, set up monitoring alerts (with SRE assistance), and schedule biweekly mentor office hours.
5. Month 2: Lead first project retro and write a short process RFC for one internal workflow.
6. Month 3: Submit self-assessment against the IC leadership rubric; manager and reviewer provide feedback.

IC LEADERSHIP AND PROMOTION RUBRIC (OVERVIEW)
Promotion decisions that consider manager-like responsibilities use the standard IC ladder plus three operational axes:
- Delivery & technical impact (feature ownership, cross-team outcomes).
- People leadership (mentorship quality, interview impact, cross-team coordination).
- Operational ownership (incidence handling, runbook completeness, cost optimization).

Scoring guidance (used in calibration, simplified for transparency):
- Meets expectations: consistently reliable delivery, contributes to team health, maintains runbooks.
- Exceeds expectations: leads cross-team initiatives, mentors multiple ICs, drives cost or reliability improvements.
- Exceptional: sustained organizational impact, repeatable mentoring outcomes, recognized as go-to lead for service area.

PROMOTION CHECKLIST (SAMPLE)
- 2+ demonstrated end-to-end projects with measurable impact (KPIs defined).
- 6+ months of consistent mentorship/leadership activity and documented mentee outcomes.
- Clear operational ownership: runbooks updated, SLA/SLO observability checks in place.
- Peer and manager endorsements (2–4 reviewers recommended).
- Up-to-date career mapping document and manager-derived competency examples.

BENEFITS & PERKS ALIGNMENT
ICs with Toolbox privileges become eligible for a set of role-expansion benefits while retaining IC employment terms. Benefit eligibility examples:
- Leadership Stipend: a monthly $250 stipend to support team-building (offsite snacks, swag, books).
- Mentorship Hours Bank: up to 4 hours/week of protected time for mentoring and interviews (tracked in weekly capacity).
- Professional Development Boost: $2,000/year training allowance for leadership or coaching classes in addition to baseline L&D.
- Ergonomics/Hybrid Office Upgrade: one-time $600 allowance when increased coordination is required (team hubs, extended travel).
These benefits are granted for the approved duration and reviewed at the end of the term for continuation.

PERMISSION SCAFFOLD (EXAMPLE TABLE)
| Permission | When granted | Scope | Revocation condition |
|-----------|--------------|-------|----------------------|
| Jira Project Admin (limited) | On approval | Only for assigned project boards | Project handover or end date |
| Confluence Space Admin | On approval | Own project space templates | Major policy violation or end date |
| On-call roster edit | After shadowing | Services assigned only | If operational errors exceed thresholds |

ESCALATION & GUARDRAILS
- ICs are not line managers by default. This playbook does not change headcount or performance management responsibilities. Any direct reports remain the manager's responsibility.
- If an IC needs to perform personnel actions (e.g., formal performance feedback, salary discussions), they must escalate to People Ops and the direct manager.
- Operational error threshold: 3 unmitigated incidents in a 6-month period where runbooks or monitoring were not followed will trigger a review and potential temporary revocation of toolbox privileges.

INTERNAL TOOLS QUICK REFERENCE AND CONTACTS
- Eng Platform: eng-platform@redwood.com — responsible for Confluence/Jira templates and access grants.
- SRE: sre@redwood.com — runbook reviews, on-call onboarding, monitoring.
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com — nominations, benefit approvals, conflict resolution.
- Finance Ops: finance-ops@redwood.com — cost console view grants and budget questions.

TEMPLATES AND EXAMPLES (SNIPPETS)

OWNERSHIP, REVIEW CYCLE, AND EXCEPTIONS
- Owner: People Ops maintains this playbook; Eng Platform, SRE, and Finance Ops operate the underlying tooling.
- Review cadence: Annual review every Q1 with ad-hoc updates for platform changes.
- Exceptions: Request exception via People Ops; all exceptions must include a rollback plan and defined expiry.

RELATED PAGES
- /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-and-career-safety-net-2028
- /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027

FEEDBACK
Send feedback and improvement suggestions to people-ops@redwood.com or open a PR on the HR handbook repo.

APPENDIX (PROMOTION TEMPLATE CHECKLIST)
1) Impact summary (one page)
2) Measurable outcomes (metrics and dates)
3) Manager endorsement and time allocation confirmation
4) 2–4 peer reviewers with short statements
5) Updated career mapping document

sections.body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the operating model for role enablement, first‑year tooling access, and career stage expectations at Redwood. It harmonizes People Ops workflows, the internal toolchain, and engineering/product role ladders so new hires and movers get the right access, learning path, and milestones with minimal friction.

Purpose
-------
- Reduce friction and time-to-impact for new hires and internal role changes.
- Centralize ownership and SLAs for access requests and provisioning.
- Provide a transparent, stage-based career enablement blueprint that aligns onboarding tasks with measurable milestones.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors with >3 months engagement, and interns on multi-month rotations. Covers: provisioning for company systems (SSO apps, cloud accounts, repositories, internal dashboards), mandatory training, role-specific tool access, and first-year staged milestones.

Principles
----------
1) Least Privilege by Default: roles receive minimal default access; additional access is granted via documented approval flows.
2) Time-to-Impact Targets: new hires should reach baseline productivity within 30 days and role-level competence within 120 days.
3) Self-Serve When Safe: automated badges and access requests are preferred for low-risk tools; manual approvals retained for sensitive systems (KMS, billing, production clusters).
4) Stage-aligned Learning: onboarding tasks map to defined career stages and measurable outputs.

Role & Career Stage Matrix (summary)
----------------------------------
Columns: Role Family | Typical Entry Level | 30d Baseline | 120d Competency | Access Tier
| Engineering | SWE-I | Local dev environment, repo read + CI debug | Can ship small bugfixes, own a low-risk service | Tier 2 (dev infra, staging)
| Product | PM-I | Product wiki, analytics dashboards | Run small scope features end-to-end | Tier 1 (product analytics)
| Infra/SRE | SRE-I | Monitoring dashboards, dev clusters | Triage incidents, own runbooks | Tier 3 (prod oncall with approvals)
Notes: Tier 1 = non-sensitive business tooling; Tier 2 = staging infra and feature flags; Tier 3 = production infrastructure, KMS, billing.

Onboarding & Access Checklist (first 30 days)
-------------------------------------------
1. Pre-Start (People Ops): create SSO account, set up device stipend and hardware order, assign buddy and manager. Target: 5 days before start.
2. Day 0–3: account activation, MFA enrollment, company policies acknowledgement, baseline security training (30 min).
3. Day 3–10: toolchain setup: local dev environment, repo access, CI read, Slack & calendar groups. Badge provisioning: Developer-Basic / Product-Basic / Analyst-Basic.
4. Day 10–30: sandbox tasks, first PR or product write-up, mentor check-ins weekly, request additional scoped access (databases, staging) via Access Request form.

Access Request Flow (owners and SLAs)
-----------------------------------
- Low-risk (Tier 1)
  - Owner: People Ops
  - Process: Self-serve portal (Internal Access Hub) -> auto-approval if role mapping matches.
  - SLA: 8 business hours for provisioning.
- Medium-risk (Tier 2)
  - Owner: Team Lead (Engineering/Product) + Infra approver
  - Process: Submit request in Access Hub -> Slack notification to approvers -> manual approval -> provisioning job.
  - SLA: 2 business days.
- High-risk (Tier 3)
  - Owner: Security + Product/Infra Manager
  - Process: Access Hub -> security review -> logged justification + training completion -> ephemeral credential issuance where possible.
  - SLA: 3–5 business days depending on context.

Example: request production DB read access (Tier 3)
1. Submit Access Hub form with justification, linked ticket or runbook entry.
2. Attach manager approval (email or Slack thread).
3. Security reviews logs, requests brief architecture note from requestor.
4. If approved: ephemeral read-only credentials issued for 12 hours; long-term access requires quarterly re-approval.

Request CLI snippet (for self-serve tooling)
------------------------------------------

redwood-iam request-access --resource staging-cluster --role dev

------------------------------
- Mandatory (all hires): Security Essentials (30m), Code of Conduct (15m), Data Handling Primer (20m).
- Role-specific 30d tracks: Engineering Setup & CI, Product Metrics 101, Analytics SQL primers.
- 120d stretch goals: own a small project, present a demo at team retro, pass a role-specific checklist review with manager.

Access Matrix (condensed table)
------------------------------
Service | Default for New Hire | Request Flow | Tier
staff-ldap | No | People Ops auto-provision | 1
repo-org | Read | Manager request for write | 2
staging-cluster | No | Team Lead approval -> infra provisioning | 2
prod-cluster | No | Security + Manager approval -> ephemeral creds | 3
billing-console | No | Finance approval required | 3
KMS/HSM | No | Security-only with audit justification | 3

Stage-based Milestones and Signals
----------------------------------
- Day 30 Signal: first merged PR or product spec, buddy sign-off on environment.
- Day 60 Signal: independent troubleshooting of a minor incident / ability to run central integration tests.
- Day 120 Signal: owns an end-to-end card, delivered and reviewed; manager checklist completed.

Escalation & Exceptional Cases
-----------------------------
- If a provisioning SLA is missed by >48 hours, the People Ops on-call (escalation channel #people-ops-escalations) is notified and a ticket is auto-created with urgency P2.
- For denied high-risk requests, Security will provide a written rationale and recommend mitigations (read-only, ephemeral, masked dataset).

Maintenance & Ownership
-----------------------
- People Ops: maintain baseline badges, onboarding timeline, and low-risk provisioning.

- Security: governs Tier 3 approvals, quarterly access reviews, and audit evidence.

Operational Metrics (tracked in Redwood Console)
---------------------------------------------

- % of new hires reaching Day 30 signal — target: 90%.
- Quarterly access review completion rate — target: 100% for Tier3 scoped owners.

Frequently Asked Questions
-------------------------
Q: I need temporary production access to investigate a customer issue.
A: Open an urgent Access Hub request and tag your manager and security in the form. For high-severity incidents, on-call security provides emergency elevation (audited, ephemeral).
