sections.body:
Purpose:
This document is a single-source playbook for GTM and sales engineering when engaging enterprise prospects for Redwood Inference. It combines positioning and messaging for buyer personas, competitive battlecards, a repeatable POC and deal-acceleration checklist, pricing guidance and negotiation guardrails, a compact pitch-deck outline, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this to shorten sales cycles, reduce back-and-forth on security questions, and align SDR/AE/SE actions during evaluation windows.

Executive summary:
- Redwood Inference sells a production-first inference platform (hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployment) that optimizes latency, cost, and reliability for LLM-powered features.
- This playbook focuses on enterprise deals (>= $50k ARR) that require SLA, audit evidence, and predictable capacity.
- Primary win themes: predictable economics, deployment flexibility (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and production observability (token-level cost tracing, rollouts, regressions).

Elevator pitches (30s):
- For Engineering Leaders: "Ship LLM features reliably — Redwood gives predictable latency and token economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, plus observability to catch regressions before customers do."
- For Platform/Infra: "Standardize inference across teams with a single runtime and rollout tooling — same API, consistent metrics, and fine-grained cost controls for tenant isolation."
- For Security/Compliance: "Private control plane, KMS integrations, and audit-grade logs let you run sensitive workloads on-prem or in a customer VPC while preserving developer ergonomics."

Positioning by persona (key messages and proof points):
- Engineering / ML Engineers:
  - Message: predictable throughput and latency with model lifecycle controls.
  - Proof points: per-route latency SLOs (e.g. p95 < 120ms for curated models on Dedicated), continuous batching and KV cache to reduce token cost by 10–40% depending on workload.
- Platform / Infra:
  - Message: unified runtime across environments reduces operational variance.
  - Proof points: identical API surface, automated fallbacks to compatible model variants, autoscaling policies tied to commit tiers.
- Product / PMs:
  - Message: deliver differentiated LLM features faster and retain cost control.
  - Proof points: referencing two-week POC -> production patterns and built-in quality monitoring / eval integrations.
- Security / Legal:
  - Message: private deployment option, SOC 2 controls, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM support, and full audit logging.
  - Proof points: sample SOC2 report page, example audit-log retention policies, and customer reference (see case study).

Competitive battlecards (short form):
- General cloud AI endpoints (major cloud provider managed endpoints):
  - Differentiator: Redwood focuses on inference economics + unified runtime for private/hybrid deployment; better tools for rollouts and regression detection.
  - Pressure points: cloud endpoints may win on raw model variety and account consolidation; emphasize Redwood's predictable throughput and cost controls.
- LLM API providers (hosted-first vendors):
  - Differentiator: Redwood offers Dedicated pools and Private deployment for customers who need isolation or committed throughput.
  - Pressure points: hosted-only providers can be simpler for small teams; push on enterprise risk and SLO guarantees.
- Inference infra vendors / self-hosted runtimes:
  - Differentiator: Redwood bundles runtime optimizations + orchestration + support + observability; less engineering lift than building in-house.
  - Pressure points: very large infra orgs may want full control — for those, highlight Redwood Private packaged options and on-prem support agreements.

Suggested rebuttals / objection scripts:
- "We can build this ourselves": 
  - Response: Building a runtime with production-grade autoscaling, KV cache, quantization profiles and rollouts is typically 9–18 months of focused effort. Redwood reduces time-to-production risk and provides measurable cost and latency telemetry out-of-the-box.
- "We are worried about data residency":
  - Response: We offer VPC/private control plane and on-prem packaging. We integrate with cloud KMS and support region-specific hosting for EU/APAC.
- "How do you handle model regressions?":
  - Response: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt/eval sets and raises regression alerts tied to rollouts. We support canary and auto-fallback policies to reduce customer impact.

Deal acceleration playbook (16-week enterprise cadence — condensed):
1) Discovery (week 0–1):
   - Owner: AE + SE.
   - Actions: capture business KPI (latency targets, cost targets, SLA needs), compliance constraints, expected QPS and peak bursts, preferred deployment mode.
   - Deliverable: Discovery memo (1 page) and preliminary sizing estimate.
2) Proposal & POC scoping (week 1–2):
   - Owner: AE + Solutions Architect.
   - Actions: define POC success criteria (latency, throughput, integration points), sample dataset rules, data handling plan (PII scramble or synthetic).
   - Deliverable: POC plan and timeline (max 4 weeks).
3) POC execution (week 2–6):
   - Owner: SE + Customer Eng.
   - Actions: run POC in Hosted or Dedicated sandbox, run load profile, collect latency/cost traces, validate SDK integration.
   - Success criteria (example): sustained p95 latency < target; per-token cost within 10% of estimate; no unresolvable quality regressions for key prompts.
4) Commercial & Security review (week 6–10):
   - Owner: AE + Legal + Security Eng.
   - Actions: lock down commercial terms, review DPA and SOC2 evidence, finalize procurement timelines and SOW.
5) Pilot -> Ramp (week 10–16):
   - Owner: Customer Success + SE.
   - Actions: production cutover plan, rollback policies, SLA handover, train internal ops.

POC checklist (must-have items):
- Sample traffic generator and expected QPS profile.
- Representative prompt set and evaluation harness.
- Performance trace access (token-level cost + latency heatmaps).
- Security review package (DPA, SOC2 summary, network diagrams).
- Contact list for escalation and support SLA.

Pricing guidance and negotiation guardrails (framework, not fixed price list):
- Pricing pillars:
  - Hosted (usage-based): per-token generation/embedding rates with tiered volume discounts. Ideal for fast time-to-value and small-to-medium workloads.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed GPU pools with guaranteed throughput and burst capacity add-ons. Best for predictable, high-volume inference.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): platform fee + deployment/setup + optional support contract. For regulated / air-gapped customers.

- Commercial play examples (anchor figures are illustrative ranges for negotiation; adjust with finance guidance):
  - Small enterprise POC (3–6 months): Hosted credits + implementation services ($25k–$75k total TCV).
  - Mid-enterprise (Dedicated small commit): $20k–$60k/month committed for predictable throughput.
  - Large enterprise / Private: Multi-month onboarding + platform fee $200k+ and support retainer.

- Discount guardrails:
  - Volume discounts: predefined breaks at 100k, 1M, and 5M monthly tokens for hosted volume.
  - Committed-term discounts: 10–30% off list for 12–36 month reserved Dedicated contracts.
  - Giveaways: implementation credits or extended trial (time boxed), not unlimited usage.
  - Escalation path for exceptions: require approvals from Sales Ops and VP Sales for any > 35% discount or early termination concession.

Pitch deck outline (10–15 slides recommended):
1) Title & hook: quick problem statement and proof point (latency/cost).
2) Customer pain: common infra/ops problems with existing inference (cost surprises, rolling upgrades, regressions).
3) Redwood solution: product overview (hosted/dedicated/private, runtime + console).
4) How it works: runtime + routing + caching + rollout diagram (textual diagram ok).
5) Performance & economics: sample benchmarks, cost delta examples for common workloads.
6) Security & compliance: deployment modes, KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
7) Case study highlight: concise success metrics.
8) POC plan & timeline: what we deliver in 4 weeks.
9) Pricing snapshot & next steps.
10) Appendix: deeper tech proofs, integration checklist.

One-page case study (sales-ready — useable as customer-facing collateral with permission):
- Customer: FinTech SaaS (anonymized: "LeadingPaymentsCo")
- Problem: inconsistent latency during peak billing window and cost overruns when using naive autoscaling.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Dedicated pool + KV caching + prefix caching for session prompts; integrated with existing SSO and KMS.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 430ms to 95ms during peak; per-token cost reduced by 28% due to caching and batching; 99.95% availability during billing cycles.
- Contact / reference: Customer success path available upon approval.

Security FAQ for prospects (short-form answers for AEs/SEs):
- Q: Where is my data stored and how do you support region controls?
  - A: Hosted offerings are region-aware and can be constrained to US/EU/APAC regions. Dedicated and Private give you full control of physical placement. We publish our region list in the deployment guide.
- Q: Do you provide a private control plane or on-prem deployment?
  - A: Yes — Redwood Private provides a customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem package) with optional air-gapped installation for regulated workloads.
- Q: How is data encrypted?
  - A: All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted (AES-256). For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
- Q: What audit evidence do you provide?
  - A: SOC 2 Type II report summary, system architecture diagrams, and audit-log exports (SIEM-compatible JSON). Full reports provided under NDA.
- Q: How do you handle PII / redaction?
  - A: PII policies are handled via ingestion rules (can redact or hash before storage). For POCs we recommend synthetic or redacted datasets; for production we integrate with customer data-masking pipelines.
- Q: What SLAs and support tiers are available?
  - A: Hosted: standard support with published uptime targets. Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; response and escalation per enterprise support tier. Private: configurable support with on-call options.
- Q: Do you perform penetration testing?
  - A: Yes — Redwood runs regular internal and annual third-party penetration tests. Summaries available under NDA.
- Q: Who owns the model outputs and telemetry?
  - A: Customer retains ownership of their data and outputs. Telemetry required for billing and performance tuning is accessible via console and APIs; customers can request deletion per data retention policies.

Operational playbook snippets (ops & enablement):
- SE enablement kit: 1) one-week internal ramp with product engineer, 2) scripted POC runbook with load generator, 3) templated discovery memo, 4) security package bundle (DPA, SOC2 summary, network diagram).
- Escalation matrix: include primary SE, solutions architect, customer success manager, and head of enterprise success. Attach PS engagement SLA for technical escalations.

Ownership & next steps:
- Playbook owner: Maya Patel (GTM enablement).
- Required reviews before publish: Security, Legal, and Sales Ops.
- Action items:
  1) SEs: validate the POC checklist during next 3 deals and provide feedback.
  2) AEs: adopt pricing guardrails and route any discount >35% to Sales Ops.
  3) PM/Product: update the performance benchmark table quarterly.

Appendix: Useful CLI/commands & references
- Example quick trace extraction (CLI):
  - redwoodctl traces export --service inference --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-01-07 --format json
- Contact list: AE escalation: ae-escalations@redwood.com; Enterprise SE on-call: se-enterprise@redwood.com

Last updated notes:
- 2026-02-15: Added security FAQ, pricing guardrails, and updated POC timeline based on field feedback (Q4 2025).
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft and structure created.

Purpose: This playbook provides field sales, solutions engineering, and technical account teams with a single-page style toolkit for running deployment-driven pilots and accelerating expansion. sections.body:
- Shorten pilot-to-contract cycle by reducing technical risk and clarifying success metrics.
- Equip sellers with crisp technical language and competitive differentiation for architecture and SLA conversations.
- Reduce legal/security cycles by surfacing standard answers and evidence.

Audience and when to use
- Sales Engineers: technical framing, demo checklists, POC success criteria.
- AEs and Solutions ETOs: value messaging for execs and procurement.
- Customer Security/Compliance: standardized FAQ and evidence links.
- Customer Success: onboarding checklist for day-1 production readiness.

Positioning and messaging summary

Core positioning statement
Redwood Inference is the inference platform that lets engineering teams move from experimental LLM proof-of-concept to predictable, cost-efficient production without rebuilding serving infrastructure. We combine a production-first runtime, policy-driven routing, and transparent economics so customers can control latency, cost, and availability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.

Top three buyer messages (short)
1) Predictable economics: per-token and per-embedding transparency plus batching and cache controls that reduce unit costs by up to 5x vs ad-hoc self-hosted stacks.
2) Production reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity with automated fallback to compatible model variants to meet 99.9% availability targets.
3) Enterprise controls: VPC/private deployments, KMS integration, and audit logging to meet regulated workloads.

Technical storylines for discovery calls
- Latency-first apps: highlight continuous batching, KV cache, and smart kernel selection to meet 50-200ms p95 token latency for short prompts on Dedicated tiers.
- Cost-constrained throughput: demonstrate batching/caching profiles and Optimize recommendations to model expected spend at target QPS.
- Data residency and isolation: present Redwood Private topology, KMS integration points, and audit log retention options.

Competitive brief (one-page table)
Competitor | Redwood advantage | Typical buyer objection | Short rebuttal
---|---|---|---
Large cloud AI endpoints | Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private | Buyer: cloud provider already has managed endpoints | Redwood: provides consistent SLA + predictable economics across regions and supports private air-gapped deployments that major providers do not offer out-of-the-box
Open-source self-hosting | Lower cost at scale but high ops burden | Buyer: we can run LLMs ourselves for cheaper | Redwood: reduces ops burden, provides quantization and kernel optimizations, and includes rollouts/fallbacks that reduce MTTD for regressions
Specialized inference vendors | Deep kernel tuning for specific hardware | Buyer: vendor claims better latency on niche hardware | Redwood: integrates kernel selection + routing and backs end-to-end SLOs with fallbacks and performance transparency for model variants

Pitch deck guidance and demo narrative (5 slides)
1) Problem slide: inconsistent latency, runaway inference costs, risky rollouts, and long ops cycles for custom stacks. Use customer stat: "66% of pilots stall due to serving complexity" (field sourced).
2) Value prop: show Redwood runtime, Optimize toolkit, and Console observability in a single diagram.
3) Demo: live generate (low-latency), show tracing and token-level cost KPI, then flip to dashboard showing canary rollout and regression alert.
4) Pricing & pilot: propose 8-week pilot, Dedicated trial credits, and success criteria.
5) Next steps & risks mitigations: security review path and escalation owner.

Pilot design template (numbered steps)
1) Align stakeholders: engineering, security, procurement, and a single executive sponsor.
2) Define success criteria: production QPS, p95 latency target, cost per 1M tokens, and qualitative tolerance for hallucination in top 100 prompts.
3) Select deployment mode: hosted API for feature proofs, Dedicated for latency/cost predictability, Private for regulatory needs.
4) Measure baseline: run standard prompt suite for 24 hours to capture token distribution, seq length, and cold/warm KV hit rates.
5) Configure runtime: batch policy, caching TTLs, quantization profile, and canary routing. Document config in 1 pager.
6) Run and iterate: weekly checkpoints, data for Optimize recommendations, and acceptance testing.
7) Hand-off: runbook and console dashboards delivered to customer success.

Technical configuration checklist (table)
Setting | Recommended default | Why it matters
---|---|---
Batch policy | 50ms dynamic batching / max batch 64 | Balances latency and throughput; reduces cost per token
KV cache TTL | 10 minutes for conversational workloads | Reduces repeated prefix compute; improves cold start behavior
Quantization profile | 8-bit dynamic for v2 models | Good latency/cost tradeoff; avoid for highest-fidelity ranking models
Tracing | Enabled with 7-day retention for pilot | Enables regression triage and cost attribution
SLO targets | p95 latency <= 250ms; availability >= 99.9% (Dedicated) | Standard commitments for production workloads

Pricing scenarios (short table)
Scenario | Suggested offer | How to sell it
---|---|---
Proof-of-value pilot | 8 weeks, Hosted credits 500k tokens, Free canary Dedicated hours (if applicable) | Frame as risk-free exploration with data to estimate run-rate
Deterministic production | Monthly Dedicated reservation with 6-month commit and burst capacity | Emphasize predictable unit economics and SLA
Private deployment | Annual platform license + onboarding fee + optional on-prem appliance | Position as compliance-first path with long-term TCO benefits

Short field scripts: objection handling
- Objection: "We already have model infra"
  Rebuttal: "Great — Redwood complements existing infra. We can route non-sensitive requests through hosted API for fast time-to-value while keeping sensitive inference in Private to reduce ops overhead and accelerate product launches."
- Objection: "Your pricing is opaque"
  Rebuttal: "We will run a benchmarking pilot to produce a per-1M-token cost model using your real prompts. Console shows token-level breakdown during the pilot so nothing is hidden."

Reference case study (compact)
Customer: FinTech data enrichment platform
Challenge: Unpredictable latency during peak market hours and unclear inference costs across teams
Pilot approach: 6-week Dedicated pilot with sequence-length characterization, dynamic batching, and KV caching. We ran a synthetic 48-hour peak simulation to validate p95 and cost.
Results: Reduced 95th percentile token latency from 420ms to 180ms and achieved a 3x reduction in cost per generated token using quantization and batching recommendations. Pilot converted to an annual Dedicated contract.

Security & compliance FAQ (targeted for prospect security teams)
Q1: What deployment modes support customer-managed keys?
A1: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS on request. Hosted API supports per-customer encryption keys for stored artifacts.

Q2: How are logs/audit trails handled?
A2: Console provides audit logs for inference requests, model changes, and rollout events. Retention defaults to 90 days for pilots and is configurable up to 7 years for enterprise contracts. Logs can be shipped to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog) via secure forwarders.

Q3: Is data used for model training?
A3: We do not use customer inference data to train public models. For hosted API we provide an opt-out; for Dedicated and Private customer data remains under their control.

Q4: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and patching?
A4: We maintain a public security disclosure policy and a quarterly patch cadence for managed components. Private customers can opt into an accelerated security patch SLA.

Q5: What certifications and audits are available?
A5: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is working toward ISO 27001. For enterprise Private deployments we provide evidence and can coordinate third-party audits under NDA.

Evidence checklist to attach to buyer packet
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- Encryption architecture diagram and key flow (PDF)
- Sample audit log export and schema
- Data residency and retention options table

Operational escalation and owners
- Regional SE owner: assign by AE during deal registration.
- Security contact: security-oncall@redwood.ai (initial triage)
- Enterprise GTM owner: Senior AE (contracting) and Solutions Eng lead for delivery.

Call-to-action and templates

Appendix: links and artifacts to include in prospect pack

Owners and next steps
- Owner: Asha Patel, GTM Technical Enablement

End of doc.

sections.body:
Overview

This page is a consolidated sales enablement handbook for GTM teams working with technical buyers evaluating Redwood Inference for conversational products. It couples user journey maps (developer and product-owner perspectives) with empirical price-sensitivity test templates and an evidence-backed competitive brief. The goal is to equip Sales Engineers, Solutions Architects, and AEs with repeatable conversation scripts, testable pricing scenarios, and clear security FAQ answers for prospect diligence.

Use cases in scope
- Real-time chatbots (sub-200ms token latency targets)
- Multi-turn assistants with long context (up to 64k tokens)
- High-throughput embedding and reranking pipelines
- Edge / hybrid deployments for regulated customers

Quick reference: what to carry to a technical call
1) Two-slide technical narrative (latency/cost tradeoffs + fallback story)
2) One-page pricing sensitivity table with 3 scenarios (pilot / scale / enterprise commit)
3) Live demo checklist (API keys, sample prompts, sample dataset, model variant to demo)
4) Security evidence bundle pointer (redwood-kms-evidence.pdf)

Section 1 — Conversational journey maps\nPurpose: map buyer personas to technical triggers, evaluation criteria, and Redwood talking points. For each persona, we present a short narrative, key metrics they care about, and suggested demo prompts.

Persona A: Platform Engineer (internal platform team)
- Evaluation triggers: standardize inference across teams, predictable unit economics, RBAC and compliance integration.
- Key metrics: tokens/sec per GPU, p95 latency, per-token cost, failure modes.
- Talking points: Dedicated pools, autoscale policies, per-route token accounting in Redwood Console, KMS integrations.
- Demo prompts: multi-tenant routing example + trace showing per-route latency breakdown.

Persona B: Product Lead (customer-facing feature owner)
- Evaluation triggers: response quality, consistent latency, rollback capability during quality regressions.
- Key metrics: quality eval pass rate on golden prompts, 99th percentile total time-to-first-token, canary rollout success rate.
- Talking points: Redwood Optimize for recommended quantization & batching, automatic rollback policies, prompt-set linked quality alerts.
- Demo prompts: A/B response comparison to show model variant choice impact and Redwood’s rollout controls.

Persona C: Security & Compliance Officer
- Evaluation triggers: data residency, auditability, key controls.
- Key metrics: encryption at rest/in transit, audit log retention, isolation topology (VPC + Private).
- Talking points: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), HSM/KMS integrations, per-request audit IDs, SOC2 and ISO evidence pointer.
- Demo prompts: audit log drilldown + show request header obfuscation and PII scrubbing options.

Section 2 — Price sensitivity test templates (method + scenarios)

Overview: We recommend running three price-sensitivity experiments during a pilot to calibrate required capacity and convert to a committed plan. The templates below are designed for customer pilots that will later become Dedicated or Private deployments.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Duration: 7–14 days per experiment
- Dataset: 5k representative user interactions (include extremes: long context, short prompts, multimodal if applicable)
- Metrics to capture: avg tokens/request, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens (hosted), end-to-end throughput
- Instrumentation: enable token-level billing metadata, route-level latency traces, and KV cache hit rate in Redwood Console

Pricing scenario matrix (table)
| Scenario | Description | Key thresholds | Recommended Redwood ask | Success criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Trial-Pilot | Low-volume proof (<= 5M tokens/month) | p95 < 500ms, cost < $0.02/1k tokens (hosted) | Free pilot credits + 2-week Dedicated trial | Evidence of consistent p95 and expected unit cost |
| Growth | Steady product usage (5M - 50M tokens/month) | p95 < 250ms, cost < $0.01/1k tokens | 6–12 month reserved capacity (Dedicated) with autoscale buffer | Unit economics within 15% of pilot projection |
| Enterprise-Commit | High volume + compliance (50M+ tokens/month or Private) | p95 < 150ms, contractual SLA 99.9% | Annual Reserved + Private deployment option and premium SLAs | Contract value aligns with expected TCO and cost-savings vs self-hosting |

Notes on negotiation levers
- Batching and caching profiles: quantify expected token reduction due to prefix caching (report cache hit rate).
- Model variants: provide cost deltas for top-performing 2–3 open models and a Redwood-optimized quantized variant.
- Commitment term: show 12 vs 36 month unit price curves and step-down discounts.

Section 3 — Proof points and compact case studies

Case study: FastReply (mid-market, conversational support)
- Problem: inconsistent SLA with prior LLM vendor, high per-session cost during peak spikes.
- What we did: migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled prefix caching for common support threads, and used Redwood Optimize recommendations to move to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-latency-critical routes.
- Result: 48% reduction in per-session cost, p95 latency improved from 820ms to 190ms, and successful canary rollout across 12k daily sessions.
- Materials: sample benchmarking report (redwood-fastreply-bench-2028.pdf).

Case study: FinAssist (regulated financial assistant)
- Problem: requirement for audit logs, KMS integration, and on-premise model hosting.
- What we did: deployed Redwood Private in customer VPC, integrated customer KMS with HSM-backed keys, and configured per-request audit IDs sent to the customer SIEM.
- Result: passed internal security review, met data residency requirements, and enabled product launch in an EU market.

Section 4 — Competitive brief (concise)

This section summarizes how to position Redwood against the three common counteroffers during technical evaluation. Keep this on a single page for deal rooms.

Competitor A: Large cloud provider managed endpoints
- Strengths: deep cloud integrations, global regions, brand trust.
- Redwood counter: lower unit cost for inference at scale via runtime batching + prefix/KV cache and transparent model-performance profiles; unified API across hosted/dedicated/private reduces migration friction.

Competitor B: LLM API pure-play (simple dev UX)
- Strengths: easy onboarding, strong docs, low initial friction.
- Redwood counter: comparable developer UX plus explicit production controls (SLOs, per-route cost tracking, rollout policies) and deployed options for regulated workloads.

Competitor C: Self-hosted inference frameworks
- Strengths: full control of stack and cost if large engineering org.
- Redwood counter: fewer ops overheads, predictable SLAs, Smart Routing to preserve uptime during capacity constraints, and cost-advantage analyses showing faster time-to-value.

Section 5 — Sales engineer conversation scripts and objection handling

Intro: below are short scripts to use live in a call. Keep them tight and metric-backed.

Script: latency concern
- Buyer: "We need <200ms p95 for chat."
- SE: "Understood. For comparable deployments we've delivered p95 <= 180ms using Dedicated pools with optimized kernels and continuous batching. On the pilot we instrument trace data and share a p95 baseline within 72 hours so you can validate. Would you prefer we size the Dedicated trial for peak concurrency or average load?"

Script: pricing pushback ("Your hosted price is higher than competitor")
- SE: "We often see higher apparent hosted cost if comparing raw per-token numbers. Two key differences: (1) our reported per-token cost accounts for throughput-optimizing features like KV cache and batch scheduling which reduce effective downstream cost; (2) we include guaranteed performance and rollback tooling that lower product risk. For fairness, let us run one of our sensitivity tests against your dataset and return a visible cost projection in <7 business days."

Section 6 — Security FAQ (concise answers for prospect diligence)

Q: Can customer keys be used for encryption at rest?
A: Yes. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) and HSM-backed key rotation. We provide a template integration runbook for Private deployments.

Q: How are audit logs provided?
A: Request-level audit logs with request IDs, model variant, and route metadata can be streamed to customer SIEM or stored in our encrypted audit store. Retention policies are configurable per customer.

Q: Is data used to train models?
A: No. For enterprise and Dedicated customers, data is not used to train public models. We maintain strict data-use contracts and provide an evidence package in the security bundle.

Q: What certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. Private/Enterprise customers can request our compliance package via the Contracting team.

Section 7 — Live-demo checklist and commands

Pre-call (15 minutes)
- Verify API key scoped to demo org and route-level rate limits
- Upload small sample dataset (<= 200 prompts) for on-the-fly tests
- Configure a canary route and rollback policy in Redwood Console

Minimal curl to run a sample chat (replace API_KEY and MODEL_VAR):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"MODEL_VAR","prompt":"Summarize recent user messages","max_tokens":128}'

Post-demo deliverables
- Baseline telemetry report (p50/p95 latency, token counts, cache hit rate)
- Cost projection workbook (three scenarios from Section 2)
- Security evidence package link and next-step recommended architecture

Appendix: conversion checklist for pilots to committed deals
1) Capture baseline telemetry for pilot across peak windows
2) Validate quality regressions with Redwood Optimize prompt set testing
3) Agree on a clear success metric (SLA or cost-savings target)
4) Propose a 12-month reserved capacity term with a 10% holdback for first-month refunds if SLO missed

If you have questions or need a bespoke slide pack for an executive briefing, contact: go-to-market@redwood.ai or add a request to the 'SE resources' channel in Slack.

This playbook is a practical, sales-enabled guide designed for data platform and analytics engineering teams evaluating Redwood Inference as the inference layer for data products and ML pipelines. It combines positioning and messaging, competitor differentiation, an actionable pilot runbook, pitch-deck slide outline, pricing guardrails, two short case vignettes, and a security FAQ tailored for technical procurement conversations.

Audience: platform engineers, data platform leads, ML infrastructure owners, and solution architects.

Intent: enable a fast, low-risk pilot that demonstrates cost, latency, and operational improvements and creates a clear path to Dedicated or Private deployment.

Owner: Go-to-market enablement; technical ownership and supporting collateral maintained by Eng: Serving Runtime and Eng: Platform teams.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Elevator (for engineers): "Redwood Inference lets your data platform serve production LLM features with predictable latency, clear unit economics, and controlled deployment options — from hosted API to private VPCs — without re-architecting pipelines."
- Value hooks for data platforms:
  - Predictable cost per inference through batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations.
  - Low-impact integration: standard REST/SDK endpoints and native connectors to existing feature stores and event streams.
  - Deployment flexibility: start hosted, move to Dedicated pools or Private VPC with identical APIs and metrics.
- Top technical proof points to emphasize in conversations:
  1. p95 latency guardrails and live sampling traces (Redwood Console per-route traces).
  2. Measured token-unit cost delta after applying batching + KV caching recommendations.
  3. Consistent model rollouts with canary and automatic fallback policies across environments.
sections.heading: Key positioning and messaging (elevator + technical hooks)

sections.body:

  - Unified serving API across hosted, dedicated, and private modes (same SDK + rollout semantics).

sections.body:

2. Week 1: Baseline capture — run 72-hour traffic replay, capture latency, token counts, sequence-length distribution, and cold-cache behavior.

4. Week 3: Integrate tracing + console dashboards; deploy canary route to 1% production traffic if safe.

sections.heading: Cost-safeguard checklist for pilots

sections.body:
1) Acero Health (synthetic vignette)

- Pilot outcome: 38% unit-cost reduction after enabling prefix caching and a conservative quantization profile; p95 latency reduced from 420ms to 160ms on user queries.

2) Nimbus Commerce (synthetic vignette)
- Context: Real-time product feed enrichment for mobile shopping experiences.
- Pilot outcome: Canary rollout across 5% traffic validated fallbacks and reduced cold-start errors; overall inference spend for pilot was $2.6k and projected 44% savings at steady state with Dedicated capacity.
- Business outcome: Enabled feature launch and cost guardrails for scale.
sections.heading: Short case vignettes (two concise examples)

sections.body:
Q: Can Redwood run inside our VPC / on-prem environment?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a customer-controlled control plane with optional on-prem packaging. Networking and peering templates are available in the deployment guide (see related pages).

Q: How does key management work?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers and supports HSM-backed keys for model encryption and auditable key access. Keys can be rotated on your schedule.

Q: What kind of audit logging and traceability do you provide?
A: Per-request audit logs, per-route traces in Redwood Console, and optional long-term log export to customer S3/GCS/secure SIEM. We capture token counts and route identifiers but do not store plaintext inputs for customers who enable strict retention; retention settings are configurable.

Q: Can we limit data residency and retention?
A: Yes. Private deployments and regional Dedicated pools can enforce residency controls. Retention windows for logs and prompts are configurable (default 30 days; can be reduced).

Q: What certifications / evidence can we provide?
A: We provide SOC2 and ISO sensitivity statements, penetration-test reports under NDA, and a compliance pack for procurement. For higher assurance needs we offer engagement with our security team to produce tailored evidence bundles.

Q: How do you prevent model drift from hurting product quality after rollouts?
A: Redwood supports model versioning, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automated quality regression alerts tied to stored prompt sets and evals. Canary traffic can be routed with automatic rollback on metric degradation.

sections.body:
Executive summary

This brief equips sales and solutions teams selling Redwood’s inference platform into Energy & Utilities (E&U) customers. It covers: elevator positioning, competitive differentiators, a short pitch-deck outline, a pragmatic pricing / TCO model for common E&U workloads, a compact customer case study narrative, and a security & compliance FAQ tailored to procurement and infosec reviewers. Use this as a single-page source to accelerate discovery calls and risk conversations; link into deeper collateral where noted.

1) Target problem statements (why E&U cares)
- Grid operators, trading desks, and field ops need real-time, reliable model inference for forecasting, anomaly detection, and assistant workflows.
- Constraints: strict availability windows, predictable latency for automation loops, sensitive operational data, and long-term cost pressure.
- Procurement focus: demonstrable SLA, auditability, and migration path from pilot to plant-wide deployments.

2) One-line positioning and three supporting points
Positioning (elevator): Redwood Inference delivers predictable, auditable, and cost-efficient LLM inference for mission-critical Energy & Utilities applications — from secure private deployments at the plant edge to elastic hosted capacity for short-lived analytics bursts.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Production-first reliability: SLA-backed latency SLOs, automatic fallback policies, and canary rollouts to reduce operational risk.
- Data boundary controls: VPC/private control plane options, KMS/HSM integrations, and detailed audit logging for regulated workflows.
- Cost-aware serving: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching and quantization profiles tuned to time-series and short-prompt patterns common in E&U.

3) Competitive brief (how to position vs competitors)
- Major cloud-managed endpoints (Cloud A/B): Strength is simplicity and scale; weakness is limited control over inference kernels, less predictable latency for small persistent workloads, and fewer private deployment controls for air-gapped sites.
  - Win theme: Redwood offers the same API ergonomics with explicit private deployment and deterministic performance at low per-token cost for production workloads.
- Inference runtimes / self-hosted vendors: Strength is low-level control; weakness is heavy operational burden and missing unified observability across hosted and private.
  - Win theme: Redwood removes operational lift with an opinionated runtime + orchestration layer and built-in analytics targeted at ML engineers and platform teams.
- Hosted LLM APIs (API-first vendors): Strength is model freshness and managed scaling; weakness is pricing unpredictability and limited SLO guarantees.
  - Win theme: Redwood’s Reserved/Dedicated options + cost controls (batching policies and quantization suggestions) produce predictable unit economics for long-running E&U workloads.

4) Recommended pitch deck outline (6 slides, 8–12 min)
- Slide 1: Title & hook — "Predictable LLM inference for mission-critical energy operations" (include logo, customer name if known).
- Slide 2: Customer pain — operational examples (SCADA alerts, forecast pipelines, field-assistants) and cost/latency constraints.
- Slide 3: Redwood value prop — unified runtime across Hosted / Dedicated / Private, key benefits mapped to E&U requirements.
- Slide 4: Architecture patterns — 2-column: Plant Edge (private deployment) vs Cloud Bursts (hosted); show data flows and controls.
- Slide 5: Economics snapshot — sample TCO for a realistic workload (see model below).
- Slide 6: Security/compliance callouts & pilot next steps (SLA, audit, rollout plan).

5) Pricing guidance & TCO model (example use case: distribution grid anomaly detection + triage assistant)
sections.heading: Supporting points

sections.body:
- 20k inference requests/day (mixed: 70% short prompts for triage, 30% 1–2k token forecasting batches)
- Reserved Dedicated pool for steady throughput covering 60% baseline; hosted bursts for spikes (40%).
- Target latency P95 < 300ms for triage prompts; batch windows tolerable for forecasts up to 2s.
sections.heading: Assumptions (monthly)

sections.body:
| Component | Units | Monthly cost estimate | Notes |
|-----------|-------:|---------------------:|-------|
| Reserved Dedicated GPU pool | 4 x A100-equivalent reserved | $18,000 | baseline steady-state throughput and low P95 latency |
| Hosted burst tokens | 600k tokens | $1,800 | per-token hosted pricing for burst capacity |
| Storage & networking | n/a | $800 | model artifacts, KV caches, egress (assumed limited) |

sections.body:
- Predictability: reserved capacity reduces per-request variance and caps monthly spend for baseline throughput.
- Unit economics: batching + caching can reduce effective tokens consumed by 25–40% for this workload class.
- Migration path: start with hosted pilot (4–6 weeks) then switch baseline steady traffic to Dedicated.

6) Quick customer case study narrative (1-paragraph)
Customer: NorthernGrid (regional distribution operator)
Problem: High false positive rates in SCADA anomaly alerts and long mean-time-to-resolution for field tickets.
Solution: NorthernGrid adopted Redwood’s hybrid inference model: private deployment at two control centers for low-latency triage, and hosted model bursts for cross-region forecast recomputations.
Outcome: 42% reduction in unnecessary field dispatches, P95 triage latency improved from 1.2s to 220ms, and operational inference costs were reduced by 31% vs their incumbent managed endpoint during steady-state.

7) Security & procurement FAQ (short answers sales can use in discovery)
Q: Can Redwood run on air-gapped networks?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments. We provide an installation bundle and an offline upgrade procedure; hardware compatibility and pre-install checklist are part of the deployment scoping.

Q: How do you handle model and data encryption?
A: Encryption at rest uses customer-managed KMS keys (optional) for model artifacts and KV caches. In transit TLS 1.2+ and optional mTLS for service-to-service. HSM integrations available for key storage where required.

Q: Is audit logging and tamper-proofing available for regulatory review?
A: Audit logs include request metadata, model version, and operator actions. For restricted deployments we can forward logs to customer Splunk/SIEM with immutable storage policies.

Q: What SLAs can Redwood commit to for production inference?
A: Redwood offers SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers (99.9% by contract) and latency SLO guidance (e.g., P95 < 300ms for triage-style requests on configured Dedicated pools). Specific SLOs are agreed during procurement and sizing.

Q: How are model updates handled and validated?
A: We support version pinning, staged rollouts (canary, A/B), and evaluation hooks that run predefined prompt sets against candidate versions. Regression alerts can be tied to those evals before traffic is shifted.

Q: Data residency and compliance — can you restrict where inference runs?
A: Yes. Private deployments and Dedicated capacity can be constrained to specific regions. We document region-by-region compliance postures and support SOC2-type evidence collection for enterprise buyers.

8) Demo & pilot blueprint (recommended 6-week pilot)
Week 0: Discovery & data access agreements (NDA + scope).
Week 1–2: Hosted proof-of-concept with sample prompts and an SLO matrix; initial metrics dashboard.
Week 3–4: Private staging deployment for 1 control center; integration with KMS and SIEM.
Week 5: Canary for a subset of production traffic; run evals and regression checks.
Week 6: Review + pricing proposal and recommended Dedicated sizing for steady-state.

9) Sales playbook snippets (talking points & objections)
- Objection: "We can just use cloud vendor endpoints."
  - Response: "Cloud endpoints are great for experiments. For predictable operational workloads you need reserved capacity, repeatable SLOs, and private deployment controls — that’s what Redwood standardizes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private."
- Objection: "We can self-host an open-source runtime."
  - Response: "Self-hosting gives control but often lacks the orchestration, batching optimizations, and lifecycle tools needed at scale. Redwood bundles the runtime with rollout policies, observability, and cost controls that reduce platform team effort."

payload.page_title: Consolidation and Split-Testing Playbook for LLM Deployment

sections.body:
Summary:
This playbook helps field teams and platform engineers run consolidation pilots (migrating multiple smaller LLM endpoints to a unified Redwood deployment) while simultaneously running split-tests to validate model quality, cost, and latency trade-offs. It combines positioning and messaging guidance, a competitive brief (how to counter common objections), an executable pitch deck outline, pricing scenarios and worksheets, a short case study template, and a targeted security FAQ for prospects evaluating consolidation or A/B split-testing strategies.

When to use this playbook:
- Prospect has multiple in-house or multi-vendor endpoints and is evaluating consolidation to reduce unit cost and operational overhead.
- Engineering teams want to validate a migration strategy with canary + split-testing across 1–3 user journeys.
- Platform/infra buyers need clear ROI scenarios tied to latency SLOs and failure-recovery behavior.

Primary objectives:
1. Demonstrate predictable unit economics (tokens/second and $/1M tokens) after consolidation.
2. Maintain or improve latency SLOs (p90 and p99) during rollout.
3. Preserve model quality via split-testing and automated eval gating.
4. Surpass competitor objections on security, vendor lock-in, and migration risk.

Owner and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Marcus Chen (Field Solutions)
- Technical escalation: Evelyn Harper (Solutions Engineering)
- Pricing and commercial: Diego Ramirez (Revenue Operations)
- Slack channels: #sales-field, #solutions-eng, #revops

Positioning & messaging (battle-tested lines)
- Core message: "Consolidate inference, control economics." Follow with three pillars: predictable performance, measurable unit costs, and flexible deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Quick opener for CTO/Platform: "We help you move from brittle, vendor-sprawled endpoints to a single inference plane that enforces latency SLOs and reduces per-token cost by ~30–60% depending on workload characteristics."
- Quick opener for Security/CISO: "We integrate with KMS/HSM, provide VPC/private deployments, and ship audit-ready logs for model access and data residency controls."

Competitive brief (objections + rebuttals)
- Objection: "We already have optimized on-prem endpoints; why migrate?"
  - Rebuttal: Highlight Redwood's continuous batching and KV caching that reduces cost per token for conversational workloads. Share a mini-benchmark: 40–55% lower token cost vs. single-shot on-prem endpoints for high re-use prefix distributions. Offer a pilot with replayed traffic to quantify.
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in concerns."
  - Rebuttal: Explain model-variant routing, open model catalog, and pin/version controls; show how tokens, prompts, and eval sets can be exported and migrated. Provide TOS excerpts on portability.
- Objection: "Security/compliance risk."
  - Rebuttal: Provide specific artifacts (SOC2 Type II in progress/completed, KMS integrations, VPC mode, on-prem packaging) and reference our security checklist in the demo.

Pitch deck guide (10-slide minimal flow)
1. Title & TL;DR — outcome-oriented one-liner: consolidation ROI and risk mitigation.
2. Customer pain & evidence — map their current endpoint estate and baseline cost/latency.
3. Redwood solution — architecture diagram (hosted + dedicated + private).
4. How consolidation works — traffic routing, canary policies, split-testing flow.
5. Performance evidence — p50/p90/p99 and token unit economics for representative workloads.
6. Security & compliance — KMS, VPC, audit logs, on-prem option.
7. Pilot plan & success criteria — metrics, duration, gating.
8. Pricing scenarios — pay-as-you-go vs. reserved capacity with break-even math.
9. Customer stories & expected outcomes — short case.
10. Next steps & asks — technical contacts, data access, pilot start date.

Pilot design: consolidation + split-testing (step-by-step)
1. Discovery (1 week)
   - Inventory endpoints, sample traffic, SLOs, model families in use.
   - Deliverable: baseline report (RPS, token distribution, p50/p90/p99 latencies, cost per 1M tokens).
2. Pilot config (1 week)
   - Provision Redwood sandbox with matching models.
   - Define split-test: 10% traffic to Redwood consolidated path, 90% to existing systems.
   - Define quality gates: automated eval on 5 key prompt sets and manual review on 50 random conversations.
3. Run & measure (2–4 weeks)
   - Monitor latency (p50/p90/p99), error rates, cost, and quality regressions.
   - Use canary rollback thresholds: if p99 increases >25% or quality degrades >5% on weighted eval, rollback.
4. Scale & optimize (2 weeks)
   - Apply batching and cache suggestions from Redwood Optimize; test quantized variants if cost-sensitive.
5. Finalize commercial ask
   - Present runbook, estimated savings, and recommended capacity commitment.

Success criteria (sample gating)
- Latency: p90 <= baseline p90 * 1.10 and p99 <= baseline p99 * 1.25 during steady-state (excluding cold-start periods).
- Cost: projected $/1M tokens <= baseline $/1M tokens * 0.75 (target 25% savings).
- Quality: automated eval delta <= 2% on primary prompts and manual review shows no critical defects.

Pricing guidance (scenarios & worksheet)
- Recommended approach for sellers: present three scenarios (pilot, scale, dedicated).
- Scenario A — Pilot (no commit): PAYG hosting, estimate usage with buffer. Example: 1M tokens/month = $X (show calculation) — use customer baseline tokens * 1.2 to cover spike risk.
- Scenario B — Scale (6–12 month): Reserved capacity with discount tiers. Example math: 20% discount at 3-month commit, 35% at annual. Show break-even compared to PAYG.
- Scenario C — Dedicated/Private (enterprise): Include platform fee + managed capacity + optional on-prem license. Show example TCO over 12 months including SRE effort saved.

Pricing worksheet (text table)
- Inputs: baseline tokens/month, average token length, request distribution (chat vs. completion), p90 latency requirement.
- Outputs: PAYG monthly cost estimate, reserved monthly cost estimate, projected savings, recommended commit.

Mini case study template (one page for slides)
- Customer: "Online Commerce Platform" (anon)
- Problem: 15 disparate endpoints, unpredictable latency spikes during peak, high token cost.
- Pilot: 30-day consolidation to Redwood hosted + 10% split-test for control.
- Results: 37% reduction in token cost, p90 improved from 420ms -> 260ms, zero customer-facing incidents during migration.
- Quote: "Redwood let us centralize inference without regressing latency — and the cost math was straightforward."

Security FAQ for consolidation & split-testing
Q: How is customer data protected in hosted pilots?
A: Hosted pilots support VPC peering and private endpoints; data in transit is TLS 1.3, data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS keys where required. Audit logs with request-level IDs are available for the pilot.

Q: Can we run split-tests without routing PII to Redwood?
A: Yes. Customers can redact or pseudonymize PII before routing, or run the pilot on a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to ensure no data leaves the customer boundary.

Q: What compliance evidence can we provide?
A: We can provide SOC2 Type II report summary, penetration test report excerpts, and a deployment checklist showing KMS integrations, VPC config artifacts, and operational runbooks used during the pilot.

Q: What are typical isolation and network options?
A: Hosted with private endpoints, Dedicated in a customer-segregated cluster, VPC peering, and on-prem appliance packaging for air-gapped environments. Each option includes logging/audit and key management controls.

Q: Failure and fallback behavior during split-tests?
A: Redwood supports transparent traffic mirroring, canary traffic with automatic percentage rollback, and automatic fallback to the origin endpoint on error or increased latency per the configured policy. We recommend a max 5xx rate threshold of 1% and p99 latency threshold defined per-customer during pilot config.

Demo artifacts and CLI examples
- Traffic replay (example):
  - rtx-replay --source logs.json --target https://<redwood-sandbox>/ingest --concurrency 20
- Simple curl to exercise a unified API endpoint (chat):
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize sales pipeline improvements"}]}'

Rollout playbook (checklist)
1. Preflight: obtain sample traffic, identify 3 critical flows, confirm SLOs.
2. Sandbox: run replay; produce baseline report.
3. Canary: route 5–10% traffic for 48–72 hours. Monitor metrics and quality gates.
4. Ramp: increment in 10–20% steps with 24–48 hour observation windows.
5. Full cutover: switch primary traffic path; retain origin for 14 days in passive mode for quick rollback.
6. Post-mortem: deliver lessons learned and optimize batching/quantization settings.

Sales collateral & assets to attach to a deal
- Pilot scope template (editable)
- Baseline report template (CSV)
- Short case-study slide (1 page)
- Security checklist and SOC2 summary
- Pricing worksheet (spreadsheet)

Appendix: recommended KPIs to track during pilot (minimum)
- Token consumption by route (tokens/request)
- p50/p90/p99 latency per route
- 5xx/error rate per route
- Cost per 1M tokens
- Eval pass rate on guardrail prompt sets

Notes & references:
- For technical play guidance see: sales-enablement/pilot-activation-playbook-and-technical-economics-2027
- For pricing mechanics see: sales-enablement/deal-engineering-cheatsheet-conversations-pricing-and-safeguards-2026

Contact and next steps:
- To run a quantified consolidation pilot, request a pilot scoping call with Marcus Chen and Evelyn Harper. Use the pilot scope template in the assets list to collect baseline data ahead of the call.

payload.page_title: Architect-to-Commit Playbook: Customer Technical Workshop

sections.body: This playbook is designed for solution architects, platform engineers, and CISOs running an "architect-to-commit" technical workshop with prospective enterprise customers. The goal is to accelerate commercial commitment by aligning architecture decisions, proving performance and security, and presenting a clear pricing/operational path from pilot to production.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Primary: Platform engineers, infrastructure architects, security leads (CISO/InfoSec), SREs
- Secondary: Product/ML engineers evaluating model behavior and cost tradeoffs

TL;DR Messaging (what to surface in the first 10 minutes):
- Redwood is a production-first inference platform: predictable latency SLOs, clear unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
- We prioritize deterministic serving: continuous batching, KV cache, and fallback routing minimize cost while protecting latency SLOs.
- We enable compliance through private control planes, KMS/HSM integrations, and auditable telemetry.
- Workshop outcomes: validated architecture diagram, 3 prioritized tests (latency, throughput, data residency), anchored pricing scenarios to match risk appetite.
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- Versus general cloud-managed endpoints: focus on inference economics (per-token costs + reserved capacity) and smart routing that reduces tail latency without manual sharding.
- Versus simple API-first LLM vendors: emphasize dedicated capacity and observability (token-level cost breakdowns, per-route tracing) as the difference for production SLAs.
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: show time-to-commit advantage (workshop -> pilot -> reserved commit) and removal of ops burden for kernel selection, autoscaling, and evictions.
sections.heading: Competitive Positioning Notes (talking points)

sections.body:
1) 0–10 min: Introductions + goals and success criteria (define commit signals)
2) 10–25 min: Target architecture walkthrough (customer presents current stack)
3) 25–45 min: Redwood reference architecture and deterministic performance story (include SLO examples)
4) 45–65 min: Hands-on validation plan and test vector design (latency/throughput/security tests)
5) 65–80 min: Pricing anchor and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
6) 80–90 min: Ownership, next steps, and acceptance criteria
sections.heading: Suggested Workshop Agenda (90 minutes)

sections.body:
- Latency: p95 < 150 ms for interactive prompts of 256 tokens on dedicated tier; p99 < 250 ms is acceptable for non-interactive batch jobs.
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/min per logical shard at 1k token avg with ≤ 10% CPU/GPU saturation headroom.
- Security: ability to provision a VPC private control plane and verify KMS integration in the pilot window.
- Economics: estimated per-1M-token cost within 10% of customer's target or clear roadmap to achieve it via caching/quantization.

Technical Validation Checklist (items for the workshop and follow-up pilot):
- Confirm tokenization and prompt-length distribution (provide example CSV of prompt lengths).
- Define dataset for quality regression (50–200 prompts + expected outputs).
- Agree test harness: client request patterns, synthetic replay, and load schedule.
- Verify model selection and quantization profile (e.g., FP16 vs 4-bit) with test quality baselines.
- Confirm KV cache hot-key behavior and prefix caching candidates.
- Capture network topology and egress constraints for Private deployment.

Practical Slide Deck Outline (5–10 slides):
- Slide 1: Workshop goals and commit signals
- Slide 2: Customer architecture snapshot (left) vs Redwood reference (right)
- Slide 3: Performance profile and SLO commitments (numbers + graphs)
- Slide 4: Deployment options and tradeoffs (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Slide 5: Pricing anchor: pilot, reserved, and enterprise commit tiers (simple table)
- Slide 6: Security and compliance summary (controls, audit artifacts, timelines)
- Slide 7: Pilot plan and acceptance criteria (tests, owners, timeline)
- Slide 8: Next steps and legal/commercial touchpoints
sections.heading: Sample Workshop Success Criteria (mutually agreed)

sections.body:
- Pilot offer (timeboxed, proof-of-value): 6–8 weeks, hosted or dedicated pilot with monitoring + 10k–100k tokens/day sample. Price: complimentary for small pilots; paid pilots for heavy throughput with discounted reserved rate.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) tier: commit monthly with baseline throughput. Anchor example: "Small Dedicated (8 GPUs): baseline throughput X, effective per-1M-token cost $Y after caching and batching optimizations."
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): platform fee (one-time) + per-instance license + optional managed-support retainer.
- Pricing negotiation levers to present: burst capacity buckets, model quantization credits, observability retention windows, and enterprise support SLAs.
sections.heading: Pricing Guidance (anchoring language and examples)

sections.body:
- Column headers: Tier | Commitment | Included GPU Hours | Typical p95 Latency | Anchor per-1M-token cost (est)
- Row 1: Pilot | 0–8 weeks | shared pool | 80–200 ms | $X
- Row 2: Dedicated - Small | 12 mo | 8 GPUs | 60–150 ms | $Y
- Row 3: Dedicated - Medium | 12 mo | 32 GPUs | 40–120 ms | $Z
- Row 4: Private (on-prem) | 36 mo | customer-managed | depends | custom

Case Vignettes (concise, proof points):
- FinServ analytics vendor: reduced inference spend 42% by enabling prefix caching and switching to a 4-bit quantized model for high-throughput reranking; pilot -> production in 10 weeks.
- Marketplace search product: lowered p99 latency from 420 ms to 160 ms after moving from single-hosted endpoints to Redwood dedicated with KV cache hot-paths.

Security FAQ (short, ready-to-read answers to surface in workshop):
Q: How do you integrate with customer KMS?
A: Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSMs via standard KMIP; keys can be customer-managed and rotated on schedule.

Q: Is data persisted on shared tenants in hosted mode?
A: No customer prompt/response data is persisted beyond retention windows by default; for hosted customers requiring strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

Q: Can we run a conformance test for data exfiltration?
A: Yes — we provide an agreed test harness within the pilot to validate telemetry, no-eval logs, and egress monitoring.

Q: What compliance certifications do you provide for private deployments?
A: We provide evidence packages for SOC2 Type II and can support customer attestation using Private deployment with locked-down control plane and audit logging.
sections.heading: Sample Pricing Table (copyable into slides)

sections.body:
1) Delivery owner (SE) to circulate the signed workshop notes and prioritized test matrix within 48 hours.
2) Schedule pilot kickoff within the next 7 business days with named owners for test execution.
3) Product/infra engineering sync to map identified configurables (batching window, cache TTLs, model variant pins).
4) Commercial: circulate draft pilot SOW and anchor pricing within 5 business days.
sections.heading: Operational Next Steps (post-workshop)

sections.body:

Appendix: Example CLI and JSON snippets to include in workshop materials:
- Example: request profiling command (pseudo):

- Example: minimal pilot model config (JSON snippet):
  {
    "deployment": "dedicated",

    "quantization": "4bit",
    "batching": {
      "max_tokens": 1024,

    }
  }

Notes on storytelling: always tie metrics to a business outcome (reduced latency -> lower abandonment; lower cost -> higher lifetime value per active user). Avoid deep benchmarking slides in the first 25 minutes; use them only to answer technical objections.

Document maintenance: this playbook should be reviewed quarterly and updated after three workshop cycles to capture new pricing levers, hardware options, and evidence from recent customer pilots.

sections.heading: Strategic Account Engagement Kit & Risk Fact Sheet

sections.body:
- Positioning: Redwood Inference provides production-grade LLM inference that makes latency, cost, and reliability predictable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

sections.heading: 1) One-line positioning and 30-second elevator

- Typical competitor objections and counters:
  1) "We can run models ourselves": counter — running is easy; operating a predictable, economical inference layer at scale with SLAs is not. Offer a pilot with hybrid (hosted + canary to private) to prove economics.
  2) "Cloud vendor has deeper discounts": counter — Redwood can optimize model/runtime to reduce unit costs and provides deployment flexibility that cloud-managed endpoints often lack.

Notes: These are starting-point estimates for qualification only. Provide a deeper TCO after an initial traffic trace and prompt-profile review. Emphasize that model selection/quantization can materially change costs.
sections.heading: 5) Pricing guidance (field cheat-sheet)

sections.body:
Customer: FinServe Inc. (anonymized)
Problem: Production chat agent faced 2–3s p95 latency spikes and unpredictable token spend during peak volume.
Solution: Redeployed inference through Greenwood's Redwood Dedicated pool with prefix caching, reduced batching latency with request priorities, and quantized model variant for non-sensitive traffic.
Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 2.8s -> 420ms, monthly inference spend down 36% with preserved answer quality per their evaluation set. Pilot -> production in 9 weeks.
(Use this excerpt to demonstrate economic impact and operational velocity.)
sections.heading: 6) Case study excerpt (1-paragraph, field-ready)

sections.body:
1) Q: Can Redwood run in our VPC/on-prem?
   A: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPCs and an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments. We provide deployment manifests and an installation runbook; professional services available for initial install.
2) Q: How do you manage keys and secrets?
   A: We integrate with customer KMS providers and support HSM-backed key stores. For Private deployments, keys remain in-customer control.
3) Q: Is there audit logging and evidence for compliance reviews?
   A: Yes. We provide structured audit logs for API calls, model versioning events, rollout actions, and admin changes. We maintain a compliance evidence bundle for SOC2/ISO requests.
4) Q: How do you guarantee data isolation with Dedicated?
   A: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated at the orchestration and network layer. We provide network-level controls and per-tenant storage isolation for persisted artifacts.
5) Q: What is your incident response process and SLAs?
   A: For Dedicated and Private customers we offer SLA-backed uptime guarantees, 24/7 support for P1 incidents, and runbooks for escalation. Refer to the contract SLA section and our incident-response runbook.
6) Q: Do you retain or use customer prompts/responses?

sections.body:
Overview:

This page is a concise, sales-facing playbook designed for conversations with CTOs, VP Engineering, and platform leads evaluating inference infrastructure. It combines high-level positioning, explicit differentiators compared to common alternatives, three pragmatic pricing scenarios with assumptions, brief objection responses, a short anonymized case study, and a compact security FAQ to use during technical calls. Use this as a single-sheet reference before and during technical discovery.

One-line positioning for CTOs:

Redwood Inference: predictable, high-throughput LLM serving that lets platform teams govern cost, latency, and deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private) without building an inference stack from scratch.

Audience and use-cases:
- CTOs evaluating inference for product features (search, summarization, copilots)
- Platform teams deciding between cloud-managed endpoints and self-hosted runtimes
- Procurement / security stakeholders needing an operational and compliance story

Key differentiators (talking points):
1) Deployment parity: single API + tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private VPC/on-prem installs — reduces integration complexity and supports multi-environment rollouts.
2) Production economics controls: explicit knobs for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles with measurable cost deltas.
3) Smart routing & graceful fallbacks: policy-driven routing by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to compatible model variants during capacity constraints.
4) Observability & attribution: per-token cost breakdowns, per-model latency histograms, and token-level tracing for debugging regressions.
5) Kernel & runtime optimizations: architecture-aware kernel selection and KV cache management tuned for sustained throughput.
6) Enterprise-grade operations: SLA-backed Dedicated, audit logs, KMS integrations for Private deployments, and formal runbooks for upgrades and rollbacks.

Competitive snapshot (concise grid for quick reference):
Note: competitors are anonymized categories to keep this doc evergreen.

| Dimension | Managed LLM Platforms (Large Cloud) | Open-source Self-host / Inference Stack | Redwood Inference (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Time-to-value | Fast (managed endpoints) | Slow (internal ops) | Fast (hosted) + predictable for Dedicated/Private |
| Cost transparency | Low (complex bills) | High variability | High (token/unit economics + tooling) |
| Deployment options | Limited (cloud only) | Flexible but high maintenance | Multi-mode: hosted, dedicated, private |
| Reliability & fallbacks | Region-dependent | Operator-managed | Built-in fallback policies, canary rollouts |
| Observability | Varies | Requires custom tooling | Native dashboards: per-route, per-token, eval regressions |
| Enterprise controls | Varies | Full control but heavy lift | Enterprise features + support for Private/KMS/auditing |

Pricing scenarios (examples to use in discovery; show order-of-magnitude economics). Assumptions: baseline LLM (2B–13B range), token pricing converted to monthly, includes compute + networking + platform fees for Hosted; Dedicated shown as committed monthly for equivalent throughput; Private shown as license + support amortized monthly. These are illustrative—use deal desk for final numbers.

Scenario A — Early product pilot (low usage)
- Monthly request volume: 25M tokens
- Model: moderate (7B) on Hosted API
- Typical latency target: 200–300ms
- Economics estimate: Hosted plan: $1,800–$2,800 / month
- Recommended approach: Hosted API with evaluation credits, SLO of 200–500ms, track cache hit rates

Scenario B — Growth / production feature (steady mid usage)
- Monthly request volume: 500M tokens
- Model: 13B (mixed accuracy/latency)
- Typical latency target: 100–200ms
- Economics estimate: Dedicated reserved capacity: $12k–$25k / month (depends on commit and burst policy)
- Recommended approach: Jump to Dedicated with autoscale policy and prefix-caching enabled; include cost profiling in Redwood Console

Scenario C — Regulated or data-sensitive (enterprise)
- Monthly request volume: 1B+ tokens
- Model: 13B–70B (quantized variants for cost)
- Typical latency target: 50–200ms (region-dependent)
- Economics estimate: Private deployment: license + infra (example amortized figure) $40k–$120k / month (depends on on-prem hardware)
- Recommended approach: Private deployment with KMS, audit logging, and SRE runbook; pilot with a Dedicated fall-through for burst capacity

How to present pricing in a discovery call (recommended script):
1) Confirm token volume ranges and peak concurrency.
2) Ask about latency SLOs and data residency needs.
3) Offer a straightforward Hosted projection for pilots, a Dedicated estimate with commit tiers for steady-state, and a Private architecture ballpark if compliance requires it.
4) Emphasize unit economics levers (batching, cache, quantization) that can reduce cost by 20–60% depending on workload.

Sample pitch deck outline (6–8 slides; use as starter):
1) Executive summary (one slide): problem, Redwood as the solution, primary ROI metric (cost per 1M tokens or latency improvement)
2) How teams break inference complexity: deployment parity + operational controls
3) Performance & reliability story (benchmarks + SLOs)
4) Economics: pricing scenarios and cost reduction levers
5) Security & compliance (audit logs, KMS, network isolation)
6) Migration path & timeline (pilot -> Dedicated -> Private)
7) An anonymized case study with measured outcomes
8) Next steps & ask (POC criteria, decision owners, procurement path)

Objection handling cheatsheet (short responses):
- "We can self-host and save money."
  Response: "You can, but the surface area includes kernel tuning, batching, KV cache management, upgrade rollback processes, and model-variant routing. Many teams end up spending 3–6x engineering time beyond initial expectations. Redwood purpose-built tooling buys that time back while preserving cost controls."
- "I need strict data residency and key control."
  Response: "We provide Private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations and an isolated control plane. We also support dedicated cloud tenancy for stricter network controls."
- "How do we avoid quality regressions after model changes?"
  Response: "We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and eval baselines, with regression alerts prior to rollout and canary A/B policies that automatically fallback."

Short anonymized customer case study (engineer-facing):
- Customer: Large B2B search product (GA 2025)
- Challenge: Unpredictable unit cost and frequent latency spikes during peak queries
- Solution: Pilot on Hosted API; migrated high-volume traffic to Dedicated with prefix caching and model quantization for bulk inference. Implemented per-route dashboards and automated fallback policies.
- Results (90 days): 45% reduction in average per-token cost, 60% reduction in 95th percentile latency, and zero production incidents related to inference during the migration window.

Security FAQ (short, shareable answers for prospects):
Q1: Where does data go when using Hosted API?
A1: For Hosted API, request payloads are processed in the region selected at configuration and retained per retention policy. We offer options to disable logging of raw inputs and token-level artifacts for sensitive workloads.

Q2: Can we manage encryption keys?
A2: Yes. Private deployments support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated customers, KMS integration is available for stored artifacts and audit logs.

Q3: What audit capabilities exist?
A3: Token-level audit trails, model version auditing, access logs, and admin activity logs are available and can be exported to SIEM solutions.

Q4: How are upgrades and CVEs handled in Private deployments?
A4: We publish upgrade schedules and security advisories. We ship hotfixes for critical CVEs and provide a documented upgrade and rollback runbook. For Private, we coordinate upgrade windows with the customer’s SRE.

Q5: Do you support network isolation / VPC peering?
A5: Yes. Private deployments support VPC-only access and optional on-prem installation; Dedicated supports private subnets and restricted egress configurations.

Q6: What compliance frameworks do you support?
A6: Redwood maintains documentation and processes to support SOC 2 readiness, and we assist enterprise customers with architecture patterns for ISO/GDPR compliance. Formal attestation depends on the deployment model.

Q7: How do you prevent model leakage or exfiltration?
A7: Controls include request/response masking, retention controls, KMS for stored artifacts, and network egress restrictions; we also recommend application-level filtering for sensitive prompts.

Q8: Can we run an air-gapped deployment?
A8: Yes—our on-prem Private packaging supports air-gapped installs with customer-managed model assets and telemetry collectors controlled locally.

Practical call checklist (what to capture during the technical discovery):
- Primary decision owners and procurement timelines
- Current monthly token volumes (p50, p90, p99) and concurrency peaks
- Latency SLOs and acceptable 95th percentile targets
- Data residency, key management, and compliance needs
- Existing inference architecture and pain points (ops time, incidents, costs)
- Willingness to pilot (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and target success metrics

Appendix: quick configuration table (example knobs and recommended defaults)

| Knob | Description | Starter default | Impact on cost/latency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Batch size | Number of requests batched for the same model | 4–16 requests | Increases throughput, may add tail latency |
| Prefix / KV cache | Cache warm KV for conversational workloads | Enabled for sessions > 3 turns | Reduces per-token compute by 10–40% |
| Quantization profile | Lower-precision model variant | 4-bit/8-bit where compatible | Lowers compute cost 20–60%, may affect accuracy |
| Autoscale policy | Burst capacity and commit thresholds | Steady baseline + 2x burst | Controls Dedicated cost and availability |

Owner & next steps:
- Owner: Asha Patel (Field Solutions, go-to-market) — asha.patel@redwood.example
- Recommended next action: Schedule a 45-minute technical discovery with infra sample metrics, bring an SRE and a security reviewer. Use this doc as the meeting pre-read and attach the sample demo template.

- 2027-01-05: Created initial draft for CTO conversations.
- 2027-03-10: Added updated pricing ranges and security FAQ suggestions based on recent customer pilots.
