sections.body:
Purpose
-----
This page provides a concise, reproducible sales artifact that combines solution architecture patterns with an explicit risk mosaic (security, compliance, economics). It is intended for AE/SEs preparing tailored narratives for mid-market and enterprise prospects where procurement, platform engineering, and InfoSec are decision participants. Use this as a modular deck script and an on-call Q&A reference during technical conversations.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Problem: Teams struggle to run LLMs at production scale while keeping latency predictable, costs bounded, and security/compliance auditable.
- Redwood positioning: A single inference runtime and orchestration layer that delivers predictable latency, cost controls, and private deployment options (VPC / on-prem) with observability and fallbacks.
- Outcome for buyer: Reduce per-token cost by 25–60% vs self-hosted naive deployments with SLA-backed latency controls and documented audit trails.

Audience & usage
----------------
- Primary users: AEs and Sales Engineers building technical pitch decks for platform/product teams, InfoSec reviewers, and procurement.
- When to use: High-touch pilots, formal security reviews, executive economics briefings, and procurement evaluation cycles.
- Recommended format: 12–16 slide deck for execs + 4–8 appendix slides for engineering/security + one-page pricing scenarios.

Core messaging pillars (talking points)
-------------------------------------
1) Production economics: predictable unit costs + levers to control spend
   - Emphasize batching, KV cache, quantization profiles, and model routing as demonstrated knobs.
   - Callout: Redwood Optimize recommendations typically yield 25–40% token cost reduction for conversational workloads.
2) Deterministic latency & reliability
   - SLA options for Dedicated capacity, region routing, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
   - Observable, token-level latency breakdown available in Redwood Console.
3) Deployment flexibility & security
   - Hosted API for rapid proofs-of-concept; Dedicated pools for predictable throughput; Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data.
   - Integrations: KMS/HSM support, SOC2-ready audit logging, and customizable retention policies.
4) Developer-first experience
   - SDKs, eval harness, and per-route analytics enable rapid iteration while preserving quality safeguards.

Competitive brief (summary of differentiation)
--------------------------------------------
- Large cloud provider endpoints: compete on scale and bundled infra; Redwood differentiates on inference-specific kernel optimizations, cost per token transparency, and unified rollouts across hosted/private modes.
- LLM API pure-plays: focus on simplicity; Redwood competes on production economics, predictable SLOs, and private deployments.
- Self-hosted stacks (open-source runtimes): lower sticker infra cost but high ops burden; Redwood removes operational lift with reserved capacity, autoscaling policies, and rollout tooling.

Buyer personas and tailored hooks
--------------------------------
- Platform Engineering (technical buyer)
  - Hook: predictable throughput, autoscaling policies, and programmable rollout controls; show runtime architecture and request routing.
  - Key questions: how KV cache is shared/isolated, cold-start characteristics, and rollback ability.

- InfoSec / Compliance (security buyer)
  - Hook: private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and data residency controls.
  - Key questions: network topology, credential lifecycle, and log retention / redaction capabilities.

- Procurement / Finance (economic buyer)
  - Hook: unit economics, committed discounted capacity, pilot-to-production cost predictability, and chargeback telemetry.
  - Key questions: overage policies, reserved capacity terms, and cost modeling templates.

Pricing scenarios (one-page guide)
---------------------------------
Use this table to orient prospects. Numbers below are illustrative; use official calculator for proposals.

| Scenario | Typical workload | Recommended plan | Pricing levers | Expected delta vs naive self-hosted |
|----------|------------------|------------------|----------------|------------------------------------|
| Pilot (small) | 200k tokens/day, low concurrency | Hosted API + caching | Prompt cache, small model | -10% unit cost |
| Growth | 1–3M tokens/day, bursty | Dedicated (shared) | Reserved capacity, batching | -25–40% unit cost |
| Regulated | 3–10M tokens/day, strict controls | Private (VPC) + Dedicated | Quantization + private runtime | -30–60% unit cost |
sections.heading: Quick summary (elevator)

sections.body:
- Offer a 60-day pilot with consumption cap and clear success metrics.
- For Dedicated: standard three-tier commit (monthly, quarterly, annual) with clear overage rules.
- For Private: platform fee + implementation support; provide a TCO bridge showing reduced Ops FTE burden.

Pilot success criteria (example measurable metrics)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Latency: p95 request latency <= 500ms for 2k token responses in the target region.
2) Cost: measured tokens/unit cost within 20% of proposal model after Optimize recommendations.
3) Reliability: 99.5% availability during pilot window for production route.
4) Security: passed initial architecture review and filled SOC2/ISO questionnaire items.

Technical appendix: common architecture patterns
-----------------------------------------------
Pattern A — Hosted-first rapid POC
- Components: Redwood Hosted API -> Customer App; optional private data connectors.
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra footprint.
- Cons: limited network isolation for regulated data.

Pattern B — Dedicated reserved capacity
- Components: Redwood Dedicated GPU pool (tenant-scoped) -> VPC peering for ingress -> Customer app.
- Pros: predictable throughput; soft isolation; SLA-backed latency.
- Cons: commit required for discounts.

Pattern C — Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Components: Customer VPC + Redwood Private control plane; optional on-prem inference nodes; KMS integration.
- Pros: full network isolation, auditability.
- Cons: implementation timeline 4–12 weeks depending on customer environment.

Security FAQ (concise answers to common prospect concerns)
---------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where do logs live and how long are they retained?
A: Audit logs are stored in the customer-dedicated log store for Private and Dedicated deployments by default; retention configurable per-account. Hosted API retains logs per policy and can be exported to customer SIEM via connector.

Q: Does Redwood support enterprise key management (bring-your-own-key)?
A: Yes. KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated deployments. Hosted API supports managed keys with optional customer-controlled rotations.

Q: How is PII handled during model evaluation and caching?
A: PII redaction and strict cache scoping are configurable. KV caches can be disabled or scoped per-customer; cached keys are encrypted at rest.

Q: What compliance evidence is available for procurement?
A: We provide SOC2 Type II report excerpts, penetration test summaries, and a compliance pack including data flow diagrams and retention matrices for Private deployments.

Q: What network controls support private deployments?
A: VPC peering, private endpoints, explicit IP allowlists, and optional on-prem air-gapped packaging.

Deal engineering cheat sheet (SE talking points)
------------------------------------------------
- If prospect cites a committed spend target, propose a staged reserved capacity agreement: pilot consumption cap -> 3-month ramp -> committed baseline.
- Use Optimize baseline to quantify expected savings and include token-level telemetry in the contract appendix.
- For security-conscious buyers, map each control to a deliverable artifact (e.g., KMS config, audit log export, architecture diagram).

Case study snapshot (short narrative to reuse in decks)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Customer: FintechPaymentsCo (mid-sized, regulated)
- Challenge: real-time fraud scoring with sub-second SLAs and zero-PHI leakage.
- Solution: Private deployment with reserved inference pools, strict KV cache scoping, and KMS integration for key lifecycle management.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in per-eval cost, 45% improvement in p95 latency compared to prior self-hosted stack, completed SOC2 questionnaire in 6 weeks.

Presentation playbook (how to run the deck live)
------------------------------------------------
1) Open with outcomes and economic framing (30–60 seconds).
2) Walk architecture patterns relevant to the prospect (2–4 mins).
3) Bring an engineering appendix for InfoSec questions and invite technical deep-dive only when asked.
4) Close with pilot proposal and suggested success metrics; leave time for procurement questions.

Owners and escalation
---------------------
- Primary owner: Maya López (go-to-market enablement).
- Technical SME: Daniel Park (solutions engineering).
- Security SME: Priya Menon (security & compliance).
- Escalation path: SE -> Solutions Engineering Manager -> Security Engineering -> Legal for contract items.

Appendix: reusable artifacts to attach
-------------------------------------
- One-page pricing scenarios (editable CSV).
- Architecture diagram templates (draw.io).
- Security checklist (PDF) and SOC2/pen test excerpts.

Editing notes
-------------
- Keep the executive deck concise; move deep technical content to the appendix.
- Update pricing deltas based on the latest Optimize benchmarks before submitting final proposal.

References and links
--------------------
- Redwood product pages: /product/overview, /product/dedicated, /product/private
- Internal: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture, /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence

payload.page_title: Risk-led adoption sprint kit for technical buyers

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This kit is a compact, field-ready bundle for technical buyers (platform engineers, ML engineers, infrastructure architects, and security leads) who need a short, prescriptive path from pilot to committed deployment. It combines positioning, a tight competitive brief, a slide outline for a 10-minute technical pitch, pricing negotiation anchors, three micro case studies, an operational rollout checklist, and a targeted security FAQ for prospect conversations.

When to use this document
------------------------
- Short pilot-to-POC cycles (2–6 weeks) where risk and control are the gating factors.
- Procurement conversations requiring both technical evidence and commercial anchors.
- Platform teams evaluating hybrid deployment (hosted + private) and looking to quantify runbook effort and cost.

TL;DR positioning for technical buyers
------------------------------------
- Redwood is a production-first inference platform: predictable latency, clear unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private/VPC-on-prem).
- Value anchors: consistent API surface for all deployment modes, automated batching and caching to reduce token spend, and transparent performance profiles for each model variant.
- Risk reduction: model fallbacks, canary rollouts, audit trails, and KMS integrations so security teams can map Redwood to existing controls quickly.

Buyer-focused messaging (by persona)
----------------------------------
1) Platform Engineers
   - Message: Replace brittle custom endpoints with a single runtime that respects latency SLOs and autoscaling policies.
   - Proof points: Dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling policies with burst capacity, p95 observed latency targets under load testing, and examples of Terraform snippets for infra provisioning.

2) ML Engineers
   - Message: Ship models faster and keep quality consistent using model versioning, selective quantization profiles, and Redwood’s eval hooks.
   - Proof points: Built-in evals for regression detection, KV cache control for long-context models, and recommended quantization profiles per architecture.

3) Security & Compliance Leads
   - Message: Control plane separation, VPC/private deployment options, KMS/HSM support, audit logging, and evidence for common certifications.
   - Proof points: On-prem packaging option, SOC2 readiness artifacts, and sample audit log schema.

Competitive brief (concise)
-------------------------
Below is an at-a-glance comparison you can use in workshops.

Tool | Deployment modes | Typical differentiation vs Redwood | When Redwood wins
----|------------------|------------------------------------|----------------
Redwood | Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem) | Unified runtime with production guardrails, built-in cost controls | Teams that need consistent behavior across hostings + strong observability
Cloud AI vendor X | Hosted managed endpoints | Integrated into cloud stack but varying latency/cost profiles | When customers fully accept cloud lock-in and want simplest path
Open-source stack + orchestration | Self-hosted only | Total control but high ops overhead and inconsistent perf | When customers must own every detail and have heavy SRE staff
Dedicated hosting vendor Y | Dedicated hardware leases | Good SLAs but limited model catalog and tooling | Customers focused only on throughput and contractual SLAs

Pitch deck outline — 10 minute technical brief (slide-by-slide)
-------------------------------------------------------------
1) Problem statement (30s): inconsistent inference economics and brittle rollouts
2) What Redwood is (60s): runtime + orchestration + tooling overview
3) Architecture sketch (90s): request routing, caching, fallback policies (diagram)
4) Performance proof (60s): benchmark snapshot p50/p95 and token cost delta vs baseline
5) Security & control (60s): VPC, KMS, audit logs, evidence checklist
6) Pricing & sample commitment (60s): three commitment tiers + negotiation levers
7) Pilot plan (60s): 4-week technical sprint with milestones and success criteria
8) Ask & next steps (30s): access, POC scope, procurement template

Pricing guidance and negotiation anchors
-------------------------------------
Use these as starting anchors for deal engineering. Be explicit on negotiation levers.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): list per-token and per-embedding unit rates. Anchor example: 0.6–1.4 cents per 1K tokens depending on model family and volume tier.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): monthly committed capacity buckets (e.g., 4, 16, 64 GPU equivalents) with step-down unit costs and guaranteed throughput. Typical anchor: committed discount of 40–65% vs hosted at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + deployment engineering SOW. Anchor example: platform licensing fee (annual) + deployment SOW (one-time), with an example total first-year cost for a mid-market customer: $450k–$1.2M depending on capacity and support tier.

Negotiation levers to propose
- Trial credit and metered pilot with success-based conversion.
- Phased ramp: start hosted trial, then Dedicated reserve on conversion for predictable throughput.
- Capacity commitment floors for price breaks (e.g., 12-month baseline).
- Observability add-ons (longer retention, custom dashboards) as revenue-friendly concessions.

Sample pricing template (compact)
- Pilot (4 weeks): $0–$25k (credit-based), includes performance profiling, basic SLO testing, and 1 integration workshop.
- Entry Dedicated (monthly): $25k/mo — 4 GPU-equivalent pool, 2-week on-call coverage, 99.9% infra uptime SLA.
- Enterprise Private (annual): platform license $300k/yr + deployment SOW $150k–$400k + support.

Operational rollout checklist (technical sprint)
---------------------------------------------
1) Pre-engagement (week -1): sign NDA, security questionnaire kickoff, list of contact points.
2) Provisioning & network (day 0–3): create service account, exchange IP allowlists, prepare VPC peering or VPN tunnel.
3) Baseline tests (day 3–7): run synthetic p50/p95 and cost-per-token profiling on expected traffic shapes.
4) Integration (day 7–14): API integration, credential rotation, and CI deploy tests.
5) Safeguards & SLOs (day 14–21): configure rate limits, fallback policies, and alerting thresholds.
6) Validation & handoff (day 21–28): run production-like load, finalize runbooks, enable stakeholder handover.
Owners: Solutions Engineer (SE) leads integration; Platform Eng (customer) owns VPC and ingress controls; Redwood SRE validates SLO tests.

Example runbook snippet (curl)
----------------------------
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-moderate-3.2b","input":"Summarize logs"}'

Security FAQ for prospect conversations (concise answers)
---------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Customers choose: (1) Hosted regionally with tenant isolation, (2) Dedicated pools with per-tenant isolation in our cloud, or (3) Private deployment inside customer VPC or on-prem. We map residency to the contract and label workload regions in Redwood Console.

Q: Do you support enterprise KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Redwood integrates with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and offers an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. Key management is configurable per-tenant.

Q: What audit evidence can you provide?
A: We provide structured audit logs (JSON schema) for API calls, model version usage, key rotations, and admin actions. For enterprise contracts we share SOC2 Type II summary reports and an evidence package for security review.

Q: How do you protect prompt/data privacy when using hosted inference?
A: Data-in-transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. We support network allowlisting and do not use customer input to retrain shared models. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated pools; we also support field-level redaction and request-level encryption on the client side.

Q: What compliance frameworks are supported or in progress?
A: SOC2 Type II (attestation available), ISO 27001 preparation underway, and European data residency controls for GDPR. We provide artifact templates to customers for their audits.

Q: How are model rollouts and regressions handled?
A: Redwood supports canary rollouts by traffic percentage, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant on quality regressions or SLA violations. We also integrate with our eval harness to trigger alerts on regression thresholds.

Q: What network/topology options exist for Private deployments?
A: VPC peering, customer-managed VPN, or air-gapped on-prem appliance. Typical design patterns and required ports/ACLs are provided in the deployment runbook.

Customer vignettes (micro case studies)
-------------------------------------
1) FinOps SaaS company (mid-market) — Outcome: reduced token spend by 38% using Redwood Optimize autosuggestions and prefix caching; moved from a pilot to a 12-month Dedicated commitment.
2) Healthcare analytics vendor — Outcome: migrated to Private deployment with HSM keying to satisfy regulatory review; went live with 99.95% infra uptime and private control plane.
3) Marketplace platform — Outcome: used canary routing and model fallbacks to avoid a production regression during a model update; avoided customer-facing incidents and extended contract.

Objection handling bullets (quick)
---------------------------------
- "We can self-host cheaper": Point to SRE cost, variance in performance, and time-to-market; show a conservative 6–9 month break-even model.
- "We need guaranteed latency": Offer Dedicated commitment + SLAs and run a targeted latency verification test.
- "Data leaves our network": Recommend Private deployment or a short bridge pilot with encrypted peering.

Appendix: Useful artifacts to attach to a prospect packet
--------------------------------------------------------
- 2-page technical brief for platform teams (PDF)
- 1-page risk mapping for security reviewers (PDF)
- Example SOW templates and procurement language (Word/PDF)
- Short benchmark report (CSV + graphs) used in the pilot
- Sample audit log schema (JSON)

Ownership & maintenance
----------------------
- Primary owner: GTM Solutions Engineering (Sofia Martinez)
- Secondary: Product Marketing (Liam Chen)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any pricing or feature change that impacts deployment or compliance.

Contact & next steps
--------------------
For packaged assets or an upcoming workshop, open a ticket with the Solutions Engineering intake (link: /confluence/sales-enablement/plug-and-play-inference-pilot-playbook-for-platform-engs-2028) and request the "risk-led sprint" pack.

Notes
-----
Preserve this kit as a living artifact: replace pricing anchors when we publish quarter pricing updates and refresh benchmark numbers after major runtime/kernel improvements.

1) Open with the one-page positioning brief (Section: "Key positioning lines").
2) If the prospect is cost-sensitive, lead with the Pricing Scenarios and the unit-economics calculator.
3) If the prospect is security-sensitive, surface the Security FAQ early and offer a data-room call with Security & Product.

Key positioning lines (one-liners to tailor to buyer persona)

- For Security/Compliance leads: "Run the same Redwood inference runtime in VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS and audit-forwarding to SIEM — we treat your tenancy and logs as first-class outputs."
- For Product/ML leads: "Ship model rollouts and rollback policies with per-route tracing and quality guards; iterate on prompts without risking production regressions."
- For Procurement/Finance: "Reserved Dedicated capacity gives you predictable unit costs — we provide the math and conservatively estimate a 30–45% TCO reduction vs unmanaged GPU fleet rebuilds on 6–12 month horizons."

Competitive snapshot (1-page matrix)
- Table: (columns: Capability / Redwood / Leading Managed API / Self‑Hosted Open Runtime)
  - Production SLOs: Redwood: SLA-backed latency targets + canary rollouts; Managed API: best-effort; Self-hosted: varies by team
  - Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): Redwood: Supported + integration playbook; Managed API: usually no; Self-hosted: yes (but heavy ops)

sections.heading: How to use this pack

sections.body:
- Against managed API incumbents: emphasize economics controls (batching + caching) and predictable reserved capacity options.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize time-to-production, operational hygiene, and integrated rollouts + fallback policies.

Pricing guidance and example scenarios
- Pricing constructs we use: per-token generation units, per-embedding unit, hourly reserved capacity (Dedicated), and professional services for Private deployments.
- Example scenario A — Customer-facing chat bot (moderate throughput):
  * 5M generation tokens / month, 2M embedding units / month.
  * Hosted with Redwood: blended unit price -> estimated monthly cost = $3,800 (illustrative).
  * Dedicated commitment (6 GPU equivalent) -> monthly commitment = $22,000, estimated unit cost reduction 40% at sustained load; break-even vs hosted at ~9 months depending on utilization.
- Example scenario B — Regulated financial institution (sensitive data, on-prem):
  * On-prem subscription: platform license + annual support. Typical first-year TCO includes packaging & professional services: license $120k, PS $75k, HW ops incremental cost $50k. Value: full control over data residency, audit log pipeline integration.

Security FAQ (prioritized, short answers to use in sales calls)
1) Q: Can Redwood run entirely inside our VPC or air-gapped environment?

4) Q: What KMS/HSM integrations do you support?

Summary:

This briefcase is a scenario-driven sales kit designed for pre-sales conversations with platform and infrastructure leaders (CTO/Head of Platform) evaluating inference architectures. It bundles: concise positioning, a competitive comparison matrix, three customer scenarios with suggested pricing anchors, an exemplar one‑slide pitch, an abbreviated security FAQ for technical reviewers, and a short results-focused case study. Use as a compact, reproducible artifact in demos, field calls, and technical deep dives.

Contents (quick navigation):
1) Leading positioning statements
2) Competitive snapshot (matrix)
3) Three realistic customer scenarios + pricing anchors
4) Single-slide pitch script and structure
5) Security & procurement FAQ (short answers)
6) Compact case study: Nimbus Retail
7) Action checklist and owner assignments

1) Leading positioning statements

- One-line elevator: "Deliver predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments so your product teams avoid costly rework and unpredictable unit economics."
- For CTOs: Emphasize measurable operational levers: latency SLOs, per‑token USD economics, and deterministic fallbacks (model variant routing).
- For Platform Leads: Emphasize a single API, observable model-level telemetry, and rollout controls that integrate with existing CI/CD.
- For Security/Compliance: Emphasize VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit-grade logs + exportable evidence.

Positioning bullets to use in calls:
- "Run the same inference contract in public, dedicated or fully private environments without code changes."
- "We trade upfront model-wrangling for runtime automation—intelligent batching, KV prefix cache and quantization profiles that reduce token costs by 30–60% on common workloads."
- "When capacity or region issues arise, automated policy routing downgrades gracefully to compatible variants to meet SLAs."

2) Competitive snapshot (matrix)

Explanation: Use this 3-way matrix to quickly position Redwood against common alternatives.

Competitor types: Cloud Managed Endpoints (big cloud providers), LLM API Providers (simplicity-first), Self-hosted Inference Runtimes (engineering-first).

Comparison table (short):

| Dimension                        | Redwood Inference                    | Cloud Managed Endpoints              | Self-hosted Runtimes                 |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Deployment Modes                | Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC)   | Hosted                               | Private only                         |
| Predictable Unit Economics     | Optimized with batching + caching    | Variable, often higher at scale      | Controlled but requires ops overhead  |
| Observability & Tooling        | Token-level, per-model dashboards    | Basic metrics                        | Varies (team builds instrumentation)  |
| Rollout & Fallbacks            | Canary/A-B + automatic fallbacks     | Limited                              | Custom solutions required             |
| Compliance & Private Deploy    | Private control plane + KMS/HSM      | Strong (but multi-tenant)            | Strong (but heavy integration)        |
| Time to Prod (typical)         | Days – weeks (self-serve -> dedicated)| Days – weeks                         | Weeks – months                        |

How to use:
- If prospect already on cloud managed endpoints: emphasize cost predictability and fallback routing to avoid throttling during peaks.
- If prospect leaning self-hosted: emphasize Redwood reduces engineering lift and accelerates guardrailed rollouts.

3) Three customer scenarios + pricing anchors

Scenario A — High-throughput conversational SaaS (PLG):
- Profile: Multi-tenant product with bursts, ~400 qps peak per region, median seq len 64 tokens, sensitive to 99th percentile latency.
- Suggested deployment: Dedicated capacity with autoscale and burst pool. Enable prefix caching and 8-bit quantization.
- Pricing anchor (example): Dedicated commit: $18,000/month for baseline pod group (supports ~120 sustained qps); incremental burst units billed at $0.22 per 1k tokens; projected unit cost reduction vs cloud-managed baseline: ~45% for typical prompt mixes.
- Sales hooks: emphasize predictable commit price, SLA for 99th p95 latency, and per-route cost dashboards.

Scenario B — Regulated enterprise (financial services):
- Profile: On‑prem or VPC-only, strict audit and key control, data residency in EU.
- Suggested deployment: Private (customer-managed VPC) with Redwood control plane in region, KMS/HSM integration, 12‑month enterprise licensing + support.
- Pricing anchor (example): Platform license $85k/year + per-GPU support/ops fee $2,400/month per GPU; professional services: 6 weeks integration at $40k.
- Sales hooks: compliance pack, SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SCIM and audit log exports.

Scenario C — R&D / Proof-of-Concept (low commitment):
- Profile: Team experimenting with embeddings and reranking for search, low qps but variable seq lengths.
- Suggested deployment: Hosted API, pay-as-you-go, pre-configured quantization suggestions for embeddings, and shared sandbox.
- Pricing anchor (example): Hosted rate: $0.006 per 1k embedding units, $0.035 per 1k generation tokens for opt-weighted models; free trial credits for 30 days.
- Sales hooks: quick onboarding, usage dashboards, and a clear migration path to Dedicated if needed.

4) One-slide pitch structure (30–90 seconds)

Title (5–10s): "Inference you can rely on in production"
Problem (10–15s): "Teams face unpredictable unit costs, flaky latency at scale, and brittle rollouts across environments."
Solution (20–30s): "Redwood provides a single inference contract across hosted, dedicated and private environments — with automatic batching, KV caching, and deterministic fallback policies that preserve SLA and reduce token costs."
Evidence (10–15s): "Customers see 30–60% unit cost reductions on typical generation workloads and deterministic failover across regions."
Call to action (5–10s): "Run a 4‑week bounded POC: we’ll set a dedicated pool, collect metrics, and produce a cost/latency delta report."

Speaker notes (short):
- Start with the customer scenario most similar to the prospect (pick A/B/C).
- Repeat the measurable outcomes (percent cost reduction, SLO numbers).
- Close by offering a concrete next step: "I’ll send a 4‑week POC plan and the measurement dashboard template."

5) Security & procurement FAQ (short answers for technical reviewers)

Q: How are customer inputs and outputs protected?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. For Private deployments, keys may be customer-managed via KMS or HSM. All request/response payloads can be redacted from logs on a per‑route basis.

Q: Do you provide SOC2 / ISO / penetration test evidence?
A: Yes — SOC2 Type II report available under NDA. Annual penetration testing reports and vulnerability scans are available for enterprise procurement packages.

Q: How do you support data residency and export controls?
A: Deployments can be scoped to region (hosted region selection) and Private deployments run fully inside customer VPC. We provide retention controls and automated exportable audit logs (JSON) for compliance.

Q: What access control integrations exist?
A: SAML/SCIM for SSO and provisioning, RBAC at token and route levels, IP allowlists, and optional short‑lived credentials for ephemeral workloads.

Q: How do you ensure model lineage and evidence for audits?
A: Every model version is tracked with immutable metadata: checksum, quantization profile used, kernel selection hints, and the rollout window. We can export model-versioned inference logs linked to request IDs for audit chains.

Q: What is the incident response SLA?
A: For Dedicated customers on enterprise SLAs: page within 15 minutes, 24/7 escalation, and a post‑incident report within 72 hours.

6) Compact case study: Nimbus Retail (abstracted)

Context:
- Customer: Omni-channel retail product team shipping smart search and summary features in their app.
- Challenge: Seasonality-driven traffic spikes overloaded existing endpoint-based model hosting; costs ballooned and 99th percentile latency spiked to 1.8s on peak.

Approach:
1) Deployed Redwood Dedicated pool in primary region with autoscale + burst pool.
2) Enabled KV prefix caching for 70% of queries; applied recommended quantization profile for the target model.
3) Rolled out conservative canary (5% traffic) with automatic fallback policy to a smaller variant when latency risk exceeded thresholds.

Results (30-day rolling window):
- 99th percentile latency reduced from 1.8s -> 0.45s.
- Average inference token cost reduced by 48%.
- User-perceived errors due to timeouts fell 86%.
- Migration time from POC to production: 3 weeks.

Testimonial (paraphrased): "Redwood gave us a reliable path to keep features live during holiday peaks without hiring more infra engineers." — Head of Platform, Nimbus Retail

7) Action checklist and owner assignments

- Pre-call prep (AE+SE): pick scenario A/B/C that matches prospect and prepare the corresponding pricing anchor (owner: AE).
- Technical review packet (SE): attach SOC2 NDA, region/tenant configuration doc, and model-versioning evidence template (owner: SE).
- POC plan template: 4-week measurable plan with success criteria: p50/p95 latency, per-token unit costs, and error rate (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Legal & procurement: attach Enterprise Licensing outline for Private (owner: legal).

Appendix: Suggested POC success criteria (short table)

| Metric                      | Baseline (example)            | Target (POC)                      | Owner |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------|
| p95 latency                | 1200 ms                       | <= 500 ms                          | SE    |
| Token cost per 1k tokens   | $0.60                         | <= $0.35                           | Finance/Sales |
| Error rate (timeouts)      | 1.6%                          | <= 0.3%                            | SE    |
| Model-variant fallback hit | 0%                            | <= 1% (expected)                   | Infra |

Contact & next step:
- For tailored pricing anchors and a POC pack, contact: jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com and cc: se-ops@redwoodinference.com.

Document history & ownership:
- Owner: Go-to-market (Solutions Engineering + Field Marketing)
- Maintenance cadence: Quarterly review or after major pricing/product changes.
- Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Ava Martinez and Ravi Patel.

End of briefcase.

sections.body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook is a compact, field-ready guide intended for platform engineering teams, security architects, and procurement partners who must evaluate LLM inference choices under three constraints: predictable economics, operational trust, and fast time-to-value. It combines concise positioning, a competitor-focused economics brief, a 10-slide pitch outline, concrete pricing scenarios, two succinct case studies, a prospect-friendly Security FAQ, and a recommended 6-week pilot template.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Platform teams choosing Redwood Inference get a single runtime abstraction across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that reduces integration surface area, exposes cost levers (batching, KV prefix caching, quantization), and provides enterprise-grade controls (KMS/HSM integration, request audit logs, RBAC). The outcome for customers is lower and more predictable unit cost, fewer operational incidents during rollouts, and a compliance posture suitable for regulated workloads.

Target audiences and decision makers:
- Platform engineering lead / head of platform
- Cloud architects and SRE leads
- CISO / security & tech risk
- Procurement and vendor selection committees

Core positioning statements (short bullets to use in briefing decks):
- For platform engineers: "One API to serve everywhere — identical operational model across hosted, reserved, and private deployments."
- For finance/procurement: "Transparent per-1k-token economics and reserve options that smooth monthly spend volatility."
- For security teams: "Private deployment options and customer-managed key integration for data and key sovereignty."

Competitive economics brief (practical takeaways):
- Competitor buckets: public cloud managed endpoints, API-first LLM providers, and self-hosted runtimes.
- Key differentiators vs each:
  * Public cloud endpoints: better ecosystem but limited token-level controls and generally higher egress/operational cost for sustained inference.
  * API-first vendors: usually fastest to integrate; fewer enterprise controls (on-prem, HSM) and limited SLAs.
  * Self-hosted/runtime builds: maximum control but highest ops burden and slower time-to-production.
- Compelling field claim: Redwood reduces operational integration time compared with self-hosting, and reduces sustained per-token cost vs cloud endpoints by making batching, caching, and quantization practical and observable.

10-slide pitch deck (fieldable, with slide guidance):
1) Cover: audience, use case, one-line outcome (tailor to platform/security/procurement)
2) Problem: fragmentation between model ownership and serving reliability/economics
3) Outcome snapshot: latency, cost, reliability improvements from customers
4) Product modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (one-liner each)
5) How it works (high level): routing, KV cache, batching, quantization, rollout policies
6) Economics worked example (summary table)
7) Security & controls: KMS, audit logs, RBAC, data residency options
8) Migration path: trial -> pilot -> reserved commit -> enterprise private
9) Case studies: two one-paragraph callouts (see case study section)
10) Ask & next steps: pilot scope, metrics, timeline, contact

Field presentation tips (two-liners):
- Start with slide 6 for procurement-heavy audiences; dive into slide 7 for CISOs; for platform teams expand slide 5 into a technical session.
- Always carry a priced pilot worksheet (see appendix link) with per-route assumptions.

Pricing guidance and worked scenarios (practical rules of thumb):
Principles to follow when proposing pricing:
- Anchor conversations on per-1k-token economics and total service cost (tokens + reserved pool amortized fees + egress + retention).
- Offer three entry motions: trial (metered hosted), reserved capacity (monthly commit + lower unit fee), private (license + support + optional capacity).
- Use commit discounts to lock predictable high-utilization flows; preserve higher short-term unit fees for bursty traffic.

Scenario 1: Customer support assistant (midmarket SaaS)
- Traffic: 80k monthly queries, avg 600 tokens/request
- Incumbent cloud endpoint (public): approx $0.07 per 1k tokens -> monthly cost ~ $3,360
- Redwood hosted (with batching & caching layer): estimate $0.028 per 1k tokens -> monthly cost ~ $1,344 (approx 60% reduction)
- Reserved capacity (12mo) example: pool cost $5,500/mo + $0.008 per 1k tokens -> net monthly ~ $2,224; breakeven vs incumbent at sustained growth above ~115k queries/month

Scenario 2: Regulated health product (private deployment)
- One-time deployment & services: $120,000 (installation, network integration, validation)
- Annual support & licensing: 15% of license in year 1.
- First-year fully-burdened cost depends on consolidation: multiple product lines > 2x consolidation typically yields ROI in year 1.

Discount and concession guidance (sales play):
- Typical reserved-commit discounts: 10-30% (scale with term and committed throughput).
- Professional services: price as T&M or fixed milestone, include a 10% contingency for network/security complexity.
- Preserve observability add-ons (longer retention, premium SLAs) as margin-preserving concessions.

Pilot template (recommended 6-week structure):
Week 0: Kickoff & metrics definition (traffic slice, latency targets, eval prompts)
Weeks 1-3: Integration, smoke tests, initial telemetry (route 5-10% of traffic)
Week 4: Capacity tuning (batching, cache policies, quantization profile) and cost run-rate update
Week 5: Security validation (audit log inspection, pen test scope)
Week 6: Decision review (go/no-go; convert to reserved or extend pilot)
Success metrics (suggested):
- Latency: 95th percentile below agreed SLO (e.g., 300ms for short-text generation)
- Cost: >= 40% reduction in per-token unit cost vs incumbent (pilot subset)
- Quality: no regression on agreed prompt evals (50-prompt set; mean preference score unchanged or improved)

Two condensed case studies (one-paragraph each):
- Case study A: FinOps analytics platform (midmarket). Problem: high recurring cost for embeddings and summarization across product modules. Action: Routed embeddings and short summarization requests to Redwood hosted, tuned batching and introduced KV prefix caching for repeated context. Outcome: 56% token-cost reduction and a 70% drop in inference-related operational incidents during model rollouts. Pilot moved to a 12-month reserved commit in 9 weeks.
- Case study B: Clinical workflow platform (regulated). Problem: required inference inside customer VPC with HSM-backed KMS and strict audit retention. Action: Deployed Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, performed SOC2 evidence exchange and audit log validation. Outcome: Private deployment completed in 14 weeks, met the provider's compliance gates and consolidated inference workloads across three product lines; net first-year ROI estimated at ~1.4x after consolidation.

Security & compliance FAQ (prospect-friendly):
Q: Where is data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Data for Hosted customers is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest; retention windows are configurable per-route. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to honor customer retention policies and store logs in customer-managed buckets when required.

Q: Can we use our KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed KMS; Private on-prem installs can integrate with customer HSM for key storage and signing operations.

Q: Do you provide request-level audit logs and request tracing?
A: Yes. Audit logs (request metadata, model version, route id) are supported for Dedicated and Private customers and retention is configurable to meet compliance needs.

Q: Which compliance artifacts do you provide?
A: We provide SOC 2 Type II reports and an enterprise security evidence binder. We can provide ISO guidance artifacts and a GDPR data residency playbook on request.

Q: How are model artifacts protected?
A: Model artifacts run in isolated runtime namespaces. For Private installs, artifacts and model weights can be stored on customer-managed storage. Access to artifacts is governed by RBAC and SSO integration.

Operational readiness checklist (for platform teams):
- Network: VPC planning (ingress/egress), private endpoints, routing policies
- IAM: RBAC mapping (admin/operator/viewer), SSO integration test
- Observability: enable token-level telemetry, per-route dashboards, alerts for latency & error rate
- Recovery: snapshot model configs and rollout policies prior to canary

Negotiation and conversion play tips for field teams (practical):
- Offer a scoped pilot with explicit conversion criteria tied to unit economics (e.g., X% cost reduction on pilot subset within 6 weeks).
- Trade longer-term commit for lower unit fees and staged reductions at 6/12/24 months rather than one-off deep discounts.
- Bundle observability retention and premium SLAs as add-ons to preserve margin while meeting procurement asks.

Appendix: quick CLI example for trial call (curl) and sample response (illustrative):
- Example request: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd/lite-7b","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'
- Example response (illustrative): {"request_id":"req_abc123","model":"rwd/lite-7b","latency_ms":95,"tokens_consumed":210,"output":"..."}

Contacts and next steps:
- Field contact: Maya Alvarez (GTM Solutions Engineer) — maya.alvarez@redwood.ai
- Recommended next step: send a one-paragraph use-case, traffic estimate, and preferred pilot timeline to the field contact; attach a list of five canonical prompts for quality gating.

Overview:

This kit is a compact, technical sales enablement artifact intended for platform engineers, CTOs, and sales engineering teams running a 2–6 week value sprint (pilot). It combines concise positioning and messaging, a competitive signal brief, a pitch outline for technical decision-makers, pricing scenarios for pilot-to-production conversion, a short case study template, and a focused security FAQ designed for initial prospect diligence.

Goals and audience:
- Primary audience: platform engineers, lead SREs, CTOs evaluating inference platforms.
- Secondary audience: sales engineers, solutions architects, procurement leads.
- Pilot goal: validate 3 production metrics (latency, token cost, and reliability) on representative workload within 2–6 weeks.

What success looks like (pilot acceptance criteria):
1) Latency: median 95th percentile request latency <= target (customer-provided baseline or 150ms for short-text generation).
2) Cost: measured per-token cost reduction or parity vs baseline within expected quantization/batching uplift (target: <=1.2x baseline for first-pass integration).
3) Reliability: >=99.5% successful calls over a 7-day window under the pilot traffic profile.
4) Quality: automated evals on a shortlist of 200 prompts must show no more than X% regression on defined metrics (to be agreed with customer; default 5%).

Positioning and core messaging (elevator + tech hooks):
- Elevator: "Redwood Inference delivers predictable inference economics and strong latency SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so engineering teams ship LLM features without re-architecting for each model or region."
- Tech hooks to use in conversations: unified runtime, automated batching and KV caching, per-route token and latency telemetry, model variant fallback policy, private deployment controls (VPC/KMS), deterministic autoscaling for reserved capacity.

Competitive brief (signals to surface during evaluation):
- Strengths to emphasize:
  - Production-first runtime (continuous batching + KV cache) that reduces per-token cost without heavy client engineering.
  - Straightforward private deployment path: VPC + on-prem bundle with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
  - Built-in rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic rollback when quality gates fail.
- Common competitor claims and rebuttals:
  - Competitor: "Lowest API latency" — Rebuttal: measure with our synthetic latency harness and look at 95p under customer traffic shape; Redwood provides transparent per-route breakdown and fallback strategies to preserve SLAs.
  - Competitor: "Cheaper at scale" — Rebuttal: Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization profiles) and telemetry-driven cost analysis close that gap while preserving quality guarantees.

Pitch deck / demo outline for a 20–30 minute technical session:
1) Slide 1: One-line value + customer logo examples
2) Slide 2: Short architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private lanes) with routing policies
3) Slide 3: Key metrics we will measure in the pilot (latency, cost per 1K tokens, error rate, eval quality)
4) Slide 4: Pilot plan and timeline (see next section)
5) Slide 5: Security & compliance summary (KMS, audit logs, network options)
6) Slide 6: Pricing scenarios and conversion path to Reserved Capacity or Private Deployment

Rapid pilot plan (2–6 week template):
Week 0 (pre-commit): scoping session, data/sample prompts, access and NDA.
Week 1: onboarding — API keys, baseline tests, instrument telemetry (SDK or curl), and a first synthetic throughput/latency run.
Week 2: integration — prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and autotuning recommended batching/quantization profile.
Week 3: production-style load run and quality evals; surface cost and latency dashboards.
Week 4: finalize go/no-go metrics and handoff plan; prepare proposal to convert to Dedicated or Private.
Optional extension (weeks 5–6): region failover and long-tail regression checks.

Pilot onboarding checklist (engineer-facing):

Sample API call (curl) to include in demo: 
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

- Conversion paths:
  - Reserved Capacity (Dedicated): monthly commitment with SLA and unit discount (typical discounts 30–50% vs hosted on-demand).
  - Private (VPC/On-prem): platform license + support and optional managed services fee; pricing varies by core footprint and retention requirements.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---|

Security FAQ (concise answers for early diligence):
Q: How is customer data protected in hosted deployments?
A: Data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest. We support per-customer keying via KMS (cloud or customer-managed HSM for Private). Audit logs capture model invocations and admin actions.

Q: Can we run inference on-prem or in our VPC?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-prem installer for air-gapped environments. We provide integration guidance for KMS and logging, and an optional managed service layer for installs.

Q: What logs and telemetry are available to customers?
A: Per-route token accounting, per-request latency and error traces, model versioning, and KV cache hit metrics. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs using secure streaming connectors (S3/CloudWatch/Events).

Q: How do you support compliance and audits?
A: We provide artifacts for SOC2 readiness, help integrate with customer audit processes, and can support contractual data residency and retention terms for Private deployments.

Q: What mitigations exist for model drift or quality regressions?
A: Redwood Optimize includes eval suites and regression alerts tethered to prompt sets. Rollouts support automatic rollback or fallback to a verified model variant when quality or latency thresholds are breached.

sections.body:
Overview
========

This dossier is a compact, cross-functional playbook for activating and scaling a Redwood inference pilot with enterprise prospects. It combines concise positioning for each stakeholder (CISO, CTO, Platform/Infra, Product, Finance), a competitive snapshot you can share during discovery, scripts for short elevator and objection handling, sample pricing scenarios with transparent math, and a targeted security FAQ for prospects evaluating embedded or private deployments. Use this as the single-page advocacy brief in workshops, executive previews, and technical pilots.

Executive summary
-----------------

- Goal: Convert a 6–12 week pilot into an enterprise deployment by aligning evidence across security, platform, product, and finance stakeholders.
- Outcome metrics to prove: end-to-end P99 latency under target, cost per 1,000 tokens vs. incumbent, error rate <0.1% for production routes, and successful audit of data residency/KMS controls.
- Suggested pilot scope: 2 production routes (low latency + high throughput), up to 500k tokens/day, SLA-backed dedicated capacity for peak test windows.

Who to engage and why
---------------------

1) CISO / Head of Security
- Primary concerns: data residency, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, key management, audit logs, and supply-chain risk.
- One-line pitch: "Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane with KMS/HSM integrations and full audit trails so security decisions remain in your hands."

2) CTO / VP Engineering
- Primary concerns: operational predictability, deployability, compatibility with infra, rollback safety.
- One-line pitch: "Same API and rollout primitives across hosted, dedicated, and private modes — minimize app changes while gaining predictable inference economics."

3) Platform / SRE
- Primary concerns: autoscaling behavior, observability, SLOs, tracing hooks, and cost controls.
- One-line pitch: "Per-route dashboards, token-level cost attribution, and configurable autoscale/burst policies so platform teams can enforce economics without developer changes."

4) Product / ML Engineers
- Primary concerns: quality regressions, model versioning, latency, and prompt experiments.
- One-line pitch: "Model pinning, canary rollouts, and integrated evaluation hooks guard quality while you iterate on prompts and model variants."

5) Finance / Procurement
- Primary concerns: TCO, commitment flexibility, pilot-to-production migration costs, and auditability of usage.
- One-line pitch: "Transparent per-token economics, optional reserved capacity for predictable unit costs, and migration credits for pilots that convert."

Tailored messaging snippets (short scripts)
------------------------------------------

- 30s CISO elevator: "For customers that cannot have vendor-managed keys or need region isolation, Redwood Private runs with a customer control plane and integrates with your KMS/HSM. We provide an audit log export and a prescriptive SOC2/ISO evidence package for pilots."

- 45s CTO elevator: "You can swap your model endpoint to Redwood with minimal SDK changes and benefit from deterministic batching and fallback policies. During pilot we'll instrument one critical route to measure production SLOs and cost delta."

Objection handling (concise scripts)
-----------------------------------

- Objection: "We can't trust vendor-managed data flows."
  - Script: "Understood — we recommend Redwood Private with VPC-only egress, customer-managed KMS, and an initial SOC2 evidence review. We can provide an engineering runbook and a 2-week on‑site/remote security validation window."

- Objection: "This will be too expensive compared to our internal GPUs."
  - Script: "We’ll run an apples-to-apples throughput and latency benchmark against your baseline (same prompts/seq lengths). Redwood Optimize then simulates batching and quantization profiles; typical pilots see 20–50% per-token cost improvement for production workloads."

Competitive snapshot (one-paragraph)
------------------------------------

Redwood positions between large managed API vendors and self-hosted inference runtimes: we provide the developer velocity and integrations of a hosted API, but with a deterministic, production-grade serving runtime and options for dedicated or private deployments. Notable differentiators for buyers: clear per-route cost attribution, automated fallback policies for reliability, and first-class model lifecycle controls (pinning, canary rollouts). For buyers leaning toward full self-hosting, highlight Redwood’s private deployment patterns and our migration credits for enterprise conversions.

Pilot configuration templates (recommended)
-----------------------------------------

Template A — Latency-focused pilot (recommended for consumer-facing UX)
1) Routes: 1 conversational route with streaming enabled; 1 reranking route for post-processing.
2) Traffic: mirror 5–10% of production traffic or simulate 100 concurrent sessions.
3) Targets: P50 < 150ms token, P95 < 350ms, model quality delta <2% from baseline.
4) Observability: tracing enabled, token-level cost export, and error-rate alert at 0.1%.

Template B — Throughput-focused pilot (recommended for batch/embedding workloads)
1) Routes: batch-embeddings, bulk-generation.
2) Traffic: 500k embeddings/day simulated with mixed vector sizes.
3) Targets: CPU/GPU utilization 60–85% during peak; throughput > target per commit.
4) Observability: queue latency histogram, batch sizing reports, and cache hit metrics.

Pricing guidance and worked examples
----------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Unit costs used in examples are illustrative — adapt to current rate card during quotes.
- Pilot discount: 25% off hosted list for pilot periods under an MSA that converts.

ASCII pricing table (example math)

| Scenario | Mode | Usage | Example unit price | Monthly cost estimate | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Small pilot | Hosted API | 10M tokens | $0.0008 / token | $8,000 | Basic integration, no reserved capacity |
| Dedicated pilot | Dedicated | 50M tokens | $0.00045 / token (committed) | $22,500 | Reserved pool, predictable throughput |
| Private PoC | Private | 50M tokens | $0.00035 / token (incl. infra credit) | $17,500 + infra | Includes on-prem packaging and limited support |

Worked example: If a platform route uses 5M tokens/month and you aim to scale to 50M:
- Hosted list: 5M * $0.0008 = $4,000/month
- Reserved (dedicated) forecast: 50M * $0.00045 = $22,500/month (but unit cost decreases with higher commitment)
- Recommendation: start with hosted for 4–8 weeks to validate SLOs, then move to a modest reserved pool sized for 2–4x peak if conversion probability >40%.

Success criteria and metrics
---------------------------

- Technical success: P95 latency below agreed threshold, error rate <0.1%, model parity within guardrails on evaluation prompt set.
- Financial success: measured per-token cost delta vs. incumbent <= target threshold (e.g., 20% improvement or breakeven after reserved capacity).
- Business success: conversion to a 6–12 month reserved commitment or signed Private license.

Security FAQ for prospect meetings (ready-to-read answers)
---------------------------------------------------------

Q: Where is customer data stored during the pilot?
A: For Redwood Private, all persistent data remains in customer-controlled storage in the selected region. For Dedicated/Hosted pilots we can configure VPC peering and enable strict retention policies; short-lived token caches are stored on encrypted local volumes and rotated per best practice.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Private deployments and Dedicated customers can use customer-managed KMS or HSM. Keys can be rotated under customer policy and access is limited to approved operator roles.

Q: Can we run a vendor security review / on-site audit?
A: Yes. We have a standardized audit package (SOC2 summary, threat model, patching cadence) and an accelerated review process for pilot conversions. For Private pilots we support scheduled remote validation and a 2‑week engineering validation window.

Q: How do you handle secrets, tokens, and telemetry?
A: Secrets are stored encrypted at rest with strict RBAC controls. Token-level telemetry is anonymized by default for hosted deployments; for Private deployments telemetry can be forwarded to customer observability endpoints without vendor retention.

Rollout & escalation playbook (brief)
------------------------------------

1) Week 0: kickoff — align SLOs, success metrics, and security checklist.
2) Week 1–2: integration — instrument one critical route, enable tracing, and run baseline load tests.
3) Week 3–5: validation — run 2 production-like windows, capture metrics, and run Redwood Optimize suggestions.
4) Week 6–8: decision — present success evidence to stakeholders, propose conversion options (reserved capacity or Private license).
5) Escalation path: bench-level SRE -> Platform eng lead -> CTO/CSO. Include on-call contact from Redwood engagement team.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------

- Deal owner (Redwood): [RM assigned at time of engagement — replace before sharing].
- Technical lead (Redwood): Solutions Engineer — Marcus Green (marcus.green@redwood.ai).
- Security liaison (Redwood): Priya Shah (priya.shah@redwood.ai).

Appendix: quick checklist to attach to customer workshops
-------------------------------------------------------

- Signed NDA and SRA (security review annex)
- Pilot MSA with pilot discount clause
- List of evaluation prompts and sample payloads
- Expected peak hours and representative traffic patterns
- Contact list for escalation and weekly sync cadence

Notes on sharing: This dossier is intended to be shared with prospect buying committees during pilot negotiation, and adapted per vertical (finance/healthcare/legal) by appending any vertical-specific evidence or compliance artifacts. For restricted or customer-sensitive pilots mark this file as restricted and attach compliance artifacts from the security vault.

Related resources
-----------------

- Platform adoption decision playbook (internal)
- Pilot activation playbook and technical economics (internal)
- Security evidence package: SOC2/ISO/PCI summaries (security vault)

This playbook (the Solution Advocacy Lab) is designed to equip partner account teams, systems integrators, and channel engineers with a single, evidence-driven kit for sell‑through of Redwood Inference to platform and ISV customers. It focuses on three objectives: (1) concise positioning for technical and economic decision makers, (2) compact competitive rebuttals and battlecards, and (3) templated collateral (pitch outline, ROI scenarios, security FAQ) that teams can reuse and localize.

TL;DR:
- Position Redwood as the production‑grade inference layer that reduces per‑token cost while preserving output quality and providing deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Use the "workload-first" economic story: show live throughput/lower latency and 20–60% token cost improvement via batching + KV caching + quantization recommendations.
- Lead with an ROI scenario (pilot → 6‑month run rate) and attach a short security evidence pack for CISO review.

1) Key positioning statements (single‑sentence hooks):
- For platform teams who need predictable inference economics and enterprise controls, Redwood delivers a unified runtime and toolset to run, monitor, and optimize LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Unlike single‑model APIs, Redwood optimizes at the serving layer—intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and model routing—so customers get consistent latency, lower unit cost, and safe fallbacks.

2) Audience-specific messages (3 lines each):
- CTO / Platform Engineering: "Run inference at scale with predictable latency and per‑token economics; pin model versions, use canary rollouts, and keep observability across routes and models."
- Head of ML / Lead ML Engineer: "Ship quality with model versioning, rollout control, and integrated evals to guard against degradations during quantization or model swaps."
- CISO / Security: "Deploy in VPC or air‑gapped on‑prem mode, integrate with KMS/HSM, and get audit logs for every request—no vendor data retention by default in Private mode."
- Product Manager / Growth PM: "Prototype on hosted API, then switch to Dedicated for predictable cost when the feature scales—no code changes required."

3) Competitive brief (summary + recommended rebuttals):
- Primary competitor themes we face: (A) simple model-access APIs (fast to adopt, weaker operational SLOs); (B) cloud-managed endpoints tied to a cloud vendor (harder multi‑cloud or private deployment); (C) self‑hosted inference stacks (control but high ops burden).
- Rebuttals and evidence points:
  - Against model-access APIs: emphasize SLA, routing/fallback, and cost controls (token-level dashboards, batching recommendations). Provide 95th/99th p50 latency comparisons for a 2048 token sequence.
  - Against cloud provider endpoints: emphasize deployment parity (same API across hosted/dedicated/private), lower middle-mile latency via regional routing, and enterprise-grade rollout mechanics.
  - Against self‑hosted vendors: cite time‑to‑value and maintenance burden; show migration path from PoC to Dedicated to Private with effort estimates (pilot: 2–4 weeks; Dedicated baseline: 6–10 weeks; Private: 8–16 weeks depending on networking).

4) Battlecard (one‑page script for SEs):
- Lead: "Are you optimizing inference costs or just buying model access?"
- Pain anchors: token overages, unpredictable tail latency, regressions after quantization, vendor lock‑in.
- Product levers to highlight: batching policies, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles (4‑bit/8‑bit guidance), canary rollouts, model routing policies, tracing hooks in Console.
- Quick win demo suggestions (5–10 minutes): low-latency text generation with streaming, embedding + reranking flow, live dashboard showing token cost drop after enabling caching.

5) Pricing guidance (scenarios and anchoring language):
- Guiding principle: price to reflect three levers—model class (decoder/encoder/decoder‑only), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and unit economics improvements (batching + cache).
- Example scenarios (for sales conversations):
  - PoC (Developer Pilot): hosted API, up to 100k tokens / month, free credits or deeply discounted rates to prove latency and functional fit.
  - Growth Pilot: Dedicated burst pool estimate: commit to $Xk/month (example anchor $15k) for predictable throughput and 20–30% discounted unit rate vs hosted list.
  - Enterprise Production: Private/VPC with platform fee + committed GPU hours—price as custom quote with typical contract size $250k–$2M ARR depending on scale and support.
- How to use the ROI artifact: plug in customer throughput, average tokens per request, desired latency SLO; we produce a 6‑month run‑rate delta vs third‑party API. (See ROI snippet below.)

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips platform advocates (platform engineers, infra leads, and SRE champions inside prospect orgs) with a compact evidence kit and a repeatable set of asks to accelerate pilot approvals and secure committed Dedicated/Private conversations. It bundles messaging, adversarial questions and counters, a short competitive snapshot, pilot pricing scenarios, and a lightweight security FAQ that maps to typical RFP checkpoints.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:

sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body: - "Ship LLM features with predictable latency, real unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls — from sandbox to private deployment without rebuilding your serving stack."
sections.heading: Topline positioning (one-liner for advocates)

sections.body:
- Predictability: SLA-backed Dedicated offering and deterministic latency for 95th/99th percentiles. Example: 95th-token-latency target = 150ms for 4k context models on p4-equivalent nodes.
- Portability: same API and rollout semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Cost controls: Token-level cost visibility, auto-batching knobs, and quantization advisory for 30–60% TCO reductions on typical chat workloads.
- Reliability & resilience: Cross-region fallbacks, model-variant routing, and transparent degradation paths.

Stakeholder-specific talking points (short bullets you can use verbatim)
- Platform Engineer: "Redwood gives you a single endpoint and a config surface for batching, caching and autoscaling — no model infra to maintain. You keep ownership of the network and KMS."
- SRE Lead: "We provide SLO dashboards, token-level latency histograms, and an error budget alerting pattern you can hook into PagerDuty. Rollouts support canary and A/B with instant rollback."
- Security Architect: "Private deployment options provide a customer-managed control plane with HSM/KMS integrations and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or S3."
- Product Manager: "We ship predictable request economics and offer prompt regressions detection tied to evaluators so feature regressions are caught before release."

Competitive snapshot (how to frame Redwood vs three archetypes)
- Cloud AI endpoints: "Easier to start, but limited routing and cost control. Redwood wins when predictable cost and cross-environment parity matter."
- LLM endpoint-only vendors: "Fast API but opaque performance profiles; Redwood provides verified performance profiles and deterministic latency tuning."
- Self-hosted runtimes + orchestration: "Max control but high ops burden. Redwood offers near-self-host control with much lower operational overhead and out-of-the-box fallbacks."

Quick win proof points (short evidence pieces to present in a pilot brief)
- Latency profile: 95th token latency = 150ms, 99th token latency = 260ms (internal benchmark on batch=8, 4k context, gpt-style model).
- Cost delta example: Chat application (1M tokens / month) — typical unit cost saving 38% using recommended batching + int8 quantization path vs baseline hosted single-request mode.
- Reliability story: Canary rollback demonstration completed for customer X (internal case id: CX-2025-114); rollback < 2 mins, no customer-facing errors.

Pilot structure & standard asks (recommended asks to include in pilot acceptance email)
1) Scope: 30-day pilot for a single service route (conversation API) limited to non-production traffic.
2) Success criteria (pick 3):
   - 95th token latency < 200ms under 90th percentile traffic pattern,
   - Observed per-token unit cost reduction >= 25% after applying batching/quantization,
   - No critical security gaps as defined by the security checklist below.
3) Data and access: Provide test dataset (anonymized) and one infra contact with VPN/VPC peering privileges for Private/Dedicated pilots.
4) Ramp plan: Week 1 — integration and baseline profiling. Week 2 — enable KV/prefix caching and initial batching. Week 3 — apply quantization recommendations and run synthetic load. Week 4 — evaluate metrics and handoff to customer SRE.

Sample pilot pricing scenarios (playbook numbers for discussion; customize per customer)
- Sandbox Hosted pilot: Free-tier credits + metered usage. Typical engagement cost = $0–$2k (covering metered usage).
- Dedicated trial (30 days): Minimum commit equivalent to 0.5 GPU pool. Suggested billable: $12k flat (covers reserved capacity + ops support + 2 weekly runbooks).
- Private on-prem trial (30–60 days): Professional services + packaging fee. Suggested starting ask: $25k (includes packaging, airgap validation, and 1 week on-site enablement).

Pitch deck outline (one-slide descriptions to put in a customer-facing deck)
- Slide 1 — Executive summary & ask (pilot duration, primary success metric, decision owner)
- Slide 2 — Customer problem statement (latency/cost/ops pain)
- Slide 3 — How Redwood solves it (runtime + routing + cost controls)
- Slide 4 — Proof points (latency, cost delta, case study snippet)
- Slide 5 — Pilot plan (timeline, roles, success criteria)
- Slide 6 — Security & compliance mapping (high level controls + required next steps)
- Slide 7 — Commercial ask & next steps (pricing scenario and decision timeline)

Concise case study vignette (one-paragraph you can read aloud)
- "A payments SaaS migrated customer-facing chat routing to Redwood Dedicated to reduce latency variance and control unit costs. After a 45-day pilot they achieved a 35% reduction in per-interaction cost and reduced 99th-percentile latency by 120ms. Deployment used Dedicated capacity with regional fallbacks and an automated rollback policy; the customer moved to a 12-month reserved capacity the following quarter."

Security FAQ (short, mapped to common prospect checkpoints)
- Q: What deployment models protect customer data?
  A: Hosted (data in tenant buckets, encrypted at rest), Dedicated (isolated GPU pool with customer network controls), Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem packaging). All models support KMS/HSM integrations for key control.
- Q: Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM?
  A: Yes — audit logging can be forwarded via syslog, S3 sinks, or API pull to your SIEM. Retention windows are configurable per contract.
- Q: How do you handle model provenance and model-change alerts?
  A: All model versions are cataloged with verifiable provenance. Platform supports automated quality checks on rollouts and can trigger regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Q: What certifications are available?
  A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the control plane. Private deployments inherit customer controls; we provide evidence packages for ISO/SOC/PCI conversations on request.
- Q: What is the incident response model for pilot customers?
  A: For pilots, we assign a named technical lead, provide a runbook for escalation and a 4-hour P1 response target during business hours. Dedicated/Enterprise SLAs are contractual.

Objection handling cheatsheet (two-line counters)
- "We built our own runtime": Counter — "We see 6–9 months of steady effort to reach parity on batching, KV cache correctness, and cost-aware routing. We provide the same controls with far lower operational risk and built-in rollbacks to protect users while you iterate."
- "Vendor lock-in concerns": Counter — "Redwood’s API and rollout artifacts are exportable; you can pin model versions and export cache keys and config to a shim layer if you decide to move."

Assets to attach to pilot proposal (checklist)

- Security checklist with evidence links (SOC2 report excerpt, audit logging config example)
- Quickstart repo for platform engineers with sample IaC snippets (VPC peering, KMS example)

Ownership & next steps
