Embedded inference positioning & CISO seller scripts

Overview
This document provides a concise, reproducible sales enablement package tailored for deals where customers evaluate embedded or private inference (VPC, on-prem, or dedicated capacity). It includes: positioning statements, competitive brief, pricing guidance examples, concise pitch scripts for technical and security stakeholders (CTO, Platform Eng, CISO), demo checklist, a short anonymized case study, objection handling, and a focused security FAQ for prospects.

Audience
- Account executives (AE) and sales engineers (SE) running discovery and technical validation calls
- Solutions architects preparing proposals for regulated or latency-sensitive customers
- Enterprise sellers negotiating reserved capacity and private deployment contracts

Key one-line messages (choose 1–2 per call)
- For Platform/Infra leads: "Deploy predictable, low-latency LLM inference in your VPC or on-prem with the same API and rollout controls you already use in hosted mode."
- For CTOs: "Reduce inference cost per meaningful token by combining quantization profiles, caching, and Redwood Optimize recommendations — without rebuilding your inference stack."
- For CISOs: "Keep data inside your network, retain full audit trails, and use your KMS while leveraging Redwood’s runtime optimizations and canary rollout controls."

Top value props (short bullets, use in sequence)*
- Predictable economics: reserved capacity + Optimize recommendations -> typical 30–60% unit cost reduction vs unmanaged self-hosted stacks for production workloads.
- Unified developer UX: same REST/SDK surface and rollout primitives across hosted, dedicated, and private.
- Production SLOs: configurable latency SLAs (p50/p95 targets) and automatic model-fallback policies.
- Security posture: customer-managed KMS/HSM, VPC peering/direct-connect support, detailed audit logs per token.

Competitive brief (high-level, for SE prep)
Use this at the start of technical calls to frame differentiation.
| Capability | Redwood Inference | Large Cloud ML Endpoints | OSS self-hosting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Developer API parity (hosted/private) | Yes — identical API / SDKs | Partial — different endpoints | Varies; often custom wrappers |
| Cost controls | Optimize toolkit + reserved pricing | Some discounts; limited optimizer | Full control but requires ops investment |
| Latency SLOs & fallbacks | SLA-backed for Dedicated; smart routing | SLA varies by offering | Depends on team ops maturity |
| Security & compliance | KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, VPC & on-prem | Strong cloud-native options, less turnkey on-prem | Needs heavy engineering, audit work |
| Model catalog & profiling | Curated models + quantization profiles | Model marketplace, fewer curated perf guarantees | Model ops entirely internal |

Pricing & packaging guidance (quick reference)
- Hosted (self-serve): per-token generation + embedding units. Best for trials and fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitment; tiered pricing by GPU class and guaranteed throughput. Ideal when predictable latency and cost are required.
- Private (VPC / on-prem license): platform fee + support; optional professional services for initial packaging and air-gapped installs.

Illustrative pricing scenarios (do not share externally; use in negotiation)
| Scenario | Baseline | Redwood outcome | Expected benefit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Customer X (SaaS search, 10M tokens/day) | Self-host (spot) 8x ops hours monthly | Dedicated g4dn-style reserved + caching | 35–50% lower TCO, 2x fewer incidents |
| Enterprise Y (PII-sensitive, 5k QPS) | In-house LLM infra + ops team | Private deployment + KMS + 24/7 SRE | Predictable latency, compliance evidence for audit |

Sample seller scripts (short, switchable snippets)
- Opening (platform engineer): "We help you keep inference in your environment while giving your engineers the same API and rollout controls they use for other services. This reduces integration time and lets you govern model change through canary and A/B rollouts."
- CTO (economics): "If your goal is predictable cost per request, Redwood’s Optimize recommendations — combined with dedicated pools and prefix caching — typically reduce per-token spend and smooth variance caused by dynamic batching at scale."
- CISO (security): "You can run Redwood Private with your KMS/HSM, enable full audit logging by tenant and token, and require mutual TLS plus VPC peering. We also provide evidence packages for SOC2 and controlled data residency configurations."

Objection handling cheat-sheet
- "We can just host it ourselves" → "Yes, but build vs buy tradeoff: Redwood removes repeated optimizations (KV caching, quantization profiles, kernel selection) and provides operational SLAs — all of which materially lower ongoing MTTI and ops cost. We’ll quantify the delta in the pricing appendix."
- "I’m worried about model drift and quality regressions" → "We surface per-prompt evals and regression alerts as part of Optimize; we can run initial guardrail evals on your production prompt set during a pilot."
- "Your hosted offering might see spikes" → "Use Dedicated + smart routing to ensure predictable throughput and configure fallbacks to lower-cost variants during regional outages."

Demo checklist (for SEs)
1. Confirm network path: VPN/VPC peering details and IP allowlist.
2. Validate auth flow: KMS key access patterns and service principal setup.
3. Show identical API call in hosted vs private (curl example).
4. Run a 1k-token workload to demonstrate p95 latency and KV caching impact.
5. Show audit log entry for the request and where it appears in the Console.

Quick curl example (for demo scripts)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-2b-quant","input":"Summarize user intent for this query"}'

Sample private config snippet (JSON, for solutions architects)
{
  "deploy_mode": "private",
  "network": {"vpc_id": "vpc-012345", "subnet_ids": ["subnet-1","subnet-2"]},
  "kms_key": "projects/myproj/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/key1",
  "audit": {"enabled": true, "retention_days": 365}
}

Short anonymized case study (e-commerce search, 3–4 bullets)
- Situation: Large online retailer needed sub-50ms p95 product search reranking and to maintain customer PII entirely on-prem.
- Solution: Redwood Private with quantized rwd-4b variant, prefix caching for top queries, and canary rollout for reranker updates.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 120ms to 42ms; per-request inference cost dropped ~40% after Optimize recommendations; audit package produced for PCI review.

Security FAQ (focused for CISOs, concise answers)
Q: Can we keep all inference data in our VPC?
A: Yes. Redwood Private and Dedicated options support VPC-only deployment and peering. No training data or logs are transmitted to Redwood’s hosted control plane unless you enable that integration.

Q: How does key management work?
A: You provide the KMS/HSM keys. Redwood integrates with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or brings-your-own-HSM for on-prem installs. Keys never leave customer control.

Q: What does auditing and logging look like?
A: Audit logs include request metadata, model version, and route. Logs are delivered to your logging endpoint (S3, GCS, or SIEM) and we support configurable retention and redaction policies.

Q: Can you support air-gapped installations?
A: Yes. We have a validated on-prem packaging process and an air-gapped deployment plan (see /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging). Professional services required for initial installation.

Q: How do you prove compliance for sales cycles?
A: We provide an evidence bundle: architecture diagrams, SOC2 summary, encryption and key management statements, network diagrams, and a deployment checklist used by our delivery team.

Next steps & playbook for conversion (AE + SE)
1. Discovery: confirm workloads (tokens/day, p95 requirement, data residency). Capture in the qualification checklist.
2. POA: schedule an architecture review with eng-private-deployments and request a delivery estimate.
3. Pilot: run a 2–4 week pilot using a dedicated pool with prefix caching enabled, collect latency and cost baselines.
4. Close: present pricing appendix with reserved capacity options and agreed SLAs; provide delivery and support SLAs in contract.

Owners and contacts
- Sales enablement (owner): Aisha Patel — aisha.patel@redwood.example
- Solution delivery: Daniel Wu — daniel.wu@redwood.example
- Security & compliance advisory: Sofia Alvarez — sofia.alvarez@redwood.example

Related resources
- Internal: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides, /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes
- External: Append detailed pricing spreadsheet and pilot acceptance criteria when engaging procurement.

Revision history
- 2026-02-14: Drafted by Aisha Patel
- 2026-03-01: Updated with demo checklist and pricing scenario inputs (reviewers: Marcus Chen, Sofia Alvarez)

*Use these scripts as starting points — adapt to customer language and discovery signals.

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook explains how to structure a Redwood Inference pilot (aka Value Lab) for technical buyers and platform teams. It combines positioning, a competitive brief, concrete pricing options, activation steps, success metrics, and a short security FAQ tailored for pilot-stage conversations. Use this page when a customer asks for a hands-on evaluation to validate latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

Audience
- Sales engineers and AE executing pilots with mid-market and enterprise product/platform teams.
- Solutions and customer engineers who will run the initial integration and success metrics.

One-line pilot positioning
- "Run a 4–6 week Value Lab that proves Redwood reduces per-token inference cost by ~25–45% while meeting target latency for your production workload."

Target buyer personas and objectives
- Platform/Infra Owner: Validate deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and observability hooks.
- ML/Model Owner: Compare model variants, quantization impact, and quality regressions.
- Product Manager: Demonstrate user-facing latency and conversion impact.
- Security/Compliance: Validate data residency, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration.

Core messages for pilots
1) Predictable economics: transparent per-token cost modeling, batching/caching levers you can change during the pilot.
2) Production-first: same API and rollout controls used in production — no prototype lock-in.
3) Measurable quality: integrated evals and sample-level regressions with guardrails.
4) Fast time-to-validate: sample app + SDKs + pre-built metrics dashboards to prove outcomes within 4–6 weeks.

Competitive brief (high-level)
- Competitors often trade coverage for observability or require significant ops work to reach production SLAs. Redwood’s differentiator for pilots is a pre-baked observability + cost model and optional dedicated pilot capacity so customers get production-like behavior without full procurement.

Competitive snapshot (talking points table)
| Dimension | Redwood Pilot (Value Lab) | Typical Managed API | Self-hosted/Open-source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time to first meaningful metric | 3–7 days (sample app + dashboards) | 1–2 days but limited observability | 3–8 weeks setup + infra |
| Visibility into unit economics | Per-route token breakdown, batching/caching models, projection tool | Basic per-token billing | Ad hoc cost models |
| Production fidelity | Dedicated pilot pools or private deployment option | Shared noisy neighbor effects | Can be high but needs ops investment |
| Security & compliance | KMS, audit logs, VPC, SOC-ready artifacts for pilot | Varies; sometimes limited evidence | Depends on customer's infra |
| Model switching & rollback | Canary/A-B + automatic fallbacks | Usually manual | Manual or custom tooling |

Pilot offers and pricing guidance
- Standard Value Lab (recommended for most pilots): 4-week engagement, hosted pilot pool, up to 10M tokens included, pre-built dashboard, 2 SEs (30 hours total) for integration and tuning. Price: credit-based promo or reduced pilot fee (examples below).
- Dedicated Proof-of-Value: 6-week engagement with reserved GPU capacity, model quantization testing, extended observability retention. Recommended for regulated workloads.
- Hybrid (Private test): Short on-prem or VPC deployment with limited data egress; pricing includes airgap packaging and 2-week on-site/remote operations support.

Sample pricing scenarios (guidance, subject to discounts)
| Offer | Duration | Included tokens | SE hours | Typical commercial anchor | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Standard Value Lab (pilot credit) | 4 weeks | 10M | 30 | $15k list pilot fee (often waived) | Good for fast proof |
| Dedicated PoV | 6 weeks | 50M | 80 | $45k | For enterprise/regulatory needs |
| Hybrid Private Test | 4–6 weeks | 20M | 60 | $60k + packaging | Includes on-prem package |

Pricing mechanics and economics to highlight
- Unit models: show per-1k-token run rate before/after batching and cache: e.g., baseline managed API: $0.60 / 1k tokens vs Redwood optimized pilot: $0.22–0.40 / 1k tokens depending on workload and cache hit-rate.
- Cost levers: batch size, KV/prefix caching, quantization profile. Provide customers with a short spreadsheet template to project 12-month run rate under multiple adoption scenarios.
- Upside protection: offer an "economic guardrail" clause in pilots that maps observed production token mix to committed pricing conversation.

Activation checklist (step-by-step)
1) Kickoff (day 0): introduce teams, confirm success metrics, share sample dataset, sign pilot MOU.
2) Architecture choose (day 1–3): hosted vs dedicated pilot pool vs VPC test. Confirm network routes, IP allowlists, and KMS plan.
3) Integration (day 3–10): SDK integration, sample app deployment, enable tracing tags and per-request metadata.
4) Baseline run (day 10–14): run representative traffic (10–20k requests) to capture p50/p95 latency, token distribution, and quality baselines.
5) Optimization & tuning (day 14–28): enable batching, try quantized model variants, enable prefix/KV caching. Track cost delta per experiment.
6) Validation (day 28–35): run A/B test or canary to validate user-facing metrics and guardrails.
7) Wrap-up & next steps (week 6): deliver final report, recommended production configuration, and commercial proposal.

Success metrics to include in pilot SOW
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-turn queries with seq_len <= 256 (or customer-defined).
- Cost target: demonstrable >= 20% reduction in per-unit inference cost vs customer's current baseline.
- Quality delta: automated evals show <= 1.5% regression on critical prompt set (or stakeholder-approved threshold).
- Reliability: availability >= 99.5% during pilot window for routed requests.

Observability & dashboard deliverables
- Per-route token & cost breakdown (CSV export).
- Latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99) by model variant.
- Request traces mapped to model variant and caching state.
- Quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

Customer case study (pilot example): NorthBridge Retail (fictional condensed summary)
- Objective: replace a rule-based search-reranker with semantic reranking for product discovery while keeping p95 < 300ms.
- Approach: 4-week Value Lab using hosted dedicated pool, evaluated two quantized Llama-family variants and prefix caching.
- Outcome: 38% reduction in per-interaction inference cost, p95 improved from 420ms to 280ms, A/B showed a 4.2% lift in conversion for product searches.
- Deliverables: final runbook, recommended production config (dedicated pool + 2-stage reranker), and a commercial term sheet for annual reserved capacity.

Security FAQ for prospects in pilot stage
Q: Will my customer data be stored or used to train models?
A: No. By default, Redwood’s hosted pilot mode does not use customer data to improve public models. For private deployments we provide an air-gapped option.

Q: How do you handle keys and secrets?
A: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM, temporary access tokens scoped per-pilot, and audit logs for all key operations.

Q: Can we run the pilot in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes — we offer hybrid private tests and on-prem packaging for pilots that require no egress. These require a short checklist for network and patch levels.

Q: What evidence do you provide for compliance reviews?
A: Pilot packages include SOC-style artifacts: architecture diagrams, data flow descriptions, sample audit logs, and an attestation checklist. For regulated customers we add a demo of KMS bindings.

Battlecard: common competitor objections + rebuttals
- Objection: "We already use a managed API, it's cheaper and faster to iterate."
  Rebuttal: "Managed APIs can be fast to start but often lack the unit economics visibility and production fidelity needed at scale. Our pilot model shows end-to-end cost and SLO tradeoffs and gives you knobs you can tune immediately (batching, cache, quantization)."

- Objection: "Self-hosting gives us the lowest cost."
  Rebuttal: "Self-hosting can offer low marginal compute cost, but total cost of ownership (ops, reliability, observability) and time-to-production are substantial. Redwood pilots provide production-like fidelity without long-term ops investment, and we can hand off an ops runbook for an eventual migration."

Slide deck outline (10 slides recommended)
1) Title & objectives for the Value Lab
2) Executive summary: expected outcomes and anchor metrics
3) Pilot scope & timeline (include success metrics)
4) Architecture options (hosted/dedicated/private) with recommended path
5) Economics: baseline vs projected post-optimization (sample spreadsheet excerpt)
6) Observability & quality monitoring demo screenshots
7) Security/compliance evidence checklist
8) Sample results (if available from baseline run)
9) Commercial options & next steps
10) Appendix: technical checklist & escalation contacts

Ownership and escalation
- Pilot owner (Commercial): AE assigned to the account (named in SOW).
- Technical owner: Solutions Engineer (SE) — typically SE + 1 customer engineer.
- Escalation: for infra/perf issues, engage Eng-Serving-Runtime on-call channel and Product-Infra lead (contact list included in appendix).

Templates and artifacts to attach to SOW
- Sample MOU (pilot statement of work).
- Sample cost projection spreadsheet (CSV).
- Integration checklist (network, KMS, logging).
- Sample prompt set and eval harness to run automated quality checks.

Next steps for AEs/SEs
1) Use this playbook to align internal stakeholders and draft the pilot MOU.
2) Book a 30-minute kickoff slot with customer and attach the integration checklist.
3) Deliver baseline report (week 2) and schedule optimization showback (week 3–4).

Appendix: useful commands and quick references
- SDK quickstart snippet (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-v1","input":"Example prompt"}'

- Internal contacts: SE rotation spreadsheet, eng-serving-runtime oncall link, pricing operations alias (use internal directory).

Document maintenance
- Owner: Elena Schwartz (go-to-market). Please update after each pilot cycle; reviewers should add lessons learned and representative cost deltas to the shared spreadsheet.

sections.body:
Overview:

This playbook is designed for Sales Engineers and Solutions teams running 30–90 day pilots with enterprise prospects where the primary buyer concern is risk reduction: latency predictability, data residency, and predictable unit economics. It bundles positioning, a concise competitive brief, three pricing scenarios for pilots, a one-page case study, pitch-deck talking points, and a targeted security FAQ to accelerate procurement and technical validation.

Goals and acceptance criteria (pilot):
1) Business success metrics (customer-defined):
   - P0: Integrated Redwood inference path in staging and processing representative workload.
   - P1: Measured 95th-percentile generation latency < 300ms for single-stream requests (model: rw-instruct-13b) under pilot traffic profile.
   - P2: Cost-per-1M-output-tokens estimate validated to +/- 15% after 2 weeks of representative traffic.
   - P3: Security checklist signed by customer security (encryption in transit/rest, KMS integration, logging).

2) Sales success metrics:
   - Pilot-to-paid conversion target: >= 60% within 90 days of pilot completion.
   - Decision maker consent: CTO, Head of Platform, and Security approver identified.

Value propositions / positioning (elevator and three-pronged brief):
- Elevator: "Redwood gives engineering teams production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency, clear unit economics, and enterprise-grade control. Run in our hosted cloud for fast time-to-value, or bring Redwood Dedicated/Private for regulated workloads."
- Three-pronged value for risk-focused buyers:
  1) Predictability: latency SLOs and deterministic autoscaling policies with canary fallback to smaller model variants.
  2) Cost transparency: token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console and pilot budgets that map to product metrics.
  3) Controls: VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM key management, and per-route RBAC for auditability.

Competitive brief (one page):
- Primary competitors to frame vs: general cloud-managed endpoints (CLOUD-A endpoints), small LLM API vendors, and self-hosted inference stacks (OSS runtimes).
- Strengths to call out: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, intelligent batching and KV caching that empirically reduce per-token cost for conversational workloads, and integrated rollouts + tracing to avoid blind production regressions.
- Weaknesses to pre-empt: customers often ask about model choice/accuracy vs vendor X; position Redwood's model catalog and evaluation harness as the mitigation (we run benchmark sets and show quality/cost tradeoffs).

Quick competitive matrix (talking bullets):
- CLOUD-A managed endpoints: simple but limited fallback and higher tail latency under burst; fewer private deployment options.
- Vendor-B APIs: low entry cost but weaker observability and no reserved capacity SLA.
- OSS self-host: lower software license cost but large ops burden and slower time-to-value; limited unit economics analytics.

Pilot economics: three standard scenarios (examples, adjust to deal):
- Baseline PoC ("Developer Proof"): 30-day hosted pilot, up to 2M tokens total, free account credits cover first 200k tokens, additional tokens billed at pilot discounted rate. Estimated bill: $150–$450 (depending on model). Goal: validate integration and latency.
- Risk-Reduced Pilot ("Prod-lite"): 60-day pilot with reserved Dedicated pool (small allocation), peak throughput guarantee 50 rps, 20% reserved-capacity discount for pilot. Typical commit: $15,000 for 60 days (covers compute + support), reverts to consumption billing after pilot unless converted. Goal: validate SLOs and throughput for production.
- Strategic Private Proof ("Compliance-first"): 90-day Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), includes KMS integration, 1-day on-site install support, SOC2 report exchange, and custom legal addendum. Typical T&M: estimate $40k–$80k depending on packaging. Goal: complete security & procurement gate.

Pricing guidance and negotiation levers (for SEs):
- Use credits to remove friction for Developer Proof pilots.
- Offer time-limited reserved capacity at 15–25% discount to lock in predictable throughput.
- Include an "economics sandbox" session with customer engineers: run Redwood Console cost reports on representative traces to produce an accurate 12-month TCO comparison.
- Offer optional "Quality Safety Band" (QA-run prompts + regressions) as a billable add-on: $5k for a 2-week tailored eval and alert setup.

Pilot runbook (30–90 day):
1) Pre-kickoff (Sales + SE): identify success metrics, target models, and sample traffic. Obtain security questionnaire.
2) Kickoff week (days 0–7): grant pilot access, deploy example client SDK snippet, configure Redwood Console dashboards (latency, tokens, cost), and set up SLO alerts.
3) Validation phase (days 7–21): run smoke tests, transfer 10% realistic traffic or replay workloads, collect baseline cost and latency reports.
4) Stress and edge case (days 21–45): increased concurrency tests, failure injection (timeout/fallback), and canary rollout validation.
5) Close and convert (last 7–14 days): present final report (latency, cost, security signoffs), propose conversion path (Dedicated/Private contract or hosted consumption).

Pitch deck talking points (1-slide snippets):
- Slide: "Why Redwood for Production?" bullets: unified runtime, predictable latency, caching & batching economics, rollout controls.
- Slide: "Pilot Plan" bullets: duration, acceptance criteria (latency+cost+security), owner list, conversion options.
- Slide: "Cost Transparency" bullets: per-route token breakdowns, unit economics sandbox, expected pilot cost ranges.
- Slide: "Security & Compliance" bullets: SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC & private control plane, audit logs export.

One-page case study (customer-friendly summary):
- Customer: FinLens (mid-market fintech) — use case: summarization and redaction for loan documents.
- Pilot scope: 60-day Risk-Reduced Pilot on Redwood Dedicated (rw-instruct-13b variant).
- Outcome: 95th PCT latency fell from 480ms (self-hosted baseline) to 220ms; estimated per-1M tokens cost reduced by 34% after enabling prefix caching and batching. Pilot converted to a paid Dedicated contract in 45 days.
- Testimonial quote (anonymized): "Redwood removed our ops uncertainty and delivered predictable latency under load — procurement cleared the private deployment in record time."

Security & compliance FAQ (targeted to pilots):
Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Redwood supports KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. For hosted pilots we provide envelope encryption and can enable KMIP/HSM on request.

Q: What evidence do you provide for security reviews?
A: We provide SOC2 Type II report excerpts, pen-test summaries, and a standard security questionnaire (SSQ) template. For Private deployments we produce architecture diagrams and runbook excerpts.

Q: How do you handle data residency and retention for pilot artifacts?
A: Pilot instances can be region-locked. Logs and telemetry retention can be limited to a pilot window (e.g., 30–90 days) and we provide exports for customer archival.

Q: How is PII handled in training/retention?
A: Redwood does not use customer data for model training unless explicitly contracted. For pilots, all inference request payloads are treated as transient and access-controlled.

Q: What controls exist for access and audit?
A: Per-route API keys, token-scoped roles, RBAC in Redwood Console, and audit logs with request/response metadata (excluding full raw content unless enabled). Logs can be streamed to customer SIEM via secure forwarding.

Q: What is the incident and escalation path during a pilot?
A: Assigned SE + customer success manager (CSM) are primary contacts. Critical incidents escalate to SRE oncall with a 1-hour response SLA for Dedicated pilots; hosted pilots use standard support channels with documented SLA tiers.

Operational checklist for security review (deliverable to customer security team):
- Architecture diagram (region, VPC peering, subnets)
- KMS integration plan and key rotation schedule
- Data flow and retention policy for pilot traces
- Logs export and SIEM integration plan
- Pen-test summary and SOC2 artifacts

Assets to attach to pilot packet (recommended):
- Short pitch deck (4 slides): Vision, Pilot Plan, Economics, Security & Next Steps
- One-page cost report template (CSV) and instructions
- Runbook snippet: how to reproduce latency benchmarks (curl examples and test harness instructions)
- Security questionnaire template and SOC2 excerpt
- Case study PDF of FinLens (anonymized)

Appendix: example commands and reporting snippets
- Example curl (hosted API):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-13b","input":"Summarize this loan document...","max_tokens":200}'

- Example Redwood Console report CSV columns:
  date,route,model,requests,total_input_tokens,total_output_tokens,cost_usd,median_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms

Contact and ownership
- Primary SE owner (pilot orchestration): Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- CSM handoff for conversions: Dinesh Kapoor (dinesh@redwood.ai)
- Legal & security escalation: Olivia Baker (olivia@redwood.ai)

Notes and recommended next steps for field teams:
- When security concerns appear early, prioritize the Strategic Private Proof path and engage legal/security immediately.
- Use the economics sandbox before pricing concessions — real data reduces discount creep.
- Collect testimonialable metrics (latency reductions, cost delta, MTTI improvement) during pilot to accelerate procurement approval.

Change log:
- 2025-03-21: Created initial draft.
- 2025-06-10: Added Competitive brief and updated pricing ranges.
- 2025-10-12: Finalized security FAQ and case study summary for FinLens.

sections.body:
Summary:

This document is a compact sell-through kit designed for field sellers and SEs engaging mid-market and enterprise buyers who are evaluating hybrid inference architectures (hosted API + private/Dedicated deployments). It bundles concise positioning, a competitive brief, two short case studies, recommended slide flow for a 20-minute technical pitch, sample pricing scenarios, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical one-pager to tailor follow-ups and create customer-facing slide decks.

Audience:
- Technical buyer (ML/Platform/Infra)
- Product/Feature owner evaluating cost, latency, and compliance tradeoffs
- Procurement/security reviewers who will sign off on deployment model

1) One-line value props (quick soundbites)
- For engineers: "Ship consistent, low-latency LLM inference across cloud and on-prem with the same API and rollout controls."
- For infra/platform: "Predictable throughput with reserved Dedicated pools and autoscaling policies reduces tail latency and operational toil."
- For security/compliance: "Private deployments with customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations meet common regulatory controls without re-architecting your stack."

2) Core differentiation pillars (3 bullets with backing statements)
- Unified runtime & API: Single SDK and model catalog across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reduces work required for multi-environment deployments and simplifies testing (same model versioning and rollout semantics).
- Cost-aware serving controls: Batching/caching suggestions, quantization profiles, and routing policies let customers reduce per-token cost by 20–60% in practice depending on workload shape. We ship telemetry that maps these levers to expected $/1M tokens.
- Reliability and automatic graceful degradation: Smart routing + model fallbacks keep customer apps online when capacity or regions are constrained. Built-in canaries and line-item observability reduce regression risk.

3) Competitive brief (executive table you can read out in 2 minutes)
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | Major cloud LLM APIs | Self-hosted OSS runtimes | Inference-specialized vendors |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Deployment models | Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC & on-prem) | Hosted ± partner integrations | On-prem only | Hosted or on-prem but limited ecosystem |
| Unified API across modes | Yes | No (hosted only) | Varies | Varies |
| Pricing control (batching/quantization) | Built-in recommendations + telemetry | Minimal | Manual | Partial |
| SLOs & enterprise SLAs | SLA for Dedicated + observability | SLA varies by provider | Customer-managed | Vendor-dependent |
| Security integrations | KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs | Cloud-native tooling only | Depends | Select integrations |
| Typical buyer wins | Platform teams, regulated enterprises | Rapid prototypes | RL/infra-first teams | Cost-conscious deployments |

Callout: When the conversation is purely cost-centric with engineering bandwidth to self-host, OSS is competitive. For regulated customers needing a low-ops private plane or predictable burst capacity for production, Redwood’s Dedicated + Private options accelerate time-to-production and reduce long-term total cost of ownership.

4) Two short customer vignettes (1–2 paragraphs each)
- FinOps SaaS (Mid-market) — "SmartInvoice": needed sub-300ms latency for the summarization microservice and data residency for EU customers. Implemented Redwood Dedicated pools (1x p4d-equivalent reserved + burst), configured prefix caching for standard invoice templates, and applied int8 quantization profile recommended by Redwood Optimize. Result: 45% reduction in per-request cost, median p50 latency 220ms, and compliance review completed in 6 weeks.

- Regulated Healthcare Enterprise — "Horizon Health": required on-prem inference for PHI plus centralized observability for product owners. Deployed Redwood Private (air-gapped bundle) with KMS integration and automated rollout policy that mirrors hosted behavior. Eng team reused the same API tests and eval prompts from hosted staging environment, reducing validation time by 60%.

5) Recommended 20-minute field pitch flow (slide-by-slide + talking points)
- Slide 1 (2 min): Problem & Impact — show customer-specific cost/latency regressions and compliance constraints.
- Slide 2 (3 min): Redwood value props — unified API, reserved capacity, private plane. Use the one-liners above.
- Slide 3 (4 min): Architecture options — quick diagrams for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with switching/fallback behavior.
- Slide 4 (3 min): Risk & mitigation — model quality regressions, capacity limits, data egress. Explain canaries and automatic fallbacks.
- Slide 5 (4 min): Pricing scenarios — show sample math for 3 workload archetypes (below).
- Slide 6 (2 min): Security & compliance summary — answer common checklist items.
- Slide 7 (2 min): Next steps & pilot proposal — propose scope, success metrics, timeline (pilot = 6 weeks).

6) Pricing guidance & sample scenarios (high-level; use for commercial discussions, not a binding quote)
Assumptions (example): p1) 5M tokens/day; 2) mix 70% generation, 30% embeddings; 3) commit to Dedicated baseline of 2 GPUs; 4) predicted batching and caching yield 30% token reduction.
- Quick-tier math (hosted): baseline hosted list-rate = $0.0008 per generation token (example). Estimated monthly spend: 5M tokens/day x 30 days x $0.0008 = $120,000/month. After batching/caching guidance (30% reduction): $84,000/month.
- Dedicated scenario: Reserved capacity (2 x rtx-a6000-equivalent) = $40k/month committed + usage overage at $0.00045 per token. With caching reductions, total estimated = $40k + (5M*30*0.00045*0.7) ≈ $43k/month.
- Private (on-prem): Platform license + deployment and ops retainer. Typical structure: one-time packaging + integration fee (~$120k) + annual platform license (~$200k) + optional support. TCO advantage appears for sustained > ~100M tokens/month and strict compliance needs.

Pricing callouts for negotiation:
- Emphasize predictability of Dedicated commitments vs variable hosted spend.
- Offer a measured pilot: 6-week committed Dedicated at ~50% of expected steady-state to validate latency and unit economics.
- For strategic accounts, we can layer a 3–6 month ramp with graduated commit discounts.

7) Objections & short rebuttals
- "We can just self-host and save money." — If your team has >1 FTE dedicated to infra and SRE, OSS can work. For product teams needing fast iteration, Redwood removes operational burden and provides observability and SLAs that accelerate product launches.
- "We can’t send data to hosted services." — Private deployments with VPC and on-prem packaging address most regulated needs; discuss the specific control (KMS/HSM, audit logs, network isolation) the customer requires.
- "We need peak throughput that varies monthly." — Recommend Dedicated + burst policies and smart routing; autoscaling policies and regional fallbacks mitigate spikes without overcommitting.

8) Prospect-facing Security FAQ (copyable into an RFP response)
Q: What deployment options support PHI and regulated data?
A: Redwood supports Private (on-prem and VPC) and Dedicated with customer-controlled networking. Private deployments can be delivered as an air-gapped package; Dedicated can be configured with private peering and strict egress controls.

Q: How is encryption handled at rest and in transit?
A: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit. At-rest encryption via customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM-backed keys on request). Audit logs include key rotation events and access records.

Q: Do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)?
A: Yes — BYOK via standard KMS integrations is supported for both Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q: How do you provide auditability for model inference?
A: Request-level logging with metadata (model version, route, request id, latency, token counts) stored in customer-controlled retention buckets. Full audit trails are available in Private deployments; Hosted retains logs per tenant with configurable retention windows.

Q: What certifications / compliance evidence do you provide?
A: We publish SOC 2 Type II reports for the hosted control plane and provide architecture diagrams, data flow docs, and assessor-friendly evidence packages to support customer audits for Dedicated and Private engagements.

Q: How are vulnerabilities in models handled?
A: We provide model vetting guidance and can operate a controlled model onboarding workflow: static checks, test prompt-sets, and staged rollout with canaries. For Private, we include a triage runbook for urgent patches.

9) Sales assets & templates included (links to shared drive)
- 20-minute field deck (template) — use slide flow in section 5.
- 6-week pilot SOW (scoped template).
- Security FAQ one-pager (RFP-ready).
- Cost model spreadsheet (editable) — includes inputs: tokens/day, generation vs embeddings, average token length, expected caching delta.

10) Success metrics for pilot (proposed)
- Latency: p50 < 300ms for generation endpoints in the chosen region.
- Cost: measured $/1M tokens within ±15% of predicted model after caching recommendations.
- Reliability: <1% error rate during pilot and successful rollout of canary policy.
- Validation: product team-completed 10 production-like prompts with pass/fail quality metrics.

11) Ownership & next steps
- Field readiness: SE leader (Marcus Li) owns customizing the deck; commercial lead (Priya Nair) owns pilot SOW and pricing exceptions.
- Playbook actions: schedule technical deep-dive, propose 6-week pilot, assemble security package (KMS config, architecture diagram, evidence).

Appendix: Sample architecture diagrams (text descriptions)
- Hosted-first (fast test): App -> Redwood Hosted API (multi-region) -> model catalog. Suitable for prototypes and first 90-day user tests.
- Dedicated baseline: App -> VPC peering -> Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) -> autoscale worker groups -> metrics -> Redwood Console. Use when predictable throughput is needed.
- Private plane: App (on-prem) -> Private control plane -> on-prem GPU cluster (air-gapped) -> local KMS/HSM integration. Use when data residency and strict network controls are required.

End of document.

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook helps platform engineers and solution teams run a short, high-impact pilot with Redwood Inference focused on developer ergonomics, predictable latency, and unit-cost validation. The document bundles positioning language, a competitive brief, a 6-week pilot plan, pricing guidance, a compact pitch outline for SEs, success metrics, a short customer case study vignette, and a security FAQ tailored to technical buyers.

Who this is for
- Platform engineers evaluating an LLM inference provider for productization.
- Solution engineers running pilot proofs-of-value for developer adoption.
- Procurement/security teams validating risk controls for production rollout.

Executive positioning (one-paragraph)
Redwood Inference offers a developer-first inference platform that abstracts away underlying GPU and network complexity while giving platform teams explicit controls to trade latency for unit cost. For teams that care about predictable production economics, compliance options, and fast developer onboarding, Redwood provides a consistent API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment models plus tooling to measure and control token-level cost. Use this playbook to demonstrate how Redwood reduces iteration time for developer teams while bounding inference spend.

Competitive brief (concise)
- Primary competitor profiles and how to position:
  - Cloud-managed endpoints (e.g., large cloud provider managed model endpoints): emphasize Redwood's unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and transparent per-token economics vs opaque cloud egress/instance cost.
  - LLM API vendors (single-model, closed): emphasize Redwood's model catalog and model-variant fallbacks to preserve availability and quality.
  - Self-hosted runtimes (open-source + infra ops): emphasize Redwood's compile-time kernel selection, auto-batching heuristics, and production observability that reduce devops overhead and time-to-scale.

Key differentiators to call out in conversations
- Predictable unit economics: token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost allocation.
- Unified API: Same interface and rollout controls across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Reliability fallbacks: automatic model-variant routing, region fallback and canary rollouts integrated into the control plane.
- Developer ergonomics: quickstart SDKs, structured output and streaming for interactive integrations.

6-week pilot plan (recommended timeline and milestones)
1) Week 0: Kickoff & Success Criteria (1 day)
   - Participants: platform eng, SE, product lead, security reviewer.
   - Output: signed pilot charter with KPIs (latency p50/p95 target, per-1000-token cost, dev onboarding time).
2) Week 1: Environment & Ingestion (3 days)
   - Provision Redwood test tenant (hosted) or private eval (VPC) depending on security needs.
   - Wire a representative sample API route and dataset (5–10 prompts or flows).
3) Week 2: Baseline Metrics & Profiling (5 days)
   - Run baseline traffic at representative concurrency; collect p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-cost breakdown.
   - Run profiling: sequence length distribution, tail-latency triggers, KV cache hit-rate.
4) Week 3: Optimization & Controls (5 days)
   - Enable prefix/KV caching, test batching policies, try quantized model variant.
   - Document latency vs cost trade-offs and recommended config for production.
5) Week 4: Reliability & Rollout Testing (4 days)
   - Configure canary rollout with fallback policy. Simulate capacity event and validate graceful degradation.
6) Week 5: Security Review & Compliance Checks (3 days)
   - Obtain evidence bundles: audit logs, KMS integration guide, network topology diagram.
7) Week 6: Wrap-up & Next Steps (3 days)
   - Present results: KPI dashboard, cost delta vs baseline, recommended deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and proposal for 90-day production ramp.

Pilot success criteria (example KPIs)
- Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 450ms at target concurrency.
- Cost: incremental inference cost < $0.25 per 1K tokens after optimization (example target; adjust by workload).
- Developer time-to-first-API-call: < 2 hours for SDK quickstart.
- Reliability: automated fallback keeps error rate < 0.5% during induced fault test.
- Observability coverage: token-level cost and per-route latency traces available in console.

Pricing guidance (practical approach for pilots)
- Pilot pricing model options to offer prospects (pick one):
  1) Timeboxed credits: $X in hosted credit covering N tokens / 30 days.
  2) Metered pilot with reporting: standard per-token units with a capped monthly commit.
  3) Short-term Dedicated trial: discounted reserved capacity for a 6–8 week trial.
- Example cost projection (simple table):
  | Scenario | Avg tokens / req | Req/sec | Monthly Requests | Monthly tokens | Estimated cost (hosted) |
  |---------|-----------------|---------|------------------|----------------|------------------------|
  | Chat 1   | 600             | 1.2     | 3,110,400        | 1.86B          | $3,720                |
  | Embeddings | 512           | 0.2     | 518,400          | 265M           | $1,060                |
- Guidance: run with representative traces from production or staging traffic. Batching and caching recommendations often reduce cost by 25–65% depending on prompt reuse.

SE pitch deck outline (5 slides, one-line purpose each)
1) Problem (1 slide): inconsistent inference economics, noisy latency, fragmentation between hosted and private.
2) Solution (1 slide): Redwood’s unified runtime + controls that let dev teams predict cost and latency.
3) Pilot approach & success criteria (1 slide): 6-week plan, KPIs, and low-effort onboarding.
4) Economics & reliability proof points (1 slide): sample cost projection, fallback examples, SLOs met in prior customers.
5) Next steps & ask (1 slide): pilot activation, decision gates, and procurement timeline.

Customer vignette (short case study)
- Customer: Arbor Health (fictional synthesis to illustrate narrative).
- Problem: High variability in inference cost and slow model rollouts across internal teams.
- Pilot outcome (6 weeks): reduced median token cost by 38% through KV caching + selective quantized model variants; p95 latency improved by 22% after batching policy tweaks; developer time-to-first-call reduced from 2 days to 90 minutes with SDK templates.
- Business impact: estimated annualized inference savings of $180k for the initial product team, faster feature iteration leading to a 2-week speedup in release cadence.

Security FAQ (targeted for platform/security reviewers)
Q: What deployment models are available during a pilot?
A: Hosted (fastest) and Private VPC (customer-managed networking). For sensitive workloads we offer an on-prem package with air-gapped options; pilot can start hosted with a plan to migrate to private if required.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers. For Private deployments the customer retains KMS control; Hosted uses per-tenant customer keys when requested.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and traceability?
A: Yes — token-level usage records, model/version metadata, and per-request traces are available via the Console and can be exported to SIEMs.

Q: What network controls exist for private deployments?
A: Private VPC deployments support customer-specified subnets, security groups, and private peering. We provide a network diagram and step-by-step connectivity checklist during onboarding.

Q: How is data residency handled in hosted mode?
A: Customers can select region-specific deployments; audit artifacts include data flow diagrams and retention policies. For strict residency requirements, we recommend Private deployments.

Onboarding checklist (compact)
- [ ] Pilot charter signed (KPIs and success criteria)
- [ ] Tenant provisioned (hosted or private)
- [ ] Sample prompt set and traces uploaded
- [ ] Initial baseline run completed and dashboard shared
- [ ] Optimization changes applied and retested
- [ ] Security evidence bundle submitted
- [ ] Final report with recommended next steps delivered

Runbooks & artifacts delivered with pilot
- Baseline performance dashboard (p50/p95, throughput, token-cost).
- Optimization notes: batching settings, cache TTLs, quantization profile used.
- Security evidence: network diagram, KMS integration guide, audit-log sample.
- Rollout recipe: canary steps and rollback triggers.

Appendix: sample curl quickstart (hosted)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4b-optimized","input":"Summarize the following customer query...","stream":true}'

Notes on tailoring the playbook
- Replace sample token-cost estimates with actual traces for each prospect.
- For regulated customers, schedule the Private evaluation early (Week 0–1).
- Use the customer vignette to highlight economic and developer velocity outcomes rather than raw bench numbers.

Contact & ownership
- SE lead for pilot activation: Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai)
- Solution owner: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai)
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair (pnair@redwood.ai)

Related artifacts to attach to pilot ticket
- SDK quickstart repo link, sample prompt set (CSV), default batching profiles (YAML), security evidence checklist (PDF).

Document history
- 2028-03-15: draft created by Maya Chen.
- 2028-04-05: final review and published (added pricing projection and security FAQ).

sections.body:
OVERVIEW

Purpose: This playbook is a pragmatic engagement framework for reps and solutions engineers to position Redwood Inference during mid-to-large prospect cycles. It combines: concise messaging, competitive differentiation, three pricing scenarios with example math, a pitch-deck outline with speaker notes, a compact case study, a security FAQ tailored to prospect concerns, and objection-handling scripts. Use this as a living doc — update pricing examples with current rate cards and redirect technical questions to eng-se or product-ops.

Target personas
- Head of ML / ML Platform: cost/operationalization, model versioning, SLAs.
- Backend / Product Engineering Lead: latency, integration effort, SDKs, API stability.
- Security / Infra: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, compliance evidence.
- Procurement / Finance: predictable spend, reserved options, contract terms.

TOP-LINE MESSAGING (1-sentence and 3-line)
- 1-sentence: Redwood Inference provides a single runtime and control plane to serve LLMs with production reliability, predictable economics, and a unified developer experience across hosted, reserved, and private deployments.
- 3-line: Ship LLM features fast with our hosted API, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost, and adopt Private for regulated or air-gapped needs — all with per-route observability, rollouts, and cost controls to avoid surprise bills.

POSITIONING & VALUE HYPOTHESES
- Cost predictability: Dedicated/reserved capacity with predictable token throughput reduces variable spend for high-volume inference (customers routinely see 20–60% lower per-token costs vs fully hosted on high-throughput workloads).
- Latency & reliability: GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart batching and KV caching deliver consistent p95/p99 latency; we support automatic model fallbacks and multi-region routing to meet SLAs.
- Developer productivity: Single API + SDKs and rollout primitives (canary/A-B/fallback) enable teams to iterate without bespoke infra.
- Compliance & isolation: Private deployments provide a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and audit trails for regulated workloads.

USE-CASE MESSAGING (30–60s per vertical)
- Customer Support Automation: Reduce avg handle time by 25–40% (RAG + tuned generation). Position: hosted for pilot, Dedicated when throughput hits 50 concurrent sessions.
- Search & Reranking: Improve relevance metrics and reduce expensive downstream compute via embeddings + reranker; latency SLOs of <150ms for p95.
- Knowledge & Summarization for Regulated Data: Private deployment + HSM + retention controls; emphasize auditability and deterministic model versions.

PRICING SCENARIOS (EXAMPLE NUMBERS FOR DISCUSSION)
Notes: These are template scenarios — replace with current rate card when quoting. All prices are illustrative and in USD.
1) Proof-of-concept (pilot, hosted)
- Assumptions: 1M tokens / month generation, 50k embeddings/month, 3-month pilot.
- Host rates (example): text gen $0.0006 / token, embeddings $0.00075 / unit.
- Monthly: gen = 1,000,000 * $0.0006 = $600; embeddings = 50,000 * $0.00075 = $37.50; estimated monthly = ~$637.50.
- Sales hook: Fast time-to-value, free tiers/credits to reduce friction.

2) Scale (growth SaaS using Hosted + caching)
- Assumptions: 100M tokens / month, caching reduces 40% effective tokens, embeddings 1M/month.
- Effective tokens billed = 60M.
- Hosted enterprise negotiated rate (example): $0.00035 / token; embeddings $0.0005 / unit.
- Monthly: gen = 60,000,000 * $0.00035 = $21,000; embeddings = 1,000,000 * $0.0005 = $500; total = ~$21,500.
- Levers to reduce cost: enable prefix/KV caching, batch config tuning, use quantized smaller model variants for non-sensitive workloads.

3) Predictable/Committed (Dedicated reserved capacity)
- Assumptions: Customer commits to a 3-node A100-equivalent pool (reserved) supporting 400M tokens / month baseline; burst to shared capacity allowed.
- Pricing: reserved capacity = monthly platform + reserved GPU commit. Example: platform fee $4,500 / mo + reserved node equivalent $12,000 / node / mo => 3 nodes = $36,000.
- Effective unit economics: with 400M tokens baseline, per-token baseline = ($40,500 / 400M) = $0.000101 / token — excluding embeddings and overage.
- Sales hook: predictable monthly capex/opex, SLA-backed latency and availability, better total cost at scale.

COST-REDUCTION RECOMMENDATIONS (for SEs/CS to propose)
- Deploy prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated context tokens by 30–70% depending on workflow.
- Use batching aggressively for back-of-house jobs; tune batching thresholds to balance latency/throughput.
- Quantize models for non-sensitive workloads where quality impact is acceptable.
- Route low-priority or long-context jobs to cheaper model variants or off-peak capacity.

COMPETITIVE BRIEF (top competitors and positioning)
Format: Competitor — What they sell — Redwood angle to win
- OpenAI (hosted-first, broad dev ecosystem) — Strengths: wide adoption, strong baseline models; Weaknesses: price variability at scale, less control for private/enterprise on-prem. Redwood angle: predictable economics (Dedicated), private deployments, and clear performance profiles + observability.
- Anthropic / Claude (safety-first models) — Strengths: model safety and contextual handling; Weaknesses: enterprise integration and on-prem options vary. Redwood angle: flexibility to host/serve multiple model families, rollouts and regressions guardrails for productized safety testing.
- Vector DB + ML infra stacks (self-hosted: TorchServe, KServe, BentoML) — Strengths: total control, cost at large scale; Weaknesses: operational burden, engineering time. Redwood angle: unified runtime + ops tooling removes engineering overhead while preserving control in Private.
- Cloud-managed endpoints by hyperscalers (GCP/AWS model endpoints) — Strengths: deep infra integration; Weaknesses: fragmented tooling for LLM-specific optimizations. Redwood angle: LLM-optimized runtime, quantization recommendations, and per-route cost/latency observability.

BATTLECARD: Objections and concise rebuttals
- "We can just use OpenAI / hyperscaler APIs and be done." -> Rebuttal: For pilots yes; but at scale you’ll face unit cost creep and less control for regulated or latency-sensitive apps. We provide a migration path and predictable reserved pricing to manage spend and SLAs.
- "We need full control / will self-host." -> Rebuttal: Self-hosting avoids vendor lock but duplicates years of operational investment. Redwood Private gives control + hardened ops templates (onprem packaging + day-2 ops) with productized rollouts and support.
- "How do we know model regressions won't break UX?" -> Rebuttal: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring + evals to rollouts so you can gate deployments on prompt-set metrics and trigger automatic rollback.

PITCH DECK: 10-slide outline + speaker notes (concise)
1. Title / TL;DR: What Redwood does and one-sentence customer outcome. (Speaker note: set the economic frame — lower cost per request, predictable SLAs).
2. Customer problem: unpredictable inference costs, brittle rollouts, and ops overhead. (Note: use prospect-specific metrics if available).
3. Product overview: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private + Console. (Note: diagram showing same API across deployment modes).
4. Performance & economics: benchmarks (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost curves). (Note: reference our model catalog/verified profiles).
5. Case studies / outcomes (one-slide): key metric lifts and timelines.
6. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC/ISO evidence. (Note: emphasize Private and turnkey evidence).
7. Integration & migration path: pilot -> dedicated -> private, plus SDKs & templates. (Note: propose a 6–8 week path).
8. Pricing options and example scenarios (use the pricing scenarios above). (Note: include TCO snapshot).
9. Go-to-production (SLA, support tiers, onboarding). (Note: highlight Technical Account Manager + playbook delivery).
10. Next steps & ask (pilot proposal, architecture workshop, POC success criteria). (Note: end with clear CTA).

SAMPLE CASE STUDY (1-page summary)
Title: Observability SaaS reduced inference costs and improved p95 latency
Customer: AtlasTrace (mid-market SaaS observability vendor) — anonymized
Challenge: At 20M tokens/month, variable costs and p95 generation latency were causing customer churn for the trial experience.
Approach: Pilot on Hosted API for 4 weeks, then moved heavy inference to Dedicated reserved pool + enabled prefix caching and smaller quantized reranker for lower-cost pages.
Outcome (30 days post-migration): 42% reduction in per-token spend vs baseline, p95 latency improved from 420ms to 140ms for web-facing flows, and time-to-resolution for technical support decreased by 18%.
Quote: "Redwood let us iterate quickly and then lock in predictable economics when scale mattered." — Head of Platform, AtlasTrace

SECURITY FAQ (prospect-facing, concise answers)
Q: What deployment modes are available and which is right for regulated data?
A: Hosted API (fastest path to value), Dedicated (reserved, isolated GPU pools), Private (customer-managed control plane for VPC/on-prem). For regulated data we recommend Private with KMS and audit logging.
Q: How do you handle encryption and key management?
A: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+/mTLS for service-to-service. At-rest encryption supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments.
Q: Are audit logs and model usage trails available?
A: Yes — the Console exposes per-token usage logs, model version histories, who invoked routes, and retention options for audit export.
Q: What certifications/compliance artifacts can you provide?
A: We publish SOC2 Type II report excerpts and can provide architecture diagrams and control narratives. For regulated customers we offer an evidence package and an on-boarding compliance checklist.
Q: How do you protect against data exfiltration in model outputs?
A: Multiple layers: route-based policies, token redaction hooks, output filters, and optional private deployments that keep data in customer networks. We pair that with evals and regression testing on prompt sets to detect unexpected memorization.

SALES PLAY: 6–8 WEEK ENGAGEMENT PATH (recommended)
1) Week 0–1: Discovery + success criteria (data volumes, latency targets, compliance constraints).
2) Week 1–3: Pilot (Hosted): sample integration using SDKs, minimal data, measure latencies/costs, run baseline evals.
3) Week 3–5: Architecture workshop (Dedicated vs Private), sizing guidance, draft MSA/commit terms.
4) Week 5–8: Onboard Dedicated or Private, migrate traffic, enable optimize knobs (caching, batching), and run QA/eval guardrails.

OBJECTIONS & ONE-LINERS (cheat-sheet)
- "Too expensive" -> "We offer Reserved capacity and engineering best-practices that often reduce total cost by 20–60% compared to unmanaged hosted spend at scale."
- "Integration will take forever" -> "Most customers complete a pilot in 1–3 weeks using our SDKs and integration templates; Dedicated onboarding is a 4–8 week engagement with a TAM."

OPERATIONS & HANDOFFS
- SEs should deliver: pilot success criteria doc, sample prompt set (for evals), perf baseline, and a sizing worksheet.
- Post-sale handoff to CS: include reserved commit details, SLA ladder, runbooks, and rollout policy.

APPENDIX: SIZING CHECKLIST (quick)
- Expected qps and average response tokens per request
- Concurrent sessions and burst profile
- Retention/retention rules for KV/prefix caches
- Compliance requirements (e.g., data residency, encryption, audit retention)
- Preferred deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)

OWNER & CONTACT
- Playbook owner: Sofia Alvarez (go-to-market).
- Technical SME: Marcus Chen (solutions engineering).
- For pricing exceptions: Finance-legal (pricing-ops).

DOCUMENT CHANGE LOG
- 2026-02-10: Created (S. Alvarez).
- 2026-03-01: Added Dedicated pricing scenario and AtlasTrace case study (reviewers: M. Chen, E. Park).

END OF DOCUMENT

sections.body: This guide is intended for field sellers, solutions engineers, and technical buyers evaluating Redwood Inference. It combines three concrete buyer evaluation scenarios (with pass/fail criteria and recommended configurations) plus a concise security and compliance FAQ tailored for technical due diligence. Use this page as the canonical reference during pilot scoping calls and technical procurement reviews.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Primary audience: Technical buyers (platform engineers, ML infra leads, security architects) and product/engineering teams running inference in production.
- When to use:
  - Scoping pilots to validate latency, throughput, or data residency requirements.
  - Preparing security/compliance documents and demo checklists before an NDA/data access.
  - Negotiating dedicated capacity or private deployment commercial terms.
sections.heading: Audience and use cases

sections.body:
- Redwood delivers consistent inference economics and predictable latency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- We provide a single API and rollout tooling so engineering teams can iterate without re-architecting.
- For regulated workloads we support VPC/private control planes, KMS/HSM integration, and deep audit logs out-of-the-box.
sections.heading: Key messaging (short)

sections.body:
- Strengths: Production-grade runtime (continuous batching, KV cache, kernel selection), unified API across deployment modes, clear cost-performance levers.
- Typical competitor gaps: limited private deployment automation, opaque unit economics, fewer observability primitives (token-level cost, per-route tracing).
- Quick rebuttal lines:
  - "If you need a predictable latency SLO while reducing per-token cost, we can show a matched-benchmark with your dataset in 48 hours."
  - "Our rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) minimize risk during model upgrades without downtime."
sections.heading: Competitive posture summary (for the technical buyer)

sections.body:
1) Latency-sensitive chat assistant (real-time support agent)
2) High-throughput embeddings search (semantic search across 50M docs)
3) Regulated private deployment (PII-sensitive recommender)

Scenario 1 — Latency-sensitive chat assistant
- Goal: 95th percentile token-response latency < 120ms for 4k-context summary requests, concurrent users: 1,000 (burst to 3,000).
- Success criteria (must meet all):
  1. p95 per-token latency < 120ms under steady load of 1,000 concurrent active sessions.
  2. Tail latency during 3x burst < 250ms and no dropped requests (graceful backpressure).
  3. End-to-end SLA reportable in Redwood Console with traces and cost-per-request breakdown.
- Recommended baseline config:
  - Model variant: rwd-neo-latency-opt-7B (quantized int8), fallback rwd-neo-compat-7B
  - Deployment: Dedicated pool (GPU type: A100-40GB or equivalent) + autoscaling (scale window: 60s, max pool size: calculated during benchmark).
  - Runtime settings: max_tokens_per_request tuned to 512, KV cache enabled, per-route batching disabled for sub-50ms requests but continuous batching enabled for small windows.
- Pilot measurement plan (steps):
  1. Baseline: run 10-minute steady load at 1,000 concurrent simulated sessions; collect p50/p95/p99 latency.
  2. Burst: run three 30s bursts at 3,000 sessions; capture tail latency and error rates.
  3. Stability: 2-hour run with slow ramp to validate autoscaling and cache warmup.
- Typical sales talking points: emphasize cache warm-up effects on early tokens, propose a short optimization sprint to tune batching thresholds.

Scenario 2 — High-throughput embeddings search
- Goal: sustain 5,000 QPS embedding generation for semantic search across 50M documents with average vector size 1536, cost target <$0.0008 per embedding on committed throughput.
- Success criteria:
  1. Sustained throughput 5k QPS for 60 minutes with <0.1% error rate.
  2. Embedding vector fidelity within benchmark MRR delta < 1.5% vs. reference model.
  3. Storage/ingest pipeline supports vector retrieval latency < 30ms for top-10 queries.
- Recommended baseline config:
  - Model variant: embeddings-large-1536-v2 (float16), batching optimized for throughput, optional quantized 8-bit variant for additional cost savings.
  - Deployment: Dedicated with burst capacity and external vector store (e.g., FAISS/Annoy/RocksDB) colocated in same VPC/region.
  - Runtime settings: large continuous batches (batch_size target 512–1024), CPU->GPU sharding for preprocessing.
- Pilot measurement plan:
  1. Warmup ingest of 50M docs (batch ingestion using parallel workers).
  2. 60-minute steady-state 5k QPS run; validate memory/IO saturation.
  3. A/B run with quantized variant to measure cost vs. fidelity trade-off.

Scenario 3 — Regulated private deployment (PII-sensitive recommender)
- Goal: Private control plane in customer VPC with full KMS/HSM integration, SOC2+ISO evidence, and audit trail to satisfy security review for a healthcare pilot.
- Success criteria:
  1. Private deployment launched in customer VPC with no egress to public internet for model payloads.
  2. KMS-based envelope encryption for model artifacts and request data at rest, with customer-managed keys (CMK).
  3. Audit logs available for 90 days in customer’s SIEM and compliance report generated for reviewers.
- Recommended baseline config:
  - Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC mode) with optional air-gapped on-prem package for higher assurance.
  - Integrations: AWS KMS/CloudHSM or equivalent, SAML for SSO, SCIM for identity provisioning, and EFK or Splunk forwarding for logs.
  - Runtime: Dedicated GPU pools within VPC, private NAT or egress controls as required.
- Pilot measurement plan:
  1. Architecture review and customer security checklist completion (includes network diagram and data flows).
  2. Provision CMK and validate key rotation workflow and access control tests.
  3. Compliance smoke tests: pen-test window, audit log forwarding validation, and vulnerability scan.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Demo and pilot prerequisites (technical checklist)

sections.body:
Q: How does Redwood handle customer data in Hosted mode?
A: Hosted API: request payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+), at rest using our platform-managed KMS. We provide options to disable retention of request payloads (ephemeral mode) and to opt into customer-managed keys for model artifacts in Dedicated/Private modes.

Q: Can we run Redwood entirely within our VPC without egress?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports a VPC-first control plane and on-prem package options. For full air-gap requirements we offer an on-prem appliance and a validated deployment guide. Network diagrams and prescriptive firewall rules are provided during onboarding.

Q: What encryption and key management options exist?
A: Supported options: platform-managed KMS, AWS KMS customer-managed CMK, HashiCorp Vault integration, and CloudHSM for HSM-backed keys. We document key rotation and access review procedures as part of the compliance deliverables.

Q: How are audit logs surfaced?
A: Audit logs include API request metadata, model version used, token counts, and operator actions. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM via S3/Syslog/HTTPS. Retention policies are configurable; standard private deployments include 90 days by default.

Q: Do you provide penetration testing and third-party audit artifacts?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and provides ISO 27001 evidence upon enterprise contracting. We coordinate third-party penetration tests during Private deployments; remediation timelines are provided in the security onboarding plan.

Q: How do you protect model IP and customer prompts?
A: Model artifacts are stored in encrypted stores with role-based access controls. For private deployments, artifacts remain in the customer VPC. Prompt data can be configured to never be persisted in Hosted mode and to be routed through customer-managed storage for Private.

Q: What identity and access controls are available?
A: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC in Redwood Console, and token scoping for API keys (per-route, per-model). We recommend short-lived credentials for automation and enforce MFA for operator accounts.

Q: How do incident response and breach notification work?
A: For Hosted customers we follow our public incident response playbook with SLA'd notifications for P1/P0 incidents; notifications occur via customer-configured channels (email, PagerDuty). For Private deployments, we integrate with the customer incident response process and agree on runbook playbooks and SLAs during onboarding.
sections.heading: Security & compliance FAQ (technical buyer focused)

sections.body:
- Objection: "We can self-host and save money."
  - Rebuttal: "Self-hosting shifts long-term maintenance, kernel/optimization, and SRE burden to your team. We can run a pilot that quantifies ops cost and latency variance in 2–4 weeks."
- Objection: "We can’t share production prompts due to compliance."
  - Rebuttal: "We accept synthetic datasets or a small redacted sample for benchmarking; for Private pilots we enable a fully isolated environment where data never leaves your VPC."

Standard pilot runbook (recommended 6–8 week cadence):
1. Week 0: Kickoff, NDA, and security checklist completion.
2. Week 1: Environment provisioning (Hosted sandbox or Dedicated pool); ingest representative data.
3. Week 2–3: Benchmark runs and initial tuning (latency & batching).
4. Week 4: Optimization sprint (2-week focused tuning with SE and runtime engineers).
5. Week 5–6: Stability and regression tests; finalize SLOs.
6. Week 7–8: Executive review, pricing proposal, and contract handoff.

Appendix: sample configuration snippets
- Example CLI snippet to create a dedicated pool (illustrative):
  - rwdctl pool create --name "prospect-dedicated" --gpu a100_40gb --min 2 --max 16 --autoscale-window 60

- Example YAML for private deployment network rules (illustrative):
  - policies:
    - name: allow-internal-control
      source: 10.0.0.0/16
      destination: 10.0.1.0/24
      ports: [443, 22]

sections.body:
Overview
This document is a field-focused, sector-agnostic companion for sales architects, solution engineers, and account executives engaging security-conscious buyers (CISO/CSO, Head of Platform, Cloud Architects). It consolidates: positioning and messaging, an abbreviated competitive brief, a buyer-oriented pitch deck outline, pragmatic pricing guidance & examples, a short customer case study, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect evaluation. Use this resource during discovery, technical workshops, and contract negotiation.

Goals and audience
- Primary audience: Sales Architects, Solutions Engineers, AE for mid-market and enterprise accounts.
- Secondary audience: Pre-sales leadership, Customer Success, Enablement.
- Goal: Reduce friction in technical conversations by providing reproducible messaging, clear objections handling, and concrete economics and security evidence for rapid pilots and procurement.

One-line positioning (for technical buyers)
Redwood Inference provides a production-first inference platform that guarantees predictable latency, measurable unit economics, and operational controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so platform teams can ship LLM features without building and owning the serving stack.

Talking tracks (by buyer persona)
- Platform Engineer / SRE:
  - Core needs: predictable latency, capacity planning, observability, SLO guarantees.
  - Key message: Dedicated and Private modes support pinned model versions, autoscaling policies, and token-level cost/latency breakdowns. Deploy with existing CI/CD and use our rollout features (canary, A/B, automatic fallback).
- ML/Model Ops:
  - Core needs: model versioning, quality monitoring, efficient KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles.
  - Key message: Redwood Optimize recommends quantization and batching profiles by workload and delivers regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We support shadow testing against canary variants and automatic fallbacks if quality drops.
- Security / Compliance / Legal:
  - Core needs: data residency, auditability, key management, minimal attack surface.
  - Key message: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) provides customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. For hosted customers we provide configurable data handling policies and SOC/ISO evidence.
- Finance / Procurement:
  - Core needs: predictable TCO, commitment math, usage governance.
  - Key message: Multiple contracting options (pay-as-you-go, reserved Dedicated capacity, enterprise Private licensing); tooling provides token-level cost attribution and batch/caching recommendations to reduce unit cost.

Competitive brief (concise, field-friendly)
Table: Strengths / Weaknesses relative to typical competitors (managed LLM APIs and self-hosted runtimes)\- Redwood strengths: production-first runtime, unified API across deployment modes, cost controls (batching/caching/quantization suggestions), rollout & fallback primitives, token-level observability.\- Typical managed API competitor: fastest to integrate, limited customization and higher per-token variance, weaker private deployment controls.\- Open-source/self-hosted runtime: maximum control and lowest infra sticker for big scale but requires significant engineering investment (operational risk, lacking out-of-the-box rollout/observability).
