sections.body:
- "We can self-host cheaper." -> Rebuttal: True for raw monthly GPU spend at extreme scale; however, Redwood reduces engineering OPEX and time-to-market, provides autoscaling, multi-variant rollouts, and predictable SLO-backed options. We provide reserved capacity agreements to lower unit costs without the full build.
- "Managed APIs are simpler." -> Rebuttal: Simpler initially yes; Redwood's hosted API is equivalently easy for POC but uniquely offers Dedicated and Private paths with minimal integration changes when you need isolation or SLAs.
- "How is your accuracy vs model X?" -> Rebuttal: We don't alter model semantics; we surface model/variant performance profiles, and our Optimize tooling recommends quantization that preserves output quality per workload. Bring your eval suite and we’ll run regression checks as part of onboarding.

Pitch deck outline (10-slide technical storyline)
1) Title + contact + short value prop (2 lines)
2) Customer problem (latency unpredictability, unit-cost surprises, rollout & infra fragility) with 2 customer quotes/sources
3) Redwood solution: single-platform overview (hosted / dedicated / private) with diagram
4) How it works: serving runtime + smart routing + caching + compile/kernel selection (1-slide technical flow)
5) Measurable outcomes: median latency improvements, cost delta examples, SLOs (sample numbers below)
6) Security & compliance: private deployments, KMS/HSM support, audit logs
7) Operational controls: rollout, tracing, cost attribution, alerts and regressions
8) Pricing options and example TCO (POC -> production path)
9) Case study summary (see case study section)
10) Pilot ask and next steps (technical workshop + two-week pilot with defined success criteria)

Sample SLOs and thresholds (for argument and negotiation)
- 99th percentile generation latency: 200–800ms (depends on model & payload); Redwood can commit to SLA-backed targets on Dedicated.
- Uptime: 99.95% for Dedicated contracts (enterprise tier).
- Billing anomaly alert threshold: spend drift >20% week-over-week triggers an automatic review for customers in paid tiers.
- Regression detection: quality drop >3% on guardrail prompt set triggers rollback/fallback.

Pricing guidance and worked examples
sections.heading: Key attack lines and rebuttals

sections.body:
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation + per-embedding units; ideal for pilots and low-to-medium volume.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commit for GPU pools; predictable throughput and lower per-token cost; includes autoscaling policies and SLA.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support + optional on-prem packaging for regulated customers.

Worked example 1: Pilot (hosted)
- Customer: fintech analytics startup
- Expected usage: 20 million tokens/month generation; 500k embeddings/month
- Hosted estimate: 20M tokens x $0.0006 = $12,000; embeddings 500k x $0.0003 = $150; total ~ $12,150/month (sample numbers; replace with current pricing).
- Recommendation: Start hosted POC with 30 days of feature parity tests; instrument prompt sets for regression checks.

Worked example 2: Mid-market predictable commit (Dedicated)
- Customer: mid-market SaaS (support automation)
- Expected throughput: sustained 40 concurrent requests at p50 response <250ms for a medium LLM
- Suggested Dedicated commit: equivalent of 4 A100-class GPUs reserved monthly -> baseline fee + usage; expected unit-cost reduction 20–40% vs hosted.
- Recommendation: 90-day reserved pilot with canary rollout, auto-scale headroom at 1.5x, and monthly performance reviews.

Procurement and pilot checklist (two-week technical workshop -> 90-day pilot)
1) Scope: agreed prompt sets, eval metrics (latency, quality, cost), data handling requirements.
2) Environment: choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
3) Access: API keys, service accounts, network peering for Dedicated/Private.
4) Security: sign mutual NDA if required; confirm KMS/HSM preferences and encryption-at-rest policies.
5) Success criteria: e.g., latency 95p < target, no quality regressions on guardrail prompts, cost per 1k tokens within X% of estimate.
6) Rollout plan: shadow test -> dark traffic -> canary -> full cutover.

Case study (compact)
- Customer: Atlas Insights (pseudonym for reference)
- Problem: Latency spikes and runaway inference costs after scaling a document-summarization feature.
- Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated, applied workload-aware batching and prefix caching, pinned a tuned model variant, and used rollout + fallback for staged release.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in per-token cost, 3x reduction in p99 latency variance, and a seamless canary-based deploy that avoided production regressions.

Security FAQ for prospect conversations (CISO-focused, concise answers)
Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Depends on deployment mode. Hosted: regional tenancy with configurable data handling policies and optional retention controls. Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation. Private: full customer control over networking and storage.

Q: Do you support KMS/HSM integration?
A: Yes. We integrate with major cloud KMS providers; for air-gapped/private deployments we support HSM and customer-supplied key management.

Q: Can we review audit logs and request-level traces?
A: Yes. The Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-request trace links. For Private deployments, logs are shipped to customer systems per agreed retention windows.

Q: How do you prevent model theft / exfiltration risk?
A: We preserve model artifacts in the runtime with least-privilege access controls; private deployments keep models on-customer infrastructure. We also support request-level redaction and a configurable output policy layer to block sensitive output classes.

Q: What certifications/evidence do you provide?
A: Hosted and Dedicated offerings are backed by ISO/SOC evidence where applicable; for enterprise deals we provide artifact packages, architecture diagrams, and support for audits.

Q: How is PII handled?
A: We recommend minimizing PII in prompt inputs. For regulated customers, Private deployments enable complete control; otherwise hosted options include configurable retention and deletion policies.

Q: What are the incident response commitments?
A: Incident classification, escalation, and communications are defined in the enterprise SLA. Customers on enterprise tiers receive 24/7 pager escalation and monthly incident reports.

Objection handling snippets (field-ready)
- Objection: "We already have feature parity with another provider." -> Snippet: "Great — is it predictable as you scale? Our customers choose Redwood when they need consistent unit economics and deterministic latency under load. We can run a controlled benchmark against your workload in a week."
- Objection: "We can't change our data residency rules." -> Snippet: "We support Private deployments and on-prem packaging that meet strict residency controls — let’s map your controls to our architecture checklist in the technical workshop."

Appendix: Short technical snippet & demo commands
1) Simple hosted generation (curl):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

2) Sample JSON: rollout policy (CLI-friendly)
{
  "policy_name": "support-bot-canary",
  "variants": [
    {"model":"rwd-medium-1","weight":0.1},
    {"model":"rwd-medium-1-quant","weight":0.9}
  ],
  "metrics": ["latency_p95","quality_regressions"],
  "rollback_on": {"quality_regressions": ">3%"}
}

3) Suggested monitoring alert thresholds (Prometheus-style):
- redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"} < 0.90 for 5m -> severity=P1
- redwood_request_error_rate > 0.02 for 10m -> severity=P2

sections.body:
Purpose
=======
This playbook is a go-to-market and engineering-aligned guide for running a successful inference pilot with regulated healthcare customers. It covers positioning and messaging, a concise competitive brief, archetypal pilot scope, security & compliance checkpoints (PHI/PII handling, BAA, encryption), pricing scenarios, a sample customer case study, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this document when engaging hospitals, digital health startups, or payer platforms considering production LLM inference.

Executive summary
-----------------
- Objective: Convert a 4–8 week pilot into a committed deployment (Dedicated or Private) by demonstrating safety, latency, cost predictability, and compliance controls.
- Key buyer personas: Platform/infra engineers, Head of ML, Security/Privacy Officer, Health IT/Integrations, Procurement.
- Success metrics for pilot: PHI-safe API surface, latency P99 < 350ms (for text assistant workflows), end-to-end accuracy parity within ±2% vs baseline, controlled inference unit cost <= target.

Positioning and messaging (one-liners)
-------------------------------------
- For security and compliance leads: "Run regulated LLM inference with a vendor that provides a private control plane, BAA-ready tooling, KMS integrations, and audit-grade logging—without rebuilding your serving stack."
- For platform/ML engineers: "Ship predictable, low-latency inference across hosted, dedicated, and VPC/private deployments with the same API, rollout tooling, and observability."
- For product owners: "Deliver a safer, faster clinical assistant with model-level rollouts and behavioral regression alerts to keep production quality steady as models evolve."

Quick competitive brief
-----------------------
- Primary competitors considered by healthcare buyers: large cloud vendor-managed endpoints, specialized inference service vendors, and open-source self-hosted stacks.
- Redwood differentiation: Unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, turnkey BAA-ready controls, KV/prefix caching to reduce PHI surface and cost, deterministic rollouts + eval hooks for quality regressions.
- Seller bullets vs typical objections:
  - "We already have model endpoints in the cloud": Redwood supports VPC Private deployments + audit logs + KMS to match security posture while offering lower per-token cost through runtime optimizations.
  - "We need on-prem": Use Redwood Private (on-prem packaging + air-gapped install) with documented day-2 ops and upgrade paths.
  - "We worry about hallucinations and regressions": Redwood Optimize integrates evals and regression alerts tied to your canonical prompt set and clinical prompts.

Pilot scope: recommended configuration
------------------------------------
- Duration: 4–8 weeks (negotiable).
- Workloads: clinical summarization, triage-assist prompts, discharge note templates (avoid direct diagnostic replacement during pilot).
- Deployment options: start with VPC Private or Dedicated in the region the customer requires. Hosted may be acceptable for non-PHI-sandboxed pilots.
- Models: include one production-calibrated LLM (quantized variant) + a smaller fallback model for degraded mode.
- SLOs and targets:
  - Latency: P95 < 200ms, P99 < 350ms for typical 512-token requests.
  - Availability: 99.9% (pilot-focused).
  - Cost targets: aim to show >=25% improvement from customer baseline via caching/quantization.

Pilot timeline and responsibilities (numbered)
--------------------------------------------
1. Pre-sales checklist (week -1 to 0): legal (BAA draft), security Ask (networking, IP allowlist), initial data sample request, define pilot success criteria. Owner: AE + SE.
2. Kickoff (day 0): architecture review, data flows, roles/contacts, and rollback plan. Owner: Solutions Engineer.
3. Deployment (days 1–7): Provision Dedicated or Private environment, integrate KMS, configure audit logging. Owner: Infra Eng + Customer IT.
4. Integration & prompts (days 7–14): run prompt calibration, add prefix/KV caching policies, measure throughput. Owner: ML Eng + Customer ML.
5. Evaluation (days 14–28): run structured evals, compare quality metrics, run security tests (pen-test checklist). Owner: Applied ML + Security.
6. Review & conversion (days 28–42): present results, propose committed capacity and price. Owner: AE + Product Specialist.

Technical configuration examples
--------------------------------

Observability & SLOs (table)
----------------------------
| Metric | Pilot Target | Owner | Alert threshold |
|--------|--------------|-------|-----------------|
| Request latency (P95) | <200ms | Platform | >250ms for 5m |
| Error rate (4xx/5xx) | <1% | Oncall | >2% for 10m |
| Tokens per second | Baseline+20% | Capacity | Sustained >80% of limit |
| Quality regression (eval score) | <=1.5% drop | Applied ML | >2% drop |

Pricing guidance (example scenarios)
-----------------------------------
- Hosted pilot (no PHI): metered usage, typical pilot spend $5k–$20k depending on traffic and eval runs. Per-token example: $0.0006 per 1k prompt tokens (example).
- Dedicated pilot (recommended for PHI): reserved monthly seat + metered overage. Example pilot pricing: $18,000/month reserved for 2x A100-equivalent nodes (pilot discount applied) + usage egress fees.
- Conversion proposal: tiered committed capacity with volume discounts; include migration credits for pilot artifacts and sustained discount for 12m commit.

Sales collateral: prospect talking points and objection handling
------------------------------------------------------------
- Trusted controls: "We provide an auditable control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and a documented BAA offering to minimize legal friction."
- Speed to production: "Same API and SDKs across deployment models — your integration work is reusable when you move from pilot to Dedicated or Private."
- TCO framing: Present cost delta from customer baseline and show runtime levers (batching, caching, quantization) that yield unit cost reductions.

Case study: MediTrack Health (pilot summary)
------------------------------------------
- Customer: MediTrack Health (fictional but representative midsize telehealth provider).
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks.
- Scope: discharge-summary drafting and triage-assist workflows (non-diagnostic).
- Outcome:
  - Latency: P95 improved from 320ms (baseline) to 180ms.
  - Cost: unit token cost reduced by 38% after enabling prefix caching and a q4 quantized model.
  - Quality: clinical summary ROUGE-L maintained within 0.8% of baseline.
  - Business result: product team moved to a 12-month Dedicated commitment with a projected 3x throughput target.

Security & compliance checklist (must-complete before pilot with PHI)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Signed BAA in place.
- VPC / private connectivity or on-prem deployment approved.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys; customer controls encryption keys where required.
- Audit logs enabled for all inference requests and model activities; retention agreed.
- Data minimization applied to prompts: strip direct PHI where possible; map identifiers rather than free-text.
- Penetration test schedule and responsible parties documented.

Prospect-facing Security FAQ (concise)
------------------------------------
Q: Do you sign a BAA?
A: Yes. Redwood has a standard BAA template and a track record of signing BAAs with healthcare customers. For on-prem or air-gapped installs, the BAA is scoped to the delivered package and support model.

Q: How is PHI protected in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
A: Hosted: recommended only for non-PHI pilots. Dedicated: physically isolated compute and tenant separation; network controls and audit logs. Private: full control plane in your VPC or on-premises with keys and logs under your management. All modes support KMS/HSM.

Q: Can you restrict model access and keep raw prompts out of logs?
A: Yes. We support redaction and selective logging (masking policies) and can route logging for sensitive endpoints to a customer-managed SIEM.

Q: What certifications do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane and provides documentation packages for customer security review. For Private deployments, we provide hardened packaging and guidance to satisfy certs under customer responsibility.

Q: What is your data retention and deletion policy for pilot artifacts?
A: Pilot artifacts retention is configurable; short pilot default is 30 days unless customer requests otherwise. Deletion requests for customer-provided artifacts are honored and logged.

Conversion & next steps checklist for AE/SEs

payload.page_title: Resilience & Fallback Sales Deck for Critical Inference

sections.body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document is a field-ready sales deck and evidence pack that surfaces Redwood Inference's resilience and graceful-degradation story for mission-critical inference workloads (finance fraud detection, live customer support routing, automated decisioning). It bundles positioning, competitive differentiators, a slide-level pitch outline, pilot pricing guidance, a short case study, technical rollout patterns, and a security FAQ for buyer conversations.

Use: Sales engineers and account teams should use this as a single-page narrative + slide checklist when proposing pilots to prospects that require high availability, predictable latency, and clear fallback guarantees.

Key message (one-liner)
-----------------------
"Predictable inference when everything else fails: keep latency SLOs, control unit economics, and preserve confidentiality with tiered fallbacks and multi-path routing."

Positioning & Messaging (3 elevator lines)
----------------------------------------
- For platform and infra teams that must guarantee uninterrupted user experiences, Redwood provides an inference runtime and control plane that prioritizes reliability and graceful degradation over ideal-case throughput numbers.
- Unlike single-endpoint cloud APIs or self-built runtimes, Redwood couples an operational playbook (canaries, automatic fallback policies, cross-region routing) with economic controls so resilience is measurable and affordable.
- Our default selling point: SLAs you can instrument (uptime, latency SLOs, error budgets) and automated fallbacks that prevent application-visible failures.

Competitive Brief (quick takeaways)
----------------------------------
Competitors considered: public cloud model endpoints, large API-first LLM providers, and self-managed inference stacks.

Differentiators (table as text)
- Smart routing and fallbacks: route to cheaper/compatible model variants or regionally isolated Dedicated pools when primary capacity is constrained.
- Observability-first: token-level cost & latency breakdowns, route tracing, and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Operational guarantees: canary rollouts, A/B controlled rollouts, transparent rollback triggers based on quality and latency thresholds.
- Cost controls: batching and caching recommendations specific to workload, quantization profiles, and precise per-route unit economics.

Performance & SLO snapshots (typical published benchmarks)
- Hosted API (general workloads): p50 35–60ms, p95 110–220ms depending on model size and sequence length.
- Dedicated reserved pools: p50 20–40ms, p95 70–150ms for optimized-medium models.
- Platform SLA examples: 99.95% uptime, target p95 latency for a given route with error budget tied to token-level retries.

Pitch Deck Outline (12-slide recommended flow)
------------------------------------------------
1) Cover: Logo, prospect name, meeting date, objective (pilot ask).
2) Problem: What breaks in production (latency spikes, model-serving outages, cost overruns, regulatory constraints).
3) Why it matters: user/business impact with KPI examples (abandon rate, fraud loss, revenue per minute).
4) Redwood value prop: unified runtime + fallbacks + observability.
5) How it works (simplified diagram): request routing -> KV/prefix cache -> model variants -> fallback paths.
6) Resilience model: SLOs, retry/circuit-breaker logic, fallback tiers (same-model-smaller, distilled variant, cached response).
7) Security & compliance: VPC/private, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
8) Pricing & pilot structure: example pricing scenarios (see below).
9) Case study: short wins from a comparable customer (results and metrics).
10) Pilot plan & success criteria: timelines, data access, monitoring checklist.
11) Next steps & commercial ask: pilot length, committed throughput or burst credits.
12) Appendix & technical contact: integration owner and SRE contact.

Pilot Pricing Guidance (field-ready scripts and examples)
-------------------------------------------------------
Guiding principle: For resilience pilots, price for predictability, not just tokens. Structure pilots to allow capacity guarantees and observable metrics.

Sample pilot models (numbers are example guidance for field conversations):
- Trial (proof-of-concept): 2–4 week window, $0 setup, free credits up to $5k for hosted API with monitoring instrumentation.
- Resilience Pilot (recommended): 6–8 weeks, dedicated small pool (N GPU equivalents), $12k/month (discounted trial price), includes SRE onboarding, route-level dashboards, and automated fallback policy set-up.
- Proof to Commit: Convert pilot metrics to a committed Dedicated offering: e.g., 2x pilot throughput committed for 12 months at $45k/month with priority support and a 99.95% SLA.

Example per-token framing for conversations: use token-equivalent units (TEUs) for cross-model comparisons.
- Hosted baseline: $0.0007 per generation token for medium models (ballpark; aim for customer-specific quoting).
- Dedicated amortized: effectively $0.0003–$0.0005 per token once reserved throughput and batching optimizations are applied for steady workloads.

Commercial ask scripts (example wording)
- "To validate resilience end-to-end we recommend a six-week Resilience Pilot: we’ll provision a small Dedicated pool, instrument three critical routes, and implement two fallback tiers. If your systems meet the success criteria (p95 latency under X ms, <0.5% fallbacks to cached responses), we’ll translate telemetry into a reserved-capacity proposal you can evaluate."

Field Playbook: Objections & Responses (common prospect concerns)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- Objection: "We cannot tolerate any data leakage to third parties."
  Response: "We offer Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem packaging; keys remain in your KMS/HSM and audit logs are exported to your SIEM."
- Objection: "What happens if primary model capacity is exhausted?"
  Response: "We’ll configure multi-tier fallbacks: 1) reroute to your Dedicated pool, 2) fall back to a lightweight compatible model we host with lower cost, 3) serve cached or templated responses with graceful downgrade messaging to users. All fallbacks are counted in metrics and visible in the dashboard."
- Objection: "How do you guarantee the fallback quality?"
  Response: "Fallback models are pre-evaluated on your prompt set and have automatic quality gates; we only enable fallback paths that meet a defined BLEU/accuracy threshold or pass your custom eval harness."

Technical Appendix: Integration & Rollout Patterns
--------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Test prompt corpus (1k–10k examples) covering edge cases and typical length distributions.
- Defined success metrics: p95 latency target, fallback rate ceiling, false positive/negative thresholds for quality.
- Network connectivity: whitelist Redwood control-plane IPs for Dedicated/VPC onboarding, or provide peering details for Private.

Canary / Rollout recipe (recommended)
1) Provision route in staging with tracing enabled.
2) Run synthetic traffic for 48–72 hours, collect p50/p95/p99 and error counts.
3) Enable canary (2–5% of production traffic) with automatic rollback if daily error rate exceeds 0.2% or p95 increases by >40%.
4) Gradually increase to 25%, monitor for 72 hours, then switch traffic.

Sample API snippet (fallback policy)
```json
{ "route": "/messages/generate", "slo": { "p95_ms": 150 }, "fallback_policy": [
  { "type": "same-model-quantized", "max_latency_ms": 200 },
  { "type": "smaller-variant", "model": "redwood-compact-3b", "max_latency_ms": 300 },
  { "type": "kv_cache_response", "max_age_seconds": 3600 }
] }
```
(Use this example in technical appendix slides to show that fallback policies are declarative and instrumented.)

Case Study: ParcelPro (logistics) — two-page customer brief
---------------------------------------------------------
Context: ParcelPro is a large logistics platform that runs real-time address normalization and delivery exception triage. Their user-facing systems historically suffered from model-serving outages during Black Friday-like peaks.
sections.heading: Minimum required items for a resilience pilot

sections.body: - Spiky inference demand during peak windows increased p95 latency to >700ms and caused ~4% request failures that translated to delayed deliveries and customer support overload.
sections.heading: Challenge

sections.body: - Provisioned a Dedicated pool for critical routes, configured automatic multi-tier fallback (quantized variant + cached responses), and implemented prefix-KV caching for repetitive address normalizations.
sections.heading: Redwood solution

sections.body:
- p95 latency reduced from 700ms to 120ms for critical route.
- Failures visible to applications dropped from 4% to 0.03% (exceeded 99.95% uptime target).
- Unit cost for peak windows dropped 31% due to batching and quantization profiles.

Buyer quote (paraphrased): "Redwood allowed us to stop apologizing for downtime — our routing system stayed resilient through the busiest weekend we’ve seen."

Security & Compliance FAQ (top questions for prospect meetings)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Data residency is configured per-customer. For Hosted we provide region controls and retention policies configurable by route (default 90 days for logs, 30 days for KV cache metadata). Private deployments mirror customer policies.

Q: Can I bring my own KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM integrations for key wrapping and signing of model artifacts.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and SIEM integration?
A: Yes — all request/response metadata, authorization events, and fallback activations are exported via our audit pipeline to S3/BigQuery/your SIEM with configurable retention.

Q: What certifications or independent audits do you have?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and perform annual penetration testing with third-party vendors; we supply audit artifacts under NDA for enterprise due diligence.

Q: How are fallbacks tested for model safety and data leakage?
A: Fallback variants are vetted in the same onboarding eval harness as primary models. We run tokenizer-based leakage scans and prompt-perturbation tests before enabling fallback.

Owners, Contacts & Next Steps
----------------------------
- Sales enablement lead: Nadia Kline (n.kline@redwood.ai) — primary owner for decks and pilot collateral.
- Platform engineering sponsor: Arjun Patel — technical scoping and Dedicated pool configuration.
- SRE oncall (resilience pilots): eng-sre@redwood.ai — runbook and incident escalation.

Next steps (playbook for closing a resilience pilot)
1) Discovery call: 60-minute technical and business alignment; capture SLOs and critical routes.
2) Proposal: 3–5 business days to produce pilot scope, monitoring checklist, and provisional quote.
3) Onboarding: 1–2 week setup with platform + SRE pairing.
4) Pilot run: 6–8 weeks with weekly syncs and a final telemetry review.
5) Commercial conversion: translate pilot telemetry into committed capacity and SLA contract.

Appendix: Slide checklist for live demo
- Synthetic traffic generator configured for p99 stress test.
- Live dashboard: route p50/p95/p99, fallback percentages, token cost breakdown.
- Canary controls visible and ready to toggle.

Document maintenance
--------------------
Owner: Nadia Kline (go-to-market). Update cadence: quarterly or after any major runtime or SLA change.

Related internal references
- eng-sre/runbooks/inference-fallback-runbook
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/high-availability-patterns
- product-docs/requirements/resilience-and-fallback-requirements

End of document.

sections.body:
A structured, tactical commercial playbook that helps sales and solutions teams diagnose a prospect's inference needs, position Redwood's unique value, run a lightweight TCO and risk comparison, and close with tailored pricing and security points. Includes competitive brief, pitch outline, three short case vignettes, and a prospect-facing security FAQ.
Overview

Purpose: Provide a repeatable decision framework and companion collateral for sellers and solutions engineers engaging mid-market and enterprise buyers evaluating LLM inference platforms. This doc prioritizes lifecycle risks (cost, latency, reliability, compliance) and gives concrete talk tracks, objection responses, and example pricing scenarios.

How to use this playbook
1) Qualification checklist (5 minutes): use during initial discovery call. If 3+ boxes checked, recommend a Technical Brief and Demo.
   - Expected concurrent requests > 20 QPS or bursty spikes > 100 QPS
   - Hard latency SLOs (p99 < 500ms) for interactive flows
   - Data residency, audit, or regulatory controls needed (HIPAA, PCI, GDPR localized data)
   - Budget sensitivity where per-token economics matter (high volume generation or embeddings)
   - Multi-cloud or private deployment preference

2) Rapid diagnosis (10–30 minutes with SE): map prospect to one of three buyer archetypes below to tailor messaging and pricing.

Buyer archetypes
- Developer-first startup (PLG flow): Prioritizes time-to-value, simple hosted API, cost transparency, sample-based benchmarks.
- Product team at scale (SaaS): Requires predictable throughput, predictable pricing (Reserved/Dedicated), and rollout controls.
- Regulated enterprise (Finance/Healthcare/Gov): Needs Private/VPC, KMS/HSM, audit trail, compliance evidence and professional services.

Positioning & Talk tracks (by archetype)
- Developer-first: "Ship quickly with our hosted API, free credits, and SDKs — benchmarked latency and cost profiles let you plan growth."
- Product team: "Lock predictable capacity and unit economics with Dedicated pools; integrate with Redwood Console for per-route observability and cost allocation."
- Regulated enterprise: "Deploy Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem bundle with KMS integration and SLA-backed support for regulated workloads."

Competitive brief (concise)
Use this as a one-page sheet when prospects ask how Redwood differs vs typical alternatives.

Competitors considered: Managed cloud AI endpoints, pure open-source self-hosted runtimes, and LLM API providers.

Comparison matrix (high level)
| Dimension                   | Redwood Inference                   | Managed Cloud Endpoints        | Open self-hosted runtimes         | LLM API provider (low-cost)    |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Time-to-value              | High (hosted + SDKs + templates)    | Medium                        | Low (build + ops)                 | High                           |
| Predictable cost           | High (Dedicated + Optimize tooling) | Low/Varies                    | Depends on operator               | Variable                       |
| Private deployment         | VPC/on-prem supported                | Limited                       | Supported but heavy ops           | Rare                           |
| Observability & rollout    | Native Console + per-route metrics   | Basic                        | Custom-built                      | Minimal                        |
| Compliance evidence        | Prebuilt artifacts & PS offering     | Varies                        | Depends on implementation         | Low                            |
| SLAs & enterprise support  | SLA-backed (Dedicated/Private)       | Varies                        | No vendor SLA                     | Limited                        |

Key competitive messages to use in sales calls
- "We are inference-first: our runtime and orchestration optimize latency and cost specifically for LLM workloads, not generic CPU/GPU endpoints."
- "Unified experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — reduces your integration and operational complexity."
- "You can start hosted for speed and migrate to Dedicated or Private with preserved API and tooling."

Pitch deck outline (10–12 slides, quick sequence)
1. Title / TL;DR — one-sentence value prop and fit (30s)
2. Customer problem — latency, cost, reliability, and compliance gaps (1–2 slides)
3. Redwood solution overview — runtime + routing + tooling (1 slide)
4. Deployment paths — Hosted, Dedicated, Private with example personas (1 slide)
5. Measured outcomes — benchmark snapshots: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (1 slide)
6. Security & compliance highlights — KMS, VPC, audit logs (1 slide)
7. Pricing models & example TCO (1–2 slides)
8. 30/60/90 pilot plan — success criteria and checkpoints (1 slide)
9. Case vignettes — 2 short wins (1 slide)
10. Next steps & ask — trial, POC scope, stakeholders (1 slide)

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb and example scenarios)
- Pricing levers: hosted per-token, embeddings units, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), professional services (onboarding/validation), retention/observability add-ons.
- Rules of thumb:
  * For experimental/low-volume projects: recommend hosted API with monthly spend cap and SDK guides.
  * For predictable product features (>=$10k/month): propose Dedicated pooled capacity to achieve predictable latency and lower unit cost.
  * For regulated workloads: price Private deployment as a platform fee + annual support + optional on-prem binpack.

Q: Can you sign a BAA or SOC2 addendum?

Operational playbook for SEs: step-by-step during a POC

2. Baseline test: run 1k synthetic requests and measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, concurrency behavior.
3. Performance tuning: suggest batching windows, quantization profile, and caching rules.
4. Review & sign-off: present results, present pricing options, and agree on success criteria.

Appendix: useful metrics and thresholds
- p50 / p95 / p99 latencies — target p99 < 500ms for interactive products.
- Cost per 1M tokens — tracked in Console; use Optimize recommendations to reduce cost by 15–40%.

Ownership and contacts

sections.body: This short playbook is designed for sales engineers and account teams engaging financial-services prospects who must evaluate inference economics, operational risk, and security assurances before pilot approval. The goal: give a repeatable, technical narrative and concrete cost/latency scenarios that accelerate pilot-to-contract conversations while surfacing common compliance objections up front.
sections.heading: Executive summary

sections.body:
- Target customers: retail banks, payments platforms, wealth-management SaaS, and insurance analytics teams.

1) Positioning and core messaging (what to say to buyers)
sections.heading: Use case scope

sections.body: "Redwood makes inference economics predictable for regulated financial teams: fast, auditable model serving whether you run in our hosted cloud, on dedicated capacity, or inside your VPC — with clear cost controls and fallbacks to keep customer-facing flows within SLA during peak events."

2) Competitive brief (single-slide summary for buyer decks)

Competitors: In-house self-hosted runtimes, Major cloud vendor managed endpoints, LLM API providers with hosted-only offerings.
sections.heading: Key proof points to cite in meetings

sections.body:

- Explicit economic controls (batching policies, per-route quotas, quantization profiles) not typically exposed by hyperscalers.

3) Pilot architecture and sample runbook (technical audience)
sections.heading: Comparison table (abbreviated)

sections.body: - Client services -> (1) Redwood Edge Gateway (TLS) -> (2) Inference Router -> (3) Model Serving Pool (dedicated GPUs) -> (4) Observability & Audit Log Sink (SIEM/Kafka)

4) Concrete pricing guidance & negotiation levers (playbook for AE/SE)
sections.heading: Runbook (high level)

sections.body:
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): token-based usage billing. Example ballpark: $0.004–$0.012 per 1k prompt tokens depending on model class and concurrency.
- Dedicated (reserved): Monthly committed spend, volume-discount tiers, SLA crediting. Typical commitment: 1–3 months minimum for pilot proofs of concept.

sections.body:
- Pilot credit (one-off $X): covers first N tokens or two-week dedicated capacity.
- Pilot discount: time-boxed discount for first 90 days if committing to reserved capacity within 60 days of pilot close.
- Engineering assurance: guaranteed onboarding window and dedicated SRE hours (billed or included in package depending on tier).

Pricing scenario (example) — fraud scoring workload:
- Workload: 25 requests/s steady, each request 120 prompt tokens + 30 completion tokens, 30% prefix cache hit.
- Effective tokens/s: 25 * (120+30) * (1 - 0.3) = 25 * 150 * 0.7 = 2,625 tokens/s => ~9.45M tokens/hour.
- Hosted cost (example): 9.45M tokens/hr * 24 hr * $0.006 / 1000 = ~$1,361/day.
- With dedicated + batching/cache tuning: expect 30–40% cost reduction.

5) Short case study (anonymized, representative)

Customer: "Global Payments Platform" (anonymized)
Problem: Real-time fraud scoring had unpredictable per-transaction costs and missed SLA targets during peak.

- 37% reduction in per-transaction inference cost.
- 95th percentile latency reduced from 220 ms to 120 ms for real-time scoring path.
- Audit logs integrated into SIEM for proof-of-replay in investigations.

6) Security & compliance FAQ (common prospect questions and short answers)

Q: Can Redwood run entirely inside my VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. We offer VPC deployment and an on-prem package. The private deployment keeps the control plane in your network and integrates with your KMS/HSM for key management.

Q: How long are audit logs retained and can we export them?
A: Logs are retained per the contract; typical pilot retention is 90 days. Export to S3/Kafka or direct SIEM integration is supported and can be included in dedicated/private offers.

Q: Is data used to retrain Redwood models?
A: Customer data is never used to retrain Redwood public models. For hosted services we provide data isolation guarantees and options to opt-out of aggregated telemetry. Private deployments never send customer payloads to Redwood-managed training pipelines.

Q: How do you prove model outputs weren't tampered with?
A: Per-request signed envelopes (HMAC) and immutable audit logs with sequence numbers can be enabled. We also provide deterministic request tracing to map inputs to outputs and system metadata for each inference call.

Q: What are typical SLOs we can expect?

Answer: Present private deployment + KMS/HSM + network peering options. Offer a time-limited on-prem pilot if needed.
Objection: "We need guaranteed costs under heavy load."
Answer: Recommend Dedicated with reserved throughput and pre-defined fallback models. Show pilot runbook demonstrating behavior under replayed peak loads.

sections.body:
Summary:
This compendium is an engineer-first sales reference for pre-sales, solutions engineers, and account teams. It combines: concise positioning, conversation scripts tuned for technical audiences, competitive talking points, three pragmatic pricing scenarios with unit economics, a compact case study narrative suitable for slide inclusion, and a targeted security FAQ for technical and security reviewers. Use the conversation scripts verbatim or adapt as appropriate for the buyer persona.

1) One‑paragraph positioning (lead with what engineers care about)
Redwood Inference is a production-first LLM inference platform that gives platform and ML engineers consistent latency, predictable unit cost, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private) without rebuilding the serving stack. We pair a GPU-optimized runtime (continuous batching, KV cache control, quantization profiles) with a unified control plane for routing, rollouts, and observability so teams hit latency, cost, and reliability targets faster.

2) Quick value bullets for technical audiences (elevator bullets)
- Predictable tail latency at p95/p99 via smart routing and autoscaling policies.
- 20–60% token-cost reductions on typical chat workloads by combining prefix caching and quantization profiles (customer-observed range).
- Single API and rollout model across hosted, dedicated, and private (reduces engineering maintenance).
- First-class observability: token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency heatmaps, and prompt-set regression alerts.

3) Conversation scripts (engineer → engineer)
- Opening (discovery-focused): "Walk me through the end-to-end path from user request to model output in your app — where do you see the most variability in latency or the highest token cost today?"
- Value framing: "If you need predictable p99 latency under load and want to avoid building batching/eviction/caching logic, Redwood gives you the runtime primitives and control plane so your team can focus on product logic, not serving plumbing."
- Cost objection: "Instead of comparing MSRP, let’s model a real workload. Give me your avg tokens per request and expected qps and I’ll show a 3-way comparison (open self-host, other managed provider, Redwood Dedicated) with real unit economics."
- Vendor lock-in concern: "We expose standard model versions, can pin to specific weights, and our routing policies support seamless fallback to compatible model variants. For Private deployments, the control plane can be customer-hosted to reduce control-plane lock-in concerns."

4) Technical demo narrative (5–7 minute walkthrough)
1. Show a quick sample: REST request to Redwood API returning a streaming response.
2. Open Console: highlight per-route latency breakdown and token charge visualization.
3. Explain a rollout: canary 1% traffic -> metrics check -> auto-increment with rollback window.
4. Toggle quantization profile and show simulated cost/latency delta.
5. Show fallbacks: primary model OOMs -> auto-fallback to quantized variant with preserved output schema.

5) Competitive brief (one-paragraph takes + short table)
- MajorCloudAI: Strong on ecosystem integrations and data services; weaker in continuous-batching optimizations and observability granularity. Good fit for customers prioritizing managed MLOps beyond inference.
- ModelServeCo: Focused on self-hosted runtimes; flexible but requires substantial engineering to hit production economics at scale.
- EdgeOps: Excellent at ultra-low-latency on-device inference; less strong for centralized multi-tenant cost optimizations and rollout tooling.

Competitive snapshot (concise):
| Competitor   | Strengths                              | Typical gap vs Redwood                   | When to recommend Redwood |
|--------------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| MajorCloudAI | Broad managed infra & data services    | higher per-token cost, less batching     | When product needs predictable unit economics and observability |
| ModelServeCo  | Self-host control, open runtimes       | heavy engineering lift for autoscaling   | When customer wants production-grade runtime without building it |
| EdgeOps       | On-device latency & offline inference  | limited centralized cost and rollout tooling | When centralized routing/rollouts and cost reductions matter |

6) Pricing guidance + three sample scenarios (numbers are illustrative; always run an EA-specific model with Deal Engineering)
Guiding principles:
- Hosted: pay per token + embeddings. Fastest time-to-value.
- Dedicated: committed monthly capacity with discounted unit cost and guaranteed SLOs.
- Private: platform fee + optional support/maintenance for on-prem/VPC; quoted per-customer.

Scenario A — Search/chat assistant (SaaS, mid-market)
- Assumptions: 10k MAU, 15 qps peak, avg 350 tokens/request, 70% user messages are short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (>=512 tokens).
- Redwood Hosted estimate (monthly): tokens/month = 15 qps * 3600 * 24 * 30 * avg 350 ≈ 13.5B tokens.
- Typical pricing: $0.0006 per generation token (example) -> $8,100/month.
- Benefit callouts: Enable prefix caching reduces gen tokens by ~18% (savings ≈ $1,458/month). If moved to Dedicated with 6-month commit, unit cost drops 30% -> net $5,670/month.

Scenario B — High-throughput reranking (adtech)
- Assumptions: 500 rps during peak, avg 40 tokens/candidate, 5 candidates per request.
- Token volume triple; cost-sensitive.
- Recommendation: Redwood Dedicated with aggressive batching & quantized variants. Expected unit reductions 40–60% vs naive hosted calls.

Scenario C — Regulated enterprise (finance)
- Assumptions: 1M transactions/month, require VPC + KMS + audit logs and 99.9% uptime SLA.
- Pricing: Private deployment: one-time platform fee + annual support + consumption. Typical structure: platform fee (one-time) $125k, annual support 18% of platform fee, per-token at negotiated enterprise rate.
- Value: predictable latency SLOs, encryption with customer-managed keys, and SOC2/ISO-ready evidence.

7) Short case study (one-slide narrative, 3 bullets + results)
Customer: LexiBank (regional bank) — scenario: chatbot + document ingestion for fraud detection triage.
- Challenge: inconsistent tail latency under concurrent batch ingestion and strict data residency requirements.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, implemented KV prefix caching for common prompts, rolled a quantized reranker for low-latency triage.
- Results (90-day): p99 latency improved from 3.2s to 0.9s; token unit cost dropped by 38%; compliance audit passed with zero findings related to key management.

8) Security & compliance FAQ (designed for prospect security reviewers)
Q: What certifications and audits does Redwood maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is in the process of ISO 27001 certification for the control plane. For Private deployments, customers can supply their own evidence packages and we support third-party attestation reviews.

Q: How is customer data protected in transit and at rest?
A: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest data is AES-256 encrypted. For Redwood Hosted, we use provider-managed KMS with the option for customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own key). Private deployments can be configured with HSM-backed key stores.

Q: Where is customer data stored (data residency)?
A: Hosted customer data can be region-pinned to AWS/GCP regions we operate. Dedicated and Private allow explicit region control and on-prem options. We provide data retention and deletion controls per contract.

Q: How are model weights handled and can customers bring their own models?
A: Customers can bring their own model weights; Redwood supports onboarding with validation and performance profiling. Model weights can be stored in customer-controlled stores for Private deployments; for Hosted we provide vetted model hosting and versioning controls.

Q: What controls exist to prevent model drift and regression?
A: Redwood Optimize includes prompt-set based monitoring and regression alerts; teams can configure automatic rollback policies and can pin models to a specific version until manual approval.

Q: Do you support customer-managed audit logs?
A: Yes — we expose detailed audit logs (API keys used, route, token counts, model versions, timestamps). For Private customers we offer a streaming audit log integration to SIEMs.

Q: What is your incident response posture?
A: We have documented IR runbooks, an on-call rotation for SRE, and an SLA-based incident escalation path for Dedicated/Private customers. We provide post-incident RCA and mitigation plans.

9) Common objections + scripted responses
- "Your pricing is higher than X": "Let’s model your actual workload together. We focus on unit economics and SLO guarantees — in many cases we save cost once prefix caching and dedicated capacity are applied."
- "We can self-host cheaper": "Self-hosting shifts cost to time-to-market and ops headcount; we can run a TCO comparison across 12–18 months that includes infra, SRE, and opportunity cost."
- "We don’t want provider lock-in": "We support pinning, model export, and private control plane deployments. We prioritize portable artifacts (model versioning, schemaed outputs) to lower switching cost."

10) Deal close checklist (technical gating items for contract)
- Confirm region and data residency requirements.
- Confirm KMS/HSM needs and key ownership model.
- Agree on SLOs (p95, p99 latency targets) and measurement windows.
- Confirm rollout plan and rollback criteria (canary % schedule).
- Agree on retention windows and log streaming for SIEM.
- Define support SLOs and escalation contacts.

11) Appendix — quick CLI examples and JSON snippets (for engineering reviewers)
- Sample request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1", "input":"Summarize the following...", "stream":true}'

- Sample rollout policy (YAML excerpt):
  policy:
    name: canary-chat-rollout
    steps:
      - percent: 1
        duration: 30m
      - percent: 10
        duration: 1h
      - percent: 50

Use guidance: Always run a workload-based pricing simulation with Deal Engineering before final pricing. Update the token-pricing numbers in the Pricing playbook spreadsheet (Sales Drive) when a customer publishes real workloads.

Document ownership and updates:
Owner: Samira Chen (go-to-market) — update cadence: quarterly or after any material pricing/feature change.

sections.body:
Purpose
Provide a single, sharable sales brief that the field can use for pre-sales conversations with engineering and platform stakeholders. The document bundles messaging, key competitive differentials, sample pricing guidance, a short customer case example, a pilot offer, objection-handling, and a concise security FAQ for prospects.

1) One-line positioning
Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency, measurable unit economics, and a single operational surface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

2) Core value pillars (talking points)
- Performance certainty: predictable p50/p95/p99 tail latency profiles and autoscaling that keeps production SLAs intact.
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles tuned for workload tradeoffs to reduce per-token costs.
- Deployment flexibility: same API/ops experience across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on‑prem) for regulated workloads.
- Reliability & fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallbacks, regional routing, and transparent degraded-mode behaviors.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and prompt-regression alerts.

3) Elevator pitch (30–60s)
"If your team is building LLM features you care about predictable inference economics and disruption-free rollouts. Redwood gives you a single API and console to ship fast on hosted infrastructure, move to reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or run privately behind your network controls — all while lowering per‑token cost through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations, and giving you SLOs and observability you can rely on."

4) Quick technical highlights (for engineering stakeholders)
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized continuous batching, KV cache-aware execution and quantization-friendly kernels.
- Smart routing: policies for latency, cost, region and customer tier; automated fallback to compatible model variants.
- Observability: per-request token timeline, cost attribution (model, compute, I/O), and alerting for quality regressions tied to labeled prompt sets.
- Integrations: Kubernetes-based Dedicated runtime or OCI-compliant on‑prem package; KMS/HSM integrations for keys; SSO and fine-grained RBAC.

5) Competitive brief — concise battlecard
Competitors considered: OpenAI (hosted), Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Self-hosted runtimes (KServe/Replicate), Hybrid vendors.
- Differentiators (what to emphasize):
  - Unified product surface across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (most competitors split these experiences).
  - Production-first telemetry: token-level cost + latency timelines and regression alerts (rare at this granularity).
  - Cost control levers exposed to customers: batching, caching, quantization recommendations and policy-based routing.
  - Enterprise-grade private deployment with optional air-gap and KMS/HSM integration.
- Weaknesses / concessions to acknowledge proactively:
  - We do not have the broadest model catalog compared to general model marketplaces; we focus on verified models and performance profiles.
  - For very small teams wanting a purely managed black-box API, OpenAI may be simpler — but lacks deterministic cost controls and private deployment options at scale.

6) Short battlecard table (talk-to bullets)
Product area | Redwood priority message | Competitive contrast
Hosted latency & SLOs | Predictable p95/p99 tail SLOs and circuit-breaker fallbacks | OpenAI: low friction but less transparent unit economics
Cost & TCO | Active batching/caching and quantization recommendations reduce token cost by up to ~30–60% depending on workload | Bedrock: managed but limited cost optimization controls
Private deployment | Single API + VPC/on‑prem option + KMS/HSM | Self-hosted: control but no unified SaaS dev DX; cloud vendors: private options are fragmented
Observability | Token-level tracing and regression alerts tied to prompt sets | Competitors: per-request logs but not consistent token-level cost attribution

7) Pricing guidance (rules of thumb for reps)
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing. Position conservatively: $0.05–0.40 per 1k input+output tokens depending on model class and size. (Use exact SKU pricing from pricing sheet for quotes.)
- Embeddings: price per 1k vectors; sample guidance: $0.10–0.50 per 1k depending on dimensionality and throughput SLA.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed spend with sliding discounts; typical deals for medium enterprise: $15k–$150k/month depending on GPU class and throughput.
- Private deployment: licensing + support (one-time platform fee + annual support). Typical structure: platform license tier (based on vCPU/GPU capacity) + support SLA and optional deployment engineering.
- Commerce levers for negotiation: minimum commitment length (6/12/24 months), committed throughput (reserve QPS), feature packs (longer retention, advanced observability), professional services (onboarding, private deployment).
- Sample quick TCO framing (for buyer’s infra team):
  - Self-hosting 8x A100 equivalent cluster (incl. infra, infra ops, 24/7 rotations): N months to ROI; approximate monthly infra+ops = $80k–$150k+; Redwood Dedicated can often be more cost-effective when factoring ops and autoscaling.

8) Pilot / proof-of-value offer (standard prescriptive play)
- Typical pilot: 8–12 weeks; goals: validate latency and throughput, measure per-token cost reductions (batching + quant), and trial rollout.
- Standard pilot package: $25k–$50k in hosted credits + engineering concierge + 2 dedicated onboarding sessions. For larger enterprise pilots, propose a time-boxed Dedicated proof with discounted first 3 months.
- Success criteria (agreed at kickoff): p99 latency <= target, per-token cost reduction >= X% vs baseline, integration of telemetry into buyer’s dashboards.

9) Short customer case example (sales-friendly)
Customer: Acme Retail (mid-market, e-commerce personalization)
Problem: Sudden latency spikes and unpredictable inference costs after model upgrade.
Solution: Migrated recommendation inference to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV prefix caching for user sessions, and applied a 4-bit quantization profile for the candidate model.

11) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers reps can use)
Q: Where does customer data live?

Q: How is data encrypted?

A: Yes—Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on‑prem package with an air‑gap option for regulated environments (deployment engineering required).
Q: What compliance certifications do you maintain?
A: SOC 2 Type II in-scope for the hosted control plane; evidence packages available under NDA. We provide artifacts for ISO/Sec assessments during enterprise sales cycles.
Q: Who has access to logs or model outputs?
A: Access is controlled via SSO and RBAC. Audit logs are retained per the contract and can be exported. For the highest assurance customers we enable restricted log access and give them the option to ship logs to their SIEM.
Q: What about incident response and notification?
A: We maintain an incident response playbook, dedicated SE escalation paths for customers with SLAs, and monthly security reviews for large accounts. Full post-incident reports available for incidents affecting customer data.
Q: Can we use our own keys?
A: Yes. KMS/HSM integration supported for Hosted and Dedicated. Private deployments can be configured to use an entirely customer-managed key hierarchy.

12) Sales collateral & assets to attach / point to

payload.page_title: Postmortem Writeup Style Guide and Executive Summary Templates

sections.body:
Purpose
This document defines the standard structure, language guidance, and templates for producing postmortem writeups and short executive summaries at Redwood Inference. Our goal is faster, higher-quality postmortems that surface actionable remediation, respect blameless culture, and provide concise executive-ready summaries suitable for customers and leadership.

Scope
- All incidents that meet the postmortem threshold (see "Incident Triage and Postmortem Thresholds" below)
- Game-day exercises where a formal writeup is required
- Customer-impacting outages and incidents requiring external communication or regulatory evidence

Quick reference: When to write a postmortem
1) Severity P1 or P2 incident that impacts >1% of customers or violates an SLO for >10 minutes.
2) Any incident with regulatory evidence requirements (enterprise customers, data residency, security incidents).
3) Any game day or chaos experiment that requires lessons learned.

1. Required structure of a postmortem page (order matters)
- Title: short, specific, include incident date and primary symptom (e.g., "2026-02-18 — Multi-region KV-cache Eviction Causing 5xx Spike")
- Severity and duration: single line (Severity: P1, Start: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC, End: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC, Duration: 00h00m)
- Executive summary (one paragraph + 3 bullets) — see template below
- Impact summary: number of customers, affected routes, estimated error budget/percentage, and key metrics (e.g., 95th latency, error rate)
- Timeline: ordered, timestamped events (ISO 8601) and short descriptions; include detection, mitigation, and closure events
- Root cause analysis: concise causal chain (not a laundry list) with evidence links (logs, dashboards, traces)
- Mitigations applied during the incident (with timestamps and owners)
- Long-term corrective actions: 90-day plan with owner and target completion date (format: ACTION — OWNER — ETA)
- Verification plan: how we will validate the fix (synthetic tests, load tests, monitoring checks)
- Lessons learned / Preventative measures: short list, prioritized
- Postmortem checklist and artifacts: list of evidence files retained and retention policy
- Distribution list and stakeholder notifications: who was informed and when
- Closure criteria and sign-off: product, SRE, and legal (if required) approval

2. Executive summary template (target length: 3–6 sentences + up to 3 bullets)
- One-line incident description: what happened and when.
- Top-level impact: number of customers or percentage affected, and key metric delta (e.g., "peak error rate 18% (baseline 0.3%)").
- Root cause (one sentence): the proximate failure in plain language.
- Short statement of immediate mitigation and current state.
- Bulleted quick actions: 2–3 highest-priority next steps with owners.

Example executive summary (copyable)
"On 2026-02-18 at 14:02 UTC a multi-region KV-cache eviction path was triggered during a rolling kernel update, causing sustained 5xx errors on text-generation routes for ~72 minutes. Approximately 12% of production requests experienced errors at peak; SLOs for 99th percentile latency and error budget were violated. The proximate cause was a race condition in the cache eviction handler under parallel evacuation; a mis-sized eviction window was exposed by the higher-than-expected GC pressure. Immediate mitigation reverted the kernel update and scaled replicas to drain hot partitions; customer-facing traffic is back to nominal. Short-term actions: 1) Fix eviction race (owner: Sasha) — ETA 2026-03-15; 2) Add synthetic canary for kernel-update path (owner: Infra Team) — ETA 2026-02-28."

3. Blameless language checklist (must be enforced)
- Use facts, not attributions. Replace: "Engineer X deployed a bad patch" with "A patch containing an eviction-window change was deployed during maintenance".
- Avoid "caused by" that implies intent. Use "contributed to" or "exposed".
- Attribute systemic factors (process, tests, monitoring, documentation), not people.
- Include timeline evidence that supports statements.

4. Incident triage and postmortem thresholds (short table in text)
- P1 (complete service outage or major data loss): postmortem required and must be published within 5 business days.
- P2 (partial degradation impacting many customers): postmortem required within 10 business days.
- P3 & below: postmortem encouraged where cross-team learning is likely; product or incident owner can opt-in.

5. Evidence and artifact retention (minimums)
- Full APM trace export for the incident window (retain 90 days)
- Raw logs for implicated services (retain 30 days unless regulatory hold)
- Correlated metrics, synthetic test outputs, and timeline screenshots (retain 180 days)
- Incident bridge recording and decision artifacts (retain 365 days)
- For enterprise customers or regulatory incidents, follow the Incident Evidence Chain runbook for extended retention and legal hold.

6. Timeline guidance (best practice)
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps (UTC).
- Each event row: TIMESTAMP — ROLE — ACTION/OBSERVATION — LINK TO EVIDENCE.
- Distinguish detection vs mitigation events.
- Annotate who made the decision and why (brief rationale).

Sample timeline fragment (text table)
2026-02-18T14:02:12Z — Monitoring — Spike detected: 5xx rate > 10% on /v1/generate — link: grafana/dashboard/err-rate
2026-02-18T14:05:30Z — Oncall — Opened incident bridge (bridge-id) and paged Platform team
2026-02-18T14:12:10Z — Platform — Scoped to kv-eviction logs; identified eviction storms — link: logs/query?id=evict
2026-02-18T14:25:00Z — SRE — Rolled back kernel update in eu-west-1; began draining replicas — link: deploy/rollback/1234

7. Action item format and tracking (required fields)
- Each action must be entered into the action tracker (JIRA) and referenced in the postmortem using JIRA-ID. Required fields in the tracker: Summary, Owner, Risk/Impact, ETA, Acceptance Criteria, Verification Plan.

8. Customer and status-page messaging templates (short, adjustable by severity)
A) P1 public status-page (initial notice)
- Title: "Service disruption affecting text-generation routes — investigating"
- Body: "We are investigating elevated error rates for text-generation routes (v1). Affected customers may experience 5xx errors. Our engineers have opened a bridge and are actively investigating. We will provide an update by [time]."
- Follow-up updates: factual, timestamped, short; avoid technical blame in public messages.

B) P2 customer email (post-incident summary)
- Subject: "Incident summary: Partial degradation impacting inference latency (YYYY-MM-DD)"
- Body: Short executive summary + impact bullets + what we did to resolve + link to full postmortem page + next steps and contact for support.

C) Enterprise sensitive notice (when legal or customer data exposure is suspected)
- Contact: CSM and Legal must be looped immediately using the enterprise incident escalation matrix. Do not send external text until Legal approves.

9. Postmortem workflow and SLAs
- Owner assignment: The incident commander (IC) assigns the postmortem author within 24 hours of incident closure.
- Draft: Author produces a complete draft within the SLA window (5 or 10 business days depending on severity).
- Peer review: Two reviewers (one SRE, one Product) must provide comments within 48 hours.
- Publication: Postmortem page is published and linked from the incident tracker; exec summary is emailed to leadership and attached to the incident.
- Closure: Postmortem is closed only after all action items have owners and an initial verification test is scheduled.

10. Examples: poor vs. improved phrasing
- Poor: "Alice's deploy broke the cache and caused the outage."
- Improved: "A deploy that modified the cache eviction parameters coincided with increased GC pressure; the change was a proximate factor in exposing an eviction race."

11. Game day specific guidance
- If a game day triggers a postmortem requirement, label the page with the game-day tag and include: exercise hypothesis, injected fault, expected outcome, observed outcome, and recommended changes to the runbook.
- Always include a dedicated section "What behaved as expected" to keep the learning balanced.

12. Publishing checklist (confluence-specific quick steps)
1) Create page under /oncall-and-incident-response/YYYY/MM/ with title format above.
2) Paste executive summary at the top and pin the page to the incident tracker.
3) Add labels: postmortem, incident, severity-P1/P2, owner-[team].
4) Attach artifacts (screenshots, recordings) and add evidence links (do not paste large logs inline).
5) Assign reviewers and request comment turn-around of 48 hours.
6) After reviewers sign off, set status to "published" and notify distribution list.

13. Metrics and dashboards to include in every postmortem (minimum)
- Request volume (qps) and error rate time series for implicated endpoints
- 50/95/99/99.9 latency percentiles for inference routes
- Pod/node-level resource utilization (GPU/CPU/memory) for implicated clusters
- Cache hit ratio and eviction counts (if applicable)
- Autoscaler events and queue length

14. Ownership and escalation for postmortem defects
- If a defect spans multiple teams, the service owner nominates the primary assignee; SRE co-owns verification.
- For regressions that impact customers repeatedly, the head of SRE sponsors an incident review (30-day retro) and may escalate to leadership for additional resourcing.

15. Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Who writes the postmortem?
A: The IC assigns the primary author; typically an oncall SRE or the service owner.
Q: Can we redact internal names before publishing externally?
A: Yes — redact PII and internal-only notes. Use the public executive summary for customers.
Q: How do I request extended evidence retention?
A: Follow the Incident Evidence Chain runbook and open a legal hold ticket via the runbook link.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets and pointers
- Export traces for incident window (example: jaeger)
$ jaeger-export --start 2026-02-18T14:00:00Z --end 2026-02-18T15:30:00Z --service inference --output ./traces.json
- Query logs (example using our internal logs service):
$ logs query "service:inference AND status:5xx" --start 2026-02-18T14:00:00Z --end 2026-02-18T15:30:00Z --save evict-logs.ndjson
- Snapshot dashboards: open Grafana panel and click "share -> snapshot"; attach link to postmortem.

Contact and governance
- Postmortem process owner: Marcus Chen (SRE) — process@redwood.com
- Escalation: see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/escalation-lattice-restoration-blueprint-2026 for the escalation matrix and legal contacts.

Revision history
- 2026-01-12: Created (Marcus Chen)
- 2026-02-10: Clarified retention and added game-day guidance (Anika Patel)
- 2026-03-02: Updated review SLAs and added sample CLI snippets (Rohit Singh)

End of document

payload.page_title: Migration Advantage Playbook: Transitioning to Redwood Inference

sections.body:
A field-ready playbook that articulates Redwood's migration value for customers moving off legacy managed endpoints or DIY inference stacks. Includes positioning, competitive differentiators, pricing scenarios, objection handling, a compact pitch flow, migration milestones, and a security FAQ tailored for technical buyers.
Overview
-------
This playbook helps sales, solutions engineering, and customer success teams articulate the commercial and technical value of migrating inference workloads to Redwood Inference. It is focused on enterprise and platform teams evaluating migrations from: (a) third-party managed endpoints with opaque performance, (b) cloud-provider hosted endpoints with limited cost controls, and (c) internal DIY model-serving stacks.

Use cases covered: low-latency chat, high-throughput batch embeddings, multi-tenant customer inference, and regulated PII-sensitive workloads.

Positioning and Core Messages
----------------------------
Lead with outcomes, not features. Use these short, auditionable messages:
- "Reduce per-token inference spend while improving 99th-percentile latency through smart batching and prefix caching."
- "Ship consistent inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with the same API and rollout controls."
- "Move from brittle, ops-heavy DIY stacks to a production-grade runtime with SLAs and predictable economics."
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Unified API for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking — reduces engineering integration time by 40–60% in our customer studies.
- Intelligent batching + KV prefix caching saves 25–60% on tokens for conversational products.
- Dedicated capacity and Private VPC options for regulated customers; HSM/KMS integrations available for secrets.

Competitive Brief (one-page)
--------------------------
Competitors in scope: CloudAI Endpoints (big cloud vendor), ModelServeCo (inference infra vendor), OpenHost (API-first LLM provider).
sections.heading: Supporting bullet points to use in pitch

sections.body:
| Capability | Redwood | CloudAI Endpoints | ModelServeCo | OpenHost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Multi-mode deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) | Yes | Hosted only | Self-host only | Hosted only |
| Predictable per-token economics | Yes (Optimize toolkit) | Limited | Variable (customer ops) | Limited |
| Latency SLOs & fallbacks | SLA + routing & model fallbacks | Region-level only | Customer-managed | Best-effort |
| Prefix/KV caching | Built-in | No | Optional (customer) | No |
| Enterprise integrations (KMS, audit) | Yes | Partial | Depends on deployment | No |
| Typical migration lift | Low to moderate (30–90 days) | Moderate | High (ops + infra) | Low (if compatible) |
sections.heading: Comparative snapshot (simplified)

sections.body:
- Against CloudAI Endpoints: emphasize cost transparency, smarter batching, and multi-deployment consistency.
- Against ModelServeCo: emphasize managed operational burden, integrated SLOs, and Redwood Optimize recommendations so customers don’t need deep infra teams to keep costs in check.
- Against OpenHost: emphasize private deployments, audit controls, and enterprise rollouts with canary/A-B policies.

Pricing and Commercial Guidance
------------------------------
High-level pricing levers to discuss: committed capacity (Dedicated), per-token rates (Hosted), model family premiums, and add-ons (observability retention, compliance).
sections.heading: Competitive talking points

sections.body:
- Conversational AI (customer support bot)
  - 1M messages/month, avg 50 tokens/request, mix of short/medium responses
  - Hosted baseline: 1M * 50 = 50M tokens -> show Hosted per-token price vs Redwood Optimize savings (assume 30% effective token reduction via caching/batching)
  - Dedicated baseline: reserved pool priced to meet 99th-percentile latency at target concurrency; present a 12-month committed cost and a per-request effective cost after queuing and utilization improvements.

- Batch embeddings (analytics pipeline)
  - 5M short documents processed in window -> emphasize throughput guarantees on Dedicated and cost reductions from quantization profiles.
sections.heading: Sample scenario templates (use during discovery)

sections.body:
1. Start with hosted TCO to get customer using the API quickly (free credits / pilot).
2. After pilot, run a 4-week traffic profile assessment to estimate steady-state throughput and cost drivers.
3. Propose Dedicated when projected monthly spend exceeds threshold X (typical: $40k+/month) or latency consistency is required.
4. Offer migration uplift credits for first 3 months of Dedicated to offset integration effort.
sections.heading: Pricing playbook snippets

sections.body:
- "Your committed price is higher than current cloud endpoint spend." -> point to unit economics: predictable per-token after Optimize, reduced ops cost, and improved P99 latency. Provide a migration ROI slide showing 6–18 month breakeven.
- "We prefer to self-host to control costs." -> highlight hidden ops costs (engineering time, incident toil, security burden) and Redwood's Private offering with on-prem appliance.

Pitch Flow (10–12 minute engineering-focused run)
------------------------------------------------
1. Problem framing (2 mins): latency tail, unpredictable costs, and rollouts.
2. Redwood value props (3 mins): runtime optimizations, unified deployments, and observability.
3. Demo checklist (3–4 mins): API call, streaming token latencies, tracing from Console, a quick cost simulation from Optimize.
4. Migration plan & next steps (2 mins): pilot proposal and timelines.

Sales Engineering Playbook: Migration Milestones
------------------------------------------------
Minimum viable migration (30–45 day plan):
1. Pilot kickoff (Week 0): collect sample traffic, define success metrics (P99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy retention). Owner: SE + Customer Eng.
2. Integration (Week 1–2): implement API client, flush KV prefix rules, validate tokenization parity across models. Owner: Customer Eng.
3. Pilot tuning (Week 2–4): enable recommended batching/quantization profiles, run synthetic load tests, observe P99 and throughput. Owner: Runtime Eng + SE.
4. Validation & security review (Week 4–5): SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, audit log sampling. Owner: Security + Customer Eng.
5. Cutover & runbook handoff (Week 5–6): rollback plan, monitoring dashboards, on-call contacts. Owner: Customer Eng + SRE.

KPIs to capture during pilot: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens per second, percent token savings from caching, error rates, cost per 1k tokens.

Case Study Snapshot (compact, anonymized)
-----------------------------------------
Customer: Global travel SaaS (anonymized)
Problem: High-cost conversational engine with frequent P99 spikes and inconsistent embeddings throughput.
Solution: 3-month pilot on Redwood Hosted -> moved to Dedicated (reserved capacity) with prefix caching and optimized quantization.
Outcome: 45% reduction in per-request cost, 2.5x improvement in P99 latency, and successful rollout to production across two regions.
Key quote: "Redwood cut our inference bill almost in half while giving us predictable SLAs for our support bot."

Security FAQ for Technical Prospects (concise)
---------------------------------------------
Q: How does Redwood ensure tenant isolation on Dedicated hosts?
A: Dedicated capacity is deployed as isolated GPU pools with network segmentation, customer-managed VPC peering, and per-tenant key material. Access to model artifacts and KV caches is role-based with audit trails.

Q: Can we run Redwood Private on air-gapped networks?
A: Yes. The Private deployment supports on-prem packaging and an offline installer. We provide documented checklist for secure installs and KMS/HSM integration.

Q: What evidence do you supply for compliance audits?
A: SOC2 Type II report, architecture diagrams, encryption at rest/in transit details, and sample audit logs for ingestion. Additional documentation available under NDA for regulated customers.

Q: How are model weights protected when using Hosted API?
A: Model weights are stored on encrypted volumes with strict IAM controls. For customers with strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
sections.heading: Objection handling (pricing)

sections.body:
- Offer a short security package: architecture review, threat model session, and 30-day security validation during pilot.
- For regulated customers, lead with Private deployment and KMS/HSM integration options.

Collateral & Pitch Assets
------------------------
- One-slide migration ROI calculator (attached in deal kit).
- 6–8 slide engineering pitch deck covering architecture differences and a short demo script.
- Security evidence packet (SOC2 summary, KMS integration guide, audit log samples).
- Migration checklist for SEs (playbook excerpt).

Owners and Contact Paths
-----------------------
- GTM owner: Lead AE (Deal origin) + Solutions Engineering (technical lead).
- SE escalation: se-oncall@redwood.ai (standard) and se-migrations@redwood.ai (migration specialists).
- Security questions: security-engagements@redwood.ai

Related pages
-------------
- link: /confluence/sales-enablement/platform-ops-inference-adoption-playbook-2026 (migration ROI calculators and templates)
- link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/ (Private deployment runbooks)

Appendix: Quick checklist for discovery calls
-------------------------------------------
- Current monthly inference spend and 12-month trend.
- Peak concurrency and desired P99 latency.
- Whether data residency / private hosting is required.
- Existing model families in use (e.g., Llama, Falcon family, LLM-Prod-X).
- Ops team size and preferred level of managed service.

Document history
----------------
- 2026-02-15: Drafted by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-22: Reviewed by Jonah Reed and Mariana López, added pricing scenarios.
- 2026-03-02: Published after SE playtest and security review.
