payload.page_title: Multi-signal prefetch governance and telemetry contract

sections.body:
Summary
This page defines the governance model, telemetry contract, and operational playbook for multi-signal prefetching in the runtime. It standardizes the signals we will accept, the scoring formula, the telemetry schema, dashboard/alert mappings, experimentation requirements, rollout safety gates, and post-rollout validation steps. This doc is meant to be the single source of truth for teams that build or operate prefetch/warmer logic (platform, runtime, operator tools).

Goals
- Reduce cold-start tail latency for interactive LLMs without increasing GPU token-cost by more than 8% at steady state.
- Make prefetch decisions auditable and debuggable with a stable telemetry contract.
- Provide a safe experiment and rollout pathway to tune prefetch behavior per-tenant and per-region.

Scope
Applies to: KV/prefix prefetcher, edge-warmers, region-local cohort prefetching, and operator-triggered warmup scripts. Does NOT cover proactive model weight loading (separate infra).

Definitions
- Signal: any input used to score a candidate for prefetch (history access, tenant SLA, synthetic ranking).
- PrefetchCandidate: a unique key (tenant_id, model_id, prefix_hash).
- PrefetchScore: single numeric score (0-100) computed using the telemetry signals and feature weights.

Approved Signals (canonical names and description)
1) recent_prefix_count_1h — count of requests matching the prefix in the last hour
2) tenant_priority_score — static tenant weight from billing/contract (0-1.0)
3) kv_cache_hit_rate_24h — recent hit-rate for same tenant/model
4) projected_token_savings — approximate tokens saved if cache-hit occurs
5) synthetic_sla_risk — risk signal from synthetic lab (0-1.0)
6) op_manual_inhibit — operator override (boolean)

Scoring formula (canonical)
- PrefetchScore = clamp(0,100, 20*normalize(recent_prefix_count_1h) + 30*tenant_priority_score + 25*normalize(kv_cache_hit_rate_24h) + 15*normalize(projected_token_savings) + 10*(1 - synthetic_sla_risk) - 50*op_manual_inhibit)
- Normalization functions MUST be the canonical helpers in infra-libs/prefetch (v2.1).

Telemetry contract (required fields)
All prefetch decisions MUST emit a structured event to telemetry with the following keys (JSON schema):
| field | type | description | example |
| tenant_id | string | canonical tenant id | t-01234 |
| model_id | string | model version id | llama-13b-vq-2026-11 |
| prefix_hash | string | sha1 of prefix | 3f2a... |
| decision_ts | iso8601 | timestamp of scoring | 2027-02-09T14:22:00Z |
| score | number | computed prefetch score (0-100) | 73.2 |
| signals | map<string,number> | raw normalized signals used in scoring | see example |
| decided_action | enum | {no-op, prefetch-queued, prefetch-executed, inhibit} | prefetch-queued |
| reason | string | human-readable rationale (optional) | high recent_prefix_count |
| operator_run_id | string | optional, if triggered by operator | run-20270201-42 |

Implementation notes
- Event emission must be idempotent for a given (tenant_id, model_id, prefix_hash, decision_ts). Use event deduplication key: <tenant_id>::<model_id>::<prefix_hash>::<minute-ts>.
- Signals must be calculated from the canonical time-windowers (1h,24h) and should not sample from offline backfills during normal scoring.

Dashboard and alert mappings
- Dashboards (must ship before rollout):
  - Prefetch Decisions Overview: timeseries of decisions/second, queued vs executed, mean score distribution (by model tier).
  - Cost Impact Viewer: token-cost delta attributable to prefetch (daily) with tenant breakdown.
  - Prefetch Reliability: event success rate, dedupe rate, and failure reasons.
- Alerts (initial thresholds):
  1) prefetch-error-rate > 1% sustained for 15m -> P3 alert to platform-ops.
  2) cost-delta > +12% across >24h -> P2 alert and rollback candidate.
  3) automated-prefetch-fallbacks > 0.5% -> investigate kernel/IO contention (P2).

Experimentation and rollout checklist (required for all changes to weights, new signals, or new prefetch actor)
1) Write experiment spec: hypothesis, target metric (tail P99 latency for interactive routes), safety metric (token-cost delta), cohorts, duration.
2) Synthetic validation: run the new scoring function in the synthetic lab for at least 48h across representative tenants and sequences.
3) Shadow run in production (no-op decisions logged) for 7 days; gather telemetry and cost projection.
4) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in a non-critical region for 72h; monitor SLOs and cost.
5) Ramp to 25% if canary green for 72h; run retrospective.
6) Full ramp to 100% with automated rollback gates (see safety gates).

Safety gates (automated)
- If cost-delta > +10% sustained 2h => auto-disable prefetcher for the cohort and raise P1.
- If tail latency (P99) for interactive route degrades > 10% vs baseline for 30m => auto-disable and roll back weights.
- If prefetch-error-rate > 5% in 10m window => throttle queue drain and notify platform-ops.

Operator runbook (short)
1) Investigate: open Prefetch Decisions Overview for the region/tenant, filter by operator_run_id or prefix_hash.
2) If cost spike: throttle prefetch queue (CLI: infractl prefetch throttle --tenant t-... --percent 0) and open incident.
3) If latency spike: disable prefetch scoring (infractl prefetch set-mode --mode off) and route tenant to warmset fallback.
4) Postmortem: capture the score distribution, synthetic_sla_risk trend, and tenant_priority changes into the incident doc.

Ownership and SLAs
- Owner: platform-prefetch team (primary), eng-sre (oncall escalation).
- Oncall SLA: P1 response target 15 minutes, P2 2 hours.
- Telemetry retention: decision events retained at full fidelity for 90 days, aggregated rollups for 2 years.

Schema examples
- Signals payload example (JSON string emitted as signals field):
{"recent_prefix_count_1h": 42, "tenant_priority_score": 0.8, "kv_cache_hit_rate_24h": 0.24, "projected_token_savings": 1200, "synthetic_sla_risk": 0.12, "op_manual_inhibit": 0}

FAQs and non-goals
- Q: Can teams add arbitrary signals? A: Not without a governance review. New signals must be registered, have owner, unit tests for normalizers, and pass synthetic lab validation.
- Non-goal: This doc does not specify runtime kernel selection or hardware affinity for executed prefetch tasks. Those remain in eng-serving-runtime docs.

Related artifacts and follow-ups (action items)
1) Create dashboard templates in Grafana: pref-prefetch-overview, cost-impact-viewer (owner: telemetry-bench). Due: 2027-02-20.
2) Add canonical normalizers to infra-libs/prefetch v2.1 (owner: runtime-lib eng). Due: 2027-02-15.
3) Run a company-wide triage tabletop for prefetch-induced cost vs latency tradeoffs (owner: platform-ops). Due: Q2 2027.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets
- Throttle prefetch queue: infractl prefetch throttle --tenant t-01234 --percent 10 --region us-west-2
- Disable scoring (unsafe immediate): infractl prefetch set-mode --mode off --region eu-central-1

Change history
- 2026-11-15: initial draft (Priya Anand).
- 2027-01-05: added synthetic_sla_risk and operator_run_id fields (reviewers: Maria, Ethan).
- 2027-02-10: finalized scoring weights and rollout thresholds after synthetic lab run.

payload.page_title: Batching, Cache Cohesion, and Eviction: Platform Roadmap 2025

sections.body:
Summary:

This roadmap defines the 2025 initiative to unify and harden our request batching, KV/prefix cache cohesion, and eviction policies across the Redwood serving runtime. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by 18–30% for typical multi-tenant workloads, hold 99th-percentile latency SLOs, and provide deterministic operator controls for capacity events and spot/burst usage.

Context and motivation:

- Current state: The serving runtime supports continuous batching and a prefix/KV cache, but batching heuristics, cache sharding, and eviction behaviors are implemented in multiple places and tuned per-service. This causes unpredictable tail latency under mixed-sequence-length workloads and uneven cost distribution between tenants.
- Business drivers: Lower unit cost for hosted inference, clearer tenant billing signals, fewer incidents related to cache thrash and eviction storms, and simpler migration path to Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goals (measurable):

1. Cost: Reduce median per-token GPU cost by 18% and P95 per-token cost by 25% for our top-10 multi-tenant workloads within six months of rollout.
2. Latency: Preserve 99th-percentile latency SLOs for interactive (<300ms target) workloads; maintain P95 <= 120ms where current baseline is <120ms.
3. Observability: Deliver dedicated dashboards and alerting for batch composition, cache hit/miss by prefix, eviction rate, and tenant-level token-cost drift within the first quarter.
4. Operational controls: Implement operator-level throttles, graceful eviction deltas, and fast rollback switches with documented runbooks.

Design principles:

- Workload-aware heuristics: Batching decisions should use historical sequence-length distributions per route/tenant to avoid prefix padding that increases cost.
- Cache cohesion: Shard cache by tenant/route affinity where possible; prefer per-tenant soft quotas over global LRU whenever tenant isolation is required.
- Predictable degradation: Implement staged eviction ramps with telemetry gates to avoid eviction storms that degrade latency across many tenants.
- Observability-first: Every change includes a dashboard, SLI, and a synthetic test in the degradation lab.

Key milestones and timeline (high-level):

- Q1 2025 (Design & prototype):
  - Completion of unified batching API (routing + runtime hints). Owner: runtime team.
  - Prototype tenant-aware cache sharding in staging with synthetic mixes. Owner: platform-ops.
  - Dashboard spec and alert SLI definitions. Owner: observability.

- Q2 2025 (Integration & telemetry):
  - Integrate batching API into router and clients (Python/Go SDKs).
  - Deploy cache-sharding in canary region; collect cohort telemetry.
  - Add eviction ramping control and operator toggle.

- Q3 2025 (Rollout & optimization):
  - Gradual rollout to 50% of traffic with A/B validation and cost/perf comparison.
  - Add automated prefetch hints for frequently repeated prefixes discovered in telemetry.
  - Begin tightening batch composition defaults and hardware kernel routing rules.

- Q4 2025 (Hardening & docs):
  - Complete runbooks, gating tests, and cross-region policy alignment.
  - Publish performance / cost case study and playbook for Dedicated customers.

Success metrics and acceptance criteria:

- Telemetry shows >=18% reduction in median token cost for target workloads at 90% confidence.
- No increase in customer-facing 99th-percentile latency incidents attributable to batching/cache changes during rollout windows.
- Dashboards report stable eviction rates <0.5% of cache size per hour outside scheduled maintenance in steady state.

Operational considerations and runbooks (short):

1) Emergency throttle and rollback

- Trigger conditions: sudden rise in eviction_rate > 2%/hour, P99 latency increase > 30% for >10 minutes, or token-cost drift > 50% vs baseline.
- Operator actions (ordered):
  1. Flip operator toggle: disable tenant-aware sharding (falls back to previous global cache policy).
  2. Scale up short-lived burst capacity (if available) to drain backlog.
  3. Engage model-swap runbook (fallback to cheaper, lower-memory variant) if token-cost spike persists.
  4. Open incident in PagerDuty with labels: cache-eviction, batching, region.

2) Eviction ramping runbook (routine maintenance)

- Purpose: Gradually reduce cache footprint with staged eviction to observe tenant impact.
- Steps:
  1. Schedule maintenance window and enable eviction-ramp=10% in control plane.
  2. Monitor eviction-rate, tenant-miss-rate, and P95 latency for 20 minutes.
  3. If any SLI breach, rollback to previous ramp level and escalate to owners.

Telemetry and dashboards (required panels):

- Batch Composition: histogram of batch sizes, median/95, and per-route breakdown.
- Cache Cohesion: cache-hit-rate by tenant and prefix, per-shard occupancy.
- Eviction Metrics: eviction-rate (per-minute), evicted-keys / second, time-since-last-eviction per shard.
- Cost-KPI: tokens/second vs GPU utilization, per-tenant token cost and drift alert.

Alert matrix (examples):

| Severity | Trigger | Primary on-call | Escalation |
|---------|---------|------------------|------------|
| P1 | P99 latency > SLO for 15m and eviction_rate > 1%/min | Platform oncall | SRE lead, Runtime owner |
| P2 | Eviction rate sustained > 0.5%/min for 30m | Platform oncall | Observability engineer |
| P3 | Tenant token-cost drift > 40% vs baseline for 1h | Product Ops | Billing team |

Dependencies and constraints:

- Runtime kernel routing changes require coordination with infra for GPU kernel upgrades (tracking ticket INFRA-823).
- SDK changes require deprecation plan for older clients (Python SDK v1.x).
- Some customer tenants (enterprise/Private) may require opt-out; we need policy flags and per-customer overrides.

Migration strategy and API contracts:

- New routing header: X-Redwood-Batch-Hint: {"sequence_estimate_ms":120, "affinity_key":"tenant-123"}
- Backwards compatibility: If header missing, runtime uses historical defaults per route.

Open decisions (to be resolved in Q1 design reviews):

- Global LRU vs per-tenant LFU default: which is safer for mixed latency workloads? (Proposed: soft per-tenant quotas with global LFU as fallback.)
- How aggressive should kernel-level batching be for very short sequences (<32 tokens) vs higher throughput?
- Standard for prefix prefetch TTL and staleness tolerances for heavy long-running contexts.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Eviction storms causing cascading latency increases. Mitigation: staged eviction ramps + circuit-breaker that pauses eviction until telemetry stabilizes.
- Risk: Incorrect batch composition reducing model throughput due to excessive padding. Mitigation: telemetry-based composition metrics and automated rollback.
- Risk: Billing confusion for customers during rollout. Mitigation: clear communication, per-customer telemetry, and opt-out flags.

Appendix: Example configuration snippets

- Operator toggle (CLI):

  # Disable tenant shard policy
  redwoodctl config set runtime.cache.sharding.enabled false --region us-west-2

- Example batch hint header (JSON):

  X-Redwood-Batch-Hint: {"sequence_estimate_ms": 110, "affinity_key": "tenant-42"}

- Eviction ramp config (YAML):

  eviction_ramp:
    enabled: true
    target_reduction_percent: 10
    ramp_interval_minutes: 20
    telemetry_gate: "eviction_rate < 0.5%/min and p95_latency <= baseline*1.2"

Next steps and action items (owner -> date):

- Runtime team: finalize batching API spec (Anika Patel) -> 2025-02-14
- Observability: dashboard templates and synthetic tests (Marcus Lee) -> 2025-02-28
- Platform Ops: staging canary and cohort telemetry (Sofia Moreno) -> 2025-03-15
- Product: customer communication plan and opt-out policy (Evan Park) -> 2025-03-01

Notes and references:

- Related playbooks: cache-prefetch-prioritization-for-llm-workloads-2026 (see related_pages).
- Deployed experiments and raw telemetry queries live under telemetry:dashboards/batching-cache-2025.

If you are an owner for any milestone above and need clarification, ping the reviewers or add comments below.

payload.page_title: ML-Assisted Triage and Runbook Automation Roadmap

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This roadmap describes Redwood's plan to introduce ML-assisted operator tooling for triage and runbook automation across the platform-operator surface. The initiative focuses on reducing mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolution (MTTR) for multi-tenant inference degradations by 30% within 12 months while keeping operator cognitive load and false-positive automation under strict guardrails.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- MTTA reduction: target 25% within 6 months, 40% within 12 months for P1/P2 incidents where automation applies.
- MTTR reduction: target 30% within 12 months for incidents with deterministic remediation paths.
- Operator acceptability: >= 85% operator approval for recommended actions in pilot cohort.
- Safety: <= 2% accidental automated rollbacks that require operator revert in pilot group.
- Coverage: ML-assist should meaningfully surface recommendations for at least 50% of high-frequency incident classes (prefix-cache misses, token-burst forensics, GPU preemption spikes).

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Platform operators spend a disproportionate amount of time on repetitive triage tasks: classifying signal combs, matching incidents to known runbooks, filling initial incident context, and executing routine remediation steps (cache drains, model swaps, transient throttles). A combination of structured telemetry, labeled historical incidents, and canonical runbook actions creates an opportunity to apply lightweight ML ranking + deterministic automation to reduce operator work and improve consistency.

Scope
-----
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Triage recommendation model (incident-class ranker) that maps telemetry bundles to the most-likely runbook(s).
- Action suggestion layer (human-in-the-loop) that proposes a ranked list of operator actions with confidence scores.
- Safe automation hooks for fully automated tasks with explicit guardrails (e.g., prefetched cache refresh, model variant swap to a pinned-compatible quantized variant) behind opt-in policies.
- Dashboards & alerting changes to surface recommendations and model health.
sections.heading: Included

sections.body:
- Autonomous state changes for customer-visible tenant throttles without explicit tenant-owner approval.
- Cross-region failovers as first-phase automated actions.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
sections.heading: Excluded

sections.body:
- incident-scorer: a microservice that consumes consolidated telemetry bundles from telemetry-fanout and returns ranked runbooks and action items.
- runbook-store: canonical JSON/YAML runbook repository (already exists) with stable IDs and action primitives.
- operator-assist-ui: Console surface that shows ranked recommendations in the incident panel, allows one-click action execution for approved primitives.
- automation-gateway: performs guarded automation calls with audit logging and reversible checkpoints.
- ml-metrics-exporter: exports training and inference metrics to prometheus/telemetry-fanout and feeds the model-eval pipeline.

Data and model requirements
---------------------------
- Training data: 24 months of labeled incidents, labeled by incident class and remediations (anonymized). Minimum dataset size: 8k incidents across major classes.
- Features: token-latency histograms, KV-prefix-hit ratios, GPU preemption counters, tenant-priority, call-graph fingerprints, recent rollout history.
- Model constraints: concise ranker (<20ms P95 inference), explainability hooks (top contributing signals), and versioned model artifacts stored in model-registry.

SLOs and operational constraints
--------------------------------
- incident-scorer P95 latency <= 25ms for operator UI RPCs.
- automation-gateway audit log retention: 1 year (indexed by runbook ID and tenant).
- Model rollback safety: automatic rollback if recommendation precision on live traffic drops > 10% vs baseline within 24h.
- Canary policy: start with read-only recommendations for first 6 weeks per region; enable human-in-loop action execution in pilot after operator signoff.

Milestones and timeline
-----------------------
sections.heading: Services involved (examples)

sections.body:
- Q1 2026: Discovery & data hygiene
  1) Inventory runbook-store and tag canonical remediations with primitives.
  2) Curate and anonymize incident dataset; define label schema and labeling SOP.
  3) Prototype incident-scorer: baseline TF-IDF + gradient-boosted ranker on vectorized telemetry.
- Q2 2026: MVP & pilot
  1) Deploy incident-scorer in read-only mode hooked into the incident console.
  2) Instrument ml-metrics-exporter and set up model-eval dashboards (precision/recall, operator override rate).
  3) Run 2-week pilot with platform-operator cohort A in us-west-2 region.
- Q3 2026: Human-in-loop execution and limited automation
  1) Launch operator-assist-ui one-click action flow for approved primitives.
  2) Implement automation-gateway with reversible checkpoints and dry-run audit trails.
  3) Measure operator acceptance and false-positive rate; freeze automation primitives list.
- Q4 2026: Broader rollout and SRE integration
  1) Expand pilot to additional regions (eu-central-1) and platform teams.
  2) Integrate model health alerts into platform SLO dashboards; define automatic rollback triggers.
  3) Document runbook changes and authoring guidelines for ML-readability.
- Q1 2027: Optimization and road to scale
  1) Iterate model to incorporate embeddings and lightweight sequence features for higher recall.
  2) Begin safe full-automation experiments for low-blast-radius primitives (non-customer-visible cache refreshes).
  3) Cost/benefit analysis and decision to move to org-wide rollout or refocus.

Implementation playbook (operator-facing)
----------------------------------------
1) Pilot opt-in: Operators must opt-in per region via the Console > Settings > Operator Labs.
2) Review recommendations: For each active incident, incident-scorer will display 3 recommended runbook IDs with confidence and top-3 contributing signals.
3) Execute with confirmation: One-click actions require a confirmation modal for primitives with irreversible effects.
4) Feedback loop: Operators can mark recommendations as useful/not useful; these labels feed the nightly training job.

Example operator CLI (for scripted runbook execution)
-----------------------------------------------------
sections.heading: Quarter-by-quarter plan (high level)

sections.body: redwoodctl incidents recommend --incident-id 2026-IL-42 --region us-west-2
sections.heading: fetch recommendations for incident 2026-IL-42

sections.body:
redwoodctl runbook execute --runbook-id rb-prefetch-refresh-v2 --incident 2026-IL-42 --dry-run=false

Example runbook-store JSON primitive (simplified)
--------------------------------------------------
{
  "runbook_id": "rb-prefetch-refresh-v2",
  "title": "KV prefix prefetch refresh",
  "primitives": ["prefetch_refresh", "verify_kv_hit_increase"],
  "blast_radius": "low",
  "required_approvals": ["operator"],
  "rollback": "prefetch-recover-state"
}

Monitoring and dashboards
-------------------------
- New dashboards:
  - ML Assist: recommendation precision/recall by incident class (per-region)
  - Operator UX: recommendation acceptance rate, median decision latency
  - Automation Safety: audit log volume, automated-action revert rate
- Alerting changes:
  - Create a paged alert (P3) when recommendation precision falls below 60% for 6 consecutive hours in a region.
  - Auto-create a ticket in triage-board when automation-gateway fails > 0.1% of attempts in 1h window.

Data governance and privacy
---------------------------
- Anonymization: no tenant-identifying fields should be present in model training payloads; use tenant-hash with reversible mapping stored in a KMS-protected vault for post-hoc investigation.
- Access controls: model-registry, runbook-store, and automation-gateway require RBAC role: platform-operator, platform-sre, platform-admin.
- Audit trail: all suggested actions and executed automations must be immutable-log entries with executor identity, timestamp, and playback hook.

Experimentation & evaluation
----------------------------
- A/B plan: split incoming incidents into control vs. ML-assist buckets (10/90 for early experiments) by region and tenant cohort.
- Evaluation metrics: precision@1, recall@3 for recommended runbooks, operator override rate, MTTR delta, cost of incorrect automations.
- Nightly retrain: schedule nightly incremental training job that incorporates new operator feedback for the prior 48h window. Full retrain weekly.

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: automation misfires cause customer-visible regressions.
  Mitigation: start with low-blast-radius primitives and implement automatic safety rollback checkpoints and circuit-breaker on a per-primitive basis.
- Risk: model drift on new modes of failure (e.g., novel model variants or hardware changes).
  Mitigation: model-eval monitors and auto-disable on precision drop; maintain a fallback deterministic rule-engine.
- Risk: operator mistrust and low adoption.
  Mitigation: invest in explainability UI, provide manual feedback paths, and mandate read-only mode for first 6 weeks.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Product lead: Claire Nguyen (eng-platform) — roadmap, KPIs, and operator engagement.
- ML lead: Samir Rao (applied-ml-and-evals) — model design, training pipeline, evaluation.
- Infra/Runtime: Jordan Lee (eng-serving-runtime) — latency & runtime constraints, automation gateways.
- Operator liaison: Priya Malhotra (eng-sre) — pilot coordination and operator training.

Acceptance criteria for GA
-------------------------
- Recommendation precision@1 >= 70% across pilot classes and regions.
- Operator acceptance rate >= 50% (meaningful adoption) for non-trivial recommendations.
- No high-severity customer impact incidents caused by automated actions during the 90-day expanded pilot.
- Documentation, runbook-store tagging, and UI flows completed and reviewed.

Next steps (short-term)
-----------------------
1) Kickoff: create a cross-functional task force and schedule weekly 60-minute syncs.
2) Data sprint: label 3,000 high-frequency incidents and publish the labeling SOP by 2026-01-15.
3) Prototype deploy: incident-scorer read-only deploy to us-west-2 by 2026-03-01.

Appendix
-------
- Glossary: "primitive" = smallest executable runbook action (e.g., cache refresh, model swap), "recommendation precision" = fraction of top-1 recommendations that operators judge useful.
- Sample YAML: minimal automation-gateway policy (example)

apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: AutomationPolicy
metadata:
  name: safe-cache-refresh
  region: us-west-2
spec:
  primitives:
    - prefetch_refresh
  approvalsRequired:
    - operator
  maxExecutionsPerHour: 5
  rollbackOnError: true

- Contact: Claire Nguyen (claire@redwood.ai) for product/roadmap questions; Samir Rao for ML questions; Jordan Lee for infra/runtime.

payload.page_title: Operator Autonomy & Economic Signal Roadmap (2029)

sections.body:
Overview

This roadmap defines a 12–18 month program to increase platform operator autonomy while surfacing and acting on economic signals from the runtime. The goal is to reduce operator cognitive load, reclaim 20% of operational time spent on manual capacity adjustments, and improve token-unit marginal cost by 12% across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Why this matters
- Operators currently execute frequent manual interventions during regional surges and quantization rollouts; these interventions are a major source of error and time-to-stable.
- The platform lacks unified economic signals (cost-per-token, burst cost delta) in operator tooling and dashboards, so decisions are conservative and expensive.
- Increasing autonomy reduces MTTI for common degradations and enables predictable capacity scaling that lowers unit economics.

Objectives (measurable)
1. Operator time reclaimed: reduce manual intervention mean time per week from ~8 hours to <=2 hours for routine events.
2. Cost efficiency: lower marginal token cost by >=12% for top-10 tenants through policy-driven routing and prefetch optimization.
3. Alert fidelity: reduce false-positive operator alerts by 40% through telemetry fusion and economic thresholds.
4. Safety: maintain customer-facing SLOs (P99 token latency and error rate) within current bounds during all automated actions.

Key results / success metrics
- Operator MTTR for cache-miss storms: <=25 minutes.
- Percentage of capacity adjustments automated: >=65% for non-PSL (pre-specified level) tenants.
- Cost delta dashboard: visible cost savings of >=12% for at least 50% of tested workloads within 3 months of rollout.
- False alert rate on operator channels: <=10% of alerts after tuning.

Milestones & timeline (high level)
- Q1 2027: Baseline measurement & pilot design. Instrument cost-per-token pipelines, create synthetic workloads for burst economics lab.
- Q2 2027: Economic signal schema and API. Implement cost-synthesis service (service name: cost-synth) and expose signals to operator UIs and runtime-allocator.
- Q3 2027: Autonomy primitives v1. Safe autoscale and prefetch hints enforced by operator-guard rails (runtime-allocator v2, prefetch-service).
- Q4 2027: Canary automation for low-risk tenants. Integrate with rollout DSL and operator-approval queue.
- Q1–Q2 2028: Expanded automation and operator UX improvements. Replace manual change templates with guided automation workflows.
- Q3 2028: Cross-region economic fallback policies and full rollout.

Dependencies
- Telemetry: High-fidelity cost attribution (token attribution across models and routes). Owner: billing-infra.
- Runtime: runtime-allocator changes to accept economic-weighted routing. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Prefetch & KV cache: prefetch-service readiness for operator-safe hints. Owner: eng-platform.
- RBAC & approvals: fine-grained operator roles in console. Owner: eng-platform + security.

Phases & implementation details
Phase 0 — Baseline (Q1 2027)
1. Run cost-sensitivity experiments for 30 representative tenants (open-source workloads + enterprise traces).
2. Create baseline dashboards: cost-per-tenant, cost-per-model-version, cold-cache cost multipliers.
3. Document operator workflows and current manual decision trees.

Phase 1 — Signal & UI (Q2 2027)
1. Implement cost-synth (stateless microservice) that aggregates request traces, token counts, GPU-time, and memory residency to produce per-request cost estimate. API: /v1/cost-signals {tenant_id, model, route, window, cost_est}.
2. Add a new dashboard panel: Operator Economic Lens (operator-dashboard:econ-lens).
3. Roll out read-only visibility to operators and SREs; collect feedback.

Phase 2 — Safe Autonomy Primitives (Q3 2027)
1. Extend runtime-allocator to accept "economic-weight" in placement decisions. Default multiplier = 1.0; can be scaled down for cheap model variants.
2. Implement prefetch-service hooks: hint priority, TTL, and eviction-safeguards.
3. Safety net: all automated actions create operator-tickets with auto-rollback predicates (error_rate > 0.5% OR P99 latency degrade > 10% for 5m).

Phase 3 — Canary & Operator Workflow Automation (Q4 2027)
1. Create an operator-approval queue with progressive automation (manual -> semi-auto -> fully-auto).
2. Integrate rollout DSL to run small-scale economic experiments (cohort size 2–5%) and collect A/B metrics: token-cost, QPS, error-rate.

Phase 4 — Scale & Cross-region Policies (2028)
1. Extend policies to regional-fallbacks and preemptible capacity pools.
2. Add multi-tenant fairness constraints to avoid negative externalities.

Monitoring, dashboards & alerting changes
- New dashboards to create/update:
  - Operator Economic Lens (operator-dashboard:econ-lens): cost-per-token heatmap, model-variant deltas, marginal GPU-minutes per 1k tokens.
  - Automation Safety Console (operator-dashboard:auto-safety): active automations, rollbacks, recent ticketed actions.
  - Prefetch Efficacy (prefetch-metrics): hit-rate change vs. cost delta, eviction churn.
- Alert thresholds and SLO checks to add:
  - Auto-action abort alert: when an automated action triggers rollback predicate (severity P1 if customer SLO violated).
  - Economic regression alert: sustained cost-per-token increase >8% over baseline for 15 minutes.
  - Prefetch-exhaustion alert: tenant prefetch queue >90% capacity for >10 minutes.

Runbook updates required (high priority list)
- operator-autonomy-fallback-runbook (new): how to pause/revoke automation, manual rollback steps, and emergency revert to conservative routing.
- kv-prefix-cache-eviction-troubleshoot (update): add sections on prefetch hint burnout and recommended TTL tuning.
- operator-oncall-cost-blast-response (new): triage steps when automation causes unexpected cost spikes.

Operational SLOs and safety constraints
- Maintain existing customer-facing SLOs: P99 token latency <= 600ms for hosted small models; error-rate <= 0.5% across cohorts.
- Automation safety guard: any automated change must run a 10-minute synthetic smoke test that verifies no SLO regressions before being promoted.

Ownership & stakeholders
- Program lead: Maya R. Chen (eng-platform).
- Runtime changes: Kairos Gomez (eng-serving-runtime).
- Cost pipeline & billing telemetry: Priya Nambiar (billing-infra).
- Operator UX + Console changes: Diego Alvarez (eng-platform UI).
- Security & RBAC: Sara H. Morgan (security).
- SRE validation & oncall playbook: Evan K. Li (eng-sre).

Budget & resource estimate (rough)
| Item                                   | FTE months | One-time infra | Notes                             |
|----------------------------------------|------------|----------------|-----------------------------------|
| cost-synth service                      | 4          | $12k           | instrumentation + storage         |
| runtime-allocator changes               | 6          | $8k            | kernel selection and QA           |
| operator UI and dashboard               | 3          | $5k            | dashboarding and access controls  |
| prefetched cache improvements           | 4          | $10k           | eviction/ttl tuning + experiments |
| Safety & testing harness                | 2          | $6k            | synthetic labs and canary infra   |

Total (approx): 19 FTE-months, $41k infra.

Rollout checklist (pre-canary)
1. Unit & integration tests for cost-synth API.
2. Synthetic workload runbook and baselines captured in dashboards.
3. Operator training session and playbook distribution.
4. RBAC roles for automation toggles verified.
5. Canary cohort selection criteria documented and approved.

Safety, risks & mitigations
- Risk: Automation causes unintended cross-tenant latency regressions.
  - Mitigation: automatic abort predicates + immediate rollback; restrict early automations to low-risk tenants.
- Risk: Cost signal inaccuracies lead to harmful routing changes.
  - Mitigation: conservative confidence intervals; require 2 independent signal windows before action.
- Risk: Operator trust erosion from noisy automations.
  - Mitigation: progressive rollout with human-in-the-loop, clear audit trail in tickets and dashboards.

Post-rollout retrospectives & checkpoints
- 30-day retrospective: operator time metrics, SLO adherence, cost delta analysis.
- 90-day deep dive: fairness impact on multi-tenant workloads, cross-region cost shift analysis.
- Quarterly: evaluate whether automation should be extended to enterprise/dedicated tiers.

Appendices & references

- Related dashboards: operator-dashboard:econ-lens (internal).
- Draft API spec: /api/internal/cost-synth/v1/spec (internal reference).

Action items (next 30 days)

2. Instrument three pilot tenants and publish baseline dashboards.
3. Draft operator-autonomy-fallback-runbook and circulate for review.

payload.page_title: Operational service contracts and capacity roadmap

sections.body:
Overview

This document defines the next 12–18 month operational roadmap for service-level contracts (SLCs) and capacity planning across the Redwood inference platform. It sets concrete SLO targets, capacity assumptions, and rollout phases for Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to align product, SRE, and platform engineering on predictable economics, clear owners, and an executable migration path for high-volume customers.

Audience
- Platform engineering and SRE
- Product managers for Redwood API and Dedicated
- Solutions engineering and customer success

Goals (measurable)
- Define and publish standard SLC templates for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private by Q1 2026.
- Achieve 99.9% availability for Hosted inference endpoints and 99.95% for Dedicated pools (monthly) by Q3 2026.
- Implement capacity-driven billing telemetry to within 5% accuracy of true GPU utilization by Q2 2026.
- Reduce cost-per-token for median generation workloads by 18% via batching and quantization profiles by Q4 2026.

Service contracts and standard SLOs
- Hosted API (public tenants):
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly uptime), exclude scheduled maintenance windows (48h notice).
  - Latency: p95 <= 120ms for short generation requests (<=128 tokens); p95 <= 650ms for up-to-512 tokens.
  - Error budget: 0.1% per month.
  - Throttling policy: soft quotas with 429 responses when sustained > 2x baseline QPS for 2 minutes.
- Dedicated (reserved pools):
  - Availability: 99.95% (monthly) for configured capacity.
  - Latency: p95 <= 80ms for <=128 token requests using pinned model variants.
  - Capacity guarantee: baseline throughput commitments documented in the contract (GPU slot count + burst policy).
- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Availability SLA is negotiated per-customer; default operational playbook assumes 99.5% unless additional SLAs purchased.
  - Support windows and on-call escalation differ; see Customer Private Deployment Guide link in Related Pages.

Ownership and contacts
- SLO/contract template owner: Platform & Product (primary: Marco Hernandez, secondary: Priya Singh).
- Capacity forecasting and billing correlation: Finance + Eng-SRE (lead: Lin Zhao).
- Dedicated onboarding and migration playbook: Eng Private Deployments (lead: Diego Morales).
- Observability and SLI instrumentation: Eng Platform (rt-collector, dashboard owners).

Assumptions for capacity modeling (canonical workload profile)
- Baseline request mix (median customer): 60% short chat messages (avg 40 tokens), 30% medium generations (avg 200 tokens), 10% embedding/rerank calls.
- Average tokens per request: 70 tokens.
- Average GPU throughput: 80 tokens/sec for our production quantized model variant on A100-80GB equivalent under continuous batching.
- Effective throughput after KV-cache sharing and prefix caching: +25% for chat workloads (hot prefixes).
- Operational buffer: 20% headroom for autoscaling and burst capacity.

Capacity formula (example)
- Required GPU slots = ceil( (expected_avg_qps * avg_tokens_per_request) / (tokens_per_gpu_sec * 3600) * safety_factor )
- Example: expected_avg_qps = 120 requests/sec, avg_tokens = 70, tokens_per_gpu_sec = 80 -> base_gpus = ceil((120*70)/(80)) = ceil(105) = 105 GPU-seconds equivalent; apply safety_factor 1.2 -> 126 slots (rounded per pool sizing rules).

Telemetry and billing correlation
- Implement a capacity billing metric that maps request tokens + batching efficiency to GPU-slot-seconds. This metric has to be exportable from runtime (batcher + router) and correlatable with cloud provider GPU usage.
- Key telemetry points: tokens_emitted, batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_variant_id, gpu_util_percent, gpu_slot_seconds_by_pool.
- Target: telemetry pipeline must provide end-to-end reconciliation within 5 business days of invoice start by Q2 2026.

Roadmap & milestones (high level)
1) Q4 2025 – Discovery & templates\   - Finalize SLC templates for Hosted and Dedicated.\   - Run retrospective on 2025 incident impact on capacity (see Retrospective section).
2) Q1 2026 – Instrumentation & billing prototype\   - Ship runtime exports for gpu_slot_seconds_by_pool and tokens_emitted.\   - Start pilot billing reconciliation with 3 enterprise customers.
3) Q2 2026 – SLO publication & automated alerts\   - Publish SLO dashboards and automated error-budget alerts in Grafana / Opsgenie.\   - Integrate billing telemetry into Console cost reports (token-level -> capacity mapping).
4) Q3 2026 – Dedicated guarantees and GA features\   - Ship Dedicated SLA page and contract boilerplate.\   - Improve autoscaler to honor per-tenant burst budget and pre-warm slots.
5) Q4 2026 – Cost optimization wave\   - Roll out quantization profiles per-workload class and validate output-quality regressions.\   - Target 18% unit cost reduction across median workloads.\\nDeployment phases and rollout playbook
- Phase 0 (Prep): Update service descriptor catalog with SLO tags and add contract boilerplate to legal templates.
- Phase 1 (Pilot): Enable telemetry for 3 candidate customers (mix of Hosted/Dedicated) and run two-week soak tests. Document regressions in the regression-triage page.
- Phase 2 (Controlled rollout): Open SLCs to new Dedicated customers with contractual language for capacity and burst. Use canary assignment for autoscaler changes (5% of pools).
- Phase 3 (GA): Publish public SLOs for Hosted, update Console to show per-tenant capacity burn rates and alerts.

Alerting and dashboard requirements
- SLI set (minimum): request_success_rate, p50_latency, p95_latency, p99_latency, tokens_emitted_per_minute, batch_size_avg, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_util_percent, ready_gpu_slots.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - request_success_rate drop below 99.0% for 5m -> P1 page + oncall.
  - p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10m -> P1 page.
  - gpu_util_percent sustained > 92% for 15m and ready_gpu_slots < 10% -> scale-up runbook.
  - batch_size_avg drops below configured baseline for 30m -> investigate router backpressure.
- Dashboards: per-region and per-pool SLO dashboard, per-model performance heatmap, capacity forecast widget (12h/72h/30d).

Runbooks and automation hooks (summary)
- Scale-up runbook (automated):
  1. Check autoscaler logs for failed provisioning events.
  2. Verify cloud provider quota and pre-warm API calls.
  3. If provisioning failed > 3 attempts, trigger manual provisioning escalation to cloud-ops (Escalation matrix id: ENG-PLAT-ESC-02).
- Degradation fallback runbook:
  1. Route new requests to compatible smaller model variant with fallback-rules in router-svc.
  2. Enable prefix-only KV cache mode to reduce memory pressure.
  3. Notify affected customers and mark incident on status page.

Risk matrix and mitigations
- Risk: Overcommit of GPU slots causes sustained saturation -> Mitigation: conservative safety_factor (default 1.2), automated headroom monitors.
- Risk: Inaccurate telemetry mapping leads to billing disputes -> Mitigation: reconciliation pilot, daily reconciliation reports during pilot.
- Risk: Latency regression after quantization -> Mitigation: auto-eval regression harness with guardrail thresholds and rollback rules.

Retrospective summary (2025 incidents & learnings)
- Incident: Nov 2025 cross-region failover resulted in 30% capacity loss in eu-west-1 due to mis-ordered autoscaler dependencies.\- Root cause: autoscaler bootstrap ordering + missing readiness probe for router-svc.\- Actions taken: 1) Added readiness dependency checks for router-svc; 2) Implemented pre-warm policy for hot pools; 3) Added capacity contingency of +15% for cross-region failover.

Operational checklist for new Dedicated customer onboarding
1. Contract & SLC signed with stated baseline GPU slots and burst policy.
2. Pre-provision Dedicated pool in staging and run 48h soak test with customer workload.
3. Enable detailed telemetry exports and share sample reconciliations.\4. Approve go-live via joint runbook rehearsal and rollback plan.

Appendices
- A. Example SLC snippet (contract appendix):
  {
    "modeling": "baseline_throughput": "10k req/min",
    "availability": "99.95%",
    "burst_policy": "2x baseline for up to 10 minutes per hour"
  }
- B. Example CLI to dump pool telemetry (runtime debug):
  ```bash
  # Query pool telemetry for the last hour\  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/pools/$POOL_ID/telemetry?from=-60m\" | jq '.metrics | {tokens_emitted, batch_size_avg, gpu_util_percent}'
  ```

References and related docs
- Platform critical path handbook (service expectations)
- Runtime cost instrumentation and alerting
- Private deployment onboarding playbook

Next steps (action items)
- (Marco) Draft legal SLC appendix and circulate to Priya and Legal by 2026-03-01.
- (Lin) Stand up billing prototype pipeline and first reconciliation dashboard by 2026-04-15.
- (Diego) Prepare Dedicated pilot customer list and schedule onboarding rehearsals by 2026-04-01.

Document history
- 2025-11-12: Created (initial discovery and templates).
- 2026-02-20: Updated with telemetry schema and detailed rollout phases.

Contact
- Primary contact: Marco Hernandez (marco@redwood.ai)
- Slack channel: #platform-capacity

payload.page_title: Operator Telemetry Convergence & Skill Roadmap (2026)

sections.body:
Overview

This roadmap captures a 4-quarter program to converge platform telemetry, reduce noise and cost, standardize operator tooling, and run a phased skill uplift for platform operators. The program is scoped to the Platform Telemetry domain (ingestion, enrichment, dashboards, alerting, synthetic validation) and the Operator Surface (console, runbooks, preflight checks).

Goals

- Consolidate overlapping telemetry pipelines into a single Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) to improve signal quality and lower ingestion costs by 25% by Q1 2027.
- Reduce actionable alert volume by 40% through smarter alert synthesis and SLI reweighting.
- Shorten mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for degradation incidents to < 5 minutes for P1s and < 15 minutes for P2s.
- Certify 80% of operators on the new Operator Skill Path (OSP) by end of program.

Scope and Non-Goals
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Telemetry convergence for LLM serving stacks (batching, kv-cache, scheduler) and platform control plane.
- Dashboard and alert library standardization and ownership handoff.
- Operator training curriculum and certification.
sections.heading: In scope

sections.body:
- Upstream model infra changes (model code or kernels).
- Billing/finance rework beyond token cost dashboards.

Principles

1. One source of truth: pipelines should feed PTH; downstream consumers should not maintain independent ingestion.
2. Signal over noise: prefer composite signals (SLOs, token burn rate, cold-start rate) to single noisy metrics.
3. Operator-first UX: dashboards and runbooks prioritized for oncall efficiency.
4. Iterative rollout with synthetic validation and game-day verification.

High-level Timeline (by quarter)

- Q2 2026 (Discovery & Pilot):
  - Audit existing telemetry owners and catalogs. Deliver telemetry dependency map.
  - Build PTH prototype with ingestion adapters for: serve-metrics, prefixcache-proxy, batching-router, tenant-credit-service.
  - Run two operator game-days using prototype dashboards.

- Q3 2026 (Consolidation & Alert Baseline):
  - Migrate 50% of consumers to PTH.
  - Establish baseline alert volume and false positive rate per SLO.
  - Launch Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) v0: groups related signals and suppresses duplicates.
  - Publish initial Operator Skill Path (OSP) curriculum: Fundamentals, Telemetry Forensics, Escalation Decision Canvas.

- Q4 2026 (Optimization & Training):
  - Complete migration of core serving signals into PTH.
  - Implement cost-signal gating: tiered retention for low-value metrics. Target 18% ingestion reduction this quarter.
  - ASE v1 adds cost-aware ranking and context enrichment hooks for runbooks.
  - Run live cert exams for OSP Level 1.

- Q1 2027 (Stabilize & Handback):
  - SLA bake-in and SLO contract signoffs with customer-success and product.
  - Finalize dashboard library and documented handback to service owners.
  - 80% operator certification target met; program enters steady-state training cadence.

Deliverables and Success Metrics

- Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) deployed in prod (service name: platform-telemetry-hub).
- Dashboard library: 12 canonical dashboards (Latency, Token Cost, Cache Health, Prefetch Cohorts, Batch Efficiency, Tenant Credit Exposure, SLO Burn Overview).
- Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) with configurable grouping and suppression rules.
- Operator Skill Path (OSP) with 3 certification levels and exam artifacts.
- Success metrics: ingestion cost down 25%, actionable alerts down 40%, MTTA < 5m for P1s, operator survey NPS >= +35 after training.

Instrumentation Specification (required metrics)

Operators and service owners must ensure the following metrics are emitted with these labels:

- serve_request_latency_ms{service, model_variant, region, tenant} (histogram)
- token_consumption{tenant, request_type} (counter)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{shard, model_variant} (gauge)
- batch_efficiency{pool_id, seq_len_bucket} (gauge)
- cold_start_rate{instance_type} (counter)
- operator_action_latency{operator_id, action} (timer)

For each metric include resource tags: cluster, AZ, build_sha, deploy_env.

Dashboard & Alerting Standards

- Dashboards must:
  1) Use SLO-centric top-level panel.
  2) Surface correlated cost and latency panels side-by-side.
  3) Include pre-filtered time ranges: 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d.

- Alert thresholds guidance (examples):
  - P1: serving_p99_latency > 1200ms for 3m AND token_consumption rate spike > 3x baseline => pager duty P1.
  - P2: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m => notify oncall with playbook link.
  - Cost alert: token_consumption for a tenant > 5x rolling 7d median and not explained by release tag => create ticket and notify billing-signal channel.

Sample ASE rule (YAML)

code:
  - name: p99-latency-spike-composite
    group_by: [service, region]
    conditions:
      - metric: serve_request_latency_ms_p99
        comparator: '>'
        threshold: 1200
        duration: 180s
      - metric: token_consumption_rate
        comparator: '>'
        threshold: '3 * baseline'
    actions:
      - notify: pd-oncall
      - attach-dashboard: dashboard-id:latency-slo
      - run-suppression: if correlated_cache_drop within 5m

Operator Skill Path (OSP) outline

- Level 0 (Observer): 1 hour course, dashboard walkthrough, intro runbook.
- Level 1 (Responder): 1 day lab, two simulated incidents, written exam.
- Level 2 (Diagnostician): 3 day deep-dive, ownership of a telemetry domain, live proctored incident.

Training and Certification Plan

1. Q3 2026: Publish self-paced modules and host weekly office hours.
2. Q4 2026: Instructor-led labs and first cert run.
3. Q1 2027: Mentorship pairs; require shadowing two P1 incidents for Level 2.
4. Ongoing: Quarterly recertification via 2-hour practical exam.

Rollout & Migration Playbook (high level)

1. Telemetry Audit: maintain a CSV of producers, consumers, and cardinality. (Owner: telemetry-platform)
2. Pilot consumer migration: pick two low-risk consumers (prefetch-lab, shadow-latency) and migrate to PTH.
3. Validation: run synthetic scenarios (cold-cache storm, token-burst) and compare alerts.
4. Bulk migration in waves with operator training scheduled between waves.
5. Handback: update service-level dashboard links and archive old pipelines.

Ownership & RACI (text table)

- Program Lead: Lena Martinez (engineering)
- Telemetry Platform: telemetry-platform (team)
- Operator Training: platform-ops-learning (team)
- Cost & Billing Signals: finance-ops (team)
- ASE Delivery: runtime-observability (team)

Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Loss of legacy signals during migration. Mitigation: Dual-write for 4 weeks and automated reconciliation checks.
- Risk: Operators overwhelmed by retraining. Mitigation: Staggered cohorts and recorded sessions.
- Risk: Cost savings not realized. Mitigation: Quarterly cost reviews and retention tuning.

Game-Day and Validation Recipes

- Cold-Cache Storm: simulate 10x prefix cache miss rate for 30m, verify ASE groups related alerts and does not pageduty for known degradation pattern.
- Token Surge: synthetic tenant emits 10x token rate for 15m; verify cost alert, token attribution traces, and runbook activation.

Post-Implementation Reviews

- Schedule structured retrospectives after each migration wave. Use the following template:
  1) What happened (facts)
  2) What went well
  3) Where we were surprised
  4) Action items with owners and due dates

Related Artifacts and References

- Telemetry dependency map (link to internal Confluence page)
- PTH design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/platform-telemetry-hub-design-2026
- ASE design: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/alert-synthesis-engine-design-2026
- Operator Skill Path curriculum (drive link)

Next steps (this week)

- Run telemetry owner audit; populate the CSV (owner: telemetry-platform).
- Schedule two pilot migrations and two game-days (owner: program lead).
- Draft OSP Level 0 module and solicit SME reviewers (owner: platform-ops-learning).

Contact

For questions or to volunteer as a pilot consumer, ping Lena Martinez (@lena) or the telemetry-platform slack channel (#telemetry-platform).

payload.page_title: Platform operator reskilling and automation roadmap: 2027-2028

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This roadmap describes a 3-phase plan (Pilot, Scale, Stabilize) to reskill platform operators and automate routine oncall/runbook tasks with the twin goals of reducing mean time to remediate (MTTR) for LLM-inference incidents and lowering cognitive load for operators. It combines training sprints, tooling work, and new dashboard/alert standards so that operator skill development and automation reinforce each other.

Scope: eng-platform operator team, platform-operator tooling, dashboards and alerts, runbook templates, training labs, and hiring/onboarding. Not in scope: external customer runbooks, product-facing docs, and proprietary customer remediation flows.

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce average platform MTTR for high-severity LLM inference incidents from current baseline by 30% within 6 months of Phase 2 completion.
- Automate detection + remediation playbooks for the top 5 recurring incident classes (token cost spikes, prefix-cache thrash, GPU OOM, regional latency surge, model-variant fallback misfires).
- Certify 80% of platform operators to Level 2 (can lead a 2-hour incident play) in the new operator certification within 9 months.

Success metrics and KPIs
- MTTR per incident class (minutes) — tracked weekly. Target: -30% by Q3 2028.
- Automated remediation rate (incidents fully resolved by automation) — target >= 40% for Tier-1 incidents.
- Operator certification pass rate (%) and time-to-certification (weeks).
- Oncall saturation index (avg alerts/hour/operator) — target <= 0.6 sustained.

Timeline and phases (high level)
- Phase 0 — Prep (Dec 2026): align stakeholders, inventory runbooks, baseline metrics, and create training curriculum.
- Phase 1 — Pilot (Jan 2027 - Apr 2027): run 6-week skill sprints with 2 pilot teams, build 3 automation prototypes (prefetch validator, prefix cache auto-throttle, automated model swap rollback), and ship dashboard templates.
- Phase 2 — Scale (May 2027 - Nov 2027): roll automation to all regions, integrate automation into runbook runner, certify operators, and add SLI/SLO dashboards.
- Phase 3 — Stabilize (Dec 2027 - Mar 2028): focus on reliability, observability debt, and retrospective-driven improvements; measure impact and determine next roadmap.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- M0 (2026-12): Runbook inventory completed; baseline MTTR collected.
- M1 (2027-04): Pilot automations deployed to staging; first 2 operator sprints completed; dashboard template v1.
- M2 (2027-08): Automated remediation for top-3 incident classes in prod; 50% operator certs.
- M3 (2028-03): SLOs revalidated; MTTR target review; roadmap decision for 2028-2029.

Deliverables per phase
- Phase 1: runbook inventory, 3 automation prototypes (each with unit tests and playbook docs), pilot syllabus, dashboard template v1 (SLO + action links).
- Phase 2: runbook-runner integration, automation policy library, canary playbook for automation, training portal with quizzes and labs, alert tuning guidelines.
- Phase 3: operationalization checklist, SLI heatmap dashboard, post-certification mentoring program, retrospective report.

Ownership and roles (who does what)
- Program Lead: Aisha Raman — roadmap coordination, stakeholder alignment, reporting.
- Automation Lead: Diego Morales — design/implementation of runbook automations and developer API.
- Observability Lead: Lina Chen — dashboards, SLI definitions, alert playbooks.
- Training SME: Marcus Patel — curriculum, labs, certification.
- Platform Ops Squad(s): execute sprints, participate in canaries, provide feedback.

Standards: dashboard and alert contract (short)
- All SLO dashboards must include: SLO line, burn rate widget, recent-degradations list, top-5 contributing traces (by cost/latency), and direct links to the canonical runbook.
- Alerts should be actionable: each alert must map to a runbook ID and include severity, suggested next steps, and automation prerequisite flag.
- Naming convention: alert names use the pattern: PLAT.<component>.<class>.<severity> (e.g., PLAT.kv-cache.thrashing.P1).

Runbook automation design patterns (examples)
1) Safe auto-remediate (prefetch limiter)
- Trigger: sustained prefetch TTL increase > 3x baseline for 3m.
- Action: apply soft throttle policy for the affected tenant cohort; post action add annotation with automation run id.
- Safety gates: dry-run for first 5 occurrences, operator approval if changes affect >15% of tenant traffic.

2) Observability-first rollback (model variant swap)
- Trigger: new model variant rollout causes immediate 95th percentile token latency increase > 40% relative to baseline in canary cohort.
- Action: automated rollback to previous variant; create incident ticket with logs and rerun small synthetic test.
- Safety gates: require canary pass threshold configured in rollout policy.

Procedural checklist (operator-facing)
1) Preflight (before any automation deploy):
   - Verify runbook inventory and link IDs.
   - Ensure metrics consumers configured (token-latency, kv-hit-rate, prefetch-ops).
   - Confirm automated test harness (synthetic scenario runner) is green.
2) Canary rollout (3-step):
   - Alpha: deploy automation in staging with synthetic load.
   - Beta: enable automation in canary region (1% traffic) with operator alerting to monitor.
   - GA: enable in all regions with automatic enablement only if Beta metrics stable for 48h.
3) Post-deploy: review automation runbook logs weekly for 4 weeks and collect operator feedback.

Runbook fragment (example)
- Title: Prefix cache thrash: auto-throttle and rewarm
- Symptoms: erratic cache hit-rate drop (>20pp) and token cost spike > 30% sustained for 5m.
- Steps:
  1) Check cache hit-rate dashboard widget and recent eviction traces.
  2) If automation enabled, review automation run id via: rbxctl runbook-runs show <run-id>
  3) To run manual throttle: rbxctl kv prefetch-throttle --cohort <cohort-id> --scale 0.6
  4) To rewarm: rbxctl kv prefetch-rewarm --cohort <cohort-id> --preset hot-90

Example alert rule (YAML snippet)
- alert: PLAT.prefix-cache.thrashing.P1
  expr: |
    increase(prefix_cache.evictions_total[5m]) / increase(prefix_cache.requests_total[5m]) > 0.20
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: "Prefix cache eviction ratio >20% for 5m"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/prefix-cache-thrash-runbook-2027"

Dashboard widget spec (text table)
- Widget: Prefix Cache Health
  - Metrics: cache_hit_rate_5m, eviction_rate_5m, avg_token_latency_1m
  - Visuals: stacked area for hit/evict, single stat for avg latency, recent automation runs table
  - Action: link to runbook + rbxctl quick actions (throttle, rewarm)

Training & certification plan (outline)
- 6-week operator sprint (weekly cadence):
  - Week 1: systems map & incident taxonomy (lectures + lab).
  - Week 2: observability deep-dive + dashboard building lab.
  - Week 3: automation primitives (rbxctl, runbook-runner) + lab.
  - Week 4: synthetic incident day (chaos + safe remediations).
  - Week 5: exam & curated failure postmortem.
  - Week 6: certification exercise (hands-on incident run).
- Certification levels: Level 1 (familiar), Level 2 (lead incident tabletop), Level 3 (mentor + automation author).

Operator tooling checklist (minimum viable)
- rbxctl v1.8+ with runbook-runner plugin
- runbook-runner deployed to staging and canary
- automation policy store (git-backed) with CI checks
- synthetic scenario runner and lab harness
- centralized automation audit log (immutable for 90d)

Canary and rollback policy (short)
- Canary window: 48h minimum; require stability on SLI set (latency, error-rate, cost) for 48h.
- Immediate rollback triggers: 95p latency regresses by >30% OR error-rate doubles OR automation causes >5% tenant impact.
- Operator override: any operator may flip automation flag to manual with justification logged.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: automation misapplies to the wrong tenant cohort. Mitigation: cohort validation step and soft-run mode before enforcement.
- Risk: operator skill friction. Mitigation: pairing sessions, mentoring, and recorded labs.
- Risk: observability gaps hide regressions. Mitigation: mandatory SLI checklist and telemetry sanity tests during CI.

Retro & measurement cadence
- Weekly: automation runbook health digest and top 5 false positives/negatives.
- Monthly: operator certification progress and MTTR trend review.
- Quarterly: full retrospective with sample incidents and roadmap adjustment.

Appendix (references and examples)
- CLI examples: rbxctl runbook-runner apply --policy policies/prefetch-throttle.yaml
- Example policy (text): name: prefetch-throttle
  conditions: [prefetch_eviction_ratio>0.2]
  action: throttle_cohort
- Links: runbook templates (/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks), dashboard templates (/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts), training portal (internal LMS link).

Next steps (immediate)
1) Approve Phase 1 budget and allocate 2 pilot squads by 2026-12-15.
2) Program Lead to schedule stakeholder kickoff and create Phase 1 Jira epic.
3) Observability Lead to publish dashboard template v1 by 2027-01-10.

- 2027-02-15: updated with Phase 2 scaling milestones and certification targets.

payload.page_title: Cross-team SLO Contracts and Capacity Mediation Guide

sections.body:
Overview

This guide defines a lightweight, actionable contract pattern for cross-team SLOs and a structured mediation procedure for resolving contested capacity requests. It is intended for service owners, product engineers, platform teams, and SREs who must negotiate performance targets and capacity allocations for shared inference services.

Purpose

- Reduce friction when teams request dedicated capacity or priority routing.
- Provide a repeatable decision flow for settling SLOs, error budget allocations, and capacity gating.
- Ensure operational observability and tooling are in place before a binding SLO contract is approved.

Scope
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Redwood-hosted model endpoints and Dedicated GPU pools.
- Any service that consumes shared inference capacity (hosted API tenants, internal batch jobs, and integrations).
Excludes: on-prem private deployments, which follow Customer Private Deployment SLAs but should reuse this template where helpful.

Principles

1) Contracts are explicit and timeboxed: every cross-team SLO agreement is a 90-day contract by default.
2) Error budgets are the control plane: allocation decisions are based on measurable error budget impact, not anecdote.
3) Observability before commitment: no contract is accepted without tracing, latency histograms, token-cost estimates, and load tests.
4) Least privilege for capacity: prefer routing/policy changes over long-lived reserved capacity when possible.

SLO Contract Template (fillable)

- Service name: <service>
- Consumer team: <team>
- Owner: <primary owner email>
- Contract period: <start date> -> <end date> (default 90 days)
- SLO metric: p95 latency for generate endpoint (ms) / availability (%) / correctness metric (pass rate)
- Target: e.g., p95 <= 250ms, availability >= 99.5%
- Error budget: 0.5% over contract period = <allowed minutes>
- Capacity commitment: e.g., 2x c5-gpu-equivalent sustained; burst policy up to 4x for 10 minutes every 6 hours
- Cost allocation: billback model (usage-based) or internal chargeback agreed? <yes/no>
- Observability requirements: span sampling 1%, token breakdown per request, heatmap and SLI dashboard id
- Rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours with rollback on >50% of error budget burn in any 6h window
- Acceptance criteria checklist: load test results, dry-run traces, load spike simulation, security review complete

Capacity Mediation Procedure (step-by-step)

1) Request initiation: consumer files a Contract Request (CR) in the SRE intake tracker with fields from template.
2) Triage (24 hours): SRE triages request, assigns Impact score (Low/Medium/High) using the Impact Matrix below.
3) Data collection (3 business days): run load-test harness with representative prompt sets; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, token cost per request.
4) Draft proposal (SRE + consumer): propose either routing policy change, caching strategy, quantization profile, or reserved capacity. Include cost estimate (USD/mo) and error budget projection.
5) Mediation meeting (if contested): 1-hour session with SRE chair, consumer PO, platform capacity owner, and an arbitration engineer. Decision recorded in CR.
6) Decision and contract signing: approved contracts are written into the SLO registry and scheduled for enforcement.
7) Review checkpoint at 30 and 75 days: verify telemetry and adjust if necessary.

Impact Matrix (summary table)

| Impact | Description | Typical outcome | Decision owner |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Low | Minor SLO change, <1% projected error budget burn | Routing tweak / cache | SRE + consumer |
| Medium | Noticeable cost or capacity shift, 1–5% error budget | Temporary reserved capacity, increased monitoring | Platform + SRE |
| High | >5% error budget or cross-service risk | Formal capacity allocation, possible cost commit | Exec-level approval (SRE Manager + Product) |

Runbook: Immediate Actions for Contract Breach (error budget burn or latency regression)

1) Automated signal fires: SLO alert -> create incident with tag slo-contract:<id>.
2) Triage: SRE oncall evaluates whether to throttle consumer or enable fallback routing.
3) Rapid mitigations (first 15 minutes):
   - Enable model-fallback policy (reduce model size or change quantization profile).
   - Increase batching or activate cached-prefix route.
   - Temporarily throttle non-critical consumer flows via edge policy.
4) Escalation (15–60 minutes):
   - If mitigations fail, convene mediation panel. Consider emergency capacity borrow from less critical tenants.
5) Post-incident: automated evidence collection and contract review meeting within 3 business days.

Tooling and Automation (minimum required integrations)

- SLO Registry: Git-backed YAML stored in /infra/slo-registry (example below). Syncs to the SLO dashboard.
- Load-test harness: infra/bench/inference-load (runbook script provided).
- Capacity simulator: runs predictive cost and error budget burn projections for proposed contract.
- Alerting: PagerDuty escalation path: slo-contract policy -> SRE oncall.
- Telemetry: Prometheus histograms, OTLP traces, per-request token metrics exported to data warehouse.

Example SLO YAML snippet (example only)

service: image-captioning-api
metric: request_latency_ms_p95
target: 250
window_days: 30
error_budget: 0.5
contact: oncall-image-captioning@sre.redwood.com
contract_id: CR-2025-045

Acceptance Checklist (pre-contract)

- [ ] Representative prompt set chosen and signed off
- [ ] Load test (50% projected traffic) completed and results attached
- [ ] Observability dashboards provisioned and shared
- [ ] Fault-injection scenario executed and rollback validated
- [ ] Cost estimate and chargeback model documented

Ownership matrix

- Consumer team: provides prompt set, business SLA, PO signoff.
- SRE: triage, load testing, drafting contract language, enforcement.
- Platform/Capacity team: capacity projection, reserved pool management, cost modeling.
- Security/Compliance: signoff for sensitive data flows.

Mediation templates and evidence to include in the CR

- Load test artifact (JTL / CSV).
- Prometheus query snapshots for p95/p99 before/after.
- Cost projection spreadsheet.
- Heatmap of per-tenant KV cache hit rates.

Governance and review cadence

- Standard contract length: 90 days (exceptions require SRE Manager approval).
- Quarterly review board: all active contracts reviewed for consolidation opportunities.
- Failed contracts: any contract with >30% error budget burn in 30 days moves to the corrective action track.

Appendix: Common Negotiation Patterns

- Prefer "priority routing + cache" over "reserved capacity" for short-lived spikes.
- If predictability trumps cost, reserve capacity but include a dynamic burst clause.
- Use canaries with progressively increasing percent and automatic rollback thresholds tied to error budget burn.

Contacts and escalation

- SRE intake board: sre-intake@redwood.com
- Emergency mediation: mediation-chair@sre.redwood.com
- Platform capacity owner: platform-capacity@redwood.com

Related pages

- See also: Service Capacity Governance handbook, SLO error budget lifecycle guide, and the Capacity Simulator runbook (links in related_pages).

Revision history

- 2025-11-03: Created by Maya Chen.
- 2025-12-18: Added automated mitigation patterns and tooling checklist.
- 2026-02-12: Clarified 30/75 day checkpoints and added acceptance checklist items.

payload.page_title: Operator Empowerment: Decision Canvas and Telemetry Unification Roadmap

sections.body:
Summary:

This roadmap describes a two-phase program to unify operator-facing telemetry, codify an actionable decision canvas, and progressively hand autonomy to platform operators. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-resolution for platform degradations by 35% and decrease high-severity incident recurrence by 50% within 12 months of the rollout baseline.

Context and motivation:
- Over the last two years telemetry streams have proliferated: runtime traces (trace-ingest), token cost signals (cost-telemetry), SLI windows, and operator notes. Operators spend an average of 22 minutes aggregating signals before making remediation decisions.
- Multiple teams (serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-sre) maintain fragmented dashboards. This program will consolidate a canonical operator view, a decision canvas (templated remediation playbooks), and an operator capability growth plan.

Primary objectives:
1. Telemetry Unification: build a fused operator telemetry layer (telemetry-fuse) that ingests traces, SLI time-series, and token/cost signals and exposes a single query surface for operator UIs and automations.
2. Decision Canvas: author a structured, team-wide remediation decision canvas (decision-canvas-service) with priority heuristics, impact estimates, and quick-action runbooks.
3. Operator Empowerment: evolve operator tooling so runbooks become first-class, verifiable assets with automated runbook validation and operator certification pathway.

Scope (in / out):
- In: platform-level incidents affecting multi-tenant inference, token-cost spikes, KV prefix/cache failures, model-variant fallback misfires, and regional capacity shortages.
- Out: product-level feature bugs, customer-specific integration bugs (handled by customer-success), and product roadmap feature development.

Key deliverables and timeline (high level):
| Quarter | Deliverable | Owner | Success metric |
| Q4 2025 | Telemetry ingestion prototype (telemetry-fuse v0) + canonical SLI schema | eng-platform | End-to-end ingest test w/ 3 services; 95% event fidelity |
| Q1 2026 | Decision Canvas MVP + 8 templated runbooks | eng-platform + eng-sre | 60% operator adoption in synthetic drills |
| Q2 2026 | Operator UI + single-pane incident dashboard | eng-platform | 50% reduction in time-to-evidence collection during drills |
| Q3 2026 | Runbook validation pipeline and automated regression tests | eng-platform | Runbook tests included in PRs; 0 false-positive failures in 4-week window |
| Q4 2026 | Operator certification and phased autonomy pilot | eng-sre | 35% faster incident mitigations in pilot cohort |

Detailed milestones and activities:
- Telemetry-fuse (MVP to GA):
  - Define canonical SLI/event schema (fields, cardinality, cost attributes). Owner: telemetry team. Target schema: service, region, tenant_priority, token_delta, slo_window, trace_id, sample_rate.
  - Implement adapters for: trace-ingest, cost-telemetry, slo-synth, prefetch-cohort signals.
  - Provide a PromQL-like query surface + a stable gRPC API for operator tools.
  - Deliver a quiet-day ingestion run to validate fidelity and cost.

- Decision-canvas-service:
  - Create a JSON-based decision grammar that maps signals -> hypotheses -> actions. Example grammar fragment (simplified):

  ```json
  {
    "trigger": {"signal": "token_spike", "threshold": 1.2},
    "hypotheses": ["model-variant-swap", "kv-cache-degradation", "billing-anomaly"],
    "actions": ["invoke-model-swap", "escalate-billing"],
    "playbook_refs": ["runbooks/model-swap-operator-stepby-step"]
  }
  ```

  - Author canonical templated runbooks for: model swap, KV prefix cache reconstitution, regional failover, token-cost surge mitigation, and tenant throttling. Each runbook should include: preconditions, impact estimate, step-by-step actions, automated checks, rollback steps, and postmortem triggers.

- Operator UI and dashboards:
  - Single-pane incident dashboard should present: active hypothesis, supporting evidence, SLO burn chart, token cost timeline, and quick actions (UI-triggered runbook steps).
  - Dashboard rules: SLO burn > 2%/5min, token-cost delta > 15%/15min, tail-latency p99 > 200ms for 5min.

- Runbook validation pipeline:
  - Add unit/integration gates for runbook-side effects. Example CI step: validate-runbook.yaml checks that every automated action has a dry-run mode and a <= 90s verification probe.
  - Example CI snippet:

  ```bash
  # validate runbooks prior to merge
  ./scripts/validate_runbook.sh runbooks/model-swap.yaml
  ```

- Operator certification and autonomy pilot:
  - Certification tracks: visibility, decision-canvas mastery, safe-rollback proficiency. Operators must pass 3 synthetic deception drills and one live supervised incident to be certified.
  - Pilot: 12 certified operators across three shifts; supervised autonomy (operators can run automated runbook steps without SRE approval).

Ownership and roles:
- Eng-Platform (owners): telemetry-fuse, operator-UI, runbook CI integration.
- Eng-SRE (co-owners): runbook definitions, operator drills, certification criteria.
- Serving-Runtime (integrations): adapters for model-swap and KV cache actions.
- Security (advisor): review runbook actions that touch KMS/HSM or customer crypto materials.

Operational constraints and SLOs:
- Telemetry-fuse must maintain 99.9% ingest availability and <3s propagation latency for high-priority signals (region-local).
- Decision-canvas lookups should return within 200ms for operator UI calls.
- Runbook automated actions must include a verifiable dry-run and a human-confirmation step for destructive actions.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Automated runbooks cause unintended cross-tenant impact.
  - Mitigation: Require tenant-scoped checks, and restrict destructive actions to certified operators during pilot. All automated actions run in safe-mode by default.
- Risk: Telemetry-fuse cost growth due to high-cardinality signals.
  - Mitigation: Enforce cardinality caps, sampling rules, and adaptive retention. Provide a cost dashboard and quota alerts.

Rollout procedure (numbered):
1. Prototype telemetry-fuse and run a 2-week ingest-only experiment using 3 non-critical services. Measure cost and fidelity.
2. Ship decision-canvas-service MVP and author 3 core runbooks (model-swap, kv-cache, token-surge).
3. Wire the operator UI to telemetry-fuse and decision-canvas; run tabletop drills with eng-sre.
4. Implement runbook CI validations and require them in runbook PRs.
5. Certify pilot cohort and enable supervised automated actions in a single region.
6. Monitor KPIs for 8 weeks; expand region and scale cohort if KPIs meet thresholds.

KPIs and success criteria (quantitative):
- Mean time to evidence collection reduced from 22m -> <12m in drills.
- Time to mitigation (for pilot cohort) reduced by 35%.
- Runbook false positive activation rate < 2% over 60 days.
- Telemetry ingest cost growth <= 12% while supporting unified queries.

Dependencies and integration checklist:
- trace-ingest (team: telemetry)
- cost-telemetry (team: finance-telemetry)
- slo-synth (team: eng-platform)
- decision-canvas-service API contract (documented in /api/decision-canvas/v1)
- runbook action adapters in serving-runtime: model-swap, kv-cache-drain, tenant-throttle

Testing and validation plan:
- Synthetic drills every 4 weeks with changing hypotheses and seeded noise.
- Chaos-runbook tests to ensure runbooks can be rolled back in <10 minutes.
- Cost gate in CI: any change that increases telemetry ingest cost by >8% must include compensating cardinality or sampling improvements.

Open questions (for review):
- Do we want runbook automation to support scheduled throttles (time-windowed) or only immediate operator-triggered actions?
- Which team will own the long-term SLAs for telemetry-fuse (eng-platform versus telemetry)?
- What guardrails are required before expanding autonomy to customer-facing production changes?

Appendix: sample runbook excerpt (text table form):
| Field | Example |
| Name | model-swap-operator-stepby-step |
| Preconditions | model-variant A p99 > 500ms AND p99 delta vs variant B > 20% |
| Automated checks | validate-variant-compatibility.sh; traffic-slice-sanity-check (<= 5% population) |
| Actions | 1) dry-run model swap; 2) promote variant B; 3) monitor p50/p95/p99 for 15m; 4) rollback if p99 increases > 10% |
| Rollback | human-confirmed rollback via operator UI |

Links and references:
- Decision Canvas API spec: /api/decision-canvas/v1 (internal)
- Runbook CI: git@repo:platform/runbooks
- Operator training curriculum: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026

Next steps (immediate action items):
- [ ] Telemetry team: finalize canonical SLI schema by 2025-11-01.
- [ ] Eng-Platform: create telemetry-fuse prototype board and invite serving-runtime for onboarding by 2025-12-01.
- [ ] Eng-SRE: draft 8 templated runbooks and host the first tabletop on 2026-01-12.

If you are reviewing, please leave feedback in the inline comments or add reviewers to the document. The roadmap will be updated monthly and the next major checkpoint is the Q1 2026 tabletop drill.
