payload.page_title: Postmortem Action Bank and Regression Signal Library

sections.body:
Overview

This page centralizes: 1) a curated, searchable Action Bank of repeatable remediation steps distilled from past postmortems and operator playbooks; and 2) a Regression Signal Library — concrete telemetry rules and detection queries that have historically predicted production-quality regressions for Redwood's LLM inference platform. The purpose is to shorten time-to-remediate and reduce recurrence by making investigator knowledge explicit and actionable.

Scope

- Applies to platform incidents, degradations, and recurring reliability/cost regressions impacting hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Primary audience: platform operators, SREs, runtime engineers, and oncall rotation leads.
- This is an operational reference; do not copy incident narratives here — link to original postmortems instead.

How to use this page

1. When a new postmortem is opened, attach an Action Candidate (see procedure below).
2. If a telemetry alert or dashboard anomaly matches a Regression Signal, mark the incident as a possible regression and follow the triage checklist.
3. Use prioritization matrix to convert Action Candidates into tracked tickets (JIRA/GitHub) and schedule execution windows.

Action Bank (canonical entries)

Format: ID | Short Description | Typical Owner | Time-to-implement | Preconditions | Post-implementation checks

| ID | Description | Owner | ETA | Preconditions | Post-checks |
|-----|-------------|-------:|-----:|-------------|------------:|
| AB-101 | Reduce batch size for 8k seq workloads on tenant-facing pools | runtime-team | 2h | Canary pool available | 99th pct latency drop, token-cost delta measured |
| AB-114 | Evict stale KV-prefix shards and rebuild manifests | platform-operator | 4h | Shard rebuild automation enabled | KV miss-rate back to baseline, SLO stable |
| AB-127 | Roll back last quantized kernel for model-variant v3 | serving-runtime | 1h | Fallback binary staged | Regression tests pass, latency normalized |
| AB-139 | Apply short-lived tenant throttling (soft quota) and notify customer | platform-ops | 30m | Softquota feature enabled | Token burn reduced 40% within window |
| AB-150 | Reconfigure regional egress routing to avoid noisy peering | infra-net | 6h | Alternate route validated | P95 RTT improved, egress cost within budget |

Each Action Bank entry includes: owner (team alias + rotation contact), related runbook links, required access (K8s, infra, model config), rollback steps, and a small test-plan to validate.

Procedure: From Postmortem to Tracked Ticket

1. Author extracts concrete remediation and maps to an AB-ID (or creates a new AB entry).
2. Run a sanity check: estimate tax (ETA, risk, rollback).
3. Assign owner and add to the weekly SRE triage board.
4. Create ticket with label "action-bank" and link to source postmortem.
5. Owner schedules work and updates the Action Bank entry with status: proposed -> in_progress -> complete -> verified.

Prioritization matrix (short)

- High priority: Affects >=1% of tenants or SLO burn > 2% per hour OR security impact.
- Medium priority: Latency/cost regressions with measurable P95/P99 increases impacting internal customers.
- Low priority: Cosmetic alerts, low-frequency anomalies with no SLO impact.

Regression Signal Library (examples and detection recipes)

Goal: provide deterministic queries and thresholds operators can reuse or import into alerting tooling. Each signal maps to an SLI, a query, a baseline window, and suggested cadence.

Signal: Token-to-latency divergence
- SLI: per-tenant tokens / P95_latency_ms by model-family
- Detection query (example PromQL-like):
  avg_over_time(rate(tokens_total{model_family=~"(gpt.*|redwood.*)"}[5m]) / avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, latency_bucket{route!="internal"}[5m]))[15m:1m]) > 1.5 * baseline_last_7d
- Baseline: rolling 7-day median
- Typical action: AB-101 or scale dedicated pool for tenant cohort

Signal: KV miss-rate spike with prefix churn
- SLI: kv_cache_hit_ratio by shard
- Detection rule (SQL for analytics):
  SELECT shard, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY miss_rate) AS p95_miss
  FROM prefixes_telemetry
  WHERE time >= now() - interval '10 minutes'
  GROUP BY shard
  HAVING p95_miss > 0.08;
- Typical action: AB-114, and run cache-consistency recheck

Signal: Model-variant quality regression (eval micro-regression)
- SLI: eval_accuracy_delta_by_promptset
- Detection recipe: scheduled nightly evaluation comparing latest candidate to baseline model using anchor prompts; if delta < -0.5% on critical promptset, create regression ticket automatically.
- Typical action: AB-127 + rollback cadence

Signal: Cost spike correlated with small increase in latency (indicator of inefficient batching)
- SLI: cost_per_token_daily AND p95_latency
- Detection: correlate daily_cost anomalies with 95th-percentile latencies by tenant; run an automated affinity clustering to surface probable model-config changes.
- Typical action: AB-139 + operator notification

Oncall triage checklist (short)

1. Confirm SLI breach and match to a Regression Signal.
2. Identify affected tenants/regions and customer-facing impact.
3. Select immediate mitigations (from Action Bank).
4. Raise Incident/SEV ticket and assign owner; reference AB-ID(s).
5. If mitigation uses a migration/rollback, run preflight checklist.
6. After mitigation, schedule deeper root-cause analysis and map upstream follow-ups to owners.

Automation and integration patterns

- Alerting: signals should be published as low-noise, actionable alerts with links to AB entries and runbooks (alert body MUST contain AB-ID suggestions).
- Ticket creation: novel regression rules can auto-open "regression-candidate" tickets with a triage checklist template.
- Dashboarding: maintain an "Action Bank adoption" dashboard that shows actions open/closed over time and recurrence rate for AB-IDs.

Operational metrics to track for this program

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Owner |
|-------|--------|------------|------|
| Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for AB actions | < 6 hours for high-priority | incident tracker + AB status | eng-platform |
| Fraction of incidents with AB mapping | > 80% | postmortem tagging | eng-platform |
| Regression repeat rate for mapped AB-IDs | < 10% within 90 days | incident deduping | runtime-team |
| Automated detection precision | > 60% precision for top-10 signals | signal-to-incident mapping | observability-team |

Governance and cadence

- Weekly: Triage board reviews proposed AB actions and assigns owners.
- Monthly: Signal hygiene sweep — remove stale rules, tune thresholds with current baselines.
- Quarterly: Action Bank cleanup — retire AB-IDs with no usage, and publish a one-page summary to the platform forum.

Ownership matrix

- eng-platform: program owner, triage chair, backlog governance
- serving-runtime: kernel/quantization action owners (AB-127 family)
- platform-operator: operational playbooks and AB execution (AB-114 family)
- infra-net: routing and peering fixes (AB-150 family)
- observability: detection rules and oncall alert integration

Appendix A: Postmortem -> AB extraction template (to copy into postmortem)

1. Symptom (one line)
2. Concrete remediation (one actionable sentence) -> Proposed AB-ID or new AB entry
3. Owner (team + rotation contact)
4. Risk and rollback plan
5. Test plan and verification criteria
6. Link to runbook(s) and dashboards

Appendix B: Example alert body (copyable)

ALERT: Token-to-latency divergence detected (AB-101 suggested)
- Signal: token_latency_divergence
- Affected: region-us-west-2, tenants: [tenanta, tenantb]
- Suggested actions: AB-101 (reduce batch size), AB-139 (soft throttle)
- Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/token-latency-divergence
- Postmortem template link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/template

Appendix C: Links and references

- Runbook: platform-incident-statemachine-catalog-and-decision-runbook (see related pages)
- Triage board: https://redwood.internal/boards/platform-action-bank
- Automation repo for signal rules: git@github.com:redwood/observability/signal-library.git
- Export/import tooling: signal rules are stored as YAML in the repo and referenced by alertmanager.

Contact and feedback

For feedback or to nominate an AB entry for addition, open PR against the observability repo or ping #platform-action-bank Slack channel.

Last verified: 2026-11-20 by Maya Chen

payload.page_title: telemetry-aggregation-pipeline-rearchitecture-retrospective-2025

sections.body: This retrospective documents the design, rollout, and outcomes of the Telemetry Aggregation Pipeline rearchitecture (internal codename: TARP). The project converted our previous per-service push model into a region-aware, event-driven aggregation layer to reduce cardinality, eliminate redundant ingestion, and align telemetry delivery with SLOs for metric/trace/trace-event availability across regions.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Prior state: each service pushed metrics directly into region-local collectors. This caused noisy cardinality growth, duplicate events for multi-region services, wide variance in ingestion latency (P50=5s, P95=18s, P99=90s), and frequent alert flapping when cross-region clients hit inconsistent views.
- Goals: reduce ingest cost by 35% via deduplication + batching, stabilize metric delivery so 99.9% of important telemetry arrives within 60s, simplify downstream dashboards by providing a single canonical time-series per logical entity, and provide a safe migration path with rollbacks.
sections.heading: Background and motivation

sections.body:
- Introduced three new components: ingest-router (region-aware front door), event-aggregator (de-duplicate + continuous-batch), and canonical-sharder (assigns logical entity -> canonical shard).
- Kept existing telemetry-collector as a thin adapter so clients required minimal change (SDK version 2.1.0).
- Added per-tenant sampling policies + prefix-based metric normalization rules (config stored in config-service /telemetry/policies).
sections.heading: High-level architecture changes made

sections.body:
1) 2024-07-02: Design review (architecture ADR-2024-11-TARP) approved.
2) 2024-08-10: Prototype of event-aggregator + local synthetic load tests (k8s namespaces: tarp-dev).
3) 2024-09-15: Canary deploy to us-west-2 (10% of traffic for non-critical namespaces).
4) 2024-10-07: Expanded canary to multi-region (us-west-2 + eu-central-1) with feature flag gating.
5) 2024-10-28: Production rollout completed for non-enterprise tenants.
6) 2024-11-12: Enterprise tenant phased rollouts started with Dedicated-only paths.
7) 2024-12-01: Full production: cross-region dedupe and canonical metrics enabled globally.
sections.heading: Key timeline (major milestones)

sections.body:
| Metric | Baseline (Aug 2024) | After rollout (Dec 2024) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ingest cost (monthly) | $320,000 | $198,000 | -38% |
| Cardinality (unique metrics/day) | 9.4M | 5.6M | -40% |
| Metric delivery P95 (s) | 18 | 9 | -50% |
| Missing metric alerts per week (global) | 24 | 6 | -75% |
| Dashboard mismatch incidents (per quarter) | 7 | 1 | -86% |
sections.heading: Quantitative outcomes (pre vs post)

sections.body:
- SDK compatibility strategy: allowing telemetry-collector as thin adapter reduced required client changes to environment variables (SDK upgrade adoption: 88% within 6 weeks).
- Canary phasing by tenant-type (non-critical -> multi-region -> enterprise) avoided large-scale regressions and allowed targeted rollback for a handful of enterprise integrations with custom scraping behavior.
- Operator tooling: we developed a fast verification dashboard that correlated ingest rates, dedupe counts, and canonical shard reassignments that was invaluable during rollout.
- Cost and SLO improvements measured above (notable cost savings were recognized in finance runbook and monthly invoices).
sections.heading: What went well

sections.body:
- Unexpected dedupe churn: During the multi-region canary, the canonical-sharder reassigned ~0.7% of entities more than once due to clock skew and inconsistent entity tags. Root cause: incomplete tag normalization rules and a missing TTL on pre-shard claims.
- Migration warnings overload: Operators experienced alert storms from validation rules that assumed pre-rollout cardinality. Root cause: alert thresholds were not parameterized per-phase and used absolute counts rather than rate-of-change.
- Enterprise scraping edge cases: Several enterprise customers used custom scraping endpoints that emitted ephemeral labels leading to high churn. Root cause: lack of integration tests that represent customer scraping diversity.
sections.heading: What didn't go well / Root causes

sections.body:
- Fast patch: added a 60s soft-claim TTL and strengthened namespace->entity tag normalization in canonical-sharder (rollout 2024-10-12).
- Alert tuning: implemented phased alert multipliers (factor=0.5 during canary) and switched to rate-based derivations for validation alarms.
- Enterprise remediation: created an enterprise-scrape-compatibility guide and a compatibility testing harness (tarp-enterprise-testkit) for solutions engineers.

Operator runbook (short version) — for incidents where metric delivery degradation is detected:

1) Verify scope: open the TARP verification dashboard and check ingest-router throughput, aggregator dedupe-rate, and canonical-sharder reassignment rate. Note region(s) and tenants impacted.
2) If dedupe-rate spikes > 5x baseline or shard reassignments > 1%/5m, flip feature flag: tarp-aggregation = disabled for impacted region.
3) If ingestion falls to < 70% of baseline: scale ingest-router replicas (kubectl -n telemetry scale deploy/ingest-router --replicas=<n>) and check backpressure metrics on Kafka topic tarp-events.
4) For enterprise tenants reporting missing metrics, enable per-tenant bypass (config-service /telemetry/skip-aggregation/<tenant-id>) and notify solutions engineering.
5) After stabilization, run a backfill job (backfill-aggregates --start=<iso> --end=<iso>) and verify canonical counts match expected totals.
sections.heading: Mitigations taken during rollout

sections.body:
- Notify stakeholders (oncall, product, solutions engineering, customer success).
- Flip tarp-global-mode = passive in feature-flagging service.
- Recreate per-region direct-forwarding routes by toggling ingest-router -> collector route to direct.
- Ensure telemetry-collector adapters are set to pre-aggregation mode (env TELEMETRY_ADAPTER_MODE=legacy).
- Monitor for 2x ingress and potential cost surge; request temporary budget approval from finance if expected.

Lessons learned and recommended standards to adopt company-wide:

- Phased alerting: alerts that run during rollout must be parameterized by phase (canary / phased-rollout / GA) and derive thresholds via both absolute and rate-of-change signals.
- Claim/lease semantics: any component that 'claims' canonical ownership must use soft TTLs and Versioned-Claims to avoid oscillation during partial network partitions.
- Tenant integration testing: expand integration test matrix in CI to include enterprise scrape diversity (custom labels, ephemeral endpoints, multi-scrape intervals).
- Cost telemetry: shipping monthly cost deltas to finance early enables quicker business sign-off and reduces surprise escalations.
- Operator dashboards: create a single verification dashboard per major rollout that shows pre/post deltas and a small checklist for safe promotion.
sections.heading: Rollback checklist (if a full rollback is required)

sections.body:
- [P0] Tag normalization rulesheet (owner: Priya Kapoor) — due 2025-02-01.
- [P0] Implement Versioned-Claims for canonical-sharder (owner: Carlos Mendes) — due 2025-03-01.
- [P1] Add enterprise-testkit to CI (owner: Evan Liu) — due 2025-02-15.
- [P1] Alert parameterization library (owner: Diego Santos) — due 2025-01-30.
- [P2] Finance integration for monthly cost deltas (owner: Finance-API team) — due 2025-04-01.

Appendix: Useful commands and links:

- Quick verification dashboard: /dashboards/tarp/verification (internal link)
- Canary feature flag path: /flags/tarp-aggregation (use rollout tags: canary,multi-region,enterprise,ga)
- Backfill job: ./ops/backfill-aggregates --help
- Test clusters: tarp-dev (k8s), tarp-staging (k8s), tarp-prod (k8s)
- Relevant ADR: ADR-2024-11-TARP (link internal)
sections.heading: Action items (owners and dates)

sections.body: The Telemetry Aggregation Pipeline rearchitecture delivered substantial cost and SLO improvements while revealing important operational and testing gaps—particularly around claim semantics and enterprise scraping diversity. The mitigations and action items above are prioritized to reduce future migration risk and to codify safe rollout practices for future platform-wide changes.
sections.heading: Conclusion

sections.body:
- Project lead: Asha Patel (Platform Observability)
- Engineering owners: Carlos Mendes, Evan Liu
- Product & Delivery contact: Maya Thompson
- SRE verification: Diego Santos

If you have questions or need access to the verification dashboard or canaries, ping #platform-ops or open a ticket with the Observability team.

payload.page_title: Operator Handbook Synthesis from Chaos Week — Compact Action Playbook

sections.body:
Summary

This retrospective distills the operational learnings from 'Chaos Week 2026' into a compact, prioritized set of handbook changes, decision heuristics, and runnable playbooks. The goal is to convert observed failure modes and operator improvisations into durable procedures so that future operators can resolve similar incidents reliably and faster.

Background

In 2026-01-08 through 2026-01-10 we ran a focused chaos campaign across platform services (batching layer, kv-prefix cache, tenant router, and model-variant fallback). The exercise intentionally injected degraded network conditions, slow kernels, and simulated preemption. Operators exercised their existing handbooks and created ad-hoc mitigations. This document synthesizes what worked, what failed, and the minimal actionable changes to the operator handbook and observability surface.

Scope and intended readers

- Primary: Platform operators and oncall engineers owning runtime/allocator/traffic-shaping.
- Secondary: Platform product managers, SRE leads, and devs who author runbooks.

Key findings (top-level)

1) Operators often relied on a single mental model for eviction vs. degrade: prefer a two-stage decision canvas (evict vs degrade).
2) Alert context lacked token-cost and tenant-priority signals; operators spent 12–18 minutes per incident assembling them manually.
3) Cross-service fallback logic (model swap -> tenant fallback) had unclear owner and rollback instructions.
4) Several ad-hoc CLI commands used during the exercise are safe and should be formalized; two were unsafe and removed.
5) Runbook prose was too verbose for high-severity incidents; a one-page "Incident Action Card" per runbook speeds triage.

Concrete metrics observed

- Median time-to-first-action (operator) during Chaos Week: 9m 40s (target: <5m).
- Median resolution time for degraded kv-prefix cache scenarios: 43m (target: <30m).
- Operators queried token-cost and tenant-priority signals manually in 78% of incidents.
- 3 unsafe mitigation commands were executed once (no production impact but high risk).

Synthesis: Where to change the handbook now (top 5 prioritized changes)

1) Add a standardized Incident Action Card (IAC) template to every runbook.
   - What it is: a single page checklist with the first 6 diagnostic steps, immediate mitigations, and safe-rollbacks.
   - When to use: SEV2/SEV1 for runtime services.

2) Introduce a Two-Stage Decision Canvas for eviction vs degrade.
   - Stage A: Fast eligibility checks (is tenant critical, SLO burn rate, warmset heat).
   - Stage B: Operator mitigation choices (soft-evict, reduce tokens per request, model-variant swap).

3) Create a small telemetry bundle that surfaces token-cost and tenant-priority in alert context.
   - Implementation: enrich alert payloads with three fields: tenant_priority (high|medium|low), recent_1m_token_rate, 1h_budget_spend_pct.

4) Formalize and publish safe CLI primitives and deprecate unsafe ones.

5) Define ownership and rollback clauses for model-variant fallback logic across runtime and routing teams.

Incident Action Card (IAC) — template (to be added to runbooks)

- Title: [Service] — IAC — [Scenario]
- Severity: [SEV1|SEV2]
- Immediate diagnosis (first 6 checks, < 4 minutes):
  1) Confirm alert signature and scope: alert_id, affected_regions, affected_models.
  2) Query operator context panel: tenant_priority, token_rate_1m, slot_utilization.
  3) Run healthcheck summary: curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/health/service/[svc] | jq '.summary'.
  4) Verify KV cache hit ratio and prefix shard errors: kvestats --service [svc] --window 5m.
  5) Check kernel wait and GPU utilization: gpu-proc top --json | jq '[.gpus[] | {util, mem}]'.
  6) Capture and pin the current model-variant routing snapshot: rroute snapshot create --note \"chaos-injection\"
- Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  a) Set temporary tenant throttle: rquota set --tenant $TENANT --rate 0.5 --expire 15m  # safe throttle
  b) Engage soft-eviction on warmset: opsctl warmset evict --shard $SHARD --fraction 0.2
  c) If token-cost spike > 250% and tenant_priority=low, apply auto-buydown credit: billing-adm credit-apply --tenant $TENANT --amt 0.
- Safe rollback steps: reverse mitigations in reverse order. Document timestamps to audit.

Runbook change table (summary of edits)

| Runbook | Edit type | Owner | ETA |
|---------|-----------|-------|-----|
| kv-prefix-cache | add IAC + safe CLI list + telemetry enrichment | runtime-team | 2026-03-15 |
| tenant-router | add Decision Canvas + rollback clauses | platform-routing | 2026-03-22 |
| model-variant-fallback | clarify cross-team ownership + canned rollback | serving-runtime | 2026-03-10 |
| operator-oncall-playbook | shorten SEV path to 1 page + training checklist | eng-sre | 2026-03-08 |

(Above table is a compact summary; full change diffs are linked in related_pages.)

Example alert enrichment payload (pseudo-JSON)

{ "alert_id": "ALRT-2026-00073", "service": "kv-prefix-cache", "region": "us-west-2", "context": { "tenant_priority": "low", "recent_1m_token_rate": "4500/tokens", "1h_budget_spend_pct": "68%" } }

Note: keep enrichment payload under 2KB to avoid alerting pipeline amplification.

Operator heuristics (codified)

- Heuristic 1: If tenant_priority == high AND 1h_budget_spend_pct < 85% AND kv_hit_ratio > 40% then prefer graceful degrade (reduce token window) over eviction.
- Heuristic 2: If kernel wait > 80% and GPU memory pressure > 90% then trigger model-variant swap to a quantized variant (preview models allowed only in dedicated namespaces).
- Heuristic 3: If multiple tenants show simultaneous SLO burn with correlated token spikes, prioritize by tenant_priority and apply soft-throttles starting from low priority tenants.

Safe CLI primitives (approved)

1) rquota set --tenant <id> --rate <float> --expire <duration>  # throttles tenant traffic safely (idempotent)
2) opsctl warmset evict --shard <id> --fraction <0.0-1.0>  # controlled warmset eviction
3) rroute snapshot create --note <string>  # capture routing state (write-only snapshot)
4) backend-rollout pause --component <comp> --reason <string>  # soft pause for automated rollouts

Unsafe commands observed (deprecated)

- runtime-force-evict --shard X --all  # performs immediate full shard eviction, caused cascading cold starts in the exercise. Remove from operator path and place in engineering-only tooling.

Training and verification plan

1) Update runbooks and IAC templates (owners listed in table) — owners must submit PR with edits by ETA.
2) Publish a 60-minute microtraining for operators covering: Decision Canvas, IAC usage, and approved CLI list (target date: 2026-03-29).
3) Run a focused tabletop in the next gameday (April 2026) with 3 injected scenarios derived from Chaos Week. Each scenario must include a measurable median time-to-first-action target.

Roadmap alignment and follow-ups (how this maps to platform roadmap)

- Q2 2026: Telemetry enrichment rollout and alert-payload schema v1 (owner: observability).
- Q2 2026: Runbook consolidation sprint (owner: eng-platform runbook guild).
- Q3 2026: Automation for frequent safe mitigations (owner: eng-platform/operator-automation).

Action items (owner/accountability)

1) runtime-team: Draft runbook IAC and safe CLI list PR — due 2026-03-15. (owner: Priya Menon)
2) observability: Implement alert enrichment fields and test with synthetic alerts — due 2026-04-05. (owner: Elena Rivera)
3) platform-routing: Add Decision Canvas and rollback clauses to tenant-router runbook — due 2026-03-22. (owner: Jamal Ortiz)
4) eng-sre: Schedule and run 60-minute microtraining and April tabletop — schedule by 2026-03-20. (owner: Marcus Chen)
5) security: Review CLI primitives for privilege hardening — due 2026-03-10. (owner: Serena Gupta)

Appendix A — Short cookbook for triage (command snippets)

1) Quick health summary (single-liner):
   curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/health/service/kv-prefix-cache | jq '.summary // \"unknown\"'
2) Capture routing snapshot:
   rroute snapshot create --note \"triage-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)\"
3) Apply a safe throttle to tenant 42 for 10 minutes at 0.4 RPS:
   rquota set --tenant 42 --rate 0.4 --expire 10m

Appendix B — Postmortem checklist for converting ad-hoc fixes into handbook text

1) Was the action repeatable and low-risk? If yes, add as a Safe CLI primitive.
2) Did the action require cross-team approvals? If yes, document the ownership and rollback clause.
3) Can the action be automated? If yes, create a follow-up ticket to build and test automation.
4) Add IAC references and sample alert contexts to the runbook.

Closing note

Chaos Week revealed that small edits to the operator handbook and a compact incident action card can reduce cognitive load and shave 4–12 minutes off median time-to-first-action. The prioritized edits above are intentionally conservative: they convert observed safe operator behavior into repeatable processes while deferring heavier automation until telemetry enrichment and rollback guarantees exist.

If you have questions, objections, or additional observations from the exercise, add comments to this page or file a follow-up ticket in the runbook guild backlog (label: runbook-updates).
sections.heading: Overview

payload.page_title: Crosswalk: Cache Heuristics Harmonization & Operator Knowledge Transfer

sections.body: This retrospective documents a three-month cross-team program ("Crosswalk") to harmonize cache eviction and prefetch heuristics across the platform, plus the accompanying operator knowledge transfer and playbook updates. The goal was to reduce SLO volatility driven by heuristic drift across schedulers, reduce token-cost variance, and make on-call actions reproducible.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Problem: Multiple teams had independently tuned runtime cache and prefetch heuristics (edge prefetch, KV-prefix warmset, tenant warmset thresholds). Over time small local changes resulted in inconsistent behavior during bursts: some regions aggressively prefetched, driving unexpected token cost and cold-cache misses elsewhere.
- Impact observed: 2.8% median increase in 95th-percentile token latency for multi-tenant inference during the November surge; token-cost spikes (single-day delta) up to 14% for a subset of tenants on mixed workloads.
- Scope: runtime scheduling, platform prefetch layer, operator runbooks, and dashboards/alerts. Not in scope: model architecture or serving kernel-level changes.
sections.heading: Background and motivation

sections.body:
1. 2026-08-12: Incident trigger — regional latency spike flagged by SLO burn monitor.
2. 2026-08-18: Working group chartered (Platform runtime, Serving, SRE, Observability).
3. 2026-09 to 2026-10: Inventory phase — collect heuristics, config, and operator runbooks.
4. 2026-11: Harmonization trial (canary in eu-west-1 then us-west-2).
5. 2026-11-15: Retrospective draft (this doc created).
6. 2026-12: Cross-team training sessions and runbook updates.
7. 2027-01-10: Finalized action items and dashboard templates.
sections.heading: Timeline of Crosswalk program

sections.body:
- Divergent defaults: Four services used different default warmset retention windows (10s, 30s, 60s, 120s). The shortest window caused thrash during noisy bursts.
- Priority mismatch: Tenant-priority scoring was being applied inconsistently; some delegating components treated score >= 70 as burst-capable while others used >= 85.
- Operator mental model gap: On-call runbooks documented manual prefills for cold-cache incidents, but the procedures were ambiguous and differed by region.
- Observability blind spots: Existing dashboards showed aggregate warmset hit-rate but not by tenant class and workload fingerprint (chat vs. embeddings).
sections.heading: Key findings

sections.body:
- eu-west-1 canary (harmonized heuristics): 95th P99 token latency decreased from 420 ms to 360 ms (-14.3%).
- Token-cost variance across tenants (sampled cohort): coefficient of variation down from 0.22 to 0.12.
- Operator time-to-diagnosis for cache-related incidents: median reduced from 28 minutes to 11 minutes.
sections.heading: Quantified impact (post-canary measurements)

sections.body:
- Standardize a conservative baseline for warmset retention: default = 60s, tenant-class overrides allowed with explicit review.
- Adopt a single tenant-priority scale (0-100) and canonical thresholding: burst-capable = >= 80.
- Add a "graceful backoff" circuit inside prefetcher: exponential backoff up to 5 minutes when warmset thrash detected.
- Treat heuristics changes as "config-feature" releases requiring canary and observability checklist signoff.
sections.heading: Decisions made

sections.body:
1) Publish canonical heuristics spec and config table (owner: Platform runtime team — Maya Santos) — due 2027-01-31.

2) Dashboard templates (owner: Observability — Evan Chen) — create 3 panels and an alert:
   - Panel A: warmset hit-rate by tenant-class (last 30d window).
   - Panel B: prefetch-trigger rate and backoff events (per region).
   - Panel C: token-cost variance histogram (per-tenant daily).
   - Alert: >= 15% reduction in warmset hit-rate for > 5 min for >= 5 tenants in same shard.
sections.heading: Action items and rollout plan (owners and dates)

sections.body:
"avg:llm.prefetch.hit_rate{environment:prod,region:eu-west-1}.rollup(avg,3600) by {tenant_class} < 0.65"

3) Runbook harmonization (owner: SRE/Oncall — Diego Ramirez) — migrate and consolidate duplicate pages into: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/crosswalk-prefetch-and-warmset-runbook-2027.json — due 2027-02-14. Steps will include:
   a) Pre-incident checklist (what metrics to collect).
   b) Operator remediation steps (order-of-operations for manual warmfill, prefills, and soft-evictions).
   c) Post-remediation validation queries.

4) Operator training and exercises (owner: Platform learning lead — Priya Nair) — run three 90-minute labs covering:
   - Lab 1: Identifying warmset thrash and isolating the offending tenant.
   - Lab 2: Safe manual-prefill and rollback.
   - Lab 3: Interpreting dashboard panels and handoff notes.
   Schedule: one session per fortnight starting 2027-02-21.

5) Canary policy update and automation (owner: Serving runtime — Jacob O'Connor) — implement automated canary guardrails to ensure observability checklist completion before heuristics config promotion — due 2027-03-07.
sections.heading: Example Datadog query (sample)

sections.body:
- SLO: Maintain 95th-percentile token latency target (global) <= baseline_pre_crosswalk + 3% for 30 days post-rollout.
- Cost: No >10% sustained token-cost uplift for any tenant cohort for 14 days post-change.
- Operator efficiency: median time-to-detect and time-to-diagnose remain <= 15 minutes for cache-related incidents.
sections.heading: Monitoring and acceptance criteria

sections.body:
- Quick triage checklist:
  1. Check warmset hit-rate by tenant_class -> panel A.
  2. If hit-rate < 0.6 for > 5 minutes, check prefetch-trigger rate -> panel B.
  3. Correlate tenant fingerprint (chat vs. embedding) using request_label parsed traces.
  4. If thrash confirmed, apply soft backoff toggle (ui/infra flag) and observe for 3 minutes.
  5. If no improvement, perform manual warmfill for impacted warmset shard (follow manual-prefill substeps).

- Manual-prefill substeps (operator):
  1) Identify top 5 requests for shard using sampling query.
  2) Run prefill-hydrate command (cli):
     ./platform-prefill --shard <shard-id> --requests-file requests.json --concurrency 4 --dry-run=false
  3) Monitor token-latency and warmset hit-rate; revert if error rate > 0.5% or latency increases.
sections.heading: Runbook extracts (operator quick-reference)

sections.body:
- Governance beats heroics: consistent defaults and release gates prevent asymmetric tuning.
- Observability is granular: aggregate metrics hide tenant-level pathologies; always sample and tag by fingerprint.
- Invest in operator pedagogy: short labs with scenario-based playbooks were the most effective way to close knowledge gaps.

Appendix A — Canonical heuristics table (excerpt):

| Component                | Default | Rationale                          | Override scope      | Owner          |
|-------------------------|---------|------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Warmset retention       | 60s     | Balance cold miss vs. memory churn | tenant-class only   | Platform runtime|
| Prefetch concurrency    | 8       | Prevent requester overload         | region-level only   | Serving runtime |
| Backoff multiplier      | 2x      | Fast graceful reduction of thrash  | global only         | Platform runtime|
| Tenant priority burst   | >= 80  | Clear burst-capable threshold      | tenant exceptions   | Product/Revenue |

Appendix B — Checklist for config-feature release:

- [ ] Spec published and reviewed by runtime + serving + observability.
- [ ] Canary plan documented (regions, sampling fraction, rollback criteria).
- [ ] Dashboards deployed and alerting wired to oncall.
- [ ] Operator lab scheduled and recording archived.

Appendix C — Links & artifacts:

- Inventory spreadsheet (internal link): platform-cache-inventory-2026.csv
- Canary experiment notebook: /notebooks/harmonize-prefetch-canary-2026.ipynb
- Training slides: /assets/platform-training/crosswalk-prefetch-2026.pdf
sections.heading: Lessons learned and recommendations

sections.body: Thanks to all contributors from Platform runtime, Serving, Observability, Product, and SRE who participated in the Crosswalk program. This retrospective is intended as a stable reference for future heuristics alignment efforts.

payload.page_title: Operator Chaos Gradebook and Experimentation Handbook

sections.body:
Overview
-------
This handbook defines a standardized, operator-friendly "gradebook" and execution process for platform chaos and resiliency experiments. The goal is to make experiments repeatable, measurable, and actionable so platform teams can continuously improve SLO resilience (latency, availability, token cost) across model-serving subsystems (prefetch/KV cache, batching, routing, fallbacks).

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: platform operators, SREs, runtime engineers, and feature owners.
- Systems covered: KV prefix cache, prefetch cohorts, batching pipeline, model-variant routing, regional failover, tenant isolation.
- Excluded: infra-level hardware failures that require vendor escalation (separate process).

Why a gradebook?
----------------
Operators run many experiments; the gradebook:
- Enforces consistent metrics and severity-weighting
- Produces a single numeric resilience score per experiment
- Stores remediation actions and regression risk for future runbooks

Metrics and scoring rubric
-------------------------
Primary metrics (measured during baseline and during experiment):
- Tail P95/P99 latency (ms) for foreground requests
- Successful token throughput (tokens/sec) per model variant
- Error rate (5xx-equivalent) and silent-fallback counts
- Unit cost delta (USD/token or internal units)
- SLO burn: percent of requests that violated customer-visible SLO in the window

Scoring (0-100): weighted composite where higher is better. Example weights: latency 30, errors 30, throughput 15, cost 15, graceful_degradation 10.

Experiment taxonomy (examples)
-----------------------------
1) Controlled prefetch miss storm
   - Objective: validate cache prefetch admission and operator rollback paths
   - Failure mode: synthetic cohort TTL expiry + cold-prefix surge
2) Batcher head-of-line contention
   - Objective: observe fairness and soft-eviction heuristics under mixed-tenant loads
3) Model-variant cascade
   - Objective: force a primary variant to degrade and verify routing/fallback correctness
4) Regional routing partition
   - Objective: simulate a regional control-plane delay and verify graceful cross-region routing

Pre-experiment checklist (must pass to run in production-sim)
------------------------------------------------------------
1. Stakeholders: assign owner and reviewers, notify oncall rotation.
2. Safety gates: have canary range; define blast radius (tenant subset, region).
3. Monitoring: instrument dashboards and open an experiment run ticket.
4. Automated rollback: pre-configure a playbook to cancel experiment and revert config.
5. Communication plan: Slack channel, Pager duty escalation contact, and expected run window.

Runbook: executing an experiment (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create experiment ticket using template (see Appendix B). Include: hypothesis, blast radius, observability links, rollback steps.
2. Warm baseline: run 30-minute baseline collection at normal traffic to establish priors.
3. Stage 1 (canary): apply failure to 1% of traffic for 10 minutes. Observe metrics and SLI burn.
   - Abort if SLO burn > 5% during canary or unhandled 5xx spike > 2x baseline.
4. Stage 2 (ramp): increase to 10% for 20 minutes. Run gradebook scoring script.
5. Stage 3 (full): expand to full blast radius if Stage 2 passes. Record final grade and remediation notes.
6. Post-run: immediately run smoke check suite and re-collect 30-minute post-recovery baseline.

Abort and rollback criteria (operator checklist)
--------------------------------------------
- Immediate abort triggers: API gateway 5xx > 5% absolute, customer-visible SLO burn > 15%, tenant escalations via support.
- Soft rollback triggers: unexpected long-tail latency increase (P99 > 2x baseline) without throughput benefit.

Dashboards and alert templates
------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Real-time SLI panel (P95, P99, error rate) with baseline overlay
- Token throughput per-variant and aggregate cost delta panel
- Operator-gradebook scorecard showing component-level sub-scores (latency/errors/throughput/cost)
- Synthetic canary trace panel showing request scatter and tail examples
sections.heading: Minimum dashboard panels

sections.body:
- name: Experiment_P99_Regression
  expr: increase(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="llm-runtime",quantile="0.99"}[10m]) > (baseline * 2)
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "P99 regression during chaos experiment: {{ $labels.instance }}"

- name: Gradebook_Score_Drop
  expr: llm_experiment_gradebook_score{experiment="current-run"} < 50
  for: 2m

Postmortem and gradebook entry template
--------------------------------------
Every experiment must create a gradebook entry with these fields (stored in experiment-ticket):
- Experiment ID: string
- Hypothesis: short statement
- Blast radius: tenants/regions/percent traffic
- Run owner: name + pager contact
- Final score: numeric (0-100) and sub-scores per metric
- Observed failures and root cause hypothesis
- Remediation actions and owners (with due dates)
- Regression risk: low/medium/high and why
- Learnings: concrete configuration or code changes planned
sections.heading: Alert rule examples (Prometheus / Alertmanager style)

sections.body:
| Experiment ID | Score | Latency | Errors | Throughput | Cost | Owner | Status |
| EX-2026-321 | 72 | 85/100 | 60/100 | 70/100 | 75/100 | Maya Patel | remediation_open |

Retrospective cadence and template
----------------------------------
- Quarterly deep-dive: aggregate top 5 regressions and follow through on long-lived remediations.
- Post-experiment: short blameless retro within 3 business days with slides covering: hypothesis, what happened, why, next steps.

Roadmap: 6–12 months (prioritized)
--------------------------------
1. Gradebook automation: ingest baseline and compute composite score automatically (Q4 2026).
2. Synthetic runner: scheduling and safe-environment harness to run low-risk regressions nightly (Q1 2027).
3. Cross-team experiment ledger: searchable store for past gradebook entries and owners (Q2 2027).
4. Dashboard library: curated templates for each experiment taxonomy (ongoing).

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Run owner: platform-ops (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary)
- Dashboard maintenance: observability team (owner)
- Gradebook storage & tooling: eng-platform infra team

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets
--------------------------------
sections.heading: Sample gradebook table (rendered)

sections.body:
```
$ rx-ticket create --title "Prefetch miss storm - cohort A" --assignee maya.patel --labels chaos,canary --meta blast_radius=5%
```
sections.heading: Create an experiment ticket (CLI)

sections.body:
```
$ python tools/gradebook/compute_score.py --experiment EX-2026-321 --baseline-window 30m --run-window 30m
```
sections.heading: Run gradebook scoring script (local)

sections.body:
```
{
  "title": "Experiment - SLI Overview",
  "panels": [ { "type": "graph", "targets": [ {"expr":"histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"llm-runtime\"}[5m])) by (le))"} ] } ]
}
```

Appendix B — Ticket template (copy into new run ticket)
-------------------------------------------------------
- Title: [Taxonomy] - short description
- Experiment ID: auto-generated
- Owner: name + pager
- Blast radius:
- Hypothesis:
- KPIs to monitor:
  - P95/P99 latency
  - Error rate
  - Throughput (tokens/s)
  - Cost delta
- Abort conditions:
- Rollback steps:
- Observability links:
- Postmortem owner and expected due date:

Notes and references
--------------------
- See the operator-safety-cage guidelines for allowed blast radii and blocked tenants.
- Link: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/operator-safety-cage-and-experimentation-guidelines-2026

Contact
-------
For questions about this handbook, contact Maya Patel (maya.patel@redwood.ai) or join #platform-chaos on Slack.

payload.page_title: Ephemeral Environments: Cost Controls, RBAC, and Lifecycle Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents the standard process for provisioning, governing, and retiring ephemeral environments (dev/test/feature-preview) intended for platform and product teams. Focus areas: cost containment, role-based access controls (RBAC), observability onboarding, automated TTL lifecycle, and post-mortem templates for environment incidents.

Goals
-----
- Keep per-environment monthly cost under $200 for single-node GPUless environments and under $1,500 for multi-node GPU previews unless explicitly approved.
- Enforce least-privilege access by default; require approval for write-level network or KMS access.
- Reduce orphaned ephemeral environments >72 hours by 90% within three months via automation and alerting.
- Provide a reproducible teardown process and clear ownership for each environment.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
Use for: feature branch previews, demo environments, partner staging, customer PoC sandboxes. Do NOT use for: production replicas handling live data, long-running performance experiments without prior capacity sign-off.

Key concepts and vocabulary
---------------------------
- Ephemeral environment: short-lived environment spun up automatically from PRs or by CLI; expected TTL = 24–72 hours.
- Owner tag: metadata identifying a primary owner (team and oncall) that appears in dashboards. Format: owner:team/name@redwood.com.
- Cost cap: a soft limit (monthly estimate) enforced via budget policies and throttling.
- Preview role: RBAC profile with read-only infra network + limited secret access.

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Environments (eng-platform) — rotation lead: Maya Chen (primary) / Liam O'Connor (backup).
- Escalation path: Environment owner -> Platform oncall -> Infra SRE lead -> CTO operations if >8 hours outage impacting demos.

Provisioning checklist (automated CI flow)
-----------------------------------------
1. PR triggers pipeline: runs IaC plan (Terragrunt/Terraform) in a sandbox workspace.
2. Create ephemeral namespace with labels: project, pr-id, owner, cost-center.
3. Apply a Preview role binding (Kubernetes RBAC) limiting access to: get/list/describe for core infra, no cluster-admin.
4. Inject secrets via ephemeral secret store scoped to preview role (no KMS unwrapping).
5. Deploy observability sidecars: tracing and metrics exporters are mandatory.
6. Run smoke healthcheck and register environment in Ephemeral Registry service.
7. Assign TTL and schedule automatic teardown.

RBAC profile (recommended)
-------------------------
- preview-role (k8s ClusterRole):
  - allowed: get, list, watch for Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets (read-only); exec into pods disabled.
  - denied: create/patch/delete on node/cluster-resources, no persistentVolumeClaims by default.
- admin-preview (approval required):
  - allowed: elevated service account for operations teams; requires a JIRA ticket and time-bounded grant (max 48 hours).

Example Kubernetes YAML snippet
------------------------------
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: preview-rolebinding-pr-1234
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: preview-runner
  namespace: preview-pr-1234
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: preview-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

Cost controls and enforcement
-----------------------------
- Default machine types: t3.medium-equivalent for app nodes; g4dn.xlarge disallowed unless GPU-request approved.
- Quotas: Ephemeral Registry enforces a per-team concurrent environment quota (default 5).
- Budget trigger: Cloud billing alert when estimated monthly cost > 85% of cost cap; triggers environment suspension (read-only) and notifies owner.
- Auto-throttle policy: scale replicas to 1 and reduce CPU to 200m when idle metric <5% CPU for 15m.

Monitoring, dashboards, and alerts
----------------------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Ephemeral Overview: shows active envs, owner, ttl, estimated hourly cost.
- Cost by PR: chargeback view grouped by repo and team.
- Health Summary: error rate, latency P95 for preview APIs.

Alert thresholds (examples)
- Orphaned env (>72h without latest commit): p1 alert to platform-owner mailing list.
- Cost spike (env hourly >3x baseline for 30m): p2 alert to owner and SRE.
- Observability missing (no traces for 10m): p2 alert and auto-tag env as degraded.

Runbook: immediate actions for a cost spike
-----------------------------------------
1. Identify environment from dashboard -> click into Ephemeral Registry.
2. Check owner tag and notify via Slack (#platform-ephemeral).
3. If spike is benign (load test), acknowledge and document run in registry.
4. If spike is unexpected: scale down replicas, restrict external ingress, and snapshot logs.
5. If cost exceeds 200% of expected for 1h, suspend environment and open a JIRA with label "ephemeral-cost-incident".

Automated TTL lifecycle policy (implementation notes)
----------------------------------------------------
- When created, env gets TTL metadata: created_at, expires_at. A cleanup controller runs every 15 minutes and:
  - If expires_at < now -> mark for termination and send pre-termination notice 30 minutes prior.
  - If marked 'extended' -> evaluate remaining budget; extensions require owner approval via Jira API.

API examples
------------
- Create preview (CLI):
  redwood preview create --repo infra/repo --pr 1234 --owner "team/backend/alex@redwood.com" --ttl 48h
- Extend preview (via API):
  POST /api/v1/previews/1234/extend {"owner":"alex@redwood.com","hours":24}

Chargeback and tagging rules
---------------------------
- Tagging format: repo:team:pr (e.g., agent-service:payments:2345). Billing pipeline aggregates tags hourly.
- Teams with recurring high spend (>10 env-hours/day avg) get notified monthly with optimization recommendations.

Security hardening checklist (must pass before public partner previews)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- No production dataset mounts.
- Secrets are read-only and ephemeral; rotate service tokens every 24h.
- Private network endpoints require approval and documented justification.
- Penetration checklist: static-scan, dependency-scan, credentials-scan passed.

Post-incident retrospective template for environment outages
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Incident summary (one-liner)
2. Timeline (UTC)
3. Impacted envs and owners
4. Root cause analysis (technical + process)
5. Corrective actions and owners (with due dates)
6. Metrics to monitor and SLO changes (if any)
7. Retro notes and follow-up meeting date

Retro example (brief)
--------------------
- Incident: Excessive egress billing from preview-pr-839 on 2026-01-21.
- Root cause: A misconfigured data sink in third-party integration created a background job.
- Fix: Added network egress policy, revoked third-party token, added smoke test.
- Action items: ticket #PLAT-342 (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2026-02-02).

Roadmap and improvements (Q1–Q3 2026)
-------------------------------------
- Q1: Implement quota-aware preflight checks in CI pipelines.
- Q2: Add budget-aware autoscaling rules integrated with billing metrics.
- Q3: Fine-grained RBAC self-serve granting interface with audit trail.

Appendices
---------
A. Failure-mode matrix (short)
- Missing TTL: Orphaned envs -> remediations: alert + automated termination.
- Secret leakage risk: Immediate revoke + audit, rotate relevant tokens.
- High cost from external traffic: throttle ingress + block egress to unapproved endpoints.

B. Quick commands
- List previews: redwood preview list --team payments
- Force terminate: redwood preview terminate --id preview-pr-1234 --reason "cost spike"

Contact and ownership
---------------------
- Platform Environments (eng-platform): platforms-environments@redwood.com
- Rotation lead: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.com)
- Oncall Slack: #platform-oncall

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-04: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2026-01-12: Added automated throttle policy and cost spike runbook (Liam O'Connor).
- 2026-02-18: Finalized RBAC profiles and retro template; published (Priya Menon).

payload.page_title: Operator automation rollout (Q3 2025) — postmortem and action plan

sections.body:
Summary:

In Q3 2025 we rolled out the first global version of the Operator Automation feature (v1.0) across production regions. Operator Automation is a set of automated remediation workflows that detect degraded inference worker pools and apply corrective actions (scale, restart, route around) without requiring manual intervention. The rollout aimed to reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for common transient faults and to lower cognitive load on on-call operators.

Unfortunately, within 48 hours of enabling the feature by default for all tenants, we observed repeated SLO burn for background and interactive text-generation requests in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Multiple customers reported elevated 95th percentile latency and several internal SLIs crossed the 1% error budget threshold.

This document summarizes the timeline, root causes, key contributing factors, mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized action plan with owners and deadlines. It also captures recommendations for safer automation rollouts and a proposed validation suite for future releases.

Impact:

- Regions affected: us-west-2 (primary), eu-west-1 (secondary).
- Customer impact: ~7 customers experienced >10% increase in 95p latency for generation endpoints; 2 customers had temporary degraded SLAs (billing credits applied).
- SLO metrics: 95p response latency SLO (<= 200ms) breached by 18% for a 3-hour window on 2025-10-07. Error budget consumption spiked 12% across the platform during the incident week.
- MTTR: Initial mitigation took ~210 minutes to stabilize traffic after rollback.

Timeline (chronological):

1) 2025-10-05 02:00 UTC — Canary rollout of Operator Automation v1.0 to 10% of non-prod and a single canary tenant in us-west-2. Observability signals stable.
2) 2025-10-06 18:30 UTC — Gradual promotion to 100% of non-prod and 50% of production tenant traffic via feature flag. No immediate anomalies.
3) 2025-10-07 03:10 UTC — Automated remediation triggers: operator-autoremediation started automated rebalancing of KV cache shards on several GPU nodes. Remediation entailed ephemeral process restarts and temporary eviction of in-memory prefixes.
4) 2025-10-07 03:40 UTC — Platform dashboards show correlated 95p latency increase (us-west-2). Several rate-limited retries from client SDKs amplified traffic spikes.
5) 2025-10-07 05:00 UTC — On-call notified via pager for slo-burn alert (operator.slo_burn > 5% over 30m).
6) 2025-10-07 06:40 UTC — Emergency rollback of Operator Automation feature flag in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; traffic stabilized by 06:50 UTC.
7) 2025-10-07 07:30 UTC — Post-rollback validation and targeted remediation complete.

Root causes and contributing factors:

Primary root causes (direct):
- Aggressive automation sequence that performed concurrent KV shard eviction and instance-level restarts without global rate limiting. This caused synchronized regeneration of KV caches across many replicas, producing a temporary surge in CPU/GPU memory pressure and I/O which increased tail latency.
- Automation algorithm assumed a soft window of 30s between dependent actions; in production observed interleaving that created a thundering-herd effect.

Secondary contributors (systemic & process):
- Canary surface and traffic shaping did not model multi-tenant retry amplification; canary tenants had lower retry rates and different client SDK versions compared to many real customers.
- Dashboards lacked a causal decomposition view combining KV-cache-regeneration events with tenant-level retry patterns. Operators could see SLOs and node CPU but not the causal link quickly enough.
- No global automation circuit breaker that would stop concurrent remediations above an operational concurrency threshold per-region.
- Runbook and escalation playbooks assumed manual operator intervention for restarts, so automation had less conservative safety checks.

Immediate mitigations taken during the incident:

- Feature flag rollback to disable Operator Automation across affected regions (2025-10-07 06:40 UTC).
- Throttling introduced at the request ingress layer for traffic from SDKs with high retry rates to dampen amplification while rollback completed.
- Short-term dashboard added: operator.autoremediation.activity showing "in-flight" remediation count and per-tenant KV-eviction events.

Detailed timeline of mitigations and diagnostic commands used by operators (runbook excerpts):

1) Verify automation state and in-flight remediation (internal API):

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_OP_TOKEN" https://platform-api.internal/operator-autoremediation/status | jq

2) List nodes under eviction pressure and tail-latency contributors:

kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=worker -o wide
kubectl -n runtime top pods --containers | grep worker

3) To temporarily mark a region as automation-disabled from operator console CLI:

redwood ops automation disable --region us-west-2 --reason "post-rollback stabilization"

Runbook for emergency rollback (condensed):

1) Pin feature flag to OFF via LaunchDarkly (or internal flag service).
2) Confirm disabled state across all regions: query operator-autoremediation/status for all regions.
3) Re-route priority tenants to dedicated pool if degradation persists: redwood routing promote --tenant $TENANT_ID --pool dedicated-pool-1
4) Monitor slo-dashboard/95p-latency and autoremediation.activity until values return to baseline for 30m.

Lessons learned and recommended changes (short, medium, long term):

Short term (<= 30 days):
- Implement a per-region automation concurrency limiter and soft circuit-breaker that prevents >N concurrent remediations (default N=3). Owner: Ramon Alvarez. Due: 2025-11-01.
- Expand canary traffic profiles to include synthetic retry amplification tests that emulate worst-case SDK behaviour. Owner: QA/Platform SRE. Due: 2025-11-05.
- Add an observability dashboard that shows correlation between automation events and tenant-level retry rates (operator.autoremediation.causal-map). Owner: Observability team. Due: 2025-10-20.

Medium term (30–90 days):
- Introduce staged remediation orchestration with exponential backoff between dependent actions and randomized jitter windows. Owner: Serving Runtime. Due: 2026-01-10.
- Implement an automation safety harness with offline simulation capability (runbook-sim) that replays historical traffic and measures expected tail-latency impact. Owner: Applied ML & Evals. Due: 2026-01-31.

Long term (>90 days):
- Policy: All automation rollouts that can affect KV caches or memory must pass a stability gate that includes: synthetic amplification tests, replay simulation, and a chaos-probing run in staging. Owner: Eng Platform. Due: 2026-04-01.
- Product change: Expose an "automation-sensitivity" tenant preference so customers can opt into conservative automation behavior for regulated workloads. Owner: Product. Due: 2026-06-01.

Prioritized action items (table):

| Priority | Action | Owner | Due | Status |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| P0 | Implement per-region automation concurrency limiter and circuit-breaker | Ramon Alvarez | 2025-11-01 | in_progress |
| P0 | Create synthetic retry-amplification canary profile and add to CI pipeline | QA/Platform SRE | 2025-11-05 | todo |
| P1 | Add "autoremediation.causal-map" dashboard and alert | Observability Team | 2025-10-20 | done |
| P1 | Add exponential backoff + jitter to remediation sequences | Serving Runtime | 2026-01-10 | todo |
| P2 | Build offline runbook-sim and validation harness | Applied ML & Evals | 2026-01-31 | todo |

Metrics and dashboards to track going forward:

- operator.autoremediation.inflight_count (gauge) — target: <= 3 per-region by default.
- operator.autoremediation.throttle_rate (counter) — shows how often circuit-breaker engages.
- slo.95p.latency.by-region (timeseries) — monitor for deviation from baseline.
- tenant.retry.amplification.index — synthetic metric introduced to quantify a tenant's retry behavior.

Example alert rule (Prometheus-style pseudo):

alert: OperatorAutomationConcurrentRemediations
expr: operator_autoremediation_inflight_count{region="us-west-2"} > 3
for: 5m
labels: {severity="major", team="eng-platform"}
annotations: {summary=">3 concurrent remediations in us-west-2"}

Communication and customer handling:

- Immediately after rollback we notified impacted customers via standard incident template and offered a follow-up technical review. Two customers requested dedicated debrief sessions which were completed by 2025-11-20.
- Applied goodwill credits where SLAs were breached. Finance and Customer Success coordinated credits and post-incident outreach.

Appendix — quick diagnostic checklist for oncall operators (cheat-sheet):

1) Check automation status: curl https://platform-api.internal/operator-autoremediation/status
2) If inflight_count > 3 in the region, consider disabling automation and promote priority tenants to dedicated pools.
3) To re-enable automation for a region after stabilization: redwood ops automation enable --region <region> --dry-run; monitor operator.autoremediation.inflight_count for 60 minutes.
4) Escalation: if SLOs remain degraded > 60 minutes after rollback, page Eng Platform lead and SRE manager (pager codes listed in Oncall directory).

Related pages:

- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026
- /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/llm-quality-regression-alerting-and-dashboard-guidelines-2026

Author note: This postmortem was drafted collaboratively by the Platform and SRE teams. The action items above are tracked in the operational backlog (JIRA project PLATOPS) and progress will be reviewed in the Platform weekly retro.

payload.page_title: Operator Skill Atrophy and Retraining Retrospective

sections.body:
Summary:

This retrospective analyzes a multi-week increase in operator error rate and time-to-resolution (TTR) during November–December 2025 that correlated with several production incidents involving degraded prefix cache behavior and tenant token surges. The investigation found measurable skill atrophy in the platform operator pool after rapid headcount expansion and a gap in targeted retraining and runbook ergonomics.

Goals of this doc:
- Record timeline, evidence, and root causes.
- Capture immediate mitigations and permanent fixes.
- Define a repeatable retraining and certification workflow for operators.
- Propose dashboard and alert changes to reduce cognitive load during incidents.

1) Incident timeline and measurable symptoms
- 2025-11-12: First moderate cache-degradation alert in us-west-2; operator resolved with manual prefix eviction but required escalation to runtime team.
- 2025-11-23 to 2025-12-08: 7 incidents triggered by tenant token bursts; mean TTR rose from 22m to 67m.
- 2025-12-11: Regional burst led to a cross-tenant fallback; rollback required across two model-serving pools.

Metrics observed (aggregate Nov–Dec 2025):
| Metric | Baseline (Oct) | Peak (Dec) | Delta |
|-------|---------------:|----------:|-----:|
| Mean TTR (operator-handled) | 22m | 67m | +305% |
| Escalation rate (to runtime) | 6% | 28% | +366% |
| Operator command errors (CLI retries) | 4/day | 18/day | +350% |

2) Root cause analysis
Primary root causes we identified: 
A. Skill atrophy and uneven onboarding: rapid hiring in Q3–Q4 2025 doubled operator headcount; onboarding focused on service-level orientation but lacked practical incident simulations for prefix cache and tenant-burst scenarios.
B. Runbook and tool ergonomics: runbooks assumed operator familiarity with multi-step CLI flows and ad-hoc prefix-key discovery; dashboards hid the most actionable signals behind several clicks.
C. Alert noise and unclear runbook-entry points: frequent low-value alerts led to context switching; when a high-severity cache degradation occurred, operators had difficulty differentiating between root symptoms (hot-tenant vs. local shard failure).
D. Certification decay: there was no enforced recertification cadence after initial onboarding.

Supporting evidence:
- Interview excerpts: multiple operators reported that the prefix cache troubleshooting steps did not match the live telemetry outputs they saw.
- Pager logs: sequence of commands showed repeated retries and late execution of the safe-evict procedure.
- Training records: only 18% of operators had completed the new-tiered simulation lab by Nov 1, 2025.

3) Immediate mitigations (operational) — owners and deadlines
1. Deploy simplified emergency runbook (v0.1) with one-click orchestrations for safe-evict and model-swap. Owner: Runtime Ops (A. Ramos). Deadline: 2026-01-20.
2. Create an on-call quick-reference widget in Console with the top 3 signals and the exact next CLI command. Owner: Eng Platform UI (S. Walker). Deadline: 2026-01-31.
3. Add a temporary suppression window for low-value cache alerts to reduce noise during peak hours. Owner: Observability (P. Nair). Deadline: 2026-01-12.
4. Mandatory troubleshooting shadowing: require new operators to shadow a senior operator for first 60 days. Owner: Oncall Manager (J. Alvarez). Deadline: immediate.

4) Long-term remediation and roadmap entries
A. Retraining & certification program (Platform Learning path) — high priority
- Quarterly recertification based on simulation completion and written checks.
- Certification levels: Associate, Operator, Senior Operator, Operator-Runbook-Author.
- Implementation steps: build a simulation lab (see section 7), author evaluation rubrics, integrate badge issuance with HR/LMS.
- Owner: People-ops + Eng Platform training lead (M. Chen). Target delivery: Q2 2026.

B. Runbook redesign and operator ergonomics — medium priority
- Convert long linear runbooks into triage-first decision trees with pre-populated commands and runnable steps.
- Add a ‘safe-mode’ orchestrator UI for performing common actions (prefetch evict, model swap, tenant throttle) with an audit log.
- Owner: Runbooks and UI teams. Target: Q3 2026.

C. Dashboard and alert modernization — medium-high priority
- Create an incident starter dashboard template that surfaces: token-rate per-tenant heatmap, prefix-cache hit/miss ratio by shard, and replicate-lag with top-3 suspected causes.
- Alerting changes: move from static-threshold alerts to anomaly-score alerts for prefix-cache; craft combined alert bundles that reduce noise and call out the most-likely cause.
- Owner: Observability product. Target: Q2 2026.

D. Knowledge retention instrumentation — low-medium priority
- Track operator CLI flows (opt-in), measure retry rates and time between successful runs, and feed signals into training needs dashboard.
- Owner: Platform Analytics. Target: Q4 2026.

5) Changes to SLOs, SLIs and on-call contracts
- No change to external customer SLOs at this time.
- Internal SLI: mean TTR for operator-resolvable incidents to be <30m with 95th percentile <2h. Target by Q4 2026.
- On-call hours: limit mandatory pager coverage to 5 weeks per quarter per operator to reduce burnout and allow training. Owner: Eng SRE leadership.

6) Runbook excerpt: simplified safe-evict flow (human + UI fallback)
- Purpose: safely evict a hot prefix without evicting shared KV.
- Preconditions: ensure model-swap fallback available, notify customers if eviction exceeds 2m.
- Steps:
  1) Identify hot prefix with dashboard quick-view.
  2) Run: redwood-admin cache inspect --shard $SHARD --prefix $PREFIX --attrs.
  3) If affected-tenants > 1, follow multi-tenant handshake: redwood-admin cache prepare-evict --prefix $PREFIX --dry-run.
  4) Execute safe-evict: redwood-admin cache evict --prefix $PREFIX --safe-confirm "operator:<id>" --max-objects 1000
  5) Monitor metrics for 5 minutes, and if error-rate reduces, close incident.

CLI example:
$ redwood-admin cache inspect --shard s42 --prefix tok_h_2025-11 --attrs
{"shard":"s42","hit_rate":0.12,"top_tenants":["tenant-123","tenant-987"]}

7) Simulation lab specification (for training and certification)
- Purpose: replicate common operator incidents in a non-prod controlled environment so operators can practice fast diagnosis and execution.
- Scenarios to include:
  - Hot-tenant prefix cache burst with noisy neighbors.
  - Cold-small-shard eviction and prefetch miscoordination.
  - Model-variant fallback misfire and rollback under load.
  - Cross-region failover with partial telemetry loss.
- Lab requirements table:
| Requirement | Description | Owner |
|---|---|---:|
| Sandbox runtime | Small cluster that can simulate token surges and KV prefix behaviors | Eng Infra |
| Telemetry injection tool | Ability to inject token-rate spikes and synthetic traces | Observability |
| Grading harness | Auto-scores runbook steps and time-to-resolution | DevX |

8) Dashboard and alert config example (YAML)
alerts:
  prefix_cache_anomaly:
    type: anomaly_score
    window: 5m
    score_threshold: 0.85
    primary_actions: [notify-oncall, open-incident, surface-dashboard]

dashboard: "incident-starter"
panels:
  - id: token-rate-heatmap
    datasource: metrics_api
    query: "topk(10, token_rate{region=\"us-west-2\"}) by (tenant)"
  - id: prefix-cache-ratio
    datasource: metrics_api
    query: "sum(hit_rate) by (shard) / sum(requests) by (shard)"

9) Owner and accountability roster
- Program owner: Maya Chen (Eng Platform) — accountable for retraining program.
- Observability changes: Priya Nair — accountable for dashboard and alert changes.
- Runbook ergonomics: Jordan Alvarez — accountable for runbook redesign and UI safe-mode.
- Measurement and analytics: Platform Analytics team.

10) Postmortem actions and acceptance criteria
- Deliver simulation lab and pass-rate target: >= 85% pass for Associate level within 3 months of launch.
- Reduce mean TTR to <30m for operator-resolved incidents within 6 months.
- Decrease escalation rate to runtime team to <12% within 6 months.
- Runbook v1 acceptance: verified by 3 live drills with senior operators and zero critical errors.

11) Retrospective lessons learned (one-liners)
- Hiring velocity without structured practice leads to brittle operational response.
- Runbooks should be runnable, not just readable.
- Observability must pre-emptively guide action — surface the next-click not just the symptom.
- Invest in small automated scaffolds (UI safe-mode) — reduces cognitive load during pressure.

Appendix: quick checklist for other teams
- Hiring teams: allocate 10% of initial onboarding time for simulation lab practice.
- Product: review Console widgets to ensure operator-facing quick-actions are not disabled by default.
- Security: ensure the CLI orchestrator records are audited and RBAC enforced for safe-evict actions.

Contact and follow-up
- Questions or to volunteer as a simulation exercise volunteer: maya@redwood.example.com
- Quarterly review meeting scheduled: 2026-04-05 (owner: M. Chen)

Document history:
- 2026-01-10: created by Maya Chen
- 2026-02-15: updated with Simulation Lab spec and alert YAML by Priya Nair
