payload.page_title: Dynamic allocator fallback contracts and testing cookbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This cookbook defines machine-readable fallback contracts for the dynamic allocator (service: allocator-api) and a compact, repeatable testing matrix operators and QA engineers can run before, during, and after rollouts. It focuses on preserving critical SLOs (p95 latency, availability) while allowing safe degradation of non-critical tenants. The guide codifies:

- The contract language (edges, invariants, and signals).
- A prioritized test matrix across failure modes (capacity pressure, kernel faults, network partitions, API throttles).
- Operator playbook for controlled experiments and emergency rollback.
- CI harness examples and CLI recipes for local reproduction.

Context and goals
-----------------
Problem: allocator-api routes multi-tenant inference requests across GPU pools using heuristics and capacity credits. Real-world failure modes (e.g., stale capacity view, preemption, cross-tenant KV-cache thrash) have previously caused opaque evictions that violated premium-tenant p95 SLOs.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Define deterministic fallback behaviors that are testable and observable.
2) Provide a small set of gates and test cases to verify the contract before enabling a rollout flag.
3) Ensure operator safety: human-in-loop thresholds, automated rollback triggers, and clear owner responsibilities.

Contract definitions (human readable + machine hints)
---------------------------------------------------
Contract v1.2 (summary):

- Primary invariant: premium-tenant p95 <= 120ms for steady-state traffic; when this cannot be met, allocator-api must fall back to model-variant-routing (cheaper, lower-memory variants) rather than evicting active premium work.
- Secondary invariant: best-effort tenants may be queued or soft-evicted but must not exceed a 30s retry window before a hard reject.
- Capacity view staleness threshold: if capacity snapshot age > 7s, switch to conservative allocation mode (no preemption, use overflow pool).
- Safety cutoff: if global GPU utilization > 91% for 15s, start throttling new best-effort requests and set telemetry tag allocator.fallback=throttle.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- decision_priority: [premium, standard, best_effort]
- fallback_action: [model_variant_swap, queue_soft, throttle_new, hard_reject]
- max_queue_time_secs: integer
- staleness_threshold_secs: integer
- trigger_metrics: list of metric expressions (e.g., cpu:gpu_utilization>0.91@15s, kv_cache_miss_rate>0.12@30s)

Testing matrix (owner: allocator-test-team)
-----------------------------------------
Run each test in the matrix in an isolated stage environment with the same operator flags used for the target rollout. Tests are ordered by importance.

1) Capacity-pressure happy path\   Purpose: validate model_variant_swap before eviction\   Steps: create steady premium stream (1k rps), inject burst of best-effort 3x baseline until GPU util reaches 88%-92%.\   Expected: premium p95 stays <=120ms; best-effort requests enter soft queue, queue depth <= configured max_queue_time_secs.

2) Stale snapshot scenario\   Purpose: validate conservative allocation switch\   Steps: block capacity-updater updates (simulate 10s pause) while load remains steady.\   Expected: allocator logs "conservative-mode"; no preemptions; routing uses overflow pool; premium p95 impact < 15% relative.

3) Prefetch-KV thrash\   Purpose: detect high KV miss cascade leading to latency spikes\   Steps: create many short-seq requests to blow KV cache working set.\   Expected: trigger kv_cache_miss_rate metric; allocator sets fallback_action=model_variant_swap for affected tenants; emit event allocator.kv_thrash_alert.

4) Preemption and eviction safety\   Purpose: ensure preemption never targets premium in fallback window\   Steps: force spot eviction on a GPU host; monitor eviction candidates.\   Expected: eviction list excludes premium-tagged tasks unless operator override.

5) Partitioned control plane\   Purpose: ensure safe degradation when control plane connectivity is limited.\   Steps: cut control-plane -> region control messages for 20s while compute nodes remain healthy.\   Expected: nodes switch to local-policy mode; policy logs include last-known-contract-hash; consistency check emits operator-facing summary.

Test matrix table (quick view)
-----------------------------
| Test id | Failure mode         | Expected primary fallback     | Key metric to assert      | Owner |
|---------|----------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| T1      | capacity_pressure    | model_variant_swap, throttle  | premium_p95, queue_depth  | allocator-test-team |
| T2      | stale_snapshot       | conservative_mode, no_preempt | capacity_snapshot_age     | allocator-test-team |
| T3      | kv_thrash            | model_variant_swap            | kv_cache_miss_rate        | runtime-team |
| T4      | host_preempt         | exclude_premium_from_eviction | eviction_candidates       | infra-sim |
| T5      | control_plane_netcut | local_policy_mode             | control_plane_last_seen   | allocator-test-team |

Operator runbook (when a test fails in staging or during canary)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Triage: check dashboard `allocator-contracts/canary` for failing asserts and tagged events (allocator.fallback_*).
2) If premium_p95 is breached > 20% from baseline for > 3m: immediately disable new traffic to the canary cohort via feature-flag `alloc.canary.accept=false` and notify on-call.
3) If queue_depth exceeds configured max_queue_time_secs for > 90s: flip `alloc.queue_backoff=aggressive` and open mitigation ticket.
4) For control plane partition symptoms: promote operator to runbook step `promote-local-mode` which sets `alloc.enforce_local_policy=true` and runs `allocatorctl reconcile --grace 60s` to ensure node-local decisions.
5) Escalation: if human intervention fails within 10m and premium SLOs remain violated, trigger rollback to previous allocator release: `deployctl rollback allocator-api --tag vX.Y.Z` and follow regional failover procedure.

Rollout checklist (pre-merge + pre-flag)
---------------------------------------
- [ ] Contract unit tests added (CI target: allocator-contracts-suite).
- [ ] Integration harness test T1..T5 passing in staging for 2 sequential runs.
- [ ] Canary cohort defined (5% traffic, non-overlapping high-value tenants).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created under `allocator-contracts/canary` and alerts configured (see Alert rules below).
- [ ] Operator playbook attached to the feature flag UI with run link to this doc.

Alert rules (samples)
--------------------
- alert: AllocatorPremiumP95Spike
  expr: increase(allocator_p95_premium[3m]) > 0.20
  for: 3m
  severity: page
  runbook: "See Operator runbook -> triage"

- alert: AllocatorQueueDepthHigh
  expr: allocator_queue_depth_seconds{queue_type="best_effort"} > 30
  for: 2m
  severity: ticket

- alert: AllocatorSnapshotStaleness
  expr: max_over_time(capacity_snapshot_age[1m]) > 7
  for: 30s
  severity: page

CI / local test harness examples
--------------------------------
- Local harness uses `alloc-sim` and synthetic traffic generator `simgen`. Example:
sections.heading: Contract fields (machine-binding)

sections.body:
simgen --premium-rps 1000 --best-effort-rps 3000 &
alloc-sim --profile staging --inject-burst 3x --target-gpu-util 0.9

- Contract unit test sample (pseudo-yaml)
---
contract_id: c01
decision_priority: [premium, standard, best_effort]
staleness_threshold_secs: 7
max_queue_time_secs: 30
triggers:
  - expr: gpu_utilization>0.91@15s
    action: throttle_new
---

Observability and dashboards
---------------------------
Create a focused dashboard `allocator-contracts/canary` with these tiles:
- premium_p95 time-series (baseline overlaid)
- queue depth by tenant_class
- capacity_snapshot_age gauge
- eviction_candidates list (last 30m)
- allocator.fallback.* event stream (recent 100)

Ownership, SLAs and handoffs
----------------------------
- Primary owner: allocator-api team (oncall pager: @allocator-oncall).
- Test harness ownership: allocator-test-team.
- Runtime mitigations: runtime-team.
- SLA expectations: allocator-api must preserve premium p95 <=120ms 99.9% of the time in steady-state. Any change to these numeric targets requires product sign-off and a new contract version published in this doc.

Postmortem and retrospective guidance (if an incident occurs)
------------------------------------------------------------
1) Within 48 hours: produce a short incident timeline and attach failing asserts and test reproducer artifacts to the postmortem.
2) Within 7 days: run a contracted test suite with production-like traffic and publish results to `eng-platform/retrospectives/allocator-contract-breaks-YYYY`.
3) Actionable outputs: either tighten the contract (smaller staleness threshold, lower throttles) or add compensating operator tooling (e.g., automatic warm-up for overflow pool).

Appendix A: quick CLI recipes
-----------------------------
sections.heading: Run T1 locally (bash)

sections.body: allocatorctl verify-contract --contract-id c01 --until 60s
sections.heading: Check contract hash across nodes

sections.body: allocatorctl set-mode --region eu-west-1 --mode conservative --reason "test"
sections.heading: Force conservative switch on region (operator only)

sections.body:
allocatorctl reconcile --grace 60s --dry-run=false

Appendix B: examples of synthetic failure scripts
------------------------------------------------
- capacity_burner.py (python): script that progressively increases best-effort load while recording metrics to prometheus.
- kv_thrash_sim.sh (bash): starts 1k short-L prompt workers to drive KV miss rate.

Document history and governance
-------------------------------
- v1.0 2026-04-05: initial draft by Avery Chen.
- v1.1 2026-09-13: added kv_thrash test (Sara Patel).
- v1.2 2026-11-02: tightened staleness threshold and added snapshot assertions.
- v1.3 2027-01-15: added rollback playbook, updated alerts (reviewers: Diego Morales, Joon Kim).

If you are adding a new automated test or modifying the contract, update the contract YAML examples in `infra/allocator/contracts/` and tag a CI artifact with `contract-hash:<sha>` so we can correlate test runs with deployed behavior.

References
----------
- Related runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026
- Observability pattern: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/token-cost-attribution-and-explainable-trace-playbook-2026
- Test harness repo: git@github.com:redwood/allocator-test-harness.git

Contact
-------
For questions or to request changes, ping Avery Chen (@averyc) and allocate reviewers from allocator-test-team.

payload.page_title: LLM-assisted runbook cookbook and synthetic verification

sections.body:
Overview

This page documents a standardized, operator-friendly workflow for generating, reviewing, and verifying runbooks using LLM-assisted authoring paired with our synthetic verification harness. The goal is to reduce authoring time, improve coverage for edge cases, and ensure runbook correctness via automated scenario replay. This is targeted at platform operators and service owners who maintain platform runbooks for critical services (platform-runbook-service, kv-prefix-cache, tenant-allocator).

Why LLM-assisted authoring?
- Reduces initial drafting overhead for routine failure modes.
- Produces consistent structure and checklists for new/updated playbooks.
- Scales runbook coverage for low-frequency, high-impact scenarios when combined with synthetic verification.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: runbooks for platform operator-visible remediation steps, safe fallbacks, customer-impact minimization for multi-tenant inference services.
- Not a replacement for subject-matter expert (SME) review — LLM outputs must be reviewed by oncall owners.

Key concepts and terms
- Authoring Agent: the internal LLM tool configured with a runbook prompt template. Service: platform-runbook-service, synthetic-lab.
- Synthetic verification lab (SynthLab): sandbox that can replay synthetic tenant traffic, inject faults, and assert expected telemetry and side effects.
- Verification Gate: automated pass/fail gating policy before runbook is marked as verified/published.

High-level workflow
1) Draft runbook with LLM-assisted template.
2) SME review and labeling.
3) Convert to executable test scenarios (YAML) for SynthLab.
4) Run automated verification; collect metrics.
5) Gate: pass -> publish; fail -> iterate.

Runbook authoring checklist (what the LLM outputs must include)
- Title and one-line impact statement.
- Owner and escalation chain (primary, secondary, SRE contact).
- Preconditions and detection predicates (metric thresholds, alert names).
- Step-by-step remediation with CLI/console commands and safety checks.
- Rollback and postmortem triggers.
- Verification plan: list of synthetic scenarios that will validate each step.

Prompt template (example)
```
You are an operator-runbook assistant. Given the service name, SLOs, and a root cause candidate, produce a Confluence-style runbook with: title, impact one-liner, owner_team, primary_contact, detection (alerts/metrics), preconditions, step-by-step mitigation steps (idempotent where possible), verification steps, rollback, postmortem triggers, and a short YAML scenario for the synthetic verifier. Keep steps concise and add explicit safety checks.
Service: {{service}}
SLOs: {{slo}}
Root cause: {{root_cause}}
```

SME review and labeling
- Reviewer must confirm: correctness, privilege requirements for commands, and side-effects.
- Add label: runbook-reviewed:yes and fill reviewer field.

Converting runbook to SynthLab scenarios
- Every verification item becomes a scenario (YAML). The scenario must declare: traffic profile, fault injection points, expected assertions, and teardown steps. Example YAML snippet:
```
scenario_name: kv-prefix-cache-miss-pressure
traffic: |
  tenants: 50
  qps_per_tenant: 2
faults:
  - type: cache-eviction-spike
    duration_ms: 30000
assertions:
  - metric: llm.runtime.token-latency.p90
    comparator: <
    threshold_ms: 120
  - metric: tenant.error-rate
    comparator: <
    threshold: 0.01
```

Verification gate definition
- Gate name: runbook-synth-verify-v1
- Pass criteria (default):
  - All scenarios complete without infrastructure exceptions.
  - Scenario assertions: pass rate >= 95%.
  - No step in the remediation plan causes any unsafe side-effect (defined below).
- Unsafe side-effects (auto-fails): data-loss deletes that are not reversible, mass tenant-suspension, KMS key rotations without approval.

Runbook Lint rules (automated checks)
- Must declare primary_owner and oncall_pager.
- Every remediation step that performs write/delete must include an explicit safety-check command.
- No step can include escalation to customer without the owner tag.

End-to-end example: kv-prefix-cache degraded runbook (excerpt)
- Title: kv-prefix-cache: degraded read latency under small-hotset
- Impact: increased token latency for ~2% of production tenants. SLO: p90 < 100ms, error-rate < 0.5%.
- Owner: Platform SRE (oncall: @sre-kv)
- Detection predicate:
  - Alert: cache-prefetch-latency-spike-v2 firing >= 3m
  - Metric: llm.runtime.token-latency.p90 > 140ms for 5m

Mitigation steps (high-level)
1) Check cluster health: `./platctl cluster status --cluster kv-1`
2) If prefetch queue > 100k, enable temporary backpressure: `platctl config set allocator.backpressure=soft-evict --duration 10m` (safety: requires `operator` role).
3) If backpressure applied, verify p90 drops below 120ms within 2 minutes.
4) If no improvement, trigger graceful tenant-rebalance: `platctl rebalance --target hotset=coalesce --rate 50` (verify in synthlab scenario before production rollout).

Automation hooks and CI integration
- Pull request process: store generated runbook under `confluence-drafts/` and attach synthesized scenarios in `synthlab/scenarios/`.
- CI job `synth-verify` (jenkins/gitlab runner) executes scenarios against a dedicated sandbox cluster and posts results as check on the PR.
- Example CI step (pseudo):
```
steps:
- checkout
- run: synthlab run --scenarios synthlab/scenarios/kv-prefix-cache-miss-pressure.yaml --env sandbox-1
- artifact: results/*.json
- run: synthlab report --input results/*.json --output synth-report.html
```

Operator acceptance criteria (for publish)
- PR has at least one SME reviewer approval.
- CI `synth-verify` job marks gate as PASS.
- Runbook lint returns zero critical warnings.

Rollout and rollback guidance
- When making changes to a published runbook, use canary rollout: announce edited runbook as draft, run scenarios in a canary tenant cohort in SynthLab, then mark as staged.
- If automated verification fails post-rollout, revert to previous runbook revision and open a postmortem.

Escalation and postmortem triggers
- Open postmortem when any of:
  - A runbook step executed in prod causes SLO degradation > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes.
  - Runbook step leads to irreversible change or customer-impacting outage.

Operational metrics to track
- Runbook creation time (LLM-assisted draft -> first SME review). Target: < 60 minutes for common templates.
- Synthesis pass rate (per runbook). Target: >= 95%.
- Operator manual edits after LLM draft: fraction of runs where SME changed remediation steps. Target: < 30% for routine ops.

Security and privilege notes
- LLM prompt outputs containing operator commands must be redacted of any secrets. The CI must run a secret-scan on generated artifacts.
- Change that requires high-privilege operations (KMS rotation, mass-eviction) must include explicit multi-approver flag and not be automatically executed by CI.

Ownership and maintenance
- Service owners are responsible for: keeping verification scenarios in sync with runbook steps, SME review, and scheduling re-verification annually or after major infra changes.
- Platform-runbook-service team maintains the template, lint rules, and synthlab integration.

Appendix: Runbook lint rule table
| Rule id | Severity | Description | Failure action |
|--------|----------|-------------|----------------|
| R001 | critical | missing primary_owner | block publish |
| R002 | high | write/delete without safety check | PR comment + block |
| R003 | medium | no verification scenario | warn |
| R004 | low | missing tags/labels | fixme |

Appendix: Example operator CLI snippets
- Check cluster: `./platctl cluster status --cluster <name>`
- Apply temporary config: `platctl config set <key>=<value> --duration 10m --as operator`
- Rebalance command: `platctl rebalance --target <policy> --rate <percent>`

Appendix: Useful links
- Platform Runbook Handbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/operator-runbook-handbook-2024
- SynthLab quickstart: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/synthlab-quickstart-2025

Contact and feedback
- For template changes: open PR against `platform-runbook-templates` repo and tag `@platform-runbook-service`.
- Questions: ping Maya Chen (@mchen) or the Platform Runbook Service channel (#platform-runbooks).

payload.page_title: How-to: Apply an Optimization Config with Canary (Validate → Canary → Promote)

sections.body:
This page describes the operator workflow for applying an **Optimization Config** change safely using a **staged canary rollout**. It covers:
- Creating an immutable config version
- Validating schema + semantic constraints
- Running a canary (tenant/model/region scoped) with automated gates
- Promoting to 100% (or broader scope)
- Monitoring and documenting the change

This workflow applies to **Hosted** and **Dedicated** (managed by the Redwood control plane). For **Private** deployments, see the Private operator guide referenced under Related Pages.

---
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Use a canary rollout for any change that can affect latency/cost/reliability, including:
- Batching heuristics (max batch size, queue delay, target tokens/step)
- Cache toggles (prefix/KV cache enablement, cache size limits)
- Quantization profile changes
sections.heading: When to use this procedure

sections.body:
- **Low** (single tenant + single model + single region): canary recommended, may be waived in incident mitigation with SRE approval.
- **Medium** (single tenant across multiple regions OR multiple models): canary required.
- **High** (multiple tenants or global default): canary + extended soak required; requires explicit approvals (see Change Policy).

---
sections.heading: Canary requirement by blast radius (default policy)

sections.body:
- `optimization_change_operator` (can create/validate/apply within allowed scopes)
- `optimization_change_admin` (can promote to broader scopes and rollback)

If you cannot see the apply/promote/rollback actions in Console or receive `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, verify your role assignment with Security/IT (see INT-3390).
sections.heading: You must have one of the following

sections.body:
- `redwoodctl` v1.28+ (or equivalent internal CLI)
- Access to the Optimization Rollout Health dashboard
- For quantization changes: access to the eval harness project + the relevant prompt set

---
sections.heading: Required tooling

sections.body:
- **Optimization Config Version**: an immutable record (e.g., `ocv_01J2…`) containing the effective optimization settings + metadata.
- **Scope**: where the config is applied. This procedure uses `tenant_id`, `model`, `region` (and optionally `route`).
- **Rollout**: a staged controller run that applies a config version to a scope at a percentage or shard level. Rollouts emit gate signals.
- **Active version**: the version currently serving traffic for a given scope.

Operational note: all apply/rollback operations are **idempotent**. Retrying the same command should not create mixed worker states; if it does, treat as a bug and escalate to Serving Runtime on-call.

---
sections.heading: Concepts and definitions

sections.body:
1) Identify the exact scope you want to change:
- Tenant: `tnt_…`
- Model: e.g., `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- Region: e.g., `us-east-1`
- Route (optional): e.g., `/v1/chat/completions`

2) Confirm the current active version and capture a baseline:
- p95/p99 latency
- 5xx rate
- throughput (tokens/s)
- GPU utilization / saturation
sections.heading: Step 1 — Prepare the change (and minimize blast radius)

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config active \
  --tenant tnt_4H9Q2 \
  --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct \
  --region us-east-1
```
sections.heading: Example (CLI)

sections.body:
```
active_version: ocv_01J2K8TQ7Q2S5GJZ8ZK2
updated_at: 2026-02-18T21:04:12Z
scope: tenant=tnt_4H9Q2 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct region=us-east-1
```

---
sections.heading: Example output (abbreviated)

sections.body: Create a candidate config file and commit it to the appropriate repo (or attach to the change request). Use descriptive metadata.
sections.heading: Step 2 — Create a new Optimization Config Version

sections.body:
version: 1
name: "batching-tune-queue-delay"
description: "Reduce queue delay and cap batch size to reduce p99 spikes under bursty traffic"
settings:
  batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_size: 24
    max_queue_delay_ms: 8
    target_tokens_per_step: 8192
  caching:
    prefix_cache:
      enabled: true
      max_prefixes: 25000
  quantization:
    profile_id: "qp_fp16"   # unchanged in this example
```
sections.heading: optimize-config.yaml

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config versions create \
  --file ./optimize-config.yaml \
  --change-reason "SRE ticket SRE-2214: reduce p99 under burst" \
  --owner "eng-platform" \
  --labels "batching,latency"
```
sections.heading: Create the immutable version

sections.body:
```
created_version: ocv_01J2M1Y0D6KQ8R2H5C9P
status: DRAFT
```

Tip: keep the version in `DRAFT` until validation passes.

---
sections.heading: Expected output

sections.body: Validation catches common failure modes (invalid ranges, incompatible knobs, known-bad combinations).
sections.heading: Step 3 — Validate (schema + semantic checks)

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config versions validate \
  --version ocv_01J2M1Y0D6KQ8R2H5C9P
```

If validation fails, you’ll get actionable errors. Example:
```
ERROR semantic_validation_failed
- batching.max_queue_delay_ms must be <= 20 (got 45)
- caching.prefix_cache.enabled requires caching prefix store to be provisioned in region us-east-1
```

Fix the config, create a new version, and re-validate. (Versions are immutable; do not “edit in place”.)
sections.heading: Run validation

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config versions diff \
  --from active \
  --to ocv_01J2M1Y0D6KQ8R2H5C9P \
  --tenant tnt_4H9Q2 --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct --region us-east-1
```

Console note: the Diff view highlights “high-risk” fields (quantization profile changes, cache disablement, large batch size increases).

---
sections.heading: Optional: review diff against current active

sections.body:
Unless you have a reason to override, use:
- Canary: **5%** traffic
- Step duration: **10–15 minutes** per step (longer for highly variable workloads)
- Gate evaluation window: **5 minutes rolling**, evaluated every **60s**
- Promote criteria: all gates pass for 2 consecutive evaluation windows
sections.heading: Default canary parameters

sections.body:
These are the standard safe-apply gates. If you need to override, note the reason in the change record.
- 5xx rate: must not exceed **baseline + 0.20% absolute** OR **+50% relative** (whichever is stricter)
- p95 latency: must not regress by more than **10%** vs baseline
- p99 latency: must not regress by more than **15%** vs baseline
- Saturation: GPU SM utilization or queue depth must not exceed configured redline for > 3 minutes
- Quantization-only: eval harness must meet thresholds (see Applied ML doc)
sections.heading: Gate thresholds (defaults)

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config rollouts start \
  --version ocv_01J2M1Y0D6KQ8R2H5C9P \
  --tenant tnt_4H9Q2 \
  --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --canary-percent 5 \
  --step-duration 10m \
  --notes "Canary for batching tune; monitor p95/p99 + 5xx"
```
sections.heading: Start the canary

sections.body:
```
rollout_id: ocr_01J2M24K0QH8X9V6N2TQ
state: RUNNING
current_stage: CANARY_5
```
sections.heading: Expected output

sections.body:
- Control plane records the rollout and desired state
- Runtime workers fetch the new `config_version` and apply it via idempotent checkpoints
- Metrics are tagged with `tenant`, `model`, `region`, `config_version`, and `rollout_id`
- The gate evaluator reads SLO metrics and produces PASS/FAIL/PENDING signals

---
sections.heading: What the system is doing during canary

sections.body:
Open the **Optimization Rollout Health** dashboard and filter to:
- `rollout_id = ocr_…`
- `config_version = ocv_…`
- plus `tenant/model/region`
sections.heading: Primary monitoring location

sections.body:
1) **Gate status panel**
- PASS/PENDING/FAIL by gate type (5xx, p95, p99, saturation, eval)

2) **Side-by-side comparison**
- Canary vs control (remaining traffic) for latency/error rate

3) **Runtime signals**
- Worker apply success rate
- Any “mixed state” warnings (should be 0)
sections.heading: What to look for

sections.body:
- If gates FAIL: the rollout controller should automatically pause progression.
- If you observe clear user impact even before a gate FAIL (e.g., high p99 spikes), manually pause or rollback.
sections.heading: If you see a regression

sections.body:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config rollouts pause --rollout ocr_01J2M24K0QH8X9V6N2TQ
```

Rollback criteria (typical)
- 5xx increases beyond threshold for > 2 minutes
- p95/p99 regression beyond threshold sustained for > 5 minutes
- Any sign of widespread worker apply failures or mixed states

Rollback procedure is documented in the runbook (Related Pages).

---
sections.heading: Pause a rollout

sections.body:
If canary passes and the change is acceptable, promote.

Promote to 50% (recommended for medium/high blast radius):
```
redwoodctl optimize-config rollouts promote \
  --rollout ocr_01J2M24K0QH8X9V6N2TQ \
  --to-percent 50
```

Then monitor again for at least one evaluation window.

Promote to 100%:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config rollouts promote \
  --rollout ocr_01J2M24K0QH8X9V6N2TQ \
  --to-percent 100
```
sections.heading: Step 6 — Promote the rollout

sections.body:
```
state: COMPLETED
active_version: ocv_01J2M1Y0D6KQ8R2H5C9P
```

Important: for broader rollouts (e.g., multi-region), do not “jump” scopes. Complete the smallest scoped rollout first, then repeat per region/model as planned.

---
sections.heading: Expected output

sections.body:
1) Verify active version:
```
redwoodctl optimize-config active \
  --tenant tnt_4H9Q2 --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct --region us-east-1
```

2) Verify metrics stabilized:
- p95/p99 within expected range
- 5xx within expected range
- no sustained saturation redlines

3) Verify apply health:
- 100% workers applied the new version
- no repeated apply retries

4) Verify customer-visible symptoms (if applicable):
- sample requests succeed
- streaming behavior unchanged

---
sections.heading: After promotion completes

sections.body:
Record the following in the change ticket and/or the customer-facing changelog (when applicable):
- Config version ID: `ocv_…`
- Scope: tenant/model/region (and route if used)
- Summary: what changed (batching/caching/quantization)
- Expected impact: cost/latency tradeoff
- Canary duration and results (include key charts or snapshots)
- Gate outcomes (PASS/FAIL) + any overrides and rationale
- Rollback plan: prior known-good version ID and link to runbook
sections.heading: Minimum documentation fields

sections.body:
- Title: “Optimization Config change: batching queue delay tuned”
- What changed: `batching.max_queue_delay_ms 12 → 8`, `batching.max_batch_size 32 → 24`
- Why: reduce p99 spikes under bursty traffic
- Observed impact: p95 -4%, p99 -7%, 5xx unchanged
- Rollback: available to `ocv_01J2K8TQ7Q2S5GJZ8ZK2`

---
sections.heading: Suggested changelog entry format

sections.body:
If the change modifies `quantization.profile_id` or any quantization settings:
1) Run evals for the candidate version (or confirm the eval signal is attached to the rollout).
2) Ensure eval gates are configured and visible before canary begins.
3) Do not promote if eval signals are noisy or missing; pause and resolve signal quality with Applied ML.

Operational rule: quantization promotions require an explicit acknowledgment in the rollout notes (include eval run ID).

---
sections.heading: Quantization-specific steps (additional requirements)

sections.body:
- Insufficient traffic volume to compute stable p95/p99
- Metrics tagging mismatch (missing `config_version` or `rollout_id`)
- Dashboard filter not aligned to scope
sections.heading: Common causes

sections.body:
- Extend step duration to 20–30 minutes
- Confirm metric tags are present in the metrics explorer
- If tags are missing, escalate to Observability (include rollout_id and a sample request_id)
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body: This should not happen. Treat as severity-2 reliability bug.
sections.heading: Workers show mixed config versions after promote

sections.body:
- Pause rollout immediately
- Start rollback to last known-good version (runbook)
- Page Serving Runtime on-call with rollout_id + worker logs
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body:
- Confirm role assignment (`optimization_change_operator` vs `optimization_change_admin`)
- Confirm scope is within your allowed tenant boundaries
- For incidents, follow on-call escalation path documented in the rollback runbook

---
sections.heading: Permission denied when promoting or rolling back

sections.body:
If you are integrating with automation, use the Optimization Config Service APIs (names may vary by environment):
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/versions` (create)
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/versions/{id}:validate`
- `GET /v1/optimization-config/versions/{id}`
- `GET /v1/optimization-config/diff?from=…&to=…&scope=…`
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/rollouts` (start)
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/rollouts/{id}:pause`
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/rollouts/{id}:promote`
- `POST /v1/optimization-config/rollouts/{id}:rollback` (or rollback endpoint; see runbook)

All lifecycle actions emit audit events (create/validate/apply/promote/rollback) with request IDs suitable for SIEM export.

---
sections.heading: Appendix A — API equivalents (for automation)

sections.body:
- [ ] Confirm current active config version + baseline metrics
- [ ] Create new immutable version (include reason/labels)
- [ ] Validate (schema + semantic)
- [ ] Diff review (look for high-risk fields)
- [ ] Start canary at 5% with default gates
- [ ] Monitor gates + dashboards (latency/5xx/saturation)
- [ ] Promote to 50% (if medium/high blast radius)
- [ ] Promote to 100%
- [ ] Verify active version + stable metrics
- [ ] Document results + rollback plan

payload.page_title: Decommission and Data Rotation Security Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
This playbook documents the security-safe decommission and data rotation process for Redwood services and supporting systems. It combines RBAC revocation steps, audit logging and evidence collection requirements, data retention matrix updates, secure deletion and key-management patterns, and incident handling guidance for decommission windows. The goal is to ensure regulatory alignment (GDPR, SOC2 Evidence), preserve necessary audit artifacts, and safely remove access and data across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to decommission of services, environments, storage buckets, model artifacts, logging indices, and service accounts associated with: artifact-store, model-registry, s3-retention-bucket, redis-kv-caches, and ephemeral inference logs.
- Does NOT replace tenant offboarding or legal holds; see Legal Hold procedure before starting.

Definitions
- Data Rotation: periodic overwrite/removal of old records per retention matrix.
- Decommission: final shutdown and removal of a resource (VM, bucket, index, or service).
- Evidence Package: exported audit records, manifests, and checksums required for regulatory audits.

Prerequisites and Safety Checks
1) Verify there are no active legal holds: run: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/legal-holds?env=<env> and confirm zero holds.
2) Confirm owner sign-off: a ticket in JIRA with approval from data-owner and product-owner is required (JIRA project: INF-SEC).
3) Snapshot essential artifacts: manifest of artifact-store snapshot (sha256 checksums) and model-registry version map.
4) Ensure backup retention policy is compatible with target retention window and compliance requirements.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Requestor: raises the decommission ticket and validates service-level prechecks.
- Data Owner: approves retention decisions and legal hold checks.
- Security Engineer (owner): runs RBAC revocation, audit export, evidence packaging.
- Infra SRE: executes infrastructure teardown and ensures secure deletion.
- Compliance: signs the final evidence package and retention update.

SLOs and Timelines
- Pre-decommission window: 5 business days for approvals and evidence exports.
- RBAC revocation: immediate (within 2 hours of start) for non-production secrets; within 24 hours for production service accounts when a staged rollback is required.
- Evidence packaging delivery: within 48 hours of decommission.

Step-by-step Decommission Procedure
1) Ticket and Approval
  - Create JIRA INF-SEC ticket with: list of resources, data-owner, product-owner, KMS key IDs, and proposed deletion date.
  - Attach retention matrix decision and legal-hold verification.
2) Pre-Export Audit Snapshot
  - Export authz logs for 90 days (or configured retention) from audit-elasticsearch:
    - curl -XPOST "https://audit.internal/api/export" -d '{"index":"authz-*","range":"last_90_days","format":"ndjson"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN' > authz-90d.ndjson
  - Run access-list report for affected resources: python tools/access_report.py --resource <resource-id> --output access-report.csv
3) RBAC Revocation (IdP + IAM)
  - Break down changes in two phases: revoke user access first, archive group bindings, then rotate service principals.
  - User access: remove users/groups in IdP (Okta) and confirm via SCIM sync. Example Okta CLI: okta apps deassign --app <app-id> --group <group-id>
  - Service principals: create replacement principal if needed, and rotate keys before deletion. For GCP: gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <KEY_ID> --iam-account=<SA>@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  - Update RBAC audit table: INSERT row in decommission_audit with action="rbac-revoked", actor, timestamp, resource. (Operations team will run the insert using internal tooling.)
4) Quarantine and Read-Only Phase (optional for high-risk resources)
  - Switch buckets/indexes to read-only: s3 lifecycle rule or elasticsearch index block write API.
  - Monitor error rates and service telemetry for 48 hours.
5) Evidence Packaging and Hashing
  - Package exported logs, access reports, manifests into an evidence bundle. Provide checksums: sha256sum evidence-bundle.tar.gz > evidence-bundle.sha256
  - Store evidence in evidence-collector (WORM storage) with metadata including JIRA ticket ID, retention classification, and approver: curl -XPUT https://evidence-collector.internal/store -F file=@evidence-bundle.tar.gz -F metadata='{"ticket":"INF-SEC-1234","classification":"audit","approver":"Priya Menon"}'
6) Secure Deletion and Key Rotation
  - For object storage: over-write sensitive objects using rotational deletes where required and then run bucket-level permanent delete after WORM retention expiry.
  - For KMS: schedule key destruction per KMS policy. Before schedule, rotate keys for any dependent services and revoke access.
  - Perform NIST SP 800-88 compliant wipe for on-prem disks where applicable; document wipe tool and serial numbers in evidence bundle.
7) Verification and Post-Deletion Audit
  - Verify resource absence with automated scans: tools/inventory-scan --resource <id> --assert-absent
  - Run a post-decommission report and attach to the JIRA ticket.
  - Compliance signs off and sets final retention on evidence package.

Data Rotation Schedule and Retention Matrix (sample)
- Log type: inference-audit (token-level) | Retention: 90 days | Action: rotate to cold-tier after 30 days, then delete after 90 days
- Log type: authz-events | Retention: 7 years (for regulated customers) | Action: export to evidence-collector and index-archive (WORM)
- Artifact: model-checkpoint | Retention: 1 year | Action: snapshot + move to cold-store; delete after 1 year unless flagged by legal hold
- Backup snapshot: infra-backup | Retention: 30 days | Action: incremental rotation, purge older snapshots daily maintenance

RBAC Considerations (detailed)
- Principle of least privilege: any user/service not explicitly required for the decommission workflow must be removed from associated groups before teardown starts.
- Temporary elevated roles: use JIT (just-in-time) elevation and ensure time-bound bindings with automatic revocation (Okta PCE and internal-timebound-service).
- Evidence: capture the before/after membership of all groups that lost access and include as CSV in evidence bundle.

Audit Logging & Evidence Requirements
- Minimum audit window to export: 90 days for standard operations, 7 years when regulatory obligations require it.
- Logs to include: authn/authz events, KMS key operations, account provisioning, object delete events, index deletion in search clusters, and tenant-aware access traces.
- Anti-tamper: store exported audits to evidence-collector with checksum and attestations, and record the storage location in the JIRA ticket.

Automations and Tooling
- inventory-scan: verifies presence/absence of resources across clouds.
- access_report.py: enumerates principals with bindings to given resource.
- evidence-collector CLI: redwood-evidence upload --file evidence-bundle.tar.gz --ticket INF-SEC-1234
- retention-sync job: updates retention matrix in the metadata DB.

Incident Playbook (if issues arise during decommission)
1) Scenario: Unexpected access detected post-revocation\  - Immediate action: re-instate quarantine and rotate any compromised keys.
  - Forensics: snapshot current authz logs (append-only) and escalate to Incident Response (pager: #sec-ir).
  - Communicate: update the INF-SEC ticket with findings and schedule a hot review within 2 business hours.
2) Scenario: Evidence bundle mismatch (checksum failure)\  - Re-export the raw logs and re-run packaging. If discrepancies continue, preserve both bundles and create an evidence integrity exception for Compliance.

Verification Checklist (to attach to JIRA)
- [ ] Legal hold check completed and attached
- [ ] Data owner sign-off obtained
- [ ] Authz logs exported and checksum verified
- [ ] RBAC revocations recorded and CSV attached
- [ ] Evidence bundle stored in WORM with metadata
- [ ] KMS keys rotated/scheduled for destruction or archived per policy
- [ ] Inventory scan confirms resource absence
- [ ] Compliance sign-off (name + date)

Appendix: Example CLI snippets and SQL queries
- Export access list (SQL):
  SELECT principal, binding, resource, granted_at FROM rbac_bindings WHERE resource_id = '<resource-id>' AND revoked_at IS NULL;
- Example s3 lifecycle to set read-only (AWS CLI):
  aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket my-bucket --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
  aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket my-bucket --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json
- Evidence checksum: sha256sum evidence-bundle.tar.gz > evidence-bundle.sha256

Owners and Contacts
- Security owner: Priya Menon (pager: priya-sec@redwood.com)
- Infra SRE lead: Marco Alvarez (pager: marco-sre@redwood.com)
- Compliance reviewer: Janelle Wu (compliance@redwood.com)
- Incident Response channel: #sec-ir (Slack, monitored 24/7)

References and Related Policies
- NIST SP 800-88 Guidelines on Media Sanitization
- Redwood retention-policy (internal): /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-policy-2024
- Legal Hold Procedure: /confluence/legal/legal-holds-guidelines

Change Log
- 2025-03-12: Initial authoring by Priya Menon
- 2025-09-01: Added automated evidence-collector workflow and WORM guidance
- 2026-02-18: Revised RBAC revocation timelines and incident playbook

End of document

payload.page_title: How to enable the Optimization Suggestions beta per org (feature flag)

sections.body:
This page explains how to enable the **Optimization Suggestions (batching/caching) beta** for a specific customer org using feature flags.

This is an internal-only operational procedure used by Product/CS/Solutions and on-call engineering during beta rollout.

---
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
The beta is gated by **two controls**:

1) **Console UI flag** (shows the Suggestions entry point, list view, and details drawer)
- Flag key: `console.optimize_suggestions_beta`

2) **Backend API allowlist flag** (permits `/optimize/suggestions` reads for the org)
- Flag key: `optimize.suggestions_api_enabled`

Both flags must be enabled for the org to have a functional experience.

Why two flags?
- The API flag prevents accidental exposure via direct API calls.
- The UI flag allows gradual UX rollout and easy UI-only rollback without fully disabling the service.

---
sections.heading: What gets enabled

sections.body:
**Owners**
- Console UX: Dylan Brooks / Marissa Cole
- Backend/RBAC: Chloe Martin / Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Telemetry readiness: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman

**Approval requirement (beta)**
- At minimum: Product lead (Marissa or Aditya) + Engineering on-call (eng-platform) for the enabling action.
- For regulated/enterprise orgs: add Security review sign-off (Marcus Lin) if the customer requires additional audit evidence.

---
sections.heading: Ownership and approvals

sections.body:
- The org has at least one user with the permission scope: `optimize:suggestions:read`.
- If the customer reports “page exists but empty/denied,” check RBAC first.
sections.heading: A) RBAC / permissions

sections.body:
The suggestions pipeline requires sufficient telemetry to compute estimates.
- Traffic: at least one eligible route with sustained requests (rule of thumb: \~1k+ requests/day over the last 7 days).
- Telemetry: request metrics and cost attribution signals present (route/model, token counts, latency distributions, cache metrics where applicable).

If telemetry is missing, enabling the UI will likely show an “Insufficient telemetry” empty state.
sections.heading: B) Telemetry readiness

sections.body:
Confirm the org matches beta criteria (telemetry maturity + cost sensitivity + willingness to provide feedback). See the beta target list owned by PM/CS.

---
sections.heading: C) Customer eligibility (Product)

sections.body:
Redwood uses **Switchboard** (internal feature flag service) with:
- Web UI: Switchboard Console
- CLI: `rwd switchboard`

Prefer the CLI for auditable, copy/pasteable changes, but UI is acceptable if you complete the audit fields.

---
sections.heading: Where to make the change

sections.body:
- Org ID (UUID) and Org name
- Requesting stakeholder (PM/CS owner)
- Enablement reason (e.g., “Private beta cohort #2”)
- Ticket reference (Linear/Jira/HubSpot) for traceability
sections.heading: Collect the following

sections.body:
`rwd switchboard flags get console.optimize_suggestions_beta --org <ORG_ID>`

`rwd switchboard flags get optimize.suggestions_api_enabled --org <ORG_ID>`

Expected output should clearly indicate `on/off` plus last actor.
sections.heading: Using CLI

sections.body:
Enable the API first to avoid a UI that renders but can’t fetch.

`rwd switchboard flags set optimize.suggestions_api_enabled --org <ORG_ID> --on \
  --reason "Suggestions beta enablement" \
  --ticket "PM-857" \
  --expires "2026-05-01"`
sections.heading: Step 3 — Enable backend API allowlist flag

sections.body:
- Always include `--ticket` and `--reason`.
- Use `--expires` for beta flags so we have an automatic cleanup point.
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body:
`rwd switchboard flags set console.optimize_suggestions_beta --org <ORG_ID> --on \
  --reason "Suggestions beta enablement" \
  --ticket "PM-857" \
  --expires "2026-05-01"`
sections.heading: Step 4 — Enable Console UI flag

sections.body:
1) **API permission**: impersonate an org admin (or use a test user in the org) and call:
   - `GET /optimize/suggestions?project_id=<PROJECT_ID>&limit=25`
   Expected: `200` with an array (may be empty) and `stale_as_of` if present.
2) **Console**: navigate to Console → Optimize → Suggestions.
3) Confirm the page shows one of:
   - Suggestion list (ideal)
   - Empty state: “Insufficient telemetry” (acceptable if expected)
   - Empty state: “No suggestions right now” (acceptable)
sections.heading: Verify in this order

sections.body:
Within 5 minutes, confirm:
- Switchboard audit log has entries for both flag toggles.
- The `#eng-platform-flag-changes` Slack channel shows an automated notification.

If either is missing, treat as an operational issue; open an eng-platform incident if multiple changes are not being audited.

---
sections.heading: Step 6 — Confirm audit logging and notifications

sections.body: Every enable/disable action must be traceable.
sections.heading: Audit and logging expectations (required)

sections.body:
When toggling any beta flag, record:
- Actor (must be a named Redwood employee account; no shared accounts)
- Org ID
- Flag key and new value
- Reason
- Ticket/reference
- Expiration date (beta only)
sections.heading: Required fields

sections.body:
- Switchboard audit log: `FeatureFlagChange` events
- Data warehouse: `audit.feature_flag_changes` (hourly export)
- Slack: `#eng-platform-flag-changes` (best-effort notification)
sections.heading: Where the audit trail lives

sections.body:
Do not paste customer prompts, payloads, or request bodies into the reason field.

---
sections.heading: Do NOT include customer data

sections.body: Rollback should be fast and reversible. Prefer UI rollback first unless there is an API/security issue.
sections.heading: Rollback procedure

sections.body:
- Suggestions API p95 latency regression attributable to the org (or global) and mitigations aren’t sufficient.
- Elevated 5xx rates or repeated timeouts.
- Data correctness issue that materially misleads (e.g., obviously inflated $/day estimates confirmed by investigation).
- Access control/RBAC issue with risk of cross-tenant exposure (immediate rollback; escalate to Security).
sections.heading: Rollback if any of the following occur

sections.body:
1) Disable Console UI flag:

`rwd switchboard flags set console.optimize_suggestions_beta --org <ORG_ID> --off \
  --reason "Rollback Suggestions beta" \
  --ticket "ENG-<ID or incident>"`

2) If needed (API issue), disable API flag:

`rwd switchboard flags set optimize.suggestions_api_enabled --org <ORG_ID> --off \
  --reason "Rollback Suggestions beta" \
  --ticket "ENG-<ID or incident>"`

3) Verify:
- Console no longer shows Suggestions entry point for the org.
- API returns `403` (or `404` depending on gateway behavior) for org-scoped requests.

4) Notify stakeholders:
- Post in `#product-optimize` and `#eng-platform` with org name, reason, ticket, and next steps.

---
sections.heading: Rollback steps

sections.body:
- Telemetry pipeline lag/backfill delay
- Missing cost attribution fields for that project
- Org is enabled but project-scoped query has no eligible routes
sections.heading: Common causes

sections.body:
- Check telemetry freshness and compute lag dashboards.
- Confirm the org/project has events in the last 24h.
- If compute lag is present, follow the Suggestions API latency/error triage runbook.
sections.heading: Actions

sections.body:
- Confirm the user has `optimize:suggestions:read`.
- Check recent RBAC changes and audit log.
- If support needs to request access changes, route through the internal helpdesk workflow.
sections.heading: “User cannot access Suggestions (RBAC denied)”

sections.body:
- Remind: estimates are directional and based on recent telemetry windows.
- Verify the time window shown in the UI and the estimator assumptions.
- Escalate to Applied ML/Optimize only after verifying the org has correct input signals.

---
sections.heading: “Estimates don’t match billing”

sections.body:
| Flag key | Scope | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `console.optimize_suggestions_beta` | org | OFF | Shows UI surfaces in Console |
| `optimize.suggestions_api_enabled` | org | OFF | Allows `/optimize/suggestions` reads |
sections.heading: Appendix: Flag keys and notes

sections.body:
- Always set an expiration date.
- Review enabled orgs weekly during beta.
- Remove/replace flags as part of GA readiness work (per PM-857).
sections.heading: Beta hygiene

payload.page_title: Runbook authoring and maintenance guidelines

sections.body: This document defines standardized conventions, minimum content, and maintenance cadence for runbooks used by Platform Operators at Redwood Inference. It is intended for authors (SREs, Platform Engineers, Operators) who create or update runbooks that are used during oncall, incident response, and routine maintenance.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Ensure runbooks are actionable in the first 5 minutes of an incident.
- Make ownership, escalation, and rollback steps explicit.
- Reduce cognitive load for oncall engineers by standardizing format and signal-to-action mappings.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
1) New operational procedure that must be executed by oncall (eg. graceful cache shard rebalance).
2) A recurring incident pattern with a documented fast-path mitigation.
3) Any manual play that is part of a scheduled maintenance or emergency operation.
sections.heading: When to write a runbook

sections.body:
1. Title and short summary (1 sentence)
2. Service(s) / components covered (explicit service names and team ownership)
3. Severity and WHEN to use this runbook (SLO triggers / alerts)
4. Preconditions / safety checks (what must be true before you start)
5. Step-by-step mitigation (numbered) with exact CLI/API commands
6. Rollback / undo steps
7. Post-incident validation (observability checks, dashboards to inspect)
8. Estimated RTO / RPO and expected impact during mitigation
9. Owner and reviewer (with oncall rotation alignment)
10. Change history and test notes
sections.heading: Runbook minimum schema (required sections)

sections.body:
- Keep the first actionable step visible above the fold. The doc should surface the 2–3 commands an operator needs immediately.
- Use explicit commands (not "run the deploy script") with a code block including arguments. When secrets/KMS keys are required, reference the secret by path (e.g., secrets/kms/ops-tool) but do not include values.
- Use the active voice and imperative form for steps (e.g., "Run: curl -X POST ...").
- Annotate each step with: expected duration, blast radius (low/medium/high), and safety checks.
- Prefer idempotent operations where possible and explain when an operation is non-idempotent.
sections.heading: Authoring conventions (style & content)

sections.body:
---
Title: <short-summary>
Service: <service-name> (team: <team-name>)
When to run: <alert-name / SLO threshold / metric condition>
Impact: <user-facing impact description>
sections.heading: Template (copy into a new runbook)

sections.body:
- <check 1>
- <check 2>
sections.heading: Preconditions

sections.body:
1) Step description
   - Command: ```bash
     <command with flags>
     ```
   - Expected time: 30s-2m
   - Blast radius: medium
   - Safety checks: <eg. check healthy replicas > 2>
2) Verification:
   - Query: ```bash
     curl -s "https://metrics/api?query=up{service=\"<service-name>\"}"
     ```
sections.heading: Primary run steps

sections.body: - Step A: description and command
sections.heading: Rollback steps

sections.body:
- Notify: channel #platform-incident and tag owner
- Run smoke tests: <link to smoke suite>
sections.heading: Post-incident tasks

sections.body:
- 2026-01-12: Minor wording updates (Priya Shah)
---
sections.heading: Changelog

sections.body:
- Primary alert name and runbook link (alert rule metadata must include runbook link)
- 3 quick queries for triage (latency, error-rate, token-cost), with example PromQL/Flux/SQL
- Dashboard panels to check (provide direct panel URLs when possible)
- Synthetic checks to run after mitigation (example curl or synthetic ID)
sections.heading: Observability mappings (what to include in the runbook)

sections.body:
- High error rate triage:
  promql: 'sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-proxy\",status=~\"5..\"}[1m])) by (instance) > 10'
  quick-check: 'curl -sS https://platform-proxy.internal/health || true'

Ownership, review and lifecycle:
- Primary owner: the team responsible for the service (not the person oncall). Use the team alias in the owner field (eg. infra-platform).
- Reviewer: at least one cross-team reviewer when the runbook action could affect multiple services (eg. network, tenant-slice).
- Review cadence: quarterly automated reminders for runbooks that are tagged with the label 'oncall-critical'.
- Review required when: alerting thresholds change, SLOs are updated, or the service release includes behavioral changes to request handling.
sections.heading: Example observability snippet (Prometheus style)

sections.body:
- Small edits (typo/clarity) can be merged to the runbook with a reviewer approval. Record change in the Changelog section.
- Major changes (new destructive steps, changes to safety checks) require a review from 2 approvers including an SRE and a Platform Owner. Mark the runbook as 'in_review' until approved.
- Runbooks are treated as code: store critical runbooks in the infra-docs repo as markdown with a link to the Confluence page and include CI validation (see CI checks below).
sections.heading: Change control and versioning

sections.body:
- Linting: ensure required sections exist and header formats match the template.
- Link checking: verify referenced dashboard/panel URLs respond 200.
- Command safety scan: basic static checks to flag non-idempotent shell constructs (eg. unchecked 'rm -rf').
- Secret detection: fail on inline secrets or credentials.
sections.heading: CI validation checklist (examples to include in repo CI)

sections.body:
- Weekly: oncall engineers may flag out-of-date runbooks in the #runbook-maintenance channel.
- Monthly: runbook owners receive automated emails for runbooks with > 6 months since last validation.
- Quarterly: 'oncall-critical' runbooks must be exercise-tested in a tabletop or live-gameday. Record test results in the runbook's Change history.
- Yearly: archive runbooks that have not been exercised and have no active alerts referencing them.
sections.heading: Maintenance cadence and automation

sections.body:
1) Author and owner coordinate a 30–60 minute tabletop with at least two operators present.
2) Walk through steps aloud and confirm commands produce the expected checks.
3) If safe, perform the primary verification steps in a staging environment and capture logs/screenshots.
4) Record results and update the Changelog and last_validated date.
sections.heading: How to exercise a runbook (tabletop / canary test)

sections.body:
- Alert fires -> Oncall pulls runbook -> Triage (3 quick queries) -> Execute mitigation steps 1..N -> Verify -> Escalate if not resolved -> Run rollback if required -> Post-incident tasks.

Example: "kv-prefix-cache partial degradation" runbook highlights:
- When to run: 'kv_prefix_cache_high_load' alert sustained > 3 min and p99 latency > 250ms
- First step (visible top): Query shard health and redirect traffic to warm shards
- Safety check: ensure eviction backlog < 1000 before redirecting writes
- Rollback: re-enable routing weights to original values and monitor p50/p99 for 10m

Appendix A — Recommended table of metadata (copy into top of runbook):
| field | example | notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| title | kv-prefix-cache partial degradation | short and action oriented |
| service | kv-prefix-cache | canonical service name |
| owner | infra-platform | team alias |
| severity | P1 | mapping to incident response process |
| runbook_link | /confluence/... | add to alert metadata |

Appendix B — Quick maintenance checklist (to paste into PR descriptions):
- [ ] Confirm owner & reviewer fields are current
- [ ] Validate all commands in a staging sandbox or annotate as untested
- [ ] Confirm linked dashboards resolve and show expected signals
- [ ] Add test notes to Change history
sections.heading: Incident-to-runbook flow (practical)

sections.body:
Q: Who can mark a runbook as deprecated?
A: The service owner or Platform Oncall Lead. Deprecation requires publishing a replacement or confirmation there is no active alert referencing the runbook.

Q: Can runbooks include scripts?
A: Prefer inline commands in the runbook and reference scripts in a versioned repo. If including scripts, include exact repo tag/commit and CI badge.

Appendix C — Useful links and templates:
- Runbook template (markdown): https://repo.internal/infra-docs/runbook-template.md
- Runbook CI checks: https://ci.internal/pipelines/runbook-lint
- Oncall rotation calendar: https://calendar.internal/platform-oncall
sections.heading: FAQs

sections.body:
- Primary author: Priya Shah (pri@redwood.ai)
- Platform Oncall Lead: Ethan Brooks
- Documentation steward: Marta Kowalski
sections.heading: Ownership & contact

sections.body:
- 2025-02-10: Created (Priya Shah)
- 2025-06-18: Added CI validation checklist (Ethan Brooks)
- 2026-01-12: Clarified review cadence and tabletop process (Priya Shah)

payload.page_title: Role Transition Playbook: Embedded Contractor to Full-Time Conversion

sections.body: This playbook documents the standardized process for converting embedded contractors, consultants, or long-term vendors into Redwood Inference full-time employees (FTEs). It covers hiring approvals, technical and cultural onboarding, role-level competency checks, IT/security provisioning, compensation calibration, and a 120-day ramp to role parity. The goal is a repeatable, transparent conversion that minimizes disruption to delivery and protects security and compliance posture.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- A contractor has received a formal offer and accepted moving to an FTE role.
- A long-term vendor engagement is transitioning to an internal headcount.
- The destination team requests a full-time role to replace contractor work.
sections.heading: When to use this guide

sections.body:
- Complete all HR and security provisioning prior to first day as FTE.
- Ensure at least 3 documented artifacts and 2 knowledge-transfer sessions exist before role transfer.
- Achieve role competency checkpoints by day 30, 60, 120.
sections.heading: Key objectives

sections.body:
- Hiring Manager: sponsor the conversion, define role expectations, run technical and cultural assessment, and own 120-day ramp plan.
- People Ops: lead offer coordination, background checks, compensation calibration, and new-hire admin tasks.
- IT/Security: validate access changes and complete privileged access approval prior to start date.
- Finance: assign budget code and start-date for payroll provisioning.
- Peer Sponsor (Buddy): assigned by hiring manager to provide daily operational support for first 60 days.
sections.heading: Primary stakeholders and responsibilities

sections.body:
1) Validate headcount and budget with Finance.
2) Verify contractor status, IP clauses, and any non-compete implications with Legal.
3) Confirm eligibility for full-time benefits and relocation needs.
4) Calibrate compensation band using banding matrix and recent comp benchmarks.
5) Prepare offer letter template and proposed start date.
sections.heading: Pre-offer checklist (Hiring Manager & People Ops)

sections.body:
- Standard timeline: 3 business days for initial offer response window.
- Include: start date, compensation, title, reporting manager, benefits overview, probation period (if applicable), and relocation/visa contingencies.
- Trigger items on acceptance: background check initiation, payroll onboarding form, corporate email reservation, and badge request.
sections.heading: Offer and acceptance (People Ops)

sections.body:
- Background check clearance.
- IP assignment and contractor termination/contract amendment completed.
- Any vendor/third-party agreements reviewed such that data ownership and access policies are preserved.
- MFA and SSO provisioning plan scheduled.

Technical and operational handoff (Hiring Manager and Peer Sponsor):
- Artifact inventory: code repos, runbooks, dashboards, deployment keys, vendor accounts. List links and owners.
- 2x knowledge-transfer sessions documented (recording or written notes).
- Create an access de-escalation plan if contractor credentials need to be retired.
- Define first 30/60/120 deliverables aligned to an objective success metric (example templates below).
sections.heading: Security and legal gating (must complete before start)

sections.body:
- HR: benefits orientation, payroll confirmation, and new-hire paperwork completion.
- IT: compute device assigned, VPN/SSO access, standard toolchain installed.
- Security: privileged access exceptions (if needed) validated and logged.
- Manager: daily check-ins, buddy pairing, role expectations and success metrics reviewed.
- Team: welcome intro, stakeholder directory, and calendar invites for recurring meetings.

30/60/120 day competency milestones (examples to adapt by role):
- 30 days: Completed onboarding tasks, executed at least one end-to-end code change or deliverable with review, attended key cross-team syncs, and passed a basic ops/runbook walk-through.
- 60 days: Independently delivers on recurring tasks, demonstrates operational ownership in one area (e.g., monitoring, deploys), and contributes to planning.
- 120 days: Reaches parity with peers on productivity and code quality; leads a small project and mentors others on transferred knowledge.
sections.heading: First-week checklist (Day 0-7)

sections.body:
- Technical proficiency: passes a practical review (PRs, feature ownership, incident participation).
- Process adoption: uses team workflows, ticketing, CI/CD pipeline, and observability tools.
- Collaboration: integrates into team rituals, communicates with stakeholders, and receives positive feedback from buddy and cross-functional partners.
sections.heading: Role parity assessment criteria (used at day 120)

sections.body:
- Contractors converting within 6 months: standard band review; manager provides justification for above-band offers.
- Contractors converting after 12+ months: include performance summary and manager endorsement for accelerated banding if applicable.
- Equity eligibility: clarified at offer time per People Ops policy; vesting start date established in offer.

Examples: First 30-day deliverable templates
1) Individual contributor (engineer): "Deliver a small bugfix or feature with automated tests and deployment runbook updated."
2) Product manager: "Author a 1-page customer problem brief and run the first prioritization triage with stakeholders."
3) Designer: "Deliver a prototype and usability notes; present to cross-functional partners for feedback."
sections.heading: Compensation and benefits notes

sections.body:
- If contractor had vendor-managed credentials, issue new corporate credentials to avoid shared secrets.
- Rotate any keys or tokens used during contractor period on day 0 of FTE status.
- For sensitive systems, escalate privileges in two stages: limited access on day 1, expanded after 30-day review.
sections.heading: Access and credentialing patterns (common scenarios)

sections.body:
- Buddy time allocation: 1 hour/day for first 2 weeks, tapering to 1-2 hours/week by week 6.
- Suggested activities: guided walkthroughs, shadowing deploys, calendar clean-up, and culture Q&A.
- Feedback: buddies submit a short 1-page onboarding summary at day 30 and day 60.
sections.heading: Buddy program guidance (Peer Sponsor)

sections.body:
- If contractor had access to customer data, require an audit of prior access and explicit re-certification before conversion.
- Any unresolved IP or contractual obligations must block offer finalization.
- For visa-sponsored contractors, coordinate early with immigration counsel; do not set start date until visa transfer is confirmed.
sections.heading: Risk controls and compliance exceptions

sections.body:
- Week 1: confirm paperwork, buddy assigned, access validated, first deliverable scoped.
- Week 2-4: weekly 1:1s focused on knowledge gaps and artifacts completion.
- Month 2: 30/60 progress review and calibration with manager and people-ops.
- Month 3: 120-day parity review and final sign-off; determine any ongoing development plan.
sections.heading: Manager checklist for first 120 days (summary)

sections.body:
- People Ops will retain conversion packet (offer, background check confirmation, IP assignment, role activation) in HRIS.
- Hiring Manager must upload artifact inventory and buddy reports to the team's onboarding folder and link to the HR packet.
sections.heading: Reporting and audit trail requirements

sections.body:
- If critical access or security issues are found, notify Security and People Ops immediately; pause conversion if needed.
- For compensation disputes, People Ops and Finance mediate with documented rationale and final approval by Head of People.
sections.heading: Escalation paths

sections.body:
- people-ops/onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026 (for immersive onboarding templates)
- people-ops/role-activation-and-90-day-sponsor-playbook-2026 (alternate sponsor model and 90-day checklist)
sections.heading: Related pages and templates

sections.body:
- 2026-03-05: Created and published
- 2026-03-08: Minor edits to security gating steps and buddy time guidance
sections.heading: Revision history

sections.body: - For questions or exceptions, email people-ops@redwood.com or open a ticket in the People Ops intake queue.
sections.heading: Contact

payload.page_title: Onboarding Tasks Automation and Skill Certification Catalog (2029)

sections.body:
Summary

This document defines the canonical automated onboarding task workflows and the Skill Certification Catalog used for role activation and manager sign-off at Redwood Inference. It describes the end-to-end automation triggers, task owners, competency gates, evidence requirements, and the timeline for 0–90 day signoffs. The goal is to reduce manual checklist work, ensure consistent competency measurement across teams, and provide an auditable trail for compliance-sensitive hires.

Key goals
- Reduce manual manager checklist time by 50% through automation by Q3 2029.
- Standardize competency evidence for role activation so 95% of new hires reach pass criteria within 90 days.
- Ensure auditability: every signoff has timestamped evidence (LMS completion, code reviews, manager notes).

Scope
- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hires (90+ days) across Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and SRE. Excluded: hourly contractors and brief interns (handled by simplified flow).
- Covers technical and non-technical competencies required to be considered "fully activated" for the role.

Ownership and escalation
- People Systems (owner): automation pipelines, HRIS + identity provisioning integrations.
- People Ops (owner): certification rubric, templates, manager guidance.
- Hiring Manager (owner): day-to-day coaching, final competency signoffs.
- Engineering Manager Guild (review): validates role-specific rubrics for engineering disciplines.
- Escalation: if a hire misses 60-day competency gates, Hiring Manager escalates to People Ops and the Manager's Director for an individualized remediation plan.

Automated workflows (high level)
1) Offer accepted (Greenhouse) -> trigger People Systems job: create Workday profile, create Okta identity (dev-okta:group), allocate Slack, license request, and create a Jira onboarding epic.
2) HRIS -> create onboarding tasks in the Onboarding Task Service (OTS). OTS pushes tasks to Slack via the onboarding-bot and to email for managers.
3) Learning Management (Litmos) enrolls new hire in role track automatically. Completion events post back to OTS via webhook.
4) GitHub & Code Access: People Systems creates team memberships and triggers a repository access ticket to be auto-approved if manager has completed repo onboarding checklist in OTS.
5) 30/60/90 triggers: based on hire start_date, the OTS creates manager-review milestones and a calendar invite for the signoff. If evidence is missing, the system adds remediation tasks and notifies People Ops.

Design details and examples
- Event sources: Greenhouse (offer_accepted), Workday (employment_verified), Litmos (course_completed), GitHub (first-PR-merged), OTS (task_completed).
- Idempotency: every webhook includes onboarding_id to deduplicate events.
- Observability: onboarding-task SLOs are monitored on the People Ops dashboard: task completion within 7 days (SLO target 90%), manager signoff within 10 business days after milestone (SLO target 95%).

Skill Certification Catalog (structure)
Each role has a certification track composed of competency areas. Every competency area has: level (fundamental / proficient / advanced), pass criteria, required evidence types, and owner. Examples below show canonical fields and sample entries.

Catalog fields (for each competency)
- competency_name
- level
- pass_criteria
- evidence_required
- owner_team
- verification_method

Sample certification table (text)
Role | Competency | Level | Pass criteria | Evidence | Owner
Software Engineer | Core Coding & Tests | Proficient | Complete 2 paired PRs; 1 end-to-end unit+integration test | Merged PRs + CI badge | Eng Onboarding
ML Engineer | Model Understanding | Proficient | Demonstrate model inference pipeline end-to-end, document KV caching behavior | Notebook + runbook + manager review note | Research Applied ML
SRE | Incident Response | Fundamental | Participate in 1 game day; complete incident triage checklist | Game day ticket + manager signoff | Eng SRE
Customer Success | Product Knowledge | Fundamental | Complete product fundamentals course; shadow 2 customer calls | LMS completion + call notes | Customer Success Enablement

Evidence types (ordered by auditability)
1) LMS completion with timestamped certificate (preferred)
2) Merged code artifacts (PR link + CI badge)
3) Documented runbooks / notebooks with author metadata
4) Manager signed review note (in OTS)
5) Customer call notes or recordings (consent required)

Manager guidance: 0–90 gate checklist
- Day 0–7 (Activate): ensure identity + tooling access, complete security training, enroll in role track. Manager tasks: welcome 1:1, set 30/60/90 expectations.
- Day 8–30 (Foundations): complete fundamental competencies. Manager tasks: schedule paired work, assign first prioritised ticket, request initial check-in note in OTS.
- Day 31–60 (Contribution): complete proficient competencies and at least one merged PR or customer deliverable. Manager tasks: mid-point calibration, determine remediation if missing.
- Day 61–90 (Activation): satisfy outstanding evidence and complete final manager signoff in OTS. If any pass criteria are unmet, escalate per remediation protocol.

Automated manager signoff flow (detailed)
1. OTS generates a signoff summary with all evidence links and a pass/fail recommendation computed by the Certification Engine.
2. Manager receives the summary via Slack and email with a 7-day action window.
3. Manager can accept, request more evidence, or schedule a remediation plan. All actions create an immutable audit record.
4. If no manager action within window, People Ops receives an automated nudge and, at 14 days, creates a follow-up task assigned to the Hiring Manager's director.

Certification Engine (rules & scoring)
- Each competency gets a weighted score. Evidence types have confidence scores (LMS cert=1.0, merged PR=0.9, manager note=0.6).
- Role pass threshold is 0.80 by default but may be tuned per role (e.g., SRE activation threshold = 0.75 to emphasize on-call fundamentals).
- Edge cases: partial evidence is allowed if manager documents a remediation plan and sets new target dates in OTS.

Templates and snippets
- Example automation rule (pseudo JSON, used in People Systems pipeline):
{
  "trigger": "greenhouse.offer_accepted",
  "actions": ["create_workday_profile", "create_okta_identity", "enroll_litmos_role_track", "create_jira_onboarding_epic"]
}
- Manager signoff checklist (text):
  1) Identity & access verified (Okta group, GitHub teams)
  2) Security training complete (Litmos cert)
  3) Role-specific competencies satisfied (see Certification summary)
  4) First contribution approved (PR or CS deliverable)

KPIs and dashboards
- Onboarding Completion Rate (30 days): target 85%
- Time to First Merge / First Customer Interaction: target median 18 days
- Manager Signoff Compliance (90 days): target 95%
- People Systems SLA for provisioning: 95% of access granted within 3 business days
- Tracking: People Ops dashboard, Eng Ops dashboard, and People Systems incident alerts (pager duty).

Rollout plan and change management
- Phase 1 (pilot, Q2 2029): run workflow with Eng New Hires (n=25), collect manager feedback, tune evidence scoring.
- Phase 2 (scale, Q3 2029): enable SRE + ML Eng. Integrate remediation templates.
- Phase 3 (company-wide, Q4 2029): full rollout with analytics and HR audit support.

Accessibility, International hires, and timezones
- All automated emails and LMS content must be available in en-US and en-GB at launch. Additional languages scheduled per regional adoption.
- Calendar scheduling respects local business hours; signoff deadlines are business-day aware.

Security and privacy considerations
- Evidence that includes PII or customer data must be redacted before attaching to OTS records.
- Access grants follow least-privilege and are time-boxed until manager signoff. Permanent repo rights require manager + Eng Platform approval.

Appendix A — Remediation protocol (short)
1) Missed 60-day gate -> create remediation plan in OTS (owner, deliverables, due date).
2) People Ops review within 5 business days and offer coaching resources.
3) If not resolved by 120 days, follow performance improvement timeline per People Ops policy.

Appendix B — Common automation integrations
- HRIS: Workday
- ATS: Greenhouse
- Identity: Okta
- LMS: Litmos
- Ticketing: Jira
- Onboarding Task Service (internal): onboarding-bot service (api onboarding.redwood.internal)

Related pages
- Hire & Onboard Accelerate Playbook (link above)
- Onboarding Immersion Rotation Playbook (link above)

Contact
For questions or to propose changes to the catalog, contact People Systems (people-systems@redwood.com) or People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
