payload.page_title: Operator Decision Frequency and Escalation Scheduler — Playbook & Simulation Kit

sections.body:
Overview
=======

This playbook defines the Operator Decision Frequency & Escalation Scheduler (ODF-ES), a platform-level component and set of operational practices designed to: reduce operator alert noise, protect operator attention budgets, and ensure escalations happen at controlled cadence while preserving customer SLOs. It includes an operator-friendly scheduler, safe defaults, a small simulation kit for validation, and a dashboard spec for monitoring the system impact.

Why we built it
----------------
- Operators were receiving bursts of repetitive escalations for the same degradation events causing cognitive overload and delayed responses.
- We need a mechanism to: de-duplicate, schedule, and rate-limit escalation delivery while retaining deterministic routing for critical faults.
- ODF-ES balances two opposing constraints: minimize time-to-human for critical incidents and minimize operator burnout caused by high-frequency noise.

Goals & SLO alignment
----------------------
- Primary goal: keep mean time to actionable human (MTAH) under 8 minutes for P1s, 30 minutes for P2s while limiting operator interruption frequency to <= 6 distinct interrupting alerts per 24h per operator on-call.
- Secondary goal: reduce duplicate escalations by 80% for the same incident fingerprint within a 10-minute window.
- Tertiary: provide deterministic, auditable scheduling policy and simulation harness for playbook rollouts.

Key concepts
-------------
- Incident fingerprint: a normalized key (service, region, fingerprint-hash) used to identify related alerts.
- Escalation budget: per-operator soft cap measured as "interrupts per rolling 24h". Budget refill policy is configurable per rotation.
- Decision frequency: the minimum interval between successive human-facing escalations for the same fingerprint. Default: 10 minutes for P1, 30 minutes for P2.
- Circuit-breaker: a fast-path that bypasses scheduling for high-confidence, high-severity signals.

Architecture (high level)
------------------------
1. Alert producers (prometheus-alerts, ingestion webhooks) -> normalized event bus (kafka).
2. Event enrichers: attach fingerprint, model confidence, tenant impact, and SLO score.
3. ODF-ES Scheduler: de-duplicates, computes decision frequency, consults operator budgets and routing rules.
4. Notification layer: routed to Slack/PagerDuty/email with per-channel rate limits and grouping.
5. Dashboard and simulation harness for validation and post-rollout metrics.

Diagram (text)
---------------
Alert sources -> Kafka -> Enricher -> Scheduler -> Notifier -> Paging system
               
Configuration table (parameters)
------------------------------
| parameter | default | description | impact if tightened |
|-----------|---------|-------------|---------------------|
| decision_frequency.p1 | 600s | min seconds between escalations for same fingerprint, P1 | faster response, more interrupts |
| decision_frequency.p2 | 1800s | as above for P2 | fewer interrupts, slower reaction |
| operator_budget_per_24h | 6 | soft interrupts cap per operator per 24h | protects operators; may delay noncritical escalations |
| circuit_breaker_threshold | 0.95 | probability/confidence above which scheduler bypasses delay | ensures urgent faults surface immediately |
| group_window | 120s | window to batch alerts with same fingerprint | reduces messages, may increase message size |
| max_queued_per_fingerprint | 10 | backpressure cap | prevents unbounded queue growth |

(Use the YAML snippet below to configure the scheduler for a service)

Example scheduler config (YAML)
-------------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: ODFSchedulerConfig
metadata:
  service: "runtime-prefix-cache"
spec:
  decision_frequency:
    P1: 600 # seconds
    P2: 1800
  operator_budget_per_24h: 6
  circuit_breaker_threshold: 0.96
  group_window_seconds: 120
  routing_policies:
    - name: "regional-default"
      route: "team-runtime-ops"
      fallback: "team-platform-sre"

Runbook: Deploying the scheduler (safe rollout)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create a feature-flagged ODF-ES deployment in staging.
2. Apply a conservative config (P1=600, P2=1800, budget=8) and enable simulation mode.
3. Run the attached simulation kit for 48h against a replay of the last-30-day alert stream. See "Simulation recipe" section.
4. Validate: duplicate rate reduction >= 60%, MTAH for P1 < 12 minutes.
5. Gradually flip the feature flag in canary (10% of regional traffic), monitor dashboards for 2 business days.
6. Roll forward to 50%, validate, then to 100% if no regressions.
7. Conduct a post-rollout review in next SRE retro.

Operator flow: what an SRE sees
-------------------------------
- If fingerprint arrives and operator budget is available: immediate escalation (grouped if within group_window).
- If budget exhausted: escalation is queued and a single digest is sent to the next rotation after the budget refill event, with a link to the running incident.
- If circuit-breaker conditions met: immediate escalation regardless of budget.

PromQL examples for SLO & scheduler metrics
------------------------------------------
- P1 mean full MTAH (reporting):
  sum by (service) (rate(odf_es_mta_histogram_sum{severity="P1"}[1h])) / sum by (service) (rate(odf_es_mta_histogram_count{severity="P1"}[1h]))

- Duplicate escalation rate (10m window):
  rate(odf_es_duplicate_count[10m]) / rate(odf_es_total_escalations[10m])

- Operator interrupt count per oncall (24h):
  increase(odf_es_operator_interrupts_total[24h])

Alertmanager routing snippet (example)
-------------------------------------
receivers:
  - name: "team-runtime-ops"
    slack_configs:
      - channel: "#runtime-ops-critical"
        send_resolved: true
route:
  group_by: [fingerprint, service]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 2m
  repeat_interval: 4h

Simulation recipe (quick start)
-------------------------------
1. Obtain the last-30-day alert export from the alert bus: CLI: 
   $ odfctl export --window 30d --out=alerts-30d.ndjson
2. Run the harness: 
   $ odf-sim --config examples/staging-config.yaml --input alerts-30d.ndjson --out sim-results/
3. Run the analysis script to compute metrics: 
   $ python tools/sim-analysis.py --dir sim-results --metrics duplicate_rate,mta,paging_delay
4. Inspect dashboards (see "Dashboards" below) and the generated CSV to confirm target reductions.

Dashboard spec: panels to create
-------------------------------
- Escalations per fingerprint (heatmap)
- Duplicate escalation rate (timeseries)
- Operator interrupts per oncall (bar)
- Queue depth per fingerprint (timeseries + alert if > 50 for 1h)
- MTAH distribution by severity (histogram)
- Simulation vs production comparison pane

Acceptance tests & validation checks
------------------------------------
1. Unit tests for fingerprint function (coverage >= 95%).
2. Integration tests: simulated traffic shows duplicate_rate reduced >= 50% compared to baseline.
3. Load test: scheduler handles 10k alerts/min sustained with median enqueue latency < 2s.
4. Canary safety checks (automated): no P1 MTAH regression > 50% over baseline in 4h window.

Operator playbook (during an active degradation)
-----------------------------------------------
1. When a P1 page arrives, follow the P1 incident checklist in the standard incident runbook.
2. If multiple operators receive grouped messages, the first responder should claim the running incident in the incident manager UI.
3. To force immediate re-alerting for an in-flight fingerprint (operator override): run CLI: 
   $ odfctl override --fingerprint <id> --action escalate-now --reason "operator-override"
4. If operator budget prevents escalation for a critical-seeming signal, use the incident manager "Escalate -> immediate" button; this triggers an audit log entry and bypasses the decision frequency.

Rollout timeline & responsibilities
-----------------------------------
- Owner: Platform Reliability team (team-platform-sre).
- Primary on-call reviewers during rollout: runtime-ops@redwood.com.
- Q1 2026: staging deployment and simulation validation.
- Q2 2026: canary (10% -> 50%) and runbook practice run.
- Q3 2026: global rollout and postmortem retro.

Retrospective template (to run 2 weeks after rollout)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Summary: what we changed, config values, traffic % rolled.
2. Metrics: duplicate_rate, MTAH, operator interrupts, queue depth.
3. Incidents influenced by ODF-ES: list and classification.
4. Operator feedback: qualitative notes on cognitive load.
5. Action items and owners (deadline).

Appendix: quick links and references
------------------------------------
- Scheduler code repo: git@github.com:redwood/odf-es.git
- Simulation tool: git@github.com:redwood/odf-sim.git
- Incident runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-incident-statemachine-catalog-and-decision-runbook-2026
- Alerting contract: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/alert-context-enrichment-and-priority-scorer-playbook-2026

Changelog
---------
- 2025-11-12 (Asha Patel): initial draft and simulation kit added.
- 2026-02-07 (Dmitri Novak): adjusted default decision_frequency for P1 to 600s; added circuit-breaker threshold.
- 2026-09-14 (Asha Patel): updated rollout timeline and added operator override CLI pattern.

Contact & ownership
--------------------
- Document owner: Asha Patel (Platform Reliability)
- Implementation owner: team-platform-sre@redwood.com
- For security or customer-sensitive edge cases set confidentiality=restricted and contact security@redwood.com

payload.page_title: Evidence-driven offer evaluation and onboarding trigger playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines a measurable, evidence-driven process for offer evaluation and the automated triggering of role-specific onboarding pathways at Redwood Inference. It replaces ad-hoc offer decisions and fragmented onboarding handoffs with a single decision matrix, a negotiation and risk log, and concrete onboarding triggers tied to role risk, compliance needs, and ramp objectives.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Hiring managers
- Recruiters and Talent Acquisition
- HR Business Partners (HRBPs)
- People Ops specialists who build onboarding curricula
- Legal and Finance for offer approvals
sections.heading: Who this is for

sections.body:
- Make offer decisions transparent and auditable using a standardized scorecard.
- Reduce time-to-offer while preserving quality of decision-making (target: 48-hour typical offer SLA from verbal approval).
- Trigger onboarding pathways automatically based on objective signals (role, clearance, vendor status, critical deliverables).
- Record negotiation outcomes and commitments centrally for manager and HR ownership.
sections.heading: Goals and principles

sections.body:
- Recruiter: manage candidate communications, prepare initial offer package, populate scorecard.
- Hiring Manager: complete technical/cultural evaluation, set ramp objectives, confirm L4/L5+ approvals.
- HRBP: ensure compliance with compensation bands and local labor law; finalize benefits language.
- Finance: sign-off on salary above band midpoint + 15% (approval threshold).
- Legal: review for contractor/consultant engagements and NDAs.
sections.heading: Key owners and roles

sections.body:
1) Populate Offer Scorecard (required before verbal offer)
   - Responsible: Recruiter + Hiring Manager
   - Required fields: role level, base salary proposed, equity award, bonus eligibility, reason for hire, candidate score (0–5) across: technical fit, problem-solving, role-specific skills, team fit, ramp risk.
   - Attach: interview scorecards, reference-check notes, and compensation benchmarking snapshot.

2) Automated Decision Matrix applies
   - If candidate_score >= 4.0 AND proposed_comp <= band_midpoint + 10% -> auto-approve (Recruiter/HRBP finalize).
   - If candidate_score between 3.0–4.0 OR proposed_comp between band_midpoint + 10% and +25% -> HRBP + Hiring Manager sign-off required.
   - If candidate_score < 3.0 OR proposed_comp > band_midpoint + 25% OR offer contains atypical clauses -> Finance + Legal review and exec sponsor.

3) Negotiation and Risk Log (template)
   - Fields to capture: candidate_request (text), impact_on_budget (Y/N), manager_commitments (Y/N), date, negotiator name, final decision.
   - All negotiated deviations from the standard package must be recorded and stored in the candidate dossier.

4) Offer SLA targets
   - Verbal offer: within 48 hours of decision to hire.
   - Written offer (signed by HRBP/Legal): within 72 hours of verbal acceptance.
   - Exception path: roles requiring external contractor conversion, export control, or security clearance: review window up to 10 business days.

Offer Scorecard (required fields — flat table representation)
- candidate_name | role | level | technical_score (0-5) | problem_solving (0-5) | team_fit (0-5) | ramp_risk (low/med/high) | aggregate_score (0-5) | proposed_comp_pct_vs_band_mid | approvals_required

Decision and approval thresholds (examples)
- Aggregate score >= 4.0 and comp <= +10% => Recruiter + HRBP sign.
- Aggregate score 3.0–3.9 or comp +10%–+25% => Hiring Manager + HRBP required.
- Aggregate score < 3.0 or comp > +25% => Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor.

Onboarding trigger taxonomy
This section maps objective signals in the scorecard and offer to an onboarding pathway. Triggers are evaluated automatically by the People Ops intake system when the candidate signs the offer.
- Role risk triggers (immediately escalate): access to PII/PHI, admin network access, SOC2 high-impact role. => Trigger: Restricted onboarding pathway (security clearance checklist, 1:1 with Security engineer before first day).
- Compliance triggers: EEA employment, contractor vs. employee conversion, background check flags. => Trigger: Extended HR/Legal onboarding (pre-hire paperwork, local labor compliance steps).
- Ramp-critical triggers: role with measurable Q1 deliverables or cross-team dependencies. => Trigger: accelerated immersion track (prestart reading list, assigned buddy, condensed 30-day objectives).
- Remote/new-country triggers: candidate located outside primary region or requiring relocation. => Trigger: remote-localization packet and payroll/accounting enrollment steps.

Onboarding pathways (short descriptions)
- Core Standard Onboarding: baseline 90-day plan with security training, benefits enrollment, manager 30/60/90 goals and weekly 1:1 cadence.
- Restricted Onboarding: additional security orientation, expedited IAM provisioning, elevated audit logging for first 30 days.
- Accelerated Immersion: preboarding reading checklist, assigned project with narrow scope, daily standups first 2 weeks, weekly deliverable reviews.
- Compliance-Extended: staged paperwork, legal sign-offs, delayed access to production until checks complete.

Manager checklist (first 30/60/90 — condensed)

payload.page_title: Onboarding Security Handoff for Customer‑Facing Hires

sections.body: A focused playbook that defines a repeatable security and data‑readiness handoff for new hires whose role requires early access to customer data, accounts, or PII. Includes timeline, owner matrix, access checklists, training requirements, and audit evidence templates.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This document defines the required steps and owner responsibilities for onboarding customer‑facing hires (Support, CSM, Solutions, Sales Eng, Account Teams, and early-product pilots) who require access to production customer data, accounts, or other restricted resources during their first 30 days. The goal is to reduce risk while enabling a fast time to impact through a clear, auditable security handoff.
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Applies to any role that requires read or write access to customer PII, production databases, live logs, or customer tenant environments within the first 30 days.
- Exclusions: strictly marketing-only hires, contractors with strictly non‑prod access (see contractor onboarding policy).
sections.heading: Scope and applicability

sections.body:
- Customer‑facing roles often need access early to do demos, troubleshooting, or account work. Uncoordinated access creates security, compliance, and support risk.
- This playbook balances speed and control with automated checks and human approvals so hires are productive without bypassing controls.
sections.heading: Why this exists

sections.body:
- Access readiness: 90% of approved hires have required low‑risk access by Day 2 and high‑risk access by Day 10.
- Training completion: 100% completion of mandatory security and data handling modules by Day 7.
- Audit evidence: 100% of access approvals recorded in the access log and associated with a signed manager attestation before Day 10.
sections.heading: Core SLOs (service level objectives)

sections.body:
- Hiring Manager (owner of readiness): submit access intake, provide business justification, perform manager attestation.
- People Ops (onboarding coordinator): track timeline, trigger security/IT tasks, schedule buddy/mentor.
- Security (access reviewer): validate justification, apply compensating controls, approve or deny high‑risk accesses.
- IT/Cloud Ops (provisioning): create accounts, grant groups/roles, enable MFA.
- Customer Success/Support buddy (operational trainer): run shadowing sessions and approve operational readiness.
sections.heading: Roles & responsibilities

sections.body:
1) Low risk: non‑production dashboards, read‑only product analytics, marketing CRM non‑PII fields.
2) Medium risk: internal tooling with customer identifiers (non‑PII), staging tenant access, runbook modification rights.
3) High risk: production customer PII, customer tenant admin roles, ability to modify production customer resources, billing and contract systems.
sections.heading: Access categories (definitions)

sections.body:
- Low risk: Manager approval + People Ops intake -> grant by IT automatically after Day 0 enrollment.
- Medium risk: Manager approval + Security review -> granted after training completion and 1:1 review with buddy.
- High risk: Manager approval + Security + Legal sign-off (if PII) -> staged access with time‑boxed session and audit logging enabled; no permanent write access without 30‑day probation signoff.

Step‑by‑step process (preparing before Day 0):
1. Hiring Manager completes 'Security & Data Readiness' intake form in the People Ops portal with: justification, access categories requested, expected date of first use, proposed compensating controls if any.
2. People Ops opens ticket with Security and IT automatically.
3. Security performs risk classification and returns a checklist with mandatory training modules and any suggested mitigations (e.g., VPN only, session recording).
4. IT schedules account creation window timed for Day 0 or Day 1 depending on complexity.
sections.heading: Access decision matrix (text table)

sections.body:
- Day 0: account skeleton created; manager attestation email sent to Security (template below).
- Day 1: low‑risk access enabled; new hire completes MFA enrollment and baseline onboarding training (security essentials, data handling).
- Day 2: People Ops confirms training completion and triggers medium/high‑risk review if requested.
sections.heading: Day 0 to Day 2 (initial activation)

sections.body:
- Medium risk: buddy shadowing and 1:1 operational signoff required prior to enabling write access.
- High risk: temporary elevated access window can be granted for supervised sessions (session recording and keystroke logging enabled where appropriate). Permanent wide‑scope access requires: 2 week operational shadowing + manager attestation + Security checklist complete.
sections.heading: Day 3 to Day 10 (staged escalation)

sections.body:
- Mandatory: Security Essentials for Customer Teams (1 hr), Data Handling Basics (45 mins), Phishing & Device Hygiene (30 mins).
- Conditional: PII handling and contract‑system usage (for high risk); TPRM awareness if customer access crosses partner integrations.
- Training evidence: People Ops records completion timestamps and attaches to the onboarding ticket.
sections.heading: Required training and certification (examples)

sections.body:
"I confirm that the access requested for [New Hire name, role] is necessary for the business function outlined. I accept ownership for monitoring usage during the initial 30‑day probation and will sign off on permanent access after operational shadowing completes. — [Manager name]"

Operational readiness checklist (must be completed & attached to ticket):
- [ ] Account created and MFA enforced
- [ ] Mandatory training completed (timestamps)
- [ ] Buddy shadowing scheduled (dates)
- [ ] Manager attestation received
- [ ] Security review complete (if medium/high)
- [ ] Audit logging configured for high‑risk actions
sections.heading: Manager attestation template (email or form snippet)

sections.body:
- Grant group (example): rbaccmd grant --user newhire@redwood.ai --group cs-readonly --expires 2026-09-01
- Create ticket (People Ops automation): peopleops-cli create-onboard --name "New Hire" --access "customer-read" --mgr "manager@redwood.ai"
(Replace commands with the equivalent in our internal tooling; automation will normally invoke these steps.)
sections.heading: Examples & CLI snippets (internal tooling)

sections.body:
- Every access grant must include: intake form ID, manager attestation record, training completion artifacts, security review ID, provisioning ticket ID.
- Retention: store onboarding evidence for 7 years in the compliance bucket (encrypted). Searchable index keys: hire_id, intake_id, manager.

Acceptance criteria & signoff (for permanent high‑risk access):
- Operational competency demonstrated (buddy signoff).
- No security exception raised during supervised period.
- Manager and Security both sign the access change ticket. The ticket must be closed with final signoff comments and timestamp.
sections.heading: Audit evidence & retention

sections.body: - Read‑only modes, timeboxed sessions, increased logging, shadowing with recorded sessions, limiting access to specific tenants only.
sections.heading: Compensating controls for early access (temporary options)

sections.body:
1. Manager requests exception via People Ops (include business justification, risk mitigations).
2. Security reviews and issues a conditional temporary grant (timeboxed or scoped).
3. Legal review required if PII handling or contract systems are involved.
4. Any exception longer than 30 days must be approved by Head of Security + Head of People Ops.
sections.heading: Escalation & exceptions flow

sections.body:
- Time to first useful access (by risk category).
- Percentage of hires completing mandatory training by Day 7.
- Number of temporary exception grants and their average duration.
- Audit gaps (missing attachments) per onboarding ticket.
sections.heading: Metrics to track (dashboards)

sections.body:
- People Ops intake form (internal link): /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-intake-forms
- Security training modules: /confluence/security-and-compliance/training-catalog
- Access request automation: /confluence/eng-infra/automation/request-scripts

Appendix A: Example manager attestation (form JSON as text):
{
  "hire_name": "[Name]",
  "role": "[Role]",
  "requested_access": "[Low/Medium/High]",
  "manager": "[Manager email]",
  "attestation_timestamp": "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ"
}
(Attach this JSON as text to the People Ops ticket; our automation will parse it.)

Appendix B: Common pitfalls and remediations:
- Pitfall: Manager over‑requests high‑risk access without a plan. Remediation: require a detailed runbook and temporary scope.
- Pitfall: Training incomplete but access created. Remediation: automation rejects medium/high grants until completion timestamps are present.

sections.body:

- Reviewers: Security (Aisha Banerjee), IT/Cloud Ops (Marco Lopez), Customer Success (Samir Patel).
- Review cadence: annual or on significant product/ compliance changes.

Questions or exceptions: contact people-ops@redwood.ai and security@redwood.ai.

payload.page_title: Interview Calibration and Hiring Scorecard Guidelines

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a single, operationalized set of rules and artifacts for interview panels, scorecards, and cross-functional calibration to improve hiring quality, reduce bias, and standardize decision-making across Redwood Inference. This doc aligns recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops on process, responsibilities, and measurable SLAs.

Scope: Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires globally unless a role is marked as ‘legal/security restricted’ (see Compliance section). Does not replace role-specific technical evaluation guides maintained by each engineering sub-team; instead it defines the wrapper process for consistent evaluation and calibration.

Key outcomes
- Consistent scorecards used for every candidate at on-site / final-stage interviews
- Structured calibration meetings with artifacts stored in the ATS for auditability
- Candidate experience SLAs: responses and next steps timelines
- Centralized metrics to monitor panel effectiveness and hiring bias indicators

Roles & responsibilities
- Hiring Manager: owns the job rubric, defines top-3 success outcomes for the role, selects panel, makes the final hiring recommendation (in partnership with people-ops).
- Recruiter: schedules interviews, ensures scorecards are completed by panel within 48 hours, prepares calibration packet, executes offer logistics.
- Interviewers/Panelists: evaluate using the scorecard, document behavioral evidence, and attend calibration.
- People Ops (Hiring Partner): facilitates final calibration, validates compensation band, ensures compliance with EEO and background-check policies.
- Legal/Privacy: reviews privileged roles and approves any deviations to standard process.

Interview panel composition guidelines
- Minimum: 3 interviewers for final-stage loop (one peer, one cross-functional stakeholder, hiring manager).
- Balanced perspectives: include at least one interviewer outside the immediate team for broad context.
- Diversity: strive for demographic and seniority diversity on panels where possible; document constraints when not feasible.
- Conflict-of-interest rule: anyone with a personal relationship (family or close friend) to the candidate must recuse.

Standard scorecard template (required fields)
- Overall recommendation (Hire / No Hire / Hire with reservations) — single choice.
- Competency buckets (each scored 1–5 with behavioral evidence):
  - Role-specific technical skills (e.g., model-serving, infra, SDK design)
  - Problem solving and system design
  - Collaboration and communication
  - Delivery and ownership
  - Cultural add / alignment with Redwood values
- Candidate risks & open questions (free text)
- Compensation expectation (if disclosed) and interview notes about negotiation constraints
- Interviewer confidence level (low / medium / high)

Scoring rubric and thresholds
- 1 = Does not meet the bar; 2 = Below expectations; 3 = Meets expectations (baseline); 4 = Above expectations; 5 = Exceptional.
- Passing rule for final-stage: median score >= 3 and no competency bucket with median <= 2.
- Clear hire signal: >=3 interviewers with score >=4 and at least two interviewers with high confidence.
- No-hire veto: any documented legal/security concern, or unanimous scores <=2.

Calibration workflow (step-by-step)
1) Recruiter compiles packet: resume, anonymized scorecards (redact demographic PII), coding/system design artifacts, and recommended compensation band. Packet must be uploaded to the ATS 24 hours before calibration.
2) Panel attends a scheduled 45–60 minute calibration meeting within 72 hours of final interview. If panelists disagree strongly (>2 pt variance on the same competency), a deeper technical follow-up may be scheduled.
3) Calibration meeting agenda: 10m candidate recap (recruiter), 20–30m scorecard review and discussion, 10m risk assessment and reference checks plan, 10m decision and next steps.
4) Final decision recorded in the ATS immediately after meeting with all scorecards attached and a 2–3 sentence hiring rationale from the hiring manager.

Decision governance & escalation
- Hiring Manager has the primary recommendation authority but cannot extend an offer until people-ops confirms compensation and compliance checks.
- In cases of tied or close decisions, the hiring manager must escalate to the Business Unit Hiring Committee (BUHC) within 48 hours. The BUHC consists of a senior engineering leader, a senior product leader, and a people-ops representative.
- For executive-level and privileged roles, a second-stage interview with Security and Legal is mandatory before any offer.

Candidate experience SLAs (operational targets)
- Acknowledgement of application: within 48 hours of application receipt.
- Recruiter intro call scheduled: within 5 business days of application passing screen.
- Feedback after final interview (offer or rejection): within 72 hours of calibration decision.
- Offer expiry standard: 7 business days (exceptions handled by hiring partner).

Bias mitigation & structured interviewing rules
- Use the standard scorecard; free-text-only evaluations are not accepted for final-stage decisions.
- Interviewers must record behavioral evidence for any score <=2 or >=4 to justify extremes.
- Avoid hypothetical questions tied to demographic assumptions. Use scenario-based prompts aligned to the rubric.
- Where possible, anonymize early-stage work sample reviews for initial technical screening.

Data, metrics, and reporting
- Tracked KPIs (reported weekly to People Ops and hiring managers): time-to-offer median, offer acceptance rate, panel no-show rate, percent of hires passing probation, diversity funnel metrics per stage.
- Quality KPIs (monthly): new-hire retention @90 days, hiring manager satisfaction score (post-hire survey), calibration variance (average stdev per competency across panels).
- Thresholds to trigger a hiring process review: time-to-offer > 28 days (median) sustained for 2 consecutive months, offer acceptance rate < 65% in a quarter, calibration variance > 1.0 average.

Onboarding handoff checklist (to be completed before offer is accepted if possible)
- Job description final copy and first-90-day success plan attached to candidate record.
- Tools and access list drafted (engineering onboarding owner to attach required infra access).
- Manager onboarding tasks scheduled (first-week 1:1s, codebase walkthrough, security onboarding).
- HR forms queued and background check initiation ready to trigger upon offer acceptance.

Compensation & offer timing guidance
- Recruiters propose initial offer within band and include a short justification memo referencing market data or internal comp-equivalents.
- People Ops must approve final compensation within 48 hours of calibration decision before recruiter extends an offer.
- For high-priority roles identified by the hiring manager and recruiter, use fast-track approval: defined as roles with <7 day time-to-fill target; fast-track requires BUHC pre-approval of band.

Legal, background checks, and data privacy
- Standard background checks: employment verification and criminal background where permitted by local law. Certain regulated roles require additional checks (list maintained by Legal).
- Candidate PII handling: only recruiter, hiring manager, and people-ops should retain full PII. Publicly stored artifacts (e.g., scorecards) must have PII redacted.
- International hires: ensure visa and tax obligations are reviewed with Finance and Legal before offers. For offshore contractors, include contractor compliance checklist.

Training & interviewer enablement
- Mandatory annual interviewer training covering: structured interviewing, unconscious bias, scorecard use, and Redwood’s values.
- New interviewers must shadow two loops before conducting independent final-stage interviews.
- Interviewer performance tracked and remediated if average variance from panel > 1.2 or repeated low-quality feedback (as measured by hiring manager survey).

Exceptions and deviations
- Any deviation from the required 3-interviewer minimum, scorecard use, or calibration timeline must be documented with rationale and approved by People Ops.

Appendices (artifacts to reuse)
- Appendix A — Scorecard template (copy/paste):
  - Candidate name:
  - Role:
  - Interviewer:
  - Date:
  - Competency 1: score 1–5 + evidence
  - Competency 2: score 1–5 + evidence
  - Competency 3: score 1–5 + evidence
  - Overall recommendation: Hire / No Hire / Hire with reservations
  - Confidence: low/medium/high

- Appendix B — Calibration meeting notes template (copy/paste):
  - Candidate:
  - Packet link:
  - Attendees:
  - Consensus decision:
  - Key risks:
  - Compensation notes:
  - Decision rationale (2–3 sentences):

- Appendix C — Example behavioral question bank (by competency):
  - Problem solving: "Tell me about a time you diagnosed a production performance regression and the steps you took to isolate and remediate it."
  - Collaboration: "Describe a cross-team disagreement you influenced to a successful outcome."
  - Delivery: "Give an example of a time you had to de-scope features to meet a delivery deadline — what trade-offs did you make?"

Change log
- 2025-03-18: Initial published version (Maya Chen).
- 2025-06-10: Added fast-track approval guidance and explicit candidate SLAs (Priya Nair).
- 2025-10-02: Updated calibration variance thresholds and reporting KPIs (Liam O'Connor).

Related resources
- See also: Talent acquisition handbook (Talent Acquisition and First 120 Days), Manager interview guides, and the HR compliance playbook.

Contact
- For questions or feedback on this guide, contact Maya Chen (People Ops Hiring Partner) or the People Ops Slack channel #people-ops-hiring.

payload.page_title: Role Activation and 90-Day Sponsor Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines a repeatable, role-based approach for taking a new hire from offer-accept through to independent contributor status by day 90. It emphasizes a sponsor model (an appointed cross-functional peer/manager), concrete activation milestones, manager responsibilities, and integration into Redwood Inference’s performance and feedback cycles.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Reduce time-to-productivity for ICs and managers via standardized activation steps.
- Improve cross-team alignment during onboarding so product, infra, and platform dependencies are resolved within the first 30 days.
- Provide clear manager and sponsor accountabilities to prevent orphaned context.
- Applicable to full-time hires (IC & manager), contractors with >3 month terms, and internal transfers.
sections.heading: Goals and scope

sections.body:
- Hiring Manager (HM): responsible for role outcomes, 1:1 cadence, goal setting, performance calibration, and final signoff on 90-day assessment.
- Sponsor: named peer (not skip-level) who coordinates cross-functional introductions, environment access, and first project scope.
- People Ops (PO): coordinates offer, pre-boarding logistics, and company-level orientation.
- IT/Onboarding Coordinator: creates accounts, hardware provisioning, and access tickets.
- Mentor (optional): technical guide for first 90 days for deeper craft transition.
sections.heading: Key roles and ownership

sections.body:
- Offer -> Day 0 (Pre-boarding, 1–5 business days)
  1. PO sends welcome packet and role activation checklist template.
  2. HM assigns Sponsor & Mentor; Sponsor accepts role in writing.
  3. IT ticket created: laptop, credentials, VPN, email, SSO groups.
  4. Team onboarding calendar seeded (first-week 1:1s, cross-team syncs).

- Day 0 -> Day 7 (First week: orientation & context)
  1. Company orientation (People Ops): culture, benefits, security policy, SLAs for support.
  2. Team onboarding (sponsor-led): tech stack tour, service map, runbook locations, local dev env setup.
  3. First-week objective: successful local build, authenticated access to staging, run a minimal smoke test.

- Day 8 -> Day 30 (Foundational work & impact plan)
  1. HM and hire co-create 30/60/90 OKRs using the included template.
  2. Sponsor facilitates two cross-functional touchpoints to unblock infra/product dependencies.
  3. Goal: deliver a small scoped change or prototype with a documented PR and demo.

- Day 31 -> Day 60 (Ownership & cross-team integration)
  1. Expect increasing velocity on squad tickets; mentor support for architecture/design.
  2. HM runs a 45-day check-in (goals, blockers, career conversation).
  3. Sponsor hands off operational contacts and shift responsibilities for on-call if applicable.

- Day 61 -> Day 90 (Independence & assessment)
  1. HM conducts formal 90-day assessment using the standardized rubric.
  2. If gaps exist, create a targeted development plan (30-day remedy).
  3. Successful activation: owner-level ticket throughput, reliable CI/CD commits, and positive peer feedback.
sections.heading: High-level timeline (offer through day 90)

sections.body:
- Workspace: laptop provisioned, VPN, SSO groups, calendar and Slack access.
- Systems: staging access, service accounts, secrets manager read-only, observability dashboards access.
- Knowledge: README for primary service, architecture diagram viewed, runbooks bookmarked.
- Connections: Sponsor intro calls with product, infra, SRE, and security owners.
- Deliverable: at least one merged PR with test coverage and a demo recorded.
sections.heading: Activation checklist (required items to complete by day 30)

sections.body:
1. Assign sponsor and mentor within 48 hours of acceptance.
2. Prepare a focused 30/60/90 objective template prior to day 1.
3. Schedule weekly 1:1s for first 90 days (first four are mandatory).
4. Provide timely feedback after first demo (within 3 business days).
5. Run 90-day calibration with manager’s manager and PO.
sections.heading: Manager responsibilities (concise list)

sections.body:
1. Host first-week technical orientation and walkthrough of local dev loop.
2. Book cross-team meetings to introduce service owners and dependencies.
3. Provide two short shadow sessions (pair programming or design review) in the first 30 days.
4. Triage access or escalate to IT/PO when blocked.

90-day assessment rubric (scored per area: 1–5)
- Technical proficiency: understanding of codebase, ability to implement changes.
- Operational readiness: knows deployment path, monitoring, and incident playbooks.
- Collaboration: communicates effectively with cross-functional partners.
- Impact: measurable contributions (tickets, features, bugs fixed).
- Growth mindset: receptivity to feedback and learning cadence.
Scoring guidance: 4–5 means on-track or exceeding expectations; 3 requires close manager coaching; <=2 triggers a performance improvement plan conversation.
sections.heading: Sponsor responsibilities (concise list)

sections.body:
- 30/60/90 objective template: SMART description, success metrics, dependencies, owner.
- Sponsor acceptance email (one-liner): "I accept the sponsor role for [name], available for 2x 30-mins/week in first month."
- 90-day assessment form: rubric fields and manager comments.
- Offer-to-Day-1 checklist (CSV-ready): role, HM, Sponsor, mentor, laptop request, security training link.
sections.heading: Templates and artifacts (copy & adapt)

sections.body:
- New hire 90-day assessment results are stored in the employee record and inform the next formal review cycle.
- Managers must incorporate 90-day outcomes into quarterly calibration to align leveling/compensation recommendations.
- Midpoint feedback: HM must provide written feedback at day 45 and record action items in the performance system.
sections.heading: Integration with performance cycles and feedback

sections.body:
- Time off: accrual begins on first payroll; refer to People Ops page for detailed eligibility.
- Security & compliance: complete mandatory security training within first 7 days. Access to production requires completion of production access checklist and manager signoff.
- Remote work: managers may approve full remote arrangements per team policy; ensure onboarding tasks accommodate time zone differences.
sections.heading: Policy highlights for new hires (quick reference)

sections.body:
- If hire is blocked on critical access for >3 business days, Sponsor escalates to IT lead and copies PO.
- If the HM identifies sustained underperformance between day 45–90, engage People Ops within 5 business days to align next steps (coaching plan, extension, or transition).
sections.heading: Manager escalation and safety net

sections.body:
- Mean time to first merged PR (target: <=25 days).
- % of hires completing all activation checklist items by day 30 (target: 95%).
- 90-day on-target rate (rubric >=4 aggregate score) (target: 85%).
- Manager satisfaction with onboarding (pulse survey) (target: 4.3/5).
sections.heading: Operational metrics (recommend tracking)

sections.body:
- Populate Offer-to-Day-1 checklist from ATS on offer acceptance to trigger IT and Sponsor assignment.
- Use badge on team dashboards to indicate "Activation Status" (Not started / In progress / Completed).
- Capture 90-day assessment as a structured form in performance system to enable cross-team analytics.

Appendix: sample 30/60/90 objective template (text)
- 30-day: "Understand codebase X; ship initial fix Y; demo to team; measure: merged PR + test coverage >=80%."
- 60-day: "Own feature Z; decrease bug backlog by N%; measure: tickets closed, customer-impacting incidents zeroed."
- 90-day: "Manage small release end-to-end; mentor a new teammate; measure: successful release + peer feedback."
sections.heading: Suggested automation and tooling

sections.body:
- People Ops owners: Aisha Patel (lead), Noah Kim (onboarding ops).
- Manager resource: People Ops manager playbook page (link in related_pages).
- Review cadence: Playbook reviewed annually by People Ops and cross-checked with Eng leadership; next scheduled review Q1 2027.
sections.heading: Contact and governance

sections.body:

- 2025-11-04: added sponsor escalation paths and access checklist.
- 2026-02-10: updated metrics and benchmarking targets; published.

End of document.

payload.page_title: Cross-Functional Onboarding Playbook for Lateral Hires

sections.body:
Purpose: This playbook defines a repeatable, measurable onboarding process tailored to "lateral hires" — candidates joining Redwood Inference with prior industry experience (senior ICs, managers, and product/ops leaders) who are expected to ramp quickly across one or more functional boundaries. The goal is to accelerate contribution while preserving role clarity, cross-team alignment, and long-term retention.

Scope: Applies to all lateral hires joining engineering, product, SRE, and platform functions. Excludes entry-level/new-grad onboarding and reorganizations where a current employee changes roles.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Role-first ramp: clarify scope and success metrics before day one.
- Cross-functional pairing: early structured touchpoints with adjacent teams to reduce integration debt.
- Measurable milestones: 20/60/90 goals tied to manager and peer-reviewed evidence.
- Asynchronous documentation + synchronous alignment: use written artifacts for context and scheduled live syncs for open questions.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
- Recruiting and Hiring Managers (pre-offer preparation)
- People Ops and Onboarding Coordinators (preboarding logistics)
- Hiring Managers and Skip-levels (day-to-day ramp supervision)
- Buddies/mentors assigned to lateral hires

Quick-start checklist (pre-boarding, day 0, day 1–30, ongoing):
sections.heading: Who should use this doc

sections.body:
1) Draft a Role Acceptance Packet with:
   - One-sentence role summary (what problem you solve)
   - Top 3 outcomes expected at 90 days
   - Critical cross-team dependencies (names/services/owners)
2) Confirm relocation/visa needs and timeline with People Ops.
3) Agree on the "20/60/90" success metrics and deliverables.
4) Identify buddy (peer in adjacent team) and calendar 1:1s for first 30 days.

Pre-boarding (People Ops / IT, 1–7 days before start):
- Provision accounts: GitHub, Jira, internal docs, Slack, Okta, calendar.
- Ship welcome kit and hardware; include seat/office access instructions if on-site.
- Share Role Acceptance Packet and 20/60/90 goals with hire and manager.
- Create first-week schedule: orientation, team kickoff, and two cross-team introductions.

Day 0–7 (On-site or remote first week):
- Orientation: benefits, payroll, security, code of conduct (People Ops).
- Manager 1:1: confirm first 30-day priorities and communication norms.
- Buddy sessions: 30–60 minute walkthroughs of day-to-day tools and patterns.
- Quick wins: assign a low-risk, high-value task that touches production or docs.

0–30 Days (Ramp foundations):
- Deliverables: complete the quick win, write a runbook or design note for the first area touched.
- Meetings: weekly manager 1:1, two cross-functional syncs, onboarding retro at day 30.
- Evidence of progress: merged PR, test coverage, or customer/partner feedback.

30–60 Days (Cross-functional integration):
- Deliverables: owner of a small feature or stabilization initiative; present a 15-minute walkthrough to related teams.
- Meetings: biweekly stakeholder demos; alignment meeting with product/infra owners.

payload.page_title: Offer Acceptance to Autonomy: Accelerated Pathways for New Hires

sections.body:
Overview:
This playbook defines an accelerated offering for select new hires and internal transfers that aims to shorten the time from offer acceptance to role autonomy (target: 90 days). It contains eligibility criteria, manager and People Ops responsibilities, a week-by-week manager checklist, feedback cadence, contractor-to-perm conversion guidance, and sample templates. The goal is predictable outcomes: clarity of expectations, measurable ramp metrics, and reduced time-to-impact without sacrificing quality or fairness.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Individual contributors across Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and Design; excludes executive hires, heavily regulated roles (security/infosec-senior), and roles requiring multi-week facility onboarding.
- Audience: Hiring managers, people-partners, new hire buddy/mentors, hiring coordinators, and L4+ managers approving accelerated pathways.

Why an accelerated pathway?
- Market realities: high demand for senior ICs and internal mobility pressure require faster impact windows.
- Business impact: shorten time-to-first-feature/first-customer-impact to improve velocity and reduce cost per hire.
- Candidate experience: a structured fast path reduces ambiguity for candidates who can onboard quickly.

Eligibility (must meet all):
1) Candidate type: external hire with 5+ years experience in comparable domain OR internal transferee with documented successful performance in previous role.
2) Hiring signal: hiring manager attests readiness with a short rubric (see "Manager Attestation" below).
3) Role readiness: onboarding content, environment access, and at least one low-risk initial project pre-defined in the role requisition.
4) Compensation & compliance: offer banded within target range and background checks complete before start.

Manager Attestation (required at offer stage):
- One-paragraph justification of candidate’s propulsion to autonomy (skills + prior similar context).
- A named buddy/mentor and initial project with success criteria.
- Expected 30/60/90 deliverables.

Target metrics (example SLOs people-ops will monitor):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (Engineering): 7 days (target), 14 days (max)
- First customer-facing doc/demo (Product/CS): 14 days (target)
- Ramp score (manager-run weekly rubric): achieve >= 3/5 by day 60 and >= 4/5 by day 90
- Access completeness: 95% of required systems provisioned by day 1

Accelerated Pathway Responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager:
  - Submit Manager Attestation at offer stage.
  - Define project and success criteria in job requisition prior to offer.
  - Schedule onboarding calendar for weeks 1–4 before start date.
  - Hold weekly 1:1s focused on ramp metrics (explicit agenda template below).
- People Ops (Talent Partner):
  - Validate eligibility, approve accelerated flag, and add "Accelerated" tag to People Ops dashboard.
  - Coordinate cross-functional access provisioning (IT, security, infra).
  - Assign central onboarding checkpoint at day 7, 30, 60, and 90 to audit and escalate missing items.
- Buddy/Mentor:
  - Hold daily drop-in support first week and three office hours/week until day 30.
  - Run hands-on sessions for codebase/processes.

Manager checklist (accelerated timeline) — week-by-week highlights:
- Pre-start (at offer acceptance):
  1) Finalize Manager Attestation and initial project scope (one paragraph, success metrics).
  2) Provision an onboarding calendar and invite core stakeholders.
  3) Ensure documentation pointers and reading list are ready.
- Week 1: Foundation
  - Day 0–1: Welcome, hardware/access check, team intro, set up dev environment or product accounts.
  - Day 2–5: Pairing sessions, first small task assigned (clear acceptance criteria).
  - End of week 1: 30-minute manager checkpoint (barometer: morale, blockers, access).
- Week 2: Deliverability
  - Assign the first scoped deliverable with clear owner and review gates.
  - Buddy runs three focused walkthroughs (codebase, infra, product flows).
  - Manager sends mid-point note to people-partner confirming progress.
- Week 3–4: Consolidation
  - First deliverable review and merge/ship.
  - 1:1 focused on engineering/process deep dive and growth expectations.
  - Confirm training completion (security, data handling, compliance).
- Weeks 5–8: Expansion
  - Increase ticket complexity; introduce cross-team stakeholders.
  - Manager-run calibrated feedback at day 30 with written summary; people-partner added as reviewer.
- Weeks 9–12: Autonomy push
  - Candidate owns at least one end-to-end workflow or feature.
  - Final ramp review at day 90 documenting outcome: autonomous | needs-extension | transition-out.

Feedback and performance cadence (structured):
1) Weekly short-form ramp note (manager): 6 questions (progress, blockers, risks, confidence, next steps, support needed).
2) 30-day written checkpoint: manager + people-partner + hire signoff on progress against 30-day deliverables.
3) 60-day calibrations: optional peer input for cross-functional roles.
4) 90-day formal ramp review: final decision with one of three outcomes.

90-day outcomes and next steps:
- Autonomous: hire moves to standard performance cycle; manager creates development plan and schedules 1:1 cadence.
- Needs-extension (30 days): defined extension with concrete milestones and weekly scorecards; additional learning resources assigned.
- Transition-out: rare and documented with HR partner; offers internal redeployment or managed offboarding.

Contractor -> Permanent conversion pathway (accelerated variant):
- Eligibility: contractor has >= 6 months tenure and positive mid-contract review.
- Process summary: manager recommends conversion -> people-partner evaluates role budget and banding -> formal offer within 30 days -> conversion start-date aligned to payroll cycle.
- Conversion evaluation components: deliverables, peer feedback, security clearance, and compensation mapping.

Decision points & risk mitigation:
- If access is delayed > 3 business days: initiate critical access escalation to Infrastructure & Security with SLA of 48 hours.
- If early deliverable delayed: manager to de-scope non-critical work and adjust acceptance criteria; escalate to people-partner if recovery not seen in 7 days.
- For high-risk hires (systems with PII/PHI), default to standard 120-day onboarding unless security signs off.

Templates & examples:
- Manager Attestation (one-paragraph):
  "I confirm that Jane Doe has prior product infra experience in a codebase of similar scale, will be paired with Sam Patel as a buddy, and will own the telemetry ingestion POC (success = ingest 100k events/min in staging and owned PR merged). Expected 30/60/90 deliverables attached."

- Weekly ramp note template (email/Confluence blurb):
  "Week X Ramp Note:
   - Progress: 
   - Blockers: 
   - Risks: 
   - Confidence (1-5): 
   - Next steps: 
   - Support needed:"

- Sample onboarding calendar (text table):
  | Day | Focus | Owner | Success criteria |
  |-----|-------|-------|------------------|
  | 0   | Welcome + access | Manager/IT | Accounts provisioned |
  | 2   | Dev environment | Buddy/Infra | First app runs locally |
  | 7   | First small task | Manager | PR opened |
  | 30  | First project review | Manager + PeopleOps | Project accepted |
  | 90  | Ramp review | Manager + PeopleOps | Autonomous / extension decision |

- Example requisition JSON (for hiring coordinators) — add into ATS when flagging accelerated:
  "{ "position": "Senior Backend Engineer", "accelerated_onboarding": true, "initial_project": "telemetry-ingest-poc" }"
Ownership and escalation:
- People Ops: process owner — Sofia Martinez (people-ops).
- Manager: responsible for day-to-day ramping and final recommendation.
- Escalation path: Manager -> People Partner -> Head of People Ops -> Director of the hiring org.

Equity and fairness considerations:
- Accelerated pathway is optional and available to eligible hires; non-accelerated hires receive the standard 120-day onboarding plan.
- All candidates receive consistent scoring rubrics; managers must document rationale to avoid bias.
- People Ops will audit accelerated cases quarterly for demographic parity and outcome variance.

Measurement and reporting (People Ops Dashboard):
- Quarterly KPIs tracked: % hires on accelerated pathway, median time-to-first-merge, % autonomous at day 90, accelerated vs standard attrition at 6 months.
- Review cadence: monthly People Ops dashboard review; quarterly leadership review.

Appendix: quick checklists
- Pre-start checklist (for hiring coordinator): Offer accepted, background completed, Manager Attestation filed, onboarding calendar created, buddy assigned, accelerated tag added to ATS.
- Day 1 checklist (manager): Welcome note, environment verification, 1:1 scheduled, first task assigned, invite to team channel.

Related documents and links:
- Onboarding immersion rotation playbook (internal link)
- Interview calibration and hiring scorecard (internal link)
- Manager 1:1 and feedback guide (internal link)

Last updated notes:
- Changes in this version (2027-01-15): tightened eligibility for high-risk roles, added contractor->perm accelerated steps, introduced mandatory People Ops checkpoints at days 7 and 60.

Contact:
- People Ops owner: Sofia Martinez, sofia.martinez@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Skills Banking and Hiring Forecast Playbook

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook standardizes how Redwood forecasts headcount needs and maintains a living "skills bank" of internal talent and stretch-ready candidates to reduce time-to-fill, improve role fit, and optimize hiring spend. The playbook covers quarterly forecast rhythms, the skills bank data model and maintenance, intake templates, approval gates, and post-hire follow-up that ties into performance and onboarding cycles.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hiring requests across engineering, product, and GTM functions.
- Does not replace team-level hiring approvals but provides a single canonical forecast and a prioritized queue for DRIs (directly responsible individuals).

Goals
- Reduce external hiring time-to-fill by 25% within 12 months by improving internal match rates and forecast accuracy.
- Increase internal mobility fills to 18% of total hires for roles that map cleanly to existing job families.
- Provide finance and recruiting with a rolling 6-quarter demand forecast and a 12-month skills hedge.

Definitions
- Skills Bank: A searchable inventory of internal employees and alumni who have recorded skill tags, stretch readiness, and availability windows.
- Hiring Forecast: A rolling forecast document (quarterly) of open roles, expected start windows, impact priority, and budget posture.
- Role Readiness Level (RRL): A 1–5 scale indicating how close an internal candidate is to performing at target for the role (1 = no overlap, 5 = ready to transition).

Ownership and Roles
- People Ops (Forecast Owner): Maintains the forecast cadence and publishes the rolling document.
- Hiring Manager (Requester): Completes intake, defines success metrics and ramp timeline.
- Recruiting: Provides time-to-fill estimates and sourcing plans; updates status in the queue.
- Finance: Signs off on budget exposure per quarter for committed hires.
- Mobility Panel (ad hoc): Reviews internal matches and recommends stretch assignments.

Quarterly Forecast Rhythm (Canonical Process)
1. Forecast Kickoff (weeks 1–2 of quarter)
   - Hiring managers submit role intents using the intake template (see below).
   - People Ops consolidates inputs and publishes a draft forecast to the leadership channel.
2. Prioritization Workshop (week 2)
   - Panel: People Ops, Recruiting Lead, Finance, 2 product/eng reps.
   - Output: Prioritized roster (A/B/C) and recommended hiring quarters.
3. Budget Gate (week 3)
   - Finance confirms budget for A and prioritized B items; unapproved items moved to the next quarter or paused.
4. Source Planning (week 3–4)
   - Recruiting assigns sourcers for approved items; internal mobility candidates pulled from Skills Bank first.
5. Execution & Rolling Review
   - Status updated weekly; forecast re-run mid-quarter if >20% change in committed headcount.

Intake Template (required fields)
| Field | Guidance |
| Role Title | Nominal title aligned to job family |
| Team | Team name and manager |
| Impact Priority (A/B/C) | A = mission critical this quarter |
| Target Start Quarter | e.g., Q4 2026 |
| Minimum Qualifications | Must-have skills |
| Preferred Qualifications | Nice-to-have or stretch skills |
| Ramp Metric | Specific metric for 90-day success (e.g., feature delivery, infra onboarding task) |
| Budget Code | Finance cost center |
| Internal Match Allowed | yes/no |

Approval Workflow (summary)
1. Hiring manager completes intake in People Ops form.
2. Recruiting validates time-to-fill and suggests sourcing mix.
3. Prioritization workshop assigns queue position.
4. Finance signs budget gate for A/B items.
5. Recruiting posts role; internal mobility candidates notified.

Skills Bank: Data Model and Maintenance
- Core attributes: employee_id, name, primary_team, job_family, skill_tags (list), RRL (1–5), last_updated, availability_window, coach/mentor, preferred_location.
- Ownership: Each manager confirms their team members' skills quarterly. People Ops performs a verification sweep during performance cycles.
- Update triggers: role change, end of project, 6-month cadence, or when an employee expresses mobility interest.

Search & Match Rules
- Exact match: RRL >= 4 and skill_tags cover >= 80% of required tags.
- Stretch match: RRL 2–3 with recorded mentor and 60–80% tag overlap; requires a 30–60 day development plan before start.
- Disqualification: RRL 1 or gaps in fundamental certifications for regulated roles (e.g., SOC/PDC-required).

Example Skills Bank JSON record (for Recruiting/Engineering tools)
{
  "employee_id": "E-11472",
  "name": "Nguyen Tran",
  "primary_team": "serving-runtime",
  "job_family": "infra_engineering",
  "skill_tags": ["CUDA","kernel-opt","python","profiling"],
  "RRL": "4",
  "last_updated": "2025-11-02",
  "availability_window": "Q1 2026",
  "coach": "Samira Ortiz"
}

Note: The above object is a canonical snippet; actual Skills Bank is stored in the HRIS + People Ops managed DB. Recruiting tools will sync a read-only subset nightly.

Internal Mobility Process
- Notification: When a role is posted, People Ops sends a digest to employees who match tags and have RRL >= 2.
- Mobility Panel Review: For RRL 2–3, a 30-minute panel (manager, receiving manager, mobility rep) sets a development plan and timeline.
- Transition Options: 1) Immediate transfer (RRL 4–5) with 2-week cross-training; 2) Stretch assignment (RRL 2–3) with 30–60 day upskilling and conditional transfer; 3) Mentored trial (part-time) for critical hires.

Onboarding & Post-Hire Linkage
- Each forecasted hire must define a 30/60/90 success plan at offer acceptance time. That plan becomes part of the onboarding checklist and the first manager 1:1 agenda items.
- Recruit-to-onboard handoff checklist (required to mark role as "Started"):
  - Offer accepted and paperwork complete
  - Cost center assigned and payroll initiated
  - New hire 30/60/90 plan uploaded to People Ops portal
  - Assigned mentor identified and calendar invites sent
  - Access list and critical systems provisioning requested (see Security handoff)

Metrics and Reporting (examples)
- Forecast accuracy: % of hires that start in the quarter they were forecasted. Target: 85%.
- Internal fill rate: % of roles filled by internal candidates. Target: 18%.
- Average time-to-fill for A-priority roles: target < 35 days.
- Skills Bank freshness: % of records updated in the last 180 days. Target: 90%.

Audit, Compliance and Data Handling
- Skills Bank contains personal data; retention and access follow the Data Management policy. Access limited to People Ops, Recruiting, managers, and authorized mobility panel members.
- Quarterly audit: People Ops runs a permissions report and an accuracy sample (20% of records) and publishes a short remediation report.

Manager Checklist (for hiring managers)
- Complete intake with clear success metrics.
- Confirm internal matches and discuss with Mobility Panel before external posting.
- Define ramp goals and 30/60/90 success signals at offer.
- Participate in the prioritization workshop and provide timely clarifications.

Playbook Exceptions and Edge Cases
- Emergency hires (business-critical, <14 days to fill) can bypass normal prioritization but must be ratified by VP People Ops and Finance within one week of start.
- Regulated roles requiring background certifications (legal/security) will have an additional compliance gate and a dedicated audit trail.

Change Log
- 2025-08-15: Initial draft and pilot with infra and product organizations.
- 2025-11-02: Skills Bank schema updated; added RRL definitions and stretch-match rules.
- 2026-01-20: Published playbook; targets and metrics added.

Related References
- Talent Intake & Role Certification (link internal): /confluence/people-ops/talent-intake-and-role-certification-protocol-2028
- Requisition to Ramp Runbook: /confluence/people-ops/requisition-to-ramp-hiring-velocity-and-budget-approval-runbook-2026
- Data Management policy: /confluence/policies-and-process/data-management

Contact
- People Ops Forecast Owner: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.example)
- Recruiting Lead: Carlos Mendes (carlos.mendes@redwood.example)

payload.page_title: Role Activation — Failure Mode Analysis and Recovery Playbook

sections.body:
Summary

Purpose: This playbook documents the common failure modes that delay or block role activation (the state where a new hire has full access, assigned mentor, and first-week objectives) and prescribes step-by-step recovery actions, ownership, SLAs, and escalation paths. Use this doc when an activation milestone is missed or when recurring failure patterns are identified.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time, contractor, and intern hires across engineering, product, and GTM who require cross-functional provisioning (accounts, desk equipment, manager/mentor pairing).
- Excludes contractors on short-term task-only engagements that follow a separate light-onboarding checklist.

Expected outcomes
- Restore a blocked activation within defined SLAs.
- Capture root cause and action items to prevent recurrence.
- Update metric dashboards for Time-to-Activation and Activation Success Rate.

Key definitions
- Role Activation: New hire has (a) corporate account & required service accounts; (b) equipment assigned; (c) manager and mentor assigned; (d) Day-1 and Week-1 objectives visible in LMS/OKR tool.
- Activation Failure: Any event causing Role Activation to exceed 7 business days or miss required Day-1 deliverables.

Ownership and responsibilities
- People Ops (Onboarding Team): Primary owner for provisioning coordination, SLA tracking, and first escalation. (Contact: onboarding@redwood.com)
- IT/Cloud Access (Infra): Responsible for cloud accounts, VPN/VPC access, service accounts, MFA enforcement and device imaging.
- Hiring Manager: Responsible for mentor assignment, role-specific access approvals, and first-week objectives.
- Facilities/Hardware Ops: Device procurement and physical provisioning.
- Security: Clearances, privileged access approvals, and KBA where required.

Activation SLAs and metrics
(Goal: measure and enforce predictable activations)

SLA table
| Metric | Target | Escalation threshold | Owner | Notes |
|--------|--------|----------------------|-------|-------|
| Time-to-Activation (full) | <= 7 business days (95% of hires) | 5 business days | People Ops | Start timer at offer acceptance + signed I-9/equivalent where applicable |
| Account Provisioning (corporate) | <= 2 business days | 2 business days | IT/Cloud Access | Includes email, SSO, device enrollment |
| Cloud Service Access (role-specific) | <= 5 business days | 3 business days | IT/Cloud Access + Manager | Approvals often require manager action; track via access-request ticket |
| Equipment Delivery | <= 5 business days (US) | 3 business days | Facilities/Hardware Ops | International shipping windows vary; document exceptions |
| Mentor Assignment | <= 3 business days | 3 business days | Hiring Manager | If not assigned, People Ops assigns temporary buddy |

Operational metrics to report weekly
- Activation Success Rate (30d rolling)
- Median Time-to-Activation
- Number of incidents per cohort that triggered this playbook
- Top 3 recurring root causes

Common failure modes and recovery steps
1) Missing or delayed corporate account provisioning
- Symptoms: No SSO account, cannot access email or Slack, identity provider shows "pending".
- Immediate triage (first 30 minutes): People Ops confirms identity docs present in HRIS and that provisioning ticket exists. Capture ticket ID and timestamp.
- Recovery steps:
  a) People Ops opens priority ticket with IT/Cloud Access and tags "activation-critical".
  b) IT validates SSO config and forces provisioning; if tenant limit reached, IT notifies Cloud Access lead.
  c) If device-dependent (device not imaged) provide temporary web-based workstation and escalate device shipment.
- Owner: IT/Cloud Access (primary), People Ops (coordinator)
- Post-mortem: Update provisioning checklist and track whether a human approval step was the blocker.

2) Manager/mentor not assigned or unavailable
- Symptoms: New hire has no scheduled check-in, no day-1 objectives.
- Immediate triage: People Ops pings hiring manager; if no response in 4 business hours, People Ops assigns an interim buddy from the team schedule.
- Recovery steps:
  a) People Ops uses 'Manager Escalation Matrix' to reach manager's backup.
  b) Assign interim mentor and schedule day-1 intro.
  c) Notify manager that failure to assign repeatedly will trigger manager coaching and a note in performance calibration.
- Owner: Hiring Manager (primary), People Ops (escalation executor)

3) Privileged/cloud access approval stalled by security review
- Symptoms: Access ticket in "awaiting security review" for >48 hours.
- Immediate triage: People Ops/IT opens a policy exception request or temporary least-privilege access with an expiration (48–72 hours).
- Recovery steps:
  a) Security toggles temporary access with strict monitoring and requirement to submit required docs within 72 hours.
  b) People Ops schedules a compliance check and documents the exception with justification.
- Owner: Security (approver), IT (implementation), People Ops (documentation)

4) Hardware or shipping delays (international hires)
- Symptoms: Device delivery delayed beyond expected window, customs hold, or lost shipment.
- Immediate triage: Facilities confirms carrier status and triggers RMA/expedite.
- Recovery steps:
  a) Offer loaner device or secure desktop access.
  b) For long delays (>10 business days) issue stipend and document cost center.
- Owner: Facilities/Hardware Ops

5) Mismatch between role expectation and job setup (wrong groups/permissions)
- Symptoms: User has access but key services missing (e.g., repo access, dataset access).
- Immediate triage: Hiring Manager and People Ops audit role checklist; create list of missing items.
- Recovery steps:
  a) Submit role-specific access ticket with clear list and justification.
  b) Cross-team owner meeting within 48 hours to resolve entitlement mapping.
- Owner: Hiring Manager (requester), IT (entitlements), Product/Platform (resource owners)

Escalation matrix
- Level 1 (Operational): People Ops onboarding lead — onboarding@redwood.com — response SLA 4 business hours.
- Level 2 (Team lead): IT Cloud Access lead / Facilities lead / Security lead — response SLA 8 business hours.
- Level 3 (Director): Director, People Ops and Director, IT — response SLA 24 business hours; engage exec on-call for customer-impacting delays.

Runbook: Immediate 8-step triage (use when an activation misses an SLA threshold)
1) Record the hire and what was missed in the Activation Tracker (spreadsheet/ticket).
2) Capture ticket IDs for every affected system and assign severity=high.
3) Contact hiring manager and confirm critical services required day-1.
4) Assign an interim buddy if mentor is not available.
5) Create temporary access if security allows least-privilege exceptions.
6) Expedite device shipping or provision cloud workstation.
7) Communicate status to hire with expected timeline and single point of contact.
8) Trigger post-mortem if activation > 7 business days or if a recurring failure pattern emerges.

Templates and artifacts (copy into HRIS / onboarding ticket)
- Activation ticket template (subject): [Activation-Critical] New Hire: <Name> — Missing: <items> — TicketIDs: <list>
- Communication template (to new hire):
  Hi <Name>, we are working on the remaining items needed for your activation. Current ETA: <date>. Your onboarding lead is <Name> (<email>). We will provide temporary access where possible.

Post-mortem and continuous improvement
- Trigger conditions: activation > 7 business days OR identical failure mode for 3 hires in 30 days.
- Post-mortem steps:
  1) People Ops creates incident doc with timeline, owners, root cause, and action items.
  2) Assign owners to remediate systemic issues (e.g., add automation, update runbooks, change SLAs).
  3) Track remediation to closure in the 'Activation Reliability' board and report monthly to People Ops leadership.

Preventative actions and long-term mitigations
- Automate provisioning for repeatable role templates (engineer, data scientist, sales) using Terraform or IAM automation.
- Maintain a pool of loaner devices and pre-imaged images for cross-region hires.
- Quarterly access entitlement audits to identify misconfigured role templates.
- Manager readiness checklist and automated reminders 5 business days before start date to ensure mentor assignment and project setup.

Tooling and dashboards
- Activation Tracker (Google Sheet) — primary ledger for SLA calculation.
- Onboarding tickets: our Jira project ONB- (labels: activation-critical).
- Weekly report: Activation Metrics dashboard in Looker / internal observability.

Related policies and links
- Hiring policy for international shipments: /people-ops/shipping-policy-2025
