payload.page_title: Coaching 1:1 Playbook and Performance Mapping

sections.body: This playbook provides a practical, repeatable framework for managers to run regular 1:1s, perform structured performance mapping, and drive consistent development outcomes across teams. It combines a reusable 1:1 agenda, coaching prompts, a performance mapping matrix, probation/90-day checklists, calibration meeting guidance, and lightweight templates for written feedback. The goal is to reduce variance in manager coaching quality and create defensible records for growth and promotion conversations.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Frontline managers across engineering, product, and support
- People Ops partners and HRBP reviewers
- People managers new to Redwood or switching teams
sections.heading: Who this is for

sections.body:
- Playbook owner: People Ops (Sophie Tran)
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review or after major org changes
- Adoption SLO: 95% of managers run documented 1:1s at least twice/month for direct reports within 3 months of rollout

1) 1:1 Cadence and Format
- Frequency: recommended weekly for ICs in active projects; bi-weekly acceptable for senior ICs or low-touch roles.
- Minimum expectation: every direct report should have at least 20 documented 1:1s per year.
- Length: 30–45 minutes for ICs; 45–60 minutes for managers and senior ICs.
- Mode: in-person preferred when onboarding or discussing promotion; remote OK with videocall and notes shared.

Standard 1:1 agenda (use as a template):
- 2 mins: Quick personal check-in (energy, context)
- 5 mins: Wins since last meeting (celebrate progress)
- 10 mins: Roadblocks & support needed (clear asks and owners)
- 10 mins: Development focus (skills, stretch projects, feedback)
- 5 mins: Career conversation or long-term goals (rotate monthly)
- 3 mins: Commitments & next steps (owner + due date)
sections.heading: Owner and SLAs

sections.body:
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD | Focus: [project|development|blocker|career] | Summary: 1-2 lines | Action items: owner (due)

2) Coaching Prompts and Feedback Frameworks
- Goal of coaching: increase capability and autonomy; reduce ambiguity for the report.
- Use 'RAD' shorthand for feedback:
  - Recognize: what worked?
  - Adjust: what to change?
  - Develop: growth action for next 4–8 weeks
- When delivering corrective feedback, use structured observation + impact + request pattern:
  1. Observable fact (what happened)
  2. Impact (on team, customer, delivery)
  3. Clear request (what change you want to see, timeline)

3) Performance Mapping Matrix (one-page view)
- Purpose: translate ongoing 1:1 evidence into a consistent rubric for development conversations and promotion calibration.
- Matrix axes and guidance (manager fill-in per report):
  - X-axis: Results (consistently delivers to expectations -> exceeds expectations)
  - Y-axis: Behaviors & Collaboration (needs support -> role-model)
- Quadrant actions:
  - Q1 (Low results / Low behaviors): immediate development plan + 30/60/90 checkpoints
  - Q2 (Low results / High behaviors): focus on role clarity, pairing, and accountability rhythm
  - Q3 (High results / Low behaviors): coaching on collaboration, cross-team impact; document expectations
  - Q4 (High results / High behaviors): candidate for stretch assignments & promotion discussion
sections.heading: Note template for managers (one-line entries encouraged)

sections.body:
- Name: Jordan Patel | Results: Meets (=> moving to Exceeds) | Behaviors: Role-model | Current quadrant: Q4 | Evidence summary: shipped X feature with cross-team coordination; peer praise; mentored two new hires.

4) 30/60/90 and Probation Review Checklist
- Use for every new hire, internal transfer, or performance-improvement plan.
- Checkpoints: 30-day touch (engagement + training), 60-day progress (shipping/ownership evidence), 90-day outcome (role alignment and next steps).
- Probation template (to share with employee at start):
  - Objective: clear 3 measurable outcomes to achieve by day 90
  - Weekly owner: manager weekly 1:1 notes + shared progress doc
  - Failure criteria: not making measurable progress after documented support and two formal checkpoints -> escalate to People Ops for next steps

5) Promotion Readiness Evidence Pack (what managers should prepare)
- Required artifacts:
  - 1:1 notes (last 6–12 months) — bulletized highlights
  - Impact examples (3–5 clear examples with metrics where possible)
  - Stakeholder feedback (peers, partner engineering/product) — 1–3 short quotes
  - Growth areas and development plan if promoted
- Timeline: Nomination -> Manager packet due -> Calibration meeting (bi-weekly) -> Decision communicated within 10 business days.

6) Calibration Meeting Playbook
- Purpose: ensure consistent standards and defendable decisions across teams.
- Cadence: bi-weekly for engineering & product leadership; monthly for other orgs.
- Pre-reads (sent 48 hours before): manager packets (see above) and a one-slide summary per candidate.
- Meeting flow (30–45 minutes):
  1. Quick status (5 mins): number of cases, conflicts
  2. Candidate reviews (5–10 mins each): manager presents evidence, panel asks clarifying Qs
  3. Tone check & decision capture (10 mins): consensus + minority opinions recorded
  4. Action items (5 mins): Communicator, timeline, appeal route
- Decision rules: at least 60% of present calibrators must support promotion. If split, escalate to next-level manager + People Ops.

7) Documenting Difficult Conversations and Escalation Path
- For corrective coaching: create a short "Coaching Record" entry in the manager's notes with date, behavior, impact, request, and employee response.
- If improvement is not observed after 2 documented cycles (typically 8–12 weeks), escalate to People Ops with: coaching records, performance mapping, and suggested next steps.
- Escalation owners: People Ops lead (Priya Kapoor), HRBP for the org, and Partner Manager.

8) Onboarding Handoff & Early Development (first 60 days)
- Manager must provide within 3 days of start: role charter, initial OKRs, list of 3 people to introduce, and first 30/60/90 objectives.
- Week 1 checklist: access + 1:1 cadence set + buddy assigned + learning path link shared.
- Weeks 2–8: weekly manager 1:1 focused on context, deliverables, and integration into team rituals.

9) Templates (copyable)
- 1:1 note (one-line): "2027-02-01 | project: infra-opt | summary: removed blocker X, paired on Y | action: follow-up with ops (Michael) by 2027-02-07"
- Coaching note (short): "2027-01-15 | observation: missed SLA in Q4 deploy | impact: customer incident | request: write runbook and pair on next deploy by 2027-01-31"
- Promotion one-slide summary: "Name / Current role / Recommendation / Top 3 evidence bullets / Potential role after promotion / Ramp risks & plan"

10) Manager Training and Enablement
- People Ops runs quarterly workshops: "Effective 1:1s", "Giving Tough Feedback", and "Calibration Facilitation".
- New managers must attend a 2-hr onboarding workshop within 30 days of promotion to people manager.

11) Metrics and Reporting
- People Ops will track: 1) % of managers meeting 1:1 cadence, 2) % of hires with completed 90-day reviews, 3) distribution across performance quadrants, 4) time-to-decision for promotions.
- Monthly dashboard owner: People Ops Reporting (reporting@redwood-inference.internal) — includes anonymized counts and trends.

Appendix: Quick Reference Cheat Sheet
- Weekly 1:1s: 30 mins; Agenda = Check-in | Wins | Blockers | Development | Commitments
- Feedback framework: RAD (Recognize, Adjust, Develop)
- Promotion prep: 6–12 months of evidence, 3 impact examples, peer feedback
- Calibration rule: 60%+ support required or escalate

payload.page_title: Technical Lead Onboarding Playbook and Inter-team Handover — First 60 Days

sections.body: This playbook defines a repeatable, cross-functional onboarding and handover process for new technical leads (TLs) joining an engineering team at Redwood Inference. It consolidates hiring touchpoints, a pragmatic first-60-day curriculum, inter-team handover checklist, and a lightweight performance & feedback cadence for managers and peer mentors. The intent is to accelerate impact while preserving knowledge continuity across teams.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- New technical leads and their hiring managers
- Peer mentors and direct reports
- People Ops partners supporting role activation
- Hiring panels participating in handoffs and transition interviews
sections.heading: Audience

sections.body:
- Enable TLs to be independently productive on core deliverables by day 60.
- Reduce knowledge debt and single‑person dependencies during role transitions.
- Standardize expectations for feedback and performance checkpoints.
- Ensure consistent security, access, and compliance handover.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Primary owner: People Ops (onboarding enablement)
- Role owner: Hiring manager (day-to-day execution)
- Cross-team coordination: Source team manager (outgoing) and destination team manager (incoming)
- Escalation path: Hiring manager -> Director of Engineering -> People Ops partner
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation

sections.body:
1. Offer acceptance and role handbook sent to candidate.
2. Access request ticket created (See "Access & Security checklist" below).
3. Mentor assigned and 1:1 schedule provisioned for first 30 days.
4. First sprint/context docs, architecture maps, and current ROADMAP link shared.

60-day curriculum (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (pre-boarding, 7 days before start):
  - Confirm laptop and environment provisioning (image, VPN, KMS access).
  - Send reading pack: team charter, open PRs, incident history, oncall roster, and sprint board.
  - Quick intro video from outgoing TL if possible (5–10 min).

- Week 1 (orientation & context):
  - Day 1: HR check-in, security briefing, team all-hands, and 30-min manager expectations sync.
  - Set developer environment; validate ability to run test-suite and local server.
  - Shadow 1:1s with each direct report (30m) to capture team priorities and blockers.
  - Deliverable: Update personal onboarding checklist in team wiki.

- Week 2 (codebase immersion & stakeholder map):
  - Read key RFCs/ADRs, review top 5 failing CI tests historically, and exercise a small bug fix.
  - Stakeholder meetings: Product PM, SRE lead, Data/ML counterpart, Security contact.
  - Deliverable: Draft 30/60-day goals and share with manager.

- Weeks 3–4 (ownership & early wins):
  - Lead a small planning session and own at least one low-risk PR to production.
  - Participate in oncall shadowing rotation.
  - Run a 1-hour "architecture walkthrough" for the team.
  - Deliverable: One merged PR and a public post-mortem of the change (short doc).

- Weeks 5–8 (scale leadership & process improvements):
  - Propose one process or tooling improvement (e.g., CI flake reduction, pre-merge tests).
  - Facilitate a cross-team sync to resolve integration gaps.
  - Begin mentoring cycle: schedule recurring 1:1s with direct reports and set career checkpoints.
  - Deliverable: Publish a 60-day readout with risks and hire needs.

Inter-team handover checklist (used by outgoing TL and People Ops):
- Role knowledge transfer:
  - List of active projects with owners, status, and next steps.
  - Architectural diagrams and key RFC/ADR links.
  - Oncall runbook and known incident patterns.
  - CI/CD pipelines and deployment playbooks.

- People and relationships:
  - Current feedback summaries for direct reports (last 6 months).
  - Mentoring relationships and ongoing development plans.
  - Key external stakeholders and SLAs with partner teams.

- Operational and administrative:
  - Access inventory: repos, cloud projects, dashboards, KMS keys (redact secrets - share IDs).
  - Scheduled recurring meetings ownership transfer (calendar updates).
  - Outstanding hiring requests and candidate scorecards.

- Handover acceptance criteria (incoming TL signs off):
  - Able to run the main deployment pipeline with peer present.
  - Can summarize incident escalation flow and key oncall contacts.
  - Validated access to monitoring, error logs, and build artifacts.
sections.heading: Prerequisites (before start date)

sections.body:
- Accounts to provision (core): GitHub org, CI runner access, GCP project viewer/editor, Sentry, Datadog (read), Console access to model-serving cluster (RBAC session).
- Secrets & KMS: Request per-policy access with approval ticket; do not transfer private keys in email.
- Compliance: If team handles regulated data, confirm egress/VPC config and ensure Private deployment onboarding steps are completed.
sections.heading: Access & security checklist (minimum)

sections.body:
- Panels: TLs should participate in at least two interview loops within first 60 days (scheduling prioritized by manager).
- Calibration: Attend a 60-minute interview calibration session run by People Ops within week 4.
- Scorecard usage: Use the team’s competency rubric (see table below) and attach high-level notes to the candidate record.

Performance and feedback cadence (manager + TL):
- Week 2: informal 1:1 to confirm onboarding logistics and early blockers.
- Week 4: 30-minute checkpoint to review 30-day goals and early wins.
- Week 8 (end of 60-day period): written 60-day readout and manager evaluation.
- Ongoing: transition into standard 1:1 cadence and quarterly performance cycle.
sections.heading: Hiring & interview involvement for TLs (expectations)

sections.body:
- Positive reinforcement: "In the last sprint, your ownership of X reduced incident MTTR by Y%. I’d like to see you continue to..."
- Constructive: "I noticed X. For the next two weeks, please try Y and schedule a sync so we can iterate."

Competency rubric (one-line criteria used in interview/hire feedback):
| Area | Expectation at TL level | Evidence examples |
|------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| System design | Designs reliable, observable services with clear tradeoffs | Architecture docs, ADR authorship |
| Execution | Drives delivery, unblock teams, lands changes to prod | Merged features, reduced backlogs |
| People leadership | Coaches engineers and enables growth | Mentoring notes, promotion nominees |
| Cross-team influence | Negotiates scope with product and infra partners | Meeting notes, cross-team initiatives |

(Interviewers: capture 1–2 lines of evidence against each area; attach code sample/PR references where relevant.)

Manager guide: how to run the 60-day readout meeting
1. 20 min: TL presents accomplishments, blockers, and risks.
2. 10 min: Manager provides calibrated feedback with examples.
3. 10 min: Agree on updated 90-day objectives and any hiring or resourcing needs.
4. Follow-up: Manager uploads 60-day writeup to People Ops with recommended pulse (pass/needs-development/high-support).
sections.heading: Quick feedback templates (for managers)

sections.body:
- Failure: TL lacks access to critical repos. Mitigation: Escalate to Cloud Access team within 24 hours; use emergency guest tokens to unblock.
- Failure: Knowledge gaps in oncall expectations. Mitigation: Pair with outgoing TL for two full oncall rotations or escalate to SRE for shadowing.
- Failure: Poor alignment with PM on priorities. Mitigation: Host triage meeting with PM + Director to re-scope objectives.
sections.heading: Common failure modes and mitigations

sections.body:
- 30/60-day goal template (copy into personal wiki):
  - Objective: "{impact statement}"
  - Success metrics: "{1–3 measurable outcomes}"
  - Risks: "{key assumptions and blockers}"
  - Stakeholders: "{names and roles}"

- 60-day readout doc outline (to upload to People Ops):
  - Summary (3–4 bullet impact statement)
  - Outcomes achieved
  - Open risks and mitigation plan
  - Suggested hires/support requests

- Handover artifact checklist (to attach to acceptance ticket):
  - Link to architecture diagram, list of top-5 PRs, open incidents list, and access inventory CSV.
sections.heading: Templates and artifacts (links & snippets)

sections.body:
- Recommended e-learning: "Effective Technical Leadership" (internal L&D link), SRE oncall fundamentals, and Redwood security basics.
- Must-read RFCs: list of three team/infra RFCs (attach links in team wiki).

Metrics to track (people + operational):
- Time-to-first-merge (target: <= 21 days)
- Number of knowledge transfer artifacts produced (target: >= 3 by day 30)
- Oncall readiness: observed shadowing shifts completed (target: 2 full shifts)
- Manager satisfaction pulse (People Ops survey at day 60)

Appendix A — Example calendar for first 4 weeks (high level):
- Monday: 1:1 with manager, team standup, environment setup.
- Tuesday: Stakeholder intro meetings.
- Wednesday: Codebase walkthrough and first PR.
- Thursday: Oncall shadow and CI exercise.
- Friday: 30-minute "show and tell" and sync with mentor.

Appendix B — Quick checklist for outgoing TLs:
- Export short bios of direct reports and current development plans.
- Flag technical debt items and label high risk areas.
- Provide schedule of recurring vendor/partner meetings and contractual notes.

sections.body:

If you have questions or need role-specific adjustments, contact People Ops onboarding (people-ops@redwood.com) or the author.

payload.page_title: hiring-for-impact-competency-sprints-and-100-day-outcomes-2029

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is designed for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners who want a structured, repeatable path from role intake to first-100-day measurable outcomes. It formalizes short competency sprints during hiring and prescribes a manager-led feedback cadence to get new hires to independent impact faster while maintaining equitable assessment.

Scope: Applies to all individual contributor and manager-level hires at Redwood Inference. Exclusions: executive hiring (handled by Talent & Exec Recruiting) and very short-term contractors (<30 days).

Key definitions
- Competency Sprint: A two-week focused evaluation and onboarding sub-phase that defines 2–3 observable competencies to validate in hiring and to train during ramp.
- 100-Day Outcomes: A small set (3–5) of measurable outcomes a manager and new hire agree on during onboarding.

Roles & Ownership
- Hiring Manager: defines role-level outcomes, selects competency sprint goals, owns interview panel and final hire decision.
- People Ops Partner: validates hiring rubric equity, ensures diverse panels, schedules competency sprint tasks, owns offer & coordination.
- Interviewers: evaluate against rubric and provide calibrated written feedback within 48 hours.
- New Hire Buddy: peer from a neighboring team who provides day-to-day orientation for first 4 weeks.

Hiring intake -> Competency Sprint (3-step flow)
1) Intake & Outcome Draft (Manager pre-reqs)
   - Manager completes the Role Readiness brief (template below) in Greenhouse before the JD is posted. Required fields: primary 100-day outcomes (3), top 3 competencies for sprint, minimal technical screen criteria, salary band, escalation contacts.
   - People Ops validates banding and reviewer panel diversity within 48 hours.

2) Competency Sprint design (People Ops + Manager, 48–72 hours)
   - For IC roles, sprints are typically engineering tasks or product problem statements that can be completed asynchronously (4–12 hours of candidate work). For managers, sprints are a short case exercise and two structured interviews.
   - Each sprint includes: success rubric, timebox, data or artifact submission instructions, and reviewer rubric questions.

3) Candidate evaluation & calibration (Interviewers)
   - Interviewers score against the rubric (numeric 1–5) and add a short narrative. Scores and narratives must be in Greenhouse within 48 hours of stage completion.
   - Hiring manager runs a 30-minute calibration meeting with the panel within 72 hours of final interview. If calibration variance >1.0 on any competency, arrange a tie-break interview or sample work review.

Manager checklist: Pre-offer -> Day 1
- Pre-offer: confirm final 100-day outcomes, identify buddy, schedule first-week meetings, and confirm onboarding equipment and access with IT and Infra.
- Day 0 (Offer accepted): send Welcome note with first-week agenda and the Outcome Draft PDF.
- Day 1: 30-minute one-on-one to review the 100-day outcomes and competency sprint expectations.

100-Day outcome template (example)
- Outcome 1 (Product/Feature impact): Deliver a validated improvement to the inference logging pipeline that reduces mean tail latency for 95th percentile tail by 5% for synthetic benchmark workload. Acceptance criteria: PR merged to main, benchmark results in CI show reduction, and post-deploy monitoring shows no regression for 7 days.
- Outcome 2 (Operational mastery): Complete the Redwood infra runbook certification with two successful runbook drills signed off by oncall lead.
- Outcome 3 (Team & process): Lead a cross-team retrospective and produce an action list with owners and SLAs.

Performance & feedback cadence during first 100 days
- Weekly 30m 1:1s during first 8 weeks, with explicit agenda items: blockers, outcomes progress, learning needs.
- Bi-weekly written scorecard from manager (short rubric: Learning, Delivery, Collaboration) at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Each scorecard is shared with new hire and People Ops.
- Formal 100-day review (week 12): manager prepares a 2-slide summary of outcomes, evidence, and recommended ongoing development plan. People Ops uses this artifact for calibration and banding adjustments if needed.

Calibration and fairness checks
- People Ops will run a calibration pool for hires at the same band every quarter. Metrics monitored: offer acceptance rate, time-to-ramp (measured by % of 100-day outcomes achieved), and variance in interview scores across demographics.
- If a candidate’s competency sprint is scored with high reviewer variance or conflicting narratives, People Ops will trigger a post-hire audit and provide an independent assessor to reconcile scores.

Example competency sprint rubric (table rendered as text)
| Competency | Evidence | Success threshold | Evaluator notes |
|------------|----------|------------------:|------------------|
| Service design | Design doc + diagram | 3/5 or higher across all reviewers | Look for clear tradeoffs and rollout plan |
| Code quality | PR with tests | No critical issues, 2 reviewers signoff | Tests + CI passing |
| Cross-team comms | Presentation deck | Clear goals + next steps | Evidence of stakeholder mapping |

Manager decision tree: offer -> low confidence -> hire with ramp plan -> no hire
1) If panel consensus is strong (>=3 reviewers, median score >=4), proceed to offer.
2) If median score is 3 with low variance, manager may request a short follow-up assignment.
3) If panel is split (variance >1.0) and concerns are about fit, consider: a) a second look interview led by a neutral reviewer, or b) decline and record learnings in the hiring postmortem.

Onboarding accelerators (practical tools)
- Competency Sprint Library: curated tasks for common roles (engineering, infra, data infra, product ops) maintained in the People Ops repo: git@redwood-internal:people-ops/competency-sprints.git.
- Role Onboarding Checklist (automated): HR triggers account provisioning 7 days before start. SLA: 95% of hires have accounts provisioned by Day 0.
- Runbook certification: a short multiple-choice + live drill validated by SRE.

Escalation & remediation
- If a new hire is not meeting agreed 100-day outcomes at week 8, manager opens a 4-week Remediation Sprint: documented plan, weekly checkpoints, and People Ops involvement. Outcome options: success (stay), extended ramp (up to 8 additional weeks), or transition support (role change or exit).
- People Ops must be notified before any formal performance step (e.g., PIP) is initiated.

Metrics & KPIs (tracked quarterly)
- Median time-to-first-impact: target <= 75 days for IC hires.
- 100-day outcomes achieved: target 80% across organization.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 65% for priority roles.
- Onboarding provisioning SLA: 95% Day-0-ready.

Templates & artifacts (appendix)
1) Role Readiness brief (fields): Role summary; 3x 100-day outcomes; competency sprint items; interview panel; salary band; urgency level (1–3).
2) Example 100-day review slide (two bullets per slide): Evidence, Result, Next steps.
3) Competency sprint email template for candidates (includes timebox and submission link).

Implementation notes for managers
- Keep outcomes measurable and narrow. Avoid more than three 100-day outcomes.
- Use competency sprints to reduce interviewing noise — they standardize evidence across candidates.
- Document learning opportunities publicly in the team wiki so future hiring loops improve.

Related links
- People Ops competency-sprint repo: git@redwood-internal:people-ops/competency-sprints.git
- Onboarding automation: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-tasks-automation-and-skill-certification-catalog-2029
- Managers handbook (short): /confluence/people-ops/manager-accelerated-integration-and-feedback-sprint-2025

Revision history
- 2028-11-06: Draft authored by Elena Morales.
- 2028-12-12: Added remediation sprint process and metrics (reviewers: Jordan Lee).
- 2029-01-15: Finalized templates, updated SLA targets after Q4 2028 calibration (reviewers: Priya Desai).

payload.page_title: Deferred Onboarding and Role Reskilling Playbook (Bridge Program)

sections.body:
Overview

Summary: This playbook documents the accepted process for managing hires or internal transfers who start later than their original start date (deferred starts) and the structured reskilling pathways (Bridge Program) for employees who change roles and require a focused ramp. It combines People Ops operational tasks, manager responsibilities, expected timelines, and metrics to minimize time-to-impact while protecting candidate experience and compliance.

Scope
- Applies to: new hires with confirmed but delayed start dates, accepted offers where the candidate requests a deferral (>2 weeks), and internal transfers that require reskilling (>3 weeks of formal training).
- Not in scope: short reschedules under 2 business days, contractors with ad-hoc start windows, apprenticeship/returnship special programs (see related pages).

Goals
- Maintain candidate/employee engagement during deferral windows.
- Provide repeatable manager/People Ops steps to re-onboard or bridge skills.
- Target median time-to-competency: 8 weeks for lateral transfers, 12 weeks for role transitions with new technical domains.
- Reduce churn during pre-start and early employment by 50% vs ad-hoc approaches.

Definitions
- Deferred Start: an accepted offer with a confirmed start date > 2 weeks after offer acceptance.
- Bridge Program: a targeted, time-bound reskilling curriculum for employees changing role families or adding new core competencies.
- Reskilling Path: curated set of courses, mentors, shadow tasks, and evaluation gates to certify readiness.

Principles
- Candidate-centric: prioritize transparent comms and predictable checkpoints.
- Manager accountability: manager owns role-specific curriculum and success criteria.
- People Ops partnership: People Ops owns program templates, compliance, and reporting.
- Measured ramp: use objective checkpoints (skills checks, paired sessions, feature contributions).

Roles & Ownership
- Hiring Manager: defines technical and behavioral competency gates; assigns mentor and initial project.
- People Ops Lead (onboarding specialist): confirms schedule, maintains pre-start comm cadence, provisions access, and manages legal/comp paperwork timelines.
- Learning & Development (L&D): curates learning modules and schedules cohort sessions.
- Mentor (peer): provides weekly 1:1 for first 8 weeks of ramp.
- IT/Security: completes device, network, and role-based access setup no later than 3 business days before actual start.

Deferred-Start Playbook (People Ops + Hiring Manager)
1) At offer acceptance (Day 0)
   - Capture preferred start window and any planned deferred dates in Workday/HRIS.
   - Set expected timeline expectations in offer email: include sample pre-start comm cadence.
   - People Ops: schedule one formal check-in 2 weeks before proposed start and an optional weekly update for longer deferrals (>6 weeks).

2) If candidate requests deferral before signature
   - Treat as negotiation: update offer terms, confirm final start date, reissue paperwork, and update recruiter/finance.

3) For confirmed deferral (>2 weeks) after signature
   - People Ops tasks (timeline):
     - Day 1 (post-confirmation): create Deferred Onboarding record, notify IT and Security.
     - Weekly: short status email to candidate (one paragraph) with 2–3 highlights about team and product.
     - T-minus 21 days before start: confirm equipment timeline, training plan, and 1:1 schedule with manager.
     - T-minus 3 business days: tech access provisioning and calendar invites for Day 1.

4) Pre-start engagement (recommended cadence)
   - 6–8 weeks out (if deferral is long): invite to optional monthly Product Office Hours and shared learning channels.
   - 2–3 weeks out: send Welcome Guide (high level org map, first-week agenda, pre-work).
   - 2–3 business days out: final logistics email (parking/remote links, Slack invite, hardware delivery windows).

5) Day 1 adjustments (for deferred starts)
   - Manager to run a tailored 90-minute immersion rather than standard 30–60 minute check-in.
   - Assign 30-day objectives that are realistic given deferral.

Bridge Program: Role Reskilling Process (internal transfers or hires needing skills bridge)
- Program length banding by scope:
  - Minor reskill (tooling or process change, <2 new competencies): 4–6 weeks.
  - Moderate reskill (new framework/team conventions, 2–4 competencies): 8–12 weeks.
  - Major reskill (different discipline, e.g., infra -> model-serving, >4 competencies): 12–16 weeks.

- Standard Bridge program components (template):
  - Week-by-week learning plan with milestone outcomes.
  - Assigned mentor and owner of weekly tasks.
  - Sprint-style project: small scoped deliverable to demonstrate applied learning (typically delivered by week 6–8).
  - Formal competency check at program mid-point and end (skill rubric).
  - 1:1 cadence: weekly for first 12 weeks, then biweekly until certification.

Example Training Matrix (use as template)
| Competency | Learning Assets | Hands-on Tasks | Cert Gate | Owner | Target Week |
|------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|-------|-------------|
| Core infra patterns | internal wiki, 2-hour workshop | shadow deploy + runbook update | review PR + runbook | Manager | 1–4 |
| Model-serving basics | L&D course, external reading | local inference test + perf summary | evaluation quiz + demo | Mentor | 2–6 |
| Observability and SLOs | dashboard walkthroughs | build one alert + dashboard | peer review | SRE partner | 4–8 |

(When importing into Confluence, render the table natively. Above is a simple markdown-style table for reference.)

Manager Checklist (Pre-start and Weeks 0–12)
- Pre-start (T-minus 21d): confirm mentor, first sprint, and access.
- Day 1: 90-minute immersion, calendar and expectation alignment.
- Week 1: set 30/60/90 objectives and small first deliverable.
- Week 2–4: weekly 1:1, confirm hands-on tasks and pair sessions.
- Week 6: mid-program checkpoint (objective evidence review + rubric scoring).
- Week 12: final certification meeting and plan next steps (stretch assignments, recurring mentoring cadence).

People Ops / L&D Checklist
- Create Deferred Onboarding record and enable pre-start comms.
- Reserve cohort space in L&D calendar (if curriculum required).
- Track access ticket age; escalate to SOC/IT owner after 48 hours.
- Log program enrollments for quarterly Bridge Program reporting.

Templates & Example Messages
- Pre-start check-in (2 weeks out):
  "Hi <Candidate Name>, hope you're well — just checking in ahead of your start on <Start Date>. We've scheduled your first-day agenda and have updated the equipment plan. Let me know if anything has changed; otherwise we'll connect again one week before. — <People Ops Rep>"

- Manager Day 1 invitation (subject): "Welcome + 90-minute immersion: practical first steps"
  Body: short agenda, 1:1 mentor intro, and first sprint description.

Evaluation & Metrics
- Primary KPIs (tracked quarterly):
  - Median time-to-competency (weeks to hit objective gate): target 8–12 weeks depending on banding.
  - Pre-start engagement rate: % candidates responding to at least one pre-start comm in last 4 weeks (target > 80%).
  - Equipment/access SLA: % of hires with full access by Day 0 (target 95%).
  - Deferred-start churn: % of deferred hires who do not start (target < 4%).

Escalation & Exceptions
- If access is not provisioned by T-minus 3 business days: People Ops escalates to IT lead and copies Security.
- If candidate requests second deferral: treat as re-negotiation and require manager+People Ops approval; document changes in offer record.
- If mid-program competency score < 60% at mid-point: extend bridge by 2–4 weeks with revised milestone and L&D support.

Recordkeeping & Reporting
- Store deferred-start notes in HRIS under candidate record and tag with "deferred-bridge" label.
- People Ops to publish quarterly Bridge Program summary: enrollment, pass rate, average time-to-certification, and any action items.

Related Pages & Resources
- Returnship and internal mobility guidelines (see related_pages).
- Onboarding immersion rotation playbook for Day 1 templates.
- L&D course catalog (internal link).

Appendices
A. Sample 8-week Bridge program outline (week-by-week bullets):
- Week 1: orientation, pairing, small hands-on ticket.
- Week 2: core concept deep dive, automated test + PR.
- Week 3: mini-project planning.
- Week 4: mid-program review + rubric feedback.
- Week 5–6: project execution, demos.
- Week 7: stabilization and cross-team shadow.
- Week 8: final demo, competency certification, next assignment.

B. Suggested rubric dimensions (score 0–5 each):
- Technical correctness, independent delivery, code quality, system understanding, observability contributions, communication.

C. FAQ (short)
- Q: Can a deferred start be lengthened twice?
  A: Only with Manager + People Ops approval; third deferral triggers review by Head of Talent.

- Q: Who pays for equipment delays?
  A: Redwood covers shipping and standard hardware; exceptions require finance approval.

Versioning & Ownership
- Owner: People Ops (Onboarding Specialist team)
- Last reviewed: 2026-02-14
- Review cadence: annual or after any material change to onboarding or HRIS flows.

Contact
- For questions or exceptions: people-ops@redwood.com or @Maya.Chen on Slack.

payload.page_title: Rapid Hiring Blitz & Volatile Headcount Playbook

sections.body: This playbook describes an operational pattern for executing a time-boxed, high-throughput hiring surge (a "hiring blitz") while also managing volatile headcount plans (hiring freezes, rapid rollbacks, conversion of contractors). It condenses processes, ownership, and guardrails so hiring quality and new-hire experience do not degrade during fast growth or contraction cycles.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to company-level or org-level hiring surges lasting between 2 and 12 weeks.
- Covers sourcing, screening, offer flow, rapid onboarding, manager handoffs, and contingency de-escalation when headcount changes.
- Not a replacement for long-term recruiting strategy or diversity initiatives; those run in parallel.
sections.heading: Scope and intent

sections.body:
1) Quality over volume: retain minimum scorecard thresholds and structured interviews to avoid bad hires.
2) Transparent capacity signals: hiring managers must publish role prioritization and de-prioritization triggers before a blitz begins.
3) Short feedback loops: reviewers must return feedback within 36 hours during an active blitz.
4) Safe retraction: have an offer retraction and conversion policy ready to preserve fairness and legal compliance.
sections.heading: Key principles

sections.body:
- Blitz Lead (people-ops): overall coordinator, daily standup facilitator, escalation owner.
- Sourcing Captain (recruiting): channel allocation and pipeline pacing.
- Hiring Managers: interview commitment, final decision, onboarding sponsor.
- Interview Ops (people-ops/recruiting): scheduling, scorecard enforcement, candidate communications.
- Finance Partner: verifies budget approvals and backstops contingency scenarios.

Pre-blitz checklist (to be completed 7–3 days before start):
1. Confirm executive approval and budget: finance signature required.
2. Publish prioritized role list with 3 tiers (A: critical, B: backfill, C: discretionary).
3. Assign interview panels and backups; guarantee at least two trained interviewers per role.
4. Prepare templated offer letters and compensation bands for rapid approval.
5. Update ATS tags and create blitz pipeline views.
6. Schedule daily 15-minute standups (Blitz Lead + Sourcing + Hiring Managers).
sections.heading: Roles & ownership

sections.body:
- 09:00 — Pipeline sync (exceptions, blockers).
- 10:00 — Interview slot release and scheduling window opens.
- 14:00 — Manager review block; managers commit 2 hours to deconflict feedback.
- 16:00 — Offer approvals and comp decision window.
- 17:00 — End-of-day report (pipeline movements, offers extended, declines).
sections.heading: Blitz operating cadence (example daily rhythm)

sections.body:
- Score 1–4 across three dimensions: Role Match, Problem Solving, Team Fit.
- Minimum pass: average >= 3.0 and no single dimension < 2.

Quick reference: scorecard table (copy into ATS/scorecard form):
| Field | Description | Threshold |
| Role Match | Demonstrated technical/functional skills | avg >= 3.0 |
| Problem Solving | Clear approach and trade-off reasoning | avg >= 3.0 |
| Team Fit | Communication, collaboration, and values alignment | avg >= 3.0 |
sections.heading: Structured interview scale (mandatory)

sections.body:
1. Interviewers submit structured feedback within 36 hours.
2. Hiring manager consolidates feedback and makes a tentative decision.
3. Compensation approval route: Manager -> Recruiting Lead -> Finance (auto-approve if within band).
4. Blitz Lead validates candidate experience checks (no back-to-back technical interviews > 2 hours without a break, compensation within published bands).
5. Offer is extended and tracked in the blitz offer tracker.
sections.heading: Decision & offer flow (numbered procedure)

sections.body:
- All offers must include a written justification if compensation exceeds band by > 10%.
- Rolling re-evaluation: candidates who receive offers but have > 10 days lapse are re-run through a 1-hour reconfirmation interview with the hiring manager.
- Offer retraction policy: in contraction scenarios, priority-based retraction is used only after legal review and with transition support. People-ops manages communications and severance guidance.
sections.heading: Offer management and fairness guardrails

sections.body: Purpose: compress essential onboarding so new hires are productive while preserving mentorship and cultural integration.
sections.heading: Onboarding fast-path (first 30 days)

sections.body:
- IT provisioning checklist (device, VPN, account creation) completed 48 hours before start.
- Welcome packet & role objectives delivered via onboarding portal.
sections.heading: Week 0 (pre-boarding)

sections.body:
- Day 1 orientation (people-ops): company values, security, benefits, payroll, policies (2 hours).
- Manager 30/60/90 expectation sync (30 minutes).
- Buddy pairing assigned.
Week 2–4 (ramp):
- Technical onboarding tasks and two starter tickets assigned by manager.
- Weekly 1:1 with manager + weekly onboarding cohort sync.
sections.heading: Week 1 (foundation)

sections.body:
- 1:1 frequency: weekly for first 8 weeks, then biweekly until quarter-end.
- Written 30/60/90 goals due by day 7.
- Early talent review: at week 6, hiring manager submits a 6-week progress snapshot to people-ops and L&D for targeted interventions.
sections.heading: Manager handoff & performance check cadence for blitz hires

sections.body:
- Trigger A (Revenue shock > 10% QoQ): freeze Tier C roles immediately; pause Tier B hires in 48 hours.
- Trigger B (Budget reduction confirmed): people-ops initiates offer pause and conversion review within 72 hours.
- Trigger C (Unexpected scale-down): retract offers only after legal and manager-level mitigation plans are prepared.
sections.heading: Trigger matrix (examples)

sections.body:
- Draft templates for (a) offer pauses, (b) rescind letters, (c) contractor conversion offers, (d) internal manager notice.
- People-ops to run empathy-first outreach and provide relocation/transition support where appropriate.
sections.heading: Contingency communications checklist

sections.body:
- Time-to-offer (median) target: <= 10 days from first interview to offer.
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 65% during blitz; monitor by channel.
- Interviewer turnaround: 90% of interviewer feedback returned within 36 hours.
- New-hire retention at 90 days: >= 85% for hires made during the blitz (tracked cohort).
sections.heading: Metrics and SLAs (blitz KPIs)

sections.body:
- Quality decay: mitigate with strict scorecards and post-hire audits.
- Candidate experience issues: mitigate with dedicated candidate communications lead.
- Legal/regulatory exposure for retractions: mitigate with early legal involvement and standardized severance packages.

Post-blitz retrospective and data capture (3–10 days after):
1. Blitz Lead runs a 90-minute retrospective with stakeholders: sourcing, hiring managers, interviewers, legal, finance.
2. Capture quantitative outcomes (time-to-hire, acceptance, cost-per-hire) and qualitative feedback.
3. Create a one-page lessons-learned and update this playbook.
sections.heading: Risk register (top items)

sections.body:
- Blitz pipeline tracker (spreadsheet): columns = Role, Tier, Status, Candidate, Stage, Interviewer, Score, Offer Date, Offer Outcome.
- Offer letter templates (with local legal clauses for US, UK, EU).
- Manager 30/60/90 goal template.
- Candidate communication templates for pause/retract/accept.
sections.heading: Templates and artifacts (available in HR drive)

sections.body:
- Hiring panel calibration guidelines (link in related_pages).
- Onboarding immersion rotation playbook for extended ramp support.

Appendix A — Example blitz timeline (4-week sample):
Week 0: prep, roles prioritized, panels assigned.
Week 1: sourcing surge, 60% of interviews scheduled, first offers extended.
Week 2: accelerated debriefs, remaining offers extended, onboarding slots reserved.
Week 3: ramp cohorts start, early 6-week reviews scheduled.
Week 4: retrospective and adjustment of remaining open roles.

Appendix B — Quick legal notes (non-exhaustive):
- Local labor law differences may constrain offer retraction and notice periods. Always involve legal before any retraction.
- Use standardized severance bands to expedite approvals when retraction is unavoidable.
sections.heading: References and related docs

sections.body:
- Blitz Lead (People Ops): maya.chen@redwood.ai
- Recruiting Lead: recruiting-lead@redwood.ai
- Legal escalation: legal-escalations@redwood.ai

This playbook is a living document. If you run a blitz, file the post-blitz lessons-learned and update the playbook within 10 business days.

payload.page_title: Leader Feedback and Performance Sprint Guide

sections.body:
Purpose
-------
This guide defines a lightweight, repeatable approach for managers and people-ops to run short, outcome-oriented performance cycles called "performance sprints". The goal is to increase feedback frequency, reduce ambiguity in expectations, and create actionable development plans aligned to team priorities.

Scope
-----
Applies to all managers and ICs at Redwood Inference. The approach is intended to complement annual performance reviews, not replace them. Use performance sprints for: onboarding checkpoints, quarterly goal pulses, skill development pushes, and short-term performance recovery.

Principles
----------
- Frequent: shorter cycles (4–8 weeks) make adjustments predictable and lower-stakes.
- Transparent: shared goals, measurable outcomes, and documented follow-ups.
- Coaching-first: emphasize growth; corrective steps should escalate only when coaching fails.
- Evidence-based: base assessments on observable outcomes and examples.

High-level cadence (recommended)
-------------------------------
1. Sprint planning (week 0): manager + contributor agree 2–3 outcomes and signals of success.
2. Weekly 1:1 syncs (15–30m): focused on blockers and evidence collection.
3. Mid-sprint check (week 2 or week 4): short calibration with peer or skip-level if needed.
4. Sprint review (final week): document results, decide next steps (continue, scale, adjust, or initiate improvement plan).

Roles & ownership
------------------
- Manager: owns sprint framing, weekly 1:1 facilitation, evidence collection, and final decision.
- Contributor: co-owns outcomes, provides status updates, and curates evidence/artifacts.
- People Ops: provides templates, moderates calibration sessions, and ensures consistency across teams.
- Skip-level/Peer Reviewer: optional reviewer during mid-sprint check for cross-team context.

Sprint Planning Template (to document in HRIS or shared doc)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Sprint title:
- Start / end dates:
- Priority (onboarding / growth / execution / recovery):
- 2–3 outcomes (headline + measurable signal of success):
  1. Outcome A — success if: [metric / deliverable / behavior].
  2. Outcome B — success if: [metric / deliverable / behavior].
- Key blockers & support requested:
- Checkpoints (dates for mid-sprint, artifacts):

Weekly 1:1 structure (15–30 minutes)
-----------------------------------
1. Quick pulse (1–2 min): energy + focus indicator.
2. Evidence update (3–6 min): concrete progress, links to PRs, docs, demo recordings.
3. Blockers & rapid decisions (5–10 min): what manager will unblock this week.
4. Development micro-task (2–5 min): one small growth activity (read, pairing, refactor).
5. Calendar & next steps (1 min).

Evidence examples (acceptable artifacts)
--------------------------------------
- Merged PRs with release notes
- Demo video or RFC with reviewer comments
- Customer feedback or bug triage tickets closed
- Quantitative signals (latency reduction %, cost/unit change, embeddings accuracy delta)

Calibration rubric (use for consistency in manager assessments)
-------------------------------------------------------------
| Dimension | Exceeds expectations | Meets expectations | Needs improvement |
|-----------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Outcomes  | Delivers reliably and drives additional value | Delivers agreed outcomes on time | Misses multiple outcomes or delivers poor quality |
| Collaboration | Proactively aligns, mentors peers, and removes blockers | Works well within team and communicates updates | Frequent friction, missed handoffs |
| Craft & Execution | Produces high-quality artifacts; anticipates issues | Completes work with acceptable quality | Rework/bugs or repeated missed acceptance criteria |
| Growth mindset | Seeks feedback and applies learning quickly | Accepts feedback and shows progress | Resistant to feedback or slow to change |

Manager assessment guidance
--------------------------
- Use concrete examples (link to artifacts). Avoid vague phrases like "needs to improve communication" without situational evidence.
- Prefer patterns over single incidents. Document 2–3 representative examples per dimension.
- When rating "needs improvement": capture specific behaviors, past coaching attempts, and proposed manager support.

Promotion readiness checklist (for ICs)
--------------------------------------
- Clear impact on product or platform (examples & metrics)
- Cross-team influence documented (RFCs, shared libs, stakeholder testimonials)
- Demonstrated leadership behaviors (mentorship, design ownership)
- Sustained performance across 2+ sprints and peer calibration
- Manager endorsement + documented development gaps and plan

Progression outcomes and next steps
----------------------------------
- Continue: outcomes met; prepare for next sprint with escalated scope.
- Scale: exceeded outcomes; identify stretch assignments and potential promotion timeline.
- Adjust: partial success; run a follow-up sprint with revised outcomes.
- Improvement Plan: significant gaps after coaching; open a 30–60–90 improvement plan (see flow).

Improvement Plan flow (30–60–90)
--------------------------------
1. Trigger: Two consecutive sprints rated as "needs improvement" or a single severe incident.
2. Draft plan: manager + people-ops co-author clear expectations and timeline (30/60/90 days).
3. Weekly progress notes: short updates in HRIS and 1:1s.
4. Midpoint review (30 days): determine if sufficient progress.
5. Final review (60/90 days): decide next step (return to normal cadence, extend plan, role change, or separation).

Conversation frameworks (phrases and structure)
---------------------------------------------
- Situation-Behavior-Impact-Request (SBIR):
  1. Situation: "In last sprint during the API rollout..."
  2. Behavior: "I noticed the PR lacked test coverage and missing schema docs."
  3. Impact: "This led to a rollback and customer downtime for 2 hours."
  4. Request: "Can we agree on a pre-merge checklist for the next release?"
- Radical candor prompts: "I'm invested in your success" before delivering hard feedback.

Onboarding checkpoints aligned to sprints (new hire first 90 days)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Sprint 1 (week 0–4): Setup, first small deliverable, buddy pairing, team intro presentation.
- Sprint 2 (week 5–8): Ownership of a non-critical feature or infra task, demonstrate code review competency.
- Sprint 3 (week 9–12): Lead a small project, show cross-team collaboration, present outcomes to stakeholders.

Manager toolkit (templates & commands)
-------------------------------------
- Sprint planning doc template: use /templates/perf-sprint-template in the shared drive.
- HRIS: create sprint record: CLI example (internal HR tool):
  curl -X POST https://hr.internal.redwood/v1/sprints -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"owner":"<manager>","contributor":"<name>","start":"YYYY-MM-DD","end":"YYYY-MM-DD","outcomes":["..."]}'
- Weekly note snippet (paste to HRIS or PR comment): "Week 2: shipping on track; unblocked by infra review. Artifacts: PR#123, demo.mp4"

Privacy & legal notes
---------------------
- Keep all sprint documentation in Redwood internal systems only. Do not post personal performance notes in public repos.
- For disciplinary actions or PIPs that may affect employment status, loop in People Ops and Legal before finalizing.

Frequently asked questions
--------------------------
Q: How do sprints interact with annual reviews?
A: Performance sprints generate the evidence set that managers use for annual calibration. They should be referenced in the review narrative.

Q: Can an IC request a sprint?
A: Yes — contributors may ask for a sprint to accelerate development or clarify expectations; manager approval required.

Q: What if a manager is overloaded and cannot run weekly 1:1s?
A: Prioritize 1:1s; if not possible, schedule a 20m replaceable sync and seek peer/skip-level touchpoints to ensure continuity. Inform People Ops if sustained backlog occurs.

Appendix: sample sprint review note (copy into HRIS)
--------------------------------------------------
Sprint: Reduce inference tail latency
Dates: 2026-01-05 to 2026-02-02
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Outcome 1: Identify and close top 3 latency hotspots — SUCCESS (PR#452, benchmark report link)
 - Outcome 2: Ship LRU cache micro-optimizations — PARTIAL (deployed behind flag, 8% improvement in p95)
sections.heading: Outcomes

sections.body:
- Outcomes: Meets expectations
 - Collaboration: Exceeds expectations (led cross-team incident simulation)
 - Growth: Demonstrated learning in kernel-level perf analysis
sections.heading: Manager assessment

sections.body:
- Follow-up sprint to roll out cache to production with rollout plan; mentor pairing on kernel profiling.

Related resources
-----------------
- /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-checklist-2025
- /confluence/people-ops/promotion-guidelines-2024
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-onboarding

Owner & contacts
----------------
People Ops (Lead): Priya Natarajan — people-ops@redwood.ai
Manager lead: Aisha Khan — aisha@redwood.ai

Change history
--------------
- 2025-11-10 — Created (Aisha Khan)
- 2026-01-15 — Updated calibration rubric and PIP flow (Miguel Alvarez)
- 2026-02-20 — Finalized templates and CLI examples; publish (Aisha Khan)

payload.page_title: Offer Rationale Kit and Decision Traceability Protocol

sections.body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s standard for composing, approving, and storing offer rationales and the associated decision traceability artifacts. It ensures hires, internal promotions, and compensation exceptions are: auditable, defensible, and consistent with compensation bands, legal constraints, and diversity-equity goals.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time, part-time, contractor conversion offers, internal promotions with comp changes, and any off-band or sign-on exceptions.
- Excludes routine offer renewals that are administrative (see HR payroll runbook).

Goals:
- Capture the evidence and approver trail for every offer.
- Reduce time-to-offer without sacrificing compliance or manager accountability.
- Provide a searchable decision log for audit, calibration, and future reference.

When to use this kit:
1) New hire offers (external candidates).
2) Internal promotions or role changes that change pay, grade, or equity.
3) Any requested deviation from published comp bands or standard sign-on practices.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager: Provide role context, candidate assessment, and initial compensation recommendation. Responsible for writing the offer rationale.
- People Partner (Recruiter/HRBP): Validate market data, flag policy exceptions, submit to approval workflow, and ensure documentation is complete.
- Compensation Approver (Finance/People ops): Final sign-off on off-band requests and any non-standard equity.
- Legal (when applicable): Review clauses for regulated hires or international hires with special contract terms.
- Hiring Committee (optional): For senior ICs, managers, and leadership hires; provides recorded consensus notes.

Process (step-by-step):
1. Manager completes the Offer Rationale Template (section below) within the ATS or People Ops portal. Attachments: candidate resume, interview scorecards, reference check summary, market comp data (LinkedIn/levels.fyi/internal comp pulls).
2. People Partner checks completeness and market alignment; if within band, marks for People Partner approval.
3. If the request is off-band or includes sign-on/relocation/equity exceptions, route to Compensation Approver.
4. Compensation Approver reviews within 48 hours (SLA). Approver either Approves, Requests more justification, or Rejects.
5. Upon approval, People Partner issues the offer and saves the executed offer letter and signed acceptance to the candidate record.
6. All artifacts are archived to the Offer Decision Log (see Documentation & storage).

Approval matrix (roles vs authority):
| Decision type                         | Hiring Manager | People Partner | Compensation Approver | Legal |
|---------------------------------------|----------------|----------------|-----------------------|-------|
| Within-band base comp                 | Recommend      | Approve        | N/A                   | N/A   |
| Off-band base comp (+/- 10%)          | Recommend      | Recommend      | Approve               | N/A   |
| Off-band base comp (> +/-10%)         | Recommend      | Recommend      | Approve (CFO signoff)| N/A   |
| Sign-on bonus / relocation             | Recommend      | Recommend      | Approve               | N/A   |
| Equity > standard grant               | Recommend      | Recommend      | Approve               | N/A   |
| Non-standard clauses (NDAs/IP/custom) | Recommend      | Recommend      | Recommend             | Review|

Time targets & SLAs:
- People Partner initial completeness check: 24 hours.
- Compensation Approver decision on off-band: 48 hours.
- Total time-to-offer target (from verbal approval to written offer): 24 hours for within-band; 72 hours for off-band.

Offer Rationale Template (required fields):
- Role (title, team, location):
- Reason for hire (replace headcount, new capability, critical business need):
- Candidate summary (2–3 sentences):
- Recommended base salary: $ value + currency
- Market comp evidence: source links and median comp for role/level
- Equity recommendation: RSU/option amount, vesting, and rationale
- Sign-on or relocation: amount and justification
- Off-band explanation (if applicable): why standard band does not apply; examples of market constraints or candidate unique skills
- Interview score summary: list of interviewers and final scores (attach scorecards)
- References summary (positive/concerns)
- People Partner notes: market context and recommended approver route
- Approvals: name, role, timestamp, decision (approve/deny/conditional)

Required attachments checklist:
1. Resume/CV
2. Interview scorecards (PDF)
3. Reference check notes
4. Market comp evidence (screenshots, reports)
5. Draft offer letter

Documentation & storage:
- All completed templates and attachments MUST be stored in the centralized Offer Decision Log (serviced by People Ops). Entry keys: candidate ID, role ID, hiring manager, date, approval chain.
- Archive retention: 7 years for hires (legal/regulatory requirement for some locations).
- Access: restricted to People Ops, Compensation, hiring manager, HRBP, and Legal (on request).

Audit & reconciliation:
- Quarterly audit: sampling of 10% of hires for compliance with template and approvals. Audit owner: Head of People Ops.
- Monthly calibration: cross-team review of high-band and off-band approvals to surface systemic issues.
- Metrics reported: average time-to-offer, % off-band offers, median approved deviation from band, diversity indicators for hires.

Decision traceability fields (machine/searchable):
- decision_id: unique UUID
- created_by: user id
- role_id, candidate_id, manager_id
- approval_chain (ordered list of approver ids)
- final_decision, decision_timestamp
- attached_documents_ids (list)
(These fields are implemented in the People Ops portal schema — use the portal form; do not try to replicate ad-hoc spreadsheets.)

Escalation & exceptions:
- If Compensation Approver does not respond in 48 hours, escalate to Head of People Ops.
- For international hires with country-specific rules, Legal must be looped before offer issuance.
- Emergency hires (market-critical within 7 calendar days): use the Emergency Approval route and document retrospective approvals within 5 business days.

Training & rollout:
- People Ops runs a 30-minute training for hiring managers and recruiters covering the template and the approval workflow.
- New manager checklist (must complete prior to first hire): Attend training, review 5 sample rationales, and shadow an offer review.

Appendix: Example filled rationale (redacted)
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer, Serving Runtime
- Reason: Replace departed senior IC to maintain backlog velocity on kernel optimizations
- Candidate summary: Ex-ML infra engineer with 7 years in inference systems, specialized in kernel fusion and quantization.
- Recommended base: $180,000 USD (Level: IC4)
- Market evidence: Internal median for IC4 is $170k; external offers indicate $175–185k in Bay Area; candidate has direct experience shipping open-source kernels.
- Equity: 8,000 RSUs one-time grant (above standard 6,000) justified by rare skill set and retention risk.
- Sign-on: $10,000 (relocation assistance).
- Interview scores: 8/10 average across system design and coding; references positive.
- Approvals: People Partner (Elena Gomez) — approved; Compensation Approver (Finance) — approved.

Appendix: Quick checklist for hiring managers (pre-offer)
1. Complete Offer Rationale Template in portal.
2. Attach scorecards, references, market evidence.
3. Confirm headcount and requisition is active.
4. Notify People Partner to start approval route.
5. Do not verbally commit off-band terms prior to Compensation Approver sign-off.

Related resources and links:
- Offer letter templates (People Ops template library)
- Compensation bands and leveling guide
- Offer Decision Log (People Ops portal)

Ownership & contact:
- Document owner: People Ops (Samantha Lee)
- Operational contact: People Partner team (people-partners@redwood.ai)

Change history:
- 2028-03-10: Created by Samantha Lee.
- 2028-03-21: Updated SLA language and added emergency approvals.

payload.page_title: First 30: Remote Sprint and Cross-Team Handoff Procedures

sections.body:
Overview:

This document defines a focused, manager-led 30-day remote sprint for newly hired or reassigned contributors whose work requires rapid cross-team integration (product, platform, and customer-facing teams). The goal is to convert Day-0 orientation into measurable contribution by Day 30 while ensuring clean handoffs and knowledge transfer across teams. This is an operational supplement to the standard onboarding playbooks and is intended for roles that must engage with multiple stakeholders during initial delivery windows.

Use cases:
- New IC joining a product team who will take ownership of an active feature in a cross-team roadmap.
- Internal mobility where the hire is embedded into a partner org and must deliver a first ticket/bugfix.
- Contractors/short-term hires that need fast alignment and a clear handoff at 30 days.

Key principles:
- Manager sponsorship: a named manager sponsor owns the 30-day sprint and the handoff readiness decision.
- Timebox outputs: prioritize 2–3 concrete deliverables for Day 30 (bugfix, doc, tech spike, customer ticket closure).
- Lightweight but auditable handoffs: use the Handoff Checklist (table below) with explicit owner signatures.
- Async-first communication: default to documented updates and threaded async questions; reserve synchronous time for unblockers and demos.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Hiring manager (or receiving manager): sets sprint goals, assigns sponsor, approves readiness on Day 30.
- Sponsor (peer/mentor): daily touchpoint owner; first escalation for blockers.
- Cross-team counterpart(s): provide systems access, architecture overview, and integration test expectations.
- People Ops: ensures new-hire admin tasks are complete and nudges for training completion.

30-day sprint cadence (recommended):
1) Day 0–2 (Orientation and access validation)
   - Confirm accounts (git, CI, Slack, Ticketing, VPN).
   - Run the quick-access checklist: local dev build, unit tests pass, basic infra credentials.
   - 30-minute orientation with sponsor + cross-team counterpart.
2) Day 3–10 (Discovery & small win)
   - Shadow a maintainer and review the core PR/issue backlog.
   - Deliver first small win (triage + fix or docs improvement).
   - Weekly writeup (short async note): what I inspected, what I changed, next blockers.
3) Day 11–20 (Integration & ownership)
   - Take ownership of a scoped ticket with cross-team acceptance criteria.
   - Run integration tests with guidance; update runbook or architecture note.
   - Mid-sprint review with manager and cross-team counterpart; adjust success criteria if needed.
4) Day 21–29 (Stabilize & document)
   - Complete ticket, fix follow-ups, address integration edge cases.
   - Produce a 10-minute demo recording and the handoff packet.
5) Day 30 (Handoff readiness & sign-off)
   - Demo to manager and cross-team counterpart.
   - Complete the Handoff Checklist and obtain signatures.
   - Close sprint with brief retrospective and a 30-day impact note posted to the team channel.

Handoff Checklist (required items for Day 30 sign-off):
| Item | Owner | Evidence required | Accept/Reject criteria |
|------|-------|-------------------|------------------------|
| Dev environment reproducible | IC | CI build log, run commands | Contributor can run app and tests locally with no manual secrets exchange |
| Ticket/PR merged or documented follow-up | IC | Link to PR or follow-up ticket | PR merged to main or ticket with assignee created and scheduled |
| Integration tests passing | Cross-team QA | CI badge link | Tests pass in staging and smoke checks documented |
| Runbook or ops note updated | IC | Link to doc | Steps for rollback and common troubleshooting updated |
| Demo recording + slide summary | IC | Link to recording and 1-page summary | Demo shows end-to-end flow and known gaps |
| Acceptance sign-off | Manager & Cross-team counterpart | Slack confirmation + ticket comment | Explicit approve comment in ticket or thread |

Templates and artifacts (quick copy-paste):
- Daily async update (one-sentence template):
  - "Day N: Looked at <area>; blocked by <issue>; next: <task>. Help requested from <person> if needed."
- Demo slide bullet points (1 slide):
  - Problem, Approach, What I built/fixed, How to run, Known gaps.
- Handoff packet filename convention: team-role-first30-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf

Manager's checklist (before Day 0):
- Appoint sponsor and cross-team counterpart.
- Publish 2–3 measurable sprint goals with acceptance criteria.
- Reserve 2 x 30-minute syncs per week for the first 3 weeks for unblockers.
- Ensure access escalations are prepared (security/infrastructure).

Escalation flow (blocking longer than 48 hours):
1) Sponsor escalates to manager (email + slack) with "Priority: 30-day block" label.
2) Manager opens a triage thread with cross-team counterpart and infrastructure owner.
3) If unresolved after 24 hours, people-ops is notified to support access or contracting remedies.

Success metrics (examples; choose 2–3 that map to role):
- Time-to-first-merge: target <= 14 days.
- Time-to-handoff-ready: target <= 30 days.
- Number of cross-team acceptance failures post-handoff: target 0–1 in first 30 days.
- Peer confidence survey (1–5): goal average >= 4 on "ready to support" question.

Common edge cases and remedies:
- Missing infra access: use the Access Escalation shortcut (link: /confluence/policies/access-and-permissions) and temporarily enable reviewer pair-programming until resolved.
- Role mismatch discovered in Week 2: run a 1-hour scope-reset with manager and sponsor, document agreed pivot, and adjust acceptance criteria.
- Timezone-heavy dependencies: schedule overlapping collaboration windows and convert critical handoffs to video demos for async review.

Retention-minded additions (if role is permanent):
- Pair the hire with a 6-week mentor rotation (two 1-hour shadow sessions per week).
- Set a 15-min career check-in at Day 30 focused on growth signals and role clarity.

Appendix: example Day 30 sign-off comment (copyable)
"Day 30 sign-off: I (Manager Name) confirm that <Person> has completed the agreed sprint goals: [link to PR], [link to runbook], [link to demo]. Cross-team counterpart <Name> confirms integration acceptance. Follow-ups: <list>."

Related references:
- New hire impact pathways and manager templates (/confluence/people-ops/new-hire-impact-pathways-and-manager-templates-2026)
- Access and permissions policy (/confluence/policies-and-process/access-and-permissions)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: annual or after any onboarding platform change.
- Change log: 2028-08-01 created; 2028-11-02 clarified test acceptance criteria and added retention items.

payload.page_title: Talent acquisition and first-120-days handbook

sections.body:
Summary
This handbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard hiring workflow, interviewer calibration guidance, candidate SLAs, offer/negotiation guardrails, and the structured first-120-days (manager + new-hire) ramp plan. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, and people-ops partners.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce variability in hiring outcomes, accelerate new-hire productivity, and provide managers pragmatic checklists to own execution.
- Scope: All full-time and core contractor hires across engineering, product, and go-to-market teams. Excludes contingent vendors and agency contractors (see vendor onboarding doc).

Principles we follow
1) Candidate experience matters: respond within SLA windows, transparent feedback, respectful scheduling.
2) Evidence-based hiring: decisions rely on rubric scores + hiring manager calibration.
3) Manager ownership: hiring, onboarding logistics, and performance signals are manager responsibilities with people-ops support.
4) Continuous calibration: interviewers attend quarterly calibration sessions and update rubrics.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference)
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview panel selection, final decision, first-120-days plan, career conversation at 90/120 days.
- Recruiter: sourcing strategy, scheduling, offer preparation, candidate communications, diversity sourcing targets.
- Interviewers: complete rubrics, provide written feedback within 48 hours, surface concerns early.
- People Ops: compensation bands, background checks, documentation, onboarding logistics, run manager calibration training.

Standard hiring workflow (timeline expectations)
1) Role kickoff (Day 0–3)
   - Manager completes role brief template (template link) and must attach: job mission, top 3 success metrics for first 6 months, required vs nice-to-have skills, proposed interview loop.
2) Sourcing and sieve (Day 1–14)
   - Recruiter returns shortlist within 7–10 business days for active reqs. Diversity-sourcing target: at least 30% of longlist from underrepresented groups where feasible.
3) Interview loop (Day 7–21)
   - Interview panel: 4–6 interviews (technical, design, system sense, collaboration/culture) recommended. No more than 2 back-to-back interviews without a 15-minute break.
4) Decision and offer (Day 21–28)
   - Hiring manager submits hire memo with anonymized rubric summary. Recruiter prepares offer within 48 hours of approval.
5) Acceptance to start (Day 30–60)
   - Standard notice period target: 30 days. Escalate if longer to people-ops for special onboarding support.

Candidate experience SLA (service-level agreements)
- Recruiter initial reply to inbound application: 2 business days.
- First interview scheduled after initial screen: within 7 business days for active roles.
- Interview feedback provided to candidate: within 7 business days of final interview.
- Offer response window: standard 7 calendar days (extendable with recruiter approval).

Interview rubric (scoring and guidance)
- Scoring scale: 1–5 (1 = does not meet, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = outstanding).
- Dimensions (apply per role):
  - Core competency (domain knowledge / technical skill)
  - Problem solving & debugging
  - System design / architecture (if applicable)
  - Collaboration & communication
  - Ownership & execution
  - Role-specific signals (product sense, sales aptitude, security mindshare)
- Minimum hire thresholds (guideline): average score >= 3.5 AND no single dimension < 2 unless hiring manager documents a compelling exception.

Example rubric table (paste into interview form)
| Dimension | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Problem solving | Incorrect approach, cannot reason about tradeoffs | Basic solution with gaps | Solid approach, some clarity issues | Strong approach with good tradeoffs | Exceptional insight and tradeoff analysis |
| Collaboration | Unable to accept feedback | Limited examples of teamwork | Clear examples of cross-team work | Drives collaboration proactively | Influences cross-org outcomes |

Calibration & training
- Quarterly calibration sessions run by people-ops (60 minutes). Attendance required for interviewers who did >6 interviews that quarter.
- Calibration agenda: 3 anonymized debriefs, rubric edge cases, signal alignment for leveling.

Offer & comp guidelines
- Compensation anchors: use current comp bands (see related_pages). Compensation must be approved by people-ops for any offer above band midpoint + 15%.
- Equity: recommended grants for ICs and managers based on level (see comp bands doc).
- Counter-offer handling: recruiter and manager coordinate; avoid incentivizing multiple-stage counter cycles.

Background checks & compliance
- Standard pre-hire checks: identity verification, employment verification, and reference check for ICs at level 4+.
- For hires in regulated markets (EU data residency or healthcare customers): initiate enhanced checks (people-ops will advise).

First-120-days structured ramp (manager + new-hire checklists)
Manager checklist (pre-boarding) — 2 weeks before start:
- Confirm offer acceptance and start date in HRIS.
- Add to team calendar, assign buddy, confirm hardware & network access, create agenda for day 1.

Day 1–14: orientation & context
- Week 1 objectives:
  - Orientation: company mission, code of conduct, security basics (complete security course by day 5).
  - Team orientation: context doc, architecture tour, current roadmap, key stakeholders.
  - Quick win: assign a read-only task and a small actionable task to deliver in week 2.
- Manager deliverables: 30-minute daily check-ins for week 1, assign a mentor, set expectations for 1:1 cadence.

Day 15–60: ownership & delivery
- Objectives:
  - Deliver the small project and present findings.
  - Shadow main workflows (deploys, triage, design reviews).
  - Complete two cross-functional introductions.
- Manager deliverables: weekly 1:1s, feedback at 30-day checkpoint.

Day 61–120: impact & career conversation
- Objectives:
  - Lead a medium-scope project or feature.
  - Demonstrate independent execution and cross-team coordination.
  - Prepare a 90–120 day review packet: accomplishments, blockers, and development goals.
- Manager deliverables: 90 and 120-day review conversations; align on success metrics and development plan.

90/120-day evaluation rubric (manager uses to guide conversation)
- Signals of success (examples): delivered assigned scope, communicative and responsive, adopted team practices, positive peer feedback.
- Areas requiring attention: needs additional mentorship, performance gaps, cultural/behavioral concerns.

Performance & feedback cycles integration
- New hires are added to the standard performance cadence after their 90-day checkpoint. For levels with probationary reviews, managers must document progress and escalate to people-ops if risk of separation is >30% at day 90.
- Feedback cadence: 1:1 weekly for first 90 days, then standard 1:1 cadence per team. People-ops recommends documented 1:1 notes stored in manager wiki.

Onboarding success metrics (people-ops will track quarterly)
- Time to first PR/merge (goal: <= 30 days for engineering ICs).
- Time to independent ownership of a component (goal: <= 90 days).
- New-hire onboarding NPS (survey at day 14 and day 90; target NPS >= +40).

Escalation and separation guidance
- If a new-hire shows sustained performance issues between day 30–90, manager must: 1) document examples, 2) run an improvement plan with clear milestones (30 days), 3) loop in people-ops for coaching.
- People-ops will provide legal/termination checklist if separation proceeds.

Manager quick-start guide (5-minute read)
- Before offer: write a crisp success profile (3 success metrics).
- Before day 1: assign buddy, create 30/60/90 outcomes, reserve 1 hour for architecture deep dive.
- Weekly: document one piece of feedback, schedule a short peer sync for cross-team visibility.

Templates and examples
- Interview scheduling email (short):
  "Hi {candidate}, thanks for applying. We’d like to schedule a 45‑minute interview to go over your experience and a technical exercise. Are you available: [times]?"
- 30-day checkpoint template (manager -> people-ops):
  "New hire: {name}, start: {date}, status: on-track/at-risk, notes: {summary}"

Sample JSON snippet: interview feedback (to paste into the interview form)
```
{
  "candidate": "Jane Doe",
  "role": "Software Engineer",
  "interviewer": "Alex Chen",
  "scores": {"problem_solving": 4, "system_design": 3, "collaboration": 5},
  "recommendation": "hire_with_feedback",
  "notes": "Strong collaborator; needs deeper system design examples."
}
```
Related documents & links
- Offer approval and comp bands (related_pages)
- IT & security new-hire checklist (related_pages)

Maintenance and governance
- Owner: people-ops (Aisha Patel). Review cadence: annual review in Q4 + immediate updates for legal or significant process changes.
- Change process: propose changes in PR to this doc, run pilot for one quarter, then update handbook after calibration session.

Appendix: common scenarios (fast answers)
- Remote hires across APAC: set start times that accommodate overlap with US teams; ensure payroll and benefits check with finance.
- Hires requiring visa sponsorship: escalate at role kickoff; expect 60+ day timeline and variable costs.
- Re-hiring ex-employees: follow rehiring policy and cooling period (see policies doc).

End of handbook. For questions or to request templates, contact people-ops@redwood.com.
