payload.page_title: Structured Contributor Onboarding and Observable Outcomes

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a standardized, competency-centered onboarding pathway for individual contributors and IC+ roles that focuses on observable outcomes, measurable checkpoints, and a lightweight certification at the end of the probation period. It synthesizes recruiting handoffs, manager preboarding, the first 90-day plan, and the role certification rubric into one reference.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time IC hires (engineers, data scientists, product managers, design) and long-term contractors converting to headcount.
- Not a substitute for team-specific immersion rotations; it is the baseline that every manager must implement and adapt.

Principles

1. Observable outcomes over subjective impressions: define three concrete signals of success by day 30, 60, and 90.
2. Manager-led but cross-functional: managers own delivery; peers and platform teams provide access, mentoring, and code reviews.
3. Lightweight, evidence-based certification: avoid long forms — evidence is artifacts (PRs, docs, dashboard) and short rubrics.
4. Equity and consistency: every candidate receives the same minimum set of resources, timelines, and evaluation criteria.

Quick summary checklist (manager preboarding, to be completed before new hire start)

1) Offer to onboarding handoff completed by People Ops (relevant docs & benefits)
2) Manager: welcome note and 90-day objectives sent to candidate and people-ops on calendar (template below)
3) Access requests created: cloud account, code repo, Slack, ticketing, payroll
4) Hardware order placed and delivery ETA confirmed
5) Buddy assigned and 1:1 schedule for first 6 weeks created

Detailed 90-day outcome map

| Time window | Focus area | Observable signals (examples) | Owner |
|-------------|------------|-----------------------------|-------|
| Day 0–30 | Orientation & small-impact delivery | Onboarding PR merged; one customer-facing doc updated; first meaningful code review completed | Manager + Buddy |
| Day 30–60 | Ownership and integration | Independent ownership of one minor feature or bug sprint; demonstrates monitoring/alert understanding; contributes to design discussion | Manager + Tech Lead |
| Day 60–90 | Scale & impact | Delivers feature to production or ships measurable improvement; mentor a peer during handoff; documents runbook or operational checklist | Manager + Product/PM |

Procedures and templates

A) Manager welcome note (email/Slack template)

```
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — first week plan
Hi [Name], welcome to the team! For your first week please expect: 1) orientation call at 09:30 on Monday; 2) access & device setup; 3) a short pairing session with [Buddy]. My 90-day outcomes for you are attached — we will review them on day 7 and weekly after. Let me know any questions. — [Manager name]
```

B) First week schedule (minimum)

- Day 1: HR & benefits overview (People Ops), team kickoff, hardware check, security briefing
- Day 2: Dev environment setup, first story assigned (small), buddy pairing
- Day 3: Product context deep-dive, metrics & dashboards intro, local run of service
- Day 4: Cross-functional sync & design walkthroughs
- Day 5: Small demo + retro with manager and buddy

C) Evidence capture & folder structure (required)

- Personal onboarding folder: /teams/<team>/onboarding/<firstname_lastname>
- Required artifacts: onboarding PR link, first feature ticket, monitoring/dashboard screenshot, 30/60/90 retrospective note

Role certification rubric (end of probation — 90 days)

Instructions: Manager and tech lead jointly score the IC on 5 criteria; use 1–5 scale (1 = not observed / 5 = exceeds expectations). Pass threshold: average >= 3.25 and no single criterion < 2.

| Criterion | What to look for | Example evidence |
|-----------|------------------|------------------|
| Technical delivery | Completes assigned tasks; code quality; shipping to prod | PRs merged, release notes, peer review comments |
| Product/context understanding | Knows customer goals & metrics | Dashboard snapshots, design notes, tickets linked to metrics |
| Collaboration & communication | Participates in async & sync, gives/receives feedback | Meeting notes, code review feedback, stakeholder threads |
| Operational ownership | Understands alerts, oncall basics, runbooks | Runbook created/updated, incident toy example handled |
| Learning velocity & initiative | Seeks feedback, grows skills quickly | Training completions, paired sessions, mentorship notes |

Scoring matrix (example)

- 5: Consistently above expectations; independently improves processes
- 4: Meets expectations and occasionally exceeds them
- 3: Meets expectations with normal guidance
- 2: Partially meets expectations; several gaps require active coaching
- 1: Does not meet expectations; escalation required

Decision outcomes and next steps

- Pass: IC is certified into role. Update HR systems, set next-level goals, consider increased autonomy and ownership.
- Conditional pass: Extend probation 30 days with documented improvement plan and weekly check-ins.
- Fail: Initiate offboarding or role change procedure per HR policy. Always coordinate with People Ops and Legal for risk & compliance steps.

Escalation and support flow

- If scoring shows any criterion <= 2 after week 8, manager must notify People Ops and present evidence-based improvement plan within 5 business days.
- People Ops will triage, recommend coaching resources, or escalate to Director-level review if necessary.

Operational playbooks and integrations (quick links)

- Access request template: /confluence/eng-infra/access-request-playbook
- Device procurement SLA: device should be delivered by day 3 where possible, see /confluence/people-ops/hardware-and-equipment-guidelines
- Security onboarding checklist: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth

Metrics and reporting

Each manager should report aggregated onboarding health monthly to People Ops including: time-to-first-PR, time-to-production, percent passing probation, and mean rubric scores. People Ops will run quarterly analyses to detect systematic bias or bottlenecks (e.g., hardware delays, access failures).

Manager responsibilities (summary)

- Own writing and communicating the 90-day outcomes before start date.
- Schedule and run weekly 1:1s for first 12 weeks.
- Collect evidence artifacts and score with tech lead at day 90.
- Escalate concerns early and partner with People Ops.

Appendices

A. Example 90-day outcome template (editable)
- Outcome 1 (30d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]
- Outcome 2 (60d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]
- Outcome 3 (90d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]

B. Short checklist for buddies

- Intro to team norms and cadence
- Schedule three pairing sessions in weeks 1–3
- Provide at least two inline review examples and one retrospective on day 30

Change log

- 2026-01-15 — Created by Aisha Thompson (initial published version).
- 2026-03-22 — Updated scoring threshold and added escalation SLA (reviewers: Jae Park, Marta Alvarez).

Owners

- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Thompson)
- Implementation owner: Hiring managers (each respective manager)

Related policies and references

- Employee handbook: /confluence/company-handbook/01_working-at-redwood
- Interview and scorecard standards: /confluence/people-ops/interview-calibration-and-hiring-scorecard-guidelines-2025
- Probation guidance: /confluence/people-ops/probation-acceleration-and-360-guidelines-2026

End of document

payload.page_title: Deceleration and Re‑Entry Playbook: Sabbaticals, Parental Leave, and Extended Absences

sections.body: This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard process for supporting employees who take extended leaves (sabbaticals, parental leave, medical leave >8 weeks) and for their structured re‑entry. The goal is to preserve psychological safety and career trajectory while maintaining team continuity and measurable ramp-up to full productivity. This is a people-ops + manager playbook, intended for managers, HR business partners, people-ops leads, and SRE/product partners who must coordinate coverage and knowledge transfer.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Applies to all full-time employees and long-term contractors with approved leaves of 8+ weeks.
- Covers pre-leave deceleration, formal handoff, coverage plans, re-entry options (full-time, phased, part-time), 30/60/90 re-onboarding, promotion/compensation considerations, and measurement.
- Does NOT replace legal leave entitlement or benefits policies; see Payroll & Leaves policy for statutory specifics.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Respect autonomy: Encourage employee-driven leave plans and voluntary check-in cadence.
- Career neutrality: Time on leave should not be a de facto blocker for promotion or role changes; managers must document rationale for any adverse decisions.
- Predictable coverage: Teams must plan a coverage path with named owners and success criteria.
- Measured ramp: Define concrete metrics that signal readiness to be considered ‘fully productive’.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
1) Pre-Leave (8–4 weeks before): Deceleration and documentation phase.
   - Employee + manager agree on public leave dates, expected return window, and preferred communication.
   - Create Handoff Plan (see template below).
   - Identify interim owner(s) and prepare temporary access/role changes.
2) Pre-Leave (4–0 weeks): Freeze and transition.
   - Code freeze for major changes tied to feature slates if feasible.
   - Execute knowledge-transfer sessions (recorded).
   - Confirm payroll/benefits and HR checklists complete.
3) Leave period: Minimal required check-ins (employee preference drives cadence).
4) Return (0–2 weeks): Administrative re-onboarding.
   - Restore access, reintroduce to team, set re-entry 30/60/90 plan.
5) Re-Entry Ramp (weeks 1–12): Measured skill/capacity recovery with staged ownership.
sections.heading: High-level timeline (recommended)

sections.body:
- Manager:
  - Initiate leave planning conversation and file Handoff Plan.
  - Nominate interim owners and set rolling goals.
  - Own performance calibration implications and document decisions.
- Employee on leave:
  - Provide prioritized list of active projects, single-line definitions, and contact preferences.
  - Record 2–3 short ‘how-to’ videos for key workflows when possible.
- Interim Owner(s):
  - Maintain the listed SLOs, keep stakeholder updates, and escalate unresolved issues.
- People-ops (HRBP):
  - Validate legal/benefits steps, advise on re-entry options, and ensure equity checks.
- Tech Ops / SRE / Security:
  - Manage temporary access changes and audit logging.
sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities

sections.body:
- Document title: Handoff — [Employee] — [Primary projects]
- Top-line summary (1 paragraph)
- Active tickets and their owners (link to ticket list)
- Pending PRs and blockers (include approximate effort estimate)
- Release windows and rollback plans (if applicable)
- Decision log: recent trade-offs and rationale (2–5 bullets)
- Who to contact for escalation and their communication channel
- Known risks and mitigation steps
sections.heading: Handoff Plan (must be created pre-leave)

sections.body:
- Short-term shift: redistribute tasks across existing team members (low cost, high distributed risk).
- Interim IC hire (contractor) for critical path work (preferred when specialized knowledge is required).
- Temporary backfill (headcount reallocation for leaves > 6 months).

Administrative steps checklist (manager + HR):
- [ ] Submit Leave Request in Workday or internal portal
- [ ] Handoff Plan filed in team space and linked to calendar
- [ ] Define interim owner(s) and permissions
- [ ] Schedule recorded knowledge-transfer sessions
- [ ] Update oncall rota and runbooks (SRE)
- [ ] Confirm benefits/payroll entries
- [ ] Schedule re-entry meeting 2–4 weeks before return (employee preference)

Re-Entry options (employee choice; manager + HR to support):
- Full-time immediate return (standard)
- Phased return (recommended default for medical/parental leaves): 2–8 weeks of reduced hours with a documented ramp plan
- Part-time for an agreed window (documented impact to compensation/benefits where applicable)

30/60/90 Re-Entry Plan template (manager + employee co-authored):
- 30 days (intended outcomes): reconnect to codebase, close 1 small ticket, attend core syncs, pair with two teammates. Success signals: unblock time <48h for core repo, two integration PRs merged.
- 60 days (intended outcomes): re-assume ownership for a medium-priority subcomponent, lead one demo. Success signals: owner signoff, automated tests passing, stakeholder acceptance.
- 90 days (intended outcomes): full role responsibilities restored (unless a longer phased plan agreed). Success signals: measurable baseline metrics tied to pre-leave performance or documented adjusted goals.
sections.heading: Coverage options (choose one and document rationale)

sections.body:
- Default: time on approved leave is not punitive. If promotion cycles occur during leave, managers must:
  1) Proactively evaluate evidence available (pre-leave work, handoff artifacts, return ramp progress).
  2) If insufficient evidence exists, document a clear path and timeline to collect evaluation evidence post-return (e.g., 6–12 weeks of performance).
  3) Any exceptions must be routed to people-ops/compensation for review.
sections.heading: Promotion and compensation guidance

sections.body:
- Weekly 1:1s for first 8 weeks focused on reorientation and well-being.
- Monthly milestone review against 30/60/90 plan up to 6 months.
- Explicitly document any performance concerns and remediation timeline; managers should avoid surprises by initiating early feedback sessions.
sections.heading: Performance management and feedback cadence post-return

sections.body:
- Time-to-first-merge (target: within 14 business days)
- Number of restored primary responsibilities (target: 80% by day 90)
- Manager-reported confidence score (weekly, 1–5 scale)
- Employee-reported readiness and well-being check (pulse at weeks 2, 6, 12)
sections.heading: Measurement and signals of successful re-entry

sections.body:
- People-ops will run quarterly audits comparing promotion/payout outcomes for employees who took leaves vs. similar peers.
- Any perceived negative impact should trigger a case review with the HRBP and manager.
sections.heading: Equity & exceptions

sections.body:
- Access suspension should be minimal and reversible. Use documented groups and temporary tokens.
- SRE must record all access changes in the access audit log; manager must confirm access restoration on day 0 of return.
sections.heading: Security and access notes

sections.body:
- All-hands leave announcement (short):
  "[Name] will be on leave from [start] to [end]. During this period, [Interim Owner] will own [projects]. Please route urgent issues to [email/contact]. Join us in wishing them well."

- Re-entry welcome note (team message):
  "Welcome back [Name]! We'll do a light re-onboarding schedule: 1:1 at 10am, team sync at 2pm, and a reorientation doc linked here. Reach out if you need adjustments to your schedule."
sections.heading: Sample communications (templates)

sections.body:
- 2–4 short screen-capture videos (5–10 min) for high-value workflows
- A README that answers: What it is, Where to look, Who to call (top three people), Quick triage steps
- Tag important PRs with label "reentry-reference"
sections.heading: Knowledge transfer artifacts (recommended)

sections.body:
- If interim owner disagrees on priority, escalate to manager -> product lead -> people-ops.
- If manager and employee disagree on phased return terms, HRBP mediates and documents final agreement.
sections.heading: Conflict scenarios and escalation path

sections.body:
- Internal: Payroll & Leaves policy (link)
- Internal: Manager Performance Calibration playbook (link)
- Template: Handoff Plan (link)
- Template: Re-entry 30/60/90 (link)

Appendix A — Example Handoff checklist (text table):
- Column headers: Item | Owner | Status | Notes
- Example row: "Feature X integration" | "Nina Patel (interim)" | "In progress" | "API contract stable; tests flake on staging"

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: Can employees be contacted during leave?
A: Contact frequency is employee preference; only urgent safety or legal matters may warrant outreach. Document preferred method in the Handoff Plan.

Q: Who signs off on ending phased return early?
A: The manager and employee mutually agree; people-ops should be informed and the decision recorded in the performance notes.
sections.heading: Related pages and templates (links)

sections.body:
- Document owner: People Ops — Aisha Patel
- Last major revision: 2029-05-02 — added measurement signals and promotion guidance
- Minor edits tracked in page history.

If you have questions or need a custom accommodation, contact people-ops@redwood.com or your HRBP.

payload.page_title: Position Readiness Sprint and Manager Handbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This handbook defines the Position Readiness Sprint (PRS): a structured 2-week pre-boarding and 90-day ramp framework that shifts ownership of role activation from People Ops to hiring managers. The PRS reduces time-to-impact, standardizes manager responsibilities, and ensures consistent data capture for hiring and calibration.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all new full-time and contractor technical and product roles.
- Optional lightweight variant for customer success, sales, and corporate roles (see Related Templates).
- Excludes promotions/transfers within the first 90 days (use internal transfer checklist).

Desired outcomes and KPIs
------------------------
- Time-to-impact: target median = 45 days to first independent deliverable.
- Ramp completion rate: 85% of hires reach baseline competency by day 90.
- Manager compliance: 95% of PRS checklists completed within deadlines.
- Access SLA: 95% of accounts and tools provisioned by Day -1 (pre-boarding).

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- Hiring Manager (owner): lead PRS, create role-specific success criteria, run weekly check-ins, complete evaluation at 30/60/90 days.
- People Ops (enablement): run PRS templates, schedule orientation sessions, audit checklist completion, support calibration.
- New Hire Buddy: day‑to‑day onboarding partner for first 30 days.
- IT/Security: provision accounts, grant required access, confirm MFA and SSO.
- Hiring Panel/Team Lead: provide 1:1 shadow/knowledge transfer sessions in week 2–4.

Position Readiness Sprint (2-week pre-boarding) — step-by-step
------------------------------------------------------------
1) Initiate PRS (Immediately after offer accepted)
   - Manager opens PRS ticket in People Ops portal within 24 hours and attaches: role success criteria, 90-day deliverables, and preferred buddy.
   - People Ops sends pre-boarding checklist to hiring manager and new hire.

2) Week -2 to -1: Pre-boarding tasks (People Ops / IT SLA)
   - IT: create accounts, add to org groups, enable SSO, and verify MFA (SLA: 48 hours).
   - Manager: share first-week schedule and welcome doc; assign buddy; confirm equipment requests.
   - New Hire: complete HR forms, benefits enrollment, and security training module.

3) Day 0 — orientation and role kickoff
   - 90-minute orientation (People Ops): company mission, culture, policies, benefits, security.
   - Manager: 60-minute role kickoff covering success criteria, immediate deliverables, and team norms.
   - Buddy: schedule recurring micro-check-ins (15m) for first 30 days.

4) Week 1–4: Foundations and early deliverable
   - Manager sets a small, clear first deliverable due by day 30.
   - Weekly 1:1 focused on blockers and learning plan.
   - Week 2: shadow session with primary stakeholders.

5) Day 30 / Day 60 / Day 90 reviews (structured)
   - Manager completes templated evaluation and ratings against success criteria.
   - Calibration: People Ops aggregates results for hiring cohort review every 6 weeks.

90-day ramp plan (example table)
--------------------------------
| Period     | Focus                      | Manager actions                              | Measurement/Artifacts                     |
| Week 0     | Role setup & access        | Confirm tools, intro, assign buddy           | Access checklist complete                  |
| Week 1–4   | Learning + first deliverable| Weekly 1:1, pair programming, stakeholder intros | Deliverable demo, feedback notes          |
| Week 5–8   | Increasing autonomy        | Reduce pair work, assign independent tasks   | Code review independence, feature PRs     |
| Week 9–12  | Owner of feature area      | Handover small features, lead retro          | Completed project, manager sign-off       |

Manager Checklist (must-complete items)
--------------------------------------
- [ ] PRS ticket opened within 24h of offer acceptance.
- [ ] Role success criteria defined and shared.
- [ ] Buddy assigned and introduced by Day -1.
- [ ] First deliverable assigned and deadline set.
- [ ] Weekly 1:1 scheduled for 90 days.
- [ ] 30/60/90 evaluations submitted on schedule.

Templates and sample communications
----------------------------------
Sample pre-boarding email (send Day -10 to -3)
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — First steps and your week 0 schedule
Hi [Name],
Welcome — we’re excited to have you join as [Title]. Attached is your week 0 schedule, company handbook links, and a short welcome doc from your manager. Please complete the HR and security forms before Day 0.
Best,
[Manager name]

Sample 30-day manager evaluation snippet
"Has the new hire demonstrated the technical baseline required for independent contributions?
- Evidence: PR merged with minimal revisions, stakeholder feedback attached."

Operational SLAs and tooling
---------------------------
- IT provisioning: create accounts + grant core tool access within 48 hours of PRS ticket.
- Equipment fulfillment: shipping within 5 business days after equipment request approval.
- PRS ticketing: People Ops will auto-remind managers at Day -7 and Day 0 if checklists are incomplete.
- Data capture: all PRS artifacts (evaluations, deliverables, feedback) stored in HRIS and linked to People Ops PRS ticket.

Measurement and continuous improvement
-------------------------------------
- People Ops runs monthly reports on: median time-to-impact, checklist compliance, and ramp completion rate.
- Quarterly retro: at least one hiring cohort retro per quarter to identify friction (tooling, slack channels, access issues).
- Experiment: alternate PRS with cohort onboarding once per quarter to measure signal on team cohesion.

Escalation path
---------------
1) Manager-level blocker: contact People Ops (prs-ops@redwood.ai) for exceptions.
2) Access/security blocker: open a Priority-1 ticket with IT, CC People Ops.
3) Performance concerns before Day 90: manager and People Ops schedule a check-in and follow progressive performance framework.

Manager success rubric (quick reference)
--------------------------------------
- Green: Completes all checklists, hires reach baseline by Day 60.
- Yellow: Minor checklist misses, hires meet baseline by Day 90 with support.
- Red: Multiple misses, hires do not meet baseline; triggers coaching and calibration with People Ops.

Appendices
---------
- Appendix A: PRS ticket template (copy into People Ops portal).
- Appendix B: Role success criteria examples (engineering, product, data).
- Appendix C: Links to learning resources and mandatory trainings.

Related pages
-------------
See also: onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026 (templates), first-year-engagement-and-success-milestones-2028 (career milestones).

----------------

payload.page_title: Off-Cycle Performance Snapshots and Calibration Process

sections.body: Overview
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This document defines Redwood Inference’s process for running off-cycle performance snapshots and the subsequent calibration protocol. Off-cycle snapshots are lightweight, evidence-backed evaluations used when a formal quarterly or annual review is not appropriate but a documented assessment is required (e.g., role change, manager transition, accelerated promotion consideration, serious performance concern, or return-from-leave reintegration).
sections.heading: Purpose

sections.body:
- Applies to all full-time and fixed-term employees globally.
- Excludes contractors on engagements shorter than 90 days unless a manager requests evidence for a conversion decision.
- Operated by People Ops in partnership with the employee’s manager and the manager’s manager for calibration.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body:
- Provide consistent, time-bounded evidence to support ad-hoc talent decisions.
- Reduce bias by using a shared rubric and normalization step.
- Keep evidence lightweight (2–4 artifacts + calibrated rating) to avoid review fatigue.
sections.heading: Why we run off-cycle snapshots

sections.body:
- Snapshot: A 7–14 calendar day evidence collection and assessment for an individual.
- Snapshot Outcome: One of {No Action, Focus Plan (30–60d), Promotion Recommendation, Role Alignment Review, Offboarding Recommendation}.
- Calibration Review: A decision meeting where managers compare snapshots and normalize ratings before People Ops finalizes outcomes.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) Promotion acceleration request (manager-submitted).
2) Manager change or reassignment.
3) Return from leave >60 days seeking role/level confirmation.
4) Clear performance regression observed and requiring documented short-term intervention.
5) Role misalignment identified during onboarding or cross-functional transfer.
sections.heading: Triggers (non-exhaustive)

sections.body:
1) Initiation (Day 0)
   - Owner: Manager or People Ops.
   - Action: Complete the Snapshot Intake Form (see Appendix A). Form fields include trigger type, proposed outcome, core evidence items, and deadline (7–14 days).
   - SLA: People Ops acknowledges request within 1 business day.
2) Evidence Collection (Days 1–10)
   - Owner: Manager + Employee.
   - Required artifacts (pick at least 2):
     • Recent code PRs or design docs with reviewer comments (if applicable).
     • Customer/partner feedback emails or support tickets.
     • Product metrics/experiments showing impact (dashboard links).
     • Peer feedback (2–3 short notes; use standardized feedback template).
     • On-call incident participation notes or post-incident analysis.
   - Optional artifacts: training completion certificates, mentor notes, speed-of-delivery metrics.
3) Manager Assessment (within 2 business days of evidence close)
   - Owner: Manager.
   - Action: Complete the Snapshot Assessment using the standardized rubric (Skills, Impact, Autonomy, Collaboration). Each dimension scored on a 1–5 scale with 1–2 = Below Expectations, 3 = Meets Expectations, 4 = Exceeds, 5 = Strongly Exceeds.
   - Deliverable: One-page assessment summary and suggested Snapshot Outcome.
4) Peer/Counterbalance Review (optional for high-impact or promotion requests)
   - Owner: Cross-functional peer reviewers (identified by manager).
   - Action: Provide short corroborating comments (use People Ops micro-feedback form).
5) Calibration Review (within 7 business days of manager assessment)
   - Owner: People Ops facilitates.
   - Participants: Manager, Manager’s Manager, People Ops representative; for promotions, include a Leveling Panel member from Product or Eng leadership.
   - Agenda: Pre-read distribution, 10–15 minute discussion per snapshot, normalization, and final outcome recording.
   - Decision authority: Manager’s Manager signs off on outcome; People Ops records the decision and next steps.
6) Outcome communication (within 2 business days of calibration)
   - Owner: Manager (with People Ops copy).
   - Action: Deliver outcome to employee in one-on-one; for Focus Plans or Promotion Recommendations, attach a written plan or promotion packet template.
7) Follow-up and Closure
   - Owner: Manager and People Ops.
   - Action: Track Focus Plan progress weekly; for Promotions, assemble full promotion packet within 30 days and follow standard promotion workflow.
sections.heading: Process (step-by-step)

sections.body:
- Acknowledgement: 1 business day after initiation.
- Evidence window: 7–14 calendar days (default 10).
- Calibration completion: within 7 business days of manager assessment.
- Outcome communicated: within 2 business days of calibration.
- Total end-to-end target: 21 calendar days.
sections.heading: Timelines and SLAs

sections.body:
- Skills (technical / role skills): 1–5
- Impact (customer, revenue, product): 1–5
- Autonomy (problem solving, decision quality): 1–5
- Collaboration (communication, cross-team work, mentorship): 1–5
- Notes: Attach concrete evidence links and one-line summary per dimension.
sections.heading: Standardized Rubric (short)

sections.body:
- Use historical distribution: mean rating per level documented in Leveling Panel page.
- If manager’s suggested outcome differs from distribution by >1 level, Manager’s Manager must present concrete evidence during calibration.
- For promotions, require at least two independent corroborating artifacts beyond manager testimony.
sections.heading: Normalization guidance

sections.body:
- Average score <2.5 -> Focus Plan or Offboarding Recommendation (depending on evidence severity).
- Average score 2.5–3.5 -> No Action or Development Focus Plan.
- Average score 3.6–4.2 -> Meets to Exceeds: consider stretch assignments or role alignment.
- Average score >4.2 -> Promotion Recommendation (requires corroboration).

Table: Snapshot outcomes and owner actions

| Outcome | Required artifacts | Next owner action | Timebox |
|---------|--------------------|-------------------|---------|
| No Action | Assessment summary | Document in HRIS; monitor via normal cadence | 0–30 days |
| Focus Plan | Assessment + 2 evidence links | 30–60d plan, weekly check-ins, people-ops notified | 30–60 days |
| Promotion Recommendation | Assessment + 3 artifacts + peer notes | Assemble promotion packet, Leveling Panel | 30 days |
| Role Alignment Review | Role description + gap analysis | Manager & Hiring Partner to propose options | 14–30 days |
| Offboarding Recommendation | Incident logs + formal warnings | Escalate to People Ops + Legal for next steps | immediate |
sections.heading: Decision matrix (example)

sections.body:
- Initiate Snapshot Intake Form for eligible triggers.
- Collect at least two artifacts and request peer feedback where required.
- Complete rubric with clear evidence links and one-paragraph narrative.
- Attend calibration and present the case concisely.
- Deliver outcome and follow-up plan to the employee.
sections.heading: Manager responsibilities checklist

sections.body:
- Validate that paperwork and privacy-sensitive items are redacted.
- Schedule calibration meetings and distribute pre-reads.
- Record outcomes in HRIS and maintain snapshot audit trail.
- Monitor metrics and publish quarterly summary of off-cycle snapshot outcomes by team (anonymized).
sections.heading: People Ops responsibilities

sections.body:
- Employees may request clarification within 5 business days of outcome.
- If the employee disputes a Promotion Recommendation denial, they can request an appeal to the Leveling Panel within 10 business days.
- Managers may escalate timeliness concerns to the People Ops Director.
sections.heading: Appeals and Escalations

sections.body:
- All snapshot documentation is confidential and stored in the HRIS restricted folder with role-based access.
- Sensitive customer data must be redacted unless the employee has explicit permission to share.
sections.heading: Privacy and evidence handling

sections.body:
- Time to outcome (target 21 days).
- Percentage of snapshots that lead to promotion recommendations.
- Distribution variance vs. quarterly reviews (target < 10% variance).
- Employee satisfaction with process (pulse survey after closure).

Appendix A — Snapshot Intake Form (example YAML snippet):

---
trigger: "manager_promotion_request"
proposed_outcome: "promotion_recommendation"
requested_deadline: "2026-02-17"
artifacts:
  - "PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234"
  - "Customer email: redacted@example.com"
peer_reviewers:
  - "eng-peer@example.com"
notes: "Employee led the new request routing feature and achieved 18% latency improvement."
---

Appendix B — Suggested manager communication templates (short):
- Promotion approval: "Congratulations — after calibration we are recommending promotion to [level]. Next steps: People Ops will assemble the packet and confirm comp. We will meet on [date] to discuss details."
- Focus Plan start: "We are starting a 45-day development plan focused on [skill]. We will meet weekly to review progress. I will document expectations and success criteria."
- No Action: "After review, we are not changing your level/comp at this time. We acknowledge recent work and will continue monitoring as part of regular check-ins."
sections.heading: Measurement and KPIs (sample)

sections.body:
- People Ops will review the off-cycle snapshot process annually and update rubrics based on observed variance and stakeholder feedback.
- Quarterly anonymized summary reports will be shared with People Ops leadership and Engineering HR partners.
sections.heading: Governance and review cadence

sections.body:
- Process Owner: People Ops — Sofia Martinez (people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: Director of People Ops — Asha Raman (asha@redwood.ai)
- Leveling Panel coordinator: Liam Chen (liam@redwood.ai)
sections.heading: Ownership and contacts

sections.body:
- Performance and feedback cadence (canonical quarterly review doc).
- Promotion pathways and calibration protocol.
- HRIS documentation for storing restricted artifacts.
sections.heading: Related documentation

sections.body:

- 2026-02-10: Updated normalization guidance and timelines (reviewers: Asha Raman, Liam Chen).

payload.page_title: Manager Accelerated Integration & Feedback Sprint

sections.body: This document describes the "Accelerated Integration & Feedback Sprint" — a structured, manager-led program to reduce time-to-impact for newly hired engineers and product managers. It blends an intensive first-6-month checklist with recurring mini-feedback sprints so managers and new hires reach reliable performance, cultural alignment, and measurable outcomes faster than a standard 90-day plan.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Audience: managers (IC managers, engineering managers, product managers), people-ops partners, and new hires.
- Scope: first 6 months post-offer-accept through the candidate’s first performance cycle. Applies to full-time ICs, PMs, and engineering managers. Does not replace role-specific technical onboarding tracked by teams.
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
- Make ramp predictable: define clear signals of readiness and objective milestones.
- High-frequency feedback reduces misunderstandings and accelerates behavior change.
- Manager accountability: managers own the integration outcome and coordinate cross-functional onboarding.
- Lightweight, repeatable rituals that scale across teams.
sections.heading: Principles (why this exists)

sections.body:
- Time-to-first-merge for engineers: median target 3 weeks for small fixes, 8 weeks for core-area contributions.
- First 6-month performance-readiness: 85% of hires rated “on-track” or higher in manager checkpoint.
- New-hire satisfaction (pulse): Net Promoter Score (NPS) >= 30 after 90 days.
sections.heading: Outcomes and success metrics (examples)

sections.body:
1) Pre-boarding (2 weeks before start)
   - Manager: confirm workspace, access list, team buddy, and initial project stub.
   - People-ops: share welcome packet, first-week schedule, benefits setup checklist.
2) Day 0–7: Orientation and tactical setup
   - Kick-off 1:1 + team welcome, security/IT checks, role expectations meeting.
   - Buddy assigned and onboarding sprint tasks created in JIRA.
3) Week 2–4: Early contribution loop
   - Deliverable: first changelist/PR + paired review with buddy.
   - Feedback sprint: weekly 30-minute check-in with manager focusing on blockers and clarity of scope.
4) Month 2–3: Ownership and expansion
   - Deliverable: ownerable ticket and cross-functional demo.
   - Feedback sprint: switch to bi-weekly 45-minute check-ins.
5) Month 4–6: Stabilize and measure impact
   - Deliverable: measurable impact outcome (e.g., performance improvement, feature completion, process doc).
   - 6-month review and calibration: manager writes calibration note and schedule formal checkpoint with people-ops.
sections.heading: Program overview (high level)

sections.body:
- Week 0 (Pre-boarding):
  - Send welcome email, confirm equipment, add to Slack/Teams channels.
  - Create 90-day OKRs stub in team tracker.
- Week 1:
  - Role expectations meeting, security training, and first pairing sessions.
  - Manager sets 1–3 immediate success criteria (measurable).
- Week 2–4:
  - Small production PR, feedback loop, buddy-led systems tour.
  - Document knowledge gaps in a shared doc.
- Month 2:
  - First domain ownership ticket assigned; cross-team introduction.
- Month 3:
  - Mini demo to team, publish a 1-page decision log for area.
- Month 4–5:
  - Focus on throughput and quality signals; begin mentoring others.
- Month 6:
  - 6-month calibration and development plan.
sections.heading: Week-by-week checklist (condensed)

sections.body:
- Week 0–4: Ensure low-friction access, schedule daily/weekly check-ins, remove blockers.
- Set measurable early success criteria with the new hire within the first 72 hours.
- Run weekly feedback sprints for first 4 weeks, then bi-weekly until month 3, then monthly check-ins.
- Document progress in the onboarding tracker (link to team tracker) and nominate calibration attendees.
- Provide concrete examples in feedback. Focus on behaviors and outcomes, not personality.

Feedback sprint template (30–45 minutes):
1) 5 min: state progress and wins since last meeting.
2) 10 min: discuss blockers and ask for support.
3) 15 min: focused, specific feedback from manager (2–3 action items).
4) 5–15 min: forward-looking plan and next deliverable.

Sample manager language (dos and don’ts):
- Do: "This PR had clear tests; next time, add a short note describing the performance tradeoff."
- Do: "You took initiative on the release checklist — that aligns with our team expectations for ownership."
- Don’t: "You’re too slow" (vague). Instead: "I noticed three delayed reviews this sprint; can we troubleshoot calendar conflicts?"
sections.heading: Manager responsibilities (explicit)

sections.body:
1) Offer accepted → people-ops triggers pre-boarding packet and equipment request (within 24 hours).
2) Hiring manager: select buddy and draft first-week project brief (within 48 hours).
3) IT/security: grant baseline access and enroll in MFA (by Day 0).
4) Finance/payroll: confirm benefits effective date and send benefits orientation (by Day 3).

6-month calibration rubric (table):
| Signal | On-track | Needs coaching | Misalignment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Delivery velocity | Completed 60–100% of planned tickets | 30–60% with partial blockers | <30% or repeat missed commitments |
| Code/review quality | Minor comments, consistent standards | Frequent rework but learning | Repeated critical issues |
| Collaboration | Proactive cross-team communication | Needs prompting | Avoids collaboration / repeated conflicts |
| Ownership | Drives a small project end-to-end | Contributes but needs help | No ownership demonstrated |
sections.heading: Hiring handoffs and coordination (concrete steps)

sections.body:
- On-track: continue development plan and nominate stretch goal for next cycle.
- Needs coaching: 90-day focused coaching plan with weekly manager check-ins and buddy pairing.
- Misalignment: initiate role re-scope discussion with HR and people-ops; determine performance improvement plan or role change.
sections.heading: Calibration outcomes and next steps (examples)

sections.body:
- Failure: Too many ad-hoc requests overwhelm the new hire.
  - Mitigation: Manager protects 60% focus time for onboarding during first 4 weeks.
- Failure: Feedback is infrequent or vague.
  - Mitigation: Use feedback sprint template and keep a one-line action log visible to the hire.
- Failure: New hire lacks cross-functional context.
  - Mitigation: Schedule three cross-team brown-bag sessions in month 1–2.
sections.heading: Common failure modes and mitigations

sections.body:
- First-week project brief (copyable):
  - Goal: Ship a small diagnostic fix that touches the logging pipeline.
  - Deliverables: PR, test, brief doc describing approach.
  - Success: PR merged and QA sign-off.
- Weekly inline feedback note (sample):
  - "Wins: PR X merged; Blocker: test environment flakiness; Action: I will clear test infra by Tue."
sections.heading: Templates and artifacts (included examples)

sections.body:
- People-ops maintains the master pre-boarding checklist and provides quarterly onboarding health metrics to managers.
- Each manager must attach onboarding tracker link to the hire’s profile in the HRIS.
- Escalation path: manager → people-ops partner → HR business partner → VP People.

Appendix A: Example calendar for first 4 weeks (sample)
- Mon Week 1: Orientation, security, role expectations (2 hours), team lunch.
- Tue–Wed Week 1: Systems tour and pair-programming with buddy (4 hours/day).
- Week 1 Fri: 30-min feedback sprint.
- Week 2–4: Focused work blocks, weekly sprint check-ins, 1 cross-team intro.

Appendix B: Quick checklist for people-ops (copyable)
- Send contract and benefits packet day of offer.
- Confirm start date and equipment 10 business days prior.
- Ensure buddy assigned before Day 0.
- Run 30-day onboarding pulse survey and share anonymized results with manager.
sections.heading: Operational notes and ownership

sections.body:
- Team-specific 90-day OKR templates (link to team wiki).
- Security onboarding runbook (link to eng-sre page).
sections.heading: Related references and links

sections.body:
- 2026-10-15: Created by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-12-08: Updated to add 6-month rubric (Rina Shah).
- 2027-02-01: Minor wording updates and added sample calendar (Marcus Lee).

If you have questions or suggested improvements, ping people-ops or the author.

payload.page_title: Equitable Hiring & Accessibility Standards

sections.body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's standards for equitable hiring, interview accessibility, and inclusive onboarding adjustments. It sets mandatory practices for job postings, interviewing panels, accommodation handling, and manager responsibilities during the first 90 days. The goal is to reduce bias, increase access for candidates and employees with disabilities, and ensure consistent, traceable handling of accommodation requests.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, recruiters, and people managers responsible for onboarding new hires across Redwood Inference.
- Covers external candidates, internal transfers, reboarding (returning from leave), and contractors converting to full-time employees.

Guiding principles:
1) Accessibility-first: Make the default experience accessible rather than offering accommodations as an afterthought.
2) Structure reduces bias: Use job-focused rubrics and structured interviews for all technical and role-critical interviews.
3) Timely & confidential: Acknowledge accommodation requests within 2 business days and protect candidate privacy.
4) Reasonable & pragmatic: Provide reasonable accommodations promptly unless there is a documented business constraint; consult Legal only for edge cases.

Job posting & sourcing checklist (mandatory):
- Use clear, inclusive language: prefer "required" only for non-negotiable skills; otherwise use "preferred". Avoid gendered phrasing.
- Accessibility statement: Add the standard paragraph below to every posting.
  "Redwood Inference is committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@redwood.ai or reply to your recruiter; we will respond within 2 business days."
- Minimum hiring timeline published in posting: "Typical process: application → phone screen (7 days) → on-site/loop (within 14 days) → offer (target 28 days)."
- Sourcing: track outreach channels and include at least one underrepresented talent source (university programs, affinity groups, community orgs) for every open role above IC2 / L3.

Structured interview & rubric standards (required):
- Every role must define 3–5 core competencies used to evaluate candidates (examples: system design, problem solving, collaboration, impact).
- Create a scorecard with behavioral anchors for scores 1–5 for each competency.
- Interviewers must complete scorecards within 24 hours of the interview.
- Offer threshold: candidates must meet or exceed the minimum on at least 2/3 core competencies and not score below 2 on any essential competency.
- Panel composition guidance: at least 2 interviewers per loop, diverse by team/function where feasible; include a hiring manager and a peer. Consider cross-team representation for senior roles.

Bias mitigation & interviewer training:
- Annual mandatory training for all interviewers: structured interviewing, unconscious bias, disability etiquette.
- Interviewers should avoid asking about medical history or disability during interviews. Instead, ask work-relevant questions and offer accommodations.
- Use anonymized resume review for high-volume roles when possible.

Accommodation request handling (process):
1) Candidate or employee submits request to accommodations@redwood.ai or tells recruiter/manager.
2) People-ops acknowledges receipt within 2 business days and logs a confidential accommodation ticket (internal ID).
3) People-ops coordinates with the hiring manager and recruiter to propose reasonable accommodations within 3 business days of acknowledgement.
4) If the accommodation requires third-party services (ASL interpreter, assistive tech), people-ops will coordinate procurement and cover costs.
5) Confirm accommodation in writing and document any agreed timeline changes to the interview loop.

Common accommodations and recommended options:
- Extended coding assignment time (e.g., +50%).
- Remote interview by default on request (video or phone).
- Option for screen-reader-friendly materials, accessible slide decks, transcripts, and alt-text on images.
- ASL interpreter or real-time captioning for interviews.
- Sensory-friendly interview slots (shorter sessions, extra breaks, low-video options).

Confidentiality and recordkeeping:
- Accommodation requests are stored in a secure HR system with restricted access (people-ops and the hiring manager only).
- Do not include accommodation details in candidate-facing offer letters unless necessary and consented to.

Onboarding & reboarding standards (first 90 days):
- Pre-boarding (before day 1): confirm accommodation needs and provide an accessibility checklist tailored to the role (hardware, software, environment).
- Day 0 checklist for people managers: confirm meeting preferences, calendar visibility, preferred communication channels, and any assistive tech set-up.
- Buddy assignment: assign a peer buddy trained in accessibility-aware onboarding within the first week.
- 30/60/90 plan: managers co-create the plan with the new hire in week 1, explicitly noting any adjustments (e.g., extended timelines for training tasks).
- Reboarding flow (return from extended leave): conduct a "reboard" meeting 7 days prior to return when feasible to review any workplace adjustments.

Performance review & feedback adjustments:
- Use the same structured competency-based rubric used in hiring for performance reviews to increase consistency.
- At performance review kickoff, managers must ask if any accommodations are needed for the review process itself (format, timing, support person).
- Calibration: people-ops will include an accessibility lens in calibration cycles to identify possible bias against candidates/employees who use accommodations (e.g., different communication cadence).
- Reasonable adjustments to development plans or timelines should be documented in the employee's development plan; do not equate accommodations with lowered expectations—clarify objective performance criteria and adjusted support.

Manager guide: first 30 / 60 / 90 day checklist (short):
- Day 0–7:
  1. Confirm accessibility needs and schedule technical setup with IT.
  2. Introduce buddy and schedule daily check-ins for week 1.
  3. Share 30/60/90 draft and review with new hire; incorporate preferred communication cadence.
- Day 8–30:
  1. Ensure training materials are available in accessible formats.
  2. Hold weekly 1:1 focused on role clarity and friction removal.
  3. Collect feedback from buddy and update onboarding actions.
- Day 31–90:
  1. Move from onboarding to development goals; set measurable deliverables.
  2. Schedule mid-probation check-in at day 60.
  3. Confirm whether further accommodations or adjustments are needed.

Operational metrics & targets (recommended):
- Time-to-offer target: median <= 28 calendar days from screening of qualified candidate.
- Accommodation acknowledgment SLA: 2 business days; accommodation resolution target: within 5 business days for common requests.
- Interview scorecard completion: >= 95% within 24 hours.
- Return-to-work reboarding meeting scheduled >= 7 days before return for 90% of cases.
- Candidate satisfaction (post-process survey): target NPS >= 30 for candidates who request accommodations.

Escalation & edge cases:
- If an accommodation imposes undue hardship or a legal conflict, people-ops will escalate to Legal and the Head of People for a decision within 5 business days.
- If a manager or interviewer violates confidentiality or mishandles an accommodation, report to people-ops immediately; incidents will be investigated and may lead to remedial training or disciplinary action.

Templates & examples (appendix):

  "Hi [Name],

  Thanks for letting us know about your accommodation needs. We received your request on [date] and will follow up with proposed arrangements by [date+3 business days]. If you prefer to discuss by phone, please let us know a convenient time.

  Regards,
  People Ops"

payload.page_title: Asynchronous Performance Radar and Calibration Playbook

sections.body: This playbook defines Redwood's Asynchronous Performance Radar: a lightweight, calendar-driven approach to continuous performance signals, manager calibration, and integration checkpoints that span hiring through the first year. The goal is to reduce synchronous meeting load, speed decisioning, and embed objective signal collection into the existing hiring/onboarding lifecycle.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- People Ops partners
- Engineering managers and people managers
- ICs preparing self-assessments
- Hiring managers and interview panel leads
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body:
- Provide a reliable, repeatable quarterly "radar" that aggregates: hiring fit signals, onboarding progress, 1:1 feedback extracts, and objective contribution metrics.
- Reduce time-to-decision for promotion/role changes by 25% compared to a purely synchronous calibration cycle.
- Maintain calibration coverage across 100% of managers each quarter.
- Surface candidates and new hires with risks within the first 90 days for proactive intervention.
sections.heading: Goals and success criteria

sections.body:
- Scope: Full-time employees and contractors in technical and product functions during hire -> first 12 months -> ongoing quarterly cadence. Applies to distributed and remote-work locations.
- Exclusions: Executive promotion committees (follow executive promotion process) and localized legal/performance-withdrawal processes (those follow HR casework templates).
sections.heading: Scope and exclusions

sections.body:
- Radar window: A 2-week asynchronous collection period at the end of each quarter where managers and stakeholders submit standardized signals.
- Signal types: Quantitative (OKR progress, ticket throughput, latency of code reviews) and Qualitative (peer praise, feedback snippets, interview calibration notes).
- Calibration packet: A per-manager aggregated summary used by People Ops to run lightweight cross-team calibration.
sections.heading: Key concepts

sections.body:
1) Pre-window (Q-1 week): People Ops publishes the radar packet template and runs a freshness check on onboarding checklists and hiring artifacts.
2) Window open (Day 0 — 2 weeks): Managers submit radar packets for each direct report. Hiring managers must attach interview feedback summary for hires in the last 120 days. ICs may optionally submit self-notes (recommended for promotion candidates).
3) Aggregation (Day 15—17): People Ops validates packets for completeness and computes derived metrics for reportbacks.
4) Calibration (Day 18—21): Asynchronous calibration comments collected in the packet; People Ops publishes a short highlights digest and a list of action items.
5) Close and follow-up (Day 22—30): Managers execute identified actions (career conversations, onboarding plans, PIP triggers) and update the ticket. People Ops tracks closure.
sections.heading: Process overview (high level)

sections.body:
- People Ops:
  - Publish radar window calendar at least one quarter in advance.
  - Maintain the packet template and scoring rubric.
  - Run completeness checks and surface outliers.
  - Facilitate escalation to HR for potential formal performance issues.
- Manager:
  - Complete one radar packet per direct report during the window. Attach required artifacts for new hires (interview feedback, onboarding checklist status, first-30/60/90 comments).
  - Provide at least two concrete examples (bullet points) each for strengths and areas to watch.
  - Schedule follow-up discussions within 10 business days when action is required.
- IC/Individual contributor:
  - Optional self-notes (recommended when seeking promotion).
  - Keep role-specific metrics updated in the team dashboard to feed quantitative signals.
- Hiring manager / Interview panel leads:
  - Attach the interview calibration memo for hires within first 120 days. Call out any post-hire concerns (knowledge gaps, ramp delays).
sections.heading: Detailed responsibilities

sections.body:
- Employee name
- Role and manager
- Hire date (if under 12 months)
- Onboarding status (Complete / Partial / Behind) with checklist link
- Core contribution highlights (3 bullets)
- Strengths (2 bullets)
- Areas to watch (2 bullets)
- Example evidence (links to PRs, tickets, meeting notes)
- Quantitative metrics (list metrics & values; e.g., OKR progress 60%, code review mean latency 1.2 days)
- Interview calibration note (if <120 days since hire)
- Recommended action (None / Coaching / Development Plan / Formal HR Process)
- Manager confidence level (High / Medium / Low)
sections.heading: Packet template (fields to be completed)

sections.body:
- Overall banding: Exceeds / Meets / Partially Meets / Below
- Signals and weight:
  - Objective contribution metrics: 40%
  - Peer and cross-team feedback: 25%
  - Manager assessment and examples: 25%
  - Interview/onboarding fit signals: 10%
sections.heading: Scoring rubric (text table)

sections.body:
- Exceeds: Objective metrics above target AND corroborating peer feedback OR multiple high-impact deliverables in the window.
- Meets: Mostly on-target metrics, reliable fulfillment of role responsibilities.
- Partially Meets: Several missing metrics or one sustained area of concern; recommended short coaching plan.
- Below: Repeated missed commitments, multiple negative peer signals — escalate to formal HR casework.

Hiring + onboarding touchpoints integrated into radar:
- Interview phase: Panel lead completes "post-hire calibration memo" 1 week after start if candidate accepted. Memo includes interview contradictions, onboarding risk flags, and recommended early learning plan.
- Day 7 checkpoint: Hiring manager posts a 7-day first impressions note in the packet (highly recommended).
- Day 30/60/90: Standard onboarding checklist items mapped to radar packet fields (status and blockers must be present if not complete).

Asynchronous calibration guidance (how to contribute comments):
- All comments should be evidence-linked and <300 words. Provide clear examples: dates, PR numbers, or links.
- When disagreeing with a manager assessment, mark as peer-comment and include the alternative signal. People Ops will mediate where disagreement exceeds two commenters.
- Use tags in the packet for speed: #onboarding-risk #promotion-candidate #needs-coaching
sections.heading: Example rubric interpretation

sections.body:
- Before window opens: Sync team dashboards and ensure metrics are updated.
- During window: For each direct report, fill packet, attach artifacts, mark recommended action.
- After window: Schedule follow-up conversations and update People Ops ticket with completion notes.
sections.heading: Manager checklists (quick)

sections.body:
- Formal HR escalation should be initiated if a packet maps to "Below" band or if manager confidence is Low with corroborating negative signals.
- For urgent issues surfaced between windows (safety, legal, or severe misconduct), use the immediate HR incident channel — do not wait for the radar window.
- For role transitions requested out-of-cycle (rapid promotion or demotion), submit a fast-track packet with supporting artifacts; People Ops will triage within 5 business days.
sections.heading: Escalations and exceptions

sections.body:
- People Ops produces a quarterly calibration digest containing: number of packets, band distribution, number of promotion recommendations, onboarding-risk list, time-to-resolution for action items.
- Dashboards: Team leads must maintain one canonical team dashboard that exports metrics to the People Ops data pipeline (fields: employee_id, role, manager, OKR_percent_complete, onboarding_percent).
sections.heading: Data & reporting

sections.body:
- Week -12: Calendar published for next four quarters.
- Week -1: People Ops sanity-check and template refresh.
- Window Day 0—14: Manager submissions open.
- Day 15—17: People Ops aggregation and outlier detection.
- Day 18—21: Asynchronous calibration comments.
- Day 22—30: Action item execution and closeout.
sections.heading: Sample timeline (example quarter)

sections.body:
- 7-day first impressions note (example):
  - Role: Senior Backend Engineer
  - Positive: Shipped infra test harness (PR #2341) within first week; proactively paired on onboarding docs.
  - Risk: Unfamiliarity with internal RBAC conventions — assigned buddy.
- Promotion candidate self-note (example):
  - Objective list of deliverables in the review period with links and outcomes.
  - Two peer references and a short impact statement.
sections.heading: Templates (appendix)

sections.body:
- Keep signal bandwidth low: only submit signals you would include in a promotion packet. If evidence is weak, mark as "needs more data."
- Avoid over-reliance on single metrics; use the weighted rubric above.
- Ensure all packet artifacts are accessible to People Ops and relevant calibrators.
sections.heading: Operational considerations and best practices

sections.body:
- This playbook is owned by People Ops. Major changes must be approved by the Head of People Ops and communicated one quarter in advance.
- Minor changes (template tweaks, rubric weight adjustments <=5%) can be applied directly by People Ops with a one-week notice to stakeholders.
sections.heading: Change history and governance

sections.body:
- Promotion pathways and calibration protocol (link in related_pages).
- First year engagement milestones (link in related_pages).
- HR formal casework and investigation process (internal legal link).

Appendix: example JSON payload for a single packet (for integrators / scripts):
- Note: include to help SRE or Eng DX automate uploads; store in the team repo for automation.
sections.heading: Related resources

sections.body:
- Teams are encouraged to pilot a 1-month trial using the radar for a single pod before full org rollout. People Ops will provide a pilot checklist and dedicated support.

If you have questions or want the packet template as a Google form or CSV for automation, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) or ping on #people-ops.

payload.page_title: Structured Hiring Committee and Decision Protocol

sections.body:
Purpose

This page codifies the charter, membership, meeting cadence, and formal decision protocol for hiring committees across Redwood Inference. The goal is to ensure consistent, equitable, and efficient hiring decisions while preserving manager autonomy and accountability. This process applies to IC and manager hires through L6; executive / VP-level hires follow a separate executive search protocol described in the leadership hiring appendix (link at bottom).

Scope and goals

- Scope: All full-time and long-term contractor hires (>6 months) for engineering, product, data, and platform teams.
- Primary goals:
  - Reduce time-to-offer to <= 21 calendar days for priority roles.
  - Increase offer-acceptance rate to >= 75% through calibrated offers and improved candidate experience.
  - Ensure consistent application of scorecards and diversity & inclusion best practices.
  - Provide a repeatable record for audit and post-hire review.

Committee charter and membership

- Charter: Provide a cross-functional panel that validates role requirements, confirms scorecard alignment, and signs off on final offers for senior and cross-team roles. The committee is not a veto body for manager-level hiring decisions except where the role is cross-functional or above the manager's compensation band.
- Standard membership:
  1. Hiring Manager (chair) — presents role context, impact, and preferred candidate.
  2. HR Partner — ensures process compliance, EEO & compensation alignment.
  3. Peer Engineer/Product Lead — assesses on-skill fit and team dynamics.
  4. Technical Reviewer (subject matter expert) — deep technical validation.
  5. Program / Product Manager or Customer-facing stakeholder (as applicable) — for cross-functional roles.
- Optional members when needed: Security reviewer, Privacy lead, Finance approver (for unusual budget exceptions), People Ops Sr.

Decision authority and boundaries

- Hiring Manager retains primary authority up to L5 for individual contributor hires. The committee provides advisory scoring and a formal sign-off for L6+ or cross-team hires.
- Committee sign-off is required in the following scenarios:
  - Role band >= L6 (senior IC / manager level).
  - Director or manager roles that will span multiple teams.
  - Compensation requests exceeding the baseline band by >15%.
  - Roles flagged for regulatory, security, or customer-data access.

Meeting cadence and minimum artifacts

- Cadence: Standing 45-minute committee slots every Tuesday and Thursday at 10:00 PT for teams with active searches. Occasional ad-hoc reviews can be scheduled for urgent offers.
- Required artifacts submitted by Hiring Manager at least 24 hours before the meeting:
  - Completed role scorecard (template below).
  - Candidate packet: resume, interview notes, anonymized score summary, reference check summary (if available).
  - Proposed offer terms and rationale.

Scorecard template (text table)

Use this normalized scorecard to make comparisons easier across candidates. Each criterion is scored 1–5; total and comments required.

| Criterion | Weight | Score (1-5) | Weighted | Notes |
| Role-fit / impact potential | 30% | ___ | ___ | Candidate's likely contribution in first 6 months |
| Technical depth | 25% | ___ | ___ | Core technical skills and learning velocity |
| Collaboration & communication | 20% | ___ | ___ | Cross-team partnership and influence |
| Ownership & execution | 15% | ___ | ___ | Evidence of delivering end-to-end outcomes |
| Culture & values alignment | 10% | ___ | ___ | Behavioral alignment with Redwood values |
| TOTAL | 100% | | ___ |

Decision protocol (step-by-step)

1. Intake: Hiring Manager opens req in Greenhouse and attaches draft scorecard.
2. Pre-screen: HR Partner verifies role description, compensation band, and sourcing plan.
3. Interview loop: Standardized interview loop executed; interviewers submit scorecards within 48 hours.
4. Committee review: Candidate packet and composite score submitted to committee; committee meets to discuss.
5. Decision matrix applied:
   - If composite score >= 4.2: Committee recommends hire; hiring manager may extend offer after HR confirms comp and references.
   - If composite score 3.6–4.19: Committee recommends hire subject to manager justification and at least one additional reference check.
   - If composite score < 3.6: Committee recommends decline. Manager may escalate with documented rationale.
6. Compensation exceptions: Any requested comp above the band midpoint +15% requires People Ops and Finance approval before an offer is extended.
7. Final approval: HR Partner signs off on offer terms; Hiring Manager communicates offer within 48 hours of approval.

Offer approval flow and timelines

- Time targets:
  - Acceptable maximum time from final interview to offer (internal approval complete): 5 business days.
  - Target time-to-offer (final interview to verbal): 48 hours.
  - Target time-to-fill (req open to accepted start date): < 35 days for priority roles.
- Escalation: If approvals stall >72 hours, the hiring manager flags People Ops for priority routing; People Ops will convene expedited committee within 24 hours for qualified cases.

Onboarding handoff checklist (for committee to validate)

- Required artifacts at time of offer acceptance:
  - Confirmed start date and first-week agenda (manager-provided).
  - Clear role objectives for first 30/60/90 days (manager-provided).
  - Permanent hires: legal paperwork completed, payroll and benefits created.
  - IT & tools access request submitted: GitHub, Slack, internal dashboards, Google Workspace, internal CI/CD access list.
  - First-week meetings scheduled: team intro, platform orientation, security & privacy training slot.

Manager expectations: onboarding & early performance

- First 2 weeks:
  - Daily check-ins during first 5 working days.
  - Clear orientation plan with at least 3 knowledge transfer sessions.
- 30-day:
  - Manager provides written 30-day goals and schedules a 30-day feedback checkpoint.
- 60-day:
  - Progress review with focus on ownership of a defined deliverable.
- 90-day:
  - Formal 90-day hiring review: hiring manager completes a 90-day evaluation and submits it to People Ops for the talent record.

Performance and feedback rituals aligned to hiring outcomes

- Calibration: Quarterly hiring calibration sessions per department to review mid-year hiring patterns, offer accept rates, and common score distribution.
- Feedback loop: For all hires where the candidate score was within 0.2 points of the threshold or where offers were declined, the hiring manager completes a short "post-offer retrospective" form stored on the candidate record.
- New-hire NPS: People Ops sends a 30- and 120-day onboarding survey with an internal NPS target >= 60.

Metrics and KPIs maintained by People Ops

- Time-to-offer (median): target <= 21 days for priority roles.
- Time-to-fill (median): target <= 35 days for priority roles.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 75%.
- New-hire first-year retention: target >= 90%.
- Proportion of hires needing corrective performance action in first 12 months: target <= 7%.

Equity and inclusion safeguards

- Interview anonymization: For initial resume screening, remove names and non-essential demographic identifiers when possible for high-volume roles.
- Diverse slates: Hiring managers must present at least one diverse candidate slate (as defined in Redwood sourcing guidelines) before advancing to committee for all external senior hires.
- Standardized questions & rubrics: Interviewers must use the canonical scorecard and at least two structured behavioral questions drawn from our catalog to reduce variance.

Documentation and audit trail

- All committee decisions, scorecards, and approvals are logged in the candidate's Greenhouse record and retained for 24 months for review and audit. People Ops will maintain a quarterly digest of "committee decisions vs outcomes" to identify systemic drift.

Exceptions and urgent hiring flow

- Fast-track: For time-sensitive customer-impact hires, the hiring manager may request expedited approval. Criteria for fast-track:
  - Demonstrable customer-impact or revenue risk within 30 days.
  - Written justification attached to the req.
- Fast-track process:
  - HR Partner confirms eligibility and convenes an ad-hoc mini-committee (hiring manager, HR Partner, one technical reviewer) with a target decision time of 24 hours.

Appendix: Templates and links

- Role scorecard template (copyable) — attach this page.
- Offer approval matrix (spreadsheet) — People Ops shared drive link.
- New hire 30/60/90 template — templates/docs/onboarding-templates.
- Leadership hiring appendix — contact People Ops senior recruiter for access.

Ownership and review cadence

- Owner: People Ops (process owner: Jordan Kim).
- Review cycle: Annual review in Q4 or earlier if metrics show process drift.
- Change control: Any changes to decision thresholds or committee makeup require People Ops and two stakeholder approvals (Engineering Head and HR Director).

Contact

- For questions or to request an exception, email people-ops@redwood.ai and CC your HR Partner.
