payload.page_title: Talent benchmarking and skill supply mapping framework

sections.body:
Overview

This document defines the Talent Benchmarking and Skill Supply Mapping (TBSSM) framework used by People Ops and hiring managers to: 1) quantify the current capability base across engineering and product teams, 2) benchmark role-level expectations against market signals, and 3) produce a prioritized skill supply plan (hire vs. upskill vs. contractor) for the next two quarters. TBSSM is intended to standardize evidence, cadence, and decision-making so hiring and development dollars are targeted where they produce measurable impact.

Objectives

- Create a single source of truth for role-level capabilities and supply gaps.
- Provide an evidence-backed prioritization for hiring vs training vs redeployment.
- Reduce time-to-fill for high-priority gaps by 20% within two quarters.
- Improve first-90-day effectiveness for new hires by aligning onboarding to benchmarked competency targets.

Scope

- Teams in scope: Engineering, Product, Applied ML, SRE, DevRel for the initial pilot (Q1–Q2 2028).
- Roles: IC and manager levels up to L6 / Sr Manager. Leadership and exec-level role profiling will follow a different cadence.
- Outputs: Quarterly skill supply map, prioritized resourcing plan (hire/upskill/contractor), and one-page role benchmark for each role family.

Key definitions

- Role benchmark: Articulated target proficiencies across 8 canonical competencies for a role (see Competency Matrix).
- Supply map: A snapshot of headcount, demonstrated proficiency, and time-to-competency (T2C) per role family.
- Gap closure plan: The set of actions (hire/upskill/contractor/internal mobility) with owners and timeline.

Ownership and governance

- Program owner: People Ops (lead: Asha Patel).
- Quarterly review owner: Workforce Planning (Diego Ramirez) + Hiring Velocity Squad.
- Role-family stewards: Hiring manager(s) for each team (primary) and Discipline Lead (secondary).
- Executive sponsor (pilot): VP People (Maya Chen).

Inputs and data sources

- HRIS: Workday — canonical headcount and tenure.
- People Data Warehouse (PDW) — aggregated training completions, performance evidence tags, and skills survey responses.
- ATS: Greenhouse — active reqs, funnel metrics, time-to-offer.
- Manager evidence packets — new-hire 30/60/90 notes, probationals, and internal transfer reviews.
- Market signals — compiled biquarterly by Recruiting (benchmarks: salary ranges, required skills from job market, and supply scarcity index).

Process (quarterly cadence)

1. Role-family inventory (week 1–2):
   - People Ops triggers a refresh job that extracts current headcount, active requisitions, and last competency assessment timestamp from PDW.
   - Output: Raw CSV — [role_family, role_level, headcount, active_reqs, last_assessed_date].

2. Evidence gathering (week 2–3):
   - Role-family steward collects manager evidence packets for all incumbents in-scope.
   - Managers submit a short skills self-assessment for each direct report using the standardized survey (10–15 min).

3. Benchmark generation (week 3–4):
   - People Ops combines internal evidence with market signals to produce a Role Benchmark (one page).
   - Role Benchmark includes target proficiency per competency, salary midpoints, and expected T2C for external hires.

4. Supply mapping and gap analysis (week 4–5):
   - PDW produces a Skill Supply Map: for each role family, compute % of incumbents at or above target proficiency, projected attrition (next 6 months), and backlog of requisitions.

5. Prioritization and resourcing plan (week 5–6):
   - Hiring Velocity Squad convenes a 60-minute prioritization review with role-family stewards and Finance rep.
   - Action outcomes: Approve hiring reqs, approve training plans, or reassign internal candidates.

6. Publish and track (week 6):
   - People Ops publishes the quarter's Skill Supply Map and Gap Closure Plan to the People Ops workspace and notifies stakeholders.

Competency Matrix (canonical competencies)

| Competency | Level 1 (Foundational) | Level 3 (Proficient) | Level 5 (Expert) |
|------------|-------------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Systems Thinking | Understands basic service boundaries | Designs moderately complex systems with tradeoffs | Architect-level design with system-wide impact |
| Product Judgment | Follows product specs and tickets | Shapes feature scope and tradeoffs | Defines multi-quarter product strategy |
| Code Quality & Ownership | Contributes with reviews | Owns services end-to-end | Mentors across teams, drives standards |
| Reliability & Ops | Can use runbooks | Sets SLOs and incident playbooks | Leads reliability strategy across platform |
| ML & Data Literacy (if applicable) | Interprets simple metrics | Evaluates model outputs and drift | Sets model governance & evals |
| Collaboration & Communication | Communicates within team | Influences cross-functional partners | Coaches leaders on communication strategy |
| Leadership (for manager tracks) | Manages small projects | Leads team-level outcomes | Scales org capability and talent |
| Learning Agility | Completes assigned training | Applies new skills in projects | Systematically spreads learning practices |

(Each competency row is scored on a 1–5 rubric in the operating spreadsheet.)

Templates and artifact checklist

- Role Benchmark (one-pager): role_family, role_level, canonical competencies with target scores, salary midpoint, external T2C estimate, recommended interview rubric.
- Evidence packet: last performance rating, 30/60/90 notes, sample PR/feature, training completions, manager assessment (200–400 words).
- Skill Supply Map CSV headers: role_family, role_level, incumbents, pct_at_or_above_target, projected_attrition_6m, open_reqs, recommended_action.

Prioritization rubric (applied in weekly review)

Score each gap 0–10 and compute weighted total:
- Business criticality (40%): Impact on revenue, customer SLAs, or launch commitments.
- Time sensitivity (25%): How quickly gap must be closed to avoid delivery risk.
- Internal readiness (15%): Availability of internal candidates or trainers.
- Hire difficulty (20%): Market scarcity and expected time-to-hire.

Decision thresholds

- Hire: Weighted score >= 7.5 and headcount budget available.
- Upskill: Weighted score between 4.0–7.4 and internal readiness >= 60%.
- Contractor/Interim: Weighted score >= 6.0 and time sensitivity high (T2C < 8 weeks required).

Tooling and automation

- Data extraction: weekly ETL job from Workday/Greenhouse into PDW (owned by Data Platform).
- Survey collection: 1-click manager survey distributed via Slack workflow (People Ops maintains templates).
- Automated dashboard: Skill Supply Map dashboard in Looker (People Ops + Workforce Planning) with filters by team, role level, and recruitment stage.

KPIs and SLAs (program-level)

- Mapping freshness: 100% of in-scope role families updated every quarter; PDW snapshots finished within 10 business days of quarter start.
- Gap closure velocity: 60% of approved gap closure actions closed or in active progress within 90 days.
- Time-to-hire (priority gaps): reduce median TTH from offer to start by 20% within two quarters for gaps scoped as Hire.
- First-90-day time-to-impact: measure via onboarding impact survey; target 70% of new hires meeting role benchmark or above at day 90 for prioritized hires.

Rollout plan (pilot -> broader adoption)

- Q1 pilot: 6 role-families (Engineering infra, Inference runtime, Applied ML, Product, SRE, DevRel). Collect learnings and refine rubric.
- Q2 expansion: add remaining engineering and product families; incorporate feedback loops to Recruiting and L&D.
- Q3+: add non-engineering functions after validating tool flows (HRIS integration, manager training).

Implementation checklist (first quarter)

- [ ] Finalize canonical competencies and rubrics with Discipline Leads. (Owner: People Ops)
- [ ] Wire PDW ETL and Looker dashboard. (Owner: Data Platform)
- [ ] Publish manager survey and manager training (30-minute onboarding session). (Owner: People Ops + L&D)
- [ ] Run pilot for 6 role families. (Owner: Program Owner)
- [ ] Convene prioritization review and record decisions in the Recruiting board. (Owner: Hiring Velocity)

Communication and manager expectations

- Managers must submit evidence packets for direct reports during the evidence gathering window. Missing packets trigger an escalation email to the manager and their director.
- Hiring decisions that exceed base budget require Finance and VP People approval and an updated business case.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Manager survey fatigue leading to low-quality evidence.
  - Mitigation: Keep survey < 15 minutes and provide an autopopulated evidence template.
- Risk: Market signals lag leading to mis-prioritization.
  - Mitigation: Recruiting to run a short market check for flagged high-difficulty roles each month.

FAQ

Q: How often will my team be assessed?
A: Every quarter for in-scope families. Ad-hoc updates can be requested before the quarterly run for urgent reorganizations.

Q: Can managers request exceptions to the prioritization outcome?
A: Yes — exceptions are reviewed by the Workforce Planning chair and People Ops; the request must include a 1-page impact memo.

Appendix: CSV export sample header

role_family,role_level,incumbents,pct_at_or_above_target,projected_attrition_6m,open_reqs,recommended_action,priority_score,notes

Contact

For questions or to nominate additional role families for the pilot, contact Asha Patel (People Ops) or Diego Ramirez (Workforce Planning).

End of document

payload.page_title: Optimize Quality Gates: Eval-Harness Integration Contracts (v1)

sections.body: This page defines the interface contract between **Optimize** (producer of proposed serving config diffs) and the **Eval Harness** (runner of offline quality evaluations) for **quality guardrails gating**.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Inputs required to run a gate (config diff, baseline, tier, prompt sets, model/runtime metadata)
- Output schema (per-suite scores, deltas vs baseline, confidence/variance metadata, artifact pointers)
- State machine + polling semantics
- SLAs (latency, availability), retry/idempotency rules, and cancellation
- Versioning and backwards compatibility expectations

This contract is for **Hosted API** gating (initial rollout). Dedicated/Private extensions should follow the same shapes but may use different auth and artifact backends.

---
sections.heading: The contract covers

sections.body:
- **Gate run**: An eval-harness execution comparing a *candidate* configuration to a *baseline* configuration.
- **Candidate**: The proposed config (post-Optimize recommendation) to be applied to a route.
- **Baseline**: The current production config or an explicit historical baseline (e.g., last-known-good gate run).
- **Tier**: Gate strictness level.
  - **SMOKE**: fast subset to catch obvious regressions; bounded runtime.
  - **FULL**: broader coverage + stricter statistical requirements.
- **Suite**: A named eval bundle (prompt set + metric computation). Suites are the unit of reporting.

---
sections.heading: Glossary

sections.body:
- **Optimize integration owner:** Yara Haddad
- **Eval Harness integration owner:** Olivia Grant
- **Evals methodology:** Jonas Weber / Selene Huang
- **SLO / operational readiness:** Sean Gallagher (SRE), Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)

Support channel: `#eng-ml` (primary), `#eng-sre` (for SLA/availability issues)

---
sections.heading: Ownership and on-call

sections.body:
1. Optimize produces a proposed **config diff** for a route/model.
2. Optimize selects a **baseline** (either explicit baseline snapshot or “current production snapshot”).
3. Optimize calls Eval Harness to **create** a gate run.
4. Eval Harness transitions state: `PENDING → RUNNING → (PASSED|FAILED|CANCELED|ERROR)`.
5. Optimize **polls** for completion and persists the results (and surfaces them in Console).
6. If passed, Optimize/rollout-controller may proceed with canary enablement; if failed, apply is blocked unless overridden (handled outside this contract).

---
sections.heading: High-level flow

sections.body:
| Environment | Base URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Staging | `https://eval-harness.staging.redwood.internal` | Non-customer data; smaller prompt sets; relaxed quotas |
| Production | `https://eval-harness.prod.redwood.internal` | Customer gating; SLO-backed |

> The service is reachable only from Redwood control-plane networks. External access is not supported.

---
sections.heading: Environments

sections.body:
- **Auth:** mTLS (service identity) + bearer token (short-lived service token).
- **Required header:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **Service identity allowlist:** `optimize-service`, `rollout-controller` (read-only on results)
sections.heading: Authentication and authorization

sections.body:
- Optimize may only create gate runs for routes/accounts it is authorized to operate on.
- Read access to artifacts is via **signed URLs** (time-limited) or via an internal artifact proxy.

---
sections.heading: Authorization constraints

sections.body:
- All endpoints are namespaced: `/v1/...`
- Backwards-incompatible changes require a new major version: `/v2/...`
sections.heading: Endpoint versioning

sections.body:
- `X-Redwood-Schema-Version: 1.3` (semver string)
- `X-Redwood-EvalHarness-Version: <git_sha>` (for debugging)
sections.heading: Requests and responses include

sections.body:
- Eval Harness **must** accept requests with the current `1.x` schema version.
- Eval Harness **may** accept a limited set of older `1.x` minors during rollouts.
- New fields are additive; clients must ignore unknown fields.

---
sections.heading: Rules

sections.body:
| State | Meaning | Terminal | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `PENDING` | Accepted but not scheduled | No | Usually short; may be longer during GPU scarcity |
| `RUNNING` | Currently executing suites | No | Partial progress may be available |
| `PASSED` | All required suites passed thresholds | Yes | Includes tier-specific details |
| `FAILED` | At least one required suite failed | Yes | Includes failure reasons |
| `CANCELED` | Canceled by client or system | Yes | Used for superseded diffs |
| `ERROR` | System error prevented completion | Yes | Retry behavior depends on error type |

---
sections.heading: Gate run state machine

sections.body: `POST /v1/gates/runs`
sections.heading: Endpoint

sections.body:
- Optimize **must** include `Idempotency-Key` header.
- Eval Harness will deduplicate for **24 hours** based on `(caller_identity, Idempotency-Key)`.
- If a duplicate is received, Eval Harness returns the original gate run.
sections.heading: Idempotency

sections.body: - `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>`
sections.heading: Header

sections.body:
The request is defined here in descriptive form; field types are normative.

**Top-level fields**
- `request_id` (string, required): Caller-generated UUID for tracing.
- `gate_policy_id` (string, required): Policy identifier from Optimize (e.g., `hosted-default-v1`, `enterprise-strict-v1`).
- `tier` (string enum, required): `SMOKE` | `FULL`.
- `priority` (string enum, optional): `LOW` | `NORMAL` | `HIGH` (default `NORMAL`).
- `route` (object, required): Route identity.
- `model` (object, required): Model identity and serving parameters.
- `baseline` (object, required): Baseline selection info.
- `candidate` (object, required): Candidate configuration, expressed as a **config diff**.
- `suites` (array, required): Suites to run (prompt sets + metric bundle).
- `constraints` (object, optional): Hard bounds for runtime/cost.
- `metadata` (object, optional): Debug and attribution tags.

**Route object**
- `route_id` (string, required): Internal route identifier.
- `account_id` (string, required): Customer/account identifier.
- `project_id` (string, optional): Optional project grouping.
- `region` (string, required): Region where runtime knobs apply (e.g., `us-east`, `eu-west`).

**Model object**
- `model_id` (string, required): e.g., `rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct`.
- `model_family` (string, required): e.g., `llama3.1`.
- `model_version` (string, required): e.g., `2026-01-18`.
- `tokenizer_version` (string, optional)
- `serving_sku` (string, required): Hardware/runtime SKU, e.g., `h100-sxm-80gb`.

**Baseline object**
sections.heading: Request body (JSON)

sections.body:
- `baseline_snapshot_id` (string): A pinned snapshot of production config.
- `baseline_gate_run_id` (string): A prior gate run to compare against.
- `baseline_tag` (string): e.g., `current-production` (resolved by Optimize before calling, preferred for v1).
sections.heading: Exactly one of

sections.body:
- Baseline must match `model_id` + `serving_sku`.
- If baseline cannot be resolved, Optimize should not call Eval Harness (treat as pre-gate validation failure in Optimize).

**Candidate object**
- `config_diff` (object, required): Typed diff produced by Optimize.
- `config_diff_schema_version` (string, required): Version of diff schema, e.g., `1.0`.
sections.heading: Baseline requirements

sections.body:
- Batching policy updates
- Prefix/KV caching settings
- Quantization profile changes

Eval Harness treats `config_diff` as opaque except for logging and reproducibility; semantics are owned by Optimize/runtime. (Eval Harness only needs it to record what was tested.)

**Suites array**
sections.heading: Supported diff change types (v1 scope)

sections.body:
- `suite_id` (string, required): e.g., `optimize-gate-core-chat-v1`.
- `prompt_set_id` (string, required): e.g., `ps_chat_core_2026q1`.
- `metric_bundle_id` (string, required): e.g., `mb_task_success_rubric_v1`.
- `required` (boolean, required): If `true`, suite failure fails the gate.
- `min_samples` (integer, optional): Overrides defaults for this run.

**Constraints object**
- `max_wall_clock_seconds` (integer, optional): Hard timeout.
- `max_cost_usd` (number-as-string, optional): Soft cap; if exceeded, run transitions to `ERROR` with reason `COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

**Metadata object**
- `optimize_recommendation_id` (string, required): The recommendation being gated.
- `change_set_id` (string, required): Stable identifier for the config change set.
- `initiator` (string, required): `auto-apply` | `one-click` | `api`.
- `git_sha_optimize` (string, optional)
- `trace_id` (string, optional)
sections.heading: Each suite item

sections.body:
- `gate_run_id` (string): Primary identifier.
- `state` (string): Usually `PENDING`.
- `created_at` (RFC3339 string)
- `poll_after_seconds` (integer)
- `links` (object): URLs for status/results (clients must treat as opaque).
sections.heading: Response (JSON)

sections.body:
- `POST /v1/gates/runs`
- `Idempotency-Key: 7c3b4f83-4cf4-4e60-8c93-0f7d13c9a7e2`
sections.heading: Request

sections.body:
- `tier: FULL`
- `route.region: eu-west`
- `baseline_snapshot_id: bsnap_01HRK...`
- `candidate.config_diff_schema_version: 1.0`
- `suites: [optimize-gate-core-chat-v1, optimize-gate-retrieval-v1]`

---
sections.heading: Body (illustrative)

sections.body: `GET /v1/gates/runs/{gate_run_id}`
sections.heading: Endpoint

sections.body:
- `gate_run_id` (string)
- `state` (string)
- `tier` (string)
- `progress` (string): Human-readable progress (e.g., `2/5 suites complete`).
- `started_at` (RFC3339 string, nullable)
- `finished_at` (RFC3339 string, nullable)
- `poll_after_seconds` (integer)
- `latest_heartbeat_at` (RFC3339 string, nullable)
- `failure_summary` (string, nullable): Present for `FAILED`/`ERROR`.
sections.heading: Response fields (JSON)

sections.body:
- Clients should respect `poll_after_seconds` to avoid thundering herds.
- `latest_heartbeat_at` is used for stuck-run detection by SRE.

---
sections.heading: Notes

sections.body: `GET /v1/gates/runs/{gate_run_id}/results`
sections.heading: Endpoint

sections.body:
- `gate_run_id` (string)
- `state` (string)
- `tier` (string)
- `baseline_reference` (string): Echo of baseline selection used.
- `candidate_reference` (string): Echo of candidate change id.
- `overall` (object): Gate decision summary.
- `suites` (array): Per-suite metrics and deltas.
- `artifacts` (array): Artifact pointers for reproduction.
- `statistics` (object): Aggregation + flake/variance signals.

**Overall object**
- `decision` (string): `PASSED` | `FAILED` | `ERROR` | `CANCELED`
- `reason_codes` (array of strings): e.g., `QUALITY_REGRESSION`, `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLES`, `FLAKY_SUITE_QUARANTINED`.
- `human_summary` (string): 1–3 sentence summary for Console.

**Suites array item**
- `suite_id` (string)
- `required` (boolean)
- `status` (string): `PASSED` | `FAILED` | `SKIPPED` | `ERROR`
- `baseline_scores` (string): Human-readable compact form (for v1; numeric schema tracked in eval-harness). Example: `task_success=0.842; rubric_mean=3.71`.
- `candidate_scores` (string)
- `delta` (string): Human-readable compact form. Example: `task_success=-0.018; rubric_mean=-0.07`.
- `confidence` (string): Human-readable CI or significance note. Example: `95% CI task_success [-0.030, -0.006]`.
- `sample_size` (string): Example: `n=120`.
- `thresholds_applied` (string): Example: `task_success_delta >= -0.01 (FULL)`.
- `failure_details` (string, nullable): Short reason if failed.

**Artifacts array item**
- `artifact_type` (string): `RUN_MANIFEST` | `PER_PROMPT_RESULTS` | `AGGREGATE_REPORT` | `RAW_MODEL_OUTPUTS` | `ERROR_LOGS`.
- `artifact_id` (string)
- `uri` (string): Signed URL or internal URI.
- `expires_at` (RFC3339 string)
- `sha256` (string, optional)

**Statistics object**
- `flake_score` (string): `0.00-1.00` encoded as string; higher is flakier.
- `reruns_performed` (string): e.g., `1`.
- `rerun_policy` (string): e.g., `auto_rerun_on_borderline_or_infra_error_v1`.
- `variance_notes` (string, optional): e.g., `High variance on long-context subset`.
sections.heading: Top-level

sections.body:
For v1, some numeric bundles are represented as compact strings to preserve backwards compatibility with existing Console ingestion. Eval Harness remains the system of record for the structured numeric representation.

A v1.1 follow-up may add optional structured numeric fields while preserving the string fields.

---
sections.heading: Notes on numeric encoding

sections.body: `POST /v1/gates/runs/{gate_run_id}/cancel`
sections.heading: Endpoint

sections.body:
- If `PENDING`, run transitions to `CANCELED` quickly.
- If `RUNNING`, Eval Harness attempts best-effort cancellation; some suites may finish.
- Results endpoint will remain available for **7 days** for audit/debug.
sections.heading: Behavior

sections.body:
- Optimize should cancel superseded gate runs (e.g., user edits recommendation or a newer config diff replaces the old one).

---
sections.heading: Client guidance

sections.body:
- `429` (rate limited)
- `503` (temporary unavailable)
- `504` (gateway timeout)
- `5xx` (except where body indicates non-retryable)
sections.heading: Optimize should retry on

sections.body:
- Max attempts: 3
- Exponential backoff with jitter: 1s, 3s, 10s
- Respect `Retry-After` header when present
sections.heading: Backoff policy (client-side)

sections.body:
- `400` invalid request (schema or required fields)
- `401/403` authz failure
- `409` invalid state transition (e.g., canceling a terminal run)
- `422` semantic validation error (e.g., baseline mismatch with model/SKU)
sections.heading: Non-retryable errors

sections.body:
- `error_code` (string): stable machine code
- `message` (string): human-readable
- `request_id` (string): echo from caller if present

Common `error_code` values:
- `INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `BASELINE_NOT_FOUND`
- `BASELINE_MODEL_MISMATCH`
- `GPU_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE`
- `COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`
- `SUITE_QUARANTINED`
- `INTERNAL_ERROR`

---
sections.heading: All error responses include

sections.body:
- **Availability SLO:** 99.5% monthly for `GET status/results` endpoints
- **Create run acceptance SLO:** 99.0% monthly (excluding `429` due to quota enforcement)
sections.heading: Service availability (production)

sections.body:
These are targets, not hard guarantees; hard timeouts should be set using `constraints.max_wall_clock_seconds`.

| Tier | Target P95 completion | Hard timeout default | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `SMOKE` | ≤ 15 minutes | 25 minutes | Small prompt subset; fast feedback for one-click apply |
| `FULL` | ≤ 90 minutes | 120 minutes | Broader coverage; may rerun borderline suites |
sections.heading: Gate runtime targets (wall-clock)

sections.body:
- Eval Harness retains artifacts for **30 days** (production).
- Signed URLs returned via API expire within **24 hours**; clients should store `artifact_id` for later retrieval via internal artifact proxy.
sections.heading: Artifact retention

sections.body:
- Default per-caller limit: **10 concurrent gate runs** per region.
- Burst: up to **20 concurrent** for `HIGH` priority (subject to GPU capacity).
- Excess requests receive `429` with `Retry-After`.

---
sections.heading: Quotas / rate limits

sections.body:
Eval Harness must record enough metadata to reproduce results:
- Model id/version, tokenizer version (if applicable)
- Serving SKU + runtime image id
- Baseline reference (snapshot id or gate run id)
- Candidate config diff (as received) + schema version
- Prompt set versions (immutable ids)
- Metric bundle versions
- Random seeds where used (and note if nondeterministic decoding is allowed)
sections.heading: Result determinism and reproducibility requirements

sections.body:
- Provide stable `change_set_id` and `optimize_recommendation_id`.
- Ensure the candidate config diff is the exact diff intended to be applied.

---
sections.heading: Optimize requirements

sections.body:
Eval Harness does not interpret the config diff, but it **does** enforce the following for audit and safety:
- `config_diff_schema_version` must be present and supported.
- `candidate.config_diff` must be under 256KB.
- `change_set_id` must be stable across retries.

Runtime-level validation (unsafe combinations, unsupported knobs) happens **before** this contract is invoked (see Optimize pre-gate static checks).

---
sections.heading: Compatibility requirements for config diffs

sections.body:
- Metrics:
  - `quality_gate_runs_started_total{tier,region}`
  - `quality_gate_runs_completed_total{tier,region,state}`
  - `quality_gate_run_duration_seconds{tier,region}`
  - `quality_gate_suite_failure_total{suite_id}`
  - `quality_gate_flake_score{suite_id}` (gauge)
- Traces:
  - Root span per gate run, with `gate_run_id`, `request_id`, `change_set_id`
- Logs:
  - Structured log per state transition (`PENDING→RUNNING`, etc.)
sections.heading: Eval Harness must emit

sections.body:
- `request_id` and (when present) `trace_id` for cross-service correlation.

---
sections.heading: Optimize must propagate

sections.body:
- Prompt sets used for gating may contain customer-derived examples in anonymized form. Treat as **internal**.
- Raw model outputs may include sensitive tokens; artifact access is controlled via signed URLs and internal RBAC.
- Do not export artifacts outside Redwood systems without a security review.

---
sections.heading: Security and data handling

sections.body:
- required request fields
- state machine semantics
- result fields used for pass/fail decisions
- artifact retention/access patterns

…requires:
1) Review from Optimize + Applied ML + SRE owners
2) A staged rollout in staging → production
3) Updated schema version and release notes in the Eval Harness changelog

---
sections.heading: Any change to

sections.body:
When creating a run, Optimize must include:
- `request_id`
- `gate_policy_id`
- `tier`
- `route.route_id`, `route.account_id`, `route.region`
- `model.model_id`, `model.model_family`, `model.model_version`, `model.serving_sku`
- `baseline.(baseline_snapshot_id|baseline_gate_run_id|baseline_tag)`
- `candidate.config_diff`, `candidate.config_diff_schema_version`
- At least one `suites[]` item
- `metadata.optimize_recommendation_id`, `metadata.change_set_id`, `metadata.initiator`

---
sections.heading: Appendix A: Minimal required fields checklist (Optimize)

sections.body:
- Some numeric metrics are returned as compact strings; structured numeric fields will be added in a minor schema update.
- Prompt-level result payloads may be large; consumers should use artifact links instead of expecting full inline data.
- Cross-region baselines are not supported; baseline must match the run region + serving SKU.

---
sections.heading: Appendix B: Known limitations (v1)

sections.body:
- Eval Harness paging: follow `runbook-optimize-quality-gate-failures` and page **Applied ML on-call** if gate failure patterns indicate metric regression.
- Capacity/timeouts: engage **SRE on-call** for GPU scarcity or regional queue buildup.
sections.heading: Appendix C: Contact and escalation

payload.page_title: Observability SLI/Tracing Guidelines and Cost Guardrails (ADR) - 2024

sections.body:
Overview

Purpose: Define a standardized, production-ready set of SLIs, tracing conventions, logging schema, and cost-aware sampling guardrails for Redwood inference services. This doc records the decision to adopt OpenTelemetry as the primary telemetry surface, the canonical SLI definitions for inference endpoints, and the rollout plan for migrating existing services.

Scope
- Services in scope: all API-facing inference routes (hosted API), Redwood Dedicated control-plane services, and the Private control-plane agent.
- Out of scope: offline batch model training jobs, developer local runtimes.

Goals
1) Provide unambiguous SLIs that map to SLOs used by SRE and product.
2) Ensure traces capture request lifecycle end-to-end across frontend, router, runtime, and GPU workers.
3) Keep telemetry cost predictable via sampling & adaptive policies.
4) Offer concrete dashboards and alert thresholds for oncall use.

Decision summary (ADR)
- Chosen telemetry stack: OpenTelemetry for instrumentation, Prometheus for long-lived metrics, Tempo/Jaeger-compatible backend for traces, Grafana for dashboards, and Loki for logs.
- Sampling model: Dynamic trace sampling with 100% sampling for error traces, 5% baseline for successful requests, and a capacity-aware progressive ramp (up to 25%) when experimentation mode is enabled.
- Metric naming convention: metric names must be prefixed with redwood_<service>_ and follow snake_case; labels must include service_version and model_id when applicable.

Rationale
- OpenTelemetry provides vendor neutrality and standardized context propagation (W3C traceparent).
- Prometheus is used for aggregated numeric SLI computation at scrape-time and integrates with existing alerting.
- Cost guardrails are necessary: inference generates large request volumes; uncontrolled tracing would increase egress and storage costs on hosted offerings. The dynamic sampling policy balances observability needs with cost.

SLI definitions (canonical)
- Request latency (P95, P99): histogram on end-to-end request duration measured at the API ingress. Label by route, model_id, deployment_tier. Unit: milliseconds.
- Request success rate: percentage of requests with http_status in the 2xx class and no downstream runtime errors (runtime_error=false).
- Token generation rate: tokens_per_second per model_id and per-instance. Useful for capacity planning.
- Cold-start rate: fraction of requests that experienced model load > 200ms.
- KV-cache hit rate: fraction of requests served from KV cache layer.
- Model-quality-regressions: periodic evaluation job-derived metric (regression_count_over_1000_prompts). See applied-ml-and-evals for eval harness.

Suggested SLO examples (for product teams to adopt)
| SLO name | SLI | Target | Window | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| API latency (interactive) | P95 latency (text.generate) | <= 350 ms | 30d | api-platform-team |
| API availability | request success rate | >= 99.95% | 30d | api-platform-team |
| Dedicated throughput | 95th percentile throughput per-GPU | >= configured commit | 30d | infra-capacity-team |

Metric names and labels (required fields)
- Metric name pattern: redwood_<service>_<metric>
- Required labels: environment (prod/staging/dev), region, service_version, model_id (if applicable), route (e.g. /v1/generate-chat).
- Example Prometheus exposition (instrumentation guideline):
```
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
redwood_api_request_duration_ms_bucket{le="50",environment="prod",region="us-west-2",service_version="v2.1",model_id="gpt-open-8k",route="/v1/generate-chat"} 12345
redwood_api_request_duration_ms_sum{environment="prod",region="us-west-2",service_version="v2.1",model_id="gpt-open-8k",route="/v1/generate-chat"} 9876543
redwood_api_request_duration_ms_count{environment="prod",region="us-west-2",service_version="v2.1",model_id="gpt-open-8k",route="/v1/generate-chat"} 45678
```

Tracing conventions
- Instrumentation libraries: Use OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for core languages (Go, Python, Node). Custom spans must be created for: request_ingress, router_dispatch, runtime_infer, kv_cache_lookup, gpu_batch_execute.
- Context propagation: Use W3C traceparent header. All internal service-to-service calls must forward traceparent.
- Span naming: <service>.<action> (e.g. router.dispatch, runtime.infer).
- Span attributes (required): trace.service, trace.route, model_id, request_id, runtime_gpu_id (when applicable), batch_size, token_count, sampling.priority.
- Error handling: Spans with errors must set status=ERROR and include exception.type and exception.message attributes.

Sampling policy (cost guardrails)
1) Baseline: 5% of successful requests sampled uniformly per service/region.
2) Error amplification: 100% of error traces sampled (http_status >= 500, runtime_error=true, model_timeout=true).
3) Adaptive ramp: For A/B experiments or detailed investigation, teams may opt-in to a higher sampling window for a given service or route. Opt-in is gated behind a quota and must include a cost owner approval.
4) Retention: Full traces retained for 14 days by default; aggregated trace-derived metrics retained in Prometheus for 90 days. Longer retention for traces requires explicit business justification.

Dashboards & Alerts (operational runbooks)
- Default dashboards (to be created in Grafana):
  - API Overview: P50/P95/P99 latency, request rate, error rate, token rate by model.
  - Runtime Health: queue depth, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes.
  - Cost telemetry: sampled trace volume, metrics ingestion rate, estimated telemetry cost per region.

- Alert rules (examples):
  - High API latency (P95 > 500ms for 5m) -> SEV2 -> paging to api-platform oncall.
  - Error budget burn (error_rate > SLO threshold for 60m) -> SEV1 if sustained 4h.
  - Unusual telemetry spike (ingestion rate > 3x baseline) -> SEV2 -> paging to eng-telemetry.

Rolling out the standard (migration plan)
1) Inventory: run telemetry-discovery job to list services without OpenTelemetry keys. (owner: eng-telemetry).
2) Bootstrapping: instrument a pilot set of 3 services (api-router, runtime-proxy, dedicated-control-plane) using OTEL collector config. (timeline: 2 weeks).
3) Validate: confirm SLIs are reported, dashboards populate, and sampling reduces ingestion to target. (owner: eng-sre).
4) Gradual rollout: migrate remaining services in waves (by team), each wave limited to 6 services/week.
5) Post-migration audit: run a cost & quality audit 30 days after migration.

Ownership and runbooks
- Eng-telemetry owns collector configs, sampling policies, and cost guardrail enforcement.
- Eng-sre owns SLO monitoring, alerting rules, and oncall runbooks.
- Runtime-team owns span instrumentation inside the serving runtime and provides helper libs.

Runbook: High latency in production
1) Triage: check API Overview dashboard and latency histograms.
2) Drill down: identify the span with highest self-time (router.dispatch vs runtime.infer).
3) If runtime_infer is dominant: check GPU queue depth and batch_size heatmap. Scale or adjust batching policy as needed.
4) If router.dispatch is dominant: check recent deploys and routing table changes; rollback if necessary.
5) If KV-cache hit rate dropped: invalidate or warm cache; check cache service health.
6) Document incident in postmortem and tag related traces with postmortem id.

Appendix: Example OTEL collector snippet (yaml)
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http: {}
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
  probabilistic_sampler:
    sampling_percentage: 5
exporters:
  prometheus:
    endpoint: "0.0.0.0:9464"
  tempo:
    endpoint: "tempo-us-west-2.redwood.svc:14268"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [probabilistic_sampler, batch]
      exporters: [tempo]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [prometheus]
```

Change log
- 2024-09-12: Initial published version (Aisha Patel).
- 2024-11-01: Added adaptive ramp rules and clarified retention defaults (reviewer: Miguel Torres).
- 2025-02-10: Tightened baseline sampling guidance from 10% to 5% after cost modeling (Priya Nair).

References
- OpenTelemetry specification (W3C Trace Context): https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/
- Prometheus naming best practices: https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/naming/
- Applied ML eval harness (internal): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness

Contacts
- Eng-telemetry: telemetry@redwood.ai
- Eng-sre: oncall@redwood.ai

payload.page_title: Attribute-access rollout and evidence retention roadmap

sections.body:
Overview

This document provides a practical, phased roadmap for adopting Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) across Redwood Inference resources and services. It ties RBAC compatibility, audit logging requirements, evidence retention timelines, secure-SDLC gating, and incident-response triggers into a single operational playbook. Intended audience: security engineers, IAM owners, product platform teams, SRE, and compliance reviewers.

Goals
- Reduce over-provisioning by expressing access as attributes and policies instead of large role collections.
- Ensure auditability and compliance: every attribute evaluation must be traceable and retained per the evidence matrix below.
- Provide deterministic migration steps from existing RBAC constructs to ABAC, with explicit exception handling.
- Integrate ABAC checks into SDLC and incident response so policy drift and attribute abuse are detectable and recoverable.

Scope
- In-scope: all internal control plane services, model-serving endpoints, customer tenancy metadata, and privileged admin functions.
- Out-of-scope: ephemeral internal dev-only feature flags (will be addressed in a follow-up).

Definitions
- Attribute: a key-value pair about a subject (user/service), resource, action, or environment (e.g., department:engineering, resource.sensitivity:high, request.origin:private_vpc).
- ABAC policy: world-readable policy that combines attributes into allow/deny logic.
- Evidence artifact: packaged set of logs, policy snapshots, and attribute-change records required for audits or investigations.

Ownership and roles
- IAM Security Team (owner): policy design, central attribute catalog, evidence retention policy enforcement.
- Platform Engineering: runtime enforcement hooks, policy evaluation libraries, SDKs.
- Service Owners: map service-specific attributes to the central catalog and own migration of local roles.
- Compliance: validates evidence packaging and retention during audits.

High-level migration phases
1) Discovery (0-2 months)
   - Inventory: export current role assignments, service accounts, role-to-permission mappings.
   - Attribute catalog kickoff: seed attributes (department, tier, environment, resource.sensitivity, customer_org_id).
   - Deliverable: discovery report and attribute catalog v0.

2) Pilot (2-5 months)
   - Select 2 services (one infra service, one product-facing) for ABAC pilot.
   - Implement policy-evaluation middleware and audit hooks.
   - Run RBAC side-by-side: enforce ABAC in allow-mode while RBAC remains authoritative.
   - Deliverable: pilot runbook, sample policy set, lessons learned.

3) Gradual rollout (6-12 months)
   - Phased cutover by business unit.
   - Enforce ABAC for read-only ops first, then move to write/privileged ops after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
   - Automate attribute syncs from HR and customer directories.

4) Harden & Optimize (ongoing)
   - Enforce periodic policy review, anomaly detection, and evidence packaging for audits.

Mapping to RBAC (compatibility pattern)
- Pattern: Role -> Policy shim
  1. For each RBAC role, define an ABAC policy that reproduces permissions using subject attributes (e.g., department, job_level) and resource tags.
  2. Create a compatibility layer that evaluates both RBAC and ABAC for a transition window.
  3. Decommission roles when no bindings remain and policy test coverage shows parity.

Example ABAC policy (JSON policy snippet)
{
  "id": "policy.allow.data-read.engineering",
  "target": { "resource.sensitivity": "low", "action": "read" },
  "condition": "subject.department == \"engineering\" && subject.job_level >= 2",
  "effect": "allow"
}

Audit logging and evidence retention matrix
- All ABAC evaluations must produce an evaluation event with the following minimal fields: timestamp, request_id, subject.id, subject.attributes(snapshot_id), resource.id, resource.attributes(snapshot_id), policy_id, decision(allow|deny), decision_reason, evaluator_version.

Retention matrix (summary)
- Evaluation events: 3 years (primary evidence)
- Policy snapshots: 7 years (archival, per compliance)
- Attribute source sync logs (HR/SCIM/KMS): 1 year (sensitive PII redaction applied)
- Attribute-change records (who changed attribute, why, approval id): 7 years
- Role to policy deprecation logs: 5 years

Evidence packaging format (required fields)
- Evidence artifact must be a zipped manifest containing:
  - manifest.json (list of files, policy_ids, snapshot timestamps)
  - evaluation_events.ndjson (queryable event stream)
  - policies/ (policy snapshots in JSON)
  - attribute_snapshots/ (CSV of attribute key-values with snapshot_id)
  - acl_mappings/ (legacy RBAC role exports for the time window)
  - signer.txt (PKI-signed hash of the manifest)

Sample manifest.json (mini example)
{
  "artifact_id": "evidence-2029-01-10-0001",
  "time_range": "2028-12-01/2029-01-10",
  "included_files": ["evaluation_events.ndjson", "policies/policy.allow.*.json"]
}

Retention and storage considerations
- Primary evidence store: write-once, encrypted S3 bucket (KMS CMK: evidence-primary).
- Archival: cold store with immutability flags (7y).
- Access to evidence artifacts: RBAC+ABAC gated; access requests require documented business justification and TTR < 48 hours for compliance requests.

Secure SDLC gates
- Policy changes must follow this pipeline: dev -> peer review -> staging (test harness with replayed evaluation events) -> canary -> production.
- PR templates must include a policy-testing checklist and required unit tests for decision coverage.
- All policy PR merges trigger a policy-snapshot commit (immutable) and generate a signed manifest entry.

Incident response integration
- Attribute change anomaly detection: trigger when >5% of attributes for a domain change within 1 hour or any attribute change to resource.sensitivity:high.
- Incident playbook steps when triggered:
  1. Auto-create incident and tag with "abac-attribute-anomaly".
  2. Freeze attribute propagation pipelines (HR sync, SCIM connectors, internal APIs).
  3. Collect evidence artifact covering the 72 hours prior to anomaly and lock it for forensic analysis.
  4. Rotate any affected service credentials if policy evaluations affected privileged flows.
  5. Post-incident: run attribution analysis, policy/role rollback if required, and create a remediation timeline.

Risk exceptions and approvals
- Short-lived exceptions (<=14 days): product manager + service owner approval in ticketing system; must include compensating controls and evidence snapshot.
- Medium exceptions (15-90 days): security approver + business SLA review; artifact retention must be extended to cover exception period.
- Long exceptions (>90 days): require CISO review and recorded board-level approval.

Operational runbook (quick checklist)
- Daily:
  - Monitor ABAC evaluation error rate (<0.05% target).
  - Verify attribute sync success (last sync age < 5 minutes).
- Weekly:
  - Run policy coverage test suite for active services.
  - Review top-10 denied-but-requested cases for potential false positives.
- Quarterly:
  - Evidence retention audit (verify manifests and cold-store integrity).
  - Policy review with service owners.

Queries and dashboards to build
- Live: ABAC evaluation rate, deny-rate by service, average decision latency, evaluator version distribution.
- Forensics: event-explorer filtering by policy_id, subject.id, attribute snapshot_id, and time range.

Appendix A: SDK enforcement snippets
- Example Golang evaluator call (pseudo):
  resp, err := evaluator.Evaluate(ctx, &EvaluateRequest{
    Subject: subjectSnapshot,
    Resource: resourceSnapshot,
    Action: "write",
    RequestId: reqID,
  })
  // resp.Decision -> log to evaluation_events.ndjson

Appendix B: Policy test harness checklist
- Unit tests for deny/allow boundary cases
- Fuzz tests for unexpected attribute values
- Replay of historical evaluation events to validate decision parity with RBAC baseline

References and related reading
- Central attribute catalog (link to internal catalog)
- Event schema contract and retention runbook
- Entitlement binding and archival playbook

Document change log
- 2028-06-15: Created (Leah Nakamura).
- 2028-09-10: Pilot results and attribute catalog v1 added (Ethan Cole review).
- 2029-01-10: Clarified retention matrix and incident triggers; marked as published.

Contact
- For questions or to request a migration consult, email iam-security@redwood-inference.com or open the "ABAC Migration" Jira board and tag the IAM Security team.

payload.page_title: Authentication + Audit Evidence Correlation Playbook

sections.body:
Overview
========

Purpose
-------
This playbook defines a standardized, auditable process for correlating authentication/authorization (authN/authZ) events with system audit logs and data-residency markers to produce compact evidence bundles for compliance reviews and incident investigations. It reduces triage time, ensures reproducible evidence packages across regions, and documents retention controls that satisfy internal and external auditors.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood-hosted control plane services, Dedicated control plane components, and Private deployment integrations managed by Redwood teams.
- Covers: authN (login, token issuance), authZ (role checks, policy decisions), resource-access audit entries, data-residency attributes, and chain-of-custody metadata required for evidence packages.
- Excludes third-party SaaS where vendor-managed logging is solely external — integration points are covered in related vendor onboarding docs.

Key definitions
---------------
- AuthN event: identity verification occurrences (e.g., OAuth token issuance, SAML assertion, service identity key rotation).
- AuthZ event: authorization decision or policy evaluation (e.g., ALLOW/DENY, role check outcome).
- Evidence bundle: time-bounded set of log slices, policy snapshots, configuration hashes, and a signed manifest.
- Residency marker: metadata attribute associated with a request or object that indicates geographic and legal residency constraints.

Owners & stakeholders
---------------------
- Security (primary): maintains playbook, reviews evidence schema.
- Eng-sre: owns log retention and streaming pipelines.
- Eng-platform: implements indexing and query endpoints.
- Product/compliance: requests evidence for audits and supports exceptions.
- Customer-success: request-facilitator for customer-facing evidence packages.

High-level flow
---------------
1. Detection or request for evidence (audit, QBR, or incident).
2. Determine scope: tenant(s), time window, environment(s), residency constraints.
3. Query and filter authN/authZ indices.
4. Correlate auth events with resource access audit entries and residency markers.
5. Produce evidence bundle: logs, policy snapshot, configuration checksum, signed manifest.
6. Store bundle in immutable evidence store (cataloged with retention policy), and notify requestor.

Technical controls and requirements
----------------------------------
- Per-tenant correlation keys: every request pipeline must inject a request-level correlation id (header: X-RW-REQ-ID) and an identity id (sub claim or service_id).
- Event schemas: all services must emit structured JSON logs to the audit stream with fields: timestamp, service, env, tenant_id, request_id, identity_id, action, resource, decision, residency_marker.
- Immutable evidence store: S3-backed bucket with object lock enabled (+WORM for regulated bundles), bucket-level MFA delete for cross-account restores.
- Signing: manifests are signed by the security signing key (KMS/HSM).
- Retention: default audit log retention is 7 years for regulated tenants; 90 days for standard tenants (policy-driven).

Minimum event schema (example)
-----------------------------
Note: the following block is a JSON-like event example used to validate parsers and must be emitted in raw log streams by services.

{
  "timestamp": "2028-05-01T14:22:41Z",
  "service": "redwood-control-plane",
  "env": "prod-us-west-2",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-abc123",
  "request_id": "rq-0001a2b3",
  "identity_id": "user:alice@example.com",
  "action": "model.infer",
  "resource": "model:ggml-7b.v2",
  "decision": "ALLOW",
  "residency_marker": "EEA:NO_TRANSIT",
  "meta": { "policy_version": "2028-03-10-rc1" }
}

Evidence assembly checklist
---------------------------
- [ ] Time window verified and timezone-normalized to UTC.
- [ ] Tenant and environment filters applied.
- [ ] AuthN/authZ event slice exported (minimum surrounding +/- 30s).
- [ ] Resource-access audit slice exported (transaction-level).
- [ ] Residency markers and object identifiers included.
- [ ] Policy snapshot (policy code and version) included.
- [ ] Config checksums (terraform plan/apply hashes) attached where relevant.
- [ ] Manifest signed and uploaded to immutable store.
- [ ] Evidence id issued and tracked in governance tracker.

Evidence bundle manifest (fields)
--------------------------------
- evidence_id: unique id (rw-evidence-YYYYMMDD-<seq>)
- produced_by: team/service name
- time_window: start/end UTC
- tenant_ids: comma-separated list
- artifacts: list of object paths (logs, snapshots, checksums)
- residency_decl: text note of residency constraints
- signing_key_id: KMS key alias
- signature: base64 signature
- retention_policy_tag: tag name

Correlation playbook: step-by-step
----------------------------------
1. Intake and scope
   - Intake through the Evidence Portal or Security Pager.
   - Validate caller permissions and record requester identity.
   - Enforce least-privilege: only allow evidence requests with a business justification and an approval token for regulated tenants.
2. Build queries
   - Use request_id and identity_id as primary join keys.
   - If request_id absent, fallback to windowed join using tenant_id + source_ip + approximate timestamp.
   - For policy drift investigations, include policy_version in joins.
3. Run correlation queries (examples)\   - LogQL (audit pipeline):
     {service=\"redwood-control-plane\", tenant_id=\"tenant-abc123\"} | json | line_format | query request_id=rq-0001a2b3
   - SQL on audit materialized view:
     SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE tenant_id='tenant-abc123' AND request_id='rq-0001a2b3';
4. Validate residency constraints
   - Cross-reference resource identifiers with the data-residency registry table.
   - If residency_marker indicates restricted transit, ensure no cross-region logs or transfers are present in the window.
5. Package and sign
   - Assemble logs and policy snapshots into a tarball, produce manifest.json, sign via KMS/HSM.
6. Publish and notify
   - Upload to evidence store with retention tag and immutable flags, notify requestor and compliance via the Evidence Tracker ticket.

SDLC and deployment controls that enable evidence quality
-------------------------------------------------------
- CI gates: all changes that affect authN/authZ or audit schemas require: automated linting of schema, schema migration plan, compatibility tests (backfill/forward-compat), and security review approval.
- Versioning: policy artifacts and RBAC role definitions are stored in git with tags formatted: policy/<service>/<semver>.
- Build provenance: every deployment must attach build metadata (git_sha, pipeline_id, artifact_checksum) to the deployed configuration object retrievable by the evidence assembler.

Incident response integration
-----------------------------
- On incident page creation, Incident Commander chooses a prioritized evidence list (authN stream first, then authZ, then resource access, then infra events).
- Triage runbook: immediate 0–15m actions include preserving the relevant audit topics (set them to non-retention or higher retention temporarily), snapshot configuration states, and trigger an evidence packaging job.
- For cross-tenant incidents, the packaging job runs in a restricted Forensics workspace with JIT access and generates separate tenant-scoped bundles.

Risk exceptions and approval workflow
------------------------------------
- Exceptions (for example, shortened retention for non-critical staging tenants) must be requested using the Exception Request form and include compensating controls.
- Exception approval path: Requestor -> Security reviewer -> Compliance approver -> Risk committee (for >90 days or production exceptions).
- Approved exceptions are recorded in the Exception Register with: id, justification, owner, expiration date, compensating controls, and link to evidence artifacts if any.

Operational runbooks and fast-play commands
-------------------------------------------
- Preserve topic (kafka): rw-audit-prod-01 -> kafka-cli preserve --topic rw-audit-prod-01 --duration 72h --ticket <inc-id>
- Query logs (GQL): /audit/query?tenant=tenant-abc123&from=2028-05-01T14:20Z&to=2028-05-01T14:25Z&filter=identity_id:alice@example.com
- Create evidence package (cli): rw-evidence create --tenant tenant-abc123 --from 2028-05-01T14:20Z --to 2028-05-01T14:25Z --out /tmp/evidence-rw-0001.tar.gz --sign-with alias/security-evidence

Acceptance criteria for compliance reviewers
-------------------------------------------
- Evidence package contains: authN/authZ events, resource-access logs, policy snapshot (versioned), deployment provenance, signed manifest.
- All items are checksum-verified and the manifest signature validates against a recognized KMS key.
- Residency constraints are explicit and no evidence artifacts violate the stated residency policy.

Metrics and KPIs
---------------
- Mean time to evidence (MTTE): target <= 4 hours for high-priority incidents.
- Evidence completeness score: percent of packages that include all required artifacts (target >= 98%).
- Packaging errors per 100 packages: target <= 0.5.

Appendix: common scenarios and notes
-----------------------------------
1) Missing request_id: fall back to identity_id + source_ip + 60s window. Note in manifest that correlation was heuristic.
2) Cross-region residency conflict: escalate to Legal and mark evidence bundle as restricted; do not export outside EEA if object marked EEA:NO_TRANSIT.
3) Third-party logs: if vendor-managed, request vendor-signed export and include vendor attestation in manifest.

Related documents and templates
-------------------------------
- Exception Request template (link in Governance templates)
- Evidence manifest template (JSON)
- RBAC role lifecycle policy

Revision history
----------------
- 2028-03-14: Initial draft by Alyssa Chen.
- 2028-04-10: Added SDLC controls and KMS signing details (review: Marcus Patel).
- 2028-05-02: Published — expanded runbook commands and clarified residency validation (review: Rina Alvarez, Samir Gupta).

payload.page_title: Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract and Diagnostic Playbook

sections.body:
Summary:
This page defines the Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract used by the serving runtime to capture lightweight, deterministic kernel-level state for fast post-hoc diagnostics, profiling correlation, and benchmark reproducibility. The contract describes snapshot contents, TTL/retention semantics, collection cadence, storage indexing, query semantics, and the recommended operational playbook for using snapshots during incidents and regressions.

Why we need a formal contract:
- Reduce triage time: snapshots provide a small, self-contained view of kernel scheduling state across shards without requiring full traces.
- Reproducible regression hunts: standardized fields make automated delta comparison (hashes/digests) possible across releases and benchmarks.
- Safe production capture: contract enforces size and cost limits to keep collection cheap and non-disruptive.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: GPU-scheduling kernels, kernel selector hints, active batch queue heads, kvcache hot entries metadata, and per-request token-progress markers. Not intended to replace full GPU traces or perf counters.
- Goals: <= 2KB compressed per snapshot per shard typical, capture latency < 5ms end-to-end, snapshot ingestion availability 99.9%.

Contract: snapshot manifest fields (string names and semantic description)
- manifest_type: "kernel-snapshot-v1" (identifies schema version).
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339 string (origin of capture).
- host_id: runtime host identifier (short hash).
- shard_id: logical shard name/id.
- kernel_hint: canonical kernel name in scheduler (e.g. "attn_sharded_kv_v2").
- active_requests: comma-separated list of up to 8 request_ids with short metadata (see Active Request Encoding below).
- batch_head_shape: concurrency/sequence-length tuple (e.g. "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128").
- kv_hot_prefix_digest: 64-bit hex digest of most-frequent KV prefixes (comma-separated up to 4).
- queue_depth: integer (number of queued kernel tasks).
- slot_usage_pct: integer 0-100 (measured GPU slot occupancy estimate).
- mem_watermark_mb: integer (resident MB attributed to shard at capture).
- fallback_flags: short tokenized list of active degradation flags (e.g. "quantized-fallback,eviction-throttle").
- capture_id: uuid string (unique id for this snapshot).
- sample_hash: sha1 hex of the canonicalized manifest (for fast equality checks).

Active Request Encoding (embedded): up to 8 items, each encoded as colon-separated tokens: request_id|model:ver|priority|est_remaining_tokens
Example: "r1234|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p2|est32"

Size and performance constraints:
- Uncompressed manifest must be <= 8KB. Producers MUST gzip the payload before upload.
- Capture must be non-blocking for request latency: producers should sample at scheduling safe points (e.g. pre-dispatch / post-eviction) and limit synchronous work to timestamping and copying small metadata.
- Max capture cadence per shard: 1 snapshot / 5s by default; bursts up to 1/second allowed during active debugging windows.

Capture lifecycle and TTL semantics:
- Local ephemeral cache: snapshots are kept in-memory for 30s to enable immediate correlation with live traces.
- Short-term storage: snapshots forwarded to an indexed store with 7-day retention for operational triage.
- Long-term archive: on-demand (by capture_id or sample_hash) snapshots older than 7 days may be kept in cold archive for 90 days if pinned by a runbook or regression alert.
- Automatic eviction: snapshots exceeding store quotas are evicted by oldest-first per-host.

Storage & indexing conventions:
- Index keys: sample_hash, capture_id, host_id, shard_id, kernel_hint, timestamp_utc.
- Tags: release_tag (e.g. "canary-2026-03-10"), experiment_id (if collection was triggered by an experiment), incident_id (if captured during an incident).
- Searchable fields must be text-tokenized and exact-match filterable for sample_hash and kernel_hint.

Producer responsibilities and API contract:
1) Capture API (local agent): POST /v1/internal/kernel-snapshot 
   - Headers: X-Host-ID, X-Shard-ID, X-Capture-Src (auto|manual|diag).
   - Body: gzip'd manifest (UTF-8).
   - Response: 202 Accepted with JSON {"capture_id":"...","sample_hash":"...","ingest_ts":"..."}.
2) Backoff: if remote ingestion errors with 5xx more than 3 consecutive times, agent falls back to local retention only and emits metric runtime.snapshot.ingest.failures.
3) Priority: manual-triggered captures (via runbook) should include X-Capture-Priority: high and are exempt from per-shard cadence limits for a 60s window.

Query and diagnosis workflow (runbook):
1) Triage start: on a latency SLO violation or kernel regression alert, runbook owner initiates "snapshot-hunt".
2) Retrieve matching snapshots by filter: sample_hash, kernel_hint, timeframe, release_tag.
3) Run a delta comparison on sample_hash across canary vs baseline to find divergence.
4) If sample_hash matches but incident persists, escalate to full trace capture: enable continuous tracing for affected shards (see profiling-playbook integration below).

Integration with profiling playbooks and benchmarking suite:
- Profiling correlation: snapshots are lightweight keys to join streaming traces and microbenchmarks. Include capture_id in trace span attribute: runtime.kernel_snapshot.capture_id.
- Benchmark gating: nightly benchmarks must capture a deterministic snapshot for each workload and store sample_hash in benchmark results CSV. Regression rule: any benchmark run where the sample_hash distribution differs from baseline for > 20% of shards triggers a quality alert.
- Kernel scheduler experiments: when rolling out kernel changes, collect snapshot cohorts (baseline/canary) and run a pairwise hash-difference analysis as part of the release checklist.

Release gating checklist (minimum):
- Collect cohort snapshots for baseline and canary for 24 hours with at least 1000 snapshots per cohort.
- Run automated sample_hash cluster analysis and ensure no new kernel_hint set appears in >5% of canary shards unless intentionally rolled out.
- Verify average slot_usage_pct and queue_depth remain within +/- 10% of baseline.
- Sign-off required by runtime-scheduling and profiling owners.

Alerting and SLOs:
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.ingest.latency_p50 < 30ms, p95 < 100ms.
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.size_bytes_p95 < 4096 bytes compressed.
- Alert: snapshot-ingest-error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> paging to infra-oncall.
- Alert: sample_hash-drift-score > 0.2 across canary vs baseline -> notify runtime-release-team.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Not a full trace: snapshots are intentionally small and do not include per-kernel GPU counters. Use them to triage and then escalate to detailed tracing.
- Digest collisions: sample_hash uses sha1 of a canonicalized manifest; collisions are possible but extremely unlikely. If collision suspected, attach raw manifest comparison.
- Cost: high-frequency snapshots across all shards increase storage costs; default cadence and burst limits are enforced by agents.

Operational playbook: incident example (step-by-step)
1) Pager fires for high tail latency on model X.
2) Oncall: run "snapshot-query --kernel attn_sharded_kv_v2 --since 5m --format table" across implicated shards.
3) If sample_hash variance high between recently-deployed canary and baseline: run pairwise-diff tool and note differing fields.
4) If mem_watermark_mb spike correlates with queue_depth rise -> trigger immediate spillover rollback (see runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook).
5) Capture extended traces for 10 minutes and mark capture_ids of interest.

CLI examples and snippets:
- Query tool (example):
  # list snapshots matching kernel and timeframe
  snapshot-query --kernel "attn_sharded_kv_v2" --since "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z" --limit 200 --output json

- Minimal producer example (bash curl):
  payload=$(printf '{"manifest_type":"kernel-snapshot-v1","timestamp_utc":"%s","host_id":"h-abc123","shard_id":"s1","kernel_hint":"attn_sharded_kv_v2","active_requests":"r1|m:1|p1|est24","batch_head_shape":"concurrency=8;avg_seq=64","kv_hot_prefix_digest":"%s","queue_depth":12,"slot_usage_pct":72,"mem_watermark_mb":12288,"fallback_flags":"none","capture_id":"%s"}' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "deadbeefcafebabe" "$(uuidgen)")
  echo "$payload" | gzip -c | curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "X-Host-ID: h-abc123" -H "X-Shard-ID: s1" --data-binary @- https://internal-ingest.redwood/v1/internal/kernel-snapshot

Appendix A — Example canonical manifest (pretty-printed):
{
  "manifest_type": "kernel-snapshot-v1",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-05-03T14:12:02Z",
  "host_id": "h-0a1b2c",
  "shard_id": "s1",
  "kernel_hint": "attn_sharded_kv_v2",
  "active_requests": "r1234|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p2|est32,r1240|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p1|est8",
  "batch_head_shape": "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128",
  "kv_hot_prefix_digest": "0x9f8e7d6c",
  "queue_depth": 4,
  "slot_usage_pct": 68,
  "mem_watermark_mb": 11876,
  "fallback_flags": "quantized-fallback",
  "capture_id": "6f8d7b2a-2a5c-4b8e-9bf0-0a1c2d3e4f5a",
  "sample_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6..."
}

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Runtime Observability (oncall: #infra-runtime-observability)
- Reviewers: see metadata above.
- Escalation path: runtime-scheduling -> eng-sre -> infra-ops.

Change history and notes:
- 2026-01-12: initial draft and prototype collector written (A. Patel).
- 2026-03-18: added benchmark integration rules and sample_hash gating (M. Ivanov).
- 2026-05-03: tightened ingest latency SLO and clarified retention windows (D. Kim).

References:
- Profiling playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/continuous-runtime-profiling-strategy-2026
- Kernel telemetry: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/kernel-telemetry-annotation-guidelines-2025
- Release gating: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/canary-sla-oracle-and-benchmark-gate-spec-2026

If you are implementing a producer or a diagnostic tool that uses this contract, please open a lightweight RFC in the runtime team tracker and tag runtime-observability for review.

payload.page_title: Heterogeneous GPU Pool Integration Playbook

sections.body:
Summary
This playbook describes recommended patterns and step-by-step procedures for integrating heterogeneous GPU pools (different GPU types, instance families, and cloud providers) into Redwood's inference capacity plane. It covers Terraform/IaC patterns, CI/CD image and image promotion practices, autoscaler integration, networking considerations, and runbook actions for capacity incidents. The goal is predictable latency, controlled cost, and safe rollout paths for new pool types.

Scope and audience
- Scope: infra owners, platform SREs, and infra engineers implementing or onboarding new GPU pool types (on-prem, AWS, GCP, and partner clouds).
- Audience: engineers building capacity IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines, and oncall responders for GPU capacity incidents.

Goals
- Provide a reusable Terraform pattern for multi-cloud GPU pools.
- Ensure safe CI/CD promotion for GPU runtime images.
- Define autoscaler integration points and SLO-aware thresholds.
- Give a clear runbook for capacity-related incidents (scale-up, spot-preemption, network egress saturation).

Key concepts and components
- gpu-allocator: service that maps tenant demand to pool capabilities.
- infer-scheduler: request router that chooses target pool based on routing policy (latency, cost, region, model compatibility).
- spot-fallback-autoscaler: service that manages preemptible/spot fallback rules.
- runtime-image-registry: container registry for signed GPU runtime images (immutable tags).

Prerequisites
1) Terraform modules for target cloud exist (see Naming & Outputs below).
2) Signed runtime image build in registry (sha256 digest).
3) Network egress path validated (VPC route or private link) and firewall rules applied.
4) Capacity owner and oncall rotation defined in PagerDuty.

Naming & outputs (IaC pattern)
- Module naming convention: modules/gpu_pool/{provider}/{flavor} (e.g. modules/gpu_pool/aws/a10xlarge, modules/gpu_pool/gcp/a100-80gb).
- Required outputs from module: pool_id, region, vpc_subnet_ids (comma-separated), egress_nat_gateway, instance_role_arn (or service_account_email).
- Optional outputs: snipe_node_group_name, taint_key (for workload isolation).

Example Terraform pattern (high level)
- Compose a root module that assembles provider-specific modules and exposes a unified map to the allocator service. Example snippet:

terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.4"
}

module "gpu_pool_aws_a10" {
  source       = "../modules/gpu_pool/aws/a10xlarge"
  region       = var.aws_region
  desired_min  = 2
  desired_max  = 40
  tenant_tags  = var.tenant_tags
}

output "pools_map" {
  value = {
    aws_a10 = module.gpu_pool_aws_a10.pool_id
  }
}

Best practices: keep cloud-specific footguns in module boundary; only pass high-level capacity policies from root. Use remote state per environment and per-account to avoid cross-account shock on apply.

CI/CD and image promotion for GPU runtimes
- Build pipeline responsibilities:
  - Build image pinned to base driver version (NVIDIA driver + CUDA) and test smoke startup on a small instance type with one model.
  - Run hardware-aware integration tests (memory, nvlink, multi-process).
  - Sign image artifact and publish immutable tag: runtime:v1.12-20251001+sha256:<digest>

- Promotion flow: canary -> staged -> global. Use feature flags for new runtime behavior. Promotion steps:
  1) Deploy to playground pool with <5 nodes.
  2) Run synthetic eval harness (latency p50/p95, tokens/s, memory).
  3) Monitor real traffic via canary route (5% traffic) for 24 hours.
  4) If SLOs hold and no regression alerts, promote to staged (regional) then to global.

sections.body:
name: build-runtime-image
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=12.1 -t ${{ secrets.REGISTRY }}/runtime:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Push and sign
        run: |
          docker push ${{ secrets.REGISTRY }}/runtime:${{ github.sha }}
          echo ${{ secrets.SIGN_KEY }} | cosign sign --key - ${{ secrets.REGISTRY }}/runtime:${{ github.sha }}

Autoscaler integration patterns
- Autoscaler contract with gpu-allocator:
  - Inputs: pool_id, desired_min, desired_max, safe_padding_percentage (default 10%), scaling_cooldown_seconds.
  - Behavior: prefer non-preemptible capacity; scale to preemptible only if forecasted demand > 80% of non-preemptible capacity.

- Safe thresholds recommended (tune per workload):
  - scale_up_trigger: 75% average GPU utilization over 3min window OR queue depth > 30 across pool.
  - scale_down_trigger: average GPU utilization < 30% over 10min and no queued requests.
  - preemptible_engagement_point: when non-preemptible headroom < 20% and forecasted demand for next 30min > 50%.

Network and egress considerations
- Ensure VPC native routing for inter-region inference traffic where possible.
- Validate MTU (especially for NVLink/GPUDirect setups in on-prem racks).
- Egress shaping requirements for multi-tenant pools: enforce per-tenant QOS token bucket at the NAT or egress gateway. Example iptables tc recipe (conceptual):
sections.heading: Sample CI YAML (GitLab/GitHub Actions style)

sections.body:
Runbook: sudden capacity shortage (common symptoms: queued requests increasing, p95 latency spikes, allocate-fail events)
1) Page the GPU-capacity oncall.
2) Check allocator dashboard: current_pools, queued_requests, per-pool_utilization. Command examples:
   - kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=gpu-allocator -o wide
   - curl -sS https://allocator.internal/v1/metrics?pools=true | jq
3) Validate if preemptible pools are healthy and not fractured:
   - aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --region $REGION --names $ASG_NAME
4) If immediate headroom needed:
   - Increase desired capacity on root Terraform variable file and trigger a module apply for targeted pool (only with approval from capacity owner). Example: terraform apply -var 'desired_max=60' -target=module.gpu_pool_aws_a10
   - Alternatively toggle temporary overflow routing in infer-scheduler: set route rule to send 10% of traffic to a lower-cost compatible model variant.
5) If preemption causing failures: engage spot-fallback-autoscaler to shift queued work to non-preemptible pools: PATCH /autoscaler/api/v1/eviction-policy {"force_nonpreemptible": true}
6) After stabilization, open an incident with summary and attach traces.

Post-incident checklist
- Timeline of events and detection.
- Root cause analysis (misforecast, runaway eval job, bad rollout of expensive runtime).
- Capacity delta: nodes added/removed.
- Action items: max_limit increase, scheduler rule change, add synthetic probe.

SLOs and capacity SLAs (example baseline)
- p50 latency SLO (intra-pool): < 120ms for 4k token inference.
- p95 latency SLO (intra-pool): < 500ms.
- Availability: 99.9% per-region for non-preemptible inference pools.
- Queuing time SLO: 99% requests start execution within 200ms of enqueue when capacity available.

Ownership and escalation
- Pool creation: infra-gpu-team (oncall: @gpu-infra-rotation).
- Runtime image builds: infra-ci-team.
- Network egress/QoS: cloud-networking-team.
- Escalation path: capacity oncall -> infra lead -> platform SRE manager.

Safety & change windows
- Non-emergency scaling changes during business hours (09:00–18:00 local region).
- Runtime upgrades require staged canary and 24h observation before global promotion.
- Any change to taints/labels must be coordinated with platform and ML-systems teams to avoid silent placement failures.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Check pool utilization (example CLI):
  curl -sS https://allocator.internal/v1/pools/metrics | jq '.pools[] | {id: .id, util: .gpu_util, queued: .queue_len}'

- Example terraform workspace flow for safe apply:
  1) terraform workspace select env-prod || terraform workspace new env-prod
  2) terraform plan -var-file=env-prod.tfvars -out plan.tfout
  3) terraform apply plan.tfout

- Quick revert: set runtime image tag back to last-known-good tag in the infer-scheduler configmap and restart rollout (kubectl rollout restart deployment/infer-scheduler).

References and related pages
- See also: gpu-fleet-scaling-metrics-and-oncall-runbook (capacity metrics), gpu-provisioning-immutable-state-and-disaster-recovery (IaC patterns), cross-account-gpu-vpc-modules-and-network-runbook (networking patterns).

Last updated notes
- 2025-10-05: Added preemptible_engagement_point guidance and sample Terraform pattern.
- 2025-03-01: Introduced CI/CD promotion flow and signing guidance.

If you find gaps in this playbook or want a new provider example added (Azure, OCI), open a PR against eng-infra team-wiki and assign @Samira Patel for review.
