payload.page_title: Ephemeral GPU Load-Testing Sandbox Operator and CI Integration

sections.body:
Summary

This document describes the Ephemeral GPU Sandbox Operator (EGSO) pattern and the recommended CI/CD integration for safe, reproducible load-testing of inference workloads. EGSO provides short-lived GPU environments that mirror production networking and routing but enforce strict cost, egress, and tenant-quota controls. This page covers operator architecture, Terraform snippets, GitHub Actions examples, safety controls, SLOs and alerts, ownership, incident runbook, and deprovisioning policies.

Why this exists

- Teams need realistic token-latency and memory-pressure experiments against the serving runtime without consuming long-lived fleet capacity.
- Self-serve sandboxes reduce noisy neighbor incidents by isolating ephemeral tests and providing explicit economic limits.
- Integrating sandboxes into CI enables repeatable canary runs for kernel/quantization/ batching changes.

Goals and non-goals

- Goals: reproducible load-testing, low-latency realistic networking, cost-capped GPU usage, auditable billing tags, automated cleanup, CI gating for runtime/kernel changes.
- Non-goals: simulating full production traffic volume (use dedicated stress-farm for very large scale), hosting customer workloads.

Overview and architecture

- Components:
  - EGSO controller (K8s operator) that provisions ephemeral node pools via Terraform Cloud/Account API and registers instances into the internal allocator.
  - Sandbox manager service (internal API) that: accepts requests, assigns quota, mints short-lived credentials, and applies egress/egress-rate limits.
  - CI integration (GitHub Actions/GitLab CI) that launches sandboxes, runs load profiles, collects telemetry, and tears down resources.
  - Billing sidecar that annotates usage with tags: sandbox_id, ci_run_id, change_id, owner_team.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
Developer/CI -> Sandbox Manager -> EGSO Controller -> Terraform -> Cloud GPU Pool -> Inference Node(s)

  Telemetry -> Prometheus -> Grafana (sandbox dashboards)
  Billing -> Cost Exporter -> Billing Ledger (tagged)

Provisioning flow (high level)

1. CI job requests a sandbox via the Sandbox Manager API (/v1/sandboxes). Request includes desired profile (small/medium/large), expected duration, and test token.
2. Sandbox Manager validates against org quotas and owner-team limits. It returns a sandbox_id and ephemeral credentials.
3. EGSO controller reconciles a Terraform module (sandbox module) that creates the node pool and a K8s namespace with network policies.
4. Once nodes are healthy and the runtime provided, CI runs the test profile. Telemetry and logs stream to a tagged sandbox dashboard.
5. On completion or timeout, sandbox is destroyed automatically by EGSO and billing is exported with sandbox tags.

Safety controls and constraints

- Maximum wall-clock duration: 6 hours (configurable by org).
- Maximum GPU-hours per sandbox: 12 GPU-hours default.
- Per-team daily GPU-hour cap: enforced by Sandbox Manager (quota backplane).
- Egress must pass through sandbox egress-proxy with per-sandbox rate-limiter (default 50 MB/s).
- No inbound public IPs; access via ephemeral bastion with time-limited SSH certs.
- All sandboxes are created with a default CPU and memory resource quota to avoid cluster-level resource starvation.

Terraform module example (recommended pattern)

- Purpose: spawn a small heterogeneous GPU node pool, attach to the internal allocator, and label nodes for sandbox_id.

Example snippet (HCL)

provider "aws" { region = var.region }
module "egso_sandbox_pool" {
  source = "git::git@github.com:redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//egso-sandbox-pool?ref=v1.2.0"
  sandbox_id = var.sandbox_id
  profile    = var.profile  # small | medium | large
  node_count = var.node_count
  labels = {
    sandbox = var.sandbox_id
    ci_run  = var.ci_run_id
  }
  tags = {
    Project = "egso"
    Team    = var.owner_team
    Owner   = var.owner_email
  }
}

Required Terraform variables table (as text)

| variable | type | example | purpose |
|---|---|---:|---|
| sandbox_id | string | sbox-2025-0421 | unique id for sandbox lifecycle |
| profile | string | medium | mapping to GPU types and sizes |
| node_count | number | 2 | initial node count to create |
| owner_team | string | inference-team | used for billing/tags |
| owner_email | string | dev@example.com | contact for auto-notify |

GitHub Actions example (abridged)

- Workflow steps:
  - request-sandbox (POST /v1/sandboxes) -> returns SANDBOX_ID, KUBECONFIG (base64), TEST_CREDENTIALS
  - run-load-profile -> uses load-generator (internal tool: rload) with test manifest
  - collect-artifacts -> push telemetry and traces to artifact store and notify sandbox dashboard
  - teardown -> DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{SANDBOX_ID} (falls back to auto-teardown after TTL)
sections.heading: Diagram (text)

sections.body:
jobs:
  sandbox-load-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Request sandbox
        run: |
          curl -X POST "${{ secrets.SANDBOX_API }}/v1/sandboxes" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.SANDBOX_TOKEN }}" \
            -d '{"profile":"medium","duration_hours":3,"ci_run_id":"${{ github.run_id }}","owner_email":"dev@example.com"}' \
            | jq -r '.sandbox_id, .kubeconfig' > /tmp/sandbox_info
      - name: Run load generator
        env:
          KUBECONFIG: ${{ steps.request.outputs.kubeconfig }}
        run: |
          rload --manifest tests/perf/token-latency.yml --target postgresql://inference-router/sandbox --out artifacts/perf.json

Telemetry and SLOs

- Mandatory metrics (exported by sandbox runtime):
  - sandbox.request.latency.p95 < 80ms for small sequences (SLO for sandbox fidelity)
  - gpu.utilization.average < 95% (alert if > 98% sustained 5m)
  - sandbox.liveness.up (gauge) -> must be true while the sandbox is allocated
  - sandbox.billed.gpu_hours (cumulative)

- Alerts (prometheus alert rules examples, thresholds):
  - ALERT SandboxGPUHotspot: gpu_utilization > 98 for 5m -> severity=critical -> notify infra-oncall, owner_team
  - ALERT SandboxEgressExceeded: sandbox_egress_bytes_rate > 60MB/s -> severity=high -> pause network, notify owner
  - ALERT SandboxStale: sandbox.liveness.up == 0 AND sandbox_age > 10m -> severity=high -> auto-reap fallback

Operational runbook: incidents and recovery

1. Symptom: CI job times out waiting for sandbox provision
   - Check Sandbox Manager logs (service: sandbox-manager.prod)
   - Verify Terraform run status in the Terraform Cloud workspace for sandbox_{sandbox_id}
   - If TF run failed due to quota, escalate to infra-capacity and create transient allocation ticket with required size and region
   - If controller stuck reconciling, restart EGSO controller pod (kubectl -n infra-rollouts rollout restart deploy/egso-controller)

2. Symptom: High GPU temperature / node flakiness during test
   - Check node metrics gpu_temp and thermal_throttle
   - Cordon the node: kubectl cordon <node>
   - Drain safely (preserve KV cache if required): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
   - If thermal stress continues across nodes, pause sandbox creation (flip feature flag: egso.allow_new_sandboxes=false) and notify hw-ops

3. Symptom: Unexpected billing spike for a sandbox
   - Confirm sandbox tags in cost-exporter; query billing ledger for sandbox_id
   - If charges exceed policy, open billing dispute and rollback any sustained allocations
   - Verify sandbox max GPU-hours enforcement: sandbox.billed.gpu_hours <= sandbox.quota.gpu_hours

Ownership and contacts

- EGSO controller owner: infra-platform@redwood.example.com (pager: #infra-oncall)
- Sandbox Manager owner: platform-tools@redwood.example.com
- Billing/exporter owner: infra-finops@redwood.example.com
- CI integration and tests: eng-dx@redwood.example.com

Onboarding checklist for teams

1. Request onboarding with infra-platform via the internal portal.
2. Allocate team quota (daily and monthly GPU-hour caps).
3. Add owner_email and team labels to CI workflows.
4. Validate test manifest against the standard load profiles (token-latency, memory-flood, kv-eviction).
5. Run baseline canary and confirm telemetry dashboards show expected baselines.

CI best-practices and cost controls

- Always run small profile on PRs; reserve medium/large for nightly regression runs.
- Use sample rate limiter in rload to avoid synthetic egress spikes (example --egress-rate 40MB/s).
- Keep artifact retention to minimum: metrics (90 days), traces (14 days), raw logs (7 days).
- Apply cost tags early; billing pipeline aggregates by sandbox_id, owner_team and ci_run_id.

Deprovisioning and TTL policy

- Default TTL: 3 hours. Auto-extend only if: test signals extend_allowed and team has remaining quota.
- Soft teardown (at TTL-10m): send 10-minute warning via Slack mention to owner_email and create explicit incident if job still active.
- Hard teardown (TTL + 5m): Terraform destroy triggered, resources removed, billing finalized and exported.

Audit and observability

- All sandbox lifecycle events are logged to an append-only audit stream (audit-sbox) with fields: timestamp, sandbox_id, action, actor, reason, tf_run_id, ci_run_id.
- Use Grafana playbooks to switch to sandbox-specific dashboards: query by sandbox_id or ci_run_id.

Appendix: Common CLI shortcuts and checks

- Check sandbox status:
  curl -s $SANDBOX_API/v1/sandboxes/{sandbox_id} | jq
- Reap stalled Terraform run (use terraform-cloud token with limited scope):
  tfe run cancel <run_id> --token=$TFE_TOKEN
- Force teardown from controller namespace:
  kubectl exec -n infra-rollouts deploy/egso-controller -- /usr/local/bin/egsoctl teardown --id {sandbox_id}

Change log

- 2024-07-12: Initial draft by Jordan Meyer
- 2024-09-08: Added Terraform module recommendations and tags (Aditi Shah review)
- 2025-03-19: Tightened default egress limits and added GPU-hours quota enforcement (Luca Romano)
- 2025-11-02: Published with CI job examples and alert rules (Priya Anand)

Related references

- terraform-modules/egso-sandbox-pool (internal git repo)
- rload (internal load generator)
- sandbox-manager API spec (internal)

If you are the owner of a failing CI sandbox run, follow the Operational runbook above and ping #infra-oncall if escalation is needed.

payload.page_title: Deploy Metadata Export Spec (for Incident Bot v2 and Diagnostics)

sections.body: This document specifies how Redwood exports **deploy metadata** in a machine-readable form so automated diagnostics (primarily **incident-bot v2**) can attach reliable “recent deploy context” during incident triage.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- A canonical **Deploy Event** schema (push) for deployment pipelines to emit.
- A **Deploy Metadata API** (pull) for consumers (incident-bot, Console deep links, SRE tooling).
- Field semantics for **service/version**, **rollout phase**, and **canary results**.
- Reliability and guardrails (rate limits, pagination, caching, partial availability behavior).
sections.heading: The spec defines

sections.body:
1) Provide incident responders with accurate “what changed recently” context: service, image/commit, rollout phase, and canary health.
2) Standardize deploy metadata across environments (hosted, dedicated pools, private/VPC where applicable).
3) Make the export robust during incidents (bounded query cost, cached responses, predictable latency).
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Replacing the source CI/CD system of record (e.g., Argo CD / Buildkite / GitHub).
- Full change management or approval workflow.
- Tenant/customer-specific rollout details (deploy metadata is service/infrastructure scoped, not tenant scoped).
sections.heading: Non-goals

sections.body: - **incident-bot** “Recent deploys” context card in #incidents / #eng-oncall.
sections.heading: Primary

sections.body:
- **Redwood Console** deep links (deploy timeline view).
- SRE scripts for postmortem timeline export.
sections.heading: Secondary

sections.body:
- **Service**: A deployable unit with a stable identifier registered in the Service Registry (e.g., `hosted-api`, `router`, `scheduler`, `config-service`).
- **Artifact**: The immutable runtime unit (container image digest and/or binary build ID).
- **Rollout**: A multi-step process that changes the running artifact in one or more regions/cells.
- **Canary**: A staged rollout step routed to a limited slice of traffic/capacity.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
1) CI/CD pipeline (or deploy controller) emits a `deploy.event.v1` event at key state transitions (started, canary complete, ramp, complete, rollback).
2) Events are ingested by the Deploy Metadata service (`deploy-registry`) and written to a durable store.
3) Consumers query recent deploys via HTTP API; responses are cacheable and paginated.
sections.heading: Overview: data flow

sections.body:
- GitHub: PR + merge commit SHA
- Build system: build ID, image digest
- Deploy orchestrator: environment, region/cell, rollout state machine
- Canary analyzer: canary metrics and pass/fail
sections.heading: Sources (typical)

sections.body:
- Topic: `deploy.event.v1` (internal event bus)
- Encoding: JSON
- Ordering: best-effort ordering per `(service_id, environment, rollout_id, region)`; consumers must handle reordering.
- Delivery: at-least-once; consumers must dedupe by `event_id`.
sections.heading: Transport

sections.body:
- `schema_version`: string, must be `"1"`
- `event_id`: string (UUID)
- `emitted_at`: RFC3339 timestamp
- `source`: string (e.g., `argo-cd`, `release-orchestrator`, `private-deploy-agent`)
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- `service_id`: string (canonical Service Registry ID)
- `environment`: string enum: `prod` | `staging` | `dev` (incident-bot uses `prod` and select `staging` for pre-prod incidents)
- `rollout_id`: string (stable across all steps of a rollout; required for joins)
- `deployment_id`: string (unique per region/cell execution; may differ from rollout_id)
sections.heading: Required identifiers

sections.body:
- `artifact_type`: string enum: `container` | `binary`
- `image_repo`: string (if container)
- `image_digest`: string (e.g., `sha256:...`) (if container)
- `image_tag`: string (optional; NOT relied on for uniqueness)
- `build_id`: string (optional)
- `commit_sha`: string (40-hex)
sections.heading: Artifact fields

sections.body:
- `regions`: array of strings (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`) (may be empty if this event is region-scoped)
- `region`: string (preferred when known; set for region-scoped events)
- `cell`: string (optional, e.g., `cell-a`, `cell-b`)
- `cluster`: string (optional)
sections.heading: Rollout targeting

sections.body:
- `rollout_phase`: string enum:
  - `queued`
  - `started`
  - `canary_running`
  - `canary_passed`
  - `canary_failed`
  - `ramp_running`
  - `completed`
  - `rollback_started`
  - `rollback_completed`
  - `aborted`
- `rollout_percent`: number (0–100) (optional; required when `ramp_running`)
- `initiator`: string (e.g., `"connor.obrien"` or `"automation"`)
- `change_reason`: string (optional; brief human-readable)
sections.heading: Rollout state

sections.body:
- `repo`: string (e.g., `github.com/redwoodinference/redwood`)
- `pr_number`: number (optional)
- `pr_title`: string (optional)
- `release_notes_url`: string (optional)

Canary results (optional; required when phase is `canary_passed` or `canary_failed`):
- `canary`: object serialized as JSON in the event payload under key `canary_json` (see “Canary JSON” below)

Notes on `canary_json`:
- To keep the event schema stable while we iterate on canary metrics, `canary_json` is a JSON-encoded string containing a small structured object. Consumers must treat unknown keys as optional.
sections.heading: GitHub linkage

sections.body:
- `status`: `pass` | `fail` | `inconclusive`
- `analysis_window_minutes`: integer
- `baseline_ref`: string (e.g., `previous_release`, `control_pool`)
- `signal_summary`: string (short text; safe for Slack)
sections.heading: Required keys when present

sections.body:
- `metrics`: array of objects, each including:
  - `name`: string (e.g., `http_5xx_rate`, `p95_latency_ms`, `stream_disconnect_rate`)
  - `delta`: number (current - baseline, in same units)
  - `current`: number
  - `baseline`: number
  - `threshold`: number (optional)
  - `verdict`: `pass` | `fail` | `warn`
- `dashboard_url`: string (deep link)
- `runbook_url`: string
sections.heading: Recommended keys

sections.body:
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "event_id": "7b98f3d0-2f7c-4c3c-8b0e-2c4b4f7cf54e",
  "emitted_at": "2025-04-08T19:22:41Z",
  "source": "release-orchestrator",
  "service_id": "hosted-api",
  "environment": "prod",
  "rollout_id": "rollout_2025-04-08_1921Z_hosted-api_29104",
  "deployment_id": "deploy_us-east-1_cell-a_2025-04-08_1921Z",
  "artifact_type": "container",
  "image_repo": "registry.redwood.internal/hosted-api",
  "image_digest": "sha256:4f9f9b0e0c0a5c7b8b2f7d9c1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0",
  "commit_sha": "3a1b7f1b8a1d64c6dca3b8b3e2f9b2d4a1c0e9ff",
  "repo": "github.com/redwoodinference/redwood",
  "pr_number": 29104,
  "pr_title": "Export deploy metadata to incident-bot",
  "rollout_phase": "canary_passed",
  "rollout_percent": 5,
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "cell": "cell-a",
  "initiator": "automation",
  "canary_json": "{\"status\":\"pass\",\"analysis_window_minutes\":15,\"baseline_ref\":\"previous_release\",\"signal_summary\":\"No regression detected (5xx, p95, streaming)\",\"dashboard_url\":\"https://console.redwood.internal/obs/deploys?service=hosted-api&region=us-east-1&rollout_id=rollout_2025-04-08_1921Z_hosted-api_29104\"}"
}
sections.heading: Example deploy.event.v1

sections.body:
- Name: `deploy-registry`
- Audience: internal services only (incident-bot, Console backend, SRE tooling)
- Auth: service-to-service mTLS + OAuth2 service identity (see ADR-013 for permission model)
sections.heading: Service

sections.body: `GET /v1/deploys/recent`
sections.heading: Endpoint: Recent deploys

sections.body:
- `service_id` (required)
- `environment` (optional; default `prod`)
- `region` (optional; when absent returns global + region-scoped entries)
- `cell` (optional)
- `since` (optional RFC3339; default `now-24h`)
- `limit` (optional; default 10; max 25)
sections.heading: Query params

sections.body:
- `Cache-Control: private, max-age=30` (bot-friendly; short cache)
- `ETag` (supported)
sections.heading: Response headers

sections.body:
- JSON array of deploy records, newest first.
- Each record is a flattened view derived from events; see “Deploy Record Schema (API)” below.
sections.heading: Response body

sections.body:
`GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}`

Returns a full timeline (events) for a rollout. Intended for Console and deep debugging; incident-bot should avoid calling this in the hot path unless a user clicks “More details”.
sections.heading: Endpoint: Rollout detail

sections.body: The API returns a stable deploy record representation that is safe to display in Slack and to persist in incident context payloads.
sections.heading: Deploy Record Schema (API)

sections.body:
- `schema_version`: `"1"`
- `service_id`
- `environment`
- `rollout_id`
- `region` (may be `"global"` if not region-scoped)
- `started_at` (RFC3339; earliest known start)
- `last_updated_at` (RFC3339)
- `rollout_phase` (current phase)
- `artifact_fingerprint` (string; preferred value is `image_digest` when present, else `build_id`)
- `commit_sha`
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- `image_repo`
- `image_digest`
- `build_id`
- `pr_url`
- `commit_url`
- `release_notes_url`
- `initiator`
- `rollout_percent`
- `canary_status`: `pass` | `fail` | `inconclusive` | `unknown`
- `canary_summary`: short string
- `canary_dashboard_url`
sections.heading: Recommended

sections.body:
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "service_id": "router",
  "environment": "prod",
  "rollout_id": "rollout_2025-04-08_1644Z_router_1857",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "started_at": "2025-04-08T16:44:12Z",
  "last_updated_at": "2025-04-08T17:05:03Z",
  "rollout_phase": "ramp_running",
  "rollout_percent": 40,
  "artifact_fingerprint": "sha256:8ad0...",
  "image_repo": "registry.redwood.internal/router",
  "image_digest": "sha256:8ad0...",
  "commit_sha": "9b7f3b6c0dfb9cc2f0b4f3f14b2ab8e1b2e0d111",
  "pr_url": "https://github.com/redwoodinference/redwood/pull/29161",
  "commit_url": "https://github.com/redwoodinference/redwood/commit/9b7f3b6c0dfb9cc2f0b4f3f14b2ab8e1b2e0d111",
  "canary_status": "pass",
  "canary_summary": "p95 stable; 5xx -0.01% vs baseline (15m)"
}
sections.heading: Example response item

sections.body:
- Must match the canonical ID in the Service Registry.
- Do not use human aliases (e.g., “Hosted API”) in machine fields; aliases belong in UI.
sections.heading: `service_id`

sections.body:
- `image_digest` is required for container artifacts.
- `image_tag` is optional and must not be used as the unique identifier.
sections.heading: Artifact identity: `image_digest` over tags

sections.body:
- The phase represents the current state of the rollout in a single region/cell scope.
- If the orchestrator only produces a global state, set `region` to `"global"`.
sections.heading: `rollout_phase`

sections.body:
- Canary evaluation must be attached when the canary completes.
- If canary analysis fails (tooling outage), emit `canary_json` with `status=inconclusive` and a human-readable `signal_summary`.
sections.heading: Canary results

sections.body:
- `emitted_at` must be in UTC.
- `started_at` is derived by `deploy-registry` from earliest observed event for `(rollout_id, region, cell)`.
sections.heading: Time fields

sections.body:
- P95 latency for `GET /v1/deploys/recent`: < 250ms (in-region)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly
sections.heading: SLO target (deploy-registry API)

sections.body:
- `GET /v1/deploys/recent`: 60 RPM sustained, burst 20
- `GET /v1/rollouts/{id}`: 30 RPM sustained, burst 10
sections.heading: Default (per calling service identity)

sections.body:
- Use cached responses for thread interactions.
- Prefer `/recent` in the “first 5 minutes” path.
sections.heading: Incident-bot guidance

sections.body:
- `/recent` responses are cacheable for 30s.
- `deploy-registry` should return partial results rather than fail when one backing store is degraded.
sections.heading: Caching behavior

sections.body:
- If the deploy store is unavailable, return HTTP 200 with an empty array and `X-Deploy-Registry-Degraded: true`.
- If fields cannot be resolved (e.g., missing PR linkage), return the record with the known identifiers and omit unknown optional fields.
sections.heading: Failure modes and degraded behavior

sections.body:
- Deploy metadata is classified **internal** and must not include tenant identifiers, customer payloads, or secrets.
- AuthN/AuthZ is service-to-service; no end-user tokens.
- All API access is logged (service identity, endpoint, params excluding any free-form text).
sections.heading: Security and access control

sections.body:
- Tenant/customer IDs
- Feature flag values
- Request payload samples
- Any secret material (tokens, keys)
sections.heading: Explicitly prohibited fields

sections.body:
- Raw events: 30 days (event bus retention)
- Materialized deploy records: 180 days (supports postmortems and trend analysis)
sections.heading: Data retention

sections.body:
- Event schema is versioned via `schema_version`. v1 is the baseline for incident-bot v2 GA.
- Additive changes are allowed (new optional fields).
- Breaking changes require a new major schema version (v2) and a migration plan with at least 4 weeks dual-write.
sections.heading: Versioning and compatibility

sections.body:
1) Emit `deploy.event.v1` on rollout start and completion, plus canary completion.
2) Include `service_id`, `environment`, `rollout_id`, `region` (or `global`), `commit_sha`, and `image_digest`.
3) Provide PR linkage when available (`repo`, `pr_number`, `pr_title`).
4) Include `canary_json` for `canary_passed` / `canary_failed`.
5) Validate JSON against the v1 rules in CI (see internal linter: `deploy-event-lint`).
sections.heading: Implementation checklist (for deploy emitters)

sections.body:
**Q: Why both events and an API?**
A: Events are the canonical ingest mechanism (cheap, reliable, decoupled). The API provides a bounded, cacheable query surface for incident-bot and UI surfaces.

**Q: What if a service has no canary?**
A: Emit phases without canary states; `canary_status` will be `unknown`. Incident-bot will still show “recent deploy started/completed” context.

**Q: How do private deployments participate?**
A: Private deploy agents emit the same event schema. If connectivity to the central bus is restricted, the private control plane can proxy events and/or expose a local deploy-registry API for the bot running in that environment.
sections.heading: FAQ

sections.body:
- Spec owner: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien)
- API implementation owner: Eng Infra / CI-CD (Sahana Iyer)
- Primary consumer owner: Incident Automation (Miles Thornton)
sections.heading: Owners

sections.body:
- 2025-02-18: Initial draft (v1 schema + /recent endpoint)
- 2025-03-11: Added canary_json rules and degraded behavior header
- 2025-04-09: Finalized rate limits, retention, and rollout phase enum for GA
sections.heading: Change log

payload.page_title: Reproducible Builds and Artifact Signing for Runtime LTS

sections.body:
This page defines **build + CI standards** for the Runtime **Long Term Support (LTS)** channel artifacts (e.g., `runtime-1.18-lts`). The goal is to ensure every LTS patch release produces artifacts that are:
- **Reproducible** (same inputs yield the same outputs within defined tolerance)
- **Auditable** (provenance, SBOM, and traceability to source commits)
- **Verifiable** (signatures and checksums customers can validate)
- **Consistent across packaging** (Hosted/Dedicated image pipeline and Private/Helm distribution)

This is a normative document. Deviations require an explicit waiver in the release issue and approval from Release Engineering + Security.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Runtime container images (primary distribution)
- Private distribution bundles (offline/air-gapped friendly)
- Helm chart values support and release note URL annotations (distribution metadata; chart signing is tracked separately)
- Release provenance attestations
- Checksums for all downloadable artifacts
- SBOM generation and publication requirements
sections.heading: In scope artifacts (LTS)

sections.body:
- Feature builds on mainline branches (covered by standard runtime CI policies)
- Third-party artifacts not produced by Redwood CI (GPU drivers, OS base images), except as recorded inputs in SBOM
sections.heading: Out of scope

sections.body:
- **LTS branch:** A long-lived release branch (example: `runtime-1.18-lts`) that receives controlled backports.
- **Patch version:** A patch release for an LTS branch (example: `1.18.1-lts`, `1.18.2-lts`).
- **Provenance:** Machine-verifiable metadata describing what was built, from which source, by which builder, and with what inputs.
- **SBOM:** Software Bill of Materials describing components (packages, versions, licenses) present in an artifact.
- **SLSA:** Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts. LTS aims for SLSA-aligned attestations (target: SLSA v1 provenance at build time).
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
The following requirements are **MUST** for every LTS patch release:
1. **Immutable versioning:** Every artifact is tied to a unique runtime version and git commit.
2. **Deterministic build inputs:** Toolchains, dependencies, and build configs are pinned and recorded.
3. **Checksums:** SHA-256 checksums are generated for all downloadable artifacts.
4. **Signing:** Container images and downloadable bundles are signed.
5. **Provenance:** Provenance attestations are generated and published for signed artifacts.
6. **SBOM:** SBOM is generated, published, and referenced from release notes.
7. **Traceability:** Customers and internal teams can map an artifact → digest → commit → release notes entry.
sections.heading: Policy summary (what’s required)

sections.body:
- LTS patch version format: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-lts` (example: `1.18.1-lts`)
- Git tag format: `runtime-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-lts` (example: `runtime-v1.18.1-lts`)
sections.heading: Version strings

sections.body:
- LTS patches are cut from `runtime-<major>.<minor>-lts`.
- The tagged commit **MUST** be the merge commit of the release PR (or a fast-forward equivalent), and must match what is recorded in provenance.
sections.heading: Branch-to-tag rules

sections.body:
The runtime binary and/or image labels **MUST** include:
- `org.opencontainers.image.revision` (git SHA)
- `org.opencontainers.image.version` (e.g., `1.18.1-lts`)
- `org.opencontainers.image.source` (repo URL)
- `org.opencontainers.image.created` (UTC ISO-8601)

For non-container artifacts, a `BUILDINFO` file is required (see “Private distribution bundles”).
sections.heading: Required embedded build metadata

sections.body:
LTS artifacts must be built using the **release builder** workflow with:
- Pinned build container image (builder image tag is immutable and stored in the release manifest)
- Pinned compiler/toolchain versions
- Pinned dependency lockfiles (language-specific)
- No network-dependent downloads during the final build step, except from explicitly whitelisted artifact mirrors (recorded in provenance)
sections.heading: Builder environment

sections.body:
- Use `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set to the tagged commit timestamp (UTC)
- Strip or stabilize non-deterministic metadata (timestamps, absolute paths, random seeds)
- Ensure build steps do not depend on local machine identity (hostname, username)
- Enforce consistent ordering when packaging (tar/zip file ordering)
sections.heading: Determinism controls (required)

sections.body:
Because GPU kernels and compilation paths can introduce variance, our reproducibility definition is:
- **Byte-for-byte reproducible** for: release manifests, checksum files, provenance, SBOM artifacts, and non-GPU ancillary binaries.
- **Content-reproducible** for: container image filesystem contents and runtime binaries, where any permitted variance must be documented and attributable to approved non-determinism sources. Any variance requires a release waiver and Security approval.
sections.heading: Reproducibility tolerance

sections.body: **Primary artifact** for Hosted/Dedicated and default for Private/Helm.
sections.heading: Runtime container images

sections.body:
- Image tag: `redwood/runtime:<version>` (example: `redwood/runtime:1.18.1-lts`)
- Immutable digest recorded in the release manifest
- Signature (cosign) attached to the image digest
- Provenance attestation (SLSA-style) attached to the digest
- SBOM attached to the digest and/or published alongside release notes
sections.heading: Required

sections.body:
- `org.opencontainers.image.version`
- `org.opencontainers.image.revision`
- `org.opencontainers.image.source`
sections.heading: Minimum OCI labels

sections.body: Private customers often require offline verification.
sections.heading: Private distribution bundles (downloadable)

sections.body:
- `runtime-image-digest.txt` (the exact image digest that must be pulled/loaded)
- `CHECKSUMS.sha256` for all files in the bundle
- `CHECKSUMS.sha256.sig` (signature over checksum file)
- `PROVENANCE.intoto.jsonl` (or equivalent attestation format)
- `SBOM.spdx.json` (or CycloneDX, see SBOM section)
- `BUILDINFO` file

`BUILDINFO` MUST contain:
- version
- git SHA
- build timestamp (UTC)
- builder workflow identifier (CI run URL and run ID)
- dependency lockfile hashes
- base image digest (if applicable)
sections.heading: Required bundle contents

sections.body: For each patch release, publish a single release manifest (human-readable) linked from release notes.
sections.heading: Release manifest

sections.body:
- Version and git tag
- Commit SHA
- Container image digest(s)
- Checksums URL
- Signature verification instructions
- Provenance location
- SBOM location
sections.heading: Release manifest MUST include

sections.body:
- Container images (by digest)
- `CHECKSUMS.sha256` for Private bundles and any downloadable artifacts
sections.heading: What we sign

sections.body:
- **cosign** is the standard signing tool for LTS artifacts.
- Keys are managed by Security (KMS-backed where possible). Access is restricted to release workflows.
sections.heading: Mechanism

sections.body:
- Signing keys must not be accessible to developer laptops.
- CI uses short-lived identity where possible; long-lived keys (if any) must be kept in secured key management.
- Any manual signing is an exception and requires:
  - Security approval
  - documented incident/change record
  - post-facto audit note in the release ticket
sections.heading: Key management and access controls

sections.body:
Release notes must include a short “Verify artifacts” section describing:
- How to verify image signatures by digest
- How to validate `CHECKSUMS.sha256` signature
- Where to retrieve provenance and SBOM
sections.heading: Customer verification instructions (must be included in release notes)

sections.body:
- Use **SHA-256** for all downloadable artifacts.
- Checksums must be generated in CI from the final produced artifacts.
- `CHECKSUMS.sha256` must be deterministic and include:
  - one line per file
  - stable ordering
  - relative paths within the bundle
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body: - Checksums are published in the same location as artifacts and linked from release notes.
sections.heading: Publication

sections.body:
- Subject(s): artifact identifiers (image digest and/or file checksum)
- Builder identity: CI workflow name and run ID
- Source repository URL
- Source revision (git SHA)
- Build invocation parameters (at least high-level)
- Materials: base image digests and critical dependencies
sections.heading: Every provenance attestation must include

sections.body:
- For container artifacts: provenance is attached as an OCI attestation to the image digest.
- For downloadable bundles: provenance is included as a file in the bundle and also stored in the release artifact repository.
sections.heading: Storage

sections.body:
Release notes must link to the provenance artifact(s) and include:
- git tag
- CI build run URL
- image digest
sections.heading: Relationship to release notes

sections.body:
- Preferred format: **SPDX JSON** (`SBOM.spdx.json`).
- Acceptable alternative: **CycloneDX JSON**.
sections.heading: Format

sections.body: SBOM must be generated during the release build from the final artifacts, not from source-only dependency graphs.
sections.heading: Generation

sections.body:
- OS packages in the container image
- Language-level dependencies (pip/npm/cargo/go modules, as applicable)
- Embedded native libraries (if present)
- License metadata where available
sections.heading: SBOM must capture

sections.body:
- SBOM is published alongside the patch release and referenced in the release notes.
- Retention: minimum 24 months for LTS artifacts (aligns with enterprise audit timelines).
sections.heading: Publication and retention

sections.body: - Some GPU driver or kernel-level components may not be present in the container image and therefore won’t appear in SBOM; this should be called out explicitly when customers request full stack attestation.
sections.heading: Known limitations (document in release notes if relevant)

sections.body: This section defines the canonical path from an installed artifact back to the corresponding LTS notes and source.

1. Start from artifact identifier:

2. Resolve to provenance:

payload.page_title: GPU canary burst backstop and CI safety harness

sections.body: This document defines the design, IaC integration, and operational runbook for the 'GPU Canary Burst Backstop' — a CI/CD safety harness that automatically exercises limited burst capacity during GPU image and kernel rollouts and provides automated backstop actions (throttle, rollback, and postmortem hooks) when defined safety gates fail. The goal is to let build/infra teams validate real allocation and egress behaviour without exposing production SLAs to undue risk.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Recent rollouts of mixed-precision kernels and new driver bundles caused transient tenant preemptions and elevated egress traffic.
- We need a reproducible CI-driven mechanism that:
  - Exercises warm-pool and burst paths during canaries.
  - Runs lightweight traffic simulations to detect allocation regressions.
  - Enforces Terraform plan-level policy and CI gates before promotion.
sections.heading: Motivation

sections.body:
- Audience: GPU platform engineers, CI/CD owners, oncall SRE.
- Scope: Host (managed) and Dedicated fleet rollouts that touch node images, runtime kernels, or instance-level network egress rules. Does NOT cover on-prem air-gapped Private bundles (these use the airgap promotion checklist).
sections.heading: Scope and audience

sections.body:
- Canary lane: a controlled canary topology consisting of 1–3 tenant shadow workloads routed to a dedicated warm-pool slice.
- Burst backstop: automated steps executed when canary telemetry crosses thresholds (throttle, scale-down, abort, rollback).
- Safety gate: metric-based condition in CI that must pass for rollout to continue.
sections.heading: Definitions

sections.body:
- Warm-pool allocation success >= 99.0% within 60s for canary requests.
- No more than 5% increase in 95th p99 tokenization/latency CPU (canary workload baseline).
- Egress spike delta <= +20% compared to baseline for the same synthetic workload.
- Canary incident must auto-abort rollback within 10 minutes of safety gate breach.
sections.heading: Safety goals and SLOs for canary lane

sections.body:
1) CI job composition (example names):
   - ci/gpu-image/build -> publishes signed image tag to registry.
   - ci/gpu-image/canary-deploy -> triggers canary deployment to warm-pool slice and runs simulator.
   - ci/gpu-image/validate -> checks metric gates and Terraform plan policy.
   - ci/gpu-image/promote -> promotes Terraform variables and triggers global rollout.

2) Canary topology and networking:
   - Dedicated warm-pool slice with min_size=2, max_size=6 GPUs (pool type: canary).
   - VPC egress path uses egress-shard 'canary' and an egress-proxy to limit blast radius.
   - Canary IAM role limited with tenant-stub credentials to avoid customer data access.

3) IaC / Terraform integration:
   - Terraform modules must expose a 'canary' bool and 'canary_pool_id' output.
   - Pre-merge: policy check via tflint/OPA policy that blocks plan when canary_pool_id is absent and rollout touches image_version or kernel_tag.
   - Promotion: promotion pipeline updates module var canary=false -> triggers full rollout.

4) Simulation and synthetic traffic:
   - Use the 'burst-smoke' harness (repo: infra/burst-sim) to generate 5–50 short LLM requests with realistic token distribution and KV-cache patterns.
   - The harness runs 3 iterations (low, medium, high concurrency) with 30s warmup and captures allocation, preemption, and egress metrics.
sections.heading: High level design

sections.body:
- Allocation success rate >= 99.0% within 60s.
- p95 latency change <= +15% from baseline.
- Egress spike delta <= +20% from baseline.
- No worker OOMs or kernel crashes logged.
- No preempt_count increase > 2 per node.
sections.heading: Safety gates (checked by ci/gpu-image/validate)

sections.body:
- Metrics used: warm_pool_allocation_success, gpu_preempt_count, tenant_kv_cache_misses, inference_p95_latency, egress_bytes_per_min.
- Validation job writes a JSON verdict to S3 (path: s3://redwood-ci-canary-verdicts/<build_id>.json) consumed by promo controller.
sections.heading: Metric sources and alert hooks

sections.body:
1) Soft throttle: ci/controller sets canary_pool.max_size = current and scales min_size down to 1 to reduce new allocations.
2) Abort traffic: route engine flips canary routing to traffic-sink (no customer impact).
3) Rollback image: pipeline triggers image revert using previous signed image tag and redeploys to canary pool.
4) Create incident: automatic PagerDuty incident with pre-populated playbook and timeline snapshoter.

Runbook: Canary abort and rollback (oncall steps)
1) PagerDuty alerted with tag 'gpu-canary-failure'.
2) Oncall verifies verdict JSON in S3 and checks grafana dashboard 'Canary / ci/gpu-image/<build_id>'.
3) If verdict says 'abort', confirm that controller executed Soft throttle. If not, run: infractl canary throttle --pool <id> --min 1 --reason "CI gate breach".
4) If rollback not executed, run: infractl image rollback --pool <id> --to-tag <previous-tag> and observe pod restarts.
5) Validate post-rollback metrics for 15 minutes; if instability persists escalate to platform-eng escalation channel.
6) Capture logs: kernel crash logs, dmesg snapshots, and egress proxy logs; attach to incident.

Post-deploy verification checklist (ci/gpu-image/validate runbook):
- CI verdict present and marked PASS.
- grafana: allocation success and p95 within threshold for three consecutive 5-min windows.
- No node-level kernel oops in last 30 minutes.
- Egress proxy throttle events absent.
sections.heading: Automated backstop actions (ordered)

sections.body:
- OPA rule (pseudo):
  package redwood.iac
  deny[msg] {
    input.change.type == "module"
    input.change.module == "gpu_pool"
    not input.change.variables.canary_pool_id
    msg = "gpu pool changes require an explicit canary_pool_id variable for safe promotion"
  }
sections.heading: Terraform / OPA policy snippets (example)

sections.body:
name: Canary deploy and validate
  on: [workflow_dispatch]
  jobs:
    canary-deploy:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - name: terraform init & plan
          run: |
            terraform init -backend-config=...
            terraform workspace select canary || terraform workspace new canary
            terraform apply -var='image_tag=${{ github.sha }}' -auto-approve
        - name: kick simulator
          run: infra/burst-sim/run --pool ${POOL_ID} --profile medium --out verdict.json
        - name: upload verdict
          uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
          with:
            name: verdict-${{ github.sha }}
            path: verdict.json
sections.heading: Example GitHub Actions job (trimmed)

sections.body:
- Owner: GPU Platform (oncall rotation) — primary contact: @gpu-platform-oncall.
- CI job owners: ci-team (ci-owner@redwood.ai).
- Expected MTTD for canary failures: 5 minutes (automated detection).
- Expected MTTR for automated rollback: 10–30 minutes depending on image size and pool churn.
sections.heading: Operational ownership and SLAs

sections.body:
- The harness can run in 'dry-run' mode that produces a verdict without mutating pool sizes (useful for PR validation).
- Nightly canary rehearsals run in sandbox accounts and publish a weekly summary to #gpu-canary-feedback.
sections.heading: Testing and dry-run guidance

sections.body:
- False positive rate (CI gates that caused rollback but no production impact).
- Time-to-rollback and time-to-stable.
- Number of canary verifications per month and pass rate.

Appendix A: Quick commands
- Check verdict: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ci-canary-verdicts/<build_id>.json -
- Force rollback (manual): infractl image rollback --pool <id> --to-tag <previous-tag> --reason "manual reversion"
- Canary throttle: infractl pool update --id <id> --min-size 1 --max-size <current>

Appendix B: Troubleshooting matrix (summary)
| Symptom | Likely cause | Immediate action | Owner |
|---------|--------------|------------------|-------|
| High preempt_count during canary | driver/kernel regression | Soft throttle, capture dmesg, rollback | oncall |
| Egress spike > +20% | regression in client batching logic or proxy misroute | Abort traffic to sink, throttle egress proxy rules | networking |
| Allocation failures | wrong instance profile or IAM | Verify canary role has compute:AttachPermissions, revert terraform change | infra-iac |
sections.heading: Metrics to collect for continuous improvement

sections.body:
- Primary escalation: @gpu-platform-oncall (Slack)
- Secondary: infra-sre-escalation@redwood.ai
- For security-sensitive issues (e.g., unexpected data access), open a security-incident and notify security@redwood.ai.
sections.heading: Contact and escalation

sections.body:
- 2024-09-20: Initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2024-11-15: Added OPA policy and soft-throttle step (reviewers: Diego Alvarez).
- 2025-02-05: Formalized SLAs and added CI job templates; published.
sections.heading: Change history

sections.body:
- infra/burst-sim repo (internal link)
- grafana/dashboard/canary-deployments
- runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook
sections.heading: Related resources

sections.body:
- Add an integration test that runs the same harness against a heterogenous slow-node pool (action: Priya Nair, target Q2 2025).
- Evaluate if egress delta thresholds should be scoped per-region (action: networking team).

This playbook is intentionally conservative: prefer abort and rollback over continuing a rollout when the canary reveals resource or kernel regressions.

payload.page_title: GPU image promotion and canary CD playbook

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the end-to-end process for building, validating, promoting, and performing controlled canary rollouts of GPU node images and accelerator runtime artifacts across Redwood Inference clusters and cloud accounts. It codifies CI/CD jobs, Terraform/IaC interactions, safety gates, metrics to observe during canaries, and runbook steps for fast rollback. Purpose: reduce runtime regressions, improve reproducibility, and make image promotion auditable across accounts and regions.

Scope
-----
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- GPU node AMIs/VM images and container images that include: kernel modules, NVIDIA drivers, CUDA/CUDNN, runtime libraries, custom accelerator optimizations (e.g., Triton init hooks), and the Redwood node agent.
- Promotion across: staging -> qa -> production (regional) accounts and Dedicated/private customers when applicable.
Excludes: model container images and user payloads (handled by model release pipelines).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Image build: CI job that composes OS base, driver packages, accelerator firmware, and final configuration.
- Promotion: tagging/publishing an image version and updating Terraform image IDs in environment state.
- Canary: controlled rollout to a small percentage of fleet for a specified validation window.
- Gate: a set of automated and manual approvals required before moving to next stage.

Prerequisites
-------------
1) IaC: Terraform modules for node pools must accept image_id, image_version, and image_metadata tags.
2) CI: Build pipeline must publish artifacts to an image registry (AMI/OCI) and create a signed release record in the artifact store.
3) RBAC: CI service identity and release engineers have access to image promotion job in each cloud account.
4) Observability: dashboards and alerts defined (see Metrics and SLOs).

Promotion pipeline (high level)
------------------------------
1) Build & unit tests (CI): produce image vX.Y.Z and run deterministic smoke tests in hermetic environment.
2) Integration tests: spin ephemeral GPU instance in isolated VPC; run driver compatibility, NVML, and small inference workload.
3) Publish to staging registry and create release metadata (SHA256, bill-of-materials).
4) Canary deploy to 2% of nodes in staging cluster for 2 hours. Verify gates.
5) If pass, promote to QA account for cross-account tests and network egress validation.
6) After QA, create Terraform plan diff for production node pools and open canary rollout MR.
7) Apply canary: update 1–5% of production nodes by rolling-replace with image version, observe, then increment per policy.
8) Full promotion: once canary passes all gates, merge and apply across remaining nodes by region.

Detailed Canary Strategy
------------------------
- Canary cohorts: small subsets selected by label: role=worker-gpu and tag=canary-eligible. Prefer underutilized availability zones.
- Canary size progression: 1% -> 2.5% -> 5% -> 10% (each step minimum observation window 30–120 minutes depending on workload).
- Safety windows: if any critical alert fires (see alert list), immediate pause and rollback.
- Auto-rollback policy: CI job sets canary TTL; if failing thresholds are met, automation triggers Terraform to revert changed instances or triggers node replace with previous image.

Automated Gates and Tests
-------------------------
sections.heading: Applies to

sections.body:
- Driver sanity: nvidia-smi returns expected GPU list and driver version.
- NVML memory test: allocate & release 90% of a test device repeatedly.
- Model inference smoke: run 5 end-to-end small samples through locally-deployed model server and validate outputs against golden set.
- Kernel oops regression scan: kernel message buffer scanned for new oops/panic line patterns post-boot.
- Boot time and readiness: node must register with k8s within 4 minutes and pass node-exporter liveness.

Example CI job snippets
-----------------------
sections.heading: Automated gates run in CI/CD and during canary

sections.body:
jobs:
    build-image:
      steps: [checkout, build, unit-tests, publish-artifact]
    image-integration-tests:
      steps: [spin-gpu, install-image, run-nvml-tests, run-smoke]
    promote-to-staging:
      steps: [register-release, tag-image, notify-team]
    kick-canary:
      steps: [terraform-plan-canary, terraform-apply-canary, monitor-canary]

Terraform and IaC interactions
-----------------------------
- Image metadata: every image must have tags: image_version, build_id, sha256, built_by, base_os. These are written to SSM/ParameterStore and the artifact registry.
- Promotion process: CI writes a release JSON to a central S3 bucket: release-(image_version).json. A Terraform data source in infra modules reads the release JSON to populate image IDs for Terraform plan.
- Immutable references: production Terraform state must reference immutable image IDs (AMI_ID or digest). Avoid referencing mutable tags for production pools.

Configuration table (required fields)
------------------------------------
| field | purpose | example |
| image_version | human-readable version | v2025.01.09-rc1 |
| image_digest | immutable image digest | sha256:abcdef... |
| build_id | CI build identifier | circleci/12345 |
| canary_window_minutes | observation window per step | 60 |
| canary_cohort_label | node label used to select canary nodes | canary-eligible=true |
| rollback_thresholds | thresholds causing rollback | cpu_err_rate>0.5% or gpu_oops=true |

Metrics and SLOs to watch during canary
--------------------------------------
- Node registration latency: target < 4 minutes.
- GPU driver error-rate (rate of nvml/device-failure logs): target < 0.01% per minute.
- Inference p50/p95 latency vs baseline: p95 must not regress more than 15%.
- Scheduler pod eviction rates and OOM events: zero tolerated for canary cohort.
- Cost anomalies: unexpected GPU-hours spike -> pause rollout.

Alert list (examples)
---------------------
- GPU_DRIVER_CRIT: nvml errors >= 5 within 10m in canary cohort.
- NODE_UNREGISTERED: node fails to register within 6m post-boot.
- INFERENCE_REGRESSION: p95 latency > 15% vs baseline or error rate increases by +0.5%.
- KERNEL_OOPS_DETECTED: new oops lines matching regex in syslog.

Manual checkpoints and approvals
-------------------------------
- Promotion from QA -> Production requires at least one on-call sign-off and documentation that all automated gates passed.
- For Private/Customer-dedicated clusters, Customer Success must consent to image changes that affect underlying runtime.

Runbook: Rapid rollback (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
1) Pause pipeline: cancel further Terraform applies and stop CI promote jobs.
2) Isolate canary cohort: taint node pools or cordon nodes to avoid scheduling.
3) Trigger rollback job: CI invokes terraform apply with previous immutable image id.
4) Monitor: watch node registration and key alerts for 30 minutes.
5) Postmortem: collect boot logs, dmesg, journalctl, driver logs, and attach to incident ticket.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Owners: Infra - GPU Platform team (primary), SRE on-call (secondary).
- Pager escalation: 20 min internal response SLA for canary-critical alerts.
- Post-incident: GPU Platform lead owns the postmortem within 5 business days.

Appendix A: Validation checklist (pre-promotion)
------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Release JSON exists and is signed in S3.
- [ ] Integration tests pass (exit code 0).
- [ ] Canary cohort label applied and nodes available.
- [ ] Observability dashboards added to runbook view.
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed and MR opened with canary policy.

Appendix B: Example troubleshooting commands
-------------------------------------------
- Check driver: ssh node && sudo nvidia-smi -q
- Check node join logs: kubectl describe node <node>
- Inspect kernel messages: journalctl -k -b | tail -n 200
- Re-image single node: terraform taint module.node_pool.aws_instance.example[3] && terraform apply -target=module.node_pool.aws_instance.example[3]

Appendix C: Frequently asked questions
-------------------------------------
Q: Why use immutable image ids for production?
A: Prevents accidental drift, simplifies rollback, and makes audits reproducible.

Q: What if a canary fails intermittently across regions?
A: Pause global rollouts and split by region; diagnose base OS/driver combo differences using the compatibility matrix in team wiki.

Related docs and links
----------------------
- Golden image pipeline (internal): /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/gpu-node-bootstrap-and-golden-image-pipeline.json
- IaC provisioning patterns: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/provisioning-accelerators-via-iac-and-network-design.json
- Node bootstrap scripts repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/gpu-node-bootstrap.git

Change log
----------
- 2024-06-15: Created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2024-09-02: Added automated NVML tests and canary progression policy (reviewed by Diego).
- 2025-01-10: Updated Terraform integration pattern to use release JSON and added rollback automation steps.

payload.page_title: GPU artifact provenance and promote hash-lock

sections.body: Operational runbook and design for ensuring GPU model/runtime artifact provenance, deterministic promotion between CI lanes, and a hash-lock promotion gate to prevent accidental or malicious artifact swaps.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body: This document defines the provenance and promotion controls we use for GPU-facing artifacts (model weights, quantized kernels, runtime bundles, and OCI images) and the hash-lock promotion gate implemented in CI/CD. It combines security-minded signing, deterministic metadata, and a lightweight lockfile mechanism to ensure promotes are auditable and atomic across regions and accounts.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- Prevent accidental / silent replacement of artifacts during promotion.
- Make artifact lineage auditable end-to-end (source commit, build inputs, build env, checksum, signer).
- Keep CI promotion fast and automatable while providing a human-reviewable checkpoint for high-risk changes.
- Integrate with existing Terraform/IaC and image registries used by the GPU fleet.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Artifact: any deployable binary used by the runtime or evals pipeline: OCI image, tarball with kernels, .pt/.bin model weights, quantization tables, or signed kernel blobs.
- Provenance record: JSON document containing build inputs (git sha, module versions, TF vars), environment hash (BUILD_IMAGE, toolchain versions), artifact checksum (sha256), and signer identity.
- Promote: moving an artifact from a lower lane (e.g., canary, staging) to a higher lane (prod/dedicated).
- Hash-lock: a small lockfile checked into the promotion branch that records the expected artifact checksum; the gate requires the artifact checksum to match before the promotion pipeline allows the move.
sections.heading: Scope and definitions

sections.body:
1. Build: CI job produces artifact + provenance.json (signed by build-service key).
2. Upload: artifact pushed to registry (OCI or S3) under a lane-specific path with immutable tags (sha256).
3. Lock generation: build job writes a lockfile (artifact-name:sha256) and files it as a PR against the promote branch.
4. Review & sign-off: reviewers verify the provenance and approve the PR.
5. Promote job: verifies lockfile checksum matches registry artifact and that the provenance signature validates; if OK, updates infra promotion state (Terraform var, image tag alias) via a controlled apply.
sections.heading: High-level flow (summary)

sections.body:
- Build-service (buildkite/github-actions): runs hermetic builds using the pinned runner image: ghcr.io/redwood/build-runner:v2025-03-01. Generates: artifact.tar.gz, provenance.json, artifact.sha256, provenance.json.sig.
- Registry patterns:
  - OCI images: us-east1.gcr.io/rw/gpu-images/<lane>/<artifact>:sha256-<short>
  - S3 bundles: s3://rw-gpu-artifacts/<lane>/<artifact>/sha256-<long>.tar.gz
- Provenance schema (example; actual file attached in repo as schema/provenance-v1.json):
  {
    "version": "1",
    "artifact_name": "kernels-nightly-quantized-v2",
    "git_sha": "abcd1234",
    "build_image": "ghcr.io/redwood/build-runner:v2025-03-01",
    "toolchain": {"bazel": "6.2.0", "python": "3.11.2"},
    "build_args": ["--strip-debug","--enable-quant"],
    "artifact_sha256": "<sha256-hex>",
    "timestamp": "2025-11-03T17:02:00Z",
    "signed_by": "build-service@redwood-infra"
  }
(We require the provenance.json to be produced by a single build step to avoid piecemeal assembly.)
sections.heading: Detailed components

sections.body:
- Lockfile format (PROMOTE_LOCKS/locks.yaml):
  - artifact: kernels-nightly-quantized-v2
  - lane_from: staging
  - lane_to: prod
  - artifact_sha256: 012345abcdef...
  - provenance_path: s3://rw-gpu-artifacts/staging/kernels-nightly-quantized-v2/provenance-v1/012345.json
  - requested_by: dev-queue
  - approvals: []
- Lock lifecycle:
  1) Build job opens PR to promote branch with locks.yaml entry for the artifact. PR title must start with [promote-lock].
  2) At least one reviewer from the gpu-fleet or infra-cd team must approve PR if lane_to == prod or dedicated (policy).
  3) CI promotion job runs on merge: it resolves the lock entry, downloads the artifact from registry, computes sha256, verifies equals artifact_sha256 in lockfile.
  4) It then fetches provenance.json and verifies signature using our internal KMS-backed signing key (see crypto section).
  5) If checks pass, promotion job updates Terraform varstore (terraform workspace:gpu-prod) with the new immutable image reference (sha256) and triggers a targeted apply via the promotion pipeline.
sections.heading: Hash-lock promotion pattern (implementation details)

sections.body:
1) Build completed and PR opened (check PR body: provenance link, build logs).
2) Reviewer verifies provenance.json: confirm git_sha, toolchain, and no unexpected external downloads.
3) Approve PR.
4) After merge, monitor promotion job in buildkite: job steps: verify-sha -> verify-signature -> terraform-apply -> rollout-watcher.
5) After apply, confirm Canary metrics (latency P95, error rate) for 30 minutes before wide rollout.
sections.heading: Operator checklist (fast path)

sections.body:
1) If promotion job fails hash-check: do not apply. Revert the lock PR and re-run build.
2) If rollout causes regressions: trigger terraform rollback by applying the previous known-good sha256 alias in the varstore (we keep last-3 releases in promotion metadata).
3) Incident process: open an infra-incident, attach provenance, and run the regression-triage checklist.
sections.heading: Rollback procedure (if mismatch or regression)
Terraform and IaC interactions

sections.body:
- Build machines hold a short-lived signing token issued by the HSM/KMS service (key rotation every 30 days).
- provenance.json.sig is an RFC5652/CMS-style signature with the signer identity embedded.
- Verification uses the public key bundle pinned in the promotion job (fetched from internal secrets store).
sections.heading: Signing and key custody

sections.body:
- Build step (bash):
  set -euo pipefail
  bazel build //gpu/kernels:release --config=quant
  tar czf artifact.tar.gz bazel-bin/gpu/kernels/release
  sha256sum artifact.tar.gz > artifact.sha256
  ./sign-provenance.sh provenance.json > provenance.json.sig
  aws s3 cp artifact.tar.gz s3://rw-gpu-artifacts/staging/kernels-nightly-quantized-v2/sha256-$(cat artifact.sha256 | cut -d' ' -f1).tar.gz
  gh pr create --title "[promote-lock] promote kernels-nightly-quantized-v2" --body "provenance: ${PROVENANCE_URL}" --base promote/locks
- Promote step (outline):
  - download locks.yaml from merged branch
  - for each lock: curl registry -> compute sha256 -> compare -> verify provenance sig via kms verify -> if ok write tfvars and run terraform apply
sections.heading: CI/CD snippets (Buildkite/GHA simplified)

sections.body:
- Telemetry points to emit:
  - build.provenance.generated (counter)
  - promote.hashcheck.success/failure (counter)
  - promote.provenance.verify.duration (histogram)
  - promotion.terraform.apply.duration (histogram)
- Dashboards: GPU infra > Promotions: last 30d promotions, failures by cause, time-to-promote percentiles.
sections.heading: Monitoring and observability

sections.body:
- Threat: Malicious actor swaps an image tag in registry after PR approval. Mitigation: strict use of immutable sha256 references and lockfile checks.
- Threat: Compromised build runner. Mitigation: ephemeral build credentials, signer key guarded by KMS with usage policy, and human reviewer check before prod promotes.
- Threat: Man-in-the-middle between registry and promotion job. Mitigation: HTTPS + registry auth, compute and compare checksums locally.
sections.heading: Security considerations and threat model

sections.body:
- Availability: promotion pipeline should succeed (or fail noisily) within 10 minutes for staged artifacts (SLO: 99.5%).
- Security: every prod promotion must have at least one reviewer approval and a provenance signature.
- Audit: provenance + lockfile + pipeline logs must be retained for 1 year (compliance).
sections.heading: Operational guidance and SLOs for promotion pipeline

sections.body:
- Extend proof-of-build reproducibility (rebuild-from-source) to close the reproducibility loop for kernels.
- Integrate sigstore/cosign for wider community tooling compatibility.
- Automatic heuristics to detect suspicious provenance attributes (e.g., unusual toolchain versions) and require additional reviewers.
sections.heading: Open questions and future work

sections.body:
- Example provenance verification CLI:
  rw-infra verify-provenance --provenance s3://.../provenance.json --sig s3://.../provenance.json.sig --pubkeys /secrets/publishers.pub
- Back-of-envelope timing: full build + upload + PR creation = ~12-18 minutes on standard runners; promote verify + terraform apply (canary only) = 4-8 minutes.
sections.heading: Appendices

sections.body:
- Primary owner: Marco Chen (infra-cd)
- Secondary: Aisha Patel (gpu-fleet)
- Pager: #infra-oncall for urgent failures
sections.heading: Ownership and contacts

sections.body:
- Terraform module: git@github.com:redwood/terraform-modules//gpu-service (ref v1.4.2)
- CI pipelines: buildkite.com/redwood/gpu-builds
- Signing key policy: security-and-compliance/key-management/gpu-build-signing-policy
sections.heading: Related reading and links

sections.body:
- 2024-02-14: document created (Marco Chen)
- 2024-10-10: added KMS signing flow and lockfile lifecycle (Priya Nair)
- 2025-11-03: tightened review policy for dedicated lanes and updated build image reference (Aisha Patel)
sections.heading: Revision history

payload.page_title: provisioning-latency-slo-and-failure-injection-fit-tests

sections.body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the provisioning latency SLOs for GPU-backed tenancy (warm and cold paths), describes a CI/CD-integrated fit-test suite that validates time-to-ready against those SLOs, and prescribes a failure-injection matrix and Terraform gating pattern to prevent regressing provisioning latency during platform or IaC changes. It is intended for infra engineers owning GPU provisioning modules, CI/CD authors, and SRE oncall.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all Terraform modules and orchestration pipelines that create or scale GPU worker pools across public cloud accounts used for: hosted inference, dedicated tenant pools, eval/CI sandboxes.
- Covers control-plane and data-plane readiness up to the point where nodes accept inference traffic (kubelet registration + network egress validated).
- Excludes long-term image bake times for airgapped customer flows (handled in eng-private-deployments).

Definitions
-----------
- Provisioning latency: wall-clock time from Terraform apply completing (API response OK) to a node reporting Ready and passing the network/keystore health probe.
- Warm path: attaching a pre-provisioned warm instance from a pool or snapshot restore. Target: low single-digit minutes.
- Cold path: provisioning a new instance from scratch (boot + attach + image init). Target: higher, expected minutes.

SLOs and Targets
-----------------
- Global SLO (per-region): 95th percentile provisioning-latency <= 6 minutes (warm path) over 30d and 99th percentile <= 12 minutes for cold path for non-critical test tenants.
- Canary SLO (per-change): 90th percentile <= 4 minutes for warm path on canary accounts during TF module promotion.
- Safety budget: any PR change that increases canary 90p by >20% blocks merge.

Measurement and Metrics
-----------------------
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
- gpu_provisioning_latency_seconds_bucket{path="warm|cold",region,account} (histogram)
- gpu_provisioning_success_total{region,account,reason} (counter)
- gpu_provisioning_failures{stage="boot|kube-register|network-probe|attach"} (counter)
sections.heading: Key metrics we publish to the infra telemetry pipeline

sections.body:
- 95p warm path (30d): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_provisioning_latency_seconds_bucket{path="warm"}[30d])) by (le, region))
- failure rate over 1h: sum(rate(gpu_provisioning_failures[1h])) by (stage, region) / sum(rate(gpu_provisioning_success_total[1h])) by (region)

CI/CD Fit-test Design
---------------------
Goals: detect regressions in provisioning time introduced by changes to Terraform, cloud provider upgrades, or network templates before promotion to prod.
sections.heading: Suggested PromQL queries (copy into dashboards)

sections.body:
1) Tests run in ephemeral canary accounts or dedicated canary namespaces (isolated billing tags).
2) Tests are deterministic for the warm path by reusing a standardized golden-launch-template and warm pool snapshot.
3) Measurements are recorded to the telemetry pipeline and compared against baseline stored in the canary-metrics bucket.
4) Non-deterministic flakes are tolerated but require triage; >3 consecutive CI failures block promotion.
sections.heading: Principles

sections.body:
1. Checkout PR branch and build TF plan for module under test.
2. Apply to a short-lived canary account using the canary workspace: terraform workspace select canary || terraform workspace new canary
3. Kick off a small warm-pool attach or scale-up (n=3).
4. Start a synthetic readiness-check agent that polls node ready state and runs a lightweight inference REST probe (curl POST /v1/predict) until success or timeout (20m).
5. Collect timing metrics and publish to telemetry via the ci-metrics API (job_id, region, module, path, latencies).
6. Compare the aggregated 90/95p to the baseline; if delta > threshold (default 20% for 90p), fail the job and attach the raw traces.
sections.heading: Fit-test steps (example automated job)

sections.body:
- name: Run provisioning fit-test
  uses: ./ci/actions/run-provisioning-fit-test@v1
  with:
    terraform_module: modules/gpu/worker-pool
    workspace: canary
    instances: 3
    path: warm
    timeout: 1200

Terraform Gate Integration
--------------------------
sections.heading: Sample GitHub Actions snippet (conceptual)

sections.body:
- automatically runs the fit-test flow for changes touching resource types: aws_instance, aws_launch_template, aws_autoscaling_group, google_compute_instance_template, azure_virtual_machine_scale_set, local-exec customization blocks.
- requires a successful canary metric comparison before merging to the main module registry.
sections.heading: We gate module promotion with a lightweight adapter that

sections.body:
1) dev opens PR -> CI runs unit TF validate + plan + static checks (tfsec/opa).
2) CI applies canary workspace -> run provisioning fit-test -> publish metrics.
3) If fit-test passes, CI promotes a plan to staging for manual smoke verification.
4) Upon staging signoff, module is published to the module registry.

Failure Injection Matrix
------------------------
sections.heading: Recommended Terraform workflow (high level)

sections.body:
- Network egress delay (simulate 200–2000 ms latency) between instance and metadata endpoints. Expected detection: kubelet register failure, alert stage=network-probe.
- Control plane API throttling (HTTP 429) for cloud provider calls. Expected detection: attach/boot failures increment attach stage counter.
- Image pull timeouts (simulate corrupted image layer) to exercise timeout logic.
- IAM/role misbinding: simulate misapplied role to ensure failure surfaced as permission error.

Each fault injection variant must be run at least once per quarterly module release. CI configuration toggles injection via parameter: fault_injection_matrix = [none, network_delay, api_throttle, image_delay, iam_fail].

Monitoring, Alerts and Escalation
--------------------------------
sections.heading: Inject faults during CI to validate robustness and alerting

sections.body:
- P1: regional provisioning failure rate > 5% over 10m AND 95p provisioning latency (warm) > 8 minutes -> Pager on SRE oncall + channel #infra-paging.
- P2: canary fit-test delta > 20% for 90p on PR -> block merge, notify PR author via CI comments and #ci-failures.
- P3: repeated TF apply errors (3 applies in 1h) -> alert to owners of the module (see Ownership table).

Runbook: Oncall immediate steps
1) Acknowledge Pager and check the regional dashboard (Provisioning > Latency & Failures).
2) If failure rate spike: open a triage ticket and add runbook tag 'provisioning-latency'.
3) Identify whether the issue stems from: recent TF change (check merge timeline), cloud provider incident (check provider status pages), or warm-pool depletion (check warm pool metrics).
4) Mitigation steps (choose one based on root cause):
   - For warm-pool exhaustion: temporarily enlarge warm pool, set burst policy = true, notify customers.
   - For control-plane throttling: reduce parallelism in TF apply (TF_PARALLELISM=2), retry with backoff.
   - For image pull issues: roll pool to previous image ID and re-trigger warm seeding.
5) After mitigation, run a targeted CI fit-test against an isolated canary account to validate recovery.
6) Post-incident: fill postmortem template and include the canary job artifacts and telemetry snapshots.

Ownership and Escalation Paths
------------------------------
- Module owner: infra/compute-team (primary contact: @compute-oncall).
- CI fit-test infra: eng-ci-team (primary contact: @ci-platform).
- SRE escalation: infra-sre (primary contact: @infra-sre-oncall).

Policy for SLO evolution
------------------------
- SLOs are reviewed quarterly by infra capacity + SRE.
- To change a global SLO, run a proposal RFC referencing 6 months of historical telemetry and estimate impact on safety budget.
- Any SLO loosening requires approval by the Reliability Committee and Product if it affects customer SLA.

Appendices
---------
A. Example PromQL (for dashboard panels):
  # 95th percentile warm path (7d window)
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_provisioning_latency_seconds_bucket{path=~"warm"}[7d])) by (le, region))

B. Example minimal TF wrapper for canary (pseudo):
  module "canary-worker" {
    source = "github.com/redwood/modules//gpu/worker-pool?ref=canary"
    name_prefix = "ci-canary"
    desired_capacity = 3
    warm_pool = true
  }

C. CI artifact retention
- Keep raw fit-test traces and perf histograms for 90 days (ci-metrics-bucket). Aggregated baselines stored for 18 months.

D. Acceptance checklist for module promotion:
- [ ] TF plan and validate (no diffs in unrelated resources)
- [ ] Fit-test canary run: 90p within threshold
- [ ] No new critical tfsec/opa findings
- [ ] Staging smoke verified (manual signoff)
- [ ] Module docs updated (upgrade notes)

Contacts and docs
-----------------
- Canonical dashboard: /dashboards/infra/provisioning-latency
- Canary workspace policy: /eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/canary-workspace-policy
- For questions: ping #infra-compute or email compute-eng@redwood.ai

Change history
--------------
- 2024-02-15 Created initial draft (Maya R. Chen)
- 2024-06-20 Added PromQL examples and CI snippet (Diego Alvarez)
- 2025-09-11 Reworked SLO thresholds and added failure-injection matrix after Q3 incident (Priya Kaur)
