payload.page_title: GPU Node Golden Image & Bootstrap Pipeline

sections.body:
Overview
-------
This document describes the end-to-end golden image and node bootstrap pipeline we use to produce immutable GPU node images for Redwood Inference (AWS AMIs and GCP custom images). The goal is to provide a reproducible, secure, and verifiable artifact used by autoscaling groups, Dedicated clusters, and Private on-prem node pools. This doc covers:
- baking process and tooling (Packer + bake jobs)
- CI/CD jobs and gate checks (GitHub Actions + internal helm/tf apply gates)
- validation test-suite and acceptance criteria
- rollout and rollback playbooks for replacing node pools
- ownership, runbook steps, and common troubleshooting

Why we bake images
------------------
- Determinism: identical base OS, drivers, and system-level tuning across fleets.
- Faster node startup: preinstalled drivers and runtime layers reduce kubelet warmup.
- Security & compliance: images are scanned and signed before release.
- Reproducible rollbacks: image version pinning in Terraform to restore previous state.

Scope and supported variants
--------------------------
- AWS: Amazon Linux 2023 based AMIs, NVidia driver bundle (driver 535.x), CUDA 12.1, containerd 1.8.x, runtimes preconfigured for MIG-aware scheduling.
- GCP: cos-custom or Ubuntu image families with identical package sets and kernel tuning.
- On-prem/air-gapped: image tarballs (OCI-compressed) and attestation artifacts for manual import.

Key SLAs for the pipeline
-------------------------
- Bake job completion target: 45 minutes (95th percentile).
- Post-bake acceptance tests must pass: 100% for gate to progress.
- Image publishing delay: <= 10 minutes from acceptance to repo/AMI family update.

Pipeline components and responsibilities
--------------------------------------
- Packer recipes: sources/infra/packer/gpu-node/ (maintained by infra/images-team).
- Bake runners: ephemeral EC2/GCE build agents launched by GitHub Actions.
- Artifact registry: AWS AMI families (redwood-gpu-ami-*), GCP image families (redwood-gpu-*).
- Signing and metadata: cosign signatures and SLSA-like metadata written to S3/GCS.
- Terraform modules: modules/compute/gpu-node-image (referenceable by consumer infra stacks).
- CI gates: GitHub Actions + internal pipeline that triggers acceptance tests and publishes promotion results to Slack #infra-images.

Packer configuration highlights (concrete)
--------------------------------------
- HCL packer template: gpu-node.pkr.hcl
- Example snippets (kept concise here):
  - builders: amazon-ebs / googlecompute with kms_encrypted_root = true
  - provisioners: shell scripts that call bootstrap scripts from infra-artifacts repo
  - post-processors: manifest and cosign signing step producing manifest.json and manifest.sig

Security and compliance requirements
----------------------------------
- Root device encrypted (KMS key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/redwood-images).
- Image hardening: CIS benchmark baseline automation (CIS-Audit exit code 0 required).
- Vulnerability scanning: Trivy CVE scan; no critical CVEs with public exploit for included packages.
- Signed artifacts: cosign signature and packer manifest stored in s3://redwood-image-manifests/{image-version}/

Acceptance test-suite (post-bake)
--------------------------------
The acceptance step runs a short test-suite on an instance launched from the baked image. All tests run in < 5 minutes where possible. Key tests:
1) Kernel and driver verification
   - nvidia-smi shows driver 535.x and CUDA visible to container runtimes
   - NCCL tests (simple allreduce small message) run without error
2) Kubelet / kube-proxy smoke
   - kubelet registers, node Ready within 90s of kubelet start
3) Container runtime
   - containerd pull + run of minimal runtime image (redwood/ci-gpu-smoke:latest)
4) Security checks
   - CIS audit pass, rootfs readonly when expected, systemd hardening checks
5) Runtime perf smoke (optional)
   - Token throughput microbenchmark completes and latency within expected range (< 12ms median for 512-token synthetic workload)

Promotion and tagging policy
---------------------------
- Image semantic versioning: vYYYY.MM.DD+build (e.g., v2024.06.03+42)
- AMI/GCP family tags: latest -> updated only after a green acceptance run and manual approval (unless auto-promote label is set).
- Terraform pinning: terraform modules should reference image_id or image_family with a required "image_ref" variable; auto-updates only via infra image bump PR.

CI/CD job flow (GitHub Actions canonical flow)
-------------------------------------------
1) PR to infra/artifacts with Packer or bootstrap changes triggers: packer-lint -> packer-bake-test -> publish-manifest (draft).
2) Acceptance job launches ephemeral instance, runs acceptance-suite, collects logs and metrics, uploads to S3/GCS.
3) On success, job creates a release artifact and posts to Slack + creates an infra PR to update module default image_ref.
4) Manual approver in the reviewers list merges the infra PR to propagate the image to Terraform staging.

Terraform integration and module contract
--------------------------------------
- Module: modules/compute/gpu-node-image (inputs):
  - image_ref (string) - required
  - instance_type_overrides (map) - optional
  - kms_key_id (string) - optional
- Output: image_id, image_family, bake_metadata_url
- Consumers: aws/eks/gke node pools and autoscaling groups must consume module outputs and expose a single variable image_ref for release management.

Rollout playbook (canary -> staggered -> full)
-----------------------------------------------
1) Pre-rollout checks
   - Check that SLOs are healthy for serving clusters (error budget >= 75% available)
   - Verify image acceptance artifact and cosign signature URL exists
   - Notify #oncall and schedule a maintenance window for Dedicated clusters if > 10% of fleet will cycle
2) Canary (a small pool)
   - Update Terraform for one node-pool with max_unavailable=1 and set image_ref to new image
   - Apply with plan and wait 10 minutes for nodes to become Ready and smoke tests to pass
   - Observe application tail latency and pod restart rates for 30m
3) Staggered rollout
   - Batch updates in 10-25% increments with 15-minute observation windows per batch
   - If any worker-level metrics spike (pod crashloop > 0.5% or 99th tail latency > x2 baseline), pause and rollback
4) Full rollout
   - Apply to remaining pools during low-traffic windows; monitor closely for 2 hours

Rollback playbook (quick revert)
------------------------------
1) If canary fails or > threshold triggers: immediately set image_ref back to prior known-good image and apply with force-replace set to true where supported.
2) For AWS ASG: set autoscaling group LaunchTemplate to previous AMI and perform instance refresh with MinHealthyPercentage = 90 to gradually replace nodes.
3) For GKE: use node pool versioning to pin to previous image family and cordon/drain failing nodes.
4) Post-rollback: open an urgent incident, collect bake logs, acceptance logs, and packer manifests for triage.

Monitoring and drift detection
----------------------------
- Image metadata exporter (Prometheus) emits: current_image_ref{pool,region}, bake_duration_seconds, acceptance_status{pass|fail}, last_bake_timestamp.
- Alerts:
  - Bake failure rate > 3 in 1hr -> PagerDuty P1 to infra-images team.
  - Node bootstrap time > 6m (Ready not reached) -> P2 to oncall.
  - Image drift alert: if node pool reports image_ref != terraform-applied image_ref -> P2.

Common troubleshooting checklist
------------------------------
1) Instance fails to boot after bake
   - Verify encrypted root KMS grants to build account
   - Inspect serial console logs via cloud provider console
2) GPU driver missing or wrong version
   - Confirm driver package in /opt/nvidia and compare against manifest.json
   - Check systemd service nvidia-persistenced status
3) Kubelet not registering
   - Check kubelet logs (/var/log/syslog or journalctl -u kubelet) for certificate/auth errors
4) Acceptance test failures
   - Download acceptance logs from s3://redwood-image-logs/{build-id}/ and run locally against an equivalent instance

Owner and contact matrix
------------------------
- Primary owner: infra/images-team (oncall: @infra-images-oncall)
- CI pipeline owner: infra-ci-team
- Security reviewers: security/compliance team
- Escalation: file an incident and tag @infra-eng @platform-sre

Appendices
----------
A) Useful commands
- Trigger a local packer build for debugging: packer build -var 'version=local-debug' gpu-node.pkr.hcl
- Launch a manual acceptance instance (AWS):
  aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0123456789abcdef0 --instance-type p3.2xlarge --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=redwood-image-test}]'
- Inspect manifest and signature: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-image-manifests/v2024.12.12+5/manifest.json -

B) Minimum image bake checklist
- Base OS kernel pinned
- GPU driver and CUDA present and versioned
- containerd and cri-tools installed
- Kubelet version aligned with cluster minor version
- CIS and Trivy scans completed
- Cosign signature present
- Bake manifest uploaded and accessible

C) Future work / backlog items
- Add ephemeral MIG partitioning bake variants for A100/MIG3 profiles
- Introduce automated perf regression detection using historical microbenchmarks
- Move to SLSA v1 attestation for deeper provenance

D) Related policies and docs
- Image publishing policy: /confluence/policies-and-process/image-publishing-policy (TBD)
- Node pool lifecycle runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/node-pool-lifecycle

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Owner: infra/images-team (maintain content and update on driver or OS upgrades)
- Review cadence: quarterly or on every major driver/kernel bump.
- Edit process: open PR in infra/docs and request reviewers listed above.

payload.page_title: GPU immutable launch bundle and Terraform policy-scan playbook

sections.body:
Overview

This playbook documents the end-to-end process to produce an immutable GPU runtime launch bundle (OCI image + baked TF modules + manifest), validate it with automated policy scans, and release it via a staged CI/CD pipeline. The goal is to provide a reproducible, auditable artifact that can be deployed to hosted, dedicated, and private clusters with minimal drift and clear rollback semantics.

Scope
- Producing immutable launch bundles for inference nodes and warm-pools.
- Enforcing Terraform policy checks (OPA/Rego + tfsec) and image SBOM verification in CI.
- Canary/staged promotion to canary -> regional -> global.
- Fast rollback and emergency patch paths.

Non-goals
- Low-level GPU kernel tuning (covered in eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling).
- Tenant-specific pricing policies.

Definitions and artifacts
- Launch bundle: OCI image (gpu-runtime:v{semver}), a hashed Terraform module tarball (tf-modules-{sha256}.tar.gz), and a JSON manifest tying image/module hashes to a release id.
- Release ID: redwood-launch-YYYYMMDD-NN (example: redwood-launch-20250110-02).
- Policy scan: combination of tfsec, OPA/Rego checks for org policies, and SCA/SBOM verification for container images.

Ownership and contacts
- Pipeline owner: eng-infra/ci-cd (primary: Maya Patel).
- IaC ownership: eng-infra/terraform-and-iac (primary: Diego Alvarez).
- Fleet/SRE oncall: eng-sre (pager: #sre-gpu).
- Security reviewers: security-and-compliance (Priya Raman).

SLOs and thresholds for launch validation
- CI green rate: 100% policy checks and unit tests.
- Image SBOM completeness: >= 95% dependency resolution.
- Tf module plan drift: no resource changes allowed for immutable modules (plan exit code != 0 on detected drift).
- Canary latency regression: 95th percentile token-latency must not increase by > 10% vs baseline.
- Canary error-rate: < 0.5% increased 5xx across 1h window.

Preconditions (checks before creating a bundle)
1. All feature branches merged to release branch (release/*).
2. All infra module versions pinned in module manifest (modules.json).
3. No active critical incidents for GPU fleet (check #sre-gpu).

Release pipeline (high level)
1) Build phase (CI runner: buildkite-gpu-builders)
   - Step 1. Checkout release branch at tag.
   - Step 2. Build OCI image using buildkite buildkite-gpu-image pipeline. Image must be signed with cosign and uploaded to registry (registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v{semver}).
   - Step 3. Produce SBOM (syft) and attach to image.
   - Example commands:
     - docker build -t registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v1.4.0 .
     - cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/cosign/ci registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v1.4.0
     - syft registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v1.4.0 -o json > sbom-v1.4.0.json

2) IaC packaging
   - Archive the exact set of TF modules used by runtime into tf-modules-{sha256}.tar.gz and push to artifact-store (s3://redwood-iac-bundles/).
   - Modules must include a modules-lock.json with provider and version pins.
   - Generate manifest.json with image/hash/module references and GPG-sign the manifest.

3) Policy & security scans (gating)
   - Run tfsec against the extracted TF modules (tfsec --config .tfsec.yaml).
   - Run rego policies (opa test ./policies -v) for org constraints: no public S3, KMS required, egres-slicing enabled, egress-proxy required for private deployments.
   - Verify SBOM: ensure no critical CVEs with exploitable severity (policy: CVSS >= 9.0 -> fail).
   - Container image scanning: trivy --severity HIGH,CRITICAL registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v{semver}. Fail on CRITICAL.

4) Integration tests (GPU-enabled runners)
   - Run nightly synthetic load tests (locust) in a dedicated canary account that mirrors customer tenancy.
   - KV-cache replay smoke tests using a 5k-token prefix set. Pass condition: cache hit-rate >= 85% and p95 latency within SLO.

5) Staged promotion
   - Promote to canary pool in region-us-west-2 (10% of traffic, routing via router-service canary-tag).
   - Observe for 2 hours with automated monitors (prometheus alert: canary-latency-regression, canary-5xx-spike).
   - If green, promote to regional (30%) for 12 hours, then global for full rollout.

Validation matrix (example)
| Check | Tool | Accept criteria | Remediation on failure | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| TF policy | OPA + tfsec | 0 policy rejects | Fix policy violations in module, re-run packaging | eng-infra/terraform-and-iac |
| Image CVEs | trivy | No CRITICAL CVEs | Patch base image or update dependency, rebuild | eng-infra/ci-cd |
| SBOM completeness | syft | >95% resolved | Investigate reproducible build inputs | eng-infra/ci-cd |
| Canary latency | prom | p95 <= baseline * 1.10 | Rollback canary, file perf investigation | eng-sre |
| KV cache hit-rate | smoke harness | >=85% | Re-evaluate warm-pool seeding strategy | eng-serving-runtime |

Release playbook (operational steps)
- Normal release (green checks): follow staged promotion sequence and update release registry (internal: releases.redwood-infra). Notify #release-notifications and update release-notes page.
- Soft-failure in stage: pause promotion, open release incident (tag: release-blocker), assign eng-sre and module owner.
- Hard failure or critical user impact: immediate rollback to previous release id (known-good) via orchestration service: orchestrator rollback --release <release-id> --force.

Rollback procedure (quick steps)
1. Identify release-id to rollback to (check release registry).
2. Run orchestration rollback (CLI example):
   - rwd-orch rollback --target release=redwood-launch-20250102-05 --scope region=us-west-2 --reason "canary latency spike"
3. Verify rollback finished and confirm canary metrics have returned to baseline for 30 minutes.
4. Postmortem: owners file a 72-hour incident review if rollback due to correctness/regressions.

CI gates and automation rules (detailed)
- Gate A: Build signing. Image must be cosign-signed by CI key and key rotation status validated.
- Gate B: Policy scan. tfsec + opa must exit 0.
- Gate C: Integration tests. Must run on GPU runners with a minimum of 4 concurrent users in the synthetic harness.
- Gate D: Manual approval for cross-account/private deployments (approval from eng-infra/priv-deploy).

Terraform policy examples (Rego snippets)
- Deny public S3 buckets (rego excerpt):
  package redwood.iac.denials

  deny[msg] {
    resource := input.resources[_]
    resource.type == "aws_s3_bucket"
    resource.config.acl == "public-read"
    msg = sprintf("s3 bucket %v is public", [resource.name])
  }

- Require KMS on EBS encryption:
  package redwood.iac.requirements

  violation[msg] {
    res := input.resources[_]
    res.type == "aws_ebs_volume"
    not res.config.kms_key_id
    msg = sprintf("ebs volume %v missing KMS", [res.name])
  }

CI/CD pipeline snippet (buildkite YAML excerpt)
- steps:
  - label: ":docker: build gpu-runtime"
    command: "scripts/build_and_sign.sh {{build.version}}"
    agents: [queue=gpu-builders]
    plugins: [docker#v3.5.0]
  - label: ":lock: policy scan"
    command: "./ci/policy_scan.sh modules.tar.gz sbom.json"
  - wait
  - label: ":rocket: promote to canary"
    command: "./ci/promote.sh --stage canary"
    concurrency: 1
    concurrency_group: "release-{{build.version}}"

Operational runbooks (troubleshooting snippets)
- If cosign signature missing: check KMS cosign key permissions and CI runner logs. Use: cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/cosign/ci registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v{semver}
- If tfsec fails with ECR public access: ensure module pins do not reference remote modules with unapproved provenance. Use modules-lock.json to pin.
- If canary latency spikes: scale canary pool to double capacity (orchestrator scale --pool canary --replicas +100%), enable fallback routing to model-variant (router-service set-fallback) and initiate KV-cache warm seeding from snapshot.

Chaos and canary drills (quarterly)
- Run a controlled canary rollback drill every quarter using the release orchestration dry-run mode: rwd-orch rollback --dry-run --release <release-id>. Document findings in the release-retrospective page.

Telemetry and dashboards to monitor
- dashboards/release/canary_overview (Grafana) — p95 latency, 5xx rate, dps (requests/sec), cache-hit-rate
- alerts: canary-latency-regression (p95 > baseline*1.10 for 15m), canary-error-spike (>0.5% 5xx increase over 10m), policy-scan-failure (CI job failure alert)

Appendix: example manifest.json (single-line sample)
{
  "release_id": "redwood-launch-20250110-02",
  "image": "registry.redwood-infr/gpu-runtime:v1.4.0",
  "image_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "tf_modules": "s3://redwood-iac-bundles/tf-modules-abc123.tar.gz",
  "manifest_signature": "GPG:..."
}

Notes and links
- Related playbooks: eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-warm-pool-replenishment-and-iac-sync.json
- Policy repository: git@github.com:redwood-infra/iac-policies.git
- Release registry: https://releases.redwood-infra.internal/

Change log
- 2024-08-12: Initial draft by Maya Patel.
- 2024-11-03: Added SBOM gating and trivy policy (security review).
- 2025-01-17: Promoted to published; added rollback CLI examples and canary thresholds (eng-sre review).

payload.page_title: CI deploy orchestration contract and audit playbook

sections.body: This document defines the formal deployment orchestration contract for Redwood Inference CI pipelines, plus the operational playbook and audit taxonomy required for production-safe rollouts. The goal is to standardize how services and model artifacts progress from build -> staging -> canary -> prod, how gates are evaluated, what events are auditable, and who owns each step.
sections.heading: Summary

sections.body:
- Platform engineers who operate the CI/CD system
- Service owners and release engineers performing rollouts
- Security & compliance reviewers and auditors
sections.heading: Intended audience

sections.body:
1) Single source of truth for promotion: every promotion must be driven by a signed artifact and an immutable promotion record stored in the deployment ledger.
2) Gate-first rollouts: automated quality gates (tests, telemetry, canary metrics) must pass before manual/automated promotion.
3) Auditable by design: every pipeline run emits structured audit events ingested into the central logging cluster and retained for 365 days.
4) Minimal blast radius: default canary size = 5% traffic, max 25% without explicit owner approval.
5) Reproducibility: every deploy is reproducible from the build id and container image digest.

Contract: deployment orchestration API and required fields
The CI/CD orchestration layer provides a REST API and a CLI wrapper. All promotions must supply the following canonical fields (ledger record):
- build_id: unique build number (string)
- artifact_digest: sha256://... (container or model artifact digest)
- artifact_signature: cosign signature base64 (or key-id)
- target_env: staging|canary|production
- release_notes_id: internal doc id or changelog URL
- owner: team-name or service-owner (email)
- rollout_policy: immediate|gradual|manual
- canary_config: stringified JSON (see example)
- required_gates: list of gate ids (unit-tests, integration-tests, telemetry-sli, security-scan)
- correlation_id: UUID for end-to-end tracing
sections.heading: Scope and principles

sections.body:
{
  "build_id": "20250912-817",
  "artifact_digest": "sha256:3b9a...f8b",
  "artifact_signature": "cosign:ci-key-1:BASE64SIG==",
  "target_env": "canary",
  "release_notes_id": "RN-3421",
  "owner": "incorporation-service-team@redwood.com",
  "rollout_policy": "gradual",
  "canary_config": "{\"traffic_percent\":5,\"duration_minutes\":30}",
  "required_gates": ["unit-tests", "integration-tests", "telemetry-sli", "security-scan"],
  "correlation_id": "b7a9d4c6-..."
}

Gate definitions and enforcement matrix
| Gate id | What is checked | Enforcement action | Owner |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------|-------|
| unit-tests | CI job pass (exit 0) and coverage threshold >= 80% for critical packages | block promotion | service owner (CI job) |
| integration-tests | end-to-end tests against staging fixtures (including model smoke) | block promotion | release engineer |
| telemetry-sli | canary metrics for latency (p50/p95), errors, and correctness evals | block or auto-rollforward with approval | platform SRE |
| security-scan | SCA scan, container CVE threshold (no critical), binary signing present | block and open ticket | security team |
| data-provenance | model artifact has provenance metadata and lineage | block | model-onboarding team |
sections.heading: Sample ledger JSON (stored as an immutable record)

sections.body:
- Latency p95 increase vs baseline <= 15%
- Error rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points OR absolute error rate <= 0.5%
- Regression in eval accuracy <= 1% relative drop on canary prompt set

Canary orchestration playbook (gradual rollout)
1) Start canary (CI command): redwood-ci promote --build $BUILD_ID --target canary --policy gradual --canary 5 --duration 30m
2) Platform creates canary slice and routes 5% production traffic to canary variant. Canary telemetry is tagged with correlation_id and canary=true.
3) Wait for warmup period: 3 minutes for cold-start stabilization, then monitor for duration window: 30 minutes.
4) Evaluate automated gates: telemetry-sli and correctness evals run in background. If gates pass, automatically scale to 25% over an owner-defined step schedule, otherwise trigger rollback.
5) Final approval: once at 25% for 60 minutes with gates green, CI promotions may progress to production if rollout_policy allows. Otherwise, manual approval required.

Failure modes and immediate actions
- Telemetry anomaly (exceeded latency/error thresholds): pause rollout, revert traffic to baseline, notify oncall, create investigation ticket with tags: deploy-failure, canary, service-name.
- Security scan failure discovered post-promotion: immediate quarantine of artifact, block further promotions using that artifact digest, notify security and product owners, and start incident review per incident process.
- Stalled promotion (operator stuck > 120 minutes): auto-escalate to oncall and send digest to paging channel.

Rollback procedure (fast path)
1) Execute: redwood-ci rollback --artifact-digest sha256:... --env production --reason "telemetry-regression"
2) Orchestrator switches route table to previous stable digest using atomic flip; validate health checks for 2 minutes.
3) Emit audit event: deploy.rollback with correlation_id, failing_gate, initiator.
4) Open postmortem ticket and assign owner from ledger owner field.

Audit event taxonomy (structured events emitted by pipeline):
- deploy.requested
- deploy.candidate.validated
- deploy.canary.started
- deploy.canary.metric_snapshot (p50/p95/error/accuracy)
- deploy.canary.decision (pass|fail|escalate)
- deploy.promoted
- deploy.rollback
- deploy.quarantine (security)
- deploy.signing.verification
Each event MUST include: timestamp ISO8601, build_id, artifact_digest, correlation_id, initiator, target_env, and optional details (reason, metric snapshot).

Retention and access
- Audit event retention: 365 days in central logstore (write-once).
- Audit view: read-only dashboards for compliance and security reviewers; access controlled via RBAC.
- Export format: JSONL with event types documented above.

SLOs and operational objectives for the orchestration subsystem
- Deploy success rate (from canary start to prod without rollback): 99% monthly.
- Mean time to promote (canary->prod for gradual policy): P50 < 45 minutes, P95 < 180 minutes.
- Time to rollback (fast path): P50 < 3 minutes, P95 < 10 minutes.
- Ledger write latency: 99% < 250ms for promotion record writes.

Ownership and responsibilities
- CI platform team: implement orchestration API, ledger storage, audit emission, RBAC enforcement, and canary plumbing.
- Service owner: provide release notes, review gate failures, and accept the final promotion.
- SRE: maintain telemetry SLOs and run housekeeping for canary traffic routing.
- Security: define scanning thresholds and key management for signing.

Tooling and example commands
- Build + sign artifact (container):
  docker build -t registry.redwood.com/incorp:20250912-817 .
  docker push registry.redwood.com/incorp@sha256:3b9a...f8b
  cosign sign --key ksm://projects/ci/cosign-key registry.redwood.com/incorp@sha256:3b9a...f8b

- Promote to canary (CLI):
  redwood-ci promote --build 20250912-817 --digest sha256:3b9a...f8b --target canary --canary 5 --duration 30m --correlation b7a9d4c6-...

- Rollback (CLI):
  redwood-ci rollback --artifact-digest sha256:previousStable --env production --reason 'p95-latency-regression' --correlation b7a9d4c6-...
sections.heading: Required thresholds (default)

sections.body:
pipeline:
  stages:
    - name: build-and-sign
      image: docker:stable
      script:
        - make build
        - docker push $IMAGE
        - cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY $IMAGE
    - name: promote
      image: redwood/ci-agent:latest
      script:
        - redwood-ci validate --build $BUILD_ID --gates unit-tests,integration-tests,security-scan
        - redwood-ci promote --build $BUILD_ID --digest $ARTIFACT_DIGEST --target canary --canary 5 --duration 30m

Checklist before a manual production promotion
1) Artifact signed and ledger entry exists.
2) All required gates green for the canary window.
3) Runbook URL and post-deploy contact listed in release_notes.
4) Observability dashboard pre-saved with correlation filtering.
5) Approval from service owner (email/approver id).

Metrics to populate dashboards
- deploy.attempts (per service, per day)
- deploy.successes
- deploy.rollbacks
- deploy.ledger.write_latency_ms
- canary.p95_latency_delta
- canary.error_rate_delta
- artifact.signature_verification_failures

Escalation and oncall flow
1) Automatic alert if telemetry-sli gate fails: page SRE oncall and post message to #deployments with correlation_id.
2) If the rollout is > 120 minutes without decision, page release-engineer oncall.
3) For security quarantine, page security response team and create high-priority ticket.

Testing and staging guidance
- Every service MUST include a synthetic canary job that runs the canonical canary prompt set against the model/service in staging and reports expected correctness metrics to the telemetry SLI system before promotion.
- Periodic chaos exercises: run one simulated-canary-failure game-day per quarter to validate rollback paths and telemetry coverage.

Appendix: sample telemetry SLI snapshot (JSON example)
{
  "p50_latency_ms": 23.4,
  "p95_latency_ms": 81.2,
  "error_rate": 0.003,
  "accuracy_eval": 0.912,
  "baseline_p95_latency_ms": 70.2
}

payload.page_title: Safe Apply + Rollback: E2E Test Strategy (CI/CD + Synthetic Load)

sections.body:
This page defines the end-to-end (E2E) test strategy for the Safe Apply + Rollback mechanism for Optimization Config changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles). The focus is validating:
- Correctness of config versioning and scoping (tenant/model/region)
- Safe apply staged rollout behavior (canary + promote)
- Gating signal evaluation and pause/fail behavior
- One-click/API rollback semantics and runtime idempotency under retry and concurrency
- Audit log emission + RBAC enforcement

The strategy is designed to run in CI (PR gating + merge queues) and in pre-release staging pipelines with synthetic load and controlled failure injection.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
1) Catch regressions before release trains enable the feature flag.
2) Provide high-signal failures (actionable diagnostics; minimal flakes).
3) Validate distributed semantics: partial apply, retries, race conditions (apply vs rollback), and eventual convergence across workers.
4) Validate gating correctness using real metrics plumbing (not mocked), including required tags: tenant, model, region, config_version.
5) Keep runtime reasonable for PR checks; run heavier soak/chaos tests on nightly or pre-release.
sections.heading: Goals

sections.body:
- Full performance benchmarking of all model families (covered in benchmark-lab and perf-canary workflows).
- Automatically proving quality improvements; we only validate that quantization quality gates behave as specified (pass/fail/noise handling).
- Comprehensive cross-subsystem transactional rollback coverage (out of scope in project definition).
sections.heading: Non-goals (initial)

sections.body:
The E2E tests treat the following as a single integrated system:
- Optimization Config Service (version storage, validation, diff, apply/rollback APIs)
- Canary Rollout Controller (progressive apply + pause/resume/fail)
- Serving runtime apply pipeline (fetch/cache/apply config version; idempotency; rollback)
- SLO gate evaluation hooks (error rate, latency; plus optional eval gates for quantization)
- Console backend endpoints (history + rollback action) where applicable
- Audit log pipeline (structured events; export compatibility)
- RBAC policy bundle checks for role-based actions
sections.heading: System under test (SUT)

sections.body: Purpose: high-signal functional correctness with minimal infra cost.
sections.heading: 1) CI Ephemeral Environment (required for PRs)

sections.body:
- Single region (e.g., staging-us-east-1)
- Minimal GPU pool (shared), supporting 1–2 models used for tests
- Dedicated test tenant namespace: `ci-safe-apply-e2e` (unique per run via suffix)
- Control plane + config service + rollout controller deployed from current commit
- Runtime workers deployed from current commit
- Observability stack available (Prometheus-compatible metrics + log aggregation) with short retention
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body: - Must finish PR suite within 20–30 minutes end-to-end.
sections.heading: Constraints

sections.body: Purpose: validate gating signals with realistic traffic patterns; detect race conditions under load.
sections.heading: 2) Pre-release Staging Environment (required for release trains)

sections.body:
- Multi-region (at least 2 regions) to validate scoping and region isolation
- Larger worker pool (still staging), with at least two model deployments:
  - A chat/generation model (streaming enabled)
  - An embedding model (optional; to validate non-chat endpoints are unaffected)
- Gate evaluation stack identical to production (same SLO toolkit rules, same metric tag schema)
- Audit log sink configured to staging SIEM export (or staging equivalent) for schema validation
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body: Purpose: validate version pinning + rollback procedure in an operator-managed setting.
sections.heading: 3) Private Deployment Integration Environment (periodic)

sections.body:
- Spin a representative Kubernetes environment (kind/eks staging) with Redwood Private chart/installer
- Validate operator workflow for pinning config version and executing rollback (no Console dependency)
sections.heading: Requirements

sections.body: We split tests into three tiers.
sections.heading: Test plan summary

sections.body:
- config service / schema / validation
- runtime apply pipeline
- rollout controller
- audit logging / RBAC
- Console rollback APIs

Target runtime: 10–20 minutes.
sections.heading: Runs on every PR touching

sections.body:
1) Create config version → validate schema → ensure immutable version record
2) Safe apply to scoped target (tenant + model + region) with 5% canary → promote to 100%
3) Gate evaluation wiring: confirm gate queries include required tags, and that gating decisions are honored
4) Rollback to prior known-good version → confirm convergence across workers
5) Audit events are emitted with required fields for each lifecycle action
6) RBAC enforcement blocks unauthorized apply/rollback
sections.heading: Coverage

sections.body:
Runs nightly and on demand before enablement.

Target runtime: 45–90 minutes.
sections.heading: Tier B: Nightly E2E + load + failure injection (medium)

sections.body:
- Controlled latency regression injection to force gate failure
- Apply/rollback concurrency tests (race conditions)
- Worker restarts during apply (idempotency and eventual convergence)
- Longer canary windows to detect metric noise issues
sections.heading: Adds

sections.body:
Runs for release trains (or weekly) and before Limited GA expansions.

Target runtime: 2–4 hours.
sections.heading: Tier C: Pre-release soak + multi-region (heavy)

sections.body:
- Multi-region scoping validation under sustained load
- Multi-tenant isolation validation (no leakage of config_version tags)
- Rollback under high concurrency; ensure rollback completes within target MTTR
sections.heading: Adds

sections.body: Below are the canonical scenarios, intended to map to the core user workflows.
sections.heading: Detailed E2E scenarios (what we assert)

sections.body:
1) Create baseline Optimization Config v1 for scope S (tenant T, model M, region R).
2) Create v2 with a small safe change (e.g., batching.max_batch_size increase within allowed range).
3) Fetch v1 and v2; assert:
   - Version IDs differ; v1 content unchanged
   - Metadata present: created_by, created_at, change_reason
4) Fetch diff; assert:
   - Diff highlights changed fields
   - Risk classification flags fields known to be risky (e.g., quantization_profile, cache.enabled)
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Writes are append-only (no in-place mutation)
- Diff endpoint stable and deterministic
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body:
1) Apply v2 to scope S with canary=5%.
2) Start synthetic load against S. (See “Synthetic load spec”.)
3) Gate evaluation passes for required window (e.g., 5 minutes).
4) Promote to 100%.
5) Verify runtime convergence:
   - All workers serving S report active config_version=v2
   - Response headers (if enabled in test env) include active config version for traceability
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Gate is consulted at each progression checkpoint
- Promotion updates the “active pointer” for S (or equivalent) and workers converge
- No cross-scope bleed (other tenants/models/regions remain at v1)
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body: Goal: prove that bad changes do not auto-promote.
sections.heading: Scenario 3: Gate failure pauses rollout (latency regression)

sections.body:
1) Create v3 that will cause measurable latency regression in staging (e.g., disable prefix cache or set overly aggressive batching timeout) OR use fault injection hook to add server-side delay for config_version=v3.
2) Apply v3 with canary=5%.
3) Generate load; validate p95 or error-rate gate triggers failure within the window.
4) Rollout controller should move to PAUSED or FAILED state (per design) and not proceed.
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Rollout controller does not progress beyond canary
- Gate failure reason is recorded (which metric, threshold, observed value)
- Audit event includes gate failure context
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body:
1) Ensure v2 is known-good and currently active at 100%.
2) Apply v3 to canary and force a gate failure.
3) Trigger rollback to v2 via API (Console path is validated separately; this is API truth).
4) Verify:
   - Active pointer returns to v2
   - Workers converge on v2 within bounded time
   - Synthetic load metrics recover (p95 back within threshold)
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Rollback is idempotent (repeating the rollback request is safe)
- Rollback emits the correct audit event with request_id + previous/target version IDs
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body: Goal: validate fix for concurrent operations leaving mixed worker state.
sections.heading: Scenario 5: Apply vs rollback race safety

sections.body:
1) Start apply v3 to 50% (paused midway via controller hook or time window).
2) Concurrently trigger rollback to v2.
3) Restart a subset of workers during the race.
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Final system converges on v2 across all workers
- Controller state machine ends in a consistent terminal state
- No “stuck” shards remain at v3 after rollback completion
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body:
1) Attempt apply/rollback with a token missing `optimization_config.rollback` (or equivalent) permission.
2) Attempt list/read endpoints with read-only role.
sections.heading: Steps

sections.body:
- Unauthorized actions are rejected with clear error messages (403 + reason)
- Audit event is emitted for denied attempts only if policy requires (align with security guidance)
sections.heading: Assertions

sections.body:
For each lifecycle action (create, validate, apply start, apply progression, promote, rollback), assert:
- Event name matches taxonomy
- Required fields present (at minimum): actor, actor_type, tenant, model, region, config_version, previous_config_version (where applicable), request_id, timestamp, outcome, reason
- Events can be exported to staging SIEM sink without schema errors
sections.heading: Scenario 7: Audit event schema compliance

sections.body: Synthetic load is required to make gating meaningful.
sections.heading: Synthetic load spec

sections.body:
- Must tag traffic to the exact scope under test (tenant/model/region)
- Must be able to run deterministic request mixes and concurrency
- Must report:
  - request success/failure counts
  - latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
  - token counts (optional but recommended)
sections.heading: Load generator requirements

sections.body:
- 70% short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
- 25% medium prompts (256–512 tokens)
- 5% long prompts (>= 1024 tokens) to stress KV cache behavior
- Concurrency: 32 in CI; 128 in staging
- Streaming: enabled for 30% of generation calls
sections.heading: Request mix (default)

sections.body:
- CI: 5–8 minutes per scenario (short gate window)
- Nightly: 15–20 minutes for canary windows (noise detection)
- Soak: 60+ minutes sustained
sections.heading: Duration

sections.body:
- Config-induced regression (preferred when deterministic)
- Runtime fault injection keyed by config_version (fallback) with bounded impact:
  - add fixed latency (e.g., +75ms) to a percentage of requests
  - force a controlled 5xx rate (e.g., 1–2%) to validate error-rate gate

All fault injection must be guarded behind a test-only flag and must never be enabled in production.
sections.heading: Use one of

sections.body:
- Each E2E run creates a unique tenant and cleans up resources.
- Model deployments use standardized names:
  - `ci-e2e-chat-model` (generation)
  - `ci-e2e-embed-model` (optional)
- Optimization configs must be created with an explicit `change_reason` and `created_by` referencing the CI actor.
sections.heading: Staging data and test tenants

sections.body:
- CI: delete tenant and all associated config versions at end of run
- Staging soak: retain artifacts for 7 days for debugging (configs + controller state + audit event samples)
sections.heading: Cleanup policy

sections.body: - Changes to `optimization-config-service`, `rollout-controller`, `runtime-config-applier`, `rbac-policy-bundle`, `audit-log-schema`, Console rollback endpoints
sections.heading: Trigger conditions

sections.body:
1) Build + unit tests
2) Spin ephemeral environment (control plane + runtime)
3) Run Tier A E2E suite
4) Collect artifacts:
   - rollout controller state transitions
   - gate evaluation queries and results
   - runtime worker “active config version” snapshots
   - audit log samples (JSON)
5) Teardown
sections.heading: Workflow outline

sections.body: - E2E must pass for merge. Flaky tests cannot be “allowed failures” on PR checks.
sections.heading: Gating

sections.body:
- Run Tier B suite with load + failure injection
- Post summary to #eng-infra-ci and file an issue automatically on regression
sections.heading: Nightly

sections.body: - Run Tier C suite and require sign-off from Release Engineering + SRE
sections.heading: Release train / pre-GA

sections.body: E2E tests for distributed rollouts can be flaky without discipline. The following rules are mandatory.
sections.heading: Flake reduction guidelines

sections.body:
- Poll controller and runtime state with timeouts and clear progress logging.
- Use bounded exponential backoff.
sections.heading: 1) Prefer state-based waits over sleep

sections.body:
- Use short, explicit measurement windows in CI.
- Ensure load generator warms up before gate evaluation begins.
sections.heading: 2) Make gate windows deterministic

sections.body:
- Limit concurrent E2E jobs that share GPU pools.
- Avoid running multiple “heavy” scenarios simultaneously.
sections.heading: 3) Control parallelism and resource contention

sections.body: - Metrics backend must be local/staging-owned. Avoid cross-region dependencies in PR checks.
sections.heading: 4) Minimize reliance on external services

sections.body:
- Test-level retries are allowed only for known transient infrastructure steps (environment spin-up).
- Do not retry business-logic assertions (e.g., “rollback succeeded”)—these should fail loudly.
sections.heading: 5) Define retry policy explicitly

sections.body:
- A failing test may be quarantined only with:
  - owner assigned
  - root cause hypothesis
  - expiration date (<= 14 days)
  - tracking ticket
sections.heading: 6) Quarantine process

sections.body:
The Safe Apply + Rollback feature is considered E2E-test-ready when:
- Tier A suite passes with >= 99% success rate over 20 consecutive runs
- Tier A completes within 30 minutes at p95
- Tier B nightly suite detects injected regressions reliably (>= 95% detection) and has <= 2% false positives
- Artifacts are sufficient to debug failures without re-running locally
sections.heading: Acceptance criteria (definition of “CI-ready”)

sections.body:
- Primary owner: CI/Build (Sahana Iyer)
- Runtime semantics: Serving Runtime (Noah Patel)
- Gate signal correctness and dashboards: SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant)
- Release gating: Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien)
sections.heading: Ownership and escalation

sections.body:
- CI infrastructure failures → #eng-infra-ci
- Gate metric/tagging issues → #eng-sre
- Rollout controller logic/state machine → #eng-platform
- Runtime convergence/idempotency → #eng-runtime
sections.heading: Escalation path

sections.body:
Primary engineering ticket for this doc’s implementation: ENG-4830 (CI e2e tests covering validate→canary→promote→rollback with failure injection).

Changes to this strategy must be reviewed by Release Engineering and SRE before they become PR-blocking requirements.
sections.heading: Tracking

payload.page_title: Private Installer Integration Test Matrix (CI/CD + Build)

sections.body:
h1. Purpose
This page defines the CI integration test matrix for *Redwood Private* upgrades and rollbacks. It is the single source of truth for:
* Which environments we validate (Kubernetes versions, storage backends, VPC vs on-prem).
* Which tests are required for PRs vs merge-to-main vs nightly.
* Release gating requirements for cutting a Private release train build.

This matrix is focused on *upgrade safety*: prechecks, upgrade-plan generation, Helm ordering, backup/restore hooks, and deterministic rollback entry points.

h1. Definitions
* *Private Installer* = redwood-private-installer (operator-facing CLI orchestrating prechecks, plan generation, backups, upgrade execution, rollback).
* *Control plane (CP)* = Redwood Private control services (API/control, auth integrations, upgrade coordinator).
* *Data plane (DP)* = model-serving workers, gateways, runtime components, model cache.
* *N-1 → N* = supported default automated upgrade path (initial GA). Multi-hop upgrades are not fully automated.
* *Online mode* = artifacts fetched from remote registries/repos.
* *Air-gapped mode* = artifacts provided via offline upgrade bundle + local registry/mirror endpoints.

h1. Goals
* Catch upgrade regressions before they reach design partners/customers.
* Validate that installer can *block unsafe upgrades* via preflight checks with actionable remediation.
* Prove rollback can be invoked and completes with post-rollback health validation.
* Maintain a pragmatic CI runtime: PR gating stays fast; deep coverage runs nightly.

h1. Non-goals
* Full combinatorial coverage across every K8s distro and storage system.
* Performance/throughput benchmarking (tracked separately under runtime perf suites).

h1. Test tiers and when they run
h2. Tier 0: Unit + static checks (always)
Runs on every PR for installer/charts/terraform.
* Lint, unit tests
* Plan schema validation
* Helm template render checks
* Basic policy/matrix evaluation tests

h2. Tier 1: PR gating integration tests (required to merge)
*Target runtime:* 20–45 minutes per PR (parallelized).

*What it covers*
1) Fresh install smoke
2) Upgrade plan generation + artifact validation
3) Preflight checks (blocking vs warning)
4) In-place N-1 → N upgrade in a representative environment
5) Rollback command *dry-run* (plan + state machine validation) and one *real rollback* case in nightly only (see Tier 3)

*Merge gate policy*
* Required for changes in:
  * redwood-private-installer
  * redwood-helm-charts (Private charts)
  * redwood (control-plane compatibility / migrations)
* Recommended (non-blocking) for:
  * redwood-terraform (unless upgrade-related variables change)

h2. Tier 2: Merge-to-main integration tests (post-merge confidence)
Triggered on merge to main (or release branches) for relevant repos.
* Broader matrix than PR gating
* Captures issues that only appear with combined changes
* Files issues automatically in ENG + annotates release train

h2. Tier 3: Nightly full matrix + failure injection
Scheduled nightly in UTC.
* Expanded K8s and storage coverage
* Air-gapped verification tests
* Backup + restore hooks exercised
* Real rollback scenario validation
* Failure injection scenarios (DB migration timeout, CP readiness gate failure, artifact mismatch)

h2. Tier 4: Release candidate (RC) gating (must pass to cut a Private release)
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
* Required subset of Tier 3 must pass (see “Release gating” section)
* Evidence is attached to the release train notes by Release Eng

h1. Supported test infrastructure
We run ephemeral clusters and supporting dependencies in CI.

h2. Kubernetes providers
* Primary: EKS (VPC scenarios)
* Secondary: kOps (for more configurable networking cases) and kind (fast smoke only)
* On-prem simulation: kOps cluster with “restricted egress” and local registries to approximate air-gapped flows

h2. Cluster sizing (default CI)
* CP nodes: 2–3
* DP nodes: 2 (GPU not required for upgrade tests; DP charts validated for readiness and rollout ordering)
* DB: Postgres (managed-like for VPC; self-hosted for on-prem simulation)

h2. Artifact sources
* Online mode: Redwood staging registries + chart repo
* Air-gapped mode: offline bundle stored in CI artifact store + local registry mirror container

h1. Kubernetes version policy
We test a rolling window: *current supported* + *next* + *lowest supported*. When a K8s version is added/removed from support, we update this page and the pipeline config in the same PR.

*Current CI coverage targets*
|| Category || Versions || Notes ||
| Lowest supported | 1.27 | Included in nightly and RC gating |
| Current default | 1.28 | Primary PR gating target |
| Newer supported | 1.29 | Included in nightly; add PR gating when adoption increases |
| Next (preview) | 1.30 | Nightly “canary”; failures are tracked but do not block releases unless elevated |

h1. Storage backend matrix
We cover the storage systems most likely to impact backup/snapshot hooks and Helm upgrade safety.

|| Storage backend || Where tested || Why it matters ||
| EBS (gp3) via CSI | PR gating + nightly | Snapshot hooks + PV behavior |
| EFS | Nightly | RWX semantics; common in CP shared assets |
| CSI hostPath (kind) | Smoke only | Fast feedback; not representative |
| Ceph/Rook (CSI) | Nightly (best-effort) | On-prem common; snapshot/restore differences |
| Longhorn | Nightly (best-effort) | On-prem common; PV attachment edge cases |

*Notes*
* “Best-effort” means we run it nightly and triage failures as P1 if repeatable; we do not block PR merges on single-run flakes.

h1. Environment scenarios (VPC vs on-prem)
We classify test scenarios by constraints that affect upgrade reliability.

|| Scenario || Connectivity || Artifact flow || Primary risks || Coverage tier ||
| VPC (standard) | Full egress | Online registries/repos | Version gating; Helm ordering; migrations | Tier 1/2/3 |
| VPC (restricted egress) | Limited egress | Mirror endpoints | Artifact reachability, TLS/DNS | Tier 3 + RC |
| On-prem (connected) | Egress allowed but controlled | Online or mirror | DNS/TLS, RBAC/SSO, storage variability | Tier 3 |
| On-prem (air-gapped) | No egress | Offline bundle + local registry | Bundle verification, missing artifacts, rollback safety | Tier 3 + RC |

h1. Required test cases (what each pipeline must validate)
h2. Common assertions (all tiers)
* Installer outputs an *upgrade plan artifact* and persists it in the run workspace.
* Preflight checks produce structured results with:
  * severity (block/warn/info)
  * remediation pointers
  * stable check IDs for dashboards
* Helm upgrade respects CP/DP ordering and readiness gates.
* Post-upgrade health verification passes:
  * CP deployments ready
  * DP deployments rolled out (or explicitly skipped if configured)
  * DB migrations in expected state (no pending locks; schema version recorded)

h2. Test case catalog
|| ID || Test case || Pass criteria || Tiers ||
| IT-01 | Fresh install smoke | All core namespaces ready; API health endpoint OK | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-02 | Upgrade plan generation | Plan includes staged CP then DP steps; includes rollback entry points; artifact URLs resolved | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-03 | Preflight: cluster health | Blocks if nodes not Ready; blocks on critical PodDisruptionBudget violations | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-04 | Preflight: storage headroom | Blocks when below threshold; warning when near threshold | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-05 | Preflight: DB connectivity | Blocks if cannot reach DB or auth fails; emits remediation | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-06 | Preflight: RBAC/SSO reachability | Warns or blocks based on configuration; must be deterministic | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-07 | N-1 → N upgrade | Upgrade completes; CP before DP; audit events emitted; no crash loops | 1/2/3/RC |
| IT-08 | Backup hook (snapshot/logical) | Backup completes; verification step confirms restore point exists | 3/RC |
| IT-09 | Rollback (real) after induced failure | Rollback returns system to N-1; post-rollback health passes | 3/RC |
| IT-10 | Air-gapped bundle verification | Bundle checksum/signature verified; missing artifact fails fast with clear error | 3/RC |

h1. CI matrix (what runs where)
The table below is the *authoritative matrix* for gating.

h2. Tier 1 (PR gating) matrix
|| Dimension || Default || Variants ||
| K8s version | 1.28 | none |
| Storage | EBS gp3 | none |
| Scenario | VPC (standard) | none |
| Artifact flow | Online | none |
| Upgrade path | N-1 → N | none |
| Tests | IT-01..IT-07 | rollback is dry-run only |

h2. Tier 2 (merge-to-main) matrix
|| Dimension || Values ||
| K8s version | 1.28, 1.29 |
| Storage | EBS gp3 |
| Scenario | VPC (standard) |
| Artifact flow | Online |
| Tests | IT-01..IT-07 |

h2. Tier 3 (nightly) matrix
|| Dimension || Values ||
| K8s version | 1.27, 1.28, 1.29, 1.30 (preview) |
| Storage | EBS gp3, EFS, Ceph/Rook (best-effort), Longhorn (best-effort) |
| Scenario | VPC (standard), VPC (restricted egress), on-prem (connected sim), on-prem (air-gapped sim) |
| Artifact flow | Online, Mirror endpoints, Offline bundle |
| Tests | IT-01..IT-10 (includes backup + real rollback) |

h2. RC gating (minimum required before release promotion)
*Must pass (hard gate)*
* K8s 1.27 + EBS gp3 + VPC (standard) + Online: IT-01..IT-10
* K8s 1.28 + EBS gp3 + VPC (restricted egress) + Mirror: IT-01..IT-07 + IT-10
* K8s 1.28 + EBS gp3 + On-prem (air-gapped sim) + Offline bundle: IT-02 + IT-07 + IT-10 + IT-09

*Soft signals (review required if failing)*
* K8s 1.29 coverage
* EFS coverage
* Ceph/Rook and Longhorn (best-effort)

h1. Job orchestration and naming
h2. GitHub Actions / CI job families
(Exact implementation may vary per repo; names are standardized for dashboards.)
* *private-it-pr-gate* (Tier 1)
* *private-it-post-merge* (Tier 2)
* *private-it-nightly-matrix* (Tier 3)
* *private-it-rc-gate* (Tier 4)

h2. Artifact retention
* Tier 1/2: retain logs + plan artifacts for 14 days
* Tier 3: retain for 30 days
* RC gating: retain for 180 days (audit evidence for enterprise customers)

h2. What each job must upload
* Installer logs (structured + human-readable)
* Upgrade plan artifact (JSON)
* Precheck result bundle
* Helm release state snapshots (selected namespaces)
* Backup/restore verification logs (Tier 3/RC)
* Rollback run logs (Tier 3/RC)

h1. Failure injection (nightly + RC)
We intentionally induce failures to validate rollback and determinism.

|| Failure mode || How induced || Expected behavior ||
| DB migration lock timeout | Reduce lock timeout; create competing lock | Upgrade halts; operator-friendly error; rollback succeeds |
| Control-plane readiness gate failure | Block CP readiness endpoint / force crashloop | DP rollout must not start; rollback path remains valid |
| Artifact mismatch | Swap bundle manifest checksum / missing chart | Installer fails fast during prechecks/verification |
| Insufficient storage headroom | Fill PV to cross threshold | Precheck blocks with remediation guidance |

h1. Flakiness policy
* Tier 1 flake tolerance: *zero*. A flaky Tier 1 test is treated as a release blocker until fixed or removed.
* Tier 3 best-effort jobs may retry once automatically. If the same signature fails 2 nights in a row, file an issue and mark as *P1 if upgrade/rollback correctness is affected*.
* Any failure in IT-07/IT-09/IT-10 in RC gating is a hard stop.

payload.page_title: GPU CI credential rotation and image promotion safety kit

sections.body:
Summary

Purpose
This document defines a safety-first pattern for: (1) rotating CI credentials used by GPU provisioning and image-promotion pipelines, and (2) promoting GPU runtime images (golden bundles) to production pools with provable checks and fast rollback paths. The kit bundles Terraform/IaC patterns, CI job templates, runtime verification checks, SLO-driven gating, and an operator runbook for emergency credential revocation.

Why this matters
- Credential rotation without careful orchestration can leave running inference pools unable to pull images, causing degraded capacity and failed deployments.
- Image promotion (CI -> staging -> prod) must be atomic and verifiable: a mismatched image in a GPU pool can produce model-regression incidents.
- Past incidents show the majority of image-promotion outages occur during key rotation + cross-account image copy windows. This doc reduces blast radius.

Scope
Applies to: all CI pipelines that build GPU runtime images, the Terraform modules that provision tenant GPU hosts and warm pools, and the image-signing/attestation services used by Redwood Inference.

Owner and contacts
- Owner team: engineering (Infra Reliability)
- Primary oncall for rollout windows: infra-oncall@redwood.com
- Escalation: Diego Ramos (Lead - GPU Infra), Priya Shah (Security), Evan Liu (CI/CD)

Terminology
- Golden image: signed OCI image bundle used for production inference nodes.
- Image promoter: CI job that signs, copies, and tags artifacts into the production registry.
- Promotion window: the short period where an image transitions from staging to prod and cross-account copies may be in-flight.

Safety principles (high level)
1) Always sign images with key versioning (KMS key alias + key-id). Verification must include key version metadata.
2) Use a promotion plan that stages in-region canaries before full fleet promotion.
3) Make credential rotation a two-phase operation: preflight (test) then swap (cutover) with automatic rollback on failure.
4) Prefer short-lived credentials (ephemeral IAM role / signed cert) for CI agents; store long-term secrets only in HSM-backed KMS.
5) Maintain an explicit PROMOTION SAFETY MATRIX mapping signals to actions (below).

Promotion safety matrix\
| Signal | Threshold | Action | Rollback trigger |
|--------|-----------:|--------|-----------------|
| Canary 99th latency increase | +40% vs baseline | Halt promotion, mark image suspect, run deeper perf trace | Auto-revert to previous tag in 15m if >2 buckets exceed threshold |
| Error rate (5xx) | >0.5% absolute | Re-route 100% traffic off canary nodes, abort promotion | Full fleet rollback if persisted for 10m |
| Tokenization mismatch (new tokenizer failure) | any runtime error | Halt; capture failing prompt, block image | Manual rollback after investigation |
| Image signature verification failures | any | Stop promotion, alert security, revoke CI key version | Block until signature chain validated |
| Pull auth errors across >=2 regions | >=3% pull failures | Pause promotion; force ephemeral credential refresh | If persists 10m, automated rollback and revoke ephemeral role |

Preflight checklist (CI + Terraform)
1) CI builds image and signs with signing service (key alias: kms/gpu-image-signer). Artifact metadata must include key-version and build-id.
2) CI runs integration smoke: small inference harness against a staging warm pool (tag: staging-smoke). Verify latency and correctness metrics.
3) Terraform plan for registry permissions and cross-account roles is generated and reviewed via tfsec/gate. Module names referenced: tf-modules/registry-crosscopy, tf-modules/ephemeral-ci-role, tf-modules/warm-pool-provisioner.
4) Register promotion intent in the promotion ledger (tagged Git commit + promotion ticket).

CI pipeline example (GitHub Actions / Buildkite style)
- name: build-and-sign-gpu-image
  runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
  steps:
    - checkout
    - run: |
        docker build -t staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} -f infra/Dockerfile .
        docker push staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
    - uses: redwood/sign-image-action@v1
      with:
        image: staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
        kms-key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/gpu/cryptoKeys/gpu-image-signer
    - run: |
        curl -X POST https://signing.redwood.internal/attest -d '{"image":"staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}","key_version":"v3"}'

Promotion job (partial)
- name: promote-to-canary
  env:
    EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
  steps:
    - assume-role $EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN --duration 900
    - run: |
        ./scripts/cross-account-copy --src staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} --dst prod-gpu:${{PROMOTION_TAG}} --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1
    - run: |
        terraform -chdir=infra/promotion apply -auto-approve -var='image_tag=${PROMOTION_TAG}'

Terraform patterns and recommendations
- Module: registry-crosscopy
  - Purpose: declaratively model cross-account ECR/GCR copy permissions and a short-lived promotion task.
  - Inputs: src_repo, dst_repo, allowed_regions, promotion_role_arn
  - Outputs: promotion_task_id, crosscopy_logs_s3
- Module: ephemeral-ci-role
  - Purpose: create an IAM role the CI system assumes for promotion. Short-lived session only; require MFA for manual triggers. Use OPA policy to prevent wide-scoped permissions.
- Remote state gating: the promotion apply must assert a remote state lock and include a semaphore key in a central tfstate bucket to avoid concurrent promotions.

Credential rotation protocol (two-phase)
Phase A: Preflight (no live swap)
1) Provision new KMS key version and create alias kms/gpu-image-signer -> key-vN.
2) Deploy CI adapters (sign-image-action) to use key-vN in a feature-flagged mode and run 100% test-signings that do not change promotion ledger. Verify that attestation services accept key-vN signatures.
3) Run shadow cross-account copy with ephemeral role using new signing metadata. Confirm copies succeed across all target regions.
4) Monitor for 24h (or 3 release windows) for any unexpected pull auth regressions.

Phase B: Cutover (the swap)
1) Schedule change window (SLO: <30m blind window).
2) Update alias kms/gpu-image-signer -> key-vN (atomic alias swap).
3) Revoke short-lived CI credentials associated with key-v(N-1) after 5m grace. Rotate ephemeral role sessions.
4) Promote a canary image signed with key-vN. Verify canary health for 20m across latency/error metrics.
5) Proceed to full fleet promotion if no triggers fired; otherwise, revert alias to key-v(N-1) and mark key-vN as revocation-pending for forensic review.

Emergency rollback runbook (oncall steps)
1) Detect: Pager fires for pull auth failures or mass pod CrashLoopBackOff when pulling prod images.
2) Immediate action (within first 5 minutes):
   - Confirm via cross-region registry metrics whether pull auth errors are present and their percentage.
   - If pull auth failures >=3% across >=2 regions, run: ./scripts/revoke-ci-ephemeral-sessions --role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
   - If image signature mismatch reported, quarantine the image tag: mark in the promotion ledger as blocked.
3) If problems persist >10m:
   - Revert registry image tag on affected warm pools to previous production tag via terraform apply -var='image_tag=${PREV_TAG}'
   - Recreate node groups (if nodes are stuck) by triggering warm-pool rolling-replace job.
4) Post-incident: open an incident review, attach promotion ledger entries, CI logs, KMS audit trail, and the short-lived session token logs.

Observability and SLOs to enforce
- Canary latency delta SLO: canary 99th must stay within +25% of baseline during canary window.
- Image pull success: >=99.5% successful pulls within 1m of request at steady state.
- Promotion lead time: preflight checks must finish within 90 minutes for standard releases; emergencies may use expedited path with manual approver.

Telemetry dashboards (must include)
- Registry pull success rate by region and account (1m and 5m windows)
- Image signature verification failures by key-version
- Promotion job success/failure histogram (by commit)
- Canary latency and error rate trends vs baseline (auto-annotate promotion events)

Automation safety checks (required CI gates)
- Signatures must be validated by attestation service and include key-version metadata. Job fails on mismatches.
- OPA admission check in promotion Terraform that asserts promotion_task_id is unique and no concurrent promotions are in progress.
- Pre-promotion smoke harness that runs 100 inference prompts and validates outputs against a golden-response set (fuzzy matching allowed; threshold 95% similarity).

FAQ and edge cases
Q: What if a region's image copy lags by more than 30 minutes?
A: Pause promotion and trigger a manual crosscopy re-run. If unable to copy within 60 minutes, postpone full promotion and continue with a limited regional promotion strategy.

Q: Who can manually trigger expedited promotions?
A: CI admins with MFA + a signed approval from the Release Lead and Security. The ephemeral role requires an MFA assertion to be assumed for manual flows.

Appendix A — Example Terraform stub for ephemeral role
resource "aws_iam_role" "ci_ephemeral_publisher" {
  name               = "ci-ephemeral-publisher-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume.json
  tags = { team = "gpu-infra", created_by = "ci-pipeline" }
}

payload.page_title: Preflight GPU IaC Load Validator and CI Gate

sections.body:
Summary

This document describes the Preflight GPU IaC Load Validator (PGILV) — a test harness and CI gating pattern that runs realistic synthetic inference workloads against proposed Terraform/Helm changes to detect capacity, network, egress, and SLO regressions before they merge. The PGILV reduces post-deploy incidents by validating behavioral and cost-safety invariants in a short, repeatable CI stage.

Goals

- Prevent IaC changes that would cause: GPU contention, SLO regressions (>5% tail latency increase), cross-account egress spikes, or Terraform drift that violates tenancy constraints.
- Provide a deterministic, low-cost synthetic load that approximates production mixes (chat vs. embeddings vs. eval batch).
- Provide signal and remediation suggestions (fail, require canary, or auto-rollback) integrated into the GitHub Actions pipeline and Terraform plan checks.

Scope and non-goals

- Scope: Changes to gpu pool definitions, autoscaler policies, VPC egress rules, NAT/transit gateway routing, and tenant-affinity Terraform modules. Also useful for operator changes to allocator-svc and burst-orchestrator.
- Non-goals: Full-scale production soak tests (those run in the long-running stress lab) or model quality evaluations. PGILV is a fast preflight (15–30 minutes).

Architecture overview

- Components:
  - sim-runner: containerized executor that replays a parametric mix of request shapes (token lengths, concurrent sessions, KV cache warm vs cold) and records telemetry.
  - tf-guard: a small Terraform provider/plan-check wrapper that exposes the planned sizing/quotas to the CI job.
  - preflight-broker: lightweight orchestration service in CI that provisions temporary namespaces (tenant-sandbox), attaches ephemeral GPU leases, deploys the proposed artifacts, runs sim-runner, and gathers telemetry.
  - telemetry-collector: collects Prometheus metrics, gpu-util traces, egress bytes, and topk latency histograms.

Workflow (high-level)

1. Developer opens PR with Terraform/Helm changes.
2. CI triggers PGILV stage after unit tests and tf fmt/validate pass.
3. tf-guard extracts planned capacity changes and early-qualifies trivial fixes (e.g., tag corrections).
4. preflight-broker provisions a tenant-sandbox forged from the TF plan (uses existing sandbox account and a short-lived lease).
5. The proposed infra is applied in the sandbox (via a focused terraform workspace and module stubbing to avoid production mutation).
6. sim-runner runs a set of deterministic scenarios (see Scenarios section) for 12 minutes each while telemetry-collector captures signals.
7. Analyzer evaluates invariants (SLO, egress, GPU packing, kernel fallback). The job returns PASS/FAIL and annotated artifacts (prometheus snapshots, flame graphs, and a short verdict).

Preflight invariants and thresholds

- Latency SLO (interactive routes): 95th p99 latency must not increase by >5% relative to the baseline snapshot.
- Batch throughput (large-batch routes): throughput must be within 90–110% of baseline for equal resource allocation.
- GPU oversubscription: sustained CUDA SM utilization >92% for more than 90 seconds flags potential contention.
- KV cache miss-rate: increase >10 percentage points triggers a warning (indicates config may break warm-prefix performance).
- Egress spike: %% increase in egress bytes per tenant must be below 20% for the simulated window.
- Terraform safety: no changes that reduce per-tenant minimum quota, remove egress filters, or lower NAT SNAT pool size below policy threshold.

Baseline snapshots

- Baseline snapshots are stored per-service and digest (model:resets) in the artifacts bucket. The CI job uses the most recent stable baseline (tagged) for comparisons. Baseline refresh requires an owner-approved run (monthly or after a major runtime release).

Sim-runner scenarios (examples)

1. Chat-heavy (60% small tokens / 30% medium / 10% long): 200 concurrent sessions, ramp 0->200 in 60s, sustain 10m.
2. Embedding storm: 1k short concurrent requests batched at the sidecar; measures egress and batching delta.
3. Cold KV cache spike: new-prefix traffic that forces KV warmup across GPU shards; observe cold-miss rates and tail latency.
4. Mixed canary: 10% noisy tenant (heavy token sequences) in a shared pool to validate fairness throttles.

Terraform / module validation patterns

- tf-guard performs plan-time assertions by parsing the plan output (JSON) and verifying:
  - node pool sizes, instance types, and GPU counts match allowed families (policy).
  - autoscaler min/max bounds are within runway budgets.
  - egress routing changes do not remove NAT or transit gateway filters.
sections.heading: Overview

sections.body:
# run plan and validate assertions
  terraform init -backend-config=\"bucket=ci-tf-state\" && terraform plan -out=pr.plan && terraform show -json pr.plan | tf-guard assert --policy-file=ci/policies/preflight-policy.yaml

Sample preflight-policy.yaml (key checks)

  allow_instance_families: [\"a100\",\"h100\",\"v100\"]
  min_gpu_per_node: 1
  max_preemptable_ratio: 0.6
  nat_pool_min_ports: 2048

CI pipeline snippet (GitHub Actions, simplified)

  name: preflight-gpu-iac
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    preflight:
      runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - name: terraform validate
          run: terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
        - name: terraform plan + tf-guard
          run: |
            terraform plan -out=pr.plan
            terraform show -json pr.plan | tf-guard assert --policy-file=ci/policies/preflight-policy.yaml
        - name: apply to sandbox and run sim
          uses: redwoodci/preflight-runner@v1
          with:
            plan: pr.plan
            sim: ci/scenarios/chat-heavy.yaml
            timeout-minutes: 40
        - name: upload results
          run: rcli upload-artifact --path=./preflight-results --tag=pr-1234

Telemetry and observability

- Collector integrates with Prometheus (pushgateway for ephemeral sandboxes) and writes snapshots to the artifacts bucket. Captured metrics:
  - allocator_slo_latency_ms{route}
  - gpu_sm_util_percent{node}
  - kernel_fallback_count
  - kv_cache_miss_ratio
  - egress_bytes_by_tenant
sections.heading: Example tf-guard command (CI)

sections.body:
- P99 interactive latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(allocator_slo_latency_ms_bucket[2m])) by (le, route))
- GPU sustained util: avg_over_time(gpu_sm_util_percent[2m]) > 92
- Egress delta: (sum(rate(egress_bytes_total[2m])) by (tenant) - baseline_egress_bytes) / baseline_egress_bytes

Analyzer verdicts and actions

- PASS: No invariant violations. CI proceeds to merge checks.
- WARNING: Non-fatal regressions (e.g., modest KV miss) — add reviewer ack required.
- FAIL: Any hard threshold breach (latency >5% or GPU oversubscription) — block merge and attach artifact bundle.

- Remediation hints included in analyzer output (e.g., recommend raising autoscaler max, reducing default tenant burst credits, or increasing NAT ports).

Runbook: triage a failed preflight

1. Open the preflight artifact bundle from build (artifact tag shows plan snapshot, prom snapshot, flame graphs).
2. Re-run sim-runner locally against the same plan: redwood-sim run --plan pr.plan --scenario debug-cold-kv --output ./local-run
3. If GPU oversubscription: check node type, gpu_count, and packing constraints in the TF plan; propose increasing node count or changing instance_family.
4. If egress spike: inspect new routing blocks or service account changes that might force traffic through NAT.
5. If SLO regression: compare histogram snapshots; identify which route/model produced tail. Attach flame graph and ask model-onboarding or runtime-team for kernel/fallback check.
6. Mark the PR with the triage label and request an approver from the infra-owner list.

Ownership and ops

- Owners:
  - infra-preflight: Maya Chen (infra/ci-cd)
  - allocator-slo: Diego Alvarez (serving-runtime)
  - tf-guard: Priya Suresh (infra-iac)

Operational play: schedule and cost

- Each preflight execution runs in the sandbox account and consumes a capped ephemeral lease (default 1 x a100 for 40 minutes). Billing tags are attached to the PR id.
- Cost limits: a single PR job should not exceed $60 in compute; monitor via the cost-tag report. Jobs exceeding cost limits are aborted and marked as REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Safety caveats and edge cases

- False positives: Short synthetic runs can be noisy — analyzer includes a noise-tolerant comparator (statistical bootstrap with 95% confidence) but maintainers should be careful for low-sample routes.
- Stale baselines: Baseline mismatches after runtime releases may produce spurious failures; baseline refresh requires a weekly owner job or a tagged runtime release to trigger automated baseline update.

Integration roadmap and future work

- Integrate with policy-as-code (OPA) to centralize guard checks and make policies reusable across repos.
- Extend sim-runner scenarios with model-weighted mixes (replicate top-10 tenant fingerprints).
- Add an optional longer-duration canary stage that, on PASS, will schedule a 6-hour canary in a federated warm-pool cluster before full rollout.

Appendices

A. Example Terraform assertion snippet (tf-guard rule)

  - name: node_pool_family_check
    type: allow-list
    attribute: aws_instance_type
    allowed: [\"p4d.24xlarge\",\"p5.24xlarge\",\"trn1.32xlarge\"]

B. Helpful CLI commands

  # re-run a preflight locally
  redwood-preflight run --plan pr.plan --scenario chat-heavy --local

  # fetch artifacts
  rcli download-artifact --tag=pr-1234 --dest=./artifacts

C. Contacts and escalation

- Pager for infra-preflight: #infra-oncall (pager duty)
- Slack channels: #infra-ci, #gpu-fleet, #runtime-perf

D. Quick links

- Sandbox account onboarding: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/onboard-tenant-gpu-portal-terraform-guardrails-and-release-playbook.json
- Runbook for rollback: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook.json

If you are implementing or modifying PGILV, follow the steps in the Workflow section and add new scenarios to ci/scenarios with representative seed traffic. For policy changes to tf-guard, coordinate with the infra-iac team and include a unit test that covers the new assertion.
